data.projectName: :  Evaluation of Historical Building Material Properties for Repair and Restoration by Using Advanced Techniques
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The durability of the historical building materials deteriorates over time, affecting the serviceability of the building. This impairment is mainly due to environmental, chemical and temperature changes. The historical buildings in Pakistan have also gone through these changes and are at present in need of repair and restoration. However, restoring structures to their original form requires a selection or development of building materials having similar or compatible physical and mechanical properties, as those of original materials of construction. For this, extensive onsite and laboratory investigation including mineralogy, morphology, petrographic, chemical composition of historical material is required. The use of non-destructive techniques for historical material investigation is not common in Pakistan due to which material choices are limited. In this proposed study the samples from historical sites/buildings of Sindh will be collected and their properties will be characterized by employing non-destructive testing on-site and laboratory. Such as X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray fluorescence (XRF), thermal analyses (TGA). Based on test results, a variety of materials will be developed/proposed for use as repair and restoration for historical sites. It is expected that this proposed study will result in the formulation of material analysis and design guidelines for historic sites/buildings in Sindh. These guidelines will help historical buildings preservation agencies/organizations in restoring buildings in their original shape with long-lasting strength. In the long run, the restoration of historic buildings will add to the economy by attracting tourists and historians.

data.projectName: Estimation of Genetic Diversity of pheasants of Malakand Division, Pakistan.
data.projectDigest: Once adequate data from surveys and research have been collected, the information needs to be synthesized and large-scale patterns described. It is at this stage that species can be allocated meaningfully to threat categories, thereby placing the need for conservation action in a global context. With the extremely limited resources available for conservation action, this is necessary before more specific local conservation actions can be recommended. Wherever possible, conservation recommendations should be based on existing structures and frameworks (Dai Bo et al., 1998). Taxonomists have always considered the pheasants to be more closely related to the Old World partridge, quail, and francolin species than to any other group in the Galliformes. Peters (1934), Johnsgard (1973), and Delacour (1977) placed all of these species in the subfamily Phasianinae within the family Phasianidae, which also included the grouse and New World quails. Johnsgard (1973, 1986, and 1999) suggested that the Phasianinae should be split into two tribes: the pheasants in the Phasianini and the Old World partridge, quail, and francolin species in the Perdicini. On the basis of DNA hybridisation analysis, Sibley and Monroe (1990, 1993) classified the pheasants and the Old World partridge, quail, and francolin species (i.e., excluding grouse and New World quails) as the family Phasianidae. There has been much less argument about which species of Galliformes are pheasants and which belong to other groups, although a recent study founded on molecular evidence has indicated that the pheasants and partridges may not be best represented as separate natural groupings (Kimball et al. 1999).

data.projectName: Biosynthesis of nanoparticles from different halophytes and their potential to alleviate salt stress
data.projectDigest: Soil salinity is one of the causes of abiotic stress that decrease crop performance. Halophytes which are useful in industrial purposes and characterized by special physiological adaptations to challenge severe salinity. A number of metabolites are present in halophytes which can be used to induce NaCl resistant in other salt sensitive crops. Recently, nanotechnology has gained the attentions of scientists in various disciplines including agriculture science. However, adequate information on the salinity resistance mechanism mediated by halophyte based nanoparticles on crop plants is not available. Use of nanoparticles is expected to improve the crop productivity by enhancing plant nutrition, precision farming, water use efficiency etc. Exogenous application of different chemicals extracted from halophytes can trigger the salt tolerance mechanisms in other plants. Thus, the aim of present work is to 1) optimize the conditions to synthesize nanoparticles from different halophytes, 2) application of halophytic nanoparticles for alleviating salt stress in tomato plants 3) understanding the mechanism of plant growth, water relation, ion flux, photosynthesis, metabolic adjustment and antioxidant defense subjected to nanoparticles treatment in salinity. Nanoparticles prepared from halophytes could be applied as a promising natural organic bio-fertilizer to combat the saline effect of agricultural lands, which hinders improvements of plant growth and suggests future perspectives as well as several research limitations in this field. The present project will explore the possibility of reducing pressure on conventional crop by providing sustainable biomass of tomato with less efforts and make use of saline soil and brackish water.

data.projectName: Pharmacogenomic analysis of drugs in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis in Pakistani population
data.projectDigest:
Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disease primarily causing joint inflammation and degradation. Estimated prevalence of self-reported rheumatic diseases is 14.8% in Pakistan thus responsible for substantial socioeconomic burden. RA is a chronic illness requiring life-long treatment. However, the choice of appropriate drug remains a clinical challenge due to inter-individual variability in drug responsiveness and adverse drug reactions (ADR). Resulting delayed or inappropriate therapy renders the affected individuals less productive due to mild-to-severe permanent disability. 
Genetic factors are important in ADR and also account for 20-95% of drug response variability. Pharmacogenomics seeks to identify genetic factors responsible for these variable responses. The pharmacogenomics research on RA is still rudimentary particularly in Pakistan.  Therefore, the proposed study is intended on the genetic analysis of RA patients by identifying responders and non-responders to specific drugs. DNA and serum samples will be extracted from whole blood for the analysis of candidate genetic factors and pro-inflammatory markers, respectively.
This pharmacogenomics study is expected to identify novel genetic factors that could be used as predictive markers detectable through laboratory tests to help rheumatologists in precision medicine to effectively reduce the risk of disability among productive middle-aged population of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Biomagnification of hazardous heavy metals and pesticides in the food chains of Faisalabad
data.projectDigest: Faisalabad  is the industrial as well as the agricultural zone of Pakistan.. and a major producer of superphosphates, textiles, industrial chemicals, paper, agricultural equipment, and ghee  (FCCI 2018) thereby adding heavy metals in Faisalabad (Shahid & Hussain 2013). Mercury, Lead, Arsenic and Chromium have been found exceeding limits of NEQs of Faisalabad Region (Aziz and Altaf, 2018). Along with these contaminants, farmers have been convinced by the pesticide companies to spray more pesticides than that recommended by the label through media campaign, for effective control in different crops (Tariq, 2005). The regions will be screened for the presence of Chlorpyrifos, dieldrin Endosulfan sulphate, Methamidophos, Heptachlor, Monocrotophos, o,p, DDT, p,p DDT, using plants (preferably edible) gastropods (detrivore and calcium source for animals), fish, frogs, and finally crows (as omnivore and scavenger) as bioindicator species along with being representative of major classes. The humans blood will be further tested for the presence of the heavy metals and pesticides along with other biochemical assays to corelate the concentration with that of the human health. The trophic transfer of organophosphates and heavy metals may lead to the long distance transport of these substances. Detrivores such as gastropods and primary producers are important as they bridge the abiotic and biotic components. These heavy metals and pesticides have been chosen as these are cancer causing (Eqani et al. 2012b) and disrupt various physiological processes. (Balkhair and Ashraf 2016).

data.projectName: IoT-based Forest Monitoring System using Acoustic Properties of Tree-cutting in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Internet of Things (IoT) is made up of devices that connect to the internet and share data with each other. There are many applications of IoT including forest monitoring, smart cities, smart home, smart health services, E-businesses, and so on. Deforestation is a major challenge in Pakistan. Illegal logging of forest is one of the major causes of the deforestation. Although, there are some mechanism to thwart against this activity like monitoring of forest using forest guards, satellite, GIS and remote sensing monitoring, however, these solutions are not robust and do not provide any real-time information about the  illegal logging. In this research, we will develop IoT-based forest monitoring system which will provide the guard against the illegal logging of forest. We will deploy IoT-based wireless sensor network, which will acquire the real time data about the ongoing activities in the forest. The main activity that will be sensed by the sensors will be the sound of cutting trees. These sensors will send the data to the remote sink using multi-hop communication. The acquired data will be classified using machine learning algorithms. Based on the data, the system will be trained to differentiate between the different sounds.

data.projectName: Collection, identification and documentation (CID) of Rubus species from  the State of Azad Jammu and Kashmir
data.projectDigest: Rubus is a large and diverse species of flowering plants in the rose family Rosaceae with 250-700 species. The most common and widely distributed members of the genus are raspberries, blackberries and dewberries. Among small fruits group, raspberries are considered the richest source of anthocyanins and other bioactive compounds. Most of the species of Rubus are native to eastern North America and are deciduous in nature. Being temperate fruit species, they grow very well when temperatures are moderate in summer and cold in winter. Moreover, they also require enough sunlight to produce flowers. Fortunately, the State of Azad Jammu and Kashmir is blessed with both, the ideal temperature for their growth and enough sunlight throughout the year and therefore, huge plantation could be found in wild. Azad Jammu and Kashmir is part of Lesser Himalayas ranges situated in the north eastern part of Pakistan and extend from low subtropical plains in the south to high alpine slopes of 3,000 meter or more in elevation in the north. Due to variation in the topography, altitudes aspects and vegetation cover, the climate of Lesser Himalayas ranges show tremendous variation. Even within the range inner and outer parts contrastingly differ in amount of rainfall, snowfall and temperature conditions. There is enormous need and scope for the conservation of genetic resources of Rubus species in this area. So far no studies have been conducted for collection, identification and documentation of these plants. Therefore, this study has been designed to collect these wildly grown species from three divisions of Azad Jammu and Kashmir, identify them and document their characteristics for future studies and research planning.

data.projectName: Bioluminescence (Vibrio ?scheri) and mutagenicity assay for the identification of inorganic toxic compounds from dairy and food products in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Unrestrained use of fertilizers in agriculture is posing a serious high risk to consumer’s health and the environment. To enhance the yield, extensive fertilizers are applied to the crops and resultantly, the toxic moieties are get mixed in food chain, which can be harmful to the consumers. The nitrogenous compounds are known to cause several health complications i.e., vitamin A deficiency and cancer. They can also decrease the oxygen carrying capacity of the blood. Bioluminescence assays (Vibrio fischeri) a gram negative bacteria is widely used for environmental toxicity monitoring. For the assessment of nitrate/nitrite bioavailability in different vegetable and crops, it is simple, fast, convenient and inexpensive method to check the level of nitrate/nitrite in different grains and vegetable. A bioluminescence assays kit will be developed which will be easy to carry and monitor the toxicity level within short duration. In many country, for the initial screening of toxicity, bioluminescence assays is widely used. But unfortunately, here in Pakistan, for the detection of nitrate/ nitrite and heavy metal still expensive method. A biological screening tool for the monitoring of nitrate/nitrite in vegetables and grains will be developed, which is short term assay to evaluate the toxicity level quantitatively. Using this biological monitoring assay, can control the unrestrained use of fertilizers in agriculture sector, and prevent their negative impacts, particularly to children to avoid the neurological disorder and vitamin A deficiency.

data.projectName: Perissodactyl Fossils from  Miocene Localities of Pakistan.
data.projectDigest: Understanding the evolution is one of the major advancements in the history of mankind and civilization. our mother earth is enriched with the most reasonable source of information about evolution, the fossils. These fossils are present in Siwalik Hills of Pakistan. New Perissodactyl fossils will be recovered from the Miocene localities of Siwalik (Pakistan). These localities are present in Kamlial, Chinji, Nagri, and Dhok pathan Formations with estimated age 18.3–5.3 Ma. To collect ancestral forms of Perissodactyl fossils, special attention will be given to the outcrops of Kamlial and Chinji Formation. The studied specimens will be compared with the relevant samples housed in different Paleontological Museums in Pakistan and other foreign countries. We will also find out reasons that why early Perissodactyl species could not survive with large species and they disappeared around 10 Ma from the Subcontinent. The comparison between Miocene Perissodactyl species of Pakistan with Asian, African and European faunal elements will be helpful to update paleoecology and faunal correlation of the Siwalik species.

data.projectName: Oligodendrocyte regeneration by synergistic efficacy of Honey and Black Seed .
data.projectDigest: Nervous system is the most important system of the body as it coordinates all activities. Oligodendrocytes are the most prevalent non-neural cell type in the central nervous system (CNS). These cells are responsible for myelin synthesis, supply of lactate and iron and maintenance of axonal integrity. Oligodendrocyte loss or dysfunction is therefore associated with several neurodegenerative diseases like multiple sclerosis, Alzheimer’s disease, and schizophrenia etc. Regeneration of oligodendrocytes after demyelination, is one the major therapeutic strategy for the treatment of multiple sclerosis, using either hormones, growth factors and synthetic drugs or different types of stem cells. However, success is either limited or associated with side effects. So, present study will assess the oligodendrocyte regenerative potential of a combination of honey and back seeds. Therapeutic potential will be analyzed in cell culture by isolating and growing oligodendrocyte precursor cells from chick embryo brain. Similarly, demyelination will be induced in 8-10 weeks old chickens using cuprizone to assess the efficacy of honey + black seed combination in animal model. Extracts with positive effects will be further analyzed to isolate and characterize bioactive molecules. Being two most important components of Tibe e Nabawi (SAWW) they are expected to exhibit potential of oligodendrocyte regeneration.

data.projectName: Genome wide association study (GWAS) for fecundity, growth and morphological traits in Beetal goat
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Goat is considered as a “Future Animal” for rural and urban prosperity  due to its greater ability to tolerate hot climatic conditions , better productivity , small size, ability to utilize poor quality roughages , and non-competitiveness with man for food. Fecundity, growth and morphological traits are the major traits of economic importance in goat. With the increasing ever human population, the demand for goat mutton is also increasing day-by-day and subsequently it is out of reach of poor and lower middle-class (majority of population) peoples of Pakistan. Moreover, there is high demand of Beetal for sacrificial purposes on Eid-ul-Adha. The genetic improvement for fecundity, and growth traits in this goat breeds, would result not only in enhancing meat production but also of making farming/production of Beetal goat more profitable. Genome-wide association studies for twining and growth traits had been demonstrated in different breeds of sheep and goat internationally. But there is a no such type of work has been done todate on any small ruminant breed of Pakistan. Therefore, the present study is designed to explore the genetic variations associated in controlling in fecundity, growth and morphological traits in Beetal goat.

data.projectName: Epigenetic signature of Advance Glycation end Products (AGE) and Skin Autofluorescence As a Risk predictor in metabolically healthy and unhealthy obese adults
data.projectDigest: Many obese individuals remain healthy throughout their life span i.e. ‘Metabolically Healthy Obese’ whereas some normal weight individuals develop diabetes i.e. ‘Metabolically Unhealthy Normal Weight’. It is hypothesized that Nesfatin (feeding suppressing) and Desnutrin (lipid breakdown) may also be deranged in these individuals. A preliminary analysis by my group showed that every unit decrease in Desnutrin was associated with a higher odd of developing fatty liver. Advanced glycation end products (AGEs) are formed due to environmental effect i.e. epigenetics and lead to insulin resistance. A novel method of measuring AGE is through skin auto-fluorescence (simple, swift & noninvasive). Mobile health applications offer economical and operational approaches to prevent non-communicable diseases by providing an enabling environment to individuals. Yet, this cost-effective strategy is still not utilized in Pakistan. Therefore, we hypothesize that i) epigenetic changes in benign obesity may lead to accumulation of AGE in subjects independent of symptoms of diabetes and ii) using an intervention such as mobile health application lead to improvement in health outcomes in LIMC setting.  These results can serve as a bench mark for future researchers in developing guidelines to cater for the South Asian gene- lifestyle-diet pattern and use of Artificial intelligence in obesity intervention.

data.projectName: Exploration of the Mechanism of change in Learning behavior of Special Children along with the progression of Inclusive Atmosphere
data.projectDigest: Special children are facing a lot of difficulties in the course of their adjustment in society. These difficulties are multidimensional in nature including their limited abilities and attitude of the community. No doubt, inclusion is one of the solutions to their problem. The enhancement of technology in human society made this phenomenon more complicated. There is a need to understand the process of learning of special children towards the inclusive atmosphere in this advance area. This research project will focus on the understanding of the learning process of special children during the development of the inclusive atmosphere. To make these researches up to international level two international sectoral collaborators have been involved. Dr. Christopher Jolly (Jolly Learning Ltd, UK) will support the research activities in the process of phonics, language and reading development with the help of multisensory and synthetic approaches. Dr. Beverly Moskowitz (Size Matter Handwriting Program) will support the researchers in the motor development patterns for the learning of handwriting development. These researches along with these collaborators will help us to understand the mechanism of learning in special children. That proposed project may be helpful in the development of theory on the new learning behavior of special children.

data.projectName: Optimizing irrigation water and economic return of high yielding maize under changing climate of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Water shortage is very serious concern due to climate change throughout the world especially areas like Pakistan lying in arid to semi-arid regions. Future predicted changes in climate and expected scenarios of elevated temperature and uneven rainfall distributions in Pakistan will challenge the production of high-water demanding crops. The present water application technique to maize crop is a simple and results in low water use efficiency (WUE) with low crop productivity. The current study aims at assessing maize yield response and WUE in four Provinces of Pakistan. The proposed study will be conducted with three different irrigation regimes (100, 75 and 50% field capacity) and five irrigation water saving techniques (plastic film, rice straw, wheat straw, sugarcane bagasse mulch and control (field without any water saving techniques). As the technology required budget and farmers hesitate to adopt new techniques requiring input that increases the cost production and decrease the farm profit. However, these techniques may increase their farm profit by input saving under their limited expenses if manage properly. Therefore, economic and marginal return of farm profit will be analyzed at the end of the study. A two consecutive year experiment of autumn maize will be carried out in all four Provinces of Pakistan with varying climatic condition. The study will be helpful in optimize irrigation technology with maximum grain yield, WUE and economic return under changing climate of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Atmospheric and soil Radon Time Series data  based earthquake Forecasting using machine learning techniques
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest:
In the current project, Radon Time Series (RTS) data will be obtained, while installing RADON station on fault line. Three  state of art instruments, RAD7, RTM 1688-2 and PYLON AB6, which are already available in our laboratory, will be deployed for on field RTS measurements. A weather Station Davis USA Model Cabled Vantage Pro2 plus Cat # 6162C will be installed for continuous monitoring of environmental parameters. RTS and environmental parameters data will be collected extending over the period of one year. 
Computational Intelligence (CI) models and different Machine Learning Techniques (MLTs) viz., Support vector regression (SVR), artificial neural network (ANN) applications etc., will be used to automatically detect anomalous behavior in soil and atmospheric radon (222Rn) gas time series data. Seismic data, for a complete year, will be obtained from Pakistan Meteorological Department, Meteorological Complex, University Road, Karachi-75270. Obtained RTS data will be tested for anomalies using statistical techniques. RTS data will be modelled with corresponding meteorological and statistical parameters using computational intelligence techniques. A method will be developed to distinguish between environmental parameters, noise of instrument initiated anomalies with seismic events based anomalies. Anomalies in RTS data will be further tested against seismic events and a reliable prediction is expected from this whole mechanism.

data.projectName: Effect of Ibandronate Therapy on Apelin, Visfatin, Irisin and Asprosin in Postmenopausal Osteoporotic Females
data.projectDigest:
In post-menopausal women, osteoporosis is a major health problem, characterized by a reduction of bone mineral density (BMD), this decreased in bone mineral density results in increased risk of fractures which may affect the quality of life adversely. One of the most common fracture in this case is hip fracture. Hip fracture is categorized in serious fractures and result in serious morbidity. The health complications of hip fractures are severe. There is loss of function which is usually progressive in nature and the patient is unable to move without support. In Pakistan, the burden of osteoporosis in females is increasing at an alarming rate because of lack of awareness and their financial and physical limitations.
            Bisphosphonates are the agents of choice for osteoporosis treatment. Oral nitrogen-containing bisphosphonates (eg, ibandronate) are the standard of care in osteoporosis. Many studies have shown that bisphosphonates reduce the risk of osteoporosis in postmenopausal females.
It is still unclear that how bisphosphonate helped in osteoporosis. There are many theories however the exact mechanism is unknown. The adipokines such as Apelin, Visfatin, Irisin and Asprosin play an important role in the regulation of food intake, energy expenditure, and body weight. They have been reported to influence the bone development and remodeling. However, it is not clear whether these are stimulators or inhibitors of bone growth. As little is known about their relationship with bone mass, and changes in levels after Bisphosphonate therapy, the present study has been designed to find out the effects of Bisphosphonate therapy (Ibandronate) on serum Apelin, Visfatin, Irisin and Asprosin. This study can established whether these adipokines can be of use in the diagnosis

data.projectName: Spatial distribution, health risk assessment and batch-pilot scale remediation of arsenic by developing bimetallic composites of biosorbents: A cohort study in Ravi-Sutlej interbasin
data.projectDigest: Among the heavy metal(loid)s contamination, arsenic (As) is classified as the most toxic and class I human carcinogen. Recent reports have highlighted As-contaminated drinking water dilemma in Pakistan. Therefore, it is highly imperative to assess As-contamination of surface and groundwater resources, its accumulation in animals/human as well as developing low-cost As removal unit at the local/national level. The present project aims to estimate As-contamination in surface/groundwater resources in ten unexplored districts of rural Punjab receiving water from rivers; Ravi and Sutlej. Surface/groundwater samples (1675), soil/sediments samples (480), animal milk samples (435) and humans’ biological samples (870) will be collected from aforementioned districts based on population/km2. Such detailed knowledge on hydro-geochemical behavior of As concentrations in water and biological samples, their covariance and correlation will greatly assist in assessing As exposure status and associated health hazards. The second aim of the project is to design a novel, cost-effective water remediation technique using almond shells biosorbents, its modification with bismuth (Bi), with zerovalent copper nanoparticles (Cu0), and bismuth coupled copper assisted biosorbents using batch-column scale experiments. The third and the most important objective is to develop an As remediation unit at a pilot scale, that can be used commercially at the local/national scale. Moreover, a questionnaire will be developed to assess the demographic information of respondents, sources of water treatment and sanitation, knowledge about drinking water, and clinical diseases at the district level.

data.projectName: A mathematical study on the dynamics of blood flow through diseased arteries
data.projectDigest: This project is focused to have a thorough insight of the blood flow through a diseased artery. Blood flow will be investigated through different physical realistic configurations. Different constitutive relationships describing various blood models will be considered in the present study. It will include the development of mathematical models through different geometries containing stenosis and catheter and formulations of the governing differential systems for the problems under consideration. Realistic assumptions of flowing blood in the arteries will be incorporated. Suitable solutions methodologies both analytic and approximate, whichever applicable, will be adopted to tackle the governing highly nonlinear differential systems. Analytical study for various varying parameters for the important flow quantities will be given due attention. This project along with its results will help the reader in understanding the rheology of blood through diseased arteries on more realistic grounds. It has its clinical and medical importance for the treatment and cure of several diseases. The outcome of this project will add a nice contribution in the literature. The manpower trained shall be an asset for further research in this area. Mathematical models, different solution methodologies or techniques shall be useful to the new non specialist readers and students in this area. This project will lead to the dissemination of equitable quality education and lifelong learning opportunities for new readers.

data.projectName: Development of sustainable protocol for the production of high performance biodiesel by using novel nano-biocatalysts and nano-additives
data.projectDigest: Alternative fuels are considered to play pivotal role for future energy security, and among these biodiesel is most promising one. It is synthesized mostly by transesterification of feedstock chemically or enzymatically. However, higher operational costs, poor catalytic efficiency, low biodiesel yields, high reaction time/temperature requirements, and difficulty in recovery of by-products etc. are constrains associated with the use of homogeneous acid/alkaline catalysts. Enzyme mediated reactions are comparatively more effective due to their higher catalytic efficiencies, and substrate specificity, but still they are comparatively expensive with low thermal stabilities and could easily be denatured. The best possible way to overcome above said constrains is usage of nano-biocatalysts (enzymes fabricated nano-moieties). This will improve their thermal stabilities and reusability making the process sustainable and economically feasible. Other major constrains associated with direct use of biodiesel in a diesel engine are poor performance characteristics viz., lower engine power, higher brake specific fuel consumption, poor brake thermal efficiency, lower calorific values and higher NOx emissions. The use of nano-moieties as additives can be emphatic option toward optimizing biodiesel performance parameters. Present project is therefore designed with the objective to develop sustainable protocol for the production of high performance biodiesel using novel nano-biocatalysts and nano-additives.

data.projectName: enhancement of Zinc Content in rice varieties cultivated in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Micronutrient malnutrition is a major global concern of human beings affecting almost half of the world's population. Zinc (Zn) deficiency is a major issue of human nutrition worldwide. It is arguably one of the leading micro nutritional restraints to crops as well. It negatively impacts the development and health of plants and crop yield. Cereals serve as the main staple food for a large proportion of the world's population but have low essential trace elements such as Zn in their edible tissues. Rice is one of the most important staple crops providing 20% of global calories. It is an important foreign exchange contributor to the economy of Pakistan. White milled rice grains lose essential nutrients through polishing thereby causing seed-specific higher accumulation of essential nutrients a necessity. Significant increases in Zinc along with other essential minerals could become possible in rice grain through bio fortification. When experiencing low Zn, plants undergo an adaptive response to maintain Zn homeostasis. bZIPs proteins are one of the largest  families of transcription factors widely distributed in  all eukaryotes including plants. They have been implicated to be involved in the regulation of fundamental physiological and developmental processes in plants. An intricate network regulating responses to low Zn in plants has revealed the involvement of bZIPs proteins in Zinc homeostasis. Our current proposal aims to evaluate the role of F-group bZIPs transcription factors in regulating the uptake of Zinc through ZIP transporters in response to Zn deficiency in rice adapting to Zn deficiency. It therefore could represent novel targets for improving nutrient efficiency in crops.

data.projectName: Analysis of genetic and epigenetic modification in miRNA-21 promoter associated with up-regulation of miRNA-21 expression in gliomas
data.projectDigest:
Gliomas constitute 30% of all the brain tumors. It is most common and also aggressive tumor with less than five year survival rate. World Health Organization (WHO) has classified Gliomas into four histopathologic grades i.e. (I-IV) including pilocytic astrocytomas (WHO Grade I), diffuse astrocytomas (WHO Grade II), anaplastic astrocytomas (WHO Grade III), and glioblastoma multiforme (WHO Grade IV), on the basis of rapid cell proliferation, treatment resistance, and abundant angiogenesis. Therefore, it is very important to devise better therapies and establish potential therapeutic targets for different aspects of glioma pathogenesis.
The micro-RNA 21 (miR21) plays an important role in regulation of cellular gene expression, cell cycle, apoptosis, autophagy, DNA repair etc. Its aberrant expression is associated with number of disease conditions. Role of miR21 expression has been extensively studied in gliomas in order to use it as early non-invasive diagnostic marker. In this study, we will investigate the possible role of miR21 promoter (DNA methylation and promoter binding proteins) in its aberrant expression in gliomas. We will also investigate whether DMOG treatment can repress miR21 expression by inducing miR21 promoter methylation, and promote cell death in glioma cell line (HCM-BROD-0003-C71). DMOG (dimethyloxallyl glycine), a known DNA demethylation inhibitor, treatment have shown to promote apoptosis in lymphoma cell line and in multiple cancer types (bladder, ovarian and breast) by initiating promoters hyper-methylation.

data.projectName: Controlled growth and study of the semiconductor materials for photo-voltaic applications
data.projectDigest: Pakistan being a developing country has to look at possibilities to harvest energy from renewable resources such as solar energy to overcome energy crises in the country. Scientists are looking for low-cost high performance materials to enhance efficiency of the solar cell device. This project will focus on the controlled growth and characterization of low-cost high performance semiconductor thin films for solar cell applications. This project mainly divided into two parts: In first part, controlled growth of binary semiconductor compounds such as AB (where A = Mn, Sn, Ge, Pb; B= S, Se) in to thin films will be grown by chemical bath deposition (CBD). CBD is a low-cost chemical synthesis route which allows synthesis of different materials in to thin films. In-the-lines of proposed project , synthesis protocol for the growth of tin monosulfide (SnS) thin films  has already been established in “Thin Film Laboratory” Department of Physics, University of the Punjab, Lahore. Some preliminary results studying the structural and optical properties of SnS has been reported in high-impact Elsevier Journal “Journal of Alloys and Compounds” 759 (2018) 14-21, which evidenced the working of synthesis protocol. Structural, optical and electrical properties of semiconductor films will be studied experimentally to look at the possibilities of film's application as an absorber layer in solar cells. Finally, a prototype solar cell device will be fabricated to study its characteristics. In second part of the project, proposed materials will also be studied by implementing theoretical approach. Theoretical work will be done in collaboration with Dr. Altaf Hussain, Co-PI in this project . Overall, this project will allow to synthesize and study materials suitable for solar cell device.

Structural, optical and electrical properties of semiconductor films will be studied experimentally to look at the possibilities of film's application as an absorber layer in solar cells. Finally, a prototype solar cell device will be fabricated to study its characteristics. In second part of the project, proposed materials will also be studied by implementing theoretical approach. Theoretical work will be done in collaboration with Dr. Altaf Hussain, Co-PI in this project . Overall, this project will allow to synthesize and study materials suitable for solar cell device.

data.projectName: Brain to Mobile wireless Communication in opportunistic ambient adhoc networks
data.projectDigest: In this proposal, the idea of the brain to mobile communication is presented in the first part existing research work has been reviewed. In the second part the problem has been identified with the proposed solution. Its point to point communication in ad-hoc networks will be employed. The source node will send data or signals to the destination node so that a disabled person can communicate or can deliver their message to other people. In existing research, it has been demonstrated that it's possible to turn a person's thoughts into a legible phrase using what they're calling a "brain-to-text" interface. The continuously spoken speech can be decoded into the expressed words from intracranial electrocorticographic signals in human (ECoG) recordings. This involves using needles to record signals directly from a person's neurons; it's an invasive procedure requiring an incision through the skull. To overcome, this invasive process, an ad-hoc network based wireless link with brain of disabled persons who can’t speak or express with hands movement, human mind intensions/thoughts will be translated through ECoG and will be expressed on mobile application. Electrographic signals in humans.

data.projectName: A STUDY OF THE TEACHINGS OF SEMITIC RELIGIONS TO FIND AN EFFECTIVE AND DURABLE NARRATIVE FOR GLOBAL PEACE
data.projectDigest: Religion plays a vital role in creating inner and outer peace and has remained one of the most important factors for harmony and peaceful co-existence. And this cannot be affiliated to a single religion rather one of the most significant preaching of all religions all about acceptance, love and respect for humanity. And there is no room for any sort of compulsion in religious matters. On the other hand history has witnessed many wars fought in the name of religions. It is the followers of a specific religion not the religion itself which comes up with a hate narrative. Encountering such hate narratives with the help of the teachings of any specific religion has not worked so far and has faced a lot of criticism. The counter narrative was perceived as a western product or having some sort of hidden agenda which was considered contradictory to the basic teachings of our religion. This twofold (Islamic Studies and Psychology) research will try to find a counter narrative for global peace with the help of the teachings of Semitic religions i.e. Islam, Christianity and Judaism and Non Semitic Religions i.e. Hinduism, Sikhism and Buddhism. This research will also include a psychological study of human mind in terms of accepting or negating any notion or narrative

data.projectName: Development of Up-flow Column Reactor for Optimization and Stimulation of Microbial Conversion of Coal into Methane
data.projectDigest: The increasing carbon dioxide emissions are forcing the authorities to redesign the energy mix with reduced dependence on carbon-dense fuels. Under these circumstances, natural gas still appears to be one of the viable options, which could survive its position for foreseeable future, because of its low carbon footprint. However, with increasing demands of natural gas, the need of exploitation of unconventional resources is emerging. One of those resources is biogenic coalbed methane, which results from the natural transformation of coal-based organics to methane in sub-surface environment. Biogenic nature of coalbed methane in major coal reserves has been observed in various countries, including USA, Australia, China, Japan and India. Coalbed methane reservoirs have started playing significant role in global unconventional natural gas production. Though, this transformation is based on microbial syntrophic cooperation, but various factors may influence the yield of methane generation from coal. Pakistani low rank coal has also been reported to be susceptible to biogenic methane generation, however, methane generation from local coal needs to be optimized. The present research activity is principally aimed at developing an extended up-flow reactor, which could be used for optimizing the conversion of coal into methane while studying all affecting parameters.

data.projectName: Some generalized results regarding differential inclusions of fuzzy intuitionistic and Pythagorean fuzzy mappings involving fractional boundary value problems
data.projectDigest: In this project, firstly we will present some new generalized results regarding differential inclusions of fuzzy, intuitionistic and Pythagorean fuzzy mappings involving fractional boundary value problems with fractional derivative of Caputo and Febrizio type.  This will extend, mapping types as well as more generalized fractional derivative. Secondly we will find existence results of differential inclusions of fuzzy mappings with the help of selection theorems of Yannelis, Prabhakar and Bohnenblust-Karlin and also by using the technique of Nadler’s fixed point theorem. Thirdly we will utilize our results to prove the existence results for the class of functional inclusions. This research will not only be a good addition in the area of nonlinear analysis but also inspire other mathematicians to contribute further in this field. The collaboration of the researchers from two different universities will also be beneficial for the students in future.

data.projectName: Glaciers Melting and Hidden Risks of Legacy Pollutants  and their Atmospheric Transport to Karakorum Hindukush and Himalayas, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Persistent organic pollutants (POPs) and poly cyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are environmental xenobiotics groups that are persistent, bio-accumulative and bio-magnified in environment with potential of long-range atmospheric transport (LRAT) to cold regions. In Pakistan, applications of advanced technologies in industrial and agriculture sectors without proper management release toxic pollutants to environment. In the past, organochlorine pesticides (OCPs) were used abundantly because of cost effectiveness and their easily availability but later on, due to persistence and toxic nature, they were banned in Stockholm Convention globally. The present project is focusing on PAHs and POPs whether the residues and isomers are still exist in our environment or not? The study will identify the PAHs and POPs pathways through LRAT and stores in cold regions and during glacier’s melting cascade through downstream ecosystems. Moreover, this study will assess the adverse health effects of POPs and PAHs specially on pregnant’s women and their placental transfer to neonates. This study will be useful for practitioners and policy makers to address and establish regular monitoring, valuation and reporting measures with proper environmentally friendly policies, laws and guidelines in order to reduce PAHs and POPs exposure in different environmental compartments and its implication for regional cycling.

data.projectName: The role of Nitric Oxide in Insect Biology
data.projectDigest: From research over the last few decades, Nitric Oxide has gone from being a noxious poison to one of the most fascinating cellular messenger molecules and is now widely known as a membrane-permeable signalling molecule in different species across the different kingdoms of life including microbes, plants and animals including mammals and insects. In plants and animals it regulates the development of several development features throughout life and is a key component of the innate immunity. NO regulates several key physiological process at the transcriptome level, relatively upstream as well as at the proteome level via the famous post-translational modifications know as S-Nitrosylation and Tyrosine-Nitration. However, very little is known about the role of NO in insect biology. We intend to investigate the role of NO in the insect biology via transcriptomics and functional genomics studies and intend to elucidate the conserved and divergent/unique functions of NO in insects.

data.projectName: Monitoring Underground Water Leakage Pattern by Using Non-Destructive High-Resolution Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) Measurements
data.projectDigest:
Loss of water due to leakage from buried pipes is a serious concern for water distribution authorities due to environmental, water audit, sustainability and potentially an issue related to health as well as safety. In metropolitan cities water leakages in pipes can damage foundation of roads and other manmade structures.  Different methods are used for water leakage monitoring. The proposed study presented here is focused on detection and monitoring of water leakage patterns using non-invasive geophysical method like ground penetrating radar (GPR) in a controlled environment of laboratory and in field. Water leakage in metallic and PVC pipes of different diameter will be buried in a sand box. Experiments will be conducted in a controlled water injection at fixed position in the pipes and time-lapse GPR measurements will be performed to monitor leakage patterns in different pipes. To validate the results, GPR survey will be performed with in Peshawar city on known as well as suspected sites to identify and locate the leak points to assist in the management of a network of water distribution
The proposed technique should allow to significantly improve water leakage detection, in terms of speed and efficiency as compared to other existing techniques, and therefore to decrease the percentage of leaks in distribution networks. According to Water & Sanitation Services of Peshawar (WSSP), water leakage in buried pipes account for more than 35% of the drinking water produced in Peshawar and therefore have economic and environmental impact. For example, 1% reduction in the rate of leak equals to 157,500 liters of water, which can be utilized by end user of WSSP. Thus, the proposed research aims at addressing the serious issue of water leaks affecting  common citizen.

data.projectName: Eradicating Energy Poverty & Enhancing Social Structure Through Micro-Hydropower Projects in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Title: Eradicating Energy Poverty & Enhancing Social Structure Through Micro-Hydropower Projects in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan

The increasing trend of energy demand calls for innovative and clean energy solutions. The small hydropower project remains as the readily available option which is cheap, and time effective and cost-efficient. The energy scarcity has propelled Pakistan to explore the full potential of her untapped hydropower in water-rich areas of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) province. It had been planned to install 1,000 micro-hydropower plants aiming to ensure sustained energy provision for localised economic activities through livelihood diversification and thereupon enhancement of social structure. The whole ideas was laid-upon active involvement the stakeholders This research study will be based on primary data collection through questionnaires and focus group discussions from the beneficiaries of the 16 micro-hydropower projects installed in two districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province namely; Battagram and Mansehra in Hazara Division. This study will gauge the effectivity of the bottom-up approach adapted for community oriented and community based managements framework for MHPPs and thereupon the findings of this research will help concerned stakeholders (government and ngos) to timely adjust the running project and plan the future project accordingly. The study results will also help to check the intended and actual benefits and impacts of micro-hydro power plants (MHPPs) on economic conditions through the prevalence of energy poverty at the household level. Furthermore, the envisioned and real spillover impacts on the standard of living, access to- and affordability of social-services through cheap and clean energy provision will also be studied.

data.projectName: Metal-doped MFe2O4 (M = Co, Mn, Ni, Cu, Zn)-based Nanostructures and their Applications towards the Sensing of Biological Molecules
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: Electrochemical sensors are being exploited for a myriad of applications ranging from the health monitoring to the environmental remediation. They afford the sensing of chemical/biological species to monitor the type, concentration, and level of species in the environment or the biological samples. In health monitoring, electrochemical sensors have been designed for the sensing of different types of molecules. Enzyme-immobilized sensors possess high selectivity and sensitivity than that of the non-enzymatic biosensors; however, the high cost and lengthy enzyme-immobilization procedures impede the wide spread utilization of enzyme-based sensors. Consequently, the development of cost-effective and efficient non-enzymatic sensors is in progress. Whereas, different types of materials including nobel metals, transition metal oxides, carbon-based materials as well as their composites have been explored for the fabrication of electrochemical sensors, mixed transition metal oxides including spinel-type ferrites may possess higher electrical, optical, magnetic, and electro-catalytic properties as compared to single oxide materials. The aim of this project is therefore to develop metal-doped spinel-type MFe2O4 (M = Co, Mn, Ni, Cu, Zn)-based nanostructures and to evaluate their potential as sensors for biologically-important molecules such as, glucose, hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), neurotransmitters, and drug/toxin which could be helpful for the disease diagnostics and real time/continuous health monitoring.

data.projectName: An integrated approach to appraise population dynamics, demography and endurance of mudskippers (Pisces: Gobiidae) with reference to the emerging climate change
data.projectDigest:
Over 1700 known species of the family Gobiidae has prominence it as the largest and an obscure fish family in the world. Among them mudskippers (amphibious fishes) possess unique characters that enable them to breathe in aquatic and terrestrial environments. They exhibit an interesting fashion by forming network of outlets in mudflats for feeding, mating, hibernation and spawning purposes. Moreover, outlets created by mudskippers provides locale to larvae of various shrimps and fish species during high tides. Over thirty species of the gobies documented by Hoda from (1980?1991) in Pakistan lacking taxonomic descriptions, images and inapt nomenclature in line with international fish sciences. In addition, Global Climate Risk Index ranked Pakistan 5th and foresees more losses due to inconsistent weather changes. These catastrophes would not solely impact nation’s economy but would also bang terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems. Nevertheless, managing aquatic biodiversity is obligatory because Pakistan is signatory of various international biological diversity conventions. 
Despite enormous ecological significance, there is no reliable information on population dynamics, demography and climatic influence on gobies available in Pakistan. This study encompasses (I) to establish species inventory on taxonomy and molecular markers (II) figure out role in coastal fisheries development (II) understand extreme weather impacts on survival, reproductive potential and behaviour (III) identify sensory (skin and olfactory) cell structure using histological & SEM images to understand cellular structure that enable gobies to maintain temperature, encounter climate influence and pollution (IV) evaluate aphrodisiac values of some species to comprehend traditional medicinal use.

data.projectDigest:
Differential equations (Des) have an influential part in the main disciplines of sciences such as Physics, Chemistry and Engineering etc. It is basic foundation for convenient understanding of various prestigious physical phenomena and processes which exist in nature. The formulation of generalized DE for applicable area of any branch reduces in particular form for specific problem of that discipline. On solving that reduced, particular differential equation (PDE) we acquire a fruitful solution in the form of functions, which gives the complete illustration of process as well as phenomena being under investigation. 
Solution of DEs elaborates insight of physical processes some of them are interaction of molecules and atoms, flow properties in fluid dynamics and structure forces. data.projectName: Fabrication of semiconductor Metal Oxide Based Gas Sensors for Safety Applications in Domestic Sector
data.piUniversity: Balochistan University of Information Technology, Engineering and Management Sciences,Quetta
data.projectDigest: Gas leakage is a major domestic and industrial problem worldwide. Natural gas mainly consists of methane is widely used as fuel for heating and cooking purpose in domestic sector. The CH4 is highly explosive and can become deadly when it exceeds from it permissible exposure limit. In unventilated areas a small amount of leaked gas concentration could result in precious loss of lives. Baluchistan is largest province of Pakistan and some of its areas i.e. Quetta and Ziarat, face extreme weather condition (-10 °C) during winter season resulting in an increased gas utilization for heating purpose throughout the season. Moreover, this region is rich in mineral resources and many mining sites are available which needs a high quality controlled safe working environment. Due to lack of the safety precautions subjected to unavailability of efficient gas detection sensors and unawareness, many precious lives lost in Balochistan during last year. Therefore, this research aims to develop metal oxide nanoparticles based highly sensitive and economical gas leakage sensor in general but particular for residents of Balochistan. Zinc Oxide (ZnO) nanoparticles offers a flexible nature in terms of various morphologies making it suitable semiconductor for sensor development. Synthesized ZnO based material for sensor will be characterized by Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD) and sensor will be fabricated using as synthesized particles.

data.projectName: Financial Inclusion: Gap and Elucidation
data.projectDigest:
In Recent research financial inclusion, i.e., individuals and businesses have access to useful and affordable financial products and services that meet their needs i.e. transactions, payments, savings, credit and insurance delivered in a responsible and sustainable way, is directly linked to poverty reduction and welfare of people. Technology based financial services, especially ‘mobile money’ services, have made it possible to extend services to clients who are not cost-effective to be reached by formal and traditional financial services providers such as banks. 
In Pakistan, despite number of different initiatives by State Bank of Pakistan and different Govt. agencies, only 14% of adults, who have formally opened their account with financial institutions, are financially included (Financial Inclusion Insights, 2017). This is substantially lower than the South Asia average where 30% of adults are financially included and 41.4% of all lower-middle income countries.  According to Financial Inclusion Insights (2014), about 56% of adult population don’t use formal or informal financial products, whereas 36% of adults reported saving and among them only 4% save with formal financial institutions.
The primary objective of this study is to understand the reason behind low level of financial inclusion. It is done by investigating the role of mobile banking services, such Easypaisa, in financial inclusions, and to understand customer perception about the services of mobile banking. Both quantitative and qualitative data collection tools will be used. For qualitative data, a survey questionnaire will be conducted from the target participants. For qualitative data, we will employ case study method. Focus group interviews will be used as a data collection method.

data.projectName: Ecological Therapy via Non-Thermal Plasma -a novel solution for CO2 conversion
data.projectDigest:
Carbon dioxide CO_2 is highly stable heat-trapping gas which contributes to greenhouse effect. Its excess amount in atmosphere causes global warming. Several approaches are developed for dissociation of CO_2 e.g., carbon capture and utilization, thermal and catalytic. The scope of these  techniques is limited due to high cost and environmental consequences. 
Non-thermal plasma is recently developing technology using for degradation of CO_2 due to less time consumption, low energy cost, and exceptional ability to initiate chemical reactions at low temperature. Plasma Assisted Catalytic technology (PACT) is worth mentioning because  it exploits simultaneously catalytic effects of dielectric materials, for  CO_2  dissociation,  and plasma. In this fashion, joint venture of plasma and catalyst “synergy effect” provides distinct opportunity to convert dissociated  CO_2 into useful bi products e.g., CO,O, CH_4, ethanol, methanol etc.
In this proposed project, dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) and microwave (MW) system will be (developed locally) used to dissociate CO_2 into useful bi products by exploiting synergy effect. For this, MW and DBD system will be optimized as function of discharge parameters like gases concentration, applied power and flow rates. Finally, the developed DBD and MW system will be scaled up for commercialization especially for bricks factories of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Synthesis of metallic nanoparticles and characterization techniques for surface analysis and deposition over various surfaces for optoelectronics, photonics, sensors and medical applications.
data.projectDigest: This project will allow us to develop metallic nano-particles in various shapes and sizes.  These nano-particles produced electron vibrations when visible light fall on it. These vibrations of electrons by visible light can produce electric and magnetic effects. Such electrons (negatively charged particles) vibrations in a single nano-particle absorb light and produce electricity. If many of such nano-particles are placed side-by-side with each other than this effect will add up.  Such enhancement in electromagnetic response can be employed in many relevant applications such as photonics, sensors, and medical applications. For instant, gold nano-rod can increase temperature up-to 70 degree centigrade in its surrounding when exposed to light. This increase in temperature can be used to destroy cancer cells. There are many other applications such nanoparticles can be used in cosmetics owing to their deep penetration in skin and easily delivers nutrients to skin layers. For example, Ponds face creams use ultrafine Zinc Oxide and Titanium dioxide for that purpose.

data.projectName: Working Young People on the Streets: From Exclusion to Inclusionni Society
data.projectDigest:
Social exclusion of marginalized and vulnerable groups make them a non-productive part of the society in this globalized world, where they can be productive, if a chance is given to them. It is argued in the literature that marginalized groups such as street children and youth and working young people on the streets are usually stigmatized as ‘vagrants’ and with ‘deviant’ behavior. The current scenario of Pakistan as far as street children and working young people is concerned does not depict an optimistic view. Working young people on the streets are not the priority of the federal government (as far as law making is concerned) and district government does not show concerns for them as well. Considering this situation, this project aims to explore the issues and problems of working young people in Rawalpindi city and nearby tehsils. The researchers will explore the possibilities to take some initiatives by working closely with government officials, non-governmental organizations working in the project areas and other stakeholders. In this project, it is anticipated that working young people will be integrated into the society socially, economically and politically. This project will give them a chance to work and negotiate with the district government and other stakeholders to explore the avenues to contribute to the society in a positive way. This project will help them to be responsible citizens of Pakistan. 

In this project, Riphah International University’s ORIC office is working as Academic Collaborator. Through this collaboration, a faculty member will work as Co-PI.

It is also envisaged that TEVTA (Technical and Vocational Training Authority) will be the sectoral partner in this project.

data.projectName: Securing the next-generation wireless networks by extracting features from the physical layer
data.projectDigest: Wireless medium is a broadcast medium; therefore, wireless communication systems are inherently prone to various active attacks (e.g., jamming, impersonation etc.) and passive attacks (e.g., eavesdropping) by the adversaries nearby. This project is first of its kind to investigate a wide range of security threats to upcoming next generation cellular and WiFi networks in order to provide efficient countermeasures at the physical layer. Specifically, there are numerous kinds of possible attacks, e.g., jamming, impersonation, eavesdropping, denial-of-service attack, man-in-the-middle attack, and Sybil attack. Nevertheless, this project will focus on impersonation attack only and propose efficient authentication algorithms to counter it, for various use case scenarios under 6G landscape, e.g., intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS)-aided communication, internet of nano-things (IoNT) leveraging communication in terahertz band and bio-inspired communication via diffusion of molecules, machine-to-machine communication for industrial/factory automation, backscatter communication, communication in millimeter wave band etc. For each of the considered 6G scenarios, we will design novel algorithms for user authentication and shared secret key generation by extracting unique (transmitter-specific) features at the physical layer, and validate them by prototyping on software-defined radios. Finally, we will also provide insights into theoretical performance limits of 6G systems operating under hostile/non-friendly conditions by computing metrics such as secrecy capacity, equivocation rate etc.

data.projectName: Exploring effects of different feed supplements on economic traits and morphology of ostrich skin for improvement in leather products
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Worldwide, the luxurious and attractive high-grade leather products and fashion-wear such as leather handbag, purses and wallets, shoes, jackets, belts, briefcases, key rings and other commercial commodities are widely manufactured from ostrich skin. Ostrich farming is emerging as entrepreneurship in Pakistan to apprehend the huge profit in the local and international markets. Therefore, to compete in international ostrich market, higher production and better product quality are characteristics features that need to be upgraded with the purpose to become economically viable. Hence, it is imperative to supplement the growing ostrich with appropriate substances such as Boron, vitamin-E selenium; secoisolariciresinol diglucoside; flaxseed extract; aloe Vera etc. to boosts the quality of skin to sustain profitability in ostrich farming enterprise. A prototype will be developed, feasibility will be tested, and finally the results will be discussed and passed to ostrich farmers. The technology is very simple and easy to adopt. There is great possibility of the commercialization of the investigated factors. These will greatly help the poor ostrich farmer to sale out the skin of slaughtered ostrich with high prices. This will not only encourage ostrich farmers to expand their business but also provide high quality luxurious leather to Pakistan leather industry.

data.projectName: Potential of psychrophilic plant growth promoting rhizobacteria in sustainable production of cereal crops
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Benazir Bhutto University, Sheringal, Dir
data.projectDigest:
Human development, at local famers’ scale to the global production is only possible through agricultural sustainability. Recently, integrated approach involving chemical, organic and biofertilizers has been proved a sustainable strategy in order to feed rapidly growing population of the world. The bacteria that are found in close relation with plant roots are known as rhizobacteria. The rhizobacteria having the ability to enhance growth and productivity of crop plants directly or indirectly through various mechanisms are known as plant growth promoting rhizobacteria (PRPR). For sustainable agriculture, application of PGPR has been proved preferable to their counterparts in the form of chemical fertilizers. 
In Pakistan, there are limited reports regarding the impact of PGPR in enhancing crop growth and productivity under mountainous agroecosystem. Moreover, the northern parts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa have been unexplored regarding the isolation, screening and characterization of PGPR and their potential to enhance growth and productivity of crops especially cereal crops. Based on this hypothesis, the present research project will be conducted to isolate, screen and characterize PGPR and their potential to enhance growth and productivity of cereal under laboratory, pot and field conditions. Moreover, potentially effective PGPR will be used to formulate biofertilizer for a commercial product.

data.projectName: Isolation, characterization and mechanism of action studies of natural products from Berberis lyceum against Alzheimer's disease
data.projectDigest: Products of natural origin have been a very productive source of lead compounds for the development of new medicines. Berberis lyceum, is an indigenous plant of Pakistan having many therapeutic potentials and is also being used against various diseases by local practitioners since centuries. B. lyceum preparations has been used against sore and swollen eyes, wounds, broken bones, curative piles, gonorrhoea, acute conjunctive, unhealthy ulcers and in chronic ophthalmia. Considering the neuropsychiatric importance of Berberis lycium, the scientific hypothesis is that: Is this medical plant and the bioactive compounds especially alkaloids found in the crude extracts of fruit, stem and roots are effective for the treatment of Alzheimer? Therefore, in the present study, we intend to investigate the anti-Alzheimer’s potential effect of the extract of B. lyceum through evaluation of acetylcholinesterase activity, protection effect against aluminium chloride induce neurotoxicity, and the identification of the main constituents. Enzyme activity-based fractionation, purification and characterization processes will be used to isolate the anti-Alzheimer active compounds from B. lyceum by using different chromatographic techniques. The isolated compounds will be identified by analyzing spectral data (UV, NMR and MS). The identified compounds will be evaluated for anti-Alzheimer’s potential by different behavioural assays. Finally, to determine the mechanism of action of these compounds the Western Blotting studies will be carried out on the protein extracted from rat tissues. In conclusion, based on ethnopharmacological study, we believe that the compounds isolated from Berberis lyceum will have positive effect for the management of Alzheimer’s disease.

data.projectName: Combined in vitro and in silico approaches for investigation of protein modifications as potential biomarkers in breast cancer
data.piUniversity: Lahore College for Women University, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Breast cancer is turning into a worldwide epidemic, with highest frequency in the developed world. Breast cancer is caused by genetic changes triggering aberrant expression of protein or malfunctioning protein leading to oncogenic events. Though several research on potential markers of breast cancer in the blood, including proteins made by oncogenes, developing tests to detect tumor cells in blood, have been conducted, none of these are sensitive enough to be useful as diagnostic breast cancer markers. In this study small chemical modifications such as phosphorylation, glycosylation and acetylation will be investigated to determine their role in the early and late stage breast cancer. Two different breast cancer cell lines will be utilized for this work. The early stage (MCF-7) and late metastic stage (MDA) breast cancer cell lines will be provided by Prof. Dr. Daniel C. Hoessli from University of Geneva, Geneva. Protein will be extracted and their specific modification status will be determined by immunoprecipitation and western-blotting. Furthermore, bioinformatics tools will be used for docking of these small chemical modifications with proteins, which will be helpful to determine which modification can serve as a potential marker for early and/or late stage breast cancer.

data.projectName: Development of Highly potent herbal based product  for the management of diabetic diseases and its related complications in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Federal Urdu University of Arts, Sciences & Technology
data.projectDigest: Diabetes spread all over the world including Pakistan due to unhealthy life routine, in particular type-2 diabetes. The lack of education amongst diabetic people towards diabetes is also one of the major reasons of high rate in Pakistan. The development of diabetic complications, such as coronary heart disease, cancer, obesity, hypertension etc is directly related to the diet intake and the time duration of diabetes. The High saturated fats exist as lipoproteins in the form of LDL-c, HDL-c, and very low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (VLDL-c) also responsible for diabetic complications. At present available therapies include insulin sulfonylureas, biguanides, ?-glucosidase inhibitors, glinides and glyburide. In developing countries due to the potential side effects of most anti-diabetic drugs there is growing interest in herbal remedies is seen. Natural herbs contain bioactive compounds that fight against various diseases without producing adverse effects and are comparably cost effective than synthetic formulations. Centratherum anthelminticum is a magnificent plant found richly in Pakistan. It possesses biologically active compounds in its various parts like seeds leaves and fruits that can resist the metabolic abnormalities in the diabetes and would be a potential future remedy. Focusing herbal medicines (obtained from plants) in the management of diabetes is the main objective of current study in order  to find out potential hypoglycaemic agents in Pakistan origin Centratherum anthelminticum seeds, their extraction will be done to obtain their active and inhibitory components (Spectrophotometry) for the development of effectual, cost effective and safer novel treatment of hyperglycemia and its associated complications.

data.projectName: Nutrient management for oilseed crops (canola and sunflower) in salt-affected soils
data.projectDigest:
Effective nutrients management involves the appropriate rate, time and method of application as well as selection of suitable nutrient material.  Although information regarding the response of varieties/crops to fertilizer nutrient under salt-affected soils conditions is available, but it is limited in case of oil-seed crops especially canola and sunflower. Therefore, further information is urgently needed to utilize the salt-affected land and to increase the crop yield to fulfill oil requirement of ever growing population of the world.
The results of present research will provide useful information to utilize the salt-affected wasteland for oil-seed production plants through proper, suitable and accurate amendments of macro- and micro-nutrients and will bring socio-economic gains. The present research project is proposed with following aims and objectives:

i)	To generate information about the agronomic as well as nutrient use efficiency of various macro/micro nutrient fertilizers (e.g. NPK and micro-nutrient elements) for enhancing yield of two oil-seed crops on salt-affected soils. 
ii)	To identify environment friendly new fertilizer products. 
iii)	Identification/evaluation of organic manures for increasing oil-seed crop yield on salt-affected soils and their amelioration  
iv)	To formulate proper macro and micro-nutrient management practices using different macro-nutrient fertilizers in combination with other micro-nutrients to enhance oil seed crop production on soils with high sodium (Na).

data.projectName: Soft Computing Paradigms and their Ensemble Applications
data.piUniversity: Kohat University of Science and Technology, Kohat
data.projectDigest: Energy is the most important resource and its demand is growing day by day. Due to negligence, a lot of Energy is being wasted annually which can be saved for the future generations. The scientists and researchers are trying to minimize the consumption of energy by applying different  Soft Computing  Paradigms. Most of these optimization algorithms are based on manual formulation of objective function which  are  not suitable for the complex problems, where they fail to provide the desired accuracy. The training  data sets  play an important role in the success of optimization algorithms accuracy. The larger data improves accuracy as compared to  incomplete data. Ensemble soft computing  methodologies  can discover objective function by using  limited available data  and  can play key role in the improvement of optimization algorithms accuracy. Very few algorithms have focused on the maximization of user comfort. We  will propose  hybrid methods for the energy consumption optimization, and prediction, without considering the user comfort index. A very few have considered the comfort index in their studies. The consideration of user comfort index is as important as optimization of energy consumption. If we achieve maximum optimization of energy but the user comfort index has not been achieved that method will be useless for the resident of house. The demand of every user is different like a person feels too much coldness on 24 degrees, but the other user of the house feels comfortable with 24 degrees. So, the target of this study is to satisfy every resident of the house by selecting best range of the comfort parameters and considering the minimum possible energy consumption.In this project, hybrid optimization techniques will develop to solve energy consumption problem.

data.projectName: Modeling and Simulation of Low temperature plasma for medical, environmental and material processing
data.projectDigest:
Plasma consists of ions, neutrals and excited species. It is considered as the fourth state of matter, next to solid, liquid and gaseous state. It exists in nature and can also be generated in laboratories. Laboratory plasma is further classified as high temperature plasma and low temperature plasma also called gas discharge plasma. Low temperature plasma can be generated by applying electric fields, magnetic fields and or heat to a gas. It consists of gas molecules, but also many reactive species, like electrons, various types of ions, radicals and excited species. This highly reactive chemical cocktail makes plasma interesting for many industrial applications. We are studying the underlying mechanisms in plasma, including the plasma chemistry, plasma reactor design and plasma?surface interactions, by means of computer simulations using different plasma models, to improve the following applications: 
i.	Material science:  (for nanotechnology and microchip fabrication),
ii.	Environmental/ energy applications 
iii.	Biomedical applications (i.e. Medicine, mainly cancer research).

data.projectName: Polydactyly as potential forensic phenotypic attribute.
data.projectDigest:
Forensic science is the association of different disciplines of science and law. Forensic DNA typing has the ability to identify the individual especially in the cases where no eyewitness is available. There are many forensically important markers: mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), autosomal STRs, Y-STRs, SNPs, ancestry informative markers (AIMs) and Forensic DNA phenotyping (FDP) markers.
“Traditional” forensic DNA usually uses STR markers for identification of an individual on the basis of DNA that says nothing about the personal characteristics of that individual. STRs are present in non-coding region of DNA and therefore, do not provide information about person’s personal trait. FDP is a newly developing technology based on probabilistic identification of a person’s phenotype from DNA. FDP markers, in contrast to STRs, objects to analyze and purposely find out an unknown person’s phenotype. 
Polydactyly, is a genetics related phenotypic characters. Polydactyly is condition in which a child has additional fingers or toes. It is quite common. One in 1,339 newborns among the Caucasian race has polydactyly. The prevalence of polydactyly is one in 1,339 live births among the Caucasian race, 
Hence, the current project proposes to establish an FDP of polydactyly covering random population of Pakistan, for forensic casework and medical diagnostics use. The aim of this project is to support criminal investigative agencies by identifying unknown criminals, or to aid the cases of non-criminal missing individuals.
