data.projectName: Proximity Services for Ultra Reliable Low Latency Communication in 5G New Radio  based Cellular Networks
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: 5G New Radio (NR) has been established as the global standard for the Air Interface of 5G cellular networks and considering the expected launch of 5G services in near future, it is important to develop techniques for enabling various applications expected to be deployed in 5G networks using NR and gauge their performance. One such application involves providing proximity services to users and devices for various high capacity, reliability and time critical applications. In this project, we intend to extend the flexible testbed for D2D communication (NRPU-6054, 2016) and develop and investigate techniques for enabling proximity services using 5G NR as the air interface. The major use cases of 5G NR include enhanced mobile broadband, ultra-reliable low latency communication (URLLC) and massive machine type communication. Each type require different and often contradicting demands on the radio interface, necessitating trade-off in the design process. 5G NR is capable of acquiring this high degree of freedom, unlike 4G LTE air interface. In this project, we will be developing and investigating techniques for URLLC, enabling time and mission critical applications like tele-medicine, disaster management and vehicular communication (V2X). This project is expected to open new paradigms of research on 5G Air interface and address deployment of various proximity services in practical scenarios.

data.projectName: Software Defined Network Connectivity in Wireless Edge Network
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Today IoT devices have increased the use of Wireless Networks [1] and interference from different wireless sources is common in working environment. The multitude of interconnected devices includes smart vehicles (e.g. unmanned aerial vehicles and autonomous cars), smart fridges, and intelligent home assistant devices.  
Working of SDN controller in edge network is ongoing research to make IOT devices process faster than ever before. We will observe the impact of multiple wireless signals on open flow messages of SDN controller. Using virtualization would enable us to see different perspective of wireless domain which may lead us provide to reliable solution of Wi-Fi. To handle wireless interference, efforts are being made, such include spectrum analysis tools that are now being integrated into access points to assist IT staff visualize and determine Wi-Fi interference. Similarly before wireless deployment, corporate business conduct wireless surveys so that they avoid wireless interference in the environment.  However, these efforts are undone when a new wireless device activates. As mentioned earlier, we cannot control the usage of Wi-Fi frequency. Therefore all the efforts that were made before deployment or during operation can be easily undone with introduction of new wireless domain or signals.
The proposed research will attempt to achieve the following goals: 
• To observe and study the performance of Wireless network with SDN controller on the extreme of network. 
• Observing the impact of wireless interference on SDN controller open flow message transmission 
• Provide feasibility of SDN controller placement with acquired results.

data.projectName: Energy and Bandwidth Efficient synchronous OFDM based Next Generation Passive Optical Network for Sustainable Green Communication
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The increasing bandwidth demand of ICT networks has led to the evolution of Access network from Copper to Optical Access Network. In Optical Access network the evolution started from Fiber to the Area / Building/ Curb (FTTA/B/C) to Fiber to the Home (FTTH). GPON is the most popular FTTH  technology being widely deployed across the globe.  To cope up with increasing bandwidth demands in future, the GPON has evolved further to XGPON and now to TWDM PON. The TWDM PON has the problem that it uses WDM technology and requires wavelength tuning which increases its cost and makes hardware complex. To overcome these problems, OFDM PON has been reported in literature to be more suitable candidate for next generation PON technology. This research will focus on the medium access layer issues of OFDM PON such as dynamic carrier assignment and energy efficiency of the end user equipment.

data.projectName: Disease management in leguminous plants  through bio-control agents  and their screening via  FLIR (Forward Looking Thermal Sensing) and Florescence techniques.
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan urbanization and population are the main contributors that create hindrance in achieving substantial yield of economically important crop like chick pea. Research on scientific and innovative agricultural techniques for sustainable agriculture is the only hope to execute the increasing food demand and also maintain the soil fertility in agricultural land.  It was evident from the literature that the use of soil micro-organisms like fungus and bacteria for the disease management’s practices could be a better choice to improve the agricultural production and also maintain soil conditioning.Basic cum applied physiological evaluation techniques of plant functioning against the use of bio control agents in disease management would provide valuable insights. In this regards non-invasive phenotyping approaches such as FLIR thermography (Forward looking thermal sensing) and chlorophyll fluorescence could be a useful tool to provide rapid and non destructive evaluation of plant in disease management assessment.   Phenotyping through FLIR is an accurate, quantifiable, non-contact diagnostic technique also used to visualize and quantify changes in leaf surface temperatures is often regulated by several biotic (disease) and abiotic factor.  In Pakistan, the legumes (chick pea, peas and bean) are mostly affected by fungi, bacteria, viruses and nematodes causes upto 44% lost depending on crop varieties. In this regards government has to bear a heavy cost of foreign exchanges against import of large quantities of legumes.    Therefore present study justifies the need to evaluate disease management in legumes using biocontrol agents and their assessment with modern tool like FLIR.

data.projectName: A Proposed Study on the Practice of Mortality Beliefs and Risk Management in Retirement Financial Planning
data.projectDigest: Mortality risk has a very crucial impact on future financial planning and our most of the planning depends on the risk situation as well. Although death is a universal reality but still no one want to image his/her own mortality or passes through the pain of grief.  Death related thoughts causes tension and induces the people to make a proper financial plan that can help them to lessen the grief of loved ones left behind. Prior studies supported that the acceptance to mortality can reduce the fear of death. But still researchers emphasized the need to in depth understand the concept of mortality beliefs and its influence on saving-investment decisions of individuals. As the individual mortality risk perception, their coping up strategies and support mechanism varies according to different age groups so there is a need to explore its role in future planning. Therefore, the aim of the project is to identify the mortality risk factors among different age groups, their perception towards it and their behavior in financial planning in risk situations.

data.projectDigest: Pain is defined as extremely unpleasant physical sensation caused by illness or injury. Pain is the common symptom of any disease or ailment at early stage. It is the sign of defensive, protective mechanism of body in harmful situation. It is subjective receptive and emotional experience . Analgesics are drugs specially designed to relieve pain. Analgesics are for everyone to get rid of pain due to surgery, broken bones, arthritis and even for any other type of pain in body. Analgesics range from Acetoaminophen which is available without prescription to opioids which prescribed only in highly chronic pains. There are many classes of analgesic like, NSAIDS, Opioids, Cannabis, Alcohols and many more. The choice of analgesic based on the type of pain in body i.e NSAIDs are usually given in mild pain whereas orphenadrine id being used for muscular pain. Similarly, phloroglucinol used for abdominal pain and pregabalin is used to treat pain associated with neuropathy. Extensive use of analgesics reduces the efficacy of existing drugs. Hence new drugs are needed to be discovered. The present study is designed to synthesis new derivatives of existing analgesics for potent and less toxic medicines.

data.projectName: Energy Crisis and its only Solution Organic Photovoltaic Materials
data.projectDigest:
This project is related to designation and theoretically investigation of organic solar cells materials for photovoltaic devices. Globally, conventional sources of energy such as coal, gas and fossil fuels are not eco-friendly due to the production of gases which are harmful for our environment. On the other hand, solar energy is the best alternative to fulfill energy short fall on earth. Moreover, silicon based solar cells are replaced by organic solar cells (OSCs) due to their remarkable properties i.e. cheap, flexibility and light weight. So far, the power conversion efficiency (PCE) values obtained through small molecular based OSCs are less than polymer based OSCs. 
Therefore, in this project we aim to design a series of acceptor-donor-acceptor-donor-acceptor (A-D-A-D-A) topology based small molecules for OSCs applications. DFT and TD-DFT analysis will be performed to study electronic and optical properties. Reorganization calculation will be performed to study charge transfer phenomena.  All these calculation will be run by Gaussian 16 package. After ground and excited state properties detailed analysis, we will testify one of best molecule as standard for crystal state calculations to find mobility using Material Studio software for practical applications. In order to predict for experimental findings, power conversion (PCE) will be calculated by matching these designed donors with one of typically used Acceptor material for OSCs. It is expected that we are going to achieve highest PCE among currently designed small donor materials for OSCs. It will helpful for fabrication scientists to fabricate the cost and efficiency effective materials for OSCs.

After ground and excited state properties detailed analysis, we will testify one of best molecule as standard for crystal state calculations to find mobility using Material Studio software for practical applications. In order to predict for experimental findings, power conversion (PCE) will be calculated by matching these designed donors with one of typically used Acceptor material for OSCs. It is expected that we are going to achieve highest PCE among currently designed small donor materials for OSCs. It will helpful for fabrication scientists to fabricate the cost and efficiency effective materials for OSCs.

data.projectName: Estimation and simulation of the current and future land use land cover changes and their impact of land surface temperature in context of urban warming trends in northern Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The rapid urban growth has negative impact on land use by replacing vegetation with built-up areas resulting in an increase in the land surface temperature (LST). This increase in LST leads the formation of Urban Heat Island (UHI) in the major cities. The main purpose of the proposed project is to assess the Land Use Land Cover (LULC) changes due to urban growth in KP (Khyber Pakhtunkhwa) province of Pakistan and their impact on LST trends. This study will be based on data from satellite remote sensing (1990-2019) and field observations. LULC will be estimated from multi-temporal satellite imagery after validation with ground data. For LST determination, thermal band of the same satellite images will be used. Future LULC and LST trends will be predicted under growing urban area scenarios using suitable ecological models. Land use change will be simulated in context of urbanization and project like “China Pakistan Economic Corridor” CPEC scenario up to 2047 using Cellular Automata model and Artificial Neural Network (ANN). Recommendations will be suggested for a sustainable development in the major tourist regions of Pakistan under future LST trends. PI and CoPI have all the expertise to conduct this study successfully at COMSATS University.

data.projectName: Nano-agriculture for ensuring food security in Pakistan by economical crop production from salt-affected areas
data.projectDigest:
Soil salinity is a severe environmental problem limiting crop production and causing economic losses. It also poses severe threat to food security especially arid regions of the world including Pakistan. However, the productive use of the salt-affected areas by latest technologies presents us with opportunity to ensure food security by increasing crop production. 
The advent of nanotechnology has opened new horizons of research in all fields of science including the agriculture.  The use of nano-particles in agriculture is known as "nano-farming" or "nano-agriculture" is new aspect of agriculture especially under abiotic stresses to enhance crop's adaptability and increase yields.
The potassium Ferrite nano particles for increasing crop growth and yield is a new form of technology. The potassium ferrite nano particles supposed to enhance crop yield under salinity stress by limiting the uptake and translocation of sodium ions.
The project aims at enhancing wheat and tomato crop growth and yield under salinity by the application of potassium ferrite nano particle. For this purpose, nano particles will be prepared in lab and experiments will performed in hydroponics and soil.

data.projectName: enhancement of Optoelectronic Properties of Zinc Oxide based Nanostructures
data.projectDigest: Transparent conducting oxides (TCO’s) are the novel materials which are under the consideration of most of researchers working in Semiconductor Industry. ZnO based transparent materials are the novel materials which are cost effective and stable. Such a property of these materials makes ZnO based coatings to be used as defogging, antistatic coatings in various applications like heating elements on aircraft windows, out-door displays etc. Such a combination of conductivity and transparency is not possible in intrinsic oxides; however, non-stoichiometric composition of some other materials results in such materials which show above mentioned properties. A lot of work has been done on ZnO as TCO’s but we will optimize the concentration of graphite, Al, TiO2 and Ge to obtain good optical transparency and electrical conductivity. Nanostructures of ZnO embedded with the previously mentioned materials will be synthesized through laser ablation method. They will be initially characterized to see their structural properties through X-Ray diffraction and scanning electron microscope, compositional analysis will also be carried out through EDX as well as their electrical and optical properties will be studied simultaneously. Dr Shaista Shahzada at department of Physics at international Islamic University Islamabad will be the Co-PI and we will use LASER at LASER lab, IIUI for the synthesis of nanostructures.

data.projectName: Engineering disease and Stress (biotic and abiotic) Resistance in tomato Using Combination of Recombinant DNA and Marker Free Selection Technologies
data.projectDigest: Pakistan’s economy is mainly based on agriculture, and most of our trade has depended on agriculture-based product’s exports for past decades, but climate changes; due to global warming and industrial pollution has caused a remarkable drop in crops yields of our important crops. Once not only, we were self-sufficient in staple food crops, but we were also able to export some of them.  For example, wheat and rice crops are prone to diseases caused by bacterial and fungal pathogens, that come into play in changed climate. In addition, same phenomenon can be applied to pests like herbivores, insects and pathogens . Therefore, the need of day is to develop disease and stress resistant crops that are sustainable and their desired traits are long lasting. In our preliminary research on GLP genes (stress resistant) and their promoters from local rice cultivars, we have found regulatory elements that are responsible for induction of corresponding gene ,in response to both biotic and abiotic stresses and render it to offer resistance to corresponding stresses. Now we are looking forward to exploit GLP genes and their promoters using modern recombinant DNA technology approaches to develop powerful constructs, in context of conferring resistance to diseases and stresses, to be ultimately used for developing disease and stress resistant transgenic crops.

data.projectName: Performance Modeling of Aircraft Engine for Fault Diagnostics
data.projectDigest: An aircraft consists of modules like engine, avionics, flight controls, electrical system and hydraulics. The engine is an integral part of any aircraft. The heart of an engine is an engine control unit (ECU). ECU controls the main working of an aircraft engine. ECU are not only used in aircraft engines (both military and commercial) but also in automobiles and gas turbine power plants. Since Pakistan is not indigenously manufacturing engines, hence the domain knowledge of ECU logic is quite limited. However, fault prediction based on engine parameters relies on knowledge of ECU logic.  This project aims to develop data-driven models for various performance parameters like fuel flow, engine speed and exhaust gas temperature. This project aims to model the complex dynamics of ECU. The first step in this regard is to consider ECU as a black-box model and then to model it using the archived input-output data. The parameters values are collected through various sensors and are analyzed through different techniques. This project will develop the black-box model for the ECU system by employing artificial neural networks (ANN) based techniques. An accurate model of ECU will be very useful in fault diagnostic of the engine.

data.projectName: Multifunctional nanocomposite membrane for wound dressings
data.projectDigest: Wound and burn injuries have become the global issue among the world's top health care problems. The attack of pathogen and opportunistic microorganisms into skin wounds impedes the healing process. Thus, the control of infections is mandatory in the wound care facilities. Chitosan (CS) is demonstrating desirable features for wound dressing applications due to its biodegradability and antimicrobial properties. CS also promotes wound healing. Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) hydrogel is demonstrating desirable features for wound dressing applications due to its low-cost, viscoelastic, hydrophilicity and good film properties. However, the white appearance of PVA hydrogels has restricted its use for wound healing due to difficulty in observing the wound-healing progress through the hydrogel. The fabrication of nanocomposite membrane is a desirable approach to treat this issue. Nanocomposite membranes are produced by an addition of nanoscale entities (nanofibers/nanoparticles/nanoplatelets) onto polymer matrix. The nanocomposite membranes demonstrated significant enhancement of mechanical properties, healing capacity, antibacterial features as compared to polymer alone. Sepiolite (a natural clay) (SP) is a potential candidate for reinforcement of synthetic polymers. data.projectName: Design and Development of a Low Cost Metal Additive manufacturing (AM) system for Manufacturing of Biomedical  Implants
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Additive Manufacturing (AM) also known as 3D printing technology has revolutionised the way products were designed and manufactured. In 3D printing/ AM, the parts are build by applying the material layer-by-layer were it is required , thus provides flexibility of manufacturing complex geometries without the need for advanced tooling. Am technologies can work with a wide variety of materials such as metals ceramics, polymers and resins etc. During the past 5 years, polymer based AM technologies have become more economical, however, metal based AM technologies are still very expensive. The major cost in these metal AM system, is the cost of integration of lasers and software for making 3D metallic parts. A very good quality laser (300 Watts) from leading laser manufacturer would cost approx 10 Million PKR, cost of optics approx 5 Million PKR and gantry system at 3 Million PKR, totalling to 18 Million PKR. The cost of a commercially available small size (bed size 12 x 16 inches) metallic 3D printer/ AM system starts at approx. 500 Million PKR. This project focuses on the development of metallic 3D printer by integrating laser, selection of suitable process parameters by experimentation and software development for manufacturing of biomedical implants.

data.projectName: Time-domain based numerical approach in the hybrid modeling of the vocal tract for speech generation
data.projectDigest: Speech technology has a major contribution to human-machine interaction. The speech production system comprises two organs such as the vocal folds and the vocal tract. The action of the vocal folds generates the train of pulses which are used to identify the voice of males and females by the pitch of these pulses. However, the characteristics of the vocal tract have a major role in the quality of the speech. The hybrid approach of Navier-Stokes equations and the digital waveguide model are both used to solve the flow problem in the vocal tract with different meshing styles of the computational domain. The basic drawback of this hybrid approach is the discontinuity between the solutions of these two models which is not good for the quality of speech. The solution of Navier-Stokes equations gives a good quality of sound in the case of consonants while the digital waveguide model is used for the generation of vowels. In the current work, we will address the drawback of the hybrid model by using the same unstructured meshing of the computational domain to maintain the smooth transition between consonants and vowels. This approach will lead to a good quality of speech generation.

data.projectName: Genome editing through CRISPR-Cas9 in rice (Oryza sativa L.) to produce drought resistant cultivars rather than conventional breeding
data.projectDigest: Throughout the world, most important abiotic stress for growth limitation and plants productivity is drought. Premium quality of rice is the demand of growing population with better living standards. Presently, the CRISPR/Cas9 system has all genome editing capabilities, e.g., knock-in, knockout, knockdown and expression activation. Using many approaches responses of stress responses have been operated for various regulatory networks as well as genes/ pathways, regulatory networks. Editing of genome is very beneficial methods for deletion/ insertion, introducing targeted mutation and accurate sequence of modification using customized nucleases in many organisms. Commonly tools of editing of genome are transcriptional activator-like effector nucleases, To expose the function of genome, engineering of CRISPR-Cas9 genome may assist close sequences manipulation in the genome. Consequently, the 1st publication revealing editing of genomic plant in 2013 by using CRISPR/Cas9 system, this framework has been useful to numerous species of plant such as Arabidopsis. This exploration work can have a significant advancement to produce resistance in rice against drought stress that can be beginning guidelines to create obstruction in plants as opposed to traditional reproducing techniques. Along these lines, it can result to uplift the economy of the nation through agribusiness.

data.projectName: Air pollution in relation to glucose homeostasis and inflammatory markers in Lahore, Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Lahore College for Women University, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Diabetes is a metabolic disorder distinguished by hyperglycemia caused due to genetic and environmental conditions. Air pollution is one of the leading environmental factors that occur due to rapid industrial growth and urbanization over the last few decades. Pakistan has undergone substantial increase in terms of emission sources of air pollutants. The prevalence of diabetes is increasing day by day and it was reported in 2019 that in Lahore it’s prevalence in adults is 33.7%. The possibility that exposure to air pollution may be a new and heretofore unrecognized contributing factor to the development of diabetes, and it strengthen the rationale for studying the link between air pollution and diabetes. So in this cross sectional study the subjects from different towns of Lahore will be enrolled and blood samples will be collected. Blood glucose level and inflammatory cytokines will be measured. The relationship between particulate matter and glucose homeostasis will be determined by using statistical analysis. As the economic impact of the disease is enormous and exposure to environmental pollutants may be an additional risk factor that, if prevented, could facilitate a reduction in disease incidence and in the over¬all associated health and economic burden.

data.projectName: Earthworm gut-soil microbiome mediated remediation of polluted soils: a low cost natural biotechnology tool for environment clean up
data.projectDigest: At present, our environment is heavily contaminated with pollutants such as plastics, pesticides and heavy metals and poses great threat to soil ecosystems as well as its fauna. Earthworms are widely accepted “ecosystem's engineers and their diversified gut microbiome is considered to be one of the key drivers of pollutant degradation. Hence, current project will focus on “Earthworm Metaphire posthuma gut microbiome diversity and bioremediation potential against soils polluted with plastic, pesticide and heavy metals”. Low density polyethelene (LDPE), 4,4?-dichloro-diphenyl and decachlorobiphenyl (DDT) and cadmium chloride  (CdCl2) will be used as representative of microplastic, pesticide reservoirs and heavy metal pollution respectively. Obtained results will enable us to determine the microbiome diversity and relative abundance of different taxa alongwith degradation extent of each pollutant, determined by atomic absorption spectrophotometery (AAS), gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC-MS), fourier. Additionally, possible role of different taxa as biomarkers of exposure for polluted soils will be explored. data.projectName: A survey of wood-boring and bark beetles (Coleoptera) in Balochistan from faunistic and pest management
data.piUniversity: Federal Urdu University of Arts, Sciences & Technology
data.projectDigest: Biodiversity, as variety of plant and animal life, is the essential element of a functional ecosystem. Environment integrity, obtainable through the protection of biodiversity, determines greater resilience towards disturbing factors, such as climate change, and guarantees a series of ecosystem services capable of support and improves the subsistence of the local people communities. Coleoptera (Beetles) thanks to their pivotal role in the ecosystem provide important information on environmental conservation or have strong effects on human activities, such as trade in goods, agricultural production and food safety. Wood-boring and bark beetles have a relevant role in forest dynamics and are important bioindicators; however, some species act as pests on fruit and timber trees, determining serious environmental damages and causing significant economic and production losses, with consequent important repercussions on local and international markets. Furthermore, globalization and international trade are causing important movements of fauna with a consequent increase in the rate of introduction of exotic species, including potential pests. Wood- related beetles of Pakistan are poorly known in general and very little in known about their biology, ecology and real distribution. This knowledge gap poses several problems in the development of protection plans for threatened species or the implementation of effective control measures against pest. The aim of this project is to develop a cheap but highly effective monitoring plant in Balochistan in order to characterize the local community of wood-borer and bark beetles, understand species phenology, describe new species, identify pests and eventually intercept newly exotic and invasive species.

data.projectName: Fluoride contamination into the groundwater of Punjab, Pakistan and associated health risk in children population
data.piName: Syed Ali Musstjab Akber Shah  Eqani
data.projectDigest: Over 200 million people and 25 different nations including Pakistan are at severe risk of fluoride poisoning due to contaminated groundwater. In Pakistan, based on our recent data, 12 major districts in Punjab have shown exceeded fluoride levels (>1.5 mg/L) in the collected water samples.  Although it is also well documented that fluoride contents in serum, urine and in blood is a good indicator of internal exposure and these indicators are helpful for understanding the molecular mechanism of fluoride toxicity. Additionally, urinary metabolomics are the valuable tool to detect potential biomarker associated with fluoride toxicity and for the early health characterization of exposed populations. Previous studies have reported the risk evaluation and occurrence of  Fluorosis and its association with fluoride toxicity. However, to our knowledge, none of the studies in Pakistan assessed and association with urinary metabolomics based biomarker(s)  in context of fluoride exposure and the role of the candidate genes involved in the development of Fluorosis in individuals exposed to fluoride. In this proposed project, we will carry out integrated investigation of the geogenic factors’ health risk(s) (fluoride contamination into household drinking water) to the associated children populations,  fluoride toxicity biomarker identification and the role of genetic factors.

data.projectName: Selenium Enriched Fodders-A sustainable way to improve health and milk yield of dairy cattle
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest: Selenium (Se) is an important micronutrient considered essential for animals and influences plant metabolism as well. It promotes animal health by increasing the production of antibodies and enhancing resistance against various diseases. Se deficiency may lead to reduced growth and fertility, whereas excess Se causes hoof deformation and respiratory failure in animals. Hence, the development of balanced livestock ration is essential to prevent animal diseases linked with malnutrition. Considering the Se for plants as well, the exogenous application with Se or Se-enriched compounds can be used as an efficient, cost effective and viable approach to enrich animal fodders with Se. The proposed project is aimed at evaluating the beneficial role of Se supplementation on milk yield and quality of dairy cattle. The study would involve a series of field experiments on fodder crops followed by feeding of dairy cattle with Se treated forages. Initially, the forage species (maize, sorghum and lucerne) will be treated with different levels of Se to optimize Se doses. Later, the Se-fortified fodders, containing optimized Se levels, will be fed to dairy cattle to determine their effects on milk yield and quality. In addition, Se effects on inflammatory response of the cow’s udder would be monitored.

data.projectName: Designing of two-dimensional IV-monochalcogenide materials for next-generation energy production technologies
data.projectDigest: The severe environmental pollution caused by the consumption of fossil fuels has raised global warming to an alarming level in recent years. Consequently, a remarkable interest has been paid by researchers to introduce novel alternative resources of clean energy to combat the effects of global warming on the mother earth. Sun is considered as the most feasible and large energy resource of clean energy to replace the traditional energy resources. Among several potential energy from the sun and waste heat, photovoltaics and thermoelectrics have been proved as the most feasible approaches to convert solar energy into electrical energy.  However, materials that covert solar/heat energy to electrical energy are mostly expensive and of low efficiency. In this project, we are committed to the designing of low-cost and high-efficiency materials to convert solar/heat energy to clean energy via photovoltaic and thermoelectric approaches. We will adopt both theoretical and experimental approaches to execute this study. Advanced and accurate theoretical approaches will be adopted to design and recognize materials of low-cost and high efficiency.  Such cost-effective and efficient materials will be fabricated experimentally for clean energy applications. We believe that the construction of a high-performance clean energy production devices will help in resolving issues relating to energy crises and environmental pollution.

data.projectName: Archeological Explorations in the Districts of Gilgit, Ghizer, Hunza and Nagir, Gilgit-Baltistan—Pakistan
data.projectDigest: This proposed research will extend further the scope of previous explorations in Gilgit Division in three different Phases. In the first phase, further explorations will be conducted in Gilgit, Ghizer, Hunza and Nagir Districts, collectively called as Gilgit Division of Gilgit-Baltistan. In the second phase, the activities of experimental archaeology and trial excavations will be conducted on the selected suitable sites, explored during the survey phase. In the third phase, archaeometric study of the selected ancient rock art will be conducted, which will help us to date the pre-historic rock sites in the area, depicting the movement of earliest human being, reached this part of the world. This research work of three years will result an improved set of data, with thematic results, for the establishment of a Museum in Gilgit zone, in future, which will house the heritage of Gilgit-Baltistan.

data.projectName: CHARACTERIZATION AND HETEROLOGOUS EXPRESSION OF ANTITHROMBOTIC FIBRINOLYTIC ENZYMES AND THEIR THERAPEUTIC APPLICATIONS
data.projectDigest: A thrombus (blood clot),  If developed when it is not desirable this can create considerable penalty like heart attack, stroke embolism, and ischemia.  According to report (2011) by World Health Organization (WHO) 17.3 million community died by cardiovascular diseases in 2008, which represent 30% of all Worldwide deaths. Expected increase to death by cardiovascular diseases is 23.3 million people by 2030.  The major cause of cardiovascular diseases is intra vascular thrombosis. The intravenous administration of exogenous plasminogen activator is the root of antithrombic therapy that breaks the blood clot and restores blood stream. Nevertheless, the agents being employed are costly, heat sensitive and can create detrimental effects, for instance gastrointestinal hemorrhage, and allergic reactions.  Current research project will explore the role and application of fibrinolytic enzymes from local  leach and earthworms species for finding of novel plasmin-like proteases.  Genes encoding different anti-coagulating fibrinolytic  enzymes will be  identified and characterized.  Their biological role will also be explored through sequence analysis. This study will enable us to better understand the underlying mechanism and identification of potential therapeutic targets for commercial scale production.  Production of these enzymes will be enhanced by heterologous expression using recombinant DNA technology.  The products efficacy and biological role will be analyzed by studying their biochemical properties.  This study will enable us to better understand the therapeutic targets from local leach and earthworm species for commercial scale production

data.projectName: Genome-wide subtractive approach to prioritize a hypothetical protein of XDR Salmonella typhi as potential drug target.
data.projectDigest: Salmonella typhi, the potent human pathogen causing typhoid fever, continues to be a major public health concern affecting millions of people everywhere in the world. Poor hygiene condition is one of the root causes, ascribed to the S. typhi infection. It has been reported by WHO that around 21 million new cases and 0.2 million global deaths reported annually, of whom 90% occurs in Asia. Southeast Asia remains the hot spot for the S. typhi associated infections with an estimated incidence of 412.9 to 493.5 per 100,000 person years in Pakistan, which represents the third highest incidence rate for any region. Moreover, extensive use of antibiotics such as chloramphenicol, ampicillin and trimethoprim/ sulfamethoxazole has been resulted in the prevalence of extensively drug resistance in Salmonellae. Currently, azithromycin is the only remaining reliable and affordable therapeutic option to manage patients with XDR typhoid in low-resource settings. Phytochemicals and herbal medicines are useful and viable alternatives to pharmaceuticals because they are economical, effective, non-resistance-forming, renewable, and environmentally friendly. By keeping this approach in mind the project is designed, that encircling around the subtractive genomics of locally circulating XDR S. typhi isolates against small molecules that helps to identify new therapeutic agents.

data.projectName: Nano material grafted ion exchange membranes (NM grafted-IEMs): Synthesis, characterization and study of the effects of nano composites on membrane properties and performance.
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: With energy cost rising and environmental problems worsening, the challenge currently lies in the production or storage of energy and supply of fresh water by renewable and sustainable resources. Ion exchange membranes (IEMs) have attracted much attention to achieve the energy task and to alleviate environment related issues. Ion exchange membranes have wide-ranging applications from pharmaceuticals to waste treatment, desalination to water purification and energy production to energy storage. Its application extends into many industrial and electrochemical processes including, Reverse Electrodialysis (RED), Pressure Retarded Osmosis (PRO), Electrodialysis (ED), Fuel Cell (FC), Microbial Fuel Cell (MFC), Diffusion Dialysis (DD), CAPMIX batteries, and Redox flow batteries. The most crucial point is to compromise the desired membrane properties for high performance with the criteria for commercial and environmental relevance. Incorporation of nanomaterial to ion exchange membrane is one way to synthesize ion exchange membrane with better properties and improved electrochemical performance. The aim of this project is to synthesize novel IEM by incorporation of nano materials and to connect the new synthesis with the improved properties and electrochemical performance of modified IEMs, for sustainable development goals and better future.

data.projectName: Genetic analysis of drug resistance and vaccine candidates genes in malarial parasites in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is one of those countries facing increasing burden of annual malaria cases for the last three years, despite of sufficient malaria control measures, due to the emergence of continuous drug resistance in the local malarial parasites. The major causative species is Plasmodium vivax causing 84% of total malaria cases in Pakistan. Among the 374,513 confirmed cases of malaria in Pakistan in 2019, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa ranked 1st contributing 32% cases followed by Sindh (31%) and tribal districts (19%). Currently molecular markers are the only valuable tool for monitoring introduction and spread of drug resistance. Alternatively vaccine development against malaria is the best approach to combat and eliminate malaria from endemic countries. However, the genetic polymorphisms in some immunogenic parasite proteins create hurdles in development of effective vaccines. Therefore, extensive evaluation of genetic variants in these vaccine candidate antigenic proteins in P. vivax populations is important for effective vaccine development. This study is aimed study the genetic structure of some vaccine candidate antigens and to assess the presence of mutations in genes associated with drug resistance in P. vivax from highly endemic districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and tribal districts that have not been included in previous studies. data.projectName: State-of-the-Art Technologies in Bioremediation of Contaminated Effluent – The Textile Industry Case
data.piUniversity: Abbottabad University of Science & Technology (AUST), Abbottabad
data.projectDigest: Textile sector has an overwhelming impact on the economy of Pakistan, accounting for 25% of the GDP and contribute approximately 57% to the country’s exports. Pakistan has an industrial importance being 4th largest cotton producer and with the third largest spinning capacity in Asia. On contrary textile processing discharge numerous hazardous chemicals depending on nature of raw material and product. The effluents containing these pollutants leads to major health concerns including sever and chronic damage to blood composition, lower energy levels, reduced CNS functioning, mental health and damage due to kidneys, lungs and liver due to carcinogenic and mutagenic nature. Removal of these hazardous contaminants from metal contaminated water and soil through microbial remediation is one of the promising approach by using environmental friendly and cost-effective process as compared to traditional methods. The selected industrial area has neither been explored previously for evaluating heavy metals concentrations in the water and soil environment nor its indigenous microbial community has been identified and tested for its potential to remove toxic heavy metals from contaminated soil. Therefore, this study will provides first ever insight into the indigenous metallotolerant microbial strains having application for effective heavy metals removal from industrial effluent and contaminated soil.

data.projectName: Targeting Neuro-inflammatory Markers to Propose Better Drug Regimen for the Treatment of Epilepsy: A Pre-clinical study
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Epilepsy is an excitatory neuronal (brain) disorder that effects 1% of the worldwide population. Prevalence of epilepsy in Pakistan is 9.99/1000 which is around 1/10th of the world burden of epilepsy. Several anti-epileptic drugs (AEDs) are available for its treatment but approximately 35-40% of the patients get resistant to them. This requires establishment of new, safe and effective therapies for the patients of epilepsy. Recent studies have shown that inflammation have a role in the pathophysiology of epilepsy and. Further, inflammation has also shown to damage blood brain barrier (BBB), which further enhance neuro-inflammation leading to the severity of seizures and contributes to treatment resistance. Therefore, it can be presumed that anti-inflammatory agents can enhance the efficacy of available AEDs when used in combination with them. Therefore, we aimed to explore the therapeutic potential of anti-inflammatory drug Diclofenac (DFS) in combination with available AEDs (Valproic acid; VA and Levetiracetam; LEV) against epilepsy. Further we have also planned to investigate the anti-epileptic potential of natural anti inflammatory compound(s) named opuntiol and its derivatives. To achieve our aims epilepsy will be developed in mice, and animals will be divided into control and different treatment groups. Therapeutic potential of the given drugs combination and natural compounds will be evaluated at both behavioral and molecular level. The study will provide a rational if DFS can be used in combination with either Valproic acid or Levetiracetam. Further If our work is successful, we might also identify  a natural compound that could undergo further testing to determine if they may be suitable to work either alone or with available AEDs to combat epilepsy.

data.projectName: Analysis of Computational Complexity and Algorithms for  Choice  Model
data.projectDigest: Computational choice theory [1-7] is an interdisciplinary field of scientific inquiry which is related to choice theory and computer science, ideas are exchanged in both fields of study.  In computer science, it is concerned with the development of new techniques, such as to  design an efficient algorithm and to avoid computational complexity. In choice theory fair division algorithm, voting theories and preference aggregation are studies for a collective choice.  In this project, we solve the time complexity and NP-hard [15-21] for a coalition of two or more individuals for some choice models. It is very common to occur computational complexity in  choice  rules, coins as,  dictatorship, unanimity, anonymity, Independence of irrelevant alternatives and Pareto principle. It is very hard to satisfy all the properties of a fair choice model.  In the framework of preference relations such as majority judgment theory[4-6], the Borda majority count[7], we try to develop a sophisticated technique  which satisfy these properties and design an efficient algorithm to reduce computational complexities  in the collective decision making.

data.projectName: Multilayered Thin Films Structure of  Nickle Oxide for Electronic Transport Properties
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is the victim of adverse energy crises since last few decades, which has the biggest challenge for the vendors of developing countries in 21st century. The increasing gap between demand and supply of energy resources has been the major driving force for the various methods used to decrease energy consumption. For the purpose highly conductive electrodes and materials  for long time charge retention are the novel approaches for the practitioners. Multilayered thin films are the promising materials for above mentioned approaches. data.projectName: Structure-Based Discovery of ?-Lactamase Inhibitors for the Targeted Treatment of Multidrug Resistance Tuberculosis (TB)
data.projectDigest: This research project is envisaged to discover the ?-lactamase inhibitors through structure guided approaches for the effective treatment of Tuberculosis (TB). Beta-Lactamase is a key enzyme secreted by Mycobacterium tuberculosis and is the main cause of beta-lactam drug resistance. Tuberculosis is an infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It is among the most ancient, most pathogenic, highly recurrence, and need long time period for treatment. Besides this, it also has developed multidrug resistance against beta-lactam drug. The resistance arises due to beta-lactamase enzyme, which involved in the hydrolysis of beta-lactam ring of this class of drug. Appearance of resistance against most of the antibacterial agents has become a significant health threat. As a result, only a limited number of antimicrobial agents are available for the treatment of diseases caused by different bacterial pathogens, including Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Beta-Lactam antibiotics can be made useful against tuberculosis if we can use the effective beta-lactamase inhibitors in combination with antibiotics against bacterial infections. Therefore, more effective, potent and less toxic beta-lactamase inhibitors are urgently needed for the effective treatment of Tuberculosis. During this study, new and potent inhibitors will be identified, through bioassay and structural biological tools such as protein crystallography.

data.projectName: FORMULATION AND CHARACTERIZATION OF LEVOSULPIRIDE CONTAINING LIPID NANOCARRIERS FOR ENHANCEMENT OF ITS BIOAVAILABILITY AND GASTROKINETICS
data.projectDigest: The low solubility and bioavailability of levosulpiride is a challenge for its solid oral unit dosage formulations. In order to overcome this problem, study will be focused on developing nanostructured lipid carriers as drug delivery system. Lipids as carriers have the ability to enhance gastrointestinal absorption of poorly bioavailable drugs. The properties of lipids like physiochemical diversity and biocompatibility can enhance oral bioavailability of poorly water soluble, lipophilic and less permeable drugs. Lipid nanocarriers such as solid lipid nanoparticles (SLNs) and nanostructured lipid carriers (NLCs) have been investigated as an established colloidal drug carrier system. NLCs composed of a solid lipid matrix exhibit high drug-loading capacity due to the presence of liquid lipids which create imperfections in the matrix accommodating more drug molecules reducing drug expulsion during storage. NLCs have been investigated extensively to improve the oral bioavailability of many poorly water-soluble drugs.

data.projectName: Pharmacological screening of selected synthetic benzimidazole derivatives against painful diabetic neuropathy in animal models
data.piUniversity: Capital University of Science and Technology, Islamabad
data.projectDigest: Diabetes mellitus is a metabolic disorder characterized by increased blood glucose level (hyperglycemia). Beside hyperglycemia, other harmful effects such as nephropathy, retinopathy and painful diabetic neuropathy are also associated with diabetes mellitus and are main cause of morbidity and death. Diabetes mellitus is expected to become one of the world’s main disablers and killers within the next 25 years. It is at the forefront of public health problems. Regions with greatest potential are Asia and Africa, where diabetes mellitus rates could rise to two to three-folds than the present rates. According to national survey 2016-17, every 4th individual in Pakistan is suffering from diabetes mellitus.  The painful diabetic neuropathy is the most debilitating adverse effect of diabetes mellitus and is associated with increased neuroinflammation and associated mediators. Research studies have shown that peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPAR-gamma) activation reduces neuroinflammation. Additionally, benzimidazole derivatives are known to activate PPAR- gamma and possess anti-inflammatory potential. Therefore, we believe that newly synthesized benzimidazole derivatives might decrease neuroinflammation involving PPAR- gamma activation and might reduce painful diabetic neuropathy. Therefore, benzimidazole derivatives might be potential drug candidates for the management of painful diabetic neuropathy.

data.projectName: Anti-venom Antibody production against Krait (Bungarus spp.) in Poultry Birds
data.projectDigest:
Currently available snake antivenom is from mammalian source (horse serum). Antivenom produced by this method is more expensive, time consuming and are lower than country requirements. As well there are more chances of serum sickness.
Present project is focused to replace mammalian snake antivenom production with chicken antivenom (IgY antibodies production). This method is cost effective; more antivenom production can be assured within shorter period of time. In Pakistan NIH (Islamabad) is the only institute which is preparing  snake antivenom within its limited resources.  This project will facilitate and boost up the production of antivenom within the country that will save import cost and will be frequently available throughout the country.

data.projectName: Transforming ESP teaching in Higher Education Institutions in Pakistan: bridging the gap between curricula and job markets
data.projectDigest:
Professional practices in the 21st century are getting increasingly diversified in the wake of globalization during the last more than three decades. With this diversification, English for Specific Purposes (ESP) graduates are expected to acquire relevant language, communication, and interpersonal skills that could make them useful and effective participants in their target job market. However, in Pakistan, the absorption of ESP graduates into job markets has been reported to be slow in the national and international professional markets. A significant reason of this relates to inadequate preparation of the graduates at the university level. This project researches the current state of ESP curricula, syllabi and pedagogic practice in university departments across Pakistan to analyze learning gaps between academic courses and the target job market requirements. Data will be collected from eight different regions to which the country has been divided (both from the universities and the target job market for each discipline).
The project aims to formulate recommendations and solutions to add value to these programs through targeting misalignment between ESP in academia and the job market for two main reasons: a) to help universities generate economic revenue by adding job-oriented value to the ESP courses they offer; b) enable learners to absorb effectively and quickly into the job market to reduce graduates’ unemployment and boost their economic prosperity. Both aims of the project are linked to the broader aim of enhancing economic activity in Pakistan to minimize poverty to fight social problems including extremism.

data.projectName: Citrus autotetraploid rootstock-induced transcriptomic, molecular and physiological responses associated with combined and individual effects of heat stress and water deficit conditions in Citrus sinensis.
data.projectDigest: Citrus orchards are grown under irrigation and faces numerous biotic (Tristeza, Phytophtora etc.) and abiotic constraints (water deficit, salt stress, heat stress etc.) that negatively affect yield- and fruit quality. In citrus, for the last two decades, numerous polyploidy rootstocks have been established in different countries across the world, which presented better tolerance against different abiotic and biotic constraints. In this research project, two diploid (Carrizo citrange and Citrumello 4475) and their corresponding autotetraploid rootstocks will be evaluated under heat and drought stress individually and in combination. For this purpose, in preliminary experiments citrus rootstocks will be exposed to drought stress and heat stress individually. In the next experiment, these rootstocks will be evaluated under combined stress of drought and heat. Further, these rootstocks will be grafted with sweet orange cv. succari and evaluated under combined stress. Different physiological (net photosynthesis rate, stomatal conductance, transpiration rate, sap flow etc) and molecular parameters (e.g.activities of different antioxidative enzymes) will also be measured both in leaf and roots. For in-depth study, transcriptomic analysis will be performed for better understanding of rootstocks-induced responses at genetic level involved in the tolerance and sensitivity of heat and drought stress in leaves of succari.

data.projectName: Training Artificial Intelligence Classifiers Though Depth Images for Identification of Intruders Carrying Explosives
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest: Safety and security of humans have always been an important concern in every aspect. With the advancement in engineering, sciences, and technology new methods to harm human have also been introduced. At the same time, scientists are paying attention to the security aspects by developing new software and hardware gadgets. Suicide bombing is one such nuisance that is still an open challenge for the world to detect/predict. This project deals with the identification of a suicide bomber using a 3D depth camera and machine learning techniques. This work will utilizes the skeletal data provided by the 3D depth camera to identify a bomber wearing a suicide jacket. The prediction will be based on real-time 3D posture data of the body joints obtained using a 3D depth sensor. This work will extracts 3D spatial features of the human body for 25 joints. Using a comprehensive experimental design, a dataset will be created consisting of 3D spatial gait information of 20 joints obtained through multiple participants. The dataset will record at least 20 joints information for each of the participants with and without wearing a suicide jacket. Utilizing this dataset, machine learning will be applied to identify a suspected suicide bomber.

data.projectName: A component mdoel for cyber-phtsical systems
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
In the current era of advanced technology, cyber-physical systems (e.g., IoT based smart city projects, autonomous automobile systems etc.) are part of our daily life. One way or another, we interact with such systems. A combination of heterogeneous devices for the construction of such systems demands a component based off-the-shelf approach. With such an approach, systems can be built in a shorter time without compromising the desired reliability. 

In this context of aforesaid, based on the comparative analysis and features between component-based development approaches, we would like to use an approach named EX-MAN component model. The overall objective of our proposed research is to extend EX-MAN for the construction of self-adaptive distributed cyber-physical systems. With the proposed approach, we would be able to provide a model and a process to build such systems in shorter time.

The possible industry and user of the proposed model would be the software development organizations; these organization would undertake the development projects of cyber-physical systems. We would provide a software development model and a process along with a user-friendly prototype tool for the construction of cyber-physical systems.

data.projectName: Genetic basis of resistance to carbapenems, the spread and the acquisition of carbapenemase encoding genes in pathogenic Gram-negative bacteria
data.projectDigest: Gram-negative bacteria, such as Klebsiella pneumoniae, Escherichia coli, Acinetobacter baumannii, and Enterobacter cloacae are clinically very important causing pneumonia urinary tract, and blood stream infections in the hospital setting. Carbapenems present the most effective antibacterial therapy against the antibiotic-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, since antibiotic resistance in these bacteria is very common. However, over the last few years Pakistani hospitals have experienced the emergence of carbapenem resistance in Gram-negative bacteria. The carbapenem-resistant strains have acquired mobile plasmids harboring the carbapenemase encoding genes referred to as blaKPC, blaNDM-1, and blaOXA-48 type which can be transferred from one genera to other genera of bacteria, increasing the spread of resistance and limiting the treatment options. The proposed research will collect and genetically analyze carbapenem resistant clinical isolates of Klebsiella pneumoniae, Escherichia coli, Acinetobacter baumannii, and Enterobacter cloacae from all district hospitals in Sindh area to unravel the molecular epidemiology underpinning the emergence of carbapenem resistance. Further molecular characterization of the carbapenem- resistant strains will reveal whether the emergence and rise in the rate of carbapenem resistance is the result of spread of a successful resistant clone with extensive resistance or the development of many different resistant strains which are simultaneously spreading. The outcomes of the proposed research will extend our understanding of this emerging public health crisis and likely inform current and future control strategies.

data.projectName: To investigate the cross-sectional association between oral microbiota, inflammation and type 2 diabetes mellitus
data.projectDigest:
Diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a metabolic disorder with both genetic and environmental components. A growing body of evidences suggest that T2DM leads to inflammation and disturbed of oral microbes. We hypothesized that inflammation might link oral microbial exposures to diabetes. Two recent studies carried out by our group have indicated abnormality in oral microbiota and perturbed expression of inflammatory genes in Pakistani T2DM patients.
During the proposed project, a detailed clinical and laboratory-based research will be done to investigate the association between oral microbiota, inflammation and T2DM in Pakistani population. Saliva and blood samples from diabetic patients (n = 300) and healthy individuals (n = 100) will be used for (a) characterization of oral microbiota by next generation DNA sequencing followed by bioinformatics and (b) expression profiling of a gene panel involved in inflammation. Salivary pH, glucose and lactate of study participants will be estimated. Biochemical and hematological tests including blood glucose, HbA1c, liver function tests, complete blood picture, lipid profile will be carried out. Moreover, waist circumference, body mass index, oral and dental health profiles of participants will be examined. The obtained rich clinical dataset will provide novel insights regarding pathophysiology of association between oral microbiota, inflammation and T2DM in Pakistani population.

data.projectName: Synthesis and Applications of Molecularly Imprinted Nanophotocatalysts for the Abatement of Pesticides
data.projectDigest: One major concern to the farmers in agricultural lands is the pesticide resistance. When it happens, the existing pesticides are no more effective and require the introduction of new products in the market.  Hence, diverse types of pesticides are being introduced day by day to meet up the challenge. These pesticides on one hand play a prime role in protecting crops from invaders while on the other hand, they are a major source of water pollution and result in vicious diseases. Therefore, to tackle the challenges imposed by such pollutants, it is necessary to sort out techniques which are effective and economical in combating them. Hence, we propose the synthesis of novel imprinted photocatalysts efficiently capable of degrading the pesticides in the presence of sunlight with selective recognition. The synthesized materials will be characterized to elucidate their structural composition and will be casted into reusable devices.

data.projectName: Adaptation to climate change through smart city green infrastructure
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Massive urbanization and transportation in cities are major sources of Green House Gases (GHGs), which is affecting environment adversely. Due to greenhouse gasses global temperature on the earth rises which ultimately increase the energy demand and consuming more resources of energy. An urban heat island (UHI) is an urban area or metropolitan area that is significantly warmer than its surrounding rural areas. A review of literature indicates that small trees, shrubs and grasslands and green belts are very much effective in controlling and regulating temperature. Islamabad which has grown enormously in the previous few decades also experiences state of urban heat island. This research aims to contemplate the impacts of vegetation on reduction of urban heat island in Islamabad.

data.projectName: Documentation  of Endangered Domaaki Language and Culture
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest:
Domaaki ([?oma:ki], aka Dumaki, Domaki; ISO 639-3: dmk; Glottolog: doma1260) is a severely endangered language spoken in two villages by dozen of fluent speakers in northern Pakistan. It belongs to the central zone of the Indo-Aryan branch of the Indo-Iranian group, which is part of the Indo-European language family. Some published estimates list 500 Dooma (Backstrom 1992, Kreutzmann 2005), but these appear to focus on ethnicity rather than actual speakers. Observations made in 2002 and 2004 (Rahman 2003, Weinreich 2008), estimate that there are only 40 speakers of the Nagar dialect, and approximately 300 of the Hunza dialect. The majority of them are elderly; and children are no longer taught the language (Buddruss 1984, Schmid 2007:116, Weinreich 2015). Based on these data, Unesco classifies Domaaki as severely endangered (Moseley 2010), while Ethnologue rates it as moribund (Lewis et al. 2016). 

The project will: (a) create a corpus of 40 hours audio and video recordings of different genres, with 12 hours of annotated data, (b) compile a trilingual Domaaki-Urdu-English dictionary of 2000 entries, and (c) develop a sketch grammar of Domaaki.  The documentation of Domaaki will provide a number of intellectual contributions to the field of linguistics and beyond. As already mentioned, the number of speakers of both dialects is small and steadily decreasing; the Nagar dialect may only have few speakers in total. Thus, the preservation of the language is worthy in itself. Native speakers will be involved as collaborators at all levels of the project. The research results will be disseminated to the local community.  The data acquired will be useful for linguists working in language description and comparative linguistics.

data.projectName: Validation, Translations  and Norms-establishment of Impact of Climate Change on Mental Health Scale
data.projectDigest: Climate change has emerged as a disastrous reality of today’s world. It has far reaching impacts on almost all facets of human health, notably mental health. For many years this reality has been denied but it can no longer be ignored or avoided. There are numerous researches that have been conducted all over the world that indicate that there is a strong relationship between climate change and mental health but unfortunately, not even a single scale was developed to measure this impact. For this purpose a scale was recently developed by the principle investigator (PI) with her students which require data from entire Pakistan for its validation and establishment of norms. The scale will be translated into different languages for enhancing its understandability and to ensure the genuineness and authenticity of data. This scale was developed to assess the overall impact of climate change on mental health which is becoming a global influencing factor. In consideration of indigenous perspective Pakistan is among the list of those countries which are most affected by Climate Change. Every year the number of people who are affected is increasing. World Health Organization (2015) reported an increase of 250000 excess deaths per year due to well established impacts of climate change is expected. The extreme weather events include Floods, Extreme temperature fluctuations, lack of resources and precautionary measures. Therefore, there is a need to develop a scale to check the impacts of climate change on mental health so the prevalence can be measured and necessary measures can be taken in this regard to promote mental health and well-being.

data.projectName: Optimization of site specific production of canola (Brassica napus L.) in different agroclimatic conditions of Punjab
data.projectDigest: Canola (Brassica napus L.) being an oil seed crop is a marvelous gift as its oil is considered as good edible oil for human health and used for multipurposes as cooking, making pickles and lubricant industry. The meal is used as a source of feed for animal and birds particularly for poultry. Pakistan is shortage of edible oil and it is third largest imported commodity to fulfill the gap between local production (supply) and consumption (demand). Pakistan had to import 3.13 million tones of edible oil and oil seed which is 88% of requirements to fulfills the domestic needs by spending Rs.382 billion rupees. The area under oil seed crops like canola is very small as well as farmer do not used site specific recommendation of production technology like nutrient application as well as sowing of varieties according to agro climatic conditions. As the Govt. of Punjab has also announced subsidy for the promotion of area of canola, so it is needed to optimize or site specific recommendation for maximum production. The field experiments will be conducted for two consecutive years at three different location of Punjab i.e. Vehari, Faisalabad and Sheikhupura to test the yield and quality of canola crop at different sowing time as well as nutrients combination. The finding of proposed study could provide possible solution through dissemination of site specific packages of production technology like optimization of sowing time of canola varieties according to the different agro-climatic conditions and nutrients recommendation to achieve the destination of self sufficiency.

data.projectName: Forecasting Dengue Outbreak in Pakistan using White, Grey and Black Box Models
data.projectDigest:
Scientific research that would conclusively link a particular spike in dengue to a clearly climate-related warmer, wetter season somewhere does not yet exist. But the general risk must be there; and in all likelihood it’s intensifying especially in developing countries such as Pakistan.
This never, arguably, has the need been greater for such research to separate the various factors involved and enable early action to address rising risks.  By using machine learning approach (white, grey, and black box modeling), this proposed research study will support to forecast the dengue outbreak in Pakistan which will ultimately help to develop a better dengue control strategy/policy in the country.

data.projectName: Exploring the potentiality of electric discharge machining process for fabrication of bio-active surface in context of artificial human implants
data.projectDigest: Surface modification of biomedical implants is one of the vital areas of concern in biomedical and manufacturing sector. The project mainly focuses on recent technological developments and advancements in the field of orthopedic biomaterials with prominent emphasis on surface integrity evaluation through design and fabrication using electric discharge machining. In modern era, different alloys are developed which mimics similar properties and functions to that of the natural tissue and bones, are becoming a popular choice for making customized orthopedic implants and bone scaffolds. Tradeoff between mechanical and biological properties is needed to be optimized for better acceptability of these materials in the human body. The project will provide comprehensive overview of the state-of-the-art research in this rapidly evolving field in biomedical, manufacturing, nano characterization of surface. Electric discharge machining along with cutting-edge methods for the synthesis and surface evaluation of these materials can be expected as outcome. Focusing on various orthopedic applications, electric discharge coating and nanoscale surface evaluation is critical and research area yet to be explored. Surface modification enhancing osseointegration, tissue growth and mechanical properties improvement are critical factors while replacing the weakened bone with artificial one, the potential is yet to be evaluated.

data.projectName: MODULATING THE GLYCEMIC INDEX FOR PERSONALIZATION OF DIETARY STAPLE
data.projectDigest: Metabolic disorders such as diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular diseases are plaguing our society at an alarming rate and have enormous share towards morbidity and mortality in Pakistan. Risk of metabolic diseases is rapidly increasing owing to poor dietary choices, low educational level and changing lifestyle. Occurrence of Diabetes Mellitus in Pakistan is mainly attributed to excessive use of refined carbohydrate in diet. Strategies aimed at reducing the risks of these ailments and improving the quality of life must be devised in order to cope with this menace. Glycemic index (GI) and satiating potential of foods are strongly linked with metabolic diseases particularly diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular diseases. Low GI diets are considered to reduce the incidence of diabetes by preventing the sudden spike of blood glucose response and improving the insulin sensitivity. Therefore, a research project geared to modulate GI and satiating potential of cereal staples commonly consumed (wheat and rice) in Pakistan will be a step forward to address this challenge. Purposely, glycemic index of wheat based chapati/roti will be tailored through either addition of barley and oat or use of greater proportion of shrunken grains. Likewise, glycemic load of rice will be manipulated through use of brown rice or parboiling etc.

data.projectName: Intelligent Traffic Engineering
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Ease of mobility is a desideratum for building smart cities and intelligent transportation system. Intelligent traffic engineering system aids the ease of mobility initiative by navigating traffic to save citizens with time and resources and from hazels. Traffic engineering is a challenge for authorities in transportation primarily in developing nations and substantially in developed nations. One of the many reasons is manual maneuvering with limited human resource and less updated information about traffic flow. 
Computer science and technology advents make it possible to consider automating the traffic engineering. The real time information about the traffic situation can be captured using CCTV mounted on entrance and exit highways of cities like Islamabad. The digitized maps provide information about the road infrastructure and the transportation regulator can annotate the map with traffic signals data. A simulation tool can then model the real time traffic situation with provided information. An automated control system can assist with control of traffic flow maneuvering. Additional to the traffic signal control, the system can help in planning maintenance and other special purpose rerouting of traffic in view of its impact on traffic flow. The recorded data can be used to feed an artificial intelligence system which can further help in planning ahead for certain seasonal events and occasional assemblage. 
Intelligent traffic engineering system supports Pakistan in achieving United Nation’s sustainable development goals (SDG) emphasizing sustainable cities and communities (SDG 11), Climate action (SDG 12) and partnerships for goals (SDG 17).  An automated system with such capacities is indispensable for modern cities and modern life.

data.projectName: Novel integrated technology for recycling chromium from tanning industry waste
data.projectDigest: The waste of modern  industries contain a huge amount of heavy and critical metals. These contaminations easily leached in ground water bodies and put a potential risk on human  health and on aquatic environment. Chromium is main pollutant of tanning industries waste but it is also considered critical metal due to its low supply than demand. A huge amount of chromium +6 is being dispose of in unwanted amounts to the subsurface sites of tanning industries. Chromium +6 is a strong oxidant and form chromate ions upon dissolution that corrodes the organs and involves in respiration failure. Reduction of  Cr(VI) to Cr(III) serve as  initial step for removal of chromium +6 from tanning industrial waste but during reduction formation of intermediates oxidation states (IV, V), oxyanions and oxygen radical take place  that have serious health issues on biota. Along chromium tanning industrial waste also contain some other heavy metals like (Fe, Zn and Cu) that have adverse effect on ecosystem. Hence, it is absolute necessity of time to developed integrated and  novel technology to recycle chromium and other heavy metals before discharge to environment.

data.projectName: Assessment of underwater biodiversity with reference to corals and their sustainable use for the promotion of ecotourism in coastal areas of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Corals are diverse group of organisms belonging to phylum Cnidaria which produce calcium carbonate. Corals grow in size and form reefs. Besides other benefits, they are an important source of ecotourism and play a vital role in strengthening the economy of the state. Overall, US$36 billion is contributed annually to word economy alone by reef tourism. Currently, global warming and ocean acidification caused by industrialization are major threats to reef system. Pakistan has a long coast line. Unfortunately, marine studies in Pakistan are mainly confined to intertidal areas. With few exceptions, no data is available on corals distribution in Pakistan waters. Present study is designed to record corals distribution, environmental conditions, conservation and their sustainable use for promotion of ecotourism in the coastal areas of Pakistan.  The targets will be achieved through diving at coral sites, recording of visual data and photography of general habitat and species. Physical parameter such as temperature, salinity, depth, etc. will be recorded for each diving site. Water samples will be collected from within and outside the corals habitat to assess physico-chemical quality of sea water. Local coastal communities and other stake holders will be involved for conservation. Electronic and print media will be involved to highlight corals significance in general public and also for the promotion of sustainable ecotourism. The benefit of the proposed research not only includes more obvious concerns, but it will also indirectly provide opportunity to develop research and education, sports and tourism and many other similar benefits. The outcomes of the research will also help in developing conservation strategies and future coastal zone management plans.
