data.projectName: Fabrication of PEGylated Nanocarriers for the Improvement in Therapeutic Efficacy of Anticancerous Drugs: A Technological Revolution for New Generation of Therapeutics
data.projectDigest: Despite the advances in science and technology, medical science has been facing several challenges in the target delivery of therapeutics. Polymeric drug nanocarriers have emerged as a technological revolution and powerful tool to improve the therapeutic efficacy of antimicrobial/anticancerous drugs. In order to enhance their persistence in blood circulation, there is a need to modify the physicochemical properties of the nanocarriers. Keeping all the considerations in view, the current study is hypothesize that the PEGylation of nanocarriers that are active against cancerous cells and non-cytotoxic to normal body cells might resulted in the development of  improved drug delivery. To achieve this goal the aim of the study is to fabricate and characterize a PEGylated nanocarriers for the improve competence of antimicrobials/anticancerous drugs ex vivo. Different antimicrobial compounds will screen for their non-cytotoxic and anticancerous effect on normal and cancer cell lines, respectively. These compounds will be PEGylated using polyethylene glycol as polymeric agent. The PEGylated nanocarriers will be characterized using UV visible spectroscopy, electron microscopy, dynamic light scattering and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy. Therapeutic efficiency of PEGylated and non-PEGylated nanocarriers will be compared. This fabricated new generation of therapeutics will resolve the darkest avenue of medical and clinical sciences.

data.projectName: Development and Evaluation of Mode Choice Models for Mobility-as-a-Service Solutions
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Sharif University of Engineering & Technology, Multan, Punjab, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: In order to address the challenge of transportation issues e.g. emissions, congestion, urban mobility etc., it is necessary to improve the conditions for sustainable travel through development of vehicle technology and infrastructure but changes in people's travel behavior are also necessary in order to reduce private car dependency and the share of trips made with fossil - fueled vehicles.  Several types of interventions have been implemented to encourage individuals to shift their travel behavior, primarily from driving their private car to more sustainable alternatives including public transport (PT). A different approach involves making structural changes to the transport system in order to increase the availability and quality of alternative transport options, such as the introduction of car sharing schemes and multimodal solutions. Most recently, the concept described as Mobility as a Service or MaaS, i.e. a mobility distribution model has been proposed as feasible way forward. The key concept behind MaaS is to place the road users at the core of transport services, offering them mobility solutions based on their individual needs. This can be achieved by providing a single platform for combining all mobility options and presenting them to the customer in a simple and integrated manner. MaaS has the potential to fundamentally change the behaviour of people and reduce reliance on car ownership by providing easy on-demand access to a range of mobility options. There is a need to develop mode choice model that individual or group of individuals make in selecting the conventional transportation modes and MaaS option in order to predict and project shares of trips attracted to MaaS option.

data.projectDigest:
Educating community, teachers and caregivers about psychosocial issues of children is imperative. Since staff at Institutionalized Care (IC) are the main caregivers of children, their understanding and perception of children’s problems and behaviors is vital. Based on the gaps identified in the literature discussed above, the proposed study aims to conduct a detailed assessment of wellbeing and screening of psychological, emotional and social problem behaviors of adolescents living at in ICs running by the Government of Punjab Social Welfare Department. data.projectName: Development of CAD system for breast cancer diagnosis
data.projectDigest: Breast cancer is considered to be one of the most commonly diagnosed cancer among women. Unfortunately, the actual cause of this cancer is unknown. The only way to be save from the severe effect of this cancer is the early diagnosis so that the cancer can be effectively treated at early stages. The purpose of the proposed research is to come up with solutions for breast cancer diagnosis which can be implemented in hospitals to assist radiologists and doctors in early stage cancer diagnosis (by developing a Computer Aided Diagnosis (CADx) system). Such a CADx system can be helpful for doctors/radiologists to verify the outcome of their assessment.  The primary goal of our research will be  to develop CADx tools for the detection and classification of specific abnormalities using multiple types of databases to prove their validity. The proposed work is expected to ultimately help in saving women's lives and reduce healthcare costs.

data.projectName: Effect of Clinostating on Gene Expression of Nicotiana benthamiana Callus Cultures
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest:
Gravity is an important environmental factor affecting plant growth and development. The 3D clinostats are a valuable device as weightlessness simulators and provide an opportunity for experimentation in a simulated gravity-free space environment (Hoson, 1997; Wang, 2006). Dedolph and Dipert explained the physics of gravity insignificance by clinostat rotation (1971). It is known that gravity is not only perceived by specialized cells but also by undifferentiated cultured cells (Babbick, 2007; Fengler, 2015). Number of studies have shown that the exposure of callus cells to clinostat rotation alters gene expression (Centis-Aubay, 2003; Yoshioka, 2003). Kordyum and Chapman (2017) have also suggested a change in gene expression under simulated microgravity in ground-based experiments. Gene expression profiling has been used in the past to highlight the up/down-regulated genes for identification of the molecular signatures of the calli regeneration from explants (Ping, 2006).

The proposed study suggests exposure of the Nicotiana benthamiana callus cultures to clinostat rotation followed by the comparison of the up/down regulation of genes with those of stationary control. This research has the potential to open new research avenues. The clinostat will be indigenously developed by the sectoral collaborator SUPARCO.

data.projectName: Economic valuation of Dir-Kohistan Forest Ecosystem, Dir Kohistan Forest Division, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Dir-Kohistan Forest Ecosystem (DKFE), Upper Dir District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, is a temperate forest zone. DKFE inhabits rich fauna and flora having economic value for local and distant populations. This study is aimed to provide baseline data and valuate the good and services of DKFE. For that purpose, various marketed and non market valuation techniques will be applied to measure goods and services produced by DKFE. Water and soil of the study areas will be analyzed for geochemical characteristics using the atomic absorptionspectrometry (AAS) and inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). Findings will be compared with the national and international guidelines values and will be evaluated for the potential risk.
These goods and services are competitive with each other beyond certain level, which benefit various stakeholders differently. The local population, including local and indigenous people, is extremely poor and highly dependent on forest resources. The forest policy/management mainly focused on only commercial exploitation of timber. There is an urgent need to frame proper policy, strategy and programme for obtaining optimum economic benefits with social equity and ecological sustainability from DKFE and its realistic incorporation in National Accounts. This would require economic (monetary) valuation of DKFE which is missing so for. Natural resources in the form of biodiversity and ecosystem services are limited and need to be valued. This study is intended to address this problem.

data.projectName: deforestation
data.projectDigest: More than 70% of the land area of Pakistan experiences arid to semi-arid climatic conditions which make us vulnerable to drought hazards and water scarcity. The recent few decades have witnessed a substantial depletion of water resources throughout the country. The ground water table has gone deep and the river feeding reserves are depleted. The present research project is a proposed step towards the scientific assessment of the degradation of water reserves and the underlying factors. An attempt will be made to present the dynamics of water resources through a series of case studies from both the plain and mountainous areas. Three major issues related to water scarcity will be addressed in the project including; the temporal dynamics of water resources during the past 3 to 5 decades; the coupling effect of human and natural changes on water resources; and the future of water resources in Pakistan. The project will be of help to both the policy makers and consumers. The successful completion of the project will be a great step towards bringing awareness in the public as well as the stake holders about the availability and sustainability of the very essential and precious water resources.

data.projectName: Ethno-veterinary therapeutic practices for improving the livestock performance, feeding and immunity against Goats Plague and Gastro-intestinal parasites
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Ethno-veterinary medicine, provides the traditional way of treating animal health problems as to allopathic drugs. This community based research improves the animal health and provide basic veterinary services in rural areas. It also provides the people idea about the knowledge, skills, methods, practices, and beliefs of ethno-veterinary medicine. Ethno-veterinary medicinal plants and therapeutic practices are common in Pakistan due to the diversity of plants and geographical locations. Due to the economic status, lack of sufficient and modern animal healthcare facilities people depends on these local medicines. Goats, called as poor man’s cow; producing meat and milk, cash income, many offspring in less time making them at highest population of 42 million in Pakistan. The Beetal breed; a very productive due to higher milk and meat production and immunity to the environmental and diseased conditions. But by low quality feeding, they are prone to many health issues. The hypothesis of this project is by finding the plant secondary compounds as saponins, alkaloids, etc. for boosting immunity in goats and improving digestion towards better meat production/ performance. The main health issues currently are Gastrointestinal worms and Peste des Petits Ruminants. This study will be document the local knowledge through questionnaire about plant usage, dosage. These plants will be be preserved and identified by taxonomist. Certain biochemical profiling (Polish inst. of soil sciences and Plant nutrition), methane mitigation (Uni. of Sao Paulo), Microbiological / pathological /in-vitro assays for diseases / digestibility, GIT worm’s infestation and carcass parameters will be conducted at UAAR-Rawalpindi, Uni. of Agriculture Peshawer.

data.projectName: Investigation on Skutterudites based thermoelectric materials
data.projectDigest: Thermoelectric materials (ThM’s) convert heat energy to electrical energy. The thermal energy (lost by many processes) can be efficiently used into productive applications as efficient as possible. The efficiency of conversion is estimated by Seebeck coefficient “S”, thermal conductivity “k” and absolute temperature “T”. The low thermal and high electrical conductivity is required for thermoelectric materials. Currently Bi2Te3 and PdTe are thermoelectric materials with highest efficiency but unfortunately these materials are not environment-friendly. Currently intensive research is going on for the search of stable eco-friendly and economical thermoelectric materials. The novel applications of ThM’s include biothermal batteries, automotive power generation, optoelectronic devices, solid state thermoelectric cooling and space technology. The theme of this project is to discover some novel ThM’s through density functional theory and advanced computational tools. From this theoretically justified data, implementation of successful experiments could be conducted in future to achieve aforementioned applications.

data.projectName: REAL-TIME INDOOR NAVIGATION AND INFORMATION DISSEMINATION  SYSTEM
data.projectDigest: An indoor positioning system (IPS) is a network of devices used to locate people or objects where GPS and other satellite technologies lack precision or fail entirely, such as inside multistory buildings, airports, alleys, parking garages, and underground locations. Global navigation satellite systems (GPS or GNSS) are generally not suitable to establish indoor locations, since microwaves will be attenuated and scattered by roofs, walls and other objects. IPS has broad applications in commercial, military, retail, and inventory tracking industries. Such type of system at best of our knowledge, doesn’t exist or is being used in Pakistan, especially for navigation assistance in emergency evacuation. As its application is in several domains. Therefore this project aims to build such system that can be used by military as well as commercially organizations. This system will obtain the real time location of a target such as a smartphone user, and guides a user along a certain direction or disseminate specific information corresponding to its standing position.

data.projectName: Assessing the genetic polymorphisms in oral cancer as potential early detection biomarkers in the Pakistani population
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan, oral cancer is second most commonly diagnosed cancer and leading cause of cancer related deaths. Hence, there is an urgent need to identify potential factors responsible for this disease in Pakistani population. Several risk factors like age, gender, human papilloma virus(HPV) infection, poor dental hygiene, tobacco, betel, and alcohol are important in development and progression of this cancer, but significance of genetic background cannot be ruled out. Oral cancer is polygenic disorder as several genes play crucial role in its development and spread to distant parts of body. As genetic components critically contribute to prognosis, several genes involved in inflammatory and metabolic pathways have been implicated in the initiation and metastasis of oral cancer. Single nucleotide polymorphisms(SNPs) or genetic changes at one nucleotide in genes involved in inflammatory and metabolic pathways are significant in determining the likelihood of oral cancer susceptibility. This project aims to investigate SNPs involved in crucial pathways of metabolism and inflammation through several state of the art techniques. The association of identified SNPs will be investigated with oral cancer susceptibility in Pakistani population. Through sectoral collaboration these results will be communicated to health policy making departments to consider them as biomarkers for local population.

The successful fish culture operations depend on the provision and utilization of adequate quantity of nutritionally balanced palatable feed by fish. Nutrients requirement can be fulfill by various type of food items, based on the feeding preference of the animal, price and availability (Das at al. 1991). Utilization of waste materials as fish feed ingredients not only fulfills the nutritional requirements of fish but also helps in minimizing the level of organic environmental pollution. data.projectName: Attenuating the drought stress by exogenous application of yield stabilizing agents in wheat.
data.projectDigest: Wheat (Triticum aestivum.L) is one of the major cereal crops of the country and it has an important impact on the financial system of Pakistan.  The contribution of wheat towards the GDP of Pakistan is 1.6 percent and 8.9 percent in the vale addition. Wheat production in Pakistan is about 25.195 million tons which is far lower than other advanced countries on the globe. The factors which adversely affected the wheat yield include scarcity of available water and seasonal drought. In order to lessen the drastic effects of water stress and to increase the drought tolerance, the loss of water by evaporation and transpiration must be checked without affecting other growth promoting processes. Transpiration rate can be balanced either by wrapping the canopies of the plants with film-forming or by use of anti-transpirants that regulate stomata. This is a novel approach with a great potential of improving drought tolerance in crop plants. A series of experiments will be conducted at the Department of Agronomy, University of Agriculture Faisalabad. Different types of anti-traspirants like film-forming, reflecting materials and stomata closing will be foliarly applied at seedling stage to evaluate proper dose and source of anti-transpirants. Field trails will be conducted along with the demonstration trials at farmer’s field to test the combination of best dose and source of anti-transpirants to improve drought tolerance in wheat

data.projectName: Rapid identification of multiple drug resistance T.B bacteria using surface enhanced Raman spectroscopy
data.projectDigest:
According to WHO, Pakistan is ranked fifth among high TB burden countries worldwide because 510000 new normal TB and 15000 MDR TB cases are emerging each year therefore it accounts for 61% of the TB burden in the WHO Eastern Mediterranean Region list. Modern day practice for identification of TB bacteria involves (mostly blood and sputum) sample preprocess, culturing, Gram typing, and the identification of type and strain of the bacterium. The entire process takes one-four months to complete, involves the use of several pieces of instruments and is labor intensive. Therefore, the need for a fast and low cost method for the identification of TB
bacteria is obvious and pressing.
Working with the academia and health professionals (medical doctors) in Pakistan, the proposed project aims to develop the protocol for addressing this need using a nano-engineered platform/assay. During the project, we will collect samples from patients mainly of rural regions of Pakistan, testing the samples using conventional methods and our platform in parallel during the process of establishing the database. Upon the establishment and validation of the database, future patients will be tested using our technology

data.projectName: Technology Development for Next Generation Fighter Aircraft (NGFA) : Aerodynamics, Stealth & Flight Stability Considerations of Chined Forebodies
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan has recently ventured in designing of Next Generation Fighter Aircraft (NGFA) and named it as “Project AZM” at Pakistan Aeronautical Complex (PAC), Kamra. There are different contemporary technologies that will be developed indigenously over the next two decades to raise the design and development capability of Pakistan. These technologies are typically of restricted / proprietary nature. Chined forebodies are specialized nose shapes that are used on advanced / contemproary fighter aircrafts and Unmanned Combat Air Vehicles (UCAVs). 
In this research endeavor, an aerodynamic & Radar Cross Section (RCS) coupled design optimization framework will be developed.  The optimized shapes will be evaluated for high angle of attack dynamic behavior and for limit cycle oscillations (LCO) in the roll mode. Suppression / Control of LCO will be explored through opposing jets. 
All the results / findings / trained human resource will become a direct input to aviation industry. The complete project will be executed in close collaboration / cooperation / partnership with Project AZM, Pakistan Aeronautical Complex, Kamra commonly dubbed as Aviation City.

data.projectName: Ion Beam Irradiation of One Dimensional Nanostructured Materials for Optoelectronic Applications
data.projectDigest: In this research work, we will irradiate different ions (light ions (e.g., proton and helium) and heavy ions (e.g., copper, carbon etc.)) with different energies (keV to MeV) and substrate temperatures to investigate ion irradiation-induced defects and characterize respective changes in physical properties of Nanowires (NWs), Nanorods (NRs) and Nanotubes (NTs) of metals and other 1D-nanostructures of various materials (e.g., semiconductor, metal oxides etc.) for applications in nanodevices. We will employ ion beam irradiation-induced nanoscale welding approach to weld individual NWs/NRs/NTs of metals or semiconductors and other 1D nanomaterial using suitable ions and substrate temperature for diverse applications. In addition, we will try to fabricate large-scale metal nanowires (MNWs) networks using different inexpensive methods such as spray coating, spin coating etc and will irradiate these MNWs networks with different ions to get large-scale welded networks.

data.projectName: Behavioral studies of important insects of crops in response to volatile plants compounds emissions under different environmental pollutants
data.projectDigest: Since the last century, industrialization, climate change and other anthropogenic sources lead to an increase in global temperature, CO2 and ozone concentrations at ground level.  Volatile plants compounds (VPC) emit  in response to altered environmental conditions that have dual functions i) VPC emission protect plants from stresses ii) insects and pests attract by the odor of these VPC emission and  damage both the crops and tree plants. Because combinations of altered environmental conditions have been shown to act in unpredictable manner and the general expectations are that the increased and/or decreased levels of ozone, CO2 and temperature tend to change the emissions of plant volatile compounds (VPC). Here, for the very first time, we want to investigate different temperature, CO2 and ozone concentrations on VPC genes and metabolites as well as insect attraction or repletion under different VPC emissions from Maize, Poplar and Oak plants. These objectives will be achieved by: i) quantifying the different VPC under different environmental conditions; ii) characterizing transcriptomic profiles of genes and key enzyme activities of VPC biosynthetic pathways in plants; iii) assessing the plants photosynthetic and gas exchange activities iv) study the insects attraction and / or repletion towards VPC that will produce from plants in response to altered environmental conditions

data.projectName: School Improvement in Multi-grade Situation. Capacity building of Teachers and Schools with Multi-grade Setting
data.projectDigest: Primary school of public sector in the rural Sindh are characterized by multi-grade situation where one teachers teaches more than one levels at a time. Since the teachers teaching in this situation lack training on handling multi-grade classes, student achievement in these schools has been desperately low. In this background, this research proposes a plan to support the teachers and schools having multi-grade situation in District Sukkur, Sindh. The intervention will consist of four  main phases. Firstly, the existing situation of the schools having multi-grade setting will be analyzed to collect baseline data on these schools and teachers as well as the challenges teachers face while teaching in these classes. During the second stage, based on the outcomes of the situational analysis, training on multi-grade teaching will be conducted for the teachers who will be provided with ideas and skills to engage students of multi-grade classes in meaningful learning activities.  In the third stage, the project schools will be provided with school based support in implementing the concept of multi-teaching. Some required resources such as learning materials, mats, stationery and so on will also be provided to these projects schools. The last phase will consist of project evaluation, dissemination and policy dialogue.

data.projectName: Lignocelluloses Fibers based Flexible and High Absorbing Metal Oxide Photoanodes for Hybrid Energy Storage/Conversion Applications for Development of Smart Windows to Reduce Electricity Cost
data.projectDigest:
Photoanode materials are one of the most effective materials that are used in dye-sensitized solar cell (DSSC) for green and renewable energy storage and energy conversion applications. 
For this purpose metal oxides are better than the conventional photoanodic materials because of the absence of the corrosive effect of light illumination. Photoanode metal oxides having higher band gap energy appear to be most appropriate materials in Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells (DSSCs) and batteries. Synthesis of zinc oxide (ZnO), titanium dioxide (TiO2), tin oxide (SnO?), ZnO/SnO? and TiO2/ SnO? photoanode films on flexible substrate/binders via fast microwave assisted method, which will help to incorporate flexibility and eco-friendly aspects for the energy storage and energy conversion applications. Lignocelluloses fibers are considered as abundant, environmentally safe and flexible substrate/binders for the deposition of metal based nanostructures for high-tech applications in energy storage and energy conversion devices.Various characterization techniques will be employed to observe morphology, surface area and to find charge storage capability. In the era of modern disposable and flexible technology, the proposed work is an attempt to employ green substrates/binders for metal oxide photoanode films to decrease the photo corrosion effect and to make them environmentally safe. Highly efficient  and  cost effective microwave-assisted method will be employed to synthesize photoanode based on ZnO, TiO2, SnO2, ZnO/SnO? and TiO2/ SnO? nanostructures for DSSC that have potential applications in smart windows.

data.projectName: Design of Modern Agricultural Microgrids with Adaptable Load Management for sustainable and social growth in Islanded Rural Areas of Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Islanded microgrids have served the purpose of providing power to islanded areas while utilizing own generation, transmission and load systems. Successful implementation of microgrids in the rural areas has shown the great potential and has been utilized as a source of lifeline to the unconnected potential areas. 
The theme of this project is to provide uninterrupted power to the remote islanded areas that can serve as useable lands for cultivation and agricultural needs.  The idea is to design and develop the multipurpose agricultural microgrid that encompasses the technical and social needs of the areas by providing uninterrupted power using Adaptable Load Management using Deep learning algorithm. The objective is to identify the key performance parameters of the islanded agricultural microgrids while providing power to the agricultural and domestic loads hence empowering the social and agricultural needs.
The proposed system will use adaptive load utilization algorithm while using a single source onto domestic as well as agricultural load utilization.
The artificial intelligence algorithm will be applied for efficient and appropriate power distribution to load based on the available information. The sensory data of weather conditions, domestic load utility and agricultural needs will be mathematically modeled and simulated.

data.projectName: Putting Health Care, systems and Research together: A community-based Approach.
data.projectDigest:
Punjab has a very vibrant healthcare system which comprises of public and private stake holders. Despite the extensive network of health care facilities, health status of the people of the province is still below the desired level. With high Infant mortality contributed mainly by the Neonatal mortality, the Nutritional status needs improvement. Environment and Awareness of the population to preventive diseases deserves special mention. 
Moreover, Health care providers have a little exposure to the actual living conditions and the problem faced by the populations, ranging from awareness to timely health seeking. Community-based approach will be able to not only train the health care providers but also provide them with an insight into the researchable issues highlighting the health of the populations, scientific evidence/s (data based) leading to policy changes. Using a Longitudinal study design, the objectives are to conduct a baseline survey describing the characteristics of the identified communities and develop and assess the impact of various interventions in the areas of Maternal and Child Health, Nutrition, Health Systems, economic impacts etc., providing evidence for policy strategies and advice for the policy makers to improve the health of the communities, train academics and make better policies.

data.projectName: Design and implementation of power converters for DC and AC microgrids
data.projectDigest: The high energy cost and limited resources to construct large power plants and centralized power system are main constraints to cater the growing energy demand. In order to meet future energy demand, a flexible, configurable and informative energy system in low voltage distribution networks is mandatory.  As a result, micro-grids are emerging with the integration of renewable based distributed generation (DG) units. The DG units provide a relief to stressed conventional power distribution and transmission network. The micro-grid (MG) has the capability to optimize the utilization of renewable energy resources more efficiently. The major focus of this research proposal is the development and implementation of an application based multi-port power converters and inverter topologies for efficient energy harvest and dispatch through renewable sources. These multiple-port converter are used to interface various sources and loads in micro-grids. The designed converters will have higher energy efficiency, high power density and compact size. Modern control schemes such as modular predictive control (MPC) will be implemented  for an optimized feedback operation to cater for the stochastic nature of the renewable resources

data.projectName: "Association of Vitamin D receptor genetic variants with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease and their influence on efficacy of Vitamin D supplements for suppressing the disease's symptoms”
data.projectDigest: COPD is progressive, airflow limitation. Most often physicians have difficulty in distinguishing asthma, emphysema, COPD as  most of their symptoms are overlapping therefore one face difficulty in its diagnostics and management strategies . Pakistan is one of highly populated country among South east Asia . Due to increase in urbanization trend there is ultimate increased exposure to pollutants like smog and allergens which lead to rise in percentage of chronic airways inflammation diseases . Prevalence of COPD in Pakistan is higher than other neighboring countries i.e., 13.8% . This may be even more high due to misdiagnosis of COPD as Asthma in Pakistan. Besides environmental affect there are many generic factors that are also involved in development of COPD. It is a common trend among medical practitioners to prescribe Vitamin D supplements to COPD patients owing its immunity boosting properties. But this therapy has been non effective in majority of the patients. This case control association study is designed to look for the SNP variants within and around Vitamin D Receptor (that is essential for its absorption) gene that associate with COPD . Also, identification of potential VDR SNP variants and patients’ subgroups based upon these genetic profiles may lead not only to proper diagnosis whether patient has COPD or not but also will be helpful to categorize whether he/ she might respond to Vitamin D therapy or not. This may lead to improved management of this underdiagnosed disease in our country. Thus, quality of life of patients will improve owing early diagnosis of the disease leading to accurate personalized treatment plan.

data.projectName: CHANGING STATUS OF WOMEN'S EDUCATION AND ITS IMPACT ON WOMEN'S DECISION-MAKING POWER IN KHYBER PAKHTUNKHWA
data.piUniversity: University of Malakand, Chakdara, Dir, Malakand
data.projectDigest: Gender and development has always been the major concern of modern world, which is prevalent throughout the globe in one shape or the other. Women in traditional structures are supposed to be marginalized and susceptible in the cultural domain living miserable and dependent lives. Decision-making almost in all spheres of life such as education, employment, property / inheritance, and mate selection are solely dominated by men in traditional social structures where women's status confronts negligence and dependence. Pakistan ranks low in overall education, among other developmental indexes. Women’s education being the issue that has been debated the most in Pakistani context, fruitful results are, however yet to be achieved. The idea is supposed to be materialized by initiating a two-fold process. Firstly, grass-root level checks of women educational impediments and secondly evolving a local/regional educational strategy or plan, which ensures bringing women into the stream of higher education and decisional empowerment. The project is supposed to be theoretically inquisitive and curative in nature, aiming at locating and identifying the local potential hindrances that block women in their way to higher education and obstruct their decisional independence. A wide array of empirical efforts and tools are supposed to be employed to draw a realistic picture of the local scenario. Observation techniques, Interview guides, Questionnaires, FGDs, would be applied to extract the required data for further analysis. In addition, the project would be characterized as “curative”, that will encompass a workable local educational plan or strategy is supposed to be formulated based on the empirical investigations.

data.projectName: Designing and nutritional evaluation of cheese stick for malnourished children
data.projectDigest: Malnutrition is one of the world's most serious but least-addressed development challenges National Nutritional Survey Pakistan 2018 provided alarming statistics about children under 5 years; 4 out of 10 children stunted, 17.7% wasted, 28.9% underweight and 9.5% are overweight (NNS, 2018). Nutritious foods are needed by toddlers and children for the growth and development of their body. Their food must be rich in macronutrients (carbohydrates, fats and proteins) and micronutrients (vitamins and minerals). Unfortunately, there are limited options available for children. Therefore, they are buying only junk food and unhealthy snack that is deficient in nutrients and contains only empty calories leading to nutritional insufficiencies. Cheese is a rich source of energy, macro (proteins and fats) and micronutrients (calcium, zinc, vitamin A and D) needed for the growth and development of the children in their growing age. Present project is designed with the objective to develop cheese sticks: a super healthy snack as dietary intervention for malnourished children. Development of cheese sticks will definitely help to reduce malnutrition.  Efficacy trial of the selected product will be carried out in children to assess potential of cheese sticks in mitigation malnutrition. Reduction in malnutrition will result in improved cognitive function, enhanced immunity.

data.projectName: Waste water treatment: an ultimate solution to combat water shortage for irrigation under climate change
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest:
Due to water scarcity challenges around the world, it is essential to think about non-conventional water resources to address the increased demand in clean freshwater. Environmental and public health problems may result from insufficient provision of sanitation and wastewater disposal facilities. Because of this, wastewater treatment and recycling methods will be vital to provide sufficient freshwater in the coming decades, since water resources are limited and more than 70% of water are consumed for irrigation purposes. Therefore, the application of treated wastewater for agricultural irrigation has much potential. 
In Pakistan, only 1% of wastewater is treated by industries before being discharged directly into rivers and drains. Multan is the fifth largest city of Pakistan in producing wastewater (66 × 106 m3) annually and its receiving water bodies include river Chenab, irrigation canal, and agricultural land, causing significant health and economic risks. The proposed study will be construction of wetland for the treatment of waste water for its reuse in agriculture sector. After treatment, wastewater can substitute for freshwater and contribute significantly in irrigation to address the global water deficit. This research will help in finding an economical way of treating wastewater and identifying the potential constituents of CW suitable in local conditions.

data.projectName: Implementing automated AI pipeline through a GUI for early detection of leukemia sub-types using CBC reports
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Leukemia is a type of cancer that originates in the bone marrow and causes abnormal proliferation of white blood cells, red blood cells and platelets which results in  various infections, anaemia and bleeding as well [1].In leukemia the normal differentiation pathway is blocked, and most cells do not move on to terminal differentiation [2], [3] . Now a days Computer aided diagnosis systems have also been designed to predict various diseases including cancer [4]. 
Leukemia is a clonal proliferation of hematopoietic stem cells in the bone marrow. The four broad subtypes are acute lymphocytic, acute myeloid, chronic lymphocytic, and chronic myeloid leukemia. Acute lymphocytic leukemia occurs more often in children, whereas the other subtypes are more common in adults [4].  The basic and modest investigation test which can signify this disease is complete blood count (CBC) that measures the quantity of all the different types of cells in the blood. Digital image processing on the blood samples in detail  has already been done but CBC specific has yet to be carried out. To predict the disease at early stage an Artificial Intelligence (AI) prediction model based on Complete Blood Count (CBC) test is required which gives information about all the circulating cells in the blood like RBC, WBC, hemoglobin, hematocrit, lymphocytes, eosinophils, basophils, neutrophils and platelet count. This process creates a baseline that can be used for assessment with future test results. [8].

data.projectName: Synthesis of novel Schiff based metal complexes and evaluation of their biological potential using green chemistry approach.
data.piUniversity: Women University of Azad Jammu and Kashmir Bagh
data.projectDigest: Green Chemistry is a new chemistry starts from late 1990s in order to provide pollution free methods to protect the environment. Green chemistry revolutionized many fields of chemistry but this encouraged organic chemist especially those who were focusing their work to synthesize organic compounds. As many organic compounds have been synthesized through green approach in order to get rid of conventional or petrochemical solvents and chemicals which were giving low yield and consume lot of energy and time. From many years Schiff bases play a vital role as chelating ligands with a large variety of metal ions in inorganic chemistry. Schiff base metal complexes help in understanding complex chemical reactions. Due to their excellent importance for specific metal ions as inorganic ions, a large variety of Schiff bases are used as cation carriers in potentiometric sensors, also show catalytic activity in the hydrogenation of olefins.

data.projectName: DEVELOPMENT OF ANTENNA SENSOR SYSTEM FOR DETECTION OF EXPLOSIVE GASES
data.projectDigest:
We, as a nation, are fighting with terrorism since last two decades, and bomb blasts are triggered time to time costing precious lives of our people. To save these precious lives, a proper system is required to detect, report, and monitor presence of any explosive material well in time.  
       Recently, researchers are working on sensor antennas for different applications around the world. These include gas sensors, temperature sensors, meat sensors, fruit ripening sensors, and IED sensors. Explosive gases are sensed by IED Sensors. There are few explosive detectors in market which are heavy, and costly to be installed on multiple sites for precise 24/7 monitoring of explosive gases in an open area or building. The relevant local security companies, like KARSAZ and others, are already contacted and they appreciated the project idea. We are looking forward to seek valuable input and support from them.
       This proposal is about the development of a low-cost prototype of antenna sensor system for detection of explosive gases. The antenna sensors comprise of an antenna with a certain type of chemical (sensitive to explosive gases) for sensing applications. These chemicals are conductive in nature and include Carbon Nanotubes (CNTs), rGO (Reduced Graphene Oxide), and others. The antenna, with the chemical loaded, acts as the antenna sensor which sends a signal to the transmitter attached to it upon detection of explosive gas. The transmitter sends the signal to a loud buzzer which informs about the presence of explosive gases. Also, a GSM Module will send a text for attention to security personnel upon detection. The academic collaborator will help us in measurement of radiation pattern of the sensor for publication in peer reviewed reputed journal.

data.projectName: Optimization of  performance of the parabolic dish receiver system by providing a constant heat flux to heat transfer fluid
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
This research proposal aims to design and develop a pilot research facility at NED University to investigate the performance of the series of high-efficient heat collection systems integrated with the solar parabolic dish-receiver system. The parabolic dish/engine system (PDS) is a concentrating solar power (CSP) technology that produces smaller amounts of electricity than other CSP technologies typically in the range of 3 to 25 kilowatts, but is beneficial for modular use.
Solar energy received at the receiver is basically transient in nature. Due to this transient behavior, the solar energy received at the cavity receiver is inconsistent. The cavity receiver needs the semi-constant temperatures on their walls; however inconsistency in the solar radiation decreases the performance of PDS.
The main purpose of this research is to enhance the performance of PDS by introducing a system that can provide the uniform heat flux to the Heat transfer flow (HTF). data.projectName: Dengue Vector's transcriptome response to green nanoparticles
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: There is a significant surge in vector borne disease spread worldwide, estimating at 17% of total disease burden, mosquito-borne infectious diseases share highest number. Mosquitoes are known to be a potent vector in the spread of various diseases like malaria, chikungunya, yellow fever and dengue. Dengue is a lethal disease caused by dengue virus and vector is Aedes aegypti. As per WHO guidelines, developing a comprehensive response plan is a necessity to tackle the spread. One of the main responses is the vector surveillance and control activities by using different insecticides, however, mosquitoes are emerging as insecticide resistance. Many plants have been tested as sources of either insect repellents or control measures. To overcome the increasing prevalence of dengue, green synthesized silver nanoparticles may offer a potent measure for vector control. Less efforts have been made to understand the short-term transcriptome response of mosquitoes to insecticides. Here transcriptome analysis of larvae exposed to these green AgNPs will be performed. The transcriptome analysis of vectors will help in identification of genetic alterations because of green AgNPs. Understanding of cross responses of mosquitoes to green AgNPs and insecticides at the whole transcriptome level may ultimately lead to improvements in vector control strategies.

data.projectDigest:
The farming of catfish is important to many large producing countries that it provides a source of income, creates employment opportunities, contributes towards Gross Domestic Product (GDP), fetches higher price than tilapia due to the fact that it can be sold live at the market. Of highest importance in addressing food insecurities, it provides animal protein to the consumer and has lower cholesterol content. Characteristics of catfish that makes it ideal for farming include;
•	It grows fast and feeds on a large variety of agricultural by-products
•	It is hardy and tolerates adverse water quality conditions
•	It can be raised in high densities, resulting in high net yields
•	It attains higher price than carps and other catfish in other countries and can be sold live at the market
•	It matures and relatively easily reproduces in captivity
•	It requires less space, time, money and has a higher feed conserving rate

data.projectName: Introgression of heat and drought stress tolerance in cotton under climate change scenario
data.projectDigest: Climate change is a global issue and its main target is agriculture. Increase in temperature coupled with drought and erratic rainfalls affect agriculture severely. In 2018-19, national production of cotton was less than 31% than the target. Similarly, available irrigation was 18% less than the average yearly available water. Cotton is the most important cash crop of Pakistan and is lifeline of national exports, but due to climate change effects especially drought and heat stress its production is decreasing at national levels. Existing cotton cultivars are not performing well in climate change scenario, which has resulted in production losses. Therefore, major objective of this project is to investigate the real mechanism behind the heat and drought stress tolerance and to find the inheritance pattern of that mechanism which will help to introgress the heat and drought tolerance related traits/genes into high yielding cotton cultivars or to develop such a cultivar which will be best suited to climate change conditions. For this purpose, we will collect germplasm including inter-specific derived hybrids/genotypes from all over the country, representative for all cotton growing regions. This germplasm will be evaluated for yield and quality related traits for heat and drought stress simultaneously. To understand the tolerance mechanism data will be collected for physiological and biochemical traits and their association with yield and related traits will be analyzed. Genotypes will also be characterized with functional markers associated with heat and drought stress genes.    This information will be made available to the breeders by arranging national level seminars and to farmers invited in the seminar by guiding them for genotypes best adopted to the climate change.

data.projectName: Smart Contracts: Investigating Block Chain Technology for the Improvement in Trade Processes
data.projectDigest: The rapid changes in technology has changed the way businesses operate. It is noticed that a suitable adoption of technology may improve efficiency and effectiveness of the business operations. As trade significantly contributes the economy and has greatly affected by the technological advancement. Its tedious and lengthy procedures hinder the smooth flow of trade across borders. Therefore it is important for the countries to pay more attention on it. In order to have convenience in the trading process, companies can gain advantage by using cyber technology. Block chain, one of the cyber technology that records transaction between distinct parties. It has unique features like immutability, decentralization, security, time-stamped. Smart contracts, one of the feature of BCT, is able to facilitate trade process based on block chain environment through contract terms and agreement between parties. Therefore, in this project, we aim to understand the complexities and improve the efficiency of the trade process through the Smart Contracts of Block Chain technology.

data.projectName: Molecular Characterization of sunflower germplasm and development of disease resistant sunflower  (Helianthus annuus L.) hybrids
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is an edible oil deficient country which imports large amount of Malaysian Palm and Sunflower oil to meet its domestic edible oil demand. Therefore, enhancement of its domestic production is the key to attain self sufficiency and save the import budget of the country.  Sunflower is an important oilseed crop of masses which supplies 10% of the total global oil seed production. Development of indigenous hybrids is an important step for the availability of cost effective hybrid seed and high yielding hybrids seed. However, global climate change may evolve new races of the disease. Selection of diverse germplasm which is also resistant to various diseases may help to develop high yielding sustainable hybrids.  Therefore, present research proposal is submitted to characterize the sunflower elite inbred lines for various genes related to cytoplasmic male sterility sources, disease resistance, and fertility restorer genes. The selected diverse inbred lines may be mated to develop sunflower hybrids. These hybrids will be tested under multi-location trials and evaluated for achene yield and oil contents. The developed hybrids may able to perform better than available hybrids. Project may benefit our local seed and oil industry.

data.projectName: Development of Bifunctional Catalytic Hydrogel blocks for Viscosity Reduction and Yield Improvement of Apple Juice
data.projectDigest: Beverage industry constitutes largest contribution in industrial zone of Pakistan. Presently thirty eight production units are operating in the country. Current research focuses on two major concerns of fruit juice industry that are juice extraction and its clarification. The aforementioned processes are usually accomplished by mechanical and chemical methods. This project involves the use of enzymes in juice clarification and extraction in place of chemical and mechanical approaches. Hydrolytic enzymes would be used to incorporate during the pulping process. They deteriorate cell structure and causes more of the cell sap to come out as a result of which more juice would be extracted. Clarification of juice plays an important role in its sale as more clear and transparent juices appeal the consumers readily. Some natural compounds present in juice bring turbidity and make it cloudy. These compounds can be degraded by using the hydrolytic enzymes and therefore juice quality can be improved. Regarding the cost and availability of enzymes, firstly, the enzymes will produce in our laboratory from bacterial species isolated from garden soil and used to treat the juice and compare with that of the high cost commercially available enzymes. Due to the facile nature of enzymes, they can be easily inactivated during the industrial process. Therefore in our project, we are also going to immobilize the enzymes in operationally stable hydrogel blocks made up of gelatin, an eco-friendly biomass. Immobilized enzymes can be reuse in the juice treatment process and the cost of enzyme production or commercial enzyme purchasing will be saved. Thus, the overall process will be economical for the industry.

data.projectName: Primed Mesenchymal Stem Cells Impregnated Biodegradable Scaffolds for worn out Cartilage Repair
data.projectDigest:
Osteoarthritis of the knee is very frequent in the aged people and is a major cause of discomfort. This disease is also linked with reduced physical activity and may affect health quality of life. Degeneration of cartilage results in substantial economic costs and health problems after retirement age. It is very common in Pakistan. Females greater than 55 years of age frequently visit tertiary care hospitals due to knee osteoarthritis in Pakistan. Total knee replacement and other surgical procedures are used worldwide but results are not promising. Total knee replacements costs are high and the procedure is often not successful. As of now there is no radical treatment available to cure OA. So there is need of cell based therapies for cartilage
regeneration of damaged knee. Mesenchymal stem cells therapy can play a major role in treatment of osteoarthritis. Mesenchymal stem cells transplantation strategy needs a support system for better growth and regeneration potential. Antioxidant preconditioning of cells and use of scaffold as carrier shows better homing of transplanted cells which enhance regeneration of injured tissue. This study will use natural sources for development of scaffolds. Silk fibres will be used as supporting matrix for stem cells growth and regeneration of osteoarthritic damaged cartilage in animal model. In future, this scaffolds based therapy may benefit patients with osteoarthritis and can improve their life.

data.projectName: Elucidating the Molecular Basis of Maturity Onset Diabetes of the Young  (MODY) in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Maturity onset diabetes of the young (MODY) is a genetic disease transmitted in an autosomal dominant manner affecting 1–6% of pediatric cases of diabetes. The MODY usually appears before 25 years of age and misdiagnosed as type-I or type II. It is estimated that there are 1-5% of MODY cases among all diabetic cases. As reported by International Diabetes Federation (IDF), there are 7 million diabetic people in Pakistan and therefore 70,000-140,000 MODY patients are expected. To date there are 14 different genes as a causative of MODY. Mutations in GCK, HNF1?, HNF4?, and HNF1? are the most frequently identified etiologies of MODY.  Frequencies of these etiologies may differ among Asian and Caucasian populations.   Unidentified genes may cause MODY in Asian populations.The treatment for these types differ from type-I and type-II diabetes, therefore it is very important to diagnose MODY in our population.  This study is therefore designed to determine the frequency of common reported MODY genes in Pakistan and screen the patients for new genes involved for accurate treatment management.

data.projectName: Investigation of Transition Metal Doped ZnO Nano-Particles for Thermoelectric Application
data.projectDigest: Transition metal (TM)-doped ZnO has emerged as an attractive candidate for high temperature thermoelectric applications because it is economical, environmental friendly and it has better conversion efficiency compared to other oxides. In this project we aim to investigate the effect of transition metal ions doping on the structural and thermoelectric properties of ZnO nano-particles. For this purpose hydrothermal method will be employed to synthesize (Zn1-xYx)O with 0.00 ? Y ? 0.10 (Y = Cu, Ni, Co, Fe, Mn) nano-particles. The structural and thermoelectric properties of the synthesized materials will be characterized by X-rays diffractions and thermoelectric properties measurement system. The figure-of-merit, which is characterized by Z=S2?/?, will be estimated from the quantities such as thermal conductivity, thermoelectric power and resistivity. Our proposed research project will address fundamental problems in physics. It will also explore the industrial applications of our material.

data.projectName: Design of a low-cost battery for electric rickshaw
data.projectDigest:
Due to the inadequate public transport system, the people in Pakistan prefer to use personal vehicles for everyday commutation. Most of the vehicles in Pakistan rely on gasoline, as a result Pakistan must spend billions of USD to import crude oil. Therefore, there is a need to introduce fuel saving technologies like hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) and electric vehicles (EVs). These technologies not only shrink the export of the crude oil but also save the environment from the detrimental effects of combustion of fossil fuels. Therefore, the introduction of EV technology to the mass transit system of Pakistan can decrease the consumption of gasoline and helps to control the emission of greenhouse gases. The main components of an EV system are battery, mechanical transmission, motor and power converters.
As battery serves as a powerhouse of an EV, we propose to develop a low-cost battery for small EVs, such as an electric rickshaw, which is an integral part of the mass transit in Pakistan. This project proposes a fuel saving option for the automotive industry of Pakistan. Currently, Pakistan has to spend billions of USD to import oil for the transportation industry. Through the introduction of EV technology, dependence on gasoline can be reduced and some foreign exchange reserves can be saved.

data.projectName: Mixed-ligands palladium(II) dithiocarbamate complexes and their pharmacological applications
data.projectDigest: This project will focus on the synthesis of new Pd-base complexes with amine/dithiocarboxylate ligands. It is well-established that ligands play a major role in the activity of these complexes. Thus through judicious choice of ligands, especially those with substituents that have a secondary non-covalent contact formation capability with neighboring molecules, can modulate the properties of the complexes. Metallodrugs containing such ligands may exert their antimicrobial/antioxidant and anticancer action by interacting with DNA-bases or other cell constituents. The formation of such drug-DNA adducts will alter the structural machinery of the DNA and hinder its replication; ultimately leading to death of microbes or cancerous cells. An important aspect of this project is the comparison of antimicrobial and anticancer potency of Pd(II) complexes. In addition, cyclic voltammetry (CV), UV-visible spectroscopy, light-scattering and viscometry will be exploited to understand the strength of interaction of the complexes with DNA, and to probe their mechanism of their action.

data.projectName: GENETIC DIVERSITY OF MALARIAL PARASITE (PLASMODIUM VIVAX) AND ITS INVITRO CONTROL WITH TRADITIONALLY USED MEDICINAL PLANTS
data.piUniversity: Kohat University of Science and Technology, Kohat
data.projectDigest: Malaria is a serious community health issue of Pakistan. It causes more than 1.6 million registered cases annually. (WHO, 2012).  In Pakistan both Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium falciparum malaria exists. Vivax malaria is the most common type. Chloroquine plus Primaquine is considered to be principal treatment for Plasmodium vivax infection throughout the world including Pakistan. In Asia Sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) turn out to be more dominant treatment after chloroquine resistance in Plasmodium species. Thought P. vivax is the prevailing cause of malaria infection but it is not yet well characterized with in terms of its drug resistance to Sulphadoxinepyrimethamine and chloroquine. Drugs i.e. Chloroquine (CQ) and the antifolates sulfadoxine- pyrimethamine (SP) are the key antimalarial drugs used in this area, largely as monotherapies. information on the molecular epidemiology of antimalarial drug resistance in Pakistan is lacking. The monotherapeutic use of CQ and SP is expected to trigger drug resistance in both species. There is a variety mutant genes in plasmodium species of Pakistan specially Province Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Genetic variability of Plasmodium species leads to maltreatment of Malaria infection. Malaria infection is traditionally treated by the usage of some medicinal plants. Due to an elevated drug resistance of Plasmodium vivax the current study is designed to address the information gap by of the drug resistance-associated polymorphisms and identification of specific gene mutations of P. vivax and also to search for a new antimalarial compound using traditionally used medicinal plants which could be highly effective against drug resistance strains of Plasmodium vivax.

data.projectName: Molecular and Phylogenetic analyses of potential medicinal, edible and ectomycorrhizal fleshy poroid fungi associated with economically important forest trees of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa for accomplishing some sustainable development goals
data.piUniversity: Lahore College for Women University, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Proposed project is prepared to take step for achieving some sustainable development goals i.e., poverty alleviation, food security and climate change through screening of a specific group of fungi (Fleshy poroid mushrooms, Boletales, Basidiomycetes) by using molecular approaches. These mushrooms play key role in ecosystem as tree symbionts, food and medicinal source. Unfortunately, these mushrooms have been largely understudied in Pakistan as well as Pakistani literature regarding genomically identified edible and medicinal mushrooms is scarce despite of the fact that there is great diversity of these creatures in Himalayan moist temperate forests (typically fall in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province). Proposed project emphasize the need of such advanced molecular research for identification of mushrooms occurring in Pakistan because every year many valuable mushrooms decayed due to local people negligence about their importance. Through this project we will also be able to assess and document status i.e., threatened, rare, endangered, and common species of this group of macrofungi from selected previously unexplored areas. All sequences after molecular analysis would be made available in easily accessible GenBank database and new taxa names into Index fungorum for other researchers use. Preliminary related research has already been done during PhD research by Principal investigator.

data.projectName: Linguistic Survey of Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Proposed study is interdisciplinary in its nature and has two major facets; Firstly, it documents languages of Pakistan with their demographic reach (approximate number of their speakers) and  their geographical positioning on one hand, and their linguistic features including phonology, vowels and consonants, grammatical structures (whether they are SOV, SVO or OSV and their typology), everyday colloquial utterances and their proverbs, code switching and lexical gaps, their literary content; Prose and Poetry , their writing systems and their media exposure both in written and audio visual format on the other hand. 
Secondly, channels of perpetual propagation of underrepresented languages and their culture, through popular commercial media and social media, will be established. In the course of study youth of these language speaking communities will be apprised how to use, social media, say youtube channels for example, to disseminate their unique languages and corresponding social activities like weddings, congregations, juries(locally called JIRGAS) and funerals. With the help and supervision of nearest colleges and universities we would also determine chances to establish local community radio stations serving these communities.

data.projectName: Enhancing the economic returns of poor rural communities by introducing  modern and sustainable silkworm rearing techniques
data.projectDigest: Sericulture is an agro-based cottage industry that can help to uplift the economy of our country. Around the globe, this industry is providing employment to more than 30 million families. Despite the growing demand for natural silk, this industry could not flourish in Pakistan and facing numerous challenges such as lack of trained personnel, high mortality rate in local silk breed, and poor economic conditions of the farmers. This industry not only has significant potential to provide livelihood for rural poor families but silk proteins produced by this technology also have wide range of applications in textile, food, cosmetics and pharmaceutical industry as well as in traditional medicines. Unfortunately, this industry has not been on the list of priorities of our Government. Currently, Pakistan is importing about 70% raw silk from other countries to meet the demand of local market. The aims of this project are to record the problems being faced by the local farmers during silkworm rearing, to enhance the silk productivity by intensive laboratory experiments and quality of silk by enriching the mulberry leaves with different food supplements. Furthermore, farmers will be empowered with modern and sustainable techniques so that they may minimize the risks of diseases and rear silkworms throughout the years. Public awareness seminars and workshops will also be organized to create awareness about the potentials of sericulture industry among local communities and sensitizing the Government officials to play their role to revive sericulture industry in Pakistan. By promoting sericulture industry we can not only save millions of dollars which we spent to import raw silk but also support thousands of poor rural families by involving them in silkworm rearing activities.

data.projectName: An Expert System for Livestock Management
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan’s annual milk production is approximately 57 million tonnes, making it one of the world’s top milk producers. The two major types of marketing chain in the country are informal and formal chains, accounting for 97 and 3 percent, respectively, of total milk supply. Fresh, raw milk is the preferred consumer product in Pakistan. Lack of hygiene, mixing of various agents, and absence of cold chains are primary contributors to the low quality, adulterated milk to the consumers in Pakistan.
In order to provide stores/homes with milk/dairy products we consume, a dairy farm goes through several processes. The real processes that are actually executed in a dairy farm are different from ideal farm practices, leading to poor health of dairy cattle, low milk production, low-quality dairy production, as well as environmental damage. Through this proposal, we aim to develop an intelligent system that monitors and manages livestock and provides expert advice for producing sustainable high-quality dairy products in Pakistan. The system will identify, monitor, and improve the real processes in dairy farms while effectively using the land and water resources as guided by IoT-sensors, Artificial Intelligence, and Process Mining.

data.projectName: Spectrophotometric quantification of bioactive compounds in naturally growing and tissue culturally produced callus of medicinal plants of Cholistan deserts of Bahawalpur
data.projectDigest: It is generally considered that quantity and quality of phenolics and antioxidants not vary in naturally growing and in tissue culturally produced root shoots and undifferentiated mass of callus. It is necessary to evaluate quality and quantity of bioactive compounds in various endanger medicinal fruits, vegetables and herbs to identify preciousness of these medicinal plant species for industry. The results need to compare with assessment of phenolics and antioxidants level in tissue culturally induced callus and in situ plants growing in desert regions. The study will help in screening of good quality endanger medicinal plants based on the type and concentration of phenolics and antioxidants. Moreover, good quality bioactive compounds of herbal medicines could easily be extracted from callus instead of plant leaves. This will also cut down various laborious steps and reduce extraction cost. This study will ensure the sustainable supply of bioactive compounds to the pharmaceutical industry through continuous supply of callus material and help to conserve medicinal herbs and plants to reduce the impact of extinction from Cholistan deserts of Bahawalpur because of climate extremes, deforestation and over grazing.

data.projectName: ANALYZING WOMEN’S CONTRIBUTION IN AGRICULTURE, THEIR     LEVEL OF AWARENESS AND SCOPE FOR CAPACITY BUILDING IN KHYBER PAKHTUNKHWA, PAKISTAN
data.projectDigest: Growth and prosperity of a nation depends on the growth and development of its people. Women and men are the two main segments of society and pillars of economic growth. The project “analyzing women’s contribution in agriculture, their level of awareness and scope for capacity building in KP, Pakistan” will be initiated. Women’s contribution is almost equal to men but they are still working on their own traditional methods as they do not have easy access to information because of the rigid and conservative social norms and values. The study will find out the gaps and constraints due to which women are restricted from learning opportunities, identify the information dissemination sources and the role of government and private sector in performing extension services. Training needs of women in agriculture and livestock sectors will also be identified and recommendations will be provided to Government and private sector to help in capacity building of women farming community. Women’s contribution in agriculture and livestock sector are countless but their access to and control over resources is limited. This study will find out the level of women participation in decision making and their access and control over the resources relevant to agriculture and livestock.

data.projectName: Facilitating CPEC based Entrepreneurial Opportunity Recognition for Socioeconomic Development in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: China–Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) is a collection of infrastructure projects, which is generating opportunities by knocking the doors of businesspersons across Pakistan. The entrepreneurs are agents which can connect SMEs with CPEC, however, unfortunately the SMEs are not able to strongly link with the CPEC and its prospects because the SMEs has its own challenges and certain limitations. Therefore, there is an urgent need to find ways for creating favourable business environment for the SMEs by overcoming prevalent challenges. Moreover, there is a need for development of mechanism through which the local entrepreneurs who can comprehend the CPEC needs and opportunities and fulfil these needs through active SMEs. This will be sequential mixed-mode research focusing on opportunity recognition and on the identification and use of effective entrepreneurial capital for an entrepreneurial class development through SMEs. Data will be collected and analyzed in three stages, i.e., stage one will be about systematic review of literature on construct of study, in stage two will be about expert review and stage three will be about theoretical validation through real time data. This research project will carry multifold significance and benefits at individual, institutional and policy levels.

data.projectName: Promotion of Non-Neutral Plasma Modeling and Simulations Research
data.projectDigest:
The proposed research plan is Promotion of Non-Neutral Plasma Modeling and Simulations Research at Department of Physics of Hazara University Mansehra. Non-Neutral Plasma experts and facilities not available in Pakistan. The objective is students training and devising good lab assignments for research students to understand the frontier problems in the following:
1.	To study weakly ionized processing plasmas will use commercially available Particle-In-Cell (PIC) code with a Monte Carlo Collision (MCC) package. The MCC package models the collisions between charged and neutral particles, which are needed to obtain a self-sustained plasma and the proper electron and ion energy loss mechanisms. Monte Carlo collision will investigate under different pressure using different back ground gases, e.g. H, Li, He, Ne, Ar, Xe, etc.
2.	To investigate non-neutral plasma heating mechanism through various radio frequency (MHz and GHz) and power level. Also, to elaborate the relation between energy and energy distribution in different confinement geometry. 
3.	To analyze plasma-wall interactions and impurity accumulation as well as the impurity behavior at ultra-high vacuum condition to determine the impurity behavior in the different topological configuration in confinement devices. 
4.	To analyze systematically the pure electron and ion plasma in various approach of Electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH) in ELTRAP. The produced single component plasmas which may will be caused by the heating mechanism, density and temperature profiles and underlying atomic and molecular processes. 
5.	To explore energy and energy distribution at various parameters and geometry of confinement device expected to be a vital and productive area in fusion plasma physics research for foreseeable future

data.projectName: Redox properties of Bromide/Bromine system for multipurpose applications: An Eelectrochemical Investigation
data.projectDigest: The electrochemical behavior of Br?/Br2 redox system is extensively investigated because of its significance in many fields of research which includes redox flow battery (RFB) for energy storage, dye synthesized solar cell (DSSC) technology, and selective electro-organic synthesis. Beside these applications, the reactions of bromine atom free radical, Br? (generated electrochemically as a result of bromide oxidation) with biologically important compounds such as amino acid DNA basis, and sugar are also studied. In our previous studies, Br? was generated from bromide ion oxidation and its reactions with Biochemical such as glycine, cytosine, and thymine were studied. More recently, our group has also investigated bromide electrooxidation in organic aprotic-protic mixed media. The present project proposal envisages: the electrooxidation of bromide at liquid-liquid interface (i.e. in binary immiscible solvents), at solid-liquid interface (i.e. at DNA and biomolecule modified electrode in aqueous and non-aqueous solvents), and in  room temperature ionic liquids (RTILs) for it potential applications in selective electro organic synthesis, cancer therapy, and utilizing it as mediator in DSSC technology and flow batteries. data.projectDigest:
Technological advancements in oil and gas exploration have led to discoveries in the past 20 years of new natural gas resources. No major new traditional hydrocarbon reserves are discovered in Pakistan in recent past. Discovery of new hydrocarbon resources are necessary to meet energy demands for a growing population. An important source of gas is tight, organic-rich black shale and mud stone. In these shales, the rock acts as the source, reservoir and trap for the hydrocarbons, although most shales have lost some of their total hydrocarbons (i.e. migration of liquid/gas out of the host rock). However, part of the generated hydrocarbon remains in these organic-rich shales because their porosity is high but permeability is low. The production and utilization of shale gas in North America over the last 20 years has great bearing on the oil and gas industry. However, outside the North America, these unconventional plays remain largely untapped. Pakistan is listed among top 10 countries of the world for its shale gas potential measured around 330 Trillion Cubic Feet (TCF) of gas in place out of which 105 TCF is technically recoverable as per EIA, 2013-14 report. But unfortunately no shale gas well is drilled so far in Pakistan. The shale reservoir formation of Lower Indus Basin, Pakistan is mainly Sembar which is complex and present many explorations related challenges. data.projectName: An insight into the Glycemic Index of Pakistani Rice cultivars through genotyping of Wx allele
data.projectDigest: Recent outbreaks of chronic diseases, particularly diabetes, obesity and colorectal cancers which were common only in developed countries, are now becoming the main cause of death worldwide while Pakistan ranked 7th in diabetes prevalence. Thus, appreciable investigation is recommended to explore the therapeutic and preventive measures  and consumption of high (>3%) resistant starch (high-RS) and high (26–33%)  apparent amylose content (AAC) rice is recommended because shifting from brown rice (glycemic index (GI<55) to white rice (GI>70) has been shown to play key role in the prevalence of these diseases.  Rice is the prime source of energy, however rice has been considered as worse source of high GI food. The diversity of rice GI is governed by the type of starch in rice grains. Particularly, apparent amylose content (AAC) is positively correlated with resistant starch (RS), which is a type of starch that escapes digestion and pass on large intestine. Genotypic variation of Granule Bound Starch Synthase I (GBSSI) gene, known as Waxy (Wx) gene, are mostly responsible for the diversified AAC and RS in rice grains however genotypic variation of RS in Pakistani rice cultivars remained undiscovered. Therefore, this study will address the first large-scale phenotyping of AAC and RS in Pakistani rice varieties in conjunction with allelic variation of GBSSI. The study will explore the role of GBSSI allele in diversifying rice grain characteristics based on AAC and RS. Moreover, it will provide significant evidence for dietitians to detect and measure the effect of low glycemic rice on blood sugar level while diabetic patients may choice specific types of rice as their preference of carbohydrate .
