data.projectName: Using Plant-Microbes-bioChar interactions in rhizosphere to Reduce Nitrogen fertilizer use and enhancing soil organic matter reserves (UPMicroChar-ReduceNitro)
data.projectDigest: Given the poor organic matter content and consequently the lower use efficiency of inputs, Pakistan's agriculture is experiencing high rates of chemical fertilizer inputs. This is resulting into increasing cost of production and environmental degradation in terms of N2O emissions (a potent greenhouse gas) and nitrate leaching into ground water. Here we propose that biochar- a nutrient-rich, slow decomposing material made from organic wastes- could be an excellent solution in lowering the fertilizer input rate, increasing the organic matter of soils and decreasing the economic & environmental cost of agricultural production. Consequently, we propose to test these hypotheses by studying interactions of roots of the two most important cereals i.e. wheat and rice, with biochar and soil microbes. We will use 13C isotopic tracers to track the C being contributed from three sources i.e. plant, biochar & soil. Similarly, 15N isotopic tracer will be used to estimate the sources of nitrate leaching & N2O in these combinations. Moreover, key microbial actors will be revealed using DNA sequencing. We expect that the mechanisms revealed in the project would provide key tools for crop growers to control nutrient release in soils in a way to limit leaching and increase use-efficiency of inputs.

data.projectName: Development of bioactive and antibacterial coatings for biomedical applications
data.projectDigest:
The main focus of this study will be to address basic health issues related to the biomedical implants and cancer treatment. Implanted biomedical devices reside within millions of patients and are being involved in millions of new and revisionary surgeries every year worldwide. As such, they comprise a major component of modern medicine and are essential for many clinical applications ranging from hip/knee replacement, tissue repair /reconstruction, prosthesis and controlled drug release. In order to develop sustainable biomedical implants for orthopedic application.  We propose here multi-structured coatings capable of exhibiting potent antibacterial effect against variety  of bacteria. It is important to mention here that the number of people in Pakistan suffering from the accidents and other bone related disease have increased significantly over the last few years. Thus, their is a striving need for the development of cheap and efficient implants and design the targeted drug delivery systems for the people of Pakistan.  We have published several high Impact factor papers, which focuses on drug delivery systems, bone repair and healing, and the development of bioactive and antibacterial coatings through multiple processing route. Currently, we are in good position to develop optimum quality of the orthopedic implants and the targeted delivery systems for the wide range of applications, including the cancer therapy. The funding obtained from the project will be utilized to further extend over current study to in-vivo models and eventually the clinical trials.

data.projectName: Developing salt tolerant wheat cultivar through integrated use of conventional breeding and molecular biology approaches
data.projectDigest: The changing climate and growing global population is increasing pressure on our ability to produce sufficient food. Abiotic stresses such as salt and drought stresses are additional factors that reduce crop productivity. The development of crop cultivars with greater salt tolerance and higher yield in new targeted environment are required on salt affect lands. Plant breeders are trying to develop salt tolerant cultivars using conventional breeding strategies. Wheat is moderately salt tolerant. However, its yield is reduced by 50% where salinity stress increases 10 dS/m. During the last 40 years, a number of attempts have been made to screen and select for salt tolerance but a few salt tolerant cultivars have been developed through targeted breeding in Pakistan such as LU26S, SARC-I, S-24. The cultivar LU26S was found to be susceptible to rust. Thus, development of salt tolerant wheat cultivar is of great concern. During the past 30 years, the PI contributed in the development of a salt tolerant wheat line S-24 (Fully acknowledge in Ashraf, 2010) which is susceptible to lodging due to its tall stature. In continuation of that work, we have crossed some of elite high yielding, short stature, salinity and drought tolerant Pakistani cultivars and have F5 progeny from 7 crosses and needs to be selected for salinity tolerance through integrated approaches. Thus in the proposed project, the breeding material will be subjected to analyze for salinity tolerance based on mechanism of salt tolerance and then characterize them using molecular biology based tools such as gene expression of K and Na transporters or regulatory proteins that support salt exclusion (CBL, CIPK16 etc). The selected accessions/lines will process further to develop highly salt tolerant wheat cultivar.

data.projectName: Enabling Technology as pathway for improving brain performance
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Improving professional performance through mental trainings remains in high demand for students as well as professions such as: athletes, employers, executives, security forces, lawyers, and journalists. As per World Bank report 2019, mental health issues due to work stress, optimal performance pressure, and other neurological disorders have been ignored and cause economic loss of about 1 trillion USD. Mental health issues accounts for up to 16% of total population of Pakistan provided with restricted interventions. World Bank highlighted importance of technology to address mental health issues. Among different technologies, Neurofeedback has gained a significant attraction because it is a non-invasive and a non-pharmacological intervention and does not require any external stimulation. Cost of existing commercially available neurofeedback systems ranges from $800 to $10,000 apart from session costs of $12,000 - $24,000; without providing all-stage tools in one package. This project aims to develop a technology eco-system providing all-stage tools including assessments, interventions, diagnostic support and reporting; to elevate mental health care standards, promote capacity building and enhance productivity thereby increasing knowledge-based economy. The objectives are aligned with sustainable development goals, Pakistan vision 2025, and Digital Pakistan vision. The outcomes will impact not only medical domain but other fields such as education, sports and human resource sectors.

data.projectName: Assessing mobile phone access, usage and willingness among women to receive voice message-based mHealth intervention to improve antenatal care attendance in District Thatta: A cross-sectional study
data.projectDigest: The Pakistan Demographic and Health survey (PDHS) 2017-18 shows that only 51% percent of women received four or more ANC visits and thus there is missed opportunities for almost half of the women who were not able to seek the recommended antenatal visits. In Thatta district of Sindh, the maternal mortality ratio is estimated at 313/100,000 live births and only 40% of women receive at least four ANC visits. Various studies reported that mobile health interventions, particularly those delivered through SMS and voice calls, are associated with improved utilization of preventive maternal healthcare services. However, the feasibility and effectiveness of mHealth interventions may be different in different settings due to differing patient demographics; cultural considerations; environmental and behavioral factors and budgetary constraints. Prior to implementing a similar intervention in district Thatta, it is crucially important to assess the mobile phone access, usage and willingness among women to receive voice-message based mHealth intervention to improve ANC services. A cross-sectional quantitative study design will be conducted used in 20 villages of Taluka, Mirpur Sakro of district Thatta.  We anticipate that the study will also highlight demographic, sociocultural and economic factors associated with women willingness to receive voice messages regarding ANC. These insights will guide researchers on how mHealth programs can be tailored to local context, through developing cultural-sensitive messages in local languages, and following societal norms (sending messages on specific time of the day), to ensure successful implementation of such programs.

data.projectName: Developing Automated Tools to Compute Multimodal Features for early Detection and Prediction of Breast Cancer by Optimizing Machine learning and Deep learning Algorithms
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest: Breast cancer is a major medical imaging problem due to which millions of deaths occur all over the world especially in USA and UK. In the state of Azad Jammu and Kashmir, there is dire need to investigate the breast cancer cases by developing computerized methods. Developing automated tools with multimodal feature can improve early detection thereby decreasing the mortality rate. In this study, we will develop methods based on multimodal feature extracting approach for improved diagnostic system. Firstly, we will develop different image enhancement and morphological operations on cancer images to improve the image enhancement and will then extract multimodal feature such as texture, morphological, geometrical, epileptic Fourier descripts (EFDs), scale invariant Fourier transform (SIFT), Reconstruction ICA, Sparse filter, autoencoder and complexity-based features to capture the multivariant dynamics and variations. We proposed robust machine learning methods to compute the detection performance by optimizing the parameters. We also proposed and optimized novel Deep Learning Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models using transfer learning strategy for improved detection performance. The proposed methods will provide better diagnostic system for early detection and prognostic to decrease to mortality rate and will help the health professionals for proper curing and treatment.

data.projectName: Comprehensive research on causes, impacts and repair of potholes on roads
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Potholes are one of the major pavement distresses which cause significant impact of travel speed, capacity, fuel required and emissions. The existing literature lacks detailed studies on impact of pothole .

This research will investigate the causes of pothole formation including the quality of material, quality of construction, domestic water ponding, and sewage water ponding. The effect of quality of material and construction will be invested by extracting cores from the road segments with potholes and without potholes. The cores will be investigated for the materials used and the quality of compaction in road construction. The effect of water and sewage water ponding on pothole formation will be investigated by preparing asphalt samples in the lab. The samples will be poured into the water for 1 to 14 days. Samples will be taken with 1-day interval to model the effect of water ponding on the compressive strength of asphalt samples, thus relating it to the loss of strength and pothole formation on selected road segments. 

The research will be performed by selecting 100 potholes, which will be repaired in this research. The impact of potholes will be evaluated by comparing the speed and capacity values of pre-repair and post-repair.

data.projectDigest: Pakistan has natural gas reserves like Qadirpur, Swan and Sui gas fields etc. These gas reserves are huge source of natural gas which is being used as main source of fuel for domestic and industrial use. Natural gas is also being used as a fuel for vehicles and as a feed stock for process industry. Apart from CH4, natural gas also contains significant amount of CO2, depending upon the reservoir. CO2 is a major greenhouse gas and primary contributor to disastrous climate change. Gas Separation using polymeric membranes is considered as the most feasible technique due to easy scale up and least requirements in terms of energy, maintenance and cost. Membrane separation process became economically competitive in 1970s and since then it has always been more attractive than conventional processes like adsorption and absorption. CO2/CH4 is at second place among the most investigated gas pairs. In the view of above, there is a need to indigenously synthesize polymeric membrane which can capture CO2 with high permeability and selectivity. Therefore, the proposed research work will be focused on the development of Hollow fiber polymeric membranes for carbon dioxide capture from natural gas. The primary objective of this proposal is to develop Hollow fiber polymer membrane which will lead to an integrated, cost effective membrane based separation process which would be environment friendly and less energy intensive.

data.projectName: 3DPTBomics: Functional Genomics Analysis of Pre-term Birth Related Biomarkers
data.projectDigest: Translational research or translational medicine is a highly interdisciplinary field to improve the global healthcare system significantly, supported by three main pillars: bench side, bedside and community. In a medical research context, it aims to "translate" findings in fundamental research into medical practice and meaningful health outcomes to enhance well-being. Pre-term birth is encompassed by genetic and environmental factors and have been life-threating for many decades. With the concept of translation research, this project aims to focus the effect of causal genetic variants at molecular and functional level involved pre-term birth. The aim is to decipher responsible gene mutations, already associated with pre-term birth, the downstream functional effect at molecular level, and eventually to propose possible drug candidates. In the area of gene mutation analysis, the focus is to prioritize the responsible gene mutations by using Biostatistics and Bioinformatics approaches. On the other hand, the 3D structure prediction of the responsible gene products and structure-based analysis will be carried out. This project aims to propose the new effective therapeutic regimen having potential to reduce the burden of pre-term birth.

data.projectName: AWARENESS AND PRACTICE OF GREEN HRM IN DISTRICT ABBOTTTABAD, KPK
data.piUniversity: Abbottabad University of Science & Technology (AUST), Abbottabad
data.projectDigest: Global warming is a major threat the world is facing. The Industrial pollutants and carbon emissions leading to eco imbalance which is endangering the environment. Each and every human has to take responsibility to save the world from the increasing threat of climate change. According to the Germanwatch- Global Climate Risk Index 2019, Pakistan is the eight most affected country due to climate change from 1998 to 2017 (annual averages). The government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, in the last tenure launched a billion tree Tsunami as a response to challenge the global warming. The Universities, SME’s and industry should also put environment sustainability as top priority. The Majority of Human Resource (HR) at the lower level in these organization are less educated due to which the awareness level of precautions of global warming is low or none. A large number of top and middle management are also not contributing their share in the fight of global warming. Pakistan need a cultural to encourage green business. The first step toward green business is to train the HR department and create an awareness at the top level to develop an organizational culture and strategies that develop a Green Human Resource Management (GHRM) force. GHRM is an emerging field dealing with the policies and practices in line with the social, economic and environmental issues, which constitute the three pillars of sustainability (Muster & Schrader, 2011; Renwick, Redman, & Maguire, 2013). GHRM conscious and assurance to the employee in each phase to practice and enhance sustainability (Hussain, 2018). This project will promote green business practices and create awareness of developing a GHRM force, benefiting the country and the world at large to fight the risk of Global warming.

data.projectName: Next generation genomics and proteomics approaches to trace extensively drug-resistant (XDR) typhoid in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Salmonella typhi is the cause for typhoid fever, that is highly infectious illness and may prove life-threatening if remains untreated. Multidrug resistant (MDR) strains of S. typhi, resistant to several antibiotics, have been a cause of typhoid outbreak across the globe. Recently, thousands of cases of extensively drug-resistant (XDR) typhoid have been reported across South East Asia. During the recent XDR typhoid epidemic (since 2016) several thousand cases of extreme typhoid fever have been reported in Pakistan as treatment failures and deadly outbreaks caused by a superbug XDR Salmonella enterica serovar typhi have emerged. This strain is highly resistant to available five classes of antibiotics. In 2018, WHO issued warnings regarding spread of XDR typhoid and recommended it to be treated on the high priority list. 
	Like many other microbial strains, these XDR typhi has been overlooked by commonly used diagnostic approaches and went untreated. The purpose of the current study designed here, is to trace XDR strains using high throughput proteomic and metagenomic based on next generation methods. These investigations based on next generation genomics will lead to the development of infection-based screening, as well as it will also help to understand the infection mechanism in newly evolved strains resistant to antibiotics. Next generation genomics would enable us to detect previously overlooked bacterial strains as it is independent of marker-based detection and cultivation biasness. This would also help us understanding the infection mechanism at community level ultimately leading to the identification of novel diagnostic markers, identification of disease carriers and strategies for better the treatment of the disease.

data.projectName: Development of plant based antibiofilm agents that  inhibit biofilm formation of pathogenic bacteria and identification of molecular mechanism underlying their inhibitory character
data.projectDigest:
Biofilm is a sessile microbial community in which microbes attach to solid surfaces and produce a matrix which surrounds these microbes. Number of pathogenic bacteria such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Staphylococcus aureus, etc has ability to form biofilms during their severe infections. Pseudomonas aeruginosa is the most studied organisms in reference to biofilm formation. It is an opportunistic pathogen and causes chronic infections in humans. It becomes lethal when forms biofilm and develops resistance to various antibiotics, especially during cystic fibrosis. Staphylococcus aureus causes various infections and becomes lethal when forms biofilm. The biofilm formation ability of S. aureus is a major concern in the diagnosis and treatment of its infection. Therefore, it is important to develop some novel strategies to overcome biofilm related problems. 
Mostly bacteria have intercellular communication via the production and response to cell density dependent signal molecules, which are termed as quorum sensing. Bacterial quorum sensing play vital role in pathogenicity and therefore can be the target for developing new treatments against microbial infections. Medicinal plants can be the potential candidates to inhibit bacterial communication, therefore  the current study is designe to isolate such compounds from indigenous plant species and to study their mechanism of action.

Whereas the existing wheat area of 8.99 Million hectares is estimated to remain constant. data.projectName: Assessment of Biological screening of different potential endemic plants of Pakistan
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Efficacy of therapy for diseases such as infections or cancerous diseases is dramatically affected by the occurrence of resistance or lack of effective drugs, respectively. Therefore, screening programs to identify new leads for the development of new drugs are essential. Due to the production of many different secondary metabolites, plants provide a source of biologically active compounds, which is far from being fully explored. Endemic plants, which are used in folk medicine for a diversity of illnesses. These are important that they have a generally restricted distribution, threats to endemics carry more risk of extinction than for broadly distributed species.  Exploration of their biological active compounds can lead to the production of many life-saving drugs and lead to the conservation strategies of these plants. In current study, two main species Berberis and Astragalus from northern areas of Pakistan and Balochistan will be taken respectively. Selection is based upon the extensive use of these species among local population and literature review. Their phytochemical analysis will be carried out. Then complete biological potential will be explored through antibacterial, anticancerous, anti-gentotoxicity and oxidative stress of these plant extracts. Findings of this study would help in the identification of novel bioactive compounds that could be used for future medicinal products and treatment of various drug resistant and cancerous diseases. The end results of this project might help the creation of Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), based in the production of cosmetics, food additives or raw products for pharmaceuticals based in the local flora of Pakistan. Moreover, this project is a step towards the conservation of our important endemic flora.

data.projectName: SYNTHESIS OF ADVANCED FUNCTIONAL MATERIALS USING DEEP EUTECTIC SOLVENTS (DESS) FOR ENVIRONMENTAL APPLICATIONS
data.projectDigest: The present proposal is focused on the synthesis of advanced functional materials more precisely for environmental applications by means of deep eutectic solvents (DESs). DESs are the solvents that have many comparable properties like ionic solvents but are more industrially promising than ionic solvents due to their low cost and high lenience to humidity. DESs have received an increasing attention for its use in functional materials that can further be applied for environmental applications. In the present project, DESs have been explained based on their three main roles that they play in solution process of functional materials. DESs, being an inert media or applied as reactive reagent for the synthesis of materials with specific geometry, they can also be adopted directly as functional materials such as electrolytes for energy storage devices or as CO2 adsorbents. The present research project will open new window in the synthesis of several functional materials like noble metals, transition metal compounds, carbonaceous materials and DESs themselves for potential applications in the field of energy and environment. In conclusion, our proposed project deals about the synthesis of advanced functional materials in which DES will act both as solvent as well as reagent for engineering the geometry of functional materials with unique structures and properties.

data.projectName: Genetic Counselling of Rare Disorders of Pakistani Population through Whole-Exome Sequencing: A Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Perspective
data.projectDigest:
Aim of every research project in medical genetics and genomics is to benefit a common man; however, in our societies most of the projects are very specific to certain diseases or very much restricted to ethnic or sub ethnic groups, in which general populations are less benefited.  With the recent advances in robust genomics data generation and analysis it has become very easy to understand our genetic makeup and to trace our history back to our ancestors. Similarly, it has also been possible to investigate a probable disease risk in our future generations. 
Genetic counselling is the specified field of medical genetics which applies laboratory based investigations and psychological approaches towards disease risk managements. These strategies improve public awareness and attitude towards genetic testing and helps community about its outcomes. 
Pakistan is one of those populations where marriages within relatives are more frequent, which is leading cause of genetic diseases worldwide. In this project we have planned to work parallel on laboratory based screening of 1,000 apparently healthy young men and women from at least ten different tribes of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Laboratory procedures will include, blood samples collection, genomic DNA isolation, next generation sequencing of coding genes (exome), bioinformatics (computational analysis). Selected alterations in the exome data will further processed for family based genetic counselling or disease risk awareness of general population. 
To decrease the rare disease risk in future generations of Pakistan, we do need nation-wide thorough screening programs for our un-married healthy males and females. Our project is primarily proposed for KP  population; however, it could be replicated in other provinces as well.

data.projectName: Micro Hydro Kinetic Turbine for Northern Areas of Pakistan
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan, there are lot of hills, lake, rivers, canals and mountains in the northern areas along the Indus River in the provinces of Gilgit-Baltistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa as well as the Jhelum River in the provinces of Punjab and Azad Jammu and Kashmir. There is a great emphasis of the present government on the development of hydropower potential, and to fulfill this ambition, the government has relied heavily on foreign investment from private investors, foreign governments and multilateral development banks. A number of hydropower plants were completed or commissioned in 2016 including Ranolia (17 MW), Daral Khwar (37 MW) and Machai (2.6 MW), all located in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. These mega projects required lot of investment as well as time. But Still remote villages in above areas, local electrification still a challenge due to heavy infrastructure cost . Therefore, our research based hydrokinetic turbine is one step towards local indigenous electrification without any heavy transmission lines or infrastructure. Hence its more efficient and cheaper with the ease in installation and maintenance with time.

data.projectName: Pd (0) Catalysis! A modern Synthetic tool to synthesize Novel Arylated Heterocycles having Potential Against Multidrug Resistant Tuberculosis (MDR-TB) and Extensive Drug Resistant Tuberculosis (XDR-TB)
data.projectDigest:
One of the major fatal diseases in third world countries is Tuberculosis; due to this bacterial infection approximately 2 million deaths are reported per year. The cause of tuberculosis is a bacterial strain named as mycobacterium tuberculosis has got resistance against 1st and 2nd line antituberculosic drugs. Now it is need of time to develop new drugs that can become vital force against this resistant tuberculosis cases i.e. MDR-TB and XDR-TB. Four decades ago in 1979 Akira Suzuki developed a reaction, which is high yielding and open a way towards synthesis of new compounds in an efficient way, as this is high yielding reaction. By using methodology developed by Akira Suzuki, novel arylated heterocycles will be synthesized from halogenated heterocyclic compounds. Unique properties of heterocycles and boronic acid will end with novel compounds; that are expected to have excellent potential against mycobacterium tuberculosis.
Our aim is to synthesize novel arylated heterocyclic compounds which are similar to drugs which are already in use against TB. These novel compounds will be characterized with help of NMR, Mass, IR and single crystal XRD. These novel compounds will be subjected to studies against resistant strains of mycobacterium tuberculosis. It is expected that these novel motifs will become 1st line drug therapy against XDR-TB and MDR-TB.

data.projectName: Development and Commercialization of Plant-Based Irradiated Designer Meat for Immuno-compromised People
data.projectDigest: The immunity profile of elderly and children is decreasing day by day due to consumption of unhealthy foods. Immunity may leads to the development of different lifestyle disorders. Therefore, it is need of the time to develop designer foods for the immune-compromised people which will decrease the use and cost of medicated drugs. In this project, we aimed to develop a plant based designer meat treated with gamma irradiation. According to my knowledge, there is no work reported for the immune-compromised patients. The findings of the current project will lead to exploitation of the plant sources such as poppy seed and celery as the food ingredients which might be incorporated in chicken nuggets, chicken patties and fish fillets to provide culinary option for the immune-compromised patients to boost their immunity and fight the chronic illnesses and lessening of healthcare burden on society. The meat industry is directly benefited with the outcomes of this project. The developed designer meat will be commercialized with the help of industrial collaborator not only at national level but also at International level which will helpful in the national economy.

data.projectName: Photo-reduction Reduction of Carbon dioxide (CO2) into Useful Fuel
data.projectDigest: The main goal of this project is to developed new hybrid nanosturctures under Green Chemistry with the goal, to convert the atmospheric CO2 into useful fuels and carbon based chemicals, with inexpensive and environmentally benig photocatalysts, Photochemical carbon dioxide reduction harnesses solar energy to convert CO2 into higher-energy products. The chemical conversion of CO2 already occurs on an industrial scale in the manufacture of solvents such as formic acid, but photochemical reduction differs in that it relies on a renewable energy source, the sun. Because CO2 is a greenhouse gas, there is environmental interest in producing artificial systems that are efficient photocatalysts, but the low conversion rates of current methods have prohibited wide-scale industrial application.

data.projectName: Sustainable supply chain management in the construction sector: A system dynamics approach
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
The construction supply chain is complex with multiple stakeholders such as clients, consultants, contractors, sub-contractors and suppliers gathered together to carry out a single bespoke project. There is a growing need to make the supply chain more sustainable. This can be achieved through the implementation of sustainable practices in the construction supply chain. Sustainable supply chain management (SCM) is defined as the management of material, information and capital flows as well as cooperation among companies along the supply chain while taking goals from all three dimensions of sustainable development i.e. economic, environmental and social, into account.
Nonetheless, the process is not straightforward and involves complexity in the implementation of SSCM in the construction sector. Complexity issues can be addressed using system dynamics approach involving modeling and simulation techniques. The aim of the research is to address complexity using system dynamics approach in the implementation of sustainable supply chain management (SSCM) in the construction sector with a focus on construction small and medium-sized enterprises to increase productivity and performance.

data.projectName: Dissecting molecular pathways for movement disorders and related syndromes
data.projectDigest: Movement disorders are characterized by excessive or limited movement of any of different body parts. This project is based on the hypothesis that we will identify the genetic defects underlying incapacitating movement disorder syndromes and will determine mechanism of disease. Our objectives include identification of genetic mutations in the patients and determining how the mutations affect cellular processes and function. To achieve our aims we will identify and enroll families with history of ataxic and dystonic movement disorders. This will be followed by using genetic approaches such as sequencing all genes (whole-exome sequencing) to identify the causative mutations. We will determine the effect of selected mutations in cell lines and animal models using different approaches including gene knockdown. The research team includes scientists from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and USA. The proposed work is innovative because it combines human genetics, cell biology and animal models research. Immediate beneficiary of this work will be the families who will derive genetic diagnoses and use the information to reduce birth of further affected individuals. In addition, clinical indicators for better diagnosis will be identified. The genetic landscape of these diseases will be determined which will provide a framework for targeted therapies of the patients.

data.projectName: Effects of Anti-Inflammatory Plant Extracts and Their Active Components in Animal Model of Neuroinflammation
data.projectDigest: Neurodegeneration is a phenomenon that occurs in the central nervous system through the hallmarks associate with the loss of neuronal structure and function. This study is designed to identify the effects of anti-inflammatory plant extracts in animal model of neuroinflammation. The major emphasis will be given to Centella asiatica (L.) and Rosa damascene because of their reported anti-inflammatory effects in vitro and in some preclinical studies. The animal model of neuroinflammation will be treated with aqueous plant extract and active constituent. Behavioral parameters will be done to confirm the development of animal model of neuroinflammation and effectiveness of treatments at selected doses. The study will further extend to analyze biochemical, neurochemical and molecular analysis. The findings of the current study will be validated by using electrophysiological tools to find out long term potentiation using field potential technique in disease as well as treatment animals. This will highlight the importance of use of plant-based medicine for the treatment of different abnormalities associated with brain disorders. This study will develop a model that can be used in future studies for the identification of novel synthetic and natural compounds which are being continuously synthesized in the home institute for their possible effects on brain functions.

data.projectName: Visual Attention using Facial Expressions
data.projectDigest: Knowledge transfer through E-learning is an effective way. Students use Multimedia tools and applications for this purpose. Measuring and analysing the student’s visual attention are significant challenges in this domain. In the E-Learning environment, students do not directly interact with teachers. Analysing student’s visual attention along with emotions can play an essential role in E-Learning environment. Machine learning techniques and multimedia tools can be used to examine the visual attention of a student. Firstly, we will use the webcam of the laptop to capture the video of student when the student is taking lecture. The video captured will be analysed to calculate student’s attention score. We will extract images from the webcam using multimedia tools. Image processing will be used to convert each image to grayscale image. These images will be used to detect face and eyes A real-time analysis of the video will generate a dataset having the values of detected faces, eyes and emotions. Secondly, the emotions of the student during lecture are identified. The emotions play a vital role in understanding or judging the attention of the student in the class. If the student is taking an interest in the lecture, teacher can judge it by reading his emotions and the learning will be increased and students will pay more attention and will gain more in the classroom. By the addition of emotions, we may ensure that in e-learning environment it is possible to know about the student’s learning capabilities and to judge student is learning what has been taught in the classroom.

data.projectName: Optimizing the evidence based nutraceuticals to treat the metabolic disorders using environment friendly green extraction approach
data.projectDigest: Through Nagai Foundation Tokyo, Japan funding to co-PI, we have successfully prepared the crude ethanol extracts of pomegranate peel, peanut kernel coat and walnut hulls using microwave assisted green extraction (MAE) process, and comparatively evaluated for antidiabetic and anticancer potential of the crude extracts and their marker compounds (ellagic acid (EA) of pomegranate peel, resveratrol (RT) of peanut kernel coat and juglone (JN) of walnut hulls) was conducted. We intend to prepare standardized enriched extracts from these fruits byproducts using green technology, to determine their stability, bio-evaluation and clinical application in diabetes, obesity and cancer. EA, RT and JN have therapeutic potential in metabolic disorders. However, the multi-stage and high cost purification process along with the consumption of toxic organic solvents in the purification of EA, RT and JN obstructs its application in the drug development. The alternative to synthetic and expensive EA, RT and JN, is to prepare their standardized enriched extract using fruit byproducts which will be value added utilization of environmental wastes. Working in collaboration with researchers from PSU Thailand the current project is aimed to prepare EA, RT and JN enriched extracts using green MAE and bioconsumable solvents. For EA, RT and JN enrichment, semi-purification of the crude extracts will be perform by single step fractionation with recyclable and biodegradable resins (Amberlite® and Diaon®) columns using ethanol and water. For stability study of the extracts, suitable HPLC analysis will be performed to quantify the EA, RT and JN in enriched extracts. Comparative antidiabetic, antiobesity, anticancer and safety evaluation of enriched extracts will be performed.

data.projectName: Self Charging lithium ion batteries using sunlight
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest:
Modern electronic devices increasingly demand for innovative technologies for energy generation and storage. Combining energy generation and storage in a single device is highly desirable as an efficient and portable energy source for portable electronic devices. Proposed project belongs to thematic area i.e. Energy (conversion, distribution and storage) of innovative and collaborative research grant and we are aiming to develop battery devices which will use sun light for charging as an autonomous power source for portable electronic devices. This research project will focus on the development of photo-active composite material while exploiting organic and inorganic materials for the development of photo-rechargeable battery. Generally for lithium ion battery, layered materials are used for lithium intercalation such as Titanium dioxide, Lithium titanate etc. Luckily materials used for lithium intercalation also demonstrate semiconducting and dielectric properties which could be used to charge lithium ion battery while using sunlight. Semiconducting properties of such materials will allow us to excite the electron from valance band to conduction band which could be exploited for lithium intercalation in such materials whereas dielectric properties will be used to scatter the light inside the electrode material of the battery for achieving maximum efficiency.
The research group at National Institute of Lasers and Optronics, Pakistan will focus on the development of layered semiconductor materials for lithium intercalation along with structural designing of materials for efficient light scattering inside electrode of the battery. The research group at Durham University will focus on the development of organic material for increasing electronic conductivity inside battery

data.projectName: Molecular Genetic Investigation of isolated Ventricular Septal Defects (VSDs) in Pakistani children and designing a Prenatal screening and Awareness strategy
data.projectDigest: The number of children with a hole in the heart (ventricular septal defect, VSD) visiting cardiac surgery units is increasing at an alarming rate in Pakistan. Due to specific social and cultural practices, blood marriages are quite common in Pakistan which result in high risk of birth of children with genetic defects.  Despite high prevalence, there is no data available on the genetics of VSDs in our society. We aim to identify the genetic causes of these defects in Pakistani children. Based on the results, the next aim is to educate the high risk families and general public about the role of genetics in the development of VSD during gestation. Finally, , an easy, cost-effective and rapid method will be developed to identify these defects early in the pregnancy so that the parents can be counselled regarding continuation or termination of pregnancy. For accomplishing these tasks, a comprehensive and experienced team including PI, Co-PI, collaborators and the PhD/MS/MPhil/MSc/BS(hons) research students will work together focusing different aspects of the project. We have established international and national collaborations for the proposed project. If sufficient funding is available, we expect a society based outcome that will improve the lives of many at risk.

data.projectName: Multifunctional Scaffold Materials for Highly Efficient and stable Hybrid Halide Perovskite Solar Cells
data.projectDigest: The world is facing energy crisis and especially Pakistan. Renewable energy has increased much due to the gradual fossil energy consumption, which facilitates the global warming and causes serious environment pollution. Of the possible renewable energy approaches, photovoltaics, the conversion of sunlight into electricity, represents a promising route. The current photovoltaics landscape is dominated by silicon solar cells, which have benefited from recent advances leading to reduced manufacturing costs. But, this mature technology is constrained by some fundamental cost barriers, such as high temperature processing. Recently, organic–inorganic metal halide perovskite semiconductors have offered the promise of a breakthrough for next-generation solar cell devices, and the PCE is up to 22.6% over the past few years. However, despite the big excitement, the low-stability of the perovskite material and charge transport material (ETL and HTL) will become problematic in the future for widespread deployment of this technology. This proposal targets air-stable perovskite solar cell by developing new perovskite materials and transporting layers with high power conversion efficiency. The expected outcomes of the project will contribute to the  People of Pakistan excellence and attractiveness in the area of renewable energy.

data.projectName: Push-pull strategy evaluation and application for the sustainable management of aphids in wheat ecosystem of Punjab
data.projectDigest: For socio-economic development of Pakistani wheat industry-export commodities, there is dire need to study different wheat aphid species in relation to resistant wheat varieties which vital to be controlled non-chemically by using push-pull strategy that might be mixed up with the use of semiochemicals to attract the natural enemies and repel the aphids. The evaluation and then application of successful trap or repellent crops will be conducted during 2021-2024 in Multan and Faisalabad by open field survey fortnightly. The ultimate goal is to screen out the wheat resistant germplasm for green technology control with the help of Institute of Plant Protection, Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences and Huanghuai University of Zhumadian, China as academic collaborator while and Department of Entomology, Bahauddin Zakaryia University Multan and Entomological Research Institute of AARI, Faisalabad as Co-PIs. The purpose of this study is to find the sustainable control strategy by using onion, garlic, canola, camelina and peas in push-pull strategy. The findings of this study will provide the way forward for integrated pest management of wheat aphids in different wheat growing regions of Punjab province. It will enhance the productivity, farmers health improvement, less expenditures and environmentally safe.

data.projectName: Exploiting modern technology and enhanced policies for bridging the gaps between farmers and the markets: A novel methodology to cut the middle man
data.projectDigest: The agricultural productivity has certainly increased in the country due to the usage of advanced machinery and modern farm practices. Theoretically, this increased output should have been complemented with the increased income of the farmers. However, the farmer's income only represents a meagre share of the total income generated per acre, whereas, the middle-man takes majority of the earned capital. The dominance of middle-man is often severely criticized for worsening financial conditions of the small farmers. However, it’s also true that without the help of a middleman, the small farmers will not be able to arrange even basic farming ingredients which include, but not limited to, seed, fertilizer, and even the diesel for farming operations. The financial dependence of farmers on the middleman makes him an obligatory component of our agriculture. However, with increasing cost of inputs and decreasing governmental subsidies with an intention to make agriculture a self-sustainable sector, the role of middle man needs to be eliminated so that farmers could afford the increasing cost of production while getting maximum benefit out of farming.

data.projectName: A way forward for sustainable Prawn production: Seed production of Freshwater prawn in genus Macrobrachium (Bate, 1868).
data.projectDigest:
Growing human population calls for exploring applied methods of producing food.  Fin Fish and Shellfish fit the model for healthy sources of protein. 
Freshwater prawn culture is growing throughout world due to its potential for fulfilling the protein demand of growing human population. Prawn of genus Macrobrachium (Bate, 1848) are important economic resources in the world’s crustacean fishery (8). 
Macrobrachium malcolmsonii (monsoon river prawn) is the second largest freshwater prawn with high aquaculture and fisheries potential (6,1) based on its reproductive potential and larger size (9).
Currently Prawn farmers collect the seed from wild therefore, many other fish seed unwantedly enters in the ponds which sometimes includes catfish fry and they effect the production of targeted species due to predation and competition. 
In Pakistan another Sub-species of M. malcolmsonii is also reported i.e. Macrobrachium mlamcolmsonii Kotreanum (Johnson, 1973). The species has reported from the area of Kotri barrage.
All the previous attempts of prawn culture are based on wild seed collection. However, no successful attempt has been made for the complete larval rearing and seed production and hatchery management of the spp. 
 Sustainable fisheries enhancement of the species calls for the successful attempt of larval rearing and hatchery management of M. malcalmsonii Spp.

data.projectName: Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) to Mitigate Climate Change
data.projectDigest: Mineral carbonation converts CO2 into stable mineral carbonates such as MgCO3 and CaCO3 and this is permanent sequestration and there is no chance for CO2 to escape. Pakistan has much serpentine reserves in Taleri Mohammad Jan Village. Calcium and Magnesium rich minerals such as serpentine (lizardite, antigorite), olivine, pyroxene and amphibole are also found in Chilas, Jijal, Dargai, and Alpuri areas of Pakistan. The serpentine and olivine reserves of Chilas, Jijal, Dargai and Alpuri are able to  fix 1268, 94, 48, and 2 million metric tons carbon dioxide into stable mineral carbonates and these figures are much greater as compared to 92 million metric tons carbon emissions in Pakistan in 1999. Magnesite which is a product of the mineral carbonation have the potential to be used as a cement substitute to reduce pollution.

data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Amphibians constitute highest percentage of threatened (41%) as well as Data Deficient species (21%) among the vertebrate groups in the world. The notable threats include habitat destruction, fragmentation and loss, pollution due to agricultural and industrial chemicals, global warming and epidemics. The lack of data on space use, conservation status, response to anthropogenic and natural threats and role of amphibians in agricultural landscape merits immediate research, management and conservation interventions in Pakistan. We aim to determine how habitat degradation, fragmentation and loss influence amphibians with different life history characteristics and dispersal abilities; to examine allelic variation in uncommon/rare amphibian species, contrasting highly modified with less modified habitats and to investigate the pest species form diet of amphibians. The proposed study will be conducted in Rawalpindi and Murree Tehsil, (District Rawalpindi) and Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT). The study area will be divided into: croplands, fragmented habitat, degraded habitat and natural forest. The data will be gathered in two field years by employing standard methods for amphibian survey (are-constrained searches), trapping (pitfall traps), marking (passive integrated transponders, visible implant elastomers, toe clipping), abundance estimation (mark-recapture), diet (stomach content analysts) and genetic erosion (allelic frequencies). The findings are expected to quantify the response of amphibians to habitat destruction and fragmentation. The data generated will be useful in establishing the role of amphibians as biological control in arid agricultural landscape. The funds will help cater departments’ research needs.

data.projectName: Elucidation of the mutational spectrum of autosomal recessive non syndromic hearing impairment in different ethnic groups of Pakistan: a comparative study
data.projectDigest:
Hearing loss is a major health concern and considered as fourth leading cause of disability in 2015 with the prevalence of 0.2% in newborns worldwide (Sheffield and Smith 2019). According to WHO factsheets an estimated 900 million people will have disabling hearing loss by the year 2050.
The prevalence of hearing impairment in Pakistan is 1.6 per 1,000 live births (Elahi et al., 1998; Jaber et al., 1992) which is higher than world average of 1 per 1000 live births (Atar and Avraham, 2005).
The mutational spectrum of Hearing Impairment in different ethnic groups i.e. Sindhi, Balochi, Pathan, Punjabi, Saraiki, Kashmiri, Mahajor, Hindkowans, Chitralis of Pakistan, remains mostly undetermined. This significantly hampers the progress toward establishing an effective genetic screening method and early customized rehabilitation modalities for hearing loss. In this study, we will evaluate the genetic profile of severe-to-profound hearing loss in a Pakistani population to screened 31 known deafness-causing variants using Amplification Refractory Mutation System Polymerase Chain Reaction (ARMS) amplification and Sanger Sequencing. This Study will help in establishing an effective genetic screening method and early customized rehabilitation modalities for hearing loss in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Identification and Characterization of TRIM Family Proteins that Inhibit Hepatitis C Virus Infection
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is the second largest country in the globe with highest prevalence rate of HCV. Interferon (IFN) treatment was the standard care for HCV patients, however poor efficacy in IFN-treated patients necessitated the development of IFN-free therapeutic strategies. To this end the introduction of direct-acting antiviral (DAA) drugs revolutionized the field of HCV therapeutics. Recently we have reported the high relapse rates in HCV patients against DAA for the first time. Multiple TRIM proteins suppress HCV replication. Recently we did pilot studies on the expression of TRIM14 & TRIM22 genes in the peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMCs) of HCV patients and seen very promising results. Based on the promising results of two TRIM proteins and high relapse rates of DDA against HCV patients thus, we designed the proposed study for the innovative therapeutics against HCV. We will test the expression of TRIM proteins in PBMCs of HCV patients and discriminate those TRIM proteins that inhibit HCV infection in PBMCs. Then we will proceed TRIM proteins in cell lines for HCV inhibition. The success of this work will lead to uncover an innovative mechanism accountable for host defense against HCV infection and could potentially aid the development of novel anti-HCV therapeutics.

data.projectName: BEHAVIORAL AND NEUROCHEMICAL STUDIES OF SELECTED ANTICONVULSANT ON DIABETES INDUCED NEUROPATHIC PAIN IN ANIMAL MODELS
data.piUniversity: Kohat University of Science and Technology, Kohat
data.projectDigest: Diabetes mellitus is a chronic, extensively spread human illness described by hyperglycemia. Patients having type II diabetes suffering from many problems including neuropathy, atherosclerosis, retinopathy and nephropathy (El-Wassef, El-Saeed et al. 2012). Diabetic neuropathy is a common and actual complicated impairment that causes suffering among 60% of the patients encountering from diabetes mellitus (Said, 2007). It has been represented that neuropathic pain may happen as a result of metabolic variations such as diabetes mellitus (Elliott, 1994). It is normally described by unique chronic neuropathic pain that is stinging and expending in nature with hyperthesia, paresthesia and painful sensitivity which cause significant impairing that is extended in view of touch (Backonja and Krause, 2003). It is increasingly significant around night time (Boulton et al., 2005) and occurs in feet, lower legs and may incorporate hands (Vinik et al., 2000), affecting rest, mentality, certainty and social activity (Said, 2007) and ability to work (Galer et al., 2000; Vileikyte et al., 2003). Numbers of medication are studies against painful diabetic neuropathy like gabapentin (Gorson et al., 1999), Topiramate (Thienel et al., 2004), tramadol (Harati et al., 1998), Capsaicin (Chad et al., 1990), oxycodone (Gimbel et al., 2003). However, these medicines are related to side effects and/or lesser clinical effectiveness. So, there's need for medicine that are more effective and are related with least side effects resulting in hyperbolic drug compliance.

data.projectName: Real-time Non-Linear Approach For Direct Torque Control of Induction Motor For Electric Vehicle Applications
data.projectDigest: Direct torque control (DTC) is famous and a very convenient method to produce fast robust and fast torque response in 3-phase AC adjustable induction motor. But during the course of their steady state operation, fluctuations of toruqe, flux and current appear. A non-linear direct torque and flux control strategy of induction motor sensor less drive is proposed for Electric Vehicle application based on non-linear backstepping control and using a high power 3-phase inverter based on SVPWM. The benefits of transient reductions and robustness of DTC control behavior is preserved and the steady state behavior of the overall system will be improved by reducing transient and pulsation in torque and flux of induction motor. The proposed model will be simulated on Matlab Simulink and simulation results will be studied and presented. Moreover, real-world hardware will be implemented for the proposed technique which will be tested on a real prototype of Electric vehicle.

data.projectName: Detailed study of soil and water properties of potential aquaculture fields along the coastline of Pakistan.
data.projectDigest: The aim of the project is to determine the properties of water and soils that are currently used/marked as a potential aquaculture sites along the Sind and Baluchistan coast. The major nutrients associated with water and soil include chlorophyll content, nitrate, nitrite, phosphate, ammonia, silicate. apart from nutrients, soil properties that are related to aquaculture field/land assessment are sulfur content, sodium, magnesium, chloride ions, water holding capacity, organic and inorganic content and grain size analysis. All these parameters facilitate aquaculture farmers to determine the water quality, health of soil and predict age/longevity of ponds. As aquaculture pond management take away the highest percentage of investment, maintaining and keeping an eye on water and soil status will reduce the maintenance cost by more than half of initial spending. There is no recent baseline data of these areas and so many farmers are doing aqua farming on little information about soil health and water quality. The scientific hypothesis is that, the soil and water along the coastline of Pakistan is favorable for Mari culture/Aquaculture and the Baluchistan area is more suitable as compared to Sindh. The goal is to work with local farmers and stakeholders/private investors and determine overall pond health for them to better invest in the field of Mari culture and Aquaculture.

data.projectName: Photocatalytic activity of doped TiO2 grafted on highly porous silica nanoparticles towards hazardous pollutants
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan, large industrial sector consists of textile, leather and pharmaceutical industry releases large amount of toxic chemicals, which can lead to various diseases to human beings, animals and also destroy the aquatic environment. Therefore to prevent the hazards of such pollutants, an effective approach to remove such pollutants is ever needed. In this regard, photocatalysis provides an easy practicable and efficient approach, utilizing sunlight as source to initiate the photocatalytic reactions to degrade toxic chemicals. TiO2, ZnO etc. are preferred due to their large band gap (2.5ev) and photo corrosion stability. Such large band gaps limit the light absorption to a very small range of light spectrum making these less efficient. Therefore, robust approaches are required to develop efficient photocatalysts with the optimum light absorption providing the maximum surface for reactions. This project focuses on the development of metal / non-metal doped TiO2 grafted on nano-silica (derived from rice husk), which will substantially enhance surface area of TiO2. We will test the newly developed photocatalysts with various hazardous textile effluents for their degradation into environmentally friendly chemicals. Moreover, silica nanoparticles (derived from rice husk) are economic, efficient and environment friendly as compared to existing materials.

data.projectName: Understanding biochemical and molecular mechanisms of insecticide resistance in sand fly vectors of Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
In Pakistan various epidemics of particularly of cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL) type are reported from different parts of the country, with major outbreaks particularly from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP). Phlebotomus sergenti and P. papatasi are known to be the suspected vectors of CL. 
Indiscriminate and improper use of insecticides in many malaria control campaigns has altered the susceptibility of other associated insects to these insecticides including sand flies. This has resulted in insecticide resistance and thus control measures against these vectors is at risk of failure. 
This proposed research is focused on identifying biochemical and molecular basis of resistance in sand fly vector population of Pakistan. Insecticides resistance will be assessed against commonly used insecticides on wild caught sand fly species from in leishmaniasis epidemic districts of KP. We will perform insecticide susceptibility assays on reared sand flies from field. At the same time activity of enzymes contributing towards insecticide resistance. The specimens will also be analyzed for the presence and frequency of target-sit knockdown resistance mutations on the voltage-gated sodium channel (Vgsc) gene. This proposed research work will provide evidence/es for the specific insecticides resistance in sand fly species probably resulted from anti-malarial or other insets control activities in the region.

data.projectName: Microwave Assisted Synthesis, Characterization and Performance Evaluation of Flavonoid Capped Au@Ag Core Shell Nanoparticles as Colorimetric Sensors for Pharmaceutical Applications.
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Quantitative determination of pharmaceutically active ingredients is essential step of the drug development process. Analytical techniques of choice for drug monitoring should be efficient, sensitive with low LOD and LOQ, cost effective and user friendly. Nanomaterial sensors are emerging as rapid, sensitive, cost effective and selective tool for quantification of drugs in pharmaceutical formulation and biological fluids. We are interested in synthesizing and evaluating epicatechin and quercetin capped Au@Ag nanosensors bimetallic colorimetric nanonsensors as colorimetric nanosensors.  Epicatechin capped Au@Ag and quercetin capped Au@Ag nanoparticle will be synthesized using microwave irradiation. UV-Visible Spectroscopy, FTIR, AFM, TEM and XRD, etc. techniques will be used for characterization of synthesized nanosensors. Sensing ability of synthesized nanosensors will be evaluated by screening pharmaceutical compounds particularly those containing amine group. Surface Response Methodology (RSM) will also be employed to optimize sensing ability of synthesized flavonoid capped nanosensors. Validation parameters will also be determined. The proposed study will also explore nanoprobes-analytes interaction mechanism as well as role played by different functional groups of both capping agents. We expect that our developed nanosensors will provide an advanced drug quantification method for pharmaceutical and other health related industries.

data.projectName: Mathematical Modeling of Experimental Data for Rheological Properties of Nanofluids
data.projectDigest: This project is focused on theoretical and experimental investigations of Rheological characteristics for nanofluids. Nanofluid is an essential heat transfer fluid, which have wide applications covers potential region for example, electronics cooling, solar collector , refrigerators ,  automotive , nuclear reactor cooling , heat exchangers, thermal conductivity  and Cancer therapeutics etc. Before use it in these applications, it is compulsory to investigate the behavior of nanofluid in different aspects. In the literature, much attention has been paid in aspect of thermal behavior. Limited studies are available related to rheological behavior and found diverse results in their studies. In addition, there are many mathematical studies are available related to nanofluids flow in literature, but mostly authors choose the Newtonian model which have contradiction with experimental studies. So, it is needed to perform more experiments and developed the mathematical model that can helps us to find the actual behavior of nanofluids. So, the results of this project can help to chemical engineers to predict the behavior of these fluids to design a more efficient and environmental friendly process.

data.projectName: Present status and future strategy of forage development in Azad Jammu and Kashmir
data.projectDigest: Livestock is an integral part of agricultural production system in Pakistan. Animal feed have been one of the major production inputs drawing attention of the producers. In Azad Jammu & Kashmir, there is availability of green forage during the monsoon period, but for the remaining months, over the winter and spring, there is a lack of feed. Forage availability during winter months reduced because of slow growth of plants, thus the farmers suffer huge problem to feed their livestock. Traditionally summer grazing and cereal straw feeding in winter are the major sources of feed for livestock which is nutritionally poor to maintain the health and productivity of animals. In commercialized farming situations farmers compensate for shortages of forages with supplementation of expensive concentrate feeds. In Kashmir, there is no land for grazing, so animals are kept at the homestead and stall-fed on cultivated forage, crop residues, and concentrates. The scarcity of green fodder during winter months is even more severe and farmers have no option to feed their animals on dry stalks of summer cereals and grasses in these areas. Due to poor quality and quantity of forage results in low productivity of livestock in rainfed areas which adversely affect the livelihood of the inhabitants. To improve forage production is the need of time to meet the increasing fodder requirements in dry land situations. Farmers are unaware of the improved and potential fodder crop varieties. Winter forage cereals offer possible solution to mitigate fodder shortages. Barley and oats have shown potential as a food crop in the rainfed region of Pothwar, but the potential of barley, oat, rye and triticale crops remains to be explored in rainfed region of Azad Jammu and Kashmir. Hay and silage are consider

data.projectName: 3 Years
data.projectDigest:
Sustainable Urbanization is an emerging matter around the globe however it is a major challenge in the developing countries like Pakistan due to lack of required resources.  A large number of people are drifting from rural to urban areas which needs an effective usage of land usage. This study aims to:
•	To inspect and review the relationship of sustainability and urbanization. 
•	To find out the risks encountered in integrated land use planning. 
•	To explore the factors encountered during sustainable integrated land use planning. 

As a result of this study a framework for the successful adaptation of integrated land use planning as a means of sustainable urbanization will be developed.

data.projectName: Ecological Risk Assessment and modeling of gas emissions from solid waste dumping sites in Punjab, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Open dumping of solid waste is common issue in Pakistan. This situation gets worse when the dumped waste is in unsorted condition, containing huge amount of organic, electronic and hospital waste. A thick blackish liquid, called leachate, starts to generate out of it, as a result of degradation of solid waste. This leachate contains a number of hazardous and toxic compounds, which seep into the underneath groundwater table and become a liability for people living in the vicinity of these sites. This project focuses to develop a risk estimation framework for the assessment of different dumping sites of Punjab, to evaluate the characteristics of leachate and groundwater, treatment of leachate with chemical and biological processes, GIS mapping of pollutants in groundwater and estimation of gas emissions from dumping sites and its modeling for future predictions.

data.projectName: Intelligent Control Shed Poultry Farm System Incorporating with Machine Learning
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: This proposal aims to develop a smart control-shed poultry farming based on Wireless Sensors Network (WSN) and Machine Learning. The proposed approach comprises of learning and mastering phase. In learning phase, the system will observe/learn from user behavior patterns in terms of poultry activity operations for specific time duration. This time duration could be a week or a month longer. Upon completion of training/learning/observation phase the mastering phase will take in place. This phase will eventually automate and control the environment parameters (ventilation, temperature, humidity, water level and water quality, soil moisture, hazardous gases) based on the historical data or in other words the system will replicate the operators past business control behavior.  Obviously, the operator has a priority if a certain action triggered by the trained system is not required. The system actions will be overruled by the operator. The new action will be adopted by the system if the current behavior carried out persistently by the operator/user. The successful model will be delegated to other such Control Shed Poultry Farm (CSPF), this leads to develop a smart community culture where successful business experiences (model) will be exchanged among community to get a collective benefit in terms of revenue.

data.projectName: Generalized Fuzzy Sets with Complexities and their Applications in Signals & Systems
data.projectDigest:
The concept of fuzzy set (FS) was first given by Zadeh in 1965 [17]. A fuzzy set address unpredictability in real life problems. It became famous tool to deal with problems involve uncertainty.
Attanssov presented the idea of Intuitionistic fuzzy set [1], its membership and non-membership functions are denoted by µ and ? and has values in [0, 1]. More generalized form of Intuitionistic fuzzy set named as Neutrosophic fuzzy set was first studied by Samarandache in 1998 [3]. It is characterized by truth, intermediate and false membership function.
Ramot gave the concept of a Complex fuzzy set (CFS) which is more generalized form of a fuzzy set, whose range is extended to a disc of radius one in complex plane [12]. A grade value of a CFS is denoted by ?_s (x)=r_s (x)e^(i?_s (x)) that assigns all the values in the disc of radius one in complex plane. 
Here, we will try to define some new operations on a complex fuzzy set and will try to explore it further. My main work is to find applications of a complex fuzzy set in signals and systems by using discrete as well as continuous Fourier transform.

data.projectName: Process development for the production of Rabies vaccine
data.projectDigest: Rabies is a viral disease caused by the bite of rabid animal such as dogs etc. Rabies is a preventable and curable disease if proper vaccination and treatment is provided in time. Nevertheless, in Pakistan it is causing havoc according to NIH report 100,000 to 150,000 dog bites are reported and 800,000 doses of ARV are required annually. Pakistan primarily relies on the import of rabies vaccine from India but due to its shortage, country is facing huge crisis. It is highly unlikely that NIH will be able to rapidly produce efficacious ARV and RIG to fill the gap for the entire country. So an efficient methodology for the large scale commercial production of rabies vaccine is the need of the hour. With this research proposal we aim to produce recombinant rabies vaccine which is the modern, efficacious for rapid large scale production as compared to the cell culture technique. For this purpose nucleotide sequence of the G glycoprotein will be retrieved from NCBI and gene will be amplified using PCR by designing appropriate primers and then it will be purified and ligated in a plasmid and transformed in E.coli  for producing multiple clones, the clones will then be ligated in a eukaryotic plasmid and transformed in eukaryotic system such as yeast for overexpression and lastly it will be purified for use. This vaccine will be tested on rabbits and will evaluate its efficacy. By employing this methodology, we will be able to produce effective rabies vaccine which will be of relatively low cost, and it will also alleviate the import burden and its rapid large scale production will be able to meet the growing needs.

data.projectName: Gold/silver nanoparticles for their potential as theranostic agents
data.projectDigest: This project concentrates towards synthesis of  gold and silver nanoparticles and then using these nanoparticles for the enhancement of radiation dose during the treatment of cancer. Since tumor cells resist to radiations hence there was a need to overcome this resistance and enhance the effect of treatment outcome. The objective of this project is to evaluate the radiosensitization of silver and gold nanoparticles in vitro and in vivo studies as well as evaluating the potential applications in different imaging modalities. This work will highlight the potential application of gold/silver nanoparticles in radiation applications in cancer management.

data.projectName: Biogas digestate as bio-fertilizer: Evaluating bio-polymers and clay minerals for the development of slow release fertilizer from biogas digestate
data.projectDigest:
To feed this increasing population the use of chemical fertilizers has been increased which negatively impacted the environment. And to meet the increasing demand for electricity, biogas generation has recently been developed from floral biomass, animal waste, or agro-food industry waste. But biogas generation leaves a lot of waste “called biogas digestate”, which could be again a burden on the environment. It is well documented that the biogas digestate is rich in nutrients (i.e N, P, K etc.) which are essential for plants’ growth.
But despite of the possibility of use of biogas digestates as biofertilizer, the nutrient release from biogas digestates does not match the crop requirement according to developmental stages. So, synchronization of nutrient release with crop developmental demand is a solution. And this synchronization can be attained by developing slow release fertilizers (SRFs) from biogas digestates. SRFs from biogas digestates can be developed by using natural clay minerals and degradable biopolymers because they are environment friendly, less costly and widely available.
Pakistan, being among the biggest consumers of chemical fertilizers, the development of SRF from biogas digestates will reduce the economic burden of the country and will address the sustainable waste management and crop production.

data.projectName: Metagenomic and Transcriptomic  study of  Wheat under drought  stress and co-application of hydrogen sulfide and rhizobacteria
data.projectDigest: Wheat is the staple food of millions of people all around the world, and drought is the major threat in its production. The country’s average wheat yield is  low as compared with other countries. To feed rising population, there is a matter  of great concern  to  develop  drought tolerant crops that can easily grow under water deficient area. Drought stress is one of the consequences of climate change that has a negative impact on crop growth and yield. Improving drought stress tolerance is a very challenging task for wheat researchers and more research is needed to better understand this stress. Drought  affects wheat crop both at seedling and reproductive stage. Our designed project will be the advancement in the studies related to drought  tolerance characterization in response to H2S exogenous and microbe’s treatment to Wheat   genotypes. Strategies such as reclamation of drought affected soils (labour extensive) and transgenic application is significantly affective in producing tolerant plants, but the outcomes always take long time. Therefore, introduction of some simple but efficient strategies in terms of fast outcomes delivery such as drought tolerance induction by application of plant growth regulators (PGR), signaling molecules and  plant growth promoting bacteria PGPR are utmost important. For instance, exogenous H2S application and rhizobacteria  could induce tolerance in plants against various stresses such as drought , photo-oxidative, heavy-metal and some other abiotic factors However, there is paucity of information reporting the functional attributes of H2S  and microbes to mitigate  drought stress  in Wheat. Synergistic  effect of signaling molecule hydrogen Sulfide and microbes on transcriptomic, metagenomic, morphological  and physiological  aspect

data.projectName: Hall Effect Measurements of Semiconductors Thin Films
data.projectDigest: This proposed research project deals with the electronic/electrical characterizations of semiconductors films by using Hall Effect measurements. The Hall effect characterizations include the measurement of  carrier concentrations, carrier mobility and electrical resistivity of the semiconductors films. Since these films are used in various sensors and electronic devices, therefore these measurements are of significant importance. The research carried out under this project will be useful for light sensing applications of semiconductor materials.

data.projectName: Theoretical Investigation of Unsteady MHDFlow within non-Stationary Porous Plates
data.projectDigest:
Porous-permeable structures and structured fins are the principal operational mechanism for enhancing the efficiency  of transport properties and dissipation  capacities of system because of their many physio-chemical characteristics. From several years, the stream of the unsteady viscid liquefied materials owing to its numerous methodological and systematic submissions have been a significant topic in the numerous widespread investigations of micro and  nano-fluidics. Applications of these systems are nuclear facility, high tech- refrigeration, computer architecture, rotational machinery, heat exchangers, computers based storage maneuvers, greases of porous-permeable machine parts  and anywhere the surfaces and discs are disconnected for  grease that is inserted within the discs.  

In this project, a study will be carried out in order to analyze behavior of the unsteady magneto-hydro-dynamic (MHD) flow, incompressible and two-dimensional viscid flow in two orthogonal movable porous-permeable plates . Amount of axial, rotational speed in the entire dominion will be investigated.  Behavior of circular velocity contour will also be studied near midpoint and  its declination or inclination  on  the  exteriors. Heat transfer studies will also be important to note.
