data.projectName: Efficient Visible-Light-Induced Integrated Photocatalytic Material for Disinfection of Air
data.projectDigest: Formation of the microbial colonies in wet and damp environment affect the indoor air quality thus posing severe threats to human health. Among various heterogeneous photocatalyst TiO2 gained much attention due to its non-toxic nature, high stability, excellent photocatalytic ability, self-cleaning and antibacterial properties and most of all low cost and commercial availability. It is among the basic materials being used in various commercial products like as white pigment in paints for building coating. The antibacterial properties are associated with the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in the presence of light source. Some of the reported TiO2 based nanomaterials-based air-filters and building coatings are reported with the major drawbacks like, lower surface area, inactivation in the absence of light (dark) and activation only under UV light irradiation. Thus, requirement for cost effective, safer and energy efficient materials are the need of the day. Aim of the proposed project is to develop a visible active TiO2 based integrated filtration material to solve the above reported issues. Activities to be undertaken to achieve the goal is the synthesis and performance evaluation of the visible light active heterogenous material using metal and non-metal TiO2 oxides and MOF-TiO2. Antimicrobial activities of the synthesized nanomaterial will be tested against G-ive and G+ive bacterial strains and their modes of interactions with DNA will be predicted using molecular docking simulation. To get knowledge about the insights of nanomaterials performance, most important is to understand their physicochemical properties by utilizing different characterization techniques. The proposed research project will contribute to multiple disciplines like material synthesis,

data.projectName: Virtual Reality for AMblyopia: The VRAM study
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Ophthalmology is one of the most technology dependent medical specialties that makes use of multiple imaging and electrodiagnostic tools along with software for diagnosis and effective treatment. Amongst the various eye diseases, amblyopia has the most impact on productivity and Disability Adjusted Life Years (DALY) of patients. Amblyopia, monocular or binocular, is commonly acquired during early childhood secondary to multiple ocular conditions, most common being uncorrected refractive error and ocular misalignment. Our proposed research aims to provide a solution that is low-cost and non-invasive VR-based system for recognition and treatment of amblyopia. This research is based on detailed study where we plan to enhance the treatment of amblyopia by projecting real time dynamic contrast and focus differential between the two eyes in form of engaging and fun games and activities. Our academic and sectorial collaborators like University of Pittsburgh, USA, and Armed forces institute of ophthalmology (AFIO), RWP will help in conducting detailed research study and finalizing the results to convert them into a product. Impact of such low-cost standardized system will have significant benefit for Pakistan. It will augment limited ophthalmology resources, reduce the economic and social burden of vision loss.

data.projectName: Enhancing coal mine safety through reinforced support system
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is blessed with vast mineral resources including both metallic and non-metallic types. In Punjab coal resources are distributed in the Salt range and Surghar range areas; extending from Jogi Tilla to Makerwal covering more than 250 km in length. Coal is being mined by local operators and some Government corporations and some semi-government corporations by employing modified form of longwall mining method in which the coal is approached via inclined opening or a shaft. Generally, the coal seam is thin (about 10 cm to 100 cm). The mine openings generally follow the orientation of the coal seam. These inclines and openings are constructed by drill and blast method and are supported with timber in the form of tri-doors based on the rules of thumb. The timber type in use is acacia-nilotica and eucalyptus. The working coal face is usually supported by the same timber in the form of chock support and T sets. The timber is believed to be very good support for local coal mines since it is cheap and gives warning sound before breaking in to pieces leading to rock falls. Also, it is easier to cut, adjust and install them in the small underground openings. Timber is unable to prevent roof-failure causing accidents which cause significant loss of money and precious lives. As mine timber is a natural material having inhomogeneous structure and anisotropic properties, there is a need to characterize mine timber and relate timber support design specifications and installation with local geology. Secondly strategies to reinforce mine timbers should be investigated while saving costs. This study will characterize mine timber with the help of laboratory testing. data.projectName: Preparation of 3D Printed Bioscaffolds from Decellularized Umbilical Cord for Cartilage Regeneration
data.projectDigest: Osteoarthritis is a degenerative disease, which affects more than 150 million people around the world. Since articular cartilage tissue has no or few number of vessels, therefore, after damage, it cannot regenerate itself. Biological scaffolds from the decellularization of native tissue provide signals in order to support the cellular mechanisms which support the cartilage regeneration. In this study, we plan to use the 3D fabricated bioscaffolds using decellularized umbilical cord for cartilage regeneration. The hydrated nature of umbilical cord is due to the amount of collagen, hyaluronic acid, and glycosaminoglycan present in it, which make it similar to cartilage tissue. Therefore this tissue can be used in cartilage tissue engineering applications due to its availability. This project aims to 3D fabricate the decellularized bioscaffolds using umbilical cord which will biomemic the native cartilage because of its composition and will solve the problem of using native cartilage, which is not available abundantly to be used as a decellularized tissue for cartilage regeneration. Further, these scaffolds can also be used with combination to patient specific lipoaspirate and platelet rich plasma which are already being used during surgical procedures to treat the osteoarthritis patients.

data.projectName: Fractional order Calculus based-filters for Biomedical Signal Processing
data.projectDigest: The fractional order calculus is a generalization of familiar classic integer order calculus. It investigates the possibility of taking real numbers and complex numbers as the power of differential and integral operators. Fractional order calculus has played influential part in biomedical signal processing and image processing. There is a wider range of applications in this domain based on fractional order calculus, for example, ECG waves detection, iris localization, image segmentation, fractal signals generation, and design of digital filters. A number of definitions of fractional differentiation and integration operators can be found in literature e.g. Riemann-Liouville, Caputo, Grünwald Letnikov, etc. Caputo's definition is beneficial when initial value problems arises,  Grünwald Letnikov's definition is exerted for numerical computation. From the viewpoint of system theory, fractional operators are implemented when passing an input signal by means of a filter using a transfer function. This filter links to a fractional differentiator or fractional integrator. The goal of this project is to present new definitions and generalizations of existing definitions such as the k-Riemann-Liouville fractional derivative and new approximations of fractional order operators and their utilization in the efficiency of results in signal modeling and in the design of digital filters in biomedical signal processing.

data.projectName: Development of IR paint for camouflage application in defence indusry
data.projectDigest: Being invisible to both the human eye and thermal imaging cameras is one of the most important factors to be considered in the defense sector. Special paints and color patterns are used for the camouflage of armored vehicles, tanks and soldiers etc. Special color patterns are painted on the body of the vehicle in such a way that it merges in the background and the vehicle cannot be distinguished from background.  In other words, that vehicle is invisible to the human eye. Everything emits infrared (IR) radiation of specific energy depending on their temperature, color, type of material, emissivity of material etc. Thermal imaging cameras use these IR radiations to produce an image. Vehicles, the human body etc will appear as high-temperature areas in thermal image. When IR paint is applied, it will control the emitted IR radiations from a body in such a way that its energy matches with the radiations coming from the objects in the background and so the vehicle and background will appear as same temperature areas and thus it will become invisible to thermal imaging camera as well.

data.projectName: Circulating microRNAs Profiling for Detection of Potential Noninvasive Biomarkers for Endometriosis
data.projectDigest:
Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory disorder characterized by presence of endometrial-like tissues outside the uterine cavity and causes considerable morbidity affecting overall 10% women of childbearing age and upto 50% women with infertility. Recently, endometriosis is  considered a progressive condition associated with heightened risk of different cancers and autoimmune disorders in affected women. Due to its chronic nature and incapacitating symptoms, endometriosis causes physical and mental distress and adds major health care costs. The diagnosis of endometriosis is still a challenging task. To date, there is no non-invasive test for endometriosis. The gold standard for diagnosis is an invasive surgical laparoscopic procedure followed by histological confirmation that is associated with risk of intraoperative or postoperative complications. On average there is a 7-12 years of delay period between the onset of clinical symptom and final diagnosis. The diagnostic delays may further lead to severity of the condition. Hence, the discovery of a non-invasive biomarker or a panel of such to reduce delay time in the diagnosis of endometriosis and decrease the need for surgery is an unmet clinical need. 
The proposed project aims to evaluate genome wide microRNAs (miRNAs) expression profile in plasma of endometriosis patients by RNA-seq approach followed by validation of prioritized candidate miRNAs in independent patient cohort for discovery of potential molecular biomarkers for endometriosis.

data.projectName: Harnessing of Spatial and Temporal Nanofibrous Smart-Scaffold for Bone Regeneration using In-vitro and In-vivo Model Systems
data.projectDigest: Bone defects due to incidents such as diseases (osteoporosis and osteosarcoma), fractures, or surgeries (tumor removal) are treated using allografts (from a donor of the same species), autografts (tissue from the person’s own body), or xenografts (from a donor of a different species). These agents have shown variable clinical efficacy based on their limited availability, disease transfer, donor scarcity, ability to modulate inflammatory responses and stimulate immune rejection. Tissue engineering has attracted significant interest in solving the crises of organ transplantation. However, the induction of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) during tissue regeneration remains a big challenge. Thus, we proposed a biomimetic three-dimensional (3D) scaffold system in combination with small molecule (Tideglusib, a GSK-3? inhibitor) for spatial and temporal induction system that have the potential to enhance stem cells differentiation and bone tissue regeneration. Tideglusib that induce the Wnt signaling have the capability to stimulate the cellular functions and are becoming attractive for bone tissue engineering purposes. However, tideglusib-incorporated nanofibrous matrix induces BMSCs differentiation and bone regeneration is unknown. Therefore, we hypothesized the use of tideglusib-incorporated nanofibrous scaffold for proliferation and differentiation of BMSCs cells in-vitro and finally for the bone regeneration in-vivo.

data.projectName: Patronizing camel milk pasteurization and commercialization for Sustainable Dairy Development in Rahim Yar Khan-Punjab-Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: Cholistan (Rahim Yar khan) is one of the largest deserts of Pakistan and part of the great Indian desert Rajasthan having rich diversity of temperature ranges from 6 to 50 0C and homeland of many precious animal genetic resources particularly with variety of Camel breeds. Unfortunately, camel is employed for transportation purposes and least utilized as dairy animal. Camel milk is nutritionally balanced (52 U insulin/L and three times more vitamin C) in all aspects and is considered as nature’s pharmacy for masses owing to its medicinal and therapeutic characteristics. In Cholistan, a big chunk of camel milk is utilized by the camel rearing people to fulfil their dietary requirements and hinders camel milk to cold supply chain. This proposed project will channelize camel milk production that will ultimately benefit to dairy processors while reduce pressure on already available milk resources and also become a new milk resource. Camel milk pasteurization and commercialization will not only be enabling us to address food insecurity and also a significant tool for poverty alleviation of the nomads of the desert. In terms of business opportunity this project will provide us a chance for patronizing camel milk pasteurization and commercialization as sole proprietorship.

data.projectName: Differential Ion Transport Mediated Guard Cell Regulation between Glycophyte and Halophyte under Salinity
data.projectDigest: Soil salinity is environmental issue which affects crop productivity.  In Pakistan, 6.68 Mha land is saline, and its increasing every year due to continuous salt buildup. Therefore, salinity becomes an everlasting challenge for agriculture and requires innovative approaches to improve food security by making crop plants more salt tolerant. For achieving this target a better knowledge about mechanisms of naturally salt tolerant plants (halophytes) is needed which help in identifying the basic requirements for enhance salt tolerance of crops. Salinity inhibits yield by imposing several constraints including reduced water availability, accumulation of toxic ions and increased ROS production. Plant yield is determined by their ability to gain/assimilate CO2 which is regulated by stomatal aperture. Stomata are tiny pores on leaves formed via pair of guard cells that open/close to regulate CO2 intake for photosynthesis and water loss by transpiration. Halophytes more efficiently regulate guard cells in salinity than glycophytes, but still comprehensive information is lacking about special guard cells regulatory mechanism of halophytes. Therefore, our focus is to understand the “Differential ion transport mediated guard cell regulation between glycophyte and halophyte under salinity”. Such information could be useful in future to better improve the salinity tolerance of crops especially wheat.

data.projectName: Developing Inexpensive Plasma Treatment Reactor for Controlling Foodborne and Human Pathogens
data.projectDigest:
The ecological environment degradation, the acceleration of natural cataclysms and environmental concerns are of increasing importance among the top challenges and issues of human society due to recent advancement and sharp world population growth. The urgency of microbiological safety maintenance rises steeply. In this context, utilization of clean sources such as solar energy, heating, Ultraviolet radiations and plasma, all of which are inexhaustible at no cost, is considered to be the most appropriate and effective systems in solving the human health and environmental related issues. A conspicuous example is that of plasma, which is efficient sterilizing agent, portable, short range, and user-friendly productive system. 
In this regard, atmospheric-pressure plasmas have been widely investigated and used in health care, medical, electrochemistry, surface treatment and sterilization. Among plasmas, atmospheric pressure plasma in liquid are very effective in bacterial disinfection and inhibition of biofilms on meat surface. 
The aim of this project is to develop a novel plasma reactor with the help of single and multi-electrodes in a capillary tube with canonical base having saline solution powered by voltage pulses of direct current (DC) source. Highly reactive plasma species such as electrons and ions, atomic and molecular radicals will be produced during this process. In liquid discharge, these species include reactive oxygen species (ROS) such as O, O2, O3 and hydroxyl ions (OH).  Then these reactive species will be allowed to interact with the food-born and human pathogens to study the peculiarities of microorganism’s inactivation. This setup will be an efficient system for sterile both food surfaces and water from the environment and in turn reduces the risk.

data.projectName: Genetic diversity and insecticide resistance patterns of Tephritid flies and their insecticide resistance patterns in erstwhile FATA, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Fruit flies (Diptera: Tephritidae) are economically important horticulture pests that cause significant losses to horticulture industry. They lay eggs under the skin that hatch into larvae and feed on flesh resulting in premature falling of fruits or vegetable. Pakistan earn billions from its horticultural industry but in-depth studies on fruit fly fauna is deficient particularly the previously known FATA regions of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. An estimated loss of 24 % to cucurbits, 50 to 80% infestation  level in peach, fig, apricot and pear, 50 to 55 % damage to guava has been reported in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Fruit flies have been controlled through integrated pest  management strategies. Although use of insecticides is more frequently practiced in Pakistan and particularly in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. This proposed research proposal will provide baseline information regarding fruit fly bionomics in the unexplored region of FATA.  This study will also focus on biochemical and molecular aspects of insecticide resistance. Moreover, molecular characterisation of fruit fly species in the region will provide an insight towards the genetic diversity of the pests  compared to its neighbouring countries. The project has implications towards improving the pest management strategies in the FATA region.

data.projectName: Assessment of 21st Century skills among University students: An analytical comparative study of USA and Pakistani Classrooms
data.piUniversity: National University of Modern Languages, Islamabad (NUML)
data.projectDigest: Research indicates that the ways in which students look at learning are influenced by the ways in which they perceive assessment tasks. In this backdrop, the main purpose of the current study is to investigate the contemporary trends and practices regarding classroom assessments at Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) in Pakistan and USA. Moreover, to design an appropriate classroom assessment framework to develop 21st century skills among University students. Both qualitative and quantitative research methods will be used in this study to probe the appropriate assessment practices and to develop tenable assessment framework model for Pakistani HEIs. Questionnaire and interviews will be conducted to determine the current assessment practices in the USA and Pakistan’s HEIs. Recommendations will be made on the basis of findings regarding appropriate assessment practices in HEIs to foster students learning and untimely producing best possible graduates for the nation. The findings of this two-year project would directly be useful to US HEIs, Higher Education Commissions (HEC) of Pakistan, and HEIs from other developing countries. The current study will provide organizational leaders and policymaker with a framework for effective implementation of classroom assessment to help graduates to meet the 21st century job market needs.

data.projectName: COMBINATION THERAPY IN TREATMENT OF LEISHMANIASIS
data.projectDigest:
Leishmaniasis is parasitic disease which is geographically distributed in Africa, Asia, and rest of world. Scientists are working on safe, potent and economical drug. This work was performed to understand the mode of action of combination therapy on targeted molecules like Ornithine decarboxylase against Leishmaniasis. 
Combination therapy is promising tool to reduce toxicity, and to improve efficacy of drugs. Topical utilization of gels at obsessive destinations offer incredible favorable actions in fast on set of medications when compared with other dosage form like ointments and creams. The validated targeted molecules like Ornithine decarboxylase enzymes have affinity to metallic compounds, and Flavonoids and other phenolic compounds which may result in inhibition of microbial enzymes activity. 
In vitro test was performed on cell lines which after positive results lead to in vivo analysis of targeted molecules with 24 hours up to 48 hours. As reference drug, Sodium Stibogluconate was used. During BALB/c mice analysis, size of Lesions was determined after administration of test compounds. Lymphocytes were used in cytotoxic analysis which showed that test agents are Non-toxic. Emulgel was prepared and applied to CL patients.
Analysis revealed that combination therapy has inhibitory effect against Leishmania Tropica which is due to ornithine decarboxylase.

data.projectName: Genome wide association mapping of disease resistance traits in Juniper species and genetic stability of Juniper plants produced via in vitro culture.
data.piUniversity: Balochistan University of Information Technology, Engineering and Management Sciences,Quetta
data.projectDigest: Juniper is the world oldest living species on the earth called as living fossils, their age is up to 2000 years. Balochistan has approximately 141,000 hector of Juniperus forests. The forest has potential scientific value because of the advanced age of stands and individual trees. However, Juniper is threatened tree in Pakistan reported by IUCN Red List Pakistan. The species is facing great disease due to dwarf mistletoe, an epiphytic angiosperm and a destructive parasite Arceuthobium oxycedri (DC). Almost 25% of the forest is infected and the remaining huge numbers of trees turn into the entity of the disease. No effective remedial measures have been established yet to combat with this disease except to cut the tree. To evade extinction, Juniper population must be resistant against the diseases, adapt, or migrate. Plant tissue culture technique has enabled us to produce tremendous quantities of Juniper plantlets. Furthermore, proper check on molecular level using molecular markers has ensured strict quality control for a desired clone production. Whereas, the genetic interaction for host- pathogen determines the various natural variations in genes found in the host for disease resistance.  The proposed research project aims to develop the optimum micro propagation system and to monitor the genetic uniformity of the micro propagated plant  and to identify the genes/QTLs linked with resistance to dwarf mistletoes.

However, Juniper is threatened tree in Pakistan reported by IUCN Red List Pakistan. The species is facing great disease due to dwarf mistletoe, an epiphytic angiosperm and a destructive parasite Arceuthobium oxycedri (DC). Almost 25% of the forest is infected and the remaining huge numbers of trees turn into the entity of the disease. No effective remedial measures have been established yet to combat with this disease except to cut the tree. To evade extinction, Juniper population must be resistant against the diseases, adapt, or migrate. Plant tissue culture technique has enabled us to produce tremendous quantities of Juniper plantlets. Furthermore, proper check on molecular level using molecular markers has ensured strict quality control for a desired clone production. Whereas, the genetic interaction for host- pathogen determines the various natural variations in genes found in the host for disease resistance.  The proposed research project aims to develop the optimum micro propagation system and to monitor the genetic uniformity of the micro propagated plant  and to identify the genes/QTLs linked with resistance to dwarf mistletoes.

data.projectName: The removal of Cr from tannery wastewater using surfactants modified  biochars
data.projectDigest: Chromium is highly toxic metal for living organisms. It is employed in various industries including leather tanning, glass industries, production of steel, mining and electroplating etc. There are various methods to remove chromium from wastewaters like filtration, ion exchange, chemical precipitation and adsorption. Tannery wastewaters in Pakistan with toxic levels of Chromium are posing threats to livestock, humans and plants. Treatment plants established at the contaminated sites are unable to filter the wastewaters completely and are costly. Biochar, a form of charcoal pyrolysed under low oxygen conditions is a cost effective and environmental friendly sorbent. Biochar can be used to treat wastewaters due to its porous structure and cation exchange properties. The present study aims to evaluate the applicability of biochars derived from algae, eucalyptus and Jatropha Curcas for the sorptive removal of chromium from tannery wastewater. The woody organic feedstocks of algae, eucalyptus and Jatropha will be subjected to various pre and post pyrolysis treatments with surfactants to activate or enhance adsorption capacity of biochars. This study will also assess the effect of different parameters on the sorption process. The key parameters will be contact time, initial ion concentration, solution pH and sorbent particle size.  A filter will be developed on pilot scale. Batch and column studies will be planned in laboratory to assess biochar potential for enhanced sorption. A small pot study and a field trial will be conducted to check the chromium uptake of plant from biochar amended contaminated soil. This study will help in tannery wastewater treatment cost effectively as well as conservation of the soil and environment by application of biochar.

data.projectName: :  Molecular characterization of Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus, causal agent of citrus greening disease and its vector Asian citrus Psyllid: Use of RNA interference for disease management
data.piUniversity: Lahore College for Women University, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Huanglongbing (HLB) or citrus greening is a devastating disease of citrus crops worldwide. The introduced Asian citrus psyllid (ACP) Diaphorina citri Kuwayama transmits the (putative) causal uncultured bacterial pathogen, Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus (CLas). CLas infects most citrus cultivars, species and hybrids and even some citrus relatives. Infected leaves develop a blotchy mottle appearance while fruit becomes small, lopsided, poorly colored, and contain aborted seeds. The juice from affected fruit is low in soluble solids, high in acids and abnormally bitter. 
	Disease management is complicated and it includes production of disease-free nursery, psyllid control by insecticides, salicylic acid and/or phosphite and removal of symptomatic trees but there is agreement that none of these control strategies completely eliminates HLB transmission. 
	One of the most promising technologies for disease management that have been used in agriculture is the use of RNA interference (RNAi). This method allows a gene-specific silencing of transcripts responsible for the maintenance of the cellular homeostasis, resulting in the reduction of the vector in the field. In this project RNAi will be used to silence candidate target genes of ACP by synthesizing dsRNA and feeding ACP.

data.projectName: In situ-Mechanical, Tribological and Electrochemical behavior of Thermally sprayed Aluminum composite coatings reinforced with ceramic particles
data.projectDigest: Aluminum (Al) and its alloys are widely used in automotive and aerospace industry owing to low density (light weight), high strength, good ductility, and corrosion resistance. This metal and its alloys can also be deposited on different metallic substrates as decorative and corrosion resistant coatings but cannot improve wear resistance of the metallic substrates. In order to improve wear, abrasion, corrosion, and erosion resistance different ceramic materials like tungsten carbide (WC), alumina (Al2O3), titania (TiO2) etc. can be added to the coating. The coating material can be deposited on the substrate using thermal spraying technique in which molten or semi-molten powder particles are sprayed onto the surface of metallic substrate. By the deposition of Al-WC or Al-Al2O3 novel coatings on low cost/ductile plain carbon steels, their in-service performance and lifetime can be remarkably improved. The testing will involve state of the art near palm sized micro-tensile testing device which could be placed under AFM tip or objective lens of optical-microscope or inside SEM chamber to observe the deformation and fracture mechanism of coated samples under loads. After successful experimentation during this project, the samples from industry will be thermally sprayed with Al-composite coatings, and subjected to required real-time quality testing.

data.projectName: Molecular characterization and epidemiology of antibiotic resistance genes of BETA-Lactamase producing Klebsiella pneumoniae from clinical isolates of tertiary care hospitals, District Peshawar.
data.projectDigest:
Resistance towards available antibiotics provides ability to various pathogenic bacteria to resist the effects of an antibiotic in different ways for making its survival possible in the presence of a chemical, drug or other active agents, causing more damage. 
Resistance against antibiotics is one of the world's most critical community health troubles. Due to antibiotic resistance most of the treatable illnesses with available antibiotics are now becoming treacherous infections. There are different pathogens that cause brutal human infections but our study is specific for Klebsiella pneumoniae. The most resistant strains of K. pneumoniae produces ?-lactamase enzymes which make them resistant to ?-lactam antibiotics. 
Infections caused by multi drug resistant Gram negative bacilli producing ?-lactamases are associated with high death rates. Their treatment is challenging because of resistant to various antimicrobial agent. 
The rapidly growing population of Pakistan faces enormous range of infectious diseases and an antibiotic resistance disaster at the forefront thrust in Pakistan, the panorama of threatening medical blow is looming. Antibiotics intended for treatment of infections and slab the increase of bacteria as super bugs have developed resistance over quite a few decades. According to an estimate 1.1 billion people are affected with ?-lactamase producing bacteria in South Asia including Pakistan. Efforts to mitigate the negative impact of antibiotic resistance should be based on sound surveillance data; knowledge of the epidemiology (prevalence, sources and transmission routes) of these resistant bacteria will be critical in controlling their spread in the community, which will ultimately lead to reduce the incidence of antibiotic-resistant infections.

data.projectName: A novel gene selection algorithm for microarray cancer classification using self-hybrid inertia weight adaptive particle swarm optimization
data.projectDigest: Gene selection is important steps in for the classification of microarray data. Gene expression data (DNA microarray) facilitate researchers to concurrently measure the levels of expression of several number of genes. Since hybrid particle swarm optimization has no complex evolutionary operators and less parameters required to tune, it has been used for gene selection. To select predictive genes with low redundancy as well as not filtering out key genes is still a challenge. To overcome the deficiencies of traditional particle swarm optimization based gene selection methods, a hybrid gene selection method based on gene scoring strategy and self-hybrid inertia weight adaptive particle swarm optimization is proposed in this manuscript.  In the proposed method, SIWAPSO encoding gene to class sensitivity information is used to achieve gene selection. The gene to class sensitivity information, removed from the models by extreme learning machine is prearranged into the selection process is stars with initializing particles, updating the particles, modifying maximum velocity, and then adopting mutation operation adaptively. With the few discriminative genes selected by the proposed method, ELM, K- centroid nearest neighbor (KCNN) with k=1 and support vector machine (SVM) achieve much high prediction accuracy on different public microarray data, which in turn verifies the efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed gene selection method.

data.projectName: Genomic Prospect of Triple Negative breast cancer  (TNBC) of Population of Sindh .
data.projectDigest: Cancer is one of the major causes of death throughout the world, According to WHO estimates for 2011, cancer now causes more deaths than all coronary heart disease or all stroke. The rate of cancer in Pakistan increases day by day. Asian countries are more victims to cancer in this era especially Pakistan has been more alarming condition regarding breast cancer, while breast cancer was uncommon few years back in Pakistan, but now breast cancer is most common carcinoma found in Pakistani female.  The Triple negative breast cancer is the lack of expression of hormones e.g. estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR) and Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2), it is reported that 12–17% of breast cancers and clinically apparent as a distinct breast cancer subgroup. TNBC mostly frequently occur in younger women and these types of tumor are generally larger in size more aggressive and higher grade, and show the lymph node involvements at the time of diagnosis.  However, TNBC has been shown to constitute a vastly heterogeneous disease encompassing a wide spectrum of entities with marked genetic, transcriptional, histological and clinical differences. Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is highly heterogeneous. TNBCs demonstrated higher frequencies of PIK3CA mutations and the luminal androgen receptor subtype, implying a need for the adjustment of clinical management. In Pakistan there is limited number of TNBCs have been analyzed, and molecular prognosis of the breast cancer has not established yet therefore it is necessary to develop the frame work of the TNBC, genetic study and their  treatment is essential to save the Pakistani population. A key determinant of breast cancer outcome in any population is the degree to which it is detected at an early stage.

data.projectName: Realization of colossal dielectric constant in ZnO based materials
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Materials which have dielectric constant (real part of permittivity) are of great interest due to their applications in miniaturization of microelectronic devices  and high density energy  storage. Recently, Hu et al. have proposed a defect engineering approach to achieve high dielectric constant in indium (In) and niobium (Nb) co-doped titania (TiO2). They reported realization of high dielectric constant (>104) having no frequency & temperature dependence with negligible losses (<0.05). Separate doping of Nb (i.e. donor) or In (i.e. acceptor) in TiO2 could not produce CP independent of temperature & frequency with low tangent loss. Electron-pinned defect-dipoles, in which donor donates electrons for hopping while acceptor localizes electron around defect, were argued to be the reason for high dielectric constant. The aim of this project is to employ ZnO for the realization of CP by using electron-pinned defects-dipoles by employing donor and acceptor doping at the same time. Furthermore, composite of different band gap materials can introduce interface effects that may lead to CP with low dielectric losses. Therefore, ZnO composite with other high permittivity materials may also disclose unique and unexplored physics of the interfaces.

data.projectName: Convergence Analysis of Proximal Point Algorithm in Spaces of Non-Positive Sectional Curvature
data.projectDigest:
Optimization has been a basic tool in all areas of applied mathematics
including applications in engineering, medicine, economics, management, industry and other sciences. Moreover, optimization has been a major motivation and driving force for the development of differential and integral calculus. As a consequence, this subject is not only expanding in all directions of sciences but also serve as interdisciplinary bridge between various branches of sciences. In order to solve an optimization problem, one can use either optimization algorithms or iterative methods for the feasible solution. Iterative
methods are ubiquitous in the theory of optimization and still new iterative and theoretical techniques have been proposed and analyzed for the solution of various real world and theoretical problems which can be modeled in the general framework of optimization.

The class of proximal point algorithms (PPA) is prominent in the
theory of optimization. This class includes the classical PPA and its variants for optimization. Most of the results in the theory of optimization involving PPA are ineffective as the results do not provide any numerical rates of convergence. The purpose of the present research proposal is to establish convergence characteristics of PPA in spaces of non-positive sectional curvature and compute corresponding rates of convergence and metastability for the class of PPA. We use tools from mathematical logic - - which have been used successfully for the above said purpose in various fields such as numerical analysis, functional analysis, metric fixed point theory, number theory and algebra - - for the extraction of rates of convergence for the class of gradient iterative methods.

data.projectName: Microbial Electrochemical Cells: Green technology to convert organic waste into sustainable bio-electricity and valuable chemicals
data.projectDigest: Waste water and environmental pollution is a major concern for developing countries besides energy crisis.  Various treatment technologies previously used to turn waste into energy are not sustainable. They require lot of energy and cost is intensive without any economical benefit. Pakistan alone is responsible for about 48.5 million tons of solid waste a year, with 2% increase annually. Problems like provision of adequate energy and clean water supply have been a challenging task for nations. Microbial electrochemical cell is a sustainable green technology which uses microbial bioelectrochemical potential to generate bio-electricity by oxidizing organic substrate present in variety of wastes e.g. municipal sewage, dairy, agricultural, food and industrial. The basic concept in it is to use bacteria for oxidation of biodegradable organic/inorganic compounds in the anode compartment releasing electrons to the anode. Protons produced in anode compartment are transferred to cathode comportment via conductive membrane. Microbial electrochemical cell through anaerobic digestion generates bio-electricity or valuable chemical compounds like ethanol, methane and hydrogen peroxide.  We aim to study basics of wastewater treatment, organic substrate utilization, nutrient and metal recovery capacity, energy  production using microbial electrochemical cells.

data.projectName: Chitosan-silver nanocomposite-driven angiogenic intervention for effective infection control and skin wound recovery
data.projectDigest: Skin is the largest body organ. Healthy skin has three layers including epidermis, dermis, and hypodermis. Its main functions are protection, regulation, and sensation, which are dependent on its structure’s integrity. Skin functioning is adversely affected when there is skin injury. Skin injury could be due to some cut or burn. Skin wounds, especially deep tissue wounds, are very prone to bacterial infections. Traditional treatments such as ointments and creams are widely used to assist the treatment of the wounds. However, their frequent application, inability to absorb exudates, need for repeated washing of wound bed, and poor drug penetration results in poor healing leading to chronic wounds. Particular safety protocols are needed for wound decontamination and therapeutic purpose that can be achieved by using wound dressing, which controls the biochemical conditions of the wound to aid the healing process. No wound dressing is ideal, but a dressing must meet the minimum requirements, i.e. low frequency of application, ability to absorb exudates, no need for repeated washing of wound bed, and improved drug penetration. In this study, polymeric nanocomposite-based wound dressing would be fabricated for effective infection control and skin wound recovery.

data.projectName: Antibiotic loaded Nano-Drug Carriers for treatment of resistant bacterial infections
data.projectDigest: Antibiotics are the chemical entities, which either stop the growth of bacteria or exterminate the bacteria depending upon the mechanism of action of the compound. All over the world the emergence of multidrug resistant bacteria due to the abuse of antibiotics have provoked a prototype swing in the well-known understanding of antibiotic and bacteria–human relations. Some of the important factors leading to the poor clinical outcomes of conventional antibiotics are an early enzymatic degradation of antibiotics, slow penetration of antibiotics at the site of infection, washout of natural microflora and development of mutational resistance against the antibiotics.  Drug delivery systems developed so far, can shield/protect antibiotics from enzyme deactivation, increasing the therapeutic effectiveness of the drug. These formulations hinder the early washout from the gut and prolong the stay time of antibiotic therapeutics. To the best of our knowledge, not a single drug delivery system, so far, have been developed to address the permeation and efflux pump related resistant mechanism of bacteria. Therefore, the aim of the project is develop novel drug delivery systems, which not only protect the therapeutic compound against the gastric environment, also increase the permeation through bacterial cell membranes by inhibiting the efflux pump.

data.projectName: Development of Green Composites with Enhanced Thermal Stability, Mechanical Properties and Eco-friendly Characteristics to Replace the Synthetic Plastic Based Material
data.projectDigest: Consumption of non-biodegradable materials is causing landfills, ocean pollution, drainage blockages and health hazards. Replacing the synthetic plastic material with biodegradable material is the only solution to avoid such problems in future. This proposal suggests the development of eco-friendly Natural Fibers Reinforced Composites (NFRC) for application in interior parts of automobiles, aerospace, marines, insulation and packaging industries. Besides their low cost, renewability and biodegradable characteristics, NFRC have some drawbacks which include poor thermal stability and higher flammability. This proposal is aimed to enhance thermal stability and fire retardant properties of NFRC. For this purpose, some nano-fillers (including bio-waste) will be incorporated into the composites to modify their flammability mechanism. The addition of fire retardant fillers decreases some of the mechanical properties of the composites, which will also be studied in the current research work. It is also aimed to add some micro-seeds to the composites during fabrication. Once this material is dumped, the seeds will grow a plant from the soil, while the bioplastic and natural fibers will degrade and help in enhancing the soil fertilization. Overall, an eco-friendly material with improved fire resistance and mechanical properties will be developed for targeted applications.

data.projectName: Development of a Hybrid Air Cleaning System for Indoor Air Pollution Control
data.projectDigest: Household air pollution is a major threat to the health.There are at least sixty sources of household air pollution. The main sources include the fuels, tobacco smoking, construction material, furniture, carpets, dry cleaning, paints, pesticides and chemicals for cleaning, artificial fragrances. These pollutants may include carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, black carbon emission, nitrogen dioxide, benzene, particulate matters, 1, 3 butadiene formaldehyde, and poly aromatic compounds such as benzo (?) pyrene. During peak cooking hours, the concentration of indoor air pollution can be several times greater than safety limits. It results in respiratory diseases such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), acute lower respiratory infections (IRI) but also with tuberculosis and lung cancer. The aim of this project is to develop an air cleaning system to control indoor air pollution. The air cleaning system will be based on techniques such as photocatalysis, adsorption and most importantly a hybrid of these two technologies. Photocatalysts are materials when activated by light can destroy harmful pollutants. Likewise, adsorbents can adsorb harmful pollutants by physio- or chemosorption. The combination of photocatalysis and adsorption is expected to show more promising results as it will have the capacity to control all type of air pollutants.
data.projectSummary: Household air pollution is a major threat to the health.There are at least sixty sources of household air pollution. The main sources include the fuels, tobacco smoking, construction material, furniture, carpets, dry cleaning, paints, pesticides and chemicals for cleaning, artificial fragrances. These pollutants may include carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, black carbon emission, nitrogen dioxide, benzene, particulate matters, 1, 3 butadiene formaldehyde, and poly aromatic compounds such as benzo (?) pyrene. During peak cooking hours, the concentration of indoor air pollution can be several times greater than safety limits. It results in respiratory diseases such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), acute lower respiratory infections (IRI) but also with tuberculosis and lung cancer. The aim of this project is to develop an air cleaning system to control indoor air pollution. The air cleaning system will be based on techniques such as photocatalysis, adsorption and most importantly a hybrid of these two technologies. Photocatalysts are materials when activated by light can destroy harmful pollutants. Likewise, adsorbents can adsorb harmful pollutants by physio- or chemosorption. The combination of photocatalysis and adsorption is expected to show more promising results as it will have the capacity to control all type of air pollutants.

This project will also reveal the remarkable potential of archival research on SDGs. In a developing country like Pakistan, the community needs pragmatic implementation of SDGs with authentic leaders.

data.projectName: Genetic etiology of suicidal behavior with serotonin related genes in psychiatric patients
data.projectDigest: Suicide is an intentional way to end one’s own life or to finish him. Suicide constitutes a multifactorial public health problem that involves many biological, psychological, cultural, social, and family determinants. The WHO estimates that nearly 800,000 people die by suicide every year, making it a global phenomenon. This outbreak has plagued Pakistani citizens for many decades and now this issue is rising day by day, but despite its fatal consequences in the form of untimely and unnatural deaths, there are no official statistics available on the suicide rates nationwide, nor are the statistics reported to World Health Organization (WHO). Suicidal behaviors (SBs), which range from suicidal ideation to suicide attempts and completed suicide, represent a lethal dimension of mental ill-health.The serotonergic pathway has been incriminated for several decades as having a major character in the pathophysiology of SB. A number of reviews of the literature have studied the association of SB with common serotonergic gene polymorphisms. This study will help to find out the main genetic culprit for the suicide which will play a role in the control of suicides.

data.projectName: Potential therapeutic approach in breast cancer patients from Pakistani Population: An in vitro Preclinical Study
data.projectDigest: Breast cancer is the most common health disorder among women throughout the globe and the second foremost cause of death in Pakistani women. Among Asian countries, Pakistan is on the top with 43 years of median age. The most prevalent diagnostic age group is 36 to 45 year with a high incidence in young females which is alarming. It has been hypothesized that for better treatment impact of combination therapy is more effective than single drug medication. Aim of current study is to investigate Mevalonate (MVA) inhibitor in Breast cancer patients from Pakistani population. MVA pathway regulates metabolic cellular processes and growth of cell cycle. Previously we have determined alone and synergistic effect of bisphosphonate and a chemotherapeutic drug on breast cancer cell line (Patent applied). Current study aims to demonstrate effect of proposed regimen in our population by preparing primary breast cell culture directly from human breast tissue. Genomic and proteomic approach will be performed to identify differential gene and protein expression of key regulatory enzymes of MVA pathway along with immunocytochemistry to validate protein expression. Current proposal may provide an insight to understand the role of combination therapy as effective anticancer regimen that could be a new therapeutic approach for our population.

data.projectName: liquid biopsy:molecular characterization of circulating tumor cells and their clinical significance in epithelial ovarian carcinoma
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Ovarian malignancy is a leading cause of gynaecological related cancer mortality throughout the world. Ovarian cancer encompasses heterogenous group of malignant tumor of ovarian origin that may arise from germ cells, stromal tissue or epithelial tissue within the ovary. Epithelial ovarian cancer constitute about 90% of ovarian malignancy1 and is further classified into five main types: high grade serous, endometrioid, clear cell, mucinous and low grade serous carcinomas.2 The prognosis for survival is dependent on staging and histopathologic type. High grade serous carcinoma found in approximately 80% of ovarian cancers usually diagnosed at an advanced stage iii or iv which is responsible for poor outcome and prognosis.The initial management include Primary surgery which is required for diagnosis, staging and maximal cytoreduction .CTCs are the tumor cells which are shed from the primary tumor, local recurrence or metastasis in circulatory system. These cells are viable with specific phenotypic and genotypic characteristicsDetecting CTCs in peripheral blood of patients with epithelial ovarian cancer is found to be feasible. It is a noninvasive test which is relatively easy for collection, enumeration and monitoring of the disease. The CTCs can be used with other diagnostic tests to increase its sensitivity and specificity and improve the diagnosis of ovarian cancer. It can also be employed in advanced stages of malignancy for neo adjuvant chemotherapy followed by interval debulking to improve the survival of the patients.
Dectection of CTCs in remission period will help in early prediction of recurrence and thus starting specific targeted drugs will prolong a good healthy survival in these advanced stage cancers.

data.projectName: Isolation and characterization of efficient Bacillus strains as catalysts for sustainable production of Soyabean/Sugarcane in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Plant infections and productivity losses are among the most important global issues considering the current population growth rate index. During the recent years, a continued decline in agriculture output has been recorded due to changing climate, deterioration of the habitats and infections of the plants by microbial pathogens. In Pakistan, these loses are quite high and may reach up to 40 % of the total production. In order to increase crop yield, supplementation of the chemical pesticides and fertilizers are the integral component of the current agriculture practices. Extensive use of the agro-chemicals poses serious environmental and health repercussions, therefore, new insights should be taken into account for developing future plant protection strategies with least negative effects. Considering the present situation of environmental pollution and food security issues, it is high time to develop innovative, cost effective and sustainable agriculture methods. The use of soil microorganisms as catalysts for effective pest management and promoting plant growth has been among the contemporary approaches being successfully implementation across the globe. Being an agriculture country, Pakistan needs to adopt these innovative technologies in order to reduce production lose during pre and post harvesting stages. Current project will typically focus on the application of beneficial soil microbes having the abilities to control plant pathogens and stimulating plant growth and development for better crop production

data.projectName: Carotenoids Fingerprinting of Edible Fruits and Vegetables
data.piUniversity: University of Malakand, Chakdara, Dir, Malakand
data.projectDigest: Carotenoids are organic compounds widely distributed in nature. Because of the special structural variety, and numerous important functions, it is well known from food to pharmaceutical industries. More than seven hundreds carotenoids have been identified and characterized from plant comprise of fruits, vegetables and none vegetable foods. Carotenoids are one of the main source of pro-vitamin A. Pakistan is severely affected by the deficiency of vitamin A. This deficiency is not only limited to vision, but also competes for other chronic conditions such as premature aging, heart diseases, and cancer. In order to overcome such conditions, carotenoids from foods are widely used. However, there is no information available regarding the carotenoids contents of foods available in Pakistan. For this purpose, fruits and vegetables will be collected from the different regions of Pakistan. Carotenoids will be extracted and analyzed using HPLC-DAD and quantified against the available standards and procedures. A database will be developed and will be used for the analysis of carotenoids in other sources. Formulation of daily dietary requirement will be carried out based on the database. The database will be available for the public in order to minimize the chronic conditions related to antioxidants and carotenoids.

data.projectName: The effect of nutritional status and gut microbial diversity on stunt growth in Sindh
data.projectDigest: Growth retardation is highly prevalent in developing countries which is caused by inadequate food intake and infections. This retardation leads to the development of stunted growth. In developing countries, stunting affects one-third of children under 5 years and 14% of childhood deaths are caused by it. Pakistan has high rate of child malnutrition leading to stunted growth and as per UNICEF report 38 percent of the children under 5 years are stunted. The province of Sindh has particularly high rate of stunted growth where almost 50 percent of the children are stunted and the number is increasing. No information is available regarding the role of malnutrition, minerals, vitamins, heavy metal and gut microbiome in stunted growth in children of Sindh. As the nutritional status and gut microbiome have role in the healthy life, the hypothesis of this study is to check either there is any association of nutritional status, minerals, vitamins, heavy metal and gut microbiome with the stunted growth in children of Sindh. In this project we will determine the individual’s nutritional status and Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) based gut microbiome potentially leading to personalized microbial medicine to mitigate stunted growth.

data.projectName: Exploration of the Nonlinear Optical and Optoelectronic Properties of D-?-A and Octupolar Organic Materials for Modern Hi-Tech Applications
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: The nonlinear optical (NLO) field has become a fascinating research area for researchers due to promising NLO applications in diverse photonic technologies. Recently, the researchers reported NLO properties of inorganic and organic compounds. However, according to the best of our knowledge, NLO properties of proposed systems have not been studied yet. Therefore, we plan two main axis of this research proposal: (i) design new-conjugated based push-pull organic compounds through structural tuning of auxiliary units on synthesized functional materials (triphenylamine-dicyanovinylene, fluorene and non fluorene compounds), (ii) novel 1,3,4-oxadiazoles derivatives will be synthesized to explore the octupolar and non-centrosymmetric crystals. Moreover, density functional theory will be applied to study NLO properties of proposed systems. For testing purpose, we selected one derivative from designed fluorene-based D-PI-A dyes series to determine the NLO response using B3LYP/311+G(d,p) functional. Subsequently, its NLO response (Beta total) has been achieved as 268148.4661 (a.u). The standard compound as 4-(dimethylamino)-4-nitrostylbene (DANS) is taken for comparative analysis, which is usually considered as NLO standard in the literature. The NLO response of our designed compound is found 49 times greater than a reference DANS molecule. Therefore, it is expected to explore new insights into the NLO parameters of conjugated D-PI-A compounds using state-of-the-art computational modeling.

data.projectName: Microstructural Tuning of Human Friendly "Shape Memory Alloys" for Cardiovascular and other Biomedical Applications
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest:
Materials are being developed continuously to meet the demands of various field and applications. However, development of a materials in biomedical field is a challenge, particularly for those devices that are implanted in the human body because of accurate biological as well as mechanical requirements and for high quality of life. Metals and alloys are widely used in this area but unfortunately some failure are observed after long time use in human body since they cannot fulfill some vital requirements. Among alloys, Ni-Ti alloys possess most of the applications in cardiovascular system, bone plates and compression staples which promote healing. They are implanted directly into cardiac vessels and the area of the break to compress the two parts of the bone due to their shape memory effect. 
Ni-Ti alloys have some disadvantages due to high density, toxic nature, carcinogenic and allergenic properties of Ni that make Ni-Ti alloys inappropriate for biomedical applications. However, these shortcomings of Ni can be overcome by the addition of small quantity of aluminum to Ni-Ti alloys. Aluminum on the other hand is soft, bio-compatible and cost effective. So, the addition of aluminum will make Ni-Ti alloys more suitable for biomedical applications.

data.projectName: Molecular study of genetic variants controlling different signaling pathways leading to development of Polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) in Pakistani female population
data.projectDigest: Polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) is a common, heterogeneous, metabolic and complex endocrine condition affecting 7-9% of all women of reproductive age and its prevalence is increasing. It is a major cause of 75% of an-ovulatory infertility in women; other conditions associated with PCOS include insulin resistance, obesity, increased risk of type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease. Children born to PCOS mothers may even exhibit increased cardio metabolic risk due to endocrine abnormalities and endothelial dysfunction. The etiology of PCOS remains unclear. A large number of genes involved in development of PCOS are identified worldwide. Different variants of these genes are found among different ethnic groups worldwide. In Pakistan researchers are working on basic aspects symptoms, general awareness and hormone level study. Although very important, no research is being done on molecular basis of the disease. Pakistani nation is multiethnic, there is a strong need to find out the gene variants involved in regulation of follicular development, steroidogenesis and different signaling pathways that lead to development of PCOS. The proposed project will improve our understanding about PCOS and research outcome will help answer prevention of disease and problems related to women health that will ultimately lead to improved quality of life of the Pakistani women.

Among these, As III (arsenite) and As V (arsenate) are the most abundant in the environment. As III is more toxic than As V. Its effective management have become a serious challenge for the farmers due to insecticide, even Bt cotton resistance, and its acquired oligophagous nature. Extensive use of insecticides cause very serious threats like insecticide resistance and environment pollution. The trend of using plant derived phytocompounds is becoming very popular because of their eco-friendly and biodegradable nature. These chemicals are being used for different insect and mite pest control and have been reported, by various scientist, as a very effective control strategy. But we do not know the active chemical compounds in plant essential oils and its target site in the insect pest. data.projectName: Performance evaluation of Punjab Criminal Prosecution Service in Criminal Justice System
data.projectDigest: In this research project, researcher will evaluate the performance of Punjab Criminal Prosecution Service which is an important part of Criminal Justice System. The objective of this research is to critically examine and evaluate the performance of Punjab Criminal Prosecution Service in the Criminal Justice System of Punjab.  This research will not only examine the working and performance of Punjab Criminal Prosecution Service from the perspective of Prosecutors but also from the all other stakeholders i.e. lawyers, judges and Police Officers. Through structured and semi-structured interviews and surveys from lawyers, judges, police officers and prosecutors, this project will evaluate performance of Punjab Criminal Prosecution Service since it started in 2007. It will also identify the major problems and difficulties associated with the Prosecution and recommend suggestions for the policy makers. The project will bridge the huge research gap in this particular area of law in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Is she creation of a Lesser God? An in-depth evaluation of societal gender bias at baby birth
data.projectDigest: Women health and child mortality are always been a key focus of policy in developed as well as developing countries. The focus was mainly on the provision of better prenatal and postnatal health facilities to women in all countries. In developing countries, circumstances for a woman at childbearing age are strongly linked with the cultural and social structure of that society where she resides. Her prenatal and postnatal care not only depends upon the availability of healthcare and family norms but also on male gender preferences. Strong gender preferences and sex-selective abortions may lead to a serious distortion in the natural sex ratio. This study by taking this phenomenon into consideration will analyze the factors which influence male gender preferences in rural and urban areas of Pakistan and its consequences faced by women. Mixed methods [field survey, key informant interviews, focus group discussions] shall be used to generate data on qualitative as well as quantitative aspects. For quantitative data, stratified multistage sampling shall be used and data will be collected in capital cities of the provinces and independent states of Pakistan. The project will expect to come up with a policy intervention for the planning commission, government entities, and NGOs working for the wellbeing of women in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Production of biofuel from microalgae bloom by using waste water and flue gas
data.projectDigest: Air pollution, water pollution and energy crises in Pakistan are the major problems for unsustainability. Industrialization, and transportation cause air and water pollution that trigger the degradation of environment. Our aim is to reuse the resources by using waste water and flue gases for the production of biofuel by micro-alga to overcome the situation of energy crises. Flue gases are major problem that increase the level of air pollution also cause smog in Pakistan. Biofuel will be helpful to overcome the crises of energy and environment.

data.projectName: Energy Efficiency Enhancement of Biomass Gasification Power Generation System by Optimal Utilization of Waste Heat in Organic Rankine Cycle
data.projectDigest:
In Pakistan, energy demand is annually increasing by 11-13% and is predicted to reach 179 million tons of oil equivalent in 2020 and is expected to reach approximately three times by 2050. Possible immediate solutions to cater this problem could be; utilization of renewable energy sources, upgradation of less efficient energy generation and improve the efficiency of existing conventional power generation systems.  
Biomass has some attractive features including abundance, availability and potential of producing various kind of fuels (e.g. H2) and value-added chemicals through gasification. Moreover, through biomass gasification, versatile fuels owing higher energy density can be produced i.e. syngas. Syngas is utilized for power generation through internal combustion engine (ICE) as it is an effective fuel for ICE operation. The application of ORC as the bottoming cycle for various waste heat sources is gaining much attraction over the past few years. 
This project is based on the upgradation of existing biomass gasification-ICE by effectively extracting the waste heat from ICE waste gas through ORC. This is proposed to improve energy efficiency of an existing biomass gasification power generation system. Beside additional power generation in the system, waste energy utilization also reduces the carbon footprint and global warming.

data.projectName: Sustainable and clean Power generation using low quality solar/waste heat in Tesla turbine for small enterprises
data.projectDigest:
The growth of country’s economy depends on its industrial status and industrial growth depends on the energy. Particularly small scale enterprises are prime victim of load shedding (due to shortage of electricity) in the country.  Currently, in Pakistan most of the energy (65 %) is being produced from fossil which accounts largest share among other resources. A spectacular amount of Pakistan’s foreign resources have been consumed in import of oil for energy production. Besides, this source of energy also causes the degradation of environment with emission of large quantity of CO2. 
Therefore, to address economy, energy and environmental problem, there is a need to identify indigenous resources which ensure sustainable cheap and clean energy production.
This proposed setup will utilize solar energy to vaporize a low boiling point organic fluid which would turn a turbine to produce electricity. In this project a blade less turbine  (Tesla turbine) is proposed which has more advantageous over the conventional turbine in terms of efficiency for and maintenance cost due to absence of blades.
The proposed set up will provide sustainable and clean energy to small scale business entities like schools, hospitals, restaurants, plazas and farmers.

data.projectName: ECOLOGY OF THE INDIAN FLYING FOX (Pteropus giganteus) WITH SPECIAL REFERENCE TO THE ORCHARD FRUITS IN POTHWAR, KP, AND AJK
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
The Indian flying fox is the largest bat of the subcontinent. Fruits are the chief staples of its diet, yet it also feeds on flowers, nectar, and leaves. As such it plays an important role in seed dispersal and pollination.
	Pothwar, the northern most part of its range in Pakistan, used to be sparsely populated by the flying fox. There is some evidence that the bat’s population of Pothwar is increasing and that its range is expanding northward, beyond its reported northern limit of its range of distribution in Pakistan, to the neighbouring fruit producing tracts of Khyber Pukhtunkhwa (KP) and Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK). Being a voracious fruit eater with a predilection for commercial fruits, the possibility of a conflict of interest with the fruit growers is imminent. This may lead to the destruction of its roosts and overhunting. If subjected to drastic declines, the bat population (because of its slow rate of reproduction) will take a long time to recover or revive.
	An interesting question arises– whether the bat’s advancement beyond its described northern limit of distribution is simply in response to the expansion in commercial fruit industry in the north, or to the warmer climatic condition due to global warming, or due to both.
	Whatever is the case, appropriate data need to be generated to a) show beyond doubt that the population of the flying fox is increasing and advancing northward, b) assess the importance of commercial fruits in the diet of the bat, and c) provide a baseline data on the bat that might be useful in the management or conservation of its population. Finally, an attempt shall also be made to define the factor(s) that is facilitating northward extension in the range of the flying fox population.

data.projectName: Monitoring of Hydrological and Water Quality Parameters of rivers and streams of Punjab and KP, North Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Water scarcity and quality have been major problems for communities living around the world in this era of climate change. Pakistan is ranked as 5th most affected country by climate change, with descending rains and ascending population the water resources are under stress.it is need of time to monitor water resources in terms of discharge and quality in order to tackle growing water management crisis. The proposed project aims to measure the discharge at selected rivers/streams of Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Haripur and Havelian areas along with the water quality and microplastic pollution analysis of the rivers/ streams and population surrounding them. The direct method will be employed in measuring the discharge by instruments available at CCRD, both the instruments will be operated simultaneously to test their effectiveness and reliability. The acquired data will be correlated with available metrological parameters to identify the variations impacted by climate change. The physiochemical parameters of water samples acquired from rivers/ streams and their vicinity will be tested for water quality with special emphasis on microplastics which is a growing problem in Pakistan. Based on the water quality and microplastic pollution results the zones surrounding the rivers/streams will be classified into high or low contaminated.

data.projectName: Biocontrol of fungal phytopathogens using endophytic bacterial biopesticides
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is an agriculture based economy and this sector remains under the threat of plant pests and pathogens. We rely heavily on chemicals pesticides to control these crop and grain spoiling organisms, which are mostly toxic to humans and other non-targeted organisms, and also recalcitrant. Moreover, their overuse has prompted the issue of pest resistance. Crop damaging microbes develop resistance to pesticides very quickly due to their faster growth rate and dynamic genome. Biopesticides are a safe, target specific, eco-friendly and cost effective means of controlling phytopathogens, predominantly bacteria and fungi. Numerous studies have identified rhizospheric and endophytic microbes being active against phytopathogens. Endophytic bacteria have gained prominence over other plant beneficial microbes in that they live in a closer association with their host and not disturbed by changing environmental conditions. In the present work, four prominent plant beneficial endophytic bacteria isolated from wild plants will be tested for their usefulness as biocontrol agents of wheat and maize fungal phytopathogens. These bacteria exhibit multiple plant beneficial traits and have been shown to antagonize the growth of two phytopathogenic fungi. These bacteria will be tested for their biocontrol potential on wheat and maize plants infected with pathogenic fungi in lab and green house conditions. The bacterial antifungal secondary metabolites will be characterized and their formulations, bacterial and biochemical, will be designed. These bacteria remain prospective as they have not been fully characterized for their biocontrol potential. Successful completion of the proposed study will enable us to develop biopesticides based on these bacteria and their designed formulations can

data.projectName: Fabrication of third-generation photovoltaic device for solar energy harvesting
data.projectDigest:
Renewable energy is promising as an alternative energy source to replace the dependence of fossil energy and nuclear power. Solar energy, in particular, is
an attractive candidate among the renewable energy resources as the sunlight is an abundant energy resource. Various technologies closely related to the
solar energy have emerged such as solar heating, solar photovoltaics and solar thermal electricity. In particular, solar photovoltaics is a direct method to
convert the solar energy to electricity.
The main objective of this project is to develop the synthesis of metal thin films and nanoparticles/nanostructures to explore their applications in energy sector. In this regard, our focus is on the chemical synthesis of metal nanostructures (Zinc oxide, Titanium dioxide etc.) nanoparticles to explore their applications in solar cell research in particular; dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs ) which is known as third generation of solar cells that have become a very interesting and practical alternative for advances in solar cell technology.

data.projectName: Potential role of exosomes in carcinogenesis, diagnosis and treatment
data.projectDigest: Exosomes are small diameter endosomal vesicles secreted in all biological fluids and play biological/pathological role which is being played by cargo molecules through inter cellular communication. These cargo molecules contain proteins and microRNAs. MicroRNAs are usually small non coding RNA fragments which are involved in reduction of final protein output by destabilizing or suppressing translation of target messenger RNA (mRNA) and deregulate the protein involved in different physiological functions and ultimately accelerate the process of carcinogenesis. Cancer is a multifactorial disease and leading cause of mortalities around the globe. Only due to cancer, there are 7.4 million mortalities which is 13% of total mortalities. Highest incidence/death rates are observed in low/middle income countries including Pakistan. Aim of this research is to test the hypothesis that cancer cells secrete exosomes which can be isolated from cell culture supernatant and body fluids including saliva, blood and plasma. If this hypothesis is true, a liquid biopsy based on exosomes can possibly overcome the limitation of tumor heterogeneity associated with conventional biopsy of tumors and will allow multiple biopsies to check treatment response and prognosis.

data.projectName: IoT based Digital Agriculture Farming for organic vegetables/crops in changing climatic conditions of southern Punjab-Pakistan.
data.projectDigest: Human population by year 2050 is expected to be around 9.8 billion. According to FAO by 2030 there would be 5 billion people deprived from basic food needs. To meet basic necessities of increasing population there is a dire need to maximize agricultural productivity. Therefore, there is an obvious need of more precise and sustainable agriculture system that not only alleviates the lack of food supply by maximizing our productivity but also help in judicious use of scarce natural resources like soil and water.Most recently use of modern agriculture techniques, which can be centrally and remotely controlled is becoming famous in advance countries. One of these modern techniques, known as smart farming/IoT (Internet of things) based digital agriculture farming. In this advance agriculture tool irrigation system is the most significant element to help farming community. In addition to that agricultural efficiency needs to speculation in smart IoT techniques with more precise sensors, which can help the producers to have data regarding biotic and abiotic stresses. This project will enhance on farm irrigation and nutrient use efficiency by IoT and simulation techniques. Additionally, it will also help us in capacity building for students, researchers, scientists, government personals and farmers.
