data.projectName: Genetic Determinants of Pulmonary arterial hypertension in Children of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Congenital heart diseases remain one of the main causes of child mortality worldwide as well as in Pakistan. It is commonly known as (hole in the heart). The etiology is based on mainly genetic and environmental factors however in more than 80% cases the death of children in many CHDs cases remain unexplanatory. South Asian Region including Pakistan is unique in its genetic diversity, our genome is an amalgam of multiple ethnicities. PAH associated with congenital heart disease (PAH-CHD) in which a long-standing increase in blood flow to the pulmonary arteries eventually results in permanent and progressive stiffening of the pulmonary arteries. PAH-CHD requires a substantial time, approx. 5-10 years to become severe. Registry at NICVD, Karachi indicates that this condition is appearing more quickly in less than two years and more frequently in our children. The causes and prognosis are unexplained yet, but the mechanism is different. The study focuses and tries to find out the reasons, logical scientific explanation for this situation through next generation sequencing technology. It is designed for two years, In the first year the equipment and logistics will be prepared for the sample collection and in-depth discussion before sampling and software knowledge. The second year of project will be the execution samples for NGS and data will be retrieved and analyzed.

data.projectName: Use Of Technology Integration And Innovative Teaching Practices In Classroom At Primary Level For Enhancing Sustainability Of Quality Education
data.projectDigest:
Primary education is the most integral part for building foundation of a student. With the advancement, use of technology has become part and parcel for increasing efficacy and student learning capabilities .In Pakistan Primary education is neglected for using technology and this is basic need of today. Information technology should be a primary tool for education/learning in the country. For this purpose, it has been debated that the department of information technology in Pakistan should take initials in order to affect upon the status of education sector of the country.
The project shall high light the importance of integrating technology and innovative teaching practices in classroom at primary level for enhancing sustainability of quality education.  It shall be focused that the skills of  the teachers shall be enhanced in following aspect 1: conceptual understanding of subjects 2: critical thinking approach among leaners 3: better pedagogical approach 4:logical reasoning 5: assessment .This all shall be focused entirely to establish a learning environment among students .Quality of education is target of every nation around the globe but its sustainability is still a major challenge .The project shall highlight the impact of technology integration in classroom at primary level with better and innovative teaching practices and how this reflect upon the sustainability of quality of education.

data.projectName: Development of strategies for the bioscouring of cotton fabric by multienzyme consortium of microbial pectin lyases
data.projectDigest: Pectic enzymes account for about one quarter of the world enzyme production with an estimated market value of $6.0 billion in 2016. Therefore, the biotechnological potential of microbial pectin lyases has drawn a great deal of attention from numerous scientists worldwide. In order to use pectin lyases as a suitable industrial bio-catalyst and to apply these in different research areas, production, purification and improved knowledge of enzyme characteristics is very critical. So the present project will initially focus on pectin lyase production under submerged fermentation method from bacterial consortium under statistical approach. and various nutritional and physical parameters will be  optimized in detail. Further it will be partially purified using ammonium sulphate precipitation technique.  This partially purified PL will be immobilized on various support materials nanoparticles, Na-alginate, chitosan, gluteraldehyde crosslinking etc. in order to improve the thermal stability characteristics and reusability followed by FTIR characterization. Biochemical properties and thermodynamic parameters of native and immobilized enzyme will be studied in detail to determine the structure function relationship. In the final step, the potential of pectin lyase will be checked for the bioscouring of cotton fibers via native and immobilized PL. The results obtained will be analyzed statistically using appropriate regression techniques.

data.projectName: Design and development of automatic formal tool for verifying hardware circuits
data.projectDigest:
Hardware components are the major ingredient of any computer system which works collectively with the software running on the system to achieve certain objectives. Failure in one or more hardware components leads to the overall system failure.  Errors in life-critical and business-critical systems may lead to loss of human lives and/or huge monetary loss. To avoid human and financial loss, it must be ensured that the hardware components are correct, error-free and give output as and when desired.
Currently, hardware circuits are designed using hardware description languages such as Verilog and VHDL, but cannot be proved correct mathematically. In this project, we aim to build a tool to automatically check errors in hardware components designed in a description language Verilog. The tool, with an easy-to-use interface, would allow the designers to feed existing or newly created hardware designs as input and it will translate and then run/simulate the design in a reliable and sound environment. The chip manufacturers would design hardware components using conventional hardware description language Verilog, but would be able to test their design in a highly trusted running environment with mathematical foundation.

data.projectName: Pathophysiology of type 2 diabetes mellitus is governed by platelet hyperactivity and its’ inflammatory profile
data.projectDigest:
Dysregulation of platelets and endothelial interplay climaxes in thrombus formation. The thrombogenic status of an individual is highly influenced by the endothelial release of mediators in the circulation such as prostacyclin (PGI2).  Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) has been highlighted by hyperglycemia, oxidative stress and endothelial dysfunction which has its toll on platelets to become hyperactive. Thereby increasing the risk of developing occlusive thrombi; leading to silent myocardial infarction, as had been the usual scenario with T2DM patients.
Assessment of platelets in their spread form depicts their status in a clot. PGI2 has already been identified to inhibit spread platelets from healthy participants. This is an in-vitro project that emphasizes to observe if PGI2 does have an effect on platelets from T2DM patients. Do they respond in the same manner as platelets obtained from healthy controls? Are the number of PGI2 receptors at fault, or is it the dysfunctional downstream signaling, or the absence of PGI2 in the system or a combination of these that lead to hyperactive platelets? This project will dissect the role of PGI2 with relevance to hyperglycemia, endothelial dysfunction and their effect on platelet reactivity on formation of a thrombus in T2DM.

data.projectName: A Unified Modelling and Simulation Framework  with Different Model Reduction Techniques for Power, Water and Gas Distribution Networks
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Modeling and simulation is considered as the third mode of discovery after theory and experimentation. It importance grows even further for large-scale models. The underlying concept is to use the laws of physics to represent the system by a mathematical model and solve the model on computer for different possible inputs (simulation). Mathematical models of distribution networks are large and involve nonlinear differential as well as algebraic equations. The solution or simulation of such model is computationally cumbersome. An alternate is to compute an easy to simulate model from the original large-scale model using model reduction techniques. This project focuses on the development of model reduction techniques for nonlinear models of distribution networks. Two important classes of model reduction techniques will be extended to the models of distribution networks.  Prof. Tatjana Stykel from the University of Augsburg, Germany is international collaborator in the project and she is expert in the area of model reduction for descriptor systems. The two principal investigators are experts in the analysis and design of large-scale models. The implication of the project includes identifying erroneous regions of distribution network, designing new network and developing industry-academia collaboration.

data.projectName: Communicating with the Mute
data.projectDigest: The total number of the mute (approximately) in the world is 800,000  and in Pakistan 244196 . The mute cannot speak, and they can communicate only through gestures mostly generated by hands, head and face. Most of the speaking persons are un-familiar with the meanings of the gestures. It is very difficult for the mute and the speaking to communicate with each other. To resolve this issue machine learning based systems can understand the meanings of the gestures, and translate them into the natural language of the speaking persons. In this way they can understand each other. We, in this project, will develop machine learning based system that will understand the meanings of the gestures, and translate them into Urdu language. The machine will be trained as per the standard gestures of the Pakistan Sign Language (PSL) . We have already trained Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model on few Urdu Alphabets as per PSL standard. The performance of the CNNs is encouraging. The CNNs can be used in real time scenarios where the mute and the speaking can communicate with each other.

data.projectName: Fasciola Excretory/Secretory Antigens for Early Field Based Immunodetection and Immunization to Control Fasciolosis
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: The liver flukes Fasciola (F.) hepatica and F. gigantica cause infectious disease in ruminants and humans all around the world. The traditional approaches for the identification of Fasciola species have been used from a long time, but due to limitations of these techniques, various other approaches such as DNA and protein based diagnostic techniques have been developed. The available diagnostic kits helpful for the detection of disease but due antigenic variation of Fasciola in different geographic location their sensitivity and specificity effected. To overcome these limitation, we aim to develop a field diagnostic test (Latex Agglutination Test and Dot-blot Assay) by using excretory secretory antigens (ES Ag) of Fasciola. The control of Fasciola infection is primarily by the use of anthelminthic drugs. The appearance of drug resistance in the parasite has increased the need for a vaccine and find out effective medicinal plants to control fasciolosis. Vaccine target antigens have been isolated and characterised from the fluke. However, it is assumed that use of selected ES Ag will be helpful to define the commercial potential of vaccine. Due to development of antihelminthics resistance, natural indigenous plant products are best choice to control fasciolosis and to find alternate of antihelminthics drugs.

data.projectName: Vitamin D status and associated metabolic risk factors among Pakistani women: Influence of endocrine disrupting chemical, Bisphenol A.
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Vitamin D is a fat soluble prohormone, which plays an important role in various physiological processes. Vitamin D status depends on several environmental and endogenous factors. Additionally, recent literature have suggested that exposure to endocrine disrupting chemicals can also influence vitamin D status and may alter circulating 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels. 
Bisphenol A (BPA) is known as endocrine disrupting chemical, and is recently been classified as reproductive toxin by the European chemical classification and labeling.
Several studies have shown adverse health effects of BPA. BPA have been shown to alter hormonal levels in body particularly levels of steroid and thyroid hormones by interacting with their nuclear receptors. Because there is structural similarity between active vitamin D metabolite and steroid hormones and also their nuclear receptor belongs to the same superfamily of proteins, it is possible that this environmental chemical may also interfere with vitamin D endocrine system. 
Vitamin D deficiency has become major public health concern among Pakistani population. Currently, there are no published data that assess the levels of BPA and the association between BPA exposure and circulating 25-hydroxyvitamin D in our population. Therefore, we intend to investigate these relationships in a sample of healthy female Pakistani adults.

data.projectName: Compactified Non-Singular Coordinates of a Charged Spherically Symmetric Black Hole in f(R) Gravity.
data.projectDigest:
“The theory of relativity” is recognized as the extreme successes in physics. In 1905, Einstein lay down, “The special theory”, excluding gravity to mark out certain upsetting proofs that had stand up in learning the electromagnetism. Mainly his famous assumption, “the speed of light in vacuum remains constant for all observers” compelled many scientists to reject numerous commonsense suppositions, like the utter nature of time. After 10 years, Einstein published the “General theory of Relativity” (GR) which cleared up the concept that “all motions are relative”. Time is then no longer considered to be absolute and uniform. Relativity, Cosmology and Astrophysics envisage amazing phenomena like neutron stars, black hole (BH) and gravitational waves.
Black holes are one of the most esoteric objects in the universe (astrophysics) i.e. classically, objects can fall into the BH but nothing can escape from it, not even light. The formation of BH’s via the gravitational collapse of a super-giant star is fairly well-studied in the literature and well-understood, however, the double-null form, foliation of certain hyper-surfaces, butterfly coordinates and rainbow gravity of some BH’sarising in f(R) gravity are still not well-explored yet. In this project, we want to investigate some aspects of space-time coordinates in f(R) gravity that arises in gravitation. We will consider various kinds of BH’s, specific forms of matter, dust and magnetic field configurations, in order to study the earlier stated aspects. Our work will involve lots of analytical and numerical computations and analysis for studying the features of different types of space-time geometries.

data.projectName: Electrically Controlled Tongue Movement assistive Ball for Monitoring and Therapeutic Biomedical Application
data.projectDigest: Treatments of tongue disorders have never been so efficient until now. Different patients respond differently in terms of the recovery. Whether the treatment is invasive or non-invasive including deep brain stimulation, different muscle exercises and use of chemicals, so far scientists are not able to find any notable success to treat tongue disorders completely. This study proposes a novel ball type device made of a biocompatible silicon for the treatment of tongue related disorders. The ball incorporates a tri-axial accelerometer either on it’s boundary or inside along with eight electrodes mounted on its boundary. The ball will be placed under the patient’s tongue to monitor the tongue movement. When the patient moves his tongue, accelerometer sense the moving direction and sends signal to processing unit, which is externally connected with the device through wires.  If the tongue moves in the right direction the electrodes placed on the right side of the ball are activated and provide electrical stimulus to the tongue muscles in controlled manner and vice versa. The electrical stimulation increases the strength of the muscles and improve its movement function. The electrical activity of the tongue muscles was also recorded using EMG amplifier connected to the electrodes placed on the ball. The system keeps recording the continuous data and improvements in the movement of tongue muscles through EMG, which works as feedback. The proposed system has the ability to treat speech disorders successfully in less amount of time as compared to other non-invasive techniques.

data.projectName: To enhance the in vivo anticancer potential of docetaxel by modifying the tumor supporting cellular microenvironment in mice
data.projectDigest: The present research project is designed to validate the impact of reversing the cancer supportive microenvironment on the anticancer potential of decetaxel (DTX) in Balb/c mice by blocking the chemokine signaling, angiogenesis and adenosine A2 receptors by montelukast (MNL), metformin (MTF) and SCH-58261 (SCH) respectively. Human tumor xenograft will be induced in mice by subcutaneously injecting 100 µL of human breast adenocarcinona cells MCF7 (4 × 104) to the left flank of the mice. DTX will be administered alone and in combination with the mentioned drugs in different doses through intraperitoneal route on consecutive days from day 4th till 25th. The reduction in tumor size after 25 days treatment will be taken as a measure of synergictic anticancer effect of the administered drugs. The drugs will be loaded on the poly(allylamine hydrochloride) nanoparticles (PAH NPs) in the appropriate concentration as validated by the initial experiment. The in vivo anticancer potential of the synthesized nanoparticles will be tested in nude mice by xenograft method as mentioned above. The mice will be sacrificed and the tumor tissue samples will be subjected to real time PCR for the HIF-1?, vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), Her2, ki67, ER and CatL2 gene expression.

data.projectName: HYPOGLYCEMIC PROTEINS/PEPTIDES (HgPPs) AND THEIR GENES FROM SOME INDIGENOUS MEDICINAL PLANTS
data.projectDigest: Among all the compounds discovered from medicinal plants with hypoglycemic properties the studies on insulin-like proteins isolated from seeds, leaves or fruits have been documented rarely in the literature. However, there is much gap in research related to production of recombinant hypoglycemic proteins and/or peptides (HgPP) and in assessing their biological importance. Therefore, the present project is proposed to screen, isolate and analyze novel HgPPs from medicinal plants potentially unexplored for HgPPs. Recently, we have also isolated two genes encoding hypoglycemic peptides from plants and characterized using in silico approach. The genes encoding HgPPs will be cloned for protein expressions following assessment of antidiabetic activities of recombinant HgPPs. For large-scale applications of HgPPs to treat diabetes the supply of these HgPPs is the first and major issue that needs to be considered. In this proposed project, based on our results, we will focus on screening of medicinal plants of Cucurbitaceae and Fabaceae families for HgPPs followed by PCR and RT-PCR based isolation of HgPP genes. The recombinant HgPPs will be purified and tested for their antidiabetic activities. The study will provide an economical and expedient method to produce antidiabetic medicines at large scale with pharmaceutical applications.

data.projectDigest: What factors forcing managers to do fraud in their ?nancial statements? How best can ?nancial analysts, auditors, regulators (SECP), and investors detect misstatements/frauds? What are the implications of financial misstatements/frauds all stakeholders? It is critical important and need of current environment of Pakistan to address these questions to the ef?cient functioning of capital markets. The extant literature suggests that stakeholders try to see fair and true view of financial statements and in response to practices, financial analyst are trying to avoiding a damaged reputation, investors are looking for improved returns, an auditor is avoiding costly litigation, and regulator is striving hard to enhanced investor protection and fewer investment debacles. Despite these, Security Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) reported 124 listed companies’ misstatements during period 2018-19. Our research has two main objectives. First, we develop a comprehensive database of ?nancial misstatements/fraud. Our objective is to describe this database and make it broadly available to other researchers to promote research on earnings misstatements in Pakistan. Second, we analyze the ?nancial characteristics and other factors of misstating ?rms and develop a model to predict misstatements or frauds. The findings of this study can be used as a red ?ag or signal of the likelihood of misstatements or frauds to Security Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP). This study will also suggest to SECP how to regulate their policy against these practices.

data.projectName: Computational fluid dynamics investigation into flow behavior and acoustic mechanisms inside a handheld hairdryer
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Environmental noise is known to have adverse effects on the human health. Hairdryers are one of the most commonly used electrical appliances. Almost all of the commercially available hairdryers produce substantial noise from about 60 dB to 95 dB.
Noise in a hairdryer is generally divided into two broad categories, i.e. vibrational noise and noise from steady/unsteady flows. The vibrational noise in a hairdryer is due to imbalance of operating parts. The non-uniform wake flow present behind the rotating fan produces steady load noise.  Similarly, the unsteadiness of the incoming flow due to the existence of turbulence eddies, tip clearance inside the casing and the trailing edge vortex shedding are main sources of unsteady flow noises.
The precise prediction of the local pressure fluctuations around noise source needs is necessary to capture noise characteristics. The focus of the current research is to use high-fidelity CFD (computational fluid dynamic) simulations for the estimation of the flow field inside a handheld hairdryer. Particular emphasis will be given to the effect of inlet surface roughness and incoming flow turbulence on the noise generation. This project will help in developing the precise relationship between the characteristics of the incoming flow passing through the hairdryer and its noise radiation.

data.projectName: Development of fat and casein replacers on pilot scale from indigenous starch resources: An industrial need.
data.projectDigest: The import of fat and casein replacers has risen steeply in the last decade with former having a wider market due to changing eating patterns of population. The threat of obesity and its health consequences is affecting food choices with greater inclination of people to consume low fat foods. Casein-replacers on the other hand are used to reduce the cost of imitation cheese by replacing expensive  casein. The proposed study will develop fat and casein replacers using different sources of starch after enzymatic and chemical modifications which may include esterification and etherification. The Tayyab Agro Private Limited (TAPL) is the sectoral collaborator for the study and will give a total of 0.6 million for proposed study as the seed money. The joint venture for the first time will lead to development of fat and casein replacers using indigenous resources like potato, corn and rice. Thus, the proposed study will develop fat and casein replacers for the first time locally to cater the demands of various industries and in future these products could be exported to earn valuable foreign exchange. After successful development of starch based fat and casein replacers, the whole technology will be transferred to TAPL for commercialization.

The joint venture for the first time will lead to development of fat and casein replacers using indigenous resources like potato, corn and rice. After successful development of starch based fat and casein replacers, the whole technology will be transferred to TAPL for commercialization.

data.projectName: Vertebrate pest in the vegetable crops and their ecofriendly management in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (Pakistan)
data.piUniversity: Women University of Azad Jammu and Kashmir Bagh
data.projectDigest: Jammu and Kashmir will be the study area of the proposed research on vertebrate pest of vegetable crops and their ecofriendly management. Vertebrate pest are least studied and our existing pool of knowledge on vertebrate pests needs to be updated. While information on the vertebrate pests’ diversity, distribution and abundance in vegetable crops is generally deficient.  The state has diverse agro-climatic characteristics, ranging from sub humid, sub-tropical to temperate, depending upon altitude and rainfall with soil diversity that grows a large number of crops, fruits and vegetables in AJK to meet the requirement of population. In agriculture only 2 percent vegetables are grown of the total cropped area. (GoAJK, 2000). The vegetables grown in AJK are categorized three, mono crop area, Rabi and Kharief crop area. Rabi cultivated vegetables are (mid-November to April / May) are Turnip, Carrot, Spinach, Tomato, Cauliflower Cabbage,   Peas,   Radish, while kharief (May and ending at the latest in January) Lady finger,   Tinda ,  Brinjal, Bitter gourd, Bottle gourd, chilies, peppers, carrots, Chilies, and Pumpkin. There exist about 49 species of vertebrate pest within the territorial limits of Pakistan. Some of the species are mammals, birds which are important agricultural pests throughout the Indo-Pakistan subcontinent. In the Jammu and Kashmir, these vertebrate pests exert a serious limitation on the production of vegetables and wheat by causing extensive damage. Attempts at eliminating them from the agricultural fields by trapping or toxicants have been not successful on the long run. This study endeavors to develop an ecologically-based program for alleviating vertebrate pests problem in the vegetable cropland of Jammu and Kashmir. And conservation of  pest species

data.projectName: BRIDGing the Gap between Local Community and Mental Health SErvices in Rural and Urban Areas of District Rawalpindi Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Mental disorders make a considerable contribution in the global burden of illnesses. In Low-Middle Income Countries (LMICs) such as Pakistan, lack of resources and accessibility towards the treatment services for people with common mental disorders are among significant barriers in promoting mental health care. To increase the accessibility towards treatment and care for common mental health disorders, World Health Organization (WHO) has developed a specialized program called Problem Management Plus (PM+), that can be effectively delivered by lay professionals/ paraprofessionals. Such treatments have special significance for Pakistan, where number of mental health specialists are very limited. Mosques (usually referred as “Masajid”) and Islamic educational centers (usually referred as “Madaris”) are available and accessible in almost each and every rural (remote areas) and urban localities in Pakistan. Such religious communities have well established social channels and capitals that can be effectively utilized to increase the accessibility of mental health treatment. Therefore, the present study primarily aims to assess the therapeutic and cost effectiveness of PM+ delivered by volunteers religious scholars.

data.projectName: Can we prevent the cancer and neurotoxicity associated with food borne pesticides? Potential nutraceuticals against pesticide induced toxicity
data.projectDigest: Occupational, accidental, suicidal and food borne exposure to pesticides is among the major causes of poisoning related morbidity and mortality in Pakistan. Several newer pesticides used during the cultivation and storage of agricultural food products may have serious health implications such as carcinogenesis, neurological and developmental diseases, and endocrine disruption, like their predecessors. Phytochemicals have increasingly gained global attention for their potential health benefits such as anticancer, antidiabetic and anti-Alzheimer effects. Therefore, this project is designed to investigate the carcinogenicity and neurotoxicity of some newer pesticides and the ameliorating effect of phytochemicals against the formers’ toxic potential. For this purpose, the mutagenic potential of pesticides will be determined by Ames reverse mutation assay using genetically modified Salmonella strains while their neurotoxicity will be assessed in rats by Rotarod, elevated maize and modified Irwin tests along with determining the oxidative stress parameters. It will be followed by assessment of the preventive effects of phytochemicals against pesticides’ induced mutagenicity and neurotoxicity. Outcome of the current project shall give an insight into the mechanism, signs and symptoms of the pesticide induced toxicity, and the potential role of phytochemicals in treating and preventing the pesticide induced cancer and neurological diseases in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Introgression and Marker Assisted Selection for Anthracnose Resistance in Grapes
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Potohar has been declared as grape valley and area under its cultivation is increasing. However, high humidity during monsoon season causes spread of fungal diseases leading to reduction in yield and quality. Improvement in grapes can be done by using conventional as well as modern techniques. But conventional methods are laborious and time consuming therefore different biotechnological techniques are used for improvement and development of disease resistant cultivars. Marker assisted selection can be very beneficial for identification of disease resistant genotypes. Different molecular markers can be used for identification of disease resistant gene and expression of gene can also be analyzed using transcriptome profiling. Therefore, present study is designed to identify genes involved in anthracnose resistance. Transcriptome profiling will be done using next generation sequencing. Ten different genotypes of grapes i.e. white vine, himroid, like mount, NARC black, Sugra one, Sultanina C, king ruby, sunderkhani, red globe and vitro black will be used for screening against resistant to anthracnose by using artificial inoculation method. Two contrasting (highly susceptible and highly resistant) varieties will be selected for transcriptome profiling. The differently expressed genes will be selected and confirmed for their expression under control and disease conditions using qPCR. These genes could be utilized for marker assisted selection regarding disease resistance. An introgression of resistant markers/genes will be done by crossing resistant and susceptible genotypes followed by embryo rescue. The developed F1 plants will be screened using markers developed in current study. The F1 plants with improved resistance will be available to research and farming community.

data.projectName: Production of biodegradable Packaging material from agricultural waste
data.projectDigest: Plastic waste is considered to be one of most harmful and visible harmful pollutants that harshly destroy our environment. Currently, 250 million garbage of Pakistan predominantly consist of pet bottles, plastic bag and food scrapes. Pakistan, working proactively now against environmental degradation and climate change in the country by planting trees. One foremost feature of protecting the nation’s environment is reducing pollution, particularly of non-biodegradable materials like plastic. Estimations specify that it takes up to thousand years for plastic to degrade and decompose. When discarded, plastic breaks down into micro plastic particles and does not biodegrade which move into oceans and pollute our environment. It has led to the manufacturing of polymers prepared from renewable sources for food packaging. Natural polymers resulting from agricultural products (such as starch, proteins, cellulose and plant oils) are the chief source for producing biodegradable and renewable polymer materials. The polylactic acid (PLA) is the mostly consumed biopolymers as packaging material for food industry. In the current project PLA will be manufactured from lactic acid, that can be made from of agricultural waste hydrolysate by fermentation. Lactide synthesized from lactic acid will be utilized for to produce poly lactic acid. The objective of this study was to investigate the PLA production from agricultural waste i.e sugarcane bagasse in laboratory scale.

data.projectName: Lean Canvas for Invention - Development and Implementation of an innovative Graduate Educational Tool
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest: Bhutto and Furse (2019) has developed the Lean Canvas for Invention (LCI), an innovative educational tool for STEM graduates, to bridge the knowledge asymmetries between scientists, engineers and entrepreneurs. The Business Model Canvas developed by Osterwalder and Pigneur (2010) seems to train managers to be entrepreneurs, however, its relevance for the STEM graduates is not explicitly identified. The LCI is hence developed for improving the translation of scientific and technological ideas to market with development and implementation of its teaching module. A delivery of the LCI training module by Prof. Dr. Arabella Bhutto (PI of this proposal) during the Six Week Skills Based Summer Faculty Development Workshop by NAHE, HEC  in 2019 received a very positive feedback and identified a need of further development and implementation of this module at the national level. Therefore, the proposed research intends to enrich the contents of the LCI teaching module and its implementation as the LCI Training workshops at ORICs established at different universities of Pakistan to the graduates and faculty of the STEM education. The objective is to deliver this newly designed course through the ORICs of different universities and enriching its contents with the national examples. Once training module is fully developed and delivered then the objective is to convert this entire information in a form of a Handbook accompanied with video lectures to be taught as a part of the STEM education curricula in order to transfer the research from bench to the market.

data.projectName: Development of Recombinant Tetravalent Vaccine against Dengue virus
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Dengue virus (DENV) is a major health concern globally. WHO reported 390 million DENV infections per year and has now become endemic in Pakistan. It circulates throughout the year and spread via mosquitoes (Aedes aegyti and Aedes albopictus). In 2019, there were 47,120 DENV fever confirmed cases reported from all over Pakistan. Since, Pakistan is badly hit by the epidemics of DENV in recent times. There is immediate need to cope with this notorious disease in time. Prophylactic vaccine approach is the most appropriate remedy to control DENV. Our, proposed project will produce indigenised vaccine that will be used against all the four serotypes of dengue virus. This project will not only lead to vaccine intervention against dengue but will also pave the path to setup an indigenous pipeline for recombinant vaccine production against other viruses. Completion of this project will lead to tetravalent recombinant protein vaccine production process against DENV that can be adopted by our local pharmaceutical industries for mass scale production. Thus, the project goals will not only meet to transfer its impact to the masses of the country but also will contribute to economy once the pipeline of vaccine production is adopted by the pharmaceutical industry.

data.projectName: Transphobic Discourse and Heteronormative Knowledge: Articulating a Gendered Epistemic Discourse Praxis
data.projectDigest: Transgender community does not enjoy any respect and is flagrantly denied rights in Pakistan. Because of dissemination of totalitarian heterosexual knowledge and resultant discourses, the overwhelming majority of the country do not want to talk about transgender community and their rights.  In closed collectivist societies like Pakistan, insecurity and expected punitivity do not let gender-variants come out and declare their non-conformist identities. Such inhibitions are hallmark of a society where sexual and gender stereotypes conflate, and any digression from stereotypical ways is scrutinized. Such scrutiny creates a kind of cognitive dissonance in transgender people and leads to affect their sense of identity. Thus, the standards of wider society make gender-variants believe that they fall short of what they really ought to be. Pakistan represents a society where transgender people become a myopic view of sexual negativity. This is an outcome of the hegemonic equation of heterosexuality with natural human experience. It is in this context that this research aims to explore the relativist understanding of discourse and knowledge as they align the legitimization of hetero-normative beliefs in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Effect of various feeding management systems on feeding behavior and performance of Balochi sheep and Kamori goats in Lasbela region of Balochistan
data.piUniversity: Lasbela University of Agriculture, Water and Marine Sciences, Lasbela
data.projectDigest: Pakistan’s population is increasing at a rapid rate a huge segment of this population exists in rural and marginal areas of the country depending on livestock. In this respect, The demand of such population can be met by increasing the productivity of the ruminants. Small ruminants make a very valuable contribution, especially to the poor in the rural areas. Feeding behavior and feed intake of small ruminants on different fodders varies and can affect their performance. In Pakistan, mostly people raise livestock on fodders in rural and urban areas. The availability of required fodder species and fodder production depends mainly on the climate and on the soils. The small ruminants are usually grazed on these fodders for maintenance and production requirements. Such type of conventional livestock raising is creating a gape between demand and supply. To bridge this gap, commercial livestock production demands a change in feeding trend towards stall feeding for efficient utilization of scarce resources. Use of total mixed ration (TMR) is increasing in ruminants rations. Many experiments have been conducted in large ruminants in Pakistan and elsewhere using large ruminants. However information on small ruminants is scanty in Pakistan (Particularly Balochistan). Keeping in view these facts, the present study is planned to evaluate the performance of sheep and goats under different feeding management systems.  Experiments will be conducted to evaluate the performance of both species by using various feeding and management systems to get maximum productivity per animal and to develop a viable grazing method.

data.projectName: Development of sustain release drug loaded biodegradable film for regeneration of diabetic ulcer
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Diabetes often a financial concern for health-care system, it also imposes catastrophic personal overheads out-of-pocket payments. The direct cost of treatment of diabetic foot ulcer at a tertiary care hospital is 2700 RS. Simvastatin (SMV) is an antihyperlipidemic agent used in high cholesterol disorders but recently, it has found that SMV have pleiotropic effects that would be useful for wound healing. Major mechanism of SMV in wound healing is angiogenesis and lymph-angiogenesis. Hydroxytyrosol (HTy) obtain from olive have additional anti-oxidant and anti-inflammatory activity. So statin and HTy loaded nano-film will be developed.
Firstly, SMV and HTy co-loaded chitosan nanoparticles (CSNPs) will be prepared by using ionic gelation method. NPs will be characterized and optimized for their size, shape and zeta potential using Zetasizer, entrapment efficiency, drug loading and drug release using, UV-spectrophotometer. NPs will further incorporated into the film prepared by solvent casting method. Films will be characterized for thickness, tensile strength, physical appearance, water vapor transmission and expansion percentage. Optimized SMV-HTy loaded nanofilms will be selected for further analysis. In-vitro permeation test will be performed. Wound will be created in Diabetic rat model. Optimized formulation will be applied on wound area and evaluated for its diabetic wound healing efficacy.

data.projectName: Role of Wnt Pathway Regulators in the Differentiation of Mesenchymal Stem Cells into Hepatocytes in Rat Model of Cirrhosis
data.projectDigest: End stage liver diseases e.g. liver cirrhosis, are emerging health issues affecting millions of people globally.  Transplantation of exogenously differentiated stem cells could be a better therapeutic option and has gained interest in scientific community due to the ability of these stem cells to differentiate into any cell type. Bone marrow contains numerous adult stem cell types with mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) showing great potential to differentiate towards multiple tissue lineages. Previously, different strategies were adopted to enhance homing and engraftment of MSCs as well as their pre-differentiation into hepatic lineage. However, lack of optimized protocols and poor understanding of molecular mechanisms have hindered the translation of stem cell therapy to clinics. The proposed project is based on the use of Wnt pathway regulators in enhancing the differentiation potential of MSCs into hepatocytes using rat model of liver cirrhosis. Wnt pathway plays a significant role in cellular differentiation and organogenesis and regulation of this pathway through specific modulators could direct specific differentiation of stem cells into hepatocytes. In this study, rat bone marrow MSCs will be treated with chemical agents that are known to play significant role as Wnt pathway regulators. Therapeutic potential of these pre-differentiated cells will be analyzed in vitro and in rat cirrhosis model by transplanting these cells and analyzing their subsequent effect on hepatic regeneration. To explore their molecular mechanism, differentiated MSCs will be analyzed for key signaling targets both at gene and protein levels. The proposed study will aid in optimizing effective differentiation of MSCs towards hepatocytes and provide promising cell based therapy for cirrhosis.

data.projectName: Improving Psychosocial Well-Being of Children and Adolescence with Congenital Heart       Disease and their Families: Efficacy of Congenital Heart Disease Intervention Program (CHIP)
data.projectDigest: Congenital Heart Disease (CHD) is a defect of heart and its surrounding arteries and muscles,  present at the time of birth. This is the most common birth defect presenting all over the world especially in Asia. Pakistan is among the countries that have the highest ratio in population of this defect. According to a research published in 2017, sixty thousands infants are born with CHD each year. The true prevalence may be higher because of incomplete data registry. Prospect of longer and healthier living of CHD population has been improved over the years. CHD not only adversely affects physical and mental health of the patients but also influences their families in term of overall quality of life. The present research aims at assessment of different psychosocial aspects related to Quality of Life of children and adolescence CHD and their families. Furthermore, a standardized Congenital Heart Disease Intervention Program (CHIP) including psycho-education, social skill training and behavior management will be used with patients to enhance mental, social, emotional and behavioral wellness that is likely improve their health related outcomes. CHIP training workshops will also educate families (parents and siblings) about dealing with stress related to health condition of children and adolescents with CHD.  Aims of this unique study are consistent with United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals for 2020 in terms of providing quality healthcare and promoting well-being of the patients. CHIP will enable the patients and their families to become self-sufficient in their lifelong psycho-social adjustment related to CHD. The successful completion of this project will serve as a milestone in the field health psychology and pediatric cardiology.

data.projectName: The Dynamics of Violence in Pakistan: Parameter Estimation and Sensitivity Analysis
data.projectDigest: This study focuses on the dynamics of violence in Pakistan. In this study we investigate socio-economic and cultural dynamics of violence by mathematical formulation and sensitivity analysis of the parameters that influence the phenomena the most. In this study violence is not specified to any gender rather it is measured in terms of physical force or power with the intention to cause physical or psychological harm carried out by either male or female in the society. Initially this project will focus on the theoretical aspects of the phenomena and afterwards for authenticity of the obtained results we will formulate a mathematical model on the dynamics of violence and then show the sensitivity of the parameters to identify which parameters are influential or sensitive the most.

data.projectName: Formulation of fixed dose combination of Ibuprofen and loratadine: In vitro and in vivo evaluation
data.projectDigest: Common cold accompanied by runny nose, watery eyes and body aches is an ailment which disturbs routine life.  A lot of medications are available for this condition in the market. Some of the available products contain only one active component such as Fexet (trade name) for the treatment of the allergy. Other products contain more than one component (known as fixed dose combination) such as Arinac (Ibuprofen & pseudoephedrine). Most of these fixed dose combination for common cold have some undesirable effects such as dizziness, drowsiness etc.  To have a relatively safe and effective fixed dose combination, coordination with a physician was developed. For the better health of patients, an idea was forwarded by the physician; it was suggested to have the combination of ibuprofen and loratadine. Ibuprofen can treat the fever and body aches which are usually accompanied by common cold. Ibuprofen also reduces the sneezing frequency. Loratadine is an anti-allergic drug which does not cause sedation, dizziness and drowsiness. These two drugs in one tablet will improve patient conditions and routine life will not be affected by the side effects of this combination. The product will be developed with the collaboration of local industry.

data.projectName: Niche Overlap and Spatial Distribution of Carnivores in Kala Chitta Hills National Park, Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Carnivores are an important mammalian group, which have crucial role in regulating and maintaining ecosystems. They maintain herbivore populations at a healthy level, preventing an overabundance of herbivores and thereby protecting vegetation from being too heavily grazed or browsed. In this manner, these species maintain the vertebrate pest population, indirectly. The proposed research project has been designed to investigate the population distribution, dietary overlap and problems of human carnivore conflicts and their mitigative strategies in the Kala Chita hills National Park, Pakistan, which is one of the highly important habitat for a number of carnivores species of the country. The wild animals in the study area enjoys relatively better protection as sufficient area of the national park is under armed forces use. For the current study the area will be thoroughly investigated for selection of study sites (4 – 6 points will be identified, where sampling and recording of observation will be carried out). The data will be gathered for estimating the relative abundance and distribution pattern of the carnivores in the area for three years. Carnivore scats shall be collected, on monthly basis and the diet of different carnivore species will be investigated through. In addition, a detailed study will be conducted to investigate the human carnivore conflicts in the area. The information generated will help us to understand the distribution pattern and dietary niche overlap among carnivores in the study area, which may be helpful to conserve the carnivore species of the area and to educate the masses for the role of these species in the control of their rodent pest species, especially the Indian porcupine, which is a serious vertebrate pest of the area.

data.projectName: Pollutant Mixing Dynamics Downstream of Kabul-Indus River Confluence using Satellite Remote Sensing
data.projectDigest:
Rivers have been serving as life lines for most of the human population around the globe throughout the history. If a polluted material is discharged into the rivers, it affects the population and aquatic habitat downstream of the pollutant source. The impact on the masses is largely determined by the pollutant concentrations at the sites where water is being consumed, for example for drinking. To understand if the water will be safer for consumption downstream of a pollutant disposal site, pollutant mixing dynamics across and along the river needs to be understood. 
River confluences are the locations where two rivers join together and are ubiquitous features of a drainage network. Large rivers often drain vastly different watersheds and hence possess very distinct physical and chemical properties. As flows from major tributaries converge at confluences, the waters from both tributaries start to mix. The rate of transverse mixing largely determines the quality of water downstream from these locations. In this sense, confluences serve as natural analogs for the introduction of pollutant material into a river system and provide the basis for studying rates of transverse mixing in rivers. The purpose of this study is to understand transverse mixing processes in rivers

data.projectName: Effects of exercise on cognition among geriatric population by secretory protein
data.projectDigest:
Old age is not a disease but a physiological mechanism of the body. One of the most affected components that slows down with age is the hippocampus which is responsible for the cognition of the person. The somatic structures as well as the functional cognitive capabilities changes with age including changes in the neurons with its nuclear death, reduced synapses along with damage to the neuronal network. This results in difficulty to perform many daily activities impairing their lives in misery. 
Now the evidences are coming with major focus on changing lifestyle, good eating habits and exercises. Many researchers had tried to use medications and learning protocols for the improvement of cognition among old age but the component of exercise has been a missed component in case of cognition. The project main aims to identify the exercise regimn (dose, intensity and duration of exercises) to improve cognition through secretory protein i.e. Cathepsin B (a myokine released after exercise by skeletal muscle and cross the blood brain barrier to the hippocampus for improving cognition). Once the regime is identified, it will help the old age community to improve their cognition level acting as preventive as well as curative for those individuals.

data.projectName: Main group metal complexes as inexpensive precursors for OLEDs
data.projectDigest:
Efficient light emitting compounds are important components in light emitting devices, which have potential applications in displays and area light sources. In particular the latter are considered as efficient, economic and thus environmentally friendly alternatives to presently used illumination systems. There are various technologies to realize such systems. A system investigated in detail is the triplet emitter Ir(ppy)3 (Ir(C6H4-C5H4N)3, tris(phenylpyridyl)iridium (III)), because this compound has a very short-lived excited triplet state. The structural chemistry of this compound has been investigated in detail and further quantumchemical calculations have demonstrated the importance of spin-orbit coupling, which are still difficult to be described by standard theoretical methods. Such effects are also known from  platinum complexes. The obvious disadvantage of such compounds is the limited availability and the high costs of the platinum metals. The search for alternatives was directed to other transition metal and also the lanthanide elements, but so far the heavy main group metals have only been very scarcely investigated in this direction. This is surprising in the light of the well documented strong spin-orbit coupling effects in the chemistry of elements like antimony or bismuth. These elements have further advantages like low-price, ready accessibility and –particularly in the case of bismuth – low toxicity. 
The proposed chemistry in this project is thus a fundamental exploration of the preparative accessibility and properties of a broad range of relatively in-expensive Sb(III) and Bi(III) compounds. We plan to investigate their structures and electronic properties of light emission in detail.

data.projectName: Fabrication of Novel, Low Cost Agrowaste Based Graphene Oxide/Biochar Composites for Decontamination of Textile Industry Effluents
data.projectDigest: The textile industry is playing a key role in the economy of many countries but the textile industry is also responsible for intensifying the environmental problems by generating the colored effluents. The treatment of textile effluents for removal of dyes in an economic and cost effective manner remains a major problem for textile industries. There are various techniques used to eliminate the contaminants from water as: ion exchange, adsorption, precipitation, biodegradation electrochemical methods and photo-catalysis. However, these methods pose techno-economical limitations for field scale applications. Although the adsorption is considered as most effective in removal of dyes in textile effluents with greater efficiency, the adsorbent materials can also be regenerated at the end. So, researchers all over the world develop and explore most economical and efficient methods that need minimum energy consumptions, chemicals, electrode and little space for installation. Currently, biochar based graphene oxide composites adsorbents using agro waste biomass are getting severe attention because of easy availability and low cost of agro waste materials and marvelous adsorption properties of graphene oxide.   These biocomposites, displaying a higher reactivity for surface mediated processes will be used for real application of wastewater purification system.

data.projectName: Community Structure and Species Diversity of Macro-zoobenthos of the two   Sandy Beaches of Karachi.
data.projectDigest: Analysis of macro-benthic animals or zoobenthos in soft bottom sediments is an essential part of the assessment of marine environmental conditions. Macro-zoobenthos are relatively sedentary or sessile in nature and have long life span as compared to zooplanktons. Their sedentary or sessile habit make them unable to escape environmental stress and for this reason they are widely used as indicator of change in coastal environmental conditions. .The coastal belt of Karachi is stressed due to maritime activities in the sea and anthropogenic activities on the land. These stresses are reflected in the community structure of benthic organisms living in the soft bottoms of the coast. The base-line studies of these benthic communities must be undertaken to assess any future changes in the coastal ecosystem due to human activities either in the sea or on the land. In the event of an oil spill or coastal development, the information regarding biodiversity of the area is a prerequisite to assess the damages, if any. The structure of zoobenthic communities have not been studied in detail, especially from Sandspit and Hawks bay sandy beaches of Karachi. The proposed research project is aimed to fill this gap.

data.projectName: Using AI Techniques with PSO and SLAM for Unmanned Aircraft Navigation and Collision Avoidance
data.projectDigest:
We integrate Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) into real-time aircraft flight state estimation filter to measure the navigation map of the surrounding and vehicle pose covariance and focus with artificial feature patterns to optimize the strategies to avoid the collision in Unmanned Aircraft in flight formation. 
Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is a global optimization paradigm that has gained prominence in the last two decades due to its ease of application in unsupervised, complex multidimensional problems, which cannot be solved using traditional deterministic algorithms. With the advent of Unmanned aerial vehicles, have become increasingly important in both military and civilian applications in the past few decades, such as remote sensing, senor data collection, UAV-Enabled communications, relay for the ad hoc networks, disaster monitoring, flood area surveillance and wildfire tracking. As a fundamental element of unmanned aerial vehicle autonomous control module, UAV trajectory planning problem have been studied for decades. It can be formulated as an optimization problem which finds the feasible path from the source point to the destination point. In addition, the optimal trajectory is usually associated with the path that maximize (or minimize) the certain optimization index. We derive the optimal surveillance trajectories for multiple monitoring drones for surveilling the certain operation area to detect the existence of illegal drones following the shortest path. Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) achieves the purpose of simultaneous positioning and map construction based on self-perception. data.projectName: Does Financial Styles of Managers matter for firm efficiency: Evidence from United Kingdom and Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Financial markets are experiencing rapid growth in Islamic finance, which follows a unique form of investment which are related to the Muslim values regarding socially responsible investing. One of the most important and rapidly growing investor of current age is Islamic investors. For an Islamic investor basic thing is the company in which he/she is investing must follow laws and principles of Islam for revenue generation. These laws and principles are collectively termed as sharia and firms who follows these principles are termed as sharia complaint firms. Top management of any company are responsible for setting policies and principles for any organization. Extend literature suggest that managerial traits and characteristics play and important role in determination of firm’s decision and firm outcome (performance an efficiency). Using trait activation theory (Tatt and Guterman 2000) and upper echelon theory (Hambrick & Mason, 1984) this study argues that financial styles of managers matter for firm’s decisions. Thus, the objective of this research project is to study the role of top management team in firm efficiency at sharia and non-sharia compliant firms. Using our academic collaboration, we will use data from two different economies one developed (United Kingdom) and one emerging economy (Pakistan). For each firm in the sample, a manager-firm matched panel will be used to identify the impact of top manager’s financial styles across the sharia compliant firms over the time. Moreover in this research we will also study the improvement in firm efficiency when managers move from non-sharia to sharia firm or when they move from sharia to sharia complaint firms.

data.projectName: Indigenous plant species as a source of bio active components for development of nutraceutical baked foods
data.projectDigest:
The role of diet therapy in the prevention or management of human chronic diseases is well established all over the world. In Pakistan around seven million people are suffering from diabetes mellitus and seven million are reported with secondary symptoms. A huge Pakistani population that is around 37% declared as obese. According to IAEA (international atomic energy agency) reports every year 150000 patients in Pakistan diagnosed with cancer. These statistics demand research in producing health promoting foods which can manage/prevent such diseases.
Potential researches have been conducted on indigenous plants species that may be utilized for manufacturing of processed functional foods. Cordia myxa (gondni) is a native plant widely grown in south Asia and highly nutritive with several properties such as anti-diabetic, antiulcer, anti-inflammatory, immune-modulator and analgesics. Jambolin seeds are undoubtedly one of the best natural remedies for diabetes, lowering blood pressure, partially cure heart disease and help in curing hepatic disorder. Dates and date pits are well known for health benefits especially dietary fiber and high in antioxidant capacities. Such examples of native plants as source ingredients may use in food industry can initiate a nutraceutical foods sector and may promote marketing of these products at "health shops"

data.projectName: Thermoelectric properties of 1-2-2 structured Zintl materials for thermoelectric technology
data.projectDigest: Energy consumption of the world is increasing day by day to fulfill the basic and industrial needs.  Most part of it comes from the burning of the fossil fuels. In the burning process most part of the useful heat is wasted due to non-ideal machines (which can not completely convert the heat energy into useful work).  This heat is added to the environment and cause the global warming and pollution. It is therefore very natural to investigate and develop strategies to convert this heat into the useful work. One of the best way is to use the thermometric devices which can convert heat into electrical energy. In the current work new materials will be studied which have high thermometric efficiency and different strategies will be adopted to increase the thermometric efficiency of these materials.

data.projectName: Phenomenological Effects of Flavored Gauge Mediated Supersymmetry Breaking and Higgs Physics
data.projectDigest: Standard model (SM) of particle physics is our best understanding of the universe at present. Though this model has been tested successfully with high precision, however, it lacks explanation for some experimental facts as well as some theoretical arguments. Neutrino masses and mixing, dark matter, dark energy and Higgs mass Hierarchy problem are the sectors where SM need to be modified or extended. Supersymmetric (SUSY) extension of the SM is the best candidate that can explain the short comings in the SM. The large hadron collider experiment (LHC) at CERN has been built to test SM as well as its SUSY extension. LHC was able to confirm the prediction laid down by SM but there is no direct experimental verification for SUSY particles yet. This leaves us with the only option to study SUSY via its indirect effects. On the other hand, LHC experiment is putting severe constraint on the conventional SUSY models. In this project, we will explore different SUSY breaking mechanisms and study the phenomenological effects of these mechanisms via electroweak precision observables, Higgs boson masses and B-Physics observables. We hope that this study will help experimentalists in their quest for SUSY particle searches at colliders.

This leaves us with the only option to study SUSY via its indirect effects. On the other hand, LHC experiment is putting severe constraint on the conventional SUSY models. In this project, we will explore different SUSY breaking mechanisms and study the phenomenological effects of these mechanisms via electroweak precision observables, Higgs boson masses and B-Physics observables. We hope that this study will help experimentalists in their quest for SUSY particle searches at colliders.

data.projectName: How Nitric Oxide and the mitochondrial gene SAG12 contribute towards the tolerance of rice to stress.
data.projectDigest: Rice production in recent years has been around 487.46 million metric tons that placed it third worldwide (Statista, worldwide production of grains 2017). This is the second staple food of Pakistan after wheat. This valuable crop is being affected due to climate change factors as well as various biotic factors such as plant pathogens. Therefore, this project aims to produce rice varieties of improved tolerance towards biotic and abiotic stresses. Senescence associated gene SAG12/AtSAG12 belonging to the late embryogenesis-associated (LEA) protein family has been reported to contribute to disease resistance. Senescence is an important part of crop development as it influences how and when nutrients are moved to the seeds from the rest of the plant.  Although SAG12 has been implicated in growth and stress responses (reference), its precise role remains obscure. The orthologues of this gene are present in rice. Therefore, this project aims to study the role of this gene in Rice. Rice being rich in proteins of high nutritional value and hypoallergenic properties, is a staple diet of many Asian countries and is under constant threat of biotic and abiotic stresses. Therefore, the aim of the current project is the surveillance of this significant crop from the potent threats.

data.projectName: Socio- cognitive Correlates and Psychopathological Outcomes of Psychopathic Tendencies in Non- forensic Populations of Punjab Province
data.projectDigest: The accelerated crime rate in Pakistan is alarming for law and enforcement agencies. A well-documented literature is found on the relationship between psychopathy and crime. Most of the criminals even non- criminals are found to have high psychopathic tendencies. Psychopathy is known as a personality construct, associated with negative outcomes such as aggressive personality traits and antisocial behaviors (Williams, Paulhus & Hare, 2007). Therefore, the current research project will aim to assess these psychopathic tendencies among  non- forensic populations by an indigenously developed assessment tool. Steps will also be taken to establish the psychometric properties of this newly developed scale so that a psychometrically sound measure should be available for future use. The study further intended to assess various socio- cognitive processes and psychopathological outcomes of psychopathic tendencies among non- forensic population of community and student. The differences on study variables across various demographic variables (i.e., gender, age, educational levels and types of profession) will also be considered. The findings of this research project can be implemented in various community and educational settings to generate an awareness regarding correlates and negative outcomes of psychopathic tendencies and in providing services for improving mental health.

data.projectName: Commercialization and propagation of local and exotic landraces  of Moringa oleifera as a fodder crop and forest tree
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: Nature has blessed us with moringa tree which is commonly found in southern Punjab. However, we could not explore its potential. The proposed project will screen the moringa landraces for fodder crop. The findings of this project will provide new gateway for researchers to further explore the hidden benefits of our native tree. Collaboration between institutions will be initiated and more productive research will be done on the right way for the benefits of end users. Local dairy industry will be involved in this research. Currently, Herbyzone Private Limited, Lahore is using leaves of moringa for dairy purpose. Moringa for Life, a society for the awareness of moringa in Pakistan with the support of students and teachers/researchers has registered who is providing free advisory services and moringa seeds to common people and farming community. Salient objectives of projects are Identification of moringa landraces suitable fodder, forage and grazing purpose, devising production technology for quality moringa biomass production, devising suitable drying techniques for moringa leaf powder formation and optimization of dozes of moringa dry leaf powder for different animal feeding.

data.projectName: Closing yield gap in wheat by improving nitrogen use efficiency through potassium supplementation
data.projectDigest: Wheat is highly important food grain crop worldwide and the staple food of Pakistan. The yield of wheat crop in Pakistan is much lower than the other main wheat producing countries of the world. Nitrogen is a basic plant nutrient and the most important limiting factor in crop production. Generally the nitrogen use efficiency of crops ranges from 30-50%. Recent studies show that mean wheat yields in Pakistan are far below than several of the top wheat producing countries. On the other hand, use of nitrogen fertilizers is the highest among top countries. Low yield with high N application rate is not only reducing farmer profits but is also contributing to the emission of greenhouse gases. Improved nitrogen use efficiency can increase the wheat yield and help meet the food security challenges in Pakistan. Imbalance nutrition is one of the most important factors for low nitrogen use efficiency of wheat. It is a well-established fact that potassium improves utilization of nitrogen by plants. Due to continuous cropping Pakistani soils are becoming deficient in potassium reserves. The current project is designed to improve wheat yield in Pakistan by improving nitrogen use efficiency through potassium supplementation.

data.projectName: Free Amino Acids and Short Peptide Fertilizer (FASPF) from fermentation of agro wastes by PGPR
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Seeking some environmentally sustainable practices to complement chemical-based agriculture is the need of the time. An innovative technology with promising potential entails the use of Free Amino Acids and Short Peptide Fertilizer (FASPF), preferably formed from solid state fermentation of agro wastes by Plant Growth Promoting Rhizobacteria (PGPR). At initial step, bacterial strains already available at National Culture Collection Centre of National Agricultural Research Centre will be screened for efficient strains showing the potential of plant growth promotion as well as fermentation. Different agrowastes (peanut shell, soyabean pods/pea pods and black gram husks) will be collected and processed into powder form. Selected PGPR strains will be used for solid state fermentation of this waste with optimized conditions for pH, temperature, moisture content, particle size etc. Pre and post analysis will be carried out by FTIR for functional characterization of produced Free Amino Acids and Short Peptides.  These FASPF, an organic chelate ligands, will be supplemented with micronutrients. The production process will guarantee a liquid product containing essential amino acids and micronutrients. This FASPF will be tested in hydroponics and greenhouse experiment (Green Circle Company). Collaboration with Auriga industry will help in commercial launching of our finalized tested product.

data.projectName: BIOSYNTHESIS AND EVALUATION OF ECOFRIENDLY NANOPESTICIDE AGAINST THE LOCAL URBAN PESTS
data.piUniversity: Lahore College for Women University, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Sustainable Development Goal 3 states to ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all at all ages. In developing countries infectious diseases, mostly caused by vectors or carriers are major concerns of public health. Urban pests are considered extremely dangerous vectors of pathogens and parasites. Among them, mosquitoes and houseflies represent a huge threat for millions of people worldwide. Disease transmitted by vectors/carriers are controlled by use of synthetic insecticides, which causes toxicity to non-target organisms, pest resistance and environmental pollution. Due to hazards associated with use of synthetic insecticide there has been an urgent need to explore suitable alternative approach to control urban pests. Recently, nanotechnology has emerged as a promising tool for pest management. A number of physical, chemical and biological methods are available for nanoparticles synthesis. The physico-chemical methods are expensive and environmentally unsafe as they use of harmful chemicals. The current study proposes ecofriendly method for the synthesis of nanoparticles by using Bacillus thuringiensis. The synthesized nanoparticles will be characterized by FTIR, XRD and SEM. The insecticidal potential of nanoparticles against house fly and mosquitoes will be investigated by biochemical analyses that will be help in future to develop an improved strategy to control insect pests.

data.projectName: Building the Moral and Ethical Capital of Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: It is argued that morality, ethics, and social mannerism (MES) should be one of the goals of an education system. The foremost goal of an education system should be to produce high-quality human capital stock; equipped with the traits of a decent person, such as avoiding the dependency syndrome (waiting for someone to solve your problems). This project focuses on educational institutions of Pakistan, to generate debate on MES; request for collaboration shall be sent to educational institutions (on the basis of our professional contacts we guarantee that at least 10 educational institutions shall participate). Training sessions on MES shall be organized at all participating institutions; behavior change is a slow and steady process, we shall ensure that information material regarding MES is displayed in each institution’s notice boards, MES related messages shall be regularly sent to the students/teachers. This project shall follow Dr. Fogg’s Behavior Change Model to improve the conduct of the participants regarding MES. Impact assessment of the continuous information dissemination shall be carried out after 12—15 months; determinants of better MES scores shall be analyzed. This project shall help Pakistan to work for the Goal-4, and Goal 11 of the United Nation’s Sustainable Development Goals.

data.projectName: Explosive detection by IR thermal imaging
data.projectDigest: Detection of explosive is very important in Pakistan due to threat posed by terrorism. Tracing small amount of explosive is the main theme of this project. Usually it is seen that long ques are present on barrier in sensitive areas. The officers have to check the cars one by one. The advantage of this technique is it can detect the explosive from a distance. This ensures overall safety of the protecting team. Also this technique covers large area as compare to checking of individual car.  In this research an autonomous robot is developed which can detect explosive material using IR thermal imaging. A compact infrared quantum cascade laser is stationed on robot for strong absorption band in the explosive materials which illuminate the surface of interest. The research will also show viability of this robot’s function on variety of surfaces having different properties of reflection. It also have detection selectivity to variety of explosives. Finally the compactness of robot makes it’s a very good alternative to all the traditional techniques.

data.projectName: Estimation of carbon sequestration in salt-affected soils during reclamation using organic and inorganic amendments for mitigation of climate change
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan, large area of agricultural soils is salt-affected which is either cultivated non-seriously or abandoned due to high degree of degradation. With passage of time, the problem of secondary salinity/sodicity is increasing due to several factors like non-scientific irrigation practices and use of poor quality ground water for irrigation. Coupled with the problem of salinity and sodicity, other factors like urbanization, industrialization and network of highways and other communication infrastructures, cultivated area is decreasing.  In addition to this, change in land use pattern, industrial and vehicular emissions has significantly increased the concentration of CO2 in the atmosphere which resulted in climate change and global warming. Under such conditions, slightly to moderately salt-affected soils can be efficiently cultivated to grow rice and wheat crops by adopting different reclamation/management strategies to ensure food security and enhancing soil carbon sequestration. Similarly, highly salt-affected soils (degraded soils) can be rehabilitated by growing fruit trees like Jaman, Guava, Ber and Date Palm which not only provide fruits to masses but also improve the carbon sequestration in soils to mitigate climate change.

data.projectName: DESIGN AND DEVELOPMENT OF AN ELECTROMAGNETIC ENERGY HARVESTER FOR POWERING MICROELECTONIC DEVICES
data.projectDigest: Durable and readily available energy sources have become an essential requirement for modern electromechanical engineering systems.Pervasive mechatronic systems characterizing smart structures lead designers to consider renewable energy sources targeted to feed the increasing number of embedded sensing and actuation devices.Energy harvesters provide a small amount of power for low-energy electronics (e.g smart phones, micro sensors).The source for energy harvesters is present as ambient background (vibrations) and is free.We are proposing a non-linear vibration based energy harvesting device that will be designed and developed indigenously at Air University.We will design an energy harvester that will be based on compliant structures benefited with displacement amplification mechanism.The project will develop skilled manpower in the area of energy harvesting.The project will benefit academic institutions, strategic organizations and especially the research groups working in the field of inertial sensors and energy harvesting devices.The proposed project will eventually lead to the development of a design and testing facility to all National Universities/Organizations doing R & D in the area of energy harvesting.We are already doing research in the area of energy harvesters and have almost finalized the design, however fabrication and testing facilities are not available for which we are seeking funding through this proposal.
