data.projectName: SEQUENCE ANALYSIS AND COMPARISON OF MULTI DRUG RESISTANT GENES OF BACTERIA CAUSING URINARY TRACT INFECTION AND EVALUATION OF SYNERGISTIC EFFECTS OF DIFFERENT ANTIBIOTICS ALONG WITH MEDICINAL PLANT EXTRACTS AND ITS NANO-PARTICLES ON MDR BACTERIA.
data.projectDigest: The propose work will be on screening of different UTI,s patients for the presence of multi drug resistant (MDR) bacteria in their urine and its identification through different biochemical and molecular techniques. Sequence analysis and comparison of different MDR and virulent genes in bacteria involved in Urinary tract infections. Secondly, synergistic affects of different antibiotics and its nanoparticles will be checked against these multi drug resistant isolates.  Natural extracts from various medicinal plants and its Nanoparticles will also be checked against multi drug resistant isolates to find out alternate effective natural drug. The current propose work will help to explored different effective combination of antibiotics and medicinally important natural drugs against multi drug resistant isolates causing UTI, s infection. Various characterizations and application will make sure the utilization of these drugs for human consumptions on MDR bacteria isolated from UTI, s patients. The overall purpose of the propose work is identify the sequence or genes responsible for drug resistance that will help in future for drug targeting and to search out or design effective synergetic drug against MDR bacteria from the antibiotics or medicinal plants.

data.projectName: Extraction, Isolation and Application of Selected Medicinal Plants Using Natural Deep Eutectic Solvent System on Cancer Cell Lines
data.projectDigest: Keeping in view, the current worldwide cancer statistics, treatments for different types of cancer need to be improved a lot to avoid the newer cases and cure the older ones. The challenges that are being faced are poor/ untargeted access of drug at the cancer site, different types of side effects with required drug quantities, nonspecific tissue distribution, and resistance against effectiveness of various cancer drugs.  Furthermore the therapeutic effect of the anticancer drugs can also be increased by using some effective solvent system that not only provide solubility of phytochemicals effective for cancer treatment which is not only health effective but also environment friendly. These solvents will not only increase the solubility of active compounds in plant extracts but also enhance the bioavailability of these compounds. In present project the isolation of these compounds will also be done that will be helpful to distinguish the active compounds extracted using ethanol and those with natural deep eutectic solvents.

data.projectName: Biopolymeric encapsulation of fourth generation probiotics with prebiotics in food matrices
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: There is an increasing demand of functional foods during the past few years. Probiotics are part of functional foods and its importance must be communicated to consumers. However, probiotics face great challenges of its viability, survivability, stability in harsh conditions including low pH, at high or non- chilled temperature and in high water activity foods. Moreover, its targeted delivery or controlled release is also very important for its proper functionality. These issues can be resolved by using different techniques in which encapsulation is one of them. Different polymers or wall materials have been used for this purpose, but still lot of work is required to see the “Smart biopolymers” for encapsulation. Prebiotics are the dietary fibers which help in the bacterial proliferation. We can extract it from different fruit peels which we normally thrown away. Together probiotics with prebiotics will show symbiotic relationship which if encapsulated will possess beneficial effects. This synbiotic capsules with different biopolymers can be used in the incorporation in different food products and can be useful for infants, adults, pregnant women and elderly.

data.projectName: Propagation techniques and use of elicitors to enhance Ginkgolide contents in Ginkgo biloba L. cell suspension cultures
data.projectDigest: Ginkgo biloba L. with its wild population confined to China has a unique history of its primitive characters and therapeutic properties. Limited population of this ancient plant due to its recalcitrant seeds and low potential of propagation pose immense difficulty to fulfill huge pharmaceutical demands of Ginkgo extracts worldwide. Investigating some sustainable propagation strategies is therefore, of prime importance especially in areas where this plant is not indigenous as is the case with Pakistan. Present study will deal to optimize conditions for Ginkgo propagation under greenhouse conditions as well as in vitro. Rooting potential of stem cuttings will be investigated under greenhouse conditions and will also be experimented to avail sufficient supply of juvenile explants to establish in vitro systems for Ginkgo propagation. Micropropagation, callus, regeneration and cell suspension cultures will be then tested for their potential to multiply the plant. Elicitors like Chitosan and Yeast extract will be used to induce ginkgolide and flavonoid accumulation in suspension cultures established from callus lines rich in these contents. Optimized methods with best propagation potential and most appropriate treatment of these elicitors might be then proposed to be used at commercial level in order to fulfill our country’s demands of pharmaceutical industries to get ample supply of Ginkgo extract in a cost effective manner.

data.projectName: Assessment of phytoremediation potential of indigenous plants at physiological and molecular level
data.projectDigest: Heavy metals released from the mining and industrial waste/tailing deposit or solid waste dump site and wastewater are the major source contamination in soil and water. The alleviation of heavy metals contamination in soil/wastewater has been paid much attention due to their potential threat to living organisms. For that purpose, a number of physical, chemical, biological techniques were applied for soil and wastewater treatment. Among these treatment methods, the phytoremediation techniques are green, sustainable and promising solution to problems of such environmental contaminants. Moreover, phytoremediation is a low cost, environmentally friendly and green solution to the heavy metals’ contamination problem, thus it is imperative to identify the native hyper-accumulator plants species and response genes involved in the heavy metal’s accumulation and stress tolerance. Therefore, this study is aimed to identify the indigenous hyper-accumulators and the heavy metals response genes and their expression. Hyper-accumulator plant species could be used for the alleviation of respective heavy metals contamination from soil, dump sites and the wastewater. The hyper-accumulator plant species have ability to decontaminate our precious water, soil resources and food crops. Provision of safe water and food will lower the potential risk and diseases and subsequently minimize the health budget.

data.projectName: national dictionary of pakistani languages
data.projectDigest: language plays a very important role in upholding  territorial integrity and ensuring national sovereignty .in today's troubled times, the seed for different linguistic communicate to connect and communicate with one another is urgent more than ever before. As an important step towards this we propose to compile a "National Dictionary of Pakistani Languages". This online as well as printed dictionary will begin with at least 30000 Urdu words that would be translated into Brahui, Balochi, Pashto, Punjabi, Saraiki, Sindhi, and finally, English. This multilingual resource would encourage translators of Pakistani languages. We plan to make a app of this dictionary that can be used in phones by traders, tourists, professionals and anyone in anyone in need of knowing a word from the language of the fellow countrymen.

data.projectName: Optimization of detection methods for zoonotic parasites in fish meat, their effect on the shelf life and quantification of resultant allergens with perspective to export market
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Fish represents a valuable source of white meat and providing one-fifth of animal protein consumption and other nutrients in many parts of the world. 
In the utilization of fish meat beside the meat quantity, food safety is of great importance as fish meat may contain different types of chemical and biological hazards. In these hazards, heavy metals, biogenic amines and parasitic presence are most important. Heavy metals come from the water while biological amines are produced by the degradation of amines by microorganisms and utilized as an indicator of freshness while parasites may be engulfed with food and later become the part of the body.
Nowadays, Anisakis allergens are included in the standard sets of allergens during allergy investigation. These allergens may be present as an excretory and secretory antigen from living larvae, somatic and cuticular antigens from dead and disintegrating larvae present in food. Among all these, Ani s4 is a clinically relevant allergen due to its heat, acid and pepsin resistant properties and its importance in the anaphylaxis process.
In general, from local consumers' health points of view and for export purposes these parameters are of great importance. The Rapid Alert System for Food and Feed (RASFF) portal shows that many Pakistan consignments are rejected due to one or two of these issues. So, quantification and preventive measure suggestions to the fish farmers and allied industries will be an important step for overall betterment.

data.projectName: Miocene Ruminants of the Siwalik Potwar Plateau: A Correlation with the Miocene Ruminants of Balkan-Irano-Afganian Province
data.projectDigest: I propose a detailed documentation of the Miocene ruminants from the Potwar Plateau of Pakistan. One of the most complete terrestrial Mio-Pliocene sequences in the world can be found in the Potwar Plateau of Pakistan, and which could support the calibration of climatic and faunal changes in the region. By documenting the Miocene ruminants of the Indian Subcontinent and carefully controlling their provenance, we can correlate the faunal events with the Miocene localities of the Balkan-Irano-Afganian province, two of the major Neogene bio-provinces that both had continuous influence by the Neogene African realm. By developing the full potential of the biotic and stratigraphic record we would be able to reconstruct habitat and faunal changes in the Indian Subcontinent. This will provide crucial information to define the mode of faunal change of this area during the Miocene against the backdrop of regional and global climatic events. The collected assemblages will be used to establish biostratigraphy of the area and make correlations with the Miocene of the Balkan-Irano-Afganian province.

data.projectName: A Framework for Reliable Link Adaptive Position-based X2X Communication using Artificial Intelligence
data.projectDigest: Ad hoc network is an infrastructure less network with decentralized nature. It has gained attention because of its self-configuring, self-organizing, self-healing, and dynamic network capabilities. One of the emerging ad hoc networks that uses Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to cooperate and share the information with each other and forward the desired information to the intended destination is commonly referred as Flying ad hoc network (FANET). FANET provides portable and flexible communication for many applications such as surveillance, environmental monitoring and disaster management. FANET can be observed as a special form of existing ad hoc network like MANET and VANET. But due to high mobility of nodes in the air and dynamic network topology, FANET has several unique design challenges; a key one of which is the successful delivery of message to destination, reliably. For reliable data communication, routing plays an important role which establishes a path between source and destination on the basis of certain criteria. the current project should be adaptable that will support aforementioned applications. Furthermore, the FANET will be linked with VANET to design and implement a framework using Artificial Intelligence techniques, which would be beneficial in managing the crimes as well as preventing the road accidents.

data.projectName: Isolation and structure characterization of secondary metabolites from Hibiscus rosa-sinenesis  flowers and their anti-diabetic evaluation
data.projectDigest: Present proposal of study emphasized on the isolation, identification, structure elucidation of secondary metabolites and their biological evaluation as anti-diabetic agent from the Hibiscus sinensis-rosa, a folk medicinal plants used in Africa, Asia and especially in traditional medicine system of China. This plant is a is used in folk drugs like anti-viral, anti-fungal, antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, anti-pyretic, anti-tumor, anti-aging, aborsifier  in its raw form like tea, nutraceutical, water extract and methanolic extract.  etc. thus, in proposed study, the plant flowers will be used to prepare their extracts and then subjected to chromatographic techniques (Column, thin layer, gel, HPLC) for purification. After purification, the secondary metabolites will be analysed to elucidate their structure by spectroscopic techniques (UV, IR, Mass, NMR (1D- & 2-D), ECD etc.). These compounds will be evaluated for their potential against diabetes. It is planned to synthesize active lead compounds for future studies. World facing a growing metabolic disease as a great challenge is the diabetes mellitus. It is attained 7th leading cause of death in USA. Today, its rate is alarming as IDF (International Diabetes Federation) estimates 62.0 million effected people in India, 36.3 million in USA and 7.1 million people suffering from diabetes and rate of increase is about 1.5 million/ year. In recent time, it is challenge to find out cost-effective.

data.projectName: Synthesis of molecular sieves  and development of portable oxygen concentrator for clinical applications
data.projectDigest: Oxygen supply system is very crucial for the patients in critical conditions. An efficient and economic oxygen concentrator can provide a great relief to those in need.  An oxygen concentrator separates the oxygen from the ambient air by employing molecular sieves that adsorb the nitrogen and other gases from the ambient air. This project is aimed at synthesis of molecular sieves and development of portable oxygen concentrator (POC) for clinical applications. The zeolite based molecular sieves will be synthesized and employed in our developed POC. Our POC will be based on pressure swing adsorption (PSA) and the performance of our synthesized molecular sieves will be evaluated for achieving the best possible efficiency. The effects of morphology, grain size, pore size of the molecular sieves will also be studied in detail. The performance of the POC will also be evaluated at different environmental conditions. The developed product will be a great blessing for the patients in critical condition and its portability can offer a variety of advantages. This project is expected to result in the material development and fabrication of a prototype POC which can be scaled for its commercial applications.

data.projectName: Ecotaxonomic Studies and Sustainable Utilization of Plant resources of District Narowal, Punjab Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
The present study will be conducted on the Plant diversity of District Narowal with special reference to their utilization and phytosociological attributes. The district has never been explored so far for such studies. Hence there is need for an integrated and comprehensive study of plants of Narowal. Most rural people of the district meet their needs by using natural resources. However, there is no recorded information available regarding the use and management of such resources. Therefore, the present study will helpful to close this knowledge gap.  Narowal, a district of Punjab Province of Pakistan, having three tehsils i.e. Narowal, Shakargarh and Zafarwal, bounded on the northwest by Sialkot district, on the north by Kathua district of Indian Jammu and Kashmir, on the southeast by Gurdaspur and Pathankot district (India), on the south by Amritsar district (India).

data.projectName: In vitro anti-ulcer activity of indigenous plants for stomach disorders used by the Pakistani herbalists
data.piUniversity: Government College for Women University, Sialkot
data.projectDigest: Stomach related disorders caused by high stomach acidity if go unchecked, may culminate in life threatening cancer and subsequent mortality.  Stomach related cancers are third largest cause of death in cancer patients. The causative agent of such diseases is a bacterium, Helicobacter pylori. This bacterium takes over the stomach and all associated organs of it and attack stomach lining causing ulcers which lead towards cancer. A huge number of people suffer from such disorders but careless lifestyle results in ulcers. Antibiotics including metronidazole, clarithromycin and amoxicillin have been used for treatment of such diseases but bacterium has gradually become resistant to antibiotics which is an alarming situation and it calls for search for alternative ways of treatment. Researchers now-a-days are looking forward to discovery of novel antibacterial agents from plants which can treat such devastating bacteria. Plants are among those natural resources that have been used by human beings since time immemorial for treatment of all kinds of human diseases and ailments, which makes them reliable alternative sources for discovery of some chemicals that can treat diseases including stomach related disorders. The present research work is focused on some selected plants from Sialkot district that have been reported in literature for treatment of stomach related disorders. It is expected that their use will be scientifically validated and some novel antibacterial agent/s will be discovered from plants against bacterium that causes such diseases. If such a compound is discovered, in this proposed research project, another project will be developed for further research on that compound to find out its effect in mouse models and ultimately on human beings in order to develop so

data.projectName: Mapping creative industries in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: The current study is an attempt to qualitatively analyze the importance of cultural and creative industries of Pakistan with respect to national policy. The countries in South Asian region are struggling to formulate an effective module for economic growth, same is the case with Pakistan. Currently, countries are realizing the fact that without the help of creative sector, one will not be able to excel the economy efficiently. So, the study in hand is trying to formulate mapping documents to explore opportunities, challenges, policy implications and point of intervention regarding creative sector (Design, Traditional media, Visual and Digital media, Theater and Performing arts, Arts and Crafts, Tangible and Intangible Heritage documentation and Creative Entrepreneurship) of Pakistan. For this purpose, the study in hand is going to employ qualitative research design along with Grounded theory as an approach to inquiry, under which semi-structured, in-depth interviews will be conducted. The interviews will be tape recorded after getting the respondent’s consent, then this video information will be uploaded on Centre for Creative economy’s website for the dissemination purpose. This research project will try to seek answers of the following questions in order to accomplish the said objectives; 1) What is the potential of cultural and creative industries of Pakistan? 2) What are the opportunities and challenges in the formation of mapping documents regarding creative industries in Pakistan? 3) What are the policy implications of assisting collaborative mechanism in document formulation? 4) How the mapping documents can assist the socio-economic potential of creative industries in Pakistan?

data.projectName: Automatic immersive visualization of text-embedded chemical structures diagrams
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Chemistry is a visual science, thus requires students to be able to interpret and apprehend spatial structures and processes. For a thorough understanding and problem solving, students must be able to integrate their spatial skills and conceptual knowledge. However, chemistry students face difficulties in abstraction, model perception, and spatial manipulation tasks as conventional teaching methods do not always aid student comprehension. Studies show 3D visualization techniques integrated into teaching methodologies greatly enhance student learning. There is a need to link 2D and 3D representations to help students gain deeper understanding of concepts.  In this project, we propose a framework to aid spatial learning process by automatically creating a link between 2D representations of chemical structures and 3D molecular visualization. This will be done by identification of structures in images captured by handheld devices followed by generation of 3D models of the identified molecular structures which could then be displayed using handheld as well as immersive head mounted display (HMD) devices. We will evaluate the effect of proposed approach on the spatial ability of students enrolled in chemistry related courses. The framework will be extended for a classroom or a laboratory environment where students (as client nodes) will be able to connect to a server (as the instructor). Multiple students wearing HMDs will be able to fetch customized lecture materials in the form of 3D models and attempt assessment exercises online. The project is expected to culminate in a proof-of-concept implementation of a tool for aiding teaching and learning of concepts in chemistry related courses along with objective analysis of its effects on students’ spatial learning ability.

data.projectName: Indigenous Surface Acoustic Waves (SAW) Sensor Development for Realtime Monitoring of Environmental Particulate Matter
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Benazir Bhutto Women University, Peshawar
data.projectDigest:
Industrial revolution has triggered urbanization at a rapid pace. In metropolitan cities specially in the developing world. Although the benefits of industrial revolution are unsurpassed when we consider the improvements in the state of life. Nevertheless, the overall urban ambient air pollution has caused over 1 million premature deaths. According to WHO Fact sheet for year 2019 air pollution has become a global public health emergency with 92% world population is exposed to the air quality levels exceeding that are suitable for public health. Fine particulate matter (PM) is among the most hazardous pollutants which is also classified as the main carcinogen in air pollution. Not only PM can penetrate through lungs but has severe respiratory as well as cardiovascular impact on the urban citizens health.
In this project, we plan to design indigenous sensors based on surface acoustic wave (SAW) technology which can provide easy detection techniques as compared to heavy and expensive optical setup. The SAW sensors basically generate and sense the acoustic waves using interdigitated transducers (IDT) designed on the surface of a piezoelectric material which are very sensitive to the mass loaded on the surface. These sensors can provide us very simple, small and effective sensors for monitoring most dangerous and small environment particulate matter PM1.
Directly being inline with the Sustainable Development Goals adopted by United Nations, this project will directly have impact on providing access to clean fuel and clean technologies (SDG 7.1.2) and most importantly improvement of air quality in urban spaces (SDG 11.6.2). These also form basis for achieving disease burden reduction on urban populations through reduction of exposure to air pollution especially PM below PM2.5

data.projectName: Bacteriophage Proteins a Novel Approach as Antimicrobials to Combat Multi Drug Resistance Bacteria
data.projectDigest: The emergence of bacteria that are resistant to antibiotics including E. coli, S. aureus etc. is becoming a grave threat to infection control that crosses international boundaries and is considered as the scourge of this era. To combat this deadly problem there is an urgent need to develop novel treatment strategies. Increased attention is being paid to the possibility that novel therapies utilizing bacteriophages could be deployed as a valuable adjunct to conventional therapeutic approaches. However, there are many complications associated with phage therapy. One alternative to the utilization of phages for treatment is the utilization of purified lytic proteins of phage origin that includes ectolysin, endolysin and holins. The ectolysins and the endolysins are peptidoglycan hydrolases that degrade bacterial cell wall leading to bacterial death. The advantage associated with phage lysins is the lower level of chances of emergence of resistance because the target of endolysin is highly conserved part of bacterial cell wall. Therefore, in this project we aim to isolate bacteriophages, sequence the whole genome to allocate lysine genes, and functional characterization of the endlolysin against MDR strains of bacteria.

data.projectName: Function of Glycotoxins in development of chronic metabolic diseases in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: One of the largest global health emergencies is diabetes.In 2019, Pakistan ranked 4th with most diabetic people in the world, while the country ranked 10th in 2017. Rate of diabetes is increasing dramatically in Pakistan from 6.9 million in 2007 to 20 million in 2019. Glycotoxins also called Advanced glycation end products (AGEs), are toxins formed in the body and outside the body. When sugar reacts with proteins. AGEs are also formed in food, when cooked at high temperature. Glycated hemoglobin (HBA1c) is also an AGEs, widely used in diagnosis of diabetes. Across the globe, AGEs  are strongly linked to development of diabetes in patients. However, studies are lacking in Pakistani population about AGEs implications in development of diabetes. Present study will address, for first time in Pakistan, glycotoxin load of diabetic patients and its association with symptoms of diabetes. Additionally, new  anti-diabetic neutraceuticals that can inhibit AGEs,  will be identified and their molecular mechanism of actions will be explored. Huge advantage of our study is that anti-AGEs agents from food are safe, simple and cost effective and can be ingested in everyday life. Results of our study can alleviate ever increasing burden of diabetes which affects millions in the world.

data.projectName: High performance Lead free  Ceramic Composite for energy harvesting applications
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Piezoelectric actuators, car buzzer and sensors have been manufactured from Pb-added piezoelectric materials (PZT). For environmental concern, RoHs has been recommended to shrink the usage of dangerous and toxic substances for human health and environment issue. Therefore lead free ceramics and their composites play an important role in piezoelectric applications. Piezoelectric based devices are widely used in commercial, industrial, and defense applications. Piezoelectric is a versatile material which is used to make sensor, actuator, energy harvester and transformers. Ceramic type lead-based piezoelectric material is most used in devices due to its high performance, application-based tuning. 
Piezoelectric material and devices are imported in Pakistan. The main reason for this import is the lack of commercial processes in Pakistan for mineral beneficiations and raw powders processing. New world export/import regulations are focusing on a lead-free piezoelectric material, which is not dangerous to health. This project aims to develop the lead-free piezoelectric ceramic material in Pakistan. An effort will be done to establish supply-chain and resources required for lead-free piezoelectric ceramic material development and manufacturing. The developed piezoelectric material will be used to make widely used piezoelectric speaker (also known as a buzzer), which is used in automobile, toys industry.

data.projectName: Establishment of PGF2alpha based fixed time artificial insemination protocol in Beetal goats by assessing developmental potential of mid-luteal phase follicles
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Artificial insemination (AI) is a tool for rapid genetic gains in livestock. For this purpose, progesterone based fixed time-AI protocols are conventionally used in goats  due to consistent ovulatory response, however,  this approach is expensive and pose public health hazards due to drug residue. On the contrary, PGF2alpha is easy to administer, cost-effective and has no public health concerns. However, PGF2 alpha based AI protocols require estrus detection which is a labour intensive and subjective procedure. In our previous research, after administering single PGF2alpha, ovulatory response varied within 20-24 h in majority of the goats (85%). Also, other studies reported a comparable pregnancy rate between PGF2alpha and progesterone based AI protocols in goats . Currently, there is limited understanding about follicle developmental potential at the time of PGF2 alpha administration during luteal phase. This information is necessary to overcome the need of estrus detection, repeated inseminations and to devise a fixed time of AI in goats during breeding season.  Hence, the current project will address the potential issues associated with the use of PGF2alpha in timed-AI protocols and will devise the best time for single AI after PGF2alpha without estrus detection in goats.

data.projectName: Internet of Things (IoT) based smart platform to enhance productivity and protection of vegetable farms
data.projectDigest: Smart farming/agriculture is a concept of farming management that utilizes modern technologies to increase the quality and quantity of products. It helps to monitor every detail related to the production of crops such as soil analysis, water level, temperature, humidity etc. The demand for smart farming is boosting because of the rapid escalation of food demand due to the growing population. Various studies show that smart farming and its market is expected to reach $23.14 billion by 2022. The growth is primarily attributed to: higher demand for crop yield, excessive use of information and communication technologies in farming, and addressing the needs for climate-smart agriculture. Smart farming is already established in developed countries; however, developing countries such as Pakistan are lacking the expertise in adopting this latest trend. This project aims to describe the current prospects of smart farming in Pakistan and present the overall benefit of using smart farming in vegetable farms. We believe that the results from our project will provide a guideline to the farmers in Pakistan while adopting smart farming for enhanced productivity and protection. We also aim to open new avenues for employment in the smart agriculture business.

data.projectName: Policies and Practices of Local E-Government in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: Open, Responsive and Participatory Governance at the Grassroots
data.projectDigest: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government claims to have transformed governance through efficient service delivery, access to information, transparency and citizen’s engagement by employing Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs). Such claims are to be validated through an investigation that looks into e-governance at grassroots level i.e local government. Local government is closest administrative setup to the citizens and therefore, It is pertinent to investigate the above claims at the lowest tier of government. Additionally, it is also pertinent to probe the extent to which the policies and practices of local e-government in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa are in line with international commitments made by Pakistan to the UN Sustainable Development Goals. In nutshell, this project is about investigating policies and practices of e-governance at the lowest tier of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government. The data will be collected through reading the relevant policy documents, reports and by interviewing a range of officers of provincial and local governments. The findings of the project would help the provincial government to reflect on their local e-government endeavours and would also help the researchers and students of e-governance in Pakistan to learn about the less explored area of local e-governance in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Monitoring and Tracking of Dengue Fever using Smartphone via GPS
data.projectDigest: In the age of modern technology use of modern technologies for monitoring, tracking and identifying the disease is vital. On the other hand various nations use these technologies i.e Smartphone for data collection and GPS for tracking and identification of disease affected areas.  However, in Pakistan use of Smartphone, GPS and SMS technology not implemented yet for surveillance of disease in health sector.  Therefore, incorporation of these technologies for real time monitoring and tracking the epidemic disease dengue which causing number of deaths every year is necessary.  Hence it is a challenge and need of time to monitor the behavior of the dengue and offer awareness to the patients.  Furthermore, the data of affected patients and breading sites will helpful for authorities for taking prompt and proactive decisions to counter the outburst of the dengue.   This research may result in development of monitoring and tracking dengue fever framework using Smartphone via GPS and also a prototype of android application and software module which may handle to collect data and generation map for identification of dengue affected areas.

data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest: A core issue like hunger remains an everyday battle for millions of people worldwide. The right to food is a basic human right addressed in the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), which includes a target to end hunger by 2030. This looming scene crafts a demand to apprehend this multi-faceted issue to be accomplished. Going forward, the goal of ending hunger requires more than words. Right to food under international human rights law is that all human beings should have access to food regardless of their age, gender, religion, location and social status. We need to enlist everyone’s support if we are to ensure food security and adequate nutrition on a global scale and truly become the Zero Hunger generation. It requires collective actions, including efforts to double global food production, reduce waste and experiment with food alternatives. The use of wild plants as food is an integral part of the culture and tradition of many indigenous communities around the world. Documentation of wild edible plants contributes in defining the ownership of wild food and the model of its production to determine the extent to be self-reliant by protecting domestic food and regulate trade for sustainable development objectives.

data.projectName: Condition Assessment of RC Bridges: Devising Bridge Rating System
data.projectDigest: While bridges represent the might of a country’s infrastructure; their collapse causes equally detrimental economy and life losses. Reinforced-concrete bridges are subject to continuous deterioration due to environmental effects and material degradation. As, overly damaged bridges may collapse under excessive loads, bridges should be periodically checked for concrete and reinforcing-steel quality and rated according to specified guidelines to identify the bridge conditions for urgent repair. Such guidelines exist in all the developed countries like USA, Canada, Japan etc. Unfortunately an effective and viable bridge assessment and rating system is not in practice in our country. Consequently, a feasible bridge assessment system needs to be developed incorporating visual inspection and non-destructive testing techniques. The proposed research project targets this deficiency by developing a viable bridge assessment and rating system. In this research study, various bridges will be inspected visually. Later, the selected bridges will be tested using various non-destructive testing techniques to determine bridges’ quality. Furthermore, the test data will be used to formulate a bridge rating system which will facilitate various national authorities towards the sustainable asset management and will also serve as a benchmark for the future development of similar systems.

Such guidelines exist in all the developed countries like USA, Canada, Japan etc. Unfortunately an effective and viable bridge assessment and rating system is not in practice in our country. Consequently, a feasible bridge assessment system needs to be developed incorporating visual inspection and non-destructive testing techniques. The proposed research project targets this deficiency by developing a viable bridge assessment and rating system. In this research study, various bridges will be inspected visually. Later, the selected bridges will be tested using various non-destructive testing techniques to determine bridges’ quality. Furthermore, the test data will be used to formulate a bridge rating system which will facilitate various national authorities towards the sustainable asset management and will also serve as a benchmark for the future development of similar systems.

data.projectName: value addition and shelf life extension of Sweet Potato
data.projectDigest: Sweet potato is one of the starchy root vegetables that grown on warm temperate and tropical regions of globe but unfortunately in Pakistan it is being ignored since decades instead of its high nutritional profile. Although it is cultivated in Punjab and Sindh on limited scale due to its low market demand because most of the people are unaware about the nutritional health benefits of the sweet potato. It is rich source of beta-Carotene which is precursor of vitamin A.  It also contains an appreciable amount of Vitamin C, Vitamin K, Zinc, Potassium and Selenium. Its antioxidant activity and total phenolic contents are also high. A large amount of polyphenols like gallic acid, catechin, caffeic acid, quercitrin, elleagic acid and rutin are present in considerable amounts.  The shelf life of sweet potato at room temperature is about to 2 weeks and no value-added products of sweet potato are available in our local market. Keeping in view the present scenario of food security and dietary pattern diversity the present study is designed to escalate the shelf life of sweet potato by applying controlled atmosphere conditions in combination with pretreatments and production of value-added products by utilizing sweet potato in different recipes

data.projectName: Application of Neuroscientific techniques in Business
data.projectDigest:
This project aims to establish neurobusiness lab and conduct neuromarketing and neuroleadership studies in the organizational and market context of Pakistan. Research in these fields has focused on developed economy contexts with little research in under developed or developing contexts. Henceforth, the project will introduce the fields of neuromarketing and neuroleadership to the Pakistani academia and industry. Secondly, it will add a developing economy perspective to the literature in these fields . The project aims to apply Electroencephalograph (EEG) based neuroimaging technique and eye tracking based bio-metric approach to study cognitive functioning of both leaders, employees and consumers within the business environment of Pakistan. The project will have experiments based on four phases. Experimental design created for marketing and business environment context, signal processing of neurological and biometric data, statistical processing of psychometric research and biological data, psychoanalytical qualitative techniques and finally big data operations. We within the project have designed a team who are experts in the aforementioned phases. 
The ultimate beneficiaries of the project are academia and researchers. In addition, non-profit organizations, social entrepreneurs, small and medium enterprises and socially-conscious big organizations and businesses would be the beneficiary of this project through collaboration.

data.projectName: Development of novel reactive dyes for cotton with enhanced dyeability
data.projectDigest: The backbone of pakistan’s economy is textile industry which is mostly cotton oriented. The processing of cotton based fabric particularly their dyeing with reactive dyes produces huge environmental impact due to the consumption of huge clean water, energy,  salts, dyes and alkali, and generation of effluent. The effluent of textile dyeing industry contains unfixed dyes, salts, alkalis etc. These agents contaminate clean water streams thus affecting aquatic life. The contaminated water is used for irrigation of crops, vegetables and fruits which cause reduction in their yield. The present project is aimed at synthesis and application of such dyes which require very low quantity of water, less energy, less requirement of salts, ultimatley produce very low qunatity of textile effluent. In this way, we can conserve water, energy and environment.

data.projectName: Development of laccase mediator system (LMS) for the detoxification of multiple mycotoxins posing severe health hazards: An innovative strategy
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest:
Mycotoxins are fungal secondary metabolites, contaminate food or feedstuff and poses a serious health threat to both humans and livestock population. Fungi including Aspergillus, Penicillium and Fusarium grow on variety of livestock feedstuffs due to inadequate conditions of harvesting, storage, handling and processing. The most commonly observed mycotoxins that cause a concern to human health and livestock include aflatoxins (AFB1, AFB2, AFG1, AFG2), ochratoxin A (OTA), fumonisins (FB1, FB2), zearalenone (ZEA) and deoxynivalenol (DON) etc. 
	At present, different strategies have been adopted to detoxify feedstuff contaminated with mycotoxins include physical (irradiation, adsorption and toxin-binders) and chemical methods (acid and base treatment etc.). These methods have many shortcoming e.g. reduction in nutritional value and palatability of the foodstuffs. The irreversible detoxification of mycotoxins through catabolizing enzymes and their coding genes is a safe strategy to decontaminate food and feedstuff and can be applied to address the issues of global trade, sustainability and maintaining the nutritional value and palatability of feedstuff. In Pakistan the environment is favorable for aflatoxicosis and ochratoxicosis in commercial poultry. The consumption of mycotoxins contaminated feed adversely affects the performance of livestock/poultry including decrease in productivity, and weight gain. The feedstuff contained mycotoxins are destroyed often with heavy economic losses. The current project has been proposed to develop laccase mediator system (LMS) for the detoxification of multiple mycotoxins posing severe health hazards.

data.projectName: Gender Roles and Hegemony of Pakhtun Culture on Performance of Male Academics in KP Universities: Intervention Model for Promotion of Gender Equality
data.piUniversity: Kohat University of Science and Technology, Kohat
data.projectDigest:
The proponent's (P.I) PhD explores the cultural context of Pakistan and theorises how social constructs regulate gendering in human relationships. The study concludes the power of religious interpretation which identifies women as representatives of family honour restricts their social interactions on one hand but on the other hand it subjects men into the position of more responsibility. In joint family system, domestic life and the home are considered natural and essential domains for women, which consequently make men responsible to live a public life where they have to earn for the whole family to live (Crettelli 2010). The researcher's PhD also suggests that a series of inequalities stems from the culture of patriarchy which places men in leadership positions in both the domestic and public life, as head of the family in the former, and in managerial roles in the latter. This leads to men taking up culturally configured positions which mean they enjoy power, but which also bring more responsibilities both in private and public spheres (Moghadam 1992). The question therefore arises as to whether men are subjected to hegemonic influences stemming from the Pakhtun culture, and whether they are aware of the impact of their gender role on their wellbeing and performance in organisations. The researcher identify this issue as a potential area for research, and aim to carry out a further project to investigate in this related research question. 
Moreover from the popular activist base (universities) this project is proposed to execute four-step intervention model for promoting equality to embrace the notion of gender studies as a source of improving the human condition.

data.projectName: Evaluation of cytokines/chemokines dynamics and virological factors associated with Direct-acting antivirals in chronic HCV patients
data.projectDigest:
Hepatitis C virus (HCV) is a single strand RNA virus that resides and replicates in the liver. The virus is smart enough and has evolved various approaches to evade immune responses thus establish chronic infection and progresses into cirrhosis, liver cancer, and even liver failure. The signals (both immunological and genetic) of severe liver complications are little understood and can be a better predictor of treatment in case of HCV infection. Various cytokines/chemokines and their genetic variations are responsible for giving direction to combating cells (WBCs) against the pathogen and are associated with liver injury. The new direct-acting antiviral therapy claims with pan-genotypic complete eradication of the virus but various reports from different parts of the world presented resistance. There is a need of indicators/biomarkers which may predict the treatment response and disease progression. The cytokines and their genetic polymorphism along with HCV RNA quantification are considered to be good treatment and advance liver disease predictors. 
This study will evaluate various cytokines/chemokines level and HCV RNA quantity in serum of Hep-C patients (infected by various HCV genotypes) under treatment and genetic polymorphisms in cytokines genes to assess their role as treatment biomarkers.

data.projectName: Newborn Jaundice Detection using Smart Phones
data.projectDigest: Jaundice is visible sign of an underlying disease process and is common in newborns. Jaundice is the yellow staining of the skin caused by high blood levels bile pigment known as bilirubin. Early detection of jaundice is necessary to prevent health issues especially brain damage. It is estimated that around 84 percent of newborns develop jaundice. Bilirubin is an orange-yellow stain that normally occur when red blood cell break down. The bilirubin levels usually high after babies are discharged from the clinic or hospital. Clinical technology is unavailable for visual assessment and observing of jaundice at home. Recently used state of the art techniques need specialized tools and clinical tests with blood samples. As newborns often depend on visual assessments of their skin colors at homes, that is unreliable. This study proposed a low-cost automated system named BabyJan to detect and assess newborn jaundice in an efficient and reliable way. This system will use coloring balancing and machine learning techniques to detect and assess jaundice in newborns.

data.projectName: Toxico-pathological evaluation of selected poisonous plants of Muzaffarabad Division Azad Kashmir
data.projectDigest: Muzaffarabad division in the State of Azad Jammu and Kashmir is a place of very rich source all kind of plants wealth. The toxic plants of this region have great potential to produce toxicity during grazing and result in high economic loses in livestock industry. These poisonous plants directly or indirectly effect the large number of animals belonging to local people, nomads and tribal communities. The taxine alkaloid, for example, is a poisonous compound from yews (Taxus spp.). The economic impact of these toxic plants is difficult to quantify, as both direct and indirect losses must be incorporated. Animal poisoning by plants often results from management errors forage conditions, and depends upon the type of animal rather than just the presence of toxic plants. There may be a difference in toxicity levels between different varieties of plants growing in different climates or soils. Poisonous plants interfering reproductive efficiency is the most important economic factor in livestock production. Toxic materials can affect reproductive success by causing abortions, interfering with libido, estrus, oogenesis, or spermatogenesis, causing emaciation and subsequent abnormal mating behavior, birth defects, and increasing the time between parturition and rebreeding. To date, no investigation has been made on the poisonous plants and their effects on livestock in selected region of Azad Kashmir. The present investigation is aimed to develop a science-based guideline for grazing livestock, reduce the risks of livestock losses through improvisation in feed and food safety by analyzing animal tissues and develop improved procedures and guidelines for diagnostic and prognostic evaluation to reduce negative impacts of poisonous plants on livestock reproduction and performance.

data.projectName: Fuel added to Fire: The Energy Crises of Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
The corporate sector of Pakistan has encountered the severe financial distress starting from the year 2006. The main reasons behind this distress include the poor economic conditions, terrorism, energy crises (both electricity shortage and high oil prices), and lack of Foreign Direct Investment because of peace conditions etc. Despite being unaffected by Global Financial Crises (2008), this period has been proved critical for the Pakistani corporate sector and result in numbers of bankruptcy and incorporation of financial distress in all sectors of economy. One of the main behind this distress is the energy crises i.e. electricity shortage which affect all the industrial sector especially the textile sector. The massive blackout of power alone has impact on all the sectors of economy and is the underlying reason for the economic disruption. According to an estimation, for every 1% GDP growth rate in Pakistan, an increase of 1.25 % in electricity production is required. But the electricity supply remained extremely low and this persistent shortage has severely affected the national economy. The purpose of this project is to investigates the relationship and impact of energy crises in the form of electricity shortage to the corporate sector of Pakistan. 

.

data.projectName: Prevalence of Extended Spectrum Beta Lactamase (ESBL) producing E. coli in Wild Animals in captivity and antimicrobial efficacy evaluation of ideginous medicinal plants against ESBL E. coli
data.projectDigest: Extended spectrum b-lactamases (ESBL) are the main source of acquired antibiotic resistance in Gram-negative bacteria. ESBLs capabale to hydrolyse the b-lactam antibiotics by exhibiting homology with penicillin-binding proteins for oxyimino compounds and increase the affinity of enzyme by altering its configuration at the active site while simultaneously weakening overall enzyme efficiency. They confer resistance to cephalosporin, penicillin, oxyimino-b-lactams, cefotaxime, aztreonam and ceftazidime. ESBL prevalence in wild animals from Pakistan has never been studied. The main goal of my study is to identify ESBL Escherichia coli (E. coli) and its molecular characterization in animals of zoo, wildlife parks and National parks of Punjab, Pakistan. Faecal/Recto-anal mucosal Swab (RAMS) will be taken for sample collection and inoculates will be cultured to MacConkey agar. For conformation of E. coli, biochemical tests will be performed and for ESBL E. coli detection, execution of DDST and DDDT will be done. Emphasis will be given to the identification of ESBL E. coli as its understanding is important to eradicate ESBL producing resistance. The plants reported having antimicrobial efficacy i.e., Chamomilla recutita, Achillea millefolium , Salvia officinalis, Thymus vulgaris, Pinus sylvestris, Mentha  piperita, Valeriana officinalis, Foeniculum vulgare, Moringa oliefera, Tamarindus indica, Citrullus colocynthis, Momordica charantia, Rosmarinus officinalis, Thymus vulgaris, Ocimum basilicum, Melissa officinalis, Salvia officinalis, Achillea millefolium, Syzygium aromaticum, Punica granatum, Syzygium cumini, Psidium guajava, Citrus peel, Allium sativum, Azadirachta indica, Murraya paniculata, Cinnamomum tamala, Zingiber officinale, Hibiscus rosa-sinensis, Hypericum perforatum

data.projectName: Development of locally characterized Recombinant Thermostable Enzymatic Mixture for Poultry Feed Industry of Pakistan
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Poultry sector in Pakistan is an important industry committed to provide quality meat to the population. The major component for the high cost of poultry is feed. The feed contributes about 60-70% of total cost of poultry. Animal or plant based feeds can be developed. Animal based feeds are expensive while plant based feeds are economic and various agriculture byproducts or wastes are being utilized for the preparation of feed. These feeds have some anti-nutritional factors or some components those are not being utilized by the mon-gastric animals (broiler chicks) due to lack of enzymes and thus results in low nutritive value. The supplementation of exogenous enzymes increases the availability of nutrients by improving the digestibility of feed components in gastrointestinal tract. Potentially enzymes such as phytase, cellulase, xylanase, protease and amylase are being used in poultry feed from last several years for enhancement of growth of birds. These enzymes are responsible to convert the anti-nutritional/complex/ non-absorbable components of feed to simple/absorbable/monomeric units which can be utilized by the poultry bird for the enhancement of bird growth. 
Current project is being designed to produce recombinant thermostable phytase, cellulase, xylanase and amylase by recombinant DNA Technology, to develop recombinant enzymatic mixture at domestic level and to evaluate the efficacy of the locally developed enzymatic mixture in poultry birds. The production of enzymatic mixture at domestic level will be a step for the fulfilment of industrial demand of Pakistan and to reduce huge foreign exchange for the import of these enzymes.

data.projectName: Synthesis, Characterization and Evaluation of Advanced Stationary Phases in Liquid Chromatography
data.piUniversity: University of Malakand, Chakdara, Dir, Malakand
data.projectDigest: Separation science is an interdisciplinary area of research which makes use of Chemistry, Engineering and material Science. The development of new stationary phases having small particle size, large pore size with induced monolithic architecture along with sophisticate packing protocol will take the liquid chromatography to the next stage of super improved analysis with much enhanced chromatographic performance. The development of effective stationary phases and improvement in the column technology in Reverse Phase liquid chromatography is very important for the accurate and precise analysis of the complex mixtures in different fields such as natural, pharmaceutical, bioanalytical and clinical sciences. Out of a list of stationary phases the partially porous silica monolith particles impregnated with polystyrene co-polymer film of diverse composition is an important division of stationary phases which finds numerous applications in different fields, as mentioned above. The stationary phases comprising of the polystyrene modified partially porous silica monolith particles can be used both in the conventional and multimode liquid chromatography (MMC). Current project will focus on; 1. The development of new stationary phases, 2. Improvement in column technology with respect to packing protocol, 3. Characterization of the newly synthesized stationary phases, 4. The evaluation of packed columns in the homemade HPLC system and 5. Demonstration of real sample analysis. While developing new stationary phases we will synthesize small size silica particles in sub-1µm range with increased pore size of about 400 Å, modification of those particles with polystyrene copolymer layer. Improvement in the column technology will be tried by developing effective packing protocol.

data.projectName: Development of metallic nano materials for gas/chemical sensing applications
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: Nanotechnology is a field of science which has evolved during the last three decades, nowadays comprises many different fields and starts to play an important role as key technology in application and business.  The development of ever more powerful electronics depends on continued progress in miniaturizing their components. Cu oxide NWs, like the other nanoparticles, not only could increase the electrochemical activity but also are relatively inexpensive and have a good biocompatibility. Moreover they are chemically more stable respect to metallic copper and so they are suitable for various application including electrochemical hydrogen peroxide sensors. For example, the detection of H2O2 is of great importance in food and environmental monitoring, diagnosis, and biological studies. Conventional techniques for hydrogen peroxide determination such as fluorimetry, chemiluminescence, fluorescence, and spectrophotometry are complex, costly and time consuming. Metal nanowires are one of the most attractive materials because of their unique properties that may lead to a variety of applications. Metal nanowires are emerging as important active materials for applications such as chemical/gas sensors. Their one dimensional geometry serves them as potential candidate for sensing applications. This research work aims to explore their possible applications for sensing of various gases and chemicals.

data.projectDigest: Currently, at least 10 new coal fired power plants in Pakistan are being installed having design capacity of 6,898 MW which will generate 5.2 million ton of fly ash each year. Therefore, the proposed R&D endeavor of this project will not only offer a solution to the bigger upcoming environmental threat but also provide an indigenous supply of a vital product i.e. zeolites.

data.projectName: Unraveling the molecular details of dual COX-2/5-LOX inhibitors in the clinical management of inflammation
data.projectDigest: Chronic inflammation is associated with the pathogenesis of arthritis, autoimmune disorders, neurological problems, cardiovascular diseases and cancer. Major inflammatory mediators, prostaglandins and leukotrienes, arose from cyclooxygenase (COX-2) and lipoxygenase (5-LOX) enzymes pathways, respectively. Majority of traditional marketed medicines are non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) that are able to inhibit cyclooxygenase enzyme non-selectively (COX-1 and COX-2 both) and displayed severe gastrointestinal toxicity. Selective COX-2 inhibitors “Coxibs” are gastrointestinal safe but produce undesirable cardiovascular events and eventually withdrawn from the market. Hence, the development of a clinically useful NSAID with favorable efficacy and devoid of side effects is a continuing endeavor. Dual COX-2/5-LOX inhibitors (simultaneous blocking the formation of prostaglandins and leukotrienes) provide a logical approach to offer better therapeutic efficacy in chronic inflammatory states with high ulcer tolerability. Hence, the designing of dual COX-2/5-LOX inhibitors are the ultimate choice for safer anti-inflammatory clinicals. The main objective of this project is the realistic use of smart computational drug designing tools to discover the molecular details that helps for the clinical availability of dual COX-2/5-LOX inhibitors as safer NSAIDs. To achieve specific aims, molecular docking, 3D-QSAR, in-silico ADMET evaluation, pharmacophore model generation followed by virtual screening and long MD-simulations will be employed.

data.projectName: Impact of climate change on quality of vegetables
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan Chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.) is cultivated in arid and semiarid zone where the variations in precipitation and temperature affect the crop yield and quality. Due to change in climatic and environmental factors the composition and amount of the phytochemicals in plant species can be affected. Therefore a thorough understanding of the environmental factors will be fruitful in emerging approaches to increase the production and preservation of standard substances in chickpea and enhancing the bioavailability and bio accessibility of these phytochemicals to improve the human health. In this context, the proposed project will be the first effort to elaborate the influence of environmental conditions on the production, quality and antioxidant properties of chickpea based on a precise and innovative metabolomics approach, which is used to obtain the individual chemical profiles and to compare them with environmental data along with molecular profiling. Samples will be collected from all the four provinces where it is cultivated. The collected samples will be analyzed for total phenolic contents, total flavonoids, total proteins, total carbohydrates, antioxidant activity and genetic makeup. Based on analysis the variety with best nutritious value and temperature resistance will be selected and introduced to breeder.

data.projectName: Rational design of high-energy density vanadium based spinel oxides hierarchical nanomaterials for supercapacitor green technology devices
data.projectDigest: As scaled-down consumer products appear on the horizon, there is a great need for energy storage in compact environments. Due to globalization, industrialization and increase in population the use of hi-tech portable electronic devices such as cell phones, personal digital assistants (PDA) and laptops has been increased abundantly making these gadgets an integral part of daily life. These changing paradigms are swiftly exhausting traditional energy resources causing problems of environment pollution. These recent trends have trickled up the need for green and alternative renewable energy storage systems. Recently various substitutes are proposed as alternative of oil and fossil fuels such as lithium ion batteries, supercapacitors, hydrogen storage materials and so forth. Supercapacitors are regarded as promising storage devices for use in portable devices, industrial power management, energy backups, electric vehicles and so on. They proffer higher power densities with shorter charging time, longer operating life cycles and better safety tolerance than batteries. The proposed research, for the first time, enable the use of novel hierarchical nanostructures of vanadium based transition metal oxides to economically fabrication of next generation of supercapacitors.

data.projectName: Machine Learning Based Optimization of Many-Body Quantum Mechanical Dynamics
data.piUniversity: Kohat University of Science and Technology, Kohat
data.projectDigest:
Quantum computers are devices that can perform powerful computations at the exponentially higher speeds as compared to their classical counterparts. Once realized in their full capacity they will bring change in the current scenarios of business and even world economy by solving problems that seem impossible today. Gartner has predicted that 20 % of organizations will be investing in quantum computers by the end of 2023.  

Quantum gates are essential elements of quantum computers, high-performance quantum gates are necessary tools for working quantum computers.

On the other hand, coherent quantum control plays a key role in all sorts of present and future quantum technologies including quantum gates. It is still a formidable challenge to accurately and efficiently gain quantum control.  At present, there are many different theories and techniques which try to do the task but none of them are satisfactory. 

Machine learning has gained big attention in recent years and got applications in almost every field. Methods based on machine learning proven to be very useful especially in solving many-body problems in quantum mechanics. 
In this project we propose, a novel method based on machine learning to achieve quantum control for implementing quantum gates to active high fidelity.

data.projectName: Comparative study for effect of synthetic and biofungicides on growth, metabolism, phytochemical profile and transcriptome of sunflower (Helianthus annuus L.) under Alternaria blight stress
data.piUniversity: Lahore College for Women University, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
The fungal attack on crops results in yield losses up to 20% worldwide. Application of synthetic fungicides is a routine procedure to combat these fungal infections. However, extensive use of these fungicides causes serious damages in plants including growth retardation, disturbance in carbon and/or nitrogen metabolism, disorders in reproductive organs, alteration in photosynthesis, changes in pigment levels like chlorophyll and carotenoids etc. Besides, these synthetic fungicides are also carcinogenic to man and many fungal strains are also developing resistance against them.
Plant derived antifungal agents termed biofungicides are proving to be safer than that of synthetic fungicides as they show toxicity against the target species only, are relatively less toxic, biodegradable and are cost effective. The trend of using plant derived fungicides by Asian and African farmers has been found. In Asian region, China is the leading user of biopesticides. Korea registered total 33 biopesticides, out of which, 19 are fungicides. In case of Pakistan, officially no biopesticide has been registered or used commercially. The proposed research is planned to target plant-derived fungicides and explore their effects on physiology and genome of targeted plant infected with fungal pathogens. The results of biofungicides will be compared with synthetic fungicides.

data.projectName: Removal of toxic heavy metals by bioaccumulation from wastewater using microorganisms
data.projectDigest: Microorganisms are known to play important role in the environmental processing and recycling of different elements. they are involved in decomposition and removal of different toxic chemicals and contaminants.  With the increased industrialization and use of different xenobiotics (man made synthesized chemicals), different kinds of contaminants are accumulating in soil, water and air. Those released toxic contaminants get their way to enter in food chain. The proposed project is about to check the level of heavy metals in wastewater and to isolate the different heavy metal tolerant bacteria and fungi. The isolated microorganisms will be applied on lab scale to remove heavy metals from wastewater and accumulate inside the cell. The proposed study will help to minimize the concentration of heavy metals in wastewater and ultimately control the concentration of metals in vegetables irrigated by wastewater.

data.projectName: Delineating Genes Underlying Inherited Epilepsy Syndromes through Next-Generation Genomic Tools
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
The term “Syndrome” refers to collection of signs and symptoms that are observed in, and characteristic of, a single condition. Geneticists try to identify the underlying cause of an inherited syndrome in different ways, e.g., either they observe the way of its transmission from one generation to another or study its frequency among relatives. Epilepsy is a group of neurological diseases characterized by epileptic seizures which are episodes that can vary from brief and nearly undetectable to long periods of vigorous shaking. Epilepsy specialists use a variety of factors to classify epilepsy syndromes. 
Purpose of initiating this project is to find out the genetic causes of rare epilepsy syndromes in Pakistani families with the help of unambiguous clinical phenotype. Next generation genomic tool  will be used to identify mutations in these families. 
Pakistani population provides an ideal environment for the study of rare genetic disorders including inherited epilepsy syndromes due to early and consanguineous marriages and large family size .  Previously, our research group have also published many related articles on families with epilepsy as one of the clinical finding. 
An important reason for studying the pattern of inheritance of rare epilepsy syndromes within families is to enable advice to be given to members of a family regarding the likelihood of their developing it or passing it onto their children i-e genetic counseling. This will certainly help in enhancement of our understanding regarding the etiology of these syndromes and would stimulate further studies for research on targeted therapies, genetic counseling and management of these ailments.

data.projectName: Probing the Renewable Technology Adoption Challenges in Small and Medium Industry of Pakistan: An Empirical Investigation for Multivariate Sectorial Analysis
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan is facing severe challenges of energy crises from the last one and half decade due to increasing population and industry with decreasing hydel energy resources. This situation has drastically affected the residential, industrial and commercial sector of the country. Under these circumstances, the research has been become essential to explore of renewable energy sources in the country to fulfill the deficit scenario of the country. This study explores the key barriers and drivers that are in?uencing the adoption of solar technologies on the one hand, and to examine various strategies to overcome these barriers on the other. 
A positivist methodology will be used and data will be collected from operational managers and experts from three different industry of Sialkot. Descriptive and inferential statistical techniques will be applied to analyze the data.
Our findings provide information to policy makers and government to launching a comprehensive program for R&D, commercialization and awareness of the community by incentivizing for the wide scale adaption of solar energy technologies in future. The project also discusses the policy implications of the barriers and drivers identi?ed, and outlines several challenges for future research.

data.projectName: Deep Vision based Intelligent Cloudlet Farming Consultant using Drone Technology: DroneFarming
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan is one of the world’s largest producers of farm products such as Chickpea, Cotton, Wheat, Rice, Sugarcane. However, it still lacks in output as per its potential.
 According to PARC, 83.33% of cotton varieties found high severity disease. Farmers do not have timely and accurate information about all the crop diseases. Agriculturists only know the common weeds so if field suffer from different weeds they remain unaware about it and its remedy due to lack of agricultural education. Thus, there is a bigger need of a virtual consultant, automatic, cost effective and accurate system for timely detection of weeds and maintenance of environmental factors. 
The proposed system targets to frequently visit fields with help of drones, which as an edge communicates to the cloud for the transmission of relevant information not only to the farmers but also to the monitoring authorities like departments of agriculture, health and environment. The system performs a detailed analysis of weeds, environmental parameters and their origins to predict the fertilizer for the assistance of farmers and stakeholders. The system helps in the yield improvement of food crops to align with the vision 2030 of Pakistan for climate change and food.

data.projectName: Development of Halal Uni & Bi functional Bioactive Scaffolds for Advanced Skeletal Defect Repair
data.projectDigest: The need for bone repair & regeneration arises due to disease, trauma, birth defects or aesthetic reasons. Traditional approaches involve use of bone harvested from the same patient (increases morbidity and discomfort). Bone or its derivatives from cadaveric, bovine or porcine sources are also used. This raises ethical and religious questions. Synthetic bone grafts are hence a viable option. Related materials need to be imported into Pakistan as expensive imports. Using polymers with bioactive ceramics (as spongy porous scaffolds) eases handling for the surgeon and ensures better defect filling. This may also require a retention membrane. This project focuses on synthesizing bioactive ceramics using a novel flow synthesis system. It also focuses on extraction of collagen from halal sources. Collagen will be used with bioceramics to develop spongy porous scaffolds. Use of hydroxyapatite will facilitate bone regeneration whereas addition of metal oxides will ensure angiogensis making the materials bifunctional. Collagen will also be used to develop a retention membrane. Materials developed will be characterized intensively. Biocompatibility will also be assessed using in-vitro and in-vivo (animal) models. This project brings together a team of scientists, an orthopaedic surgeon, a dentist and a pharmaceutical company to develop an affordable bone regenerative solution.

data.projectName: Molecular Identification and Characterization of Emerging Variant Strains of Avian Infectious Bronchitis in Sindh
data.projectDigest: Avian infectious bronchitis (IB) is an acute upper respiratory tract viral disease of chicken caused by avian infectious bronchitis virus (IBV) and is one of the major viral disease reported in flocks of layers and broilers in Pakistan. The IB virus is acquired following inhalation or direct contact with contaminated poultry, litter, equipment. Young chickens are more high risk to IBV infection. Many serotypes cause drops in egg production accompanied by reduced shell quality and albumen quality. Loss of shell color in brown egg layers is a very common effect of IBV. That’s why after broiler, IB is also an economically significant problem for the commercial egg industry. Although live attenuated vaccines and inactivated vaccines are universally used in the control of IBV. Several variant serotypes continue to evolve and cause disease episodes. data.projectName: Discovery of new Pharmaceutical molecules and DNA damage repair investigation of Boerhavia diffusa
data.projectDigest: The main objective of the present project is to isolate biologically active secondary metabolites from the selected plant species of through solvent separation and chromatographic techniques. The structures of pure isolated compounds will be elucidated using advanced spectroscopic technique such as 1H-NMR, 13C -NMR, HMQC, HMBC, COSY, NOESY, EI-MS and single x-rays analysis where required. The sub-fractions and identified pure phytochemicals will be subjected to in vitro and in vivo biological assays such as ant-bacterial, anti-fungal, cytotoxic, phytotoxic, antioxidant, analgesic, sedative, anti-diarrheal and leishmanicidal, inhibitory activities. The active compounds will be further subjected to molecular docking analysis to identify the active sites of the molecules. The obtained active chemical constituents may prove potential candidates for further development as new drugs. The results will be published in high impact factor international journals. The extracts and it isolated compounds will also be subjected to DNA damage repair study.

data.projectName: Screening and Characterization of Novel Antimicrobial and Antibiofilm Compounds from Indigenous Plants of Potohar Region
data.projectDigest:
Microorganisms have developed many defensive strategies like antibiotic resistance patterns and the formation of complex communities of cells known as biofilms. Biofilms are the cause of contamination and serious infections leading to fatalities. With the advent of increased evolutionary resistance, the need to explore novel anti-microbial and anti-biofilm compounds have become foreseeable. In Pakistan, plants are the primary source for food, shelter and herbal medicines. To expand the spectrum of anti-microbial and anti-biofilm agents from natural resources, indigenous plants of the Potohar region are selected based on their traditional ethnobotanical uses. Highly resistant biofilms are largely unexplored. To the best of our knowledge, there is a gap in research on the anti-biofilm activity of plants of Potohar region. The project aims to screen and characterize the anti-microbial and anti-biofilm potential of indigenous plants and to provide an effective solution to the biofilm-associated infections. 
Lab facilities at UW have the potential to serve the requirements of this project. Besides, we have collected clinical and food-based strains that may use in this project for further investigations. Project aims are the isolation and characterization of novel anti-microbial and anti-biofilm phytochemicals, Biofilm structural analysis and pilot - scale preparation of anti-biofilm spray.
