data.projectName: user Controlled Hearing Aid Technology (uCHAT)
data.projectDigest:
As per the WHO reports millions of the world population is suffering from hearing loss, associated with poor quality of life. Modern hearing aid devices are either expensive and beyond the budget of most of the users or of limited use in the presence of noise. It is important to exploit recent technological development to address this problem by developing a low cost and user controllable hearing aid that can give better results in the presence of noise. This project will work towards developing a disruptive new class of assistive hearing device addressing the problem of cost, user friendliness and improved speech intelligibility in the presence of noise.
The current project will develop a reprogrammable hearing aid device (using the BioAid algorithm) for simulating innovative and competitive hearing aid strategies reducing burden not only on the users but also on the health system. This project offers the possibility of founding a new research topic that is normally ignored in our society. We also expect that publications and the conference papers arising from the project will have a positive impact on the community of academic scholars and beyond.

data.projectDigest:
Globally, incidence of more than half a million human cases of brucellosis on annual basis has brought attention of international healthcare community. Currently the diseases is one of major public health concern for much of the world. Globally, 500,000 cases are reported yearly and currently 2.4 billion people are at risk worldwide.  The disease is prevalent in 10/100,000 in endemic areas. In Pakistan, the disease is endemic but according to World Health Animal Information Database, 2011, there is no proper data and reporting system from Pakistan. In last five years, most of study has been conducted in Punjab province and to some extent from Sindh province but no proper data has been collected from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Baluchistan provinces. This data will help Pakistan to estimate total loss due to brucellosis in both livestock and public sector. In India, the annual total loss due to brucellosis in livestock sector is US $ 3.4 billion. data.projectName: Mathematical Analysis and Behavior of Some Non-Linear Discrete Dynamical Systems
data.projectDigest:
The dynamical characteristics of population systems have been modeled, among others by differential equations in the case of species with overlapping generations and by difference equations in the case of species with non-overlapping generations. In practice, one can formulate a discrete model directly from experiments and observations. Sometimes, for numerical purposes one wants to propose a finite difference scheme to numerically solved a given differential equation model, especially when the differential equation cannot be solved explicitly. For a given differential equation a difference equation approximation would be most acceptable if the solution of the difference equation is the same as the differential equation at the discrete points. As the dynamics of infectious diseases in a population is highly nonlinear in nature and it is better to investigate it through reliable mathematical modeling techniques. 
Throughout human history, infectious diseases have caused premature death to large portions of the human population, leading to serious social-economic concerns. Many factors have contributed to the persistence and increase in the occurrence of infectious diseases (demographic factors, political, social and economic changes, environmental change, public health care and infrastructure,microbial adaptation, etc.).Infectious diseases are still causing suffering and mortality in developing countries. Malaria, yellow fever, AIDS, Dengue and other names will have marked the memory of humanity for-ever. Mathematical modeling has contributed significantly to our understanding of the epidemiology of infectious diseases  and is beginning to have a substantial impact on research at the immunological and molecular levels.

data.projectName: Metformin and glimepiride blended nano medicine adsorbed on Syzigium cumini based silver nanopmedicines for the treatment of Diabetes Mellitus Type-2.
data.piUniversity: University of Kotli Azad Jammu and Kashmir
data.projectDigest:
Diabetes Mellitus (DM) is the one of the major causes of morbidity and mortality around the world. Non-traumatic amputations, blindness and renal failure are the conditions related with diabetes. According to International Diabetic Federation (IDF) report 2015, 415 million people around the globe suffers from DM which is expected to cross 642 million by 2040. Across the world Diabetes was responsible for about 5.0 million deaths in 2015. Pakistan has been ranked 7th in terms of diabetes prevalence rate in adults. The present scenario of Diabetes type-2 (DMT2) prevalence in Pakistan is about 11.77% (Male: 11.20 % and Female: 9.19 %). DMT2 is prevalent throughout Pakistan. The mean prevalence is Sindh is 11.70 % (females) and 16 % (males); In Punjab 10 % in females and 12 % in males. In Baluchistan 13.3 % among males and 9 % in females; while in KPK it is 10 % in males and 12 % in females. Overall the existence of DMT2 in urban areas is 14.81 % and 10.34 % in rural areas.
In this research work we plan to prepare potent, better bioavailable and less toxic mutually blended nano medicine of metformin, glimepiride and Syzigium cumini for the treatment of DMT2.

data.projectName: ISOLATION OF MICRO FAUNA FROM THE SALIVA OF FRUGIVOROUS BATS
data.piUniversity: Women University of Azad Jammu and Kashmir Bagh
data.projectDigest: Bats are natural reservoir and sources of several pathogenic microorganisms, many of which are causative agent of severe human diseases (Veikkolainen et al., 2014). Because of close contact between bats, animals and human beings, there is possibility for interspecies disease transmissions and subsequent disease outbreaks (Vashi et al., 2010). The purpose of this study is to isolate microbial fauna from saliva of bats that may have the potential to cause diseases in human being. Since the bats are frugivorous, during eating they contaminate the fruits of human interest. When these are used up by human being they become infected with these microbes and their spores. As the saliva contain many pathogens that has not been studied so for in Pakistan, so saliva will be explored for the isolation and identification of potential pathogens of public health. Number of infectious diseases has been observed in locations where human being and bats are living in close proximity (Lagadec et al., 2012). In proposed study area, Azad Kashmir, variety of fruit plants are present. Bats are not only decreasing economic value, also vector of many diseases. Exploratory visits will be made to find out roosts in the area. Potential sites are old and large sized tree and forest, Bat sound detector will also be used for finding the roost. Once traced, the global position of each will be noted by using Garmin etrax H GPS. Mist nets will be erected at the strategic positions for maximum flux. The saliva of each  bat will be taken by using a sterile cotton swab, gently placing inside mouth and slowly circled then dipped into trypticase soya or peptone broth (3ml) and will be transported at 40C for laboratory processing, samples, Molecular identification will be done through (16S) rDNA sequencing

data.projectName: Revitalizing orphan crop: sorghum for food,fodder and bio-ethanol production under climate change scenario
data.projectDigest: Sorghum is a fourth important cereal (fodder) Crop in Pakistan. This is cultivated in irrigated and semi-arid dry areas for grains, feed and fodder. Its bio-ethanol production attribute is unknown locally. This orphan crop was grown on 242 thousand hectares achieving yield of 149 metric tons during 2018-19 with a production decline of 2.3 percent. Current national activities are limited to evaluation and varietal development. 600 accessions and elite cultivars’ collections is lying unexploited at the national gene bank. Considering scenario, the proposed project will regain sorghum as a potential crop with capacity to produce yield, grains, feed, fodder and bio-ethanol. After seed multiplication and selection, 80-120 lines/accessions will be planted at multilocations for morphological, grain yield, fodder and bio-ethanol production studies. The proposed potential areas include Tandojam, Kachho(Sindh), Sargodha (Punjab) and NARC, Islamabad. Evaluation will narrow down the germplasm pool adapted to potential areas. Genomics will identify the genomic regions for above traits using Genotyping-by-Sequencing (GBS). The genomic studies will help to introgress and select haplotypes using marker-assisted selection for future breeding. The superior lines will be shared with breeding programmes for breeding, will be deposited in gene bank and utilized as candidate lines for further genetic studies.

data.projectName: SKILLED BASED EDUCATION AS A PROMISING INDICATOR OF KNOWLEDGE-BASED ECONOMY
data.projectDigest: Researchers are engaged in teaching and research activities for the last around ten years at various university level and observed that university graduates pass their masters/hons (16-year education) without equipping themselves with the 21 century skills to name a few like communication, presentation, academic and problem solving needed at job. This deficiency not only hinders the employability of prospective job candidates, it also makes them professionally weak that in turn results in slow progression of their carrier. This highlights there is a gap of skill-based education that prospective workers need to know and equip with a range of skills. This growing need is inevitable to address because of the rapid advancement in technology, globalization and changing work place contexts because of various other factors such as diversity. Therefore, it is much needed that prospective job applicants (university graduates) should be equipped with 2 st century skills that is demand of the local and global market that in turn put professionals on ‘driver seat’ of their career. Researcher’s conceptual schema  presents the way forward that will be followed in this project to map-out skill-based education that later could be used in HEIs to develop human resource into human capital in order to contribute in knowledge-based economy.

data.projectName: Genetic manipulation of lignin reduces recalcitrance to improve biofuel production from Agave sisalana to combat with environmental issues.
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan is among the countries who are facing energy scarcity severely which is a key factor for the development of a country. Pakistan mostly dependent on fossil fuels to fulfill its all requirement. For this purpose most of the fuel is imported from abroad that is so much costly for a under developed country. The consumption of fossil fuels result in decline in resources along with increase in Co2 in environment ultimately result in Global warming. Consequently the rapidly increasing global warming adversely affecting the climate including shortage of water. To combat this situation it is need of the time that some environment friendly fuels should be produced from plants that require less water for their propagation. 
Genus Agave sisalana is ideal source of biomass production and considered important as bioenergy crop that require less water for its propagation and also absorb carbon dioxide from environment because of its crassulacean acid metabolism (CAM). The key feature of the CAM photosynthetic pathway used by Agave sisalana is the opening of stomata and CO2 uptake during the night, thus allowing less water to be lost by transpiration. In genus Agave sisalana, lignocellulosic biomass is made up of the complex structures of cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin.  Cellulose and hemicelluloses can be hydrolyzed to simple sugars for further fermentation to produce liquid biofuels. The resistance of cell walls to breakdown to sugars is called recalcitrance. data.projectName: Unearthing of salivary bio-markers in patients pf lung cancer
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Cancer has been a significant cause of mortality and morbidity both in developing and developed nations worldwide. Early identification of cancer with reliable diagnostic accuracy has still been one of the mainstay challenges of an oncologist clinic. Moreover, the routine lab work carried out for assessing cancer progression is equally discomforting for the patient as the disease itself.  Among various cancers, lung cancer ranks as one of the entities with bad prognosis. Tackling such entities requires early diagnosis and aggressive follow up to save patient from falling in death trap. This requires application of noninvasive diagnostic methods for cancer diagnosis. With the advancement of new diagnostic bio-markers among various body fluids and tissues, salivary biomarkers can be an attractive option to pursue. The research on salivary biomarkers in various cancers is still in infancy; however, promising results have been reported from Hao-wei chu et al. (30)  in case of salivary biomarkers in oral cancers and Lei Zhang et. al. (19) reported in breast cancers. On the precedence of reported findings, biological plausibility exists for salivary biomarker identification in more aggressively behaving cancers like lung cancer. As lung cancer is also one of the top ranked cancers with high incidence rate from Pakistan as per GLOBOCAN report from 2018, this further emphasizes the need for identification of salivary biomarkers and for a noninvasive approach for diagnosis. The proposed work will not only identify biomarkers in saliva but will also quantitatively compare and validate the potentially identified biomarkers with serum levels and in healthy controls.  Furthermore, the intended work may create opportunities for Pakistani biotech market for new detection options.

data.projectName: Extrusion processing under alkaline conditions as a preventive tool to mitigate mycotoxins in corn-based breakfast cereals
data.projectDigest: Fungi have been considered as a major food contaminar throughout the world. Mycotoxin contamination cause serious deteriorative consequences on liver, kidney and brain. In-vivo studies have proved them as potent cause of cancers in animal’s researches. Cereals are mostly affected by the mycotoxins and among them corn is heavily contaminated by the mold. Moreover, the climatic condition of Pakistan supports the proliferation of mold as it need hot and humid conditions for its growth. The climate remains hot in Pakistan, where high temperature (30-48 °C), and relative humidity ranging from 25% to 50% during summer. During harvesting, handling, storage, and distribution, agricultural commodities are subjected to infection by toxigenic molds, which may cause spoilage and produce toxic metabolites called mycotoxins. Infant and breakfast cereals are mostly consumed by the vulnerable group of population i.e. children who have lower body weight, higher metabolic rate and reduced ability to detoxify toxins as compared to the adults. Extrusion being harsh processing method owing to its high temperature, pressure and mechanical shear can be utilized as managing tool for the destruction of these toxins. Optimize extrusion processing conditions may resulted in the production of safe and quality infant and breakfast cereals in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Mathematical Foundations of Chemical Kinetics and the Theory of Chemical Measurements
data.projectDigest:
The proposed work involves both the physicochemical conceptual assumptions (used for species behavior and their model reduction) and a set of mathematical tools (for their dynamical behavior and simplification). The tasks are related to the theoretical and mathematical computations to understand the properties of complex chemical reactions and describe the behavior of molecular and condensed matter. This work comprises handlings of data as well as resources (material), for this purpose, we will apply our recently developed methods.
Typically, the linear invariants will be determined based on the three key matrices of the chemical kinetics, i.e. molecular, Horiuti and stoichiometric matrices. Recently there was rigorously shown that all three matrices can be implemented into one universal matrix, so-called C-matrix.   
To solve the multi-route complex reaction mechanism, we have initiated this idea with the help of modern model reduction techniques (MRT) along with all new strategies. Now we are at the stage where we can address the multi-surface of the reaction mechanism along with their comparisons with overall reactions mechanism. We will construct and analyze such ‘mechanistic’ invariants for more complex mechanisms which include nonlinear (bimolecular) reactions and different routes as well. The goals mentioned will be achieved for mathematical models of complex catalytic reactions of complete and partial oxidation. We will also apply some refinement techniques to get the invariants for stiff problems.

data.projectName: Transcriptomics and metagenomics profiling of dairy cows in response to mastitis in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Mastitis is one of the top diseases of dairy cows in Pakistan. It influences milk production and animal performance by affecting the mammary quarters. It usually arises when pathogenic microbes enter the body through mammary glands during dry period or early lactation. In the current study, we plan to investigate the role of mastitis in dairy cows by using transcriptomic and metagenomic techniques. Our main objectives are to explore the role of differentially expressed genes and their related biological pathways using transcriptomics and to explore the local microbiota and their characterization using metagenomics. The sampling will be conducted using blood and milk samples for transcriptomic and metagenomic studies respectively and in each part, 12 samples will be taken (6 control and 6 affected). The data from these samples will be extracted using next generation RNA sequencing and 16S metagenomic profiling techniques. Further, RNA sequencing and metagenomics data analysis pipelines will be employed for the data mining. The results will be further analyzed using computational resources for biological pathways, gene ontology (GO) terms, gene regulatory networks, bacterial species identification, and functional characterization. These results will provide us deep insight into the mastitis causing bacterial pathogens, and overall biology of the animal.

data.projectName: Exploitation of natural products and ergastic substances as an alternative strategy to extend shelf life of horticulture products
data.projectDigest: Fruits are very sensitive and highly perishable, extension of shelf life and quality maintenance is highly challenging in Pakistan. Fruits start spoiling after detachment. Another aspect is transport of fruits, a substantial quantity of horticultural product is lost during handling, storing and in transportation. Postharvest treatments and packaging materials are utilized to enhance shelf life of fruits and maintain quality. Postharvest treatments are chemical based, these chemicals leave their residues over the surface of fruits that can very harmful for human health. There is a need to introduce ecofriendly methods for extension of shelf life, edible coatings are greatly focused. Edible coatings are actually ecofriendly and have no harmful effect on human health. These are obtained from plants and vary in composition, structure, form and functions. Edible coatings will be applied on fresh horticultural products and sliced fruits to enhance the shelf life and reduce the browning of sliced fruits. These coatings will include chitosan, waxes, plant extracts, essential oils, plant mucilage, gums, sea weeds and chemicals like citric acid, ascorbic acid, salicylic acid, gibberellic acids and combination of nanoparticles. Different packaging materials will be applied to explore beneficial packaging for transportation of fruits.

data.projectName: Microfiber 3D Bio-Models Construction for Ophthalmic Pathophysiology and Drug Development Applications
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan is one of the most polluted country among the top 3 most polluted countries. The international researchers exposed that high polluted area peoples have high risk of glaucoma and other complication of eyes. Cataract is the leading cause of blindness worldwide and also reported in Pakistan for about 50% of blindness. Similarly, another study in Pakistan observed the retinal pigment epithelial detachment was observed in 45.3% cases. The retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) is a sheet of cells exist attach to the photoreceptor layer of the neural retina in vertebrate eye, which is highly pigmented cells that fit together in a tight matrix for nourishing of neural retina. This simple layer of RPE play several vital functions in vertebrate eye regulation.  
Unfortunately, the conventional techniques for practicing the commonly ophthalmology problem are based on two-dimensional (2D), while, 2D cell cultures are poor surrogates of complex three-dimensional (3D) natural milieu. Limited ophthalmology tool available for common practicing that provide affordable cost and productive result for analysis of ophthalmic pathophysiology and valuable drug screening. Therefore, our current designed 3D bio-fabricated model would provide a more valued culture systems with an ease and cheap method for RPE and retinal studies in near future.

data.projectName: Folate-Modified Chitosan-5-FU nanoparticles for colon cncer delivery
data.projectDigest: Colon cancer is the 3rd most common cancer and major cause of death throughout the world. The major cause of colon cancer is high intake of sucrose and spicy food. alterations in the bowl habit is one of the most common complaint. In Pakistan incidence of Colon cancer is increasing day by day.  The standard treatment for colon cancer is surgery and chemotherapy. Most commonly used drugs include 5-fluorouracil and leucovorin. The main drawback of the drugs is their non-specificity which results in toxicity.  One of the approach is to formulate targeted nanoparticles which will be more specific in action and will reduce the unwanted side effects. For this we will formulate folate modified chitosan-5-fluorouracil nanoparticles for colon cancer delivery. folic acid is well know targeting ligand, and it will guides the nanoparticles towards cancer cells.

data.projectName: Production of Iron nano supplement for enhanced poultry production during stress
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan, there is a recent trend of establishing commercial environmentally controlled houses for rearing poultry. However, the housed poultry have little access to dietary Iron (Fe). Day old chicks are solely dependent on feed for their Fe intake. The deficiency of Fe may predispose day old chicks to iron deficiency. This can cause hypoxia, anemia and stress due to poor housing. The daily Fe supplements have reduced bio-availability and do not effectively relieve the problem. Fe is an important micro-nutrient for poultry feed, where it is mixed in premixes in the form of inorganic salts and used as a supplement in infectious diseases like chicken infectious anemia. An excess of iron, however, can reduce the absorption of other nutrients like calcium, phosphorous, manganese and zinc. Present iron preparations have low absorption, negative interactions with other feed components as well as high cost. There is therefore a need to investigate new forms of Fe. Nanotechnology is a promising technology that can reduce iron particles to few nano-meters, thereby increasing bio-availability. The production of iron oxide nano-particles can help in improving the current deficits in diet of poultry, keeping in mind its cost effectiveness.

data.projectName: Gram production under water deficit conditions of Dera Ghazi Khan
data.projectDigest:
Different screening techniques will be used for evaluating the gram genotypes for drought tolerance. These techniques will be seed germination at -0.6 MPa external water potential (PEG-6000), seedling growth rate after 14 days at -0.6 MPa external water potential (PEG-6000), cell membrane stability of leaf discs taken 6 weeks old plant and plant water relations of 6 weeks old plant. Tested gram genotypes will be categorized in two groups’ viz., drought tolerant and drought sensitive.   
Each genotype will be compare by application of full irrigation and skipping irrigation at flowering. Drought stress treatment will be imposed at flowering stage by skipping the irrigation 50 days after sowing (DAS). Control plants (irrigated) will be given three irrigations (at 25, 50 and 65 DAS) from the date of sowing to maturity. Drought stressed plants received only two irrigations (25 and 65 DAS). Observations will be taken on normal and stressed plants at 40 and 75 days after sowing.

data.projectName: Investigation of antihyperglycemic mechanisms of Catechins from green tea: Development of dietary approaches for the treatment of diabetes mellitus
data.projectDigest: Diabetes mellitus is a metabolic disorder which is manly characterized by high blood glucose level and insulin resistance. Presently nutritional therapy and neutraceuticals are gaining more attention due to their safety profile and nutritional value for the treatment of several chronic diseases.  Green tea is most commonly consumed beverage worldwide and it is rich in catechins which are strong antioxidants.  In present project we aimed to extract catechins from green tea using UV-Visible spectrophotometric analysis. High performance liquid chromatographic method will be used to determine the concentration of different catechins. The antidiabetic potential of green tea catechins will be determined by conducting In-vivo trial via biochemical, histopathological, immunocytochemical, gene expression (Insulin signaling pathway, Calcium signaling pathway, JNK pathway), insulin receptor sensitivity, glucose uptake by skeletal muscles (translocation of glucose transporter 4 (GLUT4)) analysis. The above mentioned clinical and molecular investigations of green tea catechins will explore the development of dietary source based therapeutic regimens for the treatment of diabetes mellitus.

data.projectName: Analyzing the anti-viral and regenerative potential of IL-6 and IL-22 in ameliorating HCV infection
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Hepatitis C virus (HCV) has created a huge burden worldwide with 185 million people suffering from hepatitis C infection, among which 80% are residing in low income and underdeveloped countries. These chronic infections result in great stress on the community both economically and socially. In a low-income country, like Pakistan, the standard care of antiviral regimes, including interferon and direct acting antiviral therapies, resulted in enormous burden on government budget as well as community and have their own limitations. Latest antivirals present in market have very promising results, but still they are unable to undo liver damage and have no role in assisting hepatocyte regeneration. New treatment options must be explored to overcome the limitations and ensure better survival of HCV patients. 
Present study aims to investigate protective and regenerative effect of IL-6 and IL-22 on HCV infected hepatocytes. The study would be performed in in vitro setting for duration of two year. 
IL-6 and IL-22 may have a promising role in reducing viral titer as well as protection and regeneration of healthy naive hepatocytes via STAT3 mediated pathway. Comparative analysis of HCV infected liver cell line and biopsies/explanted liver tissues of chronic HCV patients undergo liver transplantation will be performed with or without cytokine treatment. Apoptosis and liver regeneration shall be determined via Annexin staining, Tunnel assay and immunostaining for cell proliferation markers in order to check the toxicity of the cytokines as drugs if any along with its regenerative property.

data.projectName: Genome wide association analysis of local sorghum (Sorghum bicolor L. Moench) cultivars/landraces for important agronomic traits under stress conditions.
data.piUniversity: Kohat University of Science and Technology, Kohat
data.projectDigest: The proposed project takes into account a thorough assessment of sorghum (Sorghum bicolor L. Moench) under drought and salinity stress. As drought and salinity tolerance are complex phenomenon and involve morphological, biochemical and physiological alterations in sorghum therefore, to well elucidate these traits will be a greater contribution in crop improvement programmes. Traditionally, the evaluation of genetic populations derived from bi-parental crosses were used for the identification of genetic loci linked with important agronomic traits. However, in this approach there are certain limitations, because of less genomic resolution and limited allelic diversity as only allelic segregates among the parents of the recombinant progenies can be tested. Genome-wide association analysis is now more widely used technique for the identification of genomic regions associated with traits of interest. This approach overcome the major deficiencies of bi-parental populations and becoming a more valuable method in trait identification. Due to the ideal genome size and the capability of sorghum to tolerate adverse conditions, make it an ideal crop for genome wide association mapping. Several studies have been reported the use of GWAS (genome wide association mapping) to mapped genetic loci with important traits in sorghum but there is still a huge gap remain in mapping of the genetic loci correlated with important traits in sorghum under stress conditions.

Several studies have been reported the use of GWAS (genome wide association mapping) to mapped genetic loci with important traits in sorghum but there is still a huge gap remain in mapping of the genetic loci correlated with important traits in sorghum under stress conditions.

data.projectName: Detailed Investigations on Use of Sustainable Supplementary Cementitious Materials in Concrete and other Construction Products: A Multiscale Approach
data.projectDigest:
A lot of research work has been done on concrete using the supplementary cementitious materials(SCMs). In Pakistan, the researchers have explored the possible use of supplementary cementitious materials, however, the application of that research in different construction sectors of Pakistan is minimal. The reason being, incomplete findings, lack of detailed investigations at different levels of concrete and potential fear of stakeholders in using these materials as partial or total replacement of cement. The question is, still after decades, why these materials have not been used by the construction industries of Pakistan.
This motivate us to find the existing gap and revisit use of sustainable supplementary cementitious materials not only in concrete but open few new horizons to use it in other constructional products and extend its application further. In addition, detailed investigation starting from smaller level(matrix phase) to larger level(Concrete/Construction product), elaborated as multiscale investigation,  will be the part of this project.
This research work is multiphase that includes development of concrete, composites and other constructional products using multiple techniques and by involving different SCMs,  then comes the detailed investigation of the developed products at multiscale level, and at last application of the results will be studied at larger level.

data.projectName: Investigation of somaclonal variation in Cotton (Gossypium hirsutum)
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest: Cotton is found recalcitrant towards somatic embryogenesis due to its complex genome and genotype dependency. Somatic embryogenesis is the routine procedure that is being adopted in the modern cotton improvement methods including genome editing and genetic transformation methods. However, somatic embryogenesis is only restricted to some model cultivars, due to their responsive behavior towards tissue culture. Due to such limitations, there are no cell lines developed in cotton till now. However, somaclonal variations may cause both epigenetic and genetic variations during tissue culture. Such variations may cause undesirable results in the genotypes . Moreover, there is no mechanized system to investigate the  degree of variations develop during tissue culture procedure, therefore, it is of immense need to develop a stable and efficient  to understand and control the somaclonal variations.  This project aims at to develop the genetically stable cotton cell lines and also the methods that may identify and mitigate the somaclonal variations.

data.projectName: To Explore the Pharmacogenetic Predictors of Blood Pressure Response to Antihypertensive Medications
data.projectDigest: Blood pressure (BP) responses to antihypertensive medication varies widely among individuals and are difficult to predict. The rise in hypertension (HTN) prevalence and fall in its control rates make it a very challenging phenotype to study globally. In Pakistan attention need to predict individual blood pressure responses to antihypertensive medications to improve optimization of its therapy. Many genetics and laboratory predictors of BP responses have been suggested to antihypertensive medications.  We will describe here to conduct an up to date overview of the HTN and to find possible genetic and laboratory predictors. Initially, we will recruit 2000 individuals from various approved facilities to determine the prevalence trend and will extract a subset of the most relevant individuals for further analyses (200-300) on exploring the genetic and laboratory predictors to both BP and BP response to antihypertensive medications. We will develop a genetic risk score based on our previous findings which will provide a more precise estimates of an individual variations to HTN medications. We ultimately aimed to set up a pharmacogenomic resources on HTN in Pakistan to collaborate in future with International Consortium of Antihypertensive Pharmacogenomics Study, with a goal to improve optimization of HTN therapy. This proposal will add substantial understanding of the laboratory and genetic determinants of the lacking BP responses variability in our population.

data.projectName: Molecular detection of citrus greening disease in district Sargodha and integrated management of its vector Asian citrus psyllid, Diaphorina citri
data.projectDigest: Citrus is the major fruit crop of Pakistan and serve as a key source of foreign exchange. Citrus industry and growers are facing many threats in the form of insect pests and diseases. An estimated 15-20% loss in citrus is attributed towards insect pests. This loss is increased when insect pests serve as a vector of several devastating citrus diseases like citrus canker and citrus greening, thus contributing to additional losses in citrus production. Citrus psylla, Diaphorina citri Kuwayama (Hemiptera: Liviidae) also known as Asian citrus psyllid (ACP), is a key citrus insect pest and serve as a vector of the citrus greening known as Huanglongbing (HLB) significantly reduces the citrus yield. Molecular techniques will be used for HLB and its vector, ACP. The adults of ACP have the ability of strong dispersal hence a potential establishment of this insect in our citrus. So, there is a need for extensive management efforts to mitigate the threat of this vector-pathogen complex. We will use some organic products alone and in combination to check their effectiveness. Biological control agents will be collected and their effectiveness will be evaluated against ACP using alone and in combination with bio-products.

data.projectName: Potential source and reservoir rock assessment in the Permian-Triassic successions in frontier parts of Baluchistan, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The Permian and Triassic of Pakistan pose promising rock units for petroleum exploration. Globally, these rocks represent humongous oil, and gas bearing strata and the Permian alone contributes >30% share in the hydrocarbon productivity. The contribution from the Triassic is >2%. So they jointly contribute to 32% hydrocarbon generation of the world. In Pakistan, there is little interest seen from the oil and gas companies in the past, partly because they had been drilling to the rock units younger than the Permian and Triassic, which would save them cost of drilling and partly because their geological occurrences covered the frontier areas of Baluchistan, which makes the availability of data very fragmentary. However, with the growing depletion from the younger strata, an interest has been developed to target the deep lying reservoirs, which makes this research highly valid and in time. The present research will focus on determining hydrocarbon generation potential of Permian and Triassic successions of Baluchistan, using source, reservoirs rock studies and facies analysis. The source and reservoir rock assessment will provide a base-line database for compiling the potential of these successions to generate hydrocarbons, to provide essential data for new hydrocarbon exploration in these frontier parts of Baluchistan.

data.projectName: RF Front-End Using EM Lens Assisted Massive MIMO Technology for Next Generation (5G) Wireless Systems and the Internet-of-Things
data.piUniversity: Karachi Institute of Economics & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The groundbreaking technologies i.e., massive multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) proposed for the next-generation 5G wireless systems and the internet-of-things (IoT) are expected to revolutionize the ways of communication and connectivity among people with enhanced performance and reliability. However, the massive MIMO technique based radio frequency (RF) Front-End at a base station requires massive number of hardware (RF chains) and increases computational complexity in processing the large volumes of data signals which appears a hurdle in developing, deploying, and operating them to serve the people at affordable cost particularly in low-and-middle income countries like Pakistan. Therefore, the vision of the project is to enable a paradigm shift in RF Front-End design for next-generation 5G wireless systems and IoT. In this project, we, in a consortium of two academia and one industry partners, propose a novel, low-cost and complexity simplified RF Front-End, based on electromagnetic (EM) lens assisted massive MIMO technique. The realization of the above vision is centered on demonstrating RF Front-End platform through proof of concept of EM lens assisted Massive MIMO enabled RF Front-End, development of the EM lens assisted Massive MIMO enabled RF Front-End prototype at 5G mid-band, performing radio localization, and investigation of fully digital and/or mixed analog-digital architectures.

data.projectName: Machine Learning based quantification of ejection fraction by automated cardiovascular MRI
data.projectDigest: Cardiovascular disease increases globally and is a major cause for fatality. World Health Organization figures and statistics reveals that the death rate due to cardiovascular disease is 31%. Despite the seriousness of heart diseases, minimal attention is given to diagnose the cardiovascular diseases in Pakistan. Therefore, a considerable effort is required to early diagnose the cardiovascular related diseases. EF is the remarkable measure to evaluate the health of the heart. EF is calculated by the amount of blood pumped out from the lower chamber (LV) of the heart during each heartbeat. The project is focusing on developing the novel hybrid approach; combining automated segmentation of the myocardium region and machine learning methods to precisely estimate the EF of the heart. The proposed solution will provide an opportunity for comprehensive analysis of EF by automatically contouring the systolic and diastolic boundary of the lower chamber from all the cardiac phases of MR data. The project will make the immense influence on the healthcare sector by early diagnosing the cardiovascular diseases and providing the optimized and cost-effective solution. Furthermore, researchers will have an opportunity to participate and collaborate in the groundbreaking research by producing high quality publications.

data.projectName: Academic Integrity and the Peril of Plagiarism: A multi-university experimental study
data.piUniversity: National University of Modern Languages, Islamabad (NUML)
data.projectDigest: The project proposal  is an applied research project that aims at investigating and improving the quality of academic integrity at the higher educational institutions (HEIs) of Pakistan. Through this project we intend to understand the perceptions and attitudes of graduate students and researchers toward academic integrity and train them to successfully avoid plagiarism in their scholarly work. The study will assess the impact of the intervention (workshops) by employing a pretest-posttest design. It is multi-university experimental study, involving ten public sector universities that offer various research degrees (MS/M.Phil/Ph.D) in social sciences. The study will be employing an experimental design with pretest/posttest method to measure the success of the project and gauge its sustainability in the future. This approach opens another path of innovation, offering the possibility to design and develop a professional workshop on the academic integrity. The workshop manual/instructional material will be used across the country to improve graduate students’ perceptions and attitudes toward academic integrity. This will not only improve the quality of scholarly work done in Pakistan but will also help in getting acknowledged internationally in the high impact research journals. The relationship of process/product in the form of skill service with the participants will enable the rise in academic marketability of Pakistani education. The study will collaborate with the Higher Education Commission (HEC) and will have ten different universities from all provinces of Pakistan.

data.projectName: On certain new trends in inequalities on real line and complex plane
data.piUniversity: Abbottabad University of Science & Technology (AUST), Abbottabad
data.projectDigest:
Integral inequalities is an elegant part of analysis and provide many tools to apply in other branches of Mathematics. Integral inequalities that involves bounds on physical objects are of special interest not only for mathematics but also in Physics, Decision making theory and information technology and biology.

This project will focus on certain new developments in the field of integral inequalities. The integral inequalities such as Hermite-Hamdard type and Ostrowski type will be the main point of investigations. Several researcher currently set new trends in this area and obtained very useful and fruitful results which found many connections in other fields such as probability theory, Information Sciences, Numerical Integration and Operator theory.
In this project we will study certain new trends of  inequalities on real line as well as complex plane.  

 
These inequalities and their variant forms will be investigated throughout the project by using the concepts of fuzzy integrals, fractional calculus, q-calculus and stochastic convex processes.

data.projectName: Combining Urdu Accent Classification with Identification of Regional Languages of Pakistan for Forensic Speaker Recognition from Short Utterances
data.piUniversity: National University of Modern Languages, Islamabad (NUML)
data.projectDigest: The project investigates Urdu Accent Classification (AC) and identification of regional languages of Pakistan from short utterances for forensic Speaker recognition. Accent Classification (AC) and Language Identification (LI) are based on state of the art Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques, known as Deep Learning.  AC and LI play a vital role in the identification of people of different communities and origins due to their different speaking styles and native languages. AC and LI are important in the context of Pakistan as people speak multiple languages along with the national language of Pakistan i.e, Urdu. Currently, the forensic experts manually analyze audio recordings to get information about AC and LI to limit the search space for suspect (speaker) recognition to regional and ethnic group(s). In the proposed project this process will be investigated and automated by using a new method(s) based on state of the art Deep Learning Methods in order to assist forensic experts in making decisions about suspect (speaker) recognition and identification.

data.projectName: ANTICANCER EFFECT OF GLYCYRRHIZIN AGAINST BREAST CANCER IN COMPARISON WITH TAMOXIFEN
data.projectDigest:
Breast cancer is the most common malignancy prevailing among female population worldwide. It is the leading cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality that has exhausted resources all over the world for its screening, diagnosis, staging and management. Diagnosis of breast cancer is done by triple assessment i.e. history and clinical assessment, tissue biopsy and radiological testing that includes breast ultrasound and mammography. 
Breast cancer management includes chemotherapy, surgery, radiation and targeted therapy i.e. endocrine therapy. Though many advancements have been done in all aspects of breast cancer, the increasing disease burden demands development of newer treatment options. Natural sources have been widely explored for extraction of active principles that can be used effectively for their activity against various diseases. Glycyrrhizin is one of the many active principle extracted from Glycyrrhiza glabra (liquorice root). It has been studied extensively for its anti-inflammatory, anti- viral as well as anti -proliferative properties. In this study we will check role of glycyrrhizin as a preventive and curative agent against breast cancer and this can lead to a milestone in the development of new anticancer agent against breast cancer.

data.projectName: Design of Long Acting Tenofovir Alafenamide-Fatty Acid Conjugates and Evaluation of their Enhanced Anti-HIV and Other Anti-viral Activities
data.projectDigest: During the last three decades, HIV response have been pioneering and had a global impact. 75 million people have been infected with the HIV and about 32 million people have died of HIV. Globally, 37.9 million people were living with HIV at the end of 2018. Pakistan is one of the countries in the WHO Eastern Mediterranean Region where new HIV infections are increasing at an alarming level since 1987. In 2019 there was a major outbreak of the HIV infection in the children of district Larkana. There are medicines to treat HIV infection unfortunately the virus get mutate, and develop drug-resistance. A part from this there are multiple side effects of current medicines being used for the treatment of HIV infections which includes lipodystrophy, diarrhea, high cholesterol, fatigue and etc. Current project envisaged the designing of Tenofovir (TFV)-fatty acid derivatives which posses sustained long-acting effect and lymphatic delivery and thus have enhanced therapeutic profile. This combination may result in the development of anti-HIV prodrugs having enhanced efficacy, longer action through the sustained intracellular release of active substrates and higher uptake into infected cells. Released TFV and myristic acid analogs act as reverse transcriptase inhibitors (RTIs) and viral NMT inhibitors.

data.projectName: Preparation and application of Bio-fertilizer to enhance growth, yield and drought tolerance of plants
data.piUniversity: University of Malakand, Chakdara, Dir, Malakand
data.projectDigest: Microbes can be harmful as well beneficial, however most of the bacteria related to plants are beneficial. These beneficial bacteria are generally called plant growth promoting bacteria because they produce various substance which help plants to enhance its growth and yield. While some other bacteria have also been proven for their role in enhancing biotic and abiotic stress tolerance in plants. These bacteria will be isolated from the legume plants (generally their roots and rhizosphere are rich in plant growth promoting bacteria) and tested in the lab for their plant growth promotion and drought tolerance characters. After selection of plant growth promoting bacteria, these bacteria will be tested on plants to inoculate them with the plants if they are enhancing plant growth and drought tolerance. Those bacteria will be used as bio-fertilizers that enhanced plant growth and drought tolerance of plants. The lab tested bio-fertilizers will be further tested in large quantity in the field if they are actually working in the field. Finally, those bacteria will be released as bio-fertilizer that enhance plant growth and drought tolerance of plant.

data.projectName: Nanocellulose Fiber Based Highly Porous and Efficient Photoelectrodes for Low cost and large area Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells (DSSCs)
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest:
Energy and environment as among the highest 10 problems which human being are facing form fifty years. Indeed, world’s energy consumption is rising year by year, about fifty percent increase in energy consumption is expected by 2050. Energy deficiency has become an international issue hindering community development.
To overcome this problem, significant progress has been made in the development of renewable energy technologies e.g. wind, solar, hydropower, etc. Among them, solar energy is the most promising being abundant and totally free.The conversion of solar energy to electricity is fulfilled by solar cell devices, which can be divided into three types: (i) silicon solar cells (ii) thin film solar cells (iii) dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs). The manufacturing process of silicon solar cell is difficult and materials used in thin film solar cells are costly and toxic.  Whereas, DSSCs are low-cost, more efficient and flexible. However, large area DSSCs modules lack in performance compared to their laboratory scale devices and also suffers from long term stability and electrolyte leakage issues. In this project, we will resolve these two big issues of DSSCs with the help of ligno-cellulose based nanocomposite-photoanodes. After fabricating DSSCs, we will resolve the current energy crisis in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Synthesis and characterization of iron and boron modified clay based geopolymer cement from local clay and its applications
data.projectDigest:
Cement manufacturing process suffer from a number of problems in which production of greenhouse gases and consumption of high amount of fuel are the two most important. The first one deals with environmental while the second one is economic issue as the price of cement is increasing on monthly basis. Both these issues are closely related to one another. Production of one ton of cement produces one ton of carbon dioxide which mainly come from the combustion of fuel.  Moreover, corrosion and chloride penetration are the main problems of cement mortar and concrete, upon which the durability of cement products depends, must be addressed by the researchers of cement. To overcome all these problems including corrosion and chloride attack, different alternatives are being made. 
Geopolymer is the best alternative of Portland cement for some applications, being the highly resistant to corrosion, chloride penetration, producing very low amount of greenhouse gas as there is no calcination and requires comparatively less fuel as no clinkerization is involved. 
The present geopolymer face a big problem as it requires highly pure kaolinite clay free from impurities like iron etc as it lower the compressive strength of geopolymer. So if iron and boron are incorporated in the main skeleton of geopolymer replacing some of aluminum, the problem of selected clay for geopolymerization will be solved. Moreover Iron and boron modified geopolymer are expected to exhibit good cementing and adsorption properties as compared to ordinary geopolymer. Furthermore the production of geopolymer may reduce the consumption of fuel and production of greenhouse gases upto 30%, hence the cement production will become more sustainable and environment friendly.

data.projectName: Study of rare decays of pseudo-scalar mesons within 331 model.
data.projectDigest:
Standard Model(SM) is a coherent framework that enables us to study particle’s interactions involving strong and electroweak interactions. It does not incorporate neutrino oscillation and is also unable to account for the quantum of gravitation. It is also unable to explain the replication of three lepton-quark families. Yet, the discovery of Higgs boson has confirmed one of the predictions of electroweak SM. 
The 331 Model is an extension of SM that incorporates three families of lepton and quarks, explains the stability Higgs mass. 
The aim of this project is to study 331 model in pure leptonic and semi-leptonic decays of pseudo-scalar mesons i.e. (K, B and D). Current measurements on branching fraction confirm with the predictions made by SM within experimental errors. For this purpose an error analysis of the experimental observables like decay rate and forward backward asymmetry, e.t.c w.r.t the parameters of 331 model will be performed within experimental errors.

data.projectName: Economic empowerment and livelihood  sustainability of both male and female faculty, students and graduates of "MADAARIS" in Khyber Pukhtunkhwa : An entrepreneurial capacity building perspective.
data.projectDigest:
In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa the religious leaders are given high value. Generally the “Ulema and Tuleba” are meant to serve religion, belong to financially poor backgrounds or experience extreme poverty and livelihood issues. They lack personal and environmental motivation other than serving in a Masjid or MADRAASA on very low wage rates, doesn't even cover their and their families’ basic needs. The integrity and societal status quo also acts as a psychological barrier in addressing this stagnancy. Consequently, they lack a proper entrepreneurial mind set and even are  far from learning skills. So they hold them selves back from being more productive, creating value for both spiritual and physical human needs and have negligible share in GDP, HDI and per capita income. There passiveness massively effects other segments of society because of their influential status.
•	This project at first intends to develop a robust curriculum through a joint research collaboration between university faculty and religious scholars of the region. 
•	Secondly such training modules will be imparted to both male and female faculty,students, and graduates of madaaris in 34 districts of KP. 
•	Finally this tested course material will be recommended to be incorporated in the scheme of studies of Wifaq ul Mdaaris Al Arabia.

data.projectName: Study of Biochemical and Genetic Architecture of consanguineous SLI families from Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Specific language impairment (SLI) is a multifactorial neurodevelopmental disorder that delays the mastery of language in children who have no hearing loss nor other behavioral disorders like autism. Individuals with SLI may have life-long issues with academics and problems in relationships with their peers. The SLI disorder is common, with a prevalence of 7% and has high heritability (>50%) estimates. The etiology of SLI is not fully defined, but research that has been conducted during last few years provides strong evidence which support polygenic genetic basis of SLI. Previous studies have identified several loci, SLI1-SLI5 and different variants in genes associated with it. Recently, our researches group determined six loci by linkage analysis and homozygosity mapping in Pakistani PKSLI families. Although, efforts have identified several important genetic loci in SLI, but these explain small fraction of this disorder. There is an acute need to expand the characterization of SLI and genetic studies to consanguineous population. Funding is required to collect the further families having SLI and normalized the clinical tests including PPVT measures, SLAS, TAAPU along with digit-span measures of working memory for Pakistani population to give the affection status of individuals in Pakistani population.

data.projectName: BIODEGRADATION OF INDIGO DYE FROM SEGREGATED TEXTILE EFFLUENT USING AN INNOVATIVE MEMBRANE BIOREACTOR AND REUSE OF RECLAIMED WATER
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest: The textile sector of Pakistan is responsible for ecological damage in Pakistan through a discharge of a tremendous volume of wastewater into water bodies, particularly from the dyeing process. It is feasible and cost-effective to treat segregated dye effluent as an individual stream before combined with other waste streams of textile industries. This idea of treatment of segregated dye effluent is particularly feasible for indigo dye effluent, which is generated from denim production (a highly export-oriented product of Pakistan). Conventional treatment systems are not effective in making treated water reusable and require a large area, which is a constraint. This proposal suggests an innovative configuration of membrane bioreactor for the treatment of indigo dye effluent at discharge point within the textile facility to make treated water reuse, reducing overall pollution load to water bodies as well as treatment costs. We have successfully demonstrated the treatment of indigo dye effluent with the removal of dye completely, high organic and nutrient removal, and complete color removal. The treated water was fit for reuse for other textile processing activities. It is necessary to optimize the operating parameters of the membrane bioreactor before applying at the pilot scale within a denim processing mill.

data.projectName: Automation of Sewerage Disposal Station and its Structure by Programmable Logic Controller with Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is the fifth largest country regarding population in the world. Due to the rapid growth of population several problems are incorporating into our system including poor housing quality and affordability, water and sanitation, transportation, health and education. Water and Sanitation is one of the key sectors for the development and operation of the cities. Several problems are existing in the current sewerage structure of the Pakistan sanitation system. One of the major problems is the outdated system of sewerage disposal structure which need to improve. In existing structure of sewerage system, all problems are identified manually which are very slow and time consuming.  In views of these difficulties a Supervisory control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) based system is proposed for fully autonomous operation, saving of city from domestic/industrial waste water, operation branches, proper provision of water supply system, industrial control process improvements and maintenance. This system will provide useful results with full autonomy and positive impacts. In the proposed design, the work includes about the up-gradation of sewage network, its design criteria, and their operation capacity during peak load/off-peak hours, electro-mechanical machinery involvement and human-being interface graphical design.

data.projectName: Authenticity of honey bee products and their assessment as environmental indicator in selected areas of Azad Jammu &Kashmir (AJK)
data.projectDigest:
Title of Project:  Authenticity of honey bee products and their assessment as environmental indicator in selected areas of Azad Jammu &Kashmir (AJK)

Principal Investigator: Dr. Sofia Khalid    Co-PI: Dr. Mehwish Jamil Noor

Main products obtained from honey bees are honey and wax. Azad Jammu & Kashmir has diverse flora that can support honey bees in the farm as well as wild. It is important to determine the quality of honey bee products so that these can be exported. Honey, for example can be unifloral or multifloral. The first part of the project will address the quality issue of honey bee products from AJK. Palynological analysis, nutritional content and physicochemical analyses of locally available honeybee products will be carried out to document information regarding geographical and botanical origin, medicinal properties and authenticity of labeling for export.
Many urban and industrial centers have been developed in Azad Jammu and Kashmir in past many years. Studies have reported that unplanned development has deteriorated the quality of water, air and soil.  Plants being the major contributor to honey production have also been reported to be metal contaminated. The problem needs to be reported because the whole food chain from production to consumption is neither controlled nor regulated. The second part of project will analyze the quality of soil and identified bee pollinating plant species for different pollution monitoring parameters

data.projectName: Establishing the prevalence of Cystic Echinococcosis (CE) in the Punjab province of Pakistan: An Ultrasound based field survey
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan is an agricultural country and livestock is backbone of the country. Livestock having share of 60.54% in agriculture and 11.22% in Gross Domestic Product (GDP). It is the source of 35-40% of income for over 8 million rural families. Livestock diseases are one important factor, which cause economic losses due to their prevalence. These diseases from livestock also transmitted to human population due to their zoonotic mode of transmission. Considering that more than 60% of infectious diseases are zoonotic, they have an important and increasing impact on human health. 
Echinococcosis, is a neglected zoonotic parasitic disease caused by tape-worm of genus Echinococcus (Family:Taeniidae). It is a serious public health problems, which cause the alveolar echinococcosis (AE) and the cystic echinococcosis (CE) respectively. The most widespread and frequent form of this disease is cystic echinococcosis (CE), today most prevalent in resource-poor and developing countries of central Asia. The global human echinococcosis has been estimated to 2-3 million people affected and 200000 new infection annually. Currently,  prevalence of 1–3 million cases of human CE, with a burden of 1–3.6 million disability adjusted life years and over 2 billion US$ costs.
In Pakistan the disease is prevalent in human and not explored yet. The diagnosis of CE is mainly based on imaging, with serology having a mainly confirmatory role. In addition, resource poor settings often lack both the infrastructure for complex serological analysis and clinicians skilled in the use of Ultrasound (US) to make the diagnosis and no data on genotyping from human is available ye. So there is a dire need of research work on this topic.

data.projectName: Identification and Management of antibiotics and antibiotic resistance genes to reduce prevalence in drinking water
data.piUniversity: Balochistan University of Information Technology, Engineering and Management Sciences,Quetta
data.projectDigest: Mortality and morbidity due to bacterial infections is decreasing from the last 60 years due to development in the field of antibiotics. Presently, specific disease causing bacteria can be targeted by antibiotics. Presently, 80 out of 40000 identified antibiotics are in use for bacterial infection treatment (Alanis, 2005; Joshi, 2002). Major portion of antibiotics remain unchanged and enter into the environment in active form through hospital and municipal wastewater (Brown, et al., 2006; Zhang, et al., 2012). The issue of antibiotic resistance was started since first use of antibiotic (Hiramatsu, et al., 2012). Most of water bodies are contaminated with antibiotics due to ineffective treatment (Ma, et al., 2015) and complete removal of antibiotics from wastewater is not possible by using conventional wastewater facilities (Batt, et al., 2006). No data available about level of antibiotic pollution in local water bodies and about level of antibiotic resistance in pathogenic and non-pathogenic strains. So the present study is designed to (i) generate date about level of antibiotics and antibiotic resistance in the city and (ii) to develop cost effective and sustainable procedure/technique to control the antibiotic pollution by biological treatment under local environmental conditions by using local species.

In this project Pathogenic bacterial (Bacterial speck, halo blight, and bleeding canker, Brown rot, bacterial wilt and Black rot) diseases in tomato will be controlled by introduction of Cysteine protease. Tomato is the world’s second most cultivated vegetable. During cultivation or post-harvest storage, it is susceptible pathogenic bacteria. Although wide range of chemical pesticides is currently available to manage plant diseases, continuous application of pesticides not only affects the nutritional contents of tomato but also the texture or productivity of soil. In this way resistance variety of tomato will be developed against the Pathogenic bacterial diseases.

data.projectName: Chromosome engineering of the bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) genome: strategies for genomic restoration and development of climate smart wheat cultivars
data.projectDigest:
There is no simple solution to sustainably feed global population as large as 10 billions. Strong drifts in global climate change have already been recorded, indicative that prospects of further deterioration are inevitable. Sustaining future food security poses a serious challenge in the face of mounting population, climatic instability, emergence of new pathogens. Bread wheat is a major food crop in Pakistan and the importance to increase wheat production is widely acknowledged. With almost no opportunity to expand agriculture on existing land, increasing genetic gains for grain yield and resistance could reduce the number of people at the risk of hunger. 
For wheat genetic restoration is possible by exploiting the wild gene pools that possess valuable traits for yield, quality and tolerance. These genetic resources have been successfully used and desirable genes have been incorporated into the wheat backgrounds. To enhance genetic gains and make agricultural systems climate-resilient, an integrated approach is urgently needed that rapidly introgress favorable alleles from wild relatives into modern wheats. The current project will screen wheat-alien lines displaying resistance to virulent fungal pathogens and abiotic stresses. The results will facilitate pyramiding of novel genes and directed chromosome-engineering efforts to develop agronomically desirable wheat cultivars.

data.projectName: Therapeutic Potential of Selected Medicinal Plants on Peripheral Nerve Regeneration
data.projectDigest: The peripheral nerve injuries are prominent among global problems and result in huge socio-economic burden. Prolong suffering time and long-lasting disabilities in severe nerve injuries worsen the quality of life of affected individuals. The regeneration rate of injured peripheral nerve is extremely slow. Currently, effective treatment strategies and standard Food and Drug Administration approved drugs are lacking to treat peripheral nerve injuries. To this grim situation, preliminary pre-clinical studies points to the beneficial properties of medicinal plants in treating the peripheral nerve injuries and demand further investigations to estimate therapeutic potential on peripheral nerve regeneration. Local medicinal plants such as Moringa oleifera and Azadirachta indica are rich source of bioactive ingredients such as polyphenols, flavonoids and related anti-oxidant ingredients and may augment the recovery process through promoting regeneration rates of injured nerve. Thus, current proposed study is aimed to estimate the therapeutic potential of selected medicinal plants on peripheral nerve regeneration. The probable outcomes of the proposed pre-clinical study would provide foundations for the development of effective strategy to treat peripheral nerve injuries in clinics.

data.projectName: Bifurcation analysis and chaos control in larch budmoth interaction
data.projectDigest: The larch budmoth interaction is one of the population cycles of classical type. Experiments show that density of budmoth changes by approximately fifth order of magnitude, whereas amplitude and period remain remarkably constant. The interaction between budmoth, supply of its food and needles of larch, is a topic of great interest and many researchers are attracted by this field for the last few decades. This population cycle is described as resource-consumer interaction, in which larch needles behave like a source and budmoth is considered as consumer. The high-quality needles of larch trees are badly affected due to outbreaks of budmoth, and in a result low-quality leaves are produced for the next year. Ultimately, the length of needles remains shorter with higher raw quantity of fiber. Feeding on these affected needles gives less larval survival chance and female fertility. Several years can take for the improvement of leaves quality. Mathematical models related to these larch budmoth interaction can produce cycles with great resemblance to observed data.  Larch budmoth is a worm of grey color which became famous for its periodic behavior of outbreaks and infestations on large-scale with larch trees located in Alpine valleys of Europe. For further description related to biology of larch budmoth, their natural enemies, their population cycles, reconstruction of historical cycles, reasons behinds the creation of cycles, negative feedback of needle quality, regulation by natural enemies, fitness of various ecotypes, migration of moth and dispersal, cycles in the nutshell, variation of cycles with respect to climate change, importance of larch budmoth, possible sources of confusion and control measures, the interested readers are referred to  [1].

data.projectName: Development of small scale method to estimate protein polymerization in wheat flour
data.projectDigest: The most important wheat flour product across different parts of the world is bread. Bread-making quality of wheat flour depends on its protein content and composition. A protein content of 13% is considered good for bread-making. Further, gluten protein composition, i.e. monomeric gliadins and polymeric glutenins strongly effect the bread-making quality of wheat flour. The gliadins play important role towards viscosity and extensibility while the polymeric glutenins contribute mainly to the elasticity of dough.High Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC) and spectrophotometric methods are used for analysing the protein polymer distribution and pentosans in wheat flour to assess the bread-making quality. However, the application of these methods in breeding programs is not practical because of several reasons such as high cost, time, special equipment, breeding stage to select initiation, sample size, repeatability and labour requirement etc. Therefore, although these methods are more reliable and classical for determination of bread-making quality, they can only be used at advance stages of breeding program. In contrast, small scale methods that require less time such as SDS sedimentation and solvent retention capacity (SRC) may be the better option for breeders at early stage of selection for bread-making quality. Thus, the present study has been planned to investigate the relationship among SRCs and  protein polymerization of wheat flour and developing a method to quantify protein polymers based on SRC.

data.projectName: CMMI Compliant Workflow Model for the Implementation of Configuration Management Process in Small and Medium Sized Software Development Organizations in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
The software industry has grown exponentially over the past more than three decades. However, developing quality software is still a challenge. Traditionally, efforts to improve software quality have centered on the detection and the correction of defects at the end of product development lifecycle. On the contrary, new approaches for enhancing software quality encompass all phases of a product development lifecycle: from the requirements analysis to the final delivery to the customer. Thus, software organizations are keenly investing to improve their software development processes. To this end, practitioners and researchers have proposed software process improvement (SPI) methodologies, such as, CMMI (Capability Maturity Model Integration), SPS, SPICE, etc. CMMI is a renowned SPI quality assurance standard for evaluating and enhancing an organization’s software development processes, however, no significant number of software setups is making use of it especially in Pakistan.
By default, every organization is at Level 1 of CMMI. In order  to achieve Level 2 an organization have implement few key process areas and configuration management (CM) is one of them. Researcher argues that CMMI does not throw light on how to achieve a particular CMMI process area, i.e., CMMI tells what activities are expected, but does not spell out how to do part of the same. The theme of this project is developing a workflow model that drives the implementation of CM towards achieving CMMI Maturity Level 2 for small and medium sized software organizations in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Application of endophytic plant beneficial microbes to induce tolerance against salinity for Sustainable Agricultural Production.
data.projectDigest: Salinity is the most perilous factors reducing the yield of crop plants and around 50% of land is affected. Similarly, cotton and tomato crops are badly affected by salinity stress through stunt vegetative growth, osmotic stress, ionic imbalance (Na+ and Cl ions), and unavailability of essential nutrients that leads to lower agricultural production. A growing approach to tackle these challenges is to benefit from plant endophytic growth improving bacteria and fungi which have a vital role in alleviation of salinity stress because of their potential capabilities of tolerance to extremities. While the agricultural and biotechnological perspective, the knowledge of endophytes and their capabilities in improving crop yields, resistance toward diseases and survival of crops against abiotic stresses are greatly desirable. The aim of proposed study is to isolates and identifies the potential strains of endophytic fluorescent Pseudomonas and fungi that induce systemic resistance in plants against salinity stress and develop a cost effective method for their field application using cotton and tomato as test crops. The proposed work will also evaluate the exploration of proline, ERFs, and MAPK pathways to understand the molecular mechanisms involved in plant-endophyte interaction responsible for salinity tolerance.

data.projectName: Molecular evaluation of Pyrus genotypes present in northern Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Pears and its wild allies are present in wild as well as in cultivated form in temperate areas of Pakistan. Domesticated plants and their wild relatives are significant for food security of a region and population. Therefore, their identification, documentation and censing of their locations are very significant for agricultural and industrial development of the country. Up till now, only eight species of Pyrus have been identified and published from Pakistan. Besides these achivements, northern Pakistan and Azad Jammu & Kashmir have a great potential for availability of new records and species of Pyrus (Pear). Therefore, in the current research, the study is further extended and elaborated through modern and recently developed molecular techniques such as the use of nuclear and organelles loci for molecular characterization of the genus Pyrus, in which specific nucleotide sequence of the unknown genotypes of  pear are amplified through PCR, the specific fragment of DNA will be sequenced. After successful sequencing of DAN samples, the sequence of each unknown genotype will analyze through a series of bioinformatics software’s. After analysis, different characters such as total number of characters, conserved region, nucleotide variation, parsimony informative and singleton sites will be generated. The final data set of each query genotype will be used for establishment of phylogenetic relationship among the query genotypes and with the reference library species/ varieties/cultivars through Mega 6.0 software. The phylogenetic relationship will be presented in the form of tree, in which the similar and most closely related genotypes are cluster to gather. Moreover, in such a way the query genotypes are investigated/identify with the help of online reference library.

data.projectName: Mitigate the effects of global warming on rice panicle traits through molecular and agronomic approaches
data.projectDigest: Raising of temperature and shifting of precipitation are the result of global warming/climate change. Pakistan is among the top 10 countries where global warming effects are more severe and significant. Crop productivity is being declined under climate change. Rice yield is severely affected in tropical and subtropical regions of the world, in Pakistan too. Panicle traits are the key part of yield components. Panicle traits are severely affected under high temperature, ultimately rice yield is reduced. Therefore, current proposal is focused on three aspects; the genetics of panicle traits under high temperature, the effects of biochar, P and K on restoring the panicle fertility under high temperature, and initiation of awareness campaign among farmers regarding climate change and its effects on crop productivity. Quantitative Trait Loci (QTLs) identified in genetic studies would lead to produce climate change resilient rice varieties, an appropriate combination of biochar, P and K would help to restore the rice yield under the changing environment while awareness campaign enable the farmers to combat with effects of global warming.
