data.projectName: Mathematical modeling and analysis of the environmental impact of CPEC
data.projectDigest: Global warming is one of the dominant environmental issues linked with the worldwide economy and the greenhouse gases (GHGs) effect from emissions of six gases. China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) which contains the economic and development projects can dramatically affect the environment and Pakistan will have to face serious environmental pollution issues if necessary safety measures are not taken for satisfactory environmental protection. Pakistan is already at risk of climate-induced threats. Pakistan is among the 10 most-affected countries point out by the Global Climate Risk Index of 2017, which grades countries based on effects of extreme weather events both in terms of mortalities and economic losses. Pakistan has been in the countries that are facing worst heat waves over the recent couple of years. It has been transmitting carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions over multiple times higher than what it was discharged in 1971. The primal contribution of the present research project is to model and forecast the environmental degradation indicators for Pakistan due to the implementation of the CPEC project. To quantify the marginal impact, various mathematical, statistical, econometric and environmental techniques will be employed. This research will contribute to minimizing negative environmental effects for local citizens to perceive favorable outcomes of the CPEC projects.

data.projectName: Redefining Heat Waves for Better Prevention of Health Hazards in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Lasbela University of Agriculture, Water and Marine Sciences, Lasbela
data.projectDigest: As heat waves over Pakistan have increased due to global warming, heat waves have become deadly in the last few years, resulting in hundreds and thousands of deaths each year especially in eastern densely populated regions. The early warning provided by Pakistan meteorological department is found insufficient to reduce the effect heat waves which is mainly due to poor definition of heat waves adapted in country. The existing definition is not appropriate for all the eco-systems and age groups as it is not sufficient to provide necessary warnings for different age groups or activities. The objective of the proposed research is to redefine heat waves considering different meteorological factors responsible to health hazards during high temperature and categorized heat waves into different severity in order to taking necessary prevention measures. The new definition would help to understand the severity of heat waves more elaborately and propose actions needed for different level of heat waves, such as limited outdoor activities during mild heat waves, school closure during moderate heat waves, etc. The outcomes of the proposed project will help to reduce the mortality caused by heat waves in Pakistan.

data.projectName: “NAPHTHOQUINONES: Synthesis of Derivatives as Potential Anti-diabetic Agents”
data.projectDigest: The present proposal has been designed to study the antidiabetic effects of synthesized naphthoquinone derivatives. The idea was intuited by the findings of very assenting results obtained from the studies performed in past for the antidiabetic potential of Nigella sativa L. (black cumin), or exclusively for its active compound ‘thymoquinone’. Thymoquinone’s antidiabetic activity has also been investigated in recent years. Experimentations on diabetes-induced animal models have guided to propose possible biochemical modifications necessary for altered carbohydrate/ lipid metabolism in diabetes. However, no specific drug has been proposed currently to treat the metabolic disorders induced during progression of diabetes. As thymoquinone has shown potent antidiabetic activity in various studies, therefore, the present proposal has been planned to design some drug compounds with structure similarity to thymoquinone, and may show potential antidiabetic effect comparable to/ or more than the thymoquinone. Present studies will definitely form the bases for drug discovery and development to treat diabetes. Different diabetes effected biochemical pathways, and the effects of synthesized naphthoquinone derivatives on their operation will be studied in streptozotocin induced type-2 diabetic rats. The main focus will be to get some findings about the antidiabetic potential of synthesized compounds to treat widely prevailing type II diabetes in humans.

data.projectName: Exploring the Treatment Options for Multidrug Resistant Bacterial Infections
data.projectDigest: Multidrug resistance is a major issue worldwide and hampers all the efforts being done for curing different diseases. The whole genome sequencing of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis TB (MDR-TB) has provided new insight into understanding the molecular pathogenesis of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB). In this project, we had proposed that in order to understand the disease pathogenesis of MTB, it is imperative to screen a panel of patients where immunity along with different diseases promoting regulatory inflammation plays a vital role in disease manifestation and progression. This project will result in the possibility that the molecular diagnostics for TB drug resistance could be improved. Furthermore, the strains which are circulating will be examined not only for intrinsic and acquired but also focus on cases of unexplained TB drug resistance. In addition, exploring genetic factors will help in better disease diagnostics and management. Aim of the current project is to generate the data that might be helpful in reducing the global burden of TB and reduce the rate of onward transmission of MDR-TB in high burden countries such as Pakistan, identifying resistance profiles directly from patients may also enable a better tailored drug regimen where possible. Furthermore, this project will spread awareness about MDR-TB and is likely to provide bases for protecting vulnerable and poor populations from MDR-TB in future.

data.projectName: Design and Development of Phase Change Material (PCM) based Solar Thermal Energy Storage System for medium temperature decentralized post-harvest processes
data.projectDigest: Solar energy is the most promising form of renewable energy. Despite this, it is sporadic in nature which causes fluctuations in energy output. In order to counterbalance, it is necessary to devise a system to store surplus energy during sunshine hours and releasing it when required. Latent heat thermal energy storage system (LHTESS) is the most interesting technique to store thermal energy which utilizes phase change material (PCM) as a storage medium. The current project is focused on finding the possibility to integrate LHTESS in various suitable solar thermal processes in Agricultural activities like food drying etc. Although solar energy is being utilized for these kind of activities in agriculture (limited) but has to integrate with grid power supply for backup. In order to make a process completely decentralized for on-farm processing, there is need to develop a system to store thermal energy. Most of the agricultural processes (drying, roasting, hydrolyzing, sterilization, extraction, pasteurization) require heat under temperature range of 60-260 °C and this temperature range can easily be achieved by using different solar concentrators. For this, a setup will be consisted of a 10 m2 paraboloidal concentrator, heat receiver, PCM storage tank and a shell and tube heat exchanger. The system is expected to absorb, store and release an appreciable amount of thermal energy in the form of latent heat at nearly constant temperature to be used as backup. The project is expected to play a significant role in identifying and understanding the possibility of utilizing PCM based thermal energy storage system for operating suitable agricultural operations like grain drying, water heating for animal farm etc.

The current project is focused on finding the possibility to integrate LHTESS in various suitable solar thermal processes in Agricultural activities like food drying etc. Although solar energy is being utilized for these kind of activities in agriculture (limited) but has to integrate with grid power supply for backup. In order to make a process completely decentralized for on-farm processing, there is need to develop a system to store thermal energy. Most of the agricultural processes (drying, roasting, hydrolyzing, sterilization, extraction, pasteurization) require heat under temperature range of 60-260 °C and this temperature range can easily be achieved by using different solar concentrators. For this, a setup will be consisted of a 10 m2 paraboloidal concentrator, heat receiver, PCM storage tank and a shell and tube heat exchanger. The system is expected to absorb, store and release an appreciable amount of thermal energy in the form of latent heat at nearly constant temperature to be used as backup. The project is expected to play a significant role in identifying and understanding the possibility of utilizing PCM based thermal energy storage system for operating suitable agricultural operations like grain drying, water heating for animal farm etc.

data.projectName: Molecular modeling based designing of high potential bioactive peptides and their recombinant expression against multi-drug resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis
data.projectDigest:
Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is major challenge to human health. Genetic mutation and improper use of medication lead to rapid increase in drug-resistant strains. Highest level of AMR has been reported in Pakistan, India and Bangladesh. Resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis has been developed due to mutations in catalase peroxidase, beta-subunit of RNA-polymerase genes. There are no drugs in pipeline for the treatment of TB and this huge gap is needed to be filled, which this study can do by accessing potential of bioactive peptides for inhibition/ control/ treatment of TB.
Bioactive peptides (BPs) have been reported to showcase antibacterial, antifungal, anti-insecticidal, anti-mulluscidal, antiviral activities. Library of potential BPs will be produced and docked against MDR genes of M. tuberculosis. The sequence of BPs will be modified to increase binding energy of peptides against MDR genes. The modified bioactive potential peptides (MBPPs) will be reverse translated to get coding sequence of DNA. Anti-tubercular activity will be performed on different cultured strains of M. tuberculosis in the presence of recombinant purified bioactive peptides (RPBPs). The RPBPs with anti-tubercular potential will be virtuous candidates for in-vivo experimentation and clinical trials. This proposed study can make Pakistan to lead the world in development of drugs against multi-drug resistant infectious agents and to combat antimicrobial resistance. Moreover, the project will help achieve a part of one of the eight Millennium Development Goals; combating HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and other significant communicable diseases.

data.projectName: Exploration, biology and potentials of predatory mites from vegetable growing areas of different tehsils of District Faisalabad.
data.projectDigest: The identification of invertebrates (insect and mite species) are the basis of entomology since the dawn of human civilization. Many plant feeding arthropod species are menace for sustainable agriculture and food security. Among these, mites comprise a large group that belong to subclass Acari of the class Arachnida and widely distributed. Phytophagous mites belong to family Tetranychiidae that infest many cultivated crops, vegetables, fruits, ornamental and forest trees. On the other hand, a large group of predatory mites feed on harmful mites, small soft bodied insects and their eggs. These predators have a considerable importance in biological control programs. In Pakistan, more than 35 kinds of vegetables are grown in numerous ecosystems.  The attack of different insect and mite pest are the important factors, which causes significant loss to vegetable yield. Very little work has been done on these arachnid mite species regarding their systematics, ecology, biology, diversity and predatory potentials from Pakistan. There is a need of comprehensive survey to explore such important predatory mite species from different Tehsils of District Faisalabad that are famous for vegetable production. During project work, the identification, biology and predatory potentials of some important mite species will be observed under laboratory conditions.

data.projectName: Genetic and Molecular analysis of inherited Growth hormone disorders in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Growth hormone disorders are group of disorders caused by deficiency or insensitivity of growth hormone. Short Stature due to inherited Growth hormone disorders is a serious problem worldwide. Due to high rates of cousin marriages, large family structure and lack of awareness, recessive genetic disorders including short stature are big issue in Pakistan. The most common short stature due to growth hormone disorder is isolated growth hormone deficiency (IGHD) which is characterized by low growth hormone levels. Laron syndrome, another growth hormone related disorder, is caused due to defects in growth hormone receptor protein. Multiple tests are required for their differential diagnosis which are costly and can’t offer fully reliable results without genetic testing. For cheaper genetic testing population data is needed which is not available yet as there is no reported research study on genetic and molecular basis of Laron syndrome or IGHD in Pakistani population. 
Results of this study will help to identify diagnostically important mutations/exons for cheaper genetic testing in Pakistani population. Application of this strategy will save time and resources required for accurate differential diagnosis of these disorders which in turn will benefit patients/families, doctors and pathology labs. Data produced in this study will be useful for genetic counseling, carrier screening, DNA based diagnosis, molecular/personalized medicine and upcoming gene therapy which are useful strategies in prevention of the disease in Pakistan. Training of Ph.D, M.Phil scholars, creation of awareness of causation and prevention of diseases in affected families are additional advantages of the study.

data.projectName: Experimental Investigation of Gas Hydrate Inhibition in Reservoirs using Smart Drilling Fluids
data.projectDigest:
Water-based drilling fluids are widely used to dugout the oil and gas field reservoirs. Conventional water-based drilling fluids in oil and gas field have many shortcomings which includes fluid loss to formations, the loss of rheological properties at deep well elevated temperature and high-pressure conditions. In this proposed work, the bentonite suspension will be used as base drilling fluids. The impact of acrylamide/ATBS copolymer, nanoparticles and SiO2-AMPS composite will be assessed on rheology, filtration and gas hydrate properties at various temperatures and pressures. The effect of temperature on rheological properties, fluid loss properties of base drilling fluid will be compared with the polymer, nanoparticles and composite based drilling fluid. It is expected that substantial reduction in fluid loss will be observed by adding polymer, nanoparticles and synthesized composite compared to base drilling fluid. The gas hydrate inhibition properties of all the drilling fluids will be studied at various temperatures to investigate the hydrate formation time during drilling operations.
The novel synthesized smart drilling fluid would be used as potential additive in the water-based drilling fluids to improve the gas hydrate inhibition characteristics. It is believed that the issues of drilling gas reservoirs will be reduced by employing smart drilling fluids.

data.projectName: Better Stevia production by Integrating the soil and water management practices in Cholistan region

data.projectName: probable solution of pollutant free enviroment
data.projectDigest: Industries play a key role in sustainable damage to the surface water as well as ground water in Pakistan. They pollute water by discharging of their industrial effluents which not only adds hazardous material in water but also degrade the water quality. Most of them do not have any wastewater treatment plant before disposing off. They dispose their effluent in an open area, causing an environment polluted. The colored pigments used in textile, printing, scientific laboratories, leather and dyeing industries are disposed into the environment as waste water effluents. They are stable to light and not biodegradable therefore highly toxic to life. They should be removed from the industrial effluent before disposing into water. The key purpose of this work is to clean water and make it available for drinking, irrigation and industrial purposes. Various methods have been adopted to  remove water stress, but Adsorption is effective and low cost treatment method used for the elimination of dissolved colored pigments from polluted water. The colored pigments pollutant disposed by industries will be removed by marble powder which is another industrial pollutant.i.e removing one industrial pollutant by using other industrial pollutant.

data.projectName: A universal and efficient fault tolerant control-based diagnosis system for wind turbines
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan is an energy deficit country and facing the problem of load shedding from the last two decades. The energy demand of the country is constantly increasing due to the population increase. Energy deficiency greatly influences the economic growth of the country due to less energy supply to industrial consumers. Similarly, natural energy resources such as oil and gas are constantly decreasing and cause severe environmental hazards in the energy generation process. Therefore, Pakistan, as well as the world, has focused on other means of generation such as renewable energy resources. Among these renewable energy resources, wind energy is the most common one.  
The wind turbines (WTs) are used for the extraction of energy from wind and are installed in an environment that faces turbulent winds, and other severe environmental conditions. Therefore, the occurrence of faults in different components associated with WTs is very common. Consequently, this results in the interruption of the power supply to the main grid and reduces the overall efficiency of WTs. The aim of this project is to minimize this interruption due to the faults and improve the overall efficiency of the WTs by utilization of advanced fault detection and isolation and fault-tolerant control schemes.

data.projectName: Fabrication of DES and DES@silica based hydrophobic membrane for the removal of heavy metals from aqueous solution
data.projectDigest:
The presence of heavy metals in the environment become a serious issue as it causes many diseases in human beings and also in aquatic life. Industrial waste water is a big source of water pollution as it contains several heavy metals like Arsenic, Cadmium, Mercury, Chromium, Lead, Zinc and many others. The removal of heavy metals is of special distress by reason of their persistence and recalcitrance in the environment. There are many methods for waste water treatments like, filtration, adsorption, coagulation, evaporation and so many others but membrane separation method is most easy and feasible technique for waste water treatment. Existing membrane technologies like ultrafiltration (UF), microfiltration (MF), nano filtration (NF), polymeric membranes and reverse osmosis (R-O), are very useful against heavy metals but less efficient. The current research work will help to fabricate a funionalized polymeric membrane for the removal of hazardous heavy metals in water purification appliances. It emphasis on the synthesis of hydrophobic membranes by using polymer (polysulfone) and deep eutectic solvent (DES) with functionalized silica as an additive or filler. Different weight percentages of DES-f-Silica will be blended with polysulfone polymer to fabricate mixed matrix membranes (MMM) by using phase inversion technique for the removal of heavy metals.

The characterization of DES and functionalized silica can be carried out by FT-IR and viscosity. morphology  of membran

data.projectName: A Study of Pronominal Siffixation in North Western Indo-Aryan Languages
data.piUniversity: Lasbela University of Agriculture, Water and Marine Sciences, Lasbela
data.projectDigest: Pronominal suffixation means suffixes of pronouns attached with verbs. Some languages have single and some have double pronominal suffixes attached with verbs.  Persian, Pashto, Kashmiri, Sindhi, Saraiki and Khetrani languages have double pronominal suffixation. For example, a single Persian word 'guftamish' (I said to him) carries full information of verb, tense, speaker and listener. Previous studies have analyzed pronominal suffixes in Persian, Pashto and Kashmiri. But work on Saraiki, Sindhi and Khetrani is extremely rare. Particularly Saraiki and Khetrani are under studied in this regard. Above all, comparative and typological studies on these languages are non-existent. Saraiki, Sindhi and Khetrani lie in the same linguistic sub-family which is called North Western Indo Aryan. This context provides an interesting scenario for comparative study of pronominal suffixes in NWIA languages to see how this phenomenon has developed in this sub-family. These languages are being spoken in the areas adjacent with areas where Pashto and Persian are also spoken. The locational significance brings this study in the ambit of areal linguistics. This project aims to study pronominal suffixes in NWIA languages and compare them with Pashto and Persian to define a typological profile of NWIA languages regarding pronominal suffixation.

data.projectName: Development of some new cost-effective and efficient sampling technique under ranked set sampling for estimation of population mean and median
data.projectDigest: Sampling is used in many disciplines like agriculture, education, environmental science etc. The sampling method which utilize minimum resources and give high efficiency is preferred. Ranked set sampling (RSS) is one of the cost-effective sampling methods which incorporate the cost-free ranking mechanism in selection procedure. This method can be further modified to more cost effective and efficient schemes. In addition, the RSS method is not applicable in many situations. Therefore, this method can be modified to more practical scheme. In this study we will introduce sampling schemes which are more cost effective and efficient. Simulation study will be conducted to test the performance of estimators under proposed schemes. The suggested schemes will also be illustrated with real data set.

data.projectName: AI and Machine Learning based Seed Classification System
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan’s economy largely depends on its agriculture. According to a survey, the agriculture sector accounts nearly 20.9% of GDP and 43.5% of employment. However, due to lack of cutting-edge technology, the growth rate of agriculture sector in Pakistan is decreasing rapidly. Low quality seeds and export of raw items (instead of finished product) are two major factors for this decline. Around the globe, seeds are digitally analyzed and classified according to soil germination properties and grain quality. However, in Pakistan, there are few operational agriculture research centers with very limited (mostly obsolete) equipment. Under these circumstances, it is necessary to develop state-of-the-art seed analysis equipment to fulfill the actual indigenous need. 
 In this project we aim to develop a digital portable system for analysis and classification of different seeds. The developed system will be a self-sufficient device which will incorporate hardware software co-design using onboard microcomputer. The hardware portion of the project comprises of sensors, processing and display units. The software potion consists of different pre-processing algorithms (filtering, contrast adjustment, projection correction and interpolation etc.) segmentation, data fusion, feature extraction (statistical, morphological, shape, color and texture etc.) and classification algorithms which will be developed for this particular application considering all the local constraints.

data.projectName: Design and development of an efficient artificial pancreas for expeditious blood glucose monitoring and insulin dosage
data.projectDigest: Artificial Pancreas (AP) is the closed loop blood glucose regulation consisting of a continuous glucose monitoring system (CGMS), a controller and an insulin pump. The different sources of noise and lag in an Artificial Pancreas include CGMS, insulin pump and biological processes. Currently available devices do not cater these lags completely. Hence, to provide an expedite control, PID with time varying set point algorithm has been implemented to a simulator in an effort to build an efficient device. Although, improvements have been observed as compared to the currently available solutions, we intend to dig deep in order to further improve the solution.

data.projectName: Smart Irrigation through Floppy Sprinkler System under control climate conditions
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest: A Floppy sprinkler system (FSS) as a new innovative irrigation method was introduced by project experts through technology development fund program. In the continuation of previous work, a computer-based program for determining the crop water requirement for high crop yield at different growth stages is being proposed with above mention irrigation system. This system can be integrated with the network of soil moisture measuring sensors placed at different places in the field to give real time irrigation requirement and irrigation scheduling. With this system, it will be able to manage the irrigation quantity and irrigation frequency specifically during the kharif season when temperature is high. The real objectives of this proposed research are to implement FSS for climate change condition such as Egypt and south Africa did same research and frost control as many studies recommended for sprinkler irrigation. Thus, this automated irrigation system allows it to be scaled up for larger greenhouses or open fields. The system will have a distributed wireless network of soil moisture and temperature sensors placed in the root zone of the plants and water level sensor will be placed in tank for checking the water level in tank. In addition, a gateway unit handles sensor information, triggers actuators, and transmits data to a web application. An algorithm will be developed with threshold values of temperature, soil moisture and water level that will be programmed into a micro-controller-based gateway to control water quantity.

data.projectDigest:
Neurodegenerative disease (NDs), refer to a group of conditions which occur due to neuronal cell death of the central nervous system. The most common neurodegenerative diseases include Parkinson’s disease (PD), Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). There are various causative agents which are responsible for neurodegenerative diseases amongst which, neuroinflammation is one of the core reasons. Therefore, in order to minimize the neurodegeneration process one of the promising treatment or preventive approach is to cope the neuro-inflammatory process with anti-inflammatory drugs. Most of the currently available synthetic drugs are associated with serious undesirable side effects, secondly due to decrease efficacy after prolonged usage and high cost as well, have compelled the scientist to search for plant based novel drug candidates for the treatment of neuroinflammation. 
             Since the time immemorial medicinal plants are the veritable source of medicines to mankind. Traditional medicine offers a potential alternative source of medicines around the globe. Numerous research groups have reported the effectiveness of flavonoids isolated from plants for treatment of neuroinflammation and memory enhancement. Therefore, the current research project has been structured with a view point to carry out bio-assay guided isolation of flavonoids from selected medicinal plants and evaluation of nuro-antiinflammatory potentials for effective treatment of neuro-inflammation. The successful results will not only provide natural, effective and economical alternatives for the treatment of neuroinflammation but would also increase the professional competence of the research scholars.

data.projectName: Assessment of Field Evolved Insecticide Resistance in Fruit Flies of Pakistan for Future Food Security
data.projectDigest: Global food security is threatened by several abiotic and biotic factors including; natural calamities, plant diseases and pests. Resulting in the decline of country food economics and loss of valuable genetic resources. Fruit flies known as the major pests of soft, fleshy fruits and remains the most significant agricultural polyphagous pests in Pakistan and worldwide.  It is responsible for valuable economic losses and health problem. Moreover, the long term usage of the different insecticidal chemistries for fruit flies control, not only responsible for insecticide resistance development in fruit flies but also possess serious hazardous risk to the environment. Unfortunately, fruit flies have developed resistance against all classes of chemical insecticides worldwide and in Pakistan. These flies have evolved resistance against insecticides through different physiological mechanisms including; modifications in the cuticle, increased metabolic detoxification and target site insensitivity. It is hypothesized that in Pakistan majority of the fruit plants may be infested by fruit flies due to high and unregulated practices of insecticide, resulting in insecticides resistance development. The present study is aimed to explore the diversity of fruit flies and to evaluate the toxicity level of different insecticidal chemistries used against them and to determine the resistance at molecular level.

data.projectName: Design and Development of EMG Driven Exoskeleton for Post Stroke Rehabilitation
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Stroke is the major neurological disease of our time. It results from ischemic infarction or bleeding into part of the brain. Its incidence in Pakistan is increasing because of high prevalence of risk factors in our society such as high blood pressure and high level s of cholesterol.
A large number of stroke survivors are left permanently disabled and need rehabilitation to return to functional life. Unfortunately, rehabilitative programs that are currently running in Pakistan are costly and require the help of physiotherapists with regular and frequent visits for physical therapy over many months. This results in less commitment over time and hefty cost on our health care services . These limitations significantly reduce the number of patients who can get adequate  treatment and hence majority of stroke patients are left disabled and unable to have a good quality of life. 
In this project our aim is to develop a simple intuitive wearable robotic device that will help patients to do physical exercise in the comfort of their homes. This device will be non-invasive and  cost effective. It will help in speedy and significant recovery and make stroke survivors a functional part of our society again.

data.projectName: Assessment of Bisphenol Endocrine Disrupting  Agents in Milk,  Water and Soft Drinks Sold in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest:
Endocrine disruptor agents (EDAs) comprise of both naturally occurring and synthetic chemicals in plastic food containers. Some chemicals of this class also are present in epoxy resins used for the polymeric coatings on metal cans and are additives in polyvinyl chloride plastics. Various bisphenol derivatives mainly bisphenol F, bisphenol A, bisphenol B, bisphenol F diglycidyl ether, and bisphenol A diglycidyl ether are currently used in the production of polycarbonate food containers. These chemicals can transfer into milk due to environmental contamination, feed contamination, leaching from milking machine components, cleaning agents or processing. This research will focus on strategies for the successful and accurate detection of these chemicals in milk, water and soft drinks by HPLC equipped with ultra violet and fluorescence detector. Chemical analysis using liquid chromatography coupled to tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) will be required to authenticate the HPLC results. 
Using the technology developed on this project levels of bisphenol EDAs will be found in milk, water and soft drinks samples but further investigations should be carried out to identify the source of residues. 
The findings of this research will lead to a relatively cheap method to assess the levels of various bisphenol derivatives in foods. The information generated may be useful for the food and health regulatory authorities to set food safety standards regarding the maximum permissible levels of the bisphenols. This will also be a step forward towards the food and health safety awareness among the end users.

data.projectName: A83-01 and CHIR99021 mediated differentiation of Human Wharton’s Jelly derived Mesenchymal Stem Cells into Hepatocyte like cells and its therapeutic role in fibrotic liver regeneration
data.projectDigest: This study  aims to isolate and characterize Mesenchymal Stem Cells (MSCs) from the Wharton’s Jelly (WJ) of Human Umbilical cord (UC) tissues. As the WJ is supposed to entrap stem cells at the time of development so the availability of MSCs in these tissue is much higher as compared to other adult tissues. Furthermore, these perinatal stem cells have the ability to differentiate into derivatives of three embryonic germ layers. As the culture environment has been shown to influence the phenotype ad physiology of stem cells, therefore, we will differentiated these cells into hepatocyte like cells (HLCs) through microenvironment modulation with addition of two small molecules (A83-01, CHIR99021). Finally, the in vivo hepatic regeneration ability of WJMSCs and HLCs will be evaluated in CCL4 induced liver fibrosis mouse mode.

data.projectName: Artificial Intelligence based Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CADx) System for Breast Cancer using Digital Pathology
data.projectDigest: A lot of medical imaging data have been digitized with the passage of time. The digital data allow the doctors to view the situation of patient in a new way. It helps the doctor to diagnose the disease more effectively. The rapid development in digital imaging technology and computational processing reflects the growth of algorithms towards health care industry. The availability of huge memory in modern systems also plays a vital role in this development. The modern Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CADx) systems based on deep learning assist the pathologists in tedious tasks. Pakistan is the country which have the highest breast cancer mortality rate in Asia as 83,000 new cases are appeared every year and out of which 40,000 cases are died. To decrease mortality rate, our goal is to develop a computer-aided diagnostic system, which will have the capability to assist the pathologist in various tedious tasks such as nuclei detection, segmentation of abnormal areas in whole slide image, and classification of tissues etc.

data.projectName: Evaluation  of fertilizer amended  carbon-based waste composite materials to boost the water conservation capacity of different agri-soils
data.projectDigest: Pakistan lies in a subtropical region characterized by harsh weather, drastic environment and uneven rainfalls. In the recent years of global warming Pakistan has suffered severe fluctuations in weather-hot weather has expanded its wings into the domain of winter-that normal rainfalls seem to be stopped and in future there is an acute danger of water shortage and famine. So, a composite should be available that might work better in harsh environment. In Pakistan, There is a chronic shortage of water predict in near future; so, to avoid the effect of barrenation of soil and to maintain the crop yield this research project title “evaluation of fertilizer amended carbon-based waste material composition to boost the water conservation capacity of different agri-soils” is therefore planedl, useful and beneficial to great extent. For this purpose agro waste rice husk will be converted into pulp which will be amended with the biopolymers of guar gum, alginate and polydextran cellulose instead of polyacrylamide. Compositions will be optimized using various operational conditions like pH, particle size of soil, temperature and type of soil. Optimized composite will be amended with the required minerals and nutrients/fertilizers for further use into agriculture soil.

data.projectName: Highly Organized 3D Scaffolds of BioGlass Containing Injectable Dicalcium Phosphate Bone Cements
data.projectDigest:
Healing of segmental bone defects remains a difficult problem in orthopedic and trauma surgery. One reason for this difficulty is the limited availability of bone material to fill the defect and promote bone growth.  Tissue engineering involving synthetic materials offers a practical approach to combat this problem.  The desirable orthopedic scaffold material should be able to facilitate bone tissue growth without compromising the mechanical strength of the material and at the same time it should be biocompatible with the local cell environment.  Ceramic materials based on calcium phosphates (CPs) are used in a range of orthopedic applications from resorbable / non-resorbable disease-free bone replacement materials (porous bone grafts) to bone cements  and coatings on biomedical implants  to promote fixation and osteointegration after surgery.
 In this project we will utilize 2-axis motion stage, controlled by a computer-aided direct write program to design several implants for potential craniofacial/orthopedic surgery. Bio-glass (BG) will be incorporated into dicalcium phosphate bone cement for the purpose of developing an injectable and bioactive composite cement with suitable physicochemical and biocompatible performance. Biomaterial will be synthesized in our lab and then used to fabricate the implant. The main aim of the work is to fabricate highly porous 3D Scaffolds with good mechanical strength

data.projectName: The relativistic effects  on  waves in various plasma environments
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Plasma often called the fourth state of matter, is a fully or partially ionized gas which can be considered as a collection of charged particles whose dynamics is dominated by electromagnetic forces. The important parameters in the discussion of plasma are its density and temperature. When the thermal energy is of the order of the rest mass energy (k_B T ~m_0 c^2) the relativistic effects are important and when the thermal energy is less than the rest mass energy (k_B T <m_0 c^2) then relativistic effects are negligible. The relativistic effects on the waves appear due to an increase in the mass of a particle (or decrease in the cyclotron frequency) as it moves with relativistic velocity. The relativistic plasmas received much importance due to its application in different environments, including laboratory plasma (fusion experiment) and astrophysical plasma (white dwarfs and neutron stars).  Such plasmas contain particles with high thermal velocities, and relativistic effects may play an important role in the propagation characteristics of the wave. 
In this project, we will study these relativistic effects on the propagation of various waves in plasma. It is difficult to obtain exact analytical results when we introduce relativistic effects in our calculation as the integrals get complicated. People usually use certain approximations to get the dispersion relations specifying the dependence of wave frequency on the wavenumber (k). However,  we will use some numerical techniques to solve these integrals. This will provide us with a better understanding of the relativistic effects on various waves in a relativistic plasma environment.

data.projectName: Pakistani’s Academician Writing for Publication Practices and Writing Facilitation Center
data.projectDigest: Due to globalization and advancement in research and technology, the gap between developed and developing countries is increasing. The disparities and inequalities in scientific output is alarming. One aspect of this gulf is the role of English language in scientific publication. Scholars in non-English speaking countries face double divide on one hand lacking research opportunities and on the other hand linguistic resources to publish their work in recognized journals. This project is designed to explore the writing for publication practices of Pakistani academicians including faculty members and graduate students. The study will help in understanding affordances and challenges of Pakistani academicians’ research publications. Research publications are not only crucial for individuals personal development and promotion, but also needed for valuing the higher education institutions of any society. They are also required for socioeconomic uplifting of the society. The project also envisioned to establish a writing facilitation center to provide individual support to academicians in the country. The project also includes arrangement of an international conference on writing to sensitize Pakistani academicians to explore writing as field of research inquiry. The project will be useful for academicians, policy makers, and will help in improving the research output of Pakistani scholars.

data.projectName: Molecular characterization and epidemiology of antibiotic resistance genes of ?eta Lactamase producing bacterial pathogens causing septicaemia from tertiary care hospitals, District Peshawar.
data.projectDigest: Septicemia (presence of bacteria and their toxin in blood) leads to weakness and fever and is usually treated with antibiotics. But some of these bacterial pathogens are not treatable with these antibiotics now because of a phenomenon known as antibiotic resistance. It is a critical health problem around the globe. The current study will focus on to identify the most common Gram positive and negative bacterial pathogens causing septicemia and will also focus to explore the importance of multidrug resistance (resistance to three or more classes of antibiotics) in bacterial pathogens. These bacteria are resistant to a class of antibiotics, ?-lactams, because they produce enzymes (protein) known as Beta-Lactamases (BLs). ?-lactam antibiotics are widely used to treat different infections caused by these pathogens, however, resistance to various ?-lactams is increasing at an alarming rate worldwide. The current proposal is part of effort to tackle antibiotic resistance in the proposed area. If we are able to identify the most prevalent bacteria of septicemia and their antibiotic sensitivity pattern, we will be able to manage septicemia in an effective way. This can act as policy guideline for health professionals and government to better tackle cases of septicemia to reduce mortality and morbidity.

data.projectName: Nano-encapsulation of essential oils from Cinnamon and Garlic and blends therefrom; A value added agri-based product
data.projectDigest: The biologically active components in food give flavor, aroma along with neutraceutical benefits. In this project, these health beneficial compounds will be extracted from garlic and cinnamon. Nano-encapsulation with rice starch base will be used to protect characteristic flavor and efficiency of active ingredients of individual garlic, cinnamon and blend of both commodities. The garlic and cinnamon are both widely used flavors in local and international cuisines (garlic bread, cinnamon rolls etc) and herbal medicines (teas and extracts). Therefore, formulated nano-capsules will have demand in various food processing, neutraceutical and pharmaceutical industries. Rice starch has distinguishing white colour, bland taste and it is hypoallergenic. Hence, rice starch will not cause any hurdle in the development of nano-capsules, product processing and will be safe for the end consumer of any age group. The major active ingredients in garlic and cinnamon are allicin and cinnamic aldehyde, respectively. The blended garlic/cinnamon essential oils could have stronger antimicrobial, antifungal and antioxidant effects because of the potential synergic effects of the essential oils from two different sources. This knowledge may ultimately form the basis for the development of ‘green’ food additives and possibly improve shelf life of food with dramatically reduced side effects in humans.

The alternate energy sources are gaining interest day by day in order to meet the energy demands of the world. Thermoelectric energy harvesting is an alternate energy technique to convert heat energy into electrical energy. This technology will reduce the global warming and also provide useful energy. 
The energy demand and resources, worldwide, are very important and its demand is increasing with world population. Exploring alternate sources of energy is gaining interest in scientific community due to decrease in traditional resources of energy such as coal, gas, petroleum etc. These conventional resources also pollute the environment as they emit carbon dioxide (CO2) and other toxic elements thus leading towards global warming. To achieve these two goals, i.e., energy harvesting and reduce global warming, thermoelectric technology is used as a renewable energy resource. As  earth is also receiving heat energy and light from the sun which is about 10,000 times more than the consumption. Therefore, its effective utilization is to use photo-thermoelectric devices to utilize both light and heat for electrical energy conversion.

data.projectName: Development of natural meat preservative from plant Extracts
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Food insecurity and spoilage is one of the most urgent developmental challenges worldwide. About 2 million people are effected by food born pathogen and diseases annually.. Artificial food preservatives have revolutionized the industry in near past by providing an extended shelf-life and mass distribution of food. However they are being criticized due to reduction in the quality and producing life-threatening side effect i.e. Obesity and gut diseases and cancer. Now a days there is an increased consumer awareness concerning the usage of processed food with no chemical preservatives. Meat and meat products are more prone to oxidative and microbial spoilage with very short shelf life. Existing costly meat preservation techniques include irradiation, low-temperature storage, vacuum packaging and  chemical preservatives. Electricity shortage in Pakistan has  further increased  the quantity of  spoiled meat by degradation of refrigerated products. Chemicals preservatives are reported to decrease taste, color and nutrient contents of meat besides very deleterious effects like food poisoning gut diseases and  even cancer. This led to an amplified pressure on meat producers to completely remove preservatives from them and to develop an alternative method of meat preservation such as the use of natural preservatives. The present project is aimed to develop plant derived preservatives having very high antimicrobial and antioxidant properties. For this purpose selected plant species would be extracted and extracts would be applied on meat after confirmation of antioxidant and microbial food spoilage efficacy. Standard procedures would be employed related to extraction separation of components and standardization in order to develop natural and healthy preservatives.

data.projectName: Feasibility Study of Isolation of Potential Xanthine Oxidase Inhibitors from Domestic Medicinal Plants: In-vivo and In-silico Studies of Hypouricemic and Antioxidant Activity Along with Optimization Modeling Using Response Surface Methodology Technique an
data.projectDigest:
In the proposed research project medicinal plants have been selected. To approach the optimized conditions for extraction and in-vivo conditions, computational techniques including response surface methodology and the neural network will be employed. The bioactive compounds for hypouricemic effects will be characterized by measuring total oxidant and antioxidant moieties, GC-MS, HPLC based analysis of bioactive compounds in extracts, their purification and X-ray crystallography. Through clinical trials, in-vivo hypouricemic potential of plant extracts will be evaluated by hyperuricemia induced mice model for effect of plant extracts on mice health and vital organs will be evaluated by baseline biochemical and histopathological studies. With clinical studies, interaction between newly screened plants compounds will be studied by Molecular Docking. Results will be analyzed by neural network systems using complicated mathematical relationships and response surface methodology techniques to present most possible productiveness perspective of involved variants in inhibiting xanthene oxidation. Results will be further evaluated by different algorithms and compared together. The prime goal is to provide herbal industry, lacking functional R&D divisions, with authentic roadmap for manufacturing herbal formulations based on scientific research. 
The current project has been discussed with the officials of Ehsan Herbal Pharmacy, Bahawalpur for the subsequent product formation and commercialization.

data.projectName: Building Microbial Factories for Novel Sesquiterpenes via Metabolic Engineering and Synthetic Biology strategies
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Pakistan imports more than 90% of raw material used in pharmaceuticals, food and flavor industry for the manufacturing of value added compounds. This results in sharp increase of import bills for raw materials and other active ingredients because of inflation. This proposal focuses on the indigenize production of sesquiterpenes and other broad spectrum analogues like nootkatone. All these are of high value in market and could be used as flavor and fragrance, antioxidants, insecticides with other potent anti-cancer and anti-inflammatory activities. More than 80% of current used sesquiterpenes are derived from plant sources, which largely dependent on plant cultivation and extraction. The expensive extraction processes, toxicity and other concerns like seasonal variations and amount of agricultural land used i.e. 400,000 kg of grape fruit can give us only 1 kg of nootkatone. Therefore, alternative methods for production of such compounds in more renewable and sustainable approach will be applied using yeast bio factories.  We intend to transplant the genetic pathways for precursor and other target molecules in a cost effective manner using Metabolic Engineering and Synthetic Biology. We also intend to use single and co-culture approaches for bio-transformation of precursors to broad spectrum sesquiterpenes in a fermentation tank.

data.projectName: Biochemical and Molecular Characterization of Health Beneficial Metabolites of Apple Under Different Climatic Conditions of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The proposed project is aimed to find out for the first time in Pakistan, the health beneficial metabolites and their underlying genes in apple fruit which is a common man daily use fruit crop. These include minerals, vitamins, flavonoids such as kaempferol rutin, quercetin, and anthocyanin and phenolic acids e.g., chlorogenic acid. The available literature has clear indications of the health benefits of these metabolites. For example, these metabolites are anti-cancer, anti-aging, anti-cardiovascular and anti-cerebrovascular agents. Quercetin and other flavonoids in apple reduce the risk of various types of cancers, such as prostate and lung cancer, and may have also beneficial effects on prevention of cardiovascular diseases. These benefits are believed to be due to the antioxidant properties of these compounds. To get all these benefits there is need for developing an apple which will be more health beneficial. The available literature shows three major issues in this regard, 1. The natural genetic variations of these metabolites in different apple varieties, 2. The current climate change that affects apple andthis changing climate regimes may have severe consequences for the apple metabolites and 3. The various diseases such mould causing by Penicillium expansum that produce toxic compound known as patulin that reduce the apple quality.  As many of the plant developmental processes depend on a certain range of temperature, rainfall and other relevant environmental parameters. Due to the change climatic conditions, the synthesis and development of these important compounds is affected that ultimately results in the change taste, size and shape of the fruits. In this project, the important health beneficial metabolites such as rutin, quercetin, kaempferol, anthocyanin

data.projectName: Analytic Study on Optical Solitons and Conservation Laws for Nonlinear Schrödinger”
data.projectDigest:
Optical fiber is a flexible and transparent fiber. It is made of glass and its thickness is not more than a human hair. It transmits light between the two ends of fiber. Optical fibers are used for transmission over long distances and at high bandwidths. They are used as alternatives of wires as they are not affected by electromagnetic waves and posses less loss of signals. In the area of optics, NLSE is a good model for optical pulse propagation in nonlinear fibers.
The nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLSE) is a nonlinear partial differential equation (NLPDE) and generally it is not integrable. NLSE support soliton solutions for different kind of nonlinearities. NLSE have lots of application in plasma physics, in the theory of molecular chains and optical fiber. NLSE possess dispersion and non linear effects and can be used to discuss the propagation of light in single-mode fibers. The evolution variable in NLSE is the space variable which is called the longitudinal coordinate of fiber. Bright and dark are two classes of envelope solitons in NLSE model, can be found in nonlinear media. A localized stimulation on the envelope of a large-amplitude carrier wave is a bright envelope soliton. It classically makes a hyperbolic secant graph and has a fixed phase over its width. The large-amplitude wave background has a dip or null which is dark envelope soliton. A dark soliton has breaks in phase at its center. 
We will find solitary waves solutions for different kinds of NLSE. We will find dark, bright, singular, lump soliton with kink and anti-kink soliton for unstable NLSE, paraxial NLSE, Radha Krishnan Kundu model and other NLSEs with different laws of nonlinearities like Kerr law, cubic quintic law, anti cubi law, parabolic law etc. We will also study soliton interaction

data.projectName: Role of micro RNAs in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
INTRODUCTION: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) is a group of clinical diseases mostly caused by endothelial dysfunction based on atherosclerosis (AS), including coronary heart disease, stroke, and other various cardiovascular diseases. The pathogenesis of ASCVD is extremely complex, mainly including lipid infiltration, endothelial damage reactions, and chronic inflammatory damage. Emerging technologies and multiple complementary experimental systems for studying atherosclerosis are rapidly transforming the approaches that can be utilized to understand the molecular basis of this disease. Here, we explore the roles of microRNA (MiR) in the etiology of atherosclerosis and provide a guide to researchers and clinicians regarding emerging technologies for epigenetic profiling.  
MicroRNAs are single-stranded noncoding RNA molecules of 22 nucleotides present in the cell cytoplasm. MiR could regulate gene expression on the post-transcriptional level by binding to the 3’UTR of mRNA, which may either inhibit the translation of protein from mRNA or promote the degradation of mRNA. MiRs have been found in plasma and other body fluids as stable molecules protected from endogenous RNase activity, which suggests that circulating miRs might be ideal biomarkers in cardiovascular diseases. Plasma and serum levels of miR-145, miR-155, and miR-17/92a cluster (miR-17, miR-126, miR-92a) related to the vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMC), inflammatory response-associated cells and endothelial cells (ECs), respectively. The present study is aimed to establish the role of microRNAs regarding prediction of the atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease in genetically susceptible individuals.

data.projectName: Identification and characterization  of useful Indigenous biofilms forming rhizobacteria from the different rhizospheres of cereals, leguminous and oil seed crops
data.projectDigest: Bacteria attach to plant root surface produce signals and send messages to other nearby bacterial specie. These messages are in the form of chemicals and different bacterial species produce different chemicals for signaling. These signals are very helpful in bacterial and plant interaction in the biotic or aboitic stress conditions due to strong root attachment. Moreover, plant growth improvement, increment in plant tolerance level to contaminants and effective defensive mechanism against plant pathogens is observed in such types of plants. This project is designed to isolate, identify and characterize rhizobacteria and their signal molecules for the first time from the rhizospheres of cereals, leguminous and oil seed crops of Pakistan. After identification, we will characterize these species against heavy metal stresses and the best surviving bacterial species will be identified and characterized by using molecular techniques such as Polymerase Chain Reactions and enzymes assay. The best heavy metal resistant bacteria species that will increase the growth of plants will be identified in this research and they will be used to induce the growth and yield of cereal, oil seed and leguminous crops in heavy metals contaminated areas of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Potential of Cholistan desert flora against cereal aphids as an IPM strategy
data.projectDigest:
Among the pests, aphids play a vital role in limiting the cereal crop production. Though chemical insecticides are utilized to a great extent but there are many harmful effects of these insecticides on living organisms (including human) and on the environment. Therefore, there is a need to shift the scales of controlling these pests towards safer resources, the natural and safer botanical insecticides. For this purpose four different botanicals e.g. (Aerva javanica (booh), Capparis decidua (forssk), Cleome brachycarpa (shamako), Dipterygium glaucum (safrawi)) will be used. After botanicals application, adult body weight, fecundity, longevity and maturity rate of the surviving aphids and the aphid mortality will be measured. 
Furthermore, the effects of these botanicals on the natural enemies of cereal aphid e.g. ladybird beetle will also be measured. For this purpose, aphids treated with botanicals will be provided to ladybird beetle as their feed and then the biology of ladybird beetle will be evaluated.
The botanical with best efficiency under laboratory conditions will again be evaluated in the field also. Formulation of the most effective botanical as insecticide and its registration as patent will be the last step of this proposal.

data.projectName: DESIGN AND REAL TIME IMPLEMENTATION OF ADAPTIVE FAULT TOLERANT AND SENSOR FAULT RECONSTRUCTION SCHEMES FOR INDIGENOUS MEDIUM RANGE SECURITY MONITORING UNMANNED AIR VEHICLE SYSTEM
data.projectDigest:
Fault tolerant control is used in emergency situations to ensure the overall stability by engaging the redundant actuators and sensors so that an
acceptable level of performance can be achieved to avoid any economic loss and human mortalities. The situations where actuator fault (reduced
functionality) or failure (complete breakdown) information is not available the proposed computationally efficient adaptive and passive nature of fault tolerant control schemes can play a vital role by adaptively updating the controller gains to mitigate the effects of such faults or failures. It is well known fact that faults in sensors can degrade the performance of feedback system even though a best-designed fault tolerant controller is present in the loop. In this project the problem of output redundancy will be addressed wherein sensor faults will be reconstructed by a robust sliding mode theory approach. The proposed sensor fault reconstruction scheme will help to correct the corrupted measured signals before applying them to the fault tolerant controller.
       The proposed adaptive fault tolerant and sensor fault reconstruction scheme will be tested and implemented in real time on the medium range unmanned aerial vehicle.

data.projectName: Formulation and Evaluation of Value-added Enriched Vermi-compost for Tomato production in Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Pakistan
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest: The aim of current research is to develop the PGPR-Vermi-compost integrated management system for the improvement of tomatoes production in Pakistan. Our mission is to develop an integrated management system that not only increased the seed germination, growth and development, but also fulfill the country need. To obtain higher tomatoes production, vermi-compost will be produced and PGPVB (Plant growth promoting vermi-bacteria will be isolated from earthworm’s gut and used along with the vermi-compost (VC). The growth parameters such as shoot length, surface area of roots, dry weights, plant growth hormones (gibberellins and auxins), chlorophyll contents and other nutrients of harvested plant will be analyzed. Hopefully, the results would support the utilization of PGPVB-vermi-compost for the tomatoes production in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Improving anaerobic germination tolerance and early stand establishment in dry direct seeded rice through seed enhancements
data.projectDigest: Early flooding in dry direct seeded rice (DSR) can reduce weed pressure and when integrated with early vigor traits can reduce crop-weed competition and toxic herbicides use resulting in higher yields. However, early flooding can be detrimental to rapid germination and early seedling stand under anaerobic conditions and no information are available in cultivated coarse and fine aromatic rice varieties for these traits in dry DSR. The proposed project will screen rice germplasm for rapid germination and seedling survival rate under anaerobic early flooding condition in dry DSR. Selected tolerant and intolerant genotypes will be further investigated for seedling growth and survival traits, physiological and biochemical mechanisms including soluble carbohydrates, amylase activity, total proteins and anaerobic enzymes activities. Novel peroxides molecules (CaO2, MgO2, ZnO2) and inorganic salts (CaCl2, KCl) will be applied using innovative seed enhancements techniques (seed coating, pelleting and priming) to improve the anaerobic germination tolerance and early vigor in rice genotypes. Their levels will be optimized based on germination, seedling survival percentage and growth traits including physiological and biochemical aspects. The optimized seed enhancements techniques will be evaluated for rapid emergence and early vigor traits, weed competitiveness, and yield performance under field conditions for demonstration and dissemination.

data.projectName: D-Mine : A real time asset tracking and monitoring system for Mines.
data.projectDigest: Pakistan has been graced with extensive reserves of minerals across a range of 600,000 sq. Kms, and the mineral industry is one of the crucial sources of economic development. However, despite having vast resources and competitive benefits, the Pakistan mineral sector remains straggling far behind the world’s mineral market. Moreover, due to market volatility, commodity price depression along with many other factors is reducing the profit margins. Therefore, there is a need to enhance the productivity performance of the mining industry through digital and technology innovations. We intend to provide an indigenous solution that will address the local needs of Pakistan Mine sites. The proposed D-mine project will provide more agile and productive business in addition to staff’s improved health and safety with the environmental impact that will assists in reducing the death-rates, decrease injuries, diminished emissions and waste. We aim to train Mine professionals so that they utilize the potential of the D-Mine framework to the maximum extent.

data.projectName: Pathway to Nationalism through Student Unions
data.projectDigest: In hand research is an attempt to understand and explain how the ban on student unions has influenced the student politics through promoting regionalism, ethnicity, intolerance, power politics, religious differences and weaponisation in educational institutions. Out of 207 million, 60 percent of Pakistan’s population comprises of youth which is under the influence of student politics directly or indirectly. But it is dismal that their potential is utilized for sectarianism, promoting regional feelings, provincialism, linguistic differences, and ethnic groups. The research project will be carried out in the various universities of Pakistan i.e. University of Punjab, Lahore, GC University Faisalabad, Quaid-i-Azam University, Islamabad, Bahaudin Zikrya University Multan and university of Sargodha. The post-graduate students which are enrolled in Master Degree program i.e. History, Pakistan Studies, Political Science, International Relations, and South Asian Studies, in these universities will be target population. Fifteen hundred respondents will be interviewed and 250 focus group will be conducted to collect information. Moreover, one day seminar will be arranged in every university to disseminate the idea. This exercise may be changed the mind set up of the youth about regionalism or ethnicity and inspire them toward nationalism.

data.projectName: Development of National Database for Academic Industry Collaboration: An Attempt towards Evidence-based Policy Making in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Despite increasing debate on the importance of academic-industry collaboration in Pakistan, there is no valid measurement tool that allows policymakers to assess the strength of this relationship in devising strategies for human development and economic growth. This research project aims at developing an Academic-Industry Collaboration Index (AICI) that will enable the Higher Education Commission (HEC) of Pakistan, industrial entities and the general public to rank universities’ relevance for specific sectors in terms of employment opportunities, student’s start-up businesses and applied research contribution. We adopt a quantitative approach in examining academia-industry collaboration in Pakistan that involves developing an effective survey-design and subsequent testing of the indicators in line with international standards.  We intend to generate a database of first-hand information from all public and private sector universities and their partner industrial entities to measure, analyze and predict key academic, industrial and economic outcomes. We plan to engage all public and private sector universities across Pakistan in obtaining quantitative data on the number, type, and nature of university-industry collaboration. The outcome of this project is expected to significantly contribute to designing policies for higher education and industrial development in Pakistan.

data.projectName: A high throughput approach to uncover new inborn errors of Immunity and biomarker in Pakistani Patients infected with dengue, Chikungunya and Zika Viruses.
data.projectDigest: Arboviruses  (dengue virus, chikungunya virus and zika virus) of severe public health problem in Pakistan and is transmitted by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes. Among these Dengue virus causing high morbidity and mortality leading to an international public health emergency. In Pakistan, in 2019 approximately 147200 cases of dengue infection and over 800 deaths have reported and represent a public health emergency . Curiously,  most of the subjects infected with ZIKV and DENV are asymptomatic. The development of DENV, CHIKV and ZIKV also depend upon the host immunogenetic background, influencing the resistance or susceptibility to the diseases, which is a research field that remains to be explored. The present proposal aims to identify common and specific immunological signatures, pathways and genetic variations in patients infected by DENV. To achieve this, stepwise, integrated systemic immunology RNA sequencing and whole exome sequencing (WES)-based approach should be followed. After clinical and laboratorial characterization RNAseq will be carried out to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) of signatures and signaling pathways regulated by DENV, CHIKV and ZIKV . In parallel, genomic DNA will be analysed using whole exome sequencing (WES). The genetic variations identified will be compared to mutational databases of genome-wide association studies that have identified risk loci for arboviruses and/or autoimmune diseases and checked for family segregation and functional validation. In this project  we will promote a translational and multidisciplinary study, which will identify new immunopathological mechanisms and disease biomarkers, opening avenues to develop novel therapies to reduce mortality and morbidity induced by DENV and other arbovirus

data.projectName: Particle Physics Beyond Standard Model
data.projectDigest:
At the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) in Switzerland, the largest particle accelerator on Earth, we are searching for brand new particles not included in the established laws of particle physics known as the Standard Model.  
The discovery of a new particle, the Higgs boson, in 2012 was something that we’ve been waiting for for a long time.  But there are many questions still left that could be answered by further new particles that we could discover directly, or infer from deviations in precise measurements of known particles.
My work revolves around the top quark, which is the heaviest known elementary particle.  I will search for a new particle, a “charged Higgs boson”, which would be a partner to the Higgs boson that we have discovered, and which could decay to a top quark.  I will also make precise measurements of the ambient environment around top quarks in order to model their production better.  Finally I will search for the rare production of top quarks in association with other heavy bosons, and will use those measurements to probe for new physics effects at high energies.

data.projectName: Consensus Based Multi-criteria Group Decision Making using AHP Structure with Incomplete Hesitant Fuzzy Preference Relations
data.projectDigest:
The supply chain consists of units involved in the design of new products and services, in the purchase of raw materials, in giving them semi-finished and finished shapes and in providing them to end-customers. The method of identifying and choosing relevant suppliers plays a significant role in the long-term commitment and quality of supply chains in manufacturing organizations. Therefore, a systematic and efficient strategy or method for choosing the most appropriate supplier leads to a reduction in buying risk and increases the number of just-in-time suppliers available and improves the “total quality management” (TQM) of production. Fundamentally, the supplier selection problem is considered as a multi-criteria decision making (MCDM) problem in a multi-person setting. The reliability of the approach to MCDM problems is influenced by the preferences of the experts.
The primary objective of the proposed project is to develop a method to minimize the risk of negligent, incompetent and reckless multi-criteria decision-making by assigning accuracy weights to experts on the basis of the information provided. To address the hesitation associated with ambiguity or impression, an expert may give her/his findings in form of incomplete hesitant fuzzy preference relations (IHFPRs) during the decision making process.

data.projectName: 3-DoF Motion based Car Driving Simulator Platform
data.projectDigest: From the viewpoint of cognitive thinking, driving ability needs a host of cognitive and decision-making skills in an extensive range of situations. Driving simulators allow investigators to generate such driving scenarios in a harmless and precise environment. Such situations might range from simply following another car to a difficult dilemma where a deadly accident is unavoidable, and choices must be made about justifying damage. The state-of-art driving simulators consists of three main components, (a) Dome/cylindrical projection as the visual system, (b) High degree-of-freedom (DOF) motion platform, and (c) Physical model of a vehicle. These components to work well together, the vehicle model must be placed at a distance from a wide projection screen to provide a proper visual field, while being on top of a bulky moving base for the rotational DOF through simultaneous rotation of all three components. Therefore, in this project, we intend to create a low-cost motion-based dynamic car driving simulator that can provide a handful driving experience to the new drivers close to reality before physically went on the road. The concept of Steward platform will be used to develop the DOF motion platform and a customize motion cueing algorithm will be used to maintain the synchrony of visual stimulation and vestibular stimulation.

data.projectName: Physiology and Growth of Stevia (Stevia rebaudiana L.) Plant under Different Environmental Stresses in Diverse Ecological Zones of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Stevia is the source of calories free sugar, and short duration crop as compared to sugarcane which could make it hot choice for Pakistani farmers. Like other crop plants, stevia is also exposed to different environmental stresses like drought, heat and salinity stress during their growth and development. Present study has planned to assess the adaptation of stevia under ten diverse ecological zones of Pakistan. The experiments will be carried out in Vehari, Multan, Sahiwal, Bahawalpur, Sargodha, Faisalabad, Lahore, Islamabad, Chakwal, and Layyah. Three experiments will be conducted at each station and applied the specific treatments. In drought experiments, drought stress will be 40, 80, 100% FC while in heat stress experiments, the temperature will be increased up to 2 and 4 oC than the normal atmospheric temperature. As far as salinity experiments are concerned; the salinity level will be 0, 40, 80, 120 dSm-1. The physiological, growth and biochemical attributes will be recorded to find its optimum growing zone in Pakistan. According to our best of knowledge, it is first comprehensive study which will be carried under different stresses in diverse ecological zone of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Sustainable University Excellence: Development, validation, and implementation of assessment framework
data.projectDigest: The human resource is a vital element of every organizational system. To ensure efficient operations functioning of business, operations and services skilled and knowledgeable human capital is inevitable. One of the prime sources of such a human talent is the University. The universities are expected to shape up the societies through providing the human resource equipped with leadership qualities, professional characteristics, and sound knowledge of their field. For the sustainable societies and communities, it is essential to have sustainable universities.  This proposed research project is meant to explore the theme of a sustainable university through identifying its main characteristics, structures, systems, processes, and operations. The topic has gained an appreciable amount of interest from both academia and practitioners from last couple of decades around the globe. This proposed research envisions architecture of a modern era sustainable excellent University. Initially, we coined a definition of a sustainable university as the integrated form of its capability to outshine in essential competencies of creation and dissemination of knowledge through marshaling is talent capitals economic, social, and societal fronts. It is expected that the output of this project will be beneficial for the HEIs, governments, and the societies at large.

data.projectName: Fabrication of Nanomaterials for Rapid, Early and Cost-effective Detection of Tuberculosis
data.projectDigest:
Tuberculosis (TB) is caused by the bacteria called mycobacterium tuberculosis in humans. It is among top ten leading diseases for deaths and according to WHO 1.5 million people died of it out of 10 million effected patients in 2018 worldwide. As per the WHO report, Pakistan is among the eight TB high burden countries with two third of the total TB cases of the world. It is a fatal and contagious disease which not only effects the lungs but also effects other parts of the body such as brain, kidney and spine etc. Early Detection of active tuberculosis (TB) remains so far, a major challenge for global public health. Number of methods are now used for the detection of TB, which include tuberculin skin test, interferon-? release assays, Acid-fast bacilli staining of sputum, Nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs) etc. All of these tests take 24 hours minimum to few weeks to give final results. And some are not very reliable as well. Therefore, there is a need to look for more reliable, fast, cost effective and easy to use methods.
We intend to prepare nanomaterials based colorimetric and fluorescence platforms for the point of care detection has huge potential due to the added advantages associated with them such as less time for detection, ease of use, low cost, easy synthesis and good stability etc.
