data.projectName: Therapeutic co-delivery nanoparticles of natural and synthetic anti-diabetic drugs
data.projectDigest:
As the conventional dosage forms of oral hypoglycemic drugs offer various limitations such as short duration of action due to their short half-lives, frequent dosing, risk of hypoglycemia, low bioavailability, high protein binding, gastric irritation, diarrhea, insolubility in water and do not comply with the safety and efficacy of the patients. Therefore this project will be carried out:

To search more effective and safer hypoglycemic drugs of natural origin
To investigate antidiabetic potential of locally available plants regarding their therapeutic dose so that lo- cally growing plants can be utilized for therapeutic purposes.
To prepare and characterize nanoparticles of new anti diabetic formulations of synthetic and natural origin
To fabricate optimized dosage form to prolong or sustain the drug release, increase the bioavailability of the drugs, increase the stability of drugs and to reduce the side effects of the drugs.
	To compare the pharmaceutical characteristics and therapeutic efficiencies of all nanoparticles so that the best formulation can be selected.

data.projectName: Clinical features and Molecular genetics of Neurological and Developmental disorders in Rural areas of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
data.projectDigest: Neurological and neuro-developmental disorders have become a major public health problem in Pakistan in recent years. Its treatment and management strategies are a daunting problem in Pakistan due to lack of funding, poorly developed primary and basic health facilities and weak political processes. Neurological and developmental disorders are increasing both in low and middle developing countries. This increasing rate depends upon certain rare, neglected and often difficult to understand neurological conditions. These disorders therefore require special attention, particularly in rural areas where these disorders remains unexplored. Similarly, the effect on rural populations by such severe disorders expected to be extremely painful. These issues are emerging as serious public health challenges in rural areas due to lake of awareness, illiteracy and the unavailability of affordable and efficient treatments. Identifying specific genetic markers may provide a useful explanation for disease ethiology, molecular characterization and pathogenesis. In this project we intend to use Next generation sequencing and genome-wide studies to investigate the novel causative gene(s) and understand the role in order to develop effective treatments for neurological and neuro-developmental disorders (rare and common). These biomarkers, along with other parameters, can be used to systematically design molecular assays and models for improving disease diagnosis. It is further expected that personal genetic profiling will also become more relevant, with implications for patient care in line with the proposed idea of personalized medicine.

data.projectName: Synthesis and Evaluation of Carbon-Based Catalysts and their Application for Developing Efficient Remediation Technology for the Treatment of Endocrine Disruptors in Water
data.projectDigest: Anthropogenic activities cause the release of extensive number of chemicals to water on a daily basis which has caused a threat to aquatic life and affecting public health. Among these contaminants endocrine disruptor (chemicals that trigger the normal endocrine system and cause diseases) are prominent and they can be released from enormous number of sources including agriculture, domestic and municipal wastes. Therefore, these toxic and health hazardous OCs need to be removed or degraded into non-toxic substances. EDs can be removed by various methods in which advance oxidation processes (AOPs) an emerging technique. The treatment of endocrine disruptors by reactive oxygen species are activated by toxic metals which are themselves are pollutants. Therefore, carbon-based catalysts (CBCs) like graphene, carbon frameworks and carbon nanotubes are proven efficient for the activation for persulfates. Recently, the modification of CBCs with hetero atoms has shown better performance with boron, nitrogen, phosphorous and sulfur doped CBCs and modified CBCs. Therefore, cost effective and efficient, doped and modified CBCs will be prepared for the Treatment of EDs in aqueous systems. The synthesized material will be characterized for elemental contents, adsorption capabilities and microscopic structure analysis. And will be used for the purification of real waste water.

data.projectName: Fabrication of functionalized nanocellulose- metal nanoparticles based electrochemical sensor for simultaneous detection of multiple trace metal ions
data.projectDigest: Trace metal contamination of surface and ground water resources from various anthropogenic sources is a serious environmental challenge for Pakistan. Due to absence of water quality testing and monitoring infrastructure together with limited financial resources, common people in Pakistan are facing serious problem in the availability of clean and safe water for drinking and domestic purposes. It is estimated that only 26.1% population has access to safe water in Pakistan. These contaminated water resources are a significant threat to Pakistan’s agrarian economy too, as elevated level of trace metals cause soil pollution, leading to bioaccumulation of potential carcinogens in agricultural products. Among different techniques available currently for the fast and accurate detection of trace metals in water, electrochemical sensing is the most attractive option due to quick analysis along with low operational and maintenance cost.  Performance of electroanalytical technique strongly depends on electrode material hence, synthesis of novel efficient electrode materials for robust, highly sensitive and selective detection of trace metal ions is very important. This proposed research project aims at employing nanocellulose, a natural polymer, as promising sensing platform. It is anticipated that functionalization of nanocellulose and integration with various metal/metal oxide nanoparticles will produce a highly conductive nanocomposite that could be applied for the fabrication of electrochemical sensor for the simultaneous detection of trace metal samples in water. It is expected that this green hybrid nano-architecture will result in fast electron transfer kinetics that will enhance the robustness and sensitivity of the sensor.
data.projectSummary: Trace metal contamination of surface and ground water resources from various anthropogenic sources is a serious environmental challenge for Pakistan. Due to absence of water quality testing and monitoring infrastructure together with limited financial resources, common people in Pakistan are facing serious problem in the availability of clean and safe water for drinking and domestic purposes. It is estimated that only 26.1% population has access to safe water in Pakistan. These contaminated water resources are a significant threat to Pakistan’s agrarian economy too, as elevated level of trace metals cause soil pollution, leading to bioaccumulation of potential carcinogens in agricultural products. Among different techniques available currently for the fast and accurate detection of trace metals in water, electrochemical sensing is the most attractive option due to quick analysis along with low operational and maintenance cost.  Performance of electroanalytical technique strongly depends on electrode material hence, synthesis of novel efficient electrode materials for robust, highly sensitive and selective detection of trace metal ions is very important. This proposed research project aims at employing nanocellulose, a natural polymer, as promising sensing platform. It is anticipated that functionalization of nanocellulose and integration with various metal/metal oxide nanoparticles will produce a highly conductive nanocomposite that could be applied for the fabrication of electrochemical sensor for the simultaneous detection of trace metal samples in water. It is expected that this green hybrid nano-architecture will result in fast electron transfer kinetics that will enhance the robustness and sensitivity of the sensor.

data.projectName: Microplasma synthesized metallic conductive ink for inkjet printer
data.projectDigest: Inkjet printing offer promising contribution in revolution of printed electronics industry. Size, dispersion and stability of nanoparticles play a critical role in conductive ink. Moreover, the physical properties of metallic/semiconductor nanoparticles effect the performance of product to a great extent. This project is completed in two steps. The formation of stable colloidal is completed in first step. The effectiveness of atmospheric microplasma electrochemistry is the most reliable, attractive, fast and environment-friendly as compared to other reported fabrication methods used for metallic/carbon nanostructures (NSs). A micro hollow capillary cathode was developed for the synthesis of NSs. The interaction of argon produced microplasma with the electrolytic solution will change the color within a few minutes, which is indicative of the production of NSs. It is possible to tune the size and size distribution of the NSs by controlling the processing parameters of the atmospheric microplasma-assisted electrochemical method. Finally, homogenous colloidal solution is converted into conductive ink by mixing it with co solvent.  This ink will be printed on polymer substrate utilizing inkjet printer. High quality conductive ink is useful in RFID antennas, flexible electronic devices and wearable devices, packing, tissue engineering, water filtration.

data.projectName: Synthesis and characterization of novel materials and its fabricated prototypes for 3D printed applications
data.projectDigest: 3D printing technology has same tendency of growth as that of internet in terms of impact. This technology is going to provide manufacturing approach to mass public as compared to conservative ways of manufacturing. This technology has paved its way in art, fashion, medicine and construction. Filament in 3d printing is counterpart as cartridges in conventional printers. Paper printers have used different cartridges with different properties for desired results. Similarly Filament properties can widen its use in different fields. For the moment, shortage in strength and limited functionality has caused to use 3D printed polymer products as conceptual prototypes rather than functional components in many fields.Therefore many researchers have diverted their attention towards developing printable polymer composites.This project proposes to combine novel materials into already used polymers to enhance conductive and magnetic properties of filaments and to utilize these materials for customized fused filament manufacturing for PLA/ABS 3D printing. These filaments will further be used as source in additive manufacturing. Fused filament fabrication (FFF) is additive manufacturing, which produces three-dimensional objects by adding one highly refined layer at a time. This process use extruded filament to produce layer by layer structure and each layer bonds to other layer of melted material. These two types of filament will be used in immense applications. Both types of filament are used in microwave devices and electric devices used in aerospace technology. This filament manufacturing will allow us to develop 3d structures of goal specific properties.

data.projectName: Forensic based intelligent black box system for car
data.projectDigest:
Like every airline which is equipped with a black box system that records its various activities and in case the airline crashes, the officials can find the cause of the crash and rectify the cause in future. The same concept we are applying in cars of the future. 
The purpose of the project is to make safety based system called Black Box System for cars to ensure human and vehicle safety and reduce the accidents by collecting data from environment and inside the car.
The black box system will do various tasks that is important for passengers and vehicle safety. The system will also reduce the risk of collision by measuring distance of the surrounding cars with the help of cameras and sensors and apply breaks automatically.
The Black Box will also record data on hard drive gathered from sensor and cameras which  will help Law & enforcement department & Insurance Companies to know cause of a particular accident. The video feed will also analyze whether the driver is feeling sleepy or not.
The Data from the system will be used by Automobile companies to build more safer vehicles.

data.projectName: Transition metal dichalcogenide nano-layers for wearable energy harvesting generators
data.projectDigest: Thermoelectric power generation system is a promising energy harvesting technology because of its eco-friendly and stable properties. With the recent growth in e-skins and wearable electronics, the use of self-powered DC supplier is imperative for the development of wearable devices. The basic idea of this project is to develop an intrinsically high stretchable and foldable thermoelectric power generator based on transition metal dichalcogenide (TMDC) nano-sheets (NSs) to harvest body heat. Recently, TMDC nano-sheets have gained substantial attention as a potential candidate for next generation electronic devices because of their 2D nanostructure, similar to graphene, which have very high young’s moduli and charge carrier mobilities as compared to layered-bulk materials. Ultra thermal conductivity and high seebeck coefficient are also reported for TMDC nano-sheets which are essential to determine the thermoelectricity of wearable devices. This project will consist of two parts. In the first part, a theoretical investigation of TMDC NSs will be done with density functional theory to understand deeply the electron interface nature between TMDC monolayers to increase the charge mobilities for energy conversion properties prior to fabrication. After getting the accurate structural information, we will encounter the major problem relating to the enhancement of sensing response to heat by modifying their surfaces. The second part of the project is to synthesize transition metal dichalcogenide nano-sheets to enhance the self-power of thermoelectric generators after device configuration and optimizing the material combinations. These synthesized TMDC NSs are expected to be capable of showing efficient performance due to their high ability of heat to electricity conversion

data.projectName: Development and evaluation of hydrogel based anticancer drug-loaded temperature dependent nanocargo system
data.projectDigest: Multi-responsive hydrogels, or ‘intelligent’ hydrogels that respond to more than one environmental stimulus, have demonstrated great utility as a regenerative biomaterial in recent years. They are structured biocompatible materials that provide specific and distinct responses to varied physiological or externally applied stimuli. As evidenced from the literature multi-responsive hydrogels are endowed with tunable, controllable and even biomimetic behavior well-suited for drug delivery and tissue engineering or regenerative growth applications. The instant research proposal is planned to investigate the developments and evaluation of hydrogel-based antitumor drug-loaded dual reverse thermos responsive nanoparticles and their applications to drug delivery of anti-cancer drugs to the targets. This novel system would result in enhanced bioavailability, abridged side effects and augmented antitumor efficiency of the loaded anticancer drugs.

data.projectName: Environmental and Industrial Safety: Real Time Smoke and Fire Detection Using Artificial Intelligence and Embedded Systems
data.projectDigest: The project will be a comprehensive research and development targeting the area of smoke and fire detection, which will aim at developing a reliable mechanism for smoke and fire detection under both indoor and outdoor environments. The project will focus on developing solution using both general purpose and embedded platform. The end solution be delivered in the form of a product that will provide features like image/video surveillance, smoke and fire identification in the images and videos, smoke and fire annotation in the scene and smoke and fire indication system. The objective of smoke and fire recognition framework is to detect, distinguish, and indicate alert for smoke and fires before it moves toward becoming wild by giving prior notice through sending message to the competent authority.

data.projectName: Targeting histone like DNA binding protein (HU) of Streptococcus pneumonia with structure-based inhibitors as a novel therapeutic option
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The Streptococcus pneumoniae nucleoid associated Heat Unstable protein (spnHU) is a small, basic DNA bending protein associated with the bacterial nucleoid. It plays a global role in DNA transactions in bacteria and participates in all DNA dependent functions that include DNA replication, gene regulation and recombination and DNA repair. HU introduces negative supercoils to the supercoiled DNA. HU protein deficient cells are reported to be defective in their growth as it is essential for maintaining the cell viability in S. pneumoniae. SpnHU also contributes to the pathogenicity of this organism and act as a virulence factor.  Despite knowing the importance of spnHU, there hasn’t been much work done on it. Our goal is to signpost spnHU as a probable target for the development of therapies against this virulent organism.  This study aimed at to analyze the interaction of spnHU protein with the structure based inhibitors. The selected inhibitor/s will be checked in laboratory to assess its effect on the growth of S. pneumoniae. Influence of the selected compound/s on the nucleoid structure of the test organism will be analyzed through fluorescence microscopy.  The effective compound/s can be use a drug to target S. pneumoniae and to treat infections caused by this organism

data.projectName: Novel Carbazole-Coumarin hybrids as efficient sensitizers for dye-sensitized solar cells: A combined experimental and computational study
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Dye sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) have gained much attention in current years attributed to their flexibility, low-cost, light-weight  and high efficiency as compared to the conventional inorganic solar cells. They have proven to be the best economical and sustainable power supply because solar energy is the most abundant form of renewable energy.
Keeping in mind extensive energy demand of Pakistan, present project has been designed. In Pakistan, every year more than 9% energy demand is increasing. Present project proposal focuses on computational DFT and experimental approaches to model novel coumarin, and carbazole dye-coumarin hybrids to be used as photosensitizers in DSSC to clarify the elementary processes involved in the working principles of DSSC. Synthesis, detailed spectroscopic, electrochemical and computational studies would be carried out on ten novel carbazol dyes, coumarines and their hybrids. Charge transfer from the donor side to the acceptor side upon excitation will be studied using experimental electrochemical, spectroscopic and computational DFT methods., It is expected newly synthesized carbazole azodye and their coumarin hybrids will have promising role as efficient photosensitizers with enhanced efficiency of DSSC to convert solar energy into electrical energy. Proposed project will have promising role to use photosensitizers with enhanced efficiency of DSSC

data.projectName: Rational Engineering of Microbial Protease for Thermostability
data.projectDigest: Enzymes are responsible to speed up the chemical reactions in the living systems by lowering the activation energy. Currently, there is an increase in the use of this biological catalyst in the various industries due to their advantages over conventional organic and metallic catalysts. The global industrial enzymes market is expected to be 6.3 billion US$ in 2020. Approximately, four thousand enzymes from various sources are characterized and reported in the scientific literature. Among them, the fractions of enzymes are currently used in various industries because all naturally occurring enzymes are not suitable for industrial applications. Usually, enzymes are marginally stable and are not compatible with harsh industrial conditions. This scenario demands the tailoring of enzymes using protein engineering tools to make them compatible for industrial applications. Proteases are one important industrial enzymes. The proteases are widely used in many industries, including therapeutics, detergent, feed, etc.  This research project aims to engineer the serine protease enzyme for high catalytic activity and thermal stability for industrial applications.

data.projectName: Adoptability screening, performance evaluation and commercial potential of Cholistan desert grasses as climate resilient fodder and silage crop
data.projectDigest:
The traditional forage sources only fulfills one third of the actual needs of the livestock in Pakistan. About half of the remaining requirements are being fulfilled by the crop residues and industrial by products. Cultivation of traditional fodders requires huge amounts of irrigation water, good quality land and high inputs. There is a dire need to explore for climate resilient new plant resources suiting to both irrigated and dry lands that may have very limited water and nutrient requirements and equally good for saline unproductive lands. Cholistan desert grasses have great potential to grow on deteriorated/saline lands with very little water and fertilizer requirements. 

This study will investigate the adoptability potential of Cholistan Desert grasses as a drought tolerant fodder and silage crops and will look for their comparative advantage over the traditional winter and summer fodders. These grasses are selected due to multiple aspects; perennial, fast growth, high biomass production, adapted to arid lands, good protein and mineral composition, multi-cutting, drought tolerance and climate resilience. This project is of applied nature which will involve R&D for optimizing desert grasses adoptability, sowing time and method, planting geometry, NPK requirements, irrigation scheduling, water use efficiency and cutting frequency under flooded and sprinkler irrigation systems. The study will also compare animal preference, nutritional composition, silage quality and rumen degradability of these grasses. Moreover, a detailed analysis will be performed to assess the commercial potential and constraints for adaptability of such valuable fodder crops among the farming community, ranchers, silage and seed producers.

data.projectName: Survey & Documentation of Gujrat District, Punjab, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Gujrat had been an important region since the ancient times. Located between the rivers Jhelum and Chenab, caught the attention of the great rulers who desired to control this region. Conquered by Mauryan, Indo-Greek, Indo-Scythian and Indo -Parthian and Kushan rulers respectively, it possesses a rich historical and archaeological worth. Khawas Khan, Sher Shah Suri’s governor of Rhotas founded Khawaspur near Gujrat. A fort was built by Mughal Emperor Akbar to control the Gujjars and named it as Gujrat. After the Mughals it passed in to the hands of Nadir Shah and then it was conquered by the Sikhs. The project aims to conduct a detailed archaeological survey of Gujrat District, Punjab since the region is not yet properly investigated. Located on a strategic location and proven by the ancient and medieval literary records, Gujrat District has a potential of the discovery of many unidentified archaeological sites. There are several unexplored mounds which can reveal a good deal of information leading to the reconstruction of Gujrat’s history and connecting the missing links. Few shrines of Muslim Saints also remain undocumented. Surveys and exploration will be carried out in all the three tehsils  (sub-divisions) of Gujrat district to investigate and document its tangible and intangible heritage.

data.projectName: Damage assessment of Reinforced concrete bridges using nonlinear behavior
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan, the highway infrastructure is developing rapidly by increasing number of reinforced concrete bridges. However, the current bridge health assessment methods are based on visual inspection and are inefficient and consume significant human and financial resources. Vibration-based damage assessment methods have proven effective and convenient in other fields, however due to inverse engineering problem, have not been able to make breakthrough in civil engineering. Inverse engineering problem arises when damage assessment is to be carried out on an existing structure and the data from its undamaged state is not available. The proposed research is aimed at developing and implementing a concrete material model in computational modeling that represents the structure accurately. The model will be analyzed from undamaged state to complete damaged state and the vibration characteristics, that are sensitive to damage, will be identified and, based on those vibration characteristics, a damage assessment method will be proposed while addressing the inverse engineering problem. After experimental validation, the proposed methodology will further be optimized by implementing on a reinforced concrete bridge to evaluate its current state and predict the remaining life of the structure.

data.projectName: Design and Development of Isotropic Antennas for Spectrum Sensing
data.projectDigest: The proposed project is aimed at the design and development of wide band isotropic antennas.  Isotropic antennas find applications in spectrum sensing, detection of unlawful transmission as well as energy harvesting, A common use case in all of these applications is that the receiver is unaware of the location of incoming signal as well as transmission frequency. Although there are techniques that exist for estimating the direction of arrival  but such techniques require complex signal processing algorithms as well as costly RF front end. During the course of this project, theoretical model for the design of isotropic antennas will be developed. Several antenna designs will be explored for maximisation of isotropy as well band width.

data.projectName: Chemo-therapeutic Effects of Berberine Alkaloid on Salmonella typhimurium and Salmonella enteritidis infections: A One Health Perspective
data.projectDigest:
Poultry serves a natural reservoir for Salmonella which can be infected through both vertical and horizontal transmission. Human salmonellosis has been widely reported to be linked to direct and indirect contact with poultry in terms of utilization of affected meat and eggs making this disease a rising public health concern from One Health perspective. For last few decades, various outbreaks of human salmonellosis linked to poultry exposure were reported with serious illnesses, hospitalizations and even deaths. However, an increasing antimicrobial resistance in Salmonella typhimirium and Salmonella enteritidis, the causative agents of typhoid and other gastro-intestinal problems are a great public health concern. The multidrug resistance in salmonella including Fluoroquinolones and ceftriaxone has been widely reported globally especially in Asian and African countries.
Berberine is an isquinoline alkaloid compound derived from many medicinal plants including turmeric, goldenseal, Oregon grape etc. In Chinese medicine, it has been extensively used as an anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial and anti-tumor agent. For last few years, its antibacterial activity has been reported as an alternative to antibiotic in various bacterial infections. Keeping in view One Health perspectives, this compound can be used for prevention and treatment purposes against Salmonella infections as an alternative approach in poultry and humans.

The multidrug resistance in salmonella including Fluoroquinolones and ceftriaxone has been widely reported globally especially in Asian and African countries.
Berberine is an isquinoline alkaloid compound derived from many medicinal plants including turmeric, goldenseal, Oregon grape etc. In Chinese medicine, it has been extensively used as an anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial and anti-tumor agent. For last few years, its antibacterial activity has been reported as an alternative to antibiotic in various bacterial infections. Keeping in view One Health perspectives, this compound can be used for prevention and treatment purposes against Salmonella infections as an alternative approach in poultry and humans.

data.projectName: Development of custom fit apparel and size prediction using three-dimensional (3D) scanning, modeling, and printing
data.projectDigest: In future, 3D technologies will bring a fundamental and revolutionary change in the global fashion supply chain. These technologies will be more widely used in near future but their technological awareness and application is almost nil in the apparel industry of Pakistan. This project has been planned to create awareness about usage of 3D technologies in Pakistani textile universities and industry. Project will perform size survey of Pakistani population using 3D body scanner to develop a standardized size chart that can be adopted by apparel industry. 3D scanning will be used to address various issues such as categorization of body shapes, body movement analysis, and reliability of 3D scanner measurements. In addition, 3D scanning, 3D CAD modeling, and 3D printing will be used to design, evaluate, and manufacture several apparel products. In addition, students will be trained for application of 3D technologies in the fashion industry. Furthermore, other possible applications of 3D technologies will be discovered. Moreover, sustainable and efficient 3D techniques will be compared to conventional less efficient garment making techniques. Results will provide many benefits such as creation of perfectly fit and customized products for Pakistani people, cost saving, labor saving, time saving, less wastage, and global competitiveness.

data.projectName: Dynamical Aspects of Fractional Differential Equations & Its Application in Highly Oscillatory Phenomena
data.projectDigest: This project will concern to the study of classes of nonlocal boundary value problems via topological degree method. We will investigate new classes under different conditions of nonlocal type and their system for positive results of their solutions. We will also construct new models of applied problems in physics, chemistry, biology, psychology and other disciplines and will study them through degree methods for positive solutions as well as explore qualitative aspects of these proposed models. Since nonlocal boundary value problems are arising in modeling of mechanics, signal and image processing phenomena etc. Therefore, we will develop and extend the known existing fixed-point theory to coincidence degree theory of topological type that relax the strict conditions of compactness to weak compactness and provide great information for well-posedness, and multiplicity of positive solution to nonlocal boundary value problems of nonlinear fractional order differential equations. Coincidence degree approach is an active mathematical tool for investigating existence results to nonlocal boundary value problems. Also the method becomes more powerful when coupled with the method of iterative technique of monotone type. The aforesaid techniques are used to develop conditions for approximating the solutions of systems of nonlocal fractional order differential equations. Therefore, we will apply the aforesaid technique to establish an iterative scheme for approximating the solutions for highly nonlinear system of non-integer order differential equation arising in the mathematical modeling of various phenomena of biology, physics, chemistry, ecology, etc. Since in modern nanotechnology, accuracy of experimental results is very important and for nonlinear phenomena.

data.projectName: Maximizing Gaming Effect in Virtual Reality: A Categorical Study of Players’ Affective Neuroscience
data.projectDigest: The primary aim of the proposed series of studies is to maximize Virtual Reality (VR) gaming effect and to minimize any potential side-effects of this new technology such as VR sickness (also called cybersickness). The planned experiments will categorically examine players’ motivational affordances, experiences, performance, and wellbeing throughout VR gameplay via a novel and innovative mix of real-time Electroencephalography (EEG) recording and questionnaire-based feedback. This systematic investigation will reveal important insights about the neural and psychological mechanisms under the intense VR environment that impel personality, emotion, and mood of the players and will allow the identification of VR game scenarios that are more provocative in terms of inducing VR sickness. The conclusions derived via the proposed studies will contribute substantially to the field of affective neuroscience and will have substantial implications for the development of more effective, safer, and yet entertaining treatments for the range of medical and psychological problems.

data.projectName: Exploring Epiproteomic Crosstalk in Oral Carcinomas under Tumor Microenvironment and Targeting with Epigenetic Drugs for Therapeutics
data.projectDigest: This project will focus on the proteomic analysis of changes in histone PTMs, also termed as epiproteomics, to reveal the epigenetic crosstalk between hypoxic and acidic microenvironment and OSCC progression. The studies will employ oral carcinoma cell lines cultured with TME conditions compared to normoxic conditions and will constitute three steps. 1) Epiproteomic investigations using advanced mass spectrometric tools to evaluate the impact of TME on epigenetic landscape i.e. patterns in histone PTMs. 2) To explore the effect of TME in combinations with administered epigenetic drugs on the histone PTMs levels. 3) Effect of targeted therapies such as nano-liposomal formulations of epigenetic drugs in combination with TME on the epigenetic landscape will also be studied using the above-mentioned strategy. The proposed study could pinpoint novel insight into a mechanistic understanding of oral carcinoma, drug resistance and epigenetic approaches utilizing nanocarriers in cancer therapies to combat the cancer resistance.

data.projectName: Nanoparticles: From Synthesis to Application as Burning Rate Catalysts
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest: To overcome force of gravity and to ?y in sky, several techniques have been used, such as ?re balloons, planes, rockets, missiles, etc. Among these, rockets are fastest way to conquer force of gravity. One of the important components that provide driving force to the rocket is the propellant. The propellants are the energy sources, which are used in rocket motors for the propulsion of launch vehicles. Burning rate catalyst shows a ballistic nature in the propellants, increases burning characters and eliminates primary smoke propellant. In general, there are several kinds of BRCs, such as nanometal particles, transition metal oxides, metal chelates, ferrocene-based polymers, dendrimers, compounds, etc. Among different BRCs, nanoparticles are easy to synthesize, cost effective and have larger surface area. The simple ferrocene-based BRCs show intrinsic disadvantages such as migration to the surface of the propellant on long-time storage and sublimation or evaporation loss during processing. Various scientists have tried to overcome the migration problems of the BRCs and to increase burning rate of the AP-based propellant, but till now, migration problems of BRCs have not completely overcome. In this scenario, the nanoparticles can be synthesized to enhance burning rate of the propellant and to overcome migration problems.

data.projectName: Agronomic managements to enhance fertilizer use efficiency for sustainable wheat production
data.projectDigest: Wheat is staple food in Pakistan. Under current scenario of urbanization, there is need to produce more food from less area under cultivation. Food security of increased population is only possible with judicious and wise use of available resources for crop production. This can only possible through precision agriculture. Use of synthetic fertilizer is one of the methods used to raise the crop production but actually the fertilizer use efficiency is quite low in field crops. On the other hand, adverse climatic conditions during the wheat growing season in Pakistan is further making it difficult to enhance the nutrient use efficiency. Most of the wheat farmers in Pakistan have small land holding with low fertilizer application for wheat production. If some using fertilizer, they don't know the exact time of application. In precision agriculture, "3R" management technique is important to enhance the fertilizer use efficiency. 3R means application of fertilizer in Right amount, at Right place at Right time, that will enhance its efficiency to be transformed in the production. Among the nutrients, Nitrogen is most important nutrient to be managed properly to enhance the yield and quality of wheat for its sustainable production in Punjab-Pakistan.

data.projectName: Use of different biosorbents loaded with nanoparticles for sequestration of dyes from  wastewater
data.projectDigest: Treatment of effluents in the textile industry is one of the most significant environmental problems. The total dye consumption in the textile industry worldwide is more than 10,000 tonnes/year and approximately 100 tonnes/year of dyes is discharged into water bodies. Latest and promising strategy is to use nanoparticles for removal of contaminants from aqueous systems but there are few issues in direct use of nanoparticles e.g. aggregation and stabilization of the particles. Therefore, the present study would be the first attempt to prepare biosorbents assisted with nanoparticles of Mg-oxide, Mn-oxide and Fe-oxide and use these materials for remediation of dyes contaminated wastewater thereby reducing the problem of particles stabilization. The present study will evaluate the potential of Trianthema portulacastrum and Tribulus terrestris at batch and column scale by doping with different doses of nanoparticles of Mg-oxide, Mn-oxide and Fe-oxide at various loading rates of biosorbent as well, initial concentration of dyes, time and pH. The synthesized composite materials will be characterized using FTIR, SEM and EDX. In addition to aforementioned experiments, few column scale experiments will also be conducted by collecting wastewater samples from textile industry located in Faisalabad. The experimental results will be validated with kinetic and equilibrium models.

data.projectName: Biodegradation of Plastic
data.projectDigest:
The assessment of biodegradable nature of plastic can be done by performing the
measurement of structural changes by microscope observation or by evaluating the growth of
microorganism after the biological and enzymatic action along with the evolution of carbon
dioxide (Kissi et al., 2001). Plastics are of numerous kinds such as polyethylene (PE),
polypropylene (PP), poly (vinyl chloride) (PVC), polystyrene (PS), poly (ethylene terephthalate)
(PET) and polyurethane (PU) (Gewert et al., 2015). Plastic polymers basically comprise of
hydrocarbon monomers created by natural and synthetic organic and inorganic raw material
(Suaria et al., 2016). The plastic is formed by poly addition and poly condensation process,
termed as polymerization (Thomas et al., 2015). Generally, there are two main kinds of plastic
i.e. thermoplastics and thermoset plastics (Suaria et al., 2016). Thermoplastics are long linear
carbon chains, having different molecules which are joined end to ends. Among different kinds
of plastics, the micro plastic is more dangerous (Cole et al., 2011) as it is difficult to identify and
tracked (Wright et al., 2013) and is accumulating inside the body of different organisms causing
severe anomalies resulting visible decline in abundance and diversity of fish and coastal birds
(Andrady, 2011).

data.projectName: An Investigation into Digital Identity Construction of English Language Faculty in Higher Education of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: As we are far behind in the cutting-edge area of technology, the slogan of the present government is “Digital Pakistan” which aims at putting digital skills at the heart of the entire education landscape, internship and apprenticeship to revolutionize the entire perspective of the country. In this context, this study will illustrate the identity construction of English language faculty in the digital age through their pedagogical beliefs, class room practices, the challenges and the effects of using digital tools in the class room. Thus, the research will also explore whether the pedagogical beliefs align with class room practices and the contextual reasons behind their beliefs and practices. Twenty-four Pakistani universities are the sample of this study and the data will be collected through primary source i.e. questionnaire, class room observation and interviews. Based upon the results, the researchers would suggest an appropriate course of action which will help in formulating suitable policy regarding usage of latest technology in English language class rooms.

data.projectName: CRISPR/Cas9 based strategies to control Chickpea Chlorotic Dwarf Virus  of tomato in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Chickpea Chlorotic Dwarf Virus is the emerging issue in the modern agriculture. Tomato has been reported as a new host to Chickpea Chlorotic Dwarf Virus in Pakistan. It can damage tomato crop from 75% to 95% once strikes. Development of strong approaches/strategies to control this notorious Chickpea Chlorotic Dwarf Virus before its outbreak in Pakistan is the need of time. This study is focused to control Chickpea Chlorotic Dwarf Virus by application of state of art technology CRISPR/Cas9 based approach against conserved regions of different genes responsible for different virus activities. For this purpose, a twenty base pair sequence called protospacer will be designed from the different regions of the virus having NGG. The best protospacer will be selected through agro-infiltration screening of CRISPR/Cas9 based constructs in tomato plant followed by agro-infiltration of infectious clone of CpCDV.  Molecular analysis will be performed to determine the viral titer in plants which have already been agro-infiltrated by CRISPR/Cas9 construct and will be compared with control plants. The selected protospacer will then be stably transformed in tomato through Agrobacterium mediated transformation. Putative transgenic tomato plants will be studied in T0 generations by using different molecular techniques for confirmation of successful introduction of sgRNA into plants and determination of its knockout efficacy. Technically, the knockout will result in interference with its replication inside the plants. The successful outcome of this study can be a step ahead to be utilized for the control of Geminiviruses in future.

data.projectName: Experimental and analytical seismic assessment of RC shear walls
data.projectDigest:
Recent disastrous earthquakes reveal the vulnerability of the existing reinforced concrete (RC) buildings in Pakistan. The increased level of awareness about possible seismic hazard raises serious concerns about the structural performance of RC buildings in Pakistan. Therefore, it is necessary to conduct experimental studies of primary earthquake resistant structural elements, such as RC columns and RC Walls.
As a preliminary inquiry, a detailed survey was conducted in Rawalpindi/Islamabad (zone-2B) to collect the data of existing buildings. The collected data was analyzed and scale-down models are selected of RC walls representing the current practices in Islamabad and Rawalpindi region. 
The proposed experimental program includes 20 RC walls scale down models specifications similar to the existing RC walls buildings in Rawalpindi and Islamabad region will be tested. Qusai-static test will be existing RC walls to assess their seismic performance. Based on the experimental results, finite element models of existing RC walls will be developed.
This project aims to address the deficiencies in the current construction practices and in lab experimental data, which will not only enhance our understanding about the expected structural performance of structures but also will provide the experimental data necessary for improvement in Pakistan building code.

data.projectName: Cord Blood Mesenchymal Stem Cells Derived Chondrocytes for Cartilage Regeneration: Cell therapy for Osteoarthritis
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
The injuries affecting the articular cartilage result in significant musculo- skeletal morbidity both in elderly and young patients. The restoration of this damage from joint injuries has always been a great challenge since it cannot regenerate spontaneously; moreover, over a period of time it can also lead to the development of osteoarthritis which is a prevalent disease affecting many mammalian species and has shown to have a significant burden on welfare and economy in affected individuals and populations. In vitro models of osteoarthritis are essential to facilitate research into disease parthenogenesis, and the subsequent design of potential therapeutic targets. Articular cartilage cannot repair itself so it is clinically needed that to recognize new treatment strategies to delay process of osteoarthritis. It has been suggested that targeting inflammatory pathways could be a good option in treatment of osteoarthritis.
The proposed study aims at isolating mesenchymal stem cells from the umbilical cord blood sample received after delivery followed by in vitro expansion of mesenchymal stem cells and their differentiation towards chondrocytes. These chondrocytes will be exposed to inflammatory stress thus mimicking osteoarthritic invitro model and identifying potential therapeutic targets along with Cartilage tissue engineering using 3D culture in Plasma lysate scaffolds.

These chondrocytes will be exposed to inflammatory stress thus mimicking osteoarthritic invitro model and identifying potential therapeutic targets along with Cartilage tissue engineering using 3D culture in Plasma lysate scaffolds.

data.projectName: Circular Economy for Plastic and the Future of 3D Printing in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Plastic accounts for 10% of the global pollution, and it continues to increase with years going by. As result the environmental challenges are upscaling drastically and at the same time the regarding manufacturing industry faces indirect losses with the discarded materials going to waste, which could have been otherwise reused. This adverse pattern continues to trend upwards, being attributed to the linear consumption practices that aim to design products for one life cycle only and discard them into landfills at the end of their use. On the contrary circular economy encourages the revamping of the whole design and development process, so that more and more efficiency and effectiveness could be brought into the finished products. Moreover, the said approach promotes the utilization of lesser materials during the product development and also ensure their reusability at the end of their lifecycle. Considering the essentiality of the circular economy practices, the current research project aims to explore the plastic consumption trends of the industrial sector across Pakistan, measure its alignment towards the globally recognized circular economy practices and further evaluate its respective feasibility in the 3D printing industry. To accomplish the feat the current research will take into account the size of the organization, its product distribution scope, as well as the types of products it produces. To determine the manufacturing trends of the plastic industry the criterions will include aspects like utilization of recyclable material, types of manufacturing processes, energy resources used and the magnitude of production level. Further to evaluate the circular sustainability aspect of the industry the regarding manufacturers will be assessed upon the amount of recycle

data.projectName: Genome-wide Identification and Functional Analysis of circular RNAs in Benign and Malignant Breast Tumors
data.projectDigest: Breast cancer (BC) is one of the most reported type of cancers worldwide. Pakistani women are considered at high-risk for BC due to significantly higher incidence and mortality rates. BC is highly heterogeneous in nature and difficult to manage at advanced stages. Therefore, in-depth understanding of molecular mechanisms contributing towards pathogenesis of BC remains essential. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are non-coding RNAs that form a closed loop structure due to back-splicing of pre-mRNA molecules. Advancements in sequencing technologies have led to re-identification and functional characterization of these unique class of RNAs as “sponges or decoys” for microRNAs and proteins. circRNAs are stable, abundantly expressed, exhibit tissue specificity and regulate gene expression in several diseases including cancers. The in-depth information on expression and involvement of circRNAs in BC pathogenesis remains largely unknown. The aim of present study is to address this gap by performing RNA-seq based expression profiling of circRNAs in benign and malignant breast tumor tissues for the identification of tumor-specific expression patterns and to understand the involvement of circRNAs in development of BC. It is expected that findings of present study will assist in setting path towards the development of novel circRNA-based therapeutic and diagnostic candidates in near future.

data.projectName: Serological survey, Genetic Analysis and Risk factors of Human and Animal Fascioliasis in selected districts of Punjab, Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Government College for Women University, Sialkot
data.projectDigest: Background: Fascioliasis is an important world widely distributed parasitic disease caused by Fasciola gigantica and F. hepatica. Its prevalent in animal and humans as well. Fascioliasis is considered as one of the neglected tropical diseases. Animal fascioliasis caused by F. gigantica and F. hepatica is reported from all four provinces i.e., Punjab, Sindh, Baluchistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhawa past. These studies are usually based on coprological surveys. Identification of Fasciola sp. is also mainly based on morphometry of either eggs or phenotypic analysis of adult worms. Punjab Province of Pakistan is an agriculture area where sheep, goat, buffalo and cattle are also raised. Rice is an important crop cultivated in Punjab. Rice fields provide habitat for freshwater snails growth which act as intermediate host of Fasciola sp. Human fascioliasis is a neglected parasitic disease and much attention is not given to it in Pakistan. Only two reports are published on human fascioliasis from Punjab. Serological survey, knowledge of risk factors of the infection in human and animals, and role of intermediate host is necessary to address in Pakistan. This study is designed to assess the prevalence and incidence of human and animal fascioliasis through serological survey, relation between human and animal fascioliasis, genetic characterization of causative agent, and intermediate snail host and assessment of associated risk factors in some districts having agricultural importance, of Punjab Province. Hypothesis: We are expecting very high prevalence of animal and human fasciolosis in study area due to agricultural land, climate change and human activities. Moreover, canal system for irrigation providing habitat for intermediate snail host for maintaining life-cycle of Fasciola sp.

data.projectName: Computational Modelling and Simulation of Nano Fluids
data.projectDigest:
The aim of this research project is to study the the generalized mathematical
models of nanofluids with various rheological
aspects including heat source/sink, suction and injection phenomenon,
magnetohydrodynamics, nano particles thermal-diffusion and diffusion-thermo
effects. The resulting partial differential equations are reduced into a system of
nonlinear ordinary differential equations using appropriate transformations. The
convergent expressions of the velocity, temperature and concentration
expressions are derived. Numerical values for local skin friction coefficient,
Local Nusselt and Sherwood numbers are obtained and discussed. A
comparative study between the present and previous results is made in a
limiting sense. The manpower trained shall be an asset for further research in
this area. The found results will be useful for engineers and scientists.

data.projectName: Design, Development and Testing of Guidance and Control algorithm of small satellites by using micro thrusters
data.projectDigest: Satellites are sent to orbit around earth for different applications. A satellite could function as per desired mission profile if there is no disturbance in the space. But there are many sources of disturbances in space which can change path and orientation of satellites, like effect of gravity, drag due to atmosphere, environmental effects, shape of earth and path of satellite around earth etc. To overcome disturbances induced by different sources, correction has to be made frequently for which certain algorithms and actuation mechanism are required. The algorithms which are known as guidance and control algorithms are designed in such a way that satellites do not lose its track and keep the desired orientation. To achieve this task, external force has to be exerted which is provided by thrusters. The thrusters have to be small with light weight. The proposed project is about design, development and validation of guidance and control schemes and micro-thrusters. For validation purpose testing platform will also be designed and developed. Furthermore, to simulate space environment, a simulator which can simulate actual environment of satellite orbiting around earth will be developed. And complete system will be tested by using developed simulator and testing platform.

data.projectName: Development of novel biopesticide formulations for the control of dengue vector mosquitoes
data.projectDigest: Mosquitoes are vectors of a wide range of diseases including malaria, chikungunya, and dengue. Dengue is the fastest emerging disease in Pakistan affecting health of people and national economy. Since, no vaccine is available to cure dengue virus, dengue control relies on control of mosquitoes with chemical insecticides, however, indiscriminate use of chemicals has resulted in development of resistance in mosquitoes this making then ineffective. Furthermore, chemical insecticides pose serious health risks to humans, cause environmental pollution and contaminate ground water. The present project is being proposed as ecofriendly alternative of chemicals utilizing entomopathogic fungi to control insect resistant populations of mosquitoes. The aims of project are (1) to improve production methods to reduce cost of these microbes, (2) to develop formulations that enhance shelf life and field efficacy, (3) develop lures which improve monitoring to allow for more targeted control and (4) use adult attractants to lure the pest to the control agent i.e. lure & kill” which will reduce cost and be more target specific, (5) dissemination and outreach activities.. The goals of this project will be achieved by a consortium consisting of a multidisciplinary team of UK-Pakistan researchers and other pertinent stakeholders

data.projectName: Utilization of locally produced fly ash in geopolymer concrete: An eco-friendly solution for future construction
data.projectDigest: The temperature of the planet Earth is rising due to global warming. One of the main causes of global warming are carbon dioxide gas emissions. The concrete is the second most used material in the world. The cement is the main constituent of concrete and widespread use of cement in construction industry is one of the major source of carbon dioxide emissions. In Pakistan under CPEC project, numerous coal power plants are established to generate electricity and Sahiwal Coal Power Plant is one such power plant which produces fly ash as a by-product. The disposal off large quantities of fly ash is expensive as land filling is not a viable solution. Fly ash has cementitious properties. In this research, cement will be hundred percent replaced with fly ash to develop concrete known as geopolymer concrete. In this research, the geopolymer concrete mix with 4000 psi target compressive strength will be developed. The structural performance of geopolymer concrete will also be investigated. The goal is to develop the locally produced fly ash based geopolymer concrete for Naya Pakistan Housing Scheme Project, a mega project to provide low priced homes to middle and lower middle-class citizens all over Pakistan.

data.projectName: URDU TURKEY LINGUISTICS RELATION
data.piUniversity: Sarhad University of Science and Information Technology, Peshawar
data.projectDigest:
Linguistics is the scientific study of human language. Language is that source of expression without which a man cannot progress in the field of Science, Law, Economics, Culture, Traditions and Literature. One needs language for personal as well as for social life.
The subject work aims at finding out whether similar terms analyzed here are loanwords that Urdu and Turkish have borrowed from other languages or they are cognates. Furthermore, the study will undertake a comparative analysis from lexical, etymological, and semantic aspects.
	The fact is true about Turkish language. Urdu language not only contains borrowed from Turkish language, but also Proverbs, Idioms, Metaphors and Similes; the Phonetics Phonology, Morphology, Semantics Pragmatics, Syntax, of both languages is surprisingly similar.
	Culture, traditionally and conceptually Turkish and Urdu languages are related to each other. Through Turkish and Urdu languages transcend from two different language families, yet Turkish language has played a vital role in the development of Urdu language; Even the very name of the language, Urdu is a word of Turkish origin that originates from the word “Ordu”, means army. This word is still in common parlance in Turkish language such as Ordug h and Orduevi).

data.projectName: Association of genetic polymorphism with poor prognosis in Cyclophosphamide-treated breast cancer patients
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed cancer in womens but is very rarely observed to occur in men. In Asia, Pakistan has the largest rate of breast cancer. It is the second leading cause of death among women. Total of 83,000 cases are being annually reported in our country, and over 40,000 deaths are caused by it, which is alarming. 1 in every 9 Pakistani women develops breast cancer at some stage of her life. The age-related incidence rate of breast cancer affecting Pakistani females is almost 50.1/100,000 per year. The lack of a national cancer registry in Pakistan is the main reason of low quality incidence, mortality and prevalence data for the country. According to facility- based studies and projections, the number of new cases is estimated between 34,038 and 90,000 cases and mortality around 16,232 deaths in 2017. Findings of our study are likely to shed light on the currently obscure mechanism(s) of observed variation in the clinical response and efficacy to Cyclophosphamide in Breast Cancer patients. Furthermore, our study can explore whether investigated SNPs in target genes are among genetic risk factors for failure to response and toxicity during Breast Cancer treatment with Cyclophosphamide.

data.projectName: Modeling Heat and Mass Transport in Membrane Distillation Process for  Desalination Application
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Membrane systems are extensively used for water treatment and other separation processes. The common problems in the membrane distillation processes are concentration / temperature polarization and membrane fouling which greatly affects the lifetime of membrane elements. A method to reduce these problems is to use turbulence promoters such as spacers or baffles. These components adjust the fluid flow direction and promote turbulence and mixing of the particles accumulated at the membrane with the bulk stream. The dimensions of the spacer / baffle such as thickness, height and inclination and its orientation are important parameters which can greatly affect the membrane efficiency.
In the proposed work, thermal and flow modeling will be carried out for the membrane distillation modules.  The modeling work will identify effects of various operating conditions such as pressure, mass flow rate and membrane characteristics.  The governing equations for flow simulations will be solved through commercial CFD codes. The fluid flow and concentration profiles in rectangular / cylindrical channel will be analyzed and the effect of baffle dimensions on membrane performance will be examined. The study is expected to indicate optimal dimensions of baffle for membrane process. Numerical predictions will be validated through experimental results.

data.projectName: Artificial Intelligence (AI) based non-intrusive load monitoring for IoT-based energy management system
data.projectDigest: In developing countries like Pakistan, energy demand and economic growth share a tight bond. Therefore, any rise in electricity prices affects the economic activity of both domestic and commercial consumers. Consequently, the private and public sectors in Pakistan are always interested to invest in energy management projects. The objective of this proposal is to develop a real-time Artificial Intelligence (AI) based non-intrusive load monitoring for IoT-based energy management system. The proposed system will provide a real-time energy management solution for domestic and commercial/industrial consumers, owing to its ability to automatically detect and control the electrical appliances using machine learning techniques and gives itemized information of power consumption.  The proposed system provides the real-time control and monitoring system to (i) better manage the energy consumption with AI-based NLM module, (ii) enables consumers/operators to predict equipment faults, (iii) scheduling and switching on/off electrical appliances using IoT-based control system (iv) enables data logging for transparent billing, (v) enable performance evaluation of electrical appliances (vi) provides a low-cost energy-saving solution to the residential, commercial, and industrial consumers. The proposed system will not only reduce the utility cost across the board but will also provide a standardized road map to advance sustainable energy efficiency in the industry as well as other sectors in Pakistan. There is a great market need for such an energy management system in Pakistan as there are very limited methodologies available to analyze the comprehensive cost-benefit analysis based on the energy management system.

data.projectName: Nano-encapsulation for targeted delivery of chemotherapeutics
data.projectDigest: Cancer is among the major causes of mortality across the globe. The main hurdle in the targeted drug delivery of chemotherapeutics is the cancer metastasis and constantly changing expression signatures of the cancer cells. Moreover, in certain types of tumors, almost 80% of tumor mass consists of stromal cells. Hence it is important to design drug formulations which can selectively target the cancer cells in the complex milieu of tumor, fibroblasts and macrophage cells. We aim to develop a nano-vehicle incorporating anti-cancer drugs inside their cavities while labelled with tumor targeting ligands and immune suppressing moieties on their outermost walls. Hence, the anti-cancer drugs can be targeted to the tumor cells without disrupting majority of healthy cells surrounding the tumor. After in vitro evaluation of their localization and toxicity profile in cancer cell lines, the optimized formulations will be tested for their in vivo efficacy in animal (mice) models of disease. The design of the proposed nano-vehicles will help to explore the new frontiers in the field of nano-medicine and set a milestone in future disease diagnosis and treatment. The cost effectiveness of this nano-drug delivery system will also bring economic benefits to our country.

data.projectName: Flexible, binder free and high voltage modified textile fabric supercapacitor as a harmless wearable electronic device
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest:
The smart and portable electronic market has grown rapidly owing to the expanding needs for wearable energy storage devices such as smart watch, and wireless ear buds etc. The advancement of such electronics includes smart designing, light weight and toxic free plans to improve the ease of wearing on the human body. But in general practice, the conventionally available batteries are expensive, heavy and assembled with toxic materials (electrolytes) which would constrain the progress of next?generation wearable electronics. Keeping in view all the above perspectives, this project can be summarized in a single line as: fabrication of low cost, lightweight, and harmless wearable energy storage devices by structural modifications of textile fabrics. The potential applications of this research could be for personal health care and safe electrodes in wearable energy storage devices.
We proposed a simple strategy for the value-addition of widely used and economically feasible textile fabrics by a single step CVD process, leading to the structural modifications using active materials via simple chemical methods to explore different morphologies to obtain efficient energy storage devices with safe and harmless salt electrolytes. In addition, the proposed wearable device is also planned to be commercialize with the help of collaborators.
data.projectSummary:
The smart and portable electronic market has grown rapidly owing to the expanding needs for wearable energy storage devices such as smart watch, and wireless ear buds etc. The advancement of such electronics includes smart designing, light weight and toxic free plans to improve the ease of wearing on the human body. But in general practice, the conventionally available batteries are expensive, heavy and assembled with toxic materials (electrolytes) which would constrain the progress of next?generation wearable electronics. Keeping in view all the above perspectives, this project can be summarized in a single line as: fabrication of low cost, lightweight, and harmless wearable energy storage devices by structural modifications of textile fabrics. The potential applications of this research could be for personal health care and safe electrodes in wearable energy storage devices.
We proposed a simple strategy for the value-addition of widely used and economically feasible textile fabrics by a single step CVD process, leading to the structural modifications using active materials via simple chemical methods to explore different morphologies to obtain efficient energy storage devices with safe and harmless salt electrolytes. In addition, the proposed wearable device is also planned to be commercialize with the help of collaborators.

data.projectName: Plasma peptidome profile of Childhood Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia with its association to Prognostic factors
data.projectDigest: Human plasma has myriad of proteins and peptides that differ in health and disease. As normal cells evolve into tumor cells, their genetic transformation produce proteins that vary from their normal counterparts. These tumor-specific proteins are released into circulation and undergo proteolytic digestion, yielding low molecular weight (LMW) peptides. Hence, these peptides might have an unexplored archive of tumorigenesis and expect to yield potential biomarkers for initiation, progression and metastasis of disease. Peptidomics is defined as the quantitative and qualitative analysis of endogenous peptides in biological samples. Few studies done on solid tumors e.g.  cancer of breast, pancreas, colon, cervix using biological samples and cell lines, have identified tumour specific peptides that can have diagnostic and therapeutic implications.  Similarly, the role of peptidomics in acute childhood leukemia (ALL) is explored in few studies only, however on limited samples and mostly cell lines. As Mass spectrometry, (MS) platforms have become faster and sensitive, high-throughput strategies and bioinformatics tools have boosted the profiling of native peptides in human fluids and the identification of the potential associated proteases envisioning its applicability for clinical purpose. Therefore, it is needful to identify Leukemia specific peptides and associate them with prognostic factors of ALL.

data.projectName: Synthesis and single crystal study and anticancer activities of Cu(II) and Zn(II) coordination complexes of 4,6-dipyridyl-2-phenylpyrimidine
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Cancer is one of the fatal diseases with the leading cause of moralities in humans all over the world. Over the several decades, different metal complexes have been identified for the treatment of cancer therapy. The studies on the cisplatin revealed some side effects and acquired resistance over prolonged treatment. Therefore, investigation of novel, efficient, and cost effective chemotherapeutic agents has always been a subject of interest. For that reason, several other metal complexes such as Ru, Zn, Fe, Au, Co, and Cu attained much attention for their chemotherapeutic activities. Cu and Zn based complexes have been explored as potential anticancer agents. In the current project, we will focus on the anti-cancer activity and mechanisms of actions of copper and Zinc based complexes. The project completion will involve the activities of compound synthesis, cell culture, treatment, RNA and protein genes levels, cell migration and invasion assays, anti-cancer morphology and apoptosis analysis. Overall this research work will contribute towards the discovery of novel anti-cancer drugs with minimal side-effects and low cost for cancer patients. Moreover, this research will provide a platform for pharmaceutical industries in Pakistan for large-scale production and commercialization of new drugs, after clinical trials.

data.projectName: "Diagnostic Tool Kit" development to identify Bacterial Blight resistance in Pakistani Rice accessions
data.projectDigest:
Indigenous Development of “Diagnostic Toolkit” to identify Bacterial Blight-resistance in Pakistani Rice accessions
The bacterial Blight (BB) pathogen of rice has evolved a virulent strategy to turn on a specific class of susceptibility genes in rice known as SWEET genes family by injecting its special weapons known as transcription activator like effectors (TALes). TALe weapons are basically engine “drivers” of the pathogen which when injected into host cell by the pathogen, bind/adjust to promoters, the “engine” of SWEET gene(s). Binding/adjustment drives induction of the SWEET genes on, making the host susceptible to the disease. Certain accessions of rice have mutated/modified their SWEET gene “engines” due to which TALes, the “drivers” cannot bind/adjust to the “modified” engine, and thus cannot drive the SWEET genes on, making the host resistant.

             The proposed project will hunt for such accessions among Pakistani rice 
collection using pathogenicity, gene expression and gene sequencing approaches. Rice accessions will be challenged with Pakistani BB strains and observed for disease or resistance symptoms. Resistant accessions will be confirmed by RNA induction of the candidate SWEET genes through RT-qPCR to quantify the magnitude of induction. Promoters, the “engines” of the candidate SWEET genes, will also be studied for sequencing to know the nature of mutation/ “modification” evolved therein. The validated resistant accessions will be put on field trials and recommended to concerned departments.

data.projectName: Sequential and Simultaneous Adsorption of Mixed Dyes using Organoclays: Sorptive Capacity, kinetics, and Mechanism
data.projectDigest:
The Textile industry is the largest manufacturing industry in Pakistan, Pakistan is the 8th largest exporter of textile commodities in Asia and the 4th largest producer of cotton with the third largest spinning capacity in Asia after China and India. At present, there are 1,221 ginning units, 442 spinning units, 124 large spinning units and 425 small units which produce textile. 
Treatment Methods for Dyes Removal from Textile Industry Wastewater Physical, Oxidative and Biological In spite of the greater success stories by these conventional methods, key issues like regeneration/ reusing ability of adsorbent, cost and lower sorption capacity in multiple pollutant systems are still the main concern that halt their use in the treatment process.
Aim of the research is to study the potential of different domestic materials; clays including bentonite, Smectite and Montmorillonite for the removal of Dyes from locally situated Textile Industry wastewater. 
Objectives of the research can be explaining as the following Synthesis of organoclays with different long and short chain cationic surfactants and characterize them with SEM, FTIR and TOC. Investigation of the sorption capacity of synthesize organoclays in Sequential and simultaneous dye pollutant system. Regeneration of Spent Organoclays. Evaluation of Reaction Rate Kinetics under different conditions such as Temperature, pH, Flow Rate, Amount of Adsorbate and Concentration of Adsorbent.  
Novelty – innovation / new work In Pakistan this will be the first study in which organoclay is being used for the treatment of wastewater as dye pollutant sorbent and the textile dyes which we are using have never been reported before, for sequential and simultaneous study of dyes.

data.projectName: Studies of Clupeidae Fish Brain in Numbers (FiBraN) of Tenualosa ilisha and T. toli
data.projectDigest:
The present project aims to apply for the first time the technique isotropic fractionator (Hercoulano-Houzel and Lent, 2005), which allows to evaluate the number of neurons, neuron density and glia/neuron ratio in a given nervous structure, to the brain of fish. That relatively new technique has been developed in 2005 and, since then, it has been used mainly in mammals, some birds and one reptile species. Only the olfactory bulb of one bony fish species (Ferrando et al., 2019) and two cartilaginous fish species (Aicardi et al., submitted) were analyzed to date by isotropic fractionator, demonstrating that the technique is usable in fish too and making up the base for the present project.
How phylogenetic and ecologic signals can affect the brain size and allometry in fish is still unclear. Investigating the number of neurons, neuron density and glia/neuron ratio together with mass, instead of considering barely the mass of brain and brain regions, is expected to provide new information to the discussion about brain evolution and plasticity in fish. 
In the present project, two species of the same genus of Clupeidae fish have been chosen because of their suitable ecological features. In particular, the selected species are the two congeneric Tenualosa ilisha and T. toli, respectively anadromous and marine.
Quantitative data will be obtained for adult males and females of these species, in different moment of the reproductive cycle. The brains will not be analyzed as a whole. Different regions will be evaluated separately instead, allowing to functionally interpreting the data, considering the known main function for each brain region, as reported by Edmunds et al. (2016).

data.projectName: Marker assisted breeding and gene mapping for early maturity and peg biology in peanut (Arachis hypogaea L.)
data.piUniversity: University of Kotli Azad Jammu and Kashmir
data.projectDigest:
Peanut (Arachis hypogaea), is the one of world’s most important legume and oilseed crop due to its high nutritive and economic values. In rainfed areas of Pakistan it is the only cash crop with immense economic importance, while due to change in the pattern of sowing to avoid the drought spell during flowering, farming community is facing yield  losses.  The proposal is designed to reduce the yield losses, by introducing early maturing varieties with better peg physiology. The proposed research is aimed to screen the early maturing exotic lines (USDA) and hybridize with the local high yielding varieties to produce F1 with short life span. Moreover, pegs biology on the basis of peg morphology, including peg length, width, peg hair and SEM analysis at different stages from peg emergence to peg penetration, pods formation will be studied.
Genomic analysis of early maturity and peg biology associated attributes: like flowering time, gravitropism and auxin hormone biosynthesis genes would be done for a comprehensive mapping based on molecular marker study. The selected genes after amplification will be sequenced and reported in the data base. This research will provide a  ground for improvement of peanut varieties using conventional hybridization and advanced molecular tools.
