data.projectName: An historical investigation into archaeological research in    Bahawalpur
data.projectDigest:
The archaeology of Bahawalpur is of significant importance in the historical reconstructions of Indo-Pakistan history. Archaeological works in the area both in colonial period and since independence have enhanced our understanding to a greater extent. What is needed now is to investigate in a historical way archaeological activities in Bahawalpur. The present proposed study aims to carry out such a historical investigation with two-fold purpose. It compiles in summarized forms all the works if archaeological nature about Bahawalpur with a subsequent historical and critical analysis of all the data.
  Archaeological research has always been influenced interest in historical problems and political thought of the time. Bahawalpur archaeology is also not an exception. This study primarily aims to investigate both these contexts.
Archaeological research in Bahawalpur goes back to colonial period and this activity got momentum since 1970s. The proposed historical investigation into the archaeological activities in the area is all about quarrying rare texts and sources of publication. Both pre- and pist-1947 texts make focus of our analysis. Moreover, this study will also make all attempts to add archival background to the archaeology of Bahawalpur as well.
In this way, this study will lead to show the deep historical basis of Pakistan; let the world know about the cultural and historical riches of Pakistan and introduce historiographical practice into archaeology of the country.
This work is historical in nature with a primary focus on historiography of archaeology. However, social theory will constantly inform our approach towards various problem if historical and political nature.

data.projectName: Flow analysis of pollution particle deposition in human respiratory tract
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Air pollution is a worldwide health threat and annually results in millions of human deaths. Air pollution in current years has become an important subject for health professionals from both the clinical and public health perspective. Many scientists from all parts of world have conducted studies and have found that daily increases in pollution levels are associated with different pathologies, respiratory tract disease. Pollution particles with potential health effects are generated by combustion sources such as cigarettes, diesel engines, and kerosene heaters. Evaluation of diseases from inhalation exposure to toxic pollution particles requires detailed knowledge of inhaled aerosol transport and deposition in human airways.
The dose to the tracheobronchial airways from inhaled particles highly depends on the efficacy in which the particles are deposited on airway surfaces and the particle deposition pattern. The deposition configuration is principally critical for aerosols that affect tissue on contact. Therefore, current study will focus on ultrafine particles and we will study particle deposition pattern and effects of their sizes in this project. To study the effects of particle concentration, diameter and other influencing parameters of simulation Multi phase fluid flow simulations will be performed using Ansys fluid Flow module on the design space generated through DOE. Response Surface methodology will be employed to study the interaction and importance of different parameters.

data.projectName: Non-Invasive Deep Learning Methods for Analysis Retinal Vessels of Retinal Images and Diagnostics of Eye Diseases.
data.piUniversity: Quaid-e-Awam University of Engineering, Sciences & Technology, Nawabshah
data.projectDigest: Automatic analysis of medical images is essential to diagnose the progression of eye disease. Retinal fundus images are used to observe the progression of the disease.  This research proposal will present the implementation of the new image-enhancement model based on learning methods as well as conventional image processing techniques for retinal fundus images.  The main objective of the proposing image enhancement technique will be to compare the improvement of the contrast of the color fundus images with fluorescein angiography images. The experimental results will be based on the evidence that image contrast enhancement techniques work much better than fluorescein angiography images of the fundus while providing comparable levels of contrast. For more validation, this research will implement a technique of image contrast improvement based on the stage’s sensitive to contrast. Finally, two Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) algorithms will be a semi-implemented and automated tool for the diagnosis of ocular diseases, in particular, DR to assess the severity of the DR of normal to severe cases and allow an ophthalmologist to recommend early treatment. The result of this project will be an automated enhancement retinal image, segmentation of the retinal vessels, a screening and diagnostic system.

data.projectName: China-Pakistan Economic Corridor-A Transformation Towards New-Regional Consensus
data.projectDigest: CPEC as an off shoot of BRI has been seen as a Socio-economic initiative that has potential to reform Pakistan through anticipated socio-economicdividend, that may emancipate the society in a manner that prosperity prevails. CPEC offers multiple opportunities not to not only Pakistan but other countries of the Region that may become partners of the CPEC. Intertwined gains and commonality of interests of the member states is likely to help usher peace and stability in the region. CPEC and BRI can potentially offer these opportunities to neighboring states like Iran, Afghanistan, India andEurasia as a whole. Pakistan, hard-hit internal issues and proxy wars, has suffered a lot socialeconomic and in security domains. CPEC, carries promise, hope and potential for mutually beneficial long-termpartnershipthrough renewed as well as fresh economic partnerships of Pakistan with Afghanistan, Iran and Central Asian States. This warrants consensus and collective approach, which creates challenges for policy makers, states as well as non-state entities. Historical moorings, cultural heritage, religious linkages and commonality of goals of emancipation of the people of member countries are likely to help in forging census based economic partnerships that ensures equitable gains.  This studywill be aimedat analyzing these possibilities and proffer pragmatic recommendations for a consensus based and mutually beneficial execution of planning and execution of this important project.

data.projectName: IoT enabled Condition Monitoring for Railways and Utilities
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
Scientific research and technological innovation have reshaped our routine activities. Today, we live in a dynamic, fast spaced world that is entrenched in technological innovation – becoming integrated part of our lifestyle. The term smart city is globally well-established concept, which has reshaped the lifestyle of inhabitants of urban cities. Smart city uses information and communication technologies to increase operational efficiency, share data with the public and enhance both citizen enrollment and quality of government. It provides sustainable development to nations and contribute towards knowledge economy. In the echo system of smart cities, smart Railways and smart Utilities play vital role. There is a dire need of reshaping the future of Pak Railways to avoid incidents such as of 
 Taizgam incident in Oct 2019 and derailing of trains. Accordingly, we propose IoT enabled railway track condition monitoring which plays pivotal role to achieve the vision of Internet of Trains. Similarly, distribution of Utilities in a smart city plays important role especially the distribution network. Any disruption to utility distribution network will result in loss of confidence of inhabitants as well as revenue. Recently, NTDC come across major revenue loss due to damage caused by culprits to distribution towers resulting in electricity outage in many cities. It was found out that over the time the culprits take out the braces of towers and sell them in local market due to which the towers were not able to balance and came to ground. We have developed an intruder detection system for NTDC along with measurement of environmental factors which cause tripping and oxidization on the transmission lines.

data.projectName: Identification of jumps in seasonal diseases through stochastic modeling:
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: By the motivation of these three models we propose a new model which is for medical field. Using Cox-Ingersoll we developed new stochastic model with jumps whereas existing model was based on mean-reversion without jumps.  For this purpose, Primary data shall be collected from the hospitals of selected cities of Punjab (Lahore, Rawalpindi and Multan) and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (Peshwar, Charsada and Kohat). The proposed stochastic jump diffusion model provides the best prediction in the case of Dengue disease due its nonlinearity in nature will help to identify future hotspot of the dengue mosquito spread in the country. This project will infer probabilistic infection routes of a vector borne disease, by modeling internal dynamics of Meta populations driven by human mobility as stochastic processes with jumps. In this way, our proposed model uncovers the self excitation and mutual excitation nature of disease spread across a heterogeneous social system with rich context. It will be applicable to a wide range of intra-group and intergroup jump diffusion processes in social and natural systems and can infer probabilistic causality between discrete events.

data.projectName: The Role of Climatic and Vegetational Change in Late Quaternary Faunal Crisis in the Siwaliks of Pakistan: Implications for the Future
data.projectDigest: Until or unless we build time machines, we have to rely upon our past to interpret our future. The palaeoecological and geochemical records reveal a prolonged effect of climate and vegetational change on ecosystem structure and faunal stability. The ecocrisis of late Miocene time span (7.3 Ma) aroused a prompt response and triggered the extinction of various large and small mammalian species in the low latitude regions worldwide. The Siwaliks of Pakistan represent an exceptional case where a rich mammalian assemblage was present before the late Miocene transition happened which caused the extinction of ~75% of the species. But what happened after the late Miocene faunal transition, is still a mystery to be solved. How the mammalian communities thrived and what type of adaptations they made for the survival? What type of environmental factors forged the mammalian lineages and what was the role of seasonality? Such questions require an in-depth study of what was happening in the past. The studies have revealed that, the present climatic factors are not adequate to answer the diversity and long-term survival of mammalian communities. In addition to direct evidences regarding faunal diversity and ecological evolution through fossil and palaeonological records, the stable isotopes of carbon and oxygen have also served as pivotal proxies for understanding such phenomena in the recent times. This study will yield first comprehensive records of the effect of climatic change on mammalian communities from Pliocene to Holocene and will reveals the upcoming challenges which can potentially be faced by the recent mammals of Pakistan in low latitude regions.

data.projectName: Investigating Fracture Properties of Human and Animal Bones and Establishing National Center of Excellence for 3D PrintAbility Fabrication of Prosthetics and Orthotics
data.piUniversity: Capital University of Science and Technology, Islamabad
data.projectDigest: This proposal is about investigating biomechanical properties of human and animal bones followed by establishment of, “National Center of Excellence using 3D Printability technologies for development of Prosthesis and Orthotics” at Capital University Islamabad. Prediction of fracture and its analysis in human and animal bones has been an area of research interest since long; however 3D printing technologies have given it a new dimension. Researchers at Harvard, MIT, Stanford, Cambridge and John Hopkins University have been continuously working on various areas of biomechanical Engineering including 3D printing of human tissues such as Kidneys and Heart etc.   Present research is being undertaken on evaluating the basic biomechanical properties of human and animal bones to establish its fracture behavior. Experimental and Finite Element simulation (FEM) techniques will be used to investigate the properties of bones in which limited research work has been done in the past. Theoretical results of stress distribution under various loading conditions will be investigated for prediction of fracture locations in bones. Similar conditions will be applied to bones taken from cadavers for experimental testing and results of FEM and experiments will be compared. Therefore; a close conformity of FEM and experimental results will provide possibilities of other approaches for further studies. Present research will take the advantage of basic research on bones and will focus on investigating 3D printability of prosthesis and orthotics as direct application of this project research to patients with amputated arms, legs and any other parts of body.  In this way our basic research on biomechanical properties of bones will directly contribute towards establishment of a National Center .

data.projectName: Theoretical Study of Double Perovskites for Energy Devices
data.projectDigest: The main objective of the proposed research project is the formation of highly efficient, reliable and cost-effective energy devices (e.g., solar cells, batteries etc.). The double perovskites compounds are most suitable and appropriate for energy applications because their band gap in visible to infrared range. The proposed project results will be very useful and helpful from the point of view of economy and industry in general for physics fields and in particular for material sciences field in Pakistan. These perovskites materials can be advantageous due to their high stability, as stable industries are the need of fastly growing modern world. The proposed materials can be potential candidate for cheap solar cell manufacturing as perovskites have high abundance in earth’s mantle. The advantage of these perovskites will benefit industry and materials manufacturers by allowing them to manufacture new devices or products at reduced processing costs. It will not only help industry grow but also fulfill the energy needs of Pakistan and overall mankind.

data.projectName: Synthesis, thermophysical properties and rheological study of ionogels for the selective removal of dyes from aqueous medium by using ionogel doped membrane.
data.projectDigest: Discharge of effluents containing contaminants like dyes into the surface water are found harmful to aquatic life and humans because of their cancer-causing ability. Nowadays use of dyes has been drastically increased because of fastest growth in textile industries for production of colorful clothes and other products. It is really very difficult to remove colorful dyes from waste water because they are non-biodegradable. Many processes have been used for removal of dyes like coagulation/flocculation, adsorption, ozonation, chemical oxidation and photochemical degradation  but they have a lot of limitations.  Separation of dyes through membranes has been found promising as pores of membranes are usually filled with ionic liquids which usually helps in selective removal of organic compounds or dyes. To increase the conductivity, chemical & mechanical properties as well as thermal stability, nano particles of silica embedded with ionic liquids (Ionogel) will be used in this project. If rheological and mechanical properties of ionogel could be changed than it could fulfill the requirements to make membrane suitable for removal of dyes from aqueous medium.  In silica nanoparticle dispersions, the formation & breakage of Hydrogen bonds might be able to describe the rheological properties in an ILs. Similarly, thermophysical properties can provide us an idea about solute to solute and solute to solvent interactions. It is hypothesized that ionogel membranes will be more stable than the normal supported liquid membranes founded on organic solvents. The success of this project will provide a breakthrough for ionogel membranes for separation of dyes and can be used for waste water treatment.

data.projectName: Bio-prospecting of marine natural compounds for future pharmaceuticals application
data.projectDigest: Pakistan has blessed with 1050 km coastal belt and Pakistan enjoys the 350 nautical miles from the coastline as well. Ocean is filled with unique creatures which are still unknown to human beings. These creatures possess a wide range of bioactive compounds that is required to treat many lethal medical illnesses and have application in medical biotechnology. Therefore, this study is being proposed aiming to investigate unknown metabolites from the organisms inhabiting the northern Arabian Sea and deduce possible beneficial therapeutic properties of these compounds or extracts for use in the pharmaceutical industry. As a part of the project an experiment is designed to test the extract for hypoglycaemic activity using rat model and hyperglycaemia-induced   cell line.

data.projectName: Remodeling of existing Motor-Rikshaw incorporating Design, Ergonomics and Environmental friendly fuel system for daily commute to facilitate low-income group
data.projectDigest:
The continuing struggle of Pakistani cities to develop and manage their public transport systems in such a way as to provide a high level of mobility, equity, and environmental sustainability has always been in process. Identifying weaknesses in the current rickshaw, developing a design solution to address problems found, and exploring the possibility of converting it into a Nobel public traveling vehicle for short distances. Major concerns i.e. health and safety, privacy, comfort, and ergonomics will be addressed by implementing design upgrades. The resultant will provide a positive experience in a low budget, giving advantage to Rikshaw users for daily commute (which will include regular users, school children pick & drop, office/educational institute going students etc).

People will prefer cheap travel commute option which will provide comfort and properly
designed vehicle rather than their own private vehicle. Incorporating modern vehicle design
concepts, studying terrain and environmental requirements of the region, an optimized
conceptual vehicle model can be designed providing an easily approachable option. With this
design people can enjoy more affordable transport vehicle while insuring their comfort and
safety. The research areas will include automobile structure, vehicle dynamics and static
stability, interior space efficiency and user ergonomics.

data.projectName: New approach to synthesize bimetallic silver-copper core shell nano fibers decorated anode for lithium ion batteries for 2030 & beyond.
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Nanotechnology will be used to increase the storage capacity of lithium ion batteries (LIBs).We will make high performance anode electrode for (LIBs).To achieve this goal we will synthesize bimetallic silver- copper core shell nano fibers decorated anode. LIBs have been used as the power sources for a wide range of portable gadgets, such as laptops, digital cameras, cell phones etc. There are many advantages of LIBs, they're lighter than other rechargeable batteries. The electrodes of a LIBs are made of lithium and carbon. LIBs has a very high energy density i.e.  more charge storage capacity. Unfortunately, practical application of lithium ion batteries is currently hampered by multiple challenges due to carbon anode. An easy and efficient sol?gel/electro spinning technique would be employed for the preparation of high aspect ratio bimetallic silver-copper core shell nano fibers. The nano fibers are of great interest for lithium ion storage devices because of their high surface area, porosity, etc. As anticipated these silver-copper core shell nano fibers decorated anode as a lithium storage material will exhibit excellent electrochemical properties with high reversible capacity, good rate, energy density 7 to 8 folds more, and the energy storage capacity would also be increased by 70-80%.

data.projectName: Hate speech and explicit content detection
data.projectDigest:
At present, we spent lots of time on social media for the sake of communication, information searching, and entertainment. Use of abusive language by social media users is widespread because of the anonymity of these platforms, which exploits social media, as well as hurts and disturbs social media users. Most famous social sites are still unable to control this type of language. Moreover, hate speech against an individual or group of people based on the race, caste, gender, or religion is prevalent nowadays which results in instability of peace in society as well as in the region. Explicit content available on social media platforms affect the brain, changes behavior can lead to sexual dysfunction and harm sense of healthy sexuality of social media users’ especially underage children. We are envisioned to develop such an intelligent system which will automatically identify such abusive language/hate speech/content and block it.
Our purposed system has multiple real-time applications including safeguarding the social media usage, identification, and blocking of abusive/offensive/hate speech by social media users, restriction towards explicit content either in the form of video, audio or images, and barrier for those who exploit the social media platform.
This system will be useful for both SocioON as well as by ISPs to block explicit content websites, social media to identify and block inappropriate content and messages, and further be the base of other parental control applications.
The commercial partners and investors may include government and other sponsors from social media channels including SocioON, Twitter, and Facebook. The potential customers and target market of the proposed system will different public and private sectors including ISP, government agencies

data.projectName: Colloidal particle manipulation at the emulsion interface for the bottom up fabrication of microcapsules using electric field
data.projectDigest: Micro-encapsulation involves the encapsulation of microscopic particles or water droplets with a thin film, which protects the internal material from the external influence. This technology can be used in various fields such as food, medicine, agriculture, pharmaceutical, cosmetic industry and petrochemical industry. In particular, microcapsules do not have a uniform membrane, but are formed of many nano- and micro-sized particles called colloidosome and has recently attracted much attention due to its potential importance in various fields.  The ultimate goal of this research is to develop new technology for microcapsule fabrication using electric field, utilizing electrohydrodynamic characteristics of micro particles. In order to achieve the goal, nano-micro particles-based suspensions will be used. It is a research area that has only been started recently. Most of the conducted research is based on experimental approach and the research is being started only by a small number of groups around the world. As a result, it is still not possible to establish the applicability of this technology, and therefore more extensive research is needed. In addition, since the application areas are very broad that range from pharmaceuticals, medicine, cosmetics, and go as far as petrochemical industries, it necessary to conduct more research in this area.

data.projectName: Green synthesis of nanofertilizers and their application for plant growth enhancement
data.projectDigest: In the present world, crop production is generally carried out by using chemical-dependent farming methods using synthetic fertilizers especially for cereal crops which are extensively used as food globally. These chemical fertilizers are one of the leading cause of environmental pollution contributing towards soil, air and water pollution and playing their part alarmingly in raising the rate of occurrence of fatal human diseases such as cancer. In order to feed the growing world population,there is a dire need of an alternative sustainable and eco-friendly approach for better growth and development of plants especially for developing countries where greater food demands are to be managed due to population expansion. Nanotechnology is one of the latest technologies which can be utilized to minimize environmental pollution caused by chemical fertilizers and improve crop yield in an ecofriendly manner. Biological method of silver nanoparticles synthesis using indigenous plant growth promoting bacteria is one of the most economic, safe and ecofriendly method as compared to chemical and physical methods of nanoparticles production. Current study deals with the biological production of silver nanoparticles using indigenous rhizospheric and phyllospheric bacterial isolates. Biosynthesized silver nanoparticles will be characterized by using advanced techniques such as such as UV-visible spectroscopy, Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) and Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopic analysis. These green silver nanoparticles will be applied to study their impact on plant growth improvement and development so that these can be utilized as nanofertilizers and can be recommended to replace chemical fertilizers, thus, mitigating the health hazards caused by chemical fertilizers.

data.projectName: Application of Solid State Fermentation (SSF) for Upgradation of Nutrient Profile and Digestibility of Traditional and Novel Ingredients of Poultry Feed as a Model of Technology Based Economy
data.projectDigest: Increase in poultry feed ingredient prices has boosted the search for alternate feed ingredients. High fiber and low protein contents in addition to anti nutritional factors in feed ingredients are the limitations to this move. Fermentation has been reported to have increased crude protein contents and decreased crude fiber of diet. Present project is aimed to investigate nutrients digestibility and performance of meat and egg type chicken using fermented traditional and novel cereals in poultry feed. Effect of the fermented cereals on fibre digestion, gut health, deformation of feed toxins and anti nutritional factors, bird’ immunity status and provision of pathogens free eggs and meat will be studied. Feasibility of solid state fermentation for poultry feed will be investigated. In proposed project total six cereals will be fermented using five different feed grade fungi. Fermented cereals will be evaluated for proximate composition, mineral and amino acid profile to find the best fungi and substrate combination. The best combination in terms of the desired improvement in nutrient profile and toxin load will be validated through feeding trials using meat and egg type chicken. Successful completion will result into a 30 to 35% decrease in poultry feed cost and thereafter in the prices of poultry products. Total 15 thesis researches including two PhD and 13 MS studies will be completed under the project.  Moreover, facilities for preparation of fermented feed will be established in the department.

data.projectName: Climate change impact on the river flow of Indus river at Taunsa barrage
data.projectDigest:
In the past three decades, the heat balance of the earth surface has suffered due to greenhouse gases. Due to which changes are occurring in the hydrological cycle of the earth. Meteorological data of the last hundred years shows us a 0.07 oC rise per ten years. It raised 15cm in the worldwide sea level. The drastic decline of forty percent in the Arctic sea is evident by research. Climate change has drastic effects on the present hydrological resources; increase in the drought, low flows and flood intensification. From discharge data of the largest European rivers, it is evident that their annual peak has increased by seven percent. 
Our hypothesis is that “The prediction of considerable number of floods of specific ranges in any period of time can be estimated with precision if the fluvial characteristics of a flood river are well known. And temperature change has a strong correlation to the occurrence of the floods in rivers”.

data.projectName: Algorithm for solution of Volterra population growth model with fractional order via Haar wavelet
data.projectDigest: Haar wavelet method is much more elegant in Biomathematics and engineering, more convenient in numerical calculations and most of all, it is much faster in data processing. The Haar method is very accurate in detecting singularities of irregular structures and transient phenomena exhibited by the analyzed functions. Sometimes the exact solution of the problem in biomathematics is not possible then we are interested to find the approximate solution of the problems. There are different methods for numerical solution of the problem.   The proposed research work is to find out an efficient and accurate approximate for the solution of fractional Volterra population growth model using one-dimensional Haar wavelet collocation technique with combination of Caputo derivative.

data.projectName: Development of a sustainable Indigo dyeing process: Application of green reducing agent and analysis of colorimetric properties
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
The need for ‘‘Natural’’ or “Eco-safe” or ‘‘Green’’ goods and services is grabbing and rising public awareness to expand premium market. The present research involves the development of an environment friendly or “green dyeing process” for dyeing cotton with indigo dyes. The main objective of the project is to replace the conventional reducing agent, sodium hydrosulphite/sodium dithionite with an organic or biodegradable alternative. The activities mainly involve the process development by selecting a suitable reducing agent and optimizing the process parameters by experimental design technique. The feasibility of different kinds of reducing agents (commercial and natural products) would be explored to attain the maximum benefits. 
The scientific hypothesis is based on the attainment of the desired colour strength and fastness properties with a green reducing agent against the conventional. The process developed would be essential to the field of conventional textile colouration which would be highly beneficial for the local and international market.

data.projectName: Gas Pricing in Pakistan: Two-Pronged Optimization in the Context of Economic Efficiency and Consumer Welfare
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
The dilemma of balancing act between social welfare of consumers through energy subsidies versus improving national exchequer through revenue generation has always been a difficult proposition for all policy, makers especially in developing countries.  Subsidies are designed to benefit the deprived sections of the society but poorly targeted subsidy may hamper the wellbeing of the concerned masses. 

Pakistan provides a substantial subsidy on to its consumers in energy sectors. Although electricity subsidy has been well debated and thoroughly discussed, impact of subsidies on natural gas has rarely been evaluated.  In 2019, as per the requirements of Extended Fund Facility Arrangements with IMF, gas prices in Pakistan have been increased significantly. In December 2019, on request of Sui Northern and Sui Southern Gas Pipelines Limited, OGRA directed government for a further increase in gas prices w.e.f 1st January, 2020. In Pakistan different gas prices are charged from different category slabs based on their consumption levels. The recent proposed increase of nearly 200% in gas prices for the lowest consumption category is likely to have an adverse impact on the welfare of households falling in this consumption category.

In the light of this situation, the proposed study aims at examining the impact of increased natural gas prices on the consumer welfare in Pakistan. The study will estimate the magnitude of reduction in consumer welfare and the resultant gain in economic efficiency. The proposed study also desires to devise a gas pricing strategy which can ensure maximum efficiency with least possible comprise on consumer welfare.

data.projectName: Sustainable production of lactic acid from fermentation of pine needle hydrolysates by furfural resistant bacterial isolates
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest: It is well known that pine forest soil become acidic due to presence of acids released into soil upon natural decomposition of dropped pine needles. Thus, pine forest acidic soil could be potential to find lactic acid producing bacteria naturally adopted under such conditions for laboratory and commercial scale production of lactic acid. Current challenge in efficient and sustainable use of such pine needle biomass for production of lactic acid has not been reported. In addition, fermentation inhibitors which are furfural and 5-hydroxymethyfurfural present in hydrolysate of pine needle (alike lignocellulose) are possibly major hurdle towards it potential utilization for microbial assist production of biomolecules. However, steps are required to remove these furfural inhibitors prior to efficient use of pine needle hydrolysates as fermentation medium for lactic acid bacteria. In this backdrop, current proposal proposed Sustainable production of lactic acid from fermentation of pine needle hydrolysates by furfural resistant bacterial isolates. The possible outcome of this proposed research will contribute to ending of poverty, hunger, attain food security and better-quality nutrition and stimulate sustainable agriculture; accessibility to clean water; lessen climate changes; shield, reinstate and sponsor maintainable usage of terrestrial ecosystems and forests, minimize desertification.

data.projectName: Harnessing Green Energy from Arabian Sea
data.projectDigest:
Genesis of Oscillating Water Column (OWC).
The steady wind over sea surface transfer some of its kinetic energy into ocean surface. The sea surface roughness creates waves in ocean. These ocean waves’ stays coupled with steady wind for some duration and increase in height. The process is called fetch, higher the fetch, higher the energy stored in waves. The longer the winds work on these ocean wave the greater the amount of energy stored in these waves, then this energy in waves is discharged at the shore lines and the phenomena is called wave breaking. The idea is to harness this wave energy by using a turbine that is connected to a generator which runs by compressed air inside a housing facility at the coast before the wave breaking occurs. The up-and-down wave motion will run the turbine and causes the generation of electricity. Since these waves are a constant feature of ocean and therefore guarantees the uninterrupted supply of power. 
From above discussion it is clear that there is a huge amount of ocean wave energy available at coastlines. The power reaching the world’s shorelines is estimated at about 2 ´ 1012 W (Gillett J; 1990). The efficient extraction of this energy source can supplement in energy deficiency in less developed coastal areas.

data.projectName: Preparation of reduced metal oxide thin films and metal decorated metal oxide thin films for water splitting
data.projectDigest:
Energy has been a major economical, political, and environmental issue of the 20th century and will be  the number one issue of the 21th century. At present time, the world consumption of energy is almost 18.5 TW. In future, the increase in world population and industrialization, the energy demand will reach 50 TW by the end of this century. Nowadays most of the energy consumed at present comes from the fossil fuels. The use of fossil fuel generate green house gases particular carbon dioxide, with irreversible effect on the globe climate. It is necessary to fulfill the energy demand of the world and to save world environment from green house gases, a clean energy source is required.
Most of the universe is made of hydrogen and it is considered as an energy vector. On earth, hydrogen is found in compound form like water. Hydrogen can be extracted by electrolysis of water. Water splitting is an endergonic reaction and energy to dissociated the water molecule and to overcome activation energy. Water molecule can be split into hydrogen and oxygen molecules via photocatalysis using efficient photocatalyst. Metal oxides semiconductor are cheap, nontoxic and easily available on earth and they are considered a best option to use them as a photocatalyst. Unfortunately, metal oxides are large band gap semiconductors and they have ability to absorb on UV light of solar radiation. For better solar light to hydrogen conversion efficiency, photocatalyst should absorb maximum solar light. It can be achieved by decreasing the bandgap of the semiconductor that is used as photocatalyst. In this Project, absorption ability of metal oxide thin films will be enhanced by decreasing the band gap through reduction and by making junction of metal oxide thin films with metal (Au, Ag, Al, Rh etc)

data.projectName: Effects of the Guided Disclosure Protocol on Post-Traumatic Growth: A randomized control trial designed to observe psychophysiological alterations in traumatic stress subjects
data.projectDigest:
The two constructs traumatic stress and Post-Traumatic Growth (PTG) are distinct and the psychophysiological relationship is yet to be explained. It’s a long debate that the victims who survive through the traumatic event only perceive that their suffering has helped them in improving their lives after the event or the experience actually improved functioning. The purpose of designing this randomized control trial is to observe psychophysiological alterations associated with post traumatic growth in traumatic stress subjects. This Multicenter study is planned to investigate the effectiveness of the guided disclosure protocol for the promotion of post-traumatic growth (PTG), in the traumatic stress subjects and to determine whether PTG is associated with psychophysiological alterations i.e. (C-Reactive Protein, Brain Derived Neurotropic Factor, Interlukin-6, Cortisol, Heart Rate Variability and brain waves). Study subjects meeting eligibility criteria will be randomized into two groups. Guided disclosure protocol (GDP) will be used as intervention vs the control. Blinded treatment will be provided and the subjects will be made to complete study questionnaires (Screening, Traumatic Stress Scale SSS, Trauma Symptom Checklist, Post-traumatic growth Inventory) at baseline and at post-intervention (3-months later).

This study might give us insight about application and efficacy of Guided disclosure protocol in a population that is seeking help and underrepresented to be clinical. Moreover, one of the more hopeful findings of this research will be significant information about trauma-related psychophysiological effects.

These losses (10-60%) are associated with mechanical injury, physiological disorders and postharvest diseases. So, in recent years, single alternative mean is ineffective to reduce decay, so integration of alternative means can be worthwhile to control diseases and residual free papaya fruit which are eco-friendly, safer to human being and environment Thus, any struggle that can improve the fruit quality attributes, shelf life, reduce losses and diseases will be important in order to obtain the higher monetary return. data.projectName: Development of a Prototype Multivalent Vaccine for Puerpral Metritis
data.piUniversity: Lasbela University of Agriculture, Water and Marine Sciences, Lasbela
data.projectDigest: Metritis is a postpartum uterine disease, characterized by uterus size enlargement with red, brown or white purulent watery discharge having bad odor. The present project proposed as a preliminary study to develop the prototype multivalent vaccine for puerperal metritis at Faculty of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lasbela University of Agriculture Water and Marine Sciences (LUAWMS), Uthal, Baluchistan. For this purpose, 15 primiparous cow / hiefers infected with metritis of 10 days of postpartum will be selected. The isolation and identification of candidate pathogens will be done by using uterine samples for vaccine formulation. Prototype Formalin killed whole cell vaccine of Actinomyces pyogenes, Corynebacterium puedotuberculosis, fusobacterium necrophorum, Clostridrium spp., E. coli and Bacteriode spp. will be prepared in four different formulations i.e. A, B, C and D using adjuvant system. Total 60 mice will be used for preliminary immunization, blood samples, reproductive and visceral organs will be evaluated to antibodies (IgG and IgM) and histopathological evaluation. For evaluation of efficacy of vaccine, total 30 pregnant (210±5) cows will be divided in to treatment groups 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 for immunization. Animals in group 6 will be kept as control. Blood will be collected at each week of experiment. Serologically biomarkers include complete blood test (CBC), Antibodies (IgG and IgM), cytokines parameters (IL-1?and IL-6), total bilirubin, aspartate aminotransferase, creatine kinase, serum creatinine, and blood urea nitrogen (BUN) will be analysed. Endometritis prevalence (%) and artificial insemination (AI) on first oestrus will be recorded to evaluate the efficacy of prototype multivalent vaccine for puerpral metritis.

data.projectName: PREPARATION AND PHARMACOLOGICAL EVALUATION OF HONOKIOL LOADED TRANSFEROSOME gel FOR THE TREATMENT OF SCIATIC PAIN
data.projectDigest: Neuropathic pain is characterized by sensation of persistent pain and results from the injury of the peripheral nerves, which respond poorly to existing therapies because the involvement of the multiple distinct mechanism. To deal with the neuropathic pain several therapeutic strategies are in clinical practice, however, these therapies are related either with inadequate pain relief or results in bothersome adverse effect. Currently, nanomedicine has attracted the attention of many researchers for ailment of many diseases, because nanomedicine pertain unique physicochemical and biological attributes. The nanomedcine has emerged as an important field of nanotechnology with widespread application in health and medicine, which has overcome the various limitations associated with the conventional dosage forms. The natural products are an important source for the treatment of various diseases and several products from natural sources are in clinical practice. Honokiol a natural lignan biphenol compound isolated from magnolia officinalis plant and have been reported for various biological activities. The honokiol showed significant activity against the partial sciatic nerve ligation (PSNL)-induced neuropathic pain (during preliminary invetiagtion) and significantly ameliorated the sign and symptoms related with neuropathic pain. During the proposed project, the honokiol loaded transferosomes gel will be formulated and evaluated against neuropathic pain.

data.projectName: Hybrid semiconductors for opto-magnetic properties
data.projectDigest:
The purpose of this theme is to study magnetic properties along with optical and electrical properties of semiconductors to make good opto-magnetic material used as hybrid material. This is very attention able part of today’s emerging science and technology for energy or memory storage devices. To get this target different transition metals will be used as a dopant in the semiconductors which will affect the optical and electrical properties as well as the magnetic behavior. These selected dopants would have magnetic aspect for better magnetic response in semiconductors. Furthermore, magnetic and optical properties with different temperature ranges would be characterized for optimization of different parameters. The results of this applied research may be used for magnetic device with optical response.   
Hands on experience for young female of newly established Department of Physics, Fatima Jinnah Women University Rawalpindi. It will boost the confidence level of female scholars in social sciences dominant university towards science and technology. The Material Synthesis & Characterizations (MSC) Laboratory at Department of Physics is state-of-the-Art research laboratory and a kick start towards research in faculty of Science & Technology.

data.projectName: Development of Biological Dressing for Skin Wounds
data.projectDigest: Burns are destructive injuries, often resulting in high morbidity. It also impacts on emotional well-being and quality of life of the patient. Burn injuries are a major burden in hospitals of Pakistan mainly affecting low- and middle income class in terms of physical, psychological and economic implications. Expensive treatment, prolonged hospital stays, multidrug resistance infections are some of the factors which contribute to poor wound healing outcomes in such burn patients. Therefore, the aim of the study is to develop easily available, cost effective and efficient membrane as burn dressing with better healing and antibacterial properties which would help the clinicians in effectively managing such patients.

data.projectName: Identification of Psychosocial Predictors and Efficacy of Mentalization Based  Treatment (MBT) for Prison Inmates with Genetic and Non Genetic causes of Personality
data.projectDigest: The present study aims at studying the Psychosocial Predictors and Efficacy of Indigenous Treatment for Prison Inmates with Genetic and Non Genetic causes of Personality.  The research will be comprised of three studies. In study I, screening of the prison inmates having anti-social and borderline personality traits will be done. Correlational research design will be used. Inmates who have been punished for imprisonment with a duration of less than two years will be excluded. A demographic questionnaire form, Urdu translation of Standardized Mini-Mental Status Examination (Molloy, Alemayehu & Roberts, 1991); Comprehensive Diagnostic Instrument for Personality Disorder (CDIP) (Dawood & Khan, 2010) and Psychopathy Checklist Revised (Hare, 1991) will be used to screen the participants with antisocial and borderline personality traits. data.projectName: Recombinant DNA vaccine production and its evaluation against specific   bacterial infection of farmed fish in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The major species of carp cultivated in Punjab, Pakistan are Labeo rohita, Cirrhinus mrigala, Ctenopharygodon idella, Catla catla, Hypopthalmichthys molitrix and Onchorynchus mykiss. In cultured carps various bacterial infections including the abdominal dropsy and fin rot are most common. The Aeromonas spp along with other gram negative and gram positive microbes are the etiological agents for such infections. Vaccination plays a significant part in eradication of the infections. Vaccines are available in four categories i.e. Attenuated (Live), Inactivated (killed), Purified subunits (Glycoprotein and protein subunits) and DNA vaccine.  In fish, DNA vaccines have been proven very efficient and inexpensive because of the identical processes and able to induce strong and long-lasting humoral and cellular immune responses which are similar to live vaccine. For this purpose, we will isolate DNA sequences of pathogens that act as an immunogenic protein (epitope). DNA will be inserted into expression vector to form recombinant plasmid. Fish will be immunized with this recombinant DNA by intramuscular injection. We expect that Immunized fish will show significant production of specific antibodies and interferons, which will indicate the activation of humoral and cellular immune response after vaccination.

data.projectName: Exploring the “Type of Role” Women are playing in the Livestock Development
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: In rural areas of Pakistan where 63.62 % of total population of Pakistan (Census - 2017 Pakistan) is living, Livestock is normally considered a key asset for rural population and presents considerable prospect for lifting of household income. Moreover, livestock sector has been repeatedly associated with poverty alleviation. In an attempt to address the issue of poverty, many projects have been launched by government and non-government entities aiming at improving the female literacy rate, increasing the women participation in public sector, encouraging women participation in political activity, encouraging women entrepreneurship and providing micro-financing for their entrepreneurial endeavors. The most recent project launched by the current government “Egg and Chicken” also aims at providing chicken and eggs to the rural women to start poultry businesses. Females perform major role in management of livestock however their role in decision making is still questionable (Arshad, S., Muhammad, S., Randhawa, M. A., Ashraf, I., & Chaudhary, K. M. 2010). Although women empowerment has become an important agenda item on the government policy table, however these projects do not have a follow-up mechanism to confirm that financing awarded to women is really used by women themselves or their male partners are retaining that money also. Despite of serious efforts targeted at empowering women through financing their entrepreneurial endeavors the role of women in decision making is still unclear and questionable. Therefore, the proposed project aims at identifying the role of women in livestock production and management process in a time when women empowerment in economic decisions is being claimed and propagated through different initiatives.

data.projectName: Piloting Water Quality Surveillance and Response System in District Peshawar
data.projectDigest: Drinking water contamination is one of the core issues in many developing countries and of the challenges confronting scientists and planners. The need of water quality assessment in different parts of the country is thus imperative to analyze state of the water consumed for different purposes especially for drinking purpose. Pakistan is blessed with abundant water resources. However, due to lack of proper management strategy for water resources, the country faces problems of quantity and quality. Only limited population has access to public water supply (not even clean), while the rest of population is dependent upon direct withdrawal of water from both surface and ground sources, where available, for its daily needs. There are many sources of water but ground water is an important source of water as compared to other sources, especially from drinking point of view. Ground water is considered comparatively safer source of water, because it is naturally purified and filtered (Iftikhar, Bashirullah et al. 2016). Environmental pollution and low quality of drinking water is one of the global as well as national issues for under developed countries like Pakistan. The Environmental profile of Pakistan indicates that about 40 percent of deaths are related to water borne diseases resulting from the effluent added by different sources. A report published by UNICEF expressed that Pakistan does not have access to safe drinking water and more than 90,000 children die every year due to diarrhea and other diseases related to unsafe water and poor sanitation facilities. If improved water supply is achieved it can reduce the diarrhea morbidity by 6 to 25% per year (Zahid 2018)

data.projectName: Economic Evaluation of Food and Nutrition Insecurities and Malnutrition Status among Different Population Groups of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Food and nutrition insecurities are global concerns in all age groups including children, adolescents and adults. Despite food self-sufficient country, Pakistan is one of the most food and nutrition insecure countries in South Asia. Moreover, Pakistan is stood at second after India, in terms of highest proportion of stunted and wasted children under five years. Existing national data sources like Household Integrated Economic Survey (HIES) and Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) could not measure food and nutrition insecurities and malnutrition status in all age groups. In the light of this background, this study examines the prevalence of food insecurity, nutrition insecurity, and malnutrition indicators for child, adolescent and adult population of Pakistan. Moreover, this study evaluates the socio-economic factors at individual, maternal, household and community levels to address food and nutrition insecurities and malnutrition for child, adolescent and adult population of Pakistan. This study will collect household data from four provinces of Pakistan and employs multi-level mixed effects logistic regression technique. The findings of this project will help policy makers to devise food and nutrition specific strategies for different population groups for achieving zero hunger and food and nutrition securities goal of sustainable development.

data.projectName: Modeling of Practical Quantum Communication and Interferometric Setups
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Conventional methods of communication have been proven to be insecure with the development of quantum computers. The most vulnerable are the communication protocols based on secret keys, where secrecy is ensured by difficulty in solving one way functions. Quantum communication provides unconditional security based on the laws of Physics. However, the distance up to which secure communication can be done and the length of the secret key being distributed, is limited by practical limitations of the resources being used. With the world moving to inter-continental secure communication, the achievable distances are the key to secure communication success. We plan to model different communication set ups, including quantum key distribution and quantum interferometers and explore to what extent these set ups can be useful. 

This work is planned to be built on our previous work on long-distance communication, where photonic based long-distance key distribution protocols are proposed. However, in this project the exact modeling of quantum memories is planned by exploiting the spectral distribution of incident signal and the response of the whole setup to it. The spectral analysis will be then extended to photon interferometry, which is an essential component of quantum measurement.

data.projectName: PHARMACOLOGICAL VALIDATION OF PAKISTANI MEDICINAL PLANTS FOR ANTIDIABETIC POTENTIAL AND POSSIBLE EFFECT ON GLUCOSE METABOLISM REGULATING GENES
data.projectDigest:
Diabetes mellitus (generally known as sugar) is a common and fastest growing disease affecting a large population of the world including Pakistan. Obviously, it has become a serious problem for modern communities due to life-threatening complications. Several therapies are used by the clinician for the management of raised blood glucose level. The treatment generally involves life-long application of several drugs which create various other complications because of adverse effects, and also puts financial burden on the sufferers and their families. Hence, the search for new affordable drug(s) with better efficacy and safety profile has been the focus of various research groups. There is strong belief that certain functional foods  have potential to control  blood glucose . Strong scientific evidence is required to justify this belief.
The therapeutic potential of indigenous  medicinal plants is well known (Khan, 2014). The ethnobotanical survey indicates that numerous plant species have been used for the effective management of diabetes in different parts of the country (Ahmad et al., 2009), which need scientific exploration for the beneficial effects as otherwise, could be dangerous for human use. The current study is based on the pharmacological evaluation of traditional/folk uses of these plant species as antidiabetic in well-established paradigms (in-vivo and in-vitro) for efficacy and potency including various enzymes that interfering plasma glucose levels and effect on glucose metabolism regulating gene expression. Based on the results, the selected plant species will be subjected to phytochemical analysis.

data.projectName: Exploitation of synergistic phenomena for hyper production of cellulases by thermophilic  fungal consortium  and  its application
data.piUniversity: Lahore College for Women University, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Modern industry is experiencing a major operational shift and many traditional processes are being replaced with efficient mechanisms. Textile, food, paper, and detergent industries are  important,where many of the bioprocesses are substituting  the  traditional macro-industrial operations.  Cellulases can be obtained from the microbes present in our surroundings, but a handful of knowledge about the growth conditions specifically the environment for their optimal production are the pre-requisites for the exploitation of full yield potential of these microorganism. Microorganisms are seldom found in environment as pure cultures and most natural environments are designated by a great variety of microbial species interacting in intricate ways. The growth of microorganism in consortium is different from pure culture  due to synergistic or antagonistic interactions. Synergistic interactions are of great interest for enzyme production.  Because a positive interaction result in an increase in the growth rate of an organism  and subsequently enzyme production. This project will contribute in  assessing the unexplored fungal genetic resources and exploitation of synergestic phennomena for enhanced  enzyme production and its probable utility for industrial applications. For this purpose  locally isolated  fungal consortium will be screened  for cellulases production. Enzyme characterization and its application at lab scale will also be carried out.

data.projectName: QUANTIFICATION OF DEBRIS FLOWS AT REGIONAL SCALE: A STUDY IN NORTH PAKISTAN
data.projectDigest:
The collision of India and Eurasian plates in NW Pakistan is reflected by world highest mountain
belts as Karakoram and western Himalayas. Seismicity and precipitation are the two main controlling factors of geohazards in North Pakistan. Debris flow is recognized as the most destructive geohazard in mountainous regions causing financial losses and causalities. Unfortunately, in Pakistan, debris flow is the most neglected geohazard. Quantification of debris flows on a regional scale is always challenging. Current study aims to produce a spatial database of debris flows along the Karakoram highway and in Chitral valley This task will be accomplished through remote sensing techniques and GIS technologies aided with extensive fieldworks. A digital/spatial database of debris flow becomes more crucial for countries like Pakistan which is facing difficulties in energy crisis but on the other hand heading towards DIGITAL Pakistan. Besides, Pakistan is a major pillar of mega Chinese “Belt one Road” project which is spread to number of countries in the world. The results in the form of a complete digital database of debris flows will provide a meaningful insight into their spatial distribution and future susceptibility mapping and hazard assessment approaches in the region.

data.projectDigest:
Pesticides worth more than US$30 billion are intentionally released into the global environment every year. Many of these are highly toxic and have immediate adverse effects on human health and wildlife or contaminate local food, water, soil and air. Pesticides harm may result from direct exposure during handling, spray drift, washing contaminated work clothes, storing pesticides in the home, or indirectly via pesticide dumps and persistence in the environment. Growing without chemical pesticides is based on alternative preventive and curative pest control methods. If preventive measures are not sufficient, insecticides derived from natural plant extracts like neem and many more sources can be applied (Haffmans, 2008). Non-selective use of pesticides is responsible for water pollution, soil degradation, insect resistance and resurgence, destruction of native flora and fauna. Some are responsible for ozone depletion and contribute to the greenhouse effect (Baloch and Haseeb, 1996). Although pesticides offer one way to manage pests, there are other alternatives that do not present the same environmental problems. These alternatives include integrated pest management, which is bringing together and utilizing all the control measures concurrently or successively in an integrated way against a particular pest and thereby minimizing the need for chemical control. And if there is still a need for chemical control, then as a last resort pesticides should be applied very carefully and intelligently to obtain cheap, environmentally safe and effective control (Shahid, 2003).

data.projectName: Maple Package: for computation of travelling wave solutions of differential equations
data.projectDigest: Many physical phenomenon are described in mathematical equations. One of the important class of these equations is differential equations (DEs).  DEs have been used widely to analyze and control different types of robots, population growth, electrodynamics, stochastic calculus, fluid mechanics, propagation of heat and many other physical and engineering problems.  The analytical solutions of these DEs are always a hot topic of research to know the insight. This proposal aims to write the Maple codes for the computations of analytical solutions of these DEs. Main concern of the project will be to implement Maple code for various classical methods available in literature for the solutions of ordinary differential equations.  Some of them are: the tanh-function method, inverse scattering method, the extended tanh-method, the Jacobi expansion method, the generalized method, traveling wave hypothesis and many more. The purpose is to make such a user friendly package which can be ultimately used for the calculations of the solutions for complicated differential equations under our consideration. Further, execution of the code will be made by taking up four inputs including name of the technique, differential equation, parameters to be computed, and homogeneous balancing terms. This will help to get solution to analyze the physical system in depth despite of their physical complexity.  The proposed Maple package will ease  the researchers in computation of the solutions of DEs.

data.projectName: Renewable Energy Consumption and Socio-Economic Development of Agriculture and Business Sector : A Case Study of Larkana Division
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Zulfikar Ali Bhutto Institute of Science & Technology (SZABIST) University, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Energy crisis, sluggish economic growth, and environment pollution are eminent issues (problems) in economy of Pakistan. One of the solutions of these problems is renewable energy consumption that can abolish the above mentioned problems. Besides solving these problems, renewable energy consumption is also affecting our socio-economic development (wellbeing) e.g. health, education, poverty, and employment etc. This study will probe the effect of renewable energy consumption on socio-economic wellbeing in agriculture sector and small scale business. In agriculture sector, there are many farmers who are now using renewable energy e.g. solar tube wells, so, this study will pay special attention to these farmers to examine the effect of renewable energy consumption. There would also be a comparison among those farmers who are using renewable energy and who are not using renewable energy. Moreover, there are many businesses that are using solar energy (renewable energy) e.g. filling stations and shopping malls etc. This study will also investigate the impact of renewable energy consumption on the socio-economic wellbeing of those businesses. The locale would be Larkana Division. The study is based on surveys & questionnaires, which, would be used to collect data from the respondents. Mixed method research methodology would be used to get the results and data of 100 farmers and 100 business owners would be collected. The study will be helpful for business men, investors, and government for decision making. The outcome of the study would help to achieve many SDGs and improving trade deficit.

data.projectName: Women Issues presented in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Short Stories (Afsana)
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Benazir Bhutto Women University, Peshawar
data.projectDigest:
Literature reflects life. Various forms of life have been presented in various disciplines. Short Story is the focus of attention, because it is based on routine social issues. In today's modern life, man cannot be expected to read long stories. Short Stories not only attract the reader because of its shortcomings, while also portrays its commitment to the realization of society? 
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is a region where traditions are banned. Men are given more importance in society, while women are mostly confined to the premises of the house. In the life of education, business, marriage and other accessories of life, a woman is not allowed to come out of a particular circle. In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Urdu fiction has portrayed the society as a whole and made women's issues the subject of fiction. 
This project will present an overview of Short Stories by the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa narrators in which the problems of the woman are described. The Project focus on the issues of women, presented in the myths of Farigh Bukhari, Raza Hamdani, Naeema Shahnaz, Munawar Rauf, Zaitoon Bano, Tahir Afridi, Syeda Hina, Um e Amara, Feroza Bukhari, Ghazala Nigar Orakzai.

In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Urdu fiction has portrayed the society as a whole and made women's issues the subject of fiction. 
This project will present an overview of Short Stories by the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa narrators in which the problems of the woman are described. The Project focus on the issues of women, presented in the myths of Farigh Bukhari, Raza Hamdani, Naeema Shahnaz, Munawar Rauf, Zaitoon Bano, Tahir Afridi, Syeda Hina, Um e Amara, Feroza Bukhari, Ghazala Nigar Orakzai.

People in Pakistan are mixed in their opinions about the impact of CPEC. This can be ascertained by a comprehensive and detail survey about what CPEC can contribute towards achievement of SDGs.

data.projectName: DEVELOPMENT OF INDEGINOUS HERBAL MEDICINE THROUGH CELL BASED TRIALS OF CALOTROPIS PROCERA AS TREATMENT OF THEILERIOSIS IN LIVESTOCK
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: The blood protozoan diseases include the transmissible diseases which are considered to be of socio- economic and/or public health importance within countries and which are significant in the international trade of animals and animal products. Theileriosis, caused by Theileria annulata, is transmitted by ticks of the genus Hyalomma. Previously HEC funded project (666) Epidemiology of theileriosis in bovine at CMS, UVAS, Lahore has made it possible to diagnose the disease by PCR and IFA that has allowed the development of sensitive diagnostic assays for Theileria annulata. Among the several alternative Theileria control measures considered to date, only the host vaccination against Theileria has proved promising (Elvin & Kemp, 2000). There are currently only one effective but expensive drug for the treatment of theileriosis available in Pakistan namely buparvaquone (Butalex, ICI 2400/- Single Dose) not affordable for small famers. Herbal plant called Ak with botanical name Calotropis gigantea (Singh et al. 1996).This plant has been used by many researchers. Leaves of Calotropis gigantea were used by Dolan et.al. (1999) & Warden et.al. (2003) as antibacterial, for expulsion of guineaworms, swellings, sores, wounds, inhibits excessive granulation of wounds and ulcers, skin diseases, killing lice, tonic, stimulant for ruminants. The therapeutic efficacy of calitropis gigantea was previously studied in a pilot study and it was found out to be 80% against theileriosis in bovine. The present study has been designed to study the efficacy of herbal medicine in cell based system via toxicity and effective dose estimation of medicine. Further HPLC profiling of the product with the objective to develop this herbal medicine for manufacturing by private sector

data.projectName: In vivo Evaluation of Ficus carica and biosynthesized Cerium Oxide Nanoparticles as Promising Agents Against Metabolic Syndrome Induced Reproductive Dysregulation
data.piUniversity: Lahore College for Women University, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) a major disorder is a constellation of metabolic disturbances i.e., hypertension, abdominal obesity and insulin resistance leading to type II diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular diseases and infertility both in male and female. Major risk factors considered are sedentary life style and dietary habits especially in young population. Infertility is considered to be a major problem in Pakistan like other global areas. Amelioration of this condition helps people to live a better life and improving their physical health and social well being. Currently, nanoparticles are considered as a useful therapeutic agent due to their small size and specific in their targeting. Green synthesized nanoparticles in which natural substances are used as a stabilizer are more biocompatible due to their physicochemical properties. Certain natural plants have shown promising remedy for the treatment of various ailments. Present study aimed to investigate the comparative effect of green synthesized biogenic cerium oxide nanoparticles and Ficus carica leaves extract for treating reproductive dysregulation and metabolic abnormalities in animal model. Different parameters of metabolic syndrome along with reproductive parameters, DNA damage, histological examination of ovary, testes and protein expression will be estimated in both sexes of albino mice.

data.projectName: Tumor Cell Intrinsic mTOR Signaling and PTEN Deletion Regulating PD-L1 Expression in Prostate Adenocarcinoma
data.projectDigest:
Cancer of prostate is the most commonly occurring cancer in men and shares large burden of cancer related death in Pakistan. Unfortunately, no cure is available and treatment plans employed at the moment eventually becomes ineffective as disease starts to spread. Hence, there is an urgent need to develop new treatments and also distinguish cases that has potential to spread within body in order to identify candidates suitable for more aggressive treatment.
  
Treatment targeting novel molecule termed; PD-L1 is the recipient of noble 2018 award for being the most promising treatment of certain cancers. Now the research is focused on finding PD-L1 molecule in prostate cancer and exploring the benefits of PD-L1 treatment for curing this deadly disease. Besides that, understanding science behind PD-L1 upregulation is also important. Ongoing studies suggested; PTEN/Akt/mTOR/S6K molecular axis; contributes to PD-L1 upregulation in prostate cancer. Additionally, apart from PD-L1, growing evidence in literature suggested that evaluating levels of PTEN/Akt/mTOR/S6K molecules could best predict the future behavior of disease if performed on initial work up.

Thus, current proposal is designed to explore PD-L1 molecule and its regulatory node which has dual significance; developing novel treatment and provide upfront information for future course of prostate cancer.

data.projectName: Isolation and identification of antibacterial compounds from plants for possible therapeutic formulation intended to cure skin disorders
data.projectDigest:
Plants have always been considered and utilized by humans as the chief source of food, fuel and shelter. A much appreciated role of these are as relievers of illnesses and afflictions. As more and more researches pour in, scientists are led to credit this feature to the multitude and variety of compounds that particularly make up the plant structures; leaves, roots, stem, stem bark, fruits, flowers, seeds etc. These compounds singly and in combinations have been utilized to make formulations and drugs particularly aimed at curing the human body. The application of this propensity of plants in therapeutics and products of daily use has helped tremendously in alleviating human suffering.

There are thousands of products on the market that are plant based. People, in general feel comfortable in using such products in routine and in afflicted and diseased conditions. Furthermore, research on preparing such products as alternate means of treatment must be continued, as the incidence of antibiotic resistant bacterial strains is currently exhausting available treatment regimens.

data.projectName: TVET-Industry Collaboration in Punjab: Opportunities and Challenges
data.projectDigest: Technical and Vocational Education and Training has historically been used as a policy intervention to ensure abundant skillful workforce in a designated area of technological and economic interest. Ideally, the requirement for skill-set and level of learning should be determined through collaboration of industry and TVET institutions, however, because of communication gap, this is not happening in Pakistan. So the main question to be answered is how good is the education that our young people are getting, for theirs and our prosperous future. It is good only in parts, but not as good as it should be. One of the biggest reasons of this weakness is far more limited interaction of academic-industry stakeholders, than what it could be. The demand of 21st century for skillful and innovative employees can only be achieved if academia-industry gap is bridged. Thus, academia and industry need to be directly involved with each other and with regulatory authorities. The regulatory bodies need to play supervisory role and abandon the practice of micro-management. If this could be done, I am sure, TVET institutions can play enormous role in progress and prosperity of our young population. Thus, we must make sure such change start to happen now.

data.projectName: Bio-crude production from Crop Residue employing Hydrothermal Liquefaction (HTL) for Sustainable Biorefineries
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest:
The transition from a fossil based energy and product supply to a sustainable, renewable supply relies on intelligent use of the limited resources available. One of these is biomass, which will become the major source of fuel and intermediates for carbon-containing products in the decades to come. Thermo-chemical conversion of biomass can become a key in this transition due to their feedstock flexibility, general high throughput, unrivalled efficiency in conversion and range of products.
The thermochemical conversion process targeted in this proposal is hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) of biomass feedstock. This technology has been pinpointed for high conversion rate i.e. more than 70% of the energy of the feedstock in the product and significant potential. The proposal will be focused on HTL technology for the production of bio-crude and chemicals, with extensions to local feedstock use and preparation as well as issues regarding end use of the bio-crude such as upgrading, mixing, storage stability, physical properties and chemical reactivity.

data.projectName: Household Food-Consumption Behaviour And Food Waste: A Study On the Metropolitan Cities Of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The objective of this project is to determine the impact of Consumer food-related behavior on household food waste. The purpose is to build an understanding of the influence of various household food- consumption behaviors on domestic food waste in the metropolitan cities of Pakistan. Metropolitan cities of Pakistan are chosen because the food waste is anticipated to be influential due to suburban living style of urban class. Moreover, metropolitan cities have a large number of people from a diverse culture living in ages. This study will contribute to scarce literature related to food waste which is according to the best of our knowledge is rare in Pakistan. The study will adopt a mixed-method research approach. The quantitative data will be collected through questionnaires and the interview method will be used for qualitative data collection. The focus population of the study consists of households of the populous metropolitan cities of Pakistan. NVIVO and PLS smart softwares will be used for data analysis. The result of this study will help the policymakers to set policies to delimit the food waste at the household level as previous research concludes that households comprise a major source of food waste. In addition, the study will help in saving resources used in food production and protecting the environment from greenhouses gasses caused by wastage of food. This project will be carried out with the assistance of three academic collaborators from three different institutes of Pakistan which will aid in the enhancement of research quality of this project.
