data.projectName: FABRICATION OF MICRO- AND NANOSTRUCTURES OF TRANSITION METALS AND THEIR OXIDES FOR SELECTIVE OXIDATION OF BENZYL ALCOHOL
data.projectDigest:
Researchers from around the world have taken keen interest in the study of selective oxidation of benzyl alcohol, mainly due to its importance from laboratory as well as industrial perspective. Usually, oxidation of benzyl alcohol is investigated by varying catalyst, reagent, oxidant, solvent and other reaction parameters. Use of inorganic oxidants like dichromate and permanganate, which are toxic, resulted in large amount of waste and a costly separation step to get valuable reaction products. Disposal of waste raised environmental concerns as well. Thus, there is room for further investigation to find a heterogeneous catalyst, which can provide a greener and efficient route for the selective oxidation of benzyl alcohol employing clean oxidant such as air, oxygen and hydrogen peroxide.
Researchers have fabricated various novel morphologies of micro- and nanostructures and explored their improved and unique optical, electronic, magnetic and catalytic properties. In this quest, hollow structures have captured the most interest because of their unique structural features which gives them edge over others. Hollow structures can effectively isolate catalytic species, prevent sintering and enhance stability.  Selectivity of catalytic reaction is enhanced due to better control of pore sizes. Reaction rates get a boost provided reagents are concentrated in the voids, which can be facilitated by controlling hydrophilicity/hydrophobicity in the system.
In this project, our aim is to prepare a micro- and nanostructures (catalysts) with different morphologies for oxidation of benzyl alcohol, which will be based on less costly transition metals and their oxides. Thus, our proposed synthesis route will provide an environment friendly and economical alternative.

data.projectName: Investigation and Prototyping of Energy Harvesting Nanogenerators for Flexible Electronic Devices
data.projectDigest: In the proposed research, inorganic, organic and hybrid material’s nanostructures will be synthesized at optimum processing conditions. The inorganic materials include ZnO, BaTiO3, Pb(Zr1-xTix)O3, (K0.5Na0.5)NbO3, etc while Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-trifluoroethylene) (PVDF-TrFE), etc will be used as organic materials. Various synthesis techniques such as electrospinning, hydrothermal, solvothermal, spin coating, wet chemical route etc., will be employed to synthesized the hybrid and non-hybrid nanostructures (i.e., nanofibers, nanowires, nanorods, nanoparticles etc.,) and thin films. All synthesis techniques will be carried out at Nano Physics Laboratory, AWKUM. XRD, FESEM, EDS, UV/Vis/NIR spectrometer, FTIR, TG/DTA, IV characteristics, etc., will be carried out. Temperature dependent impedance spectroscopy will be used to investigate qualitatively and quantitatively different electro-active regions (bulk or grain, grain boundary, electrode effect, etc). Flexible nanogenerator devices such as electromagnetic-triboelectric hybrid nanogenerator based on Fe3O4-NPs@PVDF composite fibers & thin film, vertically aligned ZnO-NRs on ITO/Glass, FTO/Glass and ITO/PET (flexible) substrates, aligned ZnO-NRs with and without PVDF on different substrates, flexible piezoelectric NGs devices on aligned ZnO-NRs on Ni-Foam, Ag-NPs@PVDF, KNN-NRs@PVDF, BT-NPs@PVDF & ZnO-NRs@PVDF composite fibers and thin film for TENGs devices will be fabricated.  All these NG-devices will test for output power generation and the efficiency per unit area will be evaluated.

data.projectName: Performance Analysis of Substation Grounding Grid in Harsh Electromagnetic Environment
data.projectDigest: In this project, the electromagnetic and independent vector analysis (IVA) techniques will be used to analyze the performance of substation grounding grid without halting the flow of electric power. The performance analysis of grounding grid incorporates corrosion diagnosis, breakpoints, depth and configuration detection. The use of electromagnetic method in the proximity of substation is highly vulnerable to electromagnetic interferences (EMI). This is due to the presence of wide number of electromagnetic devices such as transformers, relays, busbars, etc. Therefore, IVA will be utilized to overcome the influence of substation EMI on the proposed electromagnetic method.

data.projectName: Development of solid waste pelletizer machine for RDF production
data.projectDigest: Persisting energy crises as a result of depleting fossil fuels are drastically affecting the sustainability of the communities. On the other hand, solid waste, generated in different domestic, agricultural, commercial and industrial activities, is also a major problem these days. Conventional dumping of this huge amount of solid waste in the open land is not a suitable option as it causes different social and environmental problems. Controlled combustion of solid waste has been found as an attractive way to manage and treat the solid wastes as it reduces the initial volume significantly. Energy generation is another benefit which can be used in place of fossil fuels like coal etc. in the boilers and other firing stations. However, utilization of solid waste as an alternative to the fossil fuels need certain processing to make it feasible and efficient. Refused Derived Fuel (RDF) pallets formation is one of the waste-to-energy techniques in which the raw solid waste is converted into an efficient fuel energy generation. In the proposed study, a pilot scale RDF pelletizer machine will be developed for different solid wastes. The study will come up with a universal RDF pallet forming machine with optimized parameters and raw material inputs.

data.projectName: Extraction and synthesis of chitosan and its derivatives for different applications
data.projectDigest: In this project, novel cost effective formulations of water soluble chitosan (Carboxymethyl/Carboxyethyl-chitosan) and other sulfonamides derivatives will be synthesized using standard methods from synthesized chitin/chitosan (of different molecular weight and degree of deacetylation (DDA) extracted from easily available crabs and prawns wastes). Finally, chitosan based marketable products will be prepared for different drug delivery systems, cotton dressing for wound healing, skin care products, superabsorbent materials (napkins), as preservative for fruits and vegetable without cold storage, and coating agent in textile will be developed which could be proposed as market products with the respective companies. Also, chitosan required in solution form and other formulations will also be available for different end users. This chitosan will also be blended with other biocompatible polymers using low pressure stirred reactor. A variety of biocompatible polymers like poly (vinyl alcohol) (PVA), poly (ethylene glycol) (PEG), poly (vinyl pyrolidone (PVP) etc. will be blended with chitin/chitosan and/or other biopolymers using simple dissolution casting methods to establish the structure-property relationship.

data.projectName: IMPACT OF NANO-MATERIAL TREATED IRRIGATION WATER ON GENETIC DIVERSITY AND PHARMACOLOGICAL POTENTIAL OF NIGELLA SATIVA L
data.piUniversity: Lahore College for Women University, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Human beings in all ancient civilizations have been dependented upon herbs for disease treatment. Unfortunately, still herbs are mainly collected from wild resources, without considering time, part and amount of collection. Hence a huge material collected in every visit is wasted. There is need to develop technology for bring these herbs into cultivation with enhanced phytochemical and genetic diversity. Nigella sativa (Ranunculacea) known as black seed is annual flowering plant, native to South and Southwest Asia. The seed is utilized as spice, and for their carminative, condiment and aromatic properties and to treat several human disorders like indigestion, diabetes, rheumatism and various cancers. Unfavorable climatic conditions are the biggest factor for Nigella sativa L. being a neglected crop in Pakistan, hence imported. The sequential protracted period of cold and wet weather adversely affect the quantity and quality of seed at the time of harvest. Nano materials are being considered effective for improving quality and quantity of seeds from last two decades. It is hypothesized that use of nano material can modify metabolic activity, yield and genetic diversity. Therefore project is proposed to evaluate impact of nano-material treated irrigation water on quality/quantity of seed, genetic diversity and pharmacological potential of N. sativa.

data.projectName: MOLECULAR, BIOCHEMICAL AND MANAGEMENT STUDIES OF NOXIOUS WEEDS IN DIFFERENT CHICKPEA GROWING AREAS OF KHYBER PAKHTUNKHWA.
data.projectDigest:
The shortage of chickpea in Pakistan and elsewhere in the world can be witnessed by its extremely high prices. The activities of the project will enhance the per hectare yield of the target crop through the effective management of weeds. Farmers will be trained on safe use of herbicides for weeds as enemy number one in crop husbandry. All these endeavours will eventually raise the socio-economic status of the chickpea growers of Pakistan. Moreover, the increased yield will have an impact on the local market and will be helpful in reducing prices for the consumers. The improved grain quality will fetch higher prices to the growers in the market. 
The molecular and biochemical study of the weeds will help in finding the diversity among different species of weeds associated with chickpea and this data will be used as reference data on the diversification of weeds based on the specific cropping system. The integrated weed management (IWM) technology generated in this project could also be extrapolated to other areas of Pakistan like Mianwali, Bhakar, Jhang, Layyah, Chakwal and Attock. (Major chickpea growing areas).

data.projectName: Inhibition of metastatic human prostatic cancer cells by using adeno-associated virus CRISPR/Cas9 system.
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Prostate cancer (PCa) is becoming one of the most common emerging cancer in Pakistan and developing countries. According to American Cancer Society 2016 report, almost 2 million new cases of prostate cancer were reported, and about 27% of these patients died. The annual death (mortality) rate associated with PCa is extremely alarming in Pakistan as it has increased by 35% to what it was in 2010.  Although PCa is associated with old age, usually 50 years of age or above, there have been increase of occurrences of the disease in age group of 35-40-year if genetic factors are involved. At present, the main treatment approach includes surgical removal of the tumour with radiotherapy and chemotherapy. As notorious as cancer is, PCa has also ability to spread (metastasis) to different parts of the body which makes medical treatment very difficult. There has been 92% increase in metastatic PCa cases since 2004. With advancement of genetic editing tools like CRISPR/Cas9 system, we can now disrupt PCa cells at the genetic level and stop progression of the disease. Hence, the essence of this research proposal is to develop CRISPR/Cas9 system and to find targets in PCa cells to halt cancer cell progression.

data.projectName: Application of cold formed steel sandwich panels and pultruded GFRP structural profiles in the construction industry of Pakistan.
data.projectDigest:
•	In Pakistan the most used construction materials are Steel and concrete until now. 
•	The major drawback of Steel and concrete (RCC) structural materials are higher self-weight, Steel corrosion, concrete disintegration and sulphate attack on the structure. Also, the construction and time period are longer. 
•	An alternative to RCC material is prefabricated panels which are directly supplied from the factory to the construction site. This considerably reduces the self-weight of the member and also saving in construction time. These profiles include cold form steel sandwich panels which are of less thickness, lighter cross-section and resistant to acidic and corrosion. Second option is pultruded GFRP profiles, available in all structural shapes i.e. I, W, HSC are HRC. Different combinations of these profiles can produce a variety of wall panels. GFRP pultruded profiles are very light (one fifth of steel), are free from corrosion and are inert to temperature and electric shocks. The result of the research will demonstrate suitably and preferred use of these prefabricated panels for construction industry.

data.projectName: Power Generation for Rural Areas of Pakistan having  Low Wind Velocity
data.projectDigest: In US, Renewable energy resources accounted for more than one-fifth of net domestic power generation. In 2019, government of Pakistan sets milestone of over 30% power generation through renewable energy till 2030 which are currently less than 4%. Power generation from wind becomes difficult when regions have low wind velocity. So, the concept of Invelox wind turbine is presented here. Basically, it is instrumental way to upgrade velocity using concept of aerodynamics. It is  omnidirectional  wind  power  transporting  system containing large funnel to capture wind,  followed by a tapered  section  to  concentrate  and  finally  a  venturi  to  accelerate before delivering it to turbines safely and efficiently at ground level.  Placing turbine in venturi makes it more innovative and reliable because multiple turbines can be placed keeping birds away from turbine blades. In New Zealand, multiple Invelox projects are in development for energy generation totalling over 337 MW. There is still chances in improving efficiency, cost and reliability by increasing the mass flow rate in existing design to extract more power by adding funnel and changing area ratio. The prototype of 150 watts is being developed at IST for Islamabad and this proposal is extension for 1 KW wind turbine.

data.projectName: Development of sustainable aquaponic system in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Aquaponics is the combination of aquaculture (fish farming) and hydroponics (soilless plant culture). In aquaponics, the nutrient-rich water that results from raising fish provides a source of natural fertilizer for the growing plants. As the plants consume the nutrients, they help to purify the water that the fish live in.  Hydroponics is growing plants in a solution of water and nutrients, without soil. In aquaculture, the water quickly becomes nutrient rich due to the fish digesting their food and excreting waste.  In aquaponics, the fish waste provides a food source for the growing plants and the plants provide a natural filter for the fish. This creates a mini ecosystem where both plants and fish can thrive. Aquaponics is the ideal answer to a fish farmers problem of disposing of nutrient rich water and a hydroponic growers need for nutrient rich water.

data.projectName: Fractionalization of metric parameters of graphs
data.projectDigest:
In a university campus, IT department is providing internet services to entire cam-
pus. There is a sub-department responsible to control all computers in campus to which they are providing services. Consider computers represent vertices and their connections as edges.  A robot can move freely from one vertex to another in this setup. The computers in control room are landmarks.  Any computer can be identify/control using distance metric from landmarks. The minimum numbers of landmarks required to uniquely identify all computers in campus is called metric dimension. Modifying integer valued concepts to take non integral values is called fractionalization. Fractional versions of various concepts in mathematics are being used to broaden the scope and range of applications in different areas of study namely, fractionalization of factorial function is Gamma function, fractral geometry identifies fraction dimensional objects and analysts are considering fractional derivatives and partial derivatives.  Similarly, in graph theory it extended the range of application in scheduling, assignment and operational research.  It is observed that fractional version of theorems is more interesting to prove than classical ones. A bound for fractional parameters of graphs is also a bound for their classical analogues.

data.projectName: Enhancement of Omega-3 Fatty Acids in Maize
data.projectDigest:
Omega 3 fatty acid is a class of essential long chain polyunsaturated fatty acids needed by the human body for many functions. Apart from playing a major role in cell signaling, lipid metabolism and maintaining cell membrane fluidity, recent studies have demonstrated their part in preventing cardiovascular and neuronal diseases. EPA and DHA are the two biologically active forms of Omega 3 fatty acids while ALA and SDA acts as intermediates. Despite their significance, the human body lacks the enzymes to convert ALA to EPA and DHA, so, requiring these from external sources either in form of food or as supplements. Maize being the third most important cereal crop in Pakistan appears to be a viable candidate as alternative source for omega 3 fatty acids. The overall objective of the proposed research is to transform maize with FADS1 and FADS2 gene which accelerates the conversion of precursor ALA into EPA and DHA.
The developed transgenic maize will be enriched in biologically active EPA and DHA omega 3 fatty acids. Direct consumption of this transgenic maize or in the form of corn oil, corn syrup, corn flour will help in mitigating the omega 3 fatty acid deficiencies in the human body.

data.projectName: Assessing facilities, problems and support for transition from special education to inclusive education
data.projectDigest: Globally latest concept of education of special need persons is focused on inclusive education. Pakistan is one of the signatory of sustainable development goal that ensure education to all without any discrimination. Presently Pakistan is far behind in achieving its target of inclusive education, we lack a clear guideline or model of work to follow, positive attitude for inclusion, trained teachers, and required facilities and collaboration among stakeholders. This project focuses on finding problems of stakeholders in the process of transition from special to inclusive education system. Analyzing facilities and support offered by the NGOs, for special and inclusive education. Providing skill based training to the teachers of general government schools to prepare them for transition process, and designing a workable model of inclusive education for promoting inclusive education in Pakistan. This research project will be a collaborative work among government and private universities and between department of education and department of computer science. This project will be beneficial for special need persons who need transition from special to inclusive education, for the parents of special need children, for the teachers to get skilled based training related to inclusive education. It will also help policy makers in designing their programs and at large for the community as stake holder in this process.

data.projectName: Monitoring and Alert Communication System for Landslide Prediction Using Wireless Sensor Network and Internet of Things
data.projectDigest: This research project aims to design, develop and deploy a landslide monitoring and alert communication system based upon wireless sensor network (WSN) and internet of things (IoT). For this purpose, we plan to develop a wireless sensor node equipped with two sets of sensors. One set of inexpensive geotechnical sensors embedded in the ground will provide real time land monitoring whereas another set of meteorological sensors will provide real time ambient and meteorological details of the landslide site. Using a number of these sensor nodes, a WSN will be designed, developed and deployed across the landslide. The entire sensor network (the things) will be connected to the Internet through a gateway node thereby resulting an IoT network. The real time data will be transmitted to a central computer for processing and storage in a database. For landslide prediction, we also plan to design and develop a slope failure and landslide prediction model. Depending upon the data and assessed condition of the landslide, the model will assign a level of risk to the landslide. Risk assessment will be communicated to the general public and other stakeholders using website, SMS alerts, emails and mobile application. Our proposed project is the first of its kind in our country. It will be the first project to develop a landslide characterization database, the first to develop a landslide prediction model, the first to deploy a wireless sensor network and internet of things to monitor a landslide and the first to develop landslide alert communication system.

data.projectName: Enhancing nitrogen use efficiency in wheat through CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing approach
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest:
Wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) is the major staple and food security crop in Pakistan. Since "Green Revolution" inception of short stature and high yielding wheat varieties have been introduced. These wheat varieties require high amount of inorganic nitrogen fertilizer input to maintain their yield potential but wheat plant can consume only 30-31% nitrogen fertilizers. While remaining 69-70 fertilizers are lost through leaching, consumed by soil microbes, volatilized to ammonia and cause serious environmental issues.

data.projectName: Pilot Scale Co-processing and Conversion of Sugarcane Baggasse and Water Hyacinth Biomasses into Bioethanol
data.projectDigest:
The increasing price of gasoline associated with the shortfall of the conventional energy resources and the subsequent environmental issues has induced great interest to search for renewable energy resources. Production of ethanol from the lignocelluloses is among today’s promising energy resources. Ethanol has been used as a fuel in various countries in the past and it is being exercised again across the globe. Ethanol can be used mainly as biofuel as an alternative to gasoline, which is almost widely used in Brazil for running cars. As ethanol production from common raw material is cheap and is gaining a great attention as alternative to conventional fuels. The selection of lignocellulose biomass affects the cost of process as the type and availability of biomass determine the cost of ethanol. Keeping in view these facts, the sugarcane baggasse and water hyacinth biomass have been selected as precursors in the proposed project. As the District Charsadda is famous for production of sugarcane and the University is almost completely surrounded by the sugarcane crop, thus there is a great potential of bioethanol production from the sugarcane baggasse in Charsadda. The water hyacinth biomass was also selected keeping in view its greater availability in the Charsadda due to plenty of water bodies as a result of multiple rivers. 
Objectives of the proposed work are to produce ethanol from the processing of sugarcane baggasse and water hyacinth biomass using various yeasts under various conditions in order to optimize the process conditions e.g. substrates concentration, ratio, temperature and pH etc. for maximum production of ethanol and cost effectiveness. The process will also be carried out at the pilot scale in order to evaluate its applicability at industrial scale.

data.projectName: The Role of Rare Earth Ions in Color Tunable Upconversion Emissions in Newly synthesized Phosphors
data.projectDigest:
Upconversion Luminescence is a pure anti-stokes non linear effect where Multiple lower energy excitation photons produce high energy emission photon. The phenomenon of upconversion contrary to the luminescene sensitize the materials to produce shorter wavelengths with high energies. Therefore, this process is used in in many applications including displays, infrared detectors, light emitting diodes, biolabels, security markers, lasers, temperature sensors, solar cells etc. 

Fabrication of upconversion materials require an inorganic host containing normal or transition metal ions. These materials are doped with bi or trimetallic lanthanides and actinides to achieve upconversion. The emitted radiations are either belonging to a specific wavelength region or the different emitted energies are optimized such that the emitted light belongs to white light. The combination of Red, Green and Blue lights or RGB are mixed in such a proportion that white light is emitted. Due to diversity and applications of the materials in industries we will be focusing on the fabrication of upconverting luminescent materials which may be belonging to one of the regions of RGB or combinations of these color.

data.projectName: Production of an anticancer drug (Taxol) from cell culture of taxus sp.
data.projectDigest:
Taxol is one of the most effective anti-cancer drugs ever developed. The natural source of taxol is the inner bark of several Taxus species, but it accumulates at a very low concentration and with a prohibitively high cost of extraction. Another problem is that the use of inner bark for taxol production implies the destruction of yew trees. For all these reasons, the growing demand for taxol greatly exceeds the supply that can be sustained by isolation from its natural source and alternative sources of the drug are being sought. Although taxol has been prepared by total synthesis, the process is not commercially viable. Taxol can also be semisynthetically produced
via the conversion of baccatin III or 10-deacethylbaccatinIII found in Taxus needles but the cost and difficulty of the extraction process of the semisynthetic precursors are also very high. The most promising approach for the sustainable production of taxol and related taxoids is provided by plant cell cultures at an industrial level. Taxol is used for the treatment of different types of cancers which includes breast, lung, ovarian, leukemia, murine, sarcoma and other diseases. It has the ability to kill tumor cells by inhibiting the depolymerisation of the microtubules during the cell division. Now a days Taxol is obtained from taxus plants. The production of Taxol from plant sources has some problems which includes: 1) limited quantity of active compounds in plant; 2) low plant growth rate; 3) the limited localization of active ingredients in the specific organs; and 4) from the perspective of the conservation of natural resources. Plant cell culture is an attractive technology to solve these problems by securing the stable supply of the active compounds without damage to the natural plant resources

data.projectName: In Vitro Mass Propagation of High Yielding and Disease Free Banana Plants through Tissue Culture Technology
data.projectDigest: Banana is an important fruit crop in Pakistan. Around 98% area under banana cultivation is covered by one Basrai variety (Cavendish dwarf) in Pakistan that produces only 4.4 tons per hectare which is very low as compared to other banana cultivating countries of the world where the average production is 30-35 tons per hectare. The major cause of low yield of banana in Pakistan is unavailability of healthy planting material. Banana is propagated through suckers that takes a long time and produces a limited number of planting material. Moreover, the propagation done by suckers carries various diseases with planting materials. Therefore, the present project has been designed to produce disease free banana plants through tissue culture technology all-round the year. The plants produced by this technology are uniform, true to type, pest and disease free, mature early and give more yields as compared to suckers. The banana plants produced by this project will be sent to banana growing areas of province Sindh, Pakistan because the successful growing conditions of banana such as soil and environment have been found to be favorable in those areas, and the farmers also have accessibility to tissue culture plants.

data.projectName: Synthesis of new heterocyclic compounds based on triazole- and isoxazole-related moieties and their evaluation as ?- glucosidase inhibitors”
data.projectDigest:
Diabetes is one of the leading health problems worldwide affecting millions of people, and it is expected to affect twice the population/be doubled by the next 25 years. Recent study showed high prevalence of type-II diabetes in entire Pakistan, hence, strategies are required to be developed at a community level to control this metabolic disorder. The disease is characterized by hyperglycemia and leads to several complications such as heart disease, kidney complications, blurry vision, and foot amputation. ?-Glucosidase inhibitors (AGIs) are available as common and efficient therapy for hyperglycemia, but showed adverse side effects. Therefore, there is dire to focus on the discovery of new, safe and efficient ?-glucosidase inhibitors.
Previous results on AGIs from our group on triazole and isoxazole encouraged us to explore new inhibitors of this enzyme via linking these scaffolds with other heterocycles. Thus, this project will be helpful in searching new leads for the development of new anti-diabetic agents, which could contribute for national needs against diabetes.

data.projectName: Stimuli-responsive (polymeric & magnetic) Nanohybrids for potential targeted drug delivery and smart textile applications
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Stimuli-responsive polymers (SRP) and respective nanocomposites have expanded applications in different chemical, biological, and smart textile progressions. The major potential application involves the involvement of SRP and respective magnetic nanocomposites is targeted drug delivery and smart textile. SRP-nanocomposite (SRP-Fe-MWCNTs) with Lower Critical Solution Temperature (LCST) will be synthesized in the study. Poly (vinyl-caprolactam) PVCL will be polymerized with Magnetic MWCNTs (metallic nanocomposite), by free radical polymerization technique. The polymerized product will be characterized and applied to evaluate various physicochemical properties of the prepared nanocomposite.

data.projectName: DOCUMENTATION OF ENDANGERED LANGUAGES   SPOKEN IN THE STATE OF AZAD JAMMU AND KASHMIR
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest:
The proposed project is to collect discourse data on Gojri (ISO-639-3, Code gju), Kashmiri (ISO-639-3, Code kas) and Hindko (ISO-639-3, Code hno).
Multiple genre of text and lexical items of these languages will be collected with an aim to prepare sketch grammars with a dictionary of 2000 words each. Moreover, a comparative study of these languages will be aimed at determining the salient features of these languages and language varieties. The focus of the project will be to maintain the vitality of the languages that are still robust, and to revitalize those languages showing signs of endangerment by enhancing their prestige and speakers’ self-confidence. 
Importance of preservation of the said languages will be highlighted through awareness workshops, and devising viable writing systems (orthographies). Material for developing literacy programs in the local languages will be developed and translated into English and Urdu for learning these languages.

data.projectName: Study and development of minimally invasive thermal management techniques to enhance electrical efficiency of commercial photovoltaic panels for floating/land-based solar energy generation
data.projectDigest: This project aims to be part of the greater effort to increase the contribution of renewable energy generation within Pakistan to comply with united nations’ sustainable development goals (SDGs). In particular, the target of this project is to contribute towards achieving SDG no. 7 which aims to ensure access to affordable, reliable, sustainable and modern energy for all. Under this scope, the project is aimed at developing and experimentally characterizing minimally invasive thermal management methods and techniques capable of enhancing the output capacity of already installed public and privately-owned solar energy generation infrastructure within Pakistan by improving the electrical efficiency of individual photovoltaic (PV) panels. The considered systems include the traditional land-based PV systems and their relatively novel alternative to generate electricity from floating PV arrays installed on surface of lakes and dams of Pakistan. This will be achieved by initially designing and simulating cooling structures employing thermal management techniques employing forced water circulation, Phase change materials, heat pipes and methods to improve natural conductive cooling.

data.projectName: Bio-refinery of non-edible seeds; Sequential process for production of energy carriers and bioactive compounds
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Import of unconventional petroleum and usage of fossil fuels is continuously increasing to meet the energy demands in Pakistan. Pakistan invested 6.28 billion US dollars for import of crude oil in 2018. Not only the reserves of the fossil fuels are depleted continuously, but also the dependence on fossil diesel is impacting the local economy which is negatively influences the environment and human health. To cope with all these challenges bio-fuels has the potential to handle with the demands need to be fulfilled by fossil diesel. In this regards current project is focused on, to check the potential of the non-edible seeds of Taramira, castor and rice bran (oil of rice bran is of low quality and is non-edible), for the production of biofuels (biodiesel and biogas). This project will focus on the production of biodiesel from three different sources by using two approaches; biological and chemical methods to produce eco-friendly and low cost biofuels that will provide environment and social sustainability. Hence, in this project by utilizing all the local natural resources starting from the non-edible feedstock to the final production of biofuels makes this project more feasible, doable, cost effective and environmental friendly.

data.projectName: Nano encapsulation and technological application of essential oil extracted from plant sources
data.projectDigest: This project is designed to utilize available sources including spices and herbs for the extraction of essential oils having such compounds possessing the health benefits. For extraction purpose such techniques (supercritical fluid extraction and ultrasound assisted extraction) will be used having high efficiency and least effect on the compounds. After extraction these essential oils will be further analyzed for their biological activity though various analysis. Moreover these extracted essential oils will also be subjected to GC-MS and FTIR analysis techniques to further confirm the presence of active compounds. Then essential oils will be then converted to nano-emulsions. The purpose of formation of nanoencapsulation is actually the ability of these nanoparticles to be very stable, non toxic and delivered at specific target. These will be further used for enrichment of fruit juices which will be resulting in food product that can be utilized in replacement of drugs for the management of specific disease.

data.projectName: Exploring hyperaccumulation potential of rapeseed (Brassica napus) to mitigate cadmium toxicity using integrated breeding and molecular approaches
data.projectDigest:
Cadmium is considered as the third most abundantly present contaminant capable of fast accumulation in soil and ultimately in edible parts of plants due to pollutants released by sewage water, mining operations, agricultural and industrial effluents. The alarming part of cadmium toxicity is that it targets vital organs in humans for instance, liver, kidneys and lungs. In plants it caused damage by silently becoming part of plant tissues even at low concentrations without showing any observable symptoms of toxicity. However, among various practices to reduce heavy metal deposits, phytoaccumlation offers an eco-friendly, efficient, cost-effective and natural remedy. Considering phytoextractor plant species, anola is one such model hyperaccumulator. This proposed project will focus on exploring hyperaccumulation potential of canola for cadmium by determining threshold level. The effect of cadmium intake by roots on canola oil content and quality will also be studied using an integrated approach. 
A set of canola varieties will be subjected to morpho-physiological screening under different cadmium levels at seedling stage. The results of phenotypic screening will be validated with molecular marker studies. Canola varieties showing tolerance and susceptibility to maximum cadmium levels will be selected as parents for hybridization. Parents and hybrids will be evaluated at maturity under cadmium level optimized during screening experiment.

data.projectName: Efficient use of Noise Pollution for Electricity Generation through Acoustic Energy Harvester
data.projectDigest: Energy is vital for running all the resources. With respect to supply, the demand for energy is continuously increasing in Pakistan, resultantly crisis for energy has emerged. Energy crisis directly influences all the sectors of economy such as agriculture, industrial, unemployment, poverty, lower GDP and higher inflation. Hydro, oil, and natural gas are the primary energy resources of Pakistan that are used to fulfill the energy needs. It is a time to find other sources for electricity production to overcome the present energy crisis. Energy harvesting are a buzzword these days in which ambient energy is converted into useful energy. There are various sources in the environment from which energy can be harvested like solar, thermal, vibration, wind, mechanical and sound etc.  In this work, sound will be used as a source to harvest energy. One can observe that several machines in industries produce noise in daily routine which causes pollution and wasted. It is, therefore, important to use that noise pollution for energy production. The aim here is to design, fabricate and install the acoustic energy harvester in noise producing environment for the production of electricity. This work will contribute to energy sector and national economy by providing source for electricity generation and by reducing the export of oil and gas from international market.

data.projectName: Qualitative and quantitative assessment of the rooftop solar PV market: an insight into the opportunities, challenges and prospects of this technology in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: To achieve sustainable power sector in Pakistan, government has extended the efforts to enhance the share of renewable resources in energy mix. In this context, GoP has set the target of 30% of renewable energy share by 2030. To achieve the target netmetering policy was introduced in 2015.  It has been now more than 4 years since inception of net metering however, the stakeholder’s response towards adoption of this technology is still passive. The unresponsiveness of the stakeholders confirms the existence of certain challenges that affect the development of net metering market.  Therefore, this research endeavors to assess the existing net metering policies, the stakeholder’s perspective including consumers, vendors, regulator and electricity generation and distribution companies. For the purpose, both qualitative and quantitative tools were employed.  The purpose of this project is not only to evaluate the existing net metering policies but also to devise a comprehensive policy guideline to make it more convenient for all the stakeholders. The project focuses on the net metering market in Pakistan in terms of opportunities, challenges and future prospective. The outcome of this research project will enable policy makers to get the stakeholder’s insights which will help them to redesign the policy according to country specific environment. The generalized results of the project will be equally important for other countries.

data.projectDigest:
Sialkot is the second largest revenue earner for the Government after Karachi as exporting goods worth 02 billion. The people are highly innovative and entrepreneurs having skills to run small organizations. This is an organic growth model as centuries old skills of craftsmanship are transformed into international export. Sialkot business community has set leadership examples in the country by setting up Airport, dry port, community hospitals and lot of other welfare projects.

The planned growth under triple helix concept can develop Sialkot an innovation cluster. The planned growth can also increase its export 10 times yielding lot of indirect benefits like increased tax collection, increased employment, increased infrastructure, increased economic activities, reduction in poverty of local people , increase health care and improved life quality index of Sialkot.

The proposed study will investigate how this target of 10 times growth can be achieved along with trickle down impacts. The study will also explore scope of growth in current industries, areas of future industries, requirements of public infrastructures and facilities, international collaborations and other development aspects. 

The study will present a blue print of 10 x growth of Sialkot from USD 02 billion export to USD 20 billion export.

data.projectName: Energy absorbing capabilities of a natural fibers based safety helmet – Design,  development and performance evaluation
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest:
This project targets the utilization of plant based natural fibers in an energy absorbing application. The present study will be hosted at Composite Structures Lab (CSL) recently established at Faculty of Mechanical Engineering (FME) of the Ghulam Ishaq Khan (GIK) Institute of Engineering Sciences and Technology.
The safety helmets are part of the protective gearing worn to safeguard against accidents. These helmets are utilized in sports, automotive and heavy industries etc. The use of safety helmets has shown to significantly reduce the head injuries. The design of these helmets is based on the principle of impact energy absorption by deformation of helmet body. These helmets are traditionally made of synthetic materials, the latter being harmful to our environment.
There are some industrial safety helmets which have been sourced form biodegradable constituents, but these are being imported in our country. In Pakistan, a potential exists for extracting the natural fibers from either the agricultural residue produced every year or other plants (e.g. bamboo). These sustainable sources can serve to provide raw material for production of safety equipment. The product thus produced, in this case a helmet, will of interest to both the agriculturists as well as automobile industry.

data.projectName: KNOWLEDGE ECONOMY BASED EDUCATION USING COMPUTATIONAL THINKING
data.projectDigest:
The proposal under the title “KNOWLEDGE ECONOMY BASED EDUCATION USING COMPUTATIONAL THINKING” is proposed with the theme “To transform COMPUTATIONAL THINKING (CT) IN EDUCATION to accomplish the goal of attaining the KNOWLEDGE ECONOMY”. Computational thinking is the procedure of transformation of computational problem solving approach to the community. This computational problem solving approach is based on typical computer science problem tackling method.  This project is to seed for the “advance computing research” and to promote the extensive use of CT for the improvement of people's lives. 
Moreover, it will be helpful to involve Computational Thinking to make collaboration between computing people  with other domain experts by providing  training/lectures/seminars to the teachers of various departments of university about CT skill development for KE based education, assisting teachers/ trainers to develop course contents using CT skills and providing teachers and students with online resources ( lectures/videos) developed using CT concepts. 
This project will contribute as a lighthouse to benefit the learners and teachers to be the Computational thinkers to be able to problem solver in each and every sector of their career.

data.projectName: Indigenization of ICT Resources for Teaching of Science
data.projectDigest: There are persuasive arguments in literature about the potential of Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs) in all facets of life. The digitalization of course content is an influential tool to motivate the students for learning. The current proposal is based on the findings of previous research project, wherein, the results indicated that in order to implement flipped classroom instructional strategy into Pakistani classrooms, teachers and students both need content specific videos. However, for teachers, access to the internet was not easy, and searching the specific videos from online resources consumed much time. Moreover, available online videos are not according to Pakistani context including culture and language. Therefore, the main focus of the current research project is to develop indigenized videos for teaching and learning of science for the students of class VII. The instructional material will be developed in line with Pakistani context, and available to the teachers and students in the form of CD along with the textbook of science. These videos will contribute in the conceptual understanding of science content and make the classroom environment conducive, lively and energetic. Above all local language and culture give them feelings of belongingness and they participate in learning more effectively. Additionally it would be beneficial to achieve the benefits of flipped classroom, web based instructions and online resources.

data.projectName: Optimization of multiplex Real-Time PCR for the prevalence of milk-borne pathogens in District Faisalabad
data.projectDigest: Milk and milk products are highly enriched with nutritional components including carbohydrates, proteins, lipids that makes milk as good food and energy source. On the other hand, milk can be contaminated by pathogens from various sources and high nutritional contents help these pathogens to survive and grow in the milk. The contact or consumption of this contaminated milk or milk products may lead to variety of diseases with varying pathogenicity. Currently, these pathogens can be detected with conventional techniques but these methods are either tedious, laborious, time consuming and give non-precise results. Alternatively, molecular detection techniques can counter all these constrains but these methods give false negative results due to difficult isolation of genomic DNA of pathogens from milk or milk products. Therefore, pre-enrichment of the milk sample will not only allow the enrich the desired pathogens but it also facilitates the growth of viable but notculturable (VBNC) bacteria also. Finally, optimization of multiplex Real-Time PCR will enable to detect the pathogenic bacteria specifically and quicker. This will enable to declare a milk sample free from these important pathogenic bacteria simultaneously or to trace back the origin of contamination.

data.projectName: Polymeric composites for enhanced bioavailability of a quinone derivative
data.projectDigest: Treatment of diseases is done using chemicals, known as drugs. Drugs, in the form of medicine (tablet, capsules etc.), are mostly swallowed by the patients. After entering the digestive system, a drug must get dissolved in the digestive juice (which is water-based in nature) as solid drug cannot be absorbed from the digestive system to blood. Through blood, drug reaches specific receptors-site and stimulates them to start the desired clinical effects which relieve the disease. This is called bioavailability. Atovaquone is a diverse drug used in the treatment of malaria, Leishmaniasis, Babesiosis, PCP pneumonia and neurotoxoplasmosis. It has very poor bioavailability due to limited solubility in the digestive juice; therefore, it is given at high doses (1500 mg) to produce sufficient intensity clinical effects. High dose is not favourable to the patient, both economically and health-wise as some drugs are very expensive and produce bad side effects. This project aims at the microwave assisted  formulation of atovaquone to improve bioavailability through dissolution enhancement  which subsequently potentiate pharmacologic response by efficient absorption.

data.projectName: Development of Grid Integrated DFIG based Wind Energy Conversion System
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest: The Wind energy in Pakistan has an extremely bright future. There is no denying the fact that wind power plays an active role in the renewable energy sector. It is the major source in adding clean and non-polluting energy in the power grid. Contrary to this, fossil fuel based power plants produce tons of greenhouse gasses and CO2 emission into the atmosphere, which are directly responsible for global warming. Statistics show that about 67.4% of total electricity comes from burning fossil fuels that contribute 40% of total greenhouse gas emission. According to World Bank, around 1.1 billion people still do not have access to electricity due to non-availability of the electricity grid in these areas and other constraints. Pakistan has a huge potential of harnessing wind energy. The wind power can contribute towards the adequacy of power system network. On the contrary, as a developing country, Pakistan suffers from the poor infrastructure of Power System Network. The huge integration wind power generation with induction and synchronous generators may result into low power quality problems. It is necessary to address these problems for taking benefit from the natural resource in order to overcome the looming energy crisis in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Cost Effective Replacement of Natural Host (Cattle) with Experimental animals (Guinea pigs and Mice) for Adaptation of Foot and Mouth Disease Virus (O Serotype)
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Foot and mouth Disease is a fatal extremely spreading problem of cattle and small animals like sheep and goat in Pakistan. The disease is responsible for vast economic losses to livestock industry and restriction to trade is another threat to economy. Mutation is a continuous process of RNA family virus especially of FMD virus.  Cross protection is not present in different strains and sub strains of virus so effective vaccination is a complicated process to control the disease. A continuous surveillance of the disease out breaks, regular isolation and adaptation of virus and then after incorporation in vaccine can be an effective tool towards eradication program. According to available data FMD is a major disease problem in Punjab. The lack of proper infrastructure of our local laboratories, adaptation is not a routine job and the vaccines used in the field fail to provide proper immunization. Furthermore, cattle are difficult to use experimentally due to budget limitations. If some other animals like guinea pigs and mice can be used for this purpose, development procedures towards effective control and immunization of animals can be fastened.

data.projectName: Novel Solid Oxide Fuel Cell (SOFC) Electrodes for Stationary Applications
data.piUniversity: CECOS University of Information Technology and Emerging Sciences, Peshawar
data.projectDigest: The fuel cells represent an environmentally friendly and highly efficient alternative technology for energy production. In particular solid oxide fuel cells (SOFC’s) are among the most promising systems as they produce electric power and heat with lower noise, higher efficiency and low pollutant emissions than conventional heat engines, steam and gas turbines and combined cycle systems (GTCC) [1]. The SOFC units can use, in addition to hydrogen, alternative and commercially attractive fuels such as natural gas, biofuel, LPG and gasoline [1-2]. Nevertheless, SOFC’s using carbon containing fuels still meet lot of challenges arising from the fact that anodes operate under severe conditions leading to low activity towards oxidation reactions, instability due to the presence of Sulphur compounds and fast deactivation due to carbon formation [2-8]. Moreover, performance degradation of cathode due to the presence of SO2 in the oxygen or air supply further worsen the scenario [4-8]. Intensive research has been carried out on stated issues, however, no major technological breakthroughs have been so far with respect to robust operation, sufficient operational lifetime and competitive cost [1-5]. The aim of the proposed work is to address the Sulphur tolerance, carbon deposition and impure oxygen/air problem by the development of efficient electrodes inactive for cracking reactions and thus tolerant to degradation, for stationary power generation SOFC’s. Our approach is based on the deployment of two strategies to improve the electrodes: i) ceramic/metal oxide coatings (for example, gadolinium doped cerium oxide - GCO, samarium doped cerium oxide - SDC, PrO6 etc.) compatible with base material of electrodes (for example, LSCF), ii) composite electrode of ceramic/metal oxide with L

data.projectName: :  Establishment of Pakistan’s first Foresight Provincial Responsibility Index
data.piUniversity: National University of Modern Languages, Islamabad (NUML)
data.projectDigest: This project is about the establishment of Pakistan’s first Foresight Provincial Responsibility Index to create and foster the ecology of foresight perspectives in Pakistan with the stakeholders. It will enable the decision-makers opt for appropriate policy choice and establish strategic narrative in support. The future thinking basically facilitates the process of institutionalized decisions amongst the leadership corridors as an on-going deliberative practice looking at both medium and long-term implications of a policy action. This improves learning faculty and increases the quality of policy inputs and strategic outcomes – ultimately reducing the chances of policy failures. This project has a multidimensional focus, which will contribute towards stronger relationships and alliances among leaders from across organizations and sectors’ clearer intentions and commitments as to what these leaders need to do as a result of these insights, relationships, intentions, initiatives and actions to co-create better futures. The purpose of the Foresight Provincial Responsibility Index is to create Pakistan’s Futures’ Discourse Discussions on the futures not just for the domestic stakeholders but globally.

data.projectName: N-body simulation using heuristics
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The N-body problem is one of the classical mechanics problem. W.r.t to Physics, it deals with calculating the motions of celestial objects interacting with each other under the force of gravity. From the very beginning understanding the motions of the sun, planets, moons, and stars have always been a point of attention. Understanding the dynamics of cluster star systems has become an important n-body problem. N-body problem, however is not just limited to celestial gravitational impact analysis, same mechanics is also used in analyzing charged particles and their interactions. The goal of this study is to propose a simulation that is accurate but at the same time more efficient in terms of computational efficiency. We aim to simplify the simulation using a heuristic approach - heuristic refers to the algorithms which find best solution among the possible solutions.

data.projectName: Cleanify: Data-driven Solid Waste Management using Battery-less IoT
data.projectDigest: Major metropolitan cities of Pakistan face eminent crisis in solid waste disposal. At present, Pakistan generates about 48.5 million tons of solid waste a year, which has been increasing by more than 2 percent annually. Pakistan, like any other developing country, does not have an adequate waste management infrastructure that causes serious environmental problems. In the absence of proper infrastructure and financial constraints, some waste never gets collected (or gets delayed), causing a serious health and environmental risk. Regular cycles of checking and cleaning waste dumpster can provide a remedy, however, they put a financial burden on the resource-constrained local governments to provide humongous manpower to track the status of waste dumpsters manually. Solid waste disposal, thus, demands an effective and economically sustainable waste management system in order to minimize adverse environmental effects. In this project, we propose Cleanify, an IoT inspired waste management system. Cleanify envisions installation of cheap and maintenance-free battery-less IoT devices in waste dumpsters. These devices will sense the amount of waste in a dumpster and periodically report their measurements wirelessly to a centralized base station. The resulting, machine learning based, analysis of the data will ensure effective and cost-efficient waste collection and disposal through, for example, identification of waste hotspots that must be visited more frequently, suggestions for dumpster placement depending on where exactly they are needed, and optimal route planning for waste trucks to reduce operational costs and carbon footprint. Our major departure from existing work in this domain is the development of a maintenance-free and sustainable solution for developing economies.

data.projectName: Abstract analysis of solutions of certain fractional differential equations on time scales
data.projectDigest:
Fractional calculus, the study  of integration and differentiation of fractional order, has recently been extended to include its discrete analogues of fractional difference calculus and fractional quantum calculus. Due to this, there was a question whether there exist a single theory pertaining the above theory. Answer to this task was proposed by great scientist Stephen Hilger (1988), P. A. Williams and Bastos (2012), Jiang Zhu et al. (2013). This field is diverse, having a lot of applications in different fields of sciences such as: differential equations, probability theory, Mathematical and Economical models, optimization theory, signal processing, chaotic dynamics, atomic Bose-Einstein condensation, theory of inequalities etc.

Inequalities play a significant role in many branches of Sciences as well as to discuss the abstract analysis of the solutions of differential, difference equations and Cauchy type problems. The principle aim of the proposed work is to establish some fractional integral inequalities on time scales which can be used as powerful tools in the qualitative analysis of the solutions of certain fractional dynamic problems. We will discuss the modern theory of fractional time scale calculus which is helpful to find the solutions of complicated phenomena in a more descriptive and compact form.  

For the validity of the results established, we shall try to give applications to analyze the qualitative behavior of fractional dynamic equations such as fractional Stochastic differential equation on time scale.  Also, we shall try to apply our results in analyzing the model of financial system.

data.projectName: Development of Reliability based Design, Testing Methodologies and Computational Models for RF-MEMS Switches
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: RF MEMS offer outstanding characteristics in terms of low–loss, high–isolation, high quality factor, good linearity and tunability. RF MEMS field is a rapidly growing application area of MEMS technology, consisting of antennas, varactors, inductors, resonators, filters and RF MEMS switches. The main motivation for using small size and low mass MEMS devices for space applications is to reduce launching cost (current cost of launching spacecraft into Earth orbit is about $10,000 per Kg) their resistance to vibrations and radiations. The main limitation for incorporation of RF-MEMS in present space technologies is their reliability over billions of operating cycles. The long term reliable operation of MEMS in general and RF-MEMS in particular is dependent on material properties of thin film metal used for microfabrication. This requires the development of characterization procedures at micro level for reliability based characterization of metal thin films. At the design level MEMS designers generally use commercially available modeling software for design optimization of devices which have high costs. In this project, we propose to develop a universal testing machine at microscale, test microstructures, and micromanipulation tools using MEMS technology along with computational tools for the reliability based characterization of RF MEMS metal thin films

data.projectName: Investigation of charge-density- wave multiphases in rare-earth (RE) tritellurides RETe3 by using high-pressure and low-temperature Raman Spectroscopy
data.projectDigest:
This project is about to investigate the charge-density-wave (CDW) physics of Rare-earth (RE) tritelluride RETe3 compounds. These are layered compounds with 2D electronic structure and are known for multi CDW phases with the variation of temperature. The first type of CDW already exists at room temperature in many of RETe3 compounds. In some compounds, the CDW ordering with the application of external pressure is also observed. The phonon modes belonging to CDW amplitude are Raman active by symmetry. 

It is known that the pressure is an important parameter affecting the electronic and structural properties of the system and the external pressure is considered to be a cleaner way to tune the properties of the material compared to chemical pressure (doping) which additionally affects the translational symmetry of the crystal lattice and adds impurities during substitution.

data.projectDigest: In 1947 Punjab was divided into two parts. East Punjab was given to Pakistan and West Punjab remained under the domain of Indian Government.  In united Punjab two major communities Muslims and Sikhs lived together and contributed collectively in its economic growth. The both communities established their religious places and practiced their religion without any interference.  That's why the Sikh community still claims Punjab due to four reasons i.e. religious places, Land of their ancestral rulers, Punjabi as their mother tongue, settlement of canal colonies. This research is related to one aspect of the Sikh community in the Punjab i.e. the shrines / Gurdwaras of Sikh community  which exist in Eastern Punjab. Its a descriptive research in its nature and a historical compilation of the religious places. Punjab is an important province of Pakistan which contributes major share in the economy of Pakistan. It is necessary to preserve historically the religious places of minorities and to give impression to the world that the rights of the minorities in Pakistan are being fully observed through religious tolerance and religious harmony. The present research project will be carried out through the collection of data of the Sikh Gurdwaras which were established from time to time in Eastern Punjab. This project will present a positive and soft image of Pakistan nationally and internationally. It will also provide guidelines to the international tourists in Punjab that will contribute in the economy of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Real Time Mixed Criticality Scheduling on Multi Core Systems
data.projectDigest: The architecture of multicore consists of a single chip that incorporates the core logic of more than one processor whereas Mixed criticality system is a system containing computer software that can execute several applications of different criticality, such as safety-critical and non-safety critical, or of different Safety Integrity Level (SIL). Scheduling of mixed critical real time systems on multicore is one of the major issues in such real time systems. The objective of this research work is to design such scheduling algorithms that schedule the tasks in real time manner on multicore platform taking into consideration fault-tolerant, energy efficiency , reward based scheduling algorithm, compositional framework, pre-emption and migration overhead, task splitting mechanism, task dependency, mixed criticality system on Earliest Deadline First (EDF) scheduling and to develop efficient scheduling algorithm for mixed criticality system on multicore platforms of the IoT based real time systems.

data.projectName: Establishment of Ultra-sensitive blood test for brain-specific tau for the Early detection of Alzheimer’s disease.
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Alzheimer’s disease is a brain disease where brain cells die leading towards memory loss and intellectual competencies and symptoms get worse day by day leading to death. The exact reason of the disease is still not known but malnutrition and stress factors at childhood could be one reason. In Pakistan approximately 2 million cases referred/misdiagnosed as probable Alzheimer’s disease cases. With increase of average age, its occurrence is swiftly increasing in Pakistan, thus burdening the cost of health care, underscoring the need for primary preventive measures. 
This current proposed project will benefit both at patient level by detecting the disease at early stage and at national level by reducing the patient care burden. In Pakistan, currently there is no specific test available that confirms a diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease. This test will be the first detection system in Pakistan and will benefit the community at large scale. 
Project also interlinked with the ‘Pakistan-vision 2025: agenda by providing mental health care at cost effective manner, and comedies linked with malnutrition at childhood’. 
Ultimately, this proposed project will revolutionize the costly, non-reachable PET scans and brain-fluid test (cost approximately 50,000-150000Pkr) to blood-based (1500-5000Pkr) cost effective test system, leading towards the therapeutic interventions.

data.projectName: “Syntheses and Biological Evaluation of the Selective Inhibitors of 17?-Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase and Novel Tubulin-Binding Agents: Potential New Drugs for Cancer Treatment”
data.projectDigest:
Breast cancer is the most common cancer among women, Nearly 2.1 million women are suffering each year, and also causes the greatest number of cancer-related deaths among women. Approximately, 627,000 women died from breast cancer in 2018, nearly 15% of all cancer deaths among women.
Starting from the three-dimensional structures of both the protein and its substrate E1 it was possible to derive a pharmacophore model which led to the discovery of highly potent, non-steroidal inhibitors of 17beta-HSD1. Therefore, we envision the synthesis of structurally simple steroidomimetics from commercially available tetralone, indole aldehyde, benzofuran aldehyde and indazole-6-carboxaldehyde. These analogs (Fig 2) retain active phenolic hydroxy groups, but have aromatic and heteroaromatic rings which could bind more easily with the enzyme systems. 
Another aim of this proposal is synthesis and biological evaluation of novel tubulin-binding drugs that will be the potential new drug molecules for the treatment of cancer. During the course of the research work small molecules will be synthesized from the commercially available starting materials. The innovative aspect of this research proposal is that the designed compounds have similarity with tubulin-binding combretastatin, antiestrogen tamoxifen and also have structural diversity. Moreover, these compounds will be synthesized by using an easy and economical methodology. The designed compounds are all aimed at improving on (1) anti-tumour activity, (2) toxicity profile and (3) pharmacology. The overall aim of this research proposal is: To design inhibitors of 17beta-HSD1, tubulin-binding and antiangiogenic agents as the potential new drugs for cancer treatment with an improved activity, selectivity and drug likeness.

data.projectName: Virtual World to Increase Social Emotional Learning
data.projectDigest:
The physical, emotional, and social development of young kids has a direct effect on their overall development and adult life. Emotions are an essential part of cognitive reasoning because the brain cannot organize priorities and make decisions without it. 
Latterly, emotional intelligence has become a popular topic of research. 
Studies about children showed a downswing impact in emotional conditions beyond the industrial and social world. This trend is throwback by anxiety, widespread withdrawal, depression, short attention span, and neglectful behavior. Children should be trained for emotional intelligence skill. This research aims to develop a game based virtual world that provides scenario-based learning opportunities to the children so that their skills of emotional self-awareness, emotional management, empathy, relationship management, and conflict resolution improves.

data.projectName: Fabrication of metal oxide based Green nanoparticles(GNPs) devices and their applications for the treating metabolic disorders
data.projectDigest: The state of art to use metal oxide  green nanoparticles ( MOGNPs) is relatively emerging field in many sectors to improve economy ; there is growing interest in biological and environmental safety of their production. The main objective of this work is to synthesize MOGNPs, detailed structural and optical characterization and fabrication of MOGNPs based devices i.e., batteries and cells to detect different metabolites in blood. The detection of blood metabolites, ultimately, helps us to know the status of health. Consequently, the stage of metabolic disorders can be diagnosed efficiently and, later on, treated according to its relative stage. Briefly, the analysis of MOGNPs would be based on their structural and optical characterization, antimicrobial effect and effects on human cells. The device will be fabricated after an extensive physical and biological characterization of MOGNPs to diagnose and treat metabolic disorders.

data.projectName: Fake Twitter Trends Detection using Artificial Intelligence
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest: The research project is targeted towards detecting “fake trends” and the accounts that are used to generate them. A fake trend is one which does not result from a natural trending process and may, in full or in part, be artificially promoted by user(s) with intention to quickly generate enough activity so as to make it into the list of top trends. The proposed project will provide a framework to accomplish the task. We will conduct research in ways to gather data from such social media platforms, analyze them in real-time (or very quickly), and detect fake trends before they become viral. The proposed framework could be used in a generic manner and may, in future, be applied to other frameworks and data types. It will incorporate ideas from APIs, data warehousing, text processing and analysis, natural language processing, graph theory, and artificial intelligence.

data.projectName: Mitigating the impact of climate change through managing agroforestry systems in central Punjab
data.projectDigest: The impact of climate change on agriculture, plant health and forest sector is visible in all continents of the world. Among developing countries Pakistan has severely been affected by climate change. In Pakistan some research work has been conducted in agriculture sector in relation to rapidly changing climatic conditions but almost no or very little research has been carried out to study the role of agroforestry systems in climate change mitigation. Similarly agroforestry systems are not practiced on scientific basis in Pakistan. So there is an urgent need of the time to determine the ecosystem services being provided by the trees in various agroforestry systems to create awareness by using appropriate channels. This will be a field oriented project that will involve farming community (agroforesters) we well. Tree inventories will be maintained for proper stock assessment and for identifying the role of farm trees in climate change mitigation. Role of trees in microclimate and soil properties modification will also be determined. It will foster economic stability through risk diversification at farmlands with good economic returns in changing climate. Hence, the designed project is aimed to quantify the agroforestry services and to assess the role of agroforestry practices in the mitigation of climate change.

data.projectName: HEALTH AND SAFETY RISK MINIMIZATION, AND ACCIDENTS REDUCTION IN THE WORKING MINES OF PAKISTAN
data.projectDigest: Mining is one of the most hazardous and risky professions worldwide. Each year, thousands of miners are involved in mine accidents which cause large number of fatalities, minor, and major injuries. Due to the improved mining practices and technological advancement, mine fatalities and accidents are generally decreasing worldwide. Today, mining in technologically advanced mining countries like the USA, Australia Canada, South Africa has become much safer. Contrary to many mining countries, accidents rate in Pakistan mining sector is very high. Mining in Pakistan, especially underground mines operate in a very unique way, as most of these mines are still using primitive mining practices. In addition, factors like thin coal seams, depleting resources, small sized mine openings, and unorganized mining, has increased health hazards and safety risks. This ultimately causes more accidents. Accidents rate in Pakistan mining industry can be improved by properly studying mine accidents, identifying their causes, and suggesting their controls. In addition, establishing risk ratings for mine hazard, improving accidents reporting and investigations protocols can improve overall mine health and safety conditions. This research aims to address existing gaps in the area of mine health, safety and promote the culture of safety in Pakistan mining industry.

data.projectName: Towards a Mountain Information System: Development of interactive Hazard Assessment Information Tool for Landslides and GLOFs in Gilgit-Baltistan
data.piUniversity: Karakurum International University, Gilgit, Gilgit Baltistan
data.projectDigest: Gilgit-Baltistan (GB), located in the north of Pakistan, has geographical as well as economic importance particularly in the context of China-Pakistan Economic Corridor as it provides the only connecting highway between China and Pakistan. In addition, GB attracts millions of domestic and foreign tourists each year and this trend is increasing day by day. On the other hand, due to climatic change conditions, the glaciers and mountainous areas of GB due their high sensitiveness are facing a lot of challenges that include increase in frequency of landslides along highways and raise in glacial lake outburst flood (GLOFs) events. Most of the time, these landslides and GLOFs events results into loss of many lives like Attabad, Hunza lake event where 19 people loss their lives and economic properties. To minimize and avoid such types of events there is a need to use the latest technologies like Artificial Intelligence (AI) and web GIS to provide tourists and local population an updated information regarding landslide and GLOFs.  To develop such a tool as the first step there is a need to develop an authentic or validated database of landslides and GLOFs for a specific area which we can use as reference data to validate our AI classification algorithms and initial results. Once, we are sure of our high accuracy of classification algorithms of AI, we will select the best algorithm to develop the database of landslides and GLOFs for the whole GB. In the next step, a time series of the database will be developed using open and multi-source remotely sensed data. Then users will be provided current and future trends of susceptibility indices for the whole GB.

data.projectName: Characterization of air pollution particulates: Toxicity to human and plant cells and remediation by local large tree species
data.projectDigest: The proposed study will help to find out the Particulate matter (PM) concentrations in the 3 most populated cities (Faisalabad, Lahore, Rawalpindi) of Pakistan and analyze their toxic effects on human  epidermal cells, lung cells, growth and structure of cells of edible crop species and remediation potential of large tree species to reduce the PAH concentration in soil. The idea behind the project is that population increase is causing increased use of vehicles this increase is causing excessive emission of PM in the environment, the components of PM such as metals and PAHs are a threat for the human and plant health. The pm concentrations will be measured by using high volume sampler and micro dust pro sampler from Faisalabad, Lahore and Sialkot. The PM samples collected will be extracted and analyzed to find out the concentrations of 16 priority polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in the sample at different sites as these are known to cause toxic effects in human beings and plant species. These extracts then will be given as a treatment to human white blood cells, lung cells, epidermal cells and the toxic effects will be assessed using different end point indicators .

data.projectName: Quantum Computing based IoT Security Solution
data.projectDigest: Internet of Things (IoT) is a global infrastructure comprised of smart sensors, processing system (an embedded system) and heterogeneous communication networks.  All these technologies interconnect directly or indirectly through internet to form the infrastructure of the IoT network. Since a large amount of user specific data is being generated, the security and privacy of an IoT network is a key challenge for the technology’s wide scale deployment. In this project, we shall define a security and privacy model for the perception layer to ensure Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability and Authentication (CIAA). We shall be developing the cryptographic suit encompassing CIAA capabilities for resource constraint IoT nodes. The resource constraint IoT nodes have limited power and computational resources, therefore, the security model will be based on ultralightweight algorithms. . In proposed model, rules of quantum cryptography will be implemented for key distribution. This will enhance the confusion and diffusion capabilities of public messages being communicated at perception layer.
