The resource constraint IoT nodes have limited power and computational resources, therefore, the security model will be based on ultralightweight algorithms. . In proposed model, rules of quantum cryptography will be implemented for key distribution. This will enhance the confusion and diffusion capabilities of public messages being communicated at perception layer.

data.projectName: Identification of Novel Scaffolds for the Inhibition of Enzymes Associated With Alzheimers Disease, Reversing the Memory Loss and Cognitive Deficits
data.piUniversity: Abbottabad University of Science & Technology (AUST), Abbottabad
data.projectDigest: Every three seconds, someone in our world develops underlying progression to Alzheimer’s disease (AD). It is a neurodegenerative disorder, responsible for progressive loss of memory coupled with additional cognitive deficits like clarity in thinking, decline in decision making, impairment with speech and overall communication. Around 3.5 million Pakistanis are suffering from Alzheimer’s preventable conditions but the number is mounting. It becomes irreversible if not timely treated as the survival period is 8 years after first diagnosis. Since (AD) is linked with old age (early 60s) so millions are at risk and may be affected worldwide as average life-expectancy has increased. It will clearly lead to an extensive burden on health, society and economy around the globe. In absence of a medical cure or definitive cause and diagnosis till date, (AD) is one of the six incurable reasons of death. The purpose of this study is to explore potent and highly selective inhibitors for the eradication of this devastating disease. A vast and resourceful compound bank developed with the collaboration of highly advanced research labs across the world will be systematically investigated for potential molecules via High Throughput Screening. From the promising compounds, the most active candidates will be selected as “lead” for further multitargetted trials and Molecular Docking Studies.

data.projectName: Nephroprotective activity of Dodonaea viscosa (L.) in drug induced nephrotoxic animal model: in-vivo and in-silico experiments
data.projectDigest: Recently, kidney failure has become a major cause of mortality and morbidity around the world. Renal failure is a life-threatening condition in which kidneys are unable to perform its function properly. The major cause of renal failure is nephrotoxicity which is due to use of certain drugs or environmental toxins, thus leading to temporary or permanent renal impairment. Thus, the focus on drug-induced nephrotoxicity has been increased as it is a significant contributor in acute and chronic kidney failure. The treatment of kidney disease is highly complicated as it requires multiple interventions with long-term hospitalization and financial burden. Many commonly used drugs are responsible for nephrotoxicity including antibiotics, anticancer drugs, NSAIDS etc. In Pakistan nephrotoxicity due to use of certain drugs is increasing day by day, creating a burden on country. This leads to high mortality rate due to kidney failure in Pakistan. Therefore, the present project is designed to investigate nephroprotective effect of Dodonaea viscosa (L.) Jacq., belongs to family Spindaceae and found in many areas of Pakistan. Previously D. viscosa has been investigated for number of activities but its nephroprotective effect has not been investigated yet. Therefore, its extracts will be investigated for cisplatin and gentamicin-induced nephrotoxicity.

data.projectName: Breaking into Transgender Life through Media: An Exploration of Transgender Audiences’ Lived Experiences in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: This research will identify the ground realities that at this critical juncture of the history of Pakistan, how the media constructs the identity of third gender. The researcher would employ the constructionist perspective framing to investigate the framing techniques used to construct the identity of transgender in Islamic Republic of Pakistan. This would help to understand and pursue further in the field opening new avenues for the media providing opportunities to understand the issue under examination. The study will help to develop an understanding regarding the sensitivity of the matter through media and also seeking response from the other major stake holders including civil society and the state examining the issue focusing multiple perspectives. The study will provide a platform to investigate the issue in hand working jointly with media, civil society, state along with other key stake holders. The study will help to provide a road-map for future studies as well providing an opportunity to investigate further in the field under investigation.

data.projectName: Developing an Intelligent Virtual Laboratory Tool Using Intelligent Agent Technology
data.projectDigest: A virtual laboratory offers an integrated environment of web services through which one can perform/run experiments online from anywhere, as long as they have access to internet. It also facilitates those students who have an accessibility issue, especially those in rural areas who also face the problem of lack of required experimental equipment due to high cost. An intelligent Virtual Laboratory (IVL) tool enables virtual lab projects to be carried out as these labs are available online. IVL can facilitate and improve the practical experience and can enhance investigative learning of students. A virtual lab tool is one of the challenging aspects in the distribution on a large scale of online experimentation in the distance and blended education system due to lack of practical lab instruments in science laboratories and limitation of insufficient time, geographically need, financially and maintaining the lab equipment for many institutions in developing country like Pakistan. The proposed project aims at developing the cognitive architecture based pedagogical agent for monitoring and guide students during the practical task work in different fields of science and technology. In this project, the pedagogical agent will guide the students for performing different practical courses Lab tasks based on cognitive ability.

data.projectName: Identification of diagnostic and anti-virulence targets for diabetic foot infections in Punjab
data.projectDigest: Diabetes and its complications including foot ulcer constitute a global public health challenge attributing to a significant cause of morbidity and mortality. Foot ulcer is one of the long-term complication of diabetes which lead to infection and amputation of lower extremities. This creates health, social and economic burden. The pathophysiology of diabetic foot infections (DFIs) is relatively complex and their prevalence and severity are largely depending upon diabetic pateint’s immunopathy, arteriopathy and neuropathy as well as bacterial features (microbial load, microbial diversity, virulence, and antibiotic- resistance). Mostly, the mixed micro-flora is present in infectious foot ulcers.  Therefore, choosing the most suitable antibiotic drug needs defining the specific causative pathogens. If clinicians well aware about type of infection and their drug susceptibility pattern, then they can select and prescribe effective antimicrobial treatment. Analysis of microbial community with respect to their virulence potential and drug susceptibility profile will be very helpful for diabetic ulcer treatment and management. Outcomes of this work will help to find out any correlation between virulence profile with disease severity and drug susceptibility. The virulence gene profile of DFI will provide baseline data for anti-virulence therapy. This will help clinicians to successfully and timely treat DFI.

data.projectName: SOCIO-ECONOMIC DETERMINANTS OF TAX FILERS: A MICRODATA COMPARISONS ACROSS FEDERAL AND PROVINCIAL CAPITALS OF PAKISTAN
data.projectDigest:
Narrow tax base is also one of the main reasons in low tax collection in developing countries. Broadening the tax base has proven as the biggest challenge for the complete nation. By increasing the number of tax filers leads to have been successfully increased in documented economy, simplifying tax administration, increase the tax coverage, government introduces the broader governance and regulatory reforms. The objective of the present study is to empirically explore the determinants of tax filers. Data will be collected from federal capital and all the provinces of Pakistan. The survey method is used to collect information and 1000 questionnaires will be distributed among tax filers and non-tax filers across the regions. 
The major purpose of the study is to evaluate the reasons of not filing tax returns and determinants of filing tax return in Pakistan. Previous researches put variety of components in e-filing system in all over the nation. In the present study, we will discuss the profile of the tax filers and determinants of tax filer’s i.e. demographic factors, socio-economics factors, economic factors and tax related factors.

data.projectName: Enhancing Automobile Recycling in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
The automotive industry of Pakistan is among the fastest growing industries of the country, accounting for 4% of Pakistan’s GDP with over 1.8 million of employees. Presently, there are 3,200 automotive manufacturing plants across the country with an investment of 92 billion PKR (US$ 595 million), producing over 200,000 vehicles annually as of 2018-19. Automobile recycling is the major target of this applied research. Considering the fact that no proper vehicle recycling is being done in Pakistan at the moment, which is also the need of the time when automotive sector of Pakistan is facing persistent inflation and relentless devaluation, this applied-research project could turn out to be a boon to flip the lowering industrial growth into a stepping stone towards the zenith. This will not only benefit the automotive industry in Pakistan but also embark a rapid industrial evolution as more material will be recycled rather than discarded.
Proposed research project is sought to complete in the span of two years, together with the development of Automotive Recycling Laboratory in NED University of Engineering and Technology, Karachi. Upon successful investigation of the modified recycled material, the industrial and institutional link could prove to be a dynamic step to increase productivity and interest of students in the automotive sector. This methodology will undoubtedly escalate the research in the field of material recycling and will positively affect the economic growth with high internal manufacturing and low import from abroad. Not to negate the fact that Pakistan has an abundant supply of end-of life vehicles (ELVs), there is an utmost need to rehabilitate the effective material from within the abandoned ones without letting them sold at the prices of the scrap.

data.projectName: Characterization of a series of hits against Phosphoglycerate Mutase 1 to give a lead for the treatment of oral cancer
data.projectDigest:
Oral cancer is 11th most common cancer worldwide while 1st leading cause of cancer deaths in Pakistan with an estimated 5-year prevalence of 30647 cases and 7266 deaths in 2012. Despite advances in surgery, the 5-year survival rate of oral cancer remains less than 50% after diagnosis. Therefore, there is an urgent need for the development of the novel therapeutics against oral cancer. 
It is now widely recognized that targeting the cancer specific metabolic and mitochondrial remodeling may offer selectivity in cancer treatment. One of such promising novel anti-cancer drug targets is Phosphoglycerate Mutase 1 (PGAM1). PGAM1 predominantly overexpress in a number of tumors such as oral cancer and its inhibition results in decreased tumor growth and metastasis. Therefore, targeting PGAM1 has potential to provide selective treatment for oral cancer. This drug discovery approach represents a paradigm shift to develop new therapeutics, ultimately addressing the concerns for toxicity and non-selectivity of available chemo drugs which have restricted their widespread application and efficacy.
We have successfully identified novel anticancer drug candidates of PGAM1 (5/600000 hits) by in silico screening. To generate IC50 values, a second screen by enzymatic activity assays will be performed. We will typify the mechanism of action and potential ability of these hits during screen using recent technique termed as cellular thermal shift assay. Animal model and cancer xenografts will be considered to generate in vivo Proof of concept. Further, in vivo studies will be carried out to evaluate toxicological profile. At the end of the project, intellectual property of novel drug candidate will be protected and negotiated with a pharmaceutical industry for pilot scale commercialization.

data.projectName: Denim dyeing effluent treatment by electro-coagulation for maximum reduction in indigo and sulphur black dye discharge.
data.projectDigest: This project is about wastewater treatment of a major pollutant, denim textile dying dyes. Denim textile dying is one of the largest users of vat and sulphur dyes. The dying waste is dumped directly into waste streams by the textile manufacturers causing enormous pollution. This project will address reduction of the polluting waste by its pretreatment using the electrocoagulation technique. The electrocoagulation of denim dye wastes have has already been successfully tested at the Department of Applied Chemistry Electrocoagulation Labs and at pilot scale at the Indigio Textiles Port Qasim Karachi. It is a powerful and even a low-cost option offering high removal efficiencies, especially for dyes. It is a low temperature process and requires no additional chemicals. On average, 80 – 96% reduction in COD is achieved. The unique characteristics of the electrochemical oxidation process are its ease and  robustness of operation. It is possible that this process could be developed as a cost-effective technology for textile wastewater treatment.

data.projectName: STUDY OF COMPARATIVE VIRULENCE FACTORS DETERMINATION IN HOSPITAL-ACQUIRED AND COMMUNITY-ACQUIRED STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS AT HYDERABAD, PAKISTAN
data.projectDigest:
Facultative pathogenic Staphylococcus aureus are part of the normal commensals of skin and nasal membranes in15 – 30 % healthy individuals. 
These Gram-positive cocci are known to be associated with infections in both community (Community associated S. aureus CA-SA) and hospital environment (Hospital associated S. aureus HA-SA).
This study is designed to comprehend aggressiveness markers in CA-SA and HA-SA strains isolated from healthy carriers and clinical samples from hospitals at Hyderabad region. To understand how these clinical isolates differ from commensal strains to evaluate the importance and impact of virulence in the evolution of the resistance phenotype. The determination of comparative virulence traits in S. aureus among asymptomatic carriers and from infection(s) would be suggestive for precise host-pathogen interaction and ultimately decision making process by healthcare individuals. 
Besides virulence factors I want to focus on factors that are involved in colonization and survival during infection. These factors are particularly enzymes that modify the lipid structure of lipoproteins and that modify the bacterial cell wall. Therefore, I am also interested in the role of lipoprotein diacylglyceryl transferase (lgt) and O-acetyl-peptidoglycan transferase (oatA). Both genes (corresponding enzymes) play a crucial role in immune stimulation, colonization, host cell invasion and inflammation in S. aureus.

data.projectName: Poloxamer and polyoxyethylated nonionic surfactant based targeted vesicular drug delivery system of flutamide for effective prostate cancer therapy
data.projectDigest:
Prostate cancer is a disease very common in males after age of 50 years all over the world including Pakistan. Flutamide is highly recommended for the treatment of prostate cancer. Flutamide is poorly water soluble drug and hence has poor bioavailability which results into less therapeutic benefits. In addition to this flutamide is metabolized in liver extensively. Dose of flutamide is 250mg thrice a day.  Conventional products of Flutamide (Tablets) offer drawbacks such as poor bioavailability, unaccepptability to patients for multiple doses and side effects.
Modern era is focussing on research for presenting anticancer drugs with good therapeutic outcomes, minimum doses (convenient for patients), and less side effects. In the field of pharmaceutical  Nonionic surfactants based vesicles have drawn considerable attention to solve such medical issues. The proposed research is an attempt to suppress such  shortcomings of conventional treatments of prostate cancer through developing niosome vesicle of drugs. The suggested raw material used for preparation include poloxamers and polyoxyethylated surfactants  have potential to address solubility and toxicity of drugs. Therefore flutamide will be prepared in the form of vesicles .i.e niosomes, their properties will be determined as quality control tests, how vesicles liberate drug from their micro-environment will be performed. After successful evaulaution (lab tests), further investigations will be extended to assess behavior of flutamide vesicles in biological subjects (rats/rabbits). Treatment with newly prepared vesicles of flutamide is anticipated to have minimum side  effects, once time dosing (making patients more convenient) and improve therapeutic outcomes.

data.projectName: Theoretical Study of   Electromagnetic Wave  Interaction with Quantum Plasma and Parametric Instabilities
data.piUniversity: Kohat University of Science and Technology, Kohat
data.projectDigest:
Plasma is a many body complex system of charged and neutral particles. Temperature and density are the two important parameters which describe the state of plasma. When the density is very large and /or temperature is very low, the associated wave functions of the constituent particles (generally the lighter ones) start overlapping and the quantum effects (quantum diffraction, barrier tunneling, spin dynamics, Bohm potential, etc.) must be included to study the numerous linear and nonlinear properties of quantum plasma. An ordinary example of quantum plasma is the electron gas in metals. When the wavelength of the dynamical component/s is of the order of the Compton length (  ) then it starts to oscillate with speed comparable to the speed of light, and relativistic effects come into play its role in changing the dynamics of the plasma. Different mathematical models have been developed to study the linear and nonlinear properties of the quantum plasma in both non-relativistic and relativistic regimes. Some of these models are: i) Hydrodynamic model ii) Schrodinger-Maxwell model iii) Klein-Gordon-Maxell model iv) Dirac-Maxell model etc.
	In this project we will study the interaction of electromagnetic wave with the multi-components (electron, positron, hole, ion etc.) quantum plasma (both non-relativistic and relativistic) by using the appropriate mathematical models.  The coupling between electromagnetic wave and quantum plasma will be carried out through Maxwell equations with the help of electromagnetic scalar and vector potentials.  We will solve these coupled equations by Fourier analysis and will study different linear and non-linear properties analytically as well as computationally.

Plasma is a many body complex system of charged and neutral particles. Temperature and density are the two important parameters which describe the state of plasma. When the density is very large and /or temperature is very low, the associated wave functions of the constituent particles (generally the lighter ones) start overlapping and the quantum effects (quantum diffraction, barrier tunneling, spin dynamics, Bohm potential, etc.) must be included to study the numerous linear and nonlinear properties of quantum plasma. An ordinary example of quantum plasma is the electron gas in metals. When the wavelength of the dynamical component/s is of the order of the Compton length (  ) then it starts to oscillate with speed comparable to the speed of light, and relativistic effects come into play its role in changing the dynamics of the plasma. Different mathematical models have been developed to study the linear and nonlinear properties of the quantum plasma in both non-relativistic and relativistic regimes. Some of these models are: i) Hydrodynamic model ii) Schrodinger-Maxwell model iii) Klein-Gordon-Maxell model iv) Dirac-Maxell model etc.
	In this project we will study the interaction of electromagnetic wave with the multi-components (electron, positron, hole, ion etc.) quantum plasma (both non-relativistic and relativistic) by using the appropriate mathematical models.  The coupling between electromagnetic wave and quantum plasma will be carried out through Maxwell equations with the help of electromagnetic scalar and vector potentials.  We will solve these coupled equations by Fourier analysis and will study different linear and non-linear properties analytically as well as computationally.

data.projectName: Climate Smart Enhancement of Forest Resources through Socioeconomic Motivation
data.piUniversity: University of Kotli Azad Jammu and Kashmir
data.projectDigest: Urbanization and dependency on forest resources for livelihood requirements is the major threat to forest ecosystems. Synergies between poverty and forest exploitation is key limiting factor that is yet to be addressed to design and implement climate change mitigation. Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) need to be examined in this context for rational use of forest resources as it they comprise some of the vital vegetation cover of temperate region in Pakistan. We therefore propose climate smart holistic framework to ensure that (i) forest health in AJK is enhanced; (ii) livelihood of forest-dependent population is preserved; (iii) carbon sequestration stock is monitored and verified; (iv) threat linked with social determinants are transformed into outcomes of climate smart forest initiatives. By converging all these targets into forest preservation, we anticipate to develop specific guidelines to encourage local population to use forest resources in sustainable way. This proposed project will follow an approach based on raising awareness among local people of AJK inhabiting selected forest reserves that they are sole custodian of this vital ecosystem entity and must adopt sustainable livelihood practice to slow down the negative impacts of climate change on forest ecosystem.

data.piUniversity: National College of Business Administration & Economics, Lahore
data.projectDigest: It’s important to appreciate that this is highly multidisciplinary research that addresses some fundamental questions of how we learn, what part is played by our eyes, what part is played by our ears and what part is playing by the feeling of touch. If any of the feelings are absent then conventional pedagogy fail to provide any substantial results and we need to go back to the fundamental question of how we learn. To limit the scope of this research, we limit ourselves to high school physics and mathematics. We concentrate on these two subjects because they pose a relatively higher challenge and a solution for one may help us in the other domain.

Collar rot, caused by Sclerotium rolfsii. is of prime importance in reducing its yield in Pakistan and many other countries. Generally, chemical fungicides are used to control soil-borne diseases. data.projectName: SentiACM: Sentiment based Access Control Management in Online Social Networks
data.projectDigest:
We propose a novel access control management technique where we harness the power of social networks to diffuse resources through the use of sentiment analysis techniques. The contribution of this work will be the measurement and classification of trust to act as an attribute for rule based access control models.
The impact of our research will be:
i.	The fields of Psychology, Sociology, Law and Technology will be combined to provide security and privacy of social network users of the society.
ii.	National image will be improved by giving priority to the basic human right of privacy.
iii.	Peoples trust on technology will be regained in the region as social media information has been an avenue of harassment and blackmailing in the past.
iv.	New tools and technologies will be introduced to the students that will work on the project

data.projectName: Communicating Health Campaigns: Assessment and Preventive Measures for Controlling the Epidemic of Dengue
data.projectDigest: Dengue fever (DF) is a mosquito-borne viral infection. Given the existing approximations of over 100 million cases universal each year and over 2.5 billion individuals at the risk of infection; it is now considered as one of the most important arthropod-borne diseases from a public health point of view.  In Pakistan, dengue is emerging as a major public health hazard. The situation has recently become more severe due to increasing number of complicated and uncomplicated cases on a background of limited resources, poor socio-economic conditions and lack of public health awareness. In 1994, first time Dengue reported in Pakistan, but the country witnessed a major outbreak of dengue fever in 2011. Since then government of Pakistan launching dengue prevention campaigns through mass media. In 2014 government of Punjab started Standard Operating Procedures (Sops) for 2014 Prevention & Control of Dengue, campaigns through media were part of that project. While campaigns have launched for public awareness, but this disease is not stopping. A total of 19,296 dengue positive cases have been confirmed as of 2 October 2019 based on Federal Disease Surveillance and Response Unit from Field Epidemiology and Disease Surveillance Division. The aim of this research project is to evaluate the past campaigns for preventive measures and find out better communication techniques, finding lope holes and create a new communication strategy for creating awareness regarding prevention of dengue fever in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Conversion of a conventional X-Ray machine to a digital radiography (DR) system
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
X-ray machine is first contact of a patient brought to hospital for radio-graphic diagnosis.  Conventional X-ray machines have certain limitations like delays and cost involved in film processing, subjective reporting, dark room requirements and non-provision of online transmission of diagnostic reports. Advanced trends in X-ray technology such as Computerized Radiography (CR) Systems and Digital Radiography (DR) Systems do cater for above mentioned limitations but at an exponentially higher price tag. 
This research proposes a cost effective solution for addressing limitations of a conventional X-ray machine by retrofitting Flat Panel Detectors (FPD) and thus converting a conventional X-ray machine to a Digital Radiography (DR) System at a very low cost.

data.projectName: Development of Nanoparticles (NPs) based methods to detect adulterations and authenticity of Basmati Rice
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest:
Rice is second major cereal crop of Pakistan after wheat and is a major source of foreign exchange. The regular mixing of unapproved basmati and long grained non-Basmati indica with the traditional and approved basmati by the traders/exporters for their personal financial benefits are spoiling the reputation of Pakistan in the world market. 

Among modern genomic analysis tools, DNA fingerprinting show the promise of providing unbiased and broad approach in detecting biologically relevant differences among morphologically similar rice type. But this is a tedious, cumbersome and expensive approach. Nanomaterials based devices such as nano-biosensors may prove a good option to resolve the issue of Basmati rice adulteration.

In proposed project, we aim to develop nanoparticles based DNA detection of different basmati varieties and their adulterants. All Basmati varieties from different institutes of Pakistan and their adulterants will be screened for the detection SNPs/InDels. The identified SNPs/InDels will be targeted for making nanoparticle based probes. The method would be efficient and cost effective in comparison to available techniques being used.
This is a novel approach for the detection of adulteration in basmati rice as no study has been published in any crop so far for within species individual identification.

data.projectName: Carbon Sequestration in Agricultural and Humus Deprived Soils through Solid Waste Compost: A Potential Solution to Enhance Carbon Credits of Pakistan and to Combat Climate Change
data.projectDigest:
This project suggests mitigation and adaption mechanism to combat the global issue of climate change as a consequence of addressing the local and severely damaging issue of solid waste mismanagement and soil degradation. It is proposed to apply compost prepared from the organic fraction of solid waste on soils that have lost their organic matter or humus over the years due to intensive agricultural practices and landform changes. This familiar technique will not only revive the soil stability, fertility and yield, but also achieve long term storage of carbon in the soil sinks. 
The implementation, however, is the tricky part of this well-known technique and this is where there is a need for policy intervention. Landowners, farmers and municipalities must be encouraged for compost application instead of chemical fertilizers due to the numerous long term benefits of this natural replenishment of soil nutrients. This can be realized with the help of utilizing the concept of carbon trading system. This is a system where credits holding economic value are given to entities that are achieving carbon offset through their operational projects. Compost facilities can earn these credits in exchange for offsetting greenhouse gas emission from decomposing waste whereas parties responsible for application of this compost will be given carbon credits in return for storing carbon into the land that they own. These credits can then be sold to companies or countries that have been limited in their carbon emissions under Kyoto Protocol and wish to sustain their economic activity.

data.projectName: Studies on acute and chronic toxicity of some pesticides to major carps
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Pesticides are generally applied widely in forestry, agriculture, veterinary practices and public health. These pesticides find their way to water bodies by leaching through different channels. Their bioaccumulation in the bodies of aquatic animals particularly fish induces physiological changes ultimately causing fish mortality. The accumulation of these pesticides not only causing fish mortality but also biomagnifying in food chain ultimately causing damage to human health as human is the largest consumer of fish. Water quality deterioration has been as issue since years and many research has done on heavy metals pollution. These days pesticides are causing severe damage to animals and need to be worked out. Pesticides are used against insects, water weeds, plant diseases and in agriculture, however, highly toxic to untargeted organisms.  These pesticides have also been detected in the soil, sediments, surface and river waters, food stuffs and atmosphere. The toxicity of pesticides has created a situation to cause serious damage to the fish fauna in the natural water bodies. The study has been planned to study the harmful effects of these pesticides on fish. 
The major carps viz. Catla catla, Labeo rohita and Cirrhina mrigala will show variable tolerance limits against individual pesticides viz. bifenthrin, Endosulfan and carbofuran. Toxicity trials will evaluate the toxicity biomarkers. Fish growth will predict and integrate all the toxic effects of pesticide toxicity in the fish body.
This project will be helpful in exploring the health hazards of pesticides to fish that ultimately cause worst effects to Human beings. This experiment will be helpful in determining the permissible limits of pesticides.

data.projectName: Entrepreneurial Grants: Predicting the Success and Evaluating the Performance of Beneficiaries of Prime Minister’s Kamyab Jawan Youth Entrepreneurship Scheme
data.piUniversity: National University of Modern Languages, Islamabad (NUML)
data.projectDigest: The research project titled “Entrepreneurial Grants: Predicting the Success and Evaluating the Performance of Beneficiaries of Prime Minister’s Kamyab Jawan Youth Entrepreneurship Scheme” is intended to benefit multi folds: Firstly, the project intends to develop a criteria to predict the success of the awardees of the recent Prime Minister’s Kamyab Jawan Program to support entrepreneurial culture in Pakistan. For this purpose Analysis shall be conducted to predict whether the awardees of entrepreneurial grant will be successful in their ventures or not. Secondly, the project shall perform a  longitudinal evaluation of the Awardees of the Prime Minister’s Kamyab Jawan Program across a three year period from June 2020 to June 2023. This shall require self-administered data collection using questionnaire at multiple time periods. Thirdly, it shall serve to perform a periodic review of the performance of the Awardees. Fourthly, it shall enable the researchers to make recommendations for success of similar programs in the future.  Lastly, the study shall provide descriptive as well as quantitative assessment of the Prime Minister’s Kamyab Jawan Program. The researchers shall use qualitative and quantitative assessment tools for the above purposes. The analysis of the data shall provide the discussion platform for future benefits academically as well as to sectoral stakeholders for Award of Government Funding for Startups.

data.projectName: Development and genetic evaluation of new cotton mutant lines with enhanced resistance to high temperature stress
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan cotton is as an important cash crop which accounts for 10.5% of value added in agriculture and 2.4% of gross domestic product. Due to the concerted efforts of cotton breeders and growers, the country harvested record production of 14.3 million bales in 2004.  Unfortunately, this level of production could not be sustained because of different biotic and abiotic stresses  especially high temperature. Almost all the cotton varieties previously tolerant/resistant to heat stress/temperature  are  now susceptible. Therefore, in the current scenario it is necessary to identify new sources of high temperature/heat resistance and utilized in breeding programme. The objective of the study is screening of advanced level (F6/M6) level germplasm and checking in field conditions. The study will generate new breeding material as well advanced stable lines suitable for planting in present harsh conditions.

data.projectName: Assessment of Marine Water  Pollution Index: Coastal Water of Sindh Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
An enormous volume of data is required in order to make a complete and credible assessment of the marine pollution. data.projectName: A synthetic approach towards the development of lead compounds in search of their therapeutics uses.
data.projectDigest:

appliance in drug discovery and development. Benzothiazole-based compounds display
several biological activities such as anti-inflammatory, anticonvulsant, antimicrobial, anti-diabetic and anticancer activities . 
In continuation of designing of potent compounds in search of on potential therapeutic drugs, we synthesized novel routes of benzothiazole derivatives and evaluated for their in vitro ?-glucosidase inhibitory activity. Furthermore, molecular docking was also performed to predict the binding interaction of the compounds in the binding pocket of the enzyme. 
The aim of this project is to make Pakistan independent in the field of many potential drugs which are frequently used in pharmaceutical industries. The aim of this project is to form lead compounds which can be beneficial for making an interactive drugs regarding various diseases.

Purchasing of glassware set up, chemicals and some instruments which are quite necessary for the analysis of products. After successful lab trials this product will be produced on large scale. This project will generate employment opportunities for our nation.

data.projectName: Design and Development of Vehicle Seat Assistance for Handicapped People
data.projectDigest:
In recent years there have been number of devices developed which enabled persons to operate automobiles. Many of these devices are in common use and are very significant assistance to the handicapped and elderly people. Although these devices are providing assistance to handicapped people and adding ease to their life by enhancing their mobility, however they do not assist handicapped people in entry and exit of vehicle.  Many people especially handicapped and elderly people don’t get in and out of the vehicle in easiest way. Therefore, in order for the ease and convenience of handicapped and elderly people new sliding seat will be designed which literally can be extended from the vehicle itself so as to enable the handicapped in entering and alighting from the vehicle.
Presently used vehicle seats such as the conventional car passenger or driver seat in the automobiles in Pakistan is not well equipped to accommodate person for whom there is considerable difficulty in seating himself/herself while entering or exiting the vehicle. Therefore, swivel seats allow easier exit and entrance into vehicle, which serves the handicapped person for easy and faster entry and exit.

data.projectName: Human Activity Recognition on Smartphones using Machine Learning Algorithms
data.projectDigest: Specialist knowhow in the fields of health, particularly rehabilitation assistance, physiotherapist assistance and the care of the elderly. Sensors record and monitor patient actions and routinely record them, so that a large number of resources can be saved, whilst abnormalities are detected. Various programs such as the human survey system and the position predictor all benefit from this.   Recognition of Activity is one of the most imperative periods for various applications, such as human survey, clinical research and a working exam in smart home and smart health. Smart mobiles have various sensors, including gyroscopes, accelerometers, GPS sensors and compass sensors. We can design a device to determine the user's condition. The goal of this research will provide a strategy to build a classifier that can automatically identify the activity type given the sensor measurements. This project is specifically related to the Machine Learning Algorithm for Human Activity Learning Using Mobile Phone Data by using the android application in the mobile device. The main focus of this project or application is to facilitate and increase the fast recovery of patient’s mobility for handicapped, injured and old aged people who are not able to move well because of their disabilities of organs. In this project we will check the status of human activity taken from smart phones wear by people while doing different activities (walking, lying, sitting etc.)

data.projectName: Lifestyle Intervention in the management of type 2 diabetes: effect on glycaemic control and type 2 related Epigenetic modifications
data.projectDigest:
Type 2 Diabetes mellitus (T2D), a lifelong disease, is emerging as an important public health issue with multiple complications. Factors contributing to the increased prevalence of T2D at global level includes aging, physical inactivity, obesity, urbanization, sedentary lifestyle and unhealthy diet. Worldwide it has been projected that the number of individuals with T2D will increase from 451 million in 2017 to 693 million by 20451. According to the estimates from International Diabetes Federation, one third of the people with T2D are in low and middle- income countries, that includes Pakistan.
Epigenetics is defined as variations in the structure of chromatin without modifications in DNA sequence, which may either silence or activate the gene. Evidence from developed countries suggests that lifestyle interventions can improve glycemic control in patients with T2D, hence delaying and even preventing the development of T2D complications. There is consistent evidence that the improvement in glycemic control as a result of lifestyle modification, specifically increase in physical activity levels, may be the result of epigenetic modifications. Yet, to date, programs that have been explicitly adapted to the needs and circumstances of low-middle income countries,who are specifically are at high risk, have not been well developed or evaluated. Pakistan is facing a tremendous burden of T2D and related comorbidities. The current project aims to evaluate the effect of lifestyle intervention on the glycemic control and epigenetic changes amongst patients with T2D and establish a cost effective, sustainable and culturally appropriate lifestyle intervention guide.

data.projectName: Application of medicinally important plant cell cultures of Stevia rebaudiana and Moringa oleifera to produce value added compounds using biotransformation technique
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
The Flora of Pakistan has rich reserves of medicinal plants, making it suitable candidate for biotechnological utilization. The plant kingdom has provided exquisite natural products with diverse chemical structures and vast array of biological activities that have numerous applications in the health sciences.  Stevia rebaudiana (sweet herb) is particularly use as a substance strengthening the heart, the circulatory system and regulating blood pressure. This plant is commercially used as non-caloric sweetener for diabetic patient. Its leaves possessed both hypoglycemic and body weight reducing effect without any adverse effects for diabetic patients. Moringa oleifera, also known as super food because of its greater nutrient contents and also significant antidiabetic, antioxidant, antiinflammatory activities and also use as cholesterol lowering agent, it helps to protect heart, brain and liver. Various parts of this plant have been studied for several pharmacological actions. 
Biotransformation is being applied for the production and bio-conversion of less valuable complex compounds into more capable and value-added compounds. Cell suspension culture of these medicinally important plants and their enzyme system will transform the chemical compounds such as alkaloids, terpenoids, steroids, and other chemical substances that could be more valuable after biotransformation in prevention and therapy of cancer and several other diseases.

data.projectName: Modeling of Reconfiguration based Demand Response Programs for Optimal Operation of the Micro Grids.
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Due to huge tangible benefits of Electric Vehicles (EVs) Pakistan transport sector is motivated towards introducing 0.5 million EVs by 2025. Hence, penetration of these vehicles may cause challenges about demand uncertainties and peak load. Therefore, proposed project aims to tackle the problem of optimal operation of EV integrated power grids by modeling of reconfiguration based demand response program (DRP). In this respect, both time and incentive DRP schemes with and without renewable energy resources connected to grid will be modeled and analyzed on available distribution test system under different scenarios.  The impacts and results may serve as a planning tool for energy planners and electric utilities of Pakistan.

data.projectName: EXPLORING THE NEXUS BETWEEN YOUTH COHORT AND MILITANCY/SOCIAL UNREST: EVIDENCES FROM PUNJAB PROVINCE, PAKISTAN
data.projectDigest:
This study was focusing on the opportunity and motives of the youth bulge situation in Pakistan in the lens of youth bulge theory. Some recent academic scholars suggests that large youth cohorts, or ‘youth bulges’, under conditions of social, economic and political exclusion, increase the risk of crime, violence and conflict. But large youth cohorts may also represent a significant resource that can boost development, in the form of so-called ‘demographic dividends’.  Following will be the hypothesis for the proposed study on the basis of objectives and theoretical framework:
1.	Economic recession in the country leads youth towards social unrest
2.	Productive use of working age population brings prosperity in society
3.	Job backlog in the state create violence in state
4.	Youth empowerment and welfare policies brings sustainable development among nation

data.projectName: Treatment of surface water for drinking purpose using low cost nanoparticles coated membrane
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan, the quality and quantity of drinking water deteriorates day by day therefore it is a compulsory requirement to treat water. As groundwater is not available to all the citizens of Pakistan therefore alternative source of drinking water needs to introduce. one of the sources is surface water. unfortunately, the surface water contains many impurities which needs to be removed. this study will provide a nanoparticle embedded membrane which will remove the impurities to such an extent that the surface water can be used for drinking. The nanoparticles are established adsorbent and membranes are widely used for filtration. Combining both the technique will enhance the removal efficiency and improve water treatment. The nanoparticle will be synthesized and characterized. The nanoparticle (Fe, Cu and Zn) which gave best results for water treatment will be used for further studies. On the other hand, polymer membrane structure having best filtration efficiency at room pressure will be selected. Afterwards, selected nanoparticle will be embedded in the selected polymer membrane which will treat surface water. Using this nanoparticle embedded membrane, a filtration design will be developed for commercial use.

data.projectName: Political Economy of EU Trade Preferences for Third Countries: Case of EU’s GSP+ Status for Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Modern Languages, Islamabad (NUML)
data.projectDigest: European Union (EU) being world's largest trading block offers the largest and one of the richest single market to states worldwide. Notably, EU's trade concessions for third countries stand as the most significant in terms of scope and volume.  As Pakistan faces poor economic growth and declining exports, EU's GSP+ status for Pakistan since January 2014 remains the most important economic development on part of Pakistan. However, this economic reward is bound to an internal as well as external political process which Pakistan needs to understand and pursue to ensure the continuity of EU trade preferences.  This study aims at highlighting the politics of EU's GSP+ scheme for Pakistan and evaluating the latter's performance in this regard.

data.projectName: Synthesis and Mechanical characterization of Swellable Gels used in petroleum applications
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Current research project is based on synthesis and mechanical characterization of solid state swellable gels that explicitly developed for swellable packer applications used in petroleum industry for enhance oil recovery.  
Swellable gels being used had issues related to reliability and longevity, hence development of new advanced swellable gels are of great importance and significance for proper deployment along with durable solution. Also, these gels affect greatly the wealth of oil based economies and can save huge cost by making abandoned wells productive for comparatively bigger periods. The above mentioned research work will be able to introduce indigenous technology and product development facility that will serve as a continuous platform for research and innovation in the field of swellable gels within Pakistan. Current project mainly target the local and regional oil exploration companies predominantly middle-east and south east countries.
Broad research objective of current work is to develop Solid State Swellable Gel Material that can be used in packers for zonal isolation in EOR petroleum applications. Research proposal is comprises of four phases. First phase requires procurement of equipment, material etc for setting up the lab. Second phase focuses on development of solid state swellable gels. In third phase short term as well as long-term mechanical and material characterization of synthesized gels is executed considering the actual conditions of local well environment. Fourth phase discusses the outcome of research in terms of results obtained, research publications, conferences, seminars etc. It is to note that above phases not necessary executed in series, they might run in parallel with other phases.

data.projectName: Privacy-Preserving Cryptographic Solutions for Big Data Analytics
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Machine learning and IoT paradigms are fundamentally data-intensive in that they require large amounts of user data to deliver results. However, this need conflicts sharply with the notions of citizen data privacy and personal data ownership. We seek to harmonize these two concerns through novel and effective use of cryptography.

We propose to adapt cryptographic techniques from next-generation electronic voting systems to devise privacy preserving  Big Data analytics solutions. We envision a novel approach to analytics wherein surveyors query users directly for their personal information with the specific restriction that user responses may only be deciphered in aggregate form. Users may therefore be confident that their individual responses cannot be accessed by publishers and advertisers and users themselves retain fundamental ownership of their personal data. 

This solution would provide different and vastly improved privacy guarantees compared to several existing solutions, enable prior ethical oversight, would not require significant changes to existing analytics ecosystems, and would facilitate collection of more fine-grained and accurate analytics data. 

In addition we will undertake research on privacy preserving machine learning techniques to work with our analytics solution, and also investigate the use of smart contracts and blockchain technology to improve transparency and ethical oversight of this process, as well as options on how to monetize the analytics process for participants.

We believe there are strong commercialization possibilities for our research and we intend to pursue these fully with a committed industrial partner.

data.projectName: MEDIA’s ROLE IN AFFECTING POLITICAL TOLERANCE LEVELS OF PAKISTANI SOCIETY
data.projectDigest:
Political intolerance is becoming the order of the day in the Pakistani society. Political parties leaders, anchors and analysts are becoming intolerant to each other in order to expose opposing political ideas. People doo not see this political intolerance as social problem in Pakistani society. This research will look at the social variable; the media and its ability to ensure tolerance in Pakistani Society. With the advent and spread of the social media in Pakistan this political intolerance is very visible. Political debates are getting abusive and intolerant. The menace of Political intolerance is gradually taking root in the Pakistani society. In recent years, the problem has shown some serious manifestation in extremely horrific incidences (Hussain, 2017).  
Voters and supporters of different political parties are not tolerant enough for opposing views. News channels are major source of political information in Pakistan and can play role in building political tolerance through their editorial policies. Therefore, this research will try to find out relationship between story framing, selectivity in news channels content by audience and its impact on the political tolerance of the society.

data.projectName: Analytical and Numerical Simulation of Heat Transfer in Flow of Non-Newtonian Fluid on Curved Geometries
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest:
The theory of boundary layer region has received remarkable importance in industrial applications point of view. Various aspects of flow and transport phenomenon in fluid mechanics have been explored by considering the boundary layer theory and a good comparison amongst the theoretical and experimental results is attained. A glance at literature survey reals that less amount of attention is paid on flow on curved geometries.
Study of non-Newtonian fluids are significant part of fluid mechanics because of its developing industrial importance. There is a particular type of fluid known as viscoelastic fluid which has attracted the various researchers for varying reasons. Maxwell fluid is categorized as a viscoelastic fluid that depicts the time relaxation behavior of the fluid. Also, Cross fluid model is type of shear thinning non-Newtonian fluids.
The purpose of this project is to study heat transfer in flow Maxwell and Cross fluid generated by continuously moving curved geometries. The two-dimensional Maxwell and Cross fluid will be modeled in terms of nonlinear partial differential equations. data.projectName: DEVELOPMENT OF PERSONALIZED COOLING SYSTEM USING PHASE CHANGE MATERIALS
data.projectDigest: Thermal comfort is one of the basic needs of human beings. In countries such as Pakistan, where summers are extremely hot and prolonged, this comfort is provided by the air conditioning industry. For a single person, who works outdoors, conventional air conditioners cannot be used as they are expensive and immobile. People working in severe conditions like firemen, policemen, soldiers and laborers are the working class which is most affected by the heat stress. Phase change materials (PCMs) have a higher capability of absorbing/releasing energy when they change their phase. If the melting temperature of these materials falls within the range of human comfort, then their higher heat of fusion can be used to provide thermal comfort. Such materials employed in vests can be worn by individuals providing relief against the heat. The melted PCMs are then solidified in refrigerators, recharging them for use again. Extensive research has already been done in the field of phase change materials and cooling vests are available in the global market. However, lack of awareness and high cost of such systems has opened an avenue to develop such devices indigenously. This research is aimed at developing PCMs by induction of carbon nanoparticles in conventional materials in order to improve the operational time of these materials. The objective is to develop a non-toxic, low cost PCM having high heat of fusion and thermal conductivity. In addition, the material should be able to maintain the desired properties after multiple cycles of melting-solidification. The final objective is incorporation of the developed material in vests and provision of these vests in Pakistan’s local market.

data.projectName: Computational Study and Designing of Materials using Density Functional Theory & Symmetry-adapted Perturbation Theory
data.projectDigest: Physicists have always been wanting to be able to predict the possibility of formation of materials of desired properties without doing any experiments. One could rely only on the first principles approaches as empiricism is less likely to succeed for novel materials. The cutting edge quantum mechanical methods (Density Functional Theory (DFT) & Symmetry-Adapted Perturbation Theory (SAPT)) are being used for this purpose but they either have low accuracy (DFT) or limited applicability (SAPT). We want to develop DFT such that its accuracy becomes comparable to that of SAPT and one could use it for all kinds of materials to get reliable predictions.

data.projectName: Enhancing Textile SMEs sustainability through financial literacy
data.projectDigest:
Financial literacy can enhance financial decision making, which can positively impact household’s financial wellbeing and ultimately financial and economic stability of the country. The role of financial literacy as a complementary ingredient to financial inclusion and financial consumer protection is being acknowledged around the globe  (OECD, 2012). In today’s world where organizations are facing immense competition, the need to use scarce financial resources efficiently is increasing. Financial literacy can play an important role in efficient management of financial resources. 
Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) are considered backbone of an economy. They are more responsive towards customers’ need of quality products in comparison with large scale manufacturers. Despite their important role in economy, SMEs lack of financial literacy make them more vulnerable to crisis situations than their larger counterparts. Development of financial literacy among SMEs will lead to development of SME sector and financial markets in the countries. Motivated by the SMEs’ need of financial literacy, the current study will focus on the identification of level of financial literacy among SMEs’ of textile sector of Pakistan. Afterwards, study will focus on provision of training and helping material in native language. So that financial literacy among SMEs’ can be increased for enabling them in better financial decision making.

data.projectName: Hybrid Polymer Matrix based Composite for Ballistic Armor Applications
data.projectDigest: The proposed project provides a light weight and cost-effective bullet-proof solution using composites. The existing bullet proof solutions are heavy in weight and mobility of these solutions is grave problem for armed personals and bullet proof vehicles. The composites consist of the matrix and the reinforcement phase. The matrix and reinforcement of the composite plays a pivotal role in the ballistic performance of composites. Polymer matrix and hybrid high performance yarns will be used. Rubber / epoxy matrix will be used due to its excellent damping properties. The curing and impact mechanism will be studied using numerical tools and compared with experimental results. Testing will be done according to NIJ standards.

data.projectName: Development of an Experimental Test Rig to Study High Cycle Fatigue Failure of the Turbo-Machinery Blades
data.projectDigest:
In turbo-machinery, vibration in the blades can leads to High Cycle Fatigue (HCF). Due to the tremendous environment inside the turbine, a blade with resonance-free working range is not possible. HCF in the turbines is so malignant in nature that a very small crack invisible to the naked eye on a single blade can leads to a complete failure of the engine. Therefore, one of the prime concerns of designers is to limit these vibrations and overcome the failure. However, it is quite challenging to propose the solution of this problem and requires precise instrumentation along with a solid background of the nonlinear vibration dynamics. 
The PI has already worked for more than five years in this particular field and has developed an experimental test bench to mitigate turbine blade vibrations to avoid HCF of the engine. The ultimate aim of the project is to develop a similar apparatus here in Pakistan, with some improved and customized features. In Pakistan, not only the educational institutes but also R&D organizations throughout the country, lack in latest equipment and laboratory apparatus in this field. It is a great opportunity as a researcher to develop an international level test apparatus here which can be further utilized by the potential clients for their corresponding applications e.g. MRF or HIT etc. Moreover, introducing this latest research field can provide us an opportunity to collaborate with the well-known high-tech institutes and research groups/organizations in the world.

data.projectName: Facile Synthesis and Remarkable Third Order Nonlinear Optical Response of Covalent-Bonded Polyoxometalate-Porphyrin Hybrids: The Role of the Attached Wells-Dawson Type Polyoxometalate Groups
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: Six porphyrin-polyoxometalate hybrids, having molecular formulas as, [(C4H9)4N)]5H[COHNC(CH2O)3P2V3W15O59{C41N7H26}]·CH3CN (3Py-P@1POM) [C4 H9)4N]10H2[{COHNC(CH2O)3P2V3W15O59}2C44N4H28] (trans-2PyP@2POM), [C4H9)4N] 10H2[{COHNC(CH2O)3P2V3W15O59}2C42N6H26] (cis-2PyP@2POM),  [C4H9)4N]15H3 [{COHNC(CH2O)3P2V3W15O59}3C43N5H26].C3H7NO (1Py-P@3POM), [(C4H9)4N]10H2 [{COHNC(CH2O)3P2V3W15O59}2C44N4H28].CH3CN (trans-2PhP@2POM), [C4H9)4N]10 H2[{COHNC(CH2O)3P2V3W15O59}2C44N4H28] (cis-2PhP@2POM) will be synthesized and thoroughly characterized by means of elemental analysis, FT IR, 1H (31P, 51V) NMR, MALDI-TOF-MS, UV vis. spectra and cyclic voltammetry measurement. Experimental results will show  that all the compounds show remarkable third-order optical nonlinear responses, the hybrids 3Py-P@1POM, trans-2PyP@2POM, cis-2PyP@2POM and cis-2PhP@2POM will be superior to their corresponding porphyrin precursors while hybrid 1Py-P@3POM will inferior in nonlinear optical response than its corresponding porphyrin precursor. Furthermore, the comparison of nonlinear optical responses of trans-2PyP@2POM and cis-2PyP@2POM disclosed that cis-2PyP@2POM wherein Dawson-type polyoxometalates will be tried to attach at cis position of porphyrin will superior in optical nonlinear response than trans-2PyP@2POM wherein Dawson-type polyoxometalates are attached at trans position of porphyrin. Identically, comparison of nonlinear optical responses of trans-2PhP@2POM and cis-2PhP@2POM will reveal that cis-2PhP@2POM wherein Dawson polyoxometalates will be attached at cis position of porphyrin is superior in nonlinear optical response than trans-2PhP@2POM wherein Dawson-type polyoxometalates are attached at trans position of porphyrin.

data.projectName: Morpho-Physiological assessment of bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) for drought tolerance
data.projectDigest: Climate change affecting our day today life is a combination of seasonal changes. Drought stress includes in such climatic changes that affects growth and development of plants. Drought continues to be an important challenge to agricultural sector. It is assumed that by the year 2025, around 1.8 billion people will face absolute water shortage and 65% of the world’s population will live under water-stressed environments. Such changes in climate will bring issues to ensure food security. Cereal crops like wheat demonstrate various morphological, physiological, biochemical and molecular responses to tackle drought stress. Wheat, play a major role in global economy and food security due to its rich source of micronutrients, minerals, vitamins and calories. Wheat varieties with excellent quality and resistance to biotic and abiotic stresses are of prime importance to securing food security of the mounted population. Wheat is mainly grown in arid and semi-arid areas with drought conditions. Keeping in mind the effect of drought on wheat, the study is proposed to overcome the problem of food security. This study will not only lead identification of drought tolerant wheat lines, but will also ensure the release of new wheat varieties from the Department of Agriculture, Hazara University, Mansehra.

data.projectName: In-vitro antiviral activity of bioactive Actinomycetes compounds from untapped ecological niches of Pakistan against different serotypes of HIV
data.projectDigest: HIV infections is a devastating viral infection and it leads to AIDS which is one of the most lethal life threatening condition with global annual diagnosis exceeding one million new cases. In Pakistan recently we have witnessed a sharp increase in the number of cases in different areas. Present Anti-HIV drugs are very expensive, less effective and their numbers are also limited. Therefore it is necessary to find out some alternative potent Anti-HIV compounds. With having the above theme in mind we have selected one gram positive filamentous microbial group known as “Actinomycetes” for the isolation of potent Anti-HIV compounds. This group is already known for its production of different chemotherapeutic agents, as above 60% of the known antibiotics currently in market have been isolated from its different species. Despite of the fact that the actinomycetes have been significantly explored worldwide, these bacteria are still unexplored in our area and harbors an immense potential for the production of Anti-HIV compounds. By identifying these potent actinomycetes compounds for the treatment of HIV and facilitating their production on commercial level will not only strengthen our economy, local pharmaceutical industries but also help us to save many precious lives who lost their battle to HIV owing to very expensive nature of currently available management.

data.projectName: Removal of carcinogenic heavy metals by magnetic activated carbon extracted from waste onion
data.projectDigest: Arsenic, cadmium, chromium, and nickel are classified as group 1 carcinogens.  These heavy metals are highly toxic causing cancer in body cells even in a very low concentration (permissible limit < 5 ppb). Recently, it has been reported that the concentration of arsenic in Pakistan is getting high, which is threatening more than 60 million people of the country. The biosorption offers many advantages over the conventional methods as mentioned above. On the other hand, development of novel biomaterial for the removal of carcinogenic metals from aqueous solutions is worth important. In literature, various bio-sorbents were investigated for the potential removal of toxic metals include apple waste, corncobs, cereal crops, woody materials such as bark, leaves and sawdust and most recently, the banana peels. In this project, highly porous carbon will be extracted from the onion waste. To the best of our knowledge, based on literature review, onion waste has never been used to extract carbon and its activation. The porous carbon thus formed will be magnetized by incorporating magnetic nanoparticles like Fe2O3, Fe3O4, Co3O4, and CoFe2O4. This idea is quite a novel to remove the carcinogenic metals by magnetic carbon for the complete recovery and reutilization of adsorbent.

data.projectName: Advanced agricultural applications of nano-coated natural materials in remedial measures for fighting shisham die-back in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Shisham plants are cultivated in the tropical regions throughout the world because of its high-quality timber. In last two decades, shisham plant has faced large decline at an epidemic rate. This enormous decline caused billions dollars lost to forest economy in several subcontinent countries. The main cause of the Shisham plant decline is die-back which is caused by the several bacteria and fungi. Nowadays, shisham plantations in Pakistan is facing major constraints is also due to the die back disease. There is no proper treatment for the control of this disease. In the present project an effort has been made for the treatment of diseased Shisham plant by analyzing the essential oils (Chemical profile) of the diseased plant at various stages in order to recommend the treatment to the plant. When it will be analyzed, what chemical is missed or what quantity of the chemical has been changed in diseased plant as compared to that of unaffected plant will be considered to suggest the proper treatment for the diseased plant. Furthermore, in the present project, specialized essential oils along with the metallic nanoparticles will be prepared for the inhibition of the bacterial and fungal growth responsible for the die-back disease.

data.projectDigest:
According to Pakistan Economic Survey (2018-19), total labor force is 65.5 million consisting of only 14.76 million females. The benefits of this proposed scheme are manifold: women could get financial autonomy, voice in decision making, better lifestyle and high literacy rate. 

The study shall be conducted in slum areas of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Synthesis of Calixarene Based Nanocomposite Sensors/Membrans for Sensing /Scavenging Water Pollutants
data.projectDigest: The main objective is to develop calixarene based novel multi-functional nano composites for multipurpose applications by providing novel synthetic materials. These ionophores associated with greater surface area and high stability would be used both for sensing and removal of the toxin present in drinking water. These newer strategies will encourage new approaches, such as “learning from nature” or materials “made to measure”, using whenever appropriate the potential of solvent extraction and membrane technology. Emphasis should be put on developing novel materials by means of “design approaches”, including prediction and modeling, on exploring new complex multi-functional properties of materials and on tailoring the materials in order to obtain a desired set of properties suitable for given applications and respecting site reclamation needs and perceptions. In using the potential of separation science, a particular attention should be given to synthetic host-guest materials. This project emphasis on utilizing the combined properties of calixarene and nanomaterial for ornamenting chemical sensors. The proposed strategy will help in developing sensors with more rapid responses, miniature size. The synthesized material will also be used to enhance the properties of newly developed sensors and in fabrication of filtration membranes for remediation of environmental threats due to pollutants especially mercury and arsenic ions. The end product would be based on using cheaper and greener materials as compared to previously reported expensive and hazardous material. This would make the sensing and remediation quite economical and could be commercialized easily. Such cheaper products/ technology could be easily in reach and hence of great benefit for poor folk of our country.

data.projectName: Relationship between serum levels of vitamin D during various seasons and disease activity in patients with inflammatory bowel disease
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Deficiency of vitamin D is frequent among patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) as compared to general population; thus it has been receiving increasing attention over its possible role in the disease mechanism of IBD. Literature suggests that patients with IBD having low levels of vitamin D in serum needed more drugs like steroids, and they had increased risk of relapse, indicating a more severe course of the disease. Considering distinct climate and location of every country, intensity and duration of sunlight and its exposure is different. Therefore, results of study conducted in one country cannot be generalized to others. The objective of the proposed study is to explore relationship between serum levels of vitamin D during va rious seasons and disease activity in IBD in Karachi, Pakistan. The proposed study will be an observational study and data will be collected in summer (May to August 2020) and in winter (November 2020 to February 2021). Thus, baseline and end line data will be collected from same individuals. Patients diagnosed with ulcerative colitis (UC) and Crohn’s disease (CD) will be recruited at Dow University of Health Sciences (DUHS) Hospital, Ojha Campus, Karachi. Characteristics such as age, gender, disease duration, medications for IBD, and smoking status will be obtained from hospital database. Regarding disease activity of IBD, the Harvey Bradshaw Index (HBI) for CD, and the Modified Truelove and Witts Severity Index (MTWSI) for UC will be used.  The erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP), and leukocytes will be evaluated as serological inflammatory markers. For vitamin D levels, Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin (25-OH-) total vitamin D (D2+D3) will be assessed.

data.projectName: Integrating transgenic and biocontrol approaches to enhance yield and disease resistance in Tomato
data.projectDigest: Tomato is a source of many important ingredients and it is consumed on regular basis as fruit and vegetable. Its production in Pakistan is low because of environmental and biotic factors, as compared to its consumption. As a result, Pakistan has to import tomatoes to meet its needs. The main cause of tomato yield reduction is biotic stress, instigating more than 200 diseases. The major setback that plant has to deal with biotic stress, is the production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) causing oxidative stress. There are various ways to improve the plant immunity against oxidative stress, but the genetic transformation and biocontrol approaches are the safest and eco-friendly ways to enhance disease resistance. Plants have an intricate antioxidant defense system which is known to stabilize the oxidative environment of cell. Nucleoredoxins are an important component of the plant antioxidant machinery. By the overexpression of nucleoredoxin the probability of tolerance and growth in the economically important crops like tomato is expected to be high. In this project, we will be integrating transgenic and biocontrol approaches to achieve our objectives. Overexpressed nucleoredoxin genes will be transformed in tomato. The genetic transformation, expression analysis of NRX as well as other defense related genes and application of biocontrol formulations on transgenic and non-transgenic plants will be investigated in tomato for disease resistance. These formulations will be prepared by the plant extracts of Chenopodium quinoa which is a climate resilient crop, and its root endophytic as well as rhizospheric plant growth promoting rhizobacteria (PGPRs).

data.projectName: An intelligent tool to assist neurologist in diagnosis and summarization of epileptic EEG events
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Each year, thousands of patients are diagnosed and treated in local hospitals for epilepsy. Electroencephalography (EEG) is the most widely used medical procedure for diagnosing epilepsy in hospitals. Diagnosis of epilepsy is made based upon the presence of epileptic discharges (ED) present in EEG data. Interpretation of EEG data and identification of epileptic discharges (ED) is non-trivial and various factors need to be taken into account before making a diagnosis, such as the state of the patients (drowsiness, light sleep, sleep deprivation) and the conditions during the procedure (such as hyperventilation, photic-stimulation). In Video-EEG involves simultaneous videotaping and acquisition of EEG data is a“gold-standard” procedure for differentiating epileptogenic seizures from non-epileptogenic seizures and is for longer durations spanning days.
Availability of support software for Neurologists is therefore necessary as manual inspection of is especially cumbersome and he/she may have to really of neuro-technicians for initial potential interpretation. Furthermore with the availability of wearable EEG sensors for home use and portable devices the amount of available data is becoming immense.
Not all hospitals in the country treating epilepsy have the privilege of procuring expensive software and systems from abroad. Moreover, they are suitable for diagnosing just the very common type of epilepsy i.e. the Absence seizures. 
The fundamental objective of this research is to combine signal and image processing techniques with pattern classification to develop low-cost and user-friendly tools that could assist the clinicians in detecting events of interest, thus increasing the sensitivity and minimising the effort required to screen the data

data.projectName: Assessment for Air-Pollution Mitigation ability and Therapeutic effect of Ornamental plants on Human Health
data.projectDigest: Considering the present scenario of urban environmental pollution, there is a growing need for changing the current remedial approaches and introduces a new sustainable remedy strategy. Inclusion of the ornamental plants and tress having pollution mitigating ability in the landscape plan will serve the duel purpose of making the cities green and pollution free in the long run. The present study investigates and recommends the choice of eco–friendly plant species and their right placement in indoor and outdoor urban environment to overcome the air pollution problems. The study will recommend various tree species for urban plantings, so that a wider usage of local as well as exotic tree species can be explored for controlling airborne particulate pollution in urban climate. Furthermore, present study also introduces a very novel Non-pharmacological and Non-invasive treatment approach medically beneficial to the wellbeing of hospital patients, technically known as Horticulture therapy. Nature and green atmosphere develops positive emotions that ameliorate pain and stress, thus distracting patients’ mindset from their worries or making them feel more competent to cope with it. This therapy approach will be introduced in various hospitals of mardan city to investigate its influence on patients health and overall hospital atmosphere.
