data.projectName: Utilization of Plantain as the Source of Resistant Starch in Combating Deficient Macro &Micro Nutrients Required In Body
data.projectDigest:
Increasing trends in food consumption and scarcity of food at the same pace has lead to emergence of various diseases and deficiencies. Plantains(Musa paradisiaca) are potent source of micronutrients especially vitamins B6 and VitC,which exhibit positive health effects on human brain and body, whereas plantains are known to be rich in resistant starch .Though resistant starch doesn’t add to the caloric content of food but has many physiological benefits. Resistant starch has been shown to increase absorption of macro minerals such that calcium and magnesium,Magnesium deficiency is most common in western diets and plantains provide 16% of the daily need for magnesium. Magnesium directly affects absorption of calcium which can avert or reverse osteoporosis. Generally, Plantains are consumed in chopped,baked,cooked or fried forms even mashed in most parts of the world.The aim of this research is to utilize plantain as a source of resistant starch for combating required magnesium and calcium levels as well as to determine effect of Vitamin B6 and VitaminC.The product approach includes drink and plantain powder as a readymade product made up of plantain.Commercialiazation and manufacturing of such products using local materials make it convenient for the people in both rural as well as urban areas to change and modify their dietary patterns on a positive scale.

Problem Statement: If Resistant starch obtained from plantain then it will overcome the mineral deficiencies and revert osteoporosis.

data.projectName: Rate-a-Dotor:A Data-Driven Strategy to Improve Service Delivery of Healthcare Providers in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Quality healthcare services are essential for the well-being of population. The increasing demand for this service has caused emergence of many private clinics/medical practitioners and healthcare providers. Many of them lack the requisite formalities to start these services. Mushroom spreading of this trade requires effective regulatory mechanism to provide beneficial services to common people. Government regulatory bodies already exist to regulate healthcare providers but have limited capacity to regulate them on macro-scale. Moreover, the state regulatory bodies have no control over micro-operations of the service providers such as affordability, availability of specialized professionals and caring attitude for patients / customers. Moreover, lack of knowledge about these fields also restrict common people to get expert, economical and pleasant service. In this project, we are inclined to develop a system that will regulate medical service providers based upon market reputation and people’s true sentiments. In this pursuit, a web application will be developed to build a database of hospitals / private practitioners that will be ranked according to patients/cutomers’ feedbacks. Those feedbacks will develop market reputation of healthcare providers and customers will be able to pick a specific service provider based upon its reputation. This will develop a self-correcting regulatory framework to check malpractices of healthcare pratitioners, help them to improve their services based upon public ratings / feedbacks and eradicate non-professional practitioners to provide economical, expert and pleasant services in the field of health.

data.projectName: Synthesis and application of nano-ceramic coatings for thermal and abrasion resistant textiles
data.projectDigest: With the growing awareness about personal protection, the demand for protective textiles is increasing rapidly. Such textiles which have protective features in addition to just aesthetic properties are rapidly replacing those textiles which are used for just covering of body. The market for functional textiles is increasing rapidly and it is expected that it will reach at $150 billion in 2022. Presently, the share of Pakistan in this market is negligible. In this context, it is the need to hour to work on development of functional textiles with protective features. The present project is aimed at exploring an emerging field of technical textiles with properties such as abrasion resistance, thermal insulation and flame retardancy. The objectives of this project will be achieved through sol gel process which has potential to be scalable at industrial level. The textiles developed in this project will have diverse applications ranging from sports to military textiles. For instance, a biker needs protection against bruises if he falls. The ceramic coated textiles developed may be used to protect wearer against impact abrasion. The soldiers in extreme cold weather need highly insulation textiles to prevent heat loss. The aluminium oxide coated textiles will provide very high thermal insulation. A textile developed with hybrid coating containing phosphorus and ceramic will be used in firefighters clothing where thermal insulation and flame retardancy are required

data.projectName: Development and Characterization of a Sustainable Resilient Asphalt
data.projectDigest:
Road networks play a significant role in developing the economics of a country. The Highway Authority of Pakistan allocates more than sixty billion rupees per annum budget on the maintenance of roads. Local highways fail due to increase in axle loads, poor binder properties, inadequate mixing, poor compaction and practicing old construction techniques/specifications. Conventional bitumen is unable to resist distresses in extreme weather conditions. Modification of bitumen by specialized refining practices and chemicals has been an effective technique to achieve wide range of performances. Researchers are trying to improve the performance of asphalt by using different additives, but every additive has some limitations.

It is also important to understand the chemical nature of additive and further its selection on the basis of its chemical behavior within the mix but there is no defined protocol available for selection of modifier in local highway general specifications.

It is expected that this research will help develop and characterize resilient asphalt by defining protocol for selection of modifier that may then be made part of the local highway specifications. This study will produce storage stable product with high PG grade, positive impact on durability, fatigue resistance and rutting resistance properties of modified asphalt. The implementation of research may result in saving of several billion rupees maintenance funds per annum of local highways department.

data.projectName: Synthesis and Characterization of Congruently melting Intermetallic compound (Ni3Ge/Ni3Fe/ Ni3Si)
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Congruently melting Intermetallic compounds are characterized by strong order and mixed covalent/ionic and metallic bonding, which gives rise to mechanical behavior intermediate between ceramics and metals. Due to these characteristics they can display desirable magnetic, superconducting and chemical properties. They also have a range of potential applications as high temperature structural materials due to good chemical stability and high hardness at elevated temperatures. However, the production of congruently melting compounds (Ni3Ge/ Ni3Fe / Ni3Si) is difficult due to their narrow range of composition. Though, it could be possible through Vacuum Induction Melting system under vacuum condition. Because this system provides close control of chemical composition, slag free melting and superior process control. 
These compounds will be verified and characterized using wide range of advanced equipment such as X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDX) and line-scan technique, electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD), transmission electron microscopy (TEM) bright field and dark field techniques, TEM selected area diffraction pattern (SADP), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and also Micro-Vickers hardness tester (for measurement of mechanical properties-hardness). After the confirmation of all characteristics and desired properties of congruently melting compounds through above tests, this model will be promoted for the greatest benefit of country in particular metallurgical & materials industry for the production of these compounds in large scale.

data.projectName: Indigenous design and development of force and material testing Automated solutions for medical, pharmaceutical, textile and food/beverages industries (Industry 3.0-4.0 compliant).
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
In developing countries with greater population like Pakistan, it is a big challenge to provide a quality controlled surgical sutures to well-trained surgeons. In order to check the quality of surgical suture, the common conventional practices are usually being used such as via spring based dead weight approach. Due to high cost of the advanced solutions, most of the local medical entities are unable to utilize it thereby needing a cheaper in-house solution. Keeping this in mind, we proposed a custom-made device design for accurate and reliable measurement with the characteristics such as (but no limited to) Tensile strength of Surgical suture, Needle – Fiber attachment force, Bending force/material strength of Surgical needles, etc.
Research Areas includes 
1.	Mechanical modeling and design of the proposed device, 
2.	Instrumentation and measurement control using advanced filtering algorithms. 
3.	Working simulation of the proposed design 
4.	Testing in industrial environment with real samples.
Research Objectives include
1.	Validation of the product with the certificate of analysis. 
2.	To support local industry with accurate, reliable and smart testing machines able to generate time-stamped report hardcopy 
3.	Develop experiments for training medical students to study, analyze and measure surgical suture.
4.	Publications and Patent.

data.projectDigest: A specialized online course for repair training of automobile (with focus on two and four wheelers) will be developed with easy accessibility independent of time and space limitations. An open courseware (OCW) will be prepared for automotive repair in Urdu language for the portable device users where they can understand the local language easily accompanied by a video tutorial and online assessment. Use of native language (Urdu) will certainly help in approaching vast majority of low educated HR willing to learn in time/space of own choice. Ease and quality of learning being delivered earlier and after implementing this course will be compared for making the finalized model. After successful completion of curriculum modules (video tutorials/assignments/evaluations), the trainee will gain a range of theoretical knowledge required to proceed in the world of repair work.

data.projectName: Dose optimization of Antifungal drugs through population pharmacokinetic modelling in Pakistani patients
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Fungal infections can affect the treatment outcomes of the patients who are receiving chemotherapeutic agent, undergone bone marrow or organ transplant, diabetic patients or the patients with pulmonary disease. The use of antifungal agents in such patients can prevent the worsening of the patient’s conditions however, there is variability among the individuals in term of kinetics of antifungal agents which ultimately leads to the need for administration of individualized dose to the patients which is also termed as precision dosing. The administration of inappropriate dose to the patients can lead to either failure of therapy or toxicity in case of less or higher than required dose respectively. The precision dosing of antifungal drugs can be ensured through population pharmacokinetic (popPK) modeling where the effect of all the possible factors which can affect the pharmacokinetics of drugs are quantified in the form of mathematical equations. The popPK modeling is the emerging technique for dose optimization based on the clinical and physiological conditions of the patient and is still at initial stages in Pakistan. In this project we will develop a popPK model for two antifungal drugs (fluconazole and voriconazole) in order to optimize the dosing strategy for Pakistani patients.

data.projectName: Measuring the impact of CPEC on socio-economic empowerment of local people of Sindh.
data.projectDigest:
Road and transport play a significant role in the development of the country.  This study examines the socio economic impact of China Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) in the districts of interior Sindh (Sukkur, Ghotki). Sukkur Multan motorway (M5) was completed with the estimated cost of 2880 million (US $). The total length of this road is 392 km and it was constructed within short duration of 3 years.  China Pakistan economic corridor is very significant for both countries as it provide access of China to the warm water of Arabian Sea through a short and safe route which will save billions of shipping charges and time and will cover the current energy crises in Pakistan and provide employment and trade opportunities for the local people which will minimize unemployment and poverty in Pakistan and will improve the living standard and boost the economy of Pakistan. 
It will be very interesting and innovating, if I will be able to calculate the economical impact of CPEC on people of this region.

data.projectName: Virtual Reality and Augmented Reality based Serios Games for Rehabilitation of Special Needs Children
data.projectDigest: The use of Virtual Reality (VR) and Augmented Reality (AR) in in various different domains for learning and training purpose is gaining huge momentum. In this research work, the problem of teaching and educating the Special needs children; that possess a certain mental disorder like Dyslexia and Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), is addressed using Virtual Reality and Augmented Reality techniques. A heuristic cognitive model of multimedia learning would be developed based on Virtual Reality and Separate model for Augmented Reality applications. Dyslexia and Autism are a complex mental brain related syndrome, effecting the children in various ways including verbal and nonverbal communications, social interactions, understanding instructions, reading, writing, learning, problems, etc. The use of interactive VR and AR based multimedia application to facilitate and provide a pedagogy for such type of special children would ascertain a unique and new dimension of treating and helping such young hearts in overcoming their disabilities in a very fun and easy way.  The research encompasses designing a framework based on Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning (CTML) for interactive VR and AR learning applications. The use of Assistive Technology based on Interactive VR and AR applications would be a new dimension and mode of learning for such special needs children.  Through this interactive application, the child would be able to react and respond to unique 3D animations, based on situations involving pedagogical learning driven through CTML and Blooms Taxonomy.

data.projectName: A New Paradigm of Islamic Microfinance: Development and Assessment of an Indigenous Model based on Profit and Loss Sharing
data.projectDigest:
Micro-financing is considered a bottom up approach for poverty alleviation and economic development in poor countries. However, its effectiveness is questioned due to higher operational costs, translated into higher interest rates charged from the poor. Certain micro-finance models have used Islamic modes of financing , which do not charge interest;  but rely on Qard-e-Hasna. This model has limitations as micro-finance institutes are not able to cover their costs and model becomes unsustainable in the long run. 
This project integrate the conception of One Village One Product Movement (OVOP), where micro-finance institute would provide financing on the basis of profit and loss sharing and will also support borrower in marketing the product.
We believe that a viable model of Islamic Microfinance could be developed based on  Islamic principle of profit and loss sharing. This project will develop such a model and also conduct a pilot testing to validate the model and its impact on various outcomes like poverty alleviation, financial inclusion, and women empowerment.

data.projectName: Development of Diagnostic Reverse Dot Blot Macro-arrays for selected human disorders
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
“Made in Pakistan” is the need of time for economic growth and stability of Pakistan. The proposed development of prototype for diagnostic macroarrays using reverse dot blot technique also encompases the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) #3, “Health and well-being”. As rare genetic disorders are not very “rare” in Pakistani population. There are around 7000 rare genetic diseases which affect 400 million people around the globe. A huge number of these are not well understood with only 5% which have approved treatments. There is a dire need for the early and accurate diagnosis of genetic disorders in affected and carriers within a family (pre-marital and pre-natal) to reduce the burden of genetic diseases. Conventional methods involve clinical diagnosis which is not very accurate in many cases because of overlapping symptoms among different diseases and syndromes. In some cases, molecular geneticists employ candidate gene screening for monogenic disorders whereas for complex ones, Whole exome sequencing followed by Sanger sequencing is used. 
Conventional methods available for mutation detection are time consuming, require expensive equipment and labour intensive. Such methods are not acceptable in a resource-limited setting of the developing countries like Pakistan. The situation demands a consumer-friendly, rapid, sensitive, reproducible, accurate, affordable yet simple and portable diagnostic test . The test should also screen multiple mutations associated with disease within a single experiment. 
Here we propose “development and validation of indigenous diagnostic reverse dot blot macro-arrays for detecting mutations”. It is anticipated that these macro-arrays will serve as the prototypes for pilot and large scale production in near future.

data.projectName: Entrepreneurial Process: Effectuation or Causation?
data.projectDigest:
Entrepreneurship is largely being taught by the instructors at Business Schools, Incubation Centers and training institutes as a ‘causation’ process involving extensive planning. Some authors led by Sarasvathy (2001) suggest that in practice entrepreneurs might be using ‘Effectuation’ involving the exploitation of contingencies to launch their ventures. However, as yet, the evidence in favor of effectuation is mixed and the jury is still out on the subject. Given the level of literacy in Pakistan and the kind of knowledge a typical entrepreneur in Pakistan is likely to be equipped with, leads one to suspect that use of effectuation as an entrepreneurial process may not be uncommon.
A clear evidence in favor of ‘effectuation’ or even in favor of a hybrid of effectuation and causation has the potential to alter the curriculum of entrepreneurship followed at Business Schools, Incubation Centers and training centers leading to greater emphasis on teaching the effectual process of entrepreneurship. 
The objectives of this study are to establish what kind of entrepreneurial process – effectuation, causation or hybrid effectuation and causation, the entrepreneurs in Pakistan use to launch and operate their ventures (at different life-stages of the venture). The study will also document the entrepreneurial journey of 50 entrepreneurs (startups) in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Development of  Computational Limbic Brain to Improve Decision Making Capabilities of Autonomous Agents in the Collaborative Environment
data.projectDigest: With the development in the field of Artificial Intelligence (AI), autonomous agents are being deployed in many fields. In the multi-agent systems, more than one autonomous agent has to interact and collaborate to solve such problems that are tough, difficult or unsolvable for an individual agent. The major challenge is to improve the decision-making capabilities of the virtual agents for the interaction and collaboration of the agents. Currently, autonomous reinforcement learning agents are rational, with only one goal that is to maximize their own reward. This reward maximization method for agents is inspired by the reward mechanism present in the rational brain of the humans. Researches on cognitive sciences and psychology proves that human brain has two parts: Rational Brain and Limbic Brain. Both of these brains contribute in the decision-making processes of humans. Currently, the agents have only the rational brain but they lack emotions because of the absence of limbic brain. Our hypothesis is that if we introduce the limbic brain into rational agents it improves their decision-making capabilities in the collaborative environment because limbic brain gives birth to emotions. The existing researches have introduced many computational models for introducing emotions in virtual agents but they lack the regulation of emotions through neurotransmitters. We believe that introduction of bio-inspired Computational limbic brain in multi-agents is a suitable choice for emotion modeling in rational agents that will improve the decision-making capabilities of these agents. The proposed model will regulate the emotions of the agents by controlling the virtual neurotransmitters according to the personality of the agent.

data.projectName: Growth and characterization of Si-Ge nanowires for thermoelectric power generation
data.projectDigest:
Due to huge demand of energy in the world, the primary focus of research around the globe is the production of cheap electrical energy.  Due to limited reservoirs of oil and gas, world is striving hard to meet the huge demand for electricity. Therefore, renewable energy technologies (Solar, Wind and Geothermal) attracting the attention of researchers. However, renewable energy sources supply only a small fraction of total energy consumed in the world due to their high cost and sophisticated technology. Heat is good alternate of sustainable energy source but about 60% of heat produced in home heating, automobiles and in industrial process is wasted. Thermoelectricity, direct conversion of heat into electricity, has significant potential to fulfill the energy needs. Many poor communities like Pakistan cannot afford the cost of power plants and electricity grid; whereas, small thermoelectric modules could significantly improve the quality of life especially in rural areas. In Pakistan there are many poor communities which have not access to this basic need of human.   
Thermoelectricity is based on the Seebeck effect, demonstrated by Seebeck in 1821, stated that two dissimilar materials with temperature difference can produce a voltage. The efficiency of thermoelectricity, therefore, strongly depends upon the material used. The materials with high Seebeck coefficient, high electrical conductivity and smaller thermal conductivity are desirable. 
This Project is a collaborative work between two groups at GCUF and University of Education to grow low cost and quality Si-Ge nanowires to explore the potential of this material for thermoelectric energy production. During this project Si-Ge nanowires with improved thermoelectric properties will be grown by thermal coating unit. Th

data.projectName: Genetic diversity of local and exotic fish species in the Rivers of Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Karakurum International University, Gilgit, Gilgit Baltistan
data.projectDigest: Fishes are important cheap source of proteins along with important nutrients for human health. The fresh water bodies, like rivers, streams and lakes of Gilgit Baltistan are abundant with various types of local and exotic species. Around 19 fish species have been reported from the rivers of Gilgit Baltistan, out of which 4 are exotic. Native fish species are facing an intense competition with exotic trout in the rivers of GB. Apart from some fragmentary reports, the local fishes are poorly studied and information about their number, species identification, distribution, and more importantly genetic diversity and conservation status, is lacking. The identification of fishes at species level is a challenging and difficult task, even for some expert taxonomists. Traditional identification is based on morphometric and meristic characters. Morphological identification of fishes is tedious, time consuming and sometime misleading due to presence of various developmental stages in fishes and also due to loss of obvious morphological traits. The DNA barcoding is widely used molecular based technique that is an authentic, fast and accurate method for the identification of fishes. Since its inception this DNA based identification method has greatly revolutionized the field of ecology, taxonomy and conservation biology in fishes. Most researchers consider it as an alternate method of taxonomy. The species barcode which is most commonly used is the mitochondrial CO1 gene. BOLD-FISH is global initiative database that accumulates sequences of all fishes round the world. The sequence of any unidentified fish species is compared with fish database for species identification. After species identification, the next most important task is identification of the extent of genetic diversity,

data.projectName: Socio-cultural Exchanges between Central Asia and South Asia and its impacts on the region
data.projectDigest: This study attempts to understand the dynamics of Socio-cultural relations between Central Asia and South Asia. The underlying hypothesis of the study is that the Islam reached South Asia through the central Asia, therefore the influx and flow of intellectuals, philosophers and scientists from Central Asia impacted the Socio-cultural orientation of South Asia. This intellectual flow from Central Asia to South and South Asia to Central Asia slowly but surely brought about strong and deep rooted friendly ties between the two regions. This study intends to find answer to the following questions: what kind of relations these two regions developed; why intellectuals/ philosophers travelled to opposite directions and what was the outcome of their interactions with each other and how far it brought about cultural changes in the regions.

data.projectName: CHILD LABOUR WITHIN INFORMAL ENTREPRENEURSHIP: YOU SAY ILLEGAL, WE SAY ENTREPRENEURIAL
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: Conventionally, child labour was seen as marginalized populations which participate in work due to poverty, education, and lack of other options.  Indeed, some of children are engaged in work on voluntarily basis. However, a growing number of scholars, in recent years, have drawn their attention to the valuable question, “Why are child labours engaging in informal entrepreneurship?”  There are only a few studies which has explored the motives of informal workers. But until now, no one has explored the motives of child labour who work in the informal entrepreneurship. Neither have any studies evaluated the entrepreneurial intention within child labour. The purpose of this paper is to highlight the entry motives and intention of children to entrepreneurial spawning who work in the informal entrepreneurship at automobile workshops. The survey sample will cover from automobile workshops located in Lahore, Sialkot and Multan districts of Punjab. Researchers will conduct face to face interviews with working children who work in automobile workshops in above mentioned cities. Results will show that today's child labour will be the entrepreneurial tomorrow, who start their own business after getting practical experience. This study will suggest some policy guidelines for such child labour who want to become an entrepreneur.

data.projectName: Improving the Stability of Perovskite Solar Cells
data.projectDigest: The four important requirements for an adaptable solar cell technology are; (i) high efficiency, (ii) high stability, (iii) low cost, and (iv) added functionality such as flexibility, transparency, aesthetics, and less stringent operating conditions. While the first and second generation solar cells offer the first three (i, ii, and iii) while the third-generation solution processable solar cells offer the last and the third one. However, the early members of this group, i.e., dye-sensitized and bulk heterojunction polymer solar cells, fail to a great extent in exhibiting the first three criteria. Emergence of hybrid organic inorganic perovskite solar cells (PSCs) boosted the morale of the third-generation solar cells by efficiency like the first two generations with a cost lower than these. The first peer-reviewed report came in 2009, where the perovskite (CH3NH3PbI3) absorber resulted in a 3.5% efficient sensitized solar cell termed as PSCs employing the iodide/triiodide redox couple. Subsequently, a 6.5% efficiency was reported and the efficiency doubled in mid-2012 and the recent breakthroughs in PSCs have brought the efficiency to a value of >25 %, where other PVs technology took 70 years to touch such a milestone.

data.projectName: Exploitation of pharmacological use of indigenously developed bioactive compounds to improve livestock and poultry health

Briefly, 30 plants from different families will be screened in this study. The plants will be collected, identified by taxonomists, shade dried, grinded and will be dissolved in different solvents (distilled water, methanol, butanol, n-hexane and ethyl acetate). The crude fractions will be tested for antiviral/antimicrobial activities. Later, the crude extracts will be purified through column chromatography, TLC and HPLC. In parallel, a series of synthetic azo compounds will be synthesized by conventional and environment friendly approach and finally characterized by spectroscopic techniques such as Uv-Vis, FTIR, NMR     (1H, 13C) and MS. The stock solutions of synthetic compounds and pure fractions of plant extracts (1 mg/mL) will be made. data.projectName: “Preparation of Vinca Alkaloid loaded Zinc oxide nanocarriers for pH responsive targeted drug delivery”
data.projectDigest: Cancer is the most widespread invasive disease and is the major root of deaths. There is dire need to develop the more potent and compromised drugs to fight and defeat the cancer without developing resistant. Chemical chemotherapeutic drugs produce lot of side effects along with therapeutic activity due to incompatibility to the living system as compared to herbal based agents. Innovation in the field of metal nanoparticle synthesis by using plant extracts, an amazing increase in anticancer activity has gained a significant attention. Catharanthus roseus is the prominent sources of vinca alkaloid derived anticancer drugs. Vinblastine vindesine, vinorelbine and vincristine are the major vinca alkaloids of great anticancer and other medicinal activity. In the present project VBL, VDS, VRL, VCR will be extracted from Catharanthus roseus and loading of Catharanthus roseus extracted & commercially available VBL, VDS, VRL, VCR to ZnO-nanoconjugates, will be conducted. They will be characterized by FTIR, XRD, and SEM. The cytotoxic effect of metal NPs and vinca alkaloid based ZnO-nanoconjugate against human normal cell line (human corneal epithelial cells, HCEC), breast cancer cell lines (MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231) will be confirmed by MTT assays. IC50 will be calculated for extracts with positive MTT assay. To evaluate anticancer activity in-vivo, the mouse model will be used. Phytochemical profile of the extracts will also be determined by thin layer chromatography. This may be the first report on anti-MCF-7 property and angiogenesis process of ZnO-nanoconjugates in the field of cancer. The present work will propose the hallmark for the synthesis of powerful economically effective nanoconjugates with maximum efficacy and no or minimum toxicity and targeted delivery of anticancer

data.projectName: A micromechanical investigation of stress and strain behavior of medium carbon steel using crystal plasticity based numerical simulation model
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest:
A bigger portion of the technological border, humans face these days, is because of limitations in versatility and usage of materials available. Therefore, the traditional hit and trial experimental procedures for the fabrication and analysis of the materials are needed to be shifted towards modelling and simulation using robust and reliable simulation tools, followed by synthesizing them at minimum cost, less time consumption and maximum durability. This is also needed to modify the time and energy consuming steps involved in experimentation into sustainable soft solution for fabrication and analysis of the new engineering materials. The micromechanical modelling and simulation of the materials will help first in investigating the real phenomena taking place at the crystal level instead of just look the material at macro scale, which can help further in validating the simulation software and providing a theoretical background for the manufacturing and development of exactly optimized microstructures depending upon crystallographic attributes.  
This will provide latest data to study the micromechanics at granular scale which can serve as platform for production and development of newly engineered materials at refined microstructure holding better mechanical properties. This can bring a very positive change in the process of material manufacturing by reducing the costly experimental procedures and by increasing the percentage elongation limits during cold forming of steel sheets with refined microstructure especially in automobile industry and generally in manufacturing sector.

data.projectName: Quantitative Monitoring of Sugar Level in Blood and Skin Cancer with Optical Coherence Tomography
data.projectDigest:
It is a common observation in medicine that early intervention improves outcome. In certain cases, such as cancer and angiogenesis disease, the difference between early and late detection can mean life or death . Light, and advance fiber-optic technologies in particular, open the prospect for minimally invasive diagnosis of early disease stages . Our research work falls in the area of the science and technology sector having a powerful slogan “Light for Life”; a direct application in improvement of the health sector i.e. biophotonics. Biophotonics is the sub filed of the Physics in which light-tissue interaction is investigated that underlines the Photodiagnosis and treatment of many life threading diseases like, skin tumor (dermatology), lungs cancer, liver carcinoma, ophthalmology, and diabetics, etc. The photodiagnosis methodologies include optical diffuse reflectance (ODR), optical coherence tomography (OCT), light microscopy, fluorescence and treatment techniques like Photodynamic therapy etc. 
We have completed a startup research work in optical imaging to diagnose the bio tissue like skin and liver and to monitor glucose levels in blood that will surely now lead towards early detection of skin tumor both in normal and diabetics.  Hence, to boost the research in this important subject, highly resolved optical coherence tomography setup is necessary to envision the blood microvasculature in three dimensions. Diabetic microvasculature bed is aimed to be imaged for monitoring of the glucose without puncturing the finger for in vivo case scenario. Recently, we have implemented this OCT in glucose quantification of blood in vitro . In the perspective of quantification of blood flow dynamics, that is microcirculation, we want to implement this technique for in vivo case

data.projectName: Isolation and Characterization of Haloalkaliphilic Actinomycetes from Brackish/Saline Lakes for New Drug Candidates against Multi-Drug Resistant Pathogens
data.projectDigest: Almost all the capable infecting agents have employed high levels of multidrug resistance (MDR) with enhanced morbidity and mortality due to the emergence of new resistance mechanisms. This results in decrease in efficiency of treating common infectious diseases by the standard treatment. Therefore, discovering new antibiotics against hard-to-treat and multidrug-resistant pathogens is now crucial than ever before. Natural Product drug discovery has been traditionally focused on empirical exploitation of most prolific microbial groups including actinomycetes and specifically Streptomyces. Actinomycetes have been the origin of largest number of new antibiotic drug candidates. Microorganisms inhabited in the extreme environments have been attracted a great attention in the recent years due to the production of various biotechnologically important natural compounds and their specific mechanisms to adapt these extreme conditions. Haloalkaliphilic actinomycetes are among these organisms which can tolerate and grow in high alkalinity and moderate to high salt concentration in the environment.  The salt range of Pakistan is well known for its rich and unique assemblage of flora and fauna. There are very few reports pertaining to the exploration of actinomycetes flora of the salt range. To continue these efforts, the present study is designed to investigate  haloalkaliphilic actinomycete flora of two lakes in the salt range through various biological and chemical screening against clinically isolated MDR resistant microbial pathogens.

data.projectName: Standardization of Withania coagulans Dunal for commercialization of anti-inflammatory and analgesic herbal preparation
data.projectDigest: The miracles of botanical preparations for the mitigation and treatment of various human diseases has been witnessed from the prehistoric times and requires no further advocacy. Despite of the agricultural potential for commercial scale cultivation of medicinal plants, rich biodiversity, socioeconomic constraints posed by modern treatment regimens, the revenue generated by our local herbal industry is negligible. The commercialization of medicinal plants research in Pakistan is a neglected area that could otherwise play a substantial role in alleviation of poverty, provision of cost-effective treatment by complimenting or substituting the contemporary allopathic system and economic growth through industrialization of local natural resources.  Nevertheless, scientific data on the institutional provisions, the capacities of various medicinal plant manufacturing systems, and the exploitation techniques, remain extremely fragmented. This incomprehensive data along with sub-regional variations in phytochemical contents of plant species necessitates the development of a comprehensive research agenda to improve the current body of knowledge regarding the standardization of ethnomedicinal plants thus, making them viable for commercial use. One of the abundantly present ethnomedicinal remedy with a huge potential for commercialization as herbal preparation is Withania coagulans a well-recognized herb among Hakims here with a history of 3,000 years of use in traditional Ayurvedic and Unani Indian medical systems and still no botanical commercial product is available in Pakistan. The presence of withanolides as phytochemicals in W. coagulans and their association in the mitigation of inflammation and pain give important clues that it can serve as a potential herbal preparation

data.projectName: ON TOPOLOGICAL INDICES  OF  MOLECULAR GRAPHS
data.projectDigest:
Chemical graph theory has a variety of applications in the study of chemical compounds.
The manipulation and examination of chemical structural information is made conceivable by using
molecular descriptors. A great variety of topological indices are studied and used in the theoretical
chemistry and pharmaceutical fields. Graph theory plays the role of the mathematical part for
modeling and designing of chemical structures and complex networks. The chemical graph theory
applies combinatorial and geometrical graph theory to the mathematical modeling of molecular
phenomena, which is helpful for the study of molecular structure. This theory contributes a prominent role in the field of chemical sciences. In graph theory, a chemical structure can be represented by vertices and edges where vertices denotes atoms and edges denotes molecular bonds. A topological index is a numeric number, which indicates some useful information about shape and analysis of molecular structure. It is the numerical invariant of a molecular graph and are useful to correlate with their bio-activity and physio-chemical properties. Over the years, researchers have found topological indices as a powerful and useful tool in the description of molecular structure. The research work in
the field of chemical graph theory about the topological applications of carbon nanocones, extremal pentagonal chains, tree like polyphenylene, spiro hexagonal systems.A topological index is actually designed by transforming a chemical structure into a number. These topological indices associate  physico-chemical properties like boiling point, stability, strain energy etc of chemical compounds. Graph theory has found a considerable use in this area of research. The topological properties of certain networks are studied.

data.projectName: stem cells embedded Silk hydrogel  for the treatment of dermal wounds
data.projectDigest: Impaired wound healing is a major problem in many clinical settings and associated with morbidity and mortality. The process of wound healing is complicated involving many types of cells and extra cellular matrix elements. No definite pharmacological treatment is available as a treatment for wounds which ultimately leads to limb amputation in some cases. Autografts are the gold standard therapy for cutaneous wounds but with limited application due to less availability and in case of extensive and deep burns. Cell based therapies have shown potential to treat many diseases and are being accepted in clinical applications gradually. These therapies can make up the cellular loss as well as restore the functionality of damaged tissue. Among different cells types, Mesenchymal Stem Cells (MSCs) isolated from different tissues have shown in vivo tissue restoration. These cells have been used alone and along with some scaffolds for skin wound healing. Silk fibroin is one such material which holds the promise of a biodegradable hydrogel with negligible provocation of inflammation. This study is designed to use MSCs embedded silk fibroin hydrogel to treat skin wound healing in rodent model.

data.projectName: Determining industry 4.0 soft-skills, training and evaluation practices, and their employee-level and organizational outcomes
data.projectDigest:
This study will address three key objectives: 
First, this study will develop an understanding about the needs of industry 4.0 employers, nature of soft skills training provided them, delivery mechanisms, and soft-skills training evaluation practices, and the budgetary investments made by industry4.0 employers on such training programs.
Second, this study will develop a theoretical framework that may guide training evaluation professionals  about how to evaluate soft-skills training programs.
Third, this study will determine the outcomes of soft-skills training programs on different employee-level (career growth, employability, skill proficiency,  social and financial inclusion) and organizational outcomes (profitability, market share, customer satisfaction etc.).

data.projectName: Synthesis, characterization and properties of graphene oxide-based nanocomposite membranes and their applications in wastewater treatment and antibacterial assessment
data.projectDigest:
Water purification and desalination have always been key issue faced by globe in recent years. It is basic need for economically development of each country. Since the rapid progresses in industrialization, increase in population and infrastructure development have widely contributed to the growing number of pollutant including heavy metals, dyes, crude oil, microorganisms. They are entering water supplies from anthropogenic activity, which causes severe environmental and ecological problems each year. Consequently, both developing and developed countries are facing severe environmental problems such as contamination of aqueous system. These issues have resulted in one of the most pervasive problems to the world: inadequate access to clean water. As a result, removal of ion and microorganisms from water is becoming increasingly important to the sustainable development. Recently membrane technology has attracted great attention due to its extraordinary benefits such as low capital and operating costs, lower energy requirements and simple operation. On the other hand, development of cost effective and energy efficient membranes remains challenge for scientific community. To achieve this target, extraordinary materials are needed.  
Recently, many industries and organizations are working in this area to develop more efficient membrane for separation of industrial wastewater, however could not get success. This project is a part of such efforts and has been undertaken, in collaboration with Defence Science & Technology Organization (DESTO), to develop commercial membranes based on graphene and other two-dimensional materials of purification of industrial wastewater.

data.projectName: Inverse Control System based Covert Random Communication for future Nanobots and Nano Devices
data.projectDigest:
Background:
Nano-communications have been emerging as a field which can revolutionize the traditional vision of current wireless communication systems. However, no investigation has been conducted yet to ensure the security of communication devices at the nanoscale.
 
Project Scope:
Therefore, in order to the enhance security of future nano devices especially Nanobots (Nano-robots), Nano-machines and 6G nano-communication-system-on-chip for biomedical, military, environmental, industrial and consumer goods applications, this project aimed to utilize the concept of multiple inverse control systems and alpha-stable random noise based random communication systems. Since, the PI has already independently conducted the initial assessment study that has been published as "Covert Electromagnetic Nanoscale Communication System in the Terahertz Channel", therefore, the chances are that the proposed project will be the first complete attempt to achieve secure transmission in the terahertz channel. The project will surely persuade researchers to conduct future investigations concerning the security of nano communication systems, nano-networks and future nano-machines.

Project Aims and Objectives:
1)	Multiple inverse control system based random communication systems.
2)	Applicability of the proposed system for Terahertz channel.
3)	SISO and MISO model for Secure Nano Communication devices.
4)	Development of security standards for future covert nano-communications.
5)	Performance & Security Analysis of the proposed system.

data.projectName: Floristic inventory of economically important trees within flora of Sindh
data.projectDigest: Sindh is a rich region with respect to flora. Although there are many studies found on trees of Sindh but they are either quite old or restricted to small area. Due to recent plantation drives in the region there is great potential that tree flora has been changed as people mostly grow trees during plantation campaigns. Proposed study is an attempt to form inventory of trees present in Sindh and their potential uses. Moreover, diagnostic characters with pictorial view of trees and their important parts will be recorded. Trees which are endangered/ threatened will be identified. Wild trees which are important medicinally or for other uses will be identified for future conservation and cultivation strategies. For this purpose ethnobotanical surveys will be carried out. Interaction with local people and herbalists across the area will be made. Students will be trained for taxonomic and ethnobotanical studies. Local communities will be urged to grow local and beneficial trees and Importance of natural native flora will be highlighted.

data.projectName: The neuroinflammatory road through mitochondrial warehouse and provisions for neuropharmacological tools
data.projectDigest: Successful management of neurodegenerative diseases such as stroke, alzheimer's and parkinson remains a major challenge in the clinical setup. Pre-clinical studies from the last decade have identified hundreds of neuroprotective agents, but not a single moiety successfully passed the clinical trials. A long list of perplex factors such as complex brain structure, diverse outcome strategies, and no precise target, are the major variants of drug failure in clinical trials. As a result, drug development is severely slow down due to high expenditure which rises from US$ 4 billion in 1975 to US$ 40 billion in 2009. Moreover, de novo drug development in neurodegenerative models remains a risky and costly process. Approximately 90% of drugs failed during development either from lack of efficacy or safety concerns. Collectively, It takes approximate 13-15 years and $US2.6 billion to bring a new drug to the market. These mounting obstacles in novel drug developments demand substitute methodologies, including drug re-profiling or repositioning. This innovative paradigm in drug development is economically attractive and time-saving. The purpose of this project will be the identification of novel FDA drugs against novel protein targets, which will be validated by both in silico simulation studies and in vivo experimentation.

The purpose of this project will be the identification of novel FDA drugs against novel protein targets, which will be validated by both in silico simulation studies and in vivo experimentation.

data.projectName: Linearization of MIMO Transmitters for Wireless Applications
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The power efficiency and higher bandwidth are the key demands for battery powered wireless devices.  There is a well-known trade-off between efficiency and linearity. In the MIMO system, the large array configuration further increases the nonlinearity problem. An applied linearization technique for an efficient transmitter in MIMO system will be developed. This technique shall be able to optimize the nonlinearity and delay mismatch conditions by compensating phase and gain. The improved Error Vector Magnitude (EVM) and Adjacent Channel Power Ratio (ACPR) are likely to be better than existing MIMO transmitters. This improvement will help in energy conservation

data.projectName: Optimum Ion-trap designs for Quantum Computers and Quantum Sensors
data.projectDigest: In recent years, trapped atomic ions (charged atoms) have proven a powerful tool to implement quantum algorithms and quantum simulations. Recent developments in the field show strong evidence that the quantum computer based on trapped ions is not a distant dream. Trapped ions working as Quantum Bit or Qubit in linear Paul traps are largely isolated from interaction with the environment. This property of trapped ions makes them a primary choice for quantum technology and quantum sensing devices.  In order to implement useful quantum computation, the scalability of linear ion traps is one of the most essential requirement to handle large numbers of ‘Qubits’. Advance micro-fabrication technology allows the realization of scalable ion traps. The study can be further exceeding to explore the methods to optimize two-dimensional (2D) lattice ion trap geometries for trapped ion quantum simulation. These 2D traps have proven potential to be used as quantum simulator in the field of metrology, sensing and atom–ion interactions. Further developments of micro-trap designs, for the purpose of scalable quantum technology, require inter-disciplinary investigations of ion traps. Since there is a severe shortage of physicists working in the emerging field of quantum computation and technology in Pakistan, this project will serve to build a core quantum technology group in the country.

data.projectName: Comparative Nanotoxicity Assessment of Engineered and Plant Mediated Metals (Ag, Cu) and Metals Oxides (Ti , Al) Nanoparticles in Indian Major Carps.
data.projectDigest: Nanoscience is attaining popularity due to high demand of nanoscale metal and metal oxides applicability in different science fields. Due to excessive use they entered into the environment. So, the study of their impacts on the eco-system, at both biotic and abiotic level, has become compulsory. A comparative study that will be done to investigate the bio-toxic impacts of plant-synthesized and engineered metal and metal oxide nanoparticals viz. silver (Ag), copper (Cu), titanium dioxide (TiO2), and aluminium oxide (Al2O3) on Catla catla, Labeo rohita and Cirrhinus mirigala, trial will be executed under specific lab conditions. Firstly, 96-h acute toxicity of all types of nanoparticles will be determined in indian major carps. Secondly, all fish species will be exposed to different sub-lethal concentrations of all selected nanoparticles, separately to check bioaccumulation pattern and DNA damage in fish peripheral erythrocytes (RBCs).  Bioaccumulation and genomic level would show major carps sensitiveness to each type of nanoparticles and their effects in bioaccumulation pattern and genetic level would be a helpful tool to measure early exposure to nanoparticles.

data.projectName: Development of bioluminescent-based whole cell biosensor for real-time monitoring of heavy metals in industrial waste
data.projectDigest: Heavy metals are widespread non-biodegradable chemical contaminants found in overlying water and sediment of river systems receiving disposal of city wastes, sewage, and industrial effluents. However, effective monitoring and remediation of these toxic pollutants is lacking, partially due to the difficulty of directly measuring these metals in environmental samples. The theme of this project endeavors towards biotechnological development of living bioreporter systems for the real-time detection and monitoring of environmental contaminants (heavy metals) in soil and water. In the current research program, we propose: Objective 1: Identification of metallotolerant microorganisms isolated from metal polluted site(s), and characterization of their maximum metal tolerance capacity; Objective 2:  Detection of metal resistance gene(s) by using molecular approaches; Objective 3: Construction of bioluminescent based microbial sensor cell systems; Objective 4: Field application of fiber optic biosensors for real time monitoring of heavy metals in the environment. The potential economic benefit of this project will be the development of bioluminescent-based microbial sensor cell systems (fiber optic biosensors) for toxic heavy metals like lead, cadmium, mercury and arsenic. This project will jointly be conducted in collaboration with a research group at the Department of Electronics, Quaid-i-Azam University Islamabad and Center for Environmental Biotechnology, University of Tennessee, USA that will help in construction and field application of fiber optic biosensor (objective 4). The Environmental Protection Agency (Pak-EPA) and a pharmaceutical industry (Jupiter Pharma) will be the sectoral collaborators for successful implementation of project output.

data.projectName: Production of micro-nutrient fortified rice through nano-scale fertilization
data.projectDigest: Zinc (Zn) and Fe are important micro-nutrients that are essential for biological systems and receiving renowned attention in recent age due to increasing reports of Zn and Fe deficiencies in both crop plants and human population worldwide. Pakistan is also facing the mal-nutrition problem and the situations is getting worse day-by-day. Therefore, the availability of Zn and Fe-enriched cereals such as rice is necessary to combat the growing challenge of ‘hidden huger’. Unfortunately, no Zn and Fe-enriched rice cultivar is available up-till now which signifies the importance of some other strategies to address this growing challenge timely. So, agronomic bio-fortification is now become the best alternative approach to get Zn and Fe-enriched rice grains. Previously, supplementation of Zn and Fe-containing fertilizers/salts were applied but as per our knowledge, there is a lack of research in the targeted and precise application of nano-scale fertilization to improve the Zn and Fe-uptake efficiency with minimum nutrient loss. In present study, we intend to apply different concentrations of Zn and Fe oxide nano-particles (NPs) and their composites to commonly grown rice cultivars to get Zn and Fe enriched rice grains. The experiments will be conducted under controlled and field conditions at two locations i.e., Faisalabad and Sialkot (CMB, Farms). The aim of the proposed research is to improve the quality and nutritional characteristics of rice grains with improved nutrient use efficiency and yield in rice-wheat cropping system of Punjab, Pakistan.

data.projectName: Quality Monitoring in Health Care with Control Charts: Development and Application
data.projectDigest: A control chart is used to monitor the quality of a production process.  There are lot of uses of control charts in health & medical care and public health surveillance. Some of the medical & health work in this area was developed autonomously, for the development of industrial statistical process control (SPC) methods. Thus, there is an opportunity for a relocation of knowledge between these two application areas. In this study, the control charts will be introduced to observe the fluctuations in healthcare by plotting these fluctuations after adjusting the risk factors. It will take into account different prior risk factors of patients when assessing treatment risk. These risk factors can be related to the general health of the patient. The statistical models, such as logistic regression can be used to adjust the risk factors. The developed control charts will be helpful to monitor the healthcare quality.

data.projectName: Investigations on mitigation of adverse effect of salinity by halophilic plant growth promoting rhizobacteria in wheat
data.projectDigest: Wastewater and sludge are being disposed of on land from a long time ago globally including Pakistan which helps to avoid the cost of incineration however this practice is deteriorating agricultural land and environment. Such practice loaded several heavy metals especially arsenic (As) in the soil which have been accumulated and transferred into the food chain and are very toxic, carcinogenic and imposed serious human health disorders. Recently, bacterial assisted phytoremediation emerged as a novel biotechnological approach helpful to remediation of toxic heavy metals. Keeping in view the above facts, the current research project will be conducted to isolate, characterize for plant growth-promoting attributes of As-resistant bacterial strains and to evaluate the potential ability to promote wheat growth by As-resistant bacterial strains. To achieve these objectives, soil samples will be taken from the various wheat grown by irrigating through wastewater and will be analyzed for concentrations of heavy metals and arsenic resistant bacterial strain will be isolated. These strains will be characterized for various plant growth promoting characteristic of selected arsenic resistant bacterial strains. The plant growth promoting ability of these strains will be evaluated through inoculating them in wheat seed and grown in arsenic condition condition under jar trails. The resulted best plant growth promoting bacterial strains will also be evaluated for their ability to promote wheat growth, yield, physiology, ionic  concentration, and grain quality attributes under pot and field trials. The bioremediation ability of selected strains will be evaluated through analyzing the post sowing soil analysis. The best bacterial strains will used for biofertilizers development.

data.projectName: B-vitamin intensification of wheat products
data.projectDigest: The group of water-soluble organic compounds, B-vitamins, plays crucial roles in the maintenance of body functions (proper cellular function, tissue growth and development). The B vitamin family includes vitamin B1 (thiamine), B2 (riboflavin), B3 (niacin), B5 (pantothenic acid), B6 (pyridoxine), B9 (folate), and B12 (cobalamin). With the exception of vitamin B3, which can be synthesized from tryptophan, all of the B vitamins must be provided from a dietary or exogenous source to fulfill human needs. B-vitamin deficiency can arise within weeks of inadequate intake, depending on the B vitamin, and can lead to various ailments. Wheat is staple to the diet of Pakistani people but lack of nutrients due to flour refinement, and the deficiency of B-vitamins can be corrected by intensification of the levels of B-vitamins by various means (fermentation, fortification, etc). This piece of work has been designed to prepare products from wheat flour and to estimate levels of B-vitamin (thiamin, riboflavin, pyridoxine), in the second phase the products are again prepared but after the application of processes for the augmentation of the B-vitamins and these levels will be quantified. Finally the comparison of the levels of B-vitamins in whole wheat products as well as in the products prepared by various treatments will be made and the best method for B-vitamin augmentation will be sorted out. The results will be of prime importance for the nutritionists to cope with the B-vitamin deficiencies.

data.projectName: Some Interesting Identities, Refined And Generalized Inequalities And New Bounds via Interpolating Polynomials
data.projectDigest:
The theory of inequalities plays a remarkable part in almost all branches of mathematics and in major fields of science. Convex functions are closely associated with the theory of inequalities and several well known inequalities are a result of the applications of convex functions. The concept of majorization, which is closely related to the convexity, is discussed very nicely in [2].

In [1] Agarwal and Wong constructed the Lidstone, Hermite and Abel - Gontscharoff Interpolating Polynomials and these interpolating polynomials, convexity, r-convexity and majorization would play a very important role in our research. 

We will construct several new inequalities in the classical polynomial interpolation theory and in fact the obtained results would be of great importance in the analysis of the boundary value problems for the ordinary differential equations. We will present

	some interesting identities, 
	inequalities for r-convex functions,
	Gruss and Ostrowski type inequalities and
	some new bounds 

by using these interpolating polynomials. Further, we will generalize some well known inequalities for r-convex functions by using Taylor’s Formula, Green and Fink Identity and Generalized Montgomery Identity. In addition, we will also obtain many significant results related to the refinements and generalizations of the

	weighted majorization type inequalities and
	Favard and Berwald type inequalities.

[1]   R. P. Agarwal, P. J. Y. Wong: Error Inequalities in Polynomial Interpolation and their 
         Applications, Kluwer Academic Publishers, Dordrecht / Boston/ London, 1993

[2]   A. W. Marshall, I. Olkin, B. C.  Arnold: Inequalities; Theory of  majorization and its Applications 
          (Second Edition), Springer Series in Statistics, New York, 2011

data.projectName: Image-based phenotyping for detection and quantification of disease resistance in wheat and rice crops
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: Advancement in artificial intelligence and smart computing have shifted the agricultural practices toward adapting smarter technologies to increase the yield of crops. The advancement of genome and transcriptome sequencing technologies has helped to explore the genetic diversity present in plants however, better understanding of such diversity can be achieved by unveiling the relationship between genotype and phenotype. A lack of advanced and efficient plant phenotyping techniques limits our ability to dissect the genetics of quantitative traits particularly those related to disease tolerance. Phenotyping of plant traits based on images has divert the focus of using image-based phenotyping for comprehensive description of plants disease severity and host defense related responses. In image-based phenotyping, a variety of imaging methodologies (visible imaging, thermal fluorescence imaging infrared imaging, 3D imaging and tomographic imaging) are being used to collect data of quantitative and complex traits related to the growth and adaptation to disease epidemic conditions. The overall objective of the project is the detection and estimation of disease severity and resistance responses in rice and wheat crops through image-based phenotyping. It can improve the precision in detection and quantification of disease responses in rice and wheat crops by generating more effective and reliable phenotyping data. Image-based phenotyping approaches may help to develop robust disease screening protocols in wheat and rice crops compared to conventional methods of disease assessments. The outcome of the project will improve our understanding of plant-pathogen interaction and help in screening of disease resistant breeding materials.

data.projectName: Value chain analysis of policy options for the Sunflower oilseeds in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Agriculture constitutes the biggest sector of Pakistan economy. A large number of the population engage with and depend on agriculture sector.The total cultivated land in Pakistan constitutes around 2.37 million ha, and 79.65% of this cultivated land is irrigated. The oilseeds occupied around 3% of this total cultivated land in 1970-71 and is decreased to 2.5% by 2002-03.
Sunflower (Helianthus annuus L.) is one of the four most important oil seeds in the world. It is suitable for cultivation in many regions of the world due to its high drought resistance and adaptation to some excessive soil varieties. The cultivation of Sunflower is increasing specially in Asia and Africa because of high quality of its oil and high demand. (Jocic et al., 2015).
Sunflower represents one of the major seed oil product in Pakistan, but still the production is insufficient for local needs as majority of the people in Pakistan use Sunflower oil for cooking, and more than half of the local demand is fulfilled through imports. A majority of the people in Pakistan prefer sunflower oil for cooking. Pakistan is the third largest importer of edible oil in the world. Pakistan produces about 27 percent of its vegetable oil needs domestically (13 percent from local oilseeds and 14 percent from imported oilseeds) and 2017/18 production is forecast to increase from the revised 2015/16 and 2016/17 estimates that reflect official assessments. 
This research proposes to do a Value chain Analysis of sunflower oil seeds in Pakistan to assist in guiding government strategies.

data.projectName: Differential Geometry and Spectral Geometry  of  Graphs
data.projectDigest:
Differential geometry is a mathematical branch that takes tools from linear algebra, multilinear algebra, calculus, integral and differential calculus to analysis the problems in geometry. 
Spectral geometry is although a new but is speedily developing field of mathematics.  Spectral geometry  in fact is a combination of differential geometry, differential equations and analysis.  In spectral geometry we study the relationship between spectrum of differential operators and geometric structures on manifolds. Basically spectral geometry is divided into two parts; first direct problems, where we find spectra and study its properties and secondly Inverse problems, where we draw geometrical information from spectrum. Spectral geometry of graphs also known as spectral graph theory basically studies the properties of graphs from characteristic polynomial, eigen values and eigen vectors of adjacency or Laplacian matrix. Due to a large number of applications of graph eigen values, a very important and interesting connection has developed between differential geometry, Riemannian geometry and spectral graph theory.
Because of merging techniques from differential geometry, Riemannain geometry and graph theory, spectral geometry of graphs has a wide range of applications in the field of mathematics, physics, chemistry, computer science and is therefore rapidly growing area of research now a days.
The objectives of this project are to study already proved results related to spectral geometry of graphs and to establish new results and their applications. These results will be a good increment and will increase the number of publications in this field. Unfortunately this is some rare field in Pakistan.
data.projectSummary:
Differential geometry is a mathematical branch that takes tools from linear algebra, multilinear algebra, calculus, integral and differential calculus to analysis the problems in geometry. 
Spectral geometry is although a new but is speedily developing field of mathematics.  Spectral geometry  in fact is a combination of differential geometry, differential equations and analysis.  In spectral geometry we study the relationship between spectrum of differential operators and geometric structures on manifolds. Basically spectral geometry is divided into two parts; first direct problems, where we find spectra and study its properties and secondly Inverse problems, where we draw geometrical information from spectrum. Spectral geometry of graphs also known as spectral graph theory basically studies the properties of graphs from characteristic polynomial, eigen values and eigen vectors of adjacency or Laplacian matrix. Due to a large number of applications of graph eigen values, a very important and interesting connection has developed between differential geometry, Riemannian geometry and spectral graph theory.
Because of merging techniques from differential geometry, Riemannain geometry and graph theory, spectral geometry of graphs has a wide range of applications in the field of mathematics, physics, chemistry, computer science and is therefore rapidly growing area of research now a days.
The objectives of this project are to study already proved results related to spectral geometry of graphs and to establish new results and their applications. These results will be a good increment and will increase the number of publications in this field. Unfortunately this is some rare field in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Development of New Adsorbent Materials for Efficient Removal of Pharmaceutical Compounds (PCs) From Aqueous Media: Advanced Physical Modeling and Computational Studies
data.projectDigest: The project is focusing on removal of  selected  pharmaceuticals compounds (PCs) i.e. diclofenac, Ibuprofen, amoxicillin, tetracycline, Ciprofloxacin hydrochloride, Ofloxacin hydrochloride and Paracetamol using cellulose extracted from agroindustrial wastes i.e   rice husk, bagasse, sawdust and paper mill waste. The adsorption studies for the selected PCs on selected adsorbents will be carried out in batch and column mode. For batch single and competitive advanced physical models will be applied on data to understand the adsorption mechanism. The fitness of different equilibrium and  kinetic models using non-linear regression and error functions will be done. The column mode adsorption will be carried out by applying models like Thomas and Bed depth Service model to optimize maximum removal of PCs. Computational studies using Gaussian 16 will be carried out for composites and PCs adsorption. Characterization studies will be carried out by FTIR, TGA, SEM-EDX, BET and EDX. Real water samples containing PCs will also be carried out using developed method. No study is still reported on using proposed cellulose composites for selected PCs and adsorption studies using advanced models and computational studies. The proposed method will provide ecofriendly and cost effective method for the treatment of water containing pharmaceutical compounds being discharged frequently in water bodies by human beings and pharmaceutical industries.

data.projectName: Molecular detection and seasonal prevalence of Theileria ovis and Theileria lestoquardi in blood samples of goats collected from District Muzaffargarh in Punjab (Pakistan)
data.projectDigest: Livestock is our natural resource for the conversion of roughage into good quality-foods like milk and meat.. According to a recent report, livestock sector is contributing 53.2% in agricultural output and has shared 11.4% share in GDP of Pakistan. Small ruminants like goat and sheep are the livestock of the choice of small farm holders due to their fast growth, economic and less hectic farming. Preference for goat meat is the major reason for its increased demand and hence increased forming. However, tick borne diseases (TBDs) are among the major constraints to this industry in developing countries like Pakistan and they are adversely affecting economic performance, mainly by the spread of severe pathogens and causing physical damage to animals.  Theileria ovis and Theileria lestoquardi are among the major tick transmitted parasites across the globe and also in Pakistan and every year affect a significant number of ruminants causing bovine and ovine theileriosis. The aim of the present study is to report the seasonal prevalence of Theileria ovis and Theileria lestoquardi in apparently healthy goats from District Muzaffargarh in Punjab by highly specific and sensitive molecular tool, the polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and to compare this method with traditional blood smear screening. This study will establish the protocols for the prophylactic detection of Theileria ovis and Theileria lestoquardi (responsible to cause ovine theileriosis) and subsequently its treatment and can be used by formers and livestock department to uplift meat, milk and hide production from the goats.

data.projectName: :  Green Microfinance : A Validating Pattern For Women Development & Sustainability
data.projectDigest:
This research project will focus  on "Green Microfinance : A Validating Pattern For Women Development & Sustainability"
Microfinance basically is the first-rate platform to serve the lowest rank communities by providing them soft loans to develop and maintain business, jobs and progressive economic environment in  last 40 years and reach on geographic magnitude. Women were the target of Microfinance Institutes , MFIs thought that the women will repay the loans easily and they invest the money just to feed their family, educate their children and work for well-being of family. 
Recently at global level  Microfinance institutes create another application in which they support local poor communities by providing them financial system that makes them sustainable in economic, social and environmental context. 
Project Statement:-To promote green business development  in Pakistan this research explore how MFIs   can be structured to create  sustainable  development  through  green micro-finance  while  simultaneously achieving  economic, social and environmental goals for   women self-employment.
Study Objectives 
1. To validate that a green micro finance is in practice & quantify its contribution for women`s economic ,social sustainable livelihood as a strategic interest  of investors, stakeholders with corporate social responsibility feelings .
Study Design 
Primary Research
A Quantitative --survey--Microfinance Environmental Performance Index (MEPI)
 A Qualitative  ------semi structured interview
Secondary Research (online literature review to exploit  developed countries model of Green Microfinance ) 
Population :-Khushali &U Microfinance Bank  ,Sindh 
 Sample Size 5% of total populations/ Sampling Method stratified sampling
Collaborative organizations will help in data

data.projectName: Understanding heart development by analyzing congenital heart disease through Next Generation Sequencing technologies
data.projectDigest: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is a defect in the structure of heart that arise during development and is present at birth. CHD is the most common birth defect, found in almost 0.8-1% of newborns. Symptoms of CHD may vary from mild asymptomatic cases to life threatening condition. Identifying genes and pathways involved in CHD is an urgent research priority, as they lead the way to more mechanistic insights, which is needed for the development of better prevention, diagnosis, and treatment strategies. In human patients only a small fraction of CHD genes has been elucidated (700 in mouse models). In the current proposed study, we will use an alternative strategy based on Mendelian genetics in rare consanguineous families having 2 or more CHD patients, which has proven to be very powerful and cost effective for identification of disease genes for a range of disorders in human. However, as yet the strategy has not been utilized to identify disease genes in CHD. We will perform whole exome and if required whole genome sequencing of 200 affected individuals (>100 families; already enrolled 80 consanguineous families samples having CHD from PIC, Lahore, and blood samples are taken for DNA extraction) in collaboration with University of Copenhagen, Denmark. The data will be systematically analyzed to identify causing genetic variants. Genetic variants will be confirmed and their consequences will be analyzed by functional analysis using bioinformatic tools and experiments in cell models and animal models to explore the developmental mechanisms which are disturbed by the gene mutations. The study will pave way for the development of better prevention strategies by carrier screening and prenatal diagnosis, better treatment strategies, and substantial reduction in socio-economic
