data.projectName: Understanding distribution, diet and genetics of Wolf species occurring in Pakistan for Conservation
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: The wolves of South Asia, notably the Himalayan and Indian wolf, are evolutionary distinct wolf lineages but the most endangered ones too. These are vital apex predators but are persecuted in response to depredation on livestock such as goat and sheep, and it results in decreasing their populations in the country. Almost nothing is known about the status, phylogeny and distribution of wolves in Pakistan. Two sub-species of wolf occur in Pakistan; Indian grey wolf (Canis lupus pallipes) and the Tibetan wolf (Canis lupus chanco). The current study aims at investigating distribution, diet menu and phylogenetic analysis of wolves in Pakistan. The distribution of the species will be recorded through field surveys conducted in all potential areas of the country (all four provinces and Gilgit-Baltistan), using motion-triggered “Camera Trapping”. The scats of wolf will be collected from the field for their dietary analysis to assess wild and domestic animal prey species consumed. The alcohol preserved scats of the species will be used for genetic analysis of wolves, using microsatellite DNA segments that gives insight into gene flow among populations, possible hybridization with dogs and other wolf subspecies, and genetic diversity. The Human-wolf conflict will also be investigated through self-designed “questionnaires”.

data.projectName: Establishment of Novel Elicitation Strategies to Produce Useful Anticancer Terpenoids from In vitro Cultures of Fagonia Indica
data.piUniversity: University of Malakand, Chakdara, Dir, Malakand
data.projectDigest: Fagonia indica belongs to family Zygophyllaceae, distributed worldwide. Different studies the anticancer potency of F. indica which has been attributed to constituent secondary metabolites especially terpenoids. Different classes of terpenoids have been isolated from wild grown plants of F. indica. However, there is lesser work done on the feasible protocols for regeneration of plantlets from In vitro cultures of the plants as well as the enhanced production of the medicinally very important terpenoids in F. indica. In vitro cultures hold enormous potential for large-scale plant multiplication, propagation of endangered species, and enhanced production of secondary metabolites such as terpenoids. The high-yield production of secondary metabolites is usually triggered through elicitation via supply of chemicals or environmental stimuli such as manipulation in light supply.  This project therefore aims at the establishement of such protocls for the plant Fagonia indica inside the laboratory setting and the high yield of important anticancer terpenoids from the plant.  The plant can be then upscaled at industrial level to produce these compounds in mass scale for treatment of breast cancer patients.

data.projectName: Development of Nanofiberous Flexible and Efficient Triboelectric Nanogenerators for Smart Textile Applications
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
The propose project aims at development of nanofiberous triboelectric nanogenerators (TENG) for self powering smart textiles and ambient energy harvesting applications. The TENG were first introduced in 2012. They are sustainable, simple, flexible, cost effective and efficient next generation electric power generation technique. Generally a TENG system consists of a negative and a positive tribo-layer which generates electrostatic charges upon contact or sliding based on their operational mode. Upon connection with external source via electrodes the generated charges can be exploited for practical applications.

Although some research has already been carried-out, however, the technology still remains immature for practical application mainly due to lower power generation, lower environmental sustenance (i.e. humidity) and lower tribo-electric power generation life.   
The proposed project focuses on improvement of TENG efficiency, sustained electric power generation, environmental sustenance and increasing the triboelectric power generation life.  

For the proposed TENG devices electrospun nanofibers will be utilized. The research objectives will be achieved by selection of appropriate materials or blends for fabricating nanofiberous tribo-pairs, surface chemical modification for increasing charge density and hydrophobicity, generation of nanopores on nanofiber surfaces for increasing contact surface. An effective TENG device design based on contact-separation mode will be developed.

data.projectName: Electrochemical Evaluation of Nanocomposite Materials For Supercapacitor Component
data.projectDigest:
‘We need circuits to complete our set targets’. An electric circuit is a close current loop to draw a desired output by including components appropriately such as capacitor. There is also supercapacitor. Both have fundamental charge storing nature. But charge storing ability of supercapacitor is greater than normal capacitor. Enhancement of capacitance can be done by tuning properties of certain electrode material through atoms by atoms nanomaterial synthesis techniques. Underlying properties of nanomaterials depend upon size, shape, constituents etc. Based on ultrafast deliverance of power, supercapacitor have uses in electrical systems; electrical grid stabilization, actuators, boats, buses and handpicked smart gadgets etc. 
Project will focusing on material/s for plates of a supercapacitors. TiO2 is selected due to easy preparation, electrochemical activity and high specific energy density. By opting four different methods: 1) combustion, 2) co-precipitation, 3) hydrothermal and 4) electrochemical synthesis, TiO2 will be further co-doped with Ag, Cu, Ni and Cd. Prepared materials will be brought to heated treatment for homogenization. The selected material can also be considered for further ion implantation to modify electrical and surface properties of nanomaterials. Surface to volume ratio of prepared nanoparticle of selected metal doped into the titanium oxide material will vary according to procedure of production. Structural, morphological studies and importantly Electrical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) will identify best of doped nanomaterial. Such a nanomaterial with well suitable properties is the goal of underlying basic research of this project. 
The proposed research topic has potential of basic research and it is believed that it is do able and beneficent.

data.projectName: Synthesis and characterization of magnetic graphene oxide coupled with zirconium based metal organic frameworks to study their potential in simultaneous electrochemical detection of heavy metal ions
data.projectDigest: Environmental and water pollution due to heavy metal ions has been a major global concern and even threat to human survival on planet earth. Presence of heavy metals in our atmospheres can be due to various anthropogenic activities. These metals in the form of ions, can enter into food web by adsorption, and if exceed permissible limits, can even breach the metabolic mechanisms by accumulating and disrupting functions in various vital organs like kidneys, liver, heart, bones etc. Therefore, sensitive and rapid detection of these metal ions is very essential. In these lines, variety of advance materials and nanocomposites are being used. Recently, Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOF) equipped with variety of intrinsic adsorption, porosity and enlarged surface area related properties have been proved as ideal candidates in metal ions detection. Moreover, Graphene Oxide (GO) based nanocomposites have also attracted intense interest over the last decade owing to their promising performances in a wide range of applications including adsorption/separation, catalysis, super-capacitors and electrochemistry. Additionally, lot of work has been carried out on individual ions detection but  very less attention has been paid to simultaneous detection of various heavy metal ions. Therefore, we propose  the strategy to combine these materials to give stable nanocomposites bearing the intrinsic properties of all the starting materials. These novel nanocomposites are expected to have excellent response against various metal ions. Differential pulse anodic stripping voltammetry would be employed to simultaneously detect these metal ions using these materials as smart adsorbents/substrates.

data.projectName: A Feasibility Study of a Randomized Control Trial to Examine the Impact of Spiritually Modified Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (SmCBT) on Obsessive Compulsive Disorder
data.projectDigest: Mental health disorders contribute about 7.4 % to the overall global burden of disease. These disorders were responsible for more of the global burden than were HIV/AIDS and tuberculosis, diabetes, or transport injuries. The prevalence of Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (OCD)  is noted with rate of 0.5–3 % in children and adolescents. OCD has a chronic course in about 40–75 % of cases. Clinical trials utilizing CBT and E/RP for the treatment of OCD have shown reasonable outcomes with significant reduction in symptoms of OCD and increased functioning. However, much of these studies have been carried out in western culture and such evidence is scarce in countries with Muslim majority. Therefore, the present study aims to adapt the Western based CBT model to Spritually modified Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (SmCBT). Further on, the SmCBT will be assessed in feasibility trial, in order to assess whether such treatment is acceptable to patients and clinicians. Initially, the traditional Western model based CBT will be adapted by a work group of professionals having sufficient experience in cultural and religious aspects of CBT. Further, this intervention will be tested on the group of 60 individuals diagnosed with OCD.

These disorders were responsible for more of the global burden than were HIV/AIDS and tuberculosis, diabetes, or transport injuries. The prevalence of Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (OCD)  is noted with rate of 0.5–3 % in children and adolescents. OCD has a chronic course in about 40–75 % of cases. Clinical trials utilizing CBT and E/RP for the treatment of OCD have shown reasonable outcomes with significant reduction in symptoms of OCD and increased functioning. However, much of these studies have been carried out in western culture and such evidence is scarce in countries with Muslim majority. Therefore, the present study aims to adapt the Western based CBT model to Spritually modified Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (SmCBT). Further on, the SmCBT will be assessed in feasibility trial, in order to assess whether such treatment is acceptable to patients and clinicians. Initially, the traditional Western model based CBT will be adapted by a work group of professionals having sufficient experience in cultural and religious aspects of CBT. Further, this intervention will be tested on the group of 60 individuals diagnosed with OCD.

data.projectName: DEVELOPMENT OF NANOSPONGES FOR ANTICANCER DRUGS USED AGAINST ORAL CANCER WITH ENHANCED BIOAVAILABILITY AND MORE PATIENT COMPLIANCE RATE
data.piUniversity: University of Malakand, Chakdara, Dir, Malakand
data.projectDigest:
Only in 2018 the newly registered cases of lip and oral cancer were 18,881 (10.9%) in Pakistan. That’s why the use of oral anticancer drugs has increased during the last decade, because of patient preference, lower costs, proven efficacy, lack of infusion-related inconveniences, and the opportunity to develop chronic treatment regimens. Oral administration of anticancer drugs is, however, often hampered by limited bioavailability of the drug, which is associated with a wide variability. Since most anticancer drugs have a narrow therapeutic window and are dosed at or close to the maximum tolerated dose, a wide variability in the bioavailability can have a negative impact on treatment outcome. 
In this project we will evaluate the pharmacokinetics of anticancer drugs used against oral cancer like Cisplatin, Carboplatin, 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), Paclitaxel, Docetaxel and Hydroxyurea after loaded them in suitable nanosponges (an emerging technology). We will also evaluate the intrinsic effect of the dosage form on the improvement of oral bioavailability of these drugs. Drug loaded nanosponges will be prepared and characterized in terms of size distribution, drug solubilization, and the kinetics of sedimentation. Commercially available and our fabricated anticancer drug-loaded nanosponges will be administered orally to animals to evaluate them for improvement in term of bioavailability. The current study is based on size reduction  by using biodegradable, biocompatible & low cost material using different techniques for selected anticancer drugs, followed by characterization, lab scale production and finally pilot commercial production. This study will result in increased aqueous solubility & bioavailability, reduced cost and improve patient compliance rate.

data.projectName: Nano-formulation of Chia seed as food supplement in diabetes management
data.projectDigest: Chia seeds are reported to possess antidiabetic potential due to their outer fibrous layer (mucilage). This layer retains glucose longer time and decreases blood glucose level. The mucilage will be separated from chia seeds and their nano-formulation will be prepared for better results. Moreover, certain antidiabetic phytochemicals will be encapsulated in this formulation to restore normal metabolic functions in diabetic patients. Overall, the dual functions of our formulation will provide fruitful outcomes in diabetes management with minimal side effects.

data.projectName: Antidiabetic effect of Caralluma fimbriata on histomorphology of pancreas and intestine and serum biochemical profile of rats
data.projectDigest: Diabetes is major global concern characterized by high blood sugar level in body. It produces various complications associated to heart, kidneys and eyes. It is caused by either insufficient production of insulin by beta cells of pancreatic islets or insulin resistance by the cells. It has bad effect on health as well as economical status of individuals suffering from diabetes. Various drugs used to control diabetes are mostly imported that are not only expensive for the poor community of Pakistan but also have adverse effects on health. Strategies must be adopted to explore economical drugs having less adverse effects.  Caralluma fimbriata (C. fimbriata) is succulent plant that has antiobesic, anti-inflamatory, anticarcinogenic properties. Some antidiabetic properties of C. fimbriata extract have also been documented. However, little is known regarding effects of C. fimbriata on histomorphology of pancreas, kidneys and serum biochemical profile. C. fimbriata is the natural herbal and easily available plant to be used against diabetes having low adverse effects on health. The present study will explore guideline for researchers for further study on the said plant that will lead to manufacturing drug against diabetes that will be easily available as well as economical.

data.projectName: Estimating the Contribution of Atmospheric Aerosols in Smog Formation from North-Eastern Pakistan: Source Apportionment and Implications for Trans-Boundary Movement
data.projectDigest: Since 2016, the prolonged and severe wintertime-smog has blanketed many areas in North-Eastern Pakistan. Tackling the current air pollution has become crucial to Pakistan’s long-term economic and social sustainable development. To study the severe issue of smog, information on the airborne concentrations of toxic pollutants in developed countries is relatively abundant. However, for less-developed countries with a predominantly arid climate, the availability of data is far lower. The extensive atmospheric aerosol layer over South Asia and the Indian Ocean persists during the winter season, and its cooling effect may regionally balance and even surpass the warming effect of greenhouse gases (GHGs) with predicted effects including changed circulation and monsoon patterns with amplified droughts and floods as well as increased melting of Himalayan glaciers. Therefore, this study will mainly focus on the contribution of atmospheric aerosols from Pakistan to smog formation while radiocarbon and molecular/organic tracers will be used for the source apportionment. These advanced techniques synergized by ground and space based remote sensing will accurately identify the actual sources of aerosols and will give us more reliable data. Most importantly this study will be a baseline study of aerosols in major areas of North-Eastern, Pakistan.

data.projectName: Spatio-temporal Study of Intertidal Benthic Macrofauna Along the Coast of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The muddy or sandy intertidal zones serve for variety of micro ecosystems for epibenthic, infauna and meiofaunal invertebrates. It is imperative that the intertidal zones provide a habitat for feeding to small organisms like juvenile fishes and shrimps. The variation in distribution and abundance of fishes in the surf zone is one of the characteristic occurred due to seasonal changes. Many of the inshore fish and shrimp species were commonly found species in the mangrove and mudflat habitats. The macrofauna forms an important link between mangrove detritus at the base of the mangrove food web and consumers at higher trophic levels, which include birds and commercial fish species. The quantitative assessment of benthic infauna has been of more focused than epibenthic mobile and nektonic. In coastal waters the behavioral changes in different species occur according to the tidal variation. Tidal states, lunar phases and day-night alternations affecting the short term changes in abundance. The higher catches of fish are associated with habitat utilization in daytime, while diversity and species richness is linked to night hours. Therefore, macrofauna are important to regulate and coordinate in the restructuring of some physical, chemical and biological factors in the marine ecosystem. There have been few objectives identified for the titled project. The baseline data and recording of biodiversity provide the basis for the advanced studies in any area of interest in biological sciences. The sandy and muddy and rocky substrata provide the rich nutrients to planktonic life and to early life stages of many marine animals. The abundance, diversity and population biology of intertidal animals provide a source to secure some forecasts about the potential estimates of our fisheries

data.projectName: Special Economic Zones, Local Industry and CPEC: Step Towards Export Promotion Strategy
data.projectDigest: Over the past five decades, Pakistan has pursued many policies focused on exports promotion, poverty reduction, and hence the promotion of economic growth. These policies generally focused on supply side components. The multi-billion dollar China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), a flagship project of the One Belt, One Road (B&R) initiative, has begun to bring tangible benefits to Pakistan's economy, which is likely to have a positive demonstration effect for persuading other countries in the region . The development of infrastructure including energy projects under CPEC plan will help in uplifting the industrial growth in Pakistan. The need is to develop such policy framework that should ensure that the trickle down benefits should contribute to the growth of country across provinces and regions.

data.projectName: Reinforcement Learning Based Cognitive Radar for improved Anti-jamming performance
data.projectDigest:
Radar is a system that uses radio waves to find velocity, range and angle of objects in the environment. It can be used for tracking and surveillance of aircraft, ships and motor vehicles. Radar is the key element in Electronic Warfare (EW). With the rapid evolution of the technology, EW performance is affected by radar electronic countermeasures like jamming. The jammer tries to intercept radar’s transmitted waveform and sends back the deceptive information like wrong range and velocity of target to deceive radar. Electronic counter-countermeasures (anti-jamming) are used by radar to reduce the influence of jammer. Cognitive radar continuously learns the environment to select the optimal values of waveform parameters to achieve better performance. 
Due to heterogeneous environment and presence of different types of jammers in environment, it is almost impossible to know their behavior. Hence, we have to use a method which learns the environment and jammer’s activities. We will consider reinforcement learning to learn the environment and jammer’s activities. Reinforcement learning is a type of machine learning in which we have an agent that learns the environment on the basis of current state and action. It receives an award on basis of that state during the action. Our problem will consider cognitive radar as agent, actions will be different parameters of waveform, reward will be the SINR and states will be selected on basis of previous action and reward. Agent will take an action in the current state and receives a reward. Agent will choose those actions that will give maximum reward as a policy. That policy will define each parameter optimal value that will give the best anti-jamming performance.

data.projectName: Generation of Structured Light
data.projectDigest: Light beams can carry both spin  optical angular momenta. Light with optical angular momentum is also known as structured light, twisted light, shaped light or sculpted light. This project deals with the detection and generation of structured light in atomic and semiconductor materials.  The main objective of the research project is human resource development and to familiar the students with modern quantum technology by edify them with basic techniques used in quantum optics and quantum information.  The structured light has already been used in modern technology such as quantum computing, quantum information, quantum cryptography, optical communication and nonlinear quantum optics.

data.projectName: production of nanoparicles for potential application in hyperurecimia reduction
data.projectDigest: Change in lifestyle and dietary habits has resulted in numerus side-effect which start appearing with time. One of the major side effect is taking to much purines (nitrogenous bases) in your diet. e.g. taking too much red meat and rice etc. As the purines increase in body the metabolic endproduct  uric acid starts to accumulate and result in Hyperuricimea.  Urate-lowering drugs that inhibit an  xanthine oxidase (XO, an enzyme responsible for uric acid production) are recommended to treat hperuricemia. Allopurinol and febuxostat are the medicines which inhibit the medicine, both drug have greater side effects and should be used carefully with proper monitoring. For the long term treatment or prevention of hperuricemia related diseases, there has been great effort to develop XO inhibitor drugs with no or less side effect. Nanoparticles are famous due to their specific properties and are used in many field of science. In present research, nanoparticles (molybdenium, selenium, cerium, silica etc ) will be assays for uric acid lowering agents.  In vitro analysis will be performed on ability of nanoparticles for breakdown of uric acid crystal and XO inhibition. The nanoparticles which show better in vitro anit-hyperuricemic activity will be test in vivo method. For this mice will be given nanoparticles at different concentration. For this test hyperuricemia will be induce in mice by injecting MSU crystal. Biochemical test will be perform to check the uric acid level and possible side effects on liver and kidney. The research may help in development of alternative medicine for hyperuricemia.

data.projectName: Controlled designing of 3D-coordination polymers as efficient materials for rechargeable Lithium/Sodium ion batteries
data.projectDigest:
Developing high-energy and low-cost chargeable batteries (CB) are critically important for the storage of renewable energy, future portable electronics, and electric vehicles. New material systems are needed for next generation of high performance batteries, so it is need of the hour to develop some new electrochemically active materials for energy storage taking advantage of indigenous expertise and facilities in this context. This project is a step forward to develop a new strategic way to consolidate the expertise from several fronts namely inorganic chemistry, nanostructure synthesis and electrochemical device testing, and structural analysis and characterization.
3-dimentional coordination polymers (Prussian Blue analogues networks) have recently shown to have numerous scientific and technological breakthroughs in novel nano-device applications, especially in electronics. Owing to its excellent electronic conductivity, this material could be thought of as fabricating electrode in the chargeable batteries.  In this proposal, we will elaborate our methodology to make various forms of Prussian Blue analogues together with CNTs/rGO to get nanocomposite powders and consequently use them as electrode for CBs. CNTs will be synthesized through our own chemical vapor deposition (CVD) facility and rGo will be synthesized according to modified Hummer’s method. Prussian Blue analogues will be prepared via controlled precipitation method with defined morphology followed by nanocomposites formation with CNTs/rGO. Prior to using it inside an electrochemical cell, various structural techniques such as XRD, FTIR, Raman spectroscopy, XPS, SEM, TEM, and TGA will be used to identify the correct phase and composition

data.projectName: :  Therapeutic targeting of Interleukin-17 in Human Blood Lymphocytes using Nano-particle to Limit Coronary Artery Disease in Patients
data.projectDigest: Interleukin-17A is a pro-inflammatory cytokine connected in the disease pathophysiology in patients with coronary artery disease. Experimental studies showed that the IL-17 expresses from the human blood T lymphocytes. Students from our lab group recently conducted a study to evaluate the association of IL-17 with coronary artery disease in a small samples (Un-published data) showed a pathogenic role in CAD. From this point of view, we can easily conclude that upregulated IL-17 is crucial in the CAD development. Hence, if IL-17 counteracted by right therapeutic means then it could be result in controlling of CAD events. No study has conducted until date to show the neutralizing effect of metallic nanoparticles on IL-17 in CAD patients. Therefore, in the present proposed work, we intend to examine the effect of gold, zinc oxide, and Iron oxide nanoparticles (NPs) on human T-cells isolated from the blood of CAD cases and healthy control individuals. We proposed to recruit 350 patients with documented CAD and 350 healthy volunteers. We will study the association of genetic polymorphisms in IL-17A with CAD in first phase, while, neutralizing effect of metallic nanoparticles will be study from selected subjects through the T cells separation and growth from blood samples

data.projectName: Screening for new AEDs Molecules for Treatment of Resistant Epilepsy in the Context of Genetic manipulation in Zebra Fish and mice models
data.piUniversity: University of Malakand, Chakdara, Dir, Malakand
data.projectDigest: Epilepsy is very common neurological disease with heterogenous cause and still not explored properly. There are 20 anti-epileptic drugs available but still about 27% patients are resistant to available treatment. It is important to discover new molecules with potential anti-seizure activity. According to our experience during my post doctorate study we have screened different commercially new molecules for epilepsy using zebra fish models. Because genetic manipulation is zebra fish is very easy. As Pakistan have a rich medicinal plant flora and not properly explored for the isolation of new molecules. So, I have interest to discover a new potential AEDs especially for resistant epilepsy by genetic manipulation in zebra fish and to pin point the mechanism of action.  I will also use chemically induced mice model to explore the basic mechanism of the new molecules at molecular level. After exploration I have the plan to translate the research to applied form/clinical research. If we succeed in discovering more effective drug for epilepsy our local pharmaceutical industry and community can get more economical benefits.

data.projectName: Artificial Intelligence Based  Extreme Events Forecasting System: The Need for a More Systematic Approach
data.projectDigest: Extreme Events such as flood, drought or hurricane can cause a hazardous situation in the country and can cause hundreds of causalities of livestock and damages of crops and properties. Effective and timescale management of such an extreme event is required to minimize a number of health effects such as immediate effects: human and animals’ injuries during the event, intermediate effects: food shortage for livestock and long lasting effects: lack of public health facilities and interruption. To overcome these issues, the disaster management needs some expert systems. Current Computer models are required to make judgments of several large-scale phenomena like how does  sun heat the earth’s atmosphere, how does pressure differences affect wind patterns and how water-changing phases affect energy flow through the atmosphere. These models provide only predicted information about an event over large region but these systems are unable to provide any risk information and risk alerts for community at real time. In the current computer models, the use of Artificial intelligence (AI) can help to improve the weather forecasters’ ability to predict rational patterns in clouds.  For this purpose, we have proposed a machine learning based linear classifiers- a kind of artificial intelligence based system that could improve the accuracy and reliability of extreme events forecasting.

data.projectName: Bio-bricks formation using using locally extracted bacteria and sand
data.projectDigest:
Fired clay bricks are one of the most extensively used building materials, and worldwide around 2.4 Trillion bricks are produced annually. This process consumes a significant proportion of our energy sources such as Charcoal, Wood and Coal. This process besides using up a significant proportion of our already depleting energy sources, is also responsible for emitting huge amounts of CO2 into the atmosphere. How about if we could make bricks without using such high amounts of fuel sources, and without emitting such high amounts of CO2 into the atmosphere. 
The project will use desert sand, which is normally not useful for the commercial scale production of bricks. Urease positive bacteria will be isolated from the environment and engineered for maximum urease production. The binding solution in the presence of the bacterial culture will be mixed with different types of desert sands extracted from different regions of Pakistan. The bacteria will hydrolyze urea with production of carbonate. This calcite precipitation hold the sand grains together and serve as a glue to seal the spaces between the sand grains. 
The protocol will be a highly environment friendly approach for making bricks.

data.projectName: Biofilms development for the treatment of polluted tannery wastewater
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Tannery industry is the second largest industrial sector of Pakistan after textile. There are over 2500 tanneries and foot manufacturing units mainly located in Karachi, Sialkot, Kasur and Karimabad in Peshawar. Among many industries worldwide, leather tanning industry produces large amount of both organic and inorganic chemicals. Hexavalent chromium Cr(VI) and persistent organic pollutants (POPs) including organochlorine pesticides are the toxic pollutants released from tannery industry. Direct release of tannery wastewater into streams and ponds and its accumulation into food chain risks the biodiversity of ecosystem. It is estimated that about 40% of wastewater is co-contaminated with organic pollutants and metal. Both Cr(VI) and organochlorine pesticides are very hazardous as these are carcinogenic, mutagenic. High solubility in water enables them to move across cell membranes which makes it dangerous to adjacent environment and living things. Co-occurrence of both pollutants requires a synchronized strategy for their treatment in single system. Biofilm system is a well-developed technology which is helpful in increasing the microbial concentration in a medium that intern help in accelerated degradation of pollutants. Present study will explore the potential for simultaneous biotransformation of heavy metals and pesticide organic compounds using biofilms grown on carbon-based materials as vehicle delivery system.

data.projectName: The protective role of native medicinal plants against heavy metals induced male infertility and hepatotoxicity
data.projectDigest: With the advent of industrialization, environmental contaminants are wide spread and reported to affect the public health. Heavy metal contaminants are serious problem for human health. Heavy metals are identified as affecting the human fertility. Among the heavy metals, chromium, arsenic, lead and mercury are known toxicants and causes damage to liver and male reproductive parts. For example, lead exposure is related to infertility as well as with chromosomal damage in spermatozoa. Cadmium is involved in tissue damage, necrosis and reduction of blood flow to the testes. Chromium induces sperm abnormalities, damages in interstitial cells and deposition of fat in testes. Mercury is also causing agent for decreased spermatogenesis, low sperm count and motility. Mercury and Arsenic also induce DNA damage and chromosomal abrasions in liver. Chromium in known toxicant for hepatic cells as damage mitochondria the power house of cell through alteration in signaling pathway.  Plants have antioxidants especially flavonoids that ameliorate the toxic effects caused by heavy metals. Different plants have been found to repair tissue damage, maintain hormone level and promote sperm production in males hence increase fertility. They protect liver tissue, maintain enzyme level and protect mitochondria as well. The present proposed project aims to investigate the protective role of four plants [Jambul (Syzygium cumini), Olive (Olea europaea), Black seeds of kalonji (Nigella sativa) and Aloe vera (Aloe barbadensis)] against toxicities induced by aforementioned four heavy metals to enhance the fertility in experimental animals and provide the basis to translate these findings for the application of such herbal remedies in human medicine practice.

data.projectName: Nanotechnology  Based Biodegradable Plastic from renewable resources for Sustainable Environment
data.piUniversity: University of Kotli Azad Jammu and Kashmir
data.projectDigest: Plastic packaging materials are everywhere in our daily lives. From food wrappings and containers to detergent and soft drink bottles to foam packaging used in shipping delicate goods, many products are surrounded by or contained in polymeric materials. Currently, most polymeric packaging materials are based on non-renewable fossil fuel feed stocks like polyethylene, which comes from non-renewable sources. Other polymers involve the use of malignant solvents during their manufacture which cause environmental pollution. There is a dire need to develop "green" packaging materials based on renewable resources that do not involve the use of toxic or noxious components in their manufacture. The present project based on Nanotechnology  Based Biodegradable Plastic from renewable resources for Sustainable Environment.

data.projectName: Sketching professional and social adjustment of women employed in Universities with rural backdrop in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Social ecology appeals world to work together with harmony while ignoring social restraints and accept, promote diversity, creativity and freedom. Discriminatory view with regard to women is not supported to social ecology. Contribution of women towards community is well established narrative around the globe. Women are the important part in social promotion and their role is inevitable. Discrimination negatively affect career of women and lead to result in deviation towards social development. Sketching professional and social adjustment of working women in universities with rural background for providing them equal opportunity as right is the aim of our study. Intentions behind this is to promote professionalism among employees to facilitate women in their social adjustment in universities particularly established in the rural vicinity or less developed areas of Pakistan. A total of twelve universities will be purposively selected from less developed areas of central and south Punjab of Pakistan. Sketching of professional and social adjustment of women demands qualitative approach, henceforward in-depth interviews will be conducted from about 120 women employed in the universities. Nearly sixty women engaged in administrative tasks and sixty women engaged in teaching will be selected on voluntarily basis. NVivo of latest version will be applied for analyzing the qualitative data collected through interviews. Recommendations of the study will be disseminated among concerned quarters.

data.projectName: Victims of terrorism attack, Cognitive distortion, post-traumatic stress disorder and coping mechanism for their Well-being
data.projectDigest:
Terrorism is one of the major reason to disturb the normal routine of functional society. There effects are more sever in that regions which are at risk of terrorist attacks. Pakistan is one of that regions that have been the target of continuous terrorist attacks. For example, In 2019; Lahore and Quetta bombing, Balochistan, Loralai and Pearl continental hotel Gawader attack, Makran massacre etc. Global terrorism threat index 2018 indicates that from last five years Pakistan is on 5th number that is most effected by terrorism not only with the number of deaths falling 37percent to 537 even with the number of incidents falling 36 percent to 366.
In Pakistan proclaimed terrorizations become a common phenomenon. Soft targets for terrorism are hospitals, educational institutions, shopping malls, clubs and transportation places since these places have high population concentration but have formal security. Attacks in these places are more painful and disgusting that may not only cause by deaths of people but also disturb the social and psychological functioning of victimized families. Such events effect their well-being and produce cognitive distortion and even post-traumatic stress disorder.
Most existing studies focused on adverse effects of these attacks on Pakistani economy. A little concentration found about how badly effect the families of victims and how they suffer from psychological health problems. This disturb health condition leads to negative emotions and feelings of revenge against Govt. So explore the effects of Terrorism attack on cognitive distortion and post-traumatic stress disorder: Interventions for Coping and Well-being of Victims is the main purpose of this study.

data.projectName: Studies on biofilms formation in food environments, relationship of pathogens and non-pathogens in multi-specie biofilms
data.projectDigest: Food items placed in refrigerators and other places after certain time period promotes microbial growth. These bacteria may include biofilm formers and non-formers. Within biofilm other non-formers bacteria may find shelter and food, hence forming a collaborative environment which is suitable for growth of all types of bacteria including pathogens also in multi specie biofilm. Biofilms have been reported as one of many reasons of emergence of antibiotic resistance. Our aim is to explore this consortia of variety of bacteria and to study the effect of different physical and chemical factors to invade biofilms for effective encounter of pathogenic and nonpathogenic bacteria. This study may help to understand the behaviors of bacteria towards different species and how they support each other. Antibiotic susceptibility tests will reveal the rate of acquisition of resistance against panel of effective antibiotics followed by testing natural compounds independently and in combination with antibiotics to overcome this issue. Rationale of designing this study is that biofilms are very common and can be formed in refrigerators’ food, found at homes, hotels and hospitals which are frequently handled by multiple users which may increase the chance of transportation of biofilm formers from one place to another place easily.

data.projectName: Identification of antihypertensive herbal drugs and active constituents usin g in vivo and in vitro pharmacological investigations; Using Non-Invasive Blood Pressure Monitoring
data.projectDigest: Indigenous traditional medicines have played a vital role in the development of novel drugs throughout the years. Current medicines have limitations of side effects, cost, availability and selectivity. There is need to explore alternative sources including herbal drugs and the active constituents. Traditional herbal drugs proved to be effective alternative source, however pharmacological investigation of needs to be conducted to identify the important potential therapeutic agents. Six plants, based on their traditional medicinal use in the management of high blood pressure, have been selected. These important herbal drugs include Agrimonia eupatoria, Cichorium intybus, Rosa brunonii Lindl., Olea ferruginea Royle, Cotoneaster acuminatus, and Maytenus royleanus. The selected medicinal plants will be collected and subjected to extraction (cold maceration) with methanol. Phytochemical studies will be carried out to identify different constituents and  comparison studies will be carried out with standards. This project will be an endeavor to investigate the pharmacological effects of these plants using animal models of hypertension. In vivo studies will be performed on the crude extract, fractions and constituents in different hypertensive rat models, using non-invasive method of blood pressure monitoring. This is a direct method allowing to study antihypertensive effect over a period of time. This will be followed by extensive in vitro studies to investigate the underling mechanisms of the antihypertensive effect. data.projectName: Tissue culture and Macropropagtion of Teak (Tactona grandis) tree for developing alternative to sheesham for boosting furniture industry
data.projectDigest: World furniture industry is worth $23.2 billion a year and Pakistan has a meager share out of itMajor tree species used for wood furniture is Sheesham. During last two decades sheesham dieback disease outbreak has resulted in death of huge number of mature trees and at the same time destroyed many new plantations. In our neighborhood India has developed multiple alternatives of sheesham. To give an example Teak wood is equally useful for furniture and native to India, Bangladesh, Burma and Sri Lanka. It can grow in tropical to subtropical environment with temperatures as high as 40-45 °C and as low as 5-10 °C with annual rainfall as low as 200-700 mm and as high as 770-2350mm. After the outbreak of sheesham dieback India has stressed upon the natural as well as managed population of teak. Unlike sheesham teak nurseries are tough to maintain as at seedling stage it is highly frost susceptible. Seedling planted after first shower in Moonsoon are most successful. Plant is also ideal for agroforestry due to its height and small crown on the top. In order to make it success we require developing tissue culture, micropropagation and seedlings development protocols from twigs/culms (Mass Multiplication/Macropropagation).

data.projectName: Identification of lung related pathologies using computerized breath sound analysis.
data.projectDigest: Pulmonary acoustic signals heard over the chest wall gives valuable information regarding the present state of the respiratory system which can be used in the diagnosis of pathology. Wheeze sounds manifest in asthma, COPD and pneumonia. The aim of this study is to differentiate wheeze sound in three pathologies. Objective of study is to define spectral or frequency features which can differentiate three pathologies. To date, no computerized model differentiate different pathologies, existing systems only differentiate between normal, continues and non-continues sounds. Such a model requires which can differentiate pathologies, as treatment of patient is related to pathology. The primary objective is to define set of features which can differentiate sounds manifest by different pathologies. Secondary objective is to define – Spectral behavior of sounds for each selected pathology, define per metric and non-parametric features for breath sounds. Data will be collected from normal subjects and patients suffering from different pathologies. The signal will be analyzed with a selected set of features. Statistical analysis will be done to analyze hypothesis. Finally classifier will be applied to achieve the accuracy of the system. An accurate computerized model for the diagnosis of pulmonary pathologies can spur the development of an accurate, portable, non-invasive, real-time and reliable system for asthmatic patients.

data.projectName: evaluation of mitochondrial DNA for species identification of meat and meat products
data.projectDigest:
Authentication of animal species in foodstuff is an issue which raise religious, economical, legal as well as medical concerns. In this regard, several analyses methods have been proposed for authentication of animal species both in pure and mixed samples for protection of consumers from fraudulent marketing. Proteomic techniques relying on identification of some peptide markers through electrophoretic, chromatographic or immunological procedures have been established providing information on the protein profile of the food. But the molecular analyses especially the techniques based on polymerase chain reaction (PCR) are considered as an efficient and authentic for species identification in raw and processed meat. PCR based DNA analyses including PCR amplification with species-specific primers, real-time PCR and nucleotide sequencing are very useful to identify animal species under various cooking/processing conditions. The current proposed study will focus amplification through species specific markers producing variable DNA fragment length/sequence for identification of species. 
Hence, this project is proposed in an attempt to establish authentic protocols for species identification based on the possible PCR analytical techniques that could help in finding origin of meat and meat products. This study will provide simple, efficient, authentic and validated procedures for forensic investigations in the fields of food security and wildlife protection. The aim of this project is to support food authorities in protection of consumers from misleading claims in marketing of the meat stuffs.

The aim of this project is to support food authorities in protection of consumers from misleading claims in marketing of the meat stuffs.

data.projectName: Smart Pet Robot
data.projectDigest:
Smart Pet Robot is a programmable and highly maneuverable robotic pet for STEM education and AI-enhanced services. Designed to perform tricks and tug at your heartstrings, works as a companion and an assistant for its owner. It can work as a safety robot guarding the house, will alert in case a burglar comes in, as a care-taker for a patient, making appointments for the owner, nursing in case of illness, and even would be able to call for help. 
The system will be housed in a container mounted on a robotic body. The device will utilize sensors, actuators, and programmable micro-controller to "teach" tricks, behaviors, and attitude as you program it and help it grow. Our robot will use face recognition to identify owners, use his/her voice for commands, will also be able to control by a remote controller. It will take inputs in real-time and make decisions based on it. Potential customers and investors could be education institutes using it for teaching, hospitals for its patients, a household using it as a normal pet or a guard. 
Robotics as a version in Pet world is still new, there are not many robots in market right now which are affordable and work for a common user. Those who are available are extremely costly and not available in local market. If imported in case a need for maintenance it will be quite costly. A robot for self-help is a great opportunity, which can make things easier for a user. It will be programmable so one could add or edit its actions on his/her own way. It will be fully interacted with its owner, so using it will be a fun thing to do.

data.projectName: Molecular sub types of gastric cancer in Pakistani population
data.projectDigest: Gastric cancer is the third leading cause of mortality worldwide. Most common histopathology in gastric cancer is adenocarcinoma. Currently all adenocarcinomas of stomach, depending of their stage are treated similarly however the outcome is different for different patients. Analysis of stomach cancer genes have shown that they can be further subdivided into four different sub-types. These sub-types have prognostic and predictive significance.  Meaning each sub-type clinically behaves differently. Therefor clinical outcome of each sub-type is different. There is evidence that certain treatment options are better for certain cancer sub-types.  However it may not be good for the other. Currently there is no data to show the status of these molecular gastric cancer sub-types in Pakistani population. The aim of this study is to determine the molecular sub-types of gastric cancer in our patient population. This can help us direct or chose treatment accordingly.

data.projectName: Evaluation of Zinc oxide-loaded Mannan Oligosaccharide OR Chitosan nano-particles for enhanced skeletal development, meat quality and production genes of broilers reared at high heat stress environment.
data.projectDigest:
The goal is to reduce the number of losses and illnesses in poultry from hazardous chemicals and air, water and soil pollution and contamination. Indiscriminate use of antibiotics in poultry feed pollutes the poultry products with antibiotics residues. These products such as broiler meat, when consumed by the general public leads to advance of resistant strains of bacteria and ultimately to development and spread of diseases that are not curable by available antibiotics. Through proposed intervention of replacing antibiotics in poultry feed with Zinc oxide-loaded Mannan Oligosaccharide or Chitosan Oligosaccharide nano-particles (MOS-zinc oxide or COS-Zinc oxide combination), we intend to contribute towards achievement of this goal. 

As the broiler birds will be fed antibiotic free supplement, their meat will certainly be free from any contamination with the residues of drugs. Such antibiotic residues-free meat, when taken by the consumers, will provide high quality animal proteins to them and will generally promote health. It is expected that the proposed research will strengthen our national capacity for risk reduction and management of national health risks associated with consumption of food that carries antibiotic residues.

Flood is one of the most frequent natural hazards that happened in Pakistan. Immediate and prominent impacts of this hazardous phenomenon include loss of human life, damage to property, deterioration of health condition owing to waterborne diseases and non-functioning of infrastructure facilities. Despite having functional flood early warning system in Flood Forecasting Division (FFD) of Pakistan Meteorological Department, Pakistan faces frequent devastating floods in Indus River system.  This forecasting system uses real time satellite rainfall data to predict flood at rim stations. Upstream areas of trans-boundary Chenab River basin lie outside of the Pakistan boundary and flood reaches in flood plains in very short time. Furthermore, such flash floods, with little or no warning time, in areas used for social-economic activities, cause more negative impacts on economy and life than slow-rising riverine floods.

The increase lipid peroxidation causes blocking or clogging of arteries in hyperlipidemic state. Under optimum physiological state, there is a crucial balance in the production of active oxygen radicals and antioxidant defense mechanisms. Defects in the oxidant/antioxidant balance stimulate the condition of oxidative stress, usually due to the over production of ROS. Oxidative stress leads to the damage of various molecular and cellular tissues in a wide range of human ailments. Supplementation of antioxidant is helpful in changing the situation.

data.projectName: Renovating B.Ed. Hons teaching practicum at UE: Inoculation of 21st-century skills through comparative Evaluation & Piloting a New practicum model
data.projectDigest: Teacher education is considered as one of the major factors in the development of an educational system. University of Education is the first largest producer of professionally qualified teachers both at elementary and secondary levels in Pakistan. The UE is offering B.Ed. Hons program to future teachers in all campuses with practicum model. By reserving the lens of empirical researches, it was found that this model is letting down in developing the professional skills among future teachers. Keeping in mind the objectives of National Education Policy 2017 chapter 8th titled “Teacher Education” the pre services teacher education programs are not aligned with the national policy of Pakistan, but we are training and certifying future teacher under that model.  There is always a way to change and improvement that is research and development. Through this proposed action plan, I anticipate renovation in (Planning, Implementation and evaluation) sections of the existing model of Teaching practicum by comparatively testing it. The prosed project would be conducted in four phases i.e. Documentation, empirical evaluation and training, piloting practicum model and evaluation of the projected model.  Across campus, piloting will certify the validity of tested practicum model.

data.projectName: Instability Analysis of Hydromagnetic Channel Flows
data.projectDigest: In the study of fluid dynamics, the dimensionless partial differential equations contain dimensionless parameters. For the solution of this differential equations most of the researchers take the numerical values of these dimensionless parameter randomly. To avoid this situation or for choosing the correct numerical values of these parameters, the stability analysis plays an important role. Stability analysis provides the range of the  these parameters for stable solution through this range we can take correct numerical values of these parameters. The main objective of this project is to perform stability analysis of magneto-hydrodynamic channel flows.

data.projectName: Formation of spectral data to differentiate Halal and Non-Halal-slaughtered chicken meat based on quality parameters
data.projectDigest: Halal authenticity of food products is vital for us due to several safety and religious concerns. Pakistan is currently facing the problem of marketing fraudulent meat products due to poor legislation. Additionally, we do not have any standard reference method for on-line detection of Halal authenticity of meat. Hence, it is need of the present time that we must establish proper analytical techniques that can be used for detection of Halal authenticity of meat-based products in the market. Accordingly, the current project is aimed to introduce spectroscopic methods as rapid and comprehensive tools to detect slaughtering authenticity of poultry meat by collecting spectral information based on various biochemical parameters of meat.  The findings of the proposed work will be quite helpful in providing a baseline to  generate a library which will aid in on-the-spot detection of non-Halal and dead meat samples from the market.

data.projectName: Exploring the earth abundant and less toxic low-dimensional chalcogenide materials for renewable energy applications: A combined theoretical and experimental study
data.projectDigest:
In the present project, low dimensional structures of the potential materials for clean energy production will be explored theoretically. The materials will be experimental prepared via thermal evaporation approach after their stability and efficiency for energy production in terms of photovoltaic and/or thermoelectric applications is confirmed theoretically. The fabricated films will be annealed at different temperatures for various intervals of time in order to optimize the structural and optical properties of the obtained samples. The optimized samples will be used as an absorber layer in the fabrication of solar cell devices. The efficiency and fill factor of the device will be measured using the solar simulator.
Furthermore, using these samples we will explore the low-cost and less toxic two-dimensional materials for renewable energy applications. Also the physical properties of the proposed materials is desirable for technological applications. To, recognize their potential for energy harvesting in terms of photovoltaic and solar energy applications

data.projectName: Development of a Robust Framework for the Next Generation Computational Sequence Analysis and Alignment
data.projectDigest:
Due to recent advances in the sequencing technology we encountered with enormous amount of genomic data. Proper analysis of huge amount of biological sequencing data is a hot research topic nowadays. Analysis is carried out through sequence matching or comparison. In Bioinformatics the most challenging task is the simultaneous computational matching of multiple sequences, called as multiple sequence alignment (MSA). 
MSA is crucial for proper annotation of different genomes.
Researchers throughout the country are busy in proper annotation of novel sequences. This area catch much attention due to Cancer and other epidemic diseases.

data.projectName: Role of  alpha Co(OH)2 Semiconductor as a Photocatalyst in Hydrogen Production
data.projectDigest: World is facing extreme shortage of energy in spite of the extensive use of environment hostile conventional energy resources. To fulfill the present and future generation’s energy demands, clean, renewable and long-lasting energy resources are desperately required. Hydrogen energy produced via water splitting using sunlight with the help of a semiconductor photocatalyst is considered as sustainable source of alternate clean energy. For the said purpose, numbers of different photocatalysts (oxides, nitrides) have been studied to investigate the water splitting and hydrogen production but the efficiency of most of these photocatalysts is strongly limited by higher energy gaps dominantly in UV range. Keeping in view the efficiency of such semiconducting materials, it is strongly required to implement such as material whose band gap and band edges are aligned with potential required for water splitting. Co(OH)2 is one of such materials, which has the capability to absorb most of the light from solar spectrum. This material has shown thermal and chemical stability, and can play a vital role in hydrogen production to eliminate energy catastrophe in coming days. The energy production via photocatalysis of water using sun light is considered as the cheapest, renewable and environment friendly .

data.projectName: Synthesis and characterization of novel veterinary nano-medicine for prevalent bovine mastitogen
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Metal oxide nano-structures will be synthesized by green approach and characterization of green synthesized nano-structures will be further accessed for appropriate and optimized synthesis. Activated salts will be reacted with fresh roots of Zingiber officinale  and Allium sativum roots powders resulting green reduction. Optimization of the green synthesized nano-structures will be proceeded by changing various ratios of root’s extracts, pH and reaction temperature and further parameters. The synthesized nano-structures will be characterized by UV-vis, FTIR, XRD, EDX, XPS, FESEM and HR-TEM.
The bovine milk samples will be collected and cultured to isolate Streptococcus species, S. aureus and E. coli. Bacterial colonies will be confirmed by typical morphological characteristics, Gram’s staining procedure and various biochemical tests. The final confirmation of selected isolates will be preceded by PCR for multiple drug resistance (MDR) issolates. In-vitro and in-vivo antimicrobial efficacy of green synthesized metal oxide nano-structures will be analyzed on laboratory animals
data.projectSummary:
Metal oxide nano-structures will be synthesized by green approach and characterization of green synthesized nano-structures will be further accessed for appropriate and optimized synthesis. Activated salts will be reacted with fresh roots of Zingiber officinale  and Allium sativum roots powders resulting green reduction. Optimization of the green synthesized nano-structures will be proceeded by changing various ratios of root’s extracts, pH and reaction temperature and further parameters. The synthesized nano-structures will be characterized by UV-vis, FTIR, XRD, EDX, XPS, FESEM and HR-TEM.
The bovine milk samples will be collected and cultured to isolate Streptococcus species, S. aureus and E. coli. Bacterial colonies will be confirmed by typical morphological characteristics, Gram’s staining procedure and various biochemical tests. The final confirmation of selected isolates will be preceded by PCR for multiple drug resistance (MDR) issolates. In-vitro and in-vivo antimicrobial efficacy of green synthesized metal oxide nano-structures will be analyzed on laboratory animals

data.projectName: Catalyst development for carbon dioxide hydrogenation to methanol
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest: Methanol is a key industrial chemical, used to synthesize several other important chemicals. Its consumption has reached 80 million tons/ year in 2018 and global methanol market size is expected to reach 91.53 billion US$ by 2026 at annual growth rate of 9.8%. Moreover, an increasing amount of methanol is going to synthesis high quality gasoline additive. Motivation behind the use of methanol as an additive in the fuels is its high energy content. Contrary to the conventional fossil fuels, combustion of methanol in internal combustion engines produces no harmful gases. Methanol has also become feasible choice for the storage of hydrogen gas. Hydrogen can be obtained from water splitting using excess electric energy and is a promising sustainable alternative of depleting fossil fuels. However, there are several challenges associated with the transportation and use of hydrogen gas. Methanol has higher stored content of hydrogen than hydrogen itself and methane, it is liquid at room temperature and has low freezing point around -96 ºC. In view of rising carbon dioxide level in atmosphere coupled with advantages of using methanol over hydrogen, there is dire need of methanol synthesis from hydrogenation of carbon dioxide.

data.projectName: Monitoring Land Deformation and Seawater Intrusion in Coastal Areas of Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Coastal areas of Pakistan are undergoing planned & unplanned development such as residential, commercial, and tourist areas. Vulnerability of geohazards such as seawater intrusion, flooding, and sediments depositions along  coast are increased due to land deformation. Recent case studies by PI, his team and few other researchers has reported  significant evidences of sea water intrusion, erosion, and land deformation in  coastal areas of Pakistan. Unfortunately, there have been no in-depth research for identifying  land deformation and its associated causes as well as effects along coast of Pakistan. 
Pakistan being a developing country cannot afford deployment of traditional ground-based equipment to monitor sea water intrusion and land deformation in its 1100km coastal belt. However, advancement in  field of satellite-based RADAR and optical imaging has capabilities to monitor land deformation and sea water intrusion over large area for extended time-period in all weathers. 
Therefore, study is proposed for monitoring land deformation and associated seawater intrusion on multi-temporal scale and identification of  hazardous areas prone to land deformation using optical and RADAR satellite data since 1972. 
Findings of proposed project will help in strengthening Coastal Zone Management and precise mapping of  Sea Water Intrusion of vulnerable areas along Sindh and Baluchistan coastal cities.

data.projectName: Improving  Teachers’ Classroom Assessment Literacy at Higher Education Through Related Training
data.projectDigest: Assessment is the most important component in the system of higher education. The achievement of educational objectives at higher education demands accurate and proper assessment, for this the role of teachers' is vital. The results of my previous research studies (Shams, Iqbal;2018a, 2019b; Iqbal and Saleem, 2019) showed that teachers' have low to moderate level of assessment literacy at higher education.  at higher education, no complete training manual exists for improving CAL of teachers in Pakistan. SO, the purpose of this research is to develop and implement classroom assessment literacy (CAL) training manual for teachers at higher education. It will be developed in consultation of assessment experts. Workshops will be arranged to finalize the major topics and developing related hand-on activities with the help of assessment experts’.  The developed draft of the training manual will be piloted on a small similar sample.   With the permission of the VCs/Rectors/Department and heads of institutions the training will be delivered to the post graduate colleges and university teachers using CAL training manual. The effectiveness of the training manual will be measured through CAL test. The test will be conducted before and after the training. The PI and Co-PI will train the teachers having the experience of such training at higher education level. The training will be of two weeks for each institution and one hour each day. The rigorous work will be done at the stage of developing CAL training manual and then at he stage of conduction training sessions. The effectiveness of the CAL training may help the teachers to improve their CAL to do accurate assessment of their students at higher education.

data.projectName: Development of extraction method and Characterization of Dissolved  Proteins from the Sea for future industrial applications
data.projectDigest: Oceanic dissolved organic matter (DOM) is one of the largest reservoirs of organic matter and reactive organic carbon. Marine DOM is composed of a variety of organic molecules including proteins and proteins. The proteins in the marine living organisms are eventually transferred to the dissolved pool (<0.7?m) via various biogeochemical processes. The sources of dissolved proteins in sea are the excretion by microbial community, breakage of cells, decomposition and sloppy feeding for higher faunal groups. Microbial community express and secrete previously unknown proteins which are of tremendous value in the novel and sustainable industrial applications and as food for bacteria and other higher animals. The Pakistan waters have high primary productivity which warrants discovery of novel chemicals. Lack of information about dissolved bio-molecules present in these waters emphasizes the need for further studies. The seawater and microbial exudates recovered in large quantities will be concentrated into small volume using ultra-filtration and ultra-centrifugation. The dissolved proteins will be precipitated and characterized and also assessed for bioactivity and toxicity. The proposed research will therefore tremendous outcome and provide the data on the diversity of proteins in the sea water and bulk quantities may be available for future use and novel applications.

data.projectName: Structural and Tectonostratigraphic Evolution of the Lower Orakzai, KP, Pakistan: Implications for the Hydrocarbon Potential
data.projectDigest: In this project we aim to investigate the hydrocarbon potential of previously unexplored area, the lower Orakzai, district Orakzai, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. The topic is selected owing to the grim energy and financial crisis Pakistan is going through at present while the area is selected due to lack of previous work of this kind in the area as well as the reason that the area contains promising rock types (formations) that constitute the proven “Petroleum system” elsewhere in the country.

data.projectName: Technology as a pathway to reduce local language skills gap in Pakistani youth
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Pakistani youth is facing skillsets gap within local language contexts. This will have severe consequences from national historic and cultural perseverance and continuity perspective – the likes of those faced by Malaysia and Turkey. The overall objective is to employ technology as a pathway to improve Urdu language skillset (reading, typing, and focus) of Pakistani Children. In partnership with NUST and Hamdard Foundation, NED University envisages to execute the idea through developing a searchable digital archive of Hamdard Naunehal magazine and integrate it with dynamic digital application. Then, with involvement of children (~7 to 14 years) from various schools, the project studies the impact of these digital interventions in improving their skillsets such as Urdu typing, focus spans, increase in reading times etc. The findings will enable us and other local language archives in the country to build digital infrastructures aligned with national contexts, thus raising the impact and becoming more meaningful for the society. At the same time, it allows local capacity for digitizing and enriching the internet with local language content. The project deliverables include searchable digitized content from a popular Urdu children magazine, API for digitization from printed Urdu text which can be used by News archives and publishers, mobile app tuned to user experience for Urdu language readership, Digital literacy workshop and conference, manuscripts, patents and sustainability report.

data.projectName: Task Allocation Strategy for Global Software Development
data.projectDigest:
The research that we plan to carry is future work of the PhD thesis of principal investigator (Dr. Salma Imtiaz) titled as “Task Allocation in Global Software Development” (GSD). A task allocation framework was designed based on data collected from GSD practitioners from around the globe via mixed method approach. An initial validation was performed with help of an online focus group. The participants of the focus group who are all GSD practitioners having 10-30 years GSD experience stressed upon the need to realize the framework in form of a strategy with an associated tool, so that validation of the strategy can be performed via real world case studies. The recommendations of the focus group participants are attached as Appendix A with the proposal. As a first step we plan to realize the framework in form of a task allocation strategy and develop a tool that would allocate work to globally distributed sites in an effective manner (based on the developed task allocation strategy). Since the task allocation problem exists at the work allocating site, therefore the validation requires traveling to identify the cases for case study and training the participants on the use of the tool.  The design and development of the tool will be followed by the execution of the case study on at least two representative cases carefully chosen from the GSD industry. Therefore, the main objectives of the research are:
1.	Realization of the task allocation framework in form of a strategy. Alignment of the task allocation strategy with software development lifecycle and identification of points where allocation/reallocation decisión may be required.
2.	Design and development of a task allocation tool that is basedon the task allocation strategy.
3.	Validation of the task allocation strategy

data.projectName: Heavy metal(loid) indexing and balances of soils in semi-desert irrigated zone of Punjab, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Heavy metal(loid) accumulation in agricultural soils can seriously decrease soil quality and productivity. For sustainable agriculture, soil must be protected from toxic levels of heavy metal(loid)s. Atmospheric deposition, fertilizer application and artificial irrigation may be adding significant amounts of heavy metal(loid)s in soils of semi-desert irrigated (agro-ecological) zone of Punjab. Heavy metal(loid) balances in soils is important to predict future possible risks to sustainable production from agro-ecological zones and human exposure to heavy metal(loid)s.  However, such information is lacking regarding any agro-ecological zone of Pakistan. The objectives of the present research proposal, therefore, are to index heavy metal(loid) status and their build-up rates in agricultural soils as determined by their inflows (irrigation, deposition, pesticides, fertilizers, manures) and outflows (crop removal, leaching).  The project will generate novel knowledge on the prevailing status of heavy metal(loid)s in agricultural soils, their balance, and their accumulation trends in the zone. Such information would contribute to sustainable heavy metal(loid) management in the agricultural soils to ensure crop production and soil protection, and ultimately to human health.

data.projectName: Mathematical modeling of super-active cutinase production from derepressed mutant strain of Aspergillus oryzae for polyester hydrolysis
data.projectDigest: All around the world plastic pollution is an ever increasing problem. In Pakistan, majority of the industries produce plastic based products which are non-degradable resulting in pollution. In order to face this dilemma, the ability of some enzymes to hydrolyze these polymers is being investigated as a probable solution to this major problem. One such enzyme is cutinase. This enzyme can degrade polyester polymers. In the present study, an extracellular thermostable cutinase from A. oryzae ISL-9 will be produced using submerged fermentation. Through induced mutagenesis by using methyl methane-sulfonate (MMS) as a mutagen, the strain will be improved for the process development. Different parameters like enzyme thermostability, effect of metallic and non-metallic micro-minerals and stabilizers on enzyme activity will be investigated. A model will be developed by methodical equations and solved with initial conditions by implementing mathematical techniques. The accuracy and efficiency of mathematical derivation will be exhibited through graphical illustrations and computed results will then be drafted in tabular form for specific values of physical parameters to validate the experimental design. The polyester degrading potential of the mutant enzyme will also be investigated. The thermal and kinetic stability of enzyme will be raised by immobilization on a macroporous support.

data.projectName: Antibiotics exposure
data.projectDigest: Environmental stresses are major constraint to plant production. Besides other stresses, antibiotics are major major inhibitor for plant growth and development. Antibiotics are available over the counter in our country and are being consumed in substantial amount by both in animals and humans. However, in developed countries the use of antibiotics is limited because of strict regulation and non-availability without a prescription. This overuse of antibiotics is posing a severe threat to the environment and our agriculture. The antibiotics are commonly used by humans but their use in animal husbandry is also enormous. This overuse of antibiotics by humans and animals has created the problem of antimicrobial resistance throughout the globe. Menadione sodium bisulphite (MSB) has been recently identified as plant growth regulator. So keeping in view the effectiveness of this compound we have planned to apply this compound to reduce antibiotics toxicity in plants in order to reduce its entry into the food chain. In the present experiment, MSB-mediated tolerance in wheat against antibiotics will be studied.

data.projectName: SCREENING OF MEDICINAL PLANTS FOR DIABETIES BY USING BIOCHEMICAL AND IN-SILICO STUDIES FROM DISTRICT HUNZA.
data.piUniversity: Karakurum International University, Gilgit, Gilgit Baltistan
data.projectDigest:
Diabetes mellitus are a big problem in our society and these are causing a big number of population to live a life of hardship. Arthritis leads to disability and depression. There is no proper treatment available for arthritis at the moment. Only pain management options are used for it. Currently used medicines are having adverse effects leading to other serious health issues. Diabetes mellitus is also threatening problem in the society. Diabetic patients are continuously living a life of pain and taking the medicines which are creating other diseases for them. There is no proper treatment available for diabetes at the time and it is also effecting other body systems. Medicines which are synthetic are having serious side effects and cannot be used safely for long duration. So the world is seeking alternative solutions for these problems.
Hunza valley is having most unique environment and so have plant species which are very unique. This area is rich with medicinal plants and many plants are already in use for the treatment of many such diseases in crude form. We could work on those plants to detect the bioactive molecules from them and would be check their toxic effect as drug. Berberis lycium Royle is such a plant which is locally found and is useful for diabetes and many other diseases. This project will lead to the exploration of more medicinal plants for diabetes like Berberis lycium Royle. We will identify the alkaloids found in these plants and we will further optimize them to become a more potent drug for treatment of these diseases in future.
