data.projectName: Heavy metal accumulation, health risk assessment and plant adaptation strategies in wild vegetable and fruit species of Azad Kashmir
data.projectDigest: In Azad Kashmir, use of wild vegetables and fruits by the people is very common in urban and sub-urban areas These natural foods are considered safe and health, and are being preferred over unnatural and procced ones available in markets and super stores. According to reports, about 90% of total metal intake is provided by consumption of vegetables and fruits contaminated with heavy metals [6]. Health risks associated with wild vegetables and fruits contaminated with heavy metals have been rarely investigated in Azad Kashmir, while plant adaptation strategies under metal stress (anatomical settings) are largely unknown till date [7]. Although desirable, it may not always be possible to attain quality control on vegetables and fruits from the farm to the final product, because of the large number of individual producers, but a reliable assessment with agricultural technology support can improve the quality of growing practices. Thus, continual monitoring of vegetable and fruit species, soil and species chemical investigations for heavy metal prior to cultivation and human health risk assessments are of great significance. Therefore, the basic idea and goal of this study is to examine the quality of wild foods and associated health risks of metal pollution that reach consumers as a function of cultivation site in different districts of Azad Kahmir. Based on outcomes of this study, methods of examination and calibration can be devised and suggestions on better selection of agricultural land for cultivation purposes and how to reduce the application of fertilizers can be provided to the local producers and consumers of these foods.

data.projectName: Quantum Information using Quantum Dark-Soliton Qubits
data.projectDigest:
Quantum Information Theory is multidisciplinary and rapidly developing research field. In the past decade many interesting breakthroughs were reported both theoretically and in experimental implementations of quantum communication, cryptography and quantum computation. 
One of the major challenges for in physical realization of quantum information theoretic protocols is decoherence. It is the noise introduced in quantum systems due to unwanted and unavoidable interaction with their environments. The search of physical systems/protocols more robust against decoherence is a problem of fundamental importance. The manipulation of quantum states for useful quantum computation becomes unsustainable at macroscopic scales as the quantum effects are defamed into classical averages. An important exception to these systems are Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) where quantum effects are distinctive at macroscopic level. 
We propose to use of quantum dark-solitons qubits, constructed by combining the intrinsic nonlinearity in BECs with dark solitons, for quantum communication and computation. These recently proposed qubits not only offer the possibility to construct perfectly isolated systems but also have lifetimes under typical experimental conditions. The usefulness of such systems is twofold; one the initialization of the quantum system in a desirable state and two ample time for quantum computation and communication before the system decays.

This research is intended to develop an artificial intelligence based system which will detect and predict about the disease which will help doctors to diagnose disease accurately with machine instead of manual diagnosis and patient can have better cure and better quality of life

data.projectName: Design of a Vascular Analysis Framework for Automated Quantification of Non-Calcified Coronary Plaques
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
In recent years, Cardiovascular diseases (CVD) have become the leading cause of death globally; i.e. CVDs resulted in approximately 17.9 million deaths (32.1%) in 2015 up from 12.3 million (25.8%) in 1990.  From a local perspective, Pakistani population has one of the highest risks of coronary heart disease in the world with annual deaths approximately equal to 265,000. According to the latest WHO data published, CHD is responsible for about 21.76% of total deaths. These high levels of mortality & morbidity have raised interest of research community towards early and accurate identification of the CHD at both national and international levels.
State-of-the-art imaging equipment has increased clinician's ability to make non-invasive diagnoses of coronary heart disease (CHD) in recent years; however, high volumes of imaging data make manual abnormality detection cumbersome in practice. In addition, the interpretation of CTA heavily relies upon the previous knowledge of the clinician and it always remains subjective to the second opinion. Accordingly, these limitations have driven an intense research in the context of automated solutions for fast, reliable and accurate diagnosis.
Consequently, in this research, we aim to design a working model for automated detection and quantification of the non-calcified coronary plaques in cardiac computed tomography angiography (CTA) images.

data.projectName: Fusion of Ensemble and Deep Learning for Automated Video Surveillance
data.piUniversity: Karachi Institute of Economics & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: With ever increasing security threats, the need of automated video surveillance systems is becoming more critical.  In developing countries in particular, the increasing rate of street crimes, snatching, robbery, kidnapping and other criminal activities, has become a major concern for the authorities.  In this project we propose to develop artificial intelligence (AI) – based video surveillance system to ensure security and well-being of the citizens.  In this research we propose to use the concept of ensemble machine learning to improve performance of Deep Neural Networks (DNN) for the problem of anomaly detection.  Our proposal is based on the rational that averaging of various models will result in a more robust model as different models will not make the same error.  Stated in a different way, we propose to form a “committee of experts” consisting of various deep networks and then fuse the decision of each expert to make a final decision.  To the best of our knowledge, this is a novel fusion of classical ensemble machine learning and the modern deep learning which has never been explored in the domain of anomaly detection.

data.projectName: Development of Effective Leadership and Management Theories for School, College and University: Evidence from Pakistani Context
data.projectDigest:
The project is planned in the area of ‘educational leadership and management’ of the subject ‘education’. The project is focused to develop leadership and management theories for school, college and university leaders and managers. When existing literature in the area of educational leadership and management is looked at closely, one do not finds any theory of leadership and management that is developed in the Pakistani organizational and societal context. Almost all the studies conducted in the selected area in Pakistan are focused either to test the theories developed in the western context or to find the relationships between various variables and these theories. This practice will not solve the problem unless theories are developed in the local societal and organizational cultural context.  Therefore, this project is planned to develop educational leadership and management theories in the Pakistani societal culture and organizational context to address the local issues.
Keeping in view the focus of the project, following research objectives are advanced:
1-	To develop leadership and management theories for schools.
2-	To develop leadership and management theories for colleges.
3-	To develop leadership and management theories for universities.

data.projectName: Automated detection system for tomato Plant leaf disease using faster R-CNN
data.projectDigest: Tomato is a type of plant called it tomato plant. Tomatoes (Solanum lycopersicum) can be grown on almost any moderately well-drained soil type. A good supply of organic matter can increase yield and reduce production problems. Tomatoes and related vegetables, such as potatoes, peppers and eggplants, should not be planted on the same land more than once in three years. After studying literature critically, it was conclude that in our daily life real time system play very important. It was obtain that mostly researcher had worked on the most popular plants leaf disease of the world but a very limited number of researches have been conducted on tomato crops. Some of the researcher used image processing just like segmentation for disease detection, some are used support victor machine and some are used Deep learning CNN. Therefore in this research work proposed Faster RCNN model based on CNN for tomato leaf disease classification and detection. This proposed model having ability to resolve the detection of effected area of tomato leaf disease which are the issue of earlier models. In this research the experimental results will be based on CNN models, Alex Net model and proposed Faster R-CNN model.

data.projectName: Role of Biochar and Silicon in Mitigation of Heavy Metal Stresses in Wheat Crop.
data.projectDigest: From last few years, heavy metal contamination in soil and water has be increased due to anthropogenic activities. The higher exposure of cereal crops to heavy metal stress reduces growth and yield, and significantly affected the sustainability of agricultural production. In this regard, the use of biochar and silicon (Si) supplementation offers a promising prospect to reducing heavy metals stresses. the beneficial role of biochar and silicon in mitigating stresses imposed by biotic as well as abiotic factors including heavy metal stress. The fundamental mechanisms involved in the biochar and Si-mediated heavy metal stress tolerance include reduction of metal ions in soil substrate, co-precipitation of toxic metals, metal-transport related gene regulation, chelation, stimulation of antioxidants, compartmentation of metal ions, and structural alterations in crops. Exogenous application of  Si and biochar alone and in combination will be increase heavy metal tolerance in numerous ceral crop species. The beneficial effects of biochar and Si are particularly evident in plants to enhance metal tolerance in plants, the inherent genetic potential for Si uptake should be improved. In the present review, we have discussed the potential role and mechanisms involved in the biochar and Si-mediated alleviation of metal toxicity as well as different approaches for enhancing Si-derived benefits in crop plants.

data.projectName: Partition Resolvability in graphs and its applications
data.projectDigest:
Networking and navigation can be studied in a graph-structured framework in which the navigation agent, e.g. robots, moves from node to node of a graph space.
• It can locate itself by the presence of distinctly labeled landmark nodes.
• Its navigation in Euclidean space, visual detection of a distinctive landmark provides information about the direction to the landmark, and allows the robot to determine its position by triangulation.
• On a graph, however, there is neither the concept of direction nor that of visibility. Instead, we shall assume that a robot navigating on a graph can sense the distances to a set of landmarks.
Evidently, if the robot knows its distances to a sufficiently large set of landmarks, its position on the graph is uniquely determined.
• This suggests the following problem: given a graph, what are the fewest number of landmarks needed, and where they should be located, so that the distances to the landmarks uniquely determine the robots position on the graph?
• This is actually a classical problem about metric spaces. A minimum set of landmarks which uniquely determines the robots position is called a metric basis, and the minimum number of landmarks is called the metric dimension of a graph.

data.projectName: Understanding the pathophysiology of congenital skeletal anomalies in Kashmiri families: A path towards diagnosis and cure
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest:
There are over 450 different types of skeletal dysplasia and among them more than 50 are without any known etiology. Collectively, these diseases affect 1/5,000 individuals. The major purpose of proposed study is to identify the genetic causes underlying skeletal dysplasias in Kashmiri population by using most advance molecular techniques. In Azad Kashmir due to its ethnic diversity and social customs, harbor large consanguineous families, this is the major source of conventional methods for mapping of defective genes. According to an estimate, 15-20 families with skeletal anomalies including osteogenesis imperfecta, brachydactyly, polydactyly, chondrodysplasia and dwarfism have already been identified, pedigrees generated and clinical, radiographic information and blood samples have also been collected by the principal investigator and PhD scholars from remote hilly areas of Azad Kashmir, Pakistan.
The current study will involve the mutational analysis of several Kashmiri, Pakistani families segregating autosomal recessive skeletal disabilities using Whole Exome Sequencing (WES). Identification of causative genes in these families will help us to explain the genetic nature of these skeletal dystrophies in Kashmiri population, which can lead to the better understanding in development of different genetic phenotypes. The expected results of this proposed study will be very helpful in investigation of carriers for skeletal anomalies in suspected familial cases of Kashmiri population. I am extremely convinced that by gaining new insights in skeletal physiology, in future I will be able to apply this new knowledge to develop better-targeted therapies for rare and common congenital skeletal anomalies.

data.projectDigest:
Workplace environment is important as it plays a key role in mental and physical health of the workers.  The existing literature acknowledge the importance of workplace environment in workers’ health, satisfaction and motivation. Improper workplace environment causes mental and physical disorders. The researchers and practitioners have introduced various types and levels of interventions at individual and organizational levels. These intervention help in improving well-being and health of the workers which ultimately result in increased productivity and service level. Unfortunately, working conditions in Pakistan are not up to the mark, not only because of lacks in physical infrastructure but also due to mismanagement caused due to lack of knowledge and training.
The main focus of this research is to identify the causes of physiological and psychological stress and to facilitate the workers in overcoming these issues. The project is planned to be conducted in three sectors including industry, healthcare and academia. These sectors are selected on the basis of their importance and role in society. The project is planned for three years and to be completed in phases. The first phase is to analyze the causes of stress through survey, interviews and observations. In last phase, the comparison would be made in order to find out the impact of interventions.

data.projectName: Anatomical and Biochemical Characterization of Few Road Side Plants in Lahore
data.projectDigest: Plant leaves have great potential to work as sinks of air pollution and are promising features to indicate the environmental changes. However, anatomical and morphological features of leaves has not been given much attention in this regard. We hereby combine the study of morpho-anatomical and biochemical attributes in order to broaden our knowledge of plant selection to be used against the wide range of environmental pollutants. The point is not how do the plants cope or resist with the environmental pollution rather it is to undertake these parameters to know about those plants which can help us in the reduction or control of increasing levels of air pollutants. Our proposal considers one of the populous city Lahore which is the victim of unplanned urbanization, industrialization and vehicular influx. The study focus to analyze the leaf samples from vegetation of green belts and roadsides and to refine the selection of plants to be used for the purpose.

data.projectName: ‘Re-politicizing Human Rights: Governance Assessment for enhanced GSP+ compliance in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Pakistan has enjoyed tremendous benefits from European Union’s Generalized Scheme of Preferences Plus, which is a special incentive arrangement for advancing Sustainable Development and Good Governance. Despite tremendous gains from the deal amounting over US$ 15 billion, the progress on social development and human rights continues to be skewed. The situation has put Pakistan’s GSP+ status in jeopardy and the government is lobbying with European Parliament to seek an extension until 2023. The single most dominant factor impeding human rights growth has been inadequate governance mechanisms for implementation of core 27 UN treaties. The 18 months proposed interventional case study seeks to assess governance structures for enhanced compliance of human rights in Pakistan. The study will generate concrete actionable recommendations at the provincial as well as national level.

data.projectName: Media Anthropology of Intangible Cultural Heritage: A Case Study of Kalasha
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
In response to UNESCO’s Convention for Safeguarding Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH), international, national and local level institutions, associations and individuals from around the world have started exploiting the power of Social Media to co-create/produce/author their intangible cultural heritage and practices. While the prior research on the subject concentrates on the impact of online platforms for the protection and promotion of ICH, there is dire need to explore the full potential of traditional and new media outlets in the safeguarding endangered intangible heritage. 
In this context, this research will employ a grounded theory approach to explore the potential of traditional and new media outlets in facilitating institutions, associations and individuals for safeguarding intangible cultural heritage. 
As a case study, an intensive media anthropology of Kalasha’s intangible cultural heritage will be conducted in the span of 12 months. Located in the Chitral District of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan, Kalasha Valley’s Intangible Culture Heritage (ICH) faces severe threat of extinction in the wake of modernization and increased cultural tourism. The valley remains a special focus of UNESCO where a network of actors has collaborated with the Kalasha community to safeguard their Intangible Cultural Practices.

data.projectName: Susceptibility of type 2 diabetic gene associated polymorphisms in the development and progression of breast cancer”.
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Zulfikar Ali Bhutto Institute of Science & Technology (SZABIST) University, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The genetic basis of common and complex diseases has become better understandable by the completion of the human genome project. Through number of genetic study methodologies including linkage analyses of potential genes and through genome wide association studies (GWAS), several single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) have been reported as risk loci for type 2 diabetes (T2D) in groups of European and Asian population. Breast cancer is the most frequent cancer among women, impacting 2.1 million women each year, and also causes the greatest number of cancer-related deaths among women.Epidemiologic study suggests that people with diabetes are at significantly higher risk for many forms of cancer and greater cancer mortality, predominantly type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), Different cancer types, as well as T2DM could share a number of major risk factors. Type 2 diabetic gene polymorphisms are associated with an increased susceptibility to breast cancer. Therefore, objective of this study is to identify and analyze the T2D gene and to assess the association of gene polymorphisms in controls and in cases of Type 2 Diabetes and breast cancer.This study will be done in collaboration so that more and different sample sizes can be collected to influence the genetic population study.

data.projectName: Bioadhesive For Suture Less Wound Closure and Minimally Invasive Surgeries
data.projectDigest:
Bioadhesives are high molecular weight, biocompatible, biodegradable polymers used to join two surfaces where at least one of them is a living tissue. These are used for two main purposes, first as a replacement for surgical sutures and second as a substitute for traditional drug dosage systems.
Tissue reconstruction and wound closure depend on sutures, staples and clips in recent practiced surgical procedures. These traditional devices are nonetheless unable to prevent leakage of fluids from a variety of tissue including blood vessels. Sutures are usually difficult to apply during minimal invasive surgery and often induce detrimental scarring that may impair healing. Bioadhesives can enhance tissue repair and wound healing while reducing operative risks. They represent a fast and less traumatic closure method resulting less pain and for that reason does not require secondary operative procedure and also eliminate the problem of suture removal. Cyanoacrylate glues create typically very strong tissue bonds but have mostly been applied externally for skin wound closure because of their residual cytotoxicity. Other adhesive biomaterials are also emerging; these glues and adhesives are usually based on proteins such as albumin and collagen or polysaccharides like chitosan, and Dextran. Present proposal focuses on the synthesis of a novel tissue adhesive based on biocompatible and bio-degradable polysaccharides (Chitosan, Dextran) or egg albumin incorporating  chemical inspired by marine mussel and introducing photocrosslinkable vinyl group by chemical modification on to polysaccharides backbone  which can be photocrosslinked under the ultraviolet (UV) irradiation in presence of initiator.

data.projectName: Computational Assessment of Solar Energy Aspects on Nanofluid Flows due to Bi-directionally Stretchable Surface
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest: In this research proposal, we planned to analyze the performance of solar radiation on bi-directionally stretchable nanomaterial (Newtonian and non-Newtonian) flow with aspects of Brownian movement and thermophoresis. Additionally, this newly investigated proposal will be more authentic, where it is introduced that the surface temperature and concentration are adjustable on the surface boundaries. Industrial and engineering quantities of interest namely drag forces, Nusselt number, and Sherwood number will be analyzed in a more effective way by utilizing the solar radiation aspects.  The solution of non-dimensionlized model equations (either ODEs or PDEs) will be numerically obtained by using Keller box method (KBM) or Chebyshev spectral newton iterative scheme (CSNIS).  Finally, the key importance of involved constraints on nanomaterial (Newtonian and non-Newtonian) velocity components, temperature distribution, and concentration distribution will be elucidated graphically in detail.

data.projectName: Reducing arsenic exposure to human through modified bentonite clays
data.projectDigest: Arsenic (As) contaminated drinking water can have adverse health effects including lung cancer and cardiovascular diseases. Pakistan has a major arsenic problem, as 50 to 60 million people in the Indus plain use groundwater are at risk. Bentonite clays are abundant in nature, inexpensive and environment friendly and can be modified for efficient removal of contaminants including As. Arsenic sorption capacity of local clay deposits can be enhanced by modification of bentonite clays. The objective of the study is to modify the bentonite clays with organic molecules and inorganic cation pillaring to enhance their As sorption capacity in aqueous environment. Bentonite samples will be selected after X-ray diffraction analysis and will be modified by intercalating organic and inorganic species in the interlayer spaces of bentonite. Modified clays will be characterized using XRD, XRF, FTIR and transmission electron microscopy prior and after their As sorption determination. Large indigenous clay deposits especially bentonite can be used efficiently as As adsorbent from drinking water and help reduce As exposure to humans. Poor and rural communities of Pakistan cannot afford expensive treatment systems or bottled water and need an affordable low-tech solution which can be provided by using modified bentonite in household filter systems.

data.projectName: Determination of Luteal Efficiency for Production of Progesterone through Doppler Ultrasonography and for Prevention of Embryonic Mortality in Nili-Ravi Buffaloes
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Nili-Ravi buffalo is known as the black gold of Pakistan and has the ability to thrive in tropical and subtropical conditions, best converter of low quality roughages, its greater milk taste, butter color and quality. Paradoxically, buffaloes are blamed for its reproductive sluggishness due to several reasons including poor estrus expression, delayed puberty, longer post partum ovarian quiescence, lowered pregnancy rates particularly when bred artificially, improper timing of insemination summer anestrus and higher embryonic and fetal losses. 
Progesterone (P4) concentration depends corpus luteum (CL) volume and blood flow. Buffalo fail to establish successful pregnancy in early days of gestation (21-45). Embryonic mortality can be prevented by applying different strategies to increase concentration of P4. Additionally, blood flow indices of the CL can be predict its viability P4 production. 
Nili-Ravi buffaloes (n=240) will be synchronized and inseminated with CIDR-GnRH and divided into four groups days 7 post insemination for production of accessory CL. This project aimed to increase productive and reproductive performance by of decreasing  the calving interval, embryonic losses, cost of semen and increase calf per year cumulative pregnancy rate which will increase the overall productivity and profitability of buffalo farmers by producing more meat, milk and by products.

data.projectName: Isolation and Evaluation of Plant Growth Promoting Rhizobacteria (PGPRs) Associated with different plants from Charsadda, KPK, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Often not perceptible to the naked eye, interactions between plants and microorganisms occur in many different ways and on many different levels. Virtually all organs of the plant interact with microorganisms at a certain stage of their life, and this interaction is not necessarily negative for the plant. Indeed, there are plenty of interactions where the plant benefits either through direct or through indirect effects of the associated microbes. In these interactions, plants serve as sheltered habitats for the microorganisms that may colonize apoplastic spaces, plant surface areas or areas adjacent to the plant surface, e.g., the rhizosoil, the soil in the vicinity of roots. In addition to a sheltered habitat and a future source of nutrients that are liberated upon plant death, many plants release compounds that attract and feed the associated microbes. The associated microbes may in turn secrete compounds that favor plant growth, they may make the plant more resistant to abiotic or biotic stress, or they may defend the plant against more malignant microbes. To the best of our knowledge, there is no research setup for this kind of analysis in Pakistan. This project will serve as a critical part for development of biofertilizers system in the abundant sugarcane growing area of Pakistan's.

data.projectName: Development of lightweight aggregate concrete and structural applications
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Lightweight Aggregate Concrete (LWAC) is about 25 to 30% ighter than Normal Weight Concrete (NWAC). The typical aggregates used in LWAC are shale, slate, natural pumice, vermiculite perlite and expanded clay.  The use of LWAC significantly increases bridge, building, or marine structure functionality. The reduction in foundation loads results in smaller footings, fewer piles, smaller pile caps, less reinforcement and smaller supporting members (decks, beams, girder, and piers), resulting in a major reduction in cost. Also, LWAC will mean reduced inertial seismic forces. Pakistan has massive lightweight aggregate (LWA) deposits in numerous mountainous ranges e.g. Margalla and Attock-Cherat mountainous ranges near Islamabad, Peshawar and Naka Pabni situated in the north of Karachi. Thus, it is essential that a comprehensive investigation be conducted to characterize the physical characteristics and chemical composition of all possible LWA’s naturally occurring in Pakistan using the protocol of relevant ASTM (PSQCA) Standards. Subsequently rheological and mechanical and durability properties of LWAC (using selected LWA’s) should be characterized. To date, the use of LWAC (with local LWA’s) for structural applications (Behavior of structural member, e.g. slab, beam and column) has not been investigated in Pakistan. Thus, this project is the demand of current social and economic perspective.

data.projectName: An empirical survey to determine the factors that limit the technology adoption in the bricks making industry of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is the 3rd largest brick producer in the world. However, since most of the production is based on the conventional methods of kilns, the brick making industry in Pakistan is one of the most emission intensive industry. Despite being an important industrial sector that plays crucial role toward country’s infrastructure development, the brick making industry is still informal and unregulated. It is the home of the largest child- and bonded-labour in the country. The sector is highly labor intensive and inefficient. In general, it is the most backward sectors in terms of the technology perspective.   Although, some studies in the recent past have been conducted, but none of the studies have look up the technological factor, which is considered remedial to all the socio-economic bad associated with the industry. Thus, this project offers a comprehensive empirical survey based on the data collected from all over the country to determine what limits the brick making industry from embracing new technology. The project possesses important policy implications for the most criticised yet an important industry of the country.

data.projectName: Molecular genetic studies of neurodegenerative diseases in population of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
data.projectDigest: It is complicated to identify the disease responsible genes in complex disorders than to associate gene with diseases following Mendelian or near Mendelian inheritance. In the past years through genome wide association studies, whole genome sequencing and whole exome sequencing many genetic variants have been identified that influence complex diseases such as neurodegenerative disorders. A fundamental challenge of genetic studies of neurodegenerative disorders is to identify and understand patients genetic pattern in comparison to the symptoms produced. In many populations there is a strong preference for consanguineous marriages like in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa population. In the present study homozygosity mapping, sequencing, genome wide association study, linkage analysis and mutations identification will be performed to recognize the disease causing mutations as well as the associated SNPs. Consanguinity and large family size with many affected individuals provides a great potential of finding neurodegenerative disease susceptibility gene/s. The present study will help in understanding frequent hot spot genetic risk loci associated with common neurodegenerative diseases, gene function, prenatal diagnosis, genetic counseling and carrier screening. Application of data generated from this study may be helpful for the affected individuals as well as for their families by making the affected individuals useful members of the community.

data.projectName: Livestock extension & future strategies: implication for the small-scale farmers in Punjab Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Most important and the backbone of the Pakistan, agriculture is losing its strength with every passing year. Contribution of agriculture has depleted down over the couple of decades from 50% to 18.5% till now. Over the years, the livestock sub-sector has surpassed the crop sub-sector as the largest contributor to value added in agriculture. The Dairy sector in Pakistan consists of three types of producers; 80% small farmers, 17% medium-sized farmers, 3% large-scale. The present yield of the animal is far behind the potential level. Increase in milk or meat production in the country is just because of the increasing population of livestock. Per animal production is stagnant. This can only be increased through the appropriate application of modern livestock technologies in this sector. It is, therefore, essential that the livestock farming community must be made familiar with the scientific knowledge and improved livestock practices and techniques. All the above motioned constrained directly or indirectly comes under the umbrella of one department and that is extension. Hence lack of proper extension services result in non adoption of improved livestock technologies among the livestock farmers. The universe of the study will be the Punjab Pakistan. There are total 36 districts in the districts and three districts will be selected purposively keeping in view the objective of the study. Target population of the study will be the small livestock farmers and public livestock extension staff. Both qualitative and quantitative data will be collected from the selected sample.

data.projectName: Validating The Relation Between Various Hematological Attributes for Diagnostic/Prognostic Approach to Anemia in Cholistani Livestock
data.projectDigest: A convention has been adopted in human medical laboratory practice in estimating hemoglobin (Hb) concentration as a third of packed cell volume (PCV) or vice versa. However, there is hardly any information on the validity of this commonly used relationship between Hb concentration and PCV, and other relationships / mathematical nexus between various hematological attributes for veterinary medical practice. The present work has, hence, been proposed with an aim to validating various hematological attributes for Cholistani livestock (camel and Cholistani cattle). Ultimate outcome will be a set of economical, quick, precise and validated tests/formulae which can be utilized in field to assess anemia and its type. The PCV will be validated as quick and economical method for estimating other blood attributes of livestock. On-site/field diagnostic kit/formulae for quick diagnosis of anemia in livestock will also be validated.  The project will be carried out on blood samples of Cholistani camels & cattle both at Tobas of desert and various govt. livestock farms in collaboration with various units of Livestock & dairy Development Department of Punjab.  Ultimate outcome will be an on site anemia diagnostic kit and various mathematical relationships between various hematological attributes.

data.projectName: Assessment Of Patterns Of Patient Reported Outcomes In Adults With Congenital Heart Disease – International Study - APPROACH-IS collaborative
data.projectDigest:
Congenital Heart Disease (CHD) is a life-long disease and the patients go through physical and mental health issues. Therefore it is very important to understand the health related quality of life (HRQOL) of this patient population. The HRQOL vary based on factors including disease complexity, early treatment, higher income and education. 
 
We plan to develop a database (over 18,000 patients’ representation from developing and developed countries), first of its kind, focusing on HRQOL of life of adults with CHD. We will also use artificial intelligence to predict the HRQOL of these patients for early identification and management of the issues. 

About 90% of the population in the world live in developing countries facing issues related to cost, travelling, lack of health care facilities and expert health care professionals. To bypass these issues, we plan to develop a smart phone app to reach the adult CHD patients and explore their quality of life. It will be more convenient for these patients to respond at their own time, setting and in their own language. Using technology, the app will translate the response to English for analyzing the responses.

Based on the findings of this study, we will strengthen our health care systems.

data.projectName: Photonic Bragg Stacks: A Soft Fabrication Strategy for Electrochromic Device Applications
data.projectDigest:
Many biological materials with an inbuilt structural hierarchy, ranging from opals and beetles, peacock feathers, squids to butterfly wings, show brilliant colors due to interference of light. These natural Photonic crystals show direction-dependent color that arises due to structural interference due to a refractive index contrast between the constituent materials. The periodic nature of photonic materials ensures that travelling light waves will undergo interference at the constantly changing interfaces. A photonic band gap thus arises in the direction of periodicity, through which waves of certain frequencies cannot travel, if the wavelength of light is comparable to the structural periodicity. For example, naturally occurring gemstones, such as opals, are 3D photonics, with a complete bandgap. 
Photonic crystals with a uni-directional band gap are known as Bragg stacks. These have been relatively understudied, and mainly by the expensive semi-conductor fabrication techniques. This research proposal aims to build photonic Bragg stacks via a soft matter approach, which is versatile, cost-effective and offers easy color tunability by employing nanochemistry. The photonic band gap, and hence color, can be tuned by synthesizing nanostructures of variable refractive index with different shape, sizes and packing, and building up the photonics by the simple procedure of spin-coating. This soft matter approach offers high control over structure organization in photonic stacks that could be of particular efficacy, due to the ease in designing, and the  wide choice of available materials, including polymers. Additionally, using electrochromic moieties as constituents can lead to electrically responsive smart photonic devices that can switch color on application of potential.

data.projectName: Identification and characterization of Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) strains and  recombinant cry toxin proteins production to inhibit the insects of important crops of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The emergence and spread of increasing resistance in many insects species can no longer be safely based upon the use of chemicals pesticides alone. Therefore, now a day, biological control of insects and pests is widely used worldwide as a desirable technique due to i) less danger for the environment ii) natural control iii) safe for the microbial community present in the soil. Among the biological control agents, Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) is one of the most promising biological control agents for pest and insect management. In developed countries, Bacillus thuringiensis products account for 90-95 percent of the total pesticide market but in Pakistan, no such product is available for insect’s control. Pakistan and particularly Hazara Division may have huge diversity of Bt strains that needed to be explored. Therefore, in this study, we will isolate, culture, identify and preserve the different Bt strains from Abbottabad, Haripur and Mansehra.  In addition, we will identify the different cry genes in isolated Bt strains that could be involved to kill insects of important crops. Moreover, we will produce cry proteins in huge quantity by cloning identified cry genes in pET30 (Ek/LIC) vector and expressed them in E. coli BL21 (DE3) strains. The cry proteins expressed in E. coli BL21 (DE3) will be purified using affinity chromatography. Therefore, now a day, biological control of insects and pests is widely used worldwide as a desirable technique due to i) less danger for the environment ii) natural control iii) safe for the microbial community present in the soil. Among the biological control agents, Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) is one of the most promising biological control agents for pest and insect management. In developed countries, Bacillus thuringiensis products account for 90-95 percent of the total pesticide market but in Pakistan, no such product is available for insect’s control. data.projectName: A DNA Barcoding approach to Construct Lichen Database of Pakistan and Exploration of their Persuasive Metabolites
data.projectDigest: In this particular venture, we aim to explore lichens distributed all over Pakistan. A lichen looks like a single organism, but it is actually a symbiotic relationship between different organisms, one of them is the fungal partner (mycobiont) and other can be one or more photosynthetic partners (photobiont). The collections made therefrom will be preserved, processed, characterized and properly identified through the classical means such as morphology, anatomy, spore phenotypes and spore tests. The species recognized thereby will further be verified through the advanced DNA technology and related compound analysis methods (TLC). The central aim of this study is to investigate chemical composition of acetone and other organic and inorganic extracts of different lichens and their antimicrobial and anticancer activities. Moreover, our aim is determination of total phenolic compounds in various extracts. The antimicrobial activity will be estimated by determination of the minimal inhibitory concentration by the broth microdilution method. Anticancer activity will also be tested against LS174 (human colon carcinoma cell line), A549 (human lung carcinoma cell line), Fem-x (malignant melanoma cell line), and a chronic myelogeneous leukaemia K562 cell line using the MTT method. This information will be made available to scientists, industrialist and general public on the specially designed National Biotechnology Database for Fungi of Pakistan.

data.projectName: DEVELOPING FUNGAL HEAVY METAL REMOVAL ASSEMBLIES COUPLED WITH SOLARIZED ADVANCED OXIDATION & EVAPORATION SYSTEMS FOR TREATMENT OF TANNERY EFFLUENT
data.projectDigest: Tanned leather is the 2nd largest export earner of Pakistan contributing > 5 % of GDP but at the expense of fresh water pollution due to discharge of untreated tannery effluent (TE), absolutely not permitted by the environmental regulatory authorities. For ? 5 % of the total discharged TE, an inadequate treatment is carried out that stays incapable of removing toxic hazardous chromium (Cr). Its removal from TE has been a big challenge due to presence of interfering agents such as, inorganic matter, organic load, salts, sulfides and sulfates, total Kjeldahl nitrogen, ammonia, chlorides and heavy metals. Bioremediation approaches are considered adaptive in terms of being cost-effective; however, amongst them bioremediation with hyperaccumulator fungi show far more Cr uptake per unit biomass than hyperaccumulator plants. But growing fungi in water without anchorage is a big challenge. In the proposed project, a fungal heavy metal removal assembly will be developed in which fungi can thrive extremely rapidly on very low cost substrates while being coupled with a solarized advanced oxidation & evaporation systems. The key outcomes of the proposed project are overcoming challenge of growing fungi in water for its treatment and bioextraction of Cr from TE of very complex composition.

data.projectName: Distributed Machine Learning based Intrusion Detection and Prevention System
data.projectDigest:
Due to increased digitization and networking the associated threats have become a matter of grave concern for all especially for the government and private organizations.  To protect against such threats the most widely used approach is the deployment of Intrusion Detection / Prevention Systems that could effectively detect network-based intrusion attempts from malicious sources and then mitigate them. Although conventional IDS / IPS can easily detect and prevent existing attacks, which are already known, they cannot detect the new attacks. 

Moreover, due to the increase in applications of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and emergence of technologies such as 5G Networks and Internet of Things (IOT), an enormous amount of network traffic is being generated, known as the Big Data. Although the ML-based IDS are considered efficient for Anomaly-based Intrusion Detection on Low Speed Networks, these techniques require very expensive hardware while coping with High-Speed Networks. 

Therefore, our aim is to distribute the computational load to multiple machines that coordinate with each other to complete the overall task. And the system has the capability to detect and prevent existing as well as the new attacks.

data.projectName: Isolation, Culture and Characterization of Endothelial Cells from Umbilical Cord of Pakistani Women
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Introduction
The endothelial cells, line all of our blood vessels such as arteries, arterioles, venules, veins and capillaries. The primary function of endothelial lining (endothelium) is to maintain permeability of vessel wall and regulate blood flow. The selective permeability property of endothelial cells has wider biomedical applications such as investigation in the blood-brain-barrier system, drug development that can cross the endothelial barrier efficiently. 

Limitations in Pakistan
In Pakistan not much research is going on in the above-mentioned areas due to following limitations: (a) limited cell culture facilities across Pakistan (b) high cost of endothelial cells in market (c) and costly media used for the growth of endothelial cells in culture. 

Need for Proposed Study
Commercially available endothelial cells are very costly and demand a continuous supply due short life span of endothelial cells therefore, this calls for a need for in- vitro isolation and culturing of endothelial cells from rich sources like umbilical cord. 
Thus, the aim of this project is to develop a reliable and user friendly protocol for isolation and culture of endothelial cells from umbilical cord. The protocol set will be according to the conditions and resources of Pakistan so that it can be adopted effortlessly.

data.projectName: Development of enriched organic fertilizer for mango orchards using composted press mud from sugarcane industries
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: Mango (Mangifera indica L.) is an eminent and second important fruit of southern Punjab, Pakistan because of its delicious taste, fragrances, aesthetic values and colors. However, its per capita yield is only 11.2 tonnes/ha, which is half of world per capita yield (25 tonnes/ha). This difference is due to inadequate mango orchard fertilizer and nutrient deficiency of soil which weakens the plant, consequently the death of mango trees. Pakistan produces and exports high quality mango but there is a large gap between production capacity and export demand. The need of time is to increase mango yield using eco-friendly and practical solutions. This project aims to ameliorate the mango yield by developing an organic fertilizer to replenish soil with suitable macro/micronutrients and plant growth promoting rhizobacteria. The press mud which is a by-product of sugarcane industry will be used as alternate source of essential nutrients i.e. NPK, B, Cu, Fe, Mn, and Zn. These nutrients will be available added after composting of press-mud and enriched with plant growth promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR). This study will furnish an organic fertilizer for growing mango with less fertilizer and high yield.

data.projectName: Early Diagnosis of Alzheimer’s Disease using Data-mining Techniques on Behavioral Data
data.projectDigest: According to World Health Organization (WHO), approximately 50 million people live with dementia throughout the world. Nearly, 60 % are living in low and middle-income countries. It is expected that this population will reach 82 million in 2030 and 152 million in 2050. Alzheimer's disease (AD), is an incurable and progressive disease and is the most common type of dementia. Memory loss and confusion that disrupts daily life and misplacing objects are common symptoms of AD. Early diagnosis of memory disorders can help physicians, caregivers and patients to cope with daily life and improve their quality of life. Since, in the primary stage of these diseases, people still have the ability to report their status and are more able to help with their treatment, rehabilitation processes can be run sooner and health-care costs reduced. Since Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) can be a predictor for some types of dementia, such as Alzheimer's disease (AD), diagnosing mental disorders at a healthy age is significantly crucial. In the field of medical diagnosis, classification algorithms and data-mining techniques play an effective role in the analysis of diseases and health conditions. In other words, predictive models have been developed to determine people at high risk of disease and to reduce the associated health-care costs. Further research is required to detect memory disorders in their early stages and to distinguish cognitive decline at a healthy age. Identifying behavioral changes and activities in people with MCI can help physicians to begin treatments as soon as possible to reduce the speed of developing AD. The purpose of this research is to use machine learning algorithm for the prediction of MCI that leads to AD.

data.projectName: Theoretical and computational properties of topological indices and characterization of extremal graphs
data.projectDigest:
The proposed research project is in graph theory. Graph theory has numerous applications in all branches of applied sciences. A graph is a mathematical structure that can be thought of, informally, as a collection of points (usually called vertices), with some of the points joined by lines, and others not. So in this context graphs are not the graphs we know from school mathematics.

Chemical graph theory is a recent and rapidly developing interdisciplinary science branch. In chemical graph theory, topological indices help in the development of quantitative structure-activity relationship and quantitative structure-property relationships in which the physical, chemical and other properties of molecules are correlates with their structure.

Every molecule has its chemical structure which consist of atoms and bonds. A molecular graph is obtained by representing atoms via vertices and bonds by the lines between the atoms.  Now, by applying the definition of a topological index on this molecular graph we obtain a number and this number can predict certain properties of the molecule. 

In this project, we are interested in
•	 investigating certain degree and distance based topological indices to examine the physico-chemical properties of molecular graphs,
•	establishing algorithmic and computational techniques to compute the certain topological indices of carbon based molecular structures,
•	new graph operations that can generate new graphs from the existing ones,
•	studying the mathematical behavior of certain topological indices for different classes of graphs. Then we will characterize the family of graph(s) with the minimum and maximum topological index.

data.projectName: Nanosensors
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Chemical sensors are devices that detect or measure any chemical quantity by converting it into an analytically useful signal. A good sensor should exhibit fast response, high sensitivity, high reliability, high volume production with low cost that can be operated on site and in situ. Chemical sensors have attracted great attention due to their wide spread uses in environmental monitoring, industry, pharmaceutics and bio medicine. Sensors with high selectivity and sensitivity are needed for the real-time detection of leakage of hazardous chemicals, and for the detection of toxic gases in industries (e.g ammonia, hydrogen chloride, hydrogen sulfide, etc). The demand to monitor and control our environment is very high. Moreover sensing of nerve agents for the homeland security has also become an important issue nowadays. The essential criteria for the potent chemical sensors are: (i) speedy recovery and response time, (ii) high selectivity and sensitivity, (iii) stability in performance, and (iv) low operating temperature and temperature independence. The principal objective of this research is to prepare functionalized graphene and carbon nanotubes based nanosensors, with high sensitivity, durability and low detection limit, for the analysis and detection of different organophosphate volatile toxic compounds.

data.projectName: Immunotherapeutic Targets of Chronically Infected Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) Patients
data.projectDigest: Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) is a widely distributed blood borne pathogen that targets hepatocytes and thereby enters acute phase followed by chronic infection. Chronically infected HCV patients (CHC) are likely to develop several severe metabolic and extra hepatic manifestations such as Insulin resistance and Fibrosis. In Pakistan, more than 10% of total population is suffering from chronic HCV infections that makes them resistant towards sustained virological response (SVR) i.e. viral clearance. In this regard, few studies have depicted the plausible role of genetic variants of certain cytokines in the treatment outcome. Nevertheless, no study has focused towards mechanisms of these HCV associated pathologies and their link with the genetic variants of cytokines. In addition, we would try to come up with some novel RNA helicases that can have the potential to naturally degrade viral RNA and enhance the treatment outcomes. As cytokines are anti-viral in action and different level is found in different patients, therefore, this study is pilot study that encircles the plausible role of genetic variants of certain cytokines as well as the elucidation of novel RNA helicases that can influence treatment outcome i.e. development or rejection of Sustained virological resposnse (SVR).

data.projectName: Geochemical and Geophysical techniques for exploration and economic evaluation of Iron ores from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Iron ores are used for the extraction of iron and is used for making steel, cement and alloys. Reconnaissance studies based on geochemical information give some indications for the occurrence of iron ores. However more detailed studies involving processing and geophysical techniques are required in order to increase the probability of finding economic iron ores for rapid economy growth and industrialization. The sedimentary block covering the districts of Haripur, Nowshera, Kohat, Hangu, Karak, Lakki Marwat and D.I. Khan, is a prospective geological domain for basing steel as well as chemical and other manufacturing industries. Advance mineral and geochemical / processing specially with the use of advance equipment like ICP-MS, Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) and Quantitative evaluation of minerals using Scanning Electron Microscopy (QEMSCAN). Among these, QEMSCAN is widely used in the mineral industry around the world because it can rapidly identify minerals (%age) and also give information about mineral associations as visible in digital images. The use of Geophysical techniques such as Ground Penetration Radar (GPR) and Resistivity Survey (Induced Polarization) will add a new life to exploration of iron ores in the country. In Pakistan rarely such studies have been carried out. In this context the current study is required for generating bankable data required for local and international investors.

data.projectName: Integration of 21st Century Learning Skills in Higher Education Curriculum, Pedagogy and Assessment
data.projectDigest: 21st century learning skills contain abilities, capacities, and learning that have been distinguished as being required in 21st century society and working environments. These skills vary from scholastic abilities in that they are not essentially content based. data.projectName: Evaluation of infectious burden and antibiotic resistance in hospital laboratories in remote areas of Punjab
data.projectDigest: Health care workers and laboratory staff working in health care laboratories are at high risk of exposure to various types of infections caused by a diverse array of pathogens including antibiotic resistant microorganism. This situation is more alarming in health care laboratories located in the remote areas of Punjab because of inadequate infrastructure, shortage of trained personnel, irregular supply of gloves, masks, disinfectants, poor laboratory set up. The proposed project is to determine the microbial burden and their antibiotic resistance in laboratory staff and laboratories environment, associated with Tehsil Headquarter Hospitals (THQ), Rural Health Centers (RHC) and Basic Health Units (BHUs) situated in remote areas of Punjab. For this purpose a total of at 500 samples will be collected from health care laboratories and laboratory staff of district Okara, Punjab province, through sterile aseptic techniques. The samples will be evaluated for bacterial and fungal loads by inoculation on general purpose media followed by growth on differential media specific for bacterial and fungal growth. Biochemical characterization of the pure colonies will performed via a standard procedure based on Bergey’s manual of systemic bacteriology. Antibiotic susceptibility testing will be performed by disk diffusion method according to Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) guidelines, only for those isolates that are clinically relevant for infections. Statistical significance of the data will be determined by Graph pad prism software. Data obtained from this study will identify flaws in Biosafety infrastructure in hospital laboratories in remote areas of Punjab and will provide suggestions for improvement resulting into better health status of workers.

data.projectName: Nonlinear Dynamics of Semiconductor Lasers
data.projectDigest: The current trends in technology propose optical computing and communication to perform logical operations more efficiently. In this project we propose optical injections in lasers. That is, the output of one laser (i.e. master laser) is injected as input to the other laser (i.e. slave laser). The output of slave laser is analyzed under different parameters (power, temperature, current). One phenomenon of optical injection is polarization switching bi-stability. Our experiments will investigate the bi-stability to design efficient computer systems in future.

data.projectName: Synthesis of magnetic Bio-char as an economically feasible safe and  a renewable material for treatment of contaminated bodies
data.projectDigest: In order to deal with biomass or communal waste, pyrolysis is the most suitable energy recycling method that leads to breakdown of bonds on heating. Bio-char managed the open ended bio-waste disposal into the closed loop materials along with attaining multiple co-benefits in the form of energy provision, improve soil quality with enhance crop yield and also ensure better environmental quality. A large number of literature available on using bio-char‘s batch experiment for water purification but the optimization and appropriate design for the purification of waste water for useful purpose is still un-explored. Bio-char is a solid material obtained through pyrolysis or carbonization of biomass. Additionally, bio-char limits emission of greenhouse gases in atmosphere, lower fertilizers requirement and reduce erosion. This current research proposal suggests that bio-char is an economically feasible safe bio-adsorbent and a renewable technology for clean water provision along with others co-benefits of improving environmental air quality. The purpose of this research proposal is twofold one is formulate an industrially applicable plan of bio-char-based water purification and second is to develop a path for new researchers ager to explore in this field.

data.projectName: Formulation Development of Acyclovir microcapsules by using Spray Drying ,Double emulsion techniques  and its in Vitro & in vivo characterization
data.projectDigest:
Background: Acyclovir is a safe and effective antiviral product. It has short half life of 2-4 hr, poorly absorbed in intestine, best absorbed in stomach, and undergo extensive first pass effect (95%).So it,s ideal candidate for microencapsulation.
The microencapsulation is the technique of surrounding or enveloping one substance within another substance on a very small scale, yielding capsules ranging from less than one micron to several hundred micron in size. The encapsulation efficiency of the microparticles depends on concentration of polymer, solubility of polymer in solvent, rate of solvent removal, solubility of organic solvent in water etc.the  microencapsulation of Acyclovir by spray drying and double emulsion  techniques . Pre-formulation studies  will be performed on active ingredient to establish the suitability of active ingredient. Test formulations characterization ( encapsulation efficiency, scanning electron microscopy, DSC, FTIR, powdered x-ray difraction ),will be done for best efficiency and possible interactions among ingredients. The IN-VITRO drug release profile will be studied to observe release mechanism of drug from polymer. Further the  bioavailability and bioequivalence studies will be performed on test formulations by comparing with commercially available products Outcome:	
The recommended daily dose of Acyclovir is 4-6 hours, this study will help to reduce the dosing frequency, per day and total cost of treatment. The microencapsulation will also increase the patient compliance. As no controlled release formulation of Acyclovir is available in Pakistan, so this research area has huge potential to give advantageous superior product for patients and pharmaceutical industry.
.

data.projectName: Layered Manufacturing of Steel Parts for Automobile Industry through Selective Laser Melting (SLM)
data.projectDigest: In the current automobiles industry there is greater emphasis on fabricating the parts with good quality characteristics and homogeneity. Precise dimensional accuracy with good surface finish are the prime objectives expected from the part performance in automobiles. The mechanical properties as desired by the application are fundamental prospects controlling the performance and failure of a part. Stainless steel in different grades are widely used to manufacture different parts used in various industries such as dies and mold, automobile, and medical implants etc. 316L is one of the commonly used steel grade in automobile parts such as crank shafts, couplings, and piston etc. Although, steels can be processed by forging, casting and machining but in order to achieve the end-use part requires multiple processes and/or operations of a single process to achieve desired part characteristics. Layered manufacturing is one of the latest technologies for producing near net shape metal parts. The advantages of this technology are many which includes ability to produce: highly dense solid parts, near-net shape parts with little or no post-processing, parts with materials difficult to machine or forge. Selective laser melting (SLM), one of the layered manufacturing technologies, has successful application to deliver 3D part in one step. SLM) has a broad application prospects in molds and dies [1], automobiles, aviation [2], [3], aerospace [4], medical implants, and special material processing [5]. SLM is assumed to be highly suitable to manufacture wide range of 3D metallic parts ranging from small-scale to large-scale parts.

data.projectName: Metabolic and Reproductive Response To Stress In Off Springs Of Parents Exposed To Stress In Chronic Stress Rat Model
data.projectDigest: Humans are exposed to a lot of stress in daily life. Stress during career building years which are also child bearing years can affect the offspring.3 Is there any difference in response to stress in offspring of stressed vs non stressed parents? Finding out the transgenerational effect of stress in humans require many years so this study was devised to be carried out on rats; as they get mature and develop reproductive capability much earlier than humans. 4 We will take two groups of rats in the parent generation and give stressors to one group (cases) and no stress to the other group (controls). After stress phase we will allow them to breed. Offspring of both groups will be given stressors; early life, late life and some in both early and late life. Stress in parent generation and/or early life may have deleterious effects on metabolic and reproductive responses in the offspring’s. In contrast one form, or timing of stress may make the organism adapt and become resistant to stress; proposing a beneficial effect. We will compare the metabolic and reproductive responses in the control versus cases groups. This will guide about the effects of stress and their management strategies.

data.projectName: Quorum Sensing of Microbial Community as a Versatile Tool for Rhizospheric Competence: A Step to Increase the Consistency of Bioinoculants
data.projectDigest: Agriculture has major share in Pakistan’s economy. The intensive farming has resulted depletion of nutrients. This nutrient deficiency is replenished by adding chemical and biofertilizers. Although biofertilizers has gained the popularity due to natural, economic  and environment friendly nature yet its in consistent performance is a question mark for its success. As biofertilizers being living organisms could not perform well in all agricultural zones due to decreased survival efficiencies in the new environment. As per recent feedback of agro industry (FFC); performance of plant growth promoting bacteria fortified fertilizer (PGPB FF) is limited and inconsistent in different field conditions. To resolve this issue, in present study FFC recommended field soil will be analysed for its physico chemical properties and microbial diversity. Microbial culturable community analysis of targeted soil will be done to understand the specie abundance. Culturable strains, ingredients of PGPB FF and other potent PGPR strains will be analysed for their quorum sense signalling. Current research is proposed to strengthen the microbial industry in Pakistan by developing  prerequisite criteria for PGPB FF application in the field. Bioinoculum or Biofertilizer will be recommended on the basis of  soil microbial community and their quorum sense signalling.

data.projectName: MXene 2D-Layered Materials: Developing the Next Generation Energy Storage/Conversion Devices
data.projectDigest: In recent years, lithium-ion batteries have emerged as the best technology for electric vehicles and many electronic gadgets. The increased energy demand has increased the serious environmental concerns and fear of limited supplies of lithium. These have driven the development of green chemistries and finding the most appealing alternatives. In this regards: (i) lithum ion batteries (LIB) have been modified by using carbon and graphene-based electrodes to increase the efficiency with lowering the Lithium consumption, (ii) replacement of lithium (Li) by sodium (Na) is the most tempting alternative, however, has presumed concerns and  (iii) MXenes are the newly discovered family of two-dimensional (2D) materials by Prof. Yury Gogotsi & Prof. Barsoum’s group, which is found favorable for development of next generation of batteries and supercapacitors. Talking about the option (i) and (ii), i.e., modification and replacement of lithium has increased the efficiency somehow, but they are also facing limitations and environmental issues, which needed to be addressed. While MXenes consists of transition metal carbides, carbonitrides and nitrides found applications in many fields like lithium-ion & sodium-ion energy storage systems, supercapacitors, antennas, electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding and water purification. MXenes found their fame due to their good flexibility, easy processing, highest EMI shielding effect, antibacterial effect and high conductivity with a minimal thickness among all the other synthetic materials. Thus, to contribute to the development of a new generation of technology, we want to focus on MXenes materials for measurement of energy storage and conversion applications.

data.projectName: An Association between green energy and hotel industry
data.projectDigest: Tourism and traveling industry are the most popular industries of the world, this leads to improve employment, up-lift exports and made the world’s economies prosperous. The total contribution of these industries was $ 22,286.3 million which was 7.4% of the total GDP of Pakistan in 2017 while the 5.8% contribution to GDP were forecast at 2018 and up-to $39,851.6 million as 7.4% of the total GDP at 2028 World Travel and Tourism Council [WTTC (2019)].The main aim of this research is to evaluate various factors affecting decision-making regarding sustainable energy initiatives, in the hotel industry in Pakistan. Different objectives are To review the business case for green energy initiatives for the hotel industry. To evaluate challenges to adoption of green energy initiatives in the hotel industry. To examine factors affecting decision-making about commitment level of hotels regarding green initiatives. The research follows qualitative as well as quantitative methods. The qualitative approach includes review of literature and analyzing relevant published material. Understanding will be developed from different websites of environmental protection and energy. A self-administered questionnaire will be developed for hotel owner’s department supervisors and managers of different categories hotels in Kaghan/Naran in Pakistan.

data.projectName: PPERFORMANCE VERIFICATION OF UV-VISIBLE LIGHT DRIVEN PHOTOCATALYST OF METAL OXIDES/MAGNETIZED GRAPHENE/METAL ORGANIC FRAMEWORK FOR ENHANCED WATER PURIFICATION
data.projectDigest:
This research project is aimed at photodegrading the organic pollutants in the presence of Uv-visible sunlight by composite of metal oxides, magnetized graphene and metal organic frame work (MOFs). The organic pollutants will cover a broad range of pesticides, drugs and dyes which are regularly added to the environmental water bodies by various industries (pharmaceutical, dye and food) and farming practices on larger scale. The composite synthesized will be durable and reusable, cost effective and environmental friendly. The Uv-visible light driven composites of MOFs will be synthesized, characterized and then applied for the said purpose.
It is hypothesized that the photocatalytic property of these MOFs composites will be superb with excellent stability by having the properties of a narrow gap conduction band, excellent hole generation ability, greater surface area, low resistance to mass transfer of electrons enhanced by the nanoparticles of magnetized graphene. This will ultimately proliferate the outflow probability of electrons of the MOFs composite and will also enhance the contact of holes with MOFs composite. The use to UV-visible light will enhance the importance of the composite and will make the complete process of photodegradation easy, cheap and applicable to the organic water pollutants on larger scale.

data.projectName: Mathematical Study of some Topological Indices with application in Chemistry
data.projectDigest: A Topological descriptor is a numerical number associated to a molecular graph. It is well known that the topological descriptors are invariant under graph isomorphism. These molecular descriptors determine many physical, chemical or biological properties such as molecular volume, electron population, energy volumes, etc. of the underlying molecular structures. A large number of topological descriptors have been defined through the year and they are very well correlated with many physical or chemical properties of the molecule. Among these Topological descriptors Mostar Index, Lanzhou Index and modified first Zagreb connection index are the recently defined indices. Is has been observed that these indices outperform in predicting certain physiochemical properties of the molecules. The Mostar index of a molecular graph calculates the measure of its perpherality. In a molecule the peripheral atoms, groups and bonds mostly determines their physical and chemical properties.  It has been observed that the Lanzhou Index performs well in predicting the logarithm of octanol water partition coefficient of nonane isomers. Also, Modified Zagreb connection index is well correlated with the two of the molecular properties namely entropy and acentric factor. Therefore it is important to explore the mathematical properties of these topological descriptors. In this project we will focus on the study of some of the mathematical properties if these indices.

data.projectName: Physicochemical Characterization & Bioactivities of Polysaccharides from Fruits and Crop Wastes
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is an agricultural country, but its agricultural sector fails to achieve its true potential. There are many reasons to account for this eventuality, but this study advocates minimizing wastes from agricultural products as a means for increasing farmer’s income as well as for mitigating the environmental hazard associated with such wastes. Some local fruits and a cash crop, widely used in local food industry and consumed in households, have been selected. The proposed study, in essence, is based on the hypothesis that wastes from the selected fruits/crop are potential, hitherto untapped, source of bioactive polysaccharides. Polysaccharides are continuously gaining interest from the scientific community for their wide-ranging biological activities. The hypothesis of the proposed study is justified by the presence of reported bioactive polysaccharides in the selected fruits/crop. The study, henceforth, has the potential to achieve its objectives with regards to extraction, physicochemical characterization and antioxidant and hypoglycemic potential evaluation of polysaccharides. The study includes a number of established techniques for characterization of polysaccharides. This focus of interest is based on the fact that structure of a compound dictates its biological activity. Therefore, more knowledge about the structure will ultimately help better understand the basis underlying the bioactivities of the extracted polysaccharides. Antioxidants are in demand by pharmaceutical and cosmeceutical industries. Moreover, novel alternative antidiabetic drugs are also becoming more and more important because of the increase in the occurrence of this devastating disease.

data.projectDigest: Microcavity exciton-polaritons are half-light, half-matter quantum quasi-bosonic particles, resulting from the strong light-matter coupling in a combined structure of quantum wells and cavity photons.  In 2006 a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) of these particles was observed. The attribute of the exciton-polariton system is that number of identical experiments that can be performed in atomic physics can be done in the semiconductor system. From a quantum information technology point of view, the semiconductor exciton-polariton BEC system has numerous practical advantages over the atomic systems. The temperatures that are normally used to form exciton-polariton BECs are in the vicinity of T=10K, far higher than the nanokelvin temperatures required for atomic BECs. By using various semiconductors it should be achievable to increase these temperatures to room temperatures, opening the expectation for brand-new devices that use the BEC phenomenon. BECs are auspicious in terms of brand-new quantum technologies since quantum effects can happen on a macroscopic level, unlike many systems where quantum effects are quite easily destroyed by temperature and decoherence. Since a random disorder is naturally present in the semiconductor structures, the study of exciton-polariton condensates in random disordered potentials is even more crucial than in Bose-Einstein condensates of cold atoms. For this work, the principal investigator has in mind to build advanced dynamical simulation techniques in C programing language and compare the corresponding numerical results with analytical results. The precise knowledge of the underlying exciton-polariton condensates in random disordered potentials will be essential to exposit and predict many interesting effects, for instance, disorder-drive

data.projectName: Evaluation of Bacoside(s) (Bacoside-A3, Bacoside II and Bacoside C) as Potential anti-emetic candidates against cisplatin induced vomiting in vomit model(s); Neurochemical Evidences
data.projectDigest:
Nausea and vomiting induced by cancer chemotherapeutic agents are the distressing side effects, which ultimately result in non-compliance and even refusal of curative treatment in patients undergoing cancer chemotherapy. Anti-emetics are used to control the nausea and vomiting induced by such type of chemotherapy. Even by following the standard guidelines for the use of anti-emetics; nausea and vomiting is still a challenge clinically. The recent developments have added remission of the emetogenesis of cancer chemotherapy but still there is no complete control and the patients still vomit and the nausea most poorly controlled.
Keeping in view the importance of this clinical challenge, current study is designed to explore some new anti-emetic from natural sources indigenous to Pakistan for the better control of nausea and vomiting induced by cancer chemotherapy pre-clinically in vomit models.
