data.projectName: Development of phage-therapy for the treatment of chicken enteritis: an alternative therapy to minimize drug abuse and overcome emergence of antibiotic resistance
data.projectDigest:
Describe the proposed research geared to the non-specialist reader(max 200 words)
Broiler chicken is a main and cheap source of meat for Pakistani people. To cope with the demand, huge antibiotics are used during poultry production in order to prevent and treat different bacterial diseases and secure fast growth.  This trend speeds up the development of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) concomitantly making chicken as reservoir of multidrug resistance (MDR). More worrisome is the usage of human-life saving and clinically crucial drugs which also retain in the meat. We, therefore, suggest investigating alternate effective- and contemporary methods of treatment and prevention such as application of bacteriophage. Viral Phages (bacteriophages) are natural killer of bacteria, and are safe, specific and has not been associated with other environmental risks. With the current emergence of high level of AMR, more research has been focused on replacing antibiotics with phages. This recent inclination towards phage research resulted in a number of phage products, which are routinely use in many parts of the world. We therefore propose to find found out phages that could potentially kill enteritis-causing bacteria and could thus replace/minimise the use of antibiotics.

data.projectName: Design and synthesis of  PPAR?/? agonists for the management of Diabetes and related neurodegeneration
data.projectDigest: According to WHO reports, approximately 370 million people will suffer from Diabetes by 2030 (Wild et al., 2004). With this increasing number of diabetic people, the risk of neurodegenerative diseases is highly increased with a crucial effect on overall social and economic burden for developing countries like Pakistan. According to statistical data,Pakistan has been ranked sixth worldwide in 2000, where the diabetic prevalence was 5.2 million in 2000 and is expected to be raised to 13.9 in 2030. Recently research has established the link between Diabetes Mellitus and neurodegeneration especially Alzheimer disease, that share common pathological pathways. Keeping this in mind it is desired to discover new drugs which act on common targets involved in the progression of DM and AD. This will ultimately manage diabetes along with neuroprotection, thereby reducing social as well as economic burden for developing countries.

data.projectName: VALUE CHAINS OF CITRUS IN PUNJAB AND THEIR ROLE IN POVERTY ALLEVIATION
data.projectDigest: Value chain analysis is a tool that we use to define development opportunity, looking at each distinct step in the life of a product, the actors at each step, how value is added, and how much they earn for that value created (Piper, 2007). A “value chain” denotes all the actions involved in making a product and delivering it to retail and the consumer. It is a supply chain consisting of the input suppliers, producers, processors and buyers that bring a product from its conception to its end use. It seeks to address the major constraints at each level of the supply chain, rather than focusing on just one group or on one geographical location (Dempsey and Campbell, 2007). The potential beneficiaries of the study will be the market intermediaries; such as producer, pre-harvest contractors, wholesalers, retailers, consumers and factory owners etc. It will, in turn, help to reduce their deprivations by increasing their incomes.

data.projectName: Autonomous Six Degree of Freedom Machining Bed
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest:
The material removal techniques used now a days provide very high spindle speed. The tools at high speed are vulnerable to external and internal vibrations. As a result of these vibrations, the cuts produced on the surface of the work-piece can be inaccurate and with less precision. This research proposes a solution to this problem by giving the work-piece six degree of freedom (DoF) i.e. providing the work-piece three rotational and three translational motions. For this purpose, an autonomous machining bed having a parallel mechanism is proposed to give the workpiece six degrees of freedom.
 To achieve the aim, a control strategy will be designed and verified with detailed modeling, analysis, and verification of the system. A physical machining bed will be fabricated with the addition of sensors, actuators and controllers to validate/implement the control algorithm. Accuracy evaluation for various machining processes is also one of the key objectives of this project. This machining bed will be fully computer-controlled.

data.projectName: Neonatal Assessment System for Newborn Babies using Deep Learning and Image Analysis to predict Medical Abnormalities and Future  Mortality Rate
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
The purpose of this research is to develop an AI based model of neonatal assessment system by using sophisticated machine learning and deep learning algorithms, and (Open CV) computer vision tools, along with pulse oximeter output waveforms and further real time essential parameters like weight, skin color of newborn, reflexes of body parts through general purpose camera and patient monitor which is going to be used by physicians to predict abnormalities in newborn babies even from remote areas in order to reduce the mortality and morbidity rates of neonates( Al-Naji, A.; Gibson, K.; Lee, S.-H.; Chahl, J. , 2017) in Pakistan. 
This project falls in the area of AI(artificial intelligence), OpenCV (Open Source Computer Vision), machine-learning (ML) and deep learning (DL). For collecting images, three movable and adjustable cameras will be placed on the patient bed. One will be placed on the top of the patient bed while the other two will be placed opposite to each other.  These cameras will capture the required images from different angles and directions and then  these images will  be sent to the computer for image processing. The data which will be collected from pulse oximeter and BMI (body mass index) along with the data collected from preprocessed images will be trained and tested by using ML (machine learning and DP (deep learning) algorithms.

data.projectName: application of stem cells in the treatment of spinal cord injury of canines
data.projectDigest: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is associated with high morbidity and mortality. It severely deteriorates the quality of life of patients. Mostly the therapeutic interventions are nonresponsive and the disease mostly culminate in to permanent disability or death of patient. The SCI can be divided in to primary SCI which causes mechanical damage to the neurons and blood vessels. It leads to secondary SCI which activates multiple pathological pathways such as vascular disruption, ischemia, excitotoxicity, oxidation, inflammation and apoptotic cell death. Therefore, it is crucial to control inflammation and oxidation injury to minimize the nerve cell death during secondary SCI. Therapeutic strategies till adopted are 1) Reducing neuro-inflammation with immunosuppressive drugs 2) Reducing free Radical damage with Glucocorticoids etc., 3) Reducing Excitotoxic Damage, 4) Cytotherapy: transplantation of stem cells, shwan sells, astrocytes etc. Stem cell therapy has been widely focused in SCI treatment, because of its dual function of providing mechanical support at the injured site through neural differentiation and by providing paracrine support in-terms of producing antioxidants, anti-inflammatory cytokines and growth factors. Both wild type of stem cells, neural induced stem cells and transgenic stem cells have been used with improved clinical outcomes in dogs, rabbits and rats etc. with SCI. Stem cells have been manipulated in vitro to improve their biological characteristics. It has been found that heat shock treatment improves the immunosuppressive capability, viability, proliferation and anti-oxidative functions of stem cells. There is no data available which delineate the function of stem cell sheet therefore it will be used to assess healing of spinal cord injury.

data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:

This intensive system of food production faces many challenges where “food safety” has emerged as a critical concern. Infectious micro-organisms which are transmissible from farm animals to human beings, render otherwise valuable food stuff unsafe to consume. Campylobacter infections are generally mild, but can be fatal among very young children, elderly, and immunosuppressed individuals.
Campylobacter spp., particularly C. jejuni and C. coli, are a major cause of enteritis in humans. Many animals carry Campylobacter spp. asymptomatically and shed the organism in their feces. Poultry, particularly broiler chickens, are an especially important source of the bacterium, though they usually do not become ill. Consumption of contaminated poultry meat is a lead cause of food born Campylobacteriosis in human beings. data.projectName: Polymer Based Ionic Liquid Membranes for Efficient CO2 Separation
data.projectDigest:
The use of membranes for gas separation is considered to be one of the promising approaches due to several advantages that involves low capital cost,  low energy utilization and environmental friendly. CO2 separation from flue gases involving various energy sources such as post combustion from  major power plants is efficiently addressed by using membranes.  However, various factors are associated for improving membrane performance through permeability and selectivity. 
The use of polymeric ionic liquids considered in this proposal, are one of the emerging class of ion-conducting polymers with excellent conductivities, thermal stability, chemical stability and are robust in nature. They provide significant importance as they are bind cations or anions to polymer backbone and thus minimizing the leakage of charged species into contiguous materials. Furthermore, the use of PILs with high performance polymers will facilitate membranes to operate at elevated temperatures due to absence of water contents in contrast to commercially available ion conducting membranes.  It is expected that the membranes involving crosslinking agents with design modification of materials and efficient methodologies will progress to achieve high tradeoff between CO2 permeability and selectivity for further workable commercialization.

data.projectName: The influence of Zinc loaded China Clay (ZnCC) in limiting soil arsenic uptake by wheat (Triticum aestivum L.)
data.piUniversity: Government College for Women University, Sialkot
data.projectDigest: This project is designed to have direct impact on economy and people’s health. Wheat is very important food crop cultivated in Sialkot district. However, its production is limited by the adverse effects of either application of industrial waste water or cultivation on contaminated lands. Arsenic (As) heavy metal is a big concern here because it is used as preservative in leather processing units and it ends up in fresh water streams through tanneries waste disposals. We have been working on interactions between plants and contaminated soil systems for a long time. Thus, we proposed this study to reduce the uptake of As by wheat plants by the use of some soil amendments. The basic components of soil amendment will be China Clay and Zn-oxide. The Zn-oxide has great ability to quench As from aqueous solution and China Clay provides a greater surface area for the adsorption of As ions bound to oxides of Zn. Unlike other toxic heavy metals like Cd, Pb, Cr etc, As does not have affinity for organic materials in the soil as previous researches have used the organic soil amendments to get rid of As from the soil solution. Hence, our inorganic amendment, Zn loaded China Clay (ZnCC) is perfectly designed to restrict the absorption of As into the wheat plants. It is absolutely non-toxic as Zn is also a mineral nutrient and will work for the proper growth of plants when it will be used in controlled and appropriate amounts. So, with this background, we will perform a pot experiment in GC Women University Sialkot. Different dozes of the ZnCC in various combinations will be applied in As contaminated soil on two varieties of wheat. The experiment will be performed twice to have a comprehensive understanding of the impact ZnCC will have on wheat varieties.

data.projectName: Development of optimized and sustainable textile manufacturing process for Pakistani Better Cotton and organic cotton
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is the fourth largest producer of cotton in the world, and importantly also holds the third largest spinning capacity in Asia. Textile industry is the backbone of Pakistan economy. It contributes 9.5% to the GDP of the country and employs 45% of the total labor of the country. Due to global policy on sustainable and environment friendly manufacturing there is a strong demand from foreign textile customers and top brands to adopt sustainable cotton like Better cotton and organic cotton to minimize the effects of environmental pollution due to cotton production and textile manufacturing processes. Pakistani farmers are already growing organic cotton and better cotton but unfortunately, these raw materials are at adoption phase in the industry and due to lack of technical know-how and research and development there exists no sustainable and optimized textile manufacturing processes from these cottons. The main aim of this project is to develop sustainable textile manufacturing processes e.g. from yarn to finished fabric to help industry easily adopt these highly sought textile materials. Adoption of these sustainable cottons in comparison to the conventional cotton will also help the industry to contribute towards cleaner and greener Pakistan and attract a large number of foreign customers that will ultimately lead to inflow of billions of dollars to the country economy and employment opportunities for the fellow countrymen.

data.projectName: Development of plant growth promoting microbial amendment for mitigating negative impact of brackish water on maize growth
data.projectDigest: Owing to shortage of canal water, poor quality underground water is being used for crop production that is causing negative impact on plant growth. Such water also results in development of salt-affected soils. Chemical amendments like gypsum and sulfuric acid are used to mitigate negative impact of brackish water however; these amendments are not providing sustainable results due to certain draw backs. To overcome this problem, the application of bacteria with gypsum or sulfur could be an emerging approach. A number of bacterial strains will be isolated and tested for their potential to solubilize calcium carbonate, gypsum and to xidize sulfur. Efficient strains will be checked for their compatibility. The compatible strains will be used in various combinations in presence of gypsum and sulfur to mitigate the negative impact of brackish water under controlled conditions by using maize as a test crop. Formulation of microbial amendment will be done. Column study will be conducted to evaluate the impact on soil properties. Further evaluation will be done by conducting pot trial. The data regarding physiological, growth and yield parameters of maize will be determined. The interaction of Na with micro and macronutrients in the presence of microbial amendment will be analysed.

data.projectName: Super magnetic nanocrystalline ferrites thin films for storage devices
data.projectDigest:
For advanced energy storage applications, manufacturing of nanocrystalline super magnetic
thin films through experimental research is required.
International industry requires quality nanocrystalline super magnetic thin films (NC-SMTF) and
Pakistan needs industry to have healthy technology. The study of nanocrystalline super
magnetic thin films and their applications is undergoing a concentrated research effort.  The
situation is intensified in Pakistan where even the cost of the conventional method is out of
reach of the most companies. The need for a fast and low-cost method is obvious and
pressing.
In the search for new NC-SMTF compositions, the focus on the recording high density in
nanocrystalline ferrites magnetic thin films utilized for storage devices to ameliorate the
technology in Pakistan. The aim of this project is the fabrication of nanocrystalline magnetic
thin films at low cost for storage devices. NC-SMTF are easy to analyze, therefore can be used in
a wide range of energy storage devices.

data.projectName: Design and Fabrication of a Low Cost, Multifunctional Infant Incubator using Thermo-electric coolers
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Pre-mature births of infants is one of the major problems of Pakistan especially in the rural areas of the country which needs to be addressed as early as possible. Facts and studies show that the lack of Infants Incubators in the rural health facilities is the issue which is causing deaths of infants. Infant Incubators are the need of an hour for our country to decrease the mortality rate of infants. 
There are no locally manufactured incubators available in the market and due to which Pakistan has to import incubators from the China and other countries. The cost of imported incubators is way much higher and thus incubators are not affordable.
For this purpose, there is a need of a portable, locally manufactured, low cost, multifunctional infant incubator to be made which should serve in various health centers across the country.
An infant incubator will be designed and fabricated which will be low cost and having the necessary features like temperature control, humidity control and oxygen supply provision. A micro-controller will be designed to regulate temperature and humidity levels and will also have a LED display of current temperature and humidity levels.

data.projectName: synthesis of Pyrene based materails and their potential applications
data.piUniversity: Kohat University of Science and Technology, Kohat
data.projectDigest:
Nowadays, energy demand is increasing exponentially. Many energy storage devices, including capacitors, fuel cells, lithium ion batteries have been discoved to meet the rising demands. Supercapacitors (SCs) have gained tremendous attentions because of their distinguishing characteristics, such as high power density, fast charge/discharge rate, and good safety. The energy density of SCs can be enhanced by increasing specific capacitance or potential. This can be accomplished by chosing an electrode with high specific capacitance and with electrolytes having broad potential. Recently, two-dimensional Covalent Organic Frame works (2D COFs), have drawn increasing attention due to their high surface area, extended ? conjugated structure. A well-defined pore structure facilitates the electron/ion transport, electrolyte diffusion and the adjustable functionality enables to tune the capacitive character. However, low electrochemical stability still remains hurdle in their poor rate performance.
Herein, we plan to prepare electrochemically stable pyrene based 2D COF that would facilitate the electron transport in SCs. Pyrene based COFs have a highly crystalline structure, well-defined pores and outstanding electrochemical stability, which is responsible for delivering extraordinary capacitance in a wide potential range, giving the excellent energy density. Most importantly, Pyrene based COFs showed excellent cycling stability after numerous charge-discharge cycles.

data.projectName: Formulation development of new antitubercular analogues of ciprofloxacin: their Physicochemical and Pharmacokinetics study
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
The purpose of this study is to prepare a medicine from few new antitubercular compounds that will be helpful for the treatment of Tuberculosis in patients particularly who have become resistant to conventional therapy. These compounds are synthesized at Pharmaceutical Chemistry Lab of Dow College of Pharmacy from the parent compound of Ciprofloxacin (fluoroquinolones) and will used for the development of dosage form like tablet or capsule.
Anti-TB activity of these compounds on the microorganism of TB known as Mycobacterium tuberculosis has already been done in our previous project funded by HEC. Also the Acute and subacute toxicity studies have been performed of synthesized compounds in different doses on animal models of rats and mice in the same project.
In this project, the re-synthesis of same compounds will be performed and their structural elucidation will be done by Spectroscopic methods like FT-IR, Mass spectrophotometer and NMR. While the physical properties and stability will be checked in the instrument known as stability chamber present at our Pharmaceutics lab of Dow College of Pharmacy. In this lab Dosage form design will also be performed. Here also the physical and chemical tests of prepare tablets/ capsules like their disintegration and dissolution rates and their stability will also be checked by the help of different instruments.
Pharmacokinetics means Absorption of designed dosage form of drug/ compound in blood, its Distribution in Body tissues, its Metabolism by liver and its Excretion by kidneys will be checked on animal models. Instruments like High Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC) and Spectrophotometer (UV- Visible) will used for this purpose. 
The toxic effects and drug interactions will also be evaluated of designed dosage form.

data.projectName: “Development of Antimicrobial and Biomimetic Composites Coating on metallic implants for Orthopedic Applications
data.projectDigest: Biomaterial implants require biocompatible surfaces in order to minimize potential immune system reactions and to promote implant integration with the host tissue. In this project, I am developing a robust process to create uniform antimicrobial and biomimetic Composites coatings on orthopedic implants using electrophoretic technique. In details, biomimetic ceramics  containing various amounts of the antimicrobial agent  will be synthesized using low cost and time consuming microwave method. Then coating, will be prepared by depositing optimized composition of bioactive ceramics and polymers (PCL PLAA and PLGA) layers on the surface of the metallic implant using electrophoretic technique. The process parameters such as time, temperature, conductivity, size of particles, voltage, etc. will be optimized to get homogeneous crack free surface coatings. Our team is experienced in the. Basic physicochemical characterization of these coatings along with cytocompatibility and antimicrobial assessments.

data.projectName: Molecular Characterization of Gram Negative Clinical Isolates from In-Patients admitted in Medical Wards of Dow University Hospital of Karachi, Pakistan: A Prospective Study
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Infections involving gram negative bacteria including Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Acinetobacter baumannii, etc is a global issue. During the last two decades, changes in health care, infection-control practices, and antimicrobial use and resistance may have influenced the incidence of gram-negative organisms’ infections.  Gram negative bacilli genetic variability results in attaining virulence factors and antibiotic resistance genes. This attainment augments bacterial capacity to live in the host environment and to acclimate to it. An increasing prevalence of ?-lactamase resistance due to extended spectrum beta lactamases ESBL, the presence of allied antibiotic resistance in gram negative bacilli is also a serious global clinical problem. 

In Pakistan, virulence attributes and antibiotic susceptibility profile of different gram negative bacilli strains does not fully discovered. This study will provide data from Pakistan related to virulence attributes and resistance profile of different gram negative bacilli strains involved in infections. Therefore, the aims of this study will include determination of the virulence patterns and the pathotype on a collection of gram negative bacilli strains recovered from In-patients of Dow University Hospital which will generate data regarding antibiotic resistance available for physicians to select better antibiotic therapy for their patients.

data.projectName: 3D Multilayer Lung on a chip and emulator for pathological modelling of smog based chronic diseases of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The proposed research goal is the design and fabrication of lung on a chip using a new reconfigurable 3D multi-layer chip concept. An emulator is also proposed to mimic the SMOG environment. The chronic lung diseases caused by SMOG will be pathologically modeled. To achieve this goal, an inter-disciplinary research will be performed by the team from two academic collaborators (AIR University and Fazaia Medical College) and two sectoral collaborators (Pakistan AIR Force Hospital and Analytical Measurement Systems). The proposed lung on chip design will use nanofiber membrane for better cell adhesion to facilitate tissue like co-culture. It is also possible to simulate lung respiratory movement from epithelial to endothelial cells, which is not achieved previously. All the cells will be tissue specific primary cells rather than general cell lines. True organ anatomy will be mimicked by establishing vascular connection between endothelial & epithelial tissues through ECM for nutrient exchange. Integrated camera sensor will be used for real-time monitoring of physical and biological markers. The final Lung on chip device and emulator will be patented with DRAP certification. The developed system can have a huge impact on Pakistan’s pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries in terms of drug testing and diagnosis.

data.projectName: Agricultural and Environmental implication due to soil salinity by Right Bank Outfall Drain, causing socio-economic deprivation in Sindh
data.projectDigest:
The Right Bank Out fall Drain (RBOD) is a project of WAPDA starts from the 2009 and still it is not completed. The Project is flowing at the right bank of River Indus crossing Kamber Shahdadkot, Dadu and Jamshoro districts of Sindh Province.  Social and Economic degradation of the RBOD in the area are frequently observed since the ten years, aim of this project was to drain out the effluent water of Balochistan and Sindh in the Arabian Sea at the Gharo. The project has three segments like RBOD-I, RBOD-II and RBOD-III. Total length of the Project is 273 Km. It is designed for 3500 cusec influent water. 
Three main Natural Lakes (Hamal Lake Kamber-Shahdadkot, Manchar Lake Dadu and Saroh Lake Kamber Shahdadkot) of the Research area are located at left bank of the project. The RBOD is entered into Manchar Lake near the Sehwan City, where the water of this drain canal (RBOD) changed the Physical and chemical properties of water of Manchhar Lake. Expect this, due to seepage of the project Chemical properties of the Soil are also changed, it is observed that pH, TDS and E.C of soil at both banks of RBOD has been changed.

data.projectName: Hepatic Differentiation of Human Amniotic Epithelial Cells on  Decellularized Extracellular Matrix  based 3D Hydrogel for Liver Tissue Engineering
data.projectDigest: Liver diseases are affecting millions of people worldwide. Orthotropic liver transplantation is the only current treatment option available for end stage liver disease. However, lack of suitable organ donors and life-long immune suppression are hurdle in the treatment of end stage liver disease. Transplantation of hepatocytes may offer an alternative to liver transplantation. However, this approach still suffers from practical limitations, primarily due to the difficulty of producing enough functional hepatocytes for therapeutic efficacy. Finding the best cell type with unlimited potential, easy access, minimal ethical issues, non-tumorigenic and immunomodulatory properties is desperately required for differentiation into hepatocyte. Moreover, there is also a dire need of a cost effective and efficient method that can counteract the disadvantages of cellular transplantation associated with the 2D culture. Tissue engineering approaches offers superior alternative to these limitations with 3D culture, to better mimic the in vivo microenvironment. Therefore, this study has been designed to investigate the potential of a new abundant, non-controversial, and safe source of stem cells i.e Amniotic epithelial cells for the differentiation of hepatocytes on deceullarized ECM hydrogel (3D culture) to obtain abundant quantity of functional hepatocytes and to analyze their therapeutic effect after transplantation in liver diseased model.

One of the most important and widely consumed functional foods is probiotics containing diets. Probiotics are live microorganism (bacteria and yeast) when administered confer health benefit. Among the probiotics, Lactobacilli species are widely consumed in Pakistan and other south Asian regions. These probiotics have shown immuno-booster and protective actions in liver and intestinal injury. These organ systems are main tissue adversely affected by the anticancer drugs. The current project is aimed to evaluate the beneficial potential of these functional foods in amelioration of the adverse effects associated with use chemotherapeutic agents like methotrexate, cisplatin and etc.

data.projectName: Economizing fish culture employing unconventional ingredients based pretreated fermented aqua-feed
data.projectDigest: Fish growth is a plastic process that can change with quality of feed. Cost of feeding is contributed with about 70% of the total running expenses in fish farming. In recent decade, uncertain availability and high cost of traditional fish feed ingredients (e.g. fish meal) is the major challenge especially for developing countries. To replace traditional feed ingredients with unconventional feed ingredients (vegetable wastes, fruit peels wastes, bakery wastes etc) is one of alternative strategy to cope with this issue. Every year, huge amount of agro-industrial wastes are produced in Pakistan. Most of which are discarded as garbage. This leads to wasted resources and contributes to environmental pollution. Utilization of these resources not only benefited to reduce the cost of fish feed but also contribute to reduce environmental pollution. The major limitation factors of using unconventional feed ingredients comprise the occurrence of anti-nutritional factors (ANFs), deficiency of certain essential amino acids etc. Pretreatment techniques have been used to reduce ANFs. However, several of the ANFs are heat stable. The maximum reduction of ANFs can be achieved by employing the micro-organism(s) in Solid State Fermentation technology. In our lab, several bacteria have been preserved after isolation from different fish species. The present proposal is intended to formulate scientifically balanced yet economical unconventional ingredients based pretreated fermented feed with already isolated microbes for supporting maximum fish growth within reasonable short period of time with minimum cost. This project will open a new gateway for entrepreneurship for the progressive fish formers and fish feed industry.

To replace traditional feed ingredients with unconventional feed ingredients (vegetable wastes, fruit peels wastes, bakery wastes etc) is one of alternative strategy to cope with this issue. Every year, huge amount of agro-industrial wastes are produced in Pakistan. Most of which are discarded as garbage. This leads to wasted resources and contributes to environmental pollution. Utilization of these resources not only benefited to reduce the cost of fish feed but also contribute to reduce environmental pollution. The major limitation factors of using unconventional feed ingredients comprise the occurrence of anti-nutritional factors (ANFs), deficiency of certain essential amino acids etc. Pretreatment techniques have been used to reduce ANFs. However, several of the ANFs are heat stable. The maximum reduction of ANFs can be achieved by employing the micro-organism(s) in Solid State Fermentation technology. In our lab, several bacteria have been preserved after isolation from different fish species. The present proposal is intended to formulate scientifically balanced yet economical unconventional ingredients based pretreated fermented feed with already isolated microbes for supporting maximum fish growth within reasonable short period of time with minimum cost. This project will open a new gateway for entrepreneurship for the progressive fish formers and fish feed industry.

data.projectName: Development of human recombinant erythropoietin  Biosimilar
data.projectDigest:
Erythropoietin (Epo) has been used in patients with chronic renal failure and for treating anemia in cancer patients who develop chemotherapy-associated anemia. Over one million patients worldwide have responded effectively to either rhEpo or derivatives which have an enhanced plasma half-life approx. 22 hours.  Epo is also effective in AIDs patients with severe anemia as a result of antiviral therapy. In addition, Epo is used clinically for the treatment of the anemia of prematurity as well for surgical patients. Despite all the uses, many hindrances still stand in the way of rhEpo therapy, the most important of which is high cost of treatment. It is commercially available with a minimum price of 1150 rupees for 4000IU/0.4mL epoetin injection. 
The main objective of this project is develop erythropoietin biosimilar at CEMB. This novel protein would be available at an affordable price resulting in decrease of the death rates associated with kidney disorders and anemia. Moreover, this will be a patent technology of CEMB. By exporting this novel protein, we can increase the GDP of our country.

data.projectName: Influence of halophilic microbial biofilms developed from kallar grass (Leptochola Fusa) to mitigate saline/alkaline stress responses in rice
data.projectDigest:
Soil salinity is one of the many serious abiotic problems that cause significant damages to agricultural production, particularly in arid and semi-arid regions of the world. The problem of soil salinity has been found in many countries around the world and severity is expected to increase, particularly among agricultural countries. In Pakistan, soil salinity is a major agricultural constraint affecting more than 6.3 million ha of land, with an estimated 40 000 ha of land lost to salinity annually. The government of Pakistan has employed different engineering and biological reclamation measures for saline affected lands; however, the progress of the project was short-lived due to increased operational and maintenance costs and increased rate of salt deposition due to the use of groundwater. Therefore, there is a high demand for inexpensive and environmental friendly solutions to reclaim and manage these soils. 
Bioremediation strategy such as planting of halophytes (Phytoremediation) has been adopted for the reclamation of saline/alkaline soils in Pakistan. For example, plants such as the kallar grass or the salt grass (Leptochloa fusca) and the Old man saltbush (Atriplex nummularia Lindl.) are well-known halophytes that are being used to reclaim alkaline and saline lowlands. However, despite the significant benefits of phytoremediation, there still exist a few limitations. For example, the survival of plant seedlings at the initial growth stage could be a challenge; after plant establishment, it can take several seasons for the benefits to be evident. Moreover, most farm lands are owned  by low income earning farmers who cannot afford to leave the land uncultivated for the period of restoration. The use of halophilic microbes for the reclamation of saline/alkaline soils

data.projectName: ROLE OF HUMAN UMBILICAL CORD DERIVED STEM CELLS IN HEART REGENERATION: A PROTEOMIC APPROACH
data.projectDigest: Cardiac diseases are the leading cause of death worldwide. Myocardiac cells only show proliferation in neonatal period while in adolescence period the majority of cardiomyocytes exit cell cycle. Thus, the adult cardiomyocyte cells are not able to recover the entire lost tissue, therefore it is mandatory to find out crucial factors promoting cardiac regeneration. Transcription factors (TFs) have great potential to direct cell fate decision during embryo development. A number of studies have been conducted to investigate the role of cardiac TFs in cardiac differentiation processes. Until recently, understanding of the molecular mechanism of transcription machinery that directs myocardiac like cells formation from undifferentiated cells have been reported via gene expression studies. The knowledge about the role of proteins that involve in differentiation process is remains to be fully investigated. Therefore, it is crucial to expand our knowledge about cardiac differentiation on the protein level. A complete proteomic analysis could provide information regarding stem cells mediated heart regeneration. The aim of the present study is to investigate the cellular and molecular mechanisms involved in cardiac differentiation of stem cells using proteomics approach.  Here, we will generate a myocardial infarction (MI) rat model by ligation of the left descending coronary artery. The proteome, after transplanting differentiated stem cells in MI model, will be detected and analysed. This study will highlight the potential proteins that play a part in heart regeneration.  Thus, the results of this research will provide the in depth mechanism underlying the stem cells based cardiac regeneration. It may facilitate the future clinical applications for the treatment of heart failure.

data.projectName: Factors Responsible for Delayed Completion of Research Projects Funded by HEC
data.projectDigest: National Research Programs for Universities (NRPU) is an important initiative of HEC. It grants funds for research on competitive grounds for conducting scientific research that are having strategic relevance for uplifting local industry and the society (Higher-Education-Commission, 2013). In order to promote the basic and applied research in country financial support is being provided to the Principal Investigators (PIs) and Co- Principal Investigators (Co-PIs) for more than fifteen years; but unfortunately a sizeable number of research projects remained incomplete or was delayed due to certain reasons (Ullah et al., 2017). The proposed study aims at exploring the underlying causes of delay in NRPU research projects. PI and Co-PI will be taking all the concerned officials at both ends – HEC and University – on board to dig out the reasons for the delay in completing these research projects. After completion of the study ten seminars (Punjab-2, KP-2, Sindh-2, Baluchistan-1, AJK-1, Gilgit Baltistan-1 and ICT-1) will be conducted to disseminate the findings. The study will contribute to avoid delay which will help to fully harness the potential benefits of NRPU projects.

data.projectName: Fabrication of 2D Transition Metal Dichalcogenides (TMDs) Atomic Layers for Electronic, Magnetic and Energy Applications
data.projectDigest: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) are focus of intriguing research since last few decades owing to their unmatched physical and electrical properties. TMDs possess layer dependent novel tunable properties that were first observed in graphene, but the absence of band gap in graphene paved the way for TMDs.  It is possible to reduce the dimension of these materials to a monolayer limit of nearly atomic thickness having multiple crystal structures with unique electrical properties. Tunable, layer dependent band gap makes these TMDs vital materials for p-n junctions , high mobility field effect transistors , memory and switching devices  , optoelectronic , photovoltaic and energy applications. These materials are perceived to be the material of the future.  In this project, we plan to explore the amazing potential of TMDs for technological applications and fabricate different TMD materials to use them in electronic devices, magnetism and energy applications.

data.projectName: Near infrared irradiation induced photothermal therapy of breast cancer castled by guided iron oxide coated gold nanorods loaded with Dox
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: Cancer is the second leading cause of death globally, and is responsible for an estimated 9.6 million deaths in 2018. Globally, about 1 in 6 deaths is due to cancer.  In South Asia, unfortunately Pakistan is leading as mortality rate is 25.2/100,000. Therefore, it is urgent need to develop some diagnostic and therapeutic treatment methods to control over this serious disease. Recently, nanotechnology has provided promising platform in the development of science and technology especially in energy and medical areas. The aim of this study is to design very simple method to fabricate gold nanorods with different shapes and variable sizes. This will help to find out a potential shape to produce high temperature (40-50 oC) after absorbing electromagnetic radiation for killing of the tumor. To save the healthy tissues around the tumor, the AuNRs will be coated with iron oxide layer to be traced by magnetic resonance imaging technique. Furthermore, the coated AuNRs will transport thermally-activated medicine doxorubicin (Dox) to the cancer cells guided by folic acid acting as target agent. Finally, sufficient heat is provided to Dox by AuNPs/AuNRs, irradiated by near infrared source (5–50) Watt to kill tumor surgically and leaving the healthy cell undisturbed.

data.projectName: Aptamer guided-indocyanine green loaded chitosan magnetic nanoparticles for selective antileishmanial activity with near infrared radiations
data.projectDigest:
Leishmaniasis is the major vector born protozoal disease and is endemic to many tropical and subtropical counties like Pakistan according to World Health Organization. There are many clinical manifestations of these protozoa, including cutaneous, visceral and mucocutaneous leishmaniasis. Inadequate efficacy, drug toxicity, cost and prolonged treatment are the limitation of current medication against this disease. These factors are also increasing the parasitic resistance against current therapy. 
The consequence of this resistance gives new challenges to health care professionals to modify current treatment regimen and use of higher doses of existing drugs. Hence the novel anti-leishmanial strategies are the need of time. Nanotechnology gave a new alternative therapy which by it improving the bioavailability and reducing the toxicity of conventional drugs in nanosized. Along with this, other characteristics like also improved that help to relieve the burden of this disease. Another promising approach to combat this problem is the use of photodynamic therapy that produces reactive oxygen species that cause killing effect by destroying cell membrane and nucleic acids.
The present study is therefore aiming to fabricate more effective deep lesion penetrating low-level laser therapy with aptamer guided-indocyanine green loaded magnetic chitosan nanosized formulation for selective killing of leishmanial parasite. New formulation is aiming to selectively kill the protozoa in deep tissues with enhanced penetration of magnetic chitosan nanoparticles under the influence of magnetic field. It would ameliorate the targeted treatment options against leishmaniasis and will also help to gain knowledge about innovative drug formulations that can be implemented in further healthcare.

data.projectName: Production of Flexible and Light Weight Thin Films for development of Perovskite Solar Cell Applications
data.projectDigest:
Solar energy has become one of the most popular renewable energy sources because solar based energy can never reach to an end naturally and particularly exist as one of the cleanest energy sources. Nowadays, perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have become one of the most popular solar cells among all-solid-state solar cells. Due to large absorption coefficients, low exciton binding energy and long carrier diffusion lengths mixed organic–inorganic halide perovskites are considered as most favourable material for optoelectronics. Mainly flexible PSCs have wide range of applications in latest portable electronics, self-assisted airplanes and sun-oriented automobiles.
The most commonly utilised substrates for flexible PSCs are ITO coated polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and polyethylene naphthalate (PEN). These substrates can cause serious issues of pollution as they are not easily degradable. To overcome such kind of issues natural fibers-based papers are used as a flexible substrate to achieve portable electronics. For flexible PSCs paper substrate with homogenous surface are highly feasible due to novel properties e.g. appropriate mechanical strength, thermal and chemical stability, in particular, high transparency and low surface roughness.

data.projectName: SECURE COMMUNICATION WITH PRACTICAL QUANTUM KEY DISTRIBUTION
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
This project focuses on practical Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) technology, which is highly secure way of end-to-end communication. Conventionally, secret communication is done using complex mathematical algorithms which are believed to be secure based upon the assumption that it is not possible for anyone in the world to attain such a massive computational resources that could solve these algorithms in limited time. However, after the successful recent experiments of Quantum Computers by many renowned companies of the world including Google, IBM, D-Wave etc. it is generally believed by the research community that if a full fledged Quantum Computer will ever exist then it will be able to break the existing cryptographic algorithms in very limited time. 

In this project we first aim to model and simulate our own QKD system to facilitate highly secure communication. We will explore different QKD system designs and cryptographic algorithms to determine the most secure possible combination. Based on the obtained results we intend to develop a practical QKD system for highly secure communication. This indigenously designed and developed framework will be available to local research community and industry for further research and development of commercial QKD systems.

data.projectName: Efficient Resource Allocation for 5G enabled Intelligent Transportation Systems
data.projectDigest: Intelligent Transportation System (ITS) is a core component of future smart cities. With the help of wireless communication between vehicles and infrastructure units on the road, many applications such as vehicle safety, traffic management, autonomous driving and infotainment can be realized. 5G technology is the main enabler for future ITS. Recently, a new 5G standard known as Cellular Vehicle-to-everything (C-V2X) has been released to support ITS. C-V2X provides two different modes of transmission, cellular mode for traffic management and less urgent data traffic, and direct mode for safety and urgent data traffic. Resource allocation (frequency and time allocation for message transmission, transmission power to be used by the vehicles and which mode of transmission should be used for message transmission) is a key challenge in C-V2X as traditional resource allocation techniques does not work for the new modes of transmission. In this project, we will develop novel protocols for efficient resource allocation in C-V2X. This project will train several research students in this trending research domain and develop a research collaboration between COMSATS University Pakistan and Manchester Metropolitan University United Kingdom.

data.projectName: Comparison of Interventions for Reversibility of Polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOs)
data.projectDigest:
Poly cystic Ovarian Syndrome is a common problem in young females. It is increasing and some studies report it as high as 52% in South Asians. It presents as weight gain, mensural cycle irregularity, facial and body hair and acne. Many body systems are affected in polycystic ovary syndrome, resulting in several health complication like diabetes, stroke and uterine cancer . To date there is no standard treatment of this disease. The cause is genetic which is exacerbated through environmental factors.
 Our study is multicenter, in 4 medical universities.It will be focused on female medical students year 1-3 having PCOS clinical symptoms. Then the diagnosis will be confirmed  on the basis of clinical symptoms and hormonal tests and ultrasound. These students will be randomised in 2 groups. One group will get routine hormonal treatment and the other will have sessions on diet and exercise and diary plus smart phone application. Data will be collected every six months for clinical improvement in symptoms and blood tests will be repeated of both groups. Results will be compiled.
To our knowledge such study looking at a no cost, no side effect intervention has not been done before in young women.

data.projectName: Molecular characterization of Camelina sativa germplasm variability for yield and biodiesel production under saline condition
data.projectDigest:
Energy is important factor for any country progress and economic stability. Camelina sativa called gold of pleasure is one of the best economic renewable energy sources to cope energy crises issue in the world including Pakistan. Crop plants productivity is rigorously affected by salinity. In Pakistan, about 6.30 million hectare lands are salt affected, and these lands are almost uncultivated.   Developing countries including Pakistan are searching for land where biodiesel producing crops can be grown without scarifying major crop land. Camelina sativa  is one of the most important best crop plant, which has broad range of adaptability and can be easily grown under adverse weather  and  soils conditions like water logging, marshy areas, sea shores, marginal lands, as well as, it can be easily grown on salt effected soils. It provides one of the best raw materials for biodiesel production and edible oil, with very low inputs. Its oil resembled with ordinary petroleum oil of better quality and quantity. In Camelina sativa, AtPAP2 overexpression resulted in increased seed yield, seed size, growth rate, and earlier flowering.
Present research work is planned to evaluate available camelina sativa germplasm for adaptability, and variability for selection of high yielding, salt tolerant genotype. Likewise available germplasm will be evaluated for biodiesel production and good quality edible oil. Molecular characterization will be performed to investigate AtPAP2 overexpression in Camelina sativa germplasm and for salinity tolerance using salt tolerant gene primers.

Camelina sativa  is one of the most important best crop plant, which has broad range of adaptability and can be easily grown under adverse weather  and  soils conditions like water logging, marshy areas, sea shores, marginal lands, as well as, it can be easily grown on salt effected soils. It provides one of the best raw materials for biodiesel production and edible oil, with very low inputs. Its oil resembled with ordinary petroleum oil of better quality and quantity. In Camelina sativa, AtPAP2 overexpression resulted in increased seed yield, seed size, growth rate, and earlier flowering.
Present research work is planned to evaluate available camelina sativa germplasm for adaptability, and variability for selection of high yielding, salt tolerant genotype. Likewise available germplasm will be evaluated for biodiesel production and good quality edible oil. Molecular characterization will be performed to investigate AtPAP2 overexpression in Camelina sativa germplasm and for salinity tolerance using salt tolerant gene primers.

data.projectName: Combined effects of dietary Bacillus subtilis and Sodium butyrate on gut health and immune system in broiler chickens
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Modulation of the gut morphology and microarchitecture of the immune organs is assumed to improve health indicators and production performance in birds, but the intermediate structural changes, which result in improved performance in this case, are not adequately documented. This study, therefore, intends to fill this gap in information and document the combined effect of dietary inclusion of Bacillus subtilis (probiotic) and Sodium Butyrate (organic acid) on Anatomy and Physiology of the gut and immune system in commercial broiler chickens. In this study sampling will be made twice per trial. Parameters to be studied will include growth performance (weekly feed intake, weekly weight gain and FCR) and relative organ weights. Microscopic parameters will include villus height, width, absorptive surface area, crypts depth, villus height: crypt depth ratio, histochemical differentiation of goblet cells based on mucins nature and microarchitecture of immune tissues (thymus, spleen and bursa of Fabricius). Immune response evaluation will be performed using antibody titer against sheep RBCs and Delayed type hypersensitivity reaction to PHA-P. The study will help to evaluate the combined effects of B. subtilis and sodium butyrate as substitutes to synthetic antibiotics, and as growth promoters and immune modulators in commercial broiler chickens.

data.projectName: Bio-evaluation of immunotherapeutic potential of bovine colostrum based nutraceutical products
data.projectDigest: The infectious diseases are the major cause of morbidity and mortality among children under 5 years of age in developing countries. Among reasons behind the dilemma, the lack of immunity is the most causative agent. The lack of immunity develops due to poor nutrition (malnutrition), results in frequent episodes of infections ultimately forwarding towards further malnutrition. In this way a cycle between infections and malnutrition continues to prevail in society and from generation to generation. The need of the time is to develop such ready to use food product which are not only energy providers but also act as immune boosters for children. Among such immune boosters, bovine colostrum (first milk from cattle postpartum) is capturing the eyes of researchers and industries due to its efficiency to enhance immunity and provision of essential nutrients for growth and development. Therefore, the present study has been planned based on the hypothesis that enrichment of colostrum in baby foods may act as immune booster nutraceuticals in pediatrics nutrition and will help to prevent as well mange the episodes of infections in children leading towards better nutritional status.

data.projectDigest:
Spray drying is a convective drying technique used to transform a liquid feed in the form of a formulated solution emulsion suspension or slurry into a dry free flowing powder. Encapsulation assists sensitive and fragile materials to survive processing and packaging conditions and stabilize the shelf life of the active ingredient. Encapsulation is used to overcome all challenge by providing viable texture blending, appealing aroma releases. Another benefit of encapsulations is less evaporation and degradation of volatile actives, such as aroma, which usually contains mixture of volatile and odorous organic molecules.  Objectives:
•	Design  and of Fabrication of spray drying  machine
•	Tabulating and Encapsulation  
•	Performance evaluation and optimization of fabricated machine
•	Demonstration of the machine to stakeholders

data.projectName: Metabolomic and proteomic profiling of the patients with coronary heart diseases and heart failure
data.projectDigest: Heart diseases leading to heart failure are one of the dominant factors of morbidity and mortality in developed countries. The molecular causes of heart dysfunction are still unknown but it is likely to be the result of underlying alterations in gene and protein expression. However, the underlying molecular causes of cardiac dysfunction in most heart diseases are still largely unknown. Metabolomics and proteomics based studies can be used to identify clinically impactful novel biomarkers for the development of diseases, like coronary heart disease (CHD) . In this study, we will examine the plasma metabolomic and proteomic characteristics of CHD for the purpose of identifying potential biomarkers of changes to metabolomes and proteomes of CHD that may benefit the early detection of heart failure. The goal is to identify potential biomarkers for the differential diagnosis of CHD and insights into the underlying dysregulated biochemical pathways via their metabolomes and proteomes that are potentially involved in CHD pathogenesis.

data.projectName: Development of inocula for simultaneous plant growth promotion and herbicide remediation in direct seeded rice system
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest:
Sulfonylurea herbicides e.g., metsulfuron methyl, tribenuron methyl and bensulfuron methyl are extensively used for the post-emergent control of broadleaf weeds and grasses in wheat-rice cropping system. These herbicides are highly phytotoxic as their mode of action involves inhibition of acetolactate synthase (ALS) that catalyzes the first step in the synthesis of the branched-chain amino acids (valine, leucine, and isoleucine). These herbicides have potential to disturb natural soil biota that are important for biogeochemical and nutrient cycling and long-term soil sustainability. Also, they have tendency to leach into the waterbodies resulting and environmental and health issues. They undergo a variety of transformations in soil and hence providing a complex pattern of metabolites which can be even more toxic than the parent compounds. Presence of such contaminants in agricultural soil is also reported to affect seed germination and establishment of subsequent crops. 
Bioremediation presents an environmental friendly approach to remediate the herbicide residues at point source i.e. in agricultural fields. The potential of indigenously isolated bacterial consortia for bioremediation of sulfonylurea herbicide residues and plant growth promotion in wheat-rice cropping system will be explored over two growing periods. Metagenomic analyses will be carried out to evaluate the effect of these herbicide and bacterial inocula on rhizospheric soil microbial populations. Efficacy of bacterial inocula alone and after immobilization on a carrier material e.g. biochar for the remediation of sulfonylurea herbicides, conservation of soil microbial populations and improving agronomic parameters of crop plants will also be investigated.

data.projectName: Investigation of Novel Approaches for degradation of refractory oncogenic proteins of acute myeloid and acute promyelocytic leukemia
data.projectDigest: Acute Myeloid leukemia (AML) is a blood cancer that is responsible for a large proportion of deaths world widely and similarly in Pakistan. This disease affects all ages from children to older people. The median survival of the current treatment protocols is even less than 5 years and majorly based on intensive chemotherapy that is associated with a high proportion of adverse effects. With the help of the current proposed project, we shall establish cell culture lab. With the help of this lab, we would be able to screen some novel compounds that have some potential for screening against acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) and as well as for AML. Combination of arsenic and ATRA is already an established targeted therapy regimen for the PML-RAR? associated APL. Similarly, the purpose of the project is to establish target-oriented therapy development for variant drug resistant APL and AML.

data.projectName: Proposals for Reform to Premiere Accountability Law of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Check and balance is the beauty of democracy. Without check and balance the true spirit of democracy is difficult to attain. The concept of accountability is conceived in order to ensure check and balance. The research proposal is an attempt to put forward a plan for writing two articles on the national accountability bureau ordinance,1999 of Pakistan (accountability law in Pakistan), which will gauge the maintainability of some of the provisions of this ordinance on the touchstone of basic fundamental rights as enshrined in the developed nations constitutions of the modern world and of the Constitution of Pakistan itself. The proposed articles will inter-alia focus on the accountability laws of different developed nations and propose solutions for the betterment of the premier accountability law of Pakistan. One of the article will focus on current media ethics while reporting accountability cases and study the laws involved therein while proposing solutions for betterment in reporting accountability trials.

data.projectName: Novel Biochar-Based Fertilizer: For Enhancing Nitrogen Use Efficiency, Plant Growth and Reducing Nitrogen Leaching
data.projectDigest:
The current research project ‘’Novel Biochar-Based Fertilizer: For Enhancing Nitrogen Use Efficiency, Plant Growth and Reducing Nitrogen Leaching’’ has been designed to enhanced nitrogen use efficiency and reduce leaching from urea fertilizer. Every year Pakistan import millions of tons urea which put pressure on country economic. An agriculture, excesses application of N fertilization had been extremely alarmed as a main cause of radiative N (Nr). This result in nitrate leaching, ammonia volatilization, and nitrous oxide emissions which are severe environmental problems by contaminated groundwater quality. Subsequently reducing N use efficiency causes high N losses, and high economic costs.. Biochar is a byproduct of biomass pyrolysis and is usually characterized as rich in recalcitrant C with a large surface area, and diverse functional groups. These unique properties of biochar facilitating to hold nutrients, predominantly N, in soil and solution. Application of functionally enhanced biochar products in small quantity could be a low cost but high agronomic ef?ciency. Due to unique characteristics, biochar could be blended with urea fertilizer for concurrently increasing crop yield and reducing environmental risk.
We hypothesize that (1) Biochar Blended Urea (BBU) will enhanced N retention from urea through reaction and surface adsorption; anand (2)  Application of BBU could reduce N release but improve supply for plant growth.
The objectives of the study is to insights if BBU could be a potential substitute for chemical urea to enhance N use efficiency, plant growth and reduce N leaching loss.

data.projectName: Development of 2D semiconductor-based quantum emitters for optoelectronic application
data.projectDigest: The field of two-dimensional materials gain immense boost after the award of Nobel prize in 2010 for the discovery of graphene. These are least possible stable sub-nanometer scale atomic layers which possess exceptional and unique electrical, optical and physical properties based on their band gap structure. An outstanding property of such materials is its transformation of bandgap from indirect to direct at atomic scale along with flexible and transparent properties.  A specialized field of research that is emerging rapidly from this concept is the formation of heterostructures. It is based on devices made from 2D vertically stacked layers grown one over the other. The stack thus formed represents a hybrid material arranged in a desired vertical sequence. When these atomic layers vertically stacked, due to spin-valley locking and individual atoms arrangement a periodic potential landscape is generated which is just like quantum emitters. By controlling the individual atoms and interlayer excitons, charge transfer across these layers will be tuned further. These quantum emitters have wide applications in optoelectronic and semiconductor industry. This technology will be used in fabrication of cheap hybrid semiconductor-based devices which are ultra-sensitive, fast and promising for transparent electronics.

data.projectName: ORGANOGEL-CHAR STRATEGY: FOR SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTION OF CANOLA (Brassica napus L.) AND SUNFLOWER (Helianthus annuus L.) UNDER WATER STRESS
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is being categorised among the most water-stressed countries in the world, as most of the areas in Pakistan are arid or semiarid with extremely low rainfall frequencies and facing drastic levels of drought. Furthermore, inappropriate soil management practices, with excessive agricultural activities and enhanced drought scenarios are becoming persistent threats for the agricultural sector, as these are associated with the overall reduction in soil quality and crop production. Hence, it is a domineering need of the hour to devise some strategies that assist in maintaining the stability of agricultural soils with enhanced nutrient and moisture absorption properties. Biochar, compost, and hydrogel are widely reported in the literature as soil conditioners and enhancers of soil absorption characteristics. But very limited literature is available regarding their combined effects on soil characteristics in combination with detailed analysis of crops growing with these amendments.  For this purpose biochar, composted biochar, and hydrogel will be applied in the pot soil separately and in combination to find the best soil amendment for improving soil characteristics and yield attributes of two major oilseed crops (i.e., canola and sunflower) under water stress. The screened amendment then will be studied under field conditions to test its reliability under natural conditions.

data.projectName: CPEC: A corridor of strategic and economic development; potentials for KP
data.projectDigest: China Pakistan signed agreement on November 8, 2014 known as CPEC, “China Pakistan Economic Corridor” with preliminary cost of US $ 48 billion. Further The study would enlist the opportunities for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in term of economic development and  would focus that how the project would convert Pakistan’s location into an asset.

data.projectName: Effects and mechanism of viola serpens, cordia rothii and Equisetum arvense on adopted nuclear receptor PXR/ CAR, furthermore to determine its herb-drug interaction and Pharmaceutics.
data.projectDigest:
Medicinal herbs have been a part of human medicine for thousands of years. The herb-drug interaction is an extension of drug-drug interaction, in which the consumptions of herbs cause alterations in the metabolism of drugs the patients happen to take at the same time. viola serpens, cordia rothii and equisetum arvense are also used for jaundice, tuberculosis, hepatitis, brittle fingernails, joint diseases, gout, osteoarthritis, weak bones (osteoporosis), high cholesterol levels, frostbite, weight loss, heavy menstrual periods, and uncontrolled bleeding (hemorrhage) of the nose, lung, or stomach.
	The constitutive-androstane-receptor (CAR) and pregnane X receptor (PXR) has been established as one of the most important transcriptional factors that regulate the expression of phase I enzymes, phase II enzymes, and drug transporters in the xenobiotic responses. CAR & PXR have been implicated in multiple herb-drug interactions that can lead to alterations of the drug's pharmacokinetic properties and cause fluctuating therapeutic efficacies, possibly leading to complications. Regions of the world that heavily incorporate herbalism into their primary health care and people turning to alternative medicines as a personal choice could be at risk for adverse reactions or unintended results from these interactions. This project is designed for the safe and effective use of this medicinal plant.

• Decipher the conjectures on trees as well as to obtain the results for arbitrary graphs
 • Settle on the different algorithms to find efficiency of different type of irregular labeling for different type of graphs 
• Explore the collision of this topic to the other topics.

data.projectName: Colistin resistance in Pakistan: Comparison of various phenotypic susceptibility methods and Molecular epidemiology of mobile colistin resistance (mcr) determinants
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
Antimicrobial resistance is the most serious global health threats with the ESKAPE group of pathogens being a large problem. Limited treatment options to treat multidrug resistant (MDR) and extremely drug resistant (XDR) gram negative rods (GNRs) has triggered the reintroduction of the older and less user-friendly antibiotic colistin. Since last many years, there is ongoing debate regarding colistin susceptibility methods. The only recommended broth microdilution (BMD) method is expensive, requires technical expertise and difficult to perform routinely in day today susceptibility testing. There is a dire need of an efficient, economical and user friendly method to be used for routine colistin susceptibility. 
The recent discovery of mobile colistin resistance (mcr) determinants in humans and animals has brought concerns regarding the future of this antimicrobial. The usefulness of colistin as a last resort antimicrobial is now compromised by the presence of an increasing number of mobile colistin resistance genes (mcr). To date, eight different mcr and their variants have been described, mainly mcr-1, mcr-2, mcr-3, mcr-4, mcr-5, mcr-6, mcr-7 and mcr-8. The colistin resistance mechanisms are not exactly known in Pakistan.
The purpose of this study is; 
o	to determine comparison of various phenotypic colistin susceptibility methods to select an efficient, economical and user friendly method to be used in routine laboratory work, 
o	to determine most prevalent colistin resistance genes (mcr) in our settings and their association to already reported human / animal mcr genes thus helping understanding possible mechanism of spread and therefore prevention, 
o	to determine the concordance of genotype to phenotype, thus helping in better patient management.

To date, eight different mcr and their variants have been described, mainly mcr-1, mcr-2, mcr-3, mcr-4, mcr-5, mcr-6, mcr-7 and mcr-8. The colistin resistance mechanisms are not exactly known in Pakistan.
The purpose of this study is; 
o	to determine comparison of various phenotypic colistin susceptibility methods to select an efficient, economical and user friendly method to be used in routine laboratory work, 
o	to determine most prevalent colistin resistance genes (mcr) in our settings and their association to already reported human / animal mcr genes thus helping understanding possible mechanism of spread and therefore prevention, 
o	to determine the concordance of genotype to phenotype, thus helping in better patient management.

data.projectName: Exploring new scintillating materials for high pressure and temperature applications in particle physics detectors
data.projectDigest: Scintillation detectors (SD’s) are used for the determination of the high-energy particle’s spectrum. In SD’s the material absorb high energy photons or particles to produce luminescence. Commonly used materials are NaI or CsI crystals activated with thallium. These aforementioned crystals provide high photon efficiency and good transparency. But to detect radioactive traces and advance materials characterizations under extreme conditions, some new materials required which could sustain high temperature and pressure. The experimental equipment (Scintillating Detector) is recently installed in National Centre for Physics to achieve aforesaid properties. We expect this project will support experimental scientists (nationally or internationally) to select suitable scintillating material to perform High Energy Physics experiments. This project will also provide opportunities for postgraduate students to get involved in advanced research activities in Centre for High Energy Physics.

data.projectName: Enhancing Drought and Heat Stress Tolerance Against Soybean Seed Shattering Through Plant Growth Promoting Bacteria and Plant Growth Regulators
data.projectDigest: Soybean (Glycine max L.) pod shattering is a key factor allied with 34 to 99% yield losses globally. Several studies have been conducted in the past such as genetics of pod shattering resistance on individual varieties, early harvesting and harvesting when temperature is still low are not very effective and limited to the soybean growers. Soybean is an important oil, food and protein crop. In arid areas, soybean matures in the peak of dry season that’s the big reason of pod shattering and some varieties are susceptible to the pod shattering will augment the seed yield losses. Drought and heat stresses are the major abiotic constraints, under the current and climate change scenario in future. Any further increase in the occurrence, and extremity of these stresses, either individually or in combination at all the growth stages would severely reduce the crop productivity and causes considerable yield losses. Plant response to physiological adaptations are faster to decrease the effects of these stresses. Plant growth promoting bacteria (PGPB) and plant growth regulators (PGR) influence positively to enhance the abiotic stress tolerance in soybean plants. Therefore, the use of PGPB and PGR found helpful to keep photosynthetic rate and water status in soybean under abiotic stresses to reducing production losses by improving morphological and physiological parameters that modify the plant capacity of water uses. The proposed study will serve not only to mitigate drought and heat stress but also to improve the productivity of soybean crop under such environments. As a consequence of this study, seed yield and oil quality will be promoted in drought prone areas with different sowing dates. Finally, the results will be shared to the farmers, fertilizer industry and researchers.

data.projectName: Therapeutic strategies against high fat diet-associated pathophysiological alterations in cardiovascular system
data.projectDigest: Atherosclerosis is a metabolic disorder, causes narrowing of the arteries associated with lipid and other endothelial alteration. Cardiovascular disorders are the major cause of death and its estimated prevalence is 1.9 billion individuals or one third world’s population. Prickly pear (Opuntia ficus indica) fruit contains polyphenols, vitamin C, betalain pigments, fatty acids and fibers having the radical-scavenging properties as well as antioxidant activities. Current study is designed to evaluate therapeutic efficacy of  ethanolic extract of Cactus pear (Opuntia ficus-indica) fruit in restoration of pathophysiological alterations in high fat diet-associated atherosclerotic rat model. For this purpose adult Wistar rats (Rattus norvegicus) weighing about 180-200g (n=50) will be divided into five groups. Physical parameters include body weight and feed intake. For diagnostic measures blood pressure and ECG will be performed. Blood samples will be taken at the end of trial for measuring blood glucose level, lipid profile, liver functioning tests, MDA, TAC and TOS. Tissue samples of heart (aorta) will be collected in RNA latter for mRNA isolation and gene expression analysis.  Tissue samples of heart (aorta) kidneys and liver will be collected for histopathology and immunohistochemistry. Statistically data will be analyzed through analysis of variance (ANOVA) and Duncan’s Multiple Range test at 5% level of significance

data.projectName: Elucidation of Drought and Temperature Tolerance for Yield Maximization and Genomic Assisted Selection under Changing Climate through Transcriptome and Methylome Mapping of Lentil

Lentil production is affected in Pakistan and nearly 98% of lentil is imported for local use. 
Current project is based on our recent findings that lentil nodulation not only depends upon variation in genotype but also vary from one cropping season to another, mainly due to climatic changes. Heat waves and drought tolerance are the two main adaptive traits that have been identified for lentil success in changing environment.

data.projectName: Synthesis of Sulphur based Anticancerous Azole Derivatives and Molecular Docking Studies to Combat Cancer
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is the 6th most populous country in this world, where a huge number of people are suffering from cancer. Cancer is a disease by which affected body cells grow violently and withdraw appropriate function of normal body cells. Cancer has many different types which are treated by a number of ways including chemotherapy, radiotherapy, targeted therapy etc. Anyhow, Triple negative breast cancer has become resistant to most of the available chemotherpeutic drugs and the major treatment available for this type of cancer is chemotherapy. Therefore, there is a need to develop more and more chemotherapeutic agents.  Among heterocycles, sulphur based azole rings i.e. thiadiazoles, Imidazo[2,1-b]thiadiazoles and thiazoles have been found to possess wide range of applications. They exhibit promising biological potential against cancer, and HIV along with other pharmacological activities. The synthesis of novel thiadiazoles, Imidazo [2,1-b] thiadiazoles and thiazoles seems quite significant on account of their medicinal impact, more potency and lesser toxicity. They act as important scaffolds and better agents in terms of efficacy and safety. The biological and structural features of thiadiazoles, imidazo[ 2,1-b]thiadiazoles and thiazoles prompted us to synthesize libraries of such compounds and evaluate their biological impact through in vitro and Molecular Docking studies.
