data.projectName: Assessment of biology and fishery status  of economically important stingrays (Myliobatiformes) of Balochistan Coast for conservation
data.projectDigest:
Stingrays have cartilaginous endoskeleton and represent the elasmobranchs. Stingrays have dorsoventrally compressed body plan in which pectoral fin directly fused to the body. This flattened body allows them to live on the ocean floor where they swim by flapping the body. The tail is long and contains venomous spines which vary in number and position in different species. Many species have one or more venomous spines on their tail, which can delivers a painful sting. 
Ray fisheries have a commercial and economic value. Stingrays are the dominant components of the fishery catch worldwide. Stingrays have been used for food and in the manufacturing of fine leather products. In Pakistan rays are caught in nets as a by-catch along with other commercially valuable fishes. The unavailability of data on the diversity, abundance and catch statistics of different stingray fishes from the coastal waters of Pakistan led the proposal of this research who’s main objective is to ascertain the species diversity and catch statistics of stingray fishes. The collected data will be used to identify the stock and fishery status of this important group. The data will help the fishery authority in the management and conservation of the stingrays in future.

data.projectName: Development and physical characterization of the environmental friendly metal oxides (spinel Zinc Ferrites) nanostructures for gas sensor applications.
data.projectDigest: The major part of the proposed project will be concerned with the fabrication of metal doped zinc ferrite nanoparticles [Zn (1-x) MxFe2O4 where x ? 0.1 and M stands for divalent transition metals] by utilizing co-precipitation technique. The dopant concentrations are kept less than 10% because these compositions are not studied in detail. The reports on electrical measurements, super-capacitor and gas sensing properties are limited. The structure of the prepared nanoparticles will be analyzed with x-ray diffraction (XRD) technique which will provide information about the lattice constant, the purity of the compound, porosity and the particle size. Morphology of the prepared nanoparticles will be studied by using scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The chemical composition of the prepared samples will be obtained by EDX measurements. Magnetic properties of the samples will be measured and the cation distribution in the present system is derived from the site preference energy and magnetization method. Initial permittivity and relative loss factor would be studied as a function of frequency at room temperature. The electrical and dielectric properties will be measured as a function of temperature also. Metal doped zinc ferrite nanoparticles will be used as electrode for the super-capacitors application. For gas sensing study, the resistance of the sensor will be monitored by using semiconductor parameter analyzer.

data.projectName: MEASURING DYNAMICS OF MULTIDIMENSIONAL POVERTY AND SOCIO ECONOMIC CONDITIONS IN THE SLUMS OF PUNJAB
data.projectDigest:
Rapid urbanization took place during the previous years. The most deprived
segment of poor population was unable to build appropriate shelter for
themselves. They settled in open spaces around the urban slumps. The word
Katchi Abadis is used parallel to urban slums in Pakistan. Most of the people
residing in these areas are without formal ownership rights of land. Moreover,
they are living in vulnerable conditions and have not access to basic
necessities of life. Poverty, illiteracy, unemployment, poor health facilities, poor
sanitation and non-availability of safe drinking water facilities are the common
characteristics of the urban slums.
The major aim of the study in hand is to find those determinants which
contribute in poor socio-economic conditions and also to estimate
multidimensional well-being in the slums of Lahore, Faisalabad, Multan and
Rawalpindi which cover all the regions (southern, central and northern) of
Punjab, a province of Pakistan. Education, health, poverty and standard of
living will be used for measurement of socio-economic conditions and
multidimensional well-being. After finding the results in the slums of these
mega cities, they would be generalized for whole Pakistan.

data.projectName: Preparation and evaluation of chitosan nanoparticles coated with phytochemicals as drought and salt stress emulators in wheat
data.projectDigest:
Over the last few decades, the productivity of field crops have been reduced due a number of abiotic and biotic factors. Especially in Pakistan under water deficient scenario, the salinity and drought has badly affected the yields of crops including wheat. To this end, a number of stress management strategies have been adopted which met partial successful. Mainly, synthetic chemicals have been used as plant growth regulators (PGRs) to induce tolerance against a variety of biotic and abiotic stress. They are applied as seed priming agents, foliar sprays or in soil drenching. Certain crops require multiple applications of hazardous PGRs which results in the deterioration of soil fertility and the loss of much needed soil microbial community.
Recent magnificent expansion of nanotechnology and biogenic has opened up new endeavors helping the transformation of agriculture to new standards. In this context, chitosan-based nanoparticles (CNPs) have been developed as excellent carriers for natural and synthetic bioactive molecules. The CNPs with altered physiochemical properties like cationic nature, surface area and size resulting in much improved growth promontory, stress protectants and antioxidant activities. The CNPs are less toxic and more stable compared to pure biomolecules and widely used as carriers of bioactive molecules.
The present study has been designed to prepare and evaluate the effects of chitosan nanoparticles coated with phytochemicals on wheat under salt and drought stress. We will investigate the effects of phytochemical-based nano-formulations on seed biochemistry, germination and growth in wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) under normal and above-said stress conditions with special emphasis on modulations of antioxidant defense potential.

The CNPs with altered physiochemical properties like cationic nature, surface area and size resulting in much improved growth promontory, stress protectants and antioxidant activities. The CNPs are less toxic and more stable compared to pure biomolecules and widely used as carriers of bioactive molecules.
The present study has been designed to prepare and evaluate the effects of chitosan nanoparticles coated with phytochemicals on wheat under salt and drought stress. We will investigate the effects of phytochemical-based nano-formulations on seed biochemistry, germination and growth in wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) under normal and above-said stress conditions with special emphasis on modulations of antioxidant defense potential.

data.projectName: Hepatitis C management in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Pakistan has the 2nd highest burden of hepatitis C virus in the world, with over 10 million people suffering from this disease. World Health Organization has developed a strategy to eliminate hepatitis by 2030. Globally, no funding is available to eliminate hepatitis. The global hepatitis leaders are stressing to find the local financing for hepatitis elimination. Pakistan needs to invest millions of dollar to control hepatitis from the country, otherwise the number of cases in the country will continuously increase. With our discussion with leading hepatitis physicians and our experiences, we identify the key issues linked with hepatitis C in Pakistan. One of the major issue linked with HCV treatment in Pakistan is antiviral resistance, which is due to mutations in HCV genome and involvement of certain host genetic polymorphism, which influence the treatment outcome. Approximately, 80% of HCV patients in Pakistan are undiagnosed, there is strong need to diagnose these patients and enrolled them in treatment programs. The knowledge about HCV transmission routes is also very low in Pakistan. In this study, we will work on HCV drug resistance, HCV screening, HCV awareness and Ageing in HCV patients. The results of study will help us to develop treatment guidelines for HCV non-responders patients in Pakistan, which will be shared from the platform of Pakistan Society for the Study of Liver Diseases and Pakistan Society of Gastroenterology with the physicians treating Hepatitis C patients in the country.

data.projectName: MOLECULAR INVESTIGATION OF ARBUSCULAR MYCORRHIZAL FUNGAL SPECIES FROM SELECTED  PLAIN AND MOUNTANEOUS STUDY SITES OF KHYBER PAKHTUNKHWA AND ITS EFFECTS ON GRAIN YIELD AND YIELD RELATED PARAMETERS OF A GIVEN CROP
data.projectDigest:
Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) live in plant roots, improving the nutrients uptake of host plants and its subsequent growth through its extended network of hyphae and mycelium from soil region where plant roots cannot normally reach. AMF have also been reported in conferring resistance / tolerance to host plants against biotic and abiotic stresses which necessitate having full information about its species and species distribution. Most of the studies conducted in Pakistan relating to AMF species distribution / richness are based on morphological characteristics which are laborious and time demanding. As per my knowledge, almost no molecular study has been conducted in Pakistan investigating the AMF species distribution, diversity and host specificity.
To introduce molecular characterization of AMF species in Pakistan, this study has been designed to monitor AMF species diversity and distribution in rhizosphere of selected crop (any crop available after release of research grant) collected from selected study sites (plain and mountains) of KP. This may reveal whether similar AMF species exist in both plain and mountain area or choice of AMF species colonization vary with varying agro climatic conditions. This may also reveal whether there is any significant difference in response of AMF (i.e. AMF collected from plain and mountainous study sites) towards increasing crop yield and yield related parameters

data.projectName: Programmable toys for increasing Problem-Solving Skills and emotional Intelligence in students
data.projectDigest: Emotional intelligence is the ability to examine one's own and the emotions of others, to distinguish among them, and to use these facts to guide one's analytical thinking and actions. In recent years, emotional intelligence has become a popular topic of research. On the other hand, programming is an essential component of computer science students. Students can develop these skills with regular practices and instructions. There are  many programmable toys that are available in the market that helps in learning programming but they do not help in increasing emotional intelligence. Also, these toys are expensive, so we aim to design robots at a reasonable price affordable for everyone.  These robots will be used by students to learn different concepts of programming that will increase their problem-solving skills. They will perform different activities through this robot  that will increase their emotional intelligence.  The student will draw the instructions in the form of arrows on the cardboard, the robot will scan it and follow these instructions to reach the final goal.

data.projectName: A Machine Learning and Translational Bioinformatics Based Approach to Prioritize Small Molecules Binders of Potential Drug Targets to Treat Resistant Super Bug causing the Typhoid
data.projectDigest:
Typhoid caused by the Salmonella typhi is foremost health issue globally as well as locally. It causes huge number of deaths on global scale. The situation has now exacerbated by the emergence of the drug resistant strains such as the recent outbreak of extensively resistant super bug typhi in Karachi and in Hyderabad regions. This resistant form of S. typhi is non-responsive towards conventional drugs.
Therefore, if we are able to understand the complete new genomics data obtained by the super bug extensively drug resistant (XDR) S. typhi then we can propose new and unique metabolic pathways responsible to confer the resistance to this super bug and for which there is limited drug available now. Identification of such metabolic pathways will lead to design new inhibitors against those enzymes taking part in unique metabolic pathways of the XDR S. typhi. 
To address this problem, we aimed to use emerging technology of Machine Learning and Translational Bioinformatics to, firstly identifying the novel drug target and later, screen a large number of ligands from chemical databases against identified drug targets to shortlist the potential drug candidates. The ultimate result is to discover the potential drug candidates against XDR S. typhi.

data.projectName: Cyber Resilience for Cloud Services using Quantum Computing Based Cognitive Correlates (QCCC)
data.projectDigest: In this research project we will secure the online storage data by human inspired security mechanism. Cloud computing based systems are using various security measures for network security, application security to secure organization’s data, applications, platform, virtualization, hardware and data centers, but if we compare this progress with the goals of AGI then perhaps it is more appropriate to elaborate cognitive memory functions to attain human-like information protection and manipulation through AGI-agents for cloud services.

data.projectName: Speech Therapy Assistant: Mobile application for the children with Speech disorders
data.projectDigest:
Children with communication disorders (including speech and language)  having a prevalence rate of 6-9% along with concomitant disordered groups of children face an increased risk of social, emotional and academic challenges. The literature review indicates that the effects of speech disorder in childhood may persist into adulthood and span multiple domains of activity limitations and participation restrictions [ALPR], as defined by the World Health Organization’s (WHO) International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) model.
In Pakistan the desirable coordination between education, health and community services is disorganized or non-existent and the paramedic staff for communication therapy are often inaccessible. Teaching and integration aids are insufficient while cost of these services is a great impediment. There is a dire need to explore a modernized economical solution available at the fingertips of this marginalized group of children. Mobile applications for health are categorized as m-Health applications are gaining a considerable interest in the children with special needs.  
The present study aims to develop a spirited based mobile application to provide opportunities to learn and improve the speech deficiencies by using game-based learning approach. The proposed application also allows the parents to monitor and evaluate the performance of children and amicably interact with the speech therapist.

data.projectName: Development of Solvent Microextraction Procedures for Preconcentration, Separation and Atomic Absorption Spectrometry for Determinations of Pt, Pd, Ni, Cu at Low Trace Levels in Environmental Samples
data.projectDigest: The determination of  copper, nickel, platinum and Palladium metals at trace levels with accurately from water, food, pharmaceutical preparations and biological samples are main objectives of this scientific work. Development of dispersive microextraction procedures and metals complexation with imine type Schiff-bases, followed by extraction of metal ion in single drop of extracting solvent and determination based frequently available atomic absorption technique.  The metals of interest with their broader use especially nickel which is involved for enhancement of some enzymes and insulin activity in normal or diabetics patients, platinum as cis-platin drug is used for cancer patients, palladium is used for jewellery and reduction of car emissions for safe environment, and copper that has important functions in metabolism and used in electrical appliances. The procedures will be checked for correct analysis and optimized for sensitivity, selectivity, reproducibility and accuracy of the determinations. The method will be applied for real samples analysis.

data.projectDigest:

Newer prolonged-release preparations of sulfonylureas derivatives can undoubtedly safer, mainly due to reducing hypoglycemia, and for this reason should be preferred [1].

Antimicrobial [6-9], anti-inflammatory [10. 11], antiviral [12], anti-tuberculosis [13], trypanocidal [14] and prominent scavenger or antioxidant [32 15] activities of organotin(IV) derivatives have been reported. data.projectName: “Isolation of new/novel anticancer diterpenoid alkaloids from local aconitum species of Dir Kohistan, KP”
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Benazir Bhutto University, Sheringal, Dir
data.projectDigest:
Medicinal plants are used for the treatment and prevention of diseases throughout the world.  In fact, plants produce a diverse range of bioactive molecules, making them a rich source of different types of medicines. Among the most prevailed and fetal diseases around the world, cancer is one of the deadly disease, characterized by the irregular cell proliferation, and makes major public health problems in both the developing as well as in developed countries. Due to its high mortality and prevalence rate, it is an important health and economic issue which needs an effective prevention. 
As plant derived natural products are more tolerable, more potent and non-toxic as compare to the available conventional therapy for cancers, therefore, they are in high demand and several species of medicinal plants have been investigated and selected for the preparation of cancer medicines. An extensive research work is required in this field to investigate/develop safe and effective anti-cancer drugs from natural source. In the past few years, diterpenoid alkaloids from genus aconitum got ample attention due to their promising potential in the treatment of various type of cancers.
Keeping in view the importance of diterpenoid alkaloids, the present research was designed to investigate the indigenous aconitum species of Dir (Kohistan) for their pharmacological potentials specifically against lungs and breast cancers with an aim to find out safe and economical new/novel natural anti-cancer drug molecules. 
The nature of this study is basic and we hypothesized that aconitum species are rich source of diterpenoid alkaloids possessing strong anticancer potential. Our main objectives here is to;

data.projectName: Intelligent Urdu Fake News Detection System
data.projectDigest: Due to low cost, and ease of use, millions of Internet users are interacting on social media and web platforms generating large amounts of data, in which a large amount of content is unverified and unauthenticated. Among such content, fake news can change the mindset, and perceptions of the Internet users. For example, Pakistan’s polio eradication campaign has been adversely impacted by different fake stories related to the usage of polio vaccine. Such content has made parents to refrain from getting their children vaccinated. Fake news is a worldwide problem and research on its automatic detection is underway. Urdu is the national language and lingua franca of Pakistan with around 100 million speakers worldwide. Only one research work exists for Urdu fake news detection system, but the work is conducted on a very small data set. In this project, we plan to detect Urdu fake news from the big online data repositories of web and social media platforms. We will develop a large data set and design latest artificial intelligence techniques such as word embeddings to develop our system. We will also identify those websites that are publishing Urdu fake news constantly.

data.projectName: Biochemical and Molecular characterization of medicinally important selected species of Family phyllanthacae
data.projectDigest: Infectious diseases caused by many pathogens are worldwide a major cause of deaths. The problem is compounded by the growing drug resistance exhibited by several human pathogens. Therefore, there is a need to develop alternative natural antimicrobial drugs with no or less side effects. Recent decades have witnessed a renewed enhancement in the demand of herb-based nutraceutical products because of, inter alia, safety and affordability. Phytochemical and molecular characterization of plant cell is an important task in drug discovery. Recently, transcriptome and metabolomics analysis have been interlinked in identifying differential gene expression and then further metabolite identification. Chloroplast genome is important in phylogenetics and provide deep insight into evolution. We are interested to increase genomic resources of selected species of family phyllanthacae growing in Pakistan by characterization of transcriptome and chloroplast genome. Studying the genomics of ecologically and medicinally important species can help in understanding the tree life, evolution, taxonomy, genetic diversity and active metabolic pathways. On the basis of genetic information we will isolate and identify the biochemical constituent and their biological activities will be determined. The use of these plant for medicinal purpose will be safe compare to other commercial product and also economically favorable to pharmaceutical industries.

data.projectName: Study on Bioactive Compounds of anti-microbial and anti-tumor potential from entophytic fungi isolated of some medicinally important plants.
data.piUniversity: Federal Urdu University of Arts, Sciences & Technology
data.projectDigest:
Cancer and various other infectious diseases are major causes of deaths around the world. There is a constant need for the discovery and development antimicrobial and anti-cancer drugs because of shortcomings of low tumor selectivity, narrow therapeutic index and development of multidrug resistance of currently available drugs. Endophytes are micro-organisms that reside in plants at few or at all part of their life, without harming the host. Surface saprophytes, latent pathogens and mycorrhizal fungi are some of the micro-organisms which inhabit the internal tissues at certain part of their lifecycle. During their part of life cycle in the plant tissues, some of the endophytic fungi are found to be produce same or similar bioactive secondary metabolites as their host’s chemical constituents. Due to their enormous production of bioactive metabolites, they have been considered to be a potential anticancer source. Camptothecin, taxol, combretastatins, are anti tumour drugs of plant origin.
Keeping this importance of endophytes in mind, present study was designed to isolate the endophytic fungi from some medicinal plants (e.g Neem and Poly althia etc).endophytic fungi will be identified based on morphological and microscopic characteristics and biochemically  and molecularly.the antimicrobial activity will be detected using agar well diffusion technique.  Mtt assay will be used to detect cytotoxicity of the extracts/compounds against transformed hella cancerous cell lines.  Bioactive metabolite in the extract producing will be identified and purified using preparative TLC and GCMS (gas chromatography-mass spectrometry) analysis.

data.projectName: Food quality monitoring, food processing and agricultural weed control using Microwave Energy
data.projectDigest:
This project proposes innovative use of Microwave energy for food quality monitoring, food processing and agricultural weed control. Cost effective, easy to use,  handheld microwave sensors to detect the adulteration in foodstuff such as water/uread/detergent in milk,  grinded bricks in chili powder will be developed.
Besides this a microwave reactor would be designed to efficiently dry the vegetables and fruits for preservation and transportation without loosing their quality attributes.
The 3rd goal of the project is to develop a microwave equipment which could kill the agricultural weed without needing chemical herbicides.

data.projectName: Role of Arbuscular Mycorrhizal fungi in growth and development of resistance in salt affected wheat plants
data.projectDigest: Arbuscular Mycorrhizal fungi play a very important role in the improvement of yield of crops by nutrients uptake especially phosphorus. Several researchers have demonstrated the useful effects of AM fungi in the alleviation of salinity as well as heavy metal stress conditions. This research project has been designed to develop the resistance in salt affected wheat plants by using specific AM fungal strains.  This may also result in the improvement of growth of wheat plants. AMF colonization improves tolerance of plants to stressful conditions by bringing about several changes in their morpho-physiological traits. This project consists of three parts. First part will be basic research in which potential AM fungal strains will be identified from the rhizosphere of hundred plants. Different molecular techniques will be used for these AM fungal strains. Second part of the research will be the application of these AM fungi in the form of bio-fertilizers to wheat plants. Third part will consist of analyzing the AM inoculated  and un-inoculated wheat plants for testing their growth, yield and resistance to salinity conditions. This research may result in identification of specific Arbuscular Mycorrhizal bio-fertilizer for wheat plants of salt stress areas of Pakistan which may enhance it's productivity and  may result in the development of an environment friendly bio-fertilizer

data.projectName: Plant Disease Detection and Remedy Recommendation System
data.projectDigest: The aim of this project is to develop an application for plant disease detection and remedies recommendation. In the first phase of this project a plant leaves image dataset will be prepared. The dataset will contain the images of healthy and defected plant leaves. In the initial stage we will consider the following crops rice, soybean, wheat, corn, cotton, melon, sugarcane, tomato, pepper, potato, apple, cherry, banana, strawberry, grape, peach, orange. Later on the dataset will be extended by adding more crops and cultivation regions. During data collection the geographic location and environmental conditions will also be considered, because the disease symptoms, severity level and its remedies vary in different geographic location and environmental conditions. In order to label the dataset, the collected images will be evaluated by plant pathologists in the pathology laboratory to manually diagnose the plant diseases. After that different machine learning and digital image processing techniques such as image segmentation, image pre-processing, image normalization, image resizing, data augmentation, artificial neural network and convolutional neural network models will be developed to recognize the plant diseases. Finally, a fully functional application will be developed to automatically recognize the plant diseases from plant leaves. The application will also recommend the remedies of detected diseases with the help of videos and textual information.

data.projectName: Assessing the determinants of spatial variation in the dengue disease through Geospatial techniques, A case study of Punjab Province
data.projectDigest: Dengue is a huge problem of Pakistan as it has continuously affected the country since 1994. Its recent disastrous attack affected a significant population in twin cities (Rawalpindi and Islamabad). This research proposes a geospatial solution to this risk.  For this, contemporary technologies (Geo-informatics) are being used to assist the authorities and society against this menace. We will try to detect dengue-affected areas and try to figure out the environmental and socio economic reasons behind its outbreaks. Further, we will also try to estimate the level of danger and their capacity to handle it through these advanced techniques. This will benefit our society and economy by making smart moves against this disease.

data.projectName: CrimePredictor: Deep Learning Based Energy-Efficient System For Robust Predictive Criminal Analysis in Smart City Environment
data.projectDigest: The CrimePredictor project aims to provide an efficient and effective advanced system capable of collecting, analyzing videos from surveillance videos from heterogeneous camera environment in the smart city, to extract the intra/inter-camera video analytics, helping investigators in predicting the  doubtful illicit criminal activities, thus, resulting in the considerable reduction of human resources needed for the investigations. It is anticipated that the proposed system would be made up of two principal modules (1)  A Tracking System (non-obtrusive) that can constantly (i) Track, all objects in a distributed camera network, (ii) Analyze spatio-temporal pattern of each moving object, (iii) discover and determine continuously,  the illustrative information of each object being tracked, (iv) super resolution for low-quality images using temporal information for accurate detection and (v) novel algorithms for night-mode based object detection. (2) A Decision System that can generate (i) the models of criminal/suspicious activity by correlating the spatio temporal information of each object using deep recurrent networks, and (ii)  activity alerts for the security personnel who makes critical decisions based on monitoring.

data.projectName: Designing and Development of Inner Transition Metal Oxides and Chalcogenides for Catalytic Applications in Renewable Energy Sector
data.projectDigest: Sustainable energy and clean environment are the most inestimable resources and substructure of our modern enlightenment. The emission of CO2 due to increased consumption of petroleum oil in transportation and industry effect the environment badly and one of main cause of global warming. Our plan is to convert it into chemical fuel like methanol using solar energy driven newly synthesized inner transition metal oxides and chalcogenides.  Photocatalyst nanostructures can be cost-effective and versatile key partner for photocatalytic reduction of carbon dioxide CO2 to chemical fuels such as methanol. The obtained methanol will be used in transesterification of waste biomass based oil (triglycerides) into biodiesel (fatty acid methyl esters-FAMEs, chemical name of biodiesel). Biodiesel is alternative fuel to petro-diesel. Transesterification will be carried out using newly synthesized inner transition metal oxides as catalyst. The outcome of this project will resolve the problem of increased carbon dioxide concentration and we will get multiple benefits such as clean environment, reducing the global warming effect, chemical fuel like methanol  and alternative fuel biodiesel using prepared methanol in transesterification.

data.projectName: Mental Health, Quality of Life and Post Traumatic Growth of Survivors and Families of Non-Survivors of Child Sexual Abuse:  Counseling in Perspective
data.projectDigest: Pakistan has witnessed exponential rise (33%) in reported cases of child sexual abuse during the year 2018 with alarming increase in murder after sexual abuse. Families witnessing the life loss of their children as an aftermath of sexual abuse bears additional trauma and continued threat to mental health and associated psychological problems. Literature shows that every third female and fifth male have a personal account of being sexually abused as a child. Dark experiential accounts of child abuse lead to grave psychological health issues in adults, thereby, affecting quality of life and familial relationships. Prevention of sexual abuse and legislation of Zainab Alert law has been undertaken in National assembly of Pakistan; nevertheless, ample scarcity of comprehensive understanding of social and psychological repercussions associated with heinous crimes affecting victims and collective lives of uncountable people. Therefore, present project aims at studying child sexual abuse phenomena with three-fold design. Firstly, to focus on the families of non-survivors who bear the repercussions of psychological and social trauma. Secondly, individual victims of child sexual abuse will be assessed for their mental health and psychological coping during adulthood. Thirdly, post counseling appraisals will be carried out on both families of non-survivors and survivors.

data.projectName: Chemical and molecular analysis of provitamin A carotenoids and their bio fortification in high yielding sweet potato cultivars of Pakistan by multiple gene engineering approaches
data.projectDigest: Carotenoids are bioactive materials that have been studied extensively across species of higher and lower organisms for their role in plants and microorganisms including their role in human nutrition, health, pharmaceuticals, drugs, foods, feeds, and cosmetic industries. Sweetpotato (Ipomoea batatas), the seventh most important crop of the world is rich in carotenoids especially the beta-carotene but no research is reported for Pakistani cultivars of sweetpotato. Beta-carotene supply through sweetpotato based foods is not only maintaining general health but also minimizing the risks of vitamin A related blindness especially in developing countries. Sweetpotato is attractive since it is also enriched with other bioactive compounds such as iron, starch, proteins, and anthocyanins. The conventional methods for beta-carotene (vitamin A) enhancement in sweetpotato have been unsuccessful because of complex genetic make-up of sweetpotato.  However, modern gene engineering such as, metabolic engineering and pathway engineering approaches are promising. The present project is aimed to explore the carotenoids potential of sweetpotato in high yielding Pakistani cultivars by chemical and molecular analyses and provitamin A biofortification utilizing modern genetic engineering methods of metabolic and pathway engineering to combat malnutrition(hiddenhunger) specially among the poor communities of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Accounts of History in Urdu Literature
data.projectDigest: This project will discover and highlight the links of history writing with the Urdu literature produced during colonial period (1857-1947) in British India. How the literary sources were utilized to write the history and how history was narrated and viewed in the masterpieces of representative literature during the period under study will be explored. Political, social and economic history of British India as mentioned in the Urdu literature will be compared with the historical accounts present in main historical books. The study will be an inter-disciplinary work with joint venture of Urdu Literature and History.

data.projectName: Permeation studies of azole antifungal drugs cocrystallized with aliphatic dicarboxylic acids of varying chain lengths
data.piUniversity: Kohat University of Science and Technology, Kohat
data.projectDigest: Physicochemical properties improvement of drugs by cocrystallization (a crystal engineering technique) including solubility, dissolution performance, hygroscopicity, and compressibility has been proven and well-documented. As triazole antifugal drugs i.e. itraconazole and ketoconazole are used to treat fungal mycotic infections of skin. Recent reports have proven that highly soluble coformers cocrystallized with both these antifungal drugs  led to major solubility enhancement of  these both BCS class II drugs.  However, reports related to permeability enhancement of these drugs using cocrystals and to understand the influence of conformer type and concentration on diffusion rate of drug are scarce in the literature. Our hypothesis is that long chain aliphatic carboxylic acids cocrystallized with these drugs will lead to skin permeation enhancement due to acids hydrophobic nature. Fruitful results will let us a step forward in using this novel solid form into a suitable topical formulation.

data.projectName: Therapeutic Elucidation of Activated Sirtuins in Diabetic Wound Healing
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Mechanical skin rupture exposes it to the infectious microorganism which may cause serious infectious diseases. In patients with diabetes mellitus (especially type II), the risk of infection increases because of prolonged skin wound healing. Sirtuins, a family of specialized enzymes, are cellular sensors for metabolism and energy production. We have reported previously that activation of Sirtuins promotes the skin wound healing. However, poor comprehension of the underlying mechanism poses a hurdle for efficient translation of the sirtuin modulators to the clinics. Our proposed project aims to uncover the molecular mechanisms of the increased rate of normal and diabetic skin wound healing upon activation of Sirtuins. The special focus will be on Sirt1 and Sirt3 because we have preliminary data confirming the involvement of these two Sirtuins in skin wound healing. The findings of the proposed study will reveal the exact role of Sirtuins in wound healing and confirm their potential as drug targets for curing wound healing defects. This project, therefore, promises a lot in a country like Pakistan where the prevalence of diabetes and delayed wound healing is increasing every passing year. This will pave the way for translation of Sirtuin activators from bench to bedside.

data.projectName: Recognition of Pesticide Contaminated Fruits through Multivariate Modelling Based on Spectroscopic Experiments.
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Pakistani fruits and vegetables have high demand all over the world; hence fruits and vegetables are the reasonably good part of national exports.  Fruits and vegetables are mainly affected by insect pests and diseases which result in increased cost of production and low yield. To overcome such issues, a heavy rely on chemical insecticides is considered as predominant pest control approach.  The world is setting new standards for the import of fruits and vegetables related to the  elimination of pesticide residue . Which is making difficult and cost expensive conditions and hence affecting the exports. International bodies and government of Pakistan has concerns regarding the  pesticides residue does not exceed maximum residues levels (MRLs) in fruits and vegetables.
For pesticides recognition  FTIR Spectroscopy is the potential applicant. Multivariate modeling of the spectroscopic experiment data forms a powerful combination for obtaining both qualitative and quantitative information.  The aim of the project is to  conduct  spectroscopic experiments to have spectrum data  of different classes of pesticide contaminated fruits is to conduct  the comprehensive multivariate analysis and modeling of spectrum data; is to develop the PLS based classification  method to improve the recognition of pesticide contaminated fruits; is the comparison of standard existing classification methods with proposed PLS based classification methods to ensure the best recognition of pesticides contaminated fruits.

The project will assist the fruit industry and related government departments to ensure the pesticide related quality of fruits for export and in local market as well.

data.projectName: Effect of Brain drain/Brain waste on the healthcare sector of Punjab Province
data.projectDigest:
The mobility of well-recognized talents is one of the most severe threats that are posed by the era. The forces of modernization and globalization not only provide opportunities for the people but also characterize risk to various national policymakers for the brain drain. It is the reality of the world that every country needs professional skills for its development. It is observed that better living standards of developed countries attract the talented individuals from underdeveloped countries. 
It has been observed that the rate of human capital flight is very high among medical students in Pakistan. According to an estimate by HEC every year 15,000 doctors leave the country, and as a result, Pakistan is depriving of skilled medical practitioners. It is found that brain drain is not the only problem Pakistan is facing; Brain waste is also causing a number of problems for the health sector. 
In this research, the researcher will analyze the brain drain among young healthcare final year students and house officers. The main focus is to find the inclination of young professionals towards migration and also to find out the push and pull factors that contributed to the higher human flight from Pakistan to other developed countries. Through the analysis of push and pull factors researcher will be able to identify the basic reason of brain drain in Pakistan. Further, the researcher will study the impact of a medical student's brain drain and brain waste on the national health care sector.

data.projectName: Strategic imperatives and initiatives of Green Human Resource Management: The need of the hour
data.projectDigest:
Today's business is all about going green and contributing towards environmental sustainability. Organizations cannot work towards green environment and environmental sustainability without compelling all of the departments and functionaries to incorporate green behaviors. Thus, human resource management plays a pivotal role towards incorporating green behavior organization wide.  Green human resource management means promoting environmental friendly practices and reducing carbon footprint from HR practices. To help in decreasing the carbon emission, organizations should finance green technology and pollution reducing projects. The present paper aims to highlight the initiatives done by several organizations adopting green human resource practices in Pakistan. Moreover, an effort has been made to show the importance of adopting green human resource practices and employee green behavior. This study aims to find the impact of green recruitment & selection, green training & development, green reward and compensation, green performance management & appraisal and green empowerment on enabling the employee green behavior. Due to which, these activities contribute to environmental sustainability ultimately. 
Data from around 500 employees will be gathered who work at several organizations in service sector all across Pakistan. Results revealed that green HRM practices positively affected the environmental sustainability and employee green behavior mediated this link.

data.projectName: Floating wetlands in combination with microbial consortium : a novel technique to remediate industrial wastewater and sediment/soils
data.projectDigest: Terrestrial and aquatic environments received huge amount of untreated, hazardous or even carcinogenic waste from industries regularly. This waste may accelerate the chemical oxygen demand, biological oxygen demand and total dissolved solids, chloride or sulphate anions, sodium salts, some toxic and hazardous inorganic and organic halogenated compounds in the environment. This effects the microbial activity, plant growth and human health. This slows the process of microbial and plants degradation of contaminants naturally. Physical, mechanical or chemical mode of treatment of such contaminants is laborious and costly. Regulatory authorities are interested to adopt to some economic, rapid and eco-environmentally friendly methods to reclaim the environment. Floating wetlands is a new, novel and emerging technique adopted to reclaim inorganic contaminants from industrial wastewater in Punjab. Nonetheless information about the use of floating wetlands in combination with microbes and nutrients to remove halogenated organic compounds from wastewater, river sediments and soils is in scarcity. This is the first study to reclaim the organic halogenated compounds from wastewater, river sediments and soils using floating wetlands in combination with microbes and nutrients in Peshawar.

data.projectName: Development, Characterization and Validation of Yogurt Starter Culture from Indigenous Sources.
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan is the 4th largest milk producing country throughout the world and its annual milk production is about 59.75 million tons with 170 liters per capita consumption of milk and milk products. Although Pakistan is a big milk producer but only 5-6% of milk is processed on commercial scale and a lot of dairy products are still being imported from different countries of the world.
Yogurt is one of the most common types of fermented dairy products. It is rich source of protein, a variety of fatty acids, minerals and vitamins. It also contain live culture which impart beneficial effect on the consumers. For the virtuous quality and texture of the yogurt the type of the starter culture is very important. The starter culture not only effect the physicochemical properties of the yogurt but also have great influence on processing parameters and cost of production. Traditionally in Pakistan the yogurt is prepared with nonspecific cultures, but for commercial scale production the starter culture is imported from Italy, Denmark, UK and USA which cause a huge amount of cash flow from the country. 
The current project is designed to isolate, identify and characterize the various strains of cultures phenotypically and genotypically from traditional Dahi and Lassi and also to investigate their fermentation behavior and product quality with respect to consumer acceptability. The genotypic characterization will be done by using specific species PCR test. After the isolation, purification of these strains will be done with the help of 16S rRNA and enzymatic characterization. These isolated cultures will be preserved using different techniques like broth culture, glycerol preservation at -20° C, under oil emersion, and lyophilized conditions.

data.projectName: Large scale production of plant  extracts prepared from crop residues to serve as organic fertilizer
data.projectDigest: Crop residues are the largest product of agricultural harvests which contain higher concentrations of nutrients. Their safe environmental disposal require crop residue management practices. With reference to Pakistan farmers adopt various residue management practices which includes the burning of residues after the harvest as well. The crop residue burning is an environmental problem, because it generates black carbon which is now considered a second largest contributor to global warming after carbon dioxide. Black carbon emissions and other types of aerosols also give rise to atmospheric brown clouds (ABCs) in Asia. The aerosols in ABCs decrease the intensity of sunlight reaching the earth’s surface thereby enhancing atmospheric solar heating (Ahmed and Ahmad., 2013). In the present scenario such strategies must be adopted that may help to reduce the burden on environment due to agricultural waste accumulation and harmful emissions. Therefore, the utilization of crop residues in the preparation of nutritionally rich extracts may be a simplest yet effective possible solution to cope up with these problems. The water based plant extracts either in pure form or with certain modification may be applied to the soil as the liquid organic fertilizers in order to increase the fertility and microbial activity of the soil. Though the plant extracts have been mostly evaluated for their growth inhibitory ability however, the preliminary studies carried out in our laboratory has clearly revealed the potential of plant based extracts to possess growth supporting ability for fungi. The comparative lab experiments conducted in the pots also indicate that plant extract formulations helped to support the plant growth by supplying required nutrients.

data.projectName: An A.I. enabled customized gait analysis tool for medical applications
data.projectDigest:
There are a number of pathologies which result in the degradation of the gait pattern such as Stroke, Polio and the Parkinson's disease. Assessment of gait parameters are vital for the diagnosis, treatment and rehabilitation of such patients.
Since the first studies looking at pathological gait solutions in the 1970s, researchers and clinicians were restricted to laboratory conditions (using photogrammetric cameras, EMG, force plates, etc.) to study gait. These involve expensive equipment requiring dedicated lab space and large setup/data acquisition times. While many such laboratories have been established in developed countries of the world, developing countries like Pakistan cannot afford to setup such facilities. There is not a single gait lab in Pakistan, either in clinical or research setting. 
The goal of this project is to develop a set of embedded wearable sensors employing miniature inertial measurement units (IMUs) which should provide valuable feedback about a patient’s gait to the clinicians when attached to various locations of the body. The idea is to enable clinicians to conduct a quantitative rather than qualitative examination of a patient’s gait and be able to diagnose the pathology and monitor the recovery. Such gait data can predict changes in a patient’s health and whether the patient is prone to fall.

data.projectName: Synthesis of Long circulating NSAIDs prodrugs nanoparticles for passive targeting in the treatment of Rheumatoid Arthritis
data.projectDigest:
Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are the most prescribed medications for the treatment of inflammatory conditions, such as arthritis. Undesirable pharmacokinetics of these drugs, such as short half-life, rapid elimination, and increased volume of their distribution, need frequent administration for sustained anti-inflammatory activity causing severe side-effects. Nanocarriers, as delivery vehicles for NSAIDs, can improve NSAIDs pharmacokinetics, and increase their concentrations at inflamed sites. Though several successful nanocarriers have been formulated yet they still suffer from issues, such as limited drug loading and premature burst release, limiting their clinical translation.
The proposed study is designed to synthesize selected NSAIDs (diclofenac, celecoxib, and ibuprofen) prodrugs. Each of these prodrug will be encapsulated into nanoparticles using biocompatible and biodegradable lipids/polymers, e.g., DSPE-PEG2000 methoxy, as colloid stabilizer, to address issues related to limited drug loading and premature release. Designed nanoparticles will be physico-chemically characterized, followed by the evaluation of their cytotoxicity, and in vitro and in vivo anti-inflammatory activity. Our aim is to overcome problems related to NSAIDs, such as their undesirable pharmacokinetics, short half-life, rapid elimination, adverse side effects and increased volume of their distribution causing toxicity. Hence, nanoparticles designed in this project might offer high advantages in terms of pharmacokinetics, bio-distribution and therapeutics.

data.projectName: Development of Smart Aqua gel based Multi Layered Microspheres Technology for Controlled Drug Delivery in Sub-Acute Ruminal Acidosis
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Livestock system contributes to the livelihood and food security of billions of people. Meat and milk are the primary source of protein that can be produced throughout the year. livestock can suffer from various health-related issues, thus decreasing productivity.

Subacute-Ruminal acidosis in the dairy and feed lot sector is an ongoing problem. The economic loss associated with SARA has been reported to be $500 million to $1 billion per year. Various strategies minimize the occurrence of SARA. However, practical implementation is limited because of the challenges related to uncontrolled drug delivery and drug dosing regimens.

This research addresses these issues through the development of an aqua gel based multilayered microsphere technology (AGMMT) for sustained drug delivery. This has not been investigated in SARA. Through this research, we aim to develop and characterize a drug formulation that offers precise spatio-temporal control over the amount of drug delivered; thereby minimizing adverse effects. The developed formulation will be tested through extensive in vitro as well as in vivo testing. This technology development will potentially open up new avenues into treatment options for relevant disease conditions in livestock, thereby curtailing the socio-economic problems caused by the prevalence of sub-acute ruminal acidosis in our country

data.projectName: Application of artificial neural network in assessment and diagnosis of  non-communicable diseases
data.projectDigest: Non-communicable diseases are one of the leading causes of death globally. They include cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, osteoporosis, cancer, stroke, osteoarthritis and chronic respiratory diseases. NCDs contribute 63% of deaths worldwide. Therefore, the early detection of diseases has become the dire need of time. In this project Artificial Neural Network, a type of Artificial Intelligence will be applied for predicting non communicable diseases based on risk factors. Targeted population group will be selected to measure the risk factors such as diet, physical activity, anthropometric measurements, serum biomarkers and clinical symptoms. This data set will be used to assess the onset of diseases via developing computer controlled software commonly associated with intelligent being.

data.projectName: Anti-inflammatory potential of Chamomile flower (Matricaria recutita L.) through Nutraceuticals
data.projectDigest: Inflammatory disorders especially arthritis is one of the chronic diseases that can be controlled, but cannot be cured. One of the most common types of inflammatory arthritis is rheumatoid arthritis (RA) which s is prevailing progressively worldwide and makes a significant fiscal loss. The best way to cope these chronic conditions is through nutritional intervention, by the use of indigenous plant sources which are less toxic and have negligible side effects. Among these plants, utilization of Chamomile as a cheap indigenous nutritious food plants is considered as the best approach towards fighting against diseases. Therefore, the project has been planned for the for the management of inflammatory disorders through nutritional intervention using nutraceuticals as a vehicle which will be prepared by chamomile flowers. It will be prepared using different treatments and evaluated for their qualitative and nutritional profiles, toxicity will be checked on rats and the efficacy trials will be conducted on the arthritis patients. The blood biochemistry will be assessed and safety study on liver and kidney biomarkers will be done to study the impact of nutritional intervention. Moreover, the food industry will also get potential economic benefits by the successful completion of this project by preparing and commercializing nutraceuticals for vulnerable masses of community.

data.projectName: Grant Free Random Access with NOMA and Network Slicing for IoT in 5G and Beyond
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: In near future, million of devices are expected to work as internet of things (IoT). These devices will be connected to the network to send their data to other peer devices or to the internet. This large number naturally puts challenge on existing networks to serve all these devices and specially when these devices try to connect to the network simultaneously. Long term evolution (LTE/LTE-A) has the infrastructure to provide services to IoT in 5G but it also needs to adapt to traffic requirements of IoT as these requirements are different from human to human (H2H) traffic. For 5G, random access process for IoTs is not yet standardized and efforts are being put in to improve its performance. Currently, the random access procedure in LTE/LTE-A depends on four step handshaking. Our project will focus on developing grant free random access procedure with NOMA used as physical layer technique to improve the throughput. It is also necessary to evaluate whether Pakistan is ready for 5G or not and what are the requirements in terms of spectrum for providing satisfactory quality of service (QoS) to the users. This project will also develop strategy to evaluate spectrum requirements for the spectrum. As the spectrum is an important resource, it is necessary to use it optimally. Our project proposes to allocate the spectrum dynamically to each application depending upon the condition of traffic in that particular application.

data.projectName: Nutraceutical Characterization and Storage Stability Assessment of Indigenous Guava (Psidium guajava L.) Cultivars in response to different post-harvest interventions
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Fruits have naturally been recognized as the predominant sources of vitamins, minerals and phytochemicals. They are carrying potential nutraceutical attributes with additional health benefits beside basic nutrition. Amongst fruits, Guava is an important commercial fruit crop specifically known for its significant antioxidant potential. As “poor man’s apple of tropics”, guava truly happens to be the fruit for masses in terms of its commercial availability and offer four times more vitamin-C than citrus. Pharmacological studies proved its antidiarrheal, antidiabetic, antimicrobial, hepatoprotective, anti-allergic, anti-plasmodia, anti-spasmodic, anti-inflammatory activities and found equally effective in cardiovascular disorders. Guava (Psidium guajava L.) ranked third after Citrus and Mango with 0.586 million tons of annual production in Pakistan. Predominant indigenous guava cultivars are Gola, Chota Gola, Ramzani, Surahi, Choti Surahi, Lal Badshah/Apple Guava, Sdabahar, Sufaida, Surkha, Kohati, etc. However, the indigenous guava cultivars have not been characterized properly in terms of their physical, chemical, biochemical and nutraceutical attributes. Therefore, varietal characterizations have significant importance to acquire key scientific data that would be handy in defining the intended use of a specific guava cultivar. Comprehensive characterization will also be helpful for industry specific selection of certain guava cultivars for the development of nutraceutical products. Furthermore, due to climacteric nature of guava fruit, it has limited shelf life i.e. up to three to four days at ambient temperature which results in 40% postharvest losses. Resultantly, it leads to huge economic loss to the farmers, nutrient loss to the consumer and waste disposal issues.

data.projectName: MEASURING THE IMPACT OF MICRO FINANCE ON MICRO ENTERPRISES : COMPARISON OF GOV. AND NON GOV. MISCROFINANCE PROGRAMME IN PAKISTAN
data.projectDigest:
According to World Bank, Asia is home to 1.7 billion (approx. two third of
world’s poor) people living on less than USD 1.2 per day. Despite the
economic growth, poverty in the region is still at large. However, the ways in
which such grinding poverty and entrepreneurial activities impact each other
remains largely unexplored by business scholars.
Over the period of time association of microfinance and entrepreneurship has
been increasingly recognized as a tool for socioeconomic development of
dawdling regions. Firstly, this study seeks to analyze the contribution of the
microfinance programs offered by GOs and NGOs in poverty eradication and
in the development of the dawdling regions.We aim to investigate the impacts
of microfinance programs offered by the GOs and NGOs on the profitability,
sales growth and employment growth of the treatment and control groups, by
controlling for enterprise characteristics, personal characteristics and
community effects and other variables.Secondly,the study also aims to analyze
the performance of the treatment and control groups by segregating them on
the owner’s gender basis and comparing them with the performance of the
reference category i.e. mixed ownership.
The results of the study would be beneficial for the microfinance donors,
practicing organizations and the policy makers.

data.projectName: Nutraceutical Approach for Chemical and Drug Induced Toxic Hepatitis: A New Challenge for Health in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Toxic hepatitis (TH) is threatening the world. It is accelerating through acquired factors including industrial toxicants like carbon tetrachloride (grease removing agent in leather industry), and life-saving medicines like anti-tuberculosis (Anti-TB) drugs that are playing important role in developing oxidative stress that gradually damage liver and induced toxic hepatitis (inflammation, cirrhosis and fibrosis), if ignored. In this modern era there are few not very effective medicines available for liver diseases. Nutraceuticals like food ingredients/ natural products are also enlightening their significance in the treatment of ailments and make their presence felt as pharmaceuticals. Therefore, the research makes to investigate the nutraceutical potential of seeds of Centratherum anthelminticum (bitter cumin) and Avena fatua (wild oat) and fruits of raisins (Vitis vinifera) against Anti-TB drug and carbon tetrachloride induced TH. The research will screen different organic solvents extracts of experimental food ingredients against TH in rat models by evaluating their effects on hematological, liver specific biochemical, molecular and histopathological parameters, then will identify the possible phytochemicals in extracts/fractions through chromatographic techniques, and finally will combine them to find out their synergetic effect against TH in order to make single/multicomponent nutraceutical having liver regenerating ability and patent them. The research is economical as it will upgrading routinely used dietary ingredients from kitchen cabinet to liver regenerative nutraceutical.

data.projectName: Udder microbiome analysis and development of indigenous probiotics for prevention and treatment of bovine mastitis
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Mastitis is one of the most costly diseases affecting dairy animals. Mastitis leads to reduced milk yield and quality, and increased veterinary costs. In current study, we hypothesize that there is difference in the udder microbiota of healthy, sub-clinical mastitic and mastitic animals, and these difference in microbial diversity may help us in selection of efficient probiotics for the control and treatment of mastitis. We will determine teat microbiota diversity of mastitic, subclinical mastitic and healthy bovine by meta-genomic approaches. We will also determine the etiology of mastitis and their antibiotic resistance pattern. Furthermore, on the basis of comparative teat microbial diversity, we will isolate, screen and select probiotic bacteria i.e lactobacilli from healthy buffalo and cattle. Potential probiotics will be characterized in-vitro by their ability to inhibit the MCM in broth culture as well as their ability to inhibit and competitively exclude the MCM in mammary epithelial cells. Potential probiotics inhibiting the MCM will be used to further in-vivo evaluation. Probiotics will be injected intramammary in animals having sub clinical mastitis and their effect on mastitis development and teat microbial diversity will be determined by molecular approaches.

data.projectName: Photoinhibition of leishmanial parasites in the presence of Zinc Oxide activated by Amphotericin B bound Ag doped metal Oxides (ZnO-Ag@MO) nanofibers: A view towards nanomedication
data.projectDigest:
Nanotechnology has got much interest among the research due to its high applications in almost all the fields. Silver, ZnO and TiO2 etc has got a proper position due to its toxic effect on almost all parasites. The nanoparticles of these metals are cheap, low toxic and highly efficient. Literatures shows that Silver, ZnO and TiO2 nanoparticles are recently used as an antileishmanial agents. The activity of these nanomaterials against leishmanial parasites was satisfactory.
Keep it in mind the antileishmanial efficiency of Ag, ZnO and TiO2 etc, they will be combined by new hydrothermal method to get ZnO-Ag@MO (MO= metal oxide). With the help of this method, the MO shells will be uniformly coated on the ZnO surface to form core-shell structure and the silver will be incorporated in the MO shells. To further increase the antileishmanial efficiency of the said nanomaterials, the antileishmanial drug Amphotericin B (Amp B) will be coated. The anti-leishmanial efficiency of the prepared nanomaterials will be examined both in light and dark. These nanomaterials will destroy ATP of cell via oxidative stress caused by the production of reactive oxygen species especially under UV and visible light irradiataion. Moreover the surface characteristics of nanoparticles and nanocomposites (i.e. their controlled size and shape) also provide the enhanced specificity, bioavailability, solubility and increased efficiency. The synthesized nanomaterials will be more favorable for the external leishmanial infection because it is directly expose to light and the ROS will be easily produced on exposure to sunlight. The production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) will also be examined by using different scavengers.

To further increase the antileishmanial efficiency of the said nanomaterials, the antileishmanial drug Amphotericin B (Amp B) will be coated. The anti-leishmanial efficiency of the prepared nanomaterials will be examined both in light and dark. These nanomaterials will destroy ATP of cell via oxidative stress caused by the production of reactive oxygen species especially under UV and visible light irradiataion. Moreover the surface characteristics of nanoparticles and nanocomposites (i.e. their controlled size and shape) also provide the enhanced specificity, bioavailability, solubility and increased efficiency. The synthesized nanomaterials will be more favorable for the external leishmanial infection because it is directly expose to light and the ROS will be easily produced on exposure to sunlight. The production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) will also be examined by using different scavengers.

data.projectName: Development of thermoelectric materials for renewable energy applications.
data.projectDigest:
Since the last decade remarkable growing interests is observed in thermoelectric materials for energy conversion applications. One of the major motivations for recent importance is the need for safe, clean, and sustainable energy source. Currently, the world is facing various challenges concerning energy supply and demand. Overall, the need for oil is persistently increasing and oil prices also getting much higher. Moreover, about 57.8% of the total produced energy in 2009 in the USA was wasted into the atmosphere, the majority being from power plants, transportation and manufacturing industries. For any thermoelectric material, potential difference / heat can be converted or used to generate cooling / electricity based on the Peltier and Seebeck effects. Ever since the dawn of modern science and semiconductor physics, thermoelectric materials have been used in government as well as commercial applications. 
In this project we will synthesize different thermoelectric materials including oxides, Bismuth Telluride and half-Heuslers. Different methods i.e. sol-gel, co-precipitation, induction melting and arc-melting synthesis method will be employed for the synthesis of materials. Suitable dopants will be tested for optimum performance of the materials. Selected high performance thermoelectric materials will be embedded in soft matrix (polymer networks) like polyaniline (PANI) or polyvinyl alcohol to make flexible thermoelectric materials. In the third phase, the purity, morphology, Seebeck coefficient, electrical conductivity and thermal conductivity of the sintered (densified) will be measured. Efforts will be made to achieve high performance thermoelectric materials and to decouple the thermoelectric parameters.

data.projectName: A Transgene and Chemical-pesticide Free Approach for Control of Sucking Pest Complex Based on Double-stranded RNA Stabilized through Nanomaterials
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: Cotton is among the most valuable crops in the world. Whitefly (responsible of CLCuD), Aphid, jassid and mealybug are among the top devastating insect pests of cotton causing reduction of cotton yield in Pakistan. The current approaches to manage pests and diseases rely on plant genetic resistance and/or transgenes coupled with pesticides sprays while many pesticides applied are harmful to humans and environment. One of the most promising novel pest control strategies is exploiting the RNA interference (RNAi) mechanism to target essential genes for knockdown and incite toxic effects in the target species without harming non-target organisms. Topical application of double standard RNA (dsRNA) as a biopesticide for control of insect-pests and viruses is emerging as an attractive and ecofriendly approach. Topical application of dsRNA showed efficient penetration and proficient silencing in aphid and mealybug. The dsRNA loaded on non-toxic layered double hydroxide (LDH) clay nanosheets, Chitosan and carbon quantum dot (CQD) have shown efficient protection against rice striped stem borer by stabilizing and enhancing cellular uptake ability of dsRNA. Through the proposed research work we will develop dsRNA loaded on three types of nanomaterials (LDH, CQDs and Chitosan) for effective control of whitefly (ecdysone) and aphids (cathepsin) in cotton.

data.projectName: SYNTHESIS OF LIPID BASED NANO-PARTICLES OF LEFLUNOMIDE METAL COMPLEXES: A BETTER STEP TO TREAT RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS AND ITS ASSOCIATED DEPRESSION
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Use of new technologies in the field of medicine usually has a positive influence to improve overall health system in the world. Among various technologies, synthesis of nanoparticles in the drug delivery system has a great impact which improves number of drug qualities as its absorption, potency, efficacy, resistance to degradation of the loaded medicine .
Rheumatoid arthritis  is an autoimmune disorder in which patients not only suffer from joint misery but also face its associated depression. Leflunomide  is a leading drug among DMARDs to treat RA. It acts by modifying the inflammatory processes, particularly in RA. But it produces some serious side effect because of its systemic toxicity as hepatotoxicity, allergic reactions, anxiety and depression etc . These side effects are mainly due to its systemic bioavailability. A site specific delivery of the drug can reduce these systemic side effects. Lymphatic system, which plays a great role in the pathogenesis of RA, is considered to be one of the effective delivery sites for the treatment of RA . 
In our previous work, we highlight that leflunomide activity is altered after its metal complexes synthesis in acute arthritic model . Now by making lipid base nanoparticles of leflunomide and its metal complexes the goal of this research is to decreased systemic toxicity. Thus the systemic and unwanted side effects can be avoided which improves overall therapeutic index of these complexes.

data.projectName: Dendroclimatic Reconstruction and resiliency of conifer forests growing in  high altitude region of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Climate change and its related phenomenon have an adverse impact on the forest ecosystem, food security, water resources, and related live hood. Northern Pakistan is characterized by Hindukush-Karakorum-Himalayan (KHHK) regions with different altitudinal zonation of climate. In recent decades, the northern Pakistan also experiencing climate change which has noteworthy impact on water resource, social and economic growth. Prior to current few dendroclimatic reconstruction studies has been carried out in this region, which mainly focused on glacier and temperature. Although, these studies provided some useful information. However, these were limited to single site or valley and did not cover the overall northern area of Pakistan. Further, in the prior studies little attention were paid to find out the key driver factors of climatic change in the region. Therefore, knowledge of long-term climate variability using the natural tree-ring proxy, focusing on various species and sites are crucial from this region. Beside this, climate change has significant influence on function and structure of forest ecosystem and possess essential role in forest health, which did not explore yet. We will sample Takht-e-Sulaiman region and teleconnection analysis of tree-ring data with see surface temperature and northern area Pakistan climate to draw a clear picture. This study will enhance our understanding of key driving climatic factor, which lead to climatic change and influence of climatic change on forest ecosystem and health.

data.projectName: Enhancing Profitability of Agriculture Farm(s) by Promoting Energy Efficient Measures in Agriculture Sector of Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
There are about one million agriculture tube wells in Punjab, majority (85%) have engine /motor size less than 20 HP. The quality of locally manufactured pumps is not at par with international standards. The imported pumps are costly and but consume less energy. There is no government regulatory body in Punjab which may check and certify the quality of locally manufactured tube well components. The farmers need technical guidance by the qualified engineers for the selection and installation of energy efficient tube wells as well as training for efficient operation of the pumps [4, 5].
 
The operational cost of one million tube wells is about Rs.160 billion per annum and this can be reduced by 30%-40%, using energy efficient pumps. According to Agriculture Department Study [4], a survey of 110 tube wells in Faisalabad region (2015) revealed majority had in-efficient pumps which consume more energy. The energy consumption efficiency of surveyed tube wells was 31% only which could be increased to 75%, hence loss of 40% electrical energy was observed.  69% of the surveyed tube wells were found to have improper size of motor and pump [4]. The survey concluded the reasons for poor efficiency of pumps including improper design and use of high rated power equipment; low quality and aging equipment; poor transmission efficiency; inadequate knowledge for efficient operation and management of tube wells.
The prevailing energy crisis in Pakistan has adversely affected the productivity of agriculture sector; its growth declined to 3%-4% per annum [1]. Oil and electricity are the main sources of energy consumed in on-farm activities [2] i.e. operation of tube wells and tractors. Currently, the consumption of commercial energy is 1.5% of the total energy [2].

data.projectName: Fractional Calculus Operators based-filters for Signal and Control Processing
data.projectDigest: Applications of fractional calculus to several problems was developed corresponding to theoretical beginnings. Firstly invention was made by Abel (1823, 1825) by using solution of integral equation via an integral transform. The Boole (1844) principle used as a power series of an arbitrary function f (D) which is formal expansion of differential operator and solution of differential equations by formal inversion. Oustaloup introduced first fractional-order (FO) controller in 1988 . Shen introduced the occurrence of Duffing oscillator with fractional order derivative. Fractional calculus is becoming abundant in various fields of science and engineering such as signal processing control applications, fractional diffusion equations and biomedical submissions. By using the applications of fractional calculus this project suggests a widespread scheme and operation of fractional- order system to custom of electronic circuits that may be used for signal processing and control engineering submissions. From history of fractional calculus and mathematical definitions we start the project. In the second part of project we explain fractional-order differential equations and schemes. Elaboration of some papers associated to this extent circuit design examples and submission are discussed. Final part of project offers feasible research topics related to the area.

data.projectName: Anticancer Effect of De Novo Designed and Synthesized Peptides in In Vitro And In Vivo Hepatocellular Carcinoma Mouse Model
data.projectDigest: Among different types of cancer, Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) boasts high prevalence. However, therapeutic options are limited on account of late detection and scarcity of adequate chemotherapeutic measures. Currently pharmacological strategy is VEGFR/PDGFR-receptor targeting, which is essential growth marker for this cancer. Proposed research capitalizes on the current body of evidence, exploiting intracellular tyrosine kinase (TK) domain of the receptor. Instead of using a chemical agent, the objective is to synthesize a small peptide that can block the TK domain. Peptide will be designed using in silico techniques. Synthesized peptides will be evaluated for their anticancer effect in both HCC cell lines and induced HCC mouse model. In vitro anti-tumor effect will be ascertained through cell viability and apoptosis assays. After positive confirmation through in vitro assays, selected peptides will be utilized in in vivo induced HCC mouse model coupled with during-treatment survival assays and post-treatment change in harvested tumor sizes. Both treated cell lines and mice HCC tissue will be subjected to functional genomics studies, which will entail expression profiling of VEGR2 signaling molecules/intermediates and cellular apoptotic markers through qPCR. Similarly, the effect will be further elucidated at protein level using Western immunoblotting of TK and apoptotic markers.
