data.projectName: Strategic flood risk management by integrated hydro-geomorphological approach for mountainous catchments in Upper Indus Basin Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The evaluation of basin characteristics from the hydro-geomorphometric parameters helps in understanding the physical behaviour of the catchments with respect to floods. Geomorphological hazard assessment is an important component of natural hazard risk assessment especially floods hazard assessment and mass wasting potential. The aim of this study is to estimate the hydro-geomorphometric characteristics and then examine their significant impact/response on the flood risk potential in different mountainous watersheds of Upper Indus Basin (UIB), Pakistan, with integrated use of remote sensing and GIS environment, which could be used for the integrated watershed management. The basic geomorphologic characteristics will be carried out using the standard mathematical formulae. Two methods will be employed to assess flash floods and to generate flooding risk susceptibility maps. The first method is El-Shamy’s approach, and the second is the morphometric hazard degree assessment method. Consequently, sub-basins with high and extreme flooding susceptibility will be demarcated and displayed spatially using GIS. Furthermore, a strategic framework (sustainable and integrated management strategy) will be developed for flood risk management. The maps so will be produced will to help planners and decision makers to devise appropriate plans to mitigate harmful flooding impacts, and to deal with flooding hazards.

data.projectName: OBESITY AND OXIDATIVE STRESS BIOMARKERS AMONG YOUNG ADULT OVER WEIGHT AND OBESE FEMALES
data.projectDigest:
Prevalence of obesity among people around the world, especially in teens and young adults, has been increasing day by day. Studies showed that rate of obesity have doubled since 1980 in not only high-income countries but also in other socio-demographic levels. Obesity is such a condition in which a person is packed with excess amount of body fat such that it results in negative impact on life. 
The study is design to obtain the occurrence of overweight and obesity in association with body mass index (BMI) according to WHO classification in young adult females. A self-completed questionnaire is prepare to gather information, including age, height, weight, and socioeconomic position. Anthropometric indices/ measurements, Biochemical and oxidative stress biomarkers analysis are performed according to standard laboratory procedures. The Statistical Package for Social Sciences software is used for statistical analyses. 
The proposed project helps to estimate the prevalence and possible number of individual at risk of health problems and develop approaches in prevention and control of obesity at national level. Height and weight measurements (BMI) are simple and low-cost method of health examinations.

data.projectName: Discovery of antiviral agents to inhibit Foot-and-Mouth Disease Virus replication
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest:
Foot-and-mouth virus (FMD) infection is highly contagious and economically devastating disease of cloven-hoofed animals. In Pakistan, ~50% of the animals are exposed to FMD virus during their life cycle and country suffered a loss of Rs. 8-9 billion/annum and country cannot export meat and dairy products. To control the disease there are two strategies existed, “test and slaughter” and/or “vaccination and treatment”. But Pakistan could not adapt slaughtering approach due to heavy cost. The only options left are prevention and treatment of FMDV. Currently, inactivated trivalent vaccines (O, A, Asia 1) are being practiced in FMD eradication programs in Pakistan. data.projectName: Design, synthesis and biological evaluation of chromone-Cyclic imide hybrid molecules as anticancer and anti-inflammatory agents
data.projectDigest: Cancer is the deadliest disease all over the world which kills million of peoples every year. Currently available anticancer agents are associated with numerous side effects some of which are life-threatening. Similarly, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agents (NSAIDs) are widely prescribed medicines but are linked with problems of gastrointestinal tract (GIT) toxicity. Therefore the discovery of new anticancer and anti-inflammatory agents is of paramount importance. The project has been designed to synthesize new hybrid drug molecules comprising the structural features of chromone and cyclic imides. In the new drug discovery, the hybrid molecular strategy is becoming popular in which two biologically active molecules are tethered with each other to produce new molecules with interesting pharmacological properties. Chromone is an important molecule originally from natural sources and possesses diverse pharmacological activities such as anticancer, anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial. Cyclic imides are also a large and important class of heterocyclic organic compounds and possess antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties. Therefore, these two moieties are important scaffold and have drawn the attention of organic and medicinal chemists for the synthesis of new drugs. The combination of these two scaffolds can lead to the synthesis of new drug molecules with better pharmacological properties.

data.projectName: Preparation of Dressings Coated with Growth Factors/Cytokines Loaded Hydrogel for Faster Diabetic/Chronic Wound Healing
data.piUniversity: Mirpur University of Science and Technology (MUST), AJ&K
data.projectDigest: Diabetes is one of the fastest growing diseases in Pakistan and around the world that is linked to the highest numbers of mortalities. About 11% Pakistani between the ages of 20 and 79 suffered from diabetes and this number is estimated to become double by 2030. Non-healing wounds caused by diabetes leads to increased healthcare cost, decreased quality of life, amputations and death. The wide prevalence of diabetes and its projected increase in the near future has further necessitated a need for therapeutics aimed at enhancing the healing of diabetic wounds. Decreased growth factor production and blood vessel formation in diabetes are responsible for the impaired wound healing. The latter process is impaired due to a deficiency of angiogenic growth factors and reduced endothelial progenitor cell (EPC) recruitment. Recent strategy is to use the skin substitutes but the success of this technique has been limited by high cost, short lifespan and safety concerns for using allogenic cells. Furthermore, there is little control over the biochemical and mechanical properties of these therapeutic products. The goal of our proposal is to engineer a novel, bioactive angiogenic dressing coated with nanoparticles and Growth factors loaded hydrogels to enhance wound healing in diabetic conditions.

data.projectName: Quality evaluation of available baked snacks and other fried food products for acrylamide produced during open and uncontrolled processing and development of an innovative acrylamide free business process, a milestone to food safety and good health.
data.projectDigest: The project will be divided into 3 steps. In the first step, the objective of will be to carry out comparative analysis of acrylamide present in openly processed 20-25 each baked snacks and fried food products. After collecting the food products from various corners of Sialkot city and preliminary preparation, the samples will be analysed for acrylamide already present in these products, by using HPLC technique. In the second step, an acrylamide free business process will be developed in laboratory to prepare safe-to-health baked snacks and fried products. After treating the dough or mix of each product with the already set appropriate dose of asparaginase enzyme starter, the mix of enzyme-product-mixture will be kept at 40-42oC for 45 min to hydrolyse the asparagine present in dough/ mix. After processing accordingly, the prepared samples will be analysed for acryl amide contents with the HPLC technique, to ensure content validation. For effect validation, biological study will be carried on albino rats after feeding each food sample (5 rats in each set), collected from market and also prepared in laboratory, for 15 days. The blood of each rat will be analysed after 5 days interval during this period for hemoglobin as a biomarker. The claim validation will then be ensured after statistical analysis of the results obtained. In the last step, the outcomes of this research studies will then be disseminated to academia and students of 50 public and private schools and colleges each, during the 2nd and 3rd years of study, to make them aware to use the safe and quality food products.

data.projectName: Interconnecting multifunctional apatite nanoparticles by egg white proteins to build a biomimetic moldable grafts for dental and bone tissue engineering
data.projectDigest:
Bone is the most common transplanted tissue after blood. Efficiency of materials produced by nature is still un-matchable when compared with their synthetic counterpart. Innovative grafts can be designed by mimicking the nature. Bone contains about 70% apatite arranged in protein matrix that maintains its hierarchical structure and performance. Natural apatite is substituted with many ions that regulate its biological function. 
There are two main objectives of this proposed research, (1) to improve the biological performance of synthetic hydroxyapatite (HA). It will be achieved functionalization of HA surface with amino acids and substitution of its lattice with borate and zinc. The former will optimize its surface charge, surface properties and later will install angiogenic and antibacterial properties Angiogenesis provides oxygen and nutrition to developing tissue. Infections is common reason that delayed healing and lead to implant failure. (2) To synthesize biologically active, mechanically stable and easy to use grafts which are easily filled irregular defected sites of injured bones by minimal invasive way. Biologically active, biocompatible, economical proteins - the egg white (EW) - will be used for this purpose. EW and functionalized HA will be connected by using primary amine-based crosslinker, crosslinker will be helpful to establish good interconnectivity and required mechanical strength. After that to achieve desire handling capacity some additives such as polyethylene oxide and glycerol will be used. The in vitro study will be performed to evaluate biological performance. Proof of concept study of easier surgical handling will be evaluated by using the in vitro protocols.

data.projectName: Application of Organic Amendments to Mitigate Agricultral Threats and Remediate Heavy Metals Contamination in Food Chain
data.projectDigest: Rapid increase in the world population, industrialization, modern agricultural practices and improper environmental planning are key factors responsible for discharge of wastewater and shortage of quality water resources. To cope up with this problem, wastewater irrigation is an alternative in agricultural activities. Wastewater consists of various types of contaminants including heavy metals, and metalloids. Long term irrigation with wastewater to the agricultural plants contaminates agricultural soils with heavy metals. The heavy metals contaminated soils transfer the contaminants to food crops, animals and humans. These contaminants pose serious threat to the human and animal health and environment. A large number of remediation techniques for agricultural soils are in practice among which use of biochar is a valuable and environment friendly technique.  Biochar is a carbon rich compound, made from organic waste through pyrolysis at different temperatures. It is a soil conditioner, pollutant absorber (removes heavy metal and other inorganic and organic pollutants) from wastewater and soil. Moreover, agricultural soils lack essential elements and can adversely affect plant growth and human health. Parthenium is a common weed silently spreading in agricultural and non-agricultural fields of Pakistan damaging agricultural productivity, causing various animal and human health problems.Parthenium feedstock-based biochar preparation and its use in heavy metal contaminated soil can induce triple effect, i.e. removal of Parthenium threat from agricultural fields, remediating polluted soil and improving soil productivity. Furthermore, the large surface area made biochar useful for carbon sequestration is a result its application to agricultural soils combat climate change.

data.projectName: Evaluation of wheat derived benzoxazinones as alternative to antibiotics in Salmonella typhimurium and Clostridium perferingens infection in broiler chickens
data.projectDigest:
Microbial diseases are the major constraints in achieving food security. Largely, microbial diseases in poultry are treated with indiscriminate use of broad spectrum antibiotics. Exorbitant use of these chemicals are associated with a number of negative effects such as antimicrobial resistance, environmental hazards, and antibiotics residues in meat and eggs in addition to the growing cost of these agents. Salmonella typhimurium and Clostridium perferingens are some of the deadliest diseases and causing huge economic losses in poultry sector through stunt growth and huge mortality. Most often the diseases are prevented through the use of broad spectrum antibiotics, however, the use of antibiotics in poultry is being banned throughout the world. Therefore, there is a need of finding suitable alternatives.  
The benzoxazinones (BXs) also known as hydroximic acids are derived from wheat, maize and rye with broad antibacterial activities. The compound has not been tested in poultry diseases as safe, natural, cheap and with no side effects. The aim of the project is to screen wheat varieties in Pakistan for the isolation of BXs from the different parts and that variety with the highest activity will be tested for the antibacterial activity against Salmonella typhimurium and Clostridium perferingens in broiler in experimentally induced cases. The outcome product will be distributed among poultry farmers to control the disease. This project will provide a novel, safe and alternative solution to control pathogenic diseases.

data.projectName: Public Opinion Manipulation Detection for Pakistani Twitter Users
data.projectDigest: In this project, we aim to develop algorithms to detect political bots for Pakistani Twitter users tweeting political content in English and Urdu. In addition, we will study the correlation between political bots to identify the political bot squads. Also, the algorithms will  be developed to classify the political content from Twitter data. To help the political entities, we will further analyze users to identify the political influencers with high impact on users of Pakistani Twitter community.  This research will help the government, political parties, and members to identify users responsible for misinformation and defamation on Twitter platform. Moreover, our research project will help political entities in selection of influencers with potential impact to run political campaigns. Furthermore, we will develop a labelled dataset of 15,000 political tweets posted by human and bot users to  provide new opportunities to the research community.

data.projectName: Development of Specialized Hybrid Electrode Materials for Long Lasting Sodium Ion Batteries
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Renewable energy resources like solar and wind technology could be the ultimate solution of our country’s prevailing energy crises. Energy storage devices (i.e. batteries) are an indispensable unit of this technology for continuous provision of power specially in off-timings of solar and wind farms. Currently, lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are being used world-wide for energy storage. However, LIBs are neither economical nor sustainable for large scale grid applications such as solar or wind energy farms. Hence, development of a low-cost alternative energy storage system could be a game-changer in renewable energy technology. In this context, this project will focus on basic, as well as applied research for the development of sodium ion batteries (SIBs) as a competent alternate to LIBs owing to low cost, extensive abundance and wide availability of sodium in world. This project will be the first of its kind in Pakistan and surely open up paths for successful development of SIBs locally. As basic research will be conducted from scratch, several patents and research articles are expected to be the major achievement. However, a close collaboration with industry, will also ensure the commercialization of this technology.

data.projectName: Dynamics of Nonlinear Chaotic Models with Memory: Circuit, Simulations and Cryptography (DNCMM: CSC)
data.projectDigest: Chaos is an interesting phenomenon that often happens in various fields, e.g., finance, physics, psychology, ecology, etc. Especially, chaos property randomness, have been proved to be suitable for designing the means for data protection. Chaos-based cryptography is a new research field across two fields, i.e., chaos (nonlinear dynamic system) and cryptography (computer and data security). To access the latest research related to chaos applications in cryptography, we want to start this project. During the past decade, many chaos-based cryptographic techniques have been studied, such as the chaos-based secret communication, chaos-based random number generation, chaos-based hash, etc. Additionally, some secure applications based on chaos have been investigated, e.g., chaos-based image, video/audio scrambling, etc. The primary objective of this project is to assemble as much research coverage as possible related to the field by defining the latest innovative technologies and providing the most comprehensive list of research references. Furthermore, the contributions included in this project will be instrumental in the expansion of the body of knowledge in this field. It is our sincere hope that this project and its great amount of information and research will assist our all faculties, students, and user makers in enhancing their understanding of this research field.

data.projectName: humidity and temperature sensors for environmental monitoring
data.projectDigest: In this proposed project the PI and collaborators will synthesize the metal sulfides/oxides nanoparticles and micro-scale materials. The structural confirmation of materials will be carried using XRD, SEM, TEM, techniques and the surface morphology of the materials will be studied which plays very sumptuous role in the sensing mechanism. EDX, FTIR analyses will be done for elemental confirmation. UV-Vis spectroscopy analysis will be utilized to find the energy gap of the materials used in the fabrication of the proposed sensors. The role of energy gap is very crucial in the transportation of charges and electrical properties of the materials. The energy gap of the materials will tuned via doping and the role of the dopants and composite materials will be checked in the structural and energy gap tuning. The synthesized materials will be then used in the fabrication of capacitive and resistive sensors. Interdigitated electrodes will be employed for this purpose. The proposed fabricated sensors will tested for different humidity levels and temperature. The response/ recovery time of the sensors will be measured and the effect of applied frequencies will checked on the performance of the proposed sensors. Hysteresis losses, linearity, sensitivity, repeatability, and stability will be measured and calculated for the proposed sensors. The sensing mechanism of the proposed sensors will be carefully examined and evaluated and the physics and chemistry of the sensing properties will be discussed on the basis of structural analyses of the materials used in the fabrication of the proposed sensors. The acquired data will be compared with the reported data in the literature and will be sent to international impact journals of repute.

data.projectName: Improving productivity and nitrogen use efficiency of cotton by adopting best management practices
data.projectDigest: Cotton is a major cash crop in Pakistan. Stagnant yields during the past decade forced the cotton growers to increase inputs particularly nitrogen (N) fertilizers. Resultantly, profit margins and area under cotton cultivation are rapidly decreasing. Pakistan uses highest N application rates (202 kg N ha-1) for cotton among the cotton producing countries which along with low mean yields results in lowest nitrogen use efficiencies (NUE) and highest nitrogen surplus. N use in cotton has already reached to the level of diminishing returns. Overuse of N fertilizers not only reduces the farm profits but also contributes to environmental pollution. Probable causes for N overuse could include no/ less use of potash fertilizers, poor application methods, and use of less efficient cultivars etc. Therefore, main aim of the current project is to increase cotton yields with improved NUE by adopting modern agronomic practices. During the three-year project, field trials will be conducted to find out optimum doses of nitrogen and potassium fertilizers, best application method and timing for nitrogen and potassium. Additionally, genotypic variation for nitrogen use efficiency will also be explored among high yielding Bt cotton cultivars.

data.projectName: Ultra sensitive and selective sensor for methane gas based on noble metal decorated metal oxide spheroids
data.projectDigest: Methane is an odorless, colorless and inflammable gas. It is a major constituent of natural gas which is widely used as fuel in houses and industries. The combustibility of natural gas is due to the presence of methane. The leakage of natural gas causes fire and explosion which results in huge loss of lives and economy. These losses can be avoided by timely detection and monitoring of the gas leakage. The present work deals with the synthesis of noble metal decorated metal oxide based gas sensing materials which can be used for the sensitive detection of the gas at room temperature. Currently, various smoke and temperature based sensors are used for this purpose. However, the goal of the proposed work is to synthesize a material which can respond to the target gas before any fire or other damages. Similarly, the sensor will also be make selective towards methane gas as the response of most of the reported gas sensors is interfered by the ambient humidity. After characterizing for various properties through high-tech sophisticated instruments, the materials will be fabricated for gas sensing studies and the gas sensing performance will be checked for methane and other possible interfering gases.

data.projectName: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning to Develop Smart Mathematical Model for Lubrication of Engineering Application using Bio-based Green Lubricants Enriched with Nanoparticles
data.projectDigest: Machine elements are used in numerous engineering applications. These machine elements include, but not limited to, bearing, cam-followers, piston and plungers, and bushes. A large amount of energy is lost in surface-to-surface interaction in said machine elements. For instance, 14% of global prime energy from all of the resources is used in road vehicles. Most of this energy input to the vehicle is lost in parasitic machine elements even after adopting friction-preventive measures including lubrication. Moreover, lubricants used in the machine elements are fossil-based which are environmental hazards. Improper disposing of these lubricants raises severe environmental concerns and serious illnesses including deadly diseases. Therefore, there is a dire need to develop green lubricants that can lower friction better than fossil-based lubricants and are friendly toward the environment and echo-system. Bio-based lubricating oils, also known as green lubricants, driven from the non-fossil resource are one of the alternatives. Nanoparticles have shown anti-wear anti-corrosive behaviors in addition to improving thermal and frictional responses when blended in green lubricants. However, there is no mathematical model is available to predict responses of bio-based nanoparticle enriched lubricant oil. This is because of the complex physical phenomenon involved in the nanoparticle-based reduction in friction and wear. Artificial intelligence (AI) has been shown to predict behaviors of complex multiphysics phenomena. Therefore, AI and machine learning will be used in this project to develop a model to predict tribological performances of bio-based lubricants blended with nanoparticles.

data.projectName: Isolation, identification, molecular characterization and surveillance studies of dengue Virus in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Dengue virus infections are prevalent in world and many episodes of outbreaks have been occurred in Pakistan in past decades. DENV infections need to be addressed continuously and surveillance studies are needed for reduction and elimination of DENV infections. Unfortunately, in Pakistan research on viruses in general and DENV sepecifically is in its initial stages. there is a need to establish a systematic mechanism of surveillance of DENV infection. This project will provide a platform for continuous monitoring of DENV infections.  In addition to surveillance, synthetic substances and botanical extracts assessment against DENV will be carried out, which in case of positive findings will be source of additional export material helping in raising the economy of the Pakistan.

data.projectName: Design and Development of Novel OAM Transmitarrays to Generate and Multiplex Orthogonal Twisted Beams for 5G Communication
data.projectDigest:
It is recently explored that an electromagnetic beam can be used to multiplex several orthogonal orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes to significantly improve the spectral efficiency that makes it suitable for 5G communication. OAM may increase the capacity without using traditional access techniques such as frequency, time and code. 
Various approaches had been proposed so far to produce the OAM beam that includes spiral phase plate, holograms generated by computer, microstrip antenna arrays, reflectarrays and transmitarrays. The transmitarray has become popular option to generate OAM beam due to its advantage of no feed blockage and high radiation efficiency. However, multilayer structure to realize 360° phase range and higher profile of transmitarray are still big issues to be solved. So, the broader objective of this research is to scientifically investigate and develop novel low profile and highly efficient transmitarray.
The team for the development of the proposed project is carefully selected; all the team members have enough technical expertise in the field and capability to complete the project successfully.  It includes, Dr. Abdul Aziz (PI from IUB), Dr. Qasim Mehmood (Co-PI from ITU), Dr. Asjad Amin (Co-Pi from IUB) and Dr. Hammad Cheema (Collaborator from NUST).

data.projectName: Wireless indoor communication through Integration of visible light and power line communication systems
data.projectDigest: A big problem being faced by current wireless communication systems is the scarcity of available spectrum for data communication. Different methods, including frequency repetition and re-usage, have been used to solve this constraint, but these techniques have their own problems of introducing interference in neighboring electromagnetic signals. Emerging technologies such as power-line communication (PLC) and visible light communication (VLC) as well as their merger for different applications are viable solutions to especially improve indoor wireless connectivity. The purpose of this research is to explore the integration techniques for PLC and VLC as well as to develop heterogeneous indoor channel models for VLC to provide solutions for overcoming the problems associated with RF communication cost-effectively by exploiting the existing infrastructure. For our prevailing situation of energy crisis, the proposed project will be helpful in developing models for delivering both illuminance as well as data communication efficiently and without requiring extra infrastructure. Further, PLC is documented in vision 2020 of PTA to be a vital technology for deployment in Pakistan in ten years. Being innovative and a very lesser explored field, the developed and tested models/techniques for PLC-VLC integration will be helpful for future researchers and to solve our energy problems.

data.projectDigest: Waste to Energy (WtE) technologies offer attractive option to solve not only the pressing waste disposal problems but several other challenges simultaneously such as greenhouse gas emissions from inappropriate waste disposal, shortages in power generation and limited space for landfills. Hence, WtE technologies have come across a success in developed as well as in developing countries. The scope of the term WtE is very wide, consisting of a range of technologies of different scales and complexity. WtE can not only reduce the significant amount solid waste but can also produce useful electricity from MSW. Presently, in most cities there is no mechanism in place for the safe disposal of solid waste at dumping sites. Un-controlled open dumping of MSW is a serious threat to the environment as it releases methane gas and mix with the ambient air. Emission of methane gas from MSW into open environment is extremely potent as compared to SOx & NOx. In addition, untreated leachate from wet MSW make under-ground water contaminated which is unfit for drinking water purposes

data.projectName: Epidemiologico-molecular characterization of abortifacient protozoan (Neospora caninum) in dairy cattle and buffalo herds with  its economic implications
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Neospora (N.) caninum is one of the major protozoal pathogens causing abortions and productive losses in bovine. Bovine abortion, is a crucial impediment in profitable dairy farming desisting farmers from exploiting true productive potential of animals exaggertaed by collateral losses. This study will be executed in richly populated dairy area (with cattle >4.7 and buffalo > 6.9 million heads) of Jhang (Punjab) to determine epidemiological and molecular characterization of pathogen in breeding cows and buffaloes along with its economic implications to dairy owners. Study animals (n=450 Cattle; n=450 Buffalo) will comprise adult bovine raised at selected farms. Randomized and repeated blood sampling will be undertaken for serological screening and tracking epidemiological dynamics of N. caninum using Enzyme linked Immunosorbant Assay in pregnant and non-pregnant animals at different stages. Seropositive animals with and without abortions and aborted fetuses will be confirmed for prevalent N. caninum strain using polymerase chain reaction and phylogenetic analysis. During second phase, direct (still birth, abortion etc.) and indirect (rebreeding, labour, veterinary services costs etc.) losses will be evaluated statistically to appraise the financial implications of neosporosis. The study is expected to update the economic scenario of this significant disease in breeding dairy animals for dairy enetrpreneurs.

data.projectName: Practices and Challenges towards Women Political Participation in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Historically, involvement of female in politics and their part in making political decision appears to be nominal even though women possess half of the population across the globe. The previous body of knowledge illustrates that women face obstacles in their practice of political participation that might be linked with the perceived notions of patriarchy, gender stereotypes and the lack of decision-making power among women. data.projectName: Clinical Studies on Bacterial Cellulose Based Advanced Therapeutic Wound Dressing Products on Burn Patients: Translating Basic Science into Applied Research
data.projectDigest: Burns are among the most devastating of all injuries, having high prevalence rate in developing countries including Pakistan. It is the leading cause of deaths and disabilities worldwide. In Pakistan, use of conventional treatment methods, lack of basic health care facilities, inadequate staff, and overburdened burn units further worsens the situation. The traditional guaze bandages are widely used for covering the burnt area. These guaze dressings do not possess inherited antimicrobial and wound healing properties. The main objective of the current study is to develop bacterial cellulose based advanced therapeutic wound dressing products for burn patients. It is also aimed to translate the findings of our basic research into clinical settings through collaboration with surgeons of burn unit of Ayub Teaching Hospital, Abbottabad. The successful completion of the project will help in the development of advanced therapeutic wound dressing products for burn patients. It is expected that these products will be an effective and innovative alternative to traditional guaze bandage. The clinical applications will improve the burn care facilities in the country, which may ultimately save millions of human lives. This study can also lead towards commercialization of the product that will contribute to the economic growth of the country.

data.projectName: Probiotic soy milk and okara utilization in bakery items as a pragmatic approach to mitigate protein energy malnutrition (PEM) for school going children in Southern Punjab
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: Soybean  is the only legume which is considered as a source of complete plant based protein containing all essential amino acids..  The seeds can also be used to prepare milk, known as soy milk which contains comparable nutritional profile as that of animal and human milk. It is free from cholesterol and lactose and can benefit  to overcome PEM, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, obesity, breast and prostate cancer, to boost up immunity and is easy to digest. However, the beany flavor and some anti-nutritional factors of soy milk can be overcome with fermentation. data.projectName: weed crop competition
data.projectDigest: Management of weeds is a major challenge to sustainability of global agriculture. Economical weed management is therefore crucial to ensure food security. Weeds compete with crops for resources such as water, nutrients and light etc. and generally result in significant yield losses. In order to control weeds, chemical weed control has been used for many years but information regarding time of herbicide application is lacking in Pakistan. In contrast, in the developed world, critical time for weed removal (CTWR) and economic threshold levels (ETL) has been determined by nonlinear regression modeling. Critical time based weed management strategies increase profits but also improve environment stewardship.  However, there are very limited published reports (only five) in Pakistan that have employed mathematical modeling to determine critical period of weed crop competition. Therefore, there is need to determine the weed crop competition time and economic threshold level of weeds in major field crops. Information regarding time of weed control and economic threshold level of weeds will enable farmers to make prudent and economically sound decisions regarding time of herbicide application. The critical time based weed control would also save herbicides up to (50%), minimize chances of herbicide resistance, increased crop yields (10%) and increase profits up to 20% for farmers.

data.projectName: Investigating mechanisms of disease pathogenesis in triple-negative Myeloproliferative Neoplasms
data.projectDigest: Blood cancers are some of the most common causes of cancer-related death in the world. Not only are these aggressive diseases, they are often resistant to treatment. One such rare group of blood cancers is Myeloproliferative Neoplasms (MPN). In this disease, the normal blood forming stem cells acquire genetic mutations. As a result of these mutations, the abnormal cells grow and replace the normal cells of the bone marrow. Genetic mechanism of a proportion of MPN patients is known. However, what causes disease in nearly 30% patients (so called triple-negative MPNs)  is not known. Furthermore, the diagnostic assays available in Pakistan are imported from technologically advanced countries. There is a need to develop cheaper more suitable assays for the diagnosis of MPNs in Pakistan. There is also a need to identify the cause of disease in triple-negative MPNs. The aims of this research study are two fold: First, to investigate genetic causes of triple-negative MPN patients, and second, to develop cheaper diagnostic assays for use in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Productive innovation in wheat value addition: Conserving the resources, employment generation, improving export potential and reducing hunger to zero level
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Food is the necessity and right of any individual in any country to survive. The prime segment of national strength is its population. Healthy population leads the nation towards progress avoiding un-necessary expenses to health issues and adapting productive activities. The food security is a challenging issue of current times in the world including our country. About 40.2% population is facing stunting growth, 18% are facing wasting disease problem, 25% is underweight in our country. This type of statistics in human growth is directly linked with food and with this situation, the dream of prosperity will never come true. This food scarcity becomes more devastating on uneven distribution of food items or resources in the population. Despite of plenty of resources in our country, we are facing a significant food security challenge, while developed countries, despite of having less resources, are self-sufficient. The other main escalating factor in food shortage is wastage of resources in uncivilized way. The wise use and equal distribution of food stuffs can alleviate the problem of hungry population. The use of technology and value addition may help to overcome this situation as in developed countries. This project is designed to search alternatives and introduction of technology to utilize the resources in a better efficient way by improving the shelf life, storage time and hence improving export potential by the application of value addition in most consumed wheat products.

data.projectName: Street Beggars in Pakistan: Status, Challenges, and Implications
data.projectDigest: The purpose of study is to analyse different trends, current status, and challenges caused by street beggars in Pakistan. The purpose of study is to also analyse beggary as an organized crime in Pakistan, with a focus on the economic, religious, and political factors that enable the lucrative business to thrive. The need is to discover and remove the criminal networks thrive under adverse radical conditions also including government weakness and corruption. By looking at the effects of begging, Government hold a big responsibility to minimize the phenomenon. The primary objective of this research proposal is to address the nature of this prevalent problem, key factors behind the issue, and the difficulties and problems that local citizens are confronted with because of beggars. In this project, researchers intend to investigate the basic factors involved in creating the phenomenon and what strategies or guidelines would be effective in reducing the issue of begging. The study would be conducted through direct observation, in-depth interviews, and focus group discussions with the key-informants in order to thoroughly understand the trend of begging. The researchers also intend to survey selected social worker organizations and road workers with the purpose of improving validity of the results. Based on the findings from initial research, evidence-based solutions will be recommended to meet the challenges caused by begging both for the victims and local citizens. In this regard, this project will help to develop programmes or policies that foster resilience, that is, compensate for the strengths and abilities of the street beggars, in providing the maximum opportunity for positive results in society.

data.projectName: SUTURING PROCESS AND TIMING OF INDIA-ASIA COLLISION ALONG THE NORTHWESTERN MARGIN OF INDIAN PLATE, PAKISTAN
data.projectDigest:
The Himalayan orogeny is defined as the India-Eurasia collision and the successive continental subduction, as well as the induced tectonics, magmatism, metamorphism and plateau uplift. As a result, the distinct Himalayan orogeny eventually led to the formation of the great Himalaya-Tibetan orogen, which has become a natural laboratory for investigating the theories of plate tectonics and continental geodynamics, and a profound driving force for Asian resources and environments. However, the initial collision between the Indian and Eurasian continents and the destiny of the subducted continents remain the most fundamental and critical scientific issues related to building the theory of the continental geodynamics and the formation and evolution of the Himalayan orogen. 
The collision timing is the most debatable topic since last two decades. The array of collision age exist that range from 74 Ma to as young as 25 Ma. It is more complex in the northwestern Himalaya, where Kohistan Island arc is trapped between Indian and Eurasian plate. The collision of Kohistan Island arc first with Indian or Eurasia is also controversial. Therefore, in the proposed project, an attempt will be made to address the issues related to collision timing of the Indian and Eurasian plates in the northwestern Himalaya. Keeping in the view the collision related issues, we proposed to study the sections to the north in Chitral Valley and along west in Sulaiman fold-thrust belt, to constrain the India-Eurasia collision timing in the north and west. By constraining the collision timing differences from north to west, we will be able to understand the collision process in the Himalaya and will provide an updated model for collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates in the northwestern Himalaya.

data.projectName: Identification of Spam Product Reviews written in Roman Urdu Script
data.projectDigest: In recent years, online customer reviews have become the main source to determine public opinion about offered products or services. Consequently, sellers are extremely concerned with customer reviews as these opinions can have a direct impact on their businesses. Unfortunately, there is an increasing trend to write spam reviews to promote or demote targeted products or services. This practice, known as review spamming, has posed many questions regarding the authenticity and dependability of customers’ review-based business processes. Distinguishing fake reviewers from the genuine reviewer is challenging and an open research issue. Existing studies on Spam Review Detection have mostly worked on datasets of English, Chinese and Arabic languages. Very little work on South Asian language like Roman Urdu (written using English alphabets) has been done. It is estimated that large number of people use Roman Urdu in daily communication particularly in writing online reviews, twitter tweets and Facebook posts in the South Asian region. The objective of this research is to devise a method for identification of spam reviews written in Roman Urdu by an individual or a group of spammers. The outcome of this research may help to boost customers’ confidence of South Asian region, particularly in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Development of Rhizobacterial based Biopesticide for the management of Foliar diseases of Groundnut and for yield enhancement.
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.) is the most significant summer season cash as well as oil seed crop in the world. The average yield of groundnut is about 1400 kg/ha. Per hectare yield of groundnut in Pakistan is 1100 kg/ha i.e very low due to combination of factors. Among these actors, the foliar fungal diseases are of importance. Every year enormous amount of hazardous chemicals are used to manage these threats which lead to various environmental and toxicological issues. There is a requirement to develop alternatives to chemical pesticides for crop protection. The export oriented agricultural crops depends on the export of residue free produce and has created a great potential and demand for the incorporation of biopesticides in crop protection. Biopesticides are developing from naturally occurring living organisms such as animals, plants, and microorganisms (e.g., bacteria, fungi, and viruses) that can control serious plant damaging pathogens by their nontoxic eco-friendly mode of actions. Bio-control with PGPR is an acceptable green approach. The formulation of rhizobacteria as biopesticides, will be an alternative choice to use of chemical fungicides. Biopesticides will extend a unique chance to developing countries to research, and they will possess to develop natural biopesticide resources in protecting crops.

data.projectName: Transcriptome sequence analysis of salt sensitive and salt tolerant rice (Oryza sativa) in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Excessive salinity present in soil is one of the major environmental factors that minimize plant growth and yield of a wide variety of crops including rice. On the basis of tolerance ability against salinity, rice is considered as salt sensitive crop, and growth and yield of rice are greatly affected by salinity. In general, rice can tolerate a small amount of saline water without effecting the growth and yield. There is few rice varieties show salt-stress tolerance at an extent. The genetic makeup of plant plays very important role in development of stress tolerance mechanism. Gene expression increases in stress condition and it can be study at transcript/mRNA level. The transcriptome sequencing of salt stress tolerant varieties help to understand the role of genes in different molecular pathways helping in tolerance development. The aim of this study is transcriptome sequencing, analysis and expression profiling in salt-sensitive and salt-tolerant rice varieties. The result of analysis will help the deferentially expressed gens (DEGs) in salt sensitive and salt tolerant rice plant. The function of deferentially expressed genes will be study through online available tools. The validation of expression profiling will be confirmed through quantitative real time PCR. The expected results may be the screened key genes involve in the salt-stress tolerance mechanism in the tolerant rice variety. These genes can be confirmed by further genetic analysis and transformation experiments to test their role in salt tolerance in the rice genotypes.

data.projectName: Centralized Patient Information Monitoring System using Wireless Body Area Networks
data.projectDigest: We work towards development of a Centralized Patient Information Monitoring System using Wireless Body Area Sensor Network (WBAN) which include a home data gathering station (Home server) and it would be able to monitor  the wireless sensors deployed on the patient  and gather the data from these sensors and a remote data gathering-station (Hospital Server) which should be able to monitor and gather the data generated from Home server. The main theme is developing a WSN-based ubiquitous healthcare platform. The developed u-healthcare platform includes most of the possible WSN-compatible applications, including health parameter monitoring and activity monitoring. The reliability of wireless data propagation in a wireless sensor network environment can be considered to represent special features of the monitored health parameters. Emergency data delivery is an important service for medical Wireless Body Area Networks (WBAN). The successful dissemination of emergency messages can make a huge difference between life and death. The utmost importance of emergency message dissemination requires high reliability while the intermittent nature of emergency data requires minimum channel access delay for almost instantaneous delivery. To increase the reliability of health data transfer in wireless sensor networks, we need to know that healthcare data (i.e., data collected from different sensors) consists of wavelike data and linear data. Wavelike healthcare data (such as ECG or EEG) require a higher sampling rate and are more dependent on monitoring reliability than linear signals (including body temperature, blood pressure and oxygen content). As a result we would be able to remotely monitor the data categories, computational algorithm efficiency contributing to minimal delay.

data.projectName: Preparation and Utilization of ZnO Nano-fiber as micronutrient fertilizer for enhancing zinc use efficiency (ZUE), Zinc fortification of wheat grain and wheat yield
data.projectDigest: Soil ability to produce crops is affected by natural and anthropogenic processes resulting in reduced capacity of the soil to support life (Ahmad et al. 2019). In Pakistan, depleting fertility and low input use efficiency (Lal, 2018) are affecting soil’s crop yield potential. Significant efforts have been carried out through research to revert the depleted soil fertility (FAO, 2009). However, micro nutrients like Zn are still neglected and its deficiency is affecting cereal yield and quality (WHO, 2016). Low (20 mg kg-1) Zn content in wheat grain due to low Zn use efficiency (2 to 5%) from ZnSO4 fertilizers (Awais and Ahmad, 2019) is compelling scientists to investigate novel means to increase Zn use efficiency. Most recently, nanotechnology; the manipulation of material at < 1µm scale has been successfully tested for crops Zn bio-fortification (Dapkekar et al., 2018) with increased Zn uptake. The nanofibers; the one dimensional nano-materials with cross sectional diameters in nanometer range has exhibited further improved surface area (Kenry and Lim, 2017). In the current project, ZnO nanoparticles will be synthesized (Santoshkumar et al,. 2017) from ZnO nano-particles, ZnO nanofibers will be prepared through electrospinning (Greiner and Wendorff, 2007). The project will comprise of four studies, In study 1, nanofibers will be prepared and characterized through XRD, FTIAR and SEM analysis. In study 2, Kinetic release of Zn from nanofibers will be checked at different pH ranges and nanofibe concentration. In study 3, uptake of Zn through roots from ZnO nano-fibers will be checked in sand culture. In study 4, seed priming, foliar application, and seed coating of nanofibers shall be tested in field experiment on wheat growth characteristics, Zn uptake and use efficiency

data.projectName: Integrated photooxidation of biomass and water into fuels  and chemicals
data.projectDigest: Photo/catalytic water splitting and the photo/catalytic oxidation of biomass, both, are well-established research fields. In this research area emphasis is on the development of catalysts options and their optimization. This search has led us to a point where further tuning of catalysts in terms of efficiency has attained plateau. To improve efficiency further, a way forward can be the replacement of energetically intensive processes with low energy processes. As the effect of integrating HER and BOR or replacing OER (high energy) with BOR (less energy) needs a thorough study to understood and realize the potential. In this project we intend to explore this role.

data.projectName: Battery Management System for Electric Vehicle
data.projectDigest:
The aim of the work has to design and implement a BMS for lithium batteries using MATLAB/Simulink©, which has been able to predict, monitor and control charge, energy, health and aging effect in terms of capacity fade and internal resistance increase. The BMS system is either connected inside the EV or it is mounted outside the EV for charging purpose. However, due to environmental conditions and charging rate, the overall life of the batteries can be damaged. At the end, the model will be validated with the help of different driving profiles at different ambient temperatures. Linear and non-linear modeling and self-adapting characteristic map using lookup table will also be used. The data for the building of model will be considered from accelerated aging of battery tests and different data set will be considered for the validation of model specifically the weather trends of the Pakistan will be considered. At the end, hardware
implementation of the model will also be considered.

data.projectName: 6G Wireless Communication based on Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface
data.projectDigest: Although the commercialization of fifth-generation (5G) mobile networks is in its initial stage, sixth-generation (6G) research effort has been kicked off from the academic and industrial points of view. Among the enabling technologies for 6G, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs)  are regarded as a promising emerging hardware technology to improve the spectrum and energy efficiency of wireless networks by artificially reconfiguring the propagation environment of electromagnetic waves. In this proposed research work, we focus on three main challenges of implementing RISs in wireless networks, namely, channel state information acquisition, passive information transfer, and resource allocation of RIS-aided communication systems.

data.projectName: Randomized Comparative Study of Performance of Ultrasonic dissection for Laparoscopic assisted Vaginal Hysterectomy: Cordless Versus Wired laparoscopy
data.projectDigest:
A substantial technological revolution was the introduction of ultrasonic energy in dissecting surgical devices in laparoscopy in the decade of 1990s. These ultrasonic devices offer dissecting, grasping, cutting and coagulation, all in single system with the smallest thermal footprints around (about -1 mm). The safety and versatility make it a convincing technology to contemplate for any surgeon thoughtful about performing surgeries into the deep pelvis. 
This Sonicision* ultrasonic cordless dissection device performs like reliable HARMONIC ACE*, but it works without a power cord. The freedom is much appreciated by the surgeons as they naturally tangle the cords on the patient’s body from one trocar to another. It is also a pleasant surprise for the surgeons that how quickly they master the single energy button. The surgeons also appreciate the cutting speed and coagulation of the instrument. 
A Prospective Randomized trial is planned to compare the cordless laparoscope - Sonicision™ with the wired laparoscope- HARMONIC ACE® ultrasonic while doing laparoscopic assisted vaginal hysterectomy (LAVH) with the following goals/objectives:
I.	to compare the two ultrasonic laparoscope devices in safety, efficacy and ergonomics, while doing LAVH.
II.	to perform the LAVH with this cordless laparoscope and to establish the benefits of the innovative technology for the first time in Pakistan.
III.	Teaching and training of gynecologists, surgeons, residents and paramedical staff for the ultimate better care of patients and community.

data.projectName: Evaluation of Synthesized and Fabricated Perovskite Materials for Energy Application
data.projectDigest:
Energy adequacy is reassurance to excel any country’s economy because energy is the foremost requirement to achieve sustainable growth. At the present, world is fulfilling about 90% of its energy requirements through fossil fuels which are not only depleting exponentially but also creating adverse impact on environment. The world especially developing countries are now looking for eco-friendly energy sources to full fill their energy demands. 
Perovskite-type compounds have attained remarkable consideration during past decade as functional materials in devices for energy conversion and storage like solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs), supercapacitors, solar cell, oxy-combustion process, metal-air batteries, proton exchange membrane fuel cell etc but number of vital performance parameters still need to be explored before their utilization in practical applications.
The current project has three objectives; (i) Synthesis of perovskite materials with different composition for components of SOFCs through wet chemical method (co-precipitation, auto combustion, hydrothermal process etc), (ii) Fabrication of components of SOFC from synthesized perovskite materials through “Tape Casting” and uniaxial pressing and (iii) finally synthesized and fabricated perovskite materials will be evaluated for their application as SOFC components through different  characterization techniques.

data.projectName: Development of an overseas conformity index to enhance overseas adjustment of Pakistani workforce
data.projectDigest: A significant percentage of employees going abroad to find work are quitting their jobs and returning home. Inadaptability to host-country?s culture is being considered among major reasons for their non adjustment in foreign environment. A lot of resources are spent when a person undertakes a foreign work assignment and this is going waste due to lack of adjustment. Among many reasons one proposed one is overseas non-conformity, this can occur from different reasons like difference in culture, work settings, lack of training etc. This research project will try to identify causes of non-conformity among Pakistani nationals going abroad for job and develop an overseas conformity index. This index will guide expats from Pakistan to check which attributes will help them in overseas job adjustment. This will be helpful in selection, training and development of workers for overseas assignments.

data.projectName: Determinants of Improved Livestock Practices and Technology Adoption: Evidence from District Lasbela, Balochistan
data.piUniversity: Lasbela University of Agriculture, Water and Marine Sciences, Lasbela
data.projectDigest: Livestock in Balochistan safeguards food security, particularly to the underprivileged and impoverished localities. Nonetheless, livestock production in Balochistan is not adequate primarily due to the inauspicious agricultural system, poor application of improved farming practices and the lack of improved livestock breeds, inadequacy or non-availability of information related to standard practices i.e. animal feed, treatment from the veterinary supervisor, dairy farm management, use of antibiotics, appropriate disposal of waste, animal health, and record-keeping, etc. In fact, many of the farmers are marginalized and living in remote villages with subsistence income, where livelihoods are entirely dependent upon livestock.  In addition, they face huge challenges over the adaptability of Improved Livestock Practices and Technology due to their subsistence income. The study will be pointed out that institutional coverage is minimal and concluded that the introduction of agricultural technology is an important contribution to the sustainable development of the agricultural sector. The purpose of the study is to evaluate the degree to which ILPT farming is embraced, as well as to identify and quantify factors that influence the implementation of ILPT in rural areas of Balochistan. In addition, to illustrate the key socio-economic determinants that have a notable impact on ILPT adoption and spread.

data.projectName: Assessment of different Ziziphus species for meliferous potential and production of prime export quality Pakistani honey-Phase-I
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Apiculture is a profitable business through honeybee (Apis mellifera) rearing for producing honey and other products. In Pakistan, there are more than 450,000 bee colonies with 12000 tons honey production. The country exported approximately honey worth of $6.9 million to Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates and Kuwait during the previous year; however, the export is far below than its actual potential. Honey produced from Beri or Sidr (Ziziphus spp.) is among the most popular honey varieties of Pakistan. Due to its peculiar color, taste and medicinal properties, it is very much popular in local and foreign customers and most of it is exported every year. Beri honey, although produced in many areas but still there is a big gap regarding timing, availability and characteristics of nectar produced from domestic Ziziphus species and varieties growing in different ecological zones. In the world, beri honey produced from some Ziziphus spina-christi fetches 3-fold high prices than the others. This project is aimed at identifying the nectar potential of various native Ziziphus species for producing supreme export quality honey of Pakistani origin for enhancing export values. For this purpose, the monofloral and multifloral honey of Ziziphus species shall be collected from various ecological zones and their physico-chemical antioxidant, antibacterial and antifungal activity shall also be determined. The output of this project shall be development of Pakistani honey of prime quality comparable with world class Yemeni Sidr honey that would be patented coupled with introducing modern honey bee production technology that shall not only uplift the export and economy of the country but also improve the life of local people of the rural areas.

data.projectName: Investigation of Fouling Mechanism of Reverse Osmosis Polyamide Membranes Using Molecular Dynamics Simulation
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: The world is facing water scarcity in general and drinking water shortage in particular. Seawater is the abundant source of water on earth, however, seawater is highly saline and can't be used directly. Among several seawater treatment technologies, reverse osmosis is the most widely used and commercially viable technology to produce freshwater. Reverse osmosis employs polyamide membranes for water treatment. However, the membrane surface is fouled due to salts and other organic matter in feed water. The membrane fouling results in high applied pressure of pumps on feed side and shortening of membrane life leading to a rise in water price. Several experimental and modeling studies have been carried out to investigate the fouling mechanism. Unfortunately, there has been no single and general consensus on fouling mechanism to control and ultimately mitigate membrane fouling. Molecular dynamics has been proved to be the most promising technique to understand the processes on molecular scale and acceptability and applicability of its results commercially. The objective of this project is to study and understand the fouling mechanism of polyamide membranes and present the underlying phenomena of membrane fouling to the academia and industry. This study will lead to production of freshwater economically worldwide.

data.projectName: Enabling Arsenic contaminated wastewater for reuse in agriculture and its health implications
data.projectDigest: Pakistan, a region with arid to semi-arid conditions is also facing this problem, where crops are regularly irrigated with wastewater and this problem is further aggravated due to no pre-treatment of wastewater. Wastewater is potentially contaminated with plethora of contaminants, for instance abiotic (heavy metals) and biotic (pathogens). These contaminants may include potentially toxic elements (PTEs): zinc (Zn), lead (Pb), arsenic (As), and cadmium (Cd) which may lead to various ailments in human beings upon exposure and also affect various environmental components.  The As has gained considerably more attention among the pollutants and several researchers are constantly putting their efforts to develop strategies that can remove As from environmental systems in environmental friendly manner for a long time. Sustainable wastewater use has become imperative in order to fulfill the demand of water for irrigation. Adsorption via biochar can help to decrease adverse effects of As in the environment. Biochar can be used as an adsorbent, but simple biochars are not efficient enough to completely remove and/or immobilize As, Therefore, biochar modifications are critical in improving its surface characteristics. Since Silicon (Si) has been widely used for the treatment of As and is reported to reduce As induced toxicity in plants (e.g., rice, maize). Silicon can be coupled with biochar to attain dual benefits to decrease uptake of As by crops and enhance their growth at the same time. The hypothesis for this project is that the utilization of biochar modified with Si may reduce mobility of As in soil and subsequently reduce its uptake in vegetables under wastewater irrigation.

data.projectName: Systematics study and Biological activities of medicinal plants in Hazara division Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
Medicinal plant resources play a vital and effective role in traditional herbal therapy.  In this project we will scientifically assessed medicinal species used by inhabitants of Hazara division Pakistan to treat various diseases. This study aimed to compile the data on traditional uses of medicinal plants in health-care practices among rural communities and provides baseline for natural drug discovery.
Study is mainly focused on correct identification, distribution, status, scientific and vernacular name, plant part used, mode of preparation, herbal recipes, morphology, leaf epidermal anatomy, palynology, medicinal uses, phytochemical analysis and biological activities of medicinal plants. Field trips and surveys will be conducted to collect plant specimens. Taxonomic, phytochemical and biological work will be conducted in Department of Botany, PMAS Arid agriculture university, Rawalpindi. 
This study also provides significant information about medicinal plants usage for treatment of various diseases among indigenous communities of Hazara Division. The baseline findings of this study might be useful in compiling data for future phytochemical and pharmacological screening of plants. To best of our knowledge none of such studies has been done before. This project will first report to compile baseline linked to applied aspect of medicinal plants for biological activities lead to natural drug discovery development.

data.projectName: Investigation of solitons in optical fibers and nonlinear optics
data.projectDigest: The soliton is a well known concept in nonlinear dynamics. This phenomenon is not only important for mathematical point of view, it has an imperative impact on many fields of sciences like nanoscience, optical fiber communication system and plasma physics etc. Solitons have been explored in neuroscience trying to explain how an electrical signal travels along a neuron and propagation of optical waves in nonlinear optical fiber communication system, which is the foundation stone for advances in information technology. Soliton molecules are also considered the basic ingredients for information transfer, through optical fibers for trans-continental and transoceanic distances.

data.projectName: Extraction and characterization of secondary metabolites for the treatment of Parkinson diseases from selected medicinal plants of Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Parkinson Disease is a neurodegenerative disease causes bradykinesia, rigidity in muscles, speech abnormality, loss of body balance and dementia. Levodopa, Tolcapone, Pramipexole and carbidopa etc are the available drugs in the market for the treatment of PD, which provides symptomatic relief but causes complications. Considering the socioeconomic burden and undesirable side effects of synthetic drugs, natural remedies are promising avenues in the treatment of PD. Natural products obtained from medicinal plants play a crucial in controlling PD with no/less side effect such as EGb761and Ginkgetin (Ginkgo biloba), and Baicalein (flavonoid). 
The areas of North West Pakistan (District Bannu and Waziristan) have a large number of medicinal floras which are traditionally used by local people for the treatment of PD but still not evaluated pharmacologically. Initially we have characterized some medicinal plants with significant results and further studies are in process. To achieve this goal the present project is therefore aimed to isolate cost effective metabolites for the treatment of PD through pharmacological (Invitro and Invivo studies) and metabolomic (Isolation and Purification) verifications. The obtained secondary metabolites will be in easy excess with no or less side effects and will be commercialized through Ecolife Pharma.

data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest: Design and synthesis of new pharmacologically active nuclei is an active area of research/interest in organic chemistry. Ciprofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone, an antibiotic that fights bacteria in the body. Similarly acefylline acts as an adenosine receptor antagonist. Both molecules are extensively used in our daily life for the treatment of bacterial infections as well as in the treatment of cough. Similarly Quantum chemical methods by using GAUSSIAN software have gained the attention of scientific community, due to its wide range of applicability. Especially for conjugated molecules that are extensively used to investigate the structural properties like frontier molecular orbital analysis (HOMO-LUMO energy gap), natural bonding orbital analysis (NBO) and non-linear optics (NLO) properties and molecular electrostatic potential (MEP) etc. The major purpose of the proposed study is to design and synthesize some new analogues of ciprofloxacin and acefylline and to explore their structural as well as possible pharmacological potential.

data.projectName: Use Of Biochar From Pyrolysis of Organic Waste as Fertilizer For The Improvement of Semi-Arid Soil and Carbon Sequestration In Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Kohat University of Science and Technology, Kohat
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan house hold garbage and other organic waste is directly disposed off to the environment, where it decomposes and produces carbon and other green house gases, consequently it increases global warming. The organic matter also liberates toxic and other elements at decomposition and contaminates water bodies trough leaching. The best way to get ride off it is pyrolysis of organic waste and the resultant biochar will be added to agriculture soil for carbon sequestration and other additional benefits. Biochar in soil will improve soil fertility, water holding capacity, microbial community, nutrient retention and carbon sequestration. Consequently crop yield will increase and causes of global warming and other environmental contaminants will reduce. Therefore, in this proposed project biochar will be produced from available organic waste through pyrolysis in study area and will be added in soils and will be distributed as organic fertilizer in Pakistan. In addition the campaign in this regard also will be helpful to divert the attention of investors in solid waste management to use it as cheap organic fertilizer in Pakistan and can export to contribute the national revenue.

data.projectDigest: Common scab is the most important bacterial disease of potato crop caused by Streptomyces species in Pakistan. The disease is widely distributed in Pakistan and around the world. Common scab has majorly affected potato crop grown in the Northern Areas of Pakistan such as Abbottabad, Manshera, Nathiagali and Kagan. The disease is soil borne and is very difficult to control. An important goal of plant breeding and biotechnological research is the improvement economically important crop such as potato against pathogen. Therefore the main goal of this project is to identify and characterize potato WRKY70 transcription factor against Streptomyces in disease resistance. So far the role of WRKY70 transcription factor role in potato has not been explored. This will be the first study to identify and characterize wrky70 transcription factor role in disease resistance against Streptomyces species. WRKY70 transcription factor will be silenced in potato plant through RNAi mechanism and its role in disease resistance will be evaluated against bacterial pathogen. The disease resistance through WRK70 transcription factor will be further validated through RNA-seq analysis and bacterial assay to identify key regulatory pathway involved in potato crop against disease resistance which is of prime significance crop grown in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Advance Photo-Catalytic Pretreatment of Lignocellulosic Biomass for commercializable Biofuel Production
data.projectDigest: The industrial economy and country’s progress is lagging far behind due to the unavailability or expensive power input. Being an agricultural land Pakistan is rich in crop biomass that is an excellent renewable energy resources used worldwide for biofuel generation. The only hurdle associated with biomass is the close packing of structural components like cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin that are responsible for low biodegradability of biomass. Therefore, biomass requires a pretreatment that firstly loosen ups the complex biomass architecture and later on convert the pretreated biomass into biofuel by anaerobic digestion. In the past many chemical, enzymatic and mechanical pretreatment methods were introduced but each technique raised anaerobic digestion toxicity, marginal increase in biodegradability and continuous supply of catalyst. Moreover, these pretreatment strategies were also having drawbacks for industrial applications. Our project aims to introduce a novel biomass pretreatment using metal oxides as reusable photo-catalyst. In the presented project we aim to achieve the development of novel TiO2 nanocomposite to act as photo-catalyst. Moreover, conditions for lignocellulosic biomass photo-catalytic pretreatment will be optimized for wheat straw, corn stover and rice husk. Subsequently, the pretreated biomass will investigated in batch and continuous reactors for methane augmentation by anaerobic bacteria. This project mainly aims to extract more energy in the form of methane from by biomass and animal manure using pretreatment. Later on, the electrical output from methane will be evaluated to ensure the process sustainability for electrical power generation. Economic balance will also be numerically simulated to advocate the overall process efficacy.

data.projectName: Differential transcriptome analysis of selected Chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.) lines for abiotic stress tolerance and pod development.
data.projectDigest:
Chickpea (gram) is one of the nutritious pulse crop of Pakistan. The pulse contains up to 28% proteins and is highly beneficial for human consumption to meet the human body protein requirements. It is cultivated in the rainfed and semi-desert areas. Two kinds of chickpea are grown in Pakistan (Desi and Kabuli varieties). Desi varieties have some natural tolerance to drought and can withstand water scarcity to a limited extent. However, Kabuli varieties are much sensitive to water deficiency but have greater market value due to the size and smoothness of grains.
Chickpea in the field is exposed to abiotic stresses like drought, heat and salt. The desi varieties are better adopted to our environment and show various degrees of tolerance to the abiotic stresses. These natural stress tolerance mechanisms need to be explored. RNASeq is based on Next Generation Sequencing and provides data at the genomic scale both for gene expression and transcript identification.  Moreover, the natural mutants of chickpea with double pod number do exist and are the best candidates for improving the yield potential of chickpea varieties. RNASeq can be used to identify differentially expressed and mutant genes involved in axillary meristem branching. 
This project aims to identify the key molecular mechanisms in chickpea that are involved in abiotic stress tolerance and podding. The identification of these genes will help the future research to improve Kabuli varieties for better abiotic stress tolerance and yield.

data.projectName: Elucidating molecular epidemiology of Small ruminant morbillivirus in Balochistan, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Small ruminant morbillivirus (SRMV) causes contagious transboundary  devastating   called Peste des petits ruminants (PPR) in  small domestic and/or wild ruminants. The virus has been classified into four distinct lineages (I–IV) on the basis of partial sequence of N and F genes. Pakistan has agriculture?based economy and livestock plays an integral role in the sustainability of the national economy. However, it is challenged by various infectious diseases including FMD and PPR posing severe economic losses to farmer’s community. The virus has been identified and sequenced from Punjab province only in recent years but No data is available from Balochistan. Blood andnasal  swab samples will be collected from sheep and goat in different districts [Quetta, Musakheil, Barkhan, Sikandar abad and Zhob] of the province and processed in Center for Advanced Studies in Vaccinology & Biotechnology (CASVAB) University of Balochistan, Quetta. After RNA extraction F & N gene will be amplified through RT-PCR and partial sequencing will be done of N gene. The data collected will be analyzed using specific bioinformatics tools.  The proposed results may reveal genetic differences between local circulating virus and currently used Nigerian (Vaccinal strain) to understand variations at genomic level.
