data.projectName: Identification and maintenance of virulent Newcastle Disease Virus (NDV) in Pakistan: The impact of vaccination on the virus ecology
data.projectDigest: Pakistan continues to have outbreaks of NDV (virus causing Newcastle disease in poultry) despite intensive vaccination. The continual presence of NDV is a threat to industries that produce 40 percent of the total meat consumption, which provides income for 1.8 million people in approximately 25,000 poultry farms. Since 2011, the problem has increased with the appearance of new strains able to cause disease in pets and in wild birds (peacocks, pheasants, and parrots). Vaccination has failed to prevent the recurrence of outbreaks, and it is suspected that vaccinated animals may act as reservoir of virulent viruses. As current vaccination campaigns are done without any prior understanding of their ecological consequences, circulating virulent NDV has continued to evolve and multiple genotypes have been identified. We now have evidence that vNDV strains were maintained at multiple farms utilizing vaccines for the control of ND across the  country.  We expect to identify vaccination practices that are associated with increased genomic variability of NDV. We also expect to identify new strains of virulent NDV associated with factors or with host species that contribute to the spread of this virus.  The project will provide a better understanding of the dynamics of infections, will assess the role of vaccination practices in the maintenance of the virus, and re-asses the effectiveness of the current vaccination practices on domestic poultry.

data.projectName: Investigating the Impact of Role Conflict on Mental Well-being and Job Performance in Dual Career Couples in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Background: 
Dual career couples is a marital pattern in which wife and husband are simultaneously pursuing occupational career along with family roles. A wide range of studies have found that parallel role obligations cause role overload issues and thus negatively affect job performance, satisfaction, productivity and mental well-being of dual career couples however no systematic reflection has been made on the issues of academic dual career couples in Pakistan. 
Objective: 
To explore the impact of role conflict on job performance, satisfaction, productivity and mental well-being of academic dual career couples.
Method: 
Data will be gathered from either husband/wife or both having academic career through structured questionnaire in 10 selected universities of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Data will be analysed through statistical techniques i.e. mean, standard deviation, factor analysis, regression and correlation test. 
Duration: 2 years 
1st year: literature Review, Data collection, analysis.
2nd year: Seminars and workshops will be arranged in all the targeted universities to share project findings, concepts and taxonomies to the dual career couples
Intended outcomes: 
To add knowledge to the existing literature on dual career couples
To support and train dual careerists to improve their Socio-psychological well-being and enhance their academic and research output in the Universities.

data.projectName: Depression and circadian variation in blood pressure, a cross-sectional multicenter study from Karachi, Pakistan.
data.projectDigest: Depression is a large and increasing public health problem and linked to serious consequences such as increased cardiovascular (CVD) morbidity and mortality. There is also  strong evidence to show that increased Blood pressure variability (BPV) or the circadian variability in blood pressure is independently associated with higher risk of target-organ damage, cardiovascular events, and mortality. The overall goal of this study is to increase knowledge on the mechanisms of depression leading to circadian variation in blood pressure. We will conduct a crossectional study on participants from outpatient clinical setting at the Aga Khan University hospital and Ziauddin Hospital and evaluate them for presence of depression using Pakistan Anxiety and Depression Questionnaire (PADQ) and for variability of blood pressure using 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure recording. We will partner with faculty from Ziauddin University for recuiting participants and Karolinska Instititet, Stockholm, Sweden for their expertise in mental health epidemiology. Our specific aims are  Specific aim 1: To determine the association of depression and short term blood pressure variability in normotensive individuals in an outpatient setting Specific aim 2: To determine the association of depression and short term blood pressure variability in hypertensive individuals in an outpatient setting. Significance: This study will add to a better understanding of the mechanism between depression and blood pressure circadian rhythm, and might serve as  a possible marker that could be identified in a clinical setting at an early stage and to be used in primary prevention

data.projectName: Evaluation of Phosphine resistance and coping it with alternative fumigants in stored grain insect pests
data.projectDigest:
This indiscriminate use of insecticide for the control of pests of stored grain leads to the development of resistance in insects against these insecticides. Insects are not killed by such type of ineffective fumigation. This results in the development of resistance in insects against fumigants. Majority of the grain handling personnel are reporting that insects are not controlled by fumigation, the major reason is the development of resistance. In current circumstances and keeping in view this major eco-biological issue in mind, biochemical and genetic basis of resistance development will be evaluated against major insect species of stored grains collected from Punjab. Insecticide bioassay will be conducted under laboratory conditions against the laboratory reared populations for their susceptibility or resistance which will be compared with already available susceptible populations being reared in the laborites. Qualitative analysis of protein contents and specified enzymes will be carried out using Gel electrophoresis technique. Genetic basis of the finally selected resistant populations will also be studies. 
 2nd stage of the project will be assessment of Ozone gas fumigation and nanoparticales of essential oils as an alternative control strategy against phosphine resistant insect pests of stored wheat. Insects will be treated with high concentration of Ozone gas in fumigation chamber in laboratory

data.projectName: Sensitivity Analysis of Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model to different parameterization schemes over the Upper Indus Basin
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest: High-resolution atmospheric modeling can fill the gap of observational data scarcity to advance the understanding of atmospheric variability and hydrologic uncertainty under changing climate. The WRF popularity is due to the availability of various parameterization schemes. Among all parameterization schemes, microphysics and land surface models are very critical to influence the regional precipitation and temperature patterns. This study will examine the impact of five cloud microphysical schemes (Thompson, Morrison, Goddard, Lin et al. scheme, WSM6) and two LSMs (NoahMP and CLM4) on precipitation and temperature patterns over the UIB region for the time period of 1st May 2005 through 28th February 2006, covering two full seasons (winter and summer). The WRF model will be configured with two nested domains (d01-d02) with horizontal resolutions increasing inward from 15 km to 5 km, respectively. The model results will be evaluated through a comparison with the TRMM 3B42v7 dataset and station data collected from the PMD and the WAPDA. The statistical measures for the evaluation purpose will root mean square error (RMSE), percentage bias (PBIAS), mean bias error (MBE), and Pearson correlation coefficient. This study could be useful for future climate change and other hydrological studies in this region.

data.projectName: Determinants of Mobile Money Adoption in Pakistan and its Impact on Individuals Saving behavior
data.projectDigest: The proposed project will explore the determinants of mobile money adoption and examine its impact on the savings behavior of individuals particularly to those that are vulnerable to financial exclusion, that is, the low-income earners, less-educated, female and rural habitants. Moreover, the consequences of mobile money adoption on the usage of formal and informal financial services will be investigated in Pakistan. Primary and secondary data will be used to accomplish the study objectives. Both qualitative and quantitative methods such as face-to-face interviews and structured questionnaire will be used to collected the primary data while secondary data will be collected from Global Financial Inclusion Survey by World Bank and Financial Access Survey by State Bank of Pakistan. Multiple regression model, Logistic model and the 2SLS Instrumental Variable (IV) regression model will be used as the empirical estimation methods to achieve research objectives. The possible outcomes will provide an understanding of the individual behavior for the use of mobile money. Results that will be derived from financially vulnerable group such as low-income earners, less educated, female and rural inhabitants will help to fosters financial inclusion which will be essential in the realization of the Sustainable Development Goals such as reducing poverty, increasing equality and sustained economic growth among others.

data.projectName: Investigating the acidic potential of locally available beverages in Pakistan and their effect on tooth erosion
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Globally, chemical loss of teeth is considered as the third most common dental problem. It is an irreparable and non-bacterial damage of teeth due to chemical dissolution as a result of acidic oral environment. The most common source of acidic oral environment includes consumption of acidic beverages and food. It has recently been studied that more than 80% of highly educated representative group of Pakistani population consume such beverages. It has also been suggested that the tooth structure with high degree of mineralization is more prone to chemical attack which ultimately leads to its softening. 

Various factors for instance acid content, ionic concentration, exposure time of beverages etc are responsible for the chemical loss of tooth. Until now, acidic potential and resultant tooth damage of the locally available beverages has not been investigated in Pakistan despite their frequent consumption. Therefore, this study has been proposed with an intention to thoroughly evaluate the locally available beverages in Pakistan and their effects on tooth damage with or without the presence of saliva. The findings of this research work may assist policy makers to design appropriate policies which may ultimately prevent the loss of tooth and reduce the treatment cost across the community.

data.projectName: Impact of Film Consumption and Celebrity Culture on Pakistan’s Ideology and Cultural Sustainability: Mediating Role of Subliminal Messages
data.projectDigest:
Media industry, being a major stakeholder in any society creates the bases for developing and transforming opinions and perceptions. It is highly influences cultural sustainability, which ultimately is required for maintaining ideological boundary, dignity, progress, prosperity as well as regional boundary (Francesca, 2017). The Media industry uses the medium of film consumption, celebrity culture alongside subliminal messages in promotional campaigns to influence the masses in making up their ideology and plays a vital role in constructing popular culture for awareness and decision making (Zhuang, 2018). 
Having understood the importance and power of Media industry, we can then easily analyse indian media which has indoctrinated and manipulated Pakistani society dramatically due to which we, as a Muslim nation, have and continue to suffer bitterly (Sabir, et.al., 2016) (Sabir, 2011). Indian movies, dramas and celebrities are intoxicating Pakistani youth to the extreme that they follow Indian values and philosophy blindly without noticing the distortion of their own country’s ideology and culture (Nazir, 2012). The main objective of this research is to investigate the impact of film consumption and celebrity culture on Pakistan’s Ideology and cultural sustainability.

data.projectName: Threonine Dehydrogenase: A potential target for pest control.
data.projectDigest: Threonine is an important amino acid, the utilization of which can occur via three different pathways each instigated by a different threonine catabolism enzyme. One of these enzymes is threonine dehydrogenase and a number of organisms utilize the pathway that is initiated by the enzyme threonine dehydrogenase. It catalyzes the conversion of L-threonine to L-2-amino-3-ketobutyrate which is eventually converted to glycine and acetyl CoA. Both of these products have values as precursors of various important metabolites in the organisms using this method of threonine degradation. Some of these organisms are disease spreading pests like mosquitoes. It has been found that the gene for threonine dehydrogenase in humans, is a pseudogene i.e. no threonine dehydrogenase enzyme is expressed and suggests that an alternative pathway of threonine catabolism is dominant. We propose utilization of this metabolic difference between the humans and disease causing pests be exploited for practical applications by regulating the enzyme threonine dehydrogenase. We suggest carrying out an in-depth mechanistic analysis of threonine dehydrogenase from these pest sources to identify a potential inhibitor, which may disrupt the normal enzyme function of this pathway, with an outcome of controlling vector-borne diseases like malaria and dengue caused by mosquitoes.

data.projectName: Development of an Optimal Mechanism and the Standards for Allocation of Teachers and Teaching Expenditure for Quality Education
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
This is a descriptive study that has the population of all the elementary (primary and middle) and secondary schools in Punjab. As the target of this study is standardization, a large size data is required. Moreover, the districts of the Punjab have urban and rural setting; therefore, equal presentations will be given to both of the strata. Therefore, all rural and urban schools from these 16 districts will be selected as the sample of the study. The data regarding teaching expenditure, STR and class size will be collected from all these schools. However, the sample for questionnaires will be selected through stratified random selection. Application of stratified random sampling technique will ensure equal presentation for all the sub-groups of population. It will make the sample really representative of the population. The sample for questionnaire comprises of a total of 768 schools i.e. 48 schools from each district and the sample of each district comprises 16 primary schools, 16 middle schools and 16 high schools. From each district, stratified random sampling technique will be applied to select 16 schools i.e. four girls schools and four boys’ schools from rural strata and four girls schools and four boys’ schools from urban strata, separately at primary, middle and secondary level. 
Ten experts from each district will be selected randomly from the district educational management and head teachers for interview. A group of 20 experts including policy makers, and provincial and district management for Focused Group Discussion will be randomly selected. Interview and Focused Group Discussion (FGD) will be conducted for the in-depth understanding of the issue. District Administration i.e. EDO’s, DEO’s, Deputy Education Officers and AEO’s will be involved in the study.

data.projectName: Growth of Low-dimensional Materials and Their Physics Study at Different Temperatures for Energy and Electronic Applications
data.projectDigest: Electronic Industry is one of the biggest industries of the world which has literally modernized the life of humanity. The electronic materials have proven as fantastic sources for electrical as well as energy applications. This proposed project is based on the up-gradation of existing labs at department of Physics, COMSATS University Islamabad. We have already few basic tools for the growth of electronic materials (semiconductors) and their characterizations. But, usually the characterization of prepared materials is always difficult as we have limited characterization techniques. We propose here the integration and installation of existing setup with "Cryogen free optical cryostat 3 K, (OptistatDry – the BLV model)" prepared by Oxford instruments, UK. This system will help us on large scale for the measurements of prepared nanostructured materials as it can cool down as well as the heat-up the sample from 3 Kelvin to 400 Kelvin within few minutes. It will provide significant assistance in terms of ease of use and running costs as it doesn’t use liquid cryogens e.g. liquid nitrogen or helium. This system has variety of important features such as; it can be moved from one lab to other lab easily, it can be equipped with variety of characterization tools such as electrical characterization (IV), UV-Vis, Photo-luminescence, Electroluminescence and Raman spectroscopy etc. And of course, all these characterization tools are very important in the sense of testing the electronic materials.

data.projectName: Technological Unemployment-A Myth or Reality
data.projectDigest:
Technological unemployment is meant to be losing employment opportunities merely because of technological change or in other words, we can say that technological unemployment is a type of structural unemployment that is solely caused by the shift in the technological environment of any organization or a country. Such technological shift usually comprises labor saving techniques or processes e.g., from horses to automobiles, artisan weavers to power loom, newspapers to tablets, telephone operators to an automated telephone system, drivers to driverless cars, and so on. There are plenty of examples around us that apparently show the dark side of technology. 
“Technological unemployment: a myth of reality” is an interesting debate between economists for a long time. There are, by and large, two point of views to explain the impact of technology/innovation on employment. According to the optimistic point of view, technology leads to job creation by introducing new products and cost-cutting processes which ultimately enhance the demand for labor. However, simultaneously pessimistic point of view is also prevailing in the literature which explains that technology creates hurdles in the way of employment opportunities by inventing new mechanism which can save labor or shift the tasks from labor-oriented to machine-oriented.

data.projectName: Identification of novel sources of resistance to Fusarium head blight in Pakistani wheat germplasm
data.projectDigest: Bread wheat is cultivated on about 240 million ha worldwide and is a staple food crop for 40% of the world’s population. It is estimated that about 21.5% of the crop’s production is lost to disease or insect pests. Fusarium head blight (FHB) is an important disease of wheat and other small grains that has profound economic consequences for the wheat and barley in major grain-growing regions of the world. The most common causing pathogen of FHB is Fusarium graminearum. Grain yield and end-use quality losses resulting from infected plants include sterility of the florets, formation of discolored and shrunken kernels (“tombstone” kernels), and low grain volume weight. Diseased kernels may also contain significant levels of mycotoxins (primarily deoxynivalenol) that are hazardous to animal and human health, thus making the grain unfit for food and feed. In the past, major FHB epidemic years included 1957 and 1982, with the most resent FHB epidemic occurring in 2007.Genetic diversity among Pakistani wheat germplasm and identification of novel source of FHB resistance will provide opportunities for breeders to use gene transformation and gene editing in breeding to create new sources of resistance and to accelerate the breeding process. Furthermore, exploiting the currently available resistant germplasm, characterized resistance genes and reliable markers enable routine release of new cultivars with better yield potential and high FHB resistance in the very near future. In short, development of high yield and FHB resistant wheat variety will contribute to uplift wheat production in the country and ultimately will help the farming community which will definitely contribute in poverty alleviation in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Climate Change and Food Secuity in Agriculture Sector: The case of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
data.piUniversity: Kohat University of Science and Technology, Kohat
data.projectDigest: Food security is the most serious issue in the world, especially in developing countries. It depends on agricultural performances of the countries. Pakistan is an agrarian country and agriculture is the largest sector of its economy. Despite its agrarian economy, Pakistan is facing severe problem of food security. The most significant and effective factor for food security and agriculture performance in Pakistan is its climate fluctuations. This research project will address the problem of food security under climate changes in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The population of this province is over 22 million. Highly increasing population is enhancing the demand for balanced food, but its agrarian sector is not fulfilling its food requirements. One of the major reasons of this deficiency is climate condition. KP includes different agricultural zones with different climate conditions. This comprehensive study will explore the impact of climate change on food security in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. This research project will cover both irrigated and un-irrigated areas of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Results of this research project will help the government of Pakistan, policy makers, and non-governmental organizations to prescribe some policy measures to enhance agricultural productivity and thereby address the issue of food security in the agriculture sector of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

data.projectName: Boron Nitride Nanosheets and their Complexes with Polyvinyl Chloride as a Potential Adsorbent to Remove Methylene Blue and Congo Red from Model Aqueous Solutions.
data.projectDigest: Water is one of the basic needs of human life and all other organisms. In the current decade, there has been a serious shortage of drinking water due to the destruction of water resources. Industrialization contributes to economic development, while on the other hand, they discharge wastewater containing dyes, carpets, rubber, paper, cosmetics, plastics and textiles  into water resources and causes water pollution. Industries  are the main contributors to the environment for methylene blue and Congo red. These dyes are toxic and cause several health problems.  This study aimed to analyze the efficiency of removing dyes from aqueous solutions using Boron nitrite and BN-PVC composites as adsorbents and photocatalysts. Current research is socially useful because its application is easily implemented at low cost and has no adverse impact on the environment.

data.projectName: China-Pakistan Economic Corridor : The Game Changer
data.projectDigest: This study is an endeavor to investigate the motivations of China’s FDI in Pakistan to look into the motivation in the context of natural resources and monetary returns for the mutual benefits of the countries under CPEC projects. This research project will describe the determinants such as corruption, inflation, growth rate, political stability, investment freedom, business freedom, trade freedom, financial freedom for China’s FDI in Pakistan. Furthermore, it will try to explain the conventional determinants of FDI in Pakistan as well as it holds true for China as compared to CPEC. Finally, this study will provide a framework for the future prospects of CPEC specifically on Pakistan and broadly for South Asia. This study will also help to understand the Role of Chinese FDI in Pakistan in context of economic as well as financial Game changer. Lastly, this study make to find out possible ways to establish Pak-China research study center at COMSATS University Islamabad, Wah Campus in order to make possible research in collaboration with the Chinese`s Universities and official. The purpose of Pak –China research center is to Promote and make rigorous research on the prospects of the CPEC.

data.projectName: Dynamics of solid particles passing across obstacles of different sizes and shapes using fictitious boundary method (FBM)
data.projectDigest:
Particulate flows are found in numerous natural processes such as sedimentation of particles in estuary, wind-blown sand particles or dust particles, lava flow etc. From industrial point of view, these phenomenon occur in paper pulp, particle clogging, slurry flow, aggregate formation, filtration, peristaltic transport of solid particles in fluid/blood during biological processes and a lot of applications arising in fields such as engineering, chemistry, biology, physics and mathematics.
Solid-liquid two phase flows often face the problem of particle overlapping during numerical simulations due to small truncation errors and less accurate methods which makes difficult to simulate particulate flows. A lot of collision models have been proposed to avoid overlapping of particles by adding short range repulsive forces between them but there validity for non-circular particles is still not known. Particularly for a large number of particles, it becomes difficult to estimate a minimal collision force to keep the particles at some distance while obeying the underlying physics. 
The present work was motivated by the necessity to handle particle-particle, particle-wall and particle-obstacle collisions in the direct simulation of particulate flows. Our aim is to investigate and propose collision models to handle particles in fluids passing across obstacles and forming different flow patterns. Obstacles of different sizes and shapes play a major role in defining the new path of the moving rigid particles while the particles cross these obstacles. Different geometries for the fluid domain and obstacles will be considered to study and analyze the vortex formation, particle wakes, hydrodynamic drag and lift forces and the overall impact on the particulate flow system.

data.projectName: Identification of Meat Adulteration Sources in District Haripur, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The food allowed according to the Islamic law is called permissible food. All types of animal foods are permissible in Islam except those obtained from prohibited animal sources including dogs, donkeys, horses, pigs, predators and carrions. Pakistan holds the third largest meat market among OIC countries with an annual trade of 108 billion US dollars and is included in top ten meat and live cattle exporting countries to OIC. The recent prohibited meat selling scandals in Pakistan have not only put Pakistani Muslims but Muslims living in meat importing OIC countries in red alert in determining the presence of prohibited meat ingredients. This food falsification has direct impact on fair trades, public health, religious faith and wildlife. The innovations in packaging techniques and morphological similarities among cut, cooked and processed meat products have made it difficult or even impossible to identify sources of meat, based on physical attributes. Sale of meat and meat products has plummeted across Haripur after incidents of selling donkey and dog meat to butchers and restaurants in Haripur district. Present study designed to determine meat selling points, kinds of meat products, sources of meat falsification and public response about origin of meat and its falsification in district Haripur, Pakistan. Haripur district has a growing food market situated in Hazara region on the border of Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provinces. Study will be initiated with exploratory surveys of butcher shops, supermarkets, hotels and restaurants. During these reconnaissance visits, potential meat sampling sites will be identified. Satisfaction of local residents regarding meat and meat product selling in the market will be assessed by questionnaires. For molecular analysis, reference

data.projectName: Al, Cu and Zin micro particles coating using Cold Spray Technology
data.projectDigest:
In cold spray, particles ranging in size from 1 to 50 microns are heated and accelerated to a high velocity through a converging-diverging nozzle. Spray particles travel at high speed and after passing through the shock (in front of the substrate) impact on the substrate. The solid ductile particles, plastically deform on impact and consolidate to create coatings. Cold spray means a coating process where the temperature of sprayed particles at the time of injection into the nozzle is typically much lower than the melting temperature. In other words, cold spray particles are not necessarily heated separately before injection into the nozzle. Currently, Cold spray technology is used only in the USA, Germany, and Russia. Unfortunately, there is no such facility in Pakistan where microparticles coatings can be achieved successfully using cold spray technology. 
In this Project Coating of micro size, metal particles e.g. Aluminum, Copper and Zinc, etc. will be achieved using cold spray technology. Initially, micro size metal particles will be sprayed on a different substrate. In the second stage, bio-composite material will be coated on different teeth and bones for cracks filing. Mathematical models for successful deposition on particles will be developed based on experimental and numerical results.

data.projectName: Exploring the association of insecticides resistance and insecticides detoxifying enzymes in insect pests of rice fields of Lahore, Punjab: A major step to manage the pest Population.
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is an agricultural country. After wheat, rice is the second major cereal food and cash crop. It is Cultivated on almost an area of two million hectares primarily in the Punjab and Sindh followed by NWFP and Balochistan. Major insect pests are stem borers, leaffolders, leafhoppers, planthoppers and grasshoppers that attack rice crop and cause significant yield losses. Due to introduction of high yielding varieties in Pakistan, pests which were once minor pests are now considered major pests such as yellow stem borer, white stem borer, pink stem borer and stripped stem borer. There is dire need to manage pest population. Due to excess use of insecticides, resistance against them has been reported in a large number of arthropods species. Increased metabolic detoxification is one of the major mechanisms which supports insecticides resistance. Detoxification enzyme-based resistance is due to modified activities of esetrases, glutathione S- transferases (GST) or monooxygenases which prevent insecticide from reaching its site of action. Proposed project is designed to find the association of insecticides resistance and Detoxification enzymes. This study will prove as a major step to manage pest population.

data.projectName: IImpact of Population Growth on Economy of Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
The proposed study will collect, analyze and publish report on “Impact of Population Growth on Economy of Pakistan” and; will submit the conclusion of the study to Higher Education Commission (HEC). The research study will determine the relationship between population and economic growth in Pakistan, impact of rapid population growth on national economy and conclude the causes and effects of the increasing population phenomenon based on the findings of the study. The interventions of the study will be conducted in the target districts of Pakistan given the sample criteria. The study will present policy advice to the relevant stakeholders and institutions to overcome the increasing population's negative impacts on the economy and development of the country. 
This proposed study will research on certain crucial questions to understand the causal relationship between the higher population growth in Pakistan and its impact on economy i.e. “What are the key factors affecting population growth in Pakistan? What are direct and indirect impacts of population growth on the economy of Pakistan? What is the impact of state-owned policies in reduction of population growth in Pakistan?  What are the state’s priorities to control higher population growth in Pakistan?”. The findings of this study will further answer the reasons of population growth and its impact on economy, citizens’ basic needs and related facilities in response of economic growth of Pakistan. The findings of the study will act as a model for participatory action research and policy recommendations for policy reforms at provincial and national level.

What are direct and indirect impacts of population growth on the economy of Pakistan? What is the impact of state-owned policies in reduction of population growth in Pakistan?  What are the state’s priorities to control higher population growth in Pakistan?”. The findings of this study will further answer the reasons of population growth and its impact on economy, citizens’ basic needs and related facilities in response of economic growth of Pakistan. The findings of the study will act as a model for participatory action research and policy recommendations for policy reforms at provincial and national level.

data.projectName: Development of real-time flash flood early warning system via mobile at Lai Nullah basin
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Lai Nulla basin located in the twin cities of Islamabad and Rawalpindi has greatly affected by the flash flooding caused catastrophic loss of agricultural crops, livestock and infrastructure especially in densely populated areas of Rawalpindi. Every year Lai Nullah basin receives intense rainfall averaging 500mm in the monsoon season, cause the flooding in Islamabad and Rawalpindi.  Thus, the major goal of the project is to develop the community-based early flood warning system. This project aims at transferring the real time flood information to the end users using a mobile app named “Lai Nullah Flood Alert Application”. There will be an automated routines coupled with the hydrological model running every three hours in order to show real time and upcoming predicted condition of the water level at Lai Nullah. This community-based flood alert application will be composed of three major components; i) rain and water level gauges for the accumulation of rainfall and water level data of the Lai Nullah basin; ii) automatic module for transferring of observed rainfall and water level data to the database; iii) an android based mobile application which will be able to provide real time flash flood condition and able to send a warning message to the people. The major outcomes of the project will be; i) manual siren based warning system installed by PMD will be updated to the automated smart technology based warning system, ii) system will issue timely, trustable, and easily understandable warning messages with real time water level situation to authorities and the people at risk iii) it helps to improve community-based emergency planning, awareness and training in order to focus on effective response to warning and to reduce the risk to human lives and their livelihoods.

data.projectName: Study of Developing an Integrated Transportation Network for Rawalpindi
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Urban transportation schemes are introduced for the purpose of mobility and accessibility with the purpose of reduced congestion and carbon footprints. Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) and Metro Bus Services are the newly emerged transportation schemes being implemented in many metropolitan cities with the purpose of reducing congestion and increasing mobility of passengers making trips. Islamabad-Rawalpindi Metro Bus Service was initiated for the same purpose of enhancing the quality and reliability of the transportation in the twin cities of Islamabad and Rawalpindi. Once cannot fulfill objectives of the metro and BRTs until and unless it is interconnected / integrated with other connecting feeder routes. This project is aimed to develop a framework to serve an integration of Islamabad-Rawalpindi Metro Bus Service with the other transportation modes serving a sustainable approach to transportation system. It will involve the data collection form passengers and drivers of the private vehicles regarding socio-economic characteristics, travel modes, travel time, preference of modes between Metro Bus Stations and destinations. The project will introduce the models which will specify the provision of resources to the areas for integration, and will also work on the integration of fare system, provisions for parking spaces, integration of real time data and interchange points between Metro Bus and other modes. Intelligent Transportation System will be studied and its implementation will be made possible by introducing real time data, automatic fare collection system by collaboration with the operating, planning and private agencies, and involvement of passengers and stakeholders throughout the process for better implementation.

data.projectName: Synthesis and Study of Magnetotransport Phenomena in MoS2 and WS2: A Promising 2D Nanomaterials for Spintronic Applications
data.projectDigest: In the current technological devices the charge and spin of the electron have separately initiated. However, it has rarely been done to combine the two to function simultaneously in the same material. This was a great idea to incorporate these fundamental electronic properties, viz. charge and spin to form the basis for a new class of spin dependent device so called “spintronics”. The spintronic devises are expected to overcome upon traditional electronic devices, permitting for developments in the form of energy consumption, quick operation and a multifunction device operation. A diluted magnetic semiconductors, a class of semiconductor materials added with a very low concentration of magnetic/nonmagnetic atoms, permit to the conventional semiconductor technology to be employed in such applications. In order to get DMS materials in the spintronic applications, significant challenges related to synthesis parameters, solubility of magnetic/nonmagnetic atoms and intrinsic ferromagnetism for semiconductors must be addressed. Only semiconductors which exhibit ferromagnetism comfortably above room temperature are crucial to the practical application of spin-based devices as combination of magnetic spin and electronics. The above reasons have motivated to the magnetic and materials scientists in developing intrinsic ferromagnetism in DMS systems. In the last decade, there has been some achievement in attaining room temperature ferromagnetism in various transition metal doped semiconductors, but the results are, in general, non-reproducible among research groups and contradictory to the some theoretical predictions. The conflicting experimental results raise a new problem of explaining the mechanism of ferromagnetism in the DMS systems.

data.projectName: Construction of microbial cell factory through engineered strain of Saccharomyces cerevisiae for the production of?-santalol
data.projectDigest: Santalols including ?-Santalol and ?-Santalol are important sesquiterpenes and are major constituent of sandalwood oil. These santalols are highly valuable due to their application in perfume and cosmetic industry. Moreover, it has tremendous application in pharmaceutical and food industries. The chemical methods were designed to synthesize santalols but multiple step complexities, low recovery yield and high reaction conditions made this synthesis very expensive and impractical. The biosynthesis of santalol has not been reported and there is a dire need of a biological system which could efficiently synthesize ?-Santalol as it is the major ingredient of sesquiterpenes. Saccharomyces cerevisiae could be utilized for the production of ?-Santalol. The metabolic pathway involves the formation of farnesyl diphosphate (FPP) from dimethylallyl diphosphate and isoprenyl diphosphate, by FPP synthase (FPPS) and its regulation by santalene synthase (SaSSy), which could produce mixture of both santalols i.e. santalenes (?-, ?- and epi-?-santalene) and ?-exo-bergamotene. The conceptual design includes the potential use of multi-substrate cytochrome P450 dependent monooxygenase (P450) in Saccharomyces cerevisiae which could oxidize ?-, ?-, epi-?-santalene and bergamotene to produce ?-, ?-, epi-?-santalols and bergamotol, respectively. The use of different cytochromes P450 would be investigated for the oxidative production of different santalenes and bergamotene.

data.projectName: Inflammation, oxidative stress and antioxidant status in the blood of Alzheimer’s disease patients.
data.projectDigest: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the most common cause of dementia. Many factors are involved which may increase the probability of the disease. As the life expectancy in general is increasing, so the number of people affected by AD is also increasing. This situation leads to an increase in social, economic and health problems of the AD patients and their families/caregivers. There is no curative therapy available for AD. Inflammation plays an important role during the course of AD and may be crucial for the pathogenesis of AD. In addition, reactive oxygen species or ROS when produced in excess may affect the normal functioning of the cells. A system consisting of antioxidants can remove or detoxify these harmful reactive species thus preventing the cells from damage. At normal concentrations, ROS are required for the normal functioning of the cells. A disturbance in the balance of ROS and antioxidant systems leads to oxidative stress. In this project, we shall try to evaluate if there is an alteration in inflammation, oxidative stress and antioxidants status in the blood of AD patients. This may lead towards the identification of biomarkers and the development of potential therapeutics for AD.

data.projectName: Implementing Mobile Technology for Vocabulary Learning: Perceptions of ESL learners in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: English learners in Pakistan are facing a lot of problems to communicate efficiently and effectively with their peers, teachers and other educational professionals in an environment where English is considered compulsory to be used in a classroom. It has generally been observed that very less time is allocated to teach English vocabulary to the students at Pakistani universities due to the vast amount of course contents. That’s why students often feel communication hurdles. Moreover, the concept of digital game-based mobile Learning is not given due importance in Pakistan until now as there are limited number of Information Technology (I.T) universities. The scarce amount of resources and the traditional curriculum design does not allow the usage of smart phones for learning and teaching purposes. This study therefore, implement mobile game Application 'Kahoot' that students can have an access to it in their mobiles. English learners from all the state and non-state universities of Lahore will be taken to implement this application for vocabulary learning of undergraduate students studying English as a compulsory subject. After implementation of mobile game application, the perception of university students is investigated to know to what extend they think the usage of this mobile technology is useful for them. This study is significant for English as a Second Language university learners to improve their vocabulary to communicate. To know their perception, semi-structured interviews will be conducted and transcribed for further analysis afterwards.

data.projectName: Corporate Governance Index of Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
The code of Corporate Governance has affected the performance of firms and made sure that Investor's or Shareholder's interests are protected. The code of 2002, 2012 were simpler in terms of requirements but the criterion has drastically increased in 2017 which entails the idea to form an Index. This project insists on to formulate a National Corporate Governance Index which will serve as a standard for Industry, Policy Makers, Investors/shareholders & Security and Exchange Commission of Pakistan and many other stakeholders to assess the compliance to code of Corporate Governance.
The most objective is to develop corporate governance index for Pakistani listed firms which will serve as a Benchmark for future evaluations and assessment stakeholder’s whether firms are complying to the code of Corporate Governance issued by SECP. Since, corporate governance index has not been developed for Pakistani market, so none of the relationships of Corporate Governance Index with any market factors have been tested in context of Pakistani listed companies making it valuable contribution to policy makers and other stakeholders. Once Index is formed, it can be related with Firm performance indicators and will help in Bankruptcy predictions for the firms, which has benefits to policy makers, banks and investors weather individual or institutional.

data.projectName: Economic, Environmental and Socio-institutional Impacts of Leather Industry in Pakistan: A Sustainable Development Perspective
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan impacts of leather industry on environment and labor is not less than any other developing country. The labor of this industry is more prone to cancer disease due to its exposure to toxic chemicals and heavy metals. The residents living in a tannery area are five time more likely to get leukemia than other areas (PeTA, 2018). The catastrophic impacts on society can also be assessed in terms of waste water effluent and solid waste generated by this industry. The sludge generated by the industry causes choking of drains and bad odor. The solid chemical waste heaps are harmful for human beings and cast its adversity on biodiversity as well. This scenario calls for an investigation of Environmental Impact Assessment of the said business and to draw attention of this sector towards better product design approach. The proposed research has never received much attention before in Pakistan. The initiative towards said practices may lead to prosperity and achievement of sustainable development goal of cleaner production and resource conservation.

data.projectName: Development of bi-functional cerium based bio-hybrid for degradation of organic dyes and adsorption of hazardous metals: A critical approach to environment safety
data.projectDigest: Pollution of water is a significant worldwide issue. 95 percent of urban and industrial wastewater goes untreated into environment. Only 8 percent in poor nations and 38 percent of wastewater is treated due to expensive treatment plants. About 1.8 billion human beings consume contaminated water that can cause cholera, dysentery, polio and typhoid. The present study is designed to develop highly robust cerium based bio-hybrid for photo-catalytic and adsorptive elimination of color and toxic metal (As, Cr) from water for extraordinary low-cost, regenerative, eco-friendly performance in synthetic solutions and real effluent by batch and column study. In the second step the viability of reusing the treated effluent will also assessed to save water. The proposed project will address the sustainable development goals: 1) “Ensure availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all” by improving water quality, safe reuse of treated water and strengthen the participation of local communities in sanitation management.2) Ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all by reducing the mortality rate and illnesses from hazardous contaminations.

data.projectName: Operation optimization and Economic Analysis of Hybrid Solar PV and Concentrated Solar Power System
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: Renewable energy is becoming cheap and the technology is well established now. Major benefits of solar power include availability of pollution free abundant energy, absence of monopoly market and less maintenance. For Pakistan, utilization of solar energy due to its abundance, could be an important step to meet future energy demands. Solar PV systems can be integrated with Concentrated Solar Power (CSP) System (due to thermal energy storage capability) to generate electricity during cloudy periods or for hours after sunset or before sunrise. This ability to store solar energy makes the Hybrid Solar PV and CSP System a flexible and dispatchable source of renewable energy. An optimal mix of Solar PV and CSP plant can fully match the load fluctuations and thus do not need the costly battery storage facility.  The outcome of this research will be the availability of cheap, clean and stable electricity for extended periods of time in varying weather conditions throughout the year.

data.projectName: An analysis of influence of the principles of cultural blindness on the online marketing strategy of assistive technologies for collectivist and individualist societies: a comparative survey and eye-tracking of groups in Pakistan and United Kingdom
data.projectDigest:
The aim of the study is to provide designers of online sales and marketing material in Pakistan with a more effective approach to communicating the function and value of the products. In this project, through online images of assistive products presented to individuals from collectivist and individualist markets. The outcomes of this work will lead towards enhancing social acceptance through reframing of perceptions of assistive products and those who use them. 
The study will be jointly conducted by Product and Industrial Design (PID) department of University of Engineering and Technology (UET) Pakistan and the School of Design and Creative Arts (SDCA) in Loughborough University (LU) United Kingdom to better understand how people interpret the products they purchase and use. The study will provide additional insights into the ways in which designers influence people’s perception of assistive products and those who use them leading to a more inclusive society.  
The generic insights gained from this study may be used by individuals, groups and organizations to more effectively sell their wares. The study will contribute to the underpinning knowledge to influence individuals and society towards a more inclusive perception of AT products and people.

data.projectName: Thin Film Development of Nanocomposite Materials for Advanced Energy Conversion  Device (Solid Oxide Fuel Cells)
data.projectDigest: The world’s present reserves in terms of fossil fuels are exhausting speedily. The such rapidly consumption can be caused to indefensible progress that depends upon the energy produced in any way. Therefore, the researcher’s challenges are to identify the most efficient and economical energy sources to compete and replace the ongoing conventional energy resources. Additionally, the massive utilization of fossil fuels pollutes the environment with the emissions of CO2 that creates numerous difficulties upon human life as well as others living things. In this context, fuel cell technology can play a key role and compete to convert hydrocarbon energy into electrical energy. Fuel Cell technology is a newly emerging field of science and technology and signifies a hopeful pollution free device, but the technology is not yet has an impact to compete with established conventional technologies.  Solid Oxide Fuel Cell (SOFC) is considered the most top priority power-generation technology due to efficient and clean conversion of chemical energy to electricity, no pollution and contamination, no need for water management and multi-fuel opportunity. No doubt, SOFC is a highly efficient energy conversion device, but it is in still facing numerous difficulties with i) high operating temperature (1000 oC), ii) material degradation, iii) instability factor, and cell thickness. In this project, the solution of said challenges will be addressed and efforts will be equipped to lowering the operating temperature (300-500oC). The thin film will be developed of optimized materials (high performance) and electrode's slurry will be deposited by screen printing technology in micro-range thickness to complete three layers cell. The proposed work will be initiative step towards commercialization.

data.projectName: Multivariate Extensions to the q- Generalized Extreme Value Distribution and Moment-Based Methodologies for Modelling “Big Data".
data.piUniversity: Kohat University of Science and Technology, Kohat
data.projectDigest:
Extreme value theory assumes a significant role in statistical analysis. It depends on the stochastic (random) behaviour of the extreme values in a process. For a single process, the asymptotic behaviour of the maxima can be depicted by the three extreme value distributions- the Gumbel, Fre’chet and reversed Weibull models. It can be applied to predict the occurrence of rare events. The forecast of food levels, large jumps in the stock markets and extreme insurance claims are for instance areas of application. The generalized extreme value (GEV) distributions are widely utilized in hydrology, economics, finance, actuarial science, engineering, time series modelling, material sciences, telecommunications, reliability analysis, risk management, as well as many other fields of scientific investigation involving extreme events. 
In this proposal, I am hereby proposing to introduce the bivariate q - GEV and bivariate q -Gumbel distributions.
Multivaraite density estimation approach that depends on a univariate density approximation procedure is proposed which produces differentiated log-density approximants (DLDA's) whereby the derivative of the logarithm of a density function is assumed to be expressible as a rational function. This approach just requires the moments of a distribution up to some particular order; accordingly, when utilized related to sample moments, it enables one to process large amounts of data that often arrive in streams without having to access recently gathered observations.

data.projectName: Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF) Gene Polymorphism in Diabetes Mellitus and Diabetic Retinopathy Patients of Balochistan
data.piUniversity: Balochistan University of Information Technology, Engineering and Management Sciences,Quetta
data.projectDigest: Diabetes Mellitus (DM) is a non-communicable, prevalent and group of metabolic disorders found worldwide. This disease is classified into two categories that are: Insulin Dependent DM (IDDM or Type 1) and Non-Insulin Dependent DM (NIDDM or Type 2).This disease is associated with certain microvascular complications which includes small blood vessels such as capillaries supplying eyes, brain and kidneys are affected thus leading the diabetes associated microvascular complications. This proposed research is based on microvascular complications of retina of eyes in diabetic patients termed as Diabetic Retinopathy (DR). The proposed research aims to identify the polymorphisms (Occurrence of two or more clearly different morphs or forms) in VEGF (Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor) gene DM and DR patients of Balochistan, Pakistan. Then comparison to find out the risk factors that leads to the development and progression of DR in patients of Balochistan.

data.projectName: Automation and Extension of MICE-PES Algorithm to complex natural products for their accurate conformational analysis and calculation of spectroscopic properties
data.projectDigest:
There are several drugs in the market that originated from naturally occurring molecules before their laboratory synthesis. A number of drugs are chiral and, in many cases, different isomer of a chiral drug may not be beneficial at all or even poisonous. Thus, careful determination of their structure is critical for their synthesis and investigation of pharmacological properties. A lot of these secondary metabolites are structurally flexible and can co-exist in many different conformations which makes it challenging to determine their relative configuration experimentally. To analyze the structure computationally, all the conformers that have a contribution to the chemical properties of the compound must be considered for computations.
Currently available conformational analysis tools utilize different molecular mechanics methods and generate a large number of possible conformers and are not general-purpose, thus compromising accuracy. Also, the force field methods used in available tools have been formulated for specific classes of compounds and don’t produce good results beyond their scope.
The main objective of this research proposal is to extend the scope of MICE-PES (Method for the Incremental Construction and Exploration of the Potential Energy Surface), developed by PI during his PhD research work, to condensed ring systems, add ring conformations, add other functional groups than carbon, extensively benchmark it against a number of different flexible natural molecules and catalysts, and fully automate it.

data.projectName: Gain enhancement and bandwidth improvement of 2D Metasurface Antenna using Composite Synthetic Polymers
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: This project is focused on the use of indigenously manufactured synthetic polymers in designing 2D metasurface antenna. Novelty in the proposal involves use of composite synthetic polymer as metasurface instead of Commercial of the Shelf (COTS) substrates. COTS based substrates are very expensive and have higher permittivity as compared to composite synthetic polymers. Gain enhancement and bandwidth improvement can be achieved using synthetic polymers because of their low refractive index. 2D Metasurface antenna will be designed, manufactured and tested to validate its performance. Reconfigurable metasurface antenna technology will support 5G & IoT in future.

data.projectName: Spatial Dependence Modelling and Kriging Prediction with Presence only Data
data.projectDigest: Presence-only data occurs in many disciplines such as species distribution modelling,  disease epidemiology, geocology, and many others, where often the only information that can be recorded as data is the presence of an attribute at certain coordinates location. The absences are usually hard to collect due to infinite possibilities, sampling difficulties and/or prohibitive expenses. For statistical analysis purposes pseudo-absences are generated using MAXENT at suitable locations by modelling the presences as a function of covariates (e.g. bioclimatic, anthropogenic, geographical variables). The number of pseudo-absences is still an open research question despite some authors suggests using 10,000 pseudo absences for typical regression models. It has been argued that when modelling the distributions of species using presence/absence data the distance between observations must be taken into account because the associated covariates exhibit spatial dependence within their own values. 10000 absences results in a biased kriging. We propose to use the principle of maximum entropy which enables us to choose a distribution with highest uncertainty or zero bias. This project will investigate more ways that help to better understand and model and the present spatial patterns of risk, the contribution of influential factors that lead to the presence and prevalence of species/epidemic diseases.

data.projectName: Smart Health: Health Assistance for Dementia and Sleeplessness
data.piUniversity: National University of Computer and Emerging Sciences, Islamabad
data.projectDigest: Mental healthcare services have been around for decades in most developed countries. These services consume a significant portion of health care budget. The health care workers are also overloaded as of present, due to increasing number of reported mental health related cases. To assist in the present situation, recent developments in technology can play an important role. The technology advancements introduce new and efficient means to revolutionize the existing health care infrastructure. With the use of modern technologies, smart sensors (mobile phone sensors and wearable technologies) and classification and modelling techniques, the vital conditions of patient’s mental health can be evaluated without investing too many resources and manpower. In this work, a complete system for remote sensing, communications and identification of common mental health issues along with extensive diagnosis using machine learning techniques is proposed. In the proposed system, a sensor network to detect mental health conditions, record and monitor body vitals and machine-based analysis will be introduced to identify mental health disorders like bipolar disorder, depression and schizophrenia. The proposed system will also monitor other body properties like hydration, nutrient levels, blood pressure, temperature, ECG and EMG signals to subsequently formulate and suggest suitable preventive and curing measures.

data.projectName: Molecular characterization of Multi Drug Resistant Enterobacteriacea isolates from Animal product by focusing the dissemination of resistance encoding genes to humans
data.projectDigest:
The rapidly increasing risk of antimicrobial resistance in bacteria, particularly in Gram negative bacteria of Enterobacteriacea, is seriously threatening the veterinary and public health. Theses microbes have self-developed or acquired tools to protect themselves from the deleterious effects of antimicrobial agents by making them inactive by various means such as extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBL) enzymes and carbapenemases. Consequently, ESBL-, Carbapenemase- producing Enterobacteriacea is characterized by their resistance to virtually all beta-lactam antimicrobials including cephalosporin and carbapenems. Additionally, many of these strains are also co-resistant to other non-beta-lactam antimicrobials such as fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides and sulpha drugs. Livestock including cattle, buffaloes and poultry are usually considered as one of the important reservoirs of multidrug resistant (MDR) bacteria. Therefore, knowledge on the epidemiology (prevalence, sources and transmission routes) and characterization of the resistance determinates in MDR bacteria and their spreading mechanism is crucial to plan any control and prevention strategies. It has been reported that ESBL- and carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceaare highly prevalent in cattle and chicken has been implicated as a source of those resistant Enterobacteriaceastrains present in the human population. In some previous studies, close genetic similarities were found among ESBL-, carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceaisolates from chicken meat and humans on the basis of mobile resistance elements, virulence genes, and genomic backbone. 
However, due to limited resources, comprehensive studies describing characteristics and mechanisms of spread of ESBL- and Carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriac

data.projectName: 5G Radio Simulator - An Efficient Ray-tracing based Radio Channel Simulator for Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) and UAV-assisted 5G and beyond Millimeter Wave Networks
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
The development of fifth generation of wireless networks or so-called 5G is underway to support enhanced mobile broadband for data rates up to 10 Gbps, ultra-reliable low latency communications for mission-critical applications and massive machine type communications for intelligent internet of things (IoT) applications. The efficient computer simulations based models to predict the radio signals propagation in dynamic 5G scenarios such as vehicle-to-everything (V2X) and UAV-assisted millimetre wave (mmwave) networks are not available. This research aims to develop accurate and time efficient radio channel models for V2X and UAV-assisted mmwave networks. 

The mmwave radio channel sounding equipment is not available at local universities in Pakistan. Likewise the commercially available simulation tools for radio channel modeling are very expensive. This limits the research community in Pakistan to contribute in the radio propagation modeling. The accurate and time efficient models developed in this research will be packaged in a simulator with an interactive graphical user interface. This tool will be made freely available for local universities to promote research and development in 5G in Pakistan. With the recent authorization by Pakistan Telecommunications Authority (PTA) to mobile operators for 5G trials, this simulator will be highly beneficial to the industry as well.
data.projectSummary:
The development of fifth generation of wireless networks or so-called 5G is underway to support enhanced mobile broadband for data rates up to 10 Gbps, ultra-reliable low latency communications for mission-critical applications and massive machine type communications for intelligent internet of things (IoT) applications. The efficient computer simulations based models to predict the radio signals propagation in dynamic 5G scenarios such as vehicle-to-everything (V2X) and UAV-assisted millimetre wave (mmwave) networks are not available. This research aims to develop accurate and time efficient radio channel models for V2X and UAV-assisted mmwave networks. 

The mmwave radio channel sounding equipment is not available at local universities in Pakistan. Likewise the commercially available simulation tools for radio channel modeling are very expensive. This limits the research community in Pakistan to contribute in the radio propagation modeling. The accurate and time efficient models developed in this research will be packaged in a simulator with an interactive graphical user interface. This tool will be made freely available for local universities to promote research and development in 5G in Pakistan. With the recent authorization by Pakistan Telecommunications Authority (PTA) to mobile operators for 5G trials, this simulator will be highly beneficial to the industry as well.

data.projectName: Poultry
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: The interactions between nutrition, environment and poultry production for human consumption are complex, involving multiple ingredient usage at different levels in poultry diets, environmental challenges due to nutrient loss in droppings, measures to improve growth and to reduce disease burden in poultry production. Further, combating anti-microbial resistance is one of the most important challenge under one health concept. The one objective is to analyze the feed and waste samples from poultry farms to assess nutrient loss in droppings. Indigenous production and utilization of feed enzyme with lower amount of nutrients would definitely reduce the nutrient loss and be helpful to reduce carbon footprints involved in feed production and utilization. In addition, protein meal production for poultry will be done through agriculture waste to reduce import bill. This would also improve waste utilization and reduce the burden on traditional protein supplements. The propaganda of using drugs/hormones in poultry diets will also be addressed by producing & using indigenous probiotic instead of antibiotics as growth promoters. The meat samples will be analyzed for drug residues. Therefore, the hypothesis of environmentally safe and drug free poultry production can be attained through re-formulating diet with low amount of nutrients and supplementation with indigenously produced products.

data.projectName: Deep Learning Fuzzy Information Fusion for Multiple Domain Representations
data.projectDigest: Digital image processing and analysis is an established discipline enabling many business organization to work with ease. The number of images produced by individuals and organizations of all types around the World are ever increasing and expected to generate more image data in future. This research project investigates and develops a deep learning fuzzy-based information fusion technique for digital image representations in spatial-, frequency-, and wavelet-domain. The developed technique is implemented on a super computer module based on graphics processing unit for medical image enhancement application and to achieve reduced processing time with better output for large amount of image data. The deep learning refers to the set of algorithms based on neural networks to extract information and learn from raw data. The choice of fuzzy theory is due its ability to capture the expert knowledge in the form of rules. Information fusion deals with improving results by incorporating multiple revisits to some phenomenon under investigation. Transformations in spatial, frequency, and wavelets triplet domain provide appropriate representations of a scene for better analysis and ease in extraction of useful information helpful to the medical specialist for improved disease diagnosis based on complex process of visual examination. The prototype system is implemented as a pilot in hospital setup with compliance to medical practice norms.

data.projectName: Development of microbial consortia to improve the growth and yield of sesame on salt affected soils
data.projectDigest: Salinity is a major abiotic factor responsible for low yield in Pakistan. It affects plant growth through reduction in water and nutrient uptake. Sesame is an important oil seed crop with high oil contents however, being moderately salt sensitive crop, its growth and yield is severely affected on salt affected soils. Biological approaches can alleviate harmful impacts of salt stress on plant. Salt tolerant, plant growth promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) possess the potential to promote plant growth under salt-stressed environment through different mechanisms. Extracellular enzyme production is an important mechanism to regulate the plant metabolic activities and nutrient uptake which ultimately improve plant growth. These salt tolerant PGPR can also optimize these enzyme activities under exposure to severe salt stress thereby, enhance plant growth under stressed environment. In the proposed study, PGPR having capability to survive under salt stress will be isolated and screened for their ability to produce stress regulating enzymes and plant growth promoting metabolites. Selected bacteria will be tested in series of lab, pot and field trials and a biofertilizer will be formulated to improve sesame production in salt affected fields.

data.projectName: Robust Array Signal Processing against Sensor Failures and Uncertainties
data.projectDigest:
To describe the proposed research geared to the non – specialized reader, it is necessary to relate the project with human analogy system. Let  two persons are involved in conversation inside a dark room. They cannot see each other but the listener among them can listen the speaker by receiving the voice of the speaker on his ears. After reception the voice, the human brain process the information to determine the direction of the speaker. Moreover, if additional (unwanted) speaker join the conversation, the human brain tries to reject the unwanted speaker and concentrate on the one who is desired speaker for him. At the same time, the listener can respond to the desired speaker direction by orienting his mouth (transmitter) towards the speaker.
Electrical smart antennas system function in the same way i.e., instead of human ear it uses antennas to receive the signal and then instead of human brain, the Digital Signal Processor process the signal to determine the direction of the received signal. After that it adjusts its excitation i.e., phases and gain to transmit the information in the desired direction, while placing nulls in the undesired direction. 
In many real time situation, it is  possible that one or more antennas get failed or uncertainty occurs in the  system. In this project, we will investigate robust sensor array signal processing against failures and uncertainties and their applications to sensor systems. We will investigate recently reported non uniform sensor arrays, their signal models and examine the impact of uncertainties and failures associated with sensors on the array response and their potential losses. The study of the impact of failures and uncertainties will be used in the design of more robust non uniform sensor array.

data.projectName: Search for Novel Antidiabetic Compounds from the Medicinal Plants of Jammu & Kashmir
data.piUniversity: Mirpur University of Science and Technology (MUST), AJ&K
data.projectDigest:
Diabetes mellitus has reached epidemic proportions worldwide and it has emerged as a great socioeconomic burden for the developing world. 
	The International Diabetes Federation (IDF) released new figures highlighting the alarming growth in the prevalence of diabetes around the world on World Diabetes Day marked around the globe on November 14, 2019.  Pakistan is now in the list of top 10 countries of the world for absolute increase in diabetes prevalence.
	Pakistan is spending a huge money for this import. In 2019, India ordered to its pharmaceutical companies to halt the supply of the medicinal raw material to Pakistan for an indefinite time in the wake tensions between the two countries. According to the Pakistan Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Association, around 40% to 50% of the raw material for medicine made in Pakistan is imported from India. Owing to the topographical variations, Kashmir Himalaya harbors a rich diversity of medicinal plants. With concerns regarding the emerging issue of diabetes in Pakistan, there is urgent need to investigate and search the new and efficient anti-diabetic compounds from the medicinal plants of Kashmir.
Consequently, developments of new and effective medicine is of the utmost importance for treatment of hyperglycemia in type-2 diabetes. Effective measures can be made for the identification of medicinal plants on the basis of ethno botanical information and to isolate anti-diabetic compounds from them by using classical chromatographic, rapid resolution HPLC method as well as fast and efficient high speed counter-current chromatographic (HSCCC) method. So isolation and structure elucidation of new compounds will add information to the natural product chemistry and open new area of research for natural product chemistry in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Finite Element Simulations of Fluid  Flow and Heat Transfer in Closed Geometries
data.projectDigest: Flows inside closed geometries are particularly alluring one for the computational fluid dynamists and experimentalist for many years. Flow inside cavity has been the subject of numerous computational investigations, serving as a benchmark problem for testing new or improved numerical techniques and their codes. Till to date, many researchers have successfully studied the lid-driven cavity flows and heat transfer of Newtonian fluids involving different cavity shapes under different imposed temperature gradients in the literature. Since there are many phenomena which cannot be describe by the Newtonian Fluids. The objective of the proposed research is to study, the benchmark problem of mixed convection flow of Newtonian/non-Newtonian fluid inside the cavity under different situations. The finite element simulation code will be developed and tested first as to compare our limiting results with the results available in literature. Later, this code will be used to see the effects of non-Newtonian parameters against various Reynolds number on flow bifurcation and corner eddies in the cavity regions. The results will be shown graphically and their comparison will be prepared with the experimental date if available.

data.projectName: Meta-genomic and Genomic approach to evaluate the gut associated holibiont virome changes mediated by excessive use of antibiotics.
data.projectDigest: Overuse of antibiotics and over prescription poses certain risks including antibiotic resistance, severe disease consequences, increased disease length, health complications, adverse side effects, death risk, hospitalizations and re-hospitalizations, treatment costs, that may previously resolved on their own. Moreover these medicines are known to alter the normal microbiome/ microbiota of the host. The process is known as dysbiosis. Gut is a holibiont in itself where we can find associated bacteria and viruses living in close association with their host. Although the antibiotics do not have a direct effect on viruses but by disturbing one component of ecosystem the whole system alters and this alteration in microbiomes and viromes may result in some known diseases including artherosclerosis, dyslipidemia, obesity, hypertension, diabetes mellitus and heart failure. Microbiome can alter the drug response by utilizing the ability to metabolize medications. The gut virome is also a very important component of holobiont infecting host cells and other commensals, therefore directly affecting our wellbeing. Despite its predominance, the virome remains one of the least understood components of the gut microbiota, with appropriate analysis toolkits still in development. The current study will focus on the gut virome, its composition, alterations in virome associated with antibiotic over and misuse from Pakistani population. The results will be a significant contribution towards the management of disease and designing strategies for better treatment options.
