data.projectName: Numerical solution of the boundary value problems arising in fluid dynamics, hydro magnetic stability, hydrodynamic and long wave theory
data.projectDigest:
In the study of problems arising in astrophysics, problem of heating of infinite horizontal layer of fluid, eigenvalue problems arising in thermal   instability, obstacle, unilateral, moving and free boundary-value problems, problems of the defection of plates and in a number of other scientific applications, we find a system of differential equations of different order with different boundary conditions. In general, it is not possible to obtain the analytical solution of them; we usually resort to some numerical methods for obtaining an approximate solution of these problems. 
Splines have been widely used to approximate differential equations due to their ability to produce highly accurate solutions. In mathematics, a spline is a special function defined piecewise by polynomials. Using these spline functions we drive a few consistency relations which to be used for computing approximations to the solution for high order boundary value problems.
B-spline curves and surfaces are well known geometric modeling tools in Computer
Aided Geometric Design (CAGD). The literature contains few on the solution of boundary value problems by using the B-splines. This motivates us to use Hyperbolic B-splines of order 3 to solve these problems. The recommended method transforms the boundary problem to a system of linear equations.

Using these spline functions we drive a few consistency relations which to be used for computing approximations to the solution for high order boundary value problems.
B-spline curves and surfaces are well known geometric modeling tools in Computer
Aided Geometric Design (CAGD). The literature contains few on the solution of boundary value problems by using the B-splines. This motivates us to use Hyperbolic B-splines of order 3 to solve these problems. The recommended method transforms the boundary problem to a system of linear equations.

data.projectName: Strategies to increase the meat and milk production of cholistani goats through GnRH/hCG supplementation
data.projectDigest: The present study is planned to determine the effects of hCG/GnRH on reproductive performance in local goats of  cholistan desert of Bahawalpur. It is expected that this treatment given in an appropriate dose at a specific time would improve litter size mainly by reducing embryonic mortality, which varies from 20 to 65% in some breeds. During the first phase, some breeds with higher rate of embryonic mortality will be selected and then appropriate time and dose of hCG/GnRH will be determined by hormonal analysis. Finally a field trial will be conducted to establish the efficacy of hCG/GnRH treatment in improving the pregnancy rate and litter size.

data.projectName: Development of Feasible Methods for Industrial Scale Extraction of Essential oils from local aromatic plants for their use in food and pharmaceutical industries: An applied Project to reduce import and Save Foreign Exchange
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is rich with aromatic flora, like citrus fruits, Eucalyptus, peppermint, lemon grass and black seed; however, essential oils of these plants/fruits are being imported. Thus Pakistan is spending a huge foreign exchange in importing various essential oils (Table 1), or their isolates and or the essential oil based products, which otherwise if isolated from local sources may save huge foreign exchange. Fewer oils are being produced in Pakistan to a limited extent for example menthol but it is not meeting the international standard as most of them are being extracted by the old techniques and procedures, besides have limited production capacity. Therefore, there is a crucial need to establish feasible methods for the extraction/production of essential oils from indigenous sources which will not only save the foreign exchange but also will help to improve the economy of the community. The purpose of this project is to develop cost effective feasible methods for extraction of essential oils from local aromatic plants.

data.projectName: Synthesis of efficient nanofiltration membrane for removal of toxic elements from drinking water of different resources
data.projectDigest: The aquatic environment is considered to the main factor controlling the state of health and disease in both human and animals. In aquatic systems, elements are present as dissolved ions and complexes, suspended, colloids ions and solid in sediments. Concentrations of these ions strongly depend on biological processes, redox potential, ionic strength, pH, activities of organic and inorganic chelates and scavenging processes. Therefore, surface and ground water quality determination is important factor in all regions.A literature search revealed a lack of up-to-date and detailed review articles on the use of membrane technologies for heavy metal removal. Our plan is to characterize the adsorption mechanism of different toxic elements (cadmium, lead, arsenic) on the different types of synthesized  nanofiltration membrane and modified  carbon cloth using advance analytical instrumentations. Moreover, the influence of different parameters i.e., pH of solution, toxic elemental concentrations and their species, synthesized nanofilteraturation membranebehaviour, i.e.  dosage, temperature and contact time, will be studied in detail. The thermodynamic mechanism of adsorption will be also studied

data.projectName: Stability of a headrace tunnel in a highly active seismic area
data.projectDigest: Power crises is one of the main hurdle in achieving sustainable economic development in Pakistan. In recent years, numerous hydropower projects have been planned, many are in construction phase to harness abundant green and cheap electricity. The northern mountainous region of Pakistan has lot of potential of hydropower but due to highly active seismic area the construction challenges are massive. Deep tunnelling poses many problems e.g. rock softening, rock bursting, squeezing, swelling and running ground etc. Proper assessment of rock mass parameters, understanding of geology, measurement of geo-stresses, in-situ measurement of deformation and stresses, the mechanical evolution of rock mass during excavation, and safety assessment of tunnel support during tunnelling can lead to successful completion of a tunnelling project. Suki Kinari is an 870 MW run of the river hydropower project located in the middle reaches of Kunhar River, KPK province, Pakistan. The mechanical characteristic of surrounding rock mass plays a crucial role in controlling the safety of the whole construction process. Insufficient understanding of rock mass properties and governing mechanical laws under complex geological conditions lead to accidents. In this context, this study carries out a series of research work to evaluate the mechanical properties of surrounding rocks, distribution of stresses, performance of tunnel support, stability and safety a water diversion tunnel of Suki Kinari Hydropower project in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Determination of Cyanogenic Potential of Livestock Fodders and Evaluation of Putative Antidotes for Reversal of Cyanide Toxicity using Animal Models
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Cyanide is widely distributed in the ecosystem and has been associated with toxic effects in humans and animals. Cyanide toxicity may be the result of intake from food sources, environmental pollution, intentional ingestion, chemical warfare, occupational exposure, and homicide. However, in certain countries, the highest occurrence of cyanide toxicity in animals is due to the ingestion of common plants that contains lethal levels of cyanide.  Such accidental poisonings may result in heavy economic losses due to death of animals.  The onset of cyanide toxicity is sudden! Thus, needs for dynamic and immediate treatment to overcome the toxic effects. This project will be described in four sets of studies. In study 1, levels of cyanide in different livestock fodders will be determined. In Study-2, efficacy of garlic extract and other putative antidotes against cyanide toxicity will be detemined in a mice.  In Study-3,  gralic extract and other cyanide antidotes will be evaluated in a goats. In Study-4, preventative effect of garlic against cyanide toxicity will be detemined in goats. At the completion, we will better understand the cyanogenic potential of livestock fodders, and will be able to understand cyanide antidotes especially garlic as a cheap, effective and readily available antidote.

data.projectName: Morphological and fungal induced modifications process in promising commercial cut flowers and foliage crops for commercial purposes
data.projectDigest: Cut-flower industry in Pakistan faced a critical issues of its growth, poor quality, continuously shedding of flora lets and its parts and lower production that have been observed in all major areas of Pakistan. This project will explore the effect of inoculation of AMF fungi on floriculture industry of Pakistan. VAM penetrates in the roots of a vascular plant in order to help them to capture nutrients from the soil. The role of Vesicular-arbuscular mycorrhiza VAM fungi will be monitored in terms of enhancement in essential oil production via activated system of photosynthetic apparatus. It will provides a summary of the potential applications of biotechnology in floriculture and reviews progress to date, with a particular emphasis on the manipulation of flower color. The project will also cover the analysis of several important morphological and biochemical parameters of floriculture under AM inoculation in comparison of non-inoculated plants using advanced technologies. The morphological and genetic modification with better strains will be find out as a proper regulation of the ethylene pathway and other necessary linked enzymes and biological process will be documented during dual symbiosis including all bioactive  compounds and essential elements. This project will be helpful to increase the export of Cut-flower in international market.

data.projectName: Programming and design, construction and post occupancy evaluation of a low-cost green guest house with focus on thermal behaviour and natural ventilation
data.projectDigest: The objective of this study is to re-establish and reuse the concept of natural ventilation in buildings that are greatly depended on mechanical or active cooling, rather than natural or passive cooling. It is hypothesized that designing and applying natural ventilation in buildings, will make them more efficient in cooling, improve their indoor air quality and reduce the cost of living.To achieve the mentioned goal, the research attempts to program, design and construct a 60 sqm residential unit as a prototype of a sustainable and low-cost housing component with focus on using natural ventilation as cooling system.After construction, unit will be examined for post occupancy evaluation (POE) by monitoring its thermal behavior, indoor air quality, construction techniques, workmanship and material selection. The monitoring will be done for the period of one full year to cover four seasons and actual usage of energy and co2 emissions will be calculated, considering the role of variables. All the parameters will be identified and analyzed in a quantitative and qualitative research methods.

data.projectName: Deep Vision based Suspicious Human Behavior Recognition using IoT for Surveillance
data.projectDigest:
The evolution of technology, now a days, have become the need of the people. Technology has made it possible to keep an eye on people’s actions and generating an alarm for any suspicious activity in real time. Automatic, cost effective and accurate system is required to develop a framework which works under varying environmental conditions for the monitoring of the suspicious activities. 
The broader set of human activities and diverse range of different backgrounds will play an important role in maintaining security and detecting any abnormal activity in real time happening in surroundings. The main objective is to detect the human faces, their sequence of actions, identify the suspicious actions to generate alarm or highlight them to the control centers. Internet of things (IOT) frameworks are also helpful in detection of such activities, communicating this information with other IOT devices and classification of suspicious actions. The proposed system will find its applications in public places like shopping malls, restaurants, mosques, banks, hospitals and particularly in maintaining surveillance. It will help to strengthen the economy by reducing the budget being spent on security which do not produce real time results to align with the Vision 2030 of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Comprehensive documentation of the traditional ethnobotanical utilization of plants native to Faisalabad district: An attempt towards digitization and preservation of ethnic knowledge
data.projectDigest:
Plants were imperative for human civilization. Local populations, specifically developing nations rely on them for healthcare, ornamental, nutritional, ceremonial and construction purposes; to serve as cost-effective, safe and affordable substitute. Traditional ethnobotanical knowledge passed down to generations orally. Unfortunately, this trend is vanishing due to lack of present generation interest, improper communication and lack of documentation.
Pakistan, being culturally diverse, favor innovative plants utility. Majority surveys focus on medicinal utility ignoring other services. Faisalabad district, former Lyallpur, is third largest and industrially important district of Punjab province, Pakistan. It include 6 tehsils: Chak Jhumra, Faisalabad City, Faisalabad Saddar, Jaranwala, Samundri and Tandlianwala. Ethnobotanical documentation of few areas of Faisalabad district was conducted previously but were not in line with latest ethnobotanical trends.
Ethnobotanical data will be collected via interviews, targeting respondents by random and purposive sampling. Informants’ data and provided information (local plant name, part(s) used, nature of utilization and methods of application) will be recorded. Also, native plants will be collected, identified and voucher specimen will be submitted in herbarium. Data will be analyzed by quantitative indices: Informant Consensus Factor, Use value, Relative frequency citation, Fidelity level, Relative popularity level and Rank order priority.
Project will compile detailed list of plants native to Faisalabad district, provide digital database about their ethnobotanical utility by locals, help commercial sector to develop better products for mankind and provide incentive for sustainable use and conservation of indigenous plants.

data.projectName: “Development of cognizance and linkages to promote agriprenuership conviction between Women University students and Farmers- with an application of agripreneurship portal”.
data.projectDigest: Agricultural sector has been transformed globally from the subsistence to commercial agriculture to ensure food security and self-employment through agripreneurship. However, in Pakistan the concept of agripreneurship is still at its nascent. There is a declining number of young-educated women who aspire to pursue agriculturally-related professions / careers which is mainly due to the various impediments for the women to capitalize opportunities in the subject of agripreneurship. Among the identified factors, the most challenging one is to create awareness and to train them to understand the subject of agripreneurship. Agricultural transformation has to be led by the private-sector since farmers need access to finance, inputs, information and/or markets. Hence, there is also a need for the industry linkages specifically the involvement of private sector to invigorate the concept of agripreneurship. To date agripreneurship is still an untapped area and little effort has been devoted on the research & development of women centric agripreneurship skills by the business students. The aim of the project is to introduce agripreneurship in business school curriculum as an elective subject to make it more learner-centric such that young people would be equipped with skills enabling them to develop agricultural income-generating projects to improve their livelihoods while lifting their communities. In view of the on-going context, the proposed project intends to deliver technical knowledge and market information to the selected female-students and connect them with the private-sector and ultimately with the female-farmers to understand the resources available to promote the culture of agripreneurship in urban–rural areas of Rawalpindi District & Islamabad – which can be later on

data.projectName: Rice Ratooning Technology: A sustainable and resource efficient way to enhance productivity and intensification of small-holder farms in central Punjab-Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Agriculture sector is the backbone of Pakistan’s economy, and this sector is mainly owned by small farmers. Specifically, in Punjab province, more than 90% farmers have small land holdings. Therefore, in order to sustain the Pakistan’s agricultural growth, the performance of small land holders needs to be improved. In this context, sustainable intensification of small farms is the only viable option to increase productivity and profitability with enhanced use and efficiency of local resources. Adopting rice ratooning technology may enhance the functional capacity of the rice-based systems to sustain productivity, enhance farm income, ensure food security, help conserve natural resources, and ultimately alleviate rural poverty with focus on small farmers. Although, considerable progress has been made worldwide to enhance the productivity and profitability of rice-ratoon rice system, yet, this technology has not been practiced in Pakistan probably because of lack of information and research regarding production practices and selection of suitable cultivar. In the proposed project, a series of multi-location trails will be conducted to investigate the feasibility and profitability of ratoon rice in different area of central Punjab, and to find out and recommend the ways to enhance the total rice productivity, resource use efficiency, and farmer’s income.

data.projectName: A Privacy-focused Intelligent Fog Computing System for Blood Pressure and Diabetes Care using Wearable Internet of Things
data.projectDigest:
This applied research project would develop an integrated intelligent ecosystem for the patients of blood pressure and diabetes (especially type-1 and elderly). This ecosystem would consists of four components: (i) two wearable sensors, one for glucose monitoring and the other for blood pressure, (ii) a wrist-band which would host: two wearable sensors, and a Wi-Fi module, (iii) a mobile application to receive notifications from wristband, (iv) a lightweight fog-node for performing machine learning-based computations based on wearable sensor data to predict any forthcoming medical emergency. The fog-node would call the family mobile number if the emergency danger crosses a predefined threshold. The fog-node would be owned by the patient and placed within the premises of patient. Available solutions only provide either BP or glucose monitoring but not both. They cannot predict forthcoming emergency nor handle it.

Work Flow :
=======
1. The patient shall wear wristband containing sensors.

2. To maintain privacy, an IoT sensor complaint lightweight public key cryptography shall be used.

3. The wristband shall display and, send BP and glucose levels to the Fog node.

4. The Fog node shall be equipped with a machine learning module. It would classify patient health state as normal, pre-emergency or emergency.

5. In case of pre-emergency state, the pre-configured mobile app shall be notified to avoid a forthcoming emergency hazard.

6. In case of emergency, the family member of the patient (or optionally, an emergency response unit of patient's hospital) shall receive automated call from the fog-node.

7. The family doctor of the patient would be able to view patient health summary (daily, two days, etc.) and the effects of a new medicine using mobile app.

data.projectName: Seismic Performance Assessment of Non-engineered (Dhajji and Bhattar) Structures
data.projectDigest: Bhatar and Dhajji are non-engineered structural construction techniques. They are commonly practiced in the North part of Pakistan like Chitral, Swat etc, because of its advantages as compared to concrete structure and brick/block masonry structures from economical and constructive point of view. Therefore, this research will be started with a reconnaissance survey, which will be executed in Chitral and Swat districts to study Bhatar and Dhajji construction. In the next stage, meterial properties will be determined by conducting different tests. Full scale six specimen walls of different structural configuration will be fabricated and then will be tested under Quasi-Static loading. In the next stage, prototype structures will be selected from the reconnaissance survey. A scale will be selected on the basis of shake table capacity, then similitude analysis will be performed for the reduce scale models. Four reduce scale models will be fabricated and will be tested on shake table. The objective will be to study force deformation behavior and hysteresis response. On the basis on these parameters constructional guidelines will be developed, which will be share to PDMA and to local Union Council of different Districts. These guidelines then can also be added to the Building Code of Pakistan.

data.projectDigest: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a progressive cardiopulmonary disease with increases pulmonary artery pressure and afterload causes right ventricular (RV) hypertrophy and RV failure. PH is health problem not only in the developing countries but also in developed countries but still there are limited research on PH treatment in Pakistan and worldwide. Due to the lack of effective treatment therefore it is urgent to explore new therapy for PH. Stem cell has great potential to be considered as a novel treatment option for PH. Therefore, we aim to start with cardiopulmonary progenitor (CPP) stem cells and its exosomes to find a new therapeutic target for PH. The findings will be confirmed on in-vitro analysis of rat pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cell and endothelial cell cultures. In-vivo analysis will be performed on well-established MCT-induced pulmonary hypertensive rat model. In addition, the mRNA and protein markers will be recognized at the arterial and lung level by the use of advance technology. The proposed idea of therapeutic treatment for PH is very demanding. The successful achievement and completion of this idea will be highly reducing the disability and death rate of PH patients in Pakistan as well as worldwide.

data.projectName: Development and promotion of antioxidant rich plants driven essential oil based anticoccidials for achieving sustainable control of coccidiosis in broiler chickens
data.projectDigest:
Among various parasitic diseases of poultry, coccidiosis is principally important because
of causing huge economic losses. The use of anticoccidial drugs has been the main pillar in coccidiosis control program, however, their extensive and irrational use has resulted in the emergence of resistant Eimeria parasite strains against almost all available anticoccidial drugs and ultimately limiting their use as anticoccidial agents. Immunization by using the vaccines has been
next to anticoccidial drugs but, Eimeria live vaccines have been reported to trigger severe out breaks.Because of these constraints, in the recent years,  scientists all over the world are in search of alternatives to manage the worst situation well before time. Among alternatives, antioxidants rich plants driven essential oils have gained the maximum attention because of their potential to have anticoccidial activity. Use of essential oils has shown comparable results to synthetic drugs against coccidiosis. In this project, the attempts will be made to find out the anticoccidial potential of essential oils, which may be used as a complementary and/or alternatives to anticoccidial drugs for the effective control of coccidiosis in broiler chickens.

data.projectName: DEVELOPMENT OF NOVEL DAIRY PRODUCTS FOR REGULATION OF METABOLIC SYNDROME
data.projectDigest: Consumer preferences have evolved towards an increased demand for safer, more convenient foods from the point of view of health but also in terms of nutrition and sensory aspects. This change has led the food industry to work in the implementation of new technological processes. Among them, High Pressure Processing (HPP) has received great attention as a technology enabling the introduction in the market of a wide range of new products with a high degree of quality and functionality. Despite its increasingly widespread use, HPP is still considered a novel technology in the food sector, as its performance and cost effectiveness still can be improved. The ability of high pressure to inactivate microorganisms and spoilage catalyzing enzymes, whilst retaining other quality attributes, has encouraged food companies to introduce HPP foods in the market. HPP provides the food industry with new product development opportunities that can fully exploit the functional properties of ingredients such as proteins, etc. Currently foods are mainly processed through thermal techniques that exert negative impact on the nutritive value of food products. Previous findings suggested that HPP treatment could not only be a useful tool to preserve the sensory and nutritional quality of liquid juices, taking into account the good results in terms of enzyme inactivation, but could also increase the amount of extractable bioactive components with nutritional and antioxidant capacity. Therefore, the current project is designed to prepare the ready to drink fruit beverages from HPP techniques. The overall objective of the study is to develop a new range of liquid products including fresh fruit beverages, with high nutritional and sensory quality, by  HPP in combination with other technologies.

data.projectName: Environmental Education Program; Development of Environmental Awareness Material to accelerate Sustainable Community Based Management System
data.piUniversity: Government College for Women University, Sialkot
data.projectDigest: This project is basically designed to collect and examine successful and innovative material to implement environmentally sound sustainable community development. This study is divided in two main parts. First, to develop a sustainable management system for soil waste and to train selected community groups for proper implementation of the theme. Second to develop support system to help vulnerable groups of community to implement safe and healthy environmental practices. Different community groups will be selected for training to get outstanding results like workers in industry, school students, municipal workers and social mobilizers to implement all this plan. This project will not only add up in environmental aspects but also to develop plans for sustainable community management.

data.projectName: Epidemiological, Clinical, and Molecular Elucidation of Skeletal Anomalies Present in a Multiethnic Population of Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Morbidity and mortality in early years of life have been declined and a shift from infectious diseases to noncommunicable diseases has been observed globally. Congenital and hereditary abnormalities are one of the largest parts of the non-communicable disorders that cause childhood mortality and in many cases lifelong disabilities. Skeletal anomalies are a frequently observed group of congenital abnormalities. There is substantial clinical and genetic heterogeneity in skeletal anomalies and in many cases management and prevention is possible. However, for the initiation of intervention programs, we need detailed epidemiological, clinical and molecular studies. Through such studies we can find out distribution pattern and associated risk factors of the disease. In Pakistan, there is scarcity of such studies. Inadequate resources and long time required to complete epidemiological studies, are important reasons of this lack of data. Further, it is also challenging to move in remote areas of Pakistan due to political unrest and logistic problems. So, the proposed study is designed by keeping in view all these problems. Different districts of KPK and Punjab will be screened for congenital and hereditary skeletal anomalies and detailed epidemiological, clinical and molecular data will be collected to find out underlying cause and to propose management plan in our society.

data.projectName: Climate-driven Vector-Borne Diseases Model (CVBDM): An Empirical and Spatio-Temporal Approach
data.projectDigest:
Over time, climate change has been adversely affecting the northern  areas of Pakistan and has brought drastic change in temperature and precipitation trends. Following these trends, various climatic disasters have altered the socioeconomic profile of these areas and have weaken the health and coping capacity of the communities to tackle the climatic challenges. One of the significant aspects of the climatic disasters is the  epidemics of diseases  in this vulnerable area due to climate change. These diseases can be broadly classified as direct and indirect Climate-Driven Diseases (CDDs). Direct CDDs include the vector-borne, skin, respiratory and infectious diseases (such as leshmaniasis, malaria, dengue, chikunguniya fever, crimean-congo haemorrhagic fever bronchitis, etc) whereas; indirect CDDs include the water- and food-borne diseases (such as typhoid, giardiasis, intestinal worms, diarrhea, cryptosporidium infections, and gastroenteritis) which may occur after any climatic disaster or extreme weather events.
This research, with an aim to predict CDDs future dynamics and to control disease epidemics and outbreaks, implies the development of a statistical model “Climate-Driven Diseases Model (CDDM)” which addresses the impact of climate change on the emergence or re-emergence of CDDs, their transmission, pathways and dynamics, future predictions, spatio-temporal mapping of vulnerable areas/hots pots and formulization of a strategy for national and provincial policy makers.

data.projectName: A Study on Mechanism of Bubbles in Elastic Fluids
data.projectDigest: This project is focused on theoretical investigations of different shapes and properties of bubbles occurring in transport of elastic fluids. The applications of bubble dynamics in engineering and medical sciences fascinate many scientists and engineers. These systems work effectively in both destructive and constructive ways. Different analytical and numerical techniques have been employed in literature to explore this phenomenon. The complexity in the case of non-Newtonian fluids, bubble dynamics for only few flow models have been discussed.  Few efforts were made in order to understand the dynamics of bubbles in elastic fluids. Also, the effects of heat, gravity, magnetic field and surface tension have not been fully explored. The purpose of the present project is to investigate the effects of heat, magnetic field, gravity and boundaries on the cavitation and bubble dynamics in different elastic fluid mediums for both compressible and incompressible flows.

data.projectName: Epidemiology of common scab of potato and its management in Southern Punjab
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest:
Common scab caused by Streptomyces scabies is one of the most destructive diseases of the potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) throughout the world. It adversely affects the market value of potato crop, either through occasional reduction of gross yield or through the obnoxious black spots on tuber skin. 
Development of a disease predictive model is one of the key management practice used to reduce the impact of this disease because the existence of wide variability in virulence of pathogen against potato germplasm. 
Different factors like plant age, type and time of infection, soil, type of strain of the pathogen, genetic make-up of host plant and climate factors influence the disease development in potato crop. Among climate factors such as temperature, moisture, rainfall, wind speed and wind velocity are likely to play very important role in disease development. 
Scab diseases cannot currently be controlled with pesticides application and the effects of cultural control methods, such as irrigation management or crop rotation. Management of common scab of potato through disease predictive model and genetic resistance is considered as the best management strategy. Disease predictive model and resistant source make it environment friendly and to minimize the use of chemicals. So the objective of the present study is to develop a disease predictive model and evaluate the potato germplasm against common scab of potato and the outcome of the study should be used as guidance for management of common scab disease of potato and to maximize food security through potato production in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Research and development of plasma thrustes and SLV
data.projectDigest:
The latest research field of plasma propulsion includes a broad variety of
thrusters to achieve high propellant exhaust velocity, thereby offering a large
mass savings for space vehicles as compared to chemical rockets. Whereas,
micro plasma thrusters has already been used since more than a decade to
attitude control of satellites in space.
The VASIMR (Variable Specific Impulse Magnetoplasma Rocket) is currently being developed by the private company in Houston, TX. Producing the 200kW RF generators for ionizing propellant. This project is led by former NASA astronaut Dr. Franklin Chang-Díaz. The prototype at a power level of 100 kW would produce about 2 newtons of propulsion. It would be superior to current ion drives and would be 10-60 times more fuel efficient than chemical rockets. Recently the Aerospace Company announced to test the VASIMR in space, this test phase is now expected to be conducted in 2019. The VF-200 engine could reduce the duration of flight from Earth to Jupiter or Saturn from six years to fourteen months, and Mars from 4 months to 39 days.

data.projectName: Molecular characterization of Clostridium perfringens types associated with Necrotic enteritis (NE) in poultry and comparison of various methods for experimental induction of NE
data.projectDigest: Necrotic enteritis (NE) is an economically important disease of chicken. The disease causes significant mortality during the clinical phase while in the subclinical form, there is loss of productivity due to reduced feed conversion ratio, causing annual losses of 6.25 percent per bird. Previous findings indicated highly complex pathogenesis of NE and highlighted that multiple factors are vital for induction of disease. There are many predisposing factors also, which are essential for NE pathogenesis and with the involvement of these contributing factors, various degradative enzymes & toxin production by C. perfringens stimulate the signs and symptoms of NE, therefore leading to tissue destruction, colonization of bacteria and enterotoxicity. The project is therefore planned to understand the prevalence of NE in southern Punjab and cholistan desert. Further research will be carried out to investigate the role of virulent strains of C. perfringens in the pathogenesis of NE by animal model studies and the use of those virulent strains to be considered in future for development of candidate vaccine against NE. The project duration will be for two years with main focus on outbreaks of NE reported from various regions of Bahawalpur and cholistan. The sample size will be according to the population of chicken in the selected area. Diseased chicken apparently having signs and symptoms of NE will be targeted, with healthy animals as control. In case of dead birds, samples will be collected from intestine while cloacal swabs or fecal material will be taken from live diseased/healthy birds.

data.projectName: Isolation of antivirulent alkaloids from selected medicinal plants against Pseudomonas aeriginosa
data.projectDigest: Medicinal plants are very effective against various diseases due to the presence of secondary metabolites e.g. alkaloids, flavonoids etc. Different microorganisms have varying ability to cause disease depending upon their disease causing (virulence) properties. The microbe can use any one or all of these virulence properties to establish an infection.  So there is an urgent need to target each of these virulence properties. Medicinal plants have always proved to be helpful to treat most of the infection. But there is a need to understand and educate people about the exact role of each plant part and their use in different infection caused by the same microorganism. In the present study we have proposed to isolate and characterize alkaloids from plant species belonging to Solanaceae family.  Use these alkaloids to perform various assays to check if they can be used to inhibit the virulence properties of P. aeruginosa.

data.projectName: Molecular Characterization of Methicillin Resistant Staphlococcus Aureus (MRSA) and development of plant derived antimicrobial to address Antimicrobial Resistance
data.projectDigest: Livestock sector of Pakistan is one of the most important sector which is contributing a share of 60.54% in agriculture GDP and 11.2 % in overall GDP. Almost 8 million families are directly or indirectly involved in livestock rearing getting more than 35% income. The total population of cattle, buffalos, sheep and goat are 44.4, 37.7, 30.1 and 72 million, respectively. The total milk production by these animals is about 56080 tons per annum. Gross value addition of these animals is about Rs. 1333 billion. On the other hand, the dairy sector is facing different challenges in the form of decreased productivity and improper marketing. One of the reason of decreased productivity is the existence of various contagious diseases of livestock. Among these diseases staphylococcal mastitis is one of the infectious disease that pose a great threat to dairy animals (Economic Survey of Pakistan 2018-2019).Mastitis in dairy cows is a disease of considerable economic importance, and S. aureus is among the most common pathogens of clinical and subclinical mastitis in dairy cattle. The increasing prevalence of MRSA in livestock and human has created a pressing need for development of new antimicrobial agents to overcome bacterial multidrug resistance. The aim of the proposed research is to investigate MRSA on Pakistani dairy farms, and to evaluate the intervention strategy by feeding Pakistani traditional medicinal plant A. nilotica pods on MRSA positive dairy farms.

data.projectName: The nexus of digital social innovation with entrepreneurial networks and access to finance in small business sector.
data.projectDigest: The small businesses, being the most dynamic firms, are considered as the most important catalysts to the socio-economic development worldwide. These businesses are considered as engine to socio-economic growth to alleviate poverty through job creation and provide a breeding ground for entrepreneurs. Globally, on average small business sector contribute approximately 80% of economic growth. In developing economies this sector contribute 70% to Gross domestic product and 95% to total employment. Significance of small businesses is well documented in literature as they are considered to be the highest employment generators, the biggest contributors to the economic triumph. However, despite their importance; in Pakistan small businesses suffer from dearth of digital social innovation (DSI), subsequently experienced weak performance and high failure rate. It is observed that large number of Pakistani small businesses collapse at very early stages. It indicates that there is great threat for sustainable development of Pakistani small businesses. Therefore, this research aims to understand and examine the important factors or criteria that should be considered in DSI of small businesses. This research would be blend of basic and applied research and main objective of this research is to understand and examine the indispensable factor such as entrepreneurial business networks and access to finance for creating DSI.

data.projectName: Extraction and quantification of curcumin and piperine from different varieties of turmeric rhizomes and black pepper in Pakistan for pharmaceutical applications
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest:
Turmeric “Curcuma Longa” is a traditional medicinal entity in the region of Asian sub-continent including India, Pakistan and China due to a precious molecular constituents namely Curcumin, desmethoxycurcumin (DMC) and bisdemethoxycurcumin (BDMC) and are collectively known as Curcuminoids.  The contents of curcuminoids are extremely important in turmeric used as curry powders due to their anti-oxidant capabilities and the yellow color in turmeric is imparted by curcumin present in it. The value and quality of turmeric depends on quantity of curcumin present in turmeric rhizomes. Generally, the curcumin content in turmeric powders ranges from 1 to 6%. For example, recently India has claimed to prepare a turmeric variety in which 4% curcumin is present and also yielding the crop twice per year, which is being marketed internationally and curcumin extracts are being prepared and marketed at high values thus, contributing towards GDP growth. Unfortunately, being an agricultural country, not much efforts are made for developing such varieties to enhance curcumin content in turmeric. Moreover there is not database for the quantification of curcumin content in turmeric varieties growing in different regions of Pakistan. Curcumin content depends upon the environmental conditions, soil condition, and type of agricultural land, water and supply of fertilizers.  
Similarly, black pepper is major source of piperine which also is used as spice and Vietnam is a major exporter of black pepper. Being an agricultural country, we are nowhere in the export and production of black pepper. Piperine is also very useful for medicinal purposes. The bioavailability of curcumin is enhanced 2000 times when used along with piperine

data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Dengue is a serious public health concern globally and dengue epidemics have become a serious problem in Pakistan as well. The number of cases reported this year in 2019 has increased substantially than that of the previous years. Pakistan is vulnerable to more outbreaks of dengue due to the changing climate conditions of the country. It is therefore important to monitor the virus epidemiology, spread and prevalence of the circulating virus serotypes so to respond appropriately to dengue outbreaks in future. Despite the expanding morbidity and mortality from dengue virus infections, there is still no therapeutic treatment available. The pathogenesis of dengue, DHF, DSS is poorly understood in Pakistan due to the lack of sufficient number of studies on genome variation of the circulating viruses. Thus, the focus of our research proposal is to gain insight into the entire genome of dengue virus strains circulating in Pakistan and also develop strategies to eradicate the disease through application of cutting-edge molecular biology and other virological approaches that will arrest viral replication. This research grant will overall utilize the methods in cell and molecular biology, biochemistry, virology and bioinformatics and provide basis for translational research towards improved and innovative dengue intervention strategies. This project will contribute to the overall advancement of knowledge on dengue in Pakistan to establish avenues for safe and effective means for the control of dengue virus infections.

data.projectName: Assessment of physiological modulations in seeds of future smart food crops during storage
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest: Possible threats of changing climate suggest to explore the potential of alternate crops for improving net income of the farmers and national food security. Crop diversification is a way to provide farmers with a diversity of diet, improves their income and nutrition security. Quinoa (Chenopodium quinoa), moringa (Moringa olifera) and chia (Salvia hispanica) are climate resilient crop having superior nutritional profile and may help to ensure future food security. Commercial cultivation of these future smart foods is dependent upon availability of quality seed. Seed of these crops is very sensitive to storage conditions and losses it viability very quickly. Drastic reduction in seed viability and vigor needs to be linked with biochemical processes triggered by high seed moisture contents. Detailed physiological and biochemical changes related to deterioration of quinoa, moringa and chia seed during storage are need to be explored. Therefore, seeds will be stored at different moisture contents and in different packaging materials for 18 months. Detailed physiological and biochemical changes in stored seed will be studied. Seed moisture isotherms will be developed and relationship between oil contents and equilibrium moisture contents will be explored. Dry Chain technology for safe storage of these future smart foods will be developed.

data.projectName: Design & Development of Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) Based Antennas for 5G Communication Networks
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: The project aims to produce efficient frequency selective surface (FSS) based fully integrated beam-steering antenna system for 5G communication networks, in particular, for base station applications. Initially, the research team will focus on system design at sub-6GHz band followed by design & development of antenna system at higher 5G frequencies. The proposed system of beam steering will be low profile, low loss, less costly, light weight, high degree of integration, and ease for fabrication. The comprehensive link budget analysis will also be studied to emulate the environmental effects. The project research output will be presented at various international venues through publications in reputed journals/conferences which will promote a good image of Pakistan. In addition, such research projects will play a vital role in Pakistan’s march towards becoming a knowledge economy and presents its research potential to the rest of the world.

data.projectName: Filtration and metering for rainwater harvesting as supportive tool for irrigated agriculture in rainfed area of Pothwar
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: The condition of water resources is alarming due to more food and fiber needs for growing population. Agriculture sector is largest consumer of water in Pakistan with around 91.6 percent share. Government of Pakistan has spent billions of rupees for rainwater harvesting in rainfed areas by constructing 1000+ mini-dams/water-ponds. These investments contribute in groundwater recharge, water supply, provide support for poultry, livestock, and fish culture. However, there are numerous concerns remains unattended i.e. reduction in capacity of water reservoir due to sedimentation, development of command area and catchment area, adoption of irrigated agriculture, water losses and water quality. Considering these concerns, present project has been designed to develop filtration and metering mechanism for rainwater harvesting. Two filtration systems will be developed for rainwater harvesting from which one for inlet point to control sediments and second for outpoint to improve the quality. Water metering system will be established by developing digital monitoring devices and sensors. Proper filtration mechanism would help to increase the life of rainwater ponds/mini dams and enhance the quality of harvested water. Water metering mechanism would assist the irrigation scheduling and water resources management. Research project would provide guidelines to farmers for adoption of highly efficient irrigation system with rainwater harvesting system with proper filtration and metering mechanism.

data.projectName: Synthesis and application of coal fly ash based composites in photocatalytic degradation of pollutants and EMI shielding
data.projectDigest: Fly ash is a globally recognized toxic waste by-product of coal and biomass combustion. Many countries are dealing with its management. Only a small portion of it is utilized properly. The rest is dumped into landfills. Effective recycling of coal fly ash (CFA) is necessary to prevent many environmental hazards such as soil, air and water contamination. This study is focused on utilization of coal combustion ash for remediation of water pollutants and electromagnetic interference. It will be progressive in three perspectives solving three issues which are the fly ash consumption/recycling, electromagnetic interference and (waste) water treatment. Fly ash can serve as support to various types of photocatalysts. Modification of fly ash by nanoparticles is a dynamic field. CFA will be collected from local industries which are processing local and imported coal. Fly ash based novel materials will be synthesized by different methods mainly hydrothermal, characterized by various characterization techniques, and used for the photocatalytic degradation of a range of pollutants from water under light (sunlight/UV/Visible) and the prepared nanocomposites will be evaluated for EMI shielding. The research work including synthesis and evaluation will be conducted at host institute and characterization at other sectoral institutes.

data.projectName: Discovery of new therapeutic molecules from Prosopis africana (Guill. & Perr.) Taub. against multi-drug resistance of malaria
data.projectDigest:
Malaria, as a tough infectious disease, has been keeping epidemic for several centuries, and the incidence remains increasing in some areas including Pakistan. Drug resistance occurred for both classic and some newly found molecules has become the major issue for the treatment of malaria. Discovery of novel and new functional molecules from natural sources can be an effective approach to solve drug-resistance problem. For this purpose, we have initially completed literature survey for the medicinal plants which were used traditional for malaria and remain unknown in research field. We surprisingly found that, in Mali and Nigeria, people used to treat malaria by the plant, Prosopis africana (Guill. & Perr.) Taub. However, there are very limited phytochemistry research on this plant. The responsible active compounds and the mechanism remain unidentified.  
Therefore, in this proposed project, different parts, such as leaves, fruits, stem barks, and root barks of P. africana will be comprehensively investigated by anti-malarial activity-guided isolation using modern techniques including various column chromatography and precise analytical instruments, and characterization by multiple advanced spectroscopic approaches. The identified compounds will be evaluated for anti-malarial activity, along with the general cytotoxicity test against human normal cell line. Structure-activity relationship will be summarized through all the biological activity evaluation results along with structures of substrates and all products. Finally, one or two active compounds with great potentials will be selected for mechanism study through 1H NMR-based metabolomics. Thus, the current research will generate new therapeutic approach against multi-drug resistance of malaria.

data.projectName: Design and Development of Virtual Inertia Implementation Testbed for Smart Grids
data.projectDigest:
Conventional power system consists of several synchronous generators operating in parallel. The rotor, being a rotating mass, constitutes a rotating inertia. So, any change in the grid frequency resulting from a power imbalance is resisted by this inertia. This acts as the first response to maintain the frequency before the sophisticated grid controllers come into play. The change in frequency per generation loss is increasing annually due to the increased penetration of inertia less renewable energy sources thus limiting their penetration in the conventional grid.

We propose to design and develop a test bed for virtual inertia system consisting of multiple DC sources, grid tie inverter and a controller. DC sources are there to mimic generalized energy storage systems and renewable energy sources. Inverter is a generalized grid tie inverter serving as a power electronic interface of energy storage systems and renewable energy sources to the grid. Controller is a microprocessor which implements the algorithms of grid interface and virtual inertia implementations. 

Implementation of virtual inertia for microgrids will increase the penetration of renewable energy sources in the traditional grid of Pakistan and will be a step further towards the transformation of existing grid to smart grids.

data.projectName: Isolation, Characterizations and  molecular docking simulation of pharmacologically active compounds of Echinops echinatus for new drug discovery
data.projectDigest:
The main goals of this research work to explore indigenous plant Echinops echinatu. E. echinatu used in traditional medical system for treatment of appetite, cold, cough, biliousness, urinary discharges, thirst, pain in joint, inflammation, ophthalmia, stangury, chronic fever, stimulate liver, and brain disease. This finding will provide a new drugs isolated from medicinal plants material have no side effect and will be introduced for the benefits of human life. The main objective of this research work is to isolate active phytochemical from Echinops echinatu extract which validate its folk uses. The extract and its active identified compounds will be subjected to various in vitro and in vivo biological activities including; anti-inflammatory, analgesic, antimicrobial, anti-ulcer, antioxidant, anti-cancer, sedative and muscle relaxant. The bioactive compounds will be further subjected molecular docking study to identity the exact site responsible for biological activity.   
The identification of active compounds in E. echinatu will be introduced as a new drug for the treatment of human life.

data.projectName: Role of Innovation and Farm Diversification in Agriculture Productivity and Poverty Alleviation in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: The extent to which a country attains benefit from innovation through technological advancement and farmer’s skill improvement (through enhanced human capital) will lead towards long run economic growth. The absorption of international technology (efficient utilization of innovative technology) perform vital role in productivity enhancement and to attain higher level of living standard.  In this context, the farmer’s diversification from farm to non-farm activities has vital contribution in every economy. This study will be conducted to test the two different hypotheses through time series and microeconomic survey based data. The first hypothesis is ‘technological innovation in agriculture productivity and poverty alleviation’ and the other is role of farm diversification in poverty alleviation in case of Pakistan’. The study will also test the farmers’ well being through multidimensional poverty indices. To achieve the, objectives of this research both primary and secondary sources data will be collected through properly constructed interview schedule. Policy recommendation will be formulated to alleviate poverty utilizing project data.  Furthermore, the results of the projects will be appropriately disseminated amongst the concerned academia for aligning and monitoring the outcome, the results will also be disseminated amongst all stakeholders for assimilation of the greater objectives of the project.

data.projectName: Extraction of useful resin acids from paper industry waste and their use in the synthesis of materials for liquid crystal technology
data.projectDigest:
Tall oil, a by-product of pulp and paper industry, is primarily used in manufacture of alkyl and polyamide resins, soap manufacture, as waterproofing agent and agricultural emulsifier in industrially established countries. In Pakistan, it is not processed for purification and is mostly burned with other waste materials of this industry or thrown into the sewage water, resulting in air, water and soil pollution.
Tall oil contains structurally important resin acids such as abietic acid and pimaric acid [1]. These acids after separation from tall oil can be used as starting materials for the synthesis of liquid crystals, which may find applications in liquid crystal displays [2], liquid crystal tunable optical filters in green houses and light windows [3], chemical sensing instruments [4] and photonic tunable laser devices [5]. In this way, a waste of paper industry may be beneficially used for the synthesis of commercially important materials.

data.projectName: A Network Analysis Approach of Understanding Post Conflict Communication through Social Media Discourse Regarding North and South Waziristan
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
The proposed research aims to investigate the digital public discourse regarding the post-conflict region of Waziristan. The main idea is to examine - with the help of network analysis - the nature and quality of social media discourse that revolves around Waziristan. In doing so, the researcher aims to identify the key stakeholders, their prominence, and relationships with others in a network. Furthermore, it shall allow the investigator to understand in which light Waziristan is being discussed, along with revealing the presence of non-state actors in an attempt to collude with the ongoing peace process through propagating anti-state narrative (or misinformation).  

The proposed topic is first of its kind that is focused exclusively on post-conflict region of Waziristan, and rely on advanced computational and statistical methods with the intent to understand social media users and their respective communication networks. Moreover, the proposed research is quite relevant, and important primarily because it aims to produce results that shall be helpful for respective state institutions to understand and adopt an effective peace narrative.

data.projectName: Design and fabrication of efficient graphene/perovskite photo-voltaic devices on flexible silicon substrate.
data.projectDigest:
In this era, modern industry and global population has rapidly accelerated the amount of energy consumption. More than 80 % of energy is produced by using fossil fuels such as Oil and Gas which is expensive and not ecofriendly. Alternative methods of producing cheap, efficient and environment friendly, renewable energy such as solar cells, wind power biofuel, biomass etc. has been used. Among these renewable energy resources, solar cells are more promising energy resource because of its eco-friendly and abundance.
Since 2012 the first Perovskite solar cell breakthroughs, it is now very much accepted that halide perovskite solar cells may have a strong practical impact in next-generation solar cells. Also, in the past few years, Gr/Si metal/semiconductor) solar cells have attracted great interest because of the ease of fabrication processes and low consumption of materials, which in turn lead towards lower cost solar cells. Both materials already show promising results in photo-voltaic devices.
 Multi-junction solar cell will enhance the efficiency, this is due to graphene and perovskites materials possess good optical and electronic properties at low cost and by using easy fabrication steps.  Graphene will play multi-role here; it will act as back electrode in Perovskite solar cell and make Schottky junction with silicon.
Fabrication step will take place at room temperature in clean room, spin coater will be used for spin coating. Reactive ion etching (RIE) technique will be used for cleaning the surface of a substrate and doping of a graphene. Graphene quality will be analyze using Raman spectroscopy. Current-voltage characteristics will be done using two probe measurement and Solar simulator.

data.projectName: AgriCPS - Farmer assistance System for a Smart Greenhouse
data.projectDigest: AgriBOT is a farmer assistance system to deploy and monitor crops for high quality yields. This research aims to design an AgriCPS oriented framework and workflow for increased productivity planning using state-of-the-art sensors and highly capable robots for monitoring, detecting and responding (MDR). This project plans to propose and practically realize a collaborative architecture for superior CPS communications in the agricultural farm powered by green energy. The sensor system of AgriCPS is composed of two segments. The ground based (GB) sensor system monitors the environment and soil parameters while the mobile sensing platform is composed of a camera based robotic vehicle, which provides sensing of the farm parameters and plant’s growth estimation. Artificial intelligence (AI) based techniques are used to interpret important results from the sensor data. The farm data is accessible in real time via networked communication for monitoring and control by a distant operator. In case of emergency, an alarm is generated for immediate action by the farm supervisor.

data.projectName: Arsenic detection and removal in the water environment through label-free colorimetry using DNA-dependent nanoparticle-based nanosensor and a biosand filter
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Development of mechanism and nanosensor that could rapidly detect arsenic (heavy metal) from water without using conventional laboratory procedures. The system should be easy to use, low cost and can be applied, focusing areas having limited access to conventional laboratories. The idea is not only to develop a detection mechanism but at the same time offer solution to arsenic removal. We have a persistent issue of arsenic contamination in areas of Sindh and Punjab. This project is focused on clean and safer access to drinking water. Our goal shall not only solve rapid, on-site, cost-effective detection of arsenic in water but also provide removal mechanism that can easily be applied to areas having higher arsenic contamination in Pakistan. The project also fulfills UN sustainable development goals as SGD no. 6 “clean water and sanitation”

Our goal shall not only solve rapid, on-site, cost-effective detection of arsenic in water but also provide removal mechanism that can easily be applied to areas having higher arsenic contamination in Pakistan. The project also fulfills UN sustainable development goals as SGD no. 6 “clean water and sanitation”

data.projectName: Glutathione mediated acquisition of zinc in maize for the induction of drought tolerance and improved nutritional profile
data.projectDigest: Maiz being food crop due to its tremendous use as food and its oil has great market value due to its nutritional value. However the Limited supply of water during irrigation period resuts in  limited cultivation of maize in Pakistan. The maiz grown under limited water supply  causes degradation of seed nutritional quality. Moreover, the soil of Pakistan is Zn deficient,  Under water stress condition zinc deficiency becomes more serious for plant. Plant Zn deficiency can be fulfilled by applying different chemicals as fertilizers as well as foliar spray. ZnSO4 is the major inorganic source of zinc but onward trend is the use of organic fertilizer. This project is designed to evaluate the exogenous application of Zn chelated glutathione in comparison with ZnSO4 for the improvement of seed quality and drought stress tolerance. At first, two potential maize cultivars /hybrid will be grown after seed priming with different levels of Zn chelated glutathione and ZnSO4 to evaluate most effective levels under drought stress condition. At the same time Zn will be applied with foliar spray to find out most effective levels under drought stress condition. Selected Zn levels will be used in fields under drought stress to assess changes in yield components. During last year selected levels of Zn will be applied to evaluate seed yield quality on the basis of seed proximate composition. Various physiological and biochemical attributes will be studied in addition to growth and yield. Changes in glutathione contents will be determined. Furthermore, seed nutritional quality will be determined by inorganic macro and micro minerals. So, this study will play a pivotal rule in induction of drought tolerance and improved nutritional profile of maize.

data.projectName: Genetic testing of Triple Negative Breast Cancer by locally integrated Next-generation sequencing (NGS) system in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan, Breast cancer in females is the most prevalent and worrisome disorder which originates from a genetic variation. Identification of the genetic cause of aggressive breast cancer subtype, Triple-negative breast carcinoma (TNBC), must be done. TNBC is characterized by lack of the expression of estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptors (PR) and human epidermal growth factor receptor two (HER2/neu).  According to National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) guidelines, females diagnosed with TNBC at the age of equal or less than 60, must go for genetic counselling and BRCA1/2 screening. Targeted therapy is available for BRCA mutated triple-negative breast cancer. For this purpose, sequencing of BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes which are commonly associated with breast cancer must be done.  For the first time in Pakistan, NGS system will be established for the genetic testing of triple-negative breast cancer in a clinical laboratory i.e. Armed forces institute of pathology (AFIP). Young triple-negative breast cancer females will be screened for BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations by Ampliseq BRCA panel. This panel will sequence all the exons and splice sites of BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes. Analysis of the sequencing results will be done by using bioinformatics tools. Clinical significance of the resultant variants will be characterized according to American College of Medical Genetics (ACMG) guidelines. Aim of the project is to investigate the prevalence and spectrum of BRCA1/2 germline mutations in Pakistani Triple-negative breast carcinoma patients. Results of this research project will be recorded in the international databases of cancer mutations from a Pakistani population perspective.

data.projectName: Information Geometric Approach to Statistical and Matrix Manifolds
data.projectDigest:
Information geometry applies tools from differential geometry to study properties of spaces. It generalizes certain properties of the Euclidean (flat) spaces to curved spaces whereby the notion of distance between any two points on curved spaces and a coordinate system on such spaces can be defined. The proposed research will use the information geometry framework to study structural properties of general spaces encountered in engineering problems in signal processing and machine learning. The structural information will be used to develop computational tools that are more efficient than existing ones.
The proposed research will develop local expertise in information geometry and geometric analysis. It will provide training in Riemannian manifolds and optimization on manifolds to postgraduate students. The multidisciplinary nature of the proposed research will foster collaboration and help to bridge the gap with the engineering discipline. It will lift the profile of Mathematics at Air University. It will directly impact a number of application areas such as signal processing, machine learning and control.

data.projectName: Fabrication and Performance analysis of moisture harvesting devices suitable for remote water scarcity zones of Pakistan.
data.projectDigest:
Clean fresh water is an essential resource which is necessary to sustain life and to maintain a healthy living standard. There are many sources of fresh water that could be exploited to provide fresh water for drinking, cooking, cleaning and to meet other domestic and industrial needs. These include rain, glaciers, rivers, lakes and underground water. However, there are many zones in the world and also in Pakistan where these conventional sources of fresh water are either scarce  or require huge effort and cost to access. Water present in the atmosphere in the form of vapors can be condensed to pure liquid water to meet the daily needs of remote areas efficiently. The choice of an atmospheric water harvesting system is very crucial that should be made based on the climate of the area and the potential utilization. The utilization of atmospheric water harvesting in urban areas and cities  can help reduce the stress on ground and surface resources and can solve the problem of partial water scarcity by allowing the surface and ground reservoirs to replenish and restore. 

Atmospheric or air water harvesting is a natural phenomenon and is used by certain plants and animals living in harsh environment to harvest fog, rainwater and moisture from the air. Passive AWGs are only suitable in areas with large temperature and humidity variations between day and night resulting in the formation of fog that can be harvested. . Vapor compression based systems or thermoelectric devices based AWGs have a much wider operation range and can produce fresh water in virtually any environment with varying efficiency. This project is intended to build an efficient and cost-effective design for water generation from atmospheric air.

data.projectName: Novel therapeutic intervention for clinical forms of Dengue fever by elucidating vitamin D related host viral infectivity modulating factors
data.projectDigest: Dengue fever (DF) is becoming a major public health concern in Pakistan. Latest outbreak resulted in 47,120 DF cases, including 75 deaths nationwide. Dengue virus (DENV) infection induces a wide range of clinical presentations from DF to dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF). Studies have revealed role of host genetics and nutritional status in differential immune response against DENV infection and clinical outcomes in infected cases.  Immunomodulatory actions of Vitamin D in DENV infection and associations of vitamin D receptor (VDR) gene polymorphisms to DF/DHF susceptibility are known. However, there is no such data from Pakistan. Hence, proposed study will investigate serum levels of vitamin D, C-reactive protein, cathelicidin and cytokines e.g., TNF-?, IFN-?, IL-2, IL-6 and IL-8 in DF/DHF patients through ELISA. Furthermore genetic screening of dengue cases and controls for VDR gene polymorphisms will be performed to check their association with DF/DHF susceptibility in our population. The expected outcomes will highlight the role of vitamin D in dengue related variable immune response. Informative polymorphism/s of VDR gene will serve as useful biomarker/s for early identification of DF patients at risk of progression to DHF for in time critical management to reduce dengue linked morbidity and mortality in foreseeable future.

data.projectName: Genetic Diversity and Pathogenic Potential of Variant Strains of  Infectious Bronchitis Virus in Broiler and Backyard Poultry from Punjab Province
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan poultry industry plays essential role in national economy and ranked second largest industry. There are infectious diseases which play an important role in the economic losses of poultry industry. Infectious Bronchitis (IB) virus is still ranked at the top of list. In layers egg production declines and mortality observed in IB infected poultry farms of Punjab, Pakistan. Infectious bronchitis viruses have been classified into different serotypes that based on S antigenicity. IBV genetic classification based on S1 gene sequencing that has been applied worldwide. This genetic classification of IBV has assisted for control strategies and also helped to understand the epidemiology of existing virus. The S1 portion of S gene amplified through Reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction for genome analysis. In Pakistan no proper strategies of regular monitoring for the nature or type of field circulating and current using field vaccine strains has been operating. In this context, frequent outbreaks have been observed in IBV vaccinated flocks. This justified the need to undertake further investigations about emerging variants or mutant strains of IBV in our country. Therefore, the proper detection and identification of the circulating strains of IBV is fairly a challenging task.

data.projectName: Design and Development of an AI based Building Energy Management System
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan is an energy-demanding nation but due to lack of proper infrastructure, our buildings are not efficiently designed and often mismanaged which makes them energy-hungry and thus exists a huge potential for introducing building energy management systems, both from point of view of energy conservation as well as GHG emissions reduction. This study focuses on the development of an indigenous AI-based cost-effective energy management platform to allow end-users the ability to optimize their energy use. 
The proposed BEMS solution focuses on creating technical and technological conditions for the widespread implementation of demand response strategies in commercial and domestic buildings. The proposed artificial intelligence-based BEMS shall be able to interact with smart metering platforms and make use of machine learning techniques for load disaggregation and estimate the consumption of specific appliances and allow their separate analysis to identify specific energy efficiency actions. Thus the proposed BEMS based on these usage patterns alongside user preferences would implement custom-tailored algorithms to maximize the energy conservation benefits to the end-user. The research output will be the production of a Lab model/prototype BEMS implemented in a specified limited area within the Air University premises.

data.projectName: Development of a whole cell biosensor for the toxicity monitoring of polluted water
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
Water bodies polluted with contaminants are not always easy to detect or analyze each and every type of pollutant in the water (surface, sea, and discharge water). Therefore some bioassays and biosensors based on organisms (Fish, Crustaceans, microbes etc.) are used as early alarming system for the detection of any harmful effect in the water bodies. There are several bioassays and biosensors those can be used for this purpose. A novel biosensor based on thiosulfate-oxidizing bacteria has been developed in 2014 (Qambrani, Shin, Cho, & Oh, 2014). This biosensor was based on the activity of bacteria that produce sulfate as an end product that increase electrical conductivity and decrease pH. The biosensor was quite sensitive and is able to detect 74 µg/L hexavalent chromium in water. 
In this proposal we are proposing a new method of detection for the biosensor based on the oxygen consumption to modify and improve the usability of the biosensor. It will help in biosensing different types of water such as sea water/waste water which was not possible as the electrical conductivity was high. We are also proposing to evaluate the presence of any intermediate chemicals in the oxidation process that can help us to identify better reduced sulfur form for bacteria.

data.projectName: Designing and implementation of an Occupational Health, Safety & Environmental (OHSE) intervention program for controlling respiratory impairment in small & medium sized enterprises (SMEs) of Punjab
data.projectDigest: Pulmonary or respiratory function impairment reported among workers employed in different industries due to exposure of different pollutants especially particulate matter (PM2.5 & PM10). However, no study was conducted about the controlling of respiratory impairment by applying intervention program especially in the context of SMEs. So, the proposed research work is about the designing and application of a behavior based safety (BBS) educational intervention program for workers employed in SMEs of three cities (Gujranwala, Gujrat and Sialkot) of Punjab province. In the proposed work assessment of respiratory impairment in relation to demographic parameters will be assess through administration of designed questionnaire and pulmonary function test (PFT). Particulate matter monitoring will also done in ambient environment SMEs units for assessing the dose of PM2.5 and PM10. For controlling risk of respiratory impairment and improvement of OHSE practices among workers employed in SMEs, two phases of BBS intervention program “before” & “after” will be establish. Data will be collected at two mentioned phases of the BBS intervention program and compared to check the efficiency of the applied intervention program. Arrangements of OHSE awareness sessions in three clusters of the Punjab will enhance the safety awareness, safety knowledge and choice of sustainable practices by workers. As an outcome, analysis of facts will be communicated to the relevant stakeholders for the development of Respiratory Protection Policy (RPP) for local SMEs.
