data.projectName: Pharmacological drug screening from synthetic and semi-synthetic methods to develop drug candidate(s) for immunometabolic disorders
data.projectDigest: Sedentary life style, western diet and lack of exercise have ravaged human health in general. Aforementioned habits led to the complex set of immunometabolic diseases which often culminate in carcinogenesis. Immunometabolic disorders comprise of a group of abnormalities that involves (de)regulation of metabolism by immune system and vice versa. All lipid metabolic disorders like obesity, fatty liver, diabetes, atherosclerosis and abnormal lipid profile is robustly affected by immune system that in turn (de)regulates the metabolic features. Interestingly, most of the lipid metabolic disorders have parallel immune system abnormalities. Pakistan has a strong cultural base of untapped medicinal plants, which now couples with robust synthetic portfolio.  This project envisages to isolate active component from potential plants with desired activities and put them under drug investigation, the success of which can be brought to the active pharmaceutical market to the end user. Similarly project seeks to bring best chemical compounds from chemistry laboratories to the pharmacological testing.  Key immunometabolic  parameters will be measured to analyze the results of different drug molecules. measured to Successful pharmacological testing of active compounds from chemical laboratories and plants base can be harnessed directly for patients suffering from lipid metabolic disorders and its induced cancers.

data.projectName: ClueTrip
data.projectDigest:
The available transportation modes like public transport, Uber/ Careem and Airlift/ Swvl have some limitations such as poor quality of vehicles, limited routes and high cost. Airlift/ Swvl covers only limited routes and fixed stops which are few in numbers on the other hand, Uber/ Careem operates on all the routes but their cost is not affordable. There is a need of a system which provides “Quality Transportation” at “Low Cost” but not just on “Limited Routes”.
We are going to connect the commuter with the person who is going to travel either from the same origin or within a specified range of origin to the same destination or within a specified range of destination on mutual date and time.

data.projectName: Band gap tailoring of aniline based polymers and co-polymers through doping (p-type and n-type) for synthesizing electrode materials
data.piUniversity: University of Kotli Azad Jammu and Kashmir
data.projectDigest:
Plastics are insulating materials that are using to cover metallic cables for shielding e.g polyethylene. Plastronics (plastic electronics) is a very new field of academic as well as industrial research. In the area researcher works on electronics devices using conducting polymers. This is very interesting to use conducting plastics in electronic devices as the conducting plastics possess the properties like metals as well as plastics. As a semiconductor it could be used to carry the charge and as a plastic it is light weight, having high mechanical strength and high flexibility. The other encouraging factor of using conducting plastics is its easy handling and very low cost.
Conducting plastics have emerged as a potential candidate in the field of optoelectronics due to their distinctive optical and electrical properties as compared to its inorganic counterparts. Researchers all over the world are working on conducting polymers (plastics) on the development of optical communication, storage devices and various information processing and display system by using these conjugated polymers. Conducting polymers have very interesting applications in the field of tissue engineering, drug delivery and artificial muscles as well. Thin films of desired shape could be made from their solutions. The ease of work with the conducting plastics provides opportunities for a lot of novel applications

It is considered as good source of plant nutrients that can also improve soil fertility and physical quality of soil. Inspite of these favorable effects, wastewater also contains large number of organic and inorganic toxic materials that make the soil unfit because of the accumulation of heavy metals and salts in the soil. The long-term effect of waste water induces multi-metal resistance in bacteria. These bacteria can successfully be used for bioremediation of heavy metal contaminated soils and wastewater due to their plant growth promoting characteristics. So present research project has been planned for Development of wastewater treatment technology through lead resistant plant growth promoting bacteria. Use of microorganisms for removal of heavy metal from polluted sites is a cheaper solution as compared to chemical technologies. Present project has been planned to develop wastewater treatment technology using plant growth promoting rhizobacteria isolated and characterized from heavy metal contaminated wastewater.  A series of studies will be conducted to isolate and characterize metal resistant plant growth promoting bacteria. The efficacy of selected bacterial strains for transformation of metal will be studied in laboratory experiment. The isolated bacterial strains will be subjected for various characterization test such as; mechanisms used by bacterial strains, minimum inhibitory concentration of heavy metals, heavy metal tolerance, effect of lead on bacterial growth, heavy metal biodegradable experiments, antibiotic resistance of the bacterial isolates, and plant growth promoting potential, germination test and root colonization studies. data.projectName: Development of Malicious UAV Detection and Tracking System
data.projectDigest: Unmanned air vehicles (UAVs) have captured the attention of hobbyists, surveillance organizations, and agriculture personal due to its small size and endless commercial and security applications. It has capacity to carry large payload, which in turn can be beneficial in various applications, such as in videography, package delivery, and event coverage. However, this deployment raises some serious security threats to the national institutions and organizations because it can carry the explosive and other destructive chemicals. Motivated by this, we will develop in house solution for malicious UAV detection and tracking using machine/deep learning technologies to have an intelligent and efficient solution. The supervised/un-supervised machine/deep learning models such as using convolutional neural networks (CNN) are used to develop and test the gathered data sets (include videos/pictures) for UAV detection and tracking. Firstly, the system will be trained using the gathered data set, and afterwards the real-time data is used for detection and tracking of UAVs. The proposed system would have capability to detect the UAVs in diverse and harsh environment under various light conditions and weathers.

data.projectName: 3 Years
data.projectDigest: Phosphorus (P) is one the essential and the most growth limiting plant nutrient. This is due to limited P resource and very low P mobility in most of the world soils. P unavailability poses a great threat to sustainable crop production. Like many countries of the world, Pakistan imports raw material (rock phosphates) for P fertilizer production. The rock phosphate reserves are limited and are confined to few countries. Further, excessive mining for rock phosphates especially since green revolution has resulted in depletion of economically mine-able reserves. As continuous supply of P is inevitable for successful crop production which is threatened due to P resource depletion, and as there is no alternatives to P, it is very need of the time to improve the phosphorus use efficiency (PUE) of crop plants. Wheat is staple food of 220 million Pakistanis and is mostly grown crop. Therefore, most of the P fertilizer utilization is involved in wheat production. Most of the applied P is unavailable to the plants due to precipitation in calcareous soils, predominant in Pakistan. Current wheat varieties development program in the country is mainly based on having maximum yields with respect to agro-climatic conditions and plant protection aspects. The current project is aimed to identify the genotypic variation among wheat cultivars for their ability to make P plant-available from precipitates through the release of various root exudates into soil.

data.projectName: CGE-HCAIs-Pak: Cartographic Genomic Epidemiology of Healthcare-Associated Infections in Pakistan towards development of a patho-resistome knowledgebase and real-time diagnostic platform
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Health-care associated infections (HCAIs) are infections associated with medical devices and procedures, and a patient get them in hospital who receiving treatment of another disease. HCAIs are becoming resistant to antibiotics by carrying genes that can protect them against antibiotics, limiting choice of antibiotics and resulting in prolonged illnesses, disability, and even death. Tragically, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in HCAIs in Pakistan is very high and we must take immediate actions to manage it. Therefore, we aim to launch comprehensive plan for estimation prevailing AMR in HCAIs, all across Pakistan. Further, we aim to build a web-based surveillance system (Patho-resistome Knowledge-base) and to develop a real-time diagnostic system/pipeline. To achieve our goals, we are bringing an interdisciplinary team of experts in microbiology, microbial genomics, and computer science for establishing the next generation diagnostics of pathogen in raw samples. The data and information will be stored in yet-to-develop Patho-resistome Knowledge-base for allowing precise and comprehensive identification of range of pathogens and associate AMR. The proposed real-time diagnostic pipeline/system will assist clinician in appropriate prescriptions and reducing the HCAIs in Pakistan. The project is a step towards improving the health care strategies and reducing AMR burden in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Isolation and characterization of Pakistani Morels for its anticancerous effects on breast, kidney and liver cell lines along with its antibacterial activities
data.projectDigest: Cancer is one of the most serious diseases characterized by uncontrolled growth and presence of abnormal cells that either cause local invasion or spread to other organ of the body. Cancer is considered as the second leading cause of deaths across the globe. Microorganisms, plants and marine organism contain alkaloids and lead compounds which are important source of anticancer agents. Mushrooms are rich food nutritionally and a good beneficial source in traditional Chinese Medicine. Morchella species (Mushrooms) are known as morels and known for antimicrobial, anti-obesogenic, anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory and antidiabetic agents. The cell lines will be treated with various concentration of Morels extract and cells treated with only DMSO will be used as a control. The cells proliferation rate of cell lines will be measured by WST-1 assay kits. Moreover, the current study will also analyze the antimicrobial effects of Morel extracts. Microbial infections and cancer are now major problems all over the world. Chemotherapy is treatment choice of different cancers but all cancers do not have chemotherapy or working efficiently. Similarly antibiotics are also loosing their magic against microbial infections. The active compounds extracted from Morels of the current may an addition to list of different treatment options against different cancers and microbial infections.

data.projectName: Iron doped micro biochar: A potential source to enhance nitrogen use effeciency in Agriculture
data.projectDigest: Nitrogen (N) losses as nitrification/denitrification are of major environmental concern due to intensive use of fertilizers in agriculture, worldwide. It not only caused the surface/ground water pollution but also contributes towards greenhouse gases. Despite of their harmful environmental impacts, no suitable technique has been designed to minimize the N losses. Although, organic amendments including biochar has been proposed as a promising option, but N retention in soil as nitrate nitrate achieved so far was incomplete, resulting in low N use efficiency and high capital losses in Pakistan. Thus, better retention of nitrate in soil and its slow release to plant is still a challenge that needs to be addressed. This proposed study is designed to prepare iron doped micro-biochar (FeDMB) and evaluate its nitrate sorption, retention and release efficiency to minimize losses via leaching and/or denitrification. Developed FeDMB technique, resulting from the proposed study, will have important implications in the field of agriculture, and this FeDMB will be valuable resource to enhance N use efficiency. This research will further advance our knowledge of biochar-nitrogenous fertilizers interaction in soil.

data.projectName: Role of Iron Oxide Nanoparticles and Metallothionine gene in Iron Biofortification of Rice (Oryza sativa L.): A staple food
data.piUniversity: University of Malakand, Chakdara, Dir, Malakand
data.projectDigest: Iron is one of the most essential elements and prevailing iron deficiency is the worst menace among micronutrient malnutrition worldwide. In developing countries, Fe deficiency is even more devastating, leading to serious disabilities and deaths. Pakistan is yet a long way off to surmount iron deficiency anemia (IDA) and several reports revealed the prevalence of iron deficiency anemia during pregnancy in women and in children. The maternal death rate and IDA prevalence are closely associated and raising serious concerns for international and local organizations to overcome iron deficiency anemia across Pakistan. To alleviate Fe deficiency and its associated diseases, an innovative approach which is easily accessible to unprivileged people dwelling in remote rural areas in Pakistan is Fe biofortification. Iron oxide at nanoscale range is an efficient, innovative and viable approach substituting traditional fertilizers. Metallothionines genes protect plants against heavy metals stress. Keeping in view the importance of iron nanoparticles and metallothionine genes, the current project was designed to investigate the role of iron oxide nanoparticles and metallothionine genes in iron uptake in rice plant/grains. Rice is a suitable target plant for biofortification to alleviate Fe deficiency anemia in Pakistan where rice is used as a major staple food.

data.projectName: Phytochemical and Biological Investigation on Gentianodes tianschanica
data.piUniversity: Karakurum International University, Gilgit, Gilgit Baltistan
data.projectDigest: Cancer is a metabolic syndrome affecting a major proportion of the world population through a diversified nature since the ages even early to Hippocrates. The existing global cancer burdened population is an extremely intimidating issue of current times, and the even major concern is its increasing rate. The frightening augmented rate was reflected in statistics of International Agency for Research on Cancer, that around 11 % increase in the occurrence of new cancer cases and almost 8 % increase in deaths due to cancer in 2012 as compared to 2008. Thus, more efforts are needed to be put in for investigation of medicinal plants to identify more effective natural products and herbal formulations as deliverable options. People of traditional societies rely on medicinal plants and herbal products for different common ailments. WHO also encouraged those nations who promote traditional system of medicines as a substitute of the modern allopathic system. On the other hand, fascinating biodiversity of plants makes them a attractive for new and novel secondary metabolites for cancer. Since the discovery of important medicinal plants with therapeutic potential against cancer would have extreme worth for the development of new effective and safe drugs to counter the prevailing menace of cancer. In one of our current studies, the initial anticancer tests indicated that Gentianodes tianschanica contain certain secondary metabolites which can be extremely helpful in addressing the changes of certain type of cancer. Thus, Gentianodes tianschanica planned to be investigated for biological potentials and phytochemicals.

data.projectName: Effects of Parental and Teachers’ Behavior on Personality Traits of University Students
data.projectDigest:
The objective of the current cross-cultural study is to find out the effects of parental and teachers’ behavior on personality traits of university students. Parental behavior will be used as a proxy measure for parent-child communication and emotional support towards children, teachers’ support, and classroom motivation. This study will use the survey research design. 
400 students, selected through convenient sampling technique will respond to three self-report measures of about parental behavior and teachers’ behavior and personality traits.
After checking assumptions for normality, missing in responses and running descriptive analysis, MIMIC analysis will be conducted.

data.projectName: Seimsic Microzonation of Karachi: Implication for Hazard Assessment
data.projectDigest:
Seismic microzonation is the process of subdividing the earthquake prone areas into individual zones with respect to geological and geophysical characteristics such as ground shaking, liquefaction, landslide, rock-fall and earthquake hazards. Engineers achieve workable information from the microzonation maps about the seismic designs of building and construction. 
Karachi is Pakistan's largest city and is the capital of Sindh; it lies on Pakistan's southern coast, on the Arabian Sea just northwest of the Indus River Delta. There are major four geological faults (e.g., Allah Band Fault, Pub Fault, Kirthar fault), which run from Ahmadabad and Bhuj to Ormara along Makran coast. South eastern part of Karachi city is mainly resting on the significantly thick Quaternary deposits such as beach sand, coastal sand dunes and tidal mud flat underlain by Tertiary rocks, which need to be assessed in order to understand the local soil effect for microzonation purpose. Therefore, microzonation maps need to be prepared which contain precious information for the construction of defense housing, important industries, and essential civil structures like tunnel, nuclear power station, dams, roads and other public service program.

data.projectName: Impact Of Climate Change On Stream flows Of Mangla Watershed Using Hydrological Modelling.
data.projectDigest:
Weather and climate have a very important influence on life on the earth. They are part of the daily experience of human beings and are essential for food, health and well-being (IPCC, 2001). Weather is the fluctuating state of the atmosphere, characterised by the temperature, precipitation, wind, solar radiation, clouds, air pressure and humidity (IPCC, 2001; Oliver and Hidore, 2003). Climate is defined as average statistics of meteorological conditions (Graedel et al., 1993). It refers to the average weather in terms of the mean and its variability over a period of time ranging from months to thousands or millions of years. The classical period used as modern measures of climate is 30 years. Climate on the earth varies in space and time because of natural as well as anthropogenic forcing factors (IPCC, 2001). Any change in the forcing factors and their interactions may result in climate variations leading to possible impacts on life on the earth. 
Pakistan’s economy is based on agriculture that is highly dependent on water resources originating in the mountain sources of the Upper Indus Basin. Climate change may have serious implications for the management of water resources. The aim of this study was to examine the variability analysis in temperatures and precipitation and its impact on streamflow’s of Mangla Basin, UIB Pakistan using GIS based hydrological modelling. Trend analyses will be performed by applying parametric and non-parametric tests and Sen’s method applied to estimate change values in time series. The spatial maps of hydro-meteorological variables will also be developed to examine hydro-climatologically variability in the study area. The future climate change scenarios were developed with the help of SDSM model, a statistical downscaling approach base

data.projectName: Development of porous 3D bone scaffold from Biological Based polymers (Biopolymers) for tissue reconstruction.
data.projectDigest:
Human bones have unique structures and characteristics, and replacing a natural bone in the case of bone fracture or bone diseases is a very complicated problem. Bioplastics are successfully being used now a days for replacing natural bones.
Polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA) are bioplastics which are well known as intracellular carbon and energy storage compound in large number of bacterial species. They are biodegradable and are generated from renewable resources. With respect to the molecule chain length, PHA are categorized as short chain length (scl) PHA and medium chain length (mcl) PHA. Industrial production of both PHA types involves the use of microorganisms and their enzymes. 
A number of bacteria such as Azotobacter, Bacillus, Archaebacteria, Methylobacteria, Pseudomonas have been found to synthesize the PHA to varying levels. Production of both types of PHA depends on the nature of bacterial strain and carbon source used in the culture medium. For example, almost all Pseudomonads are known for mcl-PHA production, and similarly Bacillus is well known for PHB production. Nature of substrate used in the culture medium is very important for the type of PHA monomer produced in that culture. 
PHA degrades naturally and completely into carbon dioxide and water under aerobic conditions and into methane under anaerobic conditions. The production cost of PHA is high as compared to that of the non-biodegradable plastics of fossil origin.

data.projectName: Formulation Development and Evaluation (In Vitro and In Vivo) of Oro Dispersible Tablets of Anti Diabetic Drug (Vildagliptin) for Rapid Control of Blood Glucose Level and Development of In Vitro, In Vivo Correlation
data.piUniversity: Kohat University of Science and Technology, Kohat
data.projectDigest: In the present project, it is hypothesized that rapid therapeutic effect can be produced by increasing tablets disintegration and drug dissolution. Oro dispersible tablet (ODTs) is a solid dosage form which disintegrates in oral cavity, using saliva as disintegration media and swallowed as fine dispersion. It can be taken without need of water and overcome the problem of difficulty in swallowing. In the present project, ODTs will be developed for anti diabetic drug (Vildagliptin) which will be easily taken by the patients and will produce rapid onset of action. ODTs will be prepared by simple techniques, using commonly available excipients and machinery. Developed formulations will be evaluated for various quality control tests and best formulation will be selected. Selected formulation will be evaluated in diabetic patients and control of blood glucose level will be compared with that of conventional tablets. A relationship will be developed between blood glucose level and drug concentration which will help to tailor therapy. The project will benefit both the diabetic patients and pharmaceutical industry. Commonly used excipients and machinery will enable the local pharmaceutical industry to develop novel dosage forms with minimum cost and within the available resources.

data.projectName: In-Plane and Out-of-Plane Behavior of Slender Cold Formed Sections
data.projectDigest:
Pre-Engineered Building (PEB) are rapidly growing because of low initial cost, super quality, fast project construction, functional versatility, architectural flexibility etc. This flexibility allows PEBs to fulfill an almost unlimited range of building configurations, custom designs, requirements and applications. Cold formed sections are key elements of PEB’s as roof purlins, roof covering, eave struts and wall girts.  Till time, for these sections, design codes and construction practices need further development. 

Current research work is based upon the variation of these section profiles and its effect on in-plane (tension / compression), out-of-plane (bending) and buckling behavior of cold formed members. In this study, structural shapes (Zees and Channels) will be evaluated by varying section depth, lip length and angle. Bending and compression tests will be conducted using reaction frame and automated data acquisition system. 

The aim of this project is to optimize the in-plane and out-of-plane behavior of slender cold formed sections as beam members and columns. Results regarding effective utilization of cold-formed sections in PEB Industry will be discussed with the industry and will later be published.

data.projectName: DNA Methylation of heat shock proteins and transcription factors as markers of heat stress in Dairy cattle
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Heat stress affects productivity and health of cattle. It can be reduced by identifying molecular markers and selecting heat tolerant strains of cattle which confer thermo-tolerance in animals. Heat shock proteins (HSPs) like HSP27, HSP70 and HSP90 are most important in this regard that mitigate heat stress in cattle. They are molecular chaperone that prevents denaturation of other protein during heat stress and helps in their renaturation. Up-regulation of HSP expression is reported to have protective affects during heat stress and animal with up-regulated levels have been reported to be thermo-tolerant. Regulation of HSP27, 70 and 90 levels is controlled by epigenetic variations like DNA methylation changes on these genes that affect the expression.  So, the study will compare DNA methylation variations in HSP27, 70 and 90 in Holstein (less thermo-tolerant) to Sahiwal cattle (more thermo-tolerant) and will also assess the expression levels in both cattle breeds during summer (high THI) and winter (low THI). These changes will be statistically associated with temperature humidity index, heat tolerance co-efficient, rectal temperature and milk yield.

data.projectName: Support of Media Information Literacy (MIL) for responsible new media practices by youth
data.projectDigest: This project will cover the media literacy of the indigenous media practitioners and social media users. It will explore the consumption pattern of media consumers and practitioners that how they use & produce the content for social media and why they spread this content on social media. How they can improve it for the development of both media practitioners and users at indigenous level. The goal of this project is to make users of social and indigenous media a responsible, as social responsibility theory describe; Social responsibility is ethics that guide any action, be it in media or other organizations that put an obligation towards environment, society, culture and economy. The media like any other sector should not harm, but should promote environment and socio-cultural aspects in relation to the economy of the place. This project will also helpful for students as part of their curriculum living in this digital and informative era. The purpose of being information and media literate is to engage in a digital society; one needs to be able to understand, inquire, create, communicate and think critically. It is important to effectively access, organize, analyze, evaluate, and create messages in a variety of forms. Main purpose of project is to make media users a responsible user, that can develop the society socially and economically. Different activities will be done for the training of the schools and college students regarding social media use. Findings will be helpful for curricula and common social media users.

data.projectName: IMPACT BEHAVIOUR OF REINFORCED CONCRETE STRUCTURAL ELEMENTS
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The reinforced concrete structural elements during its design and operational life may be subjected to the accidental activities which result in forces having magnitudes and intensities much higher than the typical static loading rates. For the case of reinforced concrete slabs, number of studies have been published which mainly investigated its response when subjected to the initial contact velocities of up to 1000m/s.  However, for the case of the slabs used in civil and non-protective structural construction, the loading intensities produced as a result of accidental and abnormal impact activities are mainly caused due to velocities of up to 10 m/s. Similar to the reinforced concrete slabs, the interior columns of the structures, columns located in the parking areas may also be subjected to low level velocity impacts. Besides the significant importance both in terms of safety and stability of the structure, the behaviour of reinforced concrete slabs and columns subjected to low velocity impacts have not been studied extensively in the published literature till date. Therefore, this investigation aims in studying both experimentally and numerically the response of the reinforced concrete slabs and columns subjected to low velocity impact loads. Based on the investigation conducted detailed design curves will be produced that can present the residual capacity or degree of damage sustained by structural elements when subjected to certain levels of impact energies generated due to the accidental loadings.

data.projectName: Thermal management of microelectronics devices using hybrid nano-fluid with metal foam heat sink
data.projectDigest:
One of the main challenges in the development of high-tech compact devices is to provide effective cooling system. In 1965, Moore observed this miniaturization and said that the number of transistors per square inch on integrated circuit doubled every two years since their invention and he predicted that it would continue in future as well. These devices generate heat while they are operating and it is necessary to remove this heat from these devices continuously for their reliable and efficient operation. However, due to decrease in size of these devices and increase in speed of microprocessors constantly, the provision of efficient cooling system has become an important and integral part of design of such devices. An effective cooling system is necessary to ensure reliability of these high-tech compact devices. 
The main objective of the project is to provide effective cooling system for the high-tech compact devices to improve the lives of these devices along with reliability. We will achieve our objective with combination of porous material/metal foam and hybrid nano-fluids. 
The anticipated benefits of this project include the development of effective cooling system which will allow manufacturers of high-tech devices to enhance the reliably of these devices. The industries where it can be used includes: electronics (computes, UPS), refrigeration, automobile etc.

data.projectName: Production of lactase for industrial and therapeutic value from Yeast
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Lactase is an enzyme, produced by cells in the small intestine, that convert lactose (sugar found in milk) into glucose and galactose.  Unfortunately 70% of world’s inhabitants lacks this enzyme and cannot utilize lactose therefore developing lactose maldigestion or intolerance. These people relay on Lactase enzyme supplement to digest dairy products without suffering from bloating, gas, stomach and aches. Beside this, enzymatic hydrolysis of lactose has several technological and environmental advantages for industrial applications. The application of enzyme is important in the conversion of cheese whey, a waste from dairy industry into different value added products. The present study is designed to develop method for production of Lactase enzyme from local strains. In phase one,  lab-scale parameter will be optimized and in second phase optimized condition will be up-scale for large scale industrial application.

data.projectName: Ecotoxic effects of pesticides on targeted epigenetic enzymes of ecosystem engineers (Earthworms)
data.projectDigest:
Nobel Science Laureates of 2019 stress urgency of addressing climate change. Emission of greenhouse gases drastically affect the climate and one of major ways to tackle is the sustainable use of agriculture to trap the harmful gases in the soil. Agriculture contributes 19.5 percent to gross domestic product and employs 42.3 percent of the labor force in Pakistan. Pakistan is ranked 12th among the list of highly vulnerable countries to climate change. The extensive usage of pesticides/fertilizers leads to pollution affecting target and non-target organisms such as Earthworms.

Earthworms being ecosystem engineers provide key soil functions that favour many positive ecosystem services such as soil formation, decaying organic matter, increasing soil fertility and nutrient mineralization. Earthworms are pivotal in trapping the carbon dioxide in soil; they convert the digestible carbon to a form that stays in the soil. These services are important for agroecosystem sustainability but can be degraded by intensive cultural practices such as use of pesticides.  Pesticides effects the earthworms by affecting their behavior, defile metabolism, enzymatic functioning, enhance mortality; diminish fertility, growth and reproduction. 

Prevailing lack of information on the effect of pesticides on earthworm and indirectly on climate change, it will be endeavored in the current study to analyze and unlock the impact of pesticides on targeted epigenetic enzymes of earthworm such as Acetylcholinesterase, Glutathione-S-Transferase and Gamma Amino Butyric Acid Amino Transferase. The current study will also focus on analyzing the effect of pesticides on carbon-trapping capability of Earthworms which indirectly leads to enhance the greenhouse gases emission.

data.projectName: Molecular identification of Ascaris lumbricoides in contaminated soil of different areas of Punjab, Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Lahore College for Women University, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Ascariasis is a disease which is caused by Ascaris lumricoides (A. lumbricoides). It is one of the soil transmitted Helminths (STHs) commonly present in tropical and sub-tropical regions and it infects human causing due to low sanitary conditions. A. lumricoides is worldwide in distribution. It is 80-100 % in rural areas than urban slums due to poor sewage system. Eggs of A. lumbricoides are sticky, so attach to commode seats, food utensils contaminate drinking water and might be occur in household dust, a danger for children. Approximately 59 million persons are at danger and expected 1.5 million children suffered from this disease, resulted in permanent growth hindrance even if the infection was treated. A. lumricoides live in the small intestine of human. About 180,000 eggs are produced per day and are released with the feces. If by chance due to contamination eggs are swallowed, it hatch as larvae and transfer in the intestine and then passes to the lungs through blood circulatory system. Further development of larvae occur in the lungs and then passes to esophagus, these larvae enter in the small intestine and develops into mature worms. Adult worms can live 1 to 2 years in the infected person

data.projectName: Antidotes from Traditional Medicine: Studies on Snake Venom Neutralizing Protein and Peptides from Albizia lebbeck (L.) Benth and Amaranthus viridus.
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Snake envenomation is a serious health problem commonly occur in developing countries and rural population. In Sindh, main cases of snake envenomation are caused by Cobra, Krait, Russell and Saw-scaled viper. The only treatment to this envenomation is either antidotes or folklore from traditional medicine. Many vials of antidotes are required to treat single patient in presence of trained professional and proper facilities. Antidotes production in Pakistan is not up to the required demand. Antidote vials imported from India are not effective against our snake species. Besides that, antidote administration causes severe allergic and side reactions that require additional treatment. Numerous plants extracts are used in Indian sub-continent to effectively treat envenomation. Two of these are: Albizia lebbeck and Amaranthus viridus. Therefore, the current study is designed to check the anti-venom activity of proteins and peptide from these plants against cobra and saw scaled viper venom. Also, their possible mechanism of action will be determined. These plant proteins / peptides once identified will serve as lead molecules to treat envenomation and may form basis for the development of new antidotes. These antidotes from plant will be cost effective, economic friendly and with less side effects.

data.projectName: Ecological and human health risk assessment for heavy metal contamination and its remediation along melange zone north Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Ecological and human health risk assessment for heavy metal contamination and its remediation along melange zone north Pakistan

 Environmental pollution due to natural and anthropogenic sources is of utmost concern for the survival and health of our planet. Various environmental hazards faced and risks posed to our fragile ecosystem and the vulnerable populations  not only need evaluation and assessment of these issues but also requires concrete steps for its remediation . This study addresses the issue of contamination of our valuable environmental media (drinking water, agricultural soil, food material derived from vegetation & trees) due to toxic  heavy metals, a recognized environmental problem posing risks to our ecosystems and human health and some suitable mitigating measures in this regard. These heavy metals are persistence in nature and can easily being transferred from rocks, soil to water and vegetation and travel through the food chain. Some of these metals like, arsenic, lead, chromium, cadmium etc. have been recognized for deleterious human health impacts. These toxic elements will be evaluated  for the possible hazards they posed along with their carcinogenic and non-carcinogenic risks assessment for the ecosystem in general and human health in particular. In addition, new mitigation techniques will be search out for these  toxic metals immobilization and reduction in various environmental compartments in order to save our precious water and fertile soils for our daily needs as well as for our future generations.  This study would also be helpful for contributing input towards environmental policy formulation in the region.

data.projectName: Identification of drought and salinity tolerance genes in sunflower
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: The production of oilseed crops in Pakistan is low as compared to  the national demand. Sunflower is an important oilseed crop and is successfully grown under different climatic conditions. This study will be conducted to determine the genetic diversity and population structure of sunflower inbred lines and explore putative QTLs for genes which may be involved in important developmental pathways providing drought and salt tolerance. A set of 100 word-wide oilseed sunflower inbred lines will be investigate under well-watered, drought and  salt stress conditions using simple lattice design with two replications during two cropping seasons. Genome-wide SNP genotyping will be done using the Affymetrix 10K SNP Array by TraitGenetics Company (Gatersleben, Germany). Finally, genome-wide association analysis will be conducted using a general linear model (GLM) and mixed linear model (MLM) in both TASSEL v.5 and GAPIT package in R to obtain the unbiased estimation of marker effects. This study will provide valuable information about genetic diversity of studied sunflower lines which can help sunflower breeders to select parents for crossing to find new hybrid vigor and improve sunflower germplasm's genetic diversity under different climate conditions in Pakistan and Iran. The identified markers in this study could also  provide useful genetic resources to initiate marker-assisted selection, fine mapping and cloning of the underlying genes and QTLs for salt and drought stresses tolerance.

data.projectName: COMPETENCE BASED TEACHING IN SOCIAL SCIENCE SUBJECTS
data.projectDigest: Competency means full command and grip of an individual on a particular subject both on its theoretical know how as well as the application of that acquired knowledge in practical work and life scenarios. Competency-based education (CBE) has become a hot topic in higher education circles these days. CBE takes all the three major aspects under its umbrella i.e. teacher, student and curriculum. So to speak we can further elaborate it as competency based curriculum, competency based teaching and competency based learning. In order to bridge the gap between theory and practice, a descriptive type of study is designed to collect information and viewpoints of the stakeholders. Mixed method design will be adopted for data collection purposes which will analyze the data and on the basis of these findings recommendations will be forwarded for the implementation of CBC in actual class room situations.

data.projectName: :  Computer Assisted Modeling of Natural Products As Novel Insulin Secretagogue
data.projectDigest: Diabetes is a chronic metabolic syndrome, and the Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is a global pandemic with over 463 million population suffering with this disease. Diabetes is the seventh leading cause of death.  The recent report of number of diabetes alone in Pakistan is 27.4 million. The cAMP sensor Epac2 is a direct target of antidiabetic sulfonylurea drugs, providing a potential non-ionic signaling factor to the mechanism of action of these drugs. The available insulin secretagogues associated with numerous undesirable effects such as increased risk of hepatic, kidney and cardiac problems, neurologic sequelae and the nastiest of all is sulfonylurea-induced hypoglycemia. Therefore, identification of new, effective and safer insulin secretagogues is one of the challenging demands in current clinical research. The proposed approach explains high-throughput computational virtual screening of compound using knowledge based hierarchical analysis by utilizing a unique in-house natural product database available at the ICCBS. Given our success in finding novel chemical entities that could activate the function of Epac2 protein, further we proceed with biological characterization and evaluation of insulinotropic mechanism followed by in vitro testing to provide proof-of-principle evidence for the efficacy of these compounds as therapeutic agents.

data.projectName: Intelligent Road Electric Poles for Road Accidents Detection and Vehicle Direction Management
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Benazir Bhutto University Shaheed, Benazirabad
data.projectDigest:
The current trends of technology are changing research dimensions from traditional applications to public-oriented applications. The smart transportation system and smart cities are the main public domains need to be digitized. According to the latest studies, traffic accidents are the majority cause of human death due to the dramatical increase in the number of road vehicles and poor traffic management systems. There are different types of vehicles on roads such as motorbikes, cars, cycles and buses; pedestrians also use the road as main traveling tracks in cities. data.projectName: Development of novel porous PAN-CNT-alumina hybrid membranes via electrospinning to remove toxic heavy metals from ground water.
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
In Pakistan, industrial processes produce large quantities of wastewater contaminated with trace heavy metals, such as arsenic and cadmium. Fatal effect of these heavy metals is alarming in the areas adjacent to industrial wastes and agriculture activities where the concentration of these heavy metal cations in ground water has been reported to be far more than the safety limit set by WHO. 
In the proposed study, advanced materials synthesis technique (Electrospinning) would be employed to develop porous polymer-based membranes doped with CNT’s and alumina, to remove toxic heavy metals such as arsenic from the wastewater. The idea of multi doped polymeric membrane is to utilize the excellent adsorption property of CNT’s and alumina towards the removal of heavy metal cations. We propose to utilize polyacrylonitrile (PAN) as the matrix together with the additives such as nano-alumina and CNTs to develop hybrid porous membranes. The polymer is selected due to it’s hydrophilic nature, chemical stability and proven electrospinability. Characterization of the membranes would include examination of the morphology of the fibers using electron microscopy, identification of the functional groups using FTIR, hydrophilicity of the membranes using contact angle measurements, tensile strength assessment of the membrane and heavy metal removal efficiency.

data.projectName: Economic Analysis of Export Supply Chain for Fresh Vegetables in the Case of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
This study aims to analyze exports supply chain for fresh vegetables in the districts of KP Province, Pakistan. The study will target not only small-scale producers of fresh vegetables, but also all those stakeholders involved in processing, packaging, logistics and marketing work in the export supply chain. The study will be the first of its kind for export supply chain of fresh vegetables in the country’s case. The project is expected to cover fresh vegetables products from three districts of the KP Province. The amount of the project is estimated at Rs.12.46 million.
This study will certainly provide direct information to the producer and exporters, who are involved in fresh vegetables’ production and exporting activities. The research objective is to explore and identify potential vegetable products that can boost the export earnings and welfare of stakeholders. The outcome will guide the management authorities to formulate suitable policies to promote both the farming community and business community who engaged with production and exporting of fresh vegetable. The ultimate outcomes would be to increase exports volumes, thereby increasing our earnings and improving the balance of payment and living standards.

data.projectName: Identification and characterization of abiotic stress resistant microalgae strains helpful for biodiesel production
data.projectDigest: Lack of control at high temperatures is one of the major environmental factor that has significant effects on the growth and lipid production of any organism particularly microalgae. Temperature has a profound effect on the growth and physiology of microalgae and should be critically evaluated. We will attempt to enhance the growth and total lipid production of different microalgae from different genus under high temperature stress because they can be possibly utilized as novel raw materials for biodiesel production. We will study the effects of different ranges of cultivation temperatures on biomass and lipid productivity, carbohydrate, protein, chlorophyll and carotenoids content, detailed fatty acid methyl ester (FAME) signature, reactive oxygen species, their enzymes like catalases and peroxidases particularly for ascorbate and lipid peroxidation in microalgae. We will further identify the Fatty Acid Methyl Esterases (FAMEs) for their suitability to be used as biodiesel components. We will exploit the technique of GC-MS. As an evidence we will report that temperature is a critical environmental factor and it can modulate the amount and composition of fatty acids. The responding microalgal strains can be considered as a potential strain for exploration of new renewable energy.

data.projectName: Development of Graphene-metal oxides catalysts for water treatment and production of hydrogen gas
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan is a developing country where large numbers of various industries are running for which Pakistan has always been an energy importer and is highly dependent on fossil fuels. With the rising fossil fuel prices, the cost of oil importing is creating a dent on Pakistan’s foreign exchange reserves. As a consequence, the pollution and energy crises are the emerging problems in Pakistan. Textile industry is one of them which use dyes in large amount. Textile industry release about 20% of the dyes employed in waste water. 
Therefore, this research proposal is considered as one of the solutions to pollution control and energy crises. In this project various effective metal oxide-graphene catalysts will be synthetized for treatment of water and production of green fuel, the hydrogen gas. Hydrogen is known as an alternative new energy for its advantages of non-pollution and high calorific value.

data.projectName: EFFECT OF VITAMIN D SUPPLEMENTATION ON INFLAMMATORY MARKERS (IL-6, TNF-? & CRP) AND LIPID PROFILE IN PATIENTS OF NON-ST ELEVATION ACUTE CORONARY SYNDROME
data.projectDigest:
Cardiovascular disease particularly acute coronary syndrome ACS is one of the major causes of mortality and morbidity in developed as well as under developed countries.The burden of disease is increasing with increasing risk factors and lifestyles changes. Estimated number of the patients worldwide presenting to the ER department with the chest pain is 5 to 8 million. The causes of ACS include genetic factors as well as modifiable factors. Beside the most common risk factors of acute myocardial infarction (AMI), the new emerging risk factors are being identified. Among these, a recently identified risk factor is vitamin D deficiency that is hypovitaminosis D. Studies have shown that vitamin D deficiency has been associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes and morbidity and mortality. 
Recently, Vitamin D supplementation trials are being used. Vitamin D supplementation has been given to stable angina patients to assess the improvement in symptoms clinically. Also trials with supplementation on patients  to determine the effect on inflammatory markers are done. But there is sparse data available regarding the effects of vitamin D supplementation on clinical outcome of the patients in  myocardial infarction. The aim of the present study is to determine the effects of vitamin D supplementation on markers of inflammation in patients of non ST elevation myocardial infarction.

data.projectName: Exploring effect of raw and fermented Cruciferous sprouts powder consumption on gut microbiome, satiety and obesity markers
data.projectDigest: Plant based diet is supposed to be an effective strategy to develop and promote diverse gut microbial ecosystem. Growing evidences have suggested gut microbiome as potential factor linked to the pathophysiology of obesity, metabolic disorders and comorbidities. High fiber and distinctive chemical composition of plant foods like the cruciferous vegetables promote production of short chain fatty acids (SCFAs) like acetate, butyrate and propionates that reduces ghrelin concentration, promote early satiety and reduced food intake. Short chain fatty acids like butyrates and propionates promote early satiety by inducing expression of leptin and maintaining energy homeostasis by reduced energy intake and increased energy expenditure. Dietary fibers, polyphenols and glucosinolates are distinctive features of vegetables under brassicaceae family that are readily hydrolyzed by gut microbiome to short chain fatty acids and bioactive molecules of human health significance. Fermented vegetables significantly influence gut microbiome profile and levels, and modulates desirable population to promote gut health and immunity against a myriad of diseases. Present study  has been planned to evaluate impact of fermented cabbage sprouts consumption on intestinal microbiome and short chain fatty acids composition, satiety function, obesity and co-morbidity markers in normal and obese rats’ model.

data.projectName: A hybrid approach for investigation of morphology and pharmacology of iron and zinc oxide nanoparticles utilizing Mentha asiatica added with external modifiers
data.piUniversity: Capital University of Science and Technology, Islamabad
data.projectDigest: Nanotechnology is a novel approach used for manipulation of physical and chemical properties of a substance at the molecular level. Nanoparticles and nano devices have the potential to show a positive impact on human health and they can be used in treating various serious diseases because of their nano size which is much compatible with the biological systems. In nanotechnology metal and metal oxide nanoparticles are being produced which have received global consideration because of their widespread uses in the biomedical research. Thus, in the quest of exploring new biogenic agents from natural resources, we aim to synthesize iron and zinc oxide nanoparticles using Mentha asiatica (mint) extract to prepare novel authentic agents for therapeutic usage. The main purpose of this study is to generate stabilized nanoparticles with much less effort and economic value. This study also aims to characterize these particles by UV-Vis, SEM/EDS, XRD, FTIR to find out the shape and size of iron and zinc oxide nanoparticles and other physical characteristics and the impact of adding modifiers (maleic acid, citric acid and PVP) on their morphology. The abilities performing different biological activities utilizing different in vitro (antibacterial, antioxidant, cytotoxic and antidiabetic) and in vivo (anti-inflammatory, anti-coagulant and anti-depressant) approaches will also be evaluated. Furthermore, gene expression of possible targets of breast cancer will also be evaluated after treatment of breast cancer cells with synthesized nanoparticles. These iron and zinc oxide nanoparticles can be good candidates to be explored further in combination therapies against different diseases in future.

data.projectName: Characterization and optimization of novel enterocins for pathogen eradication and control
data.projectDigest: Enterocins are small proteins released by certain bacteria, enterococci, that kill other bacteria. Multiple enterocins are produced by many strains making it difficult to know which is best in any given situation. In this proposal I will take a genetic approach to produce many enterocins individually, allowing each to be tested for killing different pathogenic bacteria. Once my first catalogue of these “recombinant enterocins” is complete I will modify individual enterocins to try and make them more potent, improving on nature to give us a new compound able to kill pathogenic bacteria more efficiently. In addition I will try mixing and matching different optimized enterocins to produce ever more powerful killing activities. My research should generate new compounds with which to treat infections caused by antibiotic resistant organisms, which are currently rising worldwide. I will also put my improved enterocins back into enterococci strains and assess them for use as probiotics where they secrete enterocins naturally to reduce pathogenic organisms in the gut and so improve general nutrition.

data.projectName: BROWN COAL BASED SLOW RELEASE NITROGEN FERTILIZER FOR CLIMATE SMART SOIL NITROGEN, CARBON, AND WATER MANAGEMENT
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Improving the efficiency of the use of nitrogen (NUE) and reducing the depletion of soil organic matter are major global challenges. Brown coal, commonly known as lignite, is characterized by very low heating capacity; however, it can be effectively used as an ingredient in slow release fertilizers (SRFs). It contains organic carbon in a complex, porous, and three dimensional network. But the composition of brown coal varies depending on the location of the deposit. Humic acids account for 10-80 % of organic matter in brown coal (Allard, 2006) and these humic substances comprise a number of functional chemical groups that help to modify and improve the soil's chemical properties. Brown coal could therefore be an alternative material with properties that make it attractive for use as a N fertilizer carrier. Brown coal–urea blended fertilizers have a long-term potential for more efficient use of N and have environmental benefits in retaining more N in the soil (Rose et al., 2016; Saha et al., 2017). In this project, granulated brown coal based slow release N fertilizer will be produced by impregnating urea in brown coal in different proportions and then coating it with polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and starch as binders. Such SRFs are expected to reduce the gaseous losses of N by slowing its release into soil, resulting in enhanced NUE in soils. It will also extend many additional benefits, including improved carbon sequestration, water retention, nutrient retention and microbial habitat in the soil. It will also reduce the rate of application of urea and labor expenditure. It will provide new  business and employment opportunities. Export of this product could make a huge foreign exchange, as Pakistan has vast reserves of brown coal that can be used as a cost-effective input.

data.projectName: Sustainable and Cost Effective and Sustainable Protein Alternatives in Carp Feedural waste
data.projectDigest:
Fish meal and soybean meal are most important and valuable ingredients in aquafeeds due to their nutrient profile (high protein content). Fish meal is the costly ingredient in fish diets and its sustained production is not guaranteed because of high catch from wild source. In order to replace animal protein source with the plant/vegetable protein, soybean meal was introduced with the hope to help reduce the prices of aquafeeds but it turned out to be expensive when used. Imported soybean with U.S. soy’s nutritional profile is preferred where cost is again a barrier. 
Aquafeed manufacturers and aquaculture nutritionists, therefore, trying to look for cheap but high protein alternatives that could reduce the ever growing cost and availability of fish and soybean meal. Plant products are naturally protein rich sources and have been reported to improve the growth in aquaculture practices (3). Locally available plant proteins have the potential to be used as sustainable feed ingredients and they can also cost effectively replace fish meal and soybean meal in fish feeds.
In order to increase fish production in developing countries, research regarding availability of cheaper high profile protein and energy feedstuffs has become a priority in order to develop low cost feed which must be suitable for use by small-scale fish farmers. There is a dire need to explore alternate high protein plant sources for fish feed formulation. To increase the propagation and sustenance of aquaculture sector, alternative viable protein sources must be explored as the sustainable substitutes of expensive feed ingredients (fish meal and soybean meal). Lower price, greater availability and improved consistency of composition are some of the advantages of using plants as protein sources. Ident

data.projectName: Survey of Small Ruminants for Mycoplasmas Associated with Contagious Agalactia and Contagious Caprine Pleuropneumonia in South Punjab
data.projectDigest: This project is designed to conduct extensive surveillance of economically important mycoplasmas, causing contagious agalactia (CA) and contagious caprine pleuropneumonia (CCPP), in sheep and goat populations. Districts of South Punjab, heavily populated with small ruminants, will be selected for this study. This study will involve serological and molecular identification techniques, and mycoplasma isolates will be further genotyped using the latest molecular genotyping approaches, e.g., multilocus sequence typing (MLST). Investigation of the evolutionary relationships of the newly isolated mycoplasma species will be useful to assess the genetic diversity of Pakistani isolates, and also the genetic relationship with pathogenic strains in other parts of the world. Information on the antibiogram of small ruminant mycoplasmas will also be generated, which will help in devising better treatment plans. Diagnostic antigens, to be used in latex agglutination tests for CA- and CCPP-associated mycoplasmas, will also be developed and optimized for the pen-side diagnosis of small ruminant mycoplasma infections at the farm level. In the future, mycoplasma isolates, recovered in this study, will be further studied to establish their pathogenicity, and highly pathogenic but immunogenic isolates will be used in the development of inactivated vaccines. It is expected that such vaccines will be useful in controlling the economically important diseases of small ruminants in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Novel multitrophic interaction-based approaches to rapidly adapt plants to problematic and poorly managed soils
data.projectDigest: One of the major consequences of industrialization in southeast Asia will be increased frequency and severity of heavy metals and organic pollutants. The proposed project will focus on hyper accumulator plants resistance and resilience to pollutants stress and will employ a novel conceptual approach, focusing on the multitrophic (the inseparable combination of the plant and its associated microbes with grazers). The overall objective is to better understand adaptation/evolution mechanisms to improve within a single or a few um horizons, the biotechnological and conceptual framework developed in this project could be used to help plants adapt to higher pollution pressure or lower fertilization or any other biotic or abiotic stress. The project will also help crop improvement and microbial inoculant industries develop novel products and approaches, strategically positioning them in the market when easily accessible inorganic fertilizer sources will be exhausted and pollution will reach its pinnacle. data.projectName: Fabrication of portable, highly sensitive, and cost-effective sensor for the monitoring of antimicrobial drug residues in food stuff: a global threat to public health
data.projectDigest: Antibiotics are used to treat and prevent bacterial infection for humans and animals, but improper use and occurrence of unsafe levels of antimicrobial drug residues in food, poses a serious threat to general public health hence adversely affecting the environment and economy of the country. Based on the above mentioned triggering facts, it is the dire need of the day to fabricate an accurate, rapid, cost effective and easy to operate screening technique for selective and highly sensitive monitoring of antimicrobial drug residue levels in animal-originated food stuff. To date various analytical techniques have been deployed to evaluate the drug residue levels in food products derived from animals. however,  their major limitations are being time-consuming, expensive, laborious, requiring highly trained persons and limited in centralized laboratories. These issues can be resolved by enzymeless electroanalytical methods by being simple, rapid, inexpensive, easy to handle and portable procedures. In this proposed research scheme, enzymeless approach will be employed to address the current challenges. Moreover, the selectivity of the sensing platform will be boosted by modifying the electrode surface by the immobilization of certain reagents or an electrochemical pre-treatment which enhances the electrochemical characteristics of the transducer’s surface. The insertion of nanomaterials such as graphene and POMs, can increase the  speed, selectivity and sensitivity to meet the requirements of detection of contaminants in food. It is envisaged that the proposed work will offer a new promising approach for low-cost, field-deployable detection of certain antimicrobial drug residues or their metabolites in real samples to ensure the food safety and quality.

data.projectName: Teaching Pediatric Resuscitation Skills in a Lower-Middle Income Country
data.projectDigest: Currently worldwide, successful educational strategies used in teaching and learning pediatric life support are in the form of short intensive courses over one to three days e.g. Pediatric Advanced Life Support (PALS) provider courses, concentrating on cardiac emergencies and Advanced Pediatric Life Support provider courses (APLS) taking a wider view and teaching cardiac as well as non-cardiac pediatric emergencies. These were introduced to teach resuscitation in a structured, universally accepted approach. But these courses are very expensive, lengthy, offered by limited institutions locally, limited to big cities only and not widely accepted among healthcare practitioner because of all these reasons. We designed this one day course with aim to make it simple, short yet providing the participants basic skill set required for delivering high quality pediatric resuscitation. We will be taking feedback from participants and will modify as and when needed. The overall objective of applying for this educational grant is to educate doctors, paramedical staff/nurses and technicians working in the emergency room, operating theater, post anesthesia recovery room and the pediatric wards in the major cities of Sind province then extend it whole country.

data.projectName: Strengthening Sustainable Entrepreneurial Farming in Pakistan: Challenges and Way Forward
data.projectDigest: Farming in Pakistan is under severe economic pressure and needs to boost entrepreneurial practices for achieving sustainable development. Conventional farmers in Pakistan are facing severe issues due to the situation of environmental, economic, and social factors. In this context, sustainable entrepreneurial farming (SEF) is the key element to empower the farmers in improving products and practices in production and marketing of agricultural products. Adoption of sustainable practices in the agricultural sector is grabbing the attention from the researchers and practitioners for achieving faster economic growth. Neighboring countries like China, Vietnam, Thailand, and India are concentrating on sustainable entrepreneurial farming. The objectives of this study will be 1) to investigate the barriers in adoption of sustainable entrepreneurial farming 2) to develop the framework for measuring / prioritizing of potential barriers 3) to suggest policy implications / way forward for the concerned stakeholders in Pakistan. In order to fulfill the research objectives, an extensive review of literature and field visits will be conducted to assess the barriers faced by farmers. The expected outcomes of this research will be helpful for Government in making strategic decisions and policies related to promote the sustainable agricultural practices at farm level.

data.projectName: Development of Double-Layered-Hydrotalcite Based Al-Ni-Ca Catalyst for Hydrogen Production by Sorption Enhanced Methane Reforming
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: It is believed that hydrogen is a clean and renewable energy source. Currently hydrogen is being produced industrially methane steam reforming, but this process cause high carbon dioxide emissions. The said process can be replaced with sorption enhanced methane reforming (SEMR). In SEMR, the produced carbon dioxide is adsorbed on the catalyst surface which can later be regenerated via steam purging. A highly stable catalyst is required for this process. In this project a Layered-structure Hydrotalcoite based Al-Ni-Ca catalyst is proposed for SEMR. Synthesis of catalyst and its performance studies are included in this project.

data.projectName: Optically Induced Magnetism in Structurally Modified Carbon Derivatives
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: Recently, the properties of structurally modified carbon derivatives have the potential for challenging fields such as nano-electronics, hydrogen storage, batteries and sensors etc. especially exploring by stacking order, layer numbers, external electric and magnetic fields. In particular, the structural engineering in graphitic layers allowed a viable route to tune the carrier movement in particular direction and manipulate these dynamics in terms of optically induced magnetism. Such manipulation of carrier dynamics could be important in understanding the carrier transport and optical phenomenon in functional devices. Owing to centrosymmetric nature of these carbon derivative, optically induced magnetism is favorable which could easily be detected by SQUID or MCD spectroscopy. Moreover, photoluminescence spectroscopy could also give insight into the circularly polarized induced transition among defect states.

data.projectName: Collection of Bacteriophages against Patient Isolated Extensively Drug Resistant Acinetobacter Baumannii
data.projectDigest: Infections caused by Acinetobacter baumannii, a bacterium, have one of the highest mortality rates. Reason behind this is their extensive drug resistance. During last two years, we have collected more than 100 strains of this bacterium which all resulted in patients’ death because no antibiotic was able to reduce infection burden. We have already isolated a virus that could kill one of these strains, raising our hopes that, one day, we can use them to clear infections in clinical settings. But an effective treatment regimen based on viruses requires that we have a library of viruses effective against broad variety of Acinetobacter strains. Therefore, current project aims to achieve this objective; collecting at least 20 different viruses against this bacterium and characterizing them at molecular level to determine their short-term and well as long term safety.  Through isolation and basic characterization of one virus against this bacterium, our lab has developed necessary expertise related to this work. But further work requires considerable resources which cannot be obtained through departmental and personal funding.

data.projectName: Design and analysis of multilayer 2D devices using DFT simulations
data.projectDigest: After the advent of the semiconductor devices in 1947 the human history has witnessed an era of emergence of digital electronics. Today everything around us is directly or indirectly linked to computer related applications, such as barcode reader in supermarkets, internet, mobile phone etc. All these electronics devices contain electronic integrated circuits (IC’s). Semiconductor devices size has shrunk to its minimum possible dimensions and can not be further miniaturised due to quantum limits. Now scientific world wants to switch towards 2D electronic devices.Density Functional Theory (DFT) simulation is used to understand the electrical behaviour of  devices based on 2D material. DFT provides an alternative method to analyse and find best configurations and materials to build devices such as transistors and sensors. This project will focus on finding best geometries and materials that could be used in real fabrication of nano devices.

data.projectName: Molecular Breeding
data.projectDigest: Variation in the population is the basic of plant breeding which lead to the development of high yielding cultivars.  A continuous selection for the high yielding plant type has narrowed the variation in existing population; so, a limited choice for the development of new rice cultivars. There are number of approaches for induction of variation in the plants, including; DNA insertion, chemical and physical mutagens., As per our knowledge, so far so Gamma-rays (?-rays), a type of physical mutagenesis, is the best approach for rice. According to FAO, during 2019, 92% of the rice mutants developed were through ?-rays. In our country, though a lot of work on generating variation in the population using gamma rays has been carried out, but, limited knowledge, regarding detection of this random mutation has been reported yet. In the current project, genetic variability in the major rice genotypes will be induced through Gamma-rays (?-rays) at NIAB (Nuclear Institute of Agricultural Biotechnology). Screening of successful inheritance of the mutation in the morphological traits in M1 and M2 generations will be studied in experimental area of Plant Breeding and genetics, IUB. The successful mutation in the desired traits will be detected through appropriate techniques. This will be the first-time detection of random mutation in the genes of yield related economically important traits of major rice genotypes. Our research outcome of detection of useful random mutation will help the scientific community to incorporate the desired traits into new cultivars.

data.projectName: Improving the Leadership and Management Skills of the school heads in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
data.projectDigest:
Project Digest
This project intends to make the conditions of the schools better by focusing on the 21st century Leadership and Management skills of the school heads/leaders (Male and Female). School heads are the core actors in educational improvement. Currently in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) over 2.5 million children are out of school. The 68% mothers fell in the illiterate category. Schools sanitation and hygiene condition is not satisfactory (Ahmed et al., 2015). There is no SLO based teaching. Dropout at schools is increasing day by day. The overall condition of education in the province is alarming. The leadership and management skills are the core area for the development of the education in the schools. The heads play their role in improving the performance of teachers which in turn change the fate of their students. This research project explores the problems of the heads of school and tries to eliminate or minimize these issues through seminars/workshops/Discussions and debates in the selected southern backward districts of KP, Pakistan. They are comprised of District Kark, District Bannu, District Lakki Marwat, District Tank and District DIKhan. All the Male a Female head of the Middle/High and higher secondary schools of the Southern Districts of Khyberpakhtunkhwa will be the target population of the study. A suitable and representative sample of 1225 heads (Male & Female) will be selected. Collaboration will be made with other universities/institutes and District education directorates on the subject. The dissemination of findings and results will be made in the form of a research report/thesis along with an effort to adjust the findings in a course at the Gomal University level.

data.projectName: Induction of SIRT 1 Can Prevent Diabetic Nephropathy by Promoting Autophagy
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: A lot of work has been done to find the pathogenesis of diabetic nephropathy. The efforts have mostly focused on ‘advanced glycation end products’ and generation of free radicals. Recently researchers have identified that the autophagy within cells is an important process for cellular health. A decline in autophagy due to any reason can damage the nephrons and conversely an increase in autophagy can improve cellular health. SIRT 1 protein (NAD-dependent deacetylase sirtuin-1) has been found to be associated with increased autophagy. It is hypothesized that SIRT 1 gene induction leads to increased autophagy and can prevent renal damage in face of diabetes. Resveratrol is a natural phenolic compound produced in plants and used as supplement in older age, is a known inducer of SIRT-1. In this study, normal and diseased (diabetic nephropathy patients) will be given resveratrol supplements for 1 month. After which mRNA and protein expression of SIRT1 will be reassessed. The autophagy status of the cells after supplementation will be checked using LC3-II. The renal functions will also be assessed before and after supplementation. An improvement in renal function will make this supplement a candidate drug for diabetic nephropathy and draw attention towards autophagy for further research.

data.projectName: STUDY OF RADIOACTIVITY IN THE BUILDING MATERIALS OF PAKISTAN
data.projectDigest: The highlights of the project are to measure the radioactivity in the marbles and granites and also methods and procedures used in the detection of radioactivity. The presence of excessive amounts/activities of 226Ra, 232Th and 40K in marbles and granites are a potential source of radiation. Studies the world over have shown that the use of marbles and granites as a building material has a potential health risk. The aim of this study is to characterize the concentrations of 226Ra 232Th and 40K, in the marbles and granites. A measurement of radioactivity in the building materials is to control the levels of radiation to which man is exposed directly or indirectly. The environment around people is radioactive due to ionizing radiation from the sky, the Earth's crust, and rocks. The objectives of this study are to determine the level of natural radioactivity and associated radiological hazard caused by natural radioactivity in rocks. The samples will be analyzed using gamma-ray spectrometry technique. The spectra of samples were collected and measured using a multichannel analyzer (MCA) connected with the measurement system for this purpose. Activity concentrations of 226Ra 232Th and 40K will be expressed in units Bq.kg-1.

data.projectName: Climate change adaptation and disaster resilience in agricultural production system of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: This study aims at formulation of adaptation option comprised of biophysical, socioeconomic, institutional and policy measures to ensure the farming returns. The second objective is economic analysis of these proposed adaptations to check the viability of these adaptation option to better assess the returns from adoption.  The proposed study is intended to conduct in Punjab province.  The primary and secondary data will be used in this research. Primary data will be collected through a well-designed survey in study area. The data will be collected through questionnaire, focal group discussion, interviews and PRAs. The Participatory research appraisal will be conducted to mobilize the community and formulate the adaptation strategies to combat climate change. The economic analysis and climate change adaptations economic rationale will be estimated through different econometric techniques. The systemic approach would be used for the adaptation framework development and The Tradeoff Analysis Model for Multi-dimensional Impact Assessment (TOA-MD) will be used to estimate the projected impacts on Poverty net farm returns in the study area. The outcome of this research will be helpful for all stakeholder in terms of better livelihood and efficient resource allocation.
