data.projectName: Formulation of Hydro-Economic Model for the Optimal Agricultural Water Allocation based on Demand and Economic Benefits
data.projectDigest: This project aims to formulate an optimized hydro-economic water allocation model for the selected agricultural areas of Pakistan. Frequent water shortages are observed and farmers (i.e., water users) growing different agricultural crops compete for limited water resources during water scarce seasons. Each water user tends to receive maximum amount of water for maximizing individual economic returns and making the water allocation as a multi-objective problem. The addition of stochastic nature of hydrological behavior and climate change factors into the water allocation problem makes it a complex process. Therefore, this project aims to formulate simple and applicable integrated water allocation model to allow the decision makers to allocate the water optimally among various water users with different cropping patterns. The results of this project can support the water release and/or regulatory authorities and decision makers who are responsible to allocate the water from dams and barrages for different uses such as WAPDA and irrigation departments. In Pakistan, water from dams and barrages is released based on the supply system which do not consider the end user demands such as agriculture, industry, domestic and environment sectors. This results inequitable water distribution among different cropping areas and arise conflicts. Moreover, the current water allocation practices do not consider the economic returns which could be attained by optimally releasing the water in dry seasons. Therefore, a successful implementation of hydro-economic model being developed in this study can support the decision makers to optimally allocate the water resources during water scarce seasons while attaining maximum benefits.

data.projectName: Optimization of membrane performance in membrane distillation coupled with other filtration system for textile water treatment and reuse.
data.projectDigest: Membrane is semipermeable micro to nano porous micrometer thin structure which allows water molecules to pass through it while resisting solutes and other impurities to keep separated from water and concentrate solution. Membrane separation is novel water treatment and desalination technology the world has been adopting on large scale with high speed. Membrane distillation is one of the novel membrane separation technology which uses temperature gradient instead pressure of difference to drive membrane separation. Membrane distillation uses hydrophobic membrane isolating hot feed side and cold permeate side. This membrane allows only water vapors to pass across it causing pure water vapors to be condensed and become pure water on permeate side. Textile processing water has high temperature in form of waste heat. This heat in addition to other supplied heat may be used for separation of dye-water solution. However, surfactants reduce surface tension of feed side cause membrane wetting to allow water molecules to pass. data.projectName: Enhancing nitrogen use efficacy with the use of natural nitrogen stabilizers and enriched biochar in wheat crop
data.projectDigest: Intensive cultivation and heavy application of inorganic fertilizer is common practice in developing countries like Pakistan. Nitrogen is considered as king pin due to its most application as compared with other nutrients. Currently, nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) is very low due to its leaching and volatilization losses. Losses nitrogen, not only enhanced the cost of crop production but also a major threat for natural resources. We hypothised, NUE efficiency can be enhanced with the use of some natural resources like biochar and neem formulations. Biochar is a pyrolysed material of crop waste in absence of oxygen which not only improve soil organic matter but can also bind nutrients when enriched physically. Similarly, neem seed has different compounds which can reduces the nitrogen losses when applied in mixture form. Furthermore, we can also mange plant waste in useful manner. Crop waste will be pyrolyzed in the furnace to form the biochar, mix with nitrogen fertilizer and analysed. Resultant material will be dried and palatalized for the further examination and field application. Similarly, neem seeds will be collected from surroundings for oil extraction and neem cake, which will be applied in schematic way along with urea to improve NUE in wheat crop.

data.projectName: Development & Optimization of Innovative Multigrain Baked Products through Chemometric Modeling- An Approach to Introduce Novel Nutritious Products in Pakistani Market
data.projectDigest: Pakistan bakery market has huge expansion potential and has showed stable earnings even during tough economic situations in the country. Bakery products like biscuits, breads, cookies, cakes and crackers are relished by all age groups especially school going children. According to Pakistan Biscuits and Confectionery Manufacturers Association, bakery and confectionery industry has shown an average annual growth of 6.7-7.5%. However, the major bakery products available in Pakistan are mainly three i.e. breads, biscuits and cakes and some of the snacks like potato chips, crackers and nimko etc. Moreover, these products are developed using white wheat flour mostly which gives enough calories but micronutrients and fiber portion is lower in conventional products.  In this proposed project, innovative products mentioned above will be developed using multigrain flours (blends of wheat, corn, oat and barley) using chemometrics modeling and response surface methodology. Products like pretzels, croissants, cinnamon rolls and multigrain baked chips can be good addition in Pakistan baking and snack industries. The immediate beneficiaries of these technologies are anticipated to be small and large baking and snacks industries and ultimately consumers particularly school going children providing them healthier snacks.

data.projectName: Food Waste to Energy Recovery: Current Practices, Management and Biogas Production
data.projectDigest: About one-third of total food production is wasting globally. Among others sources of food waste (FW), wedding halls are the biggest producers of wastes. This FW can be used as opportunity through producing energy by anaerobic digestion.  How to maximize energy recovery from FW is the crucial question confronting the world. Thus, anaerobic digestion is the promising method to maximize biogas production from FW. Therefore, the study in hand is designed to apply anaerobic digestion technique for biogas production in the wedding halls in Lahore. This study is important in number of ways. For instance, per capita FW in the marriage halls is still unknown. Moreover, currant practices regarding FW management are still needed to be explored so that burden on municipal wastes could be reduced. This is also important for Clean and Green Pakistan initiative taken by running government. Another necessity of this study is that it will ensure the gas provision to marriage halls that are main competitor of domestic gas usage. By this way net burden on gas pressure will be relieved that ultimately helpful for overall society of Pakistan. Therefore, this study is design to produce biogas from FW of the wedding halls in Lahore.

data.projectName: Integrated Climate Change Impacts Assessment on Hydrological Extremes in the Transboundary Indus River Basin
data.projectDigest:
Agriculture serves as a safeguard of Pakistan’s economy, it contributes to 19.5% in total GDP and provided the employment of 42.3 % of the country’s population. However, the agriculturally based economy of Pakistan is in danger due to climate change. As the intensity and frequency of climate-sensitive hydro-meteorological extremes have been significantly increased since the 1970s, among of them, drought and extreme precipitations are environmental disaster that adversely affects the agriculture. 
We plan to establish a multi-dimensional study to assess the dynamics of water resources under changing climate with concentrating its socio-economic demand and supply, especially in regards to agricultural perspective for wheat and rice yield areas (Gujranwala, Nawabshah and Thatha) of Indus basin by optimal mitigation of drought and flooding risks; and the best utilization of the projected water resources till 2100. 
The project outcomes in the form of extreme events hazard and vulnerability maps will be fruitful for making mitigation plans of these extreme events in rice and wheat planting areas. Moreover, management strategies investigated with suitable changes in cropping areas of wheat and rice crops along with the optimal water allocation plans in the context of available water could be fruitful to develop the agricultural GDP

data.projectName: Using Gamification to teach basic Project Management concepts
data.projectDigest: The usage of time for entertainment is unparalleled in human history and hence a topic of interest for educators. Several educators are now suggesting that video games could offer us the best opportunity to improve real learning for students. We propose to apply gaming in the teaching of Project Management We have selected Project Management because 1) Gross capital formation (money spent on projects) accounts for 24.3% of the global GDP in 2018 (World Bank, 2019) and 2) Project Management is increasingly being taught across disciplines (engineering, IT, social studies, management, medicine, etc.). In the first phase, we’ll develop the project management content to develop the game. In the second phase, we plan to explore existing gaming platforms to develop a prototype Project Management single-player game with multiple levels of difficulty. Users will be able to learn and apply Project Management concepts and complete challenges to earn a point that will be shared on a leader board. We will further test the before and after knowledge of participants to evaluate the effectiveness of the gaming approach in teaching Project Management. In the third phase seminar, we plan to organize a seminar for launching the project management games for practitioners.

data.projectName: Saving Lives Through a Dysphagia Outreach Program
data.projectDigest:
Dysphagia is the inability to swallow liquids as well solids. It is caused by a myriad of disorders such as a bi-product of stroke, cerebral palsy, traumatic brain injury or other neurodegenerative disorders.  In Cerebral Palsy alone the prevalence has been estimated as 76%  with mild and 15% moderate dysphagia. Only 1% of the sample did not have any form of dysphagia.(1) Speech and language pathologists are the only professionals who assess and manage swallowing difficulties. The dearth of therapists and particularly the emergence of the field poses difficulties for therapeutic input which through minimal input can save lives.  Dysphagia specialist facilities are scarce in major cities of Pakistan but the rural areas have lack even basic facilities. 

The research intends to develop a model of public health for a critical medical concern through training nurses for a supervised outreach for program for assessment and management of dysphagia . This will be a cost-effective method for saving lives. 

Nurses will be trained for assessment and management of swallowing problems in areas where speech and language pathologists are not available. Nurses will be trained  through a hybrid model involving face to face sessions as well as telehealth supervision by a trained clinicians and dysphagia specialist. The study will take place in Chakwal.  It will provide a novel and highly significant model for treatment of dysphagia.

data.projectName: Use of resistant oligosaccharides as a functional ingredient in food products
data.projectDigest:
The replacement of fat in cakes is a challenge as it has an important effect on the structural and sensory properties. Moreover, there is the possibility to incorporate an additional value using novel replacers. In this work, inulin will be used as fat replacer. Inulin will be extracted from chicory roots. The extracted inulin will be assessed for various analysis. Moreover, its techno-functional attributes involving water holding capacity, oil holding capacity, swelling capacity and solubility will also be determined. Afterwards, extracted inulin will be used as a fat replacer in cakes and mayonnaise. Different combinations of replacement levels will be investigated: fat replacement (0 to 50 %).Batter viscosity and weight loss during baking will also be analysed. Cake characteristics will be studied in terms of cell crumb structure, height, texture and sensory evaluation. For efficacy Studies 21 Sprague Dawley rats will be divided into 3 groups .one group will act as control. They will be fed on High Cholesterol diet . After four weeks all rats except control will be fed treated diets. Feed intake, water intake and gain in body weight will be measured regularly .  After 2 months serum Cholesterol ,HDL,LDL will be measured weekly for 2 months  and rats will be dissected and data for organs weight and intestine length be also be measured 
In addition we would like to develop techniques for efficient and sustainable production processes for the use of these natural products as raw materials and thus manufacture them with low cost and effective methods on large scale.

data.projectName: Novel approach to treat the infectious mastitis in dairy cattle by integration of Pharmacokinetics/Pharmacodynamics modeling of thymoquinone
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
In the recent decades, the need of new anti-infective agents because of the emergence of multiple antibiotic resistances has led to the search of new sources of potential antimicrobials. Thymoquinone  (2-isopropyl-5-methylbenzo-1, 4-quinone)(TQ),  the most abundant constituent of the volatile oil also present the fixed oil, is the biologically active compound of Nigella Sativa (NS) seeds. The anti-bacterial activity of TQ was reported against many gram positive and gram negative bacterial strains. 
Despite of significant contribution to the burden of infectious disease, the translation of new treatment strategies for mastitis in animals remain challenging for the researchers. Mastitis is mostly caused by Staph.aureus and TQ showed good results against this bacteria in recent researches. Pharmacokinetics/Pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) principles are important tool to study the application of an antibacterial agent. Due to the difficulty in determining the free drug concentration at the target site, the PK data in most previous PK-PD studies have often been obtained from plasma. It has been shown that the antibiotic concentration time-course in plasma is significantly different from that in bio-phase at the infection site, including the interstitial fluid (ISF) and epithelial lining fluid. The rationale of this project is to determine the active concentration of free TQ at target site such as milk present in udder using PK-PD modeling to achieve a rational dosage regimen. Our study will help to avoid the use of synthetic antibacterial drugs causing resistance and drug residues problem and hence will provide good therapeutics strategies .

data.projectName: Multi Hazard Vulnerability Risk Assessment for KPK Districts
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is facing challenges of many disasters which include earthquakes, floods and landslides. All these disasters affected country’s economy by impacting its population, built-up, agriculture, and forest. The districts of Abbottabad, Mansehra and Koshistan lie in mountainous range which face continuous disasters. According to PDMA, the houses damaged for District Kohistan, Mansehra and Abbottabad were 2000, 695 and 515 and deaths were 44, 5, and 12 and injured were 6, 10, and 1 respectively in year 2016. The country has faced severe increase in floods during last twenty years which is ranked 10th according to CRI. Different reports are prepared for disaster related incidence, but actual hazard and risk assessment was not accomplished for these districts. MHVRA provides models and tools to evaluate past damages and forecast future damages. MHVRA will provide actual assessment on past damages occurred in these districts. The impact of disasters is particularly high for these districts due to their insufficient capacities.  The role of five institutions is crucial during any disaster at district level. These institutions include District Disaster Management Authority, Rescue 1122, Education and Health.The main objectives of this project are to: (i) achieve hazard and risk assessment at union council level for earthquake, flood and landslides; (ii) evaluate institutional capacity qualitatively and quantitatively; and (iii) accomplish multi-hazard vulnerability risk assessment.

data.projectName: Analyzing common factors of admission process for post graduate students; a step towards uniform national admission policy for the universities of Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: In this modern era, universities have a vital role in the development of a country through their teaching and research. Secondly, research and innovation being the leading focus, post graduate students is the fuel of any research lead university; therefore, their admission process should be designed in such a manner that ensures the enrollment of adequate and proficient students with positive attitude towards research. This study will analyze some common factors/characteristics/variables of the applicants, usually considered by different universities of Pakistan (fully or partially) at post graduate level. These factors include previous academic record of the applicant, i.e. the performance of the applicant in sixteen year of education (ACAD); graduate record examinations (general) or graduate assessment test (general) (GAT) (a test conducted by national testing service of Pakistan for Higher Education Commission of Pakistan); and interview of the applicant (INT) conducted by the concerned school/institution/center/university. These factors are somehow in practice and quantified variably by different universities to determine the merit of the applicants. The results of this will provide valuable guidelines to national universities seeking to adopt/regulate their academic procedures/processes to design a uniform national admission policy to attract the best lot of students at post graduate level.

data.projectName: Electrospraying Technique for Enhanced Biopharmaceutical Performance of a Quinone Derivative via Polymeric Nanobeads Formation
data.projectDigest: Treatment of diseases is done using chemicals, known as drugs. Drugs, in the form of medicine (tablet, capsules etc.), are mostly swallowed by the patients. After entering the digestive system, a drug must become dissolved in the digestive juice (which is water-based in nature) as solid drug cannot be absorbed from the digestive system to the circulatory system (blood). Through blood, drug reaches specific receptors-site and stimulates them to initiate the desired clinical effects which relieve the disease. This is called bioavailability. Atovaquone is a versatile drug used in the treatment of Malaria, Leishmaniasis, Babesiosis, PCP pneumonia and Neurotoxoplasmosis. It demonstrates very poor absorption and bioavailability due to limited solubility in the digestive juice; therefore, it is given at high doses (1500 mg) to produce sufficient intensity relieving effects. High dose is not favourable to the patient, both economically and health-wise as some drugs are very expensive and produce awfully obnoxious side effects. This project aims at the development, optimization and characterization (both in-vivo and in-vitro) of a polymeric nanoparticulated drug delivery system via the electrospraying technique which is likely to efficiently enhance solubility and dissolution of Atovaquone in the digestive juice, and thereby improving its absorption and bioavailability.

data.projectName: Proangiogenic hydrogel based on inexpensive silk for fast wound healing
data.projectDigest: Skin is the largest organ of the body which acts as a barrier against external environments. When skin gets wound, usually a dressing is applied which helps in healing by providing optimum conditions to the wound. Moist dressings are more effective to chronic wounds and burns. Wound healing is also depended on the blood vascularization. Good dressing with biocompatibility and proangiogenic properties is very important. Silk Fibroin (SF) is a biocompatible protein-based polymer usually obtained from Bombyx mori or silk worm, which can be converted into different form of materials like gels. Nutrients are very important for regeneration of skin. Vitamins including A, B, C, D, E and K are already reported to have positive effect on wound healing. In this project we proposed that hydrogels of silk loaded with these vitamins will be prepared as wound dressing. Silk cocoons would be obtained from Changa Manga forest which will be used to obtain SF. Cleaned and degenerated SF solution will be loaded with vitamins and converted in to gels. The best gel composition will be identified from the obtained results. The produced gels would have great potential in Pakistan as indigenously produced inexpensive silk would be used. The best products would have potential of commercialization.

data.projectName: Analytical and Molecular Epidemiology to Control Brucellosis in Small Ruminants and High risk Human Population in Punjab, Pakistan
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Brucellosis is an important zoonotic disease caused by gram-negative facultative bacteria genus brucella which comprises many closely related species. The species Brucella abortus (infect cattle and buffalo), Brucella melitensis (infect human, sheep and goat) and Brucella suis (swine) cause significant economic losses in animals due to abortions, premature births, low reproduction rate and reduced milk production.  Brucellosis is an endemic disease of livestock population of developing countries including Pakistan.  Most of the previous studies in Pakistan emphasis the brucellosis due to Brucella abortus in cattle and buffaloes with a minor focus on epidemiology of the disease in sheep and goat populations caused by Brucella melitensis. The current project has been designed to highlight the epidemiology of Brucellosis in sheep and goat populations of Punjab with special reference to Brucella melitensis as a public health problem. In this project the risk factors, molecular characteristics of brucella species and its control programs alternative to test and slaughter policy will be studied in sheep and goats. The seroprevalence, risk factors and KAP survey for brucellosis in high risk human population will also be studied under the concept of "One Health" approach to control the disease.

data.projectName: Integrated nutrient management in Sugarbeet
data.projectDigest: Sugar beet (Beta vulgaris L.) is an herbaceous plant belonging to family Chenopodiaceae. It is the second most important crop next to sugarcane producing annually about 40 percent of sugar production all over the world.  About 30% of world sugar comes from sugar beet and Europe remains at top with regard to sugar beet cultivation as it provides 70% of the world sugar beet production. Pakistan is on 8th number as a sugar producer and consumer.Economic analysis has revealed that sugar beet gives more monetary returns (Rs.9000) on per acre basis than sugarcane and that too in a short span of time. So this crop needs government attention in the wake of emerging water shortages to maintain sugar supplies in future by encouraging its cultivation in Punjab and Sindh provinces, because sugar beet has the potential to give 70 to 90 t ha yield with sucrose contents of 15-20%, sugarcane gives only 10%.sugerm beet is alternative crop for sugarcane due short duration crop (5-6 Months) requiring 8-10 irrigations and giving sucrose content 15-20%.on the other hand sugarcane is long duration crop (13-14 months) requiring 16-20 irrigations and produce only 10% sucrose contents. By the proper nutrient management, production of beet sugar and sucrose content can be increased because Nutrients plays important roles in photosynthesis, protein synthesis, translocation of assimilates as well as increasing plant growth and yield. it will an alternative source and important crop of sugar beet with minimal input.

data.projectName: Virosome based nanocarriers for the targeted drug delivery of chemotherapeutic agents to cancer cells
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Cancer is the major cause of mortality due to the metabolic diseases in all the age groups throughout the world. Overtime, there has not only been an increase in the prevalence of the disease but also the severity and clinical presentation of the associated symptoms. Unfortunately, at the moment there is no success in the development of the protective measures against the diseases. The therapeutic options against the cancer cells are developed on the principle of killing the cancer cells in an undifferentiated manner that depends on the administration of a cytotoxic agent that has to destroy the cells. Virus particles tend to interact with specific cell surface receptors and internalize within the target tissue where they replicate and, on egress, infect other cells. Mimicking the same intelligent system of viral replication, the current project is aimed at developing targeted drug delivery systems composed of biocompatible and biodegradable lipoidal systems bearing the viral spike proteins on their surface and containing the drug molecule within their central lacunae. In order to prevent these viromimetic systems from immune surveillance, bioengineered viral proteins would be developed that can interact with the specific cell surface receptors. These proteins would then be used to biofunctionalize lipid structures and be evaluated for their targeted drug delivery potential both in vitro and in vivo. Characterization studies would be performed to ascertain the immunological, biological and physicochemical properties of the viromimetic systems.

data.projectName: Condensation Induced Water Hammering  Issues in Steam Power Plants
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest:
Direct contact condensation (DCC) of steam within subcooled water is experienced in many industries such as thermal power plant, chemical process industry, food industry, mineral refineries and in nuclear industry. The DCC phenomenon, under certain situations can cause bubble burst that leads to the generation of fast and violent pressure transients. This pressure change dynamics under the influence of steam condensation in subcooled water is often termed as condensation induced water hammering (CIWH). This Phenomena can endanger the integrity of structures leading to a possible failure of pipes, equipment and system in many industrial applications which can even result in personal injury and deaths.
CIWHs are highly stochastic, violent and are also deleterious for the environment especially when take place in nuclear industry. In the past a lot of efforts have been put forth on the avoidance and mitigation guidelines for the CIWH phenomenon. But the underlying physics of CIWH is not fully understood due to the complexity of the phenomenon and hence very limited data is available in the published literature. Thus a reliable prediction of the CIWH is necessary. 
In this project we will establish an experimental setup to collect data related to CIWH process. The project will also include the development of computational model and techniques for the reliable prediction of such abnormal events. The experimental data will help to validate the computational work. At the end of the project we will be able to guide our collaborators to enhance quality, safety and productivity in the industrial setup of Pakistan regarding CIWH.

data.projectName: ENHANCING THE SALT TOLERANCE OF RHODES GRASS (CHLORIS GAYANA) AND SILAGE NUTRITION ENRICHMENT
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest: Livestock is an important sector as it supports more than 8 million rural families and plays a major role in reducing poverty in the country. Major constraints in the development of livestock dairy sector are; nutritionally poor feed, fodder scarcity/shortage period, saline/problematic soils for fodder production and high cost of fodder in the market. This study is designed to provide a highly salt tolerant, low-cost, nutritionally rich fodder with sustainable supply to the poor farmers for cattle. The hypothesis of this study is that seed treatment with Zinc and Silicon can enhance salt tolerance in Rhodes grass (Chloris gayana) and silage nutritional enrichment can enhance its nutritional value resulting low-cost, nutrition rich, sustainable fodder/silage availability. The salt tolerant ability of Rhode grass will be enhanced through seed treatment with zinc and silicon and the silage of Rhodes grass will be treated with different materials like urea, molasses and corn ground grains to enhance its nutritional value. The proposed project will directly benefit the poor cattle farmers by providing highly salt tolerant fodder with sustainable/continuous supply and nutritionally rich low-cost silage. The huge nonproductive saline area will be turned into highly productive area resulting with the increase in  cultivation area.

data.projectName: Studies on evaluation of corn stover as an alternate dry roughages in fattening  bucks
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: During scarcity period, people extensively are using crop residues for ruminants especially in those area which having low crop cultivation. Habib et al. (2016) evaluated bulk of dry mater is being obtained from different crops as their residues which constitutes about 58.8%  and it is followed by fodder production(23.8%), ranges for the grazing (9.2%) of the whole feed supply chain. Among residue wheat straw (Toori) has identified as a key roughage source, however recently a sharp increase in wheat straw have been reported Rs.20-25 /kg in Pakistan. By feeding this price based wheat the cost of mutton production is very high.  Corn stover is by product of maize crop after grains are harvest and is abundantly available in corn growing area such as Districts of Okara, Sahiwal Pakpattan and allied areas. Corn stover is wasted in the field, around the roads after harvesting the corn crop. Corn stover is available in abundant quantity and cheaper available at Rs 2-3 / kg. Corn stover contain crude protein 6.2 that is higher than wheat straw (2.5%).The farmers in corn growing belt can use corn stovers based total mixed ration (ration congaing corn stover and concentrate) can prepare economical feed and thus economical mutton production. Total area under maize cultivation in Punjab is 390,000 hecters. One hecter produces about 50 tonns of maize. 390,000hecters produce 19500 tonns maize sovers. The end user that is livestock farmer can save income by economical feeding to goats for mutton production. In this  research  by efficient using this stover in total mixed ration in goat the amount which can be saved is over Rs.80 million per annum. By using this corn stover in replacement of wheat straw the optimum level of corn stover can be identified as well as by chemical treatment

data.projectName: Nurturing vegetable production industry in Cholistan region by adopting stress management and growth enhancement strategies
data.projectDigest: Vegetables constitute an appreciable share in human diet with provision of almost all essential nutrients which can be appraised through emerging vegetarian diet pattern in developed societies. The production status of quality vegetables in developing countries like Pakistan is very low owing to abiotic factors (salinity, low and high temperature, drought etc.) and lack of proper planting material. Almost all the vegetable varieties growing in an area are not standardized to be grown under the provided climatic conditions and thus result in low and inferior quality produce. There is a dire need of work on abiotic stress prevail in the area and to estimate its effect on vegetable production in order to standardize the procedures for yield enhancement. It will help the vegetable industry by ensuring high-quality sustainable production with enough economic potential. In the proposed study, a series of experiments will be done, wherein, local (tomato, okra, chili, bell pepper, cauliflower, cabbage) and exotic (Asparagus, Brussels sprout, Broccoli, Celery, Kale and knolkhol) vegetables will be evaluated for their tolerance against prevailing environmental adversities. The gap thus identified will be filled by adopting an alternate approach for production enhancement by exogenous application of different growth enhancing chemicals and natural extracts.

data.projectName: MCB-LPR: Mobile Cloud Based License Plate Recognition System
data.projectDigest:
The proposed project is intended to develop a Mobile Cloud Based License Plate Recognition (MCB-LPR) system that will help individuals and even security personnel to identify the suspected vehicles, so that the supplementary actions can be taken to enhance the security. License plate is one of the most exposed parts of any vehicle. Even the developed countries, for example the USA has been affected by an abrupt increase in robbery incidences since 2016 onwards. Studies on the population of various areas in Pakistan including the Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK), and Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA) indicate that vehicle robbery and criminal activities are among the top three situations in these regions. As per the report of the Citizen Police Liaisons Report (CPCL)1, every day at least 500 vehicles are being theft/snatched at various parts of the country. The apex of concern is that during the past ten years, such incidents have increased by 51% in Pakistan1.

data.projectName: Hand gesture-based speech generation for deaf and dumb people
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest:
The Deaf-Dumb peoples have the only method to communicate by using sign language. Sign language is very important for Deaf-Dumb person. Signs required great attention and time to make things clear. Communicating with normal people who cannot comprehend sign language poses a problem not only in their daily lives but also for their employability. Also, common people cannot communicate with the deaf and mutes because they are unaware of sign language and usage of speech also cannot serve the purpose. 
In this project we will try to help deaf and dumb people to communicate in a proper way like all other human beings. We will use pairs of the glove with the combination of some sensors, which sense the hand movement. These movements of hands will then be converted into some specific values. These values will be translated into proper words using machine learning techniques with the help of required dataset. In the end, we generate a voice based on our machine learning results, this voice message can easily understand by normal peoples.

data.projectName: Association of NLRP3 and CARD8 Genetic Polymorphism with Rheumatoid Arthritis in a Sample of Pakistani Population
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disease characterized by irreversible cartilage and bone damage. The prevalence of RA is 1% percent worldwide and approximately 0.5% in Pakistan. The exact cause of RA is not known, however, studies have identified the role of combination of genetic and environmental factors in the pathogenesis of RA. The pro-inflammatory cytokine IL-1? production is dependent on the activation of a cytosolic multiprotein complex known as inflammasome. Nucleotide binding domain and leucine-rich repeat pyrin 3 domain (NLRP3), which is the best characterized inflammasome protein component recognizes damage associated molecular pathogens and results in the secretion of IL-1? and IL-18. The therapeutic inhibition of IL-1? has shown reduction in the clinical signs as well as disease severity in both animal model of RA and RA patients. Genetic mutations in the inflammasome genes such as NLRP3 and CARD8 have been associated with the susceptibility and severity of various inflammatory and autoimmune diseases such as RA in different population groups. Therefore, in the proposed study, we will identify for the first time, the possible association of NLRP3 and CARD8 genetic polymorphism with RA in Pakistani population.

Therefore, in the proposed study, we will identify for the first time, the possible association of NLRP3 and CARD8 genetic polymorphism with RA in Pakistani population.

data.projectName: Machine Learning Models to Investigate Prevalence and Determinants of Unwanted Pregnancies in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
There is an increasing trend of unintended pregnancies in Pakistan.  According to Sathar et al. (2014) this rate increased between 2002 and 2012, rising from 71 to 93 per 1,000 women aged 15–49. In 2012, there were approximately nine million pregnancies in Pakistan, of which 4.2 million were unintended. Of these unintended pregnancies, 54% resulted in induced abortions and 34% in unplanned births. Furthermore, in Pakistan, the abortion law is not clear, and it is legally allowed only to save the life of a woman or to provide “necessary treatment” early in pregnancy.  The consequences of unintended pregnancy and induced abortion result in substantial costs to the country’s health care system, as well as to women and their families. 
This study sought to investigate the prevalence and determinants of unintended pregnancies among women in Pakistan by using machine learning methods namely Support vector machine, Random Forest, Artificial Neural Networks and Logistic Regression. Furthermore, we will use a recursive feature elimination algorithm for feature selection. 
This study will contribute substantially towards the discourse of maternal well-being of women by unveiling the prevalence and determinants of unintended pregnancy in Pakistan. This study will highlight the most important factors that must be focused by the Government of Pakistan and other health-focused departments/organizations that operate in Pakistan. Contributing in the health management system of Pakistan, the findings of this  study will facilitate policy revisions, budget allocation and appropriate decision making by the Government of Pakistan and other health-focused institutions.

data.projectName: Ectomycorrhizal synthesis with indigenous tree species for rehabilitation of forests
data.projectDigest: Over 3% of the total area of Pakistan is covered with forests. The major part of these forests lies in Himalayan region. Deforestation is among the greatest challenges facing this region. An annual deforestation rate is more than 3%. To uplift the economic growth of the country, forest cover should be at least 25%. To overcome this problem, rapid afforestation and reforestation strategies are required. Inoculation of ectomycorrhizal fungi growing efficiently in the Himalayas could be a leading approach in this regard. Several ectomycorrhizal fungi have been reported in association with many coniferous and deciduous tree species growing in Himalayan region.  The success of this association is mainly based upon the mutual exchange of nutrients between the symbionts. These ectomycorrhizal fungi can mitigate the stress conditions and enhance the seedling survival. Inoculation of these fungi with indigenous tree species of this region can greatly improve the plant growth and survival. This symbiosis may play a major role in function, maintenance and evolution of biodiversity and ecosystem stability and productivity.

data.projectName: Integrated Pharmacoinformatics and Machine Learning Protocol for the Activity Profiling of Natural Products in Neurological Disorders
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Despite the availability of ~30 anti-epileptic drugs (AEDs) with diverse molecular targets, there are still many challenges associated with anti-epileptic therapies such as, (1) around one-third of epilepsy patients are still pharmacoresistant, and often show significant adverse effects. (2) People with epilepsy also suffer from co-morbidities such as anxiety, depression, and cognitive impairment. (3)  Many AEDs do not aggravate these co-morbidities. This is due to insufficient understanding of the precise mechanism of epilepsy. This long-term poor control of seizures represents a heavy burden for patients. Therefore, future AEDs development efforts should (1) include deeper insights into the mechanisms of action of AEDs, (2) evaluate potential therapeutic targets for disease modification, and to (3) identify potential therapeutic interventions for the prevention of epilepsy.
In this project novel therapeutic target will be identified by dynamics simulation of knowledge driven biological regulatory networks (BRNs) using hybrid modeling and stochastic petri net simulations. Combined ligand and structure based in-silico strategies will be utilized to identify the key structural features of modulators of identified therapeutic target. Molecular dynamics simulation of selected target-modulators complexes will be followed by structure based similarity search for the identification of potential antiepileptic hits compounds form extracted natural cannabinoid compound. Hit-to-lead and toxicity prediction approaches will be utilized to prioritize hits for biological testing. Overall, work will pave the way for the design of potential anti-epileptic hits with better efficacy and reduced toxicity for the treatment of neurological disorders particularly epilepsy.

data.projectName: Post Swarm Management of Desert Locust Schistocerca gregaria to minimize the crop losses
data.projectDigest: Desert locust, (Schistocerca gregaria) has become a serious threat to crops in the southern parts of Pakistan due to heavy attacks of desert locust last years. They caused considerable losses to farming economy in the affected areas. Their occurrence, presence, and damages could not be pre-assumed due to lack of filed knowledge about this pest. The evaluation of farmers awareness and perception about this notorious pest will be helpful to devise the management policy in coming future by adding to existing IPM plans. The evaluation of different types of soils for egg laying preference and vegetation preferences will facilitate the stockholders to identify the hot spots of desert locust for effective control and monitoring of the pest in affected areas. This will also helpful to advise the farmers for effective vigilance and have non preferred cops or plant vegetations. After the preliminary knowledge, different control options like new chemicals and light traps will helpful to attract and kill the desert locust in an efficient way. The following objectives will be covered in this project 1. Assessment of Farmers Perception and awareness to monitor and manage the infestation of Desert Locust in affected areas. 2. Determination of feeding and egg laying preferences under local vegetation and soil conditions. 3. Determination of relation of meteorological data with Desert Locust infestation 4. Screening of the latest new chemical insecticide formulations for post swarm management of desert locust. 5. Evaluation of different Light Traps to Attract and kill the Desert Locusts. This integrated technique can work synergistically conditioning to achieve promising results and recommendations for better farming system in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Genomic insight of carbapenem and colistin-resistant Enterobacteriaceae in human, poultry and environmental samples - A One Health approach
data.projectDigest:
The emergence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a serious concern worldwide particularly in developing countries like Pakistan. Carbapenem and colistin antibiotics are considering the last resort to treat serious infections caused by multi-drug resistant pathogens. The main drivers are antimicrobial use and abuse in different sectors which lead to the spread of resistant bacteria within and between these sectors and around the globe. Therefore, a new concept “One Health approach” is required to tackle and determine the spread of AMR pathogens in different sources because if we do not tackle the AMR now, 1 person will die every 3 seconds and global income cost >$100 trillion by 2050. 
Therefore, we plan to determine the genetic insight and spread of AMR Enterobacteriaceae in humans, animal and the environment. A total of 1500 (n=500 each) will be collected aseptically from clinical, poultry and environment. The samples will be cultured and on carbapenem and colistin containing chrome agar and confirmed by API 20E and multi-locus sequence typing. The minimum inhibitory concentration of the carbapenem and colistin will also be performed. The whole-genome sequence of the selected bacteria will be done by Nanopore Minion sequencer to determine the SNPs, antimicrobial resistome and virulent genes.

data.projectName: Experimental Investigation of Space Cooling using low quality heat of Ground Water and Phase Change Materials
data.projectDigest:
Energy consumption is a matter of prime importance. Around the globe, nearly 50% of houses rely on traditional costly cooling systems. Energy consumption is linked to carbon dioxide emissions. A large portion of electricity comes from the combustion of fossil fuels like coal, natural gas, and diesel, etc. where carbon dioxide is emitted by their combustion. More than 40% of energy is used in the building sector which creates 24% production of greenhouse gases globally. About 30 billion tons of carbon dioxide is produced in the world annually which results in disastrous effects on the planet, e.g., climate change and ocean acidification, etc., hence, the efficient and low carbon systems are needed.
Usually, conventional mechanical air conditioners are used which create thermal comfort but are energy-intensive and, in turn, damaging the ecological system. Therefore, the use of passive cooling systems has been considered as an alternative. Passive cooling systems have high efficiencies and also exhibit features of eco-friendly systems, and consume less amount of power as compared to their counterparts. The feasibility of these methods depends greatly on the local climate. Further, uncertainties and variances pertaining to their performance among researchers have pushed to non-practice of such techniques even in favorable locations. There are different passive cooling concepts, which are needed to be investigated in Pakistan. The validation of the application of passive cooling will decrease the energy wastage in our country.

data.projectName: Identification of Molecular Determinants of Dental  Anomalies
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Medical University, Islamabad
data.projectDigest:
The present research work will help in identification of genetic causes of dental anomalies. In total 40 families segregating dental anomalies will be recruited from Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences. 3-5 ml Blood will be drawn from all affected and unaffected individuals of the affected families after obtaining informed written consent form. DNA will be extracted from available blood. Different strategies including Sanger sequencing, SNP microarray, whole exome/genome sequencing will be applied to find the genetic causes of the disease.
The present study will be helpful in identification of novel genes for dental anomalies. The study will help the affected families in carrier testing, genetic counseling, prenatal diagnosis, and awareness about the consanguineous marriages. The proposed research will also help the geneticists and clinicians in better management/prevention/treatment of the disease. Dental and/or cranio-orofacial surgeons and clinicians will benefit from databases designed using data obtained from proposed research work. The industrial sectors may also benefit from present study by designing population-specific gene panels, once we identify the most commonly mutated genes in affected families of Pakistani origin.

data.projectName: Genetically engnineered tobacco for improved leaf sugar contents
data.projectDigest:
Green plants serve as a primary source of producing food (glucose) and oxygen on earth. Plants are therefore are the living factories for existence of all life forms. The primary sugars (glucose) are produced in green parts of the plant called chloroplasts. Chloroplasts are pigmented organelles that capture light from sun to start the process of photosynthesis. Photosynthesis is a process whereby green plants combine H2O (from soil) and CO2 (from air) to produce sugars (C6H12O6) and oxygen (O2). This project utilizes this basic process to increase the sugar content in tobacco leaves. 
Sugar content in tobacco is an important quality trait and higher sugar contents are liked in tobacco industry. Unfortunately, tobacco grown in Pakistan has low sugar contents, which is around 10% compared to world tobacco sugar content of 20%. This project is aimed at expression of Chlorophylla,b gene in currently grown tobacco cultivars in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Expression of Chlorophylla,b will not only improve sugar contents, it will also increase leaf size, reduce atmospheric carbon dioxide and increasing the oxygen contents. This project is directed towards product development, a variety with improved sugar contents, which will benefit farmers, producers, and in long run economy through industrial support.

data.projectName: Synthesis and Characterization of Flavonoids Encapsulated Super Molecular Nano carrier System for Cancer Therapy
data.projectDigest: Cancer continues to be the leading cause of mortality worldwide. It is projected that new cases of cancer increase to 70% for the next two decades. Conventional treatment options are bound by multiple constrains. In the light of cancer treatment-associated complications, researchers have shifted their attention towards novel and targeted therapeutic approaches with negligible side effects. Nanoscale drug delivery systems signify a favorable strategy to treat cancer and to overcome the severe side effects of chemotherapy. Here we will address for designing a nanocarrier system to treat cancer with the advantage of least side effects and increasing bioavailability of drug via enhanced permeation and retention (EPR) effect. Therefore, current study is designed to synthesize, characterize and in vitro evaluate the stimuli-sensitive nanocontainer consisting of natural flavonoid (FL) and a standard chemotherapeutic drug (CD). After the successful completion of research, we will be able to publish our data in very good impact factor journals and we will definitely have other new research avenues based on that study. In Pakistan, there is a need to develop cheap, reliable cancer therapeutic regimen for our lower, middle income community where resources and treatment facilities are limited due to significant expensive/ barely affordable treatment.

data.projectName: PELLETED TOTAL MIXED RATIONS TECHNOLOGY IN DAIRY CALVES: EFFECTS ON GROWTH PERFORMANCE, DIGESTIBILITY METABOLIC INDICES,  RUMEN DEVELOPMENT AND ECONOMICS
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Calf rearing is a costly segment of livestock production. To reduce the cost of rearing, calves are encouraged to consume greater quantities of starters. Typically, calves are fed on high grain-based starters feeds resulting in rumen acidosis, clumping of rumen papilla and reduced growth performance. The use of straw sources in the diet of young calves improved rumen health and growth rates in calves. Its inclusion in pre-weaning and post-weaning diets are still unclear. In our recent work, the inclusion of oat straw at 15% in pelleted starter reduced the weaning age and cost of rearing in calves. Wheat straw is abundantly available and is extensively being used by farmers in Pakistan; however, limited information is available on the benefits of using wheat straw in calf diet during pre and post-weaning periods. Additionally, wheat straw is an excellent rumen stabilizer and its limited inclusion after fine grinding may help to mitigate issues related to conventional high grain starters. Therefore, a series of experiments are proposed to evaluate: 1) appropriate inclusion level of wheat straw in pelleted TMR, 2) optimal particle size of wheat straw in pelleted TMR and its long term feeding impact on growth and rumen health.

data.projectName: Design of Efficient Mapping Algorithms for Reconfigurable Multicore Application
data.projectDigest: The major problem of Pakistan e.g. health, education, transportation, security, agriculture, and clean water can be solved using Internet of Things (IoT). These systems can be designed and developed easily but the challenges of data connectivity, security and costly cloud setup creates the deployment issues. The solution of these deployment issues is to adopt the edge computing concept in which the data collection and intensive computation can be performed on the same device. This edge computing era in the IoT has motivated the researchers to design the optimization of machine learning algorithms at various hardware platforms. Current hardware platform e.g. CPU, GPU, FPGA and ASIC have low performance, large power consumption and less flexibility. Network-on-Chip (NoC) provides high performance, low latency and separates the on-chip communication from the computational infrastructure is best suited for mapping the machine learning algorithms on hardware. The aim of the proposed research work is to design and develop the optimized mapping algorithms for embedded and machine learning applications. Moreover, efficient routing algorithms and topologies will also be developed in the hardware to further enhance the performance and reliability of the proposed work.

data.projectName: Recognition, Equality and Wellbeing: A case of Transgender in Karachi, Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
The human rights, as defined in the UNO charter, includes right of liberty, freedom of expression, education and safety; whereby every member country is bound to ensure these rights for all citizens alike. Unfortunately, Transgender community in Pakistan is living wretchedly and mostly they have been observed either begging or engaged in prostitutions or both. The prime motive of this project is to explore how to bring the transgender community into the main stream of society in Pakistan.
The question for social acceptance of transgender personnel shall be put in front of influential and significant professionals of the society such as Educationists, Social Activists, Human Rights Commission, Government, Advocates, Doctors and Religious Scholars among others. To capture their insights, in-depth interviews shall be conducted with transgender personnel to determine the root causes of their delineation from the main stream of society and the barriers that the society and the transgender community face while trying to overcome such issues. Their views and preferences regarding accepting entrepreneurial or any other form of employment to transform them into active members of the mainstream society shall be taken into consideration. The policy implications of this project is that society must and shall be sensitized towards accepting them as essential members of mainstream society so that they play an active role in their own wellbeing in particular as well as for the betterment of the society in general.

data.projectName: Innovative and harmless plant extract based strategy to replace toxic synthetic disinfectants” submitted by Dr. Sammina Mahmood
data.projectDigest: The disinfection process refers to destruction of microorganism whose activity compromises the health care objectives. This can be achieved through physical or chemical means, depending upon the target surface and level of hygiene required.  However, the effectiveness of disinfection process depends on the microorganism, target surface, chances of target surface recontamination, disinfectant used and guidelines for their selection and use. In the disinfection process, germicidal substances participate in chemical reaction with microorganism, whose susceptibility to germicidal component varies greatly. Some microorganisms are inactivated at the lower germicide concentrations and in first contact, while to the other end there may be survivor. The surviving microorganisms preferably select the resistant strains against the germicidal components and overtime, establish resistomes. The development of resistomes enhances the need of multiple disinfectants with higher concentrations.  Most of these disinfectant-detergents are prepared in concentrated solution and often in aerosol form. This fact raising the concerns about human health and environmental safety with the realization that routine disinfection procedures are frequently inadequate and counterproductive, causing severe health problems.  Due to potential health risk posed by chemical agents, alternative surface disinfectants are required. Plants are the natural source of Phytochemicals which showed therapeutic and antimicrobial properties. The objective of this study is to investigate the micobicidal properties of Garlic, moringa and neem plants extracts and develop plant based disinfectants in order to reduce the toxic effect of synthetic disinfectants on environmental and human health.

data.projectName: Research on Visible light Active TiO2: Band Structure tuning, synthesis and Photoelectrochemical Properties
data.piUniversity: Kohat University of Science and Technology, Kohat
data.projectDigest: Solar fuel catalysis is one of the promising fields of photocatalysis which has taken considerable attentions from researchers during past several decades. In this process, the efficiency of a photocatalyst depends on three main factors. 1) Absorption of the solar energy photons generating electron-hole pairs, 2) Interfacial charge transfer of the generated carriers to the reactive sites, and 3) utilization of the photoexcited carriers in the oxidation/reduction process leading to the breaking of chemical bonds. The physical and chemical properties of TiO2 make it an appropriate material for being used in the solar fuel catalysis. However, the wide band gap of TiO2 restrains the multi-functional applications of TiO2 due to its intrinsic absorption spectrum. TiO2 only absorbs UV light of the solar spectrum and deprives itself from the major portion of the solar energy in the form of visible light. The wide-range functionalities of TiO2 can be activated by tailoring its band gap and make it capable to harvest the solar energy efficiently.

data.projectName: Development of environmentally friendly cellulose based bioplastic
data.projectDigest:
For packaging we usually use glass, polymers, paper, board and number of petrochemical materials. Degradation of packaging material and its shelf life are important concern for our environment . There are number of disadvantages of currently available plastic petrochemical based plastic bags such as, it plays a vital contribution towards the decrement of oil and gas recourses which in turns enhance the prices of petrochemical products. Secondly it is effecting our environment due to incineration and cause smog generation which leads to global warming. Thirdly, it is a major risk towards consumer toxicity as it is transferred to edible materials .  
There are certain limitations associated with bioplastics as well such as they are thermally not as stable as polyethylene plastic and their low melt strength with high moisture retention and porosity for oxygen permeability. Number of research has done on it with bit modification we improve their properties for better such as tensile strength and elongation to break can be varried by making composites.  
To cater all such issues and concerns we are planning to make such a composite of various natural resources of hemicelluloses with PLA (poly lactic acid) which is reported bioplastic material for packaging but possess certain limitations as well.

data.projectName: BIO-DYNAMICS OF CAMEL MILK DERIVED ENCAPSULATED PROBIOTICS UNDER SIMULATED GASTROINTESTINAL AND TECHNOLOGICAL CONDITIONS IN FOOD MATRICES
data.projectDigest: The demand for probiotics fortified foods is increasing across the world due to awareness about their benefits, and willingness of consumers to purchase premium products. However The viability and stability of probiotics is  both a marketing and technological challenge for industrial producers. Microencapsulation technology provides protection to  sensitive compound  and release the contents at target  site and appropriate time by using different release mechanisms. This technology has a wide application in different fields  including food agriculture pharmaceutical, etc.  However, in  Pakistan  this technology is still on the lab scale experiment. Keeping in view, the importance of probiotics and encapsulation technology ,the present project has been mutually designed by   industrial and academic collaborator to prolong the viability and stability of probiotics under technological conditions. Briefly, camel milk derived isolates will be encapsulated by using economical wall materials by encapsulator and later  free and encapsulated isolates will be evaluated for bioactive, technological, properties under simulated conditions to assess the viability and stability. The viability and stability will also be assessed under simulated gastrointestinal conditions and in dairy and non-dairy products. The adaptation of this technology will enhance the export value added products particularly to European and Asia Pacific  countries

post layout simulations and technological design rule checks.

Therefore, in the next step of proposed research, efficient reversible architectures of few algorithms shall be investigated along with their implementation using the standard cell library developed in the first step. Fourier transforms, channel decoders, video codecs and neural networks are few candidates that can be considered, as their classical implementations suffer from sever power consumption and complexity. data.projectName: Molecular association between reproductive hormones and H. contortus in goats
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan, goats are primarily raised for mutton. We have more than 30 breeds scattered across the country and the meat demands raise particularly during festive seasons. As per statistics of the economic survey of Pakistan, the increase in goat population has not been significant in the last three years i.e. [(2016-17, 72.2 Million), (2017-18, 74.1M), (2018-19, 76.1M)]. Goat have seasonal reproductive behavior with a sexual rest of 3-6 months. In Pakistan, goats show a seasonal reproductive pattern and mostly breed from September to November. The reproductive status of goats is underprivileged due the absence of reproductive hormones in the blood. Hormones related to reproduction are chemical substance synthesized and secreted by endocrine gland. Hormones regulate the functional activity of the target organ like ovary and pituitary. Reproductive hormones are directly in the access of blood suckling parasite like (Haemonchus contortus). Deficiency of hormones in the blood of animals will ultimately affect puberty of young animals as well as the cyclicity of older animals. This study is designed to determine the association between variations induced by H. contortus and genetic input of (FSH, LH, Estrogen and Progesterone) during high and low infestations. In this regard the market demand of mutton and milk throughout the year is possible.

data.projectName: APPLICATION OF SNP BASED MULTIPLEX SYSTEM FOR PREDICTION OF PHENOTYPE IN PAKISTANI POPULATION
data.projectDigest: One of the  emerging field of forensic biology is forensic DNA phenotyping (FDP) which has revolutionalized remarkably in the recent years. Based on the genotype of individual, externally visible characters can be predicted through single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). These SNPs are selected on the basis of their strong association  with such genes which code for specific phenotypic characters, having reported examples of skin, hair and eye color. DNA phenotyping is particularly important when evidences and unknown materials of forensic importance found at crime scene fail to produce criminal hit from database; the only possible option available to solve such cold cases is to analyze the phenotype of sample from DNA. Previously, an assay to predict eye color known as IrisPlex, predicted blue and brown eye color in different populations with high accuracy. The main aim of this project is to assess SNPs associated with phenotype in Pakistani population. For this purpose, we have augmented IrisPlex with some additional SNPs and will develop optimized and validated SNP multiplex assay including 30 SNPs, which would help to predict eye and skin color of forensic samples in Pakistani population based on SNP genotyping. The SNP multiplex assay development utilizes equipment and supplies  which are part of forensic laboratories. It is cost effective and in future it can be used for identification of novel SNPs by making use of genomic DNA efficiently. The SNP multiplex assay would be cost effective, robust, efficient and would help in investigations for identifications of missing persons, unknown perpetrators and deceased individuals through highly degraded samples, especially in the case of mass disasters, which are not recognized through conventional DNA profiling methods.

data.projectName: Role of ZnO nanoparticles in nutrition enhancement and salt stress mitigation in potentially high yielding modern wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) cultivars
data.projectDigest: Zinc malnutrition due to cereal based diet is prevalent in developing countries and has adverse impact on human health. Breeders have developed modern wheat cultivars with high grain yield which are low in essential nutrients like zinc. Agronomic biofortification strategy has been practiced to provide crops with adequate zinc through soil and foliar fertilizers. Zn fertilizers mostly in the form of zinc sulphate are used in large quantity however, use of ZnO nanoparticles in subtle amount as exogenous application on cereal crops is cost effective and might be the possible solution of Zn malnutrition. In Indo-Pakistan Zinc deficiency is associated with high soil pH and alkaline soil is a major problem globally covering almost 30% of arable land. Salinity adversely affects the productivity of cereal crops/glycophytes aggravating agribusiness worldwide and along with global climate change and population explosion is a risk for food security. Bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) including Pakistan is used as a staple food in many countries. Its yield has been reduced to significant level due to salinity and per annum expenditure to resolve this hazard globally is 27.3 billion US dollars. In order to curtail all these bearing on food security, nanotechnology especially use of ZnO nanoparticles for the enhancement in nutritional value of modern wheat cultivars under saline condition is the only possible solution.

data.projectName: Turning weeds into nanopesticides for the control of dengue vector (Aedes sp.): Green synthesis of silver nano particles
data.projectDigest: Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral disease that has rapidly spread in in the recent years. The only effective way to control this disease is the control of mosquito responsible for its transmission. Use of synthetic insecticides for this purpose is costly, polluting and a source of developing resistance in the mosquitoes.  Control strategies are needed which are more cost effective and environment friendly. Phytochemical present in various weeds are known to have insecticidal properties but these are less persistent. Silver nano particles also have biocidal potential against insects and microbes. Chemical synthesis of silver nano particles is expensive as well as hazardous. However if phytochemicals present in the weeds are used for synthesis of silver nano particles, the process of synthesis will be environmental friendly and cheap as it will use abundantly available local weeds. The combination of phytochemicals and AgNPs is also expected to produce a synergistic effect of both (phytochemicals and silver nano particles) leading to the development of an effective control arsenal against mosquito larvae.

data.projectName: Development of an Efficient and Sensitive High Resolution Melting Curve Analysis Method for Screening of Carriers and Prenatal Diagnosis of Beta Thalassemia
data.projectDigest: Beta Thalassemia is one of commonest inherited blood disease. On very conservative figures 5-8% Pakistani population has this disease. Every year more than 6000-9000 children born in Pakistan with this dangerous disease. No cure of the disease except the bone marrow transplant which is out of the reach of common man in Pakistan because of it’s a very high cost and other complications. Prevention rather than treatment is best alternative. Screening of the couples(carriers) who can transfer this disease to their offspring and pre-birth (prenatal) diagnosis through Amplification Refractory Mutation System(ARMS-PCR) have been the most important measures for its prevention in Pakistan. But this method becomes less attractive because of its limitations of time consumption and its inability to characterize new changes in DNA. The proposed High Resolution Melting curve(HRM)-PCR is an efficient, innovative and alternative approach identifying mutations. HRM is a rapid method which can be used to characterize the changes in DNA which are not being characterized by conventional ARMS method. The proposed project will help in development of a novel, rapid and sensitive method to diagnose Beta Thalassemia in Pakistan. This approach can also be adapted to diagnose other genetic diseases like hemophilia, breast cancer, and leukemia.

data.projectName: Management of noxious Parthenium Hystrophorus through bioagents transformation into nutrients enriched azolla and rock phosphate blended vermicompost for improving crop growth and soil health
data.projectDigest:
Till date several scientists have produced different types of vermicompost by using only the locally available organic wastes but no one (existed gap) has utilized Parthenium together with nitrogen rich azolla and phosphorus enriched rock phosphate (RP) for vermicompost preparation. Therefore, the current novel project/idea has been designed for the first time with the proposed aims to manage the noxious Parthenium hystrophorus through bioagents transformation into a high quality/nutrients (N&P) enriched azolla and rock phosphate (RP) blended vermicompost and to verify its role on crop productivity and soil health as a possible substitute to chemical fertilizers.
	Initially, through the application of bioagents (earthworms and isolated PGPRs), three types of nutrients (NP) enriched vermicompost will be prepared by blending a known quantity of azolla and RP with parthenium hystrophorus in vermiboxes. Afterwards, in comparison to chemical fertilizers, the efficiency of all the three types will be assessed on the growth and nutrients uptake of wheat & maize crops in a greenhouse experiment. Afterwards, the direct and residual potential of the best one type of vermicompost selected in greenhouse conditions will be further assessed on wheat and maize crop growth and nutrients uptake under field conditions in comparison to chemical fertilizers. 
	After completion, the main deliverable/results of the project for researchers and local farmers will be the transfer of noxious parthenium, azolla (high N content) and indigenous RP (high P content) into a beneficial product/vermicompost that can be used as an alternative to chemical fertilizers for improving crop production, well being of the farmers community, country's economy, producer health and environmental safety.

data.projectName: SafeRail: Railway Obstacle Detection and Warning System using Microwave Long Range Radar
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan Railways (PR) is the backbone for long distance travel and freight transport in Pakistan.  In 2018-19 alone, the passengers catered by PR was 70 Million which was up by 29% from the previous year. Moreover, PR achieved it’s highest ever revenue of Rs 54.6 Billion during 2018-19, a 10.3% increase from the preceding year. Despite these positive indicators, the year 2019 was also marred by over 100 accidents resulting in fatalities, injuries and loss to government and private property. The accidents were caused by derailments, one-on-one collisions, fire incidents, engine failures and collisions with traffic at manned or unmanned railway crossings. 

This research project aims to indigenously develop an obstacle detection and warning system (ODWS) based on microwave radar for Pakistan Railways. In comparison to other ODWS options like visual and thermal cameras,  Light Detection and Ranging (Lidar) and ultrasonic; microwave radar provides the benefits of long range reliable detection in all weather conditions such as rain, fog and dust. Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar technology that can provide accurate obstacle range and velocity information will be adopted. As very limited deployed examples are practically available worldwide, a feasibility study for choosing the frequency among 10, 24 and 77 GHz will be done considering parameters such as range and velocity resolution in addition to the Size-Weight-Power & Cost (SWAP-C) considerations.
data.projectSummary:
Pakistan Railways (PR) is the backbone for long distance travel and freight transport in Pakistan.  In 2018-19 alone, the passengers catered by PR was 70 Million which was up by 29% from the previous year. Moreover, PR achieved it’s highest ever revenue of Rs 54.6 Billion during 2018-19, a 10.3% increase from the preceding year. Despite these positive indicators, the year 2019 was also marred by over 100 accidents resulting in fatalities, injuries and loss to government and private property. The accidents were caused by derailments, one-on-one collisions, fire incidents, engine failures and collisions with traffic at manned or unmanned railway crossings. 

This research project aims to indigenously develop an obstacle detection and warning system (ODWS) based on microwave radar for Pakistan Railways. In comparison to other ODWS options like visual and thermal cameras,  Light Detection and Ranging (Lidar) and ultrasonic; microwave radar provides the benefits of long range reliable detection in all weather conditions such as rain, fog and dust. Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar technology that can provide accurate obstacle range and velocity information will be adopted. As very limited deployed examples are practically available worldwide, a feasibility study for choosing the frequency among 10, 24 and 77 GHz will be done considering parameters such as range and velocity resolution in addition to the Size-Weight-Power & Cost (SWAP-C) considerations.

data.projectName: Understanding the Behaviour toward Tax Evasion and Significance of Policy Design
data.projectDigest: Taxes are evaded by both the self-reporting workers as well as by businessmen, therefore, it is important to study income tax evasion by both separately. For this, we shall complete this study in two parts. In first part we shall conduct an experiment to study the impact of our proposed social punishment strategy against existing monetary fine strategy on tax evasion and workers’ labour decisions. While in second part, we shall analyse the effectiveness of social punishment strategy and performance incentive strategy against the in-practice strategy of monetary fine through an experiment. The effectiveness will be measured based on controlling tax evasion by the businessmen, impact on investment decisions and bribery culture prevailing in such matters. In this way, we expect to suggest alternative strategy to tax authorities that will increase the tax revenue.

data.projectName: Molecular and therapeutic characterization of TET1 and IDH mutations promoting stem cell formation in acute myeloid leukemia
data.projectDigest: The TET family of ?-ketoglutarate (?-KG) dependent dioxygenases sequentially catalyzes oxidation of 5-methylcytosine (5mC) into 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) leading to eventual DNA demethylation. The activity of TET enzymes is known to impede by IDH1/2 mutations, that results in the formation of oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate instead of ?-KG, perturbing 5mC oxidation resulting in carcinogenesis. Since TET /IDH are specific targets in various cancers, it is imperative to explore their role in regulating developmental (Wnt/?-catenin and Hh) pathways and carcinogenesis. Taking AML as the target, this project designs a comprehensive approach to explore the functions of TET/IDH genes in regulatory mechanism in tumorigenesis. The mechanisms effecting hematopoietic differentiation to produce a shared pro-leukemogenic impact will be explored utilizing genome-wide differential molecular (mutations) and epigenetic signatures (5mC & 5hm, methylation at H3K4, K9, K27, acetylation at H3K9, K3K14 and H3K27, and MDB, HDAC & Sin3 association) and their functional relevance with AML therapeutics. Tissue culture models will be used to investigate TET/IDH roles in Wnt/?-catenin and Hh signaling using GANT61 (Gli inhibitor) and sFRPs or WIF (Wnt inhibitor). This study will help understanding the true identity of TET1, and may also provide a novel target for speedy diagnosis and effective treatment of AML.
