data.projectName: Design and Development of co-braided/filament wound textile structures for composite electric/utility poles for Pakistani environmental conditions
data.projectDigest:
The power energy demand is increasing day by day globally. Electrical power distribution is done by overhead wires. To support overhead wires, poles are necessary. In Pakistan, currently, concrete or steel electric poles are being used for power distribution. These electric poles pose different problems due to their electrical conductivity, their low bending stiffness, more weight, low service life etc. Unfortunate incidents occur due to these shortcomings of conventional poles. Pakistani environment is well known for its diversity. The temperature ranges from -25?C to 50 ?C. Also the humidity conditions vary from dry to humid conditions. Moreover, Pakistani wind storm is strong enough to uproot and bend the poles. Electric poles are necessary for power distribution in all environmental conditions. Hence they should have properties which can withstand against these harsh conditions. The solution lies in the installation of light weight, non-conductive and stronger modular electric poles made of textile polymer composites. 
In this project the idea is to develop electric poles of hybrid polymer composites which can be used in Pakistani climate conditions providing the solution of above mentioned problems.

data.projectName: INVESTIGATION OF WATER, ENERGY AND FOOD NEXUS IN NORTHERN PAKISTAN; SIGNIFICANCES FOR 2030 SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT AGENDA
data.projectDigest: This project aims to study water, energy (WEF), and food nexus in northern Pakistan with a view of future implications for 2030 sustainable development (SD) agenda. Understanding the complex interactions between water, energy, and food security is essential for achieving the SD goals (SDGs). WEF are vital components of global SD in response to UN SDGs. The 2030 SDGs targets, focused the world's attention on water, energy and food security, it is essential to determine the sustainability of the relationship between the WEF nexus, to focus on geographical, economic, social,  and political areas that form the basis of decision-making. This project is designed with the overall objectives to use small and large scale field observations, AQAL framework, and to quantify the impacts of rapid geographical, economic, social, and political changes and climate variability on water/ energy consumption, and food production. A qualitative and quantitative survey will be conducted in the twelve selected different socio-economic zone of northern with the various data collection methods, including in-depth interview (ID) with 2000 randomly selected individuals and 50 group discussions (GD) sessions. The WEF nexus assessment could utilize for policy measures, planning, and institutional interventions, and various SDGs in the context of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Design, implementation and control of bidirectional power converter for a hybrid solar system
data.projectDigest:
This project mainly focuses on the development of a modern and advanced hybrid DC/AC converter for a solar system. Hybrid solar system generates electricity from solar Photo Voltaic (PV) modules along with other energy sources such as fuel cell, wind, batteries and many others. In this project the electrical grid and dc batteries will be employed as other energy sources.  The advanced hybrid converter will be capable of providing uninterruptible supply to the load and/or grid, based on the load demand and prioritized inputs. Thus the converter will have three inputs: solar, grid & batteries; and three outputs: load, batteries and the grid. If the generation from the solar becomes greater than the load demand, the generation from solar will be fed back to the grid. The priority of the inputs is as follow:  
All three sources available: load supplied by the solar
No solar but grid and batteries present: load supplied by the grid
No solar and grid but batteries present: load supplied by the batteries
If generation by the PV module is greater than load
PV generation greater than the load: supplied to the load + battery charging
PV generation greater than the load and batteries already charged: supplying load and the electrical grid.

data.projectName: Synthesis and anti-tuberculosis activity of lipophilic isoniazid derivatives
data.piUniversity: University of Malakand, Chakdara, Dir, Malakand
data.projectDigest:
Tuberculosis (TB) is an infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which is among the leading causes of death worldwide. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), one-third of the human population is infected by M. tuberculosis and around two million people die from TB every year. The emergence of AIDS and decline of social pattern have contributed to the resurgence of the disease in developed countries, while in developing countries, where the disease has always been endemic, it is becoming more severe. If left untreated or not treated appropriately, TB can be fatal, and it is claimed that TB causes more adult deaths worldwide than any other infections. The emergence of resistant strains has been affecting the efficiency of available drugs and there is an urgent need to develop new anti-TB drugs. In the last 50 years, only a few drugs have been approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to treat TB, reflecting the inherent difficulties in discovery and clinical testing of new agents [1, 2].
Isoniazid (INH, 1, Fig.1) is used in combination with other antibacterial agents to treat active TB. Indeed, because of its high activity towards M. tuberculosis and its relatively cheap cost, it is recommended that isoniazid be used in the initial phase and continuation phase of TB treatment, unless a specific contraindication or bacterial resistance is suspected [2].

data.projectName: Floods effect on soil microbial population and possible strategies to recover soil quality Post flooding
data.projectDigest: Climate change is predicted to increase flood events in some regions of the world that affect soil structure, fertility, soil quality, reducing nutrient availability and alters microbial biomass shift and composition. The loss in soil fertility and soil quality must be replenished to increase production and brings food security for ever-increasing human population. Advances in agriculture production by using available natural resources like animal and plant residues to protect soil health and sustainability is desirable for future sustainability. However, the decomposition and release of nutrients from organic manure is low. As SOM serves as a source of food for soil microbes, therefore addition of effective microorganisms along with manure will enhances manure decomposition. The objectives of this study will be 1) to determine microbial composition and its shift, population and microbial biomass in response to flood affected soil 2) To quantify the enzymes activities during and after flooding, 3) to determine the storability and decomposition rate of soil organic carbon 4) to quantify plant available nitrogen and 5) to develop possible mechanisms for minimizing the flood effects on nitrogen losses and restoration of soil fertility.

data.projectName: Fungal diversity and its implications to enrich Fungarium in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Fungi are a group of eukaryotic organisms playing several critical roles in our ecosystem. The proposed project is confined to document unexplored rich diversity of fungi in resource-based areas of Himalayas specifically and Pakistan generally. This will be accomplished by the collection of fungi from the selected sampling sites of Himalayas, their correct identification using classical and applied approaches. The nutritional values of the wild fungal taxa will be determined to find the economically important edible fungi. The identified fungal specimens will be used to enrich the Fungarium in Pakistan which will provide services for researchers, mycologists and botanists at national and international level. The identified fungal taxa will be digitized to make them available for researchers working in other parts of the country particularly and world generally. According to our knowledge, this will be the first initiative towards the exploration of fungal diversity in Himalayas with special emphasis to establish Fungarium in Pakistan. Moreover, no previous attempts have been made to digitize the fungi of Pakistan and to determine their nutritional values in Pakistan. The results obtained from this study will be used to document mycoflora of Himalayan region of Pakistan and preparation of pictorial guide and fungal atlas.

data.projectName: A Treatise on Terms of Islamic Sciences
data.projectDigest: All branches of knowledge have their own specific terms to express the precise meaning in some particular sense, e.g. atom in Physics, bond in Chemistry and so on. Likewise, Islamic Sciences have their own terminology. It is needed for a reader to have clarity about the terms used in these sciences. The Western people have not confined themselves only to the fields of pure Sciences and Social Sciences, but religion has become a field of their research. For this purpose, they have translated the Islamic literature in to their own languages, they tried to provide the equivalents to convey the explicit meaning of the Islamic terms. A researcher, even a common student of Islamic Sciences cannot deny the importance of Western sources of Islamic Knowledge. For this purpose, the Western scholars endeavored to give the glossary of the terms used in their monographs. Thomas Patrick Hughes, in 1885, has built up his “Dictionary of Islam” in elaboration to these term. But, he has mentioned his limitations in the preface. Moreover, too much time has passed, adding more to the field. So, it is needed to give clear glance regarding the terminology of Islamic Sciences. This compendium would fill this gap.

data.projectName: Corrosion behavior of Nickel Alloys in Ultra-Supercritical Water Environment
data.projectDigest: New challenges in the 21st century require the delivery of ample and economical electricity while considering environmental values to cope with the necessities of a growing population. As an application of advanced generation technologies, high-performance power generating units demands elevated working medium parameters. Supercritical water (SCW) power plants have emerged as a solution to meet high-efficiency targets while taking into account environmental concerns. Material technology has been a significant challenge in constructing both SCW conventional power plants and nuclear power plants. The development of high-temperature materials that can withstand high stresses is a leading qualifying technology for this advancement. Metallic materials are exposed to severe environments above the critical point of water that leads to corrosion, stress corrosion cracking (SCC) and corrosion fatigue (CF). For the usage of such materials in steam and SCW environments, structural materials must demonstrate high performance in terms of creep strength, weldability, and resistance to corrosion, CF, and SCC. Nickel-based alloys are known for their high temperature resistance and compatibility with high-temperature applications. However, their corrosion, SCC and CF properties are still needed to be evaluated in a high-temperature environment.  A series of experiments should be conducted to evaluate the suitability of candidate materials to be used as structural materials in both thermal power plants and nuclear power plants.  The output of the experiments will help to evaluate the corrosion properties in a high-temperature environment and the results will help in predicting the behavior anand life expectancy of materials.

data.projectName: Characterization of Laterites of Pakistan for Arsenic Scavenging Potential from Drinking Water
data.projectDigest: Arsenic  contamination in drinking water can have adverse health effects including skin disorders, lung cancer, and cardiovascular diseases. Pakistan has a major arsenic problem, as 50 to 60 million people in the Indus plain of Pakistan use groundwater are at risk with hot spots around Lahore and Hyderabad. Poor and rural communities of Pakistan can not afford expensive treatment systems or bottled water and need an affordable low-tech solution which can be provided by identifying the indigenous low-cost materials and their use in household filter systems. Laterite is a red colored mineral rock/soil which is extensively found in various parts of the country and can be used as a potential adsorbent for As removal from drinking water due to its rich iron and aluminum oxides content. Local deposits of laterite can be a cheaper alternative for arsenic removal from drinking water which makes it economical and feasible. However, the mineral composition of local deposits of laterites needs detailed investigation which has limited their potential use as arsenic adsorbent. For achieving these objectives laterites from different age groups will be sampled depending on their widespread occurrence and exposed places. The mineral characterization, structural configuration and adsorption effectiveness will be evaluated through standard methods.  Initial prototype filter will be designed and tested for various adaptability tests. The detail  characterization of country's laterite will in permit their use in arsenic removing filters. The outcome of this study well set a base for the preparation of low-cost house hold filters using laterite.

data.projectName: Development of biomass-derived carbon as robust electrocatalyst for water splitting
data.projectDigest: With exponential increase in global population and industrialization, the energy demand is growing due to the scarcity of conventional energy sources, i.e. the fossil fuel. Adding to that, the burning of fossil fuel also put environment in danger due to the emission of hazardous greenhouse gases. Thus, there is a dire need to design and develop fuel generating technologies which are renewable, sustainable, low-cost, and environment friendly. One such approach that has got recent attention is the splitting of water to produce hydrogen fuel using electrocatlysts. Hydrogen is a high energy density fuel which can be used in fuel cell to generate electricity and in combustion engines to produce heat. Conventional electrolysis uses expensive noble metals such as platinum (Pt), iridium (Ir), and ruthenium (Ru) as electrolysts. Because of the very high cost of these materials, their application for large-scale water splitting is limited. Therefore, the development of new noble metal-free catalysts as a replacement of Pt and other expansive metals is necessary. In this proposal, biomass-derived carbon will be synthesized and used as electrocatalyst for water splitting. The efficiency of the synthesized material will be enhanced via doping of heteroatom in carbon using simple synthesis procedure.

data.projectName: Synthesis, characterization, and application of silicon and zinc nanoparticles as nano-carrier for stress mitigating bio-molecules: an advanced approach of slow releasing nanofertilizer
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is facing drought and temperature increase due to urbanization, industrilization, and deforestation that is affecting agriculture system. Plants face such stresses that ultimately end up at death of plant resulting low yield. Some ions i.e. Ca, Si etc and organic molecules i.e. proline, carbohydrates, betaine derivatives etc strengthen the plant system to cope such stresses. These stress mitigating agents can be applied in form of consortium as nanofertilizer. Self-healing is a term used for the materials which have the ability to regain their parent properties e.g. shapes & size with or without any external aid. Memory polymers are highly recommended for biomedical applications because of their extraordinary self-healing (tunable) property. Polymers can be classified in two major categories (i) Natural and (ii) Synthetic. Natural polymers are easily available, cheap, non-toxic, and abundant shows attractive self-healing properties. Biopolymers like polysaccharides are a particular class of polymers produced biologically by living organisms extensively used for drug delivery, wound healing and therapeutics also in different biomedical applications as renewable biomaterials/materials purposes exhibits variety of structural and bio-functional characteristics.
The polymers which are self-healing in nature work with the three step procedure i.e. (i) sensing (ii) transporting (iii) Repairing (chemical). The polymers respond to any damage or change in defined geometry transport the required material to repair that physical damage and finally chemical treatment (chemical repair process). The chemical repairing is basically time dependent process. It also depends upon which type of chemical repairing is taking place either polymerization or crosslinking. The polymers are much more responsive in this healing process because polymers have memory and so called shape memory materials or polymers. The responding time of polymer can be adjusted during synthesis or modification of that polymer.

data.projectName: Development and evaluation of cell culture based vaccine against emerging fowl adenovirus type 8b and 11 for poultry breeder flocks
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Fowl Adenoviruses (FAdV) infections are one of the major global diseases of poultry causing huge losses. FAdV-associated list of diseases include Hydropericardium syndrome (HPS) caused by FAdV-4 and inclusion body hepatitis (IBH) is caused by FAdV-2, 8 and 11. 
In spite of vaccination efforts, FAdV disease outbreaks have been recently reported indicating significant economic losses in poultry across Pakistan in last 5 years. The Pakistan poultry industry is having a value of PRK 750 billion annually and we estimated the annual financial loss of about PKR 412.5 Million – 907.5 Million across Pakistan on commercial farms having any where between 30-60% mortality by IBH. 
Currently, major portion of FAdV vaccines are imported with high cost burden on country’s economy, whereas the locally vaccines lack robust vaccine protection and have old manufacturing systems. Poultry industry has access to FAdV-4 vaccines but do not have any vaccine available against FAdV-8 and 11. 
In this project, we aim to establish immortal cell culture based vaccine production system for FAdV8b and 11 vaccine, perform breeder vaccination and broiler challenge studies. We will also introduce an advanced technique of flow cytometry to characterize their cellular immune responses for robust protection against emerging FAdV serotypes across Pakistan.

data.projectName: MANAGEMENT TECHNIQUES FOR MITIGATION OF ANTHROPOGENIC METHANE AND NITROUS OXIDE EMISSIONS FROM RICE FIELDS
data.projectDigest:
The project titled ‘Management techniques for mitigation of anthropogenic methane and nitrous oxide emission from rice fields’ has been devised in order to develop such management techniques that is acceptable to farmers, easy to implement, need less investment, environment friendly, do not result in yield reduction and undisturbed farmer way of life. This project will focus on the lessening of green house gases (GHGs) especially the two gases i.e. methane (CH4) and nitrous oxide (N2O) which emits from the rice crop when it is in flooded condition and drained, respectively. 
Rice is essentially an Asian crop due to the fact that it produces 90 % world rice. It is a source of food for half of the world population. Pakistan is the 11th largest producer and 5th largest exporter in world. It earned foreign exchange of US $ 1.667 billion. Rice being a labor-intensive crop, is playing a pivotal role in rural-economy by providing job opportunities. 
The project will include different experiments based on comparison of traditional flooding practices of rice to different other water saving techniques at different growth stages. It will also focus on comparison of traditional irrigation practice with drainage at different growth stages of rice and its duration. Testing of different new and improved rice varieties and hybrids at multi-locations of the country will also be carried out. The residual effects of different crops on rice productivity and emission of CH4 and N2O will also be determined.
The project in hand is therefore, devised to develop management techniques in order to fulfill and achieve the above goals.

data.projectName: Investigation on pathological factors responsible for fruit drop of kinow in Punjab and its integrated management
data.projectDigest: Citrus is grown all over the world and stands first in area and production among the world’s tree fruits.  In Pakistan, there is a big gap between its average and potential yield. This yield gap is attributed to a number of cultural and environmental factors as well as due to the attack of infectious diseases, caused by different pathogens. Among these problems, excessive fruit drop is a serious problem. Fruits continue to drop at various stages of the fruit growth and development which results in the considerable reduction in yield and affects the profits of the citrus growers adversely. The dropping of fruits in citrus can be attributed to two main causes i.e. physiological and pathological. The Pakistan citrus industry obviously plays a vital role in the economy and social welfare of the country and is the trendsetter in global fresh fruit exports. Proposed research will be helpful to farmers to reduce losses due to fruit drop and yield will be improved which will directly helpful in earning and export will also be increased. Survey will be done to ascertain the losses due to fruit drop. Data will be recorded at different stage i.e. blossom, pea size fruit, unripened and mature fruit. Pathogens will be isolated, identified and purified from the collected samples. Samples will be collected from leaves, twigs and fruits. Isolated pathogens will be tested for the pathogenecity on selected trees at different locations of Punjab. Different fungicides available in market will be tested in lab conditions against isolated fungal pathogens. Fungicides giving best results in lab will be further tested in field conditions. Fungicides giving the best results in field will be integrated with macro micro nutrients and growth regulators in different combinations. Increase in yield

data.projectName: Development of Nano composite phase change materials for thermal energy systems
data.projectDigest:
The demand for sustainable energy from consumers and industry is constantly increasing. The variable demand of energy from end users cause a continuous and unsolved problem, and this demand may change during a day. In this project we are developing novel phase change materials that can store thermal energy when it is surplus and can provide later when required.
It is possible to shift peak load period to the off peak by better energy management system. Economic benefit can be achieved by improving our thermal storage system. Refrigeration companies in Pakistan have also discussed their issue with us to improve performance of their thermal systems. We have discussed this project in detail with KoldKraft Refrigeration (Pvt.) Limited company and they believe that this project has a great potential to solve problem of fluctuation in energy demand. 
Limited research on these materials have been conducted at global and national level. Moreover, these studies are limited to lab scale and not yet applied to industrial applications. The research project is aimed at the development of novel nanoparticle based phase change materials for industrially relevant operating conditions and thermal storage applications.

data.projectName: Identification and Characterization of Genetic and Molecular Elements of Otitis Media (OM) in Pakistani population
data.piUniversity: Government Sadiq College Women University, Bahawalpur
data.projectDigest: Otitis media (OM), is an inflammatory problem of the ear in children of two years with serious health, economic and societal effects on patients. Clinically, OM is characterized by pain, fever, irritability, vomiting and middle-ear effusion, which leads to hearing impairment. If in time treatment of OM is ignored, it can result in delay in speaking, deficiency of reasoning and negative behavior expression. Regardless of lot of research, the actual causes of the disease are not yet fully understood. There have been few studies on the genetic of OM, and causative variants in few genes (A2ML1, and FNDC1) have been found in OM families. Comprehensive review of the literature revealed that as of December 2019, there is only one study reported on FUT2 gene identified as genetic cause of OM (Santos-Cortez et al., 2018), which indicate a gap in our knowledge. To ameliorate this gap, we plan to identify and enroll 100 OM families, perform clinical evaluation, blood samples for DNA extraction, and ear discharges for bacterial culture. DNA will be used for genetic testing of known variants, and to identify new genes. Completion of these studies are expected to improve our understanding of the disease associated factors.

data.projectName: Effect of Asparagus racemosus and Luffa acutangula in the management of female infertility and lactation by targeting the pituitary gland in animal model
data.projectDigest: In the present study, 40 female rats will be divided into five groups (n=8) on the basis of medicinal plant treatment for female infertility and lactation. Group 1 will be the control (CON) group with chow maintance diet and group 2 will be the infertile group (Inft) with saline solution and 20% CCl4 (0.5mL/ Kg b.w intraperitoneally). Group3, 4, 5 will be treated with the Asparagus racemosus, Luffa acutangula and polyherbal formulation (Asparagus racemosus + Luffa acutangula) respectively. Then, 4 female rats from each group will be decapitated and blood sample, pituitary gland, mammary gland, ovary, uterus will be collected for further analysis. Phase II. Remaining female rats will be kept into separate cages with male rats for breeding. After the breeding, female mother rats will be decapitated during feeding and samples will be collected. Phase III. Some female offspring will be decapitated at the age of 3 weeks and all required parts will be collected as described previously. Phase Iv. Remaining offspring will be treated with same treatment as their mother treated. All animals will be decapitated and samples will be collected. Elisa test, immunostaining and histopathology will be performed for the identification of hormone levels, to detect the effect on the pituitary gland and on the reproductive tissue respectively. Similar animal trails will be run parallel to detect the gene expression of pituitary hormone releasing cells in each phase. Statistical analysis will be done by using the SPSS software. This product will be helpful to treat the infertility in less expensive way and the output of the product will be launched by the Ehsan pharma Pakistan.

data.projectName: Biofloc Technology (BFT) Application to Enhance Production during Nursery and Grow-out Culture of  Tilapia and Major Carps
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: With more expansion of biofloc system application around the world, optimizing the conditions for biofloc system is needed for efficient water utilization and for optimal fish growth performance. These efforts are especially needed under conditions of water shortages, protein sources gap and rise in world population. Optimal biofloc conditions guarantee more aquaculture intensification, best profiteering of land, water and utilization of feed recourses with no adverse effect on the environment. Microbial floc meal is an economical and sustainable ingredient that could support the aquaculture developing sector. Floc meal precipitated from biofloc system tanks considered as an unconventional ingredient to replace fish meal and other protein sources in fish or shrimp diets. Carbon sources supplementation are the backbone for initiating the biofloc system, where affording Carbone: Nitrogen ratio (C: N ratio) of (10) guarantee the activation of the heterotrophic bacteria.  The last have the ability to assimilate the nitrogen wastes and recycle it into microbial protein which considered as secondary feed source for species such as tilapia, carp and shrimp. Consequently, water quality and performance of fish culture could be enhanced. Different carbon sources and dietary composition are the main factors that may affect biofloc system integrity and nutritive value of precipitated flocs.

data.projectName: Population genetics  of commercially important crabs of Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
The present study will use commercially important crab species, inhabiting the highly heterogeneous environment along the coast of Pakistan, as the model animals to investigate how the adaptive evolution will contribute to the differentiation and hence the speciation of marine populations. By scanning through the mitochondrial  genome using the newly developed population genomic technologies based on mitochondrial DNA sequencing, the genome wide nucleotide polymorphism among the populations will be determined and used, when incorporated together  with the morphologic information, to evaluate the phylogeographical differentiation among the populations and to identify the possible cryptic or subspecies speciation among the lineages. 

	In present investigation we will analyze data from selected mitochondrial sequences. Collections will be done through different localities all along the Pakistan coast. The sequences will be evaluated to determine the genetic diversity, population differentiation and demographic patterns of commercially important crabs. The results will determine the conservation implications, fishery management for crab species inhabiting along coast of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Exploring heat tolerance traits in cotton using Genome Wide Association Studies (GWAS) approach
data.projectDigest: Elevated temperatures in upcoming years are going to be a major dilemma to cope with. Being sessile, plants need to adopt such mechanisms which can help them to cope with hostile environmental conditions. Cotton enjoys a significant position as an economically vital crop. Cotton production is threatened due to many biotic and abiotic factors and heat stress is one of them. Although cotton is a summer crop, however elevated temperatures badly effect it at all developmental stages from germination to boll formation. The proposed research is based on the hypothesis that all phenotypic and biochemical traits are controlled by genetic factors and genetic variations are responsible for variability in traits. Genetic variabilities are the key factors behind acquiring resistance to biotic and abiotic environmental conditions. This research proposal is aimed to identify genetic variations in cotton linked to heat stress. Cotton genotypes representing local germplasm of Pakistan will be collected for further analysis. Initial screening for heat tolerance will be carried out after imposing heat stress to identify tolerant and susceptible genotypes based on phenotypic and biochemical assays data. Sequence data of most genotypes is available which will be further analyzed to find SNPs and genome wide association studies to find genetic variations linked with traits associated with heat tolerance. Expression analysis of genes located in vicinity of SNPs associated to heat tolerance traits will be carried out in cotton to find genes involved in heat tolerance. This study will lead to find SNPs associated with heat tolerance traits which can further be utilized in breeding programs and MAS.

data.projectName: Fine-tuning of enhanced production technologies in Berseem (Trifolium alexandrinum L.) under Dera Ismail Khan agro-climatic conditions.
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan's population is expected to climb to 403 million by 2050. Besides increase in demand for cereals to satiate mankind, the demand of milk and its products is also rising. Pakistan is an agricultural country and the share of agriculture in GDP is 21% out of which livestock alone contributes about 12% to GDP. The major constraint in the development of livestock sector in Pakistan is poor availability of nutrients. Green fodders are not available in sufficient quantities especially in extreme hot months (June-July) and during cold seasons (December-January) and most of the animals are under-fed. This gap between nutrient requirement and availability can be minimized through proper fodder research and extension policies in terms of better quality seed, seed rate, improved agronomic practices and improved inputs (fertilizers, water and pesticides).
The proposed research will be focused to engineer high yielding varieties with higher protein content and can  reduce self incompatibility problem through inter-specific crossing  using embryo rescue techniques. Introduction of Apiculture  to reduce self incompatibility effect by cross pollination.

data.projectName: Identification, isolation of bioactive compounds from centipeda               (Asteraceae family) indigenous to Pakistan and determination of their antioxidant, analgesic and anti-inflammatory activities
data.projectDigest: Herbs have been used since ancient times to cure different diseases. Traditional use of herbal medicines is very common all over the world including Pakistan. The largest plant family asteraceae is considered medically very important. Centipeda minima (Asteraceae) is a medicinal plant reputed in China as a remedy for nasopharyngeal carcinoma, antimutagenic activities, to treat sinus infections, antibacterial, to cure snake bite, cytotoxic active toward several tumor cell lines, for the treatments of rhinitis, sinusitis, pain relieving, curing swelling, and cancer . In Pakistan, herbal medicines are used without knowing their phyto chemistry, activity, toxicity, and proper dosage. There are many risks associated with the practice of traditional herbal Chinese medicines. So, there is a dire need of scientific study of herbal medicines. This project will be a scientific landmark in the field of identification, isolation, characterization, bioactivity, toxicity, drug release , sustainability and commercialization of herbal medicines from asteraceae family selected (Pakistani flora) including one Chinese C. minima on purely scientific basis

Centipeda minima (Asteraceae) is a medicinal plant reputed in China as a remedy for nasopharyngeal carcinoma, antimutagenic activities, to treat sinus infections, antibacterial, to cure snake bite, cytotoxic active toward several tumor cell lines, for the treatments of rhinitis, sinusitis, pain relieving, curing swelling, and cancer . In Pakistan, herbal medicines are used without knowing their phyto chemistry, activity, toxicity, and proper dosage. There are many risks associated with the practice of traditional herbal Chinese medicines. So, there is a dire need of scientific study of herbal medicines. This project will be a scientific landmark in the field of identification, isolation, characterization, bioactivity, toxicity, drug release , sustainability and commercialization of herbal medicines from asteraceae family selected (Pakistani flora) including one Chinese C. minima on purely scientific basis

data.projectName: Design and development of Low cost pole changing axial flux permanent magnet machine with slotted configurations for Electric Vehicle applications
data.projectDigest: Energy efficiency and sustainability have become popular research topics in recent years due to fuel price concerns, scarcity of natural resources, and environmental protection. Therefore, to mitigate these issues, it is very important to shift on electric vehicle. The electrification of transportation systems is a major concern in this regard because a large volume of oil is consumed by vehicles. Desirable characteristics of electric machines for electric vehicle include, high power density, high efficiency over a wide speed range, high torque at low speeds for quick starting, high power at high speeds for cruising, high torque and high efficiency at low speeds for driving in urban areas. The main purpose of this project is to develop and design a novel Pole changing Axial Flux Permanent Magnet (AFPM) motor for an Electric Vehicle, which would exhibit these characteristics.

data.projectName: Utilization of struvite and phosphate mobilizing cyanobacteria for phosphorus sufficiency and soil quality enhancement under wheat cultivation
data.projectDigest: Phosphorus (P) is one of the essential nutrients required for higher crop growth and productivity. P limitation for crop plant is one of the major productive constraint in these semi-arid to arid regions. Farming potential of these soils  is further being  curtailed by water scarcity, organic matter depletion and  rapid urbanization. The problem of phosphate fertilization may become serious in coming years because of the fact that manufacture of phosphate fertilizers requires the use of non-renewable resources. The situation is further aggravated by the fact that phosphate is readily fixed in high pH soil. Struvite, a slow release P source from waste water, is getting popularity because of cost effective nature worldwide. Cyanobacteria, naturally occurring phototroph bacteria, are promising eco-friendly biofertilizer in dryland habitat, where they are routinely utilized to enhance plant growth and improve soil fertility. These bacteria have strong intrinsic ability to survive even extreme climatic fluctuation. Despite of their widespread abundance and utilization in agriculture, research reports related to their P mobilization and/or solubilization potential are sparse. With stronger persistence potential in dryland agriculture, additional P solublization and/or mobilization may further enhance their acceptance as widespread bioinoculant for degraded semi-arid and arid regions of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Electrochemical conversion of carbon from Coal in Direct Carbon Fuel Cell
data.projectDigest: Population of the world is increasing so current sources of energy are unable to meet the present energy demand. Conventional sources of energy are depleted with the passage so we must think on alternative/new source of energy. Fuel cell is a device which converts the chemical energy of fuel into electrical energy with zero or low emission of harmful gasses. Fuel cell consists of three components; an electrolyte is sandwich between the anode and cathode.  Fuel cell has zero emission in case of hydrogen fuel because the output is only heat and water. In case of any other fuel it produces only CO2 emission, that’s why fuel cell is considering environmental friendly device. Amongst various types of fuel cells solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) is fuel flexible, very low emission and high efficiency. Recently direct carbon fuel cell (DCFC) has attracted much attention due to high electrical efficiency 80%. Pakistan is rich in coal so availability of carbon fuel is not an issue. The use of carbon is a challenge in fuel cell as it produces CO2 and our focus is to produce electricity using carbon fuel in an efficient way so that CO2 emission can be minimized.

data.projectName: Distribution, Genetic Characterization and risk factors of Astrovirus and Rotavirus in domestic animals of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Astrovirus (AstV) and Rotavirus (RV) are significantly associated with the gastroenteritis world widely. Acute gastroenteritis is the main cause of mortality in human, and large spectrum of domestic and wild animals of all age groups globally particularly in neonates, by manifesting profuse diarrhea and severe dehydration. Domesticated animals are considered as natural sources and one of the most important routes for these viruses that infect humans and other animals through cross species transmission as well as reassortment. Both viruses are characterized by having a long evolutionary history, a remarkably genetically diverse emerging family, interspecies transmission potential and a broad range of host species. Globally, there is a record of a close relationship between animals and human populations. The role of both AstV and RV infections are well established in animals globally, but their prevalence, risk factors and molecular characterization of both AstV and RV has not been firmly investigated in animal in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan till date. This study will provide valuable first insights into the epidemiology and molecular characterization of AstV and RV in domesticated animals. Comparisons will also made between different variable including age, sex, season, area and the relative prevalence of the two viruses across all samples.

data.projectName: Discovering novel enzymes using an innovative deep learning framework
data.piUniversity: National University of Computer and Emerging Sciences, Islamabad
data.projectDigest:
Understanding an enzyme’s function is one of the most crucial problem domains in computational biology. Enzymes are a key component in all organisms as they speed up essential chemical reactions, help in fighting diseases, and are used in various industries including pharmaceutical, food, cosmetic, textile and agriculture. They have wide applications and therefore, the discovery of new enzymatic proteins has high significance in biological research and commercial productivity. Biological (wet lab) experiments to determine an enzyme’s function de novo are time-consuming and resource expensive. In this regard our specific objectives include:
Aim 1. Developing a novel deep learning architecture that can handle the scarce nature of data at the lower levels of a hierarchical classification problem.  
Aim 2. Developing a computational framework that uses the architecture from Aim 1 for classifying an enzyme into its EC number up till the most specific (4th) level.
Aim 3. Experimentally validating the function of novel predicted enzymes using in vitro experiments.

Beyond validating our predictions, our method can serve as a platform for identification of better and cheaper enzymes for commercial activities. According to a recent study in 2016, the global market for industrial enzymes was estimated about $4.2 billion in 2014 and expected to develop at a compound annual growth rate of approximately 7 % over the period from 2015 to 2020 to reach nearly $6.2 billion.

data.projectName: Prospective cohort study to determine the risk of developing Heart Failure in patients with Diastolic Dysfunction and its association with Galectin-3
data.projectDigest:
Heart failure is the final culminating point of cardiovascular diseases which is number one cause of morbidity and mortality word wide. Due to the alarming rise in diabetes, high blood pressure, blood cholesterol levels and sedentary lifestyle, a large portion of the Pakistani population is at risk for developing a kind of heart failure in which the main cardiac deficit is dysfunction in ‘relaxation’ or ‘diastolic ‘phase of heart function.  This diastolic dysfunction is mainly due to the development of excessive fibrosis in the heart. The objective of this project is to investigate two aspects of diastolic dysfunction in our population. First, we will investigate the role of Galectin-3 and Wnt proteins in patients with diastolic dysfunction.  These proteins modulate healing, fibrosis and cardiac remodeling. Secondly, we will look at the rate of hospitalization for heart failure and major cardiac events in these patients at one year follow up.
South Asians demonstrate significant deviation of trends in causes, disease development and progression, compared to Western populations.  Since newer treatment options are on the horizon, it is of value to have data regarding the important players and clinical events in order to inform management of this disease entity in Pakistani population.

data.projectName: Green synthesis of Graphene Oxide/Metal Oxide Nanocomposites for the photocatalytic degradation of pesticides in aqueous media
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is an agricultural country and pesticides are extensively used for different purposes. For example to kill the pests into various crops for increasing the crops production, to kill the insects in houses etc. However, these pesticides are incorporating into the water bodies and contaminate the water very badly. The presence of pesticides in water is hazardous for both flora and fauna. The water contaminated by pesticides is also harmful for human beings and cause various diseases such as skin irritation, coma, cough, vomiting, headache, diarrhea or even death. Therefore, it is necessary to remove the pesticides from wastewater before incorporating in to the water systems. In past, various methods have been tested for the treatment of contaminated water but these methods have some limitations due to which they have not acquired full attention. Recently, researchers developed various methods for the removal of pesticides and among them advance oxidation processes which based on the usage of metal oxides as catalysts for degradation of pesticides. However, the pure metal oxides have the problem of recombination of electrons and holes which affect the activity of catalysts. In the present project, an attempt will be performed to solve this problem by synthesis of graphene oxide/metal oxide Nanocomposites and will be utilized for the photocatalytic degradation of pesticides in aqueous media.

data.projectName: Development of multifunctional fertilizers through bio-coating, beneficial bacteria and micronutrients for sustainable production of biofortified wheat
data.projectDigest: Boron (B) and zinc (Zn) are two most deficient micronutrients effecting crop yield worldwide however, their uniform distribution is problematic. In human, Zn deficiency is ranked fourth, affecting about 66% of the world’s population. Boron supplements are also being used by people in developed countries as it helps to improve memory and bones health. Moreover, nitrogen use efficiency is very low due to its losses which causes several environmental and economic issues. In addition, zinc solubilizing bacteria are used worldwide to improve Zn bioavailability. However, few strains of B-tolerant bacteria have been investigated up till now thus, it is expected that PGPR may not show their full potential in the presence B. Present study aims to develop multifunctional fertilizers through bio-coating, beneficial bacteria and micronutrients for sustainable production of biofortified wheat. For this purpose, microbes will be isolated and screened for B tolerance, Zn solubilization and other characteristics. The bioactivation of B, Zn and coated material will be done by selected strains. The resulted product will be coated on urea. It is assumed that this economically viable and environmentally-friendly fertilizer will be able to enhance B and Zn uptake for the production of biofortified wheat grains.

data.projectName: Development of molecularly imprinted polymer modified magnetic nanoparticles (MIPs) for dye determination aiming to innovate in food and environmental control
data.projectDigest: This project aims to synthesize biomimetic sensors on carbon paste with magnetic nanoparticles modified with molecularly imprinted polymers (magnetic-MIPs) and for selective and sensitive detection of sunset yellow dye in food and environmental samples. The synthesis of the MIP on the surface of magnetic nanoparticles will be performed by the procedures of mini emulsion, polyol, core-shell and co-precipitation. The computer simulation tools will be used for the efficient and selective monomers in order to avoid excessive consumption of time and reagents for each functional monomer. The mag-NIP (magnetic non-imprinted polymer) will also be synthesized in order to perform comparative studies. The materials obtained will be characterized by imaging tools such as (SEM, TEM and AFM), porosity, thermal techniques, affinity and selectivity will also be studied. The materials, which present better characteristics, will be used in the construction of magnetic sensors. Modeling adsorption experiments will be carried out to interpret the dye-polymer interaction. Isothermal models, kinetics and thermodynamic aspect of the adsorption will also be studied. The conditions will be optimized for the corresponding analysis. The sensors obtained will be used for the quantification of dye (sunset yellow) in food and environmental samples. This project intends to demonstrate the real potential of these highly selective nanoporous polymers as new and alternative sensing platforms, which has further advantage such as durability and stability, whenever compared to biosensors of biological systems. Upon completion of this project, it is expected to develop rapid, low cost and alternative analytical system to the existing method for the determination of classical and emerging pollutants (dyes).

data.projectName: SYNTHESIS OF DYE SENSITIZED FLUORESCENT MOLECULES AND THEIR USAGE FOR EFFICIENCY ENHANCEMENT IN ORGANIC THIN FILM SOLAR CELLS
data.projectDigest:
The Sun is a great source of energy. Millions of lives, ripening of fruits, vegetables and other day to day matters of health are very much related with Sun. Country is blessed with all four seasons covering large land from high peak mountains to barren land and natural resources with diverse climatic conditions from extreme cold to hot summers. The very little source of sun energy is utilized efficiently; on contrary global warming, pollution, energy (gasoline, petrol, gases, coal) are the challenges of future to cope.  These natural resources are depleting (declining) and alternate green energy protocols are needed for the development. Another issue is the cost of solar cells as such conventional inorganic semiconducting materials are available in the markets which are beyond the reach of ordinary people due to their high cost. Beside this silicon based technology is expensive, time consuming and beyond the reach of a common people. 
Proposal bring  improvement in the efficiency, cost and reliability of solar cells by using dye sensitized fluorescent molecules. Solar cells are based on the production of exciton (electron-hole pair) in a dye molecule due to incident light. These dye molecules have the ability to donate and accept an electron in a conjugated (double and a single bond) system. Solar cell works on the principle of electronic transition of molecules having an acceptor, donor and a bridge in between them. Such organic molecules have lone of pair like Nitrogen, Oxygen and conjugated double and triple bond which helps in transition and localization of electron cloud in a ring. Fluorescent dyes are also candidate of study which helps in making transition in the solar cells as shown in Figure 1.

data.projectName: Growth and Oxidative Stress Management in Chickpea by Salicylic Acid Priming under Lead Stress.
data.projectDigest:
Lead (Pb) is a well-known heavy metal or pollutant with very obvious harmful effects. It causes substantial harms to soil biota as well as human after entering the food chain by natural and anthropogenic sources, which is matter of great concern to the scientific community. After accumulation in vegetation Pb not only disturbs the plant growth but also poses a serious threat to food safety. 
Scientists have coined various techniques to manage the stress tolerance in plants such as conventional breeding to develop tolerant crops, advanced molecular techniques and expression of genes to which specifically improve the tolerance against abiotic stresses including metals stress. 
This project has been planned to explore the ameliorative role of salicylic acid (SA) seed priming treatment to improve the seed germination and overall plant growth, as SA is an endogenous growth regulator and has very significant role in defense mechanism under stress conditions. So, this project has been built on the hypothesis statement that “Seed priming with SA will be helpful in alleviating the Pb toxicity on seed germination and overall plant growth”

data.projectName: Design of Flexible Fuel Combustion System through Flameless Regime
data.projectDigest:
Conventional high temperature combustion regime is shifting towards low temperature combustion, for utilizing the fossil fuels to meet the increasing energy demand. In MILD type combustion, chemical time scales are increased due to dilution and preheating of reactants by recirculation of exhaust gases. Thus, turbulence interact much strongly with chemical kinetics in slower reactions compared with conventional combustion[5]. It has become a challenge for researches to explore the turbulence chemistry interactions in MILD combustion regime with existing model, such as Standard Eddy dissipation concept (EDC) model. 
This project would clear the benefits of utilizing the flameless combustion in the combustion systems in terms of social and economic gains by removing the risk of pollutant emissions, and cost factors. This project is specific, measurable, achievable, realistic, and time bound. Experimental as well as computational studies are being done successfully to explore the reaction kinetics processes during turbulence chemistry interactions inside the flow field of flameless combustors. Therefore, this project would be done successfully by achieving certain criteria’s. Industrial sectors would achieve emissions standards while increasing the combustion efficiency of combustors as well as would be able to utilize wide range of fuels such as gaseous, biofuels, biomass, and indigenous coal in existing systems. Researchers would get a chance to do computational and experimental studies on clean combustion energy technologies, and combustion models would be developed by proposing the extended models by researchers.

data.projectName: Evaluating the potential of Balochistan marginal virgin lands for chickpea productivity using a Systems Approach
data.piUniversity: Lasbela University of Agriculture, Water and Marine Sciences, Lasbela
data.projectDigest: Chickpea yield production is low at marginal lands in arid environments of Balochistan. The crop model; Decision Support System for Agrotechnology Transfer (DSSAT) can help in appraisal of suitable genotypes and crop cultural measurements in improving the chickpea yield. Regarding to this study the main objectives is to test a diversified chickpea genotypes response to water and NPK by DSSAT model in arid environment of Balochistan province. Proposed study will be conducted at two location (Research Area of Agronomy department, University College of Dera Murad Jamali, Naseerabad Sub-Campus Lasbela University of Agriculture, Water and Marine Sciences Uthal Balochistan) over a period of two conductive growing seasons (May, 2020 to May, 2021). During the growing season demonstration of experimental plot will be done in progressive farming community as well as training will be given to M. Phil and PhD scholar about the model DSSAT. After that recommendation will be given to farmers and police maker. The study will be helpful in depicting to optimize nutrients requirements of different chickpea genotypes with maximum grain yield and water use efficiency.

data.projectName: Evaluation of the Phytochemicals and Leishmanicidal Activity from the Medicinal Plants of Balochistan.
data.piUniversity: Balochistan University of Information Technology, Engineering and Management Sciences,Quetta
data.projectDigest:
Balochistan is a land with rich source of medicinal plants that are yet to be explored on the scientific grounds. These plants have been used for centuries for the treatment of various ailments [1]. Plants are an important source for drug candidates, particularly against parasites, because of their long evolutionary association with the parasites. Over 100 plants globally have been reported to be active against various forms of leishmanial parasites. Infections caused by protozoa of the genus Leishmania are a major worldwide health problem, with high endemicity in developing countries. In the absence of a proper vaccine (due to development of drug resistance and variation in leishmania parasite species), there is an urgent need for effective drugs to replace/supplement those in current use. Therefore, plant kingdom could undoubtedly be a valuable source of new medicinal agents against such type of ailments [2]. The current therapy against leishmaniasis is unsatisfactory. data.projectName: Standard Growth Chart Development for Pediatric Population age (0 - 2 years): An Indigenous Primary Data Based Mix Design Study for Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Growth reference and Growth standards are two different measures. One defines the actual growth and other defines the optimal growth. The growth charts with respect to medical use and as well as in rest of statistical tools had a very rich history of about more than 200 years. The methods of developing started from Quetelet and Galton to WHO. Post WHO multicentre growth standard development a debate is on for utilizing this as it is or to develop one’s own indigenous charts. Many have adopted and many worked for their own. On the basis of literature post WHO 2006 study, it is quite clear that the indigenous growth charts are compulsory. The variation in charts is also due to selection, number of respondents and statistical techniques used.  The estimates given on bases of WHO standard charts for malnutrition may not be accurate so might cause huge economic implications, So it is proposed that the Pakistan’s indigenous standard growth charts specifically under two year age must be developed under immense care based on primary data collection for specific purpose.  the SDG 2.2.1 and SDG 2.2.2 can not be properly assured without indigenous growth charts.

data.projectName: Evaluation of the killing ability of planktonic and biofilm embedded bacteria by synthetic and natural bioactive compounds and study of the possible mechanism
data.projectDigest: Infections caused by pathogenic bacteria are the main cause of human mortality. A number of antibacterial drugs have been introduced into the market to cure the pathogenesis caused by these bacteria, but unfortunately their mismanagement and misuse consequently leads to the development of drugs resistant strains. As a result of bacterial resistance the known antibiotics lost their effectiveness. The situation becomes more critical due to the ability of certain strains to form biofilm on the surface of substratum. Biofilm formation ability further enhances the bacterial resistance to the available antibiotics. Now there is a dire need to introduce such drugs having ability to kill the resistant strains and also to eradicate the bacterial biofilm. In the present research work some of the synthetic and isolated natural compounds will be evaluated for their antibacterial activity against planktonic and biofilm embedded bacteria by measuring the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values, and further investigation of the possible mechanism of action for the bactericidal actions of these molecules.

data.projectName: Economized electrocatalytic hydrogen production through effective noble metal (iridium) utilization
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: A green environment in today’s world of high pace industrialization is a subtle challenge for current generation. To cope with the energy demands of rapidly increasing population, the conventional resources are being extremely utilized. Correspondingly, it results in polluting the environmental matrices with considerable adverse effects on its habitats.  Recent episodes of extreme smog in different cities of Punjab and particularly Lahore have forced the government and policy makers to think about better fuels in order to reduce emissions and restore breathable environment. Ultimately, working has started for introducing better quality fossil fuels within next three years. The proficient energy harvesting from renewables centers on the role of hydrogen in energy sector. Unfortunately, the electrolytic hydrogen production is momentously inhibited by the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) at anode. OER is a complex process involving loss of four electrons at anodic terminal while liberation of an O2 molecule. During this process, required potential is much higher than the standard reaction potential (V= 1.23 volts). Due to this, surplus energy is consumed during electrochemical processes and it also affects the wide effectuation of renewable technologies. Currently, iridium based oxides, especially IrO2, are the only state-of-the-materials that withstand these problems for electrocatalytic hydrogen production. Unfortunately, iridium is very precious; therefore, effective utilization of iridium remains a challenge to be overwhelmed. Successful accomplishment of this project by synthesizing novel iridium based composites, with minimal noble content, will help in countering one of the challenging problem worldwide associated with large scale implication of renewables.

data.projectName: Enhancing Productivity and Resilience of Agriculture System through Agro-Forestry
data.projectDigest:
Climate change predicts increase in temperature and erratic precipitation patterns that will determine productivity of future agriculture system (AS). Such situation calls for an urgent need of identification and implementation of adaptive measures to increase resilience of livelihoods and ecosystems to climate change. Integration of agroforestry is an alternate land use strategy for ecosystem conservation. However, successful future agroforestry practices will depend upon reducing tree-crop competition, which is directly linked to resource use efficiency. 
In this regard, for the first time in Pakistan the project's  goal is the characterization and selection of adaptive genotypes of four multipurpose tree species i.e. Acacia ampliceps, Albizia lebeck, Morus alba and Dalbergia  through intra specific genetic diversity and phenotypic plasticity of physiological and morphological traits especially water use efficiency (WUE; the ratio between biomass accumulated and water transpired). Second goal is to develop model plots of agro-forestry in 4 agro-ecological zones of Punjab and to characterize tree productivity in these Agroforestry farms. Finally third goal is to sensitizing farmers towards the benefits of practicing Agroforestry in the changing climate.

data.projectName: Biosynthesis of thrombolytic agent Urokinase for treatment of cardiovascular diseases.
data.projectDigest: The heart diseases is the greatest issue now a days that is due to the occurrence of thrombus within the vessels and is the main reason for high death rate. Urokinase (EC 3.4.99.26) is a known fibrinolytic enzyme that treats thrombosis by activating the fibrinolytic system that degrades the clot thus there remains no need of surgical removal of thrombi. Furthermore, it is not harmful for human use due to its non-antigenic nature (as it is produced in the human body also). Therefore, aim of the current study is the isolation of urokinase producing microbes using a range of food, soil and marine samples. Urokinase production will be optimized by assessing different physicochemical parameters. Different cheap substrates will be used for its production to make it cost effective. Scale up studies will be carried out to analyze the industrial production potential in 7, 25 and 30 L fermenters. Purification of the enzyme is very vital as it is to be used for human disease treatment. Therefore, complete purification and characterization of enzyme will be carried out in order to make it a feasible candidate as a drug which can be used for human disease treatment. The successful indigenous production of urokinase will result in the provision of this important lifesaving drug at cheaper cost. This will help in boosting country’s economy as it will result in less reliance on the traditional drugs imported from other countries to treat cardiovascular diseases.

data.projectName: Using next generation genomics to discover and characterize novel chromium resistant microbes for the bioremediation of industrial wastewater
data.projectDigest:
Environmental pollution is a major concern of the present era. Owing to industrialization, a large number of pollutants are continuously entering the ecosystem at a very fast rate. Heavy metals are commonly used in a number of engineering and chemical industries and are discharged in effluents. Their deposition in surrounding land, entrance in water bodies and ultimately becoming part of food chains has posed a very serious threat to mankind. Therefore, it is high need of time to treat the industrial effluents for removal of metal ions prior to their discharge. 
Chromium, one of the most toxic heavy metals, has been found in large concentrations in the effluents of Kot Lakhpat industrial area. Various strategies are present to remove heavy metals from industrial effluents. Among these, bioremediation is considered as the best one being cheaper and more efficient as compared to conventional chemical base systems. This project is planned to identify and isolate novel Cr resistant bacterial species from the said Cr rich environment and to characterize the Cr resistance mechanism/s in these bacteria. This may enable us to devise a more efficient bioremediation strategy.  
This study can also lead to development of bioreporters for Cr detection in environmental samples.

data.projectName: MOLECULAR IDENTIFICATION OF ARTHROPOD VECTORS OF PUBLIC HEALTH IMPORTANCE
data.piUniversity: Lahore College for Women University, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Disease vector species arthropods are transported, dispersed, and introduced  international trade, tourism, climate/ecological changes, and may eventually become established in new territories. The introduction of potential disease vector species constitutes a threat to human and animal health. Pakistan has also a very rich fauna of disease vectors, which are actual or potential disease transmitter. A comprehensive information about the arthropod vectors of animal diseases in Pakistan is lacking. Only sporadic information about the species of some families of insects and other arthropods of medical and veterinary importance is available.  Information about the disease causing agents or pathogens is even more scanty, partly due to lack of interest in the biomedical research and partly due to lack of direction and patronage by the government. Disease vectors are a prime group for the application of DNA barcoding (a molecular method of species identification) because of their higher diversity as compared to other arthropod groups. The identi?cation of some species by traditional methods is not easy, especially if when only sub-adults or museum specimens are available and if the bioacoustics data are lacking. The DNA barcoding of disease vectors may be challenging but is extremely worthwhile, as it possibly re?ects several evolutionary processes. There is no institution or organization in Pakistan, which is devoted exclusively or partly, to study the bionomics of vectors and / or pathogens, or which may impart world-class research information about them. In this study, DNA barcode data on the arthropods of medical importance will be generated and documented in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Proteomic Assessment of Redox Imbalance in Schizophrenia
data.projectDigest:
Oxidative stress and its possible modifications is considered as one of the important factors contributing to the pathophysiology and may account for deteriorating course and poor outcome in schizophrenia, a complex, multifactorial psychotic disorder with 1% global prevalence. The introduction of carbonyl groups into amino acid side chains of the protein inactivate several enzymes, often with permanent loss of function leading to the elimination or accumulation of the damaged proteins. 
Proteomics offers a rapid means of identifying oxidatively modified proteins that may involve in the onset/progression of schizophrenia. Present study will utilize several proteomic methods specifically two-dimensional electrophoresis combined with Oxy-blotting for the detection of oxidatively modified proteins in the schizophrenic autopsied brain samples. The study aims to profile/identify and evaluate specific oxidatively modified proteins that may potentially contribute to the pathogenesis of schizophrenia and will help in the diagnosis/prognosis as possible biomarkers for schizophrenia.

data.projectName: National Cyber Threat Databank: Collaborative & Autonomous Threat Collection
data.projectDigest:
In the modern era, Cybersecurity is an emerging field its significance is increasing. The global Cyber Security Market value is expected to reach USD 289.8 billion by 2026, from its current standing at USD 131.3 billion. New Cyber-attacks are being reported daily and new malware is born every four seconds. Firewalls, IDS/IPS and Anti-Virus solutions are being deployed in many organizations and to a large extent, they have proven themselves to be effective. However, the efficacy of common defence solutions are questioned against Zero-day attacks.
Honeypots are used to discover new threats and to analyse the latest hacking strategies. It is trivial to have a National distributed malware collection mechanism for gathering malware, categorization of malware, determining geographic location, the severity of the threat, sending of mitigation advisory and other defence mechanisms. In this proposal, development and deployment of National Cyber Threat Databank (NCTD), a repository of malware, is proposed. Distributed honeypots constituting a Honeynet, shall be designed for the collaborative collection of malware from various geographical locations of Pakistan. We intend to develop both software and hardware-based honeypots that can trap malware. The proposed NCTD will be integrated with the front end-user application (REST API) for Threat Intelligence.

data.projectName: WHAT IS STRESSING DAIRY FARMERS OUT? AN EMPIRICAL STUDY ON THE MENTAL HEALTH OF DAIRY FARMERS IN PAKISTAN
data.projectDigest: Stress is detrimental for the psychological and physiological well-being of humans and considered as bane for the modern existence. Established corporations like Google, IBM arrange trainings and programs for their employees on stress resilience. However, relatively little attention is paid towards the farmer's psychology. Dairy farmers are one of the important segments of Pakistan's agriculture economy. Over 92% of the milk is produced by the small dairy farmers those rear two to five cows on average. In the past studies, stress and fatigue are discovered as major contributors in many fatalities, injuries, illnesses, even suicides among the dairy farmers. This study will attempt to address and highlight the stress causes among dairy farmers. In the first phase of study, stress level of the farmers will be measured in two seasons. In the second phase, stressors (stress causes) will be identified through survey in two seasons. In the third phase, stressors will be classified in the three categories: personal factors, economic factors and environmental factors. In the final phase of research, suggestions and recommendations to eradicate the stressors will be compiled by interviewing policy makers, Punjab livestock and dairy development department, sector experts and psychologists. A comprehensive report will be forwarded to the stakeholders of dairy sector.

Even though human behavior recognition is extremely focused in computer vision abnormal behavior detection is recently attracting more research attention. Indeed, no intelligent computer vision model has been proposed as yet to guarantee alert and prevention before happening of incident. In this project we will be working to develop an intelligent system which is based on the detection of objects, abnormal activity/behaviors and identification of human 7 can be used as prevention system as well . Input Videos will be converted into sequence of frames than these frames are used for the detection of human body and object. An innovative security risk level location framework is proposed dependent on various human physiological factors, like pulse rate, disturbed feelings, outrage, fear, tension, and dread unavoidable danger, which are considered abnormal. The proposed intelligent model can easily be installed anywhere in residential areas, educational institutions,  airports, shopping malls, traffic signals, mosques and deference related organizations.

data.projectName: Higher Education from Knowledge Consumption to Knowledge Production: An In-depth Institutional Analysis of Potential Barriers and Enablers of Optimal Access and Integration of ICTs .
data.projectDigest:
Knowledge management as a matter of administrative and educational policy cannot afford to skip the optimal access, skills to access and institutional arrangements to access Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs). It’s the truism of global research on ICTs that despite heavy investments and plethora of research on technological studies of ICTs the end-user access falls short of optimal academic usage due to digital skill deficiencies and extra-educational usage. Based upon the realization that while technology is technical and access to the technology is a social and psychological matter an interdisciplinary research project has been hereby proposed. 
As such the core objective of this research consists in measuring the level of integration between class room based learning and ICTs and assessment of Digital Skills Optimality of university students and its related barriers to knowledge production in the Higher Education System of Pakistan. The basic goal is to understand the technical, social structural, psychological and organizational barriers preventing a paradigm shift from mere information consumption to knowledge production centric education. The scope of this research consists in consequent adaptation of both knowledge management processes and skill development of faculty and students.

data.projectName: Practical Solid Phase Synthesis of Cyclic Peptides to Combat Multidrug Resistant Bacteria
data.projectDigest: Drug resistance developed by microbes against current antibiotic arsenal, is a serious threat to human health. The pace is alarming in developing world including Pakistan due to overuse and weak regulation for antibiotic use. United Nations has issued multiple alerts and urged member states to do something before it is too late. Where, we need to regulate and restrict the use of antibiotics, we urgently need to equip the arsenal with new drugs. It must be kept in mind that newly discovered molecules should have lower propensity of resistance developed by the microbes. Antimicrobial Peptides (AMPs), as desired, have multiple cellular targets which makes it difficult for microbes to develop resistance against them. Having experience in the area of peptides chemistry, our aim is to find potential synthetic antimicrobial peptides and their development later on. We propose to synthesize a peptide library through mix and split method and screen them against drug resistant bacterial strains prevalent in Pakistan. After their identification, bioactive peptide sequences will be converted into cyclic ones in order to enhance their drug-likeness. Methodology developed PI, which lead to a patent application followed by a start-up company, will be applied for peptide cyclization.

data.projectName: Fusion of AI and Analytical Model for Robot Manipulation to Grasp and Manipulate Objects in Clutter: A Step Toward Industrial Automation
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest: The large workspace, repeatability, great precision and tireless working nature of robot manipulators provide significant advantages over human workers and conventional machines for industrial applications. However, performing a simple task such as grasping, manipulation of object etc. are way more complex for robot manipulator which are very easy for humans. The effective analytical models and learning through artificial intelligence can make robot performance superior over humans in terms of quality control and quickness of the task. The stated research is proposed considering the need of industrial automation and to provide the research opportunities. In this research, different techniques will be proposed to grasp the objects in cluttered environments. These techniques are based on the fusion of impulse-based model and Artificial intelligence. In cluttered environment, it is necessary to perform object singulation for identification and robot grasping. Without singulation of object, it is very hard to identify and impossible to grasp the objects in clutter. Considering the dynamic characteristics of the environment, impulse-model based, impulse-model and artificial intelligence based, and artificial intelligence based techniques will be proposed to singulate and grasp the objects in cluttered environments. The artificial intelligence based technique will be implemented based on the quasi-static manipulation method. The other two techniques will be based on the dynamic manipulation method where a virtual world simulator will be designed by using a physics engine to perform the controlled object singulation. Finally, the proposed techniques will be implemented for automatic packing of different products and detection/separation of detected item form conveyor belt.

data.projectName: SECURE MEDI_QUICK: Authentic Medicine Search nearby patient’s location
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Authenticity and availability of medicines on required time is a crucial problem of patients. Medicines prescribed by practitioners are not according to the supplies managed by drug stores/ pharmacy. Searching for medicines in emergency is frustrating for everyone. In addition to this, purchasing a medicine without its authenticity and considering problems due to counterfeit drugs can effect time, cost and health of a patient. We propose a cloud based system that will integrate multiple pharmaceutical companies, pharmacies and drug stores on a platform that provides the functionality to automate their end-to-end primary and tertiary sales. Multiple pharmacies and drug stores can choose to manage their inventories on the proposed integrated module allowing them to optimize their stock and increase their sales. This will allow end-users (general public) to know the availability of their desired medicines and get easy access to nearby drug stores. Furthermore, we aim to incorporate a decentralized module on block-chain that will serve the purpose of keeping track of the medicines being manufactured and distributed, on its immutable ledger. This will ensure the traceability of each medicine at multiple points of supply chain.
