data.projectName: Application and Impact Assessment of green synthesized silver nanoparticles on growth and yield parameters of Maize (Zea mays L.) germplasm of AJK
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest: Maize (Zea mays L.) is the third most important crop among all cereal grain crops. It is an important plant that is used as human food, livestock and poultry feed and as raw material in industry. Maize cultivation has been threatened due to many reasons such as drought, salinity, wild animals and microbial diseases all over the world. Green synthesis of nanoparticles is the most active area of research since the last decade. Silver nanoparticles (SNPs) are an excellent material having antibacterial, antifungal properties and are used in food and agriculture such as food security, food packaging and pathogen detection. The present project will be carried out to determine the impact of green - synthesized silver nanoparticles on growth parameters of Maize genotypes grown in Pakistan. The green synthesis will be done through leaf powder of medicinally important plants of AJK.  Quantitative formation of silver nanoparticles will be monitored by using UV-visible spectroscopy.  X-ray diffraction analysis (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Transmission electron microscopy (TEM), Electron dispersive spectrometry (EDS), Fourier transmission infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and metal analyzer will be used to characterize the synthesis silver nanoparticles. Field experiments will be conducted in Randomized Complete Block design (RCBD) with three replicates. Maize varieties will be treated with different concentrations of silver nanoparticles by different modes of application. This project will evaluate the overall impact of silver nanoparticles application on the growth and yield parameters of Maize crop. It can pave the way towards Smart Agriculture concept of important crops being investigated and implemented in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Diagnostic Screening of Inborn Errors of Metabolism in Pakistani Children
data.projectDigest: Inherited inborn errors of metabolism (metabolic disorders) constitute a diverse class of genetic diseases caused by impairment in biochemical processes because of defective enzymes or transporters consequent upon which compromised conversion of substrate into the product takes place. These disorders are manifested phenotypically with a wide overlapping spectrum of signs and symptoms that could either be due to accumulation of toxic upstream substrates, insufficient production of downstream products or abnormal alternative substrate metabolism. Biochemical and molecular investigations help in diagnosis of hereditary metabolic disorders and that if early, could improve therapeutic outcome in some cases. The current study will be performed to investigate the spectrum of genetic variants in Pakistani patients with inherited metabolic disorders. A cohort of patients will be enrolled in the study from local hospitals. Genomic DNA samples of these patients will be subjected to whole exome and Sanger sequencing to identify causative variants. The mutation spectra of these disorders will be defined to develop diagnostic assays / screening programs in the local population.

data.projectName: VADOSE ZONE NITRATE TRANSPORT MODEL DEVELOPMENT FOR MULTICROPPED HARIPUR AREA
data.projectDigest:
This project is based upon the excess utilization of fertilizer activities monitoring, evaluation and controls using newer state-of-the-art technologies. The work will start with conventional experimentation in the field on the maize crop and the related data will be collected to be incorporated in the newer models for the calculation of nitrogen surplus in the soils and the assessment of leaching. The experiments will be conducted from the minimum thresholds of fertilizers and irrigation to maximum levels in four different scenarios.
Present study will assess the nitrogen leaching from fields under tube well irrigation system on maize crop as it uses the extensive nitrogen fertilizers. The study will involve field experimentation and simulation of leaching and determination of surplus nitrogen applied in the farms. In the growing season period, the spatial and temporal distribution of soil, water and nitrogen to calibrate and validate the solute transport model. Hydrus 1D, latest software developed for the nitrate transport in the soils using the soil’s physicochemical and the hydrochemical data will simulate the nitrogen leaching in this study for various fertilizer quantities.

data.projectName: asdasasd
data.projectDigest: Medicinal plants play a key role in animal health care. Small ruminates like sheep and goats can be easily attacked by gastrointestinal nematodes, leads to severe economic losses to farmers interms of meat, milk and wool. The study will be conducted to diagnose and evaluate the anthelmintic efficacy of some selected indigenous medicinal plants in district attock mainly and other part of punjab. First-hand information about medicinal plants against these endoparasites will be collected from farmers and some herbalists through the use of a planned questionnaire. District Attock is a semi-arid region. Its biogeography is divided in zones of Kala Chitta mountain range, river Swan, Harro and Indus rivers and plain areas. For identification and preservation of these medicinal plants, random sampling techniques will be used. The extraction will be made and categorized into ethanol; methanol and aqueous extracts from these medicinal plants. These potential phytochemicals will be used in vitro anthelminthic trials against the gastrointestinal endoparasite of sheep and goats. The detailed Investigation will reveal the validity and safety of these selected medicinal plants for controlling of these endoparasites.  This will increase the confidence level of farmers in future. Information about seasonal effects and biogeographic conditions on endoparasites population and on regional flora will provide herbal remedies to develop. The effective medicinal flora against these endoparasites can be planted in other parts of world, also in future.

data.projectName: Enhancement in Dielectric Characteristics of Biodegradable Oil for Distribution Transformers
data.projectDigest: In this research the characteristics of bio-degradable oils will be improved using nano particles for distribution transformers. Various bio-degradable oils like jatropha, rice bran, olive, coconut, mustard, and corn and their hybrid combination will be explored to serve as viable substitutes of mineral oil. Various performance parameters including, dielectric strength, viscosity, moisture content, density, pour point, flash point, thermal aging behavior and acid number will be determined. This research will explore especially the streamer characteristics after addition of nano-particles in bio-degradable oils and their inhibition action on the propagation of streamer. The chemical structure and surface morphology after addition of nano-particles and their uniform dispersion in the base liquid will be characterized. Dissolved gases and partial discharges (PDs) which are considered as the precursor of the arc and are lethal for the insulation’s health will be detected and characterized using non-destructive techniques. PDs don’t cause an immediate breakdown but degrade the insulation internally and hence, monitoring and analyzing the PD activity is essential in order to predict the lifespan of any insulation. The research work also aims at assessing the interaction of different oils under consideration with various transformer’s accessories.

data.projectName: Incidence Patterns of Cutaneous Leishmaniasis in Pakistan: Molecular typing, Detection of Leishmania RNA Virus and Assessment of Resistant Strains.
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
Leishmaniasis is a group of parasitic diseases caused by protozoan parasite of the genus Leishmania. To date, more than 20 species of Leishmania have been reported and cutaneous leishmania (CL) is more widely distributed, with about one-third of cases occurring in each of three epidemiological regions, the Americas the Mediterranean Basin, and the Western Asia, from the Middle East to Central Asia. The increased clinical diversity and the wider global presence of Leishmania species, make the criteria inadequate for species identification. In addition, limited availability of laboratory methods to access prognosis and treatment, the scarce therapeutic options and emergence of drug resistance are further handicaps. 
Current project proposal aims to identify the Leishmania species causing CL in Pakistan, understanding the role of Leishmania RNA virus (LRV) as a possible prognostic factor with testing of antimicrobial resistance. CL is a major and rapidly increasing public health problem among the local Pakistani population, it is anticipated that the species typing and detection of resistant strains will contribute to better understanding of the epidemiology of leishmaniasis in Pakistan and more useful management both at an individual and a community level can be possible in Pakistan to improve health and quality of life.

data.projectName: Development of indigenous rotavirus vaccine candidate based on neonatal rotavirus strains in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Vaccination is one of the most significant advances in public health and global expansion of vaccine coverage saved lives. Unfortunately, Pakistan is lagging behind and continues to face vaccine-preventable diseases resulting in significant and unnecessary costs to individuals and to society including costs associated with visits to health care providers, hospital stays, disability, and deaths. Diarrhea is the leading killer of children less than 5 years of age in the country and approximately half of the reported diarrheal cases are due to rotavirus. Rotavirus is transmitted through oral fecal route and rotavirus burden is high in developing countries like Pakistan because of poor sanitation and unhygienic conditions. Since 2006, two rotavirus vaccines, Rotarix and RotaTeq have been approved and implemented in over 100 countries. Major drawbacks of these vaccines are suboptimal immune response in impoverished settings, risk of intussusceptions in vaccinated infants and reversion to virulent strain. In addition, these vaccines are relatively expensive compared to other vaccines included in expanded program on immunization and thus difficult to maintain their supply chain. Low efficacy of rotavirus vaccines might be due to genetic diversity and antigenic variations among rotavirus strains circulating in the population. Therefore, this project has been designed to explore immunogenic potential of rotavirus local strains. Inactivated rotavirus vaccine will be formulated based on local strain(s) and their immune responses will be evaluated in mice model. This study would provide an effective, safe and economical vaccine candidate for prevention and control of rotavirus infections among children in Pakistan. It would be an initial step towards indigenization of vaccines.

data.projectName: Integrated pest management for fruit fly, mealybug and codling moth in Baltistan region
data.projectDigest: Gilgit-Baltistan is an important region for the existence of Pakistan. Its geography is so much important for trade with China and India. The agriculture sector is the backbone of Pakistan. The economy of Pakistan is also supported by this region by trading different agriculturally important crops such as fruits and vegetables.  Insect pests of Mealybug, fruit fly and codling moth have created huge infestation on agriculturally important crops especially valuable fruit trees of Baltistan. These infestations have been converted into epidemic form in major parts of Baltistan. Chemical control strategies have disrupted the ecosystem of this region and also damaged the economy due to the gradual decrease in the productivity of the important crops. Gilgit-Baltistan region is also important for the economy of Pakistan due the passage of Pak-China corridor for trade. Therefore, the chemical control methods are not enough to control these pests but a combination of different control strategies in the form of IPM, is urgently needed.

data.projectName: School Activity-based Program for Nutrition Awareness (SAPNA)
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
According to National Nutrition Survey of Pakistan 2018 (NNS-2018), twelve million children suffer from stunting, 17.7% children suffer from wasting. Nutrition transition in Pakistan has led to increase prevalence of childhood overweight and obesity. Prevalence of overweight among children under five has almost doubled over seven years, increasing from 5% in 2011 to 9.5% in 2018.Diet plays an important role in children’s health and wellbeing. Forming healthy dietary practices during childhood may prevent mental distress, improve cognitive development and reduce obesity, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, cancer and dental caries in later years. According to UNICEF and FAO, effective school based nutrition education is an important, practical and preventive approach for nutritional problems among children. Therefore, the current study will be using nutrition education as a tool to improve knowledge, attitudes resulting in sustainable dietary and lifestyle behaviors change. The study objectives are:
•	To assess existing nutrition knowledge of primary school children
•	To design and develop effective and contextual nutrition education materials for primary school children
•	To see the impact of formal nutrition education materials on nutrition knowledge of primary school children
The study will collect baseline data about pre-intervention nutrition knowledge and dietary choices of primary school children. Based on the gaps in nutrition knowledge of children, appropriate nutrition education materials will be developed and implemented subsequently. A post-test will be conducted to assess the effectiveness of nutrition education materials.

data.projectName: Over Qualification and its negative repercussions among Public Sector Employees of Pakistan: Would Perceived organizational Politics and justice perception make high deleterious Metamorphosis?
data.projectDigest:
The problem of over qualification is state when an individual possesses more skill, education, or ability than is required by the job. In such scenario potential employees may not have as much leverage in negotiations or flexibility in job choices.   
Over qualification is critical area to examine and understand in the modern economy, where individuals are gaining more and more qualifications to try to stand out from their peers for a select number of jobs.  As global economy emerged from the Great Recession of 2008-2009, jobs became increasingly scarce, and individuals may have chosen to take jobs for which they are overqualified as a means of maintaining employment.  Over qualification will become more severe issue in the near future for organizations to deal with, as the more qualified individuals likely to retain unrealistic beliefs for what they can expect from work. I/O psychology has much to contribute to the research of over qualification as a cognitive state that people hold, regardless of their actual qualifications. data.projectName: Investigating and Developing an Expert System for Diagnosis of Parkinson and Heart Diseases
data.projectDigest: Recently, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning have shown outstanding performance in different applications. However, in the area of health informatics, its applications have not yet been fully investigated. In health informatics or disease diagnosis, there are many problems, that either do not have definitive test for the detection of the disease like Parkinson’s disease (PD) or the tests are too expensive like angiography for heart disease. Hence, there is a need of developing medical diagnostic Expert systems based on machine learning for such problems. In previous studies, few automated systems have been developed for these problems, but they face the problems of low rate of accuracies and not very focus specially in the area of Parkinson’s disease. In this study, we will develop Diagnostic Expert System for PD and heart disease with an aim to facilitate Physicians and patents in this very vital area with high prediction accuracies.

data.projectDigest: Modern Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) are stood up to with the need to change many of the management practices; as they are moving from being merely public service organizations to market-driven organizations. In any case, improving the performance of organizations, particularly the HEIs (universities), requires different qualities that would prompt the accomplishment of the objectives and targets of the management in the fluid and competitive environment. Consequently, HEIs must, adopt promising managerial approaches and practices   in the context of ambidexterity (Ambidextrous HR- system) in order to being aligned in the current competitive scenario  and adaptable to the changing conditions of the higher education to increase their performance. One unresolved issue to individual or firm performance in HRM is to clarify the hidden mechanisms that link the collection of HR practices to measure organizational attractiveness by highlighting particular features of employment experience that are most manifested, valued by and significant to their employees as employer branding  of higher education institutions .Like other organizations, HEIs ought to create and adjust new techniques and being flexible in adopting strategies  to react to the rapid changes in the regulatory environment where they function and to sustain competitive advantage  .

data.projectName: Linguistic Profile of Pakistan: Use and Users of Urdu, Sindhi, Punjabi and Seraiki in Sindh and Punjab
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan had over 70 Languages (ethnologue, 2018). Census data (2007) based on mother tongue only does not reveal, a) the actual use of a language in varied domains; and b) the users of a language (as first/second or additional language).  Hence, this study aims to map the use and users of  four major languages, Urdu, Sindhi, Punjabi, Seraiki in urban and rural areas of Sindh and Punjab, the 2 major provinces of Pakistan to investigate the phenomena of language change, and language maintenance and loss.

A survey questionnaire translated into Urdu, Sindhi, Punjabi, Seraiki,  will be administered by trained teams of researchers to selected households in two urban and two rural districts in each province to study the use and users of these languages  in three different domains, family and friends, education/work settings, and everyday interactions such as buying/selling or service encounters in the public domain. Data will be analyzed using SPSS. 

Study findings will inform language planning and policy in Pakistan including language-in-education policy, and help raise awareness about the value of having a multilingual repertoire that allows flexibility in terms of code selection, code-switching and mixing for improved communication at the local/community, national and global levels.

data.projectName: Funtionalization of biomass derived porous carbon and its composites used as anode materials for lithium-ion batteries
data.projectDigest:
In this modern time, energy is the fundamental need of human beings. Different  ways are adapted for the ever increasing demands of energy storage. In this regard, lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are supposed to be the best forms of energy storage devices. These devices are used in electric vehicles, mobile phones and laptops because of their  high energy density and extended cycles life. Graphite is commonly used as anode  in LIBs due to its low cost, good cycle performance and low electrochemical potential. However, it cannot fulfill the present demand because of its limited theoretical capacity  (372 mAh g-1) and experiences a large volume change. Recently, huge efforts have been made to develop new substitute electrodes for LIBs. Therefore, new substitute anode material is required such as porous carbon, which has a high specific surface area and contains a variety of pore diameters and thus maintains a high specific capacity than graphite anode. In recent years, the production of porous carbons from biomass is 
of great interest in LIBs, due to its facile process and low source cost. Porous carbon can 
be prepared from natural species or agriculture wastes, including rice husks [8], waste 
coffee beans, coconut shells , plant leaves, portobello mushroom  and algae biomass, etc. Among the various agriculture wastes, bagasse is an environmentally friendly renewable agricultural by-product obtained after the crumpling and removal of sugar from sugarcane. The allium-gigantium structure of porous carbon derived from sugarcane bagasse is very important to be used as anode material for LIBs.
Herein, a composite of functionalized porous carbon derived from sugarcane bagasse and transition metal dichalcogenides such as MoS2 or metal oxides to be combined.

data.projectName: NUTRITIONAL STATUS, DIETARY INTAKE AND EATING PRACTICES AMONG YOUTH IN SOUTH PUNJAB: SOCIOECONOMIC DETERMINANTS AND EFFECTS
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan is among those developing countries which is surrounded by multiple socio-economic and governance issues. Pakistan vision 2025 has focused on development of human and social capital along with food security. Motto of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) is to end hunger, achieve food security and improved nutrition, and promote sustainable agriculture. 
It is estimated that half of population of Pakistan experiences malnutrition. Prevalence of stunting (44%) among children aged less than five years is persistent since 1965. In Pakistan, 15% of children under age 5 suffer from acute malnutrition which is the second-highest rate in the region. Similarly, a high percentage of the population is underweight or suffers from micronutrient deficiencies. The scope of this project is to explore the socioeconomic determinants and effects of nutritional status, dietary intake and eating practices among youth in South Punjab (Pakistan). Area of South Punjab is devoid of basic needs such as education, health facilities and food availability, creating serious health issues for its inhabitants.  
While evaluating nutritional status, dietary intake and eating practices, the project will consider all relevant socio-economic factors and their effects on food and pharmaceutical industries in South Punjab. The study will also investigate the role of advertising industry on dietary intake and eating patterns. Moreover, calories based poverty and efficiency score of dietary intake and nutritional status would be calculated. 
The beneficiaries of this project will be general community as it would aware them about consequences of nutritional status. The results of study will also provide guidance to policy makers for achieving a better and more sustainable future for all.

data.projectName: Long Term Effects of  Structured Gait Training In Reducing Physical Disability of Stroke Patients
data.projectDigest: Stroke is high prevalent and most disabling condition affecting majority of adult population in Pakistan. Due to increase prevalence of diabetes, hypertension and sedentary life style, people are at high risk to develop stroke.  The patients with stroke are unable to perform daily activities of life, self-care and occupational performance. In Pakistan majority stroke survivors are adult and only sources of earning in family. Their dependence and limitation to bed bound activities not only limited them but has a huge impact on families. The stroke disability eventually leads to economic and social burden on society due to lack of earning and inability to participate in community.  Multiple traditional methods of gait assessment and training are in placed but lacking in objectivity and context specific customized protocol. The objective oriented gait assessment and customized training is the dire need to improve the gait performance and enable them to move and work independently. The main objective of project is to provide a standardized, objective oriented gait assessment and customized training to improve the overall performance and functional status to become active member of society after stroke.

data.projectName: Development of multi functional non woven for automotive applications
data.projectDigest:
Road traffic accidents are becoming one of the major causes which are not only killing people but also resulting in severe injuries like permanent disability. Because of road accidents around 3700 people lose their lives on daily basis. The statistics shows that around 31% people become the victim of fire during road accidents. Other important issues in automobile are noise and odor which create distraction and discomfort for the passengers. The emergence of new materials and manufacturing techniques in textiles not only provide aesthetics and comfort but also add functionalities to automobile such as flame retardant, sound insulation and odor absorption. To excel in the competitive environment, manufacturing companies are using different expensive materials to meet specific requirements. 
The objective of proposing this project is to develop novel low cost multi-functional activated carbon non-woven web from textile wastes with improved flame retardancy, acoustic insulation and anti-odor characteristics. The outcome of this project will help to improve the passengers safety and comfort in automotive which will ultimately encourage the local textile industry to develop infrastructure, drive the growth of non-wovens industry in Pakistan and save foreign reserves in the long run.

data.projectName: Extending the postharvest life of climacteric fruits using nanaoemulsions
data.projectDigest: Fresh fruits and vegetables are highly perishable due to extremely high moisture content (~80% on weight basis). Therefore, losses at postharvest stage are 30% of total global production. These losses exceed in developing countries due to improper and below par handling and non-mechanized supply chain management. Mango, banana and guava Most in Pakistan also suffer heavy postharvest losses. Recently, research has been focused on low-cost, eco-friendly and easy to use technologies to reduce these losses in fresh fruit and vegetables. Use of nanotechnology such as nanoemulsion have shown the potential to replace packaging and maintaining quality of fresh horticultural produces. Acacia seeds are abundant in Pakistan with no known use. The nutritious edible oil from Acacia seeds could be used to formulate nanoemulsions that can be applied to mango, guava and banana. Therefore, this project aims to use Acacia seed oil-based nanoemulsion to reduce postharvest losses of our prime fruits (mango, guava and banana).

data.projectName: Development and introduction of 3-in-1 small seed drill for mechanized cultivation of sesame, and screening of climate smart high yielding, minerals enriched, branched genotypes of sesame, suitable for broad-line cultivation by modern drill under changi
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: Sesame is edible oilseed crop with great nutritional value and is grown during summer season on an area of about 81 thousand  hectares with production of about 41 thousand tons. Low sesame yield (400-500 kg ha-1) is stagnant in Pakistan since last several years due to low yielding varieties, disease susceptibility, and lack of technological improvement in sesame cultivation. Sesame seed is also a rich source of calcium, iron, zinc, and sesamol protein which can address malnutrition and risk of heart diseases in huge population of Pakistan. During 2016-17, NIAB has released two high yielding, disease resistant varieties of sesame viz. NIAB Sesame-2016 and NIAB Pearl (contributing sesame seed export from Pakistan, around 40-50 million US $ annually). Now we want to introduce mechanized cultivation of new varieties. These varieties possess spreading type plant morphology with long fruiting branches and are suitable for mechanization. Screening of available germplasm (100 genotypes) will also be done to identify genotypes with superior quality (Zn, Fe, & Ca enriched), disease resistance, and climate smart plant architecture. A modern 3-in-I small seed drill will also be designed and introduced for a shift from conventional towards mechanized technology for at least 20% increase in sesame yield.

data.projectName: Archaeological Explorations and Investigations in the Districts of  Mardan and Swabi, Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
The Districts of Mardan and Swabi are important throughout the history of the region, right from the pre-history to our times. In previous investigations, the focus is mainly upon the Buddhist Civilization of Gandhara (3rd Century BCE-5th Century CE), while other aspects of history of the region have been neglected. In this connection, the history of some other dynasties is an ignored area of study in the cultural profile of the region. The preliminary information about other minor dynasties such as Aparacha has been traced from epigraphical sources, however, it has not been investigated in detail from other archaeological sources. This study aims to explore the detailed history of such neglected dynasties collectively from numismatic, architectural and epigraphical sources through systematic investigations. 
This study will focus upon the methods of scientific analysis of the data collected from the archaeological sites surveyed during the field activities in Mardan and Swabi. The study will lead to filling the gaps of the history of the area, while identifying some other minor but  important dynasties ruling in the region between the Mauryans and the Hindu Shahis.

data.projectName: Development of small scale Thermoelectric Generators to Overcome Energy Needs in Rural Areas of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Pakistan has been facing energy crisis for last many years and this crisis is more intense in rural areas. Among many alternatives of electrical energy from National grid, thermoelectric generators are one of the best choices. These generators are maintenance free due to having no moving parts, can generate energy round the years, no dependence on solar spectrum, no hazards for the environment. A thermoelectric generator converts heat directly into DC electrical energy based on Seebeck effect. However the efficiency of thermoelectric materials is still a key challenge to use these devices at a large scale. This project proposes development of high efficiency thermoelectric generators based on superionic semiconductor materials. This project proposes a novel technique to improve the efficiency of superionic semiconductors Cu2Te, Ag2Te, Cu2Se, Ag2Se by doping with Cr, Ga, Sn etc. The dopant type, dopant concentration, synthesis parameters will be optimized to achieve highest possible efficiency. The material with maximum conversion efficiency will be utilized to develop small scale thermoelectric generators. These generators then will be produced at large scale with the help of the local industry. The high efficiency of the generators and production at local level will help to reduce the cost of electrical energy per watt. This project is not only provide alternative and clean energy source in the rural areas, but also help the local industry to involve in the production of modern technology devices.

The best candidate for that is Laser Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy. In which by shining a powerful laser on a material will generate a plasma which on condensation will provide a emission spectrum. By analyzing that spectrum we can get the information regarding the quality and quantity of the elements present in the sample

data.projectName: Investigation of natural based novel poly phenolic molecules for neuroprotective and antidepressant effects in animal models
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Benazir Bhutto University, Sheringal, Dir
data.projectDigest:
Depression is a major public health problem, as they are usually associated with significant functional impairments and health care cost. With the development of society, the pressure of life and work has gradually increased, and the number of patients with depression has increased year by year. Depression seriously endangers people's physical and mental health, reduces the quality of life and even gain suicidal concepts and behaviors.  
Although clinical depression affects a large percentage of the world population, there is still no effective treatment, and most of the patients remain treatment resilient while using the available antidepressant medications, which are commonly in practice with many side effects. Therefore, the treatment of depression has been a big challenge for researchers. 
From the last few years, plant derived natural molecules are gaining more attraction all around the world due to its varied pharmacological potentials and widespread acceptability, so encouraging scientists across the globe to discover and develop natural products as a therapeutic alternative in the treatment of depression.
This study aimed to explore new natural polyphenol based molecules for neuroprotection and antidepressant effects in different stressor-induced depression animal models while using behavioral and biochemical analysis. This project will help in developing new natural based antidepressants molecules offering cost effective and better treatment with no/less side effects as compare to the available antidepressants.

From the last few years, plant derived natural molecules are gaining more attraction all around the world due to its varied pharmacological potentials and widespread acceptability, so encouraging scientists across the globe to discover and develop natural products as a therapeutic alternative in the treatment of depression.
This study aimed to explore new natural polyphenol based molecules for neuroprotection and antidepressant effects in different stressor-induced depression animal models while using behavioral and biochemical analysis. This project will help in developing new natural based antidepressants molecules offering cost effective and better treatment with no/less side effects as compare to the available antidepressants.

data.projectName: A Detailed Survey, Biochemical and Molecular Characterization of Medicinal Mushrooms from different Ecological zones of Azad Jammu and Kashmir Pakistan.
data.piUniversity: University of Kotli Azad Jammu and Kashmir
data.projectDigest:
Wild mushrooms are  important from medicinal and nutritional point of view due to their contribution in health and in daily food worldwide.  Many recent research reports show the medicinal and nutritional importance of mushrooms. These studies reveal that these fungi are important source of nutrients and medicines. Medicinal fungi are used for extraction of different medicinal compounds worldwide. Despite the immense popularity of mushrooms in traditional food and medicines, consumption of these as alternative food and medicines is not studied in detail in the state of AJK. Mushroom identification is mostly carried through folk taxonomy. Many cases of mushroom poisoning arouse in the past due to consumption of some poisonous or rotten mushrooms by the rural because there is no authentic data or list of medicinal mushroom of the area.
 Therefore, it is necessary to structure a checklist/database of macro fungi/mushrooms in ongoing project to retain the information on different medicinal mushroom their identification, characterization and screening of different bioactive components for drug development. 
In the present study survey and collection of mushrooms focusing on medicinal species will be carried out. Identification will be carried through anatomical and molecular study (DNA analysis). Extraction of compounds will be carried for the screening of different bioactive compounds having good biological and anticancer activities. There is no detailed work on mycoflora of State of Jammu and Kashmir/Pakistan. This study may be helpful for the researcher to collect and identify medicinal fungi from wild and may also be helpful to purify bioactive compounds to develop anticancer drugs in future. Over all studies will contribute addition of new records/ to flora of Pakistan

data.projectName: Development and Commercialization of bone Strengthening supplementary diets
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: For the demand of consumers/population for health choice of food having rich contents of bone strengthening micronutrients for curtailing bone related issues, present study is planned to prepared the bone strengthening diets for the school going children, youth, adult and old age segment of the Pakistani population. For the purpose, bone strengthening micronutrients such as vitamin D, calcium and vitamin K3 (menaquinone-7) will be prepared using the agro and agro waste by-products. Menaquinones (MK-7) will be prepared and extracted from the fermentation of soybean with Bacillus subtils (natto).  Moreover, egg shell waste is used as a dietary calcium source. Vitamin D will be extracted from indigenous vitamin D rich foods including animal waste (local fish waste), mushrooms etc. The efficacy of extracted three micro-nutrients will be evaluated through animal modelling studies. The two best treatments will be selected on basis of their bone strengthening behaviour estimated by chemical biomarkers and bone mineral density (BMD) along with their safety parameters in animal studies. On the basis of the findings, micronutrients will be used for the formulations of fortified food products i.e. bakery products, dairy products, meat-based product and fruit juices. The product acceptability, physico-chemicals content along with their storage stability will also be evaluated.

data.projectName: Multidimensional approach to combat Dengue virus and its vector (Aedes aegypti) in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
The proposed project describes applied research with specified goals. Basic aim is to minimize the intensity of the dengue outbreaks in Pakistan through controlling its vector, Aedes aegypti mosquito. The only available solution at current is the extensive use of pesticide. We aim to develop an alternate, more environment friendly approach that could prove toxic towards mosquito larvae and additionally sterilize the female mosquito from dengue virus.
The re-emergence of dengue, chikungunya and Zika arboviruses signals an increasing global danger of vector-borne infectious diseases. The only possible strategy to control these vector borne diseases is to control its vector, Aedes aegyptii mosquito. The underlying rationale for the project is that Mosquito control can be an effective approach that is both preventative and powerful because it blocks the transmission of multiple diseases simultaneously. Every year, millions of Rupees are being spent on pesticides to overcome the dengue outbreaks. 
Aquatic environment is an essential in the life cycle of the mosquito and so, killing mosquito’s larvae in water is more preventative than killing adults which may have transmitted the disease by the time they are killed. Our hypothesis is based on the assumption that the green algae, Chlamydomonas reinhardtii, in aquatic environment could be made toxic to mosquito larvae as they will express chloroplast transgenes that are based on the mosquitocidal proteins of Bacillus thuringiensis (Bti) and double stranded (ds)RNA directed against crucial genes in mosquito and against dengue virus. The proposed approach could be very useful in mosquito control as mosquito larvae when feed on algae, the Bti toxin along with dsRNAs (expressed in algae) will act as mosquiticidal &kill the insect

data.projectName: Atmospheric Water Generators (AWGs) for Alleviation of Social Water Scarcity
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Water scarcity is a serious issue across the world, especially in Pakistan, and more severe in Tharparkar district where the SDGs are fighting for their existence. Many problems of the locals’ daily life roots to the unavailability of water. The water purification means are insufficient since they fail to provide potable water and requires exhaustive maintenance unattended by the granters. Atmospheric Water Generators (AWG) also called air-to-water machines are a potential solution to water related problems. AWGs extract humidity from the air and serve drinkable water to the user after purification and mineral addition.  The research will contribute towards locals’ chronological progress in the education and health sector, simultaneously identifying parameters for better functioning of such machines at geographically severe locations. The research aims to witness an uplift in the social responsibilities of local people, after the installation and development of model which will ensure the maximum output of such machines. Both the social and technical aspects of this applied research are anticipated to receive a good appreciation due to their novelty. Capacity training of the locals involving compulsory participation of women will encourage the accustoming of such advancements.

data.projectName: Response of Brassica species to varying zinc regimes under water deficit conditions
data.projectDigest: According to survey reports, most of the soils (70%) of Pakistan are zinc deficient thus affecting growth and yield of many crops like wheat, rice, sugarcane, cotton and brassica. Despite reports regarding the effects of limited water supply on crop plants growing in different agro-climatic zones of Pakistan, no report is available regarding the response of oil seed Brassica species to zinc under drought stresses. Furthermore, no report is available regarding the recommendation of Pakistani Brassica germplasm, suitable for cultivation in areas with low water availability and low zinc fertility. Hence, the study has been planned to screen the available germplasm of summer mustard, winter rapeseed-mustard and canola for drought tolerance under different zinc treatments at morphological, physiological and molecular level.

data.projectName: Digital Literacy Skills of University Students in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
In today’s world it is impossible to imagine life without digital technology. Individuals need to acquire digital skills, as without these skills, they are likely to face problems in gaining appropriate opportunities.  Although today’s generation has been facilitated with technology to prosper, yet they need proper skills to gain access to the opportunities of digital era. So here we can say that the role of educational institutions is very important to equip the students with digital literacy. Although Government and higher education institutions are striving hard to promote digital skills but still Pakistan is lacking far behind than the rest of the world. This impression instigates the study under certain prepositions. Situational analysis of available resources of digital literacy, their utility, capacity and awareness among the students and the guidance of teaching staff for the development and advancement in academia are some of the important questions of the study that will leads to the policy formation for the effective use of digital literacy. 
The main objective of the study is to explore the awareness level of students regarding digital literacy, the available resources at university and personal level. The research will also document the role of digital technology in the development of economic and academic spheres of life. Further it will find out government initiatives and capacity of the universities to enhance the digital literacy among students and faculty members. Lastly to find out how digital technology is creating digital divide in Pakistani society.

data.projectName: Electric Field Control of Magnetism in Strain-Mediated and Exchange-Coupled Magnetoelectrics for Low Power Electronic Devices
data.projectDigest: Today's microelectronic and spintronic eras are witnessing an ever growing impulse toward the realization of novel nanoscale devices with enhanced functionalities as compared to their bulk counterparts. The co-existence of electrical and magnetic order parameters in multiferroic materials provides great opportunities for electronic devices. In particular, the presence of magnetoelectric (ME) effect offers new functionalities in device design as in such systems magnetism can be modulated by applied electric field and vice versa. Electric field control of magnetism (ECM) has emerged as an appealing solution to enhance energy efficiency in miniaturized spintronics and ME devices, such as ME random access memories (MERAMs). The aim of this proposed project is to develop composite systems consisting magnetic/magnetostrictive and ferroelectric/piezoelectric components with enhanced ME coupling to test their efficacy for various low power devices. The strength of ME coupling will be tailored in strain mediated and exchange coupled systems by choosing suitable materials for each constituent and by geometrical and microstructural designs. Since the ME effect is of interfacial origin, a deep understanding of the phenomena that take place at interface is required. The primary goal is to design a novel, highly energy efficient and ultrafast magnetization control scheme.

data.projectName: Multi-Phase flow of chemically reactive fluids
data.projectDigest:
Fluid flows can be found all around in nature and are broadly observed by those individuals who monitor nature with open eyes. The behavior of flowing or static fluids (liquid and gases) is studied under the branch of applied mechanics named as fluid mechanics. Engineering areas like plasma physics, biophysics, geophysics and physical chemistry involve applications of fluid flow phenomena. The flows enclosed by channels or conduits are prevalent in science, engineering and daily life. Civil engineers also use the theoretical results of fluid equations to understand the transport of river sediment and erosion, irrigation channels, the pollution of the air and water and to design pipeline systems, flood control systems and dams etc. 
Further fluid mechanics become imperative to mechanical engineers since it also carries its applications in the study of machinery like windmills, powerplants, fans, gas turbines, heat exchangers, air conditioning equipments, heart-lung machines and breathing aids etc. Based on fluid mechanics applications in our everyday life from flowing water through our cooking faucet to traveling in the widespread areas of our universe, fluid mechanics is a very important subject, not just for academic use. It is a matter of practical significance. This proposed project will enhance the linkage and research collaborations among academia with industries on very useful physical flow problems.

data.projectName: Mapping and Analysis of tourism value chain in AJ&K
data.piUniversity: University of Kotli Azad Jammu and Kashmir
data.projectDigest: Global tourism value chain is a phenomenon which takes on series of human interactions among individuals, firms, and public sector entities. Distribution, transport, lodging, accommodation and sports activities are some manifestation of these engagements. Socio economic development follow suit to this multi personal involvement as an  area becomes a tourist destination. Value chain framework  for  AJ&K tourism would   attempt to focus on three dimensions. Firstly,  explore and identify different avenues for pro-poor tourism development in AJ& K and impact of this development on economy. Secondly, determine the prominent features of the value chain in  AJK tourism sector and to identify the prospects for growth of the sector and constraints that are keeping this sector away from fulfilling its economic and social potential.  Thirdly, analyze current economic impact from tourism perspective with particular focus on how this economic initiative can contribute to conflict transformation and peace building. The research project will  identify different itineraries – For each itinerary, key activities along the tourism value chain will be  analyzed. The study will also examine How value chain can be extended to intra-Kashmir trade and linkages across the divide  for transformational value of political economy.

data.projectName: Biological synthesis of Zn nanoparticles from some members of family Rutaceae  and its efficiency of application on maize for drought alleviation
data.projectDigest: Maize is the most important food source around the globe. The major challenge for meeting food demands of the 21st century is to enhance nutritional quality of maize kernels. Pakistan is located in agro-ecological region with less rainfall, and facing severe impact of climatic change, resulting in nutrient deficiency in plants. Zinc is the most important micronutrient deficient in soils of Pakistan. Its deficiency in cereal grains results in malnutrition and causes serious health issues. It is a critical component of enzymes and is necessary for basic biological processes in plants. The project will help us to determine how exogenously applied ecofriendly green synthesized nanoparticles from peel of citrus fruits will be helpful to overcome Zn deficiency in maize grains in comparison with conventional ZnSO4 fertilizer, to improve nutritional quality so that it can be used for the human consumption as a food product. The application of technology will help farmers to manage the delivery of nanofertilizer in right amount at the right time in rapidly available form to be used by plants for sustainable agriculture

data.projectName: Regulating the proliferative fate of neuronal and CNS progenitor cells through potential neurogenic natural product and their derivatives
data.projectDigest:
Mechanism of repair in the adult brain which is referred as neurogenesis and it
is considered as an important target to counteract the neuronal damage. In
order to improve neurogenesis, two strategies are considered promising i.e.,
(i) stimulation of endogenous neurogenesis by neurogenic compounds or (ii)
transplantation of exogenous neural precursors. Adult neurogenesis has been
shown to modulate by range of stimuli including cytokines, neurotrophic
factors, physiological processes, trophic factors/cytokines and drugs that are
particularly used for treating neurological diseases. Hence, adult neurogenesis
is the target of drugs used for treating neurological diseases and disorders,
such as Alzheimer's disease, depression and epilepsy. The activities of
neurological drugs may be mediated by adult NSCs. The contribution and
mechanism of adult neurogenesis and newly generated neuronal cells of the
adult brain in the activities of neurological drugs remain to be determined.
Although literature has cited the major role played by the new neurons in
mediating treatment efficacy of neurological drugs on cognitive functions, it is
still questionable if the altered production of new neurons can cause the
disorders or not. By escalating the neurogenesis it may be possible to provide
beneficial gains for processes related with formation of learning and memory.
Our hypothesis is to explore the effect of novel natural compounds and their
derivatives on the modulation of neurogenesis. It will help out in managing the neurodegenerative diseases including stroke, Alzheimer's Disease, epilepsy induced neuronal damage which is affecting a major population globally.

data.projectName: Phytochemical and anti-inflammatory studies of Eremostachys superba Royle ex Benth.
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Benazir Bhutto University, Sheringal, Dir
data.projectDigest:
The genus Eremostachys contain 8 species in Pakistan. Eremostachys superba Royle ex Benth locally named as Gajar Mula belong to family Lamiaceae is endemic to Pakistan and is a perennial herb and flowers in March-April. It is used traditionally in the treatment of mastitis in cattle, to restore milching in animals and asthenia. Leaves are used as bandage for wounds and as fish poison. The seeds are also reported to use as fish poisons. Other species of the genus have been reported for various pharmacological activities like antioxidant, analgesic, antimalarial, anti-inflammatory and various compounds have been also reported. To date no phytochemical and pharmacological work have been conducted and reported so far. The current project is designed to collect the plant form District Dir and after extraction, the extract will be subjected to chromatographic procedures to isolated novel lead. During phytochemical study, anti-inflammatory, analgesic and antioxidant studies will be carried out. This will not only validate the folkloric wound healing potential of the plant according to modern scientific approaches but the active anti-inflammatory moiety may also be isolated and purified.    
Keeping in view the lack of studies both pharmacological and phytochemical force us to plan this project to investigate the traditional wound healing effect and isolate the possible novel leading anti-inflammatory compounds.

data.projectName: Synthesis, Computational and Biological Studies of Quinoline Derivatives
data.projectDigest:
Quinoline is a bicyclic heterocycle characterized by a solid-ring structure which contains benzene fused to pyridine ring at its two adjacent carbons. The IUPAC name of quinoline is benzo[b]pyridine while this is also known as 1-azanaphthalene or 1-benzazine.
Quinolines are very important in pharmaceutical industry because their derivatives, a large proportion of which are alkaloids, show useful biological effects. All the commercially available anti-malarial drugs contain quinoline ring as essential part of their structure, however, its importance is not limited to treat malaria only. Quinoline derivatives have been described to exhibit anti-oxidant, anti-cancer, anti-inflammatory, analgesic, anti-fungal, anti-bacterial, anti-viral, anti-leishmanial and antidepressant activities. They are also employed as catalysts, polymers, corrosion inhibitors and preservatives. Researchers are enthralled to synthesize new quinoline derivatives that may be effective pharmacological agents. In this research project, new quinoline derivatives will be synthesized and will be further subjected to dry and wet lab experiments including computational and biological studies. This will not only help to understand the theoretical parameters but also to identify potent bio-active compounds.

data.projectName: Local governance,  technology and formalization of street economy: A case study of Islamabad, Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Development Economics (PIDE), Islamabad
data.projectDigest: Street economy is the most visible sub-set of an informal economy in urban settings around the world. Comprising of stationary and mobile street vendors, a street economy offers both economic vibrancy and aesthetic outlook to public space, if managed properly. Due to enormity of entrants in the street economy, it is mostly dealt as an administrative issue by the authorities in Pakistan.  What is the legal and administrative framework of municipal management of licensing, placement and eviction of Street Vendors? What are the linkages between formal economy and street economy? This project aims to determine the dynamics and challenges of economic mobility in the street economy of Pakistan and propose remedial actions, and finally test a technology-based solution to formalize the street economy in Islamabad and its adjoining areas. Project will be undertaken on pilot basis in selected territories of Islamabad, which can be scaled up later. It has two components, one pertains to regulatory enhancement and survey of street vendors within existing legal framework. And second relates with the development of purpose-built mobile application for managing street vending. We will employ randomized control trial methodology to robust analysis.

data.projectName: “Design and Synthesis of novel Oxadiazole and Triazoles based acetamides as EGFR inhibitors for treatment of lung cancer”
data.projectDigest:
Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer deaths globally in both high-income and low income countries, accounting for 1.6 million cancer deaths annually (approximately 20% of total cancer deaths) worldwide. Despite advances in surgery, chemotherapy and radiotherapy in the past 30 years, the 5-year survival rate of lung cancer remains less than 55% after diagnosis. Therefore, there is an urgent need for the development of the novel therapeutics against lung cancer. 
The epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) is frequently mutated in various cancers and is the target of multiple cancer therapies currently adopted in the clinical practice. EGFR predominantly overexpress in lung cancers and its inhibition results in decreased tumor growth and metastasis. Therefore, targeting EGFR has potential to provide selective treatment for lung cancer. This drug discovery approach represents a paradigm shift to develop new therapeutics, ultimately addressing the concerns for non-selectivity of available chemo drugs which have restricted their widespread application and efficacy.
Molecular hybridization is a simple and effective tool to combine covalently two drug pharmacophores into a single molecule. Oxadiazole and triazole demonstrate profound growth inhibitory activity against different cancer cells and TK enzymes. The use of Oxadiazole and triazole based drugs such as Afatinib, lapatinib and gefitinib in clinical practice paved the way to develop new oxadiazole and triazole-based molecules acting as EGFR inhibitors. In this context, we aim to exploit conjugated oxadiazole and triazole-based novel leads with tuneable anticancer activity and low toxicity. 
We (PI lab) have successfully developed protocols for synthesis of conjugated oxadiazole and triazole nucleus with acetam

data.projectName: :  MIMO and Smart Antennas for 5G Wireless Communication
data.projectDigest: The 5G, 5th generation of wireless communications, represents a revolution in telecommunication, which will bring a paradigm shift in the way users communicate for years to come. It will provide a data rate up to 10Gbps, fibre-like user experience, 1 ms over-the-air latency, users capacity up to several billion, power consumption per bit usage reduced by a factor of 1000 and many more.  To achieve these goals, it will employ Massive MIMO, phased arrays and multiband antennas. In this work, we will present antenna system solutions for smartphones and base stations for future 5G wirless communication systems. At first stage, a compact MIMO antenna array, for lower 5G bands such as 3.5 GHz and 6 GHz will be proposed for smartphones. Then a multi-beam base station array at mm-wave such as 28 GHz will be proposed for 5G base stations applications.

data.projectName: Investigation of Ag Nanoparticles Decorated Ternary Oxide One-Dimensional Nanostructures for Wound Care Applications
data.projectDigest: The cases of chronic wounds especially foot ulcer is on the rise worldwide. The incidence of these cases is at epidemic percentage where developments of novel therapeutic approaches are highly desirable. At present there are only four FDA, USA approved therapies for this type chronic disease. However these approved therapies have been facing numerous drawbacks and almost 70% of patients treated with these FDA approved therapies remain unhealed. Thus modern and novel dressing materials are desired for the said purpose. The main objective of the proposed project is to develop Ag nanoparticles decorated ternary oxides based polymer bandages. The properties of these bandages will optimized by changing the percentage content of Ag, dimensionality of nanostructures, percent molarities of metals in ternary oxides and type of metals. ZnO will be used as based material because of its excellent physio-chemical properties, biocompatible nature and antibacterial efficacy. In addition to ZnO, second metal will be selected on bases of band gap energy. We will use narrow band gap metal oxides to be coupled with ZnO for better photodynamic activities. The third metal will be selected for enhancing the mechanical strength and stability of coating on polymers. Ag nanoparticles will increase the antibacterial potency of metal oxide nanostructures by delaying the electron hole pair recombination. These fabricated and optimized bandaging materials will be characterized by number of techniques for structural, morphological, vibrational and antibacterial characteristics. Furthermore, in vivo healing properties of these nano bandages will be tested.

data.projectName: Photostability and Photostabilization Studies of Selected Drugs and Formulated Products – I
data.projectDigest: Light exposure is known to alter the chemical and physical characteristics of drug substances and their formulated products. This change can occur during production, quality control, and packaging as well as during storage in a warehouse or pharmacy shop and hospital environment. The effect of light on drug substances and their products may result in potency loss, toxicity, and biological ineffectiveness. A large number of drugs in everyday use are sensitive to light and thus unstable in the solid-state or liquid formulations during storage. In addition to this many drugs are formulated in mixtures (e.g., multivitamins) and, therefore, may be liable to chemical interaction and greater potency loss on exposure to light. The photostability of a drug can be described as to how it responds to light exposure and undergoes degradation reactions to often therapeutically inactive or toxic products. Medicines can also cause light-induced side effects after administration to the patients on interaction with biochemical substances in the body (e.g., sulphonamides, phenothiazines, fluoroquinolones) and need stabilization. Knowledge about the photostability of drugs and their products is necessary for safety and to evaluate handling, packaging, labeling, and adverse effects and drug photoreactivity in biological systems. This field is so far unexplored in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Molecular and Functional Characterization of Retinitis Pigmentosa epithelial genes prevalent in Pakistan.
data.piUniversity: Lahore College for Women University, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Retinitis Pigmentosa (RP) is a hereditary, genetically heterogeneous disease  affecting primarily retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) cells, with blindness. It accounts for 20% of children attending blind schools in Pakistan. Out of 60 genes of RP, RPE65, RLBP1 and RP1 mutations in epithelial cells are more common in Pakistani population. Overall goal of this study is genetic profiling and functional characterization of RP genes prevailing in Pakistani population. In this study we will validate mutations responsible for RP in RPE65, RLBP1 and RP1 genes through genetic and molecular analysis. Functional significance of most of these mutations is not known. So, there is a dire need of time to characterize their functionality through molecular techniques by performing expression analysis, cytometry analysis, Western bloting and ELISA. Appropriate cell lines will be used to study the effect of these mutations. The continuum of mutations in known genes existing in Pakistani population may differ from that are described earlier in other populations of the world. The novel variants in genes of RP will aid in diagnostic assessment of RP patients thus providing new tools for molecular diagnosis of this disease. In vitro produced RPE cells represent a novel source for retinal degenerative disease healing.

data.projectName: Development of Visible Light Active Nanocomposite Photocatalysts For Degradation of Emerging Pharmaceutical Contaminants in Wastewater
data.projectDigest: Presence of pharmaceutical particularly antibiotics in wastewater can have toxic and irreversible effects on human health. In Pakistan, the situation is more critical as wastewater treatment plants (generally at municipality and specifically at hospital levels) are either absent altogether, or, are entirely unable to treat these ECs. Currently, there is meager data available regarding the presences of such contaminants in wastewater in local conditions. In this context, there is urgent need for the detection of ECs present in wastewater being used for irrigation and development of strategies to degrade these contaminants in order to ensure environmental safety and food security. Without proper identification it is difficult for regulators to restrict the use of contaminants that are a human health hazard; and scientists to improve treatment techniques for higher priority pollutants; and the public to modify consumption patterns due to the vast number of these contaminants.  Our strategy is to harness the unlimited power of solar light with the help of VLA nanomaterial photocatalysts for non-selective and destructive elimination of harmful EC's from wastewater to make it reusable. Use of greener/environmentally friendly chemical routes would make the large-scale application of VLA photocatalysts an attractive wastewater treatment option. The success of this study may provide an environmental friendly and cost-effective advanced oxidation technique for complete removal of potentially endocrine disrupting compounds as wastewater treatment, which may ultimately contribute to water resource conservation.

data.projectName: Development of biofertilizer for organic production of Chenopodium quinoa Willd
data.projectDigest:
Quinoa is an annual crop known as “mother grain” that is used as a grain and popular source of protein, and minerals. The protein contents of quinoa range from 7 to 23 %, which is much higher than any other cereal crop. Quinoa is native of South America and recently introduced by USDA in Pakistan. In Pakistan, educated people attracted to alternate protein source. These people have concern over chemicals application particular chemical fertilizer and demanding organic food. Nitrogen and phosphorus are the most frequent limiting mineral nutrients for plant growth. By fulfilling the nitrogen and phosphorous requirements of quinoa, farmers are advised to apply chemical fertilizer, which is a toxic effect on human health as well as on the environment.  PGPR can be seen as cheap and environment-friendly substitutes to chemical fertilizers. Yet, several reports showed that commercial PGPR inoculants often outcompete by indigenous strains more adapted to local soil condition.
The proposed research aims to study the bacterial diversity in the rhizosphere of quinoa varieties that are cultivated in different regions of Pakistan. Microbiological and molecular techniques will be used to characterize the isolated bacterial strains. The plant-growth promoting effect of various strains in single inocula as well as in combinations will be tested on quinoa plants grown in a controlled environment as well as in field conditions. This study will pave the way for the selection of efficient PGPR strains that are better adapted to our soils. This study will also lead us to formulate biofertilizer for commercial purpose to help farmers to adopt alternate nutrient management strategy.

This study will pave the way for the selection of efficient PGPR strains that are better adapted to our soils. This study will also lead us to formulate biofertilizer for commercial purpose to help farmers to adopt alternate nutrient management strategy.

data.projectName: Effect of Ajwa date (Phoenix dactylifera L.) derived extract and PLGA based nanoparticles for cardioprotection : from cell lines to pre-clinical Experimental model
data.projectDigest: Heart diseases are the number one cause of death worldwide, approximately 17.9 million deaths each year. Heart attack, stroke, and other thrombotic events causes ischemic injury due to inadequate blood supply to that area of tissue. When medical professionals restore blood supply of the heart after sudden heart stop or heart attack to previously ischemic tissue additional injury occurs known as reperfusion injury (cause heart damage upto 50%) due to release of free radicals and inflammatory cascade. The main focus of our study is to find new ways to provide protection against reperfusion injury. We will develop Ajwa date derived extract PLGA based nanoparticles. Dates (Ajwa) contains polyphenols having established role in inhibition of free radicals and inflammatory mediators. First time, we will use Ajwa date derived extract PLGA based nanoparticles, where first we will do its characterization, safety and effectiveness testing outside living body, in heart cells and then in rat clinically validated experimental model. This project will provide us insight of Ajwa derived polyphenols and nanoparticle delivery system to protect heart against reperfusion injury. Due to appropriate clinical model, translation of this project to human will be easy and beneficial to protect human heart from reperfusion injury.

data.projectName: Measuring and Fostering Non-Cognitive Skills through Intelligent Tutoring System
data.projectDigest: There are certain traits in individuals strongly linked with positive life outcomes and effective functioning in a society. These traits are generally termed as Non-Cognitive Skills (NCS). Despite being critical for successful life and better performance in all spheres of life including academics, NCS are mostly neglected in formal education systems. As NCS are numerous and interrelated, for every individual these skills form a complex and unique system. Therefore, assessment and development of non-cognitive skills is quite challenging in traditional teaching learning environment. However, technology has a lot of potential to reliably assess and foster these skills because of the ease of customization and provision of personalized learning experiences. This project aims to measure and develop a set of non-cognitive skills including a) Grit, b) Self - efficacy c) social behavior d) Locus of Control e) Growth Mindset and f) self-control through an Intelligent Tutoring System (ITS). This specifically designed ITS will 1) assess the existing level of NCS of undergrad students 2) identify their learning styles and learning preferences and 3) will provide a specifically designed program to foster less developed skills.

data.projectName: Establishment and molecular phylogenetic characterization of ectomycorrhizal fungi and their potential use in conservation of forests of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Pakistan has many wonderful forests that are unique only to this area. But these forests are declining due to many factors. Unfortunately the regenerative capability of these forests is slow due to many factors. One of these is Plant Fungi relationships. The fungi found on plant roots facilitate plants in absorption of water, minerals, increased resistance to drought, disease, heavy metal etc. So it is important to identify the fungi specific to one forest and at which biotic and edaphic factor these fungi dominate. After their identification, these fungi can be inoculated in forest and nursery too as well as reforestation. As recently Billion Tree project planted tress and if we can add ectomycorrhizal fungi with these roots, tree survival and growth can be ensured.

data.projectName: Plant Growth Promotion and Alleviation of Drought Stress effects by application of fertilizers and their combination-An eco-physiological study
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: As most of the Pakistani land constitute arid areas, abiotic stresses due to climate change lead to food and health insecurity. Oxidative stress and associated phenomena caused by drought conditions lead to imbalance in photosynthatic mechanism and nutrients availability. Hence, they negatively affect the growth and yield of economically important native plants. Various tree species of Punjab are economically important as they are used as timber, fuel wood, fodder and medicinal purposes. In Pakistan, no attention has been given to build adaptive strategy to conserve economic trees by studying morphological, physiological and biochemical responses to drought stress and role of fertilizers to mitigate its negative impact. Hence, the proposed study will address the morphological and biochemical responses of different economic tree species of Punjab, Pakistan towards drought stress and to find out the answer of the question “Can fertilizers (Nitrogen, Phosphorus) and their combined application alleviate the negative impact of drought and promote the growth and production of these plants”. The focus of this research will be on medicinal and fodder tree species. To fulfill these goals a randomized experimental design will be used to find out the effect of well-watered and no-water levels of irrigation and similarly with and without P and N level of phosphorous and Nitrogen fertilizers, respectively. Combined application will be in the form of four treatments (Low phosphorus low nitrogen; LPLN, High phosphorus low nitrogen; HPLN, High phosphorus high nitrogen; HPHN, Low phosphorus high nitrogen; LPHN). The results of the research will also help to fulfill goals of sustainable agronomic productivity and conservation of trees.

data.projectName: A deep learning framework for predicting functional impact of cancer specific mutations through integrated analysis of 3D structures of proteins
data.projectDigest: Mutations have a significant role in human evolution and causing a disease. Millions of mutations have been identified in cancer genome. This huge volume of mutations poses a great challenge for researchers to examine functional implication of these mutations. Currently five mutations related to cancer disease/genome have been identified. These are gain of function, loss of function, switch of function, conservation and drug resistant mutations. Classifying and predicting functional impact of these mutations are very important for understanding cancer genome and treatment of the cancer disease. Very less work has been done in this regard. According to our initial analysis, none of the available tools utilize information encoded in 3D protein structures to classify all these mutations reliably and predict their functional impact. The proposed framework will be very useful for understanding cancer causing genes and underlying molecular mechanism. This will classify and predict functional impact and cellular consequences of all these mutations.

data.projectName: Chemopreventive and Chemotherapeutic role of Moringa oleifera and its Molecular Mechanism of Action in Childhood Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
data.projectDigest:
Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) is serious cancer of white blood cells that mainly victimizes children less than 15 years of age. Majority of the paediatric leukemia cases (75%) are ALLs. The incidence of childhood ALL is not known in Pakistan due to the non-availability of National Cancer Registry. The chemotherapy applied to the ALL patients causes severe side effects. 
Moringa oleifera, commonly known as (Sohanjna) has been used as folk medicine against many diseases. Its biological potential has been explored in many research reports as antimicrobial, antifungal, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer agent. 
The objective of the proposed study is to investigate the role of M. oleifera, as chemopreventive and chemotherapeutic agent against human preB and T-ALL cell lines. The anticancerous effect of Moringa will also be analysed on gene level by using state-of-the-art techniques. 
Materials & Methods: Extracts of leaves and seeds of M. oleifera will be prepared in solvents like hexane, methanol and ethyl acetate. T-ALL and preB cell lines from human origin will be maintained in culture medium. Different assays like MMT, Cell Cycle Arrest, Apoptosis and Real-Time qPCR will be performed to evaluate the viability, death and cell cycle arrest of the cells. 
Expected Outcome: The study will provide chemopreventive and chemotherapeutic impact of Moringa oleifera in childhood ALL and its mechanism of action on molecular level.

data.projectName: Impact of Green Synthesis of Silver Nanopartilces to enhance production of Wheat
data.projectDigest: Nanotechnology is known as multidisciplinary field of 21st century, making a significant impact in the field of medical, science, agriculture etc. throughout the world. Nano-particles are tiny in size possessing diverse types of dimensions between 1-100 nm. Among nano-particles, silver nanoparticles are important at commercial level on the basis of physical, chemical and biological attributes due to presence of some unique characters. Synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNP’s) from plant extract is important for increased growth of plant, leaf area and dry weight of aerial structures and other related traits.  A collaborative research work was carried out on such innovative technology in agriculture for high yield and resistance to many disease and insct peast. Synthesis and characterization of silver nanoparticles will be accomplished at Center of Excellence for Solid State Physics, GC University, Lahore. Evaluation of impact of silver nanoparticles on seeds of ten wheat varieties by soaking in 0, 25, 50, 100, 125 ppm solutions of silver nanoparticles for 10, 15, 30, 40 and 60 minutes respectively before sowing at Department of PBG, Ghazi University, D. G. Khan to find out its effect on chemical, biochemical traits and plant growth and spike and grain related traits.. On the basis of results, it will be concluded that wheat variety treated with specific level of nanoparticles possessed most desirable traits important for high grain yield and can perform best even at high temperature (45oC). It will make the farmers to produce more and best quality grain with minimum cost benefit ratio.
