data.projectName: Investigating the potential of botanicals and elicitors to manage citrus greening disease under field conditions.
data.projectDigest: Citrus greening is currently the most economically devastating disease of citrus. It reduces 72% of fresh orange production worldwide while 21%, 25% and 31% of citrus plantation area in USA, China and Brazil, respectively. In Pakistan, citrus greening disease is posing main risks in Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and is affecting all type of citrus plantation i.e. Kinnow, Sweet orange, Grape fruit, Sweet lime and lemon by 22%, 25-40%, 15%, 10% and 2% respectively. Unfortunately, there is no curative measures for HLB, it could be ascertained to various factors i.e. non-existence of definite curative strategy and lack of genetic resistance in citrus for greening disease. However, removal of infected trees and control of vector are considered basic preventive measures for citrus greening. Therefore, finding other measures to control HLB with higher efficiency along with lower economic and environmental impact has become research priority. The plant extracts and elicitors capable of enhancing natural defense mechanisms in plants should be exploited to mitigate the effect of greening on citrus production. The outcome of this project will determine the efficacy of botanicals and elicitors to manage greening disease. Efficient management of citrus greening will enhance the yield and quality of citrus produce.

data.projectName: CNT doped Nanofibre mats strengthened multiscale hybrid composites
data.projectDigest:
Polymer composites have found diverse applications in daily life to high-tech industries. However, the major challenge of the conventional polymer composites failure at the matrix rich interlaminar region still remains and limits their performance resulting in unreliable usage of these composites. One of the potential solutions is to reduce the length scale of the reinforcing fillers to the size of organic building blocks of hosting composites. One prime candidate is the electro-spun nanofibre mat, as an interalia into the matrix rich interlaminar region of the conventional polymer composite, which is expected to improve the strength.
Controlling the alignment and distribution of the nanofibres during the chaotic electrospinning process is a major hurdle for improving the interlaminar regions. The random orientations of electrospun nanofibres mat reduce their strengthening effect and also the required material properties. Hence, the proposed research will focus on the design/modification of electrospinning process for improving the orientation and distribution of the nanofibre mats. 
The proposed electrospinning process will be used to produce random, aligned, CNT and FCNT doped nanofibre mats. These nanomats with different volume fractions will be sandwiched with the glass fibre-epoxy matrix to produce nano strengthened multiscale hybrid composites. A series of tests (destructive and non-destructive) will be carried out to ensure the effectiveness of the proposed composite. Results of the above mentioned project can be extended to the real-life applications such as high tech engineering composites, construction and medical engineering etc.

Peanut or groundnut is commonly known as “Poor man’s nut”. Peanut has potential to compete other expensive nutritious protein rich sources as meat to overcome the under nutrition in malnourished regions of Pakistan. In recent years, Pakistan is facing huge economic burden annually by importing various edible products. The import is acceptable only for those food items that are not native to Pakistan. 
The instant research project is an effort to improve the utility of peanut through its proper postharvest handling, processing and value addition which will ultimately upgrade the country’s export potential and economic status of peanut growers/farmers. The primary objective is pretreatment of peanut to reduce aflatoxin risk. The second intention of research is to develop value added peanut products. Lastly, overall acceptability of peanut products will be checked among the population.  The instant research is divided in three phases. During postharvest handling phase, the pretreatment of peanut will be carried out to reduce aflatoxin invasion. In this section, peanut will be shelled and de-hulled followed by solar drying, microwave heating and hot air oven drying to assess comparative effectiveness of drying method against aflatoxins. Moreover, raw material will also be analyzed for various compositional analysis. Secondly, the peanut based value added products will be prepared with improved nutritional profile. Finally, the organoleptic characteristics of prepared peanut items will be checked. Peanut has potential to compete other expensive nutritious protein rich sources as meat to overcome the under nutrition in malnourished regions of Pakistan. In recent years, Pakistan is facing huge economic burden annually by importing various edible products. The import is acceptable only for those food items that are not native to Pakistan. 
The instant research project is an effort to improve the utility of peanut through its proper postharvest handling, processing and value addition which will ultimately upgrade the country’s export potential and economic status of peanut growers/farmers. The primary objective is pretreatment of peanut to reduce aflatoxin risk. The second intention of research is to develop value added peanut products. Lastly, overall acceptability of peanut products will be checked among the population.  The instant research is divided in three phases. During postharvest handling phase, the pretreatment of peanut will be carried out to reduce aflatoxin invasion. In this section, peanut will be shelled and de-hulled followed by solar drying, microwave heating and hot air oven drying to assess comparative effectiveness of drying method against aflatoxins. Moreover, raw material will also be analyzed for various compositional analysis. Secondly, the peanut based value added products will be prepared with improved nutritional profile. Finally, the organoleptic characteristics of prepared peanut items will be checked. Peanut/groundnut is important both as a cash crop and food crop thus its production and processing will prove helpful to uplift Pakistan’s economy. data.projectName: Building Bridges Between Universities and Society for National Development
data.piUniversity: National University of Modern Languages, Islamabad (NUML)
data.projectDigest:
This proposed project assesses the role of scientific research in the field of social sciences in national universities and its impact on socio-economic growth of the country. The study would focus on national universities and level of their linkages with governmental agencies in order to comprehend the socio-economic and political problems. The study would also identify the leading national stakeholders and local agencies/ councils crafting the framework for their connectivity to the universities for relevant output. 
The study would also investigate to what extend the universities and governmental agencies comprehend each other’ scope and organizational goals. The study would investigate how to stimulate institutional transformation to reorient the potential base of universities, and the role of knowledge production and scientific research productivity in that to resolve national problems. For this, a combination of top-down and bottom-up organizational approaches, multidimensional notions of excellence and transparent governance model will be suggested. This research will prepare a framework to connect the HEC as a partner to create bridge between government agencies/ city councils/ national stakeholders and universities to promote/ understand the problems and find out consumable solutions. Universities, and local city councils’ linkages are significant as they should work together as partners to identify societal problems and find out solutions.  The project would map-put how can research in the higher education be reframed, thus incorporating them in one unit to contribute to the country’s policy and society.

data.projectName: Clinical application of Growth factors to control chronic mastitis in dairy cows
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Mastitis is the most substantial disease of dairy animals, it hugely effects the farm economics by decrease in production of milk and increase in treatment. Mammary gland infection is multifactor and a complex disorder of milk secretory tissues of lactating animals which requires the understanding of exact mechanism of its development. About 8.43 million people in Pakistan are involved in rearing buffaloes (29.9 million) and cattle (33.0 million) which share more than 95% of the total milk produced in country Huge efforts are underway regarding expansion in the field of dairy animal breeding, animal nutrition, husbandry practices and welfare. Affective treatment of mastitis has played important role in increasing global milk production over the last few decades to meet the increasing demand for milk, milk byproducts and meat. Chronic mastitis has great importance as a cow with fibrosed udder is slaughtered for meat consumption thus reducing its price to four times low as it is irreversible condition. Fibrosis in one quarter leads to 25 percent drop in milk production in a cow from one quarter. So this research will be very much helpful for farmer’s economic uplift by increasing production of high quality milk. It causes decline in milk production and produces huge loses in income. In this research we will find a way to cure the fibrosed mammary glands by platelet rich plasma (PRP) and EGF Epidermal growth factor.The project will enable us to identify possible protocols for treating major problems of mammary glands. The project will benefit the livestock farmers who will increase the survival rate of their precious livestock and increase in production of the animals instead of culling and slaughter their animal.

data.projectName: Synthesis of chiral amino alcohols and related functionalized molecules as potential drugs for cancer and Tuberculosis (TB)
data.projectDigest:
We are proposing a concise, efficient and highly stereospecific synthesis of 1,2-amino alcohols (1) and related compounds for treatment of cancer and tuberculosis that are deadly infectious diseases killing millions of people worldwide. Multidrug resistance (MDR) and extensive drug resistance (XDR) is major concern in treatment of these disease as strains become resistant to old and new drugs. There are numerous methods reported in literature for their synthesis but have many limitations i.e. moderate yield, sensitive reaction conditions, expensive chiral catalysts and poor stereoselectivities as its challenging to construct 1,2-adjecent stereo centers in a synthesizing complex molecules.
Our proposed methodology present synthesis of 1,2-amino alcohols (1) and related functionalized molecules in single step via stereospecific nucleophilic ring opening of epoxide using readily available chiral sulfide. Advanced methodology Sulfur ylide epoxidation will be testified to carryout conversions. Following our proposed strategy target molecules will obtained with high stereospecifity in excellent yields.
1,2-Amino alcohol (1) and related functionalized molecules are expected promising drug candidates against cancer and tuberculosis. These target molecules enriched with medicinal privileged motifs like quinoline will combat with strains of MDR and XDR. We claim that our proposed strategy will become first choice by pharmaceutical companies at industrial level.

data.projectName: Microneedle patch-based macrophage targeted nanoparticles delivery system: promising strategy to overcome the subcutaneous barriers for the enhanced therapy of Cutaneous Leishmaniasis
data.projectDigest: Leishmaniasis is an obligate intracellular parasitic disease that manifests itself either as visceral leishmaniasis (VL) or cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL) that can cause death or permanent disability if left untreated. In the past years, CL in Pakistan has increased at a considerable rate and has also extended its geographic distribution that effects the skin and mucosal tissue. Despite availability of various chemotherapeutic options, the effective control of this diseases cannot be achieved at full potential.  The failure of CL of therapy is related to the lack of permeability of antileishmanial  drugs across the skin. therefore, the designed project is focused on the development of microneedle patch based drug delivery system that will penetrate the skin and will provide the drug at the deep layers of skin where leishmania  parasite resides. Thus, it can be promising to strategy to enhance the effectiveness of antileishmanial drug. Also the local pharmaceutical industry will be encouraged to manufacture micro/nanobased drug delivery system for the cost-effective ans uninterrupted supply of antileishmanial medicine.

data.projectName: Mediating Role of social and human capital in women owned microbusiness practices in Punjab Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Small and medium enterprises are backbone of modern economy. Micro-enterprises in developing economies are less understood phenomenon. Especially very few researches and articles, focus on women owned microbusinesses. There is significant gap of literature in understanding of the microbusinesses from social and human capital lens. In this context, this research will focus on role of social and human capital in establishing and running of the microbusiness by women in Punjab Pakistan. The primary objectives of the research will be to understand common microbusinesses, business practices, choice of particular businesses and mediating role of social and human capital in running, maintenance and growth of that business.  These goals will be oriented towards developing a comprehensive understanding of women owned microbusinesses and their daily affairs.  
This study will employ mixed methods to investigate and understand the women owned microbusiness practices in the context of social and human capital. As there are no studies in Pakistan combining the role of both human and social capital, this research will employ both qualitative and quantitative approaches . The Principle investigator will collaborate with two international experts ; one of them is from Germany and one is from China. Their intellectual and technical input will boost the scope and quality of the project. In future, we can collaborate with them at Higher Education Institution level and this will help to enhance our international relations. At the moment, it is the need of time to do research on this topic this is undoubtedly the vision of present government. Organizations like SMEDA and TEVTA are working in this area.

data.projectName: Design and development of Maximum Power Point Tracking System for Photovoltaic Based Cascaded Half-Bridge Multilevel Inverter using Hybrid Algorithm
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
Photovoltaic (PV) system has conversion losses associated with it. Hence, Maximum power point tracking (MPPT) controller becomes essential for the extraction of maximum power for PV generation system. A substantial number of MPPT techniques have been proposed and implemented. These conventional techniques for MPPT get trapped in a local MPP and fail to track the global MPP particularly under partially shaded conditions due to generation of multiple peaks in power-voltage characteristics. Therefore, it is dire need to develop a hybrid algorithm for MPPT system.
In this project, the combination of two algorithms (firefly and differential evolution algorithms) will be used to track MPP. The firefly algorithm is good for optimization problems. The differential evolution algorithm is powerful dynamic evolutionary optimizers used to solve optimal power flow problems.
In this project,  a multilevel (MLI) power conversion system interconnected with PV system is also proposed. The MLI is used in this project minimized harmonics in the output voltage.  Moreover, these converters have low power dissipation and lower voltage stress on solid state devices. The proposed MLI is to generate more levels in output voltage waveform. Therefore, the proposed MLI reduces number of switching devices, switching losses, cost and size.

data.projectName: Brain Temperature Monitoring through Microwave Radiometry
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: During medical surgeries, prolonged anesthesia causes hypothermia (i.e. brain temperature drops below normal core temperature i.e. 37 oC) in patients. In some cases, hypothermia is deliberately created due to which patient’s temperature cools down to 5-18 oC, and this is done to reduce the sensitivity of critical brain tissues to ischemia. In both cases, it is critical to rewarm the body back to its normal body temperature to reduce the risk of morbid myocardial outcomes and prolonged surgical recovery. In severe head injury (SHI) conditions, the brain temperature must be continuously monitored for hypothermia and hyperthermia conditions. Apart from surgeries, brain temperature monitoring is also important in other scenarios. For example, cooling therapy of newborn babies and thermotherapy for curing cancer. Similarly, thermal protection of newborn babies is a situation where deep body temperature is monitored. The currently used thermometry devices (e.g. thermocouple probes) measure surface temperature or intercavitary surrogates temperature that do not indicate the exact core temperature of deep body organs. These methods are inherently inaccurate and have problems related to probe placement and time delays in reading. This project will provide a research base to develop such medical devices that will use microwave radiometry principle to measure non-invasively the brain core temperature. In addition, this research has a great potential to be employed by neurologists to analyze different brain disorders based on neuro-thermal coupling.

data.projectName: Conformation transition of polyelectrolyte and polyelectrolyte brushes in the presence of surfactant additives and salts.
data.projectDigest:
Polyelectrolyte brushes consist of  charged polymer chains grafted to interface.  The stretching of polyelectrolyte chains  from anchoring surface give rise to brush and these brushes have unique properties.The aim of proposed research is to investigate the interactions, organization and morphological transitions in polyelectrolytes andpolyelectrolyte brushes in the presence of different categories of surfactants  and various salts. The polyelectrolyte-surfactant complexes represent a new type of materials, which can be used for producing targeted effect on the processes taking place at supramolecular level.  Besides, they can also be used to control properties at molecular level. Different factors, such as temperature, presence of salt, solvent affect these interactions and conformation of polyelectrolyte and polyelectrolyte brushes. The aggregates of polyelectrolyte surfactant system can act as microenvironment for hydrophobic solutes.
Modified drug release generally utilizes polymers and polymer brushes. In the proposed work charged polyelectrolyte will be employed for the purpose of controlling the release of model drugs. This is due to their relevancy to biology and medicine, and because they have properties similar to amino acids and hyaluronic acid brushes. In addition, their properties are easily tunable. In the past, surfactants have been investigated to control the properties of polyelectrolyte and polyelectrolyte brushes. According to our proposition, surfactant additives and salt can be employed to control the morphology and organization of polyelectrolytes,  as a consequence a better control can be achieved in modified release of drug candidates. 
The project is basic in nature and the aim of this project is to synthesize polyelectrolytes and polyelectrol

data.projectName: Inhibition of Different Bacterial Strains by Antibiotic Functionalized Biocompatible GO-Ag Nanocomposites
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest:
Statement of Problem: Bacterial resistance from common anti-toxins is one of the most significant human health issues and has negative effects on medicinal practice. It is expected that silver NPs can enhance antibacterial action against multi-resistant bacteria and the actions of anti-toxins attached with silver NPs, particularly ampicillin, streptomycin, vancomycin, and tetracycline could show strong inhibitory effects towards resistant bacteria. The recent investigations indicated that bacteria do not able to create ?-lactamase when treated with anti-microbials functionalize with silver NPs. Dose dependent silver concentrations will require for the better improvement of antibacterial action against multi-resistant microscopic organisms. 
Synthesis of Graphene Oxide-Silver Nanocomposite: Graphene Oxide(GO) will be synthesized by Hummer’s Method. Silver Nanoparticles can be embedded over the GO by using the Green Chemistry 
Antibacterial Activity: Cytotoxicity assay will perform to evaluate the cell viability in NIH 3T3 cells for a significant medicinal application. This investigation will exhibit a potential answer for this issue, utilizing the solid synergistic impacts of anti-infection agents attached with silver nanoparticles (NPs).

data.projectName: Species’ responses to climate change: A physiological approach
data.projectDigest: Over a million species are directly threatened by the climate change. Species’ response to climate change will determine the fate of these species. It is imperative to quantify these responses as well as the factors that may add species in tolerating fast changing climatic conditions in order to mitigate the effects of climate change. One way to quantify the responses is to evaluate species fundamental niche using physiological capacities to tolerate changes in climatic conditions. In this project we intend to measure species’ fundamental niche, metabolic rates, morphological traits as well as their distribution along two contrasting mountain transects in Pakistan. One transect will be at Sulaiman ranges with very limited vegetation cover and other transect will be in Nathia Gali with forest covered mountains. The contrasting transects will help in understanding the role of habitat in determining species fundamental niche. All this information will be used in an integrative manner to predict species’ possible responses to climate change. For example, to determine whether species will shift their geographical ranges or will have capacity to adapt to newer climatic conditions. This project will give an insight how much time species has left before they start experiencing inhabitable climatic regimes.

data.projectName: Lead tolerance and phytoremediation potential of Conocarpus erectus L.
data.projectDigest:
Conocarpus erectus is commonly known as buttonwood. It is an evergreen tree or shrub and native to North America. It has been introduced in Pakistan due to its ever-green foliage and beauty. Buttonwood is a hardy plant, as it grows well in various kinds of environments like salinity, waterlogged and drought affected areas. Pakistan is an agriculture country, but now a days, most of agriculture land has been utilized for establishing industries, to fulfil the basic need of over growing populations. Industries are main source of heavy metals like cadmium and lead, as they are openly released into the agriculture fields and water canals. Lead is emerging as environmental pollutant due to its persistent nature and continuous supply from various sources. These involved extractive metallurgy, burning of lead gasoline, or use of lead-polluted medium to land. Due to its close binding to colloidal materials and organic substances, it is supposed that little amounts of Pb are soluble in soil, and therefore penetrates in plant system easily. Pb is a member of heavy metals which is not necessary for plants and is known for no specific biological function. High concentration of Pb ions present in soil, is taken by the roots of plants and a small amount is moved upward to the other parts of plant like leaves and stem. 
Due to hardy nature of Conocarpus erectus, it is hypothesized that it can tolerate various metal stresses and possess phytoremediation potential. Therefore, this project has been planned to explore its lead tolerance and phytoremediation potential based on its morpho-anatomical and physiological characteristics.

data.projectName: ADHD Classification using Shape Features of Subcortical Regions
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is the most common mental disorder diagnosed in children. The apparent symptoms in children with ADHD may be hyperactivity, uncontrollable impulsiveness and inattention. Changes in brain anatomy and functions have been identified in ADHD patients using structural MRI (sMRI) and functional MRI (fMRI). These changes could be used as biomarkers for early detection of the disease, and hence, a proper treatment could be applied for its prevention. The purpose of the proposed study is to characterize the ADHD patients by correlating the disease with the size and shape of the brain regions and their functions using advanced image processing and AI techniques.

data.projectName: Exploration of treatment against MDR-Pneumonia using invitro and insilico approach
data.projectDigest: Humans have been at the verge of war with micorganisms causing uncountable diseases since the dawn of human civilization. With the discovery of new antimicrobial drugs, these organisms are continuously fighting back with advance weapons making it difficult to cope with them and are the biggest threat to humanity. The diseases caused by these superbugs are Pneumonia, multidrug resistant Tuberculosis, skin infections and urinary tract infections. New research is paving the way for the development of innovative drugs that restore antibiotic susceptibility in antibiotic-resistant superbugs. Every year, more than 300,000 people die due to infections caused by antibiotic resistant bacteria. Statistical figures are alarming as it appears that in 2050, antibiotic resistance bacteria will claim 10 million deaths/annum and we will run out of options, if don’t take it seriously. Multidrug resistant (MDR) bacteria like Klebsiella pneumoniae and Staphylococcus aureus are among the major contributors as antibiotic resistant species, to the economic and health burden on a global scale. Due to absence of valid new therapeutic drugs as alternative, colistin is the only available drug to work with MDR strains with its limitations. Therefore, it is urgently needed to find alternative solutions that work with fewer side effects. Present research aims at exploring the possible inhibitors for MDR strain of bacteria causing pneumonia using insilico and invitro approach. With the discovery of new antimicrobial drugs, these organisms are continuously fighting back with advance weapons making it difficult to cope with them and are the biggest threat to humanity. The diseases caused by these superbugs are Pneumonia, multidrug resistant Tuberculosis, skin infections and urinary tract infections. New research is paving the way for the development of innovative drugs that restore antibiotic susceptibility in antibiotic-resistant superbugs. Every year, more than 300,000 people die due to infections caused by antibiotic resistant bacteria. Statistical figures are alarming as it appears that in 2050, antibiotic resistance bacteria will claim 10 million deaths/annum and we will run out of options, if don’t take it seriously. Due to absence of valid new therapeutic drugs as alternative, colistin is the only available drug to work with MDR strains with its limitations. Therefore, it is urgently needed to find alternative solutions that work with fewer side effects. Present research aims at exploring the possible inhibitors for MDR strain of bacteria causing pneumonia using insilico and invitro approach. We believe that the results of this new research will be a promising breakthrough in the effort to defeat these resistant superbugs by developing a new drug.

data.projectName: Fabrication of polymer Electrospun nanofibers for environmental remediation
data.projectDigest: Treatment of industrial waste waters in a manner which is not deleterious to the environment has been a challenge for the scientists and engineers working in the fields of environmental science and engineering. Therefore, the production of water for drinking and for industrial use after purification using both pre- and post-treatment has to be addressed on priority basis. There are many materials that have been employed by researchers in order to check their efficiency for water treatment, but they all possess some demerits. For water treatment, normally organic adsorbent has been used in most effective adsorbent to remove the pollutant in water. The utilization of these adsorbent has increased every year and everywhere.  The high surface area, the control of pore size distribution and the surface chemistry of adsorbents are the desired properties for removal and degradation of various kinds of organic inorganic pollutants.  The objectives of this study are to find out the degradation efficiency of nanomaterial in order to resolve the water purification issues. We will be synthesized nano-photocatalysts using already available electrospinning technology in our laboratories. These nanomaterials degrade toxic heavy metals from waste water using solar energy by photocatalysis.  This methodology takes full advantage of the most abundant renewable energy source, the sun, and degrade toxic compounds and emits only water as a byproduct. The purified water can be further filtered to remove catalysts and make it possible for drinking and household purposes.

data.projectName: Optimization of Design Parameters for New Substrates to Enhance Biogas Energy Production Based on Rheological Measurements
data.projectDigest: Diminishing fossil fuels, climate change mitigation needs, rising cost of energy/electricity and hazards of synthetic fertilizers divert attention to alternative sources of energy. Biogas produced from cattle manure provides sustainable cycle of nutrients and creates less carbon foot-print. Nearly 20,000 tons per day cow manure from the dairy industry remains un-utilized and is disposed at Karachi coastlines only, causing severe environmental damage.  Despite being the fifth largest milk producing country, Pakistan is far behind biogas or renewable energy producers . Therefore the scale of biogas production has to be increased. The new heterogenic substrates and increased organic loading rate, however, will bring challenges for process stability, complexity and sustainability of the biogas reactor. Among the thermo-physical properties of the fibrous and solid-rich biomass, the solid content and rheology determine the design of the bioreactor, energy consumption, mixing efficiency and ultimately the environmental viability of biogas process. The new substrates further complicate the rheological changes in the bioreactor and are being understood to ensure process stability.

data.projectName: Conjoint application of ACC deaminase biotechnology and biochar for sustainable wheat production on heavy metals contaminated soil
data.projectDigest: Heavy metals pose a risk to public health because of their toxic and nonbiodegradable nature and widespread occurrence in natural and human altered environments. Cadmium and lead are among the most toxic and carcinogenic heavy metals that could cause serious environmental and health problems. High application rates of persistent metals containing pesticides, burning of fossil fuels, irrigation with metals contaminated industrial sewage water and automobiles smoke not only contaminate our soils but also these metals are becoming the part of food chain through plants. In plants, such metals have become a major cause of disturbance in physiological and metabolic activates which decrease plant growth. For remediation of metals contaminated soil or to alleviate their stress in plants, biochar and ACC deaminase biotechnology can be used as an effective approach to remediate polluted soils. On the other hand, biochar can sorb these metals ions to minimize their bioavailability to plants. It is also reported that biochar directly and indirectly boosts up the microbial population in the soil. Thus, a pilot scale project is planned for the safe utilization of ACC deaminase containing PGPR and biochar to examine their cumulative effectiveness against heavy metals to improve wheat production.

data.projectName: Role of insurance based regulations for generating employment
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Zulfikar Ali Bhutto Institute of Science & Technology (SZABIST) University, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The purpose of this study is to identify the role of insurance-based SMEs and government regulation to not only assist in employment generation but also in other necessary socio-economic aspects of the country, like; better tax revenue collection, more productivity of micro-entrepreneurs, more exports, and above all government control as a regulatory body. There is a need to identify and address the gap of regulation for controlling SMEs and developing integration with MFIs. The element of micro-entrepreneurship insurance aspect which provides a new perspective of insurance-based controlling. The methodology is applied, qualitative research and inductive in nature. Interviews will be conducted from SMEs, MFIs, and ORIC departments from different metropolitan entrepreneurial hubs of Pakistan. The study tentative results will be an integrated output as regulation and micro-entrepreneurial insurance, which will cause better entrepreneurial endeavors and employment generation. The significance of the study is its contribution to the socio-economic development of Pakistan. The findings of the study will be welcomed by the regulator in terms of its innovative ideas and assistance in start-ups by funding through MFIs. Regulators will provide insurance – through insurance companies - to micro-entrepreneurs as per their revenue generation and tax payments.

data.projectName: Design and Development of a Modular and Reconfigurable Soft-Exoskeleton for Industrial Workers
data.projectDigest: The central aim of this research is to design and develop a modular and reconfigurable soft-exoskeleton for industrial workers to help them avoid muscle-fatigue during repetitive tasks. The soft-exoskeleton will use newly developed and pneumatically operated soft-actuators, contrary to conventional rigid-link exoskeletons, thus enabling us to reduce the metabolic cost of wearing such assistive devices. In order to achieve modularity and reconfigurability, a light-weight jacket-like structure will be developed on which the soft-actuators will be mounted in different configurations according to the allowable angles and range of motion of concerning muscles. This will allow us to use a common exoskeletal structure to perform a multitude of different biomechanical activities by just changing the configuration of soft-actuators. Once developed, the soft-exoskeleton may not only be used for helping industrial workers but also for physiotherapeutic treatment of patients. The exoskeleton will also be extensively tested to assess the extent of assistance it provides in avoiding muscle fatigue under different practical settings. For this purpose, the project proposed herein will also develop an experimental setup. A software will also be developed to allow a user to configure the soft-exoskeleton according to the task-requirement.

data.projectName: An Assessment of productivity and productivity differential between Public and Private Universities of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The role of productive and skillful workforce in economic growth is a universally recognized theme. The significance of this concept is well evident from the stream of growth models available in economic literature. Modern day economics highly acknowledges the human capital as a complementary and prospective factor for economic growth. Higher education is considered as a key indicator of human capital and plays a pivotal role in developing human capital in an economy. Growth prospects of an economy are largely defined by its productive capacity or potential and higher education significantly enhances this potential. This context accords a special position to the institutes offering higher education in the country. Being perceived as a hub of knowledge, the higher education institutes and universities are held responsible for providing highly productive human capital to the economy. The quality of human capital available to an economy can be implicitly assessed by the productivity of these institutes or universities. These universities or institutes provide a baseline to what can latterly be translated into a pronounced outcome; therefore, it is critical to evaluate and measure the productivity of these institutes.

data.projectName: Design and Synthesis of Non-Fullerene Acceptors for Organic Solar Cells
data.projectDigest: Due to the acute energy crisis, pollution, and global warming, Pakistan needs to decrease heavy reliance on fossil fuel energy. Solar energy is one of the most promising alternative energy sources to fossil fuels. Solar cells convert this clean, free, and infinite form of energy into electricity with the help of light-absorbing materials. Commercially available solar cells use silicon as a light-capturing material and offer reliable performance for several years. However, their production is complex, prices are high, and application is limited to outdoors. Organic solar cells (OSCs) use low-cost organic compounds to harvest energy and are light-weight, slim, and easy to produce at an affordable cost. OSCs can be printed on foldable surfaces and integrated into buildings, windows, and low-light conditions. Despite many benefits, the commercialization of OSCs still requires improvements in efficiency and durability. We aim to produce new light-absorbing materials for OSCs with increased efficiency and stability. The project will encourage public, academic, and industrial sectors to harness the underutilized solar potential of Pakistan and to fulfil the energy needs of the country safely and sustainably.

data.projectName: Predictive analytics for contraceptive use in Pakistan: causes, implications and the way forward
data.projectDigest:
The ‘‘Population Bomb’’ made dire predictions - and triggered a wave of repression around the world (Charles C. Mann, 2018)

Rapid increase in population is one of the major problems for developing countries. Pakistan is the sixth largest populated country in the world and the population growth is too high in the view of country's limited resources. The excessive population growth is the major reason for slow development process in the country and therefore it has been a great challenge and main concern for the government. Although the initiative of national family planning program was taken soon after the independence and policies were implemented in order to control the population growth, the contraceptive use is still very limited and the required results have not been achieved until today.

Previously the relationship between contraception use and different factors was analyzed by simple econometric models. However, it is well known that the survey data contain a natural hierarchical structure that can be helpful during the analysis. Furthermore, ignoring the different level within the data and drawing inferences from aggregated data is often misleading, affecting the results and consequently their interpretation. The objectives of this work are to characterize the phenomenon of contraceptive use in Pakistan, understand its implications, and identify its causes to the extent possible using advance statistical models.

data.projectName: Development of consolidate bioprocessing (CBP) for the Production, purification and characterization of biosurfactants by indigenous microbes
data.piUniversity: Mirpur University of Science and Technology (MUST), AJ&K
data.projectDigest: Biosufactants (BS) are surface active chemicals produced by certain microorganisms, these reduce surface tension between different phases (oil, water & media) and help microbes to grow. These compounds possess many important characteristics that made biosurfactants suitable for many industries like Pharmaceutical, cosmetics, food and nutrition. Currently, synthetic surfactants are used but these are mostly toxic for environment. Biosurfactants are eco-friendly and economic alternatives to synthetic surfactants with better characteristics. In proposed project, bacteria and fungi will be isolated from different sources (soil, water and rotten fruits) of AJK and Pakistan. These will be screened for biosurfactants production and positive strains will be identified on molecular basis. The production will be optimized by Response Surface Methodology (RSM) under Central Composite Design (CCD). Biosurfactants will be then purified by different techniques like solvent extraction and chromatography. The purified biosurfactants will be then subjected to structural and functional characterization.

data.projectName: Student Services and their Impacts on Students’ Academic Life in Public Sector Universities in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Previous research in the field of higher education in Pakistan, on the one side, reveals explicit dissatisfaction of faculty members and students from teaching-learning process and on the other side there is no evidence of the provision of standardized student services. The IASAS (2002), and Abu Hasan et al. (2008), strictly argue to provide students services in HEIs on the basis of public will. The services empower the students to expend more time on their studies and enable them to learn beyond the classroom. Student services available in universities build the foundations of student-university relationships on the grounds which are further than limited study periods of students (Baig & Khan, 2010). The current study is an attempt to evaluate the extent of availability and accessibility of students services in Pakistani universities. The role of provided services in students’ academic life will also be calculated to investigate the effectiveness/ineffectiveness of the services. The statement of the problem will be;
Analysis of Prevalent Student Services and their Impacts on students’ Academic Lives in Public Sector Universities in Pakistan

Analysis of Prevalent Student Services and their Impacts on students’ Academic Lives in Public Sector Universities in Pakistan

2)	Telecommunication
3)	Defence technology

data.projectName: Automated Blood Smear Stains Generation for Hemoparasites Detection and Classification
data.projectDigest:
Diseases due to the parasites are increasing on each successive day steadily and gradually . Most of the diseases are now predicted by the recognition of parasites in blood films. Image processing is an emerging field that play an significant role in the recognition and classification of parasites. Parasites are now detected with image processing by using the blood stain images. But the basic steps of creating the blood stain images are costly and time consuming. They also require the expertise of human and some technical requirements. The main process of creating the stain images is staining the blood smear. Different stain chemicals like the Wright’s, Giemsa and fields are used as stain to convert the blood smear into stain image.
Our proposed model will predict the stain image relevant to applied filter without using stain chemical. This model will train on blood smear images with stain images as labels. After training the successful training of the model, model will draw the stain image of blood smear without use of any stain chemical. Different stain filter will provide by our system and end-user will be capable to apply the different stains on a single click event. Model predicted stain image will be use for the detection and classification of parasites. A second model will train probably GAN or CNN for the recognition and classification of parasites from the produced stain image. Thus, our model will automate the staining process that required for the identification of parasite.
This totally automate system will overcome the cost and time that spent in generating the stain images from blood smear images for parasites detection. After the evaluation of the system, system will capable to deploy in laborites and hospital.

data.projectName: Cardiovascular effects of various extracts of Cannabis sativa cultivated in Pakistan-A preclinical study in rodents.
data.projectDigest: High blood pressure is a common health care challenge in Pakistan inspite of availability of effective drugs. As the therapy is lifelong, most of the patients do not want to take these drugs. On the one hand the costly drugs are out of the reach of the common people while on the other hand the side effects of the drugs are also troublesome. Thus there is a need to search for new drugs especially from natural resources which are relatively safe, economical and acceptable for the people. Plants have been the natural reservoir of so many drugs in the past. Cannabis sativa is one such plant with multiple effects. Limited research has been done to explore its potential as a blood pressure lowering agent. We expect that locally grown C. sativa has this property which should be utilized to develop novel anti-hypertensive medicine. The current research project is the first step in this direction in which plant extracts prepared from different parts of the plant will be tested on different laboratory animals to check its blood pressure lowering activity. Our research group at Aga Khan University is already working on other important aspects of the plant.

data.projectName: Determination of antibacterial effect of lactic acid bacteria on enteric pathogens and estimation of their adhesion properties to caco?2 cells
data.projectDigest: Gastrointestinal infections (GIT), one of the major causes of of human ailments account for high mortality rates annually, particularly in developing countries like Pakistan. The treatment of these infections is becoming a major challenge due to excessive use of antibiotics and developing antibiotic resistance of pathogens.  The emergence of multi drug resistant bacteria and super bugs involved in GIT infections is really becoming life threatening. Probiotics are those microbes which if consumed in sufficient amounts, impart beneficial effects to human health. Probiotics are supposed to be good candidates for prevention and treatment of drug resistant enteric pathogens. We want to investigate the hostile properties of Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) against enteric pathogens. Adhesion properties of LABs will also be estimated using Caco-2 cells and cytokine levels will be assessed which play crucial role in immune responses of intestinal tract.

data.projectName: To develop a  simple, reliable and cheap technique to uniformly embed crystalline solids of millimeter to  micrometer dimension  in different plastics. & to study  the physio chemical dynamics of the work
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The uniform embedding of solid particles of different materials in plastic bodies are one of the basic requirements for sample preparation and characterization of materials of interest. Material tests, and the applications which are sensitive to particle density , needs uniformity and homogeneity of embedding particles  in the body of embedding materials . For example ,composite materials , optical , electrical , magnetic and mechanical properties are greatly affected by the embedding material’s uniform dispersion . This project is aimed to study the parametric dynamics of different techniques that will be planned to embed crystalline solid particles of different dimensions in different plastics. The dynamics  of the parameters that determines the three dimensional distribution of different kinds and dimensions of particles in different plastic bodies  will be studied . Limitations and optimal conditions will be established for the techniques . The comparative study of particles distribution of different kinds and dimensions in different plastics will be used to get an insight in the chemical nature of the particles and plastics surface interaction under different conditions.

data.projectName: Co-digestion of Poultry Manure with Agricultural Crop Residues for Biogas and Bio-Fertilizer Production
data.projectDigest:
The main disposal method of straws in Pakistan is on-field burning which is causing smog pollution. In this regard, biogas technology (anaerobic digestion) offers attractive opportunity for waste remediation and recovery of resources.
Owing to the increased poultry farming, production of poultry manure (PM) has increased massively in Pakistan. The poultry farmers are facing a serious problem for its utilization or disposal that could be safe for the environment. To enhance biogas yield and produce bio-fertilizer with balanced nutrients and carbon and nitrogen ratio, co-digestion of PM and crop residue (straws) has pronouncedly higher potential for biogas compared to alone straw/PM anaerobic digestion.
Therefore, in proposed study, agriculture crop residues (corn straw, wheat straw, rice straw) to poultry manure ratios of 1:0, 0:1, 1:1, 2:1, 1:2, 3:1, and 1:3 will be used for biogas production under anaerobic digestion process. Quality parameters of crop residue such as crude protein, neutral detergent fibre (NDF), acid detergent fibre (ADF), lignin (ADL), ash contents and volatile solids (VS) will be determined using NIRS (Near Infra red spectroscopy). Similarly, characteristic of PM will be analyzed for chemical oxygen demand (COD), TS, VS, nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. Biogas will be measured by using methane simulator digesters. After digestion process digestate will be taken, dried and tested for the content of macro and microelements, ash contents, volatile solids and humus and feasibility for bio-fertilizer. The proposed research will not only be helpful to handle poultry manure waste and crop residue but also produce valuable products such as bio-energy and bio-fertilizer.

data.projectName: Improvement Of Brick Masonry Structures Against Seismic Forces By Using Modified Mortar
data.projectDigest:
Masonry is the one of the oldest building material that has still a large percentage in the building stock of both developing and developed countries [1]. As per the WHE Report 2013, more than 60% housing construction is of masonry and  is still the most popular building material particularly in developing countries due to its: easy handling and low costs in construction, good aesthetics view, effective heat and sound isolation, fire resistance and overall economical construction. Brick masonry buildings are prone to failure and collapse during major seismic events, representing one of the main causes of injuries and loss of human lives [1]. It is well known that brick masonry has good behavior under vertical compression while having low or negligible tensile strength. Using common types of bricks and mortar, failure due to lateral loads is almost due to weak tensile performance of mortar and high flexural stresses in masonry [1, 4].
Individually, bricks and mortar exhibit more strength as compared to their strength in assemblages [1, 4]. The reduction of strength of mortar in masonry is mostly due to: Shrinkage occurs in mortar, weak bond between bricks and mortar, less tensile strength at the interface of brick and mortar [2]. Earthquakes can cause the collapse of load bearing masonry walls, especially in buildings having relatively flexible floor diaphragms [3]. Beside all the weaknesses of brick masonry system, it is still in use in large amount, especially in developing country, because of its advantages as stated earlier.  Therefore, it is the need of time to make it stronger to resist extreme natural events like earthquake, windstorms, floods etc, by using traditional materials.

data.projectName: Analysis of Circulating Tumor Cells in Different types of Breast Cancer  for the prediction of Cancer Progression, Treatment Efficacy and Metastasis in Pakistani Population
data.projectDigest: Breast Cancer   has been the leading cause of death in women worldwide and unfortunately, and surprisingly the incidence and prevalence of breast cancer has increased enormously in Pakistan over a decade. Most of the patients ultimately die due to the spread of the disease to other body organs called metastasis. Biopsy still remains an important investigation for the diagnosis of breast cancer but it is not only painful and having side effects but also did not tell the pathologists and oncologists about the evolution of tumor and its metastatic potential. Isolation and enumeration of circulating tumor cells (CTCs)[Circulating Tumor cells are the ones which  are detached from tumor and circulate in the blood], has recently been surfaced as a breakthrough liquid biopsy technique which will give information about breast cancer progression .  Secondly, spread of the cancer to different sites leads to difficult treatments and untimely deaths.   Keeping in view of the ease of sampling over different time-points during chemotherapy for breast cancer, we will try to uncover the metastatic potential of breast cancer, in order to enhance our ability to detect metastasis early. This will further enhance the ability to devise targeted therapies accordingly

data.projectDigest: The incidence and prevalence of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease as well as oropharyngeal and lung cancers remains high in Pakistan, especially among tobacco smokers and industrial workers. Thus, this project would enable us to validate our proposed gene signature underlying increased risk of chronic inflammatory lung disease as well as cancers of mouth and respiratory tract secondary to tobacco smoke and environmental pollutants.

data.projectName: Molecular markers based genetic characterization of Major Carps fishery stocks for effective management and conservation
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: Fishery and aquaculture sectors play an important role in the economy of a country. The Major carps fish species, including Cirrhinus mrigala, Labeo rohita and Catla catla are widely distributed in aquatic reservoirs of Indo-Pakistan. These fish species have great commercial significance due to their aquaculture prospective and high consumer preference. In Pakistan, fish production in both natural and captive stocks is declining each year due to poor genetic management and has become a significant problem. Due to poor genetic management, fish survival, growth and fecundity rate decreases which results in low fish production. Genetic approaches can be used effectively in the fisheries sector to resolve various challenges. A little attention has been paid to Pakistan's aquatic genetic resource research, management and conservation. The level of genetic variation and genetic differentiation among and within populations must be recognized to manage any biological resource effectively. Genetic variation permits species to respond to the selection and breeding programs. It also allows to fish populations to adapt the changing environmental conditions. Information regarding the genetic structure of these fish populations is needed for the effective management and conservation of natural and captive fishery resources.

data.projectName: Numerical Study of Settling Non-Spherical Particles in a Newtonian Media
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: Settling particles are vital for the process industries. In every process industry, waste water is being treated either for further use or to drain it. In this treatment process, sedimentation is one of the cheapest and simple processes to remove solids from water. Sedimentation is also widely used in the drinking water treatment, in which water flows to sedimentation basin, where gravity causes the flocs to settle to the bottom. Apart from water treatment process, settling particles play key roles in emulsion, paper and pulp, and pharmaceutical industry. More recently, these suspended particles are also investigated in the drug delivery to cancer patients. In addition, it is also one of fundamental problem of Physics, which is perplexing in nature, because of long range hydrodynamics interactions and particle-particle interactions, where former depend on the shape of particles and the flow regime and latter, on the shape of particles, its position in the tank, concentration and flow regime. With the presence of many parameters that strongly influence the settling dynamics, it is difficult to present a unified theory.  Hence, despite the many investigations, there are still many open problems. This work in intended to present a unified solution to the non-spherical particles.

data.projectName: Evaluatio of selected Capsaicin-Receptor (TRPV1) Antagonists in neuropathic pain models: A behavioral, pharmacokinetic and histopathological study.
data.piUniversity: CECOS University of Information Technology and Emerging Sciences, Peshawar
data.projectDigest: Neuropathy is the most prevalent, persistent and debilitating complication of diseases like diabetes and cancer. Numerous controlled studies have demonstrated potential effectiveness of opioid, tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs), gabapentin, pregabalin, phenytoin, lamotrigine, dextromethorphan, tramadol and mexiletine for painful sensory neuropathy. However, these therapies result in a 30-50 % reduction in pain and are often restricted due to significant side effects, sedation being the most dominant. This project is designed to focus on a novel target that is capsaicin-receptor antagonism or Vanilloid-receptors antagonists, having the potential of treating neuropathic pain via anti-inflammatory mechanisms. The selected compounds will be evaluated in diabetes, chemotherapy and surgery- induced animal models of neuropathic pain. von Frey filaments will be used to test the different neuropathic pain conditions. Diabetes-induced neuropathic pain rat model will be established by injecting a single intraperitoneal injection of streptozotocin (50 mg/kg) to 12 hours fasted rats. 7 days after streptozotocin administration, animals with blood glucose level greater than 120 mg/100 mL will be selected for study. Chemotherapy induced neuropathic pain model will be established by administering cisplatin intraperitoneally (i.p) once a week at a dose of 3 mg/kg (cumulative dose, 15 mg/kg) for 5 weeks. The selected compounds will also be evaluated in a surgery-induced neuropathy model. Pharmacokinetic investigations will be conducted to explore the uptake of these drugs in plasma and brain tissues.

data.projectDigest:
To study the fundamental  particles having small dimensions, we need very high energy. The study of elementary particles at very high energy  may give us answers to many important questions; like what is matter made off? How it is confined? From where  the mass of matter comes from? To resolve these questions , to study the physics of early universe and what happen after the big bang, we need very high energy. The high energy must to equivalent to that which was present after the big bang. The energy of the order of TeV are required to answer these questions. and this range of energy is provided by the Large Hadron collider (LHC), based in CERN, Switzerland. A dedicated experiment based on LHC called ALICE provides the information about the physics of quark gluon plasma, a stater of matter just after the big bang.  ALICE is a dedicated experiment to study the physics of heavy ion collision. 
In this project we are focused to study different observables which are responsible to explore the Quark Gluon Plasma.  To study the ion ions, it is necessary to study the baseline which is provided by analysis of proton proton collision. Thus we are offering a complete project, where the analysis will start from proton- proton to proton-nucleus,nucleus nucleus and Xenon -Xenon collisions.

data.projectName: GENETIC AND FUNCTIONAL ELUCIDATION OF THE UNDERLYING MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF MULTIFACTORIAL EYE DISORDER; GLAUCOMA
data.projectDigest:
This study is designed to investigate the underlying genetic causes of  glaucoma, in the Pakistani population. The ratio of consanguinity is  highest in Pakistan as compared to the other countries. It is a multifactorial, complex and genetically heterogeneous disease, therefore, understanding its genetic mechanism is important for designing better therapeutics and diagnostic interventions. 
The linkage analysis of the families presented with glaucoma as well as case-control association analysis will be conducted. Preliminary analysis will be carried out on the affected families. The excluded families will be further analyzed by whole exome sequencing. Functional analysis, pre-symptomatic carrier testing and case control association studies will be carried out for individuals identification at risk. SNPs previously present in other populations as well as  pathogenic variants from exome sequence of familial data will be selected and screened to check their disease association. Statistical test will be applied to check SNPs association with the disease. 
This study is expected to explain possible novel genetic causes of familial glaucoma.  Moreover, the rare variants and SNPs in oxidative stress, complement and inflammatory pathway will help in depicting disease etiology. This will help in development of molecular diagnostic tools for identifying individuals at risk of disease development.

data.projectName: Prevalence of seed-borne viruses in Pakistan and their management through integrated approach
data.projectDigest: Seed-borne viruses are an important factor resulting in yield reduction of several important crops including vegetables and legumes. When the virus-infected seeds are sown, the emerging plants will be infected with the virus. Major problem with virus-infested seeds is virus infection in seeds is not easily visible. Cucumber mosaic virus, Tomato mosaic virus (ToMV), Pea early browning virus (PEBV) and Pea seed-borne mosaic (PSbMV) are different seed-borne viruses which are transmitted through seeds. Seed-borne virus diseases have become an important problem in vegetables and legumes. Seed-borne viruses are carried on seeds either internally inside the seed embryo or they are present on seed surface. If the seeds are tested before planting for the presence of virus, these viruses can be controlled to a great extent. Unfortunately, no work has been done regarding seed-borne viruses in Pakistan and this project will address this important problem. Under this project, incidence of these seed-borne viruses will be determined, their genetic characterization will be done and integrated management strategies will be developed. Seed certification standards will be established for seed transmitted viruses. Seed-transmitted viruses may serve as carryover of virus from one season to the next inspite of adopting app precautionary measures.

data.projectName: The effect of Liberal narrative on students' perception of terrorism
data.projectDigest: This key objective of this research is to determine the effect of national security narrative on students’ perception of terrorism. It is extremely important to determine the effect of national security narrative on general population and students in particular. There is already widespread criticism of Pakistan’s national security narrative in western academia and media that it is supporting terrorism in the country. Through this study, it will determine two things; firstly, it will determine the claim of western media, whether it is true or not that national security narrative in Pakistan support terrorism. Secondly it will also recommend a new national security narrative that does not only meet the security demands of the country, but also meet the threat of terrorism. It is extremely important to determine various aspects of national narratives, because they are closely associated with the national security of the country, which is the supreme value of the state. Building a coherent national security strategy is basically based on sound national security narrative. If there are conflicts between the various components of national narratives, it will be very difficult to design a strategy to meet the objectives of national security. In other words, national security of the country depends on the strength of security narrative.

data.projectName: Molecular interpretation of Post Trauma Stress disorders (PTSD) in tribal districts (North Waziristan and South Waziristan) of Kyber Pakhtoonkhwa (KPK)
data.projectDigest:
Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a prevailing and hindering anxiety condition causing   foremost health care trouble in the system. Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) come about subsequent to traumatic event exposure and recognized by discrete symptom clusters of re-experiencing, evading and deadening, and simulative prolongation for more than 1 month after trauma (1). Till now, research concentrating identification of precise genetic loci accounting for the moderate heritability is not satisfactory and this question remains unclear.  
Waziristan is a mountainous region of wazir tribe lying in the northwest of Pakistan with Afghanistan border.  The proposed area is unique in social and religious conservation. During 2004 to 2016, this area was under the influence of terrorism and different antiterrorism operations were launched. Exposure of the study area to such long time exposure has introduced symptoms of major depression and behavioral problems in the residents. The aims of the present study are to identify genetic factors responsible for PTSD in population of proposed area using Genome-wide association studies (GWAS). This study will help in promotion of current understanding about PTSD etiologies and better present and future management.

data.projectName: Some novel algebraic techniques to generate robust substitution boxes and their applications in image encryption
data.projectDigest: Substitution-boxes are crucial components in today’s mathematical cryptography. Modern block ciphers have been relying on potent S-boxes to fulfill the security requirements in different real-world areas of applications. An S-box utilized in block ciphers should have strong cryptographic strength so as to mitigate different attacks for better robustness and strength. There is no obvious distribution in the cryptographic properties of S-boxes, which is the main difficulty in constructing S-boxes. The development of new techniques to generate substitution-boxes has become an important area of present-day research.  This project is focused on the emergence of new algebraic-based innovative methods to evolve cryptographically secure S-boxes. We also use our generated S-boxes in image encryption applications to show their worth.

data.projectName: Managerial analysis of polio campaign in Pakistan: A Grounded theory analysis of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
data.projectDigest:
Poliovirus is resurgent in Pakistan again. It has raised its ugly head after four years of near reported eradication figure. The single digit figure of polio case incidence now stands at 139 with 70% occurrence in KPK. This is a huge sign of shame for the overall governance structure in general and the health infrastructure of Pakistan in particular. The old age excuses of blaming the religious extremism, hard to reach terrorism hit areas , unchecked cross border movements and problems in maintaining the polio vaccines will not more be valid in the view of international community anymore
This study argues that the failure of health institutions of Pakistani in eradicating polio virus must be understood through the four basic functions of management i.e. planning, organizing, leading and controlling. Going back to drawing board is utmost important at this stage as this study contends that the problem lies in the very basic organizational structure and without finding and taking remedial action polio eradication campaign is a lost cause. 
This study is unique in the sense that it envisages the stakeholder approach to take account of all the important opinions and understand their collective effect on the polio virus eradication campaign.

data.projectName: Identification of genetic mutations causing human male infertility in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
Parenthood is the basic right and a desire for every married couple. This desire is interrupted by any problem in which the couples fail to conceive after 2 years of marriage. The reproductive capacity is the under the control of many factors including body composition, hormonal regulation, genetics and/or environmental factors. In males, the defects process of sperm formation may lead to qualitative and/or quantitative abnormalities leading to male factor infertility. The male factor infertility is 20 to 70% and about half of them are genetic in nature. The infertile couples face social pressure of childbearing in our society which adversely affect their physical, physiological and social health. 
Despite of the fact, Pakistan is among highly populous countries with higher fertility rate. The number of infertile couples has increased in recent years. This project intends to find out the genetic basis of infertility in Pakistan. For this purpose, the infertile individuals will be recruited after clinical and laboratory examination. The genes causing infertility will be identified through Next Generation Sequencing and pathogenic variants will be validated through sanger sequencing. The study may be helpful in clinical management of patients with infertility and provide genetic counselling to families at risk.

data.projectName: Soft computing based on artificial neural networks for optimal decisions in energy production systems
data.projectDigest:
This project aims to provide practical applications of Soft Computing (SC) techniques involving Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) and state-of-the-art metaheuristics to handle optimization problems arising in thermal, green, renewable, and hybrid energy production systems to fulfill the optimal load dispatch to its consumers, considering case studies from Pakistan. 
 By finding optimal solutions to real-life case studies, it will help reduce the critical environmental, social, and economic issues in the country. Renewable energy is one of the key backup energy sources. These sources include hydrogen, biomass, sunlight, rain, wind, to name a few. Problems arising in these sectors are often with a high degree of uncertainties, non-linearity, computationally-expensive, and involving complex landscapes. 
 We will suggest mathematical models for our case studies, and several algorithmic procedures will be adopted to calculate optimal solutions for decision-making. Our findings will help policy setters, scientists, economists, and sectoral collaborators in their applications. We will design and implement soft computing approaches, such as heuristics and systems, artificial neural science and systems, Nature-inspired algorithms and their hybrids, and novel machine learning algorithms, with an objective to obtain solutions with lower costs, by considering random data with noises and uncertainties. 
 Robustness and accuracy of our approaches will be tested by simulating our experiments for different real-life data and multiple times. Our outcome will be compared with the solutions obtained by existing classical techniques.

data.projectName: Efficient Environment Monitoring by Doped Metal Oxide Gas Sensors
data.projectDigest:
Metal Oxides (MOX) nanomaterials are the most common active materials being used for detecting toxic/harmful gases[1], environment monitoring of air pollution and order nuisance, plant’s emissions, for home safety, comfort and security (to detect explosives and warfare agents), medical diagnostics (breath analysis) for early disease detection, manufacturing and quality assurance of food industry, aerospace to monitor air quality and several industrial process[8]. Such materials show high stability and low manufacturing costs, while exhibit good sensitivity as compared to other materials being used for the purpose. ZnO and SnO2 are most studied materials as compared to other n-type MOX materials. Other MOX materials being used for gas detection are TiO2, WO, CuO, Fe2O3, In2O3, NiO, CoO and others. 

This project is focused on Synthesis of Metal Oxide Nanomaterials, Followed by Characterization of Physical and Electrical properties to use for potential chemical sensing (gas/ other) applications.

data.projectName: Morphology and Image Processing of Sunspots
data.piUniversity: Sir Syed University of Engg. & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Mathematical morphology is the theory and technique for the analysis and processing of geometrical structures and for describing shapes using set theory, lattice theory, topology, and random functions. It is used to analysis the evolution of images. In image processing, mathematical morphology is used to investigate the interaction between an image and a certain chosen structuring element using the basic operations of erosion and dilation. This study deals with the image processing of largest active regions of 24 sunspots cycle and forecast evolution of sunspot cycles by using Time series analysis. The outcome will be used to forecast the evolution of sunspots cycles.

data.projectName: Examining the Association of the Spatial Layout with Quality of Life to harness sustainable cities (A case study of Lahore)
data.projectDigest:
The high vehicle-miles, insufficient level of services, sprawling cities and deteriorating air quality are challenges to conventional urban development.  New urban Planning strategies are believed to address current challenges. The spatial layout and fabrication of the land uses effects the quality of urban life significantly.Inarticulate land-uses with change in land-use policies increased trip generation in Lahore tremendously. Consequently, reliance on the motor vehicles has increased proportionately.  Land use planning of the city, merely, focuses on the spatial arrangements of land uses with a segregated layout. Inappropriate changes in the land uses in the form of commercialization policy (change in land uses policy) increase the trips generation and put an extra load to traffic infrastructure facilities. Improper spatial layout without master concept not only endanger urban environment, but also deteriorate the quality of the life. There is a gap in spatial planning, spatial policies and practices which is due to poor comprehension of the quality of urban life and its relationship with the spatial layout.
The research will sensitize land uses to enhance the quality of the life in big cities of Pakistan.It serves as a model towards the new urban planning approaches in Pakistan

data.projectName: Determination of host and viral genetic factors influencing the HIV progression and treatment in Pakistani patients.
data.piUniversity: Liaquat University of Medical and Health Sciences, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest: HIV infection has emerged as pandemic, in different regions of Pakistan, especially in Sindh province. It has been reported in clusters of population of different areas. Though, the HIV management programs are in action, but lake of awareness and education among masses has elevated the infection. The recent scientific discoveries have shown that genetic element of infected patients and genetic components of virus have mutual role in the disease manifestation and success rate of treatment. Pakistani population is genetically heterogeneous and the previous research has shown the obvious genetic difference among Pakistani and other world population. The present available HIV management/treatment strategies may not be successful, without the revelation of associated genetic profiles of the Pakistani patients and corresponding molecular makeup of virus. This study aim to determine the role of genetic variations of genes involved in the human immune system or interacts with pathogens of Pakistani patients and the role of genetic variation, essential for pathogenicity in the viral genes. This study will be carried out in three phases. In Phase one, the HIV infected patients will be enrolled and HIV related clinical data will be collected. The type of HIV and viral loads will be determined. In second phase, the host and viral genes will be sequenced for identification of potential variants associated to disease progression and treatment outcome. In third phase, based on the results of previous two phases, the selected host samples will be subjected to whole genome sequencing. The results may help to identify the ethnic based host genetic variations responsible for HIV disease progression and the information about the treatment and resistance to drugs as well.

data.projectName: Who's Carrying Guns? Localizing firearms and armed person in low resolution CCTV footage
data.projectDigest:
Gun violence incidents  (e.g. Christchurch mosque shooting, school shootings in Pakistan) are wide spread across the globe and are being observed at increasing frequency. Governments and private security entities have been expanding the use of CCTV based surveillance systems to monitor and secure buildings (banks, ATM), important public places (parks, shopping malls) and events. However, recent mass shooting events indicate the need of  augmenting human operators with automatic detection of firearms to  decrease the response time of authorities. Unfortunately, no significant research work has been done on firearms detection or localizing the people carrying firearms, much hampered by the non-existence of the reasonable dataset.

This project aims to develop a mechanism for the firearm detection and localizing armed personnel visible in the CCTV footage. Firearms in the realistic CCTV scenarios are small objects, often partially occluded by the carrier or others. The low-quality of the videos and motion blur makes their detection even more difficult. We intend to explore Human Object Interaction for creating an attention mechanism in order to do the video-based object detection. 

To help our research we will be collecting a large video dataset with people carrying firearms. We will be emphasizing that the dataset should also contain the people with local dresses and videos in local settings, to remove the bias.
