data.projectName: Fabrication and characterization of Cu doped nanoparticles for Solar Cell applications
data.projectDigest:
Zinc oxide is a versatile material and known to have a direct band gap of 3.37 eV at room temperature and has distinguishable performance in electronics, optics and photonics . Among the semiconductor nanoparticles, zinc oxide is an important semiconductor, which has been researched extensively. It also used as a catalyst. It has various high tech applications, such as optical devices, solar cells, piezoelectric devices, surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices, and gas sensors.
The purpose of this research is to prepare the zinc oxide nanoparticles, study the structure and optical properties. In order to decrease the energy gap, dopant of ZnO nanoparticles with different copper concentrations will be used so that it can be used in the manufacturing of solar cells.

data.projectName: Scientific exploration of medicinal plants for their anti-arthritic potential using in-vivo and in-vitro techniques
data.projectDigest: Medicinal plants have a great importance in natural flora. It has been used traditionally to treat rheumatism since decades. The scientific evidence of anti-rheumatic effect of most of herbal plant has not been validated yet. On the basis of Folkloric value of these plants against Rheumatoid Arthritis, the current study will be aimed to assess the useful of these plants in rheumatoid arthritis by using in vitro and in vivo techniques. Membrane stabilization of red blood cells and inhibition of denaturation of protein techniques will be employed for in-vitro studies and egg albumin induced paw edema, formaldehyde induced arthritis and Complete freund Adjuvant Arthritic models for in-vivo studies. It will be indispensable to explore the development of plant based drugs. Furthermore, phytochemical analysis will be carried out using TLC, LC-MS and HPLC standard techniques for identification of possible bio actives.

data.projectName: Utilization of Agro-industrial by-products to produce conditioned broiler meat and eggs (Omega-3 rich)
data.projectDigest: The current project is developed keeping into account the undernourished and poor health conditions of Pakistan inhabitants especially women and children. Considering the high consumption of low-quality less consumption of essential fatty acids especially omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids that are the precursors of other essential fatty acids like eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosapentaenoic acid (DHA) those are important for the brain development of children. Incorporation of agro-industrial by-products (pomegranate seed residue that is enriched source of omega-3 fatty acid) is an intelligent way to utilize the industrial by-products and take the benefits from these waste materials and reduce the environmental pollution created by their dispose. Pomegranate seed residues will improve the nutritional status, antioxidant potential, fatty acid profile of broiler meat and eggs. This project will be an important step of biotechnical intervention to incorporate the omega-2 fatty acid in broiler meat and eggs and will help to fulfill the objectives like development of an economical feed by utilizing the agro-industrial by-products, to appraise the influence of developed feed (Omega-3 enriched) on productive performance, antioxidant stability, eggs and meat quality of experimental animals, to evaluate the any toxicity/limitation of developed feed (Omega-3 enriched). This kind of study will help the poultry industry to utilize the economical feeding ingredients with better health benefits of consumers.

data.projectName: Biodegration of Plastic By locally isolated Microbial strains
data.projectDigest: Plastics  are  synthetic  or  organic  polymers,  extensively used in day to day life in almost every  aspect of life. Plastics are lightweight, strong, durable, and cheap, characteristics that make them suitable for the manufacture of a very wide range of products. Ever year eight million tones of plastic entering our oceans Polyethylene terephthalate. Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is mainly used for production of PET bottles, PET foil, and fibers in the textile industry. Plastic bags typically are made from polyethylene compounds. The shopping bags are one of the major . More then 2.0 million tons of plastic waste is produced annually in Pakistan. Currently, only a few bacteria and fungi have been described for the partial degradation of PET to oligomers or monomers.  In Pakistan not much basic research is done on the isolation of novel bacterial strains for plastic biodegradation. It is suggested that Isolate and culture potential plastic degrading bacteria from a diversity of environments and test their ability to degrade plastic-associated compounds under a broad range of conditions. Sequence the genomes of microbial isolated having the ability to degrade plastic, to elucidate novel genes and pathways for plastic degradation. Identification of novel organisms, genes and enzymes capable of degrading plastics in the environment will provide new tools to aid the degradation of plastic in the environment and within waste treatment streams.

data.projectName: COMPARATIVE STUDIES OF NEURO-IMMUNOLOGICAL PARAMETERS IN PATIENTS OF E.N.T, ONCOLOGY, GENERAL MEDICINE AND CARDIOLOGY
data.projectDigest: Neuro-immunological parameters help to find out depression, behavior deficit and mood changing with severity of allergic conditions and also factors on which these markers depend.  These markers might be disturbed in patients of E.N.T, oncology, general medicine and cardiology as our team had observed in ear infection (CSOM) patients in past. The aim of the study is to observe these chemicals which may also help to find outcomes of the current treatment according to the condition or disease of patient. For this purpose, we will use a questionnaire and blood test without any charges to the patient or any discomfort (6000 patients in total in all). It is expected that level of depression and inflammatory markers will be very high (except in general medicine where we may have patients with normal or slightly high depression). The comparison of these markers may help to find which treatment or strategy is beneficial for patients physical cure (according to the diagnosed disease in the respective ward) alongwith the mental health (for depression and allergic parameters).

data.projectName: Towards an Artificial Intelligence based Framework for Automated Screening of Patients with Psychiatric Disorders
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
Psychiatric disorders such as depression and schizophrenia are critical healthcare issues, which affect a large number of people. Depression, according to the World Health Organization, is the largest cause of disability worldwide and affects more than 300 million people. Similarly, schizophrenia affects more than 20 million people worldwide. Not only do these disorders adversely affect the quality of life of affected individuals, they also have a significant economic impact.

Pakistan as a country is currently suffering from a serious mental health crisis. According to the WHO, more than 24 million inhabitants (out of the 200 million) in the country require psychiatric assistance. However, there are on average only 0.19 psychiatrists per 100,000 people – one of the lowest psychiatrist-to-population ratios in the world.

In the proposed NRPU project, we seek to undertake research towards the development of an Artificial Intelligence (AI) based framework for automated screening methods for patients with psychiatric disorders. We envisage that such systems can initially assist psychiatrists in screening patients for depression and schizophrenia, but given enough data to train the AI, such systems can also function independently. This proposal is continuation of the Principal Investigator’s doctoral research on AI assisted human behavior understanding. Thus, it provides a pathway to conduct cutting-edge research in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Theoretical and Experimental Studies of Quantum Key Distribution
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest:
Cryptography, the art of encryption of messages and data, is one of the basic concerns in the field of communication to preserve data integrity and confidentiality. Quantum cryptography guarantees the security of the optical communication system because the “cipher-text” generated using quantum key cannot be decoded by any interceptor. The method that generates this quantum key and distributes it to the receiver, is commonly known as “Quantum Key Distribution” (QKD).
The fundamental challenge of all cryptography methods is to ensure that only Alice (sender) and Bob (receiver) know the encryption key. In the proposed project, BB84 encryption protocol developed by Charles Bennett and Gilles Brassard will be used for quantum key generation. One major advantage of using this protocol is its inherited capability for detection of an interception attack by a third party i.e., eavesdropper known as “Eve”.
This project will focus not only towards theoretical but also experimental studies related to quantum key distribution. We would like to study different theoretical schemes for discrete variable and continuous variable quantum key distribution. The plan is to study how high transmission rate can be achieved in the presence of different noise sources at long distance quantum key distribution.

data.projectName: In vitro and in vivo coal dust induced cytogenetic toxicity studies
data.projectDigest: Coal mining is one of the most important economic activities in many countries. Throughout the entire coal mining procedures including handling and transportation, coal dust emissions take place. These coal dust emissions are composed of various polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), toxic heavy metals with varying concentrations of iron and sulphur. PAHs such as benz(a)anthracene, chrysene, benzo(a)pyrene and various heavy metals, being major constituents of coal dust, can lead to DNA damage and carcinogenesis. Our investigations involve analyzing the rate of deposition of coal dust along with its direct and indirect effects on human population. This project will also cover various epidemiological surveys of coal mines and community regarding various health issues. This project will emphasize on genetic damage caused by coal dust emissions both in mines and in community. Our studies will be a modest contribution to access the mine labour working conditions, labour problems and other health related issues. The approach described here will be much more useful, simpler and cost less money as it will not only examine miners genetic damage but also would be helpful in developing mine safety and monitoring authority making assure human friendly as well as bio-friendly environment.

data.projectName: Effect of soil stabilizaing and reinforcing agents on the dynamic characteristics of soil
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Dynamic loads such as from earthquake, traffic movement, winds, waves etc. are the major sources of large scale deformations of civil engineering infrastructure. During dynamic loading natural soil is subjected to cyclic shear stresses at different amplitudes and frequencies that will induce transient and permanent deformations in the soil. In case of the soft soils, soil improvement is made through stabilization and reinforcement prior to civil engineering infrastructure construction. The effect of soil stabilizing and reinforcing agents on the dynamic properties of soft soils has little been addressed in the literature. This study is focused on the effect of soil stabilizing and reinforcing agents on the dynamic properties of soil. For this purpose laboratory investigations will be carried out on the soil samples modified with stabilizing and reinforcing agents. The modified soil samples thereafter will be investigated through static (Triaxial ) and dynamic loading ( resonant column and dynamic triaxial testing setups). The anticipated outcomes would be of significance for the engineers and construction industry of conventional and rapid mass transit system. This research will provide a relationship between academia with construction industry.

data.projectName: Organocatalytic 2+2 Cycloaddition for Dream Green Synthesis of Acrylic Acid
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: This project is based on the innovative idea for the synthesis of acrylic acid from cheap and renewable sources in environmentally friendly conditions. Based on these facts this will be the challenging green chemistry project. Acrylic acid the extremely valuable chemical intermediate had wider applications in paint, textiles, polymers, and lots of industrial and consumer products. The commercial methodis expensive as compared to the proposed project. The challenging product will be obtained by the organocatalyzed cycloaddition of CO2 with ethylene to yield propiolactone the precursor for acrylic acid. After organocatalyzed 2+2 cycloaddition the propiolactone will be formed and the seconds step will be the treatment of propiolactone with phosphoric acid to yield acrylic acid. This present invention used the less expensive feedstock. This competitive protocol will produce quantitative acrylic acid by decreasing the operating costs involved due to the use of renewable sources in green environment. Large scale production of acrylic acid for commercial scale will be done after the interviews and business dealing with stakeholders and after successful deal this designed project will contribute for economic benefits of third world countries.

data.projectName: Utilization of fruit and vegetable bio-wastes for the management of PSE meat: a persistent problem in broiler meat industry of Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Pale, soft and exudative (PSE) meat causes the yield losses of about PKR 14.5 billion per annum in the broiler meat industry of Pakistan. PSE meat exhibits inferior product developmental attributes and lower consumer acceptability. The inability of the broilers to withstand acute stress is its major cause. Moreover, the fruit and vegetable biowastes (FVW) of Pakistan worth about PKR 544 billion per annum and cause significant environmental degradation. The immunity of the broilers can be improved by the bioactive compounds derived from FVWs. The previously published reports suggest that FVWs improve growth performance, but the control of PSE through FVWs is yet to be investigated. 

This project, therefore, intends PSE management through the integration of bioactive compounds of FVWs into broiler feed. Moreover, the effects of the bioactive compounds on the structures and functions of myofibrillar proteins, product development, and shelf-life will be assessed. Finally, the market and consumer acceptability of this technology will be determined. 

The expected outcomes include the control of PSE, reduction of yield loss, and improvement of consumer acceptability of broiler meat; enhancement of the profitability for the meat industry; enhancement of environmental sustainability and augmentation of the circular economy through sustainable development.

data.projectDigest: The main purpose of this proposal is to propose new models containing Langevin equations and to investigate the existence, uniqueness and generalized Ulam--Hyers--Rassias stability of their solutions. First, we want to study the existence, uniqueness and generalized Ulam--Hyers--Rassias stability of solutions of impulsive Langevin equation involving fractional order derivatives with nonlocal integral boundary condition.  After creating a linear framework, a direct method is applied for the solutions of aforesaid models and then discuss their existence, uniqueness and generalized Ulam--Hyers--Rassias stability. Finally, we extend our ideas to a switched coupled system of impulsive fractional Langevin equations and then find the existence and generalized Ulam--Hyers--Rassias stability. The main tools for obtaining our results are Diaz--Margolis's fixed point theorem, generalized complete matric space and Picard operator. For our results, some assumptions are made along with Lipschitz conditions. Some examples are also presented that support our obtained results.

data.projectName: Development  of graphene reinforced hydrogels  for applications in enzyme based biosensors
data.projectDigest: Enzyme based biosensors are one of the largest and successful group of biosensors due to their high sensitivity, ease of use, low cost, fast and eco friendly monitoring of analytes. Selection of appropriate enzyme, immobilization technique, support, electron transport media are the important factors which decide the sensitivity, stability, detection limit and reproducibility of a biosensor. Immobilization of enzyme on a suitable support is a crucial step as enzyme needs suitable environment for its proper functioning under different conditions. Hydrogels are attractive materials for enzyme immobilization due to their biocompatible microenvironment, which can enhance the activity and stability of enzymes. However one hurdle in implementation of hydrogels is their low mechanical and electrical properties. Graphene owing to its unique physical and electrical properties can overcome these issues. In this study graphene oxide and reduced graphene oxide nanoparticles will be synthesized and reinforced in the hydrogels which will be used to entrap the enzyme. Graphene channels present in the hydrogels are expected to enhance the mechanical strength and bioelectronic signal. For this study laccase enzyme will be used as model enzyme system for the detection of phenolic compounds (dyes, drugs and pesticides etc) in food, water and soil samples.

data.projectName: Deciphering resistant pattern of mobilized colistin gene of multidrug resistant salmonella enterica using transcriptomic analysis.
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Prophylactic and therapeutic use of colistin has widely been employed for animal production. It also has been used as a last line of defense against multidrug resistant (MDR) organism such as Salmonella enterica (S. enterica) in humans. However, a little is known regarding potential transmission of mobilized colistin resistant (mcr) genes from animals to humans or vice-versa and detailed molecular characterization of these genes in Pakistan. The proposed study will involve in the detection of plasmid-mediated mcr genes of S. enterica isolates originating from both poultry and human. S. enterica isolates will be confirmed by conventional bacteriological and biochemical identification kit system (API-10S) followed by phenotypic characteristics evaluation for resistance to colistin. The resistant isolates will be screened for the presence of mcr genes and sequenced. Phylogenetic analysis will be conducted to determine the evolutionary relationship of mcr genes among poultry and human isolates. Furthermore, Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) will also be performed because it will help in identifying the factors, molecular changes and metabolic process involved in the development of colistin resistance in S. enterica.  Hence, findings of present study will not only provide current status of colistin resistance in humans but also provide information regarding possible transmission of mcr genes from poultry to humans. Additionally, this study will spread awareness in poultry producers and physicians to minimize the irrational use of colistin.

data.projectName: Establishment of Invasive Breast Cancer Cell Line of Pakistani Origin and Identification of Anti-cancer Peptides of Least Toxicity from Snake Venom: “Finding Cure in the Habitat”.
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Breast cancer is the second major cause of cancer related deaths after lung cancer in females. Cancer cell lines has emerged as one of the potential tool in understanding underlying mechanisms, as well as in find cure. Different cancer cell lines has been reported derived from Pakistani cancer patients, but unfortunately none of them has been taken into consideration for drug discovery. Many of anti-cancer drugs work only in patients of specific populations. Therefore, there is continuous need to develop new drugs that could work independently or in combination with current approved drugs with minimal side effects. The snake venom derived drugs have been used since ages to treat various ailments such as hypertension, diabetes, cardiovascular in Ayurveda and Chinese traditional medicine. Snake venom and its components are found to mainly inhibit cell growth and promote cell death. The anticancer potential of venoms from Pakistani species remains obscure. Therefore, purposed study is aimed to establish invasive breast cancer cell lines of Pakistani origin, to explore the anticancer potential of the indigenous Cobra venom, hopefully improving overall survival rate with least or no side effects. This study will be conducted at the Dow University of Health Sciences.

data.projectName: Study & Analysis of Pakistan’s Gemstones Mining Practices and Recommendations with aim to Increase Gemstones Exports
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan, most of the gemstone mining is carried out with traditional mining techniques. Individual miners or group of miners dig and search for these precious stone using old tools and traditional drill and blast method. During mining, which is done manually or by small blasting, 40 to 50 percent of the value of the stones is lost. When stones mined by blasting are cut, there is good probability of damage and cracks from inside. Many gems are sold unpolished and in uncut form and are processed in Thailand or India. Traditional mining tools, lack of investment in infrastructure, non-efficient mining techniques, lack of skills in miners, absence of cutting/polishing facilities, lack of modern marketing, absence of cutting/polishing trained personals are major hurdle for Pakistan to be a significant player in the international gem industry. The proposed project will focus on improving the mining techniques to enhance the quality and value of the gemstones being mined. The efforts will be made to introduce new mining tools to the miners. Another main goal is to develop the technical knowledge and skills of miners and their capacity building in gemstone sector. Research aim to add value to Pakistan gemstone market by conducting study on availability of cutting polishing skilled labor and facilities and its impact on gemstone exports of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Evaluation of Antiinflammatory Potential of Camel milk Derived proteins and peptides via modulation of NF?b/MAPK Pathways
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Inflammation is the normal mechanism of host immune response against harmful stimuli, such as microbes, toxic compounds damaged cells or any other foreign agent. It comprises cells and molecules of both innate and adaptive immune systems.  It principally works by removing damaging stimuli and initiating the remedial process in the host. Unnecessary production of proinflammatory mediators during inflammation lead to develop various inflammatory diseases like rheumatoid arthritis, diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease, bowel disease, cancer.  Treatment of choice for inflammatory diseases include steroidal and non- steroidal antiinflammatory agents which are mainly associated with gastrointestinal disturbance, hepatic and renal toxicities. Modern development has been using biologicals and small molecules for anti-inflammatory therapeutics for targeted modulation of endogenous signaling mediators. Therefore, discipline of alternative medicine is getting popularity and use of herbal medicine is increasing by the time. Camel milk is known to have wonderful nutritional and medicinal values including anti inflammatory activities. Camel milk possesses 3-3.9% of total proteins. The proposed study is based on investigating anti inflammatory potential of the camel milk proteins derived peptides with selective molecular mechanism by modulating the signaling molecules of NF?B or MAPK pathways which are among the main inflammatory pathways.

data.projectName: Insecticides free exportable citrus production through augmentation and conservation of potential biological control agents in citrus culture of Southern Punjab
data.projectDigest: The importance of citrus is well known by its wide distribution and dietary value. Pakistan is producing 1832 thousand tons yearly. But unfortunately a nominal quantity of citrus is capable to be exported dues to some addressable issues i.e. insecticidal residues in fruits. Insect pests cause approximately 25% yield losses of citrus, also vectors pathogens that cause dead decline in fruits production. Farmers totally rely on persistent chemistries for quick eradication of these insects and their associated diseases. A number of bio-intensive technologies have proved their effectiveness in pest management, the major components in this concern are the natural enemies; likewise predators, parasitoids and pathogens. In our previous studies a series of tests on predation were conducted in controlled conditions which needs extension as augmentation of this important biological control agent, which can be reared, mass produced and conserved to be utilized as effective bio-control agents against a wide range of insect pests. Current project is designed for mass rearing, release and conservation of those natural enemies and to evaluate their role in controlling insect pests in citrus orchards. The findings will be a road map toward commercialization of predators for insecticides free production of citrus.

data.projectName: Cancer Detection via Machine Learning Techniques
data.projectDigest:
In this research project, we are going to detect the cancerous cells. Cancer detection is one of the hot research topics in the world in 2019 and has caused the death of approximately 9.6 million people. The size and number of medical records is rising rapidly but most of these records are not analyzed for discovery of the hidden patterns and valuable knowledge of relationship. therefore, physicians demanding efficient methods for precise detection in this area. Through machine learning techniques we are going to solve it. Model developed from these techniques may useful to make right decisions for medical physicians. Breast Cancer (BC) diseases pose a great challenge in which some cells of the body grow abnormally. These cells then destroy alternative surrounding cells and their normal functions.  BC has become the risky type of cancers in the world among women. Detection in early stage of BC is integral for reducing life losses.  Yet, skin cancer is also common types of cancer in people with brighter skin. The diagnose at later stages is harder to treat. Furthermore, Kidney and Thyroid cancer as also leading causes of human death. Kidney cancer is amongst the ten most common cancers in both women and men. Mostly the people who suffer from kidney cancer are older in age. The average age of people when they are diagnosed is 64 years. While, thyroid cancer is that type in which the neck lump is observed by patient or handled by a clinician through an assessment. 
There are many Breast, Skin, Kidney and Thyroid Cancer detection techniques, but Cluster-Based Local Outlier Factors (CBLOF), K-Means and Local-Outlier Factors LOF haven’t been use so-far for these purposes. Through clustering and machine learning techniques we may achieve our goal i.e. detection of cancer.

data.projectName: Geotechnical Characterization and Erodibility of Flood Protection Earthen Embankments along eastern Banks of River Indus in Muzaffar Garh.
data.projectDigest: The current practices for design and construction of flood protection earthen infrastructure are based on selecting the geometrical sizes of the embankments and spurs and not based on the material type because of limited finances and longer lengths of rivers. In the events of flood, some of these earthen embankments would breach while the rest remain intact. This shows that their stability is also governed by soil properties and flow variations. However, the river alluvium used as the common construction material possesses significant potential of erodibility and thus requires careful examination before selection and inevitable measures after being used for construction. This project aims to shed light on the causes and mechanisms of breaching of flood protection infrastructure with a geotechnical view-point and aims at establishing design and assessment guidelines to be followed for identifying more vulnerable and potentially erodible sections in the goal area, which is approximately 60 km downstream of Taunsa Barrage along the eastern banks of River Indus in Muzaffar Garh. The outcome of this study would benefit the local population along the river Indus in protecting valuable lives, important agricultural lands and strategic highways.

Techniques regarding stevia cultivation and importance must be published by print media and electronic media to inform the farmer about the importance of stevia crop. Green extraction techniques like microwave-assisted extraction (MAE), ultrasound-assisted extraction

data.projectName: Genetic Studies of Neuromuscular Disorders (NMDs) in Pakistani families
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Over 60% of Pakistani population practices a strong custom of cousin marriages. Spouses in marriages carry rare identical gene variants, resulting in inherited disorders. Studies have revealed elevated levels of malformations among offspring of inbred. The frequency of birth defects in Pakistan is around 12.3-17% largely attributed to recessive traits and cousin marriages. Neuromuscular disorders (NMDs), characterized by congenital hypotonia, delayed motor development and progressive muscle weakness, are a frequent cause of chronic disability. Some examples are Charcot-Marie Tooth, spastic paraplegia, spinal muscular atrophies and myasthenic syndromes. Individual NMDs might be rare, in the global scenario, but their group prevalence is not. Their incidence is around 37 per 100,000 in the UK and 91 per 100,000 in India; therefore, their prevalence is feared to be even higher. NMDs are heterogeneous with more than 500 genes associated. Treatment strategies are largely palliative since these are incurable, therefore, prevention is the only affordable option. Hence, identification of the causative mutations is a prerequisite. This project has been designed to investigate the genetic basis of NMDs in Pakistani families. The expected outcome for the project include a better understanding of these disorders and, as a result, building our potential to prevent these disorders.

data.projectName: Accurate Hybrid Waveforms on fly  for LIGO Data Analysis
data.projectDigest: The discovery of gravitational waves has opened up a new window onto the universe. The Laser Gravitational Wave Observatory (LIGO) have observed gravitational waves from mergers of binary black holes and neutron stars. The detection of gravitational waves from observed LIGO signals required techniques of matched filtering, where, a theoretically modeled waveform,  obtained from solution of Einstein field equations, representing sources, are cross correlated with the observed data to detect gravitational waves and extract information about source properties. Currently, LIGO use available numerical waveforms or analytically constructed waveforms which both are available only for certain binary phases. Numerical waveforms are available for few binary configurations, and are shorter, usually only represents later inspiral and merger phases of binary due to computational cost.  Analytical waveforms are accurate for early inspiral phases of binary but lose their accuracy for later stages. In this project we are proposing hybrid binary black holes merger waveforms on fly using analytical model waveforms for the early inspiral phase and  numerical relativity waveforms for late inspiral to merger and post merger phase for more generic precessing binaries and construct longer waveforms that are sufficiently accurate for the parameter estimation techniques for upcoming LIGO observations.

data.projectName: Development of real-time In-process measurement system, for high-value components, processed through Computer Aided Manufacturing equipment, to enhance quality and reduce waste
data.piUniversity: CECOS University of Information Technology and Emerging Sciences, Peshawar
data.projectDigest: Conventional quality control procedures for 3rd industrial revolution are performed after the workpiece is manufactured. If the workpiece dimensions are outside the given tolerance range, it gets rejected.  This old technique not only affects the cost, lead time, energy, machine and labor utilized to develop the workpiece but also has long-lasting environmental effects. This project proposes development of a product (RIMMS: Real-time Intelligent Measurement system for Computer Aided Manufacturing), based on industry 4.0 through which quality control can be integrated in the manufacturing process and has the market potential of $1.95 trillion in total. Industry 4.0 and the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) are two terms that tend to appear together when the topic turns to the future of manufacturing. This is because the two concepts are closely linked: the increased interconnectivity that comes with the IIoT is a key component of the smart factories of Industry 4.0. Manufacturing forms the basis of economy for developed nations and plays a vital role in circular economy. Therefore, the focus of this research is to improve and integrate manufacturing processes and quality control. The scope of the research lies at the zenith of manufacturing process, machine vision system, metrology and quality control.  RIMMS through in-process measurement will provide both real-time data acquisition and quality control functionality in the same phase i.e. metrology operations are performed during the manufacturing process to insure quality control. RIMMS will help Pakistan’s manufacturing industry specifically into a new era through high-quality products, cost reduction, low lead time and wastage control. This will serve as catalyst for Pakistan’s industry entering Industry 4.0.

data.projectName: Governance assessment of public and private institutions of Pakistan: NBS Corporate Governance Lab.
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is a country blessed with human and natural resources. However, the institution of this country are facing bad governance. Due to which institutions are under performing. This lack of governance has also made these institutions inefficient and nonproductive. In such circumstances this is the time to develop a laboratory for their continuous assessment. The purpose of this project is to construct such state of the art governance lab, which cannot provide the continuous assessment of governance of public and private firms in Pakistan, but it can also provide their ratings on their governance mechanisms. With the establishment of this lab we will be in a position to put a monitoring mechanism on firms, further their rating will also develop the confidence of foreign investors on our firms due to which we will be able to attract more investment from outside the country. Thus indirectly this governance lab can play its vital role in growth of economy.

data.projectName: Evaluating the Effect of Seawater Intrusion on Water Resources along Shoreline of the Lower Sindh Province, Pakistan
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
The Indus Delta is landmark of Pakistan’s coastline extending up to 150 km along the Arabian Sea. It comprises of 17 major and numerous minor creeks, an extensive area of mud flats and mangrove forests. The delta holds 97% of the total mangrove forests of Pakistan. The Indus Delta occupies almost 6,00,000 ha area located mainly in Badin, Sajawal and Thatta districts of Sindh Province. Indus Delta mangroves, one of the largest tracts of arid mangroves in the world, used to cover an approximate area 2,83,000 ha till early 1980s; however, this area dropped drastically to 1,60,000 ha in 1990s. A recent study by WWF - Pakistan (2006) has estimated the existing cover of the Indus delta mangroves around 73,000 ha. The mangroves help habitat providing shelter, and breeding ground for economically important marine plants, animals and migratory birds, protect coastline and sea ports from storms, cyclones and Tsunamis, fulfill fuel and fodder requirements for local communities. 
The coastal communities’ livelihood resources are under constant threat of depletion due to the issue of brackish water. About 90% of the households in the coastal communities rely on fishing and other fisheries related activities.  The rapid degradation of coastal resources has created a threat of socio-ecological catastrophe. Access to service provision, such as primary schools, mosque schools, health services and potable water is miserably low. 
Therefore, activities have been developed based upon the robust evidence to generate high quality innovative research. Using the capacity development of institutions, a database of water quantity and water quality of the affected areas due to seawater intrusion will be established.

data.projectName: Disease Diagnosis using EEG based Neuroimaging Techniques
data.projectDigest:
Neurological mapping is the technique used for detection, diagnosis and treatment of neurological disorders. It involves very sophisticated approach that combines neurological and bioinformatics data along with signal processing and classification techniques. The early diagnosis and classification of disease is very significant for medical specialist to monitor the development and progress of such diseases which is essential for their treatment. EEG maps the brain activity into electrical signals so any abnormality in brain signals leading to serious diseases can be diagnosed. Brain disorders such as seizure, stroke, dementia, encephalopathy, brain tumors, encephalitis effects the activity of brain, as a result generate waveforms having varying frequency as compared to the normal brain activity. 
The current state of art shows that each disease has different effect on the activity of neurons. Our aim is to develop an efficient model that will map EEG data for disease diagnosis. EEG signals will be acquired and signal preprocessing techniques will be implemented to remove artifacts. After feature extraction, Classification techniques will be applied.
This system will be able to differentiate different diseases such as brain tumors, dementia, and epilepsy. Apart from different diseases, a model will be developed to diagnose different stages by comparing EEG signal of diseased person with healthy ones. This will help medical specialist to analyze the progress and its different stages.

data.projectName: Prevalence of Multidrug Resistant strains of Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeuroginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii in patients with Burn in Tertiary care Hospitals in Faisalabad.
data.projectDigest:
Burns are common and a critical problem requires much attention. Burn is the most distressing shape of trauma. Usually, after severe thermal damage requires proper care and management to prevent or reduce morbidity and mortality. Significant immune-suppression is the outcome that predisposes burn individuals to infection and other complications.  An early excision has significantly reduced the chances of persistent burn injury leading towards infection and secondary sepsis. The priorities of specific services focus on stabilizing the patient; preventing infection, and optimizing the wound healing process. Study on burns has made constant attention over the past few decades, and numerous significant progressions have caused more successful patient stabilization and reduced mortality, particularly among young individuals and those with burns of intermediate degree. However, for intensive care, challenges often exist that complicate the stabilization and support of the patient. In addition, burn wounds are multifaceted and can present typical difficulties that require late intervention or ultimate rehabilitation. Furthermore, improvements in patient care and stabilization, a study in burn injury management have made progress. Thus this project will be planned to investigate the prevalence of MDR Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii  in burn wounds patients admitted in burn wards of tertiary care hospitals.
The current project has been discussed with the officials of Saffron pharmaceutical and Ehsan Herbal Pharmacy, Bahawalpur for the subsequent product formation and commercialization.

data.projectName: Identification of environmental pollutants contributing to lung cancer in never-smokers in Punjab, Pakistan
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Incidence and mortality rates of lung cancer are predicted to be doubled till 2035 both in males & females in Pakistan. Lungs receive momentous amount of air pollutants and get impacted. Even smaller concentrations of air pollutions may cause significant damage to delicate tissues of lungs. People spend their time at different places like workplace, homes, and outdoor environment, hence are exposed to several types of airborne carcinogens. Current study would identify environmental pollutants (risk factors) contributing to lung cancer development in Pakistani population. In this study, about 200 confirmed lung cancer patients and 200 healthy individuals would be enrolled from all over the Punjab. Information about personal history, exposures to environmental pollutants (indoor, outdoor and workplace air pollutants, radiation exposures and exposure to kitchen pollutants) and socioeconomic factors would be extracted by an interviewer administered questionnaire. Air analysis for pollutants including radon, SO2, NO, NO2, CO, CO2, PM2.5, PM10, Ozone, H2S, and VOCs would be carried out at individual’s indoor, outdoor, workplace and kitchen environment. Association analysis between lung cancer and environmental pollutants would be carried out to identify cause-effect relationships. The results will help to fight this menace at low cost and will reduce the budget on healthcare.

data.projectName: Enhancing resistance to existing and emerging insects through fusion protein expression in cotton
data.projectDigest: The efficacy of Bt toxins has been supposed to be promised in near future because of resistance build up due to cotton management practices executed especially in developing countries. The traditional practices and current management of planting transgenic cotton harboring single gene toxin is not proving enough resistance to overcome the losses. Moreover, the efficacy of current toxin available in transgenic cotton plants has not proved suitable enough to overcome pink bollworm infestation owing to its nature of attack and stages of development along with receptor binding available with quantity of toxin at the spot of development. Addressing all in one, current study was attempted by fusing active domains of all toxins together under the control of tissue specific promoter. Moreover, to broaden the spectrum up to phloem feeder’s lectin protein was also considered in combination with Bt. Transgenic plants developed will be evaluated on molecular basis as well as its efficacy will be tested through feeding assay. The mortality ratio percentage of chewing and sucking insects will determine the faith of study proposed. The level of toxin specifically in insect development spot will define the efficacy of toxin developed as was proved through invitro assay. The success of study will address not only controlling some specific insects but also eliminating the fear of resistance build up in insects.

data.projectName: Evolutionary Computation Based Control Techniques for Underactuated Mechanical Systems
data.projectDigest: Control systems are essential for almost all engineering disciplines including electrical, electronic, mechanical, biomedical, and chemical engineering.  The key element in the control system problem is the control mechanism (controller) that has knowledge of the system behavior, and by processing the feedback information from the sensor, applies corrective action to achieve the desired behavior. The Underactuated mechanical systems (UAMS) are a class of mechanical systems with more number of degree of freedom as compared to the control inputs/actuators.  UAMS have numerous practical applications in robotics, marine systems, UAVS,  locomotives etc. Therefore , such systems are widely investigated in the research community. The controller design for UAMS is a challenging task and thus has remained an active area of research. Although , lot of classical and modern control techniques have been proposed for nonlinear systems but they can not be directly applied to UAMS. The performance of the controller highly depends on the proper adjustment of its parameters. The adjustment of such controller parameters is referred to as tuning of controllers. An improperly tuned controller does not only drastically degrade the performance of the control system but it also destabilizes the plant. Therefore proper tuning of controller constants is imperative to yield good dynamic performance, stability guarantee, and satisfactory steady state errors.  This project will focus on the controller design for UAMS using the application of evolutionary computation.

data.projectName: Citation Recommendation System: A novel approach to identify meaningful citations
data.piUniversity: Capital University of Science and Technology, Islamabad
data.projectDigest: The proposed project intends to provide prototype of a model Citation Recommendation System which will be able to identify meaningful citations against a query posed by a user. The project will follow the contemporary trend of binary citation classification by classifying citations into important and non-important categories by harnessing content and metadata-based parameters. The project will specifically focus on overcoming the deficiencies of existing state-of-the-art approaches. The main contributions of the project are: 1) Generation of an extensive benchmark data sets containing thousands of paper-citation pairs collected and annotated from actual citing authors from the domains of Computer Science, Mathematics and Electrical Engineering. Further, the data set will publicly be released to assist the scholarly community to further extend the idea 2) A rule-based approach formulation to extract data from PDF files 3) A novel approach to calculate relevance score among metadata and content-based parameters of citation pairs. The model will beneficiate research scholars by mitigating their cognitive effort involved in finding relevant research papers for the topic being focused and 4) academic policies formulation organizations like HEC and ORIC by providing them prototype of an automatic system to identify influential studies or researchers from different domains.

The results of the project will help clinicians  to understand the  disease burden and to treat the Staphylococcal infections in neonates more effectively.  Effective treatment will in turn help to increase the chances of survival of neonates that is the most fundamental right of the children.

data.projectName: Impact of Boundary Stresses on the Jeffery-Hamel Flow of Newtonian and Non-Newtonian Fluids
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest:
Fluid mechanics has wide variety of engineering and scientific studies. Examples include flow of fluid in human body like blood flow, urine and chyme flows, meteorology and oceanography. In this project our main focus will be on the flow confined between two non-parallel walls which is most commonly termed as Jeffery-Hamel flow because the mathematical formulation of such flows was laid down by Jeffery and Hamel. These flows are also designated as Convergent-Divergent flows. The flow of an incompressible Newtonian/non-Newtonian fluids through non-parallel plates/walls has a wide variety of applications in fluid dynamics and engineering like mechanical, civil and environmental engineering. These flows also have many applications in industry such as cold drawing operations in polymer industry, extrusion of molten polymers through converging dies, pressure driven particles flow through symmetric channel. 
	Here our objective is to address the influence of boundary stresses defined through the mixed type of boundary conditions on Jeffery-Hamel flow that will provide a counter example to the experimentally proven physical aspect that slip is a non-uniform phenomenon. Whereas from literature review it is quite clear that works are done using either no-slip or slip conditions as a uniform condition throughout the channel.
 Another objective of the proposed work is to allow the possible existence of asymmetric solution instead of imposing constraint of symmetry in channel which is most commonly assumed in works on Jeffery-Hamel flows.
The presence of boundary stresses also causes the existence of interesting bifurcations in flow of Jeffery Hamel type. 
Therefore we proposed to study the Impact of boundary stresses on Jeffery-Hamel flows of Newtonian and Non-Newtonian Fluids.

data.projectName: Development of High Density Fire Resistant Concrete as Gamma Rays Shielding Material
data.projectDigest: This research deals with shielding of harmful gamma radiations against high temperatures in concrete shields. Leakage of gamma rays has dangerous and long-lasting consequences. Concrete is the most widely used shielding material due to inexpensive and versatile nature. Concrete in nuclear power plants is subjected to high temperatures in their operating life. The breakdown inside heat exchanging systems, earthquakes, external accidents, fire or any other particular disaster may lead to even higher temperatures and pressures. The high temperatures induce compound changes in moisture content and chemical composition in concrete which leads to internal stresses and microcracking. Therefore, heavy density concrete using magnetite, dolerite, lead ore and steel aggregates as heavy density aggregates will be developed. Along with strength properties of heavy density concrete, its resistance to gamma rays and buildup factor will be assessed against high temperatures. Microstructural properties and statistical calculations are also part of the research. This research will be helpful in understanding the ability of heavyweight concrete to shield gamma rays at high temperatures

data.projectName: Improvement of anti-diabetic drugs as nanoparticles for treatment of central illnesses
data.projectDigest: Pioglitazone, a drug of choice for the treatment of Diabetes Mellitus, is a synthetic thiazolidinedione agent that has been in clinical practice. It alters the transcription of genes which is mediated by  nuclear peroxisome proliferator that activates nuclear peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors-? (PPAR-?). Metformin is another oral antidiabetic drug. It improves blood sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Mechanism of action of metformin is not clear and needs further investigations. These and other antidiabetics have also been suggested to be the drugs of choice for the treatment of, generalized anxiety disorders, depression, nociception as well as cognitive improvement and other indications. Despite a number of clinically important uses besides being used as antidiabetics, these drugs have limited use for central illnesses due to their inability to cross blood brain barrier. Therefore, utilization of these antidiabetics require the development of gold nanoparticles which can target the delivery of these drugs into brain. Therapeutic profile of these drugs may also starts to change when these drugs would be delivered as nanoparticles. Although an immediate role of glucocorticoid receptors is also there in the pathophysiology of these disorders, recent studies show that 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT; serotonin) can also play a pivotal role. Whether altered serotonergic receptors expression would be involved in the therapeutic profile of antidiabetics is yet to be determined. Impairment of therapeutic profile, if any, will also be monitored. In the proposed study, pioglitazone and metformin will be administered in animal models of anxiety, depression, pain and memory to evaluate potential of these drugs. Targeted drug delivery by synthesizing the nan

data.projectName: Neuro-imaging based Early Detection of Alzheimer's disease with Deep Learning (NEDA-DL)
data.projectDigest:
Alzheimer’s is a disease related to loss of memory and intellectual abilities which leads to dementia. Every three seconds a patient falls prey to it and the cost to combat it has surpassed $818 billion worldwide. In Pakistan alone, more than 2 million people are suffering from Alzheimer's disease (AD). The early detection of Alzheimer's disease and proper care could reduce the risk of the disease. But only 10 percent of the cases who suffer from this disease are diagnosed early by medical experts in developing countries like Pakistan. In our country, loss of memory and intellectual abilities is considered an aging factor and there is a serious lack of research and knowledge regarding this disease. Even though Alzheimer’s growth rate is alarming in Pakistan, very little research effort is focused on issues related to it.
There are four stages of Alzheimer; Pre-Dementia is the starting stage when disease actually sets in and this results in short term memory, which considered as ageing effect. In the second stage proper diagnosis is recommended, patients retain older memories but it becomes difficult for them to remember recent events. Moderate or third stage when Alzheimer actually affecting your day to day life including loss of motor neurons, speech difficulty, memory problems and reading & writing ability. The final stage of disease leads to imminent death of patient not because of Alzheimer but due to related condition such as infection or pneumonia. 
In this research, the primary objective is to develop a deep learning based architecture using neuro-imaging data for computer aided early diagnosis (CAD) of Alzheimer’s disease. Standard benchmark datasets will help in fine tuning the system. Moreover, the coordination with local hospitals and laboratories in Pakistan

data.projectName: How Increased Media use corresponds to consensus or polarization of public opinion? Sociological functions of Media Agenda-Setting at the First and Second Level
data.projectDigest:
In the contemporary world of mediated realities, we have had a little idea of what is happening out there because of our limited experience in the world. The media, to a considerable degree, shapes our realities about the issues and events happening around us. In other words, the mass media is influential enough to shape public opinion regarding different issues in society.  In sum, the increased media use (heavy versus light users) corresponds to increased consensus or polarization of public opinion among demographic subgroups (gender, age, education, income, and political party affiliation) in any given society. The core hypothesis is that in the current mass meditated age, the media play a significant role in defining what is important and what is not important in our societies. 
This study, with its longitudinal design, includes a content analysis of three leading magazines, three newspapers, three radio stations, three television channels, and three social media platforms, coupled with a systematic random sample survey of respondents, to explore the consensus of public opinion or polarization roles of the media among different demographic groups within the context of Pakistani society. The present study is a comprehensive investigation to document the particular effect of consensus or polarization roles of the media in society as a consequence of the first and second levels of agenda-setting regarding public issues and attributes of these issues. data.projectName: Enhancing the antitumor efficacy of regorafenib by synergistic interaction with other antineoplastic drugs against human metastatic colorectal cancer in pre-clinical models.
data.projectDigest:
Cancer development in large intestinal areas including colon or rectum is defined as colorectal cancer (CRC). Colorectal cancer is the world's third frequent cancer and the fourth leading cause of death, and its incidence in Asia is increasing rapidly. According to “Pakistan Health Research Council,” gastro-intestinal (GI) tract cancer is the third most common cancer and has an overall prevalence of 9.3% in Pakistan. Furthermore, it is the fourth common cancer (7%) in females and second (11.3%) in males. 
Majority of patients with metastatic CRC (mCRC) are incurable. Regorafenib, was approved for the treatment of mCRC in 2012. Now the problem is that its overall therapeutic effectiveness is quite limited. Furthermore, severe toxic effects and resistance against regorafenib is an emerging issue. 
Combination chemotherapy is a highly successful approach for reducing drug’s toxicity, boosting anticancer activity, overcoming drug resistance, and improving the overall survival of the patients. During this research, regorafenib combination with dacomitinib will be studied in preclinical models to increase the efficacy of the regorafenib. 
Enhancing the efficacy by synergistic/combine effect of regorafenib with dacomitinib will not only be useful for our country but will also help to treat mCRC patients globally.

data.projectName: Formulation of Polyoxometalates niosomes for effective treatment of cancer and diabetes
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Polyoxometalates are inorganic metal complexes which have previously been reported as highly potent therapeutic compounds in several life-threatening diseases. These compounds are known for their pancreatic beta cells regeneration power as well as inhibiting enzymes which are over-expressed in diabetes. Furthermore, POMs are useful compounds to treat several cancers both in vitro and in vivo. The major problem with these transitional metal based complexes is toxicity. In order to make these compounds useful in therapeutics an effort will be geared to encapsulate these compounds into a sustained delivery system that would release the drug into plasma in a controlled manner. For this a nano vesicular niosomes will be prepared to entrap drug into aqueous phase that limit its abrupt release into blood.

data.projectName: MWCNTs-CO-NH-Ligand decorated with magnetic nanoparticles: Synthesis, characterization and adsorptive applications
data.projectDigest:
The discharge of metallic contaminated industrial effluents into environmental aqueous bodies is potential threat to human health due to its non-biodegradable nature. Excess intake of heavy metal ions through food chain and/or other means is toxin to the human and causes serious health problems. So ultra-trace determinations of toxic metal ions in industrial waste water before discharge to environmental water samples is mandatory. In routine, Flame atomic absorption spectrometer (FAAS) has been used for the determination of metal ions in water. But this instrument has problem of insufficient sensitivity, which cannot detect the ultra-trace amount of toxic metal ions in water samples. For solving this type of problems, this project is designed. 
In this project, new methods will be developed for solid phase extractive preconcentration of toxic metal ions such as Pb(II), Zn(II), Co(II), Ni(II), Cu(II) and Cd(II), Cr(VI), As(VI), Mn(II), etc. in industrial wastewater samples prior to their ultra-trace determinations by FAAS. For solid phase extraction, selective, high efficient and high reusable Fe3O4-MWCNTs-CO-NH-Ligand adsorbents will be synthesized. The developed methods will be applied for the monitoring of toxic metal ions in industrial waste water in urban areas of Pakistan. 
Data obtained from this project will be useful for Pakistan Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). In the light of that data, Government can make possible legislation for mandatory installation of in-house treatment-plant in industries for toxic effluents treatment before discharging to environmental water bodies.

data.projectName: Fabrication of Novel Magnetic poly nanocomposites: A Convenient Reusable Tool for hazardous pollutants Removal
data.projectDigest: Approximately three million tons of emerging contaminants are detected in surrounding environment including particularly phenol and its derivatives [1]. It is obvious that, if wastewater is not properly treated, then it may cause severe and harmful diseases, frequently caused breast cancer. There are various effective methods for waste water treatment but they transfer the contaminants from one medium to another. Photocatalysis including semiconductor catalyst is very effective, cheaper and environmentally friendly, as it’s redox reactions and physically stable for degradation of organic pollutants into simple components, carbon dioxide and water. Therefore, it is still an interesting era to prepare highly stable and efficient photocatalyst on large industrial scale for the degradation of toxic and carcinogenic pollutants from environment [2]. Consequently in the proposed research project, the novel nano crystallites of poly composite perovskite La1-xTbxMnO3 / PVA/ guargum and sepeolite fiber with enhanced flexible and adjustable physical, chemical and catalytic properties will be synthesized. Various properties of LaMnO3  will be enhanced by doping of (Higher magnetic moment) Tb, which are vital to make them magnetically recyclable and detachable owing to sufficient magnetic properties. These new poly-nanocomposite photocatalysts fabricated with conducting polymers will lower band gap and these would like to show highest absorption in visible region that will ultimately enhance the rate of photodegradation of the phenol under stimulated sunlight irradiation. Therefore on the successful completion of this project we would be optimistic that the local community and water bodies will be secured from toxic phenolic pollutants.

data.projectName: Identification and characterization of entomopathogenic bacterial isolates to control agricultural insect pests in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Excessive use of synthetic chemicals is a common and easy practice to control insect pests of agriculture. The residual effects of these chemicals posed serious threats to the living organisms and the environment. There is an urgent need to develop some environment friendly strategies to control insect pest populations. Microbial pesticides emerged as an important tool to control targeted pest organisms. However, some insects develop resistance against some bacterial insecticides. There is a need to identify new bacterial strains to successfully control the insect pest populations and overcome the resistance issues. For this purpose, different ecological zones of Pakistan will be visited to collect samples from different sources including plant, soil, and dead insects. These samples will be used to get different bacterial isolates. Their entomopathogenic efficacy will be evaluated through lab and field trials. After trials, the entomopathogenic isolates will be characterized at molecular level to identify their strains. This study will help to minimize the adverse effects of synthetic insecticides to the ecosystem and promote the organic farming.

data.projectName: Development of wheat cultivars for changing environmental conditions and sustainable development
data.projectDigest: Like most parts of the developing world, bread wheat is used as a major source of protein and carbohydrate to meet daily nutrient requirements by people living in Pakistan. Wheat production has increased many folds in the country due to untiring efforts of the agriculturists in general and plant breeders in particular. As a result huge foreign reserves which were spent on wheat import earlier are now conserved. However, during the last few years wheat production has significantly reduced throughout the country due to untimely and uneven rain shower, delayed sowing in rain-fed areas and occurrence of diseases like stripe rust and leaf rust. Shortage of irrigation water in more than 70% area under wheat cultivation is the main limiting factor to wheat production in Khyber Pukhtoonkhwa province.Secondly, delay in wheat sowing due to current shift in climate is badly affecting crop yield as it squeezes wheat life cycle and invite diseases like stripe rust and leaf rust.This necessitates wheat breeders to evolve such varieties that can easily fit in our cropping pattern under the current water deficit and climate change scenario. The present study is also an attempt to test wheat advance lines, developed at the Plant Breeding and Genetics department,under moisture stress conditions of the province and identify potential lines which can tolerate disease pressure and harsh weather conditions as well as have high water use efficiency particularly in Khyber Pukhtoonkhwa.

data.projectName: Risk Management of Mastitis in dairy sector through novel plants based intra- mammary sealants.
data.projectDigest:
Livestock is playing an important role in the economy of country contributing to 3.3% of total GDP of Pakistan. A major population of livestock is facing mammary gland infection or mastitis that affects animal health, milk quality, composition of milk and low milk production. Mastitis may lead to economic loss of 80US$ to 125 US$ per animal per year. Besides that contamination of milk with antibiotic resistant pathogens and their transfer to consumers is an alarming issue to the health of human.
Based on the etiology of mastitis, infection may involve contagious pathogens like Streptococcus agalactiae and Staphylococcus aureus or environmental pathogens including E. coli and Streptococcus uberis. So, antibiotic based teat sealants are used to treat infection in dry period i.e., time from last milking to heifer birth. These sealants may lead to development of antibiotic resistant strains. Similarly, plants extracts such as cinnamon, cedar, clove, eucalyptus, peppermint and lemon have been used due to their antimicrobial activities against pathogenic bacteria. So, plants extract based intra mammary teat sealant will be developed to reduce the risk of new infection of mammary glands after heifer birth. New teats sealant will reduce antibiotic import bill of country.

data.projectName: Extraction  and Value Addition of aromatic floricultural crops through Eco friendly extraction techniques
data.projectDigest: This proposal seeks to establish a platform for the extraction of high-value products, having worth of thousands dollar in the international market, extracted from aromatic plants appropriate for Pakistan’s favorable and versatile climatic conditions. Essential oils represent a small fraction of a plant’s composition but confer the characteristic for which aromatic plants are used in the pharmaceutical, food, fragrance and cosmetic industries. There are several technologies that can be used for oil extraction, ranging from steam distillation, to more recent techniques which rely on hydrocarbon solvents or Supercritical Fluid (SCF) CO2 for oil extraction. Features in each of these extraction technologies make each platform uniquely competitive. UAF has already established pilot scale operations for steam, solvent, and SCF extraction. Technical experiments have been conducted and results have been published in scientific journals by the Rosa Laboratory.The proposed project is broader in that it extends the commercialisation of essential oil extraction to include other non-traditional floricultural crops: Jasminum sambac (Motia), and Murraya exotica (Murayya). Beyond oil extraction, further value addition in Pakistan is limited since the industries required to do so are capital intensive; further value addition is possible through packaging essential oils in small volume bottles for wholesalers in Pakistan and abroad as well.

data.projectName: Application of Economical Crystallization method in Pharmaceutical and Sugar Industries
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan

data.projectName: Towards a 30% renewable energy share by 2030 through complementary hybrid renewable energy sources in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: During this practice-led research project, therefore, we propose to quantify solar-wind complementarity in the wind corridors of Pakistan (with assistance from various industry collaborators including Master Wind Energy that operates 52.6MW wind farm in Jhimpir). In addition to this, we will also assess and quantify solar-hydro and solar-hydro complementarity for some selected regions in Punjab. The selected areas will be divided to form a grid. Grid spacing will be chosen according to the granularity of information (weather, terrain, etc.) available in open datasets. For every grid element (1 km2 or more), for example, we intend to compute solar-wind, solar-hydro, or solar-wind-hydro complementarity in different months and seasons based on multiple complementarity indices. Using Geographic Information System (GIS) software, we intend to also develop multiple complementarity maps according to months, seasons, and complementarity indices. It should be noted that solar irradiance and wind speed GIS maps are available for the entire country, but RES complementarity maps are largely missing. Through this project, therefore, we also aim to fill this gap. With the help of our complementarity maps, we will identify promising regions for hybrid RE installations, determine appropriate share of investment in solar, wind, and hydro resources, and develop appropriate policy guidelines for low-cost as well as high investment, larger hybrid RE projects. The greatest impact of our research’s outcome will be on the industry’s ability to develop hybrid energy plants because of availability of complementarity maps according to months, seasons, and complementarity indices) as well as on current and future RE policy.

data.projectName: Progress in Implementing the Sustainable Development Goals for Quality Education in institutions of Higher Education in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) significantly focused on access to education for all through poverty elevation. World nations had responded positively to achieve these MDGs for the overall progress of their countries and especially developing countries like Pakistan. In this connection, the focus of sustainable development goals (SDGs) was on quality of education. The different countries are focusing on achieving the goal of quality education. To be more focused, the objectives of the proposed research project is to keep the major focus to evaluate the progress regarding measures taken for implementing on sustainable development goals by the higher  institutions for future generations at curricula and practice level.

data.projectName: Fractionation & Pharmacological Evaluation of the Central Asian Cobra (Naja oxiana)Venom.
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Title: Fractionation & Pharmacological Evaluation of the Central Asian Cobra (Naja oxiana)Venom. 

Various drugs derived from snake venom such as ?-cobrotoxin, Alfimeprase, Cenderitide, Crotalphine are in clinical trials for reliving chronic inflammation, pain & heart diseases. Captopril, an antihypertensive drug made by venom of South American snake (Bothropsjararaca).  There is need of exploration of certain biological and pharmacological screening of cobra venom that is found in Pakistan. Cobra venom will be extracted and experimental techniques like centrifugation, electrophoresis, and spectrophotometer will be used for partial purification of peptides. The lethal dose (LD50) & protein estimation will be determined. Six animals in each group of albino mice will be used. Crude as well as the fractionated venom will be screened on developed Parkinson’s mice models. Pakistani cobra (Najaoxiana) venom will be screened for antiparkinson’s& anti-inflammatory activity. Molecular markers will be determined utilizing PCR and ELISA techniques. Effect on neuroinflmmation will be determined by cell culture technique. Aggregometer will be utilized for assay of antiplatelet activity of venom. Sub-acute toxicity, biochemical & histopathological parameters will also be determined.

data.projectName: Ameliorating negative effect of arsenic stress on Maize (Zea mays L.) through application of silicon (Si).
data.projectDigest:
About 200 million people around the word are exposed to arsenic toxicity. According to an earlier study by Podgorski et al. (2017), ground water of Pakistan is highly contaminated with Arsenic and 60 million people of Pakistan are at the risk of Arsenic toxicity. A trace amount is naturally present in ground water.  About 60% arsenic in environment is due to anthropogenic activities. A number of studies have indicated the harmful effects of As to human health by ingesting food and water containing As. The terrestrial plants usually absorb As through roots. Which is then transported to all plant parts by apoplastic pathway.  The objective of the study is to explore the impacts of Si application on alleviating arsenic (As) toxicity in Maize, its possible mechanism and to draw the relationship between various physiological and biochemical traits responsible for arsenic stress tolerance in maize, particularly PSII photochemistry, non-photochemical quenching.
Maize (Zea mays L.) is one of the main source of cereals for food, forage and processed industrial products. As has harmful impacts on grown growth and yield of corn.  The toxicity of As can be reduced by the application of Silicon.

data.projectName: Promoting small entrepreneurship as a measure of poverty alleviation in District Tharparkar
data.projectDigest: This research activity is committed to promote the small-scale business to poverty-stricken yet skillful communities of Tharparkar. The beautiful handicraft made by Tharri women is liked nationally and internationally and is a source of income for them. However, the profit which they get is very less because they are not directly connected to the market. We are therefore proposing a comprehensive plan/intervention which will improve their access and exposure with the help of technology. They will be given working capital for making few samples which they will display by mobile app. We have identified the collaborators who have expertise in the required areas.” Samanzar” has worked in Tharparkar previously as well and promoted the artisans there. We hypothesize that this intervention will improve the monthly income in an intervention arm. “Converge technologies” will train the participants on managing the online business by giving basic training which will be tailored according to the needs and level of the partipants. In addition, they will also monitor and supervise the participants so that they become proficient and sustainability can be ensured. This research will provide the scientific evidence by comparing the pre and post-intervention income as well as comparing the monthly income of control and intervention arm.

data.projectName: Model development and application of cascade waste heat recovery system for tractor engine
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest:
Use of alternate energy resources, reduce energy consumption and increase energy efficiency is the urgent need of present world. In Agriculture sector, farm tractors are major source of fuel consumption. It is estimated that more than 70% supplied fuel energy is dissipated to environment in the form of waste heat (Exhaust gas, water jacket, radiator) and not taking part in mechanical work by the tractor engine.  
The aim of this project is to harvest the wasted heat from tractor engine and add up into mechanical work efficiency of the tractor. A model development of a waste heat recovery system will be done and applied on tractor engine. The heat from exhaust of the engine and the heat potential of water jacket (radiator) will be recovered. This kind of waste heat recovery systems already in use of modern thermal power plants. It is predicted that the developed cascade methodology has the potential to increase 7-12% engine work efficiency and same in reduction of fuel consumption. Co-Principal Investigators from National University of Science and Technology (NUST) and University of Engineering and Technology, Lahore will have joint working on this cutting-edge research.

data.projectName: Efficiency improvement of solar thermal tower power plant using innovative materials.
data.projectDigest: The current research comprises solar tower thermal power plant design, optimization of solar field layout, and calculation of energy production based upon this field. Solar tower power plant efficiency improvement will be the prime focus of this research and it will be achieved using two strategies. First, the plant layout will be designed and optimized. A new optimization technique like constrained optimization by linear approximation algorithm will be introduced and layout field will be optimized. Energy calculation based on this optimized field will determine the efficiency improvement of the plant. Second, new innovative fluids will be introduced and based upon these fluid properties, plant efficiency will be calculated. In the later part of this research, thermal and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation of designed components will be carried out. This research work will be helpful in introducing green technologies and indigenous solar thermal power plant development. It will mainly contribute to the efficiency improvement of solar thermal tower power plant.
