data.projectName: Identification, Characterization and Modification of Novel Bacterial Enzymes for the Conversion of Petroleum-based Plastics to Bio-chemicals
data.projectDigest: Synthetic plastics such as polystyrene (PS), polyvinylchloride (PVC), polyethylene (PE), polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and polyurethane (PU) are some major plastic pollutants due to their high demand in industry to manufacture different consumer demanded products. The global production of plastics is estimated to be nearly 400 million tons per year. Bioplastics that are developed by using biomass obtained from different renewable sources can replace synthetic plastics but are limited to the availability of biomass hence these for the time being cannot counter plastic pollution. We have isolated Serratia sp., Pseudomonas sp. and Stenotrophomonas sp. form plastic waste dumping sites of Faisalabad. The current project aims to exploit the potential of these bacterial strains for the production, identification, purification and characterization of some novel plastic degrading enzymes along with the possible byproducts such as carboxylic acids, alcohols, amines, ethers, ethylene glycol, terephthalic acid etc. The purified enzymes will be modified to enhance its degrading activity while the byproducts produce along with the biodegradation of plastics can make this process cost effective, more efficient and economical. The structural changes in the plastic sheets will be determined by scanning electron microscope (SEM) and chemical modifications will be determined by Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy.

data.projectName: The Enigma of Crime in Pakistan: An In depth Analysis of Prisons of Pakistan.
data.projectDigest: Prison reforms and prisoners rehabilitation is always considered on priority but in developing countries like Pakistan, it has been ignored by policy makers. At the same time reform programs which already been working has a gap in planning and implementation. Keeping this gap into consideration, this study at first stage will try to make a conceptual framework not only based on socio-economic and demographic factors of committing crime but also religious, psychographics, and ethical values into account. At the same time project will also target prison conditions in Pakistan and trying to find rehabilitation planning and implementation gap by keeping prisoners expectations into consideration. Mixed methods [field survey, key informant interviews, focus group discussions] shall be used to generate data on qualitative as well as quantitative aspects. For quantitative data, stratified multistage sampling shall be used and data will be collected in capital cities of provinces and independent states of Pakistan. The project will expect to come up with policy intervention for prison management, judicial management and NGOs working for the wellbeing of prisoners.

data.projectName: The Newly Proposed Systems of Local Government in Punjab and KP: Its Assessment and Prospects for Implementation in Future
data.projectDigest: Local government systems in Pakistan had to face repeated failures in the past since 1947 and still could not be rooted even after 72 years. Gen. Ayub Khan’s BD system to the recent system established in 2016 by the then provincial governments after an utmost resistance. Always after succession in government, the new governments’ (at national and provincial level) first attack had been on the prevailing local government system. They immediately abrogated the working system without giving any replacement. Local governments are, no doubt an essential component of the political system of a country and have to perform specific local functions. However, in Pakistan it is a bitter reality that local government is highly disliked by all the political parties’ higher and middle range leaderships. There is a known jealousy between the political parties’ leadership and the local councilors. In such a situation the most significant question is the viability of the system which the PTI’s government had announced to introduce very shortly. There are many question marks on the success of this system in future because it would be the first time that the districts and municipal heads in this system would be directly elected.

data.projectName: Factors affecting rural farmers decisions in biogas technology adoption, the case of Punjab, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: With a mundane lifestyle and population growth, energy demand is increasing tremendously. Traditional means of energy causing severe effects on the environment and resulting in the reduction of natural resources. In contrast, renewable energy resources such as biogas plants have many benefits over conventional methods. Biogas plans are inexpensive, easy to use, handle and ecofriendly. Pakistan has a high potential for energy generation through biogas. Therefore, this study aims to find the factors that can affect farmers' intention to adopt biogas energy plant. A mix method approach including qualitative and quantitative, will be used for this study. First of all, interviews will be conducted and the results-driven from the qualitative research will be empirically tested. The practitioners will be able to utilize identified factors in their strategies so that unmet energy demand can be fulfilled. It will be also helpful for the government to achieve its goal of 5% energy generation from renewable resources.

data.projectName: TUNNEL GROWER’S TRAINING OF INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT: AN ECO-FRIENDLY APPROACH
data.projectDigest: Tunnel farming is an advanced technique of vegetable production which is very popular in Pakistan. Government of Punjab has also boosted tunnel farming in Punjab via F&VDP. In tunnel farming due to close structure humidity is easily increased which results in several fungal diseases in Cucumber, tomato, chilies etc. Downy mildew in cucumber damping off in chilies and collar rot in tomato are few very destructive tunnel diseases. Tunnel growers are so afraid of these pathogens that they adopt ‘prevention is better than cure’ proverb as their sole solution. Spraying on vegetables at two-day interval is a general practice of tunnel growers. The fact that fungicides are intensively misused in tunnels giving rise to potential environmental pollution and food contamination. Present study aims to assess the residual effects of various pesticides/fungicides on tunnel produce and to create awareness among tunnel growers regarding safe use of pesticides. Main goal will be to teach them integrated diseases management approach. Research will be based on the tunnel growing hubs which are luckily present in campus surrounding areas Burewala, Mailsi, Chichawatni, Kamalia and Arifwala of Punjab. Farmers will be practically trained about how to control humidity in tunnels for the prevention of fungal diseases.

data.projectName: Development of an effective antineoplastic herbal product for the treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma: Insight into its mechanism of action
data.projectDigest: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most frequent form of primary liver cancer, it is one of the most common life threatening solid tumors with global annual diagnosis exceeding one million new cases and the second cancer killer worldwide. Incidence and mortality rates of HCC are most prevalent in south and southeastern Asia. In Pakistan we import lots of drugs each year from different countries to treat HCC. Hepatoprotective drugs are very expensive and their numbers are also limited. unfortunately, no proven second-line therapy is available to date, leaving supportive care or clinical trials of investigational molecular target agents as the only remaining options for patients. Therefore it is necessary to find out some alternative herbal medication for the treatment of HCC because the inexpensive nature of herbal medicine allows the low-income households access to health care. By identifying a low cost natural product for the treatment of HCC and facilitating its production on commercial level not only strengthen our economy, local pharmaceutical industries but also help us to save many precious lives who lost their battle to HCC owing to very expensive nature of currently available treatment.

data.projectName: EDTA Chelation Therapy: Experimental and Therapeutic Trials in Cardiovascular Disease
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Coronary heart disease (CHD) is a common form of heart disease. There are certain patients with heart disease who take chelation therapy by the use of disodium ethylene diamine tetra-acetic acid (EDTA), which is a  complementary health tactic opted by some healthcare professionals. It has been found that chelation therapy had presented reasonable protection against further cardiovascular events, i.e. heart attacks and strokes, (especially in diabetics) but without proven efficacy. In general, this therapy sticks to minerals and metals in the bloodstream and create a compound which the body removes via urination. Chelation therapy can be encouraged as a therapy for heart disease, even in diabetics, because it is believed that it sticks to the calcium found in fatty deposits in arteries; but it has some known risks and side effects. The aim of this project is the determination of an EDTA-based chelation regimen that can reduce cardiovascular events; the first phase comprises the research to be done on cell lines and animal models,  to assess efficacy, safety and toxicity levels of the therapy. In the second phase, EDTA-based chelation along with vitamin-mineral regimen will be administered in patients to determine its efficacy and safety. The results may provide evidence to support routine use of chelation therapy for treating patients who had myocardial infarction; also it may help in alleviating the risk of adverse effects associated with the cardiac disease in patients with or without diabetes, thereby reducing morbidity/ mortality rates

It has been found that chelation therapy had presented reasonable protection against further cardiovascular events, i.e. heart attacks and strokes, (especially in diabetics) but without proven efficacy. In general, this therapy sticks to minerals and metals in the bloodstream and create a compound which the body removes via urination. Chelation therapy can be encouraged as a therapy for heart disease, even in diabetics, because it is believed that it sticks to the calcium found in fatty deposits in arteries; but it has some known risks and side effects. The aim of this project is the determination of an EDTA-based chelation regimen that can reduce cardiovascular events; the first phase comprises the research to be done on cell lines and animal models,  to assess efficacy, safety and toxicity levels of the therapy. In the second phase, EDTA-based chelation along with vitamin-mineral regimen will be administered in patients to determine its efficacy and safety. The results may provide evidence to support routine use of chelation therapy for treating patients who had myocardial infarction; also it may help in alleviating the risk of adverse effects associated with the cardiac disease in patients with or without diabetes, thereby reducing morbidity/ mortality rates

data.projectName: Development of fluorescence based imaging systems for monitoring plant diseases and photodynamic therapy treatment of skin cancer/leishmaniasis wounds
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest:
The Plant diseases destroy valuable crops and fruits and it imparts huge impact on national economy. Early detection may help in their eradication at low expense and to avoid unnecessary insecticide sprays. In this project, fluorescence imaging system will be developed which will image the fluorescence of chlorophyll produced from plant leaves by shining with violet light, which will become the biomarkers of disease. These images will be used in some dedicated developed software to diagnose the diseases at early stages.  
In addition, an FDA approved technique photodynamic therapy has been extensively employed worldwide for treating skin cancer and leishmaniasis wounds. During last decade, it has been used in Pakistan for treating skin cancer patients and leishmaniasis wounds. Real time monitoring of treatment may help to improve the treatment efficacy. Similarly, low level laser therapy is also very efficient treatment modality for treating skin diseases including postherpetic neuralgia, chronic pains inflammations and wounds, aphthous ulcer, burns and acne. In this project lasers at 635, 650, 830 and 980 nm and imaging system will be developed. The technology will then be transferred to private sector to produce laser and imaging systems at low cost to expedite the said treatments in the country.

data.projectName: Development of novel glasses doped with rare-earth ions for the radiation shielding
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is a nuclear power where the personnel working in the nuclear power plants encounter with hazardous radiations. In addition, there are many cancer-diagnostic centers and hospitals where patients are treated with radiation doses. In all such hospitals, radiation doses should be maintained at adequate safe levels for patients and technical staff.  Hard shielding materials, attenuating or completely stopping the radiations, are required for the safety of the personnel working in these facilities.  Presently conventional radiation shielding materials such as ordinary concrete, clay bricks, tiles and lead blocks are currently used for this purpose. However, these materials are heavy and some of them are toxic, for instance those which are lead-based. To overcome this issue, glasses are promising alternatives with distinctive features such as good transparency, easy fabrication, non-toxicity, light weight and high resistivity against ionizing irradiation. Furthermore, their physical properties such as density and effective atomic number can be tailored by various developing techniques and changing their composition. Therefore, this project aims to develop novel glasses with low cost and desired properties for radiation shielding, in order to safeguard both the personnel and patients exposed to the hazardous radiations.

data.projectName: Polymorphism of Properdin factor:  Association with Modulation of Immunity in Diabetes and its Complication in Pakistani Population
data.projectDigest: Frequency of recurrent infections in Diabetic patients is generally higher because of innate immune system dysregulation, secondary to long standing and/or poorly controlled hyperglycemia. It is associated with a higher morbidity and mortality in critical illness. One of the mechanisms by which hyperglycemia contributes to immune dysregulation is by decrease in nitric oxide production resulting in vasoconstriction which generally attenuates the ability of Neutrophils and macrophages compromising against infection. Alternative pathway of innate immunity is the first line of defense to control invading pathogens.  Among almost thirty complement cascade proteins, in healthy people, properdin factor “P” is the late appearing central enzyme. It is a stabilizing component of the alternative pathway convertase and initiates the opsonization of the pathogenic microbes. Association of its expression level and genetic polymorphism with diabetes, its complication and in infections of diabetes has not been reported yet in global literature association of some mutations with meningitis is reported in a few numbers of subjects. Its role in pathogenesis is also flimsy.We hypothesize that properdin, the final enzyme for stabilizing molecule of opsonization, become reduced in level and/or in activity is due to genetic alterations appear in this gene’s .We will like to study hypothesis by determining the  mutations of exon 4,5 and intron 3and 9. by performing polymorphism through PCR and sequencing. expression levels will be checked by molecular techniques. We expect that positive out come will provide useful information to add in panel of ealy diagnosis od diabetes complications .

data.projectName: Career Decision Making in Young Adolescents:  Development of a Career Resource for Government Schools
data.projectDigest: Students here in Pakistan, at the end of passing their 8th grade exam, struggle much to choose the subjects, e.g. whether they should go for medical, engineering, computers, arts or other vocational training courses.  How they make decisions about subject choices affects their future in terms of the career paths they are left with. One decision of making right career choice, not only brings success and prosperity to the individual or his/her family, but also brings economic prosperity at national level. Research shows that majority of the students, at this level, have little or no knowledge about the career paths that exists. Neither they have much knowledge about their own potentials, strengths, and aptitudes, nor about any career guidance and counselling services (this is more true for government schools as compared to the private sector). Current project aims at reaching 8th grade students (both males and females) from randomly selected government schools from all Punjab. Goal is to help young adolescents make better and informed career choices through these Deliverables: a) development and validation of Aptitude test (so students know their strengths and potentials), b) broadening their vision through maximum knowledge about the Job market, and new STEM and technology related jobs/careers, c) matching their strengths and potentials to the most suitable jobs and guiding them toward a career where they will succeed and really enjoy.

data.projectName: Towards the establishment of a Systemic Corporate Social Responsibility framework for Pakistan
data.projectDigest: In the developed world, the strategic and processual aspects of CSR have matured well, many academicians critique that in the context of developing countries the idea of CSR is still is in its infancy and lacks the long-term and strategic approach that add meaning and social value to the CSR endeavours and therefore limiting it to a bunch of isolated ad-hoc activities that relate only to the philanthropic dimension. Researchers also believe that the idea of CSR has failed to create a significant impact in the developing world due to the parochial understanding of the idea of CSR, which is not considered to be an integral component of how corporates do business but rather a detached activity. This then by extension also applies to the context of Pakistan, as is backed by the existing literature related to the scope and practice of CSR in Pakistan. The lack of any constitutional definition and legal characterisation of the scope of CSR is also a testimony to the same. This, therefore, creates a need of establishing a framework of CSR that is applicable to the context of Pakistan, which is sensitive to the country’s social, environmental and economic backdrop and responds to governance gap that inhibits the development of the country. This research paper will, therefore, be aimed towards the development of a CSR assessment tool, that would evaluate the existing practices and activities of the manufacturing concerns of Pakistan, establishing where they stand, and would then suggest a road map for progressing towards a more systemic approach to CSR or CSR 2.0 that would make the CSR activities contextually relevant and meaningful for the benefit of the society at large.

data.projectName: Agronomic Biofortification of Chickpea with Iron to Combat Hidden Hunger
data.projectDigest: Iron (Fe) de?ciency is the most prevalent and widespread nutrient de?ciency affecting a huge population in the world especially in developing countries. It is a general conception that, legumes have little concentrations of Fe. Agronomic biofortification is a cost effective agricultural approach to enrich micronutrient content of grains through application of mineral fertilizers by different methods. Our proposed project will focus mainly on improving grain iron content and production of chickpea through agronomic biofortification. During 1st year, Field experiment to screen out chickpea genotypes with different grain Fe potential, and pot experiment to optimize Fe application levels for four application methods (seed coating, seed priming, soil application and foliage application) to enrich grain Fe content will be carried out. During 2nd year, out of four Fe application methods, the best method for improving grain Fe content will be selected by growing two genotypes in pot as well as field experiments. In 3rd year, in order to confirm results, the 2nd year experiments will be repeated under field conditions at two different locations. At the end we will be able to find most effective and economical method of Fe application to enrich chickpea grains with Fe will be find out.

data.projectName: A Scalable Platform for EEG Data Storage and Analysis for Anxiety Disorder using Machine Learning
data.projectDigest:
Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (OCD) is kind of neural disorder in which the effected person is obsessed by certain thoughts creating a paradox in the patients mind and it makes the person do things that seems to be abnormal for a normal person. The person suffering from OCD act normal under usual conditions but the person feels unsecure and fragile to the exposed environment making him uncertain at normal activities and the patient perform the regular activities in abnormal way. The proposed project about to diagnosed and monitoring the neural activities of the person have neural disorder.
The proposed project will extract EEG data of both normal and patient subjects  and stored on cluster computing. Then after acquisition of data, research focuses to parallelize deep neural network using cluster computing platform to minimize both computation cost and training time with no loss in the performance of the system. The proposed research will be implemented on top of spark general data flow engine and execute in cluster environment to parallelizes the process of deep learning for massive amount of bigdata.  The proposed project has significant potential to become commercialize research and also has the ability to established state of art research lab have the facility to work on EEG data.
The final result of our proposed research to recognize the neuronal activation sequences of the patients suffering from anxiety and depression special Obsessive-compulsive disorder OCD patients. the comparative study will be initiated to compare the state-of-art classifiers with deep neural network in the cluster computing environment. The performance of the recognition system will be evaluated in term of computation efficiency, speedup, scalability and accuracy.

data.projectName: An Eco-Friendly and Cost-Effective Approach for the Development of Flexible Lead-Free Bi-based Piezoelectric Thick Films for Energy Storage Applications
data.projectDigest: The research focus of this project is synthesis of lead-free piezoceramics for energy storage capacitor applications, fusion of organic-inorganic hybrid films and porotype device fabrication of sensors, actuators and nanogenerators. The project will provide the platform for the development of these prototype devices and up-scale production. Synthesis of Bi-based (BNT and BF-BT) nanoparticles and polycrystalline materials to produce bulk ceramics for the fabrication of sensors and actuators devices. Development of new compositions; Bi-based oriented particles and template ceramics for incorporation with bulk ceramics for large grain sized densified ceramics for the energy storage capacitor applications. Fabrication of the facial and cost-effective processing criteria for depositing functional ceramics Bi-based thick film on flexible metallic substrate by using EPD technique. In cooperation of Bi-based nanoparticles as piezoceramics to fabricate large and flexible organic-inorganic piezoelectric nanogenerator (PNG) films consist of piezoceramics - PVDF-TrFE (vinylidene fluoride trifleoroethylene) for energy harvesting applications.

data.projectName: A Scientometrics Analysis of Research Productivity and Influence of universities in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Pakistan, according to the nature, is proud to be the top most country with the biggest rise in research output in 2018. This rise is thanks to tremendous efforts by Higher Education Commission (HEC), Pakistan which has given due importance to research and innovation in last two decades.  We intend to carry out Scientometrics based ranking of higher education institutes at three levels purely based on research productivity and influence. At macro-level, higher education institutes, at meso-level, department and then at micro-level, researchers will be ranked using the state of the art Scientometrics measures. Focusing on ranking at these three levels will help HEC to analyze, in a better way, how the research work is going on various levels, to compare and explore shortcomings in various levels and to set various future based targets for universities as well as departments. In addition to ranking based on history, trends in recent years will also be analyzed. In addition to finding top most productive as well top influential authors, rising stars authors in research horizon will be explored. The ranking will be carried out various factors such as number or publications, number of citations, the significance level of publication venue such as journal and conference, the position of the authors in the co-author list. We aim to present the work carried out in the form of a web-based system which will be based on dataset extracted from web of science, which is regarded as the authentic source for publication by HEC. The proposed system is intended to be similar like Arnetminer which is well known Scientometrics based system for worldwide authors in general and for Chinese universities and authors in particular. The system will be helpful for HEC for many decisions.

data.projectName: Investigating the Manchar Lake Ecosystem under different management and climatic scenarios
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
There are numerous wetlands in Pakistan, providing several services to surrounding communities, including fresh water, food, and livelihood sources. But, unfortunately, most of these wetlands are facing several challenges due to climate change, pollution from industries, domestic and agricultural discharges, tourist’s activities, mismanagement and governmental negligence (Nawab et al., 2018). 
Manchar Lake in Sindh province of Pakistan is an example of such a degraded wetland, whose ecological health has suffered not only due to decline in fresh water inflows caused by low rainfalls and higher evaporation losses; but also due to disposal of huge amount of untreated municipal and agricultural wastes into the lake. Resultantly, the water quality of the Lake is not fit for human consumption. This has also affected the agricultural production of the land cultivated with Lake water, loss of lake’s aquatic biodiversity including migratory birds; but also affected the livelihood of the farmers and the fishermen (Kazi et al., 2009). 
This research effort will provide spatial and temporal variations of the lake water quality; that will help in identifying the sources and trends of water pollution. The ecosystems services valuation will provide economic value of the services offered by the lake, as well as the economic costs of wetland degradation. GIS, remote sensing and modeling tools will help in framing strategies to reduce lake pollution under future management and climatic scenarios.

This research effort will provide spatial and temporal variations of the lake water quality; that will help in identifying the sources and trends of water pollution. The ecosystems services valuation will provide economic value of the services offered by the lake, as well as the economic costs of wetland degradation. GIS, remote sensing and modeling tools will help in framing strategies to reduce lake pollution under future management and climatic scenarios.

data.projectName: INTERACTIVE EFFECT OF PLANT GROWTH-PROMOTING RHIZOBACTERIA, SILICON AND PRESSMUD ON AMELIORATING SALINITY STRESS IN MAIZE
data.projectDigest: Salinity is one of the most common environmental stresses, adversely affecting the soil quality of agricultural lands and limits crop productivity worldwide, especially in arid and semiarid regions of the world. In Pakistan, about 6.8 million hectares of land are affected by salinity that reduce crop productivity. For maize, Na+ is the primary cause of ion specific damage. So, there is the need to reclaim saline soils in Pakistan. For that, salt-tolerant plant growth promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) in saline agriculture can be utilized for enhancing crop productivity. Silicon can also be applied to reduce the negative effects of soil salinity on plants. The pressmud usually contains 15-20% organic matter that is highly soluble and available to the microbial activity and soil. Due to microbial activity more CO2 is produced that may increase the solubility of lime and hence reclaim saline soils. So, the combine application of PGPR, silicon and pressmud can reduce salinity stress in maize. Several PGPR strains will be isolated and screened from maize rhizosphere based on ACC-deaminase production and salinity-tolerant assay. Potential strains in combination with silicon and pressmud will be evaluated to improve growth, quality and yield of maize crop under saline-stressed pot and field conditions.

data.projectName: Development of a Road Asset Management System using a Dynamic Approach
data.projectDigest:
Road asset management systems (RAMS) are critical for cost-effective maintenance of our roads network in a functional state. A RAMS typically includes: detailed roads inventory; pavement condition data, pavement deterioration models and decision aids for prioritization and allocation of funds. Properly developed RAMS are currently lacking in the country. This research is aimed at addressing this crucial need. A 3D scanning device – providing accuracy, offering limited to no traffic interruptions and rapid collection and analysis rates – is proposed to collect road condition data. Based on the collected data, a pavement deterioration model will be developed which shall predict the future condition state of a road segment based on its current condition, age, material, traffic and soil data. Next, a system dynamics (SD) based decision model will be developed for optimum prioritization of maintenance projects. The dynamic complexity arising due to the interconnectedness and feedback loops among technical, financial and social subsystems necessitates an SD approach.
This research shall demonstrate effectiveness of 3D scanning technology for road condition assessments, and make available a road condition database, pavement deterioration model(s), and a decision aiding model for the use of public agencies and researchers around the country.

data.projectName: Establishing TSH Reference Range for the Pakistani Population
data.projectDigest: The region where Pakistan is located is historically endemic to the iodine deficiency disorders. The current situation is also not so encouraging in spite of the fact that there was considerable improvement in the area in the recent years. Iodine become the integral part of the thyroid hormones triggered by thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH). At clinical level one of the most important biological indicator for thyroid related disorders is TSH. For example, the diagnosis of hypothyroidism depends on the upper limit of the TSH reference interval. However, the correct diagnosis of the thyroid related problems largely depends on the TSH reference inetrval established on local population, as the reference range varies with various factors like history of iodine supply to the region and current iodine nutritional status of the population apart from others. The regions across the world with current iodine deficient status i.e. Europe, the TSH reference interval tends to be lower than where there is iodine sufficiency i.e. North America and East Asia. The regions going from historical deficiency to sufficiency in terms of iodine supplementation to the population the TSH reference interval shift from left to right. This was observed in a study in the North-East German population. Clinically, the incorrect use of TSH reference interval can lead to misdiagnosis and mis prescription, proved in many studies. The unbalanced current and historical iodine nutritional status of Pakistani population urge to conduct a study with pure population-based design to develop a local TSH reference interval to avoid misdiagnosis and mis prescription and unnecessary clinical work up. This will save the extra financial burdon on the health care system of Pakistan. This study would be the first of its

data.projectName: ROLE OF FLAVONOIDS FRACTIONS ISOLATED FROM MEMBERS OF FAMILY RUTACEAE IN THE TREATMENT OF RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS
data.projectDigest:
Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disease, targeting various joints,
causing chronic inflammation. Its etiology is not known but affects the life style
of almost 1% of world population by causing functional Disability (Bandawane
et al., 2014; Choudhary et al., 2014). The overall prevalence of RA has been
reported to be very high in Western world when compared with third world
countries (Akhter et al., 2011). In Pakistan, its prevalence is more in northern
areas (0.14%) than Western (0.55%) populations. Moreover, female are the
more victim of RA (75%) as compared to male (25%) of reported cases (Alam
et al., 2011). The current treatment regimen for RA primarily focuses on the
control of inflammation. Unfortunately, allopathic drugs frequently prescribed
the physician along with other disease modifying agents accounts for large
number of unwanted effects (Aburjai et al., 2007; Thite et al., 2014). Thus, the
investigation for new therapeutic agents with considerable efficacy and safety
is the goal of researchers around the world, for which secondary metabolites
like flavonoids could be best option, once proved in scientifically.
Flavonoids has been reported to have anti-arthritic potential (Sharma
& Jnameda, 2014). Our project will deal with the scientific validation of
flavonoids from selected medicinal plants of Family Rutaceae, which needs
pharmacological foundation in terms of efficacy and safety.

data.projectName: Tackling poverty and inequality through equitable access to quality education in Balochistan
data.piUniversity: Lasbela University of Agriculture, Water and Marine Sciences, Lasbela
data.projectDigest: This proposed research programme will investigate the relationship between inequality, early childhood, education, and poverty reduction in three regions of Balochistan. We plan to examine how families fall into and break out of poverty, and how their poverty is transmitted from one generation to the other. Since early childhood is a crucial stage, we want to identify the pathways through which poverty affects the cognitive and non-cognitive skills development of young children, and then shape their educational experiences and later success in the labour market. The overarching aims of the programme are: (a) identify best ways to alleviate poverty; (b) identify ways for equal and better development of children at the early stages of their life; (c) improve schools so that they are accessible for everyone and provide quality learning to all; and lastly, (d) identify the livelihood and employment opportunities and the transition of the educated and skilled youth into labour markets for sustainable development.

data.projectName: Design, 3D printing and evaluation of high performance auxetic structures
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest: Sandwich structures have found numerous applications in aircraft, aerospace and automotive industries. The structures with negative Poisson’s ratio (called auxetic structures) can withstand greater loads in comparison to traditional ones with positive Poisson’s ratio and having equal weight, due to a fact that they experience contraction rather than expansion in lateral direction when axially loaded under compression (say). They have usually complicated design and, therefore, experience difficulty in fabrication phase. Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) is a free form 3D printing technique and can easily build such structures. The main aim of this research is to design and build, employing FDM, lightweight advanced auxetic structures (ASs) with high mechanical performance. A three-step strategy will be applied to achieve the target goal: (i) advanced structure design, (ii) topology optimization, and (iii) employment of advanced materials. The auxetic structures will be built employing three envisaging 03 advanced structures and 03 advanced materials. The structures performance will be evaluated by doing mechanical tests thereby allowing identification of the best one. This research will prove as an innovative solution for lightweight vehicle design and manufacture, and a step forward towards indigenization and competence building for aeronautical, aerospace and automotive industries of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Designing and Fabrication of Low Cost Ozone Generator and An Industrial Scale Treatment Plant for Pharmaceutical Effluent Treatment
data.projectDigest: The application of ozone for the improvement of the environment is of very wide range which includes disinfection of drinking water, treatment of waste water (especially Pharmaceutical and textile effluents) sterilization of operation theatres, hotel/living rooms from bacteria, bugs, mosquitos, cockroaches and smell. Drinking/beverages water companies are using large scale ozone generators to disinfect and increase the shelve life of their products. Pharmaceutical industries produce huge quantity of highly polluted wastewater with organic and inorganic load and discharge untreated wastewater into domestic sewage networks which contain large amounts of non-biodegradable & antibiotics composites. However, the occurrence of pharmaceuticals in the environment is gaining much more attention as posing serious threats to environmental health. Biological treatment of pharmaceutical wastewater is impossible due antibiotics in the effluent, or it will propagate the antibiotics resistant bacteria. The best option is to treat this effluent with ozone which has best results and its half live is only 30 minutes after treatment, it requires no raw materials or addition of the chemicals. The development of local ozone generator at low price with improved technology will be the best solution for the treatment of different industrial effluents especially pharmaceutical and textile.

data.projectName: Encouraging Tourism Behavior in Pakistan for Psychological well-being: An effective approach of User-Generated Content (UGC)
data.projectDigest: The Travel and Tourism Competitiveness Index (TTCI) evaluates “the set of issues and policies that permit the sustainable development of the Travel & Tourism sector, which, in turn, imparts to the growth and competitiveness of a country. It should not be a surprise that ranking of Pakistan is 121 out of 140 countries as per the Report TTCI, 2019, which is very low.  There is a vast array of factors responsible for this low ranking. These factors include, but not limited to, Business environment, Safety and Security, health and hygiene, Human Resource and Labour Market, Prioritization of Travel and Tourism, and ICT readiness. Besides these primary factors, one of a significant reason behind lagging is inadequate marketing and promotion and little use of ICT & Social media. In order to encourage tourism on sustainable grounds, user-generated content like Blogs, Vlogs, generating hashtags, posts, reviews, social media shares, face book pages etc. has a strong potential to act as a catalyst. This research project is intended to study the mediation role of UGC in order to spur growth in tourism in Pakistan for achieving psychological well-being. This project is aiming to collaborate with Pakistan Tourism Development Corporation (PTDC) and University of Malakand, Lower Dir, KPK.

data.projectName: Investigations on Biofuel production potential of Arundo donax influenced by biochemical characteristics
data.projectDigest: The rapid run out of fossil fuels made the world to consume renewable-energy resources such as biofuel to meet the increasing demands of fuels in order to satisfy both the industrial and domestic demands (Tyea et al., 2012).   Arundo donax is a good lignocellulosic biomass (LB), naturally growing in Pakistan, which comprises cellulose, hemicelluloses, lignin and pectin. Cellulose and hemicelluloses after hydrolysis can be converted to sugars which can further be fermented to bioethanol. Lignin impedes enzymatic hydrolysis of cellulose and hemicelluloses. Therefore appropriate pretreatments are required to deconstruct the structure of lignocellulose in order to overcome the recalcitrance of LB and increase the yield of fermentable sugars ultimately to enhance the yield of bioethanol.Microbiological and chemical pretreatments were found to change the content of total chemical compositions in Arundo donax biomass. Alkaline Hydrogen peroxide is well documented in literature for removing lignin and xylan, decreasing cellulose crystallinity and swelling of LB, thereby decreasing the recalcitrance of LB and enhancing the hydrolysis of cellulose. In addition, lime pretreatment is reported to increase the yield of glucose and xylose. No furfural or hydroxy methyl furfural are reported to be detected with these both lime and H2O2 treatments. The current project is proposed to explore the effect of H2O2 and lime pretreatments on yield of sugars and bioethanol from Arundo donax.Pretreatments with Trichoderma spp.and Alcaligenes pakistanensis NCCP-650T a and Cellulomonas spp. have a significant effect on the cellulosic, hemicellulosic and lignin content of LB biomass.

data.projectName: Comparative effect of dietary inclusion of domestic fly (Musca domesticus) larva meal on the production performance, blood profile, immune response and nutrient digestibility of broiler
data.projectDigest:
Eggs and poultry meat are considered to be one of the best sources of animal protein of high biological value. Poultry production has assumed the status of one of the leading sectors in the country. However, in Pakistan the bulk of soybean meal for animal feed production, especially for poultry feed, is imported which has led to increase production cost of poultry. Due to high price of imported feed ingredients feed cost accounts for more than 75% of the total cost of poultry production. Increasing cost of feed ingredients, especially soybean meal, has slowed down the growth of the poultry business in the country. Therefore it is dire need to find alternative sustainable good quality protein resources that can replace/substitute soybean meal in poultry nutrition. Such an option of economical and quality protein source may be provided by insect larva meal.
Food and Agriculture Organization has stressed upon the urgent need to explore alternative feed resources such as insect meal to fulfill the increasing demand for animal products for the growing world population (FAO, 2014). Among the insect species that have been gaining attention as alternatives to the conventional feedstuffs, larvae meal is certainly one of the most promising protein sources. Fly larva meal has been investigated as appealing for poultry  due to its good nutritional profile  therefore, it may be used a possible substitute for soybean meal.

data.projectDigest: Cancer is the growing global threat and never-ending battle. Among all cancers, breast cancer is an obvious issue in females all over the world. Recently, Pakistan has reported with high frequency of breast cancer in Asia and it will pose a greater disease burden in future. In Pakistan due to dearth of awareness and socio-cultural restrictions women are forced to keep the disease secret leading to late disease diagnosis with loss of 40,000 lives every year due to breast cancer. Even with massive efforts and promising progress in cancer research the cancer war remains a major challenge. As tumor grow, they acquire vast number of DNA mutations and mutant protein products in tumor cell that can give rise to novel antigen called “neoantigen”. Neoantigens are absent in normal tissues. Recent studies confirmed the critical role of neoantigens in reawaking the immune system. The immune system of human is the newest technology in war against cancer. Treating the cancer with human own immune system is a promising cancer therapeutics approach. The proposed project is designed to identify tumor specific neoantigens in breast cancer patients of Pakistani population using high throughput NGS technologies and cutting-edge bioinformatics algorithms. Therefore, neoantigen based vaccine design is potentially attractive with the hope to increase number of super-survivors in breast cancer.

data.projectName: Genetic Determinants of Male Human Infertility in Azoospermic and Oligozoospermic patients of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
data.projectDigest: Infertility can be defined as the inability to have conception after one year of unprotected intercourse beside the fact that the female is medically fertile. The main causes leading to male human infertility include varicocele, any obstruction in the sperm ducts, agglutination of spermatozoa, semen abnormally viscous, necrosis of spermatozoa, ejaculatory product in lesser amount, abnormalities in ejaculation process, or the sperms are too much dense. If the cause is not known, the condition is called idiopathic infertility. On the basis of their mean sperm concentrations, the men can be categorized as having azoospermia having no sperms, severe oligospermia (<5 million sperm per milliliter), oligospermia (5 million to <20 million sperm per milliliter), or normospermia (?20 million sperm per milliliter). Cytogenetic analysis of men with Y-chromosome translocations has revealed a region on the long (q) arm of the Y chromosome that is required for spermatogenesis. This region includes the azoospermia factor (AZF) locus, which contains a gene or genes required for normal spermatogenesis. In addition to AZF genes, Estrogen hormone and heat shock factor (HSF) are also the key players regulating the process of spermatogenesis and spermiogenesis. Hence, keeping in view the cultural, social and territorial values of Pashtun ethnicity in the southern belt of KP, the issue of male human infertility is addressed as Pashtun loves to have male children and that no work has been done in this regard. In this connection, the hormonal and sperm abnormalities are going to be analyzed using ELIZA technique and microscopy respectively while the genetic basis will be characterized through advanced techniques such PCR and sequencing. data.projectName: Application of electrospinning based antibiotic loaded stimulus responsive polymeric nanomaterials onto microneedle based platforms: Programmed drug delivery in wound management
data.projectDigest: The peripheral body organs with low blood supply such as skin are at higher risk infections and prolonged injuries as the defense system of the body is less effective in combating the germs. An antibiotic containing nanomaterial loaded implants may be more efficient choice for providing customized drug delivery in these conditions. This research project will aim the preparation of antibiotic loaded polymeric nanomaterials using electrospinning technique. These nanoparticles will be employed to the novel implants e.g. microneedle patches. The prepared formulation will be assessed for physicochemical properties using DSC, XRD, SEM. The in vitro drug release and antimicrobial activities will also be assessed cultures. Furthermore, therapeutic effectiveness will be determined in the infected skin wound of laboratory animals. In the last stage of this research project, a histologic study of the skin samples collected at temporal scale will be performed to mechanistic evidence of the healing process in the presence these novel dosage forms. The results will be summarized and a report will be submitted to the Higher education commission of Pakistan. The results will also be presented in the professional forums such as conferences and pharmaceutical industry.

data.projectName: Edge Metric Dimension and Fault-Tolerant Edge Metric Dimension for Families of Planar Graphs
data.projectDigest: Metric dimension is used in any arbitrary environment to explore the different ideas of navigation. It is sufficient to describe a workplace as vertex in a graph and edges denote the links between vertices. It is a very useful to minimize the devices in a network for finding the location of vertices, by using each vertex not more than once. The problem can be described by means of networks, where locations are connected to which a navigating robot passes from one place to another. A network's locations, where we put the robots are called places. The least number of places needed to find from every place in the network is called the metric dimension and the set of the minimum number of places is the metric basis. These notions have applications in the field of social sciences, physical sciences, networking, intruder location problem, master mind games and pharmaceutical chemistry. We consider fault-tolerant resolving sets for which the failure of any single station in resolving set leaves us with a set that is still is a resolving set. It means if in a network our one station is out of order then the remaining stations will still work without any interruption.

data.projectName: Artificial Intelligence based Energy Conservation System
data.piUniversity: CECOS University of Information Technology and Emerging Sciences, Peshawar
data.projectDigest: The idea of “Smart Building” has caught the researcher’s attention from a long time. By equipping the environment with sensors and other intelligent devices, the realization of the smart building concepts is made possible. Different smart buildings have been developed for different purposes, ranging from smart offices and smart homes to smart grids. This project is related to the design and development of an energy conservation system on the consumption (demand) side. The aim of this research is to develop an energy conservation system for buildings using smart technologies and artificial intelligence. The proposed system would allow (1) automation of tasks (e.g., turning the lights on when a person enters a room), (2) task scheduling (e.g., turning off the AC at 05:00 pm), and (3) setting task priorities (e.g., override the schedule if the person is setting late in the office). Considering these three aspects, it is believed that the proposed system would not only considerably reduce energy consumption, but would also improve the comfort and quality of life of its users. The proposed system would operate on the environmental data captured through sensors and other intelligent devices. This data would be processed and used to control the appliances based on the developed protocols. Further, machine learning algorithms would be used to monitor and learn the energy consumption behavior of individuals and then control the system accordingly. Another major component of the proposed system is an online platform, where all the generated data would be captured. This data would be processed using Artificial Intelligence techniques and Big Data analytics to make it useful for policy and decision making. Thus, the proposed system can be used by the government and power suppliers

data.projectName: PorAutomated Portable Electrocardiogram (ECG) Monitoring Device
data.projectDigest:
The scope of project in nutshell is to design and develop an automated, portable ECG machine that is available to a suspected or known heart patient. The problem with heart related diseases is that the anomaly condition can occur for some time and then disappear. It is important to record the ECG in that timeframe but the patient generally cannot access a hospital so readily. Systems are available which can be made available to the patient to record the data when he or she feels there is a problem. But then the second issue comes in, which is that the patient may not be able to identify that the medical 
condition being experienced is related to the heart. Also this piece of biomedical equipment is highly expensive.  This innovation aims to circumvent both issues

data.projectName: Commercialization and targeted mapping of super biomolecules against diabetes and breast cancer from genus Aphlandra.
data.projectDigest: The synthesis of natural products continues to be important. It provides new methodology, new reactions and techniques. It also provides alternative sources of natural compounds and offers routes to related but unnatural analogs. Chemists have a compelling curiosity to discover what compounds Nature provides, but to obtain this information it is necessary to isolate compounds from their natural source and to determine their structures. Cancer is the rapid and uncontrollable proliferation of the cell and is major health issue of the present time. Cancer can affect all the major organs in the body and large numbers of people die annually due to this disease. There are a number of drugs available for the treatment of cancer but they are not selective in their actions and also associated with adverse effects.  Diabetes is a condition that impairs the body's ability to process blood glucose. Natural products have long been used in traditional systems of medicine for diabetes. In the present studies, Super biomolecules was isolated characterized elucidated and then synthesized. These super biomolecules was studied in vitro as well as in vivo pharmacologically. The synthesized compounds will be purified by using open column chromatography and repeated crystallization procedures. The chemical structures of isolated super biomolecules were established with the help of spectroscopic techniques such as ultraviolet-visible, infrared, proton nuclear magnetic resonance (1H-NMR), 13C NMR (BB, DEPT-135, 90), two-dimensional correlation techniques (HMBC, HSQC) and mass spectrometry. On the basis of results obtained by these studies, super biomolecules will be selected for clinical trials and drug development in collaboration with pharmaceutical industries.

data.projectName: Satellite Remote Sensing Temporal and Spatial Observations for the determination and validation of the Land Surface Temperature and Vegetation Imagery for the Natural Disaster’s Drought and Flood Conditions over the Cropland of Punjab Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Sarhad University of Science and Information Technology, Peshawar
data.projectDigest: The global warming causes the global climate changes, and Pakistan listed in number eight of the most affected ten countries from 1995-2014 in the world. Since 1900, the natural disasters in response to drought and flood are the most common and frequently occurring hazards due to environmental, climatic and ecosystem anthropogenic factors in the region like Pakistan. Droughts and floods are the world’s costliest natural disasters due to extreme climate events under global warming conditions. Since many years ago, there have been attempts to identify ecological conditions concerning vegetation worldwide. For example, the unique spectral response of vegetation makes it possible to differentiate vegetation from other surface material remotely.  Starting from the point that Earth is an integrated complex system, with strong coupling among atmosphere, hydrosphere and biosphere processes, remote sensing represents a unique and valuable source of information to monitor changing conditions in both the atmosphere and on the Earth's surface at a variety of spatial and temporal scales. As remote sensing undergoes further technical evolution, novel remote sensing methods continue to be applied.This research study expose the Natural Hazards in terms of Droughts and Floods conditions using the satellite and on ground data products using remote sensing indices over the region (cropland) of Punjab, Pakistan. The possible suggestions and recommendations for this region due to climate changes threats to Asia and specific to the region in the form of higher temperature, drier conditions, and flooding. Therefore, to established a mechanism and safeguard the region from the natural disasters, such as, temperature changes, heat extremes, precipitations, glacier melts, rivers and agriculture.

data.projectName: EFFECT OF TOCOTRIENOL AND RESVERATROL SUPPLEMENTATION ON CARDIOMETABOLIC RISK FACTORS AND BIOCHEMICAL MARKERS IN PATIENTS WITH METABOLIC SYNDROME
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: The metabolic syndrome is characterized by central obesity, hypertension, hyperglycemia, and dyslipidemia which increase a patient's risk of developing cardiovascular disease and diabetes mellitus. Being a global health problem, its prevalence is approximately 20–25 percent of the world’s adult population and 34% in US. Dyslipidemia, oxidative stress, increase insulin resistance and chronic inflammation are the main contributing factors in causation of the disease. Efforts to reduce cardiovascular and metabolic risk factors should be the target in the patients with metabolic syndrome. Tocotrienol and Resveratrol are nutritional supplement having hypolipidemic, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and anti-proteosomic properties, can improve the patients' health by preventing the development of hypertension, atherosclerotic heart diseases and diabetes mellitus. Several animal and human’ studies have shown beneficial effects of tocotrienol and resveratrol individually in the cardiovascular, diabetes mellitus and Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD). The present study will help in identifying the combined treatment response of delta tocotrienol and resveratrol in metabolic syndrome associated biochemical markers, cytokines and circulatory microRNAs.

data.projectName: Development of Flexible and Environmentally Safe Natural Fiber based Paper Films for Perovskite Solar Cell Applications
data.projectDigest:
Solar energy is considered the most abundant energy resources and the rate at which sun energy reaches the Earth’s surface is about 10,000 times higher than the rate at which all energy is consumed on Earth. The main objectives of research on photovoltaic (PV) material devices includes the low cost energy material in stable modules with high e?ciency. The PV industry still depends intensively on subsidies and PV provides negligible contribution to the overall energy generation market. Therefore, in order for the PV industry to be competitive with conventional fossil fuel power plants they should be environmentally friendly, while their payback time should be as short as possible.
Recently, Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have gained much attention due to their mutual advantages of good flexibility along with high e?ciency. PSCs may be prepared on either metal foil or polymer film as the substrate and showed efficiency range from 2.6 to 18.3%. The advantage of these PSCs is being light weight, flexible and small size as low as millimeters. Pakistan is an agricultural country and is remarkably ironic with biological and renewable resources like algae, pulp sludge and agriculture wastes etc. These biological and renewable resources can be considered promising candidates for the extraction of cellulose fibres. Various conductive layers and metallic nanorods can be easily deposited on the obtained flexible cellulose fibers and therefore easily be employed for the various energy devices including battery and solar cell devices. Therefore these low cost flexible films can be employed for the fabrication Perovskite solar cells

data.projectName: Development and optimization of barrier and comfort properties of biological protective clothing
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest: With the improved awareness of nosocomial infection diseases, more attention is required on safety of health professionals and patients. It is established that several microorganisms such as viruses, bacteria and fungi cause infections and transmitting diseases through infectious bodily fluids in hospitals and other environments. In addition to this, the resistance of organisms against prevailing drugs and upsurge of new pathogens necessitates the protective measures to eliminate or to reduce the risk of hospital induced infections. It is driving force for hospitals to reexamine the surgical gown practices to optimize patient and staff safety, wearer comfort as well as cost effectiveness.  Though several types of disposable (nonwoven) and reusable (woven) surgical gowns and drapes are commercially available in the global market but best of our knowledge and experience during our recent research, it was found that the health professionals are performing their duties by exposing themselves to severe health and life risks by using untreated cotton gowns. However, imported Chinese nonwoven gowns of different tags were available at some stores in big cities only. The intended research will focus on the development and optimization of reusable surgical gowns from barrier fabrics that will be fictionalized with antibacterial and hydrophobic finishes to increase bacterial resistance and eliminate the chance of  blood strike through, on the other hand their thermal comfort will be tailored by using suitable material.

data.projectName: Male Manager’s career motivation perceptions of female subordinates and female career outcomes: An examination from organizational development perspective
data.projectDigest: In workplace like men, women also need job relevant human capital to advance in their careers.  Training and development, job autonomy and challenging assignments; each of these contribute to enhancing human capital. Although all these factors are important for women’s career success but their access to these human capital development initiatives is not at per with men. Based on this, current study focuses on how the career motivation perceptions of male bosses about their female subordinates affects opportunities for female subordinates about training and development, job autonomy and challenging assignments. All of these can have effect on the career outcomes of female employees including their career aspirations, career competence and career optimism. In this regard situational factors can play an important role, if women have diversity climate in their organizations, they will be better able to participate in challenging assignments, training and development activities and have job autonomy. These three factors can lead to positive career outcomes if women have a strong need for achievement. In this case they will be able to develop positive career aspirations, career optimism and career competence. This basic research will empirically investigate these propositions with filed survey data from Pakistani working women and their male bosses.

data.projectName: Forgery Detection of Digital Images and videos for Multimedia Security, Crime Detection and Prevention
data.projectDigest:
Forensic analysis of digital images and videos is a recent research area in multimedia security. The application of digital imaging and video  has increased in recent years due to the availability of low-cost and high resolution digital cameras and user-friendly digital image and video  manipulation software. The proposed project will focus on developing new techniques for robust and reliable image and video forgery detection. In particular, we will focus on detecting intrinsic imbalances and structural changes through texture analysis, using deep learning.  To model the texture of images and videos  we will use multi-resolution techniques together with deep learning. The extracted information will then be provided as input to a suitable classifier for decision making. For classification, we plan to investigate classification techniques like Support Vector Machines (SVM) and Random Forests. Public ally available benchmark data sets will be used for evaluation. The main deliverable of this project will be a robust and reliable solution for image forgery detection to meet the following objectives:
1.	Protection of society against the misuse of forged images and videos, propaganda, and coercion.
2.	Reliable reporting of images and videos for media channels.
3.	Making evidences of images and videos acceptable for investigation agencies and courts of law.

data.projectName: Assessment and Management of communication and body language problems of transgender
data.projectDigest:
According to national census 2017, the transgender persons are reported 10,418 while 7,651 lived in urban areas and 2,767 in villages. In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa 690 transgender persons lived in urban areas and 223 in rural areas. A leader of transgender rights group Mona Ali claim that there are 400,000 to 500,000 transgender person only live in the Punjab province (Rao, 2017). The said population cannot cope with the community because of their communication and body language problems. It is the need of time to help this segment of population to become a useful citizen of this country.
Current project is aimed at addressing the emerging issue of self-perception of body language and voice-related quality of life among transgender. A representative sample of transgender will be taken by Purposive sampling. The recruited sample will be screened for Transsexual Voice Questionnaire (TVQMtF) developed by Dacakis et al. (2013). Individual as well as group interventions will be used to address communication and body language problems among transgender.

data.projectName: Exploration of  Skills and Traits Required for CPEC Medium and Long Term Projects
data.projectDigest: CPEC has been considered to be the game changer for Pakistan as it is a mega project which plays a significant role to improve economy of Pakistan. But unfortunately, at the current time even Pakistan is rich in Human resource as high percentage of youth bulge, however, to have an understanding of the skills and traits required for Pakistan’s workforce is a big problem. The mega projects under CPEC will not be able to bring economic prosperity for the country without knowing and producing required skills and traits in workforce for the various sectors in medium and long term projects. Government of Pakistan has been trying to know the required skills and traits for CPEC projects. In this connection, to help the Government of Pakistan the objective of this study is to find out the skills and traits required for CPEC medium and long term projects. In the first phase experts will be identified to take the interviews for this research. They will be Government officials, United National Development Program (UNDP) personnel, Chamber of Commerce members, CPEC Personnel, and Academic experts from Baluchistan, Sindh, Punjab, KPK and Gilgit Baltistan. In the second Phase experts will be selected to prioritize the skills and traits and analyze by using AHP technique.  Initially, 16 experts from Karachi have been interviewed to check the feasibility of current research proposal. This research will help the Government to develop the strategies to prepare youth with the important skills and traits required for CPEC projects to achieve strategic goals of Pakistan from CPEC. data.projectName: Developing strategy for production of somaclonal variants in cut flowers
data.projectDigest: Production of cut flowers is considered as profitable business in the developed as well as developing countries of the world. Cut flowers are considered as high value product in the trade market of world having worth of almost 8.29 Billion US dollar. Pakistan has diverse agro-ecological zones that facilitate the production of different cut flowers. The economic returns are also high as compared to other conventional crops and also feasible for small land holders. So, Pakistan has great potential for production of cut flowers to meet the increasing need of local demand and also to earn foreign exchange through export. The major cost in the cultivation of cut flowers (gladiolus and tuberose) is planting material in the form of corms/bulbs due to import from other countries. As Pakistan has not developed a single cultivar of cut flowers especially gladiolus and tuberose due to deficiency of research in area of genetic improvement. So, present research project is designed for genetic improvement of important cut flowers including gladiolus and tuberose. To do so, plant tissue technique will be used to induce variations in the genetic material of selected cut flowers that will reflect the change in the morphological characteristics.

data.projectName: Development of ?¬-caryophyllene self-nano emulsifying drug delivery system for treatment of diabetic neuropathic pain
data.projectDigest: Diabetic neuropathic pain (DNP) is common complication of diabetes. Currently, only duloxetine, pregabalin and tapentadol are approved in the United States for the treatment of DNP with unsatisfactory pain relief for most patients which necessitates the search of new drugs. ?-Caryophyllene (BCP) has been reported to ameliorate DNP. BCP is approved by the FDA for dietary use due to its low toxicity. Therefore, its safety profile and ef?cacy makes it a potential compound for treatment and prevention of a wide variety of diseases including DNP. But BCP is characterized by high lipophilicity and poor stability in hydrophilic media which limit its absorption and bioavailability. Various reports suggest the bioavailability of some poorly water-soluble drugs can be improved by formulating their SNEDDS. In this research work BCP bioavailability will be attempted to enhance through SNEDDS formulation and will be characterized and evaluated In-vitro and In-vivo to make it a drug substance for treatment of DNP.

data.projectName: CRISPR-Cas9 mediated knockout of pro-survival BCL2 family proteins from breast and small-cell carcinoma cell lines
data.projectDigest: Cancer cells acquire the ability to suppress apoptosis and invade the other areas of the body of organisms. Apoptosis or programmed cell death is a mechanism by which living organisms eliminate dysfunctional or potentially dangerous cells, for example, cancer cells. Modulation of the cellular death is mediated by the pro-survival and anti-apoptosis cell signaling cascades that comprise of a variety of proteins. One of the key protein families involved in induction and suppression of apoptotic cell death is BCL-2 which has long been characterized for its vital role in apoptosis and comprises of more than 20 pro- and anti-apoptosis regulatory proteins. Individual members of the BCL-2 family interfere with mitochondrial integrity which leads to either activation or prevention of apoptotic cytotoxicity. Unbalanced expression of BCL-2 family members can activate pro-survival pathways via stimulation of resistance to apoptotic cell death which ultimately facilitates growth of cancer cells and confers resistance to anticancer therapy. On the basis of this fact that cancer cells manipulate expression of these proteins to evade apoptosis, a variety of inhibitors of BCL-2 family have been developed. Current study aims at knocking out of the pro-survival genes of the BCL-2 family by using CRISPR-Cas9 genome engineering in various cancer cell lines including breast cancer and small-cell lung cancer cell lines. Furthermore, chemotherapeutics will be employed in BCL-2 knockout cell lines to see the changes of knocking out these genes in various cell lines. Consequently, the study will aid in better understanding of the role of BCL-2 proteins in modulating the apoptotic cellular toxicity pathways in cancer cells which will help in rendering the cancer cells responsive to chemotherapy.

data.projectName: Barriers to Youth Entrepreneurship in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Modern Languages, Islamabad (NUML)
data.projectDigest:
The utmost aim of this study is to explore the barriers to youth entrepreneurship (BYE) in Pakistan. This study is designed to examine the effect of barriers to youth entrepreneurship (BYE) on entrepreneurial intentions (EI) and the subsequent impact on entrepreneurial actions (EA) in the presence of moderating role of Entrepreneurial Education (EE) in the youth of Pakistan. 
The project will consist of a series of five studies. The students of bachelor and master are in business administration of about thirty universities from all over Pakistan will participate in the studies. The study will have value at both the scholarly and practice level. At a scholarly level, the study will explore a new phenomenon of barriers to youth entrepreneurship and develop a reliable and valid questionnaire in the context of Pakistan. This project will investigate important contemporary issues of entrepreneurship within neglected groups of youth studying in universities of Pakistan. It will help the academicians in the development of the entrepreneurship curriculum for promoting entrepreneurship. 
The results of this study will address the issue of unemployment by promoting entrepreneurial culture. Findings of this study will help policymakers in designing the interventions to promote the entrepreneurship ecosystem in the country.

data.projectName: Safe and secure software-defined vehicular communications under foggy weather
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: The vehicular communication allows different vehicular users to take timely decisions while moving on roads. We all know that road accidents are cause of thousands of deaths all over the Pakistan every year. Due to the lack of safe and secure vehicular networking, the citizens have been suffering from critical traffic situations for years. The situation gets even more worst during foggy weather when all highways and motorways remain closed for long hours. In this project, we will design safe and secure communication protocols for vehicular networks based on software-defined networking (SDN) technology to provide efficient vehicular networking under foggy weather in Pakistan.  Compared to traditional protocols existing in literature, this project will ensure timely decision taken by drivers by considering the periodic exchange of alarming messages using SDN technology for different visibility scenarios on fog shrouded roads.

data.projectName: Characterization of Venom Proteome of Terrestrial Snakes of Pakistan for Development of Antivenom Vaccines
data.projectDigest: Snake bite is a significant problem of rural areas of Pakistan, especially agriculture workers. Pakistan is inhabited more than 97 species of snake. The most common species of snake  which are responsible for envenoming are Russell’s Viper,  Naja naja, Bungarus caeruleus, and Echis carinatus .Venom is the complex mixture of protein, peptides and enzymes with many others toxic and lethal substances. There are large differences in venom compositions, even inside a single species. The efficacy of antivenom to treat snake envenoming and its ability to neutralize and reverse the toxic effects of the venom toxins can be increased by its proteome analysis. The chemical characterization of venom (toxicological and enzymatic studies) is important for the production of snake antivenom immunoglobulins(vaccines).

data.projectName: Development of thermo- tolerant rice for sustainable rice production  under  climate change scenario
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: Development of thermo-tolerant rice is one of the most sustainable and economical intervention to combat the climate change. During the proposed project, an integrated approach involving, seedling stage screening, field testing, molecular and physio-biochemical approach will be applied for the selection of thermo tolerant rice. Results based on integrated data are effectively translated to farmer’s field. Thermo-tolerant rice, developed through the proposed project, has very strong prospects for registration as variety in the national variety registration program. Therefore, at the end of the project, at least two non-Basmati and two Basmati thermo-tolerant rice lines will be contributed in the National Uniform Rice Yield Trials (NURYTs) for variety registration with relevant Provincial and Federal agencies.

data.projectName: Are Female Nurses Victimized in Developing Countries through Workplace Bullying and Harassment?
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan, owing mainly to cultural restrictions, nursing falls in the category of those professions which has a negative image and is not welcomed among masses. Nursing is mostly seen as a feminine job and nurses are considered powerless subordinates who report to doctors. Also, the media has repeatedly portrayed nurses as heroines and sex objects who work long shifts on Friday nights and are away from home. This has defamed the overall image of nursing which is still not considered a prestigious profession in Pakistan. Like the global trend, nurses in Pakistan also face workplace bullying and harassment with its deteriorating affect on the psychological and physiological health besides dissatisfaction with the profession itself.

data.projectName: Morphological adaptations in Family Anatidae as a physiological response to migratory stress
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Avian migration is considered a significant evolutionary adaptation in response to anatomical and physiological requirements during different seasons. Birds express this migratory cycle twice a year to and from the areas of high latitude to overwintering areas termed as Vernal and Autumnal migration, respectively. These migratory birds are a key attraction for ‘Eco-Tourism’ and studies have indicated a significant increase in revenue generation, if the number and variety of these seasonal birds increases in an area. To cope with travel stress and changing ecological conditions, birds undergo several structural and functional adaptations including body size, wing-muscle ratio, gonadal development, muscle hypertrophy, adipogenesis, etc. Also, these migrations suggest that the birds will travel long distances, inhabit a variety of environments and may have a significant epidemiological role in dissemination of antimicrobial resistant bacteria and genes as reported by world health organization (WHO). Based on these facts, this project is planned to investigate and improve our understanding of the structural and functional adaptations operating to cope with the migratory stress in these birds and their contribution towards the dissemination of AMR bacteria along the migratory route.
