data.projectName: Synthesis, Characterization and Applications of Multifunctional Organo-Modified Carbon Nanotubes and Their Metal Complexes
data.projectDigest: It is now desirable that the materials used in different areas of the industry are to be multifunctional. Such materials have many advantages both economically and scientifically, relative to synthesized and/or produced materials for a single target. For this reason, the synthesis of materials to be used in more than one field is of great importance. CNTs were firstly discovered in 1991 and started to produce on industrial scale in recent years. CNTs produced as single and/or multi-walled do not have any functional group. These materials need to be modified with different compounds in order to be used in different areas of the industry. For this reason, this project is aimed to synthesize the modified SWCNTs and MWCNTs from SWCNTs and MWCNTs. In this context, the original values of the project are to i.) convert low reactive SWCNTs and MWCNTs to smart materials, ii.) use the synthesized materials in energy storage, removal of metal ions and the immobilization of peroxidase enzyme which has not been reported in the literature till date, iii.) synthesize the adsorbent materials showing selectivity to certain metal ions, iv.) focus on multiple uses for a single product, and v.) publish/patent the outcomes of the proposed project.

data.projectName: Modeling of electric vehicle charging stations, battery swapping stations and non-dispatchable generations for Karachi
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Awareness of Government and Society on the dynamic fuel cost and adverse environmental impact of conventional sources has promoted the rapid growth of both renewable energy-based generation, such as solar, wind, hydro etc. and electric vehicles in Pakistan. Few studies recommended policy regarding electric vehicles and Non-dispatchable Distributed Generation, such as solar and wind in Pakistan and now requires proposition of practical solutions. Government of Pakistan has re-evaluated energy policy to target 30% share of renewable energy and electric vehicles by 2030. Therefore, this research’s aim to provide practical solution and hence establish an efficient technical and economic model of charging stations for electric vehicles and non-dispatchable distributed generation (solar/wind) for Karachi. Moreover, the effect on the grid due to transition of electric vehicles load and non-dispatchable distributed generation will be reduced based on optimum control scheme.The proposed model is to provide benefits to energy planner, electric vehicles users, investors, battery developers, utility, power grid, manufacturers of solar panel and wind turbine.

data.projectName: Design of 5G Antennas for Future Millimeter-wave Communication Systems
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Mobile technology has evolved through generations (1G-4G) to provide high
data-rates and bandwidth. However, recent dramatic increase in mobile users
has put unprecedented challenges for service providers to cope with
bandwidth overloading. These challenges have further become complicated
due to limited available bandwidth below 20 GHz spectrum. Since lower
frequency spectrum is already occupied by various civil and military
applications, the only solution to provide large bandwidth is to use higher
frequency spectrum (i.e. above 20 GHz). The International Telecommunication
Union (ITU) will launch the Fifth Generation (5G) of mobile communication by
2020. The main feature of 5G systems is to provide extremely high data-rates
in Gbps. Another feature of 5G is the implementation of IoT (Internet of Things)
concept. Different aspects of 5G systems are under research, which primarily
includes baseband signal processing, communication network topologies,
channel modelling, RF-frontend and antennas. This project will focus on the
development of antenna prototypes for 5G handheld devices. These antennas
will operate in millimeter-wave spectrum beyond 20 GHz. ITU has specified
some key operating frequency bands for 5G including 28 and 38 GHz. The
prototype antennas developed will perform as per standard specifications set
for 5G communications.

The already made projects only have kick counts or contractions counts. Another already made project had a feature    of counting the heart   rate of fetus.

data.projectName: Theoretical and Experimental Investigation of Multi-Effect Distillation (MED) for seawater desalination using Waste Heat and Solar Energy: A Sustainable Solution for Water and Energy
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest: Owing to growing world's population, underground water resources are depleting, alternate is to desalinate brackish and seawater. The existing techniques that are being adopted for seawater desalination such as reverse osmosis, electrodialysis, multi stage flash distillation (MSF) , multi effect distillation (MED) and membrane distillation pose high operational and production cost and these are not energy efficient.  However, out of these techniques, MED process has the advantages that it can be operated at very low temperature of less than 70 ?, and it can easily be integrated with waste heat and solar energy. The trend of new MED installation for seawater desalination is increasing because of the following advantages: MED consumes least amount of electricity (1.5 kWh/m3 of water produced), MED does not require any special pre-treatment of sweater and it can accommodate weather changes and concentration variation easily. Moreover, due to operation at low temperature, issues like scaling, corrosion and fouling as faced by the other seawater desalination techniques can be avoided. Furthermore, it is highly reliable, very low maintenance cost and simple to operate. The design medication and process intensification of this process has wide gap for improvements. So the aim of this proposed research study is to develop energy efficient and economically feasible desalinated system based on MED technique. The aim will be achieved through various objectives such as design and modification of MED components, process modification, integration with solar energy and waste heat, performance evaluation of MED, cost analysis and proposing road-map to commercialization.

data.projectName: Nanoparticle based bio-Fruit wax to overcome postharvest loss of fruits and vegetables
data.projectDigest: Pakistan being an agriculture based economy produces nearly 13.674 million tons of fruits and vegetables annually. 30-40% of this quantity goes wasted due to post harvest loss. Usually, 5-8% loss occurs at harvesting and 10-12% loss occurs in transportation and storage conditions of vegetable and fruits. Owing to less developed technologies for crop management in Pakistan, the socioeconomic status of farmers is very low and the business is less profitable. The solutions of post harvest loss lies in modern agriculture practices, supply chain automation and storage techniques. Pakistan imports several millions of fruit wax every year to coat the citrus fruits produced to export them. The coating not only extends shelf life but also gives aesthetically appealing look of the items. However, due to chemical nature of the wax and addition of various fungicides (thiabendazole etc.) the coating is not edible and is very injurious to health if ingested. Also, millions of foreign exchange is needed to import wax from European countries (Spain, Italy specially) whose prices raise annually. Numerous techniques have been developed locally to produce wax from organic sources but failed due to high price of product as compared to synthetic wax and limited research and development resources to modify the product as per consumer demand. Current research proposes development of cheap, easily available raw material; marine waste to formulate a low-priced product and a consortium research between two institutes to utilize best relevant intellect and R&D resources.

data.projectName: Deficiency of energy yielding vitamins and the risk of type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Diabetes mellitus type 2 (T2DM) is one of the most common causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide. The treatments based on established pathogenesis of Diabetes are not curative. The real cause of T2DM still needs to be investigated and that may help devise curative treatment of the disease. It is hypothesized that the deficiency of energy yielding vitamins is associated with increased risk of T2DM. Vitamins thiamine, riboflavin, niacin, pantothenic acid and lipoic acid (not vitamin) are coenzymes for the key steps of glucose metabolism. The lack of these vitamins may cause reduction in glycolytic activity and decreased utility of glucose by cells. Which causes intracellular and then extracellular pooling up of glucose called hyperglycemia. The levels of these vitamins, magnesium and phosphate (cofactors with key enzymes) will be measured in plasma using high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) and flame photometry in type 2 diabetic and control individuals. The main contributor of deranged vitamin levels other than diet is expected to be a functional variant of these vitamin’s transporters. The genetic variants of the thiamine transporter (SLC19A2) and niacin receptor (NIACR1) will be studied through nucleotide sequencing and association of any polymorphism detected with risk of diabetes will be checked.

data.projectName: Impact of Reduced Snow Cover and Heat-Drought Climatic Changes on Resilience of Nitrogen Cycling Ecosystem Functioning in Lower Himalayas
data.projectDigest: Global climatic changes are critical from economic and ecological perspectives and have brought ecosystem functioning in danger. Lower Himalaya is crucial from biodiversity, agricultural and touristic perspectives but their resilience limits towards global climatic changes such as reduced sno cover and heat-droughts are yet never assessed. Since our planet is expecting a severe shift in climatic regimes (a boost of 2oC), it is direly required to assess the soil functioning upon exposure to reduced snow cover and subsequent droughts. The cycling of nitrogen, an important component of living world, in soil is mainly driven by microbial communities; engines in gearing the various processes in ecosystem. A reduced or no snow cover and subsequent heat-drought are expected to leave severe impacts on N-cycling and involved microbial communities ultimately disrupting the associated services (plant productivity, greenhouse gas balance-N2O). This project will give an insight in to the fact whether N cycling-soil ecosystems are stable if a stress period is occurred (resistance) and time taken to recover once a climate shift is over (resilience). This project is important from economic and ecological perspectives, but also of high value for policy making in scenario of future expected shifts in overall climate regimes in Pakistan.

data.projectName: piRNA -Disease association database and piRNA Target tool development
data.projectDigest: In recent years, researches focusing on PIWI-interacting RNAs (piRNAs) have increased rapidly. It has been revealed that piRNAs have strong association with a wide range of diseases; thus, it becomes very important to understand piRNAs' role(s) in disease diagnosis, prognosis and assessment of treatment response. We will search articles from Pub MED and SRA using keywords, such as `PIWI-interacting RNAs' and `piRNAs', and further scrutinized the articles using text mining approaches to collect piRNAs-disease association data. These data are highly complex and heterogeneous due to various types of piRNA identifiers (IDs) and different reference genome versions. We will use data pre-processing techniques to remove the redundancy and anomalies and thus homogenized the data. After that we will apply machine learning algorithms for the association building finally, we will develop the piRDisease database, which incorporates experimentally supported data for piRNAs' relationship with wide range of diseases.

data.projectName: The development and verification of a method for accurate estimation of solar panel output power
data.projectDigest: Due to environmental concerns and energy crises in Pakistan, the application of renewable energy (RE) technologies is rapidly growing. Among RE sources, the solar photovoltaic (PV) is the most popular one being adopted by the community due to abundant availability of sun light during day time. However, due to intermittent nature of solar irradiance, the output of PV system is uncertain.  Therefore, the researchers are developing various methods to predict output power of PV source before installation of system.  However, existing approaches are unable to forecast the solar power accurately. In this project, an improved method to predict the PV power will be developed and verified which would be applied to estimate the accurate power generation before the erection of PV system. It is based on accurate training of an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) in presence of solar irradiance, PV module temperature and the application of Newton Raphson (NR) iteration on single diode model of solar cell to compute PV current and ultimately the overall PV power. Additionally, this project will make our national researchers able to access and get the data free of cost for their research.

data.projectName: PROMOTING INDEPENDENCE THROUGH BALANCE IMPROVEMENT (PIBI) PROGRAM IN ELDERLY PEOPLE
data.projectDigest: Balance is an integral component that determines the mobility and independence of an individual. A good balance can help an individual to react to sudden changes, improves coordination both of which reduces the risk of accidental fall. Balance disorders are common in older adults and are a major cause of falls in this population which exposes them to array of complication that presents as range of socio-economic challenges for individuals, families, and societies at large. Every year more than one in three people age 65 years or older fall, and the risk increases with age. Pakistan is having an elderly population of 12 million at present with is forecasted at 20 million in next couple of decades. The challenges that an increasing population of the elderly is likely to pose to the existing health delivery systems in the country are going to be tremendous. This project is typically designed to evaluate the balance related problems in community dwelling elderly population. Besides this exercise program is also designed to improve the mobility of elderly. Improving balance in elderly will not only improve physical and mental health but will also reduce the burden on health care system with reduced fall risk.

The challenges that an increasing population of the elderly is likely to pose to the existing health delivery systems in the country are going to be tremendous. This project is typically designed to evaluate the balance related problems in community dwelling elderly population. Besides this exercise program is also designed to improve the mobility of elderly. Improving balance in elderly will not only improve physical and mental health but will also reduce the burden on health care system with reduced fall risk.

data.projectName: Association between common variants and Schizophrenia as well as bipolar disorder in Pakistani population
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest: Schizophrenia and bipolar disorders are two major psychiatric disorders. Worldwide the epidemiology of both psychiatric disorders is increasing day by day. These are multifactorial disorders and both genetic and environmental factors are involved in the etiology of these disorders. In Pakistan very few studies have documented the prevalence of schizophrenia as well as bipolar disorders. Genome wide associations studies (GWASs) have emerged to be strong platforms for the association of different genes in the pathogenesis of these disorders. In this approach number of cases and control samples are analyzed simultaneously to find the association of single nucleotide polymorphism (SNPs) at different chromosomal loci with the particular disease. In case control study we analyze normal control and affected individuals simultaneously to trace out the association of SNPs inside the particular gene or in the vicinity of the particular gene. We will exploit the case control approach to trace out the role of SNPs located in risk genes which have been found to be associated with schizophrenia in Caucasian, Chinese, Japanese and other population. In the proposed study schizophrenia and bipolar disorder cases (approximately 600) will be diagnosed from affiliated hospitals of Azad Jammu and Kashmir Medical College (AJKMC) Muzaffarabad by psychiatrists according to diagnosis and statistical manual of mental disorder 4th edition (DSM-IV) and 5th edition and International Classification of Disease (ICD-10) by World Health Organization (WHO). Normal subjects will also be collected from the same population. Informed consent will be obtained from the subjects. Blood samples will be collected from the subjects and transferred to Department of Chemistry AJK University Muzaffarabad and School

data.projectName: Molecular Characterization of Bt resistance in Pink Bollworm
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest: Pink bollworm (Pectinophora gossypiella (Saunders), greater threat to cotton. Cotton in Pakistan is facing problem by devastating damage of PBW since 2013. Many management strategies have been used to control PBW, but have insufficient resulted in money and time loss. The number of insecticides used against this pest but have gained resistance. The Bt gene are useless to manage this insect. Insecticides and Bt toxins to manage lepidopteran pests of global agriculture has imposed significant selection pressure leading to the rapid evolution of insecticide resistance. At world level transgenic cotton (Bt Cry toxins) now has cultivated to control lepidopterous pest, including Helicoverpa armigera. A last two decades Cry2Ab toxin widely used for managing H. armigera, integrate with Cry1Ac to delay the onset of resistance. However, the gene identity and genetic changes conferring this resistance were unknown, as was the detailed Cry2Ab mode of action. There was no cross-resistance to Cry1Ac observed.

data.projectName: Socio-Linguistic Landscape and Solidarity: A Case Study of Tea Houses in Lahore
data.projectDigest:
The research is significant since it highlights the convergence of public ‘spaces’ into public ‘places’, a shift from intellectual to playful and unimpressible space owing to the environment provided and maintained by the owners of tea/coffee spots. People generally visit these spots for the sake of enjoyment and tend to avoid serious talk hence demeaning the socio-political impact of public sphere. However, another, more positive, aspect of these places is the strengthening of identity through solidarity reflected through code-mixing and cultural representations projected by the owners of these tea/coffee spots. It seems that these places are transforming people’s aesthetic mind-set towards non-serious activities. The proliferation of these places with localized linguistics and social realities seems to attract the people from all social classes.
Hence, it can be deduced that although the public spaces have lost their essence as suggested by Habermas (1989), they help promote an alternative means of social cohesion. Nevertheless, it is of utmost importance to explore the behavioural trends of such places through communicative and semiotic patterns of the participants for which this study is carried out.

data.projectName: Fatigue/durability analysis of composite-composite/metal airframe parts fabricated by novel hybrid joining technique
data.projectDigest:
The recent trends have shown a high utilization of composite materials in aerospace components. The attraction for composite materials in the aerospace industry lies in their exceptionally high strength-/ stiffness-to-weight ratio and superior physical properties. The application areas range from commercial planes to fighter aircrafts and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The resulting structures are not only lightweight leading to fuel economy but also enable the designer to tailor the mechanical properties as per requirement of the primary load paths. The commercial planes (airbus A380 and Boeing Dreamliner) and fighter aircrafts (Eurofighter, F-35) have more than 50% and 35-40% composites by weight respectively.
To assemble dissimilar materials, metal to composite bonding is required. It could be accomplished either during fabrication in the form of fiber metal laminates or after fabrication by metal to composite joints. This project is intended to design and develop of hybrid joint for composite-composite/metal airframe parts and investigate their fatigue/durability. This project will include the following activities:
•	development of CFRPs and GFRPs
•	surface treatments of metals
•	characterizing the modified surface
•	metal to composite joining using number of techniques
•	composite to composite joining using number of techniques
•	using different joint configurations 
•	determining the performance and durability of joints

data.projectName: SMART INTELLIGENT GAS THEFT/LEAKAGE DETECTION SYSTEM
data.projectDigest:
All throughout history, gas theft and leakage accidents have caused a lot of deaths and loss of resources all over the world. Gas controlling companies relaying on the manual system to control the leakage and theft of gas which not sufficient. Our proposed I-GAS-DS system aims to bridge the gap between handheld and household gas detectors. This system will measure the pressure of the gas and will send reports to the company accordingly. The system is MODULAR and thus, can be implemented in residential area and as well as in industrial area while being feasible for each and every consumer.
This research focuses on monitoring, controlling and protection of natural gas usage on commercial and domestic level, highlighting theft or leakage in national transmission line based on the real time data of consummation with respect to regions. 
It also focuses on upgradation of current manual system into automation to control, monitor and protect the natural gas usage in all over the country.
This search will facilitate to both the Gas Supply Company and the Stack holders, in terms of daily or monthly reports and to analyze the trends of the gas consummation at domestic or national levels.

data.projectName: Quantum graphs: surgical transformations and spectral statistics
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: This research project is aimed at the spectral estimations of quantum graphs. Quantum graphs can be imagined as a vibrating network of strings. If we pluck any of the strings, vibration carries along the whole network. Standing waves will be formed at certain fixed frequencies of the vibration. These frequencies are called eigenvalues or more generally spectrum of the network and the corresponding standing waves are called eigenfunctions. It is understandable that any change in the lengths of strings will generate a different set of frequencies. This makes it fundamentally different from the classical combinatorial networks in which lengths of strings or edges play no role. An extraordinary fact is that the eigenvalues or frequencies correspond to the discrete energy levels of certain complex quantum mechanical systems. The aim of this project is to explore the connection and precise dependence of the spectrum on the geometrical properties of quantum graphs in an effort to develop ideas and techniques for establishing sharp estimates on the spectrum in terms of structural parameters of the underlying graph.

data.projectName: RNA-Based Drugs for Targets in Cancer Pathways
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: Global cancer burden is rising at an alarming rate, the number of deaths estimated in 2015 by World Health Organization was 8.8 million. This number is projected to increase further by 45%, there is dire need for new drugs to treat this devastating disease. Perturbations of the TGF-beta signaling are at the heart of all tumorigenesis processes through their effects on cell proliferation, extracellular matrix accumulation and cancer cell invasion. We have previously shown that suppression of latent TGF-beta1 by novel small RNA drugs inhibit growth of certain cancer cell types. Therefore, the aim of this proposal is to test therapeutic properties of novel RNA-based drugs using naturally occurring and artificial nano-particles mediated delivery systems in established cancer cell lines and cultured tumor tissues from cancer patients. This will provide a proof-of the concept for the efficacy of this approach to TGF-beta targeting for cancer treatment in preclinical setting.

data.projectName: Pre- and post-harvest paddy moisture management for aflatoxins contamination-free quality basmati rice production
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: For quality basmati rice exports, rice should be aflatoxin-contamination free without any concern of maximum residue limits (MRL) while considering the judicious use of pesticides. The work will be of great significance for enhancing rice exports. For aflatoxin-contamination free rice, pre- and post- harvest moisture management can play an important role. Pre-harvest irrigation management and harvesting at proper moisture can reduce the chances of vulnerability of rice grains to be infected by diseases. Post-harvest paddy moisture management will be the second important strategy to control aflatoxin in basmati rice.   Paddy harvesting activities such as reaping, threshing and cleaning can be done manually by the labourers or by using combine harvesters (common wheat combine harvester or rice-specific Kubota harvester). Handling during manual operations or while using combine harvesters can also affect paddy quality. It is, therefore, also important to apply good harvesting methods in order to maximize grain yield and minimize damage to rice grains. Mostly, paddy is being sun-dried in our country. Traditional field drying and stacking of paddy can lead to rapid quality deterioration and increase in harvest losses. It is, therefore, important to ensure good grain quality is preserved and losses are kept minimum for each of the harvesting systems. Crop should be harvested at right time when grain moisture content is optimum. Harvesting too early can result in higher percentage of immature or unfilled grains which leads to low yield and causes grains breakage during milling and harvesting too late can lead to excessive losses owing to increased breakage of rice grains.

data.projectName: Predictors and Implications of Offending Behavior in Adolescents and Young Adults
data.projectDigest:
The objectives of this project are: (a) to investigate psychosocial factors and implications of offending behavior in adolescents and adults from educational and non-educational settings; and (b) to see the efficacy of short-term intervention to reduce offending behavior. 
In first study, two sets of samples will be taken. The first set of samples will be comprised of 300 participants after screening for offensive behavior from different public and private schools, colleges and universities of Lahore, Pakistan. The second set of samples will be comprised of 300 participants after screening for offensive behavior from non-educational settings such as workshops, labour, etc.  Both sets of samples will be matched on age, gender, education and socioeconomic status. For assessment, offending behavior scale, self-report psychopathy (SRP) scale, parent environment questionnaire, parenting dimensions inventory, child perception of inter-parental conflicts, peer pressure inventory and mental health intervention will be used.  In second study, effectiveness of short-term intervention to reduce offending behavior will be investigated in adolescents and adults who will be scored high on psychopathy traits in study one. Short term intervention of three days will be applied.  After an intervention post assessment will be conducted after one week.

data.projectName: Potential utilization and value addition of pomegranate peel extract by exploring its therapeutic and antimicrobial potential in bakery products
data.projectDigest: A growing body of publications suggests that waste from plant foods is a promising source of nutritionally and functionally important compounds such as pectin, phenolic compounds and anthocyanins. In this regard Pomegranate (Punica granatum) peel possesses excellent phytochemical profile owing to large content of polyphenols such as punicalagin, flavonoids and hydrolysable tannins. The peel of the pomegranate represents almost 26%–30% of the fruit.  This project has been designed for the value addition of this agro waste by utilizing it in bakery products to explore its therapeutic and antimicrobial potential. This study will be carried out in three phases. In first phase the raw material will be procured from different areas and will be shifted to PI’s lab for the production of pomegranate peel powder (PPP) and pomegranate peel extract (PPE). In first phase the antimicrobial potential of PPE will also be assessed. data.projectName: Development of Virtual Reality (VR) Enabled Hazard Identification System for Construction Industry of Pakistan
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Poor construction safety performance can be partly attributed to the fact that construction safety management processes rely on the hazard recognition capability of workers. Hazards that remain unidentified can potentially result in catastrophic injuries and illnesses. Despite its importance, recent research indicates that a large proportion of hazards remain unrecognized, exposing workers to unmitigated risks. Surprisingly, safety research has not adequately focused on developing specialized strategies to develop construction worker competency in hazard recognition. Therefore, the aim of the proposed project is to enhance hazard perception of construction workers using 3D simulation and virtual reality.

data.projectName: Predicting the role of the crop diversification for conservation of natural enemies to manage Spodoptera spp. in changing climate
data.projectDigest: Army worms are regular pests of many economic crops and vegetables crops, as being polyphagous. These cause 90% losses to cabbage and cauliflower crops in Pakistan. Moreover, these species have become resistant to chemicals due to frequent sprays by the growers. Plants species diversity can be helpful to in two ways i.e. to pull the pest by planting companion crop with major crop and planting the flowering plant species which provide food and shelter to natural enemies of the pests. In Africa success has been achieved to manage stem borers in maize crop in which farmers’ sow native plants such as Napier grass to attract borers. In the second type of crop diversification, the farmers in China, Thailand and Vietnam plant flowering companion plants on the sides of the rice fields to provide food and shelter to natural enemies of sucking pests. This strategy reduced 70% of chemical sprays and ultimately increased 7.5% profit to growers. Therefore, present study has been proposed to record natural enemies on host plants available round the year, selecting the appropriate hosts for companion planting. Finally, guidelines for the farmers will be developed for area wide applications to manage these pest species.

data.projectName: AI based Automated Diagnosis System for Retinal Diseases
data.projectDigest: The most common diseases in Pakistan are diabetes and hypertension among many other systematic diseases. These diseases effect the retina very badly, sometimes causing irreversible blindness. This is because earlier changes in retina are not monitored. Therefore, prior diagnosis and treatment are very important to avoid vision loss and irreversible blindness caused by diseases such as glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, age related macular degeneration etc. Pathological changes manifest themselves in part of retina called fundus.  Hence, fundus imaging is the most common and popular method for retinal analysis. There are certain pathological changes that occur in response to various diseases discussed above. These changes are generally hard to be captured by human eye. Therefore, an automated retinal analysis system need to be designed and developed for accurate diagnosis and to track the detailed pathological changes. This developed system can widely be used by ophthalmologists, general physicians treating diabetes and hypertension. It can also be used at any diagnostic center.

data.projectName: The Cultural, Civilizational and Linguistic Impacts of Hindi on Classical Urdu Ghazal
data.projectDigest: It is general perception about Urdu Ghazal that it portrays Islamic thought and culture, although it is quite right. However, we cannot deny the other cultures and civilizations which left its impact on it. The genre was related to Muslim literary traditions. Most of the critics and researchers have done their criticism and researches in this context and denied the other aspects. There are few studies of Urdu Ghazal on its Hindi impacts. A lot of work has been done on its Islamic perspectives. This study is important that nobody has critically reviewed the Hindi elements of Urdu Ghazal in detailed. This work will lead others to research and analyze other genres of Urdu literature in this context.

data.projectName: Pharmaceutical Potential of phenolic compounds from indigenous Plants against breast cancer
data.projectDigest: Breast cancer (BC) is prevailing malignancy. Drugs used for treatment of cancer adversely effects other cells. Therefore natural remedy that have no/less harm is needed. Natural  compounds are safer and can be easily biodegradable as compared to synthetic  compounds  and problem  of  drug resistance  seen  in  synthetic  drugs  is  minimized.  Mostly synthetic medicines are not biodegradable and cause toxicity therefore natural drugs are preferred to treat diseases. Our indigenous plants have many secondary metabolites that potentially have medicinal values. Quercetin is a phenolic compound found in  food materials eg onion and Plums have been found to inhibit kinase enzymes and eventually lower down cancer.  Goal of research is to find phenolic compounds from indigenous plants to cure breast cancer safely. Breast cancer cell lines will be used to test cytotoxicity and inhibition of kinase activity. The migration of cells and that cause metastasis will also be examined.

data.projectName: Synthesis and Biological Evaluation of Mono and Bis-Thiadiazine Thiones Carrying Oxadiazole, Thiadiazole and Trizoles Moities
data.projectDigest:
Heterocyclic framework is ubiquitous and found in both natural as well man made compounds, among 20 million compounds, approximately half are heterocyclic in nature. Majority of these heterocycles act as building blocks in the natural as well as pharmacologically active compounds and have unique biologically activities. According to estimation approximately 80% of the known small drugs molecules have heterocyclic motif. Some these drugs molecules such as papaverine, theobromine, quinine, emetine, theophylline, atropine, procaine, codeine, reserpine, morphine, etc. are used as life-saving drugs and these are known as natural drugs while diazepam, chlorpromazine, isoniazid, metronidazole, azidothymidine, barbiturates, antipyrine, captopril, methotrexate, etc. are known as synthetic drugs. 
Currently, our country is dire need of drug design and development, because of over population and limited resources, most of the poor peoples of Pakistan cannot afford medicines to buy and even die without getting any drug. Moreover, the common industries in general and pharmaceutical industries in specific are in the initial stages of establishment, and largely looking to west for research. Similarly, over-population and inadequate financial resources do not allow us to rely on imported medicines, which are expensive and sometime unaffordable for common people. Like India and China, if we are self-sufficient to develop drugs within the country, it will not only be cost effective and improve easy availability of these drugs in our markets but also create the job opportunities for scientific personals. Discovery of new potential therapeutic agent is an urgent demand of Pakistan. 
Based on the above diverse range biological activities of heterocycles, and current econonmic and scientific

data.projectName: In Vitro and In vivo anticancerous efficacies of medicinal plants, their active ingredients and molecular mechanisms involved in inducing cell deaths
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Cancer is number one cause of death all over the world. According to survey, 1,735,350 new cancer cases and 609,640 cancer deaths are projected to occur in the United States in 2018. Phytotherapy has been used to treat various diseases since from thousands of years. It is a fact that several pharmacological active ingredients are derivative of natural resources including herbs and medicinal plant. Several previous studies have shown that medicinal plant like olive, black seed, curcumins, and dates are effective in cancer treatment and prevention. The present modes of treatment of cancer, based on synthetic drugs, surgery and radiotherapy are toxic, expensive and alter the functions of the normal cell while traditional herbal medicines are being cost effective, readily available and comparatively showing less side effects. 
Most chemotherapeutic drugs have lost their therapeutic effect due to drug resistance by microorganism aside from the toxicity to the host cell. Therefore, in the present scenario, there is a dire need to develop anticancer drugs which should have minimal effect on the normal cells. In Pakistan many plants and herb are used to treat cancer. In this project we will used selected plants extracts in vitro and in vivo to find either they have anticancer efficacies and if yes, then what are the active ingredient and molecular mechanisms of its anticancer effect. This will help to develop new anticancer drug against cancer.

data.projectName: A computer aided diagnostic system for wireless capsule endoscopy
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest:
The Wireless Capsule Endoscopy (WCE) was developed in the mid 1990’s. It is embedded with a wireless camera and light powered by a lithium-ion battery. The camera is small enough to fit into capsule (roughly the size of a vitamin tablet) and can therefore be swallowed. As, capsule travels through the digestive tract, it takes a thousand of pictures which are transmitted to a device attached to wearable belt. This procedure needs to fast for around 12 hours.
Capsule endoscopy is used to image the interior of whole GI tract that is difficult to image using standard endoscopy. It is very useful for examining small intestine mucosa and diagnosing different diseases.
Wireless endoscopy process is time consuming for physicians and also for patient. It is very difficult to rule out the abnormality from thousands of images. Our goal is to work on image processing so that we can get desired images from that, so physician can diagnose the disease.
Endoscopy is a nonsurgical procedure used to examine digestive tract and recognize disease like polyps, an abnormal tissue that grows on mucus membranes of GI tract. Polyps has different sizes may be small enough that look like surrounding tissues and physician unable to recognize abnormal growth during endoscopic procedure because endoscopy video is poor in quality and low contrast and presence of noise. Image processing system is used to enhance endoscopy video and help in recognition of abnormal tissue growth. Second purpose of real time image processing system is to collect data for further study after endoscopy procedure.

data.projectName: SYNTHESIS TARGETING ANTI-CANCER, ANTI-INFLAMMATORY AND ANTIOXIDANT SCREENING OF NOVEL INDOLE LIGANDS AND THEIR METAL COMPLEXES
data.projectDigest: This project is based on the synthesis of novel potential anticancer, anti-inflammatory and antioxidant agents. The drugs currently used for the cure of cancer, oxidants and inflammation have severe and unbearable side effects. So there is a crucial demand to synthesize and explore new anti cancer drugs. Literature is rich with an enormous variety of anticancer indole candidates. So a series of novel indole ligands and their metal complexes will be synthesized. The indole imines and amines due to good bidentate ligands are expected to make stable complexes. So they could be potential biological activite against some enzymes. Their metal complexes are expected to have enhanced biological activities due to metal induction. Green, nature friendly and simple methodologies will be employed for synthesis. A countless combination of variously substituted indoles will be an outcome of planned synthesis. Wide variety of substituents at different positions will lead an increase in probability of activity against variety of cancer origins. Study of quantitative structure and reactivity relationship (QSAR) of different groups (methyl, methoxy, chloro, bromo and nitro) on indole core nucleus will also be helpful to determine a standard increase or decrease of indole biological activity.

data.projectName: Applying Nutrient Enriched Manure (NEM) for improving nutritional quality and productivity of Rice-Wheat Cropping System under changing climate scenario
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: The world resources  of phosphate rock (PR) are continuously depleting due to non-judicious use of phosphate (P) fertilizers and low fertilizers use efficiency of available inorganic  P fertilizers. It is estimated that the current  resources of PR will deplete during 2030-50. Low organic matter in our soils is another problem associated with low crop productivity. Different types of abiotic stresses particularly salinity, drought and heat stress are affecting crop yields. There is dire need to develop organic manures enriched with essential nutrients such as phosphorus and other beneficial nutrients (Selenium and silicon) with enhanced nutrient use efficiency to improve crop yield and to ensure judicious use of PR resources. The current research project involves the development of nutrient enriched manure (NEM) having appropriate concentration of these nutrients.  This enriched manure will be a useful organic product for crops growing under stressed environment and will definitely enhance productivity of rice-wheat system

data.projectName: Bioinspired textured surfaces for slip reduction in belt drives
data.projectDigest:
This project focuses on the reduction of slip in belt drives of various configurations. For this purpose, it will make use of bioinspired textured surfaces. Bioinspired textures are replica of natural textures found on plant leaves or animal skins. Keeping in view the difference between the engineered and biological system, novel concepts and methods are required for biomimicry. A thorough understanding of such systems is therefore a perquisite for use in artificial systems. 
This study will focus on the preparation of various textured surfaces of belts and pulleys and their friction, wear and adhesion analysis. A test rig will also be designed for testing textured belts and pulley drives. Afterward, appropriate textures will be incorporated in belt-pulley drives and tested on a test-rig, for speed loss and wear under various conditions. 
This project is extremely important in the context of worldwide efforts towards energy efficiency. From the energy production aspect, there is a dire need for high efficiency energy conversion systems, while on consumer end energy efficient systems are needed to reduce waste of energy. This project can be of interest to a number of industries where belt drives are used for power transmission.

data.projectName: An Investigation of Leukemia Associated Mutational Spectrum of the Genes Encoding DNA Damage Response Proteins, Functional Characterization and Evaluation of the Detected Mutations as Diagnostic and Prognostic Markers
data.projectDigest:
Genetic mutations are the outcome of exposure to many mutagenic factors and may prove toxic to cell viability if left unrepaired (1). To maintain cellular genetic integrity and tackle the effect of deleterious mutations, cells have developed a complex signaling network known as DNA Damage Response Pathway (DDR). DNA damage response is activated after DNA damage and involves prolonged stable association of repair factors with chromatin (2). 
DDR pathway acts as proliferation barrier and limits the carcinogenesis in the early stages through the activation of DNA damage repair proteins encoded by various tumor suppressor genes like TP53, BRCA1/2, ATM etc (4). Mutations in these Tumor Suppressor Genes (TSGs) allow pre-cancerous tumors to cross proliferation barrier and induce malignancies by deregulating DDR pathway and affecting genomic stability (2).   
We conducted a pilot study to investigate the mutational status of TP53 and BRCA1 genes in leukemia patients of Southern Punjab, Pakistan. Results revealed the presence of some unique mutations in these patients and hence highlighted the need of extensive research study. This project is being proposed to investigate the mutational spectrum of some genes encoding DNA damage response proteins like TP53, PTEN, ATM and BRCA1 in a large group of Pakistani patients. In the previous study we predicted the functional impact of the detected mutations through various bioinformatics tools. But the proposed study will involve the functional characterization of the detected mutations through various functional assays to understand the associated biological consequences. Moreover, the observed mutations will be evaluated for their potential to be used as diagnostic & prognostic markers of leukemia.

data.projectName: Mathematical Model for Obtaining the Optimal Growth of ZnO Nanowires.
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The synthesis of Zinc Oxide nanostructures depend on many parameters like choice of precursor, amount of precursor and temperature. But the most important is the control on amount of precursor generally known as supersaturation of the reactants. It is a well-known fact that for favorable nucleation process high supersaturation level is needed, whereas for better crystal growth of the nanostructures low supersaturation levels is required. If in less time lot of hydroxyl ions are produced then zinc ions will precipitate out very quickly in the solution because of high pH in the solution. As a result nutrients will consume rapidly and therefore zinc ions will contribute very little in the synthesis of zinc oxide nanostructures and eventually the synthesis process will terminate. It is therefore very important to have a control on the concentration of hydroxyl ions to maintain low supersaturation in order to produce controlled synthesis of ZnO.

data.projectName: Artificial Intelligence techniques for Electromagnetic Metamaterials
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest:
Metamaterials are artificial materials realized by combining materials in a specific geometric pattern.
Metamaterials have found applications in electromagnetics covering the entire spectrum from RF to
Ultra violet. Applications include Radar absorbers, Ground planes for antennas, filters, and phase
shifters etc.
There are several techniques to design and/or analyze metamaterials: Analytical techniques, Numerical
techniques, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) based techniques. Application of the analytical techniques are
usually limited to structures with regular geometries and for structures with irregular geometries
therefore, numerical techniques are employed. Numerical techniques are generally computationally
heavy and only give the performance parameters[2]. Moreover, they generally cannot be used to obtain
the design parameters for a given set of desired performance parameters. Consequently, AI and
Machine Learning (ML) based techniques have gained popularity for design of metamaterials.
The optimization technique work as a black box mapping the desired performance parameters to the
require design parameters. This approach helps in realizing the desired metamaterial structure without
the need to engage in deeper understanding of the physics of the given structure. In the proposed
project the equivalent circuit parameters will be obtained using machine learning techniques in order to
develop deeper understanding the metamaterial structure.

data.projectName: Unstable Quadratic Resonances for Pattern Forming Systems in case of Spatial Boundary Conditions
data.projectDigest:
Modulation equations such as Ginzburg-landau equation, nonlinear Schrodinger equation, kdV equation, etc, have many applications in digital communications, nonlinear optics, nonlinear acoustics, plasmas, wave mixing, etc. Photonic crystals lay the principal basis of optical storage. In case of resonances, the spectrum of the crystals is detached because of the occurrence of gaps in solitons which travel large distances without releasing energy. It is the target of the present project to establish the stability of the modulation systems in case of 1:2 resonances for Turing-Hopf bifurcation. The boundary is assumed to be periodic. The truncated normal form upto third order give rise to bifurcations globally which causes peaks like structures that release almost no energy. 
The evidence of time-dependence of the phenomena occurs at sufficiently low Belj numbers. The 1:2 resonances give rise to coefficients obtained after computation of normal forms in presence of convection. This phenomena raises the important question about the stability of the system as shifting of cycles which are heteroclinic occurs more frequently indicating complex dynamics. It is expected that new bifurcations will be discovered with global behavior of trivial as well as steady states of standing waves. The nonlinear oscillations will be computed numerically which are expected to be periodic in nature. Although this phenomena is not restricted to the specific choices of the wave numbers subject to the resonances combination, but it certainly evolves the system in a more powerful way. The numerical calculations will be used to further establish the patterns of stability in case of Turing-Hopf bifurcations.

data.projectName: COMPARATIVE STATE OF HOUSING FACILITIES IN ISLAMABAD AND LAHORE: PERSPECTIVES FROM PRIVATE AND PUBLIC HOUSING SCHEMES.
data.piUniversity: Capital University of Science and Technology, Islamabad
data.projectDigest:
The housing demand in Pakistan's urban centers is growing due to a rapid increase in population and migration from rural areas. This demand cannot be met with the existing supply of housing and apartment facilities.  There is an urgent need to address the gaps between the policy makers, the real estate market and the consumers. Our study also aims to do just that by taking all the stakeholders together along with resolving the grievances of the end-user.

Via an interdisciplinary study between Urban Economics and Civil Engineering Construction Management, we construct a concrete crisis management mechanism of the real estate and construction sector. This will be useful to address the issues in providing affordable housing solutions and will be extremely crucial for the middle and lower income groups.  As per UN's Sustainable Development Goals, complying by Goal 11 is critical for economic growth and well being the society. Goall 11 categorically states that,  "making cities sustainable means creating career and business opportunities, safe and affordable housing, and building resilient societies and economies. It involves investment in public transport, creating green public spaces, and most of all improving urban planning and management in participatory and inclusive ways."  

Finally the research findings of our study will prove to be highly fruitful to the government's Ehsaas Housing Scheme in order to prevent prevalent mistakes from repeating. It is crucial that we must understand the triangle between the government, the real estate agents and the consumers. Only then can we fully address the perspectives and gapsin this 'troublesome yet promising' triangle of real estate.

data.projectName: Determining the burden of neglected zoonotic bacterial agents in Cattle Abortions & developing quick farm screening protocols
data.projectDigest: Livestock sector is one of the major contributors to the Pakistan’s agricultural gross domestic product (AGDP). With approximately 42 billion liters of milk produced per annum, Pakistan is ranked 4th among the top five milk producers worldwide. However, the dairy and livestock industry has been severely affected by abortion and weak calf birth as very little measures are taken against abortifacients due to limited diagnostic resources. Abortion in cattle can be caused by many pathogenic bacteria like Brucella abortus, Leptospira interrogans, Coxiella burnetii, Campylobacter fetus subspecies fetus, Campylobacter fetus subspecies venerealis.  Both Coxiella burnetii and Campylobacter fetus are considered as neglected zoonotic pathogens and are not routinely investigated among abortion cases due to complexity in culturing and diagnosis techniques. The bacterium can persist for long period of time in the environment and is mainly transmitted to human through direct contact with farm animals, inhalation of aerosol and contaminated dust. C. burnetii infections, in humans, may result in endocarditis and pneumonia; similarly C. fetus infection may lead to acute diarrhea and bacteremia/septicemia. The proposed study aims to investigate the prevalence of C. burnetii and C. fetus at different levels of transmission in order to track the possible spread point of infection which in turn will lead to development of preventive strategies. Samples will be collected from cattle i.e., placental/milk/serum, waste discharge of farm and serum samples of farm workers of different districts of Punjab. The collected samples will be screened for primarily for C.  burnetii and C. fetus in order to rule out burcelloseis as cause of abortion the sample will also be screened for B. abortus. C. burne

data.projectName: Existence Results for Fractal Fractional Differential Equations Via Topological Fixed Point Theory
data.projectDigest:
The aim is to find generalized Krasnoselskii, Darbo and Sadovskii type fixed point theorems (FPTs) in various directions by using different assumptions on the space and sum of two operators. For this purpose, we will generalize and improve some definitions and results to prove the FPTs for the sum of two functions. The objectives to be achieved are:
•	To find the existence results of Krasnoselskii type FPTs and apply to differential equations (DEs) and IEs.
•	To establish the FPs for monotone functions.
•	To develop fixed point results by using partial MNC and fuzzy MNC and apply it to fractional differential equations.
•	To construct fixed points by weakening the condition of norm on the space and continuity on the operators of Krasnoselskii type. 
•	To find hybrid fixed point results of hybrid fixed point problems that are combination of some topological and algebraic arguments. 
•	To show stability of differential equations.
•	To find fixed points by using contractive, condensing and expensive conditions on operators.
•	To extend fixed point results of Darbo and Sadovskii type
We will explore FP results in topological, metric, normed and Banach spaces with or without ordered hypothesis (total ordered or partial ordered topological spaces with monotonicity condition on operators) for sum of two functions with weak conditions and obtain generalized Banach, Schauder, Krasnoselski, Darbo and Sadovskii type FPTs to apply their FP results for the existence of solutions of differential and integral equations. We will also use MNC to make our analysis and investigate fixed point results by weak assumptions on the space and operator. In this context our work will provide theoretical base for the existence of solutions of fractal fractional DEs and fractal fractional IEs.

data.projectName: Exploration, Collection, Nurseries development, Biochemical characterization and DNA-bar coding of Almonds (Prunus amygdalis) collected from Chitral
data.piUniversity: University of Malakand, Chakdara, Dir, Malakand
data.projectDigest:
Almond is an important specie growing all over the world for their economic purposes. In Pakistan, a lot of work has already been documented on the almonds ecological distribution, nutritional composition and varietal improvement but little attention have been made on almonds characterization and selection of best variety. In this connection, the current project has been proposed to explore, collect, identify and characterize morphological, molecular and biochemically the endangered almonds landraces for end users. 
The proposed study will be consisted of two years. In the first year, exploration, collection and morphological identification will be carried out. Based on morphological characterization, and nutritional composition, different groups will be constructed. The potential landraces tagged in their respective location, each group will be planted in the agriculture field of Chitral University, Agriculture Research Center Mingora Swat and Malakand University Chakdara Dir lower to develop nurseries. Similarly, in the next year, the group of each landraces will be evaluated through Molecular and biochemical techniques. The plants developed in the nurseries will be planted in the experimental field of Chitral University, Agiculture Research center Mingora and Malakand University for economic gain.

data.projectName: Time and sequence of eruption of deciduous teeth of Karachi  Children,
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan, the time and sequence of the eruption of deciduous teeth used in scientific, clinical and research fields are based on estimates from other countries. Many studies of time of eruption of permanent teeth have been conducted numerous countries, whereas very few studied have been performed on the eruption time of deciduous teeth, and in particularly in Pakistani. Because environmental and individual factors vary between locations due to geography, which may have influenced the time of the tooth eruption and due to the wide variability found in previous literature, we should not follow other counties as a reference norm as Pakistani differ culturally, racially and ecologically from them. The purpose of the present study is thus to estimate the time and sequence of eruption of deciduous teeth of Karachi children

data.projectName: Probing XYZ States Through Their Charm-Less Decays
data.projectDigest:
Theories and experiments have been struggling to explore the Universe through its smallest possible constituents.
At this stage, the theoretical prediction about a special type of composite particles of fundamental particles is waiting for the experimental verification of these strange composite particles. No experiment yet has succeeded in doing so. More and more analysis studies of such particles are needed to be performed from different angles/aspects. Some aspects have already been studied and no  big success has been reported. Once experimental confirmations come about these particles, the theory and experiment will further progress and we will have better understanding of the fundamental nature of the Universe. This proposed project is aimed at performing research from a different angle and some useful scientific results are expected which will be helpful addition in the existing pool of knowledge of the concerned field of Physics.

data.projectName: Prediction of Microbial Spoilage in Bakery Items using Hyperspectral  Imaging
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest:
Bakery products are an integral part of majority of the world’s population in which every product has a pre-defined shelf-life that tends to vary with environmental conditions as well as the ingredients. Extreme Humid or dry environment will adversely affect the moisture content which may lead to early spoilage of products. 

If the bakery product is spoiled earlier than its estimated shelf life, it may cause harmful effects on human health. According to World Health Organization (2007-2015) 1 out of 10 (almost 600 million per year) human beings suffer due to foodborne diseases and around 400,000 died. On the other side, Food wastage is one of the biggest issues, where tons of healthy food are being destroyed while at the same time millions of people suffer from hunger. Therefore, if the food item has reached to its defined shelf life but is not spoiled, it may further consume to avoid the wastage.

In this work, we are proposing a novel approach using Hyperspectral Imaging System (HSI) that will predict the shelf life of a bakery item like cake sponges and bread ahead of time. It will avoid the consumption of microbially spoiled items by humans and it will also help in reducing food wastage.

data.projectName: Responsible & Sustainable Tourism, Destination Sustainability, Economic Performance, and Social Development Strategy in Pakistan: An Integrated Framework
data.piUniversity: Imperial College of Business Studies, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
The responsible tourism is an initiative to reap business opportunities using socio-economic benefits, quality of life of local residents, enhanced holiday experiences, and protection of tourism destinations. In order to achieve maximum profit from the tourism industry, organizations usually involve in negative activities like unfair trade practices, human rights issues, damage to vegetation, depletion of wildlife, waste generation, overcrowding and environmental degradation. Additionally, lack of government support, competitive environment, and cost linked with responsible tourism are major interruptions that curb the active proliferation of responsible tourism in developing countries like Pakistan. Due to blatant disregard or unawareness, these behaviors usually ended up with negative consequences for the long-term sustainability of tourist destinations. 
Although numerous studies were conducted on examining the association of responsible & sustainable tourism on organizational and individual-related outcomes, to the best knowledge of the researchers, no study has been conducted on how responsible tourism foster quality of life, socio-economic development, and sustainability in business operations. This research has significant insights for policymakers and organizations to incorporate responsible tourism initiatives in their business operations. Therefore, based on previous literature, this research focuses on testing an integrated framework that hypothesizes responsible tourism as a direct influencer to the local community’s support for tourism, socio-economic development, and quality of life.

data.projectName: Flash Floods Harnessing for the Prosperity of Arid and Resource-stressed Neglected Agro-based Communities
data.piUniversity: Capital University of Science and Technology, Islamabad
data.projectDigest:
Poor management of natural resources not only deprives a community from the associated benefits but sometimes causes fatal damages. In arid mountainous areas, flash floods are the major natural disaster which as a result brings disaster management, development, and security issues to the central priority. Due to steep gradient, flood flows with high velocity (Nquot 2014), which results in damaging the standing crops, irrigation system, houses, roads, and sometime human lives as well. Such areas have the potential for agriculture to meet the shortage of food if manage wisely.
The proposed project aims at finding acceptable flood harnessing options for the prosperity of such communities. Proposed project ‘ProNAC’ is targeting damage reduction of hazard, resource development for the community, and finally proposing combined various efficient harnessing solutions for the areas suffering hill torrents. Contemporary techniques of ‘flood protection’, ‘water harvesting’, and ‘water footprints’ will be employed blended with indigenous solutions during the course of project. Our interdisciplinary project will require complementary expertise in natural and social sciences in addition to engineering knowledge.
Expected outcome of the project is to propose economically attractive and pragmatic approach towards the flash flood harnessing.

data.piUniversity: Lahore College for Women University, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
The field of population pharmacokinetic modeling and dosing simulation has in recent years emerged as an invaluable tool for optimizing dosing strategies across the globe. Pakistan’s population exceeds 200 million with a diverse population based on their life style, eating habits, ethnicity etc. But unfortunately, despite of great potential, this area of research is still neglected in Pakistan and there is a need of population pharmacokinetic studies particularly for narrow therapeutic index drugs including anti-microbials such as ceftriaxone and ceftazidime.  The development of resistance against these antibiotics is based on inappropriate use of antibiotics in term of antibiotic selection and dose selection. The sub-therapeutic doses of antibiotics lead to development of resistance. On the other side the over dose of antibiotics is strongly associated with adverse drug reactions which sometimes lead to irreversible damage to the body e.g. nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity in case of Aminoglycosides. 
The current practice in Pakistan regarding selection of antibiotics and particularly the dose selection is based on the personal experience of the attending physicians or on the available literature where dose selection was determined in patients with normal renal and liver status. The deterioration of the kidney or liver with increasing age, genetic factors, eating habits or underlying diseases may lead to inappropriate elimination of drugs from body either through kidney or metabolism in liver. This compromised status of elimination organs is not being considered during dose selection due to unavailability of population pharmacokinetic studies in Pakistan. data.projectName: Developing Speech and Language Therapy Instruments in Local Languages of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Speech and Language Disorders are treated by the specialists named  as speech and language pathologists or therapists. In Pakistan, speech pathologists try to correct the speech of the their clients by using tools framed by experts who belong to English speaking countries while the speech pathologists of Pakistan mostly have to deal with the patients who speak either Urdu or local languages of Pakistan. In this backdrop, speech and language pathologists need assessment tools, speech therapy techniques fashioned in local languages of Pakistan. Linguists being the experts in languages can help them evolve such tools. This thing will facilitate speech pathologists across Pakistan and make their job easier by enabling  them help the local people having communication disorders. The project, being of interdisciplinary nature, will have a strong social impact and add to the knowledge in the fields of clinical linguistics, speech and language therapy and special education.

data.projectName: General Construction of Efficient Repeated Measurements Designs in Periods of k Different Sizes
data.projectDigest:
In comparative experiments involving human or animal subjects, it is very useful to allocate a sequence of treatments to each subject. For this repeated measurements designs (RMDs) are used. In RMDs more than one measurements is taken on each subject/ unit. Mostly n taken subjects/ units are human/ animals. In these designs p treatments are applied on each subject and each treatment is applied for same length of time. RMDs are widely used in animal sciences, pharmacology, psychology and medicine where residual/ carry over effects may arise. Effect which a treatment has during its period of application (treatment effect) may persist into the preceding period. Such effect is called residual effect or carry over effect. RMDs have application in many branches of scientific inquiry, therefore, choice of RMDs should be in a way that the treatments can be compared efficiently in the presence of residual effects. Minimal BRMDs (balanced RMDs) and minimal SBRMDs (Strongly BRMDs) are useful to balance out these effects at low cost. Weakly balanced RMDs (WBRMDs) should be preferred in the situations where minimal BRMDs cannot be constructed. 
In this study, using MOCS, some generators and construction procedures are discussed to obtain minimal circular BRMDs, WBRMDs, SBRMDs, NSBRMDs and SPBRMDs in periods of k different sizes. 
•	Putting k = 1, we obtain design in equal period sizes.
•	Putting k = 2, we obtain design in two different period sizes.
•	Putting k = 3, we obtain design in three different period sizes, and so on.

data.projectName: Feasibility and Experimental Assessment of Utilization of Low Cost Bio-fertilizers and Biochar for Saline Agriculture
data.projectDigest: Salinization of lands and shortage of fresh-water are major impediments to ensure food security for the fast growing population. Improving salinity tolerance of conventional crops and sustainable utilization of halophytes as non-conventional crops are hence important. However, sensitivity of seeds and seedlings to high salinity is the major bottleneck in this regard. Many agronomic and biochemical approaches are now being proposed to handle this bottleneck; however low-cost yet effective alternatives are still needed. Current soil management strategies are mainly dependent on chemical-based fertilizers, which cause a serious threat to human health and environment. Thus it is imperative to identify environmental-friendly alternatives. Application of organic/bio-fertilizers and biochar to improve soil fertility are being essential components of agriculture but there is a dire need to reduce costs of fertilizing crops. Hence, low-cost natural substances such as coast-deposited seaweeds could be an effective source for bio-fertilizer/biochar. data.projectName: Waste Driven Bio-Carbon Electrode Materials for Energy Applications: Experimental and Theoretical Studies
data.projectDigest: Concern about serious global environmental issues resulting from the use of fossil fuels has prompted researchers to seek alternative renewable energies to mitigate the current energy crisis. Energy storage devices for example electric vehicles, rechargeable batteries, fuel/solar cells have acquired significant attention over the years due to their fundamental role in replacing and reducing pollution resulting from the combustion of fossil fuels. However, the further development of these energy storage devices is hampered by their poor electrode performance. The frequently employed carbon materials to be used as electrode in most of energy storage devices are obtained from nonrenewable resources under harsh environments. Alternative to nonrenewable resources; naturally abundant biomass is considered the most reliable source for green carbon having many desired properties and a well-thought-out roadmap for the future energy scenario. This demonstrates the development trend of energy technologies with the aim of replacing fossil-based energy with renewable energy. The proposed project presents the cardiac status of new carbon materials derived from natural biomass such as indigenous plants waste materials to be used in supercapacitors, metal ion batteries and other energy applications.

data.projectName: Fabrication and optimization of Perovskite solar cells based on inorganic materials
data.projectDigest: Global environmental concerns and the escalating requirement of energy evokes the demand for environmentally benign alternative sources of energy. Photovoltaic technology brings hope in the effort to mitigate this problem but yet no solar cell fulfills requirements of the feasibility at large scale production along with low cost and high efficiency. Fortunately, recently reported organic-inorganic hybrid halide perovskites, possessing the desirable properties. But the instability of perovskite due to the presence of organic component and use of unstable charge transport layers critically impedes the development, because these materials are prone to damage upon exposure to moisture, temperature, and air. One of the promising methods to solve this issue is to replace the organic cation in perovskite material with inorganic cation and to use metal oxide and stable polymeric materials as charge transport layers. Based on the fact that these materials will be resilient to heat, light and moisture we aim to synthesize different metal oxides and perovskite materials and to utilize these materials to develop complete solar cell devices. Our approach will offer the possibility to develop next-generation solar cell devices which will be more stable than currently used perovskite solar cells.

Several different precious metallic catalytic methods have been reported for the catalytic carbon dioxide transformation into formic acid, and other value-added chemicals. data.projectName: Pulsed laser assisted cleaning of superficial degraded layers from selected artefacts
data.projectDigest:
Artefacts of historic nature are important representation of society’s struggles against the tests of time. Conservation and restoration of irreplaceable artefacts that could be fabric stamps, manuscripts, sculptures from the contaminants is very crucial and difficult task as they are the only source of historical information. For successful conservation and restoration process, a complete understanding of the materials used in these artefacts and the mechanism to be employed is a prerequisite. 
Laser cleaning, has become a special tool in the conservation of cultural heritage and has been studied on different types of materials during the past three decades, and has proved to be superior when compared with other methods. This technology has broad spectrum of applications ranging from the restoration of artwork, surface modification, restructuring and particularly the selective cleaning of contaminants. In this proposed study, the laser technology will be used as ultra-precise noncontact scalpels for the removal of unwanted contaminant depositions from the surfaces of some selected objects i.e. Artefacts and nanoparticles deposited on optics. All these artefacts are difficult to clean and conserve using conventional conservation techniques, however, by exploiting the unique properties of laser, precise control and high accuracy of the technique, the goal can be achieved successfully.

data.projectName: Enhanced efficiency and stability of quasi solid-state dye-sensitized solar cell based on Multilayered hybrid plasmonic nanoparticles
data.projectDigest: Energy plays a pivotal role in the socio-economic growth of a country. In Pakistan, we are in dire need of alternate energy resources; solar energy is one of the possible solutions. The target of the proposed project is to enhance the solar efficiency and stability by means of novel techniques. By increasing the solar cell efficiency, we will be able to generate more renewable energy and enhance the potential of solar power and solar energy market. Apart from this, thin-films are best suited for building-integrated photovoltaics, where the panel is integrated into a building’s envelope. Furthermore, PV cells are vital element in Smart Grids employed normally these days due to flexibility, transparency, light in weight, less expensive, and better power conversion efficiency (PCE). Organic, inorganic, and composite materials are better than semiconductors in terms of light weight and low cost. The third generation dye sensitized solar cell (DSSC), have become the prototype of a new generation of solar cell devices. The limitations associated with DSSC are low PCE and low stability, which limits most of the practical applications. In this work, plasmonic nanoparticles and quasi solid-state electrolyte will be used to increase the efficiency and stability of DSSC.

data.projectName: Multipartite Entanglement Dynamics under indistinguishability transition
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: The notion of indistinguishablity is rooted in the permutation symmetry of many-particle wave function and it has profound consequences for many physical phenomena. Based on this permutation symmetry, the symmetrization postulate distinctly divides the particles into two types: bosons and fermions. However, whether the indistinguishability due to particle identity is an exploitable quantum resource remains an interesting question. In first step of our proposed research we are aimed to analyze the effect of indistinguishability on multi-particle entanglement in various physical scenarios. Moreover, bosonic nature of composite bosons, for instance made up of many (even-number) elementary fermions, deviates from their ideally expected behavior. This deviation may be linked to the insufficient entanglement between the constituents of a composite boson. The second part of our research is focused on analyzing the bosonic behavior of composite bosons as a function of multipartite entanglement of their constituents. This deviation from the perfect bosonic behavior is expected to exhibit novel effects in various phenomena, such as, quantum coherence & interference, multi-particle quantum walk and Bose-Einstein Condensation, performed by composite bosons.
