data.projectName: EZETIMIBE AND ATORVASTATIN CO-LOADED BI-LIYER TABLETS: DEVELOPMENT AND EVALUATIONS
data.projectDigest: The purpose of the study is to prepare a pharmaceutical composition that includes a combination of about 10-20 milligrams of cholesterol lowering drug and from about 10-20 milligrams of statin in a single pharmaceutical dosage unit that can provide effective anti-hyperlipidemia activity. Statins are the hypolipemic treatment of choice for hyperlipidemia with confirmed atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) protective effect, proven even in normolipemic patients. The research project will be divided into six main segments i.e. formulation development and optimization of Bi-layer tablets, in-vitro characterization of Bi-layer tablets, development and validation of HPLC method, in-vivo analysis of formulated Bi-layer tablets and pharmacokinetics studies, stability studies and statistical analysis of results. The Bi-layer tablets will be prepared by wet granulation method by using single punch machine. The sustained release layer will be fabricated by using raft forming polymers and immediate release layer contain superdisintegrant.. Furthermore, the variability analysis shall be done using the modern statistical techniques such as Principal Components Analysis and Multivariate Regression. Moreover, some statistical data checks shall be imposed to detect the data problems such as ill-conditioning and multicollinearity and the data which can cause the data variables to mislead the results. If these problems shall be present, we shall also look for the solution to these problems accordingly.

data.projectName: Development and characterization of silanised silica filled rubber cots and apron for fiber spinning application
data.projectDigest: Textile is the largest export oriented sector in Pakistan. The textile sector contributed 51% of the total Pakistan’s export in last fiscal year (2018-2019). The sector includes readymade garments, hosiery, bed wear, towels, yarn, and fabric. The backbone of the textile sector is the spinning industries. Pakistan’s spinning industry is the world 3rd largest spinning industry. Keeping in view the portfolio of the spinning industry, the industry could not indigenize its self to manufacture its own machines and machine consumable parts. That is why Pakistan is spending a huge foreign exchange on the purchase of the spinning machines and its parts. This model is not sustainable for longer period of time. The proposed project will focus on the development of two pats i.e. rubber cots and rubber drafting aprons for the spinning industry. The proposed project will not only help the industry to substitute the imported parts with the locally manufactured parts but also help to create jobs if industries developed in the area mentioned above.

data.projectName: Economical Consequences of Political Connections on Non Financial Listed Firms
data.projectDigest: There are three main objectives of this project. First, to identify the firms that have political connections in Pakistan during the period of 2013-2018. Second, to empirically investigate the influence of political connections on firms reporting quality. Third, to empirically investigate how the politically connected firms respond to changes in political stability and government effectiveness. In this study, we especially investigate the response of politically connected firms in the form of reporting quality when political stability and government effectiveness is changed. This project will also establish the understanding of game theories which organization uses to get benefits from their financial reporting strategies in accordance with changing scenarios and governments. Further, this may help National Accountability Bureau (NAB), Securities Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP), and other governing bodies, in identifying the process which organization ought to establish their political connections, through which they get financial and non-financial benefits at micro and macro level.

data.projectName: Development of technical guidelines and design specifications for Ground Source Heat Pumps for environment conditioning of buildings
data.projectDigest:
Comparing the year-long utility bills of an average household in Pakistan will reveal that electricity consumption during summer is 4 times that of winter and gas consumption in winters is 3 times that of summer. This means that 2/3rd to 3/4th of domestic energy consumption is for air-conditioning only. 
This research proposal aims at exploring the use of Ground Source Heat Pumps (GSHPs) for air conditioning of buildings. A GSHP is a heating/cooling system that relies on the relatively constant temperature of the earth’s crust for use as source/sink in HVAC for buildings. The temperature of the earth at a depth of up to 6m (depending on soil and environmental characteristics) remains nearly constant throughout the year and is roughly equal to the mean annual air temperature at that latitude on the surface of the earth, in case of Peshawar it is 21C. A pipe loop buried in the ground carries water from a radiator in the building to the ground, transporting heat to/from the building. Temperature In summers (rising above 45C) can be brought down to a comfortable 24C, while in winters, to about 19C. The operating energy requirements are very low for GSHPs giving efficiencies well above 300%.

data.projectName: Development of an innovative single crystal casting based rapid tooling approach using FDM
data.projectDigest: More than Half of the polymer parts around the world are manufactured using injection molding machine. For producing a new polymer part, the main factor affecting the product cost and time to be introduced in the market is the mold design. The current method of mold design is lengthy and costly and thus not suitable for low quantity production (100,000 parts) and for new product introduction in the market.  To address this, rapid tooling has been developed which in turn has limitation of strength and compatibility. This research aim to address these limitations in rapid tooling by proposing a new method of mold design. The mold will be designed using single crystal investment casting by directly employing 3d printed mold pattern. The strength of the product will be enhanced by directional solidification also called single crystal casting. Furthermore, for investment casting, one of the cost factor is its slurry which is used to make mold. Thus, alternative low-cost slurry materials will also be identified. Furthermore, different rapid prototyping materials will be made and compared for its effectiveness in investment casting. The result of these research will help to dramatically reduce manufacturing cost and time.

data.projectName: Developmental, reproductive and neurobehavioral health hazards of methamphetamine (Ice drug) abuse: A poison of modern era
data.projectDigest: Methamphetamine (MA) is most widely used psychostimulant abused by young population worldwide. The detailed toxicodynamic evaluation of MA is lacking with reference to its developmental, reproductive and neurobehavioral implications during pregnancy and in individuals with child bearing potential. The present project is aimed to evaluate these health hazards in adult male and female rats and their offsprings at doses that correspond to its social abuse (10, 20 and 40 mg/kg/day). During the first phase of study, the effect of long-term exposure of MA will be assessed on endocrine, hematological, biochemical, oxidative, histopathological and apoptotic markers in rodents and their offsprings. data.projectName: Natural Tooth Repair using SMART Dental Composite (Self bonding, antibacterial, remineralising)
data.projectDigest:
Worldwide, tooth decay affects 60-90% of children and almost 100% of adults. Dental fillings are the materials that are used to replace the damaged-infected parts of teeth and maintain the structural integrity of the teeth. Silver fillings(amalgam) have been used for dental-filling for decades, however, a ban on their use is imminent over mercury content toxicity issues. Alternative white-filling (dental-composites) are in use due to their aesthetic pleasing effect and minimal-tooth-removal. However, its failure rate is three-times more than silver-fillings, and 80% of white filling fail. Reason for failure is debonding of composite from the tooth, allowing bacterial ingress and continuation of decay. This is a particular concern for children as their tooth-decay progresses more rapidly. 
Project aim is to develop a tooth-matching filling material that is easier to place, require minimum tooth-removal and can last longer than the current white-filling materials, while naturally remineralizing the lost-tooth. This will be achieved by using remineralizing & antibacterial components in the filling that will help to bond better with tooth, revive the damaged tooth and eradicate the bacteria that cause tooth-decay. This will especially help children, anxious patient and dentist (saving time), help towards the cost of the restoration in the longer-run

data.projectName: :  TREATMENT OF WASTEWATER BY ARTIFICIAL FLOATING ISLANDS with ENCAPSULATED BIODEGRADERS (AFIEBS)FOR SAFE AGRICULTURAL REUSE
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan is among top ten countries vulnerable to climate change. However, the major cities of Pakistan produce about 5.54×109 M3/year domestic wastewater (in urban and peri-urban/rural areas) which is mostly dumped untreated to drains and ultimately to rivers. Unlike to other countries, only a negligible fraction of this huge amount is used for irrigation purposes without any prior treatment. This wastewater could be turned to alternate and sustainable water resource by implementing centralized and decentralized treatment and reuse approach. There are many success stories in this regard, for example Israel recycles 90% of its wastewater (about 80% of reclaimed water is reused in agriculture). Similarly, Spain recycles about 20% of its wastewater and uses it for various purposes. 
This study proposes an integrated wastewater management approach though which complex wastewater could be reclaimed by efficient constructed wetland and reused as safe irrigation source. This approach will not only help to solve water shortage issues in water scarce south Punjab region but can also improve contaminant free agricultural produce, enhance water productivity, improved rural health and ultimately sustainable social setting survival. This research work will focus on optimization of the environmental parameters for the treatment of municipal as well as industrial wastewater by using constructed wetlands with attached growth biodegrades for its utilization as resource for irrigation purpose. This system will be applied on a cluster of localities and villages to adopt this methodology for maximum utilization of the wastewater effluent for irrigation purposes.

data.projectName: Engineering and Development of Industry-grade Thermostable Phytase Enzyme for Poultry Feed in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Kohat University of Science and Technology, Kohat
data.projectDigest: Genetically engineered enzymes make a fast-growing industrial sector globally that is set to reach USD 13.8 billion in size by 2026. One class of enzymes, known as Phytases, in one vertical alone (i.e. Poultry Feed) is worth north of USD 5 million in imports annually in Pakistan. Phytases are enzymes which unlock organic phosphates from phytates or phytic acids that are abundantly available in poultry feed but are otherwise unavailable to them and are excreted undigested, becoming an opportunity cost in terms of nutrition. This project bring together a highly accomplished tri-party consortium including an academic lab that focuses on molecular biology research of enzymes (PI), a computational biology lab that has expertise in molecular dynamics simulations which can guide the engineering of enzymes (Academic Collaborator), making them more thermostable and useful in the industry, and a pioneering synthetic biology company as an industrial partner which brings in technical expertise both in synthetic biology for engineering enzymes and the business aspects of the project including product design, marketing and sales. The ultimate aim of the project is to go beyond just cloning the enzyme, to producing a high-specs industry-grade enzyme that has the potential to be substitute of our imports.

data.projectName: Isolation, identification and characterization of halo-tolerant rhizobacteria from Khwera salt mines of Pakistan and their impact on wheat plant under salinity stress
data.projectDigest: Agriculture sector plays a vital role in Pakistan's economy. In the last few decades, food security and sustainable agriculture are becoming a serious threat with increasing world population, but our land resources are deteriorating gradually. The main reasons of soil degradation includes water logging, reduced soil fertility, soil contamination, soil erosion, lack of essential minerals, gradual depletion of organic matter and soil salinity. Soil salinity is one of the major problems in developed countries and this situation is worse in the agriculture sector of developing countries including Pakistan. According to a study conducted by the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), 20.8m hectares is cultivable land in the country, out of which 5.33m hectares are affected by salinity and 1.55m hectares by waterlogging. Due to soil salinity, the annual cost of crop losses has been estimated between Rs15 billion to Rs55 billion and now it requires new approaches to maintain an adequate food supply.  An important approach in addressing this issue is the ability of rhizobacteria to promote plant growth in poor quality soil. Halophytes plants are naturally salt-tolerant that are grown in salty soils. Microbial community present in rhizosphere (rhizobacteria) or in plant tissues like roots (endophytes) have the capacity to make a significant contribution to plants ability to adapt against adverse conditions. Therefore, researchers are trying to isolate halo-tolerant rhizobacteria from rhizosphere of halophyte plants as little previous work has been reported on microbiomes associated with native halophytes in Khewra salt mine of Pakistan. Here, we will focus on the microbiomes of native halophyte species that grow in highly saline environment of Khewra salt mine. A wide rang

data.projectName: Potential of breeding cotton for high temperature tolerance
data.projectDigest: Cotton crop is facing problems of high temperature stress due to increasing temperature. High temperature is affecting production of the cotton adversely. These influences can be reduced by breeding heat tolerant cotton plant. To evaluate the thermo-tolerance of cotton germplasm present project is planned. One hundred cotton genotypes against high temperature stress will be screened in field based on biochemical and morpho-physiological traits. Six to eight heat tolerant and high yielding genotypes will be selected and crossed in green house to produce F1 seeds. F1 seed along with their parents will be evaluated for high temperature stress under field conditions. Some seeds of potential F2 population will be sown in pots during October of the same year in the green house to develop seed for F3 population, while remaining F2 seed will be stored for next year. In last year of experiment, F2 seeds developed in previous year and F3 population developed by growing F2 seed in glass house will be grown under field condition for evaluation. After three years of experiments there will be wide range of heat tolerant material which would be further used for the development of high temperature stress tolerant cotton cultivars.

data.projectName: Exploring the Genetic Markers of Drug Resistance in Helminthes: The Need for Healthy Livestock Management and Production
data.projectDigest: Helminths are one of the major menaces for livestock industry causing production losses in terms of weight loss, reduction in meat and milk yield and poor wool quality. At present, there is no effective alternative to chemical control of parasitic helminths where livestock are grazed intensively. Resistance to anthelmintics has become a major problem in veterinary medicine, and threatens both agricultural income and animal welfare. The molecular and biochemical basis of this resistance is not well understood. In Pakistan the ability to monitor the spread of anthelmintic resistance is quite limited and dependent on biological methods which are not sufficiently sensitive to detect low levels of drug resistance. The multiple-drug-resistant parasites also can no longer be controlled by treatment with most of the commonly used anthelmintics and have resulted in a number of farms being forced to abandon livestock rearing. However, in order to establish a robust surveillance system to monitor drug efficacy and resistance in the country, we aimed (i) to establish diagnostic laboratory with trained researchers to undertake questionnaire survey to obtain insights into farm-level characteristics and report the data (ii) provide epidemiological data regarding helminth species diversity in ruminants to understand parasite biology  ii) investigate the changes in  efficacy of commonly used anthelmintic drugs to implement strategies to maximize the effective lifetime of our current compounds and iii) identification of molecular markers associated to anthelmintic resistance to monitor drug efficacy in helminths for control programs.

data.projectName: Integrated Management of tomato leafminer, Tuta absoluta (Meyrick); A Potential Quarantine Pest and Threat to Tomato Industry in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest: Tomato is an important food crop all over the world. Larva of tomato leafminer is an insect pest which feed on the leaf mesophyll by producing blotch type of mines. It also damaged the stem and fruit by feeding on fruit pulp. It is capable of causing 80 to 100 % losses if no control measures were adopted. Principal Investigator recently reported Tuta absoluta from tomato crop from Multan region, while there are many complaints of its attack from different parts of Punjab. It’s life history traits and possible management tactics are needed to be identified before it become a major pest. This study is expected to increase fruit yield, increase in farmers’ income, basic information generated through the project will be helpful in devising control strategies of this potential pest. Biological control findings will help to suppress its population. Natural enemies will be evaluated and recommended for future use. It will help to reduce the environmental hazards and pollution due to chemical insecticides. Safe and effective insecticides will be recommended. It will include: Knowledge generation for students, researchers, and scientific community. Production of high quality fruits will help to quality tomato production to meet local needs. Present project will help to devise integrated pest management strategies for this potential insect pest.

data.projectName: Fabrication of colloidal Indium phosphide-based quantum dot sheets with gold nanoparticle for biosensing applications
data.projectDigest:
Clean water supply is a global challenge the world is facing and microbial pathogens are critical components that lead to disastrous effects for the health of humans and others. More than 1 billion of people among the globe do not have access to clean water and waterborne illnesses constitutes up to 80% of the total illnesses among the developing countries. Our aim in this project is to provide a bio-sensing platform for the detection of microbial pathogens in the water. In this project we propose a flexible, thin solid sheet of quantum dots (QDs) for sensing the pathogens in the water samples. This is a multidisciplinary Chemistry-Physics-Biosciences project, which aims to show the feasibility of a new physicochemical method for the detection of microbial/biological pathogens in water samples utilized by the use of free standing colloidal sheets of quantum dots. 
Apart from the currently used immunoessay techniques, this novel approach will help us to reveal the advantages of plasmonics and excitonics to develop an innovative, sensitive bio-sensing platform. Our proposal will serve as a direct effort for detection of sustainable clean water across the globe.

data.projectName: Wind turbines power generation for off-grid streetlights of Motorway
data.projectDigest:
The objective of this project is to develop a micro grid wind farm to capture wind energy on Pakistan’s motorways from the high speed vehicle movement. The utilization of the energy will be to enlighten the motorways/highways with 70-watt light emitting diodes (LED) streetlights. The approximately 4,266 Km long motorway, which is maintained under the supervision of national highway authority (NHA), is a source of renewable energy generation, which has been neglected since it is deployment. 
It is to be noticed that the wind energy is considered the fastest growing source of clean energy. Highway roads provide much wind with greater speed to drive the turbine due to the continuous heavy traffic. The traffic flows on the motorway is almost continuous and throughout a day and night generating the kinetic energy. This kinetic energy is not used so far for any purpose on our motorways and going to be wasted. The proposed wind model will be used to determine the average wind speed generated by vehicles. An optimized designed of wind turbines will be proposed considering the Pakistan’s motorways. This will help producing energy and improve the economy of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Design and Development of Low Cost Axial Field Flux Switching Machine for Electric Bike
data.projectDigest:
Electrical machines are playing their vital role in reshaping the modern industry. These machines are involved in electro-mechanical energy conversion ranging from the milliwatts of power to as large as gigawatts of power. A few of the numerous applications of these machines include surgical equipment, agriculture, household applications, robotics, traction, and space applications etc. All these applications have their own specific load characteristics that must be satisfied by these electrical machines. Therefore, a large number of electrical machines variants have been researched to meet the load requirements of the specific applications.
This research aims to propose wide speed operation of axial field flux switching machine. Now days field excited flux switching machine has gained more attraction as compared to permanent magnet machines. Field excited flux switching machine is employed for high speed applications. It has both armature winding and field winding present on the stator. Permanent magnet machines have high cost due to presence of magnets. Due to high cost of permanent magnet machines, hybrid excited flux switching machines are also used. But hybrid excited machines also uses permanent magnets. This research focuses to design and develop axial field flux switching  machine with low cost. Winding will be phase group concentrated coil (PGCC). The usage of phase group concentrated coil winding allows obtaining unity winding factor. As a result fault tolerant capabilities can be gained. The proposed machine design have simple and robust structure, low manufacturing  cost, low losses and high efficiency. The performance analysis will be carried out by Finite Element Analysis (FEA). Various mathematical and sizing equations shall to be used.

data.projectName: The impact of electronic media use on health and well-being of adolescents
data.projectDigest: Over 50 years of researches have shown that excessive usage of television or computer, smart phones, or other similar electronic gadgets cannot only adversely affect the physical health of young children, but their mental development as well. Such adverse effects of excessive screen time on mental health include; aggressive behavior, risky sexual behavior, substance use/abuse, disordered eating and others. To quantify this in our population, we aim to (i) measure average daily screen time in adolescents (ii) to evaluate associations between duration of time spent on each type of electronic medium and adolescents’ health and well-being. The study also aims to design an intervention based on the findings from our baseline cross-sectional study, for adolescents in the form of a health education program. This intervention will focus on educating adolescents on (i) the adverse effects of excess screen time on mental health and (ii) how to minimize screen time effectively. We plan to conduct our study in two phases. In the first phase, we will conduct a baseline cross-sectional study, followed by a cluster randomized trial in Phase II. To ensure that the measures are sustainable enough to create an everlasting impact of study a sustainable behavioural model is designed.

data.projectName: Value addition of cheeses using herbs and spices
data.projectDigest: Growing perception about diet and health has extended the need to exploit the nutritious, biologically active and sustainable food products. Medical advantages of herbs and spices have attracted food researchers to develop novel functional dairy products and evaluate their impact on product quality and consumer acceptability. Cheese is an important dairy product with good nutritional profile and health value. However, functional and physiological properties of the cheeses can be improved by the addition of herbs and spices which are good source of phenolic acids, anthocyanidin, flavanoids and flavoring agents as well. These contribute to different health promoting properties including anti-microbial, anti-oxidant, anti-inflammatory and anti-carcinogenic potential. In addition, physical properties, texture, appearance, and flavor of product are also improved and important factors for consumer acceptability. Herbs and spices also give color to the cheese, and improve presentation and attractiveness of the cheese to consumers. Common herbs/spices and other flavors added to cheeses include red and green peppers paprika, black peppercorns, horseradish, thyme, cloves, cumin, caraway, parsley, tarragon, nutmeg, basil, onion/garlic, and sundried tomatoes. Different countries are already producing cheeses with added spices and herbs including Italy, Netherland (traditional Dutch herb cheeses), United States, Spain, Turkey and has great consumption/market potential. Such nutritional formulations with new flavors and health properties should also be manufactured and introduced in Pakistan.

Medical advantages of herbs and spices have attracted food researchers to develop novel functional dairy products and evaluate their impact on product quality and consumer acceptability. Cheese is an important dairy product with good nutritional profile and health value. However, functional and physiological properties of the cheeses can be improved by the addition of herbs and spices which are good source of phenolic acids, anthocyanidin, flavanoids and flavoring agents as well. These contribute to different health promoting properties including anti-microbial, anti-oxidant, anti-inflammatory and anti-carcinogenic potential. In addition, physical properties, texture, appearance, and flavor of product are also improved and important factors for consumer acceptability. Herbs and spices also give color to the cheese, and improve presentation and attractiveness of the cheese to consumers. Common herbs/spices and other flavors added to cheeses include red and green peppers paprika, black peppercorns, horseradish, thyme, cloves, cumin, caraway, parsley, tarragon, nutmeg, basil, onion/garlic, and sundried tomatoes. Different countries are already producing cheeses with added spices and herbs including Italy, Netherland (traditional Dutch herb cheeses), United States, Spain, Turkey and has great consumption/market potential. Such nutritional formulations with new flavors and health properties should also be manufactured and introduced in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Cultural Tourism as a Driver for Development: Case Study of Chaukhandi Tombs in Sindh, Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Development Economics (PIDE), Islamabad
data.projectDigest:
The current study is about how cultural tourism is a driver for development: case study of Chaukhandi tombs. In order to give policy recommendations and plan to develop cultural destination, one has to conduct survey and documentation of Chaukhandi tombs which will provide basis to make recommendations on how to target this dimension of cultural tourism and its significance in engaging local community. For this the survey will be conducted in two district of Sindh.  Chaukhandi tombs, which are stone-carved graves, is the name given by department of archaeology of Pakistan.
In recent years, there is a growing interest between the linkages of cultural tourism as a tool to development and participation of the local communities. The development for tourist destinations has direct impact on the community as the local products will have market.  The folk arts will be revived and produced for tourist consumption which will ultimately have socio-economic impacts on local community.    
Through this project, various barriers to local community participation will also be identified which will help policy makers to better develop the tourist cultural destination accordingly. With development of many destinations will also have greater impacts on local economy as there would be more job opportunities for the members of local community.

data.projectName: Molecular identification of carbapenemase producing clinical isolates of e.coli and klebsiella pneumoniae from tertiary care hospitals of district swabi
data.projectDigest:
In Clinical practices major health threat arises due to Infections caused by carbapenemase producing
Gram-negative bacteria. Less information from developing country is available on carbapenem resistant
bacterial including Pakistan. Therefore the aim of this study is designed to discus the burden of antibiotic
resistant strains particularly with focus on carbapenem resistant strains isolated from hospitalized and
outdoor patients attending tertiary care hospitals of district Swabi. The proposed objectives for this
project are ; Objective 1 Isolation, screening and idenfication of clinical isolates of Klebsiellae
pneumoniae and Escherichia coli. Objetive 2 Antibiotic susceptibility testing of ?-lactam and non-?-
lactam antibiotics. Objective 3 Phenotypic detection of Carbapenemase Producing strains. Objective 4
Molecular identification of carbapenem resistant genes (blaKPC-2, blaKPC_3, blaNDM_1, blaNDM_5,
blaIMP_4, and blaVIM_1, blaOXA_489) using molecular markers in K. pneumonia and Escherichia coli.
The outcomes of this project will provide important training opportunities for students in project to
learn about carbapenemase producers and their detection techniques. This project will provide
important data related to occurrence of resistant strains in district swabi. It will also provide information
regarding highly prevalent CRE in district Swabi. Identification of CRE infections at their first appearance
in district swabi will provide an opportunity to stop these infections before they spread extensively.
Furthermore, a robust molecular techniques using will help to identify genetic determinants of
carbapenem resistant strains in humans and document it, hence connecting the knowledge gap about
the molecular epidemiology of carbapenem resistant strains in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Development of Low-cost Seismic Monitoring Stations for Earthquake Hazard and Damage Assessment in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: This project aims to develop low-cost seismic hazard monitoring stations in Pakistan to assess earthquake hazard and damage assessment in the country. Pakistan is located on a highly earthquake-prone and seismically active part of the world. With such a high level of earthquake risk, there is an urgent need of combined efforts from academia, industry and all stake holders to develop a systematic approach towards (a) collection of seismic data for seismic hazard monitoring in the country, and (b) analysis of collected data to assess the extent of damage to built facilities in a post-earthquake scenario. The complete setup of a typical seismic station may cost as much as 50,000 to 80,000 USD which can be significantly reduced by assembling and utilizing low-cost sensor technology and engaging expertise of local seismologists and researchers. Initially, the development of an integrated network system comprising of 5 seismic stations is proposed. However, the technology can be expanded later to develop a comprehensive seismic monitoring network covering the whole country. The establishment of this system would not only hold the key to achieve long-term earthquake resilience in Pakistan, but also would provide an insight into seismic hazard and potential infrastructural damage in the country.

data.projectName: An Intelligent Urdu Transcription Learning Environment  [AI-UTLE]
data.projectDigest:
The focus of this research is to develop an intelligent and engaging Urdu handwriting tutoring system. Equipped with modern computational technology, handheld devices and the principles of educational psychology, this system targets to aid the learning process of Urdu transcription. 
Essential to this teaching system, is:
1.) Learning System: Based on pedagogical principles of language tutoring and the learner’s learning patterns, this system provides, interactive and intuitive ways of presenting and testing transcription skill. 
2.) Evaluation System:  Using a trained model of writer-independent Urdu transcription process, the System can recognize if the transcription is done correctly?  And if not, what went wrong and where. For that purpose, a huge data set of online Urdu Handwriting will be constructed purposefully for the said task.
3.) Feedback System: Based on evaluation, provides user with constructive feedback that can aid, learner’s progress.

data.projectName: Synthesis, characterization and utilization of metal incorporated biochar nanocomposites to reclaim salt affected soils
data.projectDigest: World soil productivity is greatly threatened by increased salinization and sodification in arable lands (arid and semi-arid regions). It is necessary to bring these cultivable barren lands under cultivation to meet the challenges of world food security. Pakistan has been severely affected by increasing salinity and it is imperative to introduce some amendments to reclaim saline soils. Recently, biochar had been used to reclaim salt affected soils by many researchers with good results. It has been noted that application of biochar has successfully reclaimed salt affected soils by improving soil physical and chemical properties and plant growth. But there are some constraints in its application to saline soils like high pH and nutrient unavailability. Therefore, modified biochar or biochar nanocomposite has been applied to improve the quality of biochar for various purposes. In this project, metal incorporated biochar nanocomposite will be made and asses for its ability to reclaim salt affected soils. Biochar from different source (sugarcane pressmud) will be made under different pyrolysis condition to check its suitability for saline soils. Later, prepared biochar will be incorporated with metal nanocomposite and will be applied to reclaim salt affected soils.

data.projectName: Development of cost-effective, sustainable and eco-friendly biofertilizer from consortium of PGPR and Biochemical elicitors as alternative for drought tolerance, disease resistance and yield Improvement of Wheat cultivars in Balochistan
data.piUniversity: Balochistan University of Information Technology, Engineering and Management Sciences,Quetta
data.projectDigest: Agriculture is considered to be the backbone of Pakistan's economy, and its contribution is 19.8% to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and absorbing 42.3% of the labor force of the country. Wheat is cultivated in an area of 8,734 thousand hectares with an annual production of 25.492 million tons in Pakistan. Each year there is a decrease of 2.6% yield because of various stress factors creating an alarming gap between ever-increasing demand and current production. The wheat production of Balochistan, the larger province by area, is further reduced not only due to the biotic but also abiotic stress. The improvement in crop yield by inputs is generally not a feasible strategy in the province. Plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) are the inhabitant microorganisms that readily colonize the root rhizosphere and result in enhancement of crop productivity and mitigation of biotic and abiotic stresses. The current project, therefore, is designed to isolate, characterize and evaluate the performances of novel PGPR strains from wheat rhizosphere, and develop a cost-effective, sustainable and eco-friendly biofertilizer to confer systemic resistance in wheat in order to biologically control the incidences of drought stress, and increase the yield and production of wheat varieties in Balochistan.

data.projectName: Developing Affordable Housing Models for Low-Income People of Punjab  in the Context of Naya Pakistan Housing Program
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is facing acute shortage of housing to the tune of 10 million units with an additional demand of approximately 350,000 units per annum. The Federal Government has recently launched Naya Pakistan Housing Program aiming to provide five million houses. Under this program, the price a built house ranges from Rs. 2 to 4 million, which is well beyond the affordability of low income people. This research aims to determine variability in the housing affordability of low-income people living in metropolitan and other cities of Punjab;  critically examine existing planning and design standards and suggest modifications for meeting the need of affordable housing; develop new housing models for meeting the needs of low-income people; redefine roles of public sector housing and finance institutions as well as private developers in implementing new housing models. Methodology includes review of literature, interviews with experts, questionnaire survey of low income people living in selected cities, qualitative and quantitative analysis of the collected data. Outcome of this research will help meeting the housing demand by the low-income people of Punjab in a sustainable manner regardless of any political regime. The new models are also expected to be replicated in other provinces of Pakistan.

data.projectName: IMPACT OF ENVIRONMENT AND BIOLOGICAL AGENTS IN DIPERSAL OF INSECT/PESTS ON DIFFERENT CROPS IN SOUTHERN PUNJAB. PAKISTAN
data.projectDigest: The yield loss in cotton by the insect pests is report to be 16%. Among sucking pests i.e. thrips (Thrips tabaci), white fly (Bemisia tebaci), and Jassids (Amrasca devastans), and chewing pests i.e. bollworms (Spotted, American, pink and spiny) are dangerous pests . These are polyphagous and found all over the world where the cropping system is prevailed. In the last decades they got special consideration in Pakistan . They can only be controlled through pesticides which are of different nature and imported from other countries approximately of 12 billion rupees per annum. Among which 70% of insecticides are only used for cotton crop. The indiscriminate and continuous use of such chemical to destroy these pests develop resistance in them against these insecticides . Not only health problem in human and animals were observed but they also pollute our environment in many different ways . In this pesticide age, IPM mean integrated pest management has attained it attention. This management exploits several tactics to prevent or even reduced the insect pest problems . Research on biological control, chemical control, host plant resistance, and resistance against insecticide management was the most important part of IPM .

data.projectName: Critical Thinking to promote Tolerance
data.projectDigest: Intolerance has become a serious challenge to the peace and progress of the world, and in countries like Pakistan, this has serious repercussions. Over the past few decades, Pakistani society has seen a rapid increase in intolerance; Dharna politics, attacks on minorities are a few examples. The primary reason for this increasing intolerance is the absence of critical thinking which enables people to formulate sound judgments and make informed decisions with regard to individual and collective matters of life. This has raised questions on the educational processes in place which are primarily supposed to foster critical thinking. Thus, there have been consistent calls to reform educational programs by including critical thinking as a key learning outcome. In line with these requirement, this study, in the first phase, attempts to investigate the deficiencies in teaching critical thinking at undergraduate level in Pakistan by drawing upon university curricula, industry feedback and surveys. In the second phase, the study aims to propose a systematic method of teaching critical thinking effectively across a range of programs. The findings of the study will be helpful in promoting critical thinking which in turn contributes to a tolerant society where disparity is valued, not confronted.

data.projectName: Characterization and Utilization of Stevia rebaudiana in Value added bakery and confectionary products as sugar Replacer
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: Hectic work schedule and workaholic lifestyles is directly impacting human health profile, but creating an imbalance between long working hours followed by sluggish and lethargic resting time. This fast lifestyle is making people more inclined towards high sugar and fat convince food. Which are the leading cause of dietary aliments like obesity and diabetes. To cope up with these problems, artificial sweeteners are used to enhance the taste and product quality without adding additional calories to the food products. But these artificial additives have their own negative health implication upon excessive use. According to Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in comparison to the artificial source, natural or nutritive sweeteners like honey, sugar beet, maple syrup, molasses have stature of Generally Recognized as Safe. Due high cost these natural sweeteners are not feasible for commercially processed food products. However, herbs like Stevia rebaudianahaving high sugar profile provide much economical source. Stevia rebaudianais a South American perennial herb commonly known as Stevia. Nowadays, powdered Stevia leaves are used as substitute to sugars and synthetic sweetener in food processing industries like beverage, milk and confectionary, bakery items and deserts. Stevia not only impart sweeter taste but also a rich source of phytochemicals, flavonoids, essential oil, tri-terpenes, gums, sterebins A to H pigments and etc. These phytochemicals possess free radical scavenging potential, thus minimizing the risk of genetic mutations, cancer, and other inflammatory diseases. Moreover, Stevia has been proved beneficial as soporific, cardiotonic dilator, anti-inflammatory medicine.

data.projectName: Optimization of isolation, fractionation and purification of bioactive compounds from selected medicinal plants and prospects of in-vivo applications
data.projectDigest: Presently the total world production of essential oil is about 12000-13000m tones out of which India, China and Brazill holding major world production. Even though Pakistan has favorable conditions for cultivation of essential oil crops but its share in world production is non-significant. This project will first time focus on cultivation of different varieties of black paper, chilli and hemp and clove and oregano. In addition to these a detailed protocol for cultivation of sage, thyme and oregano and aloevera will be developed.  The foregoing plant parts such as leaves are used as medicinal plant in many countries but in Pakistan they are not being cultivated due to absence of suitable technical support. The major constituents of these plants are diterpenoids, flavonoids, and polyphenols. The experiments will be designed for the determination of bioactive properties of essential oils and extracts from leaves of these plants. Plant excerpts and essential oils will be prepared using solvent extraction, distillation and supercritical fluid extraction. Plant investigation will be completed using advance analytical methods including GCMS, HPLC-MS. Practical features concerning the progress of fast and reliable methods of extraction, high productivity screening method, and bio autography of essential oils and crude excerpts and fractions will be improved in this present study. Complications related to efficiency, constancy and value control will also be a part of present project.

data.projectName: Genomic Analysis of Locally Cultivated Chickpea Varieties for Dehydration and High Salinity Stress Tolerance
data.projectDigest: Dehydration and high salt stress affect plant growth and productivity. At transcriptional level many genes respond to dehydration / high salt stress, and their gene products function in stress tolerance and response. The genomes of several higher plants have been sequenced, and their genes have been predicted. Previously, our research group reported key transcription factors in transcriptional network of Arabidopsis and rice under different abiotic stress conditions. Draft sequence of chickpea has been released and the transcription factors involved in abiotic stress tolerance in chickpea remain to be clarified. In this project, we propose to use oligonucleotide microarray and next generation sequencing to identify dehydration and high salt stress responsive genes and promoters in chickpea for generation of dehydration /high salt stress tolerant chickpea plants. data.projectName: Women Empowerment, Fertility Behavior and Child Wellbeing in Punjab: Role of Microcredit
data.projectDigest: Women empowerment and child well-being are necessary elements for sustainable development, since good health, quality education and gender equality are 3rd ,4th and 5th SDGs respectively. Childhood phase forms the basis for the development of social and human capital of an individual and is pivotal for sustainable development of societies. Health and education during early years of children’s life are essential not only for their success in school, but also for building capacities to contribute effectively in society. Unfortunately, in Pakistan, indicators on child health and education are not portraying an encouraging situation and are among the worst in South Asia. Development and growth of children is fundamentally formed by the economic and social opportunities provided to them. Therefore, women empowerment is the key as extent of control over resources and participation in the decision making process by females are prerequisites for the number of children and their well-being. The study aims to measure women empowerment together with analyzing the role of women empowerment in fertility behavior, child education and child health in Punjab, Pakistan. Moreover, considering micro-credit being instrumental in women empowerment, the study also focuses on role of micro-credit in women empowerment and consequently on child well-being.

data.projectName: Characterization of Indigenous cattle by using genetic and bioinformatic tools for efficient selection and breeding under climate change scenario
data.projectDigest: Heat stress is a major constraint on animal productivity in tropical conditions. The variation in climatic variables like temperature, humidity and radiations are recognized as the potential hazards in the growth and production of all domestic livestock species. Care must be taken in identifying genes for thermotolerance to avoid inadvertent selection of genes for reduced production (since genes causing low feed intake and low milk yield would increase thermotolerance). This problem could be avoided by identifying candidate genes known to be involved in thermotolerance. There is a compelling need to use modern methods to further define the physiological and cellular basis for thermotolerance in zebu cattle and to identify the genes responsible. Heat shock proteins (Hsp) are known to play major role in protection of cells from thermal stress. The present research project aimed on indigenous animals of Cholistani and Sahiwal breeds. Genetic characterization of cattle breeds for heat shock proteins (HSPs) heat shock elements (HSE), heat shock factors (HSF), prolactin genes and IGFs will be carried out. Gene sequencing of the animals will be performed presenting variation in PCR based analysis to identify the allelic variations. The temperature humidity index (THI), Skin characteristics of the animals will be documented including skin thickness, number of hair follicles per unit area and hair length. Semen from bulls of both breeds will be evaluated for the various quality parameters based on the genetic variations, at different semen production units. Molecular genetic lab. at University of Agriculture, Faisalabad will be used for genetic characterization of indigenous cattle.

data.projectName: Epidemiology and molecular screening of  Tick and Tick-borne pathogens of zoonotic importance in Pothwar region Punjab
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Ticks are known for their negative impact on animal and human health through infestation and are capable of transmitting a wide range of pathogens including protozoan, viruses, and bacteria such as the spirochetes and rickettsiae. Ticks are widely distributed in different ecological and geographical regions of Pakistan. Ticks are responsible for direct and indirect damages to their host. Ticks and tick-borne disease (TTBDs) are major constraints to livestock health (welfare), production and economic losses in developing nations as they cause huge morbidity and mortality consequently causes reduction in production of milk, meat, hide and wool. Tick-borne diseases, such as bovine babesiosis and theileriosis have been reported in Pakistan. Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever (CCHF), a tick-borne viral disease in Pakistan, affects individuals who have close contact with livestock, including those working in slaughterhouses, veterinary practices, and hospitals. In Pakistan, CCHF is vectored by Hyalomma tick species, and therefore a significant threat could be posed to human health. However, there is a paucity of data on tick-borne zoonoses in Pakistan. In the current study, tick species infesting livestock across the Pakistan will be catalogued, and molecular approaches will be utilized to gain an insight into the microbiome associated with tick species. The results of our study will help in the identification of different tick species infesting livestock, and rich diversity of microbial communities associated with the ticks.

data.projectName: Renewable Energy: A Multidimensional exploration of consumer perspicacity, willingness to pay and policy way forward to achieve national energy targets of 2030 in Punjab, Pakistan.
data.projectDigest: At present Pakistan is producing energy mainly form non-renewable resources like gas and fossil fuels. Producing energy form non-renewable sources not only leads to quick depletion of these resource but also have harmful impacts on climate. Renewable or green energy is produced from the natural resources which that can be used again and again and will never expire. There are four major types of renewable energy including solar, hydro, wind and geothermal energy. Energy generation from renewable sources avoids the danger of resource depletion and it is also environment friendly. International agencies are pressurizing Pakistan to transform its energy mix and by 2030 Pakistan must transform its energy generation mechanism such that the country should be able to acquire 30 percent of its energy from renewable energy sources. With this background in mind, present project is designed to find out whether household consumers are aware of the beneficial aspects of the renewable energy. Also, how much surcharge they would like to pay in their energy bills if they agree to pay. Awareness campaigns will be run which will educate the sampled households. This information will help energy supplying companies and government to supply an affordable energy mix through appropriate policies.

data.projectName: Waste Tire Derived Fuel – A Sustainable Solution for Diesel Engine  Performance
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest:
The application of waste tires as an alternative fuel has obtained attention due to the exponential increase in demand and price of fossil fuels, environmental impacts, open disposal, and landfilling of the waste tires. Globally, the pyrolysis process has become the leading solution to this problem by converting the waste tires to the tire pyrolysis oil (TPO). Diesel engines are extensively used in agricultural machinery, transport as well as stationary systems (generators, etc.) for the production of electricity. The improved pyrolysis process is environmentally friendly than the current practices of pyrolysis process in Pakistan. 
The physicochemical properties of the TPO are measured by different instruments and their effects on the combustion, performance, and emission characteristics of the diesel engine have been calculated.  Cylinder pressure, ignition delay, and heat release rate will be observed and noted its impact on the combustion analysis of the TPO. Brake power, brake thermal efficiency, and brake specific fuel consumption will be studied in the performance analysis of TPO. In emission analysis, nitrogen oxides, hydrocarbon emission, carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide and particulate matter emission will be observed in emission analyzers. Furthermore, tribological characteristics (friction and wear) of tire oil have been evaluated.

data.projectName: Efficacy of ?-sitosterol and tryptophan for improved growth and nutraceutical value of wheat (Triticum, aestivum L.) and chili (Capsicum annuum L.)
data.projectDigest:
With the passage of time, globally malnutrition and decline of immunity is becoming very serious issue. In developing countries like Pakistan it is worst in its impact. World health organization has pointed out it as highlighted issue for search of its solutions. Amongst the possible solutions best recommended is the use of plant source. Plant has great pool of biochemical that is beneficial for its own metabolism and also for its consumer’s health. 
It is planned to over produce these compounds within plants for better medicinal and nutritive value of food crops. For that purpose detailed biosynthetic pathway of these compounds were studied from literature. Then it is planned to treat plants with those biochemical (?-sitosterol and tryptophan) as seed treatment before sowing that can start these pathways. It may enhance their products in plant. 
The crops selected for experiment are wheat and chili. Both are major used plants in Asian kitchens. With successful results we may be able to produce routine food (wheat) and spice (chili) enriched with such compounds that are with better nutritive value and medicinal value. It would improve our immunity system without use of extra and expensive supplements. It may also reduce the risk of malnutrition symptoms in low income countries. It would help to improve health of low income countries with regular diet when successfully followed by applications upon other crops.

data.projectName: Inequality of Opportunity in Pakistan: Perspective from Labour Earnings and Educational Outcome
data.projectDigest: Equitable distribution of resources and eradication of inequality and poverty has been considered as an important tool for sustainable development. Sustainable development cannot be achieved without fairness and equality. Putting the disadvantaged group at the same level and providing them the equal opportunities and access towards resources is one the dire needs of sustainable development. Leaving no one behind and provision of level playing field across regions, ethnic groups, and gender would reduce poverty, inequality, and finally would be catalytic towards economic development. The distinction between ‘inequality of outcome’ and ‘inequality of opportunity’ attracted the interests of development economist and policy makers because inequality of opportunity affects inequality of outcome that leads to the problem of social fairness .  The study aims of estimate inequality of opportunity indices from labour earnings and educational perspectives in case of Punjab province of Pakistan through household survey.

Diaabetic foot is one of its main complication where wounds does not heal properly and get worsed over the period of time and may end in amputation. These open wounds are often colanized by various bacteria and leads to poor healing. Current avaible treatment focuses on use of topical or sytemic administration of antibiotics. So, with available treatment options healing is slow and needs prolong time. It would be interesting to design a system which not only covers the wound but also prevents growth of bacteria but also promote wound healing. Here we proposed to use natural ingredients from Pakistan fauna and flora (Okra, Seabuckthorn) to make a dressing for diabetic foot ulcer. These ingredients will work synergistically antibiotic for early recovery of diabetic foot and thus lowers the sufferings of patient and  burden on healthcare system.

data.projectName: Commercial Production of Biofertilizer/Pathocide for Tunnel Farming and Kitchen Gardening
data.projectDigest: Healthy soils are vital to sustainable agricultural where soil organisms directly affect fertility and productivity. They recycle and mobilize nutrients for crops and contribute more by antagonizing or killing pathogens. Therefore, biofertilizers and mycofungicides are considered vital tool in organic agriculture and especially in kitchen gardening. Proposed research is an effort to exploit actual potential of local strains of Trichoderma harzianum as a bioproduct with dual action properties (pathocidal and plant growth stimulator). This product will be readily available in carrier based solid biofertilizer (Granular) to enhance plant vigor and control soil borne diseases in vegetables under tunnel and for kitchen gardeners. This fungus is an avirulent plant symbiont with tremendous potential against several soil borne plant pathogens. It has been widely used as plant growth promoter and antagonist against root rots, fusarium wilt and pythium spp in vegetables. The ultimate produce of research is a bioproduct which will be commercialized specifically for organic food lovers.  The native population of T. harzianum will be characterized and optimized for standardized bioproduct in local market. Finally, product will be patented and registered with brand name of TichoPak.

data.projectName: FUNCTIONAL ANALYSIS OF NOVEL GENES INVOLVED IN NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS
data.piUniversity: Mirpur University of Science and Technology (MUST), AJ&K
data.projectDigest:
In Pakistan due to high rate of consanguinity many families are at a high risk of being affected with genetic disorders and currently, there are no potential services available in Pakistan to help families to manage their increased genetic reproductive risk. Hence in the proposed research project focus is to understand the expression pathway of novel genes involved in nervous disorders with especial emphasis on intellectual disability and microcephaly. Consanguineous families affected with nervous disorders will be explored and analyzed for novel genes involved in nervous disorders. Expression study of these genes will be helpful for better understanding of genetic diseases in Pakistani community and the treatment of genetic diseases in Pakistani population. Moreover this study will also be helpful in counseling of those families which are having a risk of producing affected children.
The burden of genetic disorders in Pakistani population can be reduced by exploring the pathways and possible mechanisms involved in these disorders. Hence this study aims to explore that mechanism in model animals e.g mouse model that would be helpful in understanding of those mechanisms in humans.

data.projectName: Evaluation and mass rearing  of resistance strains of Chrysoperla carnea
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is a mainly agriculture country which is now a days  is affected by pests on crops. Pest can be reduced by chemical and use of natural enemy. Chrysoperla carnea  is very important natural enemy of insect pests of various crops which can feed on aphids, leafhoppers, psyllids, coccids, mites, whiteflies, thrips and mealy bug.  Chemical control is one of the cheapest management strategies of many insect pests of various crops in Pakistan. But chemical control of insect pest leads to many drawbacks such as environmental toxicity, mammalian toxicity, hazards to human health and mortality of non-target insects such as natural enemies. Both chemical and biological control agents are also used to get maximum insect pest control. In recent years biological control of pest has become most important because most of the pests are becoming resistant to a number of insecticides. Also the natural enemies are exposed to insecticides but their resistance is slower than their susceptibility in this exposure likewise pest. So, compatibility of insecticide with biological control agents is a major concern for effectiveness of integrated pest management (IPM) because pesticides play a major role in most IPM programs. This compatibility could be achieved by using insecticide resistant strain of natural enemies for insect pest control. Many studies have been reported about the feeding potential of C. carnea on different insect pest, toxicity of insecticides, resistance and compatibility to insecticides. C. carnea is an ideal generalist biological control agent to develop its resistant strain for field evaluation which could be an effective strategy to control insect pests.

data.projectName: Indigenizing the Art of Moviemaking in New Media age
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan, formal education of filmmaking has never been introduced at educational institutes, particularly at public sector, because the medium of film has never been acknowledged as an art form. As a result, trained human resource from within the country is missing. Indeed, the researcher is first Pakistani to achieve his PhD in the Art of Filmmaking from UK, and has introduced a new subject of TVC and Video Production in bachelors program, at the College of Art and Design, University of the Punjab (CAD, PU), in 2017. The original content developed by the researcher during his PhD has provide the basis to develop curriculum for this new subject. A small video lab with equipment for hands on training of students has also been approved by Vice Chancellor, PU. Thus, students are learning basic skill of filmmaking; however, to further improve the quality of the production to match the industrial requirements, this research needs to be conducted. It will be helpful to develop an indigenous style of making films, and contextualize the art of making film, market demand, and the distribution networks in the age of new media.

data.projectName: Effect of Phytonanoparticles  in managing early blight disease of tomato
data.projectDigest: Early blight disease attacking tomato often inflicts severe losses up to 80%. Modern agriculture without conventional pesticides will be possible through exploring role of modern technology like nanotechnology in managing disease. This project is designed to evaluate disease managing potential of nano-fertilizers prepared from peels of banana and citrus. The peel based fertilizers will be characterized and will be applied for their efficiency through field experiment. The present study will not only provide effective disease management option by using nanotechnology but also help in finding for better fruit productivity and quality. Furthermore it will also highlight the physiological and biochemical parameters that are involved in disease tolerance and resistance mechanisms in plants.

data.projectName: SERO-EPIDEMIOLOGICAL INVESTIGATION ON Q FEVER AND ITS ASSOCIATION WITH REPRODUCTIVE DISORDERS IN SMALL RUMINANTS OF KHYBER PAKHTUNKHWA, PAKISTAN
data.projectDigest: Q (Query) fever is a highly infectious disease of bacterial origin, caused by Coxiella (C.) burnetii, a Gram-negative, coccobacillus and strictly intracellular bacterium; which is extremely hardy and ubiquitous in nature. This disease acts as a major trade barrier adversely affecting the productive and reproductive capability of the animals, and hinders with commercialization of animals product and at market level. Ruminants especially sheep and goats are considered as most important animal reservoir and source of disseminating infection to human beings. This study has been planned to conduct serological and molecular investigations on Q fever and to identify any association of seropositivity against C. burnetii antibodies with some potential risk in small ruminants of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. A structured questionnaire will be designed to collect individual and farm/herd level data. For the current study, a total of 1600 blood samples (800 from sheep and goats each) will be collected considering an expected prevalence of 50%, confidence interval of 95%, and 5% desired absolute precision. Firstly, all these samples will be analyzed using Q fever Indirect-ELISA and then pools of seropositive, and suspected serum samples will be investigated through real-time qPCR, using multicopy IS1111 gene, for detection of C. burnetii DNA. Additionally, a total of 100 tick pools will also be analyzed through real-time qPCR for genomic detection of C. burnetii. Finally sequencing of C. burnetii DNA will be performed using latest DNA sequencing technique (for samples having Ct value <28). The data on different variables obtained from this study will be analyzed using Minitab version 17 software and SPSS Statistics version 17.

data.projectName: Comprehensive study of biosorptive capacity of activated carbon derived from Ficus benghalensis and modified agrarian material for selected heavy metal ions
data.projectDigest: Toxification of heavy metals in water sources is a threat to the human life. It has raised up the dire need of heavy metals elimination from the environment. There are different treatment methods but biosorption is the most economical and eco-friendly solution for the elimination of these metal ions from contaminated water. Detoxification of toxic metal ions from the water sources are required to avoid the heavy metal contamination in biological systems. These heavy metals when absorbed in the body cause serious health problems such as accumulative poisoning, cancer, brain damage and so forth. Heavy metals are non-biodegradable and once they enter in the body, they retard the biochemical reactions in the body for long time. Removal of these toxic metal ions is appreciated by biosorption process because of multiple benefits. Cost-effective nature makes this phytoremediation process acceptable for the industries. A broad spectrum biosorption study is mandatory for the real understanding of the process. This biosorption process includes characterization of biosorbent, biosorption parameters, equilibrium and kinetic studies. Additionally, mechanism will be studied by rate determining steps including mass transfer model, intraparticle diffusion, boundary layer diffusion and boyd plot. Activated carbon will be derived from the Ficus benghalensis and its biosorptive capacity will be compared with the modified biomass of this agrarian material.

data.projectDigest: The devolution of power to the lowest tier is the essence of the 1973 constitution of Pakistan. Yet Pakistan failed to implement her constitution in its true spirits, however, in 2010 the 18th amendment was passed. The 18th constitutional amendment abolished the concurrent list that contained many subjects with joint responsibility. This amendment empowered provinces to legislate and implement policies related to the devolved ministries on their own. Education and Health are two of the 17 devolved ministries. Provinces, after taking charge, have then started formulating policies as they thought will have fruitful results for their concerned provinces. Over the course of 9 years, many laws have been passed by provincial governments regarding the new ministries they got after the 18th amendment. The transfer of power to the provincial governments may bring a shift in the priorities from developing hard infrastructure to focus on institutional evolution. Unless the devolution and decentralization are implemented in its true essence the trickle-down effect of the devolution may not be exceptional. Education has been the least priority of governments since the inception of Pakistan. The importance of implementation of the devolution plan in its true spirit is important for improved service delivery. The study will check if there is a paradigm shift in the expenditure pattern of governments and if there is some shift has the benefit of that shift reached the common man? data.projectName: Need Assessment and Capacity Building Strategies on Family Literacy through Non-formal Education
data.projectDigest: This project will contribute in need assessment on family literacy in rural Punjab, and development of capacity building strategies to promote family literacy. This study will analyze the existing situation on family literacy and the required training to educate society (NGOs) on family literacy. Proposed project will also foster development of capacity building strategies among non-formal education providers/institutions who will then give returns to the wider community including students, parents and families. Overall, this study will provide a value addition for the betterment of community in terms of educating them on family literacy. The broader aim of this project covers the community service approach to provide useful information on existing scenario on family literacy in rural Punjab and then devising family literacy strategies by using non-formal approach to attain SDG4. The broader impact of the proposed investigation will provide practical information to the policy makers for the inclusion of family literacy in future policies.

data.projectName: Biocatalytic approach towards synthesis of Anti-Alzheimer compounds
data.projectDigest:
This research proposal is based on the idea that certain chemical entities have proven abilities to affect the brain function in one way or the other, and a subtle change in their chemical structure may render them more effective against the Alzheimer disease (AD). This is a neurodegenerative disease which leads to the  loss to body functions and even death in severe cases. A biocatalytic (enzyme catalyzed) approach has been designed to achieve the goals. The proposed protocol has the capability of producing multiple products from a single starting materials in one pot, thus providing a range of structurally diverse molecules for testing against AD. Moreover, this method is convenient, cost effective, and environmentally benign. In addition, the proposed methodology is up-scalable and the results obtained are also reproducible. 
The anti-Alzheimer potential of the products will be evaluated by employing standard assay protocols.
Upon successful completion, the proposed research is expected to yield more potent and much safer molecules against AD. This will provide an opportunity to the pharma industry to obtain or produce cheap raw material for preparing dosage forms of these molecules for further studies, rather than importing it from foreign countries which costs a lot.

data.projectName: Use of plant-derived polyphenols for improving semen quality and fertility of buffalo (Bubalus bubalis) bull spermatozoa
data.projectDigest:
Spermatozoa, unlike other cells, is distinguished for possessing explicit structure, function, and the vulnerability to the oxidative stress. During cryopreservation (adaptation of spermatozoa to low temperature), higher concentrations of reactive oxygen species (ROS) are generated that circumvented the physiological limitations led to the occurrence of oxidative stress and compromised the quality of bubaline semen. The occurrence of oxidative stress is the resultant of disparity between the endogenous antioxidant capacity and generation of ROS. Moreover, the spermatozoa are equipped with higher concentrations of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) inside plasmalemma, due to which buffalo spermatozoa become more defenseless to the oxidative damage, with a succeeding loss in plasma, acrosome and DNA integrities, and even the onset of apoptosis. Moreover, oxidative damage resulting in loss in mitochondrial membrane potential, impaired motility and fertilization of buffalo spermatozoa. In this prospect, plant-derived polyphenols possess robust antioxidant features by refining the semen quality and fertility of buffalo spermatozoa. 
The specific objectives of the current project are: To 1) explore the ameliorative influences of plant-derived polyphenols on structural and functional characteristics, 2) oxidative stress indices and 3) fertility of buffalo spermatozoa.

data.projectName: Evaluation of mannan-oligosaccharides to produce healthy birds with optimal organ and muscle development: An attempt to address the issue of food safety
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Heavy metal pollution is a serious problem faced by developing and developed countries. Cadmium is listed as one of the most toxic heavy metal affecting the health and well being of living beings. Exposure of broilers to cadmium results in a reduction of performance and gastrointestinal infections, leading to excessive use of antibiotics. Further, cadmium cannot be eliminated from body and accumulates in liver, kidneys, bones and muscle hence, becomes a source of exposure for humans through consumption of contaminated meat and viscera. Cadmium has also been reported to play a role in development of antimicrobial resistance against antibiotics therefore its alleviation is imperative to avoid its exposure. Use of chelators is criticized due to their unwanted gastrointestinal and nephrotoxic effects and absence of any evidence of their efficacy in clinical trials. Prebiotic mannan-oligosaccharides (MOS) has been extensively evaluated for its potential as an alternative to antibiotics in animal feed. It is a promising agent to improve the gastrointestinal health of broiler but its potential in reducing the toxicity of cadmium is a a new concept. Therefore, this project is designed with an objective to evaluate the potential of prebiotic MOS to manage the toxic effects of cadmium in broilers.

data.projectName: Modeling and Experimental Evaluation of III-V Heterojunction Avalanche Photodiodes for Diverse UV Sensing Applications
data.projectDigest:
In the field of photonics engineering, the avalanche photodiode as a light detector, has found a renewed purpose, especially in fields like telecommunication, missile flume detection, as well as environmental monitoring. It offers a wide variety of materials and configurations, which can be customized to the desired situation and application. It also offers an ease of manufacturability and design, which leads to the attainment of the high gain. One exciting variation of the traditional APD is the choice of III-V materials (such as AlxGa1-xN and GaN materials) APD, which lends itself useful for UV photodetection in environment monitoring, as well as the defense industry, both of which are prime areas of focus within Pakistan.
The aim of this project is to analytically design and fabricate these novel III-V avalanche photodiodes. The work developed in the course of this project will investigate the variations of designs details using industrial modeling tools, and will present a realistic review for the practical implementation of these designs for the fabrication cycle. This project will also bridge the missing link between theoretical modeling and the practical culmination of such designs, by experimentally developing a prototype of this design for detecting Deep Ultraviolet light for versatile applications.

data.projectName: Experimental Investigation for the effects of Molds produced by Additive Manufacturing over the Quality of Fiber-Reinforced Composites
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Rapid tooling lack fine surface finish as compared to conventional Aluminum or other metal molds. Moreover, their tool life is comparatively much lesser than the conventional tooling. In this study, the effects of process parameters used for developing the molds by additive manufacturing and producing composite parts on the response variables, such as; surface finish of mold and parts, critical-to-quality dimension and life of mold of different composite materials are analyzed. data.projectName: Hydrologic reconstructions using tree ring chronologies and climate information for Upper Indus Basin
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Tree ring chronologies (TRC) are typically used for hydrologic reconstructions. Using climate information along with TRC may help improve the reconstruction skill. Water availability in Pakistan is largely driven by precipitation, streamflows and snowmelt. Rising population, changing climate, depleting groundwater resources and urbanization make sustainability of water reserves a critical issue in Pakistan. Better policies and planning for water resources is a crucial need to mitigate this challenging situation, however, informed planning requires knowledge regarding past hydrologic variability. Length of the available instrumental records in Pakistan, is typically limited to a few decades and may not depict the long-term hydrologic variability encompassing the severity and frequency of the past low flow events. Hydrologic reconstruction can extend the available records to several centuries. Studies have shown that climate indices of Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO), Southern Oscillation Index (SOI) and North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) influence the weather patterns of northern Pakistan. The purpose of this study is to reconstruct the snowpack, rainfall and streamflow of selected regions of Upper Indus Basin, located in northern Pakistan by using TRC along with the climate information of PDO, SOI and NAO, as predictors in a step-wise linear regression model.
