data.projectName: INVESTIGATION OF THE ROLE OF PEROXIREDOXIN-2 IN SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION AFTER SUBARACHNOID HEMORRHAGE (SAH) AND POST-SAH COMPLICATIONS
data.projectDigest: Strokes are of two types i.e., ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke. Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) is a subtype of hemorrhagic stroke characterized by the rupture of aneurysm and bleeding into the subarachnoid space of the brain. Although, the incidence is low but mortality rates are very high. SAH patients deteriorate even after securing the bleeding aneurysms by neurosurgical clipping or endovascular coiling.  Different life threatening complications such as cerebral vasospasm (CVS), seizures, chronic hydrocephalus,  delayed cerebral ischemia etc. lead to poor outcomes. Recent investigations have identified two phases of brain injury with a key role of inflammation. Studying the pathophysiological players in upregulating the inflammation has not only the prognostic and diagnostic potential but also can identify important therapeutic targets. Therefore, based on our previous experience, we are planning a study to investigate Peroxiredoxin-2, which upon cellular injury is released extracellularly and  behaves as a damage associated molecular pattern (DAMPs). DAMPs can activate immune cells and upregulate inflammation. So, our hypothesis is that Peroxiredoxin-2 will be released extracellularly after SAH and will upregulate inflammation.  Measurement of Peroxiredoxin-2 levels in serum along with other inflammatory markers will aid in the prognosis and diagnosis of different post-SAH complications. Peroxiredoxin-2 may also act as a potential therapeutic target if we found its involvement in  upregulating the inflammation.

data.projectName: DIGITAL AND REMOTE SENSING TECHNOLOGIES TO COUNTER INCREASING AIR POLLUTION IN PAKISTAN
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan, vehicular pollution has been ignored, especially the transportation emissions from trade vehicles carrying 96% of the national freight. Consequently, cities in Pakistan are facing the verse air quality degradation in the world. The situation will become even more critical due to an exponential increase in the freight volume to 7,000 vehicles across the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) trade route, which will release up to 36.5 million tonnes of emissions per day. The most practical way for developing countries to mitigate carbon emissions is to conserve and expand existing forests, so that the forests sequester more carbon and, thus, maintain the balance. However, the increased CPEC freight volume will cause immense ecosystem degradation in the mountainous forests and glaciers along the northern route, i.e., Karakorum highway (KH). The effects will sharply trigger the local climate change and badly impact the national air quality. This requires providing digital services to automated, continuous, location-based, and effective monitoring and valuation of carbon stocks/trading and related ecosystem services. This project aims to improve location-based estimation and forecasting of carbon stocks in forests on the northern CPEC route through data from satellite remote sensing, unmanned aerial vehicles, and ground sensors linked with digital platforms.

data.projectName: HIGHER EDUCATION MARKETING: AN EXPLORATION OF MARKETING PERCEPTIONS AND PRACTICES IN HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS OF PAKISTAN
data.piUniversity: University of Kotli Azad Jammu and Kashmir
data.projectDigest: The objectives of the study will be; determining the role of educational marketing in higher education institutions; to explore the perceptions of stakeholders regarding educational marketing in higher education institutions; to discover the educational marketing strategies used in higher education institutions across the country; to unveil the similarities and differences in the educational marking of higher educational institutions across the country; and to develop a framework of educational marketing for higher education institutions. The sequential exploratory strategy of mixed method will be used in the present research. In this strategy, the qualitative data will be collected in the first phase of the research through interviews (from 30 educational administrators and 60 teachers) and documentary checklists. On the basis of the descriptive analysis of the qualitative data, questionnaire will be prepared to collect quantitative data in the second phase of the research. Total 450 (150 educational administrators and 300 teachers) selected through stratified random sampling technique from the universities across Pakistan will be the sample of the study for quantitative data. The quantitative will be analysed using mean, frequency, graphs, independent sample t-test and ANOVA. The results of the study may prove beneficent for the authorities of HEC as it has the potential to explore new strategies for educational marketing in the higher education institutions of Pakistan. The study will be extremely fruitful for all of  the authorities of higher education institutions to plan better marketing practices in the light of recommendations of the proposed study. Moreover, the shortcomings of higher education marketing will also come to surface.

data.projectName: Molecular characterization of Mycoplasma putrefaciens (local strain) for the establishment of effective diagnostics and vaccines.
data.projectDigest: Mycoplasma putrefaciens (Mp) is a dreadful pathogen that causes a severe, usually fatal Contagious agalactia syndrome (CAS) in goats characterized by mastitis, arthritis, keratoconjunctivitis, pneumonia, and Septicemia (MAKePS). CAS is categorized by the OIE as a notifiable terrestrial and aquatic animal diseases. The current dearth of efficient diagnostic and control measures leaves Pakistani farmers at continuous great risk of financially dreadful Mp outbreaks. Thus far, very limited information is available on the molecular characterization of the Mp strains prevalent in Pakistan. Commercial diagnostics produces false positive and false negative results, indicating that isolates of Mp from goats of Pakistan are distinct from those previously characterized in other regions.  Without effective diagnostics, carrier goats rapidly infect entire flocks and therapeutic intervention comes too late.  Therapeutics and vaccines specific to Mp local isolates have not been developed, and costly and poor accessibility of Mp biologics in the country greatly restricts their use by poor farmers.  These conditions contribute to the costly and miserable perpetuation of Mp infection in goat flocks. We propose to apply molecular techniques to characterize endemic Mp isolates in order to produce an effective diagnostic kit and vaccine. This project will be enabled by collaboration between investigators and labs in The University of Agriculture Peshawar, Abdul Wali Khan University, Mardan, Pakistan and Veterinary Research Institute, Peshawar, Pakistan. Upon achievement of these aims, we will help to overcome a serious livestock disease, promoting growth of the goat industry, contributing to poverty alleviation campaigns and to quality of life for farmers of the “poor man’s cow” in Pakistan

data.projectName: Identification of insecticide susceptibility status of Culex quinquefasciatus to different insecticides in different parts of Malakand division and role of native medicinal plants in mosquito control
data.piUniversity: University of Malakand, Chakdara, Dir, Malakand
data.projectDigest:
Culex quinquefasciatus that belongs to the genus Culex, is the most abundant mosquito species in Pakistan. It is the vector of Wuchereria bancrofti, which is the lymphatic filarial parasite of humans that causes lymphatic filariasis commonly known as elephantiasis. Culex quinquefasciatus is also a vector of avian malaria. Control of mosquitoes is essential and currently synthetic insecticides are mostly applied for mosquito control. They are non-biodegradable and create insecticide resistance in insect pests and kill non-target organisms. Therefore, there is a need of searching and developing an alternative and environment friendly control strategies. Insecticides derived from plants are believed to be biodegradable, effective and environment friendly.  Malakand division is very rich in medicinal plants, therefore during the current project, the essential oils from native medicinal plants will be extracted and evaluated for their eco-friendly and efficient role in mosquito control. 
There is increasing trend of agricultural pesticides use in Malakand division. Contamination of larval habitats by agricultural insecticides results in development of insecticide resistance in mosquitoes.  Insecticides from agricultural sites reach to mosquito breeding sites through runoff during rainy season, and thus may affect larval population. Frequent application of agricultural pesticides for many years can exerts a huge selection pressure on larval stages of mosquitoes that can result in development of resistance to insecticides. During the current project, the insecticide resistance status of the most abundant mosquito species to insecticides in Malakand division will be investigated. The findings of such study will provide baseline information for control of disease borne vectors.

data.projectName: Target directed repurposing of bioactive compounds phytoconstituents as anticancer drugs; experimental and In-silico prospective
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Cyclin dependent kinases (CDKs) are serin/threonine kinases, plays critical role in regulating various events of cell-cycle regulation. Recently, CDK4 inhibitors have been approved by FDA to be used commercially as anticancer drugs which confirms that the CDKs are potential targets to treat cancer. Nevertheless, the identification and development of CDKs inhibitor from natural source and/or repurposing of known bioactive compounds as CDKs inhibitors is still poorly taken into considerations. This project is designed to: (i) utilize computational techniques to explore binding affinities of ligands towards targeted proteins as compared to standard, (ii) develop a 3D-QSAR model in the basis of series of compound to evaluate CDKs inhibitory potential of selected compounds prior to experimental work. (iii) MTT-assay against various cell lines with high CDK2 expression i.e. HepG2 (iv) Gene expression analysis with Real-Time qRT-PCR (v) western blotting. The exquisite combination of cheminformatics and wet-lab techniques would help to identify CDKs inhibitors as anti-cancer agents. Furthermore, it would be a state of the art lab dually equipped with natural product, pharmacology and cheminformatics related tools. It would provide opportunity to other institutes to perform multidisciplinary analysis to identify potent anti-cancer agent in such a setting which may save time any capital.

data.projectName: Comparative Assessment of Teratogenic and Toxicologic Impacts of Natural and Synthetic Preservatives in food and cosmetics on Mammalian Model.
data.projectDigest:
preservation of food and other products was exercised hundreds of years ago when man used smoke and salt to prevent things from going bad. Main reason for using preservatives is to make commodities safer from the negative influence of biological factors and to increase the shelf life of the product. But with the increase in population and modernization these methods of preserving goods became least effective and insufficient. It has been roughly estimated that about 75% today's diet is made up different kind of processed foods and with an average of 8-10lbs food additives/ preservatives, each person consuming per year, some probably using even more in the form of cosmetics and drugs (Tuula, 1994). It is obvious that for a fast result, one needs to be more specific and more selective. No doubt these chemical preservatives are more efficient, cheap and easily available besides they are disease causing and life threating too.
Hence natural alternatives for preservation included in emerging trends, as many studies have shown that the use of synthetic preservatives and chemical additives is leading to intoxication, carcinogenesis and many other diseases. This generates the necessity to look for alternatives in the form of natural agents that cover the same antimicrobial properties and compatibility with cosmetic and   food products but should be less toxic.

data.projectName: Modelling, Simulation and Optimization of Energy Sustainability for Internet of Things Enabled Smart Cities Empowered With Deep Extreme Learning Machine
data.piUniversity: National College of Business Administration & Economics, Lahore
data.projectDigest: The proposed system is a functional and successful collaboration of the computer domains. The techniques of machine learning composing the proposed methodology that is energy management in smart cities. In this thesis, a deep extreme learning machine method is proposed to meet the challenges presented and to emphasize the point of the method in energy management of smart cities. DELM has been used in the proposed work to encapsulate the benefits of ELM as well as deep learning. In addition, it has been shown that using deep extreme learning machine (DELM) significantly improves the expected results. In this research work, managing energy is regarded as the main prototype for the implementation of smart city complicated energy systems. This research work provides a short summary of energy management and difficulties in smart cities, then specify a cohesive structure for energy sustainability for IoT based smart cities. A deep extreme learning machine (DELM) approach will be used to make smart cities energy efficient with IoT enabled sensors with improved performance. Energy-efficient systems are entering future smart cities with superior equipment, control structures, and demand response policies. In this research, a model for power plant electrical energy output prediction has been proposed to improve the prediction accuracy.

data.projectName: Analysis of Sea Water Quality through Internet of Underwater Things (IoUT) for usage in Terrestrial and Aquatic Environment
data.projectDigest:
Supply of clean drinking water has been a problem not only in Pakistan but globally. The issue needs to be resolved. Sea water, oceans and lakes in Pakistan are badly affected due to pollution. When water quality is bad, it not only affects the marine life but the nearby ecosystem too. It is a global challenge equally for the developed and developing countries.
Since water is a precious resource and is a principal factor for existence of living beings below or above the surface of water, it is important to monitor the quality of water from canals to rivers and oceans. Testing and investigating quality of water is a vital part of environmental monitoring. The main objectives of this project are to develop a water quality monitoring system, to detect pollution in water through Internet of Underwater Things (IoUT). 
The scope for this research concerns with the monitoring and evaluation of the quality levels of different water reservoirs, which is crucial for the sustainability and livelihood for the ecosystem and marine life. The Principal investigator has discussed the project with the Academic and Sectoral collaborators that will contribute to the success of the proposed project.

data.projectName: Effects of antibiotics on neuro-immunological parameters with and without antidepressant or anxiolytic on CSOM induced rats
data.projectDigest:
Ear infection of middle ear (chronic suppurative otitis media) may last for a long period of time even forever with intervals. This may lead to hearing loss. Different antibiotics are available to manage this infection  but due to the long term use of antibiotics resistance  may develop. The aim of the study is to find out the effects of antibiotics on treatment of ear infection and on those chemicals which can change mood and behavior of patients or increase the risk of  allergy.  Moreover, effects of medicine which can decrease depression or anxiety with antibiotics will also be observed. Therefore, depression, anxiety and stress produced by these medicines with biological test  in healthy rats and rats with ear infection will be  studied. in order to evaluate the risk factors which can effect outcomes of medicine such as blood test and biopsy (liver) will also be carried out. 
this will help to find out the better medicine currently use in ear infection with allergy or depression and whether use of depression decreasing medicine will be useful or not in ear infection with depression or allergy.

data.projectName: Solution of Matching Problems in Machine Learning using Representation Theory
data.projectDigest: A major problem in many applications is to match diverse objects. For example, we can view search as a matching between a query and a document. Similarly image retrieval can be viewed as a problem of matching between a text query and an image. It is a fundamental challenge in areas such as machine learning, computer vision, and computational biology to achieve an optimal measure of overlap between the two objects. This problem has diverse application such as security screening systems, search engines, records retrieval. In this project we will use novel ideas from representations theory of groups to design and optimize algorithms for the matching problem. We will also experiment with well-known data sets to attain a high accuracy for practical use.

data.projectName: INVESTIGATING THE STRATEGIES TO REMEDY THE ADVERSE EFFECTS OF FAT REDUCTION ON TEXTURE AND FUNCTIONALITY OF CHEDDAR TYPE CHEESE
data.projectDigest:
The aim of reducing calories in diet, specially focusing fat, stimulates the manufacturing of reduced fat cheeses. Cheese fat reduction is difficult since milk fat adds the desired flavor and texture. The principal concern in fat reduction is undesirable hard rubbery texture. Different methods are used to enhance quality and functionality in reduced fat cheeses but no successful execution up-till now. The use of polysaccharides producing starters, hydrocolloids, fibers, fat replacers, various milk sources and elevated ripening temperatures are fictional to remedy the defects. These are under study but have certain limitations and draw-backs.
The research work is designed to produce Cheddar cheese from cow and buffalo milk at various fat levels using hydrocolloids and ripening at elevated temperatures. The poor texture development owing to fat reduction may be overcome by water absorbing and colloidal properties of hydrocolloids and accelerating the ripening especially proteolysis. The increased rate of proteolysis may eliminate texture and flavour defects. Moreover, low fat cheese from cow and buffalo milk combinations would result in better textural based on variations in protein profiles. Meltability, texture profile, proteolytic pattern and sensory quality will be studied during accelerated ripening of low fat cheese to assess the quality and functionality.

Moreover, low fat cheese from cow and buffalo milk combinations would result in better textural based on variations in protein profiles. Meltability, texture profile, proteolytic pattern and sensory quality will be studied during accelerated ripening of low fat cheese to assess the quality and functionality.

data.projectName: Designing and Development of an All-in-one three-dimensional Platform for Cultivation of Multicellular Hepatoma tumoroids to evaluate Chemoresistance
data.projectDigest: Liver cancer is the fifth most abundant solid cancer at third number worldwide. Conventional two-dimensional (2D) cell cultures could not represent the complex three-dimensional (3D) natural microenvironment of liver cancer. Specially, essential biological phenomena like adhesion, migration, gene expression, and proliferation can be more clearly reproduced by 3D culture. Currently, there are lack of the adequate 3D culture model for studying tumor microenvironment. Therefore, fabrication of a suitable 3D matrix system for Hepatoma is a major challenge to be addressed. In the current study a 3D scaffold system will be designed for the production of tumoroids. It is expected the 3D scaffold will recapitulate the hepatoma microenvironment and hence it will represent the chemoresistance phenomenon to anticancer drug that of like in vivo tumor. The possible factor involved and molecular mechanism at genetic level will be evaluated by molecular level using PCR analysis. And the level of important genes involved in chemoresistance like interleukins, tumor necrosis factors, nuclear factor kappa-B, matrix metalloproteinases, and signaling pathway genes will be evaluated. The final strategy will be accomplished by inhibiting one or more of the signaling molecule to overcome the chemoresistance to a drugs like doxorubicin and new chemotherapeutic agents like curcumin.

data.projectName: Solving games by labelling graphs: A case study of Game of Thrones
data.projectDigest: Graph theory is very important field of Mathematics. It helps theorists and students to have a picture of what they are studying. Graph theory also helps in analyzing data of complex systems and provide a platform for their solutions. Though many of the graph theoretic models have been developed but there is still a need to develop a framework that should be efficient enough to handle complex data and give an optimal solution. Game theory is also an important branch of mathematics which needs the best strategy for given conditions in order to optimize the outcomes. Games are so interesting that they are everywhere in economic systems, political systems and military systems, etc. Many methods exist in literature for solving games, but this study proposes a graph theoretic method based on graph labeling in terms of coloring that will help to seek the best alternative in a set of possible choices and narrow down the range of possibilities. An important application of graph labeling is discussed in this research, i.e., an analysis of a well known game; Game of Thrones, is proposed in this research. It is an impartial game that is related to a directed graph known as a tournament. Many other applications of this research are in business and economics.

data.projectName: Impact of Electronic and Social Media on Political Awareness of Women in the Rural Areas of South Punjab
data.projectDigest: Media is one of the major sources of developing political awareness among the masses . This might be applicable to the people living in the central areas such as big cities, but could be applied differently to those living in remote and peripheral/rural areas. Women of such areas can be expected at more disadvantaged place in this regard.  Underdeveloped areas, where people struggle to meet the basic necessities of life, it could be really hard to access electronic media for several reasons such as the cost of media equipment, very low literacy rates, unavailability of electricity, inability to understand English or even the national language Urdu, and religious/cultural attitudes towards media. This study aims to measure the level of political awareness in the women,  map the available sources of information to them, and investigate the factors which hinder the access to electronic and social media to women in rural areas of South Punjab. The data for this study will be collected on the basis of field visits, focus group interaction, and interviews and questionnaires with the women in the rural areas of South Punjab.

data.projectName: Biotechnological application of microbiome from a coastal salt marsh plant
data.projectDigest:
Holobiont or plant associated microbiome is considered as second genome of the plant influencing many activities in and around that plant. The studies related to microbiome of xerophytes such as wheat and maize have revealed many interesting aspects and led to development of inoculant formulations for plant growth promotion. However, similar studies are seldom available for the plants that thrive in an usual environment, such as salt marsh. Anthrocnemum macrostachyum, a member of family Amaranth is mainly found in coastal areas and hence can tolerate high levels of salinity even up to 1M NaCl which makes this plant to study its microbiome for salt tolerance and other industrial applications. 
It is hypothesized that the microbiome associated with the A.macrostachyum has a unique composition with the ability to produce osmoregulators, plant growth promoting hormones and industrially important enzymes. 
To test this hypothesis, sampling will be carried out across the coast of Karachi and Balochistan from the sites and sub-sites experiencing inundation. Soil ECe and eco-physiological parameters of the plant will be studies. The plant samples will be transported to the lab using standard protocol and will be surface sterilized to obtain endophytes. The microbes associated with the rhizosphere will also be studied before surface sterilization. The samples will be processed for culture independent and culture dependent techniques. For culture independent techniques, DNA will be extracted and amplified by using 16S rDNA and ITS primers. Sequencing will also carried out from BGI, Macrogen or from University of Edinburgh. Operational Taxon Units (OTUs) will be investigated and diversity indices will be calculated. 
Culture dependent studies will be proceed by adopting spread pla

data.projectName: Development of pilot-scale membrane distillation system for the production of freshwater
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest: Water is basis necessity for life. In Pakistan, a large population is drinking arsenic contaminated water which is badly affecting the health of people. Contamination of groundwater specifically with arsenic is a health hazard for Pakistan especially in Punjab and Sindh provinces. Therefore, this project will address the national issue which is arsenic contaminated water and its remedy which is to provide clean and pure drinking water. Desalination is one of the suitable solutions to overcome the said issues. There are several desalination technologies; however, membrane distillation (MD) is one of the emerging desalination technologies [1]. Recently, MD has attained great attention worldwide due to several advantages such as low temperature and pressure operation . It is important to mention that the application of MD system include seawater desalination, brine concentration, wastewater treatment, non-food chemical processes, and in the food industry.

data.projectName: Development and evaluation of amorphous solid dispersions of fenofibrate for improving its solubility and bioavailability
data.projectDigest: In the recent times, the development of innovative drug delivery systems for newly discovered drugs has become very challenging mainly due to their poor solubility/bioavailability. The success of developed drug delivery system is strongly dependent on in vivo solubility of encapsulated drug. Drugs from BCS class II present poor solubility thus their desired therapeutic outcome is deeply associated with improved bioavailability. Fenofibrate (FB), a vastly used dyslipidaemic drug belong to BCS class II, is used to lower total cholesterol in combination with other antilipidemic drugs. However, its poor water solubility leads to achieving its efficient therapeutic level very challenging.  Due to the direct solubility problems, different approaches are used to develop novel formulations that can provide improved oral bioavailability. Several strategies such as nanoparticle preparations, self-emulsifying drug delivery systems, micronization and amorphous solid dispersions have been employed to increase the dissolution as well as oral bioavailability of poorly water soluble drugs. In this project, amorphous solid dispersion (ASD) will be used as promising approach to enhance the oral bioavailability of fenofibrate due to numerous advantages linked with this technology. In addition, amorphous solid dispersion carries significant potential for preparing commercial products due to reduction of drug particle size at molecular level, increased wetting capacity and pore formation as well as resulting stable formulation by conversion of drug from crystalline to amorphous form. Hot melt extrusion technology will be used to fabricate amorphous solid dispersions due to its ease and continuous process of manufacturing. Additionally, it presents a solvent free process with less production

data.projectName: The eradication of xenophobic tendencies within Pakistani youth through the training initiatives focused on diversity acceptance and tolerance: A need of a structural change
data.projectDigest: A vast majority of people believe that CPEC can provide a major economic edge to both countries, China and Pakistan. However, there are people who view the whole scenario with the xenophobic mindset and do not want this project to flourish. What’s worrying is when these people do not keep their xenophobic convictions to themselves, but influence other people to follow their footsteps. One of the most vulnerable group of people to be influenced by them are the youngsters, particularly college and university students. Therefore, it is important for the academic institutions to introduce training programs/workshops/seminar for the youth, which focus on acceptance of diversity and promotion of tolerant culture, as a regular part of their curriculum in order to shun the adverse outcomes of xenophobia. The designing and implementation of such programs in terms of the content is a very challenging task as these are tricky subject matters, and so people may retaliate. Therefore, the proposed study involves the accomplishment of two main objectives. First objective is concerned with the designing of the training programs while the second objective is concerned with the development of the implementation strategies which will ensure the diversity accepting attributes and tolerant culture among the youth of colleges and universities. Hence, the study has important implications in the context of internationalization, particularly with regard to CPEC which has not only allowed the economic integration between China and Pakistan, but also it has led to a massive exchange of workforce between the two nations.

data.projectName: Transition Metal Chalcogenides Nanosheets for Visible Light Photocatalyst and Electrocatalyst for Energy Applications
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Harvesting solar energy effectively and efficiently to produce alternative fuels and value-added chemicals is unceasingly growing. Especially, harvesting solar energy to produce renewable hydrogen fuel from water gained significant attention. To facilitate water splitting, many heterogeneous catalysts based on specifically on semiconductor materials that can absorb solar energy are extensively applied successfully as photocatalysts and still being studied as the main technology for hydrogen production via solar water splitting process.
To overcome above-mentioned problems for hydrogen production, metal nanoparticles especially electron rich Ni or Pd nanoparticles decorated on semiconductor 2D nanosheets heterostructure is proposed. Low bandgap semiconductor transition metal oxide/ sulphides nanosheets such as WO3, MoO3, WS2, MoS2 acts as a photosensitizer for the photocatalytic process under visible light and decorated metal nanoparticles (Ni, Pd) having the tendency to donate single electrons. Such hybrid material forms a metal/semiconductor heterojunction that enables to reduce the recombination process and make it more photostable as compared with the let alone nanosheets or nanoparticles. Hence, a heterogeneous catalyst system is proposed consisting of transition metal oxide/ sulphide nanosheets decorated with metal nanoparticles of Ni or Pd active for both photo and electrocatalytic water splitting

data.projectName: Assessment of pharmaceutical compounds production in medicinal plant (Swertia chirita) in response to soil salt stress
data.projectDigest: Pharmaceutical compounds are generally extracted from medicinal plants. Enhancing pharmaceutical compounds in medicinal plants would be a great contribution for pharmaceutical industries and economic return to the farming community. Most of the medicinal plants are naturally grown, but still are not domesticated. Keeping the importance of these plants, its need to grow medicinal plants on salt stressed areas (6.3 M ha in Pakistan) to get economic return from these salt stressed barren lands. Strategies are being devised for stimulation of pharmaceutical compounds production in medicinal plants. Imposing abiotic stress on medicinal plants may increase the production of pharmaceutical compounds through changing physiology. Choraita (Swertia chirita) is a local medicinal plant, which is naturally grown in agricultural fields throughout the country. To investigate the production/enhancement of pharmaceutical compounds in response to soil salinity, this plant will be grown in salt-affected soils with different levels in combinations of drought stress, application of plant hormones, silicon, biochar and/or fertilizers. Treatment induced changes such as pH, electrical conductivity, sodium (Na), silicon (Si), etc, and plant growth and biochemical traits including chlorophyll, electrolyte leakage, antioxidant enzymes, and particularly pharmaceutical compounds will be studied.

data.projectName: Insight into Biofloc: A step forward towards sustainable fish production in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Government Sadiq College Women University, Bahawalpur
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan, like many other countries natural resources especially water is declining day by day. Therefore, there is a dire need of finding some sustainable methods to use these scarce natural resources. Biofloc is an innovative method which is about creating a balance between carbon and nitrogen in aquatic system. Furthermore, this technology as also capable of producing protein rich diet for fish. Although this technology is still at its early stages, yet it offers promising results in future of fisheries and aquaculture. In this project we aim to further explore this technology to test different beneficial micro-organisms to enhance the quality of biofloc. We will be looking at development of new monitoring techniques to obtain better composition and characteristics of biofloc and optimization of nutritional quality of produced biofloc to meet the dietary requirements of aquatic animals. Accomplishing these goals will enhance our use of water and land resources and will improve the composition of biofloc. Furthermore, by optimizing the fish diet with additional diet, we will be able to obtain a more healthy and vigorous fish culture. In conclusion this project will enhance our fish production while minimizing our use of land and water resources.

data.projectName: 36 Months
data.projectDigest: This project is proposed for the estimation of the depth and size of the arbitrarily shaped object buried below a rough interface. This problem is very important research area in view of ground-penetrating radar (GPR) which is used for the identification of the buried objects.  The working rule is that it sends an ultra-wide band pulse with a transmitter antenna and receives the backscattered signal at the receiver. The received signal can be utilized to image, locate, and quantitatively identify changes in electrical and magnetic properties in the ground.  The civilian applications are detection of pipes, conduits, and cables etc. It can provide a good survey of the road cracks. Recently, breast cancer diagnostic through pulsed microwave radar was proposed.  The military applications are the identification of the mines and unexploded devices.

data.projectName: Improvement of Local Cotton with ABA Responsive Genes to meet the Environmental Challenges under Drought Stress
data.projectDigest: The global environmental challenges are affecting the crop production in terms of yield and quality. The global warming is increasing the environmental temperature and creating the water scarcity. This is ultimately reducing the availability of irrigation water to the crops. The Abscisic acid (ABA) has the potential role in the plants to mitigate the stressful conditions as it is known as the Dormant Growth Hormone. Agave sisalana is known for its Crassulacean Acid Metabolism (CAM) and grown under extreme environmental conditions. Plant genomics/Plant biotechnology is the ultimate solution to improve the crop production sector to meet the changing environmental challenges. Cotton is our commercial crop and its production is reducing due to a number of environmental threats including drought. So there is need to improve the cotton crop. The project is designed to isolate, clone and characterize the abscisic acid (ABA) responsive transcripts/genes identified from Agave sisalana and their role in drought stress tolerance in cotton. ABA is called a stress hormone which enables the plants to cope with different abiotic stresses via increased ABA biosynthesis. The ABA binds to its receptor to initiate signal transduction and render abiotic stress resistance in plants. 14 differentially expressed ABA responsive transcripts are identified from drought stress leaves of Agave sisalana. These newly identified transcripts are needed to isolate and clone to determine their role in the drought stress tolerance in transgenic cotton plants. Hence, the said project will not only add the gene pool for abiotic stress resistance but will also produce the drought tolerant transgenic cotton plants utilizing the less irrigation water.

data.projectName: Assessing Time management Behviour of Departmental Heads in Public Sector Universities of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
data.piUniversity: University of Malakand, Chakdara, Dir, Malakand
data.projectDigest: Higher education institutions plays vital role in the socio-economic development of the country. Universities are the nurseries where future leaders are nurtured with knowledge, skills and competencies to lead the world. Moreover, students are equipped with personal, social, and technical skills to compete in the global market. In this regard, departmental head’s role in producing responsive, competitive, and innovative market oriented workforce cannot be neglected. To fit for this purpose, departmental heads have to develop efficient and effective skills to manage the scarcest resource of time for the achievement of organizational goals. Proper planning, setting realistic goals, prioritizing tasks, managing meetings, handling interruptions and establishing priorities are behaviour, skills and strategies through which one can use his time efficiently and purposely. To sharpen departmental heads skills and adopting appropriate work management style, they need to adopt such kind of behaviour through which they may be able to use their time productively and contribute to the organization goals.  The main objectives of the study are to assess the time management behaviour of departmental heads and the problems which they face in managing their personal and academic time and how these problems can be resolved according to recommended time management framework to achieve the organizational goals.  A sample of (200) departmental heads with (20) departmental heads from each sampled university through using stratified sampling technique will be selected. Through self constructed questionnaire perceptions of departmental heads will be captured. Through descriptive and inferential statistics collected data will be analyzed by using descriptive and inferential statistics.

data.projectName: Do Malaria Merozoites Directly Disrupt the integrity of Blood Brain Barrier?
data.projectDigest: Cerebral malaria (CM) which constitutes of 21% of all malaria Pakistani cases, is the most severe form of malarial infections and it results in 20% mortality and 25% long-term neurological deficits among patients. Its intra-human life cycle is well described, however the pathogenesis is still not completely understood. P. falciparum infected RBCs, platelets and endothelial cells have been seen in characteristic blockade of micro-vessels in the brains of patients who died of CM. However, the individual role of P. falciparum merozoites, RBCs and platelets in the disruption of gap junctions of the endothelial cells, one of the constituents of blood-brain-barrier (BBB), remains to be investigated. This study is designed to study the independent role of P. falciparum merozoites, associated its requirement of RBCs and platelets, in regulating the permeability and survival of an in vitro model of BBB. Further, it will be investigating if the disruption of BBB can be prevented by preserving endothelial cell transmembrane proteins in unphosphorylated state by of protein kinase inhibitor (PKI). The successful achievement of these objectives will provide us a better understanding of the true pathogenesis of CM and would allow the development of its better treatment strategies and efficient drug targets.

data.projectName: A deep Learning Approach to emotion recognition of depression patients through speech and brain activity sensing
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Until now software has been developed for emotion recognition from speech by implementing a classifier. Further performance of learning classifiers (MLP, Nave Bayes, J48 and SMO) was evaluated with different combinations of Prosodic features (Pitch-Intensity, Pitch-Formant, Intensity-Formant and Pitch- Intensity-Formant) to classify the speech emotions and identify the strength of learning classifiers in term of classification accuracy and model building time. The speech features which are not addressed up to a high extent will be consider and evaluated using deep learning technique.
The above research direction will help to analyze the behavior of speech features on patient’s emotion based on spoken utterances which may helpful to determine the existing mental condition and severity of disease. Therefore the objective of this research is to present a novel approach towards speech emotion recognition along with brain sensing waves of depressed patients using deep neural networks.

data.projectName: Matter Accretion onto Higher-Dimensional Black Holes in massive gravity Via Well Known Fluids
data.projectDigest: In this project, we will analyze the matter accretion onto higher dimensional black holes in massive gravity. We will obtain the general form of the Hamiltonian and dynamical system for the fluid by considering the steady state flow. It is possible to obtain the analytic solution for isothermal equation of state and observe the heteroclinic flow in the presence of well-known fluids such as ultra-stiff, radiation, sub-relativistic and ultra-relativistic. A homoclinic-type accretion flow will be checked for polytropic test fluid and the behavior for the adiabatic index will be discussed. In addition, we will investigate the behavior of energy density, radial velocity and mass accretion rate onto higher dimensional black holes in the presence of above mentioned fluids.

data.projectName: MANAGEMENT OF PARTHENIUM HYSTEROPHORUS USING COMPETITIVE PLANTS IN COMBINATION WITH BIO-CONTROL IN KHYBER PAKHTUNKHWA - PAKISTAN
data.projectDigest: The natural grasslands and the cultivated fodder lands are important sources for livestock production and play major role in socio-economic welfare of rural households in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Apart from many key functions of grasslands (e.g. aesthetic value, medicinal value and reduction in soil erosion), grasslands produce palatable biomass for livestock production. Similarly, the cultivated fodder lands produce a greater proportion of fodder (nearly 60%) for livestock production. Parthenium (Parthenium hysterophorus L.) is a well established invasive weed in natural grasslands and cultivated fodder lands across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Parthenium being a vigorously growing and a strong completive weed displaces native species biodiversity of grasslands rapidly. Parthenium causes greater biomass production loss to the infested grasslands reducing livestock carrying capacity as well as causes fodder production loss in cultivated fodder lands. The proposed research project aims to explore the combined value of selected grassland species and cultivated fodder species and a bio-control agent [Zygogramma bicolorata Pallister Chrysomelidae: Coleoptera] for growth and seed set suppression of parthenium in natural grasslands and cultivated fodder lands in weed infested areas across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The individual use of selected plant species and that of the Zygogramma bicolorata have shown promise to significantly reduce growth and seed production of parthenium in countries like Australia, India, Ethiopia and South Africa. The combined use of selected plant species and Zygogramma bicolorata is expected to further reduce the growth and seed production of parthenium. data.projectName: X-Ray Structure Analysis of Carbonic Anhydrase-II In-complex with Different Inhibitors: Way Forward towards Structure Based Drug Design for Glaucoma
data.projectDigest: “To live healthy” is one of man’s deepest wishes. Therefore, discovery of drugs with fewer side effects is eagerly pursued for the treatment of different diseases. Carbonic anhydrases are zinc metalloenzymes that catalyzes an important physiological reaction, i.e. conversion of CO2 into proton and bicarbonate ions. The CA reaction is involved in many biological processes, including transport of CO2 and bicarbonate in body, respiration, CO2 homeostasis and pH, ureagenesis, bone resorption, tumor formation and electrolyte secretion. But on the other hand, it is emerged that over expression of carbonic anhydrases have role in multiple disorders, such as oedema, glaucoma, obesity, epilepsy, and osteoporosis. These diseases can be treated with CA inhibitors. About 25 clinical drugs are known to possess CA-inhibitory properties, but there are many side effects associated with them, such as weight loss, decreased libido, depression, fatigue renal calculi, etc. In order to overcome these side effects, there is an urgent need to develop new inhibitors of CA-II, and to understand their mechanism of interaction. Through a systematic study, we aimed to evaluate different compounds against CA-II, and will carry out their structural analysis. This will be accomplished by crystallizing and analyzing CA-II in-complex with different ligands though state-of-the-art X-ray crystallography.

data.projectName: Effect of Gas-phase Fluorination on Dielectric properties, Flashover, and Charge Dynamics of Epoxy Resin Nanocomposites
data.projectDigest:
As epoxy resin nanocomposites have shown much improved properties, the subject of epoxy resin modification using nano-scale fillers has become increasingly important. However, the studies about nano-composites are still immature it is necessary to adopt a systematic approach. Moreover, extensive work has been carried out from basic research to industrial applications to minimize and suppress surface charge accumulation. This work included optimizing the design of the insulating spacer profile, reducing micro protrusions on the electrode surface and electric field at the conductor gas-trip triple junction. It is still inevitable to prevent space charges from reaching the insulating spacers. Alternative approach to increase in surface conductivity of the insulating spacer, without compromising the bulk insulation properties, would allow the charges reaching the insulating surface to disperse along the surface, thus inhibiting the accumulation of surface charges. Therefore, gas-phase fluorination is often considered as an intelligent solution to prevent surface charges in GIS.
The aim of this research is to improve the surface properties of epoxy resin by surface modification method based on incorporation with nano-Al2O3 and gas-phase fluorination to obtain epoxy resin nanocomposites with improved body and surface insulation strength. Furthermore, theoretical and experimental analysis was carried out for expanding the performance optimization of epoxy resin in power system.

data.projectName: Assessment of antioxidant therapy and ketogenic diet on oxidative stress biomarkers in type 11 diabetic patients with neuropathy
data.projectDigest: There are approximately 7.1 million diabetic patients in Pakistan and it is projected to have 11.4 million diabetes and rank 10th in the world in 2030.Neuropathy is one of the common complications of type II diabetes mellitus and its after effects like foot amputation can be a big burden on the economy of an underdeveloped country. Diabetic neuropathy affects as many as 50% of diabetic patients. There is as such no proper treatment of diabetic neuropathy. Till now only the symptoms of neuropathy are treated. Our research aims to find a proper treatment for diabetic neuropathy by prescribing drugs like tab Alpha lipoic acid and Tab Superoxide dismutase which tend to decrease the production of free radicals the main cause of diabetic neuropathy. We also aim to give ketogenic diet which is a low carbohydrate high fat diet to see its beneficial effects on diabetic neuropathy.

data.projectName: Developing, Implementing and Assessing Professionalism in Undergraduate Medical, Dental and Nursing Students
data.projectDigest:
Intolerance, disrespect of other healthcare professionalism and general lack of professionalism are the way in which our healthcare providers are perceived nowadays by the public. This research focuses on developing a contextually relevant curriculum for promoting professionalism in undergraduate students of healthcare professions including medicine, dentistry and nursing.
 In phase 1 of the study, the facets of professionalism in our undergraduate population will be identified. The data gathered from qualitative research will be used to develop a contextually relevant instrument to assess professionalism. The instrument (JSMU Professionalism Inventory) will be piloted and then administered to JSMU students in the first-year of undergraduate medical, dental and nursing programs before implementing the intervention. 
Phase 2 of the study will consist of development and implementation of an intervention for promoting and reinforcing professionalism namely a curriculum to foster professionalism. At the end of the year the JSMU Professionalism Inventory will be administered to the same group of students to obtain post test scores on professionalism.  
The aim of this research is to develop and evaluate an intervention to promote professionalism in aspiring healthcare professionals with a special emphasis on tolerance, respect and acceptance of diversity, which are reportedly lacking in our healthcare professionals.

data.projectName: Development of High Performance Computing (HPC) toolkit for teaching how to build and program Heterogeneous Supercomputers

data.projectDigest: Cluster computers are gaining popularity with the advent of big data and end of Moore's Law. It is a growing economy and our nation has been importing the technology as of yet. This project aims to design and develop an HPC education toolkit. This inexpensive toolkit shall be composed of single-board computers and embedded GPUs. Apart for cluster systems integration, configuration and management, case studies of applications from scientific computing and big data shall also be designed and documented. The project aims to develop an HPC toolkit which can be assembled locally using low cost on-board computers and its parts can be printed by using 3D printer. The design of HPC-toolkit and the curriculum will be made available to all educational institutes through online portal.

data.projectName: Load side management of the electric power grid to avoid load imbalance and improved reactive power profile
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: Electrical power grids are transforming from conventional operation scenarios to modern challenges with more complicated loads, distributed generation integration and much more. It is necessary to transform our grid with the requirements of the time to cope the challenges of the modern era. Distribution system are exposed to much more complicated challenges due to integration of a large variety of loads and generation components. One of the challenges in the distribution system is imbalance loads on three phases of the system that creates problems with derating of the equipment, overheating and limiting power transfer capabilities of the system. Conventional solutions by manually shifting the single phase loads from one phase to another phase to alleviate this problem are no longer suitable to maintain the dynamic stability and reliability of the system. Moreover, low voltage profile of the weak grids have always been a source of problem for the consumers. Sophisticated equipment of the future require more stable and reliable power supply. Conventional static capacitor compensation cannot meet the dynamic requirements of the system. Power electronics based system incorporating FACTs concept is proposed in the project to modernize our distribution system according to the requirements of the future system

data.projectName: Biodegradation of Polyethylene Plastics by Fungi Isolated from Soil in Karachi, Pakistan.
data.projectDigest: The unresolved issue of increasing levels of plastic disposal, decrease in the land fill capacity and insufficient plastic degradation is contributing to significant environmental pollution. Therefore, the demand for an environmentally friendly degradation method is quite high. Polythene and plastic wastes, especially of domestic origin tend to accumulate in the environment which gives rise to a major ecological threat. The reason being, they are quite recalcitrant in nature. Different strategies have been developed and implemented so far and still more research is in progress to reduce the impact of these polymeric materials. The preference of employing microbes for the biodegradation of plastic polymers have gained notable importance. It is mainly due to the inefficiency of the chemical and physical disposal methods as they result in pollutant by-products and incur additional environmental problems. In this regard, microorganisms and their enzymes are being used in the degradation of both natural and synthetic plastics effectively without causing any harm to the environment. In addition to this, works are also being carried out on potential polymer degrading fungi such as, Fusarium spp., Aspergillus spp. and Phanerochaete spp. They have proven to be versatile organisms which are able to degrade a variety of compounds, organic contaminants and polymeric materials. In the proposed study, the biodegradation of plastic will be evaluated by exposing them to fungal species isolated from soil. The potential ability to degrade polyethylene plastics by fungal spp. will be evaluated and the data obtained will be analysed statistically.

In addition to this, works are also being carried out on potential polymer degrading fungi such as, Fusarium spp., Aspergillus spp. and Phanerochaete spp. They have proven to be versatile organisms which are able to degrade a variety of compounds, organic contaminants and polymeric materials. In the proposed study, the biodegradation of plastic will be evaluated by exposing them to fungal species isolated from soil. The potential ability to degrade polyethylene plastics by fungal spp. will be evaluated and the data obtained will be analysed statistically.

data.projectName: EVALUATING ROLE OF AGRICULTURAL EXTENSION IN REDUCING POVERTY AND IMPROVING LIVELIHOOD OF FARMING COMMUNITY IN KHYBER PAKHTUNKHWA, PAKISTAN
data.projectDigest: Despite agro-based economy, immense fertile lands, the biggest irrigation system, the highest snowcapped mountains, huge forests, lot of mineral resources and hardworking communities, the farmer of Pakistan is leading a poor and miserable life. This situation is because of under-utilization of these resources. Likewise, performance of agricultural sector is considered not up to the mark because per acre yield of crops is low as compared to many countries of the world. However, the difference in yield of crops can be reduced if the latest agricultural technologies and crop management practices are effectively communicated to the farming community and ultimately these are persuaded for adoption at field level. It is the topmost responsibility of agricultural extension workers to take on this duty and thus boost up their farm productivity in general and profitability in particular. To achieve this objective many more extension approaches have so far been applied in Pakistan but all of them seem to be either failed or got partial success due to one or the other tailback in the system. In the same way, capability of Agricultural Extension Field Staff (EFS) in dissemination of the latest agricultural technologies and crop management practices among the farming community for elevating poverty is also not determined. Therefore, the proposed study is planned to evaluate the role of agricultural extension in reducing poverty and improving livelihood of farming community in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.

data.projectName: Evaluation of milk production potential and DNA fingerprinting of Camelids (Camelus dromedarius) in Punjab
data.projectDigest: Without exaggeration the camel has been the most ignoring specie among the ruminants in Pakistan. It has been remained the victim of deliberate neglect and disregard of scientists along with development workers for a long time. There were no efforts in terms of planning and research on it to improve its productivity. Growing needs and emerging awareness about the camel has changed the notion “ship of the desert” to “a food security animal” in many arid and semi-arid areas of the world. Pakistan is not exception to this – where camel is going to take a prime position that it can meet the milk and meat demands of the pastoral community as a whole. The present study is planned to investigate the milk production potential of Marecha and Brela camel breeds of Punjab. This study definitely will contribute to build a country’s data base for indigenous genetic resource and it will pave a way for further investigations in this field which will be a useful addition to the life of pastoralists and the people of arid and semi-arid areas in Pakistan. Pastoral people, rural poor of arid and semi-arid areas, students and researchers will be the beneficiary industry as this study will generate the primary data.

data.projectName: Municipal Waste Segregation: From Mess to Order
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Development Economics (PIDE), Islamabad
data.projectDigest: This research will develop a sustainable business model for the segregation of solid waste in Pakistan. We will assess how to incentivize the households, businesses, waste collectors and Municipal authorities to play their part in the waste management through agreeing to segregate the municipal solid waste. In fact, liquid waste flow due to gravity in low-laying areas or are channelized through sewerage system whereas gases escape the surface. However, solid waste is required to be managed by action as they neither flow nor evaporate. Nevertheless, solid waste management (SWM) requires a lot of current expenditure, knowledge and stakeholder’s participation. The substances that we waste; are not actually waste for all, they could be a resource for others. Governments usually strive for the improved solid waste management practices to ensure clean environment and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. But their efforts are subject to limited knowledge about optimal waste management practices and the scaling of innovative solutions. So, the need arises for investigating the success stories as well as the impeding factors in scaling keeping in mind the institutional and cultural dynamics of our country.

data.projectName: DISTRIBUTED LEDGER TECHNOLOGY BASED IMMUTABLE AUTHENTICATED CREDENTIAL SYSTEM (D-IACS)
data.projectDigest:
Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) supported blockchain technology is fourth industrial revolution (4IR) and it is transforming the current information technology paradigm as DLT can be considered a next technological breakthrough after internet. Rapid transformation of business, governments & existing traditional systems into purely Blockchain based system has many challenges and barriers, especially in developing countries. This adoption will be gradual because of infrastructure revamping and optimization that can serve as baseline reforms for such a powerful technological advancement in information technology. 
We proposed a DLT based model and framework that supports & facilitates conventional transformation of existing systems towards 4IR based blockchain systems that can accommodate smooth communication between legacy systems with latest systems. Hence, this adds value to efforts & man hours invested for making these systems in past. 
The proposed DLT model can be integrated to any existing conventional or new IT based systems for reforming capabilities handling the immutable, transparent & secured system parameters more effectively. The concept for proposed framework development & its related use-case system application development for Proof of Concept is in alignment with UNESCO Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). This activity will also support for developing policies and implementation guidelines for the concerning SDGs transition with the Government Bodies, MoIT etc., for suitable indigenous adoption of Pakistan’s Digital Policy.

data.projectName: Detection of the heavy elements in Foods, Soils, Vegetable and bio-material using spectroscopic techniques.
data.projectDigest:
Laser induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) technique is the laser based technique that can provide qualitative and quantitative measurement of the elemental composition and its abundance in various test environments. LIBS is an new emerging technology that has been successfully applied to analysis of the elemental  composition of the solid, gas, liquid samples. The spectroscopic
characterization of such transition lines gives the whole information of the individual elements present in the sample. The line width and the intensities must then be related to the number density of atoms or ions present in the plasma and the plasma temperature.
This is promising optical technique for the detection of the heavy toxic elements in the soils and foods, biomaterial, agriculture etc. It can be used for the bacterial contamination, mineral composition analysis and depth profiling and elemental surface mapping.
In the proposed research work, our focus will be on the heavy elemental concentration in the soil sample of Sindh.
The next our focus will be  effect of these toxic elements in the
soil on the agriculture products and food products
These heavy elements causes cancer.

data.projectName: Development and improvement of direct PCR protocols for avian genetic analysis
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Avian DNA analysis is vital to a lot of governmental, social, scientific, diagnostic and business activities. It is virtually unbelievable nowadays to run a successful conservation program for birds without using DNA analysis. DNA analysis is routinely performed to determine sex and genetic makeup of birds for coherent and timely breeding. Avian DNA analysis is however impeded by economic constraints and reporting time of test results, two of factors contributing to the success of veterinary diagnostics business. Both of these impediments can be overcome by developing an avian DNA analysis platform that employs direct PCR for amplification without prior DNA extraction and purification. DNA extraction and purification contributes substantially to the cost and reporting time of genetic analysis. Nearly 150 – 500 PKR and 30 minutes to 2 days are spent to perform every DNA extraction and purification. We propose here to develop and improve direct PCR protocols for avian DNA analysis. These protocols will use crude DNA for PCR amplification, which will be extracted within 2 -10 minutes, with 5 PKR cost per test specimen. We are optimist to state that the implementation of the proposed project will end up with income generation for the institution and industry-academia linkages.

data.projectName: Skill Enhancement through Scientific Methods of Training for Garment Industry of Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
The garment manufacturing mainly depends on skill and experience human labor for the required process efficiency and product quality. It is observed that most of the garment industries induct their fresh or untrained labor direct to production floor that creates diversification in skill level (unskilled to highly skilled). This situation creates unbalanced manufacturing lines that cause defective and rejected garments. While industries have to bear high production cost and poor quality. Thus, the need to develop such Scientific Methods of Training (SMOT) is very high for the said industry. 
The project will be helpful for different labor intensive processes of garment manufacturing industries like sewing, quality inspection, and packing. SMOT will provide the comprehensive guidelines/criteria in a structured way keeping in view the requirements of garment manufacturing processes. It includes the selection of labor for the required job, training, monitoring, and evaluation before inducting them to the production floor. The outcome of this project will be the creation of new knowledge that will ensure the easy, efficient, and rapid learning of unskilled human labor. The overall impact of the research is expected to be translated into increased exports of the country.

data.projectDigest: In today’s technological age smart materials are playing a very important role, for example, the use of the piezoelectric sensors in smoke detectors Recently, some research has been conducted in which smart materials are sensors and actuator, for example, active vibration control and health monitoring of structures. In this study, it will be investigated that the PZT patch is effective in varying environments.

data.projectName: NRPU:  Human-Carnivore Conflict in District Neelum, Azad Jammu and Kashmir
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest: Neelum Valley (District Neelum) is one of the most divers and distinguished valleys in AJ&K having dry and moist temperate forests, alpine scrub and sub-alpine zone at mountains. People largely have agro-pastoral based economy so they have high subsistence on natural resources. Forests of Neelum valley provide home range to a wide variety of carnivores including brown bear, black bear, common leopard, yellow throated marten, red fox, grey wolf, stone marten and snow leopard. Fewer scientific publications have been made from Neelum but carnivore conflict is almost ignored chapter. Economic loss to the local community, their behavior toward the conservation and conflict mitigation is need of the day. Proposed study aims to investigate the distribution of carnivores, extent of conflict, economic losses, attitude of local communities to the conservation and mitigation of human carnivore conflict in Neelum valley. Questionnaire and line transect methods will be used to investigate dimensions of human-conflict nature and their conservation. Scats will be collected and analyzed in the laboratory for diet breadths of each species. Awareness to local people will be provided through seminars and posters. Finally mitigation measures will be suggested for the coexistence of both of the conflict parties.

Economic loss to the local community, their behavior toward the conservation and conflict mitigation is need of the day. Proposed study aims to investigate the distribution of carnivores, extent of conflict, economic losses, attitude of local communities to the conservation and mitigation of human carnivore conflict in Neelum valley. Questionnaire and line transect methods will be used to investigate dimensions of human-conflict nature and their conservation. Scats will be collected and analyzed in the laboratory for diet breadths of each species. Awareness to local people will be provided through seminars and posters. Finally mitigation measures will be suggested for the coexistence of both of the conflict parties.

data.projectName: Sustainable development of smart Meat Quality and Source Detector
data.projectDigest: Meat and meat products have a great significance in human nutrition and help in the maintenance of consumer health. In Pakistan, meat consumption is about 18 kg per capita and ranked 9th in beef consumption. Thus, there is a chance of adulteration due to high commercial value and ever-increasing demand & consumption. Recently, adulteration of beef products with Horse/Donkey meat has raised the issues of consumer protection, fraud detection and compliance with religious codes. Thus, there is a dire need for a reliable method for detecting Haram meat for human consumption. In this regard, various methods are being used which are based on DNA, protein structure, organoleptic and fat content. These methods have higher accuracy in the determination of meat sources and quality. However, they are time consuming and costly which limits their on-spot use for various law enforcement agencies e.g. Punjab food authority etc. To overcome this issue, an alternate approach is direly needed for rapid analysis with higher accuracy. The meat source and quality may be determined based on nitrogen and electrical resistivity. These properties vary with time, temperature, storage conditions, and source. Therefore, this project aims to develop a sensor; based on electrical resistivity and nitrogen content of different meat source to detect the adulteration.

data.projectName: Mistreatment of Women in STEM: Perceptions of Female Students and Faculty in Pakistani Higher Education Institutions
data.projectDigest:
Evidence-based discussion of mistreatment (chilly climate) is hindered, however, by the relative lack of comprehensive research studies regarding the extent and dynamics of the problem in STEM education within Pakistani HEIs. In order to develop a contextual understanding of phenomena within Pakistan (an Eastern and Muslim majority country), this research intends to: (a) document the status of women’s participation, progression and achievement in STEM disciplines in Pakistani higher education system; (b) identify the factors (social, cultural, individual, and institutional) that promote incidences of incivility and sexual harassments against female students and faculty in STEM disciplines; (c) identify institutional features that help to mitigate the “chilly climate” that contributes to mistreatment against women in STEM disciplines; and (d) identify interventions for preventing mistreatment against women in STEM education and workplaces.
On a broader level, this research can be seen as a part of UN’s endeavors to promote gender-equity through women education. This research is timely and is a direct response to UN resolutions calling its member states “to end all forms of discrimination against all women and girls everywhere”. Results of this study would help us in designing effective intervention programs for preventing mistreatment against women in STEM education and workplaces.

data.projectName: To evaluate the Impact of climate change on total factor productivity of crop and livestock sub-sectors in different ecological zones of Punjab, Pakistan.
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest:
Despite of all out efforts of government during the last decade, the performance of agriculture sector was not upto mark  on account of stagnant productivity of all major crops despite of the fact that cropped area of the major crops largely remained unchanged (GOP, 2019). 
Increasing population, narrow chances of more extension of cultivated land, bringing fertile land under residential and industrial use (Chang and Zepeda, 2001), growing resource degradation ( Murgai et al. 200) and huge gap between potential and national average yields (Government of Punjab, 2007), productivity in agriculture sector can be enhanced only by increase in total factor productivity (TFP).
Aheam et al. (1998) stated that partial factor productivity was used in the past to estimate productivity; however, due to a misleading measure of productivity, TFP measure was developed. TFP is the ratio of an index of agricultural output to an index of agricultural inputs. 
Pakistan has been ranked 16th with respect to its vulnerability to environmental change (Maplecroft, 2010). Pakistan history has witnessed the worst drought during 1997 to 2004. Therefore, the study has been designed to evaluate the Effect of climate change on TFP of crop and livestock sub-sectors in different ecological zones of Punjab.

data.projectName: Invitro and Invivo identification and Evaluation of mitochondrial injury caused by various hepatotoxic drugs
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
The drug-induced liver injury is a term used to describe liver damage due to all kinds of non-prescription and prescription drugs, including natural medicines and biological agents. DILI is classified as one of the major adverse drug reactions, whose severity leads to acute liver failure and death. In 2003, USA officially launched Drug-Induced Liver Injury Network (DILIN) and in the very next year, USA conducted first DILIN prospective research. In 2014, ACG (The American College of Gastroenterology) established a clinical protocol for the management and diagnosis of idiosyncratic DILI.This data provides clinicians an important knowledge for prescribing hepatotoxic drugs and the evaluation of their hazards and advantages. However, data about DILI incidence in the general population of Pakistan is not available because of the absence of large-scale epidemiological data.
Many drugs which are available in the market have the issue of DILI, among them the most common examples include drugs for cardiovascular system, anticancer drugs, drugs for CNS, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and drugs for the treatment of tuberculosis.
Main purpose of our study is to figure out the molecular mechanisms behind the mitochondrial injury caused by various hepatotoxic drugs (e.g. cisplatin, tamoxifen ) and protective effect by herbal product like Silybum Marianum (Silymarin)..

data.projectName: Development of a testing framework to measure bond strength in asphalt pavements
data.projectDigest:
A novel test method ‘Compression Pull-Off Test (CPOT)’ was devised by the proposer of this research as part of PhD research at the University of Nottingham, UK. The research evaluated bond strength of asphalt using principle of ‘tensile strength’. The bond strength is fundamental property to evaluate moisture damage in asphalt pavements, which is the main cause of pavement deterioration. In primary publication of this work in esteem journal ‘Construction and Building Materials’, it has been demonstrated that this method is superior to traditional and contemporary methods in technical and operational aspects.

Currently, there is need to develop a stand-alone test equipment that can be presented as a standard test method. To achieve this aim, there is need to establish a complete testing framework. The objectives include; enhancement of capability for pure adhesive bond, development of integrated environmental chamber, simplification in the design of gap assembly, development of test guidelines, evaluation of moisture and material parameters, study of self-healing properties, correlation of adhesion and flow properties of binder, and evaluation of fracture energy. 

The current resource limitation is a hindrance in the development of this work. In this proposal, a justification of the proposed work and detailed outline is presented. The work is expected to lead towards a standard test method in evaluation of moisture damage based on fundamental material property (bond strength) to understand the road performance. The work has potential for commercialization and application for evaluating bond strength of the industrial adhesives.

data.projectName: Shaping Consumer Waste Reduction Behavior Food and Plastic Waste: A Longitudinal Experimental Intervention Study
data.projectDigest: Customer waste management has become an epidemic as it represents a noteworthy proportion of solid waste management. Customer waste management has got the attention of academics, policy makers and institutes as it has ramifications for economy, environment and well-being of citizens. The way how products became waste depends upon the awareness and consumption practices of customers. There is a lack of consumer awareness towards customer waste management. Among the most promising opportunities to tackle customer waste are the awareness campaigns towards waste reduction. The aim of the project is to develop and conduct awareness camping for consumer waste reduction that is food waste and plastic waste through product packaging. This research project will used a mixed method research approach sequentially from qualitative design to quantitative design. At qualitative part awareness campaign will be designed and a number of training sessions will be conducted for university students and household. At quantitative part change in awareness level and behavioral intentions will be by using the longitudinal data in three time lags. The project will be helpful to guide customers at individual as well as community level to contribute in waste reduction that is linked with economic and social aspects of Pakistan.
