data.projectName: Improved biogas and biofertilizer production through microaerobic pretreatment and anaerobic co-digestion of agro-industrial wastes
data.projectDigest: Anaerobic digestion (AD) of organic wastes offers advantage of simultaneous treatment and energy production (biogas) from organic wastes. The slurry produced at the end of AD can be used as biofertilizer for crop production. Recently the biogas development initiatives have gained renewed interest in Pakistan due to shortfall of energy generation from conventional energy sources particularly in the rural areas. Primarily the substrate used for biogas production in Pakistan is cattle manure. However, the inability of anaerobic bacteria to efficiently degrade lignin in the manure hampers the biogas production. Nevertheless, a suitable pretreatment to degrade lignin and use of co-substrates with cattle manure during AD to balance the nutrients  can improve both the biogas and biofertilizer production. Therefore, the primary objective of the current research is to determine potential of microaerobic pretreatment to degrade lignin and subsequently establish the empirical potential of agro-industrial co-substrates for AD of animal manure both at laboratory and pilot scale. Availability of such data will help in establishing the biomethane potential of locally available organic substrates, improve the performance of currently operational biogas plants, and develop guidelines for future biogas development initiatives in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Heterogeneously Catalyzed Aqueous Phase Reforming of Biomass to Obtain Bio-fuels and -chemicals Based on Model Catalysts Systems
data.projectDigest: Plant biomass is the only foreseeable source of sustainable fuels and chemicals. The proposed research project is related to the efficient utilization of biomass derived oxygenates for the production of biofuels by aqueous phase reforming. Heterogeneously catalyzed aqueous phase reforming (APR) is a potential technique to produce lighter alkanes and hydrogen from biomass derived oxygenates. This reaction is highly dependent on surface properties of support material in term of selectivity, activity, stability and feasibility of operating APR reaction. Therefore, this technique is only beneficial when used with suitable catalyst and support material. Metal oxide catalyst supports materials are usually unstable under higher temperature and pressure conditions of aqueous phase reforming. Hence, the support material with stable characteristics under higher temperature and pressure conditions along with high surface area is desired for the reforming reaction to proceed. Carbide-derived carbon (CDC) is a new class of materials featuring tunable pore size distributions in the sub-nanometer range, high specific surface area, large pore volume, highly reproducible in its properties and good mechanical stability which makes them an interesting support material in the field of catalysis. Thus, in this proposed research project, novel CDC based catalysts will be used for APR reaction to develop an optimized catalytic solution for the conversion of biomass to bio-fuels and -chemicals. Kohinoor Spinning Mills Limited, the industrial stakeholder has self-generation power plant to fulfill the energy requirements. The enterprise agreed for mutual co-operate to ascertain the commercial viability and environmental impact of the proposed research project.

data.projectName: Disaster Risk-Based Decision-Making Tool for Interdependent Regional Workforce Systems
data.projectDigest:
Natural disasters, such as pandemics, can cause mortality and morbidity in the population in an economic region. Workforce disruptions in a pandemic (dengue) can adversely impact regional economic productivity as workforce contributes significantly in the production of commodities. In addition, the recovery of the region is further slowed down by the interconnectedness among economic sectors leading to direct and indirect economic losses. 
This research proposal extends the dynamic input-output model to formulate a disaster recovery model to estimate the economic losses caused specifically by workforce disruptions in a pandemic calamity. The uncertainty involved in workforce disruptions is linked to dengue attack rate inducing a statistical dependence relationship between the epidemic (dengue) attack and the recovery period of industry sectors.
A decision-making tool is developed based on the Bayesian expert judgment technique to incorporate the responses of the subject matter expert (i.e., doctors) for risk informed decision making. This research attempts to integrate statistical dependence relationship with a pandemic (dengue) and workforce recovery in dynamic Input-Output modeling. Indeed, prioritization will help in efficient resource allocation to expedite recovery process. The research also performs risk analysis and develops a risk-based framework, which aids in managing dengue epidemics impacts on workforce economic systems.

data.projectName: Potential Application of Fabricated Green Hybrid Polymeric Layered Double Hydroxides For Polluted Water Purification: Multiple Approach
data.projectDigest: Water is the most plentiful natural resource, merely 1% of which is available for human consumption. Several natural, organic and inorganic components are added into water due to uncontrolled growth of population, prompt rise in industrialization, exploitation of resources of water due to which water quality is being deteriorated constantly making water polluted. Industrial wastewater, a chief cause of water pollution, comprises micro pollutants. These pollutants are lethally poisonous and carcinogenic that result severe toxicities like mutagenicity, allergies, cancer, dermatitis and skin irritations showing serious symptoms, not only dangerous to human beings but for ground water and earth ecosystem too. Therefore this polluted water must be treated to prevent its environmental threats. Already used technologies and different adsorbents or catalysts have constraints like lower efficiency, sensitive environment for working, requirement of high energy, incomplete removal of pollutants, greater cost and complexity along with generation of toxic sludge leading to secondary pollution making them unsuitable for use. Therefore use of Green Hybrid Polymeric Layered Double Hydroxides materials is a cost effective, sustainable and eco friendly technique to solve the issue of water pollution due to their bifunctional property of adsorption and photo catalysis (under visible light).

data.projectName: Precision Agriculture System for Distributed Fertigation with Robotic Seeding and Weeding
data.projectDigest:
A fully automated robotic crop husbandry system is proposed, providing significant conservation of water, seeds, fertilizers and pesticides as well as improved energy efficiency. A mobile robot will sow the seeds autonomously and also kill the weeds as well.  Additionally, the system will have a network of sensors and sprinklers to fertigate the land according to the specific needs of the hour and crop. This will greatly help the farmers of small to medium landholdings to maximize their yields, efficiently grow high-income crops and become more competitive. 

Once developed, this system will greatly help the farmers to efficiently perform crop-husbandry and automatically distribute the required fertilizer/irrigation recipes in a variety of different settings. Our sectoral collaborator is Famers Association of Pakistan which will help us ensure better adoption of this technology.

data.projectName: Fabrication of Nanoscale Spintronic data storage devices
data.projectDigest:
Researchers are continuously working to design Spintronic devices to achieve spin polarized transport by applying different approaches. The GMR technology can be improved either by exploring new and advanced materials or by optimizing the existing spin filtering device capabilities. Moreover, particular methodologies are being explored to generate and utilize spin-polarized currents in novel and efficient ways. Metal-based Spintronic technology has already progressed and has been utilized in hard disk drive read heads and in non-volatile type solid state memories. Furthermore, Spintronic device applications demands handling and manipulation of spin within the semiconductor because metal lacks current control. Therefore, realization of spin polarized transport mechanism in semiconductors makes it possible to have efficient spin valves. Although metal-based devices have very successful applications in switches or valves, yet, these devices do not amplify signals. Instead, the semiconductor based Spintronic devices show large amplification and can be used for multi-functional devices that may further multiply the worth of the microelectronic industry.

•	The metal based Spintronic devices do not amplify signals.
•	The same functionality can be achieved by Semiconductors based Spintronics. 
•	Semiconductors based Spintronic material provide amplification and serve as a multifunctional device

data.projectName: Co-composting of Wet Fractions of Municipal  Solid Waste and Yard Waste at the Universities of Jamshoro Sindh, Pakistan.
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
The key objective of the overall project is to manage bio-waste including wet fractions of municipal solid waste (MSW) and yard waste (YW) for the production of compost by co-composting. The project will build the local capacity in order to identify and implement environment friendly technology for bio-waste recycling and assess their potential for resource conservation, greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction and their feasibility with regard to local environment as well as socio-economic characteristics. 
The project will be completed in three years. The quantification as well as characterization of bio-waste, assessment of its management system and co-composting of wet fractions of MSW and YW will be covered in three years. In the starting, the samples of MSW will be collected and analyzed in order to examine baseline information of MSW and YW. Then, the fabrication as well as design of compost reactor (three type of reactors at different operating conditions) and co-composting of wet fractions of MSW YW will be performed. Finally, the post treatment including curing of compost product will be carried out and data will be compiled. This project would be helpful for universities to convert solid wastes into compost product.

data.projectName: Addressing health issues of transgender community through Social Support and Advocacy in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Transgender people in Pakistan are mostly deprived of their basic rights including right to job, education, health, property and justice. Cultural value system (particularly taboos) deters social acceptance, health rehabilitation and overall mainstreaming of this community which ultimately have turned them into a fragile, vulnerable and sick segment of the society (Abdullah, et al. 2012; Ahmed, et al.2014; Khan, 2016; Asghar & Shahzad, 2018). Almost 36,000 HIV positive transgender have been identified in the Punjab province of Pakistan. In this background, the present project aimed to 1) identify the various factors affecting the health status of transgender people in different cities of Pakistan including Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Lahore, Faisalabad and Multan 2) to sensitize, engage and involve transgender community for uplift their health status with the collaboration of  relevant stakeholders through conduction of workshops, seminars, and media campaign, and 3) safeguard health rights of transgender people by building liaison with health department, NGOs and other relevant stakeholders. A sample of 500 transgender people would be selected from the above mentioned cities by using the principle of equal proportion allocation, meaning by that 100 respondents will be selected from each city. Both qualitative and quantitative research methods will be used to gather information from the respondents. Consequently, the findings of the current project will be presented to the relevant governmental and nongovernmental organizations as guidelines for policy formulizations to ensure betterment in health services for transgender people in Pakistan.

data.projectName: :  Integrative Management Approach (IMA) for the remediation of heavy metals and pesticides polluted soil for better productivity and quality of Wheat
data.projectDigest: Contaminants including heavy metals and pesticides are accumulated in soil due to the anthropogenic inputs. This proposed work is planned, to investigate the proposed Integrated Management Approach (IMA) that could remediate toxic pollutants and work as a soil conditioner in the crop rotational system of Pakistan. Intercropping is a crop management system that has potential to increase utilization of soil resources efficiently. The literature study revealed that mixing of wheat with Brassica has shown no adverse effects on the grain yield of wheat by gaining maximum pecuniary benefits. Intercropping system of cereals with legumes is being practiced in some areas of Pakistan specially in winter crops. The use of brassica as an intercrop has phytoremediation abilities to remediate heavy metals and pesticides from soil. In addition, the Earthworms has a potential to convert the non-available fractions of heavy metals & pesticides and increases pollutant’s mobility and bioavailability and also play vital role in these toxins remediation. The use of straw residues mulching can have a supportive role for the main crop plants for nutrient availability and food source for earthworms, even breakdown toxic chemicals, mulching is good for moisture conservation for highest earthworm activity. Moreover, straw mulching in fields has significant role for the improvement of overall soil health and weed suppression.

data.projectName: Detection of putative virulence associated genes and their phenotypic expression among the clinical isolates of Acinetobacter baumannii
data.projectDigest: Acinetobacter baumannii are gram negative bacteria which cause infection predominantly in immune compromised patients and have emerged as one of the leading causes of nosocomial infections. The organism exhibits high genetic variability due to acquisition of mobile genetic elements from closely related pathogenic organism and various geographical clones have been identified. In recent years the multidrug resistance profile of this organism has been studied extensively, however, very little is known about the virulence characteristics of this notorious pathogen particular regarding strains circulating in our region. The main objectives of this study are to focus on the virulence related genotypic factors and their phenotypic manifestation among the clinically isolated strains of A. baumannii. Earlier Acinetobacter baumannii was considered as a normal colonizer and its definitive role in disease process is still under investigation. Most of the diagnostic labs in our region still do not report this organism in clinical specimens and is often disregarded as a commensal. The project will contribute to our understanding of the role of A. baumannii in disease and highlight significance in nosocomial infections. A virulence profile of the indigenous isolates will also be generated. The clinicians as well as the patients will benefit from the findings of this study.

data.projectName: Monitoring of Ambient Noise levels and its epidemiological impacts in Lahore
data.projectDigest: Environmental noise is increasingly becoming a community concern internationally. Sound becomes undesirable when it disturbs the activities such as working, sleeping and during conversations. It is a severe environmental problem because of the fact that we can’t see, smell or taste it. The urban environmental quality of developing countries has been deteriorated by an unlimited increase of vehicles, infrastructure and population. Besides with the growing level of air and water pollution, road traffic, noise pollution has been recognized rising as a new threat to the inhabitants of cities. The aim of this study is to determine the impacts of noise pollution generated in all zones of Lahore. The study will be carried out by comparing the NEQs and standards of Punjab Environmental Act 1997. The sound level meter of EXTECH with complex specifications will be used for precise results to carry out this study.

data.projectName: Preparation of skin substitute (Acellular dermal matrix) for acid victims and for burn patients
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Medical University, Islamabad
data.projectDigest:
We will prepare Acellular dermal matrix from human and bovine skin which is a biological skin substitute, locally. It is the best treatment available for deep burns and wounds. It is available in market but at a very high cost because it is being prepared in some developed countries only. We will make sure that this product is safe to use in terms of disease transmission(viral & bacterial) and without the risk of immune rejection by the host .To achieve these goals ,different procedures like proper de-epidermization, decellularization of dermis, tutoplast procedure, vacuum pressure and ultra violet rays irradiations will be done. The product will be applied first on rat models and after getting satisfactory results its application in deep wounds and 3rd degree burns in humans will be carried out.
In short, because of readily availability and cost effectiveness of this product, it will be a major breakthrough in the treatment of patients with 3rd degree burns and deep wounds.

data.projectName: Exploiting the impact of growth promoters in Bt cotton (Gossypium hirsutum L.) for ameliorating the adverse effects of heat and drought complex under controlled and field conditions
data.projectDigest: Severe heat spells along with water shortage create heat and drought complex which cause fruit shedding and yield reduction in cotton crop. It is essential to study underlying mechanisms of heat and drought, select tolerant varieties and induce heat and drought tolerance in cotton through management practices. Various experiments will be performed to mitigate the adverse effects of these hazards using ascorbic acid and foliar sprays of selenium (Se). Two separate experiments under field and glasshouse conditions will be conducted during the first year to determine tolerance of 10 cotton genotypes for terminal heat and drought stress. During 2nd and 3rd year experiments, heat and drought tolerant and susceptible cultivars selected from first year experiments will be exposed to heat alone, drought alone and to combination of both under field and glasshouse conditions. The study will help in quantification of yield loss in cotton due to drought and heat stress. Comprehensive information on the thermo and drought tolerance in cotton cultivars will be made available to farmers, research institutions and academia at the end of the project. This information will also help stakeholders to adapt to changing climate which is characterized by drought and heat stress.

data.projectDigest:
Cancer is one of the most lethal and painful disease in the world. About 9.6 million people died from cancer globally in 2018. About 70% of deaths occur in low and middle income countries. The currently used anticancer drugs suffer from some serious limitations of high cost, high toxicity and prolonged treatment. So it is highly needed to develop new drug which is easily accessible on low cost, biologically safe and more efficacious. 
Guanidines are biochemically and pharmacologically very active compounds having anticancer, anti-leishmanial, antidiabetic and antimicrobial activities.
The complexes of platinum such as cisplatin, oxaliplatin and carboplatin are clinically used in chemotherapy of cancer. The complexes of palladium also possess excellent anticancer properties. But both of these metals are not part of biological systems and their accumulation in body causes serious secondary problems such as neurotoxicity, leucopenia and nephrotoxicity. Some transition metals are essential elements for biological systems and play a pivotal role in metabolism. For instance, azurin is a copper containing bio-molecule and acts as electron transfer protein. The copper also acts as cofactor in several enzymes (generally called as cuproenzymes) which are involved in a number of metabolic reactions. Usually the incorporation of metal in the organic drugs enhances their activity exponentially. Cobalt is also important trace metal in body and is part of many enzymes. Its synthetic complexes can interact with DNA and hence are active anticancer agents. Cobalmine is Co containing natural product in body and its various forms are needed for the synthesis and regulation of DNA, normal function of nerves and RBCs production. Complexes containing Co(II) are less toxic as compared to Pt an

data.projectName: Formulation Development and Evaluation of Docetaxel Nanotheranostics: A Promising Approach for Targeted Drug Delivery in Breast Cancer Treatment
data.projectDigest:
For the current National Research Program for Universities (NRPU) of HEC, Pakistan, my research objective is to develop targeted drug delivery for breast cancer treatment that will enhance safety and therapeutic efficacy of anticancer drug. The non-selective toxicity, narrow therapeutic index and the high interstitial fluid pressure (IFP) of solid tumors results in poor biodistribution and penetration of drugs. The nanotechnology in drug delivery, encapsulating drugs into nanocarriers, provide promising solution of all such problems in chemotherapy by enhancing half-life, minimizing adverse effects, modifying pharmacokinetic profile and increasing therapeutic efficacy. For this purpose, peptide conjugated nanoliposomes (nanotheranostics) loaded with docetaxel will be prepared in order to release drug to its target site that is most important in the case of cancer chemotherapy. Breast cancer is the leading cause of cancer death in women worldwide, and Pakistan as well. So this of great importance and is the need of the time to develop a targeted drug delivery system of a chemotherapeutic agent to minimize harm to the normal body tissues and maximize the therapeutic efficacy of treatment.
I am fully committed and enthusiastic to execute and successfully accomplish this project and I am sure this project will be awarded.

Reinforced Concrete Structures generally suffer from durability issues over their design life. The most significant factor contributing towards deterioration of RC structures is the corrosion in steel reinforcement. Due to exposure to moisture or aggressive environment, and cracking in concrete, steel reinforcement gets corroded easily and causes internal expansion in concrete thereby resulting in damage and deterioration. There have been many alternative materials used to replace ordinary steel reinforcement in concrete. Glass fibre reinforced polymer (GFRP) bars are relatively new form of reinforcement in RC concrete with superior durability performance and low weight. There has been significant research in the developed word on the use of GFRP rebars in concrete and design guidelines have been developed. However, in developing countries and Pakistan, the use and availability of GFRP rebars is very limited. 
With some basic research done at NED University of Engineering & Technology, a local company (first in the country) has recently started producing GFRP rebars for the local industry. There has been a basic study on the use of these bars as reinforcement in concrete, however, detailed investigations are required to study the behaviour of reinforced concrete members under axial, flexural and shear loads. The present study will focus on experimental and analytical study of GFRP reinforced primary structural concrete members (beams, columns and slabs) and will develop design guidelines for use of GFRP rebars in the local industry.

data.projectName: Micro-RNA expression in glioma, glioma stem cells and serum and its association with the prognosis of the disease. A cohort study
data.projectDigest: Glioma is the most common and most lethal malignancy of the brain. It accounts for 45.2% of all brain tumors. This malignancy results from genetic aberration and deregulation of signaling pathways. Despite current treatment strategies involving surgery, chemotherapy and, radiotherapy there is a poor mean patient survival rate of 15 months. Glioma are driven and maintained by a subpopulation of clonogenic cells called Glioma Initiating Cells (GICs) which seem to play a crucial role in the tumor’s biological behavior. GICs display a malignant phenotype, ability of self-renewal, altered genomic stability and specific epigenetic signature. MicroRNAs are found to be involved in the regulation of proliferation and self-renewal of the GICs where they promote differentiation to determine the fate of stem cells. The role of MircoRNA expression has been extensively studied in gliomas in order to use them as early non-invasive diagnostic markers because of their ability to present in different body fluids after being secreted from the producing cells. We will investigate the expression of a group of mi-RNA in glioma samples, and serum samples of the same patient to identify target/s, which are aberrantly expressed in both, and have the potential of an early diagnostic biomarker for glioma diagnosis.

data.projectName: Electrophoretically Deposited Graphene Films for Corrosion Protection, Electrochemical Capacitor and Desalination Applications
data.projectDigest:
Nanotechnology is advancing rapidly to meet more demanding needs of mankind. Extensive research is carried out on one of the promising nanomaterial “graphene” due to its excellent conductivity and superior mechanical properties. 
Main goal of any applied research is to produce superior performing end-products and yield scientific advancements in basic necessity fields like, good health, clean energy and industrial innovation. These are the major sustainable development goals of United Nations which will be addressed in the present study.
Graphene have provided a freedom for scientific technological advancements in applications of automobile, aerospace and building infrastructure. In this context our proposed work “Electrophoretically Deposited Graphene Films for Corrosion Protection, Electrochemical Capacitor and Desalination Applications”  will help in to further strengthen the for local needs. 
First aim of the work is synthesize graphene economically and locally using Pakistani raw materials (graphite/coal). 
Second aim of work is to produce graphene films by using EPD technique and to characterize their performance of anticorrosion in metals, supercapacitors and water desalination. The use of EPD technique will limit the need of high temperatures to produce graphene films, need of sophisticated apparatus, and the needs of different technologies for each mentioned application.
Overall, the proposed work will help society to deliver clean water and production of cheap high performance supercapacitors locally to be used in the applied electric systems like electric cars, bikes etc. Proposed work will also help the host institute to modify the curriculum in the light of obtained outcomes to address the needs of the local society and industry.

data.projectName: Conservation of renewable feedstocks of Pakistan into eco-innovative nanocosmetics towards a circular economy
data.piUniversity: Abbottabad University of Science & Technology (AUST), Abbottabad
data.projectDigest: A feedstock is unprocessed raw material source for feeding a manufacturing process in industries. The continuous rise of feedstocks identified in the form of fish biowaste, chick eggshells and micro-algae in Pakistan, are the big mine of natural collagen, hyaluronic acid, DNA repair enzyme and ROS inhibiting compounds as renewable and sustainable. The objective of this project is to reuse these valuable renewable resources of Pakistan for conservation efficiently by converting into eco-innovative nanocosmetics to increase the aid in growth of cosmetic industry towards circular economy. In this research project, main feedstocks of Pakistan, that is, fish biowaste, chick eggshells and micro-algae will be processed and formulated to eco-innovative cosmetic formulations using nano technology. Formulations will undergo in-vitro, ex-vivo and in-vivo studies with the guidelines of Helsinki Declaration, Good Clinical Practice and Institutional Biosafety Committee. Quality control tests will be performed. Informed consent will be taken by the volunteers to start the in-vivo study. Then, skin investigation will be quantified by non-invasive bioengineering techniques after checking their the safety. Statistical analysis will be applied. Excellent results are expected after completion of this research project and could be disseminated to pursue national needs.

data.projectName: Generalized  Neutrosophic Convex Optimization Models
data.projectDigest: Optimization principles are of undisputed importance in modern design, network communication, management, data analysis, decision making and system operations. The development and availability of high speed computer with which large scale data can be solved with the exactness that previously was unapproachable is a governing factor in the establishment and enhancement of optimization techniques. In optimization a problem can be modeled by defining objective functions subject to certain set of constraints and a set of decision variables. There are several sub fields of optimization based on the nature of optimization problem that needs to be modeled. Convex optimization is one of an important subfield of optimization with a special character that all objective functions constraints and set of decision variables is convex.  The uncertainty and imprecision in real-world data can be handled by introducing fuzzy goal, fuzzy coefficients and fuzzy constraints in a fuzzy optimization problem. This laid the foundation of fuzzy optimization models. Neutrosophic set is a generalization of fuzzy set, in which each element has separate value for truth, falsity and indeterminacy. In the proposed project we will construct neutrosophic convex optimization models to deal with uncertainty and imprecision more accurately.

data.projectName: Development of Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) Hazards Maps for China Pakistan Economic Corridor
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: The glacial lakes in the Upper Indus Basin (UIB), which formed as a consequence of climate change, are potential sources of hazards to the people and infrastructure. Several projects of China-Pakistan-Economic-Corridor (CPEC) are under construction in UIB. For the safety of those projects, it is very important to identify the potentially dangerous lakes and their potential hazards of Glacial-Lake-Outburst-Floods (GLOFs). Therefore, this project is designed to analyze the variations in climate and their influences on glacial lakes, identification of potentially dangerous lakes and level of hazard severity of GLOFs on communities and infrastructure of CPEC. The climatic data of in situ gauges in conjunction with grid-based model, reanalysis and satellite products will be utilized to comprehend the local climatic variations. Digital Elevation Model (DEM) will be used to delimitate the outlines of glacial lakes, their areas, distance glacier to lake distance, slopes of downstream gullies and areas of upstream glaciers. Hazards of GLOFs will be appraised by considering local climatic conditions, scale of impoundments and slope of downstream gullies. Finally, degree GLOFs hazards will be assessed by HEC ? RAS 5.0.7 model. Outcomes of this project will be helpful to prevent human and infrastructure losses from GLOFs in the CPEC.

data.projectName: Molecular Dissemination of metallo???lactamases producers Acinetobacter baumannii in Region Swabi
data.projectDigest: Recently in field of medical sciences a lot of attention has been paid to gram negative species called as Acinetobacter baumanii which is identified as human pathogen and have remarkable potential to have inherent and acquire resistance very quickly against antibiotics. The genera is considered to be highly diverse and associated with hospital acquired infections. The basic aim of this research is to investigate the clinical burden of Acinetobacter baumannii and determine molecular epidemiology of selective resistant genes among isolated species in district Swabi. This aim will be achieved through designed objectives. Objective 1: Isolation and screening of clinical isolates of Acinetobacter baumannii.Objective2; Molecular identification of Acinetobacter baumannii using 16S rRNA markers. Objective3; Antibiotic susceptibility pattern and Minimal inhibitory concentration determination. Objective4; Determination of selective resistant genes using molecular markers. The outcomes of this project will provide important learning opportunities for students in project about antibiotic resistance and virulence in species. The project will help in expending knowledge related to antibiotic resistance virulence variation among species of Acinetobacter baumannii, particularly epidemiological status of Acinetobacter baumannii in district swabi. Our project will provide data on antibiotic resistance and highly prevalent genes in the region of swabi so that the resistance and prevalence can be monitored accordingly.

data.projectName: Development of structure based peptide inhibitor against Pakistani strains dengue virus and its administration to Mouse model.
data.projectDigest: Dengue infection is the most important infection caused by mosquito borne dengue viruses (DENV1-4). Dengue infection has emerged with highest increase rate among other infections globally. Over 390 million people become infected in 100 countries reporting 12000 deaths per year. In Pakistan DENV-1, DENV-2 is reported and it takes live of more than 400 to 500.  Infections caused by dengue virus are symptomatic. Around the world, four strains of this virus (DENV1-4) are found in tropical and subtropical areas. In Pakistan DENV-1 and DENV-2 are reported. At present no vaccine is available around the world for any type of these strains. Dengue virus genome replicates through a single open chain reading frame molecule the polyprotein. The polyprotein are processed by two multifunctional Proteases NS3 and NS5 which are essential for the life cycle of virus. NS3 protease, a multifunctional enzyme possesses protease, RTPase/NTPase and RNA helicase activities.NS2B, an integral membrane protein essentially required to NS3 protease to function. Non-structural protease NS3pro activity greatly depends on the presence of cofactor domain of NS2B. Blocking the function of the NS2B-NS3 complex or blocking NS2B-NS3 complex formation will lead to cessation of replication of DENV. A peptide inhibitor or antiviral agent against NS2B will be developed which will be test on the mouse model for its efficacy

data.projectName: Designing  and Integration of Wearable Antenna with Wireless Health Management System
data.projectDigest:
In Pakistan, several hundred thousand people are in hospital beds at any given time. As part of medical procedures, patient’s vitals and other medical parameters are to be monitored round the clock. An alarmingly high patient-to-doctor ratio and lack of nursing staff makes this monitoring very difficult.
Remote monitoring of patients using wireless monitoring system can solve this problem. Such systems can be developed for monitoring of vital parameters of the patient like heartbeat, blood pressure, temperature, sugar level etc. The monitored parameters can be further viewed by medical staff at some central/remote location. The telemedicine and remote health facility can be provided to inaccessible and sparsely populated areas with the help of wireless system. 
For any wireless system, antenna is the main device responsible for radiating the signals/data. The wireless mechanisms including antenna and electronic hardware are to be applied adjacent to human body. The wearable systems is to enhance the quality of life by integrating textiles and electronics. In relation with ISM (Industrial, Scientific and Medical) band 2.4 GHz frequency is crowded for simultaneous communication of internet of things (IoT) devices. ISM band at 5.8 GHz can be a good choice to develop a small size with less proximity antenna to communicate. The antenna can become scalable, cost effective and wearable by integrating textile material as a substrate for 5.8 GHz band.   In this work, we will present the basic characteristics of wearable antenna that defines its working capability and performance measures, design of geometrical structure, material selection, parametric analysis, designing  in simulation  tool and finally the fabrication from available facility and its integration with HMS.

data.projectName: Non-thermal decontamination of raw chicken meat and associated contact surfaces through UV light application
data.projectDigest: Meat is a very important part of our diet due to the provision of several valuable nutrients required for proper health and growth. Safety of meat is of prime importance as it is a very good medium for microbial growth due to its nutritional profile. Several physical, chemical, thermal and non-thermal techniques are available to decontaminate meat surface. However, use of thermal and chemical interventions pose serious problems such as quality degradation and residual health effects. Therefore it is need of the present time to introduce non-thermal techniques that can be used to decontaminate meat and associated surfaces in a more effective way without adversely affecting meat quality. In this regard, proposed project is an attempt to introduce UV light application as a safe and economical non-thermal technique to decontaminate meat and associated contact surfaces

data.projectName: Water dispersible nanoparticles of hydrophobic drugs for improved anti-cancer and superior pharmacokinetic profile
data.projectDigest: Most of the anti-cancer drug molecules are hydrophobic in nature. This makes them insoluble in water and thus they follow an erratic biodistribution and elimination from human body. Also, their oral formulation is difficult to compound due to their insoluble nature in aqueous gastric environment. Nanotechnology has offered a number of advantageous in biomedical and pharmaceutical research. Nanomedicine is formulation or compounding of drug molecules in nano-structured dosage form and it offers superior pharmacological, toxicological and pharmacokinetic profile of the entrapped drug molecule. This project, proposes the encapsulation of hydrophobic anti-cancer drug molecules in hydrophilic and biocompatible polymers. Different polymers from natural or synthetic sources will be employed to nano-encapsulate hydrophobic anti-cancer drugs. Anti-cancer drugs like paclitaxel, vincristine and vinblastine will be used as model drug system to test these nanoparticles. The synthesized nanoparticles will be characterized for their physical and chemical properties, pharmacological and pharmacokinetic profile in vivo and in vitro. This project will provide an opportunity to collaborate with local pharmaceutical industry and lead the path to locally manufactured and patented anti-cancer nanomedicine.

data.projectName: Smart Power Generation Through Vertical Axis Wind Turbine on roads  and highways of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The environmental pollution is becoming a major problem of today’s world. As industries are getting revolutionized each day, there would be an increase in environmental impact from energy generation aspect through utilization of fossil fuels. The greenhouse gases emitted from conventional technologies thus results in global warming. The proposed study will help in mitigating such issue by generating free energy through vertical axis wind turbine (VAWT) on highways due to wind speed generated by automobiles movement. There will be less dependent on conventional fuels to some extent with commissioning of such project on highways that would eventually results in pollution mitigation and also obliging in improving people health. In Pakistan, most of the electricity is generated through oil importation that would have an immense impact on economic stability. The final product will be accommodated on motorway highways, where its energy will be utilized in following domains i.e. road lights, illuminating sign boards, rest service areas, and toll plaza respectively. The electricity generated through VAWT can also be delivered to nearby villages for household work and in tube well operations for agriculture purpose. From future aspect, the energy can be delivered to electric charging stations to charge electric vehicles.

data.projectName: Flows of some non-Newtonian nafluids over a lubricated surface
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest: Nanomaterials are the new energy products, as there are particles of the same or smaller scale than the coherent and de Brogile waves. The nanoparticles are the materials that absorb incident radiation in a powerful or selective way. Nanofluids may be used in nuclear reactors and computers for the next generation of safer coolants. In military systems, materials and chemicals, textiles, vehicle and transformer cooling, oil and gas, paper andprinting, etc., nanofluids are also very relevant. A topic of special interest nowadays is the modeling and analysis of non-Newtonian boundary layer flows induced by moving surface. These flows are usually seen in the manufacturing processes of thinning and annealing coper wires, extrusion of plastic surfaces, cooling of metallic plates, continuously extruded polymer filaments and a thin condensation phase of liquid film. The basic theme of this research proposal is to build and interpret the mathematical model of solar radiation by non-Newtonian naofluids, keeping all such facts and applications in mind. Therefore in the presence of nanoparticles, consideration will be given to the themally radiative flows of non-Newtonian liquids. Two-dimensional flows are taken into consideration. Instead of constant surface temperature conditions we will introduce the different thermal conditions namely, convective, Newtonian and heat flux conditions. Therefore different subjects will be introduced to achieve the project’s objectives. Such topic include the mathematical formulation of various non-Newtonian fluids, solution techniques, convergence analysis, numerical data for shear stress, mass and heat transport rates and physical elucidation of the resuls.

The basic theme of this research proposal is to build and interpret the mathematical model of solar radiation by non-Newtonian naofluids, keeping all such facts and applications in mind. Therefore in the presence of nanoparticles, consideration will be given to the themally radiative flows of non-Newtonian liquids. Two-dimensional flows are taken into consideration. Instead of constant surface temperature conditions we will introduce the different thermal conditions namely, convective, Newtonian and heat flux conditions. Therefore different subjects will be introduced to achieve the project’s objectives. Such topic include the mathematical formulation of various non-Newtonian fluids, solution techniques, convergence analysis, numerical data for shear stress, mass and heat transport rates and physical elucidation of the resuls.

data.projectName: Studies on the genetic mechanism of drug resistance among clinically significant pathogens
data.projectDigest: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is one of the most serious global public health threats in this century. Multiple drug resistance among Gram negative and some Gram positive bacteria has become a serious challenge for healthcare professionals. Rate of these antibiotic resistance bacteria has much increased among the hospitalized patients especially in intensive care units.  In this respect, Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Acinetobacter baumannii (A. baumannii) have gained much attention as they are important cause of hospital acquired infection and have become resistance not only to penicillin, methicillin, and cephalosporins but also to aminoglycosides, quinolones and fluoroquinolones. The resistance to these antibiotics may be due to change in the gene that leads to change in the structure of target proteins or may be due to production of some enzyme which modify the target antibiotic. There is need to monitor the antibiotic susceptibility of these pathogens in order to identify and prevent the spread of resistant strains. The current project aims to find the drug resistance pattern of local clinical isolates of MRSA and A. baumannii. Then, the analysis for the presence of any mutation in the drug resistance gene will be done by using PCR and sequencing. Bioinformatics tools will be used to determine the possible effects of the identified mutations on protein structure and function and correlation of these mutations with anti-microbial resistance will be assessed. The information may be used to design new drug analog for better treatment.

data.projectName: Crowd Control Using Adaptive Algorithms with Cognitive Embedded System
data.projectDigest: Hajj is the fifth pillars of Islam which must be carried out by Muslims who are afford to perform this obligation at least once in their lifetime. This once a year event only takes place on 8th to 12th Dhulhijjah which is the 12th and last months in Islamic calendar. During hajj month, the pilgrimage trip always has interference from a lot of people crowding the public. Thus, this can contribute to great challenges to Hajj’s pilgrim especially when chaos or emergency that requires evacuation is necessary. A more effective management system to monitor and ensure the safety of our Pakistani pilgrims is needed so that all pilgrims’ condition may be assessed immediately after the emergency evacuation or similar events occur. Current state-of-the-art sensory technologies such as Radio Frequency Identification (RFID), vision sensors, adaptive algorithms and micro-electromechanical system (MEMs) are among the best technologies to be used for this purpose. RFID technology can be utilized to monitor the pilgrim activities at the individual level. Vision sensors and MEMs technology can be used to monitor the pilgrim activities at the group or crowd level where the group motion state can be assessed visually and statistically. The main challenge within these three technologies is that whether the current research achievements can support a huge amount of data at a time in real-time application.

data.projectName: Use of herbal extracts as an alternative of synthetic hormones for all male tilapia seed production.
data.projectDigest:
Tilapia is the second most significant cultivated fish species worldwide. The precocious maturity is the major common obstruction in tilapia culture (as early as 3 month) and frequent breeding behavior make a significant fiscal loss. The scientific community has concerned about the production of all-male tilapias, having higher growth rate. Synthetic hormones (most widely used for sex reversal) considered as contaminants with emerging concerns in the environment because of their adverse effects on human beings and ecosystem. Due to these reasons ban in some countries. Their use is expensive, time-consuming, and inaccessible for fish farmers. A long term sustainable and efficient alternative method should be established to eliminate this issue. 
The best way to cope all these problems is through natural intervention, by the use of cheap indigenous herbal extracts which are less toxic and have negligible side effects. 
Herbal extracts are considered the best alternative to synthetic hormones for all- male tilapia seed production. Therefore, the project has been planned for all-male tilapia production through herbal extracts, which will be cost effective and eco-friendly for sustainable aquaculture industry. Moreover, the aquaculture industry will also get potential economic benefits by the successful completion of this project by introducing new appropriate technology

data.projectName: ECO-FRIENDLY MANAGEMENT PACKAGES FOR BRINJAL PEST IN PUNJAB PAKISTAN
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
Brinjal, an important vegetable, comprise about 94% production in Asia. This highly consumed vegetable is facing low production in Pakistan due to several insect pests including brinjal borer, whitefly, jassid, thrips, mites, and many other minor pests and diseases. Synthetic insecticides are sprayed intensively to control them especially brinjal borer, Leucinodes orbonalis to minimize the economic losses and increase aesthetic value of marketable fruit. These intensive pesticide applications result in deterioration of the environment, human health and misbalancing of socio-economic values of producers. 
Non-chemical pest management approach is the only acceptable way to get higher market value for such directly consumables especially vegetables and fruits. Keeping in view the current scenario of our agro-climatic conditions and future demand of organic vegetables, packages will be developed for the eco-friendly management of L. orbonalis. These packages will include sex pheromones traps for adult moth timely monitoring, biocontrol agents for egg and larval control, seed treatment by Trichoderma fungi to improve soil condition and plant health with clean cultivation practices.

data.projectName: Let us save the Environment: Optimizing Energy consumption in Cloud Data centers
data.projectDigest:
Cloud computing has altered the way many businesses and individuals use technology. No doubt it offers countless advantage in present regime, but its expansion has become a serious cause of concern because of massive increase in its energy consumption.   Consequently, the power consumption can be proclaimed as one of the causes of environment pollution; according to stats 17% of the total carbon emission caused by technology is due to data centers [1] . The rapid increase in number of datacenters is equally evident in developing countries as well. According to Gallup survey, Pakistan is among notably fast growing IT countries in the world, and an increase of 680% recorded in number of internet users in the first one and a half decade of this century [2]. To meet the needs of increasing number of users, numerous data center setups are being established. Thus, in Pakistan where air quality index is already poor, these data centers may cause more carbon emission which will ultimately lead towards environmental pollution. 
Such motivation has led to the presentation of a model for optimal utilization of cloud resources using Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and differential evolution (DE), in order to allocate virtual Machines to physical hosts by considering the consumption of electrical energy. The basic idea of the proposed model is to provide resources based on estimated user demands dynamically. Provision of VMs is based on the estimated resources in terms of CPU and RAM. The predicted estimate decides the number of active resources in the system at any given time.

data.projectName: Reproduction of Inequality-Structure of Punjab: A Social Space Approach
data.projectDigest: It has generally been asked that why it is very hard for poor persons to increase their income and change their lifestyle? However, the more important question is that why they are in the same conditions across the history. In other words, the difference of wealth and lifestyle between poor and rich has been replicated across history. The general answer to this question is that poor are incapable to change their lifestyle which is victim blaming answer. On the other hand, the broader perspective, e.g. Marxists, Neo-Marxists, Bourdieusian, etc. says that although education is one of the prime factors to attain higher level job, higher income, better lifestyle, etc. but this system is actually producing such differences of wealth and lifestyle because it favors only those who already have wealth; produces labor for rich people; produces lifestyles of upper class and, conclusively, facilitates and strengthens the existed difference between poor and rich. This research will study that how education produces and replicates the difference between poor and rich, across generations. The study proposed that rich people convert their income, relationships and lifestyle into each other, which helped them to sustain their income, relationships and lifestyle across generations. The study will be conducted in Punjab Province.

data.projectName: Internet of Things (IoTs) Enabled Smart Poultry  Management System(SPMS) for Poultry Famers and Hens Keeping Houses
data.projectDigest:
Teaching a man to fish will feed him for a lifetime.  This parable can be stated that “giving somebody a chicken and showing them how to raise chickens.”  Poultry farming is a complicated and difficult process. Currently, the poultry farmers in Pakistan have no access to technology to maintain the above factors. This causes huge losses in poultry farming and hence restrict their production growth. Such conditions demotivate the local businesspersons to start poultry farming.
 Activities to be undertaken to achieve the project goals
The poultry farms need a controlled environment such as suitable temperature, humidity, ventilation to remove harmful gases (Carbon dioxide, Carbon Monoxide and Ammonia) and automatic feed/water system to yield good production. Internet of Things Based Poultry farming can play an important role in providing the desired environment to poultry farms. Smart Poultry farming will introduce IoTs enabled facility for houses (5-10 hens) and farmers with different range such as small scale (50 hens), medium-scale (500 hens) and large scale (1000 hens).  In addition to this, a chick needs such as food, water, humidity, temperature and space changes when it grows from the 1st day up to 6 months. This IoTs enabled system will provide variation in these factors according to age wise need of the chickens. 
This IoTs enabled system for above fours scale of hens will be deployed and tested in local poultry farming.  This project will focus on to develop economical IoTs enabled Poultry farming system as these local poultry farmers cannot afford expensive technology.

data.projectName: Naegleria fowleri analysis in water supply system of Hyderabad,Pakistan.
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest: A free living ameba Naegleria fowleri commonly referred as brain eating ameba cause brain infection in human called as primary amebic meningoencephalitis (PAM). The PAM is a fatal, acute, necrotizing, fulminant disease of central nervous system with mortality rate of greater than 95% and due to intensive treatment, rapid diagnosis and supportive care the survival chances are only 5%. The alarming mortality rate in Pakistan specifically in Karachi, Hyderabad and its surrounding describes the enormity and significance of PAM infection. Naegleria fowleri is closely associated with public water supply and thrive during summer and in poorly chlorinated water and gains access to brain of human through nostrils while performing ritual ablution, washing face or swimming. This project will help in the identification and detection of Naegleria fowleri in water supply of Hyderabad and its nearby cities.  This study will help water and health service providers and policymakers to strengthen and improve the quality of water and the level of preparedness in control and prevention of PAM infection in Pakistan. The proposed project provide  a foundation to establish a world class diagnostic and analytical platform dedicated to addressing the presence and identity of Naegleria Fowleri in water samples.

data.projectName: Graduates of Religious Institutions and their Knowledge about Islamic Economic, Business and Financial Teachings
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Development Economics (PIDE), Islamabad
data.projectDigest:
The influence of religious scholars (Ulema) in our Pakistan cannot be overstated. They played vital role in creation of the state and in the constitutional development of the state. They played vital role in survival of ethics and Islamic values in the society. The society seeks their guidance regarding religious teaching. The religious scholars are trained by a strong network of religious educational system. Pakistan is among the countries having high rate of philanthropy throughout the globe and it is the country that hosted millions of refugees for decades. The teaching of religious scholars have played vital role in promoting the culture of support and sacrifice for each other. 

However, despite very strong religious educational system with millions of graduates, the Pakistani society still feels problem in getting guidance regarding Shariah rulings on economic and financial matters. The economic and financial issues construct only a marginal part of the syllabus of religious educational system in Pakistan. Therefore most of the graduates of religious educational system are indecisive about the economic and financial issues prevailing in the economy.

The un-authoritative knowledge of religious scholars is evident from the opinion of religious scholars regarding the contemporary Islamic Banking System. A group of religious scholars has played role in the creation of this banking system and they express their support to the system, whereas a large group of religious scholars have expressed their deep concern about the current practices of Islamic Banking. The third and majority group of religious scholars is just silent on this matter, whereas it is clear that the religious scholars have most important role in development of Islamic financial system.

data.projectName: Effects of Telerehabilitation on Quality of life following Total Knee Arthroplasty among patients living in Remote areas
data.projectDigest: Surgical operation for severe knee pain is frequently seen procedure particularly among older population. After operation, physical exercises are very important to maintain daily activities of living. But individuals living in remote areas report difficulty in accessing hospitals and they don’t have facility of exercise specialists in their areas. The money spend on travel from home to hospital also causes them a lot of financial stress. Despite undergoing knee replacement operation, they feel less energetic in their activities because they did not follow exercise sessions with their therapist as they don’t want to spend so much money again in travelling and using local transport is troublesome for them. Therefore, rural living people are facing problems in receiving quality care and they feel themselves underprivileged. With the progress in internet technology and availability of internet services every where plus the usage of smart phone has become so common, one of the possible solution for such population is to adopt the method of communication with their specialist doctors through tele-communication and internet services. The purpose of research is to evaluate the effects of tele-health method and to identify if it can be used as alternative to face to face therapy.

data.projectName: Real-time And Robust Distributed Decision Architectures For Multi-robot Systems
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Recent advances in sensing, communication, and computing technologies are enabling the use of multi-robot systems for practical applications like warehouse management, surveillance, area mapping, and search and rescue.  The deployment of multiple robots can execute a mission with more efficiency, e.g., as measured by time, energy, cost, etc. Multi-robot architectures provide resiliency to breakdowns or even adversarial attacks through redundancy and the avoidance of a single point of failure. There are also significant challenges associated with the deployment of such systems. To fully realize the benefits of a multi-robot system, we must have an intelligent framework for distributed decision making. In the absence of an efficient distributed framework, a multi-robot system can be even more fragile and vulnerable to system failures and attacks than a centralized system. 

In this proposed project, our objective is to design a distributed decision architecture for multi-robot systems operating under dynamic and uncertain environment. Moreover, the existing distributed algorithms for multi-robot systems are not robust to adversarial attacks, i.e., an adversary can manipulate the entire system by injecting strategically designed disinformation in the system through communication. The distributed decision architecture developed in this project will be robust to adversarial attacks as well.

data.projectName: Preparation and Evaluation of vaccine against locally prevailing strains of pathogenic avian Escherichia coli
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Colibacillosis is an infectious disease caused by the bacterium Escherichia coli (also known simply as E. coli), and is seen in poultry flocks worldwide. E. coli can cause an infection under the skin, known as cellulitis, and is commonly associated with respiratory disease in birds, which in severe cases leads to septicaemia and death. Avian colibacillosis primarily affects broiler chickens between the ages of 4 and 6 weeks and is responsible for a significant proportion of the mortality found in poultry flocks. This mortality, treatment of the disease and decreased feed conversion efficiency result in significant costs to the poultry industry. Treatment of colibacillosis relies on antimicrobial therapy, but with isolates of E. coli becoming increasingly resistant to frequently used antibiotics, this treatment may fail. Vaccination is one of the various methods, which has been applied to control colibacillosis. Currently, no vaccine is prepared in Pakistan against the prevalent pathogenic strains. The aim of present study is to prepare and evaluate the safety, immunogenicity and protective ability of vaccine containing the prevalent pathogenic serotypes of APEC against avian colibacillosis in broilers

data.projectName: Disaster Management using Software Defined MIMO Radars: RF Sensing based  Detection of Earthquake Survivors or Humans  trapped in the building using micro-Doppler Signatures
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is extremely vulnerable to earthquakes and natural disasters. During the last 30 years, Pakistan has undergone extreme transformations with respect to population and economic conditions. In this project, we aim to build a solution to detect targets hidden under debris or across the wall. We will design and implement the system using software defined radios. We will investigate novel signal processing algorithms for detection of such targets using bi-static radars and prototype it using software defined radios. We’ll start with the basic radar detection algorithms with standard radar. Thereafter we’ll work on monostatic and bi-static detection across the wall or rubble. We’ll work on improving the detection performance for such targets. Our project consists of three steps; we’ll first develop novel algorithms, simulate them on LabVIEW and MATLAB, and finally implement those using USRPs.

data.projectName: A potential role of kisspeptin antagonists in Therapeutics of Diabetes Mellitus to Improve Beta Cell Function.
data.projectDigest: Impaired glucagon secretion by pancreatic ?-cells is an early hallmark of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Glucagon stimulates hepatic production of the neuropeptide kisspeptin1, which acts on ?-cells to suppress glucose stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS). Kisspeptin is a novel neuropeptide which has been found to express in brain and many other peripheral organs and also in pancreas. Kisspeptin1 is increased in livers and in serum from humans with T2DM and from mouse models of diabetes mellitus. data.projectName: Gut Microbiota profile using 16S gene sequencing among lean vs non-lean Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease: A matched case-control Study
data.projectDigest:
Affecting up to 25% of the global population, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) has emerged as a global threat. A complex interplay between genetic factors, diet, components of metabolic syndrome such as obesity, and insulin resistance plays a major role in the pathogenesis of NAFLD. However, approximately 12-20% of western and 5-26% Asian patients with NAFLD does manifest in the absence of obesity names as “lean” NAFLD. 

The gut microbiome has emerged as an important regulator of host energy and substrate metabolism that may contribute to the development of NAFLD. However, the available data exploring the microbion gut liver axis among Asians is very limited. In the absence of obesity and unrecognized traditional risk factors, the diagnosis of NAFLD in lean individuals mostly gets delayed resulting in compromised care. Characterization of gut microbiota in larger human cohorts will help to identify the subgroup of microbiota associated with NAFLD among lean and non-lean individuals and later a tailored microbiome-based therapy. The present study is a matched case-control study aiming to evaluate the gut microbiota profile among patients with NAFLD with normal BMI (lean-NAFLD) and overweight/ Obese (non-lean NAFLD) and healthy controls by performing 16S rRNA sequence analysis in the stool samples. The association of microbiomes with hepatic fat fraction will be evaluated as well.

data.projectName: Virtual Tracking System
data.projectDigest:
In this project we are proposing a tracking device that is be integrated into a belt. This tracking belt or Virtual Tracking System is able to track the user by two possible ways; one via heat
sensor and the other one through a button. if the wearer is an infant then in a dangerous
situation whether the infant is crying or is scared, this feeling will generate heat or cold
temperature from the body, which will trigger the heat sensor after a certain temperature rise
or drop. After the sensor is triggered, it will alert the parents through a text message and
through the mobile application through that parents can track the location. The other way to
track a person is by button; if a person is in danger, they can press the button, which will send a
message to the graduation of the person through GSM module and they can track the location
of the person through mobile application. The language that will be used for internal coding will
be C++.

data.projectName: Design, Synthesis and Biological Evaluation of Antagonists of Purinergic Receptors (P2X and P2Y):A Novel Approach for the Treatment of Inflammation and Neurological Disorders
data.projectDigest: P2X receptors are trimeric ATP-activated ion channels that are permeable to K+, Na+ and Ca+2. They mediate several important pathophysiological processes such as modulation of synaptic transmission and immune responses, the secretion of neurotransmitters, and smooth muscle contraction. P2Y receptors belong to family of G protein-coupled receptors, which are stimulated by extracellular purines and pyrimidines that mediate diverse biological effects through activating phospholipase C. Over-expression of P2Y receptors subtypes have been found in different diseases including neurodegenerative disorders, thrombosis, diabetes, pain, cystic fibrosis and cancer. Progress in the area of P2Y receptors has been hindered due to the lack of selective and limited availability of antagonists. The development of selective inhibitors or activators, that can block or activate the specific P2X and P2Y receptor subtype, presents a very promising approach towards the development of advanced therapeutic tools for the treatment of various neurological and cardiovascular disorders, inflammation, thrombosis and cancer.

data.projectName: Assessment of Industry Readiness for Manufacturing of Battery Electric Vehicles
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest:
This project will provide an assessment of the industry readiness for battery electric vehicles (BEVs) in Pakistan. The study will begin with an exploration of the trends in BEV adoption and manufacturing around the world.
By making use of two frameworks: firstly, through the transaction cost economics framework, the study will give a comprehensive overall picture of the industry and will identify the associated key players in the BEV value chain, and secondly, the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework will be applied on key individual players identified through the value chain framework. ¬The study will utilize secondary literature review to understand the global best practices. Data will be gathered through questionnaires designed along the TOE lines, company documents, and government policies and reports.
Potential for the local industry in the value-driven segments of the battery value chain (e.g. battery pack manufacturing), service addition and product variation leading to a profitable business for local assemblers will be studied. Furthermore, additional issues influencing the manufacturing base for example lack of financial resources, high rates of tax and custom duties, and weak business models will be explored. The study will conclude by making recommendations on how to generate domestic demand for BEVs in Pakistan

data.projectName: ANTICANCER ACTIVITY OF INSECTS VENOM AGAINST HUMAN BREAST ADENOCARCINOMA CELL LINE (MCF-7)
data.piUniversity: Lahore College for Women University, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Animal venoms comprise a mix of bioactive molecules with high affinity for multiple targets in cells and tissues. Scorpion and spider venoms and purified peptides exhibit significant effects on cancer cells, encompassing four potential mechanisms: 1) induction of cell cycle arrest, growth inhibition, and apoptosis; 2) inhibition of angiogenesis; 3) inhibition of invasion and metastasis; and 4) blocking of specific transmembrane channels. Tumor biology is complex and entails many intertwined processes, as reflected in the putative hallmarks of cancer. This complexity, however, gives rise to numerous (potential) pharmacological intervention sites. Molecules that target multiple proteins or pathways, such as components of animal venoms, may therefore be effective anti-cancer agents. Nanobees are one of the latest variations of nanoparticles, microscopic spheres that can deliver drugs and imaging agents to tumors, cardiac blockages and other sick parts of the body. In the case of cancer therapy, the idea is to deliver cancer drugs to kill tumor cells, while preserving healthy tissue that surrounds tumors.

In summary, in spite of many promising initial and pre-clinical studies, the clinical application of scorpion and spider toxins for the treatment of cancer remains a challenge, yet needs to move forward. The formation and strengthening of public-private and public-public partnerships, the application of public funds, the creation of centers for translational research expansion, the development of local businesses, and specifically the encouragement of partnerships between universities and the pharmaceutical industry are imperative to advance the translational research movement in developing countries where these venoms are sourced and studied.

data.projectName: Developing an Ideal Microbial Pesticide for Agricultural Food Sources
data.projectDigest:
According to FAO reports, to feed the increasing population of the world by 2050,  at least 50% increase in food production will be required. If we do not control agricultural pests, we may face with more than 30% crop loss in average. Microbial control of food sources has been getting very popular in recent years. Entomopathogens (microorganisms of insects= fungi, bacteria and virus) are ideal candidate for developing organic control material against crop pests.  The microbial species used in such biocontrol methods are generally non-pathogenic for non-target species such as human beings and the wildlife. Entomopathogenic fungi have great potential as biological control agents against noxious insects and are an important component in integrated pest management. Important hydrolytic enzymes including lipase, chitinase and proteases contribute towards the pathogenic nature of the fungal microflora. 
Helicoverpa armigera (Hubner.) (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae) is a significant and detrimental polyphagous pest of tobacco, tomato, maize, pepper, sunflower, sorghum, pigeon pea, groundnut, chickpea, soybean, cotton and okra. Due to its destructive and cosmopolitan nature, European and Mediterranean Plant Protection Organization (EPPO) has declared it as an A2 quarantine pest (OEPP/EPPO, 1981). 
Helicoverpa armigera management using entomopathogenic fungi is a sustainable option because of environmental safety features of the entomopathogenic fungal species. Similar studies have reported the efficacy of B. bassiana and N. rileyi against larval instars of B. bassiana, H. armigera. B. brongniartii and Metarhizium anisopliae. There is a considerable potential to exploit these agents to control H. armigera in integrated approaches. A formulation of mycoinsecticide, Beauveria bassiana,

data.projectName: Design, Synthesis and Anti-Tuberculosis Evaluation of Sulfamethoxazole Metal Complexes as Potent Drug Molecules against MDR-TB and Other MDR-Infections
data.projectDigest: Globally, tuberculosis is an ongoing threat and is rising exponentially. Unfortunately, Pakistan is also not immune to tuberculosis epidemic. There has been a growing pattern of anti-tuberculosis drug resistance witnessed over the last few years and requires urgent action to develop more effective drugs to eradicate tuberculosis. In this regard, metal complexes come to rescue and have significantly improved the dynamics of antimicrobial drugs. Sulfamethoxazole is an anti-bacterial drug that possesses pronounced activity against both bacterial susceptible organisms. All synthesized compounds will be tested for anti-bacterial activity against uropathogens and Upper respiratory pathogens as well as against tubercular activity. The objective of recent research study is envisioned to design, produce and assess the antimicrobial activity of Sulfamethoxazole metal complexes against different microbes including Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

data.projectName: Energy Profiling of Residential Customers in Pakistan for Disaggregation based Load Characterization
data.projectDigest: Residential sector being the energy intensive sector with diverse nature of loads is exploited globally for various energy management programs.  Currently, the electrical utility companies in Pakistan have merely initiated the time-of-use (TOU) based tariff scheme for energy management, but it is mostly applied to commercial/industrial consumers, leaving most of the residential consumers unattended. In order to exploit the demand flexibility potential of this sector through energy management programs, a detailed characterization of consumption profiles of residential consumers is required at aggregate as well as individual appliance level though appliance load monitoring.  Such consumption profiles are available for different regions of the world for energy analytics, management and research.  As these profiles and load types vary with demographic locations, consumer habits and culture etc., there is need to develop a dataset of these profiles for residential consumers in Pakistan. This project will develop such a dataset through installation of sensors at diverse customer premises. The collected energy profiling data will then be used to develop energy disaggregation algorithm for load characterization of individual loads. Results of disaggregation-based characterization can be used by energy managers and multiple other stakeholders in various fields to obtain diverse benefits with innovative applications.

data.projectName: Phytochemical analysis and biological activities of edible Species Allium ascalonicum
data.projectDigest: The importance of plants for the whole ecosystem of the earth can never be denied. The plants have been the prominent source of nutrition and medicine since the creation of this earth. The plants rich in primary metabolites are having importance in nutrition while the plants rich in secondary metabolite have been gaining more and more medicinal importance. Some of the plants which have been used for nutritional purposes and have variety of medicinal importance are getting the focus of advanced researchers of the era. In this regard, the current investigational study has been designed to explore the medicinal and nutritional aspects of Allium ascalonicum. The Allium ascalonicum, which is inhabitant to Waziristan, Pakistan and ethnobotanically used as a food and have also ethnomedicinal importance, will be collected in mature stage. The fixed oil will be isolated from the mature seeds and volatile oil from its leaves. Structure of fixed and essential oil will be determined through spectroscopic analysis.  Leaves which are generally used as food will be assayed for various medicinal and nutritional components. The proximate analysis, GCMS analysis, Heavy metals analysis, phytochemical screening etc will be performed on various samples of this plant, which will be later on evaluated against various types of endogenous enzymes and so the medicinal importance of this plant will be explored especially against ulcer, diabetes and Alzheimer’s disease.
