data.projectName: A way forward towards stable and efficient Perovskite solar cell using carbon integration
data.projectDigest: Perovskite solar cells (PSC) have emerged as a promising inexpensive alternate to conventional Si based solar cells and is considered to be one of the top 10 breakthroughs in 2013. PCS is a hybrid combination of organic and inorganic materials. Recently, scientists have achieved more than 20% power conversion efficiency with PSC. Although high efficiencies of these cells have been achieved in labs, long term stability still remains an issue. Some of the main factors effecting the stability are its sensitivity towards moisture, thermal stress and UV exposure. A lot of research is being done on incorporating different materials in the cell structure to increase stability & efficiency of PSC. Different success rates have been achieved with different materials. A good contender for being used in PCS among the materials is Carbon. The different carbon allotropes gives the option of variety of properties such as high thermal conductivity, mechanical strength, chemical stability, electrical conductivity, electric density and charge carrier mobility. These properties of Carbon have the potential to not only make PCS more stable but also more efficient. The purpose of this research is to study the effects of carbon and its different derivatives on stability and efficiency of PSC.

data.projectName: Analyzing Barriers to Womens’ Sustainable Occupational Role in the IT Sector of Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
In underdeveloped country, Pakistan, the deliberation regarding gender equality in terms of women’s occupational role is always challenging. Working women normally resist discussing specific barriers to their sustainable career in respective fields. Such resistance particularly in the context of glass ceiling and workplace harassment being experienced; leading to uplift status quo and lack of clear policies at organizational higher-management level. Therefore, this research study intends to provide a formal platform to working women in information technology sector to share their feedback regarding systematic barriers to women’s equality based participation in occupational roles. The research investigative platform is in alignment with one of the sustainable development goals i.e.; gender equality. The working women’s feedback regarding diversity management is also considered, therefore; this research study investigates status quo contextual aspects for working women in terms of analyzing inclusive leadership and innovative work behavior relationship under the mediating and moderating mechanism of creative self-efficacy, glass ceiling and workplace harassment, respectively. 

Such relational mechanism is supported under the social role theory (Eagly, 1987), which discloses the visible and non-visible nature of glass ceiling, leading  to stimulate gender differences across occupations. The said mechanism will be investigated across IT sector in particular.

data.projectName: Unlocking Health, Environmental and Economic Benefits of Household Renewable Energy in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Development Economics (PIDE), Islamabad
data.projectDigest: Being an agro-based economy, 60% of Pakistan’s population is residing in rural areas and heavily depends on biomass fuels such as animal dung, crops residues fuel wood as the main source of energy for heating and cooking. These solid fuels emit harmful pollutants (carbon dioxide, methane, carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide, and particulate matter), which have serious health and environmental repercussions. Total livestock population of Pakistan is 159 million producing 652 million kg dung, which has capacity to produce 16.3 million m3 of biogas daily. This implies that country has huge potential of renewable energy, which remains untapped. Moving from polluted to cleaner sources of energy is expected to generate significant health, environmental and economic benefits. The aim of this proposal is to quantify health, environmental and economic benefit of renewable energy and to evaluate its economic viability by estimating benefit cost ratio and Internal Rate of Return by collecting primary data from 1200 households of biogas users and non-users in three provinces. It will not only help to attract the attention of business community and international donors to invest in this sector but will also lead to achieve the United Nations’ sustainable development goal 7 for cleaner energy.

data.projectName: Development a novel vaccine  against  MAP infection  by using CRISPR-Cas9 mutagenesis
data.piUniversity: Balochistan University of Information Technology, Engineering and Management Sciences,Quetta
data.projectDigest: Paratuberculosis is the chronic granulomatous enteritis disease of cattle, associated with huge economic losses and occur worldwide. The diseases once infect the animal, the animal remain infected for life and act as source of infection for other healthy animal. Persistent infection causes thickening of the intestinal wall that reduces absorptive capability leading to protein-losing enteropathy. The disease has long been subject for control by applying different strategies such as “test and cull”, vaccination etc. However, the combine strategy (“test and cull” and vaccination) has been suggested with highest success rate in developed countries. In this proposal, our Long-term goal is to develop a novel vaccine by CRISPR-Cas9 genes mutagenesis (multiple gene mutation) in important virulent gene involved in pathogenesis, latency etc. The Rationale behind the research is that MAP is a facultative intracellular bacterium and so control of infection depends on both arm of immune responses.  The Objectives of this research will be achieved by vaccine candidates screening in monocyte-derived macrophage assay and then evaluate their efficacy in mice model protection assay. At the completion of this research, we Expect to be able to understand how the vaccine interact with immune system and have a novel vaccine candidates which could be promising live attenuated vaccine with highest immunogenicity. Finally, we anticipate knowledge of the immune responses generated by mutant vaccines will aid in designing a vaccine formulation for the prevention and control of Paratuberculosis in cattle, sheep and goats.

data.projectName: Design of a Simulator based on Neural Network Paradigms for approximation of non-linear systems in Tank Engine
data.projectDigest:
Most of the real world problems are modeled with the help of transcendental equations or system of nonlinear differential equation that may or may not be coupled in nature.  The mathematical researchers have proposed a number of numerical as well as analytical solutions; however, a consolidated effort is made in the proposed project to design a simulator keeping in view the need of strategic industry in Pakistan like Heavy Industry Taxila (HIT), NESCOM, PoF and PAEC etc, where such approximation is required to further develop any indigenous systems or modules. 
The approximation power of neural network modeling has proven its dominance due to continuous grid of point calculations and high domain of convergence. The applicability of these artificial intelligence based methods have even been strengthened with the advent of high performance computer platforms like GPUs and sophisticated software packages. More specifically in the design of the Tank Engine lots of modeling is required specially of non-linear nature like longitudinal dynamics of engine, control valve of three tank system, combustion engine cooling system and four stroke C.I engine.  These models and its test bed verification will help HIT to enhance his research for developing its indigenous tank engine.

data.projectName: RESPONSE OF PILED RAFT FOUNDATION :AN EXPERIMENTAL AND NUMERICAL STUDY
data.projectDigest: Combined Piled raft foundation (CPRF) is recently been recognized is an effective type of foundation for tall buildings as well as for sites having problematic soil properties. Due to limitation of land, building projects are becoming taller and taller instead of spreading in the horizontal direction. Piled raft foundation, which is a combination of shallow and deep foundation can be an economical approach from capacity as well as from settlement point of view. Major problem in design of CPRF is that piles are design for all structure loads and contribution of raft is ignored which leads to uneconomical design. Contribution of raft during lateral loading is also ignored and batter piles are provided for lateral loads which is also a major problem. Similarly, no one have ever taken lateral capacity of basement walls, which also needs to be explored. There is a need for instrumentation on small scale models to verify the load sharing percentages between piles and raft in CPRF under combined (Vertical and lateral) loading, and beneficial effects of basement walls, which will create confidence in designers to take contribution of raft and basement walls, which will ultimately lead to build tall building in Pakistan economically. A simplified method will be developed based on the instrumentation and numerical modelling for analysis and design of CPRF under combined loading. Another benefit of instrumentation is introducing building health monitoring technology in Pakistan, which is very unfamiliar.

data.projectName: Occurrence, distribution, abundance and accumulation of Microplastics in Surface waters, Soils and Sediments of selected locations and Rivers of KP: Implication for fish and human health
data.projectDigest: Plastic products are readily available and have become increasingly popular because of their versatility, durability, and ease of production, hence Plastic production has more than doubled in the last few years. Plastic bags, plastic packaging, plastic containers and many other plastic products are intended for a one time use before being discarded. Presence of plastics in rivers have become a  matter of serious concern due to the threat to humans and aquatic organisms (fish).The abundant use of single use plastic items and its unregulated disposal to surface waters (streams, rivers and irrigation channels) lead to their disintegration into smaller and smaller particles. These disintegrated plastics are known as 'Microplastics'. Their size may range from visible to microscopic. Because of their smaller size they can easily transport with water and can be ingested by Humans and aquatic organisms when consuming water. These Microplastics can accumulate in humans and Fish. They have the potential to cause serious health risks if ingested. Moreover, these plastics have the ability to absorb harmful pollutants from water bodies on their surfaces hence they can be a source of other hazardous pollutants for humans. The proposed study will identify sources of Microplastic entry into selected rivers and  major streams of the KP province; it will assess the abundance of various Microplastics in surface and drinking water and sediments; it will assess the re;ative contribution of each source ; it will detect the presence of Microplastics in fish species of selected rivers; the study findings will be helpful in regulating the sources and entry of Microplastics into water bodies.

data.projectName: Quantum speed limit time of open quantum system with non-markovianity of surrounding quantum and classical environments
data.projectDigest: A generally established perception about quantum technology, including quantum computer, is its so-called ultrafast speed and the huge capacity for storing information. In the existing classical technology, these are the two aspects that attract the attention of a common user. The manufacturers of different devices around the world mostly competes on improving these aspects. These improvements are based on the size of the components on a chip, which has already gone down to nanoscale.  Further decrease in size of the components on chips is expected to result in quantum effects in the processing and storage of information. The only solution, for further improving these aspects, lies in resorting to the principles of quantum theory. The next legitimate question to be answered is to search for the bounds of speeds and storage capacity of devices based on quantum theory. Under idealized conditions, the ultimate bounds for both of them are already known [1,2] through time-energy relation and Boltzmann’s entropy. In general, the speed of evolution refers to the minimum time needed for a quantum system to evolve from one possible state to another in the Hilbert space of the system and is known as quantum speed limit (QSL) time. This project will try to model ways for speeding up quantum evolution and will train two Ph.D. and five MS students.

data.projectName: Development of new enrichment methods for the determination of toxic metals from water samples.
data.projectDigest: Extracting toxic metals with synthetic organic reagents are often too costly and the synthesis of organic reagents required complicated and laborious laboratory processes. So there is a need of alternative complexing agents for the extraction of metals. The present project is based on the investigation of active ingredients (nalidixic acid and sulfasalazine) of drugs (Negram and Salazopyrine) for their possible use for complexation and preconcentration of toxic metals (Pb(II), Cd(II) and Cu(II) ) and their removal from the water samples. The active ingredients nalidixic acid and salfasalizine could be purified from commonly used and easily available tablets Negram and Salazopyrine respectively. These ingredients could be impregnated on solid support like XAD-7 rein and charaterized. The resin can be packed in columns and used selectively for the preconcentration/removal of toxic metals (Pb(II), Cd(II) and Cu(II) from water samples. The loaded metals can be eluted with eluent and determined spectrophotometrically or by atomic absorption spectrometry. The extracting toxic metals by using active ingredients of cheap and easily available drugs seems to be good alternate for costly synthetic organic reagents. The project will thus help us to identify drugs for their possible use as complexing agents for toxic metals and thus will help for the removal of these metals from industrial effluents also.

data.projectName: PRODUCTION OF RECOMBINANT BACTERIOLYSIN FOR THE TREATMENT OF STAPHYLOCOCCAL MASTITIS
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
In Pakistan, the contribution of livestock is approximately 56% to agriculture and 11% to GDP. In the world ranking, Pakistan is at fourth after China, India and USA in milk production. But unfortunately our dairy animals are prone to wide range of infectious diseases. Among them the Mastitis is one of the shocking maladies of our dairy animals causing production losses to our livestock industry. This economically important disease is ranked as number one disease of our milch animals. Despite the implementation of management practices and treatment strategies, mastitis control still continues to be insufficient and requires some inexpensive, effective, efficient and reliable strategy for its control. 
For this purpose, this project aims to develop a recombinant lysostaphin as bactericidal enzyme with high purity against Staphylococus aureus which is principal causative agent of mastitis. This proposed study has focus to boost up the self-protection mechanism against this contagious infection. This therapeutic agent is a zinc metalloenzyme which has a specific lytic action against Staphylococcus aureus. This chimerical endolysin has multidimensional activities of three enzymes namely, glycylglycine endopeptidase, endo-beta-N-acetyl glucosamidase and N-acteyl muramyl-L-alanine amidase. This proposed study will be the first attempt to develop cost effective and efficient approach to treat the infection of S. aureus and thus improves the health of the herd, increase milk production and reduce the treatment cost. In addition to these, this project will be helpful to reduce the prevalence of mastitis in dairy cows. This can be a potential alternate of use of antibiotics in order to combat with multifactorial disease in term of etiology.

data.projectName: IDENTIFICATION AND SCREENING OF DNA BARCODES OF LIVESTOCK AND POULTRY ECTO PARASITIC INSECT SPECIES IN HAZARA REGION, PAKISTAN
data.projectDigest: Insects as livestock/veterinary and poultry ectoparasite have a significant impact on the health and productivity of Livestock and poultry health. These insects not only suck the blood and cause weakness and reduce their efficiency but also vector of several pathogens like protozoans, virus, bacteria, helminthes and fungi. These pathogens cause serious outbreaks and thus create huge loss in the field of livestock as well. Their impacts can be either direct, through tissue damage and blood loss or indirect as vectors. The insect ectoparasites include flies, lice, fleas, beetles and bugs. More than 13,000 species of biting and vectors insects have been reported globally. The project/proposal aims to contribute fundamental scientific knowledge in the field of community ecology, host-parasite relationships, and the processes underlying the diversification of life, while also ensuring the public a level of protection from biting insects and vector-borne diseases. DNA barcoding is a taxonomic technique that uses short sequence of DNA marker for the identification of species. The DNA barcode method of identification includes; identification of insect species at a particular stage of its development; otherwise, identifying insects morphologically generally depends on adult stage and male genitalia.  Methods include trapping and other collecting techniques and molecular analyses.

data.projectName: Evaluation of Urban Sustainable Development Progress: A Case Study of South Punjab
data.projectDigest: Pakistan has the highest rate of urbanization in South Asia. According to United Nations Population Division estimates, by 2025, nearly half the country's population will be living in cities. This urbanization can accelerate economic growth and employment through more specialization, more innovation and more use of technology as 80%of global GDP is being generated from urbane centres. However, the benefits of urbanization can only be accrued by sound public policies. Unplanned and unmanaged urbanization results in urban slums, environmental degradation, poverty and inequality. Pakistan too is confronted with a host of urban environmental challenges. It is therefore, needs of time to devise strategies for sustainable urbane cities. In this backdrop, the current study intends to develop the urban sustainability indices that can measure the social, economic and environmental viability of the new emerging urbane centres in south Punjab. As the IUB is in South Punjab, this study, therefore, would study the cities of this region to provide social justification of the IUB in this area. The results of the study can be inferred for the other cities of the country.

data.projectName: Biodiesel production from non-edible indigenous resources of Pakistan cascading towards bioenergy system
data.projectDigest: Domestic renewable energy sources can play an important role in fulfilling the energy demands of a country. In 2020, biodiesel industry is going to enter in a new era of transition to alternative feed stocks, emerging biofuel technologies and revised government policies towards sustainable and environmental friendly fuels. Aim of the project is to make efforts for improved quality biodiesel production from non-edible vegetable to make it cheap and cost effective and environmental friendly for its practical application and use of by-product of biodiesel (oil-seed cake) as a source of organic fertilizer. In order to resolve the conflict between food and fuel, the non-edible oilseed crops will be selected i-e non-edible oil seed crops (Jatrpha, pongamia, carthamus, algae etc.) and waste vegetable oil. The seeds of some of the non-edible oil seed crops will be collected from the respective areas and oil will be extracted. Different experimental designs will be constructed to select best protocol for maximum biodiesel yield and quality. The efficiency of different catalysts (both conventional and nanocatalyst) will be evaluated. Then, various biodiesel quality parameters such as viscosity, acid value, fatty acid profile, saponification value and pour point etc. will be determined to compare its quality with conventional diesel. The quantity of natural antioxidant such as phenolics etc. will be determined and efficiency of best quality biodiesel will be checked for its practical implications in the generators and available engines. Use of oil seed cake  as a source of organic fertilizers will be carried out for production of environmental friendly sustainable agriculture . Efforts will be made to make biodiesel cost effective and to reduce the energy crises of the country.

data.projectName: Synthesis and electromagnetic shielding effectiveness measurement of conductive materials
data.projectDigest:
The electromagnetic (EM) radiation pollution because of the enormous use of communication devices has exponentially increased after the telecom revolution. The electromagnetic interference (EMI) is disruption of signal of one device due to its interaction with signals of surrounding.  The proper grounding, isolation, filtering and shielding can effectively isolate one device from the EM noise generated by the surrounding environment. The development of materials capable of providing a shielding environment has gain importance both in research and industry. The electromagnetic shielding effectiveness is capability to provide a shield/block in a dense EM environment. The key to these measurements is vector network analyzer (VNA) along the turnkey systems fixtures intended for specific frequency range.
The aim of the work is to synthesize conductive materials or layer and to expand the measurement capabilities of the existing experimental setup VNA.

data.projectName: Valorization of fruit waste to biodegradable plastic by submerged fermentation
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Plastics, (polypropylene), are made up of material that is derived from petrochemicals and is non-biodegradable. At present, they are causing serious environmental pollution. It is required to replace them with biodegradable polymers, like polyydroxybutyric acid (PHB). As physical properties of both the polymers are similar so it has attracted interest to be used as bioplastic. Commercially, PHB can be manufactured utilizing ?-hydroxybutyric acid as monomers; but this method is expensive. Therefore, fermentation strategy using specific microorganisms under physiological stress is recommended. High cost of substrates and recovery process employed makes fermentation an expensive process. According to research, 3 tons of glucose produce one ton of biopolymer. Production cost can be lowered by using cheap fruit wastes as carbon source for fermentation. This study is designed to produce bioplastic by the mutant hyper-producing PHB strain of A.vinelandii using fruit waste. The fruit peel extract will be prepared by steam explosion and acid hydrolysis method. After the selection of best substrate for biopolymer production, different physio-chemical parameters will be optimized to increase the yield. The bioplastic produced will be identified by FTIR and quantified by spectrophotometric method. The optimization studies at pilot scale will be conducted on 5 and 30 litre fermenter In PCSIR labs. The cheap process for the production of bioplastic will be developed using waste material that can be further used on commercial scale.

data.projectName: Simultaneous zinc and iodine biofortification and their speciation and bioavailability in wheat grain
data.projectDigest: Most of the soil in Pakistan is deficient in zinc and iodine which important micro-nutrients due to which a large population is suffering from zinc and iodine deficiency. Wheat being a major crop could be used to bio-fortified with zinc and iodine which are the most deficient nutrients in this area. Therefore, in this study we will simultaneous  supply zinc and iodine in the form of zinc iodide and zinc sulphate+potassium iodide.  The foliar spray of different doses will be applied at the late reproductive stages of wheat.  In initial experiments, the suitable levels of zinc and iodine will be selected and then the available wheat cultivars will be screen out to find the suitable cultivars. Then the field experiment will be performed to investigate how combined applications of Zn and iodine affects the speciation and localization of zinc and iodine in wheat

data.projectName: Automated Solar Powered Dual Purpose Drinking Water Purifier Using Capacitive De-ionization Technique
data.piUniversity: Balochistan University of Information Technology, Engineering and Management Sciences,Quetta
data.projectDigest: Minerals are the major components of total dissolved solids (TDS) for brackish water & sea water found in various brackish supply and wastewater applications. Capacitive deionization (CDI) is an electrochemically controlled method for removing salt/minerals and dissolved ions from impure aqueous solutions by adsorbing ions on the electrode surface when external power is applied. As a result, it can produce pure drinking water as main and concentrated salt solution as a by-product. Unclean non-drinkable water particularly sea water & brackish water can be converted into drinking water with minimal energy expanse with this concept. Over the past couple of decades, CDI has been promoted as a cheap, low-energy, high-yield competitor to reverse osmosis (RO) and electrodialysis (ED), with applications ranging from water softening to seawater desalination. CDI desalination provides efficiently and cost-effective solution over already existed technologies. This is a technology that doesn’t use chemicals used for regeneration like softeners, has minimal preventative maintenance with an electrode that isn’t replaced unlike membranes, high recovery (80+ %) and high ionic rejection (98%). Solar powered coupled CDI is a new concept in this domain which can be utilized in countries like Pakistan having abundant sun and facing scarce water crisis at a very low operational cost. Antimicrobial and char filter will be added to remove microbial contamination and bad smells from water making the water more feasible for drinking purposes. Furthermore, the concentrated salt solution produced by-product can also be utilized for household and industrials applications.

The basic aim of this topic is to get awareness about nutritional deficiencies and its effects on the health of young girls. Further more ,efforts will be made to estimate the severity of health related issues of females due to nutritional deficiencies and the effects of that ailment on their whole life as a risk.

Further more ,efforts will be made to estimate the severity of health related issues of females due to nutritional deficiencies and the effects of that ailment on their whole life as a risk.

data.projectName: Semen Collection, Evaluation and Cryopreservation of Chukar (Alectoris chukar) spermatozoa: an ex situ conservation approach
data.projectDigest: The chukar (Alectoris chukar) belongs to family Phasianidae. The climate change, pesticide use, habitat degradation, habitat loss, intensive hunting and poaching are the major threats to this species. In this instance, captive breeding is an option to preserve and propagate this species using ex situ conservation approach. Inbreeding is one of the major problems in captive breeding that reduce fitness of the species by affecting individual survival, reproductive success, and susceptibility to pathogen and/or parasites. Breeding success of chukar in captivity is vulnerable to age of male, individual variations and sub-fertility. These problems can be overcome by adopting assisted reproductive technologies i.e. semen croybanking and artificial insemination. The successful cryopreservation of chukar semen required prior knowledge of sperm physiology, response of chukar sperm to low temperatures, identification of a suitable semen extender, a suitable cryoprotectant and the development of a freezing regimen for semen cryopreservation. In present project: studies are planned on chukar to identify seasonal changes in semen characteristics, collection and evaluation methods, semen extenders for liquid/frozen storage and fertility after intracloacal insemination. It is hoped that these studies will be directly helpful in managing and propagating the Chukar species in Pakistan and all over the world.

data.projectName: A study of interlinked cytoskeleton components using Tensegrity Model embedded in viscoelastic Medium
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest:
The cytoskeleton of all eukaryotic cells is composed of Nano structural components such as intermediate filaments (IFs), protein microtubules (MTs) and actin filaments (MFs) (Alberts et al.). Among these components, the diameter of IFs are 10 nm and, therefore, intermediate in thickness between the MTs with diameter 12nm and MFs, having diameter 7nm, and are present in both cytoplasm and nucleus (Franke et al., 1978; Herrmann and Aebi, 2004; Herrmann et al., 2007).They along with MTs and MFs give strength and mechanical stability to the cell, forming a rope like structure (Chang and Goldman, 2004). They are of different types such as in the epithelia, they are known as keratins, in connective tissue as vimentin and in the nerve cells known as neurofilaments that provide support in development when the axons dramatically increases their diameter (Yoon et al., 1998). Many researchers are using different types of (IFs) in tumour characterization techniques. The main type of (IFs) found in the nucleus, is called nuclear lamins and is present in all nucleated cells which strengthens the nuclear envelope and protects the genome inside (Gruenbaum et al., 2005).  Under the inner core of nuclear envelop, nuclear lamins lie which are responsible for the mechanical support to nuclear membrane as well as providing attachment sites for the chromosomes, but do break down during mitosis cell division (Ishikawa et al., 1968; Soltys and Gupta, 1992).
IFs are of multiple types even within same cell but some IFs are specific to specialized cells 
For example, neurofilaments are specific to neurons, particularly in long axons of these cells, muscle cells contain desmin filaments, and in epithelial cells the IFs are named as keratins (Hanukoglu and Fuchs, 1982; Karabinos et al., 1998). Othe

data.projectName: Development and Characterization of Functionally Graded Porous and Dense Materials for Biomedical and Structural Applications
data.projectDigest: There is a quest to develop the new materials which mimic the nature and natural structures. For this purpose, number of materials have been developed which are serving the humanity such as thermal barrier coatings. There are some graded and hierarchical structure that cannot be made through simple techniques as well as composite materials and monolithic materials with uniform composition cannot fulfil the requirement of the graded structure and properties. Functionally graded materials (FGMs) are new engineered materials which have graded structure with changing functionality. However, the fabrication of complex structures through compaction and sintering is difficult, particularly for joint and dental prosthesis applications. The other problem associated with the FGMs fabrication is the interfacial diffusion of the layers and week bonding between the layers. To mimic the natural structure of the bones, graded porosity is also required with changing properties. It is difficult to produce graded porous structures by simple compaction and sintering process. To develop the porous and dense FGMs there is need to develop the simple technique so that the structures with complex composition and shapes can be produced for commercial applications. Slip casting is a simple and well-developed technique for the processing of ceramics, however, it is not being employed for the synthesis of metallic and metal based composite materials so much. Therefore, slip casting technique will be applied to produce the porous as well as dense metallic FGMs. It is expected that interfacial bonding  can be enhanced and internal cracks will be eliminated because there will be no need of binder to develop bonding between the layers of the FGMs.

data.projectName: SOCIO ECONOMIC EMPOWERMENT OF RURAL WOMEN THROUGH ORNAMENTAL FISH BREEDING TECHNOLOGY
data.projectDigest:
Ornamental fish keeping, and its propagation is an interesting activity, which provide not only aesthetic pleasure but also financial openings. The long-term objective of the proposal is to take steps towards the development of ornamental fish breeding technology in rural areas of the Punjab. Ornamental fish production can be increased by introducing new breeding technology. Generally, the improvement through former technique cannot be transferred while the modern techniques can be transferred to the next generation and are much more important for the sustainable development of ornamental fishes in Pakistan. Although, America, European and many Asian countries have already increased their ornamental fish production. In Pakistan demand if ornamental fish has been increased but, unfortunately, no work so far has been done on this line in Pakistan. By the development of ornament fish breeding technology not only production of fish will increase but rural women can increase their income by selling ornamental fish to the aquarium shops and can improve their livelihood. In this program, ornamental fish strain evaluation and selection is the first step because various strains of ornamental fish display large amounts of variability for many different traits like growth rate, color, disease resistance, body conformation, dressing percentage, age of maturity, time of spawning, fecundity. Thus, a major objective of the proposal is to take a step towards ornamental fish breeding technology to improve the livelihood of rural women at small scale.
Primary objectives are as follows.
1-To develop ornamental fish breeding technology and its management which offer immense scope for improving the livelihood of rural women to enhance income and eradicate the poverty in rural areas.

data.projectName: Enhanced nutritional composition and viral disease resistance in potato through multiplex CRISPR Cas based genome editing
data.projectDigest: Potato accounts for 3rd most valuable food crop all around the world. Despite availability of much food sources shortage of nutritious components are one of the key limiting factor along with devastating effect caused by notorious Potato virus X and. Beside conventional tool applied the impact in terms of nutritious improvement and disease control was not impacted which demands for application of state of art technology to combat such problems in real term. The protospacers will be selected and verified for their target specificity along with different parameters.  The verified protospacers sequence will be assembled in designed cassette while protospacer from PVX and PVY will also be assembled with cassette of U6-26 promoter RNA Scaffold with only crRNA with no tRNA along with terminator sequence and both cassettes will be sent for synthesis on commercial basis. The verified plasmid will be transformed in potato by using Agrobacterium method by using internode shoot inoculation method. The developed potato plants will be subjected to PCR, T7 assay, Digital PCR along with amplicon sequencing for knock efficacy and real time PCR. The successful knockout and improvement in trait will open new doors to apply this novel technology to cope with other agriculture problems.

data.projectName: Process design and optimization of methoxy-methylheptane production: a potential chemical for reformulated gasoline.
data.projectDigest: The objective  of the submitted project is to design and develop cost-efficient production scheme for 2-methoxy-2-methylheptane (MMH) process.  THe chemical MMH is viable alternative to existing gasoline additives (MTBE, Ethanol) which were banned in the recent years owing to their serious health and environmental issues. The existing processes develop for MMH production lacks accurate physical and thermodynamic properties which are essential for a reliable process design. Extensive experimental and simulation studies are the main task of the submitted proposal. It is hoped that the expected results will help the global refineries as well as refineries in Pakistan to  develop  cost-effective production schemes for this future gasoline additive.

data.projectName: The economic and institutional analysis of the billion trees project under alternative tenurial contracts with a focus on women in the KPK
data.projectDigest: Pakistan launched the "Billion Trees Project (BTP)" in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK) with the aim of increasing the forest area by 2%. This massive reforestation has huge socio-economic and environmental implications, especially for small farmers. However, the economic analysis of forestation remains poorly understood in Pakistan. This compel us to carry out economic and institutional analysis of forestation in Pakistan. This study extends the existing literature by taking into account the role of tenurial contracts with a focus on women in rural areas. The overall objective of the study is to examine the socio-economic and environmental impacts of the “Billion Trees” project on farm households of KPK under alternative tenurial contract, with special attention to women. The Forest Landscape Restoration (FLR) approach provides basis to model the economic and institutional implications of forestation. This study will employ mixed method approach which involves collecting, analyzing and integrating both quantitative and qualitative research. We will use stratified random sampling to collect a sample of 600 farm households in Haripur. This study helps to inform policy makers and other stakeholders about the contribution of reforestation to improve the socio-economic well-being of families and their adaptability to climate change.

data.projectName: Estimation of Women's Unpaid Household Work and using it for Advocacy of Social Empowerment of Women
data.projectDigest:
Gross domestic product (GDP) is commonly used measure of economic growth, social well-being and nation’s standard of living. But, the near past has seen extreme criticism by economists on GDP as measure of welfare. One of biggest shortcomings of GDP  is that it doesn’t accounts for the non-market household production i.e. unpaid household work. The evaluation of this sector has given birth to a new research area. Researchers have indicated that this sector can be 50% or more of the GNP. House hold production means production of goods and services by the members of a house for their own consumption by using their own capital and unpaid labor. Household production is in fact a complete process whereby intermediate produced goods like pulses, grocery items are transformed into final product like food. 
Women around the world and specially in Asian cultures have traditionally  been associated with the household work and household work has been seen as the sole responsibility of women.  Though over the decades, women have started joining workforce and the trend is increasing. However, still majority of women are associated with only household work which goes unnoticed in current national accounting systems.  Thus, policy makers while making policies for social empowerment ignore contribution of women towards society and economy as the household work of women is not a part of indicators of economic growth.  This study is an attempt to establish a figure of the unpaid household work of women in Pakistan by using time surveys. These time surveys will be conducted across Pakistan and sample will be selected using random sampling technique. Results of the study will later be used to advocate better policy making for social empowerment of women.

data.projectName: Study of dielectric and electrical properties of ZrO2 based high k stacked dielectrics prepared via water based solution processing
data.projectDigest: The substitute of SiO2 with high ? oxide dielectrics has turned out to be an inevitable and urgently required due to the expanding integration of complementary metal oxide semiconductor transistors, because their relatively thicker layers can reduce the leakage current by reducing quantum mechanical tunneling. A great deal of research efforts are continuously being carried out in search for a suitable material. There are more than one suitable candidates and promising candidates such as HfO2, ZrO2, Al2O3, and a recently studied Sc2O3; all of them offer a high value of dielectric constant ?. Moreover, a High – ? dielectric grown on the Si wafer can not only increase the insulation but together with a metal gate used would allow for Fermi level shifts as well as help in accommodating the excess charges present due to the dielectric. Thus a Metal-Insulator-Semiconductor (MIS) and metal insulator metal MIM gate stack had been proposed and investigated in the previous decade. Solution processable fabrication, such as spin coating, spray pyrolysis, and printing techniques have been developed successfully with tremendous efforts towards low-cost devices. In this project, we will explore the scaling limit as well as the interface properties of stacked high k dielectrics including ZrO2 and Sc2O3 layers in MIS structures, using water based spin coating deposition. Both dielectric and electrical properties will be investigated.

data.projectName: Proposing Community Policing Model for the Newly Merged Tribal Districts
data.projectDigest: The passage of the 25th Amendment to the Constitution of Pakistan has led to the merger of the former Tribal Agencies with the province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK). The Amendment has sought to end the colonial tribal governance model based on the Frontier Crimes Regulation (1901), and has instead provided for the introduction of democratic governance based on federal polity of Pakistan. Thus the Amendment has set forth a process of transition for the former tribal areas to move from colonial-tribal political life to modern-democratic political life. In this process of political settlement one of the key institutions is the Police. And because the police will be introduced for the first time in the Tribal districts, we therefore think that the government should carefully mull over the prospects before taking any steps. We also suggest that it is high time to consider introducing the modern community-policing model after adapting it to the local cultural, security, and services needs. Through proposing this project we suggest that developing the community policing model for the NMDs is quite timely and relevant to achieving the development and community/nation-building goals of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Evaluation of Punjab Non Formal Education Project in the Literacy & Non Formal Basic Education Department in Last Ten Years
data.projectDigest:
Punjab Non Formal Education Project (PNFEP) is largest and sole project in Literacy and Non Formal Basic Education Department aimed to increase literacy rate and provide universal primary education. This study will evaluate the effectiveness and role PNFEP to eradicate illiteracy and catch out of school children in last ten years. 
This project will follow a multi phase mixed method design. It will be completed in four consecutive phases. In first phase researcher will conduct thematic analysis of interviews and focused groups from all stakeholders including Provincial Officer, Executive District Officers, District Literacy Officers, and Literacy Mobilizers. In second phase a survey will be conducted from a large sample. Survey will be conducted from the teachers of Non Forma Education Institutions. In third phase experts opinion will be gathered through interviews to suggest a framework for sustainable research culture. In fourth phase final reports will be prepared by integrating the findings from different phases.

data.projectName: Smart Agri: An approach towards efficient and effective cultivation using Hydroponics approach incorporated with IoT
data.projectDigest:
The emergence of Internet of Things (IoT) technology has transformed various sectors of common man’s life into smart entities and agriculture is one of them. Agriculture is considered as an important economy uplifting industries of Pakistan. However, a lot of up gradation is still required. Tradition agriculture methods are exposed to various issues i.e. water shortage, soil degradation, plant diseases and productivity are the ones that need to be taken into consideration.
Recently modern farming methods such as Hydroponics techniques are adopted and incorporated with the smart technology (IoT, artificial intelligence) to provide efficient controlled and autonomous environment. Hydroponics with IoT farm business includes growing plants, greenery, etc. by providing them the optimal environment and essential nutrients without indulging in the draining and lengthy procedure of growing plants in soil. 
The main idea of this research is to develop an efficient and effective hydro cultivation system using smart technologies with the adaptability to cater to a wide variety of different plants. Hydroponics system will be installed in an indoor facility. Proper light, heat, drainage will be insured by IoT devices (notifications and alerts) on all steps. In addition, all the data can be visualize on a mobile application to monitor the plant details, sensor status and water level cycle. The application will also be supported with online market place that will help the framers and other peoples growing vegetables, fruits or flowers to sell/buy their productions.

data.projectName: Development of a low cost carbon based triboelectric generator for clean electricity harvesting in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Clean and alternate electricity generation has gained tremendous importance among the developed nations of the world. Triboelectric generator is a microelectromechanical systems based (MEMS) device that can serve as an alternate and clean energy harvesting device. A triboelectric generator utilizes the concept of static electricity by intermittently bringing two dissimilar materials in contact. The device can be constructed using hierarchy of materials and fabrication techniques but in order to manage the overall expenditure feasibility of utilizing low cost materials must be investigated. Since, energy has been a major issue of Pakistan and in many ways it is also related to better health and sustainable living. Therefore, the main focus of this research proposal is to establish the state of the art facility for developing and testing of microelectromechanical system (MEMS) based triboelectric generators that involves easily available and low cost carbon based materials. The utilization of low cost micro or nano structured carbon based materials in MEMS energy harvesting make this research an innovative step. The proposed device will be able to convert freely available actuations like vibrations, friction, kinetic energy of motion and rotations into clean electric voltage output. The research will focus on the effects of the individual carbon based micro or nano structured materials like charcoal particles, carbon fibers, graphite flakes, multi-layer graphene, nylon fibers, teflon fibers, polyester fibers, polyethylene fibers and human and animal furs on the device performance and also the effects of their combinations which has not been studied before. The different phases of this research will be the establishment of the MEMS research lab, fabrication of the device,

data.projectName: Sero-surveillance and genomic diversity of Listeria strains isolated from ruminants and occupational workers in Punjab Province
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Considering the significance and utilization of animals in our country and the substantial losses rendered by listeriosis, the present project is designed for sero-prevalence and molecular characterization of listeriosis in small ruminants and occupational workers in Punjab. A reliable diagnostic procedure will be established and local strains will be identified and isolated. Phylogenetic analysis will be carried out. The present study will be comprised of three parts. In part-I, Sero-prevalence of the disease in small ruminant and occupational workers along with the evaluation of associated risk factors with the occurrence of listeriosis will be studied. For sero-prevalence, 768 ruminants blood samples (n=384 bovine; n=384 small ruminants) and 300 human serum samples will be collected through stratified sampling technique. The collected samples will be processed using specific ELISA kit at Medicine Laboratory, University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore. In part-2, molecular characterization listeriosis will be done on those samples that will be positive through ELISA kit for identification of listeriosis using polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and further sequencing and phylogenetic analysis will be done on the PCR positive products. Part-III will encompass therapeutic trials. For chemotherapy, 30 positive small ruminants (n= 15 sheep; n= 15 goats) will be selected and further divided into three groups A, B and C. Each group will be comprised of 10 animals (n= 5 sheep; n=5 goats). Animals of group A will be treated with Penicillin G @ 40,000 IU/kg intramuscular, group B will be treated with Amoxicillin @ 20mg/kg intravenous and animals of group C will be treated with Sarsaparilla (a herbal medicine). The efficacy of antibiotics and herbal medicine will be check

data.projectName: Risk Assessment of soil erosion under variable land uses in the Azad Jammu and Kashmir
data.projectDigest: Erosion results in degraded soil quality and decline in productivity.  Globally, water erosion is 1094 million ha (Mha) and out of it 751 Mha is severely eroded. In Azad Jammu & Kashmir mostly having mountainous and sub-mountainous topographic features of the terrain, erratic and high intensity rainfalls, ignored soil and crop management practices accelerate the problem of soil water erosion. In Quantification of soil erosion is prerequisite to estimate the effectiveness of different applied measures of erosion control.  The study will be done in five districts of Azad Jammu & Kashmir and field investigations will be done.  The erosion risk will be assessed in the area by Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE) together with Geo-informatics techniques. The intensity of erosion will be mapped and the influential factors of erosion will be studied in multiple  environmental change. The area will be divided into soil erosion risk zones according to the intensity of erosion. The data will give information about development of soil and water conservation strategies and planning. This data will be helpful to conduct more specific research under same theme and will be shared with agriculture departments, communities and academics.

data.projectName: Development of Colorimetric and Fluorescent Probes for Arsenic and Fluoride Detection in Ground Water
data.projectDigest:
Elevated levels of arsenic and fluoride ions in drinking water has led to a massive epidemic poisoning in some areas of Pakistan. It has been reported that babies been born with bone deformities and cancer in adults in some industrial areas is related to arsenic and fluoride contaminated ground water which is higher than maximum permissible limits recommended by WHO. [1,2]
Several analytical techniques have been used to monitor these but high cost, time consuming procedures and sophisticated instrumentation limit their adaptability. [3,4] Fluorescent and colorimetric sensors offer an alternative route for detection of analytes. [5] A few sensors have been reported but they suffer from poor selectivity and/or low solubility in water. [6,7] Therefore, detection of arsenic and fluoride levels in water is a very crucial and challenging field of research. This project propose new economical and rapid colorimetric and fluorescent detection method for arsenic and fluoride ions with high sensitivity and selectivity.
Fluorescent benzothiazole, coumarone and amide based moieties will be synthesized for detection of these analytes by using fluorescence, UV/Vis and NMR spectroscopy.
The present project is aimed to develop low cost colorimetric and fluorescent sensor for detection of arsenic and fluoride ions concentration in ground water.

data.projectName: Expression and characterization of thermostable lipases for biodiesel production from algae
data.projectDigest:
Lipases are important group of enzymes that plays a significant role in various industries. The lipase mediated biodiesel production is an environment-friendly and sustainable alternative to solve the energy crisis. However, the success of the process is limited by the availability of highly active and thermostable lipases. Therefore, the quest for catalytic efficient lipases which have prolonged stability at a high temperature is continuous.  The proposed project is designed to clone the lipase genes from hyperthermophiles Thermotoga petrophila, Thermus aquaticus and Sulfolobus solfataricus into cloning vectors. The cloned genes will be sub-cloned into expression vectors followed by transformation and expression into the individual E. coli strains. The expressed protein will be fully characterized. 
Biodiesel synthesis requires the plant-based vegetative oil as substrate. The most commonly used oils are soybean, sunflower, palm and rapeseed. These edible oils are not good choice due to competition with food supply and arable land requirements for the plant growth. The other disadvantages of vegetative oils include higher viscosity, lower volatility and unsaturated hydrocarbon chain reactivity.  The algae have more oil contents and require less space and time for growth. So, algal oils are the more economical and sustainable alternative to edible oils.  Therefore, in this proposed project, algal species will be used as source of oils. There species of algae Oedogonium, Cladophora, and Caladorphora will be cultivated on lab scale and oil will be extracted from them individually, followed by transesterification using recombinant lipases.  Recombinant lipases from hyperthermophiles also have the potential to be used in detergents, cosmetics, food and pharmaceutical sectors

data.projectName: Role of Family Social Network in Poverty Alleviation: A Case Study of Punjab
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Punjab has made significant strides in reducing poverty headcount between 2001-02 and 2013-14. While Punjab’s progress in poverty alleviation is appreciable, the urban-rural gap hasn’t been reduced by much. Poverty headcount ratio in rural Punjab is 13 percentage points higher than urban Punjab. Similarly, the progress in poverty alleviation has been far from equal across districts. For instance, DG Khan has not shown much improvement between 2006-07 and 2014-15 (where poverty decreased by only 0.59 percentage points) whereas Chiniot has achieved significant reduction in poverty (decrease in poverty by 23.9 percentage points) during the same period. Government has announced Ehsaas poverty alleviation program for which precise targeting of the high-priority population is absolutely critical . In addition, the Government needs to identify the bottlenecks that have been preventing districts like DG Khan from breaking out of the poverty trap. Therefore, this study will identify the determinants of a successful poverty alleviation strategy by comparing the high-performing district (Chiniot) with the low-performing district (DG Khan). The study proposes that family network plays the pivotal role in mitigating poverty and it seeks to identify multifaceted roles played by family in Pakistani society for providing social insurance to the people.

data.projectName: Effects of Enhanced Physical Activity on Antioxidant Status and Cardiometabolic Markers in Prediabetic Population
data.projectDigest: Diabetes is a serious health issue with many complications for all humans over the world in common and Pakistan in special. Diabetes is preceded by Prediabetes which can be cure with regular exercise and diet modifications. This study will not only help us in understanding the basis for disease progression but will also enable us to prevent the disease at early stage.  The study will be carried out on those people who are at prediabtic stage and are prone to disease development by  asking them to recruit in the study for 2 months and 1 week time where serial exercise activities will be performed along with many blood investigations. In conclusion, the study will help us in encountering the huge disease burden in our country.

data.projectName: Import Substitution Industrialization in Automobile Industry
data.projectDigest: The vendor segment of automotive industry in Pakistan is facing multiple challenges including (i) lop-sided government policies in favor of OEMs, (ii) in-effective lobbying of vendors at policy-making forums including engineering development board, (iii) limited capacity in terms of technological development and financial resources, and (iv) narrow margins due to involvement in production of low value-added parts only. The research team intends to work closely with the vendor industry and its representative (PAAPAM) and Engineering Development Board to understand the nexus between Vendors, OEMs and EDB in the context of CPEC and provide policy recommendations and solutions for the local vendor industry.

data.projectName: Management of Soil-borne pathogens and Diseases of Rice-Wheat cropping system by Anaerobic Soil Disinfestation in Punjab
data.projectDigest:
The project deals with a natural soil pre-treatment or fumigation technique known as Anaerobic Soil Disinfestation (ASD) to eradicate soil borne pathogens and associated diseases to improve crops yield and productivity. In this technique, soil is saturated with water and covered with organic matter (molasses, rice bran etc). After this soil is covered with a polymeric liner to minimize the available oxygen for pathogens. After a few days, pathogens become facultative anaerobes and feed on organic matter, then by punching holes in the polymeric layer, oxygen is introduced which kill the remaining pathogens. This method can be proved beneficial for wheat and rice cropping system in Punjab. 
Punjab is producing the maximum amount of the two cash crops which  usually suffer from pathogenic diseases and the productivity is affected. Therefore, field trials will be performed. Furthermore, physical, chemical and biological parameters of the soils of wheat-rice cropping system of  Punjab will be assessed by collecting soil samples. Also, efficiency of ASD in reducing pathogenic disease strains will be assessed and if found beneficial, farmer organizations will be provided technical trainings in Punjab so that they can shift from chemical pre-treatments which are harmful for food chain and posing a threat to food security, towards natural ASD treatment which is not at all harmful for ecology and humans. This will be proved by testing and monitoring of soils physical, chemical and biological properties during the ASD treatment application in test fields trials.

data.projectName: Clinical and molecular investigation of hereditary conditions affecting the development of ectodermal appendages
data.projectDigest: Several signaling molecules including fibroblast growth factors (FGFs), Bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs), tumor necrosis factor (TNF) pathway proteins, sonic hedgehog (SHH) and Wnt proteins are essential for the accurate development of ectodermal appendages like hair, nails, teeth, and several eccrine glands. Defects in one or more of these pathway components have serious consequences, being evident by various hereditary ectodermal disorders. High rate of consanguinity has been the leading cause of hereditary disorder that affects the development of ectodermal appendages in developing countries like Pakistan. Molecular investigations on such families will enhance the knowledge regarding embryogenesis of ectodermal organs and will help in the genetic counselling and family screening that is not routinely done in developing countries like Pakistan. In the proposed work families demonstrating various hereditary ectodermal disorders will be located across Pakistan. After clinical analysis, molecular investigations will be initiated for the identification of potential candidate genes. This will involve direct sequencing of the coding regions of known genes followed by high through put technique; whole exome sequencing.  The potential effect of identified pathogenic variants on protein three dimensional structure and function will be studied through structural bioinformatics approaches and various functional studies like RTPCR and site directed mutagenesis.

data.projectName: DESIGNING AND FABRICATION OF A 2-DIMENSIONAL MATERIALS BASED BROADBAND METAMATERIAL ABSORBER AT TERAHERTZ REGIME FOR STEALTH PURPOSES.
data.projectDigest:
The aim of this project is to fabricate a broadband metamaterial absorber in high frequency region which can be used for the development of stealth technology research in Pakistan.
Metamaterial absorbers are artificially designed structures with a particular resonance frequency. Since after their early reports, metamaterial broadband absorbers got tremendous interest on the grounds of interesting applications. Particularly, their use in stealth application areas can play a vital role in any country’s topmost defense R & D progress. The presented project is least desired by keeping in view the recent advancement in radar and stealth areas. It would impart major contribution in the development of Hi-tech research and development in Pakistan. 
The proposed work is material, structural and fabrication-based perspective scheme to achieve the efficient broadband metamaterial absorbers for high frequency range. In this project we have planned to introduce a novel design scheme in top metal layer as well as buffer layer of 2-Dimensional layered material that is Graphene and metallic phase transition metal dichalcogenides to construct broadband metamaterial absorber. The choice of buffer 2D layered material will depend on top metal layer. Project experimental work will be supplemented and compared with finite difference time domain (FDTD) simulation results for comparison.

data.projectName: Blind Eye
data.projectDigest: Due to the increasing number of visually impaired people, researchers are focusing on inventing automatic devices to assist these people. The development of such devices is not a recently emerged problem. But due to advancements in computers and AI, the researchers have shifted their interest towards Intelligent devices. A lot of devices have been developed to aid blind people, but almost all of them have some limitations and hence are not able to meet all of the needs of such people. Current systems are either very expensive or are not efficient enough to process the data in real-time. Our aim is to develop an intelligent and efficient device using state-of-the-art AI and computer vision techniques to solve the problems that still need to be addressed. Our major focus is on the development of Smart Glasses that are easy to wear and use, under minimal cost and time. The resulting system can capture scenes using embedded cameras in the glasses, recognize all of the objects in the scene, measure distance of obstacles from the user and guide the user through voice commands to make decisions. We also look at the scientific, technological, or economic benefits. We tend to improve the current algorithms, boast the economy and through the implementation of this product encourage people towards recent technology which will be a great contribution towards the research.

A lot of devices have been developed to aid blind people, but almost all of them have some limitations and hence are not able to meet all of the needs of such people. Current systems are either very expensive or are not efficient enough to process the data in real-time. Our aim is to develop an intelligent and efficient device using state-of-the-art AI and computer vision techniques to solve the problems that still need to be addressed. Our major focus is on the development of Smart Glasses that are easy to wear and use, under minimal cost and time. The resulting system can capture scenes using embedded cameras in the glasses, recognize all of the objects in the scene, measure distance of obstacles from the user and guide the user through voice commands to make decisions. We also look at the scientific, technological, or economic benefits. We tend to improve the current algorithms, boast the economy and through the implementation of this product encourage people towards recent technology which will be a great contribution towards the research.

data.projectName: Geographical Distribution and Characterization of Major Wood Decaying Fungi Infecting Forest Trees in  up hills of Murree and  Azad Jammu and Kashmir and  incidence model development
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Studies pertaining to wood decaying fungi in moist temperate forests in Pakistan, particularly in Azad Jammu and Kashmir did not get due attention in the past. Therefore, current research has been planned to determine the status of wood decaying fungi and to explore local myco-flora of  hilly tracts of AJK and moist temperate forests of Murree, as there was no systematic study to our knowledge in past was done about these  serious issues.  The proposed study will be helpful in determining the status of wood decaying fungi prevailing in AJK forests. Survey would ultimately be helpful in indicating the areas with high wood decaying fungi. The survey will be conducted to know the current status of the problem and collection of samples from selected sampling sites will also be undertaken. The fungal pathogens will be identified on the basis of morphology. Pathogens will be subjected for molecular characterization by using universal primers and DNA sequencing will be done. Fungal incidence model using GIS will be applied to whole study area to identify the disease hot spot areas in AJK and Murree.

data.projectName: Real-time detection of adulterants and diseases in grounded red chili.
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest:
Grounded red chili is used as an important food ingredient in Pakistan. It is used in majority of food items consumed in Pakistan. It’s usage dates back centuries and is an important part of traditional cuisines and pharmaceutical industry. Pakistan is 4th largest producer of red chili and has a 5% global share of red chili market, mainly produced in Sindh and Punjab provinces.

According to Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, Pakistan produces around 200,000 tonnes of chili annually. Based on international prices, the chili produced in Pakistan is valued around $3.5 billion. Whereas the export of total fruit and vegetables of financial year 2018-19 lies around $570 million. This indicates the true potential of this vital produce is far from its utilization. An important factor of week import is weak food safety protocols being practiced in Pakistan.

Presently food authorities are making raids based on alleged reports, where they have no mechanism of testing the spice adulteration on site. They rely on observations rather than empirical results, or send the samples to distant laboratories to conduct DNA testing, which may take days or weeks to get back the results. This delay often creates a situation of conflict between food authorities and vendors. To counter these problems, we are proposing a hyperspectral imaging solution which can detect adulteration and disease in spices on site.

In this project a fully working model shall be developed to detect and identify the contamination in red chili powder to enforce strong food security protocols. The proposed project shall work in real-time environment, helping food authorities to verify the safety standards on site. This shall also cater food standards in red chili powder in processing units.

data.projectName: Molecular mechanism of neuronal protection and differentiation by natural compounds in human neural organoid cultures
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Neurodegenerative diseases, ischemic stroke and other brain related injuries have become a major health problem globally. Recent interest has focused on the therapeutic use of plant derived natural products which can decrease the neuronal damage and improve brain function. Withania somnifera commonly known as Ashwagandha or Indian ginseng extracts have traditionally used as tonic to enhance longetivity and revitalizing the body. Various studies have also shown promising results and suggest the use of compounds in various brain related diseases.  The aim of the present research is to study the mechanism of neuronal protection and regeneration by purified compounds of W. somnifera in lab grown mini brain generated from adult stem cells. It is hypothesized that compounds from W. somnifera may reduce neuronal loss and accelerate adult neurogenesis. The present study would therefore aid in exploring the neuronal protection and regeneration mechanism by compounds of W. somnifera and would be an initiative step in the direction of developing drug for the treatment of patients suffering from brain related diseases like stroke and neurodegenerative disorders.

data.projectName: Dendroclimatic studies of coniferous reserve forests of Tehsil Murree:  A step forward in sustainable conservation
data.projectDigest:
II. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Hills of Tehsil Murree was once renowned as “Thanda Jungle” which is now depicting a picture of wasteland heaps and unplanned tourisms. This increase in the number of tourists in the area related to anthropogenic activities like rapid civil work, improper solid waste management, issue of water and air pollution. Moreover, it is estimated that tourism has been increased from 12,50,000 to 16,37,650 in 2016-2018 years in Murree. Such activities are proved to be the contributing factors in change in climatic conditions. These change climatic conditions of the area increased temperature of the day and night, change in precipitation, and the composition of the plant community structure in the area.  Such drastic developments is now a days aggravating the problem of climatic drift in the nature and the atmospheric composition is being disturbed in areas like Murree.    
By considering the present scenario of tehsil Murree, it is planned to assess the dendroclimatic potential of the some coniferous trees species, it can be concluded that further sustainable conservation strategies. This project will also help to disseminate the basic knowledge to the students of plant sciences and ultimately will have the contribution to the community.

data.projectName: Development of Research Respository (PhD & MPhil
data.projectDigest: A large amount of authentic research work has been done at indigenous universities in the form of M.Phil and Ph. D dissertations. The authenticity of this research work can be gauged from the fact that all these dissertations were completed under the supervision of valid and reliable experts and were submitted as the mandatory requirement for the award of respective degrees. Moreover the linked degrees were awarded after the completion of a strict procedure of official and scientific scrutiny of these dissertations. But this valuable treasure seems to be wasted altogether due to the absence of managerial, retrieval and indexing system of the respective institutions. The researcher intends to conduct a project with the aim to prepare a database comprising all the theses and dissertations completed in the subjects of History and Pakistan studies in all the Universities of Pakistan. Considering the broad spectrum of the project, initially it is intended to launch as pilot project consisting of the research work of only three public sector universities—University of the Punjab, Bahauddin Zakariya University, and GC University Faisalabad.

data.projectName: Coordination for Cohesion in Public Sector in Pakistan: Outcome Evaluation of NPM Reforms
data.projectDigest:
Public sector reforms have been the cornerstone of public administration and management around the globe. These reforms are the reactions of the perceived weaknesses of the public sector. Based on traditional public administration model, public sector in Pakistan is also rigidly bureaucratic, lacks innovation in service delivery and face procedural delays. Multiple reforms have been introduced in Pakistan which can be categorized in different models. The study particularly investigates the impacts created by NPM reforms which include public sector fragmentation, lack of coordination and cohesion in public agencies. Federal agencies in Pakistan are selected for the study and many of them are established under NPM reforms. This study will measure the problems like lack of horizontal coordination, cohesion and communication associated with public sector in Pakistan. The study accounts the perception of the federal employees regarding the appropriateness of the reform and its implication associated to their jobs which may facilitate or hamper their own performance.  
The study will cover assessment of NPM based reforms in public sector agencies at federal level working in various sectors and domains under different ministries, divisions and departments. The overarching aim of the study is to empirically and comparatively assess the impacts (particularly coordination and fragmentation issues) of NPM based reforms in various sectors in Pakistan. Mixed method approach will be utilized including quantitative data ( through COCOPS survey)  and qualitative data (through semi-structured interviews ). The project will be completed in six work packages that are integrated with the research objectives.

data.projectName: The Impact of Husbands’ Overseas Migration on the Socio-psychological Wellbeing of Left Behind Wives in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The proposed research aims at understanding the impact of overseas migration of the husbands on the socio-psychological wellbeing of wives left behind. The phenomenon of international migration revolves around males in the case of Pakistan. The overall size of international migrants from Pakistan is increasing day by day. The current official statistics of the Government of Pakistan shows that the total number of migrants reached to 9.4 million. The majority of the overseas migrants from Pakistan are residing in the middle-east region. There are number of reasons behind overseas migration from Pakistan. Poverty could be one of the main causes of international migration from Pakistan. The process of international migration has multilayered effects not only for those who initiate it but also for the left behind families. The foremost impact of migration is in the form of economic gains for the families which consequently boost up their economic and social position in the community. The economic improvements make it possible for the left behind families to access the basic needs while those who work abroad face many difficulties to accommodate their families’ needs.

data.projectName: Indigenous Soybean value chain strengthening for sustainable poultry industry
data.projectDigest: Commercial soymeal in Pakistan’s poultry feed is relying on imported products leading to higher import bill. Soybean’s more than 100 products can be obtained pertaining to its high-quality protein, essential oils, vitamins and minerals and to address Sustainable development goals (SDG) 2, 3, 12 and 15. Unsustainable supply chain mechanism is major constraint in marginal cultivation supply poor. Development of sustainable supply chain mechanism coupled with latest production technologies, and farmers training is imperative to incentivize crop adoption for farmers. Ensuring profitable purchase of soybean at farmer-end to favor local production and discourage imports will help agro-industry to tap burgeoning demands of soybean and enable exports. Area under soybean cultivation in Pakistan is negligible and no contribution in edible oil and soya meal production. Importance of soybean and its products and recipes need to revive, promoted and explored the full potential for improving yield and quality in two suitable districts of Punjab at pilot scale which will also increase our domestic oil supply and livelihood improvement of farmers. Soybean production from seed to harvest will be optimized along with development of a mini thresher which is highly desired by farming community. Soybean elite varieties with higher potential and well adapted to local environment will be given to trained contract farmers and a production training manual will be developed too. Fortified Soymeal will be prepared as poultry feed integral component for poultry industry.
