data.projectName: Experimental and Computational study of cyclically loaded reinforced concrete knee joint
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Few researchers experimentally examined the seismic efficiency of RC joints under different axial loads. The experimental results revealed that seismic reactions in axial loads of RC beam-column joints were greatly affected by axial load variability, contributing to a significant reduction in strength and ductility of RC knee joint.
The nonlinear characteristics of the joint rotational spring were determined on the basis of mechanics principles and a semi-empirical analytical model. The analytical beam-column joint model presented by this research and study will be ideal for hand calculations to estimate joint shear potential without the need for a special software system and can therefore be easily used in practical applications. The validation of this analytical model will be then carried out by comparing its results with experimental and numerical results.

data.projectName: AFFLATOXIN M1 IN HUMAN BREAST MILK
data.projectDigest:
Breast milk is believed to be the ideal food for the infant. However, in addition to its nutritionally and immunologically beneficial components, trace amounts of carcinogenic compounds Aflatoxin (AFSs) have been observed in human milk. Children are highly susceptible population group for exposure to environmental toxicants for a variety of reasons; therefore, early child hood exposure to the carcinogenic aflatoxin may be critical determinants of later health effects. Aflatoxins are highly toxic secondary metabolites produced by several Aspergillus and Penicillium spp. Aflatoxin M1 (AFM1), the major metabolite of aflatoxin B1 (AFB1), is classified by the International Agency of Research on Cancer (IARC) as class 2B, possible human carcinogens. The exposure of infants to AFM1 is of concern as AFM1 has been found to be carcinogenic in a number of species; the evidence for pre-natal and post-natal effects on health of human could be one of the factors contributing to growth faltering and/or the early onset of hepatocellular carcinoma countries with a high incidence of the disease. Recent reports have already indicated the detection of AFM1 in dairy milk and human breast milk in different countries. 
The aim of this study was to determine the prevalence of AFM1 in breast milk samples from Karachi. This study is the first to examine the levels of Aflatoxin in breast milk samples in Pakistan. The data of the current study will serve as a baseline of exposure patterns and levels, for which a longitudinal assessment of Aflatoxin exposure and infant health can be conducted.

data.projectName: Multifunctional structural hybrid supercapacitor based polymer composites for electrical energy storage applications
data.projectDigest: Herein, we report our endeavor in providing a proof-of-concept addressing the question of how a carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) composite could be fabricated in a hybrid supercapacitor configuration while imparting the necessary mechanical properties to meet the efficient energy needs of future vehicles. These multifunctional hybrid supercapacitors will permit for full incorporation of the energy storage systems into the electric vehicle structural load paths. Simultaneously the need for traditional batteries and supercapacitors will significantly fall, allowing the total weight of future vehicles to be reduced further. The prospective applications are several and diverse; fundamentally any load-carrying part in a set-up that desires electrochemical energy. These devices can potentially ensure considerable weight and volume savings and offer huge benefits in aerospace, increasingly in automotive parts, mobile phones, laptops, and other electronic gadgets, sporting goods, marine applications, and civil engineering structures, oil, gas and chemical industries, power generation, energy supplies for emergency equipment and in the defense sector. This research has the potential to accelerate supercapacitor market growth with industry uptake driven by weight reductions and the opportunity to take advantage of first-mover pricing and greater profit margins.

data.projectName: Enhancing  growth and yield of tomatoes by  application of fish and star fruit emulsions for sustainable agriculture under drought and salt stress environments’’
data.projectDigest: Tomato is major vegetable crop consumed globally second to potatoes and main source of vitamins A, C, E, other nutritional compounds and minerals useful for the protection of body against diseases.  So its demand becoming increasing in the international market by increasing population. However, Its production is under threat from both  biotic and abiotic stresses which has profound adverse effects on its quality and quantity. To enhance  its growth and yield , especially  from drought/salt hit areas different biotechnological and chemical approaches which are not Eco-friendly are being utilized.  It is the dire need to develop environmental friendly technologies to meet the needs of nutrition, food, feed and fibre for enhancing human population pressure especially developing countries like Pakistan where, shortage of water, saline barren lands and use of chemicals/fertilizers are main problems facing to agricultural lands.  Present studies will be carried out in labs and  pots/fields in natural environments to enhance the  growth and yield of tomatoes by the use of different dilutions of fish and star fruit emulsions as fertigation and foliar application under drought/saline conditions. The fish emulsion contains large number of NPK (5:1:1) and other trace elements.  The completely randomized design will used and data will be analyzed by appropriate statistical analysis. Organic technologies will be introduced; the farmers and students will be skilled for these tactics to enhance the crop productivity especially to produce organic vegetables.

data.projectName: A Novel Approach of Abstractive Simplification: A Tool to Summarize and Simplify Scientific Literature for Pakistani Masses using Deep Learning and Big Data
data.projectDigest: Researchers, students, and professionals, in general, have a fundamental need to study existing domain-specific work to produce innovative and productive solutions, enabling societal progress. To study domain-specific work, a non-domain expert must employ a domain-specific expert to breakdown the technical terminology into a simplified summary. While some primitive tools exist to provide manually converted understandable summary documents for scientific/technical articles, or the translation of technical terminology, to this date, there is no such automated tool that can conveniently convert any provided scientific/technical literature into an easily understandable and readable summary text. Note that text simplification and text summarization are related, but different sub-tasks in Natural Language Generation. Whereas summarization attempts to reduce the length of a document, while keeping the original meaning, simplification attempts to reduce the complexity of a document. In this work, we combine both the tasks of summarization and simplification using a novel hybrid architecture of abstractive and extractive summarization. We propose to adapt the pointer generator model for the combined task of summarization and simplification. In addition, we propose to build a tool to Summarize and Simplify Scientific Literature for Pakistani Masses by leveraging the power of Deep Learning and Big Data.

data.projectName: Development of Next Generation Antivenom in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Snakebite is a known public health hazard. The threat is endemic widely in rural settings and affects about 5 million human populations each year. This resulted in 3 million envenomings with 125,000 casualties on annual basis which are 5% of mortality rate. The World Health Organization (WHO) enlisted snakebite envenomation in Neglected Tropical Diseases (NTD) in 2017. Pakistan is enlisted in snakebite envenomation with having 4-7 different types of snakes that induces about 20,000 annual mortality cases. Medically significant snakes in Pakistan are Cobra, Russell-Viper and Krait. The only available strategy being used for treatment is the administration of antisera raised against snake venoms. These antisera are monoclonal or polyclonal. Structurally, in a unit volume, the whole antisera contain various types of biological ingredients and as a result the effective and cross reactive proteins (immunoglobulins) against snake venom are lesser in quantity. Moreover, the production time of antisera is higher and resulted quantity is minimal. The cost to maintain this antiserum production is much higher. Due to all these factors, the quality and quantity of produced antisera is compromised. The recombinant technology opens new avenues in the formulation and production of recombinant anti-venoms. Through this technology, we will be able to produce recombinant anti-venom protein(s) (Immunoglobulin(s)) in a plasmid vector(s). This is a laboratory based anti-venom production strategy. This strategy is combatable to enhance timely availability of effective anti-venoms in the country.

data.projectName: Exome Sequencing and Neurofeedback Intervention in Autism Spectrum Disorders
data.projectDigest:
Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is neurodevelopmental delay disorder, ensues in childhood. The precise cause of ASD is not known. It is hypothesized that genetic mutations are associated with autism. In addition, cognitive dysfunctions in ASD may respond to Neurofeedback therapy. Furthermore, autistic kids may suffer from gastrointestinal symptoms through the gut brain axis interaction. The gut microbiota is also reported to play a role in the pathophysiology of ASDs. 
We will be doing the Neurofeedback (NFB) therapy intervention in order to check the alleviating symptoms of ASD along with tracing brain electrical activity (EEG). Moreover, the genetic analysis of the participants and their gut microbiota will be carried out simultaneously for mutations. In addition, EEG changes, cognitive functions and blood markers in different genetic mutations in ASD will be determined along with the effect of NFB on these markers and cognitive functions of autistic children.

data.projectName: Determination and risk assessment of pesticides in human/animal blood and water samples through flow injection with spectrophotometric and chemiluminescence detection.
data.projectDigest: The population of the world is increasing and everyone is in struggle to set higher standards of life. To make available food and provide hygienic life style for increasing population is a great global challenge. To accomplish these objectives, the use of pesticides is necessary in urban and rural areas. Pakistan is an agricultural country and numerous pesticides are being used without any check. Pesticides are the cause of several lethal diseases and to monitor the levels of such toxicants in various samples is a great task for analytical chemists. This proposal describes the establishment of flow injection chemiluminescence, spectrophotometric and liquid core waveguide spectrophotometric methods for analyses of varieties of widely employed pesticides. These novel methods will be applied to human and animal blood samples as well as water samples. The above-mentioned analytical techniques are associated with numerous advantages especially the lower limits of detection below the permissible levels of pesticides in the samples. Furthermore, the toxicological effects of the evaluated pesticides will also be assessed in general population of the country.

data.projectName: Investigating the Response of Nano-Modified Concrete Structures
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: The development of concrete structures in Pakistan is a dominant highlight of today’s domestic construction industry. The built environment deteriorates and fails under a variety of scenarios, ranging from design inadequacies to construction lapses. Significant research has been carried out to develop  composite concrete mixes to accommodate post-construction performance lapses, but due to the rigidity of current design standards, these advancements are far from integrated.  The scope of this research aims to reduce to potential for rehabilitation of our infrastructure and accommodate all advancements in smart concrete mixes by developing a comparative computational framework for the design and optimization of “Micro-enhanced Concrete Structures”.

data.projectName: Microbial ACC-deaminase for improving sorghum quality by reducing drought mediated cyanogenic-glucosides
data.projectDigest: Drought-stress causes more than 50% losses in crop yield under arid and semiarid conditions . It  triggers ethylene production many folds that hampers growth, yield and quality of crops. During the enzymatic conversion of 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylic acid (ACC) to ethylene, cyanogenic-glucoside is formed that is converted into cyanide in ruminants. Cyanide blocks the fourth step in the mitochondrial electron transport chain, resulting in the arrest of aerobic metabolism and death from histotoxic anoxia. ACC-deaminase is the enzyme present in some strains of plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) that can improve growth and quality of crops by lowering the ACC, a precursor of ethylene and cyanide. Several PGPR strains will be isolated and screened from sorghum rhizosphere based on ACC-deaminase production and drought-tolerant assay. Drought-tolerant ACC-deaminase containing strains will be tested for growth promotion of sorghum under gnotobiotic drought-stressed conditions. Potential strains and their combination will be evaluated to improve growth, yield and quality of sorghum crop under drought-stressed pot and field conditions. Based on results, best isolates will be formulated into a novel biofertilizer that can increase the yield by enhancing the growth and can improve the quality of sorghum by reducing the toxic HCN production under drought-stressed conditions.

data.projectName: Reinforcing demand for sustainable energy products & promoting energy conservation behaviour using social Marketing in Larkana district of Sindh
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Zulfikar Ali Bhutto Institute of Science & Technology (SZABIST) University, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Energy plays a pivotal role in economic development. Energy is one of key factors for achieving sustainable socio-economic goals. Pakistan is facing energy shortfall for last many year. The energy crisis in Pakistan cost huge to national economy. The evidence also shows that globally energy is major contributor for climate change. This study will use two pronged strategy to address clean and environment friendly energy goals and to address supply-demand issues. The clean energy goals and supply-demand gap can be narrow down with the use of sustainable energy products. Therefore, this study contributes to create demand for sustainable energy conservation products and creation of sustainable energy consumption culture in Larkana district. A baseline study will be conducted to know current use of sustainable energy consumption products in phase 1. This study will use longitudinal experimental design methodology using activity theory, a progeny of group dynamics, to achieve study objectives. Social marketing’s group centered approaches will be used to bring sustained behaviour change. The outcome of experimental interventions will be compared with baseline results. The outcome of study would contribute to achieve many of national and two of SDGs goals. The results will also identify implications for policymakers, and key stakeholders.

data.projectName: Stop Crimes by Linking the Unlinked Crime-related Social Data
data.piUniversity: National University of Computer and Emerging Sciences, Islamabad
data.projectDigest: This project proposes a framework that will link crime related information from various sources such as news reports, blogs and social data into a knowledge system based on Linked Open Data (LOD) framework. The LOD framework, which is the basis for semantic web, would enable the data to be shared for a multitude of applications such as crime pattern visualizations, detecting crime trends and various types of prediction models. As the second phase of this project, a model will be developed to profile the likely characteristics of the perpetrator/s of a crime.  The first phase of the project will involve designing a knowledge representation framework using LOD ontology.  This ontology will then be populated using natural language processing techniques with information contained in text documents, news reports and social media blogs. The knowledgebase can then be exposed via SPARQL interface to various stakeholders which may include restricted access to general public as well.

data.projectName: SEAD – A Localized Clinical Decision Support Systems for Early and Accurate Diagnosis of Cardiovascular Diseases using Artificial Intelligence
data.projectDigest: This project aims to develop a similar intelligent platform capable of integrating different types of data to offer a simple, proactive approach to deal with cardiovascular diseases, starting with myocardial infraction. It will be based on large-scale processing and novel predictive computer modeling of a variety of anamnestic and instrumental data on patients to predict myocardial infraction at an early stage. The outcome of the project will be a clinical decision support system for the diagnosis of myocardial infraction which can be used as an additional guide by the clinicians within Pakistan in the future.

data.projectName: Ensuring health and food safety: Bio-accumulation and Sustainable treatment of heavy metals
data.projectDigest: There is no organized and scientific way to manage and to reduce the practices of wastewater irrigation and the wastewater management is insufficient and sporadic. There is a dire need for proper monitoring and sustainable treatment of soil irrigated with wastewater. On the other hand, there is a big gap between increase safe food demands and decrease in the quantity and quality of surface water resources in Pakistan. The health risk assessment of this unsanitary practice is important for understanding any serious health threats. This research project addresses the overall pollution of heavy metals in peri-urban soil, foodstuff, bioaccumulation in human blood, and potential human health risks in Pakistan particularly in areas of high anthropogenic pressure. Biochar (BC) is often studied as a soil improver that can fix heavy metals in the soil. This research project also addresses the conversion of agricultural waste into so-called biochar (coal). Additionally, the produced biochar has to be environmentally friendly, locally made and renewable. Finally, the biochar from agricultural waste will contribute to the affordable and sustainable treatment of soil on one hand, and the valorization of waste management and reduction of waste disposal on the other hand.

On the other hand, there is a big gap between increase safe food demands and decrease in the quantity and quality of surface water resources in Pakistan. This research project addresses the overall pollution of heavy metals in peri-urban soil, foodstuff, bioaccumulation in human blood, and potential human health risks in Pakistan particularly in areas of high anthropogenic pressure. Biochar (BC) is often studied as a soil improver that can fix heavy metals in the soil. This research project also addresses the conversion of agricultural waste into so-called biochar (coal). Additionally, the produced biochar has to be environmentally friendly, locally made and renewable. Finally, the biochar from agricultural waste will contribute to the affordable and sustainable treatment of soil on one hand, and the valorization of waste management and reduction of waste disposal on the other hand.

data.projectName: High-k based optimal surface passivation schemes for next generation silicon solar cells
data.projectDigest:
In photovoltaic market, low cost, reliable, and efficient silicon solar cells are of high demand. Generally, the efficiency of Si solar cells is limited by recombination of photogenerated carriers at the silicon surface. Therefore, tackling this issue has strong potential in improving the performance of solar cells through various techniques. One way to reduce the surface recombination is to cover it with a capping layer which may also act as absorbing, as well as protective layers, such as high-k dielectrics. 
The main object of this project is to grow high-k dielectric films to enhance the efficiency of solar cells by surface passivation. For this purpose, we will grow nanoscale films of Al2O3, HfO2 and their stacks on Si by magnetron sputtering. High-k dielectric films will be characterized by different materials characterization techniques. High quality grown films will be deposited on the available industrial silicon solar cells (or on research grade cells available through international  collaborative projects). The efficiency of resultant devices will be evaluated by power conversion efficiency and incident photon conversion efficiency.
PI and Co-PI are already working on an international project of solar cells, which is a joint initiative of Pakistan Science Foundation and The Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey. The present project is strongly related to it. Another related project from Swedish Research Council is recently won by both partners of present project. 
In present project, Co-PI will support in providing the characterization facilities at his institute to execute project successfully.  The key output of this project by funding of HEC is the establishment of lab at host university where no lab for scientific research is available.

data.projectName: Surface Water Treatment using Plant-based Coagulants: Sustainable solution for developing countries
data.projectDigest: Surface water is an important source of water supply around the world. Typical surface water ?treatment employs coagulation as an essential step to remove colloidal impurities. Natural plant-based ?materials are being explored as alternatives to the conventional chemical coagulants, as chemical ?coagulants are disadvantageous in certain aspects. However, the studies pertaining to plant-based ?coagulants are of preliminary nature at the moment and contains certain gaps that hinders their ?widespread applicability. This project is an effort to identify local plant-based materials as potential ?coagulants, covering the identified gaps in literature. At its essence, this is an effort to provide an eco-?friendly and sustainable alternative for surface water treatment for the rural and remote ?communities. To achieve the objectives of project, plant-based coagulants will be selected through ?comprehensive screening process. The selected coagulants will be evaluated in detail for their ?capability to remove pollutants from surface water samples. Outcomes of this project will represent ?vital advancement in sustainable environmental technology as the plant-based coagulants are ?renewable resources. Their application is linked to the improvement of quality of life for ?underdeveloped communities which is a contribution to one of the UN’s Sustainable Development ?Goal “To provide safe and affordable drinking water for all”. ?

data.projectName: Evaluation of Genetic Determinants of Infertility Disorder through Next Generation Sequencing, Bioinformatics and Experimental Assays in Pakistani Female Population
data.projectDigest: Female infertility is defined as the failure to conceive naturally within 1 year for women younger than 35 years, within 6 months for women older than 35 years or carry a pregnancy to full term. A number of factors including genetic, hormonal, or environmental factors are involved to cause infertility. Nearly 50% of cases of infertility are due to genetic defects. At present only few genes have been shown to cause or to be strongly associated with infertility. In the present project, consanguineous families affected with infertility, will be sampled from different regions of Pakistan. A standard fertility evaluation which includes physical exams, medical and sexual histories of both partners will be performed. In addition family pedigree analysis will be done. The data will be analyzed to establish the diagnosis and inheritance pattern and will be followed by comparison with reported cases in various databases of several known infertility cases. These families will first be analyzed on a molecular level in Pakistan using sequencing of previously reported candidate genes and regulatory elements. Patients/families where known candidate genes or regulatory elements have been excluded will be screened using massively parallel sequencing. Candidate mutations will be followed up using various computational and experimental technologies

data.projectName: Heavy metal toxicity in economicaly important plants of the Punjab region
data.projectDigest: nvironmental pollution is a serious issue which creates a serious menace to crop plants of different regions. It is increasing day after day at a rapid rate due to shifting of rural population to urban population. Untreated city effluents, domestic wastesand industrial sewage water is polluting the environment, which eventually enters the food chain and adversely affected the plant efficiency and ultimately the human health. Tolerance mechanism in plants is highly reviewed  and It is necessary to inspect about the interactions between plant and metals as a proof to safety of our environment and also have acquaintance about the risks to our food chain due to the preface of these heavy metals. Highly economical important plant species  present in the contaminated soils and wet lands of different regions of Punjab, ranging from tropical thorn forest of the Punjab plain, bela forest and riverain along the rivers and desert of Thar, Rajanpur and Cholistan to the altitude of Murree region, sub-mountainous region of Kala-Chitta, Sulaman and the Salt Range. The level of heavy metals (Cd, Ni and Zn) in plant species collected from different areas along with the soil and water specimens will be checked, and its affect will be observed to withdraw the correlation among the anatomical parameters under normal and effluent affected areas and to explore the physiological indicators for further research programmes.

data.projectName: Stable cell lines Generation for the Production and Purification of Recombinant Human Erythropoietin (SGPPrhEPO)
data.projectDigest:
Erythropoietin is a hormone normally produced from the kidney and in bone marrow it stimulate the production of red blood cells. Its deficiency causes anemia especially in renal patient. Before the availability of recombinant erythropoietin (Lab made), renal patient required regular blood transfusion and blood transfusion is associated with several risks e.g. haemolytic and allergic reaction, transmission of blood borne diseases. Thus, blood transfusion should be avoided whenever possible and erythropoietin is the best alternative for blood transfusion. Erythropoietin is a tested and effective treatment for the anemia. Availability of recombinant human erythropoietin (rhEPO) in the market eliminate the need blood transfusion Currently, rhEPO has not only been used for the treatment of anaemia associated with renal failure but it is also used to treat the anemia associated with cancer, Hepatitis C, HIV and cardiac diseases. 
The purpose of this study is to compare the two erythropoietin producing systems to develop a better model system for its production. We are spending lot of money to import this important drug. This study is a preliminary step to develop a technology in Pakistan for erythropoietin hormone production.

data.projectName: Synthesis and Applications of Edible Coatings from Natural Sources and their Shelf Life Studies
data.projectDigest:
Use of plastic packaging materials has various drawbacks like generation of wastes related with these materials as Petroleum derived plastics produce severe environmental issues, that’s why alternate feasible solution must be found. To achieve this purpose, biodegradable/edible packaging for food products is a successful choice to resolve the issues resulting from discarding traditional packaging materials. Moreover, oxidation is one of the main reasons of quality loss in foodstuffs. Therefore, the harmful impacts can be delayed by using the active packaging containing antioxidants. Active packaging innovation is intended to expand shelf life of food, sustaining the sensory quality antimicrobial and nutritional properties. Apple containing the high levels of antioxidants which provide protection against cancer is an incredible source of essential vitamins and nutrients for humans. Food industries, particularly those related with the production of squeezed apple and dried apple businesses generate heaps of waste from apples' skin. Green apple is less susceptible to browning and oxidation as well as it has higher values of juiciness therefore it is most suitable as compared to other species. Eatable film coating can be applied on numerous items to control gas exchange, oxidation processes and moisture transfer. The major advantage of edible coatings is that these are viable means of incorporation of several food additives and substances to enhance foods texture, flavour and colour ,to control microbial development, to contribute against the deteriorating agents as well as to increase the sensory, nutritional and safety attributes.   
 In this research, food?grade biomacromolecules, in addition to fruits and vegetables, will be used for edible packaging.

data.projectName: Cultivation of Oyster Mushroom (Pleurotus spp.) for Growth of Cottage Industry in Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Mushroom is a spore that affects the body of a fungus commonly known as Khumbi. Mushroom crops can be propagated in two ways: open-air farming and controlled farming.
In the open air they grow naturally in manure piles and dump locations in fields, timber, forests, water channels, manure piles, alliances and grasslands or plains, hilly and coastal areas of Pakistan.
Mushroom is an indoor cultivated crop and can be easily grown on industrial and agricultural wastes, the crop can be easily grown in any area under controlled conditions of light, humidity and temperature.
Land is not required for farming and can be grown as a part-time activity in small houses and huts that do not require full-time labor, and all family members can easily handle various tasks. After seven days of cultivation, small pin-like heads emerge from the mushroom, which after three to five days turn into more mushrooms. A single flush or branch of a mushroom can release half a kilogram of (edible) foods after each week for three months.
Mushrooms are cultivated in more than 100 countries worldwide. The growth rate of mushroom is increasing from 6% to 7% annually. Currently, Europe, America and East Asia contribute about 96% of world mushroom demand. However, with the general increase in income levels worldwide, the demand for mushrooms is sure to increase in other parts of the world as well.
The role played by women in rural mushroom production can be very significant. Certain parts of the
mushroom cultivation process, such as filling substrates in containers and harvesting, are ideally suited
for women’s participation. Several programmes have enhanced women’s empowerment through mushroom production by giving them the opportunity to gain farming skills, financial independence
 and self respect.

data.projectName: Supercritical fluid pathway to liquefaction of aquatic biomass for the production of bio-crude and valuable bio-chemicals
data.projectDigest: Biomass being the oldest fuel in the known history of mankind has almost been thoroughly replaced by fossil fuels as a sole source of energy production for more than a century. However recently, the quest for alternative to petroleum resources has increased exponentially because of the diminishing petroleum reserves, ever-increasing demand of energy in the modern world, and environmental concerns raised about the utilization of fossil fuels contributing to greenhouse gases. Different types of biomasses are being explored as alternative to crude petroleum based on three major criteria; abundance, economy, and environment. First and second generation of biomass feedstock are under direct criticism because of food vs fuel controversy. Third generation of biomass which is primarily the “wastes” seem to be an ideal feedstock for energy production as it presents an efficient solution of waste disposal at the same time. Conversion of this biomass into bio-based energy products (bio-oil and bio-chemicals) requires an efficient, low cost and environmentally friendly pathway to explore its full potential. There have been a number of studies on utilization of water as a solvent at high temperature and high pressure for the conversion of algal biomass. Similarly, other organic solvents like alcohols, tetraline, acetone etc. have also been used for algal biomass conversion to crude bio-oil using thermal route. This study proposes a combination of optimum mixture of alcohol-water system for conversion of algal biomass to bio-based energy product including bio-gas, bio-crude and bio-char.

data.projectName: Analysis of the Fear of Terrorism and Extremism on the University Campuses
data.projectDigest: Terrorism disturbs social integration. Terrorism as violent act harms individuals and communities socially and psychologically. People of different social, political and religious backgrounds become of the multiple factors in society become motivated and become involved in terrorist and extremist activities in Sindh and Pakistan. Terrorism therefore by harming social groups cripples social development and disturbs national harmony and internal peace by creating terrorist and extremist insecurities. Perceptions and emotional reactions of people play important role to understand and devise policies to control and prevent terrorism. This qualitative study based on semi-structured interviews collects views and perceptions about how terrorism and terrorist attacks influence people’s social and psychological wellbeing. Criminologists and social scientists have attempted to understand the fear of crime and violence around the world, But in Pakistan there is almost no serious attention paid to examine the fear of crime and terrorism. No developed understanding about such serious issue encourages criminologists to study it in Pakistani context by Pakistani criminologists. It is expected that understanding of this problem will provide better insights to understanding terrorism and, in particular, how people react to this violent act. In addition, by learning from such studies, Pakistan will have better and fresh understanding to devise policies to strengthen social conditions and prevent terrorist and extremist conflicts between social groups.

data.projectName: MOLECULAR SURVEILLANCE, ECONOMIC IMPACT AND RESEARCH BASED CONTROL OF NEOSPORA CANINUM ASSOCIATED ABORTIONS IN DAIRY AND BEEF CATTLE FROM PUNJAB, PAKISTAN
data.projectDigest:
Cattle farming is very economical business and considered as major source of livelihood for livestock farmers in Pakistan.  They are reared mainly for milk, meat and hides. Cattle milk and meat is very important to meet the challenges of food scarcity. However the major constraint to livestock industry in Pakistan are abortions/reproductive disorders due to Neospora caninum that may cause both direct and indirect economic implications. The direct losses include fetal loss, reproductive problems, reduced milk production, reduced growth/feed efficiency and value of breeding stock. Potential indirect losses are professional costs and costs associated with diagnoses, rebreeding, increased lactation time. In order to fulfill the per capita milk, meat and their by product demand of growing population, there is a dire need to identify such issues through surveillance, their exact economic impact and control by the implementation of preventive measures.
In this proposal three studies will be conducted. Study 1; initial screening and molecular surveillance of Neospora caninum infection will be conducted. Study 2; the estimation of economic impact of neosporosis will be calculated by record keeping and epidemiological reporting system. Study 3; cohort study will be conducted to evaluate the major risk factors and development of affective preventive levels.

data.projectDigest: Strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa Duch.) belonging to family Rosaceae is one of the most delicious fruit with sweet flavour. It is getting high economic importance now-a-days due to its nutritional value, colour and taste. These small berries serve as a natural source of different minerals, vitamin C and also rich in antioxidants. Besides antioxidants, fruits of strawberry are rich in calcium, potassium, phosphorus, fibre and riboflavin. Because of high nutritional contents and economic importance, research institutes are developing new cultivars which are high yielding and more resistant to various biotic and abiotic stresses. In Pakistan, strawberry is grown in different areas of KPK, Punjab and Sindh. Until now, ‘Chandler’ is the only cultivars commercially cultivated throughout Pakistan. It is transplanted through runners. Since, climate of Punjab and Sindh is not suitable for nursery production, runners are mainly sourced from either Mingora or Dir districts. Nursery development in AJK has not yet been started at commercial level, but preliminary studies in district Poonch have shown good results in terms of strawberry plant health and runner production capacity. So far, no detailed studies have been conducted to explore suitability of different areas of district Poonch for nursery production of different strawberry cultivars. Moreover, commercial farming systems in district Poonch currently lacks strawberry fruit production but there seems huge potential in strawberry fruit production because strawberry fruit harvest in district Poonch starts after it’s over in Punjab and Sindh provinces. data.projectName: A Massively Parallel Processing Framework for Stereo based Digital Surface Model Generation
data.projectDigest: Stereo vision is a process of extracting 3-dimensional information from digital images by means of multiple cameras placed at prevalence points. It has received overwhelming attention of the computer vision and photogrammetry research community in the last few decades, still however, there remains an outstanding concern with most of its matching algorithms, namely: accuracy-time contradiction. While the safety-critical systems, such as self-driving cars, demand (almost) perfect accuracy, the stereo matching algorithms converge at a considerable computation cost. Therefore, such systems tend to compromise on accuracy for real-time response, which may be life threatening. Recently, it has been argued that such algorithms – involving certain iterative components – are not suitable for parallel processing GPU architectures. This work is intended to contradict this argument by proposing a method for: 1) optimal mapping of pixels on a massively parallel processing architecture, 2) optimal sizing of adaptive aggregation window including only the essential pixels. The objective of this work, therefore, is to exploring ways in which these algorithms may be divided into as many concurrent components as possible, and designing a suitable parallel processing architecture, which should be able to perform image mapping in real-time. In addition to the applications stated above, our results will be useful for the meteorological department for automated landslide and glacier monitoring in the northern areas of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Curricular Reform at Secondary School Level for Skill Based Education
data.projectDigest: More than 30 percent of population of Pakistan is under the age of 15 years. This is a significant number of school age individuals for whom we need to plan a curriculum that prepares them for future job market. Currently a student who passes secondary school certificate is not equipped with any practical skill and cannot enter or create a job for himself/herself. If we prepare our youth effectively we can not only fulfill the requirement of trained manpower in Pakistan but can also capture the global job-market. In the past whenever such initiatives were introduced, the local disparities were never taken into account, and uniform approach was adopted across the country. Therefore the proposed study will identify the skill set relevant to local industry, agriculture, arts, crafts, trades and occupations.  Get these skill-sets prioritized for inclusion /integration in mainstream secondary school curriculum at 36 districts of Punjab. Develop short courses and pilot them in one district. Having a realistic data of one district after implementation, the researchers will be able to propose a strategic plan for all other districts of Punjab.  This initiative shall not only develop human resource but also strengthen the local industry, agriculture, arts and crafts.

data.projectName: Ethnopharmacological exploration of district Mianwali for Gynecological disorders.
data.piUniversity: Lahore College for Women University, Lahore
data.projectDigest: The females of rural areas are deprived of health care facilities. Major health concerns of females are related to reproductive cycle including menstruation, pregnancy and menopause. On this account, the incidence of breast cancer and other gynecological diseases in Pakistan is 2.5 times more than in other countries of Asia such as Iran and India. Pakistani women 50 out of 100,000 as compared to Indian women is on the risk of cancer. The rural women primarily utilize medicinal plants and plant-derived medicinal products to treat the ailments. Different plants have been used indigenously to cure one disease or to cure different diseases at the same time. Therefore, it is essential for drug discovery to record and preserve the traditional knowledge of medicinal plants, that mostly depends on local practitioners and field surveys. Mianwali is south western part of Punjab with diversity of topography and flora. Flora is unique due to its location, climate and soil. The aim of this work was to provide an overview of information on traditional information related to ethnopharmacology related to gynecologic disorders to demonstrate therapeutic potential of plants and support future research in the drug discovery.

data.projectName: Enhancing productivity of wheat on salt-affected soils by integrated use of silicon and biochar
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: Salinity is one of the major threats to global food security. In Pakistan, about 6.3 million hectares (mha) of land is salt affected with 4000 hectares affected by salinity every year. Salinity damages the plants via osmotic stress and ion imbalance. Silicon and biochar amendment could alleviate the negative impacts of salt stress in crop plants. However, their combined effects on mitigating salinity stress in crop plants and on physical and chemical properties of salt-affected soil remain unknown. This project will focus on synergistic use of silicon and biochar for mitigation of salinity stress in wheat and their effect on physical and chemical properties of saline soil. Biochar will be produced and characterized in lab for various physical and chemical traits. Screening of silicon and biochar levels will be carried out in controlled conditions for plant growth promotion of wheat under salt stress. The selected levels of silicon and biochar will be used in combination for improving growth and yield of wheat under natural saline conditions in pot and field experiments. The silicon and biochar will be evaluated for inhibiting sodium uptake, regulating the antioxidant metabolism, chlorophyll synthesis, nutrient uptake, and growth and yield of wheat. The soil samples will be collected before and after the experiments to study the effect of silicon and biochar application on physical and chemical properties of saline soil. The successful completion of proposed work will lead to the development of eco-friendly and cost effective technology for enhancing crop productivity under salinity stress and for maximizing the utilization of salt-affected soils.

data.projectName: Lung Cancer Detection from CT Scan using Machine Learning
data.projectDigest: Early detection of lung cancer is extremely vital in its treatment but there are a lot of hindrances that are faced by doctors in diagnosing this lethal disease. The first and foremost, as in any medical diagnosis system is the accuracy. Only a few experience radiologists have the expertise to accurately differentiate between malignant and benign tumors. Moreover, it takes almost 1.5 to 2 hours for a panel of radiologists to view the CT image and conclude results. This poses a serious threat of time constraint during diagnosis. The availability of resources is also an important issue in this regard. Hence, in order to address all these issues, an efficient and accurate lung cancer Computer Aided Design (CAD) system is the need of the hour. With an efficient system, it will be able to provide fast diagnosis with accurate results that will quicken the pace of treatment if the need arises. The figures depicted shows how the cancer formed in lungs.

data.projectName: Design and Development of a Left Ventricular Assist Device
data.projectDigest: Heart diseases are one of the leading cause of mortality worldwide.  During end stage heart failure only viable treatment option is heart transplant, but due to shortage of donor heart it is impossible for every patient to get it. In such a case Mechanical Circulatory Support (MCS) device emerge a a vial able alternative. Left Ventricular Assist Device (LVAD) is used to support the pumping of original heart. LVAD take blood from apex of left ventricle and deliver it to the aorta. But due to high cost the existing devices are not affordable for our common fellow citizen. The purpose of this project is to build a first LVAD device in Pakistan which not only reliable but also cheap.  The current phase of the project will deal with design, analysis, manufacturing and in-vitro evaluation of the device.

data.projectName: An Electric Vehicle prototype with an indigenously designed Battery Pack and Battery Management System
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Over the past decade, various initiatives have been taken by the automakers and governments around the world to reduce not only carbon footprint but also unwavering reliance on fossil fuels. Recently, Pakistan’s first ever national Electric Vehicles (EV) policy 2019 have been announced. This policy aims to upgrade about 30% of its road vehicles to EVs by 2030. Mainstream companies such as Volkswagen, Ford, BMW, Mercedes, Toyota and Nissan have started offering a range of different hybrid and electric cars. With other companies like Tesla that are actively pursuing to increase the penetration of electric cars in the automobile markets. All such vehicles performance fundamentally rely on the battery utilization. Majority of automakers now a day have embraced the use of Lithium-Ion batteries for future hybrids and electric vehicles. During the normal operation of an EV, it would be expose to different weather conditions, terrain, loading, charging/discharging and user experience which might stress the EV’s battery pack, thus limiting there expected life and performance. To ensure long life and durability of these battery packs they are integrated with a Battery Management System (BMS) which performances the functions such as monitoring, thermal management, protection and cell balancing. Together, both the battery pack and BMS makes the most vital component of an EV, as it determines the crucial factors such as the range, cost, safety, convenience of recharging the vehicle. This project aims to design and develop this most critical component along with an EV prototype as a testing platform for R&D and a proof of concept for the local investors.

data.projectName: Genetic screening and treatment of metabolic disease in Pakistani origin patients.
data.projectDigest:
A metabolic disorder directs towards the abnormal chemical reactions which change the normal metabolic process in the body. It can also be known as an inherited single gene irregularity, majority with autosomal recessive. Herited metabolic diseases are one ground of genetic disorders and happen when a imperfect gene causes an enzyme deficit. Among the metabolic diseases, obesity is one of the complex and chronic metabolic diseases upsetting the individuals with all the ages including children and adults, ethnicities, nationalities and sexes. 
Obesity has recognized as a disease of global deaths due to its close relationship with a number of comorbid serious health complications. Worldwide, due to high prevalence, there is an expectation that by the year 2030, the obesity epidemic has the strength to influence 1.2 billion people. The etiology of obesity is complex and may be the result of many factors, such as physical activity, nutritional intake, environmental, social structures, metabolic, and genetic factors. Genetic screening of known consanguinity families with severe early-onset obesity has led as a powerful method and important tool of identifying homozygous mutations causing early onset obesity and has enabled the identification of rare damaging variants in monogenes for instance; LEP, LEPR and MC4R.

data.projectDigest: Pesticides play a vital role in agriculture all over the world and are used in excess quantity to protect crops and vegetables from pests. Due to massive use of pesticides, they have adverse effects to human health and other organisms. Most of the peoples are still unknown about their adverse effects on health and linkage of different diseases with these chemicals. Most of the districts of south Punjab have no data about the detected limits of these potential compounds. Further still space for determination of direct exposed community (Peoples directly on farm or living in area) and indirectly exposed (The consumers that receiving the residues in food).In this project a comprehensive survey for pesticide borne disease will be carried out from farming community and the local health department. The samples of blood will be collected with help of health department and diagnostic facilities will be obtained from standard laboratory. Analysis of crop produced (including vegetables and fruits) and water will be carried out using standard analytical procedures with the help of HPLC and GC at UAF Sub-Campus Burewala-Vehari. During this period, different awareness campaign at campus and in this area will be carried out for the education of farming community about the adverse effects of these pesticides including respiratory diseases, immune diseases and cancer. Further different training program will be conducted for proper selection and application of pesticides to avoid the release of these pesticides. A farmer support centre will be established at campus to provide them technical support in case of pesticide selection and proper application methods.

data.projectName: Pressures and pathways for Pakistan’s industrial transformation- A socio-technical transition study
data.projectDigest: This project will lead to an establishment of Pakistan’s first Centre for sustainability studies, namely “Sustainable Development Institute, Pakistan” (S-DIP) at Lahore Business School, University of Lahore. This Centre will be responsible for developing and contributing to Pakistan’s science and technology (innovation) policy. Overall mission of this project is to understand how industrial transformation towards a sustainable and smarter Pakistan’s economy can be fostered. To achieve this, aim of the project is threefold. First, it will investigate the preconditions, drivers and barriers for transformation process towards smarter and sustainable development in significant Pakistan’s economic sectors (this portion of the project/study will be conducted against subject grant). Second, it will address how the growth of new and sustainable industrial niches can be supported by generating new insights into relationship between transformations of existing industries and the development of new niches. These two aims will cumulatively lead to third aim, which is to understand how research and innovation policies can support the development of a smarter and greener Pakistan economy and society

data.projectName: Development of a novel PPG device for the study of non-invasive measurement of cardiovascular diseases
data.projectDigest:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) has seen a rapid growth over the last decade, and the time in which we live today is being called ‘The Golden Age of Artificial Intelligence”. Experts believe that the life in the following twenty years will likely become alien to today’s observer. Increase application of AI in healthcare (diagnosis) is eagerly anticipated, as it will ease the strain on resources, free up time for doctor-patient interactions. A recent study compared the performance of AI in diagnosing disease versus that of healthcare professionals between 2012 and 2019, and found both to be equal.

This study aims to collect various physiological signals from patient suffering from different diseases. The signals will be acquired using both state of the art systems, and low-cost system at the same time. Such a database will be useful in creating new diagnostic models of various disease. As the database will also have physiological signals acquired from low-cost apparatus, the diagnostic models trained on these signals will be much more viable for use in third world countries. The biggest challenge will be the size of database to be collected using standard protocols, as it is one of the most important parameters in accuracy of a trained model.

data.projectName: Physical-Layer Security for IoT based Communications: A Frequency Diverse Array Beamforming Approach
data.projectDigest: An IoT( Internet of Things) design comprises of several inter-linked computing machines, devices, living things and objects with unique identifiers given the ability to transfer data over a network without an essential requirement of human-to-human (H2H) or human-to-computer (H2C) interaction. This yields that the concept behind IoT will certainly advance in communication technology and networking services. Since an IoT system offers enormous association and information-gathering abilities with minimal and/or no human aid. Unfortunately, most of the existing PLS techniques for IoT has so far mainly relied on phased-array (PA) antennas with only-angle dependent beamforming. However, the range-angle dependent beamforming may improve the overall performance.Its main potentials in IoT communication applications are: improvement of signal-to-interference noise ratio (SINR), bit error rate (BER) towards the intended actuators, actuator’s detection and localization along angle and range dependent focusing, tracking of moving actuators’ receivers and guarantee better security than PA systems. On the other hand, multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) designs allow a more antenna elements for transmitting multiple orthogonal signals for multi-user communication applications, which warrants hybridized MIMO-FDA designs for PLS design in IOT based wireless communications.

data.projectName: Genetic markers elucidation for the diagnosis of hereditary male infertility: molecular and functional study approaches
data.projectDigest: Infertility is a social challenge and a source of persistent stress for married couples. Worldwide, 50% of male infertility cases are due to genetic anomalies. However, the already known genetic anomalies still only account for approximately 10% of male infertile cases. Subsequently, investigating genetic factors by utilizing a global, efficient and steadfast approach will be a good practice for the detection of probable mutations across the genome of the infertile males. As a matter of complexity and scarce knowledge of the pathophysiology of male infertility, no Panel molecular diagnostic test is available in Pakistan. The ultimate objective of the study is the development of molecular diagnostic panel and the optimization of the investigation protocol. This will be of great help to clinicians and infertility specialists in the early diagnosis and management of hereditary male infertility in Pakistan. For this the most plausible genetic hot spots will be determined in cases of genetic azoospermia by utilizing Whole Exome Sequencing (WES) and functional studies. WES is a global, reliable and efficient method to identify unknown cause of genetic azoospermia

data.projectName: Genetic and Functional Studies of Neurodevelopmental Disorders in Pakistani Families
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) affect the normal development of nervous system including brain, spinal cord, cerebrum and cerebellum. These disorders create a huge socioeconomic burden on national economy. NDDs are particularly prevalent in under developed countries with inbred populations. Pakistan has one of the highest consanguinity rates with more than half of its population marrying a close relative. Therefore, our population rests at high risk of these disorders. NDDs are incurable, therefore, ‘predict-and-prevent’ is the most viable option to combat them. Identification of causative mutations can build our capacity for screening carriers and pregnancies at risk in future. Since NDDs are genetically heterogeneous and each family has to be investigated for its causative gene. Preliminary investigations of families in our collection have been excluded to most prevalent causative genes which means that as yet undiscovered genetic mutations are underlying the disorder. In this project families will be investigated using different applications of NGS technology to identify causative mutations. Causative genes will be functionally assessed in cell and animal models. This study will provide data for prospective nation-wide carrier screening and prenatal diagnosis of in families at risk. Additionally, mutations identified in this study could be a potential target for precision medicine.

data.projectName: Development of High Performance Nanocomposite Ultrafiltration Membranes for Clarification of Fruit Juices
data.projectDigest: Quality of the fruit juices is affected by the process they are prepared and customers are aesthetically attracted to pleasantly looking color of the fruit juice. This color and quality of fruit juice is controlled by clarification process and ultrafiltration membranes are used for the purpose. However, these membranes have lower life during such processes due to contaminants clogged into their pores (fouling). So, better membranes could be prepared to resist against fouling and these membranes could offer longer operational life and more resistance to the fouling hence saving operational cost with better quality.

data.projectName: Storability of tomatoes in Zero energy cool chamber under passive modified atmosphere packaging.
data.projectDigest: It has been estimated that post-harvest losses cost for more then billion rupees to the economy and reduction in these losses is prerequisite to provide a economic boast to the economy of Pakistan. One of  the major cause is inability of farmers to store fresh produce at farm level with an energy and time efficient manner. In this regard zero energy cool chamber can be a cheap, energy efficient and Eco-friendly approach to mitigate the farm losses especially if use in conjunction with the effective post-harvest treatments and passive modification of produce environment. From decade, fluctuation in tomato price has been considered as a major problem due to its perishable nature which lead to the high percentage of losses. In this project, during first year, zero energy cool chamber will be constructed and optimized for storage of tomatoes with different combination of packaging material, ethylene scavenger, firming and anti-fungal agents to provide an opportunity to increase the storage life by retaining the quality attributes especially with reference to ZECC storage at farm level. Thereafter, in second year, the ZECC will be introduced to the farmers and their feedback will be generated. This will open a new chapter for cheap and effective storage of fresh produce at farm level.

data.projectName: Production of recombinant bioplastic utilizing phaCAB genes from Chelatococcus asaccharovorans
data.projectDigest: Petro-chemical based synthetic plastics are derived from non-renewable dwindling fossil fuels and have vast applications in every sphere of human life. However, most of the plastics or raw material for plastics are imported in Pakistan involving huge amount of foreign exchange. Moreover, plastics are infamous being one of the major contributors of environmental pollution having devastating effect on air, water and land. A variety of plastics are also considered hazardous to human health. One plausible solution to this problem is the use of biodegradable, biocompatible and bioresorbable plastics. However, the cost of production of bioplastics are very high which is a huge hurdle in their commercialization. The bioplastics such as Polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs) are produced by certain microorganisms as part of their metabolism and have similar properties as synthetic plastic polypropylene which is used in making plastic films for packaging, bottles and vast variety of other materials. In current proposal, We shall develop an efficient cost-effective indigenous bio-process for the production of recombinant PHA bioplastic by engineering an industrial friendly microorganism and optimizing the process parameters and study the properties to envisage an industrial process for the plastic manufacturing industries.

data.projectName: Advance search for Trademark Documents using Deep Learning interpretations – Text Classification and Integrating Semantics
data.projectDigest:
A statement regarding trademark judgments quoting and studying procedures are more formal and need for its precision, specification, and easy understanding. There are various types of rulings that establish various interpretations of rules and principles in relevant jurisdictions. The legal statement is a technical work, means that the statement should cover all necessary and legal aspects when it is documented. Therefore, a legal statement is understandable by a legal expert.
To ensure public access the legal documents should be easily understandable and accessible by a general public within the jurisdiction. Therefore, legal documents whether they are defined as a law or the judgments given by a court on trademark cases, should be accessible via modern technology. When the legal documents are in access and understandable to the general public, this will protect the fundamental freedom of a person in accordance with national legislation. Our work is explained in the following;
1.	There is no integration of various sections of documented trademark text because of the information provided in PDF or HTML format. If a search engine is queried, the search engine should intelligently narrow down the results to the end-user.
2.	If a lawyer wants to search for the article numbers according to the judgments in different types of trademark cases, which is also not possible because the judgments in the cases are not categorized accordingly.
3.	If a person wants to know about a similar case that occurred in the past, then there is still a requirement to allow the user to describe or upload their case and find similar results. Therefore, Language Processing techniques required to find the related text.

data.projectName: A metric for calculating the code complexity of solidity based smart contracts
data.projectDigest: The blockchain technology has revolutionized the world with its digital decentralized public ledger. Smart contract based distributed applications have been adopted by different sectors of the society such as finance, health, education, and supply chain. Currently, the worldwide spending on smart contract-based blockchain solutions is estimated at 1.5 billion and is expected to grow even further in the future. Due to this rapid utilization of smart contract-based solution, it is required that there should be a complexity metric that can measure the complexity of blockchain-based applications. Up till now, the object-oriented programming metrics are used to measure the complexity of these applications. However, these object-oriented programming complexity metrics fail to measure the complexity of smart contract-based distributed applications because these metrics only measure the complexity at a single contract level, not on an application-level as a whole. The proposed complexity metric is to quantitatively measure the complexity of the smart contract-based application on a complete application level. It needs to be evaluated using a theoretical framework and a practical case study.

data.projectName: Metal Organic Frameworks as Fluorescence turn-on Sensors for Highly Sensitive and Selective detection of Melamine, Formaldehyde, Cyanuric acid and Urea in Foodstuffs/Tableware
data.projectDigest: Formaldehyde is used to kill fungus, bacteria and germs. It is also used in various chemical processes like resins of phenol-formaldehyde, urea-formaldehyde, melamine-formaldehyde. Melamine-formaldehyde is used for the preparation kitchenware [1]. Milk plays a crucial role in the diet of humans and giving a great economic importance [2]. However, individuals aiming higher profits and flouting ethical values renders milk susceptible to several types of adulteration. Like raising the quantity, increasing the compositional values such as urea, sucrose, and starch as well as increasing the shelf [3]. Increased level of urea causes toxicological hazards [4-5]. Cyanuric acid is used in disinfectants, chlorine stabilizers, sanitizers, and bleaches. The outbreaks of nephrolithiasis and acute kidney injury from several countries during were associated with exposure to melamine and cyanuric acid [6-7]. The production of melamine and cyanuric acid was >2 million tons in 2010 [8]. Up till now there are many analytical methods particularly by  high performance liquid chromatography, fluorescence excitation-emission spectroscopy (EEM) when derivatized with pyronine  in  the  presence  of  phosphoric acid  and  sodium  iodate and electroanalytical are reported for detection of Melamine, Formaldehyde, Cyanuric acid and Urea in different kind of samples [9-11]. The detection and quantitation of these organic pollutants is very importance to various fields including food processing, environmental monitoring, clinical diagnosis, quality control and beverage industries. MOFs and their derivatives due to high surface area, high porosity and controllable structure can perfectly be used as tunable luminescence sensors. Reported method and marketed products are less specific and less sensitive

data.projectName: An Inquiry into the Market and Institutional Policy Constraints to Green Investment and their Policy Solutions: A study of Sindh Province Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The industrial production and progress based on “maximization policy” duly supported by traditional financial system are simply no longer sustainable since it has resulted in extreme ecological imbalance, which in turn  triggered environmental disasters and humanitarian crisis to the level, the world has never witnessed in its history. Consequently, promotion of green financing for protecting environment and ensuring sustainable development has become one of the top priorities of international institutions including United Nations, IMF, IFC, World Bank Group, G-20 Group, and others. Green finance refers to all forms of investment into projects that produce positive environmental impact and promote sustainable development. For Pakistan, access to green finance is central to achieving its targets under Sustainable Development Goals-SDGs initiated by United Nations, and environmental & sustainable development objectives set-forth under Pakistan Vision-2025 agenda. Nonetheless, Green finance is still in its infancy stage across the globe and faces a number of challenges. Using Exploratory Sequential Mixed Method Approach, therefore, this study aims to identify market and institutional constraints to the green investment and the degree to which scheduled banks of Sindh are in compliance with SBP’s Green Business Policy Guidelines. This study will generate market driven solutions and practicable policy interventions for scaling up green investment in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Brucellaphage lysate based therapy to control bovine brucellosis
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
There are huge economic losses in dairy industry due to bovine Brucellosis (Gul et al. 2015). These losses affect the livelihood of poor livestock stakeholders by directly causing infertility, abortions, and poor weight gain in calves and reduced milk production. The indirect losses include no access to international market (trade impeder) limiting economic growth of developing countries (Kaleem et al. 2016)(Basit et al. 2015). 
Furthermore, the animals will remain carrier for transmission throughout their lives. They will be transmitting the disease to their calves trans-placentally leading to infected and weak calves with poor growth. So, there will be a huge loss in culling of the infected animal (Cloete 2017).
This is a zoonotic disease and can be transmitted to human being by the consumption of raw milk or by direct contact with infected animal (aborted fetus, placenta or vaginal discharge) (Kaynak-Onurdag et al. 2016). The burden of the disease to the society includes significant human healthcare cost for diagnosis and treatment. It also includes non-health care cost in public awareness campaign to stop the transmission of the disease. In this way this disease is limiting the socio-economic growth of individuals, communities and nations.
Dairy Industry serves as the bread and butter of a common man, especially in the rural areas of Pakistan. More than 8 million rural families are dependent over dairy business and earn 35% of their total earnings from Dairy industry.
This project will be exploring the potential of brucellaphage lysate-based therapy to control bovine brucellosis and to compare the therapeutic efficacy cocktail (S19 + RB51) lysate, S19 lysate and RB51 lysate (Saxena and Raj 2018). For screening of animals, the Rose Bengal Test (RBT) will be performed

data.projectName: Isolation, characterization and molecular studies of anti-breast cancer secondary metabolites from Pakistani species of Otostegia
data.projectDigest: Breast carcinoma is the second leading cause of death among females. Few treatment options are available for this disease with major limitations of less efficacy, and lack of selectivity and safety. So, there is an urgent need to explore safe and effective therapeutic agents from natural sources for breast cancer. Globally, medicinal plants are the major source for the treatment of breast cancer due to the presence of potent anti-cancer secondary metabolites. Different species of Otostegia are used as folk medicine for the treatment of various diseases including eye complaints, inflammation, wounds, gum disease and anti-cancer. However, literature lacks the scientific investigation of various species of Otostegia for screening and isolation of chemical constituent(s) for anti-breast cancer activity. The initial results of our previous studies have shown that O. limbata extract inhibits the proliferation of breast cancer cells. Therefore, the aim of proposed study is to isolate various chemical constituent(s) from Pakistani species of Otostegia and to evaluate their anti-cancer effects. For this purpose, selected plants will be collected and subjected to extraction (cold maceration) with methanol followed by bio-assay guided fractionation using various solvents with increasing order of polarity. Furthermore, 3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide (MTT) assay will be performed for the preliminary cytotoxicity of crude extracts and their respective fractions. The most active fraction(s) will be subjected to isolation using different chromatographic techniques. The isolated compound(s) will be characterized using different spectroscopic techniques like UV-Visible spectroscopy (UV), infrared spectroscopy (IR), mass spectroscopy (MS) and nuclear magnetic

data.projectName: Secure Communications via Secret Key Generation from Random Wireless Channel Characteristics
data.projectDigest:
Information Security for legitimately communicating nodes requires that they communicate successfully without leaking information to an un-intended recipient. Traditionally, information security has been ensured through computational security methods implemented at higher layers of the protocol stack. These traditional methods assume that the eavesdropping device has a limited computational ability and so it cannot decipher the secret information within reasonable time. These traditional methods also require a supporting infrastructure to distribute the secret encryption key between the legitimate users. However, with ever increasing computational capabilities following the Moore’s law and the advent of new technologies such as quantum computing, the assumption of the eavesdropper’s limited computational ability is being challenged. Furthermore, in many emerging scenarios of wireless communications such as vehicular communications and the internet-of-things, the infrastructure needed for secret key distribution among legitimate users does not scale with the number of these users. To solve these problems, implementing information security at the physical layer emerges as a natural solution by exploiting the wireless channel’s randomness for secret key generation.
The wireless channel between two nodes, when observed at both nodes is theoretically identical if both observations occur within the channel coherence time and over an identical frequency span. This fact can be exploited by the legitimate nodes to generate the same secret key through independent measurements of their common channel, which is conventionally termed the main channel. data.projectName: Re-constructing social order through youth in Pakistan: A way forward to Peace and Harmony
data.projectDigest: Global scenario in post-cold war era and the rise of terrorism has escalated the risk of maneuvering social uprisings and movements with terrorist ideology. This risk raised the probability of leading social / political movements to incite chaos and lawlessness in society because of negative response by many actors. Therefore, this research aims at evaluating the role of youth in re-constructing the social order of Pakistan. By focusing on the role of youth, this study will explore the controllable and uncontrollable variables that can add to the scholarly understanding of this phenomenon. This research also aims at evaluating the array of options that a state might use to deal with forces that can disturb the social order and will analyze the impact of last decade experiences on the Pakistan. This basics research will focus on the youth specifically of students involved in public sector universities (selected), how they can contribute in re-strutting the social order of Pakistan for the promotion of Peace and Harmony

data.projectName: An Empirical Analysis between BISP’s Conditional and Unconditional Cash Transfers: a comparative study of Punjab, Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
This project aims to conduct a comparative analysis between Benazir Income Support Programme’s Unconditional Cash Transfer (UCT) programme and its Co-responsibility Cash Transfer (CCT) programme Waseela-e-Taleem (WeT). A mixed method approach – based on quantitative as well as qualitative data – will be employed to assess the effects of both the interventions individually at first which will later be compared with each other to determine which of the two interventions has had a greater influence and the reasons why it has been more impactful. 
Quantitative evaluation will largely be based on secondary data obtained from BISP along with a household survey. The household survey would target the beneficiary households as well as a control group of non-beneficiary households with BISP poverty scores just above the programme’s eligibility threshold. A distinction in difference approach comparison between the two groups would be employed to evaluate the real impact of each of the interventions on its respective beneficiaries.  The qualitative component, on the other hand, would be used to further expand the quantitative results and to provide a deeper understanding of the context in which the programme is operating.
data.projectSummary:
This project aims to conduct a comparative analysis between Benazir Income Support Programme’s Unconditional Cash Transfer (UCT) programme and its Co-responsibility Cash Transfer (CCT) programme Waseela-e-Taleem (WeT). A mixed method approach – based on quantitative as well as qualitative data – will be employed to assess the effects of both the interventions individually at first which will later be compared with each other to determine which of the two interventions has had a greater influence and the reasons why it has been more impactful. 
Quantitative evaluation will largely be based on secondary data obtained from BISP along with a household survey. The household survey would target the beneficiary households as well as a control group of non-beneficiary households with BISP poverty scores just above the programme’s eligibility threshold. A distinction in difference approach comparison between the two groups would be employed to evaluate the real impact of each of the interventions on its respective beneficiaries.  The qualitative component, on the other hand, would be used to further expand the quantitative results and to provide a deeper understanding of the context in which the programme is operating.
