data.projectName: Study of space weather effects on ionosphere
data.projectDigest:
Space weather is the physical and phenomenological state of natural space environments. The associated discipline aims, through observation, monitoring, analysis and modelling, at  understanding  and  predicting  the  state  of  the  sun,  the  interplanetary  and  planetary environments, and the solar and non-solar driven perturbations that affect them; and also at  forecasting  and  now  casting  the  possible  impacts  on  biological  and  technological 
systems. We intent to 
1-	Realize effect of space weather activities (CME and HSSWs) on the ionosphere. 
2-	To investigate the effect of SW using TEC data from dual frequency GPS receivers. 
3-	 To understand the different mechanisms causing positive and negative storm effect. 
4-	Use the earth magnetic filed data provided by different stations and evaluate ionospheric currents.
5-	To understand the strength of disturbance dynamo and prompt penetration electric fields in the different regions 
6-	We will also focus the variations in ionosphere electron content caused by recent total solar eclipse of  December 2019.

data.projectName: Morpho-anatomical and physiological characterization of Helianthus annuus L. and Brassica compestris L.for their potential utilization in phytoremediation
data.projectDigest: Saline wetland support very specific flora that is highly tolerant to salt stress. The inhabiting/crop plants adapt different structural and functional strategies to cope with high salinities and many of these adaptive components can be incorporated in crop plants to increase their degree of tolerance. It is, therefore, two plants will be selected for research, as well as the characterization based on morpho-anatomy and physiology to assess variation in degree of tolerance. The research project will be established and data for morpho-anatomy and physiology will be recorded to assess structural and functional markers for their tolerance to high salinities and metal tolerance.

data.projectName: Improving heat tolerance and grain yield of wheat by combining linkage mapping and genome wide association studies
data.projectDigest: Environmental stresses results in major reduction in the world food production. Production of wheat fluctuates across the years and locations due to unpredicted climatic conditions. Food security in present and future will rely on the improved resistance to environmental constraints such as heat, and high yielding cultivars. Wheat yield is seriously affected by high temperature stress at reproductive stage which causes reduction in grain number and weight. Therefore, to improve heat tolerance and yield under such conditions, wheat kernel related traits should be improved. This project is aimed to Improve wheat yield under heat stress conditions and  identification of novel 	QTLs and candidate genes harboring heat stress tolerance. For this purpose we have maintained a large collection of wheat germplasm. We have already screened this material against heat tolerance at Multan and had identified some tolerant genotypes. For more reliability of results, this germplasm will be further screened  under under field conditions at Faisalabad and under controlled conditions at Multan . Finally, molecular approaches will be used to identify the genes responsible for heat stress tolerance and higher grain yield.

data.projectName: Morpho-anatomic and molecular characterization and biological screening of some mushrooms of Kumrat valley, KPK, Pakistan.
data.projectDigest:
The proposed project will focus on the identification, characterization, biological screening and utilization of indigenous mushrooms as antimicrobial, antioxidant, anti-tumour, antidiabetic and antiaging agents. Mushrooms will be collected from Kumrat valley, KPK Pakistan for the purpose.  
Collected mushrooms will be characterized morpho-anatomically and phylogenetically. Molecular phylogeny will be carried out using multi-gene approach. Repository will be made annually and attempts will be made to find out biodiversity of the area. As these mushrooms are being locally used in many ways, so attempts will also be made to find out its in-vitro ethnomycological significance. 
The potential use these mushrooms as antimicrobial, antioxidant, anti-tumour, antidiabetic and antiaging agents is evident from many researches. These indigenous and novel mushrooms could be the better alternative compared with many plants and other organisms.

data.projectName: The Smog Tower to built pollution free environment
data.projectDigest:
Nowadays, one of the biggest problems we face are related to the pollution.  The air we breathe has great impact on our health. We have to reduce smog in our cities. Smog is a yellowish or blackish fog formed mainly by a mixture of pollutants in the atmosphere, which contains fine particles and ground level ozone. It occurs mainly because of air pollution and can also be defined as a mixture of various gases with dust and water vapor i.e the hazy air that makes breathing difficult. The main sources of these precursors are pollutants released directly into the air by gasoline and diesel-run vehicles, industrial plants and activities, and heating due to human activities. Smog is harmful and it is evident from the components that form it and effects that can happen from it. It is harmful to humans, animals, plants and the nature as a whole.
One of the possible method to combat this health degrading issue is to clean the air we breathe in by constructing the smog free towers. Smog Free Tower can vacuum in the smog particles. The tower can suck in dirty air like a giant vacuum cleaner. Ion technology then filters it, before returning smog-free air through the tower vents. By creating a field of ions, all the particles on the nano scale gets positively charged, therefore when the ground is negatively charged, you can drag them to the ground, and purify the air. In areas affected by severe air pollution, the smog free tower will harvest enough smog and provide cleaner air to breathe in.

data.projectName: Variations in the gene expression profile of tomato plants on exposure to pathogenic nematode (Meloidogyne incognita)
data.projectDigest: Root knot nematodes (RKN), Meloidogyne spp are important destructive plant pathogens and widely distributed throughout the Pakistan and worldwide.  Root knot nematodes disease is one of the most impactful diseases in tomato throughout the world.  RKN are biotrophic and highly sophisticated parasites that hijack host machinery by entering into roots and capable of infecting more than 2000 plant species. In our lab we have previously evaluated the effect of RKN infection on antioxidant enzymes and secondary metabolites of infected tomato plants. Our results have revealed significant association between pathogen and profile of antioxidant enzymes in infected plants. We want to extended the study to explore the detailed molecular mechanism is operating in the RKN resistance in tomato plants. Management of this pathogen is possible through appropriate knowledge of its parasitism, molecular mechanism of pathogenesis. To the best of our knowledge the proposed study is the first study from Pakistan that is designed to identify biomarkers induced by pathogenic nematode through comparative transcriptomic and proteomic analysis in tomato varieties of Punjab. For this purpose major tomato growing areas of Punjab province will be surveyed extensively in first year of project. From the study area soil and root samples will be collected from infested tomato fields/farms. Two different methods will be employed for the confirmation of RKN disease, first direct eye examination method will be used in which galls observed on root samples of tomato and growing weeds. Second bioassay based method will be used in green house. In next phase we will screen cultivated tomato varieties/ cultivars/lines of Punjab against RKN (Meloidogyne incognita) and will select highly resistant and susceptible

Agriculturist feed approximately 7.5 billion people across the world. This situation is even getting worse in many 3rd world countries including Pakistan. Researchers considered drought, famine, salinity, water scarcity, low yield varieties, poor farming management, marketing and climate change are the major causes for this dilemma. Chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.) ranks the world’s third largest annual legume of the Fabaceae family. Approximately 24.71-million-acre land is devoted for its cultivation worldwide that produces around 12.1 million tones although Asian counties secure prominent position in the world chickpea production of 90%. The total production of chickpea in Pakistan was 330,000 Metric tons in 2016. Major growing areas of Pakistan are Khushab, Layyah, Bhakkar, Mianwali, Sukkur, Rahim Yar Khan, DI Khan, Karak, Bannu, Kohat and Peshawar. As per recent information reveal by FAO, Pakistan specified largest area for chickpea cultivation however with least grain yield in the world. Plethora of research articles stresses the need to investigate the stable genotypes under diverse environments conditions that might improve the yield of chickpea better. Kabuli (white to cream with large seed coat) and Desi (brown, green or black with small wrinkled seed coat) chickpea biotypes are recognized in many parts of tropical, sub-tropical, semi-arid and temperate regions. The desi types account maximum cultivation area and splits (dal) and ?our (besan) are primarily made from desi type. Both types are acknowledged for a wide source of ph

data.projectName: Design of Sliding Mode controller for Matrix Converter based Dynamic Voltage Restorer to mitigate voltage disturbances.
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
Recently, many types of sensitive loads such as data processing devices, computers, controlling devices and power conversion loads are connected with distribution network.  These loads are affected by voltage disturbances generated by heavy motor switching, incorrect wiring, malfunctioning of protective devices and systems failures due to faults. Voltage disturbances can cause data to get corrupted or deleted.  These disturbances also affect the operation of control processes in industries, as a result production will be affected. To overcome these disturbances, Dynamic Voltage restorer (DVR) will be used in this project a more recent flexible ac transmission FACTs controller. The DVR will be designed with Matrix converter. The dynamics will be controlled with Sliding Mode Controller (SMC).  
The DVR based on a matrix converter will improve the power quality, reliability and efficiency of power system networks, thus providing disturbance free power to sensitive loads.

data.projectName: Industrial perspective of gastro-retentive hydrodynamically balanced system by QbD approach
data.projectDigest:
There are following two major objectives of the proposed research project, 
1.	Designing medicine product containing drug Ondansetron (anti-vomiting), to reduce the nausea and vomiting in complicated cancer patients receiving anti-cancer drugs (chemotherapy). Cancer patients undergo immense discomfort not only due to severe pain but also the medicines prescribed to them. The proposed project will design pellets/minitablets that will keep Ondansetron drug in stomach floating, which may control anti-cancer treatment induced vomiting for prolong time. Special techniques and methodology will be applied to design such system. The quality will be evaluated statistically. 
2.	Eating out trends have made us vulnerable to acquire stomach related infections. The most commonly found culprit bacteria (germs) is H.Pylori to cause such infections. Unfortunately, the number of cases caused by this bacterium (germ) is increasing day by day and commonly prescribed antibiotics are becoming ineffective due to the development of resistance by this smart bacterium. Moxifloxacin (antibiotic) is not currently in prescribing practice to treat such infections but has found effective in killing H.Pylori. Therefore, in proposed project a system (pellets/mini tablets) will be established by scientific approach to keep it floating in stomach, so that this antibiotic will kill the residing bacteria in stomach will full efficacy. 
Literature survey has been done extensively and it was found out that there is no stomach floating minitablet/pellets (gastro-retentive floating/ hydrodynamically stabilized) have been designed to maximize the effect of these drugs (medicines) and relief patients. The methods applied will be simple and cost effective for pharmaceutical companies .

data.projectName: Learning Arabic language for direct understanding of Quran that may create harmony in Pakistan (Challenges, opportunities and a case study of Bahawalpur).
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan is an Islamic country and religious sentiment is dominant there. People rely for understanding of islam mostly on imam of mosques, sermons and scholars; those are mostly affiliated with some sects or groups.
While following a specific scholar, sometimes people go towards extremism and intolerance. The trend of these attitudes has been increased alarmingly in the past few years.
This study will explore the causes of clannishness, linguistics differences and will give suggestions for reducing these issues.
One basic reason for these attitudes is, reliance of people on religious scholars rather than Quran. If a muslim take direct guidance from Quran these issues can be reduced.
This study will explicit the opportunities of promoting Arabic language in the society. In this regard, Bahawalpur region will be discussed as a case study.

data.projectName: Value Addition and Postharvest shelf life extension of medicinal and edible mushrooms
data.projectDigest: Mushrooms have always been valued and appreciated due to their taste, texture, medicinal constituents and used as food flavoring material. The production of mushroom is increasing rapidly throughout the world due to its taste and nutrition. However, harvested mushroom have high content of water (80-95%), high level of enzyme activity and do not have protective cuticle layer on the skin which leads to browning and senescence related signs. Due to high perishability it has a short shelf life (1-3 days) at room temperature which leads to weight loss, discoloration and texture changes leads to high waste after harvesting. The short shelf life of mushrooms become the biggest limitation of its industrial development in Pakistan. Therefore, it is necessary to develop proper preservation methods to extend the postharvest storage period and preserve the quality of mushrooms by developing various value added products. The value-added products are the need of the hour for the mushroom growers not only to reduce the losses but also to enhance the income. Therefore, this project is designed to increase the shelf life of commercially cultivated mushrooms by applying various postharvest techniques and making value added products which ultimately boost the mushroom industry in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Development of a Solar Powered Stirling Engine for the electricity generation
data.projectDigest:
This project will be comprised of developing a prototype of a solar powered Stirling engine that would be able to generate electricity up to 1000 W. A thorough literature review will provide preliminary design specifications. A numerical model will then be designed and simulated using fluid structure interaction methodologies to identify the suitable parameters of the engine. Based on those parameters, the power efficiency will be optimized to reduce the cost to power ratio. 
The end-user of the product will be small scale industries and the public sector. With the application of smart/net-metering, the users will be able to sell the excess energy to their energy supplier that would be generated during the day. Consequently, they will be able to purchase the electricity back from the supplier during the night. This will assist them financially during the night or when the Stirling engines are not able to work properly due to poor solar power. This project will help the local manufacturers develop Stirling engines of different capacities based on the customer’s requirement. Moreover, the extra dependency of the foreign markets will be reduced; hence strengthening the country’s economy and positively influencing the poverty line of the country.

data.projectName: COUNTRY LEVEL FACTORS EFFECTING EXPORT PERFORMANCE OF A COUNTRY: A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF PAKISTANI, INDIAN AND BANGLADESHI TEXTILE EXPORTS
data.projectDigest:
The Pakistani textile industry has been facing a threatening decline in export since the last decade (WTO, 2019). Textile exporters are in an uncertain situation and moving their investments to other countries, which is an alarming sign for the Pakistani economy. Recently, in 2019, Pakistani textile exports faced a decline of 3%, and textile exports droped from 1,108,889 thousand dollars to 1,062,136 thousand dollars (WTO, 2019). Moreover, all commodities faced a significant decline in export, except ready-made garments (WTO, 2019). 
Since 2007, Pakistani textile exports never went ahead of Bangladeshi textile exports. data.projectName: Wind Energy Harvester for Vehicle’s Battery Charging
data.projectDigest:
As the population and advancement of the world is expanding day by day, the electrical consumption is increasing along with it. According to a research, there will be almost 50 billion devices on internet in near future. A concept of electric cars has been introduced which will rapidly increase the demand of electricity. Here, a need of electricity production from renewable energy resources arrives, so as to reduce the emission of toxic chemicals in the environment. Ideas have been proposed for this using solar energy by solar panels and wind energy by wind turbines.
Now, electricity production from solar energy depends strongly upon the environment i.e. the presence of sun and clouds. In this project, we have come up with an idea of self-dependent vehicles. This project proposes the electricity production from wind pressure being exerted on the car [1] when it is in mobility. A fan will be mounted on the part of the vehicle where there is maximum wind pressure being exerted. The wind pressure being exerted will be converted into electrical energy via mechanical movement of fan [2]. After this, voltage rectifiers and stabilizers could be possibly used to get the required power output. Using this electric power, the vehicle’s battery will be charged. Moreover, the more the speed is, the more pressure will be exerted thus more electricity production is expected to accumulate.

data.projectName: A SURVEILLANCE STUDY ON THE OCCURRENCE OF FUSARIUM TOXINS IN POULTRY FEED AND FEED INGREDIENTS
data.projectDigest: Mycotoxins are common contaminants of agricultural commodities. They directly or indirectly affect the human and animal health. Well-known attributes of mycotoxins are hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, immunosuppression, carcinogenicity and teratogenicity. Aspergillus, Fusarium, Penicillium, and Alternaria are the major fungal genera involved in the production of these toxigenic substances. Aflatoxins, ochratoxins, trichthececns, fumonisins and zearalenone are the major group of mycotoxins affecting human and animal health. Each toxin has its permissible level in food or feed.  In Pakistan only aflatoxins and to lesser extent ochratoxins have received the limelight in poultry industry while neglecting the importance of other toxins. This has resulted in little to no comprehensive literature regarding prevalence/levels of different Fusarium toxins within poultry feed and its ingredients. Fusarium species are ubiquitous in nature, a complete prevention of a Fusarium infection and contamination with associated mycotoxins seems to be uncertain. Different Fusarium species contaminate grains including maize, corn, wheat etc. in the field and also during inappropriate storage conditions. Fusarium toxins are of several types but the most important among them are fumonisins, trichothecenes and zearalenone. The aim of present study is  to assess the presence of Fusarium toxins (Fumonisin B1, trichthecenes (T-2, deoxynivalenol) and zearalenone) in poultry feed and its ingredients.

data.projectName: Numerical treatment of differential equations and integro-differential equations with the help of subdivision schemes
data.piUniversity: Government Sadiq College Women University, Bahawalpur
data.projectDigest: CAGD short for computer-aided geometric design is a new ground that primarily developed to bring comfort for computers to industries such as automotive, aerospace and shipbuilding. CAGD deals with the mathematical description of shapes. The subdivision is an easy and attractive technique to illustrate smooth curves and surfaces. The loom of subdivision schemes is simple and skillful in the direction of its mathematical representation. In this research proposal, We will construct subdivision scheme-based algorithms (non-iterative and iterative) for the numerical solutions of different physical and engineering problems. These problems are formulated in the form of differential and integro-differential equations by Subdivision Schemes.  Especially we will construct algorithms for the numerical solutions of partial differential equations by subdivision schemes because these problems are not solved by the subdivision method in the literature.  The convergence and error estimation of the proposed algorithms will also be calculated. At the end of these proposed algorithms, we will present the applications of proposed subdivision schemes-based algorithms and comparison with existing algorithms.

data.projectName: Balancing Dual Innovation in Pakistan’s Tourism and Hospitality Industry: A Strategic Approach
data.projectDigest: The research aims at examining hotel industry and how much they are exploring or exploiting, or exploring and exploiting there current resources for the achievement of dual innovation. Since, it is recognized that organizations should pursue dual innovation to get competitive advantage and stay in the market for longer period of time. This paradigm shift has given a new approach for researchers to emphasize on ambidextrous organizations. In this study a model has been constructed which shows how knowledge sharing behavior can mediate the relationship between knowledge sharing culture and organizational ambidexterity.  The research approach of this study is a deductive approach hence the survey will be conducted among mid and high level managers employed in a hotel industry. The obtained data through questionnaires will be analyzed by using SPSS, PROCESS macros, slope analysis and PLS-SEM (for high order factors). Results of this study will be beneficial for Tourism and Hospitality industry specifically for managers who wants to be more adaptive and exploit more resources. In addition hotels can be more incremental and radical at the same time while innovating. Findings of the study will further guide them in defining new levels of guest services and embracing new technology.

data.projectName: DEVELOPMENT OF REACTIVE INKS FOR DIGITAL PRINTING OF TEXTILES
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Recently digital printing technology is gaining popularity as it offers lower water and energy use, low effluent discharge and air emissions and economical production of short to medium runs. In this printing method minute droplet of ink is injected from nozzles onto a fabric surface. This method is capable of generating rapidly multi-colour design onto the fabric. However, excellent print quality is dependent upon excellent ink quality and fabric preparation along with the quality of digital printer. Inks to be used in digital printing should be highly water soluble, pure and stable so it should not clog the nozzle of the printer. These inks when applied to fabric surface should appear brilliant and fast to washing, rubbing and light. Reactive dyes are known for their brilliance, large colour gamut along with excellent wash and rub fastness. Unfortunately most of the reactive inks are imported which is cumbersome and costly supply chain option to the local textile industry. There is a need to develop these inks indigenously to fill this gap which will assists in making our textile industry sustainable and competitive in global market. The principle aim of this project is to develop reactive inks locally which may be technically superior when applied to textile substrate and offer a cost effective solution to local industry as well.

data.projectName: Assessment of drought tolerance response in wheat to different seed size and plant stature classes in climate vulnerable conditions
data.projectDigest: The constant increase temperature due to global warming has augmented the drought affected areas throughout the world. Drought, a most common environmental stress affecting around 32% from the total of 165 million hectares under wheat cultivation. In Pakistani Punjab sensitivity for stress is highest during early vegetative growth of wheat due to low rainfall and canal closure during the months of November, December and January. The Efficient drought resistant wheat genotypes having optimum seed size and suitable stature can have the ability to cope with moisture deficit conditions during early wheat growth stage. Therefore, we designed different lab and field experiments on plant stature and seed size characteristics of different wheat varieties to identify suitable variety having appropriate plant stature and seed size that we can in general recommend for early drought tolerance in wheat. For lab experiment, six wheat varieties two from each stature class i.e. (standard height and low tillering), (low height and low tillering) and (standard height and high tillering) will be screened under different drought levels (-2, -4, -6, -8 bar osmotic potential by using PEG). In second lab experiment different seed size classes will also be screened under same drought stress levels.

data.projectName: Liquid fuel production by alkane metathesis using transition metal based tandem catalysis
data.projectDigest: Alkane metathesis (AM) is a fascinating area of great significance for the utilization of alkanes and natural gas. It has potential applicability via converting low-value alkane (C3-C9) by  Fisher-Tropsch process into linear alkanes in the diesel fuel range (C14-C22). Recently, tandem catalytic system has gained research interest for AM. The said system is comprised of a transfer dehydrogenation (TD) catalyst and olefin metathesis catalysts. In this context, a few of efficient olefin catalysts such as schrock and Grubbs catalyst, are available and reported in literature. However, the variety of efficient and active transfer dehydrogenation catalyst is limited. This scenario has posed an existing research gap to be filled by scientist. Thus, a well defined and proposedly efficient transfer TD catalystshave been proposed and designed in the form of this project. They  will then subjected to tandem catalytic system in order to assess their potential as new TDs. The envisaged test will be carried out with available olefin metathesis catalyst for the conversion of short chain hydrocarbons  diesel fuel hydrocarbons range. The highlight of the proposed designed catalyst is the presence of hybrid donor atoms on ligand i.e. hard donor atom (tertphohspine/tertamine) and soft donor rather better acceptor atom (P=C double bond and phosphite). These hybrid systems will offer enhance stability to metal centers (Rh, Ir, Pd, Ru, Ni, Fe etc.) by shifting excess electronic charge from metal center back to soft donor atom in the form of ?–back donation. This novel concept of ?-back donation has reportedly gained popularity in many catalytic processes and have been found useful in stabilizing metal catalysts during the course of catalytic cycle.

This is evident that almost 0.3 million or two third patients don’t receive any therapy or unnoticed or are not able to report to these cancer hospitals.The cancers accountable for the highest deaths (total = 101,113) in Pakistani population includes breast cancer (n = 16232, 16.1%). Relatively the mean and average monthly budget of cancer care was 1093.13 US$ and 946.42 US$ respectively. Whereas mean and average monthly earnings of these patients was 996.4 US$ and 562.5 US$  respectively. The existing treatment of cancer with chemotherapeutic agent pose problem of resistance as well as life threatening side effects. Besides these drawbacks their high cost is another bottleneck. Thus there is an urgent and crucial requirement for developing an effective, safe and inexpensive remedy. This aim may be achieved by utilizing the natural proteins of snake venom with fascinating potency against cancer. These novel drugs will hopefully not only  be curative and safe  but also reduce economic burden from the society.

data.projectName: Vector Borne Haemoparasites: An Economic Challenge of Dromedary Camels in Southern Punjab
data.projectDigest: Blood parasites are very important in the performance of production animals. Camel is considered as a new, potential and resistant condidate of milk production for next generation. Blood parasites adversly affect the milk, meat and hide production of camels. Keeping in view the described problem,  current project is designed to investigate the prevalence of haemoparasites of dromedary camel in Southern Punjab. All the districts of Southern Punjab will be involved in the study. With the help of Livestock and Dairy Development Department, population of camels will be identified in the study area and sampling will be performed from all districts. These samples will be subjected to parasitological and serological diagnostic techniques for qualitative and quantitative analysis. Positive samples will be processed further for molecular identification. Results obtained will be analysed by appropriate statistical software and significance of different parasites present in different localities of Southern Punjab will be evaluated and possible control strategies will be advised accordingly with the results along with identification of reservoirs of these parasites.

Keeping in view the described problem,  current project is designed to investigate the prevalence of haemoparasites of dromedary camel in Southern Punjab. All the districts of Southern Punjab will be involved in the study. With the help of Livestock and Dairy Development Department, population of camels will be identified in the study area and sampling will be performed from all districts. These samples will be subjected to parasitological and serological diagnostic techniques for qualitative and quantitative analysis. Positive samples will be processed further for molecular identification. Results obtained will be analysed by appropriate statistical software and significance of different parasites present in different localities of Southern Punjab will be evaluated and possible control strategies will be advised accordingly with the results along with identification of reservoirs of these parasites.

data.projectName: Pilot-scale production of novel organic fertilizers & bioproducts from different bio-waste materials
data.projectDigest: Indiscriminate use of chemical fertilizers in conventional crop production has made agriculture unviable and jeopardized our healthy environment. This increasing trend of using unsafe nutrients source has made living of poor farmers miserable and difficult. The chemical fertilizers have become beyond the purchasing capacity of farmers in Pakistan. It is right time to introduce alternative nutrients sources which are safe and cheap for raising crops. In Pakistan available mineral resources are at the verge of depletion and most of phosphate and potassium mineral are being imported from Jordan and Canada. The import of these minerals for manufacturing phosphatic & potassium fertilizers in the country has made farmer unable to use optimum doses of chemical fertilizers. In Pakistan we have abundant quantity of agricultural and bio-waste material which could be recycled into bio-products. These organic fertilizers, peat moss and compost are more valuable in restoration of natural soil environment. These quality bio-products formulated by utilizing scientific knowledge can enhance organic matter and biodynamic of the degraded and poor structured soils. With the use of organic fertilizers and other organic substrates, we can replenish and revitalize our depleted and poor soils. These practices can enhance soil productivity and quality through sustainable agriculture.

data.projectName: Support vector and local linear regression modelling for real-time streamflow forecasting using genetic algorithm.
data.projectDigest: Real time flood prediction technique is an important tool which helps in foreseeing of flood disasters. This study aims to present platform for finding early indication of flood disasters. Normally regression techniques are used for the predictions of streamflows but this study will be aimed to account for a non-linear change and variability of natural data by using Gamma Test, for input combination and data length selection, in conjunction with Support Vector Machine (SVM) Regression and Local Linear Regression (LLR) based models approach using Genetic Algorithm (GA) for forecasting of streamflows for Astore River,  tributary of River Indus, flowing in Gilgit Bultistan Province of Pakistan. This study will also investigates the impact of previous Precipitation, Temperature and discharge information on the selected models based stream flow output.  Daily Temperature, Precipitation and discharge time series, up to a maximum of five previous days will be used to forecast 1-day ahead stream flows, starting from one day previous Precipitation, Temperature and discharge information to a maximum of five. The Models performance assessment will be analyzed using various of statistical parameters globally recognized. The result will eventually help in flood forecasting, lifesaving and better management of water resources.

data.projectName: Quantitative Serum Proteome Profiling for the Identification of Diagnostic Biomarker for Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes
data.projectDigest: Diabetes mellitus has reached to epidemic proportion worldwide, with 463 million people are reported to have diabetes in 2019. People with type 2 diabetes live asymptomatic for years, not aware of disease progression.  Prediabetes also signifies the risk of the future development of type 2 diabetes. The available clinical diagnostic markers have limitations including moderate sensitivity and specificity. The hypothesis of the proposed study is to identify more sensitive and precise biomarkers capable of predicting progression to hyperglycemia states at the earliest time point when beta cell function is still relatively more optimal and may be more responsive to lifestyle modification, pharmacological agents, and improve clinical outcomes. In this project, we will apply quantitative mass spectrometric profiling of serum to explore changes in the proteins/peptides from people with prediabetes, and type 2 diabetes. Occurrence of unique peptides not only clues the biomarker, but will also bring the information of molecular pathways involved in disease development and probably the new molecular targets of the drugs. The proposed research will provide a national database of proteomics of prediabetes and type-2 diabetes patients, which will help clinicians in better treatment and management of the disease.

data.projectName: New, Enhanced Mathematical Foundations for Tropical Algebraic Cryptography
data.projectDigest: The science/art of keeping the information in a secret form in order to transfer it safely leads to the birth of cryptography. The field of cryptography may involve developing and analyzing the techniques that provide protection from unauthorized access and prevent modification of data. Algebraic cryptography is based on the use of algebraic structures to successfully encrypt and decrypt data in a logical manner. A common theme in algebra is to understand algebraic structures over arbitrary ring or more generally over semirings  by first studying it in a particular broad context and then investigating the possible ways to "descend" to the base semiring again. We combine two approaches to bring in the abstraction and complexity of a generalized algebraic structure namely tropical algebra and develop cryptosystems with enhanced levels of privacy and efficiency.

data.projectName: Degradation of aflatoxins in rice at commercial scale and the training of local rice millers for the prevention of mycotoxins production
data.projectDigest: Rice is among the leading cereal crops around the globe. Pakistan is one the biggest exporter of rice and particularly famous for producing "Basmati Rice" of supreme sensory properties. However, rice export of Pakistan is in decline during the last few years mainly due to the presence of “aflatoxins”. Aflatoxins are fungal metabolite and are reported as group 1 category carcinogen and may also cause retarded growth, immunity and reproductive problems. Therefore, a reliable method for aflatoxins degradation is direly needed to boost the rice export of Pakistan. Application of ozone gas and the use of citric acid is reported to have the potential to degrade the aflatoxins, in our initial trails we also achieved positive results for aflatoxins degradation through ozone gas and citric acid application. The said project is designed to apply ozone gas in combination with citric acid at different stages of rice processing i.e. fresh paddy, dried paddy and after husk removal. The impact of ozone treatment on nutritional quality of rice and on its sensory parameters will also be analyzed. Furthermore, workshops will be organized to educate the rice growers and rice millers regarding the ways to prevent the production of mycotoxins particularly aflatoxins.

data.projectName: Mathematical Modeling of Electro-Osmotically Flow of Non-Newtonian Fluids with Variable Properties
data.projectDigest: An electro-osmotic flow of non-Newtonian fluids has significant importance in micro-fluidic systems and micro-devices. Due to the importance of Electro-osmotic flow, in this project, a theoretical analysis shall be conducted to investigate the important features of the electro-osmotic flow of non-Newtonian fluids. In non-Newtonian fluids we will take Power-Law fluid, viscoelastic fluid, third and fourth grade fluid, Sisko-fluid, Eyring-Powell fluid and Johnson–Segalman fluid models etc. The viscosity fluid will take as a constant and function of temperature or function of pressure. In the first step, the results of this study will helpful to understand the basic idea of the electro-osmotic flow of non-Newtonian fluids. Secondly, we will develop the numerical algorithms of finite element method, finite volume method, finite difference method pseudo spectral collocation method etc. These numerical algorithms will provide the help to solve the nonlinear complex boundary values problems. Thirdly, it will be beneficial for clinicians who are working in the treatment of cancer and tumours with the help of electromagnetic hyperthermia. Further, the outcomes of this investigation are beneficial to design the thermos-fluidic micro-pumps which can be used in the separation process (chemical process) and bio-microfluidic devices that will be used in the diagnosis purpose.

data.projectName: EFFECT OF INTEGRATED MANAGEMENT OF FERTILIZER, SOWING TECHNIQUE AND TILLAGE PRACTICE ON SOIL PROPERTIES AND WHEAT YIELD
data.projectDigest: According to Shakeel et al. (2016) conventional farmers of Pakistan use cultivator four times or even more as primary tillage implement which is expensive in terms of fuel consumption, producing compaction in soil particles and negligible soil inversion. Therefore a proper combination of tillage implements should be selected to achieve high yield of cereal with less inputs. Furthermore, Pakistan’s soil is deficient in essential nutrients therefore different fertilizers or their combinations are necessary for enhancing crop yield. Liyue et al. (2016) applied cattle manure-compost and its combination with inorganic fertilizer. But the preparation of cattle manure compost needs a large number of cattle which is much expensive for almost all farmers. With the addition, there is a large amount of agricultural and kitchen wastes available throughout the country which is a cheap source of composting. On the other hand, different planting techniques have been adapted by researchers to achieve optimum yield. Every planting technique has its own advantages. But Abdul et al. (2015) claimed that for optimum wheat production, the raised bed is a significant technique than the flat bed. Aggarwal and Goswami (2003), Jiyang et al. (2007) and Abdul et al. (2015) reported different modifications in raised bed planting technique for achieving optimum yield of wheat.

data.projectName: Virtual Craniofacial Reconstruction and Bio-modelling Using CAGD
data.projectDigest:
Craniofacial region, the complex portion of the human body, constitutes various bones integrated in a complex way. The fractures are diagnosed in this portion through different imaging technologies such as CT scan and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI). There is growing percentage of road traffic accidents inflicting multiple injuries in people and head injury is significant in these. In Punjab region only, 280,381 people were reported with head injuries in recent year. On the average, at least 3000 patients undergo operation in general hospital Lahore.  
These accidents have generated demand of cranial implants which are imported from the foreign countries. Despite having potential and technological infrastructure, no serious effort has been made in Pakistan to produce this critical technology. The patients have to bear heavy expenditures to get them treated per force. 
We intend to carry out the project to develop this technology in Pakistan cost effectively and using existing tangible and intangible infrastructures of Pakistan with the aim to achieve self-reliance in this technology.
We will use CAGD (cubic B-spline and rational cubic trigonometric B-spline) based scheme for craniofacial construction that will be free from mirror image and reference skull. Moreover, the surgeon may have the control to adjust the thickness of bone as desired clinically.

data.projectName: Resource Conservation Technologies (RCTs) in wheat-based cropping systems of Pakistan: Effects on system productivity, profitability and resource use efficiency
data.projectDigest: Persistent use of conventional farming practices with conventional tillage and burning crop residues has degraded the soil resource base . Generally, the farmers of rice-wheat belt burn the rice crop residues in the field. Burning of rice stubbles and remnants leads to great loss of plant essential nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorous, sulphur and boron. Moreover, this practice considerably hampers the soil microbial activities and rigorously cuts down the organic matter contents in soil. In cotton-wheat system the sowing of wheat is delayed for greed of more cotton picking. Whereas, in mixed-wheat system the continuous growing of exhaustive crops have severely degraded the soil. The conservation agriculture (CA)-based resource conservation technologies (RCTs) practiced over an estimated area of 100 mha globally and across a variety of climatic, soil and geographic zones.  The RCTs provide opportunities to reduce the cost of production, save water and nutrients, increase yields, increase crop diversification, improve efficient use of resources, and benefit the environment. Further, escalating fuel, fertilizers and other input costs; necessitates the effective use of resources in agriculture. Hence, we designed current project comprised of 3-year series of experiments of different RCTs practices on grain yield, biomass productivity and soil organic C (SOC) accumulation rates in wheat-based intensive cropping systems such as rice-wheat, cotton-wheat and mixed-wheat. Each experiment will be conducted at two farmer fields in rice-wheat, cotton-wheat and mixed-wheat cropping systems of Pakistan. All the team members including faculty, academic and sectoral collaborators will work together to fulfill the proposed objectives of the projects.

data.projectName: The Societal Economic Burden of Dengue and Awareness Impact
data.projectDigest: Dengue is a disease, due to mosquito bite, prevail in the hot areas of world and it effects people’s health, productivity, life quality and also put financial burden on them. Over Pakistan, in 2019 only, more than 47000 cases were reported, which is the highest number of reported cases since the Dengue out-break in 2005 in Karachi. As Pakistan is one of the developing countries and majority of people belong to middle- or lower-income class, any disease that make people out of work and put extra economic burden on them severely impact their families and quality of life. This study will estimate the average economic cost borne by the dengue patient during the phase of dengue fever and so the aggregated societal expenses of dengue disease will be calculated. This study will also measure the impact of the awareness /information regarding the precautionary measures of dengue in one of the newly dengue hit area of Muzaffarabad, capital city of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, where more than 1600 dengue cases including 1 death are reported in 2019. From the result of study we will be able to get  true picture of the expenditures borne by the patient and at aggregate level , along with the success of awareness campaign, would help the policy makers in policy making while allocating resources for management prevention and controlling activities of dengue disease.

As Pakistan is one of the developing countries and majority of people belong to middle- or lower-income class, any disease that make people out of work and put extra economic burden on them severely impact their families and quality of life. This study will estimate the average economic cost borne by the dengue patient during the phase of dengue fever and so the aggregated societal expenses of dengue disease will be calculated. This study will also measure the impact of the awareness /information regarding the precautionary measures of dengue in one of the newly dengue hit area of Muzaffarabad, capital city of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, where more than 1600 dengue cases including 1 death are reported in 2019. From the result of study we will be able to get  true picture of the expenditures borne by the patient and at aggregate level , along with the success of awareness campaign, would help the policy makers in policy making while allocating resources for management prevention and controlling activities of dengue disease.

data.projectName: High Efficiency Tandem Perovskite / CZTS solar cell for Pilot Production: Experimental and Simulation study

CuZnSnS are abundant and have the potential to achieve high efficiency. Perovskite based solar cells is another class of materials have shown high efficiency potential. A combination of these two technologies of solar cells called tandem solar cells where the incident sunlight is absorbed in both cells and generating high efficiency and lower cost/watt equal to the cost of electricity generated by the non-renewable energy sources.

data.projectName: Developing Early Childhood Education program joined by webinar outreach extension in  Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is among the world’s highly populated countries.  Presently, human services are insufficient to meet all life necessities including food, shelter, health, safety, and well-being among the people. Among all the age groups, young children (birth-5 years) are growing despondently in Pakistan. In urban areas, overcrowded family settings and limited play space make childhood uncomfortable and uninspiring. Optimal development during the early years sets the course for every individual’s future educational outcomes, as well as biopsychosocial and cognitive abilities. Most developed countries, including the U.S and China have successfully introduced early childhood education program models to young children with the majority of services targeted at children 3+ years. These early childhood settings emphasize high quality child care, self-initiated learning, highly trained professional staff members, and excellent access to educational services with latest technologies.Pakistan has been missing the opportunity to intervene during children’s most important early years, and unfortunately, Pakistani Government schools are not well equipped to address the developmental needs of very young children. Moreover, poorly prepared childcare professionals; appropriate toys, books, and equipment; serious shortage of teachers; and congested classrooms impede children’s opportunity for quality early childhood experiences. These challenges, though wide-spread, affect children and families living in poverty especially. The proposed project is designed to address the current shortage of quality early childhood education (ECE), facilitate children’s enrollment in primary school, and help Pakistan meet the 2nd and 4th Millennium Developmental Goals of 100% primary school enrollment .

data.projectName: Synthesis and Characterization of chitosan encapsulated botanical macro capsules for wastewater treatment
data.projectDigest:
Water pollution by heavy metals and dyes has been reported as a major problem. Both ground and surface water can be contaminated by natural and anthropogenic sources which also affect the aesthetic properties of water system. To tackle the issue of waste water treatment some alternative method have been developed such as bio adsorbents which is an effective method to adsorb toxic heavy metals from effluents not polluting the ground water and at the same time utilizing the discarded open waste in the environment for a useful purpose of waste water treatment. 
Adsorption is referred as an efficient and environmentally, friendly decontamination technique. The proposed project involves the synthesis of macro capsules as an adsorbent by using the low-cost chitosan and cellulose extracted from the agricultural waste. Proposed adsorbents will help to reduce the cost of traditional methods for heavy metals and dyes removal and motivate the industries to adopt these environment friendly techniques by using cost effective and locally available materials for water remediation.

data.projectName: Experimental and Computational Study of Fluidized Bed Chemical Looping Combustion System with Indigenous Looping Materials
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: Thermal power plants use combustion of fossil fuels to generate electricity. These power plants are accompanied by carbon capture facilities to reduce the release of unwarranted emissions of flue gases especially carbon dioxide (CO2), carbon mono oxide (CO) and oxides of sulfur and nitrogen.  For economic and efficiency reasons, new methods to capture these hazardous gases are being considered. One such method is Chemical Looping Combustion (CLC). The CLC technology does not require any pre or post treatments for separation of CO2 exiting the power plants and has risen to prominence in recent years as compared to traditional techniques where inherent CO2 capture causes significant energy penalty. These benefits of CLC technologies point to low cost reliable process and easy availability of CO2 for further use. Current project aims to design, develop and investigate a lab scale CLC setup both experimentally as well as computationally using indigenous minerals as looping material. The project will result in a process for clean combustion of fossil fuels resulting in sustainable climate control technology as mandated by Paris Agreement of 2015 and signed by Pakistan in 2016. All fossil fuel burning power plants in the country can benefit from the outcomes of the project.

data.projectName: Post heat-treatment coldstorage potential of promising mango cultivars for refrigerated export shipments
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is one of the top ten mango growing and exporting countries in the world. Hot water and vapour heat treatment are used for fruit fly disinfestation of mangoes for export to different countries. This project proposal is focused on evaluating the impact of these treatments on fruit quality, shelflife and physiology of mango cultivars including Azeem Chaunsa, Chenab Gold, Sindhri and Sufaid Chaunsa under post treatment low temperature storage. This project will lead towards development of protocols for shipment of mangoes in refrigerated shipping containers through sea or land routes as these modes of transport of 3-4 times cheaper and have capacity of transporting bulk volumes than air-freight; thereby having potential for increasing the profit margins for stakeholders.

data.projectName: Microalgae as a cost effective option for textile wastewater ?treatment and biofuel production
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest: According to Sindh Environmental Protection Agency (SEPA) there are more than 300 textile ?industries operating in Karachi. Out of these less than 50% have installed any wastewater ?treatment system. This untreated wastewater from majority of these industries is finally ?discharged into the Arabian sea. This results in pollution of sea water and it is toxic for aquatic ?life. The textile industries which are using conventional methods can reduce organic pollutants ?from wastewater, but these methods cannot remove nitrate and phosphate from wastewater ?which are causing eutrophication problem. In the industrial treatment plants, microalgae-based ?technology can be employed right after the secondary treatment where activated sludge usually ?removes organic matter to remove the left-over COD and inorganic nutrients such as nitrogen ?and phosphorus. Microalgae have the capacity to assimilate nitrogen and phosphors in to their ?biomass while growing which can later be consumed as a biofuel production. This project is well ?suitable for the industries. At the laboratory scale, the capability of native microalgae species to ?grow in high strength textile wastewater and removal of COD/BOD and nitrates and phosphate ?will be analyzed. Further biomass characterization of the microalgae will be performed in order to ?investigate the potential of produced biomass to produce biofuel. Further, cost-benefit analysis of ?microalgae-based textile wastewater treatment would be done to realize this concept.?

data.projectName: Genetic profiling of Bipolar Disorder in Pakistani Population
data.projectDigest: Bipolar disorder (BD) is clinically characterized as mania and depression, including the elevated mood ranging between severe depression and euphoria along with suicidal thoughts, insomnia, grandiosity, and feeling of worthlessness. It is the fourth leading cause of disability with a worldwide prevalence of 2% as well as 57% to 74% co?occurring psychiatric disorder, where 15% of people die by suicide due to BD. There is no such evidence that the rate of bipolar disorder differs among different populations. Certain genes including ANK3 are reported to have a crucial role in the signaling pathway of the disease as well as involved in establishing proper neuronal connectivity during development. ANK3 gene is involved in the brain function related to voltage gated sodium and potassium channels in proximal axonal segments and nodes of Ranvier. However, the existing knowledge about the underlying molecular mechanism causing the disease needs further exploration for the development of effective drugs. Therefore, in the proposed study, we aim to analyze the genomic mutational analysis of the ANK3 gene in bipolar disorder in the Pakistani population .

In the present project firstly to developed the numerical scheme for accurately approximating such type of models and secondly to investigate whether these model have the behavior of eventually periodicity or not when Model is treated as fractional order instead of integral order as such property has been identified for integral order only in some cases Bona and co-authors (see for example [49] and the references there in).But the these investigations for fractional order are still missing.

data.projectName: The Specification and Demonstration of Reliability, Availability, Maintainability and Safety (RAMS) of Rail Transportation in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
1. Severe kind of accidents continues to occur with considerably high rate in Pakistan Railways that lead to fatalities and other economic losses.
2.  RAMS for railways is an engineering discipline that combines reliability, availability, maintainability and safety characteristics associated to the operational objectives of a railway system. RAMS management has proven to be a great potential to ensure reliability and safety and to improve cost effectiveness in many world-class railway systems. However, the Pakistan railway industry has not yet introduced and implemented RAMS management in the railway engineering process. This is a major reason for having higher rates of accidents and lower levels of reliability in Pakistan Railways. 
3. Current railway projects at global level have required the implementation of RAMS management to achieve a reliable and safe railway system and service within the defined time and limited cost. 
3. The purpose of this project work is to develop a systematic approach for integrating RAMS management into the railway transport systems and associated engineering projects in Pakistan. So that the objectives, such as operational availability, system level safety and cost competitiveness (in comparison to other modes of transportation) are achieved successfully.  
The framework developed in this project will help Pakistan railways in establishing its strategy, objectives, functional concepts and activities for the RAMS management.

data.projectName: Intelligent Traffic Camera Video Analytics
data.projectDigest: The ever-growing surge in population and vehicle sales around the globe have posed serious challenges to traffic management in recent times. Ineffective management of traffic causes great economic losses to countries, particularly the heavily populated cities. In a recent survey conducted by the Punjab Safe Cities Authority (PSCA), Rs. 1 million is wasted every week due to time wastage in traffic clogging, reduction in earning of drivers per minute, and fuel wastage due to traffic jams. Through this project, we intend to indigenously develop core technologies for intelligent processing of traffic surveillance videos in order to extract industry-standard analytics data in real-time. This analytics data will include the rate of traffic flow at different times of the day, identification of traffic rules violations, visualization of traffic densities to intuitively understand the state of traffic in a city, and perform collaborative intelligence to optimize traffic flow in real-time and ensure better management of traffic. The proposed system will also provide real time alerts for possible traffic jam and will also perform predictive analytics to determine the possibility of traffic jams, so that avoidance strategies could be implemented in time. Such automation of critical functions in obtaining real-time traffic analytics will ensure better management of traffic by the concerned authorities.

data.projectName: Molecular Surveillance of Ticks and associated Livestock Pathogens
data.projectDigest: The goal of this project is to understand how non-harmful bacteria living in the gut of a tick affect how harmful bacteria and parasites are spread by ticks. To do this, we will collect ticks as well as blood samples from the animals infected by the ticks. We will then do an analysis of the ticks and blood samples to detect which diseases and non-harmful bacteria are present in the ticks and their host animals. Finally, we will do a statistical analysis to quantify the affect of the non-harmful bacteria on the diseases. We will also use the location from which each sample was taken and what diseases were found there to do a geographical analysis which will produce maps showing high-risk areas for those diseases. Our research can then be used to help develop new strategies for controlling the spread of diseases carried by ticks.

data.projectName: Characterization of Pathogenic Bacteria from  cultured Fish in the farms of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
data.piUniversity: Kohat University of Science and Technology, Kohat
data.projectDigest:
Fish are chief source of nutriention for the human population around the globe. Fishes have a sound immune system under optimum/favorable circumstances but overcrowding making compromised their immune. Bacteria are the dominant pathogens in aquaculture systems. No fish specific antibiotics are available till to date therefore the antibiotics currently in use for other vertebrates are utilized in aquaculture. In Pakistan, the aquaculture sector is still infant but the country has abundant freshwater resources so there is a great potential for further utilization of these resources. However, one of the major issues halting the progress of this industry is the widespread prevalence of pathogenic bacterial disease, which limits the aquaculture production resulting in huge economic loses. The fish farming industry of Pakistan is based mainly on Cirrhinus mrigala, Cyprinus carpio, Labeo rohita, Catla catla, Ctenopharyngodon idella, Hypophthalmichthys nobilis and Hypophthalmichthys molitrix species.
Information about the pathogenic bacterial burden and diversity of species is important for the development of effective preventive management strategies. Moreover, it helps in the prediction of possible disease outbreaks. Analysis of organs of fish in the farms of Pakistan is therefore necessary.  So, the present study will characterise pathogenic bacterial from various farmed fish of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

data.projectName: Development of small scale olive harvesting machine for Pothwar region’s  farm setting
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Olive cultivation is gaining popularity due to its high profit as compared to conventional farming system. The Punjab government has launched an initiative worth Rs 279.88 million in collaboration with the USAID to turn the Pothwar region in to 'Olive Valley.' Pothwar Region possesses ideal climatic conditions and land for commercial cultivation of Olive orchards. Government of Punjab has a plan to develop this tract as Olive Valley and to support this vision a project with cost of Rs 2782 Million is being implemented. To translate this dream into reality, 15000 acre was being brought under olive valley cultivation over a span. In Pothwar, generally farmers have small land holdings and cannot bear high tech and expensive imported olive harvesting large machinery. Other main reason is topography of the Pothwar area, undulating hilly area large machinery is not feasible. In current study a small handy machine will be designed and fabricated for undulating hilly areas to replace manual labors with mechanical system for easy, early and economical olive harvesting.

data.projectName: Waveguide Slot Antenna with Enhanced Radiation Pattern Characteristics for X-band Applications.
data.projectDigest:
Waveguide slot antenna are widely used in satellite communications, radar systems and various other high power wireless transmission systems. These systems mostly require antennas with broad bandwidth, high efficiency, high gain and high power handling capability. The potential candidate to achieve all these requirements is waveguide slot antenna, due to absence of dielectric losses and radiation losses as compared to other planar, printed antenna arrays. 
The proposed project is focused on design and development of waveguide slot antenna operating in X -band (8.2 – 12.4 GHz). The focus of research work will be on WR-90 based rectangular waveguide slot antennas integrated with planar structures, developed through novel techniques (metamaterials (MM) or frequency selective surfaces (FSS) or electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) surfaces or superstrate etc) to further enhance the gain of conventional rectangular waveguide slot antenna. Furthermore, integration of dielectric lens for enhancement in waveguide slot antenna will also be studied.

data.projectName: Study of Advanced Glycation End Products (AGEs) Inhibitors in Local Vegetables & Fruits & their Isolation for treatment of Diabetic Complications.
data.projectDigest: Diabetes and associated complications are a major threat to human health, among which Advanced Glycation End products are especially more common. AGEs forms irreversible cross links with protein backbones such as collagen and elastin as they accumulate in tissues at an accelerated rate in diabetes. Glycation is the major cause of spontaneous damage to proteins in physiological systems. A variety of natural and synthetic inhibitors have been discovered that can prevent AGEs formation. This study is designed to find out the effect of different indigenous plant (Fruits & Vegetables) extracts on AGEs formation both in vitro and in vivo. A plant extract (Fruits & Vegetables) with anti-diabetic and anti-glycation activities will then be subjected to fractionation via HPLC to isolate the active component which will finally characterized by NMR/GC-MS.

data.projectName: Schiff Bases as potential therapeutic agents
data.projectDigest:
Schiff bases are considered as basis of medicinal chemistry due to their extensive biological and pharmacological uses and have prodigious prominence in medicinal arena. They possess inimitable physicochemical and biological activities such as antibacterial, antifungal, anticancer, anticonvulsant, anti-inflammatory, antiviral and antitumor activities. In this study we will synthesize Schiff bases using different substituted aldehydes and ketones utilizing previous reported protocols with little modifications. Structure elucidation of synthesized Schiff bases will be carried out by different spectroscopic techniques.
Nanoparticles (NP) are composed of three layers i.e. The first layer is surface layer which may be functionalized with a variety of small molecules, metal ions, surfactants and polymers, second layer is the shell layer, which is chemically different material from the core in all aspects, which is a third layer of NP. Owing to such exceptional characteristics, these materials got immense interest of researchers in multidisciplinary fields specially in biological and pharmaceuticals. In this study, we will functionalize the silver nanoparticles by selected semicarbazone and thiosemicarbazone organic ligands. The characterization of synthesized nanoparticles will be carried out with the help of TGA-DSC, SEM, AFM, XRD and Zeta potential. 
The synthesized derivatives and their silver nanoparticles will be screened for different activities such as antibacterial, anti-fungal, antioxidant and enzyme inhibition activities such as urease.
Docking studies will be performed for different biological targets. In-silico studies for the evaluation of pharmacokinetics and toxicity of newly synthesized derivatives will be performed by FAF-Drugs3 software

data.projectName: Eco biological role of Syrphids (Hoverflies: Diptera) to establish the synergies in selected agro-ecosystem of Punjab, Pakistan.
data.piUniversity: Government College for Women University, Sialkot
data.projectDigest: Agriculture is 2nd largest sector and backbone of national economy. It provide 75-80 basic needs of human beings at Pakistan. Insect are important group of agriculture biodiversity, comprises of 58% of living organisms. Aphids cause a definite decline in crop yield by damaging crop plants. To control the pest species and to increase crop yield, use of chemicals in crops is a regular practice, which is of course effective but are not environment friendly, because they not only damage the pest species, but also destroy the natural enemies of cropland. Syrphids belonging to order Diptera of insects perform dual functioning, pollinator (adult), and predator of aphids (larva). To determine the diversity of insect fauna is regular practice among researcher. The innovation of this research is to utilize the potential of Syrphids to control the pest population. Development of molecular markers of selected species will be taxonomic tool, and also for relevant fields of study. In proposed study relative abundance of Syrphids, predatory potential against pest species in cropland will be determined. This will not only control the pests, but also to increase the crop yield, it will lead towards sustainability developmental goals, to reduce poverty and to establish sustainable agroecosystem.

data.projectName: Optimizing the Bioconversion of Organic Fraction of Municipal Solid Waste to Organic Fertilizer and Volarizing its Application for the Ecological Restoration of Caralluma tuberculate
data.piUniversity: Kohat University of Science and Technology, Kohat
data.projectDigest: The current project is designed along with the collaboration to Water and Sanitation Services Company (WSSC) Kohat to convert the organic waste into a nutrient organic fertilizer by using various composting methods including in-vessel and trench (pit). For various composting methods such as in-vessel, a laboratory scale compost bioreactor made-up of plastic will be used to produce organic fertilizer. Likewise, for trench composting, pits will be made with dimension of 2 feet long and 2 feet deep into the soil that will be filled with the feedstock to make the compost. Furthermore, the produced compost will be applied in solid and liquid form for testing the growth potential of Caralluma tuberculate under greenhouse pot cultivation. C. tuberculata is consumed both as vegetable and medicine, and exported to various cities inside and outside the country. Using compost in solid and liquid form (compost tea), C. tuberculata will be tested through greenhouse cultivation to explore its growth potential. Furthermore, chemical analysis of different treatments of cultivated C. tuberculata will be performed to compare it from nutritional and medicinal point of view. Combination of these studies will identify potential conservation strategy for ecological restoration of C. tuberculata and socio-economic uplift of local people.

data.projectName: Inhibtion of CD7 in Resistant Triple Negative Breast Cancer Cell with THZ1 and Neutraceuticals
data.projectDigest: Cancer is considered by type, progression and management to be the most intriguing of human diseases. Cancer develops in the lobules, ducts, fatty tissues or fibrous connective tissues of the breast defined as the breast cancer (BC). The onset of breast cancer in women is well above that in other cancers, both in developed and developing countries. Data indicates that breast cancer is the leading cause of death in women (13.0%). Among three types are estrogen and progesterone receptor positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) positive breast cancers and triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). In addition, drug resistance is prominent across all types of breast cancers. Cycline-dependent kinase (CDK)7 is essential for transcription and function by phosphorylation of the RNA polymerase II (Pol II) c-terminal (CTD) domain for transcription initiation. Inhibition of CDK7 has shown promising results against breast cancer studies. The combinatorial antineoplastic effect of THZ1 and neutraceuticals (curcumin) against CDK7 inhibition will be examined in preclinical models to improve the efficacy of THZ1 in case of normal and resistant TNBC. In this proposed research, synergistic effects of THZ1 and neutraceuticals will be determined by examining the different oncogenic proteins expression and effect on cell cycle.

data.projectName: IIsolation, purification and characterization of antifungal and nematicidal peptides from Bacillus species.
data.projectDigest: Plant pathogenic fungi and nematodes are major destroyers of crop products by lowering nutritive value, reducing active metabolites and bringing various biochemical changes in plants. Use of synthetic agrochemicals could be an effective method to reduce plant pathogens. The extensive use of pesticides is creating number of complexities in the environment and on other beneficial organisms. Bacillus species are well known for their plant protective activity against pathogens including both fungi and nematodes. It is due to their genetic potential for synthesizing variety of unique metabolites. Recently antimicrobial proteins from different organisms including bacteria gain attention for their ability to antagonize pathogenic bacteria and fungi. Bacillus species have ability to synthesize number of such antimicrobial peptides.  However, there is a need to discover more peptides with antifungal and nematicidal potential from indigenous strains that can be use as bio-pesticide. Therefore, this study is planned to screen, isolate and characterize the antimicrobial peptides from Bacillus origin against destructive plant pathogenic fungi and parasitic nematodes.  The outcomes of this study would have a great impact in the pest management with bio-friendly strategy. That would lead to the development of a new class of bio-pesticides.

data.projectName: Molecular approach for genotyping and sequence analysis of Canine Parvovirus disease in Dogs
data.projectDigest: Dogs have been tamed by man long ago; they have strong affiliation with each other since evolution. At present, the improved socioeconomic structure has allowed people to own their favorite dog breeds as pets, which tends to increase the canine population as well. Problems associated with infectious diseases in dogs have been known since ancient times. Canine parvovirus CPV2 is the main etiological agent of severe gastroenteritis in dog population and is endemic worldwide. Parvo is of particular concern for puppy owners due to the severity of symptoms and the weak immune systems of younger dogs. Canine parvovirus is a highly contagious viral disease that can produce a life-threatening illness. The virus attacks rapidly dividing cells in a dog’s body, most severely affecting the intestinal tract. Parvovirus also attacks the white blood cells, and when young animals are infected, the virus can damage the heart muscle and cause lifelong cardiac problem. Parvovirus is extremely contagious and can be transmitted by any person, animal or object that comes in contact with an infected dog's feces. It is common for an unvaccinated dog to contract parvovirus from the streets, especially in urban areas where there are many dogs. Highly resistant, the virus can live in the environment for months, and may survive on inanimate objects such as food bowls, shoes, clothes, carpet and floors. Some of the signs of parvovirus include lethargy; loss of appetite; abdominal pain and bloating; fever or low body temperature, vomiting and severe often bloody, diarrhea. Persistent vomiting and diarrhea can cause rapid dehydration, and damage to the intestines and immune system can cause septic shock. Most deaths from parvovirus occur within 48 to 72 hours following the onset of clinical signs. La

data.projectName: Investigating the Genetic and Functional Aspects of Spastic Paraplegia in Pakistani Families
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest:
Elucidating the molecular basis of genetic diseases is critical to understand disease pathogenesis, identification of therapeutic targets and the development of effective treatments. Spastic paraplegia is clinically and genetically a diverse group of neurodegenerative diseases with a prevalence of 3–10/100,000 in most parts of the world, making it the second most important group of motor neuron diseases. Unfortunately, no specific therapy is available for spastic paraplegia. Genotypic and phenotypic heterogeneity and the challenge in diagnosis demand that this disorder should be investigated on a molecular level in the local population. 
The overall objective of this project is to investigate the genetic basis of spastic paraplegia in Pakistani patients using cutting-edge next-generation sequencing techniques (such as exome sequencing/ gene panel sequencing) and to understand the role of disease gene mutations in neuronal structures development and function.  Meanwhile, a gene-editing therapeutic technique (CRISPR/Cas) will also be used to explore its possible use for the restoration of the mutant gene using patient-derived fibroblast cell lines. The expected outcome of the proposal is improved diagnosis, disease prognosis, better understating of the disease mechanisms and possibility of therapeutic intervention.

data.projectDigest: The non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs NSAIDs are among the most commonly prescribed drugs in different arthritic conditions. The most widely encountered side effects of NSAIDs include stomach ulceration, gastrointestinal (GI) irritations, cardiovascular and renal toxicity. The topical administration of NSAIDs minimized the systemic adverse effects associated with these drugs. The topical preparations of NSAIDs approved in US and in Europe are associated with local skin reactions. The nano-emulsions drug delivery systems have certain advantages in increasing bioavailability of the active drugs. The smaller particle size, high stability and lesser surface tension, the nano-emulsions hardly allow the precipitation of the active drugs and helps to cross the barriers of dermis membranes.
