data.projectName: Cancer Genetics: National program for disease modeling, phenotypic investigations and drug screening
data.projectDigest: The Genetic diseases like Cancer, diabetes, Alzheimer’s disease, intellectual disabilities, mitochondrial genetic disorders and many other genetic syndromes are one of the major contributors to human sufferings. Firstly, to alleviate humans from genetic disorders we need to understand disease development process and its mechanisms. Secondly, the disease response towards present and future drugs have to be continuously monitored because their long-term use allows the pathogen and especially cancer cells to develop resistance against drugs. Thirdly, disease related biomarkers have to be developed to enhance the early diagnosis of diseases. The question is how do we do this? As human, we need other organisms as disease models. The disease models include animal (e.g. mouse), organoids and other cellular models like iPSCs and isogenic cells derived from various cell lines. The cellular models are cheaper and easier to generate, faster, easy to maintain and stored in frozen formats. This project will be well integrated effort to generate disease models by genome editing via CRISPR-Cas9 and transposon and to maintain as national resource in Pakistan. The disease models will used to study disease development process and mechanism which will result in potential drug targets and then will be used in drug screening process.

data.projectName: Developing Abiotic Stress Resistance in Rice Through the Role of Cation Channels
data.projectDigest:
The alarmingly increasing human population needs an increased food production to the extent of 50% by 2050; however, the plan is greatly frustrated by a series of abiotic and biotic stresses. Drought, low temperature, salt and osmotic stress, oxidative stress, flooding and heavy metal toxicity are a range of factors which affect the productivity of many crops. The factors lower the production by about 50% by these factors [1]. Among these factors, drought and salt stress are the most common ones. Drought is affecting about 30% of the world’s land [2] while 20% of cultivated land is affected by salinity [3]. Moreover, about 10 Mha land has been taken over by salinity every year [4]. Different plants are differently affected by these stresses. Some are tolerant and show resistance while others are sensitive and are highly affected. Most of the cereals crops, for example, rice are sensitive to these stresses. In Pakistan 4.2 million hectares of land is affected by salinity. Most of the affect land is in agriculturally important areas and causing great losses to the country’s economy.
Better K+ nutrition could be a strategy for improving crops tolerance against drought and salinity [5]. This could be achieved either by the addition of enhanced K fertilizers [6] or by improving plants ability to absorb maximum K from the medium [7]. Various channel and carrier proteins, such as, TPKa, TPKb and AKT1 are involved in the absorption and translocation of K in plants. data.projectName: Development of Sustainable Biogas Supply Chain Network for Karachi Cattle Colony
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
The increasing population, urbanization, and climate changes have affected energy security. The more dependence on fossil fuels needs to be substituted with the more use of renewable energy sources. The biogas production has been observed to be a practicable way. It has been showed that biogas production has significant economic, environmental and social benefits. Furthermore, being a developing country and the signatory of Kyoto protocol and other international energy agencies, Pakistan has been making efforts to reduce dependence on energy production through fossil fuels and promoting renewable energy to make sustainable economic growth.
It is found that the Karachi cattle colony has enormous potential to produce biogas. Therefore, this project aims to develop the optimal biomass supply chain for this region considering the economic, environmental, and social objectives. This research will be carried out in two phases, the first phase includes the identification of potential locations for the installation of biogas plants considering the economic, environmental, and social aspects. In the second phase, multi-objective supply chain network optimization models will be developed to optimally transport animal manure from dairy farms to proposed biogas plants to produce biogas considering economic, environmental, and social aspects.

A comprehensive definition of dyslexia was approved by the British Dyslexia Association (BDA) Management Board in 2007. According to this definition (BDA, 2007), “Dyslexia is a specific learning difficulty which mainly affects the development of literacy and language related skills. data.projectName: Designing enzyme cocktail from locally isolated alkali-thermostable cellulolytic and xylanolytic microbes for second generation ethanologenesis
data.projectDigest: Extreme on-rise economic crunch prevailing in Pakistan, demands the establishment of sustainable energy production technologies. However, the main impairment for commercialization of bio-based materials is the insufficiency of low-cost cellulolytic/hemicellulolytic biocatalysts to transform biomass poly-sugars into fermentable mono-sugars completely for further production processes. In this regard, directed evolution represent as a swift and economical technique for creating mutant enzymes with enhanced cellulosic/hemicellusosic potential and extensive variability, as necessisated in this proposed project. Libraries from local alkali-thermophilic microorganisms will be recruited and then their cloning will be done in Escherichia coli to obtain processive LCB hydrolyzing enzymes. Further employed to random mutagenesis by directed evolution is hoped to improve enzymatic activities for cellulose and hemicellulose degradation several folds. The metabolically engineered cellulases/hemicellulases cocktail (CHEC) to hydrolyze various LCB substrates with maximum digestion/saccharification will hope to play a pivotal role in the development of up-scale saccharification and ethanol fermentation processes for high throughput value.

data.projectName: Identification of Inhibitors of TTDA-A/ p8 Protein: An Approach towards Treatment of Cancer
data.projectDigest: Cancer is the second leading cause of mortality worldwide. One of the most effective ways of curing cancer could be interrupting protein–protein interactions (PPIs), which are responsible for controlling biological processes. However, they are also challenging pharmacological target.  Present study is designed to study the modulation of TTD-A /p8 dimerization by small molecules. P8 is smallest subunit of TFIIH complex. It is a multi-protein complex involved in the transcription of class I / II genes and DNA repair. The subunit p8 is a recently validated as an ideal anti-cancer target. It can switch between homodimeric and heterodimeric form after interacting with subunit p52. The heterodimer shares the same tertiary fold as that of p8-homodimer. Heterodimerization of p8 with p52 is essential for maintaining structural integrity, cellular concentration and NER activity of TFIIH complex. As transcription and NER are reported to be up-regulated in cancers, targeting the dimerization site of p8 is an intelligent way to disrupt the PPIs among the TFIIH subunits and thereby reducing the aforementioned activities in cancerous cells. In silico studies will be done initially followed by biophysical techniques. This will be followed by chemical shift mapping to get further structural insight into protein ligand interaction.

data.projectName: SUSTAINABLE E-COMMERCE FOR COMMUNITY-BASED TOURISM (CBT) IN PAKISTAN: AN ECONOMIC, CULTURAL AND SOCIAL PERSPECTIVE
data.projectDigest: The current project aims to develop a mechanism for sustainable growth in the tourism industry of Pakistan, having great potential to improve their relative position in the international market. This project will revisit the whole value-chain such as among the tourist, local people, suppliers and stakeholders by uplifting the local communities by providing direct entrepreneurial activities such as selling local products to tourist and online payment possibilities directly to local people. We will develop an E-commerce mechanism with the help of city governments and other private institutions. Public-private partnerships will provide technological infrastructure for typical rural and remote tourist areas by promoting their local products nationally and internationally, thereby helping to alleviate poverty and contribute to countries’ economies. Current project divided into three phases and various stages. Each stage comprised of different methodological sections such as to collect the data, review of Govt. existing projects, and interaction with the local people, strategy formulation, operational activities and finally implementation stage.

data.projectName: National Level Trust Evaluation Framework
data.projectDigest: It is trivial to have a National trust based framework to identify the internal attacks including denial of services, bad mouth and on-off attacks. The trust mechanism is also detecting malicious nodes and isolate them.  In this project, we propose to develop a trust based framework for National Trust Mechanism for Pakistan existing data communication networks. Moreover, the proposed approach is more suitable to monitor internal data traffic and prevent from malicious and internal attacks. The proposed framework is suitable to monitor all National Level data communication traffic.  The trust framework proves itself as a solution to prevent organizations from security threats especially against denial of services, bad mouth and on-off attacks. Moreover, the trust framework provides national cyber security monitoring platform at low cost and novel solution without trust on open source tools.

data.projectName: Child Labour in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Province: Exploring the Gaps Between Policy and Practice
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is signatory to the International Labour Organization (hereafter referred to as ILO) and United Nations (UN) Conventions on Child Labour and the Rights of the Child. Consequently, the Constitution of the country not only prohibits slavery, forced labour and human trafficking but alsobars all sorts of organizations (be that public or private) as well as individuals to engage and/or force children under 14 years of age in any sort of paid or unpaid employment. According to ILO, over the past few years child labour in Pakistan has witnessed an exponential growth rate such that the number of children under 14 years of age during 2012 transcended well beyond 12 million in Pakistan. The observed trend in child labour thus calls into question the effectiveness of child labour laws and policies in Pakistan that is why the Government of Pakistan or the relevant state institutions have grappled to cope with the unprecedented rise in child labour despite the implementation of well-crafted laws and policies concerning Child Labour and Rights of the Child? The proposed project aims to address the aforementioned question through an analysis of existing child labour policies and the implementation mechanism thereof. The proposed study will be conducted under three sub-objectives. First and foremost, the study to analyze the existing policies at both Federal and Provincial levels in terms of compatibility of the so-called policies with those enshrined in the UN Charter and/or its agencies such as ILO as well as the discrepancies between such polices and the informal norms prevalent within our society. Secondly, the study will focus on the implementation mechanisms (planning and executions phases will take center-stage in such analysis) and the efficacy of the relevant departme

data.projectName: Profiling of Reproductive hormone during Mastitis and Association of Reproductive Hormonal levels with the Incidence of Bovine Mastitis
data.projectDigest: Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and adjacent FATA (Federally Administrated Tribal Area) are rich in livestock resources valuing US $10 billion where dairy cattle are used as a tool for subsistence. However, disease of economic importance like mastitis has drastically decline the reproductive and productive performance of these dairy animals. Also reduction in successful pregnancies per A.I application has been recently observed. Additionally, this malady has adverse impact on the visible estrous recognizing efficacy resulting in the embryonic death or irregular returns. Theses adverse impacts might be the result of either the imbalance of reproductive hormonal level or the functional modification made by the mastitic-suffered dairy animal to regulate reproductive functionality. Balanced body-hormonal profile, active and potent immune system and stress free environment is crucial for better efficiency and milk production as well as for elimination of pathogens. Thus in this project, keeping in view our local environmental and management conditions,  we will investigate the level of inflammation, its impact on the overall hormonal profile, mainly sex related hormones (estrogens, progesterone, prostaglandins etc), immune status and reproductive performance. The knowledge obtained will be utilized to formulate a combinational therapy to speed of recovery of mastitis animals and minimize mastitis-related losses in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Children Understanding of Their Subjective Well-Being in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: In order to understand children’s subjective well-being in Pakistan, the proposed project will build a comparison that how native and migrant children in Pakistan define their well-being. In Pakistan, there are differences in social, cultural and economic aspects of the well-being. Therefore, this study will also explore the similarities and differences in the conception of their subjective well-being and identifies the key features of diversity among them. For achieving this purpose, the proposed research will be conducted through qualitative and quantitative studies in which various child-centered methods and approaches will be used with the local and immigrant children between 8-12 years of age in the populated states and cities in Pakistan. Furthermore, Focus Group Discussions and in-depth interviews would be conducted with the participants in to three stages. In first stage, the quantitative data would be compiled around 1000 sample with the natives and 1000 migrants’ children. In the second, stage about 8-14 FGDs will be conducted in each category with 6 children participants in a discussion. Half of these FGDs will be from native children and other half from the migrants’ children. In the third stage the research teams will conduct 100 in-depth interviews (50 from natives and 50 from migrants’ children). Besides, 10 interviews will be conducted with the relevant experts. The data will be analyzed through qualitative data software such as MAXQDA and Nvivo for qualitative data. We will use SPSS for the quantitative data analysis with the help of rigorous statistical models.

data.projectName: Sustainable approach for the development of functional fibers from waste of cotton and blended textiles
data.projectDigest: The economy of Pakistan is based on production and export of textile goods manufactured from cotton whose production, usage and disposal have very high environmental impact in terms of consumption of water, fertilizer, pesticides and generation of effluent. If somehow, we are able to enhance the life cycle of cotton fibers, the environmental impact during fiber production and their disposal can be significantly minimized. Therefore, the present project is based on concept of circular economy where the waste cotton fabrics will be recycled into regenerated fibers/textiles to address the issues of sustainability.  Moreover, value addition will be made in regenerated fibers to make them antibacterial, UV protective etc. so that more meaningful products could be made from them. The successful completion of this project will help textile industry of Pakistan to enhance exports by complying with sustainability demands of international brands.

data.projectName: Harnessing of sheep wool keratin using ionic liquid assisted probe sonication for development of GTR dental membrane
data.projectDigest: Keratin like other biopolymers has intrinsic biological activities and biocompatibility. Moreover, it can be cast as films, sponges and hydrogels for biomedical applications. Keratin derived from sheep wool will be a good source for fabrication of Guided Tissue Regeneration (GTR) membrane, being derived from animal, has excellent biocompatibility, cell adhesion, biodegradability and easy in processing. Keratin has a complex three-dimensional polypeptide chain structure which is difficult to dissolve in common solvents. Various methods like alkali hydrolysis, sodium sulfide treatment and enzyme treatment etc. are used which has issues of environmental, cost or pretreatment time. Therefore, it is needed to dissolve keratin in green solvents like ionic liquid assisted by probe sonication instead of conventional heating to process the keratin in a short time as well as to decrease the energy consumption. After extraction and dissolution of keratin, hydroxyapatite (the main constituent of bone) will be added to prepare their mixture. By adjusting the rheology of the mixture, it will be electrospun to prepare their nanomats. The nanomats (GTR membrane) will be characterized and evaluated for their mechanical, biological and stability properties. Rabbit animal model will be adopted for in-vivo analysis. The biocompatible GTR membrane will be provided to the dental clinician for the end user testing.

data.projectName: Development of System for intelligent planning and scheduling of hospitals
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is a developing country containing limited number of well-equipped healthcare facilities which are not satisfactory to provide services to the patients economically. In most of government as well as public sector hospitals, treatment of patients require different specialists which are available in hospitals for limited time. In addition, hospitals have limited resources with the constraint on their maximum capacities, constraints on surgeon’s availability and priority level constraint of patients. In these circumstances, there are long queues in hospitals and patients have to wait for long duration for proper treatment. Further, due to limited resources and use of manual methods of planning and scheduling in hospitals, cause extra delays to patients, inefficient utilization of hospital resources and ultimately causes poor services to patients and increase loss. data.projectName: Targeted sequencing of carcinoma related genes in colorectal carcinoma using Next Generation Sequencing
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
Molecular profiling of tumors has become a priority in the era of targeted therapy and personalized medicine. It is being incorporated into clinical cancer practice worldwide. Colorectal carcinoma (CRC) is a common and lethal malignancy. In Pakistan, CRC is amongst the top five malignancies in both genders. A number of mutations are involved in its carcinogenesis and prognosis. Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) performs sequencing of millions of small fragments of DNA in parallel. Targeted sequencing by NGS can be employed to provide mutational data in CRC for clinical use. 
The proposed study will be carried out on 43 patients of CRC at AFIP/ NUMS, Rawalpindi. The genomic DNA after extraction from formalin fixed paraffin tissue sections will be subjected to NGS by Illumina MiSeq Analyzer for 11 CRC related genes. Analysis of sequencing results will be done by using bioinformatics tools. Clinically significant variants will be reported.
The aim of our research project is to test feasibility of targeted sequencing in CRC by NGS. This will be done for the first time in Pakistan. It will generate mutational data of CRC in our population. It will enable  us to screen and provide genetic counseling to patients with familial risk of CRC. It will help in assessment of targetable genes for selection of chemotherapy and prediction of treatment response. The overall benefit would be establishment of a local NGS testing facility in the country to help clinicians for targeted management of colorectal carcinoma patients.

data.projectName: DESIGN AND DEVELOPMENT OF CELLULOSE BASED PACKAGING FILMS FROM SUGARCANE BAGASSE USING IONIC LIQUID SYSTEMS: A GREEN APPROACH FOR BIODEGRADABLE FILM PRODUCTION
data.projectDigest: Biodegradable packaging materials preparation from annually renewable lignocellulosic biomass are regarded as promising materials which could replace petrochemical based polymers, reduce global dependence on fossil fuel sources, enhance sustainability and eco-efficiency. Approximately, 100 billion metric tons of biomass are generated worldwide. Sugarcane bagasse is a cellulose rich by-product of sugarcane juice which remains undervalue due to high availability. Cellulose is the major biopolymer component of lignocellulosic biomass and regarded as an inexhaustible source of raw materials for generation of environment friendly and biodegradable products. Nevertheless, the full scale utilization of cellulose is warded off in that cellulose is extremely difficult to be dissolved due to its compact structure. In recent times, ionic liquids (ILs), molten organic salts, has emerged as green recyclable solvent for effective processing of cellulose on account of their unique properties such as negligible volatility, low toxicity, and thermal stability. Recently, the aprotic co-solvents at optimum conditions with ILs demonstrated significantly higher dissolution compatibility and chemical modification of cellulose, which have shown potential for production of cellulose based film from renewable biomasses. On account of the current increasing demand for eco-friendly packaging materials and green chemistry guided potential, the current project is initiated to develop plasticized all cellulose active packaging film from sugarcane bagasse. The plasticized all cellulose biodegradable film would present a promising alternative as bio-based plastic for application in packaging materials.

data.projectName: Instititutional History of Lahore High Court, 1947-2018
data.projectDigest: Lahore High Court is the oldest and largest court of Pakistan, with strength of sixty judges. It has a long history of 150 years and has played an important role in government, social and legal spheres of the Punjab. Its administrative and legal precedents are followed by other high courts of Pakistan. So Lahore High Court has gained a position of role model for other judicial institutions of Pakistan.  Pakistan judicial system is a hierarchy from top to bottom, in this regard Lahore high court as an institution performs two kinds of functions; first it is a court of appeal for the decisions of lower courts, and second it administratively controls the subordinate judiciary. It frames rules and regulation for judges and administrative staff of lower judiciary. It also keeps an eye on the lower judiciary to dispense justice and provides guidance to subordinate judiciary in case management process. This court worked as a West Pakistan High Court from 1955-1970 under Establishment of West Pakistan Act, 1955. This was a unique period in the history of this court because the whole territory of One unit was under Lahore high court and played an important role to control crimes in society of the Punjab.

data.projectName: Behavioral and Neurochemical profiling of selected Phytochemicals   in animal model of drug addiction
data.projectDigest: Polysubstance abuse, using alcohol and nicotine affects a broad range of population, primarily young ones and has serious socio economic and health implications. Recently some plant origin compounds have been documented to have a significant effect in ameliorating neurological and behavioral effects of Polysubstance abuse. The aim of the project is to screen the potential of selected natural pure Phytochemicals, with documented neuroprotective effects, on acquisition and expression of alcohol and nicotine dependence using animal models of Polysubstance abuse. Selected groups of animals  shall be made dependent on alcohol, nicotine and alcohol plus nicotine and effect of different doses of selected pure natural compounds shall be screened on various stages of addiction and its effect shall be explored on key neurotransmitters, i.e. serotonin, dopamine, and nor adrenaline implicated in key brain areas, primarily involved in addiction. The effects of selected compounds different doses shall be screened on alcohol, nicotine, and alcohol plus nicotine induced Sensitization, dependence and withdrawal. The effects of different doses of said compounds shall be assessed on various behavioral parameters of polysubstance abuse, like withdrawal induced anxiety, depression, altered pain perception and cognitive impairments. The project shall assess the effects of various doses of the compounds, in acute, sub-acute, sub chronic and chronic treatment protocols on various behavioral, neurochemical and harm reduction aspects of the polysubstance abuse.

data.projectName: FORMULATION DEVELOPMENT OF IONTOPHORESIS BASED TRANSDERMAL DELIVERY SYSTEM OF ANTI MIGRAINE DRUG
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Migraine is one of chronic disease with high socioeconomic burden affecting 19% of population.  The characteristic throbbing headache last for 2-72 hours along with associated symptoms. Zolmitriptan acts on 5HT receptors that relieves migraine. The drug is 40-48% bioavailable with half-life of 2.8-3.7 hours.  The optimal therapy should provide relief from pain within 30 minutes followed by complete relief in 2 hours and complete subsidence of associated symptom in 24 hours. One of ways to improve bioavailability and better therapeutic outcome is to formulate transdermal drug delivery system through hydrogel or microemulsion formation with or without iontophoresis application. In Pakistan no such work has been reported and drug is marketed as 2.5mg tablet only. Very few innovative pharmaceutical products are available in Pakistani market resulting in market saturation of conventional dosage forms. The development of novel delivery system will not only improve patient compliance but will benefit pharmaceutical industry through increase in revenue and export around globe will boost the economy. 
The methodology will involve preformulation studies followed by formulation development and characterization of quality attributes using various tests. Assay will performed using validated method. Formulation will be optimized based on in vitro release and permeation profile of developed formulation. Stability studies will be performed on stabilized formulation. The developed Optimized formulation will show good bioavailability, improved therapeutic outcome and patient compliance and benefits directly Pharmaceutical manufactu

data.projectName: Identification and Characterization of genes for Primary Microcephaly
data.projectDigest: Primary microcephaly (MCPH) is a neurodevelopmental disorder mainly characterized by microcephaly present at birth and nonprogressive mental retardation. The incidence of MCPH is ~ 1 in 30 000 in consanguineous populations but less in non-consanguineous populations. So far, twenty five MCPH loci and corresponding genes have been identified. The focus of this project is to estimate prevalence of known MCPH associated disease genes and identification of novel genetic variants. The main objective is to provide basis for the establishment of genetic screening and eradication of primary microcephaly from  Pakistan

data.projectName: Effect of Ni doping in Cobalt Ferrites in structural Parameters, Cationic Distribution and Dielectric Properties”
data.projectDigest: The proposed project is very fruitful from the economic and industrial point of view. The most contribution of that project is in the field of material sciences for the formation of ferrite materials designing and their dielectric properties. Ferrites are magnetic materials having spinel structure. Ferrites are transition metal oxide having formula MFe2O4 (Where M= Mg, Zn, Co, Mn). They have high value of saturation magnetization Ms but as particle size reduce from bulk to Nano, their saturation magnetization decreases. Cobalt ferrites are semi hard material. It lies between hard and soft magnetic material have magneto strictive application like in actuator and sensors while nickel is soft magnetic material which also have potential technological application like manufacturing core of transformer, data storage, recording heads, microwave equipment’s and in other electronic devices. Our focus will be to explore the ferrites materials on experimental and theoretical basis for optoelectronic and thermoelectric devices applications. For experimental point of view, we explore spinel ferrites, cobalt ferrite, Co, Bi, Mn and Ni ferrites are specifically fascinating, because of their high coercivity, high cubic magneto-crystalline anisotropy, moderate saturation magnetization and outstanding chemical stability, appropriate band gap and suitable mechanical hardness. Nano ferrites can be used for the photo degradation of various dyes from water due to its multifunctional properties. In order obtain the desire results and objective of the project we will also apply ab-initio method based on density functional theory (DFT), our main focus is to study and design Ferrite materials on theoretical basis with excellent electronic properties, high thermal/electrical conductivity.

data.projectName: Development of an indigenous model for using Internet of Things for development of smart Learning Environment in higher education institution of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The current project aims to develop an indigenous model for using Internet of Things for Smart learning Environment. The project will be divided into three phases, one is to explore ground realities for availability and access of internet of things for generation of smart learning environment; at second stage perceived value stakeholders give to these facilities for using internet of things to create smart learning environment will be identified and at third stage a contextualized model based on information of previous two data will be developed. The sample of the study for stage one will be universities, both public and private recognized by Higher Education Commission, while the sample for second phase of the study will include students, teachers and administrators of these universities. Random, ratio and cluster sampling techniques will be applied as per demand of strata of the study. A range of instruments will be used including observation checklists, survey questionnaires and interview schedules. The tentative data analysis will be test from descriptive and inferential statistical techniques, including Exploratory Factors analysis, structured equation modelling, mean differences and ANOVA. The data will reveal actual situation and perceived values given by stakeholders thus providing basis for development of model. This model will provide a sustainable theoretical implications of the concept for future research studies

data.projectName: Green and Sustainable Protection of Food Staples Against Mycotoxin Contamination using Engineered Bio-fungicides
data.projectDigest: Pakistan falls among the developing countries with longer summer and relative humidity that render it susceptical towards mycotoxin contamination of food and agricultural products. The staple food particularly during storage under high temeprature and humid air becomes contaminated with fungal strains producing toxic metabolites. The intake of mycotoxin contaminated food causes immune deficiency, hepatic, and renal carcinomas; the most common cancers in adult Pakistanis. There is divesity of physical, chemical, and biological techniques to prevent food for microbial infestation but majority of these techniques either use synthetic chemicals, thermal radiations or offer partial protection. The present study will introduce a green and sustainable management of mycotoxin while applying Nano-Biofungicides of Indigenous sources. For this purpose, plant bioactives extracted from medicinal plant will be screened for their fungicidal character which will be further enhanced through conjugation of plant bioactive with nanoparticles of Zn, Ag, and Zno nanoparticles. The final nanobiofungicides will be applied for the protection of staple food against mycotoxin contamination. The ability of Nanobiofungicides to protect food against microbial growth and mycotoxins contamination will by determined by monitoring mycotoxins level in stored food at different Intervals. The outcomes of present project will provide a sustainable and green mycotoxin management.

data.projectName: Multimodal Emotion Perception for Human-Robot Interaction in Proximity
data.projectDigest:
A proposal is hereby submitted for funding of a research project.  In this research project, we are investigating new approach in human emotion perception for human-robot interaction (HRI) in proximity.  Human emotion perception refers to the ability to understand the emotion of a human when we are interacting with him/her.  In human-robot interaction, this is an important ability for a robot to be able to effectively interact and serve its human counterpart.  As humans, we use multiple senses for better perception. Literature have revealed that using multiple senses for perception can improve decision accuracy. However, there has been no significant work done that address both accuracy and processing speed of a human emotion recognition system to enable it to be used for real-time live video analysis. Such system can find its use in HRI as well as other important areas such as security surveillance, marketing assistant, students’ interest analysis within classroom, and diagnosis in mental health. 
The research will apply deep learning models to achieve high recognition rate for human emotion with multimodal signals.  Deep learning models training are computational demanding and requires high performance computer with multicores graphic processing unit (GPU).  Without the GPU, each training would take days to complete.  Deep learning research requires significant trials to refine the model and hyper parameters. data.projectName: Optimization of culturing conditions and harvesting techniques for microalgae biomass production in  wastewater for biodiesel
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Microalgae are eukaryotic, photosynthetic, aquatic organisms simplest in structure that grow in variety of habitats ranging from wastewater to freshwater and marine water under range of environmental conditions. They assimilate CO2 and very small amount of inorganic nutrients can be cultivated in wastewater to treat it and are source of variety of valuable commercial products viz., fertilizers, aquaculture feed, animal feed, paper, medicine, biopolymer, biodiesel, bioethanol, biohydrogen, biomethane, carotenoids, cosmeceuticals and cosmetics and biocathode. The availability of all these commercial products is mainly based on the high biomass production and efficient harvesting of various algal species. Therefore, the present study aims to optimize culture conditions for the biomass synthesis and evaluation of various harvesting methods and biochemistry of algal species.  For this purpose algal species will be collected from natural habitats, isolated by streak plate method and will be cultured in the wastewater preanalyzed for the nutrient contents. The algal biomass will be harvested by various methods and carbohydrate, protein and lipid contents will be determined by standard methods. The crude lipids will be used to produce biodiesel by transesterification process.  The biochemical characterization of biodiesel such as Gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC-MS), Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (NMR), cloud point, density, viscosity, pH, moisture content, flash point, pour point and cloud point will be done. The outcomes of the study will be helpful for the phycologist, aqua culture industry and biotechnologist for commercial utilization of algal biomass.

data.projectName: Critical Sustainable Aspects of CPEC Northern Corridor: Employing GIS and Statistical Technique to Assess the Influence of Landslide Susceptibility, New City Settlement and Pavement Feasibility
data.projectDigest: The China Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) is a multi-dimensional project that is not just going to affect the economic situation but also the political and social situation between both countries i.e. China and Pakistan. This research will focus on three significant factors that might affect the sustainability of the project’s infrastructure in the future or the present and the methods to identify these problems. Landslides have a high threat to human life and they lead to severe damage to properties, infrastructures and natural resources. Thus, susceptibility maps can be used as a basic tool in managing land and planning of future construction projects in areas such as this, to protect human life and infrastructure from landslides. Another problem is the settlement of city and construction. This study will analyze the changes in settlements beyond merely assessing the conversion of non-built-up land into built-up land. Further, the pavement has a specific lifespan and for this type of road (CEPC) which will be used for heavy duty vehicles for trade, the feasibility measurement is a basic need.

data.projectName: Development of graphene electrochemical filter modified with metal oxides: a novel system for onsite  treatment of industrial wastewater
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest: Water scarcity is an urgent problem that affects many countries. There is therefore an urgent need to develop highly efficient processes to treat wastewater, if feasible, on-site and in real-time. The on-site treatment strategy would also provide a systematic tool to protect the ecosystem in contaminated water resources and eventually public health. Considering many limitations in developing countries such as Pakistan, treatment processes should be characterized with minimal efforts, less chemicals, and low energy inputs (i.e., technological needs). The overall goal is to develop a sustainable on-site decontamination system for water contaminated with emerging contaminants such as Pharmaceuticals, pesticides and dyes. The Electrochemical process has many advantages to meet the technological needs. To implement the on-site decomposition of refractory emerging pollutants and achieve the technological needs, this study aims to fabricate and characterize multifunctional electrocatalytic filters with composite metal oxide layers coated on porous PTFE (polytetrafluoroethylene) substrate, for subsequent use in solar power electrochemical reactor. This would give huge benefits to on-site treatment efforts due to utilization of solar radiation (solar panel) as a sole energy source for the process. Moreover, the coupling of other technologies with mixed oxide anodes filter would result in enhanced filtration and electrochemical oxidation.

data.projectName: Exploring the anti-inflammatory and anti-oxidative effects of HNG, a synthetic analogue of mitochondrial peptide Humanin in a rat model of psoriasis and establishing the role of mitochondrial epigenetic modulation in oxidative stress injury

This study shall generate novel scientific knowledge and ultimately contribute to emerging health modalities. Also, it has the potential to enhance collaboration between healthcare research programs and the pharmaceutical industry in the future.

data.projectName: Policy Perspective Regarding Crop Insurance as a Regulatory Mechanism in the Context of Climate Vulnerability
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan’s agriculture is prune to diverse climatic change, price volatility, poor market mechanisms and uncertain levels of yield, among many adverse factors. Therefore, a fully designed insurance policy mechanism should be prevalent, so that farmers could perform better by earning stabilized income, invest more in agriculture, and manage risks in a better way. However, crop insurance is still underdeveloped in Pakistan. 
The proposed research hence has been designed to analyze the existing crop insurance practices in Pakistan and compare it with other countries. Resultantly, propose a ground for a well-developed public-private crop insurance program on the basis of evaluation of consumer/farmer’s willingness to pay and willingness to accept.

data.projectName: Generating stable zebrafish knockout model featuring human GLI3 based morphopathies and inborn errors of development
data.projectDigest: Approximately one quarter of all birth defects are due to aneuploidy, 10% are due to copy number variations and 30% are due to mutations in single gene and the 30% are multi-factorial. Assessing the full detail mechanism of such anomaly’s human is understandably a daunting task for scientists and physicians. So, a suitable model is extremely useful to dissect the molecular pathways required for key physiological process to understand the etiology of such diseases. GLI3 is one of the most important morphogen. . The developmental anomalies in GLI3 mutants that causes GCPS and PHS are diverse, discrete, variable and pleotropic. This mutational correlation was markedly facilitated by analysis of  mice and other model organisms  gene knockdown data. However, given embryonic lethality in homozygous knockout mice, no murine model studies could present enough evidence to explore the extensive role of Gli3 in tissue functioning and morphology. Embracing the remarkable role of Zebrafish in other human diseases So, it might help to bridge this gap and provide a suitable model for human GLI3 morphopathies. It will not only increase our knowledge to understand how diseases contribute to normal human development and individual variability in common disease susceptibility, prognosis and development but will also provide a road map to translate this windfall into new therapeutics in future

data.projectName: USE OF BENEFICIAL MICROORGANISMS FOR TOMATO LEAF CURL VIRUS DISEASE AND HIGH TEMPERATURE TOLERANCE IN TOMATO PLANTS
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is an agricultural country and feeds more than 200 million peoples. Among vegetables, tomato is central item and facing significant problem of inflorescence shedding due to lack of heat tolerance in summer season crop which is coupled with tomato leaf curl virus disease. Beneficial microbes both bacteria and fungi will be collected from extreme hot conditions of Cholistan desert and will be characterized on the basis of modern molecular tools. These beneficial microbial communities in the form of beneficial endophytes will be utilized to assist the tomato plant to bear higher temperatures which usually damage the inflorescence. Use of such beneficial plant growth promoting organisms will boost the immunity of tomato plant against tomato leaf curl virus disease as well. Finally, a product will be launched on commercial basis to handle issue of higher temperature and virus disease among tomato growers to significantly uplift yield of summer crop through this environment friendly approach.

data.projectName: Utilization of Indigenous Plant Acacia nilotica (Babul) as Anticoccidial, Immunomodulatory and Therapeutic agent in Controlling Poultry Coccidiosis Disease
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest:
Livestock is an important sector of Pakistan as having share of 60.54 percent in agriculture and 11.22 percent in GDP (Economic Survey, 2018-19). In growth of Livestock sector, poultry sector has played an important as growth rate in poultry was recorded at 10-12% per annum. Besides increase in its production progress of poultry sector has been facing challenges due to incidence of endemic diseases including Parasitic, Bacterial and Viral Diseases. Among parasitic diseases, Poultry Coccidiosis is a major parasitic disease caused by Eimeria protozoa having various species. This disease is mostly controlled by synthetic anticoccidial drugs. Unfortunately, due to development of synthetic drug resistance due to their irrational use this method has become ineffective. 
Acacia nilotica locally known as 'Babul' or 'Kikar' plant is found in abundance and is widely distributed in South Punjab region of Pakistan. It has been well known for its medicinal uses due to its potential anti-oxidant activity of polyphenolic compounds and essential oils. 
Therefore, present study is also a part of probing innovative therapeutic agents from abundant indigenous plant Acacia nilotica which can be utilized for its easily availability, cheap source for development of drug against diseases of poultry like Coccidiosis in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Identification, screening and characterization of genes involved in Oligodontia and Hypodontia genetic disorders
data.projectDigest:
The genetic disorders are rarely reported anomalies found in the general population of the world. But unfortunately and socio-ethical circumstances of cousin marriages traditions in Pakistan, there number in proportional ratio are largely found than any other country of the world. So working on such molecular anomalies are of worth being important in the present scenario. Being a researcher of human molecular biology and genetics; I have designed this research project for rarely reported genetic aberrations in remaining countries but hugely important for Pakistani population i:e oligodontia and hypodontia. Ectodermal dysplasias (EDs) are the most common term used for genetic abnormalities linking with the ectodermal organs/appendages. It may be syndromic and non-syndromic and varieties found in the mode of inheritance. The specific type of ED that is linked with dental anomalies include syndromic/non-syndromic oligodontia and hypodontia disorders. Hypodontia is the most prevalent craniofacial malformation in humans. Hypodontia designates a tooth abnormality characterized by the absence of fewer than six permanent teeth, while oligodontia targets the congenital absence of six or more permanent teeth.
I have proposed this present studies based on the linkage mapping analysis and sequencing of the already reported candidate genes. It’s also deal with the exclusion mapping and may also lead to genome wide scans if required. Furthermore, it may proceed toward genes/exome sequencing as well as expression analysis and functional analysis if required.  Objective of this study is to determine the prevalence of syndromic/non-syndromic oligodontia and hypodontia and to identify the types of associated dental anomalies in the permanent dentition of affected individuals in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Environmentally sustainable dyeing of garments
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
In Pakistan, textile and garment industries are amongst the most important manufacturing sectors contributing as major portion of the total exports. In recent decades, local textile and garment consumer market in Pakistan has also grown significantly. The major business growth has been focused at apparel, denim, towel and hosiery. Country’s garments industry in particular is expanding even more due to very high demand of value added quality end-user products worldwide. The garment manufacturing industry is cotton and its blends specific industry where currently synthetic dyes are mostly used for coloration. 

	Cotton dyeing industry is known to be one of the most wastewater-pollution producing industries. That is mainly due to use of synthetic colorants (such as direct dyes, reactive dyes and vat dyes) and inorganic salts. Most of the synthetics dyes are either carcinogenic, non-biodegradable, toxic and/or producing polluted wastewater. Numerous efforts have been taken to reduce the pollution in multiple directions. This project is a part of such efforts and has been undertaken to develop sustainable methods for dyeing of garments. The target industry is Pakistan’s garment manufacturing, processing and washing industries.

data.projectName: Lignin valorization for the production of renewable aromatics
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: Pakistan being an agrarian economy produces almost 139 million tons of agricultural residues (biomass) in the form of husks and straws left over from sugar cane, rice, cotton and drupe endocarp of many fruits (walnut, peanut, peach). Despite its abundance and huge energy potential, biomass is highly underutilized in Pakistan owing to technical challenges around its collection, selective depolymerization and upgrading. Where there are some reports about the attempts to utilize such residues for the production of electricity and biogas in Pakistan, none of them addresses their potential for the derivation of organic renewable chemicals despite the fact that chemicals have a higher value (>$1000/ton) than liquid fuels ($200-400/ton) or electricity ($60-150/ton). Present project aims to utilize expertise of the PI in catalyst design and catalytic biomass conversion to develop highly active catalysts for the valorization of lignin into renewable aromatic compounds.  Valorization of lignocellulosic biomass is an active R&D area all around the globe. The work proposed here has the potential to favorably tip the economic viability of future biorefineries into profitable enterprises, thereby enabling the large-scale production of renewable aromatic-based chemicals.

data.projectName: Design of architecture and devices for cost effective and industry compliant ultra-dense WDM passive optical network roll outs
data.projectDigest:
Information and communication technologies has played a key role in uplift of modern society. It is continuously fueling the growth by enabling every individual and business, more informed and connected on high data speed connections. An important segment of technology to increase the connection speed for end users is passive optical networks. 
Our group is working for network architectures and devices for future passive optical networks. Utilization of ultra-dense wavelength division multiplexing (UDWDM) techniques to improve spectral efficiency of Optical fiber along with coherent detections is potential solution for achievement of +10Gbps connectivity for each user.Using this forum of NRPU, we propose the work of design of devices and architecture for future PON networks compliant to modern industry standards for compatible rollouts of future PONs with contemporary network layouts.

data.projectName: Numerical and Analytic Solutions of Fractional Order Obstacle Boundary Value Problems
data.projectDigest:
Many physical phenomena can be described by mathematical models that cannot have exact solutions and as well as we cannot provide the existence of solutions. In such cases we need approximate solutions and that gives us some hope about the existence of solution through numerical computational techniques. Such problems exist as initial and boundary values problem from all disciplines of physics. We have the techniques like Series and Numerical Solutions such as: Homotopi Perturbation Methods, Variation Iteration Methods, Adomian’s Decomposition Methods, Finite Difference Method, Finite element methods etc. We are able to discuss, the results accuracy, stability and convergence of solutions of mathematical models.  
Currently, the Fractional Boundary Value Problems are hot issue by researchers in the mathematical research world. Motivated by the current flow of research we are going to explore some hidden feathers of Numerical and Analytic Solutions of Fractional Order Obstacle Boundary Value Problems.

data.projectName: Development of engine cooling system based on modified coolant characteristics.
data.projectDigest:
Any indication of engine overheating is a serious proble, so the best course of action is to shut down the engine to prevent further damage to it. Driving a car with an overheated engine can warp cylinder heads and damage the radiator or internal engine parts such as valves, camshafts and pistons. Even letting the engine cool for an hour and topping off the radiator with a 50-50 mix of antifreeze and water may not fix the problem.

An efficient engine cooling system can ease the problem of overheating. One way to improve the engine cooling system is to use the more reliable coolant whose thermal properties are better than conventional coolant such as water, Ethylene Glycol, etc. Currently, nanofluids are considered as in automotive engine coolant alternatives. These nanofluid can definitely increase the thermal effieciency of cooling system. The core motivation of this project is to design engine cooling system which can use conventional and hybrid nanofluids.

The core motivation of this project is to design engine cooling system which can use conventional and hybrid nanofluids.

data.projectName: Antibiotic resistance modulation in poultry pathogens by using essential oils of indigenous medicinal plants.
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Poultry and Livestock are chief contributors of livestock production around the globe. Irrational use of antibiotics in poultry and livestock in Pakistan is creating resistance to frontline antibiotics. Recent estimates predict that economic losses incurred due to infections of multidrug resistant (MDR) pathogens are immeasurable. Elevating occurrence of microbial resistance demands plants as an alternative remedy. Essential oils are secondary metabolites from medicinal plants. The present project is designed to evaluate antibiotic resistance modulation in poultry pathogens by using essential oils of different indigenous medicinal plants. The work will be completed in two phases. In PHASE I essential oils from eight plants will be extracted and chemically characterized. Field strains from poultry will be isolated, characterized. Multiple Antibiotic Resistance (MAR) index of essential oils will be determined. All essential oils will be tested for their sensitivity alone and in combination with resistant antibiotics against clinical isolates which have shown multiple drug resistance (MDR) isolated from poultry.  During PHASE II safety profile of essential oils will be evaluated. Cytotoxic potential will be determined through MTT Assay and geno-protective evaluation through COMET Assay. Antioxidant evaluation will be evaluated through DPPH and FRAP assays. The data collected will be analyzed using SPSS software.

data.projectName: Piscicidal Evaluation of Plant Extracts on Histopathological, Haematological, Biochemical Parameters and Genotoxic Responses in Common Fishes of KhyberPakhtunkhwa
data.projectDigest: The indiscriminate use of pesticides contaminates the water bodies, thus affecting the health of aquatic organisms. Therefore, to find out alternative for pesticides and herbicides used in agricultural practices that effect aquatic organisms. In our study fish will be used as a model organism that will be collected from Hazara division and will be transported to the laboratory of Zoology Department, Hazara University Mansehra, within plastic bags containing water and oxygen. In laboratory, they will be acclimatizing for about 2 weeks before the start of experiment. After acclimatization period ten fishes will be selected randomly, stocked in each aquarium and will be subjected to different concentration of selected plants extracts labelled as, E0, E1, E2, E3, E4 and so on depending upon the number of experimental groups. E0 will be served as control group while E1, E2, E3, E4 and so on will have different concentration of selected pesticide. After experimental time period fish will be removed from aquaria and anesthetized in clove oil in order to analysis the effect of selected pesticide on their hematological, histological, biochemical parameters as well as genotoxicity. For hematological analysis about 2ml blood will be collected from caudal vein of both control and experimental groups and will be analyze through hematology analyzer. Similarly, for biochemical analysis blood will be collected from caudal vein of fish, drawn into clotted tubes which will be analyzed through various biochemical tests. For the determination of histopathological alterations fish will be sacrificed in order to dissected out the selected biomarkers i.e. liver, gills, brain, intestine and kidneys etc. these biomarkers organs will be placed in a saline solution to prevent it from decaying out

data.projectName: Supercritical Carbon Dioxide based Green and Clean Extraction of Plant Bioactives and their Biological Characterization
data.projectDigest:
Plants are the rich source of volatile and non-volatile bioactives bearing a wide range of biological and sensory applications in food, cosmetics, and pharmacological industries. The isolation, purification, and characterization of these natural bioactive have been one of the crucial research areas of prolonging the history of analytical and separation science. Traditional extraction techniques like heat reflux, hydrodistillation, aqueous and organic solvents based extraction have been ruled out for their limited recovery rates, toxic characters and end product quality concerns. 
Supercritical fluids have low viscosity, low surface tension, and high diffusivity, which means these fluids (liquids) can diffuse like gases but their ability to dissolve substrates is similar to liquids. Although a wide range of gases can behave as supercritical fluid over a certain range of thermodynamic conditions, carbon dioxide-based supercritical fluid (SCO2) seem to be more fascinating for their non-toxic, non-flammable, and availability in pure form. The SCO2 can find its applications as an extraction or reaction solvent in food science (the decaffeination of coffee, extraction of floral fragrance, colorants, functional bioactives, and lipids), cosmetics (essential oil and aroma compounds), bio- and functional materials (cleaning and curing), nano-systems, natural products, biotechnology, fossil and bio-fuels, pharmaceuticals, polymers, and microelectronics.

data.projectName: Fabrication of a Novel Prebiotic and Protein Based Nano Hydro Gel for Encapsulation of probiotics and their food applications”
data.projectDigest: Nowadays, population burden, rising healthcare cost and poor quality of life in developing economies are the fueling facets that triggered the development of functional foods. Probiotics are offered as novel buzzword for functional food industry due to their vast health potential. Probiotics are live dietary microbial supplement that beneficially affects host health through its impact on the gastrointestinal tract (GIT). However, the efficacy of probiotics depends on offering a specified number of viable cells on consumption until they reach their target site in the gastrointestinal tract. This project is aimed to fabricate novel carbohydrate/protein based nanogels for delivery of probiotics. We will use inulin a polysaccharide along with whey protein isolate to produce novel complex for entrapment of probiotics. The resultant nanogels will be studied for their encapsulation efficiency, size and stability through Dynamic light scattering (Zeta-sizer), Morphological characterization by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Thermomechanical properties using a differential scanning calorimeter (DSC) Molecular characterization by ATR-FTIR spectroscopy. Finally, yoghurt will be prepared to compare the viability and survival of free and encapsulated probiotics cells during processing and storage conditions. The whey proteins/polysaccharides nanogels delivery system can offer advantages to food industry due to its additional protection and potential prebiotic effect.

data.projectName: Introducing green/environmental sukuk through a multi-generational financial model to achieve inter-temporal pareto efficiency: A bifocal approach
data.projectDigest: Environmental change impacts every part of the planet, and the magnitude and danger do not escape. The Green Bond is proving to be a very useful tool in the green investment strategy. As a democratic Islamic republic it should be of high priority to conduct shariah compliant Islamic research emphasizing the replacement of interest (discount rate) but it can only be achieved if there is a benchmark available that can replace discount rates. The project is aimed at Introducing green/environmental sukuk through a multi-generational financial model to achieve inter-temporal pareto efficiency. For the stated purpose, the study will design a financial model (multi-generational) and will run simulations based on MATLAB, R, Python. Furthermore, linear regression analysis will be conducted to prove the hypothesis using, eviews, smart PLS etc. Designing a multigenerational mathematical model to prove our stated objective can be challenging, as there are no studies conducted in the domain as well as, the study will also face benchmark issues to replace discount rates. The study will also identify a special purpose vehicle for the green sukuks. Moreover, the study will also develop an app for the green sukuk to develop crowdfunding green sukuk platform.

data.projectName: Synthesis and characterization of new metal organic  frameworks (MOFs) for energy conversion and storage
data.projectDigest: Global climate is suffering from the adverse impact of excessive fossil fuel usage. It is now the need of the hour to turn to clean energy production and storage. Although alternative energy production has hit the market, it will take time to fully replace the traditional energy sources. The energy storage (batteries and supercapacitors) and capping greenhouse gas emissions is also striving for more understanding and better materials. Metal and organic based highly porous materials known as metal organic frameworks are one of the most promising candidates for cleaner fuel like hydrogen production and storage due to incredibly large surface area. With structural modifications they can exhibit versatile properties such as carbon dioxide conversion to hydrocarbons and storage.  Anticipating great potential of this class of functional materials, our work is designed to synthesize novel metal organic frameworks and investigate them in diverse applications from energy convesion to storage.

data.projectName: Investigation of Graphene Quantum Dots for gas sensing applications
data.piUniversity: Government Sadiq College Women University, Bahawalpur
data.projectDigest:
Early warning detection of harmful gases is the key role to be detected.Graphene has shown excellent sensing performance for various gases such as NH 3, NO2, H2O, CO and such other gases. However it is also supposed that if graphene is converted to graphene quantum dots, then exposure surface area to the adsorbing gas would be increased making it more accurate and efficient gas sensor. Therefore, in this project, Graphene and GQDs will be synthesized at host university by CVD and microwave-assisted solvothermal approach respectively. The samples will be characterized by XRD and SEM and to investigate the gas sensing ability of GQDs, the samples will be sent to our collaborator in Link?ping University Sweden. 
Moreover, if the expected results are achieved, then in future, it is planned (and already discussed) that this work will be industrialized with the help of our collaborator in Linköping University Sweden.
One better use of these sensors in Pakistan would be in places like mines where we have to detect harmful and explosive gases like hydrogen and nitrogen etc. So, these gas sensors will be productively benefit our Country in a good way.

data.projectName: Intelligent Traffic Monitoring and Control System
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest: People living in large cities of Pakistan are badly affected by the menace of road traffic. Road traffic problems not only add to the  everyday stress of the commuters, but also cause road accidents, resulting in injuries and deaths,  environmental pollution and wastage of fuel and valuable money because of inefficient flow of traffic. This asks for an improvement in the traffic management system. The world, and many of its advanced countries, are now moving towards the concept of Intelligent Transportation System, where intelligence is rendered to traffic management. This project aims to create a prototype of one of the components of an Intelligent Traffic System i.e. Smart Traffic Lights. By making use of  sensors, electronics and communication technology, a system will be created which will interface with the traffic lights installed on a fourway road junction, and which will control the traffic lights with respect to the traffic intensity on different roads. Thus, traffic lights at day and night, and similarly in peak hours vs non-peak hours will adjust according to the load on different roads, thereby maximizing the flow of traffic and minimizing the delay experienced by the commuters.

data.projectName: Pesticide Free Fodder for the Milking Animals through Transgenic Approach.
data.projectDigest: Sorghum is an important fodder crop in Pakistan. It performs better under stressed water conditions and saline soils in comparison to maize. Multi cut forage sorghum hybrid is cultivated in Pakistan on around 0.4 million ha using over 8,000 tons of seed most of which is imported at a very high cost limiting its wider adaptability. Import dependence also keeps this crop at the mercy of multi nationals who are shy in conducting any local research catering the local needs. More than 40 species of insects have been recorded on sorghum with yield loses of 25 to 100%. Stem borer as most notorious insect pests reduces the yield up to 45%. Chemical insecticides are not the solution because it harms not only the health of plant but also damages the environment. The only successful approach is to insert insecticidal toxins from soil borne bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis. The use of novel Bt gene could be a potential candidate for insecticide resistance management strategies. Given the wide spectrum and different modes of insecticidal action from cry genes, the novel gene family that are obtained from B. thuringiensis strains could potentially be very useful as a biological control against borers.

data.projectName: Development of low cost and eco-friendly feed using oil seed meal-based diets supplemented with Amino acids, Taurine and Phytase to assess the growth improvement of major carp fingerlings
data.projectDigest: With the increase in human population and poor availability of food, intensive aquaculture is being flourished day by day and demand more for over efficient aqua feed. Feed comprises the principal operating cost in fish production and traditionally main protein source is the fishmeal. It is conventional protein source in aquaculture feeds, supports higher fish growth because of its protein quality and palatability. However, fish meal is often scarce and expensive, due to limited availability and high demand, leads to higher fish production costs. Hence, replacing fish meal with low-cost ingredients of protein-rich plant sources are the basic priorities for nutritional research. Increase in the inclusion level of plant-based nutrients tend to cause serious problems in fish in-relation to growth and overall performance. Presence of phytate in plant by-products decreases the bioavailability of amino acids, minerals and nutrients to fish, resulting in decreased fish growth and higher water pollution. Use of plant derived ingredients supplemented with taurine, amino acids and phytase in feed is very beneficial for the fish health. Three plant ingredients will be fed to major carps for estimation of overall-performance and genetic analysis of high-performance fish growth genes.

data.projectName: Assessment of Carbonaceous Aerosols in Gilgit-Baltistan Region: Trends, Characterization and Source Apportionment
data.piUniversity: Karakurum International University, Gilgit, Gilgit Baltistan
data.projectDigest: Carbonaceous Aerosols have been reported for their effects on visual, optical, chemical and aesthetic nature of air. Intensity and frequency of such effects have been reported to increase in developing countries like Pakistan. Substandard fuel consumption, agriculture practices, inefficient management of waste have been identified as potential source of carbonaceous aerosols in Pakistan. Previously, it has been concluded that atmospheric aerosols have increased the green house effects in terms of cooling and heating governed by climate forcing in South Asia. Although, environment inferences of carbonaceous aerosols in Pakistan have acquired attention but there is still lot to be understood qualitatively and quantitively about role of different types of aerosols especially carbonaceous due to lack of research studies and monitoring. A few studies have assessed the levels of carbonaceous aerosols in Lahore and Karachi cities only and none is performed in background/rural areas such as Gilgit-Baltistan. This study is mainly designed to check and re-confirm the involvement of substandard fuel consumption along China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) from Gilgit-Baltistan region which is under debate these days. A longstanding orderly data on carbonaceous aerosols loading from pristine region of Northern areas in Pakistan is still lacking in the literature. Advanced source apportionment techniques synergized by ground and space based remote sensing will accurately identify the actual sources of aerosols and will give us more reliable data. Most importantly this study will be a baseline study to assess the involvement of carbonaceous aerosols in the creation of winter-time haze layer over Gilgit city.

data.projectName: Investigation for harvesting large amount of piezoelectric potential from integrated surface
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: In present project our aim is to harvest large amount of piezoelectric potential from environment friendly natural resources. Zinc oxide based nanogenerators will be fabricated for harvesting piezoelectric potential. An alternative approach of integrated surface with high quality conductive adhesion layer will be applied for the fabrication proposed nanogenerators. The effect of surface integration ultimately harvest extensive amount of piezoelectric potential through the atomic force microscopy. Surface of substrate will be clean before deposition of conductive film on substrate then softly baked for excellent adhesion of film. Later on this conductive surface will homogeneously integrate by the nanoparticles and again baked softly for seeds adhesion. The growth solution will be prepared by dissolving zinc nitrate and hexamethylenetetramine in 200 ml deionized water with equimolar concentration and chemical bath deposition technique will be used for the synthesis of nanostructures. The crystalline quality and the orientation will be examined by using X-ray diffraction technique. The aspect ratio of structural architecture will examine by the scanning electron microscope. Atomic force microscope will be used in two different modes (taping mode and contact mode) for harvesting piezoelectric potential vertically and horizontally. This approach will open the new dimension for harvesting piezoelectric potential from very small surface.

data.projectName: Connection between N-acyl homoserine lactone (AHL) mediated quorum-sensing (QS) signal molecules and Biofilm formation
data.projectDigest: Quorum-sensing (QS) is a mechanism based on several chemical signal molecules produced and utilized by microbial cells in order to contact and communicate with each other. Mainly, QS-signal molecules help microbial cells to express specific genes that perform a major role in several activities such as pathogenicity, antibiotic production and biofilm formation. There are several types of QS-signal molecules produced by different microbial communities. Among these signal molecules, N-acyl homoserine lactones (AHLs) are the most significant QS-signal molecules produced by large number of Gram-negative bacterial communities to carry out several types of physiological and biological activities. The main purpose of the current research proposal is to carry out screening of clinical isolates particularly biofilm forming bacteria to produce AHL mediated QS signal molecules and to investigate association between AHL mediated QS mechanism and biofilm formation. Initially, bacterial strains will be isolated from different clinical samples following standard methods. All the clinical isolates will be confirmed for biofilm formation and will be identified based on 16S rRNA using PCR technique. Finally, biofilm forming clinical isolates will be screened for the production of AHL mediated QS signal molecules. The production of signal molecules will be confirmed by two different bacterial biosensors such as Agrobacterium tumefaciens A136 and Chromobacterium violaceum CV026. Moreover, reversed phase thin layer chromatography (RP-TLC) will be used to identify AHL-QS signal molecules. Furthermore, association between AHL mediated QS signal molecules and biofilm formation will be monitored at each stage of biofilm with standard methods.  Mainly, QS mechanism in antibiotic resistant biofilm

data.projectName: ACADEMIC COLLABORATIVE SCHOLAR NETWROK BASED ON HETEROGENEOUS BIBLIOGRAPHIC DATA OF PAKISTANI UNIVERSITIES
data.projectDigest: In the fast growing world, the retrieval of scholarly big data (SBD) requires an efficient system for management of research documents that could be used by academics, researchers and industrialists. The rapid development in information technology has made it possible to shift from traditional storage of documents to digitalized environment for better management and quick access to SBD. The SBD is generated from scientific documents, technical reports, project proposals, and research publications where researchers, academicians and industrialists share their experiences, new techniques and results of their scientific experiments. The availability of SBD to larger community of researchers in their relevant context is critical and still an open research area. data.projectName: PREVENTIVE AND THERAPEUTIC EFFECTS OF SPIRULINA PLATENSIS IN ANIMAL MODEL OF SCHIZOPHRENIA
data.projectDigest:
II. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Spirulina platensis (blue-green algae) is one of good nutritional supplement and food which constitutes of high amount of protein containing essential amino acids, good source of antioxidants, vitamin-B complex and other nutrients such as essential fatty acids and various phytopigments. This blue green algae has been claimed to possess various neuroprotective activities such as antioxidant, anti-hyperlipidemic, anti-diabetic, anti-viral, anti- inflammatory, anti-cancer, immunomodulatory and many more. Schizophrenia (SZ) is recognized as a neuropsychiatric disorder in humans with shortened lifespan and signi?cant impairments in social and vocational functioning. The major psychotic symptoms of SZ mainly cluster into three categories: positive symptoms (hallucinations and delusions), negative symptoms (emotional blunting, social withdrawal, anhedonia) and third category (cognitive dysfunction). N-methyl D-aspartate receptor antagonist (Dizocilpine) is one of the best drugs that can mimic full spectrum of SZ and can develop an animal model of the disorder. Although, the clinical use of various antipsychotics are the approved treatment for the psychotic symptoms of SZ but they also exert adverse effects. Thus, there is an urgent need for novel treatments with negligible adverse effects.

data.projectName: Data Mining based Cancer Diagnosis System
data.projectDigest:
Cancer is a leading cause of death globally which is ranked on 2nd number. Over 9.6 million deaths are caused by cancer in 2018, cancer is a group of diseases in which cell growth is abnormal causing a neoplasm also known as tumor anywhere in body. 
Medical science has started to utilize artificial intelligence algorithms and data analysis techniques to aid the diagnostics and treatment plans of cancer patients. A significant amount of data is generated during the cancer treatment. The proposed method aggregates multiple data streams into an integrated diagnostic system including radio graphic images, pathology, and electronic health records. This is a computer-assisted diagnostic system for cancer detection and diagnosis. CT images, MRI, PET scan are used for development, training, and evaluation of this method. The algorithm will be shown multiple medical scans of organs with malignant tumor, benign tumor, and no tumor. Hence, the proposed algorithm will learn how to detect nodules in the organ, and how to identify which nodules are likely to be malignant. Automated analysis of CT scan overcomes the shortcoming of manual CT scan analysis which is time-consuming, inefficient, and a difficult task. It is an attempt to automate the process in the initial interpretation of biopsy and then detection of nodule location in the organ. This method can deliver better than radiologists at cancer screening and can facilitate in making faster and better-informed decisions.
