data.projectName: Financial Data Library (FDL)
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Zulfikar Ali Bhutto Institute of Science & Technology (SZABIST) University, Karachi
data.projectDigest: it is inevitable for the emerging economies to develop the financial markets in order to achieve long term sustainability. Unfortunately, Pakistan’s financial markets are quite under-developed, due to the asymmetric information, which hinders the confidence of local and foreign investors to pour-in their funds which consequently affects the liquidity in the economy.  The dearth of financial information also leads to the absence of the derivatives markets and the least structured commodities and money markets.  This NRPU project of Financial Data Library (FDL) is an attempt to solve the major obstacles faced in the financial sector of Pakistan and to boost the investors and savers confidence to pave a way to ease the flow of funds through the markets in an efficient way. We will attempt to provide a digital financial data library which is expected to improve the efficiency of the stock market and remove the mispricing to facilitate the flow of local and foreign funds which is essential for the accumulation of investment capital. FDL will be an extensive data library which will include risk factors used to devise the investment strategies all over the world and regularly updated annualized returns on portfolio based on different investment strategies in the context of Pakistan. Secondly, this FDL will also provide the appropriate definitions of financial variables within the context of Pakistan in order to develop a more comprehensive and coherent understanding of financial data relative to Pakistani financial sector. Furthermore, we will also construct Advanced Indices in the context of Pakistan such as Fundamental index and Smoothed Cap index which are widely applicable in developed markets but missing in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Isolation and characterization of pharmacologically important venom proteins from snakes of Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Research and development is the key to success for any country’s growth in the global market. Pharmaceutical industry is in dire need of new templates for drug design to meet challenges of finding treatments for various medical problems like dengue fever, antibiotic resistance, cancer etc. The proposed project “Isolation and characterization of pharmacologically important venom proteins from snakes of Pakistan” is a step to furnish new templates for drug design.
Nature has always been an intriguing source for drug design investigations. In this context, large number of pharmacologically useful molecules have been isolated and characterized from snake venoms. However, little investigation has been carried out on the venom from Pakistani snakes. Snake venom is a complex mixture consisting of hundreds of different molecules, which snakes use as a digesting and defensive tool. An interesting example of snake venom based drug is Captopril. It is an antihypertensive drug and was designed, using bradykinin potentiating peptide from a Brazilian snake venom.
In the present work, we want to focus on the isolation and characterization of bioactive venom proteins and peptides from selected snake species found in Pakistan. The venom samples will be collected with the help of local serpents.

data.projectName: Low Cost Smart  On-road Vehicle Emission Testing System
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is facing severely unhealthy air pollution conditions due to the rapid rise in air pollutants which are mainly coming from vehicle traffic, various industry zones and the agriculture sector. Very few serious efforts have been made in order to tackle this pollution issue. Lack of awareness from advanced technology and inadequacy of law enforcement are the major reasons for this unbounded problem. Active sensing of air pollutants such as methane, Nitrogen gas (NO) and Carbon-Dioxide (CO2) is of a great challenge due to the unavailability of suitable apparatus, accuracy of sensors, and absence of online vehicle engine health data. As a result, various solutions have been introduced such as import of electric cars, biogas based cars or usage of environmentally-friendly fuels. However, these solutions are very expensive due to high cost, and time taking therefore they become impractical for readily improving environmental conditions.  On the other hand, we need a cheap, effective and timely solution to tackle this issue. Advanced technologies such as embedded sensing devices, mobile/web software and Artificial Intelligence (AI) can be exploited to sense and test vehicle fuel emissions and notify car-owner through sensor report along with database update about the car's condition.

data.projectName: Modeling Based Evaluation and Solutions for Healthcare Infrastructural Aspects Against Various Earthquake Scenarios
data.projectDigest: Earthquake is one the natural disasters that has been seen to impact Asia significantly. Incidentally, Pakistan has many regions that lie on the fault line making it susceptible to this type of disaster. It has been seen historically that the region has suffered significantly at the hands of the adversities caused by earthquakes. The 2005 earthquake that devastated the northern regions is one of the deadliest disasters of its kind in recent history whose affects are still felt to this date. More than 70,000 fatalities along with millions of affectees have been estimated in available literature. In the context of the need of effective disaster management and the identified research gap it is seen that studies are still required to be conducted giving due consideration to the realities of the region of interest. This research aims to carry out region-specific research while considering localized constraints so that effective disaster management for this specific type of disaster (earthquake) may be achieved. This research will provide an insight about the capacity assessment of existing health care infrastructure and propose possible solution(s) (if/where needed) for better disaster preparedness.

data.projectName: Bio-Methane production using local municipal solid waste for green and sustainable environment
data.projectDigest: This study focuses on production of clean biogas (bio-methane) from municipal solid waste abundantly available in Lahore city. Recent study has approximated that city of Lahore is producing 67,230 tonnes/ year of organic composition of waste which can efficiently be processed for production of biogas. Lahore Waste Management Company (LWMC) claims that together with its partnering private companies, it collects 73% of this waste generated, and clean development Mechanism (CDM) is employed to certain extent. However, there is still ample potential to transform this waste into energy resource. This research project aims to provide clean renewable fuel attributing towards green and sustainable environment. The biogas will primarily be produced by utilization of organic solid waste material and membrane technology will be employed subsequently to capture CO2 from biogas thus confirming the clean combustion of biogas.

data.projectName: Factors Associated with Low-cost Opportunistic Breast Cancer Screening by Mammography in Resource Constraint Population of Urban and Rural Areas of Sindh, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Breast cancer when diagnosed at an asymptomatic stage makes treatment easier and cost effective with better survival as compared to poor outcomes of late stage breast cancer. Faced with an increased incidence of breast cancer and a limited budget for health care, it is difficult for the government of Pakistan to make decisions about offering breast cancer screening to all women equitably and cost effectively. Therefore, it is also important to identify factors, both barriers, and motivators, associated with screening as well as the risk profile of our women attending breast cancer screening programs. There is a dearth of research on understanding the scope of opportunistic mammography screening and evaluation for screening services at low cost. To fill this gap, this study aims to evaluate factors associated with low-cost breast cancer screening by mammography. A collaborative multidisciplinary team of epidemiologist, breast surgeon, radiologist, from different departments and hospitals will conduct a cross-sectional study in two facilities offering low cost mammography screening. Evidence based data of effective screening messages and programs for breast cancer screening mammography in our population will help formulate policies for effective promotion of low-cost screening mammography in Pakistan and early diagnosis and management of breast cancer.

data.projectName: Big Data for National Healthcare: Resource Creation and Real Time Decision Support System Development
data.projectDigest:
The present scenario of healthcare systems in Pakistan does not provide a unified and centralized data availability which could effectively be used for on-demand and timely information retrieval as well as future decision making. From electronic health records to sensor-based patient data and even social media, we have a huge sources of healthcare data scattered. Our aim is to create proper bench mark data resources and to develop real time decision support. The project would include collection and management of healthcare data from different sources including electronic patient records, IoT sensors and social media.  Following the emergence of machine learning and data science techniques, these datasets would prove to be more useful for researchers and at the same time enhance decision making for both government and private sector. As an example we can predict disease outbreak in an area by manipulating social media posts and feeds. We would involve different stakeholders from the academia, healthcare industry and government sector to collaborate as well as receive their feedback during planning and execution stages of the project.  
AI and big data analytics technologies are performing vital role in health industry. It reduces not only cost but saves significant lives. For improvement in their services different health organizations explore and analyze big data for healthcare. Health industries successfully implemented Big Data technologies in healthcare because they realized its potentials. The advantages of machine learning techniques on  big data platform gives flexibility and scalability to complex healthcare data i.e. in the form of organized, unorganized, semi organized data. Machine learning techniques are useful in disease survival prediction.

data.projectName: Molecular Dissection and Functional Analysis of the Genetic Architecture of Inherited Peripheral Neuropathies in Cousin Married Pakistani Families
data.projectDigest: Hereditary peripheral neuropathies are a large heterogeneous group of genetic disorders characterized by dysfunction of peripheral nerves (as opposed to those in the central nervous system). Patients suffering with these disorders show an array of symptoms including numbness, tremor, and impairment of balance, gait abnormality, spasms, itching, crawling, and pins-and-needles. The  overall prevalence of Hereditary peripheral neuropathies is 1:2500. In recent years, the use of so-called next-generation sequencing (NGS) has led to the identification of many previously unknown involved genes and genetic defects that cause neuropathy.  This project has been designed with the aim to use these new cutting edge technologies to dissect the genetic architecture of these inherited neuropathies in large Pakistani families and for  functional analysis of newly identified genes. Neuropathies, just like other genetic disorders are incurable in general and prevention remains the only choice for lowering the disease burden. Therefore the proposed work has the potential to better understand the gentic basis of neuropathy, improve molecular diagnosis and pave the way for genetic counselling and devising treatment modalities for  currently incurable neuropathies .

data.projectName: Nanoparticles Assisted Stem Cell for the Reduction of Liver fibrosis
data.projectDigest: Worldwide liver fibrosis is  among the top ten reasons of death .  Liver fibrosis in the alter stage lead to cirrhosis, cancer of hepatocytes, and eventually leads to death.  Currently the anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic medicine which are available in the market cannot cure  liver fibrosis successfully due to a lot of side-effects or  also have limited efficacy. However, liver transplantation is the only effective treatment for end-stage liver fibrosis. But unfortunately, shortage of donor livers, immune rejection and operative damage are the main problems . Therefore,  the need for development of new therapeutic strategies is the dire need of the day. In comparison, among various alternative therapeutic strategies, the process of stem cell transplantation is an invasive procedure, that could be performed easily and  limited potentially complications will be occur. currently the Stem cell therapy has attracted increasing attention as a promising treatment strategy for  regeneration of fibrotic liver. Nanoparticles (NPs), with their superior physical and chemical properties, have been widely utilized to assist stem cell therapy. The hypothesis of the current project is to co-administrate stem cell with nanoparticles for the efficient regeneration of liver fibrosis. With the help of NPs, stem cells  will be more potent to regenerate fibrotic liver. Besides that, NPs can also be used to enhance stem cell retention in liver. This strategy is unique and noval for the treatment of  liver disease  withe the help of  multifunctional NPs for cellular application. This project will help to develop novel cell-based strategies by understanding  the combine ability of stem cells with nanoparticles to reduce liver fibrosis and will help for clinical application in near future.

data.projectName: Staying at the Cutting Edge of Crisis: A Critical Perspective on the Rise and Emergence of Sub-Nationalism in Pakistan’s Discursive History
data.projectDigest: The present project is a critical and historical investigation into the rise and emergence of sub-nationalism – the Baluchi, the Bengali and the Pushtun – in the discursive history of Pakistan in order to understand its genesis, its principal political and ideological stance and how it is viewed and responded by the mainstream national(ist) narrative. The objective is to establish an intersection between the historical and literary archives with a view to understand the potential of sub-nationalist movements and how they have impacted on our sense of belonging to a national collective. Given the immense potential of various sub-nationalist movements emerging in different times of Pakistan’s history, the project is an attempt to reflect how can the political capital of sub-nationalisms with their diverse linguistic, ethnic and cultural identity be used in forging and strengthening a national collective without undermining their sense of distinction. In this way, the project is going to offer some vital insight into the legitimate and constructive political and symbolic capital of various sub-nationalist ideologies/ movements which can be used in the service of the polity/ nation-state). The insight of the project can be used in making national policies/programs which can offer equal and equitable opportunities to different ethnic, regional and linguistic entities who with their diverse and unlimited human and material potential, are crucial in the construction of a strong federation.

Given the immense potential of various sub-nationalist movements emerging in different times of Pakistan’s history, the project is an attempt to reflect how can the political capital of sub-nationalisms with their diverse linguistic, ethnic and cultural identity be used in forging and strengthening a national collective without undermining their sense of distinction. In this way, the project is going to offer some vital insight into the legitimate and constructive political and symbolic capital of various sub-nationalist ideologies/ movements which can be used in the service of the polity/ nation-state). The insight of the project can be used in making national policies/programs which can offer equal and equitable opportunities to different ethnic, regional and linguistic entities who with their diverse and unlimited human and material potential, are crucial in the construction of a strong federation.

data.projectName: TRANSFORMING THE URBAN FABRIC? A CASE OF HIGHLY QUALIFIED MIGRANTS RETURNING TO PAKISTAN
data.projectDigest: The literature highlights the vital role being played by the migrants in the demographic composition of larger urban centers. But still, there is a lack of understanding the relationship between the migrant’s practices and ongoing urban transformations. Likewise, return migrants could also go through a phenomenon of habitus dissonance and cultural shock on their return to the homeland. Return migrants have long been conceived as the drivers of change and development at the origin places. However, there is a contradictory scholarly debate on the notion of development and hence had pessimist views too towards this conception. Given the background, the proposed study will investigate the practices being carried out by the highly qualified migrants returned to Pakistan during the last five years and the implications of their performed practices for the urban transition.

data.projectName: Recognition of Urdu sign language by optimizing wearable sensors based on crisp fuzzified rules
data.projectDigest:
Any society’s progress in social welfare can be measured by looking at how well their disable population in integrated into becoming a useful member of the society. For a society where the disables are left dependent on others, will burden its economy, and halt their overall growth. Enabling disables is beneficial to all members of the society. And for a developing country like Pakistan, with its limited resources, and world’s fifth largest population of disables, their integration becomes a matter of utmost importance.
Mute, and Deaf-Mute people can easily be integrated into useful members of society. This will not only reduce their dependency on others, but also improve their quality of life. The only thing in the way of their progress is their ability to communicate. Even if they learn sign language, vast population of Pakistanis don’t understand sign language. So, their ability to communicate doesn’t increase significantly evening they learn sign language. Integration of disable people into the society becomes responsibility of every member of the society. 
This project proposes a wearable system that can recognize the sign language, and a speaker unit attached d which will speak out loud sign language. This way a mute, deaf-mute person would be enabled to a job where he can communicate his thought to people who don’t understand sign language.

data.projectName: Novel Lanthanide-Doped Luminescent Nano-Bioprobes and Their Biomedical Applications
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: Traditional cancer diagnostic protocols often fall short owing to the technical limitations in detection sensitivity and antibody performance. In this project, based onbackground-free luminescent biosensing of lanthanide-doped nanocrystals (Ln3+-doped NCs),we utilize versatile approaches for developing hybrid satellite nano-bioprobes based on Ln3+-doped NCs well surrounded with near-infrared absorbing dye (NIR-dye) and broad-band absorbing carbon nanodots (CNDs). The controlled synthesis, surface modification, developing satellite nano-assemblies and bioconjugation of Ln3+-doped NCs will be surveyed in detail. The luminescent mechanism of the Ln3+-doped NCs, as well as the local site-symmetry, electronic energy levels and excited-state dynamics of Ln3+ will be systematically investigated. Subsequently, efficient and practical nano-bioprobe will be selected to function as time-resolved or upconverting/down-shifting luminescence (UCL/DSL) bioprobe for ultrasensitive and specific detection of tumor markers such as carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and prostate specific antigen (PSA) in human serum and saliva, thereby laying the foundation for the applications of these nanoprobes in early cancer diagnosis. The developed luminescent nano-bioprobes are expected to exhibit much more superior features in PL intensity, photostability and sensitivity than traditional molecular probes such as organic dyes and Ln3+-chelates. Particularly, it is expected that the detection limit of CEA for human saliva samples finally reaches as low as 0.5 fM, which is record-low and fulfils the requirement of clinical assays, thus exhibiting great potentials in the fields of bioscience and clinical diagnosis.

data.projectName: Molecular epidemiology, genotyping and pathology of public health concern Chlamydia psittaci in birds
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Chlamydia psittaci is an obligate intracellular zoonotic pathogen responsible for a respiratory disease “avian chlamydiosis” in more than 457 species of poultry birds. The bacteria have 9 serovars and corresponding genotypes. In Pakistan so far, only one study has been conducted in District Faisalabad which showed a high prevalence of the bacteria in various birds. This indicates the high risk associated with this bacterium. So, our hypothesis is that” C. psittaci is prevalent in different poultry birds in Pakistan and poses a zoonotic risk for the human beings”. So, we intend to perform PCR based surveillance of the C. psittaci, its genotyping, pathology in different birds and assessment of zoonotic risk. A total of 2904 samples (384 birds, 100 humans from each district) will be collected from Lahore, Jhang, Multan, Faisalabad, Gujranwala, Rawalpindi and tested by real time PCR. Genotyping will be done on the base of sequence analysis of outer membrane protein A gene. Different organs from birds will be processed through paraffin embedding technique for investigation of cellular abnormalities. The results of the study will provide the situation analysis of this very important zoonotic pathogen in Punjab province and will help to devise the control strategies.

data.projectName: To Develop High Strength Innovative Hybrid Fiber Reinforced Concrete for Structural Members
data.projectDigest: Concrete itself is weak in tension, therefore, most of the cost of project is wasted on the flexural strengthening of concrete member or sometime expensive practice of prestressing is used to handle such situation. Use of fiber addition in concrete can enhance it all properties but different research shows that one type of fiber cannot overcome all the issues in structure. Use of single fiber in concrete started in 1950 while the addition of two or more fiber in concrete started in 2004 which is called hybridization. Combination of two or more different types of fiber in concrete can, not only, enhance the overall properties of concrete, but also enhances the various specific desired properties. Fiber-hybridization offer freedom for design in comparison to non-hybrid concrete. The use of hybridization in concrete may lead to the challenges such as, selecting the fiber type for hybridization as it effects the properties of single fiber type composites. This research will help out local industry for manufacturing of steel fibers and polypropylene in desired shape and aspect ratio. This research will build up the confidence of local construction industry for use of HYFRC.

data.projectName: Institutional and policy analysis of R&D organizations for climate smart agricultural technologies in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: Despite less than 1% contribution in Greenhouse Gases (GHGs) emission, Pakistan is 5th most affected country to climate change risks. Agriculture, being the major source of livelihoods and food security, is one of the biggest contributors to national GHGs and at the same time is the worst victim of climate change. With limited technical and financial resources, Pakistan’s vulnerability to climate change will be intensified. In order to harness existing technical resources and public investment in agriculture related R&D system, it is important to evaluate existing policies, identify gaps in existing institutional architecture within federal and provincial level organizations dedicated to agricultural R&D and propose recommendations for enhanced institutional efficiency in tackling climate change related concerns to agriculture and food security. The research draws on existing literature and analyses organizational effectiveness to supply climate smart technologies, their dissemination and acceptance by end users. The organizational mapping through experts’ interviews for the relevance of programs to address climate change vulnerability, and economic evaluation of the climate smart technologies will help to address gaps in policies and field level practices. The proposed work is an effort to address climate smart agriculture R&D through institutional lens for evidence-based policy advice.

data.projectName: Developing Taxonometric Framework for Biotechnology Education at School Level: Analyzing General Science Textbooks Prescribed for Government Schools of Karachi, Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
The core development challenge for Pakistan is to improve educational outcomes. It has been observed that switching from higher secondary level to tertiary level is not very smooth in terms of conceptual hierarchy. The present era is loaded with technology advancement and importance of Biotechnology has been recognized as an emerging profession in Technology Education. Since 1985 the inception of modern Biotechnology has been used with specific reference to agriculture, pharmacy and genetic engineering.  

The present research is an attempt to analyze the general science textbook (VI-VIII) to modify the course content using backward design curriculum following the taxonomy of major concepts of Biotechnology. Present research adopted mixed method approach and Delphi technique will be used to collect the data. Thematic analysis will be used to analyze the qualitative data and one-way ANOVA will be used to analyze the quantitative data.

The project will have a great impact on the education of the public sector and to develop the workforce and resource persons in the field of biotechnology for the economic growth and development of the country. It will also generate skilled individuals for the Biotechnology Park in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Computational Screening Two Dimensional (2D) Materials for Hydrogen Evolution Reaction (HER)
data.projectDigest: The production of hydrogen through photolytic splitting of water can be a possible source of energy that pledges to be unblemished, economical, eco-friendly and sustainable. The prediction of new of two dimensional materials (2D) would probably guide to materials with new characteristics that beneficial for several functions like photo-catalysis1. We have two major benefits of 2D materials which can be used to increase the photo catalytic regulation of splitting of water. The first one being that 2D materials increase the surface area and though display a greatly discrete for the photo catalytic reactions. The second one is the characteristic of these materials lessen the distance between the photo-generated holes and electrons which they have to cover before getting to the interface between solid/water, alleviating the chance of recombination of electron-hole and increasing the photolytic performance. The inherent properties of prospective photo catalyst, for example, their structural, electronic properties, optical absorbance and dissolution in aqueous solutions can be predicted by computational instruments that are formed on density-functional theory. These computational analysis enable the discovery of probable ways to intensify the photolytic activity of 2D materials through using strain. We took into account the forthcoming research directions   for the computational design 2D materials will be a potential candidate for the process of photo-catalysis.

data.projectName: OPTIMIZATION OF WATER ALLOCATION IN MULTAN IRRIGATION ZONE UNDER CHANGING CLIMATE: APPLICATION OF WATER EVALUATION AND PLANNING MODEL
data.projectDigest:
Climate change is one of the big challenges to irrigated agriculture of Pakistan. Due to increase in temperature, it is expected that the crop water requirements of the South Punjab will increase. While, the  farmers are helpless to utilize poor quality groundwater due to constrained canal water supplies,  resulted in soil salinization and crop production losses. According to an estimate in Pakistan, the secondary salinization degraded the crop land which reduced the production potential of major crops by 25%, valued at an estimated loss of US $250 million/year. So, there is a dire need to manage canal water supplies for reducing dependency on groundwater under future climate scenarios. 

In this proposed research study, the gap between canal water supplies will be calculated using satellite data. To do so, the latest programming tool such as R-Studio will be used. The hydrological modeling technique such as WEAP model will be used for better management of canal water supplies in Multan Irrigation Zone under different climate and cropping scenarios. This will help to save canal water and increase crop water productivity of the farmer and ultimate benefit the economy of regional and national level.

data.projectName: Nature inspired oligomer-cross-linked biomaterials for regenerative applications
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Tissue engineering and regenerative medicine (TERM) is an interdisciplinary approach that could be a possible solution to overcome constantly growing demand of organ transplantations. Biomaterials play an important role in TERM and can provide temporary support during the regeneration of many tissues like skin, muscles, bone and nerves etc. In this regard, this project is focused to develop a platform of synthetic biomaterials that can produce a variety of reactive oligomers. The flexibility of oligomer design allows the synthesis of an array of hydrophilic and reactive oligomers that are different based on composition and functionalities. Physico-chemical characterization of oligomers will be made to confirm the desired properties. The intact reactivity will be utilized to fabricate gelatin based oligomer-cross-linked matrices by inherent chemistry. These matrices will further be characterized for stiffness measurement and cytocompatibility. Cross-linked systems based on these biomaterials can help in healing the tissues, regenerating new organs to replace malfunctioned organs and develop medical implants. The science of biomaterials and tissue regeneration is still immature in our society and there is a need to develop these materials so that the ailing community can be benefited.

data.projectName: SELECTION OF CANDIDATE SPECIES OF DUNG BEETLES FOR INTRODUCTION IN AGRICULTURAL LANDSCAPES
data.projectDigest:
Anthropogenic activities associated with agriculture and engineering works has not only modifying habitat by adding pollutants but also changing the socio-agriculture patterns of farming and livelihood. Increased dependency on farm inputs (pesticides, fertilizers, herbicides, etc.) and farm mechanization has led towards environmental degradation and public health issues. In the 21st century, need for organic farming has been realized and asserted. 
Dung beetles have been exploited in many parts of the world as soil builders, bioindicators and help in decreasing the pollution. Their introduction in different landscapes has resulted in the improvement of soil. In our project, we will explore population genetics of dung beetles inhabiting agroforestry and agricultural landscapes, interspecific interactions and quantification of ecosystem services.

Dung beetles have been exploited in many parts of the world as soil builders, bioindicators and help in decreasing the pollution. Their introduction in different landscapes has resulted in the improvement of soil. In our project, we will explore population genetics of dung beetles inhabiting agroforestry and agricultural landscapes, interspecific interactions and quantification of ecosystem services.

data.projectName: Development of Textile Based Composite Wall Panels for Construction
data.projectDigest:
The world demand for houses is clearly exceeding the supply. The real state sector of Pakistan is persistently facing problems because of ballooning property/land prices and rising cost of construction materials. Land is bought and resold many times over before any construction begins, which pushes the prices upward. Housing traditionally has been built from materials, such as masonry, timber, steel, and concrete. The traditional system of housing in Pakistan is expensive, slow and less energy efficient. There are some other problems like structure being too heavy, non-resistant to weather and corrosion and needs maintenance in a shorter time period. Therefore, there is a strong need to design and develop lightweight, and high-quality houses at affordable prices keeping in view the local environmental conditions and requirements of the population so that time and money can be saved.
The objective is to develop and commercialize the textile based composite wall panels for the construction of houses using a combination of lightweight and high strength materials. The designed product will lightweight, thin and strong enabling it to bear the high structural strength. 
The local development of the proposed product will be 20-30 % lighter in weight at the cost of 5-10% lesser than the traditional walls. Moreover, it will be a quick method to make houses while reducing material, installation and other costs as compared to brick and concrete housing. There will be a solution to build with ease achieving high quality products which can be permanent or temporary.  The local manufacturing industry of Pakistan will also boost and create employment.

data.projectName: Study of in vitro induced somaclonal variations in rice  (Oryza sativa) for drought tolerance
data.projectDigest: The project is aimed to enhance the drought tolerance in selected rice varieties good in its agronomic attributes but vulnerable to moisture stress. The somaclonal variants will be produced through tissue culture techniques. Ten genotypes of rice will be used to screen at different levels of drought (0%, 8%, 10%, 12% of PEG). RAPD primers will be used for the diversity analysis of all the said varieties. Selected varieties will be used to create somaclone variants on MS media supplemented with various concentrations of 2,4-dichlorophenoxy acetic acid (2,4-D). One month old calli will be subjected to different molecular, physio-biochemical analysis to identify the drought tolerant somaclonal variant. The selected somaclones will be transferred to regeneration medium. Best regenerated plantlets after transferring to rooting medium will be acclimatized and following analysis will be performed such as molecular and physio-biochemical analysis to check drought tolerant somaclones. The resultant plants will be shifted to field for further confirmation of drought tolerance.

data.projectName: factors affecting tourism growth of KPK province in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan has always been on the list for most beautiful lakes, valleys and mountains but of course utilization of these natural resources in terms of tourism has been a question for a very long time. This research project is aimed at identifying major factors that has an impact on the tourism industry in one of the provinces in Pakistan, the challenges Pakistan is currently facing and what can be done to overcome those challenges. Research Objective is to identify the factors that has a major impact on the growth of tourism in KPK province of Pakistan and further analyze the objectives to come up with a solution to overcome these factors. 
This research is going to be a mixed method research so both quantitative and qualitative aspects will been considered for this research and will involve statistical data from various constituents. Currently tourism industry in Pakistan is facing many challenges and the most important factors identified are security concerns, Digitalization of tourism and its promotion and precedence to tourism sector. All these factors act as an independent variable. The main goal of this research is to identify the growth measures for tourism in KPK province of Pakistan and the gap that bridges these factors with growth have been identified as criteria’s and certification and co-ordination among departments which act as a mediating variable.
Major part of this research is linked with the information collected from the 14 pillars on which TTCI ranks countries globally. The same indicators will be undertaken in order to consuct research in KPK province of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Experimental Investigation of Machined Profile of Modern Alloys by Laser Machining
data.projectDigest: The conventional and non conventional machining have considerable issues of surface integrity for difficult to machine alloys. The newly developed alloys and difficult to machine materials, are always a challenge in nano fabrication for fuel injection nozzles, turbine blades, heat exchangers in nuclear plants etc. Laser material processing is an adequate controlled process in modern manufacturing world, due to its accurate dimensional results, precise profile geometry and rapid material removal rate. Machined profile and quality, is one of the important feature of industrial manufacturing, such as injector nozzles holes, etc. Recently, millisecond laser machining got huge attraction as it has definite capacity to elaborate the geometry to tight tolerance. Therefore, a series of concerns are raised, that how to define, measure and control the machined profiles by laser machining. Several technical parameters influence the laser machining process (e.g. laser parameters, mechanical parameters and assistant gas parameters). Those also have different combined effects on the machined profiles. Therefore, proposed work focused on experimental investigation of the combined effects of various technical parameters on the shape/geometry of machined surface systematically. The emphasis was given to bridge the gaps to improve the current manufacturing performance of laser.

data.projectName: Low-cost, Hardware Accelerated Microwave Imaging system for Biomedical Applications
data.piUniversity: Balochistan University of Engineering & Technology, Khuzdar
data.projectDigest: The proposed project aims at designing and building a low cost, safe,  and portable microwave imaging system based on commercially available off the shelf components  for detecting human body abnormalities, specially breast cancer early stages. This will help in treating the cancer at an early stages before it reaches to a dangerous stage.  The execution of the imaging algorithm will be reduced by the application of hardware acceleration in the FPGA's of embedded system being used in the design of the proposed system. The project aims at replacing or complementing standard screening methods will more optimized and safe screening system.  The submitted proposal will help in establishing research lab in BUET khuzdar and creating a research environment similar to international research institutes. The proposed project deals with one of the major problem which is effecting females worldwide and in Pakistan, especially in Balochistan the number of females being diagnosed with cancer is increasing at an alarming rate.

data.projectName: Ecofriendly biodegradable polymers from agro-industrial waste for various applications
data.projectDigest: The macromolecules are the resultants of small monomers which have their integral design and effect on the whole molecule. The excessive increase in the demands of plastics like macromolecules has raised certain issues for human beings and other living organisms like plants and animals. On decomposition, the plastic materials generate greenhouse gases and cause pollution. To avoid the production of greenhouse gases, landfill options seem to be suitable for plastic materials. Landfilling by the plastic materials has its limitations like reduction in soil fertility and erosion of soil due to an increase in soil fragmentations. Aquatic life has also been under huge threat due to the synthetic plastic materials because many aquatic species are destroyed by engulfing plastic waste. To avoid issues described above and many more not discussed in summary, scientists are likely to work on biodegradable polymers. Biodegradable polymers have raised their importance to sky-high due to their easy and pollution avoiding ability. The project will highlight the production of eco-friendly materials from industrial and agricultural wastes. The project is designed to fabricate biodegradable packaging materials from the above-mentioned waste materials to solve environment-related issues.

data.projectName: Performance Enhancement of Concentrated Solar Power System for Thermal Desalination of Water using a Variety of Techniques
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The immediate efforts are required to bring new water resources into our country water system. The most viable solution could be the thermal desalination of saline water reserves abundantly available in the country. The thermal desalination using efficient Concentrated Solar Power (CSP) systems like Parabolic Trough Collector (PTC), Fresnel Lenses (FL) etc. have the potential to meet country water requirements. The CSP technology is an established technology that is extensively used in electricity production, process heating, desalination, refrigeration and air-conditioning applications. The production of pure drinkable water through thermal desalination of the saline water using CSP systems is an active area of research. In the current project, the performance of CSP technology based water desalination system will be numerically investigated. An extensive numerical study will be done to find an optimum combination of different variables to get the best performance of the system. The numerical results obtained with the current research can be used in the design and fabrication phase of the system in future.

data.projectName: Induction of heat tolerance in cotton through various mitigating strategies under Changing Climate Scenario
data.projectDigest: Cotton production is severely affected by abiotic and biotic stresses resulting in reduced yield. Having indeterminate growth habit, cotton crop bears a complex set of fruiting pattern which is considered to be severely prone to climatic interactions. Cotton plant responds to various stresses differently, depending upon stress severity and developmental stage.  Among various aforementioned stresses, temperature stress in cotton is of key importance as it may cause drastic impact during reproductive stage. As the change in global climate is inclined to cause increase in average temperatures, therefore, high temperature may impact cotton crop in the form of longer growing seasons, more or fewer rainfalls, and thus a shorter growing period. Heat stress induces differential metabolic and physiological responses in cotton, through alterations in plant photosynthetic performance, oxidative balance, normal protein synthesis, stomatal closure, membrane damage and biochemicals. Keeping in view the problem stated, there is a need to screen the available cotton genotypes at heat temperature and improving their yield performance by employing the various mitigations strategies. Moreover, proposed mineral nutrition and various osmolytes will be used as seed priming to improve heat tolerance. Optimization will be assessed on the basis of growth, biochemical, physiological and yield of cotton crop

data.projectName: Mitigating heat and drought stress in mungbean through agronomic practices in changing climate
data.projectDigest: In terms of population growth vs food supply particularly pulse supply, pulse production of Pakistan has not increased in commensurate with the population growth, rather decreased. Per capita availability of pulses from local production declined and hence supplemented by import. The import bill of Pakistan on pulse crops has been increasing rapidly. Heat and drought stress are emerging issues for agriculture under changing climate due to which lower yield of crops has been projected. In this situation sustainable production of food especially pulses production is a great challenge for scientist and researchers. Mungbean is a major pulse crop of Pakistan after Chickpea and is its growth and yield is highly influenced by heat and drought especially under thal region. Sowing of drought and heat tolerant genotype/s, irrigation and nutrient management are sustainable management practices to cope these stresses. In this project local and exotic germplasm of mungbean will be evaluated for heat and drought tolerance at morphological, physiological and agronomic level. All the data will be recorded and analyzed by following the standard procedures. Economic and marginal analysis will also be performed to identify the most economical management practice to improve mungbean productivity. Selected heat and drought tolerant genotypes along with best agronomic practice will boost mungbean production in the country and also will reduce pulse import bill of country. Collected results will also be publicized through publishing results in highly impacted journals.

data.projectName: Development of fruits volatiles based lures for mass trapping of fruit flies
data.projectDigest: Horticultural fruit crops, especially mango, citrus and guava in Pakistan are currently facing huge losses mainly due to two fruit fly species; Bactrocera zonata and B. dorsalis. These fruit flies have gained much more importance due to their quarantine pest status, i.e., Pakistan cannot export the fruits, if found infested by these species, to Europe and America. Different methods such as sterile insect technique, male inhalation technique, many pre-and post-harvest measures as well as insecticidal control are being used to control infestation of these insect species. However, insecticidal control is not recommended because insecticides residues above the allowed limit are usually found in fruits which have been sprayed by chemical insecticides. Currently, two methods; mass-trapping for male flies using methyl eugenol as an active sex attractant and insecticide baits using protein hydrolysate to kill female flies are being recommended/practiced at large scale. However, farmers are not satisfied with these methods as there is no significant reduction in damage made by these flies and also both methods are expensive for small farmers. We have recently tested the volatiles of guava and mango fruits and found that fruit volatiles are stronger in attracting female flies than the commercially available products. We have also characterised the chemical composition of headspace of different varieties of guava and mango fruits. However, the key ligands need to be identified using electrophysiological techniques and then test their different combinations to find the best blend that can be further used for development of commercial lures/attractants. We propose to identify the potential blend(s) of volatile compounds from fruit using electroantennography (EAG) and Y-tube assays.

data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: Soil erosion from catchment and sediment load in river are major issues that impacts on reservoirs life and conveyance efficiency of irrigation network. Because, the canals are directly fed from river flows that brings significant sediment in their flows. Therefore, its management on scientific basis would help increasing the potential benefits of the available water by decreasing the soil losses and sediment load and ultimately increasing the dam’s life and efficient operation of irrigation system. However, assessment and management of soil erosion and sediment load transport require selection of appropriate approaches and modifications of factors. Therefore, the improved methodology is required to quantify the soil erosion from the catchment which will not only address and manage the issues but also to provide the appropriate techniques and factors to calculate the soil erosion and sediment load transport for the catchment in semi-arid regions. Therefore, objectives of the study are to assess the soil erosion and its management at catchment scale using widely used approaches with some modification in different factors (rainfall runoff erosivity and erodibility factor). For this study, Gomal Zam Dam catchment is selected because of its importance as aimed to provide the water for irrigation to the land of 200,000 acres. In addition, two pilot sites will be selected to measure the sediment load that will help to calibrate the soil erosion factors and sediment transport modelling.

data.projectName: Fabrication of gum based metal nanoparticles of etoricoxib and celecoxib for enhanced analgesic, anti-inflammatory and anti-arthritic activity
data.projectDigest: Nanotechnology is the study of tiny materials and structures in the range of a few nanometers to less than 100 nanometers in size. Metal nanoparticles are getting more scientific interest in the pharmaceutical industry for drug delivery, therapeutic and diagnostic applications. Silver and gold nanoparticles is commonly used drug delivery system among various metal nanoparticles. Similarly, these nanoparticles are highly eco-friendly and safe. Researchers are interested to use eco-friendly, cost effective and safe methods for the synthesis of metal nanoparticles. The chemical synthesis of silver nanoparticles is eliminated by Green chemistry, thus eliminate the toxicity of sever reducing agents. Gums are natural polysaccharide molecules produced by plants. Gums have various pharmaceutical applications such as emulsifying agent, thickening agent, sweeteners and binders. Celecoxib and etoricoxib are non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDS) which are used for the treatment of pain, inflammation and particularly joint pain. These drugs are poorly soluble in water. It is essential to improve aqueous solubility and dissolution rate of celecoxib and etoricoxib in order to get enhanced activity at the target site. This proposal is planned to synthesize gum stabilized silver and gold nanoparticles as loading and delivering system for celecoxib and etoricoxib. Drug loaded gum stabilized metal nanoparticles will be explored for improving the drug therapeutic efficacy in terms of increased analgesic, anti-inflammatory and anti-arthritic activity of celecoxib and etoricoxib.

data.projectName: Development of Carpooling Application; a step towards sustainable transportation
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Increasing population cause many problem in urban area including water, residential and transportation issues. Transportation system plays a vital role in mobility management of the city  which can effect at economic level. Poor transportation policies and lack of  proper investment in public transportation make this situation worse day by day.  E-hiring service and bank financing contribute further negatively in this condition. The proposed project deal with the idea that use the existing vehicle on road to make the empty seats useful for other. The concept is named as "carpool" which is already adopted in number of countries and successfully helping the transportation system in whole. Countries like India, Bangladesh, and many west countries are already running this system and motivating and attracting their citizen towards carpool.
The project is the first step towards this system which will design for NED University after successful implementation this system can reduce the traffic almost 30%.

data.projectName: A Qualitative Analysis of The Rey-Osterrieth Complex Figure Task in a Pakistani University Sample
data.projectDigest: The Rey-Osterrieth Complex Figure Task is a neuropsychological test that gives insight into the planning and organizational strategies of those dealing with complex information. Particularly, this task requires participants to copy and remember an unusual complex figure that has a great deal of detail. By understanding how students plan and organize their approach to this task, researchers can begin to build a picture of Pakistani students’ approach to understanding and remembering complex information presented to them unexpectedly. This in turn informs academic and educational policies and will ultimately provide a comparative group for Pakistani students so that they are not being unfairly compared to a Western sample in their performance on this task.

data.projectName: Syndrome Based Epidemic Preemption
data.projectDigest: Health is an important factor in the social and economic development of Pakistan. The Global Human Development report ranked Pakistan 152nd out 189 (GHD 2019). To improve this ranking, it is important to identify the health issues faced by the Pakistan and its economic burden. With more than 40% of its population urban, the risk of communicable disease and potential epidemic / pandemic is significant. An effective strategy to counter an epidemic is to detect outbreaks as early as possible in order to provide the best response and treatment, as well as improve the chances of identifying the source. Over the past several years, in developed countries, there has been an emergence of Infectious disease informatics. In the proposed project, we are proposing a real time surveillance systems for monitoring illness patterns to enable health officials to identify and localize disease outbreaks. These systems will use information routinely collected in patient care and available at the time of the patient’s interaction with his /her healthcare provider and from informal resources such as social media, blogs etc. The surveillance systems will be based on mechanisms of effective information collection, dissemination / reporting and information interpretation / analysis.

data.projectName: Effects of climate change in intensified emergence of dengue fever in major cities of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Cities in Pakistan are growing haphazardly.  Increased rate of population growth in large cities and mismanaged expansion of urban areas create a gap of demand and supply of urban services and inefficient urban infrastructure.  The situation leads to increased number of slums and squatter settlements, inefficient drainage system, improper disposal of solid waste, poor maintenance and cleanliness of residential areas. Accompanied wit Climate change, this urban growth pattern aggravates the transmission of diseases in the cities.  This project focuses on spread of dengue fever in Lahore and Karachi and intends to study the potential effects of climate change on the transmission of dengue virus. For this purpose,  spatio-temporal model of the dengue cases will be prepared and will be studied against climate variability and land use change.  Dengue risk will be mapped and based on the characteristics of the dengue cases, drivers of the virus transmission will be identified.  Project will be help improve the public health facilities and enhance the preparedness to reduce the probability of virus outbreaks  in the two cities.

data.projectName: Hazard Vulnerability Risk Assessment of Glacier related mountain Hazards (GLOF, Glacier surges, Flash flood and landslide) at key locations for the long-term sustainability of China Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Karakurum International University, Gilgit, Gilgit Baltistan
data.projectDigest: Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan has been categorized by National Disaster Manager Authority, Pakistan as “the most vulnerable” area for Glacier Lake Outburst floods, avalanches, landslides and flash floods, which have been quite frequent since 2010, potentially due to changing climatic conditions, resulting in massive destruction and human migrations. The proposed project intends to develop Geographic Information System (GIS) based hazard, risk, and vulnerability maps for the target site (along China Pakistan Economic Corridor), aimed at to produce GIS based information on potential glacier related hazards, help reduce risks through proper planning and build disaster resilience of local human communities. Hazards will be identified, ranked and risks will be assessed using both secondary and primary data. Seismic micro zonation data from the Geological Survey of Pakistan along with available climate data from the PMD; Pakistan and WAPDA; Water and Power Development Authority, Pakistan will be used as secondary data for climatic variation in the area. Primary data will be collected through ground trothing (field survey), questionnaire-based interviews. Geospatial tool will be employed to process data and prepare hazard, risk and inundation maps for the proposed area. The study will be conducted and results will be shared with concerned non-government and government organizations for use in devising, strategies and used for mitigation of risk. The hazard risk maps will also be useful for District Disaster Management Authorities of Gilgit-Baltistan in developing contingency plans at local level whereas the land use maps will be helpful for stakeholders while designing and executing infrastructure projects keeping potential hazard risks in view.

data.projectName: Detection of Adulterants, Drugs and Biological Samples in Low Concentrations Using Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest: Adulteration in food items as well as drug addiction bears a great risk to human life and detection of low concentration of both of these samples remains a challenging task. One of the important challenges that law enforcement and quality control authorities face is the on-site and rapid detection of these chemicals, especially when these are in low concentrations, in order to prove their existence and later on for trial in the court. Raman spectroscopy is a non-destructive vibrational spectroscopy and being feasible and robust detection method, it is broadly used for chemical analysis of molecules. However, for measurements of low concentration samples its detection capability is quite limited. Surface-Enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) is a promising technique that extends the detection limit down to a single molecular level. In this proposed project, extreme sensitivity of SERS will be exploited to detect adulterants and Drugs and additionally biological samples will also be tested for detection of bacteria and cancer diagnostics. The successful detection of such samples in low quantities could enable us to use portable SERS in forensic analysis, quality control of food items and medical diagnostics.

data.projectName: Development of Advance Green microextraction techniques for the determination of elemental impurities and establish research based Lab curriculum at Department of Chemistry
data.projectDigest:
These days, pharmaceutical industry is under critical attention of Pharmacopoeia and other international regulatory bodies, due to pharmaceutical drugs impurity profiling (i.e., the identity as well as the quantity of impurity in the pharmaceuticals).
In order to meet the conditions, an innovative, easy, economical and environmental friendly  analytical methodologies for the determination of elemental  impurities are need to be developed. The present work is designed using novel Green solvents  (e.g. DESs, SUPRASs) based Liquid Phase Microextraction for preconcentration of metal impurities in pharmaceutical application for chemoinformatic analysis. Deep Eutectic Solvents (DESs) and Supramolecular Restricted Access Solvents (SUPRASs), are studied as a green and eco-friendly solvents.  Performance characteristics of proposed methods will also be compared with other liquid phase microextraction procedures. Chemoinformatics will help us to abridge the entire process through machine learning method for analysis and modeling of chemical data. The importance of this field is that method can be developed for prediction of toxicity and assessment of risk.   For non-contact monitoring of elemental impurities through pharmaceutical production, XRF spectrometer will be used.
Our purposed work is designed in collaboration with Caraway Pharma, Islamabad, Pakistan (letter of interest attached). Consequently, an advance analytical instrument laboratory dealing with the critical industrial problems based on   elemental impurities will be established in department of chemistry, UoK. New research based analytical chemistry Lab. course subjected to determination of Trace Elements Impurities, will be established.

data.projectName: Switchable Quantum Light Sources with Positioned Array of Single Photon Emitters
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: Quantum technologies are transforming the technological landscape. One of its main goal is to realize a quantum web including quantum computers, simulators and sensors interconnected via a quantum networks distributing information and quantum resources like coherence and entanglement.  An integral part of quantum technologies are generators of quantum information. A fully functional quantum communication and computational systems can be developed using single photons as carriers of quantum information called “qubits”. Single photons emitters, therefore, act as generators of quantum information. Information are then encoded in photons via polarization, time binning and path encoding mechanism etc. Quantum technology puts additional demands like single photon emission be: (i) positioned, (ii) scalable and (iii) electrically controllable. The currently available quantum light generators based on parametric down-conversion and solid-state quantum emitters lack these technological features. In this project, we propose the development of an electrically controllable quantum light source consisting of positioned arrays of single photon emission points. Such a source can be an ideal platform for scaled up quantum communication and computation systems. The proposal utilizes the excellent resources available at LUMS and the experimental setup may open new avenues for quantum optical research in the country.

data.projectName: Alleviation of postharvest guava fruit losses by adapting various pre and postharvest managment techniques
data.projectDigest: Guava being the fifth major fruit crop of Pakistan gives two crops in a year; although’ summer crop usually fails due to severe attack of fruit flies, high fruit skin blemishes, limited shelf life and variable maturity. Investigations need to be conducted to identify suitable bagging type and propose quality improvement strategies for guavas which is highly prone to fruit fly attack and field blemishes. Current proposal will be focusing on assessing proportion of losses in summer as well as winter guava crops; whereas, variety specific losses will also be assessed followed by evaluation of  physical  fruit  quality characteristic  including  yield,  blemish  percentage,  peal color,  fruit  weight,  size, seed to pulp ratio etc. Meanwhile, guava trees will be bagged with different material at 30 and 60 days after fruit set and harvested at different stages to optimize harvest maturity for overall quality evaluation under ambient and cold storage condition. Obtained results will be reconfirmed during subsequent years and will be disseminated among growers for their capacity building and industry for commercial summer crop production. Economic analysis will be conducted for cost effectiveness and data will be  analyzed  using  standard  statistical  techniques  and  evaluated  data  will  be  published  in national/international journals

data.projectName: IMPACT OF FIBROBLAST GROWTH FACTOR 21 ON BEHAVIOR AND NEUROIMMUNE MODULATION IN RAT MODEL OF SCHIZOPHRENIA
data.projectDigest: Schizophrenic patients are at high risk of metabolic disturbance and brain inflammation after long-term antipsychotic treatment, and the mediators linking the conditions remain unknown. We hypothesized in this proposed research that fibroblast growth factor-21 (FGF21) may not only play a crucial role as a regulator of metabolic effects, but may also possess the therapeutic action of anti-inflammatory and antipsychotic. It is interesting to monitor the circulating levels of FGF21 in rat model of schizophrenia after long-term administration of clozapine and high fat diet in rats. The aim of selection of rat model of schizophrenia is to investigate the potential mechanism of FGF 21 as a protective neuromodulator in the predisposing effects of antipsychotic medication in Schizophrenic patients. The overall aim of this project is to determine the sites and mechanisms of action by which FGF21 regulates body fat depots. We will address the hypothesis that exogenous FGF21 can mediate favorable effects in psychosis. We also determine the mechanisms of FGF21 studying FGF21-induced changes in liver and brain using serotonergic drugs (L-tryptophan and Buspirone) and analyzing hormonal profiles in blood. Possible role of FGF21 in reducing appetite and causing weight loss in rats treated with long-term antipsychotic drugs will be discussed.

data.projectName: Climate Induced Ecohydrological Modelling to Assess the Water Productivity for the Performance Evaluation of Irrigation System
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: Water scarcity under changing climate is the real threat to food security in the increasing population especially in the developing countries where low water productivity is the major hurdle to ensure the food security. In this proposed research, the aim of the study is to evaluate the irrigation system performance under changing climate to suggest the water management strategies for the policy makers. In this study, the ecohydrological model SWAP will be used for the assessment of the water productivity at the different spatial scale Known as the simulation units. The formation of the simulation unit is based on the application of the Remote Sensing and GIS application. The simulation units comprise of the soil, crop, water and climatic data required to run the model. The assessment of the climate change impact will be performed by using the HadCM3 GCM. The statistical downscaling will be performed using the Statistical Downscaling Model SDSM to downscale the global climate model data. Bias correction will be applied to improve the accuracy of the downscaled data from the SDSM. SWAP has the ability to calculate the water productivity under three different level. Water productivity is the main indicator that is measure as the yield produced per unit amount of water utilized.  The water productivity indicators will help provides the point where water can be saved under the changing climate.

data.projectName: Enhanced tissue repair potential of preconditioned mesenchymal stem cells via down-regulation of cytochrome P450 pathway
data.projectDigest: Liver has many vital metabolic functions and is the one of the largest organs in the body that converts the nutrients from our diet into substances used by the body. It can also convert toxic substances into harmless substances, store these substances and supplies when needed by the cells of body. It also releases toxic substances out of the body. Liver cancer is account for the main cause of cancer related deaths around the globe and ranked at second number with the each year about 850,000 new cases. This study is aimed to evaluate the repair potential of preconditioned MSCs for liver injury along with their enhanced antineoplastic potential in liver cancer cell lines via involvement of cytochrome P450 pathway. Tissue lysate of normal and treated liver of rat (with ccl4) will be prepared. MSCs from rats and human will cultured and treated with tissue lysate and their effect will estimated through different assays such as MTT assay cell viability, For evaluation of Angiogenesis Immunocytochemistry and ELISA of VEGF will perform. Immunocytochemistry and ELISA of p53 will performed for the estimation of apoptosis. Furthermore LDH assay, Antioxidant enzymes activity (GSH, APOX, CAT and SOD) and mRNA expression will measured through PCR, Real Time PCR with proliferative and apoptotic markers will also performed, protein analysis will perform through western blotting. Moreover, antineoplastic effects of MSCs will be evaluated by treated the HepG2 cell with these preconditioned rat MSCs. In the current study, our goal is to evaluate that CCl4 injured hepatic tissue lysate treated MSCs can minimize the neoplastic potential of HepG2 cells and enhance the repair potential of the liver.

data.projectName: Impact of Psychological Distances on bilateral trade and portfolio flows: Case of Pakistan with the World Markets
data.projectDigest:
We will undertake work around the determinants of Foreign Portfolio Investment and Trade flows in Context of Pakistan. In particular, we will examine the role of psychic distance as moderator of bilateral portfolio investment and trade flows. We will examine short and long-term bilateral trade, debt and equity holdings. These will be examined in the context of a modified gravity model. 
This study will extend and update greatly the paper of Lucey, Brian, Aggarwal, Raj, Kearney, Colm, (2012). This paper, like many, used the Hofstede and GLOBE measures of national culture. However, work by Dow, D., & Karunaratna, A. (2006) suggests that many findings in economics which show national cultural distances might well be flawed, as distance or differences between the national cultures of a pair of countries is only a part of what they term "psychic distance".  In particular, we will investigate the potential that psychic distance might be a more complete explanation than culture alone.  This project will, we expect, generate at least two papers to be targeted at X and W category Journals. 
This project will shall pursue in-depth “Economic growth and Diversification” aspects in alignment with one of the sustainable development goals (SDGs).   The research team shall pursue awareness workshops, focus group discussions, assessment, data collection and investigation, as per research model elaborated in research proposal of NRPU.

data.projectName: Low-Cost High-efficiency Solar Cell
data.projectDigest:
Solar energy is completely natural and free and it is considered a clean energy source. It does not produce any disruption in the environment nor create a threat to Eco-systems the way oil and some other energy sources might. Energy is central to nearly every major challenge and opportunity the world faces today. Be it for jobs, security, climate change, food production or increasing incomes, access to energy for all is essential. 
Solar cell is a device that converts the sun’s energy into useful electricity. Solar energy is completely free in comparison with other expensive energy resources like gas, oil and fossil fuels. Various solar cells/modules are available in the market, which is an expensive and short service life. China is the biggest manufacturer of solar modules, which is less expensive in comparison with other country's solar modules like Singapore, Germany, UK. However, the main issues are its high cost, low conversion efficiency and service life. 
The aim of the project is to prepare a cost-effective, reliable and high-efficiency solar cell, which would be able to convert more sun’s light into electricity with the least cost and long life.

data.projectName: Conservation and Sustainable use of medicinal plants of Balochistan, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Medicinal plants are a valuable resource of natural herbal products, and are depleting at a high proportion. Up to 80 % of people in developing countries are totally dependent on herbal drugs for primary healthcare system, and over 25 % of prescribed medicines in developed countries are derived from wild plant species. Due to their active constituents and therapeutic value medicinal plants have an important role in folk medicines. This resource is an important part of indigenous medical system in Pakistan in general and Balochistan in particular. Approximately, more than 1600 wild plant species are so far been explored, out of which some 500 species are being used medicinally. Two major phyletic groups namely, Gymnospermae and Angiospermae include many medicinally important and many  Endemic taxa  making the province rich in Biodiversity. Some species of Gymnosperms such as Juniperus excelsa, Pinus geradiana and a complex genus of Ephedra spp. are endangered according to IUCN Red List of Threatened species and there is a dire need to conserve the species. This project will be undertaken by using the integrated approaches including various conservation strategies including In-situ and ex-situ along with cultivation practices for the sustainable use of medicinal plant resources.

data.projectName: Development of 3D Nanostructures for Production of Hydrogen from water Splitting
data.projectDigest:
Electrochemical water splitting devices is most promising and sustainable energy generation and storage technology in the form of Hydrogen. Hydrogen is being considered as one of the encouraging and environmental friendly alternative to depleting fossil fuel. However, for the massive production of hydrogen such technology is needed to visualize to be engineered to large scale technology. Bimetallic based chalcogenides , modification of Mil-53 as direct cathodic and anodic material offer promise for such applications, due to their high chemical stability, great abundance and low cost. Despite these promising properties, progress towards the manufacture of practical water splitting devices has been limited.
 Here we have proposed the facile hydrothermal synthesis of water splitting active metals such as Fe, Zn, Co ,Ni base composite incorporating it in flexible, porous MIL-53 layered on Nickel foam which will be engineered and assembled to photoelectrochemical cell. All the electrochemical experiments will be performed in 1M KOH alkaline media. The design and assembly of anodes and cathodes are expected to meet structural and morphological barriers of Chalcogenides while enhancing the Current density, long lifetime, sustainable after long term deployment of electrocatalyst, and foremost get the better of sluggish water oxidation reaction in overall water splitting devices.

data.projectName: Bounded Rationality in Economic Decision Making: Case of Real Estate
data.projectDigest: Decision making in economic transactions is a very complicated process. Many factors are involved in taking a decisive step towards buying/purchasing things of value. It may result in a good gain or a bad loss. The concept of bounded rationality is all about the notion that human cognition is limited to some extent and there are factors which may cause decisions having economic value. In the first step, it is imperative to ascertain that rationality in decision making process is decisive and secondly it is limited. The limited rationality has everlasting effect on what we choose to have and what we decide to forgive. It not only counts for transactions but for its costs. As Williamson (2000) put forwarded that complex contracts (almost all) are inevitably imperfect and so there is always opportunity to be lost. So in order to know how much rationality limits the transaction we have chosen real estate’s transactions which are very common in Pakistan and which are known to have gains in maximum cases. The research will pinpoint not only the effect of bounded rationality but few other variables on economic decision making. It can be very beneficial for economic theory and general purposes.

data.projectName: Correction of biomechanical problems of foot contributing to mechanical low back pain (LBP) by using Orthotic Devices and leg strengthening exercises
data.projectDigest:
This research is being done to decrease the debilitating effects of low back pain (LBP) on the functionality and quality of life of patients because of biomechanical problems of foot, which are almost always overlooked by the patients as well as the treating physicians.

The socio-economic burden of LBP is very high, not only for the individuals but for the society as well. The cost of treatment for such ailment is also very significant. The usual treatment protocols for such problem involves symptomatic treatment and not the root cause, adding further to the economic burden on the individual. 

It has been identified in researches that LBP can be caused by foot biomechanical problems. Hence, we want to evaluate and eradicate the problem of LBP by administering simple, cost-effective regimes of Exercises and Orthotic Devices (Mechanical devices used to correct biomechanical problems of foot).
