data.projectName: Intestinal flora and fecal bio-markers for early screening of colorectal cancer in local patients
data.projectDigest: Colorectal cancer (CRC), also known as colon cancer or large bowel cancer, includes cancerous growth in the colon, rectum and appendix. With about 65000 deaths per year, it is the fourth most common neoplasm worldwide and second leading cause of cancer-related deaths in the United States. Nearly 600,000 new cases are diagnosed annually worldwide. There has not been any clear data published about CRC in Pakistani population. The same trend is seen in a number of population-based studies, from other countries including Pakistan. Screening for CRC can reduce mortality and also reduce incidence by preventing cancer occurrence through the early detection. And to diagnose the colon cancer with colonoscopy is invasive, painful and expensive. Recent researches have shown that colon cancer is a dysbacteriosis-induced disease. Imbalance of the gut microbiota, especially dysregulated gut bacteria, contributes to colon cancer through mechanisms of inflammation, host defense modulations, oxidative stress, and alterations in bacterial-derived metabolism. The second player in the pathological homeostasis of colorectal cancer is the differences of the genetic features of cancer cells and the different effects that microsatellite instability, chromosomal instability and the CpG island methylator phenotype induce on the immunological organisation of the tumour microenvironment. The third player is the immunological composition of the tumour microenvironment, which changes under the influence of both genetic structures and gut microbiota. All these three players influence each other. In adenocarcinoma of Colon, Epithelial cells shed off in stool and biomarksrs on these cells e.g CK-7/CK 20 , CDX2,MUC2 as immunological markers and for DNA Markers, MLH1 promoter methylation, KRAS mutation,

data.projectName: Design and development of a portable heterogeneous blast mitigation device
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Needless to emphasize that the number one threat to global peace today is terrorism. Explosives based devices are most commonly used by the terrorists. In spite of the state-of-the-art passenger and luggage checking/examination equipment, such equipment fail to exclude 100% possibility of smuggling explosives on board of an airplane, public places, high profile meeting venues etc.. In order to mitigate blast damage effects on transportation systems (air, land & sea) and other critical infrastructures, it is imperative to develop a portable device to mitigate blast damage effects including fragmentation and suppression of thermal effects for protection against explosives on board transportation systems and similar targets. The proposed device viz Blast Mitigation Device shall comprise several elastomeric envelopes containing specialized material for the isolation of suspected object.  The device will cater for safety of targets against explosion up to 1 kg of TNT equivalent placed inside the device. In a nutshell the device shall ensure, inter alia, the safety of million dollar airplane, high speed trains, buses, humans in the main. The technology will be state-of-the-art and outcome is immeasurable in terms of money and human safety.

data.projectName: Energy Management System with Ancillary Services in a Network of Nano/Micro Grids
data.projectDigest:
The concept of Smart Grid has instilled new life in the aging energy distribution grid. The ever-increasing demand for more and reliable supply of power in every sector of life, including domestic, as well as industrial consumer, has given rise to this concept. There is a strong need for intelligent and efficient distribution and utilization of energy. Smart Grid also incorporates dynamic management of renewable energy resources, through which consumers may be able to return surplus energy to the grid. A complete realization of Smart Grid and IoT within it, connecting millions of smart meters, smart lights, in addition to other monitoring and controlling intelligent devices, may come years later.
This project aims to develop  a lab scale version of "Network of Nano/Micro Grids", for which purpose , we hope to design and develop three Isolated Nanogrids of between 500 W  to 1000 W load capacity. Each of these three Nanogrids would be connected with variable load, of linear and non-linear nature, and supported by Photo Voltaic  Renewable Energy generation  and batteries would  act as additional source.  All three Nanogrids are connected through a common bus that  allows exchange of energy as and when required, for optimal use in a  particular community/building connected to a Nanogrid. Thus, the three Nanogrids are connected in series to formulate a Microgrid. Each Nanogrid is  regulated with its own controller, while the Network power and load management is performed by a Central controller.   Ancillary services include voltage and frequency control at the Nanogrid and Microgrid level, as well as load management and battery management system.

data.projectName: Molecular Characterization of Neurodevelopmental disorders
data.projectDigest: About 1% of the population worldwide is affected by neurodevelopmental disorders (ND) including Intellectual disability (ID) epilepsy, autism and epilepsy-autism togather . The vast majority with these disorders currently receives no molecular diagnosis which is a shortcoming that significantly impacts health and lifespan. Previous studies indicate high levels of genetic heterogeneity, with estimates of over 2500 autosomal genes, with the majority being autosomal recessive (AR).  Our research group has already identified many pathogenic mutations in potential novel  genes playing role in etiology of NDs such as NRXN1, RBBP8, ABI2, MAPK8, MPDZ, PIDD1, SLAIN1, TBC1D23, TRAPPC6B, UBA7 and USP44, BBS10, MLL4, ZNF598 and HHAT by our group. Identification of causative changes in previously and newly identified genes can immediately translate into prevention strategies within the families, and potentially more broadly. Understanding the biological pathways that, when disrupted, may lead to ND, will provide a major step towards identifying therapeutic opportunities. Here, we aim to in vitro synthesize small single-stranded DNAs that code for amiRNA sequences as repair templates in Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats/CRISPR associated genes (CRISPR/Cas9) mutagenesis. This approach can be employed to demonstrate that artificial interfering messenger (amiRNA) cassettes against exogenous Green fluorescent Protein (eGFP) or endogenous genes that can be efficiently targeted to a predetermined locus in the genome and result in knockdown of gene expression.

data.projectName: Porphyrin ring coupling to get host-gust electron transfer for water splitting
data.projectDigest: Conversion of water into hydrogen and oxygen gases is called water splitting. The about 1.23 electron volt (EV) energy is required for water splitting. A porphyrin ring with metal, having ability to donate electron, will be used as gust, whereas, 2nd porphyrin ring with metal, having ability to accept electron, will be used as host hole and these two porphyrins ring will be linked with conjugated double bond to move the electron. The gust hole might absorb photon energy and excite the electron to go to the host hole. Two porphyrin rings will be used as these holes and will be connected through conjugation so that, electron can move from one hole to another. Whereas, two metals, as chelation form in two porphyrin rings, will be acted as electron donor-accepter species with the absorption of light (photon) energy. The electron donor metal may absorb light (photon) energy and exit the electron to accepter metal, resultantly, oxidation state of accepter metal decreases and oxidation state of donner atom increases with the absorption of number of photons. When the exited metal will send back electron to donor metal, extra absorbed energy emitted by the metals might be utilized for water splitting. The metals, for the said purpose, will be selected according to the redox-potential table, so that, the changes in their oxidation state may emit energy more than 1.23EV

data.projectName: Design and Analysis of Antennas and Passive Microwave Circuit Elements on Flexible Substrates for Biomedical Applications
data.projectDigest:
The continuous evolution in flexible materials research, integration of passive Radio Frequency (RF) and microwave components on these flexible materials using printing technologies have fuelled lots of novel applications in biomedical, automotive industry, human-machine interfaces, Internet of Things (IoTs), and Industry 4.0.The challenges regarding the design of passive RF components, their fabrication on flexible substrates and conformability in the wearable biomedical application is limiting the performance of these components such as antennas, filters etc. The aim of this project is to focus on the development and optimization of flexible substrates for microwave passive components that can offer added advantages such as low cost, high conformability, and high scalability in addition to seamless heterogeneous integration for biomedical applications and IoT devices. 
The research work shall cover the electromagnetic analysis of flexible materials like polyimide, kapton etc for their applications in high frequency passive component design. Antennas and filters in particular shall be investigated for their realization on flexible high frequency substrate. Full wave electromagnetic simulations shall be carried out to study the behavior of these components on flexible laminates and different fabrication techniques shall be explored for their realization. In the final phase the fabricated components shall be tested in real life environment for establish its practicality.

data.projectName: Synthesis and characterization of polymeric emulsifiers for the development of highly stable emulsions and its use as de-foaming agent
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: De-foamers are used in different industrial applications like food, cosmetics, textile, pharmaceuticals, paints, boilers, oil and gas. Billions of dollars have been spent every year on their imports to meet the needs of the country. To develop valuable and commercial products of the emulsions to act as de-foamers to control the foams in industrial applications will help to decrease the overall imports and to sustain the economy of Pakistan. De-foamers are the emulsions containing Silicone based polymeric emulsifiers that have unique properties due to its hybrid organic/inorganic moieties which provides flexibility to tune the properties of emulsions based on different hydrophilic/lipophilic/silophilic functionalities in order to cope with variety of industrial applications. Emulsions with de-foaming properties would be specifically developed. For the purpose, silicone emulsifiers plays a key role in obtaining the stability of emulsions. Emulsifiers with different functional groups would be synthesized and characterized. These emulsifiers would be further used to develop emulsions with high stability, wide pH ranges, high free energy of adsorption per segment of the silicone based emulsifiers at the interfaces and particularly could have the anti-foaming capabilities. The potential results would be deployed immediately to commercialize the products.

data.projectName: Willingness to Pay for Solid Waste Management among Urban Households in Karachi: Identifying the role of Divine Capital
data.projectDigest: Karachi is among the most populated cities in the world. The city with a population of 24 million generates 12,000 tons of solid waste daily of which more 40 percent remains on the streets. The literature suggests various methods to analyze the issue of solid waste management. In conventional economics, the crux of the analysis of welfare depends on what is exchanged in the market.  The framework assumes that humans are ‘self-regarding’. Divine Economics postulates that human actions are interdependent by divine principles, and personal gains are lesser rewarding if not coupled with wisdom emphasizing on ‘other-regarding’. This study aims to analyze the significance of divine-capital for managing solid waste among households in Karachi. It proposes a research question, what is the maximum willingness to pay among households with divine-capital attributes versus households without these virtues? To answer the question, it will analyze household Willing to Pay by considering the role of Divine attributes, I.e., religiosity, moral values, spirituality, and social capital. Hence the willingness to pay for SWM is the amount that a household would exchange in the worldly-life for the current benefit of a clean environment and stream of benefits that one would receive in his eternal- life.

data.projectName: Clinico-Haematological & molecular characterization of patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia
data.projectDigest:
Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) is the most common type of leukemia in western countries, accounting for 30-40% of all adult leukemia cases. However, CLL is very rare in Asian and African countries. In our country, CLL is reported as least frequent hematological malignancy, accountable in 9.7% amongst all the leukaemias. 
CLL is characterized by clonal proliferation and accumulation of mature B-cells in bone marrow, lymph nodes and lymphoid organs. The clinical course of patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia is heterogeneous in nature. Many studies have suggested that the clinical heterogeneity is reflected in the diversity of the molecular abnormalities found in CLL patients which ultimately drive the pathogenesis and progression of this disease. Among molecular aberrations, IGVH gene mutational status has been suggested the key factor for assessing the disease progression and clinical outcome. Likewise, TP53 & NOTCH1 gene mutational status is known to predict a poor prognosis, as these cases are refractory to conventional therapy. Most studies regarding molecular characterization of CLL with TP53, NOTCH1 & IGVH gene mutations have examined Western populations. However, as noticeable differences in disease biology and disease progression, in various geographical population groups have been observed and also, there is a lack of data regarding CLL with these molecular markers and their association with treatment response in Pakistan. Therefore, this study is designed to evaluate the clinicohematological characteristics of CLL patients having molecular abnormalities of IGVH, TP53 and NOTCH1 genes as well as to study their impact/association on treatment response.

data.projectName: Unveiling Learning Difficulties of English and  Establishing  Training Mechanism Integrated with Digital Technology for Teachers at University Level
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest:
The research is designed to unveil the learning difficulties of English and establishing training mechanism equipped with digital technology for teachers and students at university level. Objectives of the study will be; to review insights of English learning at university level, to identify the English learning difficulties at university level, and to establish training mechanism for teachers and students at university level. The research question of the study will be; which factors affect the learning process of English in university? The study will be hypothesized that training equipped with digital technology enhance students learning. The study will be survey type and descriptive in nature. The quantitative as well as qualitative techniques will be adopted. Population of the study will be consisted of head teachers, university teachers and students of university classes studying in university s of public and private sector in district Rahim Yar Khan. 
Sample of study will be consisted of 64 head teachers of university s of Rahim Yar Khan, 192 university teachers of English and 1360 students of university classes studying in university level. The data will be collected and analyzed through using relevant statistical formulas.

data.projectName: Design and Implementation of Hybrid Optical Amplifier
data.projectDigest: For telecommunication,  dense wavelength division multiplexing (DWDM) systems are in use. Internet speed and bandwidth requirements are growing rapidly. This requires the enhancement in transmission bandwidth. High capacity DWDM systems, with higher and flattened gain, are therefore needed. The performance of a WDM system largely depends on important parameters, such as choice of optical amplification scheme used, modulation technique and data rates. Amplification scheme with large gain bandwidth and low noise properties is vital for broadening the WDM bandwidth. The gain flattening over a given wavelength range for the conventional optical amplifiers depends upon the signal wavelengths and width of radiating energy bands. In this scenario, hybrid optical amplifier provides the solution, offering the required bandwidth and flat gain.  This project addresses the problem of communication of optical signals via optical fiber communication system with higher data rates than the existing  ones to the much longer distances with lower noise and of high quality by using a novel hybrid optical amplifier.

data.projectName: Variable Rate Spraying for Precision Agriculture
data.projectDigest:
The world's population is expected to rise from 7.7 billion currently to 9.7 billion in 2050, according to a recently published report by United Nations in June 2019, which will increase the consumption of agriculture by a massive 70%. It is also predicted that due to increase in population arable lands for growing crops will decrease due to urbanization and industrial activities. These reasons in upcoming years is clearly a portent on impending upsurge in global demand for food, mitigatory actions are required as if not taken can result in food scarcity and insecurity. Manual spraying which is used for protecting crops have negative implications on environment and human operators. 
This proposal presents map-based variable rate application (VRA) technique for a chemical spraying system mounted on a tractor via which precise amounts of chemicals can be applied to crops based on field or plant requirements. In this map-based VRA technique, the rate at which chemical is applied can be varied based on an electronic file, known as a prescription map, that contains information about the field/crop acquired from cameras mounted on an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV). The spraying process will be completed in two steps: (a) the first step will involve generation of a geo-tagged prescription map from images taken via RGB, thermal and multi-spectral imaging sensors mounted on a drone (UAV) using computer vision and machine learning algorithms, (b) the second step will involve physically applying spray via a boom sprayer mounted on a tractor. The sprayer will have the ability to determine its location within the field via a Global Positioning System (GPS) and relate that position to a specific desired application rate by reading the prescription map.

data.projectName: Women Led-Mobile Carts (Street Vending): An Unconventional Retailing Solution to women Poverty Alleviation: An Analysis of Challenges and Opportunities in Southern Punjab
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: Women at Pakistan are engaged in informal sector of economy to support their family and fight against poverty. They are paid less and are therefore are unable to achieve their full potential of contribution in the economy. One way to empower them is women led mobile carts (street vending), through which women can sell different items. Our research is to explore the opportunities and challenges for such women who either are involved in such practice or willing to use this tool to earn their bread and butter but are unable to do so due to cultural or other reasons. Since this research is of exploratory nature so the PI along with Co-PI and other research team will visit different women in south Punjab and conduct in depth interview. The simultaneous presence of all the research team will ensure the maximum extraction of data from the respondents through structured and unstructured questionnaires. This research will enable the policy makers to understand the role of women in informal sector of the economy and the potential impact of promoting the street vending activities in a relatively deprived area of south Punjab. Since there is no such literature available related to south Punjab so the findings will add literature will be further useful in similar kind of researches in Punjab as well as in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Disease infestation and sugar content performance base evaluation of different genotypes of sugarcane in arid ecological zone
data.projectDigest: Sugarcane is major source of sugar and about  80% sugar in whole world is extracted from sugarcane. Red rot of sugarcane is becoming serious threat in the area of Northern Punjab Pakistan, and other Asian countries due to weather variations. The causal agent (Colletotrichum falcatum) infect the main stalks which directly cause reduction in yield and sugar content extraction. Due to global environmental variation, red rot epidemics is becoming serious issue on cultivation of Saccharum officinarum. By the introduction of new varieties, pathogen gained virulence and causing epidemic disease in different agro-ecological zones, which result in significant damage to sugarcane cultivation. Hence, surveillance of pathogen in varying environment is alarming and responsible for elimination of many well performing varieties from the field. Therefore, different genotype screening methods under natural conditions ( layyah, bhakkar, muzaffarghar, and mianwali)  is best approach  determine red rot resistance at an early stage. The results will accelerate the identification of the promising genotype for sacrifice areas. Instead of varietal resistance, biological control (fungal and bacterial antagonists), soil amendments and improved fungicides will be used as effective tool in induced systematic resistance and SAR as a component of integrated disease management. Statistically all parameters will be analyzed and correlated to develop best suitable approach to control red rot disease, to enhance sugarcane yield and economic analysis for farmer cost benefit ratio. Whereas, this area of research is still unexplored and urgently need some suitable solution to avoid plant health losses due to red rot disease in arid ecological zone.

data.projectName: Women’s Heath: Improving Accessibility and Utilization of Maternal Health Care in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Pakistan
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan mostly the married women are died during pregnancy and child birth due to preventable causes. The sociologist and feminist stated that poor maternal health is not only the biological phenomenon rather the social setting both in private and public sphere are responsible for the maternal mortality and morbidity. In the country maternal mortality rate is 178/100,000 live births. In the country 48% of the births are not attended by skilled health personnel. Among the pregnant women 49% women did not make standard antenatal care visits in last five years. In the study province Khyber Pakhtunkhwa 38% of delivers are taking place in home. The major objectives of the proposed study is to investigate the socio-cultural and economic factors influence on women access to maternal health care in the province, to examine the existing health policy and program initiatives of the provincial government for improving maternal health care, to submit a revised health policy and health sector strategy to health department for adaptation and implementation, and designing a cash transfer program for poor married women to improve maternal health care among poor families in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The proposed research is comprised of both basic and applied research.

data.projectName: Establishment of Forensic Psychometric Lab
data.projectDigest:
Establishment of the Forensic Psychometric lab will be first of its kind in Pakistan. At present only Forensic Science Agency, Thokar Niaz Baig is catering the needs of the crime investigators. Their main focus is DNA testing. Only Polygraph testing is used to detect the psychological aspect. 
For establishing Forensic Psychometric Lab, apparatus and Forensic evaluation tests will be purchased. Some of the assessment measures available on internet can be used free of cost for research purpose. A complete dossier will be prepared, which will be used for in-depth assessment of at risk, offenders and convicted. 
There are no trained persons in Forensic Psychological Assessment, who can support/ provide expert opinion/ witness in the court cases. In this situation, we can not differentiate between insane and psychopaths. There is a dire need to have well trained personnel in the field, in order to reduce the rate of crime as well as smooth functioning of the law and order. 
This project will serve two purposes:
First, it will provide an opportunity for the individuals to have rigorous training in the field.
Second it will provide the facility to the law enforcement agencies to confirm the verdict of court given for offenders.

data.projectName: Inclusion of marginalized groups in Pakistan from 2001 to date
data.projectDigest: After laps of 70 years Pakistan state and society is in a process of providing basic rights to its citizens and to a great extent Pakistan has progressed a lot in every walk of life but still one sizeable section of the society still strongly feel they have been marginalized by the policies of the state. They complain they have been ignored and therefore they should be treated equally and given rights. This sections raise their voice at times and local and global media give them coverage which undermine Pakistan claim of modern Islamic state and society.  This study intends to dig out the marginalized groups in the Pakistan. Marginalized person/ person or groups are those sections of the society which are struggling for their rights which they think are not given them as per constitution of Pakistan. This study intends to explore religious minorities, ethnic groups and transgender etc., as marginalized groups in Pakistan. At present, the question in the context of marginalized groups and religious minorities has attracted little attention of scholars who have tried to explain marginalized groups, including Sikhs, Hindus, Jains; and cultural groups like Kalasha and sex workers including transgender and prostitutes.

This sections raise their voice at times and local and global media give them coverage which undermine Pakistan claim of modern Islamic state and society.  This study intends to dig out the marginalized groups in the Pakistan. Marginalized person/ person or groups are those sections of the society which are struggling for their rights which they think are not given them as per constitution of Pakistan. This study intends to explore religious minorities, ethnic groups and transgender etc., as marginalized groups in Pakistan. At present, the question in the context of marginalized groups and religious minorities has attracted little attention of scholars who have tried to explain marginalized groups, including Sikhs, Hindus, Jains; and cultural groups like Kalasha and sex workers including transgender and prostitutes.

data.projectName: Best proximity points, variational principles and completeness of quasi distance spaces with applications
data.projectDigest:
Minimization and maximization problems arises in daily life of almost every human in different forms. For example, a business man would like to maximize his profit and minimize his loss. A student would like to maximize his marks. A car production company would like to maximize its fuel economy and minimize the noise pollution and different types of frictions.  Such kind of problems when formulated in the form of numbers and variables, appear in the form of equations involving some function say F and equation can be written as 
                                                                                                            x=Fx.
If there is a point satisfying above equation exists is called fixed point and can be a solution to some maximization or minimization problem. If such point does not exists then we can find another point where the distance between x and Fx is minimum and such a point is termed as best proximity point. The problems of finding such points is called best proximity point problems. To find best proximity points we need a distance function 

In this project we will solve best proximity point problems in quasi distance spaces. We will also solve best proximity point problems in behavioral sciences, computer sciences and economics.

data.projectName: DESIGNING OF PORTABLE HOLOGRAPHIC MICROSCOPIC                      DEVICE FOR THE IDENTIFICATION OF DIFFERENT PATHOGENIC MICROORGANISMS USING IMAGE PROCESSING
data.projectDigest: Portable holographic microscope can achieve <1 um and large field of view of about 24 mm^2 without the use of bulky and expensive lens. This portable and cost-effective device weights 95 g and uses coherent light to generate a holographic image.  This wide-field and high-resolution microscope, being compact and light weight, would be important for global health problems such as diagnosis of infectious diseases in remote locations and could permit remote clinics and doctors to conduct basic diagnostic tests that are traditionally restricted to hospitals. Holographic microscope offers competitive alternatives to conventional lens-based microscopes, with several key advantages such as wide field-of-view (FOV) and large depth-of-field, yielding giga pixel range phase and amplitude images, in addition to compactness and cost-effectiveness, making them especially appealing for global health related applications.

data.projectName: Development of an antibody-detection enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay for Mycoplasma gallisepticum using local isolates and its evaluation against PCR and other commercially available tests
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Mycoplasma gallisepticum (MG) is an important avian pathogen associated with chronic respiratory disease (CRD) in chickens resulting in considerable economic loss to the poultry industry in Pakistan and worldwide. The characterization of Mycoplasma gallisepticum infection includes respiratory rales, coughing, nasal discharge and conjunctivitis. Clinical signs usually develop slowly and the disease may be chronic. Stress and concurrent bacterial or viral infections are exacerbating factors for the disease in natural by affected farms, particularly the field use of mixed live vaccine in flocks infected with Mycoplasma gallisepticum may predispose to Escherichia coli septicemia with consequent mortality.  Economic losses in the poultry industry due to Mycoplasma gallisepticum infections result from condemnations, reduced weight gain, and lessened feed efficiency in broilers and from decreased egg production in layers. The Mycoplasma organism attaches to mucosal surfaces and remains in the upper respiratory tract for the life of the bird. Furthermore, it is not uncommon for birds with mild or inapparent clinical signs to be infected with Mycoplasma gallisepticum; these birds are potentially infectious to previously unexposed flocks. Thus, it is useful to have a surveillance system to monitor the serological reactions of flocks.
There are various serological tests for monitoring Mycoplasma gallisepticum status such as serum plate agglutination (SPA), the Haemagglutination (HI) test and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). SPA is a rapid screening method. Its sensitivity is superior to ELISA and HI tests in its ability to detect antibody formation from early Mycoplasma gallisepticum infection. However, SPA is prone to give false positive reactions and different sources

data.projectName: Educating rural population of Sindh towards empowerment through technology/ Parha Likha Sindh
data.projectDigest: The study entitled “Educating rural population of Sindh towards empowerment through technology/ Parha Likha Sindh” is an attempt to increase cognitive and creative abilities of people living in the rural areas of Sindh with the help of long distance education through WhatsApp application. Experimental approach will be used in this research project. Stratified Sampling will include 50 male farmers, 50 housewives, 50 female students and 50 male students from remote villages of province Sindh. Four separate WhatsApp group will be formed. Smart phones will be provided to four groups after criterion sampling method. An expert of their domain will be hired from urban area to teach innovative farming techniques for male farmers group. Women activist will be hired to raise awareness about women rights, health issues and how they can better contribute in economic growth of Pakistan. Likewise, female and male students will be guided by social media expert who will guide them about using social media for personal and professional growth. The entire project will be carried out in four phases and evaluated through survey research to look at the deficiencies and positive outcome.

data.projectName: Anthropogenic impact on vegetation dynamics of Takkar wildlife sanctuary and community mobilization for suitable use of resources
data.projectDigest: Biodiversity is one of the essential prerequisites that sustain human society. The species diversity in an ecosystem provides valuable benefits to human beings in the form of provisioning, regulating, supporting and regulating services which are necessary to improve our living standard.  We have been losing 1-10 % of Biodiversity per decade. Anthropogenic activities are the major concern behind this decline. Mining, stone crushing and soil excavation have increased Takkar Wildlife Sanctuary in couple of decades which has resulted in devastation of the natural ecosystem of the habitat. Takkar wildlife, Sanctuary located in Khairpur Sindh, has been designated a wildlife sanctuary under IUCN Habitat Management Category IV.  This project is aimed to record the vegetation dynamics of Takkar Wildlife Sanctuary and understand the role of soil as a limiting factor in the distribution of species. The study will also assess the effect of anthropogenic activities, e.g. mining, crushing stone and soil excavation, in alteration of soil and determining the vegetation structure. The Wildlife sanctuary contains rare plant species, Tecomella undulata (desert teak), which is being exploited for its economic and medicinal value.  We intend to mobilise local inhabitants for the conservation of species and sustainable use of natural resources.

data.projectName: Insurgency and Internal Displacement in Pakistan(IDPs); An analysis of internally displaced women & families: A Case study of Swat District
data.projectDigest: Pakistan has practiced a huge measure unintentional domestic movement from its tribal areas due to insurgency and counter-insurgency phenomenon which emerged after the 9/11 incident. This displacement and violent conditions has intensely affected the displaced persons, however,   women suffered more than man as being the already fragile and subjugated segment of society. This has been observed that women specific needs, both physical and psychological, are hardly addressed when camps are built. They are more stressful in coping with the consequences of displacement as they become the target of brittle social environment, greater than before exposure of violence, psychological anguish and less protection, shelter and source of income. This incapacitates the women to rebuild their lives. In the light of the pressing demand to empower women, and proportionately support the female headed families of IDPs, this research would highlight the impact of displacement, caused by any reason, on socio-economic, political and physical aspects of the life of displaced women. The acquired information would enable governmental authorities to make effective mechanism and more focused policies for rehabilitation of women.

data.projectName: Improved Hydrological fluxes using vegetation as dynamic variable
data.projectDigest: Vegetation is a key variable for energy and matter transfer in the soil-vegetation-atmosphere continuum. It plays an important role in modifying various land surface processes, for instance various hydrological and energy fluxes. Different classes of vegetation, i.e., crops,  evergreen forests and grass meadows, have great potential to alter water and energy balances through surface albedo, level of atmospheric CO2, evapotranspiration (ET), interception, infiltration, soil moisture (SM) and surface/stream runoff. Different hydrological and energy fluxes have also direct and indirect effects over vegetation and its productivity. Soil-vegetation-atmosphere interactions are complex phenomena and needs to be studied and evaluated using different modern age state of the art remote sensing approaches and data (both ground based and satellite-based). For this purpose, the current project aims to study, estimate and monitor variables like vegetation, ET and soil moisture. The project will further evaluate the dynamics of vegetation and its correlation with spatial and temporal varying patterns of ET) and soil moisture. Various approaches developed in this project in well monitored agricultural sites in Peshawar Basin will be further applied in the arid, water stressed, drought potential regions of the country.

data.projectName: EXPERIENCES OF MORAL DISTRESS AMONG NURSES IN PAKISTAN
data.piUniversity: Abbottabad University of Science & Technology (AUST), Abbottabad
data.projectDigest: The phenomenon of moral distress has been widely investigated and recommended as a spiritual instability originated from the situations wherein the morally suitable course of action is well-known but cannot be taken. It happens once healthcare facilities providers becomes incapable to make available the attention in feeling right or takings along with what they have confidence in, morally suitable actions for their patients, therefore, moral distress is assumed to be problematic among nurses and it is linked with nurses’ job dissatisfaction leading to professional disaffiliation. This research aims to measure the moral distress level among nurses, explore implications of moral distress, identify situations causing moral distress and testing the connection of moral distress with job satisfaction, burnout and turnover intentions.

data.projectName: State-of-the-Science in 21st Century Biology: A comprehensive survey of the biotechnology landscape in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: CECOS University of Information Technology and Emerging Sciences, Peshawar
data.projectDigest: Biotechnology is emerging as a key player in economies of all leading developed countries. The bioeconomy, i.e. economic activity generated from research and innovation in biotechnology and relevant fields, makes 2% of GDP in the US which is about USD 388 billion. This includes biotech drugs, agriculture, industrial biotech and the bio-services industries. Pakistan has a bioeconomy worth 1.6% of its GDP, but disproportionately reliant on one product, i.e. cotton. One key hurdle in the development of Pakistan’s bioeconomy, is the serious dearth of data and knowledge regarding both our national capacity and market opportunities that lie ahead. This project brings together a tri-party consortium including a pioneering biotechnology research group that specializes in cutting-edge areas of systems and synthetic biology (PI), a development economics research group from the best management school in KP (co-PI) and a non-profit research organization that has worked with technology startups and innovation ecosystems for most of the past decade in Peshawar. The project intends to broadly map the biotechnology landscape in the country and dive deep as a case study into Phase V area of Hayatabad in Peshawar which is arguably the densest cluster of healthcare service providers in the country.

data.projectName: Removal of disulfide bridge; converts conotoxin analogues into an antimicrobial peptide
data.piUniversity: Federal Urdu University of Arts, Sciences & Technology
data.projectDigest:
Antimicrobial drugs have had a key role in the modern world, contributing to dramatically decrease mortality rates caused by infectious diseases worldwide. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are multifunctional effectors of the innate immune system of mucosal surfaces and present antimicrobial activity against a range of pathogenic viruses, bacteria, and fungi. However, the discovery and development of new antimicrobial drugs is a crucial step to overcome the great challenge posed by the emergence of antibiotic resistance.
Bioactive peptides with large footprints are potential drug candidates that offer advantages of high on-target specificity and low off-target adverse effects than small molecules with small footprints. However, they suffer a major limitation of poor metabolic stability. Advances in designing highly stable peptide therapeutics using End-to-end cyclization of a linear peptide improves metabolic stability by protecting peptide from exopeptidase degradation and, in some instances, improves biological activity, structural constraints such as backbone cyclization have begun to address this limitation.
Cyclic cysteine-rich peptides are useful scaffolds for engineering bioactive peptides to enhance their chemical and metabolic stability; as the huge demand of antimicrobial drugs in this era, our work should provide new insights into the design and development of novel antimicrobial Conotoxins through Fmoc solid Phase Peptide Synthesis.

data.projectName: Performance enhancement of solar operated dew point evaporative cooler through efficient hydrophilic materials and flow configurations
data.piUniversity: Mirpur University of Science and Technology (MUST), AJ&K
data.projectDigest:
Domestic and commercial building sector utilizes about 55% of the global energy with around 40% share for air conditioning application. Conventional vapor compression systems are most commonly used for the said purpose however; these are prone to environmental pollution and global warming as the working refrigerants are based on chlorofluorocarbons/ hydro chlorofluorocarbons. Therefore, ecofriendly efficient cooling technologies are required to fulfill the air-conditioning demands of domestic and commercial buildings.
The current work aims to develop an efficient solar assisted regenerative evaporative cooler capable to cool the inlet air up to its dew point temperature. The current experimental and model based research offers a complete roadmap for adoptability of such solar assisted systems for meeting cooling demand of domestic and commercial buildings including data centers. 
The heat and mass exchanger is the key component of the regenerative indirect evaporative coolers consists of dry and wet channels. Initially different hydrophilic and hydrophobic materials will be utilized to develop the wet and dry channel of heat and mass exchanger, respectively. Similarly, in order to find most appropriate internal flow configuration of heat and mass exchanger, different flow configurations of air in dry and wet channels will be analyzed. The key performance parameters include cooling capacity, pressure drop, wet blub effectiveness and dry blub effectiveness. Afterwards, an HMX of approximately one-ton cooling capacity based on most efficient hydrophilic material/flow configuration and efficient water distribution mechanism will be developed and analyzed. data.projectName: New Rankings of Single Valued Neutrosophic Numbers and their Application in Medical Treatment Option Selection and Diagnose Method
data.projectDigest: We anticipate successful development of new ranking techniques for Single Valued Neutrosophic Number (SVNN) employing enriched concept of Neutrosophic Conjunction, Disjunction, Implication, Inclusion and Similarity. Moreover, we aim to formulate a navel, cost efficient and simple Multi Criteria/Attribute Decision Making (MCDM/MADM) Model in Neutrosophic environment. The model will utilize the new ranking methodologies for SVNN’s developed in first step for its final decision process. Moreover, this model will be applied to study the diagnosis procedure and the medical treatment option selection procedure for DIABETES-a common yet a silent fatal disease in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Establishment of pharmacovigilance center and implementation of pharmacovigilance activities
data.projectDigest: The drug regulatory authorities follow a system of pre-clinical and clinical trials for approval of therapeutic goods for marketing, however this system is often criticized for inadequacies regarding the safety of marketed products. These inadequacies coupled with the thalidomide incident (1961) prompted the need for a post-marketing drug safety monitoring system. In response, the World Health Organization (WHO) initiated the international drug safety monitoring program. As part of this initiative, 96% of developed nations and 27% of developing nations have established a national pharmacovigilance (PV) program. Pakistan with the endeavor of Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan became a full member of WHO PV program in 2018 by establishing the “Pakistan National Pharmacovigilance Center” (PNPC) to monitor safety of therapeutic goods across Pakistan. However, PNPC is at its infancy and there exist no awareness or infrastructure for the successful implementation of PNPC in majority of Pakistan, including Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Therefore, this project intends to establish a model PV center in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to promote the safe use of therapeutic goods by involving all key stakeholder in hospital and community settings. Moreover, this project aims to extend its operations in harmonization with the national and global PV program and its policies.

data.projectName: Management of cholestatic liver diseases and hepatitis B by targeting sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide (NTCP)
data.projectDigest: Cholestasis is the failure of bile salt efflux from the hepatocyte , which results in accumulation of the bile in the liver and ultimately liver damage. One of the strategies to combat the cholestasis is the inhibition of sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide (NTCP) which is the main importer of bile salts into hepatocytes. Furthermore,  NTCP is also docking site for hepatitis B virus entry into the liver cells. Therefore, this study is focused to elucidate the structure function relationship of this transporter and identification/characterized and the nutraceuticals with potential NTCP inhibitory potential.

data.projectName: Hyper expression of Microbial Polysaccharide Xanthan for utilization in food industry
data.projectDigest: Xanthan gum is an extracellular heteropolysaccharide that is produced biotechnologically by Xanthomonas strains. The polysaccharide is used as suspending, stabilizing, thickening and emulsifying agent for food and non-food industrial applications. This gum is authorized by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for application as food additives without any restrictions. Today xanthan gum is commercially the most important microbial polysaccharide secreted by Xanthomonas spp. Global market for Xanthan gum, estimated at 240 thousand metric tons in 2018 and in Pakistan the total import total import value is 1.27 million USD (133 million PKR). There is no local industry for production of xanthan. This study aimed to optimize the production of xanthan gum by optimization of media and lower the cost of production. The major phases of this project are solation and characterization of Xanthomonas spp, production and analysis of Xanthan gum and application on pilot scale/analysis. Then after optimization of yield of xanthan gum by locally isolated stains in universities lab is to move towards commercialization. As Sialkot is one of that are known as the industrial golden triangle of Pakistan. This project may be provided vibrant and strong industrial base producing for local production of Xanthan gum.

data.projectName: AgriFood Distributed Ledger (AFDL): “A transparent Blockchain-based Solution for AgriFood Supply Chain in Pakistan.”
data.projectDigest: At present, the AgriFood supply chain of Pakistan is largely inefficient due to number of constraints and demands are being placed on it. Today, the AgriFood industry of Pakistan is facing number of issues related to food safety, food security, food integrity, supporting small and medium size farmers, Govt. regulation, supervision and management, and total transparency. By considering the importance of AgriFood industry in Pakistan and the latest technological advancements; we are going to propose a Blockchain enabled research project called “AgriFood Distributed Ledger (AFDL).” Our proposed research project aims to digitize the AgriFood industry of Pakistan by implementing the latest emerging technology of Blockchain. Our proposed solution will explore the different aspects of Blockchain technology and its potential implications for AgriFood supply chain. Our long-term research vision is to use Blockchain for more transparent and trusted environment to enhanced regulation, supervision, monitoring and management of AgriFood supply chain and traceability for consumers and digitized procedures and documents for international trade. We are aiming to develop the Proof of Concept (PoC) applications that initially targets the two highly consumed products (wheat and rice) of Pakistan. We will also launch a small pilot project in Sindh province. Our proposed Blockchain-based solution will support and achieve vision 2025 of Pakistan in AgriFood industry.

data.projectName: Educational Chatbot for SocioON
data.projectDigest:
We are living in the modern age of computer and intelligent machines. However, developing
countries like Pakistan is lacking to deploy intelligent machines and systems for natives. One of
the examples is non-responsive and non-user-friendly educational websites on which mostly
students surf for hours and hours in order to get information regarding admissions, scholarships,
and careers. Everything is poorly managed especially on government managed websites like
NTS, HEC and FPSC. Due to this, youth waste a lot of their valuable time in searching admissions,
universities, and guidance to their career. In order to cope with this problem, we suggest to deploy
educational chatbot on SociON. A chatbot is a concept of singularity for the students and people
who are looking for their answers from a traditional, impoverished, poorly managed system.
Singularity means a single platform as a solution to our problem. Chatbots are intelligent programs
that behave live humans. It can answer queries, just like human beings answer to queries. At a
time when students have to browse the internet to seek answer against their queries related to
admissions, scholarships, and jobs, now educational chatbots will entertain their queries. Chatbot
will collect data from different websites and structure it accordingly. This educational chatbot will
cut the cost of effort and time for the public. Students and people, who are looking for guidance
and counseling regarding admissions, scholarships, and career, can get benefit from it. Chatbot
uses deep attention model concept of Deep Learning. In deep attention model, the system tries
to understand language or queries of a user and tries to understand those problems. After
understanding, it’ll answer against those queries.

data.projectName: Impact of climatic shocks and conflicts on the vulnerability to poverty in Pakistan: Mixed Method Approach
data.piUniversity: National College of Business Administration & Economics, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Climatic changes and conflict are two important factors which can increase the vulnerability to poverty.  Pakistan is one of those countries which are confronting severe climatic shocks including floods, earthquakes, heat waves, storms and cyclones. So, the impact of climatic shocks on the vulnerability to poverty is needed to be investigated in the case of Pakistan.
           Along with climatic shocks, Pakistan is prone to various forms of conflicts i.e., crimes, militancy, sectarian and ethnic violence, foreign insurgency, cross border clashes and many others  since its inception . These conflicts can make the people slip down the poverty line. This study will try to find out that to what extent climatic shocks and conflict can make people vulnerable to poverty and what sort of coping strategies can be adopted to avoid or lessen such vulnerability.

data.projectName: Diversity and nutritional status of apricot genetic resources from Balochistan and Gilgit-Baltistan of Pakistan: Implication for effective value chain & descent living of small farmer
data.projectDigest: Apricot is one of the most appreciated specie being cultivated in Gilgit-Baltistan, Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK) regions in Pakistan, though there exist many local and wild apricots with vast morphological distinctions. Rich nutrition, sweet kernel, and high profitability are the salient features of apricot cultivation, which does not only make it “Temperate Gold of Northern Areas” since hundred years but ranks Pakistan at 6th position with 178.957 tonnes production on an area about 30.877 hectares. Apricots are definitely the important source of livelihood with instant commercial potential for the population of Balochistan, Gilgit-Baltistan and Northern Kashmir; even though farmers have yet to realize its full potential. Most of the apricot growers are living in poverty. The socio-economic significance of apricot cultivation and its relationship with diversity within cultivars, nutritional properties and market opportunities have been rarely analyzed from Pakistan. This research project is therefore proposed to study the role of diversity and nutritional status of apricot interlinked with marked value chain to enhance the source of income of apricot growers for promoting decent work through pro poor value chain improvement.

data.projectName: Development and Characterization of Novel Tumor Targeting Peptide-Cytokines Fusion Proteins for Cancer Therapy
data.projectDigest: Cancer is the most prevalent disease with high mortality rate worldwide. No single treatment exists to cure the cancer disease, but multiple therapies are utilized to treat the cancer. These therapies are unable to cure the disease permanently instead of suppressing the cancer growth. Cytokines are major factors in the regulation of immune response in both physiological and pathological situations. Data from clinical trials show the importance of the number of cytokines and their importance in various malignancies. Use of peptide is a promising strategy and can be used to target tumors and as a whole can be used as a drug. Fusion of tumor targeting peptide and cytokine has a potential to treat the human cancer more effectively due to their combine synergistic effects. So in the current project by using the recombinant DNA technology fusion genes encoding cytokines (IL-24, IL-15) and anti cancer peptides will be constructed. The recombinant fusion construct will be expressed in E.coli /Yeast expression system. In vitro study of the fusion proteins will be carried out against the HepG2 and MCF-7 cell lines. The current research project will be work as footprint towards the development of newly effective drugs for cancer treatment.

data.projectName: Synthesis of Sulfur Nanorods (S-NRs) with Enhanced Electrochemical Properties in Aqueous Medium and Exploration of Multi-wavelength Photoluminescence Potential
data.projectDigest: Nanomaterials of carbon, phosphorus, silicon, germanium, tellurium and selenium have aroused a ground-breaking research interests from basic physics to basic chemistry and even to material applications in the last few decades. Nanomaterials of these elements with different morphologies have been prepared. Nanomaterials of different morphologies have different properties and different applications. However, all of these nanomaterials have shortcomings. So, scientists are committed to improve and modify existing nanomaterials to overcome their shortcomings. Although some satisfactory progress has been made, substantial breakthroughs and exploring new types of nanomaterials with unique properties are still highly desirable. To date, sulfur-nanomaterials research is mainly focused on synthesis of sulfur nanoparticles, sulfur nanosheets, sulfur nanowires, and sulfur quantum dots. However, there is rare study on layered Sulfur Nanorods (S-NRs). So, we are interested in synthesis of S-NRs with enhanced aqueous solubility and exploration of their electrochemical and optical properties. Moreover, voltammetric behavior of sulfur in aqueous systems is also desired because sulfur is sparingly soluble in water. Electroreduction of sulfur in non-aqueous solvents (DMF, DMSO, etc.) has been studied by several authors over the past 40 years but there is little literature about the electrochemical behavior of Sulphur in aqueous systems.

data.projectName: Characterizing the antioxidant activity of watermelon rind pickle extract to mitigate obesity
data.projectDigest: Nowadays, obesity is escalating in our country that need to be resolved by formulating healthy foods. On the other hand, fruits by-products produce tons of waste hence creating environmental burden that need to tackle via their proper utilization. Considering both of these issues, watermelon rind is an example as it is a rich source of dietary fiber, antioxidants and nutritive components that could be employed to prepare healthy, sustainable and eco-friendly approach. Further, pickle based fermented food systems are functionally considered as more beneficial in comparison to their non-fermented counterpart. Hence, watermelon rind based pickle prepared using apple cider vinegar (i.e. regarded as a promising food source to alleviate obesity) would not only reduce attendant burden on our environment but also its utilization as fermented food may generate innovative bioactives to mitigate obesity. According to the previous researchers, minor differences have been noticed in antioxidant capacity of watermelon flesh and rind portion however, watermelon rind has an upper hand in terms of antioxidants like citrulline i.e. considered important against cardiac dysfunctionality. Further, watermelon rind extract supplementation in animal study indicated potent anti-diabetic effect. In this way, watermelon rind carries potential bioactive properties to fight against free radical mediated malfunctions.

data.projectName: Establishment of an Indegenious Cyber Range for Cybersecurity
data.projectDigest: Pentesting is used to test the security of an organization to find and fix vulnerabilities. With the right combination of tools (hardware and software), techniques and procedures, pentesters can simulate a real-world adversary for security improvement. In Pakistan, there are currently very few pentesting companies and no local production of commercial grade pentesting equipment. Imported off-the-shelf pentesting equipment are not only expensive but they could also have hidden backdoors. Local production of pentesting equipment is important for building state-of-the-art cyber ranges. Currently, there is no single cyber range in Pakistan to simulate our financial, health, transport, e-governance systems. Cyber ranges allow security teams to understand new cyber threats by simulating attacks and test the effectiveness of their response by rebuilding the environment along with the threat. This project focuses on infrastructure development, capacity building in the field of cybersecurity by providing knowledge-based workforce and services to the industry aiming at self-sustainability. We aim to develop a cyber range in which highly trained people, foolproof procedures and cutting-edge technology required for maintaining a superb security posture, could be produced locally at a cheaper cost that not only caters to the local needs but could also be exported abroad in future.

data.projectName: Biodegradation of plastics by microbes: An Ecofriendly approach to combat plastic pollution
data.projectDigest: Plastics are lightweight, durable material that is used in a number of ways in daily life. The plastics are used in the aeronautics, buildings construction and, packaging industry, electronics, medicines and in transportation etc. However, if these plastic wastes are not discarded properly, release detrimental chemicals into the adjacent soil which can percolate into the ground water. These plastic wastes contaminate the natural ground water resources, causing serious damages to the species that drink water. Living organisms, predominantly aquatic animals, can also be damaged through embroilment, or in contact to chemicals within plastic wastes or direct assimilation of plastics that cause disruptions in biological systems. In humans, plastic pollution also causes the disruption of the hormone levels. Some chemical and physical methods like incineration and landfill system are used to manage these plastic wastes. In Pakistan, waste disposal processes is least developed. Open burning of waste and biodegradable components of wastes like plastic bags are adding to the pollution problems. Therefore, there is a need of hour to develop a low cost, effective and environment friendly methods accomplished of degrading plastic wastes by the action of microbes for instance, fungi and bacteria.

data.projectName: RELIGION AND RITES OF PASSAGES (A -CROSS  CULTURAL ANALYSIS OF THE MUSLIM SECTARIAN ATTITUDE)
data.projectDigest:
A rite of passage is a ceremony or ritual of the passage which occurs when an individual leaves one group to enter another. According to Betty Bastien, “Traditionally, rites of passage provide initiations into tribal responsibilities; they distinguish the phases of human development by marking transitions from one stage of life to another”. 
Sunni and Shia Muslims share the most fundamental Islamic beliefs and articles of faith and are the two main sub-groups in Islam. They share the main articles of Islamic belief and are considered by most to be brethren in faith. However, they have some differences on political, religious and cultural level. Fundamentally, they share some common beliefs but practice in different manners. The objectives of the research includes to study the differences of the both branches i.e. Sunni and Shia while practicing the religious rituals(Adhan, Aqiqah, circumcision, marriage, and burial rituals)  and analyze the attitude of the Muslims of both branches  toward practicing these religious rites of passage living in their homeland and while living in West. It will be also investigated how these rites are locally elaborated.
The research will be based on qualitative and quantitative design methods that include library research, field surveys, case study, observational, and cross?cultural methods.

data.projectName: Establishing the Real Time Data on the Current Oral Health Status of School Going Children throughout the Punjab, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The oral health is very much important for the socioeconomic development and well-being of a country. The mouth can be a mirror of health or disease. So the oral health research not only has its academic significance but directly influence the health management system of a country. The advancement in such an important area of research is only possible if real time research based data is available on the dental and/or oral health status of the resident of a country. In recent years the advanced level of oral health research is going on and this advancement is due to the reason that these countries have well established real time research based data on oral health but in Pakistan no such data is available and current study will fill up this gap. These are 36 (thirty six) districts of the Punjab Pakistan. From each district 02 schools (01 private sector and 01 public sector schools) will be selected if it will fulfill the selection criteria for this oral health study. Almost 34,560 students will be included in this study. The oral examination of all the students will be take place keeping in view all the ethical issues related with human health research. For this examination the three apparatus will be used (separate apparatus for each student). These apparatus are Cotton plier, Mouth Mirror and CPITN Probe. The main objective of the study is to establish a research based large scale database for the oral health conditions of the school going children of all age groups throughout the Punjab, Pakistan. This project also has a good socioeconomic impact as the awareness workshops and seminars on oral health are also included in this project. The results of this project will also be shared at social media and the national News Papers. Along with this the outcomes of this study

data.projectName: :  Design strategy for development of cost effective, energy efficient materials for photovoltaic applications
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: With the increasing demand of global energy it is crucial to replace the conventional power productions with renewable energy sources such as solar energy. Currently per year, about 10 TW (terra watt) utilization of energy takes place by the world and it is forecasted that, it will be about 30 TW in 2050, the remaining 20 TW gap needed to be filled in cost effective and environment friendly manner. In world renewable energy resources such as solar are encouraging to be continuous due to the availability of its low cost source among all the present substitutes. Organic ?-conjugated materials have shown great potential in various electronic and photonic device applications such as photovoltaic cells, lasers and light-emitting diodes etc over past few years due to their fascinating properties like low cost, flexibility, synthetic versatility, solution processability. In determining the overall power conversion efficiency, organic HTMs plays very important role, in both PSCs and DSCs. The proposed research project is aimed to develop energy efficient, low cost hole transporting material for solar cell applications i.e. ssDSCs & PSCs. Moreover, it will promote the research environment for expansion of organic semiconducting materials for renewable energy resources. Further it will uplift the economy and promote industrialization onwards.

data.projectName: A MIXED-METHODS EXPLORATORY RESEARCH ON POSTGRADUATE RESEARCH SUPERVISION (MPHIL AND DOCTORAL) IN FACULTIES OF SOCIAL SCIENCES IN UNIVERSITIES ACROSS PAKISTAN
data.projectDigest: This proposed mixed-methods exploratory research aims at exploring postgraduate research supervision process, from selection of research supervisor to the completion of MPhil and doctoral research theses. The project involves a relatively broad inter-disciplinary approach, spanning departments across social sciences. The methodology for this research relies on a mixed-methods approach, which involves developing appropriate quantitative and qualitative tools for data gathering.  The quantitative tools would include survey tools aimed at gathering data from a representative sample of research scholars and their supervisors. In addition, a checklist will be developed and used for establishing provision of research provisions and allied facilities in the respective social sciences departments. For obtaining qualitative data, semi-structured interviews will be used. This would involve interviewing a representative purposive sample from research scholars and their supervisors. In addition, research scholars would be recruited for observing supervisor-supervisee research sessions. Prior to initiating the fieldwork and data collection phase, both quantitative and qualitative tools would be pilot tested on a select sample, which will help towards establishing validity and reliability of the instruments and consistency and credibility of the qualitative tools.

data.projectName: Integrating Maternal Mental Health in Health system of AJk & Sindh: Current Situation and Way forward
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Zulfikar Ali Bhutto Institute of Science & Technology (SZABIST) University, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Pregnancy is a deeply complex period, in which physiological and psychological changes takes place with in a shorter period of time. Which not only effect on mothers physical and mental health but also on her baby’s health. Elevated level of anxiety and depression throughout the period of antenatal, have been linked to increase risk of preterm birth, low birth weight and difficulty in labor and delivery. In perinatal period anxiety symptoms may be as common in depression. In antenatal period, the rate of generalized anxiety disorder has been estimated 8.5% and postnatal 8.2% (Vigod, 2010). In Pakistan Prevalence of anxiety and depression is >40% in pregnant women and this proposed project will improve the maternal health indicator of Pakistan by addressing the mental health issues (anxiety and depression) among pregnant women and integrate the intervention on mental health, and will increase equity in access to mental healthcare. This project will be cross-sequential study for the period of 20 months from March 2020 to October 2021. Study will be conducted in two different provinces of Pakistan, AJK and Sindh. family therapy, motivational interviewing, problem solving therapy, psychoeducation, interpersonal and cognitive therapy and also in-depth interview will be conducted to assess the factors affecting the mental health. after completion intervention monitoring follow up will be taken to avoid loss to follow up of participants and end-line assessment will be performed by filling the tool again and blood samples of those high prevalent cases to assess the impact changes after intervention. Psychology team will help in developing referral mechanism for correct diagnosing and treatment of pregnant women in health system. This study will help in developing policy framewo

data.projectName: Antigenic characterization of  Avibacterium paragallinarum and development an immunoassay of recombinant multi-epitopic antigen for detection of infectious coryza
data.projectDigest: Infectious coryza (IC), a disease of the upper respiratory tract in chickens is caused by Avibacterium paragallinarum. The economic losses associated with infectious coryza results from poor growth performance in growing birds including broilers, marked reduction in egg production in layers and increased culling rates in meat chickens.  Conventional diagnosis of infectious coryza is based on clinical signs, demonstration of satellite colonies by cultural examination and confirmation is by biochemical tests.  A. paragallinarum is a slow growing organism which will take 36-48 h or even more time to show detectable colonies. Diagnosis of the infectious coryza can be more complicated when it co-occurs with other pathogens, especially bacteria like Pasteurella multocida. Further complications can be contributed by the presence of opportunistic pathogens like Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas. For A. paragallinarum there are multiple Kume serovars under the original three Page serovars of A, B and C. A. paragallinarum  elusive and changing potential pattern pertaining to its surface protein(s) amongst various sero/immuno vars limit  the sensitivity of available ELISA test. The recombinant protein-based ELISA is relatively inexpensive and sensitive. Moreover, the recombinant protein has an advantage as it forms immunodominant epitopes and is devoid of any non-specific moieties in whole cell preparation.

data.projectName: Development of Composite Index Crop Insurance Model for Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
This research project is of huge economic and social significance for agricultural sector of Pakistan. There are 5.24 million agricultural farms in Punjab and ~90% of these are owned by small farmers (<25 acres). Due to changing climatic conditions, insufficient/untimely rainfall and flooding are becoming increasingly common and affect the crop yield and overall economic sustainability. Majority of these small farmers need financial assistance in case if the crop(s) produce is lowered due to any reason. 

To assist farmers against yield loss, Government of Punjab introduced a crop insurance program, in 2018, in which premium is paid by Punjab Government. This program is based on Area Yield Index Insurance (AYII) model, where the claims are triggered based on the yield short fall against a benchmark yield. However AYII model is unable to answer a very important question i.e. what if the yield is more than benchmark yield but the market price of the produce is not sufficient enough to cover even the cost of production? In this scenario, farmers suffer and are not compensated by insurance companies. To overcome this problem, it is essential to incorporate important missing variables of Market price and Cost of production in a model that helps in ensuring farmers loss protection.

To collect data related to market prices of crops at the start, mid and end of both harvesting seasons, a comprehensive survey of 10 major markets will be carried out. A sample of farmers will be interviewed to estimate the cost of productions. A composite crop index model will be constructed and shared with Punjab Agriculture department for their review and onward implementation.

It is hoped that resultant model will help Punjab government in formulating future crop insurance policies.

data.projectName: Isolation, identification and characterization of novel microbial s-triazine and dicamba degrading proteins
data.projectDigest: Global herbicide market stood at 21065.2 million USD in 2013 with a projected market of + 30 billion USD in 2019. Glyphosate holds main market share due to herbicide tolerant (HT) trait for glyphosate in major crops. However, this scenario is rapidly changing due to the evolution of glyphosate resistant weeds. To address weed resistance problem, new herbicide tolerance (HT) traits are discovered such as dicamba, HPPD, triazine tolerant crops. These traits are developed to broaden the weed control spectrum in glyphosate resistance weeds arena. In 2019 dicamba and glyphosate stacked HT traits are introduced in market. For HT trait development basic research work is to discover novel proteins which can degrade the target herbicide. As new stacked traits are entering into the market very quickly, with the passage of time the chances of finding novel proteins for this purpose will diminish. This project is an effort to discover other than known proteins to degrade dicamba and s-triazine herbicides. The novel proteins can be used to develop HT trait as a stack with glyphosate, broadening the spectrum of weed control. It is essential to develop traits locally, if relied on multinational’s seed products our economy will be vulnerable to multinationals monopoly reducing profits for our farmers and eliminating the share for local manufacturers. Additionally, these technologies will hold patents therefore it is necessary to do basic work of finding novel proteins for new HT traits development locally.

data.projectName: Effect Urea Treated Whet Straw and Yogurt on Milk Production of Dairy Cow and Buffalo: Mastitis Control and Potential Probiotic Development
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest: Livestock sector in Pakistan pays almost 57.2% of agriculture value and nearly 11.5% to the AGDP. Production of livestock sector has been reduced because of substandard feeding practices. .  Every 3rd animal in Pakistan has been suffering from mastitis which decreases milk quantity and quality Disease like mastitis occurs in milking cow and buffalo due to immunity break down because of unavailability high quality protenious feeding.  Most of small dairy farmer can’t afford to use high quality feeding for milking animal because of their poverty. Wheat straw is commonly available cheapest feed stuff which is being used for dairy cows and buffalo. However, alone wheat straw has no nutritious value which decreases the milk production. Interestingly, in ruminants, animal has the ability to convert the urea into valuable protein which can fulfill the protein requirement of milking animals. Yogurt consumption is considered as a vector probiotics for animal and human. Yogurt is a good source of several micronutrients and help to improve feeding pattern, health, microbial control and maintain energy balanced in the body.  So, the current project is designed to prepare the cheapest nutritious feed of dairy animals after treating the wheat straw with urea along with yogurt and evaluate its effect on production parameters of cattle and buffaloes in Multan. In this project we will also characterize the gut microbiome before and after feeding of prepared feed to study the change in gut microbiota to develop health beneficial probiotics.  This project may help to increase milk/meat production and improve the health status of dairy animals in particular controlling of mastitis and development of potential probiotics.

data.projectName: Molecular detection and characterization of bat-borne viruses from Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Emerging infectious diseases (including bat-borne virus or bat-associated virus) pose a significant threat to human and animal welfare. Viral isolates from at least eight (8) different viral families have been reported in bats. Most famous among them are Ebola  virus, SARS-CoV, Marburg virus (MARV) , Nipah virus , MERS-CoV and Hendra  virus that have been reported to infect human, and  have been linked to contaminated consumption food (fruits and bush meat),  substandard hygiene and healthcare practices, climate change, bats habitat destruction, alteration in farming patterns, wildlife  trading  in  wet  markets, urbanization and international  travel. Outbreaks of these diseases have traumatized the global interconnectivity and have affected major chunks of population. Although Pakistan is home to a diverse range of bat species and colonies of bats can be located in different parts of the country however, there is no information about the viruses inhabiting or spread by these bat populations. We aim to screen Pakistani bat populations for diverse kinds of viruses and their potential to infect humans and livestock. Moreover, we will suggest strategies (i) to contain possible risk of emerging infections from bat-borne viruses and (ii) to reduce human and economic loss resulting from such infections.
