data.projectName: Project LAPS: An Online System For Restoration Of Missing Childern
data.piUniversity: CECOS University of Information Technology and Emerging Sciences, Peshawar
data.projectDigest:
The process of tracing and reunification of the children identified as separated and unaccompanied in different provinces in Pakistan has so far been carried out in an informal way and does not follow uniform guidelines. NGOs tend to use informal means to trace families. In certain cases, the district administration is involved in the process but the tracing is mostly done through links to the community. Similarly, there are no set guidelines available for NGOs and other stakeholders for reunification and so NGOs follow their own procedures. These include: written statements by parents, copy of ID cards and photos of the reunification.
Project “LAPS” is a web based system which is proposed  for quick and efficient restoration of missing children throughout KPK. The aim is to provide an improved and advanced means of gathering and uploading the records of missing children by police and not only connecting different police stations but making it available to other police stations and the local effected public.

NGOs tend to use informal means to trace families. In certain cases, the district administration is involved in the process but the tracing is mostly done through links to the community. Similarly, there are no set guidelines available for NGOs and other stakeholders for reunification and so NGOs follow their own procedures. These include: written statements by parents, copy of ID cards and photos of the reunification.
Project “LAPS” is a web based system which is proposed  for quick and efficient restoration of missing children throughout KPK. The aim is to provide an improved and advanced means of gathering and uploading the records of missing children by police and not only connecting different police stations but making it available to other police stations and the local effected public.

data.projectName: Estimation of Fetal Exposure of steroids and anti-histamines and role of efflux transporters at the placenta
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The objective of this study is to determine the safety of antenatal administration of Budesonide (BUD) Fluticasone propionate (FP), on the fetus; whether it will restrict the intrauterine growth and or have any effects on the regulation of breast cancer resistance protein-1 (BCRP1) and P-glycoprotein (P-gp) gene expression on placenta. Pharmacokinetics parameters obtained from this study and physiochemical properties from literature, a Physiological Based Pharmacokinetic Model (PBPK) will be developed in mice to correlate drug disposition, and further, this model will be to extrapolated to humans and simulate plasma concentration profile in humans. And determination of free and total concentration of anti-histamine (Dexchlorpheniramine and Loratadine) using perfused human placenta model.

data.piUniversity: Karakurum International University, Gilgit, Gilgit Baltistan
data.projectDigest: Traditional and herbal tea is second in line after water under popular beverages due to its phenomenal taste and outstanding benefits towards health. Herbal tea is a prominent dietary source of polyphenols (categorized as ‘antioxidants’) which have the diverse biological activities and  used for treatment of various diseases. Pakistan listed on 7th for highest per capita tea consumption. In addition to black tea, herbal teas  such as Tapal tea, Lipton green tea, Herbo natural green, Johar Joshanda, Natural Herbal Tea, Cinnamon Tea Herbal, Moringa herbal tea, Neem herbal tea  etc  are preferentially used in Pakistan due to high antioxidant activities. Most of these herbal teas are prepared from fresh leaves of various herbal/medicinal plants. Gilgit-Baltistan is rich in medicinal and herb flora particularly and about 5000 medical plants have been reported so for. Among these Sea-buckthorn (Hippophae rhamnoides L.)  sub species Turkistanica, Thymus, Serpyllum, Duck Rose, saussurea, cumium, aconitum, ephedra, menthe, dadura are widely abundantly found throughout Gilgit-Baltistan. Studies showed that these plants are rich source polyphenols, wide-ranging of healthy ingredients and minerals. In the mountainous areas of Gilgit-Baltistan, these plants are still one of the most underutilized resources, despite its multiple advantages. Reports also revealed that their leaves and stems of these plants are naturally aromatic and fragrance besides of their nutritional and medic

data.projectName: IMPACTS OF CLIMATE AND PETROLEUM EXPLORATION ON GREEN MUSSELS AND RAZOR CLAM INHABITANT COASTAL AND MARINE ECOSYSTEM OF SUJAWAL, SINDH, PAKISTAN
data.projectDigest:
The Sindh coastal areas are facing serious threats to its land, soil, water and air due to climate change, sea intrusions, reduction in Indus river flows, and petroleum exploration activities. The area is also facing natural disasters; floods, droughts, cyclones, and sea intrusions. There is significant petroleum exploration activity in Sujawal district. A number of major oil and gas companies such as Mari Gas and PPL have producing gas fields in the area. The Indus delta eco-region is natural spawning ground for thousands of marine living creatures. The changing weather patterns have adversely affected marine biodiversity particularly benthic bivalves Mussles and Clams in coastal zone Sujawal, Sindh Pakistan. 
         Mussel and Clam diversity occurring in Indus delta eco-region and coastal creek system are facing drastic reduction. In past huge quantity of these shellfish production were being taken from these natural marine habitats and exporting to Fareast and Eastern countries. 
         Therefore, assessment and continuous monitoring of Mussel and Clam diversity occurring at hotspots should be done so that appropriate mitigation measures and improvement plans can be put into place.  Proposed study is needed for sustainable policies for development and conservation of most important shellfishery mussel and clam diversity.

data.projectName: Exploration of Heritage and Religious sites in AJK [Districts Muzaffarabad and Neelum Valley] for Development of Tourism Opportunities in the Region.
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest: Azad Jammu is strategically located in the south-west of Pakistan confined by Tibet in the east and by the Sinkiang (Xinjiang) province of China in north and in the west by the small mountainous stretch of Afghanistan. Historically Kashmir was part of greater Gandhara which join connecting routes of Silk Road at various locations. In the ancient past Kashmir benefitted economically, culturally and socially from the Silk Route. The CEPEC, in reality is the revival of ancient Silk Route and it offers great opportunities to adjacent belts and under development areas in AJK.Earlier surveys in District Muzaffarabad and Neelum valley suggest great connectivity which facilitated commerce trade and religious tourism in the past. To fully explore and capitalise on the potential archaeological sites research study needs to be carried out in the area. Exploration, identification and promotion of cultural heritage are highly important for strengthening national discourse against radicalism and present day challenges against national coherence. These findings will help researchers of various universities in the region including relevant stake holders. The researcher is intending to collaborate with Dept. Tourism and Archaeology Govt.AJK which help to enhance their capacity building. Moreover findings of heritage sites will help the Dept. T&A in planning and branding new tourist destinations in the areas of Districts Muzaffarabad and Neelum Valley. The objectives of study to provide a potential of Heritage sites, in AJK in order to tap, identify and help to create opportunities for a cultural heritage tourism corridor connecting AJK to rest of region. It will help achieve national objectives in the wake of developing the tourism industry.

data.projectName: Architecting dual drug-loaded liposomes incorporated in a temperature-sensitive hydrogel for nose-to-brain delivery as a multifaceted approach to treat ischemic stroke
data.projectDigest: Ischemic stroke is one of the major cause of deaths and neurological disability worldwide, and its treatment is a key financial burden on health care. The unfavorable biopharmaceutics properties of the available therapeutic agents and the presence of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) to restrict their entry into the brain are the major hurdles in successful neuroprotection against ischemic stroke. We propose designing of a dual drug-loaded liposomal system to accommodate two neuroprotective agents (Melatonin and Carnosine) with diverse physiochemical properties in a single carrier. Considering the excellent biocompatibility and high potential for clinical development, the proposed liposomal system would be a promising drug delivery system to deliver their payload into the brain through intranasal route. The nose-to-brain delivery presents a direct access of therapeutic agents to the brain without the necessity to cross the BBB. The developed liposomal system will subsequently be incorporated into the temperature-sensitive hydrogel for ease of application and to enhance the retention time of the liposomal system at the nasal site of absorption. The basic goals of the current project are therefore to design a multifaceted approach to enhance the neuroprotective effects of melatonin (MLT) and carnosine (CAR) by utilizing a single carrier and overcome the hurdles associated with their limited accessibility to the brain for the treatment of ischemic stroke.

data.projectName: Synthesis of novel indole derivatives as diabetic II inhibitors and their molecular docking studies
data.projectDigest:
Diabetes is an illness creates a lot of problems causing to defects in insulin secretion and action. This causes glucose concentration increase in blood (hyperglycemia) as well as created dysfunction to vital organs such as nerves and blood vessels. One of the main enzymes that can be used to diminish glucose level in blood is to inhibit alpha-glucosidase enzyme. This can be achieved by controlling the glucose levels in blood and contains postprandial hyperglycemia. Indoles derivatives are naturally occurring secondary metabolites of alkaloid class. Some indoles are reported as potent alpha?glucosidase inhibitors. 
This present project has been designed to synthesize hetero atom containing Indoles derivatives. Incorporating hetero atoms such as nitrogen and sulphur has been known to increase biological properties of indoles. The main application of this project will be towards development of alternatives drugs for diabetes mellitus.

data.projectName: Natural hydrogels based silver and gold nanoparticles for wound healing, cytotoxicity, targeted drug delivery, and water purification
data.projectDigest: Hydrogels are water-loving substances that absorb a large amount of water without dissolving. Hydrogels have a crosslinked structure with a porous nature. Hydrogels are responsive to various external factors such as temperature, pH, and salt solutions. Owing to the biodegradable, biocompatible and responsive nature, they are the potential candidates for the targeted release of drugs. They absorb heavy metals and toxic dyes from the wastewater and make the water potable. Hydrogels can also act as capping and reducing agents for the fabrication of nanoparticles. The nanoparticles have a strong potential to inhibit the growth of bacteria and fungi. The nanoparticles can also act as catalysts for the degradation of dyes present in wastewater. The nanoparticles can be used for the treatment of cancer owing to their cytotoxic potential. The project is aimed to isolate hydrogels from the seeds of various plants. Thoroughly characterized natural hydrogels will be utilized for the uptake of heavy metals and dyes. The fabrication of nanoparticles using green approaches will also be the main focus of the project. Moreover, nanoparticles will be evaluated for cytotoxic potential and catalysts for the degradation of dyes. Finally, the nanoparticles will be assessed for the controlled/targeted release of the drugs.

data.projectName: Seismic Performance Evaluation and Determination of R-Factor for Energy Efficient Rat-Trap Bond Masonry Buildings
data.projectDigest: Pakistan has been facing an acute energy crises over the past two decades and there is a shortfall of over 10 million houses in Pakistan according to official estimates. Therefore, the need for an economic and energy efficient construction technique cannot be over emphasized. Rat-Trap Bond (RTB) masonry is one such technique where bricks are laid on their edges vertically with three inches cavity between them. This arrangement has many advantages like cost reduction of up to 30%, better thermal insulation, dead load reduction and better aesthetic look.  The basic aim of this project is to evaluate the seismic performance of buildings in RTB, develop cost effective strengthening procedures, and guidelines for RTB implementation in the field. The introduction of RTB masonry will drastically change the construction industry of Pakistan where brick masonry is extensively used. It will reduce both the cost and construction time of masonry buildings.

data.projectName: Government's policy and propaganda implications toward the pro-environmental factors and green purchase behavior
data.projectDigest: This study deals with the green environment awareness and its outcomes on the green purchase behavior of the Pakistani citizens. Pakistan is spending over 7.5 billion rupees on environmental sustainability per year. Beside the economic loss, due to the environmental problems the loss of human lives also increasing. As per the statistics given by the world health organization (WHO) Global Health Observatory report, around 200 deaths out of 100000 population observed because of the environmental factors in Pakistan. Furthermore, the World Bank (WB) estimations regarding the Pakistan’s annual weight of disease shows that 22000 premature deaths and 163000 DALY’s (Disability-adjusted life year) lost because of the indoor and outdoor pollution.  It is also observed by WB that 40 million cases of acute respiratory infections and 28000 deaths/year also caused by the polluted environment of Pakistan. To address the above-mentioned issue, this study will attempt to address the issue of the environmental sustainability in Pakistan by investigating the factors of pro?environmental behavior (e.g., Environmental Consciousness, Recycling Intentions, Willingness to be Environmentally Friendly and Social interaction) towards the green purchase behavior and how their behavior can be socialized in order to maintain environment sustainability in Pakistan. additionally, this study will provide awareness of environmental sustainability by investigating the pro-environmental factor of green purchase behavior. Moreover, this study will investigate the impact of Govt efforts (i.e., green policy and propaganda) to enhance the relationship between the factors of pro-environmental behavior and green purchase behavior. This study will be conducted in five major metropolitan cities of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Enhancement of larvicidal activities of different compounds used against dengue mosquito through nanocapsules
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: The socioeconomic impact linked with vector born diseases such dengue is a major hurdle for the development of many countries including Pakistan, and most of these arthropods born diseases are one of the major reasons of poverty. In Pakistan, the previous epidemic of 2019 has caused more than 50,000 confirmed dengue cases and 75 deaths from the four provinces, Islamabad, and AJK. The control of dengue mosquitoes mostly rely on the use of different insecticides but vector control programs are facing operational challenges with mosquitoes becoming resistant to insecticides. Overdose and frequent use of insecticides for vector management are causing serious problems to environment and human health. To overcome these issues, scientists are looking for other alternatives which are environmental friendly and safer for human health. Among these control measures, the most important is the use of controlled release formulation using nanotechnology which has proven a new generation of environmental remediation technology. The main aim of the current work is to develop newer and ecofriendly nanocapsules using lignin, chitosan and gelatin for the enhancement of larvicidal activities of recommended compounds against Aedes mosquitoes as an innovative IVM (Integrated Vector Management) tool in the management of dengue mosquito population.

data.projectName: Metabolic Alterations in Hematological Cancer Cells: Basic Understanding and Therapeutic Potential
data.projectDigest: Cancer cells divide more frequently than normal cells hence, they exhibit increased demands for energy and macromolecules. To cope with these elevated requirements cancer cells undergo major modifications in their metabolic pathways. Since the 1920s, it has been known that, in contrast to most normal tissues, cancer cells show avid glucose uptake and tend to convert glucose to lactate through the glycolytic pathway regardless of whether oxygen is present (aerobic glycolysis). It is now widely recognized that tumors frequently exhibit an increased ability to synthesize lipids and this lipogenesis is tightly coupled to glucose metabolism. Non-Solid hematological cancers – including leukemia and multiple myeloma - are also shown to have deregulated metabolic pathways. It is very important to study that whether or not the metabolism of hematopoietic cancer cells is different from other neoplastic cells – such as prostate or breast cancer cells – that are more widely studied in the metabolic context. The presented project deals with alterations in the major metabolic circuitries of hematopoietic cancer cells and the major metabolic pathways including glycolysis, lipogenesis, and mevalonate pathway. Moreover, blood lipid profiles of hematological cancer patients are shown to be associated with pathogenesis and progression of cancer. However, there are several discrepancies in the previous reports therefore; the relationship between plasma lipid levels and hematological cancers remains elusive. Hence, one of the reasons for the previous contradictory reports might be the patient to patient variation in studying cancer cell lipid metabolism.  In the proposed project we are aiming to study this effect of various plasma metabolites on cellular metabolism of hematological cancers.

data.projectName: An epidemiological investigation of acaricide resistance in tick population: A One Health perspective to control tick-borne diseases in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Livestock-sector serves as source of livelihoods for over 40 million population and is considered to be crucial in national food security. This sector has been facing various issues including parasitic infestations in animals – particularly ticks and tick-borne diseases (TBDs) – for last several years. These TBDs not only affect the health and production of animals but also significantly contribute towards public health concerns. Various diseases of zoonotic importance such as Congo Fever are only spread by ticks. The prevention and control of TBDs through measures like vaccination etc. has not been very successful due to a number of issues. Therefore, controlling ticks’ population has been the critical success factor in controlling TBDs globally.

Acaricides are synthetic pesticide drugs that are used against ticks worldwide. However, with the passage of time, ticks are becoming resistant to acaricides leading to failure of traditional tick control strategies. Conversely, patterns of acaricide resistance have not been studied at large in Pakistan. This project will be the first of its kind to investigate epidemiological aspects of the acaricide resistance in tick population in various agro-ecological zones of Pakistan. The project will further evolve the One Health perspective in controlling the tick-borne diseases in Pakistan.

Conversely, patterns of acaricide resistance have not been studied at large in Pakistan. This project will be the first of its kind to investigate epidemiological aspects of the acaricide resistance in tick population in various agro-ecological zones of Pakistan. The project will further evolve the One Health perspective in controlling the tick-borne diseases in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Development and Characterization of Modified Ultra-high Molecular Weight Polyethylene for Use in Total Joint Replacement
data.projectDigest:
Total joint replacement (TJR) is a procedure that involves replacing an injured or ailing joint with an artificial joint or prosthesis. The procedure has dramatically improved the life of patients with joint disabilities due to osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis. . Ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene (UHMWPE) has a long successful clinical record as the articulating surface material in TJR. Performance of the implants is closely related to the performance pyramid of UHMWPE which includes: processing, wear resistance, oxidation stability and mechanical properties.  This project addresses all the above aspects of UHMWPE performance.

In the first phase processing of UHMWPE will be covered. Due to its very high melt viscosity, UHMWPE cannot be processed by injection molding and is generally processed by compression molding technique. In this study, use of injection molding with UHWMPE will be explored by using either a mixture of UHMWPE and high density polyethylene (HDPE) and/or using Oscillation Shear Injection Molding Machine. For oxidation stability generally vitamin E is used, while in this study more promising tea-polyphenol antioxidants such as epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) and lipid-soluble epigallocatechin gallate (lsEGCG) will be explored.  Wear resistance will be enhanced by either radiation crosslinking or peroxide crosslinking which have been used previously. The wear resistance will be tested by developing a bi-directional pin-on-disc testing machine, simulating physiological condition in a hip or knee joint. Finally, mechanical properties will be characterized by the nano-indentation test which is a promising technique of characterizing the comprehensive mechanical behavior of materials.

data.projectName: Oxidative and genotoxic damage to mung bean and wheat genotypes by cadmium stress and its alleviation by priming with salicylic acid and silicon
data.projectDigest:
Some metals are essential for the growth and development of plants but these are required in small quantities. There are number of heavy metals like cadmium, which are extremely dangerous for the growth and survival of plants even in small quantity. Most common source of these heavy metals are effluent of industries, mining, extensive use of fertilizers and even motor vehicles, which can easily pollute our agricultural lands, water and air.
Due to rapid industrialization and improper waste water treatment system, untreated waste water can pollute rivers and our agricultural lands. As waste water composed of number of heavy metals and most of our poor farmers cultivate crops either near the area where industries discharge their waste water or irrigate their crops with sewage water as an alternate and cheap source of fertilizer. Plants will take up these metals through roots and may affect the DNA, and number of enzymatic reactions which ultimately lead to poor or no growth of plants, thus decreases yield and ultimately our economy. If such metal contaminated plants are consumed by humans may cause toxicity. Our agricultural land area is continuously decreasing due to number of pollutions, and due to building of houses or industries on these agricultural lands.  Therefore, there is need either to screen and identify metal tolerant plants or adapt different strategies which make plants resistant to metal stress. Exogenous application of silicon and salicylic acid prior to cadmium exposure could be included in such strategies.

data.projectName: Development of aquaculture technology for the native fish of Malakand division KPK, with special emphasis on economic development.
data.piUniversity: University of Malakand, Chakdara, Dir, Malakand
data.projectDigest: Aquaculture and fisheries contribute to 800 million peoples for livelihoods and provide 20% of animal protein for 3.1 billion peoples globally. Fish production in Pakistan decreased from 654,530 to 524, 2007 metric tons from 2007 to 2017. To resolve this declining issue and compete with the future threats the only remedy is aquaculture. In Malakand Division KPK, the cold water and semi cold-water fish species has also drastically declined by many factors including human activity and climate change. There were about 41 species in Swat River before flood 2010, but only 17 species have been reported after flood 2010. Therefore, the present project was planned to develop the breeding technology for the mass production of native fish (i,e Shizothorax Spp). fry in hatchery and its feeding requirement maximum production. Strategy will be made for the formulation and assessment of the artificial feed and rearing the fish fry produced in hatchery under controlled condition in ponds. Balance artificial feed will be prepared and the tested fish diets will be fed to fish Juvenile in the Ponds present in University of Malakand for attaining the marketable size fish. To assess the health of hatchery reared fry health and first treatment will be done during this project. The technology will be transfer to the local community by involving them in the field activities. This Project will promote sustainable aquaculture and fisheries, achieve food security and improve aquatic ecosystem by restoring fisheries resources. This project will help in ensuring healthy life by including fish in human diet as healthy protein.

data.projectName: Emerging Trend of Electric Vehicle in Pakistan Employ for Resilience of Electric Grid
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Sharif University of Engineering & Technology, Multan, Punjab, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: In order to tackle air pollution the incumbent government going to shift urban transport system that is based on gasoline to electric vehicles (EVs). The introduction of EVs will bring two major advantages, firstly reduction in air pollution, employment opportunities and reduction of annual oil import bill of the country that is expected to reduce by $2 billion. Secondly technical advantages like aggregated energy storage capacity of EVs can be used for the resilience of electric grid. In this proposal how to get techno-economic benefit of aggregated electric vehicles parking lots as a storage medium is the prime concerns. EVs will be used in this proposal as an energy storage. The individual battery of EV capacity is not meaningful for electric grid.  The aggregated storage capacity of EVs is more meaningful for harvesting the technical advantages. EVs parking lots (PL) can be used for aggregated storage capacity. In future in Pakistan there will be a potential areas that will provide us aggregated storage. These potential areas can be commercial parking of EVs, institutes, hospitals, etc. The developed model will be useful for assessment of techno-economic benefits.

data.projectName: Lignans and Omega 3 fatty acid from Flaxseed against Diabetes (in vivo study).
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is an under develop country due to which not only its economy is in every time stress but health and food security issue is also very dominant.  As a chemist as an educated society person  we want to release this stress by low cost  and long lasting health planning. As the population of Pakistan is suffering from a number of degenerative diseases including Diabetics so death rate by this disease is very high not only in Pakistan but also world wild. in under develop countries people use natural plants as folk medicine for procurement of disease. In rural areas people use natural source folk medicin for different purposes. So the aim of this study is to assess and highlight the prevalence of type 2 diabetes mellitus in Pakistan. For Type 2 diabetes in which a patient cannot use his body insulin we want to prepare a prior natural vaccine against type 2. For this purpose, natural medicinal plants are good source of Vaccines against degenerative diseases, chronical diseases, cancers and Diabetes also. Among these natural plants’ flax is a well-known plant whose seeds are marvelous source of antioxidants, phenolics, flavonoids, tocopherols, fatty acids (alpha linoleic acid and alpha linolenic acid) and lignans. From literature survey it is shown that flaxseed consumption is very helping to improve blood lipids in humans and flaxseed-derived lignan has been shown to enhance glycemic control in animals. Chronic antioxidant therapy may be useful in decreasing the risk of diabetic complications.

data.projectName: Evaluation of recycled aggregates stabilized with industrial wastes for use in road construction: A sustainable solution
data.projectDigest: Virgin aggregate from different rocks deposits has been used globally as a conventional pavement material. The same routine is followed all over Pakistan. However, due to rapid development these aggregates sources are decreasing at a very quick rate. To mitigate this, the research has been proposed to use recycled aggregates obtained from the demolition of old roads or building and mix with industrial wastes including coal ash, baggase ash, blast furnace slag and glass wastes. Strength characteristics will be determined in the laboratory to check whether these recycled aggregates blended with industrial wastes has sufficient strength to be reused in road construction. This study  will provide environment friendly and economical solution for the construction of new road. Concerns to dump road, concrete of industrial waste is addressed and on the other hand natural aggregate sources remain intact for longer time

data.projectName: Exploiting molecular systematics approaches for the identification pathogens involved in peach leaf curl disease in Pakistan and their historical biogeography.
data.projectDigest:
Peach leaf curl disease (PLCuD) is a fungal disease of global economic importance that mainly affects peaches, nectarines, and sometimes other stone fruits such as apricots and almonds. This is caused by at least four distinct species of the genus Taphrina. It has approximately 28 species, but T. deformans is the most prominent and widespread species of the genus. PLCuD is one of the major constraints for peach production in Pakistan. The disease cause both quantitative and qualitative loss to the fruit yield in all growing areas of Pakistan. Though, the disease is much alarming in Pakistan but it still remains largely unnoticed. It is unclear which fungal pathogen (s) may be actually involved in PLCuD and therefore, no serious attention has been given to eradicate this disease in Pakistan. But it is hypothesized that T. deformans may be the actual causal agent for the disease. 
The project is designed to identify the fungal species involved in causing PLCuD in Pakistan and exploit bioinformatics based approaches for the eradication of this disease. The fungi will be isolated from infected peach plant, identified and will be characterized by molecular techniques. Fungal DNA will be isolated from infected peach plant, nuclear ITS1-5.8-ITS2 (ITS) and mitochondrial ribosomal rRNA gene (rns) will be amplified by PCR and sequenced. Phylogenetic and biogeographic analysis of the fungi will be done to find the evolutionary history and understand the origins and dispersal pattern of important fungal species involved in PLCuD.  The aim of this study is to analyze the evolution and bio-diversity of fungi involved in PLCuD in Pakistan. Studying the emergence and diversity of fungal species in Pakistan will help to develop novel strategies for the control of PLCuD. This study will

data.projectName: Developing a bio-based washing solution using Alfalfa (Medicago Sativa) to reduce  the pesticide residues on fruits and vegetables
data.projectDigest: Fruits and vegetables are important agricultural produce in Pakistan. However, to enhance its production and yield, lots of pesticides are sprayed on fruits and vegetables crops. Most commonly used pesticides are cypermethrin and chlorpyrifos. These pesticides have major health concerns i.e., cancer, malfunctioning of reproductive, immune and nervous system. Recently, various studies have shown that the fruits in Pakistan contain a large amount of pesticides residues that are well above the maximum residual limits (MRLs) as per given by the Codex Alimentarius. Currently used washing agents to reduce the pesticide residues are synthetic in nature such as sodium carbonate, Clorox Germicidal bleach, sodium bicarbonate, and acetic acid. These synthetic chemicals are less effective if their side effects are considered while an enhanced rate of cancer in Pakistan requires a better natural detergent for washing fruits and vegetables. Therefore, this research is aimed at developing a bio-based washing agent using alfalfa (Medicago sativa) extract in combination with baking soda. Saponins in alfalfa (Medicago sativa) extract are thought to enhance washing efficiency of baking soda. Treated fruits and vegetable samples will be assessed for cypermethrin and chlorpyrifos residues using UV spectrophotometric method. A successful completion of this project will help to develop a natural washing solution that can effectively reduce the pesticide residues while enhancing the food safety and quality in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Surveillance of Human Papillomavirus and cervical cancer among HIV seropositive women in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
Cervical cancer (CC) is the fourth most frequent cancer. Almost 85% of the cervical cancer cases are from developing countries. Human Papillomavirus (HPV) is the main causative agent in the development of cervical cancer. Like HPV, Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) is also sexually transmitted virus and these both viruses are closely connected, although genetically both viruses are different, but both complement and foster each other in many aspects, frequently producing devasting outcome in their hosts. As Compared to the normal women, HIV+ women have greater risk of prevalence and incidence of cervical HPV infections. In developed countries organized regular cervical screening has helped to decline the cases of cervical cancer and associated mortality among females. 
           In Pakistan, National AIDS control program (NACP) Pakistan, guidelines provide specific recommendations for cervical screening for HPV & other STIs in HIV positive women, but routinely this is not in practice for HIV seropositive women. This study will initiate the National cervical cancer and HPV screening among HIV seropositive females in all Antiretroviral therapy (ART) centers also known as treatment centers of NACP all over Pakistan. The availability of screening test allows early detection of pre-invasive disease and cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN). CIN can be treated to prevent progression to invasive cancer. The Data generated will further help NACP to add HPV vaccination policy and program in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Dissecting the Role of m6A RNA modification in Cancer
data.projectDigest: The most abundant internal modification in eukaryotic messenger RNAs, N6-methyladenosine (m6A), has emerged as a crucial epitranscriptomic modification controlling various normal bioprocesses. Recent studies show that these regulatory proteins have a crucial role in different cancers including bladder cancer, breast cancer, lung cancer, leukemia and brain tumor, etc. Here, we want to conduct a study on bladder cancer in Pakistani population and correlate our work with the recent study done in the bladder cancer. In order to do so, we would perform an expression analysis to determine the levels of different writers and erasers in our cancer samples.

data.projectName: Transforming the occupational health through exposure assessment promotion
data.projectDigest: Health promotion is least priority on political agenda in Pakistan in terms of budgetary allocation and concrete actions. Here a targeted approach is presented to promote health in selected occupations. In Pakistan, exposure to variety of chemical contaminants and poor physical working environment cause numerous health problems to almost every profession. Additionally, individual vulnerability of workers due to age, poor health, poverty, and lack of awareness for occupational protocols further exacerbates. In low- and middle-income countries, overall environmental pollution especially in urban areas is beyond the control of governments. Therefore, in developing countries, citizens’ health is neglected, including the health of workers associated with various occupations which is the prime cause of rising global disease burden. Addressing to this issue, the United Nations (UNO) and the World Health Organization (WHO) set up a global agenda as Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) where the 3rd goal specifically deals with health promotion and occupational health improvement. This project will screen various occupational workers to quantify hydrocarbon exposure, assess cancer risk, enlist disease symptoms such as poor health, functional capacity, and cardio-metabolic abnormalities. Using mathematical modeling, future risk and prediction of every single health risk will be documented to improve worker’s health.

data.projectName: Preparation of Comprehensive Floristic List of Wild Plants of Southern Region (Mirpur Division) of Azad Jammu and Kashmir as Pictorial Monograph
data.piUniversity: Mirpur University of Science and Technology (MUST), AJ&K
data.projectDigest: The plants are important for human life because they provide basic necessities of life. The key aim of the project is to “Prepare Comprehensive Floristic List of Wild Plants of Southern Region of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), conduct Conservation and Propagation measures through Community Participation”. Inhabitants of the region primarily depend on wild flora for coping life needs like food, fodder, forage, fuel, timber wood, shelter, traditional medicines and other commercial use. The work will be based on field visits using for collection of medicinal and economic information of plants, sight snaps with phytogeographic marking, plant specimen collection for herbarium and determination of their conservation status. Conservation, propagation and protection of medicinally and commercially important species which are becoming threatened and rare will be conducted through nursery establishment with collaboration of Department of Forest GoAJK and local community involvement as they main stakeholders. This project research will assist in poverty alleviation, pollution control, mitigation of drastic climate changes, provision of increasing demand of fuel, timber, construction, medicinal plants for traditional cultural medicines and drug development. This creates an emergence of need to conduct detailed floristic study of plants of the area and assess their scoio-economic effects on indigenous communities and recommend applied steps for conservation, propagation and protection of the flora.

The work will be based on field visits using for collection of medicinal and economic information of plants, sight snaps with phytogeographic marking, plant specimen collection for herbarium and determination of their conservation status. Conservation, propagation and protection of medicinally and commercially important species which are becoming threatened and rare will be conducted through nursery establishment with collaboration of Department of Forest GoAJK and local community involvement as they main stakeholders. This project research will assist in poverty alleviation, pollution control, mitigation of drastic climate changes, provision of increasing demand of fuel, timber, construction, medicinal plants for traditional cultural medicines and drug development. This creates an emergence of need to conduct detailed floristic study of plants of the area and assess their scoio-economic effects on indigenous communities and recommend applied steps for conservation, propagation and protection of the flora.

data.projectName: Molecular Characterization and Development of Alternate Management Strategies of Dusky  Cotton Bug, Oxycarenus Hyalinipennis (Costa) (Hemiptera: Lygaeidae)
data.projectDigest: Oxycarenus hyalinipennis (Costa), is a serious pest of cotton and other malvaceous plants and it is commonly referred to as “Dusky Cotton Bug. Adults and nymphs suck oil from mature seeds and fluid from leaves of young stems to obtain moisture. If dusky cotton bugs are present in sufficient numbers, the cotton fiber becomes stained during processing by the maceration of their bodies which ultimately affects the marketability of the cotton. Studies of genetic variability in O. hyalinipennis are very important for wise and sustainable management. Different genetic markers e.g., Internal Transcribed Spacer 1, 2, 5.8S rDNA, 28S-rDNA, CO1, etc. have been established for insect biotype identification, geographical pattern etc, which also aid in the assessment of genetic variability. After correct identification of a certain insect species the management program can be initiated. In addition the prevalence of male killing bacteria and nutritional endosymbionts in the populations of different insect pests is already known, but its presence in O. hyalinipennis needs to be explored, which can improve the pest management programs . The injudicious insecticide applications have not only polluted the environment it has also threatened the life. The exploration of alternate safe management tools for the O. hyalinipennis will be carried out in the current research. Entomopathogenic fungi are a natural source for the control of insect pests of different crops even of the soil dwelling insects. These natural enemies/microbial control agents are important for the control of majority of economic insect pests of different cash crops and can be an alternate of insecticides.

data.projectName: Evaluation of Platelet Rich Plasma as Unconventional Therapy in Mastitis
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Mastitis is among the topmost important, expensive and common health concerns of farm animals causing massive financial damages to the agro-livestock sector of Pakistan (Ali et al. 2011). The extended usage of antibiotics is leading towards serious health associated concerns such as drug residues in milk and milk products; elevated trends of antibiotics resistance in humans and animals. Platelet Rich Plasma (PRP) promotes regeneration of secretory tissue by delivering a significant amount of growth factors to that anatomical location.
In the light aforementioned scenario, it is aimed to find a different management plan for mastitis using PRP as an alternative treatment option. There is no published data to ascertain the impact of PRP on dairy animal’s mastitis. The current protocols for the management of mastitis mainly consist of antibiotics and anti-inflammatory drugs that are limited to address the infection and inflammation of the udder but do not encourage the regeneration of secretory tissue. The current study is designed to assess the role of PRP as an alternative therapy for the cure of mastitis which is predicted to be a better option due to its regenerative and antibacterial.
Our study will help reveal whether PRP will independently be a helpful management option to address the inflammatory response, progression of tissue damage to the mammary gland parenchyma, bacterial infection and microbial adherence with the linings of udder tissues or it can be used in combination with antibiotics only. Prime objective of the project will be to evaluate the contribution of PRP in early recovery and reduction of the use of antibiotics.

data.projectName: Investigating the Readiness and Acceptance of Internet of Things (IoT) Solution in Agriculture Sector of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Government of Pakistan has emphasized on technological enhancement in the agriculture sector of Pakistan. Technological solutions like Internet of Things (IoT) can play an essential role in improving the agricultural as well as economic growth. Unfortunately, in Pakistan, adoption of IoT solutions have not been accepted widely. It is therefore necessary to investigate the readiness and acceptance of IoT solution in the agriculture sector of Pakistan. Therefore, the objective of the proposed study is to investigate the readiness and acceptance of IoT solutions in agriculture sector. The study is divided into three phases including development of IoT solution, measuring the readiness and acceptance of agriculturists before and after the deployment of IoT solution and interviewing the agriculturists to identify the key factors which may help in enhancing the readiness and acceptance of IoT solution. The proposed study will have high implications on agriculture sector of Pakistan. The study will allow researchers and practitioners to understand the key requirements and factors for the easy adoption of IoT solution in agriculture sector. The proposed study directly aligns to the sustainable development goals 2, 8 and 9 by providing more food, better economic growth and technological infrastructure development.

data.projectName: Role of ghrelin in ameliorating nicotine induced renal damage in BLAB/c mice
data.projectDigest: Cigarette smoking is the prime cause of preventable death and is far more common than drug abuse, alcohol and motor vehicle accidents. The findings from recent studies depict that cigarette smoking is an independent risk factor for kidney disease, imparting high burden on our hospitals and dialysis units.  Nicotine, the main component of tobacco, widely taken via cigarette and huqa in general population and shisha by young generation, can cause severe kidney damage. Ghrelin, a hormone produced naturally, is known to exert powerful protective effects on heart, liver, brain and kidney by decreasing the toxic effects of nicotine. Therefore it can be used to reverse nicotine induced kidney injury. Present study is aimed to illustrate the protective effect of ghrelin against nicotine induced kidney damage using experimental animals. We, having a medical degree and research experience, can extrapolate these results on human population, positively impacting public health. This project aims to benefit health care system of Pakistan by decreasing the kidney disease burden on our hospitals. In addition, ghrelin is currently used in various diseases worldwide; therefore it can be manufactured by local pharmaceutical companies providing incentive for economic growth of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Personality Detection through Handwritten Document Recognition using Machine Learning Techniques
data.piUniversity: National College of Business Administration & Economics, Lahore
data.projectDigest: The proposed system is a purposeful and effective contribution of the artificial intelligence domain. The proposed methodology is comprising on the cognitive psychology, machine learning, image processing and natural language processing techniques to detect the personality of human using handwritten document recognition. The major objective of the proposed system is to detect the personality of a writer by bearing in mind the lettering context of the person through his/her handwritten document. The proposed system is majorly divided into two stages: In first stage system will recognize the handwritten document recognition to understand what writer have written in the document using image processing techniques. Whereas the second stage comprises on the personality detection of the writer by considering his/her writing context using natural language processing, cognitive psychology and machine learning techniques. This proposed system will attain the attention of researchers due to its valuable contribution as assisting technology for visually impaired person. The idea behind adding personality detection is to maximize the adaptability in the behavior of the visually impaired reader by judging the nature of writer. This personality assessment will helps the reader in his/her further social interaction.

data.projectName: Epidemiology and mechanism of spread of carbapenem and colistin resistant enterobacteriaceae in dairy milk in Khyber pakhtunkhwa
data.projectDigest: Antibiotic resistance is a global challenge specially for poor and developing countries due low investment in health sector. Many curable diseases are now becoming incurable and mortality is in high mainly because of the ability of the diseases-causing pathogens to show resistance to antibiotics. This antibiotic resistance arise mainly due to over use and irrational applications of anitibiotics. Bacteria, mainly those from enterobacteriaceae has the ability to acquire resistance against those antibiotics which are constantly available in the environment. Furthermore, the current trends of massive and persistent use of antibiotics in food animals for therapy and as growth promoters provide an ongoing selective pressure for the emergence of antibiotic-resistant pathogens, such as colistin and carbapenem resistant Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumonia, which could be then acquired by humans and animals, and could serve as a source of infections difficult to treat. Carbapenem and colistin durgs are life saving drugs which are used only when patients are infected with drug resistant-bacteria. Therefore, resistance against these drugs is exteremely dangerous as we would left with no choice of treatment. This creates a great need to identify the presence of carbapenem and colistin resistant E. coli in food producing animal as well in human and define the association between the two entities. Thus far, no solid and systemic data is available to establish the baseline prevalence of carbapenem- and colistin- resistant Escherichia coli Klebsiella pneumonia in food animals and humans in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. This lack of baseline data precludes efforts to put in place for effective monitoring and interventions to control the spread of these highly antibiotic-resistant E. coli str

data.projectName: Improving terminal heat tolerance in bread wheat through exogenous proline and fulvic acid induced regulations in physiochemical attributes
data.projectDigest: Severe heat spells during wheat anthesis and grain filling stages cause fewer grains and shriveled grains per spike, leading to reduction in yields in many parts of the world. Access to quantitative yield losses due to heat stress, study of the mechanism for effect of heat stress and induction of thermotolerance through various management practices is essential under variable climatic conditions. Various experiments will be carried out under controlled and field conditions to ameliorte the adverse effects of heat stress by adding foliar organic salts such as humic compounds, osmolytes, seaweed extracts and amino acids. Ten existing wheat cultivars will be screened under glasshouse during the first year after applying heat at booting, anthesis and grain filling stages of wheat crop. During 2nd and 3rd years, two separate experiments will be conducted under field conditions on medium heat tolerant variety selected from first year experiment. Fulvic acid and Proline will be applied after imposing heat stress through perforated polythene sheets. This project will help in quantification of yield loss in wheat due to heat stress. Comprehensive information on the thermo tolerance in wheat will be made available to all the stakeholders and will help in adaptation to changing climate.

data.projectName: Metabolic engineering of essential amino acid content of wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) to improve its nutritional value
data.projectDigest:
The human body cannot synthesize essential nutrients that are required for normal physiological activity and essential amino acids are one of them. Deficiency of these amino acid contributes to compromised immunity and several metabolic disorders. The over-dependence on staple cereals like wheat which constitutes 60 % of the daily diet intake of a common man and lack of diverse diets are making malnutrition endemic in Pakistan. Biofortification of major staple cops through transgenic approach is a promising approach to combat malnutrition. That ensures the continuous supply of essential amino acids to the population that has no or limited access to diverse diets.
Wheat is staple crop of Pakistan and it constitutes 60 % of the daily diet intake of a common man in country. Cereals like wheat are the poor source of some essential amino acids. Several transgenic approaches have been made to improve essential amino acids profile. More promising results has been achieved by the expression of seed storage protein. In maize it resulted in the enhancement of essential amino acids and overall protein content by 32 %. In proposed study, the essential amino acid content of wheat will be enhanced through expression cassette of AH gene.

data.projectName: Semiconductors based Hybrid Heterostructured Photocatalysts for Z-scheme H2 Generation Activity
data.projectDigest:
Sunlight is one of the major energy sources of the clean energy. It is highly desirable to capture and store the solar energy in the form of H2, similar to the storage done by the natural photosynthesis in green plants, so that the stored energy can be utilized sustainably when required. Researchers are constantly struggling to develop green and environmentally friendly renewable energy sources that are self-powered. 
The hydrogen may be used for reducing the CO2 emissions. In this regard, by splitting the water through the solar energy, the Z-scheme photocatalytic hydrogen production is a potential way to gain the environmental friendly energy.
Photocatalytic hydrogen generation exploiting semiconductor material, which is one of the most promising method for solar energy conversion and has been considered as one of the ultimate solutions for energy and environmental issues. Transition metals, transition metal oxides, and metal sulfides are promising photocatalysts for hydrogen production and have gained much more interest in recent years. But the low surface reactivity and selectivity limit the function of transition metal oxides and dichalcogenides. To overcome these barriers nanocomposites of transition metal oxides, metal sulfides and their Z-scheme hybrid nano composites with g-C3N4, and graphite (GO) will be synthesized to increase the reactivity, stability and selectivity of the catalysts.

data.projectName: Sustainable Phosphorus Management at the Nexus of Phytoremediation of P-driven Eutrophication, P-nutrition, and Carbon Sequestration under P-enriched and P-starved environments
data.projectDigest:
Phosphorus (P) driven eutrphication is challenging the aquatic biodiversity due to nuisance growth of phytoplankantons and algal mat.  Regrettably, over-fertilization is building a ‘soil P bank/store’ due to sorption/fixation by soil particles/organic materials or complexation with Al, Fe, Ca, Mg leading to eutrophication. Phytoremediation is a low cost promising green technology. Under P-enriched environment, macrophytes can be efficient phytosequestr of inorganics (e.g. P) due to their rapid growth, more biomass and better phytoaccumulation ability. Selected macrophytes (Azolla or water hyacinth) will be deployed to remediate P-driven eutrophicated water. Compost and biochar (C rich co-product produced via pyrolysis) will be produced from these macrophytes and their influence on soil physico-chemical properties and crop growth will be estimated in addition to its carbon sequestering potential.
Contrarily, P facts, elusive soil chemistry, P-conundrum and high fixation of orthophosphate in alkaline calcareous soils of Pakistan rendering P-bioavailability and limiting yields of maize (Zea mays) and wheat (Triticum estivum). This project has been designed to elucidate low cost eco-friendly strategies of plant P-bioavailability for sustainable P-management in maize-wheat cropping system by enhancing P-acquisition and P-use efficiency from sparingly soluble or bound P under P stress environment. The outcome of research will provide a benchmark to translate information about plant rescue traits into germplasm under P stress environment that will improve P acquisition and P-use efficiency. Similarly, dual utilization of macrophytes will not only mitigate the eutrophication but their subsequent use will also enhance soil health and nutrient status and will sequester CO2.

data.projectName: : Institutes of Higher Learning  and Services towards Society: Preparing Undergraduate Students and Creating Opportunities  for Institutes of Higher Learning to be the Vehicle of Change at Grassroots Level  in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: This research project focuses on identifying role of higher education institutes in societal development in Pakistan. This topic is very unique in nature as no one have worked on it before. This is a very important area to work on as in developed countries institutes of higher learning are considered as vehicle of changes at grassroots level while in Pakistan there is a mushroom growth of the universities/colleges but no one can site any example of such interventions for benefits of common people of the country. It will be completed in different phases. In the first phase, a rhetoric approach will be applied to understand what has been done so for the benefits of common people at the institutes of higher learning. In the next phase, possible areas of work as per the nature of discipline will be explored and comprehensive plan of actions based presentations will be prepared. Seminars will be conducted in fifteen universities and fifteen post graduate colleges across Pakistan. In the last phase of this project, successful stories of interventions carried out by teachers or undergraduate students. Data will be collected initially through interview, then discussions in the seminars followed by focus group discussions if needed and in the last narrative inquiry approach will be applied to report successful interventions.

data.projectName: Consumer Adoption Model for Solar Power System

data.projectDigest: In the past two decades, there have been vast developments noticed in the energy sector. Many companies and individuals have preferred to rely on the solar system for generating electricity and using the power systems at their homes and specific workplace. But no one has focused on to development of a frame work that helps people in selecting the most efficient and economical available energy resources. This study will be focused on to prepare a Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) that provides the consumers a way out that will help them to adopt the most economical power system that is solar power based on their socio-economic conditions. This model also enables government and private sector investors to have a better plan for the investment in renewable energy sector. Also, the government of Pakistan will be benefited from this research project to set the more realistic goals in the field of solar power adoption.

data.projectName: Development of Traffic Flow and Lane Utilization Models for Major roads in Islamabad
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan, the annual traffic growth rate is 8%, which means that the overall number of vehicles using the major roads is expected to increase considerably in the future. The study of traffic dynamics on Pakistani road is therefore a critical issue. Investigating regular traffic flow patterns has significance as it can be widely applied in transportation planning, traffic control and traffic flow modeling and simulation. In this research project, our aim is to develop different traffic flow models (speed-density models), time-headway distribution models and lane utilization models for hetrogenous traffic flow on Kashmir Highway and Islamabad Expressway, Islamabad. First, the traffic flow data will be collected from different section using pneumatic road tube counters and GoPro video cameras. Then, the traffic data will be extracted to obtain the desirable parameter values such as speed, density and flow rate. The statistical models will then be developed by using linear and non-linear regression analysis techniques as well as multinomial logit modelling. Moreover, investigation of appropriate time-headway distribution model for Kashmir Highway and Islamabad Expressway is important as reflect traffic flow behavior at different section as act as key ingredient in the queuing analytical and simulation modeling of highway sections. Accurate description of time-headway distribution will will help us to assess the average dwell time and queue length of vehicles on these highway sections. Similarly, the study of lane utilization behavior under heterogeneous traffic flow conditions is helpful to plan and implement the strategies for the improvement of highways’ performance. It also influences the stability of traffic flow and an influential factor of highway capacity.
data.projectSummary: In Pakistan, the annual traffic growth rate is 8%, which means that the overall number of vehicles using the major roads is expected to increase considerably in the future. The study of traffic dynamics on Pakistani road is therefore a critical issue. Investigating regular traffic flow patterns has significance as it can be widely applied in transportation planning, traffic control and traffic flow modeling and simulation. In this research project, our aim is to develop different traffic flow models (speed-density models), time-headway distribution models and lane utilization models for hetrogenous traffic flow on Kashmir Highway and Islamabad Expressway, Islamabad. First, the traffic flow data will be collected from different section using pneumatic road tube counters and GoPro video cameras. Then, the traffic data will be extracted to obtain the desirable parameter values such as speed, density and flow rate. The statistical models will then be developed by using linear and non-linear regression analysis techniques as well as multinomial logit modelling. Moreover, investigation of appropriate time-headway distribution model for Kashmir Highway and Islamabad Expressway is important as reflect traffic flow behavior at different section as act as key ingredient in the queuing analytical and simulation modeling of highway sections. Accurate description of time-headway distribution will will help us to assess the average dwell time and queue length of vehicles on these highway sections. Similarly, the study of lane utilization behavior under heterogeneous traffic flow conditions is helpful to plan and implement the strategies for the improvement of highways’ performance. It also influences the stability of traffic flow and an influential factor of highway capacity.

data.projectName: Artificial Intelligence based Solutions for Maternal Health Issues in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The rate of pregnancy related deaths in Pakistan is among the highest in the world. An early prediction of complications during pregnancy plays a key role in prevention and/or better management.  In Pakistan, the shortage of doctors, under trained midwives and lack of necessary equipment in the hospitals of the rural and less-developed urban areas are among the major factors that hinder the timely prediction of complications and result in poor maternal health conditions. The emerging artificial intelligence techniques have already shown significant potential in solving various human health problems. This is a joint project by technical and medical professionals and aims to provide revolutionary solutions for health sector of Pakistan. The first goal of this project is develop an artificial intelligence based system for midwives to assist them predicting possible complications in pregnant women. With an early prediction, the patient can be advised to consult the qualified medical doctor in nearby hospital. On the other hand, in developed cities, the gynecology departments of almost all of the hospitals are overburdened. Thus, the decisions of gynecologists are prone to errors. The second goal of this project to design an assistant system for these medical professionals to help in decision making.

data.projectName: Development F1 Hybrid Seed of Bitter Gourd by Intraspecific Hybridization
data.projectDigest: Bitter gourd (Momordica charantia L.) is an important vegetable crop in Pakistan. It is consists of two famous local varieties, M. charantia var. charantia, which produces large fusiform fruits, and M. charantia var. muricata, a wild variety with small and round fruits. However, these two varieties have not fulfil the required demand of farmers. Because, local verities have the lack of resistance disease and pest, and low yield. Many companies have the imported hybrid seed from other countries is not suitable our local climate and created many new problems in the agriculture. Therefore, it is the needs time, we will make the local hybrid which have the suitable local climate, and resistance diseases and pest, and high yield. This problem can be solved by the Intraspecific hybridization in bitter gourd. Institute of Horticultural Sciences, University of Agriculture Faisalabad has developed its’ own bitter gourd hybrids through intraspecific hybridization. We have also many pure parental lines that have biotic and abiotic resistance against certain stresses. Data from phenotypic and genetic characters will analyzed to understand the transfer of parental genetic attributes to the hybrid F1 generation and to establish the interrelationship of the taxa. Evaluate the F1 hybrids which are the suitable in local climate. We will be make different crosses and get the F1 hybrids generation. Later which F1 hybrid will be perform best. We will be distribute into farmers community and later in future, we will obtained next generations for good varieties.

data.projectName: Potential role of Staphlococcus aureus Sortase b (sRTB) in cross reactivity with murine pro-inflammatory cytokines and in pathogenesis of infective endocarditis
data.projectDigest: Staphlococcus aureus is the Janus faced gram positive bacteria with one face of having normal flora of human nose & skin while the other face is more aggressive as it is involved in most lethal infections. One of the important infection is in a form of metastatic infections like infective endocarditis which is the deadly infection of heart valves leading towards the mortality. This form of infection is due to the development of vegetation of bacteria within the heart tissue. The exact mechanism of infective endocarditis caused by S. aureus is still unknown. Furthermore, the antibiotic resistant form of this bacteria also make it more aggressive for causing this infection. The role of surface proteins in establishing this form of infection cannot be ignored due to the vegetation development of bacteria. Sortase is one of the key enzyme involved in the arrangement of various surface proteins of S. aureus. This project will explore the role of Sortase B in the establishment of infective endocarditis by S. aureus. Similarly this role will be used for the management of infective endocarditis using anti-sortase B antibodies both therapeutically and pro-phylactically. This approach will be effective to control the antibiotic resistant forms of S. aureus as an alternative approach. Furthermore, another important dimension of this project is to address the cross reactive nature of S. aureus with murine pro-inflammatory cytokines. As per our hypothesis Sortase B also has a potential role in cross reacting with antibodies used for the determination of murine pro-inflammatory cytokines via ELISA and western blotting.

data.projectName: Future of Oil and Gas industry in Pakistan: A perspective on electric vehicles and Non Fuel Retail Business
data.projectDigest: In near future, the automobile sector in Pakistan is expected to experience a radical revolution as the current government has proposed and sanctioned the electric vehicle (EV) policy. The policy which is aiming to convert 30% of total cars in Pakistan to Electric vehicles. Government is offering many incentives to the industry including tax reliefs in order to promote and achieve this aggressive target of electric vehicles. However, one must be careful in terms of achievement of this goal. For the successful implementation of this policy there are certain proactive measures government must plan now. For example, do Pakistan has so called electric fuel stations (charging points) for these electric vehicles? Initially the government has to support this business as it may not be feasible in terms of financial returns. The purpose of this project is to analyze the current situation and proposed policy document to the government and PSO Management. The data will be collected through qualitative research techniques namely through interviews and focus groups. The expected results of the study would the recommendations to convert the current business model into a more viable approach for traditional fuel pumps and oil and gas sector and industry at large.

data.projectName: Managing Potassium from Alternative sources for improving soil fertility and wheat-maize crops productivity
data.projectDigest: Population of Pakistan is increasing at higher rates and food security is the main problem. In this respect cereal based cropping system is the best choice for gaining food security goals. The farmers are practicing cereal cropping since long in Pakistan. They are exhaustive crops and require a large amount of nutrients from exogenous sources. Chemical fertilizers are the main sources of the nutrients, used in crop production; however the chemical or synthetic fertilizers are very costly and have some harmful effects on human health as well as on quality of the environment. Similarly, the chemical fertilizer also has a great role in soil degradation and the losses from the chemical fertilizers are more as compared to the organic fertilizers. Efficient utilization of the organic waste is another constraint on farm land. They are being utilized desperately without knowledge for gaining fewer benefits from it. Potassium (K) is the essential nutrient required by plants in large quantities and it increases crop yields as well as quality in terms of nutrition and resistant against certain diseases and drought stress. The soils of Pakistan are generally considered to be sufficient in K but continuous use of high yielding varieties and hybrids leads to deficiency of K in the soils. The K fertilizer is very costly and the farmers cannot afford to buy it. Therefore the present research is focused on utilization of different agricultural waste generated on farms as a source of K nutrient.  The beneficial effects of these organic waste used in different forms on crop productivity and soil fertility will be studied. The K organic sources organic matter obtained from maize cobs, animal dung, sesbania stem, sugarcane bagasse and wood (saw dust), biochar of maize cob, animal dung, sesb

data.projectName: Development of next-generation lithium-ion batteries by utilizing lithium-rich cathode materials
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: In recent years, environmental pollution and greenhouse gases have come up as a major global issues. Governments across the globe have implemented the projects for renewable energy to achieve zero emission and reduce the impact of pollution. Cost of energy generation by renewable energy technologies for example solar or wind energy has significantly decreased in the last decade. However, there are issues with these renewable energy technologies, i.e.; solar cells can provide energy when sun is shining in the day and wind turbines work only when strong wind is blowing. Energy storage or utilization of grid energy is compulsory with these renewable energy technologies. Moreover, vehicle industry is gradually shifting its focus from gasoline to electric vehicles, in which high energy battery is a key component. Cost of current leading electrochemical energy storage technology, lithium-ion battery is significantly high. The objective of the project to develop high energy density lithium-rich cathode materials for lithium-ion batteries to increasing their energy density and decrease the cost of these batteries. In the long run this project will create a roadmap for low cost electric vehicles and will help to tackle environmental as well as economic issues.

data.projectName: Heavy metals and essential elements appraisal in breast milk of healthy mothers and cows to set data for infant formulations, and biological study to explore correlation between metal exposure and breast cancer in women
data.piUniversity: Mirpur University of Science and Technology (MUST), AJ&K
data.projectDigest:
In this study, we will address three areas: 
No.1: Breast-milk is the paramount source of nourishment for the infants but all infants are not breast fed because of health issues of mothers or their pursuit for looking smart. Hence, as an alternative, diverse infant formulas are being developed on commercial scale without using any established reference data regarding the daily permissible intake of metals/elements. But, there is no thorough study portraying natural levels of a series of essential and toxic elements including radioactive metals in human milk. Therefore, a detailed study on breast milk regarding the estimation of concentration of metals/elements to set background data for establishing adequate daily intake is required.
No.2: Cows’ milk is also used frequently to feed neonates instead of breast feeding. Unavailability of metal contamination data is a serious threat to the health of infants and other consumers. Thus, a comprehensive study on cow milk contamination would be beneficial for the society.
No.3: In recent years, the breast cancer has become a widespread disease, yet the fundamental reasons of the disease are mostly unidentified. In etiology of breast cancer, the prominence of estrogens has led to the idea that disclosure to ecological estrogens may enhance the risk of emerging the disease. Though, the breast cancer is evidently linked to the metal exposure, the role of metalloestrogens and noxious metals as causative agents in the etiology of the ailment remains to be well-known [43-45].

data.projectName: Development and characterization of a Transdermal Patch containing FDA approved NSAID for the treatment of Arthritis
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Pain associated with inflammation is the most common problem among senior patients which restrict in performing daily activities. Different medicines are available in the market for joints pain in the form of tablets, capsule, creams and gels. But oral use of large tablets and capsules for multiple times is not convenient for aged patients due to swallowing problem and other stomach disorders. On the other hand gels and creams minimize the contact time of medicament to the skin surface. Therefore there is a need of designing a patient friendly medicinal form which would fulfill the needs of the patients. The purpose of this study is to introduce a newer pain killer agent (NSAID i.e. nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory agent) in the form of a Patch that will attach to the skin for 24 hours and release the medicine to the required area. This form of medicine will be easy to apply and remove but it will also offer benefits to the patients such as avoidance of oral intake of large sized tablet and no stomach problems along with economical medicine for patients use.

data.projectName: An integrative pan-genomics and reverse vaccinology approach for development of drug and vaccine against Treponema Pallidum induced syphilis disease
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
Syphilis is caused by the Gram negative spirochete Treponema pallidum subspecies pallidum and is considered as one of the most imperious and systemic human Sexually Transmitted Infection (STIs). Every year, the global distribution of syphilis is increasing. In Pakistan, STIs are relatively ignored. During last decade, number of cases (syphilis) has increased in Pakistan. The current worldwide prevalence of syphilis combined with the lack of effective vaccine targets and the appearing of antibiotic-resistant strains emphasizes the need for development of new strategies.
In this study, we will identify core genes, considering human as host, we will identify conserved non-host homologous proteins. Further, using subtractive genomics and reverse vaccinology, putative antigenic proteins and drug targets will be identified that are essential for the bacteria. Molecular docking will be performed for identification of potent drug molecules. The top ranked drug molecules will be assayed against T. pallidum in vitro. While, the identified antigenic proteins will be cloned, expressed and purified in E. coli. The purified antigenic protein will be screened in mice models for immunogenic activity. Our proposed approach expedites the rapid and efficient selection of T. pallidum putative proteins for developing a broad spectrum of novel drugs and vaccines in future.
