data.projectName: In-Vivo Evaluations of dermatological Creams containing Phytoconstituents for the treatment of Eczema and Psoriasis by using Non- Invasive Bioengineering- Techniques
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Children of all age groups in Pakistani are affected by dermatological disorders due to polluted and contaminated environment.. Eczema is a familiar skin disorder, although infestations and infections are a prime root of dermatological complaints in people.Eczema leads to neurodermatitus.Skin is bruised by repeated scratching which causes the cracks, open sores and potentiates the threat of infection from viruses like Hepers Simplex and staphylococcal bacteria.It demands special attention in Pakistani community where dermatological treatment is very expensive and out of the reach of a common man. The question of our research is that is it feasible for us to tackle Eczema by utilizing efficacious, safe and cheap cream formulations comprising pure plant extracts or not.The prime objective is to develop cream formulations by entrapping those botanical extracts which have published activity against Eczema. Most effected human volunteers having Eczema will be selected for application of these topical formulations. It may be concluded that efficacious and safe topical formulations against the predicament of Eczema are expedient to develop,so that a large population affected by eczema can get benefit of these formulations afterwards. For this purpose different formulations will be trialled in Eczema affected volunteers. All the skin measurements will be taken by non-invasive bioengineered probes. Results will be compiled at the end of predefined period and conclusions will be made about all aspects of the studies conducted. We hypothesize that more than 80% volunteers will get rid off eczema and associated conditions. Hence we propose that this project should be approved in public health significance of Pakistani eczema affected population.

data.projectName: New generation nanoelectrodes based Lithium battery cells
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: In a proposed study, a sustainable energy storage system comprised of innovative cathodes, anodes and solid electrolyte scheme will be studied for high density Lithium cathode-based battery system. A wet chemical technique will be adopted to synthesize and characterize non-covalent assemblies of anodes, cathodes, and new generation solid electrolyte scheme in number of approaches, respectively. The synthesized material will be studied as cost effective, easy to scale up anode/ cathode material for highly efficient lithium batteries. For the purpose, the anode and cathode will be separated by a porous membrane separator system interacted by aqueous/ nonaqueous/ hybrid liquid or solid electrolyte. The electrochemical tryouts of the synthesized assemblies will be conducted by cyclic voltammetry.

data.projectName: Housing and health: Use of C-Reactive Protein (CRP) as Biomarker Data
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Concern regarding housing health impacts has a long tradition. Britten in 1934, reported the higher rate of mortality in slum areas of the United States and the United Kingdom. Probably the most well-known connection between health and housing is that between respiratory health and damp conditions moreover cold indoor temperatures. Biomarkers are valuable for valid measurement of outcomes that may be affected by social desirability or mental status or for moderate outcomes for chronic diseases that have long development time (cholesterol or blood pressure for heart disease). In this study, we will use a biomarker associated with inflammation and stress and report associations with different housing measures. We will focus on the biomarker C-reactive protein (CRP), this marker of inflammation-related to stress or infection. This study will be conducted among residents of Karachi Central district. A questionnaire on housing condition was designed with the help of the questionnaire used in study and the standard questionnaire  on housing conditions. From the selected house, a blood sample will be obtained from earning member of the family or his/her spouse who fulfil study criteria. All collected samples will be submitted to Dow Diagnostic Research Laboratory (DDRL) same day for CRP analysis.

Biomarkers are valuable for valid measurement of outcomes that may be affected by social desirability or mental status or for moderate outcomes for chronic diseases that have long development time (cholesterol or blood pressure for heart disease). In this study, we will use a biomarker associated with inflammation and stress and report associations with different housing measures. We will focus on the biomarker C-reactive protein (CRP), this marker of inflammation-related to stress or infection. This study will be conducted among residents of Karachi Central district. A questionnaire on housing condition was designed with the help of the questionnaire used in study and the standard questionnaire  on housing conditions. From the selected house, a blood sample will be obtained from earning member of the family or his/her spouse who fulfil study criteria. All collected samples will be submitted to Dow Diagnostic Research Laboratory (DDRL) same day for CRP analysis.

As per the minimum service delivery packages developed in different provinces of Pakistan, the envelope of services provided at PHC level has evolved and now includes provision of  services  including emerging common diseases. Since health education and behavior change communication are considered as specialized fields now, it is imperative that human resource . capacity shall be built in that area to control the risk factors of emerging health challenges. In this project, the effectiveness of introducing a trained health education officer at basic health unit and its catchment area will be determined by  change in the behavior and practices of patients and the community residents.

data.projectName: On Some Integral and Discrete Inequalities
data.projectDigest:
The project is devoted to the study, developments and applications of Mathematical inequalities. The project has been designed to achieve two major objectives. One is related to research and the other is the development of the trained man power, particularly equipped with analytical skills, which may have positive influences in the field of education. The research objectives of the proposed project are to formulate and prove the inequalities comprising of integral and discrete inequalities, which may play a vital role in the future studies. We intend to establish the applications of these inequalities to the mathematics and/or other branches of science. On the other hand, we intend to develop man power equipped with research and analytical skills. For this, we plan to engage and train PhD and M. Phil students and organize short courses for undergraduate students.  The outcomes of the proposed project are: 
•	To publish 6-8 research articles in HEC recognized journals.
•	To write a book which consists of recent developments in the area of mathematical inequalities. 
•	To prepare 1 PhD and 6-8 MS theses.
•	To equip 100 Undergraduate with analytical skills.

data.projectName: Rapid personalized treatment of MDR-TB patients through genetic sequencing and Deep Learning based prediction of Mycobacterium tuberculosis resistance
data.projectDigest:
TB is usually treatable with a combined regimen of four first-line drugs for 6 months. However, Multi-drug resistance (MDR) defined by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) resistant to first-line drugs and also extensively drug resistant (XDR), MDR resistant to second-line drugs is growing. Mutations in the MTB chromosome cause resistance and these can best be determined simultaneously by whole genome sequencing (WGS) of MTB. Increasing resistance associated genetic variation in MTB requires more data on local MDR/XDR MTB isolates. Also the complexity requires new computational algorithms to interpret sequence data towards drug resistance determination. Deep learning involving convoluted neural network algorithms allows prediction of resistance based on learning of variants and can be used to interpret novel genetic sequence data. We will use a novel machine learning TACNN (TB Attention Convoluted Neural Network) tool for drug resistance prediction. This tool will be made available online to benefit researchers and TB treatment providers.
Setting: This multi-center collaboration involves strengths in molecular biology, microbiology, genomics, computer science, TB treatment. This is a Private-Public partnership involving The Aga Khan University, Mohammad Ali Jinnah University, Karachi and the Provincial TB Control Program, Sindh, Ojha Institute of Chest Diseases and Jinnah Post-graduate Medical Center, Karachi.

data.projectName: Voice-based hepatitis diagnosis
data.projectDigest:
Viral hepatitis (VH) is a leading global health threat affecting hundreds of millions of people annually. The people enduring from this disease like forgetfulness, poor concentration abnormal shaking, anxiety, loss of appetite/weight, etc. Globally, out of 325 million, 66% and 30% people are infected with hepatitis B and C respectively. This figure could be doubled if the number of people living with hepatitis remains at the current level for next 40 – 50 years. Pakistan has high disease burden of hepatitis. The main factors for the transmission of hepatitis, in Pakistan, are blood transfusion, syringe reuse, surgery, therapeutics syringes and shaving from barbers. In addition, poor disposal of hospital waste and improper sterilization of medical testing equipment contributes to the spread hepatitis to hospital staff and hospitalized population.
Recent trends indicates that a  person's voice contains a good  information about his/her health.  In this project, we propose to diagnose hepatitis through voice and by using machine learning algorithms without contributing to the spread of hepatitis. The hypothesis of this study is to assess the relation of the patient’s voice and breathe with hepatitis infection. Using the standard methods, voice samples will be recorded and processed. The relevant voice features extracted will be fed to classifiers in order to identify whether the subjects are VH infected. Diagnosis via vocal signals may lead to an alternative, noninvasive, radiation-free, portable, and economically viable solution to diagnose hepatitis. The developed tools/methods via this study can also be used by a non-expert for the analysis of VH.

data.projectName: Autonomous Vehicle Localization System Design through Sensor Fusion and Stereo Vision  using Artificial Intelligence
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The project aims to develop a control decision system for autonomous vehicles. Autonomous Vehicles have complex electro mechanical systems with multiple sensors and cameras installed & a lot of processing going on each & every second to sense the environment and to act upon the latest data. The autonomous vehicle tends to act like a robotic car which can see & sense its surroundings just like a human being & can take necessary decisions according to the current data. High processing devices and  algorithms are required to replace the responsibilities of a human brain. A microcontroller/signal processor device is needed to collect the data from the environment through multiple sensors and cameras & then interpret the data to get converted into useful information.  A fusion sensor approach is considered in the proposed idea to design & develop a control system for the autonomous vehicle localization. Different types of sensors & cameras would be installed on the vehicle & they will communicate with the processor board to convey real time information. Then the control system would instruct the actuators to act upon the data coming from all the sensors to keep the vehicle on the intended path safely.

data.projectName: Deciphering epigenetic modifications in Alzheimer's Disease: A therapeutic approach.
data.projectDigest: Epigenetic mechanisms orchestrate modifications in DNA methylation, chromatin remodeling, histone proteins and noncoding RNA regulation. These alterations play a pivotal role in the cause and progression many diseases. Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) is the most common form of dementia in advance  age. Various physiologic and molecular pathways are affected in AD that leads to neuronal cell death. The underlying mechanisms of AD are still unknown. Neurodegeneration in AD is assumed to be controlled by multiple factors including genomic, epigenomic, metabolic, and environment. Among these factors Epigenetic studies are the least focused area in AD research. Various studies endorse  a decline in methylation of cytosine residues with age in different mammalian tissues. Beside this numerous post translational modifications (PTM) including acetylation, methylation, ubiquitination and sumoylation have been reported in histone proteins in AD brain forming a complex histone code. The proposed study aims to identify dysregulation in epigenetic mechanisms in neurodegenerative AD samples. This includes the isolation characterization and modification of histone proteins alongwith DNA methylation pattern in AD samples. An interactive combinatorial effect of of these alterations will be helpful in the development of therapeutic approaches towards AD.

data.projectName: Anticipation of abnormal activities in complex urban environments using multi-camera information fusion
data.piUniversity: Capital University of Science and Technology, Islamabad
data.projectDigest:
The tragic results of recent terrorist attacks in several parts of Pakistan as well as across the globe; and worrying official statistics on insecurity reveal that, despite the employment of existing surveillance technologies, the security of crowded places such as mass transportation sites is inadequate. The complexities of the environment and less availability of security experts make these places vulnerable to the disruptive behaviours. Nowadays people are getting used to the presence of video surveillance cameras in rail stations, airports, stadiums and such public environments. These cameras are collecting huge amount of data; however, the main use of these data is post-incidence investigations. 
In this research, the focus is on the development of automatic tools that can anticipate terrorist activities (or abnormal activities, in general) initially in the urban environments that would improve the efficiency of security agencies to handle any untoward situation. The idea is to develop next generation video surveillance system to recognise activities of interest from aggregated information gathered by multiple video capturing devices deployed in crowded environments. To this end, we start with developing efficient video analysis algorithms to track objects (that may include people and vehicles etc.) within single cameras. Next, we shall extend this video analysis to track objects of interest from a network of cameras to further analyse and understand local as well as global motion patterns. This analysis will help in developing and learning models corresponding to normal and rare (abnormal) events. An efficient use of these models may predict any untoward incident in real-time, on the basis of the recognition of abnormal activities.

data.projectName: Semiconductor doped and functionalized carbon-based nanomaterials for drinking water treatment contaminated with metals and pathogens
data.projectDigest: This project addresses the important issue of mankind and UN has made it part of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) i.e. drinking water. We intend to integrate nanoscience in the drinking water purification technology. In Pakistan we waste 962,335 million gallons of water annually. We will employ the nano-technology to generate advanced porous composite materials (carbon-based nanomaterials) for water treatment. We anticipate removal of pollutants, especially metal ions and water borne pathogens thus reducing the health hazards. By the end of this proposal we will be able to develop water treatment technology which would be cost-effective, economically feasible and affordable by the masses across various households. Sustainable use of crop residues and biomass abundantly available in Pakistan will be used for the preparation of activated carbon for metal adsorption on exchange sites of these carbonized materials. Semiconducting metal oxide nanoparticles and graphitic carbon nitride nanosheets will be doped into porous carbon. The composite materials photocatalysis will inactivate pathogens ROS mechanism, thus increasing efficiency and reducing costs. Since a large portion of the Pakistani population has no access to safe and clean drinking water, we anticipate to meet the government’s agenda of providing the basic needs to all Pakistanis at their doorstep.

data.projectName: Antibiotics, acid and heat tolerance of antimicrobials adapted pathogenic microbes
data.projectDigest: Proposed work is in the context of the forth-coming food security and quality concern that will limit the availability of safe food. To face this serious concern and to increase the production of quality food production especially in the developing countries where the access to healthy food is extremely limited, the present study proposes to find innovative strategies aiming at better exploring the microbial ecology and health benefits of functional foods. Antibiotic resistance is a major threat to human health and a reason of increase in mortality rate. The microbial resistance to the antibiotics is the major problem in this era so the scientists are trying to solve this issue by using natural compounds as a supplement or medicines. Antimicrobial compounds derived from natural sources are perceived to be safe and can be use as alternative to commercially available antimicrobial agents. However there is a possibility that bacteria get adaptation to sub inhibitory concentration on exposure to natural compound leading to cross-resistance or even adaptation to unfavorable conditions. The focus of this research will be to explore the impact of sub-inhibitory concentrations of antimicrobials adapted pathogenic microbes by investigating the development of self or cross resistance to the antibiotics.

data.projectName: Smart Diabetes Management System for Type-1 Patients
data.projectDigest:
Diabetes is one of the fastest growing diseases in the world. In this condition patients body either does not produce insulin, that is required for the body to convert the food into energy, or not produce enough insulin. In the condition where the body does not produce insulin at all is referred to as Type-1 Diabetes. T-1 Diabetic patients inject insulin to maintain sugar level in their body. Depending upon the conditions, environment and life-style a patient may need to inject insulin 3-5 times a day. Diabetes management for T-1 diabetic patients is quite challenging as they need them to remember the amount and time of the insulin dosage taken. 

In this work we propose a smart diabetes management system for T1 diabetic patients. The system would consist of an attachment device for insulin pens, that will record the amount of insulin and the time of the injection, a continuous glucose monitoring system,that will continuously  record the blood sugar level of the patient, and a mobile application, to record and analyse the data from the insulin pen attachment and CGM system. The mobile application and the insulin attachment, through analysing the data, will suggest the amount of insulin to be injected. The device will contain a memory, enough to store for several days. The system will help the patients  to manage their insulin doses and improve blood sugar level control. In order to support this aim, a follow-up research will be conducted to analyse the effects of the management system on patients blood glucose control.

data.projectName: Prevalence of neuropsychiatric disorders, associated factors in Pakistan: a population based Cross sectional study.
data.projectDigest:
There is a relatively more dearth of epidemiological research of studies in Pakistan into neurological and
mental disorders. It is important to understand not only the number and distribution of these disorders
in a country, but also how they impact on health in terms of both disability and mortality, compared
with other diseases and injuries. This research study is aimed to provide an accurate prevalence
estimate of all neurological and psychiatric disorders in all the geographical regions in Pakistan and also
to investigate demographic and socio-economic factors associated with these disorders as a national
survey. This research project aims to shed light on the true epidemiological status of mental disorders in
Pakistan. Hence, after understanding of the burden and distribution of these disorders then it could be
possible to respond and support further research necessary to develop better prevention and treatment
options. In Pakistan there is a significant knowledge gap for neurological and psychiatric problems.
Therefore it is very important to conduct a national population based survey on scientific grounds to
find out the prevalence and associated demographic and socio-economic factors of neuropsychiatric
disorders in Pakistan.
This will be a cross sectional study of nationally representative sample of households. We will
use multistage cluster sampling with stratification to pick households. This household survey
will have individual based face-to-face interviews and physical examination on cases as the
main data collection method. A sample with complete information of 30,720 individuals (5120
households) will be required. Ten districts will be selected including 5 from Punjab (Rahim Yar
Khan, Qusoor, Rawalpindi, Faisalabad and Chakwal), three districts from Sind

data.projectName: Towards Knowledge Based & Export Oriented Economy for Sustainable Development in Pakistan by Value addition of Glucosamine for Product Portfolio Development of a Company viz. GLYCANE Fine Organics
data.projectDigest: This project builds upon my six months of intensive entrepreneurship training in Québec (Canada) and then three years (approx.) of relevant postdoctoral experience at Lakehead University (LU) Canada and Northern Ontario School of Medicine (NOSM) Canada, where I learned the art of gram-scale production of precious fine organics, such as Muramyl dipeptide (MDP) and its derivatives. This training resulted in the conception of GLYCANE® – a company dealing in the field of precious fine organics. Now I propose using the local raw material viz. glucosamine (bi-product of fishing industry) to prepare an elaborate product portfolio for GLYCANE®. (www.glycane.com) This will result in better sale prospects for the company in North America, since the enterprise is familiar with the dynamics of precious fine organics industry and its regulations. Moreover, focus of this ambitious project is to train two Research Officers/PhD students. They will acquire advance synthetic chemistry skills and learn the preparation of enantiopure compounds on gram-scale for the company GLYCANE. At the end of this project, they will become permanent employee of the company.

data.projectName: Metagenomics Study of Higher Termites to Develop Commercial Baiting System for Their Management
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest: Termites are social organisms and mainly feeds on cellulose materials. Their cellulose feeding ability make them serious pests of buildings, crops and trees. Their ability to digest cellulose is due to presence of various symbiotic microbial organisms present in their gut.  In Pakistan, people mostly manage termite infestation by treating soil with toxic insecticides which are very harmful to the public, non-target organisms and environment (e.g. water pollution). However, baiting is the recent and environment friendly technique. All previous baiting systems are developed to manage termites in temperate regions of the world (USA, Austrlia, Japan etc.)  and are totally ineffective for Pakistani termite species. In the current project, we intend to develop baiting system by targeting gut microbial symbionts of termites which is first time in the world. We will use different insecticides (fipronil, thiamethoxam, chlorfluzuron, ivermectin, indoxacarb, chlorfenapyr) to prepare baits through a series of experiments. We will isolate DNA of termites and their endosymbionts. After applying different doses of insecticides, we will explore the lost endosymbionts and mortality of termites. The optimum doses of insecticides will be explored and tested in field baiting studies. After comprehensive trials, commercial baiting systems will be developed for termites’ management in Asia.

data.projectName: Application and determination of umbilical cord derived Mesenchymal and Hematopoietic Stem Cells Mechanism for Diabetes Reversal
data.projectDigest: Globally diabetes is one of the metabolic disease that target millions of young and aged is the result of the dysfunction and damage of ?-cells to control regularly fasting and non-fasting blood glucose levels. From the time of insulin discovery in 1921, many diabetic peoples are therapeutically treated with injection of exogenous insulin or used compounds for sensitization of insulin, or by whole pancreas and islet transplantation or stimulate endogenous secretion of insulin, but these approaches are inadequate for appropriate in vivo ?-cell functionality, that lead to uneven blood glucose regulation and initiating many diabetic patients to writhe from longstanding complications. Progress of stem cell technologies for regenerative therapy has advanced promptly in recent years. Diabetes has long been professed as one of the applications for stem cells–derived cells due to the damage of only a specific cell of pancreas—the insulin-producing cell of pancreas (?-cell). Regardless of marvelous efforts, however, humans have been far away from attainment in finding an operative treatment approach for diabetes. Therefore our study aims to develop alternative stem cells approach for diabetes.

data.projectName: Safety and Performance Enhancement of Mining Workforce Through Virtual-Reality-Based Education and Training
data.projectDigest: Safety is one critical aspect of mining. Pakistan's mining industry is characterized by lower safety  standards and record; and the accidents and fatalities are high. Because of the hazardous nature of work, on-job safety training is generally not suitable and innovative approaches are always needed. This project is designed to lay the foundation to use virtual reality (VR) for safety and performance enhancement of mining workforce. Simplified scenarios will be simulated in the head-mounted VR and the participants will be assessed on their safety. A training module will be prepared using VR-based safety training.

data.projectName: Synchronizing the Domestic Industrial Framework with Long-term CPEC Plan: Challenges and Way forward
data.piUniversity: National University of Modern Languages, Islamabad (NUML)
data.projectDigest:
After Free Trade Agreement with China (FTA) 2006, CPEC agreement, strategic alliances of Pakistan Economy has shifted towards from west to China. In comparison with the world’s strong and mature economy, Pakistani week economy may hardly sustain against economic fluctuations as an output of such integration. Hence, this would be an important player in reshaping future of domestic market and products. 

In future, connectivity will certainly increase risk of survival for local and indigenous products and services. Current study will contribute in policy framework to counterbalance the positioning and survival of domestic products by answering the question that ‘how does strategic partnership with china affect our local market and indigenous products? Secondly to what extent this linkage can be vulnerable for our own markets and local products? Solutions to such vulnerabilities can be taken as policy measure to cope with these challenges. Therefore, in order to enhance the understanding about expected outcomes of Chinese value chain on Pakistani industries through CPEC interventions, current study will be step forward to measure feasibilities, pros and cons of allowing Chinese value chain and its impact of indigenous trade transit and electronic industries in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Characterization of endophytic and rhizospheric bacteria and their application for organophosphorus degradation and plant growth promotion in peach.
data.projectDigest: About 2.5 million tons of pesticides are being used in world while 47000 tons are sprayed on different crops in Pakistan each year. World Health Organization reported 37,000 cancer cases yearly associated with pesticide use. The proposed project is aimed at evaluating plant-bacteria based system involved in improvement of plant growth and degradation of organophosphate pesticides in peach orchards. Constant use of pesticides increases soil problems. Current project is designed to explore microbial and genetic diversity of indigenous microbes from peach orchards. Evaluation of isolated microbes from peach plants and rhizosphere will be carried out in order to investigate plant growth promotion by bioremediation of pesticide in agricultural land. Investigations will be carried out to screen endophytic and rhizospheric microbes. Plant growth promoting traits will also be examined to assess potential of isolated bacterial strains. Moreover, screening of potential microbial strains for bioremediation of organophosphates will be done. Bioremediation potential of endophytic and rhizospheric bacteria will be evaluated in order to predict deleterious effects of synthetic organophosphates in peach orchards. Understanding and manipulating natural associations between peach plant and rhizospheric bacterial communities in combination with bioremediation strategies would be an effective and comprehensive method to reduce environmental pollution.

data.projectName: Exploitation of rejected primary and secondary resources of metals for manufacturing of sustainable bio metallic catalyst for proton exchange membrane fuel cell
data.projectDigest: Reserves of valued minerals are continuously exhausting owing to utilization of minerals and their products in different industrial processes and in energy fuel cells and causing risk to the environment. Now attention has been given to the production of metals from lower grade rejected ores and electronics wastes. These wastes are note treated chemically to recover metals due to high requirement of investments and infrastructures. So, ecofriendly method of bioleaching can be used to recover metals from rejected ores and wastes to consumable. This proposed experimental study will be conducted to investigate the rejected primary and secondary resources are the potential source of valued minerals and energy. Metals will be biorecovered by selected bacterial and fungal strains. After metals recovery, bio production and deposition of nano metals from leachate will be optimized by using different bacterial strains such as E. Coli, Desulfovibrio desulfuricans, Cupriavidus metallidurans mediated via the production of enzymes and loaded on carbon paper after drying and sintering the prepared bio nano metals. Loading of carbon papers with bio nano metals will be optimized for its functioning as an anode and test in proton exchange membrane fuel cell for power generation at optimum level.

data.projectName: Image Restoration for Outdoor Imaging in Surveillance Video System
data.projectDigest: Video Surveillance systems have been installed at different strategic and commercial sites in Pakistan. During adverse atmospheric conditions like haze or fog, the performance of these systems becomes degraded. The situation becomes even worse with smog in central Punjab region. As a result, the desired detection and recognition ranges become limited making the surveillance systems unproductive.   The solution under these conditions is to effectively restore the image before any other computer vision or image processing task. The objective of this research is to develop image restoration algorithm that can be integrated with application specific software as an additional tool and can be utilized under adverse atmospheric conditions i.e. in the presence of haze or fog.

data.projectName: Genetic profiling and antibiogram analysis of biofilm-forming bacteria from mastitis affected dairy animals
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Dairy animals are commonly affected with mastitis. Mastitis results in economic losses of dairy farmers and the dairy industry are due to decreased milk production and increased cost of treatment. Once an animal is infected with mastitis pathogens, there are high chances of recurrent infection. Recurrent infections are due to insufficient eradication of mastitis pathogens from the mammary glands. Mastitis pathogens which are difficult to eradicate have more likely tendency to grow in biofilms. The present study is designed to characterize biofilm-forming mastitis pathogens on phenotypic and genetic basis. Milk samples will be collected from suspected buffaloes aseptically. Samples will be inoculated on tryptic soy agar added blood agar, mannitol salt agar and brain heart infusion agar. Identified samples will be tested for biofilm development by Congo red agar method and microtiter plate assay. The genetic basis of biofilm forming isolates will be identified by targeting adhesion genes including icaA, icaB, icaC, icaD, clfA, clfB, and sua. Efficacy of antimicrobial compounds will be assessed against developing biofilms by biofilm susceptibility assay. The study will help us to detect local biofilm-forming mastitis pathogens which can help in effective control and treatment of bovine mastitis.

data.projectName: Developing Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) of English Language Pre-service/In-service Teachers
data.projectDigest: This research project aims to address the challenges and issues of English language teaching in the country by exploring the opportunities technology offers for the pedagogy. Since HEC Pakistan and the Ministry of Education are investing more in providing technological resources to the educational institutions in general and HEIs in particular, there is a need to focus on training pre-service/in-service teachers to be competent not only in pedagogy and course content but also in use of technology. The teachers require knowledge in order to make use of educational and general technology for inculcating subject-specific content knowledge to improve outcomes and also to remain contemporary in the fast-paced digitized world. This knowledge is referred to as the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK). In Pakistan, generally there are no specified degree programs for prospective English language teachers (except MA TEFL and that too has a limited scope since the educational qualification as a minimum recruitment criterion for English Language teachers is BS English/MA English); hence, the selected teachers usually join the academia with actually no specified pedagogical training, let alone TPACK. Therefore, focusing students of BS English and MPhil English (Linguistics/Literature), who form the pre-service/in-service English language teacher population, this study is an attempt to revamp their curriculum with the focus on developing their technological pedagogical content knowledge (TPACK).

data.projectName: Development and Characterization of Microneedle Transdermal Patches to Treat Hypertension: Its Ex-vivo and In-vivo Evaluation
data.projectDigest: We propose the fabrication of microneedle patch loaded with Bisoprolol fumarate for the treatment of hypertension and associated cardiovascular problems.  Bisoprolol, a selective beta-1 receptor antagonist, is recommended for heart-rate adjustment in the presence of atrial fibrillation and chronic heart failure. In intensive care unit, it is primarily used to reduce the heart rate in addition to blood-pressure lowering effects. Despite the availability of oral dosage form, complications including dysphagia, gastrointestinal dysfunction, tracheal intubation for an operation and other unmet need persist in the treatment protocol with Bisoprolol fumarate. Microneedles successfully pass the stratum corneum, with no or minute pain sensation and limited risk of infection. It has an added advantage of bypassing the first-pass effect and higher bioavailability can be obtained with improved pharmacokinetics. Transdermal microneedles can contribute to improve drug adherence because patients or caregiver can check for the presence of the patch through direct visual observation to appropriately monitor compliance to the drug therapy.

data.projectName: Synthesis and characteristic tuning of lead free and biocompatible complex metal oxide/polymer nanocomposites
data.projectDigest: This project focuses on synthesizing high coefficient lead-free and biocompatible piezoelectric and pyroelectric materials through simple and efficient chemical techniques. The synthesis of conventional Lead based piezoelectric materials would be avoided as lead is toxic to living organisms and has environmental issues. So we aim to develop lead free metal oxide/polymer composites with additional features of biocompatibility that would widen the utility of these materials, ranging from daily usable electronic devices to medical instruments. After basic structural and morphological analysis, the materials will be tested for efficient dielectric and ferroelectric response. Temperature dependent piezoelectric and pyroelectric measurements would be performed in order to optimize conditions for high coefficient materials that would enable to develop green energy harvesting materials. Furthermore, temperature induced phase transitions would also be analyzed to determine ferro- to paraelectric phase transition. Secondly, transition temperatures can be altered with the help of functionalizing materials chemically either through doping with other transition metals or making composites. Tuned functionality for these materials would help the scientific community to overcome the barriers in the field of energy harvesting and secondly help the engineers to design green energy-based devices to benefit the humanity at large.

data.projectName: Development of efficient textile plasma process for sustainable and water less finishing of textile
data.projectDigest: Textile is the backbone of Pakistan economy and there are thousands of textile mills in the country. However, use of toxic textile chemicals and conventional fabric heating at high temperature and for longer time leads to additional cost and sustainability problems. Nevertheless, these limitations can be overcome if textile fabric surface can be made highly reactive. Plasma can be described as fourth state of matter and highly efficient for the surface activation of the textile. Typical vacuum plasma will not be used in this research as it is expensive, complicated and non-suitable for conventional textile. In this project atmospheric plasma machine and its parameters will be optimized as per the requirement of the finish performance. All the major textile finishing chemicals like softeners, resin, fire retardant, oil and water repellent and antimicrobial plasma will be generated and applied onto textile instead of application by conventional padding. This waterless technique will not only save the precious drinking water but there will be no toxic textile water effluent as finishing will be water free. Archroma, Pakistan and world top textile chemical and process developer will be the partner in this project and will contribute technically as well as in kind donation.

data.projectName: DEVELOPMENT OF INDEGENOUS CONNECTION(S) FOR PRECAST CONCRETE CONSTRUCTION IN PAKISTAN
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The objective of the proposed study is the development of indigenous connection (s) for use in precast construction in Pakistan.  In the proposed study, a combined experimental/analytical program will be conducted to explore the efficiency of using different schemes for connecting reinforced concrete precast moment-resisting beam-column at site.  Different techniques of wet (i.e. poured reinforced concrete at site) and dry (i.e. erected) connections will be investigated.  Different proposed schemes will be applied and their performance will be compared to a control specimen(s) of beam-column connection monolithically poured.  First small scale testing would be conducted to ascertain the effectiveness of the concept connection design.  This would be followed by conducting large scale testing of precast beam-column proposed connection(s).  The considered comparison parameters are the connection’s capacity and ductility.  In the current design practice, the calculation methods are mostly based on experience and empirical formulas.  In this study, an Analytical model (FEM) would be developed for calculating the strength and ductility of the connection(s) and results will be compared (calibrated) with the experimental results.  From the analytical model, simplified design equations would be developed.

data.projectName: Multilingual Speaker Recognition and Cross-modal Transfer Between Face and Voice
data.projectDigest:
Speaker recognition is one of the promising research domains having utilization in bundle of real-world application e.g. authentication in high-security systems, forensic analysis and searching etc. Speaker recognition becomes extremely challenging under real-world environment due to intrinsic and extrinsic variations. These variations include speaker gender, age, speaking style, language, background noise and acquisition hardware issues. With the availability of large-scale audio-visual datasets, applications based upon multi-modal classifications can significantly contribute in the said domain.  
In this proposal, we have aimed to develop methods and multimodal applications by exploiting the multilingual aspect with state-of-the-art speaker recognition models. Keeping in view the local application scenario, we have targeted English and Urdu languages for speaker recognition. The proposal intends to employ the audio and visual information from the real-world Youtube videos containing speech of a particular individual. Unfortunately, there is no dataset available in the literature which contain audio samples of speakers with multiple languages such as English and Urdu. Alongwith creation of new dataset for local application scenario, the project is mainly focused on three sub-domains: Cross-language speaker recognition, Cross-modal transfer between face and voice, Cross-modal distillation.
The methods and applications built on this dataset will not only open new directions in speaker recognition but also promote Urdu language in relevant application areas. The targeted state-of-the-art applications include the novel approaches as well as will be productive in digital forensics and authentication applications; having direct impact on socio-economic growth of the country.

data.projectName: p38 MAP kinase pathway inhibition; A novel therapeutic approach against hyperosmolarity triggered anemia
data.projectDigest:
Hyperosmotic stress is an often overlooked condition that potentially 
  contributes to a many human related diseases. Anemia is among the common 
  problems of different diseases including diabetes that may be due to the 
  development of hyperosmolarity in the blood. Hyperosmolarity rendering cells 
  susceptible to programmed cell death. The p38 mitogen-activated protein 
  kinase (MAPK) is activated by hyperosmotic shock and contributes actively in 
  the regulation of cell proliferation and suicidal death. Similarly, Hyperglycemia 
  in diabetes leads to hyperosmolarity that may results in p38 mitogen-activated 
  protein kinase activation. Erythrocytes are the most abundant circulating cells 
  in the blood and are the principal means of oxygen supply to the different 
  tissues, failure of which may be due to anemia. Like apoptosis of nucleated 
  cells, nucleus devoid erythrocytes may undergo suicidal death or eryptosis with 
  same feature and mechanism like hyperosmotic stress and oxidative stress. 
  The most important pathological outcome of enhanced eryptosis in several 
  clinical disorders is anemia. Enhanced eryptosis has been reported in chronic 
  diabetes patients, may be due to hyperosmolarity and can be the cause of 
  anemia. Frequent intake of plant based foods and compounds significantly 
  reduce the mortality rate due to cancer and cardiovascular diseases. In this 
  project, we have planned to find out plant based p38 inhibitors with potential 
  ability to counteract hyperosmolarity stimulated suicidal death of erythrocytes 
  and protect the patients from the complications of anemia.

data.projectName: A Software Design Tool for the AI-Based Automation of Wind Farms
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest:
The primary objective of this research is to develop a tool for the automation of wind farms based on the efficient and stable artificially intelligent soft computing techniques. The goals of automation of wind farm consist of following three parts;
1.	Structural and design optimization of wind turbine blades.
2.	Optimal micro-siting of onshore wind turbines based on AI techniques.
3.	Optimal micro-siting of wind turbines on high rise buildings of metropolitan cities based on AI techniques.
The performance of AI based algorithms will be observed and checked to the performance in order to answer the first research question. In addition, each of AI based algorithms will be compared against the others with the goal of answering the second and third research questions.  In the first research question, it is asked whether the AI based algorithms can improve the quality of the solution to the wind farm layout optimization problem as compared to a simple genetic algorithm or not. In the second research question, it would be explored that Which AI based algorithm works best for the wind farm layout optimization problem? What properties are essential for its success? In the third research question, the main focus is on the main aerodynamic and structural characteristics of the blades that can be employed as design variables for maximum annual energy production (AEP), the minimum blade mass and the minimum blade cost.

data.projectName: WHY WE ARE STAGNANT IN TERMS OF NUTRITIONAL STATUS?   CAMPAIGN FOR HEALTHIER PAKISTAN
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is one of the few countries in the world where more than half of the under-five year old population suffers from either stunting or wasting, or both. According to the latest available figures, the under-5 stunting rate in the country is as high as 46%, the third highest rate in the world. Malnutrition in its different types and forms is a critical issue for the country, which requires increased commitment on the part of government. Undernutrition has now become a stigma to the country despite of having an agriculture base. Statistics indicate that we produce enough food in terms of quantity and quality, but nutritional status of the families has become stagnant since last more than seven decades. Previous five Nutritional Surveys show no improvement in nutritional status despite of many interventions at various  levels. The question arises then what is the hidden cause for this stagnancy. The present project intends to explore the causes other than food availability by studying the dietary habits of the families. This exploratory survey will lead to dig out the real cause which can be targeted in the 2nd phase of the study period with the help of mass media campaign.

data.projectName: Design and Development of Indigenous Renewable Energy Technologies for Sustainable Rural and Agriculture Development
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: The energy sustainability of any country has a strong correlation with its social and economic development. The rapidly increasing world population has led to adverse effects on ageing infrastructure and increased energy consumption. Many developing countries have been facing severe energy crises, specifically in the last few decades which have adversely affected their domestic, commercial, industrial and agriculture sectors. It is worth mentioning that most of industrial processes like pasteurization, sterilization, drying and distillation operate in the medium temperature range. The temperature ranges for all these processes lie between 60-280 °C. The solar-based technologies results have clearly shown that lower operating costs are possible, thus increasing the net revenue by agriculture products processing as well as minimizing crop and fruit waste. The main objective of this outreach research project is to enhance collaboration in teaching and research and to investigate several applications for the processing of different agricultural products using modified designed of solar distillation system, solar drone sprayer, off-grid solar PV system and other renewable energy technologies. The most likely project outcome will be capacity building of farmers/end users, students and trainers for selection and operation of efficient, economical and environment friendly renewable energy technologies for sustainable agriculture development.

data.projectName: Exploring Control Strategies to Mitigate Outbreak Threats of Desert Locust in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Recent locust plague hit Pakistan for the first time in more than two decades .It is considered as big historical disaster to the agriculture and livestock.  It is estimated that million acres fertile land was badly affected by this sudden eruption although, earlier  plagues persist for shorter time periods but recent plagues is largest one started from May 2019 and continued till December 2019. Mostly the aerial operation was undertaken against this attack but unfortunately situation in many areas is still depraved and out of control. The purposed project will be highlighted the direct effects of climatic on migration, movement survival, and reproduction optional of locust in Pakistan along with effective control strategies. In this project we will uses the most up to date techniques: remote sensing, GPS and GIS, including well-coordinated efforts such as:  use of mycopesticies (EPFs) recommendation of cultivation of nitrogen low plantation, cultural and physical operation against locust. Beside this, Investigation on origin of swarming 2 Breeding zones of S. gregaria in Pakistan , Examination of environmental factors that affect phase change, along with the wider impact of land use and management strategies that may unwittingly create environments conducive to outbreaks 4. Estimation of crops losses and its negative impact on food security and reproductive activities with all life parameters in solitarious and gregarious phases will also be compared.

data.projectName: Designing the Nanocables based Microarrays and their Polymer Matrix as a Reliable Gas Sensors.
data.piUniversity: Mirpur University of Science and Technology (MUST), AJ&K
data.projectDigest: The Nanowires have structural anisotropy and demonstrate the properties which are very related to specific structure (111). Its surface is usually labile and become oxidized when stored for longer time. These are coated with polymer, which primarily protect the surface against oxidation, but polymer during growth process become highly induced by the structure of core and prefer to adopt the coaxial growth. The coaxial trend of growth result the unique pattern of growth, which ultimately become desirable for particular properties and applications. By this way, the special polymer properties are added alongwith protective application. Later on, the nanocables would be transformed into single orientation called microarrays. It can be achieved by torque producing force under chemical interactions. The microarrays of Carbon Nanotubes, silicon nanowires, selenides and nitrides are usually found as sensor and components of electronics devices. However, microarrays of metal nanocable which is more durable against oxidation and entertains the additional properties is still missing. We are optimizing the microarrays of nanocable for electronics and sensing. Herein, the microarrays of metal nanocables would be reinforced into polymer matrix. Such system would append the anisotropic characters of microarrays on the polymer matrix and help to increase the sensitivity of different gases mentioned in summary and also increase the adsorbing capacity of different gases also. Thus, the designed material would build a good platform having specific applications with reference to environmental, biological and social sectors.

data.projectName: Study on Interface adsorption during cathodic charge-discharge in lithium  sulfur battery
data.projectDigest:
Energy is the developmental basis of national economy and essential for people's daily life. 
Pakistan have need to set ambitious targets for renewable energy generation in the country, which will require energy storage systems to tackle the challenges of renewable energy, including inconsistent supply. Portable gadgets and boom in electric vehicles make storage system more reliable to industry and consumers. The resources of fossil fuels are exhausting and increasing global warming due to combustion of fossil fuels require the development of high-performance lithium based batteries.  In this sense, lithium-sulfur (Li-S) battery is a focus of concern, because sulfur is environmentally benign, naturally abundant and has a theoretical gravimetric energy density up to five times greater than that of present lithium-ion battery which is the solution for the main issues of energy storage, cost and supply requirement. To fabricate high performance sulfur based composite cathode material can anchor the polysulfide to avoid its dissolution and diffusion and optimize the dynamics of electrochemical precipitation of elemental sulfur and lithium sulfide. This project will deepens the cognitions on lithium-sulfur chemistry and will provide scientific basis for sulfur based battery chemistry of high cycleability and long life span.

data.projectName: Engineering of Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs) Nanocomposites and thier Use as Cargo Carriers for Therapeutic Applications
data.piUniversity: Lasbela University of Agriculture, Water and Marine Sciences, Lasbela
data.projectDigest:
Cancer is creating serious threats to human life in Pakistan causing death of thousands every year due to lack of awareness, failure in early diagnosis and inappropriate medication. Different therapeutic techniques are being used for cancer treatment viz. chemotherapy, immunotherapy, surgery, radiation therapy, thermal therapy etc. Chemotherapy has edge over other therapeutic techniques because of its effectiveness for all types of cancer. However, ineffective and irrelevant medications is causing adverse impact on patients and eventually results in death. Since the revolution in nanotechnology in late nineties, nanoparticles based cancer chemotherapeutic drugs have been industrialized in pharmaceutical industry because of their effectiveness in high accumulation on tumor site. Nanotechnology-based drug delivery systems (NDDSs) exhibit promising therapeutic efficacy and reduced side effects in cancer therapy owing to enhanced permeability and retention (EPR) effect. Apart from these advantages, impolite physiochemical features of therapeutic agents result in an unproductive distribution and uninvited or even in detrimental side-effects which eventually results in patient’s death. 
It has ever been fascinating to design nanotherapeutics loaded with heaps of anticancer drug molecules to accomplish synergistic effect between cytotoxicity of loaded drugs and drug carriers in response of macrophage inflammation. Inspired from the approach, we rationally suppose here to anticancer drug loaded anticancer different metal-organic frameworks based nanotherapeutic for cancer chemotherapy in vitro and in vivo via novel swift and facile one-pot strategy. We suppose to achieve more than 15% (wt. %) drug loading in nanohybrids by varying drug feed ratio and other factors.

data.projectName: Insilco identification of dual allosteric inhibitors of SHP2 with therapeutic potential for cancer treatment
data.projectDigest: The utilization of computer-aided drug design technologies in the research and development approaches of a company could lead to reducing the cost of drug design and development up to 50%. We are focusing on the cancer-associated target protein; SRC homology phosphatase 2 (SHP2). SHP2 is involved in different cellular processes, including cell proliferation, differentiation, and migration. SHP2 has been shown to contribute to the progression of several types of cancer, including leukemia JMML (Juvenile Myelomonocytic leukemia), AML (acute myeloid leukemia), and ALL (acute lymphocytic leukemia), gastric, and breast cancers. Although view the critical importance of SHP2 as a potential anticancer target, the discovery of pharmacologically small molecule inhibitors has attracted broad interest in the scientific community. Thus the aims of the current study are, Computer-Aided structural and mechanistic elucidations to design novel and potent dual allosteric inhibitors for SHP2 with increased potency and selectivity for the interface residue to inhibit the aberrant activation of SHP2 based on previously reported allosteric inhibitor (SHP099, SHP244) which reveal low potency and bioavailability. The computationally identified potential inhibitors will be experimentally tested in the laboratory of our collaborators. Where the identified compounds will be screened using different anti-cancer assays.

data.projectName: To study quantum transport in the presence of disorder and topology using quantum walks
data.piUniversity: Kohat University of Science and Technology, Kohat
data.projectDigest:
Topological insulators are materials  which behave like ordinary band insulators in the bulk, but is conducting at their surface (or edge) [1]. The hallmark of topological insulators is the existence of edge states which propagate unidirectionally along their boundary. A remarkable property of edge states is their robustness, i.e. these remain conducting even in the presence of gentle perturbations and impurities in the system. Due to these novel features, edge states are of great interest from the technological point of view, where these can potentially be used in spintronics devices and quantum computation [2, 3]. 
In this project, we will investigate quantum transport in a topological insulator in the presence of spatial disorder. A common intuition is that a spatial disorder in a condensed matter system results in Anderson localization [4]. However, the presence of topological order in such systems can result in a counterintuitive behavior. For example, a topological insulator can escape Anderson localization in the presence of disorder if it is tuned to a topological phase transition point [5, 6, 7]. We will use system of quantum walks to investigate the interplay between disorder and topology in a topological insulating system. 
We will aim at the following goals:
To study the effect of spatial disorder on quantum transport phenomena in the vicinity of the critical point, i.e. close to a boundary between two distinct topological phases
To study the robustness of quantum transport against different types of disorder
To identify the conditions for the localization-delocalization transition in a topological insulator in the presence of spatial disorder
We will employ scattering matrix approach to investigate the topological invariants of the disordered system

data.projectName: Hybrid Automatic Repeat Request for Error Control in OFDM Systems
data.projectDigest: We all might remember getting our first email on a mobile device. The frustration of downloading a big attachment or video streaming is also not forgettable. Today, our smartphones download largest attachments in seconds using mobile data and high definition video streaming is a normal process for a mobile user. Tomorrow, more data in magnitude will be downloaded on mobile devices as compared to the current usage. According to Cisco forecast, by 2022, our networks will be able to give a support of 20 exabytes of mobile data downloading, which is nearly 10 times per today’s consumption. Now these increasing demands of high mobile data plays a significant role in the definition of 5G. This rapid evolution of wireless communications systems has increased the demand for efficient broadband service on mobile devices with high data rates and better quality of service. The evolution of 5G does not only aim for enhanced mobile broad band rates, it is also aimed to cover Internet of Things (IoT) which may be called as machine type communications. IoT involves people to machine and machine to machine communications. It is well known that 4G uses a multicarrier technique on its air interface. Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) with digital communication systems have widely been used in earlier wired and wireless networks.  The potential candidate waveforms for 5G are different variants of OFDM. This project focuses on using Hybrid Automatic Repeat Request for correct the errors that have caused because of non-linear amplifiers in OFDM systems.

data.projectName: Numerical Study of fixed points in digital metric space and their applications in digital imaging
data.projectDigest:
In this project our focus is mainly on the numerical fixed point in digital metric space. The digital metric space is the new emerging field in the fixed point theory. It is based on general topology and functional analysis, which is helpful in analyzing the digital features of 2D and 3D images. This is used as a tool to study the digital images. The discrete object are based on the fundamental groups which are first introduced by Kong. The topological concepts in terms of digital version is defined first by Boxer. The digital metric space is used in different ways to analyze the digital features of digital images.
The fixed point theorems are defined for the digital metric space in this project. These theorems are based on the different mappings such as, commutative, weakly commutative, compatible, weakly compatible. The common fixed points will be described on these mappings in digital metric space. To support these results some constructive examples will be provided. As an application the numerical fixed points will be calculated.
This study will be helpful in the field of computer science, computer graphics and in image processing. Beside this project it deals with different sub fields in mathematics such as approximation theory, mathematical morphology and optimization theory. Fixed point theory has many potential applications in various fields such as mathematics, computer science, game theory, engineering, fuzzy theory and image processing. The fixed points are helpful in many engineering problems and can generalized in many ways.

In this project our focus is mainly on the numerical fixed point in digital metric space. The digital metric space is the new emerging field in the fixed point theory. It is based on general topology and functional analysis, which is helpful in analyzing the digital features of 2D and 3D images. This is used as a tool to study the digital images. The discrete object are based on the fundamental groups which are first introduced by Kong. The topological concepts in terms of digital version is defined first by Boxer. The digital metric space is used in different ways to analyze the digital features of digital images.
The fixed point theorems are defined for the digital metric space in this project. These theorems are based on the different mappings such as, commutative, weakly commutative, compatible, weakly compatible. The common fixed points will be described on these mappings in digital metric space. To support these results some constructive examples will be provided. As an application the numerical fixed points will be calculated.
This study will be helpful in the field of computer science, computer graphics and in image processing. Beside this project it deals with different sub fields in mathematics such as approximation theory, mathematical morphology and optimization theory. Fixed point theory has many potential applications in various fields such as mathematics, computer science, game theory, engineering, fuzzy theory and image processing. The fixed points are helpful in many engineering problems and can generalized in many ways.

data.projectName: Factorisations of restriction semigroups
data.projectDigest: A semigroup is an algebraic structure consisting of a set together with an associative binary operation. Semigroups appear and are used in many mathematical areas other than algebra, such as, theoretical computer science, category theory, analysis and number theory. This application proposes to study a wide class of semigroups known as restriction semigroups, which are a  topic of emerging importance. Such semigroups arise from the study of partial transformations in the same way that groups arise from the study of bijections. To understand the behaviour of big structures in algebra, a classical and powerful approach is to break, or `decompose’, them into small pieces. Understanding the small pieces can determine the properties of the whole structure. We aim to study restriction semigroups by decomposing them as semidirect and Zappa-Szep products. These constructions are generalisations of direct products and are famous tools to decompose algebraic structures. Thus, to determine properties of restriction semigroups we break them into components  - well understood subsemigroups or submonoids – which we then glue back together with the help of semidirect and Zappa-Szep products. This process involves actions of two semigroups on one another. The semidirect and hence Zappa-Szep product of two  restriction semigroups are not restriction in general. data.projectName: Design and development of multi-stage inverter for Photo-voltaic systems
data.projectDigest:
Solar PV is an up and coming field in Pakistan. Currently Pakistan imports approximately 1000MW of PV modules every year. The cost of the accessories required for the installation and grid integration of these solar PV systems is grossly on par with the cost of PV modules. Among these accessories solar inverters form a lion’s share of the expenditures. The proposed project will develop enhanced solar PV inverters which meet the IEC standards and are economical in manufacturing eventually contributing towards cutting the cost of solar PV technology. 
 The national exchequer incurs millions of dollars in the import of the inverters from foreign countries. In this context the development of indigenous inverter technologies that can perform much better than the imported ones would be a big boost to achieving grid parity for solar PV power in Pakistan. Additionally, this will also pave the way for realization of the plans of achieving 20% renewable energy capacity by 2030. 
Similarly, the project will serve as a capacity building platform for the students of engineering university, envisaging a career in renewable energy. The students will be amply trained on the solar PV technology and inverter design and performance enhancement. This will also contribute towards the aforementioned renewable energy national goals.

data.projectName: The invasion of Apple Snails in Pakistan: A potential threat to wetlands and rice fields of lower Sindh, Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Biological invasion has become one of the most serious threats to ecosystems worldwide (Vitousek et al., 1997; Sala et al., 2000). The economic damage caused by invasive species is US$1.5 trillion per year, about 5% of global gross domestic product (Pimentel et al., 2001).
Apple snails are among the worst invasive species in Southeast Asia. These snails are non-native mollusk to Indian subcontinent, and believed to be native to Argentina (Joshi, 2007). With high reproduction rate and tolerance to harsh environmental conditions, it is among the world’s worst invasive species (GISD, 2013). 
Apple snails are considered as pest for rice, they damage young rice seedlings and causing a major threat to the productivity and pro?tability of rice farming globally (Wada, 2004; Joshi, 2007; Horgan et al., 2014; Horgan, 2017b). The species of Pomacea were established in South and N. America, East and SE Asia. Recently they have invaded S. Asia (Pakistan) (Baloch et al., 2012; Hayes, 2012; Horgan et al., 2014). 
The invasion of apple snails to Haleji Lake, Keenjhar Lake and several large and small canals in the area require a careful documentation of the spread of apple snails and their impact on aquatic ecosystems and rice fields in District Thatta is need of the hour. 
The proposed research will encompass the magnitude of damage or threat to the water bodies and rice crop in the area by this invasive species. The infested area will be identified and damage to rice field and aquatic environments will be estimated.
Control measures through biological (ducks/ fish) and physical (hand picking) methods will be applied. The chemical method will be avoided because it may cause threat to aquatic environments. The local communities will be trained to eradicate the apple snails from the area

data.projectName: Electrical Modulation of water droplet and its applications
data.projectDigest: Liquid-solid interface has gone from an interesting academic exercise to an integral part of not only in fluidics but also many other fields of science and technology at micro and nano levels. The interfacial electrical properties are due to the electric double layer in the interface, this layer basically constitute the co-ions and counter ions. Now we can modulate the droplet or the particles inside the droplet in very controlled and with great precision by the application of the electric voltage.  This is used to move water droplet as in electrowetting or to modulate different coagulations as in displays. But as with most new technologies, the practical implementation of this technology has taken a while to happen because of some challenges for example electrowetting enables to fabricate a droplet based micro-vehicle to carry nano-particles or color pigments. But these small particles inside the droplet may cause damage underneath hydrophobic layer of the substrate. Thus, it causes instability to the droplet based micro-vehicle. Moreover, continuous propulsion of micro-vehicle needs very fine patterned electrodes on the substrate, which obviously increase complexity of prototype. By improving the stability and decreasing the complexity will have advantages to fabricated the micro-vehicle, display devices, variable focal lenses and many more. On the other hand, contact electrification also used these interfacial charges to convert untapped environmental energies to electrical energies. This device has very low efficiency therefore have need to address the low efficiency problems of such devices. At the end we have also plan to modulate the 2D colloids electrically to switch the device in very controlled way by modulating electric double layer.

data.projectDigest: Globally, climate and environmental changes occurring more quickly than ever which ultimately threatening the agriculture, and exerting significant direct and indirect impact on production of crops. In future, cotton crop is likely to face multiple abiotic stresses including extreme and prolonged high temperatures. In the 2018-2019 season, the production of cotton was sharply declined due to heat which affected the crop yield year mainly due to rise in temperature. And, Government has declared cotton emergency in the country. Therefore, it is of urgent need that the effects of heat on cotton productivity are more comprehensively examined under field conditions through sustainable and eco-efficient approaches. To achieve these goals, the combined usage of beneficial microbes and screening of cotton varieties could be one of the ways to improve the growth and production with positive impacts on environment also. data.projectName: Electronic-Waste, a Problem or an Opportunity: Barriers and Challenges of E-Waste Recycling in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
E-waste includes the consumed electrical electronic products such as printers, faxes, computers, TVs, LCDs, laptops, and mobile phones etc. The amount of e-waste is increasing. E-waste contains much hazardous and harmful material which negatively affects the environment and human health. This includes lead, cadmium, and mercury etc. Electronic-waste contains very valuable and precious metals which include copper, silver, and gold. These metals can be gained through recycling process. As the volume of e-waste is increasing, it is increasing the important need for recycling of e-waste. The major challenges for e-waste management include e-waste recycling, awareness among the people to recycle their e-waste; government’s focus on recycling and reduction, ban, or restricted permission of importing e-waste from other countries. There is a need to redefine the recycling methods being used to handle e-waste in Pakistan. As well as it is relevant to investigate what factors may contribute to Pakistani residents’ intentions towards recycling. In this study we will explore barriers to the management and recycling of e-waste in Pakistan and will study the regulations and the conditions of infrastructure needed for this purpose.
A survey based research method will be used to conduct this proposed research. We will first conduct a thorough literature review to describe our research problem and to propose a conceptual research model for exploring the barriers towards electronic. A qualitative as well as quantitative research methodology will be sued in this research. Focused group discussion involving experts from the government, academia, and industry will be conducted. Researchers will also organize awareness seminars, workshops, and conferences regarding e-waste management locally

data.projectName: Use of dietary orange peel as an alternative to synthetic antioxidants and antibiotics in the feed of Labeo rohita
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: A rapid increase in human population since past few centuries has caused nutritional problems, particularly food security concerns, all over the world. Experts have suggested that an increase in production of cheapest, high proteinaceous food, like fish, would help to cope malnutrition and to ensure food security. In contrast, a sharp decline has been observed in recent decades in harvesting of fish from natural resources, which highlighted the need of aquaculture.  Aquaculture sector provides 47% of total global fish production and is expected to increase its contribution to 52% by the end of the year 2025. Among fish species of Pakistan, rohu is the most important fish species due to its high palatability and market value. However, the daily increase in environmental pollution is making this species vulnerable to infectious diseases and oxidative stress, ultimately affecting the growth and health of fish. Fish feed manufacturer use synthetic antioxidants and antibiotics to address health issues of fish. However, these synthetic antioxidants and antibiotics have side effects on fish as well. Therefore, the proposed project will evaluate the potential of orange peels, which contain active compounds with antioxidant and antibiotic properties, as an alternative to synthetic antibiotics and antioxidants for fish.

data.projectName: Nutritional interventions against pesticides poisoning: A Silent Threat to public health
data.projectDigest: The current research focused on the development of biopesticide for the control of insects and pests of two vegetables i.e. okra and brinjal. The current study will comprises of four different phases. In the first phase pesticide residues in okra and brinjal will be determined. Samples will be collected from different Tehsil of district Vehari. Based on the results of first phase an awareness seminar will be conducted for making people aware of this silent epidemic and about prevention from getting exposed to pesticides. These samples then will be examined by laboratory tests for checking health status of people and for pesticides residual levels in blood. In the third phase interventions to control or reduce pesticide residues will be carried out. Four different field experiments will be conducted. The yield of each vegetable will be recorded and will be compared with the yield recorded from the field experiment of recommended chemical spray field trials.  Estimation of total polyphenols, antioxidant activity and free radical scavenging activity of extracts from organically produced vegetables will be determined. Hence, the project is also expected to contribute in boosting the adoption of best farming technology in vegetable production in Punjab, Pakistan.

data.projectName: A Microchip-Based End-to-End IoT-Enabled Vaccine Quality Monitoring System
data.piUniversity: National University of Computer and Emerging Sciences, Islamabad
data.projectDigest: Vaccine based immunization is one of the most effective disease control methods. Pakistan is one of the few countries in the world where polio still affects children despite a decades-long vaccination campaign run by 260,000 polio workers. The Vaccines Logistics Manual (VLM) for the Expanded Program on Immunization (WHO-EPI) in Pakistan, recommends that most of the vaccines should be stored at temperatures between +2C and +8C until the time of their delivery. According to a recent meta-analysis published in the journal, vaccine that included data from more than 20 countries, a whopping 14% to 35% of vaccines are damaged due to temperature excursions beyond the recommended limits during transportation or storage. We propose a micro-chip-based end-to-end Internet-of-Things (IoT) enabled vaccine quality (temperature) monitoring system. The main features of the system include: (1) high accuracy, (2) low-cost - in volume production, (3) compactness, (4) suitability for extreme hot or cold climates, (5) enabling complete logging of vaccine temperature from manufacturing to storage and from transportation to child administration and (6) recording each vaccine delivery details (patient ID, vaccine vial ID,  time,  and geo-location). This solves all the cold chain and false data entry problems faced during the vaccination campaigns in Pakistan.
