data.projectName: The gravitational waves in magnetized- dense/radiative  plasma
data.piUniversity: Lahore College for Women University, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
The progress reported here is mainly through the magnetization energy of degenerate electron,  which is quite relevant to the modern technology such as metallic and semiconductor nano structures. It may be utilize in a new kinds of magnetic refrigerator,  next generation intense laser-solid, controlled fusion and density matter experiments etc. Here, we shall follow the quantum magneto-hydrodynamic (QMHD) model to analyze the impact of quantized magnetic pressure on the growth rate of RTI. Next, the electromagnetic radiation pressure, being another important factor to generate impressive variation in the plasma density, to introduce instabilities, boosting the rockets up in the space, to understand the stellar luminosity etc., we also intend to investigate the impact of radiation pressure, on the RTI of electron-ion plasma to show that the radiation in plasma medium may have significant signature on the formalism of structure of white dwarfs . 
Next, in  order to understand new star formation in astrophysical environment, we shall  follow kinetic model,  to formulate  new type of kinetic Jeans instability in the presence of intense electromagnetic waves and shall also study some consequent phenomena such nonlinear Landau damping and modulation instability of gravitational waves. Rotational Jeans instability will also be investigated.

data.projectName: Detoxification of cancer causing industrial waste by ornamental plants and beneficial microbes
data.projectDigest: Industries releasing a very high concentration of toxic heavy metals affecting human health globally. Due to rapid urbanization and industrialization, the disposal of industrial waste becomes problematic due to the presence of various toxic heavy metals. Paper industry is considered to be one of the major industries in Pakistan, producing large amounts of paper waste during the paper making process contain heavy metals along with many other impurities. This waste is dumped in the nearby land filled site or incinerated in open areas creating environmental pollution. So, there is a need to find a possible solution to utilize the industrial waste (paper industry) by using some eco friendly and cost effective techniques to overcome this pollution problem. This project is designed with the selection of ornamental plants that can tolerate considerably high concentration of metals. The investigation also includes identification and isolation of unknown indigenous bacteria in the paper waste and to find their potential for the successful bioremediation of this paper industry waste.

Paper industry is considered to be one of the major industries in Pakistan, producing large amounts of paper waste during the paper making process contain heavy metals along with many other impurities. This waste is dumped in the nearby land filled site or incinerated in open areas creating environmental pollution. So, there is a need to find a possible solution to utilize the industrial waste (paper industry) by using some eco friendly and cost effective techniques to overcome this pollution problem. This project is designed with the selection of ornamental plants that can tolerate considerably high concentration of metals. The investigation also includes identification and isolation of unknown indigenous bacteria in the paper waste and to find their potential for the successful bioremediation of this paper industry waste.

data.projectName: Production of recombinant Chicken Interferon as potentially cheap prophylactic antiviral agents
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Development of good immunity during first 7-8 days of a chicken is usually compromised due to presence of maternal antibodies. Therefore it is usual practice to vaccinate the chicks on day 7. The time it takes to produce effective titer is the peak time of vulnerability for the young chick, when maternal antibodies are on decline and the protective titer is yet not achieved. Treatment by interferon alpha or beta may provide a good protective cover against a wide range of virus in the time of vulnerability as mentioned above. The present study aims to produce recombinant chicken INF-alpha for this purpose.

data.projectName: Aptness of Biorational approaches for the control of stored grain beetles
data.projectDigest: Surveys of various public and private storage facilities of various districts of Punjab (Pakistan) will be conducted to check the level of infestation (Insect pests and molds) and collection of grain samples from each locality for isolation of insects to check the level of resistance against commonly used chemical insecticides and fumigants later, and dead insect specimens will also be collected and subjected to isolation of fungi/entomopathogenic fungi in stored grains. Collected insects will be reared in the laboratory up to F2 for future experiments. In first laboratory bioassay resistance level will be determined against conventional insecticides and fumigants which are used for stored products protection for different population collected during survey. Evaluation of ecofriendly approaches to control stored product pests by using newer chemistry insecticides, plant extras and modified atmosphere alone and in integration, and their evaluation at farmer field and public sector storage facilities. Lastly, the extension based seminars will be conducted on farm fields and literature will be distributed among the farmers to facilitate them for future storage instructions.

data.projectName: Shelf life extension of chilled poultry meat using novel packaging and storage technologies for local market
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: The availability of fresh, safe and hygienic chicken meat has been an issue lately. The market structure of poultry industry in Pakistan is predominantly based on wet market because of its fresh availability and penetration in the suburban areas, despite of the fact that it always remains prone to bacterial contamination by spoilage and pathogenic microorganism hence affecting overall shelf life and safety of chicken meat. The need of industry to develop the strategies to extend the shelf life and safety of fresh chicken meat hence remains viable in order to compete with wet market to maximise its retail and export potential. The storage and preservation methods could be employed and evaluated to serve the purpose. The application of organic acids at optimum levels in combination with novel packaging technologies including vacuum packing and modified atmosphere packaging is said to minimize the bacterial contamination. Super chilling of muscle is a new potential alternative for traditional freezing and chilling which can keep the product quality as fresh with minimal impact on either microbiological or sensory shelf life. Exploring its effect will be helpful in ensuring product safety throughout the distribution and retail. The project has been designed to exploit the potential of aforementioned interventions and their application to optimize the broiler meat safety along the production, processing and distribution channels with extended shelf life without compromising microbiological or sensory attributes.

data.projectName: Illuminating the Eyes of Industry 4.0: Design and Development of Robust Algorithms, Real-time Systems and Test-bed for Machine Vision
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest:
The industrial sector as we know it is facing its latest revolution. This revolution to the so-called Industry 4.0, is to be brought about by “digitalization”: a concept that involves using smart data gathering and information processing technologies to improve efficiency, sustainability, and productivity of the industrial sector. Machine vision, referred to as eyes of Industry 4.0, allows the computers to visualize, understand and analyze the surroundings. Since machine vision enables the generation of high-resolution multidimensional data that can be exploited to carry out effective improvements in the manufacturing processes in the Industries, it serves as a key technology in the development of automation systems in Industry 4.0. This however requires machine vision algorithms to be real-time, computationally efficient and robust; and produce reliable and high-quality data. 
In this context, this proposal seeks to develop advanced, robust and real-time machine vision algorithms and novel illumination techniques; design and develop machine vision test-bed accompanied with simulation set-up and front-end software; and train the work force in the area of machine vision, develop curriculum to train the industry professionals in the area of machine vision and provide support to the industry in effectively utilization of the eyes of Industry 4.0. curriculum.

data.projectName: Water Quality Assessment (District Muzaffarabad and Jhelum Valley, Azad Kashmir): Community Awareness and Development of Purification Technology
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest: According to World Health Organization (WHO) 2.1 million people are affected with contaminated water worldwide and sources of contamination could be natural or man-made.  In case of Pakistan, the situation is the worst and according to WHO and Word Bank reports 64 % urban and 84 % rural population is using contaminated water. According to these sources, the hospitals’ data shows that 40 % deaths in the country are due to polluted water. Keeping in mind the severity of the problem and country specific needs, the present project is designed to assess the drinking water quality of District Muzaffarabad and Jehlum valley, Azad kashmir. In addition to water analysis, the community awareness and development of water purification technologies will be focused. The proposed project will be completed with the help of relevant government departments such as Department of Local Government and Rural Development and Department of Public Health Engineering, Government of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad.

data.projectName: Micro-geographies of undernutrition: Analyzing spatial prevalence and hierarchies at household, community and district level in Punjab and Sindh
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Undernutrition is one of the important development challenges Pakistan is facing. To meet the SDG target of zero hunger and poverty reduction it is utmost important to empirically examine the prevalence of undernutrition at micro-geographic level (district level) in Pakistan. This project aims at understanding and analyzing the spatial prevalence of undernutrition (i.e., stunting, wasting, underweight and low birthweight) of children less than five years. It is important to know the hotspots of undernutrition prevalence in two of the most populated provinces namely; Punjab and Sindh of Pakistan. Furthermore, the study will also empirically examine the various levels (i.e., household, community, and districts) which affect the undernutrition. This kind of analyses helps in better understanding the level of intervention and targeting. Finally, the study will analyze the contribution of each factor in reducing the prevalence of undernutrition. This proposed study will be helpful in spatial planning at micro-level.

data.projectName: Impact of ICT interactive games of Urdu on students’ learning at primary level in Public sector of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: In the competitive age, along with quantitative, qualitative changes in education are prime concerns of policy makers. It has been cited by number of researches that ICT remove many obstacles in education system, i.e. physical and human. It can be easily noticed many software and ICT components have been efficiently used in English language. Notwithstanding, various stakeholders trying to build ICT related materials in Urdu language too, but these materials are not available in sufficient quantity. As a result, teachers and learners are not able to take leverages of ICT at maximum extent.  In Urdu medium, ICT material is available in negligible quantity as compare of others. ICT enabled distance education, to a great extent, can combat this problem. One of the important barriers is lack of trained teachers to exploit ICT proficiently. We believe that Integration of technology improves quality of teaching/learning. ICT related material needs an expertise, and should be developed through professionals of their field. If ICT material is accessible to teachers/learners, they will apply this in their teaching. In addition to this, in school syllabus, in each subject topics, which appeals most to technology needs to identified and should be recommended to deals with the help of technology.

data.projectName: Fish parasites: hazard identification, novel environmental monitoring and to develop efficient strategies for parasitic control in Aquaculture
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Aquaculture has been an important vector in the aquatic diseases outbreaks, transmission of parasites and global trade of live aquatic animals and their products. Bacteria, protozoans, monogenetic trematodes and crustaceans are the major disease causing pathogens that increase the level of uncertainty which farm managers have to contend with to develop the industry. In Pakistan there is not any information about these farm diseases and parasites.  Moreover, information regarding the parasite intensity, diversity and prevalence with respect to environment is also scar.  Thus, the proposal is aimed to enlist the diseases, identifying the causative parasites on genetic level and use of eDNA technology to cope with the parasitic issue.

data.projectName: Appraisement of health risk related to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in service station wastewater and potential of indigenous hydrocarbon degrading bacteria to neutralize PAHs from service stations
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: A number of chemical and petrochemical toxins are released by service stations. Various activities are being carried at service stations involved the removal of dirt, grease and oil using different detergents and de-greasing solvents. Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) presence in automobile service station wastewater has already been described. Animal and plant growth is adversely affected by wastewater containing oil contamination including phenols, petroleum hydrocarbons and PAHs which may cause mutagenesis and carcinogenesis in humans. Using the simple biological method of oil pollution control from service stations may save a huge volume of water and will ultimately save the aquatic life and environment.  The study will observe the effect of service station wastewater containing PAHs as contaminant on worker’s health, ground water quality and ultimately on fish as sample aquatic organism. The proposed study will also observe the efficiency of biodegradation, molecular identification of key indigenous bacteria, optimize isolation methods, optimize short term and long term preservation techniques and design a cost effective and less time consuming method of culturing these bacteria by using different approaches. The cultures will be modified and tested in the field that is automobile service stations.

data.projectName: Effectiveness of Learning through Play (LTP) in My Own Way Plus Cognitive Behavior Therapy (CBT): A Parent-Based Intervention for Depressed Mothers of children with an Intellectual Disability
data.projectDigest: High rates of intellectual disabilities (ID) in Pakistan, low literacy levels, high levels of depression and anxiety in mothers (as compared to fathers) in regards to having children with disabilities, and  absence of appropriate services and systems to support mothers of children with ID led to the conceiving of this project. This project aims at reducing maternal depression by developing positive parenting skills of mothers of children with intellectual disabilities in three larger cities of Pakistan (i.e Karachi, Lahore, and Rawalpindi). The intervention will integrate “Learning through Play in my own way” and “Cognitive Behaviour Therapy” to reach a marginalized population of Pakistan in order to build the capacities of mothers who are facing challenges, exclusion and issues related to managing their children with ID.  Through researching the lived experiences of these mothers and carrying out a strategic and well-tested intervention, it is likely that positive parenting will be enhanced, the mental health of both mother and child will improve and invariably, the inclusion of the disadvantaged into mainstream society.

data.projectName: Building and Deploying Chatbots for Teaching, University Websites and Industries: A Multidisciplinary Study
data.piUniversity: National University of Modern Languages, Islamabad (NUML)
data.projectDigest: Chatbots are like those call centre workers who never sleep round the clock without feeling tiredness and they serve industries without demanding any salaries or complaining. They are such memory masters who never forget any piece of information and they never behave rudely with their clients. They are equally capable to respond to any audio or text message. These user-friendly qualities of Chatbots necessitate their use in industry, academia and educational websites. Business Insider predicts that 85% of industries will build and deploy Chatbots for their customer care and to promote their businesses in 2020. Practically, one Chatbot will take 2 months to be built and deployed after the baseline survey, web analysis, FAQ’s analysis, interviews of callers and call attendants, complaints analysis etc. This hybrid research is multidisciplinary in nature; hence, basic and applied research factors correlate with each other in this project. This 3 years long project aims to provide Chatbot facilities for 6 Educational Tutor Chatbots, 6 University websites including HEC and 6 miscellaneous industries including the banking sector, foods, hotel waiter, health sector and real estate. Timeline for the completion of the project will be 3 years and the requested budget is 16,608,375 Pak rupees. As a sustainable project, this project will transform into a business Startup to generate revenue for the Pakistani economy and it will fulfil demands of industrial Chatbots. Simultaneously, Chatbot workshops and hands-on training will be given to other Pakistani university youths throughout Pakistan and this activity will create awareness among educational institutes and industries. The Principal investigator got consent of two academic and technological and one  industrial collaborator .

data.projectName: Synthesis and characterization of multi-functional magneto-electric nano particles
data.projectDigest:
A lot of research activities has been devoted to enhance ferroelectric and ferromagnetic properties through doping and through growth conditions to control the microstructure but little progress has been made so far. New strategy adopted for preparing multiferroic materials with superior properties is making composites of ferromagnetic and ferroelectric materials. In composites, each ferroic phase has their respective strong ferroic order that couple by strain mediation between intimately connected grains of different ferroic phases. Main advantage of ME composites is their large compositional variability. ME coupling in composites is external phenomenon and microstructure play important role in tailoring properties of these composites.
          In this project, we will prepare composites of ferromagnetic ferrites ((Ni, Zn, Co, Cu,) Fe2O4, (Sr, Ba)Fe12O19 and ferroelectric titanates (BaTiO3, PbTiO3) [10] or ferromagnetic ferrites and ferroelectric BFO [11, 12] with different compositions and synthetic strategies. Different pairs of ferroelectric and ferromagnetic materials with varying compositions will be selected for study and also their microstructure will be tailored and investigated to get materials with optimum ME properties.  The synthetic route we will adopt for synthesis of magnetoelectric composites is the WOWS sol-gel method.  WOWS sol-gel method [3] is one step one pot method and that is easy to handle.

data.projectName: Low cost Point-of-Care Hepatitis C diagnostic platform using Air Jet Manipulation of Droplets on Patterned Superhydrophobic Surface
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) is responsible for higher deaths compared to any other infectious diseases according to Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) report. Hepatitis C slowly causes liver damage without showing any symptoms until reaching a chronic stage of liver scarring, cancer or even death. Early diagnosis is critical for effective treatment. For accurate viral presence, a Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) is performed making copies of DNA and amplifying the signals for detection. Typical extraction and amplification for real-time PCR equipment costs around Rs. 6 million limiting its availability with our 63% of population in resource limited areas. In this project, we will design and develop an affordable, portable, point-of-care-diagnostic (PoC) system for HCV detection and quantification using PCR. A droplet microfluidic platform will pipette reagents, actuate droplets using miniature air jets on a novel superhydrophobic platform, provide thermal cycling, and detect fluorescence all in one easy to carry device. The fully automated device will cut 30% cost compared to market systems and achieve 4 times faster response. Lastly, BioTech Scientific International will help commercialize the device across Pakistan. The developed system will have tremendous potential for HCV as well as other disease diagnostics requiring similar protocols.

data.projectName: Framework for Prediction of Desert Locust Outbreaks in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The economy of Pakistan is based upon the agricultural products such as cotton, wheat, rice, sugar cane and other cash crops. There are several number of problems which have badly affected  the production of different crops but  recently, swarm of desert locust have badly affected to agricultural areas of Sindh. It is very difficult to predict the movement of locust because these insects move there direction very rapidly. The weather condition would be one of the dimension to grow locust such as rain, moisture, wind, humidity, temperature and others. Another dimension is to examine the soil condition where these insects fix their eggs, which is vulnerable situation which provides opportunity to re-develop locust production. The objective of this research is twofold. Discovery of the locust and prediction of locust movements. Since the movement of locust is very hard to predict due to the heterogynous weather variables. Method of this research comprises over four layers. Locust identification system will work on the top of layer which consists upon several components to recognize the locust and its possible shapes. GIS system has been designed to build the spatial and temporal objects. At the third layer GIS mapping operations to plot the heterogynous GIS and locust data. At the fourth layer performance evaluation will be done to improve the accuracy of proposed solution.

data.projectName: Lightweight nanocomposites of graphene and related 2D nanomaterials for electromagnetic waves absorption
data.projectDigest:
The excessive use of electronic equipment, in this technological era is causing radiation (electromagnetic in nature) pollution. These waves, being invisible electromagnetic pollution, not only disturb the normal operation of electronic devices but also adversely affect human health, by causing headache, sleep disturbance, respiratory problems, nausea and nervous excitation. Whereas, long-term exposure to EM radiations, without any safety measures, can lead to cancer, brain tumors and DNA damage. 
To address this issue, EM wave absorption is a technique in which EM wave energy is depleted and then converted into other forms of energy, which are not damaging like EM waves. This ensures that EM wave is not permeated or either reflected back through the material. 
This project is proposed to prepare nanomaterials that can absorb these electromagnetic waves. The focus of project will be to fabricate lightweight absorber nanomaterials, to keep in pace with the miniaturization trend of the electronic devices. Moreover, these nanomaterials would also find applications in defense sector.

data.projectName: An investigation of Molecular Determinants of the Quality of Life in Patients with Down Syndrome at National and International Levels.
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Down syndrome (DS), also known as non-Mendelian inheritance, is a genetic disorder which is caused by the presence of trisomy in Chromosome 21. DS is analyzed by chromosomal analysis and clinical symptoms. DS is accompanied with plethora of other pathological symptoms including congenital heart diseases, acute megakaryoblastic leukemia (AMKL), acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), testicular germ cell cancer, pyloric stenosis, duodenal atresia, imperforate anus, Meckel diverticulum, susceptibility to gingivitis and severe periodontal disease, autism and Alzheimer’s disease, etc. Like many other diseases, genomic profile of Pakistani patients is still missing for DS patients. Moreover, treatment of associated pathologies is hampered due to the unavailability of the molecular data in these cases specifically in developing countries like Pakistan. Gene identification is very crucial for prevention, improvements in diagnosis and treatment of associated problems with DS.  Moreover, comparison of molecular profiles of DS in different age groups can increase the quality of life by administering proper and mostly related treatments and care. Therefore, it is very important to consider the new technologies in the field of genomics such as microarrays and next generation sequencing (NGS) for holistic study of different age groups of patients with DS.

data.projectName: Identification of BCL-2 inhibitors via Ligand based NMR studies for the treatment of Cancer.
data.projectDigest: BCl-2 overexpression is associated with decreased apoptosis which finally lead to cancer. Since last few decades, BCL-2 has become a validated drug target for cancer treatment. Few drug candidates were approved by FDA, but after few years they have been banned due to adverse effects such as low platelet count and others. Therefore, there is an immense need to find new BCL-2 inhibitors that show better efficacy and less adverse effects. The current project is designed to use computational tools, biochemical, and biophysical techniques that will help to identify new BCL-2 inhibitors and to have insight about their mechanism of action. The project will be initiated by in silico screening of various synthetic and natural ligands for their binding with amino acid residues of BCL-2 proteins. Selected ligand with better docking score and critical interactions with BCL-2 amino acid residues will be proceeded for in-vitro anti-cancer activity against various cell lines. Ligands with significant activity in in vitro assays will be analyzed for their epitope binding using STD-NMR. This will lead to the identification of new lead molecules that can be proceeded for pre-clinical and clinical studies.

Plant viruses (begomoviruses) have the capability to survive in alternate hosts especially in weeds, ornamental, herbaceous and woody plants. data.projectName: THE INVESTIGATION OF LANGUAGE PLANNING POLICIES; FORMULATION, IMPLEMENTION AND PUBLIC DEMAND OF MULTILINGUAL COUNTRY, PAKISTAN SINCE 1947-2020
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: This proposal aims to investigate and provide a definite solution to the problems of language planning policies and its impacts on the society. This research work will lead to broaden out the horizons of the issue and give new insights and trends thus bridging the gaps in language formulation policies in this domain. In proposed study the researcher will visit the various universities of Provinces and GB to check the standards and requirements of the teachers and students about the national language, official language and the language of instruction in education sector, and also take interviews from the public of four provinces and GB. The data will be collected to analyze the corporate sector language demands for socio-economic development. This project will thoroughly examine the language needs both at the national and international level. Adding to it, a scrutiny will be carried out to find out national and international standards of education with respect to the medium of instruction at different educational levels and to specify that which language among, viz. Chinese, English and Pakistani native languages, will fulfill the demands at national level in upcoming decades. In order to improve overall quality of teaching and learning in universities as well as to develop policies regarding language planning accordingly this research will be significant.

data.projectName: Synthesis and Application of Biochemical Material for Bioremediation of Multi-Metals Contaminated Soil
data.projectDigest: The objectives of this study to synthesis and characterization of biochemical material (BCM) using PGPB-sodium alginate-BC composite, incubation of BCM to soil without and with plants (Brassica, Maize) for bio-/phyto-remediation of multi-metals contaminated soil. PGPB will be assessed for multi-metal [Cd(II), Pb(II) and As(III)] tolerance assay, PGP activities, metal resistance genes. BC will be prepared through pyrolysis of powdered rice husk in a furnace at 300, 500 and 700 °C. The efficient PGPB will be immobilized on the BC in the presence of SA to synthesis BCM3, BCM5, BCM7 along with BSA (PGPB+SA) and B (PGPB without SA and BC) and characterized on FTIR, SEM-EDS and XRD. These treatments will be incubated without and with plants for 60 days in a completely randomized design. Soil will be drawn after (1, 10, 20, 40, 60 days) and processed for physico-chemical properties, different fractions of heavy metals, soil microbial activities and microbial communities in the bulk and the rhizosphere soils. Plant growth, biomass, physiology, metal contents, bioconcentration and translocation factors will be determined. The proposed project would synthesize novel BCM, which could be utilized by agriculture based industry to improve soil/plant health, and Government agencies to make a policy to achieve UN-SDGs.

data.projectName: Integrated wastewater treatment of pulp and paper industry and electricity generation in a microbial fuel cell
data.projectDigest: Pulp and paper is a water and energy intensive industry and generate a huge amount of wastewater. Due to scarcity of water and energy resources, there is a need to develop sustainable methods for wastewater treatment. The objective of the proposed research is to generate electricity while treating the wastewater in a microbial fuel cell and use the treated water back in the pulp and paper industry for making some product. In this method, microbes play the role of a biocatalyst and generate a flow of electrons by oxidizing the organic compounds in the wastewater. To conduct this research, wastewater sample will be collected from different local pulp and paper industries and shall be characterized for its various pollutants as well as the microbial community. The wastewater will be treated in MFC in batch mode and electrical current generation under constant voltage conditions shall be examined. The treated water shall be used to prepare some paper products and subsequently, their quality will be compared with the originally produced products. As pulp and paper industry is one of the largest business in Pakistan, therefore, this research is expected to generate a good sustainable impact on the local industry.

data.projectName: Synthesis, Characterization, Biological and Pharmacological screening of newly synthesized analogues of acetylsalicylic acid.
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Emerging antibiotic resistant development by the organisms against antibiotics is a current treatment protocol dilemma toward treating the infections. Various studies have shown that the selection of antibiotic plays an important role along with the variety of anti-inflammatory drugs used. As these NSAIDs along with the antibiotics has been given to the patient from the longer period of time. Some NSAIDs has also shown to possess the antibacterial response along with their anti-inflammatory effects.
This has led the researchers to use the non-antibiotic approach towards the treatment of infection caused by the resistant organisms. In this project, our aim is to designing via In-silico studies through molecular docking prior to synthesizing the analogues of Aspirin another NSAID which is most commonly used, their characterization and antimicrobial activities (both gram-negative and gram-positive organisms, along with some resistant species), antifungal activities, anti-mycobacterial activities will be studied.  Pharmacological profiling will be achieved by determining the change in Analgesic and Anti-inflammatory response of the newly synthesized analogues of aspirin in comparison to the parent molecule along with some other standard analgesic and anti-inflammatory drugs. 
In this way, new drug molecule will be synthesized having both antibacterial and analgesic activity with lesser side effects.

data.projectName: New Formulation of seismic action for Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Building Code of Pakistan (2007) has defined the seismic action for Pakistan in terms one parameter know as peak ground acceleration (PGA) and it divides  Pakistan  into four zones based on magnitude of PGA. The first drawback of definition of these broad PGA range is the under or over estimation of the effects of the seismic forces due to the choice of PGA values range given for the zone (e.g., 0.08-0.16 g for zone 2A). The other drawback the Building Code of Pakistan suffers from is the impact of earthquake magnitude on spectral shape of response spectrum that cannot be considered for low to medium hazard regions.
These drawbacks can be overcome by the defining uniform hazard spectrum at dense grids rather than peak ground acceleration values at coarse grids followed in the Building Code of Pakistan. The recent development in the Italian Building Code (Technical Regulations for Constructions of 2008, NTC08) has addressed these issues. In the work, seismic action for Pakistan will be formulated as in Italian Code. This outcome of this work will serve important document for revision of seismic action for Building Code Pakistan (2007).

data.projectName: Screening of Indigenous Goat Breeds of Azad Kashmir towards Trichostrongylide Nematode Species Natural and experimental  Infection
data.projectDigest: Goats are multi use animals. Gastrointestinal nematodes (GINs), affect goat welfare and health. To control GINs veterinarians and farmers mainly rely on anthelmintics. Due to certain reasons GINs establish resistance against anthelmintics. Finding alternate way to control GINs is important job that is acceptable for both farmers and veterinarians. In this respects exploring animals breeds genetic potential against infection caused by GINs is an alternate way and promotion of resistant breeds is a positive step in breed improvement programs. There are some reports presented from some parts of the world depicted that different breeds of goats have shown different response to GINs towards natural and induced infection with Trichostrongylid nematodes particularly H. contortus. In Pakistan some studies conducted on this topic showing that teddy goats showing resistance comparatively to other breeds. However, there is no such type of investigation has been conducted from selected study area. Firstly goat breeds of AJK will be screened through standard parasitological procedure for natural infection by evaluation of hematological, parasitological and biochemical parameters. Secondly goats will be screened for their response to induced infection with Trichostrongylid nematode with particular reference to H. contortus under control confinement. Keeping in view of significance of genetic potential of animals against diseases present study has been proposed to screen indigenous goat breeds of AJK towards Trichostrongylid nematode natural and experimental infection with particular reference to H. contortus.

data.projectName: Assessment of cytochrome P450 3A4 and related genes polymorphisms in the clinical efficacy and adverse effects of Cytarabine in the treatment of acute lymphoblastic/myeloid leukemia
data.projectDigest: The Interpatient variability in sensitivity to cytarabine (ara-C) during acute lymphoid/myeloid leukemia (ALL/AML) treatment results in variation in clinical response as well as its toxicity (i.e. gastrointestinal ulceration, mucoitis, myelosuppression, hepatotoxicity; neurologic toxicity, conjunctivitis). The genetic variants including single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and insertion deletion events in genes responsible for metabolism, transport and activation of ara-C, play significant role in modifying drug response and thus eventually cause alteration in the clinical potency and adverse effects in different ethnic groups patients. We intend to develop an ara-C combinatorial SNP-score using the most promising SNPs predictive of clinical response/adverse effects of ara-C in ALL/AML patients. Findings of this study can lead to individualized chemotherapy based on genetic profiling, which may help optimize ara-C dosing, leading to improvements in clinical outcome and reduced toxicity. Therefore, our SNP predictive score, once validated, in this and other cohorts, holds promise for personalizing ara-C chemotherapy.

data.projectName: The multilingual Named Entity Recognition (MNER) for National Languages of Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
A comprehensive named entity recognition is an ultimate aim of this research project in which the system is built to recognize various named entities for national languages of Pakistan. The languages under study include Urdu, Sindhi, Punjabi, Pashto, Balochi, Marwari, Kashmiri and others. The named entity recognition will provide an insight in natural language processing of local languages and uplift the processing of local languages at the level of other languages such as English and french. 
The named entity recognition system will make computers intelligent so that the computers can understand national and regional languages of Pakistan.

data.projectDigest:
Micronutrients intake is parallel to the term ‘nutrition security’ and both can be considered the two sides of the same coin. This concept evolved in mid 1990s when efforts were started to add nutritional features in the concept of food security. Generally the cross sectional studies analyzed the economic push and pull factors for energy intake and the micronutrients could not take attention among researchers especially under escalating food prices (food inflation) in the developing countries like Pakistan.
This study aims to:  
1)	Determine the economic factors affecting the micronutrient intake among the sampled population from the selected districts of Punjab, Pakistan.
2)	Calculate the adequacy level of energy and nutrient intakes for different ages of children and women in the selected sample of population.
3)	Analyze the response of real income (escalated food prices) to consumption of animal source food (meat and dairy intake) stratified through wealth and residency (rural, semi urban, arid and semi-arid districts of Punjab, Pakistan).
4)	 Investigate the disparities in intakes
5)	Explore the relationships between food prices and nutritional intakes.
6)	Assess the policy needs to address the issue of malnutrition at national level.
The absence of comprehensive surveys on socio-economic characteristics, micronutrient intakes and nutrition outcomes remained a challenge for studying the nexus among micronutrients intakes and economic and health status of population in many developing countries like Pakistan. This study will fill the research gap in the relevant paradigm and can pursue policy suggestions at provincial and national level to make the platform convenient for addressing the issue of malnutrition especially among the poor group of people in selected sites

data.projectName: Therapeutic evaluation of Potential Natural Phyto-Bioactive Compounds against Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus is a metabolic disorder marked by chronic hyperglycemia and insulin resistance stemming from progressive degeneration of pancreatic ?-cells and insufficient production of insulin. Its etiology involves a complex interplay of both genetic and environmental factors. Its global prevalence has increased alarmingly with 1 of every 11 adult suffering with T2DM. Current treatment options for T2DM are accompanied by a wide range of nonspecific effects resulting in associated comorbidities. Indigenous herbs of Pakistan have significant ethno-botanical properties but few have being explored for bioactive lead compounds. The prime objective of the proposed project is to identify novel bioactive compounds to be used as drug moieties for the formulation of anti-diabetic drugs. Various bioinformatics’ tools will be used for screening various phytochemicals for drug like properties. The selected drug moieties will be subjected to in vitro and in vivo analysis and the experimental outcomes will be compared with standard US FDA approved drugs such as Metformin as we are striving to generate a product with maximised therapeutic potential and minimal side effects. It is expected that these efforts would elucidate drugs that are natural and cost-effective remedies not only for diabetes but also for its associated comorbidities.

data.projectName: :   Human Identification Through Covariate Invariant Gait Recognition
data.projectDigest:
Gait is an important biometric trait for surveillance and forensic applications, which can be used to identify individuals at a large distance through CCTV cameras. However, it is very difficult to develop robust automated gait recognition systems, since gait may be affected by many covariate factors such as clothing, walking surface, walking speed, camera view angle, etc. 
Gait recognition is of great importance in the fields of surveillance and forensics to identify human beings since gait is a unique biometric feature that can be perceived efficiently at a distance. The application will address the effects of inherent intra-class variations caused by covariate factors such as clothing, carrying conditions, and view angle that adversely affect the recognition performance. A developing country like Pakistan requires such kind of research area to be promoted as there is a need to improve the law and order situation. Eventually, this application can be used by users to verify humans using surveillance cameras. Furthermore, it can be used to restrict access to secure sites including buildings and computer networks as well as secure the nation’s borders.

data.projectName: Poverty and Development Prediction using Satellite Imagery and Machine Learning
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: The elimination of poverty worldwide is the first of 17 United Nations Sustainable Development Goals for the year 2030. This project aims to track progress towards this goal by employing machine learning techniques on satellite imagery to map poverty impoverished and developed areas in Pakistan, and proving this approach to be a feasible alternative. The final project output will be heat maps indicating poverty and development levels over the years in Pakistan. These heat maps can be overlaid on digital maps for easy visualization. Techniques from computer vision and machine learning will be employed to extract indicators such as geographical and man-made structural features from high-resolution satellite imagery. For a developing country like Pakistan, this project is useful because the approach uses publicly available data and is a scalable and inexpensive alternative to traditional surveys. The results from the project will aid policy makers and NGOs to distribute their funds to areas that are most deserving, and enact and assess policies more effectively.

data.projectName: Implementation of Drug and Poison Information Services and Evaluation its  impact on Patient safety at Dow University Hospital (Tertiary care Hospital), Karachi, Pakistan.
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
In current era of Pakistan, Drug and poison information services(DPIC) has been recognized as a fundamental component of health  care system to prevent from any side effect, adverse effect , drug-drug interactions and ensure patient safety.  Dow University of Health Sciences (1000 beds)   is one of the tertiary care hospital delivers high standard of preventive , treatable, curable and diagnostic health care services  since 2003. 

 At Dow hospital, department of pharmacy provides true hospital pharmacy practice. Hospital has own Pharmacy and therapeutic committee, highly skilled pharmacist whose performing ambulatory, inpatient, emergency and clinical pharmacy services along with other support service to health care staff.  The concept of “Point of care Pharmacy Services”  run by clinical Pharmacist while Sterile and non-sterile compounding services is one of major component of Pharmacy department.  All of these medication management services play an important role on clinical outcome of patient.
Currently Hospital has no value added service of DPIC hence goal of current study is to establish drug and poison information center in a public sector tertiary care hospital to enhance patient safety and reduce the medication error.
Impact of Pre and Post applied services will be analyzed to compare the outcomes of services in patient safety.

data.projectName: Molecular characterization of high yielding wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) genotypes for drought tolerance
data.projectDigest: For this research project, morpho-physiological evaluation of high yielding wheat genotypes of Punjab province will be done at experimental area, Plant Breeding and Genetics for two years. After the field evaluation, the genotypes with better drought tolerance will be further studied, and identification of drought responsive genes and their relative expression analysis will be carried out using qRT-PCR. At present, due to lack of detailed genetic information regarding the drought tolerance status of our existing wheat genotypes, there has not been a significant advance in the yield in drought sensitive areas. The findings from this study will provide material foundation for the wheat breeding program of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Biochemical mechanisms of heat tolerance in thermostable wheat
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Wheat is a major staple food in many countries of the world and its demand is increasing day by day due to rapidly increasing population and decreasing land area available for agriculture.  An increase in temperature at the time of grain filling above optimum level significantly affects wheat yield. The major effect of high temperature after anthesis in wheat is the reduction in grain size. This is alarming as currently we do not have suitable genotypes for cultivation at high temperature (varieties capable of cultivation above 25oC). Extensive efforts have been employed to understand the molecular and physiological basis of heat tolerance in wheat. However, little is known about the complex biochemistry behind heat tolerance. It is well understood that increase in temperature adversely affects starch biosynthesis which constitutes more than 70% of wheat grain dry matter. This reduction in starch biosynthesis is directly associated with decreased activities of enzymes involved in starch biosynthesis. Furthermore, recent work suggests that along with enzymes activities, their post-translational modifications particularly protein-protein interactions and protein phosphorylation are also affected. At higher temperature protein complexes disassociate leading to an overall reduction in starch biosynthesis system efficiency. These findings suggest that post-translational modifications are important contributor in yield reduction at elevated temperature. Therefore, it is required to understand how these post-translational modifications are affected at higher temperature and how these protein complexes can be stabilized to avoid yield losses. The overall goal of this study will be to develop transgenic wheat expressing thermostable SSI protein.

data.projectName: Improvement of Sorghum (Sorghum bicolor) for Grain and Forage Yield  and Quality Traits under the Agro-climatic Conditions of Southern Punjab
data.projectDigest: Current studies have been proposed for the improvement of sorghum crop. Sorghum is grown as forage and grain crop in Pakistan. In rainfed and hilly areas of Dera Ghazi Khan and in adjacent areas of Blochistan, sorghum is consumed as animal forage and as roti for a large human population. Several local varieties or land races are grown since decades and favorite to the farmers. These genotypes have not been characterized and documented for their agronomic and end use quality traits. Proposed project will enhance the capability of laboratory and scientific work at newly established Ghazi University Dera Ghazi Khan.  Sorghum land races found in DG Khan Division will be explored for the native traits. New germplasm will be evaluated for roti preparation.Researchers and farmers will be the end users of the output / product.

data.projectName: Development of Drought Resistant Potato by Transgenic Approach
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest: Potato crop is cultivated worldwide with high rank global economic value. Potato is the major staple and the world 4th largest food after rice, wheat and corn having significant primal substantial for starch processing, source of animal fodder, potato vines and active ingredients in its germplasm. Potato is grown over 125 countries except Antarctica and more than 1 billion people use it as food across the world. The global warming is serious threat to agricultural crops and potato is the most susceptible to drought. Major production lost were recorded in USA and Russia with 30 % decrease due to water shortage and its yield is estimated to decrease 18 – 32 % during 2040 – 2069. In South Asia, Pakistan is severely facing drought due to global warming and political issues with India on water. Potato production in Pakistan is also suffering losses due to drought. The genetic engineering offers the key opportunity to raise the food production efficiency by avoiding losses due to disease and pests with novel desirable characteristics. Keeping in view of the threat of global warming, a project has been designed to genetically engineer potato with drought tolerant character to face future water shortage issues of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Design and Synthesis of HCV Ns3 Protease Inhibitors
data.projectDigest: Single Stranded RNA Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) is responsible for liver disorders and shares considerable portion in worldwide infection. HCV has seven genotypes that are prevalent in different regions of the globe. Pakistani population is mainly infected by genotype 3a of the virus. HCV genome encodes polyprotein that is then cleaved to independently functioning structural and non-structural proteins which enable the virus to spread its infection in host.  The structural and non-structural proteins of HCV can serve as potential target for designing anti-HCV therapies. The idea behind anti-HCV therapies is to halt the cleavage of the polyprotein and subsequently stop infection in the host. Among various potential drug targets in HCV, NS3 protease, being the major partner in HCV polyprotein cleavage, is good candidate for developing drugs against HCV. By inhibiting NS3 protease, polyprotein will not be converted into independent proteins to function independently so the infection would be stopped. So far number of drugs have been marketed to cure HCV infection, but they have not been very successful owing to rapid mutation rate of the virus and cross-genotypic resistance. FDA approved interferon-? followed by ribavirin met the same fate by not showing substantial sustained virology response. Introduction of direct acting antivirals (DAAs) has shown improved efficacy and envisaged to be further investigated and developed to improve affectivity of the anti-HCV drugs.  The aim of the current study is to find potent drugs against Pakistani prevalent HCV genotype (3a) by employing computer aided drug designing methods, synthetic pathways and experimental studies.

data.projectName: Design of a teledermatology system for classifying multiple skin lesions using a smartphone and cloud platform
data.projectDigest: Skin cancer is one of the most fatal diseases in humans, which is increasing on a daily basis affecting an estimated 1.9 billion people worldwide. Timely screening of the most destructive types of skin diseases such as melanoma can save human lives. Pakistan is a densely populated country with estimated residents of around 217 million, but unfortunately, there is no central database to record the statistical information on the incidence of different kinds of skin cancers in the country which complicates the situation further for researchers in this field. Another major issue is limited access to dermatology care due to a shortage of dermatologists, causing long wait times and leading patients to seek dermatologic care from general practitioners. This project will use advanced machine learning algorithms, smartphones and cloud platforms which will open another promising solution of broadening the availability of dermatologists. This project will also provide a centralized database to store the record of the patients having different types of skin cancer along with diagnostic results generated by the proposed teledermatology system. These recorded statistics will play a vital role to take preventive actions by the government against different kinds of skin diseases based on geographic and demographic data.

data.projectName: Requirements Patterns for Distributed Scrum
data.projectDigest: This research focuses on identifying the challenges practitioners face, while defining and managing requirements while using agile practices in offshore software development.  We will start the research by identifying challenges in each requirement engineering processes such as elicitation, analysis, documentation and validation.  We will then identify patterns from literature and semi-structure interviews that will help in overcome these challenges. Based on our findings we will design a pattern catalogue for agile offshore development. We will verify and validate our catalogue by reflection workshop. This catalogue will aid practitioners in their requirement engineering process for their offshore projects.

data.projectName: Feasibility Assessment and Prototype Model of Low-cost Housing for Urban Areas of Pakistan
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Low cost housing refer to ensuring affordable houses that can be borne by a family with low-to-medium household income. Primarily low cost housing projects have three major aspects i.e. financial, technical and execution management aspects. While the financial side is majorly an area of responsibility of the government and financial institutions, significant amount of cost effectiveness can be ensured by innovating the technical methods adopted for such construction as well as through proper and swift execution of the projects. This research mainly focuses on the latter two aspects and aims to conduct the feasibility assessment and constructing prototype low-cost house suitable for low to medium income families in urban areas of Pakistan. Extensive simulation based assessment over life cycle of the house using information modeling, Virtual Reality and life cycle cost assessment will be performed for various technical and management aspects to propose and build prototype house.

data.projectName: Investigations on the interactive functionality of cytokinin and strigolactone in controlling seed abortion
data.projectDigest: With the help of using model plant Arabidopsis thaliana, the proposed research will provide information in understanding genetic control of seed development in crop plants to avoid seed loss due to any defect caused by gene interaction at cellular level through regulation of cell cycle. This study will also help in exploring integrated plant internal signals known as phytohormones with genetic and cellular mechanisms in controlling seed abortion during seed development. The ultimate future goal of this proposed project is to modulate crop plants to increase their yield by dissecting genetic and hormonal interaction at cell cycle level during seed development.

data.projectName: Out-of-Plane Strengthening of Un-Reinforced Masonry Structures Using Engineered Cementitious Composite (ECC)
data.projectDigest: Brick masonry buildings are the most abundant buildings throughout the world. People in Pakistan prefer brick masonry residences because of readily available materials, expertise of the local masons and bearable cost of construction. On the other hand, Pakistan is located in a region of high seismicity with foreseeable earthquake recurrence in the future. Earthquakes in Pakistan have manifested the inherent weakness of masonry buildings against lateral forces with an unacceptable loss of life. Moreover, reconstruction of damaged buildings in earthquakes pose a daunting challenge to our national economy. With development of new materials, such as Engineered Cementitious Composites (ECC), engineers can foresee an opportunity to improve the behavior of masonry buildings by providing them with requisite strength and ability to deform in order to reduce the probability of loss of human life. It also provides an opportunity to the engineering community to salvage buildings that would conventionally warrant reconstruction. However, the industrial adoption of this technique requires an extensive study for development of design and construction standards. This study focuses on development of techniques for efficient adoption of ECC as a material for construction of new masonry buildings as well as strengthening of the weak ones.

data.projectName: Impact of Nutritional supplements: analysis of anthropometric measurements and biochemical data among school going children aged 5-10 years in a peri-urban community of Islamabad
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan is facing the problem of poverty and under nutrition of children at a big scale. There is also problem of less education and lack of awareness regarding healthy eating and healthy life style. This under nutrition has resulted in children with decreased height and weight , effecting their physical and mental health. It causes diseases and illness, which again adds to low productivity and economic loss to the community and the country.
Here we propose to intervene nutritional status of our children in less privileged community, so that their physical growth continues with improved cognitive and intellectual health. The purpose of our study is to intervene with basic food supplementation which are affordable and easily accessible to the general population at any stage in time. The rationale of our study is to try to overcome the dilemma of malnutrition and stunting and to improve the intellectual development with the results of improved efficiency and human capital development.

data.projectName: Structure based inhibitor design for renal lithiasis
data.projectDigest: Renal diseases are a global health issue and their prevalence is high in South Asia. In countries like Pakistan roughly 15-20% of the population is some how affected by this disease at some stage of their life. Among the renal diseases kidney stone is the most common. The reasons can be manyfold  but no systematic study has ever been conducted in Pakistan to asses the reason. This research proposal aims at understanding the kidney stone formation through a structure based understanding of the phenomenon of stone formation. For this purpose an extensive survey of the composition of urinary and liver stones will be conducted using X-rays diffraction analysis. When X-rays beam is allowed to fall on the crystalline or powder samples, they scatter the beam in a characteristic way whose analysis can reveal the structure and composition of the material . data.projectName: Detection of M. bovis induced mortality in calves and anitbacterial susceptibility testing of Cholistani herbs along with vaccine discovery
data.projectDigest: Dairy sector of Pakistan is increasing day by day rapidly, approximately 8.42 million human populations are involved in rearing dairy animals particularly buffaloes and cattle. Pakistan is ranked at number fourth on the basis of total milk (57.772 million tons) production in the world with an estimated head of 40.0 million buffalo and 47.8 million cattle directly related to milk. The bovine respiratory disease caused by Mycoplasma bovis is major threat and prominent health issue of bovine sucklers as well as adult animals. The disease is multifactorial and results by the interactions of infectious agents and different predisposing factors including stress, host defense and environment. The expression of interferon, tumor necrosis factor and interleukin immunohistochemically in lungs are important tools for the early disease diagnosis. Antibiotic therapy induces adverse impacts on the public health in terms of drugs residues in milk and meat. Whereas, medicinal plants are the best alternative for antibiotic treatments, which are widely used against different bacterial and viral infections throughout the world. Exploration, validation and antimicrobial testing of local Cholistani plants/herbs and development of vaccine can be valuable and useful tools to control infectious agent to uplift the economy of the dairy farmers and the country.

data.projectName: Screening of different Guava (Psidium guajava L.) Genotypes for High Density Plantation (A paradigm shift) and against Salinity Tolerance for its adaptation to Saline environments
data.projectDigest: Guava is an important fruit crop in tropical and subtropical areas due to the hardy nature of its tree and highly productive even in marginal lands. But, recently, this crop has showing a paradigm shift in production system, from subsistence farming to commercial production. At this time, there is a worldwide trend to plant fruit trees at high density to control tree size and maintain desired architecture is a modern method of fruit cultivation with dwarf plant and modified canopy. Secondly, soil salinity is a global problem which is hampering crop yields. Globally, almost 30% of irrigated land is affected by salinity, and in Pakistan, approximately 66,700 hectares of land are affected by salinization. Global crop production is limited by the effects of salinization, which results in insufficient water and nutrients absorption by plants and ion toxicity. Luckily, Pakistan is gifted with multi-climatic environmental conditions and guava is also successful well in different parts of the country and holds major position among fruit crops in Pakistan after Citrus, mango and Date palm. Despite being the 4th largest guava producer, no major scientific research has been carried out here on guava cultivars selection for high density plantation and saline environment. Altogether, guava is highly economic crop for farmers and during last few years guava farmers are shifting from conventional system to high density plantation (2200 plants/ha.). More specific, the core objective of this proposal is to screen out guava genotypes suitable for high density plantation with dwarf characteristics and potential of indigenous guava cultivars for salt tolerance.

data.projectName: Genetic profiling of Drug metabolizing enzyme, cytochrome p450 2C19 (cyp2C19) in normal population and cardiovascular patients
data.projectDigest:
Pharmacogenomics the use of genetic biomarkers to predict an individual’s response to drug treatment has grown alongside our understanding of the human genome. However, understanding the role of genetic variation in drug response has shifted this focus to the individual patient and their predicted response. At present a number of diseases emerging and improper treatment causes number of complications with the parent disease. Therefore a great need to diagnose disease on the genetic basis and personalized drug therapy should be recommended for patients.
Cardiovascular drugs are a highly prescribed group of compounds with broad function. These drugs are activated or metabolized by key drug metabolizing enzyme (DME) cytochrome p450 2C19 (CYP2C19), its genes are strong candidates for pharmacogenetic study. Here, I will explore the development of modern pharmacogenetic bases from a historical perspective and define the important components of a pharmacogenetic study. This will provide context and background relevant to the chief aim of the proposed research, the identification and characterization of pharmacogenetic biomarkers in DME involved in cardiovascular drug treatment and in controls.
the purpose of the study to investigate genotype/phenotype of a person with respect to specific genetic variantions, and such characterization will be highly beneficial in individualizing drug therapy of the patients so as to minimize the resistance, toxicity as well as sub therapeutic levels.

data.projectName: Electrochemical and spectrometric estimation of Iodine in biological sample of hyper and Hypothyroidism Patients in district Bannu
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan especially the region Khyber Pukhtunkhwa is one of the iodine deficient region of the subcontinent and about 70 percent of its population is at risk of iodine deficiency. The number of hypothyroid patient increases day by day in Pakistan and specifically in Khyber Pukhtunkhwa. The most important medical tests for patient of Hyper or hypothyroidism are T3, T4, and TSH, which is related to thyroxin, i.e. thyroid hormones. 
Iodine is an essential component of thyroid hormone. Thyroid gland absorbs iodine from foods stuff and combines it with amino acid of thymoglobulin to prepare two thyroid hormone, triiodothyronine (T3)  and thyroxin (T4).  Thus thyroid  gland  play an important role in regulation of human body metabolism. T3 and T4 are partially composed of iodine i.e, there are three iodine atoms in T3 while T4 contains four iodine atoms. 
Therefore, the estimation of iodide ions in human urine samples and blood serum are utmost important and have direct relation with patient suffering from hyper and hypothyroidism. The project in hand is an effort for designing a simple, sensitive and cost effective biosensor for determination of iodide ion in urine and human blood serum.

data.projectName: Interplay of immunological pathways of HCV induced OLP in a subgroup of Pakistani population
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Oral lichen planus, autoimmune non-infective condition involving oral mucosa, is believed to have unknown etiology. Several patients of OLP are reported to be HCV+ve during routine diagnostic protocol for OLP. Numerous studies have been conducted to check the role of HCV in the pathophysiology of OLP. 
Various inflammatory cytokines play important part in both. Biomarkers involved in immune modulation are the main players seen in these patients reflecting immune deregulation. A genetic predisposition to cytokines has been reported and imbalance proposed to be associated with susceptibility, clinical outcomes and treatment responses.
We aim to identify the potential communal biomarkers of HCV and OLP in our population. We intend to correlate and find the altered connection of HCV biomarkers in triggering OLP. Lastly we would check the possible genetic polymorphisms with altered expression in relevance to HCV associated with OLP.
This cross-sectional study would include 200 study subjects. Whole blood and unstimulated saliva samples would be collected for localized and generalized protein expression of respective biomarkers (IL-2, IL-4, IFN-?, NS5A, OPN and Neopterin) by ELISA. Tissue samples would be analyzed by Immunohistochemistry for syndecan-1 and periostin. Reported polymorphisms would be identified by DNA sequencing of IL-2, IL-4, IFN-?, and OPN genes.

data.projectName: The Reuse of Marble Waste Fine Particles for Drinking and Wastewater Treatment
data.projectDigest:
The marble industries are categorized as the most eco-unfriendly industries. However, the literature studies suggest that the fine particles (as pollutants) of marble wastes obtained from the crushing and processing of large stone consist of many valuable metal oxides. These metal oxides include CaO, MgO, SiO2, Al2O3, Fe2O3, Na2O, TiO2 and P2O5 etc. Previously, the metal oxides nanoparticles attained great importance due to its large surface areas and high catalytic efficiencies. The metal oxides TiO2, MgO, SiO2, Al2O3, Fe2O3, are mostly prepared with expansive procedures and are used for their photocatalytic applictions. Instead of collecting these metal oxides for various industrial and commercial applications, they are added directly to surrounding as pollutants. Meanwhile, District Buner KP, Pakistan is a minerals rich area, and well known for mining of marble stones. Approximately, more than 600 marble factories are functional here. 
Reutilization of the industrial, agricultural wastes and by-products has utmost importance for the sustainable growth of society. The innovative objective of the proposed study is separation and collection of these fine particles from District Buner. Elemental quantifications and characterizations of the collected samples using various techniques such as XRD, SEM/EDX, BET, UV-Vis DRS, and pHPZC analyses. Furthermore, green modification of these fine particles with activated carbon (AC), obtained from locally available biomass such as Pine cone, Almond and Apricot shell etc. The utmost priority would be given to monitoring underground and surface water of this specific area. Applications of these modified fine particles for drinking and wastewater treatments technology.

data.projectName: PURIFICATION OF RAW BIOGAS, DEHYDRATION OF DIGESTER EFFLUENT AND IMPACT OF BIOGAS PLANT SLURRY ON WHEAT CROP
data.projectDigest:
Research studies show that biogas is a mixture of different gases. For its optimal and efficient usage, various purification techniques were adopted. Mel et al. (2016) used NaOH to enrich CH4 in purified biogas. Zhoua (2017) reduced percent CO2 in biogas by using physi-sorbed and chemi-sorbents. Furthermore, Duran et al. (2018) showed a significant effect of wet media on percent CO2 reduction. Similarly, Ronald et al. (2016), developed a modified single water scrubber column for optimal biogas purification. Recently, Noorainet al. (2019a), developed sponge packed water scrubber, to increase the hydraulic retention time for raw biogas purification. In 2017, Srichatet al. investigated that increasing, Ca(OH)2 media concentration and its flow rate enhances methane purification. 
The aim of the study to develop an optimal absorber that enhances purification of biogas by using media concentration, its flow rate and the nature of the stone.Gupta et al. (1985) stated that sun-dried bio-digester effluent has a benefit of transportation and storage. Kadam et al. (2017) dried the bio-digester effluent at 3 cm thickness enhanced nutrients retaining. The main aim of the research to increase the drying rate with more thickness of bio-digester effluent to maintain the nutritional value of dried slurry.

data.projectName: FINDING THE CAUSATIVE GENES IN CLINICALLY DIAGNOSED FAMILIES SEGREGATING Maturity Onset Diabetes in Young (MODY).
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Medical University, Islamabad
data.projectDigest:
FINDING THE CAUSATIVE GENES IN CLINICALLY DIAGNOSED FAMILIES SEGREGATING Maturity Onset Diabetes in Young (MODY).
Summary.
Maturity-onset diabetes of the young (MODY) is a monogenic, clinically and genetically heterogeneous form of diabetes showing autosomal dominant mode of inheritance spanning up to three generations. MODY is highly penetrant and by far most common type of monogenic diabetes. At present, 14 MODY types specified by mutation in respective 14 genes with their etiologies are known.
In this study, fifty MODY families will be recruited from outdoor patient department, Pakistan Institute of Medical Science, Islamabad. A clinician will examine affected persons in the family to ascertain for MODY before recruitment of the family in this study. After the informed consent of subject, blood samples would be taken from affected person, parents as well as normal person in the family. DNA would be extracted from the blood samples by standard protocol. Linkage analysis would be employed to find out if disease in the family is due to one of the fourteen known MODY genes. Families found unlinked with fourteen known genes would be subjected to whole exome sequencing to find out any novel pathogenic variant for MODY. Genetic analysis can help diagnose subgroups of patients with speci?c molecular defects such as MODY, who otherwise are classi?ed under the broad umbrella of type 1. Genetic diagnosis can also aid in pregnancy management, also helpful in genetic counselling for the enrolled family members for making informed decisions. Continuing advances in genotyping and genome sequencing technologies, together with increasing sample sizes, will lead to the discovery of an expanding list of risk variants for diabetes and its complications, as well as drug responses.

data.projectName: Involvement of Hippo Pathway in Breast Cancer Metastasis
data.projectDigest: Breast cancer incidences are gradually increasing among young Pakistani women irrespective of their marital status. In the present study, identification and screening of those genetic factors responsible for this early disease onset are proposed. One plausible reason of the early disease onset among South Asian women is attributed to dyregulation of early developmental pathways as published several researchers (PI also published data on hedgehog pathway). Among these pathways, Hippo dysregulation play a vital role. During normal organ development, activated Hippo pathway restrict cell proliferation and maintain cell differentiation. In case of cancer a comprise on purposeless, persistent, proliferation of cells suspects inactivation of hippo pathway. In this study, a probable dysregulation of hippo pathway with cell uncontrolled growth (tumorigenesis) will be assessed among breast cancer affected patients (n=~500). Any probable correlation of clinico pathological parameters including tumor size, stage of disease, tumor grade, age of patients, with respective members of hippo pathway will be ascertained. Additionally, role of hippo pathway in regulating metastasis promotion or suppression are also assessed using cancer cell lines. This study will be helpful in identifying potential prognostic biomarkers belonging to the hippo pathway for these respective cancer patients.

data.projectName: Real-time Intelligent Monitoring of Suspicious Activities (RIMSA)
data.projectDigest: This project is focused on basic research in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning. These are rapidly growing areas of research offering potential benefits to solve challenging problems like the video analytics under the poor infrastructure and low visibility due to pollution, smog, or fog. It has several applications including real-time intelligent monitoring of suspicious activities (RIMSA) through surveillance cameras, for the deployment at sensitive places like, educational institutes, cantonment, airports, and bus/railway stations. There are major research challenges associated with RIMSA, a) Intra-class variations, viewpoint variations, occlusions, and non-rigid shape of the humans and objects, b) Lack of availability of video surveillance data, specifically related to suspicious activities for training, c) Extraction of features for accurate and efficient recognition of dangerous activities, d) Real time classification model. This project is aimed at developing research-based algorithms for a prototype of RIMSA in an educational institution with the central control, alert system and active response from the security department. RIMSA is divided into four modules, 1) Boundary wall intrusion detection, 2) Vehicle license plate and driver verification, 3) Indoor suspicious activities monitoring, and 4) Outdoor suspicious activities monitoring. This project will have broad scientific, social and academic impacts.

data.projectName: Regulated synthesis of ESAT-6 antigen against Mycobacterium  in transplastomic tomatoes
data.projectDigest: Due to increasing number of patients suffering from different contagious diseases especially in resource poor countries like Pakistan, it is important to produce efficient and cost effective alternative vaccines. Plants provide us with a unique system of foreign protein production in safe, efficient and economical way. Among plant made vaccine (PMV) systems, chloroplast transformation system has some big advantages. Besides its eco-friendliness to maternal inheritance, it offers the opportunity to use multiple copies of plastid genome per cell resulting in high level of protein expression with minimum or no risk of epigenetic effects. The aim of this study is the evaluation of the potential of chloroplast as a production platform for antigen against Mycobacterium. Production of transplastomic lines, their expression of protein, possible effects of foreign protein within plant is covered in this project.
