data.projectName: Essays on Shariah compliant investments
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Benazir Bhutto University, Sheringal, Dir
data.projectDigest:
Since the inception of Dow Jones Islamic Market Index in 1999, Shariah-compliant investment has shown tremendous growth and reached almost 3 trillion US dollars in 2019. Still the market share of Shariah-compliant products is legging well behind its counterparts. Shariah-compliant equity portfolios (SECPs) are different from conventional portfolios (CPs) because the former is governed by Shariah law which imposes additional constraints on investments and exclude firms whose core operations are non-compliant. There are number of studies that document the superior performance of SCEPs in comparison to CPs. However, majority of these studies focused on cumulative returns over a fix time horizon and fail to highlight the time variation and seasonal trends in Shariah-compliant equities. This study is an effort to fill this gap by investigating the cross-sectional seasonality in equities. Based on the seasonal trends this study will create SCEPs and their performance will be compared with conventional portfolio. 
The results of this project are important for both individual and institutional investors. First, the portfolios are designed within the scope of Shariah restrictions. Second, individual investors can benefit from the seasonal trends and can diversify their portfolios in optimal way. Finally, mutual fund industry can also benefit from this study and design portfolios that invest in Shariah-compliant equities and based on seasonal trends they can optimize both selection and weighting decisions of respective portfolios.

data.projectName: Ligand-Induced G-Quadruplex (G4) DNA Stabilization: A New Strategy for Cancer Therapy
data.projectDigest:
Cancer treatment is undergoing a significant revolution from “one-size-fits-all” cytotoxic therapy to various customized drugs that target proteins, enzymes and nucleic acids. As the precision of these drugs is poor, many side effects are observed. Moreover, the cancer treatment is also prone to aberration of extensively high cost due to expensive technologies and drugs. A cut in the cost of drug development is, therefore, a core to develop an affordable drug, and computer-aided drug design can play a remarkable role in this regime.  
Recently, it was observed that the stabilization of G-Quadruplexes (G4) DNA can play an important role in treating cancers. The fact that multiple oncogenes are reported to harbor the G4 at regulatory regions, the stabilization of G4 can regulate gene expression, and thereby treat cancer. Furthermore, the stabilization of G4 structure found at telomeres ceases elongation of telomeric ends causing cell death, and prevents cancer. The G4-stabilization can be induced by various small organic ligands, such as BRACO-19.
The aim of the current work is to identify small organic ligands that can potentially stabilize G4 DNA structures using combined in silico and in vitro techniques, and be used in cancer therapeutics.

data.projectName: Citizenship Awareness and Community Development through Participatory Action Research in the Newly Merged Districts of Erstwhile FATA
data.projectDigest: We propose a project of “Citizenship Awareness and Community Development through Participatory Action Research in the Newly Merged Districts of Erstwhile FATA” through which we will establish youth communities from the merged districts for training in the center of research in FATA University. The selected youth leaders will be trained to conduct a survey and engaged in carrying a survey on “The Need of Awareness on Democratic Rights and citizenship Education” in different parts of all seven Newly Merged Districts (NMDs). This project is not limited to training, but to organizing FDGs, conducting interview to determine what specific obstacles exist to demonstrate a better understanding of democratic rights as citizens of Pakistan to youth in NMDs and develop recommendations appropriate for Tribal context. In the first phase, a desk study would be conducted, examining level of awareness about rights and responsibilities, civic education, conflict resolution skills, and peace promotion. In the second phase, the FDGs and Interviews will be conducted to develop curriculum in collaboration with Police Department and other legal and lawful agencies to meet gaps identified by FDGs and Interviews. The third stage is intensive training of youth to cascade that to public in NMDs based on Need Analysis. Final stage is compiling a comprehensive public policy recommendation to Government of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Biochemical and molecular characterization of antidiabetic nature of commonly consumed spices of Pakistani cuisine
data.projectDigest:
The present project is based on the biochemical pattern and gene expression of culinary spices/herbs against diabetes management. In healthy state of life, insulin helps to utilize glucose in different parts of body but in case of diabetes mellitus (DM), either body is unable to make insulin or the target cells are resistant to its action. This results in increased sugar level, high level of fat and set off different metabolic changes that can harm the body and even be fatal. According to WHO, this rapidly growing metabolic disease stands at third position among commonest diseases of the world. Previous reports estimated 7-8 % prevalence rate of disease. Being a nation of low- middle income country, there is search of novel, safe, cheaper and effective therapeutic agent to fight against diabetes. Use of traditional medicine based on plants and dietary adjuncts can prove possible therapeutic candidate. 
The proposed project will evaluate the biological activities of traditional Pakistani culinary spices in term of several metabolic enzymes/ attributes involved in management of experimentally induced diabetes on animal model. Molecular characterization will consist of insulin scretogenic activity, enhanced insulin action, effect on glucose transporter, defense against oxidative stress and metabolic enzymes of sugar and fats using conventional RT-PCR and real time PCR. The information gain through this analysis will be useful for future novel drug development against diabetes

data.projectName: Morpho-anatomical and Molecular characterization of genus Carex (Cyperaceae) from Murree Region
data.projectDigest: Genus Carex belongs to Cyperaceae (Sedge family) is the largest monocot family after Orchidaceae and Poaceae, more than 70 genera and 4,000 species and cosmopolitan in distribution. In Pakistan, about 22 genera and 179 species have been reported so far. This project is based on the morpho-anatomical and molecular study of the Genus Carex within an estimated 21000 species world widely, broad range of habitats mostly present in the temperate zone. In Pakistan, represent at high altitude habitats. Only few species reported in three floras of Cyperaceae.  A study will be planned to collect plant species of Carex in the vicinity of Murree region. The morpho-anatomical and molecular variations in Carex especially will be recorded with the help of advanced tools. Photographs of the original habitat and enlarged view of the inflorescence will be presented. Species will be identified on the basis of size and number of the inflorescence, bract, shape and colour of glumes and nut by naked eye and dissecting microscope and DNA sequencing will also be finding. Anatomical variations of all parts will be done by microtome and double staining techniques. This project will be helpful for the edition of new species in the flora of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Design and Implementation of A.I. based Ophthalmological Diagnosis of Eye Diseases using Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) Machine and Image Processing.
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest: Conventional diagnostic methods rely only upon physicians’ professional experience, leading to high misdiagnosis rate. Integration of ophthalmology and AI has the potential to revolutionize current disease diagnose pattern and generate a significant clinical impact. In this project a portable interface is proposed which can readily be connected with the commercially available Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) machine and apply machine learning and artificial intelligence algorithms to detect common eye diseases like Age Related Macular Degeneration (AMD) and Diabetic Macular Edema (DME). This home-grown e-health solution will enable the OCT technician to readily generate standardized diagnostic report for the patients of retinopathy and can help the Ophthalmologists to diagnose the disease progressively from the early stages of diagnosis with high accuracy and efficiently. This will either identify the particular eye disease (AMD or DME) patient is suffering from and the extent of degradation. The project also aims to create publicly available dataset for academic research. More than 3 Million people in Pakistan suffer from one form or other of eye diseases [1,2]. Dr. Munawar Ahmed will validate the results of the generated diagnostic report. Prof. Dr. Nirvana,  will technically supervise, evaluate and contribute in developing a fuzzy logic classifier to the dataset.

data.projectName: Development of high amylose and resistant starch wheat for diabetic patients
data.projectDigest: The current research project is designed to alter through breeding the amylose and amylopectin ratio through marker assisted selection and to develop genotypes with increased amylose contents and resistant starch. The starch synthase SSII enzyme is responsible for the synthesis of increased amount of amylopectin a readily available sugar. In the mutant SSII the production of amylopectin is reduced and that of amylose and resistant starch is increased. In the current project we will screen wheat varieties and lines for mutant SSII gene through marker assisted selection. Null SSII-A1, null SSII-B1 and null SSII- D1, the three homeologous null lines identified with MAS. Null SSII-A and SSII-B lines will be crossed, F1 generation grown and F2 lines with null SSII-A + SSII–B identified with PCR. Also null SSII-B and null SSII-D lines crossed, F1 generation grown and F2 lines with null SSII-B + SSII–D identified with PCR. Then the partial null lines from the two population will be crossed, F1 generation grown and in F2 generation lines with null SSII-A + SSII-B + SSII–D identified through PCR. Thus mutant lines with increased amylose and resistant starch developed.

data.projectName: Structural and functional alterations in different ecotypes of Xanthium strumarium L. to metal and salt stress
data.projectDigest: Xantium strumarium is  economically and medicinally important weed. It is used to phytoremediate different metals and can also cope the saline stress. Different ecotypes of Xanthium strumarium will be collected from different regions of the Punjab, Pakistan and will be grown in Faisalabad environmental conditions for  period of two months. Then the adapted ecotypes will be treated with different levels of cadmium, salt and combination of cadmium and salt. Three experiments will be conducted during the period of three years. In the first experiment, four salinity levels will be maintained  i.e., 0 (control with no salinity treatment), 100, 200, and 300 mM NaCl. In the second experiment, four levels of cadmium  viz; 0, 50, 100 and 150 mg kg-1 will be applied. The third experiment will conducted to investigate the combined effect of cadmium and salinity. Four levels of salinity and cadmium viz; control, 100 mM: 50 mg kg-1, 200 mM:100 mg kg 1 and 300 mM:150 mg kg 1will be maintained. The plants will be carefully collected from the culture medium at the end of salt or cadmium treatment (after 12 weeks), and washed thoroughly with distilled water to determine various morpho-anatomical and physiological characteristics.

data.projectName: Framework Development for Risk Identification and Quantification of Roadways and Rail networks of CPEC to make Supply Chain Resilient
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: This project is on the risk identification and quantification for roadways and rail networks under CPEC which will be a game changer for Pakistan. As a developing nation, supply chain has been suffered with the economic, social, political and environmental challenges. This study will be of a great help for risk identification which then analyze the potential risks in order to overcome challenges and to make supply chain resilient. The logistics of CPEC will be designed accordingly and this will benefit the academia and perspective investors. Enhance export competitiveness also depends on resilient performance of supply chain. With CPEC aiming to be complete in 2025 the logistic network will be entirely revamped and there exists a strong need to identify the risks associated with this new logistics network. A thorough investigation needs to be done for identification and quantification of the new emerging risks. This research will also provide directions to business group and local industrialists in making investments in and around CPEC.

data.projectName: Potential neuroprotective role of natural flavonoids against alcoholic neurodegeneration and inflammation-induced Alzheimer’s disease
data.projectDigest:
Neurodegenerative disorders like Alzheimer’s disease and alcoholic neurodegeneration are one of the major causes of disability and dependency among older people worldwide. In Pakistan up to date the specialist neurodegenerative services are rare and public awareness about Alzheimer’s disease and alcoholic neurodegeneration is low, therefore need full attention of researchers. Natural substances in the form of flavonoids having potential anti-oxidant and anti-inflammatory activities have shown potent neuroprotective properties in various studies.
 This project is designed to study the underlying mechanism of inflammation-induced neurodegeneration (Alzheimer’s disease) and its possible therapeutic candidate in the form of natural substances. Next, the possible neuroprotective effect of these natural agents will also be evaluated against alcoholic neurodegeneration.  Although a number of factors are involved in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer’s disease, very less focus has been attributed to neuroinflammation-induced Alzheimer’s pathology.  A number of studies described induction of memory impairment and neuronal loss in animals subjected to systemic inflammation. Similarly it has been well studied that chronic ethanol ingestions produce neurotoxicity in distinct regions of brain which may results in a number of neurodegenerative disorders like Alzheimer’s disease or Parkinson’s disease. In this study we are supposed to develop a dietary approach by using already reported flavonoids as safe and promising therapeutic candidates for treatment of Alzheimer’s and alcoholic neurodegeneration. Next these flavonoids will be subjected to other preclinical and clinical trials as marketed drugs with the collaborating pharmaceutical industries.

data.projectName: Novel chitosan-raft forming drug delivery system for the enhancement of oral bioavailability of Ibandronic acid
data.projectDigest: Osteoporosis is the most common problem in Asian countries especially in Pakistan. The most common causes of osteoporosis are demineralization of bones and joints due to excessive use of junk food and cold drinks. Gastroretentive drug delivery system (GRDDs) retained the dosage form in stomach while improving the bioavailability of poorly water soluble drugs. GRDDs include high and low density, bioadhesive, expansion, magnetic, floating ion exchange resins and raft forming systems. Amongst these systems, raft forming system a newly emerging approach of GRDD used to overwhelm the drawbacks related with other floating system. Raft forming system exploits raft forming agents such as pectin, sodium alginate, carbopol and chitosan which form raft on contact with gastric fluid and gas generating systems like sodium bicarbonate and citric acid. This system also contains antacids for raft strengthening agent. This system forms raft on contact with gastric fluid that floats on surface of stomach contents. The proposed study will consider all possible factors like social status, economic condition, gender, age, educational level, demographic conditions, marital status, disabilities, genetic conditions, physical conditions and poverty status. The study also focuses on treatment of osteoporosis.

data.projectDigest:
The use of proteins for therapeutic purposes and vitamins in cosmetic preparations has gained a tremendous amount of popularity in the recent past due to their specificity, high efficacy and less toxicity. The discovery of nanomedicine has revolutionized the area of drug formulation and treatment of diseases. This project aims to formulate and evaluate the stability of micro and nanosponges containing therapeutic protein like enzyme collagenase for topical use that could be employed for rapid healing of wounds, burns, and skin ulcers. Similarly, a vitamin (e.g., ascorbic acid) would also be formulated in sponges that could be used for anti-aging purposes. This study will focus on the factors necessary for the preparations of effective and stable novel sponge formulations of therapeutic proteins and vitamin C, a research area untouched in Pakistan.
The preparation of such novel formulations will help pharmaceutical and cosmetic industries to further proceed towards the development of various other therapeutic protein and vitamin preparations. This project aims to formulate novel dosage forms with high effectiveness, low cost, improved patient compliance and lesser side effects. Thus, taking a step towards serving humanity as well as training postgraduate students in newly emerging interdisciplinary sciences i.e. nanomedicine and nanomaterials.

data.projectName: Thin film flows
data.projectDigest:
The flow of a thin film is a phenomenon we observe every day when we take a shower, drink a cup of coffee, or turn on the windshield wipers. All of these real world situations involve not only the flow of the liquid and the surrounding air, but also their interaction with adjacent hard surfaces. As we know from waxing our cars and cooking with non-stick cookware, the dynamics of a fluid coating a solid surface depend heavily on the surface chemistry. Many industrial processes, ranging from spin coating of microchips to de-icing of airplane wings, rely on the ability to control these
interactions.

data.projectName: A Self-Learning Framework for Search and Rescue Operations in Disastrous Areas Using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
data.projectDigest:
These SAR missions cover different domains, like finding the individuals caught up in disaster areas and providing them with humanitarian aid. This aid ranges in food, water, first aid medical kits, clothes, lifesaving jackets. To reach in higher affected areas in disaster using conventional means of transportation is a difficult task due to destroyed infrastructure and emergencies. The most crucial aspect is the time factor, as a delayed approach to people stuck in affected areas may cause more lives.
Adding Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) or drones to SAR missions could minimize the time to reach, analyze, and provide the number of suffering humans with emergency aid. UAVs are a cost-effective medium to approach humans stuck in disaster areas where destroyed infrastructure does not allow conventional transportation. 
Many models are in practice where single UAV or fleet of UAVs participate in SAR operations. Challenge is to find a system for the fleet of drones used in a rescue mission such that they can perform multiple tasks at a time. Multiple approaches are in practice to develop batter collaboration among UAVs for multiple task allocation. 
With the advancement in processing power of computers and the revival of Artificial Intelligence, "Reinforcement-Learning" techniques have been used quite efficiently in different domains. Reinforcement learning is state of the art method in AI to achieve results where agents explore and learn their environment and react/perform according to the learned-environment. We believe that with the use of "Reinforcement-Learning," multiple UAVs can perform batter in SAR operations by exploring and learning the environment by themselves. We also believe that we can increase the accuracy of UAVs in this regard to save more lives.

data.projectName: Concept to Practice: Manufacturing of Bio-lubricants from non-edible oils & renewable sources towards a circular economy
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Most lubricants on today’s global market are petroleum based and the remaining are formulated from chemicals or crude oil. Environment friendly products such as bio-lubricants or bio-based lubricants are the potential game changer because of their renewable, non-toxic, environment-friendly nature. Pakistan's lubricants market size as per the line of business consists of consumer, transport and industry. Transport sector is the largest lubricant consumer in Pakistan, generating business for all lubricating oil-manufacturing companies. Total demand of country is 400 million liters out of which 50% is produced locally by registered firms and blending plants with locally available lube base oils.
To introduce green or bio-lubricants in the market, it is essential to discuss the valuable role of indigenous oil-yielding crops as sustainable sources of energy for green-lubricant production in Pakistan. This research work will address the key challenges & requirements of bio-lubricants manufacturing from renewable or non-edible oil resources. The use of bio-lubricants is also very promising for clean water, for a clean environment, for clean mountainsides and for clean soils because of low toxicity, rapid biodegradability, good lubricating properties and longer equipment life.

data.projectName: Clinico-epidemiological study and economic consequences of Bovine Viral Diarrhea in cattle and buffaloes in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
data.projectDigest:
Bovine viral diarrhea (BVD) is caused by BVD virus (BVDV), classified in the genus Pestivirus and family Flaviviridae. Cattle are the primary host for the virus and occurs worldwide. BVD is the disease of major economic importance (milk loss, early culling, reduced dressing percentage, mortality loss, reproductive losses, and treatment costs). Clinical disease occurs after the contact of healthy cattle with persistently infected (PI) animals. The major signs of BVD include fever, diarrhea, oculonasal discharge, decreased milk yield and reproductive losses. The PI calves are major source of BVDV as they secrete copious amount of BVDV in secretions and excretions, thus easily spreading the virus to other susceptible individuals. 
In Pakistan, unfortunately little attention has been paid until now to investigate the significant problem of BVD in livestock industry. Dairy farmers and professionals mostly correlate cause of abortion to Brucellosis while ignoring the involvement of BVDV. In many developed countries, control programs are being implemented for eradication of this economically important disease. The success of all these programs depends on the ability to detect all PI animals at a young age. Undetected PI calves are the main source of the infection within herds and perpetuation of the disease in cattle and buffalos’ population.
 In light of these facts, the present research project has been designed to achieve the following objectives;
1.	Identification of PI animals; to meet this objective 1200 newborn calves (cattle calves=600, buffalos’ calves=600) in the districts of Peshawar and Charsada of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa will be tested for BVDV infection using laboratory techniques antigen-capture ELISA and PCR.
2.	Determination of seroprevalence and risk factors of BV

data.projectName: Protective-stimulating complex Palliative’’ for rice blast disease (RBD) protection and growth regulation of Rice
data.projectDigest: Rice is one of the most widely cultivated cash crops worldwide. Rice blast (Pyricularia oryaze) disease (RBD) is a key concern in combating global food insecurity given the disease is responsible for approximately 30% of rice production losses globally, the losses are equivalent of feeding to 60 million people. These losses increase globally and ultimately rice price increases with the reduced number of consumers in terms of their welfare and food security it’s a big loss. Copper based fungicides are well elucidated in rice crop production, but continuous use of copper is ultimately accumulating in rice kernels, which is the main utilizing part of the plant. That directly effect the soil and human rice consumers. Zinc deficiency is also a dilemma in rice production. Zinc fortification is an essential part of good quality rice production along with ultimate up regulation of the rice plant growth. Silicon (Si) is known to effectively mitigate various environmental stresses and enhance plant resistance against both fungal and bacterial pathogens. Collectively, Zinc (Zn), Copper (Cu) and Silicon (Si) are essential microelements and protectants for plant growth and controlling fungal rice blast disease. But little is known about the combined effects of Zn, Cu and Si as a protectant and growth stimulator on rice. Therefore, to combat against these two major concerns of RBD and zinc deficiency in rice production a complex of microelements and protectant is direly needed to escape from heavy losses. In this proposed project, a protective stimulating complex Palliative’’ formulated with Cu based Zin and silicon, the most important elements of plant protection from rice blast disease and regulation of their growth.

data.projectName: Synthesis of Imidazole Based Corrosion Inhibitors For Corrosion Mitigation Applications in Oil-Line Systems
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Corrosion (rusting) is recognized as a serious problem in industrial sectors while resulting losses are hundreds billions dollars each year. According to Mr Jeffrey Didas (President National Association of Corrosion Engineers, USA), ‘Pakistan could save Rs270-380 billion annually through corrosion prevention’. Exploration, production and transportation of petroleum oil is the most corrosion-prone industrial sector as it constantly deal with highly corrosive environments due to acid stimulation, CO2 and H2S contamination. Corrosion is a severe hazard to all engineering installations setting up for oil transportation as a part of ongoing CPEC project. Corrosion inhibitor is an effective way of protecting metallic installation against corrosion in petroleum sector. Pakistan imports more than 50 million USD per annum corrosion inhibitor chemicals. OGDCL, Integrated Well Services & Solutions (IWSS) and Redox (SMC Pvt) Ltd Pakistan have shown interest in subject proposal and will assist in execution of project.
Essence of proposed project is that a wide variety of synthetic and analytical techniques will be employed to indigenously develop imidazole based corrosion inhibitors formulation. Various derivatives of imidazole will be synthesized. Those which may prove their corrosion inhibition activities, will be explored further for corrosion inhibitor formulations. This will be blend of corrosion inhibitor chemicals, surfactants, fluid rheology stabilizers, oxygen scavengers and additives etc. Resultant formulation will be subjected to various laboratory and field testing. The proposed project is first of its kind in Pakistan where we are going to indigenously synthesize novel imidazole derivatives and its subsequent deployment in corrosion inhibitor formulation.

data.projectName: A comparative Study for the Selection of Effective Stablizer Among Poly Propylene Fiber, Styrene Butadiene Rubber (SBR), Silica Fumes for Collapsible Soils
data.projectDigest: This research proposal will help in the selection of most appropriate, effective, sustainable, and efficient stabilizer among Poly Propylene (PP) Fiber, Styrene-Butadiene Rubber (SBR) Latex, and Silica Fumes (SF) for the collapsible soils of Chasma Barrage, Dera Ismail (DI) Khan. In this study, the suitability of PP Fiber, SBR Latex, and SF will be investigated as a stabilizing agent through detailed experimentation and microstructural analysis. The testing methodology will be comprised of basic soil identification testing (sieve analysis, specific gravity test, and Attenberg’s Limit tests), modified proctor compaction test, and triaxial (Undrained-Unconsolidated (UU)) tests.  Mineralogical and microstructural studies will be conducted on the collapsible soil sample stabilized using optimum percentages of each of admixture through X-ray diffraction (XRD), and scanning electron microscope (SEM) analysis. These results will confirm the formation of cementitious compounds in the XRD pattern and show the development of dense matrix in SEM images.

data.projectName: Smart Wearable Device for Therapeutic Intervention of Children with Thalassemia
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
In Pakistan, it is estimated that an average of 9000 children are born with Beta thalassemia; a hereditary disease annually. Lack of facilities and awareness of coordination to this multi-disciplinary problem make the treatment difficult in a variety of ways. Thalassemia patients are children and they can’t stay in one place for long time to perform the iron chelation therapy (Blood Transfusion). This therapy is at times performed even thrice a week. Currently the devices used are neither disposable nor they are for a long-term use, hence millions of devices end up in junk yards causing ecological problems. This suffice for a portable automated syringe pump specially manufactured for children so they can play and perform daily routine activities during therapy.
We propose a Smart Wearable Device for Therapeutic Intervention of Children with Thalassemia fabricated with recyclable biomaterials with smart features. Added features in the device will include GSM module, which will send a text message to parents and clinician when the therapy is complete. The device will be rechargeable and will have a long-lasting battery that will be required to charge after two days.

data.projectName: UAV based Smart Environment Monitoring
data.projectDigest: To promote precision farming the country’s smart agriculture needs to be supported and enhanced. A modular approach is proposed as a solution to infrastructure that uses an Internet of Thing (IoT), machine learning and cloud computing to predict onslaught of pests and plant diseases. This in turn will help increase the agriculture productivity. To achieve this aim, design proposals on building a controlled environment (IoT enabled greenhouse) which was connected to a Ground Control Centre (gateway node). Concurrently, design work is expected on uncontrolled environment (Agri-drone or UAV housing a multispectral imager and communication link to the Ground Control Centre). Both the environments will hence be calibrated. Imagery based on NVDI and modulation based formulation of images is considered. This will enable development of multi objective optimization function to trace the optimal flight path of the UAV in the presence of pests and decay of vegetation as well as soil conditions impacted by shortest possible flight path to optimize battery and minimize variance in the image results. The output is expected in terms of improved techniques and methods to enhance crop yield for signature crops of rural Sindh / Punjab and enhancement of capacity building of companies like Tech Valley who aim to enhance the aerial spraying platform developed as part of HEC TDF. Academic partnership is established with Department of Mechatronics, National University of Science and Technology, a startup Tech Valley and between the departments of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science and Information System based at the Institute of Business Management.

Some countries having more power supers and target the ones who have no atomic power. 9/11 event is one of it, on which the use of power was to establish “Uni Polar World”. After Afghanistan, Pakistan was also suffered with economic and financial losses. Every individual of Pakistan was suffered with the effects. The writers and poets community of Pakistan was also suffered a lot and express their thinking and sentiments in their poetry.

In this project the Nazam portion of Pakistani poets will be extracted and analyzed, effected from the subject. At the end conclusion of the project will be expressed in the form of a published book.

data.projectDigest:
The plants have served the humanity through the ages for preservation of human health and civilizing the quality of life. Plants are potential source of drugs that are used for the treatment of ailments such as fever, cancer, tumor, microbial infections, etc. Pakistan is rich in medicinal plants, which are frequently used as folk medicine for the treatment of various diseases such as cancer, tumor, fever, flue, hypertension, inflammatory, wounds, etc. There is need to systematically explore the medicinal plants to isolate the bioactive secondary metabolites. The project is aimed at the isolation, structure elucidation and pharmaceutical screenings of biological active constituents from the indigenous medicinal plants Ziziphora clinopodioides Lam.  The Following steps are involve in the proposed research:

•	Collection of plants of Ziziphora clinopodioides Lam. followed by extraction and fractionation 
•	Pharmacological screening of various fractions
•	Application of column chromatographic techniques on various fractions to purify the natural products
•	Structural elucidation of new natural products through modern spectroscopy (UV, IR, NMR (1D & 2D), and Mass)
•	Pharmacological screening of newly isolated compounds
•	Training of scientific personnel in the field of natural product chemistry
•	The results would be published in reputed international journals.

data.projectName: Identification and confirmation of Okra leaf genes in local cotton genotypes
data.projectDigest: Cotton leaf shape influences multifunction roles in plant; ranging from photosynthesis as core function; followed by insect populations and drought stress. Okra leaf discourages most of the insect population including, white fly; a well-known carrier of CLCuV. During the year 2019, White fly has damaged the cotton crop severely; which lead to a huge yield loss. Besides, okra leaf cotton plants exhibit higher drought tolerance. Keeping in view the importance and influence of okra shaped leaves, there is dire need to explore more about the genes regulating okra shaped leaves in our local cultivars.  Current project has been designed for prediction and identification of genes regulating the development of okra leaf in local cotton using insilico prediction approach. The predicted genes will be amplified in the local okra leaf cotton cultivars. Further, the cross between okra leaf and normal leaf cotton genotypes will be carried out and the genes regulating okra leaf shape will be identified and amplified in the F1. Our findings will help in better understanding genes regulating okra leaf shape, which in future can be transfer to local cultivars to reduce the white fly infestation and ultimately mitigating the attack of various transmitted diseases including CLCuV.

data.projectName: Automated Exploratory Testing Using Machine Learning
data.piUniversity: National University of Computer and Emerging Sciences, Islamabad
data.projectDigest:
Modern interactive web applications are increasingly more complex due to the use of heterogeneous technologies. Such applications offer important services to the users and therefore must be reliable. Huge amount of resources is spent on testing of web applications to ensure that the services are being provided in a reliable manner and that the provided services are functionally correct. All major companies have significant interest in technologies that can improve testing of web applications. Exploratory testing is a manual test approach where test engineer relies on their domain knowledge and experience to test the web applications. A number of test engineers are asked to use the application and to perform the tasks the user is expected to perform, identifying any bugs that are encountered. While exploratory testing is the most widely used testing approach for web applications, it is labor intensive due to its manual nature, is nonsystematic and the results can vary depending on the experience of the test engineers. There is a significant interest in industry for ways to improve exploratory testing. 
In this proposal we aim to improve the performance of exploratory testing by developing novel AI and machine learning techniques that can complement or replace manual exploratory testing. Due to labor intensive nature, only few test scenarios out of possible thousands of scenarios can be tested manually. We propose to research and create ML based Automated Exploratory Testing bot that can learn from the dataset obtained from manual testers, and automate the task of exploratory testing. The Bot shall be able to explore and execute much greater number of scenarios to complement and (if required) eventually replace some of current manual exploratory testing efforts.

data.projectName: Development of low-cost and Selective Sensor for the early Detection of Dengue Fever
data.projectDigest: The project aims to develop advanced, yet low-cost optical sensor for the diagnosis of dengue - tackling a major healthcare issue of Pakistan and creating a reliable and affordable  solution for use in local clinics, exploiting the benefits of photonics, optical fiber technology and sensor technology. Dengue is an acute febrile disease caused by mosquito bites with more than 25,000 deaths annually worldwide.  At present, there is no cure or vaccine, so good patient management by early diagnosis can save life and reduce suffering. Conventional, well-established techniques are time-consuming, costly and need high-level technical skills and are not well suited to local clinic use. In this proposal, a better and simpler approach is proposed, building on the combined experience of the consortium, in developing electrochemical and optical methods to simplify and accelerate clinical diagnosis.  It proposes developing low-cost, easy to use, and multiplexed optical fiber, photonic crystal, molecular imprinted polymers and nano-particle based sensors designed for the early identification of dengue through detecting NS1 and Protein E and additionally IgG and IgM.  Furthermore, clinical samples from dengue patients will be tested to check its practicability to detect dengue biomarkers.

data.projectName: Design of Optically Transparent Antenna for 5G Communication
data.projectDigest:
With the involvement of smart cities, advanced wireless technology is required. 5G enabled antennas have low attenuation due to higher bandwidth causing the signal degradation because of scattering and reflection. The access points, signal repeaters and base stations should be deployed at existing infrastructure of towers, buildings, street lights to overcome this issue.  Transparent antennas will keep esthetics of the window thus helps in providing the network access to the vehicles and people passing by those buildings.
The transparent antennas lack good efficiency, gain and return loss as compared to conventional antennas. The possible solution is to use antenna arrays having periodic structures integrated in special pattern to improve the signal strength, beamforming and antenna gains in different polarization schemes.
The antenna will be designed for Thin wire mesh using multi arrays for various polarization schemes to improve the antenna design parameters, afterword’s band pass and band stop filters for frequency-selective surfaces (FSS) will also be designed. The results will be analyzed, and antenna parameters will be optimized.

data.projectName: Faunal analysis of honey bees, bee pathology and physicochemical characterization of honey at Malakand Division, KP, Pakistan
data.piUniversity: University of Malakand, Chakdara, Dir, Malakand
data.projectDigest:
Honey bees are the most beneficial insects by providing pollination services to agriculture sector, production of valuable products like honey, propolis, bee venom, royal jelly and wax and the provision of employment opportunities. Increased anthropogenic activities, pathogenesis and global climate change has caused a severe decline in honey bee population worldwide.
The present study is intended to evaluate the available honey bee fauna with respect to diversity, relative abundance and species richness, to assess honey bee pathology due to bacteria, viruses, fungi, mites, parasites and wax moths and finally to characterize the locally produced honey with respect to its physicochemical parameters.
The study will help to evaluate the available honey bee fauna in the study area, will help in assessing honey bee pathology which is a major restraint in the development of apiculture sector and a major factor in the decline of honey bee population. Analyzing physicochemical parameters of the local honey will give a true picture of the composition, purity, medicinal and nutritional value of different types of local honey 
The project will help to establish a Laboratory of Apiculture at the Department of Zoology, University of Malakand for sustainable utilization in research, apiculture and agriculture.

data.projectName: A framework for evasion detection inIPv6 networks
data.projectDigest:
Each year we see increased number of security breaches as well as the sophistication of attacks. Organizations usually focus on perimeter security to protect crucial assets. Modern intrusion detection evasion techniques incapacitate the Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS), to predict the change in a host’s state based on incoming traffic by exploiting ambiguities in the traffic stream. One of the reasons for such ambiguities is the difference in interpretation of request for comments (RFC) documents of protocols by different vendors. Techniques for intrusion detection evasion include  TTL manipulation, IDS MAC Address Attack, IP Fragmentation Attacks etc. The larger universe of IPv6 devices significantly increases the potential of attacks and billions of devices can become malware and botnet nodes due to the lack of protection.
The goal of this project is to investigate evasion techniques and their applicability in IPv6 networks. We plan to test the evasion attacks on multiple modern open source IDS using TCP and UDP protocols, and report the success or failure of these security devices in detecting the attacks. Based on our findings we will propose a theoretical solution and implement the framework for detection of evasion attacks on IPv6 networks.

data.projectName: Social Determinants of Helath
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: We believe that healthy population is basic requirement for the development and prosperity of any country. Health is, though, a complex phenomenon and it can be approached from many different angles, it has been realized that health is most of all a social phenomenon. The study of social determinants of health is, in other words, the study of the entire circumstances in which people live. Disease, similarly, is not merely a ‘biological condition’ but also a social construction; i.e. how people see and interpret the origin, the symptoms and treatment of disease. Following WHO definition of health, we want look at it as ‘not merely the absence of disease but a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being’ (WHO 2010). There is a serious dearth of comprehensive research in Pakistan which looks at health holistically and explores the dynamics of modern bio-technological medical infrastructure and societal dimensions. Therefore the main aim of this project is to improve the quality of existing data about health and disease in Pakistan by providing baseline data. For this purpose, we have developed a mix methodological framework and also chosen different field sites covering variety of living conditions both in urban and rural settings.

data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
As the world endures to work in the direction of a sustainable future, solar power is proving itself to be an important part of the energy landscape. Experts in solar community estimate that solar power could replace fossil fuels to become a primary energy source in some parts of the world, and it has already turn out to be highly competitive with traditional energy production in various places, including Hawaii, India, Italy, Germany, the Netherlands and Spain.
In order to truly contest the traditional methods of power production, yet, the costs associated with photovoltaics (PV) technology must be brought down in novel ways. 
For this, there are two major goals:
1.	 the first is to decrease the solar cell manufacturing  cost, 
2.	and the second is to increase its efficiency (the amount of power that can be extracted from the cell relative to incident power from the sun). 
We approach the problem through the investigation of new materials in solar cell architectures. 2-dimensional (2D) materials such as MoS2 and WSe2 are ideal candidates for cutting costs because they have the potential to improve the efficiency in solar cells, but with the lowest possible materials cost and weight: a single layer of atoms or a thin film of few microns in thickness.
This project combines three fields:
 1. Fundamental materials science to develop high quality samples of Perovskites, MoS2 and WSe2 
2. Device physics to fabricate and test a complete Si solar cell
3. Integration of investigated materials into Silicon solar cells for improvisation of efficiency (Tandem architecture).

data.projectName: Effect of Divalent and Trivalent Cations on Structural, Electrical and Dielectric Properties of Ferrites”
data.projectDigest: A ferrite is a ceramic material made by mixing and firing large proportions of iron(III) oxide (Fe2O3, rust) blended with small proportions of one or more additional metallic elements, such as barium, manganese, nickel, and zinc.[1] They are electrically non-conductive, meaning that they are insulators, and ferrimagnetic, meaning they can easily be magnetized or attracted to a magnet. Ferrites can be divided into two families based on their resistance to being demagnetized (magnetic coercivity).Hard ferrites have high coercivity, so are difficult to demagnetize. They are used to make permanent magnets for applications such as refrigerator magnets, loudspeakers, and small electric motors Soft ferrites have low coercivity, so they easily change their magnetization and act as conductors of magnetic fields. They are used in the electronics industry to make efficient magnetic cores called ferrite cores for high-frequency inductors, transformers and antennas, and in various microwave components.Ferrite compounds are extremely low cost, being made of mostly rusted iron (iron oxide), and have excellent corrosion resistance. They are very stable and difficult to demagnetize, and can be made with both high and low coercive forces. Yogoro Kato and Takeshi Takei of the Tokyo Institute of Technology synthesized the first ferrite compounds in 1930.

data.projectName: Utilization of Banana waste and peels as low-cost feed for small ruminants
data.projectDigest: Foreign exchange earnings through fruit and vegetable exports have risen every year. But a lack of post-harvest and cold chain infrastructure is seriously hampering Pakistan’s fruit export potential. Every year 2.2 million tons of vegetables and 2.8-3 million tons of fruits get wasted during and after harvest. This is roughly 30 percent of Pakistan’s total vegetable production, and about 40 per cent of fruits. Pakistan produces 154,800 tons of banana fruit. About 30?40 percent of the total banana production is rejected for failing to meet quality standards and is wasted, thus can be potentially used for feeding to livestock. Banana wastes include small-sized, damaged bananas and banana peels which can be fed to livestock. The findings of the research will benefit the small holder farmers by providing the low-cost feed supplement for their ruminant livestock. The banana waste will be converted to sustainable animal feed. This will ultimately play the integral role in poverty alleviation and food security.

data.projectDigest: Poultry industry is fulfilling the demand of animal protein for ever increasing population by providing economical and highly nutritive meat. However, rapidly growing broilers need balanced diet in terms of energy and minerals. In minerals, trace minerals are of utmost importance due to their involvement in multiple biological functions that ensure fast growth and high quality meat. Trace minerals are supplemented in inorganic forms which are less bioavailable and to compensate it, they are supplemented in much higher doses that increases the cost and chance of organismal toxicity along with environmental pollution. Alternate includes use of organic salts of minerals but they are not economical and they can be replaced with organic-nano-trace minerals which are highly bioavailable and also economical. The quality and security of meat is compromised by multiple stressors like heat stress or transportation stress which induce oxidative damage to muscles and intestine. The damaged intestine allows translocation of pathogens to muscles and compromised security of meat. These effects can be minimized by enhancing antioxidant status of both muscles and intestine which can be achieved by virtue of organic-nano-trace minerals supplementation that will boost antioxidant enzymes of muscles and intestine and therefore ensure high meat quality and security.

data.projectName: Development of shock absorber and EMI shielded maternity dress for pregnant women
data.projectDigest: Women wear maternity dress during its pregnancy period as the body size change over time. Being pregnant is a beautiful feeling and during this period, if a woman wears maternity clothes, it provides comfort for the lady as well as the baby in the womb. Protection for pregnant women is the protection of two lives. With the increasing ratio of working women all over the world, the chances of accidents during driving and working also increased. Moreover, with the increasing use of electronic devices (Mobile phones, Wifi, microwaves etc.) the human is more exposed to the electromagnetic radiation emitted from these devices. Long term exposure of these radiations during pregnancy may increase the risk of children behavioral problems, fatigue, anxiety, sleep disturbance and the birth of a disabled child. The proposed maternity dress in this research will provide protection to pregnant women during accidents as well as from electromagnetic radiation. This will decrease the death rate of babies due to disasters during the pregnancy period and also EMI shielded fabric will save the baby from electromagnetic radiation which will lead to the birth of a healthy baby.

data.projectName: Fabrication and Characterization of Sorafenib-Loaded Chitosan-Modified Polymeric Nanoparticles for the Effective Treatment of Hepatocellular Carcinoma
data.projectDigest:
The main purpose of this project is to design Chitosan modified polymeric nanoparticles of sorafenib for the treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma. The proposed dosage form will carry a significant amount of the drug to the target site crossing the various physiological barriers of the body, retain its therapeutic effect and will limit the toxic effects of conventional dosage forms. Conventional chemotherapeutic agents are associated with lack of temporal delivery, fluctuation in plasma concentration and ultimate response, poor patient compliance, repeated dosage, and increased side effects. These problems can be overcome by developing the nanoparticles formulations.
Biodegradable polymeric nanoparticles are highly preferred because they show promising effect in drug delivery system. Such nanoparticles provide controlled/sustained release property, subcellular size and bio-compatibility with tissue and cells. Polymeric nanoparticles (PNPs) increase the circulation half-life and reduce the phagocytic uptake and inactivation of the therapeutic moiety and can be used to deliver and target therapeutic agents. Nanoparticles are one of the novel drug delivery systems, which can be of potential use in controlling and targeting drug delivery. The nanoparticulate drug delivery systems seem to be a viable and promising strategy for the pharmaceutical industry. It will also increase the patient compliance.
Key Words: Formulation, PLGA, Targeting, Chitosan, Hepatocellular Carcinoma

data.projectName: Genomics assisted selection and propagation potential of elite Pinus gerardiana (Chilghoza) clones for marginal habitats of Pakistan.
data.projectDigest:
Ecosystem services are components of nature that contribute to maintenance of human well-being. People derive many essential goods from nature, yet linkages between biodiversity and ecosystem services and their roles are poorly understood. Mountain ecosystems support high biodiversity and are also home to ~12% of the global population. Pakistan is located between 34º to 37º North latitudes and 61º to 75 º East longitudes on an area of 87.98 million hectares. Pakistan prevailing environmental conditions from tropical to alpine tundra biome (K2 peak), supporting rich biodiversity, including Chilghoza (Pinus gerardiana) forests commonly known as “Neoza pine/Chilgoza”. In Pakistan Chilgoza has sparse distribution in the Hindukush and Suleman mountain ranges of 1800-3350m altitudinal variation. Pinus gerardiana has high ecological and economic importance. Pine nuts earns a high price not only in Pakistani markets but also internationally (1,5 & 9). Although collection of pine nuts is a source of livelihoods for local communities but this activity is also threatening the natural population of Chilghoza, especially by destroying the natural regeneration [6,7]. 
In Pakistan Pinus gerardiana is examined due to high anthropogenic pressure on Chilghoza forests for pine nut collection and deforestation. In past different studies were conducted either to assess the regeneration statues or conservation status [12,4,6, 1, 8 & 11] collection and trade [2,3] of P. gerardiana. But attention has not been given on the conservation this species through application of molecular approaches in the current climate change scenario.
There exists extensive diversity in taste, shape and size of the pine nuts, however no DNA based markers are existing that may facilitate identification of superior

data.projectName: E- Governance Paradigms and Enterprise Recourse Planning Projects In Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Enterprise Recourse planning (ERP) systems evaluation for performance enhancement in government sector organizations is a critical concept due to its varied nature from private concerns. In Pakistan though late but government sector innovation has been started in late 90s and is in a process of hi-fi technology applications implementations in its various departments. A few ERP implementations have been successfully made in a few government sector organizations like, Higher Education Commission (HEC), National Database & Registration Authority (NADRA), Oil and Gas Development Company Limited (OGDCL), Project for Improvement in Financial Reporting and Auditing (PIFRA), Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd (PTCL) and State Bank of Pakistan (SBP). Though these organizations are enjoying the success of their ERP but the below stated questions are still to be analyzed, what were their ideal outcomes by implementing ERP? What are their existing outcomes by adopting ERP implementation? Is there any gap between the ideal and existing outcomes, if so, what is that? In order to research this, we set our objective to explore the relationship of common performance enhancement factors in context of gap between existing and ideal ERP performance of government sector organizations of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Synthesis of calixarene based polymeric membranes and their environmental applications
data.projectDigest:
This research work is based on the synthesis of calixarene based cryogel membranes that will be economical, robust and highly selective for toxic metals. The most important feature of synthesized cryogels will be their non-toxicity and high capacity for toxic metals. Metals or metalloids (Cr, As, Cd, Hg, Tl, Pb, etc.,) are toxic either when they form poisonous soluble compounds or present in larger amounts.
Hence, there is great need to remove them from the environment. the decontamination of environment from toxic elements is different from organic toxins. However; the toxic metals may be made insoluble or collected possibly by the aid of chelating agents. Therefore, it is significant to synthesize calixarene based cryogel membranes, which will be thoroughly characterized in terms of their robustness, capacity, specificity, non-toxicity and morphology and can be utilized for the removal of toxic metals from aqueous environment.

data.projectName: Elucidation of termite Cel5B gene expressing E. coli employing water melon waste  for ethanol production
data.projectDigest: Growing international marketing and production have led to increasing accumulation of fruit waste in Pakistan. Though fruit, vegetable and food wastes being perishable are tried to disposed of safely such as incineration, dumping in landfills which leads to air and land pollution, yet the vast quantities in which they are generated as a result of diverse household and industrial practices, necessitates the requirement to look for some avenues where these can be utilized for some application. The waste represents one of the energy rich resources being organic in nature. Fruit waste serves as second generation biomass for production of ecofriendly bioethanol that is competitive to gasoline to cut off prices and overcome biofuel depletion.  For economically feasible lignocellulosic biotransformation, reduction of cost of cellulases and bioethanol production is one of the main challenges now a day. Truncated cellulases are considered a promising candidates.The ultimate goal is the elucidation of water melon waste by Cel5B expressing Escherichia coli encoding for cellulase to produce bioethanol. Cell5B gene product will be characterized to improve the cellulose conversion.The study emphasis on “energy from waste” with decreased demand and increased integration by managing low cost waste and will lead towards the reduced operating cost.

data.projectName: Invivo and Invitro study to analyze the wound healing and anticancer Potential of Natural Pakistani Honey and its isolated bioactive Compounds
data.projectDigest:
Honey is delicious natural product composed of components originated from flowers and salivary glands of honey bees. Many constituents may arise due to catalytic action of salivary enzymes. Honey is not only important due to its unique composition but also due to its tremendous therapeutic properties. Internationally a lot of work has been done and reported by different scientists on the nutritional and medicinal characterization of honeys from their respective localities. Phytochemical composition, antioxidants potential, acidic behavior and low moisture contents are responsible parameters for antimicrobial, therapeutic, anticancer and wound healing properties of this valued nutritional product. Present study is designed as an extension of previous study in which most of the natural Pakistani honeys were excellent antioxidant, antimicrobial and antitumor agents (by evaluating with potato disk assay). Honey contains bioactive compound like   amino acids, aroma compounds, phenolic compounds, flavors, flavonoids, aliphatic compounds, ascorbic acid, organic acids, terpenoids, norisoprenoids, and minerals. Honey is not only important due to its unique composition but also due to its tremendous therapeutic properties. Phytochemical constituents, antioxidants potential, low moisture contents and acidic behavior are the parameters responsible for antimicrobial, therapeutic, anticancer and wound healing properties of honey. 
Present study is designed to explore the wound healing and anticancer potential of natural Pakistani honeys. In this study honeys will be collected from different botanical and geographical origins. Wound healing properties will be evaluated by In Vivo trials on rats. Anticancer potential will be determined with the help of MTT assay and In Vivo trials on r

data.projectName: Proteome-wide Characterization of Drug Targets and Efforts to Circumvent Antimicrobial Resistance in Pakistan by addressing Emerging Pathogen
data.projectDigest: The project outcomes will strengthen the field by achieving desired therapeutics.  The emergence of multi-drug resistance has been rapidly driven by frequent use of antibiotics causing increase in the healthcare costs, morbidity and mortality rate worldwide.  Among them role of Gram-negative bacteria are clinically challenging while Pseudomonas resistant to wide range of antibiotics is our main focus. They commonly cause urinary tract infections and have shown resistance. The prevalence of Pseudomonas has been widely reported in Pakistan and globally, which has posed formidable therapeutic challenge.  Patients exhibiting increased catheterization and prolonged hospital stays are highly susceptible to multi-drug resistant infections. Persistent use of antibiotics assures that emergence of MDR pathogenic strains is a perpetual phenomenon. In past, various clinically approved drugs i.e. Captopril (antihypertensive) Saquinavir (HIV inhibitor), Aliskiren (Human renin inhibitor) etc. have been discovered through computer-aided drug design .  In silico  and in vitro analysis will be performed to identify therapeutic proteins that can be targeted to circumvent the pathogenic effects of Pseudomonas.  The outcomes of the proposed study include the identification of novel, safe and efficient therapeutics for emerging multi-drug resistant pathogens which is crucial step towards reducing rate of the mass population at a global level.

data.projectName: Synthesis and characterization of low cost hydrophobic geopolymeric membrane for desalination and aqueous solution concentrations
data.projectDigest: According to the IMF, Pakistan's per capita annual water availability is 1,017 cubic meters which is dangerously close to the scarcity threshold of 1,000 cubic meters which makes Pakistan a highly water scare country. Water desalination is the most viable option to solve this problem. Desalination through reverse osmosis is already at a well matured stage, however due to high applied pressure requirement; membrane distillation and Forward osmosis are getting attraction as membrane based water desalinations. The effectiveness of any membrane process depends in the membrane itself. Ceramic membranes are considered superior over polymeric membranes but they are expensive due to costly raw materials and high sintering temperature requirements above 1100 °C. Geopolymerization is a chemical processes that involves the reaction of aluminosilicates with aqueous alkaline solutions to produce inorganic binders called geopolymers. This method is also getting attraction for the synthesis of self-supporting inorganic membranes. Along with the benefits of sintering-free synthesis, it also utilizes fly ash as raw material which makes the membrane synthesis very cost effective and environment friendly.  In the present research work, a low cost geopolymeric membrane substrate will be synthesized using coal fly ash which is a waste of coal-fired thermal power plants.

data.projectName: Evaluation and Application of organic lectins for the control of insect pests
data.projectDigest:
Several undesired side effects of insecticidal on plant, fauna, environment and human health have been reported across the world. So scientists are shifting from chemical to natural insecticidal product. This project is also focus on the formulation of organic insecticidal. Among other organic compounds, plant lectins have been extensively studied for their different uses since their discovery in 1888. In the present study lectin from the different part of Allium cepa L. will be isolated. Isolated lectins will be checked for their different insecticidal properties. This Allium cepa lectin will be formulated and used in the field of cotton crop to evaluate its insecticidal effect.
In the second part of project, gene of lectin will be isolated and characterized and transferred to model variety of cotton. Crop will be evaluated in greenhouse condition. After approval from environmental protection department, field trial and breeding of crop will be done to select a good cultivar.

data.projectName: University Education and Occupational Skills Mismatch (A Case study of SME’s in Khyber Paktunkhwa)
data.projectDigest: This research aims to develop a discipline of soft skills needed for Pakistan. SMEs have a visible role and enormous impact on the development of every country. SME’s contribute to economic development of Pakistan in numerous ways. Regardless of the enormous value of an established SME’s sector, the government of Pakistan needs to focus and reprioritize more on the nurturing and development of SMEs to further gain extra economic benefits. This project sheds light towards a variety of important gaps and issues that have weakened the SME sector in Pakistan; the challenges range from skill mismatch between academia and industry. Which includes scarcity of skilled workforce and deficiency of advance technological framework and skill required for jobs; access to markets, limited exposure of SMEs to international market and limited capacity to explore new markets and resources and complicated or no access to financial facilities are visible challenge to SMEs sector. In view of these rooted weaknesses, the project has formulated interventions in the form of a policy framework to identify and curb the challenges arising in SME sector regarding skill mismatch. The policy framework for skill match encapsulates the recommendations for the Legislative Environment, Sectors Development Approach and Institutional Framework.

data.projectName: Explore and compare the teaching methodologies of two different school of thought: Local Education System vs. Cambridge School System. (A Case study of BISE Lahore and BISE federal)
data.projectDigest: There are numerous motives why societies need education. The key motive being, we need to be alert of things that disturb our life. There is an enormous field of education. Students can do engineering, MBBS, MBA, and MCS. An individual should choose their field of education at the stage of Higher Secondary. Higher secondary is the final stage that decides the future of the students either they are a doctor or engineers. At the stage of higher secondary, there are two schools of thoughts either students should go for FSc. or A level. The first question comes in mind that why inequality exists in education by introducing two schooling system in Pakistan. It is a basic assumption in our minds that competent and rich students did the A level. Other than these factors most of the other important factors should be considered and address that makes a better society. So, one of the most important resources is teachers. Therefore, this research project analyze and compare the teaching methodologies in local and Cambridge school system for two subjects (English and Mathematics). The main aim of this research project is to identify the reason for the unequal distribution of academic resources.

data.projectName: Information Sharing Behavior of, and the Use of Online Health Forums by, Patients with Chronic Diseases in Pakistan.
data.projectDigest:
Patients with chronic diseases, such as cancer and thalassemia, often have multiple problems and a reduced quality of life, and can spend a lot of their time worrying about their health condition and life span. The disease affects almost every aspect of their lives whether it is emotional, psychological, social or economic. For example, it can reduce their social activities in terms of having very limited or no social interactions with people. As a result, they may spend a lot of time alone and live in isolation, which can affect their morale and well-being, as well as the disease and treatment plan. 

The proposed research aims to explore the information sharing behaviour of, and the use of online health forums by, patients with chronic diseases (e.g., cancer, thalassemia) in Pakistan. 

The importance of the proposed study is significant in terms of exploring the patterns of sharing behaviours of patients with chronic diseases in Pakistan. As a result of this study, the researcher aims to propose a framework that will act as a guide towards the provision and identification of effective channels for patients with chronic disease and their families for socializing and sharing.

The importance of the proposed study is significant in terms of exploring the patterns of sharing behaviours of patients with chronic diseases in Pakistan. As a result of this study, the researcher aims to propose a framework that will act as a guide towards the provision and identification of effective channels for patients with chronic disease and their families for socializing and sharing.

data.projectName: Sensitive Colorimetric and Fluorimetric Detection of Metal Ions Using Nanoclusters
data.projectDigest:
Recently interest in development of sensors for detection of toxic metals in different matrices is increased and nanomaterials-based sensors have shown great ability in the detection of heavy metals ions. 
Noble metal nanoclusters (NCs) have recently been used for number of different applications, they have advantage of lower toxicity as compared to the organic dyes and quantum dots (QDs). There are two major problems encountered in synthesis and applications of metallic NCs first is aggregate formation which results in larger particles and second is low fluorescence quantum yield (QY) as that of the QDs. Methodologies are therefore required for synthesis of smaller particles with enhanced fluorescence efficiency. 
Modification with suitable ligand is reported to have positive effect on luminescence efficiency, however, still only few works are contributed to the fabrication of ultra-bright NCs. It is therefore very important to find out ligand which can enhance luminescence of NCs by modifying their surface With ligand modifications we anticipate a design route for synthesizing highly fluorescent metal nano-clusters with good fluorescence properties, smaller size, and low cytotoxicity. With appropriate modifications fluorescent metal NCs can be alternatives to QDs and traditional fluorophores for the development of molecular and ionic sensors.

data.projectName: Development and field evaluation of bioactive compost pellets fertilizer from restaurant food waste
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Restaurants food wastes are rich in plant nutrients but unfortunately these are wasted in Pakistan. We will develop innovative techniques for these wastes recycling. The restaurant food wastes will be processed through (i) aerobic composting, (ii) hyperthermophylic pretreatment composting and anaerobic digestion by using existing technologies with some modification according to local conditions. The high quality end products will be shade dried to maintain moisture content up to 40%. Subsequently, PGPRs will be added in it and bioactive compost pellets will be formed. Field evaluation of each type of bioactive compost pellets will be done for two consecutive years. The bioactive compost pellets from restaurant food wastes has not yet been formed and marketed in Pakistan. We will form those for the first time. This product will attract farmers due to its pellet shape with bioactive bacteria in it. It will replace bio-fertilizer and compost currently available in the market. This will be two in one product having PGPRs bacteria to solve problem of P-fixation in alkaline soils of Pakistan. Secondly, it will be rich in organic matter to improve soil structure and water holding capacity especially in marginal lands of Pakistan. This is future organic fertilizer of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Exploitation of plant residues biochars to promote soil fertility and quality of the arable lands of District Rawalakot, AJ&K
data.projectDigest:
According to Climate Change Intergovernmental Panel (IPCC), there is threshold of global warming beyond which current agricultural practices can no longer support large human civilizations. The project site is District Rawalakot that lies in northeast of Pakistan. Inappropriate inorganic fertilization and continuous removal of crop residues from the field and disposal by on-farm burning not only deplete off soil nutrients but also pose serious implications for agriculture and the environment of the area. 
Therefore, the project aimed to site-specific interventions through exploiting low and no cost plant residues as soil supplements or replacement to inorganic fertilizers. To achieve this objective, we plan to collect plant materials (trashes/crop residues) from the arable land for pyrolysis in furnace and kilns under oxygen-limiting conditions into biochars and amending with conducting series of laboratory, pot and field experiments to analyze their effect on soil properties and plant growth. The findings will deliver valuable information on transformation of large-scale agricultural waste disposal from environmental liability to a valuable asset. The policy makers, scientists and farmers will find a novel approach of disposing surplus crop residues by converting them into biochars and using as soil conditioners for better crop growth, mitigating the negative impacts of climate change on soil and environment.

data.projectName: Prospecting for enhanced drought tolerance, production, seed propagation and utilization of soybean in Pothwar
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Edible oil/oil seeds has become the second largest imported commodity of Pakistan after petroleum. Soybean is currently introduced as an oil seed crop in Pakistan and due to inclusion of poultry feed industry its imports are projected to 2.6 MMT. Soybean has become one of the most traded agricultural commodities worldwide and it is needed that Pakistan must produce its own soybean to fulfill requirements of poultry feed industry and edible oils.  The Government’s efforts for self-sufficiency in edible oil did not yield any tangible results due to existing cropping system where farmers opt more remunerative crops than oilseed crops. However, soybean can easily be incorporated in existing cropping system of Pothwar region where monocroping is prevalent. High yielding well adopted genotypes and effectual agronomics practices are essential for introduction of soybean in current cropping system of Pothwar. This project aims at: (1) collection of promising soybean germplasm and its evaluation for drought tolerance and higher yield; (2) optimization of agronomic practices for selected genotypes under rainfed conditions; (3) training of farmers for successful cultivation of soybean and to propagate their own seed of soybean; and (4) bringing the industry in the loop for procurement of the farmers’ soybean produce.

data.projectName: Tourism-A soft Power of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The real element of a successful policy of any state is not that how many enemies are punished through wars but it is about that how through soft-power previously adversaries are serving the state as friends. It is the soft power which influences others to be aliened and remain in a collaborative manner with one another that is to assure economic growth, sustainable development and most of all a soft image is a great catalyst in maintaining peaceful relation among states. The states exhibit soft-power through variety of ways; tourism is one a very powerful way that not only projects progressive image of respective state at international level but generates viable economic opportunities as well. Historically, Pakistan has been a choice for the international tourists but the post 9/11 developments halted the tourists to come to Pakistan due to ongoing war on terrorism that consequently dented both soft-image and economy of Pakistan. The ratio of foreigner tourist to Pakistan came down to its least number of recipients in 2014 and till today, Pakistan on the world tourist ranking is 125 out of 150 enlisted states. In the present world, an efficient tourism industry is too important for a state. Tourism in Pakistan has potential to help in creating a responsible soft image of country through projecting its culture and hospitality that ultimately would contribute a good amount of revenue to national economy additional to generating employment opportunities.

data.projectName: Synthesis and Characterization of High Entropy Films by Magnetron Sputtering System
data.projectDigest:
Materials are the basis of civilization, and alloy materials occupy a vital position in everyday life. Alloy design has consisted of combining single principal element with minor alloying elements to enhance the mechanical, chemical and/or structural properties Developments in Materials science critically depend on our ability to synthesize materials with the optimal properties for each individual application. 
High-entropy films (HEFs) are a new class of films, with the potential to realize excellent blends of mechanical, electrical and thermal properties unattainable by conventional films and attracting interest globally. 
Magnetron sputtering is the most developed technique for the preparation of HEFs, because a large quantity of thin films can be prepared at comparatively high purity and low cost. 
The project is based on the synthesis of high entropy films and study of their microstructural characteristics for exploration of mechanical properties. We already have setup of Magnetron Sputtering System. Through this project we are interested in 
•	Synthesis of HEFs
•	Characterization of prepared HEFs
•	Training of the students geared towards their PhD/ M.Phil. theses
•	Publishing the result of the research in peer-reviewed journals of international repute
•	Possible bridging university and industry collaboration for Exploring potential application of HEFs in power electronics and automobile industries
