data.projectName: Prototype mini RO-water purification plant with condition monitoring and integrated ozonation system
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: The clean water industry seeking a promising solution for the continuous supply of conditioned monitored pure water. The market supplied pure water has great ambiguity regarding the quality of pure water. The focus of this project is to design & develop a highly efficient and cost-effective pure water system. Reverse Osmosis (RO) purification technology is a competitive approach for both urban and remote locations.  Although, many designs of RO purification systems are available in the market with limitations regarding the condition monitoring of treated water parameters such pH, TDS, BOD, COD, toxic traces such as arsenic, E. coli and facial coliform on the control panel. In present conditions, the Reverse Osmosis (RO) plant is being controlled by solid state micro-controller devices. Each equipment has a micro-controller device which is to be checked simultaneously and frequently. PLCs based automation and control is used in many industries on different machines which have shown successful performance and operations. Whereas micro-controllers cannot withstand industry environment and can’t provide good results. The current design features of RO plant need to be improved to catch the confidence of the client and the proposed RO purification system will perform automatic condition monitoring as per suggested quality by WHO standards.

data.projectName: A facile route to novel graphene based materials for flexible supercapacitors
data.projectDigest: Flexible and wearable electronic devices such as super capacitors, electronic bio sensors, batteries, displays and memory devices attracted enormous attention and achieved rapid growth in recent years. Discovery of graphene and graphene based composites revolutionized the field of flexible electronics due to their Nano scale size, significant abundance and excellent performance. Therefore current frontier of energy storage devices has focused on the development of solid state super capacitor with flexible and wearable characteristics. The excellent electric and electrochemical efficiency, superior stability, light weight and small volume of graphene based flexible super capacitors can be potential candidate for the realization of flexible electronics.

data.projectName: Neurokinin B and attributes of infertile males: a cross sectional study in a subset of Pakistani Population
data.projectDigest:
Infertility is recognized as a social issue in all customs and societies. Approximately 10–15% couples of the reproductive age are affected by the infertility. Male infertility is the failure of male partner to accomplish pregnancy in a healthy/fertile female partner and it accounts for an estimated of 60% of couples with fertility related issues. Discovery of Neurokinin-B (NKB) in 2009 and identification of its receptor have added a new dimension to our understanding of the physiology of the reproduction and fertility.
We aim to determine whether the serum levels of NKB are associated with infertility by comparing the levels in fertile and infertile male subjects and to identify disease linked single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in TAC3 gene of infertile male cohorts. This cross-sectional study will be carried out on 270 males. The patient group will include males (230) with infertility problems aged 18-50 years and the control group include fertile/healthy males (40) of the same age range. Thorough clinical examination will be done to exclude those suffering from chronic health problems. Levels of NKB, Follicle Stimulating Hormone, Luteinizing hormone, Prolactin and Testosterone will be compared. Any polymorphism/mutation in protein exons of TAC3 in infertile group will be identified. A probable effect on genetic alterations in the TAC3 gene and its impact on the reproductive axis will be detected.

data.projectName: An Islamic Approach towards Prevention and Handling of Growing Cellphone Addiction among University Students; Transforming Harms into Benefits
data.piUniversity: National University of Modern Languages, Islamabad (NUML)
data.projectDigest: Cellphone has become the most personal item of an individual in our society that is equally difficult to part with. A huge chunk of more than 164 million cellular subscribers in Pakistan consists of youth. Despite all its benefits, unhealthy use of a cellphone may lead to various physiological, psychological, and social problems. During the past decade, a notable number of researches, surveys and reports has been performed worldwide to define the over-use of cellphones as addiction, to find reasons behind, to list symptoms and negative effects of, and to propose measures to prevent and treat this addiction. Some universities around the world limited the scope of these studies specifically around a set of their own students. The objective of this research is to estimate the scale of cellphone addiction among university students across Pakistan, comparison of various approaches toward addressing this issue and to devise an approach towards prevention and treatment of cellphone addiction based on Islamic principles specifically for university students. The research may be depicted through eight phases; Desk Review, Tool Development, Need Assessment Survey, Collecting data, Data analysis and interpretation, Module Development, Seminars, and Preparation of Final Report.. As a result, it is expected that the awareness among students regarding cellphone addiction would rise, a healthy use of cellphones within and outside of the campus would prevail, instead of negative activities, the students would use cellphones for gains in academic as well as financial fields improving their educational performance.

data.projectName: Climate smart pluses-based cropping systems in Punjab, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The research project “Climate smart pluses-based cropping systems in Punjab, Pakistan” will focus on determining the influence caused by climate change and variability on crop productivity, revenue generation, poverty and food security. Pluses are the most significant crops having impact on socio-economic conditions of farmer’s in Punjab, Pakistan. In additions to other determining factors, influence of climate change (CC) & variability and adaptation approaches for spring and autumn pluses have not been carried out in general in the country, particularly in Punjab, Pakistan. Farmers have very limited information regarding the climate smart farming practices. The elevated agricultural input prices and unexpected variations have induced the farmers to explore ways to get maximum net return from the available resources. Several adaptation strategies have been made in terms of evolving new varieties with higher growing degree-day’s requirements, improved crop management practices including fertilizer, irrigation and spraying system to maintain the interest of the farmers of the region. However, no significant research efforts have been carried towards integration of agronomic management practices and dominant changing climate and its variability. Keeping in view, significance of pluses, higher production and net return could only be achieved through adaptation of climate smart pluses production practices.

data.projectName: Exploring mutational signature in breast cancer patients of Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Medical University, Islamabad
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan, specialized laboratory testing facilities addressing genetic testing domain is limited. In this project, optimization of multi-gene mutation detection panel of 8 frequently mutated genes causing breast cancer is proposed. Federal Breast Cancer Screening Centre (FBCSC) is a state of the art facility present in PIMS hospital offering population wide breast cancer screening. It will be accomplished by initially recruiting patients (n=250) diagnosed with breast cancer at FBCSC, PIMS, Islamabad. Blood samples will be collected from patients with written informed consent. DNA will be extracted using phenol-chloroform method. A panel of genes including BRCA1, BRCA2, TP53, PTEN, CDH1, ATM, CHEK2 and PALB2 which have a substantial role in the breast carcinogenesis will be designed. These genes will be subjected to mutation analysis using targeted gene sequencing strategy. Sequence variants in candidate genes will be identified in breast cancer patients. The identified variants will be analyzed for pathogenicity using online prediction tools for deleterious mutations and variant of unknown significance. This information will help in optimization of an in-house gene mutation detection panel for novel and existing variants in aforementioned genes. After validation of specificity and sensitivity, multi-gene mutation testing panel will be offered to women attending FBCSC.

data.projectName: Enhancement in energy performance of microencapsulated phase change material (mPCM) slurry based Photovoltaic thermal system
data.projectDigest: Rapid increase in world energy use raised issues of exhaustion of nonrenewable energy resources, environmental impacts (greenhouse gases, ozone depletion, adverse climatic changes, etc.). Solar energy is one of the promising renewable energy resources. Recent advancements in photovoltaic materials and their increasing efficiencies can meet the increasing global energy demands but the rise in temperature of the panel during operation present a major impediment. About 5-15% of the incident radiation on PV cells is converted into electrical energy while remaining increases their temperature and converted into heat energy. This increase in temperature decreases the electrical efficiency of solar cells by 0.3% when cell temperature increases by 1?C.  Efficiency of PV cells can be increased by cooling them with natural or forced circulation of cooling media. The extracted heat from PV cells can be utilized for low temperature applications. Such systems which provide both the electrical and thermal energy are known as PV/T (photovoltaic thermal) systems.

data.projectName: An Analytical Study of Traditional Gender Roles and their Influence on Women's Life Living in Karachi
data.projectDigest: In a highly patriarchal society like Pakistan where men are supposed to be the supreme authority and women are considered as their subordinate, gender inequality and human rights violations against women are very common. This phenomenon has very serious implications on women’s and men’s daily life affairs and has deeply rooted in mostly Asian societies which results in discrimination of women and directly linked to gender-based violence with subsequent severe mental and physical health effects. Gender discrimination stems from social structures where cultural stereotypes are engrained in both genders and form the foundation of different life circumstances which they face. However, the gender discrimination and inequality vary from culture to culture. In Pakistan, gender roles are seen in the mirror of masculine and feminine traits of an individual which are constructed from the roots of tradition and social values based on the concepts of production and reproduction. Our focus in this study will be that gender inequality which manifests itself in a different manner according to culture, traditions, politics, religion and economic conditions, and is further strongly linked with violence against women. The main aim is to explore current gender roles, how these roles are reproduced and influence men’s and women’s life.

data.projectName: Screening of aflatoxin and value addition in milk to ensure the food safety in Sindh province
data.projectDigest: Occurrence of aflatoxin M1 in milk and milk products has a significant impact on the human health and currently it is most important issue in food safety. Therefore, proposed study will assess the presence of aflatoxin M1 in milk and milk products in Sindh province. For the representation of whole province, Sindh province will be categorized into three zones and three districts will be selected from each zone, ([Southern zone: Badin, Karachi and Thatta district], [Central zone: Shaheed Benazirabad, Hyderabad and Mirpur Khas district] and [Northern zone: Sukkur, Naushahro Feroze and Larkana district]). Proposed study is also a initiative for capacity building which includes, an awareness seminar regarding prevalence of aflatoxins in milk and milk products to aware the milk producers to improve the food safety and a training will be organized on manufacturing of milk products to enhance the skills of farmers to get maximum yield and to maintain the hygienic conditions during processing to ensure the food safety. Additionally, aflatoxin testing service will be started for the milk producers and this facility can be used by different research institutes of Sindh province for their future research projects.

data.projectName: Exploring the alternate medicine approaches for the treatment of glioblastoma multiform and its association with depression
data.projectDigest: In next five years, cancer is considered to take over all other diseases and will be the first leading cause of death worldwide. Brain cancer is involved in significant rate of cancer related death cases, and are seen to particularly affect children and young adults, causing about 30% and 20% of death incidences, respectively. Brain cancer is so deadly, that two out of three patients dies from this upon diagnosis. It needs efficient treatment option as resistance has been developed to the existing drugs. Drug repurposing or repositioning is a strategy that makes use of existing drugs for a new purpose or indications. Since it employs old drugs, it proves to be efficient and less costly as compared to new drug development. We aim to use marketed drugs (of blood pressure and stroke) to treat brain cancer. In addition, the risk factors for brain cancers are unknown but studies have reported its association with depression. Thus we also intend to see this relation of brain cancer with depression and how does the antidepressants plays its role in treating brain cancer. Since a lot of good antidepressants are already available, they cannot cross the barrier to reach to the brain. So we intend to encapsulate these drugs into nanoparticles (carriers) that will help in crossing the barrier to deliver the drug into brain. Since we will not directly work on humans, we will take the brain cancer out through surgery and will grow this cancer in our artificial incubators that will be used for different testing in our established laboratories.

data.projectName: Harvesting of omega 3 fatty acids from marine phytoplankton for developing functional food
data.projectDigest: Food requirement for world population is increasing day by day. Most effecting age group are children below age of five years. As kids grow functional disability progresses and affects children overall performance. Major reason is deficiency of essential nutrients in diet.  Mostly importantly lack of essential lipids in food. These lipids play a critical role in development of infants. Provision of sufficient quantity of these lipids can improve short term as well as long term functioning of physiological systems. Recently main objectives of emerging research is to increase these lipid content in food products. There are various dietary sources of lipids. Marine algae are primary source of these lipids. These phytoplankton are utilized by fish in oceans. Fish oil is being extracted from these fish and sell out in capsules. This method of fish oil extraction is quite expensive. Algal oil has more advantages over fish oil. Fish oil carries contaminants while microalgae are being grown on fresh water. Algal oil has enhanced greater benefits due to decreased time for production. Keeping in view benefits of algal oil current project is designed to develop transgenic microalgae having enhanced lipid. After harvesting, these fatty acids will be added to different foods.

data.projectName: Investigation of Anti-diabetic Potential and Metabolites Profiling of Polyphenol rich Medicinal Plants from Northern areas of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Diabetes Mellitus (DM) is one of the significant medical problems worldwide, which is caused by the inadequate secretion of insulin from the beta cells that might be due to the defect in the insulin discharge or resistance to insulin. Diabetes has been classified in to type I and type II, which severely affect the vital organs of the body and ultimately leads to retinopathy, nephropathy and neuropathy. Recently in 2017, it has been documented that 451 million people are suffering from diabetes around the world, however these statistics are expected to reach up to 693 million by 2045. Particularly, Pakistan with rapidly growing population the ratio of DM is 11.7% mostly affecting the younger population. In Pakistan more than 66% of the people living in rural parts of the country, having less excess to the medicines due to financial hurdles, lack of awareness and the affiliated adverse effects of synthetic medicines. Therefore, it is aimed to thoroughly investigate the unexplored medicinal plants of Northern areas of Pakistan using modern spectroscopic techniques and extensively unveil their anti-diabetic potential using in-vivo and in-vitro models, which could serve as safe, cost effective and easily available functional ingredients as phyto-pharmaceuticals against diabetes mellitus.

data.projectName: Vitamin D and oxidative stress: A reciprocal interplay in DNA damage and Repair
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Vitamin D, a pro hormone, has been reported to protect against the DNA damage. Oxidative stress generates reactive oxygen species. Our body has certain defense mechanisms to combat these reactive molecules. If left untreated, they have been involved in the generation of oxidized base adducts. These damages are corrected by certain DNA repair mechanisms. Previous data from Pakistan have reported that approximately 75-90% of the population is deficient of vitamin D. Since Vitamin D deficiency has shown to have a significant effect on increased oxidative stress, it can reflect an increased susceptibility towards DNA mutations and in turn a higher risk of developing multiple types of cancers. 
Vitamin D levels of healthy subjects will be analyzed along with oxidative stress status and DNA damage. Subjects will also be tested for their efficient DNA repair mechanism by the relative expression analysis of specific DNA repair enzymes.
The study aims to relate the vitamin D levels with the oxidative stress induced in relation to associated DNA damage and repair mechanisms. Being Vitamin D deficient population, this study will help to identify the risk factors related to DNA damage and thus reducing the susceptibility towards a range of physiological and metabolic diseases.

data.projectName: Smart Health Care System for Urban Periphery: A Prototype Model
data.projectDigest: The current project is aimed at providing a comprehensive model to ensure smart and efficient heath care system in Pakistan. Currently, the heath sector in Pakistan is beset with intricate challenges characterized by inefficient and poor service delivery system. Due to higher cost of private health sector, the major burden of health care is mainly on public hospitals, run and owned by the government authorities. Patients visiting public hospitals are more than the absorbing capacity. Therefore, they have to face numerous challenges. Inaccessibility of appropriate medicinal services in the government owned hospitals is a major reason of increasing number of deaths of general public in these hospitals.  To improve the existing situation and quality of services at public hospitals, this project can play catalytic role in various ways. Firstly, it is focused on compiling statistics on different health indicators. Secondly, this will contribute to understand the existing situation of health including the patterns of diseases, influx of patients in urban metropolis public hospitals, nature of facilities and challenges. Thirdly, the study will propose practical and sustainable measures for quality health system. The statistics will be used to establish need based centralized health unit in Islamabad as prototype model. This unit will be equipped with medical specialists who would be providing their consultation remotely to the patients in peripheral areas of Islamabad at their doorstep. This model can later be implemented in other cities.

data.projectName: IoT and AI in Precision Agriculture: Designing Smart System to support illiterate Farmers
data.projectDigest: According to the Economic Survey of Pakistan 2018-19 that the performance of agriculture remained gloomy. Its growth was just 0.85% against the target of 3.8%.  The under-performance of  agriculture is due to crop failures, unpredictable yield due to diseases, climatic variations and loss of soil fertility. However, “illiteracy” is one of the overlooked aspect of it. In Pakistan, mostly farmers are illiterate. It is difficult to introduce them new farming techniques. Further, decision maker do not pay attention on local knowledge and ideas, therefore new schemes do not get attention by illiterate farmers. They need the latest technologies to get information about weather pattern, seeds, pesticides, problem facing their peer group, latest prices, updates and farming related banking services. In this context, illiterate farmer needs platform to share their ideas and get updated information. The goal of this research is to disseminate the agricultural information to illiterate farmer through latest technologies. This research will provide graphic and audio contents to illiterate farmers through Internet of Things (IoT) Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML) and wireless communication. Farmers will be able to get digitally record information about their yield, production cycle, water management and pesticide control.

data.projectName: Synthesis, targeted delivery and evaluation of tubulin polymerization inhibitors
data.projectDigest:
Cancer is a defect in the cell division cycle and angiogenesis (formation of new blood vessels) is considered to be one of the main important factors involved in the metastasis (spreading to other sites) of cancerous cells. 
Vascular disrupting agents (VDAs) make ideal anti-cancer drugs as there are significant morphological, anatomical and behavioral differences between tumour and normal blood vessels. VDAs target the dividing endothelial cells that form the growing tumour blood vessels, in effect starving the tumour of blood and nutrients. VDAs mainly consist of flavonoids and tubulin binding agents such as combretastatin A1/A4. The discovery of combretastatin A-4, a tubulin-binding compound that induces apoptosis in proliferating endothelial cells and causes tumour vascular shutdown, has focused attention onto the re-direction of tubulin inhibitors to target tumour angiogenesis/vasculature rather than the tumour itself, on the basis that a solid tumour cannot survive or develop without a viable blood supply. Nevertheless there are difficulties associated with the selective delivery of these agents to the tumour site. Strategies that have been adopted to date for the selective targeting include the macromolecular conjugates (polymers etc), preparation of phosphate ester and amino acid based prodrugs and antibody drug conjugates. The strategy proposed here for the targeted delivery is to exploit the selective expression of aminopeptidase N (APN) on tumour vasculature undergoing angiogenesis but not quiescent vasculature and secondly APN inhibitors prevent endothelial cell migration to the tumour site. The research proposed here  involves the synthesis and targeted delivery of novel tubulin inhibitors as vascular disrupting agents.

VDAs mainly consist of flavonoids and tubulin binding agents such as combretastatin A1/A4. The discovery of combretastatin A-4, a tubulin-binding compound that induces apoptosis in proliferating endothelial cells and causes tumour vascular shutdown, has focused attention onto the re-direction of tubulin inhibitors to target tumour angiogenesis/vasculature rather than the tumour itself, on the basis that a solid tumour cannot survive or develop without a viable blood supply. Nevertheless there are difficulties associated with the selective delivery of these agents to the tumour site. Strategies that have been adopted to date for the selective targeting include the macromolecular conjugates (polymers etc), preparation of phosphate ester and amino acid based prodrugs and antibody drug conjugates. The strategy proposed here for the targeted delivery is to exploit the selective expression of aminopeptidase N (APN) on tumour vasculature undergoing angiogenesis but not quiescent vasculature and secondly APN inhibitors prevent endothelial cell migration to the tumour site. The research proposed here  involves the synthesis and targeted delivery of novel tubulin inhibitors as vascular disrupting agents.

data.projectName: In silico and In vivo exploration of Medicinal Plants against Food-Borne Microbial Toxins
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Foodborne diseases caused by microbial pathogens are a worldwide leading cause of morbidity and mortality among humans. Some foodborne diseases are related to the ingestion of foods infected with both natural and microbial toxins, as these toxins adversely affect food quality and safety. Strategies are needed to develop food compatible conditions to neutralize the bacterial, fungal, and plant toxins. Considering the urgent need to reduce the levels of toxic compounds and improve the quality of foods, we have planned this project with interdisciplinary approaches. The main objective of our research is to identify and develop the various green inhibitors that neutralize or down regulate the toxin-related pathways. We plan to achieve our proposed goal by modeling of toxin-inhibitor interactions using computational approaches like homology modeling, molecular docking and simulation studies accompanied by in vitro and in vivo exploration and confirmation of the inhibitory effect of potent natural compounds against selected food toxins. In addition, we will use the microbial biotransformation approach to generate green analogs with more selectivity. Since this project is an amalgam of various fields (Bioinformatics, Microbiology, and natural product chemistry), It is believed It will facilitate the design of new low-cost, indigenous products that effectively target the microbial food toxins.

data.projectName: Indigenous design and development of district space heating system with CSP Integration
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: The current energy demand in the buildings sector (e.g. space heating and domestic hot water) is often met by from fossil fuels as primary energy source and, consequently, this sector plays a role in the production of pollutant emissions [7]. The solar energy seems to be the most promising alternative energy source compared to fossils among all renewable energy sources and, therefore, central solar heating plants have received a great attention in literature. Nevertheless, the main drawback of solar energy is its intermittence as they fluctuate based on daily, weekly and seasonally basis. As a result, a mismatch between the energy demand and supply is frequently observed. The greatest mismatch is the one between the solar heat availability in summer and the high space heating demand in districts during winter season. Among several storage techniques, thermal energy storage (TES) seems as one of the promising technologies that can bridge the gap of intermittency in solar energy [1,2]. TES systems store the excess power generated from an intermittent energy source and makes it available on-demand in the required amount, when and where it is required. Thereby, these TES systems offer the answer to the temporal mismatch between the energy demand and supply. These systems are common in a wide range of applications. Such applications are building applications (district heating and cooling, domestic hot water, etc.) and industrial applications (storage of waste heat in chemical industries. As a large country with increasing amount of space heating loads in commercial and domestic buildings, district space heating has an expanding large market in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Development of live attenuated vaccine of Salmonella Gallinarum to control fowl typhoid
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Fowl typhoid (FT) is an acute disease of poultry and caused by Salmonella  Gallinarum  that possess a substantial threat to Pakistan’s poultry industry. Poultry industry is the largest industry in Pakistan. In spite of all modernization, technical expertise, and huge market, many farmers are getting out of their businesses due to infectious diseases. Among these, bacterial diseases particular fowl typhoid (FT) is the main area on worries for stakeholders. In Pakistan, Salmonella is being transfer through the parent stock in the broiler. The main hindrance in the export of broiler meat is Salmonella. Therefore, there is requirement that broiler meat should be free from Salmonella which plays an important role in food borne diseases. Some imported vaccines against fowl typhoid are being used in field, but they are not cost effective. Therefore, there is a urgent need of  a novel live attenuated vaccine that will not revert to virulent strains and protect against the disease. In this proposed project, local isolate of Salmonella Gallinarum which has high impact, will be isolated from local areas of Pakistan. This locally developed vaccine will be got patent in Pakistan which will be produced by local industry to generate turnover of about 400 million rupees annually by selling these vaccines.

data.projectName: Oral and Transdermal Skin Delivery of Nanomaterials as Potential Guards against Skin Problems (Nano-Cosmetics)
data.projectDigest:
Project is hypothesized to provide solution for aging (both external and internal). Skin’s structural integrity is preserved by collagen. Collagen is insoluble fibrous protein present in dermal extracellular matrix and connective tissue where it strengthens skin. Excessive ROS (reactive oxygen species) production damages skin as they oxidatively damage cells, resulting in breakdown of collagen. Degradation of ECM (extra cellular matrix) by matrix metalloproteinase (MMPs) leads to loss of tensile skin strength while collagen synthesis is activated. Suggested emulsion / drug composition of formulation contains peptide chains that penetrate viable skin layers where they restore collage and elasticity of skin. Natural extracts will inhibit activity of enzymes involved in ECM degradation such as MMPs (collagenase and gelatinases). This activity will be checked by ELISA using Collagenase activity assay, Collagen synthesis assay and Hyaluronic Acid synthesis assay. Furthermore, project aims to formulate a cream or drug which induce skin lightening by dispersing melanin.
Oral intake of synthesized peptides will enhance moisture content of stratum corneum, enhancing moisturizing ability of skin. Peptides when digested produce Hydroxyproline (Hyp) raising expression of ?-glucocerebrosidase and serine palmitoyltransferase-2 enzymes responsible for synthesis of ceramide in stratum corneum. This offers anti-aging and skin benefits by restoring skin hydration and elasticity.
Nanomaterials in form of emulsion / drug are useful in skin protective creams like sunscreens. Optical quantum dots will be used which reflect and absorb UV rays and natural plants extracts having ability to donate free electron and hydrogen to free radicals for protecting Skin Matrix.

data.projectName: Unified Medical Records and Analytics System (UMRAS)
data.projectDigest: It is usual practice of patients of chronic diseases to keep manual copies of their health records and present them to clinicians for consultancy. These practices have many drawbacks for patients and is especially limiting to clinician and medical policy makers as they have poor tracking of these patients. Electronic Health Records (EHR) is a structured mechanism of collection of patient’s health records in digital form. This form is convenient and more productive as the consolidated EHR can provide better insights to the clinician and the patient is free from hassle of paper work. The clinician can obtain other kind of statistics from patient’s health records in digital form and can make informed decisions. These health records can be stored and accessed across different network services in the form of fog computing services. These records can maintain patient’s demographic details, medical history, immunization status, allergies & medications, laboratory test, radiology images and other statistics. The proposed system will provide an interface for collection and integration of this medical data which can be used for intelligent healthcare analytics and design of clinical decision support system. These decision support systems will help the clinician to obtain healthcare warnings.

data.projectName: Turbulent and Laminar Analysis of Contaminant Transportation in Soils using Fractional Calculus
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest:
The Contaminant transport in soils is an important type of environmental contamination. Major causes of soil (land) contamination are; the xenobiotic elements by human, land-sliding, earthquake and/or flood etc. Anthropogenic sources such as, industrial, agricultural and waste disposal activities are non-natural ways of damaging the soil due to the existence of pollutants and stained elements in soil. 
From dynamical perspective, it is very natural to quantify any mathematical framework which captures the important aspects of contaminant transportation. This consideration has affirmative answers in literature as the pollutant’s transportation from higher to lower concentrations in soil is governed by the well-known advection dispersion (Diffusion) equation. In general, for one dimensional case, transport equation for pollutants in soil is  widely used to study the transport of contaminant in soils in the literature.
With the evolution of fractional Calculus, it is now worthwhile to study contaminant transport model using fractional derivative operator. Many complex rheological structures require fractional derivative operators for their governing equations. In this project, I will try to impart the effect of fractional derivatives on soil pollutant phenomenon and will study some graphical illustrations using MATHCAD. We will study the Contaminant fractionalized model using suitable initial and boundary conditions.
Moreover, a control analysis will also be observed on the concentration being transported in the land. We will try to study thoroughly about a maximum bound of concentration which can be achieved for the soils contamination using integral equations. In the end we shall try to study turbulent causes and
 effects on soil contamination.

data.projectName: Refractory Metal-Based Nanophotonic Coatings as Standalone Solar Energy Converter for Water Desalination and Heating
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest:
Contribution to overcome energy crisis and, water desalination and heating are major issues of the country in general and regional in particular, and salient features of the proposed research. It would be of great interest to develop technologies for cleaning and heating water both economically and resourcefully by using only natural light. To meet this challenge, a device will be fabricated to harvest solar energy efficiently and then use it in cleaning and heating water.
Complete absorption of incident light photons is desired in all photo-energy conversion processes. This proposal aiming at developing novel nanophotonic structured coatings of titanium-aluminum-nitride (TiAlN) by reactive magnetron sputtering system. Their composition, optical, electrical and structural properties will be optimized. The optimized coatings can manipulate all incident radiations. Further, appropriate stability of light absorbing coatings is desirable for device applications. For this purpose, the optimized coatings will be tested under adverse conditions, like elevated temperature, highly humid environment, thermal shock, and UV irradiation. Refractory metals based coatings are expected to withstand against severe conditions. In summary, development of proposed perfect absorbers with robust stability and intrinsic benign capability has huge scope for scientific as well as commercialization to attract considerable attention.

data.projectName: design and development of inexpensive and efficient hole transport layer material compatible for the perovskite solar cells
data.projectDigest:
The growing concern regarding the global warming and the depletion of the fossil fuels resources necessitates the search and development of the non-conventional and renewable energy sources.   However, most of the newly developed energy sources are beset with environmental pollution or other harmful effects on biosphere. The need of the hour is to improve the living standard without deteriorating the environment. Among the areas fulfilling the above conditions are fuels cells, water splitting and solar cells. Solar cells are among the easily maintained and least expensive of the above mentioned areas. Moreover, these are more suitable for majority of the areas of Pakistan which are exposed to sun. 
The currently used solar cells (copper-indium-gallium selenide and silicon-cadmium telluride solar cells) have a maximum power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25 %. The low efficiency has been attributed to the low transfer rate of the excited electron/hole from the photo-active material to the electron/hole transporting material (HTM). We have designed a HTM which has a comparable band gap to that of the valence band edge of the photo-active material (perovskite). This will lead to efficient and facile charge transfer to the HTM and enhanced PCE of the perovskite solar cells.

data.projectName: Development and Validation of loop-mediated isothermal amplification assay for Rapid detection of Mycobacterium avium subspecies Paratuberculosis in Small Ruminants in Punjab, Pakistan.
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Paratuberculosis is an infectious disease affecting many animal species including sheep, goats. In these animals disease is caused by a bacterium known as Mycobacterium  avium subspecies paratuberculosis. This disease is of socio-economic  importance  as it affects the dairy production and reproduction. The disease can be spread via contaminated feces to other animals and in young ones  through colostrum.  In this study different epidemiological factors that influence the disease prevalence in small animals will be studied.  Total 600 sheep, goats at four slaughterhouses of district Jhang will be focused in this study.  Diseased tissue samples, blood and feces will be collected and transported to department laboratory for further investigation.  in addition to histopathology of tissue, antibody detection through ELISA, a new  efficient and rapid technique, loop mediated isothermal amplification assay (LAMP) first time  will be used for  diagnosis of Paratuberculosis. The study will provide the baseline for future researchers for  further investigation and commercial use of this tool for efficient and  better disease diagnosis in animals. The proposed project will also update the knowledge about the current status of disease in sheep and goats.

data.projectDigest: Phosphorus (P) holds the key position amongst crucial players considered indispensable for achieving the future crop production goals. Its fertilization is the considered one of the fundamental components of crop nutrition. Deficiency of P in crop plants is wide spread due to low inherent levels of global and Pakistani soils coupled with its low bioavailability and immobilization. High pH and carbonate contents of our local soils further exasperate the situation. There is dire need for adaptation of strategies that can improve P use efficiency of crops from its inherent and applied sources. To achieve this, a series of experiments will be conducted including a wire house trial for screening of canola cultivars for estimation of agronomic phosphorus use efficiency under different phosphorus levels. Screened cultivars will be categorized on the basis of low, medium and high P use efficiency (PUE). During second year trials (Experiment II) three cultivars with low, medium and high (PUE) will be selected and grown under field conditions to enhance PUE with phosphorus solubilizing bacteria (PSB). Treatments will include different canola cultivars C1: having low PUE, C2: having medium PUE and C3: having high PUE and. phosphorus levels along with PSB. In experiment III, effect of biochar in combination of different sources of P on its use efficiency will be checked. Data regarding root characterization, shoot, yield and yield components, phosphorus uptake and PUE will be collected by using standard procedures, techniques and methods and will be statistically analyzed for comprehensive information. Deficiency of P in crop plants is wide spread due to low inherent levels of global and Pakistani soils coupled with its low bioavailability and immobilization. High pH and carbonate contents of our local soils further exasperate the situation. There is dire need for adaptation of strategies that can improve P use efficiency of crops from its inherent and applied sources. To achieve this, a series of experiments will be conducted including a wire house trial for screening of canola cultivars for estimation of agronomic phosphorus use efficiency under different phosphorus levels. Screened cultivars will be categorized on the basis of low, medium and high P use efficiency (PUE). During second year trials (Experiment II) three cultivars with low, medium and high (PUE) will be selected and grown under field conditions to enhance PUE with phosphorus solubilizing bacteria (PSB). Treatments will include different canola cultivars C1: having low PUE, C2: having medium PUE and C3: having high PUE and. phosphorus levels along with PSB. In experiment III, effect of biochar in combination of different sources of P on its use efficiency will be checked. Data regarding root characterization, shoot, yield and yield components, phosphorus uptake and PUE will be collected by using standard procedures, techniques and methods and will be statistically analyzed for comprehensive information. data.projectName: Computational Development of Materials for Alternate and Renewable Energy Applications
data.projectDigest: The purpose of this research proposal is to develop efficient hydrogen storage materials. They can reduce our dependence on fossil fuels which are not only going to deplete but also are threatening the living species through global warming. This work will be based upon the broad computational materials science to understand crystalline and amorphous materials using state-of-the-art quantum mechanics approaches. The acquired knowledge of the project team for alternate and renewable energy resources from theory and computation will be used to find new and novel promising materials for clean energy applications. The advanced research on alternate and renewable energy technologies has national importance. Therefore, we propose the computational study of materials in energy applications. During this research we will focus on the problems associated with the hydrogen storage. We will use density functional theory calculations to explore potential complex hydrides, chemical hydrides and nanomaterials in which hydrogen is either physiosorbed or chemically bonded into metal ions which will lead to the development of efficient fuel cells for automobile industry and other relevant industrial applications. The main reason for the lack of research in this area in Pakistan is unavailability of high performance computational facilities. To the best of our knowledge, there is no such public research laboratory equipped with high performance computational resources in Pakistan that is working on this significant research area. So, one of the research objectives is to develop computational materials research group in Pakistan. Another objective is to find/simulate the promising hydrogen storage materials in the Institute of Space Technology (IST), Islamabad, Pakistan.

data.projectName: Mainstreaming Religious Education through Vocational Training of Madrassa Students
data.projectDigest: This will be a plan for vocational skill building of Madrassa students and to prepare them for the modern job market. The over-arching research objective of the program is to identify skills and locate evidence that can align the skill set of the madrassa youth with the modern job market, specifically the IT sector to drastically reduce the susceptibility of extremism and radicalization of the students in targeted Madrasas and expand their development choices and opportunities for better integration in the job market. The Program will develop inclusive and gender sensitive selection criteria for learners to ensure gender parity in program participation. Research evidence for education and training will allow Madrassa youth to develop demand driven technical skills, workforce readiness skills and, where necessary, functional literacy and numeracy skills.

data.projectName: Assessment of compatibility between dried extracts of Arnebia hispidissima plant and pharmaceutical excipients by TG and DTA.
data.projectDigest: Arnebia hispidissima is a perennial grass of the family Boraginaceae. Pharmacologically and biologically the Arnebia species has antibacterial, antitumor, anti-inflammatory, antifungal, antiviral–HIV activities. Thus this study aimed to investigate the affinity of Arnebia hispidissima extract with different adjuvants by thermogravimetry and differential thermal analysis (TG/DTA). Thermogravimetric (TG and differential thermal gravimetric (DTG) are used for the pre-formulation or drug–adjuvant interactions and have attracted much attention of the researchers. The plant extract is dried with spray dryer and its binary mixtures with the pharmaceutical excipients are prepared in various proportions and analyzed with TG/DTG techniques under different ranges of temperatures and the TG curve of the dry extract showing different steps of degradation at different temperature ranges, corresponding to different mass loss. From the different stages of thermal decomposition, the %age of the adjuvant and the extract be determined, providing information about the blending proportion of the adjuvant with the dry extract and hence the extract-adjuvant compatibility. The composition and shape of the dry extracts will also be examined using FT-IR spectroscopy and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The current approach deals with the significance of using analytical techniques to evaluate the potential of the herbal drugs in pre-formulation.

data.projectName: Synthesis and characterization of new Gold(III) complexes with enhanced anticancer activity and potentially reduced side effects
data.projectDigest: Cisplatin is an anticancer drug used for the treatment of various types of cancers including breast, ovarian, cervical, prostrate, brain, lung cancers, etc. Despite of its incredible success as anticancer drug, cisplatin has severe side effects including bone marrow suppression, hearing disorders, kidney problems, vomiting, numbness, trouble walking, allergic reactions, electrolyte problems and heart diseases. Therefore, interest for the invention of new anticancer compounds is a hot area for researchers. In this context, gold(III) which has resembling electronic structure with platinum(II) is expected to be next generation anticancer drug molecule. Recently, gold(III) complexes have attracted considerable attention of researchers due to their strong antitumor activity and reduced side effects. We will design, synthesize and characterize new series of gold(III) drug compounds. After systematic characterization, compounds will be tested for anticancer activity and side effects on human cancer cells. The project outcomes will help us to develop new generation of anticancer drug compounds for chemotherapy with least side effects and improved efficiency than commercially available anticancer drugs.

data.projectName: Delivery of Newcastle Disease Virus DNA Vaccine through Nanoparticles for Effective Drug Therapy
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Newcastle disease is major viral disease of poultry which is clinically similar to avian influenza, therefore, has greatest economic impact on poultry industry.  Inspite of intensive vaccination programs to prevent chickens from being infected with this deadly virus by active  immunization with live attenuated vaccines to newly hatched chickens, chicken flocks infected with NDV still occur throughout the world. The emergence of a wide spectrum of variant strains in US and very virulent strains in Europe has been resulted from the failure of protection by current vaccines in broilers even with high levels of protective measures. In China and Pakistan, where protection levels are considered low and faring is substandard, the Newcastle disease becomes more serious and causes heavy economic losses. This all necessitate the development of novel approaches and alternative control strategies according to geographical situation of the country. As an alternative strategy, DNA vaccine, with the advantages of security, simplicity in producing and applying and the ability of inducing both humoral  and cellular immunity, draws attention from the researchers all over the world. DNA mediated vaccination refers to the induction of immune responses to a protein expressed in vivo subsequent to the injection of a plasmid DNA carrying an antigen-coding gene under a mammalian promoter. . Here we extend study of DNA vaccine by development of magnetic nanoparticles Fe3O4 coated with glutamic acid or Chitosan, which could be capable of overcoming the barrier to the cell membrane transport of DNA. This would be first of its kind of study for using NDV DNA vaccine in combination with nanoparticles for effective drug therapy.

data.projectName: Leaf Deep: In Silico Development of Leaf Image Database and Smart Morphological Diagnosis and Management of Major Diseases in High Values Crops
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest: Agriculture is the single most important occupation adopted by human beings for food and other products. Major cause of crop production losses are plant diseases which are 40% yield decline in each year. The use of traditional practices, inadequate plant protection measures and lack of adoption of modern technologies may be the cause cotton, mango, tomato and wheat yield decline in Pakistan.In proposed project an efficient, effective, intelligent and smart framework will be developed to automate the process of early disease detection and management as well as predicating next stage damages using leaf images. It is expected that this model would be first and innovative solution for farmer/ growers in Pakistan for providing the accurate and precise detection of their crop diseases that ultimately would be useful to adopt the management practices for proper and well in time. The information generated from this research project will be crucial in understanding the emergence of new technologies for identifying crop diseases as well as the management of these diseases and their impact on crop production in Southern Punjab. This study will be further helpful to develop environment-friendly and sustainable disease management packages for farmer/growers/researchers in Pakistan

data.projectName: Valorization of potato waste and sugarcane bagasse into bioplastic composites as food packaging materials
data.projectDigest: This research proposal is aimed to develop a method for the preparation of potato starch-based bioplastics. Almost 10-30% of potato consist of potato peel, which becomes the part of waste. These potato peels can be used for the production of bioplastics after extraction of starch. The only constraint in application of starch based thermoplastic polymers is their delicacy and low moisture barrier properties. The incorporation of the cellulosic nanofibers can significantly improve the mechanical properties of starch-based bioplastics without effecting their inherent biodegradation characteristics. Cellulose is most abundant naturally occurring biopolymer and an excellent source of nanofibers for use as strengthening agent. Integration of the cellulosic nanofibers is aimed to improve the mechanical properties of starch-based bioplastics. In current research project potato peel will be used as feedstock for the extraction of starch which will be transformed into bioplastics. Sugarcane bagasse will be used for the preparation of nanocellulose fiber, to be incorporated into starch-based bioplastics in order to improve their mechanical and moisture barrier properties. Cellulosic nanofibers will be characterized for their morphological properties and composition. Fabricated bioplastics will be tested for their mechanical, physical and thermal properties. On the conclusion of the project we will be able to use agricultural wastes for the production of ecofriendly bio-based plastics for packaging of food products and other related applications.

data.projectName: Integration of photovoltaic solar systems with greenhouses: Techno-economic assessment through modeling and field experimentation
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is facing major challenges around the sustainable supply of energy, food, and, water. One of the innovative approaches towards locally addressing food-energy challenges are PV greenhouses (PVG) – an intelligent system that integrates clean energy production with greenhouse farming. PVG is a dual production system that delivers solar energy and high value food production while sharing the same land/structure. A key motivation behind PVG is to deliver the maximum food-energy-water productivity from land and structure. A well-designed PVG can locally generate enough electricity to precisely control the greenhouse climate, provide supplemental LED lighting (if needed) for crops, and to deliver the surplus clean energy to rural households & agricultural. There is currently no assessment of the technology in Pakistan so far. Establishing a quantitative assessment of PVG is urgent for Pakistan where greenhouse farming has already been growing rapidly while a large surge of solar energy deployments is anticipated. We aim to develop a techno-economic model for assessment and design optimization of PVG for different agro-ecological climate zones across Pakistan using field experiments and modeling. Optimization will be done to obtain the best system configuration. (e.g., panel architecture & technology, % coverage and suitability for a given crop).

data.projectName: Vision-Based Recognition of Invasive Insects Under Unconstrained Flying Conditions
data.projectDigest:
Tremendous socio-economic impact of honeybee (Apis mellifera) has always been a driving force for struggle to preserve and breed this beneficial species. According to recent estimates, the honeybee may contribute nearly half of the global crop pollination services. Second important contribution is in the form of honey. In Pakistan, the production value of pollinated dependent crops is quantified up to 1.59 billion US$. On the other hand, beekeeping sector in Pakistan has honey production capacity up to 10,000 Metric Tons per annum.
One of the most terrifying threats to honeybees is the invasive hornet, Vespa spp. that prey primarily upon honeybees. In Pakistan, the beekeepers take prime quality honey [Berry] in October. If the hornet, Vespa spp. attack is there, the foraging force of box (beehive) is eliminated resulting in no honey harvest in Berry Nectar Flow season. The aim of the research work is to develop a computer vision-based recognition model and threat prediction model to recognize Vespa spp. under unconstrained flying conditions near beehives.
The proposed solution may become the basis of a truly non-intrusive real time embedded application that may help the beekeepers by raising an early alarm in the months of March-April by recognizing the hornet queens.Based upon the prediction model the beekeeper can have better future planning for selection of the honey harvesting area, thus contributing to the socio-economic growth of the country.

data.projectName: Economic Analysis and Trade Potential of Dates Fruit Production: Evidence from Sindh Province
data.projectDigest: Agriculture plays a pivotal role in the growth of any state. Agriculture provides raw materials to many industries which form the backbone of the nation. Most importantly, it helps a nation to strive by providing food and other agrarian products. Pakistan, for example, which is primarily an agrarian country, has a bulk of the working population engaged in agricultural activities. Among minor crops dates fruit is considered as an important cash crop of Pakistan and also has an economic importance. Pakistan grows a number of varieties of dates palm fruit, notably Sindh province alone produces 300 varieties of dates fruit.  However, this important sector faces a number of barriers in production and export, among others one is the lack of diversification of global buyers. A heavy share of Pakistani dates fruit being exported to India, on the other hand India has started their own production before a couple a years and to support the local production they have imposed a heavy duty on Pakistani dates that is an alarming situation for Pakistan. Similarly, many other barriers are also there, that needs to be settled on the government level.

data.projectName: Digital media Vigilance Sytem For Media Industry
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Advertisements displayed in TV broadcast are important part of transmission as majority of revenue for a broadcaster is generated by advertising. Tools that may perform fast and accurate advertisement discovery is a challenging task. The challenge for advertisement detection is lack of legislation for media industry in Pakistan that ensures the separate identification of advertisements and other programs. 
The objective of this research is to develop a system for TV commercials detection that may be used for the Media regulatory authority i.e. PEMRA, TV broadcasters and Advertising auditing agencies etc. The system can be used to identify specific TV commercial(s) for any further investigations.

data.projectName: Isolating the effects of climate change and human activities on streamflow in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Climate change and human activity are two major drivers that alter hydrological cycle processes and cause change in spatio-temporal distribution of water availability. Streamflow, the most important component of hydrological cycle undergoes variation which is expected to be influenced by climate change as well as human activities such as modification of land use/land cover (LULC), industrialization, and urbanization. Since these two affecting conditions are time dependent, having unequal influence, identification of the change point in natural flow regime is of utmost importance to separate the individual impact of climate change and human activities on streamflow variability. Subsequently, it is important as well for framing adaptation strategies and policies for regional water resources planning and management.

data.projectName: Biodegradation of chicken feather waste by microbial enzymes to control environmental hazards
data.projectDigest: Chicken Feather waste is the most abundant keratinous material in the nature produced with high amounts in poultry slaughterhouses and contains 91% of b-keratin. It was recorded that, the daily accumulation of feather waste reached to five million tons around the world which are generally disposed of in dumps, land filled or burnt in incinerators that produced huge environmental pollution which leads to various health hazards. Feather waste is a potential renewable source to recover valuable products because it is being a rich source of keratin proteins and amino acids. It can be used to make feather meal, fertilizer and yarn sizing agent. Thus the need for processing of feather and usage of its value-added products gives us a new area of research. Processing of feather by traditional methods are cost and labor intensive and  reduce the nutritional value of the products by destroying important amino acids. So the investigation of alternative technology is need of current times. This study mainly focused on the economical and pollution free efficient biodegradation of chicken feather waste via microbial enzymes. So in this study, we basically focused on the optimization and development of new methodology for economical and pollution free efficient biodegradation of chicken feather waste that convert the waste into useful byproduct that further utilized for various purposes.

data.projectName: Evaluation of Dynamic Soil Properties for the Seismic Ground Response Analysis of Peshawar and Islamabad
data.projectDigest: Earthquakes can cause extensive damages to life-lines and buildings and result in substantial loss of life. An assessment of dynamic deformation characteristics of soils is critical for computing the seismic response in any region. The ground response analysis (GRA), based on the actual site-specific dynamic soil properties, is important to predict earthquake ground motion prior to its occurrence as well as for the design of earthquake-resilient structures. Such studies for any region of Pakistan is lacking and therefore require investigation. The proposed study area, Peshawar/Islamabad lies in active seismic region. This study will be important to predict earthquake ground motion prior to its occurrence for the design of earthquake-resilient structures and seismic requalification studies of existing structures. Consequently, this will help the economy of the country and save the human life and property.

data.projectName: Design and Development of Energy Efficient and Economically Feasible Radiant Cooling System for Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest: One of the major energy use of the world goes to building sector wherein major part of energy is consumed for heating, ventilation, air conditioning (HVAC) and lighting. It is estimated that 10% of world energy consumption is in the building sector for attaining human thermal comfort. An energy efficient alternative to the conventional cooling system is Radiant Cooling (RC) in which chilled water is circulated in pipes and heat is removed radiantly. The results will outline all design parameters for a RC system such as Active area, Pipe diameter, Piping space, flow rates and operating water temperature. The project will assess the energy, economic and environment (3E) benefits of RC system, for different climatic zones of Pakistan. Moreover, 3E based comparative analysis will determine the benefits of using RC systems over conventional cooling system. The comparative analysis will also be carried out of using different hydronic layouts (sub-components arrangement) of RC with the best suitable design for different climatic zones of Pakistan. Furthermore, a parametric based energy and cost analysis of the models and optimization will be carried out. This project will ultimately find the most suitable economically feasible and environmentally friendly RC system for Pakistan.

The results will outline all design parameters for a RC system such as Active area, Pipe diameter, Piping space, flow rates and operating water temperature. The project will assess the energy, economic and environment (3E) benefits of RC system, for different climatic zones of Pakistan. Moreover, 3E based comparative analysis will determine the benefits of using RC systems over conventional cooling system. The comparative analysis will also be carried out of using different hydronic layouts (sub-components arrangement) of RC with the best suitable design for different climatic zones of Pakistan. Furthermore, a parametric based energy and cost analysis of the models and optimization will be carried out. This project will ultimately find the most suitable economically feasible and environmentally friendly RC system for Pakistan.

data.projectName: Developing Eco-friendly Water Saving Rice Production System in Punjab, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Declining water resources and mounting concerns of high yield of rice offering a challenge to the researchers to find out or to expand the new rice production systems optimizing water use in the tropics. Furthermore, water-intensive operations throughout the season not only create poor soil conditions but also add to the greenhouse gas emissions. To allow farmers to actively minimize water use and associated cost, various water-saving techniques like alternate wetting and drying (AWD) irrigation (also called intermittent water soaking), safe AWD and aerobic rice cultivation in direct-seeded rice are being developed. Safe AWD is the latest technique developed by IRRI where the soil is dried until soil water depth (i.e. perched water table) reaches 15 cm below the surface and field is re-watered to the standing water depth of 5 cm. However, the crop may be flooded during and after flowering to avoid the yield loss. Up to 30% of water can be saved through these management practices if applied with better understanding and keeping into consideration factors like soil, genotypes and fertilizer use adapted to the prevailing conditions of each particular region. It is important to figure out which of the local genotypes are best adapted and performing well in a particular system. Similarly, the use and timing of nitrogen applications are very vital in the adoption of a system that most of it can be utilized efficiently and should not result in nitrous oxide emissions.

data.projectName: Adaptive de-noising filter for medical images
data.projectDigest: We are living in an era where most of the information is in the form of images and videos. Quality of a digital images and videos is affected by different types of noise. The most common type of noise is impulse noise, which is malfunctioning of sensors, faulty conversions (analog to digital and vice versa), bit errors, etc. Sometimes, the input images become so important that you cannot capture that event or scene again. For example, if a certain event happens (explosion, robbery, or any other criminal activity), and the images or the videos of that event are noisy, then only option you left with is image and video restoration, not the retake of that scene. Furthermore, it is not advisable (for patients) to take the x-ray again and again till the perfect image. The only option you left with is image restoration. So image restoration is an import field in current era.

data.projectName: An Intelligent Framework Aiding Visibility Enhancement and Color Fusion for Low Light Environments
data.projectDigest: Humans receive about 85 percent of their information through sense of sight which enables human visibility. Low light natural conditions (fog, night, dusk, shadow) reduce human visibility which can be challenging or fatal for humans operating in such conditions. In recent years, research has been conducted to enhance human visibility in low light environments. Majority of contributions proposed monochrome visibility enhancement solutions which lack color fusion in output visual information (images, videos) and does not present a colored day light representation of input visual information. Other contributions rely on the feature engineering and statistical techniques which does not scale well for computer vision applications. We believe further research is required to develop a solution which can generate colorized (fused) visual output of low light visual information. We propose a technical framework which can take advantage of advances in artificial intelligence and computer vision to learn the colorized day light representation of corresponding low light visual information hence mitigating reduced human visibility in low light environments.

data.projectName: Biochemical and molecular investigation of atypical endophytes and their potential use as bioinoculants
data.projectDigest: In the past 40 years, global use of chemical fertilizer has increased many folds, interfering with the nitrogen cycle and other biological processes, as well as causing increased emission of nitrogen oxides, water eutrophication and soil acidification. Bioinoculants, which contain beneficial microorganisms, can be applied to soil or seed surfaces to promote plant growth. Nutrients provided by Bioinoculants are are less prone to leaching and volatilization, making them ideal for sustainable agriculture. Recently, atypical endophytic bacteria are reported to reside the nodules of legume plant and produce plant growth promoting substances. These atypical endophytic bacteria in combination with rhizobia have great potential to be used as bioinoculant for various crops, which is an environment friendly alternative of chemical fertilizers.

data.projectName: Cybernetics’ Named Entities Recognition Intelligent Agent Using Deep Learning
data.projectDigest: With technological advancements and new exploratory filed of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) and Machine Learning (ML). The main aim of developing this project is to raise an artificial agent names as NERCIA (Named Entity Recognition Cybernetics’ Intelligent Agent), which can mimic the human behavior in identification of Person, Place and Organization, which is known as Named Entity Recognition (NER). NER is Natural Language Processing (NLP) task of tagging the entities with their corresponding object. In this project our intelligent agent NERCIA takes input video stream, sense it, identify the frames, recognize the feature, learn the patterns, recognize the entities, and then will speak about the recognized entity by using the deep learning algorithms. NERCIA can be deployed anywhere into the industry, educational institute, or in any organization for employee’s identification, not only this NERCIA can also provide benefit in case of any mishap, crime or misconduct activities and any place where their video is available to recognize the Person, Place or Organization.

data.projectName: Mathematical Modelling of 3D printed parts as function of printing parameters.
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Progress of the industrial sector of any country depends upon its manufacturing sector industries and their advancement. The more equipped and advance the manufacturing sector is, the more developed is the industrial sector and thus the gross domestic product and economy of any country enhances. The use of computer technology in manufacturing processes has not only proved to be very successful if the development of this sector, but it also has enhanced the quality of the products. One of the most recent development in the field of manufacturing engineering is the introduction of three dimensional printing (3DP) technology. This technology has changed the concept of part production all together and have enabled the part production to be carried out even in the offices or homes. Another distinguishing aspect of 3DP is its ability to create complex shapes with high degree of repeatability. 
This project is based on developing mathematical relationships for the strength of 3D printed parts as a function of the input parameters of the process. The most commonly used 3D printing processes, i.e., fused deposition modelling will be investigated.  The developed model can then be used as standard equations. Furthermore same model can be used to develop software modules that will not only calculate “strength for the given set of parameters” but will also use to calculate “set of parameters for a given strength”.
The direct beneficiaries of this study will include prosthetics manufacturing, automotive manufacturing, aerospace/defence industry, research and development organizations, as well as equipment and machine tool producing industry.

data.projectName: Identification and study of interactions between plant-host proteins and the cotton leaf curl geminivirus pathogenicity determinant protein
data.projectDigest: Cotton leaf curl disease (CLCuD) is a caused by single stranded, circular DNA, begomoviruses (family Geminiviridae) along with a pathogenicity determinant betasatellite and a non-essential alphasatellite. To investigate host-pathogen interactions a cDNA library will be prepared for all possible genes expressed in the leaves of model host, Nicotiana benthamiana, in response to virus infection. All cloned cDNA fragments will be sequenced in their entirety. The betaC1 gene encoded by betasatellite will be checked for in-vivo interaction by yeast-two hybrid and yeast split ubiquitin (YSpUb) method. The positively interacting genes will be cloned and expressed in Escherichia coli strain BL21-Codon Plus or Rosetta. Similarly, the betaC1 gene (~356nt ORF encoded by cotton leaf curl Multan betasatellite) will be over expressed in the bacteria. These over expressed proteins from host and betasatellites will be subjected to pull down assay for their co-purification through column chromatography procedures. After validation of initial protein-protein interaction studies an interactome for virus-host proteins interaction will be developed. The orthologs of benthamiana genes will be isolated from cotton plants. By using the similar approaches of protein-protein interactions the interactome for CLCuMuB will be established. This study will help in identifying the host genes, which interact to aid or reduce the betasatellites/geminiviruses replication and pathogenicity.

data.projectName: Identification, Characterization and Expression Analyses of DNA Variants Causing Otitis Media in Pakistani Population
data.projectDigest: Otitis Media (OM) is a clinical condition in which effusion exists behind intact tympanic membrane of the middle ear with no symptoms of acute inflammation. OM with effusion can be occurred because of the mechanical obstruction in the opening of the Eustachian tube which results in poor ventilation of the middle ear. OM is the most frequent disease and the most common cause of hearing loss in children. About 90% of children up to 5 years of age at least once suffer from OM. Other complications like mastoiditis, cholesteatoma, meningitis, brain abscess and lateral sinus thrombosis can be associated to Otitis Media. The major consequence of Otitis Media is conductive hearing loss that has profound impact on speech, language and cognitive development. Approximately, 21000 people die by Otitis Media each year across whole world. The highest death rate is observed in the duration of first year of life. The clinical evaluation of children with OM shows poor performance in school and the concerns of the parents about loss of language development, behavior and hearing loss. OM has a large impact on health care across the globe. Besides the significant impact of OM, the cellular and molecular events that regulate this disease process are still poorly understood particularly in Pakistani population. There are different studies focusing on investigating human candidate genes and linkage of polymorphisms with OM susceptibility. Children with parents’ history and affected siblings are at higher risk to have OM and the disease passes in families across generations. This indicates implication of roles of genetic variants in the pathogenesis of the disease. A comprehensive understanding about the pathogenesis of OM has the potential to lighten a significant disease burden across the wo

data.projectName: Phonological variation of vowel sound in the dialects of Pashto language
data.projectDigest:
The present study focuses on the acoustic analysis of the vowels sounds in all the Pashto dialects of Pakistan in comparison to English vowel sounds. Adopting the theoretical framework of Flege (1987), the study is aimed at investigating the similarities and differences in the acoustic properties of English and Pashto Vowel sounds. In addition, it investigates the L1 Pashto effect on the acquisition of English sounds. Further, it attempts to see whether the acquisition process of Pashto learners agrees to the predictions of speech learning model presented by Flege (1987).

data.projectName: PERFORMANCE OF FIRE DAMAGED NORMAL WEIGHT AND LIGHT WEIGHT REINFORCED CONCRETE BEAM-COLUMN CONNECTIONS
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is in seismically active region.  In Pakistan, Reinforced Concrete structures are popular due to availability of cheaper materials and skilled labor. Seismic hazards sometimes come with secondary hazard like landslides, and fire, etc. In cities, fire is most common secondary hazard that combines with earthquake and phenomenon is referred as to a Fire following earthquake (FFE) event. In an FFE event, crushing and cracking of concrete, as a result of prior earthquake, results in severe thermal propagation in the reinforcing bars and concrete inner core and thus, FFE event is much more crucial as compared to fire alone. Lightweight aggregates may prove good replacement for limestone aggregates being used in Pakistan and may result in light weight structures with improved seismic and fire performance. The research is aimed to study, evaluate, quantify and compare the performance/behavior of reinforced concrete beam-column connections containing normal weight and lightweight coarse aggregates under a sequential effect of earthquake and fire load. Residual load-carrying capacity of damaged and strengthened specimens shall also be evaluated as part of this research.
