data.projectName: Development and Performance of Heavy weigh Aggregate  Concrete with locally available materials
data.projectDigest:
Concrete is the most common material used for construction all over the world. It has a very wide use in buildings, dams, roads, hydropower stations, airports, bridges and foundations. Concrete is economical as well as a versatile material. Being a composite material, its properties are variable depending upon the ingredients. By substitution of main ingredients or cementitious phase, required properties of concrete are achieved. In many civil engineering situations, for example when there is a need for stabilization, ballasting, bridge counterweights, mass concrete projects like dams etc. gravity seawall or balancing weight, heavy weight concrete with a high density is the best solution.
The concrete density depends mainly upon the type of aggregates used. Fracture analyses will be done using different techniques. Additionally, the durability performance of of concrete containing normal aggregates and dense aggregates will be evaluated against various deterioration mechanisms i.e., chloride ingress, sulphate attack and freez and thaw.

data.projectName: DeepSurveillance: An Intelligent  Weapon Detection from Low Resolution CCTV Videos using Deep Learning
data.projectDigest: Security is a basic need for any home, business and individual. With the recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) research, there is a great potential to radically change the use of information technology for providing safe and secure urban areas. Currently in Pakistan, smart security and surveillance solutions are in great demand that could assist in monitoring and maintaining secure environment to the citizens of Pakistan. Most of the criminal activities involves use of weapons such as a hand held gun, revolver or a pistol. The automated weapon detection plays a vital role in emphasizing security and safety of people.  In this project, intelligent surveillance system will be proposed that will automatically detect the weapons and generate an emergency alarm for action. The objective of this project is to investigate the deep learning algorithms for the application of intelligent assistive video surveillance system for low resolution CCTV videos with poor object visibility due to occlusion. The current developments in the field of deep learning ensure the development of a solution capable of solving aforementioned intractable problems while ensuring efficiency and optimization.

data.projectName: ZINC OXIDE MEDIATED NANO-FORMULATIONS OF BIOCHARS FOR PLANT GROWTH IN SALINE SOILS
data.projectDigest:
Sustainable agriculture assures higher crop yield at optimized agricultural practices. It modifies/ sustains the genetic makeup of soil and sorb toxic heavy metals. Chemical fertilizers enhance plant growth; but reduce soil carbon. Biochar, black carbon, is produced at optimized condition in little/no oxygen. Various agrowastes are sources. They modify physicochemical characteristics of soil. Higher used amount causes toxicity. Soil salinity is reversed by Eucalyptus. It mitigates soil pollution and reduces water run-off. Application of nanotechnology (1-100nm) particularly zinc oxide play important role in agriculture. Zinc, micronutrient, act as cofactor of enzymes. Leafy vegetables are rich source of minerals, fibers etc. 
The proposed research work is designed to make nano-formulations of Rice Husk and bagasse biochar modified with Eucalyptus (leaves and bark) under optimized conditions. These formulations will be characterized by Zeta Potential, XRD, SEM, FT-IR, applied to various soil textures (like saline) in pot/field experiments and will be compared to chemical fertilizers. Soil analysis, growth and biochemical parameters, antioxidant/antibacterial potential will be measured. The study aims to initiate and increase growth in the saline soil area allocated to GC Women University Faisalabad (New Campus) by growing leafy vegetables in rotation. This will ensure food security, cost effectiveness and eco friendliness.

data.projectName: Robustness of Response Surface Designs against Missing Observations under Restricted Randomization
data.projectDigest:
Response Surface Methodology is an important area of experimental designs for optimization processes. But randomization in not achievable when one or more factors are Hard/difficult/expensive-to-change and others are Easy-to-change. These experimental situations lead to split plot designs which allow two different randomization procedures for different groups of factors. This class of designs is also referred to ‘Response Surface Designs with Restricted Randomization’. VKM and MWP are two main methods for construction of this class of designs.
Experimental designs which work well in the presence of problems such as abnormal observations, missing values, inadequate response surface model, etc. are known as robust designs. Many situations in experimental work arise, even the experiment is planned carefully, when some observations are lost during the data collection process. Presence of missing observations adversely affects design properties like orthogonality, rotatability and optimality. Thus, design that is less effected when some observations are missed, called “Design Robust to Missing Data”. 
Broad objectives of research is to (i) study the effect of missing observation(s) on performance of a design according to some criteria and (ii) select a design robust to missing observations, for split plot response surface designs. This investigation will be useful for researchers and practitioners.

data.projectName: Solar Panel Cleaning Robot
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Solar energy is one of the key renewable energy sources and is the base to fulfill future world's energy demand. Dust accumulation, bird droppings and pollen effectively decreases the efficiency of solar cells as much as 40%. While there are many solar panel cleaning methods but the most implemented one is washing and using a wiper. Where this method requires system to be shut down because of water, it also damages the glassy surface of the cell using wiper, a lot of water is also consumed for this purpose.  Hence, an effective solution to solar panel cleaning is a dire need. A solar panel cleaning robot, which can clean dust particles and remove bird droppings without causing power cut down and damaging the cell surface is very much needed. This will not only increase the output power but also preserve water and extend life of solar cells. Such a solar panel cleaning robot is proposed, and it will cater for the problems that arise during solar panel cleaning.

Hazara division is famous for vegetables cultivation. It is the main source of income and counted as one of the important cash crops. Most of the farmers posses small lands which they utilize for a maximum output of vegetables crops throughout the year. Usually vegetables in Hazara are ready for the harvest when are not available in other parts of the country, therefore play important role in the economy of the farmers of this area. The vegetables cultivated in Mansehra are potato, tomato, cauliflower, onion, garlic, peas, spinach, chilies, cucurbits, etc. The quality and quantity of these vegetables are adversely affected by different diseases due to diverse pathogens. One of the important pathogens is bacteria which cause severe damage to the vegetables in fields as well as during its storage and transportation to other markets of the country.

data.projectName: Extraction of Bioactive Compounds from Horticultural Processing Waste and Their Possible Utilization
data.projectDigest: Plant material (fruits and vegetables) contain several compounds such as bioactive compounds, some of which contain antioxidants that may prevent certain diseases and promote aging delay. Carotenoids, phenolic compounds, anthocyanin, L-ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) and tocopherols (Vitamin E) are among the most relevant bioactive compounds, highly diffused in nature and present in fruits, leaves and flowers.The production and processing of horticultural crops, especially fruits and vegetables, have increased very significantly to fulfill the increasing demands. Significant losses and waste in the fresh and processing industries are becoming a serious nutritional, economical, and environmental problem. The waste is composed mainly of seed, skin, rind, and pomace, containing good sources of potentially valuable bioactive compounds, such as carotenoids, polyphenols, dietary fibers, vitamins, enzymes, and oils, among others. These phytochemicals can be utilized in different industries including the food industry, for the development of functional or enriched foods, the health industry for medicines and pharmaceuticals, and the textile industry, among others.

data.projectName: Genetic screening of endophytic Bacillus strains for their potential to promote plant growth by modulating the expression of growth-related genes in tomato.

In the first part we will screen endophytic bacteria genetically and biochemically for having plant growth promoting characteristics. Afterwards, a green house experiment will be conducted to check growth promoting effect of selected endophytic Bacillus strains by studying the transcriptional changes in tomato plants. data.projectName: Spatial Distributional Analysis of Students’ Learning Capacities in Public Primary Schools of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
data.projectDigest:
We are proposing a study  that will quantitatively analyze the spatial distribution (mapping) of students learning capacities in urban and outskirts of urban area public schools in Peshawar. Such distributional analysis of students’ learning capacities will provide a new type of data which policy makers can use in devising educational policies. Further, such evidence will let policy makers deeply understand the heterogeneous nature of students learning capacities across different regions and enable to set modified targets for different regions across the province. 

A primary data will be collected through designed questionnaire from Grade 5 students (age group of 5-11 years) of government primary schools in urban and rural areas of Peshawar. a) educational factors such as educational background of the family and study environment for the student in both school and home; b) question paper containing basic English and Urdu dictation, reading and speaking tests, and basic Mathematics tests; c) interviews from students about the role of their family education in their studies and the reasons behind their grades

This research study will fore mostly benefit the education department and KP government by providing spatial distribution about primary school students (Grade 5) learning capacities and the role of their families’ socio-economic characteristics in student’s school performance

data.projectName: Safeguarding Sensitive and Confidential Images Data through Encryption and Decryption
data.piUniversity: National College of Business Administration & Economics, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Today’s world is characterized by the ubiquity of images. These images are found in virtually the entire spectrum of human existence. For instance, there are medical images, space science images, marketing images, government and diplomatic facilities images, social images, military and spy images to name a few. They are frequently stored on different gadgets and are transmitted perennially through some open channel like the Internet. Their frequent storage and transmission have grave implications and repercussions if they happen to be very sensitive and confidential, blueprint of a new missile, for instance.  This reason stems from the fact that hackers and antagonists are always there in an opportunity to hack them. Traditionally, the integrity of these images has been made intact by converting them into some unrecognizable format through the application of some encryption technique. Unluckily, the classical ciphers of RSA, AES and DES were designed to encrypt the textual data. Given the peculiar characteristics of images like high redundancy, strong correlation among the pixels and of high volume, these ciphers can’t be applied. The proposed system will engineer new image ciphers through the usage of 15-puzzle artificial intelligence problem, pieces of chess, theory of chaos and DNA computing. It would address the problems of low-key space, low plaintext sensitivity and the poor design principles plaguing many of the existing image ciphers. These ciphers will help a lot in maintaining the integrity of images data in their storage and transmission. The varied and diverse national organizations like Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission, NADRA, FIA, ISI, PIA etc. would be able to capitalize on these ciphers.

For instance, there are medical images, space science images, marketing images, government and diplomatic facilities images, social images, military and spy images to name a few. They are frequently stored on different gadgets and are transmitted perennially through some open channel like the Internet. Their frequent storage and transmission have grave implications and repercussions if they happen to be very sensitive and confidential, blueprint of a new missile, for instance.  This reason stems from the fact that hackers and antagonists are always there in an opportunity to hack them. Traditionally, the integrity of these images has been made intact by converting them into some unrecognizable format through the application of some encryption technique. Unluckily, the classical ciphers of RSA, AES and DES were designed to encrypt the textual data. Given the peculiar characteristics of images like high redundancy, strong correlation among the pixels and of high volume, these ciphers can’t be applied. The proposed system will engineer new image ciphers through the usage of 15-puzzle artificial intelligence problem, pieces of chess, theory of chaos and DNA computing. It would address the problems of low-key space, low plaintext sensitivity and the poor design principles plaguing many of the existing image ciphers. These ciphers will help a lot in maintaining the integrity of images data in their storage and transmission. The varied and diverse national organizations like Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission, NADRA, FIA, ISI, PIA etc. would be able to capitalize on these ciphers.

data.projectName: Attenuation of hexavalent chromium [Cr (VI)] toxicity and enhancement of growth and productivity in wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) through exogenous amino acids
data.projectDigest: In recent years, application of natural substances on economically important crops has been intensified to enhance their resistance and productivity under abiotic stresses. Amino acids are one of these substances. However, a very little information is available on isolated as well as combined effects of exogenously applied amino acids on oxidative metabolism and improvement of growth and yield of crops under heavy metal stress. Therefore, the proposed study will be undertaken to investigate the possible amelioration of Cr (VI) toxicity in wheat in terms of improved growth and productivity by exogenously applied amino acids. By achieving this, we will be able to identify the individual as well as combined roles of amino acids in the attenuation of oxidative stress and improvement in growth and yield of wheat exposed to Cr (VI). This possible outcome in terms of enhanced productivity under stressful condition will be helpful to meet the food demand of the burgeoning population of Pakistan by efficiently consuming less natural resources and making the plants more adaptable to such environmental challenged conditions.

data.projectName: Studies on the role of CRISPR/Cas genome editing technology as a diagnostic, prophylactic and therapeutic strategy for Hepatitis C Virus in Eukaryotic cell lines
data.projectDigest: HCV infection is a global health problem globally (3.3%). Approximately 5% of the Pakistani population are HCV infected. Over the last decade, therapeutic regimes for HCV have evolved significantly from Interferon-? (IFN-?) to direct-acting antivirals (DAAs). However, the efficiency of either treatment is limited and needs new antivirals. Here, we proposed the use of Clustered Regularly-Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR), a prokaryotic adaptive immune machinery for the diagnosis and targeting of HCV. Firstly, computational approaches will be used to identify conserved and functionally important targets in HCV genome. CRISPR-associated protein-13 will be programmed to cleave HCV RNA by the guide RNAs (gRNAs) against the predicted targets to develop the preventive as well as curative anti-HCV therapy. Secondly, collateral cleavage activity of Cas13 upon activation will be exploited for the detection, genotyping and quantification of hepatitis C virus. Using different members of Cas13 family having diverse dinucleotide cleavage preference. Addition of mixture of fluorescent reporter RNAs to the reaction will produce a visible signal indicating the presence of hepatitis C virus and specifying its genotype. This will be a low cost and sensitive enough to detect small amount of virus without the use of sophisticated testing equipments.

data.projectName: Identification and molecular characterization of stress related genes in the xerophyte Panicum antidotale Retz. and their application in genetic improvement of crops
data.projectDigest:
Drought and salinity are two of the major abiotic stresses constituting a serious threat to agricultural productivity in Pakistan. The major crops such as Cotton, Wheat and Rice are sensitive to drought and salt stress, therefore, improving their stress tolerance capacity has become a foremost issue for many crop breeding researchers. Xerophytes, distributed in desert regions have developed various multiple protective mechanisms in the process of long-term evolution, therefore, they can grow successfully in the drought and saline environments. A better understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying the adaptation of xerophytes to stressful environments and the identification of abundant genetic resources from these plants will provide a solid basis for genetic improvement of important crops in arid area of Pakistan.
In this research project, we will try to find the important stress-tolerance genes in a xerophyte Panicum antidotale by RNA sequencing and functional characterization. Some of the important stress-tolerance genes will be cloned and expressed in crop plants for instance cotton. The transgenic plants will be assessed for their relative stress tolerance capacity. This project will contribute in strengthening of the scientific research and development in Pakistan for sustainable agriculture.

data.projectName: Interactive Technical Education and Vocational training Platform to enhance the technical skillset among trainees
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is one of the developing countries that are still struggling to cope with unemployment which seriously effects the economy of the country and standard of life in society. The Technical Education and Vocational training (TEVT) is very important for such countries to promote economic development, expanding employment size and improving the quality of employment. According to survey conducted by Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority (TEVTA) Punjab, 65% of their graduates are employed. However, for majority of people, it is not possible to physically appear at any vocational training institute due to many reasons. So, coupled with IT sector, a platform can be provided to all unemployed labor to gain the vocational training that can pave the way for their future employment. This research work will result into an application that will provide interactive vocational training using videos and virtual reality and will be accessible 24/7. The application will be backboned by simulations and quizzes at various levels to evaluate the student performance and learning. Students will be able to use application both on mobile device and Desktop PCs through browser. On the basis of evaluation, student strengths and weaknesses will be identified and students will be guided accordingly.

data.projectName: Integrated use of crop allelopathy and bacteria for eco-friendly weed management in two field crops, wheat and maize
data.projectDigest:
Weeds have been a threat for crop productivity since beginning of agriculture on this planet. Uncontrolled weeds may cause crop yield losses by upto 75% in agroecosystems. Synthetic herbicides are very efficient to control weeds. However, public and scientific concern is growing day by day regarding herbicides, due to increase in number of herbicide resistant weeds and harmful impact on environment. Therefore, there is a need for alterative weed management strategies. 
Allelopathy is a natural phenomenon, which is helpful to control weeds by upto 40% which is less than that is required to obtain maximum crop yield. Weed control by crop allelopathy may be enhanced by integration with bacteria. Use of bacterial strains as bioherbicides is also a natural way to manage weeds through production of toxins like cyanide. However, efficacy of bacterial bioherbicides alone is not comparable to synthetic herbicides. The best way to enhance efficacy of allelopathy and bacterial bioherbicides might be integration of both eco-friendly approaches. The combined use of allelopathy and bacteria may have synergistic effect to inhibit weeds in wheat and maize crops. Their integrated use may be helpful to obtain eco-friendly weed control to reduce reliance upon synthetic herbicides and consequently herbicide import.

data.projectName: Utilization of printable nano ink based metal oxide transport layer for boosting stability of perovksite solar cells
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) are one of the fastest-growing photovoltaic technologies because of their excellent photovoltaic performance, low cost of production and excellent optical properties. A conventional PSC consists of an electron transport layer (ETL), a perovskite absorber layer and a hole transporting layer (HTL). One of the most important parts of the PSCs is the hole transporting layer (HTL) that significantly contributes in the overall performance of the solar cell. It should possess good conductivity, low resistance and excellent interface properties to suppress recombination and hysteresis and obtain high-performance PSCs. 
Moreover, HTL must possess high stability and low-temperature processing to unable commercialization and mass production on various substrates. Conventionally used organic HTLs show excellent properties but their low stability and high electrode degradation limit their use. NiOx is one of the most promising HTL materials with high stability and low-temperature processing. However, this metal oxide has low conductivity and high surface defects. To enhance the electrical properties and suppress surface defects, we propose fabrication of p-type NiOx HTL with copper (Cu) doping using simple solution-based process. This work will not only contribute to significantly enhance hole transport capacity, conductivity and work function

data.projectName: Pre-clinical investigation to explore anticancer and toxicological evaluation of Conyza bonariensis extract against liver cancer.
data.projectDigest:
Cancer is the 2nd most common cause of death worldwide. Among the 100 types of cancers, liver cancer is the one which is becoming more prevalent with the passage of time. In a survey conducted in 2012, 782,000 new cases of liver cancer were reported in which 83 % were from the less developed regions. Between 2006 and 2015, approximately 3% annual increase of liver cancer has been reported in United States. The cancer treatment including chemotherapy, radiotherapy leaves severe adverse effects on the body. So it is direly needed to explore an anticancer drug which eradicate cancer cells effectively without harming normal cells.
Natural products either in the form of single isolated compound or a mixture of compounds with different chemical structures, have been reported to act synergistically to target multiple oncogenic pathways, and are associated with little side effects or toxicity [1]. In Asia, people use herbal products for different ailments, ranging from headache to cancer. Many plants have anticancer properties and one of the indigenous plant of Pakistan Conyza bonariensis has been selected to evaluate its anticancer potential against liver cancer. This selection is based on our previous findings regarding its anti cancer potential, furthermore, its preclinical and toxicological aspects will be evaluated in this study. Traditionally Conyza bonariensis is used traditionally for the treatment of variety of ailments [2]. Numerous scientific studies have reported the antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties of this medicinally important plant[3]. [4]. In vitro anticancer activities of C. bonariensis against a variety of cancer cell lines including MCF-7 (breast carcinoma), HCT 116 (colorectal carcinoma) and HELA (cervical carcinoma) have been reported [5], [6],

data.projectName: Synthesis and Characterization of X-type hexaferrites for various high frequency applications.
data.piUniversity: Government Sadiq College Women University, Bahawalpur
data.projectDigest:
Today, permanent magnets are an essential part of our daily lives serving as basic components in almost everything spanning from user products to large systems utilization in generators, electronic devices, sensors, MRI devices, microphones and headphones etc. Hence, the growing demands for permanent magnets with enhanced magnetic and electric characteristics, it is essential to progress the material composition and processing of permanent magnets. The ideal permanent magnetic materials include the hexagonal ferrites. Because of their low eddy current, good stability, high magnetization and high Curie temperature these materials are considered best for microwave absorption. Amongst these hexagonal ferrites are considered good microwave absorber material because of its high saturation magnetization and low coercivity. All mention characteristic depends upon the synthesis route and choice of the element based on the reported literature.  Rare- earth and transition metal ions proportions are utilized to optimize the magnetic, dielectric and microwave properties. 
The literature revealed that hexagonal ferrites of different rare earth and transition metals substituted compositions have been widely studied.. The current work mainly seeks to address this gap in the literature by providing more comprehensive study and to explain the impact of various rare earth and transition metal ions ratio on various characteristics of the hexagonal ferrites. These substituted cations may optimize the properties of the synthesized ferrites compositions which will make these hexaferrites useful in many applications.

data.projectName: Islamic Perspectives of HR
data.projectDigest:
Thousands of business graduates are produced every year in Pakistan. To uphold the quality, students are provided latest knowledge through the books widely recognized all over the world. It has been observed that the concepts and theories highlighted through latest editions of the books, have their roots in Islamic teachings and history. Unfortunately, we as teachers discuss all the concepts, phenomenon and theoretical models by giving credit to authors belong to western countries, but ignore the Islamic perspectives. Islam is a complete way of life, guiding individuals in social, family and professional life. Muslims’ believe system is based on Islam to understand concepts, happenings and phenomena. Muslims relatively follow Islamic teachings and lessons passionately comparing other religious groups. Organizational performance and work discipline may rise high to maximum, if the lessons given in Islamic literature about loyalty to organization, creativity and group working are properly inculcated to employees.  
 The core purpose of the study is to know the understanding of students and teachers about Islamic roots of key concepts and theories given in human resource management discipline. Data would be collected through semi-structured interviews as well as through respondents’ narratives. The second phase of the project would proceed by developing a book comprising Islamic lessons on core HRM functions and their practicality in professional life. Religious scholars would be approached to know the reference material for the said purpose. The content analysis will be made from Islamic literature to know the Islamic perspectives of various concepts. The book would be refined conceptually and grammatically with the help of relevant experts.

data.projectName: Tunability of Magnetic Proximity Effect and Exchange Bias in Metal-Ferrite Nanowires: Role of Surface Spins and Shape Anisotropy
data.projectDigest: The interface of two different magnetically ordered systems has attracted immense scientific and technological attention. Part of this was on the interface exchange coupling. For ferromagnetic (FM)/antiferromagnetic (AFM) interfaces, this interaction generate field shifts in the field cooled hysteresis loops of the FM i.e., exchange bias effect (EB). This phenomenon turns out to be useful in developing information storage technology because it stabilizes a reference FM magnetization in magnetic read heads, sensors, and nonvolatile memory devices. The interface exchange coupling also gives rise to another very interesting magnetic proximity effect (PE) i.e., proximity-induced changes in the magnetic order of a material near its interface with a relatively strong magnetically arranged system.  While, the EB has been in the focus of intense research activities, PE largely remains ignored and is still a relatively new research area. Apart from conventional FM/AFM interface, EB and PE have been studied for a variety of other composite interfaces. However, studies on these effects in nanowires are really scarce. Considering the fascinating physics and tremendous potential of metallic ferrite nanowires for applications in ultra-high density recording media, sensors and catalysts, the proposed project is aimed to provide better understanding of the so far unresolved issues of EB and PE. The main issues which will be addressed through this research are (i) Directional dependence of EB in core-shell nanowires and (ii) role of disordered surface spins for the PE in these systems. These systems have a promising range of applications, such as magnetic data storage, magnetic resonance imaging, targeted drug delivery, permanent magnets, microwave absorption etc.

data.projectName: A NEW MODIFIED WAY FOR OPTIMIZING THE TRANSPORTATIONAL COST
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Transportation isn’t only involved in taking the peoples from one place to other (movement of people) but also the transport of goods and products. This will involve transportation of items or products from an origin to a destination. Transportation problem deals with the problem of how to plan transportation in such a manner that people/goods can be transported from the origin to the designated places with least consumption of resources.
Many companies in the world these days provide transaction globally instead of only locally. Some of the companies transport their own product by themselves. However, some did not. This is because transporting items will need transportation facilities like Lorries, trucks, ships, airplanes or helicopters. Owning those transportation facilities will need a solid amount of budget which includes fuels, tires, registration fees, depreciation, maintenance and repairs, and it will add costs for a company. Thus, there are many transportation companies already stand in the market. Each of them might have different ways, costs, and capacities to transport an item to different destinations. Companies are used to ship their items or products in bulk within a short term period. Hence, they are needed to decide and distribute these transportation jobs to transportation services companies so that items can reach the destinations on time.
This study is to design a mechanism in order to minimize the total transportation cost and time. In this regard,  work on  new approach to find initial basic feasible solution (IBFS). For which developing a new technique which either less time consuming or required less steps to reach the result.
The beneficiaries of this study are those factories/industries which are located in Karachi and other cities of Pakistan.

data.projectName: STANDARDIZATION OFMORINGA OLEIFERA EXTRACTS ANDSYNTHESIS  OF ITS CHEMICAL MARKERAND  BIOLOGICALLY SIGNIFICANT4-?-(L-RHAMNOSYLOXY) BENZYL ISOTHIOCYANATE.
data.projectDigest:
Standardization is a tool to assure quality, efficacy and safety of herbal products. Knowledge of chemical components of a plant is essential for quality control analysis of the plant, extract or any formulation containing them. Distinguishing, core, bioactive, synergistic, and general constituents present in herbal extracts /pharmaceuticals can serve as “chemical marker”. Excellent chemical markers are the therapeutic components of herbal pharmaceuticals.  4?-(L-rhamnosyloxy) benzyl isothiocyanate (RBI) is the diagnostic constituent present in M. oleifera. Careful sifting of literature revealed its possesses significant biological properties. Hence it can be the right compound to standardize the extracts of M. oleifera.
In order to get 4?-(L-rhazmnosyloxy) benzyl isothiocyanate (RBI) in large amount for standardization and to carryout in depth biological studies, a project has been planned to synthesize it. Synthesis involves only three steps to get the desired substance. Other methods available to prepare RBI are, mostly enzymatic hydrolysis of Moringa glucosinolate to give max. 38.9% of yield. Current chemical method is expected to produce 70-90% of RBI. Synthesis of RBI will be followed by standardization of different extracts of M. oleifera and stability study of RBI in these extracts at different temperatures and time intervals.

data.projectName: Chatbot for Urdu and Roman Urdu
data.piUniversity: National University of Computer and Emerging Sciences, Islamabad
data.projectDigest: This project aims to work towards creating a chatbot framework that can understand questions in Urdu or typed Roman-Urdu language and provide helpful answers in the Urdu language. data.projectName: Exploration of bacterial diseases from feces of cage birds based on Next-generation sequencing techniques
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Clinically healthy birds in Pakistan  have been found to have bacterial community consist of Gammaproteobacteria, Avibacterium Enterobacteriaceae, Pseudomonas, Bordetella sp. and many others residing in lower respiratory tract. Furthermore, some captive birds in Lahore, Pakistan, have been detected as source Toxoplasma gondii. Fecal microbes are the potential source of avian species mortality and human illness. Many bacterial species are known to cause severe infection in avian species such as E. coli causes Colibacillosis. aerosacculitis, polyserositis, septicemia. Pseudomonas is the agent that cause upper respiratory diseases and Aeromonas are known to cause enteritis or septicaemia. Serratia marcescens causes septicemia, necrotizing fasciitis, pneumonia, mastitis, endocarditis, osteomyelitis and purulent meningoencephalitis. In this three year study program, some common captive avian species such as peafowl, pheasants, turkey, Budgerigars, doves, finches,  partridges,  pigeons and various species of parrots including macaws, black swans, Muscovy ducks and  ostrich of Pakistan will be sampled from 5 divisions of central Punjab. Fecal sample will be collected aseptically and collected fecal sample will be transported to Postgraduate laboratory of Department of Wildlife and Ecology, UVAS, Ravi campus, Pattoki. Fecal sample will be stored for further analysis. DNA extraction of the fecal sample will be done immediately by using Gene All (Exgene TM Cell SV) kit following the manufacturer’s instructions. Instead of this culture method“Next generation sequence” will be applied to study the all the residing pathogenic bacterial communities in the feces of avian species.

data.projectName: Genetic and Expression analysis of CEACAM 1 & 2 and functional roles of Adiponectin, Ghrelin, Leptin and Resistin in the progression of liver disorders associated with NAFLD in obese and non-obese diabetes patients from Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Obesity and increased hepatic lipogenesis causes insulin resistance which ends up in irreversible lethal metabolic consequences like Type 2 Diabetes, Fatty Liver Disease leading to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. If Insulin resistance is diagnosed and managed at early stage would result in possible prevention from these metabolic derangements. Leptin, Adiponectin, Ghrelin and resistin have major contribution in development of insulin resistance. In addition CEACAM family have significant role in insulin extraction and clearance which also leads to insulin resistance. It is hypothesized that certain adipokine and underlying factors may increase or decrease the expression of CEACAM 1 and CEACAM 2 resulting in NAFLD. Fatty liver disease is a reversible damage to the liver cells which can be reversed by identifying and improving the underlying factors in order to increase insulin sensitivity curing resistance. Subjects with mutations of CEACAM 1 or CEACAM 2 or both, are at a high risk to develop insulin resistance and NAFLD. So, if diagnosed early and managed accordingly (diet restriction) can possibly prevent obesity, diabetes and NAFLD in these patients.

data.projectName: Students communication, confidence, mental growth, ethics, and academic performance in gender segregated vs co-education system; a case of Pakistani universities
data.projectDigest:
Shall we shift from co-education to single gender education system in higher education in Pakistan!

A dramatic shift has been witnessed in the last few decades from single gender education system to co-education system across the world. The academic researchers have mentioned number of benefits of both gender segregating and co-education systems. If we agree with these scientific studies which suggest a difference in the cognitive and psychological capabilities between both genders, then the next logical question would be to ask whether we should use the same methods and pedagogies to teach both genders. Another important challenge would be to see if a co-education based schooling would be more effective in terms of the students’ learning.

We propose that single gender schooling graduate will have better academic performance, more confidence, better communication skills, better work and personal ethics. We will conduct a longitudinal study. Our population will be university students of management sciences and other disciplines across major cities of Pakistan. This will be a quantitative cum qualitative study (using both survey and interview techniques).

data.projectName: Detecting the Signals of Radicalization from Social Media
data.piUniversity: National College of Business Administration & Economics, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Social Media is a convenient way to express opinions and sentiments online. Recent reports show that, social giants such as Twitter, Facebook, YouTube  are gaining popularity, therefore huge volume of data is generating by the users on the web. Online Radicalization introduces an individual to the idealogy that encourages the drive to shift from mainstream beliefs to extremism through online media. The online media can be social sites, blogs, emails, direct or instant messages. This study focuses on social media platforms such as Twitter and Facebook. The internet in general and the social networks in particular, changed the way that extremists and radical groups can influence the individuals. Terrorist groups such as ISIS are trying to radicalize or recruit young people through an extensive use of social media. Today a billion of users are using social media to share their views but at the same time it is inferred that social media is a convenient way of propagation of propaganda. It has become common to view hateful text or comments attacking a person or group basing on various factors including nationality, religion, race and gender. It has significant negative impact on society. In this study our aim is to use machine learning to automatically detect the extremist contents in social media.

data.projectName: Turbulence and Chaos Studies In The Wake of Bluff Bodies
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Turbulence is found in all fields of nature and science. Designing a complex engineering system requires thorough understanding of structural mechanics and turbulence. Being chaotic in nature, the phenomenon is strongly nonlinear with wide range of spatial and temporal scales. We propose the development of flow diagnostic tools and experimental set-ups for turbulent flows. In addition, the Lab will focus on developing mathematical tools and algorithms to address turbulence flows and chaotic dynamical systems. We intend to closely work with Pakistan Aeronautical Complex, Kamra, NESCOM, HIT, and SUPARCO to provide solutions towards design and innovation. Our focal area is dynamics of single body wake, extending to multi-body dynamics in high speed flows. In applied side the research on Fluid-Structure Interaction as well as particulate matter motion in various flow regimes will be carried out.

data.projectName: Functionalized Ru(II) arene complexes with benzenesulfonamide scaffold as biological vector to cancer cells
data.projectDigest: Cancer is the greatest global health challenge and second leading cause of death worldwide followed by cardiovascular diseases. It seems, it will become number one killer in many parts of the world because the number of cancer cases are continuously growing. In year 2018, about 18.1 million new cancer cases were registered and out of these about 9.6 million deaths were observed. Approximately 70% of deaths from cancer occur in low and middle-income countries. Further, elderly people are the main prey of cancer in many countries and about 1 in 6 deaths is due to cancer. In line with the above-mentioned aspects, a considerable progress was observed in past two decades in search of targeted cancer medicines after finding adverse effects of platinum-based drugs. Further, there has been upsurge efforts observed regarding structure activity relationship with the aim to improve and develop other forms of metal-based compounds other than nonclassical platinum-based drugs with distinct mood of action from already know anticancer drugs. In line with these complexes, Ru(II) half sandwich organometallic complexes with bioactive ligands attract the attention of researchers because of their enhanced lipophilic character which facilitate their uptake into cells by altering their physicochemical and pharmacological properties.

data.projectName: Algal biomass cultivation in wastewater for recovery of energetic and non-energetic valuable products-A clean, green approach with energy and environmental aspects.
data.piUniversity: Balochistan University of Information Technology, Engineering and Management Sciences,Quetta
data.projectDigest: Depletion of fossil fuels and increasing energy demand globally requiring a serious attention to look for new energy sources, which not only meet the future generation requirement but assures an environment friendly and sustainable candidate as well. Pakistan is facing major challenges in energy sector due to increased demand in last few years. Moreover, there are serious environmental issues exists due to improper management of waste water. Algal biomass has been declared as 3rd generation source for fuel and other valuable derivatives.   In the industry, microalgae have been used as a source for a wide variety of practical and potential metabolic products, such as a food supplements, pharmacological substances, lipids, polymers, toxins, pigments, enzymes, biomass, wastewater treatment, and green energy. Microalgae are very essential in agro industry especially for nutrients supply, production of oxygen and carbon dioxide consumption, and consumption of nitrogen- based components. Microalgae have been recognized as promising candidate for lipid and pigments production. It contains about 30-50 % contents, depends upon many factors such as specie type, algal growth condition, growth rate etc. Keeping in view the energy and environmental issues of Pakistan, it is essential to explore the algal biomass potential for its multipurpose utilization. Hence, this research will focus on recycling the domestic and commercial waste water for algal biomass production in pond and photo bioreactor system followed by processing for recovery of energetic and non-energetic products recovery. Its cultivation in wastewater will ensure the proper handling of waste water and helps to reduce the CO2.

data.projectName: Noether symmetries and conservation laws for a class of dynamical systems
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Many dynamical models of physical nature can be expressed by linear and nonlinear differential equations. Conservation laws play a vital role in providing an adequate mathematical description of underlying dynamical systems. When a dynamical system has a Lagrangian formulation, Noether’s theorem provides an elegant formula for the construction of the conservation law if its Noether symmetry is known. Each transformation determines corresponding constant of motion (first integral). For instance conservation of angular momentum is related to invariance under rotational symmetry and invariance under time translation gives energy conservation. The determination of a Lagrangian of any ODE is known as the inverse problem in variational calculus.  We will find Noether symmetries, Noether-like operators and associated conservation laws for the underlying systems of practical interest. We intend to apply classical Noether symmetry approach and a recently developed complex Lagrangian technique to establish the results. We will start from numerous single scalar dynamical equations and extend the study to higher dimensional systems of practical interest. The methodology we shall adopt in the project not only help to construct the conserved quantities but also uncover the group theoretic properties of higher dimensional systems.

data.projectName: A Material/Surface That Can Trap Arsenic; A strategy for arsenic Pollution remediation
data.projectDigest:
Arsenic (As) is a highly toxic element which poses a significant threat to human health. Arsenic and its compounds are carcinogenic and cause a number of diseases in humans. The Food and Drugs administration authorities have confirmed that long terms exposure to elevated levels of arsenic causes skin, lungs, bladder cancers and heart diseases. The WHO report says that more than 50-60 millions of people are at risk from arsenic poisoning in Pakistan.  WHO recommends a limit of 50 µg/L in drinking water but In most of the cities of Pakistan the limit of arsenic is much higher than the limit set by WHO. The situation become worsen when we consider that arsenic concentration in drinking water in Manchar lake in sindh, Karachi, Lahore and other coastal cities like Bahawal Pur, Sahiwal, Muzaffargarh and Hyderabad are much more higher than WHO safe level.  
There is a dire need of developing novel waste treatment technologies and designing efficient separating material for removing arsenic from drinking water. In Pakistan, this problem is overwhelming and comprehensive strategy is lacking. Therefore this study aims to develop silica containing functionalized material/ surface that could efficiently trap arsenic from drinking and industrial waste water. The effect of various environmental features such as pH, exposure time and temperature will be evaluated. This study will help us to understand the nature of bonding and portioning conditions on soil/ liquid interface. An attempt will be made to suggest a possible mechanism for the removal of arsenic on solid/ liquid interface. Computer simulation studies will be performed to identify the nature of interactions between the surface and arsenic and to explore other physiochemical parameters.

data.projectName: in-vitro evaluation, Microscopic  and  in-vivo studies of cryopreserved skin grafts using Antarctic insects oriented anti-freeze Proteins(AFP3))
data.projectDigest:
The structural and functional conformations on different concentrations and different extent of sub-zero temperature are the primary features responsible to monitor the anti-freeze activities of Antifreeze proteins (AFP). These proteins shown extensive variety of anti-freeze activities and has fully fledged into a required phenomenon to associate the anti-freeze proteins (AFP) structure with relative activities and their further commercial uses. The structural properties are the primary features responsible for the possible anti-freeze activities of the peptides isolated from native proteins.
It is hypothesized that type3 anti-freeze proteins (AFP) are more effective than other freezing agents in order to preserve the  skin grafts with minimal detrimental effects on its microstructure and viability. Hence, the objectives of the present study are:
•	To evaluate cytotoxicity, cell viability and DNA damage in AFP cryopreserved cells using in vitro techniques.
•	To evaluate freezing effects on AFP cryopreserved skin graft histological structure using different microscopic techniques.
•	To evaluate viability of insect oriented AFP cryopreserved skin graft using immunohistochemical techniques.

data.projectName: USING MASS MEDIA FOR CREATING CIVIC CONSCIOUSNESS AMONG TEENAGERS
data.projectDigest:
In Pakistan civic consciousness is relatively insufficient and the current dissemination of media contents and methodology to cultivate the sound civic consciousness needs serious attention. Emerging gadgets and on-line services have given an un-avoidable media exposure to the members of society and lesser chances of being socialized through the company of seasoned members of the family. So there is an utmost need for deliberate efforts to generate civic consciousness among youth. It would be wise to deliver such efforts through the same route (New Media) which has been adopted by the youth for their leisure. Goal of this project is to lead the teenagers towards adoption of civic norms, in line with our cultural values.
For the execution of this project, a team of volunteers will be selected, having aptitude for Survey research and videography, to develop audio and video database. These media content will be used in workshops with focus groups of the school students and they will be motivated to do civic activities. These activities will be uploaded on our you tube channel and through other options of social media .More over selected activities of students will be aired through local TV and FM radio channels for the awareness of general public. data.projectName: INDIGENOUS DEVELIOPMENT OF CERAMIC COATING TECHNOLOGY AND TESTING CAPABILITY FOR LOCAL AND EXPORTABLE MOLD MANUFACTURING
data.projectDigest:
The thriving food, auto and domestic products industry in Pakistan are major customers for Pakistan mold manufacturing industry. Consequently, the mold manufacturer in Pakistan have developed in terms of technical capability to serve the demand of the local market. However, the cutting edge in the mold technology in Pakistan is surface enhancement of the molds for higher performance of permanent mold surfaces in term of corrosion resistance, wear resistance, pitting potential, mold filling time, mold release force, mold cleaning convenience, surface finish of the products, poor hardness and poor hot hardness of the mold surfaces. The solution is surface quality enhancement of the molds by coating binary and tertiary ceramic coatings like TiN and AlTiN etc. Development of coating and testing facilities that create this capability in local mold manufacturing industry can reduce the imports of the molds possibly make the mold industry export compatible.
Therefore, this project aims to achieve (a) development of functional grade coatings for mold manufacturing industry like TiN and AlTiN etc., (b) the testing facilities that can ensure the functional performance and (c) the industry academia linkage that make this capacity development possible and sustainable.

data.projectName: Nano-PV: Study of Nanostructured Metamaterial for improved optical transmissivity and its applicability with Next-Generation Photovoltaic technology employing Dopant-Free Carrier-selective thin-film
data.projectDigest: The aim of the project (Nano-PV) is to design and simulate a industrially-relevant and efficient crystalline silicon (c-Si) heterostructure solar cell technology.  Commercial Silvaco TCAD simulator will be employed to simulate and characterize antireflection coating (ARC) and carrier-selective thin-film.  The purpose of ARC is to reduce the reflection of sunlight from the solar cell top and to allow maximum light to transmit through the solar cell for enhanced conversion efficiency. The  ARC design will be inspired with nanostructured metasurfaces. Similarly, carrier-selective films serve to transport charge carriers towards metal contact for renewable energy generation. Existent structure design employing doped carrier-selective films impedes the charge transportation due to the presence of unfavorable energy barrier. The current project will physically modeled the behavior of dopant-free carrier film that would assist in minimizing the energy band barrier for solar cell.  With enhanced optical transmission, reduced sunlight reflection, and optimum energy barrier, a step increase in the performance of the solar cell is envisaged with this research work and will project Pakistan as a forefront in exploring the new frontiers of next-generation PV technologies.

data.projectName: Detecting Math Anxiety through Computer Vision for STEM education
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Mathematics is one of the core competencies of STEM education and is bound to make a major impact in the industry of today and the future.  Learning and mastering mathematics has been key component of school education system, however, a range of students find mathematics difficult to learn. Though some aspects of mathematics are cognitively difficult a range of disabilities including Dyscalculia and math anxiety hampers student learning impacting the learners academic progress. Identifying such disabilities is the first step in devising psychological intervention to help the learner overcome the disability. However, the methods to evaluate such disabilities are costly in terms of time and human resources. The standard test for grading the level of math anxiety (MAS) has 20 questions and assessing the results for a classroom becomes an unsurmountable task for the educator.  To assist in this process, we propose in this project, to use the state of the art computer vision and machine learning techniques to identify gestural and student actions to identify and grade the math anxiety in students. Various studies grading test anxiety and math anxiety have been conducted but to our knowledge, this will be the first use of computer vision and machine learning to achieve the task.  Such a system can assist the schools to monitor and evaluate the level of math anxiety in students in class and can greatly assess in identifying students suffering math anxiety.

data.projectName: Development of a novel medium concentrated dual photovoltaic system thermally regulated by phase change material for environmental condition of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The major aim of this project is to design a novel, low cost, customized dual cell concentrated photovoltaic system thermally regulated by phase change material. In this work, a novel concentrated photovoltaic configuration will be developed. This configuration will employ two photovoltaic cells that will be attached to an aluminium container. The aluminium container will encapsulate phase change material that will regulate the temperature of the concentrated photovoltaic system. Both cells will be irradiated with concentrated light using novel non-ideal parabolic trough and compound parabolic trough-type concentrator.  Design and experimental investigation will be carried out. It is anticipated that the developed system will harness solar energy efficiently and will generate electricity cost effectively as compared with conventional photovoltaic system.

data.projectName: Association of Onco-Viruses with brain cancer: Viral detection and in-vitro growth inhibition of patients-derived brain cancer cell cultures using viral vaccines
data.projectDigest: Cancer has become one of the most complicated diseases that has acquired resistant to current therapeutics. Among several factors, the viral infections by oncoviruses are leading the way to cause malignant cancers. Till date, different types of oncoviruses are confirmed to have caused different types of cancers; however these viral DNA segments have been rarely studied in the most lethal type of cancer – the brain cancer.  The use of existing viral vaccines is emerging to treat different types of cancers including brain cancer. We aim to detect these viruses in brain cancer’s patient-derived cell cultures following cancer treatment with viral vaccines to develop new treatment protocols

data.projectName: Development of Suitable Regional Modular Water Treatment Package for Potable Water Needs
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan, about 80% of the whole population have no access to safe drinking water because major water resources have a quality below the recommended standards for human consumption. About 250,000 child deaths have been recorded each year in Pakistan due to Diarrheia, hepatitis and other water-borne diseases. About 40% of hospital patients were suffered from water connected diseases. The availability of potable water is further aggravated when country hits the natural calamity like Earthquakes, floods, storms etc. Therefore, it is important to develop suitable options and innovative water treatment processes that are technically viable and economically suitable for applications in Pakistan particularly Southern Punjab. In view of the diversified climatic and geographic conditions of this country, a modular water treatment package will be developed to remove suspended and dissolved water impurities including pathogens. The main theme of this project is to develop a solution to the aforementioned national challenge of unavailability and inaccessibility of potable water and resultant threats. A modular multi stage (consisting of different pluggable/removable units) water treatment technology package is being proposed to remove water impurities and pathogens i.e. suspended solids, turbidity, color, dissolved solids, toxic metals, and other bacteriological contaminants.

data.projectName: Development of Traffic Impact Study Guidelines and Trip Generation Manual for Pakistan with Karachi as Case Study
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan has the highest rate of urbanization in South Asia and Karachi is the epicenter of this urbanization. This rapid growth in urban population has drastically increased the number of vehicles on the roads which in turn has resulted in extreme congestion along the arteries as well as minor roads on the network.

To manage these impacts research about the trips associated with the development is necessary. This research focuses on the analysis of the trips produced by various landuses with different economic backgrounds. The output of this study will be “Trip Generation Manual and TIA Guidelines”. This manual will serve as a reference for stakeholders involved in land-use/transport planning.

data.projectName: Intelligent Cattle Farm Management using IoT and Machine Learning
data.projectDigest:
About 40 millions population of Pakistan relies upon livestock for their livelihood. This sub-sector contributes about 55% of agriculture and 12% of overall GDP. Pakistan is the 4th largest producer of milk in the world. Domain experts of the livestock domain are not easily available for helping the farmers as the ratio of  available domain experts to number of cattle is very low. For instance, approximate expert to cattle ratio in Punjab is about 1:1000 whereas in Sind and Baluchistan, it drops horribly to as low as 1:100,000. Remoteness and sparse rural populations are the main factors because the livestock hubs are primarily based in rural areas. Average price of a cow or buffalo is about Rs. 150,000. Its significance for a common farmer is critical as the entire livelihood is associated with the health and life of the cattle. Their health is the key challenge faced by the farmers. The farmers of rural areas in Pakistan have weak access to veterinary experts to diagnose the disease of their cattle resulting into significant financial loss every year. We have recently developed an intelligent system to diagnose cattle diseases using artificial intelligence which is currently being tested and deployed in Mianwali district. Its initial usage is about 500 users with highly satisfactory response. There is no other such system in place for the livestock domain in Pakistan to the best of our knowledge. However, their some pieces of research work done across the globe in the domain which has its own limitations. 
In this proposal, we aim to develop a sophisticated farm management system using IoT and Machine Learning.

data.projectName: A Study on Peace Building as a Social Responsibility of Universities in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: This project will be executed to (a) examine the current status of social responsibility of Pakistani Universities in terms of peace building, (b) evaluate the activities designed and offered for peace-building on the campuses, (c) assess the current situation of peace and harmony on the campuses, (d) analyze factors which cause intolerance among students and violence on the campuses, and (d) develop guidelines for peace building by the universities as their social responsibility. It will be a descriptive mixed-method study. This study will be delimited to public sector general universities functioning in Pakistan (Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Balochistan, Gilgit Baltistan, Khyber Pukhtunkawah, Islamabad, Punjab, and Sindh), and faculties of education; faculties of arts and humanities; and faculties of social sciences. The data will be collected from the university stakeholders i.e.  University Administration (Vice Chancellors), University Academia, Directors of Students’ Affairs, Heads of Teaching Departments, University Students, and Opinion Leaders from the community on social responsibility of university in peace-building. Questionnaires and interview protocols will be used for collecting quantitative and qualitative data respectively from the respondents. The quantitative data will be analyzed in terms of percentage whereas the qualitative data will be analyzed thematically. In the light of the findings of the study guidelines for peace building by the university as their social responsibility will be designed along with other feasible recommendations.

data.projectName: Conversion of greenhouse gases (CH4, CO2) to hydrogen rich syngas using cold plasma reactor
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: The emission of greenhouse gases (GHG) due to the utilization of conventional fuels such as diesel, gasoline, natural gas and furnace oil; to meet energy demand commercialization and urbanization. The emission of GHGs disbalance the nature cycle and cause various environmental effects. It is requisite to reduce GHG emissions and rely on clean fuels. The utilization of GHG such as methane (CH4) and carbon dioxide (CO2) to reduce the GHG emissions and produce clean fuels for sustainable development. Various techniques are practised for GHG utilizations, however, the low energy sustainable and novel technique considered in the last decade is cold plasma reforming technique. The cold plasma technique for GHG utilization has multiple benefits such as low capital cost, easy to handle, low energy input, versatile in the feedstock, and processing. This technique can be used for various other application such as waste treatment and material preparation for various applications in industrial processes. The aforementioned advantages make this technology more suitable for this GHG mitigation and novel approach for this century and beyond for green fuels.

data.projectName: Exploration, depositional environment, geochemical prospective and geology of the Paleocene Coal, Tirah, District Khyber
data.projectDigest: Pakistan contains Gondwana age Carboniferous to Permian coal and Tethyan age Mesozoic and Cenozoic coal. In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa economically extractable coal is mined in the Paleocene Hangu Formation. Most of the Paleocene coal strata is exposed in the Main Boundary Thrust hanging wall. These coal bearing rocks are actively mined in Hazara, Cherat, Darra Adam Khel, Hangu and district Orakzai. The same Paleocene coal strata extends westward to Tirah, district Khyber. Coal exploration in Tirah will be a win-win development in highly conflict–affected area to ascertain high quality life, access to education, better health and employment. This will enables regional development and energy required for thermal power generation, steel manufacturing, cerement industry, paper products, purification filters, light weight reinforcement material and lubricants. This project involves integrated mapping of coal, geochemical, stratigraphic and structural investigations to explore the Paleocene coal strata in Tirah. This integrated research will give conclusive evidences regarding the temporal and spatial distribution of coal deposits in the Tirah valley. These models will be extremely implemental for reserve calculation, mining planning, geological structures that may affect the coal distribution, coal grade determination, ash level recognition and marketable coal recovery.

data.projectName: Partial differential equations with nonlocal terms
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: In this project, we propose to develop novel mathematical techniques to solve certain nonlocal partial differential equations, subject to appropriate conditions, which have not been solved hitherto because of the paucity of available solution techniques. These equations appear in a cell division model. Since cells in a population grow and divide simultaneously, a question of biological interest is to determine the number (density) of cells of each size at any future time if the number (density) of cells of each size are known at a given initial time. Here, size is usually the DNA content or mass of a cell.  The answer to this question lies in solving the corresponding nonlocal partial differential equations which mathematically model this biological process.

data.projectName: Stability Analysis and Chemical Treatment to mitigate Asphaltene deposition problem in upstream and downstream Oil and Gas Sector (Adhi Field)
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Adhi gas condensate field (operated by PPL) is located near Islamabad in the Eastern Potwar basin. The Adhi field condensate was produced without any problem through the NGL/LPG plants from 1990 to 2007. In 2000, color changes were observed in the fluid from one of the wells and measured API gravity changed from 54 to 34 degrees. Since 2007, choking problems have been observed at processing plants with deposition of black organic material which was identified as Asphaltene. Till date Pakistan Petroleum Limited is still facing extreme challenges in maintaining stable crude oil production due to Asphaltene deposition problem and facing heavy revenue losses. The research contributes toward understanding the root causes of deposition problem and provides optimum solutions by developing robust models to mitigate this issue. This also includes the development of workflow for the proper selection of suitable chemical additives for Asphaltene treatment. This work flow will be integrated with controlling operational parameters like temperature, pressure and mixing ratios of different flow streams of crude oil.

data.projectName: Formation of edible nano coatings enriched with hexanal and citral for preserving postharvest losses of fruits and vegetables
data.projectDigest:
In Pakistan, about 40% fruits and vegetables losses has been reported. The loss is due to microbial and chemical spoilage. Membrane deterioration in plant senescence is commonly associated with progressive decreases in membrane phospholipid content. Phospholipase is responsible for this kind of degradation of membrane. Hexanal, a volatile compound has been used to inhibit the enzyme which in return increases the shelf life of food. It is applied on fruits and vegetables before transportation and storage, but with passage of time vapor concentration decreases. To achieve its long term availability, it has been incorporated into many polymers. It is found to be effective against microbial growth which has been synergistically improved when used with citral. So it is expected that the encapsulation of citral with hexanal in nano emulsions will be resulted in controlled release of both antimicrobial agents and will synergistically inhibit the microbial growth. 
This project is hypothesized with the objective of incorporating hexanal and citral simultaneously into nanoemulsions and further embed as nanovesicles in edible coating prepared from pullulan. The post harvest losses of fruits and vegetables can be achieved by reducing respiration, inhibition of phospholipase enzymes and microbial growth which can be achieved by incorporating formulated nanoemulsions into pullulan coating.

data.projectName: Management of mosquitoes Aedes aegypti by using Nano-based entomopathogenic fungi
data.projectDigest: The effective management of vectors has become a major discussion after the new and re-emergent of vector-borne diseases globally. According to WHO, 50% population worldwide is at risk of vector-borne diseases. Multidimensional interventions for the management of these diseases intervene the world’s GDP, where the estimated annual cost of dengue alone, in 2017, was 1.66 billion USD. In this study we will focus on the environmentally safe strategies except chemicals, where we will take an initiative to isolate and use local entomopathogenic fungi for the control of all the developmental stages of mosquitoes from egg to adult. Afterwards, we embedded these entomopathogenic fungi with Nanoparticles and evaluate the efficacy and synergistic effect on various stages of mosquitoes. Moreover, we will perform the semi-field trials to evaluate the efficacy of entomopathogenic fungi embedded Nanoparticles. However, the study of this project will provide baseline data that will help to further use this technique at commercial scale and locally developed biocontrol for the native population of mosquitoes.

data.projectName: ----- Towards Economic prosperity: Capacity building of  Female entrepreneurship through workshops and Training in Universities of Punjab
data.projectDigest: This Study focus on the importance of female entrepreneurial skills which are enhanced by workshops and trainings in order to achieve economic prosperity and attain financial sustainability of the country. We focus on the integrated model of human resource management practices and female entrepreneurship capabilities and corporate performance. This study focus on three key practices of human resource management and how these practices contribute to the effectiveness of the female entrepreneurship and empower the female to contribute towards country operations and its missions: 1) skill based technical training 2) Capacity building trainings and 3) career counseling. The women entrepreurship plays a mediating role between HRM practices (skill based technical training 2) Capacity building trainings and 3) career counseling ) and  economic prosperity .The literature review presents evidence that it is logical to assume that there is strong relationship among skill based technical training, career development, and entrepreneurship, and economic prosperity. This finding influenced the authors to conceptualize an integrated model that illustrates the interconnectivity of skill based technical training, career development, entrepreneurship and corporate performance of female. Research will be carried out in three cities of Punjab (Lahore, Multan, Faisalabad).Research will specially focus on the educational sector of Punjab. Regression analysis, Pearson correlation and Sobel test will be utilized for this research. This study will help to find the policy gaps for the sustainability of economic and financial growth.

data.projectName: Nano-encapsulated Delivery of Glycine-Betaine in Spring Wheat to Mitigate the Salt Stress
data.projectDigest:
Approximately 6.67 Mha of total agricultural land area in Pakistan is affected by salinity/sodicity and had gone out of cultivation. Wheat yield losses up to 45% have been reported due to adverse effects of salinity stress. Several approaches are used for better crop production in saline soils. A very little success had been achieved. Properly functionalized nanoparticles can be successfully used to unload chemicals into localized areas of plant tissues and provide novel solutions for the treatment of plants. The nano-particles can also be used to deliver the compatible solutes in plants effective against abiotic stresses. Glycine Betaine is known to function to counter act the effects of salt stress, drought, heat and chilling in plants. Conventional methods of its application reduce its efficiency owing to photosensitivity, biodegradation, soil leaching, foliar loss that cause the use higher amount making it expensive for farmers. 
 Keeping in view the significance of innovative technology, it is planned to use Mesoporous Silica Nano -Particles (MSN) as a carrier to deliver the Glycine Betaine (GB) as salt stress protectant in spring wheat. So, the digest of the project is to enhance final yield of wheat through the ability to survive in saline conditions

data.projectName: Land use regression modeling and characterization of airborne particulate matter pollution in complex road terrains of Karachi.
data.projectDigest: Millions of people in Karachi travel through the roads with different urban terrains in Karachi to reach their destinations, daily. During travelling they lose their health gradually due to chronic air pollution exposure. Inhalation of particulate matter (PM) emitted from traffic has been reported to cause severe health effects. Therefore, tempospatial distribution models are needed for the simulation of PM patterns in air to find their exposure probability, which could result in chronic health effects. Along with this, characterization of exposed PM is also necessary for finding the root-cause of daily morbidity associated with travelling on the roads of Karachi. For this, the present study will reveal the exposure to airborne PM’s level, size and chemical composition along the roads with different urban terrains. Land Use Regression (LUR) model will be developed for the first time for on-road tempospatial distribution of PM in Karachi by using mobile monitoring, that will be a cost-effective approach. After LUR model validation, the complete knowledge about PM distribution for each road in Karachi will help in controlling the pollutants at significant levels by authorities. The findings from characterization of PM will supplement relevant epidemiological studies in reducing gradual health degradation of peoples in Karachi.

data.projectName: Peer-to-Peer Load and Energy Management System for Local Distribution Grid
data.projectDigest: The transmission losses can be bypassed if energy is generated at proximity to the load. This concept of distributed generation is vital for establishment of a smart grid. An alliance of consumers with generation capabilities can coordinate their energy resources and manage their loads to achieve an optimal energy balance scenario which will be cost effective. The goal of this project is to establish a peer-to-peer load and energy management system. The system will take real-time input from the consumers and administer optimal set points for their equipment usage (including load and generation). Henceforth, each customer will be able to benefit from the cheaper local energy pool in case of generation shortage at his end and avoid the expensive energy acquisition from the main grid. Such a scenario will also lessen the burden on the main grid and the overall energy losses will decrease. If an active involvement of customers is established in Pakistan, the energy consumption and trading profile can be reshaped towards an improved economy.

data.projectName: Evaluation of biochar produced from indigenous organic waste in priming Cotton plant defense against wilt inducing pathogens and growth stimulation
data.projectDigest: The most significant threat to food security around the globe are plant diseases and it is attaining significance day by day due to increasing population and deterioration in plant health due to the changing climate. Horticultural crops are economically important, comprising high value production systems constantly challenged by climate change and emergence of new pathogenic strains. Owing to the strict restrictions in the use of chemicals such as methyl bromide and high costs associated with chemical disease control practices emphasize the need to explore for alternative environment friendly disease management strategies. In pursuance of sustainable world food security and environment protection from toxic agronomic practices, alternative disease management strategies are required to eliminate or reduce the use of pesticides. Previously, biochars have been reported to increase the plants resistance against the aerial and soil-borne pathogenic bacteria and fungi. However, to our knowledge, the present study will be a significant milestone towards utilization of waste material into valuable agricultural inputs to stimulate plant defense and promote growth.
