data.projectName: Virtual Reality Platform for Rehabilitation
data.projectDigest:
Rehabilitation is the broadest branch of medicine ranging from patients with severe impairments and
disabilities, psychotic and emotional disturbances. The rehabilitation department bears sacred and
tedious responsibilities to bring back the patient to a state where he/she can lives his/her life normally
with the best possible potential and can contribute to the society as a useful citizen. In a country like
Pakistan where disability is a stigma and cultural norms are so strong that it is near to impossible to find
the actual number of disables. According to the last national census of Pakistan done in 1998, 4% to 6%
of the population has a disability. If this percentage is manipulated until date, 8.66 to 12.99 million
people will be considered disabled. In this situation, there is a severe need for well-equipped
rehabilitation facilities and trained medical and para-medical staff. The current situation of
rehabilitation facilities in Pakistan is not considered as compared to the extent of the severity of the
problem. On the other hand, it’s only available in developed cities and patients face problems such as
mobility, cost and time management.
The VRPR provides a Virtual/Augmented Reality Development Environment to design and generate a virtual and simulated environment under the guidance of a rehab physician and patient requirement. To acquire real-time data from the patient the VRPR uses patient wearable system and execute developed virtual simulated environment using the processing system. The proposed environment targets novel VR/AR sensing devices for rehabilitation of the patients of different categories of disablist. These devices will be accurate, noninvasive, drug free, cheap, user friendly and interactive according to the local temperament of the patients.

data.projectName: Surveillance of Antibiotic Resistance Patterns among the XDR Typhoid causing Salmonella Typhi from Pakistani Population: A predictive modelling approach towards control of future Typhoid outbreak
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Since November 2016, Pakistan is in a constant threat zone of an extensively drug resistant (XDR) Typhoid fever outbreak caused by the Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi. According to a survey conducted by World Health Organization (WHO), a total number of 5,274 cases of XDR typhoid were reported in Pakistan particularly targeting the Sindh province. Karachi and Hyderabad are the majorly affected cities owing to the poor sanitation and water drainage system. The local strain of Salmonella in these regions has found to be resistant against the first and second lines of antibiotics as well as the third generation of Cephalosporins which is alarming and raising concerns about the global public health. This project is proposed to analyze the antibiotic resistance patterns of the circulating Salmonella Typhi strains in Pakistan and report the incidence rates and disease burden. The outcomes of the current project will establish a foundation for the XDR Typhoid Surveillance Network in Pakistan and facilitate in creating awareness about the disease among the local population. With the help of the assigned collaborators, the project team aims to create a local repository of the XDR typhoid cases by collection of fresh samples followed by the complete analysis of their antimicrobial resistance patterns.

data.projectName: Education as a Tool for Promoting Resilience: Ensuring Adolescents’ Health and Well-being
data.projectDigest: This proposed multi-sectorial-disciplinary collaborative project [with FDE Cantt., Garrison Rawalpindi] is a systematic intervention based effort across 152 schools using education as a tool to promote resilience by ensuring Adolescents’ health and well-being. More specifically, this project proposes to explore the themes and patterns across curriculum of 9th and 10th grades in order to identify the content provisions and gaps of psycho-social and health issues of adolescents as a baseline. The major activities include Systematic Content Analysis of curriculum [desk research]; Survey Methods to collect empirical evidences on current pedagogical practices; provisions and frequency of academic and recreational activities; school community relationship patterns reported by teachers and principals [field research]; Focus Group Discussions with teachers and students independently [field research]; Resource Development [desk research]; execution of integrative Capacity Building of teachers—in Contemplative Pedagogies and Life Skills Based Education; and Activities and interventions employing the principles of Social Emotional Learning (SEL) for adolescents promoting their psycho-social health and wellbeing. Sequential mixed method research will be used by employing survey questionnaires, interview protocols, and question guides for data collection and data will be triangulated through various pragmatic methods to consequently present an evidence-based report to relevant stakeholders for policy formulation/adjustments.

data.projectName: CONSERVATION OF ENDANGERED HOUBARA BUSTARDS (CHLAMYDOTIS UNDULATA MACQUEENII) USING FROZEN SEMEN: INFLUENCE OF THE NUMBER OF INSEMINATION ON FERTILITY AND ABILITY TO HATCH
data.projectDigest: Asian houbara bustard (Chlamydotis undulata macqueenii ) is declared a vulnerable species by IUCN. During recent decades, populations of Houbara bustards have declined dramatically over their entire distribution. Its population in Pakistan comprises of two groups: breeding and wintering. Breeding populations are found in the remote areas of Baluchistan province, they migrate to Sindh and Punjab to spend their winter. Principal threats to houbara bustards in Pakistan include illegal trade and over-hunting by falconers. They are targeted at two steps in this sport: first in the training of flacons and then being hunted down by these trained raptors. Because of rapid decline in population of this bird in Pakistan, it needs immediate conservation employing ex-situ and in-situ approaches. There are many ex-situ in vitro conservation strategies which are helpful in maintaining the viable populations through cryopreservation of animal genetic resources and artificial insemination (AI). data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Livestock plays an important role in Pakistan economy. It contributed 11.2% to overall GDP. Meat is the only livestock commodity being exported. Pakistan is among top three buffalo holding countries. Pakistan is not even among top 10 beef exporters, while, India is 2nd largest beef exporter with buffalo meat. Having 4th largest animal herd and not being in the top 10 beef exporting countries means a huge potential is being wasted every year.Majority of Pakistan meat exports are in whole carcass and lesser proportion is in boneless form. Post slaughter marination have been proven beneficial for improving tenderness of exotic animals and these methods will be beneficial for the spent buffalo meat as well. Optimisation of marination for spent buffalo meat will help export of meat in boneless form by reducing transportation costs. Usually freezing is used for increasing meat shelf-life which deteriorates the meat quality. In vacuum and modified atmosphere packaging, environment around the meat is changed to improve meat quality and shelf-life. These packaging will help export via sea route which costs one-third of the airfare. This will make exporting meat more feasible. Industry professionals will also be trained for adopting these technologies based upon project findings.

data.projectName: Investigate the Photocatalytic Activities of Textile Based Metal Functionalized with ZnO / PAN Composite for Smart Textile Applications
data.projectDigest: The aim of this project is to develop the textile based fabric in the ultraviolet region is a great deal of interest for the defense purpose. The textile based metal functionalized with ZnO has been chosen in this work due to the properties of ZnO such as, extensive direct band gap (3.37 eV) and the high optical absorption properties of ZnO in both the UVA (spectral ranges 400 nm to 315 nm) and UVB (315 nm to 280 nm). Theoretical study of the proposed materials will be done using win2k software to optimize the photocatalytic properties. The proposed textile based UV fabric will be prepared Experimentally by two ways, First the proposed textile based fabric consist of two layers, namely fabric and coating layer of metal functionalized ZnO. The second approach is to prepare the polymer based metal functionalized ZnO micro fiber using wet / melt spinning machine. The developed fibers will be spun to make the fabric for the desired product. In the first phase of this project, the development of the metal functionalized ZnO gel is prepared by sol-gel technique. Coating of UV layer on the fabric will be done using atmospheric plasma coating machine. In the second phase the microfibers will be prepared using melt / wet / electrospinning machine. The parameters of the wet spinning machine such as flow rate, the collector drum speed and air gap on the morphology of the developed fibre’s will be optimized. Third phase is the comparison of the two developed textile based UV fabric will be done using the characterization techniques such as XRD, SEM, UV visible and FTIR etc. The final selection of the desired product will be done on the basis of the final testing. The Final proposed product will be used in designing army uniform and to prevent skin burning and skin cancer issues.

data.projectName: Digital Finance: Unlocking New Opportunities Through Mobile Banking: Unlocking New Opportunities Through Mobile Banking
data.projectDigest: M-banking was introduced in Pakistan in 2009 and currently there are 23 banks providing this facility with a current transaction value of PRs. 271.3 billion. Though M-banking is gaining its root in Pakistan, it is still at initial stages of adoption. According to the latest statistical data by PTA’s telecom indicators (2019), there are 163 cellular subscribers in Pakistan, of which 73 million are 3G and 4G subscribers. Compared to this, the number of registered mobile phone banking users are just 5.0 million.  The difference in numbers indicate that Pakistani individuals are reluctant in adopting the facility. Therefore, in this study we will try to understand the behavioral constructs behind consumer m-banking adoption.

data.projectName: Analysis of arsenic from water and the methods for its removal
data.projectDigest:
Arsenic exposure contamination is a challenging problems affecting millions of population. Arsenic investigation of groundwater is considered an essential and important activity due to its serious effects on health of people. Many countries are at arsenic exposure risk, but the countries where most adverse health effects are observed include Bangladesh, China, India (West Bengal) and the USA.  Arsenic exposure problem in Pakistan has been highlighted  in reports recently where affected  20 % population of southern Punjab and 36 % population in some districts of Sindh are exposed to arsenic contamination in drinking water  over 10 ppb. 
Arsenic exposure causes chronic health problems and dangerous diseases like lung cancer, skin, and bladder cancer. Arsenic toxicity causes kidney, prostate, liver and other various types of cancers.  In the present study, complete analytical investigation of arsenic contamination in ground water will be monitored from all sources into water.
In underground water of some areas of Ghotki and Kashmore district are reported on risk of arsenic contamination.  The study will lead a complete evaluation of concentration and correlation of hazardness of arsenic with population of different areas of Ghotki and Kashmore district and new method will be developed for arsenic removal.

data.projectName: Enhancement in Multiferroic Behavior of BiFeO3 by Destroying its Spiral Spin Structure and Controlling its Morphology
data.projectDigest:
The emerging field of spintronics will bring a revolution in science and technology by miniaturizing the devices and improving their performance. The multiferroic BiFeO3 is believed to have potential applications in spentronics due to its ability to couple ferroelectricity and ferromagnetism. However, leakage current on application of high electric field restricts large electric polarization in BiFeO3 and its spiral spin crystal structure cancels its ferromagnetism in a spiral length of 62nm. There are two objectives of this project; (a) to reduce high leakage current through BiFeO3 by improving its defect chemistry and (b) to enhance the ferromagnetism of BiFeO3 by destroying its spiral spin structure. These two goals may be achieved by suitable A and/or B site cation doping in BiFeO3 or by reducing the crystallite size of BiFeO3 less than 62nm.
To achieve the above said project goals; after hiring the human resource and procurement of lab equipment and chemicals, the BiFeO3 will be doped with suitable alkaline and/or transition elements by solid state as well as solution methods. The crystallite size of the sample will be controlled to be fractional multiple of 62nm by preparing nano structures to enhance the ferromagnetism. The crystal structure of the samples will be analyzed by X-Ray diffraction (XRD) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The electric transport properties will be examined by impedance spectroscopy (IS) and current vs voltage (I-V) measurements. The ferroelectricity will be analyzed be Sawyer Tower circuit and ferromagnetic properties will be investigated by vibrating sample magnetometer (VSM).

data.projectName: Bridging the Gap between Industry, Academia and Potential Investors to Promote Industrial and Economic Growth in Azad Jammu and Kashmir
data.piUniversity: University of Kotli Azad Jammu and Kashmir
data.projectDigest: The basic aim of this project to bridge the missing link between industry, academia, and potential investors in Azad State of Jammu and Kashmir.  This State is blessed with huge stock of natural resources. There are lot of investment opportunities in tourism and hospitality, hydro power generation, minerals, furniture, livestock, information technology, handicrafts, and relevant areas. A significant proportion of population is settled abroad.  These people have substantial earnings and savings which they generally prefer to keep at home, spend on luxury buildings and vehicles, or deposit in commercial banks. Trend of investment is not much popular due to which industrial sector has not been developed till now. In addition to this, there are six recognized universities in the State which are offering a wide range of market driven programs. The academia-industry linkage is, however, also missing in the State due to which areas of mutual benefit have not explored and implemented till now. A comprehensive awareness program intended to bridge the gap between industry, academia, and potential investors is expected to be helpful in mobilization of idle savings, identification and financing of profitable investment opportunities, creation of employment opportunities, boosting economic activities, and improving the living standard of people.

data.projectName: Development and Structural Performance of Sustainable Wall Panels Incorporating Energy Wastes: A Way Forward To Low Cost Housing
data.projectDigest: The ongoing infrastructure development play a vital role in the growth of any country. Currently, CPEC is a game changer for GDP growth by bringing large infrastructure development projects, especially energy sector. Coal based energy projects lead towards a huge production of energy waste causing an alarming situation for environment due to its open land filling. Therefore, an immediate need is to initiate research programs that targets the engineering properties of generated energy waste to utilize in various other industries as a value added product. One possible way of efficient use of energy wastes is in construction industry for production of water cured compressed bricks. Hence, this research will focus on the development of this novel brick using energy wastes and its feasibility in structural elements for its vast scale application. This will also cater the serious environmental issues (smog, CO2 emission) related to production burnt clay brick through conventional kilns. The methodology of this study will be: characterization of energy wastes (coal bottom ash and fly ash), development of water cured compressible brick incorporating energy waste, structural performance of wall panels incorporating innovative developed bricks and commercial guidelines for its vast scale implementations in local industries. It is envisioned that data established through this study will act as a benchmark for Government of Pakistan for initiating the sustainable, ecofriendly and durable building units for low cost housing.

data.projectName: “Feasibility and impact of government-funded free school meals for primary level students enrolled in government schools in districts of Punjab”
data.projectDigest: This research project aims to analyze the feasibility, sustainability and implementation of a government-funded program which provides free lunches to students enrolled in government-run primary schools in Punjab. The project aims to not just analyze but also implement the suggested program in Punjab. Such a program will have an impact on not just the daily nutritional intake of children, but also impact the rate of absenteeism, enrollment and retention of students. It has a potential to end classroom hunger, therefore, improving focus and attention.During the first module, primary research regarding children’s current meal intake, food preferences, relevancy and demand of meal programs. This will be done through a questionnaire devised by the researcher identifying the current calorie intake, food preferences of students, whether they bring lunches to school or rely on food available for purchase in school. This research will help in creating a framework of implementation, including decisions regarding which districts to target, what the meal should comprise of and whether there will be any form of opposition from parents. Based on this assessment, the second module will include a pilot implementation of the program in a Tehsil of Lahore that is Lahore Cantt. Pre-paired meals will be distributed to schools in the districts through third-party distributors.

data.projectName: THE ROLE OF PRO-INFLAMMATORY MARKERS IN THE PATHOGENESIS OF TYPE 2 DIABETES IN HUMAN & THE EFFECTS OF CINNAMON AND PAPAYA SEEDS IN RECOVERING DAMAGE BETA CELLS OF ALBINO RATS
data.projectDigest:
The emerging part of inflammatory markers in diabetes mellitus (DM) and involvement of immune system in the development of metabolic syndrome has been recognized. The work is very limited among Pakistani population with respect to the insulin resistance, DM and development of rat model along with the treatment of Dabetic rats using Cinnamon and Papaya Seeds. For this purpose 400 human individuals were selected, out of which 200 will be diabetic patients and 200 will be control participants. The subject’s profile, fasting plasma glucose, fasting plasma insulin, lipid profile, IL-6 and hsCRP will be determined. On the other hand, simultaneously rat model will be prepared by administering the streptozocin and the same biochemical estimation will be carried out. The results of both will be compared for any differences. Furthermore rats will be treated with herbs (Cinnamon and Papaya seeds) to check their effect on rat’s pancreatic cells.
The current study will reflect the role of inflammatory markers as the fundamental operator in insulin resistance and DM. Moreover, Cinnamon and Papaya seeds may be beneficial for reducing the inflammation as well as curing and reducing the chances to develop the DM and insulin resistance.

data.projectName: Efficacy and safety of Teriparatide and Strontium ranelate in Bone Lengthening by Distraction Osteogenesis - phase II, open-label, randomized-controlled trial
data.projectDigest: For delayed bone unions, non-unions, etc., treatment is a big challenge for treating surgeons. Bone grafting is used to treat such orthopedic problems. In large defects bone grafting alone may not succeed, and “distraction osteogenesis” has been proven to have greater success rate. Distraction osteogenesis is basically a technique used for bone lengthening. Conceptually, a fracture is made in a healthy segment of bone, then the segments are fixed with an external fixator (called “Ilizarov”). The external fixator permits moving the transfixed bone segments apart and the gap thus created gets filled with new soft bone. This technique has three stages: Latent, Distraction and Consolidation. At first stage “latent” no distraction is done. Then, “distraction” stage starts whereby bone segments are moved apart at a rate of 1mm per day. Once the desired length is achieved, distraction is stopped, after which the soft bone converts into mature bone, the “consolidation” phase. Large defects may require several months for distraction and consolidation. We assume that adjunct bone forming drugs Strontium Ranelate or Teriparatide, used for osteoporosis, can enhance the quality of bone regenerate when administered with distraction osteogenesis technique. This may reduce the duration of treatment and number of hospital visits.

data.projectName: Genetic Investigation and functional analysis of mutations in Intellectual Disability genes among Pakistani population

Intellectual disability (ID), previously termed as mental retardation (MR), have neurodevelopmental deficits that are characterized by precincts in intellectual functioning and adaptive behavior. The onset of ID are before the age of 18 with an IQ (intelligence quotient) below then 70 and can be related with numerous problems which includes intellectual health, neurodevelopmental, as well as neurological and clinical situations. Asian Countries where consanguineous marriages are commonly practiced exhibited greater ratio of disorder prevalence as compared to general population (1-3 %). Other high risk factors commonly contributing in ID for developing countries mainly include malnutrition, cultural deprivation and parental consanguinity. On the basis of IQ, ID is divided into five categories whereas mode of inheritance classified ID into autosomal dominant and autosomal recessive. Furthermore clinical symptoms of ID differentiates it into syndromic form, characterized by additional clinical or dysmorphological features, and nonsyndromic ID, without any additional complications (sole disability). Pakistan has more than 60% ratio of consanguineous marriages and that is the reason why genetic disorders are so common in the society. Additionally, close consanguineous relation and large family size has proved Pakistani population more valuable for genetic study.

data.projectName: “Nature of Reactive Oxygen Species-Antioxidant/Antioxidative agent Interactions”: A Quantum Mechanical, DFT/HF Molecular Orbital Calculation Study
data.projectDigest:
Cancer and atherosclerosis are the major causes of morbidity in this century. “Free radical and reactive Oxygen Species (ROS)” are proven to be the salient culprit for these diseases. A subtle balance between free radicals and antioxidants is necessary to reduce the cellular/DNA damage and proper physiological function. To reduce the risk of hyper production of free radicals, it needs to introduce antioxidants/antioxidative agents from dietary or external source which accept free electrons from ROS and scavenge the ROS radical. Finding the mode of action of antioxidant scavenging ROS and monitoring the antioxidative property at molecular level of naturally as well as synthesized antioxidants along with different ROS will be the subject of this study.
A general perception of antioxidant is  “an antioxidant is a molecule that inhibits the oxidation of other molecules”. A little more precise definition is “a chemical which scavenges the reactive reduces (molecular) oxygen species”. The most common reduced molecular oxygen species are superoxide, peroxide and hydroxide free radicals.
These reactive oxygen species (ROS), are free radicals (anion) and considered as a villain, so to remove it an antioxidant is needed. There has been extensive studies going on in discovering new antioxidants and every now and then new simple as well as complicated chemicals are claimed to have antioxidant property. But how the two, ROS and an antioxidant, interact at molecular level, no studies have been undertaken. In this project we propose to study this (these) interaction(s) at molecular level. Of course that means theoretical computational study which is envisaged to follow: to carry out most sophisticated molecular structure study of such, ROS-antioxidant interactions.

data.projectName: Channel Estimation and Transceiver Design for 5G Wireless Communication Systems and Beyond using Advanced Machine Learning Techniques
data.piUniversity: National University of Computer and Emerging Sciences, Islamabad
data.projectDigest:
In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has taken the center stage in the development of a new breed of smart devices and systems in nearly all spheres of technological advancement. This huge interest in machine learning techniques stems from the ability of these methods to uncover complex behavioral patterns that are far beyond the capabilities of conventional methods.
This research project is aimed at the application of machine learning techniques to wireless communications. With the advent of the high throughput, low latency fifth generation (5G) mobile communication system, there has been considerable interest in the use of machine learning for wireless channel estimation as an alternative to conventional channel estimation and tracking methods and the initial results have been promising. We intend to devise channel estimation methods for massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) and millimeter wave (mm-wave) channels utilizing neural network based deep learning techniques, surpassing the performance of existing methods.
Furthermore, transceiver design and optimization for 5G systems and beyond, using a combination of machine learning and conventional optimization methods would also be investigated with the aim of of achieving the optimal performance-complexity trade-off which is not possible with the currently used methods.

data.projectName: Quantum Gravity with Polymer Matter
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest:
General Relativity (GR) (our best known theory of gravity) describes gravitational interactions ranging from laboratory scales to galactic scales. In these regimes, GR has been verified to a high degree of accuracy.  However, beyond these scales, GR either breaks down (in singularities), or cannot explain observations (like dark matter). It is expected that a quantum theory of gravity can cure the singularities, and some modification of GR can help explain dark matter. 

In this work, we want to consider a theory which, in principle, could explain phenomenon on either end of the scale. Our model is to consider a modified theory of gravity with matter fields, and quantize both gravity and matter using a scheme motivated from quantum gravity known as “polymer quantization” (which is distinct from (usual) Schrodinger quantization). The expectation is that this will lead to singularity resolution at the small scales, a description of dark matter at the large scales, and will reduce to standard GR in the intermediary regimes. 

We will first consider the quantization of the simplest cosmological models in GR coupled to polymer quantized matter and then extend  these methods to cosmological models in the context of f(R) theories (a well-known modification of GR).

data.projectName: Efficient and Low-cost Plasma Synthesis of Conducting Polymer Nanostructures for Next generation High Performance Photovoltaics
data.projectDigest: Nanostructures, such as nanoparticle, nanowires, nano films, nanocomposites and nanofibers etc., are important for many applications such as fuel cells, sensors and photovoltaic cells. In order to increase the efficiency of such devices, nanoscale modification of a material’s surface plays a vital role because the catalytic and electrochemical reactions occur at the surface of a material. Therefore, to enable more reactions to take place with increased efficiency, it is required to develop such a technology which can create materials with large surface areas and a high degree of porosity. In recent years, the issues of energy shortage, climate change and global warming have been addressed by developing new technologies, and photovoltaics (PVs) is no doubt one of them.  Due to their ability to absorb wide range of solar spectrum in heterojunction and multijunction configurations, conducting polymers have a great potential in next generation organic photovoltaics (OPVs). In addition, the fast-emerging nanotechnology has opened up great opportunities to produce organic solar cells with lower cost and improved performance by employing the unique properties of nanostructures. This project will tackle the necessity of miniaturization of surface structures and the reduction of material processing costs by investigating efficient and economical atmospheric pressure plasma (APP) polymerization technique for the synthesis of conducting polymer nanostructures for high performance photovoltaics. The design, fabrication and characterisation of nanostructured organic solar cell (OSC) arrays will be done to optimize the device performance.

data.projectName: Effects of Radiation and Temperature on Casson Fluid Flowing through Porous Medium Cylindrical Objects in the Presence of Magnetic Field
data.projectDigest:
Fluids are the essential ingredient of real world according to its application almost in every field of life. The study of Fluid mechanics is of much importance due to vast application of fluids. Without knowing the behavior and structure of any fluid it is hard to deal with them and enhance their efficiency work. The Casson fluid model is very useful in  food and chemical industries. The structure of blood is based on Casson fluid which increases it’s important in medical field too. The analysis of Casson fluid in the presence of heat transfer is a fresh topic now a day. Casson fluid flowing through the cylindrical domain with effect of thermal radiation and porosity effect of walls increase its applications. Combination of heat transfer with thermal radiation attracts the researchers to all home appliances depending upon electricity and gas. Heating and cooling process of engines, nuclear system and industrial machineries are working on heat transfer and thermal radiations. The participation of fractional order derivative with heat transformation, thermal radiation and consideration of the porous medium converts the problem into a very interesting era of problem solving.     
In this project, the special example of Casson fluid Sodium alginate (SOAL–NaAlg) will be analyzed with MHD flow passing through the pipe like domain. The wall of cylinder will consider as porous medium with the effects of heat transformation and thermal radiations. The Atangana–Baleanu fractional (ABF) model of SOAL will be examined. Exact solutions will be derived by applying the integral transformation technique for ABF model. The results will be figure out applicably  and graphically with analysis of different dependent parameters.  Comparison of dependent parameters will also be examined.

data.projectName: A Framework for Developing Secure Distributed Workflow Applications
data.projectDigest:
Cloud and edge computing infrastructure has enabled the development of distributed applications that are autonomous, co-operative, exhibit emergent behavior, and support different types of trust relationships. Such applications can be realized as business processes, distributed workflows, or web service mashups. Since these applications are composed of resources and services that may belong to different organizational domains, access to the underlying resources and services is governed by the security and access control policies of the respective domain owners. A number of “Virtual Enterprises” have been realized over the last decade, based on integration of services across multiple organizations often for limited periods of time (to achieve a particular business requirement).
The proposed work aims at addressing the challenges in the development of a framework that enables development and management of distributed applications in the cloud and edge computing environment by taking into account the security, privacy, accesses control and trust requirements of the collaborating organizations.
In addition, to prove the feasibility of the system, we will develop a prototype implementation so that organizations and cloud service providers both in the public and private sector can benefit from cloud-based applications while sharing their resources and services in a secure environment.

data.projectName: Development of groundwater simulation model for sustainable water management
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
The Karachi city is facing acute shortage of water supplies; no efforts have been done to develop a groundwater model. The pace at which installation of tubewells is increased in the last few decades, add to the complexity of groundwater management. Thus, there is a need to develop a groundwater simulation model, which can predict the groundwater conditions for sustainable water management. The research study aims at understanding the response of the groundwater system. This can be achieved with the help of definition, development and calibration of a groundwater model. It requires an intellectual work of innovative nature which has not yet been undertaken as provided within the framework of this research.
Framework
1)	Procurement and Deployment of Automatic Water Level Recorder (AWLR) for monitoring of groundwater status (level and quality)
2)	Refurbishment of existing AWLR with collaboration of Department Computer Systems Engineering Laboratories and deployment along with the procured AWLR
3)	Preparing strategies for decision makers
4)	Development of a database of all relevant hydrological information with focus on subsurface hydrology for developing a conceptual and mathematical model for groundwater flow.

data.projectName: Molecular Characterization And Seroprevalance Of Pathogenic Species Of Leptospira In Cattle Of Punjab, Pakistan
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: This study is designed to see the true picture of pathogenic species of Leptospira, their phylogenic analysis and seroprevalence in five agroecological zones of Punjab, Pakistan. Out of 5 agro-ecological zones (Rice wheat, mixed crop, cotton wheat, low intensity and rain fed), Pakistan, 10 districts will be selected including Kasur, Hafizabad, Jhang, Khushab, Bahawalpur, Pakpattan, M.Garh, Mianwali, Attack, Jhelum) on the basis of livestock population. Five districts with low and five with high livestock population will be selected for urine and blood sampling. A predesigned performa will be used to note the various risk factors and history of animals. Serum sample will be tested for MAT to check the presence of antibodies against Leptospira spp. The urine samples will be subjected to PCR testing targeting 16S rRNA for confirmation of both pathogenic and non-pathogenic species of Leptospira followed by PCR for confirmation of pathogenic specie of Leptospira.  The PCR product will be sent for sequencing. One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) will be adopted to analyze obtained data statistically. The data about serovar of Leptospira prevalent in diary animals will be available to take further steps for the control of this emerging issue of livestock.

data.projectName: Diversity in Culture can contribute to formulate a Resilient Society
data.piUniversity: Karakurum International University, Gilgit, Gilgit Baltistan
data.projectDigest: Cultural diversity and its role in developing resilience in society is now universally recognized under UNESCO declaration. In Pakistan generally and in Gilgit Baltistan particularly, very little anthropological research has been conducted on the subject matter and it will help to understand the identify formation (pride) and the utilization of cultural mechanisms for cohesion and sustainable continuity of peace and cohesion. The project is aimed to find out potential among different communities for development of resilient society and its utility for the peace and harmony in the area. The Scale of the Project Activities will be multi-dimensional. Data Collection will take place in all the  regions of Gilgit and Baltistan. The region is divers in its culture and understanding of nature for the social development, the project will enlist the customary ways of conflict resolution among the sister communities. Cultural practices has the capability to cope the changes, conflict, challenges and problems within communities; that is why the approach of cultural diversity will be utilized for the study. Data will be collected through in-depth interviews, systematic surveys will be conducted for demographic information etc. It will entail a multi-sited fieldwork approach. The findings of the study will be helpful for the government, policy makers for further necessary actions.

data.projectName: Pressure driven flow analysis of Magneto-hydrodynamic different shape types nanofluid flow along radially wavy surfaces
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
The purpose of this anticipated project is to discuss the effect of magneto hydro dynamic flow through a flexible surface with nanoparticle interaction in different flow geometries. The governing equations of several mathematical models in the presence of nanoparticles will be framed in coincidence of different practical possessions. Nanofluid dynamics has caught a lot of attention which includes applications in medical science, energetic, biology and process systems engineering. Nanofluids are special type of conventional fluids which enhance the thermophysical properties especially thermal conductivity of the fluids. These fluids also enhance the heat transfer performance which can be utilized to design more efficient devices for better performance. 
Nanofluids are generally prepared by suspension of various types of nanoparticles (f metals, oxides, carbides, or carbon nanotubes) in base fluids like water, ethylene glycol and oil etc.  It is essential to analyze the thermo-physical properties of nanofluids to predict their heat transfer behavior as it is advantageous for the industrial energy saving perspectives. As nanoparticle have great potential to improve the thermal transport properties compared to conventional particles fluids suspension, millimeter and micrometer sized particles, therefore nanofluids have gained significant attention due to their enhanced thermal properties. Experimental studies show that thermal conductivity of nanofluids depends on many factors such as particle volume fraction, particle material, particle size, particle shape, base fluid material, and temperature. Amount and types of additives and the acidity of the nanofluid are also shown to be effective in the thermal conductivity enhancement. 
Project is divided into four quarters

data.projectName: Identification of Groundwater Recharging Zone(s) in Twin Cities of Pakistan: Geophysical & GIS/RS Approaches
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest: Water is one of the critical issues of the world. Surface and groundwater are under huge stress due to rapid growth in population, urbanization and industrialization. Additionally, climate change worsens the already deteriorating condition in term of lack of precipitation and torrential floods caused by disproportionate melting of glaciers. It is, therefore, need of time to adopt strategy to encounter climatic changes and make sustainable management for natural resources. In the era of computer, hydrology and hydrogeological data need to gather and make analysis to understand water status for upcoming years and to devise policies to encounter issue. Groundwater development and management mainly depends on the groundwater recharge. Groundwater recharge is essential in regions with low natural groundwater recharge mechanism. In this projects, latest geophysical and remote sensing techniques will be utilized for identification of groundwater recharge zones in twin cities of Pakistan, which are facing acute shortage of groundwater for domestic and industrial purposes. In order to accomplish the project objects, geophysical, geological, remote sensing, water chemistry data will be acquired more than 100 different sites within twin cities to identify groundwater recharge zones. Both recharge zones and water quality data will be helpful to provide future direction for safe drinking water projects in the study area.

data.projectName: Decision Making Framework using Pythagorean Fuzzy Soft Graphs
data.projectDigest: Mathematical modeling, computing of decision making problems and analysis involving uncertainty is one of the most interesting areas of interdisciplinary research, involving computational intelligence, applied mathematics and decision sciences. The aim of this research is to construct the framework for handling Pythagorean fuzzy (involving vagueness) information by applying the concept of  soft sets to graphs. We develop multiple attribute decision making methods based on Pythagorean fuzzy soft graphs. These mathematical tools give more precision, flexibility and compatibility of the system when compared to systems that are designed using fuzzy graphs and fuzzy soft graphs. The significance of our Pythagorean fuzzy soft graphs lies in the fact that such graphs represent graph theoretic problems from the viewpoint of parameters could be used to simulate human decision making processes which are certainly imprecise or not totally reliable. We also describe these methods as an algorithm.

data.projectName: Efficacy of Psychobiotics in treating ante-natal and post-partum anxiety and depression: PROTECT-D, a randomized controlled trial
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
The aim of this study is to evaluate safe treatment options for anxiety and/or depression during pregnancy and lactation as conventional treatment options have certain demerits. Sertraline is one of the safest drug that can be given both in pregnancy and during lactation however it is also reported to have adverse effects (including septal defects and respiratory system disorders). The safety profile of other anti-depressants especially Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (SSRIs) are not much promising. Similarly, in a resource-limited setting like Pakistan where healthacare system is struggling to provide basic necessities of healthcare, individual counseling is not very practical. cyclopropeneimine based organocatalysts that will be synthesized and applied to promote a wide range

catalysts (shown in figure 1) feature several major advantages, such as the presence of strongly basic
cyclopropenimines and strong hydrogen bond donors within the same chiral framework. After the

practical application of this these catalysts will be demonstrated in the asymmetric synthesis of the
flavaglines which are a medicinally appealing yet synthetic challenging class of natural products.
Amongst others, flavagline, the main member of the class flavaglines itself has shown a strong
anticancer activity1 Furthermore, when used in combination with the strong anti-tumor drug named
doxorubicin, the major side effect of doxorubicin (heart damage) is significantly suppressed.

It involves optimization of plant extraction regarding temperature and time and synthesis of monodispersed nanoparticles using these plants extract. data.projectName: Women Acceptability at Workplace
data.projectDigest:
Women acceptability in the workplace is a research plus sensitization training project submitted to Higher Education Commission (HEC) Pakistan under the aegis of National Research Programme for Universities (NRPU). In this project, researchers are interested to understand the structure and mental architecture that is underpinned the attitudes and behaviors among different genders that results in gender based discrimination and violence especially against women at workplace and hinder their workplace performance and general contribution to the society. 
In the later phase, sensitization workshops shall be arranged in order to sensitize individuals for tolerance and acceptability of opposite gender especially at workplace. The contents of the workshop shall be made and based directly in accordance with the findings of the results of the research at first phase of the project.  
Textile industry of Karachi was specifically selected to study this phenomenon.

data.projectName: Gut microbiota configuration in healthy Pakistani children
data.projectDigest: Malnutrition is a devastated problem of children living in low middle income countries.  A high proportion of children suffer from malnutrition and do not reach to their full potential in adulthood, and carry a high economic burden on country.  Among several underlying causes of malnutrition, such as food insecurity, access to safe drinking water and poor living conditions, unhealthy gut is the primary cause of malnutrition in young children.  Studies have shown that normal flora of gut play an important role in normal physiological functioning of the gut as well as support linear growth of children.  Our gut has trillions of healthy bacterial communities which makes up our microbiome.  Very little is known about healthy microbiome of Pakistani children, as longitudinal sampling is required to study microbiome development in young children.  We think that it is essential to have normal features of gut microbiome of children under two years of age as a reference to study microbiome of children in dysbiotic state such as malnutrition.  This project is focused on understanding the gut microbiome of healthy children living in an urban setting to compare the changes in the gut microbiome of children living in a rural setting.

data.projectName: A Unified Framework for Benchmarking Deepfakes Generation and Detection Algorithms
data.projectDigest: Integrity and authentication of digital media is a problem that concerns national security, the financial industry, voice-activated smart services, the intelligence community, and the public. Techniques for digital multimedia integrity and authentication are critical, as digital multimedia have become the main source of deception (by doctoring the multimedia objects). This project aims to design innovative techniques for digital multimedia integrity and authentication, performance evaluation in the presence of multiple deepfake attacks, design and development of a large-scale unified deepfakes dataset including both audio and visual forgeries, and countermeasures to mitigate impacts of anti-forensic attacks. Together, these techniques will provide answers to fundamental questions related to evidentiary recording, that is, where (it was captured), how (it was tampered), and what (is the attacker’s strategy, if any). As an outcome of the proposed research, we will develop a research common – a benchmarking dataset and forensics analysis platform which the multimedia forensics research community desperately needs. This project will have a significant impact in multiple areas, including civil and criminal proceedings, media, politics, business, social media, and science. The outcomes of the proposed research project will provide the novel fundamental concepts for deepfakes generation and detection.

data.projectName: Strategic management framework of mountain resources for sustainable development in Upper Indus Basin, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Sustainable mountain development does not receive the attention and priority it deserves despite of the evident importance of mountain areas. The main goal of sustainable mountain development is that mountain ecosystems be managed in ways that allow them to provide goods and services for local livelihoods and lowland people, now and in the future. A detailed analysis and investigation will be performed to find out physical, hydro-climatic and socio-economic characteristics of the proposed project area from the available ground and satellite data by using integrated approach of remote sensing & GIS and different time series models. The available all renewable and non-renewable mountain resources will be find out and investigated. The different mountain problems will be chalked out.  A detailed analysis will be performed to develop adoptable best management framework of resources to uplift the socio-economic condition of the community for the sustainable development of the region. To ensure bilateral stakeholder involvement and partnerships at all levels – land users, technical experts and policy-makers in identifying and implementation of projects/ research. In a challenging environment full of economic recessions the provided research will help to conserve the mountain resources through sustainable development and hence improve the wellbeing of the mountain communities.

data.projectName: Computational modelling of progressive damage in traditional Timber Braced Frame (TBF) structures.
data.projectDigest: Timber braced frame (TBF) structures have shown good performance under seismic loading in the past earthquakes in Pakistan. Seismic vulnerability analysis and design of these structures depends on accurate numerical analysis. This can be achieved through reliable computational models which are able to simulate complex failure mechanisms and their interactions. The aim of this research project is to develop a numerical framework for the analysis of timber braced frame structures. In particular, the effect of infill panels on the response of structure will be modelled. This will be achieved using the Applied Element Method (AEM) approach. The numerical model will be calibrated against experimental test data performed in University of Engineering and Technology (UET), Peshawar. The proposed study will be helpful for the students, researchers and design engineers to understand the damage mechanics and performance of TBF structures.

data.projectName: Reforming University Venture Creation Model In Pakistan
data.projectDigest: There is abundant literature on venture creation, incubation, role of universities and public policy towards promotion of startups. The literature considers many aspects from institutional, governance, and academic perspectives and builds a rationale for the existence or refinement of existing models. The present study aims to understand the existing venture creation model of universities in Pakistan and work towards helping policy in refining or reforming this prevailing model by research based information. The idea is to understand the limitations of university spinoffs and orient policy to the dividends of an ideal venture creation model that the universities may adhere to. Reforming the model is deemed to have economic, social, and governing benefits.

data.projectName: Application of micronutrients through seed invigoration techniques in lentil
data.projectDigest:
Micronutrients are important for human health and equally play a significant role in plant growth and development.  Adequate micronutrient supply not only ensured plant growth but also increase grain partitioning. These micronutrients are added in plant via foliar application and or through soil addition in all developed world with their own economic and environmental issues. Seed invigoration with micronutrients by priming and coating of seed is an easy alternative. Soaking of seed in micronutrient solution or surface adherence with micronutrient plus inert material is carried out in both methods. These techniques of invigoration will be standardized for optimization of lentil crop with micronutrients (Zinc, Boron) in this study. The techniques so developed will be then evaluated in field trials in comparison with soil and foliar application for physiology, yield and micronutrient grain enrichment in lentil. Finding of this proposal will provide an easy and economical way for micronutrient application lentil crop. Lentil seeds will be treated with micronutrients (Zn, B) using various sources as seed priming (at different rates and durations) and seed coating (with different nutrient:seed ratios). Treated and un-treated seeds will be sown in petri plates and sand filled pots. Treatments will be evaluated on the basis of seed germination rate and uniformity and early seedling growth. Lentil seeds will be treated with optimized and developed techniques and will be then sown in soil-filled earthen pots placed in glass house. After applying the micronutrient seed invigoration techniques developed during first year, lentil will be sown at the Bahauddin Zakariya University. Micronutrient application as soil incorporation and foliar spray will also be included as control.

data.projectName: Establishment of Arid Zones Botanical Garden (AZBG) for scientific and educational value
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: The project of Arid Zones Botanical Garden (AZBG) is important in current scenario of plant diversity loss due to anthropogenic activities, resulting decline in ecosystem services. The pressure of land use and climate change is especially affecting the people living in the arid areas because of already limited resources. This botanical garden would act as an institution that holds documented collection of living (garden) and preserve (herbarium) plant specimens for the purpose of scientific research and education. Botanical garden will includes plant nursery, a seed bank, a herbarium and green house. It is therefore, not merely a botanical garden but a botanical institution. Botanical garden will spread on 3.44 hectares (already reserved area at campus) which will be scientifically divided into family wise cultivation (38 plant families in Cholistan desert) of economically important arid plant species. This botanical garden will contribute toward infrastructure development to institutional capacity building in Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology (KFUEIT), Rahim Yar Khan. The large number of students will get benefits from this garden every year. This project will eventually contribute in the local as well as country’s economy by screening and improvement of superior economically important arid plant species.

data.projectName: Lifestyle management of obese young Pakistani population with special reference to physical activity and dietary modifications
data.projectDigest: Current research is designed to compare the combined effect of physical activity and dietary modification on BMI in obese persons. In phase I, 5000 subjects will be screened to assess the prevalence of obesity on the basis of their BMI (30 and above) and age (18-29 years) from five government and private universities of Faisalabad. Self-structured questionnaire will be given to the screened students. After fulfillment of predefined inclusion/exclusion criteria and informed consent, awareness workshop regarding obesity, its related complications and possible treatments (mainly diet and physical activity) will be conducted in venue suitable for all recruited students, in phase II. In Phase III, interventions regarding physical therapy and dietary modifications will be done. Recommended Canadian base physical activity guidelines and dietary guidelines for Americans will be followed to reduce the body mass index in obese young Pakistani population. After the commencement of physical therapy and dietary interventions, assessment will be done at 4th week, 8th week, 12th week, 16th week, 20th week and 24th week. Moreover, after the one month of discontinuation of study, follow up will be done. At obtained data for each parameter will be subjected for appropriate statistical design to determine the level of significance.

data.projectName: Development and Implementation  of Telemedicine for Health Care Sector in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest:

The remote accessible medical center for accurate diagnosis and treatment established for patients with the help of technology named as telemedicine. The proposed system will be time and cost efficient for quality medical care.
Moreover, this research will highlight the limitations and challenges encountered during development and implementation of telemedicine in Pakistani socioeconomic environment. The major impact of this research will provide a potential roadmap to overcome the aforementioned issues. The authorities (private and government) will need to revisit their laws and regulations to enable the telemedicine environment in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Externalities in Public Utility Project
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The construction projects, although, acknowledge the existence of associated social cost but it is not inlcuded in the estimation process of the project. The bid price by contractors does not incorporate the externalities of the construction. Therefore, the social costs are undertaken the people living, passing or working in close proximity. This study would be based on estimating and analysing some of the social costs associated with the construction work of Green Line project in Karachi. The project was announced in 2014 to alleviate the traffic congestion issue in the metropolitan city and to improve the living standard of Karachiites. The construction work of this Rapid Bus Transit system seems to be unending and it has badly affected the road infrastructure and nearby people. This study is based on identifying and assessing the social costs of Green Line Project in Karachi in terms of traffic and economic activities. The research would use primary sources of data through survey and observation methods. The results of this study would help the concerned authorities in considering the estimation of social cost of any public utility project in its construction and development phase. It would also allow improved evaluation and ranking of a development project.

The bid price by contractors does not incorporate the externalities of the construction. Therefore, the social costs are undertaken the people living, passing or working in close proximity. This study would be based on estimating and analysing some of the social costs associated with the construction work of Green Line project in Karachi. The project was announced in 2014 to alleviate the traffic congestion issue in the metropolitan city and to improve the living standard of Karachiites. The construction work of this Rapid Bus Transit system seems to be unending and it has badly affected the road infrastructure and nearby people. This study is based on identifying and assessing the social costs of Green Line Project in Karachi in terms of traffic and economic activities. The research would use primary sources of data through survey and observation methods. The results of this study would help the concerned authorities in considering the estimation of social cost of any public utility project in its construction and development phase. It would also allow improved evaluation and ranking of a development project.

data.projectName: Residual Power Series Method for  Solving Time Fractional  Conformable Fractional Differential Equations
data.projectDigest: In simple words differential equations represent a real world phenomenon in mathematical form. Differential equations are unquestionably important to modern science and engineering. Almost all of the known laws of physics and chemistry are actually differential equations, and differential equations are used extensively in biochemical reactions, nuclear physics, ecology, fluid dynamics, biology, solid state of physics, population dynamics, organism growth, and the spread of diseases etc.   Recently, most of the real world phenomenon can describe better using fractional calculus, generalization of classical calculus. In this Project, we emphasize fractional differential equations appearing in various disciplines; for instance like optical fibers, nuclear physics, ecology, fluid dynamics, biology, solid state of physics and quantum field theory, and are also concerned with rigorously justifying methods for solving them. To explore new possibilities for the solutions of such equations is the basic aim of this project so that we can describe better a real world phenomenon in mathematical form.

data.projectName: SCREENING OF NOVEL NON-EDIBLE OIL SEED PLANTS FOR SUSTAINABLE BIO ENERGY PRODUCTION
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Bioenergy is an attractive solution for offsetting fossil fuels for a number of different reasons. From an economic and social perspective edible seed oils should be substituted by non-edible, which are affirmed to be lower cost and reliable seed oils for bio energy production. Pakistan is an agriculture country; however a vast area of the country is facing the problems of salinity and drought. Pakistan has an area about 28 million hectare which is marginal and underutilized, this land can be purposefully utilized for the growing non edible oil yielding plants. According to literature survey this is the first comprehensive research based on the identification and utilization of the novel indigenous non-edible seed sources by using ultrasonic and microwave assisted for bio energy production on batch scale which will lead to a scale up production at commercial level.  This research will focus on exploration of the local non-edible seeds from the whole country and their taxonomic study, seed oil estimation and fatty acid profiling, novel catalyst  synthesis from plastic waste and characterization, research parameters for reaction time, temperature, catalyst loading and their effect on yield will be optimized by response surface methodology. and fuel standardization.

data.projectName: Evaluating the effect of Vitamin D on the production of irisin and elucidating the role of irisin on HPG-axis
data.projectDigest:
Irisin, a derivative of FNDC5 and Vitamin D, secosteroid metabolic factor are touted as endocrine hormones. Irisin and VDR (Vitamin D Receptors) are co-expressing in several tissues and influence neural proliferation, differentiation, maturation, energy balance and reproduction. Irisin is found to increase the expression of brown adipose tissue (BAT) and increase thermogenesis. While vitamin D is acting as an opponent of irisin by switching-off UCP1 expression. Studies have also shown various effects and expression of irisin and vitamin D in reproductive tissues. Co-expression of irisin and VDR in common tissues for example Brain tissues are suggesting that vitamin D is regulating irisin production either positively or negatively. Furthermore, similar functions of vitamin D and irisin in reproduction and observed expression of both irisin and vitamin D receptor in the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus, having GnRH neurons suggesting a link of irisin and vitamin D with reproduction. 
Hence it is hypothesized that i) There is some sort of relation between irisin and vitamin D and vitamin D is either positively or negatively regulating irisin production, ii) Irisin might be involved in the regulation of HPG- axis, and iii) Irisin might be regulating the production of kisspeptin in the KNDy neurons.

data.projectName: Multi-scale numerical investigation of graphene based continuous fiber reinforced polymer hybrid composites
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: The notion of industry 4.0 is all about the well-connectivity and smartness of the industry and its response to the needs of the society. The application of graphene towards smart and well-connected products, particularly in aerospace, is increasing due its excellent intrinsic characteristics such as higher electrical and thermal conductivity in addition to higher strength, and lighter in weight. European Union under its one of the biggest scientific initiatives ‘Graphene Flagship’ is investing 1 billion euros in exploring the applications of graphene in the next-generation products, and the investment is increasing rigorously over the years after the demonstration of promising results shown by graphene. Till-date, graphene has been predominantly used for sensors and thermal management, but its installation in the load bearing aero-structures have not been explored yet in spite of its superlative mechanical properties. Designers can exploit a combination of properties of interest to realize a single multifunctional component using graphene. For instance, a single part based on the graphene can act as a structural component while at the same time as a heatsink, and or an electrical sensor. The multi-functionality of a single part, as a result, will minimize the number of parts required and also will simplify the manufacturing cycle. The current research proposal will only focus on the numerical modeling of this hybrid composite under the external loading employing multi-scale approach.

data.projectName: Trauma care improvement through an IT solution for Orthopaedic outcomes data management and reporting
data.projectDigest:
In order to improve treatment of trauma victims, organised data needs to be collected. In Pakistan there is no country-wide trauma data system . We require a comprehensive and reliable data solution that is sustainable and is integrated with hospital trauma care systems, and can provide information about safety, effectiveness and cost effectiveness of care of injured patients. We hypothesize that an appropriate hospital trauma data management system can improve quality of trauma care by identifying suboptimal outcomes and treatment gaps.
Objectives:
1.	To develop a system of organized data management in our hospital as a source of data for assessing patient demographics, injuries and outcomes of treatment of trauma victims
2.	To enable continuous monitoring of quality of care data, permitting determination of areas requiring improvement in health care provision to trauma patients
3.	To evaluate clinical, radiological and functional outcomes

data.projectName: Multiple Imputation in Generalized Linear Models for High-dimensional Data
data.projectDigest: Multiple Imputation (MI) is the most commonly used imputation technique to impute the missing data. In case of Generalized Linear Models (GLM), Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) is used that demands a limited number of predictors in the imputation model to obtain the valid parameter estimates. In high-dimensional data, however, the parameter estimates are not stable when p approaches to n and the problems becomes more severe with p?n, where it is not possible to fit the imputation model. To address this issue we are combining the penalization techniques for GLMs with the chained equations imputation approach to select the imputation model and also fitting of the selected model to impute the missing values.  The  performance of the proposed techniques will be tested and compared  with the existing MI approaches using imputation error and Mean Squared Errors in a simulation study and a real data collected under a case-control study to explore the significant risk factors of asthma in major cities of Punjab.

data.projectName: Development of Irrigation Scheduling system in Cotton crop of Punjab using earth Observation data and crop Modeling (DISCOM)
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan, lot of water is wasted due to inefficient use of water during irrigation. Farmers are mostly unaware how much exact water is needed and when it is the most suitable time to provide water to crops. Mostly, they supply water to crops when it is their turn. This project brings innovation and smart practices by introducing concept of scheduling of irrigated water by using satellite based information of fields and crop water requirement based on real time information about crop health, status, soil, and prevailing weather. This research work will harness freely available satellite data and crop models to assess all needs of crops in order to communicate all information to farmers in form of visuals so that even illiterate farmers may understand all the information regarding their crop water requirement through their mobile phones.

data.projectName: A Combined Theoretical and Experimental Study of Optoelectronic and Thermophysical Properties of Ternary Topological Materials: Influence of Rare-earths and Actinides
data.projectDigest: The energy efficient thermoelectric materials (TEMs) have attracted much attention having ability to recover waste heat and generate thermoelectric power for energy applications in devices like thermocouples, solar cells, batteries, etc. The proposed research project is aimed to explore, both experimentally and theoretically, the optoelectronic, thermophysical and topological properties of some new rare-earth/actinide based chalcogenides and pnictides from the series: Re(Ac)PnCh (Re = Rare-earth;; Ac = Actinides;; Ch = Chalcogen). A material with figure of merit equal to unity is usually considered an efficient TEM. We will implement first-principles DFT formalism to calculate the desired properties, as implemented in WIEN2k package. Binary metal chalcogenides such as Bi2Te3 and Bi2Se3 have been reported as excellent TEMs as well as have properties of topological insulators (Tis). Recently, actinide based binary monochalcogenides PuCh (Ch = Se, Te) and monopnictides AmPn (Pn = N, P, Sb, and Bi) have been reported to have topological properties. More recently, first-principles calculations predicted that thorium based ternary chalcogenides namely ThOS, ThOSe, and ThOTe have prominent topological, optical and thermoelectric properties. For the comparative analysis of our theoretical predictions, we will also synthesize some of the compositions of the aforementioned compounds experimentally via standard solid state methods.

data.projectName: Discovery of new antibacterial compounds from Actinomycetes isolated from indigenous insects
data.projectDigest: Antibiotics have saved so many human lives since the discovery of penicillin in 1945. However, emerging antibiotic resistance in disease-causing bacteria in the last few decades had left no choice of therapeutics. One such extreme example is recent outbreak of ceftriaxone-resistant typhoid in Southern parts of Pakistan. For last so many years ceftriaxone and cefixime were “drugs of choice” for the treatment of typhoid but now they have become useless. If this situation prevails, we may lose the efficacy of all available antibiotics in future against common bacterial infections like diarrhea, sore throat, wound and skin infection. The most common source of most of the available antibiotics is a specialized class of filamentous bacteria called Actinomycetes which were mostly isolated from soil. But unfortunately it looks like that this source is depleted as no new class of antibiotic was discovered in the last three decades. Recently, Actinomycetes isolated from insects has been shown as a promising source of new antibiotics. In this project we are proposing to isolate Actinomycetes from locally found insects and then screen them for the discovery of novel antibacterial compounds to combat with the rising threat of antibiotic resistance.

data.projectName: In order to enable the developing country to set a trend
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Type 2 diabetes is the most common form of diabetes mellitus. The aim of this study is to  develop  and  standardize  the  polyhedral  formulation  (granule)  and  checked  its  efficacy  with regards to type 2 diabetes. The alcoholic extract of herbal plants having anti-diabetic activity will be formulated by wet granulation method. FTIR will be done to investigate the presence of active compounds. Physicochemical properties of granules will be evaluated, and antidiabetic potential will be substantiated through inhibition of carbohydrate digestive enzyme such as ?-amylase and ?-glucosidase, glucose uptake activity in yeast cells and antioxidant activity. IR spectra is expected to indicate the presence of active compounds such as phenols  and  amines  and expected to  show  the  absence  of  interaction  between  drug  and  excipients.  The dissolution profile of active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) from granules will be examined to determine the drug release profile.  Granules  which  will exhibit  better  inhibition  of  ?-amylase  and  ?-glucosidase  as  on comparison  with  the  standard  drug  will be taken as dose  dependent molecules.  The  stabilized  formulation  (granules)  will be  formed and  the presence  of  active  compounds will be  responsible  for  the  better  antidiabetic  activity  which will  inhibit carbohydrate digesting enzymes. Hence, it could lower the post prandial hyperglycemia and has the potential to use for the treatment of type II diabetes prior to determine the dose regime.

data.projectName: Distribution and susceptibility to disinfectants of clinically important bacteria isolated from the hospital environment and determination of infection prevention and control practices in tertiary care hospitals in Lahore
data.projectDigest: Decontamination of the hospital environment using proper disinfectants is one of the key components of infection prevention and control (IPC). Defective IPC practices and the use of ineffective disinfectants during everyday healthcare delivery make healthcare facilities dangerous places for disease and outbreaks amplification. Healthcare associated infections (HAI) are among the most serious public health problems of the 21st century. It is very important and crucial to record infection prevention and control (IPC) practices, find out the susceptibility of pathogens isolated from the hospital environment to commonly used disinfectants and figure out the genetic basis of reduced susceptibility towards disinfectants and association of biocide resistance genes with antimicrobial resistance genes. In this study, we aim to record IPC practices using Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s (CDC) infection control assessment tool. The clinically important bacteria will be isolated from the long-term care facilities (frequently touched surfaces, medical equipment, patient’s immediate surroundings, and ward sinks) of different tertiary care hospitals in Lahore. data.projectName: Clinical efficacy in relieving dentin hypersensitivity of novel Bioactive glasses containing dentifrices-A randomized clinical trial
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Dentin hypersensitivity (DH) is a clinical condition with acute pain of short duration that adversely influences the patient’s daily life. Clinical management of DH has been a challenging issue for dental practitioners. Numerous over the counter and in-office desensitization formulations including potassium, fluoride, arginine, strontium, bi-fluorides, Casein phosphopeptide–amorphous calcium phosphate and recently introduced bioactive glasses have been advocated clinically and claimed commercially for immediate and sustained treatment of DH   without definitive outcome. Currently no gold standard treatment modality and product for DH is available worldwide. Clinical testing is essentially required to substantiate the claims of these products, to seek out permanent management of DH without industrial influences and its potential impact on the patient’s daily life by altering physical such as dietary habits, functional such as speaking and social status. 
The aim of this study is to compare three different formulations of dentifrices; these are 8% Arginine, 8% Strontium acetate and fluoro-calcium-phospho-silicate bioactive glass to measure their clinical effectiveness for immediate and sustained reduction in the pain of DH and to evaluate the changes in the physiological and personal experiences from DH with improvement in the status of the participants oral health related quality of life (OHrQOL).

data.projectName: Rice Grain Inspector for Export Quality Monitoring
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is a major exporter of rice across the world and to maintain the image of efficient exporter, the rice quality must be maintained in international market. The continuous low quality can damage this image as an exporter and cause the country to lose the major earnings. The seeds, shapes and sizes including texture, humidity, and color are important factors to indicate the rice quality. These factors determine the eating quality, agriculture properties, and market value of rice. Manual and visual methods are still being used in rice industry for the quality control. These methods need manual authenticity and neutrality in a rival rice industry, which is based on environmental conditions and facilities of an expert. These manual methods are time-consuming, tedious, require man-power and resulting inconsistent outcomes that are very hard to predict the quality of rice grains. As a result, it is needed to develop an automated inspection system for rice quality, type and market value, which can determine these factors quickly, efficiently and effectively at lower cost. We have proposed an automated rice inspector for real time prediction that can predict the type, quality and price of rice grains.

The potent extracts of various plants may be mixed with one another to formulate a drug which is effective against all possible bacterial strains responsible for sepsis. The invented drug may resolve the worldwide issue of sepsis and will find an excellent market value.
