data.projectName: Design and Synthesis of organic-inorganic Hybrid scaffoldings for the fabrication of energy storage devices
data.projectDigest: Energy crisis is one of the biggest challenges of 21st century and Pakistan is the victim of this calamity. Energy challenges revolve around the reliable production, storage and distribution. As a material scientist, this project is a sincere effort in this regard to tackle this problem and to devise some efficient ways to store this valuable electrical energy. Rechargeable batteries and supercapacitors are the potential candidates for energy storage. Organic-Inorganic hybrid materials are a new class of functional materials. This project aims to design and synthesize porous organic-inorganic hybrid scaffoldings by exploiting bridging ligands and reducing metals. A team of experts comprising of students and faculty members will work and synthesis of desired materials will be executed using different synthetic strategies. Later these materials will be characterized by existing lab facilities available at the campus and with the help of collaborators. After complete characterization, these materials will be employed for the fabrication of supercapacitor and lithium batteries. It is expected that strategic design and fabrication of these devices will yield some reliable, cost effective, high performance and environmentally benign energy storage devices. Power and energy sector will be directly benefitted by this project.

data.projectName: Exploring the Genetic Basis of Bardet-Biedl Syndrome in a Pakistani Family
data.projectDigest: Bardet-Biedl Syndrome (BBS) is an autosomal recessive genetic disorder. It is also called ciliopathy or a disease of the cilia. Defects in cilia result in syndromic form of BBS. Cilia are cell surface structures involved in cellular motility, sensory reception and developmental signaling. Due to localization of cilia in different organs, ciliary defects cause multisystem disorders. The primary clinical features of BBS include loss of vision, extra  finger in hands and/or toes, obesity, learning difficulties, renal dysfunction and genital malformation. Patients bearing at least 4 out of 6 primary features or 3 primary features with 2 secondary features are required to confirm the presence of BBS.  Uptill now, 21 genes have been identified to be involved in the BBS disease manifestation that encode BBS proteins important for ciliary formation and function due to the mutations in BBS genes causing BBS phenotypes. data.projectName: Structural and functional diversity of bacterial communities in the rhizosphere of potato crop
data.projectDigest: Environmental problems and increasing fertilizer prices have developed a worldwide attention to reduce the use of fertilizers for optimum yields. Several studies are now testing the hypothesis that plant beneficial rhizosphere bacteria enable agricultural plants to maintain productivity with reduced rates of fertilizer application. Rhizosphere bacteria promote plant growth by several mechanisms including nitrogen fixation, phytohormones production, phosphate solubilization, and antibiotics, siderophore, amino acids and vitamins production. These bacteria as a component of integrated nutrient management system can also help to reduce the buildup of nutrients in fertilized soil. Potatoes  are  one  of  the  world's  major  food  after  rice,  wheat,  and  corn  but  potatoes  is  relatively insensitive to losses due to pathogens, drought, and low nutrient availability. Plant  Growth  Promoting  Rhizobacteria  (PGPR)  could be a potential source as  biostimulant  effort,  biofertilizer  and  bioprotectant.  These bacteria are actively colonize the rhizosphere around the root surface and provide a positive influence to spur growth plants by providing nutrients and hormones to the plant and can be antagonistic to bacterial and fungal pathogens. These bacteria have the ability to provide and facilitate the absorption  of  various  nutrients  such  as  nitrogen  and  phosphate  in  the  soil  as  well  as  synthesize phytohormones hyper growth. The present study has been planned to monitor and incorporate the biocontrol strategies by using biochemical and advanced molecular biology techniques. This study will help to understand the interaction of rhizosphere in potato field which will imply to improve the plant growth, productivity and reduce the farmer cost at field.

data.projectName: Determining feasibility of a model of care for secondary fracture prevention for implementation in health care system in Pakistan after hip fracture: a clinical outcome study
data.projectDigest:
Osteoporosis is the most common non-communicable (NCD) bone disease. However, osteoporosis and bone health issues have been neglected in Pakistan.There is an urgent need to spread awareness and build national health programs to check this problem in a systematic manner to promote social accountability, equity and justified allocation of resources.  We propose to determine feasibility of evaluating different models of care through a structured multidisciplinary path tailored to identify, assess and treat hip fracture patients in an effective timely manner that are at high risk of subsequent fracture (Type A model) and to compare its effectiveness and feasibility with a type B, C & D model as proposed by Ganda et al. Patients with hip fractures will be included in different models of SFP. Fracture risk assessment will be conducted and intervention performed as per protocol. Regular quarterly clinical case discussions and quality audits will be conducted. Assessment of the knowledge gained during this will be conducted at regular intervals in case discussions for patients monitoring.

Based on this study we will propose a model of care for SFP for application at national level in private and public sector. Our long term plan is to develop a National fragility fracture network in preventing and managing fragility fractures and to promote research aimed at better treatments of osteoporosis, sarcopenia and fracture. This information will also help us in applying clinical practice guidelines for osteoporosis and driving policy change for our country which is currently non-existent and is likely to be a step towards the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) (i.e. ensure healthy lives and promote wellbeing for all at all ages).

data.projectName: Reflection of Art and Culture of Pakistan in Shahnameh Firdousi through literature and illustration
data.piUniversity: Lahore College for Women University, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
The Shahnameh-e- Firdowsi(Book of Kings) is an epic composed by the Iranian poet Hakim Abul-Qasim Mansur (later known as Firdowsi Tusi), and completed around 1010 CE.
The epic chronicles the legends and histories of Iranian (Aryan) kings from primordial times to the Arab conquest of Iran in the 7th century CE, in three successive stages: the mythical, the heroic or legendary, and the historic. The Shahnameh was written in classical Persian when the language was emerging from its Middle Persian Pahlavi roots.
There are many relevancies between Shahnameh and art of Sindh & Hindh. As our Urdu language also the combinations of different languages in which Persian is the most important because we observed it’s writing style “Khat” and Pronunciation of some words has the utmost resemblance with Urdu. Many words in Urdu are derived from original Persian in which the names of renowned Personalities, places, things, festivals & names of books are included and still we are using it in Pakistan and India. The illustrate visuals depicted in Shahnameh represents the style and traditions of that particular era and it’s through this project it will be traced out the inspiration carried out by developed society in our region. The illustration of various characters present in Shahnameh is the amalgamation of aesthetics and artistic skills. In this research project we will discover their common Art, Language, Culture and Historical backgrounds which we can observe in Pakistan and India.

data.projectName: Experimental Investigation to Improve Seismic Performance of Masonry using Bond Beam and Horizontal Reinforcement in Mortar Joint
data.projectDigest:
In recent Mirpur Kashmir earthquake, September, 2019 severe damages to the buildings were observed in the affected area nearby epicenter. Most of the damages that were observed in post-earthquake visit to the area included cracks/failure at the reentrant corners of the openings and in masonry infilled walls. The objective of this study is to improve the seismic performance of masonry buildings by imparting bond beam and horizontal reinforcement and to develop its design and application guidelines. To achieve these objectives, a number of quasi-static cyclic loading test and shake table tests will be performed on masonry wall and scaled building specimens. 
The explored techniques can be utilized and implemented in future by involvement of policy making relevant government authorities. This project will directly benefit the construction and material manufacturing industries in Pakistan. The application of proposed technique will reduce the long-term maintenance/repairing cost of the masonry which are required for the rehabilitation of earthquake damage buildings. The guidelines proposed by the study will bring the regularity in construction practices.
The knowledge and resources of academic collaborator will be utilized in extensive experimental work involved in the research project. The sectoral collaborators in the project were involved with aim for successful completion and implementation of the project as government authority.

data.projectName: Development and implementation of new scale and business model for the ecotourism in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: We will develop and implement a new scale and business model for the ecotourism in Pakistan by achieving eight objectives: first, to conduct a thematic analysis of the existing literature on the mores of customer base (or tourists); second, to invite both academicians and practitioners to develop the mutually agreed intended meanings and breadth of the theoretical concepts; third, to develop a scale of construct(s) and refine through statistical analysis of their applicability on the customers (or tourists); fourth, to validate the refined scaled construct(s) and explore their pathway role; fifth, to formulate strategies for a new business model; sixth, to execute the new business model; seventh, to observe the performance of newly executed business model for one year; last, to conclude by taking overall discussion into perspective. For Pakistan, this project is critical as the policy makers have started to realize that without incorporating the concept of ‘eco’ into plans, the formation of strategies to develop Pakistani tourism market cannot be a big success. Moreover, the real meaning of the concept ‘eco’ varies exceptionally among entrepreneurs in Pakistan. Furthermore, the current situation of Pakistani tourism market allows a wide open space for the entry of new business models.

data.projectName: Contributing towards Professional Development of Teachers through Practicum in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Like all other professions, teachers have to show professionalism, that is, they have to attain the highest caliber of teaching quality and standards. Though, for Pakistani educators, it might be difficult to attain but it is not impossible to come up to these standards or benchmarks. They might be acquired with little effort and proper training. Currently in Pakistan, It needs some pre-requisites varying from field to field and occupation to occupation. Similarly, in Pakistan, for entry into teaching at various levels, requirements are different. For instance, being a faculty member at any varsity, a research based qualification is compulsory now days; and for being a school educator graduation along with B. Ed is mandatory. The existing teaching practicum for almost all programs of teacher education in Pakistan is traditional which is supposed to be ineffective. Some of the mandatory aspects of teaching professionalism are:
“Honesty, Integrity, Transparency, Accountability, Confidentiality, Communication Skills, Interactive Skills, Objectivity, Punctuality, Regularity, Respect for others, Obedience to law, Loyalty, Ownership, Productivity, Sense of responsibility, and Social skills.”  Therefore, in this situation, these discrete components need to be studied through pre-service training, that is, practicum as they are found rare and need to be developed by practicum.

data.projectName: Molecular epidemiology and antibiotic resistance (phenotypes and genotypes)of zoonotic Salmonella typhimurium, enteritidis and infantis from poultry food chain and humans in Punjab
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Zoonotic Non typhoidal Salmonella is one of the major causes of food poisoning in human population. Humans can get infection by handling or consuming food (particularly of poultry origin) contaminated with these bacteria. The most common symptoms are fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and abdominal cramps. The illness often occurs after 24-48 hours after exposure and illness can become life threatening in children and immunocompromised. The sources and transmission of zoonotic Non Typhoidal Salmonella in developing countries has not been well documented. In the present plan of study different samples from poultry food chain will be collected from three major cites of Punjab. The samples will be consisted of environmental samples and feacal samples from poultry farms and backyard poultry, meat samples from live bird market and retail shops and human stool samples affected with food poisoning from three tertiary care hospitals. The samples will be collected according to standard protocol and transported to Laboratory for isolation and identification of zoonotic Salmonella. The isolates will be confirmed by molecular techniques through multiplex PCR. Antimicrobial resistance of all positive isolates will be performed phenotypically and also at genetic level by identification of resistant genes. For molecular epidemiology subtyping will be performed by multi locus sequence typing (MLST) and ERIC PCR (enterobacterial repetitive Intergenic Consensus) (first time in Pakistan) and phylogenetic analysis will be performed after sequencing. This study will help in estimating the actual burden of zoonotic salmonella serovars rotating in poultry food chain and humans,also its resistance to antimicrobial agents.

data.projectName: Eigenvalues of A? Matrices and their behavior under graph perturbations
data.projectDigest: Graph theory is a branch of mathematics studying real world relationships using matrices.  The eigenvalues and eigenvectors of these matrices give a useful insight about the structure of the graph. Adjacency and signless Laplacian matrices are widely used in this context. A new kind of matrix called Convex Linear Combination of Adjacency and Degree Matrix combines these two most studied matrices into a single matrix as well as open the way for countless many other matrices. The project aims to study the behavior of these new matrices, their relationship to already established results and practices and  any new insights which can be gained.

Successful implementation of the This indigenously developed innovative technology will help to reduce reliance on imported foreign components and thus project will save foreign exchange for the country and will provide local employment by developing our own innovative technology through this project.

data.projectName: Molecular lesions in aplastic anemia and their role in tailoring the treatment in post-genomic era
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Aplastic anemia (AA) is a blood disorder characterized by low blood counts with mortality close to 100% for untreated severe and very severe cases. Treatment options for AA include immunosuppressive therapy and bone marrow transplantation. A prior knowledge of changes in genetic code (mutations) of specific genes has implications in pattern of disease progression, choice of treatment and its outcome.   We plan to design targeted gene sequencing panel of genes including BCOR/BCORL1, PIGA, DNMT3A, ASXL1, TERT, TERC, and HLA class-I and II to identify spectrum of functional mutations in 200 newly diagnosed AA patients registered at Armed Forces Bone Marrow Transplant Centre and Quaid-e-Azam International Hospital. Mutation profiling of these patients will be done at time of diagnosis and suitable treatment will be offered according to their genetic profile. These patients will be followed for 1 year in order to better understand course of disease and treatment outcome. Different therapy-related symptoms and complications will be studied. This study will help in providing a better understanding of genetic basis of AA in our population. It will lead clinicians towards improving disease prognosis through prediction of effectiveness of given treatment and thus tailoring therapies in accordance with their genetic architecture of disease.

data.projectName: Molecular characterization of patients with Bernard Soulier Syndrome
data.projectDigest: Bernard  Soulier Syndrome (BSS) is a recessively inherited severe bleeding disorder caused by the defect in platelet Willibrand receptor, GPIb-V-IX complex due to mutation/s in GP1BB , GP1BA, GP9 and GP5 genes. BSS is characterized by mucocutaneous bleeding, macrothrombocytopenia with absence of platelet aggregation in response of Ristocetine. The understanding of genotype-phenotype correlation of BSS patients is a valuable approach for disease management and futuristic therapy. Therefore, this project is designed to identify the disease-causing mutations in BSS patients and to characterize the identified mutations in GP1BB , GP1BA and GP9 genes using cell biology-based assays. Exome sequencing will be carried out for unidentified BSS families to identify novel genes associated with the disease pathogenicity. Using these approaches, we will be able to establish a complete genetic spectrum of Pakistani BSS patients.  In the end of project, a diagnostic marker will also be established for the prevalent mutations, which will be useful for carrier detection and prenatal diagnosis. Awareness will be provided to all BSS patients through genetic counseling which could be helpful in reducing the burden of genetic disorders from our population where consanguineous marriages are more frequent. Moreover, this study may also be helpful in improving the therapeutic and preventive interventions for the disease.

data.projectName: Academic Corruption: Degree of Integrity in Higher Education
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Corrupt practices in education take place in all over the world; students cheating in examination, higher authority handing over higher position to relative, researcher or faculty plagiarizing text. All such activities require a strong and rigorous response that underlie and develop the actual purpose of these institutions. Corruption leads to the distortions and cheap academic life heading towards meritocratic pathway to social mobility. The aim of higher education is to deliver truth in laboratories and in classrooms. Whatsoever, this purpose cannot be served in an environment where the truth is hemmed in by corrupt practices. It not only distorts the education system but also destructs the benefits that the country had to accrue from its establishment. This study would be based on identifying and assessing corrupt practices prevailing in the education sector of Pakistan. It would employ primary sources of data collection through survey, interviews and cases observed. The indication of prevalence of corruption would allow the federal government to truly allocate the resources to education budget and design policies to prevent the mismanagement of these resources that leave this sector under-resourced.

data.projectName: The impact of ethical leadership and green HRM on employee’s voluntary pro-environmental and societal behaviors: A case of manufacturing industry of Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: The growing worldwide interest in environmentalism has arisen from specific treaties to combat environmental change. Recently, stakeholders (e.g., customers and employees) have been demanding greater environmental responsibility from corporations. As a result, business organizations are shifting their traditional models into green models by implementing green initiatives in their operations, which can be a source of competitive advantage. This research extends the literature by testing the hypothesized relationships in a developing country context (i.e., Pakistan), which is neglected in previous research. The developed and developing countries are different in culture and economic situations; thus, this study offers an opportunity for the researchers to know contrasting conditions. Moreover, Pakistan is at the face of special challenges regarding the environmental pollution. The environmental performance index (EPI) 2018, indicating that Pakistan is ranked on 169/180 countries in environmental performance. There has been a significant increase in environmental pollution in 2016 and Pakistan is among the top 30 countries which are affected by air pollution. According to the economic survey of Pakistan , the estimated environmental degradation may cost Pakistani economy over Rs. 365 billion every year. Furthermore, Pakistan has two of its major cities in the top most polluted cities in the world.

data.projectName: Profiling Energy Poverty across Rural Households of Rawalpindi Division
data.projectDigest: The provision of secure, affordable and modern energy for all citizens is center to poverty reduction and economic growth. Energy has been for some time perceived as basic for mankind to flourish. . Rural households without access to regular energy sources like power and flammable gas, use blends of various energy sources to meet their household energy needs. These blends are frequently alluded to as the energy blend. In Pakistan 45 percent rural household are without electricity and 56 % of people still depends on traditional biomass fuels. Study will evaluate the extent and Energy access of rural households of Rawalpindi Division using Multi-Tier Framework put forward by ESMAP – World Bank at first phase. The empirical estimation would help us in approaching towards UN goals and will also identify the bottlenecks. In the second phase, the awareness/information session/seminars would be done with household that has been included in energy poverty survey. The session would guide them to improve their energy mix and helps them to get themselves out of the energy poverty. Outcomes of the research will be helpful for policy formation at both government and individual level.

data.projectName: Internationalization of Pakistani Exporting Firms
data.projectDigest: SMEs play a vital role in the economic growth and prosperity of nations. The purpose of the project is to investigate the internationalization activities of Pakistani exporters. Research and theory in international business increasingly stress the importance of incorporating the role of international SMEs, particularly, when the export-related activities lead to a firm’s entries, exits and re-entries. To address this, the present project seeks to explore the behaviour of Pakistani exporters during foreign market exit and subsequent re-entry. The aim of this project is to guide current international business thinking towards understanding the issue from the emerging market economy (EME) perspective. Thus, the broad research problem of this thesis is: “What factors influence small-medium sized enterprise (SME) exporters behaviour in the entry, exit and re-entry experiences?” The existing research on the internationalisation process model of the firm has examined the influence of internal and external factors based on forward-moving activities, but has ignored alternative explanations of foreign market exits and subsequent re-entries. An extensive critical literature review revealed that alternative research to the internationalization perspective of developing countries SME exporter is underexplored. Yet little research has been explored the developing economies exporters and their different types of internationalization activities. For the purpose of this research, we employ mixed methodologies qualitative (interviews) and quantitative (survey).

data.projectName: Establishment of Biocontrol agent for the control of Citrus Psylla  and GIS based Ecological Distribution Modeling of Citrus Greening disease and its vector
data.projectDigest: Ecological models of pathogen and its vector help in identifying potential habitats for their spatial distribution and understanding how much the ecological variables contribute in explaining these suitable habitats. This information helps in developing targeted surveillance and development of control strategies. Ecological niche modeling will be carried out by using the evolutionary algorithms implemented in maximum entropy (MaxEnt) to predict the possible hotspots of the disease incidence in different ecological zones. To prepare the prediction models, the locations of disease incidence are recorded and their environmental and ecological parameters are also recorded as the set conducive environmental conditions. Using this ecological data, the models can be designed and validated to test its prediction by collecting the samples from the potential positive locations.  Once the model is validated, it will be used for prediction of disease incidence and will be useful to avoid the epidemic before time and save unexpected crop losses.

data.projectName: Emergency healthcare supply chain performance improvement through Lean approach
data.projectDigest:
In Pakistan, the mortality rate and the number of people seeking immediate medical help has increased drastically recently due to the reasons including road accidents, terrorism, catastrophes disasters etc. This has put pressure on the emergency sections of hospitals. On contrary, facilities and supply of surgical equipment, medicines etc have not been upgraded accordingly.
In hospitals, among all others, supply of medial items is the second biggest expense adding heavy sums to the overall expenditure. There is no doubt that an efficient supply chain impacts over all patient care services grossly. The field of healthcare logistics involves all the steps from receiving the items (like pharmaceuticals, medicals equipment, surgical instruments, linen and food products) to storing them appropriately for a specified time. The proposed project tends to develop methodological internal healthcare supply chain performance evaluation framework based on relevant KPIs especially in emergency department. Proposed framework will be validated through a case study in the emergency department of a hospital. Lean approach will be used in measuring KPIs and designing intervention for performance improvement. The improved performance of emergency department will help to reduce costs, provide better patient care and strengthen the existing emergency medical services (EMS) of the facility.

data.projectName: Immunodynamics of HBsAg in HBV mono-infection and HBV-HDV co-infection
data.projectDigest: HBV is responsible for approximately two billion infections worldwide, and has been associated with hepatitis, cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma.  HBV genome has four overlapping open reading frames that code for the surface, polymerase, core and X protein. HBsAg plays a vital function in HBV life cycle as it is involved in the formation of covalently closed circular DNA (ccc-DNA), and also in viral assembly, and immune recognition.HBV patients are often found co-infected with HDV virus. We and others have previously shown that in an HBV?HDV co?infection scenario, cross?talk between the two viruses influence their co?evolution, allowing selective amplification of certain mutations in HBsAg that are specific to either HBV-mono or HBV-HDV co-infected sequences.For this study, we hypothesize that HBV-HDV co-infection leads to selective amplification of certain mutations in HBsAg that have impact on processing of HBsAg epitopes. The objective of this study is, therefore, to apply an integrated in silico- in vitro approach to study the effect of HBsAg mutations (selectively amplifying in HBV-HDV co-infected patients) on immunological processing and presentation of HBsAg epitopes. This analysis will characterize immunologically significant HBsAg mutations that are selectively amplified in backdrop on HDV and affect antiviral response.  Such analyses have direct relevance to HBV vaccination. Results from this analysis might be useful in tailor-designing vaccines for HBV-HDV co-infected patients.

data.projectName: Virtual Trust Estimation in Human Robot Interaction
data.piUniversity: National College of Business Administration & Economics, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Trust is considered as a critical part in interactions; whether it is  interaction between social cognitive agents, interactive assistants, embodied agents or any other branch covering social interactions. Although little agreement has been found on the defining and describing trust in these sort of interactions and how trust can be measured in collaborative teams specially when the opponent is an unknown. In this regard it is required to consider the dimensions and ways through which virtual trust could be calculated that could open doors for further discussion of the concept through the field of conversational environments. In collaborative teams, social network analysis has been found to have empirical and deerer understanding of the roles and activities of agents whether they are artificial cognitive agents or humans. All agents that are part of some collaborative system are assumed to share various kinds of informations with each other. these agents need secure and reliable communication setup to select their recipients wisely and according to the significance of information to be shared. In certain situations trust plays a vibrant role in identifying suitable opponent. Moreover it has also be seen that when agents converse, they develop emotional ties between them having strength according to the type and frequency of interactions they experience.

data.projectName: Overexpression of a Maize Transcription Factor ZmPHR1  and Haplotypes of Zea mays Phosphorus Transcription factor ZmPHR1 with phosphorus use efficiency in Maize.
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest: Maize is an important cash crop of Pakistan. Phosphorus (P) is one of the most important nutrients required for maize production. P from mineral fertilizer is the major source of P input in Pakistan. However, it is important to note here that between 10 and 30% of the applied P fertilizer is taken up by plants and the wastage of remainder results in lower crop yields and contamination of environment. Developing phosphorus use efficient maize varieties requires comprehensive knowledge of genetic and molecular mechanisms controlling phosphorus use efficiency (PUE) in maize. Numerous studies conducted to understand genetic bases of nutrient use efficiency in maize have shown that there are several transporters genes are involved in this process in maize. One of these transporter is ZmPHR1. Over-expression of ZmPHR1 in maize was shown to increase the PUE of maize. The expression levels of many P homeostasis related genes in maize have also been shown to be modulated by ZmPHR1 expression level. This suggests a strong link between the expression level of ZmPHR1 and PUE in maize. The objective of the proposed study would be to test the association of the level of expression of ZmPHR1 with PUE and impact of ZmPHR1 expression level on the expression of downstream genes considered to be regulated by this transcription factor in natural accessions of maize. We will also perform haplotype analysis of ZmPHR1 that will help to identify the haplotypes associated with PUE in maize. This information will be highly useful for genetic improvement of maize regarding PUE.

data.projectName: bridging the intustry-academia gap in pakistan through community inclusion ; a stakeholder theory perspective.
data.projectDigest:
This qualitative study aims to generate scientific knowledge about innovation and entrepreneurship at higher education institutions by employing the stakeholder theory (Freeman, 1984). Policy makers agree that universities (instructions) are core knowledge actors in today’s knowledge society (stakeholder). Thus, it is important to understand and conceptualize the nature and salience (Mitchel et al., 1997) of relationship between universities and various stakeholders. The study uses grounded theory methodology to empirically understand the case of eight Universities (four each in Islamabad and Peshawar). The comparative perspective can be used to fine tune the goals of universities regarding innovation and entrepreneurship (within and among cities).

The study is expected to contribute to theoretical, practical and policy fronts. It aims to suggest a prospective theory with a contextual view of two-way relationship between universities and society. Practitioners in university and society will be able to understand how their interests can be fulfilled. Policy makers would be guided towards crafting rules and regulations that emphasize the symbiotic relationship between universities and society. Overall it has the potential for increasing employment among University graduates, providing recommendations for curriculum revision as well as contextually relevant policies for BICs and ORICs.

data.projectName: To Develop and Enhance Technology enabled Teacher’s Training ,Development and Certification System   for Mountainous Areas of Gilgit and Baltistan

In order to fill the gap in research on ICT integration in teaching, learning and administration at school level, this research project will provide online training program for teachers of public and privates schools. 900 in service(school teachers)and 1000 pre-services teachers(KIU graduates) will be training in ICT for teaching, learning and educational administration. This training program will be beneficial for the teachers of rural mountainous areas and reduce the deficiency of expert teacher (e.g. science, mathematics and English etc.).  The research project will also help to develop the provincial ICT policy for education.

data.projectName: Metagenomic analysis of soil against Brucella and its seroconversion in humans & animals along with modified immunological cum chemotherapy in diseased animals.
data.piUniversity: Cholistan University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Bahawalpur
data.projectDigest: Bovine Brucellosis is a bacterial disease of zoonotic importance. It is characterized by abortion, birth of weak & unthrifty calves, orchitis and/or epididymitis in male. The organism causes abortion in cattle after the fifth month of pregnancy with retention of placenta, metritis and subsequent period of infertility. The human beings such as butchers, abattoir workers, farmers, laboratory workers and veterinarians are more prone to brucellosis.  There is huge economic loss in terms of abortions, loss of calves, decreased milk yield, infertility in males and threat to public health. Although it has been eradicated in developed countries but its prevalence in Pakistan is about 20 % in dairy animals. Human beings get Brucella infection from infected animals through ingestion of unpasteurized milk, uncooked meat, dairy products, aborted fetus etc and the causative organism survive in environment typically in the soil for a variable period of time  and then again get transferred to healthy animals. Test and slaughter policy is the only solution internationally. In the present project, animals shall be screened against Brucella and will be treated using immunotherapeutic and chemotherapeutic agents. Humans will also be screened against Brucellosis and the soil will be checked for the survival of Brucella species which is the source of spread to healthy animals. The outcome of the project will reflect the exposure of Brucella to humans, infection status in animals, its persistence on soil and beneficiary outcome of treatment.

Although it has been eradicated in developed countries but its prevalence in Pakistan is about 20 % in dairy animals. Human beings get Brucella infection from infected animals through ingestion of unpasteurized milk, uncooked meat, dairy products, aborted fetus etc and the causative organism survive in environment typically in the soil for a variable period of time  and then again get transferred to healthy animals. Test and slaughter policy is the only solution internationally. In the present project, animals shall be screened against Brucella and will be treated using immunotherapeutic and chemotherapeutic agents. Humans will also be screened against Brucellosis and the soil will be checked for the survival of Brucella species which is the source of spread to healthy animals. The outcome of the project will reflect the exposure of Brucella to humans, infection status in animals, its persistence on soil and beneficiary outcome of treatment.

data.projectName: miRNA-induced gene regulation (MIGR): a compelling remedial approach for Silent Estrus Behavior in River Buffalo of Pakistan
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is ranked second large inhabitant of river buffalo population globally. This animal not only possesses exceptional physical and behavioral capacities, which make it adaptive in temperate zones, but also carries unique genomic architecture. Issue of silent estrus in buffalo is a root cause of reproductive inefficiency and is a very significant economic burden on farmers. Genetic interventions influencing estrus cycle have been predicted in bovines but no previous work has been done to understand this whole mechanism, especially in buffaloes. miRNA-induced gene regulation (MIGR) is also getting popularity as novel curative option to regulate the expression of different genes. Current study is based on the circulatory miRNA profiling of Nili-Ravi buffalo breed of Pakistan during various stages of estrus cycle. Targetted miRNA will then be induced in rat model for in-vivo transfection via lipids based carrier reagents. Effect of this therapy will be observed in rats by reproductive cyclicity and hormonal profiling. Outcomes of this study will provide an efficient and promising approach to treat the issue of silent heat and maintain the estrus cyclicity in river buffalo of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Pellet biofuel production from agro-forest wastes in Pakistan; A Waste-to-Energy(WtE) conversion model
data.projectDigest: There is a growing interest in using bioenergy due to the environmental and economic concerns globally. Compared with unprocessed biomass (such as straw or wet sawdust), pellets have higher density and lower moisture content. Additionally, other advantages of wood pellets include a higher heating value, uniform shape, easy to be transported and so on. We are trying to apply the concept of Waste to Energy (WtE) concept in Pakistan and will convert wastes from agriculture and forestry sector to value-added energy product called "pellet biofuel". This WtE concept tickles multiple problems at once such as wastes conversion into value-added products prevent exploitation of virgin resources from natural ecosystem for production of products, saves money, reduce ecological imbalances, improve resource efficiency and sustainability, and generate jobs which ultimately improve socio-economic well-being of the society. Fuelwood has been the main source of energy in the domestic sector of Pakistan. Although, Pakistan has limited forest resources having less than 5 percent forest cover. Majority of the population has consumed fuelwood at the household level due to lack of alternative biofuels. The major problems faced by the consumers are scarcity of wood, high price of fuelwood and low calorific value or combustion properties of fuelwood as compared with wood pellet biofuel. In addition, the illicit cutting of forest trees causes deforestation which makes the ecosystem more fragile and vulnerable and causes global warming in Pakistan. According to global climate risk index 2019, Pakistan is the 7th most vulnerable country to climate change due to global warming in the world. Therefore, it is an urgent need to develop a low-emitting, cost effective and efficient biofuel in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Assessing the humic acid and ethylenediamine disuccinate assisted phytoremediation of copper by radish (Raphanus sativus L.)
data.projectDigest:
Humic acids (HA) are organic chelaters form complexes with heavy metals with highly degradability without leaching to soil as compared with synthetic chelaters. Synthetic chelaters is ethylenediamine disuccinate (EDDS) which is low degradeability as organic chelaters. Humic acids (HA) are natural, widespread, high potential for phytoremediation considered alternatives of synthetic chelaters. Humic acids made from humic substances with reasonable characteristics e.g. water insoluble in acidic media and gain solubility and extractable at high pH of soil. which gives key role as transport, bioavailability and solubility of heavy metals. Due to lower stability constant of HA as compared with synthetic chelaters makes it ideal for phytoextraction and prevents heavy metal-humic acid complexes movement across soil profile complexes with metal-humic acid increase growth and yield. Foliar spray of HA and EDDS reduced abiotic stress and increased growth and yield. 
Copper concentration beyond a certain limit becomes toxic for plant growth and development because it decreased growth, lowers chlorophyll pigments and ultimately reduced yield. In plants, a series of biochemical, physiological and morphological injuries occur due to copper stress.
Phytoremediation is a technique in which green plants use to remove, contain, and furnish contaminants or toxins from soil environment. Moreover, it is cost-effective, eco-friendly, with non or least side effects so this technique is publicly accepted.  It is with strong benefits such as applied on specific area or over largest areas. 
In view of the increasing copper stress it is necessary to find strategies to mitigate copper for growing and getting satisfactory radish yield in copper contaminated areas. Chelating agents assisted phytoreme

data.projectName: Whole Protein Profiling and Identification of Immunoreactive Proteins in Leishmania Tropica: A Step Forward Towards Vaccine Development Against Cutaneous Leishmaniasis
data.projectDigest: Leishmaniasis is vector borne disease caused by a protozoan of the genus leishmania. Leishmaniasis has broadly divided into three main types including Visceral (VL), Cutaneous (VL) and Muco-Cutaneous Leishmaniasis (MCL). In Pakistan, CL is the leading clinical type of leishmaniasis caused by Leishmania tropica and Leishmania major, among which Leishmania tropica is widely prevalent. Lack of drug availability, drug resistance, lack of proper diagnostic tools and poor life standard of the people of Pakistan are the leading factors that contribute to the severity of the disease. Vaccination hold significant importance for the prevention and management of any zoonotic disease including leishmaniasis. Till date, no proper vaccine has been developed to combat CL. Protein profiling carries promising role in determining and identifying potential immunoreactive protein that may be as potential candidate for vaccine. This project will aim to explore the whole protein profile of L. tropica and to characterize and identify immunogenic proteins that tends to develop host immunity and provoke antibody responses in host against L. tropica parasites. These proteins can be further used for the development of candidate vaccine that will not only help in management of disease but will also lower down the economic burden on Government shoulders.

So, the present project was plan with the prime objective for the documentation of these advanced techniques for seed priming. Certainly, this will result in up lift the economic standard of the people and also boost the field of oil seed crops farming in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Sustainable Treatment technologies for arsenic contamination in water
data.projectDigest:
Heavy metal ion removal from industrial waste water is a major environmental problem to be addressed. Currently, discharge of contaminated effluents into fresh water resources without treatment is a key source of deteriorating the water quality. The anthropogenic activities, modern agricultural methods and industrial wastes are globally affecting the climate; especially water. Many underdeveloped countries particularly Pakistan are facing the problems of polluted water available for domestic, agricultural and drinking purposes. These menacing chemicals mainly include heavy metal ions, dyes, pathogens, ammonia, pesticides, other inorganic and organic pollutants etc. flowing to the fresh water resources without treatment. Human health and aquatic life are at high risk of these harmful pollutants. Therefore, these factors needs to be resolved on priority basis by developing novel, ecofriendly and cost effective treatment technologies for polluted water.
The basic aim of this project is to synthesize novel metal oxide based nanohybrid photo catalysts coupled with membrane filtration for arsenic removal from industrial waste waters. Wet chemical methods and electrospinning techniques would be utilized for catalyst fabrication while characterization will be performed by different spectroscopic techniques. It is anticipated that our synthesized materials would offer cost effective and efficient candidates for water cleaning applications.

data.projectName: Assessing the impact of institutional factors on the performance of SME's in KPK
data.projectDigest:
In the developing countries SMEs play a vital role in development of a country. A better institutional environment in a country can be very handy in the better performance of the business in that country, especially the SMEs of that country. This study will use world governance indicator (WGI) to examine the impact of the country level institutional factors on the performance of the SMEs. The country level institutional factors importance was more debated by Landes (1998), Hall and Jones (1999), and Acemoglu, Johnson, and Robinson (2001).

In Pakistan although various steps are being taken to provide better country level governance for creating a more competitive environment for businesses to flourish but the question is are they sufficient enough to provide the required environment i.e. 1. Political stability 2. Voice and Accountability 3. Regulatory quality 4. Rule of Law 5. Control of Corruption 6. Government Effectiveness?   This research will investigate the impact of institutional factors impact on the performance of the SMEs operating in KPK.

data.projectName: A Multicenter Longitudinal Study to Identify the Prognostic Risk Factors and the Efficacy of Combinations of Treatments for Osteoarthritis
data.projectDigest: Osteoarthritis is chronic degenerative disease that can affect any joint in the body. It is acknowledged as the fourth leading cause of disability worldwide. It mostly affects the large weight bearing joints of the body that include knee, hip, and ankle. It can also affect the joints of upper limb e.g., elbow and shoulder joints. The women are more exposed to the condition than men between age 45 to 60 years. Also, knee OA is more evident than hip OA, especially in the Asian population. There is an observance of more patients of OA in urban areas (28%) of Pakistan than in rural areas (25%). Most common joint involved in this disease is knee followed by hip and 1st metacarpophalangeal joint of the hand. In this proposed study, we intend to investigate the OA risk factors and the treatment effect in a longitudinal scenario, among the patients in major cities of Punjab. We will see the effects of the treatment of the disease at different grades and that of drugs in the treatment for a set duration of time. This study will enable us to formulate a uniform policy for the treatment and its duration with appropriate drugs.

Recent study of 2017 conclude that the rate is now three times more than previous data. According to the opinion and research of the experts of American Diabetic Association, 70% cases of pre-diabetes lead to the development of type 2 diabetes. However, it is also evident that modification in physical activity and dietary patterns can reduce the percentage of its occurrence. Strategies targeting interventions should be aimed at the entire population to reduce key diabetes risk factors, such as adiposity and physical inactivity. However, these need to be complemented with diabetes prevention strategies speci?cally aimed at prediabetic and other high-risk individuals. data.projectName: Defense Mechanism of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle’s against Cyber Threats
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: Unmanned aerial vehicles (likely knows as drones), in recent time, have become most optimistic solution with bundle of applications in the field of Monitoring environment, Transportation, Media Live Streaming and military operations. Autopilot UAV system normally used in exigent operations for acquire critical information’s. UAV system are vulnerable to different security threats due to their deployment in serval crucial domains. data.projectName: Inducing point mutation in different bulbous flowers through in vitro and in vivo chemical application
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest: Bulbous flowers (Lily, Freesia and Iris) are important floricultural plants propagated by bulbs/corms and used for cut flowers (flowers with large flower and long stem), bedded and potted plants. These flowers have major share in world floriculture trade due to their ornamental characteristics. In Pakistan, production of Lily, Freesia and Iris has been increased with expansion of floriculture industry. To fulfil local requirement huge amount of bulbs of these flowers imported every year that is increasing cost of production along with phytosanitary requirements. Due to increasing importance of bulbous flowers in national and international markets there is need of extensive breeding research work for morpho-genetic improvement of these flowers. Point mutation is an important modern breeding method that causes mutations at high frequency with limited chromosomal damage. It can be a potential source for inducing genetic improvement in Lily, Freesia and Iris but unfortunately this aspect of research work is neglected in Pakistan. Present research project will emphasis on the production of mutants through using chemical mutagens in these bulbous plants. Furthermore, mutants will be characterized on the basis of desired characteristics that may serve to the farmer’s community as locally produced mutant at reasonable price in the future.

data.projectName: Design and Fabrication of Intelligent Insulin Infusion Device for Diabetic Patients
data.projectDigest: This research is aimed towards developing closed loop insulin device (artificial pancreas) to facilitate patients with Type-1 diabetes. The device as an outcome of this research will fulfil patient requirements without requiring human input (for calculating and injecting required amount of insulin). It will not only bring ease in the life of diabetic patients but will also enhance quality of their life. Major benefits of the developed device will be automatic regulation of insulin and prevention of hypoglycemic (low blood sugar) events with capability to maintain the effectiveness of insulin in the developed device at high temperatures. Basic technology used in the device will include feedback control system coupled with artificial intelligence/machine learning techniques for nanoparticles-based insulin storage and delivery. Worldwide Type-1 diabetic patients will be the potential customers for the developed device. Commercial and research partners will include various hospitals and diabetic research centers across Pakistan. The successful development and demonstration of prototype will open further investment opportunities for potential investors including health organizations, research institutes and private sector that are looking forward to addressing the needs of diabetic patients worldwide by equipping them with the latest technology.

data.projectName: Failure of Government Projects on Poverty Reduction: Searching for New Ways
data.projectDigest: The biggest development challenge facing Pakistan is how to meet the millennium development goal of bringing down the incidence of poverty from the current level of 39 percent to 20 percent by 2018. It may be recalled that by reaching this goal, we would have only regained the level we had attained in 1988-89. This experience shows that it is quite easy to relapse into higher incidence of poverty, but it is quite an uphill battle to recover the lost ground. Government introduce many poverty alleviation techniques including Income Generation Programmes, Khushhal Pakistan and Tameer-e-Pakistan Public Works Programmes, Drought Relief Programme, Micro-credit for the Poor in the Agriculture Sector, Micro-credit for SMEs, Disaster Management, Social Assistance Programmes for the poor, Permanent Rehabilitation Grant, Food Support Programme, Tawana Pakistan Programme, Educational Stipends (Technical), National Level Hospitals/Institutions, Employees’ Old-Age Benefits Institution (EOBI) and Workers Welfare Fund (WWF) and many more. All these and many other institutions work how to reduce poverty in the country, but they fail to reduce the poverty level up to the desire standard.

data.projectName: IoT based Realtime poultry shed environment monitoring and disease detection to explore deep learning techniques based on audio and video data
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest:
Due to increase in demand of poultry products, poultry industry needs to grow at higher rate. Government agencies are also encouraging poultry farming for poverty alleviation. But, this industry faces many serious threats regarding management and diseases. Therefore, annually loss of billions of dollars is reported worldwide. So, there is need to pay special attention to minimize the risks that’s effects the poultry farming. Hence, there is need to develop the strategies that enables adequate jobs, income generation and improvement in livelihood through this industry.  
The major part of disease incidence in indigenous poultry farming poultry is due to poor monitoring system of environmental parameters like temperature, humidity, ammonia gas which have a big role in transmission of various pathogens and diseases to poultry farming. 
Therefore, this project is designed in development of smart poultry farm automation and monitoring system for improving poultry production in southern Punjab.

data.projectName: Establishment of Internet of Things (IoT) Lab at Department of Telecommunication Engineering

data.projectName: Genome sequencing and characterization of multi drug resistant isolate from  Environmental (water) sample.
data.projectDigest: Antibiotic resistance developed by various bacterial cell specially the pathogenic bacterium posing a great threat for treatment of bacteria infection. The interesting aspect of this study is that the bacterium will not be isolated from patient sample but would be  isolated from water which is in its pure form is not a good medium for growth of microoganism/bacterial cell. However water could be contaminated from sewage, soil and other  sources such as hospital waste which are important sources of microorganisms in water.  Municipal water which is purified water of lakes and rivers is supplied to community, to houses through pipelines  for daily usage. The study has been done with SRGP Number 2288 (Myself as PI in 2018-19) has shown the contamination of water with bacterial isolates which were found resistant to more than three commonly used antibiotic groups. These results shown drug resistance isolates bacterial cell can be disseminated through water. The aim of this study is to investigate resistance of bacterial cell at genetic level. As genome sequencing will provide insight into bacterial genomic characteristics and will give us information on its genomic make up. The information obtained in turn will help to investigate the bacterial drug resistance at genetic level with bioinformatic analysis of obtained genomic sequence . Furthermore, this study will characterize the drug resistance bacterial isolate.The genomic characterization of antibiotic resistant isolate and informations obtained with this study will be helpful for future study of these drug resistance isolates,such as for vaccine development or control of these isolates at genomic level.

data.projectName: Design and implementation of security prototype for pseud-random challenges of IoT enabled botnets
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest: Fortune 500 companies use IoT devices to generate sensory data and process their large-scale data volumes in distributed computing environments through state-of-the-art big data management systems such as Apache Hadoop, MapR and Cloudera [1]. Due to the importance of generated data, the companies hire various software and internet security services to look after the security measures of IoT devices such as internet security tools, rootkits and malware protection programs [2]. Even though after applying so many security tools, companies are not able to secure IoT devices from an especial kind of internet attack such as, Distributed Denial of Services (DDoS) attack [3]. This DDoS attack became a nightmare for IoT devices, when a botnet named Mirai infected IoT devices of various organizations such as CCTV cameras, digital video recorders (DVR) and routers simultaneously in around 164 countries to attack a famous DNS organization (Dyn) in the United States [4]. In this attack, they redirected two million IoT devices for sending lightweight messaging protocol (MQTT) traffic to the DNS organization and left it without no choice but to shut down the company’s services till the attack stops [5].

data.projectName: Intracity Multi-tier Robust Data Exchange framework for CPEC Corridor
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
Global cities’ digitization is a process, that transforms digital technologies into living beings’ lifestyle in the connected planet’s global townships. We find various aspects of such a digitization that focuses on usage of gadgets, modern wireless equipment and state-of-the-art IoT devices, but to administer it in terms of managing networks and ensuring data storage is a challenging task. We are focusing the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) for digitizing its routes which consists upon inter-connection of several cities and the data workflow must be synchronized with a persistent and reliable connectivity for easy data sampling at each installed collection unit in the network. This unstructured data is supposed to be stored at few secure repository locations for required data analytics and other usage. For this, we use an open-source system software named Apache Spark, that connects and processes large-scale data samples in a reliable networked environment of CPEC. There are some challenges in achieving a smooth data processing in CPEC route, such as 
a)	Fast and reliable data processing at the nodes of cities,
b)	Reliable and fault-tolerant network among cities,
c)	Individual City-based data processing framework and,
d)	Data analytics at cities’ hub.

data.projectName: Stress induced pathophysiological adaptation or apoptosis of pancreatic beta-cell; role of fasting and calorie restriction in beta cell rescue
data.projectDigest: Pancreatic beta-cell are extremely susceptible to Oxidative Stress. In the absence of proper compensatory response from antioxidant mechanisms, High blood glucose levels lead to an increased in free radical formation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial impairment that suppress the defensive ability of endogenous antioxidant system of pancreatic beta-cells therefore leading to the cell death and the progression of Diabetes mellitus (DM). Furthermore, activation of intracellular stress-associated signaling pathways also seems to play a role in insulin resistance, reduced insulin secretion, and late diabetic complications. The prolonged exposure to increasing levels of hyperglycemia correlates with progressive loss of beta-cell differentiation, as indicated by altered expression of several key islet transcription factors and other islet genes important for normal glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. Our study aim to investigate the role of fasting and low calories intervention to limit oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction in early DM disease and also to promote long-term protection against high glucose induce oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction. It is important to explore the mechanism of stress related pathophysiological alteration or apoptosis and the role of fasting and low calories diet on the pathophysiology and antioxidant system of pancreatic beta-cell, which may help us in understanding the development of DM.

data.projectName: Biochemical and Molecular Identification of Plant Parasitic Nematodes in Southern Punjab
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest:
Phytoparasitic nematodes are an expensive burden for agricultural production. Phytoparasitic nematodes are omnipresent in nature and are associated with almost all important agricultural crops. Root knot nematodes (Meloidogyne spp.), Cyst nematodes (Heterodera spp. & Globodera spp.) and lesion nematodes (Pratylenchus spp.) rank on the list of economically and scientifically most important species according to the complex relationship with host plants, the variety of hosts and the extent of damage caused by the infection (Karssen, 2000; Sasser and Taylor, 1978; Hunt et al., 2005). Population of plant parasitic nematodes is on rise in high temperature, sandy loam soil, hot climate and short winter (Maqbool, 1987). The identification of plant-parasitic nematodes is not always easy, particularly in the case of some taxa. Identification is even more complicated when two or more species occur in the same sample. The faulty characterization and identification of species that are economically important may lead to inappropriate control measures being taken. To overcome these problems the characterization and identification of nematodes should be based not only on morphological and morphometrical characters and on host range bioassays, which are of primary importance, but also on protein and nucleic acid profiles. 
We observed that population density of plant parasitic nematodes is high in soils of Southern Punjab (Unpublished data) and there is few published work on their biochemical and molecular identification. The study is planned with following objectives;
1.	Assessment of disease losses due to plant parasitic nematodes in different vegetables and crops being cultivated and estimation of their population density 
2.	Biochemical and Molecular identification

data.projectName: Identification and Evaluation of Potential neuroprotective compounds (natural and synthetic) by establishing an indigenous Electroencephalography (EEG) recording system in animal models of Epilepsy
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Epilepsy is a brain disorder typically manifested by sudden brief periods of altered and diminished consciousness, involuntary movements, or convulsions due to abnormal electrical activity in the brain (World Health Organization 2018). The phenomenon of developing epilepsy is described by the term “epileptogenesis” (Löscher and Brandt 2010). These initial brain assaults, e.g. trauma, stroke, brain tumors, status epilepticus or infections, often accompanied by early seizures, play a role in transforming an otherwise healthy brain into an epileptic brain (Löscher and Brandt 2010, Ravizza, Balosso et al. 2011). After an initial brain insult, the failure of intrinsic repair mechanisms, followed by a second hit, gene sensitivity, or comorbidities provides a favoring milieu to develop late seizures or epilepsy (Löscher and Brandt 2010). To understand the underlying pathophysiological processes, and therapeutic interventions, rodent (mice and rat) models are widely used in epilepsy research. In order to quantify, post traumatic, brain electrical activity (EEG) along with time lapsed video (v), collectively termed as Video-EEG (vEEG), is recorded 24/7 as primary source and manually analyzed to characterize the epileptiform events (spikes & seizures) in such models. Interictal epileptiform discharges (seizures) have been associated with epilepsy and spikes have widely been accepted diagnostically as sign of epilepsy in humans. In this project we will establish a vEEG recording facility using local resources with the help of foreign experts under the auspices of transfer of technology. In our knowledge, to date, no such rodent EEG recording and analysis facility is available in Pakistan.This facility would the 1st of its kind to provide a startup for recording such brain activity

In order to quantify, post traumatic, brain electrical activity (EEG) along with time lapsed video (v), collectively termed as Video-EEG (vEEG), is recorded 24/7 as primary source and manually analyzed to characterize the epileptiform events (spikes & seizures) in such models. Interictal epileptiform discharges (seizures) have been associated with epilepsy and spikes have widely been accepted diagnostically as sign of epilepsy in humans. In this project we will establish a vEEG recording facility using local resources with the help of foreign experts under the auspices of transfer of technology. In our knowledge, to date, no such rodent EEG recording and analysis facility is available in Pakistan.This facility would the 1st of its kind to provide a startup for recording such brain activity

data.projectDigest:

The mathematical modeling results from flow of various non-Newtonian fluids with these flow features are nonlinear and often exact solutions are not possible. Such nonlinearities in higher order differential equations are remain still challenge for mathematicians especially for case of partial differential equations. 
•	Suggest various mathematical modeling of non-Newtonian fluids
•	Effects of various physical parameters with different geometries
•	Enhancement of heat transfer based on nanoparticles
•	Bioconvection flow of nanoparticles
•	Compute analytic and numerical solutions for resulting nonlinear partial as well as ordinary differential equations
•	To study comparative studies these highly nonlinear ordinary as well as partial differential equations by using various analytic and numerical techniques.

data.projectName: Investigation of Opuntia dillenii derived methanol extract, fractions and pure compounds opuntiol and opuntioside against LPS-induced neuroinflammation, memory deficiency and amyloidogenesis
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Inflammation lies at the core of several neurological disorders, especially neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimers and Parkinson’s disease. Neuroinflammation involve in the development of Alzheimer's disease (AD) via amyloidogenesis. Opuntia dillenii is medicinal plant grows widely in Pakistan, its cladode and fruit are edible and traditionally used to treat inflammation. Pharmacologically it is reported as anti-inflammatory, analgesic, antioxidant, hypoglycemic, anti-asthmatic, hypotensive, anti-microbial and hypolipedemic. Our earlier reported data has shown anti-inflammatory potential of O. dillenii (Nagphana) in periphery. We have also found O. dillenii test agents reduced LPS-induced neuroinflammation. Keeping this in view, the present study is designed to assess its effectiveness in the central inflammation together with memory related impairment. In current study, effects of O. dillenii derived extract, fractions and pure compounds opuntiol and opuntioside against lipopolysaccharide (LPS) induces neuroinflammation and amyloidogenesis, apoptotic neuronal cell death as well as memory impairment will be investigated.
O. dillenii cladode is edible, its cladode utilizes as vegetable and fodder. Chemically it constituent various flavonoid; ?- pyrones: opuntiol and opuntioside; phenolics; betalains; ?-sitosterol and vitamin C. These constituents may responsible for reduction in neuroinflammation as well as potential to enhance memory.

data.projectName: Spatio-Temporal Evaluation of Hydro-meteorological Disasters and their impacts on the lives and livelihoods in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is divulged to a variety of hydro-meteorological hazards including floods, GLOF, intense rainfall, drought, landslides, and cyclonic storms events. Amongst these floods, droughts and cyclonic storms have been causing heavy damages to people and their properties. This research project will focus on hydro-meteorological hazards and its impacts on lives and livelihood in Pakistan. Climatic variability will be assessed from meteorological station data as well as regional and global climate models. Change in climatic parameters will be assessed and the trend will be predicted using geo-statistical techniques. Climate change nexus with hydro-meteorological disasters will be analyzed in this study. Drought in the selected study area will be assessed using meteorological indices like SPI, SPEI, RDI, and TVDI. The drought risk and potential threat areas will be mapped using GIS. Flash and riverine floods vulnerable and risk areas will be identified using statistical and probabilistic modeling for flash floods in the upper catchments of main rivers while hydrological modeling will be used for riverine floods in plains of the study area. The direct impacts on lives and livelihoods in the past and future will be assessed for both drought and flood hazards in the study area using geospatial technology as well as field investigation techniques.

data.projectName: Implementation of Competency Framework for Effective People Supply Chain
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Experts believe that management of human re source when performed on competence basis brings significantly better performance. One way of presenting human resource competencies is through formal framework. This project will develop framework and use it to map various jobs by a panel of experts from various trades. It is also necessary to conduct a validation study involving practitioners before it is implemented in any organization. The project therefore, validate the scientifically developed competency framework in various organisations and assess the prospects of its adaptability and utilization in both manufacturing and service sectors. This project will go in two phases: literature review in the first phase and at later stage, workshops and survey will conducted, involving practitioners and experts from various occupations.

data.projectName: Metabolic Engineering of Brassica napus to Produce a Powerful Anti-oxidant (Astaxanthin) in the oil that Enhances Human Health
data.projectDigest: Genetic engineering approaches towards the enhancement of carotenoids in crop plants has opened new access in combating food security problems and improving human health. For nutritional enhancement and production of commercial valued carotenoids, the production of natural pigment astaxanthin has gained considerable interest because of its significant beneficial effects on human health, use in food industry as supplement, cosmetics, natural dye and as a powerful antioxidant. Astaxanthin is a unique high-value keto-carotenoid rarely found in plants and mainly found in marine algae. Chemically synthetic astaxanthin is restricted for humans and in use as a feed additive for fish farming, the demand for natural astaxanthin is expected to grow rapidly. The bioresources of astaxanthin are limited and thus expensive, which has attracted scientists to develop heterologous biosynthesis hosts for the sustainable production of natural astaxanthin. The proposed study is designed to nutritionally enhance Brassica napus by enhancing and converting its carotene contents to astaxanthin. A set of three genes including the phytoene synthase gene (CrtB), ?-carotene ketolase gene (CrBKT) and ?-carotene hydroxylase gene (HpBHY) linked together via 2A peptides will be transformed to B. napus. The expression of these genes will be checked under both 35S and seed specific promoters.

data.projectName: Comparative study of ZnO based Schottky diode parameters by using numerical methods
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Mathematical tools play an important role in fabrication of devices. This research is focused on the fact that numerical methods/simulation in the calculation of different electrical parameters of devices like diode are as vital and result oriented as the experimental results are. Numerical methods allow us to generate data faster than experimental methods. To check how the performance of devices are changed with the change of parameters it is necessary to collect data by using numerical methods which is not possible by experimental methods. This research is based on a comparative study of two numerical methods to measure electrical parameters of electronic devices at highly sensitive temperature to discuss the influence of these parameters on the performance of devices. Schottky diode are most important in order to improve the behavior and efficiency of electrical devices. ZnO based Schottky diode have taken great attention because of the substantial properties of ZnO which play a crucial role in the fabrication of high-quality devices.
The goal of this work is to study the effect of highly sensitive temperature on electrical parameters such as ideality factor, saturated current, donor concentration, built in potential and barrier height of Schottky diode. All parameters will be calculated by applying numerical methods on well-known thermionic emission model and capacitance voltage equations.

data.projectName: Using non-coding RNAs as diagnostic and therapeutic tool for metabolic syndrome; emphasis on cardiovascular diseases
data.projectDigest: Metabolic syndrome (MS) is one of the major reasons for increasing cases of cardiovascular diseases (CVD). All components of metabolic syndrome i.e. hypertension, obesity, dislipidaemia, insulin resistance and hyperglycemia are strongly linked to the initiation and progression of CVD. About 50% of Pakistani population is affected by MS and many have advanced to CVD. This might be due to high exposure to free oxygen radicals, life style and inadequate information about specific and sensitive molecular markers that can be detected at the onset of the MS, obesity and CVD. Circulating non-coding RNAs play a critical role in the pathogenesis of many diseases including obesity, MS and CVD, through the direct or indirect regulations of certain genes. Owing to the stability and specificity of these molecules, they are targeted for prognosis, diagnosis and therapeutics of many diseases. These have aroused our curiosity to explore potentials of different forms of micro RNA (miRNAs), circular RNAs (cirRNA) and long chain non-coding RNAs (lnRNA) in diagnosis and prognosis of obesity, MS and monitoring their progression to CVD in Pakistani population. The outcome of the proposed study would be beneficial in understanding the specific functional defects associated with obesity, MS and CVD at molecular level.

data.projectName: Monitoring of Environmental Toxin: Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons (PAHs) and Carcinogenic Compounds: Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs) Using Bimetallic (Au-Ag, Au-Pt and Au-Ru) Alloy Nanoparticles Based Electrochemical Sensor
data.projectDigest:
Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons (PAHs) like anthracene and penthracene cause hormonal diseases by disrupting thyroid stimulating hormones, growth hormones and sex hormones. In addition, they also retard reproduction and immune-competence. The environmental protection agency (EPA) has presented the alarming issue of uncontrollable amount of PAHs in the troposphere.  Moreover, EPA has given an alert about the toxic effects of PAHs as well. Therefore, identification, quantification and removal of PAHs from the environment is need of the day. 
In the recent era of informational technology, printers, and photocopiers are the basic necessaries for official works. These machines emit carcinogenic volatile organic compound called VOCs (including methyl isobutyl ketone). In this project our focal point includes monitoring of health hazardous and carcinogenic VOC: methyl isobutyl ketone, which causes lungs cancer, using BMANPs based electrochemical sensor. BMANPs play a vital role in development of electrochemical sensor for the detection of PAHs and VOCs. BMANPs, Gold- Silver (Au-Ag), Gold–platinum (Au-Pt) and Gold-Ruthenium (Au-Ru) can be synthesized by environmental friendly method and they find countless applications in the sphere of electrochemistry. BMANPs based electrochemical sensor can be successfully applied for the monitoring of PAHs and VOCs found in the environment even in the lowest concentration.
