data.projectName: Mirror Symmetry and Classification of log Del Pezzo Surfaces
data.projectDigest:
Connections between mathematics and physics has always proved to be fruitful for the benefit of science. The main focus of our work is to explore one such connection. Our aim is to use this connection in our advantage and study objects from mathematics. 
On physics side we are concerned with mirror symmetry which is a major tool in string theory, a branch of theoretical physics. It is in fact the study of different geometric objects arising from physical theories, which appears different but become equivalent in higher dimensions. Using this connection fundamental questions of physics turn out to be fundamental questions of mathematics and vice versa. 
The objects of mathematics which we want to construct and classify belong the branch of algebraic geometry. Primarily we want to construct and classify two dimensional objects, namely, del Pezzo surfaces. These surfaces have rich history which attracted the attention of many mathematicians over the last century.  
Our study will be a continuation of the work of Akhtar, Coates, Corti et al. who proposed a number of conjectures that in 2015 which allow one to classify a broad class of del Pezzo surfaces using mirror symmetry.  The conjectures hold trivially in simple cases. Our aim is to check validity of these conjectures for all del Pezzo surfaces and hence give a complete classification of these surfaces.

Pakistan has recently seen a surge in the usage and sale of motorbikes. Approximately 195 local companies have the license to manufacture motorcycles. Motorized bikes have almost completely marginalized the use of paddled bicycles. Only sports bicycles are seen on sale and in use. This has, on one side given independence to single users and small families to travel at a faster speed as per their convenience; it has also caused a number of problems and risks as well. Motorized bikes use petrol (gasoline), which is mostly imported or developed from imported crude oil. This does have an impact on the economy, as a lot of foreign exchange ($s) is spent by the country on fuel imports. Secondly, motor bikes rode by small families that include little children, infants and even babies. Motor bikes are normally driven by male members while the females sit on the back seat with both legs on one side, which is a cultural norm. This style of sitting is prevalent in the south Asia widely. It seems that this poses a lot of risk for the passengers. The passengers are exposed to any mishap on the road. Accidents involving bikes are quite prevalent and can be witnessed on the city roads daily [24]. One more problem with the motor bikes is that women normally wear large garments while riding and incidents like garment stuck in bike’s wheel and other moving parts causes serious accidents. During harsh hot and cold weather, or when it is raining, motor bikes provide no safety or refuge to its passengers.  When the motor bike is stopped at a road side the passengers have to standby it, until the journey starts again. 
The purpose of this project is to design and develop a vehicle that provides a stable and safer travelling to normal Pakistanis. A closed environment that protects the incumbe

data.projectName: Establishing Peace Perspectives in Teacher Education Curriculum
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: UNESCO has identified six components for culture of peace for a country: respect for human rights and freedoms; commitment to non-violence; observance to principles of justice; democracy and tolerance; commitment to development and environment; and equity in rights for women and men. Keeping in mind the above mentioned criteria, the institutions of teacher education are expected to contribute to a culture of peace through training of prospective teachers by enabling them reflecting desired behavioral change in their students by integrating it into all social levels like family, the school, and community. This study will seek the perceptions of prospective teachers towards peace education through existing curriculum of teacher education. It will probe into various methods and techniques to reflect peace activities within lesson plans that trainee teachers incorporate their real teaching practice by developing a training module of peace education. Further actual performance of trainee teachers will also be observed at field schools. Questionnaire, Nominal group technique and focus group discussion will be applied for data collection.

data.projectName: Role of Women in Agriculture and Stratifying Sustainable Livelihoods in Punjab, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Nature has bestowed Punjab with rich soil for agricultural production. Both men and women are involved in agriculture for subsistence as well as for earning profit. Women play a vital role in agricultural development by doing on-farm work and livestock rearing. When it comes to the socio-cultural rights of women necessary for a sustainable livelihood, including access to education and health, legal rights, authority of decision making, access to finance, and access to other livelihood assets, women are marginalized by depriving from such rights. Due to off-farm employment of male members of the family women have to take care of farming activities in their absence resulting in over work burden for them, where they need to work simultaneously on-farm and at-home. In Punjab women spend around 12 to 15 hours daily on agricultural activities (Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), 2015). Like in other parts of the world, female farm work is unpaid and not counted as a constraint to her access to livelihood assets. Female workload is wide and simultaneous in nature. They perform all agronomic tasks along with household chores and child care. Their problems are multiplied due to lack of access to microfinance, agricultural markets, and market information and training related to agricultural and personal development. These all factors make women vulnerable in accessing livelihood assets and act as constraints in improving their human and financial resources. This study intends to analyze workload of women working in agricultural and interrelationship of this work burden with sustaining livelihoods .

data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Inherited neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) are caused be genetic aberrations disrupting normal development of central nervous system. These cover a spectrum of structural and functional anomalies of brain and include diverse, often overlapping, diseases such as primary microcephaly (small skull) and intellectual disability  etc, to name a few more prevalent in Pakistani population.  Pakistan has high burden of NDDs due to high parental consanguinity and it casts serious socio-economic burden. Due to lack of genomic facilities locally, relevant genetics remains unknown.  The proposed project will recruit consanguineous NDD families thorough established collaborations with neurologists and field sampling. These will be analyzed employing latest genomic techniques such as whole exome sequencing and sanger sequencing. The pathophysiology of novel/under-characterized variants will also be assessed through in silico modelling and cell based functional assays. The results of this study will produce knowledge crucial for better diagnosis, disease understanding, genetic counselling. Most importantly, it will provide means to control the incidence through identifying couples and pregnancies at risk. It will also provide contribute to capacity building by training research students, and cataloging genetic epidemiology of local population that can be used to launch nationwide genetic screening programs.

data.projectName: STATISTICAL ANALYSIS OF ANXIETY AFTER REVOCATION OF THE SPECIAL STATUS OF JAMMU AND KASHMIR AMONGST THE UNIVERSITY STUDENTS OF DIVIDED FAMILIES SETTLED IN AZAD JAMMU & KASHMIR, PAKISTAN
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest:
This project recommends studying the originalities of anxiety suffered by university students of divided families in Azad Jammu & Kashmir (AJK) after revocation of the article 370 by Indian government on August 5, 2019. The project aims to evaluate the anxiety reasons amongst the university students after abrogation of the special status of Jammu & Kashmir (J&K).  Our goal is to make the people aware about the possible consequences of the anxiety and educate them about the safety measures. The project will focus on the problems faced by the affected Kashmiris because they cannot communicate with their loved ones due to communications blackout and curfew for long time ago on the other side of Indian occupied Kashmir (IOK).  The study will utilize the techniques of logistic regression for modeling the data, which is expected to be mostly primary in nature, will be collected via different tools to be designed by qualified experts. Initially, universities and institutes will be purposively selected from all public and private sector universities of AJK.
Questionnaires will be distributed among   students and university employees. The results of this study are idealized to attract attention of international community particularly United Nations (UN), Organization of Islamic Countries (OIC) private and public organizations of human rights to take more effective initiatives for arranging the plebiscite in J&K. Government will be a key beneficiary in the sense that the findings of the study would enable policy makers to understand key characteristics of Kashmir issue and this project can be initiated towards the welfare of Kashmiri population.

data.projectName: Bacterial Metabolites As potential Anti-cancer and Anti-proliferative Drug Lead against Breast Cancer
data.piUniversity: Lahore College for Women University, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Cancer is a communal health hazard worldwide and second cause of death worldwide. In Asia Pakistan has the highest rate of breast cancer cases and approximately 1 out of every 9 women are likely to suffer from it. Due to this alarming situation the proposed investigation is an effort to identify new and safer drugs by evaluating the anticancer and anti-proliferative activities of bacterial secondary metabolites against different types of breast cancers. This study could lead to new drug discovery with reduce side effects which can widen the horizon of anticancer therapeutics. Since decades bacterial secondary metabolites have provided diverse source of new therapeutic drugs against different diseases including active component of anticancer drugs but still there are numerous bioactive compounds whose fate as anticancer agents has yet to be explored and new species from new habitats are needed to be explored. Keeping in view the therapeutic potential of microbial metabolites the proposed project aim is to screen and identify the extracellular metabolites of diverse bacteria as anticancer agents and to elucidate its structure related drug like properties as a potential drug lead (candidate) against breast cancer. Keeping in view the United Nation SDGs Goal 3 and 9 i.e. “Good health and wellbeing” and “Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure” the proposed research project, apart from benefiting the cancer patients, can lead to building a confidence and bonding between academia and industry (pharmaceutical) that will eventually inflate the country’s economic status.

data.projectName: Analyzing FCER2 and CRHR1 Genotypes in Asthmatic Individuals of Rawalpindi and Islamabad
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Asthma is a major chronic and growing clinical disease manifesting pathogenesis diversity around the globe causing enormous socio-economic and psychological burden involved in long term treatment and frequent hospitalization of asthmatic individuals. Every one in five individuals suffer from asthma in Pakistan and the situation is going to be worsened in upcoming years. Previous studies have attributed role of various environmental factors in general and genetic factors in particular with the development of asthma. However, insufficient data is available on the molecular genetics of asthma susceptible genes particularly mutations in FECR2 and CRHR1 linked with the number of times of asthma onset and hospitalizations of patients receiving inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) and response to corticosteroid treatments in Pakistan. This study aims at exploring the association of single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) of candidate genes; FECR2 and CRHR1 associated with asthma in Pakistani population. Current study will help in the identification of individuals at risk for developing asthma and will help clinicians in better diagnosis of disease, prophylaxis, management and improvement in corticosteroid treatment response in local population of Rawalpindi and islamabad thus will reduce socio-economic burden on human development index particularly Health sector.

data.projectName: Management of Brown spot disease: A serious havoc to Basmati rice production in Punjab, Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: Rice, as an important food crop and major export commodity of Pakistan, is attacked by a number of fungal and bacterial pathogens. Many rice diseases which were earlier considered as minor have become economically important like Brown leaf spot caused by a fungus Bipolaris oryzae. Appearance of new and more virulent forms of the pathogen has made the disease management more challenging. To cope with, it is empirical to look for more effective strategies and broad spectrum plant protection measures. The management of brown spot disease needs strong and consolidated research efforts from fundamentals to applied side at the farmer fields. The overall objective of the current project proposal is the management of brown spot disease in Basmati rice. To cope with this challenge, the deployments of resistant varieties accompanied with safe fungicides are the most economical and effective approaches. In the present project, the monitoring will be carried out to determine the incidence and severity of the disease in Basmati rice areas of the Punjab. For host plant resistance, advance germplasm will be evaluated in disease screening nurseries of NIAB using artificial inoculation. Comparative studies of disease intensity under transplanted and direct seeding rice technology will be executed. The effectiveness of commercially available fungicides and the chemicals will be tested to manage the disease. Based on the information generated from this project, cultural, varietal resistance and chemical control strategies for disease management can be recommended to the farmers.

data.projectName: The Impact of Perceived Risk on Determinants of Customers’ Social Commerce Engagement
data.projectDigest: The use of social media is increasing at a rapid pace. This use has now expanded to cover business transactions over Internet i.e. E-commerce. Social commerce is a sub-set of E-commerce that refers to use of social media to assist online buying and selling of products and services. In Southeast Asia, social commerce is flourishing as internet users spend an average of approx. 4 hours daily on popular social media sites (such as Facebook and Instagram) (Krutaine, 2016). Pakistan e-commerce industry is expected to surpass several hundred million dollars by 2020 (Siddiqui, 2016).   Social commerce is one significant area where performance of Pakistani e-commerce businesses is not up to the mark. One significant reason behind this performance is lack of understanding of social commerce (Omer, 2017). The other significant reason is the perceived risk of social commerce in the minds of customers. This study aims to explore the impact of perceived risk on determinants of customers’ social commerce engagement.  Utilizing the available academic literature, a conceptual model would be developed and analyzed using SmartPLS software. A sample of customers would be drawn from ten most populated cities of Pakistan i.e. Karachi, Lahore, Faisalabad, Rawalpindi, Gujranwala, Peshawar, Multan, Hyderabad, Islamabad, and Quetta. The results of the study are expected to facilitate Pakistani e-commerce industry in their preparation for formulating a sound and effective social commerce strategy.

data.projectName: Identification of Synthetically Generated Videos Using Forensic Analysis Techniques
data.projectDigest:
Digital media has numerous benefits including ease of access and vast propagation of information. Any media created at a user's device can be shared with thousands of people in a matter of minutes. This has changed our lives for the better in most ways. There is however a growing concern for the authenticity of the content being shared. In recent years we have seen that intelligent systems have been used to create fake content that is so realistic that it cannot be detected by a non-suspecting person. Modification of images has been in play for quite a few years but the application of the same techniques to videos was previously too cumbersome and resource intensive. The application of machine learning models for this task has made it possible to easily create convincing fake video content. Even though most of this content is created for recreational purposes, some of the modifications are done with malicious intent and have very adverse effects on the audience it is intended for.
Video forgery is of many types and involves different level of expertise to generate it. Few famous types are Graphical based approaches, frame reselection, Facial Identity Manipulation, Facial Expression Modification. The focus of this research is facial expression modification. This is a type of forgery in which the facial expressions of one person, are mapped onto another one. To achieve this the key points of a face are extracted, tracked and replaced. This type of forgery have potential to generate a video of any person saying ANY THING. This can be very threatening in this era of social media. The proposed research aims at detecting such forgeries. It will classify the forged and pristine videos based on statistical and physiological analysis.

data.projectName: Development of Model of Success for Industrialization in Special Economic Zones under CPEC initiative: An Indigenous Industrial Entrepreneur’s Perspective
data.projectDigest:
The purpose of this project is to develop a model of success  for Industrialization in Special Economic Zones under CPEC initiative.  This  study will be commenced based on qualitative and quantitative methodology. The outcomes of this research study will significantly contribute to academic literature on CPEC project with respect to Pakistani industrial entrepreneurs’ understanding on CPEC initiatives for industrialization through establishing special economic zones. This study will link the causes of failure of economic zone in Pakistan in past and suggest a way forward for success of special economic zones to be created under CPEC initiatives. A missing link in literature that is model of success for industrialization through indigenous entrepreneurs will be full filled by this study. In order to generalize the results, the model of success to be developed in this study will also be empirically tested through statistical analysis.
This study on CPEC will help the policy makers about the significant contributing factors for success of special economic zones and industrialization in Pakistan. On the basis of this study, the policy makers will able to formulate and implement policies for success of CPEC initiatives. On the other hand, the entrepreneur of Pakistan will also enable through this study to mobilize their business towards the targeted special economic zones. In overall through the success of industrialization and new startups, Pakistan will achieve the targets of CPEC in the area of socio-economic success.

data.projectName: An Evaluation of Tacrolimus Levels and Risk of Acute Graft Versus-Host Disease in Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Background: 
Achieving therapeutic tacrolimus blood concentrations is crucial for decreasing the risk of developing acute graftversus-host-disease (aGvHD) in allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (aHSCT) patients. Studies have suggested that tacrolimus levels in the first 1-2 weeks may affect the risk of aGVHD but therapeutic goals are not well established. This study explores tacrolimus levels and risk of GVHD during that time frame. 
Methods: 
This study is a retrospective cohort single center chart review performed with 348 consecutive adult patients who received an aHSCT and were followed for at least 100 days post-transplant for aGvHD development. Patients that received a transplant from a cord blood or participated in aGvHD prophylaxis clinical trials were excluded. The primary endpoint was aGvHD grades II - IV incidence. Serum tacrolimus levels were evaluated from days -1 to +100 post-transplant. Serum tacrolimus levels were divided into time intervals of days 0 - 7 and days 0 - 14 post-transplant. Receiver operator characteristic curves (ROC) were used to quantify serum tacrolimus levels as predictors of aGvHD grades II-IV. Using the ROC analysis and Youden’s Index, optimal cutpoints in the tacrolimus level distribution for the individual time intervals were assessed. From this, patients were analyzed based on whether they achieved mean tacrolimus serum levels below the cutpoint (low group) or if they achieved a mean tacrolimus level above the cutpoint (high group).

data.projectName: Issues and Challenges of Women in South Punjab in Local Bodies Elections 2015: Implication for their Socio-Economic and Political Conditions
data.projectDigest:
Issues and Challenges of Women in South Punjab Local Bodies Elections 2015: Implication for their Socio-Economic and Political Conditions

The females' political empowerment faces serious challenges in Pakistan. Despite comprising half of nation’s population, currently 20% women are members of national legislature, and the situation at the local legislature is not encouraging either, which indicates that women face representation issues at local and national level. This empirical study addresses the political participation of women in South Punjab.
The central objectives are:  
To address challenges that women faced during the 2015 Local Bodies’ Elections in South Punjab and its implications for their socio-economic and political empowerment. 
To distinguish the nature and intensity of the issues and challenges among the targeted divisions of South Punjab. 
To identify the appropriate measures that can help promote females' political involvement and representation at local level in South Punjab. 
While there is an inordinate amount of literature on women’s empowerment, the literature on women’s challenges during the Local bodies’ election in Southern Punjab is underrepresented. The study will demonstrate that institutional, cultural, religious, historical and patriarchal challenges have directly or indirectly affected women participation during Southern Punjab Local bodies elections of 2015. Equally, this investigation will propose the measures to enhance political participation of women in the region. To this end mixed method research methodology will be employed using both primary and secondary data sources. This inspection will make contribution to the literature on females’ political empowerment at local bodies’ level.

data.projectName: Preparing a reference seismic map for the geotechnical application in the urban areas
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Urban areas are hub of construction activities which involve projects from small scale to large. Majority of these projects are small scale projects. The resilient and sustainable construction of these small projects requires to assurance the efficiency of the building design and the cost through produce accurate geotechnical design parameters. Usually, the design parameters provided by conventional geotechnical investigation using both laboratory and field tests. However, in many cases, this investigation is critically minimized or even ignored in the small project to cutdown the cost of geotechnical tests and accelerate the construction process due to the limited geotechnical investigation facilities in the urban centers in Islamabad, consequently, increase the risk of failure of the small projects. To overcome this issue, a reference seismic map (base on the correlation of geotechnical and seismic techniques) can replace the conventional geotechnical report. Thus, reduce the cost of measuring the design parameters and shorten the construction duration as resulting increase the project resilience and sustainability. The seismic map will be used as a reference guide to predict the geotechnical design parameters at the small projects. Consequently, reducing the cost of measuring the design parameters simultaneously maintenance the accuracy of it. Moreover, this map may be integrated with existing landuse regulations of concerned development authorities to ensure resilient and sustainable construction

data.projectName: Conservation of Economically Important Rare, Endemic and Threatened Aconitum Species from Hindukush Himalayan Regions of Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Aconitum species commonly known as Aconite, Monk’s hood or Atees are well-known Medicinal herbs used by local Hakims. Different plant parts are available in market and online websites e.g. Daraz.com. The price of 100 gms powder obtained from the plant parts, ranges from Rs 800-1000, which is widely used in different medicinal formulations to treat a variety of ailments. Various species of the plant are endemic and rarely available at heights in Alpine and Sub-Alpine regions of HinduKush Himalayan ranges of Pakistan. The poor local people of mountains make vigorous expeditions to collect the plant in abundance for economic benefits.  
Different factors which include over collection pressure, low seed viability, growth of plant in narrow climatic zones, misidentification of plants with no reported data of hotspots, and ineffective conservation measures are pushing the plant to extinction from its natural habitats in Pakistan. 
The project is designed to conserve native, rare and threatened species of Aconitum through different experiments; of micro-propagation, DNA and Computational Biology, and reporting of exiting populations of Aconitum species from Hindukush Himalayan Regions of Pakistan. This joint effort planned by Academia, need funding for visits, consumables, equipment and publications to meet the objectives.

data.projectName: Study of magneto-hydrodynamic convective flow of chemically reacting non-Newtonian fluids
data.projectDigest:
The concept of fluid flow is always around us either in the form of air surrounding us or water in rivers. Air and water are always moving, but this fact was unknown either they are moving themselves or some forces are involved. When fluid dynamics was not developed, people did not know the actual reason of fluid flow. Our project is concerned with the fluids flow which is largely used in everyday life, industry and engineering.
Fluid can be divided into many categories. The easiest subdivision is Newtonian (relation between rate of deformation and shear stress is linear) fluids and non-Newtonian (relation between rate of deformation and shear stress is not linear) fluids. Air and water are Newtonian fluids while honey, ketchup, toothpaste, etc., are non-Newtonian fluids.  In comparison with Newtonian fluids, non-Newtonian fluids perform an essential role in scientific applications due to their molecular structure and behavior. They have many uses in engineering, geophysics, astrophysics, soil sciences, food processing, oceanography, and so forth.
There is scarcity of the literature about the study of magneto-hydrodynamic convective flow of chemically reacting non-Newtonian fluids, but some studies regarding such flow of Newtonian fluids are reported. Engineers and academic workers are very much concerned about the geometry of such type of flow of non-Newtonian fluids; since these flows have numerous industrial usages such as bio-engineering and oil exploration.
With the ambit of this project, we want to examine the magneto-hydrodynamic convective flow of chemically reacting non-Newtonian fluids and explore new results which will constitute a foundation for further investigation concerning future development in fluid dynamics and other related fields of research.

data.projectName: Sonic Hedgehog (Shh) Pathway as a Therapeutic Target in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
data.projectDigest: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common type of primary liver cancer. HCC ranked as 5th frequent cancer and 3rd most common cause of morbidity worldwide. In Pakistan, HCC prevalence is varies from 3.7%-16% of other malignancies. Chronic liver diseases are fifth most common cause of morbidity and mortality in Pakistan. Treatment methods are available only for early stage but for advanced stage HCC chemotherapy is the only option. . Sorafenib is FDA approved drug for advanced HCC with 1% survival rate.  Thus, there is always a high need for the identification of new therapeutic targets. The objective of the study is to identify new therapeutic target and agent using proteomic and genomic approaches. Various pathways are involved in carcinogenesis such as Sonic hedghoge (Shh) signaling pathway. Shh pathway functionally active only in growing embryo. Shh pathway becomes reactivated in differentiated liver tissues that lead to rapid cell growth and proliferation. Some Shh inhibitors have been approved for use in basal cell carcinoma, leukemia and breast cancer. Therefore it is hypothesize that in HCC Shh pathway needs to be further investigated and inhibition of this pathway could be an interesting criterion for the development of novel therapeutic targets.

data.projectName: Prevalence and Determinants of Psychological Distress among Women with Primary Infertility in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The health care system in Pakistan sparsely caters the medical needs of women with infertility, and the health care professionals overlook the psychological dimension of infertility. Literature shows that infertility is not just a medical problem, it also causes psychological distress that impedes the progress in infertility treatment and leads to never ending vicious cycle of infertility. No step has ever been taken to develop and validate a need based intervention plan that could address the psychological issues faced by infertile women in Pakistan. The proposed research will empirically assess the prevalence  of infertility related distress, and the relative predictive strength of hardiness, spirituality, fate control, spousal reciprocity, and perceived social support in the psychological distress of infertile women, so that a cost effective and need based intervention plan could be proposed in the context of Pakistan. Valid and reliable tools will be used to collect data. A sample of 500 women of reproductive age (25-45year), who are seeking infertility treatment will be included in the study. The sample will be collected from different hospitals and infertility centers in Pakistan (public and private). The married women living with their husbands will participate in the study.

data.projectName: Investigating the current HIV epidemic in Sindh and its possible mode of transmission particularly in Children
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) continues to be the major global health issue responsible for the millions of death so far. The epidemiological and molecular characterization of HIV subtypes are of great interest worldwide. This has not been carried out in Sindh despite an accelerating increase in prevalence of HIV is evident. This study is aimed to determine the magnitude of the HIV problem among the population of Sindh and to better understand the genetic diversity and the epidemiologic dynamics of HIV, as well as to correlate that with the risk factors involved. During the course of study 10,000 samples will be collected by utilizing the vast network of collection points of DOW University of Health Sciences and Liaqat University of Medical and Health Sciences. RT-PCR, DNA sequencing, bioinformatics and in-depth statistical and correlation analysis will be carried out to understand the source and nature of the current epidemic.  The facilities available with the collaborating institutions make this study doable. The results of this study will not only improve the clinical management of infection but also aid the policy decision making to control the infection.

data.projectName: Developing resistant starch (RS) wheat lines using CRISPR-Cas9 and MAB-speed breeding
data.projectDigest: Wheat starch quality can be improved by increasing amylose contents. An effective strategy toward improving starch quality is to increase resistant starch (RS) by increasing amylose content in the starch. Long-term consumption of RS has the potential to prevent obesity, colonic diseases, increased insulin sensitivity and lower risk of cardiovascular diseases and Type 2 diabetes. In common wheat, amylose content can be increased by down regulating amylopectin biosynthesis genes because both amylose and amylopectin synthesis use adenosine diphosphoglucose as a substrate. Common wheat has six copies of SBEII gene. We hypothesize that wheat varieties with higher amylose and RS contents without any yield penalty can be developed by SBEII gene editing and precision breeding using Marker Assisted Backcrossing. All six SBEII genes will be knocked out using site specific clean gene technology of multiplex CRISPRCas9. In parallel, the five mutant alleles of SBEII from Patwin-515HP will be transferred in Pakistani cultivars using background and foreground marker assisted selection in speed breeding chamber. The positive stable mutant lines from CRISPRCas9 knockout work and sbeII NILs will be evaluated for yield potential. The outperforming mutant and NILs from field with increased amylose and RS contents will be registered before their commercialization.

data.projectName: POLITICAL ECONOMY OF ELECTORAL REPRESENTATION: Electoral Representation, Politics of Public Policy and Hegemonic War of Position in British India
data.projectDigest: The politics and public policy of present day Pakistan is deeply rooted in colonial India. Exploring Political economy of elections in British India is a significant attempt towards unfolding the relationship of colonisers and colonised within the framework of international political economy of 20th century.  Industrial revolution in Europe and global political economy constructed a political tone of British Empire . British empire in India capitalised gradually the process of political representation through tactical adjustment of procedures. Interestingly, electoral strategies were designed to protect the interests of colonisers. The process of colonisation of political representation was entrenched in land settlements and its codification. Restricted representation on the basis land, tax and military services provided a conducive space for creation of local bourgeois in electoral processes. The voices of subalterns remained unrepresented in the process of colonisation of political representation. The purpose of colonised political representation seemed to create a local bourgeois class from subalterns who interpret the narratives of colonisers to maintain order for maximising the interest of British Empire in India. The process of political representation and electocratization was instrumental to maximise the interest of British colonisers and undermine the representation of subaltern voices.  This study is an attempt to explore political economy of elections  in British India.

data.projectName: Efficacy of Fixed Time Artificial Insemination (FATI) to Improve the Reproductive Efficiency  of Buffaloes during Peak and Low Breeding Season
data.projectDigest:
Buffaloes suffer from poor reproductive efficiency in many areas of Pakistan. Major problems that impair the reproductive performance of buffaloes are long post-partum anestrus and lack of expression of behavioral estrus. Exact diagnosis of estrus signs in buffaloes requires the continuous observations at many times and a well qualified knowledgeable farmers and labors. In herds, failure of estrus detection results in increase number of services per conception and less number of calves. These factors can cause the long calving interval as well as the development of the stage of anestrous in buffaloes. Similarly, postpartum anestrus due to follicular and luteal cyst is also considered as important cause of poor reproductive efficiency of buffaloes.   Applications of certain reproductive tools that do not require the identification of estrus signs may contribute the increase in conception rate subsequently improve of reproductive efficiency in buffaloes. 
Keeping in view these reproductive problems of buffaloes,   this study will be performed in four tehsils of District Poonch and Kotli. Farmers having two to three animals will be registered for capacity building and their animals will be treated for fixed time artificial insemination in peak breeding and low breeding season. The blood of these inseminated animals will be collected on day 19th of AI and pregnancy will be checked through ultrasound on day 40, 60 and 90 following insemination for pregnancy diagnosis and fetal losses during peak and low breeding season. Obtained data will be subjected to appropriate statistical analysis.

data.projectName: Thermo-tolerant, phosphate solubilizing bacteria (PSB) and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) for sustainable phosphorus nutrition of cotton
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest:
Heat stress and phosphorus nutrition are of great concern in cotton growing arid-semiarid region of south Punjab. Global warming has led to intense shocks and prolonged the summer duration the growing season of cotton crop. Moreover, the depleting phosphorus resources in the world has led to establish an ecofriendly and economic strategy for efficient phosphorus nutrition of cotton. Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi and rhizobacteria having thermo tolerance and phosphate solubilization capability may improve cotton production and phosphorus nutrition.
Present project has been proposed to isolate various arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi and rhizobacteria from the rhizosphere of cotton cultivated in south Punjab. The isolates will be characterized for thermo tolerance, phosphate solubilization and plant growth promoting potential for cotton. The selected isolates will be evaluated in natural conditions for improving growth and production of cotton. A consortia of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi and rhizobacteria will be formulated and tried on different carriers for seed application in cotton. 
The successful completion of the project will lead towards substantial savings in GDP of the country, increase profitability of the resource poor farmer and contribute in poverty alleviation.

data.projectName: DEVELOPMENT AND CHARACERTIZATION OF SUSTAINABLE AND ENVIRONMENT FRIENDLY GEOPOLYMER MATERIALS FOR THERMAL, ELECTRICAL AND CTALYTIC APPLICATIONS.
data.projectDigest:
Coal ash, rice husk ash and natural soil is considered as a cheapest raw materials in our country. Although, some portion of the ash is used by the cement processing industries, but bulk is used for only landfilling application. The geopolymerization of this ash and soil may not only solve the dumping problem of coal ash but it can generate more revenue for the industry. Moreover, the bricks, mortar and concrete manufactured from coal ash can serve as a potential substitute for conventional bricks and ordinary Portland cement. Its partial replacement with geopolymers will reduce the demand of optimized Portland cement (OPC) and conventional bricks. 
This project will focus on the porosity management of the geopolymer materials which will affect three major properties like thermal, electrical insulation and catalytic properties. Geopolymers can easily be converted to insulating foams which may not only be used in low thermal conductive insulation for the buildings but also can support a catalyst in some chemical reactions by controlling the surface area. All these three properties are related to control of surface area of the geopolymer materials.
Natural soil is also a widely available and sustainable raw material and if it is processed into geopolymer mortar and foams then it would become a never-ending source of construction materials. These clay or ash based geopolymer if produced in a controlled pore size, can be used as electrical insulators in electrical industries. Their properties can be tailored according to requirements. 
Moreover, the effect of in situ-carbonation on the properties of conventional geopolymers will also be studied and this may result in geopolymers with enhanced mechanical plus electrical and catalytic properties of the foams.

data.projectName: Synthesis of 99mTc and 177Lu based radiopharmaceuticals for diagnosis and treatment of Head & Neck, Ovarian and Prostate Cancer.
data.projectDigest:
Vascular endothelial growth factor receptor (VEGF) & epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) are over expressed in a variety of tumors and has served as a well established target for diagnosis and therapy of various cancers. To target VEGF & EGFR, our aim is to develop specific anti-VEGF & anti-EGFR radiopharmaceuticals (radiotracers) for diagnosis and treatment of Head & Neck, Ovarian and Prostate cancer. To that end, monoclonal antibodies (Cetuximab & Bevacizumab) will be labeled with Technetium-99m (99mTc; gamma emitter) & Lutetium-177 (177Lu; beta emitter) using different bifunctional chelating agents, with the aim is to transport specifically the gamma and beta emitters to target cell that has been over expressing the VEGF and or EGFR, so as to obtain exact information about the actual pathology. The labeled anti-VEGF and anti-EGFR before clinical application will be assessed for its in vitro stability in saline & serum, binding with cancer cell lines, immunoreactivity & internalization, dose escalation, biodistribution and SPECT analysis in Head & Neck, Ovarian and Prostate cancer mouse/rabbit model.

Vascular endothelial growth factor receptor (VEGF) & epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) are over expressed in a variety of tumors and has served as a well established target for diagnosis and therapy of various cancers. To target VEGF & EGFR, our aim is to develop specific anti-VEGF & anti-EGFR radiopharmaceuticals (radiotracers) for diagnosis and treatment of Head & Neck, Ovarian and Prostate cancer. To that end, monoclonal antibodies (Cetuximab & Bevacizumab) will be labeled with Technetium-99m (99mTc; gamma emitter) & Lutetium-177 (177Lu; beta emitter) using different bifunctional chelating agents, with the aim is to transport specifically the gamma and beta emitters to target cell that has been over expressing the VEGF and or EGFR, so as to obtain exact information about the actual pathology. The labeled anti-VEGF and anti-EGFR before clinical application will be assessed for its in vitro stability in saline & serum, binding with cancer cell lines, immunoreactivity & internalization, dose escalation, biodistribution and SPECT analysis in Head & Neck, Ovarian and Prostate cancer mouse/rabbit model.

data.projectName: Integrated Hydraulic Modeling of Extreme Flows Influenced by Climatic Variations and Consequent Levee Failure Risk in Northern Mountain Range
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest:
South Asia in general and Pakistan in particular is prone to large scale damages from extreme flows. Furthermore, Pakistan is ranked as the 5th most vulnerable country to the climate change by the German Watch. In spite of these challenges, Pakistan lacks sophisticated flood forecasting and propagation tools suited to its environment. The current practices of flood modeling do not fully reflect the scale of climate change and its related uncertainties in the modeling output. This is true for Pakistan particularly, whereas the rest of the world is adapting its practices to integrated deterministic and stochastic approaches for flood forecasting and propagation.
This research aims to address the aforementioned challenges through integrated hydraulic modeling of floods and derive the risk of high flows to flood protection works. The project will conduct both numerical and physical modeling of extreme flows predicted from climate change effects in the Northern Mountain Region. The output will make significant direct impacts on societal challenges such as engineering design, modeling, and forecasting of extreme flooding events.

data.projectName: Development and Promotion of Efficient and Low Cost Solar Energy Dryers for Dehydration of Food Products in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
The proposed drying system shall serve as a demonstration model to six million farmers in Punjab who may adopt the technology and dry food products before selling in the market. 85% of the farmers have land holdings up to 25 acres and they will be the potential customers of the system. 
The system has wide applications in food processing, cement, textile etc. industries. The number of food industry is over 1000 where in solar heated air and liquids can be applied with low costs solutions. This will save energy required for fossil fuel fired dryers, especially during the day time. Experience shows that substantial savings (55%) of the electricity could be made by applying solar drying technologies in Industry.

data.projectName: Non-chemical management of Betel vine diseases in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Betel vine (Piper betle) locally known as “PAAN” is an important cash crop consumed by 2 billion people worldwide. Local production of betel vine in Pakistan meets only 5% of the total demands and the rest is imported from India and Bangladesh. Although it can be successfully cultivated in the coastal areas of Sindh and Balochistan, but our local farmers possess inadequate knowledge about crop management. Major limiting factor in betel vine production are pathogenic diseases that can proliferate within a short period of time due to the humid environment. The major diseases of betel vine include powdery mildew, leaf spots, anthracnose, wilts, collar rot, foot and root rots. Crop losses due to these ailments range between 30-100%. Moreover, these issues have never been practically resolved for the local farmers. On the other hand, indiscriminate use of fungicides especially over this edible foliage poses a pesticide toxicity among the consumers. Hence quality production of betel vine has become more challenging with the passage of time.
Keeping the overall requirements in view, a comprehensive project has been designed to promote the cultivation of betel vine in Pakistan by addressing the disease management practices with safe chemicals. This research will reduce the higher costs of imports and the output of study will be utilized as a technology transfer tool for our farming community.

data.projectName: Development of high energy density rechargeable batteries and supercapacitors
data.projectDigest: It is well know to everyone that recently Pakistan is facing severe energy crises and problems environmental pollution, as our industrial and transportation sector rely only on hazardous fossil fuels.  Therefore, it is very important to discover clean and renewable energy technologies. In this context, rechargeable batteries and supercapacitors are considered promising republicans to fossil fuel based energy technologies. However, these energy storage systems fail to meet the increasing demand of energy due to their low energy densities, poor life cycle and short shelf-life. Therefore, its very critical to develop battery/supercapacitors technologies with high enough energy densities and long lifespan. In this Project, new strategies will be developed to prepare nanostructured materials for use in Li based batteries and supercapacitors.

data.projectName: Biosynthesis of cloned Keratinolytic enzyme from bacterial strain with waste management potential.
data.projectDigest: With the increase in world’s population and deficiency of food, feed is emphasizing to rummage new-fangled protein sources from different waste materials like keratinous wastes. Globally, millions of tons of keratinous wastes are generated from different processing industries (agriculture and poultry, etc.), which are the prevalent and abundant reservoir of pure keratin. Management and recycling of these wastes have become one of the major environmental concerns due to the recalcitrant and complex structure of keratin. Keratin, an insoluble structural protein is present in hair, nail, feather, wool, skin and horn of animals, it is highly stable in environment due to its complex structure. Enzymatic degradation of keratin wastes are more preferred over various conventional approaches which are costly and not environmentally sound. Keratinases have numerous applications including biomedical products, leather processing, cosmetic, fiber modification, animal nutrients, processing of feather-meal for bio-fertilizer and feed, detergent formulation, pharmaceutical industries, waste management, bioremediation and biofuel production. The quest of keratinolytic enzymes has become the goal of research worldwide. The aim of this project is to produce new keratinase enzyme isolate from keratinolytic bacterium, clone and over-express in a well-organized host system using a proficient vector along with promoter. To achieve high production and overexpression of cloned enzyme various strategies will be applied. The recombinant enzyme will be characterized completely to evaluate its applicability in commercial use.

data.projectName: Need of Fields, Strings and gravity
data.projectDigest: Standard Model is very precise theory in particle physics and it reveals very interesting facts about nature  and all these are verified by the experiments. But, despite all of its  successes it is not a complete theory and we have to go beyond and it is known as new physics. There is no restriction on generation of leptons and quarks but to meet the requirements of observations matter content of standard model  is usually taken. But, to understand and explain LSND and the MiniBooNE experiments data regarding anti-neutrino of electron excess in  anti-neutrino of muon beam which cannot be fully explained by three neutrinos generations, we have to introduce 4th generation neutrino.  This will ultimately provide us the information about the new physics .

data.projectName: Technology Development for the production and evaluation of purified vaccine against Foot and Mouth Disease to  enhance the export of livestock products in international halal market
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan, Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD)Vaccine production units are producing whole culture vaccine. i.e. vaccine contains both structural proteins (SPs) and non structural  proteins (NSPs) as well as proteins of the growth media. This leads towards not only production of antibodies against NSPs but also put extra immunological burden on the immune system of the animals. Presence of antibodies against NSPs of the  FMD virus in livestock commodities represents the infection and a big hurdle for the export of livestock related products. So to improve the quality of vaccine, get access to the international market for the export of livestock products and reduce the extra burden on immune system of animals, Pakistan will have to put energies towards the production of purified (NSPs free) vaccine against FMD.

data.projectName: Anti-Helicobacter pylori activity enhancement and dosage form development of
data.projectDigest: Bergenin is a phytochemical isolated from a number of medicinal plants. The compound is pharmacologically active with anti-inflammatory, antidiabetic and antiulcer activities. The antiulcer property of bergenin is found to be due to activity against Helicobacter pylori-a causative agent of gastric and duodenal ulcers. The chemical has moderate activity against Helicobacter pylori which can be enhanced by modifying the chemical structure of the compound. Moreover, the chemical can be formulated as an oral dosage form for administration to the ulcer patients. However, a major problem in development of oral dosage form of the bergenin is its poor bioavailability attributed to low water solubility and intestinal permeability. The solubility and permeability and hence bioavailability can again be improved by structure modifications. So, the aim of present project is to modify the chemical structure of the molecule so as to enhance its anti-Helicobacter pylori activity, solubility, intestinal permeability and bioavailability and finally, to develop the oral dosage form of bergenin.  This may provide a new therapy for the treatment of gastric ulcers.

data.projectName: Application Multiple Intelligence in assessment of secondary school students and development of Model for Assesment
data.projectDigest:
Assessment of student learning is indispensible at the end of each academic year. In Pakistan, students learning are assessed only through paper and pencil examination especially in Board Examination. Due to threat of failure the teachers and students are focusing on memorizing contents instead of building concepts. They get  good marks on this basis but when exposed to some other relevant situation/s, often they fail or cannot qualify it. It is considered that each individual is intelligent and there are nine types of intelligences. Some have all and some have two or more than two types of intelligence. Students learn better if they were teach according to their style. Some are better in linguistic, while some are better in musical, logical-methematical, spatial, body-kinesthetic and etc. but when we assess their learning we use only one method for all students equally while accepting their individual differences. 
Mostly students are complaining about the assessment methods the questions were unclear, the environment was not good, cannot memorize contents, inability of writing, etc. for example the opportunity was offered to  student/s to share their knowledge in written form and it might reveal the they actually know more than they were able to write.

data.projectName: “Investigation of cardiovascular benefits of some isolated phytochemicals through dry and wet lab approaches”
data.projectDigest: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) include high blood pres¬sure, coronary heart disease; congestive heart failure and stroke and have become a serious medical problem throughout the world and are thought to be the most common cause of death by the year 2020.It is reported that 40 million people  of Pakistan are  hypertensive. As many as 1.4 million children are suffering from heart related diseases in Pakistan and some 8,000 need heart surgeries annually, but out of them only 1,200 are operated upon. Pakistan is rich with medicinal flora possess diversified quantities of phytochemicals such as glycoside, flavonoids etc. A number of these phytochemicals have been reported for their CVS benefits more of them yet to be validated for cardiovascular benefits. Therefore, the present study will be design to explore cardiovascular potential of some of these compounds. Preliminary in-silico techniques (Dry Lab) will be carried out to identify potential drug-like candidates with CVD benefits against various CVS targets such as ACE, Ca+ Channel, Beta receptor and many others. Hypotensive/Antihypertensive/diuretic effects of selected isolated phytochemicals in Sprague Dawley rats will be evaluated.Vascular reactivity studies will be carried out to using rat aorta to probe the underlining mechanism(s) of hypertension and cardiac protection. The cardioprotective activity of selected phytochemicals against isoproterenol-induced MI in Sprague Dawley rats will also be studied. The selected compounds will also be studied for their protective effect against fructose induced metabolic alteration in rats. Finally these compounds will be subjected toxicity studies. The compounds with excellent pharmacological and safety profile will be subjected for preformulation studies.

data.projectName: Preparation and evaluation of cocktail of Bacteriophages for the control and treatment of bovine mastitis
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: The treatment of bacterial infections with bacteriophages is termed as phage therapy, is one of the alternative options to reduce antimicrobial resistance. Our objective is to isolate and characterize bacteriophages from environmental samples against mastitis causing micro-organisms as an alternative of antibiotics to reduce cost and increase efficacy of treatment. The bacteriophages will be isolated from samples against isolated host strains by plaque as well as double layer agar method. After isolation of bacteriophages, physical and genetic characterization of bacteriophages will be tested. The host range of the isolated phages will be assessed on different bacteria including methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Escherichia coli. The Toxicity and safety checks of bacteriophages will be evaluated by cell culture including fibroblast cell culture, infection of bacteriophage on cell culture, toxic effects of bacteriophages in-vitro in micro plates and MTT assay. In-vivo efficacy of bacteriophages will be evaluated by administering different doses of phage lysate to experimental animals (mice) then to clinical and subclinical cases of large animals from different routes. This project will help in early treatment of mastitis in dairy animals by bacteriophages and reduction in emergence of antibiotic resistance in mastitis causing microorganisms.

data.projectName: Development of nanoparticles-based immunogenic assay through E. coli expressed CTB-fused VP2 protein
data.projectDigest: Gumboro is the second largest viral disease of the poultry which is caused by Infectious bursal disease virus (IBDV). Its outbreak can only be avoided by using immunodominant vaccine because IBDV directly disrupts immune response by destroying antibody producing B cells. In this study, we will determine the efficacy of immunodominant recombinant VP2 protein fused with Cholera toxin B subunit (CTB) in chickens and will develop nanoparticle-based immunoassay. For this purpose, the chemically synthesize immunogenic VP2 protein gene fused with CTB will be cloned in pet30a vector and expression will be verified through SDS Polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (PAGE) and western blot analysis. The efficacy of recombinant VP2 protein will further be examined through systemic and mucosal immunity in sera of immunized chickens. The purified VP2 protein (antigen) both captured and detector will be subjected to bind with gold nanoparticles respectively. After immunization, gold nanoparticles will be used as detector of immunoglobulin against IBDV after immunization with recombinant VP2 in sera of immunized chickens. The immunization results will determine the fate of VP2 protein to be used for immunization of chicks against IBDV. Moreover, the study will be helpful for development of immunosensitive assay to detect immunoglobulin through nanoparticles.

data.projectName: Transformation of Conventional linearized Tool Path to Optimized NURBS Tool Path for CNC Milling of Sculptured Surfaces.
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Computer numerical control (CNC) machining is a process in the manufacturing organizations that uses computers to control machines. The CNC tool path (NC codes) are represented either in non-parametric form (linear and circular) or parametric form. Conventionally the NC codes are written in non-parametric form which produces several problems. To take the full advantage of CNC technology during high speed and accurate machining of complex shapes like; dies, molds, aerospace and automotive components, the NC codes need to be represented in parametric form. Current state of art CAD/CAM systems are able to generate these NC codes in parametric representation from the CAD models, but it is a challenge to convert the existing non-parametric NC codes (which have already been generated by the CAM systems) into parametric form. The aim of the proposed project is to develop an integrated, interactive, and GUI based software tool which will transform these conventional NC codes into parametric (NURBS) tool paths with optimized feed rates. NURBS tool path generated by the proposed method will ensure the machining of complex shapes with high speed and accuracy. In addition, to facilitate the interpolation process during machining, the tool path will be re-parameterized with approximate arc lengths.

data.projectName: UAV based Crop Monitoring System using Deep learning
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
The development of UAV-based remote sensing systems is considered as a promising platform for Precision Agriculture (PA). The use of UAVs in monitoring of different crops offers great possibilities to acquirefield data in an easy, fast and cost-effective way compared to previous conventional methods. UAVs’ have ability to flyat a low altitude results in ultra-high spatial resolution images of the crops (i.e., a few centimeters).This significantly improves the performance of the monitoring systems, therefore increases the yields.
In this study, a low-altitude UAV platform with multispectral camera will be developed for the detection of yellow rust diseaseinstigated by plant stress in winter wheat for precision agriculture. This work mainly focuses ondiscrimination of healthy wheat plants from yellow rust infected through calculation of spectral band and Spectral Vegetation Index (SVI); and designing a frame work for low-cost crop monitoring system specially wheat yellow rust. An intelligent yellow rust detection system will be developed using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) from labeled UAV aerial multispectral imagery.CNN as one of the deep learning models is good at exploiting semantic features and classification of imagery data.

data.projectName: EFFECTS OF CONCENTRIC VERSUS ECCENT.RIC EXERCISES ALONG WITH AEROBIC TRAINING ON MUSCLE PERFORMANCE IN PATIENTS WITH TYPE II DIABETES MELLITUS
data.projectDigest:
Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) is a highly prevalent chronic metabolic disorder deteriorating multi-systemic functions of human body. It is mainly characterized by hyperglycemia due to deficiency or inefficiency of insulin hormone. The prevalence of T2DM is more than 26.3% in Pakistan and this burden is expected to be raised up to 171-366 million till 2030. T2DM decline the skeletal muscle performance and metabolic status of human body leading to compromised physical performance, aerobic capacity, and quality of life. The significant increase in T2DM burden is a challenge for the health care professionals to find new and appropriate treatment strategies to manage physical performance. 
Exercise training is an integral part of management of patients with T2DM and needs to explore and test the exercise programs to deal better with dysfunctional muscle performance. Aerobic and muscle strengthening exercises are proven part of management for patients with T2DM but different strengthening exercises are still needed to be experimented for superiority on one another.  
The current project is aimed to compare the effects of concentric versus eccentric exercises along with aerobic training on muscle performance, including muscle strength, endurance and flexibility in patients with T2DM as it is directly related to quality of life.

data.projectName: The Surface Modification of Biodegradable Magnesium Alloys for Orthopedic Implant Applications
data.projectDigest: The breakage of human bone is very unfortunate for the human being. The joining of the broken bone is a very crucial step and for the proper alignment of the bone, surgeons normally insert metallic rods to join the broken bones. The insertion of a foreign material (metal) in the human body is a very aggressive source of infection. Initially, Cobalt-Chrome (Co-Cr) alloys were used as a metallic device. These alloys were much heavier than the human bone. This extra weight carried by the patient and the low corrosion resistance of these alloys made the introduction of corrosion resistant stainless steel as a biomaterial. The stainless steel ruled as a main biomaterial. Then Titanium alloys were introduced as a lighter material than stainless steel. The patient starts feeling pain in the implanted area of the body because of the corrosion of the material within the body. The patient had to bear the second surgery of removal of this corroded implant. Magnesium Alloys, have the unique property to become the part of human body as implanted material after some time. These implants are a need of time, to avoid the pain of second surgery and the costs for the patients in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Correlative study of fluoride in drinking water and prevalence of dental fluorosis and caries in children of Sindh, Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Fluoride, is known prevent dental caries at concentrations of >0.7 mg/l in warmer climates. Worldwide, a dramatic drop in caries prevalence is seen as a result of water fluoridation. High fluoride concentrations lead to unsightly brownish-yellow discoloration of teeth known as fluorosis. In Pakistan, information in this regard is scanty.  So, it is the purpose of this study to conduct a correlative investigation about fluoride levels in drinking water, dental fluorosis and caries in Sindh, Pakistan.
The study will be carried out in two phases.  In phase-I, representative areas in districts of Sindh will be identified to collect water for analysis of fluoride levels. From the data collected, a detailed fluoride map of the province will be drawn, delineating areas of optimal, high and low fluoride. In phase II, a dental team will be trained to conduct dental examination assessing fluorosis and dental caries in a random sample of 12-16 years old Pakistani children. Data will be analyzed to determine prevalence of dental fluorosis and caries in populations consuming specific fluoride levels in their drinking water. Preventive (de-fluoridation of water with excess fluoride) or curative measures (water fluoridation in areas with low fluoride) can then be taken to prevent further detrimental effects to dentition because of fluoride levels in drinking water.

data.projectName: Identification and assessment of small and medium enterprises for technological up gradation in selected business hubs of Pakistan.
data.projectDigest: Small and medium-size enterprises (SMEs) play key role in the development of a country. Of all the private businesses of Pakistan, 90% are SMEs, employing 78% non- agriculture labor force and making 30% of total GDP of Pakistan. Furthermore, the sector’s contribution in export earnings is 25%. SME sector has substantial capacity in sugar, paper, textile, cement, ghee, sports good, rice, fruits, marble and fertilizers but the sector face numerous challenges, making it difficult to fully exploit available opportunities. Moreover, the inflow of Chinese businesses and investment can be turning point for SMEs. China is a technologically advanced country and local SMEs can benefit from their technology. This study proposes that SME sector can achieve maximum advantage of the available opportunities in national and international market when they possess updated technology. SMEs can be improve their performance through technology. Thus, the current study will carried out with the objective to identify potential SMEs and assess their technological needs. The methodology of Action research will be adopted in this study. The sample will be selected through purposive sampling technique. Two enumerators will be hired and data will be collected through interviews. For data analysis, Nvivo and Atlas.ti will be utilized. The study is significant to the development of a coherent policy regarding SME development which is backbone of the country economy.  Thus, it is imperative to examine the current challenges of SMEs by identifying potential businesses and assessing their technological needs.

data.projectName: Sutained reward based intervention towards road safety
data.projectDigest:
Human error accounts for 90% cause of a road accident. Constructing a safe driving behavior had always been a challenge and a priority of global organizations and governments. Most of the techniques and policies to intervene the driver’s behavior are either penalties or the punishment based. The theme of the subject research is that “the sustained driver’s exposure to a reward based transparent environment could help enhance positive safety behaviors”. To develop such an environment is near to impossible under conventional methods and technologies. To achieve it, 5th generation “Blockchain” technology would be deployed in parallel with automotive sensing technologies.
Two novel approaches make this research worth consideration, 
(1)- A vehicle-driver partnership to keep an accurate driving record for each drive through in-cabin sensing and a mobile application, (2)-Deployment of 5th generation “Blockchain” technology to intervene driver’s behavior through reward incentives. It would be the first time to use real human efforts (attitude and efforts to learn safe driving) as an input for token creation (cryptocurrency), (3)-If successfully deployed, the model may prove a revolutionary step towards innovative e-governance in almost any domain.

data.projectName: Synthesis and characterization of hybrid nanomaterials for biosensing application
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: The foremost requirement for the survival of human kind is better health. Therefore, regular health monitoring and checkup is imperative to ensure healthy living. There are a number of species in human blood whose levels can indicate the onset of a more serious disease. However, the abnormal levels of cholesterol and glucose in the human blood can lead to many serious diseases. Among them the cardiovascular disease, anemia, and hypertension and diabetes is very common. Therefore periodic monitoring of cholesterol in human blood serum and glucose is required to minimize the risk of these diseases. Commercially available techniques for biosensing (particularly cholesterol sensing) in blood serum rely on immobilization of enzymes using colorimetric and spectrophotometric methods. These are complex techniques and suffer from many issues. Electrochemical biosensors based on hybrid nanomaterialsthat work without the use of enzymes are imperative. Identification, synthesis and characterization of hybrid nanomaterials for non-enzymatic biosensing is need of the hour. Initial studies on biosensor materials synthesized by our group such as anodized TiO2 hybrid materials well as ZnO hybrid materials show great promise in monitoring the aforementioned species. These materials demonstrate fast response times and selective monitoring of the target analyte. This project will focus on synthesis and characterization of variety of hybrid nanomaterials for non-enzymatic biosensing application.

data.projectName: Development of Selected Natural Products For Medicinal Application in Gastrointestinal Diseases
data.projectDigest: This project is designed for the purpose of development of selected natural compounds into therapeutically useful drug molecules in gastrointestinal disorders. Natural compounds are rich source for lead discovery. Moreover, their development into medicinally useful agents can be done by pharmacological evaluation, modification through structure activity relationships and formulation into suitable dosage form. In this context we aim to perform pharmacological evaluation, molecular mechanism elucidation and therapeutic assesment of selected natural compounds for gastrointestinal diseases. Gastrointestinal (GI) diseases are one of the major health burdens globally and require multidrug regime for treatment. This development shall benefit in reducing the disease burden from community. The cost of multidrug regime for GI disorders will decrease. This will have positive impact on the health budget. The development of new drugs will also have high impact on the research and development of local pharmaceutical industry. In the long term it will benefit country’s economy and industrial development. The outcome of this research will open new areas of research in field of pharmaceutical chemistry and pharmaceutics by applying structure activity relationship technique to formulate more specific new derivaties of these compounds and their best possible dosage forms such as nanoparticles and targeted delivery molecules.

data.projectName: Phytogenic Selenium nanoparticles for biofortification and mitigation of drought stress in wheat
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) is the most important cereal crop for the majority of world’s populations, upto two billion people (36% of the world population). Drought is a major environmental stress threatening wheat productivity worldwide. SeNPs, as a special form of selenium (Se) supplement, have attracted worldwide attention due to their favorable properties and unique bioactivities. Foliar application of plants based selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs) may have the capacity to induce drought tolerance in the wheat crop. Similarly, biosynthesized SeNPs helps to induce and improve physiological, morphological and biochemical attributes and ultimately increase the productivity and grain quality of wheat crop. This research is going to be carried out to find out the most appropriate concentration of plants based SeNPs to enhance nutritional composition, productivity, biochemical and proteomics profiling of different wheat varieties under drought stress. The biosynthesized SeNPs will be characterized through Uv spectroscopy, SEM, EDX, Diffuse reflectance spectroscopy, Zeta analyzer, and XRD and FTIR. Different concentrations (10, 20, 30 and 40 ppm) of SeNPs will be exogenously applied on different wheat varieties under drought stress.  Selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs) may have the potential to enhance grains quality, productivity, biochemical and proteome profiling of wheat varieties under drought stress.

data.projectName: Water-Energy-Carbon-Climate Nexus of the Power Generation Sector of Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest: For any nation, robust energy supply is important for economic growth and improvement in living standards. In Pakistan, energy crisis has been bottlenecking economic development for the past several years. This energy shortage can be attributed to improper planning and policymaking. Pakistan lacks in integrated planning of the energy sector but recent advancements in research suggest that energy sector cannot be planned alone, there is another realm which not only requires its own proper planning but also needs to be integrated to the energy and climate policies for sustainable future; that realm is water. Climate change also affects both of these realms adversely in the future, therefore, the effects of climate change (i.e. increase in average global temperature & decrease in precipitation) on the power generation sector of Pakistan. This interconnection is famously known as Water-Energy-Climate Nexus (WEC). This project plans to conduct WEC analysis on the power generation sector of Pakistan (focusing on hydro & thermal power plants). This project will analyze and support the policymaking institutions in devising proper planning and policies. CO2 emissions of the plants will also be estimated to find whether the country is on the track to meet its 2015 Paris climate commitments.

data.projectName: Potential of thermo-acoustic method for pharmacokinetic drug-drug interactions.
data.piUniversity: Lahore College for Women University, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Adverse drug events affect millions of patients yearly. Pharmacological molecular interactions are an important component of drug-related adverse events that could be avoided in clinical practice. Different methods like chromatographic separation, UV coupled HPLC, liquid chromatography and liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry has been used for evaluation of drug-drug interactions. In recent years, Thermo-acoustic method; A Physico-chemical approach is being used to investigate molecular interactions in solutions. Thermo-acoustic method could be preferable over other conventional methods in pharmacokinetic Drug-Drug interactions too. Density and sound velocity measurements are done in one step using highly sensitive and accurate instrument with built in thermostat. Molecular interactions among anti-cancer and pain relieving drugs will be studied using thermo-acoustic method which has not been used in pharmacokinetic studies yet. Different parameters controlling these interactions will be explored Surfactants would also be used which serve as a mimic model for biological membranes which could help to study the activity of drugs within biological system. Obtained information would be helpful in understanding mechanism of pharmacokinetic interactions focusing their clinical implication. Results will prove that thermo-acoustic method could be a promising tool for pharmacokinetic studies and drug formulations too.

IR identification system provided superiority over other system that it us contactless identification and also a number of relevant information could be saved in IR tags that can be read with IR scanner at a distance from the animal. Thus data recording through IR tags would be evaluated and helpful in animal identification for breeding values estimation in progeny testing programs.
