data.projectName: Preventing Violent Extremism in University Students: Moral Disengagement, Empathy, and Self-control in Perspective
data.projectDigest: One of the most important issues faced by Pakistan is violent extremism among young adults. Even highly educated youth have been found to support and justify the use of violence to achieve one’s objectives (known as violent extremism). Although, government is continuously struggling to counter VE which is contributing to political, economic, and social instability of the country, efforts can only be successful when evidence-based interventions are implemented. There is a dire need to identify factors that lead to the development of violent extremist beliefs. The way we justify destructive behavior as being morally acceptable (Moral disengagement), lack of empathy (inability to understand others’ emotions or perspective), and low self-control (inability to control one’s own impulses and reactions) are among predictors for VE. Previously done research suggests that these capacities can be enhanced through educational interventions. data.projectName: Recycling of chicken feather waste via keratinolytic bacteria for the production of nitrogen rich bio-fertilizer/compost
data.projectDigest: Poultry is the second largest industry in the country's agro-economic sector. It generates massive amount of feather waste on daily basis. Since, there is no significant use of this waste, it is either incinerated or land filled without any processing. This practice results in environmental pollution  posing health threats to society.  Poultry feather waste is mainly (>90%) comprised of a protein called as keratin. This protein is structurally tough and resist natural degradation.  However,   an enzyme "keratinase"  produced by some microorganisms can hydrolyze keratin into amino acids.  These keratin degrading microorganisms can  transform poultry feather waste into a nitrogen rich compost which may be applied in the fields to improve soil fertility and to enhance crop yields. Thus, the main objective of this research project is  to recycle poultry feather waste into a cost effective,  farmer friendly biofertilizer using the keratin degrading bacterial strains.

data.projectName: Comparative assessment of Aloe vera growing in various regions of Pakistan for its nutraceutical and industrial potential
data.piUniversity: Kohat University of Science and Technology, Kohat
data.projectDigest: Aloe vera is a succulent plant with highly valued medicinal properties. Aloe vera gel extracted from plant leaves is widely used in various medicines, food and cosmetic products. The "jelly" inside the leaves is famous for its enormous value in food,medicines and  other industries. As a well-known fact, a plant's characteristics vary with varying climatic conditions in various geographical regions. In Pakistan also, growth regions of Aloe vera plant vary in climatic condition and so are the variations in its size, morphology and chemical constituents. Although various reports are there about medicinal and nutraceutical uses of Aloe vera., however, there is no comprehensive data explaining the variety in its constituents and efficacy due to varying climatic conditions so as to exploit the real potential of this plants. This project is therefore aimed on comparative analysis of various aloe vera varieties growing in different geographic regions of Pakistan, using morphological, biochemical and molecular approaches so as to identify the most potent plant growing in specific climatic region so as tos use in nutraceutical and industrial potential. This project is aimed to fulfill the gap in Aloe vera plant investigations covering all the aspects concerned with effect of regional-climatic variations on plant constituents, their efficacy in various biological phenomena for which they are aimed to use in various industries. This study will enable us to identify and provide the real high quality plant to the entrepreneurs and finally to be used in industry for high quality products in various fields.

data.projectName: Role of anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH)  in buffalo reproduction and its future use as bio-marker in breed improvement program
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: There are about 40 million buffaloes present in Pakistan. However, there are certain problems related to this species such as late age of maturity, long calving interval and silent heat, result in reduced reproductive efficiency, calf crop and milk yield on lifetime basis. The profitability of buffalo breeding greatly depends on genetic improvement and hence on the utilization of reproductive biotechnologies. Embryo production is the most efficient tool to enhance the maternal contribution to genetic improvement in this species, allowing greater production of embryos on a long-term basis. Anti-Mullerian hormone is known to play a critical role in folliculogenesis by modulating the follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) function and thereby limiting follicular recruitment. The pattern of expression in the GCs of growing follicles and the role in regulating folliculogenesis and steroidogenesis make AMH an ideal marker for the size of the ovarian follicle pool. Moreover, AMH has been shown to be a reliable endocrine marker of oocyte and embryo quality in humans and other species. However, many aspects still need to be investigated to clarify the role of AMH in influencing follicular growth and oocyte quality in buffalo. The aim of the proposed study is to characterize the population of antral follicles in Nili Ravi buffalo ovaries by determining AMH concentration and its relationship with oocyte quality. So, that at the end we can set an standard cut off value of AMH for selection of buffalo for different assisted reproductive biotechnologies.   Project at the end will be helpful in the selection of the required animals by a single AMH analysis for genetic up gradation in Nili Ravi buffalo breed improvement program.

data.projectName: GREEN COMPOSITES BASED ON BANANA NONWOVEN REINFORCEMENT
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Textile composite based on synthetic fibers are commercially produced and used.  These composite are hazardous for human health during its manufacturing, use and disposal. [1 and 2]
The researchers are looking at the possibilities of manufacturing composites using natural fibers as reinforcement because these composites are cost effective and would be friendly to the environment as compared to their synthetic counterparts. [1, 3 and 4]
The focus of this project is green composites based on banana fibers. Banana plant is grown in Pakistan in abundance especially in the southern region. The banana fiber is obtained from the stem of banana tree. At this moment the banana stem is wasted. [5 and 6]
The outcome of this project is to utilize banana fiber waste and manufacture a useful product. The green composites manufactured during this project will be friendly to the environment during their manufacturing process and disposal. Green composites will certainly replace glass fiber composites in some non-structural applications in the near future.
Green epoxy will be used to manufacture the composite material. The techniques of hand lay-up and compression molding will be utilized. The manufactured composites will be characterized for their mechanical properties and void content.

data.projectName: Promoting Life Skills in School Children: A Feasibility Trial
data.piUniversity: National University of Modern Languages, Islamabad (NUML)
data.projectDigest: Globally, mental health issues are increasing, debilitating, and begin early in life. Early intervention to prevent these concerns in children who are at risk could have long-term impact.  The present study is conceptualized to evaluate the effectiveness of Universal Fun Friends program to enhance life skill, and social-emotional competence of young children. The respective program will be culturally adapted in the context of urban Pakistani community using heuristic framework of cultural adaptation. Methodically, randomized controlled trial will be used for the study and randomization will be done at school level. The major objective of the study is to establish the efficacy of this program in Pakistan (when delivered to a culturally different context) in building resiliency and promoting social-emotional competence which are considered as a prerequisite life skill among school children (4-7 years old). Early intervention is emphasized by the developmental theorist; they considered “early is better” to strengthen the positive factors of life in individuals. It is hypothesized that Fun FRIENDS Program will significantly decrease the inhibited emotional and behavioral concerns in intervention group at posttest as compared to control group. This program will also promote life skills in children who receive intervention. Data will be statistically analyzed. Randomization will take place at school level therefore, data will be nested; multilevel modeling will be used to control the nested nature of data.

data.projectName: A detailed Elucidation of Ligands Structure Requirements for Super Oxide Dismutase Active Complexes of Iron and Manganese and Synthesis of new Ligands
data.projectDigest: Seven-coordinate Mn(II) macrocyclic [Mn(L)(H2O)2]2+ complexes (L = derivatives of  pentaazacyclopentadecane) are the best superoxide dismutase (SOD) mimetics known  to date with catalytic activity which exceeds that of the native mitochondrial MnSOD enzymes. As a key explanation for the remarkable SOD activity, it has been postulated in the literature that the seven-coordinate complex must first adapt to the six-coordinate geometry (upon release of the coordinated water molecule) in order to be efficiently oxidized by superoxide within an inner-sphere catalytic pathway. If it is so, an arising question is: Is the seven-coordinate geometry necessary at all? We have shown that the water release from the seven-coordinate macrocyclic Mn(II) SOD mimetics and formation of the corresponding six-coordinate intermediates is not the rate-limiting step in the overall catalytic superoxide dismutation. Now an opposite question arises: is the six-coordinate intermediate indispensable at all? A direct way to clarify this controversy is to study the reaction with superoxide already starting from six-coordinate complexes, which should be designed to mimic six-coordinate intermediates (providing stable six-coordinate geometry and preserving redox properties of the proven seven-coordinate mimetics) postulated in the catalytic SOD mechanism. These complexes will be detailed investigated in terms of their solution and electrochemical properties, substitution and redox reactivity, in general, and their possible reactivity towards superoxide, in particular.

data.projectName: Quorum quenching: A possible synergistic treatment regime against antibiotic resistant Staphylococcus aureus strains
data.projectDigest: Most of microoganisms contains some micro-molecules, which acts as source of communication between these microoganisms. These are signaling molecules responsible to sense their cell density and also contribute in the regulation of different genes significantly the virulence and antibiotic resistant genes particularly in bacterial pathogens. This mechanism is called as quorum sensing, which is present in most of pathogenic bacteria. One of the antagonistic mechanism is also present in various bacterial species called as quorum quenching. These quorum quenching molecules can inhibit and control the synthesis of these quorum sensing molecules and therefore could be used as strategy to control bacterial pathogenesis including antibiotic resistance. Our project is design to investigate the bacterial isolates with quorum quenching molecules and their application against one of the most antibiotic resistant type of bacteria, which cause several complications in human and other animals i.e. Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus. Initially the effects of Q.Q molecules will be checked directly on MRSA cultures, and some invitro investigations will also be performed. Through gene cloning and expression targeted product will be developed with high yield and finally in vivo study will be conducted to investigate the activity and side effects of desired product in mice models.

data.projectName: Investigating Correlation Between Variants Linked With Milk Production Using Whole Genome and RNA Sequencing Data in Cholistani Cattle
data.projectDigest: According to the best of our knowledge a few studies has focused on correlating variants in genomic data and variants in the transcriptomic data especially in Pakistani cattle breeds no such study exist. The proposed study will focus on investigating the variants associated with milk production in the whole genome/ transcriptomic data and expression levels of the genes in milk somatic cells of 10 Cholistani cattle, which is second highest milk producing cattle breed in Pakistan. The reason for selecting Cholistani cattle breed is that several studies have investigated genetic makeup of Sahiwal cattle and very less work has been done on the Cholistani cattle. For whole genome re-sequencing, five Cholistani cattle with high milk production and five Cholistani cattle with low milk producing will be selected. Transcriptome analysis of the same cattle will be performed by extracting genes from the somatic cells of their milk. The WGS data of high and low milk producing cattle will be analyzed to identify the potential sites associated with milk production. The identified sites will be screened in 100 samples. The proposed study will be a useful tool for further investigation into the cattle genomic studies focusing important growth and production traits.

data.projectName: Biodegradation of pyrethroid (deltamethrin) insecticide using resistant isolates from contaminated environment
data.projectDigest: There is a rapid and uncontrolled increase in pesticides consumption in Pakistan. In recent year, we have used massive amount of Delatmethrin (insecticide) to control mosquitoes/dengue and other. The half life deltamethrin range up to 209days. The excessive amount of deltamethrin accumulates in animals, plants and humans and creates the toxicity. It is needed to degrade the accumulated amount of pesticide. Bio-degradation is the most popular ways to get rid of pesticide. This study is designed to isolate resistant bacteria from contaminated environment and use these resistant bacteria for bio-degradation of deltamethrin

data.projectName: Characterization of Camel breeds, Camel habitat and Camel preferred rangeland species of Balochistan
data.piUniversity: Lasbela University of Agriculture, Water and Marine Sciences, Lasbela
data.projectDigest: Pakistan ranks eighth in world camel population.Of these total heads, Balochistan owns 41 % of that population. Despite of this rich natural wealth of milk and meat, this animal species remained neglected at both national and provincial levels. The traditional usage of this animal is diminishing resulting in lessening of its husbandry practices. If this trend remained on similar footings, future generations will not able to see it in natural landscape of Balochistan.  Conversely, at global level, camel is being termed as “The animal of Future” in view of climate change and Food Security. In Balochistan, camels are found in all ecological zones from zero sea level to 7000 feet. Each camel habitat has different animal characteristics and preferred plant species however, very rare attention has been paid and only fragmental studies with specific to regions can be found. There is dire need and high time to plan a comprehensive study that cover not only camels breeds characteristics, prevailing animal husbandry practices but also its habitat and nutritional assessment of camel preferred plant sources. Keeping these things, this basic research study is proposed to gather comprehensive knowledge on characterization of camel breeds, camel habitat and camel preferred rangeland species of Balochistan. This study will be conducted in three phases which will cover all ecological zones and 90% of major camel zones.  Camel habitat will be  ethnographically surveyed and data on camel breeds characters, husbandry practices,  dairy scoring and body weight will be recorded. Botanical identification and nutritional assessment will be done in laboratories. This study will provide foundation knowledge to conserve camels, camel preferred rangeland species and future use for of this species.

data.projectName: Manufacturing and characterisation of hybrid composites
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Synthetic fibers such as glass fiber in particular, that are used as reinforcement in the manufacturing of composites offer the advantage of superior mechanical and thermal properties of the end product compared to the composites in which natural fibers are used as reinforcement material. The main motivation of this approach is to identify the optimal blending ratios of glass fiber with different natural fibers and to analyse thoroughly how the resulting composite properties are affected.

data.projectName: Characterizing the Nutritional and Therapeutic Potential of Papaya by Using Microencapsulation Technology
data.projectDigest: Current research plan is to propose a food being utilized as a natural remedy instead of medicine to control the hyperlipidemia by adopting microencapsulation technology. Hyperlipidemia is a condition of excess fatty substances called lipids, largely cholesterol and triglycerides, in the blood. Thousands of people from various traditional living styles have resorted to practice medicinal plants and fruits for treatment of their ailments. This might be a result of high cost of the orthodox health care or no faith in it and as a consequence of global shift towards the use of natural products rather than synthetic. Therefore, food commodities having natural medicinal values have currently been given unprecedented care as a possible preventative agent. Microencapsulation is a technique in which active bio components are coated by using extremely small capsules. It is a novel technology that has gained a great attention in food industry. Fully ripe and mature papaya fruit has shelf life of 5-7 days at room temperature. Thus, microencapsulation technique is very useful in retaining potential characteristics of papaya in dried form. Some patients are intolerant and resistant to conventional pharmacotherapy. Thus, alternative approaches are eagerly required. Papaya has received special attention due to its health-promoting properties.

data.projectName: Challenges of global competitiveness and textile sector of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Textile is a major labor-intensive production sector that accounts for more than 50 percent of total export receipts, and in recent years textile sector is losing its competitiveness due to globalization induced increase in international competition. The success of every industry/sector in the highly competitive global trade environment depends on its ability to innovate. Trade diversification provides ingredient required for the invention, innovation, and development. The study is a comprehensive analysis that will explore post-globalization international competitiveness of the Pakistani textile industries with respect to major competing economies by using disaggregated data up to four and six-digit HS level and macroeconomic determinants of competitive advantage. data.projectName: Stochastic Gradient flows on Hilbert Manifold
data.projectDigest: Randomness is one of the phenomenon that exists everywhere. From physics to finance, from global warming to ecological systems, randomness dominates and understanding it to its core is an important endeavor modern mathematics and science. Typically evolution equations (time-dependent differential and partial differential equations) model the nature in a deterministic/predictable fashion, by treating some of the key factors as constants (or non-random), which in reality should be random. Therefore as a result deterministic models provide limited or oversimplified predictions and approximation of the modeled natural phenomenon. A more accurate way to model the nature is to consider the evolution/dynamics of natural phenomenon subject to the random perturbations. Such evolution equations are known as stochastic evolution equations.

data.projectName: heat stress mitigation in tomato
data.projectDigest: Tomato is the major vegetable crop of Pakistan. Tomato provides raw material for culinary uses and processing industry. In the recent years, temperature has significantly increased and prevalence of heat waves in common during summer. Heat stress leads to blossom drop, blossom end rot, pollen abortion and reduced fruit set in tomatoes. Therefore, it is needed to mitigate heat stress induced negative effects on tomato. Heat sensitive and tolerant genotypes will be identified for the growers of the country. The effect of exogenous application of silicon, brassinosteroids, abscisic acid, nitric oxide and proline will be investigated under heat stress conditions to mitigate high temperature induced detrimental influences on tomatoes.

data.projectName: Efficacy of vitamin D supplementation and metformin compared to metformin alone in infertile females with polycystic ovarian syndrome: a randomized open label trial
data.projectDigest: Research indicates that the prevalence of VD deficiency (VDD) with serum concentrations of 25(OH) D <20 ng/ml in women with Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome (PCOS) is about 67-85 per cent which may aggravate symptoms of PCOS leading to anovulation and subfertility. Aim of the study is to evaluate the impact of Oral vitamin D (VD) supplementation on metabolic and endocrine parameters of these females in randomized clinical trial setting of three years with a sample size of 150 females in each group. We will compare : i) change in size of follicles (? 14 mm) and endometrial thickness (?  8 mm), ii) reduction in Insulin Resistance and iii) correction of hyperandrogenism by Trans Vaginal Scan, HOMA -IR and Free Androgen Index respectively in intervention group receiving VD capsules and Metformin with the Metformin alone group. Proven the hypothesis, with an increase in follicular size and endometrial thickness, VD supplementation would be a simple and low-risk add-on to existing therapies (lifestyle intervention, hormonal contraceptives and insulin sensitizers) for infertile females with PCOS to improve conception in spontaneous cycles hence curtailing medical, social, psychological and economic burden of infertility and ensuring healthy lives and promoting wellbeing (Sustainable Development Goals).

data.projectName: Optimization of welding process for Aluminum (Al-6061-T6) using modern welding techniques and numerical simulations
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Aluminum 6061 is one of the important alloys of aluminum that is used in industries of strategic importance such as spacecraft, shipbuilding, automotive, etc.  This alloy usually comes in T6 Tempered condition, as a result, the conventional techniques such as Gas Tungsten Arc (GTA) Welding and Gas Metal Arc (GMA) Welding end up in significantly reducing the strength of weld joints. Modern welding techniques such as Friction Stir Welding (FSW) welds materials without melting using mechanical forces, Laser welding uses high power narrow laser beam, to melt a narrow area in material and Hybrid welding uses combination of two or more processes are modern methods of welding that can help in optimizing the welding process of Al-6061-T6 alloy . Nano technology would also be incorporated to strengthen the weld.  In the present study the above techniques would be used to optimize the welding process of Al-6061-T6 alloy with the help of experiments and flow simulations.  
The principal investigator has an honor of working on above processes in Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST) , ranked 41st in the world, on full scholarship from KAIST. Best paper award is also given to his work on Hybrid welding.

data.projectName: Development of Multi-Function Opto-Trainer (MOFT) to Realize Optical Communication Lab.
data.projectDigest:
The increased demand in term of bandwidth and data rates by an ever increasing telecom services presents an exciting challenge to communication technology. One of the most significant technological developments of the last decade that promises to play a key role in realizing these challenges is Photonics and Optical Communications. The project aims to develop a Multi-Function OPTO-Trainer (MFOT) to augment Optical Communication training to Engineering students, obviating the needs of having expensive Optical Communication system. Having such a Trainer will also mean that a large number of experiments regarding Transmitter, Receiver and Optical Fiber can be performed by students in the laboratory. The trainer will bridge the gap between academia and industry by providing a platform for product based solutions to the challenges faced by the future photonics and Optical Communication Systems.
The capabilities requirements of the Multi-Function OPTO-Trainer are summarized below:
1.	Multi-Function Opto-Trainer (MFOT) shall capable of to investigate the characteristics of LED and LASER diode at Transmitter.
2.	Multi-Function Opto-Trainer (MFOT) shall capable of to determine the response of PIN and Photo Diode at Receiver.
3.	Multi-Function Opto-Trainer (MFOT)  shall capable of to determine the response of Transmitter parameters like launch power , Pulse width and beam width on transmission characteristic of optical fiber Link .
4.	Multi-Function Opto-Trainer (MFOT) shall capable of to determine Optical Signal to Noise Ratio OSNR of transmitting Optical Signal.
5.	Multi-Function Opto-Trainer (MFOT) shall capable of to determine the response of Received Optical Power, Receiver Sensitivity and Bit Error Rate BER at receiver.

data.projectName: Experimental and Simulation Study of Magnetic Nanoparticles for Potential Application in Hyperthermia Treatment of Cancer
data.piUniversity: Kohat University of Science and Technology, Kohat
data.projectDigest: Cancer has become one of the leading causes of death in developing countries like Pakistan. Currently, there are approximately 1.4 million cancer patients in Pakistan. Annual death rate stands at 80,000, of which, 40,000 are due to breast cancer alone. There are 26 hospitals throughout the country with cancer treatment facilities. Most notable of these are the Shaukat Khanum chain in private sector, and Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission (PAEC) sponsored hospitals in public sector. High costs have driven oncologists and governments to devise novel technologies for effective cancer treatment. Recently, hyper-thermia treatment through MNPs has shown great promise for cancer treatment. The treatment makes use of magnetic MNPs that can be activated to produce appropriate amount of heat (42-48 °C) with the help of externally applied magnetic fields. In this treatment, cancerous cells are exposed to high temperatures suitable for damaging or killing them. The benefit of the approach is that there is minimum or no injury to normal cells. In this project, bio-compatible and bio-degradable MNPs will be prepared by chemical and physical methods and then will be characterized for structural and magnetic properties especially for heating efficiency to be used in magnetic hyperthermia treatment of cancer.

data.projectName: Implementing Genre-Based Pedagogy in Pakistan:  An approach towards literacy education through Reading-to-Learn
data.projectDigest: This project aims at developing effective ways through the genre-based pedagogy to ensure that all the students in schooling help themselves learn both reading and the writing skills required for any particular proficiency level. Academically, English literacy curriculum in Pakistan has not experienced any significant changes for many years. Since the present government is keen to implement a revised school education policy 2021 to achieve the targeted competences, therefore, this project will help designing curriculum based on the genre-based pedagogy. The referred policy under the Punjab Government is being designed to promote collaboration, critical thinking and creativity which will help to build a community of reflective citizens. The students will be enabled to contribute towards knowledge based economy through participatory citizenship. This means that there is growing interest as well as support from both society and the government to implement a revised pedagogy. So, as part of the government efforts to support English literacy in Pakistan, the project has capacity to pioneer the approach required in the 21st century, and offers the scope to embed literacy practices in which teachers across subjects can work together to design syllabi for teaching, and implement the genre-based pedagogy across subject areas.

data.projectName: Exploration of fungal biodiversity along Northern route of CPEC, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Fungi make integral part of biodiversity in the forests and are ecologically very important as recyclers, mycorrhizae and as host plant parasites .Different groups of macrofungi may include tooth fungi, non-gilled and gilled fungi which may be edible, poisonous, medicinal, fleshy or non-fleshy in texture. These mushrooms have been considered a rich source of trace minerals, vitamins, water contents, proteins, carbohydrates and fibers with low fats and Lichens are found worldwide mainly grow on tree bark, rocks and walls etc. plays  important role in making the environment free from pollution.Rust fungi are the largest group of plant disease fungi and a few crops seriously affected by rust disease include wheat, sugar, soybeans, coffee, ornamental flowers, fruit trees, and forest trees.The fungal  biodiversity along the Northern route of CPEC is facing the  major threat due to construction  of roads by clearing the forests. At present, research characterizing the fungi in Pakistan is based almost exclusively on morphology. No modern techniques such as DNA sequencing or observation with a SEM have been introduced into Pakistan. Such techniques are needed for the correct identification of  fungi at the species level. In this project, micro-macroscopic and molecular methods will be used to get a perception of the taxonomy, phylogeny and diversity of fungal flora in above said area of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Expression and characterization studies of commercially important hydrolases from a thermoduric alkalotolerant Bacillus clausii KP10
data.projectDigest: Enzymes are proteinaceous biocatalysts and have gained special interest in the field of research and development owing to their world-wide industrial applications. Bacteria due to ease of handling and low cost production are considered best for production of enzymes.  Hydrolases based on commercial applications (>2/3rd shares in global market) is most significant & are used in dishwashing and laundry detergents (proteases, lipases), brewing (glucanases), biofuels (lipases), improving food/feed and paper quality (cellulases, mannanases) etc. The major industries in Pakistan spend millions (dollars) on export of these enzymes. Harsh conditions of industrial processes emphasizes the need of exploration & application of extremozymic analogues from different strains specifically extremophiles. Previously, we reported an alkalo-thermotolerant Bacillus clausii KP10 strain from hot springs of Tatta Pani, Azad Kashmir. This strain has been studied for catalase and alkaline protease (industrially important enzymes) in vitro and in silico, respectively. Few reports from Pakistan describes production of industrially important extremozymes. There is need to produce these enzymes locally to reduce import costs for country’s sustainable economy. Present project will therefore focus on screening of hydrolases like proteases, ?-mannanases, ?-glucanases and lipases from B. Clausii KP10 strain (selective hydrolases based on extensive literature survey) and each enzyme’s native enzymatic activity will be assessed at optimum growth conditions of the bacteria. Genes of each enzyme will be isolated, cloned, sequenced, analysed, expressed in host cells for purification. Characterization, applicability & stability studies will be done  towards harsh industrial environments.

data.projectName: Development of Diagnostic Tool for Efficient Prognosis of Sustained Virological Response Among HCV Treated Responded Patients in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
data.projectDigest: Hepatitis C Virus is the causative agent for  liver disease. Chronic hepatitis C may lead to  liver cancer and failure.   Although drugs that are more effective have been approved for treatment of HCV yet some may not clear HCV from immune cells that can act as reservoirs for recurrence of HCV after treatment. The first objective of this study is to investigate the presence of HCV proteins in Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells (PBMCs) and their association with sustained virological response or relapse in treated responded patients.  Other objectives of this project are to establish a center where the facility of viral proteins detection in immune cells will be offered for public and is to establish permanent source of income for university that will decrease the financial burden of the institution as well as the students and also to train the human resource in the field. Blood samples from anti-HCV treated responded patients of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa will be selected. PBMCs will be separated using  Ficoll histopaque.  PBMCs will be stained by Indirect Immunofluorescence Assay using immunofluorescence microscope. This study will help to predict HCV SVR or relapse after successful completion of anti-viral therapy in the people of this region. Therefore, our study will provide diagnosis at low cost with high standard to poor and common people of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The researchers especially students will get training from this study. Excellence publication will be published. This study will give positive effect on the innovation output of our university and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa region. M.Phil and Ph. D research students will complete their Thesis, such students will get training to give their serves in Pakistani universities. The project will  effect on research.

data.projectName: Return to 4-year university education in Pakistan: Role of quality Education
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
In Pakistan, colleges and universities vary substantially in terms of both ‘quantity’ and ‘quality’ of education. In such circumstances, estimating return to education based on ‘quantity’ alone can be misleading. This study aims to explore the relationship between quality of higher education and return to education (4-year university education). 
There are several concerns which motivate us to explore this relationship in Pakistan. First, decisions related to individual human capital investment and efficient resource allocation can be informed through precise assessments of private return to 4-year university education. Policy makers cannot ignore the substantial variation in quality of education. This study will provide unbiased information to policy makers in this regard. Secondly, in recent past, Pakistan has witnessed a rapid expansion of higher education and there is a concern that we may produce over-educated population (Freedman, 1976). Thirdly, according to Card & Krueger, (1996), labor market is a natural yardstick to measure the effectiveness of higher education expansion because return to education provides the response of labor market in this regard. Thus, exploring the relationship between quality education and earnings may provide the useful insight about the recent higher education expansion in Pakistan and to what extent demand matches supply in labor market of Pakistan. Policy maker would utilize this information for effective and efficient allocation of scarce educational resources.

data.projectName: Converting sunlight into syngas, a potential energy storage medium for a sustainable future
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest:
The main objective of this project is to develop cost-efficient and scalable production pathways from SUNLIGHT to energy storage compounds that provide flexibility, convenience of use and the potential for unlimited storage. To achieve this objective and enable cost reduction, sustainability, resource efficiency, project will adopt an approach involving materials design (covering both theoretical and experimental approaches) to achieve improved light harvesting and charge separation from a catalyst material; novel reactor design concepts consisting of (a) a photo-electrochemical reactor for water splitting, (b) a photo-electrochemical reactor to reduce CO2 to CO.  This project will significantly contribute to the reduction of greenhouse gases (GHG) emitted from industrial processes by developing a novel and disruptive technology for the conversion of CO2 and water to syngas (CO and H2), this syngas will act as the basic building blocks for chemical and fuel production applications, particularly as significant market, commercial, and regulatory developments worldwide are happening. It can contribute in ultra-clean, renewable, ultra-low emission fuel for a variety of applications. 
This project will further help in portraying Pakistan’s image in rest of the world as a potential developing country who is starting to play its role for environmental mitigation despite being their limited resources.

data.projectName: Biochar from food waste as a key carbon dioxide removal approach and its application for municipal solid waste composting- a greener transformation
data.projectDigest: Biochar amendments to soil fertility is proven but its effectiveness towards adsorption of carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere as mitigation tool against climate change have not been evaluated yet. Global climate change is mainly because of increasing concentration of CO2 in the atmosphere and known as potent greenhouse gas (GHG). To remove CO2 direct from the air can actually reduce the global atmospheric CO2 concentration. Worldwide, various techniques have been developed to convert bio-waste into energy through incineration but as such food waste based biochar has never been applied for the removal of CO2 from the air. Therefore a one year project has been designed to investigate the potentials of biochar derived from food waste for  adsorption of CO2 emissions as well as determined its role in additional experiment for degradation of organic material of municipal solid waste of  the landfill. It is hoped that degradation through biochar would be considered an environmental friendly treatment relative to incineration.

data.projectName: Development of commercializable NS3 and NS5 modulators from onion and papaya peels by using green extraction technology to control the dengue fever
data.projectDigest: The current research proposal insinuates to the field of biotechnology for drug development in the area of dengue virus biology. The dengue virus nonstructural protein 3 (NS3) and nonstructural protein 5 (NS5) bear multiple enzymatic activities and represent attractive targets for antiviral therapeutic intervention. NS5 has a methyltransferase domain and RNA-dependent RNA polymerase while NS3 contains the viral serine protease and RTPase, and helicase activities. These activities are essential for viral replication, virion assembly and defense of virus against host immune system. We aim to exploit these newly discovered mechanism believed to be critical for the parasitic survival by testing our established libraries that might have potential to block these mechanisms. We will apply our currently established enzymatic assay based screening approach to screen novel inhibitors of NS3 & NS5 and demonstrate their therapeutic value for treatment of dengue. This offers the potential for development of new therapies to treat this disease. We anticipate that target-based screen will support new unbiased approaches to support the identification and characterization of novel drug candidates and drug combinations that counteract drug resistance and have maximal clinical efficacy. If this project goes successful, it will surely serve as cheapest way to cure dengue fever.

data.projectName: Development of Seismic Site Amplification Factors for Islamabad Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest:
Seismic site amplification factors (AFs) are used to define the seismic demand in terms of design response spectrum for the dynamic analysis of building structures. Current seismic provisions in Building Code of Pakistan (SP, BCP, 2007) , seismic site classifications and corresponding AFs were adopted from UBC (1997). The UBC (1997) seismic site AFs were developed after the recorded Loma Prieta (1989) earthquake in deep sites of Western US.  Site amplification is the function of local site profiles . Site explorations of Islamabad has shown shallow bed rock conditions. The site amplification characteristics  of shallow sites are predominantly dependent on short period response,  therefore the use of deep sites based developed AFs to shallow sites may underestimate response at shorter period and overestimate at longer period. 
The findings of the study can provide an insight about potential implications of current code-based AFs for the shallow sites of Islamabad. The deliverable outputs of the project (PDB, SRA and shake maps) can improve the current state of earthquake engineering practice in Pakistan. These can enable the practicing design engineers to estimate the realistic seismic demand to be defined for the dynamic analysis of building structures. The conclusions of project can also highlight the need to improve the seismic amplification factors of SP-BCP (2007) for Pakistan.

data.projectName: Voice Controlled Surveillance Drone
data.projectDigest:
Drone technology is not only used as a playing device for kids, rather it is now playing a vital role in capturing real time video of events from a suitable distance. The aim of this project is to control the drone through voice commands (eliminating the requirement of drone flying expertise) for the purpose of recording live videos of a user-defined route (through GPS coordination of latitude and longitude), while streaming and/or saving video on real-time. This will improve the monitoring of counter-terrorism devices, eliminate requirement of trained manpower to control the drone, using simplified access through a smart phone application. A smart phone will be used to set the route/radius, monitor the location through GPS signals and assign tasks through voice commands to control takeoff and land. 
The surveillance system will become invulnerable via this project. This can be used by media groups; to record political gatherings, advertisement agencies; to capture attractive and eye catching views from a significant height, photographers; to shoot events like wedding ceremonies and birthday parties being held on a roofless platform, Counter Terrorism; The Police will be able to monitor suspicious activities during Holy gatherings etc., and other crowded events which requires invincibleness security.

data.projectName: Study on Inferences and Applications of The Exponential-G Family of Distributions
data.projectDigest: In the earlier research a new generator of the continuous distributions named Exponential-G (Ex-G) family of distributions is developed. Various Statistical and mathematical properties have been derived of the proposed Ex-G generator. Then we develop new class of distributions using this generator and derive the various properties of the new class of distributions. Reliability measures, Entropy, explicit expression of the moments, quantile, mode of the new class of distributions have been derived. The parameters of the new class of distributions are estimated by maximum likelihood estimation (MLE). To assess the behavior of the estimates derived by MLE from each newly developed class of distributions, small experiments carried out for each based-on simulation study. To prove empirically the potential of the new class by means of real data sets. We compare the proposed class of distributions with some related distributions using AIC, BIC, CAIC and KS. Finally, the class of distributions found to be best fitted on real lifetime data and it is recommended that this newly developed class of distributions can be used for real life data sets specially for the positive skewed data sets and lifetime data sets.

data.projectName: IMPACT OF TYPHOID CONJUGATED VACCINE (TCV) ON SENSITIVITY PATTERN OF SALMONELLA TYPHI AND TYPHOID BURDEN IN PAKIS
data.projectDigest:
Extensive Drug Resistant Typhoid, being the major health concern and alarming health danger to global world these days, is the burning issue of today’s world. Unfortunately Pakistan is among those countries which faces epidemics of Extensive Drug Resistance typhoid fever and lost many lives in recent past.
Pakistan experienced the first outbreak of extensive drug resistant (XDR) typhoid fever in the Hyderabad district of Sindh province, in November 2016. 
From November 1, 2016 to Oct 20, 2019 total of 16,926 Typhoid Fever cases were reported from different districts of Sindh province. Out of these 11,762 were found as Extensive Drug Resistant Typhoid cases. The Drug Resistant cases are mostly reported from Karachi and District Hyderabad. A total of 12045 lab confirmed Typhoid cases were reported from ten hospitals of Karachi. Out of these 7853 were recorded as Extensive Drug Resistant (XDR) Typhoid Fever cases from January 1, 2017 to October 20th, 2019. In the week 42 of 2019, total 111 new XDR/MDR Typhoid Fever cases were reported from different hospitals in Karachi. 
From November 2016 to October 20, 2019, a total of 4881 Typhoid cases were reported at the PDSRU Hyderabad from different districts of Sindh province excluding Karachi. Out of these 3,909 are Extensive Drug Resistant (XDR) cases. Among all reported XDR cases, 2814 (72 %) were from District Hyderabad only.
Due to the possible resistant behavior of Salmonella Typhi and its immunological properties against various antibiotics WHO recommended new vaccination known as Typhoid Conjugate vaccine. Mass campaign derive has been launched at Sindh Province in Nov-Dec 2019. Pakistan is the first country which included TCV in its routine EPI schedule.

data.projectName: Transcriptomic alteration and tissue damaging assessment of endocrine disruptor bisphenol A analogues exposure as potent hazard for male and female reproductive organs
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Bisphenol A (BPA) is an industrial chemical and a building block for polycarbonate plastic and epoxy resins. BPA, and its derivatives are found in many everyday products such as the lining of metal food and drink cans, plastic baby bottles, pacifiers and baby toys, dental sealants, computers, cell phones, hard plastic water bottles, paints, adhesives, enamels, varnishes, CDs and DVDs, and certain microwavable or reusable food and drink containers. These compounds have been shown to leach into food and water from containers - particularly after heating or as plastic ages - and from dental sealants. Because of the toxicological effects of BPA, Canada, European Union and some other countries totally banned the use of BPA in daily use products and their packages. The ban and removal of BPA led the way to the introduction of other BPA alternatives like Bisphenol P, Bisphenol AP, Bisphenol AF into the plastic and thermal paper industry. These alternatives are considered safer than BPA but still there are questions over the safety of BPA analogs such as Bisphenol P, Bisphenol AP, Bisphenol AF. In such background current research project has been planned to see the transcriptomic and histomorphological effects of endocrine disruptor bisphenol A analogues on testicular and ovarian tissues.

data.projectName: DEVELOPMENT OF STRUCTURAL HEALTH MONITORING SYSTEM FOR FIBER REINFORCED POLYMER (FRP) COMPOSITE STRUCTURES
data.projectDigest:
The use of composites in the structures such as buildings, bridges, wind turbines, stadiums, automotive, aerospace, marine and defence industries has increased significantly in recent years due to its high strength/weight ratio. However, composites are prone to damages, sometime invisible, therefore, it is crucial to monitor their structural integrity by adopting sophisticated Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) techniques.
SHM is a process of implementing a damage detection mechanism for composite structures. The basis of SHM is the application of sensors on a structure, combined with minimum manual intervention to monitor the changes in material and/or geometric properties of a structure. The traditional SHM systems works when the composite structures are not in operation.
The proposed project aims to develop a novel, cost effective and efficient fibre-sensors based SHM system for the health monitoring of composites, that will provide instantaneous information about change in strains based on changes in resistance of sensors embedded in composites in real-time when in operation to identify the risk of damage propagation and catastrophic failures. To achieve this goal, the following objectives will be achieved.
1.	To develop and characterise fibre-based sensors for SHM system 
2.	To incorporates sensors into composites and to develop data collection and analysis system for SHM to process the data into desired information.
The outcomes of this research activity will mainly benefit the aircraft, war-ships, submarines, satellites, defence equipment and projectiles, wind turbines, bridges, buildings, stadiums & automotive structures industry of Pakistan to avoid expensive and catastrophic failures.

data.projectName: Design and mixed method evaluation of a personalized identification temporary sticker for smart children immunization system
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Mortality rate in Pakistan for infants and kids under the age of five is among the highest in the world. Lack of properly administered vaccinations presents significant perils to the realization of goals set by incumbent government. The project proposes a cost effective commercially scalable  smart e-registry system to link vaccinated child ID to a central system for monitoring and immunization record keeping of that child. At the heart of this technology lies the barrier that common biometric identifiers such as finger prints, retina scans, foot scans, ear patterns have very low accuracies for infants (0-8 weeks of life). The technology and healthcare team at NED University and Aga Khan University have already successfully implemented digital healthcare projects such as GCRF. The idea is to design an ecosystem for printing personalized micro QR codes on temporary stickers to be used as imprints for supplementary immunization campaign. Additionally, an IoT based scanning strategy with novel error correction coding allows the readability to last several days on an infants’ skin or nail.  This proposal is evaluation and proposal where we are requesting to move forward to integrate these technologies into a locally contextualized eco-system, and perform field trials of the integrated system for cultural and cognitive validation and to develop an e-registry system that affords live and interactive visualization of the current and previous nationwide immunization campaign.

data.projectName: Molecular epidemiology of fish viruses in Pakistan and their caused immune response: Step toward fish disease control
data.projectDigest: Fish industry in Pakistan has grown rapidly during last two decades with an annual production of 575,000 metric tons from captive and cultured fish only in 2018-2019. In order to increase the production to meet demand of food supply, fish are cultured in dense populations which predispose fish to several different pathogens that can represent a continuous threat to the aquaculture industry of Pakistan. Fish pathogens including viruses causes devasting loss to the aquaculture industry. However, our understanding of the viral diversity in aquatic animals remains far from complete. Up to date, a portion of viral diversity and their virulence has been explored which includes several RNA and DNA viruses from different aquatic animals but to date there is no any data regarding aquatic viruses from Pakistan. Although, Pakistan has a great diversity of fish species like Perciforms, Cyprinipforms, Siluiriforms and Salmoniforms including several carp species, tilapia, catfish and several unexplored species with some exotic species (trout). The proposed project for the first time in Pakistan aimed to collect data on the ecology, pathogenicity, distribution and diversity of fish viruses in Pakistan and influence of virus-host interactions on mortality and evolution of fish pathogen communities to conserve our native resources.

data.projectName: Oil Spill Detection and Risk Assessment using Satellite Remote Sensing along Gwadar Coast, Balochistan
data.projectDigest: International trade, predominantly the transportation of petroleum products primarily accomplished by maritime transportation. Oil is being transported using ships on frequent basis. Oil spill events reported due to ship accidents, installations of industrial plants on shores, pipeline ruptures and illegal operations including onshore cleaning and washing of tank. Literature states that around 380 million gallons of oil is being discharged in the ocean environment on annual basis. Oil is being discharged into the marine environment annually due to various reasons. Massive oil spread in the marine environment causes intense risks for marine habitat and effects costal environment badly. Sources of marine oil pollution can be categorized into four groups including transportation, natural seabed seepage, consumption and extraction of petroleum products. Oil pollution sources can be found both on the land and on the ocean as well. This study deals with various aspects of oil spill detection using Satellite Remote Sensing (SRS) techniques. Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery data will be utilized for oil spill detection and source identification over selected sites in the ocean and coastal areas of Gwadar, Balochistan. The impact assessment of oil spill on coastal environment due to China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) will also be analyzed.

data.projectName: Semi-Quantitative Environmental Impact Assessment of Textile Sector of Pakistan: An application of Folchi method
data.projectDigest:
The sustainable environment plays an instrumental role for the sustainable growth of the textile sector which is the leading export sector of Pakistan. The effectual assessment and management of the environmental problems are mandatory for sustainable development however, in reality, the textile sector fails to identify and assess the environmental problems. This research-intensive work would focus to investigate the current environmental protection practices and evaluate the sustainable environmental technologies. As Pakistan has very low technological support and skilled hands, it would be supportive to identify the major gap of the sustainable environmental practices in the textile sector and provide the substantial solution of the environmental issues which have the negative impacts on the external as well as internal environment of the textile industry.

 

In this research project, a comprehensive framework of Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA)
would be designated to investigate the effects of environmental issues and pollutants on the sustainable environment of the textile sector of Pakistan. This framework will help to evaluate and manage the uncertain and unpredictable risks arise from different wastes in textile processes at different stages. This study implies the methodology of Folchi to implement the identification and eradication of environmental issues and pollutants so that the environment-friendly textile manufacturing processes would be applicable persistently. It would be advantageous for the professional textile managers and society to evaluate, identify and predict the potential socio-environmental hazards for the attainment of productive and constructive outcomes in the textile sector.

data.projectName: DECIPHERING THE IMMUNOINFORMATICS APPROACH TO DESIGN SUBUNIT VACCINE FROM FOOT AND MOUTH DISEASE VIRUS PREVALENT SEROTYPES IN PAKISTAN AND ITS EVALUATION IN BOVINES
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Among infectious diseases Foot and Mouth disease (FMD) has been major threat to Livestock population and their products worldwide. FMD is economically devastating, highly contagious trans-boundary viral disease. The disease causes massive economic losses in dairy animals that are measured in terms of high mortality and morbidity, loss of milk production, working efficiency, quality of hide and weight gain, abortions, cost of treatment and consternation to the farmers. Up till now, no broad spectrum vaccine is available that can protect animals from all serotypes. Hence, it is need of the day to develop a vaccine that protects animals from heterologous strain challenges. In this project, we will use immunoinformatics approach to design sub-unit vaccine by linking T and B cell epitopes. For this purpose, first we will collect the conservative epitopes for both structural and non-structural proteins of aphtho virus serotypes; O, A and Asia-1 which are prevalent in Pakistan. The vaccine will be produced by using bicistronic AAV-Dj/helper virus system. Hence, our study will not only determine the potency and efficacy of our designed vaccine but also its T- cell memory response will be compared with already in-use field vaccine. Thus, this new techniques will equip our country to design and produce its own epitope based vaccines that will provide cross protective immunity against 3 field strains of FMDV in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Strategies to improve water use efficiency for enhanced productivity of tomato and cucumber in southern Punjab climatic conditions.
data.projectDigest: Fresh water availability is continuously declining in Pakistan. Vegetables like tomato and cucumber being highly perishable in nature require regular irrigation for their proper growth. Current project aims to train vegetable growers of four districts viz. Vehari, Pakpattan, Sahiwal and Toba Tek Singh (especially tunnel farmers) about different strategies to enhance water productivity of cucumber and tomato for their quality production even under limited water supply. Main emphasis will be on some advanced yet cheap modifications of furrow irrigation systems along with use of drought tolerant varieties and different types of mulch. For farmers with drip irrigation system, a comprehensive field study will be carried out at UAF Sub-campus Burewala on irrigation interval and irrigation amount. Results of the experiment will be disseminated among farming community in easy and understandable language. For effective results dispersal, twelve field days in four districts of Punjab along with a seminar at UAF Sub-campus Burewala will be organized. Information in printed form (as booklets and brochures) will be provided to the farming community apart from practical demonstration of the techniques. To play significant role in national and international research, findings of the project will also be published in International Journal.

data.projectName: Identification of Optimum Strategies for Processing Coal Resources of Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Physical coal processing techniques are employed worldwide to improve coal quality and meet the specific requirements of end-users by reducing the impurities in coal to certain levels. Currently, China is leading the coal processing industry with over 2000 processing plants followed by USA (268), Australia (unknown), Russia (66), South Africa (60) and India (53). Unfortunately, there is not a single state-of-the-art coal preparation plant in operation in Pakistan. The major reasons for this deficiency are the lack of systematic research and the proper coal preparation study on coal resources of Pakistan. 
A typical approach to design a coal processing plant involves the following steps: (1) characterization of feed coal properties to establish particle distributions for size, density, and floatability; (2) simulation to predict clean coal yield and quality; and (3) selection of an acceptable flowsheet. 
In this research, firstly gross samples will be collected from developed coalfields of Baluchistan, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (KPK), Gilgit-Baltistan, and Sindh (The proposed work is already done on Punjab coalfield by the principle investigator). Then, sub samples will be prepared and characterized for establishing particle distribution data of size, density and floatability. Lastly, several circuit configurations will be designed and simulated by using LIMN software to identify optimum strategy for processing coal of each developed coalfield.

data.projectName: Assessing Employability Skills: Employers and Students Perception
data.projectDigest:
This proposed study attempts to identify the employability skills that are most valued by employers in Peshawar. Because employability skills are an important set of skills which help graduates gain and maintain employment. Graduates complain that they can’t find jobs, and that jobs in the country are given on nepotism, references, or corruption. However, industry experts point to a lack of employability skills.
There is no study available on the level of employability skills in the students and graduates in Peshawar. This is why this study is proposed to first identify the most valued employability skills by employers, and then measure the perception of employers about the quality of employability skills in graduates, and also the perception of the graduates about the quality/level of their own employability skills.
This study would help identify the discord between what employers want and what the graduates offer.

data.projectName: Investor Protection in Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) after Demutualization and CPEC: Challenges and A Way forward for Policy Makers
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
After the financial crisis occurred in 2007-08, market dynamics have been shifted from internationalization to the regional connectivity, alliance and integration. This results to decrease in hitches to capital flows in regional exchanges. At present, investors can now access foreign capital markets more easily as geographical boundaries have been rendered meaningless and un-influential which nourish the notions of cross-listing and depository certificates. Earlier studies have documented numerous fruitful economic outcomes of cross-listing such as reduction of cost of capital (Bris, Cantale, Hrnji?, & Nishiotis, 2015), extension of stockholder base (Karolyi, 2017), provision of higher liquidity as well as diversified pool of investment (Peng & Su, 2014), and enhancement of firms’ visibility and exposure to participants of local and international investors.
Every market is influenced due to the global markets and the surge of foreign investment may have the positive impact on the economy. This proposed research will examine the movements of PSX with global and regional markets and then investigate its convergence towards regional market. Regarding the movement of stock market, behavior of investors has its own importance and this study will explore the investor behavior after the demutualization and CPEC whether they want to make investment or their behavior is shaky. These results will be compared with the market movements and identify the investors illusion towards their proposed investment. This study benefits the society at large as investors will know that whether increase in market will be as a result of connectivity of one market to other or it is just a boom through which market may increase.

data.projectName: Synthesis, Fabrication and Performance Evaluation of nano-filtration membranes to remove Perfluoroalkyl substances  for water purification
data.projectDigest:
Perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are the  pollutants present in the ground water due to increasing urbanization and industrialization. The PFAS are persistent in nature and can live in human body for years, however, their presence in body can create cancer cells in the human body.
These PFAS can be filtered out by membrane filtration technology, however, the pore size of membranes need to be carefully controlled. In this study, layer of polyamide would be created on the base membrane to tailor the pore structure of the selective top layer. This membrane have the potential to efficiently remove PFAS from ground water.

data.projectName: Workplace Harassment in the US and Pakistan: A rhetorical investigation
data.projectDigest: The study proposes to analyze the rhetoric of the female University employees in two countries, the US and Pakistan, regarding the workplace harassment, with the application of rhetorical tools from the antiquity, mainly, logos ethos and pathos. This will be done to understand how these women construct the reality of the phenomenon of workplace harassment in terms of coping with it. Accordingly, the similarities and differences between the US and Pakistani women in their treatment of the workplace harassment will be identified which may significantly be useful for the Pakistani women workforce. For example, the rhetoric of the US women regarding their treatment of workplace harassment may lead the Pakistani women to learn the effective treatment of harassment at their workplaces, particularly, with regard to the options available to them, other than the law, to effectively deal with the situation of workplace harassment.  This will also cover the gap created because of the ineffective implementation of the legislations to control the workplace harassment in Pakistan. Moreover, it is believed that the proposed study will be taken in a positive spirit in the US. This is not only because workplace harassment is a world-wide known problem which needs attention and resolution in both the US and Pakistan, but also because it has important implications for Pakistani women workforce. Therefore, the comparative nature of the proposed study will be extremely useful and provides the justification for the need of pursuing it in the context of the US and Pakistan. Last but not least, the proposed research will also be particularly valuable for the development of literature regarding workplace harassment in the fields of HRM, OB, associated business studies and rhetoric.

This will also cover the gap created because of the ineffective implementation of the legislations to control the workplace harassment in Pakistan. Moreover, it is believed that the proposed study will be taken in a positive spirit in the US. This is not only because workplace harassment is a world-wide known problem which needs attention and resolution in both the US and Pakistan, but also because it has important implications for Pakistani women workforce. Therefore, the comparative nature of the proposed study will be extremely useful and provides the justification for the need of pursuing it in the context of the US and Pakistan. Last but not least, the proposed research will also be particularly valuable for the development of literature regarding workplace harassment in the fields of HRM, OB, associated business studies and rhetoric.

data.projectName: Evaluation and optimization of fusion proteins for the control of insect pests
data.projectDigest: The insect pests especially phloem feeders are the greatest threat to the agriculture as they feed on phloem sap and cause nutritional deficiency to the plants. They are also potent vectors for more than two hundred viruses which also cause a lot of economic losses to the country agriculture. It is needed to find out new and effective strategies to cope with such agricultural challenges. Different strategies have already adopted including synthetic pesticides and bio-pesticides. Bt proteins are being used in the since two decades. The drawback is, due to overexpression of toxin in the field insects have developed resistance against these toxins over period of time. It is necessary to define some new strategy to develop resistance in plants against insect pests. This project is focused on to study and develop some new combinations of toxin proteins by combining two or more different proteins to kill insects. For this purpose plant lectins have been chosen. As, lectins are being produced by all kingdom of life so they are considered biologically safe to use against insect pests due to their insecticidal activity. Different combinations of proteins will be constructed and analyzed for their structural and functional modifications for data available in database. The best combination/combinations (structurally most stable) will be used for transient gene expression in a model plant system Nicotiana tabacum. Inoculated plants will then be studied for gene expression by using different molecular biology techniques and confirmed by insect bioassays.

data.projectName: Climate Extremes Projections and their Spatio-temporal Trend Analysis  in the Homogeneous Climatic Zones by using High Resolution Statistically Downscaled Climate Data
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
The project will explore about climate extremes in the homogeneous climate zone and further investigate the impacts of these extreme on various key areas which has significant role in the Gross Domestic Products (GDP) of the country including water resources, agriculture and energy etc. The project has an integrated approach and will achieve the following major objectives:

1.	Developing homogeneous climatic zones for Pakistan using the combination of statistical methods, cluster analysis and L-moment approaches.  
2.	Selection of set of best possible GCMs which Project the observed climatology better tan the other competing models. The total number of GCMs will be used in this Project are 14 or more.  
3.	Climate risk and vulnerability assessment in the homogeneous climatic regions (objective 1) for the selected GCM (objective 2).
4.	Spatio-temporal trend analysis of the projected climate extremes and their impacts on water resources, agriculture, energy and health in all developed homogeneous climate zones.

data.projectName: Bio-fertilizer: Field Evaluation and Selection of Rhizobacterial Inoculants for the Enhancement of Wheat Production under Abiotic Stress
data.piUniversity: Balochistan University of Information Technology, Engineering and Management Sciences,Quetta
data.projectDigest: The total geographical area of Pakistan is 79.6 million hectares (mha), of which only 25% or 19.82 million hectares are currently under cultivation. Pakistan falls into arid and semi-arid climatic conditions. These lands constitute about 88% of the country's total geographic area of 79.6 million hectare (mha). Agrarian based economy of Pakistan depends on the supply of water through the world’s largest system of irrigation. However, rapid increase in population and industrial development has placed immense pressure on water resources of the country. During the last decade, global warming has also affected Pakistan and the most important consequence is the rise in temperature that resulted in drought in most parts of the country. Pakistan has limited surface and groundwater resources. In our country, annual water availability per capita has been reduced from 5600 cubic metre (m) at the time of independence (1947) to a meager value of 1200 m.  Consequently, the value added in agriculture recorded a negative growth of 2.5% as against the positive 6% growth rate during the previous years. Soil salinity is another abiotic stress factor responsible for low crop production in Pakistan. It is estimated that about 6.30 million hectares of total land (79.6 mha).ha) are salt affected. Agricultural losses in Pakistan due to salinity are expected to reach US$ 28.5 million. In present scenario, biofertilizers based on the ability of crops and microbes to grow under abiotic stresses can be an effective approach for sustainable agriculture. Keeping in view the problem of water scarcity and soil salinity, rhizobacteria will be isolated from different ecological sites of Balochistan, Pakistan that are exposed to drought and salt stresses.

data.projectName: Sustainable Development of financial Inclusion: The Interaction of Economic Indicators, Financial Inclusion and Poverty Alleviation in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Financial inclusion is a multifaceted discipline and one of the main drivers of financial development. It consists of process, systems and entities to access and utilize different financial services for all the citizens of a country at reasonable and affordable costs. These services include the basic services of bank deposits, credits, saving schemes, insurance policies, payment facilitations and modes and sending of remittances. On the other hand lack of such facilities compel individuals to use high cost informal sources which results of financial exclusion of these individuals and entities. This leads to an asymmetric negative impact on different segments of individuals having different income levels. 
Inception and development of financial inclusion needs to be investigated on urgent basis. Furthermore on policy level, monetary policy and other economic fundamentals should be investigated and aligned with financial inclusion to cater for the harmonization and access of financial services across the country. Furthermore sustainable financial inclusion in line with UN-SDGs requires more attention and an investigation on policy level will contribute to the viability and sustainability of financial inclusion in Pakistan

data.projectName: Role of Investment and Financing Policies in Driving Firm’s Exports:  Behaviors of Financially Constrained and Weak Governed Firms
data.projectDigest: The study aims to test how firm’s investments and financing policies influences manufacturing exports condition to their financial constraints and corporate governance structure.  Study expects that firm's tendency to do investment out of their cash flows increases in presence of low financial constraints and strong corporate governance. While, corporation’s tendency to hold cash out of their cash flow are higher in financially constrained week governed firms.  Furthermore, such tendency to hold cash and investments negatively influences firm's level of exports. Study therefore will conduct an in-depth sectoral analysis by testing how firm's investment-cash flow sensitivity and cash-cash flow sensitivity influences their exports.  The findings of the study help managers in understanding the nexus between firm’s investment and financing policies while keep in view the financial constraints and corporate governance structure. In addition, managers can identify how particular manufacturing industry of Pakistan can increase exports. This study also helps policymakers in identifying how strong governance may role-play in decreasing firm’s financial constraints.

data.projectName: Azadirachta indica: An opportunity to modulate traditional medicines for Diabetes Mellitus
data.projectDigest: With the progression in the field of functional and nutraceutical the trend has been shifted towards the usage of valuable natural resources to curtail various disorders like diabetes and CVD which are one of the leading causes of mortality in Pakistan. According to Fifth Action Plan 2014-2018, there is 7.6% prevalence of diabetes with estimated 6.7 million people suffering from it and it is expected that it will rise to double by 2035. Since prehistoric epoch, the concept of using herbal remedies and naturopathy has been the keen interest of masses to curb different metabolic ailments. Among assorted herbal paragon, Azadirachta indica (Neem) has high recognition for its hidden potential for mankind; but limited studies are available in Pakistan. Keeping in view this scenario, the present project has been designed to assess the photochemistry of different part of neem tree (root, leaves, flower, seed) followed by their characterization and nutrient profiling. Moreover, the sensorial properties of food products blended with all these plant parts in varying ratios will be evaluated. To assess the hypoglycemic potential of all the fractions of neem plant an in vivo animal model will be examined to understand the modulating potential of all the fractions.

data.projectName: Development of a Low-cost Body worn Threat Detection System Using Vision-guided Commodity WiFi Radios
data.projectDigest: Terrorist groups are continuously using explosive devices to kill and injure thousands of people. Crowded places and infrastructural facilities like airports, railway stations, mosques, public parks, water supplies, and gas pipelines are likely targets of terrorist activities leading to insurmountable losses to country’s assets and human lives. A series of suicide bombing attacks on security personnel, mosques, buses, markets, and restaurants has created a great deal of insecurity and fear in our society. To tackle the ever-increasing wave of terrorism, remote detection of suspicious persons and hidden weapons has become an issue of paramount importance. An early warning detection system to point out suspicious activities and persons with body-worn concealed weapons at remote distances could be an important breakthrough to bolster the preventive measures that can be taken ahead of the time for mitigating, if not fully preventing, safety and security breaches. The goal of the proposed project is the development of such a system which would analyze the incoming video streams and apply signal processing algorithms on radar echoes to remotely detect and recognize suspicious persons using state-of-the-art computer vision, machine learning and radar signal processing techniques.
