data.projectName: Exploring the nutritional and Therapeutic potential of goat and sheep milk and cheeses
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Goat population world-wide is increasing, and the dairy goat sector is developing accordingly. Although the new technology applied to the goat industry is being introduced slowly because the weight of traditional subsector in the dairy sector, considerable advances have been made in the last decade. The dairy goat and sheep industry has gathered the desire of the consumer, in slow but steady growth, for products alternative to cow’s milk. Innovative goat dairy products are therefore increasing with ingredients that can satisfy the taste of today’s consumer. Dietary interventions have gained immense attention due to their health promoting aspects beyond medicinal treatments. In this perspective, the bioactive ingredients from goat and sheep milk and cheese are considered as rational and sustainable approach due to their physiological functions. The present study is designed to evaluate the nutritional and therapeutic potential of goat and sheep milk and cheese. Goat and sheep milk have unique sensory flavor and specific fatty acid profile therefore study of fatty acid profile of goat and sheep milk and cheese will be the part of this proposal. Water-soluble peptides (WSPs) extract will be derived from goat and sheep milk and cheeses and studied for anti-hypertensive, anti-thrombotic, anti-oxidant, and anti-cancer activities at different stage of ripening. Purposely, the WSPs fractions will be collected  and will be subjected to assess the degree of proteolysis, peptides profiling by RP-HPLC and in vitro assays for bioactivities of interest. Project will investigate the impact of milk source (goat, sheep), ripening time and concentration of WSPs on ACE-inhibitory, anti-thrombotic, anti-oxidant and anti-caner potential of goat and sheep milk and cheeses.

data.projectName: An IoT based Robotic System for Remote Patient Monitoring, Localization and Assisting Health Care Services
data.piUniversity: Karachi Institute of Economics & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Health care robots that utilizes modern technologies such as IoT and Intelligent Robotics (IR) technology are commercially available but very expensive to procure and maintain. To fill this gap, we take this opportunity to deploy IoT in a robotic system to create a heterogeneous system, which we call an IoT Aided Robotic (IAR) System for solving the health-care issues of the elderly people in Pakistan. The major possibilities include: detection of the abnormality in the vital signs of the patients, mood-detection, and fall-detection as well as detecting the mobility of the limbs of an elderly in cases of serious injuries. Fundamentally, one of the major aims of this project is to provide an effective solution to support autonomous living of the elderly patients with limited mobility in homes. Also the project targets to provide assistance to doctors and clinicians in health-care centers as well as the patient care-givers to remotely monitor the health-state of the patients. (1) the proposed system on one hand will provide physicians an effective remote diagnostic facility and (2) the designed alert system will keep aware the care-givers regarding any abnormality with the patient. The system will comprise of a robotic wheel-chair with both inertial as well as bio-sensors installed on it.

The control strategies of Haemonchus contortus parasite rely mainly on synthetic chemotherapeutics (Barrère et al. 2012). data.projectName: A data management framework for vehicular network
data.projectDigest: In this work, a data management framework for vehicular network is proposed as an extension of our earlier work. The computational power of the vehicles and collaboration among vehicles can be exploited to address a wide range of traffic related issues. However, in order to fully realize the true potential of vehicular network, a data management solution is desired. Based on the study, it is identified that data management for vehicular network requires addressing a range of problems such as data representation, routing, discovery, caching and economic model. To address these challenges, a data management framework is proposed in this work. The proposed framework will employ following components: i) a context-aware recommendation system to identify correlation among data items and provide a set of recommendations during data discovery (proactive/ reactive), caching and security ii) to employ a cross layer approach to data discovery and security iii) to use an ontology based approach to knowledge representation and discovery; resolving heterogeneity issues iv) to propose an economic model to ensure cooperation among vehicles. The development of such framework will pave the way for a large number of safety applications such as reducing accidents, avoiding congestion and emergency braking. Various non-safety applications such as Electronic Toll Free Collection, Travel and Tourism, Multimedia and Gaming are also possible. It is anticipated that proposition will have a huge impact on economy, health, environment and social sectors.

data.projectName: Nanotechnology based control of hazardous air pollutant emission and odor in poultry farming
data.projectDigest:
Air is the house of gases, odor, dust, and microorganisms. The most hazard gases areNO2, SO2, H 2S, CO, H2, CH4 and ammonia. NH3 is one of the major air pollutant challenge with serious impact on human and poultry health. Ammonia inhalation could irritate nose and throat and cause nausea and respiratory tract problems [1]. For controlling NH3 many traditional approaches like physicochemical processes used in industrial settings, and diet manipulation, manure confinement, and addition of inhibitors commonly employed in poultry operations are associated with technical drawbacks, excessive cost, inability to eliminate pollutants, and difficulty of implementation on a small scale. Thus, there is a need for development of more effective and feasible technologies. One such innovative approach is the use of nano-based adsorbents to mitigate the emission of this air pollutant.
Nanotechnology enables to create materials and systems with new features by manipulation of the matter at the level of atoms and molecules [2]. Nanotechnology can deliver significant improvements in terms of reducing the environmental pollutants and harmful pathogens. Keeping in views the above mentioned facts the present proposal is designed to capture individual NH3 and odors by TiO2 nanoparticles.

data.projectName: Investigation of anti-proliferative and anti-metastatic effects of different extracts of Cannabis sativa cultivated in Pakistan against human breast cancer cells
data.projectDigest: Cancer is the second leading cause of death worldwide and crucial public health problems. Its economic impact is significantly increasing day by day in developing and under developing countries including Pakistan. Nowadays, recognition of Cannabis sativa, as medicinally important plant is getting more attention. Studies reported that it possesses anticancer potential however; further studies are required to investigate and translate pharmacological findings into therapeutic interventions for breast cancer patients. We anticipated that our Cannabis sativa has more effect as compared to grown in other part of the world. Therefore, in Pakistan our research group at Aga Khan University is focused at investigating indigenously grown Cannabis sativa regarding its analgesic, anti-inflammatory and anti-cancer properties and in this regard we have an active grant (URC). This project is designed as the next step (to our first URC project) via extramural finding to explore the anti-proliferative properties, anti-metastatic effect and mechanisms including molecular pathways of different Cannabis sativa extracts against human breast cancer. We expect that the outcomes of this study will be the way-forward for the clinical trials. That is the ultimate goal of our research group to improve the standards of care in our country to benefit Pakistan’s population at large.

data.projectName: Zinc in combination with biofertilizers and biochar activate defense related enzymes to induce systemic acquired resistance (SAR) in mung bean against macrophomina phaseolina infestation in arid agro ecological zone
data.projectDigest: Macrophomina phaseolina [(Tassi) Goid] is highly destructive pathogen of mung bean [Vigna radiata (L.) Wilczek] causing charcoal rot disease. Zinc, an essential element for the metabolism of plant, when present in a lower concentration may cause significant losses in plant growth and yield and increases its susceptibility to disease. Current research work is designed to assess influence of charcoal rot pathogen on growth, yield and physiology of mung bean providing zinc deficiency as well as zinc supplements with different soil amendments. Preliminary experiment will be performed to screen out mung bean genotype against M. phaseolina. Further trials will be performed with selected moderately resistance, susceptible and highly susceptible genotypes to assess the impact of zinc deficiency on severity of charcoal rot disease. Later on, the disease management potential by proper application of zinc with and without application biofertilizers and organic amendments will be assessed. Multilateral interaction of host-pathogen-metal-organic amendment will be assessed in terms of morphology, growth, yield, physiology/biochemistry, metal uptake in V. radiata. The best combination of zinc and organic amendment/biofertilizer will be selected to conduct experiment in field and relevant growth, yield and physiological parameters will be recorded.The results of the present study will be helpful for the possible management of charcoal rot of mung bean in zinc deficient areas of Pakistan.

The objective of this research is to design and develop the Device to Device (D2D) communication via Visible Light Communication (VLC) product. To develop a new LEDs distribution in indoor VLC systems and design a new filter at the receiver in order to mitigate the multipath fading impact and shadowing effects, also study the effect of natural light or sunlight irradiance to the room and characterize the channel by measurements.

Furthermore, the optical received power, coverage area, channel capacity and SNR are expected to improve. The role of academic partners is to contribute practical knowledge in order to implement the project in real-time.

data.projectName: Monofunctional Platinum(II) based Anticancer Drugs
data.projectDigest:
Cisplatin and its variants, e.g., carboplatin and oxaliplatin, follow a similar classical mechanism of anticancer action under biophysiological conditions. Therefore, the toxicity problems associated with these particular compounds are more or less the same. Moreover, it is believed that the damaging side effects of these cisplatin derivatives is due to their square-planar structure in which off-target biomolecules can attack the exposed axial position of the platinum centre to form five-coordinate intermediates. Furthermore, it has been alleged that axial protection may reduce the damaging side effects resulting from the axial attack of off-target biomolecules.
The concept of stereochemistry lies at the heart of organic chemistry. It is often ignored, however, in the case of inorganic coordination compounds. Since stereochemical compounds have high sensitivity and selectivity towards natural stereochemical biomolecules, such as DNA and proteins, this field is a dynamic area of research at the interface of chemistry and biology. The processes by which stereochemical compounds are able to recognize various molecules in biological systems depend on their own stereochemical configurations and the sizes of the complexes. One of the distinct examples among platinum-based anticancer drugs is oxaliplatin, which features diaminocyclohexane (DACH) as a chelating spectator ligand. Empirical evidence has revealed that the R,R stereoisomer of oxaliplatin is more effective as an anticancer drug than is the S,S isomer. Later, crystallographic data showed that the R,R isomer preferentially forms a H-bond between the pseudoequatorial NH hydrogen of R,R-DACH and the O6 atom of the 3?-dG-platinated d(GpG) lesion. On the basis of these observations, we have now synthesized piperazine-base

data.projectName: Blockchain enabled supply chain management system for drugs
data.projectDigest:
Although rapid drug sales are a global problem (WHO estimates that up to 10% of global drug sales are counterfeit, Deloitte has put its price between $75 and $ 200 billion), where this case is more common in developing countries where lawbreakers are more difficult to track. In Pakistan, the Pharma Bureau evaluates that fake medicines account for 15 percent of the total pharmaceutical market of two billion rupees (WHO reports that 40 percent) designed to deal with counterfeit medicines. 
In Pakistan, there are huge number of medical stores, which are operating under questionable wholesales sources. These kinds of medical stores even do not maintain batch numbers of the medicine sold.
One of the reasons of counterfeit medicine in Pakistan is the low margin rates in profits on sale of original medicine. This encourages medical stores and pharmacies to buy counterfeit medicines at cheaper prices from the wholesalers and then generate higher profit rates.
The most important and comprehensive approach to avoid such scenario is to improve the mechanism of supply chain of drugs from manufacturers to the consumers and to make all the phases of supplies in transparent way specially raw material procurement, production, distribution and consumer market as every step of the drug's supply plays a vital role in drug safety. The system aims to diminish the risk of entering the legitimate supply chain of counterfeit drugs, enforce drug quality quickly and effectively, and complete drug recovery, along with protection and the health of customers. In this proposal, we propose hyperledger-fabric (blockchain) as a novel tool or service platform for supply chain management system for drugs.

data.projectName: SOCIO-ECONOMIC FACTORS FOR SEEKING PROTECTION IN SHELTER HOMES (DAR-UL-IMAN) BY VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE IN THE PUNJAB PAKISTAN.
data.projectDigest: Present study is designed to investigate the SOCIO-ECONOMIC FACTORS FOR SEEKING PROTECTION IN SHELTER HOMES (DAR-UL-IMAN) BY VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE IN THE PUNJAB PAKISTAN. Pakistan ranks as the sixth most dangerous country in the world for women, with cases of sexual crimes and domestic violence recording a rapid rise. It is imperative to understand the extent of violence against women in Pakistan. This Project is an attempt to unpack the social and economic factors behind the deeply embedded systematic nature of violence against women. For this we will analyze the social and economic hurdles that give rise to gender-based discrimination. The study tries to draw out the motives and driving forces behind violent actions against women. Multistage Sampling technique will be employed. At first stage three Divisions out of nine Divisions of Punjab will be selected randomly, at second stage two Districts from each  Division will be selected randomly  and finally 1000  female respondents who acquired the residence in shelter homes (Dar-ul-Imans) during the year. Data will be collected by a well-designed Interview Schedule. The collected data will be analyzed by using SPSS. Findings of the Project will be presented to the concern Agency/Organization. data.projectName: Mutational screening of hotspot genes in obese Pakistani population
data.projectDigest: Obesity is a complicated, multifactorial disease linking environmental, genetic and metabolic factors. It has been escalating at an alarming rate globally since the last two decades to the level that it is now an epidemic affecting millions of individuals worldwide, including Pakistan. Genome is a key player in the abnormal energy regulation that results in the accumulation of fats. MC4R gene is the basic regulator of metabolism and food intake. The genetics of MC4R is thus an important target for the development of the metabolic disorder. There are only a few studies related to the mutational analysis of the MC4R gene and little is known about genetic variations contributing to the development of obesity. Based on current facts, this research has been designed to study the role of MC4R and its target genes in obesity with several metabolic complications. We shall also check the mutational spectrum of those target genes, controlling the role of the MC4R gene, in blood samples of obese individuals and controls by using the Polymerase Chain Reaction technique (PCR) and Sanger sequencing. Data generated from this study will be used to analyze the significant relationship of mutations and dis-functioning of MC4R.

data.projectName: Opportunities and Threats to Apparel Exports of Pakistan: Policy Oriented Study
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is ranked 4th among cotton producing countries worldwide. However, apparel exports of Pakistan are not up to the mark e.g.  Pakistan produces best knitted T shirts in the world, but Pakistan exports only 1% of knitted shirts and is standing at 26th position in the list of exporters for this category of product in the world. Our neighbor countries India and Bangladesh are at the 1st and 3rd positions respectively. Pakistan is facing fierce competition from China, India and Bangladesh in this sector. The objective is to investigate the opportunities and threats in existing and novel markets of the world with respect to apparel exports of Pakistan through survey and expert interviews. So that appropriate guidelines can be recommended for SME sector policy makers. Furthermore, to enhance the export capabilities of domestic exporters and manufacturers seminars, trainings and workshops will be arranged.

data.projectDigest: Delimiting itself to public universities of Punjab province and federal capital, the primary aim of the proposed research is to identify the contents and structure of “entrepreneurial education” on the basis of need analysis from the perspective of the important stakeholders of university education in Pakistan.  This study is descriptive in nature and using mixed method research design (quantities and qualitative) the proposed project will be completed in three phases. will be employed for data collection. The required data will be collected through questionnaires from 2400 undergraduate students and 240 university teachers, and through interviews from 60 students, 60 teachers, 10 HODs and 10 directors academics. The draft course outline and contents will be validated by 10 experts in business studies. This study will hopefully generate the primary data about the need of entrepreneurial education at public universities of Pakistan. On entrepreneurial education, the attitudes, perceptions and beliefs of students, teachers, HODs, directors academics of the universities will come forth. Furthermore, variations in the need of entrepreneurial education will also be identified in terms of gender and discipline i.e. science and social science subjects. Most importantly, this study will identify the contents, structure and guidelines for introducing entrepreneurial education at science and social science departments of universities.

data.projectName: Poverty Reduction within the Macro Policy Framework of Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Development Economics (PIDE), Islamabad
data.projectDigest: The existing understanding of poverty in Pakistan points towards large fluctuations in the incidence of poverty over time as a major proportion of population lives around poverty line subject to frequent movements into and out of poverty resulting from negative and positive shocks. Poverty reduction strategies in the country fail to take these transitions into account as they rely on cross-sectional data. The Pakistan Institute of Development Economics (PIDE) in collaboration with the University of Bath, UK, aim to extend the understanding on the dynamics of poverty by revisiting the previous three rounds of the Pakistan Panel Household Survey (PPHS) conducted by PIDE, in 2001, 2004 and 2010, in which the same households are tracked over years.  This analysis would be complemented by an extensive qualitative analysis under the Q-Squared (mixed methods) approach to the understand poverty holistically. The proposed study would: investigate the poverty dynamics and the factors behind chronic, transient and intergenerational poverty, and those behind moving permanently out of the poverty trap; look into the underlying processes taking place behind the poverty dynamics; examine how the macro policy framework of Pakistan affects poverty dynamics; and make recommendations to improve poverty reduction strategies in the country.

data.projectName: stAging CanCer Using aRtificiAl inTelligencE (ACCURATE)
data.projectDigest: ACCURATE (stAging CanCer Using aRtificiAl inTelligencE) is a consortium of 4 project partners (RMI Peshawar, Sukkur-IBA Sindh, University of Lincoln UK and INTROGEN Ltd Istanbul) from 3 countries with leading expertise in image analysis and cancer genomics. The core objective is to build a complete ‘translatable’ pipeline for cancer prediction, detection and diagnostics. This will help in suggesting the most optimal treatment and prognosis pathways, enabling us to move forwards towards personalised medicine. The project will combine cancer imaging modalities, such as histopathology images with the genetic markers, molecular basis and understanding of characteristics of the tumour, family history of patients as well as other relevant social and economic indicators. To the best of our knowledge, no such database exists that combines the aforementioned information. This project will create the first publically available clean data repository of genetic and histopathology information representative of the Pakistani population. For the first time, genetic markers including expression data together with gut microbiome will be correlated with histopathology images using AI to accurately diagnose and precisely treat cancer patients. The project offers a high level of technical novelty in combining hybrid AI models, and in its application to cancer genetic and imaging analysis

data.projectName: Social norms and women’s labor market investments
data.projectDigest: The objective of our study is to explore the role of social norms in explaining gender disparities in the urban Pakistani labor market. We will do this by embedding new surveys and field experiments within an existing employment assistance or job search service,  which has been set up by the research team in Lahore, Pakistan.  We will collect new data to examine social norms that lead women to turn away from taking career enhancing actions due to being perceived as too ambitious by their peers, particularly male peers. This research will inform policymakers and practitioners on the design of effective policy interventions to reduce gender disparities in the urban Pakistani labor market.

data.projectName: Sustainable Buildings in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: This project will provide a detailed sustainability assessment of buildings in Pakistan and formulation of guidelines for operations of existing buildings and new construction. A rigorous study will be conducted in the major cities of Pakistan. The key areas including sustainable sites, water efficiency, energy and atmosphere, materials and resources, indoor environmental quality and innovation in design will be assessed and compared to acceptable standards and best practices. The gap will be identified and a comprehensive framework will be formulated to improve the substantiality of existing as well as future buildings. The project will also identify suitable solutions for future construction in the areas of (1) alternative materials (2) innovation in design (3) energy conservation and efficiency (4) water conservation and efficiency. A prototype typical building will be constructed in this research project and all the required features of energy efficient and sustainable buildings will be incorporated. This project will be executed jointly with the local stakeholders including city development authorities, local government and national and provincial housing authorities. Under this project, a training course for the students and faculty will be arranged. Similarly, a workshop on green buildings will also be arranged for students and public awareness.

data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Antimicrobial resistance is an imminent 21st century global health challenge. The problem is even more severe in Pakistan as compared to the developed world due to extensive misuse of antibiotics in humans and livestock. WHO in its recent assessment has declared antimicrobial resistance as a major health crisis in Pakistan. From a bio-physical perspective, one of the main contributing factors towards anti-bacterial resistance against front-line antibiotics is the formation of ‘bio-films’. This project aims to develop local resources as well international collaborations between Kings College London and the Lahore University of Management Sciences, to study Escherichia coli and Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteria. More specifically, we will focus on the structural and molecular investigations of Flagella and biofilms of bacterial colonies of E. Coli and P. aeruginosa as model systems. The proposal plans to extend the scope of work to other bacterial infections such as Salmonella and Typhoid, which are major health challenges in current pathology within Pakistan.

data.projectName: Next Generation Artificial Intelligence based Smart Prosthetic/Robotic Hand (NEXGRASP)
data.projectDigest: The aim of this research is to develop a Next-Generation Artificial Intelligence based Smart Prosthetic/Robotic Hand (NEXGRASP) to facilitate people with upper limb disabilities. The problem with present day commercial prosthetic hands is that they are unable to provide essential functionalities to patients, despite their high cost. The technological advancements in the field of machine learning, artificial intelligence and robotics provides a lot of opportunities to improve mechanical design and control architecture of bionic hands. This research will integrate artificial intelligence with the control systems and resolve the challenges faced by existing prosthetic hands. Also, a sophisticated, reliable and precise connection of the human mind and an artificial limb will be established. This joint collaborative research will provide the essential platform to develop next generation smart and robust robotic hand, that excels in performance and achieve complex tasks of daily life. It will not only bring ease and enhance the quality of life of those people who have lost their hands, but they will also retain functions like a normal hand, which will ultimately result in boosting the socio-economic growth of society.

data.projectName: Sustainable Off-grid Electricity Markets: Peer-to-Peer Sharing of Solar Energy for 56 million Pakistanis and 1 Billion People Worldwide
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: Access to electricity is key in improving the socio-economic standing of communities. Unfortunately, approx. 1 billion people worldwide and over 50 million in Pakistan have no access to electricity! Electricity provision through national grids is unviable for many of these regions due to infrastructural, generation and cost constraints. The need of the hour is to electrify these offgrid communities through renewables based innovative solution so that they are able to improve their socioeconomic standing and help the GDP of the country. In line with this rationale, this project proposes a) an indigenous development and b) actual field deployment of the proposed electrification solution based on peer-to-peer sharing of electricity through low-cost infrastructure. The integration/aggregation of solar generation in individual rural houses will be used for community applications (water filtration, pumping, school, health units etc.) on need-basis or in predefined scenarios. This will create/enable electricity markets in rural community (a novel concept within offgrid electrification). Smarts will be built on a communication layer which oversees the local solar generation, local storage, entire bi-directional exchange of energy, and thresholds the power usage at each house as per designed power sharing policy. The possibility of electricity theft is negligible as every node is monitored through either a central system or decentralized energy accounting.

data.projectName: A Multivalent Polymer Platform for Functionalising Nanostructures with Biomolecules and their Synthetic Mimics: Bionanotechnology for Enhanced Functionalities in Bacterial Control and Healthcare
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: The healthcare landscape in Pakistan is challenging. Access to specialized medical diagnostic facilities is limited and the provision of even basic medical care such as microbial control needs to be improved. In parallel, the effectiveness of the global antibiotic arsenal is decreasing due to the emergence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) arising from the excessive and imprudent use of antimicrobials, this is a major crisis facing humanity in the 21st century. In both high and low income countries, methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is a bacterium increasingly found in hospital settings and it is resistant to most antibiotics. In Pakistan, the Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M. tb) bacterium causes over 0.5 million new tuberculosis (TB) cases every year, including 15,000 cases of drug resistant TB. The situation is exacerbated by the several days to weeks that current tests take to diagnose TB. These problems collectively demand the development of novel technologies that enable the judicious use of antimicrobial agents. This project will bring about translatable bionanotechnology driven scientific innovations for controlling bacterial infection and for identifying pathogenic bacteria in an unprecedented strain specific manner. The success of the project will lead to technologies for mitigation and early detection of bacterial infections.

data.projectName: The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor: Regional, Federal and Local Challenges and Opportunities
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: In this project we will build new understanding on how the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) has impacted the Pakistani polity across three levels: the regional, the federal, and the local. While CPEC has resulted in vast—and sudden—injection of foreign capital in Pakistan’s infrastructure, we posit that only by critically evaluating CPEC at (and across) the three levels can new opportunities be fully leveraged. Our findings shall be valuable to the Pakistani government and local investors, and to international investors and policy analysts interested in the region.

data.projectName: Global impact and opportunities from large-scale solar photovoltaic electricity generation on agricultural production
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: Our world is facing grand challenges around the sustainable supply of energy, food, and, water resources. Population growth, climate change, and, escalating resource demands urgently demand holistic solutions for sustainable energy and food production. We aim to pioneer state-of-the-art agrivoltaic systems (AVS) – an innovative production system that combines solar energy and food production on a fertile land. Recent assessment of AVS, where fertile land under the partial and fluctuating shade of elevated solar arrays is leveraged to grow crops, has shown multiple synergetic benefits for food-water-energy nexus that urgently need to be capitalized with growing deployments of solar parks. Large scale energy production through AVS not only preserves agriculture on fertile land but has also demonstrated greater food production, reduced solar heat losses and reduced climate vulnerability. Potential of AVS especially for regions with extreme energy, food and water scarcity need to assessed through climate aware models and field validation. We aim to assess techno-economic potential and design of AVS globally through transdisciplinary models and experimental validation in Pakistan, UK and other international sites. Experiments will explore solar architectures and crop trials with detailed system monitoring. Local adoptability, economic sustainability, and integration with overall energy supply chain will be explored.

data.projectName: Entrepreneurship in Impoverished Communities of Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
There is growing recognition by scholars and policy makers across  the globe  of the importance of entrepreneurship and innovation in socio-economic development and transformation of impoverished regions). Many entrepreneurs from impoverished communities engage in business activities but the majority are unable to generate  viable returns and eventually fail. The research suggests that individual characteristics and institutional environment heavily influence entrepreneurial success This research also points to the  interplay between institutional and individual factors as playing a crucial role in  shaping outcome and sustainability of new venture . 
	The literature suggests that institutional factors such as  external support, property protection, access to credit and government support mechanisms influence the nature and propensity of entrepreneurial activities. Another major stream within the entrepreneurship literature suggests that individual characteristics like cognitions, education, prior knowledge, experience, opportunity identification abilities and self-efficacy are also important to entrepreneurship 
In many developing countries both institutional and individual factors are deficient resulting in non-productive entrepreneurship.  This study will further analyze the Matos and Hall (2019) framework of  Productive, Unproductive, Destructive and Non-productive Entrepreneurship in Impoverished Regions of Pakistan. It will be further to be developed in the study.  Specifically, we aim to investigate why entrepreneurs in impoverished regions of Pakistan struggle to succeed and how both individual and institutional factors influence such outcomes. To this end, following research questions are posited: 
1. Why entrepreneurs from impoverished communities struggle to succeed
2. How individual and institutional factors influence such outcomes
3. How the institutional environment and individual alertness can be improved within impoverished communities
4.  How can entrepreneurs migrate from non-productive (Quadrant 1 in Table 1) to productive entrepreneurship (Q4), and how can movement from Q1 to destructive entrepreneurship (Q2) be avoided?    
To address these questions, an inductive methodological approach will be adopted and data will be collected through a survey questionnaire and interviews from entrepreneurs located in impoverished regions of Sindh province of Pakistan. The findings of this study will be of key importance for practitioners and government policy makers by providing policy guidelines to boost productive entrepreneurship by identifying the factors that negatively affect productive entrepreneurship in impoverished communities. In addition, the findings will also shed light on the individual and institutional factors affecting productive entrepreneurship.
This research will form the base of a training and development programme for 10 Pakistani academics, academic practitioners and policy makers, who will spend 2 weeks at SPRU at the University of Sussex, this training will support the creation of interventions and activities that will promote the development of solutions, informed by the research outputs. The training programme will be at Level 7 and will result in internationally accredited award in applied research and development innovation. This training will be linked to promoting entrepreneurship and addressing the UN 2030 Sustainability Goals across Pakistan. Through engagement with EduQual (host of the original scoping visit) and Catalysts in Communities (social enterprise development specialists), as industry and community partners, the project aims to create a model for developing applied research models in developing countries to promote enterprise, social enterprise development and promote employment and economic opportunities.

data.projectName: Comparative investigation of co-pyrolysis and hydrothermal liquefaction of agricultural residues and plastic waste for production of fuel-range and aromatic hydrocarbons using Pakistan-based natural zeolite catalyst
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: This research project is an attempt to address the energy crisis, impact of excessive use of fossil fuels on climate and issues related to municipal and agricultural waste management, all at a time.  The project aims to explore the usability of natural zeolites found in Pakistan as catalyst for co-pyrolysis and hydrothermal liquefaction of the crop residues and refused plastics; the two thermochemical processes which can potentially convert the two different types of wastes (biomass and plastics) into alternative fuels and feedstock for valuable chemicals which, in turn, can potentially replace the fossil fuels and chemicals. Due to high cost and thus non-compliance with the waste disposal due processes in the developing world, both, plastic wastes and crop residues are disposed of in ways which are detrimental to environment. On the other hand, use of fossil fuels have high impact on climate. It would be a win-win situation if the wastes can be used as resources for fuel production. Catalysts used in pyrolysis and hydrothermal liquefaction processes promote the desirable reactions, thus leading to formation of high quality fuels/feedstock chemicals. However, synthetic zeolites are costly and potential of natural zeolites needs to be explored which would make the processes cost-effective.

data.projectName: SmartPath: UK-Pak academic-clinical initiative on AI and digital pathology for precision cancer diagnostics
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Cancer prevalence is high in Pakistan due to difficulties in early diagnosis related to lack of cancer registries, limited trained clinicians and hospitals, and inaccessibility to state of the art diagnostic/genetic tests. Consequently, the cancer associated socio-economic burden is continuously increasing. We propose to develop “SmartPath” which is an AI-driven indigenous solution for cancer diagnosis and management by leveraging digital pathology and genomic data. In addition to building a national histology and genomic data base it aims to correlate digital histology image signatures to molecular profiles for improved diagnosis, risk stratification and personalized treatment of Pakistani cancer patients. SmartPath aims to use novel AI based approaches for biomarker discovery with the help of cross population analysis of UK and Pakistani oral cancer cohort consisting of histology and genomic data.
SmartPath will develop a national cancer pathology platform using pathology and associated genomics data. Using low cost scanning hardware, HNC slides will be digitized and a feasibility analysis performed for diagnostic reliability and efficiency. Novel AI methods will be developed for combined histological and genomic analysis and objective quantification of histological patterns to facilitate better stratification for HNC patients. A cross population analysis will also be performed on a UK cohort for comparison to identify key etiological factors behind oral cancers.
SmartPath is a novel initiative led by an interdisciplinary team of researchers, academics, hospitals and pathology labs from the UK and Pakistan who have an established track record in the domain of AI-enabled digital pathology and genomics to tackle clinically challenging and relevant problem(s) using a sustainable strategy. The consortium is formed in collaboration with leading hospitals and pathology labs from the UK and Pakistan which include SKMCH&RC Lahore (the largest cancer hospital in Pakistan), OraLab (the only specialist Oral/Head and Neck Pathology setup in Pakistan), CMH Rawalpindi, Rehman Medical Institute Peshawar, UHCW Coventry (the first NHS Trust to implement digital pathology for diagnostic practice in the UK) and the largest and most reputable Oral Pathology centre in the UK (Sheffield). The UK members are leading parts of the PathLAKE project, which is a Center of Excellence in AI for digital pathology with a consortium of leading hospitals and industrial partners.

data.projectName: Design of Clay-based Composite Nanoparticles for Sequestering Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs) - A Systematic Approach
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Global stresses on natural resources open several avenues for environmental pollution and climate change. Persistent organic pollutants (POPs) are organic compounds that, to a varying degree, resist photolytic, biological and chemical degradation. These toxic substances can adsorb on fatty tissues and can cause cancer and mutations in living organisms. These are volatile substances and can travel through the air for long distances thus creating a worldwide challenge. Due to the industrial activities  and excessive use of agricultural chemicals, a significant amount of these pollutants already exists on a global scale. POPs such as Aldrin and DDT produce significant health risks and are present in our rivers, soils, and airborne dust. To address the problem, in parallel to enforcing illegal or unintentional production of POPs, significant research has to be made for collecting and decomposing prevailing pollutants in the ecosystem. Among all the available techniques, more stress is being laid upon heterogeneous photocatalytic degradation of organic pollutants. The process takes place on the surface of a semiconductor photoactive material in the presence of sunlight. Developments to-date have mainly relied upon experimental tests, following trial and error. A comprehensive study is needed that provides the design guidelines, and into related properties.

data.projectName: Autonomous Weed Removing AI Robot Ground Vehicle
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: In this project, an autonomous weed detecting, locating and removing robot vehicle is proposed as a potential solution to managing weeds. An autonomous robot vehicle equipped with mechanical structures along with internet-of-things (IoT) and vision sensors can achieve efficient weed management through advanced technologies of Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL). In this project, the research teams from Pakistan and the United Kingdom would jointly focus their efforts to successfully design this intelligent electro-mechanical system. In the project, Artificial Intelligence will be incorporated through advanced concepts of computer vision by exploiting advanced ML and DL techniques. It is estimated that the use of the proposed system will drastically reduce the need for environmentally damaging herbicides.

data.projectName: Oxidative Desulfurization study of Pakistani Petrochemical (diesel fuel) and textile industry effluent by reusable Zinc-Ferrite Nanocatalyst
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Sulfur content in the diesel fuel and textile effluent is well known contributor of Sulfur dioxide (SO2) gas in to the air from, which motivates acid rain. It can cause deforestation and damage of aquatic life. Sulfur dioxide (SO2) is toxic, irritating, and suffocating gas, which on continuous exposure can cause severe damage to respiratory systems of living beings. Sulfur removal from a diesel fuel is important for Pakistani Oil and Petroleum industry to attain Euro 5 standard to overcome environmental and health problems. 
The aim of the proposed work is to develop a reusable heterogeneous catalyst to accomplish high sulfur removing efficiency without affecting the hydrocarbon molecular structure of the diesel fuel in the petrochemical industry and efficient magnetic separation of Sulfur from textile effluent. In the study, Fe- ZnO nanocatalyst synthesized via modified sol–gel technique, the different doping weight percentage (mol. %) of Fe metal will be explored for oxidative desulfurization (ODS) study, in the presence of H2O2 as an oxidant. The reusability of spent catalyst will be studied for various consecutive time for efficient sulfur removal. The close catalytic cycle involving H2O2 as oxidant will be a promising pathway for sulfur removal from the diesel fuel.

data.projectName: Development of Infants Gut Microbiota and Resistome and its Association with Sepsis Burden
data.projectDigest:
Funding is sought to investigate the molecular epidemiology and genetics of multi-drug resistant organisms (MDRO) in neonates and children along with the development of their microbiota. Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is global problem and becomes a serious issue in the management of infections in neonates due to limited treatment options. Our experience on neonatal infections caused by MDRO has highlighted a serious lack of knowledge regarding the development of microbiota in neonates and children in Pakistan. Whilst there have been detailed microbiome studies from high-income countries (HICs), there are few studies from low-middle income countries (LMICs) examining the development of the microbiome and which factors determine the establishment of the resistome. The development of the infant’s microbiota is a critical aspect of neonatal development; in particular, strain acquisition in early life of the neonate and how this affects wellbeing and their relatedness with diseases such as sepsis.  There is a need to have a correlation on the acquisition of MDROs with the clinical outcome and thus assess this burden in early development. 
The study is dynamic in its design as it aims to use genomic platforms to understand the development of neonatal microbiome. Briefly, rectal/vaginal swabs and faces samples will be taken from pregnant females and their babies and will be sequenced to analyse their microbiota. The babies will be followed through first year of their life and their feeding habits and any associated problems will be recorded through the questionnaire. For babies who develop sepsis, their blood culture isolates will also be studied using detailed molecular and genomic characterization methods. The genomic traits (resistance genes, virulence factors, sequence type, plasmid incompatibility group) of microbiome and sepsis strains will be compared. The study will also address the similarities/differences in microbiome of mothers and their babies. 
The data generated in this study will help us find answers to some of the pertaining questions on the neonatal microbiota establishment in our local settings. This funding will enable us to strengthen our capacity and further understand the impact of AMR on the infant’s microbiota and early development.
data.projectSummary:
Funding is sought to investigate the molecular epidemiology and genetics of multi-drug resistant organisms (MDRO) in neonates and children along with the development of their microbiota. Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is global problem and becomes a serious issue in the management of infections in neonates due to limited treatment options. Our experience on neonatal infections caused by MDRO has highlighted a serious lack of knowledge regarding the development of microbiota in neonates and children in Pakistan. Whilst there have been detailed microbiome studies from high-income countries (HICs), there are few studies from low-middle income countries (LMICs) examining the development of the microbiome and which factors determine the establishment of the resistome. The development of the infant’s microbiota is a critical aspect of neonatal development; in particular, strain acquisition in early life of the neonate and how this affects wellbeing and their relatedness with diseases such as sepsis.  There is a need to have a correlation on the acquisition of MDROs with the clinical outcome and thus assess this burden in early development. 
The study is dynamic in its design as it aims to use genomic platforms to understand the development of neonatal microbiome. Briefly, rectal/vaginal swabs and faces samples will be taken from pregnant females and their babies and will be sequenced to analyse their microbiota. The babies will be followed through first year of their life and their feeding habits and any associated problems will be recorded through the questionnaire. For babies who develop sepsis, their blood culture isolates will also be studied using detailed molecular and genomic characterization methods. The genomic traits (resistance genes, virulence factors, sequence type, plasmid incompatibility group) of microbiome and sepsis strains will be compared. The study will also address the similarities/differences in microbiome of mothers and their babies. 
The data generated in this study will help us find answers to some of the pertaining questions on the neonatal microbiota establishment in our local settings. This funding will enable us to strengthen our capacity and further understand the impact of AMR on the infant’s microbiota and early development.

data.projectName: Discovery and Validation of Blood Based Biomarkers for Suicide Attempt Behavior in Depressive Patients in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Suicide attempts have become a major public health problem in Pakistan in recent years. Suicide prevention is a daunting problem in Pakistan due to lack of funding, poorly developed primary and mental health facilities and weak political processes. According to the World Health Organization, more than 800,000 people in the world commit suicide every year. The best method to assess a patient’s risk of suicide is to screen for past suicide attempts in the patient and their family. Patients are either interviewed or decisions are made based on self-reported measures such as questionnaires, which are subjective and difficult to standardise. Furthermore, given the stigma associated with suicide, which is especially prevalent in islamic countries, patients may not be honest about expressing themselves. Building on previous work in Korean nationals, we propose to elucidate new blood based biomarkers to improve our understanding of depression and suicide. DNA Methylation and transcriptome markers have been shown to contribute to better prediction of suicidal behavior, however, these findings have not been validated in South Asian populations. Next-generation sequencing and genome-wide studies will identify novel candidate genes and variants associated with suicidal behavior and depression. These markers, along with other parameters, can be used to systematically design machine learning models for improving risk prediction. This approach has the potential to reshape how we predict suicide risk and save many lives across the region.

data.projectName: COMBAT: Cloud Computing and Big Data Platform for Carbon Reduction and Sequestration
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: The goal of this project is to develop a Cloud Computing and Big Data platform that supports collection and integration of data from different sources and provides advanced data analytics capabilities for informed decision-making related to environmental protection. Specifically, we focus on carbon reduction and sequestration with two major application domains under the umbrella of climate change: i) transport electrification; and ii) precision forestry. In the transport electrification domain, we focus on utilizing the advanced metering infrastructure (AMI) for collection, integration, and analysis of data from different grid components to develop electricity load forecasting model to evaluate the impact of electric vehicle (EV) on the electricity load profile. This forecasting model will facilitate design and development of a framework for EV charge scheduling to ensure electricity supply-demand balance in a weak distribution grid as well as to use EV as virtual power plants for strengthening of distribution grid and for demand-side management. In the precision forestry domain, we focus on utilizing remote sensing technology coupled with real-time in-situ sensor observations, archived data from forest organizations, and advanced data analytics pipeline to support various precision forestry related activities, including monitoring & forest health evaluation, forest biodiversity estimation, and forest conservation.

data.projectName: Demand response enabled micro-grids to mitigate blackouts.
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Pakistan has faced significant power generation vs. demand mismatch in the past two decades. In the last couple of years, the country has managed to lift up the generation to the surplus end. However, in the process, the transmission and distribution network did not grow with the same pace. This results in network overloading during the peak hours, which has the potential to destroy electrical systems in the network being operated at an overloaded condition. To avoid this, blackouts are observed, especially in the densely populated areas. This project proposes a method to avoid network overloading and blackouts by efficiently utilising the load and with the application of smart grids features. Specifically batteries at user premises will be used in conjunction with the renewable generators spread around a grid node to keep the inflow to the node under an allocated budget. This will help in keeping the network away from an overloading condition.

data.projectName: Age-Invariant Face Recognition using Lightweight Deep Learning Models and its application in Finding Missing Children and Criminals
data.piUniversity: National University of Computer and Emerging Sciences, Islamabad
data.projectDigest: Big Cities in Pakistan are a source of large amount of video, social media, labour market, medical, environmental, and socio-economic surveillance data. An integrated perspective of managing and analyzing such a huge surveillance data is crucial to improve the quality of life of the citizens in Pakistan. The proposed project aims to investigate how machine learning and computer vision techniques can help in solving the two important analytical problems of surveillance data in the society. These problems are applicable to Pakistan and in almost all third world countries. One such issue which is also a serious social problem is Finding Missing Children who, either run away from their homes due to social pressures or are kidnapped to work as beggars. It should be noted that “Missing” is the first step that further leads to all other crimes i.e. physical abuse, sexual exploitation, forced labor and even murder. Another application is the surveillance of known suspects in public places like train stations, shopping centers etc. Sarim Burney Welfare Trust International and Sindh Police are keen to use these softwares that can help them in finding the missing children and the suspects simultaneously.

data.projectName: Developing an in vivo screening platform for understanding tumorigenesis and cancer drug development
data.piUniversity: CECOS University of Information Technology and Emerging Sciences, Peshawar
data.projectDigest: Drosophila melanogaster or the fruit fly is a remarkable model organism which over the past century has helped us in laying the foundation of cancer biology. We share 75% of our disease related genes with the fruit fly and a remarkable 68% of cancer genes between us and flies are the same. This makes flies great systems for us to model and test different types of cancer. This project proposes to develop a screening platform based on fruit flies that can be used to develop models of cancers that are found in the Pakistani population. This will not only help us generate terabytes of phenotypic datasets that will complement the genomic datasets that we are accumulating and help us train nuanced computational models to predict different cancers (falling into the Big Data and Cloud Computing theme) but also provide us a chance to test cancer and tumorigenesis in their organs, their embryos, their larvae (when they hatch from fly eggs) and in adult flies (tests never possible in human subjects) and also to screen large numbers of drugs and drug combinations against these models of cancers relevant to our population (falling under the Medical and Allied Health Sciences theme).

data.projectName: Increasing Female Participation in Transportation Sector by financing rickshaws using debt and equity based contracts
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: Women face significant challenges while using public transport because of concerns over safety, harassment and worries about their social reputation. There is clearly an urgent need for smartly designed, feasible transport interventions that can help improve women’s mobility to travel safely. We propose an exploratory study that will directly test the viability of safe transport option for women in Pakistan. We will do this by enabling female participation in the transportation sector, by providing them with financing for transportation assets (rickshaws). We also test whether a novel equity-based microfinance contract, which explicitly allows for  better alignment of repayments with performance, can be more effective than a fixed-repayment debt-based contract in encouraging female participation in transportation markets. We hypothesise that the contract have the potential to serve a very large number of poor Muslim entrepreneurs, many of whom remain unbanked because of the classical religious prohibition on usury. We intend to conduct a randomised controlled trial with 100 women in Lahore, 60 of whom will be offered rickshaw financing, and 40 offered “business as usual” loans by our partner organisation, Akhuwat (one of the largest MFIs in Pakistan). We also partner with Careem, the largest transportation network company in the region.

data.projectName: Design, development and demonstration of the organic Rankine cycle system for low temperature and waste heat to power conversion
data.projectDigest:
The UK has set target to bring greenhouse gas emissions to net zero by 2050. In order to achieve zero emission target by 2050, drastic measures are required to reduce the energy consumption and improve the energy efficiency. The UK and Pakistan have a great potential of waste heat from industrial as well as low temperature solar thermal and geothermal resources, which are usually are discarded as waste heat due to unavailability of the cost effective and efficient technology. Although there are several alternative technologies (at different stages of development) for waste heat recovery, such as heat exchanger, heat pump, Stirling engine and Kalina Cycle, the Organic Rankine Cycle system remains the most promising in practice. Large Organic Rankine Cycle systems are commercially viable for high-temperature applications, however, their application to low-temperature waste heat (<250 Degree C) is in its infancy. Yet more than 60% of industrial waste heat sources are in the low temperature band (<250 Degree C). There is clearly a mismatch between Organic Rankine Cycle technology supply and demand, so innovative research and development are highly in demand. In addition, the lower thermal efficiency and higher specific investment cost ($/kW) of the small scale ORC system represent major challenges for the application of ORC system for industrial waste heat recovery. In recent years, it has been reported that the use of zeotropic mixtures as working fluids in ORC system can lead to improvement in thermal efficiency and reduction in specific investment cost. However, there is no practical application of zeotropic based ORC system due to lack of the: 1) Accurate knowledge of their behaviour, which leads manufacturers to prefer the use of traditional non-environmentally-friendly fluids; 2) Fundamental understanding of heat transfer process during evaporation and condensation of the zeotropic mixtures is unknown; 3) Fundamental knowledge about the dynamic response, control of mixture composition, and control strategies of the ORC system with zeotropic mixtures as working fluid.  
The primary goal of this research is to improve the fundamental understanding of zeotropic mixtures application as working fluid in ORC system for industrial waste heat recovery. The aim is that the findings of the project should enable 15% reduction in specific investment cost of the ORC system. Most notably this refers to improve the net power out of the ORC unit by employing zeotropic binary mixtures application as working fluid in ORC system and optimized control of the ORC system. More specifically, this project will deliver: 1) a reliable tool for the estimation of the thermophysical and transport properties of the zeotropic mixtures; 2) experimentally validated heat transfer and pressure drop empirical correlation of the zeotropic mixtures; 3) development of dynamic model and control of zeotropic mixture based ORC system. Thermophysical properties of zeotropic mixtures will be estimated using Group Contribution Methods based on cubic equations of state. Based on these properties estimation model, extensive experimental campaign will be carried out to investigate the local heat transfer and pressure drop characteristics of the mixtures. A component level dynamic model and non-linear model predictive controller will be developed for zeotropic mixture based ORC system and development of tuning system for zeotropic mixtures. To this end, a state of the art experimental test rig will be developed at international Islamic university to carry out the experimentation and later implemented at the partner industrial site to demonstrate the technical and economic feasibility. 
This project will be completed in collaboration with leading academics from the UK (Aston University UK, Glasgow University UK) and Pakistan (International Islamic University Islamabad, UET Lahore Rachna Campus, NUST USPCASE) as well as industrials partners (Entropea Labs Limited UK, Ghani Glass Pakistan, Mughal Steel Pakistan, and Kor tech Auto Industries Pakistan). The project consortium consist of leading researcher in the proposed research area with relevant expertise and experience, through close collaboration it will be ensure that the project is successfully completed and the outcomes are transferred and implemented in industry. The PI (Dr. Imran & Prof. Nadeem) have proven record of accomplishment in the management of research project, conducting and communicating high quality scientific research. The UK side will carry out the development of the tool for thermophysical properties estimation and heat transfer assessment of the zeotropic mixtures. Dr. Adeel from USPCASE NUST will design and develop the turbo expander for the ORC test rig, along with the expertise of the Entropea Labs and UK partners, a test rig will be designed and developed at International Islamic University Islamabad. Dr. Byung-Sik from South Korea will serve as consultant for the development and demonstration of the ORC test rig. He agreed to provide 2 hours per month as in kind contribution. The Pakistani team will be responsible for the development of the mixture tuning system, dynamic model and control of the ORC system. Based on the industrial feedback from industrial partners in Pakistan, the ORC test rig will be implemented and test at one of the listed industrial partner site. Each industrial partner has committed for in kind contribution of 1 hours per week for the project. 
This project will resolve major barrier for successful commercialization of the ORC system for energy intensive industrial sectors such as the iron and steel industry, ceramic manufacturers, cement factories, petrochemical, paper industry, etc. The successful implementation of ORC technology in energy intense industry will improve the industrial and economic growth, reduce the carbon emission, improve the energy security, and create new business and job opportunities due to ORC development and installation. From the academic perspective, this project will provide fundamental understanding of the dynamic behaviour of the ORC system under transient heat source from design and control perspectives. In broader context, the project will contribute to improve energy efficiency and reduce carbon emissions, thus helping to attain socio-economic and environmental targets in UK and Pakistan.

data.projectName: ICRG: Characterization of Autism Spectrum Disorders using a Biomedical Approach
data.projectDigest: Children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) have difficulties with communication, social interaction and repetitive behaviours with differences in severity. Most children with ASD are not able to live independently requiring lifelong care having a devastating effect on their families. The number of children affected by ASD is increasing worldwide at an alarming rate including Pakistan, where there is little awareness. This study will look at changes in nutrients (especially folate), sugar and oxygen damaged molecules and genes in order to relate these to ASD severity. A large cohort of over 1000 children are available for this study at the Children's Hospital in Lahore. Blood, urine, saliva and skin of ASD children will be analyzed to detect changes in various molecules. The findings will help to develop a treatment for ASD. Currently there is no medication for ASD and affected children are treated by behaviour modification with variable success. This project brings together leading experts from Manchester UK with those from Lahore and Islamabad in Pakistan. In the final year of the project, a workshop on ASD for healthcare professionals and an autism awareness event for the general public will be delivered.

data.projectName: 3D printable graphene based RE-doped nano-inks for creating next-generation of solar-powered supercapacitors.
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan as a developing country has suffered severe energy supply and shortage challenges while energy plays an important role for economic development. Due to energy shortfall commercial, economic activities and quality of life adversely affected while global warming caused by fossil fuel increased. As Pakistan is in Sun Belt so its cost-effective energy demands can be completed by harvesting and storing solar energy which is renewable and clean form of abundantly available energy. Energy generation and storage are key for photo electronic devices. Due to low cost material fabrication Dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) are cost effective alternative to silicon based solar cells. Successful development of efficient, stable, low cost DSSCs will reduce fossil fuel use, greenhouse gas emissions, and global warming. The dye (sensitizer) and the counter electrode material are the main factors which influence the DSSC performance. Ruthenium based dye is widely used as photosensitizer while Platinum as counter electrode material which are expensive. The focus of this joint project is to improve the DSSC components for energy generation while energy storage by photo supercapacitors. Plants extracts and Graphene based RE-doped ink as electrode material will be used instead of Ru-based dyes and Platinum counter electrode respectively to develop low cost and easily processable DSSC for energy generation. 
To support growing demand for electronic vehicles, low-cost solar energy harvesting and storage solutions are required. Miniature supercapacitors will play key role in the future vehicles, due to their ability to quickly charge/discharge (enabling high power output) and their potentially lengthy lifespans. However, their innovative development is still limited by inefficient bulky connections between functional modules, large size due to low energy production/storage capacity, incompatible energy storage systems with poor cycling stability, and real safety concerns. This deficiency is partially due to the electrode’s materials and the manufacturing methods. Recent progress in functional nanomaterials coupled with advanced printing fabrication techniques have opened up possibilities for the development of cost-efficient, solution-processed printed electronic device. The advancements in conducting, semiconducting and dielectric nanoparticle inks can be used to create multi-functional electronic circuit and devices that are flexible, light-weight and with very low carbon footprint. 
This project will exploit, the extraordinary properties of graphene based RE-doped nano-inks for a flexible miniature solar-powered supercapacitor as multifunctional structural components. We will, develop a nano-ink for scalable and tunable electrodes, with improved conductivity and connectivity, as well as efficiently. The findings will pave a practical route toward the design of future self-powered solar based vehicles, affording favorable safety, long life, and high energy.
This cross-disciplinary work will bring together research active academics, in leading edge chemistry, materials and electrical sciences, in different universities. It will exploit the material manufacture and testing equipment in Pakistan, world-class and wide-ranging synthetic and Nanofabrication and electronic facilities at the James Watt School of engineering, Glasgow. This combination makes this a promising research collaboration as the rich research facilities and pioneer academics in the field will allow both additive Nano-fabrication and characterization to be developed in parallel and optimized for the applications that have been heavily investigated including solar panels for vehicles in collaboration with Economia Industry. 
This multidisciplinary research fits in 3 priority areas of Energy (by efficient energy generation/storage technologies, and minimising their size), Nanosciences (by developing novel 3D printable Nano-inks), and Climate Change (by developing bio-degradable solar panels and supercapacitors). The objectives are: 1) developing photosensitizer, luminescent graphene-based 3D printable nanoinks for DSSC and supercapacitors, with low cost and improved performance, 2) to characterize and optimize the developed nanoinks to meet the design requirements, and 3) improving manufacturability and implementing the nanoinks in the DSSC and miniature supercapacitor, for application tailored performance.
This research will drive forward the industrial application of nanomaterials and 3D printing techniques for energy applications by creating protocols for DSSC along with miniature solar-powered supercapacitors that can be adhered onto a wide variety of applications. In this project the industry of Economia at Pakistan will collaborate to implement developed graphene-based solar panels to power a vehicle, and a toilet block in girls’ school in a remote area with no access to electricity. The outcomes will also be disseminated with potential UK based industries who might benefit.

Recent progress in functional nanomaterials coupled with advanced printing fabrication techniques have opened up possibilities for the development of cost-efficient, solution-processed printed electronic device. The advancements in conducting, semiconducting and dielectric nanoparticle inks can be used to create multi-functional electronic circuit and devices that are flexible, light-weight and with very low carbon footprint. 
This project will exploit, the extraordinary properties of graphene based RE-doped nano-inks for a flexible miniature solar-powered supercapacitor as multifunctional structural components. We will, develop a nano-ink for scalable and tunable electrodes, with improved conductivity and connectivity, as well as efficiently. The findings will pave a practical route toward the design of future self-powered solar based vehicles, affording favorable safety, long life, and high energy.
This cross-disciplinary work will bring together research active academics, in leading edge chemistry, materials and electrical sciences, in different universities. It will exploit the material manufacture and testing equipment in Pakistan, world-class and wide-ranging synthetic and Nanofabrication and electronic facilities at the James Watt School of engineering, Glasgow. This combination makes this a promising research collaboration as the rich research facilities and pioneer academics in the field will allow both additive Nano-fabrication and characterization to be developed in parallel and optimized for the applications that have been heavily investigated including solar panels for vehicles in collaboration with Economia Industry. 
This multidisciplinary research fits in 3 priority areas of Energy (by efficient energy generation/storage technologies, and minimising their size), Nanosciences (by developing novel 3D printable Nano-inks), and Climate Change (by developing bio-degradable solar panels and supercapacitors). The objectives are: 1) developing photosensitizer, luminescent graphene-based 3D printable nanoinks for DSSC and supercapacitors, with low cost and improved performance, 2) to characterize and optimize the developed nanoinks to meet the design requirements, and 3) improving manufacturability and implementing the nanoinks in the DSSC and miniature supercapacitor, for application tailored performance.
This research will drive forward the industrial application of nanomaterials and 3D printing techniques for energy applications by creating protocols for DSSC along with miniature solar-powered supercapacitors that can be adhered onto a wide variety of applications. In this project the industry of Economia at Pakistan will collaborate to implement developed graphene-based solar panels to power a vehicle, and a toilet block in girls’ school in a remote area with no access to electricity. The outcomes will also be disseminated with potential UK based industries who might benefit.

data.projectName: Intent-driven Intelligent Automated Management and Orchestration Guaranteeing Security, Trust and Performance in 5G  (NINA)
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
NINA  aims to develop, demonstrate and evaluate an open and secure 5G communication framework addressing the need for trustworthy end-to-end performance guarantees at design time, and for inter- and intra- slice monitoring and autonomic network management and configuration at runtime. The developed solution will feature open APIs for the dynamic provision of AI-driven: (a) intent-driven, policy-based end-to-end secure traffic steering; (b) adaptive massive-scale network slicing for massive Machine Type Communications environments; and (c) core network service provision assurances via predictive resource auto-scaling. To guarantee the needed trust between tenants, host systems and service applications, the framework will employ different levels of security abstractions and performance indicators that will enable the design-time verification and the runtime validation of the required Security, Trust and Performance properties, also considering the satisfaction of predefined KPIs covering heterogeneous Proof of Concept scenarios. NINA vision in delivering intent-driven intelligent automated management and orchestration is based on two key features:

Intent-driven policy-based design patterns: provide an intent policy-based approach to enable the definition and creation of slicing policies at different levels of the 5G architecture, powered by AI reasoning.

Autonomic network management based on machine learning: provide runtime adaptation based on an intra- and inter -layer monitoring mechanism powered by AI.
