data.projectName: High energy density lead free ceramic capacitors for power pulsed applications at high temperatures
data.projectDigest:
With the deficit of energy sources and anthropogenic climate change along with the accelerating progress of industrialization, a difficult problem exists that necessitates exploration for sustainable, prosperous, and secure energy from renewable energy resources such as solar, wind and geothermal to meet the industrial and social demands. As a result, environmentally friendly and low-cost energy-storage devices are in high demand to store and controller this energy. 
Compared to batteries and electrochemical capacitors, dielectric capacitors always possess ultrahigh power density and fast charge–discharge capability, playing a crucial role in advanced pulsed power systems such as hybrid electric vehicles, high voltage pulsed-power circuits and kinetic energy weapons. The dielectric capacitor can be based either on polymer or ceramics. Polymer based capacitors have high dielectric breakdown strength (DBS) but they have low melting temperatures and often experience thermal destruction after quick charge–discharge cycling. This makes them only suitable for use in low temperature environments (<100 °C). On the other hand, ceramics not only possess high dielectric constants and relatively high energy densities, but can also sustain long term performance at higher operating temperatures. Moreover, the low dielectric losses and fast charge-discharge response of ceramic add to their superiority over polymer for energy storage applications. The lack of new, high DBS, low loss, dielectric materials, however, is a limiting factor in the miniaturization and modularizing of modern power electronics.

In this project, lead free dielectric materials in the Bi(MIMII)O3-(Ba,Sr)TiO3 system will be designed and investigated with the intention of developing a range of of high temperature (250?), low loss and high DBS ceramics and multilayers. Specifically, the project will address: i) development of new bismuth-based lead free perovskite ferroelectrics, in the Bi(MI,MII) O3-(Ba,Sr)TiO3 system; ii) the investigation of breakdown strength in the proposed materials, based on their electrical and physical microstructure; ii) improvement of dielectric breakdown strength though  optimizing microstructure and defect chemistry; iv) fabrication of multilayer prototype capacitors with high energy storage density (>15 J/cm3) for operation at elevated temperatures (~250 ?). The developed capacitors will not only be candidates for use in electrical vehicles but also in well logging and power electronics. 

Bulk samples will be prepared and characterized for energy density at the university of Science and Technology Bannu Pakisan. After achieving high energy densities in the bulk material, multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCC) will be designed and fabricated at the University of Sheffield, United Kingdom through exchange of PhD and post-doctoral fellows.

data.projectName: Urban Design as a tool for achieving Urban Resilience, facilitating the delivery of better cities.
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Through this research it is planned that urban design studios will be run in parallel between Oxford Brookes University in Oxford, UK and NED University in Karachi, in which a section of the city of Karachi, Pakistan will be taken as a case study area, and research methods will be developed to document and analyse an urban area, and to propose urban design solutions. Keeping in view different theoretical frameworks will be developed, that connect with the global south, in terms of literature and methodology. Another objective of this research would be to learn through the exchange of knowledge between urban design studio in Oxford Brookes and NED University, researching on how global and local technologies for urban design documentation and analysis can be developed and put to use.  Liaison with the Urban Policy and Strategic Planning Unit in Sindh will also be developed. The Director of this Department has already been approached, and the possibility of feeding the design outcomes into real life urban design projects have been discussed. Furthermore, another collaboration with a Belgium based startup has been established, that has developed a software called H.A.R.D., which is a simple and affordable tool that allows cities and citizens to use their knowledge and work together in preparing for, responding to and recovering from disasters in a fast, collaborative, transparent and technically-sound manner.

data.projectName: Internet of things (IoT) enabled Ambient Air Pollution Monitoring and Prediction System
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: This interdisciplinary project between UK leading Universities and National University of Science and Technology (Pakistan), non-academic Partners (Semphos-Ltd, UK, working on development of IoT applications for smart cities) and Policy makers (Planning commission, Pakistan) is geared towards the development of a low cost Internet-of-Things (IoT) platform for monitoring and prediction of air pollution in dense urban area of Pakistan. The lack of technological solutions for monitoring and prediction of air quality can mainly be attributed to the cost of such platform and lack of technical skills in policy making organizations for running and maintaining such solutions. Our proposed solution aims to significantly lower the monitoring cost by exploiting (a) a clean slate design of IoT nodes based on low cost embedded systems and wireless communication platform; (b) by reducing the fixed infrastructure maintenance and operation cost by harnessing mobility of IoT sensor nodes. We aim to build spatio-temporal map for the dynamics of urban air pollution which will be shared publically on a web portal. The identification of pollution propagative areas will help us to detect the prevailing respiratory diseases in the region and key factors in increasing the spread of these diseases. The related data will be collected from surrounding hospitals and further related analytics will help to propose remedial measures to government to quarantine the pollution sources in identified areas.

data.projectName: Energy (generation, distribution and conservation)
data.projectDigest:
This adventurous collaborative research programme will combine computational simulation and experimental fabrication strategy to design and develop two-dimensional (2D) nanomaterials-based photocathode and photoanode for artificial photosynthetic (AP) water splitting for solar fuel production (H2).  The novelty of this project lies on (i) design and synthesis of two-dimensional (2D) Metal Ferrite based pair of photocathodes and photoanode with aligned band structure for spontaneous water splitting, (ii) development of cost effective nanoarchitecture controlled fabrication methodology and (iii) performance enhancement by nanoarchitecture and surface modification. The rationally designed highly efficient photoelectrodes will make it possible to generate solar fuel (hydrogen) for sustainable energy and environment.  Our vision is to undertake an ambitious research programme to investigate two-dimensional (2D) Metal Ferrite with structural formula ABO2, ABO3 ABO4 and AB2O4 (where A= transition, post-transition metals and lanthanoids while B=Fe) for solar energy conversion. 
The ultimate aim of this ambitious collaborative project is to develop an efficient and sustainable prototype device for zero emission solar to chemical fuel (Hydrogen) production. The multidisciplinary approach will offer in-depth understandings of exploring new semiconductor materials for AP device. The Techniques developed not only used for H2 production but can be adopted for CO2 photoreduction, photocatalysis and thermoelectric devices.

data.projectName: Climate migrants, mobility and governance across emergent political and policy terrains in Sindh Executive summary
data.projectDigest: Over 36 months the project will put climate change and migration at the centre of a major new interdisciplinary and comparative study of climate-human-infrastructure interactions in Pakistan’s most environmentally precarious region. To this end it will study climate change migration in three affected locations in Sindh: In Thatta, where rural to urban migrations (towards Karachi) have created ‘’left behind’ communities; in Thar, where  long-standing rural to urban migrations due to drought, variable rainfall and food shortages are being reversed by return migrations due to CPEC-backed coal mining and energy projects; in Karachi’s agrarian periphery, where the nexus of migrant settlements, land reclamations and urban expansion are producing a highly mobile situation. In addition, the study addresses a need for climate change research and applications - which have developed successful innovations and inventions in regard to biophysical aspects - to also examine the social, cultural, political and urban processes involved in more depth. Therefore, it will combine development experts, anthropologists, political economists, urbanisation and urban planning experts, experts on governance, and climate change media and communication. It will consolidate long-term partnerships between the University of Brighton, the Institute of Business Administration, USAID and the UNDP (Islamabad), the Ministry of Climate Change, local government agencies, NGOs, community organisations, social and legal activists, environmental journalists and an international expert advisory board. It will host a series of activities designed to build and strengthen sustainable networks, pathways of knowledge exchange and production, and to develop a comparative, multi-year, multi-sited mixed-methods strategy for mapping, research, and improving sustainable responses to climate change impacts in Pakistan. It will communicate findings through a project website, media communications and curricula. It will build educational capacity through the creation of doctoral and post-doctoral fellowships, the training of research assistants, and the co-development of shared curricula

data.projectName: NANO-TREAT- Synthesis and application of novel nano composites for the removal of emerging contaminants from drinking water
data.projectDigest:
The overall strategic aim of this proposal is to establish a multi-institutional innovative collaborative research partnership to develop cutting edge low cost drinking water tertiary treatments based on novel syntheses of nanocomposites to specifically remove emerging contaminants, ECs (e.g. pharmaceuticals/antibiotics, pesticides pesticides). 
The unchecked “off the shelf” availability and extensive use of antibiotics in health and pesticides in agriculture sectors is a common practice in Pakistan. These ECs and their metabolites through municipal wastewater, mostly discharged with partial or without treatment, and surface runoff cause heavy contamination of water supply sources. The conventional water treatment processes are not capable of capturing ECs and the existing sophisticated treatments are expensive and energy intensive and require well trained skilled operators, normally not available in the developing countries including Pakistan. The optimization and application of nano-adsorbents to treat contaminants of complex structures is an emerging area that can potentially yield greener and cheaper treatment innovations capable of delivering safer drinking water and improved health and socio-economic progress.

data.projectName: Nano water splitting: a roadmap for turning nonprecious materials into precious materials
data.projectDigest: The aim of this project is to investigate the mechanisms for overcoming the poor efficiency, stability and durability of 3-d transition metal oxides in water splitting as they are not fully understood. The first work package (WP) will be experimental testing of various conducting polymers with 3-d transition metal oxides by physical methods in order to identify the most efficient conducting polymer-metal oxide protocols in water splitting. Among the conjugated conducting polymers poly(pyrrole) (PPy), polyaniline (PANI), and Poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT) will be investigated in water splitting systematically using optimum approach. In second WP, the chemical method will be adapted to synthesize nanocomposites of conducing polymers-metal oxide then their structural and composition characterization will be carried out. Then water splitting will be evaluated with optimum ratio of conducting polymer-metal oxide in the nanocomposite. In third WP, the core shell structure will be developed with optimum thickness of core and shell in order to investigate the catalytic activity at quantum level which can lead to efficient, stable and durable nonprecious catalysts for water splitting in alkaline media.  Also,  the optimized catalysts will be capitalized into working water splitting devices and the efficiency will be monitored by gas chromatography. By optimizing these nonprecious nanocomposites for efficient water splitting will strengthen the renewable energy reservoirs, thereby it will bring more sustainable and environment friendly society with minimum global warming effect.

data.projectName: Adolescent Sexual and Reproductive Health Education: Designing an evidence based intervention programme for schools and colleges in Rawalpindi, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The current proposal under the thematic area of Medical and Allied Health Sciences aims to highlight the existing gaps in the teaching of reproductive health issues to adolescents in Pakistan and to identify possible barriers to tackle this vital issue within the Pakistani communities. This study will be instrumental in laying the basis for working towards community (School) based intervention needed for the promotion of reproductive health awareness and education programmes in Pakistan and how the key stakeholders: adolescents, their parents and teachers can be involved in the process. This will be an intervention based research which will consist of collecting primary data and building a training programme based on the empirical evidence. The training will be delivered to teachers who are identified as the key influencers for the youth. Integration of the Life skills based education (LSBE) components within school curriculum will be a step towards formulating a national plan of action in the future. . Finally, the current study aims to present an evidence based report to the ministry of education which can become a guiding document for policy formulation.

data.projectName: Structure-guided development of small molecule degraders for treatment-resistant genotype 3a hepatitis C virus (HCV)
data.projectDigest:
In Pakistan, hepatitis C virus (HCV) is a major healthcare problem, with infections, acute and chronic alike, responsible for liver damage, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. HCV genotype 3a prevalence is the highest of all genotypes (64%).  This causes the problem in therapeutic management of HCV in Pakistan, as HCV genotype 3a is less responsive to direct-acting antiviral drugs (DAAs). To effectively tackle it, novel therapeutic strategies designed to target specifically HCV genotype 3a, are needed.  
	Targeted protein degradation has recently emerged as a promising approach with several potential advantages relative to traditional occupancy-driven pharmacology. The initial proof of concept for targeted protein degradation (PROTAC) as an antiviral strategy to manage HCV infection has been done using genotype 1 NS3/4A protease as a well-validated HCV target.
Overall, our project is expected to validate targeted small molecule PROTACs as a new paradigm for the development of antivirals with superior resistance profiles. The project is aligned with the Medical and Allied Health Sciences priority thematic area. Our proposed study will explore the targeted protein degradation as an innovative strategy to tackle infections with the strain that remains refractory to the treatment with state-of-the-arts DAAs, which prevails in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Device Development and a Pilot Trial of Transcutaneous Vagus Nerve Stimulation for Upper Limb Rehabilitation following a Stroke
data.projectDigest:
Recent studies suggest that Vagal nerve stimulation (VNS) enhances recovery from stroke. Previous studies uused invasive VNS which requires surgery to the chest and neck for insertion of the stimulator and is associated with considerable expense and would be difficult to adopt widely even in high income countries. An alternative and attractive approach is non-invasive VNS which is achieved by stimulation of a branch of the vagus nerve at the ear.  A pilot study from the team in Sheffield has shown that this approach is feasible, well tolerated and may also be effective in improving upper limb recovery after stroke. 
We propose the development of a smart wrist band which would detect initiation of movement of the affected limb and by Bluetooth would activate that stimulator so that stimulation of the vagus nerve at the ear can occur. The smart wrist band will have the ability to record the extent of stimulation and would also measure improvements in the quality of the movement of the affected limb. After development, the initial testing of the device for feasibility and acceptability in a pilot human study will occur at AKU in Pakistan over 18 months. This device has potential for use in other neurological conditions.

The smart wrist band will have the ability to record the extent of stimulation and would also measure improvements in the quality of the movement of the affected limb. After development, the initial testing of the device for feasibility and acceptability in a pilot human study will occur at AKU in Pakistan over 18 months. This device has potential for use in other neurological conditions.

data.projectName: Development of bacteriophages equipped with CRISPR-Cas9 machinery to target the carbapenemase producing P. aeruginosa: a novel approach to control antibiotic resistance
data.projectDigest: The problem of antibiotic resistance is affecting human and veterinary medicine, as well as food safety. In certain situations, the infections caused by antibiotic resistant pathogens are difficult to treat due to unavailability of drugs. The need for novel, effective and affordable alternatives to traditional antibiotics is abundantly clear. The genetic elements of pathogens mainly responsible for resistance against antibiotics are located on plasmid or bacterial chromosome. The discovery of Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR) Case system, a defense mechanism present in certain bacteria against foreign DNA, opens new horizons for genome editing. The Cas9, a counter part of the CRISPR/Cas9 system having helicase and endonuclease domains is the key enzyme used for targeted genome editing. The CRISPR/Cas9 system is reported to efficiently perform genome editing, starting from mammals to small animals, in plants and even in bacteria and archaea. Aim of the current project is to develop CRISPR equipped lysogenic bacteriophage going to target carbapenem resistant P. aeruginosa (CRPA) to make them antibiotic sensitive. The developed lysogenic bacteriophage will also be tuned to target key genomic portion of characterized lytic bacteriophages against P. aeruginosa. The targeted P. aeruginosa population will be infected first by the developed lysogenic bacteriophage followed by the lytic bacteriophage(s) against which the lysogenic bacteriophage was tuned. It will lead to infection by lysogenic bacteriophages to majority of population, while the lytic bacteriophages will only infect P. aeruginosa cells un-infected by modified developed lysogenic bacteriophage. This will result in conversion of carbapenem resistant P. aeruginosa population into sensitive. After optimizing the CRISPR-Case system, against carbapenem, we can target the resistance against other classes of antibiotics. This shall eliminate the antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes from the environment so the infections can be cured with available antibiotics, as well as this modality can also be used to treat infections along with antibiotics.

data.projectName: A Socio-Technical Framework for Augmented Participatory Sensing: Provisioning Citizen Centric Initiatives in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Developing countries like Pakistan have adopted the approach to selectively target problem hotspots to find ‘technology-smart’ solutions to local problems. Smartness from the perspective of developing countries is inclined towards driving community based initiatives for the exploitation of technology to address local problems. To fully exploit the benefits of these solutions, there is a growing need for a socio-technological framework to enable efficient information sharing and problem solving for citizen driven initiatives. In this project we propose a clean slate human-centred design for participatory sensing methods. From technological perspective, we aim to: (i) augment the design space of participatory methods with bespoke low cost internet-of-things (IoT) passive/active sensing solutions; and (ii) exploit digital disparity. From design and social sciences perspective, we aim to explore mechanism design methods to understand the determinants which will motivate people with superior digital capability to provide sensing as a service to those who are deprived. We particularly focus on the critical issues of human trafficking and child kidnapping for our case study.

data.projectName: The Fourth Industrial Revolution: Business Strategies and the Role of Higher Education
data.projectDigest: The change in nature of work is around the corner due to tremendous revolution in information technology and related fields. The evolution of artificial intelligence and big data will have dramatic impact on work, society and role of education. Businesses need to understand big data capabilities, universities need to accept the challenge and policy makers must ensure that the society is ready to embrace the disruption. Big data and AI revolutions are not just about technical sophistication: it has equal  importance for other factors, such as human skills, organizational culture, educational and societal readiness. Gaining data-generated insights are becoming important in today’s business environment; however, despite the interest and emphasis on big data and AI, how organizations and societies can actually reap the benefits of these new technologies remains unclear, highlighting the need to better understand how the structure of businesses and their interplay with other societal institutions

data.projectName: Biosensors for the early stage cancer detection
data.projectDigest:
Cancer is currently one of the leading causes of mortality and morbidity worldwide. According to WHO, cancer is diagnosed in around 11 million people every year and the number would increase to 16 million by 2020. The delayed and complicated diagnostic process is one of the main reason for high mortality due to cancers. The conventional technologies for cancer detection rely on the subjective judgment and expertise of skilled personnel. Cancer diagnosis via biopsy and CT scan is uncomfortable, expensive and could produce false negative rate and is not promising for early diagnosis. 
Biosensors based on the cancer biomarkers could be the solution to this challenging problem. The early cancer diagnosis will be a revolutionary and could save many lives and resources. It is a low cost, fast and efficient technique. On this challenging and demanding multidisciplinary research area, we propose a consortium of Pakistani and U.K. Physicist, biologist and biochemists that will work together on the cancer biosensors. The biomarker Smyd2 (involved in 14 types of cancers)  is very novel and is recently discovered. By making biosensors that will detect this novel biomarker will enable us detecting various cancer on a single biosensor even in their early stage.

data.projectName: Computational and Lidar-based Inter-Farm Wake Interaction Analysis to Quantify Wind and Energy Deficit in a Utility-Scale Wind Farm based in Jhimpir Wind Corridor from a Repowering Perspective
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Wind energy generation has experienced rapid growth in Pakistan with the addition of more than 1 GW of installed capacity over the last decade. The Renewable Energy Policy of 2006 set a target of injecting 9700 MW of renewable capacity in the national energy mix by 2030. Jhimpir, a region located in Sindh province of Pakistan, is one of the best wind energy sites in the country with over twenty operational wind farms and more in various stages of development. Due to limitations in the land available to install wind farms, wakes from an upstream farm reduce the power generation of downstream farms. The proposed research project will address this important issue, and thus targets the funding priority thematic area of “Energy”. This research work will be the first of its kind in Pakistan where the speed and power deficit of individual wind turbines in a commercial-scale wind farm influenced by upstream farms wake will be quantified. Identification of wind turbines with the highest power drop in the case study wind farm due to intra- and inter-farm wake interaction will assist in developing a holistic repowering strategy for wind farms resulting in improved Annual Energy Production (AEP).

data.projectName: Functional Characterization and Discovery of Novel Natural Inhibitors of hENT1
data.projectDigest:
Medical and allied health sciences have been identified as a Priority Area of HEC and the British Council. Our proposed research addresses Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC), which is one of the most lethal cancers with very few treatments available. For many decades, the only treatment has been the chemotherapy drug gemcitabine. However, this has relatively low efficacy. Each year more than 340,000 people die of the disease. Some reports project an over twofold increase in the number of PDAC deaths by 2030. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop novel drugs that can improve survival rates. 
Recently, the first crystal structure of the human equilibrative nucleoside transporter 1 (hENT1) has been resolved. We will identify new lead compounds that bind to this receptor that could act as a starting point for drug development. With a unique international collaboration between Karachi University and Leeds, we will be in a position to identify a potent natural inhibitor from Pakistani natural library compounds by combining computational (Harris group) and experimental structural biology expertise (Goldman group). We will also develop new computational tools that will help us gain a deeper understanding of the structure and dynamics of membrane bound transporters.

data.projectName: Chemical looping gasification of waste to syngas for electricity (solid oxide fuel cell), synthetic natural gas and dimethyl ether/methanol liquid fuels production production
data.projectDigest: Practical innovative solutions are essential for developing countries to address the needs of its societies. These solutions play a vital role in setting up appropriate and effective social and environmental policies too. Pakistan’s pressing need is to alter the course of dependence on imported fuels alongside conservation of the environment for present/future population. The proposed project is in line with the sensible need of finding practical solutions to utilise domestic/industrial wastes for electricity, cooking and liquid fuel production. The approach is also focused on reducing the cost and improving energy efficiency as well as reducing toxic/CO2 emissions with reliable power generation in an energy mix that will have significant intermittency from renewables such as wind and solar. This research will make a considerable contribution to the current body of knowledge on waste utilisation for greener, and more efficient power generation, especially with cyclic and flexible operating conditions. This includes detailed knowledge and in-depth understanding of the fundamental behaviours of waste, its gasification in an oxygen controlled environment with economically derived indigenous catalysts to produce synthetic gas. In short amongst the available technologies the benefit associated with the evolving drives for off-grid solutions from wastes to produce energy can’t be overlooked.

data.projectName: Climate Change – Environmental Health Nexus and Infrastructure  Development in Himalayan, Karakoram and HinduKush (HKH) Region, Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Climate Change is an inevitable and global challenge. Its impacts are forecasted to be more extreme in the fragile mountain ecosystems like Hindukush Karakoram Himalaya (HKH) region of Pakistan, resulting in broad implications for ecosystem services and livelihoods. Ever increasing sources of air pollutants emissions within HKH-Pakistan and adjacent regions are a major concern. Specifically, the likely changing emission scenarios due to the existing infrastructure development in HKH-Pakistan (Pak-China Economic Corridor and Hydropower) and their effects on the region’s cryosphere are unclear. This study will embrace quantitative and qualitative (measurements and modelling) spatio-temporal analysis of what is the existing sate of air pollutants emissions and ecosystems in the region and in what ways climate change can have local and regional societal implications (e.g. habitat and biodiversity loss, environmental health and food security ).The proposal will be comprised of integrated work on:
•	Physio-chemical and biological characterization of air pollutant emission 
•	Characterization of Environmental Sensitive Sites and Biodiversity Hotspots
•	Analysis and Modelling
•	Mitigation and Adaptation Measures
The resulting knowledge about atmospheric emission, biodiversity, livelihood/food security and climate change inter-relationships will deliver the scientific underpinning to inform local (Pakistan) as well as regional mitigation strategies to anticipate and prepare for climate change impacts.

data.projectName: Experimental and Numerical Analysis of Novel Elastic Copper Indium Gallium Diselenide (CIGS) Thin Film Solar Cell
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Copper indium gallium diselenide (CIGS) thin film solar cell has been identified as the future material for thin film photovoltaics applications. However, the fabrication cost still remains a challenge. The proposed research effort mainly focuses on studying the effect of removing the thin buffer layer of cadmium sulfide (CdS) from the overall device structure as it is an expensive and toxic material and also adds to the fabrication cost of the device, and secondly the effect of introducing sodium in the fabrication of the proposed CIGS solar cell. Sodium can be added in the substrate material during substrate preparation and it can also be added as a doping material during the synthesis of CIGS nanoparticles. The suggested steps will not only bring down the overall cost of the device but will also be able to simplify the fabrication procedure. It is to be noted that the presence of sodium is found to increase the cell efficiency. It is also important to note that the above-mentioned scheme of adding sodium to the device and the removal of CdS buffer layer makes the proposed solar cell synthesis procedure novel and innovative as compared to the past researches.

data.projectName: Development of nanostructured coatings/claddings using thermal deposition technology
data.projectDigest: Nanostructured materials can offer unique and superior mechanical properties such as high hardness, strength, corrosion and wear resistance compared to the normal microstructured materials commonly used in engineering. Therefore, this capability has made nanostructured materials of considerable interest world-wide. However, the challenge remains of how to successfully manufacture a nanostructured material to a reasonable size without losing the nanostructure during manufacture. One avenue which has considerable potential for success is the use of thermal spraying techniques to deposit nanostructured coatings onto component surfaces. This research concerns the development of thick nanostructured cermet coatings and cladding using novel “engineered” nanostructured powders which have been designed with the ability to maintain its nanostructure during the thermal deposition process. This research will produce ceramic/metal coatings based on WC-Co-Cr-Ni-Al2O3 system and these coatings will offer a three-fold increase in surface hardness, corrosion and wear resistance. The development of the next generation of advanced nanostructured surface coatings with superior mechanical properties offers enhanced production performance, efficiency and competitiveness to all industries concerned with erosive-corrosive degeneration of component surfaces such as in power plants, petrochemical plants, agricultural tools (and sugar processing machinery in mills).

data.projectName: IoT-Cloud Analytics using machine learning for climate change impact on agriculture

The Lab shall act as a hub of many academic and industry partners and target six goals, namely: Technology Commercialization and Licensing, Knowledge Contribution, Workforce Training and Development, High-Valued Shared Services, Data Repository and, last but not the least, Sustainable Economic Growth. Such techniques can not only attain extremely accurate data, (e.g. Determining which segments of a crop field require immediate irrigation) and generate repositories but can also efficiently deliver the benefits down towards the masses.

data.projectName: Benchmarking honey industry for food security, sustainable rural livelihood and economic growth: Exploration of rangelands potentials
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
Beekeeping is sustainable source of livelihood and the improvement of social life of rural communities. Pakistan produces quality honey which is sold out locally and very small quantity is exported to gulf countries; however, due to low quality in terms of data deficient about nutritional value and medicinal properties, our honey could not reach in most of the international markets. Honey composition is affected by various factors, including bee species, the plant from which the nectar collected (specific for each season), geographical area, harvesting process and storage conditions. By producing high quality honey from Pakistani origin, we may enhance our export values, food security and poverty alleviation through technology transfer and training manpower. So this project aimed for:
(1) Determining native and exotic honey bees for the production of high quantity and quality honey
(2) Characterization of the Botanical and Geographical Origin of Honey:  Identifying the nectar potential, flowering phenology, seasonal floral calendar, nectar dynamics, pollen study of native species 
(3) Identification of chemical composition and quality control of honey; Sensory, physicochemical and functional attributes 
(5) Assessment of antioxidant, antimicrobial activities in compliance of international standards. 
(6) Detection of any agrochemical pollution and veterinary residues.
(7) Training of trainers about Good Beekeeping Practices (GBP)

data.projectSummary:
Beekeeping is sustainable source of livelihood and the improvement of social life of rural communities. Pakistan produces quality honey which is sold out locally and very small quantity is exported to gulf countries; however, due to low quality in terms of data deficient about nutritional value and medicinal properties, our honey could not reach in most of the international markets. Honey composition is affected by various factors, including bee species, the plant from which the nectar collected (specific for each season), geographical area, harvesting process and storage conditions. By producing high quality honey from Pakistani origin, we may enhance our export values, food security and poverty alleviation through technology transfer and training manpower. So this project aimed for:
(1) Determining native and exotic honey bees for the production of high quantity and quality honey
(2) Characterization of the Botanical and Geographical Origin of Honey:  Identifying the nectar potential, flowering phenology, seasonal floral calendar, nectar dynamics, pollen study of native species 
(3) Identification of chemical composition and quality control of honey; Sensory, physicochemical and functional attributes 
(5) Assessment of antioxidant, antimicrobial activities in compliance of international standards. 
(6) Detection of any agrochemical pollution and veterinary residues.
(7) Training of trainers about Good Beekeeping Practices (GBP)
(8) GBP education for young students, women, disabled peoples

data.projectName: Health Impacts of Unsustainable Transport System
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Travel through private transport modes result in the lower activity level of commuters, which contributes to health issues such as diabetes and cardiovascular diseases. Pakistan is ranked at 4th position among the countries with the highest number of diabetic patients having 17.1% of the adults with diabetes. By encouraging the active modes of transport, the risk of various diseases such as diabetes and cardiovascular diseases can be reduced, along with overall health improvement of public.
This study will examine the effect of transport mode choice on activity level and health and well-being of commuters. The transport system, activity level of commuters, air quality, respiratory health and well-being of commuters in Karachi and Lahore will be evaluated and compared. Furthermore, the existing transport system of two mega-cities of Pakistan (Karachi and Lahore) will be evaluated on the parameters of sustainable transportation to develop a data-driven policy framework that transforms the existing system into a sustainable transport system by integrating the recently launched and upcoming mega projects. 
Extensive data about existing mode share of commuters and vehicles share will be collected in Karachi and Lahore. Commuters using three existing main modes of transport (car, motorbikes and public transport) in Karachi and Lahore will be selected (600 for each mode). The activity level and travel diaries of the selected participants will be recorded using a health band and mobile application. The blood samples of participants will be collected for examination of health and well-being parameters. Furthermore, the air quality in selected cities, exposure of commuters to the environment, and their respiratory health will also be examined.

data.projectName: Digitizing the Rural Communities through Solar Energy-Driven IT Educational Hubs in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Gilgit-Baltistan: A Randomized Controlled Experiment
data.projectDigest: This proposed project is aimed at achieving the two important goals of sustainable development goals i.e affordable renewable energy and basic IT education, through a randomized controlled experiment in the rural villages of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) and Gilgit Baltistan provinces, Pakistan.  This project is motivated by the large number of households in far flung rural areas of KP province where lack of electricity supply is strongly coincided with lack of basic computer literacy and education. Since the future generation is bracing for the challenge of access to IT education (towards digital Pakistan), therefore, provision of a basic electricity facility to the deprived villages is a precondition of computer related education.  For the purpose of research and rigorous impact evaluation of the project for future expansion, we initially propose the implementation of this project on randomized control trials basis.  In each randomly selected village of the far-flung KP and GB provinces, a dedicated computer-educational hub will be established that will be operated through solar energy panels.  The residents of the village will be provided with free electricity supply in the nighttime with a condition that they will ensure their children's participation in the daytime in the educational hubs. In addition, the proposed educational hubs are expected to facilitate the residents of the village in terms of internet connectivity for employment opportunities.

data.projectName: Assessment of current and future ozone and warming impacts on wheat production in Pakistan: Biotechnological approaches to control them
data.projectDigest: Wheat is an important staple food of Pakistan but its production per hectare is 2-3 times less than top wheat producing country like France and USA due to climate change huge negative impact on wheat production in Pakistan.  A number of studies estimated present-day crop losses due to O3 damage in the range of $1 to $3 billion in the U.S. and $2 billion in China. Moreover, wheat yield decreased 3–10% for every 1?C rise in atmospheric temperature and 15-20% reduction in wheat yield and grain quality is observed by increasing CO2 concentration, phytoplasma infection and salinity. However, in Pakistan, economic losses due to above mentioned factors have not been evaluated so far due to lack of study in this field of research.  Therefore, in this study, for the first time, we want to investigate the impact of current and future concentration of ozone,  warming, CO2, salinity and phytoplasma on growth, ecophysiology and genetics of wheat crop in Pakistan by forming the consortium of five different research Universities and Institutes from Abbottabad, Peshawar, Faisalabad, Bahawalpur and China  (4 National and 1 International) with the main objective to increase the yield of top wheat varieties in Pakistan through two main approaches; (i) chemical approaches, (ii) biotechnological approaches, so that our wheat production should be as much as in the developed countries like USA and France. In conclusion, this proposal will help in bringing the scientists from diverse disciplines together for improving the wheat production in Pakistan through counteracting the negative impact of climate change for sustainable agriculture as well as for feeding the large population of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Development and application of cost-effective and sustainable integrated technology for the treatment and reuse of wastewater
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: Pakistan Council of Research in Water Resources (PCRWR) has warned that Pakistan may run out of the water by 2025. The unlimited use of water and its discharge as a waste in the environment is one of the main reasons for the depletion of clean water resources in the country. This wasted water further deteriorates the quality of remaining drinking water resources, and contributes to 80% of all diseases, and 40% of death in the country. The traditional methods for wastewater treatment are not applicable in Pakistan due to their high capital, operational, and maintenance costs. Floating and constructed wetlands are highly suitable alternatives for effective wastewater reclamation that use plants and their associated microorganisms to treat wastewater. It is a low cost, self-sustaining and self-operating approach. In this project, a novel integrated wastewater treatment technology will be developed by incorporating the wetlands with anaerobic and sand filtration systems. The scientists from NIBGE Faisalabad, COMSATS Abbottabad, Quaid-e-Azam University Islamabad, Peshawar University Peshawar, Germany and Denmark will be involved in the development and application of the technology in the country to get required levels of treated water for its reuse in the same application or for agriculture.

data.projectName: Development of Photo-Rechargeable Lithium ion Batteries
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest:
Modern electronic devices increasingly demand for innovative technologies for energy generation and storage. Combining energy generation and storage in a single device is highly desirable as an efficient and portable energy source for portable electronic devices. Proposed project belongs to thematic area i.e. Energy (conversion, distribution and storage) of innovative and collaborative research grant and we are aiming to develop battery devices which will use sun light for charging as an autonomous power source for portable electronic devices. This research project will focus on the development of photo-active composite material while exploiting organic and inorganic materials for the development of photo-rechargeable battery. Generally for lithium ion battery, layered materials are used for lithium intercalation such as Titanium dioxide, Lithium titanate etc. Luckily materials used for lithium intercalation also demonstrate semiconducting and dielectric properties which could be used to charge lithium ion battery while using sunlight. Semiconducting properties of such materials will allow us to excite the electron from valance band to conduction band which could be exploited for lithium intercalation in such materials whereas dielectric properties will be used to scatter the light inside the electrode material of the battery for achieving maximum efficiency.
The research group at National Institute of Lasers and Optronics, Pakistan will focus on the development of layered semiconductor materials for lithium intercalation along with structural designing of materials for efficient light scattering inside electrode of the battery. The research group at Durham University will focus on the development of organic material for increasing electronic conductivity inside battery

data.projectName: Discovery of pyrimidine derivatives for therapeutic application in cardiovascular diseases
data.projectDigest: Cardiovascular diseases (CVD) being a non-communicable diseases have remained one of the leading causes of death throughout the world. According to World Health Organization about 600 million patients suffering from hypertension show that the incidence of hypertension exceeds more than 10% of the worldwide population. In Pakistan, incidence of hypertension is one in every four middle-aged adults. Despite various therapeutic interventions to control or treat hypertension, no individual clinical agent entirely serves the purpose. Patients often have to take multiple drugs, each of which targets various mediators responsible for high blood pressure. Therefore, there is dire need of novel agents that are more efficacious, economical with minimum side effects. The current project is planned to investigate effect of pyrimidine derivatives for their potential in cardiovascular diseases using in silico, in vitro, in vivo and molecular approaches. The development of new drugs will also have high impact on the research and development of local pharmaceutical industry. In the long term it will benefit country’s economy and industrial development. The outcome of this research will open new areas of research in field of pharmaceutical sciences and their best possible dosage forms such as nanoparticles and targeted delivery molecules.

data.projectName: The formation of human populations in Pakistan and its forensic applications
data.projectDigest: Genetic makeup of Pakistan’s various ethnic groups was forged by successive waves of immigration from Central Asia and South Asia since the end of the last Ice Age. Throughout its long ancient history, the Indus Valley has been known for welcoming different peoples, faiths and cultures. The Indus was a region where early human ancestors encountered soon after they left Africa between 50,000 to 70,000 years ago. Evidence of these early humans can be found throughout Pakist an today at Soan, Riwat, Makli Hill, Bajaur and Sanghao. Approximately 9000 years ago they began establishing cities such as Mehrgarh, which eventually expanded to represent the Harappan culture (Indus Valley Civilization) in 3000 BCE, rivaling the early city-states of Mesopotamia. Shortly after the fall of the Harappan civilization in 1500 BCE, a massive migration is said to have taken place from Eurasia to the Indus Valley, known today as the Aryan migration theory. This eventually led to the formation of the Vedic civilization by 1200 BCE. After 500 BCE, the Indus Valley would come under the influence of the Achaemenid Persians, Alexander’s Macedonian Empire, Greeks, Buddhists (Mauryans), Central Asians (Sycthians, White Huns), Mongols, Iranians, Arabs and Turks. It was through these various influences by which Pakistani ethnic groups would be forged into its multi ethnic society today. Harappans fused culturally with the Aryans, forming Indo Aryans and Indo Iranians, which today culminates in the native ethnic groups of Pakistan. Pakistanis are divided genetically into 11 major distinct groups: Baloch, Brahui, Burusho, Hazara, Kalash, Kashmiri, Makrani, Parsi, Pashton, Punjabi and Sindhi. The previous mtDNA studies showed that these ethnic groups share about 40% to 60% of their DNA with South Asian

data.projectName: Valorization of macro/micro algal species from coastal areas of Pakistan for various industrial applications (VALR-ALG-PK)
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: The prime focus of this project is commercial scale farming of specific macro/micro algal types as well as technology development/harvest of only those compounds (strain specific characteristic) that are in high demand in local and international market. Algae can grow in fresh, polluted, sea, or farm-wastewater with a potential to harvest high value co-products worth US$ 1 billion exports. The proposed project will benefit Pakistan and as well as technology enhancement for Industrial partner (Fauji Fertilizer Company, FFC) in terms of waste water/ polluted water utilization, and biomass production for high volume/value export. The project will initiate the collection of indigenous macro/micro algal species for searching the secondary metabolites (especially terpenoids, steroids, alkaloids and peptides) from the seaweeds and microalgae of coastal areas of Pakistan and to characterize and modify them to the stage of commercial products either microencapsulated one or in forms of hydrocolloids.

The scientific and technological advancement through the GCF shall bring the country into the new era of technologically emerging nations.

data.projectName: Renewable based sustainable power generation and chilling water production for air conditioning system
data.projectDigest:
Sustainable low-priced clean energy is an inevitable need of the country to overcome 	country's current energy crisis, environmental problems and to reduce dependence 	on imported fossil fuel which costs billions of dollars every year.
The electricity demand in Pakistan has increased rapidly in recent years. Mainly due to the rapid growth in air-conditioning and escalated use of electrical appliances in residential and commercial sectors. The International Institute of Refrigeration in Paris (IIF/ IIR) has estimated that approximately 45% of electricity produced is consumed by households and commercial buildings air-conditioning.
The deficiencies in electric power supply have implications in refrigeration and cooling availability especially in summer. During recent years research has aimed at the development of technologies that can offer reductions in energy consumption, peak electrical demand and energy costs without lowering the desired level of comfort.

Therefore, primary objective of this project is not only the production of clean energy but also help in reduction of energy consumed by air conditioning system that would be achieved by using chilled water for cooling the buildings.

The innovatively developed technology will solve energy supply on one end and decrease usage at the same time primarily for industry, commercial, large scale residential setups.

data.projectName: IGenomic studies and vaccine development against Dengue Virus
data.projectDigest: Dengue virus (DENV) infections disasterous epidemics are threat to economy and human health in pakistan since 1994. Mass expenses on surveillance, analysis and treatment of DENV infections has been born by our country. As vaccines against DENV infection are in its trial stage, therefore no vaccine is available against it. The treatment of DENV infection is costly and needs import of many drugs causing extra burden on foreign reserves. This economic burden and human health issue can be addressed in multiple ways. First exploration of botanical source effective against DENV infection for domestic, cheap and easily available source of treatment. Second, preparation and evaluation of synthetic derivatives of various compounds having efficacy against DENV infections so that these could be formulated and designed into a pharmaceutical dosage form for patients usage and for export purpose. Third, if vaccines are developed locally, these can be used for domestic use and for export purpose also. These three integrated activities will result in  increase export and ultimately boosting the economy of our country.

data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Provision of access to speedy and timely justice is the primary element of good governance. We need an efficient judicial system, which insures access to justice at low cost and within minimum possible time. However, the data related to judicial system of Pakistan show that 2 million cases were pending in courts by May 2020. One way of resolving this issue of pendency is implementation of conflict resolution outside courts, called Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR). ADR is considered peaceful and socially acceptable way of resolving conflicts globally. In this regard, National Assembly of Pakistan has passed a Bill in 2017 for implementing ADR system in the country. Likewise, government of Punjab also passed ADR Act in 2019. Yet, we do not find any empirical evidence that show the extent by which ADR system can decrease the burden of pendency on courts. This projects will assess the role of ADR in affecting this burden on courts. The project will also examine potential strengths and weaknesses of ADR system. Furthermore, it will provide government with an experimental guide on measures required for the implementation of successful ADR system throughout the country as per the mandate of ADR Act.

data.projectName: Development of Microbial Metabolites Based Lures for the Control of Fruit Flies
data.projectDigest: Horticultural fruit crops such as mango, citrus, peach and guava are currently facing huge losses mainly due to the infestation of two fruit fly species; Bactrocera zonata and B. dorsalis. These fruit flies have gained quite great importance due to their quarantine pest status, i.e., Pakistan cannot export fruits, if found infested by these species, to Europe and America. There is dire need to develop sustainable and ecological ways to protect fruit from flies so that good crop production could be obtained that lead to food security as well as earning of foreign exchange. In this proposed study, the microbes isolated from soil and rotten fruits/vegetables will be screened to produce volatile organic compounds (VOCs) that could be used to attract or repel the fruit flies in the field. VOCs produced by isolated microbial strains will be collected from their headspace through dynamic headspace collection on Porapak adsorbents. The identification and quantification of VOCs will be carried out by gas chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry (GC-MS). Microbial metabolites will be tested against laboratory reared and field fruit flies for their orientation behavior by using Y-tube olfactometer and electroantennograph detector. The microbes VOCs showing potent repelling or attracting activities against fruit flies will be scaled up by biotechnological techniques. The gene responsible for producing potent compounds will be identified and used to form recombinant protein that would be used to produce compounds on large scale from sustainable substrates. We are expected to find potent yeast and bacterial strains capable of producing bioactive compound for the control of fruit flies. Moreover, we shall also be able to produce bioactive compounds using genetic engineering.

data.projectName: Use of advanced genomics tools to re-boost cotton production under climate change scenario for sustainable economic growth of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Cotton is the major source of vegetable oil and textile fiber in Pakistan. Due to climate change, in cotton growing-provinces (Punjab and Sindh) of Pakistan, the seasonal temperature exceeds up to 45-50?C during the months of June and July. It is much higher than the optimum temperature for cotton production. At high temperature, greater evapo-transpiration leads to drought conditions. There is very rapid flower and boll shedding in cotton under these conditions leading to severe yield losses. These conditions also have negative affect on oil content and composition; and fiber quality. Successive negative growth rates of cotton production in Pakistan during recent years are attributed, mainly, to high temperature, drought and associated insect attack. The proposed project is designed with the objective to develop an elite advance line of cotton with good seed cotton yield; fiber quality; oil content and composition; insect tolerance under high temperature and drought conditions by using advanced genomics tools. It also aims at developing institutional capacity to solve grand challenges to crop production in shortest time for national sustained socio-economic development. Due to diverse nature, this project addresses multiple thematic areas i.e., Food Security; Sociology; Development Economics; and Climate Change and Environment.

data.projectName: Identification, Exploration, Comparison, Analysis, selection,development and road map for comercillization of Hydro-Kinetic Energy in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest:
Water current/hydrokinetic/in-stream turbines generate power from the kinetic energy of a flowing stream of water without the use of a dam or a barrage and can be installed in any water body with a flow velocity greater than 0.5 m/s. The energy flux from the water stream is dependent on density, cross-sectional area and velocity cubed. The best performance is achieved from smooth linear flow of water at high velocity. Because of low investment costs and lack of frequent maintenance, this technology is cost effective in comparison to other options. Throughout the globe different concepts have been developed to utilize power of water streams. The mini/max required flow characteristics of a river/canal stream vary for every concept. So, after comparison among these concepts, determination of potential turbine concept most suitable to our irrigation canals/rivers is required to be established. 
For this purpose, commercially available turbines based on different design concepts are proposed to be installed on the selected/available potential site for operation, comparison, and analysis to select the most suitable turbine for consistence optimum power output, accordingly. The structural design, optimization, performance efficiency, optimize manufacturing process and cost analysis of turbine will be carried out. This turbine will be developed locally after modification for mass production and installation in Pakistan to harness the available hydro kinetic potential.

data.projectName: Centre for Sustainable Energy Storage and Conversion Devices
data.projectDigest:
Human dependence on energy appliances is rising exponentially every day. The World Energy Council energy has alarmed that the present consumption of energy would be doubled by 2050. The global warming and other environmental repercussions are worsening due to increasing use of present energy devices. It is the need of the hour that researchers focus their attention on the development of sustainable and green energy resources. The lithium-ion batteries are, mainly, being used to meet the energy requirements of the society appearing in the form of electric vehicles, laptops, cell-phones, portable electronic devices, robots, etc. However, the lithium is not an environmentally friendly element and its resources are depleting rapidly. Moreover, for the development of the ‘Smart World,’ we need flexible, lightweight and more efficient energy resources but, unfortunately, the lithium-ion batteries do not fall in the word ‘Smart’. 
    In view of the above-mentioned facts, we are going to work on the development of sustainable and clean energy resources, i.e., next-generation batteries, supercapacitors, solar cells, and H2 production through biomass degradation as well as water-splitting. To implement this idea, we propose the establishment of the Centre for Sustainable Energy Storage and Conversion Devices: an extension of the Department of Physics, University of the Punjab, Lahore, where we are already working on the batteries and supercapacitors. We will work in collaboration with COMSATS, Lahore, RMIT University Australia, Beijing Institute of Technology, China, Leibniz University of Hannover, Germany and Department of Physics and Astronomy, University of Delaware, USA. This collaboration would be in terms of experimental and theoretical work.

data.projectName: Developing IoT Value-Chain Through Big-Data and AI Integration
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: The number of Internet of Things (IoT) devices are rapidly increasing worldwide. This increase directly translates into acquisition of tremendous amount of data from the physical, social as well as cyberspace data generating IoT platforms. The number of these devices is predicted to grow exponentially in the coming years, further increasing the volume of raw and heterogeneous data, thus requiring large amount of storage. In this backdrop, the recent initiative of ‘Digital Pakistan’, from the government that aims to revolutionize the technology horizon in the country and to provide digital solutions in the field of education, health, finance, agriculture, and innovation. Benefits from this digitization effort can only be reaped through the utilization of advanced technologies. Among these, IoT holds a significant role in shaping up of the modern societies.  This project proposal provides solution to the aforementioned challenge by making use of big data, machine learning, and artificial intelligence based techniques on data originating from IoT network. It will also be able to provide integration capabilities with various systems from public-private organizations to improve the productivity and efficiency of their services.

data.projectName: Digital preservation of Rock inscriptions, carvings, paintings and petroglyphs of the Bonn and Buddhist Civilizations in Baltistan.
data.projectDigest:
Exploration, documentation and digital preservation of rock carvings, inscriptions and painting  in Baltistan.

Baltistan also known as the Little Tibet in the northern part of Pakistan bordering with China and India, is the home of Zhang Zhung, Bonn and Buddhist Civilizations. The reminiscents of these civilizations and cultural heritage are scattered all around Baltistan in form of rock inscriptions, carvings, rock paintings, scripts, petroglyphs, symbols and monuments, the giant Tonpa/Buddha rock in Skardu seems the icon of this cultural heritage. Due to human actions, climate change and natural disasters, these antiquities are eroded, damaged and rapidly endangered. Around 150 sites with thousands of symbols bearing a treasure of historical records, stories, and messages are so far recorded. There are many more sites and objects yet to be recorded and preserved in detail. Digital preservation of these sites would be a great service to archeology, history, culture and civilization. The proposed project suggests full digitization of these antiquities/sites through 3-D modeling and GPS marking that can enable online access to real location and virtual tour of these sites through satellite imaging. The digital achieves will be preserved and made available at the University Digital Repository for researchers and scholars of archaeology and history. Researchers can also have virtual tour of these sites though hi-tech satellite images. In case of manageable small size high value artefacts, the project proposes replica models of the artifacts produced by 3-D printers. A project of preliminary documentation has been completed by BCDF, supervised by the PI as Chairperson of the Cultural Committee BCDF.

data.projectName: Digitalization of Energy Management Systems of Domestic Process Industries: An Integrated Framework for Securing Energy, Economy, and Environment
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Energy conservation opportunities in Pakistan are estimated to be five billion USD a year. Process industries have a substantial share in national energy consumption and equally high energy saving potentials if they adopt some integrated Energy Management System (EnMS). However, like the other developing countries, the energy management in process industries in Pakistan are mostly based on manual calculation and is not fully robust and integrated. Hence, a substantial amount of energy is lost which causes damage to the national economy, wastage of national resources, and adversely affects the environment. The applicants have developed a prototype of an automated EnMS for domestic process industries. The proposed project aims to implement the system into real industrial processes through technical support from the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) Pakistan, the National Energy Efficiency and Conservation Authority (NEECA), and the Lean Automation Company. International collaborators include Professor Patrik Thollander from Sweden and Professor Manabu Kano from Japan. The proposed system is first of its kind in the local market and will provide an easy and cheap solution to the local industries. In addition, the project will strengthen the industry-university liaison which boosts employability, industries confidence in local solutions/consultancy, and university ranking.

data.projectName: Development of An Optimal and Integrated Model for Utilization of Municipal Solid Waste (MSW)
data.projectDigest: Municipal solid waste (MSW) generation is becoming a significant problem, owing to increasing population. Currently, the major metropolitan cities of Pakistan, i.e., Karachi and Lahore, are generating huge amount of MSW, which is mainly landfilled. However, this massive landfilling may lead to serious environmental threats in terms of the release of greenhouse gas emissions and contamination of groundwater tables. Contrary to the conventional approaches of solid waste management, valorization of wastes into valuable fine chemicals and alternative fuel options is gaining interest with the time, particularly in the context environmental sustainability and improved energy efficiency. The present project is aimed at investigating the potential of valorization of locally generated MSW into valuable alternatives. The project will follow the determination of techno-economic and environmental viability of conventional thermochemical and biotechnological conversion of MSW into a variety of chemicals and fuels options. The outcomes of the comparison will be translated into an optimal and integrated model for the best and efficient utilization of local MSW. Eventually, a feasibility study will be prepared for the authorities to implement the model at pilot scale.

data.projectName: Red go Green: An Awareness Campaign to Shape Waste Reduction Behavior and Menstrual Hygiene Management among Young Females (A longitudinal Experimental Intervention Study)
data.projectDigest: Customer waste management (CWM) has become an epidemic as it represents a noteworthy proportion of solid waste management. CWM has got the attention of academics, policy makers and institutes as it has ramifications for economy, environment and well-being of citizens. The way how products became waste depends upon the awareness and consumptions practices of customers. There is a lack of consumer awareness towards CWM which arose the concerns for environment, health, education and potential for innovative product. Among the most promising opportunities to tackle customer waste are the awareness campaigns towards waste reduction. The aim of the project is to develop and conduct awareness camping for consumer waste reduction that is women sanitary waste and plastic waste used in product packaging. This research project will use a mixed method research approach sequentially from qualitative design to quantitative design. At qualitative part awareness campaign will be designed and at quantitative part change in awareness level and its impact on behavioral intentions will be examined by using the longitudinal data in three time lags. Data will be analyzed by using Structural Equation Modelling and MANOVA. The findings of the project will be helpful in building waste reduction that is linked with economic and social aspects of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Model Testing and Numerical Modelling of Onshore Wind Turbine Foundation
data.projectDigest: In a developing country like Pakistan, a reliable, sustainable, uninterrupted, and affordable energy supply is a fundamental prerequisite for reducing poverty, encouraging investment, and boosting economic growth. The best solution to achieve sustainable goals is the installation of wind turbine because a single wind turbine can generate the same amount of electricity in kWh (kilowatt-hours) as thousands of solar panels. Wind turbine is economical in long term than solar and any other source of renewable energy. The main objectives of the research are to provide short-term and long-term behavior of soil around gravity based wind turbine foundation subjected to both static and dynamic loading. Results of the proposed study will provide an effective and economical design of gravity foundation, benefit both the energy sector and to grow economy of the country, benefit existing wind turbines and its safety against the natural disasters (i.e., earthquakes).

data.projectName: Production of Transgenic Wheat Variety to Reduce the Ozone Pollution and Global Warming Impact and to Increase the Yield of Wheat
data.projectDigest:
The current project undertakes the thematic issue of food security. Abiotic stresses such as ozone, salt, drought and temperature stresses greatly reduce and limit productivity of important crops such as wheat. Ozone (O3) being a major abiotic stress causes sever damages to crop plants worldwide. The ozone (O3) concentration at ground level has increased 60–100% since pre-industrialization and is considered the atmospheric pollutant worldwide. Published literature has shown that high O3 at ground level causes yield losses of 18-21% in soybean, 29.3% in spring wheat and 7.2% in corn. data.projectName: Macroeconomic Effects of Infrastructure Investment in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Infrastructure development has been extensively discussed in the macroeconomic literature for its impact on economic growth and development of a country. The provision of improved infrastructure decreases trade and transaction cost and helps in the mobility of goods & services and capital flows which in turn affect economic growth via trade competitiveness and diversification of exports. The provision of improved infrastructure facilitates the process of economic exchange not only domestically but also internationally with increased access towards technology, education and communications. The infrastructure available in Pakistan is relatively poor to the international standards. However, Pakistan is giving considerable emphasis on provision of infrastructural facilities particularly in telecommunication, transport, and energy infrastructure in order to achieve regional cohesion, promote economic development and to decrease economic disparities. In this context, Pakistan has signed an agreement with China, China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), to develop an efficient and improved infrastructure in the country. Infrastructure projects under CPEC are expected to improve transportation infrastructure and communication network that may reduce transaction/coordination costs and facilitate the geographic rationalization of economic activities. With this backdrop, it is important to investigate the dynamic impact of infrastructure investment on growth, welfare and other key macroeconomic variables. So the current study will explore the costs and benefits of increasing public infrastructure investment and how these macroeconomic effects of infrastructure investment fluctuate with main features of the economy.

data.projectName: Formulation of new generation slow release P fertilizer from indigenous rock phosphate ore and its utilization for wheat production
data.projectDigest: Food Security is always a great challenge for the massive growing world population which depends on agriculture. One of most important challenges for agriculture in Pakistan besides enhancing food production per unit area is to provide a way to minimize the production cost per unit area along with minimum risk to soil health and environmental quality. Farming families are facing economic pressure to survive against rising prices of fuel, fertilizers and pesticides. With growth of clean energy technology, more efficient and sustainable agriculture can be attained by using carbon based slow release fertilizer derived from local nutrition resources. Pakistan is gifted naturally with huge reserves of rock phosphate. But natural resources of Pakistan are being rapidly depleted due to inappropriate use and very poor management. Wheat is major staple food in Pakistan. With increasing prices of fertilizers as a result of rising cost of energy and inflating trends in local currency, reliance on local resources of country for crop nutrition should be enhanced not only to boost yield but also to improve the quality of wheat and to maintain a good soil health for next generations that could serve as a step toward environmentally safe sustainable agriculture in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Development of an Ecosystem of Locally Designed Photonic Tools and Technologies to Enable Research and Development of Next Generation Big Data Solutions in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The global economy in upcoming decades will be driven by the widely accepted paradigm of big-data. This paradigm can only be realized by accumulation and processing of data acquired mainly through smart devices and IoT technology. The volume of big-data on the computing servers is expected to reach some 400+ billion gigabytes by 2021 and will grow at a staggering rate of 200+ million gigabytes per day. Processing of such enormous data requires development of new technologies that could enable next generation data centre solutions. Due to the fundamental physical limitations, these solutions cannot be designed using the conventional electronic approaches alone, therefore, novel photonic platforms must be incorporated. This project aims at developing an ecosystem of locally designed tools and leveraging on internationally available fabrication facilities to enable research and development of next generation big-data solutions in Pakistan. This includes development of software tools for design and optimization of photonic integrated circuits. At the end, there will be a fabless technology company with experience of successful design and fabrication of big-data solutions and enabling execution of similar projects in future. For Pakistan to remain economically competitive in the wake of big-data paradigm, capacity building in competitive areas is inevitable.

data.projectName: "Establishment of International Forgiveness Institute-Pakistan Branch: Translation, Adaptation and Validation of Forgiveness Education Curriculum for Students"
data.projectDigest: The objective to establish International Forgiveness Institute-Pakistan Branch to promote Peace and Mental Health through Forgiveness Education in Pakistan on standardized model and Curriculum of Forgiveness.  Without forgiveness education, another person may too easily equate forgiving and reconciling, thus staying in an abusive relationship.  With forgiveness education, a person can forgive, not necessarily reconcile, and heal emotionally. Teaching forgiveness is especially important to help reduce anger in children who have suffered injustice sufficient enough to compromise their emotional health. Forgiveness can also help students, now and later as adults, forge stable and meaningful relationships without anger causing discord and division. Finally, forgiveness can play a big part in how communities thrive when people begin to see more deeply the inherent worth of others. Cultivating forgiveness is important because there are senseless crimes committed in a fit of anger where one brief moment can alter the course of many lives. People whose lives are affected by these crimes may not have the ability to forgive, thereby contributing to more resentment and anger in the world. The Present research project will provide standardized curriculum guides for all standard students to promote forgiveness as a part of their everyday studies and learned activities.
