data.projectName: CRISPR/Cas based multiplex genome editing to improve Brassica spp.
data.projectDigest:
The requirement of edible oil and oilseed meals is continuously rising in Pakistan due to increasing population and expanding poultry and aquaculture sectors. Palm oil is one of the largest imports of Pakistan and during 2018-2019, Pakistan was expecting to import 3.4 million metric tons (MMT) of palm oil. In Pakistan, all predictions show a continuous increase in import of oil seed complex in future. Brassica represent 2nd largest oil seed crop in country after cotton and Pakistan is continuously trying to increase domestic oil seed production, especially Brassica to reduce the import bill. However, oil from indigenous rapeseed-mustard is not good for human health because of high erucic acid contents. In addition, higher oleic acid content, reduced post-harvest loss and higher yield in domestic Brassica species are also long-standing objectives of Pakistani scientific community to save billions of rupees. Therefore, in face of continuously increasing import of oil seed complex in country, we intend to use CRISPR/Cas based genome editing to improve domestic rapeseed mustered species for low erucic acid, high oleic acid and improved yield. Specific objectives include:
1-	Reduction of erucic acid in edible oil of domestic rapeseed-mustard spp.
2-	Improved oleic acid contents of oil from indigenous Brassica species
3-	Yield improvement through increased number of branches and improved shattering resistance in Brassica

data.projectName: Design and Development of Electric Powertrain for Electrical Vehicle including High Energy Density Electrical Traction Machine and associated technologies
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
The project is to Design and Develop Electric Powertrain for Electrical Vehicle (EV) including High Energy Density Electrical Traction Machine and associated technologies. It aimed to develop locally manufactured cost effective, low emission EV with indigenous hardware and systems. Prime Component is traction machine (high energy density); supervisory and local control, battery management; data communication and control, power inverters, conversion of existing fuel vehicles to EV and reduction gear system. Prototype EV, installed with indigenously developed hardware and other systems, is envisaged as outcome of the project which should be commercializable. 

The project addresses thematic areas of Urban & rural transport and Climate Change and Environment (pollution reduction activities). Proposed work will also have impact on industrial sector, larger jobs market will be created and economic cycle of the country will be positively affected. Furthermore, the project will also strength our industrial base by enabling SME. Capacity building of SME for production of high-end engineering products will enhance job market and revenue margins. The international PI has experience of developing Electrical bus, he will be great help in knowledge transfer, all PI have been working in relevant fields for 6-10 years. The industrial partner has significant linkages with automotive industry.

data.projectName: CO2 consuming bio-healable smart bricks for sustainable construction
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Smart interlocking building brick is proposed in unique design owing the traits of bio-healing and CO2 confiscation ability. The base elements will be fabricated via bio-enrichment of compressed soil from the ten defined agro-zones of Pakistan without any contaminative burning phase. The proposed masonry system will offer rapid construction facility accompanied with additional resilience to in-plane and out-plane bending due to provided shear key and reinforcing mechanism. The elimination of burning will result in reduction of particulate matter (PM2.5) from the environment which has been recently reported to exceed 12 µg/m³ per anum in the major cities of Pakistan contributing in smog and associated health concerns. Activation of non-pathogenic bacteria inherently present in the base material of building brick will result in excitation of bio-healing actions to auto-repair the induced cracks and prolong service life of the structure. Bio-healable bricks will offer least permeability due to sealing of inherent voids via bio-metabolic activity of stimulated microbes. Overall this development will revolutionize the field of building engineering with added friendly provisions for environment.

data.projectName: Marine Traffic Monitoring and Situational Awareness at National Harbors
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Pakistan has a coastline of approx. 1059 Km with three major commercial ports i.e Karachi, Bin Qasim and Gwadar. Seaports play a vital role in cargo transportation all around the world as it is the cheapest mode of transportation. Pakistan’s seaports hold a strong potential in boosting the country’s economy. Keeping in view such expandability of our ports, assistance of modern technology and analysis of data proves to be of utmost importance. Vessel detection and tracking are the most important tasks for situational awareness, monitoring and improving the efficiency of coastal and various maritime infrastructures, and management of local fishing fleet. Ongoing national level projects such as CPEC demands effective implementation of intelligent vessel monitoring systems in our ports. While there are operational and technical issues with classical CoTS solutions, some vision embedded international CoTS solutions available in the market are expensive and might lead to potential data leak. Similarly, vision enabled marine related CoTS are not robust due lack of local vessels dataset required essentially for algorithm training. Therefore, it is important to develop indigenous vision-based situational awareness solutions for better managed and efficient ports.

data.projectName: Economic impact of combating antimicrobial resistance in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Excessive use of antibiotics is causing havoc and causing antimicrobial resistance (AMR) throughout the world including Pakistan and UK. In Pakistan, many pathogenic bacteria has become resistant to multiple antibiotics. The problem of multi-drug resistance can be solved by the use of small antimicrobial peptides against which bacteria cannot attain resistance.

World Health organization has also raised serious concern regarding AMR against infectious diseases like tuberculosis, malaria, influenza, HIV etc. Annually AMR is the cause of the death of 700,000 people globally and figure may rise to 10 million people by the end of 2050, if antimicrobial resistance is not properly managed, with a accumulative cost of $ 100 trillion on the world economy. AMR will also threaten many Sustainable Development Goals (SDG). 

To cater the situation, antibiotics in poultry feed will be replaced with probiotics, antimicrobial peptide will be developed and will be replaced with conventional antibiotics. Further, extensive awareness program will be launched by arranging seminars, workshops and trainings for students, doctors and general public. A website and mobile application will also be developed to provide information on AMR to the doctors. A hi-tech lab will also be establish for surveillance of AMR.

data.projectName: To investigate mechanisms of genomic instability and disease progression in Chronic Myeloid Leukemia
data.projectDigest:
Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) is a stem cell disorder. The symptoms, which appear in initial phase, are non-specific including fever, anemia, fatigue, weight loss, weakness etc. CML primarily affects the adults between 25-60 years of age and accounts for 15-20% of all leukemia cases. Incidence of CML is about 0.9-1.5 per 100 000 of the population worldwide. It is one of the most common types of adulthood blood cancers and thousands of patients are diagnosed with it yearly. On an average survival for CML patients is 3-8 years after clinical manifestation of the disease. With traditional drugs like Hydroxyurea and interferon, majority of the patients showed poor response and resistance to these drugs. This is because these drugs are non-specific.
As accelerated CML patients are resistant to available treatment; finding mechanisms of genomic instability and disease progression will lead to discovery of new biomarkers for early diagnosis and/or prognosis and allow development of strategies for timely interventions to delay/inhibit the disease progression.
It will further help in finding new drug targets for designing novel and more effective drugs for treating advanced phase CML patients. Findings new mechanisms of cancer progression will result in high impact factor publications in ISI-indexed journals.

Hydrogen economy comprise of renewable hydrogen production, transportation and storage, utilization through fuel cell technology for transportation and stationary applications.

data.projectName: Developing next-generation tomato cultivars and affordable internet-of-things (IoT)-enabled solarized infrastructure for urban agriculture
data.projectDigest: It is estimated that around 60% of the global population will be living in cities by the end of 2030, and feeding such a huge population will become very challenging and will require tackling all aspects of food system. The project is well-articulated and designed holistically in following four areas: a) molecular design breeding approach to develop new tomato cultivars suitable for urban agriculture with special emphasis to modulate tomato inflorescence structure by gene editing, gene discovery for urban-tomato ideotype using next-generation sequencing, mining genbank resources using genomic selection (prediction) approaches for such ideotypes, b) designing affordable internet-of-things (IoT)-enabled solarized aquaponic-based infrastructure optimized for urban agriculture at Quaid-i-Azam University (QAU) and Muhammad Nawaz Sharif University of Agriculture Multan (MNSUAM), for practical demonstration, training and breeding, c) a social component to promote urban agriculture through training and outreach, and to train potential practitioners, d) national-level mapping for the sites and potential crops suitable for urban agriculture, and initial trials in the aforementioned infrastructures established at QAU and MNSUAM. The outcome of the project would provide strong foundation to initiate urban agriculture by: i) providing suitable cultivars, ii) affordable infrastructure to be adopted by low-income residents, iii) helping in alleviating risks of peri-urban agriculture where waste-water and contaminated industrial water is used for vegetable production, iv) contributing to household food security, especially in the time of food shortage and food crisis, and v) providing additional employment and income for low-income-residents, women and disadvantaged population.

data.projectName: Integrated Smart Traffic Management System (ISTMS)
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
The aim of Integrated Smart Traffic Management System (ISTMS) is to investigate efficient traffic management strategies, Traffic congestion, Vehicle classification, smart environmental pollution control, reliable accident management, intelligent administration of pre-hospital activities and Urban planning. The proposed project aims to recommend and implement ISTMS that will improve the traffic management into urban cities resulting into efficient traffic management through learning enabled data analytic algorithms, controlling of environmental pollution and smart management of accidents as well as providing information to vehicles for available vacancies at near-by hospitals to save the precious lives of urban commuters. The proposed investigations into ISTMS come under the umbrella of HEC GCF topic of Information Technology and Telecommunication. Furthermore, the area also focuses the United Nations’ Sustainable Development goals, i.e. good health and wellbeing and industry, innovation, and infrastructure.
The ISTMS will investigate following key problems and possible recommend solutions. 
•	Traffic density/congestion measurement in Karachi and Machine Learning based Recommended Solutions based on Real- Time Traffic Statistics and Analysis.
•	Classification of vehicles [3], Bus, Rickshaws, Buses and Tankers. This classification will be useful for measuring type of emissions and to estimate the carbon footprints. This will also help measuring environmental pollution e.g. i.e. NO2 , PM10 , PM2.5, O3  and proposing suitable solutions.
•	Machine Learning enabled analysis of driver behavior and anomaly detection of drivers:
The behavior analysis will help in reducing the number of accidents. 
•	The investigation will also develop statistics regarding health issues .

The proposed project aims to recommend and implement ISTMS that will improve the traffic management into urban cities resulting into efficient traffic management through learning enabled data analytic algorithms, controlling of environmental pollution and smart management of accidents as well as providing information to vehicles for available vacancies at near-by hospitals to save the precious lives of urban commuters. The proposed investigations into ISTMS come under the umbrella of HEC GCF topic of Information Technology and Telecommunication. Furthermore, the area also focuses the United Nations’ Sustainable Development goals, i.e. good health and wellbeing and industry, innovation, and infrastructure.
The ISTMS will investigate following key problems and possible recommend solutions. 
•	Traffic density/congestion measurement in Karachi and Machine Learning based Recommended Solutions based on Real- Time Traffic Statistics and Analysis.
•	Classification of vehicles [3], Bus, Rickshaws, Buses and Tankers. This classification will be useful for measuring type of emissions and to estimate the carbon footprints. This will also help measuring environmental pollution e.g. i.e. NO2 , PM10 , PM2.5, O3  and proposing suitable solutions.
•	Machine Learning enabled analysis of driver behavior and anomaly detection of drivers:
The behavior analysis will help in reducing the number of accidents. 
•	The investigation will also develop statistics regarding health issues .

data.projectName: Modeling and assessing the Water-Energy-Food Security Nexus in the Chenab River Basin
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Water, energy, and land resources are extremely under pressure due to demographic growth, socio-economic development, and climate change. Regional planning deficiencies have revealed that these essential resources should not anymore be administered separately. Modern technologies in water, energy and agriculture, as well as the overall intensification of natural resources, uses have further increased the interdependencies, especially at the larger regional scale. There is a need to develop integrated modeling approaches as support of resources planning at river basin scale considering the links between water availability, energy demand, and agricultural sector. Such an integrated planning approach is of high demand in Pakistan and elsewhere to tackle sustainability challenges related to the Water, Energy, and Food Nexus.

data.projectName: The influence of Climatic Extremes on land cover affecting the dynamics of Urban Vegetation, Surface Temperature and Ground Water shrinkage in Pakistan-  Implications for Sustainable Urban Development
data.projectDigest:
Climate is an interconnected system of land and atmospheric ecosystems.  A significant climate change has been observed in 20th century that has brought an amalgamation of climatic extremes that can be observed in the form of constant increase in temperature all over the globe along with high intensity storms in one part of the world while at the same time other part is facing an unexpected prolonged drought. These climatic extremes are also altering the dry ecosystem function of Pakistan and are a threat to the three major pillars of sustainability i.e. economic, social and environmental. Pakistan is also one of the most affected countries in terms of its vulnerability to climate change. Increase in the frequency of extreme events such as floods, droughts, heat and cold waves are threatening the land and water resources of the country.
The thematic areas of this study are climate change and environment, water management and urban planning and it will address the following issues.
*Spatio-temporal analysis of the concurrent climatic extremes i.e. floods, droughts, heat waves and cold waves from 1969-2019.
*To assess the ground water level conditions of climatic zones of Pakistan from the year 1989 to 2019 considering Urban Heat Islands (UHI) of Pakistan as a case. This proposed research study is a stride towards United Nations Sustainable Development Goals and supports the implication of remote sensing techniques to assess the UHI and ground water level conditions over a particular time period in Pakistan.
*Also it will investigate the key indicators which are affecting the levels of urban sustainability in developing countries like Pakistan and the development of a comprehensive framework for sustainability assessment in selected cities of Pakistan.

data.projectName: An Intelligent digital platform for disease tracking, management and risk stratification
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: Migraine,  depression, COPD, asthma, and rheumatoid arthritis are the five most common chronic diseases with episodic exacerbations (CDEE). They afflict over 2 billion people worldwide and have an annual burden of $1.2 trillion. CDEE result in a high loss of productive years and reduce the quality of life of the afflicted individual. They are more prevalent in low and middle-income countries such as Pakistan. Pakistan has not yet invested in the treatment of CDEE, so our deficit in productivity due to sick days and loss in productive years due to premature deaths are very high. Each patient has unique triggers which result in an exacerbation of their CDEE. Initially targeting two chronic diseases, migraine and depression, we propose to provide personalized migraine and depression risk assessment and prediction using a smartphone. Through smartphone application(s) combined with smartphone sensors, we will collect physiological, behavioural, and environmental data that can help identify each user's triggers. We plan to collect data of 2,000 migraine and 500 depression patients with which we can create a model that predicts migraine and depression episodes allowing users to take necessary steps to preempt an attack. The end objective is to create a larger framework that provides risk assessment and prediction for all CDEE and is validated after longitudinal impact analysis.

data.projectName: ENGINEERING A CIRCULAR ECONOMY FOR PAKISTAN: LAB-TO MARKET APPROACH FOR THE CONVERSION OF PLASTIC WASTE TO CLEAN FUELS AND ENERGY
data.projectDigest:
Systematic Management of waste is one of the major problems facing modern society and is not just limited to plastics. Of the 8.3 billion metric tons that have been produced, 6.3 billion metric tons has become plastic waste. Only nine percent (9%) of the plastic waste has been recycled. Pakistan generates about 9% of plastic waste a year, which has been increasing by more than 1% annually. All the plastic waste of Pakistan is not processed for the beneficial uses. Recycling of plastic is needed to sustain the environment. The aim behind working on this project is to enhance and acknowledge the beauty of marine life as well as protect the sea creatures from the daily hazards. The main reason for recycling is to conserve energy, help the environment, reduce pollution, slow global warming and lower waste products in landfills. By recycling, people can have something to do with the earth's overall health and keep the air, water and land clean. Additionally, valuable high-end products would be developed from toxic and environmentally hazardous plastic waste which would eventually add more to the economy of Pakistan.
There is dire need to treat solid waste in Pakistan and it is the first time that we are coming with highly educated and dedicated professional's team that will work on this high valued research project.

data.projectName: Revolutionization of Housing Construction Industry through BIM-VR-3D  Printing Technology Integration
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is the 6th most populous country in the world with total population of 207.8 million and growth rate of 2.4%. Swift rise in population and large-scale urbanization has risen scarcity of housing in the country to 19 million with a backlog of around 10 million units and an annual addition of 350,000 to 400,000 units per year. Affordability is one big issue but it is comprehended by incapacitated industry to meet such demand. Reason is construction industry reliance on primitive ways of construction requiring longer time periods, lacks integration among design requirements and old ways of construction. Thus, being not mechanized results in increasing demand and lesser or delayed housing supply.  This is unlike industrialized process of the modern world where the design and its constructability are thoroughly reviewed through innovative technology intervention. The manufacturing industries took advantage of fourth industrial revolution (4IR) to ensure quality of design of product and process of design and product remains flawless and rapid. This research aims at systematic integration of multi-disciplinary and multi-sectoral expertise to address socioeconomic issue through technology, i.e. by BIM-VR-3D Printing technology intervention to revolutionize housing construction sector in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Demand Based Water Management through Evidence Based Decission Support System under Changing Climate: A Case Study of Nara Canal
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is challenged by the confluence of increasing water scarcity and decreasing water use efficiency in agriculture. The challenge is intensifying as population and food demand grows and climate change leads to more severe and prolonged droughts. To counter the mounting crisis, the proposed project will enable farmers and farmer’s organizations with data from smart technology to increase water delivery efficiency and enhance on farm water productivity. The research will determine the effectiveness of integrating water level and soil moisture sensors with distributed storage, saline irrigation water blending, and drip irrigation to guide water use by farmers and water delivery scheduling by farmer’s organizations. The team is led by the U.S.-Pakistan Center for Advanced Studies in Water (USPCAS-W) at Mehran University of Engineering and Technology with partners from LUMS, Lahore (sensor technologies), University of Utah, USA (sensor placement-water system operations optimization), and Sindh Irrigation and Drainage Authority (farm level cooperation). The project will leverage USPCASW research and water conservation interventions of the Sindh Irrigated Agricuture for Productivity Enhancement Project. The project will achieve impacts by proving a solution for water efficiency, providing cost data to policy makers, engaging local students with games, and making farming attractive to youths and females.

data.projectName: Bio-mechanical analysis of the Pakistani Elite and sub-elite Athletes
data.projectDigest: This project will be the bio-mechanical analysis of the Pakistani athletes to compare  their performance with the international athletes. It also help to identify the mechanical causes of the poor performance of Pakistani athletes in Asian Games, Commonwealth Games, and Olympic Games. Further, it will assist the officials  of the Pakistan Sports boards for team selection and future planning on the basis of the current status of the athletes and coaching standard. Data will be collected from colleges, universities, and divisions of all provinces of Pakistan. The target population for data collection will be under-16, under-19, and adult athletes. Data profiling of all athletes will be established by considering their bio-mechanical performance of their particular sports, socio-economic background, body composition, physical fitness.  Data will be collected with the indoor and outdoor set-ups. The following instruments will be used for data collection as, 4 HDV high definition video cameras, 32 points calibration frame, 3-D indoor VICON System, Force plates, EMG (electromyogram), skinfold calipers, bone calipers, physical fitness devices, hand grip back strength dynamometers. These software’s will be used for data analysis as VICON software, APAS (Ariel performance Analysis), and somatotype. The Variables will be obtained as a ground reaction force, displacement, speed, joint moments, muscle contraction, ground reaction force, physical fitness, somatotype of athletes.

data.projectName: Attitudinal and Affective Perspectives of Secondary School Students on Science and Technology in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Economic development is generally conceived as a continuous effort to increase living standards of the people. It does not simply include the economic growth but a positive change in political, cultural and social environment also which is the consequence of a positive change in thoughts of people. It follows that the goal of socio-economic development can be achieved by producing productive scientific minded individuals. These individuals should be characterized by critical thinking, honesty, common sense, objectivity, logical reasoning, and systematic problem solving etc. The creation of such individuals is the ultimate goal of contemporary science education. Part of the rationale for having science education is not just to convey the established science knowledge, but also to inculcate respect and appreciation for scientific attitude as part of the culture. Present research project includes ROSES’ initiative, and in addition, intends to assess the life skills of students, their scientific behaviour and generic competences inevitable for productive scientific minds of twenty first century knowledge-based society. The universe of the project will encompass students, teachers, heads of institutions and departments, and their alumni across all the administrative units of Pakistan. It finally, intends to recommend necessary policy measures so that the system may produce more productive citizens.

data.projectName: Genetic Improvement of Pakistani Cotton to Circumvent the Climatic Changes
data.projectDigest: Erratic weather and a loss of $3 billion of cotton crop, requires the  need to introduce high yield cotton varieties with improved quality of fiber, which can withstand harsh weather conditions like drought and heat. The proposed project will advance the research in national interest as CEMB is identifying and characterizing the abiotic stress tolerant genes and fiber quality improvement genes, from local cotton varieties and other plant species. Genetic transformation of cotton is a routine practice in CEMB. Transcriptomic analyses will be performed by Dr Khurram Bashir in collaboration with Centre for sustainable Resource Science RIKEN, Japan. The data of transgenic cotton showing tolerance against drought and heat will be assessed in CCRI Multan which is the main cotton growing area and the fibre quality will be estimated. Four Brothers Group Pakistan is a private agri based industry and its farms will be helpful to grow and evaluate the transgenic cotton crop at commercial level and further seed multiplication and production will be done in collaboration. This public-private partnership will be helpful in the proposed research project to solve the grand challenge of the climatic threats to the cotton crop which is under loss in the prevailing scenario.

data.projectName: Intelligent Information Pollution Detection System for Pakistani Digital Media
data.projectDigest: The digital media has emerged as the largest real-time information dissemination platform. Digital media contains large amounts of unverified, unauthentic, and misinformation. This misinformation has affected large number of social sectors including politics, business, and media industry. The objective of the project is to identify and understand the characteristics of fake news, propaganda, and deepfake on digital media in the context of Pakistani digital space. First, the social surveys will be done on characteristics of polluted content such as fake news, propaganda, rumors, deepfake etc., in the context of Pakistani culture and demographics. These surveys will also provide insight on how online misinformation impacts Pakistani population with diverse demographics. Next, different systems will be developed to detect fake and propaganda news in English and Urdu. Also, systems will be developed to identify bots and bot-squads using the platform for propagation of misinformation. Moreover, the deepfake detection system will be developed for detection of manipulation in the visual as well as audio content of video. The development of systems requires datasets, Natural Language Processing (NLP), Natural Language Understanding (NLU) tools and resources for Urdu language. The fact checking service will be developed by providing flagged content to news agencies for authentication.

data.projectName: Graphene for energy: A platform to create innovation capacity from research and innovation
data.projectDigest:
This project gathers a research network in graphene with topical focus on energy applications. The consortium establishes a platform that is allocating an academic graphene energy research community in Pakistan, and which involves exchange with international partners in energy research and innovation competence as well as industrial graphene material producers. The exchange includes building innovation capacity from research and innovation as means so that a higher degree of research findings may reach a commercialization stage and support reducing the climate change. By that the knowledge flow from academia to industry is facilitated. Over time this is expected to contribute to the development economics. In Europe this is addressed by regional economic growth tools such as “Research and Innovation Strategies for Smart Specialisation”, and the international partners have leading experience in graphene, innovation and implementing smart specialisation. The academic project partners explore novel research fields in graphene for energy. The availability of industrial material with reproducible material properties is a foundation for exploring application properties. This also provides an industry-oriented solution that supports the research impact. The innovation capacity tools combined with industrial material that is standardized make it viable to initiate an industrial stage in 3-5 years in Pakistan. The international partner and associated network represent the sectoral innovation and industrial involvement. 
Graphene is a material which can have influence in many areas which affect our society. We create ways so both technology and region can have win-win situations by acting in joint ways based on creating values in research and innovation.

data.projectName: Development of mastitis vaccines for dairy cattle and buffaloes for enhanced milk quality
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Milk, a liquid secreted by the mammary glands of female mammals to feed their young for a period starting immediately after birth. Milk from domestic animals is also an important source of food for humans, either in the form of fresh liquid or processed into a number of dairy products such as butter and cheese. Milk quality is affected by many factors, including but not limited to  the health of cows, hygienic handling of milk and the udder health of dairy animals. Among these, udder health is perhaps the most important factor affecting milk quality. There are many diseases that can effect udder health but mastitis (inflammation of udder/mammary glands) is the most deleterious one. 
Mastitis is the most persistent and widely spread disease condition of importance to milk hygiene and quality among dairy cattle worldwide. Mastitis influences the total milk output and modifies milk composition and technological usability. Mastitis is the economically most important disease in lactating cows and the prevalence under any management condition is considerably high. It causes economic losses due to reduction of both quantity and quality of milk, shortening of productive life and loss in reproductive efficiency of affected cows. Losses in total milk production range from 5.0 to 25.0%, with one extreme of 83.9%. Decreases in the composition of milk have been recorded for fat, 0.1 to 0.45%; solids-not-fat, 0.1 to 0.57%; lactose, 0.1 to 0.77%; and total solids, 1.07%. Total annual economic losses to dairymen in the United States attributable to mastitis have been estimated at $400 to $500 million, or $23 per cow. data.projectName: Sustaining wheat yield under the current and future projected environments (hot and dry climates)
data.projectDigest: Wheat production in Pakistan and Australia is constrained by heat and drought stresses. In Pakistan, irrigation water supplies for the “Rabi” crops, such as wheat, were estimated to be 40 percent below the previous ten-year average in 2018-19. Air temperature has been increased by 1.5°C during the last decade which has drastically affected the wheat yield.  Over half of Australian wheat crops are affected by severe drought that drastically impacts yield, and heat stress is increasingly affecting productivity, costing an extra 240 kg ha-1 of yield per decade. To solve the problem, soil, varietal, management and climate data throughout Pakistan will be collected to quantify the impact of present and projected drought and heat stress on wheat crop through Australian modelling techniques. Efficient and easily transferable screening methods (developed by the University of Queensland) for drought and heat stress in promising Pakistani and Australian lines will be applied. Heat and drought tolerance will be induced in candidate lines/varieties through foliar application of growth regulators. The under lying mechanism of heat tolerance will be exposed through proteomic analysis technique. The proposed project will benefit the Pakistani researchers, Pakistani breeders, Pakistan extension services, Pakistani smallholder farmers and Pakistani population including women.

Efficient and easily transferable screening methods (developed by the University of Queensland) for drought and heat stress in promising Pakistani and Australian lines will be applied. Heat and drought tolerance will be induced in candidate lines/varieties through foliar application of growth regulators. The under lying mechanism of heat tolerance will be exposed through proteomic analysis technique. The proposed project will benefit the Pakistani researchers, Pakistani breeders, Pakistan extension services, Pakistani smallholder farmers and Pakistani population including women.

data.projectName: DEFORESTATION AND CLIMATE CHANGE IN NORTHERN KHYBER PAKHTUNKHWA: EXPLORING INFLUENCING FACTORS, COSTS OF INACTION AND VALUATION OF SERVICES
data.projectDigest:
Conservation of natural capital, particularly the forest resources is one of the key challenges of Pakistan. The Northern areas of Pakistan accommodate substantial forests. However, these forests degraded over time due to numerous factors causing loss of timber and non-timber products and other forest ecosystem services. The factors which degrade forests need to be explored to have informed decisions. Moreover, the lack of proper actions to tackle these challenges further cost the society and forest ecosystem services. It is also important to analyze the valuation of forest ecosystem services such as recreational, provisioning, supporting and regulating services to assess how climate change and other factors affect forests and their services. This research project will assess the relationship between deforestation and climate change in Northern KP. Moreover, the project explores the potential for sustainable use of Non-Forestry Timber Products resources for food/livelihood security. The project will carry out a comprehensive survey in six districts Swat, Upper Dir, Chitral, Shangla, Kohistan and Khyber (Tirah) with the objectives: 
1.	To explore the climatic and non-climatic factors influencing deforestation in the selected districts. 
2.	To analyze the potential impact of deforestation on climatic variables and forest ecosystem services.
3.	To estimate the cost of inaction by KP government in the forest sector.
4.	To estimate the value of non-timber forest products and services and their contribution to improving livelihood and food security of poor communities. 
5.	To suggest ways to conserve forest ecosystem services & reduce the adverse impact of climate change on local communities.
6.	To review existing institutional arrangements for forest conservation

data.projectName: GNSS BASED HYDROLOGICAL TRANSPORT MODELLING OF INDUS BASIN
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is facing acute shortage of water. According to the IMF, Pakistan ranked third among the countries facing severe water shortage. In May-18, Pakistan_Council_of_Research_in_Water_Resources announced that by 2025, there will be very little or no clean water available in the country which puts Pakistan in the category of a high stress country. The backbone of water source in Pakistan is Indus Basin. It is one of the largest contiguous water distribution and irrigation systems in the world but unfortunately never been paid attention to model and digitized its flow for its thorough study. This project extends a current pilot study at NCBC@NED which exploits the real-time data from GNSS to detect/monitor current surface water levels and flow of various water reservoirs in Pakistan. The idea is to develop a HYDROLOGICAL TRANSPORT MODEL FOR INDUS BASIN to simulate the flow of rivers, streams, groundwater movement or drainage front displacement, and calculate water quality parameters. This study will be first of its kind and will be helpful to analysis its flow pattern along with predication capabilities. It will also be helpful for government and related stakeholders to define water and related policies in much better and scientific way.

data.projectName: EnvIoT:  Air Quality Monitoring Network to Aid Data Driven Policy Making
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Objective: Conceive, design and deploy pollution measuring networks to build accurate and precise air quality models which enable evidence based policy decision making and planning.

Industrialization without effective environmental protection efforts has resulted in unprecedented levels of air pollution in the world and particularly in developing countries such as Pakistan. While most of the developed countries are already ahead in developing and implementing policies which help build a sustainable and healthy environment, Pakistan is far behind primarily because of unavailability of reliable air pollution data and practical air pollution models. This hampers both identification of air pollution sources and measurement of air pollution levels. To remedy this we propose an Environmental Air quality Monitoring Network called EnvIoT.

The EnvIoT system will consist of a three step process which starts from data collection using reliable and accurate sensors. An extensive Internet of Things based Sensor network will be deployed for this purpose. The collected data will then be analyzed and predictive air pollution models will be developed which can finally be used to establish sustainable air pollution environmental policies for Pakistan.

data.projectName: Optimization of novel compositions for supercapacitors to mitigate the challenges for the clean air.
data.projectDigest:
The discovery of a better electrode composition will bridge the gap between battery and supercapacitor performance. The present research proposal is aimed at synthesizing electrode materials for supercapacitors, making hybrids of different EDLC and pseudocapacitors, specially focusing on hybrids of Metal Molybdates ( Mx(MoO4)y ) and Metal Oxides (MxOy), where M corresponds to metals like Al, Fe, Ti etc.  The same compositions will be synthesized with dopant rich compositions in order to introduce 2-electron pathways. Synthesis will be performed by conventional solid-state routes, facile hydrothermal, non-aqueous sol gel or modified Pechini method depending upon which route is most cost and time effective. This will provide a platform for optimizing the design of new materials. Various techniques to enhance the conductivity can be employed such as carbon coating etc. The synthesized powders will be characterized using X-ray diffraction, inductively coupled plasma (ICP), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Fourier transform infra-red spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and high resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM). The electrochemical techniques [galvanostatic charge/discharge profiles, potentiostatic cycling, IV curves and electrical impedance (EIS)] will be employed to observe the performance of different energy materials for the supercapacitor testing. 
Problem 
The aim is to enable the development of compact hybrid supercapacitors with higher energy storage capacity via careful material engineering. The positive electrodes used in present day batteries suffer from inefficient performance due to their intrinsic material limitations, in relation to cyclability (degradation and capacity fade), and energy/power density.

data.projectName: Design and Fabrication of Bifacial and multibusbar Silicon Photovoltaic modules
data.projectDigest: Silicon solar cells and photovoltaic modules have dominated the PV industry for over decades. With the progress in the silicon solar cell designs and improved light absorption have made Si based solar cells to keep the lead in PV as compared to recently new materials. Besides, Silicon based solar cells have more stability and less degradation as compared to other PV materials used in fabrication. Silicon solar cells can absorb light from both surfaces called bifacial solar cells and have recently received attention as in production of such PV modules. formerly, conventional PV modules have been and still in production with innovative solar cell design but with improved multibus bar bifacial solar cell design, bifacial PV modules have shown the potential of higher efficiency. In this project, fabrication of Bifacial PV modules have been proposed to establish this technology in Pakistan. Bifacial PV modules production have the potential to generate jobs and with export market can generate revenue as well.

data.projectName: Development of Metal-Air Batteries using Electrochemical Techniques
data.projectDigest: The energy requirement of Pakistan is increasing with an increase in its population. Energy management systems consisting of storage of energy must be strong enough to meet the demand of energy. The upcoming technology for resolving energy crisis is Lithium–air battery (LAB) technology . Among the various developing rechargeable batteries, the LAB is considered to be the most favorable for long-range electric vehicles (EVs >500 km), because of increased energy density. LABs have great potential for highly efficient energy storage devices, however still several limitations need to be overcome including low capacity, inefficient rate capability, large voltage gaps between discharging and charging and short cycle life . Recent advances are being made for successful implementation of LABs, focusing especially on the fundamental understanding of Li–O2 electrochemistry of LABs.   Research on metal air batteries other than lithium is highly progressive however the need of a highly reversible metal –oxygen battery remains challenging. Significant future research directions and investigating these challenges are critical to implement a metal-air battery having high practical capacity, maximum cycling efficiency and high energy storage for future EV industrial applications.

data.projectName: Artificial Intelligence in Automating Mining Operations
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest: Data driven governance coupled with artificial intelligence (AI) is fueling the fourth industrial revolution and novel solutions are bringing a positive change in the society. It is a set of algorithms and systems to extract knowledge and insights from data. On May 6th, 2017, the economist published an article titled “The world’s most valuable resource is no longer oil, but data”. We can validate this fact that the Forbes list of most valuable brands is mostly populated by companies dealing with data as commodity. This is because data contains inherent patterns which can be exploited for intelligent decision making. The research community has therefore witnessed a renaissance of AI, powered by deep learning, in the last decade. Influential researchers have termed the recent developments in AI as the new electricity which will power the 4th industrial revolution. It is therefore very important to deploy intelligent automated solutions and resolve many of the chronic problems faced by the citizens of Pakistan. Instead of adapting an open-ended blue-sky approach, we have highlighted potential areas where grand challenges exist. We propose that data-driven decision making is the potential solution in removing these challenges.

data.projectName: Development of Thermoelectric materials for sustainable energy applications
data.projectDigest: Industries and researchers are throwing their resources and efforts in finding solutions to the rising energy crisis and the frightening global warming. These issues can be tackled by attaining higher effective thermal management which may also solve several other issues in tandem. With fossil fuel supplies decreasing continuously and a succession of environmental problems like greenhouse emissions, ozone depletion, and catastrophic oil spills have drawn broad collective concern. These have resulted in a renewed awareness in science and technology for offering a sustainable supply of clean energy. One high potential possibility for resolving these energy issues is the use of thermoelectric materials. In thermoelectrics, solid state materials are investigated to convert electricity to heat (solid state cooling) or heat to electricity (power generation).  Thermoelectric devices have the ideal features for example no noise, highly reliable, scalable, use no greenhouse gases and have no moving parts. The maximum conversion efficiency of a TE material is determined by the dimensionless figure of merit zT = ?2?T/(?e + ?L), where ?, ?, ?e, ?L, and T represent the Seebeck coefficient, electrical conductivity, electronic thermal conductivity, lattice thermal conductivity, and absolute temperature respectively .

data.projectName: Deforestation in Pakistan: Its governing factors and role in environmental degradation and climate change
data.projectDigest: Recent figures reveal that only about 4% of the land area of the country is covered by forests which is far less that the environmental standards of 25%. The figures of forest cover and deforestation in Pakistan also present a very unpleasant situation attributed to the coupled effect of climate –more than 70% of the land of Pakistan is arid – and the high rate of anthropogenic deforestation. The degradation of green cover has resulted into various environmental issues throughout the country. Climate change and environmental pollution are among the important adverse outcomes of deforestation. An attempt will be made in this project to explore the proximate and underlying factors of deforestation in Pakistan and also explore its role in the recent changes in climatic pattern. The main objective of the project is to quantify the spatial and temporal degradation of green cover of the country and correlate it with the recent climatic anomalies in a scientific way. This project will be a great step towards policy formulation to control climate change and environmental degradation not through interfering the processes of development (industrialization, urbanization and infrastructure) but through enhancing the resilience of the natural environment through forest protection and afforestation.

data.projectName: Development of nanofiberous agro-textiles for food/crop protection, water management and environmental sustainability
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest: The proposed project aims at development of nanofiberous weed and insect suppression mats, pre-harvest fruits bags and protective packagings from recycle wastes i.e. polypropylene bags and polyethyleneterephthalate bottles. The objective of the research are efffective waste management in developing useful products for food and crop security, development economics, water regulation and environmental protection. For weed and insect suppression, hollow nanofiberous mats will be fabricated. The mats will physically suppress weeds and create a physical barrier to control insect pest growth from the soil. The hollow channels in the nanofibers will function as water reservoirs and release controlled water to the plants. Being an important cash crop, source of raw material for Pakistani Textile industry and prone to attack of weeds and insect pests, cotton will be subject for the research. The pre-harvest protective bags are suggested to protect fruits from fungal, viral and rot attacks and chemical contaminations from chemical sprays. By no/lower residual chemical contaminations, the fruits can meet the worlds import safety regulations. For this study banana fruit will be used. The protective packagings are suggested for absorption of fruit excretions, microbial protection and thus increase their shelf-life. The grapes and mango are the subject of the study.

The proposed project is in the jurisdiction of the United Nation Sustainable Development Goal 13 “Climate Action” and Goal 15 “Life on Land”

data.projectName: Cementless  geopolymer concrete  for sustainable  environment
data.projectDigest: After water, concrete is the most widely used material on the earth for infrastructure development. Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC) is a basic constituent of concrete, as the requirement for concrete increases, so likewise the demand for cement. Therefore, cement is one of the world’s most significant mass-produced materials. The major environmental health and safety issues related with cement manufacture are emission of polluted gases, use of large amount of energy and release of materials waste. The Geopolymer concrete can be produced using industrial by-products such as fly ash and/or low environmental impact material such as metakaolin. The great rise in demand, large emission of harmful gases and the high cost of conventional OPC has motivated the need of developing eco-friendly alternate cementitious materials. It is, therefore, a pressing need of the time to achieve a significant reduction in the cement consumption by an alternative of cement based concrete application in reinforced concrete construction. The energy requirement for the production of geopolymer binders are also much lesser compared to conventional cements with significantly reduced carbon dioxide emissions. This research project will provide guidelines for civil engineers and industrial community for preparation and use of an alternative innovative sustainable and eco friendly construction material to the existing most resource consuming OPC.

data.projectName: Structural and Social Determinants of Malnutrition among Mother and Child in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The issue of malnutrition is on the national agenda of Pakistan and aligned with Sustainable Development Goal 2. However, still, Pakistani children are victims of malnutrition with a stunting rate of 57%, underweight 41%, and wasting is 20%. This indicates an existing gap between service delivery at the structural level and nutritious practices at the societal level.  This project is based on multi-sectoral approach and having academic and sectoral collaborators, NGOs, and the Department of Health. Methodologically, this project follows a quasi-experimental research design with control and intervention districts from Sindh and Punjab. The collaborative partners will play their significant role in evidence generation, evidence synthesis, evidence transformation, and dissemination and critical reflection on all this evidence.  The package of intervention is based on demand generation by creating awareness and execution of behavior change communication strategies (BCC) and delivery of quality health services related to malnutrition in the intervention communities. These activities will be carried out with the purpose to generate evidence by assessing, comparing and examining the efficiency of the intervention with the public sector health service delivery model concerning malnutrition. The obtained evidence will be transformed for the development of future policies and actions plans to counter the prevailing situation of malnutrition in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Moving On ABC Plus intervention for Breast Cancer Survivors
data.projectDigest: Breast cancer survivors may experience difficulties with sleeping, eating, low mood and feelings of worry, which can last up to 4-10 years after their last cancer treatment. Feelings of low mood and anxiety may stop a person from living life the way they want to and this in turn can prevent them achieving full recovery. Research found that the lack of breast health awareness, modesty and taboos related to breasts, and lack of national breast cancer screening program were major hurdles in increasing survival rates from breast cancer in Pakistan. We want to assess the effectiveness of programme called ‘Moving on After Breast Cancer’ (ABC) combined with group Cognitive Behaviour Therapy (CBT) (culturally adapted group talking treatment). The combined programme would be ‘Moving on ABC plus’ and will teach mindfulness, relaxation techniques and how to manage low mood and anxiety symptoms. Women will be recruited from Oncology clinics, GP surgeries and voluntary organisations across 4 cities in Pakistan (Karachi, Lahore, Multan, Rawalpindi). Participants will be assigned to either intervention arm or routine treatment. We will also explore the views of health professionals and service users and their carers on the treatment available and barriers to accessing treatment.

data.projectName: National Food and Nutrition Security Program (NFNSP) through SME partnerships in value added agriculture sector
data.projectDigest: Pakistan’s economy, a major contributor to food security, imparts share of 18.9% to GDP, and absorbs 42.3% of labor force. However, farmers largely practice subsistence farming, and only around 35% of farmers sell only when there is a surplus. A key reason for limited farmer business sense, is farmers’ lack of capacity to prepare business proposals for their value added agriculture products. National Food and Nutrition Security Program (NFNSP) will include the selected fruits and vegetables value chains, identified through a process of opportunity assessment during the inception phase. The project is will be targeted for enhanced profitability and capacitated SME,s  to alleviate poverty through product and process transformation of selected value chains in fruits and vegetable processing sector. The three specific objectives of the project are: a) to strengthen the capacities of farmers, particularly women, in fruits and vegetable value chains to increase sales to domestic and foreign markets; b) to strengthen the capacity of farmers through farmer enterprise groups-SME,s,  and business to operate effectively and efficiently; c) to empower food processing SMEs to improve performance and competitiveness to enhance primary production, quality and marketing of agricultural produce; and d) to increase productivity and profitability through adoption of new techniques and technological innovations.

data.projectName: PROBLEMS OF WATER AVAILABILITY IN KARACHI: AN ANALYTICAL STUDY ON THE SUPPLY & DISTRIBUTION AND SEWERAGE SYSTEM
data.projectDigest:
The Proposed Project will focus on the mechanism of supply and distribution system in the largest city of Pakistan, Karachi. The supply from the River Indus comes via canals from Kinjhar, Haleji, Gharo and through conduits to the Dhabeji pumping station. The water is then distributed via conduits and distribution mains by KWSB and private tankers in Karachi. Karachi’s bulk supply is 665 MGD with 15% of it wasted due to technical leakages however this figure varies in different reports. With the growing population and poor management of urban infrastructure, there is shortage of potable water to the domestic consumers, commercial and industrial zones of the metropolitan city of Karachi. According to an estimate, KWSB’s current annual budget (2007-2008) is Rs. 5.3 billion; Rs. 2 to 2.5 billion are recovered as the water and sewerage taxes while the rest is government subsidy. A total of Rs. 18.678 billion are outstanding dues against the government and others. There are a total of 10,000-12,000 tankers, (5000 of which belong to the PTA). About 1,00,000 to 1,20,000 trips are made daily.
Water is available in abundant quantity in Karachi but lack of management in supply and distribution of water by KWSB and by the other means; it is wasted into sewerage creating scarcity of water in the city. Besides a large quantity of water is also wasted into the homes and commercial places by the consumers who should be learnt how to use water in the quantity as per their minimum requirements. In this extensive study, current situation of supply and distribution system of water in all districts of the Karachi city and the adjoining agricultural lands from the reservoir.s. Main partners are KWSB, government bodies, private water suppliers etc.

data.projectName: Development and Prototyping of High Efficiency (>30%) MultijunctionConcentrator Solar Cells
data.projectDigest:
This research is focused onto development of high efficiency (~40%) multifunction solar cells to be used under concentrated sunlight. The prototype solar cells will be deployed on the surface of water lakes at dams (Mangla, Tarbela etc.). This will not only produce electricity for the grid, it will save the water (during daytime) that is used for electricity production. This extra water can be appropriately used for irrigation purposes.
Multiple p-n junctions will provide the opportunity to absorb various parts of radiations coming from the Sun. Thus, the absorption of multiple wavelengths improves the efficiency of solar cell by converting large amount of radiations to electricity. Solar device made up of one p-n junction can have a theoretical efficiency of more than 30%. Whereas, solar cell made up of more than one p-n junctions can produce theoretical efficiency of more than 80%, provided the maximum throughput of solar radiations. This research is focused onto development of high efficiency (~40%) multijunction solar cells to be used under concentrated sunlight.

data.projectName: Harnessing solar energy with an echo system for electricity mobility
data.projectDigest:
The reliance of Pakistan’s energy production on oil and natural gas has adverse effects on our economy while the gas reserves are depleting at an alarming rate. In addition, the hazardous emissions are polluting our environment. The way out of this is to use green energy resources.
We shall be working on the development of smart Four Quadrant Inverter (FQI). This FQI will work as core for solar energy harnessing in energy sectors namely electricity generation and electrical vehicles power train. FQI along with necessary equipment developed shall be able to deliver renewable energy to the national grid as per NEPRA regulations of net metering. The module will also act as the driver circuit for the effective utilization and management of solar energy in Electrical Vehicles (EV). The complete system will generate database for current profiles and future predictions in terms of energy generations. 
Our solution can address the Business-to-Business market but is customized and handy enough for the end user.  Not only focusing on the development of EV kits having on board charger for solar energy, our solution shall be an end user based renewable power project that shall also incorporate the needs of regular house hold customers.

data.projectName: Development of technology platform for prevention and control of haemorrhagic septicemia in livestock: A way forward to ensure food security and economic development
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan exhibits cattle and buffalo populations of 47.8 and 40.0 million, respectively, which are under threat from the haemorrhagic septicemia (HS) disease cause by Pasteurella multocida B:2 infections. Remarkably, the Pakistani buffaloes i.e., Kundi Nili-Ravi and Nili-Ravi, are the best dairy buffalo breed worldwide, but are at most risked animal from HS, which exhibits 100% mortality rate if not treated at very early stage. Death of animal can erode the economic base-line of farmer and counterproductive to food security. Formalin killed whole cell vaccines and antibiotics have reduced the intensity of the massive HS outbreaks, while sporadic outbreaks are still there. Protective-efficacy of these vaccines are not effective against heterologous field strains and also have poor shelf-stability, require refrigeration and prone to deterioration after ~6 months.

In this project, analysis of strains heterogeneity and development of diagnostic assays will be pursued to identify and type the P. multocida strains circulating in Pakistan. Development of modern vaccines (live attenuated and conjugate), improvement in efficacy/shelf-life of killed vaccines, will massively give protection against all types of P. multocida strains. The knowledge and effective vaccine(s) will be handed over to Provincial Veterinary Research Institutes for application to eradicate HS from Pakistan

data.projectName: Antisocial Personality, Emotional Intelligence and Level of Aggressive Behavior among Youth in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Youth is always considered as the cornerstone of the nation for its prosperity and development. Youth determine the future of the country so it is necessary to understand the behaviors of the youth and what are the problems which they are facing and which can hinder their performance. This is a time when everyone tried to exceed in every step of the life so there is need to polish our youth to maintain our nation and for progress (Goleman, 1995).No doubt there are environmental and social factors which determine the tendency of aggressive behavior of the youth, but there are some other personal factors as well which determine the individual differences in the youth. Antisocial personality and emotional intelligence are considered as the affecting factors to increase the tendency of youth's aggressive behavior (Torgersen et al, 2001).
The design of the present study will be descriptive and correlational in nature. In the present study, data will be collected from students between ages 15-18 years at selected colleges of all districts of Pakistan. A self-administered questionnaire will be used as a tool for data collection.. In Pakistan, colleges are the most appropriate place to study and gather data about the youth between the ages 15-18, who are mostly involved to show a greater tendency of aggressive behavior.This study will employ a cross sectional research approach. From all the districts of Pakistan, 10% sample would be selected from each district with employing random sampling techniques.The findings of the current study would be beneficial for policy makers in Pakistan, with focusing teachers in schools and colleges and political leaders to spread awareness among youth to reduce the tendency of aggressive behavior with conducting awareness programs and seminars.

data.projectName: Identification and Development of Wheat Germplasm for Efficient Phosphorus Uptake, Utilization and Allocation through a Fast Generation Cycling System and Molecular Analyses
data.projectDigest:
This century is full of opportunities as well as challenges; the biggest among them is to feed the fast growing population. Pakistan, despite being an Agriculture-based country is still facing the challenge of food security as 18% of the population is under nourished and >40% malnourished. Phosphorus (P) deficiency is one of the major limiting factors of crop production globally as about 30% of world’s arable land is considered to contain low P for plant growth (Vance et al., 2003). The situation is worse in Pakistan, as nearly 80-90% soils have been reported as P-deficient (Rashid and Memon, 2005; GOP, 2012). Phosphorus deficiency generally slows down the processes of carbohydrate assimilation in plant leaves; consequently plant growth and development cannot be continued normally (Memon, 2001; Lambers et al., 2011). Phosphorus deprivation has a large and rapid negative effect on root growth,leaf expansion (Mollier and Pellerin, 1999; Aziz et al., 2011b; Aziz et al., 2014) and grain size in cereals (Delaney et al., 2010). Application of phosphate fertilizers is a general recommendation and a means to ensure sustainable crop production. However, fear of depletion of rock P reserves and environmental issues of P application, warrants to devise strategies to improve P use efficiency in agriculture. Along with that, it is also important to produce P-efficient crops for sustainable agricultural productivity. Plant species and even cultivars within species vary greatly in P-efficiency (Gill et al., 2002; Aziz et al., 2011a; 2014). The genetic variation can be exploited to produce more P efficient wheat plant.
Hence the main goal of this project is to identify and develop wheat germplasm for efficient P uptake, utilization and mobilization through a Fast Generation Cycling Sys

data.projectName: Conceptual Design Study of very Small Modular Reactor (vSMR) for Micro-Grids of Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Electricity grids have traditionally been focused towards large urban centers. Both fossil and nuclear power plants produce 1000 MW(e) for efficient supply of energy at economies of scale. Over the last decades, this “large” approach has evolved for a number of reasons including the environmental impact of large plants, the lack of strategies for meeting flexible demands, the provision of power in more efficient mixed-supply strategies in “smart micro-grids” for off-grid communities, and the portability of energy to sites as and when required. Thus, impetus for developments towards small size, safe and environmentally friendly has attracted the attention of industry towards small modular reactor. Even below the SMR range, is a new vSMR (very Small Modular Reactor) typically less than 20 MW(e) for specialized applications. Advanced micro-nuclear reactors with electrical output typically below 20 MWe are attractive for decentralized micro-grids, are likely to incorporate evolutionary, innovative and passive safety features as well as power conversion technologies of space systems. This proposal is to establish a research base in the scientific basis, engineering design and economic viability leading to market acceptance of a micronuclear reactor based on safe passive safety heat pipe technology and power conversion on portable systems.

data.projectName: :  Indigenous design and development of fume cleaning system for manufacturing and process industry to minimize environmental degradation
data.projectDigest: Cities are rapidly expanding within Pakistan as rural inhabitants are moving to cities in quest of better health, educational and other related facilities. Small and medium sized industrial enterprises (SMEs) are increasing as country is now shifting its economical reliance from agricultural to industrial sector. Existing and new SME are generally unaware about role of their industrial operation in overall environmental deterioration. Fumes emitting from many SMEs contains many hazardous compounds, for instance particulate matter in case of steel smelters and brick kilns, prolonged exposure to such harmful compounds is causing sever health hazards (lung cancer). Legislation bodies are now forcing industries to treat emissions before dumping them into the environment, local industries now relying on import of fume cleaning system as currently they are not being locally developed. Aim of this project is to indigenously design and develop fume cleaning system for nationwide manufacturing and process industries, this will help in cleaning environment and lowering fiscal loads on imports.

data.projectName: Historic Enclaves - An Undermined Entity as Trigger for Social, Cultural and Economic Uplift
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Historic environments in Pakistan have remained under immense threat due to pressures of commercialization and uncontrolled development. Addressing this issue the Heritage Cell, Department of Architecture and Planning, NED University (HC-DAPNED) has spearheaded various heritage awareness initiatives including comprehensive inventory, mapping and documentation of historic quarters in Sindh, and community participatory programs for awareness and safeguarding of heritage. A step forward is to initiate scientific research on identified historic clusters and diagnose issues (hurdles) related to the ongoing deterioration of historic properties. Historic clusters in urban centers and secondary cities of Sindh will be taken up as pilot project case studies to experiment and explore possibilities for urban renewal involving community participation. 
The first phase of research will include comprehensive (multi-disciplinary) investigation in 2-3 identified heritage rich cluster/s in Karachi, presently subject to environmental degeneration of urban spaces and disrepair/ disuse/ under-utilization of historic structures. Primary objective of this investigative research is to develop viable methods and directions for heritage revival, involving interactive approaches engaging primary stakeholders (heritage owners, users, and responsible public sector departments). The prototype module developed in the first stage of research will then be applied and experimented on second tier cities of Sindh including Hyderabad, Sukkur, Shikarpur, Khairpur, Rohri, and Jacobabad. 
Multidisciplinary collaborations are being pursued in the project to strengthen different aspects of issues being addressed through this research.

data.projectName: Preemptive Earth Quake detection from ionosphere scintillations and ground wave motion using machine learning
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The preemptive detection of earthquake is a challenging task as the time between the notable intensity of seismic signals and the actual high intensity earthquake event is very short. This study aims to investigate the machine learning techniques for the preemptive earthquake detection in Pakistan using the ionosphere scintillation, seismic and tectonic plate's movement data.  Some earlier studies have applied supervised machine learning techniques such as Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) on the past seismic data of high intensity earthquakes and reported encouraging results but all these studies are for the post-earthquake disaster scenario. Some studies have reported that 15 to 20 days prior to earthquake occurrence the generation of Raleigh waves and radon gas from earth results in noticeable variation in the ionosphere especially the F2 layer. These variations can be analyzed from the Total Electron Content (TEC) data obtained from the Global Navigation Satellite system (GNSS) receiver. Therefore, if a machine learning classifier is trained on the past seismic, TEC and tectonic plate's movement data, the correlated study is expected to provide improved prediction results. This study will be performed in collaboration with UET Peshawar and Center for Earthquake studies (CES) Islamabad and Institute of Space studies Islamabad for the Northern and Southern areas of Pakistan.

This study will be performed in collaboration with UET Peshawar and Center for Earthquake studies (CES) Islamabad and Institute of Space studies Islamabad for the Northern and Southern areas of Pakistan.

Therefore, improving child nutrition through fish based powder and fish base agri- food solution is one of the best and most critical investments through this project in Pakistan can make. Prime Minister Imran Khan also highlighted the issue of stunting in Pakistan which shows the high commitment of the present government towards addressing nutrition issues.

data.projectName: A regional-scale integrated risk assessment and predictive modeling and simulation framework for arsenic water management and remediation in Punjab
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest:
The proposed research aims at advancing science in the priority area of Water Management and Sustainability. The research objective is to develop an integrated and validated risk assessment and predictive modeling framework for arsenic water management and remediation for Punjab. This work will provide a basis for a nation-wide management framework for other contaminants. 

The work is motivated by the fact that groundwater aquifers, contaminated with arsenic, serve as a primary source of drinking water for the majority of Pakistan’s population. Despite the known arsenic related health hazards, little or no work has been done to fully understand the problem at hand to mitigate and prevent the spread of arsenic contaminated groundwater in Pakistan. What is worse is that arsenic contaminated water and health risks are not well documented. 

To enable stakeholders to make informed decisions on this hazard,  new research developments on several topics are needed. The main topics  to be considered are (i) arsenic monitoring; (ii) field site characterization and assessment of water quality and health risks; (iii) assessment of the technologies for remediation of arsenic polluted water; (iv) development of virtual  simulation framework for surface and subsurface arsenic transport; (v) development of computer simulation framework for water remediation; (vi) lab validation of the remediation technologies.

data.projectName: Pakistan Citizen Rahbar: Inclusive and Carbon Neutral Public Service Delivery through ICT
data.projectDigest: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Provincial Secretariat and Directorates facilitate citizens through many public services (approximately 70 including vehicle licences, birth certificates, domiciles, pharmacy licences etc.). These services are seldom sensitive to citizen voice/engagement, use of technology and environmental sustainability. As for citizen engagement, a lack of literacy and education impedes citizen understanding of the processes involved in availing different services effectively. Use of technology too is seldom inbuilt in services delivery mechanisms to reduce time, cost, and improve transparency for services. Another lacuna is a total lack of including environmental footprint of public services, an angle that needs immediate attention in face of ever increasing climatic disruption.  Keeping in view these three integrated challenges, many questions could be posed; how to provide efficient public service delivery in the constraint budgetary environment; how to engage citizens more deeply for citizen centric public service delivery; how to seamlessly integrate ICTs and emerging technologies to reduce the cost and increase convenience, and finally how to reduce the carbon footprint and present actionable data for strategic and policy interventions. The proposed Pakistan Citizen Rahbar (PCR) integrates the six WPs through a systems-based approach in such a way that they provide inputs to each other for achieving the common goal of enhancing the public service delivery through citizen engagement by using a set of tools and methods inspired by ICT and AI.

After quantification different cost effective detoxification techniques will be employed including chemical , biological and some physical process.

data.projectName: Fresh Produce Supply Chain Ecosystem at Lesser Pricing for Consumer and Better Incentive for Farmer and Land Owner
data.projectDigest:
Let’s strengthen farmer by devising a system where farmers have more earnings, attracting new labor force for farming for food security, utilization of free land for farming, fresh produce supply to consumer at lesser price, show produce traceability for better taste, freshness and quality and ultimately achieve food security and sustainability of food ecosystem. 
Farmer’s produce reaches consumer through a distribution network from farm to consumer. Farmers receive 30-35% share of price paid by consumer for produce of farmer and rest goes to distribution people. However, the effort of farmer is much more than of people involved in distribution network. The project will develop online app and website for farmers to showcase their produce and consumers purchase. Agriculture value chain will manage delivery of produce from farm to consumers. Produce wastage is also expected to be reduced by such system as the overall process becomes efficient.
Other objective is to grow produce over unutilized lands in urban areas: plots in colonies, government and academic institutions, and several kilometers long boundary walls for vertical farming. Similarly, there are lot of factories, malls, academic and Government buildings etc. where roof top green-houses can be built.
