data.projectName: Green Recycling Method for Lead from Scrap Batteries
data.projectDigest: Lead, sulfur dioxide (SO2), and carbon dioxide (CO2) are the major pollutants having huge negative impact on environment creating lots of health issues alongside global warming. WHO report of 2017 reveals that air, water, soil, dust and food including vegetables, fruits, sheep, goats, fish of different parts of the world are contaminated by lead. It is estimated that lead exposure has accounted for over 500 thousand deaths worldwide. Furthermore, WHO strongly recommend proper policy making and enforcement to minimize its worst effects on environment and health. Electrolytes, lead and lead alloy grid, lead paste, organics and plastics, are the major components of lead-acid battery that are potential risk sources not only for the environment but for human health causing kidney disorders, anemia and nervous system damages. Furthermore, global warming, acid rain and several other climatic changes occur due to the release of pollutants such as sulphur dioxide and carbon dioxide that consequently have adverse effects on the health of workers and local community. Traditionally used smelting process for reclamation of lead from scrap batteries is performed at high temperatures and produce a large amount of these harmful pollutants to the environment. Hence, a green, cost-effective, recycling approach of lead batteries is imperative to minimize these devastating effects to environment and workers. The proposed method for recycling of lead in this project can yield 99.9% pure lead along with benign rather useful by-products like oxygen and sulphuric acid that won’t contribute to increase in environmental pollution or global warming. Hence, the successful execution of this project will have multi-dimensional benefits for environment protection (climate change), health, and energy.

data.projectName: Synthesis of metallic nanowires  and two dimensional Perovskite nanomaterials for solar cell applications to increase efficiency and stability
data.projectDigest:
Energy crisis is a major problem in developing countries of the world including Pakistan which is causing a delay to be in par with developed world. The purpose of this project is to fabricate nanomaterials like nanowires and Perovskites  based solar cell, explore interesting physical phenomena’s and recognize areas which can cause further improvement in energy of the solar cells, train local human resources and propose a prototype with the help of local industry working on photovoltaics. Dye sensitized solar cell (DSSC) is the cell that can give both flexibility, easy fabrication process and transparency and its efficiency is comparable to silicon solar cells but with a lower cost. 
Similarly Perovskite solar cells (PSC) using CH3NH3MX3 (M = Pb or Sn, X = Cl, Br or I) and CH3NH3PbBr3 are also third generation solar cells which are flexible, lightweight, and can be printed roll-to-roll like newsprint to cover walls, windows, and many other flat surfaces.  The obtained information from this project can be used to do research in lithium ion batteries and supercapacitors. The proposed project will help to address the energy crisis by making DSSC and PSC laboratory modules in Pakistan but also to understand basic mechanism and interesting Physics for academic research.

data.projectName: Integrated solar and RF system for continuous all-weather energy harvesting
data.projectDigest: The electromagnetic energy is freely available due to wide range of sources ranging from telecom networks and natural phenomenon such as sunlight and heat radiation. There is lot of emphasis around the scientific community to efficiently tap this free energy for useful purpose i.e., by converting into electricity.  In this context, solar cells are developed, which can convert the visible and near-infrared region of the electromagnetic spectrum into electricity.  For the microwave and infrared region, rectennas can be used to harvest the electromagnetic energy. We will integrate the two different subsystems in one platform that can provide continuous (24 hours), all-weather and self-sufficient energy solution. Moreover, to considerably increase the overall system efficiency, Origami concept (instead of inefficient Sun tracking system) will be used for the first time in this project, which can reduce the cost of land acquisition, deployment, installation and maintenance of the solar power station.

data.projectName: Pharmacogenetic study of drug metabolizing enzyme in association with chemotherapeutic toxicity and designing of a potent inhibitor in acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL)
data.projectDigest: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia is a cancer most frequently reported among the children <16 years of age. The drugs administeration to the leukemia patients is called chemotherapy. The main purpose of chemotherapy is to kill malignant white blood cells. There are some side effects of chemotherapeutic drugs that can occur during/decades after the treatment. The most reported side effects are malfunctioning of heart and enlargement of liver and spleen. These side effects highly decline the quality of life of the patients as well as increase the complication during the treatment or even contribute to the mortality. The genetic makeup of each individual is different and the changes among the individuals can increase the risk of side effects. Therefore, the first part of the study includes identification of those changes in DNA. The activity of enzymes that convert the chemotherapeutic drugs into its metabolites (chemicals) can be decreased if the extract of herbal plants is administered to the patient. Therefore, the second part includes the drug designing using the herbal plants to reduce the production of metabolites (chemicals) that induce the side effects. The lead compound will be of herbal origin, low cost and will be easily found in flora of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Governance with Particular Focus on Foreign Aided Projects in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
The proposed research aims at finding answer to the question as to why Foreign Aided projects failed to bring desirable outcomes in Pakistan. Since the development continues to be a perpetual challenge for the country, the Foreign Aid, given the scarcity of indigenous resources, will continue to be an essential element of development strategy. The proposed research, mainly divided in two stages, is planned to go through seven phases. The first stage pertains to identification of issues, problems, and challenges in the existing system of foreign aided project management. The second stage deals with finding executable and effective solutions of the problems identified.
 In this context, the Priority Thematic Area of this research proposal is Governance with particular focus on Foreign Aided Projects in Pakistan. Governance embraces the entire spectrum of public policy considerations from policy at the top to the service/value delivery to the intended beneficiary. With this vantage point, the specific goal of the research will be to develop a Foreign Aided Projects Management System. To this end, in this age of IT and Digitization, software and applications are basic ingredients of the solutions where many loopholes of the existing system can be plugged with research-based IT intervention.

data.projectName: IoT security threat and incident control system
data.projectDigest: The IoT devices are usually connected to the existing networks and become part of the enterprise networks. The resource-constraint nature of IoT device raises several security challenges. Eventually, it jeopardises the existing network since the enterprise network security solutions do not mandate the security of new emerging IoT protocols and operating systems. Moreover, there does not exist any anti-virus tools and techniques that can run on these resource constrained devices to protect them from malware. These malwares are usually injected through firmware updates or exploiting any known vulnerability or weak security configuration. To circumvent these challenges, we propose a well-engineered infrastructure for IoT-based security threat and incident controlling. The proposed IoT security threat and incident controlling system integrates many cutting-edge technologies like IDS, endpoint detection and response (EDR), security incident management (SIM), artificial intelligence (AI), etc., to effectively protect and secure the IoT devices and network from the cyber-attacks. The proposed solution will not only secure and protect the IoT network and devices from cyber-attack but also rectify the security system in case it succumbed and limit the cyber damage as well.

data.projectName: Improvement of broiler meat quality through the use of Probiotics (Bacillus clausii)
data.projectDigest:
The shelf life of white meat is less due to early decline in pH, small fibre size and early drip loss. Other most important factor affecting broiler meat quality is Salmonella infection in broilers. The salmonella infection in broiler causes various gastrointestinal diseases in consumers. Antibacterial drugs against Salmonellosis and antibiotics growth promoters in poultry also cause antibiotic resistance in broiler meat consumers. Antibiotics growth promoters been banned in European countries. To control over these problems Probiotics are the best choice. It improves digestibility of nutrients, meat quality and growth performance and boost up immunity of broilers. It also increases breast meat quality of broilers through increase in muscle fibre cross sectional area, water holding capacity and decrease early protein degeneration of muscles. The current project is designed to evaluate the effect of Bacillus clausii on broiler meat quality parameters, growth performance, immune status, and intestinal histomorphology and serum biochemical parameters in healthy broiler chicken. Special objectives are
1.	To control the Salmonellosis infection and improvement of the meat quality in broiler chicken. 
2.	Provision of antibiotic residues free meat to broiler meat consumers.
3.	To minimize cost per kg bird and medication charges.

Antibacterial drugs against Salmonellosis and antibiotics growth promoters in poultry also cause antibiotic resistance in broiler meat consumers. Antibiotics growth promoters been banned in European countries. To control over these problems Probiotics are the best choice. It improves digestibility of nutrients, meat quality and growth performance and boost up immunity of broilers. It also increases breast meat quality of broilers through increase in muscle fibre cross sectional area, water holding capacity and decrease early protein degeneration of muscles. The current project is designed to evaluate the effect of Bacillus clausii on broiler meat quality parameters, growth performance, immune status, and intestinal histomorphology and serum biochemical parameters in healthy broiler chicken. Special objectives are
1.	To control the Salmonellosis infection and improvement of the meat quality in broiler chicken. 
2.	Provision of antibiotic residues free meat to broiler meat consumers.
3.	To minimize cost per kg bird and medication charges.

data.projectName: Minerals for Collective Prosperity-The Clusters Approach
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan is rich with mineral resources. Unfortunately these resources are not properly exploited. Currently most of the minerals remained untapped and some are exported in the raw form. If these minerals are upgraded locally, this will result in large number of jobs & business opportunities, reduced dependence on imports and saving of precious foreign exchange. 
In this project, local minerals will be upgraded; some metals such as directly reduced iron, lead and zinc etc will be extracted on lab scale. Coatings will be made of some minerals such as chromite which are expected to have much better or at least comparable properties with hard chrome plating (HCP).  Its advantages include high corrosion and erosion resistance which can enhance the service life of equipment and components such as hydropower turbine blades. Chromite based powder coatings are environmental friendly, cost effective, simple and mass production method compared to HCP. 
Electro-ceramic materials will be used to develop devices for industrial and commercial applications. This project will be executed by four groups; these include, Mineral Processing, Coatings, Electroceramics devices and Commercialization groups.
The focus is on training of youth on indigenous resources, establishing linkages among different stakeholders and connecting the dots.

data.projectName: Sustainable Housing in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The rapid growth of population and urbanization has created enormous problems for Pakistan. Census of 2017 identified rapid urbanization in Pakistan along with population growth. Pakistan is facing a precarious situation of housing for all. The two important issues that are related to the housing in Pakistan are; shortage of housing and lack of sustainable houses. Sustainable housing refers to the internal and external safety of human beings by focusing on economic,environmental and social conditions. With the changing scenario of climate now housing is not just provision of a roof but it is crucial for sustainable housing development - the harmonious association between social, economic and environmental dimension in housing.

data.projectName: Identification of salt tolerance genes in halophytes
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Salinity is one of major abiotic stresses constituting a serious threat to agricultural productivity in the world. More than 6.8 million hectares of Pakistan is affected by salinity due to faulty irrigation practices. Halophytes, that are distributed in the desert region have developed multiple protective mechanisms in the process of long-term evolution, therefore, can grow successfully under saline environment. Plantation of halophytes in the affected area and selecting the best salinity resistant species is a major milestone needed to combat climate change. The biomass production and rate of growing parameters of the cultivated species will have to be measured and analyzed statistically and then the most resistant species selected based on the growth and yield parameters. In the laboratory, transcriptomic and differential gene expression (DGE) profiling of the selected species in response to salt treatment and osmotic stress will be analyzed for identification of stress-tolerance genes from transcriptomic database and DGE profiling. This project will serve as a borderline between basic and applied research where salt tolerant genes will be identified in the laboratory to make more climate-resilient crops and rangeland will be protected by the identification of most suitable halophytes.

data.projectName: Sustainable Energy Based Intelligent Health Care Monitoring and Therapeutic System with Biotelemetry for Primary Health and Disaster Management
data.projectDigest: Currently we are facing number of challenges , some of these challenges are lack of infrastructure and primary health care , Energy shortfall and unavailability of electricity, Lack of qualified medical health professional in rural areas of Pakistan and no one want to live in difficult conditions like desert or mountains, Transportation of patients for primary health care is problematic from rural areas. Climate Conditions cause flood almost every year and large population of the country is affected. All these factors cause increase death rate of adults, neonatal, premature baby and pregnant women. The Lack of primary health care which care causing death before the life begin, maternal and adults is one of our national challenge. Currently there is no solution available to address this grand challenge and Pakistan need to overcome this challenge using latest technology. . In this grand challenge funding application, a sustainable energy based intelligent health care monitoring and therapeutic system with biotelemetry for primary health and disaster management is proposed to overcome the poor health care facilities in rural areas of Pakistan. The basic idea behind this project is attain bio signals and vital parameters from a patient and then transmit the data wirelessly to a server to perform auto diagnosis suing machine learning then send the data to a physician for his/her feedback and subsequent remedial actions from staff present at the remote site. The overall system acquires and processes data of three types of population; adults, neonatal and pregnant women. The system not only receives signals from the human body but also provides therapy if required. For adults, the system provides heat stroke therapy and electrical stimulation for pregnant  women

data.projectName: Nature Based Solutions for Water Management in the Urban Context
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Globally fresh water resources are stressed by increasing water demands, environmental degradation and the multi-faceted impacts of climate change. Traditionally, the human-built or grey infrastructure approach has been adopted for managing the urban water resources. Conventional wastewater treatment systems entail heavy investment and high operating and energy costs. The contemporary wastewater treatment systems in most of the developing countries including Pakistan fail to treat wastewater satisfactorily. Reasons for failure include lack of local expertise, high maintenance costs and poor governance. Recently, NBS are being implemented in different parts of the world to mitigate the severe climatic, environmental, economic and societal challenges. NBS represent more efficient and cost-effective solutions than traditional approaches as they are energy efficient, resource efficient and resilient to change. Examples of the nature-based engineered solutions already used in water management include green roofs, constructed wetlands and vegetated infiltration basins. The continuous and unplanned expansion of Pakistan’s largest city Karachi has resulted in swelling of the gap between water supply and demand. Nature-based solutions can be implemented for treating the city's large volume of wastewater and the treated water can then be reused thus augmenting the current stressed water supply system. This project will focus on implementing NBS at intervention sites and the treated water will be reused for reforestation. The benefits of this project will include integration of NBS in urban areas for water management and mitigation of climate change impacts.

data.projectName: Digital Agriculture to Ensure Food Security and Sustainable Development of Farmers and Environment in Changing Climate
data.projectDigest: Agriculture is considered as backbone of Pakistan’s economy as it contributes ~22% to the GDP of the country. It also accounts for ~80% of the total export earnings of the country. Thus, agriculture is playing a vital role in ensuring the food security, reducing poverty and improving the economic growth of Pakistan. There are many challenges to agriculture and few of them are global warming and climate change. Pakistan includes in top 10 vulnerable countries in world. So, this international platform will be helpful to mitigate or address these challenges, we have to use some innovative techniques to increase our production technology and to utilize expert opinion from international experts with interaction to national delegates/participants.  There are two main aims of these proposed challenges. By using digital agricultural technologies for vegetable and crop production and secondly to use diverse range of soils to mitigate the impacts of climate change by covering maximum area under vegetation. We are involving researchers from USA and Middle East for betterment of agricultural products and to enhance the value addition so that agricultural products can be exported and maximum earning from foreign exchange as well as by increasing the livelihood of small holding farmers.

data.projectName: :  An integrated approach for agricultural monitoring based on Internet of Things  (IoT), remote sensing and deep learning
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: The agriculture sector poses great importance due to its impact on economic development of the country. Due to dearth of technology-based solutions, Pakistan is still reliant on costly legacy systems based on manual operations and driven by farmer’s knowledge base.  The proposed research will develop innovative Internet of Things (IoT), deep learning and low altitude remote sensing based indigenous solutions aimed to modernize the agriculture sector in Pakistan, offering wide area coverage and a holistic picture of crop health status. The key activities of proposed system include (a)development of IoT nodes and AgriEye for disease detection, (b)nitrogen content mapping, and (c)crop yield estimation. The IoT nodes will consist of sensors including soil moisture, soil temperature, humidity, air temperature, ammonia, methane etc. The AgriEye will be an electromechanical trolley powered by solar energy with a high resolution camera installed on it for capturing a closer view of crop for (i) monitoring spread of rust disease and its severity level (ii)crop-yield estimation through wheat-stalk counting based on image processing. The proposed research would be useful in taking remedial measures for preventing crop damage and maximizing crop yield by real time monitoring and decision making, improving crop productivity and contributing to national economy.

data.projectName: Biological evaluation of Anti-viral and Anti-protozoal activity of traditionally used medicinal plants in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Recent studies have demonstrated that many antiprotozoal and antiviral drugs become extreme drug resistance against the Entamoeba histolytica and respiratory tract viruses respectively. The present study will be conducted to evaluate the alternate treatment for amebiasis and respiratory tract infection caused by viruses. Hundreds of the plants will be collected from the local areas of Pakistan and china. All plants extracts will be prepared. E.histolytica and three varities of pseudovirions will be cultured. In vitro, all plants antiviral and antiprotozoal activities will be eliminated by high screeing. Then, Total 40 albino rats will be divided into eight groups, G1 will be the control group with chow maintance diet at 48g/kg body weight. G2 will have amebiasis treated with saline solution. G3 will have amebiasis treated with Metronidazole (MDR) at 300mg/kg body weight. G4-7 will have amebiasis and treated with 4 drugs with maximum efficacy against E.histolytica  and poly herbal formulation (comprise all 4 drugs) respectively for 5 days. After 5 days all the animals will be sacrificed; blood and organ tissues will be collected. The stool samples will be collected from each group. Elisa test will be performed for the evaluation of presence E.histolytica among the treated groups. DNA will be extracted from the stool samples and different test including PCR, gel electropherosis, pyrosequencing and whole genome will be performed. Anti-viral activity of the 10 herbal medicines (including above mentioned) will be evaluated from the experiment center, Shandong University of traditional Chinese medicine. This product will be helpful to treat the amoebic dysentery and respiratory tract infection caused by viruses in less expensive way without any side effects.

data.projectName: Industry 4.0 based Integrated Soft Printed Electronics Artificial Implantable Muscle for Cardiac Diseases
data.projectDigest: Despite major advances in cardiovascular medicine, heart disease remains a leading cause of death worldwide. The adult mammalian heart has only a limited capacity for regeneration and, consequently, the cardiomyocytes (CMs) that are lost to ischemic injury are typically replaced by fibrotic scar tissue that can no longer transmit electrical signals or contract, both of which are necessary for smooth and forceful heartbeats. As per data provided by the Punjab Institute of Cardiology, the average heart transplant cost lies between 10-20 Million Rupees with a survival rate of 75% or less in developed countries. In order to address this global challenge, the research objective of this proposal is the development of a novel soft printed electronics-based artificial implantable cardiac muscle device by forming cell and electronic sheets at a micro level, stacking them so that cardiac cells can be regenerated, and ECG can be monitored simultaneously. The cost of the cardiac patch will be 80% less of conventional transplant cost thus making it more feasible for middle-low income countries. The further successful development of the heart patch may lead to benefit more than 2.5 million people in Pakistan and more than 50 million people worldwide awaiting a heart transplant.

data.projectName: Development of next generation Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD) vaccine
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: The foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) is highly contagious and economically devastating disease of cloven-hoofed animals. Due to FMD, the domestic markets of the country suffer an estimated loss of 8-9 billion Rs/annum. The control and prevention of FMD by vaccination remains unsatisfactory as the existing FMD vaccines are not suitable for eradication because of 1) short term protection, 2) short shelf life and heat sensitivity, 3) lack of maintenance of cold chain from production to field and requirement of high containment facility for growing vaccine or live virus. These drawbacks warrant the urgent of next generation FMD vaccine with an improved profile, capable of preventing the viral infection including clinical signs and symptoms and also contain important antigen markers to allow differentiation of infected animals from vaccinated ones. The central goal of the proposed research project is to develop genetically engineered leaderless killed FMD-LL3B3D marker vaccine that overcomes the drawback of existing chemically inactivated FMD vaccines. FMD-LL3B3D vaccine will contain a deletion in leader protease (Lpro) gene and two marker mutations in 3B and 3D non-structural genes of the virus, thus providing a safe platform for the production of inactivated vaccine at BSL-2 level.

data.projectName: Biofilm – biochar –Plant interaction model for saline soil reclamation: turning whole plant into biofuels
data.projectDigest:
From many decades, in Pakistan salinity is among one of the major problems of cultivable land  devastation and degradation. It result in decrease in soil fertlilty, crop yield, agricultural productivity and soil biodiversity. Pakistan’s economic development is dependent upon agriculture. In this context the reclamation of saline areas is always on high priority. 
Use of Biochar as an augmented fertilizer in soil and being accessible input for agriculture, could help to rehabilitate saline áreas. Due to large surface area & internal structure biochar particles act as an excellent  habitat and  surface  for bacterial attachment which subsequently form  mono and multispecies bio?lms. In biofilm formation, expolysaccharides and the cell to cell communication is needed.  Biochar type, process of formation affect the cell to cell communication of soil microflora. Biofilms have different exopolyssachrides, functional group, osmolytes and proteins which help plants to grow under saline conditions.  Hence biochar –biofilm interaction is helpful to tune the biogeochemical cycles and soil structure.  The aim is to use this Biofilm –biochar- plant interaction for reclamation of  wasted saline soils by growing cool biofuel crops. Once the plants adapted to saline conditions they can be used for production of biofuels. Overall project will address water-food-energy-health-poverty relationship.

data.projectName: National Center for Genomics
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: The tendency of cousin marriages has resulted in a high incidence of genetic disorders in Pakistan. Treatment for these disorders is either unavailable or beyond affordability. However, informed reproductive decisions assisted by genetic screening can prevent further affected births and reduce disease burden. NIBGE is running a prevention program since 2008 for two disorders, ?-thalassemia and brain tumors, and has screened more than 5,000 families. However, financial constraint and human resource deficiency are the main limiting factors in expanding the spectrum of this program.This project has been designed to upscale our prevention program by establishing a National Center for Genomics (NCG). Families with ?-thalassemia, genetic deafness, primary microcephaly, intellectual disability, eye disorders,brain tumors, congenital heart diseases, inborn errors of metabolism and breast cancers will be diagnosed by clinicians and genetically screened by Researchers. The information generated will enable families and physicians to prevent further births with genetic disorders. Establishment of NCG is need of the time in this country of 220 million people for not only rehabilitating patients in short term but also to control diseases in the long run.NCG will also train researchers for screening programs in other parts of the country.

NIBGE is running a prevention program since 2008 for two disorders, ?-thalassemia and brain tumors, and has screened more than 5,000 families. However, financial constraint and human resource deficiency are the main limiting factors in expanding the spectrum of this program.This project has been designed to upscale our prevention program by establishing a National Center for Genomics (NCG). Families with ?-thalassemia, genetic deafness, primary microcephaly, intellectual disability, eye disorders,brain tumors, congenital heart diseases, inborn errors of metabolism and breast cancers will be diagnosed by clinicians and genetically screened by Researchers. The information generated will enable families and physicians to prevent further births with genetic disorders. Establishment of NCG is need of the time in this country of 220 million people for not only rehabilitating patients in short term but also to control diseases in the long run.NCG will also train researchers for screening programs in other parts of the country.

data.projectName: Enhancing export competitiveness of surgical industries and supporting health sector through development of next generation implant materials.
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Pakistan has been ranked highest in the vitamin D deficiency index (after India and Kuwait) that eventually lead to the bone related issues. State of the art implants are therefore required not only to address alarmingly increasing local needs but also to enhance market share of Pakistan in the international market. It is worth mentioning that global orthopaedic implant market accounted to around $ 46 billion in the 2017 and is forecasted to reach $ 67 billion in 2025 while Pakistan has been able to capture mere 0.75% of the total world market of surgical instruments. Aseptic loosening is the most important issue currently faced by implants manufacturers worldwide which resulted in the failure of implants and in the need of multiple revision surgeries.  A meeting with representatives of surgical instruments manufacturers association of Pakistan (SIMAP) revealed that successful development of implant materials capable of overcoming aseptic loosening may help in creating an edge of local manufacturers over international competitors. As a result, market share of Pakistan in international orthopaedic implants market may significantly improve. The proposed project is therefore submitted under Development Economics thematic area and is aimed at addressing the problem of aseptic loosening of implants by developing novel implant materials. In this regards, new methods internationally patented by PI and his international collaborator will be used for development of new materials that can overcome stress shielding – leading contributor of aseptic loosening. Surface modification and characterization will be carried out to improve biological response of these materials followed by their detailed in-vitro biological characterization to evaluate their functional response.

data.projectName: Small community water treatment systems
data.projectDigest: Access to pure drinking water is a basic human right, but decent water treatment is still highly ignored in Pakistan. In small residential communities which often lack water treatment systems and lack the ability to control other potential contaminants such as salinity, heavy metals, toxic micropollutants and arsenic, families typically rely on boiling to inactivate water borne pathogens. The significance, production activity and investment in the membrane sector continues to increase. data.projectName: Development of a Smart and Resource Efficient Irrigation System by Assessment of Water, Food and Energy Nexus
data.projectDigest:
In Pakistan, traditionally rotation base approach is used to provide share of irrigation water to the farmers and homogeneous irrigation is applied over the entire field. Homogeneous irrigation of the entire field might not be resource efficient at all, because some parts might be irrigated which do not necessarily need irrigation water, while others might not be irrigated enough for optimal crop growth. As a consequence, too many resources might be used in terms of irrigation water and energy for pumping. The challenges in sustainable and resource efficient irrigation system are manifold. First, the underlying heterogeneity of the field has to be known. Second, the influence of these subsurface heterogeneities on the water balance and crop growth has to be known, and third, the irrigation system has to be adapted in a way that only those areas are irrigated which do need additional water.
The overall objective of this project is to come up with vibrant and innovative socio-technical approaches concerning development and validation of Smart and Resource Efficient Irrigation System (SREIS) by aiming at optimization of the linkages within the WFE nexus and overcome the problem of homogeneous irrigation of entire fields. The SREIS will be based on Internet of Things (IoT) and shall be able to irrigate heterogeneous crop stands with optimal water supply, and therefore, reduce the total needed irrigation water and energy consumption for tubewells. An integrated assessment of WFE nexus will be carried out to understand the tradeoff and synergies for better irrigation water management in drip and central pivot irrigation methods. The final product of this project will be a smart and resource efficient irrigation system, which can be easily adapted to other regions of Pakistan.

data.projectName: ICT based - Easily Accessible Professional Training for Every Pakistani
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is the country of more than 220 Million and getting a good education/professional/other skill is the right for every citizen. Pakistanis living in the big cities can somehow manage to get good trainings with the availability of good teachers/professors/instructors and infrastructures to be available for class room teaching/trainings. On the other hand, people/students living in outskirts/suburbs/country side are deprived of direct class room interaction with those. To cope with this problem, we intend to design a couple of different ICT based-training frameworks (based on either STEM, Robotics, Haptics simulations, Virtual/Augmented Reality or Haptic/direct interaction with Real Environment etc.,), which are divided to cover every citizen according to their field of interest. The focus could be on building a rapid prototyping framework, that permits to quickly set up courses for remote training in arbitrary domains. Moreover, those trainees who are living in the cities can participate in the training either by visiting the training centers or via online training facility. In addition, those trainees living suburbs/country side will either be provided training through online interaction of Virtual/Augmented Reality or Haptic/direct interaction with real Environment and in some cases a well-equipped mobile training van may be sent to that sub-urban area to provide the training setup that may be connected the real/ virtual training module at the near/major city. The potential training areas covers the following but not limited to STEM, medical, health care, safety, security, law-enforcement, disaster management, civic sense, civil defense, agriculture, engineering, automation, vocational, sports, arts and many more.

data.projectName: Title: M-Learning Based Cognitive Assessment and Intervention Tool for Autistic Children
data.projectDigest: A primary aim of the proposed research is to develop m-learning based serious game suite, called TinyHands. An objective behind the development of TinyHands is to replace the expensive and tedious traditional assessment and intervention mechanism for the children having developmental delays (e.g. autism spectrum disorder (ASD)) with an inexpensive and entertaining solution. TinyHands aims to focus on ASD children that suffer due to developmental delays in visual performance, labeling of objects, play and leisure, basic mathematical and fine motor skills. TinyHands will be deployed in the collaborated autistic center where a series of empirical research will be carried out under a supervised environment with mild-ASD children. The planned research will continuously examine their game analytics, playability and playfulness in absence as well as presence of the encouragers and/or discouragers. This will reveal feasibility level of TinyHands for learning, intervention and assessment of the targeted functional areas and also provide valuable insights about the acceptability of the m-learning games for mild-ASD children. The conclusions derived via the proposed research will contribute substantially to the field of psychology and will have substantial implications for the development of more effective, safer, and yet entertaining treatments for the different range of ASD children.

data.projectDigest:

In addition, there is very limited check and balance on judiciary performance, especially on timeline of case decisions. The governing issues thus distort the judicial process to the extent of causing delays in justice delivery, unjust outcomes, and consequential effects on the society at large in terms of erosion of confidence in the judicial system.

This will be achieved through efficient data mining and robust software applications including case management, documenting file notes and records, automated tasks scheduling, management of litigation, establishing of a centralized digitized record and an online database. data.projectName: IoT Based Smart Solid Waste Management in Smart Cities
data.projectDigest:
Poor Solid Waste Management at Pakistan has been known to result in numerous health and environmental hazards. In addition to raising issues such as surface water contamination, soil contamination and air pollution, lack of effective waste management solutions also result in loss of revenue which could be generated through recycling. This project proposes to integrate the thematic areas of Climate change and Environment, Urban Planning and Information Technology & Telecom to deal with the challenge of Solid Waste Management at Pakistan. The scope of the project is based on using the emerging technologies of Internet of Things (IoT), Machine Learning and Crowdsourcing to solve the major challenge of solid waste management at Pakistan. It has been proposed to install a smart bin black-box at 100 locations at the major urban cities: Karachi & Islamabad, and to use crowdsourcing for identification of trash locations. The smart bin will be equipped with cameras and will transmit an immediate alarm notifying about the overflowing garbage. As a result, the garbage collectors and relevant authorities will be timely notified about the level of garbage being reached at each bin. 
In addition to using the cutting-edge technologies for waste management, it has also been proposed to utilize the community participation in the process. data.projectName: Feasibility Investigation of vibration based Structural Health Monitoring using wireless sensors nodes network
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: This research covers the continuous autonomous detection of defect of a structure automatically based on observations through wireless sensors nodes network. The system consist of necessary software and hardware within a specified architecture of service-oriented approach. A number of sensors at different locations of structures are interconnected with nodes that are connected to computer operational system through internet. The system process through algorithms and identifies the status of the structure based on statistical methods. The investigation will be carried out on prototype structure and then a selected preexisting structure. The system can be installed in new as well as old structures. This research is important for earthquake regions like Balakot, Quetta, speedy windy zones of Balochistan near Gawadr and Karachi Ports, and heavy traffic bridges of Metros, BRT, and Highway in Pakistan. This system enables us to monitor our structures (high rise buildings and long bridges) at every interval of time comfortably in an office.

data.projectName: Smart Farming Based Decision Support System For Food Security
data.projectDigest: Smart Farming techniques are used worldwide, but Pakistan an agribusiness nation is lacking the use of it. The progress about the crops is collected manually and there is no centralized national database where the progress of crops can be collected from the deployed sensors in real-time followed by solid policy decisions. Therefore, there is a need of Solar Powered Real-time Monitoring system in smart decision making for optimal yield. This project aims to develop an integrated system using remote units and android application to collect real-time data for processing, and analysis to improve the overall farming operations and management for different crops of Pakistan. Machine Learning based algorithms will give suggestions on the basis of historic trends and previous records. The proposed software will have the capability of integrating and analyzing data streams from multiple nodes deployed in farms in Pakistan. Project will be executed in collaboration with the Sectoral collaborator Potato Research Institute (PRI) Govt. of Punjab, Sahiwal, Pakistan. This Project is an important step for Digital Pakistan initiated by the current Govt. It will assist in the alignment of the ministries involved in the agriculture sector and improve the governance of related federal and provincial departments and regulators.

data.projectName: Multi-omics approach to comprehensively characterize the food and water quality in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: Increasing demands of agricultural and food products resulting from rapid increase in human populations have created food quality concerns. In farming industry, to increase the milk and meat production, different hormones are extensively used which can severely affect the human health. Similarly, overuse of antibiotics in farming is one of the factors contributing to antibiotic resistance in humans. In Pakistan, food-borne pathogens are a big issue as many diseases including polio, hepatitis, typhoid and diarrhea have been associated with food- or water-borne pathogens. Water available to common man in Pakistan is also contaminated with pathogens, agrochemicals, and several inorganic metals, which can lead to various illnesses including cancer, infertility, kidney failure and defects in neural development. Overall effect of low quality food on healthcare has enormous economic and social impact.  To devise an effective regulatory policy for ensuring a safe and contaminant-free supply of food and water for public consumption, a comprehensive profiling of these contaminants in major food components is required. In this project we aim to apply omics based approach by combining metagenomics, food metabolomics, inorganic analysis and artificial intelligence to comprehensively profile the quality of food and water in Pakistan so that precise intervention could be advised.

data.projectName: Disaster Risk-Based Decision-Making Tool for Interdependent Regional Workforce Systems
data.projectDigest:
Natural disasters, such as pandemics (such as, dengue and corona), can cause mortality and morbidity in the population in an economic region. Due to its contagious nature, outbreaks of a pandemic have prolonged effects on the working population, which consequently affects workforce levels available to industry sectors. Workforce disruptions in a pandemic can adversely impact regional economic productivity as workforce contributes significantly in the production of commodities.

data.projectName: Digital Health Solution (DHS) for Rural Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Availability of specialized consultants for diagnostics, medication and consultancy is missing in most of the rural parts of the country. Baqai Institute of Diabetotolgy (BIDE) and Atomic Energy Medical Centre (AMC) Hospital are providing remarkable health service to diabetic and cancer patients respectively. Both of the organizations have patients from remote part of the countries. Because of the expertise available at these institutions several hospitals need to communicate with them on frequent basis. Secondly, their patients need regular checkup after medication.  Through this project we aimed to establish a country level digital platform to solve the above mentioned challenges. A platform HealTalk will provide a secure basic communication: one-one, along with conferencing and data (medical) exchange capabilities all over the country. The HealTalk will be used further to be integrated with web and mobile applications for diagnostics purposes. At remote locations digital gadgets, IoT solutions, and other wearable solutions will be placed to measure the vital signs of patients in real time. Mobile phone based applications and wearable devices will be used for patient tracking and health monitoring. 
Virtual Clinics will be established with the collaboration of BIDE and AEMC across the Pakistan where medical technician along with the basic telemedicine equipment will be placed. Experts from BIDE and AEMC will be using the basic facility for monitoring, medication, prescription and consultancies with the help of proposed digital communication platform HealTalk. Furthermore cases with complexities demanding conference like discussion among medical experts will be facilitated through the same system.

data.projectName: Decision Support System to Enhance Resilience of Housing, Infrastructure, and Communities to Climate Change and Natural Disasters
data.projectDigest:
In last couple of decades, Pakistan has experienced a significant increase in losses from natural hazards which include geophysical, hydrological, meteorological and climatological hazards. A further damage increase is expected due to rapid urbanization in risk-prone areas and the effects of climate change on the severity and frequency of these hazards. An improved understanding of risk and cost-effective mitigation measures are required to reduce the impact of climate change and natural hazards on Pakistan economy and communities.

This proposed project will develop a decision support system to enhance the resilience of the housing, infrastructure, and communities in Pakistan and to build capacity to respond to natural hazards and climate change. The project will focus on climate change impacts and three most costly and frequently occurring natural hazards in Pakistan i.e. earthquakes, floods and droughts. The project team consists of experienced researchers from two Pakistani Universities (University of Engineering and Technology Taxila and National University of Science and Technology, Islamabad), one Australian University (RMIT University, Melbourne) and two German Universities (University of Potsdam and Bauhaus University Weimar). 

An asset management model developed for infrastructure, funded by the Asian Development Bank and implemented in Sri Lanka, will be used as the base. The system will be modified and customized for Pakistan and will be expanded to include resilience under disaster events.

The outcome of this research will help property owners, government, planning authorities and emergency services to assess the risks and evaluate various mitigation strategies to reduce current and future risk due to changes in climate and resulting natural disasters.

data.projectName: Optimization and Fabrication of highly efficient and air processed  hybrid Perovskite solar cells
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest:
An efficient way to fulfill the demands of energy without imposing burden on natural resources and further aggravating climate change is the need of the hour. Recently, perovskite solar cells have turned out to be one of the most efficient solar cells, reaching maximum efficiency of 23.7% [1]. Mixed organic-inorganic perovskite solar cells, are known for their excellent electrical and optical properties; high absorption coefficient, high charge mobility and long diffusion lengths [2]. Despite such exceptional characteristics for these materials, the biggest hurdle towards commercialization of perovskite solar cells is their instability and related costs [3].
This project involves the fabrication of hybrid (organic-inorganic) perovskite solar cells in which stability issue can be addressed through compositional engineering, substituting/mixing cation A, and halide ion, X, separately in ABX3 with various elements which changes the crystal structure imparting stability to solar cell. Cost can be addressed by replacing the expensive hole transport material, Spiro-oMeTaD, with cost effective alternative Copper Thiocyanate.  
The proposed research topic will not only be helpful in developing relatively stable, efficient and cost effective new functional layers of hybrid perovskite solar cells but also a big step towards commercialization of perovskite solar cells

data.projectName: Development and implementation of control methods for ticks and tick-borne diseases in rural communities of Punjab, Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Ticks and tick-borne diseases are an important cause of losses to the livestock industry, in particular the production of cattle and small ruminants in tropical and subtropical areas. World-wide losses due to diseases transmitted by ticks and the costs of tick control have been estimated to be in the range of several billion (109) U S dollars annually.
This proposed study will be concerned to the different tick and tick-parasites control methods having a major focus on the development of entomopathogenic fungi, such as Metarhizium anisopliae and Beauveria bassiana, etc. as biocontrol agents against a range of several ticks under laboratory and field conditions, namely Rhipicephalus annulatus, Ixodes scapularis, Rhipicephalus appendiculatus and Amblyomma variegatum, Argas persicus and Ornithodoros lahorensis.
For this purpose ticks will be collected from livestock population and reared in Lab. and then different fungal strains will be tested in different concentrations against that reared ticks, their larval stages and eggs. Relevant effective methods will be developed and implemented in the livestock population to enhance the productivity and annual income of the farmers.

data.projectName: Canser
data.projectDigest:
Our aim in this project is the production of non-toxic low-cost magnetic nanoparticle for the poor cancer patient of Pakistan. The use of magnetic nano materials for treating cancer disease would have less adverse effects. Our aim is to use magnetic nanoparticles for magnetic  hyperthermia cancer treatment.
One of the primary components of the proposed project is to transfer the knowledge of cancer targeted therapy with magnetic nanoparticles from UCL to GCUF to benefit the individuals of Pakistan. Moreover people from both countries will get benefits from this technology.
For cancer treatment, magnetic hyperthermia (MHT) represents one of the emerging methods currently being tested. It is a procedure that increases tissue temperature above normal in order to kill cancer cells or inhibit their growth. Magnetic-induced hyperthermia is much better than ordinary cancer treatments like chemotherapy and photo therapy as it is tissue specific , have high intensity heating in deep tissue and the heating of nanoparticles by external and contactless magnetic field make it better for transferring of heat into tumor cells. Magnetic heat therapy has ability to treat tumors present at any depth level even below than millimeters because of high penetration ability of magnetic field. 
Nanostructures such as polymers, dendrimers, lipids,  carbon based materials, several inorganic nanomaterials (iron oxide, Zn,Co) are participating for the cancer treatment by providing the thermal effect which is essential for the killing of toxic cells and not effecting the healthy cells.

data.projectName: Development of Sustainable Pollution Control and Rehabilitation Technologies for Waste Disposal Sites in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Management of Municipal Solid Waste is one of the core issues in metropolitan cities of Pakistan. Improper collection and open dumping in unscientific landfills are causing environmental degradation in the form of air, soil and water pollution. In order to purify the environment from hazardous waste contaminants, it i s necessary to rehabilitate the exiting dumpsites and construct scientific landfills with a sustainable engineering approach to coop future waste. This project will be undertaken to develop and implement site specific techniques for rehabilitation of existing dumpsites in Lahore. In addition to this, methodologies for construction of low-cost, low maintenance and low e environmental impact landfills will be developed using available indigenous resources for sustainable engineered landfilling in the country.

data.projectName: Revival of cotton production in non core areas of Punjab through integrated breeding and management for sustainable cotton production in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Cotton is prime crop of Pakistan which provides raw materials for various industries including textiles and edible oil processing industries. Despite being of prime importance for our economy, its area is shrinking in both core and non core areas of Punjab. There is dire need of reintroduction of cotton in non core areas of Punjab through partnership between institutes. Germplasm of cotton will be obtained from central cotton research institute. The seed of germplasm will be initially tested to select plants with compact fruiting, semi dwarf, and insect resistance but with similar time of maturity from elite germplasm to make varietal blend which may have better phenotypic plasticity. Multi location trials will be conducted in second and third years to demonstrate the performance of promising cultivars for the farmers. These trials will conducted in collaboration and recommendations of BCI (better cotton initiative), nonprofit organization for sustainable cotton production worldwide. National Institute of lasers and optronics (NILOP) will supply various laser applications to obtain information regarding precise application of farm inputs and insect monitoring and control. Microbial Production for growth enhancement and pesticides of cotton and sunflower will be carried out by the department of microbiology and biotechnology, University of Punjab.

data.projectName: Portable Surgical Theater
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Economic growth requires proper healthcare facilities and chances of employemnt. Lack of infrastructure in the slums of cities and in remote and underdeveloped regions where there’s no proper infrastructure for surgical procedures leads to healthcare and financial challenges. Portable surgical theatre provides a portable chamber in which minor surgical interventions can be performed. This chamber is designed in a way that will provide sterile environment and can be taken anywhere, even to the remote areas.  Portable surgical theatre will not only reduce the cost of infrastructure required for surgeries, it will also ensure self-employment as the chamber can be owned by any surgical professional, thereby reducing the unemployment. On the other hand, it may also serve to provide healthcare facilities in remote areas with reduced cost.

data.projectName: Proactive Health Management through AI based macro-nutrient and micro-nutrient focused diet
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Obesity has recently emerged as a global epidemic of serious proportion. While on the one hand, obesity has become a global public health problem, on the other hand, malnutrition in the developing countries as well as developed countries such as USA, is another challenge. Current health practices to deal with these nutrition-based epidemics have been reactive, i.e. they deal with patients who are already inflicted with either obesity or malnutrition. In addition to this, later research shows the optimal diet is highly individual and generic diet recommendations offered by regulatory bodies and health practitioners do not meet individual requirements. In this proposed project, by leveraging recent advancements in artificial intelligence and smart phones we aim to develop first of its kind solution for determining, recommending and monitoring optimal individualized diet. The solution addresses the epidemics of obesity and malnutrition and serves as first step towards preventive healthcare paradigm. The proposed solution has a smart phone-based app that tells the user what to eat, when to eat and how much to eat. The dietary propositions would be based on multi-disciplinary research that take as input a user’s genetic data, gut microbiome and amphigenetic characteristics, in addition to age, gender, weight etc.

data.projectName: Digital Archive of the Intellectual Heritage and Material Culture of Walled City Lahore
data.projectDigest: “Role of Image in Capturing the Intellectual Heritage and Material Culture of Lahore Fort and Walled City” is a research project to preserve the intellectual heritage of the city. The images and videos of the dignitaries, of 1970s and 80s, of literature, arts, and performing arts against the backdrop of the old city will be captured to develop an online database. These personalities, nurtured in Lahore, have been inspirational for many generations, and have put their entire lives to construct collective identity of the country. The project is absolutely vital, as most of these dignitaries are leaving the stage of life, so their images, memories and life in Lahore must be archived. These still and moving images have the ability to initiate certain discourse, and take the viewer to revisit the past. What? This project is a revisit to both; the individuals (artists, architects, poets, writers, directors, and painters) and the spaces they belong to, whilst using digital spatial storytelling. How? Spatial engagement of an individual inside a mediated space is a way of discovery through re-exploration of the self, the journey and the past. Why? Online database of visual and oral record of the people, the spaces and the history at large can reshape national discourse beyond local and regional boundaries.

data.projectName: Deployment of an innovative framework to train and educate farmers of Pakistan in advanced agriculture technologies of IoT and A.I to enhance yield and reduce water usage, costs & adverse effect of climate change
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The project addresses the national challenge of food security for the country. The project aims to increase the efficiency of the agriculture sector by establishing smart technology farms in different regions of Pakistan. These smart farms will serve as platforms to educate farmers about A.I and IoT and how to implement these in their farm practices. Furthermore, it will show farmers how technological alternatives are better than their current practices by physical demonstration of IoT in the smart farms. The project will improve water management and food security in Pakistan. The team will implement smart solutions, such as smart irrigation scheduling, appropriate land usage, and fertilizer and pesticide optimization.  The project aims to empower farmers through Artificial Intelligence and data. The project team will obtain farms in Sindh, Balochistan, KPK and Punjab.. data.projectName: Making Small-Scale Farming Sustainable Using Nature-Inspired Intensification, Open-Source Technology and Data-Driven Agricultural Policy
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: Pakistan’s agricultural sector consists of an extremely fragmented land-holding profile. Its small farmers are vulnerable to all types of agricultural disasters and hazards and lack the economic resources to invest in conventional methods of increasing yield. Whereas government bodies recognize the need to facilitate agricultural development, the intervention strategies have relied on providing subsidies which are often insufficient for the small farmer’s needs and result in heavy dependence on governmental support. Despite having the best soil conditions in the world, Pakistan’s yield productivity remains very low due to air, water, and land degradation, further increasing the dependence on unsustainable practices. We, therefore, face the national grand challenge to revisit conventional agricultural practices with a focus on small-farm prosperity and enhancing their domestic and global competitiveness to ensure rural development, protect livelihoods, mitigate the effects of rural-urban migration and minimize the environmental impacts of input-heavy agricultural activity. In this project, we propose a multidisciplinary and multi-stakeholder approach emphasizing innovative nature-inspired intensification practices, the use of Open-Source technologies, and data-driven agricultural policy recommendations. We undertake a comparative analysis of on-farm processes, productivity, and profitability for various sustainable intensification practices, evaluate technologies, and produce policy options for adaptation using behavioral and macro-scale analysis.

data.projectName: Investigation of train-induced vibrations on masonry structures
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Railway is one of the important factors in a country’s transportation system. Pakistan Railway was at its peak till 1965, it has been under service for decades contributing to the country’s economy .  Unfortunately, due to lack of investment in railways modernization the network expansion and upgrading has been halted. As a result, the capacity and service delivery has also suffered. Globally, railway track systems are under continuous development and many different structural forms have been introduced to fulfill different specifications. An important environmental impact of existing and future railway lines occurs due to the ground vibrations induced by trains, which is related to both surface and underground railways. 
Ground borne vibration generates at the wheel-track interface due the dynamic train-track interaction and the quasi-static axle loading along the track. The vibration produced propagates through the soil rocks coupling to building foundation and propagate through building structure producing noise and vibrations. The inhabitants of the building perceive the vibration either directly by motion of walls or by the resonating noise. Moreover, rattling of windows, doors or furnishings can also occur. In almost all the cases, railway-induced vibration is at a level which is far too low to cause structural damage to the building. However, due to the low tensile strength of the masonry structures, the effects of train-induced vibrations may amplify the damage induced by the previous earthquakes. Unfortunately, Building Codes of Pakistan, that have been developed immediately after the 2005 Muzaffarabad earthquake does not have any provision to consider the effects of train induced vibrations.

data.projectName: Interdisciplinary study of glacier surge dynamics, Karakoram, Pakistan: Implications for glacier hazards and water resource management
data.projectDigest:
Glaciers are experiencing significant melting in most parts of the world bearing implications for world's water resources e.g. Hindukush–Karakoram–Himalaya region, known as ‘water tower of Asia’, significantly contributes to the Indus River System through glacial melt. Compared to rest of world, Karakoram glaciers experience slow melting but active surging transport large volume of ice at abnormal high rates. Such type of glacier dynamics could impact future water availability and may result in cryospheric (glaciers related) hazards in terms of highway damages, glacial outbursts and associated hydropower generation process which also strongly impacts local meltwater-dependent irrigation practices and thereby, socioeconomic development processes. 

However, the extreme topography and hazardous environment do not allow to conduct detailed in-situ glaciological investigations. Non-destructive, time and cost-effective ground-based remote sensing methods e.g. GPR, and spaceborne remote sensing techniques can overcome most of these limitations due to their ease of use, high resolution, and large depth of investigation.

The proposed project will benefit from the expertise of researchers from national and international organizations with diverse scientific backgrounds including glaciology, climate change, hydrology, geology and geophysics, and geospatial will investigate the impact of changing climate on glaciers of Karakoram Himalaya.

data.projectName: Tackling Hidden Hunger in Vulnerable Population through Dietary Modifications by Exploring Nutritive Potential of Indigenous Foods
data.projectDigest: Malnutrition is the major problem of Pakistan especially the deficiency of micro nutrients exists in more than half of the population. Besides this Pakistan holds within itself a range of unexplored and unused or not adequately used food sources that can be explored to tackle prevailing burden of hidden hunger or micro nutrient deficiency. Nutritionally vulnerable districts of Pakistan will be assessed along with exploration and analysis of already existing indigenous foods in that areas. different recipes will be prepared and population will be counselled to adequately incorporate food in their daily diet. after one year of interventions again nutritional status of population will be analyzed with aim of reducing micro nutrient deficiency in people living there.

data.projectName: An efficient Consumer Adoption Model for Solar Power System
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: In the past two decades, there have been vast developments noticed in the energy sector. Many companies and individuals have preferred to rely on the solar system for generating electricity and using the power systems at their homes and specific workplace. But no one has focused on to development of a frame work that helps people in selecting the most efficient and economical available energy resources. This study will be focused on to prepare a Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) that provides the consumers a way out that will help them to adopt the most economical power system that is solar power based on their socio-economic conditions. This model also enables government and private sector investors to have a better plan for the investment in renewable energy sector. Also, the government of Pakistan will be benefited from this research project to set the more realistic goals in the field of solar power adoption.

data.projectDigest:
Breeding of Bread wheat for low phytic acid will be carried out in the department of Plant Breeding & Genetics, The University of Agriculture, Peshawar. By the Grace of Allah we have touched the level of self-sufficiency in the production of wheat. We are producing more wheat than our national needs and requirements and exporting surplus to other countries of the world for earning foreign exchange. Recently World Trade Organization (WTO) has been established which mainly monitors quality of agricultural commodities and ensures safe levels of each commodity for human consumption. Due to the aforementioned standard by WTO, now we have to concentrate on quality of bread wheat. In this regard there is a compound in wheat grain especially in aleuron layer known as a Phytic acid. This compound is technically called as Myoinositol 1,6 hexa kisphosphate. This is anti-nutritional and hinders the bioavailability of nutrients to the human body and we will try to decrease it though Breeding mechanism. This compound has 6 free valency which provides a free site for Micro and Macronutrients which are biologically unavailable to human body from unleavened bread.
  In the first phase seed of cultivars will be collected from different sources and will be planted in 5 different environments for three years which will generate 15 environments. Data of 15 environments would help in the study of environmental effect on phytic acid accumulation in wheat kernels. In the 2nd phase (Year-3) cultivars of contrasting groups will be crossed in full diallel for generating hybrid seed. Contrasting groups are required for the study of inheritance mode of any trait.

data.projectName: Design and Development of Active Electronically Scanned Array Radar
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest:
The objective of the proposed research project is to perform complete system design and development of an X-band (8-12 GHz) Digital Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA) Radar. This project falls under the thematic area of “ICT and Telecom”. Its complete indigenous development and development of an ecosystem is a national challenge and is of paramount importance to Pakistan Air Force because of the current geopolitical situation. The technology developed during this project can be used for the development of 5G/6G systems as beam steering is the key enabler of futuristic communication systems.
 One of the major challenges associated with the development of AESA radars is the development of a low cost, highly miniaturized and high-performance T/R modules, which are integrated with every antenna element. Typically, this number ranges between 800-1500 TR modules per radar. To successfully design a miniaturized T/R modules, precise requirements of beam steering, small form factor and its heat dissipation are major challenges. The other challenges include the design of antennas, complex beam forming network, multiple beamforming capability and signal processing and its implementation on embedded system platform for a multi-functional radar.
This project will be developed by a consortium of academic and industrial researchers. It will involve PI(Wasif) and co-PI(Awais and Wala) from LUMS, Yasir (Renzym) as Industry partner, Wasif Latif (Abasyn University) as Co-PI, Dr. Shahzad (PAC) as Co-PI and Bismillah Electronics(Dr. Inam Elahi Rana) as industrial partners, Dr. Aamir Iqbal Bhatti(co-PI) from Capital University of Science and Technology (CUST) as Co-PI. Some consoritium members have also developed Pakistan’s first Phased Array Radar demonstrator.

data.projectName: Energy Recovery and Treatment of Slaughter House Wastewater using Anaerobic Digester Coupled with Combined Chemical Electro -Coagulation Technique
data.projectDigest: Currently, global demand for energy has grown and the search for new ecological energy sources is one of the most significant issues we face. The meat processing industry consumes 29% of the total freshwater. Moreover, the global production of beef, pork, and poultry meat has-been doubled in the past decade and is projected to grow steadily until 2050. The meat processing industry is one of the largest consumers of total freshwater used in the agricultural and livestock industry worldwide. Meat processing plants (MPPs) produce large amounts of slaughterhouse wastewater (SWW) because of the slaughtering process and cleaning of facilities. SWWs need significant treatment for a sustainable and safe discharge to the environment due to the high content of organics and nutrients. Therefore, the treatment and final disposal of SWW are a public health necessity. This project is based on Energy Recovery and Treatment of Slaughter House Wastewater Using Anaerobic Digester Coupled with Combined Chemical Electro Coagulation Technique. Which is intend to solve the major problems of environment, more specifically ground water contamination and energy crisis by adopting zero waste strategy. The objective of this investigation is to optimize and evaluate the bioenergy production potential and COD removal efficiency of residual matter in anaerobic digester from slaughterhouse wastewater by using the combined chemical coagulation (using polyaluminum chloride (PACl) as coagulant) electro-coagulation technique (using aluminum electrodes).The proposed system is efficient enough to cater not only the high strength slaughterhouse wastewater but it will also act as a source of generating bio energy.

data.projectName: Genomic selection for sustainable mutton production in multi-breeds of sheep and goat in Pakistan: A way forward for improving Food Security, Food Safety, and Living Standards of poor population
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is the 6th most populous country in the world with an estimated population of nearly 220 million peoples. There is always growing demand for the animal protein (mainly mutton) by the ever increasing human population in the country. Though Pakistan contain 31 million sheep which belongs to 28 breeds and 75 million goats of 34 breeds but compared with the demand of the mutton the production is very less though most of sheep and goat breeds in the country are meat-type which results in hike in mutton prices. In previous decades, slighter increase in mutton production and huge demand has resulted in more than 100% increase in the price of mutton in the country. Due to which mutton has become too expansive to purchase by the poor and middle class peoples. However, it is also worth mentioning that annual increase in mutton production is due to increase in number of animals rather than increase in their production potential. In this project genomic selection (GS) would be performed for the various breeds of sheep and goat. it will he very helpful for the enhancement of mutton production in the country.

data.projectName: Development and multi-disciplinary intervention of ricin-free/low-ricin genotypes of castorbean for marginal/cultivable wastelands and to investigate its utilization as bio-fertilizers, bio-pesticides, and poultry feed
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: Castorbean (Ricinus cumminus L) is an important oil crop (with higher oil in seed as compared to other oilseed crops) being utilized in multiple industries (around 300 high value products of castorbean).  Castorbean in grown during summer and its plant has unique characteristics including; deep rooting system, drought tolerance, low inputs requirement, and wider adaptability, which make it climate smart crop for adverse environments and climate shifts. Pakistan is among few countries which are vulnerable to climate change effects with huge areas of degraded soils (~ 8 million hectares) and sharp decline in production of major crops at well fertile cultivated soils. NIAB has released an early maturity, high yielding variety of castorbean (NIAB Gold), having 52% oil content in seed and yield potential of 4000 kg ha-1.  Development of ricin-free varieties (ricin is poisonous protein in caastorbean seed) for utilization of its oil and by products for edible purpose, is a challenge for scientists. First ricin-free variety of castorbean has been developed in Brazil during 2018. Under this project we want to develop ricin-free/low ricin varieties by induced mutation technique and also want to investigate use of ricin-free/low ricin castorbean  in value added products including;  bio-fertilizer, bio-pesticides, and feed.

data.projectName: Antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory activity of green synthesized nano-structures (Zinc oxide and silver oxide) against Salmonellosis in poultry
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Salmonella is one of the major and most common bacterial pathogens of poultry. Salmonelosis in broiler chicken and hen is economically the most important disease of poultry industry all over the world. In addition to causing loss in chicken and egg production, it also possesses public health risk due to zoonotic in nature in some cases.  The efficacy of antibiotic therapy in case of Salmonella is limited, therefore, high prevalence of Salmonella and lower efficacy of antibiotics is resulting in high economic losses to industry.  In Pakistan, as there is no system to observe chicken meat and eggs with-drawl period recommended for antibiotic usage, the presence of antibiotic residues in chicken meat is causing serious human health issues including toxicity and antibiotic resistance. A study is therefore, proposed with an objective to  evaluate  zinc oxide and silver oxide nano-structures prepared by green method using turmeric roots for the treatment of Salmonella as alternate to antibiotic therapy.  The treatment will provide an effective alternate for antibiotic therapy thus reducing the import bill for antibiotics. This treatment will also be helpful in reducing antibiotic residues in chicken meat and its products thus making these safer for human use and reducing the problem of antibiotic resistance.
