data.projectName: Energy Demand Management Energy monitoring/simulating the energy consumption behaviour using AI for a balanced energy supply and demand
data.projectDigest: The proposed solution focuses on creating the technical and technological conditions for the widespread implementation of demand response strategies in domestic buildings. It is able to interact with existing metering platforms and make use of machine learning techniques to determine usage patterns and by considering the characteristics of energy devices and systems associated to buildings alongside the definition of user preferences and configurations implement custom tailored algorithms to maximize the benefits to the end-user. Load dis-aggregation techniques are supported by the solution to estimate the consumption of specific appliances and allow their separate analysis to identify specific energy efficiency actions. To meet these two contrasting requirements of developing countries as a single challenge, this project focuses on the development of a cost-effective energy management platform, to allow end-users the ability to optimize their energy use, minimize GHG emissions and at the same time contribute towards the electric grid stabilization through the implementation of load forecasting, load management, micro-generation control schemes and implementation of loss reduction strategies to contribute towards the overall electric system efficiency. The aim of such efforts worldwide is to move towards the concept of Net-Zero Energy Buildings (NZEB). Such buildings at one end endeavor to minimize the energy requirements through use of Increased Thermal Mass of the building and at the other end make use of Automated Intelligent control/management systems to use available energy efficiently and in a manner as to avoid peak-loading or low-loading periods thus leveling the energy requirements to a minimum.

data.projectName: Synthesis and understanding of the physicochemical properties of catalysts used in the mitigation of nitrogen oxide molecules, particularly emitted from the exhaust streams of Nitric acid plants.
data.projectDigest:
Nitric acid plants are among the top ten most essential large-scale chemical industries and in Pakistan numerous plants are in continuous operation . At present, 85% of the total production is consumed for fertilizer production, whereas the rest of the nitric acid is used for making polymers, dyes, and explosives [2].  In production of nitric acid, three main chemical operations (Ostwald process) are involved. These are:  NH3 oxidation (5NH3 + 5O2 ? 4NO + 6H2O), NO oxidation to NO2 (2NO + O2 ? 2NO2), and finally absorption of NO2 in water (4NO2 + 2H2O + O2 ? 4HNO3). 
In addition to NO production, N2O is also formed as a by-product during the NH3 combustion (NH3 + O2 ? 0.5N2O + 1.5H2O) reaction. This harmful greenhouse gas cannot be absorbed by water in the absorption column and eventually released into the atmosphere. Furthermore, kinetically N2O is a highly stable molecule, and effectively absorbs infrared radiations and chemically degrade ozone (O3) layer when present in the stratosphere layer (12 km to 50 km, from the surface of the earth). The main object of this project is to develop an effective and robust catalyst for dissociation of N2O into environmental friendly gases.

An agriculture, excesses application of N fertilization had been extremely alarmed as a main cause of radiative N (Nr). This result in nitrate leaching, ammonia volatilization, and nitrous oxide emissions which are severe environmental problems by contaminated groundwater quality. Subsequently reducing N use efficiency causes high N losses, and high economic costs. Thus, to reduce N release but enhance plant utilization of N fertilizer had been a priority demand for sustainable agriculture worldwide. The major environmental impacts associated with fertilizer use have been linked to leaching and runoff of nutrients, especially nitrogen, which causes aquatic eutrophication. Application of functionally enhanced biochar products in small quantity could be a low cost but high agronomic ef?ciency. Due to unique characteristics, biochar could be blended with urea fertilizer for concurrently increasing crop yield and reducing environmental risk. 
We hypothesize that (1) Biochar Blended Urea (BBU) will enhanced N retention from urea through reaction from urea through reaction and surface adsorption; and (2)  Application of BBU could reduce N release.

data.projectName: Recycling of solid and agricultural wastes into valuable bioproducts through composting technique
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is the 6th largest and most populated country around the globe, so the generation of solid waste materials in large and abundant quantities is quite natural and understandable. So, its proper management is critical as waste material does not reach to proper disposal points. In developing countries, much of the solid waste materials are shifted to landfills or similar recycling centers like incinerators. But unfortunately, in Pakistan, no such systemic and scientific management system is available for the proper disposal of a huge amount of waste materials. Consequently, it becomes a source of different types of pollutions. There are many types of solid waste management specific to the waste type like; municipal solid waste (MSW), hazardous wastes, waste minimization, agricultural wastes, bio-medical wastes and industrial wastes. Major contributing factors include lack of urban planning, improper waste collection system, inadequate waste management equipment, dumping of waste on streets and lack of awareness and education. In advanced countries, there are many methods being used for solid waste disposal and management including open burning, dumping into the sea, sanitary landfills, incineration, grinding & discharging into sewers, ploughing in fields, hog feeding and composting. Recycling of waste materials through composting is the most popular method throughout the globe. There is no alternative method to composting if we want to recycle an abundant quantity of waste materials generated in the country to the valuable and nutrient-enriched material that may be used for healthy plant growth as well as may act the best conditioner for different types of soil properties.

data.projectName: IoT Enabled AI & Blockchain based DataBank for Evidence based Policy Making
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
In times of increasing populism reliable information plays   a vital   role   in   well-informed   policy-making   based on evidence and not only on emotions and values, let alone disinformation and fake news. The popular legitimacy of any system therefore depends on its capacity to deliver good and targeted outcomes based on transparent evidence.  These outcomes need to be rooted in reliable data in order to make decisions understandable, assessable and sustainable. Unfortunately, in Pakistan, there exists no digital databank at national level that that may be used for policy making. For this grant, we propose to build Pakistan’s first Internet of Things (IoT) enabled DataBank that shall allow for evidence based policy making. Evidence-based policy helps people to make well-informed decisions about policies, programmes and projects, by placing the best available evidence from research at the heart of policy development and implementation. We shall be working with a consortium of national and international partners to create Pakistan’s first digital DataBank, what will allow for policy making across a wide spectrum of domains. The DataBank will initially consist of data on health, energy sectors and climate of the country and in due course of the project will include other domains. The Databank along with the analytics of the data will allow for better quality of different outputs such as policy brief, infographics, etc. for identification of key performance parameters and the future predications in the domains of healthcare, energy and climate change.
We anticipate that this will be the first project of its type in Pakistan and will set a course for other initiatives as well to achieve the objectives of Vision 2025.

data.projectName: Low Cost Metal Extraction and Chlorination (MEC) drinking water plant.
data.projectDigest: The designed research will emphasis on the development of 1000-liter drinking water treatment plant. The Membrane extraction chlorination (MEC) drinking water plant comprises of three separate functioning cells. One of them will be used for the electromembrane extraction/ hollow fiber extraction for trace and toxic metals. This way, toxicity related to these metals will be reduced. Another inexpensive and robust cell will be developed and used for electrooxidation of chloride into chlorine for final disinfection of filtered water. Efforts will be directed towards the development of inexpensive electrochemical monitoring cell for the residual chlorine level in water storage tank to assure sanitary storage of the treated water. The concentration of chlorine will be controlled and kept within the WHO prescribed limits (4mg.L-1). The inexpensive water treatment tank will be capable of retaining water for considerable period of time as chlorination will be monitored constantly hence there is very little chance for bacteria to grow within the tank. The whole plant will be powered by photovoltaic panels. Hence the power shortage encountered in remote areas in accordance to the MEC plant will be dealt so that it will become feasible for household to small village scale use.

data.projectName: Demographic and Pharmacogenomic profiles of Two major non-communicable diseases  (diabetes and cardiovascular diseases) of local Pakistani population.
data.projectDigest: Non communicable diseases (NCDs) are the main cause of death, disability, reduced quality of life and rising health care costs worldwide. The number of people dying worldwide due to these is twice as compared that of the combined infectious diseases, maternal and perinatal conditions and nutritional deficiencies. Cardiovascular diseases (CVD), diabetes, cancers and chronic respiratory diseases are the common NCDs. CVD is the leading cause of death in the developed nations and, the second cause in developing and under-developed countries, and accounts for about 30% of all deaths, of which 80% occur in low and middle income countries (including Pakistan that is 6th most populous country). Similarly Diabetes Mellitus (DM) is an endocrine disorder that affect around 6% of the world's population . It causes 1.5 million global deaths annually, with a projected burden of 300 million in the year 2025. 80% among these live in developing nations, including Pakistan. Many contributing factors have been identified for both of these diseases including life style, environmental and genetic susceptibility. In recent past, much work has been done to determine the genetic susceptibility, and risk alleles have being identified in different ethnicities. Studying genetic makeup is owing to a newly emerging field known as ‘pharmacogenomics’, which is a step to the concept of ‘Personalized Medicine’. However, no such study has been carried out in local Pakistani population. Therefore, this study has been designed to screen out this population for genetic profile of these diseases. It will help in devising health care strategies to control the burden of this fatal and costly disease.

data.projectName: Evaluation of microbiome directed interventions for the eradication of antimicrobial resistance and Environmental Enteric Dysfunction (EED)
data.projectDigest: Modifying the human gut microbiome is opening up new therapeutic approaches for intractable conditions such as C. difficile infection (CDI), inflammatory bowel disease, and antibiotic resistance. A key pillar of translational microbiome research is fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT). FMT involves the transfer of healthy gut microbiota to a patient in order to restore the gut microbiome. Globally there are 384 FMT trials in a wide range of indications however there are none in Pakistan. Our aim is to establish Pakistan’s first FMT program to position AKU as world leader in the field of translational microbiome research to address two national priorities, stunting (driven by environmental enteric dysfunction, EED) and antibiotic resistance. Our project will (i) establish standards for screening, sample collection, and storage, (ii) build a data and sample repository of healthy gut microbiota samples from Pakistan (iii) evaluate the effects of healthy gut microbiota samples on pre-clinical models of under-nutrition to establish in vivo proof-of-concept (iii) evaluate public perceptions of FMT and gut microbiome research to ensure such a platform is developed in a culturally appropriate way. Following on from this work, we intend to launch a clinical trial of FMT in EED and antimicrobial resistance.

data.projectName: Gasification System to Supply Gas to Domestic Network for 1000 Households
data.projectDigest: Energy security is a key global challenge. Therefore, providing an engineering solution for turning waste biomass into a transportable fuel can contribute to meet the energy supply in remote areas where gas and power networks are not available. The proposed technology provides the opportunity to greatly utilize biomass resource which will otherwise go wasted. This project will provide a sound and demonstrable technology to the rural community closer to the biomass availability to produce renewable fuel. Pakistan has also got large amount of agricultural and biomass resources. Most of them are not utilised because it is difficult to collect it and transport to the centralised energy generation facility; and waste recovered biomass is not suitable for use directly to these biomass power plants or heating boilers. It is proposed that in the first phase a demonstration facility to provide syngas into a dedicated network for domestic cooking and heating application will be developed. This will develop a sustainable infrastructure to be deployed in a variety of sectors which produce biomass from agriculture, domestic, and industrial waste sectors. The outcome of the project thus will have direct impact on the economic welfare and health of the rural and urban communities.

data.projectName: STRENGTHENING OF DIAGNOSTIC FACILITIES AND ESTABLISHMENT OF ANIMAL HOUSE AT COLLEGE OF VETERINARY & ANIMAL SCIENCES, JHANG
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Poultry industry and Livestock sector is the back bone of economy especially in rural and backward area. The sector is challenged to many infectious diseases that threaten Livestock and poultry farmers to face losses every year which amount to billions of Rupees. The proper vaccination is the best way to prevent livestock and poultry from contracting infectious agents. However, despite vaccination, diseases do occur. Recent discoveries and advances, however, in the realm of modern techniques have imparted diagnostic microbiology a totally new outlook owing to their ease, speed, accuracy, and reproducibility of results. The objective of the present project is to make use of conventional as well as modern techniques for prompt diagnosis of infectious diseases. There is no high tech diagnostic lab in Jhang that is the central hub of Punjab province. Being a teaching and research institute, College of Veterinary & Animal Sciences, Jhang must have a model Veterinary Diagnostic facilities equipped with the state-of-the-art gadgetries for carrying out required diagnostic work at advanced levels. Furthermore, the livestock and poultry stakeholders will be benefited by achieving maximum health and production potentials, which will be possible through the availability of effective diagnostic facilities in this project.

data.projectName: A One Health Approach to assess the Burden of Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) in different environments and Potential Intervention(s)
data.projectDigest:
Funding is sought to investigate the dynamics and drivers of one health antimicrobial resistance and provide possible interventions to improve public health affected by antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Multi-drug resistance (MDR) is global problem and becomes a serious issue in the management of infections due to limited treatment options. This proposal aligns with the thematic area “Development Economics” as it deals with measures to reduce the economic cost of treatment of infections which otherwise are either non-treatable due to failure of antibiotics or take longer time leading to prolonged hospital stay hence adding to economic burden of health. The study has been well thought and designed to investigate all drivers of AMR which affect the one health. The environmental impact of resistant bacteria on human and animal health has been studied but most of these reports are from developed world while none of the studies from Pakistan have analyzed this impact encompassing all sectors. Furthermore, the studies have been on small scale, mostly analyzing one or other type of bacteria/infection type and have not addressed the link between the resistant flora of poultry, wild birds/flies, human community and environment. Also, the knowledge of community reservoirs and the associated infections is limited. There is a need to understand MDR bacterial strains circulating in different environments and their relatedness. Without a holistic analysis of our key environments, any kind of intervention seems unreliable and unreasonable. 
The proposed study is dynamic in its design as it aims to access the prevalence of resistant bacteria and their genetic makeup using basic molecular and advanced genomic tools. This could lead to a standardised approach to examining AMR connectivity.

data.projectName: Sustainable Management of Construction and Demolition Waste Through Green Concrete Technology in Karachi
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
In this project, CDW management system for the Karachi city will be developed which will be adapted from selected CDW management technology used worldwide and compatible with local scenario in order to maximise the economic value and minimise the environmental impacts. The extraction of coarse aggregates from CDW will be the primary aim of this study and will be named as “recycled coarse aggregates (RCA)”. After the establishment of CDW system, the acquired CDW from different CDW sources will be characterized and utilized in the development of “Green Concrete”. Green concrete is defined as a concrete which uses waste material as at least one of its components, or its production process does not lead to environmental destruction, or it has high performance and life cycle sustainability. This “Green Concrete” will be used in the construction of Pilot/Demonstration Green Concrete Project to encourage the use of RAC based Green Concrete in civil engineering structures which is a key step towards promotion of sustainable development especially in Urban Scenario.
In the next phase, Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), Life Cycle Analysis (LCA) and Life Cycle Cost Analysis (LCCA) will be carried out. LCA will be performed to address the potential environmental impacts throughout RCA’s life cycle, from raw coarse aggregate material acquisition through production, use, end-of-life treatment, recycling and final disposal. LCCA is the most straightforward and easy-to-interpret measure of economic evaluation (e.g. benefit-to-cost ratio). 
In the end, Guidelines / Regulations for the use of CDW based on the State of National and International Practice will be developed under the guidance of International academic collaborators and national academic and sectoral collaborators.

data.projectName: Electric Vehicles Adoption Design Model for Accessible Urban Transportation and Energy Sustainability
data.projectDigest:
Adoption of Electric vehicles have always been a question of concern at user end in terms of adaptability due to range anxiety, at energy service provider’s end for availability of interrupted power supply to  electric vehicle’s fleet and at municipal administration’s end for providing accessibility of charging stations in the existing urban infrastructure for sustainable  adaptability, availability and accessibility. This project aims to address dynamic issues related to Electric Vehicle adaption while designing a sustainable and realistic integration Model. The proposed integration model includes 
•	Design of Renewable Energy Based Electric Vehicle Charging Stations for Commercial and Domestic areas integration of renewable energy based charging station
•	Design of Interlinked Communication Model for Electric Charging Stations and Electric Vehicles for Vehicle to Grid support 
•	Optimized urban planning for optimal placement of charging stations
•	Design of Bi-level vehicle to vehicle DC charging 
•	Policy to standardized uniform charging methods, price regulations  and size of charging stations
The project is based on a consortium of international and national relevant experts from academia and industry that includes RMIT Australia, American University of Kurdistan, NED UET and HAWK Engineering.
The project aims to introduce comprehensive design implementation for realistic and seamless adaption of electric vehicles in Pakistan.

data.projectDigest: Democracy and structure of classroom have complex relationship with governance and reforms agenda in Pakistan. Classroom is a backbone of all reforms and governance strategies which paved a way towards institutional building and in achieving sustainable development. The structure of classroom’s pedagogy and its relationship with social control i.e hegemony have significant axiological relationship with (de)humanization and have inverse linkage with democratization. The democratic indicators i.e diversity and pluralism, functioning of government, electoral process, civil liberties, political participation and culture is directly linked with political pedagogy of classroom which lead to promotion of critical thinking and scientific thoughts in a society. The ideological state narratives and trends of democracy at classroom in Pakistan have deep effects on governance and reforms processes in Pakistan. is an innovative and timely study to explain structure of classroom and its relationship with hegemonic power structure. This study is an attempt to address governance and reforms crises through exploring, the fundamental research question that why classroom? and how/why linked with hybrid politics in Pakistan. The sub question which lead to a main/central question are what type of pedagogy is being used? why? And to whom? And how/why pedagogical orientation of classroom is linked with state hegemonic power structure?  Both theoretical and empirical evidences will be used for exploration of this critical question. This exploration of these questions will lead to innovative governance and reforms in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Optimizing the Phosphorus Diffusion step for mass production of solar cells
data.projectDigest:
According to the International Energy Agency, solar energy will become the primary source of energy generation by 2050. During the manufacturing of commercial solar cells the phosphorus diffusion process completes the base structure of the cell and is the most important step in the manufacturing sequence. Therefore, an appreciable improvement over this particular process will have a significant impact on future global energy markets.
The diffusion process is carried out over a large batch of silicon wafers using an inexpensive gaseous method. The technique is cost-effective but provides little control over the amount of phosphorus that enters the different cells. From the point of view of the average performance of all cells, it is considered best to supply the phosphorus in excess. This in turn leads to phosphorus concentrations in wafers to exceed their solubility limit in silicon.
Phosphorus atoms below the solubility limit are electrically active, but beyond this limit the excess phosphorus atoms form precipitates that are electrically inactive. Active phosphorus improves the cell’s performance while inactive phosphorus undermines it. This project aims to substantially reduce the amount of inactive phosphorus and maintain active phosphorus levels close to maximum (solubility limit) during commercial processing of solar cells.

data.projectName: Development and Application of Foam Concrete as Energy Efficient Building Material for Pakistan Construction Industry
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Population growth and energy crisis throughout the world including Pakistan had increased the demand for sustainable, energy-efficient and low-cost housing. The global and local industry is in search of sustainable building material capable of meeting these challenges. In comparison with traditional building materials, foamed concrete, which is a lightweight and porous material has great advantages owing to its ease of compaction, good insulation, and low density. Also, with the potential for utilizing the agriculture/industrial byproducts as a pozzolan. The use of pozzolan as a supplementary cementing material supports the cement industry in reducing the carbon dioxide (CO2) emission to the desired level. 
The surge of construction and energy cost in Pakistan requires extensive use of material possessing similar qualities as of foamed concrete.  As, the use of foamed concrete is very limited in Pakistan therefore, the main purpose of this study is to develop energy-efficient foamed concrete blocks and its application protocols. This design will be based on experimental results, for which small and large scale testing will be carried out. In small scale testing mechanical, physical, thermal properties and material properties such as mineralogy, morphology, petrographic, chemical composition will be investigated. While in large-scale wall panel testing under compression, dynamics, fire, and acoustics loading will be conducted. Finally based on the experimental results a small house model will be constructed in selected areas.
It is expected that the application of foamed concrete blocks will result in affordable and energy-efficient construction, especially for the housing sector.

data.projectName: Non-transgenic delineation of rice genetic improvement for drought tolerant, low glycemic and low Arsenic rice fortified with Fe and Zn: A step towards healthy rice
data.projectDigest: The current project designed to address food security and food safety issues related to rice by identifying and developing Fe and Zn enriched low glycemic and low arsenic yet drought resilient rice though non-transgenic approaches. Because rice is second source of energy after wheat and second to cotton for foreign exchange earner for Pakistan, however rice is not a good source of Zn and Fe, instead it serves as a major source of heavy metals due to the requirement of more (standing) water as compared to other crops. In addition, rice has been considered as worst source of high glycemic food. Rice genetic improvement for less water (drought tolerance), low glycemic and low arsenic while fortified with Fe and Zn, will help to improve rice yield and quality. Moreover, application of genetic engineering to accomplish these tasks is currently not practicing due to export regulations. KIBGE will serve as the central part of this program where genomics and molecular tasks will accomplish. NIBGE and NIGAB will assist to validate the molecular (DNA) markers to implement in marker assisted selection of healthy rice. ICCBS and PSQCA, will be determining the content of amylose, amylopectin, As, Zn and Fe in selected rice grains. In addition, a simple and cost-effective screening test will be designing based on molecular (DNA), biochemical (proteins) and chemical (starch, As, Zn and Fe) markers for quality assessment of rice grains in Pakistan. This project is the first large scale study of drought stress tolerance and quality analysis of Pakistani rice varieties which will greatly improve public health and increase the production of rice in Pakistan in times of climate change. Because it addresses food security, agricultural productivity, and climate resilience.

data.projectName: Nanotechnology-based Waste Water Treatment
data.projectDigest:
Waste water treatment infrastructure is in very worse condition in Pakistan. The absence of proper treatment of effluents pose a great threat to the ecosystem of the country. The lack of treatment facilities is affecting public health and environmental quality of the country. Only a fraction of waste water is treated in the country which results in environmental degradation, underground water contamination, water borne diseases and neurological disorders in the most vulnerable groups of the society.
This project is focused on the development of efficient and economical waste water treatment methodologies based on nanotechnology to bring about a paradigm shift in this sector. New materials will be synthesized for detection, removal and degradation of pollutants present in the industrial effluents. In this regard new sensors, sorbents and photocatalysts will be developed. It will also result in complete profiling of industrial effluents in different industrial sectors. The industrial partners will provide feedback on the their requirements and performance of newly developed solutions. This project is expected to result in the development of efficient monitoring and waste water treatment methodologies for different industrial sectors which can be scaled later.

data.projectName: Developing export-oriented economy by transforming the laboratory scale synthesis of precious fine organics into bench scale synthesis in order to improve the product portfolio of a company viz. GLYCANE Fine Organics
data.projectDigest: This project builds upon my six months of intensive entrepreneurship training in Quebec (Canada) and then 2.8 years of relevant postdoctoral experience at Lakehead University, Canada and Northern Ontario School of Medicine (NOSM) Canada, where I learned the art of gram-scale production of precious fine organics. This training resulted in the conception of GLYCANE® – a company dealing in the field of precious fine organics. Now I propose using the local raw materials to prepare an elaborate product portfolio for GLYCANE® (www.glycane.com). This will result in better sale prospects for the company in North America, since the enterprise is familiar with the dynamics of precious fine organics industry and its regulations. Moreover, focus of this ambitious project is to train local chemistry graduate students, and spur a network of research collaboration between 3 Pakistani institutions (Karachi University+GC University Lahore +FC University Lahore) and 3 foreign institutions (Canada, Sweden and China) in order to meet the project goals. The students will acquire advance synthetic chemistry skills and learn the preparation of enantiopure compounds on gram-scale for the company GLYCANE. At the end of this project, they will become permanent employee of the company and help Pakistan to earn valuable foreign exchange.

data.projectName: I am not equal, I am superior... Impact of construing contemporary feministic ideology on pregnant presenteeism. Cross-Cultural implications for pregnant workingwomen.
data.projectDigest: Every day, working women confront the challenges of managing work and family effectively. The biological limitations of women bound them to advance family and career side by side. If a working woman gets pregnant, the common notion is that she will be more absent from work due to sickness and physical changes. in retaliation, they pretend to be more dutiful and punctual at the cost of their health. This tendency of pregnant women to attend work while sick is termed as pregnant presenteeism. Many researches revealed that presenteeism results into productivity loss that ends up hampering the firm and national development. Laws enforcement agencies in advanced countries ensures the proper execution of the laws about pregnant women. In transition economies, laws are there but the non-execution is a big problem. This project is designed on cross cultural comparison between Pakistan and US to investigate cultural imperatives and their influence on various individual, work and society related factors of pregnant presenteeism and its various individual and firm level outcomes. A series of studies using a mulit-method approach (i.e., surveys, focus groups, interviews)  will be conducted to get a holistic view of the causes and effects of pregnant presenteeism. This project is designed on sociology and philosophy theme of grand challenge fund and will prove an important piece of research to provide an in-depth understanding of pregnant presenteeism from a socio-cultural perspective, its antecedents and consequences, and to educate policy makers and other stakeholder about devising various strategies to address this cost phenomenon. As reducing this will lead to betterment for individual (Mother plus baby), organization, society and economy.

data.projectName: A consortium to enhance kinnow yield and export by targeting citrus pests and educating farmers through outreach services in Sargodha.
data.projectDigest: Citrus ranked at 1st position in Pakistan as compared to other fruits. More than 95% of citrus is produced in the Punjab province and 70% of citrus grown in Punjab is Kinnow. Asian citrus psylla and mites are the most serious and destructive pest of citrus. Citrus psylla is a vector of citrus greening as well; a cause of citrus quality and quantity reduction in a country. Deteriorated fruit quality and quantity due to pest infestation, bad handling and pesticide residues greater than MRL make the fruits unfit for export and result in selling the fruits in local market at low price. In this scenario, the current research aimed at coping with the challenges of deteriorating kinnow quality and declining citrus yield due to citrus declining. To this end, candidate genes detected through RNAseq will be knocked out using RNAi in collaboration with Southwest University, China. In order to improve the citrus quality and quantity, farmer training about the citrus pest management and pre-post-harvest losses will be performed in collaboration with Sargodha Mandarin Pvt.

data.projectName: Targeted resistance development in Cotton against cotton leaf curl disease through program cell death (Apoptosis) and evaluation of Cotton leaf crumple virus-VIGS vector in Nicotiana benthamiana.”
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Cotton, which accounts for 60% of Pakistan‘s local and export economies, and is a substantial export crop for Arizona, USA, is a host of a number of begomoviral pathogens that can cause yield-limiting disease. For several decades these viral pathogens and their whitefly vectors have been difficult to manage without the heavy use of pesticides. These scenarios create serious challenges for both scientists (to solve the problem) and governing bodies (crop losses and economic ramifications).
Most of the completed/ongoing projects, to control Cotton leaf curl disease (CLCuD) have been using pathogen derived resistance, RNAi/miRNA technique one way or the other. Previous studies have shown that the genome of begomoviruses (cotton virus) have many silencing suppressors. Out of six genes encoded by genomic component three (TrAP, AC4, V2) have been shown as silencing suppressors. Also, the associated betasatellite encodes a gene (ßC1) which is a key symptoms determinant and is a silencing suppressor 
This project is designed to develop and validate contemporary, innovative approaches to reduce CLCuV and CLCrV infection of cotton in Pakistan and Arizona, USA respectively, by targeting the viral genomes using either the modified CLCuV-betasatellite vector, minus the virulence gene), or the existing CLCrV-VIGS-Cyt c vector (minus the coat protein gene) to express Cyt c, which induces plant cell death in cells immediately upon virus infection. The infected cell will be dead and there will be no transmission of the virus within the plant and the virus will not be available for whitefly transmission.

data.projectName: Modelling and Forecasting of Urban Landscape Dynamics in the Face of Climate Change over Ten Major Cities of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is one of the most populous country in the world, where significant amount of people lives in the 10 major urban centers/cities. Those include the city of: Karachi, Lahore, Faisalabad, Hyderabad, Rawalpindi, Gujranwala, Peshawar, Multan, Islamabad and Quetta. The estimated total population of these cities is 45.30 million which is about 21.8% of Pakistan’s total population according to 2017 census [1]. These cities are also major growing hubs of Pakistan economy. These cities face many challenges that include population increase, urban built-up sprawl, surging transportation, environmental problems, pressure on water resources and climatic changes [3]. The urbanization improves economic activities on one end but creates pressure on urban land and natural resources on another end. Our aim is to study urban and climatic changes for these ten major cities of Pakistan. The main objectives of this research project is to: (i) model urban land and study urban land changes in past two decades; (ii) forecast urban land changes for future two decades; (iii) identify impact of urban land changes on climatic changes in past two decade; and (iv) predict climate changes for future two decades and (iv) estimate the effect of climate changes on water resources. From objectives, it is obvious that this research proposal encompasses the most import thematic areas of Global Challenge Fund that include urban planning & management, climate change and mitigation and water resource management for the most important cities of Pakistan. There are six collaborators in this research project. These include four collaborators from Pakistan and two collaborators from Canada and Australia.

data.projectName: Virtual Experiences. Real Outcomes to Transform Education in Pakistan: A scalable model of education delivery through the use of ICT
data.projectDigest:
The project will use a 3-step technology-enhanced system for addressing all three needs, empowering teachers and students through a peer communication, support and mentorship network, and providing an on-going, scalable model for educator assessment and improvement. The project will develop capacity building centers (CBC) involving three components: a classroom simulation with artificial intelligence, an individual and team learning platform with learning analytics capabilities, and a free, open-source, global learning platform. These pre-existing systems already serve hundreds of thousands to millions of people. The project will integrate the three systems, establish a permanent hub of digital learning and teacher education for Pakistan, and will demonstrate the project’s impacts with solid, ongoing research-based findings.
The partnership includes five universities from Pakistan, and four from abroad plus an education sector business from the USA who have already been working for about two years to establish relationships, conduct trainings, and support the proposal’s ideas. The roles in the partnership are well defined by the contributions to the proposed integration of platforms, prior research, teacher education capabilities and the committed ongoing relationships.

data.projectName: Energy Conservation Centre of Excellence   (ECCE)
data.projectDigest:
The research project is focused on the development of centre of excellence in energy conservation. The main focus of the project is to investigate the solutions to industrial problems at national level in process, heat transfer equipment manufacturing, refrigeration and air conditioning and building energy industry. It will help the industries to increase global competitiveness and energy conservation.

The proposal has been developed in consultation with around 30 industries in this field.
The feedback from the industrial stake holders has been incorporated into this proposal by team of experts in the field. The team comprise of heat transfer and energy conservation experts from Mechanical Department of almost all leading universities of Pakistan. Moreover, to further add value international experts from UK, Europe, Taiwan and Malaysia have also been included. These experts shall provide input on the international best practices in these industries and state of the art technologies in these industrial sectors.

It will help in Capacity building of Universities and industries in the Design of Industrial systems as per International standards with stakeholder confidence to retrofit old and implement these techniques. Moreover, we shall propose energy conservation targets and benchmarks for policy guidelines of regulatory organizations.

data.projectName: Urban Planning and Development
data.projectDigest: The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), is heralded as a ‘game changer’ for Pakistan’s social and cultural development (Ibrar et al., 2016). There was no concept of CPEC before 2015 and it started with the visit of the Chinese Prime President Xi Jinping and Pakistani Prime Minister's agreement in 2015. This is a new and emerging issue which has not been explored. Based on the notion of win-win situation, the  CPEC needs to be explored from the research point of view (Ibrar, Mi, & Rafiq, 2016). data.projectName: Climate change resilience and adaptation of marginalized and disabled population in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
This project is developed to study the climate induced vulnerabilities and adaptations of disabled population of Pakistan. This problem is not discussed in depth in the country with this narrative although; it is a double headed problem that needs to be addressed. Pakistan is highly vulnerable to the impacts of climate change along with political insecurity and economic instability as leading issues of today’s time. The poverty stricken areas of Pakistan already facing the issues of unequal distribution of resources having major climate change consequences occur frequently in last few decades with having serious implications on the marginalized disabled population. The insecurities faced by disabled population and their ability to tackle and recover from climate induced disasters are never given major importance. Frequent floods, landslides, extreme temperatures, erratic rainfall, cyclones, droughts, heat waves and many other climate irregularities are posing serious threats to disabled population of the country. Evidence suggested that there are gaps of knowledge regarding influence of climate change on people with disabilities and also the weak institutional capacities and service mechanism with respect to disabilities. The hypothesis is disabled individuals are less resilient and more prone to climate irregularities and their adaptation mechanism must be studied so as to develop knock on consequences of climate change. 
In order to understand climate change resilience in the disabled population of Pakistan, the project aims to address two key questions: 1. What are the root causes of vulnerability among disabled population to climate risks)? 2. How can external adaptation interventions  address these root causes of vulnerability.

data.projectName: Estimation of country-specific green house gas emission factors related to animal feedstuffs and animals in large ruminant production systems in Pakistan and their nutritional mitigation strategies
data.projectDigest: The green house gases (GHG) such as methane and nitrous oxide are increasing in quantity as a result of human activity. These GHG  are responsible for increasing average earth's  temperature by 1.5 degree celcius during last 50 years. This high temperature causes vulnerabilities in cropping and animal raising systems and reduces sustainability. Agriculture operations, by large contribute to about 14-18% of total world GHG emissions and livestock makes half of it within agriculture. Pakistan is an agricultural country with the contribution of livestock to more than 50% of agricultural gross domestic product. The country’s contribution to total world GHG emissions is about 5-7%. The country is holding the third largest population of ruminants in Asia (GOV, 2017), which is growing at 3.5% per annum. Our local animals are poor producers of meat or milk (Khan et al., 2008) and the animals with poor feed efficiency are greater source of GHG emissions. The poor performance is partly attributed to poor genetic make-up of the population and partly to the poor quality and availability of feed resources. Since Pakistan's contribution to world GHG is significant, we need to reduce our part. Currently, we lack any system for accurate and direct quantification and mitigation of GHG from livestock sector, systematic approaches involving multiple sectors and focused strategies at national level are required to be developed.

data.projectName: Cow Monitoring System
data.projectDigest:
Biosensors and wearable technology in animals is gaining more focus of dairy farmers in terms of  detecting diseases at earlier stages. If these devices are built properly and used correctly, can provide multiple benefits to dairy farmers including timely diagnosis of animals and minimizing the economic losses which occur due to improper detection of diseases. Pakistan is the 6th biggest milk producing country in the world. Being 6th biggest milk producing country, Pakistan’s milk export is zero because we consume all the milk within the country. Pakistan can earn over 30 Billion Dollars per year from exports of dairy products. Our average yield of milk per cow is 3.5 to 5 liters per day. This yield in not increasing due to high disease rate as cows are dying every year with an immense rate. When a Cow’s temperature rises from normal temperature, the farm owner does not know what happened to 
the cow until the disease reaches to its final stage.  Diseases which directly affect the growth and milk production in cows are “Mastitis, Ketosis, Foot & Mouth disease”. All these diseases are directly or indirectly linked with the 
rising temperature in cows. If at early stage, these diseases are captured and cured, thousands of cows can be saved every year and Pakistan can in increase its dairy exports.

data.projectName: A Unified Maturity Model of Software Testing for DevOps
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: In this era of technology advancements, software based systems are becoming part of our daily life activities. For the development of a software system from inception to deployment, many professional/experts get involved during different phases of software development life cycle (SDLC) [5]. Different SDLC processes/methods are proposed to develop different sort of systems. Not all these methods are fit for all purposes; however, the quality assurance during the complete SDLC process and to audit the compliance of quality standards during this process should be part of every such method. DevOp [1,2] is one such method becoming popular among the software development organizations (SDO). In this proposed work, we would like to explore the state of current quality standards (for assurance and auditing) being practiced in DevOp [3,4]. We intend to provide a comprehensive unified standard and a maturity model for generic use; this standard would be customizable according to the specific needs of different SDOs. In order for SDOs to adapt their working to our proposed standards, we would provide a prototype tool to support the application of our standard.

data.projectName: Maternal and child health management (M2CH) system
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Maternal and child nutrition has been on the global agenda in low-and-middle-income countries (LMIC). Recent studies highlight the need to address the problems of maternal and childhood through proven nutrition-specific and nutrition-sensitive interventions. The 1000 days of early life stages from conception to 2 years are considered critical in nutrition for enhancing short and long-term health outcomes. 
Key challenges are blood cytometry and nutrition diagnostics. These two features need to be implemented in a device which is portable and smart. Currently these devices exist in the diagnostics lab, expensive and scarceness in the rural areas. Portable device which can monitor a) blood count and b) nutrition is inevitable because of high infant mortality rate, malnutrition and non-availability of testing facility in the rural areas. 
Blood counter will calculate blood cells like red/white blood cells and platelets etc. so that blood sample of the patient can be monitored remotely by the expert doctors. Reagent-based nutrition counter will calculate the important nutrients required at different stages.  
Diet will be formulated for each region/individual group and its response will be tested.
Finally, the data will be incorporated into e-health platform which will be able to predict diet/disease based on test result.

data.projectName: Chloroplast pan-genomics based on presence/absence of variations in the plastome-contents, plastomic profiling, and field evaluation of grain Amaranthus as a gluten-free crop to supplement cereals
data.projectDigest:
Food security and malnutrition are major concerns of the world. Plant scientists are exploring the plant biodiversity using novel approaches to expand the crop list. Agricultural advantages and unique nutritional properties of grain amaranth has gained increased attention. So, amaranth is being investigated as an alternate grain crop and/or as a supplement to the cereal crops. The amino acid, lysine is very limited in cereals whereas methionine in legumes however, these amino acids are present in high amounts in Amaranth seeds. Considering Amaranth seeds as a rich source of proteins, amino acids, vitamins, and minerals the current proposal is being submitted for consideration with the following objectives:
1.	Chloroplast pan-genomics and - transcriptomic profiling of Amaranthus.
2.	Determining the association of varying plastomic contents with plastomic signatures.
3.	Functional analysis of genome through transcriptome profiling. 
4.	Field evaluation by planting the varieties on the University farm. 
Successful completion of this project will help train students in the emerging area of Pan-Genomics, High throughput analysis using microarrays, next-generation sequencing, and omics approaches. Further, the selection of high performing lines in the field will be helpful in addressing the food security and malnutrition problems in Pakistan in line with the Strategic Development Goals (SDGs) of vision 2030 of United Nations - adopted by Pakistan government.

data.projectName: Mapping out the Impact of Feminist Politics on Pakistani Culture: Issues, Gains and Challenges( A Critical Investigation of Indigenous Feminist Movement (1980-2019))
data.projectDigest: The present project is an attempt to map out the impact of feminist politics on Pakistani culture with a view to see how it has transformed into a more gender egalitarian landscape in both the private and public space of Pakistani men and women. To achieve this goal, the project seeks to undertake a critical revisioning of indigenous feminist ideologies and activism in the last four decades.It goes without saying that the feminist politics have influenced the cultural, political and economic landscape of Pakistan by promising a large section of womenfolk economic empowerment, political participation and distinct agency. By delimiting this inquiry within the material and political realities of Pakistani culture, which have been definitely shaped and influenced byfeminist ideology, the proposed project is a means to acknowledge the real gains of feminist movement in the history of Pakistan.  Nonetheless, the indigenous feminist movement has yet to acknowledged the myriad ways in which Pakistani women have contested the battle of their identity vis-à-vis societal conventions and cultural mores. Following Saba Mehmood’s theorization, the project argues that feminist activism needs to think and “move beyond the binary of resistance and subordination to understand the complex ways in which (Muslim) women in particular and Pakistani women in general have expressed their agency” (cited in Zia, p.36). Moreover, by viewing this objective as a national challenge, the project is likely to offer a blueprint of a more meaningful and constructive participation of this bulging potential of women in the political economy of Pakistan by simultaneously offering a more gender-egalitarian culture for all sections of society.

data.projectName: Self-powered Nanosensors for the Fourth Industrial Revolution
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: The fourth industrial revolution (4IR) is going to revolutionize the human society with the coming of smart homes and cities, e-health, autonomous appliances, automated robots etc. This will correspondingly translate into a massive change in the economy and industry. Considering the impact, there is a dire need at the national level to prepare for its realization and to live up with the challenges. Internet of things (IoTs), autonomous vehicles, robotics, artificial intelligence (AI) and augmented reality (AR) are among the key constituents of 4IR. However, they rely on the crucial sensory information from sensors for their operation. IoTs, in particular, is a largely distributed network of sensors. There are two crucial research challenges to realize the sensors for IoTs, autonomous vehicles, robotics, AI and AR, and so the 4IR: (1) energy supply and (2) high performance environmental sensing. Though batteries can supply energy, they have a limited life. Indeed, battery replacements can practically be impossible considering billions of distributed sensors and their location (such as within a wall, underground, inside a tyre etc.). In order to circumvent the challenge, the sensors has to be self-powered for a sustainable operation. Besides, for high performance environmental sensing, nano technologies can potentially add unique features of high density, ultra-low power consumption, reduced weight, high sensitivity and multi functionality to the sensors. This project therefore aims at developing “self-powered nanosensors for 4IR.”

data.projectName: Hybrid-solar energy efficient stoves for health resilinece of women and children against household air pollution
data.projectDigest: Burning of solid fuel (wood, crop residues, cow dung, coal etc.) in traditional three brick stoves cause household air pollution (HAP) which lead to 3.8 million global deaths annually.  About half of Pakistan’s population (and 75% rural) burn solid fuel in traditional stoves for cooking. Burning solid fuels in traditional stoves leads to inefficient combustion, generating health damaging pollutants, which are 100 times higher in kitchens and living rooms than acceptable ambient air standards. Women and young children who spend 90% time at home and in kitchens are exposed more to pollutants causing diseases primarily of heart and lungs. A household in Pakistan burns 2325 kg wood per annum. Besides affecting health, burning wood for cooking leads to deforestation and contributes to climate change. Providing clean fuel (gas/electricity) is costly. Hybrid solar stove (HSS), a gassifier is an emerging technology. It gasifies biomass fuel with the electric fan. Electric fan utilizes solar energy. HSS decreases emissions and fuel consumption. Food cooked with HSS tastes same as food cooked on traditional stove. In this project we want to test the acceptability and feasibility of HSS; determine the effects of HSS in reducing HAP and improving health of women and children.

data.projectName: DREAM30: Towards Pakistan’s Own Electric Vehicle
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
In order to reduce the burgeoning fuel import bill and air pollution in our cities, this proposal, relevant to the priority thematic area of Sustainable Energy, aims to tackle the grand challenge of developing low-cost electric mobility solutions. The project takes a holistic approach in identifying the most pressing technological EV challenges in the Pakistani context, thereby carrying indigenous R&D on essential technology enablers such as battery technology, inverters, motors, sensors and electronic control units (ECUs), charging stations, mechanical design and manufacturing and EV standardization, finally culminating into Pakistan’s own concept electric vehicle. Contrary to the internal combustion engine era, where Pakistan has remained dependent on imported technology, the vision is to make Pakistan self-reliant in critical EV sub-systems, rather be able to export the same in long term. 

The multi-disciplinary project is divided into 9 workpackages and a strong consortium of 21 PhD faculty members from 3 universities (NUST, FAST NU & Bahria University) and 11 departments has been formed. In addition, 11 local industrial partners (Sazgar engineering, Jolta Electric, Skyelectric etc), 13 international advisors (from Tesla, Karma automotive, Lucid motors etc) and government representative from Engineering Development Board (EDB) is part of the consortium to provide strategic advice during project execution.

data.projectName: Landscaping Genetic diversity in Cholistani cattle
data.projectDigest: Cholistani cattle are considered as dairy animal of Cholistan performing on water scarce areas. This cattle breed possesses certain features that are rare in other breeds like tolerance to heat, resistance to ticks to some extent and well productive in water shortage and scarcity. These are Bos indicus animals and yet have not been explored and genetically characterized. The project is aimed at breeding profiling according FAO guidelines given in breed descriptors and studying the genotypic diversity through gene markers and hopefully QTL mapping for dairy characters. This would animal us in identifying their true genetic potential and breed improvement. Ultimately generating demand in the water scare world would bring good amount of foreign exchange through export of Cholistani cattle.

data.projectName: Technology enabled medical emergency response for urban planning – a pathway towards safer and healthier cities
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Integrating health components in urban planning is among the core themes of WHO European Healthy Cities Network. Road traffic accidents (RTAs) have been regarded as a major global concern taking the lives of 1.3 million people every year and injuring 24 million peoples. Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is predominant among RTA injuries as reported in road casualties report 2008 published by “Road Traffic Injury Research & Prevention Centre” and is categorized as the most severe injuries; making it a top global health priority for which an immediate attention is required. In Pakistan, 348,947 TBI cases were reported in 1990 which have escalated to 745,843 in 2016 with highest mortality rate of 6% from RTA. This project endeavours to develop consolidated system that integrates preventive measures with health care facilities. Preventive measures include identifying accident-prone areas, implementing traffic policies and launch emergency response system for reporting RTA to nearby hospitals. Post TBI services inculcates design of clinical practical guidelines for interpretation of brain imaging, electrophysiological recordings, rehabilitation and followup. This project intends to upgrade healthy urban policies via technology driven solution. It will improve the quality of life of TBI, stroke and spinal cord injury patients by providing immediate attention in acute phase of injury.

data.projectName: Optimizing mass production of microbial control agents for commercial scale production against locusts
data.projectDigest: The destructive role of locusts in gregarious form is referred as plague and has been mentioned in Holy scripts of almost every religion. Pakistan is facing its worst locust infestation which entered in the country during June 2019 from Iran. Increasing awareness of the economic and environmental cost of failure to prevent locust swarms is leading to a call for a more integrated approach to locust and grasshopper control. The overall goal of the proposed project is to enhance the efficacy of entomopathogens, with some specific goals as improving production methods to reduce cost of these microbes, development of formulations that enhance shelf life and field efficacy, producing commercial formulation of test microbes which will reduce cost and be more target specific for commercial application, and establishment of Locust Biocontrol Unit at UAF. The goals of this project will be accomplished through a collaboration of academia and industrial partners. The consortium consists of Pakistan China and UK based researchers and industry partners who have complementary expertise. The project will benefit the academic partners in expanding their knowledge and translating it to develop novel biopesticides. The findings of this study will also help to accelerate the adoption of environmentally safe locusts control strategies in Pakistan

data.projectName: Effects of socio-economic, terrestrial and climatic factors effects on surface water quality at multiple spatial scales
data.projectDigest: The impairment of surface water quality has gained considerable attention at global scale due to increasing demand for high quality freshwater. Surface water quality is considered to be deteriorated by natural factors and anthropogenic activities such as terrestrial determinants, socioeconomic and climatic factors. The quantification of direct and indirect effects of socioeconomic, terrestrial and hydro-meteorological factors on water quality parameters is necessary for protecting ecological health. It is also important for sustainable development and policy formulation at basin scale

data.projectName: Establishement of Information System to Produce Official Statistics for Innovative Governance and Reforms
data.projectDigest: Official statistics are main source to track economic, demographic and social conditions in any country or region. National Statistical Organizations (NSO’s) in Pakistan such as Bureau of Statistics (BoS) Punjab  are collecting data using surveys and administrative data sources but facing problem of producing accurate, timely and faster official statistics due to the fact that they are not integrating big data sources with the existing data  and are not using advanced analytics tools to produce the statistical results. This project aimed at establishment of information system  with the collaboration of Bureau of Statistics (BoS) Punjab to foster the innovation and research in integration and storage of big data from various sources, development of machine learning and data mining algorithms for predictive analytics, capacity building to increase adoption and utilization of big data, conversion of structured, semi-structured and unstructured data in the form of meaningful official statistics, releasing at real time the comprehensive, multidimensional and reliable statistics for policymakers to formulate evidence based policies.

data.projectName: Indigenous Technology Development of All-Solid-State Lithium-ion Batteries for Domestic and Commercial Photovoltaic Systems
data.projectDigest: In an unstable grid environment of Pakistan, where power outages can occur regularly, it is extremely important that the batteries are charged using photovoltaic energy and ready to provide backup efficiently. Lithium-ion batteries powered by solid state electrolytes (SSEs) (all-solid-state batteries) offer significant advantages, including battery life of up to 10+ year, environment friendly, heat tolerance, improved safety, efficient fast charging and the ability to deep cycle while maintaining power. Being deprived of a manufacturing facility, in Pakistan, we are compelled to import such batteries from technologically advanced countries, which makes them unaffordable for most of the people living in the power outage areas of Pakistan. This research proposal is motivated by the ability of organic-inorganic hybrid materials to serve as a low cost and efficient solid electrolyte material in Li-ion batteries and the possibility of manufacturing durable, light weight and low cost energy storage devices for application in domestic and commercial power generation, particularly in rural areas of Pakistan where photovoltaic systems are the only pertinent solutions. The interest of this proposed work lies in the possibility to integrate both durability and high charge storage properties of the indigenously designed and synthesized materials to obtain the maximum efficiency.

data.projectName: Agriculture Productivity Enhancement through Participatory Research Approach in Potohar Plateau
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
Potwar plateau is undulated and gullied semiarid to sub-humid upland, about 250 km long and 100 km wide, between the rivers Jhelum and Indus, mainly consisting of Districts of Attock, Rawalpindi and Chakwal in Punjab, Pakistan. Of the total area of 1.8 million hectares, 0.77 million hectares is cultivated, almost all rain-fed, the remaining is grazing land. The rainfall is erratic, as heavy downpours causing soil erosion. Major crops are wheat, gram, groundnut, millets, sorghum, oilseeds, maize and sunflower. Soil, water and fertilizer management practices are poor. Agriculture productivity is low. 
The soil conservation technology and crop production technologies are available, but in spite of the efforts of various government departments, soil erosion low agriculture productivity prevails. In this context, University of Arid Agriculture proposes to adopt a farmer participatory approach for research and development and repackaging technologies to arrest erosion and increase agriculture productivity.
The proposal envisages extensive training of local farmers on site-specific packages of technologies. University of Arid Agriculture would also launch vigorous farmer participatory research for sharpening the existing technologies, in collaboration of partner institutions. Major emphasis would be on improving current farming systems, using improved soil, water and fertilizer management techniques and developing new farming systems, where indicated, likely to improve productivity, environment and income of farmers. The proposal also envisages establishing a seed bank of improved crop varieties and an Integrated Recovery Resource Centre (IRRC) at University Research Farm, Koont, Chakwal, in collaboration with Manchester University, UK, The UN Habitat, Dr.AkhtarHameed Memoria

data.projectName: Innovative, Advanced and Affordable Greener Treatment Technology for Total Arsenic Removal and its Socio-economic Impacts in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest: Providing high-quality clean drinking water is a significant challenge faced by developing countries, including Pakistan. In this project, an improved solution is proposed to remove total arsenic chemical contamination in Pakistan with affordability and rapid remediation. That will help in achieving the Sustainable Development Goal, SDG6—Clean Water and Sanitation. This technology will also reduce healthcare expenditures, hence addressing SDG1—No Poverty. More than 200 million people are affected by high concentrations of arsenic in groundwater around the world. More than 50 million people in Pakistan are at risk of arsenic in groundwater. Conventional methods do not yet offer cost-effectiveness, operational flexibility, in-situ usability, and reproducibility. These methods do not completely degrade the chemical contaminant, but rather change its phase. Advanced oxidation/reduction adsorption processes (AOPs) in nanotechnology achieve the goal of complete destruction of a metal contaminant in water. The results of a similar small scale study by PI were very promising, with 99% removal using iron oxide nanoparticles. This study proposes fabrication of greener iron nanoparticle impregnated nano filter membranes with increased removal efficiency of total arsenic from drinking water by chemical reduction method. Fifteen most contaminated districts of Pakistan in Sindh and Punjab are selected as case studies.

data.projectName: Supply chain transparency model for energy, Health and Agricultural commodities: A step towards supply chain resilience and sustainability
data.projectDigest:
Transparency is need of the hour to ensure supply chain resilience and sustainability. Opaqueness increases the probability of supply disruptions because of mismanagement and intractability, leading to several operational, financial and strategic issues. Recent shortfalls and price hikes of vegetables, medicines, sugar and wheat in Pakistan alarmed the need of sustainable supply chain models to avoid such incidents in future. The transparency in supply chains of these commodities can be helpful in overcoming issues of supply disruptions, hoarding, smuggling, lower productivity, poor utilization of resources and incompetence; to name a few. Similarly, the performances of other supply chains (energy, services, industrial etc.) can be enhanced through transparency and traceability models. 
Because of opaqueness in supply chains of almost every sector, there is no check and balance in the departments which is seriously affecting performances and economic growth. Through transparency, monitoring and control would be easy for the managers. In broader prospects, it can help in better governance, improved productivity and service level with optimum resource utilization.
Keeping in view above facts, we proposed this project of transparency in supply chains for tackling the issues of supply disruptions and economic loss in order to fulfill the gap of supply and demand.

data.projectName: Nucleic acid-based vaccines production by CRISPR/Cas9
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
Nucleic acid-based vaccines represent a major innovation towards possible vaccination strategies. Conventional vaccine development has relied on manufacturing live attenuated or inactivated pathogens. While extremely effective, this is a time-consuming and expensive approach. In contrast, recent advances in manufacturing nucleic acids for vaccination have made very promising advances. Nucleic acid-based vaccines can be manufactured much faster and can be adapted much more rapidly to changes in antigen sequence. Since no live replication-competent pathogen is handled throughout the process, the product is deemed to be far safer and requires far less infrastructure about Health and Safety for both, the manufacturer and most importantly the patients.
This proposal aims to establish bacterial strain engineering by means of directed genome editing. For this, expression of CRISPR/Cas9 endonuclease/recombinase is to be developed in the bacterial host cell lines. Expression of the Cas9 protein in combination with a sequence-specific small guide RNA allows for sequence-dependent cleavage of the chromosomal DNA at desired loci. This is an extremely rapid and cost-effective tool that allows precise editing of the genome.

data.projectName: Integrating liquid-biopsy based multimodal platform and machine learning/artificial intelligence for improved cancer management in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
With more than 170,000 new cases and 120,000 deaths (recorded during 2018), cancer has been ranked as the second leading cause of death and a major healthcare challenge in Pakistan. ‘Early-stage, cost-effective diagnosis’ is a critical component of success in cancer treatment and a way to lessen the burden of this complex and life-threatening disease. To this end, several DNA, RNA, protein or metabolite-based cancer-markers have been identified in the tumor tissues. However, none of the mono-markers exhibits sufficient diagnostic sensitivity, specificity and utility in clinical oncology.  
To address this grand challenge and an important healthcare issue, we propose a multimodal liquid biopsy approach involving scanning of exosomal cargo [nanosized extracellular vesicles carrying DNA, RNA, miRNA, proteins] in the 1,000 (1K) blood samples of cancer/non-cancer subjects by using genome-wide high throughput next generation sequencing, digital droplet PCR and mass spectrometry, and integration of multi-omic big data for parallel exhaustive exploration of sets of mutational catalogues (known & new) by machine learning (ML) and/or artificial intelligence (AI), as a promising way to improve the cancer management in Pakistan. A database and online easy-to-use tool will also be developed to allow researchers/clinicians freely access big-omic-data for research, education, patient-care and biomedical applications.

data.projectName: Development of Nanostructured Transition Metal Chalcogenides based devices for sustainable energy, water and environment
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: The project shall be addressing “Sustainable energy, energy efficiency” and “Water management and sustainability”. These are two of major hitches in progress of a developing country. Fossil fuels are imported which engulf large economical share of the budget, and the industry giant is largely dependent on this limited energy resource. It dictates the industrial production and cost. Pakistan is blessed with solar spectrum all around the year. If nanotechnology is utilized to harness this energy for both day and night, so, energy can be available 24/7 and the colossal gap of energy may be filled.  The solar energy will be utilized for the development of devices that will be able to purify water and add to the energy resource options like supercapacitors. The water is most vital resource of nature for living beings. This priceless resource must be managed properly or our future generation may face difficulty to satisfy their survival needs. Besides Pakistan being and agricultural country is dependent on water availability. Water purification is very important to rescue our water resources and make them useable.

data.projectName: Research Prototype Reactors for Bio, Plastic and mixed  waste to Energy Conversion
data.projectDigest:
Waste disposal in the open is ruining atmosphere; polluting air by the discharge of volatiles of organic nature; contaminating water and air by plastics and mixed waste. Moreover, waste is causing problems of sewerage blockage and global warming. Heaps of waste in the entire society are not only environmental problem but also worst site scenes.  Managing organic (municipal kitchen and vegetable wastes), plastics, solid and unsegregated waste huge amount of energy can be recovered in addition to by-products, i.e., fertilizer from organic and slag from the plastics or mixed waste.
In this research challenge we are proposing degeneration of waste to energy(fuel), fertilizer and slag from organic, plastics and mixed(unsorted) waste by giving three research prototype reactors for each category.
Bio waste (Kitchen waste) will be converted to energy by developing multi-stage reactors. Three and four stage will be only research while two stage will be a research and business model together
Plastic waste will be gasified to energy using low temperature treatment of plastics. Catalysts will be developed to boost gasification at low temperature.
Mixed waste will be blown to give maximum thrust and will be utilized in gas turbine for power generation by Low temperature incineration.

data.projectName: Antibiotic alternatives: An attempt to enhance aquaculture production and drug discovery from marine microbial ecosystems in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Microorganisms in nature play a vital role in escalating digestion, absorption and assimilation of nutrients, preventing growth of pathogens and can improve environmental conditions of the habitats. The extensive use of antibiotics in livestock, aquaculture, and use of pathogenic strains in aquatic environments has changed habitat characteristics by altering water chemistry. Such seawater changes negatively impacts on the growth, survival and fish production in aquaculture systems. Therefore, use of probiotics in aquaculture appeared to be an alternate source to curb growth of pathogens, enhance nutrients absorption, assimilation and improve environmental conditions to gain maximum benefits. Marine microorganisms, especially actinomycetes and Bacillus subtilis are an ideal multifunctional probiotic can efficiently break through such problems that would ultimately augment aquaculture production. This study aims to ascertain how to feed natures, formulated nutrition, and enhancement of C/N ratio that influence microbial community diversity and functionality of water and sediment of an integrated aquaculture system. Using cultivation-based techniques, namely chemically mediated interactions (co-cultivation) and chemical elicitors would give rise to varied metabolic profiles. Therefore, we will further investigate chemistry of the isolated marine microbial natural products and the possibilities for curing a range of diseases i.e. human and aquaculture. In addition, it would be possible to integrate basic microbial approaches, computational methods and technological innovations, identify and discover natural products.
