data.projectName: Central Monitoring System for Water Resource Management for Watersheds of Sindh and Balochistan
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan has arid, semi-arid, and humid regions, and lies in monsoon and western disturbance region which brings precipitation from June to September. Decreased monsoon precipitation brings drought conditions and affects agriculture production. Due to the complexity of the soil-water processes, one of the strategies to prepare for drought and flood conditions is to understand and manage precipitation at watershed scale.
The understanding of factors of a watershed like climate, topography, management practices, and water balance is important in managing water resources. Precipitation, evapotranspiration, infiltration, and surface runoff are the basic components to the water balance of a watershed. The information regarding these components in the field including spatial variation is a fundamental requirement for water and nutrient management at watershed scale in the current climate change scenario.
This research proposal addresses the critical challenge of data scarcity being faced by the researchers at the water related institutions in the country. This project is indeed about changing the tides by producing observed hydrologic data by selecting six watersheds in Sindh and Balochistan. A monitoring system will record hydrologic data using sensors indigenously designed and deployed in the selected watersheds. Overall this study would a landmark in water resources management in Pakistan.

Precipitation, evapotranspiration, infiltration, and surface runoff are the basic components to the water balance of a watershed. The information regarding these components in the field including spatial variation is a fundamental requirement for water and nutrient management at watershed scale in the current climate change scenario.
This research proposal addresses the critical challenge of data scarcity being faced by the researchers at the water related institutions in the country. This project is indeed about changing the tides by producing observed hydrologic data by selecting six watersheds in Sindh and Balochistan. A monitoring system will record hydrologic data using sensors indigenously designed and deployed in the selected watersheds. Overall this study would a landmark in water resources management in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Competitiveness Enhancement of SME Clusters through Technology Roadmapping
data.projectDigest: Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) contribute about 30% to GDP, employ 60% of the workforce and constitute over 90% of all the businesses in Pakistan. Competitiveness of these SME value chains mainly depends upon technology development and adoption which is a long-standing issue impeding their performance. Cluster Development (CD) approach is an effective way for SMEs competitiveness enhancement. Similarly, Technology Roadmapping (TRM) is widely used process for addressing technological challenges faced by industry. Hence, this research aims to address competitiveness enhancement issue of SME clusters of Pakistan by using TRM based CD approach in which a novel TRM-CD framework will be developed and implemented. The project will identify key technology related issues faced by the selected SME clusters across the country in collaboration with national and international partners from industry, academia, donor agencies and consulting firms. Technology roadmaps will be developed, and comparative assessment of proposed solutions will be made based on their social, economic and environmental aspects against global challenges and best practices. Finally, policy documents along with the technology roll-out plans will be shared with the relevant stakeholders for better realization of technology related issues and their pragmatic solutions for sustainable economic growth of the country.

data.projectName: Haptic-Visual Force Feedback System for Surgical Training Simulation.
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
Our proposed idea is to design Virtual Human Interactive Lab for Designing Surgical Simulation. In this lab, surgical training simulators will be developed for various modes. The vision is to teach and educate the medical students & novel surgeon precise techniques & procedure for efficient surgical procedures and equip them with modern medical technologies & reduce the risk factor during actual surgical procedures. With this teaching approach, practicing on surgical procedures virtually using simulator will assist students in analyzing their performance by standard criteria. The main issue in existing haptic gadgets is that they are not equipped for summoning compound haptic sensations and show multiple properties of virtual objects, including softness, texture, temperature, three-dimensional (3-D) shape and weight. Therefore, to ensure an integral sensation, the surgical device should be able to simultaneously and intelligently exert multimodal stimuli at expected locations on the user’s body. 
 The proposed project has national contribution by implementing this idea within local hospitals with advantage of local production, guaranteed efficiency & cost effectiveness. The value addition is establishment of a Haptic-visual Simulator for all types of surgical procedures. The execution of this multiple-dimension surgical procedure would be based on set of algorithms designed as per considering the medical scenarios. This is aimed to be mega project for research & development sector for Haptic-Visual technology based on human computer interface.

data.projectName: HAND-AID: A novel artificial intelligence-based algorithm for effective differential diagnosis of HIV-associated neurological disorders
data.projectDigest: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) exerts a multi-system effect on the host body. Chronic HIV-induced immune activation, together with other factors, it can also lead to development of neurological and psychological disorders, referred to as HIV Associated Neurocognitive Disorder (HAND), which is characterized by impairment in a set of cognitive, motor and behavioral symptoms, and affects almost 50% of the people living with HIV (PLHIV). Diagnosis of HAND currently is complex and currently based on a battery of neurocognitive tests most driven from cohort studies conducted in Western and African countries. HAND diagnosis can be aided by neuroimaging techniques or estimation of established biomarkers, however, both are not routinely used for diagnosis purpose. All three techniques (neurocognitive test, neuroimaging and biomarker) have individual diagnostic value, however, there is a lack of integration between diagnosis based on neurocognitive test batteries, neuroimaging techniques and HAND-specific biomarkers. Consequently, a single parameter is insufficient to give an early, and correct diagnosis of HAND, and especially differentiate between HAND and non-HIV neurological disorders. The overall aim of this proposal is to devise an integrated Artificial intelligence-based algorithm that can not only perform an early and accurate HAND diagnosis but also differentiate between HAND and non-HIV neurological disorders.

data.projectName: Smart IoT based technologies; a way forward to improve the agricultural yield, reduce water loss in irrigation  and to design agricultural waste based efficient energy and feed systems
data.projectDigest: The overall goal of this project is on the implementation of smart technologies to increase the agricultural productivity, reduce water loss during irrigation process and to design efficient energy and feed systems based on the agricultural waste.  Agriculture is the second largest sector contributing a GPD of 19.5 %, with an employment factor of 42 % of total labor. In the same way, Pakistan is facing a major problem in term of ground water depletion. The total irrigation water use in Pakistan is 151 Km3/year, equal to 95% of the total withdrawal in the country. Farming in Pakistan mostly rely on the conventional practice where excess of fertilizers, pesticides and water are employed. This ultimately results in high production cost with inefficient use of resources. Similarly, there is significant impediment to convert agricultural waste into value added products such as a source of energy.  This proposal will address these needs by (1) automated control of crop needs, crop growth factors, need based supply of crop ingredients; (2) automated field ready toxicity texting platform for food quality assessment and safety; (3) Self-driven machines for seeding, picking, harvesting purpose…etc (4) IoT based dripping irrigation and use of agriculture waste as energy source.

AN ASSESSMENT THE PREDICTORS OF CHILD MORTALITY IN DISTRICT THARPARKAR, SINDH, PAKISTAN

Thematic and content analysis will be used to develop the streamline among the respondents opinions. Descriptive and inferential statistics will be applied to dig out the under investigation issue.

data.projectName: A novel approach for rapid field detection of plant parasitic nematodes
data.projectDigest:
The growing demand for food with limited available land necessitates that the yield of major crops continues to increase over time. Advances in molecular marker technology, predictive statistics, control over parasitic entity and breeding methodology have allowed for continued increases in crop performance through genetic improvement (Gerald et al., 2013). Plant parasitic nematodes are traditionally detected by a slow and time-consuming process. This typically involves collecting soil samples, extracting the nematodes via an elutriator and identifying the nematodes by visual observation under a microscope. Furthermore, this slow and expensive process requires personnel to have advanced nematology training to identify nematodes based upon morphological features. The conventional approach alone does not justify the availability of new cultivars in shortest span (Cattivelli et al., 2008). Though conventional mode of identification of nematodes is in practice, however, the progress is too slow. Meanwhile, selection based on its component characters could be more efficient and reliable if the knowledge of genes associated with pathogenic effect is known (Muhammad et al., 2003). Transgenic and “omics” technologies promise to make progress through a more fundamental understanding of underlying mechanisms of parasitic inheritance and identifying potential candidate genes (Khan et al., 2013). (Tuberosa, Salvi, 2006).
In the field, immediate detection of nematodes will be made possible by the success of the proposed project titled “A novel approach for rapid field detection of plant parasitic nematodes”. Growers would then be able to map their farms with nematode infestations and plant seed genotypes appropriate to their fields.

data.projectName: Development and production of indigenous Drug Coated Balloon  Angioplasty Catheter in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Four decades after its introduction into clinical practice, coronary balloon angioplasty is still used during most coronary interventions. Conventional balloon angioplasty is frequently used to pre-dilate complex or severe lesions and remains of major value to optimize the results of stent implantation. Plain balloon angioplasty is still used alone in some anatomic scenarios where stent implantation is not desirable (very small vessels or diffuse lesions, large resistant thrombus burden, side branches of bifurcations). However, this technique is hampered by a relatively high restenosis risk. Recently, drug-coated balloons (DCB) have been shown to provide an attractive new tool for the "leave nothing behind" strategy. 
Drug Coated Balloon (DCB) catheters are FDA approved catheters which are being imported China, Japan and majorly from USA. The total usage of Drug Coated Balloon (DCB) catheters in Pakistan is dependent on the availability of the DCB catheters as these catheters are in available to cardiologists in very less amount. Import of Drug Coated Balloon (DCB) catheters costs Pakistan an exorbitant economic burden in international imports due to unavailability of any facility for indigenization of Drug Coated Balloon (DCB) catheters.

Our Project proposal is unique since there are no indigenous Drug Coated Balloon (DCB) catheters manufacturing facilities in the country; however, two foreign suppliers namely Boston Scientific and Abbott (imported Drug Coated Balloon (DCB) catheters) currently dominate a large part of the local market. Their products have been tested through standardized manufacturing protocols, and comply with international standards; however they are an expensive treatment option for most people.

data.projectName: Valorization of industrial by-product for synthesis of low-cost sustainable concrete.
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is a developing country and with the stage set for golden era of development, the challenges are high. There are multiple construction projects and activities being undertaken at the national level. One of the projects is “Naya Pakistan Housing Project (NPHP)” which aims at the development of 5 million homes for the underprivileged society. Generally, traditional construction materials i.e. cement, river sand, and crush are being utilized in Pakistan. These materials pose a significant impact on the sustainability since they are causing resource depletion which in turn increases the cost. Therefore, there is a need to explore alternative low-cost materials which are readily available in the country for the success of NPHP project. This research will evaluate the prospects of utilizing fly-ash, a by-product of coal combustion plants, as a replacement of ordinary Portland cement in concrete. The utilization of such smart materials has not been industrialized, in Pakistan, due to lack of academic research and recommendations on the field. The research work will adopt a systematic approach to assess technical, environmental, economic and social feasibility of utilizing fly-ash in concrete. A model house will be constructed using fly-ash based concrete blocks, slab and plaster based on recommendations.

data.projectName: Development of Technology for hyperactivation and stabilization of Microbial Alkaline Proteases for repeated industrial applications
data.projectDigest:
Protease enzyme are almost of 35% of the total microbial enzymes sale. Interest has been growing in microbial proteases that are eco-friendly as well as commercially important. In this research different microbial strains will be exploited for the optimal production of proteases. The protease production by the selected protease producing strain will be enhanced through metabolic engineering strategy Proteases will be produced under optimum conditions determined through RSM using Central Composite Design. Downstream processes will be applied using state of the art techniques for the purification of these biocatalysts. 
The catalytic efficiency, stability and repeated utilization of the enzymes in industrial batch operations are the main challenges that need to be addressed. Different strategies will be used to overcome the activity and stability limitations. Different immobilization strategies will have been developed to stabilize the enzymes for their repeated utilization in multiple industrial process cycles. In the present project the purified alkaline proteases will be immobilized by the most advanced method by developing cross-linked enzyme aggregates (CLEAs) and Cross-linked enzyme crystals (CLECs). Parallel comparative kinetics studies will be carried out for  immobilized and free proteases. The immobilized enzymes will used in consecutive repeated industrial batch operations to determine their suitability for economic industrial applications. Moreover, the process of immobilization will also be scaled up to pilot/industrial scale. The team of the current project is highly competent to execute the present project with collaboration of the industry.

data.projectName: Autonomous Healthcare Monitoring using Smart Environments with Sensor Fusion and Machine Learning
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Healthcare system in Pakistan is under significant pressure due to large population, lack of resources, poor investments and shortage in health workforce. These multi-dimensional and complex challenges underpin the fragility of primary healthcare. According to World Health Organization reports, Pakistan has 0.5 Physicians and only 20 hospital beds per 10,000 populations. We view this as a grand challenge for the country and aim to address this using advances in acquiring patient medical data and communicating, processing, and analyzing it with the use of information technology and statistical science.

In the context of rising demand for limited and expensive resources, it will increasingly become essential to perform routine monitoring with an affordable autonomous evaluation system, and free up human labour for higher value services. The need for telemedicine and eHealth, areas covered in this project, was first realized in the aftermath of 2005 earthquake.  We plan to address the national healthcare challenge at scale through the creation of smart remote monitoring environments that can autonomously monitor and analyse activities to enable patients to live more independently as well as provide access to much needed real-time data to healthcare professionals. Hence, the target groups of this project include patients and health care practitioners as well as the paramedical staff.

data.projectName: Assessing the viability of maize–soybean strip intercropping system for improving resource use efficiency, soil sustainability and livelihood security of the farming community
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan, in future, crop productivity will be affected by the irrational cropping system adopted by the farming community. The existing cropping systems in the country such as Rice–wheat, cotton-wheat, and sugarcane–wheat showed a declining trend in production because of none judiciously use of natural (soil, water, light and radiation use) and applied (cultivation, fertilizers and pesticides) resources. Decreasing trend of yield with the rapid increase of population growth will remain a serious pressure and threat in the country till the time these issues are not addressed on scientific lines. In Pakistan, rainfed and irrigated agriculture need to be redesigned according to the need of local community and available resources. There is a need to rejuvenate the cropping systems which are more efficient in utilizing natural resources and less dependent on applied resources. The maize-soybean intercropping system is the potential cropping system that can successfully replace summer fallow in rainfed areas, and it can also provide an alternative option in cotton, rice and sugarcane sown areas for resource-poor farmers to enhance sustainability and profitability. The maize-soybean strip intercropping system would be helpful to minimize the heavy consumption of water.

data.projectName: Development of a Global Construction Progress Monitoring Platform
data.projectDigest:
The current market size of Pakistan’s construction industry is 343.183 billion. The global construction market is worth US$10 Trillion. Superficially, the construction industry would seem healthy.  However, more than 90% of world infrastructure projects are late and/or over budget [3]. Losses of Billions of Dollars per year [4] are reported because of construction errors. The main cause is that, there is no centralized place where construction sites (of varying magnitudes - from small buildings to mega projects) can be monitored visually and analyzed with measurements to avoid any delays/errors.

There are two important parts of construction monitoring: quality and schedule. Costs of the project are closely tied to both. We aim to solve the problem of construction progress monitoring /auditing by providing a user-friendly low-cost solution which will centralize and simplify the management of construction sites and their operations, maximize efficiency, raise productivity and lower overall costs.

The proposed solution as a result of the R&D through this project would be a mobile-accessible, cloud-based SaaS (Software as a Service) platform, allowing users to be the master of their construction sites by providing visual and volumetric monitoring of their construction projects.

There are two important parts of construction monitoring: quality and schedule. Costs of the project are closely tied to both. We aim to solve the problem of construction progress monitoring /auditing by providing a user-friendly low-cost solution which will centralize and simplify the management of construction sites and their operations, maximize efficiency, raise productivity and lower overall costs.

The proposed solution as a result of the R&D through this project would be a mobile-accessible, cloud-based SaaS (Software as a Service) platform, allowing users to be the master of their construction sites by providing visual and volumetric monitoring of their construction projects.

data.projectName: Innovative indigenous mechanization of sugarcane sowing, intercropping and harvesting through a plenary set of technology
data.projectDigest: Principal investigator has invented indigenous mechanization systems for sugarcane sett plantation, intercropping and harvesting to address the acute problem of labor shortage and high production cost of sugarcane in Pakistan. This proposed project is to conduct research for technology generation test, its dissemination, and to facilitate the farmers to adopt this technology on economical basis. The motive of all these innovations is social wisdom, economic acceptability, and environment friendly technologies. In the first year of this project multi-location field trials will be conducted at two places to evaluate operational quality of machinery and their impact on sugarcane growth and yield in both seasons of sugarcane sowing i.e. September & March sowing. During the second year of project thirty-five acres from seven different sugarcane growing districts will be selected and tested machinery will be used for sowing, intercropping and harvesting for technology verification test in both seasons of sugarcane sowing. In the 3rd year of project, possible sugarcane growers will be facilitated through this machinery and training of labor on no profit no loss basis for said operations. The following activities will be done to achieve said objectives of project i.e. project management, mechanized scientific research, mechanized sugarcane production technology, technical assistance for machinery, technology generation test, technology verification test, amendment/improvement through reverse engineering, farmer’s training, and dissemination of this technology to the end users with the help of national and international project partners.

data.projectName: Assessment of genetic quality in the captive and wild L. rohita and initiation of selective breeding program across Pakistan by adopting molecular approaches
data.projectDigest: With the expansion of human population, the demand for high-quality protein, especially from aquatic sources, is rising dramatically. Literature reveals the decline in capture fisheries and increase in pressure on aquaculture. From the last decade, although aquaculture sector in Pakistan is growing but as compare to other leading countries at a very low rate and need further improvements or increased in the scale and efficiency in order to meet food insecurity challenges of new millennium. Fish production can be increase either by management practices or by genetic intervention but latter one has gained more attention because of the selection and transfer of desire traits generation after generation and production of superior stock. In aquaculture, use of best-performing strains is the first step in a genetic improvement program and the mechanism to make the most rapid initial progress in genetic improvement. Major objective of this project is to evaluate the genetic differences in all possible commercial traits of maximum stocks of at least one culturable species L. rohita across Pakistan, by adopting molecular tools, select best stock in each province, develop true breeding line and/or crossbreed that will shows higher growth rate, improved disease resistance, reduced production cost and better yield

data.projectName: 36 Months
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
To find the practicability of renewable energy sources powered irrigation system seems appealing approach to reduce the farming carbon footprint. The feasibility of the RES (PV, Wind) powered irrigation system depends on the water demand profile of the respected crops. The RES continuously changing output depends on meteorological elements. The water demand depends on the water requirement of a crop, irrigation type and land characteristics. The water requirements of crop future depend on growing season soil nature and varying weather elements.   
The techno-economic feasibility of the subject irrigation system will be meaningful to design the system or related policies or decision making. The aim of this research to develop a tool for techno-economic feasibility by dynamic modelling which can take into account the RES continuously varying output, water demand, and irrigation system.  This tool able will able to not only able useful for determining the type and share and ratio of RES for a particular crop in a particular region but also determine the best economical mode of irrigation. 
As per the survey report by ministry of Finance, agriculture sector which contribute around 19 % of country GDP and employed 42% of labor force is facing water shortage. Further report predicted that the water shortage will grow continuously in future. This water demand supply gap can be made shorter by introducing tech in this sector. The prime objective of 12th Five Year Plan 2018-23 is to develop and line up investments for water sector. The proposed project address this national challenge via multi thematic area of the GCF e.g. Sustainable Energy, Climate Change and Environment, Water Managements and Sustainability.

data.projectName: Sustainable and Resilient Pakistan (SARP)
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Different parts of Pakistan face natural hazards due to diversity of topography and varied climatic conditions. These hazards often turn into disasters and cause large-scale infrastructure damages and human losses. Different contributing factors include varied population density, unplanned development in disaster prone areas, vulnerability of population segments, poverty and lack of preparedness. Reconstruction of damaged infrastructure after a disaster requires substantial human, material and financial resources which puts huge burden on the economy, national output and gross domestic product of the country. In addition, this also creates challenges for the creation of sustainable and resilient built environment. 
Pakistan has been a victim of earthquakes from time to time. Despite of these occurrences of earthquakes and subsequent losses, studies related to creation of resilient built environment are limited in Pakistan. Besides earthquake, Pakistan also faces a number of other natural hazards including flood, cyclones, droughts, avalanches, etc. These hazards create emergency situations when they happen in populated regions of the country. The use of information technology can become helpful in the relief operation of response agencies. 
All the aforementioned elements of risk and aspects of disaster mitigation have been considered in the studies proposed in this project which are aimed at increasing disaster resilience of built environment in Pakistan. These studies have been designed to cover various aspects of this challenge at both macro and micro levels.

data.projectName: THRIVE (Three generational Reframing via Investing in Vocational Education and Empowerment)
data.projectDigest: Project THRIVE focuses on a three-generational approach by targeting women, their newborns, eldest out of school girl child who takes care of their younger siblings via investing in their education, vocational skills, and empowerment. The project has multidimensional benefits and alignment to the thematic focus of grand challenges of our nation Pakistan  i.e. from the food security focusing on better maternal and child development outcomes by providing them with conducive environment and regularized meals, from development economics perspective this will work as an intervention for healthy lives of three generations, from sociology and philosophy front focusing on providing opportunities to become gender empowered and increased chances of participation in the workforce and improve opportunities for family and future. Women and children are considered to be any nation’s treasures and as well as a core responsibility. Empowered women, mainstreamed children and healthy newborns have the vast potential of contributing to their best in socio-economic empowerment of any country. Hence, the purpose of this research study is to pilot and conduct an efficacy trial of project THRIVE and to propose a low-cost model to the government to provide basic skills of Daycare management to women, a conducive 1000 days program for newborns and a fast track literacy and life skills education program for adolescents girls in one union council of district Matiari.

data.projectName: Climate Change Impact Assessment on Health and Agriculture Sector and Development of Climate Outlook Model for Timely Dissemination of Early Warning in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The proposal will address the two most important sectors i.e. health and agriculture in Pakistan. These two are considered the most vulnerable sectors that are expected to be impacted by the climate change as mentioned by IPCC (2014). In health sector, we will investigate the causes of dengue outbreak, develop GIS based hotspot model and early warning system. Similarly, smog causes, peak and its transportation will be identified that would help to develop early warning mechanism. In agriculture sector, the climate change impacts on shifting of agro climatic zones, seasonal crop water demands would be investigated.  The climate change impacts on both sectors will be identified for adaptation to short- and long-term impacts during the 21st century and an early warning mechanism would be proposed and developed for timely dissemination of information to national stakeholders to better adapt and ultimately will help to mitigate/minimize its impacts.

data.projectName: Raising Rural Poultry as Organic Food under Rural Farming Community System for Food Security and Poverty Alleviation
data.projectDigest: Under the changing climatic scenario, supporting the vulnerable and poor rural households through improved chicken production is one of the viable options as it can improve family nutrition standards and help meet family and social obligations. Use of antibiotics and other performance enhancing drugs under weak law enforcement scenario also demands alternate choices. But more importantly, availability of animal’s protein source makes backyard poultry an attractive option for rural community. For this purpose, a plan is proposed to raise rural poultry as organic food under rural farming community system for food security and poverty alleviation. According to plan, 05 union councils (4-5 villages in each union council) will be selected in tehsil Toba Tek Singh to launch project activities by establishing Rural Poultry Production Centers with the help of Rural poultry farmer organization. This project will also act as employment generation as the local community will be engaged to run the project activities. The income generated from this project will be served as salaries for the local workers. The major benefit expected from the project is sustainability and self-sufficiency in egg and meat yield especially for rural community. More animal protein available to village masses will improve health and wellbeing of people and will help empower the least addressed segments of the society

data.projectName: INTEGRATED SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT PLAN FOR ENERGY RECOVERY IN PESHAWAR
data.projectDigest: Solid waste deserted by the communities and inappropriate transfer of solid waste by the industries, hospitals and hotels/ restaurants possess serious threats to the delicate environment of the Peshawar. The ecosystem is gradually degrading due to lack of awareness regarding proper solid waste management between local populace, and management agencies. Therefore, this project is proposed for the identification and quantification of solid waste generated in study area. Further, the impacts of solid waste on soil, air and water parameters will be assessed. Solid waste is a mixture of combustible and non combustible waste. This ratio will be identified in this project. The potential of energy contents will be known and communicated to policy makers for efficient utilization of solid waste in Peshawar. Soil, air and water quality will be assessed for the potential risks. The study recommends a comprehensive solid waste management plan which will focus on energy conversion in addition to reduce, reuse and recycle solid waste before it enters the waste stream.

data.projectName: Intelligence-Based Machine for Sorting Quality Wheat Seed for Cultivation
data.projectDigest: Wheat is one of the most usable seed for food purposes in Pakistan as it is categorized as high valued commodity product. Since the independence of Pakistan, our government has been paying to the foreign agencies for the wheat imported from them, and the price become higher every year in Pakistan. Besides, if see Pakistan is a cultivation land but the amount of wheat is every year decreases because of weak seeds cultivation as compare with Europe, India, Australia and America. The research aim to propose an automatic sorting intelligence-based machine solution, to classify among strong and weak wheat seeds, the strong seeds shall be classified based on weight consider a best seeds for cultivation . Our proposed solution for Pakistan wheat seeds grading a combination of image processing, deep learning and machine learning solution to automatically sort the strong seeds for cultivation into their respective grades.

data.projectName: Development of sero-specific FMD virus antisera
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) poses the serious threats to health and production of livestock. It is the one of the most significant transboundary endemic disease in Pakistan since 1954. The economic impact of FMD has been poorly characterized particularly in endemic settings where such knowledge is important for decision-making on disease control with limit resources. According to Food and agriculture organization (FAO) the approximate annual loss is $692 million due to70% prevalence of three serotypes (O, A and Asia-1) of FMD in Pakistan. FMD vaccine is commonly practiced in Pakistan by the farmers but it’s not very effective. Locally prepared vaccine doesn’t give complete protection to the animal. It has been observed in recent years the increase in the death rate and milk production of dairy animals due to FMD virus which shows the mutagenic change in FMD virus which is the serious threat to food security in rural and urban areas to the consumers and producers.Now it is a need of hour for the new molecular typing of all the serotypes of FMD in field and vaccinal isolates to observe the variants of the FMD virus and raising of antisera.

data.projectName: Wild Edible Fruits Diversity and their Products: Small to Medium Scale Food Marketing Enterprise and Data-basing in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The largest number of food-insecure human population live in South Asia, which has roughly 300 million undernourished people. In south Asian countries including Pakistan, the major challenges are food security, unemployment and poverty. Advancing food security requires improving access to food, food safety, nutritional adequacy, and sustainability, as well as increasing productivity. In Pakistan, there are hundreds of lesser-known indigenous wild edible fruits that can contribute to food security, elevation of poverty through small scale business and play vital roles in the nutrition of the people particularly the rural populace. Such species can enrich the diet of rural populace and could thrive without the use of costly agricultural inputs such as fertilizers, herbicides and pesticides. The proposed project is aimed to explore the diversity of the wild fruits, preparation and evaluation of their indigenous recipes-based products, nutraceutical evaluation, and their databasing using various georeferencing approaches for possible small-scale enterprises throughout the Pakistan.  The proposed project will be comprised of floristic survey, collection and identification of diversity of wild edible fruits; documentation and collection of indigenous recipe-based products and their nutraceutical evaluation; nutraceutical evaluation of selected wild fruits; databasing using georeferencing tools and fifth, product development using indigenous technology.

data.projectName: Addressing challenges of malnutrition across the 1,000 days of window of opportunity (pregnant and lactating mothers and children aged 6-23 months) using an integrated multisectorial approach for an improved and sustainable outcome
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: Maternal malnourishment, a leading cause of stunting in infants, is a major challenge in the developing world. Pakistan ranks second in malnutrition in Asia. Current research on malnutrition is mainly focused on adjusting calories and providing micronutrients. While such measures are unarguably critical, integrating components of social and behavioral change and targeting food insecurities simultaneously is likely to have a sustainable impact on malnutrition and stunting. We propose a multipronged approach integrating social behavioral change interventions (Maternal education on, nutritional value of ingredients, recipes, meal plans and demos for food preparation) with interventions focused on sustainability, (revolving livestock together with training on how to grow food and rear animals for food). Impact will be measured by periodic (6, 10, 14, 18 and 22 months) assessment of interventions using biological (changes in genome pre- and post-intervention), biochemical (levels of micronutrients pre- and post-interventions) and qualitative (surveys, questionnaires and interviews, assessments for improvement in stunting) measures. Results will be incorporated into models that will generate trends and provide biological signatures associated with changes in malnutrition and stunting, enabling informed. Models could be further integrated into Maternal, Neonatal and Child Health programs to tailor future interventions for effective improvement in malnutrition and stunting.

data.projectDigest: Desert of Thal in Punjab is the major contributor of country`s gram production. Chickpea is an important rabi legume of the country and major source of livelihood for farers of Thal. From the last few years, gram crop has been facing problems of severe weed infestation especially wild onion (Asphodelus tenuifolius Cav.), jeweled distaff thistle (Carthamus oxyacanthus M. Bieb.) and lambsquarters (Chenopodium album L.) and disease severity mainly gram blight (Ascochyta rabiei) and gram wilt (Fusarium oxysporum. So keeping in view the current scenario of gram decline in thal area of Punjab, a comprehensive study is proposed to develop package of integrated control of weeds (wild onion, jeweled distaff thistle and lambsquarters) and disease (gram blight and gram wilt) for gram growers of thal area. The integrated weed and disease control strategies will include combination of physical, chemical and cultural control of weeds and diseases. The laboratory and farmer field studies will be conducted for two consecutive years and dissemination of the research findings will made through local extension workers to the farmers. The sectoral collaborator of the proposed project will be responsible for providing help and guidance in selection of experimental sites and general look after of field experiments at research and adaptive farm as well as farmers’ field.

data.projectName: Development of AI based Comprehensive Solutions for Mining Industry
data.projectDigest: This project will focus on development of low cost data acquisition, resource modeling, planning and operations of the mines. Techniques and software will be developed for providing solution to Mining Industry in resource modeling, planning and operations of the mines. These techniques and software will be pitched for commercial means to the International Mining Industry.  Most of the Human Resource is available in the intelligent Information Processing Lab at NCAI UETP. Leading experts from International Industry will be linked with the Principal Investigator and Co-Principal Investigators to develop robust techniques and algorithms supervised and vetted from international teams in these areas. As part of this project a consortium will be developed between Intelligent Information Processing Lab, Part of National Centre of AI, UET Peshawar as lead institution, followed by partner Universities: Curtin University Australia, University of Exeter UK and Heceppte University Turkey.  Each area will have two post-doc positions (total 9), two PhD positions (total 10), two MSc positions (total 14) and a consultant geophysicist position. The post-doc positions will also be open to international community; Pakistani Nationals will be hired on all other positions. The PIs, Co-PIs, will work closely with their international counterparts to meet the goals of the project. Research Associates and Research Assistants already working in the project will bear no financial liability on this project since they are already working in these areas.  At the end of research project comprehensive software will be developed for resource modeling, mine planning and auxiliary operations of mines, special attention to details will be made to Pakistani environment; and international market.

data.projectName: Development of High Yield Metal Chelates as Nutrients for Medicinal Plants Cultivation using Greenhouse Hydroponic Systems
data.projectDigest: Medicinal plants or herbs have been known to be an important potential source of therapeutics or curative aids and their use has attained an imperious role in health system as well as for economy, globally. In present project, we will use greenhouse hydroponic system and laboratory growth temperature control systems for their production. The present project further deals with the synthesis of different metal chelates for studying its effects on the growth of medicinal plants under hydroponic system. Some of the selected medicinal plants are being grown under normal growing conditions within Pakistan while others in China, Indonesia and Malaysia etc. The seeds of the medicinal plants will be imported and their growth studies under hydroponic system and in the presence of synthesized metal chelates will be studied. Aim of the current investigation includes the effective growing hydroponic system for medicinal plants and the use of synthesized metal chelates as effective nutrients.

data.projectName: Edge Enhanced Video Stream Analytics in Clouds for Secure Cities
data.projectDigest: This project is focused on Intelligent Video Analytics which spans the areas of Artificial Intelligence and Cloud Computing. In recent years, video surveillance and analytics have been growing exponentially, being driven by a wide range of Urban Planning applications ranging from public security, traffic efficiency, infrastructure planning, emergency medical services, firefighting, and home security. Increasing populations in metropolitan cities result in crime, vandalism, accidents and are a major target for terrorism, these issues have become a growing impediment for the countries worldwide. To overcome these issues, many developing and developed countries have invested heavily in CCTV cameras. However, monitoring live streams of video data for detection of suspicious events by human operators is limiting, laborious and simply impractical. Intelligent video analysis techniques are required to harness useful information from such huge amount of data produced by surveillance cameras. Analyzing live video streams have great potential for extracting useful information and activity patterns, which are critical for law enforcement, civic and environmental authorities. Hence, objectives of proposed systems will be achieved with collaboration of stake holders and through interdisciplinary approaches by involving relevant experts from Pakistan and UK. The outcomes of this project will have broad scientific, social and economic impacts.

data.projectName: Massive Engagement with Low-income Populations for Maternal and Child Health and Nutrition
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: A large percentage of the Pakistani population is low-literate and low-income, where only 40% adult women are able to read and write. The combination of a lack of literacy and poverty has led to Pakistan having a maternal mortality ratio of 178 deaths per 100,000 live births and nearly nearly 10 million Pakistani children suffering from stunting. We will mass deploy ICT interventions that directly impact the knowledge within the poorest communities and engage with community members to encourage better maternal and child health practices. We aim to leverage the mass adoption of Watsapp to create and deploy maternal health and nutrition content over whatsapp to low-literate, low-income populations in an entertaining, engaging and interactive format using videos, audio stories, dramas and images.

data.projectName: CPEC and its effects on Pakistan's Socio-Economic culture, Environment and Tourism
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan is one of the countries facing a negative impact on the environmental deterioration in the coming years. Pakistan's dependence on fossil fuels as its energy sources, and industrial emissions from the developing countries in its neighborhood, threaten the country’s future. One of the studies proposed in this project is based on forecasting the increase in the carbon emission levels by 2030, once the country is transformed into an economic corridor and transportation and trade from China will increase on daily basis. As a remedial measure, another study will be targeted towards the viability assessment of electric vehicles, as an alternative to existing conventional vehicles, with the aid of Fuzzy SWOT, Fuzzy AHP, and Fuzzy Linear Programming. One of the studies will be targeted at life cycle assessment and the overall cost-benefit analysis of electric mobility with special consideration into its economic and social impacts. 
The prosed framework also focuses on Pakistan’s tourism industry under the banner of CPEC. Pakistan has vast tourism potential, both in terms of natural resorts and cultural/historical sites which has largely been unexplored due to the lack of infrastructure. Since CPEC will result in an improvement of the existing infrastructure, the tourism sector can be enhanced and turned into a revenue-generating sector. Fuzzy multiple criteria decision-making (MCDM) tools can be used to identify and rank the necessary and beneficial measures which should be taken to improve the overall situation. Fuzzy Quality function deployment tool can be used to improve the overall customer experience and satisfaction.

data.projectName: DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF PERFORMANCE-BASED TEACHER EVALUATION SYSTEM IN PAKISTAN
data.projectDigest:
Teacher evaluation is a formal and systematic process of identifying effective teachers as well as teacher shortcomings that may exist, and employing that information to serve teaching and its student learning outcomes. A plethora of research provides evidence that effective teacher is the most important individual that can make considerable contribution to student learning and achievement (Akram, 2019; Darling-Hammond, 2016). All policy documents and commission proceedings have focused on improving teacher performance as the overall impact of effective teachers is visible in the form of increased student performance, and classroom and teacher effectiveness. 
In Pakistan, there is a less focused mechanism of identifying effective teachers and it is a national challenge. The currently used Performance Evaluation Report is much generalized report and it is not aligned with the National Professional Standards for Teachers in Pakistan  and, thus, does not help identify effective teachers. Under the thematic Area “Innovative Governance and Reform” with sub theme as “Educational Governance and Reform”, this project will focus on developing and validating a Performance-Based Teacher Evaluation School System (P-BTESS) for secondary schools in Pakistan to meet this national challenge. 
The objectives of this project include to (a) identify system needs, (b) identify teachers’ roles and responsibilities, (c) develop/set performance standards with observable practices, (d) develop and validate multiple data sources of teacher evaluation), (e) pilot the project on small scale, and (f) conduct orientation sessions to  10% (approx. 13000)  master trainers in Punjab keeping in view education as provincial entity. The developed material will be disseminated throughout the country.

data.projectName: Integrating genetics, rhizosphere biology and precision agronomy; a futuristic approach to reduce nitrogen use in wheat and rice
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest:
Nitrogen (N) is an essential nutrient required in large amounts for plant growth and development. Different N-fertilizers are applied to meet N-demands of crops e.g., Urea which has 46% N contents but >50% of applied N is lost in environment due to volatilization or leaching and surface run-off. These losses are major cause of pollutions in soil and water bodies and contribute towards greenhouse gases and ultimately a threat to climate change and human population. Wheat and rice are the major staple crops of Pakistan grown on 8.7 and 2.8 mHa area with yield of 25 and 7.2 million tons, respectively (Economic Survey of Pakistan 2018-19). Both crops require high inputs of N fertilizer to obtain optimum yields but excessive fertilization practices are not sustainable due to high production costs and associated environmental damage. Furthermore, with the passage of time, many varieties developed in the genetic background of “green revolution” have become non-responsive to high N fertilizer. Due to the environmental and health concerns caused by N-pollution; a global consensus has emerged to minimize the use of N-fertilizer into the agriculture upto 25% within the next decade. Pakistan being one of the top 10 countries adversely hit by climate change needs to review its agriculture policy to get food security for rapidly growing population in an ecologically safe and environmentally sustainable manner and utilizing fewer resources. 
The aim of this project is to integrate already established, well-documented technologies for reducing the N-inputs into the agriculture ultimately reducing the N-losses, emissions and cost of production without yield and environment penalties. Instead of using high-N-responsive crops, genetic resources (wheat and rice germplasm) will be explored

data.projectName: Exploration of Xanthine Oxidase Inhibitors and antioxidants from Domestic Medicinal Plants Traditionally being used as Therapeutic Agents against Hyperuricemia
data.projectDigest: In the proposed research project, the Pakistan-native and easily available medicinal plants have been selected, based on the literature and folk usage of domestic practitioners. To approach the optimized conditions associated with the extraction and in-vivo conditions, computational techniques including response surface methodology and the neural network will be employed. The number of treatments, the combination of diverse variants and their replications will be determined at an optimum level using the response surface methodology technique.  The extracts with maximum research output will be subjected to further phytochemical/biochemical characterization. The bioactive compounds/constituents responsible for the associated pharmacological effects will be characterized using biochemical and physical investigations i.e. measuring total oxidant and antioxidant moieties, GC-MS and HPLC based analysis of bioactive compounds present in extracts, their purification and X-ray crystallography (available at the institution). Through clinical trials, in-vivohypouricemic potential of plant extracts will be evaluated by means of the hyperuricemia induced mice model. Following the in-vivo evaluations, the effect of plant extracts on mice health status and vital organs will be evaluated by means of baseline biochemical investigations and histopathological studies following animal sacrifice respectively. Along with clinical studies (in-vivo), the interaction between newly screened/regular compounds isolated from botanical sources in this experiment will be studied by Molecular Docking. In the next stage, the obtained results will be analyzed by the neural network systems using complicated mathematical relationships and simultaneously by response surface methodology techniques

data.projectName: Design for the urban water sustainability to address the Challenges of water, wastewater and climate change in three mega cities of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Rapidly increasing population, industrialization, climate change and poor governance lead toward the water resource depletion. Sustainable urban water management is urgently required to secure water related problems. Current study also focuses on sustainable water management challenges of a developing countries where underground water is reducing and deteriorating, irrigational withdrawal is increasing to alarming situation, no wastewater treatment facility is available. By executing this project, gaps in water and wastewater management of four major cities (Lahore, Faisalabad, Multan and Karachi) will be identified and suggestions will be made on integrated and sustainable water management. It will include the drinking water issues related to quality, health risks impact and treatment, rainwater harvesting in cities with efficient storage facilities, wastewater treatment through low-cost biological methods, reuse of treated wastewater for landscaping and revitalization of river Ravi and drain of Lahore. This topic is directly focus on priority thematic areas of water management and sustainability in Grand Challenge Fund. The project will enhance the socio-economic benefit at national level by addressing the hot environmental issues.

data.projectName: Automation of cancer risk prediction, diagnosis, treatment and outcome predication using AI using molecular imaging in hybrid PET/CT: Developing Regional AI radiology resource center for cancer management
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan, cancer imaging data is not equally interpreted due to difference in qualifications in a local district hospital up to private hospitals who hire international qualified physicians leading to disparity in management of patient. In current project, we focused on this national problem by using the application of artificial intelligence in management of the cancer patients using PET/CT imaging. Our aim is to develop a ubiquitous intelligent system for accurate tumor classification, grading, staging, characterization of tumor behavior, characterization of the tumor extent, expected time to recurrence, quantitation of the tumor load as well of the response to therapy for all types of PET/CT systems. A lot of work has already been done on the use of artificial intelligence in health sector however Pakistan stills lacks a national center for applications of AI in health sector. Therefore, we hope that current project shall be a milestone in this regard.

data.projectName: Targeted Delivery of Nano-antibiotics to combat resistant gram negative bacterial strains prevalent in Public Hospitals of Lahore, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a cross-cutting and an emerging challenge to the global health care – including Pakistan. Literature reports suggest that over the past decade, the antibiotic consumption in Pakistan increased almost 65%, besides dominant contribution of several antibacterial resistance causing factors. Nevertheless, a very few attempts have been made to combat this menace of antibiotic resistance in Pakistan. Thus, we aimed to conduct a study by utilizing nano-medicine approaches to battle this growing endanger, since nano-particles not only combat bacteria themselves but also act as carriers for antibiotics. In this regard, established antibiotic drugs, ciprofloxacin and cefixime will be made as liposomal and polymer loaded nano-antibiotics to be used, alone or in combination, against the prevalent gram negative resistant bacterial strains - Klebsiella, E.coli and P. aeruginosa, obtained from public hospitals of Lahore and later cultured for in vitro screening and susceptibility testing. Avant grade modalities will be used to characterize the liposomal and polymer loaded antibiotics (CPFX & CFM), such as FTIR, DLS, XRD, SEM and TEM. In vitro drug release kinetics will be examined using dialysis membrane technique and Franz diffusion cell approach. After characterization, liposomal and polymer loaded antibiotics will be tested, alone or in combination, to determine MIC, MBC and possible synergism against the resistant strains. Moreover, nano-antibiotics will be evaluated for their toxic potential against primary cells. Susceptibility of nano-antibiotics, alone or in combination, will be evaluated via disc diffusion method. After susceptibility testing, resistant gram negative bacterial strains will be sent for sequencing to identify the candidate genes

After characterization, liposomal and polymer loaded antibiotics will be tested, alone or in combination, to determine MIC, MBC and possible synergism against the resistant strains. Moreover, nano-antibiotics will be evaluated for their toxic potential against primary cells. Susceptibility of nano-antibiotics, alone or in combination, will be evaluated via disc diffusion method. After susceptibility testing, resistant gram negative bacterial strains will be sent for sequencing to identify the candidate genes

data.projectName: A multidisciplinary consortium to tackle emerging zoonotic viral pathogens in humans and animals
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
World health organization estimates a billion cases of illness and about a million deaths/year from different diseases that transfer from animals to humans.
Many new highly dangerous bugs lead to large numbers of deaths and huge economic losses, like the current world-wide lockdown after corona spread.
In this project, we will study in depth why and how these animal bugs (viruses) jump to humans and shut down their body defense systems that is responsible to fight these bugs. 
We aim to develop rapid laboratory methods to quickly detect this defense shut down in body when bugs attack. 
We plan to discover new drugs to boost body defense system against these bugs. We will also manufacture new local affordable drugs to kill those bugs efficiently as imported drugs are very expensive.
Lastly, we also plan to construct a highly advanced mobile laboratory that can be quickly driven to localities where dangerous bugs erupt and control them effectively using our products. 
Our team of specialist will produce low-cost products and commercialize them using social-technical-economic plan to ensure their success in general public. The benefit at national level includes: a reduced economic impact by decreased disease burden, a better human health will improve their life standards and less impact on the budget spent on treatment cost.

data.projectName: Optimum use of Existing Resources: A Prototype Model of Road Safety
data.projectDigest: Rampant urbanization, high population density, road crashes and traffic congestions have become serious issues in Pakistan. We lose 9 billion US$ and more than 25000 human lives every year due to road crashes. To address the urban planning challenges of road safety, traffic congestion, and deteriorated air quality, this mega project proposes four core objectives with multiple sub-objectives: (1) Designing of a prototype model of Smart Public Transport (SPT) and Smart Parking by employing and optimizing the existing resources and infrastructure; (2) Increasing the efficiency of Electronic Surveillance System with centralized command and control unit to monitor traffic, and to maximize the road safety; (3) Developing a sustainable mechanism to gauge on-road air pollution to reduce vehicles’ carbon emission; and, (4) To prepare strategies for human behavior modification for safe road usage practices through social research, and advocacy and lobbying to update legislation and transport policy. The research team has developed a comprehensive methodological plan to systematically identify and address the real and potential causes and patterns of road delinquency and inefficient planning. The project aims at improving urban planning in Pakistan by offering smart, long-term, optimum and reliable solutions for better living.

data.projectName: High Frequency Magnetic Nanodevices for absorber applications in 5G telecommunication technology
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Sharif University of Engineering & Technology, Multan, Punjab, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The project aims at strengthening the strategic field of ferrites in telecommunication technology that have been used to investigate different applications over a few decades. This field is experiencing a continuous expansion, due to the wide possible applications, which includes MIMO, millimeter wave, full duplexing TDD, antennas, resonators and absorbers. Absorbers play an important role for in data transfer applications between transmitter and receiver. Magnetic materials with versatile dielectric and magnetic properties may overcome the cross talk and EM losses. Saturation, anisotropy, low losses, mass and volumetric reduction of ferrites refer them as most preferable materials to attain these goals. By achieving the goals of project, we will be able to encounter the next generation necessities of microwave device-based technologies for 5G applications. In 5G systems, the system uses large number of antenna arrays which can both functions of receiver and transmitter. However, it is difficult to isolate the high-power transmitted signal from the adjacent received signal. The shielding alone cannot absorb all the leaked signal. Absorber material with desired properties will absorb and decrease the reflections from the other parts. The permeability, permittivity, dielectric constant, electromagnetic losses and Q factor of absorber material are most important parameters to control the absorbance. This project will focus on the manufacture, preparation, investigation and application of novel magnetic nanodevices having superior electromagnetic properties to the currently available conventional ferrite cores at high operational temperatures. These materials would be tested for the usage in absorber devices for telecommunication technology.

data.projectName: Translocation of Anti-microbial resistance in Environmental samples
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: The spread of antibacterial resistance (ABR) in human pathogens is a looming public health disaster for Pakistan. The combination of high burden of infectious disease, intensification of agriculture, poor sanitation, political instability, social inequality and largely uncontrolled, unsupervised antibiotic usage places this Low and Middle Income Country (LMIC) at undeniably high risk from ABR. A multi-scale interdisciplinary study will be undertaken to resolve the physical and social factors driving the development of antibacterial resistance (ABR) in Pakistan. The study will target agriculture, pollution, antibiotic usage and urbanization, drivers that are identified in the development phase to be most important. Uniquely study will sample not just the environment but also the microbiomes of individuals living in that environment. The resulting data will be used to parameterize predictive models of the spread of the ABR in health facilities and the environment. This will provide crucial information to policy makers and stakeholders allowing them to pursue policies that actually impact ABR with consequent benefits to the local community. Study will conduct a comprehensive multi-scale sampling plan to resolve the major reservoirs of resistance, mechanisms for transmission into humans and quantification of the levels of antibiotics across human and animal sectors in Pakistan.

data.projectName: HOLISTIC APPROACH TO AFFORDABLE LOW COST HOUSING IN PAKISTAN
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan is experiencing sustained rapid population growth, especially in the lower income sector of the population, creating an unpreceded demand for affordable housing. With increasing urbanization and migration, housing has to be a critical part of urban planning utilizing sustainable designs with the use of technologies that utilize indigenous materials. NED University of Engineering and Technology has taken the initiative of establishing a CENTER FOR AFFORDABLE HOUSING AND SUSTAINABLE BUILT ENVIRONMENT (CAHSBE). This project aims to develop a holistic approach for addressing the issue of affordable low cost housing in Pakistan. The broad objectives are to integrate the planning and sustainable design of affordable low cost housing using indigenous materials and develop connectivity with multidisciplinary partners from academia, industry, government and non-profit organizations for the housing sector. The proposed project will be in interdisciplinary with following focus areas:
•         Urban Planning 
•         Characterization of Indigenous Materials 
•         Sustainable Urban and Non-Urban Architectural Designs
•         Cost Effective Structural Design & Construction Technologies for Affordable Low cost housing
For the Project, the research team will take guidance from the Advisor, Mr. Zaigham Rizvi, Chairman PM Task Committee on Affordable Housing and will coordinate the efforts with the Naya Pakistan Housing Authority (NPHA) and Ministry of Housing.

data.projectName: Developing a Model of Inclusive Schooling System for Students with Special Needs
data.projectDigest: This study focuses on developing an indigenous model of Inclusive Schooling for students with special needs. The project comprises of three phases. Phase I will include screening of students with borderline Intellectual Disability, Specific Learning Disorder, Autism Spectrum Disorder and Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder enrolled in special schools of Lahore; screening of potential teachers for inclusive education and a survey of opinions from professionals working in mainstream as well as inclusive schools. Phase II will include development of Index for Inclusion, development of Teachers' Training Manual followed by training of teachers according to the manual. Survey will be done to identify the problems making the manual more feasible and applicable. In phase III, efficacy of inclusive education in managing the problems faced by students having disability will be studies. Studentswith physical age and corresponding mental age of 6-15 years will be selected. Two groups will be formulated i.e., Special Education System (control) and Inclusive Education System (experimental) with 50 students in each group. Education will be provide using developed Index and Manuals. Rigorous Post assessment will be done to evaluate the progress. After completing the project in Lahore, the model will be replicated in Southern and Northern Punjab.

data.projectName: Cost Effective ON-SITE Wastewater Management  & Treatment for Textile Industry
data.projectDigest:
The textile sector is a vital and leading industrial sector of Pakistan. Environmental effects of textile business are of great significance as it consumes huge quantity of water from the dyeing, bleaching, washing, and printing of finished textile products, and release highly polluted wastewater. Effluents from textile industry are usually characterized by high levels of dyestuff, chemicals, Total Suspended Solids (TDS), Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD), Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD), and color (1-2).
Although physico-chemical treatment processes of wastewater treatment have been recognized and employed by textile industries worldwide, these methods are not cost-effective, and also involve huge volumes of sludge disposal. Buildup of such concentrated sludge poses practical difficulties in the disposal of wastewater. AOP's Processes using Ozone, Hydrogen peroxide, Fenton’s reagent, etc. have been found very effective for both recycling and treatment wastewater originating from Textile industries. AOP’s form hydroxyl radicals during oxidation which are highly powerful oxidizing species with an oxidation potential of E_ = 2.8 V (3-5). 
Ozone treatment within machine is an alternative approach compared to Conventional wastewater Treatments, which are extremely expensive. If Ozone gas is successfully applied within the machine, we can eliminate the need of separate (conventional) wastewater treatment.     
Advantages and Savings 
1.	Faster Processing Time
2.	Shorter Retention Time
3.	Simple Equipment and easy operation & Automation
4.	Able to Process Various Types of Liquid waste
5.	No need of Chemical Additions 
6.	No Odor
7.	Smaller Footprint
8.	Low Sludge Production with Better Settlability

data.projectName: Composite mitigation framework for climate change impacts on the electrical grid with Micro-Grids Centric Virtual Power Plant infrastructure planning in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: In this research proposal, a two-stage composite mitigation framework is presented for climate change impacts on the electrical grid in terms of load patterns have evaluated and Micro-Grids Centric Virtual Power Plant infrastructure planning as a solution. In the first stage, a composite assessment of the climate change impact on the predominant contingents of power sectors are presented in terms of quantification. The identified areas include the policy side, climate models, and transmission and distribution network, thermal dominance in the overall generation, renewable energy generation penetration, demand patterns, and load factor issues, grid codes, and planning horizons. In the second stage (consisting of three sub-stages), micro-grids are formulated considering energy options, potential sites, and population in each province in sub-stage one. In sub-stage two, these microgrids will be integrated via tie-lines. In sub-stage three, these microgrids are incorporated into each virtual power plant in each province and strategically integrated into other virtual power plants across the country.  In all these stages, the climate impact assessment will be incorporated in the future requirements and feasible solutions will be presented in accordance with the nation's futuristic needs.

data.projectName: Corrosion of reinforcement in different modified concretes
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: The infrastructure development projects near the coastal areas of Pakistan as proposed in China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) can experience corrosion of steel in reinforced concrete (RC) structures, which not only reduces the service life of these RC structures by reducing the structural performance but also experience the cracking within the concrete. This research proposal outlines an innovative experimental program that will focus on the development of a model of the active propagation phase of reinforcing steel corrosion that includes the combined effects of galvanic corrosion currents and steel-concrete interface condition. Moreover, electro-chemical experiments and non-destructive techniques will be combined with a mechanical module that will allow for the prediction of the time to concrete cracking resulting from the pressure due to the rust expansion.  The purpose of this proposal is to provide a technology able to detect active steel corrosion early enough when no damage is visible on the structure.

data.projectName: AN EFFECTIVE APPROACH FOR THE REMOVAL OF WATER CONTAMINANTS: DEVELOPMENT OF SILVER-DOPED AND IRON-DOPED MAGNETIC NANOHYBRID SYSTEMS FOR THE ELIMINATION OF HARMFUL BIOLOGICAL AND CHEMICAL AGENTS FROM WATER.
data.projectDigest: Water is an important molecule for sustaining life on earth. Water is stored in different reservoirs throughout the world and afterwards it is supplied to different locations and finally supplied as tap water. Water quality is one of the major concerns when used for drinking purpose. Safe drinking water should not possess risks to human health. Contaminated drinking water is a common problem and instead of being a savior of life, this natural resource has become a health burden. There are several human related activities that are responsible for the contamination of water. Disease causing microorganisms and harmful chemicals are largely responsible for water contamination which are mostly present in hospital and industrial effluents. Previously, to overcome this health burden, several different precautionary measures and treatments have been adapted but long-term benefit have not been achieved. Proposed study aims to use an innovative approach of nanotechnology in which the fundamental antimicrobial property of inorganic silver and magnetic feature of iron oxide will be explored to improve the quality of water. Silver and iron nanoparticles will be used to develop two different functional hybrid systems which would be competent to exterminate the microorganism and quench heavy metal ions from water reservoirs.

data.projectName: Designing the green quantum carbon nanodots for waste water treatment
data.projectDigest: Detection and disposal of toxic components from Industrial waste has gained considerable attention in Pakistan. Toxic chemicals of industrial discharge such as heavy metals and organic dyes, is an important cause of water pollution that make the water bodies nearby the industrial areas unusable by living organisms. The proposed research will includes the synthesis of functionalized carbon dots from eco-friendly biological waste and improving its degradation performance by tuning their structure. Efficiency of the prepared composites will be checked to degrade the harmful organic dyes of industrial wastes. Furthermore, functionalized carbon dots will be used as sensors of heavy toxic metals of industrial discharge. Use of environmental friendly functionalized carbon dots derived from biological materials would make the process cost effective and would expected to be as effective step towards waste water treatment.

data.projectName: Remote Health Intelligent Intervention System (RHIIS)
data.projectDigest:
Our goal is to develop a Remote Health Monitoring for Intelligent Intervention System (RHMIIS). The system will enhance the quality of healthcare by incorporating the Artificial Intelligence and Machine learning techniques. The patient’s data (from IoT sensors, lab tests and backlog etc.) will be processed at the cloud. The cloud will implement a set of machine learning algorithms that will process the patient data and automatically generate health related diagnosis and recommendations. The suggested diagnosis and recommendations will be communicated back to the respective physicians. 

The main outcomes of the project are,
•	To design and build custom IoT modules for remote sensing
•	To design and implement Artificial and Machine Learning algorithms for different disease diagnosis (cancer, cardic diseases and diabeties etc.)
•	To design and implement telemetry and telemedicine that will connect BHUs with physicians
•	To build state-of-the-art Research and Development facility in UET Peshawar and NUTECH Islamabad to conduct research in the field of AI enabled healthcare.

data.projectName: Development of Novel Environmental Friendly Bio-composites with high thermal stability and mechanical properties for packaging and automobile applications
data.projectDigest: Natural fibers will be reinforced in biopolymers to fabricate natural fiber reinforced composites (NFRC) in this project. These composites are potential replacement of synthetic plastic and composites due to their environmental friendly characteristics. A drawback of NFRC is low thermal stability and flammability. These properties are generally enhanced by adding fire retardant fillers of micro or nano sizes. Increasing fire retardant  properties and thermal stability through particulate fillers causes to decrease the mechanical properties of these materials due to stress concentration and non-compatibility between particles and matrix. This project is aimed to enhance thermal stability and fire retardant properties of NFRC without affecting the mechanical properties. For this purpose, compatible fire retardant fillers will be encapsulated into the composites. Also, the effect of particle size variation and distribution will be evaluated on the mechanical, thermal and fire retardant properties of NFRC. Further, it is aimed to add micro-sized seeds to the composites during fabrication. The seeds will be responsible to grow plants from the soil after the material is dumped. This will hugely reduce landfills and contribute to develop green environment. Development of biodegradable materials is currently under focus of researchers and industry, but development of re-growable bio-materials is novelty of this proposal.

data.projectName: Interaction between Urban Pollution Island and Urban Heat Island for Coastal Region of Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
