data.projectName: Digital and precision technologies for improving land and water productivity in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan is facing challenges of food security for feeding its 207million population, which is increasing at the rate of about 2.4 percent. Owing to degradation and depletion of limited agricultural resources such as arable land and fresh water, adverse climate change effects, pre and post-harvest losses and crop stagnant yields, agricultural crop sector have experienced negative growth of 4.4 percent during fiscal year. Similarly, high cost of crop production and losses do not allow country’s farmers especially small and medium farmers to be competitive in export markets. On the other hand, country is spending more than $7.00 billion rupees on food imports. Therefore, agriculture remains most important sector and it must be revolutionized for sustainable livelihood and employment.
Current advancement in the field of geo-spatial and sensor technologies, it has become possible to monitor the crop yield on every part of the field to prepare their maps using nutrient, organic matter, NPK, and moisture detection wireless sensors. Use of remote sensing technologies and unmanned aerial vehicles has shown potential and being extensively used in managing agricultural inputs globally. The GIS data layers of other soil and topographic attributes can be prepared to establish cause-effect relationships between varying crop yield patterns across the field and the underlying potential of the soil and landscape attributes. This spatial analysis can help in delineating the management zones, which can be treated separately and allow precise application of inputs.

data.projectName: Indigenous development of FRP Composite Systems for Strengthening / Retrofitting of Civil Infrastructure
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Proposed aims to develop Pakistan’s first commercial grade technical textile based FRP composite system for strengthening of civil infrastructure offering an economically viable solution for repair and strengthening and/or retrofitting of concrete/reinforced concrete structures. Project will be executed in three phases equally shared between partners from Textile, Polymer and Civil Engineering Departments of host and partnering National and International institutions. Role of the Textile departments during project is to develop fabrics from high performance fibers with various textures and fiber volume ratios to find out the best optimized fabric.  Whereas Polymer Department is solely responsible for synthesizing special structural adhesives that gives strong bonding of different substrates on concrete, specifically high bonding strength between developed fabric and concrete will be targeted. Performance of developed composite under different loading conditions will be assessed by applying them on reinforced concrete structural members subjected to different types of loading. Guidelines / Regulations for the use of developed FRP Composite structural strengthening will be developed under the guidance of International academic collaborators, national academic and sectoral collaborators. Successful development and implementation of such product will help in advancement of the local textile industry and contribute in economic growth by increasing export bills of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Establishment of Sustainable Development Goals Lab (SDGL): Identification of Challenges and Opportunities to Achieve Gender-specific Targets in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The proposed project “Establishment of Sustainable Development Goals Lab (SDGL): Identification of Challenges and Opportunities to Achieve Gender-specific Targets in Pakistan,” aims to address gender-specific national challenges. SDGL will produce scientific knowledge on the thematic areas and indicators outlined in the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) to improve gender equality and women’s empowerment across the country. SGDs (1-4) set various targets of gender equality and no. 5 specifically invites attention of the states to ensure gender equality and women’s empowerment in their societies. The activities to be undertaken, to achieve the project goals, will include the establishment of branches of SDGL across four public and private sector universities through their Departments/Centers of Gender Studies. Each branch will adopt an area of specialty: Culture, Religion, Economy, and Politics, which will rotate with other branches on semester basis. Therefore, strengthening of gender-specific academic institutions; production of gender experts; exchange of gender-knowledge across provinces; introduction of gender analysis of barriers and opportunities; and promotion of evidence based gender-specific decision-making are sub-objectives of the proposed proposal which can help Pakistan attain international gender standards, especially the SDGs.

data.projectName: Mycosynthesis of Zn nanoparticles for the priming of Chickpea seeds to control Fusarium wilt
data.projectDigest: Chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.) is a major cash and food crop in the world. Pakistan is the second largest producer of chickpea but its average yield is significantly lower than other major chickpea growing countries like India, Australia, Turkey, Iran, Australia, Ethiopia, Canada, USA, Mexico and Iraq (FAOSTAT 2015). In Pakistan, Ascochyta blight and Fusarium wilt are the major yield affecting factors. Fusarium wilt is caused by Fusarium oxysporum which is a seed borne and soil borne pathogen and its eradication is very difficult. This disease causes 10–90% yield losses, annually in Pakistan. In this project, we want to use nanotechnology to apply beneficial fungi (Trichoderma and Penicillium species), as bio-control agents. We will attach anti-microbial agent (metabolites) of these fungi on nano-particles and apply them on chickpea seeds (priming). Due to very small size, these treated nano-particles will disrupt microbial cells and potentially reduce disease infestation. These nanoparticles are not harmful to plants and easily persist in the soil. Final product (treated nano-particles) will be applied to the farmer, in powder form sachets. End user can easily dissolve them in water and apply on seeds. This project can help us to provide a convenient way of disease control.

data.projectName: Genomic-assisted breeding for improving resilience in cotton—a step towards enhancing cotton production beyond 2020
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: Sustainable cotton production is hampered by biotic and abiotic stresses, and the changing climate. Among these, cotton leaf curl disease together with high heat and pink bollworm infestation are the most detrimental—suppressing 4-6 million bales annually. Introducing new genes/alleles in well-adapted cotton varieties may help in reviving cotton production in Pakistan. We identified high heat tolerant sources and were sequenced, and identified putative genomic regions conferring heat tolerance. Secondly, we have indigenously developed cry2Ab gene (NIBGE-1601 event)—demonstrated resistance to pink bollworm. In this project, multi-pronged strategy has been proposed for improving the well-adapted national cotton varieties including IUB-13, IR-NIBGE-3701, FH-142 and IR-901. NIBGE-partners will involve in introgressing high heat tolerance as well as cry2Ab gene, and will provide genomic testing services to other partners. Crossing of the NIBGE-developed cotton varieties will remain the responsibility of NIBGE-PI. While IUB-13 and FH-142 would remain the responsibility of BZU-PI. Chinese collaborator will provide access to sequence information as well as bioinformatics services. Collaborator from BZU, Multan will be involved in undertaking physiological studies (for heat tolerance). Evyol (seed company partner) partner will conduct field trials for selecting the best resilient high yielding advanced cotton lines followed by submitting their seed in national trials (NCVT).

data.projectName: To Evaluate the Role of mobile phone based Smart IVR messaging for Improving Vaccine Coverage among Children in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Pakistan ranks 3rd in child mortality worldwide, with over 60% of all deaths due to infectious diseases; many of which are vaccine-preventable. The immunization coverage in Pakistan is well below the desired level of 95% coverage. Further there is a huge difference in vaccination coverage among different provinces. In addition, Pakistan is among three polio epidemic country and requiring proof of polio vaccination for international travel. Major reasons for delayed immunization in our country are lack of knowledge, forgetfulness of the vaccination due date, fear of adverse effects, and religious belief. A mixed methods study was conducted by our group looking at the role of barrier based, personalized automated SMS and voice messages to improve vaccination coverage and found that the IVR arm showed a 26% increase in immunization coverage. Although study indicated improvement in vaccination coverage in one of the study arm, a scale up model in a real world scenario is needed. In this study we would like to evaluate whether Artificial Intelligence (AI) based personalized mobile phone automated calls can improve on-time vaccine uptake at birth, 6, 10, 14 weeks and 9 months of age for RI as compared with standard care.

data.projectName: Improving Fertilizer Use Efficiency Through Site Specific Recommendation in Various Ecological Zones of Punjab for Sustainable Agriculture Production
data.projectDigest: In present scenarios of ravaging climate change, there is a need for the scientist to work closely with the farmers in order to improve crops and cropping system. The global agriculture is currently facing most urgent problems and the situation getting worse with every passing year. There is dire need for changing approach not only from scientists but also from farmers in the wake of severe climate change with drought, erratic rainfalls, soil erosions and heat. There is also need for the farmers, scientists and government bodies to work closely to keep the crop production at pace with growing world population. Very recently (2019) Agriculture Department of Punjab releases a new list of climatic zones of Punjab owning to the changing climatic condition and cropping pattern. The new zones require cost effective technologies aimed at increasing productivity and profitability per unit land without damaging the environment. Climate change also requires urgent policies for sowing time validation in order to cope its effects on crop production, as it greatly effects crop phenology. The role of fertilizers in improving agricultural productivity and profitability cannot be underestimated but their applied efficiency is a big question. The agriculture sector is thus facing challenges of optimizing fertilizer use-efficiency, diversifying cropping patterns, improving quality and reducing cost of production. Agriculture Department of Pakistan has been recommended fertilizer application, which is very general, old and outdated but due to ever increasing cost of fertilizers and new climatic zones, the general recommendations are not paying in relation to the investment made. The nutrients are to be applied in the amount and proportion in which these are needed by specific crop .

data.projectName: A space-based observation of climate and earth with CubeSat mission
data.projectDigest: This project shall use a space-based approach to solve the climate  and environmental challenge in Pakistan and worldwide. The air pollution is causing significant problem in major cities of Pakistan due to natural and anthropogenic emissions which is also one of the main causes of air smog.  The project shall take the advantage of small satellites to  map the signatures of air pollution sources in cities  by observing from space. Once the major sources of this problem are known, it is easier to find the remedies. The proposed mission shall design and launch low earth orbit satellite to measure the emissions at selected spectral bands. The hyper spectral cameras shall be on-board the designed small satellites to sense the air pollution signatures.

data.projectName: Remediation of Ambient and Indoor Air Pollution by using Metro-scale Pollution Reduction Technologies and Predicting Air Quality through Artificial Intelligence
data.projectDigest:
According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), air pollution has emerged as the single biggest global environmental health risk. Millions of people globally die due to ambient (outdoor) and indoor air pollution. The air quality in Pakistan is deteriorating by the hour. This problem, being large, multidimensional in nature, and very severe in urban settings, requires an urgent solution.
The overall aim of this innovative proposed project is to continuously monitor and remediate air pollution comprising of particulate matter and gaseous pollutants. Monitoring of various air pollutants will take place by installing high-tech air quality monitoring stations. Sampling of various air pollutants to determine their composition and source apportionment will also take place at these stations. Reduction in ambient air pollution will be achieved by development and installation of state-of-the-art outdoor ‘Air Purification Towers’ (APTs) with international collaboration. This will ensure application of a pollution reduction technology at the metro-scale. Furthermore, to control indoor air pollution, the research will lead to installation of ‘Air Suction Purifiers’ (ASPs) which consist of air filters to improve indoor air quality. Additionally, the continuous sampling and monitoring of the ambient air pollutants will allow the prediction of air quality by using Artificial Intelligence (AI).

data.projectName: Study of nano superstructures and high resolution characterization of broad-spectrum materials for numerous applications
data.projectDigest: Nanotechnology and nanomaterials are important in the present world as it changes almost every filed of life. For instance, electronic devices made of nanomaterials are more power/performance efficient than the traditional machines. Moreover, metallic nanoparticles can produce electricity and can stores energy with visible light, no energetic radiations are needed. Besides electronic applications, nanomaterials are very much helpful for the environment (environmental catalysis, waste water treatment), renewable energy (lithium ion battery electrodes), textiles (technical & medical textiles), biomedical (cancer therapy, drug delivery, MRI contrast agent), health care (UV protection, antibacterial, sunscreen), food agriculture (food packaging, food quality analysis sensors) and many more. Nanotechnology is transforming the world and fulfilling all the modern age requirements.

data.projectName: Insight Views of Energy Crops in the Unexplored Northern Part of Baluchistan, Pakistan for Liquid Biofuel Production
data.projectDigest: Well, we all know about petroleum fuel but we still know little about the biofuel. Hence, I thought it would be interesting to discuss something new in GCF project. So what, energy, and in particularly the source of energy oil plays an important role in the global economy. Changes in the energy status have significant effects on economic growth. Increasing oil prices, rising energy demands and concerns over global warming have encouraged many countries to develop biofuels. In order to support the emergence of biofuel sector, many countries have introduced incentives, such as production subsidies, consumption targets, tax breaks and reduced border tariffs. This has stimulated the growth of biofuel production and trade globally since last years. Among others, Pakistan is seeking to take advantage of this emerging market for biofuels industry. The country has extensive opportunities to develop biofuel. In order to capitalize on this potential and reduce Pakistan’s oil import bill, Government adopted AEDB in 2003, with the objectives to increase the renewables energy use 5% of the national energy consumption by 2030. However, the major constraint to commercial scale of biofuel production for running market is the cost factor, which must be addressed for compatibility and reliability.

Increasing oil prices, rising energy demands and concerns over global warming have encouraged many countries to develop biofuels. In order to support the emergence of biofuel sector, many countries have introduced incentives, such as production subsidies, consumption targets, tax breaks and reduced border tariffs. This has stimulated the growth of biofuel production and trade globally since last years. Among others, Pakistan is seeking to take advantage of this emerging market for biofuels industry. The country has extensive opportunities to develop biofuel. In order to capitalize on this potential and reduce Pakistan’s oil import bill, Government adopted AEDB in 2003, with the objectives to increase the renewables energy use 5% of the national energy consumption by 2030. However, the major constraint to commercial scale of biofuel production for running market is the cost factor, which must be addressed for compatibility and reliability.

data.projectName: Production of second generation cellulosic ethanol as renewable bio-fuel through engagement of indigenous microbial metagenomes
data.projectDigest: The government of Pakistan annually spent an amount of $9.61 billion (1/4 of its total import bill) on oil import to meet national energy requirements (Economic survey of Pakistan, 2018-19). Plant cellulosic biomass, known to be the largest renewable energy resource on earth (Mutreja et al., 2011), is recalcitrant to degradation due to the complexity of the biomass, improper pretreatment, enzymatic hydrolysis, fermentation and fuel separation. Unfortunately, Pakistan lacks technical capacity to produce non-food competitive 2nd generation biofuel from already available 139 million tons/year of processing & harvesting residue crop biomass. The local industry requires enzymes with improved catalytic performance to process-specific parameters. The successful conversion of agricultural waste into biofuel requires reducing the interaction between lignin and the polysaccharide components of the cell wall through a process termed as pre-treatment (Wyman et al., 2005). The pre-treatment alters/disorganize the crystalline structures of lignocellulosic microfibrills to ensure fiber materials exposed to the action of enzymes for enzymatic hydrolysis (Galbe and Zacchi, 2002). In this proposed project, efficient and novel bio catalytic agents for lignocellulosic biomass degradation like Beta-glucosidases enzymes will be hunted, identified, isolated, characterized and immobilized employing metagenomics, functional screening (hydrolytic activity on different substrates), DNA sequencing and immobilization for simultaneous saccharification & fermentation (SSF), respectively. More importantly, this search shall enroll indigenous microbial consortium who has evolved to withstand local high temperature in order to provide a cost effective and novel bio-catalytic agent..

data.projectName: Harnessing Urban Geospatial Big Data for Personalization of Real Estate
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Considered to be one of the main enablers of economic growth, the construction and real estate industry accounts for 10 to 12 percent of the world’s GDP and 7 percent of global employment. The local (Pakistan) real estate industry is worth around $ 700 billion. Although the industry is progressing, transparency and efficiency in the real estate sector (including low-cost housing and creation of second tier cities and towns for effective urban planning) are key challenges due to the absence of digital and intelligent systems with predictive and personalization capabilities that will reshape the real estate industry in future. The proposed project aims to solve data challenges in the urban big data (for example, people – social networks, place, infrastructure & wealth) in real estate industry while harnessing urban big data. This will help address questions such as how this data from multiple sources can be used to improve real estate investment decisions for different communities at large. The project consists of a consortium between Pakistan, Ireland and UK Universities. Ministry of Housing and Works, Graana and Aarz.pk are industrial collaborators. Overall, the proposed research will fit into the larger framework for Naya Pakistan Housing, thus addressing Sustainable Development Goals 8 and 11.

data.projectName: Urban Flood Management through Water Smart City Approach: The Case of Lahore Metroplitan, Punjab-Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
The project deals with sustainable water management practices in urban areas. The water related issues are dichotomous in nature. On one hand they surfaced up in the form of acute water shortage and on the other hand they turn up into flooding havoc. Our contemporary urban centers are also facing this dichotomous water management issue. The project at work--while taking Lahore as case study, highlights the urban flooding as well as depletion of underground water resources. In this double sword issue at work, water smart city approach can be a very viable option to mange our water resources.
The proposed research is going to help out numerous municipal institutions such as WASA Lahore, LDA, Public Health Engineering and PDMA in short. Similarly, adopting water smart city approach will definitely improve our adaptability towards climate change, better achieving Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and lesser burden on the government exchequer in response efforts.

data.projectName: Artificial Intelligence Framework (AIF)  for Effective handling of IT sector software projects of Pakistan
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Nowadays Information Technology (IT) market is growing very fast. Different countries develop guidelines and policies to take maximum advantage of IT, as it has the potential to revolutionize the growth. The software development industry is one of the most vital and compelling fields of IT. Software project development is no doubt a part of outsourcing and is still one of the major revenue generation sources for most of the Pakistan’s software companies. Software projects have a positive impact on software exports. Software exports not only have a positive effect on the economy of the country, but also creates new jobs. In Asian countries, software project exports are growing every year, which is reflected by their contribution towards software project exports all over the world. Geographically, Pakistan is situated in a very important place in the region. It shares its borders with China, India, Afghanistan, and Iran. Among them, China and India are the leading software exporter countries in the world. Although, software exports of Pakistan are increasing every year but they are still far behind compared to her neighboring countries like India and China. For instance, in the fiscal year 2018-2019, software exports of Pakistan were $5 billion, whereas, during the same time, software exports of India and China were $137 billion and $38 billion, respectively 2018-2019. China and Pakistan have developed strong joint trade and economic ties over the last few years. The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) is more expected to strengthen trade and economic cooperation. Besides, contributing in trade and industrial development activities in Pakistan, an early focus on the software aspect of CPEC project would also help in the information technology revolution in Pakistan.

data.projectDigest: Agro-industrial food waste represent the huge problem owing to its volume, impact on climate and perishability. The dilemma has triggers the researchers and scientist for discovering some innovative processes and technologies not only for its management but also for the isolation/extraction of ingredients that provide benefits for human health. Among the different Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), ensuring food security through reducing the food wastes and losses at the end of 2030 is among the priority list because the 12.5% of the global population is estimated to be suffering from chronic hunger. According to the recent National Nutrition Survey (NNS), 60% of households in Pakistan are food insecure. data.projectName: Human, animal and environmental contributors to antibiotic resistance in infants in low resource settings: epidemiological and one health approaches
data.projectDigest:
The aim of One Health Approach is to get the best and optimum animal’s health, environment and humans [1]. The Antibiotic resistance [ABR] is a big challenge for Public Health as it is emerging rapidly and the antibiotic resistance genes and bacteria are being disseminated in humans, animals and the environment on a global scale [2]. Environmental domains of all countries have now been allocated the task to implement National action plans on antimicrobial resistance, so Pakistan has also initiated its NAP [3]. In many countries the gap in this evidence can limit the assessment of progression towards achieving the goals of NAPs [4].
ABR is an important issue that is emerging in the developed countries now a days affecting lives of people including infants, adults and young people. Many studies have shown results on ABR in animals, and humans in Pakistan. This study will be the first work to identify the transmission of ABR from animals to humans through milk and then from mothers to their infants. This study will identify the ABR trend in animals and humans and its impact on the child health. Here we will identify the routes for vertical and horizontal transmission of the ABR residues and genes.

data.projectName: Revealing the Potential of Biomass Energy in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National College of Business Administration & Economics, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is experiencing a severe energy crisis these days, which is resulting in adverse long-term economic and social problems. The electricity and gas shortages have directly influenced the common man, industry and commercial activities. The high cost of energy mix is the main underlying reason behind the power crisis. The main fuel for the local power industry is natural gas, however, due to the continued depletion of this source and demands elsewhere thepower generation companies are now dependent on furnace oil, which is relatively expensive. The way out of this crisis is to look for fuel sources, which are cheap and abundantly available within the country. This description and requirement are fulfilled by biomass resources, which have been largely ignored in the past and are available in sufficient quantities to tackle the energy crisis prevailing in the country. The potential to produce power from biomass is very promising in Pakistan. Being an agrarian economy, more than 60 per cent of the population is involved in agricultural activities in the country (SBP,18). As per World Bank statistics, around 26.28 million hectares of land is under cultivation in Pakistan. The major sources of mass energy are crop residues, animal manure, and municipal solid wastes (MSW) etc

data.projectName: Rural Housing Experiment
data.projectDigest: Rural Housing, as a challenge to address housing issue has never been addressed in Pakistan by the policy makers and planners. And it is the first time that under the Naya Pakistan Housing Program, the rural housing challenge is being addressed. Housing Task Force formulated by Prime Minister of Pakistan has taken the services of Academia wherein multiple universities are included. University of Engineering and Technology (UET), Lahore held a conference on challenges and opportunities in this regard to kick start the working on this mission. The province of Punjab, comprising 67% of the country’s land has around 255,000 villages. In the first phase of the program, we aim at developing model villages of 50-100 housing units, equipped with all social amenities etc. PHATA (Punjab Housing and Town Planning Agency) under the Naya Pakistan Housing Program, has developed an understanding with University of Management and Technology (UMT), Lahore with respect to rural housing development. Therefore, UMT has been collaborated with UET, to prepare 5 design models of village houses for their planning and development on larger scale. Proactively, both institutions have completed their initial planning, mental mapping and documentation for the project and now in need of the engine of finances for further development.

data.projectName: Changing urban-development & housing patterns and its relation with vitamin-D deficiency induced human health and wellbeing issues in Pakistan: identification of trends, causes and possible solutions.
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
The world is urbanizing rapidly and the cities are growing fast, leading to stress on land for housing. The land is not only becoming expensive but also not available much. As a result denser neighbourhoods and housing blocks are becoming norm, leaving little space for better air circulation, exposure to sunlight and other health related essentials.
The changing urban development and housing patterns have impacted the lifestyle of the; children, elderly and the women are mostly limited to their houses due to high rise accommodation and lesser open spaces. 
In addition, temperatures in the cities of Pakistan are increasing every year, recurring heat waves have made majority to rely on the air conditioners and private vehicles resulting in lesser exposure to natural outdoors.
In this background, vitamin-D deficiency induced non-communicable diseases such as rickets, bones erosion and other issues have become common. Challenging health and wellbeing of the future generation.
There is a certain lack of interdisciplinary collaboration on the issues of urban morphology, housing design and health impacts. 
The project will lead to better urban planning, design and architectural solutions for housing with the objective to improve health and well-being of the inhabitants of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Isolation of Plastic Degrading Bacteria from Different Landfill Sites in Karachi, Pakistan.
data.projectDigest: Plastic accumulation poses a serious threat to our environment and ecology. It is a naturally recalcitrant polymer which remains in the environment for many years. Many strategies have been implicated to decrease plastic waste and its accumulation, among which there are microbiological techniques as well which uses microorganisms for biodegradation. This study aims to work at the biological degradation of Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and Low Density Polyethylene (LDPE) by bacteria isolated from soil sample. Soil samples will be collected from ten different landfill sites in Karachi. From these samples, bacterial isolates will be obtained by using enrichment culture method by culturing the soil samples in Minimal Salts Medium (MSM) where PET and LDPE are provided as carbon sources. Bacteria capable of growing in presence of LDPE and PET will be selected for degradation tests. Degradation tests will be performed using PET and LDPE films and the results will be confirmed by weight loss and tensile strength analysis, and also by Scanning Electron Microscopy. The most active isolates in degradation will be identified by using biochemical and molecular characterization that is PCR.  Further, enzymatic assay will be performed to identify the enzyme responsible for biodegradation.

data.projectName: An innovative, large-scale, low-cost omics-based sustainable strategy for addressing heavy metal contamination and antimicrobial resistance in wastewater – A case study on Hudiara drain
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: Clean water availability is an Achilles heel for Pakistan. The limited clean water resources in the country are continuously being contaminated by mixing with wastewater effluents. The contaminants mainly include heavy metals and disease-causing pathogenic microbes. Hudiara is the biggest waste water cannel in the country that originates from India and crosses Lahore before emptying into River Ravi. This Hudiara wastewater contamination to clean drinking water is resulting the country health, agricultural, and economic loss as well as environmental issues. The project is divided into 3 Phases: Firstly, we aimed to profile the heavy metals, antimicrobial resistant microbes, and the associated disease along the Hudiara drain and associated ground water. Secondly, metaomics based strategies will be employed to characterize the microbes; and their structural and functional components associated to heavy metal bioremediation and antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Finally, the project aims to develop a microbial resistome which will help to cater the spread of AMR and to develop a microbial based wastewater management.

data.projectName: Point of Use Technology for Water and Wastewater Management: Application from domestic to public level
data.projectDigest: In recent years, the major problem for environment today is waste disposal issues and clean water scarcity. Water pollutant involves inorganic pollutant, suspended particulate matter, organic contaminants, microbial pathogen and heavy metal etc. The development of water treatment methodologies possesses some limitations like shortage of money, lack of technical skills to operate these systems and lack of electricity resources in remote areas. Hence, it is the need to hour to develop such technique that should be functional on frugal basis suggesting that nano-technology and greener approach to generate bio-adsorbent for water purification are at best applicable solution. In order to deal with biomass or communal waste, pyrolysis is the most suitable energy recycling method that leads to breakdown of bonds on heating. This current research proposal suggests that bio-char is an economically feasible safe bio-adsorbent and a renewable technology for clean water provision along with others co-benefits of improving environmental air quality. data.projectName: Fungicidal potential of bio-engineered nanopesticides against the rice blast disease
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan is the main grower of the world-known basmati varieties that are famous for their distinctive smell and quality. Pakistan is the main exporter of both basmati (long-grain) and non-basmati (coarse-grain) varieties. Unfortunately, rice production in Pakistan is much less than the developed countries. Not only the yield, but also the quality of the rice-grain is affected by various factors, among which rice diseases are of paramount importance. World-wide more than 70 rice diseases have been described, out of these 15 have been found in Pakistan (Ou, 1985; Mustafa, 2013). Rice blast, caused by the fungal pathogen Pyricularia oryzae, is one of the most destructive disease of rice both in Pakistan and the world. The advanced countries are imposing restrictions on the import of the food commodities that have been treated with the agro-chemicals. The world is now shifting to the organic farming. The use of synthetic pesticides have environmental and health issues. Reliance on the biopesticides is gaining momentum that has now necessitated the scientists to find avenues for their use. The use of nanoparticles has offered an alternative, environment friendly solution for the plant protection industry. Various salts of the metal elements have been found successful in providing extremely small particles that have the competency and efficiency for fighting against the diseases.
This project has been envisaged to find best metallic nanoparticle (s) or its combination with the botanical origin pesticide to combat the rice blast disease. The out-come of these studies will provide a road-mile to the farmers and the allied industry for the adoption of the technology.

data.projectName: Title of Project:	GCF:  Fruit Exports from Gilgit Baltistan
data.projectDigest: This project aims at increasing the exports of fruits from Gilgit-Baltistan (GB) region where economy is hinged to tourism and agriculture produce. The production and quality of fruits like apricot, cherry, and apple in GB region is one of the best in the world. This fruit doesn’t reach the affluent market place because of the absence of a cold chain and little acumen in the entrepreneurs to develop one on their own. This project is a multi-sectoral project. The primary purpose of this project is to equip the market with a sustainable cold chain and help develop local brands for fruit exports to Chinese market in the first phase and to EU, UK, and North American markets in the second phase. It is also based in expanding the production capacity per hectare and to bring more area under cultivation. As supplement to exports it also builds a network of cold storage trucks to transport fruits from GB to the market of Punjab where the price of the fruit increases to a level that makes the transportation viable.

data.projectName: Universal antimicrobial arsenal for system level deployment against antimicrobial resistance, microbial infections and outbreaks: Multifunctional hybrid materials for healthy life and food security interventions
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: The health and food security landscapes in Pakistan are challenging. One out of every fourteen babies born in Pakistan dies before reaching an age of 5-years because of respiratory and gastrointestinal infections. Over 0.5 million new tuberculosis (TB) cases emerge every year in Pakistan, including 15,000 cases of drug resistant TB. Over 10% of surgical procedures carried out in Pakistan develop wound related infections after surgery resulting even in deaths.  The poor sanitation, contaminated food and water, and lack of health awareness further complicate the situation. Consequently, microbial infections (viruses, bacteria and fungi) become extremely difficult to control and are among the prime causes of mortality in Pakistan. With CPEC in the deployment phase and increasing international travel and trade, microbial infections can have far reaching socioeconomic consequences as physical and political boundaries cannot protect against outbreaks. In addition, microorganisms-caused food deterioration is a huge threat to food security. About 40% food is wasted in Pakistan-partly because of exposure to microbes. These problems collectively demand the development of technologies that provide universal protection against all microbes. This project will bring about translatable materials science driven innovations to develop antimicrobial technologies targeting system-level deployment for healthy life and food security interventions.

data.projectName: AI Driven Decision Support System for Pakistan Judiciary
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: The access to justice is the basic right of every citizen in a country and an efficient judicial system enables a country to establish transparent accountability. With a population of over 220 Million, access to speedy justice is a linchpin in Pakistan's overall judicial system. A severe shortage of manpower in top positions is hindering the disbursement of quick justice to common people of the country. According to the 2020 World Justice Project Rule of Law Index, Pakistan is ranked at 120 out of 128 countries, which is very alarming. Artificial Intelligence based technologies can enable the honorable judges to work more efficiently by providing them the right information at the right time to make the right decision. The proposed solution will advance the state of Pakistan’s judicial system at the Apex court by developing AI powered indexed databases from existing judgement of Supreme Court of Pakistan. Coupled with an intelligent search to retrieve similar judgments and automatically summarize them, the proposed system will reduce the work load and increase the efficiency of honorable judges and their support staff. The successful realization of this project will contribute to achieving the long-standing dream of our nation: “Fori aur Sasta Insaaf”.

data.projectName: Solar Grade Silicon Production from Local Quartz: A way forward to Indigenization of Solar Photovoltaics
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Fossil fuels (coal, gases and oil etc.) are the major sources of energy. However, these are limited, non-renewable and cause CO2 emission. Therefore, it is need of the hour to produce energy through renewable resources (i.e. solar, wind, biothermal, hydrothermal etc.). Pakistan has taken initiative to produce electricity from silicon based PV modules as this region gets huge amount of sun-light. However, there is no such facility to fabricate these modules indigenously, and a huge amount is required to import these modules. Pakistan is an enriched country with huge potential of minerals such as quartz sand. Through complex chemical and physical processes Solar cell grade silicon can be extracted from quartz sand. Quartz sand contains crystals of silica and some other impurities which must be removed to use this SOG-Si for solar cell production as such impurities have adverse effects on the device performance. Therefore, it is necessary to purify the silica to generate SOG-Si cell fabrication. This project aims to pave the way for the possibility of producing (SOG-Si) from local quartz sand available within the country particularly in Balochistan. After refining and purifying Si upto ~6N purity these materials can be used for the fabrication of Solar cells and other semiconductor devices.

data.projectName: Development and Commercialization of Aquaponics Enterprises
data.projectDigest: The current and escalating extent of agricultural land destruction, altered soil nutrient profile, water scarceness and climate changes is afflicting agricultural productivity in different parts of the world especially in developing countries. Pakistan is one of the ten countries severely affected by climate change. Overpopulation, poor economy, reduced crop production due to environmental stresses is widening the gap between food supply and demand. Aquaponics basically combines hydroponics and aquaculture in a single set up to produce various fresh and nutritious plants including lettuce, spinach, basil, chard, arugula, tomato, eggplant, cabbage and many more in a soil free environment. Fishes provide nutrients to plants with the help of nitrifying bacteria residing inside either fish tank or grow bed. Different fish species ranging from tilapia, carp, trout, salmon, gold fish have been used successfully in different setups around the world.  This project aims to optimize different parameters related to aquaponics setup in our local climatic conditions to develop a system that can be easily operated on a small scale by local aquaculture farmers or backyard gardeners. Different local fish species will be tested with combination of variety of leafy green vegetables and to highest yield variety will be further optimized. Different grow beds will be tested for their filtration ability both mechanical and biological filtration and different bacteria associated with fish tank water will also be identified. This optimized system will help to build small scale aquaponics systems at local level including aquaculture farmers and backyard gardeners for maximizing food production.

data.projectName: Smart Livestock Farming for Improving Animal Health & Welfare
data.projectDigest:
This project aims to improve service delivery in livestock, increasing per animal productivity via a number of measures including intelligent animal monitoring, animal behaviour analysis, early disease predictions, modern diagnostic measures, and improving the impact of nutrition on milk and meat production. We are proposing to develop a practical “Smart Livestock Farming System”, enabling the farming industry to leverage the digitization and artificial intelligence to incorporate animal health and welfare monitoring, precision livestock farming (PLF) and smart waste management. 

The core objectives to meat:

•	Adoption of intelligent  techniques for automated monitoring of individual animals (precision livestock farming PLF) 
•	Improving animal husbandry while incorporating digitization, process optimization, and smart diagnosis services etc.
•	Increased animal welfare and education to decrease the impact of livestock farming on our natural resources
•	Transformation of livestock business from subsistence to commercial ventures  

This collaborative project brings together experts in machine learning, data analysis, animal behaviour and welfare.  The faculty, professionals, researchers and students from the collaborative universities will work in agile format to improve the service delivery in livestock sector while using modern technologies like artificial intelligence, cloud computing, big data analytics and domain knowledge.

data.projectName: Deployment of Nanoparticle encapsulated Synthetic, botanical and microbial insecticides for the Management of Desert Locust
data.projectDigest:
The recent outbreak of swarms of locust (Schistocerca gregaria) in Pakistan has threatened people’s livelihoods, food security, the environment and economic development of the country. Locust can reproduce rapidly, migrate long distances and devastate crops and pasture. The Desert Locust has the ability to change its behavior and appearance, under particular environmental conditions (unusually heavy rains), and transform itself from a harmless individual to part of a collective mass of insects that form a swarm, which can cross continents and seas, and quickly destroy a farmer’s field and his entire livelihood in a single day.
Insecticides are considered best option for quick control of insect pests in developing countries. Despite their beneficial role in pest control, pesticides have negative effect on non target organisms, they also hazardous effect on human health depending upon their toxicity, the degree of contamination and exposure time. Each year, approximately 2.5 million tons of pesticides applied for pest management in agriculture sector worldwide. Frequent and non judicious use of pesticide has result in development of pesticide resistance in insect pests. Moreover, it has been estimated that more than 90% of the applied pesticides are being lost to the air during the application stage itself and also as run-off, affecting both the environment and application costs to the farmers. Therefore, safe and efficient pesticide applications methods are essential for preventing the adverse effects of pesticides. In this direction, nanotechnology offers great promises and can be used as an innovative tool for delivering agrochemicals safely. Nanosized encapsulated pesticides offer a variety of enhanced features including controlled release and improved efficacy
Nanofo

data.projectName: Promoting women entrepreneurship through dairy products value addition for economic uplift of the country
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Entrepreneurship in value addition is considered as one of the most important factors contributing to the economic development of the society.  The woman entrepreneurs have been confronting to several constraints in this sector which hinder their way for development. The major constraints faced by woman dairy entrepreneurs were high cost of equipment, lack of expertise to convert milk into value added dairy product, non-remunerative price for milk etc. In Pakistan, concept of women entrepreneurship is of recent origin. Women have become aware about their rights and situations and entered in different fields of business. They have established their own successful business empires. They are contributing towards the growth of economy and improvement of their socio economic conditions. Women workforce ratio in the country is increasing due to the increase in the women literacy rate. Planners and policy makers have viewed it as an effective instrument of social and economic change. Therefore there is a dire need for the implementation of various dairy development programs by government that can change dairy scenario tremendously and help the dairy entrepreneurs to obtain higher profits.
Some of the main reasons for the gap are limited integration within the dairy value and resource constraints to implement initiatives at macro level and lack of expertise to start work with advanced techniques at industrial level and efficiency losses during production. Keeping in view the socio-economic status of the country; this proposal is designed that can promote socio-economic status of women and Pakistan through dairy entrepreneurship.

data.projectName: Smart Grain Storage using Machine Learning Approach with Fog Computing based on IoT (Smart Grain)
data.projectDigest: Grain storage is a challenging problem in Pakistan with its specific weather conditions, such as high relative humidity (RH), moisture, and temperature. The increase in production of major crops like wheat, rice, cotton and oilseeds of traditional and non-traditional varieties has caused significant services problems of long- period retention under stable and benign conditions. The existing storage facilities are insufficient at various levels. We propose a system to conceptualize, implement and validate a new IoT-based management system for grain storage at the farmer end. The system is implementing a distributed computing model. Physical sensors capture humidity, moisture, and temperature of silos at the edge nodes of the system. The data from the silo sensors is combined into rich feature vectors at the gateway nodes that can then be interpreted by Machine Learning (ML) algorithms with incremental learning capability for optimum grain condition analysis and prediction in the cloud. The analyzed data is also forwarded to mobile device so that the farmer has real-time feedback to optimize his local grain storage. The goal of the proposed system is to help the farmers to improve their grain storage systems and use smart techniques, both in existing and new facilities.

data.projectDigest: The earthquakes never kill people but the collapsing of the buildings do. The devastating earthquake of 2005 triggered development of SP-BCP 2007 for seismic safety considerations of building structures. These provisions were adopted from international codes with a condition of timely update and revision after every three years to ensure the relevance of code with current state of engineering improvements. Unfortunately, there has not been any revision to these provisions since 2007. Pakistan has substantially expanded earthquake knowledge but could not be translated in the improvement of engineering practice by revision of SP-BCP 2007. The 6.4 magnitude Mirpur Earthquake of 2019 caused 38 deaths, 3,149 fully and 11,036 partially damaged masonry structures. In active seismic countries like Japan, Taiwan and Western US large magnitude earthquakes are frequent, but it is very rare that the death toll rate crosses double digits. The reason for such resilient structures is the development and implementation of improved site-specific design building codes in these countries. Proposed project aims to improve the current state of earthquake engineering practices for the design & construction of earthquake resilient structures in Pakistan by collaborative research of academic researcher (GIKI, UET Pesh, NEDUET, QAU , UOP, HABIB UNI, BUITEMS, MIRPUR AJK), engineering practitioners  (NESPAK) & policy implementation regulatory bodies (PEC, NDMA, PDMAs).

data.projectName: Oncomining Big data  for the development of novel cancer biomarkers and  potential therapeutics
data.projectDigest: Cancer has resulted an increased health and economic burden globally, and the paramount impact it has is on the most vulnerable inhabitants of developing and underdeveloped economies. For the first time, it has been revealed that cancer has the most devastating economic impact of any cause of death across the globe. Approximately 70% of deaths from cancer occur in low- and middle-income countries. Pakistan, being a highly populated Asian country, is suffering with the economic cancer burden, especially the young and middle-aged population with deadliest cancers like, lungs, prostates, breasts, brain, liver and blood cancers. The consortium members from different institutes will perform their specialized activities to achieve the common goal of cancer treatment. The major goal is the oncomining (deep analysis of cáncer data) that will be followed by machine learning (training machines to interpret complex data) to extrapolate big information into meaningful data. Based on the achieved meaningful information, molecular docking (prediction of drug interaction with human cells) and simulations of screened libraries (available market drugs) for different new/repurposed drugs will be performed to identify novel cancer biomarkers (drug targets) and therapeutics (drugs) to be tested in preclinical trials on models generated from local Pakistani cancer patients. In the meanwhile, prototypes will be developed to monitor live cancer cell growth (portable CO2 incubator) and to diagnose cancer at early stages (biosensor-based cancer detection chips).

data.projectName: Towards transactive energy system – Blockchain based smart grid framework
data.projectDigest: It is a national energy need and one of the key concerns of the scientific community to improve the energy transportation mechanism i.e. the grid and to increase the overall efficiency of the power system. This requires a transformation of traditional grid into a sustainable energy solution consisting of a Smart Grid. Smart grids enables large scale integration of renewable energy sources in the energy system which calls for peer-to-peer (P2P) energy tradingPeer-to-Peer (P2P) energy trading represents direct energy trading between peers, where energy from small-scale Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) in dwellings, offices, factories, etc., is traded among local energy prosumers and consumers. A hierarchical system architecture model is proposed to identify and categorize the key elements and technologies involved in P2P energy trading. A P2P energy trading platform shall be designed and P2P energy trading based on blockchain technology needs to be simulated for a selected community involving close-to real time electricity planning.

data.projectName: Design and Realization of a Low-Power SoC for Energy Meters
data.projectDigest:
The global smart electric meter market is expected to reach USD 30.19 billion by 2026 [1]. Electric meters are an integral part of smart grid-based energy distribution as they not only measure the energy consumed but have also become a small gadget providing data insights to both the consumer as well as the distributor. Future smart electric meters will host a dozen applications including but not limited to data communication, catering requests from the utility, optimal load management by exploiting the control of smart appliances at its disposal. As a result, the smart meters being data hub themselves complemented with the integration of renewables at the consumer premises, it is not farfetched at all to anticipate the use of artificial intelligence pouring in the meter itself. 
With the above-mentioned diverse spectrum of applications along with stringent power requirements, traditional design flow integrating custom components on a single board does not work efficiently. As a result, a system-on-chip (SoC) (a microprocessor plus peripheral devices) approach is required that provides meter manufacturers with a low-power, area-efficient solution to rapid prototypes. In this project, we will build such SoC custom designed for energy meters.

data.projectName: Strengthening the Upcoming E-hail Policy using Perceived Passenger Satisfaction
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest: Meeting the urban travel demand without a public transport infrastructure is one of the major issues that cities of third world countries are dealing with. The issue results in excess vehicle privatization, severe pollution, and other traffic-related issues that have become a major hurdle to achieve sustainability.  To fill this gap, smart mobility service like E-hail (Uber, Careem, etc.) is catching the eyes of third-world cities to serve as an alternate to public transport. Indeed, the solution is viable due to its suitability, affordability, and adaptability, but when regularized in a proper manner. To regularize E-hail, an upcoming E-hail policy is expected soon in Pakistan. The policy is being prepared with the mutual consent of E-hail companies and the government, where the users’ consent is completely ignored. If implemented in its existing condition, the policy could have devastating consequences as it would ruin the user experience. Thus, efforts to make it a public transit alternate will be failed. Therefore, to strengthen the upcoming E-hail policy by ensuring the inclusion of users' consent, this project aims to propose policy implications based on significant quality attributes of E-hail services in the perception of the users. To conduct the study, Hyderabad will be selected as the study area.  Data will be collected from a random sample of 180 frequent E-hail users through questionnaires. To achieve the goal, results will be obtained using 2 SEMs and policy implications will be proposed on significant variables. The study is significant as, it would build a strong knowledge base for policymakers and transport planners to legalize and regularize E-hail services according to the mutual consent of all stakeholders to curtail traffic related issues.

data.projectName: Women at Work: Opportunities and challenges for women’s careers in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: A grand challenge faced by Pakistan is to increase participation of women in the workforce. While this has been recognized as a key area for improvement for many decades, the lack of any progress on this front is highlighted by the recent World Economic Forum Global Gender Gap Report 2020, where Pakistan ranks second last on the Global Gender Gap Index. Thus, this project aims to produce outputs and make recommendations to increase the economic activity of women in Pakistan. The project will examine the cultural values that affect working environment, and the lack of opportunities for women in upper management. It will also look into workplace mistreatment of women, including discrimination and harassment, and the job insecurities women face. The role of organizational practices in addressing work-life balance and diversity will also be studied. Various projects carried out at the three partner institutions will use a combination of quantitative (survey) and qualitative (semi-structured interviews) methods. The project outputs will include: motivational sessions for female students in universities and colleges; conference papers and journal articles to extend the academic debate; a Women@Work industry report to make recommendations to practitioners and policy makers; case studies; and, dissemination seminars for industry.

data.projectName: Potential of functional foods as biological alternative to the chemical additives for healthy and safe meat production
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: The world population is predicted to increase to over 9 billion by 2050, creating a challenge of securing adequate food supply for the growing population. Animal protein is important for meeting the demand for macronutrient protein, an integral part of a balanced diet. However, use of Antibiotics as Growth Promoters (AGP) in poultry as well as in small and large animals has posed serious consequences to the local meat consumption as well as its export due to health-related concerns. Use of AGP in poultry and livestock  put constraints on  export of meat by Pakistan. Similarly, Pakistan poultry products cannot reach to the Halal food market which has total worth of $3 trillion in the world (Economic survey, 2018). Halal meat contributes about 16 percent of total world trade of the commodity. To meet this challenge, the proposed project focuses on the development of functional food based feed for poultry/livestock to enhance the production of safe and healthy food. Functional foods are natural microbe-based products that beneficially affect the host by selectively stimulating the growth of beneficial bacteria in the colon, prevent pathogens from colonizing the animal gut and enhance the immunity level of the host resulting in a reduced pathogen load and improved performance of the poultry/livestock.

data.projectName: Research and development of unmanned underwater, air and land robotic systems for strengthening operational effectiveness of Rescue-1122
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest:
PES/Rescue 1122 although equipped with traditional search and rescue equipment, has several limitations. For instance in drowning cases the organization relies on divers, which are (i) limited in numbers (ii) can take up to an hour to get mission ready and (iii) Rescue 1122 SOPs do not allow divers to carry out search and rescue operation during the night time. More specifically during some complex emergencies of building collapse/water rescue etc. the approach is limited to find and evacuate the victims. The PES had to encounter a number of challenges associated with such complicated search and rescue operations. 

In a nut shell, the challenges faced by Rescue 1122 can be broadly classified as land, air and underwater search and rescue missions. To overcome these challenges, indigenous design and development of technologically advance unmanned underwater, air and ground vehicles or robots are proposed. As per investigators best of knowledge such robotic systems do not exist in Pakistan. It is envisaged that successful development and deployment of such force multiplier robots would improve many folds the operational effectiveness of Rescue 1122.

data.projectName: Women’s Participation in Workforce and National Development: The Erstwhile FATA Regions Perspective of Key Barriers
data.projectDigest: As evident, women constitute an indispensable workforce in the quest for national development of any nation. In the developed nations, women have been able to play this important role. However, in the Newly Merged Districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, especially after the merger of these districts women are still relegated to the background as they lack the educational, economic and political power necessary to actualize their innate potentials. Knowledge from Erstwhile FATA Regions perspective of women participation in workforce and national development is scarce particularly when compared to the other settled provinces of Pakistan. This project will examine the barriers in way of their participation in the workforce and national development. Particularly, the important places of women education in the empowerment of women to enable them contribute their quota to national development. This project will rely on primary and secondary sources of data and will be analyzed using content analysis. By making academic and industrial consortium, this project will recommend pro-active actions need to be taken by the government and other stakeholders in order to ensure gender parity in education through special child girls education, scholarships and effective implementation of policies and programs geared towards this.

data.projectName: Design & development of efficient extraction process of herbal nutritional & medicinal constituent from moringa oleifera for better human health for underprivileged community of rural areas
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
The project focusses on the human health with reference to malnutrition, especially in the rural areas in addition to access to the medical facilities available to those areas. In addition, it has also been used as natural preservative in food products. Maringa oleifera (sohajna) is the indigenous tree in most of the regions of Sindh & Punjab. Peoples have been using flowers & seed pod in curries and also for arthritis since very long. In the last decade more awareness has been developed & it has been identified as miracle tree and every part (flower, leaves, seeds, tree bark, roots & gum) of the tree has its own value that has not only high nutritional value but also cures number of diseases. The moringa oleifera leaf powder is also available commercially. The current research also support the increased use of herbal nutritional supplements & medicines globally.   

The aim of the project is to develop an extraction process to extract different nutritional and medicinal constituents from Moringa Oleifera tree part (leaves, seeds, flowers, root & tree bark) to fulfil the nutritional as well as cure of various diseases; targeting the underprivileged community of the rural areas, where there is a deficiency of nutrition’s & lack of medical facilities.

data.projectName: Indigenous low-cost Sustainable Passive Cooling of Buildings using Polymeric Hydrogels for Rural and Urban Areas of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The use of electricity has increased at a rate of 5-10 percent per year. Because we generate more energy at a very small pace, the losses in transmission and distribution widen the gap in supply. This results in load-shedding that affects more than 90 percent of the population directly. During the long summer season, this condition deteriorates especially in rural and remote areas where temperatures rise up to 45-50 ?C. Thermoresponsive Hydrogels provide an indigenous cost-effective solution to this problem. These hydrogels provide a temperature difference between outside and inside the building of approximately 10-14 ?C. In addition, these hydrogels are portable and sustainable and do not harm the environment or cause pollution. A hydrogel sheet when placed on a flat rooftop with an automatic irrigation system (pump & spray) can work for more than a month. This hydrogel will withstand 8 hours of intense heat when fully charged with water, and continue to act as a barrier to outside heat from entering the house. Such hydrogels can also be added to /door glass windows to avoid the heat from entering. This will reduce the demands for electricity as the use of artificial air conditioning can be minimized.

data.projectName: Controlled environment agriculture system based on hydroponics for fodder  and crop production
data.projectDigest:
According to Pakistan Bureau of statistics, agriculture sector plays a vital role in Pakistan’s economy as it contributes 18.9 percent to GDP and absorbs 42.3 percent of labor force. In recent years, continuous decline in surface water availability, food security and climate change has had a negative impact on agriculture productivity. In such a situation in Pakistan, where the crop productivity is far below the potential, also presents numerous opportunities to explore new technologies to increased crop productivity. 

This research project aims to address solve national level challenges of food security and water shortage by indigenous developing cost-effective Next Generation Artificial intelligent based CEA and VF crop production system. This research project will establish linkage between academia, industry and progressive farmers by developing cost effective alternate crop production system. The project will focus to develop a modular and scalable crop production system by integrating advanced technologies such as AI and IoT.
Project PI has formed a consortium to successfully complete the project that comprises of academic collaborator i.e. University of Warwick (UoW), United Kingdom, Bangor University (BU), United Kingdom, Agriculture University Peshawar (AUP) and Pakistan based industrial collaborating partner Spring Fox Labs (SFL) (Pakistan).

data.projectName: Role of Governance Reforms (Merger) and Cash Assistance to Promote Economic Prosperity and Trust on State Institutions for Dispute Resolution in Ex-FATA, Pakistan: Experimenting the Role of Improved Public Services
data.projectDigest: Federal Administrated Tribal Area (FATA) (now part of KPK) is one of the most underdeveloped and conflict affected areas. Around 60% of its people live below poverty. A large section of society is facing a sort of exclusion, in terms of access to basic services, women empowerment, nutrition, health and education and indulge in conflicts. People to people (PtP) conflicts – clash between two opposing individuals/groups – is on the rise, apart from external conflicts, in FATA. Around 0.17 million PtP conflicts have been reported in 2018 compared to 0.14 million in 2012 in KPK (PBS, 2019). The increasing PtP conflicts poses huge socio-economic challenges to Pakistan. There are two notable changes occur in FATA over the last one decade. First, Pakistan launched Benazir Income Support Program (BISP) to provide financial assistance to poor families. It covers around 0.16 million beneficiaries in FATA. Second, the FATA merge introduces massive governance reforms in the region. It opens new avenues for economic prosperity and social cohesion by providing opportunities to engage in productive activities. These facts lead us to consider the role of governance reforms and cash assistance in addressing conflict and choices over dispute resolution and prompting economic prosperity in FATA.

It covers around 0.16 million beneficiaries in FATA. Second, the FATA merge introduces massive governance reforms in the region. It opens new avenues for economic prosperity and social cohesion by providing opportunities to engage in productive activities. These facts lead us to consider the role of governance reforms and cash assistance in addressing conflict and choices over dispute resolution and prompting economic prosperity in FATA.

data.projectName: Development and prototyping of hybrid photovoltaic based smart windows
data.projectDigest:
Researchers, around the world, are trying hard to not only provide comfort to human beings but also to improve their living style. Both the comfort and living style can be improved by dealing with the day to day energy issues in residential as well as in official areas. All these areas are man made and thus, made up of huge buildings mostly with large glass walls and / or glass windows. Glass walls and windows are responsible for heat loss / gain because of the high transparency in IR, visible and UV region. 
Smart windows and walls are based on technology to tune the transmission / absorption of solar radiations [1-3]. For this purpose glass needs to be coated with some suitable material so that windows can act smarty and can make efficient use of the absorbed energy thus, named as smart windows. 
Therefore, the hybrid system of photovoltaic based smart windows, using organic-inorganic material, will increase the solar modulation ability with the control over transition time and temperature of organic perovskite material.

data.projectName: Genetic evaluation of forensic STRs and SNPs using the Illumina® ForenSeq ™ DNA Signature Prep Kit
data.projectDigest: It has been almost a decade since the first next generation sequencing (NGS) technologies emerged and quickly changed the way genetic research is conducted. Today, full genomes are mapped and published almost weekly and with ever increasing speed and decreasing costs. NGS methods and platforms have matured during the last 10 years, and the quality of the sequences has reached a level where NGS is used in clinical diagnostics of humans. Forensic genetic laboratories have also explored NGS technologies and especially in the last year, there has been a small explosion in the number of scientific articles and presentations at conferences with forensic aspects of NGS. These contributions have demonstrated that NGS offers new possibilities for forensic genetic case work. More information may be obtained from unique samples in a single experiment by analyzing combinations of markers (STRs, SNPs, insertion/ deletions, mRNA) that cannot be analyzed simultaneously with the standard PCR-CE methods used today. The true variation in core forensic STR loci has been uncovered, and previously unknown STR alleles have been discovered. Therefore it is highly recommended to imply this technology in Pakistani population to discover new alleles and detailed sequence information that may aid mixture interpretations and will increase the statistical weight of the evidence. It would be of great help in establishment of regional as well as international database pertaining SNPs and STR dataset.

data.projectName: Biofertilizer development from agricultural waste through vermicomposting
data.projectDigest: Agricultural waste which is actually agricultural biomass. Being an agricultural country, huge quantity of biomass is generated and remains unutilized or burned in the agricultural fields causing air pollution (Samo et al., 2016). According to a report, 40 per cent of food in Pakistan is wasted. This includes food loss during the supply chain (production, post-harvest handling, agro-processing, distribution and consumption) that occurs every year. Owing to extreme weather conditions, food loss in this country is expected to be higher than computed by agricultural departments. Food wastage is the sum of food waste and food lost. This loss not only increases food shortage but it also has various hidden costs and wastages in the form of other items like fertilizer and pesticide wastage as well electricity (Mughal 2018) The waste food can be collected from various zones to establish a system to feed the dairy animals. The gut has a number of microbes that will support the digestion of the fruits and vegetable waste and the byproduct in the form of the cowdung will be taken as a barter trade. This organic manure can further be digested culturing various earthworm for vermicomposting. Initially the region of Faisalabad will be screened for the potential species that gives best castings as garden manure which will be our final product. Long with this strategy to obtain waste from various agricultural fields and local markets will be collected and will be provided to the dairy farmers for further biological processing. This way the resource management can be effectively done for the product development, thereby reducing the environmental pollution as well human resource development.

data.projectName: Exposure Risk of  Micro and Nanoplastics in selected Human foods from some major cities in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Plastic waste gaining attention all over the world owing to its low degradability, persistent nature and negative impacts on humans. The first priority and fundamental problem to be tackled is undoubtedly the human consumption, use and disposal of plastics. Microplastics (MPs) and Nanoplastics (NPs) are cosmopolitan in distribution and detected in all components of the environment such as atmosphere, water, soil and sediments. MPs and NPs makes their way to human food and  pass through the digestive system disturbing  the normal functions of the human body. In Pakistan, limited information is available about the origin of MPs and NPs in human food and its consequences on human body and how much a layman bearing the plastic burden? The main objective of the current project to evaluate the plastic contamination in different human foods, current plastic use practices for food packing, storages and its impact on human health and behavior. To achieve these objectives, a well-planned, comprehensive methodology will be developed with consultation by collaborators from multiple disciplines such as environmentalists, chemists, medical and social scientists.  MPs and NPs in Fish and shrimps (marine and freshwater), drinking water and beverages, preserved foods and honey  will be identified and analyzed using FTIR microscopy and image analysis techniques. Exposure risks of MPs and NPs in food and its impacts on human will also be studied through oxidative potential stress. Before the conclusion of project, a pilot awareness campaign will also be launched to sensitize the local community to reduce the plastic use. The expected MPs and NPs comes will helpful in the planning for the reduction of plastic  in human food.

data.projectName: Project ‘ASAAS’ (Foundations) - “Actions, Systems and Actors for Antimicrobial Stewardship”
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The micro-organisms causing infectious diseases are increasingly developing resistance to currently available antibiotics, a phenomenon referred to as 'Antimicrobial Resistance''. This has emerged as one of the most significant global health challenges of 21st centuries. The global response to this grand challenge is 'Antimicrobial Stewardship', the deployment of which is very limited in developing world, particularly in Pakistan. The proposed project while taking the systems approach aims to bridge this gap in Pakistan. Moreover, the project aims to expand the scope and remit of 'Antimicrobial Stewardship' to health systems, policy and the community levels. This will be achieved through contextualising 'Antimicrobial Resistance' and 'Stewardship' in Pakistan through a formative research using mixed-methods in the first phase. This will lead to the implementation of informed and evidence-based multimodal health education, promotion and policy mobilisation intervention in the second phase. The subsequent analysis and findings shall be disseminated to the wider public and policy stakeholders as well as the academic community. The project will also investigate the evolution of microorganism genetics in response to irrational use of antibiotics, poor disinfection and prescribing practices through sustainable surveillance and shall inform future research and strategies for antimicrobial stewardship in Pakistan.
