data.projectName: Preparation of local fourth generation probiotics (IV-GP) for improved performance of broiler birds
data.projectDigest: Poultry production is one of the fastest growing sector in Pakistan and plays a very important role in meeting the increasing demand for animal protein around the globe. However, this led to increased pressure for a safer, efficient, and sustainable manner of poultry industry. Poultry farmer’s main issue is the cost of feed, which makes up 70% of total expenditure. Another important concern from consumer point of view is the subtherapeutic use of antibiotics growth promoters (AGP) in developing countries. Use of probiotic strains to confer health benefits to host is well studied area of research. However, their use and properties in biofilm mode has not been explored in depth.  Considering the expensive protein supplements, this study was planned to understand role of probiotic bacteria in biofilm mode. A concept which will prepare new generation of probiotics i.e 4th generation probiotics (IV-GP). IV-GP is fundamentally different from the previous probiotics. The previous probiotics do not have long shelf life and are poorly protected against the digestive action of the GI tract. Since these contain separate, solitary cells of probiotics while the IV-GP will bring pure bacterial culture in the form of a biofilm, i.e. in a structure similar to that one in which they occur on intestinal mucosa. This technology will maximize survival of probiotic strains to reach the intestine alive and in sufficient numbers to confer the beneficial health effects on the host. Dual-coating of probiotics as a result of fourth-generation coating technology will make them protected at least 100-fold or greater than the uncoated. IV-GP has greater tolerance to increased temperature, pH and mechanical forces compared to previous traditional probiotics.

data.projectName: Early Detection of Crude Oil in Water: Design and Indigenous Development of Strip- Patch Sensors
data.projectDigest: Economy of Pakistan is rising at a very solid rate that demanding huge energy consumption and putting high pressure because we having limited resources of energy. Because of the limited assets of oil, Pakistan is importing large quantity of oil, to fulfill the growing oil demand. According to the report, 728 exploratory wells have been drilled in Pakistan, out of which only 219 remained successful. Now Government of Pakistan and international companies are reluctant to invest more money on drilling new places. In near past, no such activity is found to search for crude oil in Pakistan except in Karachi Sea. So the early detection of oil in any area is big challenge and it should be solved. In order to address this problem, and to avoid dependency on variety of multi-national companies and international service providers, an indigenous and local solution is badly needed to efficiently and effectively detect-trace out the presence of crude oil in waters at different places in Pakistan. For this a smart sensor based on the very exploitation of nanotechnology is required which may be able to identify the traces of crude oil in specific terrain just by simply checking the water of that area.

data.projectName: Combating Fake News in Developing Countries
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: The widespread availability of low-cost mobile phones and mobile Internet access has led to growing use of social media platforms in Pakistan. Concurrently, we are observing an increasing trend in the spread of fake news on such platforms, which can have a profound impact on citizens and institutions ranging from election interference, polarization, to conflict. The growing complexity of how fake news is presented (e.g., deepfakes) is making it increasingly difficult to identify and respond to fake news. This is a particularly pressing problem in developing countries where a vast number of Internet users have limited digital literacy skills. Thus, fake news presents a grand challenge for our society because (i) it can have far reaching consequences, (ii) it is a multi-faceted problem involving a complex interplay of technology, economics, psychology, and culture and (iii) it is unlikely to be solved by any one sector (e.g., technology alone is insufficient to filter all fake news). In this project, we will (a) conduct large-scale surveys and experiments to understand factors (e.g., digital literacy and cognitive biases) that drive belief formation, (b) design effective educational interventions for citizens, (c) design robust technologies for identifying fake news and carry out fact-checking that are tailored to user characteristics in developing countries.

data.projectName: 5G enabled Health-Care Framework for  IoT-Based Environments
data.projectDigest: With the increase of use of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies amount of data on networks is expected to only increase more. The reliance of medical healthcare systems over communication technology can never be denied. Since the past several decades, innovations in communication technology such as 5G, have greatly benefited the multifarious medical applications, especially in the fields of diagnosis, risk assessment, and prognostication. A Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN) is a one-off category of telemetry systems consisting of implantable and/or wearable body sensors integrated with wireless interfaces (homo /heterogeneous radio technologies). WBAN is an enabling technology that is employed for applications such as medical monitoring and health-care applications. WBAN offers cost-effective solutions for patients, caregivers, medical experts. The two key advantages of WBAN are portable monitoring devices and independent monitoring facilities. The proposed project aims for the societal impact related to ease of use, remote health-care, and management facilities. The major research objectives aimed in this project are two-fold 1) efficient routing mechanisms by minimizing redundant transmissions of sensed data in WBAN, and 2) prediction and classification system to provide the futuristic values of the important vital signs for the two diseases and classify the patients’ health situations to alarm the caregivers and medical experts.

data.projectName: Endophytic entomopathogenic fungi for the management of whitefly (Bemisia tabaci) and cotton leaf curl virus disease (CLCuD)
data.projectDigest: White fly transmitted cotton leaf curl virus disease (CLCuD) is most conspicuous reason for the low yield of cotton in Pakistan. It is considered among the major factor in recent decline of cotton production in Pakistan. Traditional practices for the management of vector (whitefly) heavily relied on the use of chemicals, the indiscriminate use of such chemicals resulted development of resistance in whitefly. Endophytic entomopathogenic fungi offers as an alternative for the management of whitefly and minimized the incidence of the disease. Endophytic EPF colonization the host tissues and secreted various types of secondary metabolites, including alkaloids, flavonoids, phenolics which protects the plants against pathogen infections. Upon entering the plant, the hyphae of EEPF grow in the space between the parenchyma cells which inhibit the feeding of insect. The proposed project will focus on endophytic entomopathogenic fungi against white fly to control cotton leaf curl virus disease. Series of experiments under laboratory and field conditions will be conducted to establish endophyte entomopathogenic fungi by using different methods (seed, foliar, stem and root inoculations). The resistance induction mechanism (s) will also be studied. The outcome of this project will help the farmer community to replant cotton crop and uplift national economy.

data.projectName: A sustainable approach to enhance dietary iron content in wheat to overcome hidden hunger
data.projectDigest:
Iron, an essential micronutrient, is needed by plants and humans alike for their proper growth and development. World health organization (WHO) has declared iron deficiency as the most widespread and worrisome issue globally. Iron deficiency is the leading cause of 0.8 million premature deaths yearly worldwide. In developing countries like Pakistan, most of the population relies on nutrient poor and starch rich foods, iron deficiency poses a major threat which needs to be countered.  
Wheat is one of the most important cereal crops in Pakistan both economically; being grown on 40% of the country’s cultivated land; and comestibly by acting as staple food for more than 60% of the common population. Thus, iron fortified wheat will be an excellent alternative due to its cost effectiveness, sustainability and ample supply. The current research proposal focuses on the development of transgenic wheat expressing SoyFerH1, HvNAS1 and AtFRO2 genes under suitable promoter. 
Enhancement of bioavailability of iron in wheat will be assessed by feeding experiment. For this purpose two groups of rats will be selected. Experimental group fed on diet supplemented with transgenic wheat and control group fed on non-transgenic wheat diet. Weight data will be recorded after intervals of seven days.

data.projectName: Co-Production of Biochar and Energy from Waste Biomass and Application for the Water Treatment and Soil Amendment to Enhance Crop Productivity (BIOTREAT-WATER-SOIL)
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
Farmers in Pakistan are faced with the challenges of improving food security, managing agricultural waste, improving crop water productivity, maintaining soil health, and protecting the environment. To meet these challenges with an integrated and multidisciplinary approach, this collaborative research, BIOTREAT-WATER-SOIL, aims to connect farmers and researchers so they can co-create a multi-faceted research project. The research project will result in prototyping an appropriate technology that will enable farmers to turn their waste into carbon-rich Biochar. The project aims to (1) develop a new mobile Pyrolysis-Adsorption-Distillation (PAD) integrated technology to transform waste biomass (WAB) into Biochar for application as a soil amendment and (2) complete the necessary upscaling and proof of concept to lay the foundation for use in the agricultural sector throughout Pakistan and the world. The unique feature of the proposed PAD is its mobility from field to field and the integrated approach to creating in-field solutions for soil and crop improvement, water-nutrient management, energy recovery, wastewater (WW) management, air pollution control, and promoting public health.
The project consortium is led by the USPCASW, Mehran University of Engineering and Technology, involving national and foreign academic and sectoral collaborators. The project delivery consists of Biochar technology development and appropriate transfer.

data.projectName: Microbial biotechnology for suppression of weeds and growth promotion of rice under aerobic system
data.projectDigest: Rice is the staple food of more than half of the world's population. In 2019, its production was 515 million tons that is 0.5% lower than that of its production in 2018. Major reasons for yield-decline are climatic conditions, less water availability, drought and weeds infestation. The transplantation method of rice is becoming difficult due to water scarcity, labor and green-house-gases emissions that further aggravate the effects of climate change. Therefore, direct-seeding of rice has been found a good alternative as it reduces labor requirement, mitigates green-house-gases emissions, and has good adaptive capacity in less water. However, weeds infestation in direct-seeded-rice causes yields loss by 30-80%. Manual weeding is expensive and chemical weedicides are causing environmental degradation, human disorders, resistance in weeds, and shifting of weed flora.  Among biological techniques, the use of allelopathic bacteria (AB) for suppression of weeds is getting attention due to its cost-effectiveness and environment-friendly nature. AB colonize in the rhizosphere and release phytotoxic substances which negatively affect weed growth, germination, roots and enhance infection. Along with weed suppression, AB promote plant growth. So, AB can be tested for the inhibition of major weeds of rice and the successful formulation will be evaluated under different agroecological zones.

data.projectName: An integrated framework to determine feasible warehouse locations for the multiple goods’ supply chains and disaster management along the CPEC routes
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The objectives of the programme is to complete the four projects which are aligned to the core aims of the programme. In this programme the first project is to perform census for the warehouses, their capacities, parameters and feasibility along the CPECs. The outcome of this project will be a GIS based directory of all the existing warehouse and their attributes. The second project is designed to identify the locations of the prospective warehouses needed around the CPEC for disasters management. It provides the recommendations to the government to develop warehouses for the contingencies against the disasters and shortages, such as; weather disasters, shortages of agricultural products,  response to a terror attach or any other risks to the people of Pakistan. Based on the data gathered through the project 1 and 2, the third project will be initiated to design an integrated framework for the warehouse management and its integral supply chain.  The fourth project is to optimize three different main supply chains for the optimal results using the warehouse performance optimization. The three supply chains would be identified through the data obtained through the project 1 and 2.

data.projectName: Source tracking of XDR Salmonella typhi in Karachi using traditional and Molecular approaches
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Typhoid is an offensive bacterial disease which is causing 26 million sickness episodes globally, every year mainly in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia affecting poorer sections in society and mainly children disproportionally. XDR is progressively recognized among Salmonella typhi lineages emerging from Africa to South Asia including Pakistan, with resistance to antibiotics (chloramphenicol, co-trimoxazole and ampicillin), and fluoroquinolones and, of concern, cephalosporins which subsidize to treatment failure. Azithromycin, remaining antibiotic which is still active against extensively drug-resistant typhoid; however, further genetic mutation could make typhoid untreatable in some areas. 
 XDR in typhoid fever is not uniform and has progressed at different rates in several endemic regions. The significance of this research revolves around identifying the different trends of XDR Salmonella typhi. The objectives of this study included reviewing the clonal transmission of XDR Sallmonella typhi lineage from different areas in Karachi and to identify the potential contaminated sources of outbreak for XDR typhoid and also measuring immunological parameter to assess Typhoid Conjugate Vaccine in vaccine child candidates.

data.projectName: Boosting the Activity and Stability of Cobalt Oxides/Phosphides for Water Oxidation/Reduction Using a Combination of Alkali/Alkaline Earth Metals and Ionic Liquids
data.projectDigest: Water is vastly preferred as a source for hydrogen, which has the potential to satisfy the world’s clean-energy thirst, through a friendly energy cycle. However, water-splitting technologies are still far from being economically viable due to its high cost. There is a dearth of catalysts that are active and stable under acidic conditions, where hydrogen production is much easier, with the best electrocatalysts are based on precious metals (platinum at the cathode and oxides of iridium or ruthenium at the anode). In this regard, this project aims to improve both the activity and stability of the well-known earth-abundant electrocatalysts  cobalt oxides and phosphides for oxygen evolution (OER) and hydrogen evolution reactions (HER), respectively, in neutral and acidic conditions which is highly demanded for the commercialization of electrochemical hydrogen production from water. Our strategy to boost the activity and stability of both catalysts (OER/HER electrocatalysts) relies on their doping with some alkali/alkaline earth metals, followed by catalysts encapsulation with ultrathin layer of hydrophobic ionic liquids (ILs). Doping ofCobalt Oxides/Phosphides with alkali/alkaline earth elements will tune electronic structure, and physical and electrical properties of the electrocatalysts to increase the catalytic activity of catalysts. IL's treatment can improve catalysts’ activity and stability, via tuning the catalyst/electrolyte interface, improving ionic conductivity, and hindering electrocatalysts’ surface oxidation/dissolution.

data.projectName: Fabrication of Biosensors for Dengue Detection Using Functionalized Carbon Nano Materials Synthesized from Green Source.
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Dengue (DENV), a mosquito borne viral infection, is one of the most common infectious diseases nowadays. More than 110 countries are suffering from Dengue infection and Pakistan is one of them. In Pakistan, 20 thousands patients die every year on average. Current statistics show that more than 50,000 cases of Dengue infection have been reported in 2019, while the figures goes much higher of unreported cases. Currently, several methods are in practice to diagnose dengue in clinic including RNA-based detection, Rapid Detection Test (RTD) and Elisa. However, these methods lack either specificity and low sensitivity or feasibility. Despite that RNA-based detection is highly specific, but in developing countries like Pakistan, it loses its practicality due to economic burden and specific skill requirement, especially in rural area. Therefore, there is a room to develop a highly specific, economical tool for the early diagnosis of Dengue. It would be worth to mention that Dengue early diagnosis will significantly improve the treatment outcomes.

data.projectName: Control of dengue mosquito by using dsRNA technology through sterility and larvicidal potential of genetically modified algae.
data.projectDigest:
The proposed project describes applied research with specified goals. Basic aim is to minimize the intensity of the dengue outbreaks in Pakistan through controlling its vector, Aedes aegypti mosquito. The only available solution at current is the extensive use of pesticide. We aim to develop an alternate, more environment friendly approach that could prove toxic towards mosquito larvae and additionally sterilize the female mosquito from dengue virus.
The re-emergence of dengue, chikungunya and Zika arboviruses signals an increasing global danger of vector-borne infectious diseases. The only possible strategy to control these vector borne diseases is to control its vector, Aedes aegyptii mosquito. The underlying rationale for the project is that Mosquito control can be an effective approach that is both preventative and powerful because it blocks the transmission of multiple diseases simultaneously. Every year, millions of Rupees are being spent on pesticides to overcome the dengue outbreaks. 
Aquatic environment is an essential in the life cycle of the mosquito and so, killing mosquito’s larvae in water is more preventative than killing adults which may have transmitted the disease by the time they are killed. Our hypothesis is based on the assumption that the green algae, Chlamydomonas reinhardtii, in aquatic environment could be made toxic to mosquito larvae as they will express chloroplast transgenes that are based on the mosquitocidal proteins of Bacillus thuringiensis (Bti) and double stranded (ds)RNA directed against crucial genes in mosquito and against dengue virus. The proposed approach could be very useful in mosquito control as mosquito larvae when feed on algae, the Bti toxin along with dsRNAs (expressed in algae) will act as mosquiticidal & kill the insect.

data.projectName: The production of a Substitute Natural Gas from Waste
data.projectDigest: The power generation mix of Pakistan has shifted from the imported furnace oil to liquefied petroleum gas and coal. The 2019 statistics reported by the national electric power regulatory authority indicate a shift towards gas and coal-based generation with 23% and 13% share respectively. Scientists have already proven adverse effects on the environment and climate by burning conventional fuels for energy and heating purposes. This research proposal supports an approach of utilising nationally produced waste as a sustainable source for heat and potentially power after upgrading with relatively less adverse impact on the environment and climate. Currently, about 1.7-1.9 billion tonnes of MSW per year worldwide is generated of which Pakistan’s careful annual estimate is ~20 million tonnes per year. The existing methods of waste abatement include incineration and landfill storage which pertain huge health risks. The proposed technology for substitute natural gas production is based on co-gasification with specially designed cheap catalysts. The project will help in expanding waste utilisation program beyond basic recycling to waste to the energy sector in line with the UK and China supporting partnership. The project also offers a realistic potential to generate revenue and employment opportunities within the country. The substitute natural gas can also help to replace the heating requirement of a plant using conventional natural gas, thus, reducing the burden on natural gas consumption.

data.projectName: Developing Technology and English Language Teaching Skills: Training English Language In-service and Prospective Teachers
data.projectDigest: The use of technology for English language teaching and learning may offer a solution to the academic problems and challenges (see e.g. Fang, Hwang & Chang 2019). However, in Pakistan, little research aims at English language teachers’ preparation, ability, and attitudes towards the utilization of technology for pedagogical purposes (Irshad, 2015). There is almost a lack of formal training opportunities for English language educators and prospective teachers (Mahboob & Talat, 2008; Noor & Shahbaz, 2015). Moreover, HEC Pakistan and the Ministry of Education have been investing extensively in providing technical resources to the academic institutions in general and HEIs in particular; therefore, there is a need to develop teachers’ competence in making use of technology. To address this gap, the current project proposes to train English language teacher educators and prospective teachers (MPhil English Linguistics or/and Literature students) for educational technology integration. We hypothesize the teachers require pre-service and in-service formal training to make productive use of educational and general technology for teaching the English language. Focusing students of MPhil English (Linguistics/Literature) who form the prospective English language teachers’ population in Pakistan, this study represents an attempt to revamp the MPhil English curriculum by updating existing courses and introducing new technology-aided English language teaching courses. Moreover, targeting the English Language in-service and novice teachers, this study will conduct formal one-month training and will also pilot test a six-month English language teaching certificate course for prospective and novice teachers.

Focusing students of MPhil English (Linguistics/Literature) who form the prospective English language teachers’ population in Pakistan, this study represents an attempt to revamp the MPhil English curriculum by updating existing courses and introducing new technology-aided English language teaching courses. Moreover, targeting the English Language in-service and novice teachers, this study will conduct formal one-month training and will also pilot test a six-month English language teaching certificate course for prospective and novice teachers.

data.projectName: Low-cost Environmental Friendly Housing: A Step Towards Sustainable Cities in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Sustainable development has drawn attention worldwide due to global environmental and energy issues. The demand and supply of energy, water, and environmental conservation are vital to worldwide human development. Pakistan is facing severe challenges in these sectors. Uncontrolled urbanization in the country has further lead to the rapid consumption of resources, resulting in deterioration of the environment, haphazard planning, use of energy, water scarcity, and emission of greenhouse gases. Solid waste management is another challenging task in all the major cities of Pakistan, as more than 55% of the solid wastes have no mechanism for its collection and final disposal. The housing sector being the primary consumers of the world’s energy has also got very little attention for exploring alternative materials that could be both energy and cost effective.
This project aims at addressing the aforementioned challenges with a significant focus on the gap identification, formulation of sustainability guidelines, and assessment framework as well as capacity buildings in terms of trained human resources. This work may be regarded as a base for providing a master planning of a sustainable township, which on a broader scale, would be expanded to sustainable cities by incorporation of the main elements of sustainability.

data.projectName: Embracing 5G Technologies and Tactile Internet in a Reticent Society
data.projectDigest: Importance of data has touched new highs in recent years and a global competition to achieve 5G superiority has emerged. The reticent society of Pakistan is yet to recognize the paramount importance of acquiring 5G skills and technology for developing knowledge based economy. The grand challenge addressed in this project proposal is to facilitate embracing 5G technologies and Tactile Internet in our society.  Acquisition of 5G dexterity would influence economy, culture and lifestyle substantially. This project provides an outline for a rapid adoption of 5G practices in various integrants of the society in a phase-wise manner. Artificial intelligence and software engineering are the other prime aspects of this research, as 5G solutions correlate heavily with these fields. Social values such as women empowerment and inclusion of remote areas in high-tech research are also sought in this project by including female researchers as well as scientists from far-off areas. Industrial giants such as Huawei and Zong are also on-board in this research endeavor and Europe's premier 5G research center, the 5G Lab Germany is also collaborating in this research. From the public sector, KP Planning & Development department as well as Tourism department have vowed to support this project.

data.projectName: Assessing Water-Energy-Food (WEF) Nexus in Pakistan: An integrated modeling approach for investigating impacts of climate change on WEF nexus
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Water, Energy and Food (WEF) are the basic necessities required by human beings to run daily life activities. Out of so many differences that exist between developed and developing countries; the sustainable provision of WEF resources to general public in the long-run is one of them. This sustainability in the availability of these resources is only possible once the interrelationship/interconnectedness between WEF resources i.e. the so called WEF nexus is understood and entertained in time i.e. at planning and policy making stage. Having observed difficulties in the provision, management and security of WEF resources in Pakistan; the proposed research is designed to unveil the WEF nexus in the country. The WEF nexus shall not only be revealed in its current state, but shall be analyzed under changing climate and under various scenarios of management and policy interventions. Therefore, a holistic and integrated approach of methods and techniques are being proposed, consisting of life cycle inventories, dynamic environmental simulation and accounting procedures, crops yield modelling and climate downscaling on a national-scale. Hence, the proposed research is addressing a national challenge by questioning WEF security and therefore, the research results will be extremely useful for cross-sectoral coordination and commitment towards sustainable development.

data.projectName: Urban Edge - Deployable AI for Viable Urban Planning on the Edge
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is considered among the most urbanized countries, in South Asia, with 3% increase in its urban population each year [1]. Rural population flock into urban centers for better living and quality of life. It is expected that more than half of Pakistan’s projected 250 million citizens will live in cities by 2030 [1]. Urbanization has inflated Pakistan’s biggest cities so rapidly that they struggle to deliver basic public services necessary to provide an acceptable quality of life. “Urban Planning” is thus one of the key enablers for providing a quality of life that is well defined as per the UN’s SDGs.  As per definition, Urban planning is a technical and political process concerned with the development and design of land use and the built environment, including air, water, and the infrastructure passing into and out of urban areas, such as transportation, communications, and distribution networks. Effective Urban planning requires large-scale and affordable data acquisition and its analysis for an informed policy making and its execution. Unfortunately, for a developing country like Pakistan the technical platform required to provide the relevant data for urban planning is either non-existent or carried out via traditional and laborious manual means. We thus identify, this “lack of technological support for sustainable Urban Planning” as a Grand Challenge faced by the country. Furthermore, in order to determine the societal impact of the identified challenge we consider two sub-challenges associated with Sustainable Urban Planning. These two aspects are among the six big challenges being faced by Pakistan’s urban future in a recent [1] by International Growth Centre (IGC).

data.projectName: Designing next generation high energy density Li-based batteries and advanced supercapacitors
data.projectDigest:
To drive a car or cook food in the kitchen, we need energy. This energy comes from petroleum and coal. But using petroleum and coal can be very danger because they contain toxic materials which can make us ill. So we must think about and use a friendly energy resource. We are lucky to have electricity, which doesn’t contain any toxic materials. Thus, we can safely use electricity to drive our car, to cook our food, to power our fan and AC, and to watch TV. Unfortunately, there is still a problem, that is, electricity is not always and everywhere with us, especially while driving the car or during the electricity shortfall. 
Therefore, we need some “Magic Boxes” which can store electricity for us, and we can bring it to anywhere along with us, and use it when needed. In this project, we are thinking about to make such magic boxes, called Batteries and Supercapacitors, for storing electricity.

data.projectName: IoT based Calibration Facility for High Tech Medical Equipment
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Medical equipment has made diagnostic and therapeutic function easier than ever. With ever-growing technical advancements in medical imaging and other diagnostic / therapeutic modalities, medical practitioners’ dependence on medical equipment is on the rise. Internationally, medical devices are divided into 3 classes on the basis of associated risks of their usage by FDA and CE standards. In Developed countries, at least one annual check is performed to make sure that the medical equipment is being operated at desired standards. It is ascertained at Government level that patients undergoing various diagnostic / therapeutic procedures are exposed to a calibrated doze only, as administration of under or over dosage can cause serious threat to human health. Unfortunately, there is a great void in providing services to medical equipment in Pakistan. There is no concept of calibration to ascertain that only the standard doze is being administered to patients even in modern hospitals. Aim of this project is: 1) implementation of IoT based system for region-wise registry of entire inventory of medical equipment is use at various public / private sector hospitals and 2) establish integrated calibration facility to provide scheduled calibration to hi-tech equipment on yearly basis and after-repair calibrations.

data.projectName: Innovative Health Care Governance for Basic Health Care Issues - Application of Community Scorecard
data.projectDigest: Better health is the primary goal of a health system which is a key determinant of productivity and social welfare. From 1990 –2018 performance of Pakistan’s health indicators remained low as infant mortality has declined from 86 to 62 death per 1,000 live births, under-5 mortality has declined from 112 to 74 deaths per 1,000 live births. With this rate of progress Pakistan will not be able to achieve target of universal health coverage and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 2015-2030 particularly SDG-3 “Good Health and Well Being”. Therefore, we need to engage community perceptions/views in our health policy framework in order to identify areas for improvement. What local people feel about their health standards? Why health standards are not improving? What are the solutions they suggest? Punjab is a most populous province of Pakistan having vast economic potential, but the health statistics are not very impressive, furthermore there are significant inequalities in health indicators across province. This study will be conducted in the selected districts under “Prime Minister Health Initiative for Improving Service Delivery across Backward Districts” including Attock, Chiniot, DG Khan, Jhang, Kasur, Ladhran, Mianwali, Rajanpur at Basic Health Unit (BHU) level. A sample of 116 BHUs (50 from existing 24/7 BHUs, 50 from proposed 24/7 BHUs and 16 from proposed model BHUs) will be selected from these districts.

data.projectName: Design and Development of Model Sustainable Smart Village
data.projectDigest: The increasing trend in the urbanization is significantly effecting the economy of mega cities of Pakistan. In the coming years, there would be serious challenges of land, food, economy, transportation, and health. Therefore, presently, it is of prime most importance to forecast mass urbanization challenges and develop practicable solutions. Nowadays, such solutions are possible only with the adoption of latest –cutting edge technologies, known as “Smart Sustainable Cities”. However, prior to the full-fledged transformation of an existing mega city of Pakistan, it is necessary to design and develop a Model Smart Sustainable Village (MSSV) on the basic principles of Sustainable Smart Cities issued by United Nations (UN). In this regard, a village having population less 3500 in the vicinity of Lahore can be selected later on stages. The MSSV will be comprise of Smart Platform for each separate facility of village such as Education, Environment, transportation, and agriculture. These smart platforms will integrate sensors, communication protocols, main servers, and smart devices for the real-time two-way communication. In the final stage, these individual smart Platform will be unify over a single platform.

data.projectName: ANTI-VIOLENCE WOMEN REHABILITATION PROJECT
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan has 65% dependency ratio in total papulation. It is very high against the other developing nations that have 15 to 20% dependency ratio. The ratio describes how much pressure an economy faces in supporting its non-productive population. The higher the ratio, the greater burden carried by working-age people.
The marginalization of the women in the society is the sole reason of this high ratio. The World Bank Brief (2019) on Violence against Women and Girls states that almost 33% of the women in Pakistan is facing violence. The violence against women includes a range of the criminal activities that restrict their active participation in socio economic activities. Southern Punjab is a less developed region of a developing country. Here literacy rate is low, mostly people live in rural setting with low international exposures, poor financial, social and environmental setups. All these factors and patriarchal mind sets lead to increased violence against women. 
Proposed Project will be first in the history of the country to quantify and evaluate the degree, types, intensity of the violence against women in Southern Punjab. In addition to that it will develop a system of prevention and rehabilitation of victims.

data.projectName: Development of A Herbal Agent for Multiple Skin Diseases from TCM Formulation J-1 against Antimicrobial Resistance
data.projectDigest: Due to the poor hygiene, skin infections remain one of the most epidemic health issues in Pakistan. Drug resistance has become the major problem for the treatment of infections. It’s urgently required to discovery new agents against drug resistance. Interestingly, microorganisms are more likely to produce resistance to regents made of single component, but showed less resistance to complicated formulations. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) Formulation J-1 has been used by in TCM for treating multiple skin infections for hundreds of years with outstanding effects. Thus, this formulation has wonderful potentials for clinical application in Pakistan. Therefore, we designed this project for the pre-clinical research of Formulation J-1. This project will focus on the product development, and our Chinese partner, Hunan Anbang Pharmaceutical Company will invest for the commercialization of this product in Pakistan. It is worth mentioning that Hunan has done the successful clinical trial of another traditional Chinese medicine in ICCBS, University of Karachi, as a revolutionary step. They have established the local office and made themselves ready to invest more products. By importing new products, new technics, and invest from China to Pakistan, this project will be definitely helpful for the economics development of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Shajr-e-Pakistan -  Enabling a sustainable STEM ecosystem as pathway to fertilize future generations of high impact technology leadership in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan can be in the leading countries of the world only through uplifting of if its human resource. Currently, over 50 million students are enrolled at various stages of their education in Pakistan. We are spending Rs. 800 billion annually, and yet we then have to take ad hoc measures to up skill graduates and create employability. Globally from China to South Korea and Singapore, STEM has been demonstrated as a pathway for fertilizing young minds and create social cohesion. In Pakistan as well several wonderful STEM initiatives are underway with excellent impact. 

There is a need however to enable a STEM eco system and build capacity development systems for all stakeholders around it in a manner which can bring sustainable reform, demonstratively during and beyond project period. In our view the grand challenge is to have a sustainable STEM Eco system. NED University along with its academic collaborators – KSBL, Habib University, BUITEMS and University of Surrey, UK - and sectoral collaborators – Magnificence, Islamabad United, LRQA, media and many others sectoral including government and development agencies - propose to develop and enable a STEM ecosystem through a strong theory of change framework delivering a sustainable, generic, effective and efficient solution for the country. STEM Eco System key players include content developers, Regulators, Schools, Teachers, Students, Assessment bodies, Parents, After school experience providers, Higher education institutes and eventual employers.

data.projectName: High Performance Epoxy Nanocomposites Coatings for Corrosion Inhibition in Oil and Gas Industry
data.projectDigest: The destruction of metal infrastructures by corrosion costs billions of dollars to the economy. The loss due to corrosion affect the metal infrastructures of industry as well as society. The research project focus is to make the epoxy nano-composite coatings for corrosion inhibition of metal surfaces specially in the oil and gas industry. A systematic approach will be adopted to produce surface modified silica nano-particles and then these surface modified nano-particles will be dispersed in the epoxy matrix to make high performance of epoxy nano-composites that will serve as coatings for the inhibition of corrosion of metal structures. Various experimental techniques will be used to study the surface modified nano-particles and high-performance epoxy nano-composite coatings. Surface modified nano-particles will be characterized by FTIR and TGA analysis. The epoxy nano-composite will be assessed by polarization and electrochemical impedance technique to estimate the corrosion inhibition characteristics. The mechanical properties of epoxy composite coatings will be estimated which include the determining of adhesion properties, hardness, and tensile properties. The high-performance epoxy nano-composite coatings for the inhibition of metals corrosion will be a suitable to overcome the corrosion related issues specially for industrial and society infrastructure.

data.projectName: IoT based waste collection and management system at primary collection point in Peshawar and Karachi
data.projectDigest: Solid waste management being one of the critical problems in Pakistan,  needs to be promptly and efficiently addressed. Hence, this research shall concentrate on developing a system of  collection and management of municipal solid waste in Peshawar, KP in its pilot stage. and shall be extended to Karachi in the second phase. The system used for Municipal solid waste collection and management called as waste to point system (W2P). The W2P shall include segregated Municipal solid waste collection module. The points shall be awarded to the households based on the  quantity, quality and extent of segregation. These points shall be redeemable at various subsidized departmental stores. Revenue shall be generated by selling the collected waste to industries for recycling and other purposes. The remaining organic waste shall be converted into compost to be sold as fertilizer.

data.projectName: Catalyzing the transition of our bio-economy into the fourth industrial revolution using synthetic biology
data.projectDigest:
With the rapid pace of technological development in the life sciences, there needs to be a renewed emphasis on ‘sustainable production and exploitation of biological resources that allows for the production of more from less and even from waste.’ Pakistan cannot afford to leave out this new wave of technology (i.e. synthetic biology) in its strategy for the coming decades. This is crucial for upgrading all sectors that are bio-based and directly and indirectly connected to life sciences.
The project falls under the priority thematic area of Development Economics as it helps the country with
•	Developing indigenous capacity in cutting-edge high-value technology
•	Building new skill sets in the labour market
•	Encourages transformation innovation with the potential to spur new startups
•	Potential import substitution by producing cheaper, local alternatives
•	Enhancement of global competitiveness of Pakistani export value-chains 

The project takes a two-pronged approach to address the need for transitioning our bio-based economy into biotech-based economy by 1) producing a rich corpus of data around our bio-based industry and the gaps and opportunities in our existing value chains and 2) by developing prototypes that can be readily taken up by our industry ultimately speeding up adoption and catalyzing a faster transition.

data.projectName: Improving Education Standards of Pakistani Universities based on Student Performance mining and Industry 4.0 Technologies
data.projectDigest: We want to incorporate 4th Industrial revolution (4IR) technologies in higher education institutes, as we found that Pakistan is not coping up to 4IR. We have several milestones. First, we assume that in addition to traditional merit criteria, which is stationary and uninformed, we need to mine optimal features that contribute a students’ performance, good or bad. Second, for each semester, we want to provide comparative feedback (semester wise), to an enrolled student and to the teacher. This will be useful for students counselling (e.g. in which program a student will perform better and why?), and for admission committee, and policy makers in higher education institutes. A university can adjust, its admission criteria for optimal benefits-. as institutes, want to earn by increasing number of students, but not at the cost of quality and student’s future. The semester wise comparative students’ performance, can help teachers to adjust teaching methodology, and focus on some traits of specific students while teaching in a class room. Third, for each 4IR technology, we need to formulate policies for research collaboration with international entities (researchers, institutes, countries) and to devise curriculum based on current trends, research frontier.

data.projectName: Towards a carbon neutral and climate change resilient built environment in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: Energy consumption in buildings is a leading cause of anthropogenic climate change across the globe. In Pakistan, this problem is especially severe with almost a quarter of the population yet to be electrified. As one of the countries most at risk to climate change, Pakistan needs forward looking policies and market instruments to address both mitigation (i.e. avoiding climate forcings such as use of fossil fuels for meeting energy demand) and adaptation (i.e. designing future proof and resilient systems). This project will focus on creating such a holistic framework for decarbonizing the building stock in Pakistan. By collecting and analysing data from across a wide range of building types all over Pakistan, it will propose a unified set of building codes. At the same time, it will make use of Pakistan's renewable energy resources to help bridge the supply-demand gap, and also create a framework to make the building stock more resilient to rising global temperatures. Finally, it will develop generalizable methods to make users more aware of their climate footprint and reduce it. In doing all of this, the project intends to help Pakistan meet its climate obligations while simultaneously improving its resilience to climate change.

data.projectName: Towards the Development of a Digital Diabetes Assistant (DDA): Integrating AI and IoTs for Precision Medicine, Personalised Diagnostics, and Real-time Diabetes Monitoring
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: In a developing country like Pakistan, the physicians are limited in number, and there are a very large number of patients to be handled.  In current clinical practice, the physicians have to spend significant time in manually inspecting different reports for diagnosing diabetes with routine checks (that can be trivially optimized using modern AI methods, i.e., machine learning (ML)/deep learning (DL)).   This project aims to develop an AI-based physicians’ assistance system, i.e., the DDA that uses current advances in ML/DL while also innovating novel improvised ML models, to enable efficient and scalable diabetes diagnosis, treatment, and real-time monitoring of diabetic patients. More specifically, we propose to use state-of-the-art DL techniques for developing a novel one-stop integrated solution that works for a variety of routine clinical tasks in diabetes detection, diagnosis, and its associated co-morbidities. We will adopt a data-driven and privacy-aware approach to allow "The Diabetes Center" TDC to learn knowledge from their massive multi-modal diabetic patients’ data including medical images, relational, and textual data, and enable an automated physicians’ assistant that can allow TDC to cater to a larger set of patients more efficiently.

data.projectName: Sustainable energy production from metropolitan waste of Pakistani cities considering energy, environment and its possible contribution to economy of Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Municipal solid waste management for the metropolitan cities of Pakistan is becoming challenge for Pakistan.  In Pakistan there are more than 10 metropolitan centers which are producing more than 40,000 tons per day. This huge amount of waste generated is seriously deteriorating the environment, which is polluting not only air quality but also ground water contamination because the only method utilized for waste management in Pakistan in direct dumping. the public health especially in big commercial centers of Pakistan is in danger due to improper waste handling. the  current study involve the establishment of proper waste handling and energy production from this municipal solid waste through anaerobic digestion, gasification and utilization of solid oxide fuel cells for the production of electricity. 
Providing energy to the rural sector has become a significant challenge due to the energy shortage in Pakistan. The demand of electricity in Pakistan is increasing continuously due to rapid increase in population and the Government’s inclination towards rural electrification. Pakistan produces around 65% of its electricity through fossil fuels which is costly in the long run and an environmentally unfriendly option. The on-sight biogas production from the municipal solid waste at rural side is the best and cheapest option that can possibly reduce this gap.

data.projectName: Improve Resilience in Kinnow Production to Adverse Negative Effects of climate change in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
In Pakistan, citrus fruits are grown on an area of 195,052 hectares with production of 2.27 million tonnes in 2017 (Knoema, 2018). Pakistan is the 13th largest producer of citrus and 5th largest exporter of citrus in the world.  Pakistan has touched highest export volume of Kinnow fresh fruit (370 thousand tonnes) and value (US$ 222 million) during the season 2017-2018. Even though kinnow production outweighs local demand, Pakistan only exports 15% of total citrus produced - representing a mere 1.4% share (US$ 201 million) of the global citrus industry (valued at US$ 14.4 billion in 2017). Although there is room for Pakistan to increase its shares to the global citrus industry due to quality issues resulting from suboptimal farm management practices, ineffective post-harvest handling, limited use of technology, and limited farmer awareness about good agricultural practices currently is not possible. Moreover, climate change and lack of research facilities in the country are taking a toll on citrus production and kinnow especially.
In order for the citrus industry in Pakistan to continue to be economically viable, there is a need to optimise resource use efficiency (water and nutrients) to mitigate the negative effect of climate change. Severe weather effects such as droughts, high temperature, uneven rainfall, floods are putting the industry in risk. The proposed work will not only develop sustainable production methods but will also educate Pakistani citrus growers in how to efficiently and effectively use water and nutrients to maximise yield potential and quality and mitigate the effects of climate change.

data.projectName: Integrated Economic Model to Assess Climate Change Impacts and Policy Interventions: A study Based on Environmentally Extended Social Accounting Matrix for Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: The priority areas of SDGs require efficient use of the natural resources in the process of economic development to ensure sustainability, poverty reduction and improved well-being. The global development experience suggests that planning for the goals should be synchronized with overall economic growth strategy and cohesive policy intervention to mitigate the economic and climatic shocks. Pakistan faces water stress and is among the most vulnerable countries because of deteriorating natural capital and climate change. Agriculture is most vulnerable sector facing the environmental hazards and climatic shocks. The integrated economic models with detailed representation of sectors are increasingly used to explore simulations for a variety of shocks and results matching the needs of stakeholders. The proposed project aims to develop an integrated economic model of Pakistan's economy targeting most of the SDGs . The implementation of the project involves updating  the input-output table for Pakistan using data for 2004-05 and to develop an environmentally extended social accounting matrix (E-SAM) for Pakistan using 2017-18 data. For sustaining and making the tool effective, a Center for Economic Modeling will be established at Department of Economics, NUST that would train and conduct research on the issues of national economic priority.

data.projectName: Engineering Education in Pakistan: Overcoming Present and Future Skills gap
data.projectDigest:
Universities are the engines of change in the society. With the continuous global changes and industrialization, the role of universities especially technological and engineering universities is changing rapidly. Universities are under pressure to respond to the modern requirement in a number of areas. With the socio-political dynamics of countries, budget limitations, new skills, advancement in technology, universities need adaptation strategies that are well aligned with the requirement of the society. The governance, curriculum, skills gap analysis – skills parity, research and development – industry need, Commercialization, academia – industry partnership, financial management, dissemination of research, communicating the success stories, two-way communication between university and industry and scholarship of teaching and learning need to be reviewed and improved according to the challenges.
This project will focus on comprehensive evaluation of the public sector universities who are engaged in undergraduate, graduate and postgraduate engineering education. The governance, curriculum, scholarship of teaching and learning, social environment, financial sustainability and research and development will be through investigated. The study will comprise of a number of small projects towards the development of a comprehensive framework of training and education for universities in Pakistan. This will be a highly collaborative project with participants from reputable national universities around the country. This project will be extremely useful for identification of the gap between the persisting and required role of Pakistani universities in the development of the country, industry support, global competition and skills of the graduates.

data.projectName: Study of Pakistan’s Gemstones Mining Sector and Recommendations to Increase Gemstones Exports
data.projectDigest:
In Pakistan, most of the gemstone mining is carried out with traditional mining techniques. Individual miners or group of miners dig and search for these precious stone using old tools and traditional drill and blast method. During mining, which is done manually or by small blasting, 40 to 50 percent of the value of the stones is lost. When stones mined by blasting are cut, there is good probability of damage and cracks from inside. Many gems are sold unpolished and in uncut form and are processed in Thailand or India. Traditional mining tools, lack of investment in infrastructure, non-efficient mining techniques, lack of skills in miners, absence of cutting/polishing facilities, lack of modern marketing, absence of cutting/polishing trained personals are major hurdle for Pakistan to be a significant player in the international gem industry. The proposed project will focus on improving the mining techniques to enhance the quality and value of the gemstones being mined. The efforts will be made to introduce new mining tools to the miners. Another main goal is to develop the technical knowledge and skills of miners and their capacity building in gemstone sector. Research aim to add value to Pakistan gemstone market by conducting study on availability of cutting polishing skilled labor and facilities and its impact on gemstone exports of Pakistan.
The research team hope to achieve the following impacts/benefits;
•	Research aim to increase the quality of gemstones being mined in Pakistan.
•	Add value to remote areas economy, it can make life better for small scale mining communities
•	Increase the gemstone exports of Pakistan
•	Make Pakistan gemstone industry competitive in the world market 
•	In small scale mining, there is good number of women involved, research aim to en

data.projectName: GCF:  Energy harvesting using natural resources available in Pakistan particularly using Printable Solar Cells (EHuPC)
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Increased energy demands are more challenging for developing countries like Pakistan. To deal with this increased demand, we need either fossil fuel based like thar coal and oil-fired plants which will cause more pollution and worsen life threatening heat waves hitting Pakistan or have to take advantage of  available natural resources of renewable energies.  
The energy that can be exploited from solar radiation is huge amount (5.4 × 1024 J per year). The harvesting of energy from sun using photovoltaic materials is more appropriate to address above-mentioned challenges. Photovoltaic (PV) cells are the most suitable devices for direct transforming of sunlight into electric power. Thin-film solar cells are fabricated by the depositing colloidal solutions of semiconductor materials on a glass, polymer, or metal substrate. The proposed research firmly provides the solution for increased need of solar energy technology. It focuses difficulties like expansive fabrication, rigidity, long payback time associated to first generation solar cells like Silicon. data.projectName: Remote Condition Monitoring and Prognostics for Environment-Friendly and Sustainable Energy Solutions
data.projectDigest: Having a fragile and energy deficient national grid, the electrification of far flung rural and mountainous regions of Pakistan is associated with high infrastructure cost . Hence, one of the most viable solutions  being the deployment of distributed off-grid energy projects.  A similar drive for the electrification of these areas was initiated  by Pakhtunkhwa Energy Development Organization (PEDO)  under their Access to Clean Energy Program. Under this project a total of 356 Mini Micro hydro Power Projects (MHPs) were installed in Phase 1 and a further installation of 672  MHPs was initiated during  Phase 2 of this program. These projects once deployed, are being handed over to the local community for carrying out the operation and maintenance (O&M). Since the operational staff is non-technical, the plants are facing a lot of operational issues and are forced to shut down as a result of improper maintenance and improper load dis-aggregation. Most of these installed projects are currently non-operational due to lack of proper maintenance. This research will therefore be focused on developing a Remote Condition Monitoring System (RCMS) that will continuously monitor and transmit the current operating states of the equipment installed at the distributed Off-Grid Micro-Hydropower Projects. Thereby enabling the department to remotely monitor and control the MHPs. This RCMS will also prompt about the current failure states of the equipment. The data generated by the RCMS will then be used to predict the future failure states of the equipment.

data.projectName: DRY CHAIN TECHNOLOGY TO REDUCE FOOD LOSS AND AFLATOXINS CONTAMINATION
data.projectDigest: One-third of total food produced is lost before reaching the consumer, counteracting efforts to increase agricultural productivity and improve food security. High commodity moisture contents at harvest and damp storage conditions cause loss of food quality and enable growth of fungi that produce aflatoxin, which causes liver cancer and has been implicated in childhood stunting. Over 4.5 billion people are chronically exposed to aflatoxin in their diets. Textile and poultry industries are severely affecting in Pakistan due to feed problems contaminated with aflatoxin upsetting their health and passing on aflatoxin in meat and dairy products that cause severe health problems. We will implement our “dry chain” strategy of drying commodities immediately after harvest and packaging them in hermetic containers for storage and distribution. Once dried and packaged, no further energy or infrastructural input is required to preserve quality and prevent aflatoxin accumulation. By establishing Dry Chain Centers at specific locations in Punjab, KP and Baluchistan, we will empower small farmers and incentivize supply chain actors to adopt these technologies that reduce food loss and improve health. Capacity Building of pubic seed sector to cater the needs of private industry will be one of objectives of this project.

data.projectName: Design, Development and Deployment of Geological and Mining  Network of Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Since the inception of Pakistan, it has been continuously claimed that it is one of the richest countries of the world in mineral resources. However, no systematic efforts have been made to exploit these natural resources, and therefore, its contribution is not reflected in the annual GDP. Also, there are multiple reasons for underdeveloped mineral sector, e.g. poor infrastructure, lacking mineral policies, feudalism and security threat are few to mention. Moreover, the existing system in the country, rarely, preserve the rights of stakeholders. This situation has not only discouraged investors but also due to obsolete management infrastructure, the associated government employees are unable to deliver services expected by the business community and policy makers. 

We propose the use of fourth industrial revolution technologies to deliver a digital infrastructure that will provide a unified platform for stakeholders in mineral sector. More specifically, the system will be a state-of-the-art national knowledge base for Mineral Resource Management enabling the stakeholders to keep track of mineral resources, machinery and other critical infrastructure, mineral products, and skilled human capital in the mineral sector. In short, this will provide tremendous opportunities for business and services in the mining sector adding value to the national economic development.

data.projectName: Impacts to Adaptations: A Frame Work for the Robust Sustainable Water Resources Management to Changing Climate in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: The proposed project is based on an idea of climate change impacts assessments and adaptations strategies for policy makers. In Pakistan, the water resources system is mainly based on the water comes from high-altitude northern regions which mainly comprise of snow and glacier melts. This water transferred to the plain agriculture regions through mega storage reservoirs connected with a unique canal network (irrigation and link canals) for the purpose of agriculture. Since, the Pakistan is an agriculture country; therefore, this water resources system is tremendously important for Pakistan. However, recently, Pakistan is a hotspot for climate change impacts consequently substantial rise in temperature and alteration in precipitation patterns resulting impacts on water resources system due to rapid change in snow and glaciers situated in northern Pakistan. Idea behind proposed project is to investigate the impacts of climate change on water resources system of the Pakistan in context of snow and glacier melt, balance, glacier lakes outburst such as GLOFS, avalanches due to rise in temperature and precipitation change. Subsequently, the change in reservoir operation, canal water availability and demand at agriculture field under climate change. Finally, the framework design for adaptation strategies for the policy makers considering this critical research aspect.

data.projectName: Diverting smog contribution of urban biodegradable solid waste-based GHG emissions to C-sequestration through cross-linked value-added pathways
data.projectDigest: The proposed project is in the Priority Thematic Area of Climate Change and Environment. The poor management of biodegradable fraction (BF) of municipal solid waste (MSW) on daily basis and offals on the eve of Eid-ul-Adha has substantial contribution to climate change via release of three of major greenhouse gases (GHGs) viz. CH4, N2O and CO2. The average release of GHGs from poor MSW management is about 46.34 kg CO2-eq/day/ton significantly contributing to urban smog in major cities of Pakistan. With an average 0.4475 kg/capita/day and growth rate of 2.4% per year, the MSW generation is 7000, 13,500, 87000 tons/day in Lahore, Karachi and Pakistan respectively; releasing 4.024 × 107 kg CO2-eq/day GHGs. The one ‘central reason’ of poor MSW management in Pakistan is that MSW of very low calorific value being managed through centralized MSW management system designed for MSW of very high calorific value of developed country. An effective alternate is development of sanitation-ensured BF management systems at source-level such as in housing schemes and educational institutes, offal management coupled with short rotation forestry-based wood biomass arising from marginal lands. The proposed project will deliver opportunities for socio-environmental entrepreneurship for SMEs of Pakistan through cross-linked value added pathways.

data.projectName: Development of novel, effective, and low cost vaccines against Newcastle disease using local isolates of Newcastle disease virus to control the disease in poultry.
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
The control of ND must include strict biosecurity that prevents virulent NDV from contacting poultry, and also proper administration of efficacious vaccines. When administered correctly to healthy birds, ND vaccines formulated with NDV of low virulence or viral-vectored vaccines that express the NDV fusion protein are able to prevent clinical disease and mortality in chickens upon infection with virulent NDV. Live and inactivated vaccines have been widely used since the 1950s. Recombinant and antigenically matched vaccines have been adopted recently in some countries, and many other vaccine approaches have been evaluated experimentally. Despite decades of research and development towards formulation of an optimal ND vaccine, improvements are still needed. Impediments to prevent outbreaks the proposed project is therefore designed with following objectives
1)	Commercial vaccine production based on indigenous field strain.
2)	Introduction of autogenous vaccine production to the local market.
3)	 Continuous improvement of vaccine and vaccine technologies based on local needs.
4)	 Establishing antigen bank, preferably of local strains, as well as those from other adjoining áreas.
5)	Establishing reference lab on Newcastle Disease based on international strandards.
6)	Establishing international collaboration with Newcastle Disease researchers across the globe.
7)	To enable local poultry market to export disease free poultry products.
8)	Control and eradication of Newcastle disease using mass vaccination by enabling availability of cost effective locally made effective vaccine

data.projectName: Identity, promote and support trade and investment between China-Pakistan through a dynamic framework and decision support tool/dashboard
data.projectDigest: Despite having good ties in terms of strategic importance for a long time and economically now after CPEC/OBOR, Pakistan yet to witness any significant or sizeable inflow of Chinese investments/relocations particularly in areas which are either export-oriented, labour-intensive or technology-intensive. Most of the investments are being made are in roads, construction, energy-related infrastructure under some fixed return instruments or some investments in the industry with the purely local market target. The nine priority SEZs are yet to be opened but existing SEZs are also not bearing the gains either as envisaged. There are some serious issues/challenges which require attention and proper investigation so that Pakistan can position itself to become more attractive and conducive. At the same time, Pakistan exporters and entrepreneurs are unable to explore Chinese markets whereas Chinese products are fully drenched in Pakistan’s markets as they have better access. While having all such scenario in place, it is not providing any positive indications that may lead the country to transform its economy any time soon. Pakistan policies must dig deep to ascertain answers on the following key questions to usher in the structural transformation of the economy while leveraging China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) and other regional opportunities.

data.projectName: Cloude-Based Smart System for the Detection, Localization, Segmentation and Analysis of Acute Appendicitis in CT Scans
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest: Acute appendicitis is a severe inflammation of the vermiform appendix. Generally, it is due to obstruction of the lumen of the appendix by fecalith, normal stool, infective agents, or lymphoid hyperplasia. It's a medical emergency that almost always requires surgery as soon as possible to remove the appendix. In the current study, a novel technique is proposed for the automatic detection, localization, segmentation and analysis of acute appendicitis using machine/deep learning techniques. The data will be collected from local hospitals initially from a province and then gradually extended to cover the whole nation. The developed solution will then be deployed on cloud for immediate access by medical experts globally.

data.projectName: Modeling and experimental study of photocatalytic reduction of CO2 to useful fuel (CH4, CO, CH3OH) by adopting visible light responsive (VLR) catalysts
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest:
The detrimental effects of global warming on our climate are obvious in terms of rise in sea level, melting of glaciers and rise in average global temperature. The increasing level of CO2 is one of the major causes of the global warming with current concentration level of 406.07 ppm [1]. To save and sustain the global environment, recently, three major initiatives such as 2030 framework, COP21agreement, 2050 roadmap, have been taken to mitigate increasing concentration of CO2 in the atmosphere [2, 3]. In these agreements certain strategies and framework are proposed to deal with rising concentration of CO2 and agreed standard are proposed for future control in the atmospheric CO2. The CO2 mitigation techniques that are proposed in the literature are as follows: first technique is called Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) and the other called Reduction of CO2 to useful products also known as Utilization of CO2 [4, 5].
In first technique, CO2 is captured from the source (power plants, petrochemicals, cement industry, paper mill, and steel mills etc.) using one of the available CO2 captured methods and sequestered to deep sea. However, this method requires huge energy penalty in CO2 compression, cost involved in the compression of CO2 to transport into sea, cost of long distance piping and risk for the marine lives. Because of these drawbacks, CCS still could not be adopted as a commercial process.
In the second available method, the concept of CO2 utilization is adopted. And instead of transporting captured CO2 to deep saline water, it is converted to some useful products such as CH3OH, CO, CH4, and many other useful chemicals by photocatalytic reduction of CO2 with water or hydrogen in the presence of photocatalyst and light.

data.projectName: Participative community-based preventive and promotive strategies to reduce burden of non-communicable diseases
data.projectDigest:
The burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) continues unabated in Pakistan. World bank reported 59% of diseases burden of NCDs resulting in disability and early deaths. The major NCDs include neuropsychiatry 20% and cardiovascular diseases 21%. Approximately 40 million individuals in Pakistan suffer from high blood pressure, 32 million from heart diseases, 8 million from diabetes and about 50 million from mental health disorders. At the current rate, the burden is expected to increase by 10-15% over the next 10 years. NCDs  are amongst the serious rising health issues in Pakistan. The increased prevalence and lack of managing these NCDs pose a challenge to the already overburdened health care system.  
Conversely, the human resources are not well distributed; even the available ones are not trained to manage NCDs at primary level. Evidently, this challenge is a call for active community based participative management strategy.  A set of social and health interventions, including community-led, multi-professional approaches can significantly contribute to decrease the burden of NCDs.  
In this project the utilization of Community based Participative Action Research (CPAR) is proposed. This method provides both transformative community development and research. Participative briefly means active participation from all stakeholders, including the community members.

data.projectName: Design and Fabrication of Supercapattery for Sustainable Energy Storage
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest:
Depletion of non-renewable energy resources is one of the biggest global and local issues. It is highly desirable to find new renewable energy resources preferably green ones to reduce environmental problems at the same time. The extended storage duration and capacity of renewable energy is equally important to effectively utilize such sustainable energy resources. Considering the energy crisis within Pakistan, here we propose to develop novel supercapattery devices that combine the benefits of batteries and supercapacitors. The power density and cyclic life time of such devices are enhanced tremendously compared to the batteries making them suitable to store huge amount of energy for very long time.

data.projectName: Integrating geo-science, engineering and social science for an inclusive hazard assessment and risk mitigation from regional to local scales in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The north Pakistan region is located at the northwestern tip of the world’s most spectacular continental collision, involving the Indo-Pakistani Plate and Asian Plates. The Himalayan-Karakoram-Hindu-Kush (HKH) mountain ranges and Tibetan Plateau are key products of this continental collision. Glaciers and ice fields of the HKH region are considered the world’s ‘third pole’ and provide 70 % of the Indus Basin’s water resources. The (Indus) basin is ranked as the most significant in terms of human dependency, its water resource and agricultural livelihood support over 215 million people, at the transboundary of Afghanistan, Pakistan, India and China. The region is frequently subjected to devastating natural hazards driven by the extreme topography, high rates of tectonic uplift, active denudation, climatic conditions, climate change, and anthropogenic factors. Gilgit-Baltistan (GB) people are highly vulnerable to natural disasters. The GB population suffers from geographic isolation, poverty, food deficiency, insecurity, limited access to transport and information, limited educational opportunities, and sub-optimal infrastructure. Women are particularly vulnerable because they can lack access to education, healthcare, and power in the decision making process. GB residents face a multitude of natural hazards and climate change impacts are increasing the environmental vulnerabilities of these remote mountain communities.

data.projectName: Development of Cultivation technology for nutritionally and pharmaceutically important thermotolerant Agaricus species/strains from Pakistan; A step towards Non-green Revolution
data.projectDigest: Mushrooms (plants of immortality)are among world greatest unexploited resources of beneficial foods and new pharmaceutical products known as the meat of vegetables and “white gold” and their cultivation is a step towards non-green revolution. Agriculture is the key factor for the development of Pakistan. Quality food, health and environment are the major concerns facing our country. Mushroom cultivation helps to address the issue of food insecurity and disposal of wastes. Agaricus (primarily) A. bisporus is the major genus, contributing about 30% of the world’s cultivated mushrooms. Agaricus is probably the most important and potentially cultivatable  and palatable genus, some are delicious and widely consumed and others have considerable medicinal properties . Cultivation of wild and hybrid nutrient rich thermotolerant Agaricus species would not only help to resolve the food insecurity problem in Pakistan but because it is labour intensive it would increase the employment opportunities. Wild species of Agaricus mushrooms represent vast untapped resources which can be exploited directly for commercial markets.
