data.projectName: My White Cane is My Eyes: A Smart White Cane as a Flexible, Scalable, Spatial, and Social Assistant for the Blind People
data.projectDigest:
The WHO reports that approximately 2.2 billion people have vision related issues including blindness which directly affect their social life, health, education, and employment. The most prominent challenges that blind persons face include indoor/outdoor navigation, obstacle detection, localization, signboard detection/interpretation, knowing the social aspect of an environment, gender/age information about the occupants of a place of interest, etc. Simple white-cane has been the most common tool used by blind persons since a long time. The recent technological developments have attempted to bring intelligence into the traditional white-cane. However, blind people need fully workable, low-cost, and socially acceptable products, which unfortunately are not available till date. These solutions are disintegrated, non-scalable, without adaptation to the user/environment, expensive to replicate, expensive to maintain, and ultimately unacceptable to the blind people.
This project aims to design a smart white-cane by augmenting the traditional white-cane with smartphone technology. The proposed solution is aimed to be portable, flexible, scalable, easy to use, easy to adapt to the user needs, and does not overwhelm the user by recommending only suitable items of interest. The proposed solution will assist blind persons in pathfinding, navigation, obstacle detection, social awareness, sign-boards detection, user-system interaction, adaptation & learning, and recommendations.

data.projectName: Applications of Mass Spectrometry for the rapid identification of infectious diseases, and analysis of biomolecules
data.projectDigest:
Major challenge in combating  infectious diseases is the timely identification of the causative microorganism followed by proper antibiotic regime. We propose to coordinate research on antimicrobial resistance in three dimensions: First is the rapid identification of microorganisms present in biological samples by directly targeting them using MALDI biotyping, without needing  time-consuming  culturing methods.  Our fifteen-year experience of biological mass spectrometry has already been extended to MALDI biotyping of environmental and clinical microbial samples in collaboration with Dr Faisal Sultan (CEO, SKMCH&RC, Lhr). 
Secondly, during infections, there are disease-associated-biomolecules released in blood which can serve as a biomarker in that particular disease-condition. Search for biomarkers produced in response to microbial infection, would be carried with Prof M Najam-ul-Haq’s group (BZU, Multan) and identified by MALDI-MS.
Our third domain of research would be with Dr Hafiz Tahir (GCU, Lahore) on novel antimicrobial-agents, isolated from natural sources like venoms of scorpions and silk-worms extracts. Mass spectrometry will greatly help in the identification of these antimicrobial agents which may be effective for pathogens that have developed antimicrobial resistance to classical antibiotics.
The present project hopes to advance knowledge in an important field of antimicrobial resistance and provide improved diagnostic tests.

data.projectName: A blockchain-based technological platform to inspire industrial innovation in Pakistan - (B3iP)
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan is aiming to take the leap towards the next stage of development through advancements in manufacturing, energy, banking, tourism and other services. Successful and effective adoption of emerging technologies has profound role in this.
We propose developing a technological platform to enable national institutions, organizations and SME’s to transform their existing software infrastructures to adopt cutting-edge technological paradigm of distributed ledger technologies exemplified by blockchain. The proposed platform will enable participating organizations to transform their operations specifically with respect to achieving data transparency, integrity, decentralized decision-making process, interconnectivity, ease of data exchange, automation, informed decision, scalability of software systems, traceability in supply chain management and more. The primary focus within this project is on the grand challenge of the adoption of technology in bringing transparency and efficiency in all sectors of critical national importance. The project is envisaged to have significant societal impact as the proposed indigenously developed platform is envisaged to consider specific local challenges of Pakistani society and will develop technology-based solution in order to address them in an effective manner.

data.projectName: Development of chimeric multivalent vaccine to control clostridial infections in food animals
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Conventional preparation of vaccines involving growth of bacteria each time for production of toxoids involves hazards while unwanted elutes of bacterial compromises vaccine efficacy. Use of formalin to inactivate toxins also questions comprehensiveness of vaccine as vaccine’s adverse reactions have been documented. Wider range of known and unknown toxins compromises wholesomeness of meat and other products while millions human patients reported which cannot be ignored. Lack of enough molecular analysis and reluctancy in adoption of cutting-edge techniques put farm economy and food safety in question. Brain, muscle, liver and gut are major organs infected by toxins of clostridial bacteria. Toxins are spore forming with enough resistant potential. It is required to use updated approach involving molecular and biotechnological tools. In current project molecular analysis of clostridial species across the Pakistan will provide ground to develop effective and targeted vaccine. Whole genome sequencing will open new insights into treatment and prevention of clostridial infection in animals and to keep public health safe from its pathogenesis. Production of recombinant chimera peptides from all clostridial species will provide comprehensive and targeted approach to cover effects of clostridial intoxicants.

data.projectName: Food bio-security and bio-surveillance of arthropods and quarantine pests by generating DNA barcode reference library
data.projectDigest: Invasive/alien species pose unprecedented threats to our agro-ecosystems and require vigilant bio-surveillance. Bio-surveillance assists in early detection and effective management of alien invasive species and provides an opportunity for a better decision making on the protection of crop and animal health. It is very difficult to differentiate between invasive and native species due to unavailability of reliable reference data for all native pest species of Pakistan. Moreover, morphological discrimination of many arthropod pests, especially the cryptic species is very hard, laborious and time consuming job. This project will provide the first comprehensive barcode (standardized DNA sequence) records of all native pests from agro-ecosystems of Pakistan. This project will generate the barcode reference database for the arthropod species of Pakistan that will facilitate the species identification quickly and reliably. Sharing of the generated information with world community through BOLD will enable tracking the invasive species and curbing their entry at the border through quarantine. The barcode library will be shared with government institutions so that any invasive species may be detected swiftly and necessary steps may be taken to prevent entry of any alien pest in the country.

data.projectName: Mitigating the menace of Inflammatory Bowel Disease among Pakistani population through utilizing bran, a potential grain by product- an approach towards nutrition, value addition and waste management
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is facing a big challenge regarding food security, nutrition and various health issues. Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is one of the digestive system diseases, may lead to various other Gastro Intestinal Tract (GIT) related problems. It may affect people at any age but mostly affects the young generation, hence it exerts more burden on overall well-being of society. Some treatments of IBD are available i.e. by using medicine and surgery but these might have some health issues and side effects. So there is a dire need to make such value added products from natural food stuff that are not consumed at large scale. Proposed work is planned to develop novel value-added products by utilizing cereal brans to mitigate IBD. We will make cereal brans supplemented chapatti and cereal bran based functional beverages, which then will be subjected to efficacy studies including inflammatory and anti-inflammatory biomarkers, metabolic hormonal profiling, microbiota and gene expression analysis. By the consumption of above mentioned value added bran based products the IBD may be prevented among Pakistani population at large. The utilization of native and modified cereal brans surely a unique approach to tackle this menace. The study/project will be novel in a sense that there is not a single study in Pakistan to mitigate IBD using indigenous food among masses by studying on genetic level. By proposed project we may able to make specialized cereal brans based products for the management of IBD.

data.projectName: Wolbachia as a novel biocontrol agent to block the transmission of mosquito-borne diseases in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Wolbachia is an intracellular endosymbiotic bacterium which occurs naturally in many insect species. In recent decade Wolbachia has got much importance due to its potential of altering host reproductive processes and to suppress indirectly mosquito borne diseases such as dengue, chikungunya, Zika, malaria and West Nile fever etc. Cytoplasmic incompatibility (CI) is an important phenotypic characteristics of Wolbachia which occurs when non-infected females mate with infected males produce no offspring.  Lack of effective vaccine, antiviral drugs and proper vector control activities make it urgent to find the novel alternate approaches for the control of mosquito borne diseases in Pakistan. Our long-term goal is to establish a Wolbachia-based vector control strategy to target local mosquito vectors in Pakistan to eliminate mosquito borne diseases common in Pakistan. Mosquitoes of the three genera Anopheles, Culex and Aedes are the primary vectors for many pathogens and parasites of human and animals found abundantly in Pakistan. Mosquito borne diseases are major public health issues in many tropical countries including Pakistan. Pakistan is currently facing an extreme threat of DENV infections annually, with >4700 human cases including 75 deaths in Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Sindh provinces in 2019. The disease burned caused by Malaria and flaviviruses is a great challenge for the economic development of Pakistan. Current study will investigate the potential of locally isolated different strains of Wolbachia to control mosquito vectors from Pakistan. The Wolbachia based vector control strategies will be cost effective, environment friendly and sustainable in the environment.

data.projectName: Women, Work and Family: Legal Responses to a Changing Social Context
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest:
This project will present new research enumerating the legal status of women’s economic rights in marriage. Focusing on the economics of marriage dissolution in Pakistan, the project will take a mixed-methods multi-disciplinary approach and will chart the extent to which the changing socio-economic position of women in contemporary Pakistan has been reflected in divorce law. Specifically, our quantitative and qualitative work will highlight the economic contexts and consequences of marital instability, while our analysis of the legal framework will provide a detailed understanding of the associated corpus of divorce law in the last three decades, examining the extent of legal recognition of women’s claims to matrimonial property.  

In a context where in spite of women’s increasing financial contributions to domestic economies during their marriages their rights to matrimonial property are not recognized by family law, our work will break new ground, providing new evidence on how familial life is changing in Pakistan. Our careful assessment of the implications of women’s changing socio-economic engagements for their domestic, family and marital lives will help pave the way for a new direction for public policy and legal action on gendered vulnerabilities, labour force participation, family demography. The insights from our project will allow for more focused policy interventions aimed at improving the lives and well-being and securing the livelihoods of women in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Transboundary Atmospheric Passive Sampling Study in South Asia (TAPASSA)
data.projectDigest: South Asia (SA) accounts for over 25% of the world's population. The climate of this region varies from tropical monsoons in the south to temperate in the north. This variation is influenced by altitude, proximity to the sea and monsoonal impact. Ice core records showed the features of pollutants, as good correlations have been found between the pollutant levels in ice strata and air mass trajectories originating from SA. Realizing the carcinogenicity, long-range transport and toxic behaviour of persistent organic pollutants (POPs); surveillance of such important chemicals in the remote regions of Himalayas and glacial lakes, and impact of climate change on the emission patterns of banned chemicals is of prime significance. Notwithstanding its importance for the region, the ice masses of Himalayas have never been studied in detail for the occurrence of important banned chemicals typically legacy persistent organic pollutants viz., organochlorine pesticides (OCPs) and polychlorinated biphenyl (PCBs). The proposed study presents for the first time, regional levels of these chemicals and offers insight on sources, seasonality, accumulation features, long-range transport and risk assessment. This study can be an important tool to evaluate the contribution of SA countries (India, Pakistan, Nepal and Bangladesh) towards “Global POPs Emissions”, and of the effectiveness of control measures by regional/international authorities under the Stockholm Convention in the region.

data.projectName: Smart technologies for precision farming in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest:
In developed countries a lot of research is conducted to introduce automation in the field of agriculture, from crop harvesting to pest/weed detection and spraying systems. These methods increase the production per acre. Targeted and hence minimum use of herbicides is also beneficial for healthier yield and a safer environment. Automated methods are emerging for crop health monitoring of different crops where computers monitor the fields to detect weeds, pests and nutrient deficiency; and enable farmers in targeted spraying. 
There is broad agreement that agricultural productivity in many developing countries need to be enhanced to ensure their national food security. Increase in agricultural yield and farmer’s income is possible via technological improvement and access to improved technologies. 
Current agricultural practices are marked by low productivity in Pakistan. Limited access to technology, lack of productivity enhancement inputs, lack of awareness about best farming practices are few of the major challenges farmers encounter in the country.
In the proposed project, we are planning to develop a system that will utilize state-of-the-art technologies to improve the health of the crop in both vertical and horizontal farming. To monitor the presence of health issues in the crop, different computer vision techniques will be applied to identify the spread and intensity of the problem.

data.projectName: Capitalization of Solar Energy Harvesting by Flexible Polyurethane Encapsulation of Photovoltaic Cells
data.projectDigest: In the quest to meet the energy needs of the growing population, it is fascinating to generate new energy sources. The desperate desire to enhance the energy production has also paved the way to discover various renewable energy resources. The use of hydro-thermal power, wind and solar energies are all the connections to this series. Among all the available energies, solar energy can be supposed as a most credible solution in terms of sustainability, portability, and accessibility, it is not commercially feasible in short term as compared to conventional fuels. The researchers are passionately looking for renewable energy resources as solar devices. However, these solar panels/devices have a direct exposure to sunlight and other environmental conditions. The harsh weather conditions decrease the credibility of these devices. So, inorder to protect the solar panels they should be properly shielded to avoid the attack of foreign factors. The polymerization of low glass transition polymer diols will be carried out to develop the solar panel encapsulations for their extended efficiency and shelf life. The project is an effort to overcome the energy crisis faced by our country, and to ensure a long term solution of the problem.

data.projectName: Towards sustainable aquaculture: Reducing fish and Soyabean meal in aquaculture by using functional feed additives
data.projectDigest: Food security can be defined as access of nutrient rich and safe food require to maintain an active life style. Aquaculture is becoming the fastest growing sector that is capable of providing food security. Economic sustainability is becoming a challenge in aquaculture systems. Fish feed cost are increasing with each passing day and its putting economical pressure on fish farmers around the world. Two main ingredients used in fish feed are fish meal and soyabean meal. High demand, short supply and rising price are becoming the major challenge for food security. Aquafeed manufacturers and aquaculture nutritionists, therefore, trying to look for cheap but high protein alternatives that could reduce the ever growing cost and availability of fish and soybean meal. In order to increase fish production in developing countries, research regarding availability of cheaper high profile protein and energy feedstuffs has become a priority in order to develop low cost feed which must be suitable for use by small-scale fish farmers. Identification of suitable alternative for inclusion in fish feed can reduce the economic pressure on the use of fish meal and soybean meal.

data.projectName: Improving access to safe drinking water using Riverbank/canal bank filtration (RBF/CBF) systems from the Indus River
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest: The challenge inhibiting adopted low-cost Riverbank Filtration (RBF) in Pakistan is the concern of highly polluted waterways serving as source. If it can be proven that water drawn from the Indus River can be safely provided to communities for drinking water, a major drinking water source can be tapped safely and cost effectively. The current proposal outline is developed to improve access to safe drinking water using RBF systems from the Indus River. The proposed study will lead to information and data to facilitate and enable at least 7.92 million people access to safe water, prove technology, and create guidance for analyses and engineering design criteria to enable it being adopted throughout Pakistan. The primary objectives of the proposed study are the following: identification of suitable RBF well-fields and estimation of their capacities, characterization of extracted water quality from the RBF sites, designing of RBF well-fields and costs estimation. The outcome of the study will be presented as a comprehensive temporal and spatial water quality report for the lower Indus and extracted water from RBF systems for five different cities, a report on estimated RBF well-fields capacities, a design protocols report for installation of full-scale RBF systems, and a strategic action plan for installation of RBF systems in collaboration with the implementing agencies. Three Pakistani educational/research institutes (MUET, NED, and CEWRI) and three international experts (University of Utah, and Australia) will be involved.

data.projectName: Wire-Less Smart Cities: An Efficient & Low-Cost Energy Harvesting Solution for Wireless Sensor Nodes in Internet of Things (IoT) based Applications.
data.projectDigest:
Advances in wireless communication and cognitive radio systems widened the use of Internet of Things (IoT) in various fields ranging from electronic health systems to smart cities. Potentially large number of wireless sensor nodes and terminals will be deployed to perform various tasks with limited or no human intervention. IoT based applications have thus recently emerged in environment protection, security systems, smart farming and logistics. In most of these applications, the data nodes or wireless sensors have limitations related to cost, size, and available power supply. The IoT applications utilize battery-powered devices with a limited lifetime. Battery management and maintenance of these sensors can be extremely expensive exercise. Due to the limited lifecycle and with passage of time, batteries will result in dead terminals/nodes, which will affect the performance of an entire network. The energy/power supply problem can be solved by energy harvesting. Specially the harvesting of energy from the natural environment which is abundant and free in the form of light, heat and electromagnetic radiations. 

In this project, a low cost energy harvesting device based on the concept of rectenna will be utilized to solve the energy problems of the wireless sensor nodes for IoT applications.

data.projectName: SENSED: Development of multiplexed smart diagnostic-surveillance tools for mosquito and vector-borne disease control with initial focus on Dengue.
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Mosquitoes are vectors of a wide range of diseases including malaria, chikungunya, and dengue. Mosquito-transmitted diseases (MTDs) kill or debilitate millions of people worldwide annually. Thousands of people in Pakistan get infected with MTDs. Dengue is the fastest emerging disease in Pakistan. Besides death and morbidity there are unsustainable economic costs. Effective management of MTDs is dependent upon an integrated approach involving diagnosis, surveillance of the disease agents and vectors and targeted control of the mosquitoes.  
This project will develop inexpensive yet highly sensitive tools which rapidly identify the different strains of dengue. Nano and artificial intelligence (AI) technologies will be used to develop these new “smart” biosensors. The consortium will also use AI to develop surveillance tools to rapidly identify and quantify mosquitoes. The data will enable health workers to quickly establish dengue hotspots and allow for timely implementation of control measures. To improve monitoring, new lures will be developed based on mosquito attractants. The lures will improve trap capture and will be used to lure mosquitoes to environmentally friendly control agents such as insect-pathogenic fungi.  The goals of this project will be achieved by a consortium consisting of a multidisciplinary team of UK-Pakistan researchers and other pertinent stakeholders.

data.projectName: Multi-modal Fake Content Detection System to ensure responsible Information Dissemination
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: This research aims to develop a multi-modal fake content detection system, capable to detect fabrication in textual, visual and audio contents. During last few years, Pakistan has witnessed a revolution in the way individuals share information, driven by the growing internet connectivity and ease of sharing information via blogs and social media networks. However, the uncontrolled information dissemination has also resulted in spread of fabricated information. Propagation of fake News not only disrupts the authenticity balance of the News industry but also greatly affects individuals and societies as well as the integrity and economy of a country. Fake-News can be spread by a group of people or organizations to serve ulterior motives such as political or financial gains or to damage a country’s public image. Combating fake content has become a growing concern for both the developed and developing economies all over the world. Various countries (e.g. Thailand) and organizations (e.g. EU) have formulated plans to address the issue of disinformation by setting up anti-fake News centers. Pakistan has yet not taken any serious step towards digitizing online information and fighting fake content propagation automatically. The proposed project aims to take the initiative towards digital economy and responsible digital journalism by countering fake contents. The system aims to integrate four systems i.e. textual fake news detection system, image forgery detection system and video and audio tampering detection systems, applied on big data collected from multiple online sources, blogs, social media platforms as well as traditional newspapers. The project further aims to track the actual source of fake content generation and identify the fake content propagators.

data.projectName: Monitoring of Volatile Organic Compounds (2-Butanone and methyl isobutlyl ketone) using Cu-Ni bimetallic alloy nanoparticles based electrochemical sensor
data.projectDigest: Bimetallic alloy nanoparticles of Cu and Ni (Cu-Ni alloy NPs) using a chemical reduction method will be synthesized. Electronic absorption spectroscopy (UV-visible spectroscopy), X-Rays Diffraction Spectroscopy (XRD), Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM), Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) and Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy (EDS) will be used for the characterization of the synthesized nanoparticles. The high crystallinity of Cu-Ni alloy NPs will be evidenced by XRD analysis. Both XRD and TEM analyses will reveal that the nanoparticles’ diameter will be in nanorange. The same techniques will be used for examining morphology of the nanoparticles. Pyrrole will be potentiodynamically polymerized to polypyrrole (PPy) over a well-polished glassy carbon electrode (GCE). Environmental toxins (2-butanone and Methyl isobutyl ketone) which also cause lungs cancer and may irritate the eyes and mucous membranes, and cause weakness, headache, nausea, light headedness, vomiting, dizziness, incoordination, narcosis in humans as well, will be detected by  bimetallic (Cu-Ni) alloy nanoparticles and overoxidized polypyrol modified GCE. The PPy polymer coated electrode will further be modified with different compositions of Cu-Ni alloy NPs. The resultant composite electrode (PPyox/Cu-Ni/GCE) will successfully be applied for environmental toxins, 2-butanone and Methyl Isobutyl ketone with the lowest detection limit.

data.projectName: HaLow Pakistan: AI-enabled Connected Intelligent Transportation System (CITS) and Connected Intelligent Agricultural System (CIAS)
data.projectDigest:
The goal of this project is to expand and integrate shared connected smart services across the country to incorporate Connected Intelligent Transportation System (CITS) model and Connected Intelligent Agriculture System (CIAS) model using an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based information and communication technology (ICT)-driven approach. Pakistan has been part of the international network of fastly growing economies and has been sharing best practices with the developed countries as well, including China and Turkey. Therefore, the intended target project thematic areas of this project proposal are; urban planning (mobility and transportation) and food security (agriculture productivity and resilience) with the use of information technology and telecom (AI, cloud computing, and IoT). Our proposed CITS/CIAS framework goal is a timely next step forward and complements current Pakistan Vision 2025 goals, such as meeting the basic needs of growing population including in particular their access to essential services (public transportation) and protecting natural resources and addressing climate change using smart farming.
One of the goals is to link public transport mobility information with CITS framework to improve mobility, equity, access, safety and affordability for the purpose of reducing the cost of travel and the need to own a vehicle, saving money and time. CITS model can meet multiple transport related goals including eliminating traffic fatalities, reducing emissions and congestion. Likewise, CIAS model can meet various agriculture related goals including eliminating monoculture farming, alarming soil salinization, and to resolve water depletion.

data.projectName: Assessing the viability of forage production through smart micro-irrigation and hydroponic system to improve the livelihood of inherently rain dependent farming community
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Water scarcity in Pakistan is reaching at alarming level especially in rainfed areas. According to a recent report of International Monetary Fund (IMF), Pakistan is 3rd among the countries facing severe water shortage crises. The issue has been worsening by climate change and lack of political interests to resolve the water crises. Therefore, main challenge of today’s agriculture is to develop smart irrigation systems for sustainable forage productivity to improve the livelihood of resource poor farmers. The main objective of this project is to develop resource efficient forage/livestock production system through supplementary efficient irrigation techniques round the year and the value addition of their products for improving livelihood of resource poor farmers of rainfed regions of Pothowar Pakistan. Twenty five farmers field having mini dams will be selected one in each district Attock, Rawalpindi, Chakwal, Jhelum and Mianwali. Fodder crops like maize, sorghum and millets will be sown at each farm. Smart drip irrigation systems with IoT (internet of things) based device to automatize drip irrigation process by analysing soil moisture and climatic conditions like rainfall will be installed at each farm. The fodder produced through this system will be tested for quality. Fodder preservation will be done through silage.

data.projectName: Wind Energy Performance Improvement
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan Vision 2030 envisages plans for taking the renewable energy share in the energy mix of the country to 30% by 2030. However, there are certain factors which can constrain the successful achievement of the plans.
1.	Wind turbine effectively utilization require regular maintenance; i.e. two to three times a year incurring precious downtime and maintenance costs. 
2.	Available wind power can be effectively utilized if forecasted correctly otherwise the intermittent nature of wind power hampers the generation load balance. 
3.	Wind power plants unlike conventional power plants are exempted from system services, i.e. frequency and voltage control thus hinders its large scale integration.
This project will focus on the aforementioned problems by providing an indigenous solution to achieve the 2030 goal. The project will develop Artificial Intelligence (AI) based fault prediction technique to devise algorithms for predicting wind turbine failure and thereby increasing the operating time for wind power plants. The project will also focus on improving wind power forecast by developing artificial intelligence based hybrid models for short term wind power forecast for a wind power plant. Lastly, to increase the wind power integration through simulation studies policy research will be carried out to come up with recommendations and guidelines for devising wind energy specific grid codes which nonexistent till date.
The project will be undertaken by a consortium comprising of various organization UET Peshawar, Durham University UK, Technical University of Denmark (DTU) and Creative Engineering and Management Solutions (CEMS) along with Fauji Fertilizer Company Energy Limited (FFCEL), , Energy Department KPK and world wind energy association Pakistan (WWEA).

data.projectName: Novel scalable technology for the production of nanoscale biomaterials for healthcare
data.projectDigest: The growing demand of nanoscale biomaterials in the field of medicines stimulated the researchers to conduct research and produce materials that can be used as implant materials for biomedical applications in human beings.  Fractures and damaged body parts are major affliction causing dysfunction in body and have always been drawing huge attention of medical science to find the cure. Recently the use of biomaterials in repair, reconstruction, and replacement of diseased body parts has proved vital. Many of the literature methods are not necessarily suitable for manufacturing in developing nations due to the poor availability and low purity of the reagents. Ideally the proposed novel technology design will allow the production of nanoscale biomaterials at low cost by using readily available precursors, to fulfill the need of simplified production methods under mild conditions according to ISO standards [ISO14644]. Potentially there is a big demand and need for this novel technology as a potential bone substitute material for healthcare especially for the developing countries like Pakistan, which experiences natural disasters and has higher accident rates. Thus the process has the potential to offer high purity nanoscale biomaterials on large scale as medical device [Patent pending, UK Patent Application No. 1317747.2]. This research also aims at developing a specialized entrepreneurship and commercialization plan as one of the major outcomes of the project. This will address the local needs in the perspective of the available human resource in health care.

data.projectDigest: Currently, Pakistan is facing two major challenges of waste management and energy shortage. According to Ministry of petroleum 55% of the population has no access to natural gas and alternatively firewood has been used for their energy needs, which resulted in increased deforestation (lost 40% of our forest area just in 15 years) and affected around 16 Million females due to Hazardous Air Pollutants in firewood.  The reason behind is lack of access to cheaper fuel to run their kitchen. Moreover, Pakistan is facing the severe problems of pollution such as smog, huge plastic waste dumps, and most importantly daunting challenge of energy shortfall. According to statistics, Pakistan generates about 48.5 million tons of non-degradable solid waste a year, increasing at the rate of more than 2 percent annually. If the waste is not dealt with priority, it deteriorates the aesthetic looks and causes major health and sanitation problems. Also this resulted in CO2, which is major greenhouse gas. We propose an innovative and advanced solution designed to overcome above mentioned challenges effectively and efficiently. Our aim is to reduce huge piles of plastics and to use this as raw material for energy production by implementing new management and business strategies. The proposed solution involves development of business scale automated and controlled recycling of non-biodegradable plastic waste into liquid petroleum gas (LPG) and Designing of business structure to make this solution practical and self-sustainable.

data.projectName: Carcinogenicity of Smog Particles: A Lahore Based Study
data.projectDigest: Lahore which is famous as City of gardens and now rated as second most polluted city in the world.  Polluted air in the form of smog badly hit the city of Lahore again this year and appeared as a thick blanket of toxic grey smoke in the atmosphere and it was very hard to see few feet beyond in front. This problem of pollution is not distinctive as our neighbor countries are also dealing with this problem. Air pollution increases at high levels in Lahore due to which air quality in Lahore and near surrounding get worse in winter season. Smog season starts from October to February.

data.projectName: Using Artificial Intelligence to Preserve the Heritage of Pakistani Languages
data.projectDigest: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan and each province has its own regional languages such as, Punjabi, Balti, and Pothwari. A majority of Pakistani population cannot properly communicate in English language due to limited literacy, therefore they effectively rely on local languages for effective communication. These users have developed new deformed scripts of local languages for communication, called Roman script. The growing use of these scripts has increased the risk that the original script of these local languages may fade-out in the longer run, hence, losing our heritage and identity. Therefore, it is desirable to preserve these languages in their original scripts. Furthermore, the scarcity of the digital content of local languages has hindered the development of several text mining applications including, hate-speech detection and toxic comments detection. To address these problems, we aim to refine and extend our existing transliteration technique for Urdu language to several local languages. In particular, we aim to generate large amounts of digital contents of local languages in their actual script, develop the necessary fundamental tool sets for local language processing, and resources for machine learning. The contribution will be useful for developing product review systems, chatbots, and questioning answering systems.

data.projectName: Corporate Social Responsibility in higher education institutions: A way forward for Sustainable Development.
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
Many studies have proven that awareness of social responsibilities in corporate sector (CSR) is increasing CSR has emerged or evolved as a significant concept in the modern era. Businesses are rapidly becoming more socially responsible to achieving win-win strategy for the societal change and toward an organization`s overall reputation and performance. Moreover, academia is helping corporate sectors in becoming more and more socially responsible (Lozano, Lukman, Lozano, Huisingh & Lambrechts, 2013; Zilahy & Huisingh2009). 
This project encompasses the CSR concepts and sustainable development related-knowledge among students, faculty, and business managers and the experts will help the participants to understand United Nation`s sustainable development goals guarded in the SD goals agenda 2030. 
Hence, this project is completely aimed at training, educating, and creating awareness among students, academics, managers, and community on the ever-growing importance of CSR and SD to achieve the economic growth and sustainability. 
This project will conduct series of action research workshops and will engage Bachelor, Masters and PhD, Postdoc level students and managers for both qualitative and quantitative data from the Industry to tailor the problems of the society and sustainable development.

data.projectName: Appraisal of Geo-Climatic Evidence for Conservation of Natural Resources: A Framework for 1st Fossil Park/1st Global Geopark and 3rd Man and Biosphere Reserve of Pakistan under UNESCO
data.projectDigest: The protection of natural history resources is one of the goals identified in Pakistan’s National Conservation Strategy and National Biodiversity Strategy Action Plan. The geo-climatic imprints preserved in the fossils provide information to decipher the past and predict the future climate as well as their impact on the ecosystems and biodiversity through modern paleo-geo-ecological techniques and climate modeling methods. This project will be the first of its kind effort in Pakistan which will provide the preservation of past & present natural resource with a systematic record on climatic changes which occurred over the past ~20 million years. Likewise, the project will provide a framework to utilize the potential of this heritage to strengthen the positive image of the country across the globe among the scientific and tourist community. This non-renewable resource requires urgent attention before it is destroyed because of anthropogenic pressure which deprives Pakistan of natural, historical and geo-climatic heritage. Finally, the project will not only meet the grand challenge fund thematic area i.e. Climate change and environment and it will fulfill the commitments of the Government of Pakistan under Multilateral Environmental Agreements, United Nation’s Convention and Treaties by establishing another Man & Biosphere Reserve and or Global Geo-park.

data.projectName: Development, Sustainability and Economic Assessment of Non-Conventional Cash Crops using Brackish Water Irrigation in Desert Environment
data.projectDigest: Thar desert has been in news for children deaths and mass migration of locals owing to food security issues resulting from low rainfall, high summer temperatures and salty underground water. Cultivation of halophytes (i.e. naturally salt tolerant plants) on desert lands with available underground salty water could be a feasible option to eradicate famine. Many examples of halophyte cultivation exist; however, it would be unwise to pick a known species from one part of the world and introduce it elsewhere without assessing its impacts on environment. A better approach would be to utilize native species. This project would develop a sustainable non-conventional cropping system with major focus on fodder production, as the livelihood of Thari people depends on livestock. We will: 1) identify suitable fodder crop(s) for Thar, 2) develop a sustainable cropping system with high yield potential and minimal salinity build-up, 3) maximize yield of newly developed system through molecular and/or microbial approaches, 4) economic assessment of the non-conventional cropping system, and 5) facilitate upliftment of the lives of locals by training and value-added agriculture/livestock. This project will involve many academic (national and international) and sectoral (private sector) partners, who will work together to ensure food security in Thar.

data.projectName: Disease Monitoring and Surveillance System (DMSS)Based on Information Technology
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: In this project we are proposing an IT based surveillance and monitoring system to detect and forecast the occurrence and spread of the Hepatitis B, C across Pakistan.  The broad objectives are: 1.To develop an I.T. based Disease Monitoring and Surveillance System (DMSS) with potential to reduce the current and the future occurrences and the spread of the liver-related diseases especially Hepatitis. 2. To employ an I.T. based Disease Monitoring and Surveillance System (DMSS) to reduce the impact of factors such as current frail primary healthcare set up, improper syringe usage. 3. To use the I.T.based system to reduce the occurrence of undiagnosed Hepatitis cases, delayed diagnosis and its complications; lack of Proper disease documentation and the follow up and lack of vaccination in high risk groups. We are suggesting an IT assisted disease monitoring and surveillance system that will collect the clinical data through IT based data logging system from medical practioners and hospitals on voluntary basis. The tests shall consist of anonymized diagnostics and treatment tests conducted on patients suffering from the liver related diseases. The prevalence of Hepatitis B & C will be extracted from the clinical data of patients suffering from liver diseases. This epidemiology data will then be used to monitor the disease using I.T. based system for the prevalence and the forecast of any possible epidemic in near future.

data.projectName: “Bufflait” Development of a Precision feeding tool for dairy buffalo to improve milk production and reduce nitrogen and methane emission”
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: The Islamic Republic of Pakistan despite the world 4rth largest producer of milk annually imports dry milk and milk related items worth 185.8 million USD (Economic Survey of Pakistan 2018-19). The contribution of buffalo in total milk production of Pakistan represents 60.54% (Economic survey of Pakistan 2018-19). However, the average milk production of buffalo is low i.e. 5.45 kg compared to Holstein cow which is 28.7 kg/ animal per day(FAOSTAT, 2017), mainly because of imbalanced and non-optimized feeding practices. The biggest challenge currently for the dairy industry of Pakistan and world (where ever buffalo farming is done e.g. China and India) is that no calculator exist that can help the feed formulator or farmer to calculate the amount of protein or energy required to precisely produce a given amount of milk. Previously, our research group has already conducted up-to 8 studies on the subject. To expedite the research funds are required to complete the rest of the studies. The project includes 8 studies to see all possible combinations of protein and energy feeding on buffalo milk production response. These studies will be conducted by 3 female and 1 PhD scholars that will be deputed by the Livestock and Dairy Development Department.

data.projectName: Multilingual Speech based Intelligent Service Delivery Framework for Private and Public Sectors of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The latest wave of technological development has ushered in the era of the digital revolution and the possibilities of millions of people connected by mobile devices with enormous computational power, storage capacity and access to information are unlimited. The recent breakthroughs in artificial intelligence, big data, and cloud computing are fuelling the advancement in information and communication technologies. In this project, we aim to develop a multilingual service delivery framework for both the public and private sectors of Pakistan. This will enable small and medium enterprises, government bodies and e-commerce industries to develop innovative applications enabling access to information in the four major languages of Pakistan which account for 81% of the total population. The proposed system will bypass the language, literacy and connectivity barriers and enable access to information using speech interfaces in local languages. A consortium of local and international academic researchers will collaborate in this project to develop the core components of this framework. With the help of the sectoral representatives from Punjab Information Technology Board, Small and Medium Enterprises Association and Pakistan Meteorological Department, multiple applications will be developed to provide e-government, e-commerce and citizen services.

data.projectName: Archaeogeophysics, Aerial Photography and GIS-based Study of the Rehman Dheri Site, Northwest Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Rahman Dheri is a very important archaeological site in the Northwest Pakistan that goes back to 3300 - 1900 BC based on radiocarbon dating. It is the first and earliest proto-urban centre of south Asia with proto-literate elites. Covering 400x600 m area, the site was approximately occupied by 10,000-12,000 people according to archaeologists. The architecture of this city laid the foundation of Indus architecture in south Asia that makes this civilization distinct from the contemporary Egyptian or Mesopotamian civilizations. The sophisticated elite were involved in trade with outside world importing lapis, carnilean, shell and exporting agricultural surplus, ceramics etc. Since it’s too big a site to be excavated completely therefore complete idea of the town planning and architecture using multidimensional and state-of-the-art scientific methods (geophysics, drone geophysics, GIS-remote sensing, and environmental history) will be undertaken. Ways to develop the archaeological predictive modelling, to create insights into settlement patterns and past human behavior and the potential for impact on the community, are all of considerable interest not only to the researcher but also to insurers and reinsurers, land use planners and tourism industry mangers.

data.projectName: Pilot-scale production of green bioplastics and its use in lab plasticwares and household utensils
data.projectDigest: The extensive use, high-level production, rapid disposal, and recalcitrance of synthetic plastics to degradation have resulted in accumulation of plastic particles and microplastics into the aquatic and terrestrial environments. It is estimated that plastics and microplastics persist into environment for 300 to 400 years. On the other hand, biopolymer such as poly-3-hydroxyalkanoates (PHA) are biodegradable and non-toxic thermoplastics and are considered as an ideal substitute of plastics.  In this background, the goal of the present research project is to develop green prototypes of lab plasticwares and household utensils based on PHB and PHBV with desirable thermal, mechanical, and gases/moisture barrier properties without compromising their inherent biodegradability. For this purpose, the pilot scale production of PHB and PHBV will be carried out  in the presence of molasses as a cheap carbon source in the medium by using Bacillus cereus FA11 strain (isolated from TNT-contaminated soil). Physical, thermal, mechanical and gases/moisture barrier properties of these green bioplastics will be investigated. The green bioplastics-based prototypes for lab plasticwares (flasks, Eppendorf, pipette tips) and household utensils (bottles, containers) will be developed and their commercial viability will be evaluated. In addition to this, the effects of pretreatments (gamma irradiation and thermal treatment) and physicochemical parameters on the biodegradation of these green bioplastics-based prototypes and resulting plastic particles will be studied under the controlled lab conditions as well as in field. The interaction studies of these green plastic particles with environmental contaminants (heavy metals) will be examined.

data.projectName: Development and Preservation of Novel Biotechnology for Next Green Revolution
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: To overcome the problem of hazardous effects of agrochemicals in agriculture, the need of time is the calls for next green revolution for a sustainable ecosystem. In this regard plant beneficial microbes have been considered one of the best options for growth and bio control. Various collections of indigenous bacteria are used as biotechnology, particularly for cereals but less emphasis is given to formulate host-specific Rhizobium biofertilizer for legumes. The quality of available inoculants can be maintained through systematic screening and identification based on molecular tagging of 16Sr RNA. Keeping in view this challenging research is designed to isolate potential bacteria from cereals soil and legumes nodules. The isolates will be screened for agronomically useful traits including N2-fixation, ACC-deaminase, P-solubilization and phytohormones (IAA) synthesis, antibiotic resistance, siderophore production, antagonistic activity and biochemical characterization. The strains with potential PGP traits will be identified by 16S rRNA and housekeeping genes (atpD, recA, rpoB, glnII, gyrB) sequencing. We are expecting many novel candidate for development of agricultural biotechnology through this project.  The novel taxa will be validated using chemotaxonomic analysis (collaboration with CAAS, China) and the potential candidates will be tested under controlled and field adaptability.  A gene bank will be developed to preserve bacterial strains. The national data base (web portal) will be developed for filing and registration of strains making them easily accessible. Identified bio resource will be available for academia, research and industrial usage and will be a source of income generation for host institute.

data.projectName: Development of Material Recovery Facility (MRF) for Effective Solid Waste Management
data.projectDigest: Management of large quantities of solid waste generated from domestic, commercial and industrial activities has become a global issue particularly for metropolitan cities. Currently, the solid waste is placed or dumped in the open lands which causes many public health issues like odor, leaching of pollutants to the ground water, attraction of rodents and insects, generation of diseases etc. Therefore, there is a need to apply effective solid waste management strategies particularly in urban areas. Extraction of the recyclables and their reutilization provides promising solution for the sustainability of the modern cities. Under this concept, Material Recovery Facilities (MRFs) act as a solid waste processing plant in which the solid waste is processed for the extraction of recyclables and useful products. In the present research project, a pilot scale Material Recovery Facility (MRF) for solid waste will be developed at the University of Agriculture, Faisalabad. This consists of different components, i.e. Dropoff unit, Sortation Unit, RDF Unit, Composting Unit etc. The products of the MRF plant will recyclables, RDF fuel pallets and Compost Pallets which will be commercialize among the stakeholders. In this way, the proposed technology will result in a sustainable solution for the effective solid waste management.

data.projectName: Sustainable management of agricultural waste to reduce environmental pollution (smog) and cascading bioenergy system
data.projectDigest: In developing countries such as Pakistan, open burning of agricultural waste specifically rice husk and straw in the field is a common practice. Such practices create a plume of smoke which in combination with other pollutants form smog. This smog has deleterious health effect on human health as well as on the environment and overall biodiversity. The aim of this project is to introduce progressive technological solutions to devising sustainable ways to reduce the open burning of crop residue by promoting degradation of organic matter with the help of microorganisms and other additives in anaerobic digestion process and generate alternative forms of bioenergy. This project will cover two priority thematic areas, one is to address climate change and environment, such as to develop pollution (i-e Lahore smog) reduction technologies, and second is sustainable energy production. The outcomes of the project will not only reduce the smog problem but also major products (such as biochar, biogas and valuable nutrients) of anaerobic digestion will be usable as alternative resources. In this pilot study, agricultural waste from various crops will be collected, and different digestion experiments will be conducted to evaluate the quality of each product. Utilization of by-product and evaluation of feedstock quality for the isolation of valuable nutrients with the help of international collaborator will be adopted an effective approach. All the collaborator of this project will provide project implementation insight, utilization of available research facilities at their respective institutes and will help in the dissemination of products of the project.

This project will cover two priority thematic areas, one is to address climate change and environment, such as to develop pollution (i-e Lahore smog) reduction technologies, and second is sustainable energy production. The outcomes of the project will not only reduce the smog problem but also major products (such as biochar, biogas and valuable nutrients) of anaerobic digestion will be usable as alternative resources. In this pilot study, agricultural waste from various crops will be collected, and different digestion experiments will be conducted to evaluate the quality of each product. Utilization of by-product and evaluation of feedstock quality for the isolation of valuable nutrients with the help of international collaborator will be adopted an effective approach. All the collaborator of this project will provide project implementation insight, utilization of available research facilities at their respective institutes and will help in the dissemination of products of the project.

data.projectName: STUDY VARIOUS TECHNIQUES OF RENNET PRODUCTION FOR CHEESE MANUFACTURING INDUSTRY AND ITS COMMERCIALIZATION
data.projectDigest:
Out of natural foods chees is the most preferred food worldwide. The quality and characteristic zest of chees depends on rennet produced by calf’s abomasum. For making chees rennet was extracted by slaughtering young milk feeder calves but with the growing demand of chees and advancement of research rennet or similar products were made from various plants, fungai and bacteria. In the recent years, rennet is the most important export commodity of various countries of the world. In the current economic crisis of the country, rennet is an important export commodity. If produced in the country Pakistan can not only save thousands of dollars costing import rather be part of rennet exporting countries.
In the current project the rennet will be made traditionally and through modern methods in first phase using three each of buffalo, cattle calves and sheep and goat kids precured before weaning age. The collected rennet will be stored for future cheese making and quality evaluation as control to compare quality of cheese made with other sources.  
In the second phase "vegetable rennet" will be made from one of several plants (thistle, nettle, fig, Galium, dried caper leaves, nettles, thistles, mallow, and ground ivy, extract from and mallow, to name a few), or "microbial rennet" acquired from mold Rhizomucor miehei also termed as kosher and halal cheeses. Moreover, work will also be done on nonrennet coagulation.
In the third phase Fermentation-produced chymosin will be worked out in the lab using genetic engineering to isolate rennet genes from animals and introducing them into certain bacteria, fungi, or yeasts to make them produce chymosin during fermentation.  All the products made in the lab will be prepared in bulk and commercialized through ghazi brothers, Pakistan.

A successful demonstration of self-driving vehicle, development of the softwares used in it,  development of cheap sensors, development of general purpose driving control kits are aimed in this project. The technology transfer is a discernible prevision visible from the pedestal of this project.

data.projectName: Development of Indigenous Cancer Model and Therapeutic strategies: From Bench to bedside Studies
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest:
The geostrategic and socio-economic location of Pakistan plays an important role in the overall development of various sectors in the sub-continent i.e., economics, health, education and quality of life of general population. According to the recent collected data from different cancer hospitals located in different cities all over the Pakistan, it has been noticed that head & neck and lung cancers are the most dominant among male population while breast and cervical cancers are the most dominant in female population .  Currently more than 18 cancer hospitals are dedicated to diagnosis and therapy of this deadly disease. The modes of treatment are conventional and based on chemo or radio-therapeutic approaches . 
Rational
Major issue in dealing with patients bearing cancer is the diagnosis in later stages wherein the cancer is most of the time aggressive and metastatic in nature. It is very difficult to deal such cases with conventional approaches.  
Objective
Therefore, a dire need is felt for establishment of a center for bench to bedside translational studies based on utilization of relatively new and state-of-the-arts approaches for diagnosis and treatment of cancers. Unfortunately, there is no single in-vivo cancer model exist in Pakistan which is a vital component for assessment and evaluation of any therapeutic and diagnostic methodologies. 
The proposed project will be executed in two Phases

data.projectName: Strategic development of bioenergy supply chains: Moving towards a cleaner mix
data.projectDigest: Addressing an energy gap with a weak economy can pose a significant challenge for a developing country. A gradual and strategic development of a sustainable bioenergy system in this situation may well provide an opportunity to alleviate the connected energy and economy issues. Bioenergy systems have gained importance due to the growing energy demand and the environmental concerns of the conventional energy production. Recently, the modelling of biomass supply chains has also received a significant attention from researchers highlighting the importance of the role of logistics in the viability of bioenergy systems. Focusing on the policy dimension, we will present an optimization model to dynamically design a cost-effective and sustainable bioenergy supply chain with the objective to reduce the energy gap and increase the renewable energy share in the national energy-mix over time. Unlike the existent research, the model will take a more holistic view by considering electricity distribution and managing the trade-off between the costs of biomass/biofuel transportation and transmission loss. The model will be extensively analysed to generate policy recommendations focusing on Pakistan, a naturally resourceful but energy starved country.

data.projectName: Internet of Things (IoT) Forensics
data.projectDigest:
The recent technological advancement such as the emergence of IoT has brought ease to the lives of mankind however it has also amplified the scope of cyber-security across multidisciplinary domains. The concept of cyber-security in today's world now has broader horizon that spans not only the information security, network security and application security, rather it also include the security of devices in cyber physical systems and the multi-prong security strategies to deal with latent data breaches of IoT devices as well as their users. Moreover, the latest security inquires propose that most organizations have unprotected information and insecure cyber-security rehearses set up, making them defenseless against loss of data. 
Most of the hype around IoT has been on its applications, privacy or implementing basic security features, however very less attention has been given to incident response and forensic investigations. IoT forensics is a branch of digital forensics which deals with IoT related cybercrime. Practical application of such frameworks is found to be rare. For this very reason, the need for an intelligent, adaptable forensics methodology to investigate IoT-related crimes is becoming pertinent.
By incorporating modern tools and techniques we can form a structure that results in smooth investigation process. Furthermore the extraction of relevant data from IoT devices that is useful for investigations is a complex task. Specifically, implementation of a complete forensic investigation framework for home automation systems or industrial automation applications will propagate safety and reliability of devices.

data.projectName: Mechanical waves to protect crops from insects: an eco-friendly solution against locust attack
data.projectDigest: The introduction of pesticides greatly enhanced the economic potential of farmers in terms of exponential increase in per acre output of crop and fibre. Apart from agriculture sector, pesticides have also played a significant role in amelioration of vector-borne diseases. However, the increased usage of pesticides also resulted in very serious health related concerns to consumers and the environment. In our present proposed project, jointly run by the team of Engineers & Entomologist, we will utilize mechanical waves to repel the insects away from agriculture field. The system generating mechanical waves in the agriculture field will be such oriented that the waves are contained within the field so that no adverse impacts are translated to the human health. The system will not only be environmental-friendly but also much more economical than the pesticides. Moreover, since the system is made indigenously, it will therefore save a lot of foreign reserves. To our knowledge there is no such machine in the market that allows the usage of mechanical waves to repel the insecticides. Conclusively, this mechanism will have a great market value.

data.projectName: Supercomputing &Artificial Intelligence Center of Excellence
data.projectDigest:
we propose a Supercomputing & Artificial Intelligence Center of Excellence which merges
the artificial intelligence and High-Performance Computing systems to utilize big data. This project
proposes the development of hardware/software solutions for applications that demand intelligence
using deep learning approaches. At the heart of our hardware solution is a low-cost compute node,
which we call as “server”. This server uses heterogeneous processing cores including Central Processing
Unit (CPU), Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) and Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA). These servers can
be combined to form a centralized or decentralized cluster. By integrating several of these clusters
develops a supercomputer. Thus, offering a high-performance computing platform that scales with the
remote processing needs and financial budget. An implication of this centralized and decentralized
supercomputing solution is the support scalable performance to the AI algorithm by providing AI
frameworks. As such, we also propose an “AI Programming Framework” that execute AI tasks on the
servers of a single or various cluster located in centralized or decentralized locations.

data.projectName: YEAST PRODUCTION FOR DAIRY INDUSTRY
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Livestock and poultry are important sub-sectors of agriculture in Pakistan.  Both are source of animal protein for the growing population of the country. Presently Pakistan is facing great challenge of food security as there is a gap between demand and supply of food product of animal origin. Feed is an important requirement of food animal which accounts for about 70 % of total cost of production. Commercially available imported yeast is supplemented in animal feeds. It has several nutritional and health benefit. Yeast produces many important fermentation metabolites such as protein, carbohydrates, high potency vitamins and different types of important minerals and enzymes that makes it useful and highly nutritive feed supplement for food animals. Keeping in view the importance of yeast for dairy and poultry industry, this research study is designed on development and evaluation of indigenous yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Dietary supplementation with locally isolated strain of Saccharomyces cerevisiae is a viable and cost effective method to improve the animal health status & efficiency of production, and reduce the cost of animal production. This will help to combat the challenge of the food security and improve the economy of the country.

data.projectName: Smart, internet of things  based, self powered system for pipeline monitoring
data.projectDigest: Petroleum, natural gas and water reserves play an important role in country’s development. Usually, these resources are transported from production locations through pipeline-network that is vastly spread and passes through remote areas where manual monitoring is infeasible. A minute pipeline’s leakage can cause huge financial loses and also attribute to environmental hazard. For safe and efficient operation of pipeline, a sensing and monitoring system is required. Monitoring systems are developed for inspection; however, these are mostly non-continuous, required man power and limited to specific area. Moreover, operation of monitoring systems highly depend on life-limited battery, however, replacement of batteries in remote environment is not easy. Due to advancements in the field of ultra-low-power electronics, wireless communication, sensors and energy harvesting, a smart, internet-of-things based, self-powered monitoring system for pipeline is now viable. The project objective is to develop a monitoring system that can remotely sense the pipeline’s (pressure, discharge, velocity, temperature and vibration) and send data (through RF, GSM, Bluetooth) to main server, from where the information is accessible through internet. Furthermore, an energy harvester is integrated with the devised system to make it self-powered. For harvesting solar and fluid-flow energies are utilized to produce power for monitoring system operation.

data.projectName: AI-based enhanced diagnostic potential of MRI for molecular histopathology of brain tumors to improve cost-efficacy and reliability in diagnosis and prognostication in a resource constrained setting of an LMIC.
data.projectDigest: This proposal is about using artificial intelligence and telecommunication to improve the outcome of brain tumors in Pakistan. Gliomas are fatal brain tumors which affect many people. Their management usually includes MRI imaging followed by surgery and then radiation and chemotherapy. The process of diagnosis can be expensive and time-consuming due to lack of resources. To make this process cost-effective, reliable and quick, we want to develop a software which will be trained by using brain scans, clinical data and genetic information. Eventually, it will be able to provide histopathological information on tumor type and predict outcome by simply analyzing MRI details. A telehealth mobile application will also be developed to effectively follow patients living in remote areas. This project will be unique because it will combine the use of 3G/4G technology, Bioinformatics and Artificial Intelligence to enhance the capacity and efficiency of local healthcare set-ups in managing brain tumors. The project will be innovative because it will correlate computer-based analysis of imaging data with genomic and other biochemical alterations. Research on unique genetic features as part of this project will pave the way to brain tumor detection through blood samples (liquid biopsy).

data.projectName: Investigating the Shelter less in Karachi:  Towards sustainable housing solutions
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
The shelter less avail various options to dwell in large cities. These options are mostly informal and adopted in the absence of affordable formal shelter. Attempting to exercise their right to the city, these people muddle through the various urban locations in cities to identify possibilities to dwell and build a life. In Karachi, such informal dwelling is a visible phenomenon in a wide range of spatial options. Shelter less use these locations as dwelling spaces and continue to struggle against the various challenges.
This research documents and analyses the status of shelter less in Karachi. Using silent observations, pre-interview networking and semi structured interviews of key stakeholders as the key research methods, in several locations in the six districts that comprise Karachi. The research investigates the reasons as to why people adopt such an option; range of experiences faced by them, predicaments and emerging possibilities for shelter for the homeless taking on board local NGOs and international advisors.

data.projectName: Net zero buildings for Sustainable Energy Future
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest:
The power sector of Pakistan has already accumulated a circular debt of 1.7 trillion PKR (about 10 billion USD - end of December 2019) which is over 3% of the country’s GDP. So, instead of larger new central generation owned/operated or dealt by the Govt., it is beneficial to incentivize domestic consumers and home owners to make their own renewable investment which will be cost effective (lack of Govt. involvement and sovereign guarantees), efficient (minimum distribution losses) and cleaner (reliance on solar with reliable storage). This is where government liabilities will reduce and the power sector must focus on maintaining the exiting network. 

So, in this work, we propose complete paradigm shift in electricity generation i.e., generation, management and optimization at your own rooftop at half a price to that of the grid!  Essentially, the proposed initiative/project will enable net zero buildings/homes (self-sufficient from electricity purposes) and will result in ensuring four critical aspect of our energy future, i.e., Environmental Sustainability,   Energy Efficiency, Economic viability, and a Policy shift on decentralized  power generation. All 4 major challenges are addressed through his work and is in line with global trends towards decentralization of power/energy.

data.projectName: Establishment of an Indegenious Cyber Range for Cybersecurity
data.projectDigest: This proposal aims to improve the cybersecurity situation in Pakistan by establishing a center of excellence of cybersecurity comprising three wings, The Research and development wing, The Human resource development wing and The Consultancy wing. The Research and development wing will consist of a number of cybersecurity teams, each working on a specific security research problem. Along with the commercialization of tools (both hardware and software), establishment of a cyber-range, both of which being the product of Research and Development Wing of the proposed center, this project focuses heavily on capacity building in the field of cybersecurity by proposing an establishment of a workforce development wing. The Workforce development wing will focus solely on the development of a knowledge-based workforce. The consultancy wing (the third wing of the proposed center) will commercialize the solutions developed by the Research and the Development Wing. Overall the goal of this project is to develop an ecosystem in which highly trained people, foolproof procedures and cutting-edge technology required for maintaining a superb security posture, could be produced locally at a cheaper cost that not only caters to the local needs but could also be exported.

data.projectName: Reconstructing gender amongst school-age children: A pathway to women empowerment in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
The project aimed to progress towards gender equality by promoting equal relationships, critical analysis of social norms, redefining gender roles and responsibilities, and examining the occurrence of gender-based violence in the society. The project will focus on curricular and co-curricular activities, role plays, field projects, and games for this purpose. It is expected that through the project, students will become more supportive of women empowerment in Pakistan.
The project will be carried out in five phases. The attitudes, knowledge and practices of students and teachers at the primary, middle secondary level will be assessed in all the provinces of Pakistan. Based on the baseline, teacher training modules will be developed and training will be given to teachers across Pakistan. The End line phase will measure the impact of the teacher training on the beliefs and behaviors of students at the primary, middle and secondary levels. The project will also include the perceptions of various stakeholders regarding gender sensitization among youth and overcoming barriers to women empowerment in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Nanobased biodegradable plastics for packaging
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Plastic waste treatment is one of the top-list challenges to environmental protection. Among hard and soft plastics, food packaging materials are discarded in massive amount of plastic on daily basis in each and every corner of the world. These nondegradable pollutant has emerged as microplastic threat to both terrestrial and marine life. Moreover release of Bisphenol A, a potent carcinogen, has diverted the attention for the plastic alternatives. Among bioplastics polylactic acid had gained much importance because of its possible production from agriculture waste as well as degradation through natural process. However like other bioplastics it has inherent shortcomings such as weak mechanical properties, narrow processing windows, and thermal properties. Nanotechnology offers broad functional and chemical structures that can help to attain target performance and functionality to the material they are incorporated. Nano-based PLA composites are comprised of biopolymer matrices with incorporated organic or inorganic nanoparticles which can impart reinforcement or functionalization to PLA. This study is aimed to produce lactic acid from agriculture waste such as wheat Bran through fermentation and its chemical conversion to PLA. Inorganic nanoparticles will be incorporated into the produced polymer and the resulting composites will be analyzed for their physical, chemical, mechanical and degradation properties.

data.projectName: EMPLOYMENT, LITERACY AND LIFE SKILLS SURVEY
data.projectDigest:
Mismatch between supply and demand of educated graduates in any profession is problematic not only for students but also for the government and economy as a whole. If number of graduates in any profession is more than market capacity, some of them will not find job, and some other will have to work against a job which is not matching with their skills. As a result, lifetime efforts of the graduates on education will not be fully fruitful. On the other hand, if there is shortage of educated people in any subject, the provision of relevant services will be affected. Therefore, it is very important to investigate the mismatch between demand and supply of skilled graduates in different professions. 
This study is aimed to extend the coverage and scope of survey of skill mismatch indicators by extending the survey to the household level, so that the information from unemployed, self-employed and overseas employed people could be added. The survey will calculate the indicators including labor force, employment, lag between completing education and getting job, duration of frictional unemployment with reference to the area of specialization of the respondents and their family members.
