data.projectName: Climate Change Vulnerability  assessment & adaptation to water & soil Conservation in Northern Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is among 10 countries affected most by climate change, according to the 2018 Global Climate Risk Index rel. Under future climate change scenarios, Pakistan is expected to experience increased variability of river flows due to increased variability of precipitation and the melting of glaciers. Demand for irrigation water may increase due to higher evaporation rates. Yields of wheat and rice are expected to decline. Water availability for hydropower generation may decline. The small farming and communities living in Northern areas whose  subsistence is mainly agriculture or forest products are expected to face the hazards of climate change more due to limited water availability and declining soil fertility coupled with soil loss. These communities need to be capacitated with the various adaptation tools for sustainable livelihood and to cope with the effects of climate change. The proposed project will focus on indigenous communities living in North of the country directly depending on water in streams and rivers from glacier melt for drinking, and agriculture needs. Following a systematic approach for community vulnerability assessment, this proposed study will first evaluate the scientific evidence of climate change in Northern Pakistan then it will relate this evidence to the visible impacts on local vulnerable communities. After which it will design and test adaptation tools for water and soil conservation. Successful implementation of the adaptation tools can be replicated in other parts of the country and be useful for informed policy decisions.

data.projectName: Artificial Intelligence based smart solutions for population screening, detection and diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer)  in hepatitis B virus and hepatitis C virus patients
data.projectDigest: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the leading causes of cancer-related deaths worldwide. Pakistan is amongst few countries in the world where hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) are endemic. Around 87% of the HCC caused in Pakistan is associated with HBV (22%) and HCV (65%). We identified two main gaps in the current hepatitis care: (1) there is no hepatitis registry in the country and the data is not analyzable at patient level (2) 98% of HCC is diagnosed by ultrasound and confirmed by a CT scan, but high level expertise in radiology are required to diagnose HCC and trained radiologists are very few in number. This proposal aims to address the above-mentioned gaps in one of the biggest national public health challenges. We are going to develop a digital hepatitis cloud-based database linked with blood banks, primary, secondary and tertiary healthcare facilities at both public and private sector. Based on blood tests, ultrasound and CTscan confirmed high quality data of hepatitis patients, a computer-assisted diagnostic software will be developed both for the assessment of ultrasound and CT images together with associated ICT based solution i.e. picture archiving and communication system (PACS) for further potential analyses.

data.projectName: Development of climate smart cotton resistant to biotic and abiotic stresses
data.projectDigest: The drastic climatic changes as a result of human activities disrupts the ambient temperature, rainfall pattern, sunshine intensity ultimately leads increased biotic and abiotic stresses like Virus attack, verticillium wilt disaster, drought, salinity and water logging which negatively influence yield and quality of crop plants and pose a huge threat to food security. The sudden decline in yield of important crop plant cotton resulted in increased import exerting pressure on economy of Pakistan. Climate-smart agriculture can minimize problems and lower negative impact of climate variations on crop adaptation. The quest to deal with major biotic stresses (Whitefly, CLCuV and verticillium wilt) and abiotic stress (drought) have led to utilization of advanced biotechnological approaches like gene identification its overexpression in crop plant and genome editing by using CRISPR Cas system. The phenolic monoterpenoids thymol and carvacrol produced in plants Oliveriadecumbens were found to have insecticidal activity and were observed as major repellent of insects. Genome editing by using CRISPR Cas system by targeting beta satellite and DNA A of cotton virus along with targeting ATP carrier protein gene, 14-3-3ia (14-3-3ia) mRNA of Verticillium dahlia and alcohol dehydrogenase gene of cotton to make it drought tolerant looks promising to be addressed.

data.projectName: Development of the green performance index for incubators and the green incubation learning program for young aspirants: A holistic framework for sustainable incubation
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Researchers claim that business incubators and their tenants i.e. incubated companies have an impact on the environment, and they shall incorporate green initiatives to respond to environmental concerns. Therefore, it is imperative to assess the incubators’ green performance as young generations particularly millennials expect more than just material rewards from their employers and desire to work for an organization that also concerns and cares about the environment. This research will first assess the graduate’s perception and preferences for business incubators with higher green performance. Second, this research will design a framework to evaluate the green performance of incubators and based upon which an index for the green performance of incubators will be developed. Third, this research will assess and classify the incubators’ green performance based on the developed index. Fourth, this research will design an integrated learning program for the young aspirants to provide in-depth exposure to green incubation. Lastly, this research will develop and provide training to future entrepreneurs to establish green ventures and nurture green values among existing ventures. To achieve the objectives of this research, it will be carried out in several phases using a multi-staged mixed-method approach. This research has both practical and theoretical novelty and contributions.

data.projectName: Discovery and design of fast-charging and long-life Li-ion battery materials for automotive applications
data.projectDigest: Recent boom in electric vehicle industry around the world is triggered by rapidly growing research and development efforts in Li-ion battery technology.  The rise of electric vehicles is certainly going to reduce the demand of conventional hydrocarbon fuels and eventually curb emissions of greenhouse gases in our country. We propose to establish a vigorous research program at COMSATS University Islamabad (CUI) to accelerate the discovery of novel and innovative cheap materials for fast-charging and long-life Li-ion battery technology, especially for automotive applications. This program will bring together collaborators from world’s leading research groups in academia and industry in United States and France.  So any innovation or research effort in battery technology from discovery and design to prototyping will be complemented and supported by our collaborators at University of Central Florida USA, University of California Berkeley USA, Sorbonne University France, and at car industry as Mercedes-Benz North America. The expertise and knowledge of our collaborators will give us enormous leverage in pushing us to forefront of this field. The broad objectives of this project are based on 1) developing a complete atomic scale understanding of electrochemical mechanisms at electrode-electrolyte interfaces, 2) designing and testing better electrolytes aiding fast ionic transport, 3) designing and testing better electrodes supporting smooth and fast Li-intercalation and de-intercalation. Our main goal is to provide a complete road map from machine learning based computational design of battery materials to their practical prototyping in the form of a fast-charging and long-life battery with safe and stable electrochemistry.

data.projectName: APPLICATION OF CRISPR/CAS9 TO CONTROL COTTON LEAF CURL DISEASE (CLCUD) COMPLEX
data.projectDigest:
Cotton leaf curl disease (CLCuD) is a major threat to cotton productivity, worldwide. In Indo-Pak subcontinent CLCuD has been characterized by at least five different species belonging to the genus Begomovirus (family, Geminiviridae), associated with DNA-satellites called betasatellite and alphasatellite. 
The previous resistance strategies were provides resistance for short time. The proposed research project would target all species of CLCuD-associated begomoviruses (CABs) and their associated DNA-satellites, simultaneously to confer a broad-spectrum resistance in cotton crop through a very recent CRISPR-Cas mediated approach. Using this advanced technique CLCuD resistant commercial variety will be developed using sectorial cotton breeding program.

data.projectName: Development of novel plant based food preservatives and biopesticide for stored food items.
data.projectDigest:
Numerous compounds present in the plants possess the antimicrobial capabilities against the pathogenic microorganisms. Spoilage of food by bacteria, fungi and pests is a terrifying alarm for the fitness of human health. Control of food spoilage by use of chemical preservatives causes adverse effects and emergence of resistance among the food spoilage microorganisms/pests. Main objective of this project is the development and utilization of natural plant based food preservatives for food security purposes which will not only increase the shelf life of food products but also helpful to control the bacteria and fungi associated with various food borne diseases. 
Antimicrobial potential of the plant extract will be assessed against pathogenic bacterial strains. Active phytochemical constituents of this plant could be used cost effectively as an alternative to chemical preservatives for control of food spoilage.

data.projectName: Prototype development of concentrated solar power plant integrated with membrane distillation system
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest: Freshwater is an essential component for life, and its demand is increasing worldwide as the population continues to grow. Although 75% of the earth’s surface is covered with water; however, a large portion of the water is saline. The salinity of seawater can be reduced by desalination. There are several desalination technologies; however, membrane distillation (MD) is one of the emerging desalination technologies. The direct contact membrane distillation (DCMD)  is one of the most used configurations of MD. Recently, MD has attained great attention worldwide due to several advantages such as low temperature and pressure operation. It is important to mention that the application of the MD system includes seawater desalination, brine concentration, wastewater treatment, non-food chemical processes, and in the food industry. Desalination powered by renewable energy sources is considered to be a very promising way to cope with the growing demand of freshwater and corresponding energy requirements while mitigating environmental pollution. Particularly, Pakistan is currently facing severe energy and freshwater crises. Therefore, this project aims to develop a prototype of concentrated solar power (CSP) plant integrated with direct contact membrane distillation (DCMD) system for energy and fresh water production, respectively.

data.projectName: Formulation development and Therapeutic Trials of a Natural Contraceptive
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The long term use of contraceptives in females has been linked with high risk of developing breast cancer especially between age of 20-50 years; the females using contraceptives below the age of 20 years magnify the risk up to >twenty folds. Keeping in view this situation, it was decided to focus on development of a dosage form as natural contraceptive from Neem oil, that would suffice the need of contraception among women without or minimal adverse effects. First of all, an emulgel dosage form will be prepared from the Neem oil which will undergo various testing in order to pass the quality control. The product will also be subjected to stability testing also, to assess its shelf life. Meanwhile, mice will be used for experimentation in various groups for testing the product. After this, the stable product will be proceeded for clinical trials under the supervision of expert gynecologist at the Hospital where the women will be screened and enrolled for this project, after taking their informed consent. The participants will be compared with those who would be using the conventional contraceptives. The data will be collected on a pre-specified format and analyzed via SPSS software by the help of an expert statistician.

data.projectName: Screening cotton germplasm for drought and/or heat stress tolerance
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: Heat and drought stress are serious challenges resulting in reduced crop yields and enormous economic losses. Due to climate change worldwide, Pakistan is seriously suffering from heat and drought stress, which affect all major crops including cotton. Thus, development of plants with better water use efficiency and/or tolerant to higher temperature is important to mitigate the damages caused by drought and/or heat stress. We propose to develop drought and/or heat stress tolerant cotton plants to address grand challenges faced by cotton growers in Pakistan. We will establish an automated plant phenotype analysis screening system, which will develop and screen a mutant pool of cotton germplasm for abiotic stress tolerance based on leaf temperature. Stomatal opening regulates water loss through stomata and altered stomatal opening is indirectly a measure of leaf temperature. Plants that transpire more water appear “cool” and are generally tolerant to heat stress. On the other hand, the plants that transpire less water look “hot” and are tolerant to drought stress as they utilize less water. Developing a mutant collection of cotton by chemical treatment such as ethyl methane sulfonate (EMS, C3H8SO3) and screening a large number of plants based on leaf temperature would help us to screen plants tolerant to drought and/or heat stress. Next generation sequencing and/or TILLING would help us to identify the genes regulating leaf temperature in cotton. Molecular analysis will be performed to elucidate the mechanisms governing drought and/or heat stress in cotton. Solutions to this grand challenge will indeed provide a base to breed drought and/or heat stress tolerant cotton plants in particular and will facilitate such efforts for other cash crops in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Artificial Intelligence based Cardiovascular Diagnostics using Electrocardiogram (ECG) Data Banks
data.projectDigest: This proposal focuses on how computer-based decision making procedures, under the broad umbrella of artificial intelligence (AI), can assist in improving health sectors. The main objective of this proposal is to acquire the indigenous capacity to early diagnose the heart related diseases within the Pakistani population. Particular focus is the coronary artery diseases. The innovation of this proposal is that the ECG data if processed by the AI algorithm has a capability to predict (with appreciable accuracy) the diseased state or the future chance of the disease occurrence. The prediction of the heart disease with ECG alone is otherwise not possible. However, the AI algorithm has a capability to sense the minor changes in the ElectroCardioGram given that the input ECG data is massive to yield significant confidence of the prediction. The proposal will include components of various AI applications in the areas of heart related disorders. The significance of this project is that it will be a non-invasive procedure to diagnose the heart related disorders via ECG alone. The applications of this AI algorithm will encompass the service to the scientific research, academic training, and as well as it serves as the local hub of the big data center.

data.projectName: Design and development of Telemedicine software application for diagnostic of respiratory pathology disorder and its  severity level
data.projectDigest: IIn this work focus is to developing a Telemedicine software application that can diagnose disorder in patients related to respiratory pathology.  In addition, focus of this study also will be to identify severity level of patients suffering from respiratory related disease. The segregation of patients related to pathology and further severity levels will be identified by physician.  Respiratory sounds and other data related to diagnostics patients will be obtained from hospital. Respiratory sounds and flow rate of sounds will be collected using digital stethoscope and spirometer respectively through diagnostic patients defined by physician. Further, segmentation and reliability and labelling of data will be performed with the assistance of physician. After preprocessing of data, suitable features will be obtained from respiratory sounds. Detailed statistical analysis will be done to find out different realities of about respiratory sounds. Similarly, some suitable classifier will be used for classification purpose.  Collected data will be used for the training of the classifier and validation of the system. Finally, a prototype diagnostic system and severity level identification will be develop.

data.projectName: Preparation of ELISA Kit for the rapid Screening of Babesia under field Conditions, a Challenging infection of food Animals
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Babesiosis is caused by a parasite that infects red blood cells and spread by ticks. It can infect mammals and humans. In Pakistan the disease is known by the name of Redwater Fever and Tick Fever. There is high morbidity and mortality. It causes huge economic losses in term of low productivity and weight gain. Tick borne diseases cause 18.6 billion losses and deficiency of 3 billion pieces of hide in cattle per year. Major signs include high fever, depression, anorexia, haemoglobinuria, icterus, and death in severe cases. In recent years, the disease has been gaining interest in human medicine due to emerging zoonotic infections . An infected mother can transmit babesiosis to her baby during pregnancy or delivery. Human babesiosis transmission via tick bite is most common throughout the world. Livestock plays a pivotal role in Pakistan’s economy by uplifting the socioeconomic conditions of poor farming communities and alleviating poverty. A large number of dairy cattle are being imported into the country in order to meet an increasing demand of milk and milk products. There is no screening tool to diagnose these imported cattle for babesiosis. Imported ELISA kits are too costly to purchase for screening. About 500 million cattle are at risk throughout the globe. There are many available techniques to diagnose Babesia but all are costly and time consuming. So, there is dire need of an economical and rapid detection diagnostic tool for Babesia. No local kit for screening of Babesiosis in Pakistan. Current research may proceed for preparation of a local ELISA kit to detect the antibodies IgG against Babesiosis which will be cost effective and help to resolve the concern of farmers pertaining to diagnosis of disease.

data.projectName: Developing and Implementing Strategic IPM Module for the Management  of Fall Armyworm, Spodoptera frugiperda (Lepidoptera: Noctudiae)
data.projectDigest: Maize, Zea mays L., being a major cereal crop of Pakistan was cultivated on 1, 229 thousand hectares’ area during 2017-2018 with 5.702 million tonnes production. The fall armyworm (FAW) Spodoptera frugiperda is a key pest of maize crop and an insect native to tropical and subtropical areas of America. It is voracious lepidopteran pest preferably feeds on the leaves, stems and reproductive parts of almost 350 species of host plants, responsible to cause economic damage to nearly all-important cash crops including maize, rice, sorghum, sugarcane, cotton, wheat and most of vegetables. Ability to reproduce at much faster pace, the availability of host, migration and diverse host range let this genius pest to survive in various circumstances. There are different approaches have been used to control this pest. There is much needed to study on this major pest by using all possible techniques and methods which are suitable and compatible to overcome this pest. The objectives of the study will be the taxonomy and DNA barcoding through characterization on molecular and morphological basis. Similarly, work will be done on monitoring, Host plant susceptible indices, varietal response and artificial diets and it comparison with natural diets. The project will cover the utilization of biological control agents and entomopathogens which will be suitable and compatible for the management of FAW and their rearing in laboratory conditions. The evaluation of new chemistry Insecticides, cultural and mechanical and will also be checked. Finally, IPM model of all these control methods will be implemented which will be most suitable, sustainable and economical for the management of fall armyworm. The academic and sectorial partnership will support our project to identify the key area like DNA

data.projectName: Socio-economic uplift and sustainability of rural women through advanced backyard poultry techniques
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: A multidimensional project is proposed in the form of establishing a Rural Poultry Studies Center (RPSC) at Ravi Campus of the University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences (UVAS), Lahore. This center will provide genetically improved seed stock along with conducting the trainings of rural women with its allied institutes regarding backyard chicken production and efficient domestic budgeting. The RPSC will collaborate with College of Veterinary and Animal Sciences Jhang (sub campus of UVAS Lahore), University of Agriculture Faisalabad main campus and Toba Tek Singh campus, Poultry Research Institute Rawalpindi, Poultry Research Institute KPK, Shaheed Benazir Bhutto University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Sakrand, Sindh. This project is based upon the fact that women constitute about 51% of the total population in Pakistan. Their role in national, regional, community and even family economics is very limited. Experience has shown that women have pragmatic financial management abilities than men and if given the opportunities they can be real vehicle of growth. The concept of providing genetically improved stock to the well-trained rural women is the core of this project as it has been experienced that handing over birds to the properly trained women may yield significant results.

data.projectName: Revalorization of carbon dioxide for catalytic hydrogenation to methanol
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan needs fighting tendency to search for renewable energy resources. The proposed project deals with the CO2 conversion to methanol. Hence, the successful execution of our project provides a win-win situation, as it mitigates the emitted CO2 on one hand and delivers a valuable fuel product like methanol on the other. 
In proposed project, Pd-ZrO2/CNFs will be synthesized and characterized by different analytical techniques. The activity of the developed catalysts will be evaluated in a stirred slurry reactor. Reaction studies will be optimized in terms of reaction conditions. 
The successful execution of our project will provide renewable energy resource (methanol production) and it will also play a significant role to mitigate the global warming. The biggest project outcome is in-line with the country important priority to generation of renewable energy resources. Our proposal will surely help to management of carbon dioxide resulted from different sectors of country. CO2 emission indulges extra economic burden on country economy. After Successful completion of proposed project, we may set up a CO2 reservoir in conjunction with academic/ public/government sector in order to enhance profitable benefits of CO2 emission to large section of society as well as economic growth of country.

data.projectName: Vaccine Development against Chicken Coccidiosis
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: The poultry (worth> 700 Billion rupees; 1.2 Billion birds) contributes around 34% in total meat production of Pakistan (Economic Survey 2018-2019). Available per capita protein consumption is only 17grams far deficient against the WHO-recommended 27 grams (Hussain et al., 2015). Combating the constraints to Poultry Industry (2nd largest in the country) can help to fill this gap. A major hurdle is the industry’s heavy reliance on the imported vaccines and medicines. Avian Coccidiosis, a disease of huge economic importance, is acting as a speed breaker in the progress of poultry industry. This industry, is spending huge sum of money to control this infection by large import bills of drugs and vaccines against this disease. Imported vaccine currently in use for layer and breeder has high cost and mostly fail to protect because of the potential antigenic diversity, and is live with potential to revert and cause disease in healthy birds. No local commercial vaccine is available. This project aims to develop subunit vaccine against coccidiosis by exploiting local isolated strains of Eimeria as a cornerstone in reducing the morbidity, mortality as well the economic-losses, thus leading to the improved per-capita cheaper protein availability and consumption (SDG 2: Food Security).

data.projectName: An AI Assisted Digital Framework for National Governance Related to Integrated Public Safety & Security
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Public Safety and Security (PSS) is usually expressed as a governmental responsibility that primarily aims prevention and protection of the public from dangers like disasters, health risks, crimes or law and order incidents. These services bring innovation in governance and bring value to society by creating a stable and secure environment and protection to the people and assets at local, regional and national level.
The core challenges in enabling integrated public safety and security are the lack of effective solutions for; (i)On-site monitoring, data collection, storage, analytics (ii)Early warning, forecasting and Risk analysis of the incidents, (iii)Quick response planning and operational management through unified command & control and optimal decision making. We propose the design, development and deployment of an AI assisted digital framework for national governance related to integrated public safety & security which initially covers four key application domains: (i) Public Security, (ii) Natural Disaster Management, (iii) Accidental Disaster Management and (iv) Public health & Bio-surveillance.
This digital framework will enable the authorities for pre-emptive monitoring, preparedness, prediction, mitigation, optimal coordinated response to any catastrophe or disaster at local, provisional or national level.

data.projectName: Development of a large-scale anaerobic digester for biogas production from a cattle farm and its energy enhancement via nanoparticles
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Biomass can be used in Pakistan as one of the renewable energy source which can be utilized to create electrical power and to provide heating. Fermentation process of biomass releases biogas which acts as an energy source. A comprehensive feasibility study for biogas plant design was carried out. Literature review of various digestion techniques was carried out and design methodology was assessed. Based on finalized parameters, design calculations of Anaerobic Digester was carried out and design was finalized and analysis was carried out. Furthermore, a waste gas heat recovery system was designed for preheating input slurry and to increase plant efficiency. Suitable components like: valves, pumps, motors, agitator and Generator set have been selected. A suitable, existing design for biogas storage has also been proposed. The aim of this project is to develop large-scale anaerobic digester for biogas production from a cattle farm. Nanotechnology is one of the emerging branches of science. Nanotechnology can be applied in bioenergy field for the purpose of feedstock modification and catalysis that is more efficient. Various nanomaterials been employed for bioenergy production. The project will also focus on increasing the biogas yield and overall high energy gain by introducing nanoparticles inside anaerobic digestion process.

data.projectName: Cross talk between diabetes and depression through biomarker investigations and effectiveness of chamomile + ginger tea for the treatment depression in diabetic patients
data.projectDigest: Diabetes is a major public health concern which is spreading at a fast pace. Diabetes is a multifactorial disease posing a series of complications like dyslipidemia, hypertension, retinopathy, neuropathy and nephropathy. In addition to these complications, depression as newer complication in diabetic patients portends substantial burden to healthcare system in terms of poor glycemic control, poor quality of life, raised health expenditures and increased mortality. A bidirectional relation exists between type 2 diabetes and depression, and evidence is growing for biological correlates of depression in patients with type 2 diabetes. However, there are dearth of investigations on relationship of several biomarkers with both depression and type 2 diabetes. Moreover, the impact of herbs has not been investigated among patients in which both diabetes and depression co-exists. In this context, present study will ascertain the predictors of depression in type 2 diabetes, clinico-laboratory characteristics, and clinical outcomes among patients attending tertiary care hospital in Faisalabad Pakistan. In addition, ELISA-based biomarkers qualitative and quantitative investigations will be carried out to ascertain the relationship of important inflammatory cytokines i.e. tissue necrotic factor alpha (TNF) and interleukin-6 (IL-6) between diabetic patients with and without depression. Since chamomile and ginger provide promising results for both diabetes and psychological disorders, current study will investigate the effect of chamomile/ginger tea on depressive score and glycemic control among diabetic patients and will underscore its impact on biological markers e.g. TNF and IL6. data.projectName: Innovative Diagnostic and Strategic Management of Post-Harvest Losses by Non-Thermal Plasma of Fresh Fruit Commodities - Way Forward for Sustainable Development
data.projectDigest: Fruits and vegetables are major contributor of food for burgeoning population. However, fruit decay due to diseases at post-harvest level can claim ~ 50% of the total production worldwide. Both bacterial and fungal pathogens are involved for such losses. There exists a lacuna of sound post-harvest technology in Pakistan for proper management and quality retention from farm to consumer due to which most of fresh produces are wasted.  Thus, both quantity and quality are compromised resulting in less return. This project is aimed at development of state-of-the-art lab for diagnostic of potential pathogens involved in post-harvest losses and then up scaling of green technology - non-thermal cold plasma treatment of citrus, grapes/raisins and tomatoes and their disease etiology during storage. The pathogen load will be determined for quality assessment of treated samples with advanced microbial identification system. The technology may help in desirable structural modification of food and packaging material in addition to controlling the pathogen. The initiative to use plasma technology will help to establish large-scale post-harvest processing industry on firm footings, which will not only reduce the challenges in food security, but may also improve the export of fresh produce leading to employment-opportunities in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Development of Indigenous Efficient Energy Storage System
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
The increasing demand of energy in day to day life made energy crisis to provide more energy from the grid which is contributing too many factors like the capital costs of producing extra electrical energy to overcome the gap between supply and demand, new and efficient ways to produce electrical energy to ensure uninterrupted supply. The recent power crisis has affected both people and industries at large which highlighted the issues related with the production and use of electrical energy such as the burning of fossil fuels for electricity generation as a result releasing high amount of carbon emission and the loss of energy via electrical grids and transmission lines. It can provide a portable transmission of electrical energy to distant end-users as well as working as backup storage which provides electricity when needed. 
The proposed project aims to develop Pakistan’s first next-generation energy storage system which consists of storage devices like batteries and supercapacitors to provide necessary backup and fuel as well for the newly develop electric vehicles and also reduce the amount of electrical energy production from fossil fuel thus reducing the carbon emission and making the environment clean and healthy.

data.projectName: Recognition and Social Acceptance of Transgenders in Pakistan: An Analytical Study of Statutes and Implementation Mechanisms
data.projectDigest: Sub-Continent was divided on the basis of two nation theory and Pakistan becomes an Islamic state from its inception. In Islam every human has equal rights. But in Pakistan it is hard to say that “Transgender” has been neglected or being ignored by the former governments and society. In spite of Islamic state, the mentioned element of society Transgender are considered to be social outcast and being deprived from health care, education, government jobs and even security for their life. Supreme Court of Pakistan gave special attention to Transgender by taking decision on their rights but still implementation in the Society is unfixed. The purpose of this research work is to highlight and review various legal rights given by the constitution of Pakistan and what issues are facing the “Transgender” community of Pakistan. Pakistani Parliament has passed the Protection of Rights Act for transgender which is reckoned as milestone in protection of “Transgender”. The purpose of this research work is to investigate the legal rights given to “Transgender”and their implementation in the society and also review and highlight various aspects of issues faced by this community of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Development of Smart Farming and Complaint Management System (SFCMS) using Big Data and Artificial Intelligence
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: This project aims to resolve  problems face by farmers by providing support and advice to farmers by developing an automated system that has two major components. The first component of the proposed Smart Farming and Complaint Management System (SFCMS) is a Smart Farming System (SFS) that will be an efficient Predictive Cultivation System (PCS) for Pakistan providing Zone-wise optimal cultivation prediction and intelligent time scheduling. The main objective of the system is to ensure higher yields and economic benefits to farmers at a specific time according to their landscape and terrain, soil properties and cultivation practices. The second component of the proposed SFCMS is a ‘Visual-Bot’, an IoT based Farmer Complaint Management System (FCMS) that uses Big Data and Artificial Intelligence. It will be based on the application of knowledge discovery and intelligent decision making on agricultural big data and farmers' complaints, deployed on a Cloud platform. In knowledge discovery, analysis will be performed to find the relationships between climate, soil, crop, pests and disease data. To enable decision making using artificial intelligence, the crop prediction and monitoring models will be built by modeling the correlation between all of these factors. The proposed SFCMS will be used to provide adequate and timely advice to farmers on their queries and complaints, and also to foresee near future development of circumstances by the experts. Consequently, this will be enabling agricultural experts to broadcast early warning signals of threats, mainly pests/ disease and the needed preventive actions to be undertaken by farmers.

data.projectName: Safe Drinking Water Provision through Water Conservation (WPWC): Development of Water Metering and Pricing in Islamabad
data.projectDigest:
Smart Water Metering and Pricing Project (SWMP)
SWMP, funded by the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC) completed in November 2019, generated research that highlighted the lack of equity in water distribution in Islamabad at the municipal level. SWMP found that Capital Development Authority (CDA), the municipal water supplier, has a system of water rationing in Islamabad that is inefficient and facing capacity constraints, resulting in the formation of a private water tanker mafia, with a high cost burden on residents. Infrastructure breakdown due to intermittent water supply and non-maintenance have increased leakage along with 50% reported losses by MCI and contaminated water supply. Residential water supply on SWMP sites in Islamabad were found biologically and chemically contaminated, raising public health concerns and requiring residents to purchase drinking water as well. 
24/7 Drinking Water Supply: Changa Paani (Excellent Water) Program (CPP)
To resolve these above issues, a revenue-based 24/7 municipal drinking water supply to urban areas is recommended by the Pakistan Council for Research of Water Resources (PCRWR), the government collaborator on SWMP and the proposed project by Centre for Climate Research and Development (CCRD), COMSATS University Islamabad. A 3-year demonstration infrastructure and operations project is proposed to undertake provide 24/7 municipal drinking water supply to one of the sectors of Islamabad (Sector I-8 of Islamabad) through water metering with volumetric prices, allowing for water conservation along with different Prototype development for Smart water meters and its implementation. Ministry of Science and Technology (MoST) has provided its support for such an endeavor.

data.projectName: Semiconductor/carbon based novel electrode materials for renewable energy devices
data.projectDigest: We seek funding under GCF pertaining to the thematic area “sustainable energy”. The project proposed entitled “semiconductor/carbon based novel electrode materials for renewable energy devices”  has been designed wherein we intend to establish state of the art Laboratory for novel material fabrication for energy storage devices based on solar cells and supercapsitors, for which same class of materials as proposed above will be employed owing to their superior properties simultaneously suitable for both types of above mentioned devices. The project will be executed through a consortia of local and international partners including Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology · Functional Materials Laboratory (FML), School of Materials & Mineral Resources, Siyan Laboratory, Department of Physics, Jinan University, Guangzhou, China  and Institute of Micro Nano Systems Technology, University College Southeast Norway, Tønsberg, Norway,  Our collaborative partners will train the students and researchers by mutual cooperation/visits and joint publications whereas the laboratory will be equipped with the facilities suitable for the synthesis and testing of the devices at international level. The choice of materials will be comprised of semiconductor compounds including metal oxides, sulphides, GO and carbon based materials to address the energy technologies of the future. Through this project, a strong footing on which locally trained professionals can be produced will be established. These trained professionals will work on new ways of research on these materials with international quality and also brain storm to commercialize these materials at local level after it gets matured.

data.projectName: Development of a low cost and ecofriendly dietary supplements  for commercial application
data.projectDigest: Poultry Industry is largest industry of Pakistan contributing 1.3% to the GDP of Pakistan. More than 67 % of Pakistani population lives in rural areas dependent on agriculture means. Disease free meat is a big challenge for poultry industry of Pakistan. There were many diseases which were appeared from 1990-1991 that caused a great damage to broiler industry. This led to investigate various vaccines and proper feeding methods for the growth and development of chicks by providing them healthy feed. Use of secondary metabolites of bacteria and fungi helps in increasing the availability of phosphorous, simple fatty acids, calcium and amino acids to the animals which is considered as the latest technology. The feed dietary supplements were first introduced in late 1980s to improve the nutrient uptake. So, by keeping this scenario in mind, this project has been designed and focus of the study will be the development of ecofriendly feed which is very cost effective and can enhance the productivity of chicks. This project will be accomplished with the help of our academic collaborative and sectoral collaborators.  Our team is dedicated to outreach and extension. Participation by women will be encouraged and emphasized in research, educational, and outreach activities.

data.projectName: Geospatial and real time monitoring of indigenous air pollutants; and their association with upper respiratory tract and lungs disease burden in Lahore (Pakistan).
data.projectDigest:
WWF-Pakistan proclaim air pollution as “public health emergency” in Pakistan. Pakistan is facing severe health effects related to air pollution, especially people residing in big cities, particularly allergy and its clinical manifestations such as asthma, rhinitis, urticarial and other allergic complications. Megacity Lahore (Pakistan) is regarded as one of the top most polluted city of the world. In Lahore, the number of patients with respiratory problems linked to air pollution and smog events has been growing at an exponential rate. Phenomenal growth of anthropogenic emissions of CO (39%), NO2 (65%), CH4 (27%), CO2 (31%) and SO2 (44%) have been observed during last decade in Lahore. 
A multidisciplinary approach involving remote sensing, geospatial data analyses, and molecular biological sciences is seriously needed to map upper respiratory tract epithelium and lungs disease burden and explore its linkage with spatiotemporal patterns of air pollutants to address the ever-worsening conditions of health as well as elevating air pollution in Lahore. 
Due to absence of multidisciplinary approach, and very low technical and financial capacity, related the geospatial mapping of urban cities air pollutants, their health effects and related concerns, so far in-depth analysis is never been made in Pakistan.

data.projectName: dfdsfsdff
data.projectDigest: Starting from birth, microorganisms start establishing in association with human body i.e. human microbiome. Nearly every process is affected directly or indirectly by the functionality of these microorganisms. Till three year of age, the establishment of microbiome is almost complete. Long term dietary interventions may alter the adult microbiome. The composition and function of Gut microbiome is related to human health and disease. Different diets favour the relative abundance of different types of microorganisms. The type of microorganisms established in the gut are also responsible for the metabolism of food accordingly. So the food we eat whether it is absorbed or not depends on the microbiome. There is a link between imbalance in gut microbiome i.e. dysbiosis and chronic diseases such as obesity, hypertension, depression, inflammation, diabetes, cholesterol, colitis and the disorders related to the nutritional deficiencies. It needs addressing and a connection between the health status of individuals and the corresponding microbiome with respect to the dietary habits is to be established. This study aims to observe malnutrition among different age groups in Pakistan and the prevalence of chronic diseases by analysing samples from a selected group of people with some chronic disorder, children up to the age of five and observing their dietary habits as well as their respective microbiome. The international collaboration with researcher at MIT and Harvard will help in researcher trainings and interpretation of results. Local sectorial collaborator and researchers will insure the sustainability of the project for novel projects.

data.projectName: Design and Development of a See-Through-Wall (STW) Radar System for Personnel Sensing and Disaster Management
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Looking through walls has been an elusive dream, however, technological advances in radar technology is helping researchers come close to fulfilling this dream. In simple terms, radars are like human eyes, only that they use electromagnetic (EM) waves at few gigahertz frequencies instead of visible light.  EM waves, depending on their frequencies, can penetrate almost all types of materials around us where human sight unable to see.
The applications for such a solution are immense. For instance, the ability to locate objects behind obstacles can help in search and rescue operations in wake of natural calamities such as fire, earthquake rubble, landslides, avalanche and mines. It can potentially save lives by pin-pointing the presence or absence of human life behind blockages as well as reduce rescue time and costs dramatically.
This research project aims to address the challenges mentioned above by designing and implementing an end-to-end See-Through-Wall (STW) radar system for disaster management.

data.projectName: Linking The Water-Food-Energy Nexus With Economic Development, Institutional Stability And Macro Level Factors
data.projectDigest:
Although the Pakistan has made a remarkable progress in socio economic development in recent years but the threats persist to end in hunger and poverty, to ensure access to modern energy, nutritional food security, natural resource protection, adequate living standards and livable environmental conditions. Water energy and food are the essential resources with rapidly increasing demand and exponential limited supply. The exhaustion of fossil fuel energy, perishing water resources and looming food security are the challenges of this millennium. According to united nation’s report, by 2035 Pakistan is going to have less than five hundred cubic meter water per capita with severe water withdrawal as compare to total water renewable resources. The food and energy conditions are not different to that of water resources. 51 million people are living without energy and 144 million people are living without reliable access to energy while more than 70 percent of population is malnutrition. The inter-linkages and inter-dependency of these three important resources is termed as water food energy (WFE) nexus that elaborate how the choking in one resource might limit the availability of other resources. Traditionally these resources are planned and managed independently but due to the interdependent and interconnected nature of these resources significant issues arises as the implementation of certain polices in one sector has unintended but far reaching consequences in other sectors.
 Importantly, implementation of integrated resources management is difficult in developing countries as developing countries are characterized with poor political stability and uncertain political environment where one sector has favor on other and policies of one government discarded by the new govern

data.projectName: Smart Grid Hardware and Software Development (up to 300kV, 2000 Amp grid)
data.projectDigest: Currently, underdeveloped countries including Pakistan utilize conventional electro mechanical methods to control electric grids for transmission of power from generating stations to distributors. Which requires conventional lines and results in high power loss during transmission. This power loss means that system do not performs at its maximum efficiency. For solving this problem of making transmission efficiency maximum, smart grids are used. In power transmission, smart grid is used to switch between various type of conventional e.g. hydro, nuclear power plants etc. and renewable energy sources i.e., wind and solar etc. The main aim of this project is to develop an intelligent hardware and software-based solution for Pakistani high-voltage power transmission lines. This will be done by using modern technologies like vacuum switches, zero-power switching electronics and modern high-voltage high-current semiconductor devices, which results in fast by-pass path for dangerously high fault-current flow. The testing of the developed intelligent smart grid system will be done by preparing such test bed which can produce very high voltages and currents for testing purpose. Such project will have a great impact in Pakistan by reducing the transmission loss; switching-over from one power source to another for availability of cheap electricity; better energy and load management system; improved power factor without overheating & overloading and better voltage regulation for all kind of domestic loads.

data.projectName: Secure & Resilient 5G Networks
data.projectDigest:
The 5G is the fifth generation of mobile networks. It will elevate the mobile network to not only interconnect people, but also interconnect and control machines, objects, and devices which will revolutionize future digital services and create incredible opportunities for the economy and society. Global 5G market is projected to reach $1.3 trillion by 2025 and Asia pacific will become the leader in using 5G networks with 1.4 billion connections by 2025. It also has tremendous opportunities for Pakistan such as 5G has been projected to give strong support to the operation and development of China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) and special economic zones. Cybersecurity is a fundamental requirement and all these benefits cannot be achieved without security at all levels of 5G networks as majority of global assets will be transformed into digital assets. 

The aim of this project is to design and develop a secure and intelligent ecosystem for 5G networks to ensure efficient 5G operations at all levels. This project includes, five academic partners from Pakistan (Air University, LUMS, GIKI, FAST-NU and University of Baluchistan). International partners include Beihang University China and Fundacio i2CAT Spain. Industrial partners include CARE Pvt Ltd, XFlow Pvt Ltd and Huawei.

data.projectName: Phosphate solubilizing biofertilizers: an economical and environment friendly approach for sustainable crops production
data.projectDigest: Fertilizer is the most expensive and essential agricultural input for improved crop production. Though, self-sufficient in urea fertilizer production, but Pakistan spends 100+ billion PKRs to import diammonium phosphate (DAP) fertilizers annually. DAP is applied to the soil to provide plant with phosphorus, which is second most important essential nutrient for plant growth. Due to highly reactive nature of DAP, its major portion transforms to unavailable form when applied to the soil and cause environmental pollution. On the other hand, some soil and plant associated bacteria have the ability to provide phosphorus to plants from soil indigenous resources. These phosphate solubilizing bacteria (PSB) could be used as an alternative of DAP. PSB can also have the ability to produce plant hormones, fix nitrogen and control plant disease in an environment friendly way. So, accepting the grand challenge of replacing DAP with PSB to produce organic food, can save not only billions of rupees country’s import spending but also help to generate employment, improve environment and reduce health problems.

data.projectName: Epidemiological assessment & screening of milk sentinel sites and different supplies in District Lahore, Pakistan.
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Milk is highly perishable and nutritious food for an agriculture land like Pakistan. Most of the livelihood, food and living styles of the families in rural and urbana reas of pakistan rely on milk. The industrial milk production, supplies of aduletrated milk from open markets, veterinary clinics  are abundant source of zoonotic disease transmission. The present research study is designed to assess these sites to check viral, bacterial, parasitic and fungal pathogens which transmit from animals to humans via milk. Adulterated contents in milk supplies would also be determined to find out health and detrimental side effects on public.  Moreover, using field surveys and target observations of open markets, industrial suppliers, the problema in safe and healthy milk production would be determined and subsequently corrective measures would be recommended and applied. These objectives would find out reasons behind the major public health outbreaks, their primary and secondary risk factors and enable the mass production of milk in open markets, industries and farmer level more secure, healthier and disaese free. In a much similar way, our milk producing animals would also become safer leading to a stronger economy.

data.projectName: Lightweight blockchain-based authentication solutions for resource-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) devices and networks
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Internet of Things (IoT) and blockchain are two emerging and transformative technologies in Industry 4.0. The size of the IoT ecosystem is estimated to have exceeded the number of mobile phones in 2018. Likewise, Blockchain technology has drastically grown over the last five years. Together, these two technologies have become a focal point for competition among companies and countries. However, there are two main areas of concerns: slow performance and poor security. Blockchain has the potential to help in overcoming both these concerns. For such a new technology, it surprisingly promises features that hold substantial promise in the design of various security mechanisms especially for authentication, authorization, access control and key management. 
This research project aims to promote research and development of blockchain- based security solutions in Pakistan with particular emphasis on IoT and cloud computing environments. The academic phase of this project is expected to include the design, development, implementation and testing of secure and efficient blockchain-based solutions.  In the second phase of this project, the resulting solutions are to be adapted and enhanced for adoption in Pakistan’s academic and industrial sectors.

data.projectName: A sustainable development in the textile sector of Pakistan including water minimization and waste management
data.projectDigest: Water minimization and waste management is becoming a big challenge at the moment in Textile Industry of Pakistan. Due to the use of exhaust process in knitwear industry, a huge amount of water is consumed in dyeing and washing process causing scarcity of water. Furthermore, large amount of water used increases effluent proportionally which needs further treatment. Secondly, waste produced from textiles specially after the consumer has used the products, add pollution to land and can be converted into useful products through recycling and regeneration. The successful completion of this project will bring a big sustainable change in the environment of Pakistan by not only conserving the natural resources but also by increasing the export revenue.

data.projectName: Machine Learning based Controlled Aquaponics System for Sustainable Food Production
data.projectDigest: The project focuses to develop an aquaponics system in a greenhouse in COMSATS University Islamabad. In aquaponics the wastes produced by fish are converted to beneficial nutrients by bacteria which are then supplied to plants grown without soil. This research focuses on the design and development of an automated aquaponics system so that plant yield is maximised. Edible fish, such as Common carp, Tilapia and ornamental fish such as Goldfish and Koi will be raised in the fish tanks. Leafy greens such as lettuce and fruiting plants such as cherry tomatoes, bell peppers, strawberry and cucumber will be grown in the grow beds. The system will be monitored using a microcontroller which will send the information from sensors to a central monitoring and control center and then to the cloud. With the help of deep learning assisted image processing techniques the health of plants will be monitored and attacks of insects and other diseases will be identified. Experts in plant pathology, plant nutrition and fisheries will help maximise the yield and efficiency of the aquaponics system. The project will be carried out in collaboration with NUST, Arid Agriculture University, University of Southampton, UK and Practical Aquaponics, Australia.

data.projectName: Technology based cotton maximization
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: Climate change, diseases, insect pests, drop in cultivation area and less supportive policies have cumulatively played a role in the decline of cotton yield and fiber quality. Therefore, producing high yielding, biotic and abiotic resistant/tolerant varieties, and area under cotton cultivation need to be increased by finding new climate-supportive land and sustainable production technologies. This project will use new technologies such as genetic engineering of multiple genes, genome editing and non-GMO insect control technologies. The breeding teams at NIBGE and NIAB will be involved in developing new cotton lines and field trials using already developed and characterized transgenic plants/events with multiple genes for insect (Cry1Ac, Cry2Ab, Vip3A, Tma12, PTA and ASAL), herbicide tolerance (2XEPSPS, base editing of ALS1) and sucking pests resistance (developed by Chinese collaborator) into elite cotton germplasm having resistance to CLCuD (Mac7). Cotton germplasm from USDA will be screened for heat tolerance and drought resistance. The team at Lasbella University and Kohat University will conduct field trials for identification of the best cotton varieties/lines suitable for Balochistan, southern Khyber Pakhtunkhua and Potohar region. The team at MNSUA will be involved in testing of cotton lines/new insect control technologies cotton growing areas of Punjab.

Therefore, producing high yielding, biotic and abiotic resistant/tolerant varieties, and area under cotton cultivation need to be increased by finding new climate-supportive land and sustainable production technologies. This project will use new technologies such as genetic engineering of multiple genes, genome editing and non-GMO insect control technologies. The breeding teams at NIBGE and NIAB will be involved in developing new cotton lines and field trials using already developed and characterized transgenic plants/events with multiple genes for insect (Cry1Ac, Cry2Ab, Vip3A, Tma12, PTA and ASAL), herbicide tolerance (2XEPSPS, base editing of ALS1) and sucking pests resistance (developed by Chinese collaborator) into elite cotton germplasm having resistance to CLCuD (Mac7). Cotton germplasm from USDA will be screened for heat tolerance and drought resistance. The team at Lasbella University and Kohat University will conduct field trials for identification of the best cotton varieties/lines suitable for Balochistan, southern Khyber Pakhtunkhua and Potohar region. The team at MNSUA will be involved in testing of cotton lines/new insect control technologies cotton growing areas of Punjab.

data.projectName: Integrated Governance of Educational Supply Chain for Economic Growth
data.projectDigest:
Skills demand and supply mismatch is a concern even for developed countries despite the fact they carry out elaborate occupational forecasts . The problem is severer in developing countries like Pakistan where skills mismatch has been identified as one of the main reasons for low competitiveness of economy 
Due to absence of any mechanism for projecting and forecasting skills requirements, supply of certain skills exceeds demand resulting in unemployment, underemployment and brain drain. On the other hand, some supply of certain skills fails to match demand level and results in low growth of certain sectors as well as unavailability of certain products and services. This also leads to costly imports from other countries negatively impacting the trade balance of the country.
There is also a lack of coordination, information sharing and alignment in various tiers of educations (primary, secondary, higher secondary and higher education), rending the educational machinery of the country responding swiftly to skills demand by the market or according to priorities set by the government for fast-tracking economic growth.

data.projectName: Designing Sustainable Wastewater Treatment System: Use of Biochar as catalysis for contaminant removal, water recycling and fabrication of nutrient enriched fertilizer
data.projectDigest: The potable water reserves of Pakistan are shrinking rapidly and there is an urgent need to develop technologies for domestic and industrial wastewater treatment which requires minimal energy input and provides effective water treatment solution. Biochar, a carbon-rich solid produced by organic waste could effectively remove multiple contaminants from the aqueous medium. Biochar-based water treatment technology could provide additional benefits for environmental restoration and nutrient enriched additive for improving agriculture soil and productivity of the soils system. The current project is likely to address three important issues a) Use of waste agriculture residues to produce biochar, b) Use of biochar for the treatment of domestic waste c) Application of used biochar as a fertilizer for the growth and development of crops. For this purpose, project will be perused in three phases. It is likely that proposed project will be very helpful in reducing 1) environmental burden of the agriculture waste 2) treatment of the wastewater and decontamination 3) reuse of wastewater for agriculture 4) development of green fertilizer. Collectively, proposed project will be helpful for achieving sustainability goals i.e. water conservation and agriculture productivity improvement to ensure sustainable water supply and for addressing food security issues.

data.projectName: Development of innovative strategies for integrated citriculture researchin Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Citrus ranks first among commercial fruits of Pakistan. However, the age and productivity of old and newly planted citrus orchards is low when compared with international standards. Its pertinent to mention here several factors including poor and uncertified citrus nursery, diseased unhealthy saplings and root stocks, genetically inferior scions (with long juvenile phase, tall plant height) and non-recommended root stocks, unproductive plant geometry, poor agronomic practices, insect pests, faulty intercropping within orchards, diseases and insects susceptibility, postharvest losses, poor irrigation and fertilizer application methods which reduce the productivity and age of the orchards. Irrigating orchards with unfit water is inducing soil salinity and irrigation with sewage source can contaminate the soil, plants and fruits with heavy metals and toxic substances. Therefore, there is dire need for reviving the citrus nursery supply system (production of disease free highly vigorous true to type citrus nursery), eradication of unhealthy and low productive plants in orchards, introducing new citrus orchards plantation and management system. The project will integrate various components of agriculture such as horticulture, plant pathology, soil science, biotechnology, biochemistry, to solve various problems of citriculture from sanitation of citrus nursery to reduction of postharvest losses.

data.projectName: Preventing diarrhea by improving water, sanitation, and hygiene practices
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest: Worldwide diarrhea is the major cause of death among children under the age of five. In Pakistan every year thousands of children die due to diarrhea. The contaminated drinking water, and unavailability of water sanitation and hygiene (WaSH) facilities are the biggest contributors of diarrhea. There is a lack of information on emerging pathogens and antibiotic resistance. In Pakistan 70% population is lacking access to clean drinking water. Another reason is the lack of proper sanitation. There is lack of awareness among the communities. There is lack of data on emerging pathogens therefore our first work package will include a detailed sampling of the emerging pathogens in order to find out high risk areas so that its control measures will be taken. The diarrhea is spread due to the contamination of drinking water therefore a simple solar disinfection (SODIS) will be modified with the addition of coagulants and advanced oxidants (e.g. hydrogen peroxide) to improve its efficiency for disinfection of diarrhea causing microorganisms. A simple and low cost high rate algal pond (HRAP) system will be used for wastewater treatment. Several WaSH interventions will be introduced in schools, households, and healthcare facilities of Hyderabad district as model that can be applied to all over Pakistan after getting positive results.

data.projectName: Car Users’ Mobility Towards Sustainable Transportation System
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
"Recent traffic congestion predicting cost is the US $2.5 billion annually, will reach to $7.85 billion in the coming ten years in Karachi (Indus Toyota Research 2018). The government is adopting conventional approaches which are encouraging the car users mobility instead of adopting sustainable transportation approaches, such as public transportation. The federal government initiated Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) projects in megacities but unable to attract Single Occupant Vehicle (SOV) users. Therefore, this research will discover the factors which encourage private transport users towards private vehicles and discouraging them from the adaptability of public transportation in the mega cities of Pakistan.

Hence, this research can be helpful to highlight the key measures and factors through which private transport users can be encouraged to use an efficient and sustainable alternative mode of transport. Similarly, this study can help policymakers and stakeholders to implement balanced travel demand management push and pull measures. In conclusion, this study can help to reduce the billions of dollars of traffic congestion cost and helps to reduce environmental pollution".

data.projectName: Development of Plant-level and National Aggregate Wind Power Forecasting Technology in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Wind energy is one of the fastest growing energy sources in the world. Its recent proliferation could be attributed to its cost-effectiveness, sustainability and clean nature. Pakistan has a fledgling wind energy market. Currently, the total installed capacity stands at 1250 MW that makes up around 7% of the total power production in the country. With ever-increasing share of unpredictable wind resource in the overall energy mix, Pakistan's national energy operators, i.e., central power purchasing agency (CPPA) and national transmission and dispatch company (NTDC), are struggling to balance supply and demand across the national network. That is mainly due to the lack of wind power forecasting tool at their disposal, leading to ad hoc and inefficient scheduling strategies that result in high electricity generation and dispatch costs. To that end, we embark on developing an online wind power forecasting system that would deliver: i) plant-level forecasts and ii) national (or regional) aggregate forecasts in real time to market (CPPA) and wind farm operators in Pakistan. The project will trial and demonstrate the technology at  wind farms in Jhimpir and on aggregate national power data obtained from CPPA.

data.projectName: Computational Analysis of Magnetohydrodynamics Oscillatory flow of Nanofluids in Vertical Channel Involving Heat Radiation
data.projectDigest:
In MHD mixed convection, a periodic flow of nanofluid is generated in a rotating vertical channel with heat radiation. The aim is to solve the problem for different nanoparticles and to obtain the results by means of calculations with new numerical methods and to subsequently present these results graphically. Mathematica, Matlab and CFD software are used to achieve results.
Effective heat transfer in liquids has become a challenge in industry and academia as it is important for improving the efficiency of various devices. Accordingly, researchers have proposed various approaches to improve the ability of heat transfer in liquids; One of the best ways to increase the heat transfer rate in liquids is to use nanofluids, which are materials suspended with nanoparticles.
The investigation of the electrically conductive fluid flow, which is referred to as magnetohydrodynamic (MHD), is the subject of numerous studies described in the literature due to its various applications. The investigation of solar plasma, earth nuclei and star structures are examples of their applications in astrophysics and geophysics. In addition, MHD has numerous industrial applications such as the extraction of geothermal energy, nuclear reactors, heat and mass transfer and the stability of convection currents.

data.projectName: Sea Buckthorn Utilization in Pakistan for Economic Recovery Concept for Healthy living by Accelerating Genetic Enhancements (SUPERCHARGE)
data.projectDigest: Sea buckthorn (Hippophae rhamnoides) is a magic shrub, been used as a folk medicine with berries, oil, leaves and bark against health and nutritional problems in human beings. Despite of its significance and abundance in the country, Sea buckthorn’s potentials in Human Nutrition, health and socio economic development have not been used in Pakistan. Value addition in this potential plant has not been started on commercial or scientific basis. Comprehensive research and development about it uses and exploitation in multiple ailments have not been started in Pakistan yet. To identify the best genotypes on the basis of nutritional profile and genetic potential for value addition and cultivar development we propose the Biochemical and Nutritional Analysis of Berries, Seeds, Leaves, Bark and molecular characterization that will ensure the appropriate selection of parents to be crossed or selected for value addition. Detailed investigation will be conducted on animal models for Metabolic Syndrome and brain disorders which will help to understand the potential role of Sea Buckthorn in the management of type 2 diabetes, obesity and psychosis. The agro based economy of Pakistan will be cushioned by exploitation of Sea buckthorn on commercial scale by value addition and genetic improvement for cultivar development.

data.projectName: Development, Evaluation and commercialization of novel, indigenous and cost effective probiotics for food and pharmaceutical applications
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Our objective is to develop probiotics for human health benefits especially targeting four benefits including (i) strengthening of normal flora or dysbiosis caused by antibiotics (ii) protection from gut pathogen i.e Salmonella enteritidis, Campylobater jejuni, (iii) anti-inflammatory/anti-allergic properties, and (iv) anti-cholesterol activities. We will collect samples from healthy controls and patients with respective problem and their gut microbial diversity will be determined by doing metagenomics. From results of metagenomics and difference in microbial diversity, signature microbial candidates will be identified. Signature probiotic candidates will be isolated, screened for respective benifits, identified by 16S rDNA sequencing and characterize for probiotic properties in vitro. Potential probiotics will then be subjected to in vivo evaluation for their probiotic potential in mice or rabbit. Then probiotics will be given in controlled human population and their health benefits and effect on gut function and gut microbial diversity will be monitored. Formulations of the selected strains and will be produced at large scale and given to a Pharmaceutical Industry for formulation and to a food industry to add them in different dairy products. Pharmaceutical products will be registered with respective regulatory authorities and produced for mass scale. Furthermore, these probiotics stains as an active ingredient/raw material will be produced by the industry and provided to other industries for production of probiotic products.

data.projectName: Optimization of Energy Mix for Power Sectors of Pakistan with Reduced Greenhouse Gas Emissions
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is facing severe energy crisis including short fall as well as increased cost of electricity for last fifteen years. China Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) has opened avenues for Pakistan to generate electricity by coal burning and providing a short term solution to energy crisis. But this is resulting in huge emissions of greenhouse gases causing global warming. One of the possible solutions is to shift towards renewable energy sources which provides low cost clean electricity but they are not reliable (due to seasonal and time variations) and require huge capital investment. Future energy mix of Pakistan will include reasonable portions of fossil fuel, hydro and renewable energy sources. The objective of this project is to optimize the energy sectors of Pakistan by minimizing the cost of electricity and reducing the greenhouse gas emissions. This project will be executed by several experts from various universities of Pakistan. The outcomes of this project will be beneficial for cheap and clean energy supply.

data.projectName: No More Plastic Bags in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Currently, plastic pollution has become one of the most unrelenting environmental issues. In particular, the rapid increase in production of disposable plastic bags has engulfed global capability to deal with them. Pakistan is also facing a rising tide of plastic waste due to inefficient garbage collection systems, reduced recycling rate and non-degradable nature of the plastics. This plastic pollution is not only threatening to human health and marine life but it is also prone to larger environmental challenges i.e. climate change. According to a recent report by the Centre for International and Environmental Law (CIEL) plastic, by 2050, will be responsible for 13% of the total “carbon budget” as it emits greenhouse gases at every stage of its life cycle i.e. from production to management as a waste .This project aims to contribute to the national, as well as global environmental challenge, simultaneously. The proposed project is directed towards synthesis of biodegradable plastics with suitable mechanical properties to overcome the above concerns. Renewable and bio-based raw materials based on agricultural waste, food waste or plastic trash will be employed for this purpose.

data.projectName: The Lived Life of the Entrepreneur (LLEnt)
data.projectDigest:
The main aim of the project is to strengthen entrepreneurial development in Pakistan. With several favorable environmental conditions such as a young population, growing data connectivity and a growing economy, entrepreneurship lies at the heart of The Government of Pakistan’s economic strategy. Yet due to ecosystem and infrastructural constraints, Pakistan lags behind other comparable countries such as Bangladesh and Nigeria in terms of start-ups and entrepreneurial activity, leaving some to conclude that Pakistan is ‘equipped for take-off’ but has yet to launch (e.g. McKinsey & Company, 2019). To date, much entrepreneurship research particularly that oriented toward policy and intervention development has taken place in western developed economies leaving something of a navigational lacuna for the Government of Pakistan’s ambitions (Kiss et al., 2012) for whom the challenge is to both to design a set of enabling policies as well as a facilitating ecosystem to support entrepreneurialism at a local level.
The proposal the ‘Lived Life of the Entrepreneur’ (LLEnt), would address this gap by proposing a novel methodology exploiting the affordances of digital technologies, the personal data economy and HAT (Hub of All Things) technology to generate practical new insights into the entrepreneurial journeys of entrepreneurs in Pakistan. Specifically, the twofold purpose is to design, test and implement interventions for the development of local entrepreneurial talent derived from a fine-grained understanding of becoming and being an entrepreneur in contemporary Pakistan. As such, this proposal is firmly located in the thematic area ‘Development Economics’ and specifically focuses on entrepreneurship.
