data.projectName: Enhancement of wheat productivity through an integrated approach using genomics and phenomics
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: By 2050, ~ 9 billion people will be residing this planet earth and an increase in global food production of 44 Mt/year is needed to feed these people. Wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) is a major staple food grown in 89 countries across the globe (FAO, 2017). Frequent changes in ecosystems and environments that have changed the climatic patterns have forced the scientists to breed new resilient cultivars of wheat. The task is challenging particularly with reference to wheat as this crop is a host of about 200 diseases and pests (biotic stresses) and is prone to drought, salinity, temperature extremes, nutrient deficiencies and mineral toxicities (abiotic stresses). Hence, an integrated approach needs to be adopted to improve wheat yield under various kinds of stresses. In this project we would like to adopt a multi-sectorial approach to evaluate the available germplasm of bread wheat at NIAB for various biotic and abiotic stresses and to identify molecular markers linked to these stresses. Furthermore, known genes linked to salinity tolerance and disease resistance in bread wheat will be incorporated in already approved cultivars.

data.projectName: Environment friendly Biotechnology development through biosurfactant production  for sustainable impact on Agriculture and society
data.projectDigest:
The proposed project on microbial biotechnology, offers safe solution to address agricultural issues (product yield, food security, insect pest, soil fertility). Growing scarcity of river waters, floods, soil erosion, drought, insect pest attack and climate change have endangered food security and agriculture productivity in Pakistan. Increase food production and economic growth have often come at a substantial cost to the natural environment. Need of innovative systems based on natural resources instead of synthetic materials is inevitable. Biosurfactant are environment friendly, easily synthesized from bacteria are biodegradable multi-functional compounds, safe alternate to existing chemicals for enhanced productivity and security of agriculture products. 
This multidisciplinary research and social awareness project is offered in this regard. It will be performed at Centre for Molecular Genetics University of Karachi to develop biosurfactant from bacteria; involving Department of Chemistry, NED University of Engineering and Technology to evaluate the chemical aspect of Biosurfactant, Department of Genetics, University of Karachi will reveal agricultural application and a strong international collaboration with Ireland University will facilitate technology transfer for standardization and sharing of scientific results and expertise. The project of agriculture biotechnology will enormously benefit food security, yield and human health, further produce beneficiary impact on environment and society.

data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
Ultra-wideband (UWB) is a short-range and energy efficient radio technology that is useful in high-bandwidth wireless communication. The principal advantages of UWB over alternative technologies (such as blue-tooth, Wi-Fi, radio-frequency identification (RFID), or global positioning system (GPS) signals) are much faster data transfer rates (1 GBps or greater), far better ranging accuracies, and extended device battery life. Some of the UWB technology applications operating in different parts of the radio frequency spectrum include: Ground Penetrating Radar, Security Monitoring and Imaging Systems, Medical Imaging Applications, integration with other navigation information and earthquake rescue etc. 
This study aims to assess the performance of indoor tracking of humans behind wall that uses through wall penetrating high bandwidth the state-of-art UWB technology. The proposed project has wide applications in the area defense and military system, target tracking, prisoner supervision, and rescue surveillance situations. For example, the project application could be effectively applied in the banks, commercial apartments, industries and schools that have been seized by terrorists. With the application of this project, we can track exact number terrorists and weapons behind wall (or through closed room). Therefore, the proposed research project addresses both the thematic area and a national challenge.

data.projectName: Micro-forensics and Laser Data Bases of Indus Basin Microbiomes for Bio-disaster Managment
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: Microbial threat is a major challenge for the country. Lack of proper diagnostic and identification methods puts the biosafety and food security of the people at stake. Conventional and molecular diagnostic methods used to identify the microbial agents, sources and cause of human, animal, plant and food crop diseases are mostly inefficient, misleading, laborious, time consuming and require a substantial revenue for import of high cost materials. The project addresses the development of spectral and molecular data bases of microbiomes (bacteria, viruses, algae, fungi) occupied Indus basin track of the country using Laser and Molecular Microbiology Techniques. Conventional, molecular and spectral (LIBS, Laser induced breakdown spectroscopy and Confocal Lens Microscopy and RAMN) analyses and methods will be used to identify and prepare the library of molecular and laser data records of the microorganisms isolated from soil, water and air of the area. The data bases will not only be useful to readily identify the causative agents of diseases directly in the field and at source and help adopt immediate measures of disaster management to cope with and revert the food and biosafety microbial threats. The outcome will trigger and motivate preparation of low cost, easy to handle  laser gadgets and diagnostic instruments in the country.

data.projectName: Universal Sign Language  for Touch Free Interface and for Deaf Community
data.projectDigest: Evolution of computer based interaction has been through a number of phases. From command line interface to menu driven environment to Graphics User Interface, the communication has evolved to a better user friendly environment.  A new form of communication is on the rise and that is Gesture Based Communication, which is a touch free environment basically. Although its applications are mainly for deaf community but smart mobiles, laptops and other similar devices are encouraging this new kind of communication. Sign languages all over the world have a dictionary of signs of several thousand words. Mostly these signs are word based which means that these signs do not make use of basic alphabet signs, rather a new sign has to be designed for every new word added to the dictionary. This research  suggests use of spelling-based gestures especially while communicating with smart phones and laptops. Although word-based gestures are in use all over the world, adopting spelling-based approach can bring a revolution for deaf as well as for an effective touch free interface.  Every region has its own sign language. Although the whole research in this area started with an idea to facilitate the deaf community but it actually formed the basis of touch free interface for smart devices. This leads to a very strong need for universal sign language.  Moreover, estimating start of a gesture and end of a gesture can be a very attractive area of research. At the moment it is very hard to separate symbols however in next few years advancements in technology will be able to easily handle this issue. Present research can recognize static gestures with great accuracy.

Design and application of a new sono-photo electrochemical Plant for industrial waste water treatment

As completion of URI-II dam by India in occupied Kashmir  on Pakistani waters is a serious violation of Indus water treaty . Therefore, the consideration of this project is inevitable based on three factors 1) national emergency 2)  water management and sustainability ( thematic area) 3) environmental pollution and climate change ( thematic area).

data.projectName: Development of Infra-Red Spectroscopic Algorithms for Real-Time, Qualitative and Quantitative Monitoring of Smog Causing Air Pollutants
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: In last few years, smog has been arisen as national level challenge for Pakistan which did not only imposed health threats to peoples but also harmfully effected social activities and traffic safety due to substantial decline in atmospheric visibility. Root cause of this smog issue is unregulated air pollutant emissions due to lack of government capacities for real-time monitoring and controlling these air pollutants from various anthropogenic emission sites. Real-time monitoring of these pollutants in factories, homes, and roads is important to avoid exceeding the harmful limits. Being developing countries Pakistan could not afford extensive rigging of foreign, sophisticated and expensive instruments to regulate these atmospheric emissions by real-time analysis. Therefore, it is the call of hours that Pakistani scientists should team up with foreign expert to indigenously device a cost-effective system based on facile analytical technique like Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy for real-time, qualitative and quantitative monitoring of smog causing air pollutants. Outcome of this project will strengthen government controls over air emissions, help to curtail down smog issue, improve health quality, traffic flow and social life of nation.

data.projectName: Sustainable Vegetable Production through Vertical Farming Practices in Punjab Province of Pakistan: Capacity Building and Economic Analysis
data.projectDigest: Vertical farming is a considered as an input efficient and water saving way of growing vegetables and fruits. With the current water stress condition prevailing in Pakistan, it is highly desirable. It would be part of adaptation to dynamic climate strategies. It requires less cultivating area and other inputs. It may become part of sustainable livelihood strategies adopted by households. There are examples in Pakistan where success stories are evident, for instance, Sarhad Rural Support Programme utilized the vertical farming techniques for training farmers on growing bitter guard and tomato in Mengora (Swat, KPK). Another example in this regard is evident is Agri-tourism Development Corporation of Pakistan’s concept of ‘Living Walls’ in order to attract tourists of rural areas of Punjab. NARC and PARC’s initiative on ‘kitchen gardening’ are also proven fruitful source of income for many families. There are potentially a range of vegetables which can be grown through vertical farming method, a few of those are cucurbits, bitter guard tomato, and cucumber etc, Reportedly, this technique can provide manifold returns to farmers than using traditional horizontal farming methods by utilizing the same available cultivable area. Although, vertical farming can be done in many forms. This project, however, would identify the most practicable and feasible method of doing it for most profitable vegetables out of their wide range. The project would utilize the success stories’ spirit through establishing a proper demonstration of vertical vegetable farming; by conducting training of farmers and experts and by doing economic analysis of vertical vegetable farming in detail.

data.projectName: An ERP study on the nature of semantic processing: Why do some Pakistani late English language learners  achieve proficiency and comprehension while others cannot?
data.projectDigest: The current brain and language study, using  neurolinguistics methodology of electroencephalography (EEG) of healthy brains will not only inform us about the semantic processing differences of second language  (L2)/ target language (TL) learners while comprehending and producing English language with proficiency or less-proficiency, but also inform us about developmental and language processing disorders of first language learners (L1) in Pakistan. The patterns of neural activity through event related potentials (ERPs) can inform us about how it is happening, why it is important and what can we do to ensure that our L2/TL learners can best improve their comprehension and proficiency in English language, and how we can offer the best care/intervention for language processing disorders, too. in other words, the  findings regarding neurocognitive semantic processing  can also inform us about the following question: Can the conditions that promote language learning in neurotypical individuals be applied to aid those with developmental language disorders or do the conditions that benefit learning differ? the current project anticipates to engage and train MPhil and PhD graduates in the field of Applied Neurolinguistics so that they can undertake solution oriented projects to help improve the quality of English language learning for multilinguals in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Trust deficit in Pakistan: causes, consequences and remedies in view of State of Medina
data.projectDigest:
A Society comprises individuals with comprehensive mutual interests, wherein, their goals are devised. However, a welfare state -broadly aims to ensure welfare, is not only based upon welfare rules and regulation but trust between individuals and state as well because it’s an unwritten and unspoken legal code that binds individuals in an unspecified social contract to be performed. We trust others to whom we are even barely connected – and all the more so business partners, classmates, spouses, and friends – to behave in ways that according to our shared values and anticipations. Because of its role as a foundation for society, the trust serves as a decisive component of successful collaboration, collective moral bearings, good governance, and rapid economic growth.
The core issue of Pakistan is the growing trust deficit between the people and the government. In Pakistan, people do not pay taxes to the Government because they perceive that the government does not pay back any benefits. Most people violate the rule of law because they do not trust the judicial system and take the law into their own hands. On the other hand, Prime Minister of Pakistan has been revealing in his speeches his vision and application of the standards of The State of Medina – a model of the welfare state. This research project aims to investigate the causes of the trust deficit and to explore the measures that should be taken to build trust in contrast to the state of Medina.

data.projectName: BIOCHAR – A shifting paradigm to climate smart agriculture
data.projectDigest: Modern world agriculture faces multiple challenges due to rapid increase in food demand and environmental concerns. Food security and climate change are the major global and national challenges and are primarily the result of poor nutrient management and anthropogenic release of greenhouse gases (GHGs). The agriculture sector contributes about 10–12% of the GHGs emissions. BIOCHAR can provide a “climate smart agriculture program” in Pakistan to overcome these challenges. The overarching aim of our research program between UAF-GCUF-Soil Survey of Punjab-Log Sujag is to establish the Pakistan Biochar Research Center and launch a BIOCHAR technology for climate smart agriculture by utilizing various agricultural/industrial biowastes as feedstock. The research program aims to boost soil nutrition, crop productivity and reduce nutrient losses, particularly nitrogen leaching and volatilization, for different soil types of Pakistan. Biochar-based nitrogen fertilizer will be fabricated and systematically tested in pot and field trials for rice-wheat cropping system, allowing us to minimize nitrogen losses and boosting crop yield. The outcomes of project will be disseminated to farmers, ministries and other stake-holders through interactive workshops/hands-on training. Ultimately, it will have a substantial impact on Pakistan’s economy and agriculture, thereby rolling-out BIOCHAR production and commercialization opportunities.

data.projectName: Responses and adaptations of indigenous herbaceous plants to climate change; climate modeling and conservation strategies
data.projectDigest: The global climate changes are continuously resulting in increased threats of mean temperature rise, drought and greenhouse gases in almost all major agricultural zones of the world. The climate change experts have warned that anthropogenic activities are continuously adding greenhouse gases into our atmosphere resulting in increased threats of warming, air pollution, and altered precipitation pattern. According to the International Panel on Climate Change, the effects of climate change could linger for hundreds of years, even if we are able to stop anthropogenic activities contributing to climate change. Moreover, the urbanization trends and the rapid growing vehicle number are continuously increasing air pollution in most parts of the world and Pakistan. The changing climate has exerted serious threats on biodiversity and ecosystems and increased the extinction rate of species. Experts have warned that deterioration of ecosystems will further increase the severity of climate change and will help the invasion of exotic species.  Till now negligible work has been reported regarding the estimation of effects of climate change on flora of Pakistan and conservation strategies. The natural flora of Pakistan not only help to reduce pollution, but also a source of medicines, food, feed and raw material of many industries.   The current work aims to explore the both threatened as well as best adopted plants to future climate of Pakistan. The outcome of the study will not only help to conserve the natural plant wealth of Pakistan but also to establish a climate change study center in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Linking Food Security, Food Safety & Economics by Addressing Challenges of Stunted Growth-Understanding to Intervention Plans
data.projectDigest: Malnutrition/Undernutrition has been recognized as leading cause of global childhood mortality (45% of all under-five mortality). In Pakistan, >37% children show stunted growth (faltering in physical and mental development associated predominantly with undernourished child gut) suggesting poor nutritional status. Micronutrients and plant based foods have significant but modest effects in improving growth but animal-source foods, including milk, meat, and eggs, have been shown to dramatically decrease malnutrition in children. Pakistan is already a large livestock raising country and recent initiatives by the current Govt. for further expansion to improve income of smallholder livestock production, will enhance the risk of exposure to neglected risk factors for early childhood malnutrition i.e. enteropathogens, which severely affects the undernourished gut of child <2 years of age causing stunting. Pakistan is ranked high as a poverty and zoonoses hotspot, therefore current proposal will demonstrate value of interdisciplinary research to address key challenges i.e. 1) Probing the links between smallholder livestock production, colonization of enteropathogens (source tracking to link with different livestock reservoirs & associated environment) & their impact on gut health and undernutrition. 2) Developing and testing remedial interventions at early age 4) Sociology/Outreach Education/Campaigns to prepare parents to help their children grow well.

data.projectName: Carbon dynamics in response to tillage, nutrient management and climate change under rice-wheat cropping system of Punjab, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Changing Climate is substantially affect crop yields, soil organic matter (SOM) and associated soil organic C (SOC). Maintaining SOM is vital for soil health and sustainable small grain production to meet increasing global food demands under changing climate. Rice-wheat cropping system is comprised of 2.2 million hectare and famous for basmati rice production. Due to conventional and intensive practices its productivity is decreasing in last few years. Three years challenge project will be conducted involving five tillage combinations and nutrient management practices in five major districts of rice wheat cropping system with the primary objective to predict and evaluate soil organic carbon, soil health and crop production for future (2050). Secondary objective to establish climate smart villages for promotion of climate smart agriculture. To achieve the objectives different academic, research and private collaborators will contribute their expertise in the project. The outcomes will be finally used to design best management which can provide more carbon storage and reduction of air pollution (rice burning) under changing climate in future.  This study will be useful for farmers, policy makers to implement conservation tillage in rice wheat growing areas to increase SOC and decrease soil loss.

data.projectName: AN ICT-BASED FRAMEWORK FOR STRENGTHENING THE MECHANISMS OF REPORTING, PREDICTION, AND PREVENTION OF FEMALE VICTIMIZATION IN PUNJAB, PAKISTAN
data.projectDigest:
In Punjab, women constitute 49 percent of the population. Despite constitutional safeguards that guarantee equality to all, women’s role in social, political, and economic spheres of life and their relative status remains marginalized, when compared to men. The female labor force participation rate is 26.5 percent as compared to 70 percent for males. The female literacy rate in Punjab is 57 percent as compared to the male literacy rate of 72 percent.
Female victimization (physical attack) is one of the many evils that exist in our society. This malice prevents the accomplishment of a secure and stable environment where females can go about their businesses in a comfortable manner. Two main roadblocks in developing countries like Pakistan in this regard are minimal reporting to law enforcement agencies and decades old reporting mechanisms that lack any significant ICT assistance, thus are less verifiable.
Eventually, the emergence of such pessimistic reporting behavior will gear up the process of deterioration of the society. The role of concerned remedial authorities must not be overlooked in this regard. Furthermore, recent technological developments in ICT sector must be incorporated to improve the decades old reporting mechanisms as well as to take preventive strategies on large scale.

data.projectName: Hydrokinetic Energy Conversion System (HECS)
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Pakistan’s energy needs in the domestic, commercial, industrial and transport sectors is growing at a rate of approximately 9%, 2.8%, 3.8% and 4.8% respectively, while overall demand for electrical power is increasing 10% annually compared to an increase in capacity of 7% . The main sources of energy are oil (43.5%), gas (41.4%), LPG (0.3%), coal (4.5%), hydropower (9.2%) and nuclear (1.1%). In addition to environmental concerns the reliance on oil and gas in the absence of sufficient natural reserves of fossil fuels, places the burden of hydrocarbon imports on Pakistan’s challenged economy, motivating the pursuit of renewable energy sources. The proposed research aims to utilize computational hydrodynamic and experimental techniques for turbine efficiency enhancement and their optimal placement in irrigation networks. High fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of Hydrokinetic turbine (HKT) will be carried out and study of appropriate augmentation channel characteristics for canals and rivers using large eddy simulation (LES) method will be performed. This work package will include turbine wake modelling and optimal array configuration. The experimental work package will focus on operational monitoring and mooring of turbine in a water tunnel and will be carried out at the water tunnel facility at SMME, NUST after upgrading it for the purpose. Towards the end of the project the prototype low flow rate hydrokinetic turbines will be deployed in the field in Pakistan for assessment. data.projectName: Developing Low Cost Graphene and its applications like battery, solar cell etc.
data.projectDigest: Graphene-based materials have wide industrial applications ranging from high frequency electronics, long-life batteries for electric cars & other energy storage applications, super-capacitors, solar cells, ultra-fast lasers, membranes etc. A key requirement for such applications is the development of industrial-scale, reliable and inexpensive production processes for graphene preparation. The federal cabinet of Pakistan has approved an electric vehicle (EV) policy that aims to increase the number of electric cars on the road, slash the oil import bill and curb air pollution. The primary goal of this project is to develop techniques for mass-production of Graphene to produce low-cost Graphene that can be used for development of low-cost, long-life, and light-weight, environmental-friendly Graphene based carbon batteries to be used for electric vehicle and smart grid. To make these batteries to be used at industrial scale it demands the development of a complete infrastructure comprises of Intelligent Battery Management Systems (BMS), High-power Quick-charging stations, high-current inverters for motor drive of electric vehicles and associated testing rigs. The secondary objective is to use the Graphene for development of other applications like solar cells, water filter membrane, coatings etc. This project can act as a stepping stone to take Pakistan to the next level in green energy and transportation.

data.projectName: Online surveillance, diagnostics, and prognostics of systems, structures, and components in industrial processes
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: The project proposes solutions for online surveillance, diagnostics, and prognostics (SDP) of industrial plants. Surveillance is the continuous monitoring of the industrial plants for abnormal or faulty situation. Once an abnormal/faulty condition arises, it is very important to know the source and time of the fault and its trend. This can be achieved using diagnostic stage.  The behavior and trend of fault bears the information about the plant remaining useful life. This can be achieved using prognostics stage. At this stage the system operator takes the decision about the plant operation.  With the current situation, the SDP are mostly offline. However, the with the new industrial revolution, the trend of SDP is shifting to online. The online SDP requires automation and need substantial amount of research to propose methodologies to achieve online SDP. The benefits involve in the increase in product quality, reduce hazards, increase in working life of various components of industrial plants.

data.projectName: Molecular surveillance program of Food Borne enteric Pathogens from mega cities of Pakistan and Turkey
data.projectDigest:
Diarrhoea is one of the known global health threat. Death estimated due this accounts up to 1.3 million of which 500000 of young children worldwide. Shigella is known to cause diarrheal episodes ?125 million annually along with enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (E. coli). These bacterial diarrheal pathogens are frequently reported in paediatric populations of South Asia due to unavailability of clean water, good nutrition, sustained sanitation and healthcare. Campylobacter jejuni is the main worldwide reason for gastroenteritis. 
The majority of infections result from consumption of poor quality food or water that is contaminated by animal / human faeces. Various public health preventive measures are required that include purification of water supplies, safe sewage disposal, treatment of chronic carriers, sanitary and hygiene education, especially among food handlers. The Pakistani region is highly endemic / epidemic in typhoid fever, gastric and enteric illnesses, especially during summer season. Keeping in view all above facts associated with enteric infections, present project is been designed to start surveillance program within different regions of Pakistan and Turkey to look into various type of food material for presence of enteric pathogens.

data.projectName: 5G Integrated UAV Base Stations for Disaster Area Coverage
data.projectDigest: In remote environments like disaster areas, especially in case of earthquakes and massive floods, where the communication infrastructure gets completely toppled, it is nearly impossible to develop reliable communication.  In such situations, an effective and viable solution is necessary. One such solution proposed in this project is development of 5G integrated drone base stations that can operate providing not only calling services but also reliable and fast data services to the affected users and rescue teams in the area. To optimize the solution further, combination of 5G integrated UAV base stations with research area of artificial intelligence (AI) is proposed, where the UAVs are programmed to work intelligently by taking autonomous decisions in swarms and perform autonomous location search for the optimized coverage deployment.

data.projectName: GreenAI
data.projectDigest:
The proposed project solves the agriculture inefficiency problem by creating GreenAI, a comprehensive Precision Agriculture (PA) solution for large-scale indoor and outdoor farming optimized for Pakistan. GreenAI takes a multi-pronged approach towards Precision Agriculture, deploying drones for large scale out-door farming at one end to developing small cabinet size in-door controlled farming units at the other. The indoor units shall also serve as a controlled environment for development of smart programs to monitor & detect conditions to improve plant health, resulting in improved performance of sensors in the outdoor environment as well.  State-of-the-art equipment shall provide actionable information to farmers without requiring any technical expertise in drone operation. Combined with intelligently designed equipment, GreenAI shall provide growers insights about their crops’ health, water stress and disease conditions that cannot be detected through naked eye. This will not only lead to early detection of detrimental conditions but also application of localized remedial measures resulting in increased yield and lower costs. 
Another novel enhancement proposed in GreenAI sensing techniques is the incorporation of compact Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) based imaging sensors that can be designed to measure both sub-soil and above the surface conditions. Moreover, SAR sensing is also not limited by weather conditions.

data.projectDigest:
The demand for designing efficient new bridges and replacing the deteriorating or aging ones is a worldwide challenge and Pakistan is no exception. There is a need for responding to the ever-increasing traffic volumes while also addressing related climate change and global warming issues compatible with healthy urban planning. Additional considerations include optimal use of sustainable and environmentally friendly materials coupled with rapid and safe bridge construction methods. The word “Beam” in this context is being used to refer to a typical bridge beam girder. The HCB consists of the following components: an outer beam shell made of fiber reinforced polymer (FRP); a concealed arch made of self-consolidating concrete; steel strands fully encapsulated into FRP resin at the bottom of the shell; and polyurethane foam used to fill the hollow space. The HCB, first used in USA in 2008, has so far been used in 18 bridges in North America and Australia. The current HCB design configuration results in a very impressive increase in strength when compared with conventional bridges. However, HCB design can be further evolved by adding an effective amount of prestressing combined with an innovative use of Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymer (CFRP) material. Thus, the present research proposal seeks to take the HCB design to its next higher-level of evolution with the goal of dramatically increasing its strength as well as performance under service load conditions.

data.projectName: Development of low-cost and selective sensor for the early detection of lung cancer
data.projectDigest: Cancer is one of the major causes of death in the world and lung cancer accounts for approximately one third of all cancer-related death in men and one quarter of all cancer death in women. Its diagnosis is typically delayed to the late stages of disease due to the asymptomatic nature of cancer in its early stages. Numerous conventional techniques that mainly chromatography and spectroscopic techniques are in practice for the detection and analysis of these biomarkers for lungs cancer but these techniques require sample preparation, preconcentration and many other lengthy steps to be followed before the sample analysis and furthermore limitation of to be applicable for real-time and online analysis. Therefore, it is of substantial interest to develop miniaturized robust, precise and accurate devices. The project aims to develop advanced, yet low-cost optical and electrochemical sensors for the early prediction of lung cancer - tackling a major healthcare issue of Pakistan and creating a reliable and affordable  solution for diagnostics and cure providing health care secotor, exploiting the benefits of photonics, optical fiber technology and sensor technology. In the proposal, a photonic crystal will be prepared and used as a heptanal sensor that is the biomarker of the lung cancer. More importantly, the recognition events of the created novel cancer receptors can be directly transferred (label-free) into a readable optical signal through a change in Bragg diffraction of the ordered macropores array of the sensor and thereby induce color changes that can be detected by the naked eye.

data.projectName: development of database of physiological signals, and mathematical model for classification of various diseases
data.projectDigest: One of the major challenges in healthcare is limited resources, especially availability of specialist physicians to patients. According to a WHO survey conducted in 2015, there is only 1 physician per 1000 population in Pakistan. This number becomes even more alarming when considering rural areas, and specialist physicians. One way to ease this burden is using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to diagnose some diseases. According to a recent extensive review on the subject, it is reported that AI can indeed diagnose diseases as accurately as health professions. But in order for AI to accurately diagnose a disease, a large dataset is required to train the mathematical model. This project proposes to collect novel, normative dataset of Pakistani population for diagnosis of various diseases, and design unique mathematical models for classification of these disease. The project requires collaboration of mathematicians to develop models to diagnose the disease, Pakistan based biomedical engineers to collect database, and expert with vast research experience in the subject, to help design data collection protocols, and feature calculation methods. The collected dataset will help scientist means of understanding diseases, and develop better diagnosis and treatment methods. The project has the potential to have a significant impact on country’s healthcare system.

data.projectName: Strengthening of Karachi Electric (KE) Power System for improved reliability by developing and utilizing Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) testing facilities
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Pakistan has accelerated the integration of renewable energy sources to its generation mix and is incentivizing manufacturers of EVs to invest in the country’s automotive sector. These initiatives, aiming towards sustainability, come with their challenges. Upon increased adoption of these initiatives, the reliability of the electric power system may be affected if remedial measures are not taken. Furthermore, these initiatives have the potential of enhancing the reliability of the system by requiring them to provided grid support services such as frequency and voltage support. This project aims at focusing on the three sectors of Generation, Transmission and Distribution to identify issues related to integration of renewable energy sources for Pakistan’s electric power network. Solutions based on renewable energy sources, electric vehicles and the ICT infrastructure will be proposed. The project plans to validate the proposed solutions leveraging hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing and for this a state-of-the-art Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) laboratory will be established as part of the project. The laboratory will not only help validate the proposed outcomes of this project, but also provide the stakeholders a facility to conduct model-based design, qualification and compliance testing, personnel training, and creating innovative technology testbeds with modeled representation of their electrical networks.

data.projectName: Association of depression with diabetes mellitus, metabolic syndrome, polycystic ovarian syndrome and subfertility
data.projectDigest: Diabetes mellitus is caused by reduced synthesis, or resistance to insulin. The altered insulin production or action leads to disturbed transportation amino acids especially tryptophan in brain. Tryptophan is the precursor of serotonin that plays a vital role in mood, sleep, dietary habits and memory and therefore, diminished brain serotonin levels results in mood disturbances. Additionally, uncontrolled diabetes also leads to obesity, metabolic syndrome and hormonal imbalance, polycystic ovarian syndrome in females and subfertility. The aim of the present study is to identify the association of diabetes mellitus with psychiatric disorders (depression and anxiety) as primary outcome while obesity, polycystic ovaries and subfertility as secondary outcome in adults of Karachi, Pakistan. This adult population will be assessed on episodes of depression and anxiety through validated questionnaires. Anthropometric measurements and laboratory investigations of lipid profile, blood sugar level and hormonal profile will be done in all subjects. We will predict the manifestation of these disorders through association with blood tests and scores acquired through questionnaires. The impact of the study will be an awareness of diabetes with these associated factors and assist in identification of high-risk individuals, stimulate disease prevention and control programs, along with guidance for lifestyle modifications.

data.projectName: Artificial Intelligence for the rapid identification of P2Y12 Antagonist - Drug for Cardiovascular Diseases
data.projectDigest: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly the machine learning approaches is latest techniques for the robust drug discovery and development that may serve a fastest way to find out the remedy of a disease. In current scenario of Coronavirus outbreak in China, scientist are applying machine learning techniques, for data analysis from social media and other sources for find out the sign, symptoms, diagnosis and spread of disease.  AI is very useful in the initial stage of drug discovery, including identification of target, hit/lead discovery, optimization of lead and toxicity prediction. G  protein-couple (GPCRs) receptors  represent  the  major  druggable  family. P2Y12 receptors are members of the purinergic P2Y family of GPCRs and are located on the surface of platelets. P2Y12R controls the activation of platelets and thrombus formation; hence some antithrombotic drugs targeting P2Y12R have been accepted for the prevention of myocardial infarction and heart stroke. But these known drugs have several safety limitations. Heart diseases have been reported to be the leading cause of deaths in Pakistan and according to the World Health Organization (WHO) 46 people dying of heart diseases in Pakistan every hour. It is essential to develop robust in silico procedures to evaluate the effect of P2Y12 inhibitors for the identification of lead. In this study, artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques will be applied to find the best remedy for heart diseases.

data.projectName: Open Government Data for Citizen Engagement, Improving Public Service Delivery and Transparency
data.projectDigest: The Government of KP has several public entities which are producing and commissioning large amount of data and information, whose public availability would make public offices more transparent, trustable, and accountable to the citizens and other stake holders. However, sharing data can poses serious issues and questions for Government of KP. Therefore, a strategy is needed to be formulated for the Government of KP Open Government Data (OGD) to perform cost and benefit analysis and provide a platform to collect and upload data generated by offices.  The research proposal is aimed to design Open Government Data Strategy (OGDS for designing, implement, and sustain OGD initiatives) for Government of KP to share non-sensitive/citizen-centric data generated by its offices. The OGDS would be designed and implemented within the framework of various related policies, acts and rules of the Government of KP. Thereby, would permit a wider spectrum of data collection and sharing for planning, development, research, openness, transparency, trust, and awareness. The strategy and OGD datasets would be uploaded on dedicated open government web portal, which will provide a platform to be accessed by general public, researchers, governance experts, data analyst, domain experts, and government for governance, transparency, and public service delivery.

Lamentably, because of absence of legitimate measures for verifying and saving regular assets, our nation is experiencing water shortage. In view of these ongoing water and energy crisis a very calculated research proposal is planned to tackle the issues strategically. Perennial underground Piston based water conveyers will be an integrated approach for water and energy conservation. It proposes to installation of underground water conveyers with special spillage system and smart turbines to produce electricity too. Along this water dissemination would be attached like barrages on short level to distribute water for domestic and agricultural purposes to the area concerned. Population of that area may contribute like bills for the unhindered functioning of the projects there under governmental command which may lessen the cost of energy, water bills and may save water from being wasted in floods and unattended spilling.  It needs vast surveys, site inspections, feasibility reporting to plan real-time applicable project plan to handle water scarcity, wastage and un-planned dissemination.

data.projectName: Sustainable pulses production through development of climate smart input responsive and high yielding genotypes along with innovative technology packages
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: Global food security also requires a major re-focusing of plant sciences, crop improvement and production agronomy towards grain legumes (pulse crops) over coming decades, with intensive research and development to identify climate-resilient species and cultivars with improved grain characteristics. The global climate change is the biggest challenge of the 21st century in the scenario of food security for increasing world population. The overall national challenge will be the Development of high yielding climate smart pulses genotypes having input responsiveness. Specific objectives set to tackle this grand challenge will be 1) Identification of input responsive chickpea genotype for irrigated areas 2) Induction of input tolerance in chickpea, lentil and mungbean through foliar application of environmental friendly growth regulators and 3) Selection and application of well characterized crop specific plant growth promoting bacterial inocula in the form of biofertilizer to improve plant vigor and yield of legumes with improved soil fertility.

data.projectName: Discovery of Market Signals for Sustainable Planning and Operation of Pakistan National Grid
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Locational marginal prices (LMP) reflect the value of the energy at the specific location and time of delivery. When the lowest-priced electricity can reach all locations, prices are the same across the entire grid. However, when there is congestion – heavy use of the transmission system – the lowest-priced energy cannot flow freely to some locations. In that case, more expensive electricity is ordered to meet that demand. As a result, the locational marginal prices are higher in those locations. The calculations used to determine LMPs consider electricity demand, generation costs and limits on the transmission system. The price tells market participants the cost to serve the next megawatt of load at a specific location. The calculations factor in all the available generating sources to come up with the mix that creates the lowest production cost, while observing all limits on the transmission system. Congestion generally raises the LMP in the receiving area of the congested transmission line as compared to the LMP in the sending area. Operating conditions that limit the delivery capacity of specific transmission lines can also contribute to congestion and result in LMP changes. This funding proposal aims to achieve following impacts on Pakistan power sector. Conventional generation and transmission expansion planning efforts will be complemented by discovery of market price signals across national grid. An LMP based optimization algorithm will provide anticipated electricity prices at all nodes of the national grid. Nodes with high prices will indicate most promising locations for development of future generation plants, whereas nodes with low prices will point to most suitable locations for load growth in the form of promoting development .

data.projectName: The Hybridoma technology: A preferred method for monoclonal antibody generation for diagnostics and therapeutics
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Herceptin a biologic medicine is a monoclonal antibody (mAb) made by hybridoma technology. First manufactured by Roche in 1998, has improved both survival rate and quality of patients suffering from breast cancer furthermore, a larger number of patients with stomach cancer can also benefit from Trastuzumab (Herceptin). Non-availability and non-accessibility of biosimilar (i.e. lower price generic) particularly for biologics is the root causes of the economic burden. In Pakistan biologics have to be imported. Breast Cancer in Pakistan is a looming epidemic. The treatment cost per month varies from Rs. 150,000 to 300,000. This brings forth the significance of developing the hybridoma technology to produce biosimilar. The mAbs produced by hybridoma have multitude of applications ranging from prevention, diagnosis and treatment of diseases such as cancer, heart, eye diseases etc.
In this project we propose to make biosimilar of Herceptin using hybridoma technology. The creation of hybridoma is a six-step process which can also be described as upstream production and downstream production phase. The upstream processes comprise of all the preparatory actions performed on the mice for antibody development and on the myeloma cell to make a fusion partner. The downstream processing is inclusive of long-term growth and antibody harvesting.

data.projectName: IoT Based Smart Hydroponic System
data.projectDigest:
Agriculture sector is vital part in the economy of Pakistan as it contributes almost 19% to GDP and also it engages 42% of labor. It stimulates development in other sectors as well as it is an important source of foreign exchange. As per 6th Census of Pakistan, held in 2017, the population is the country is rising at the rate of 2.4% per annum  and same is the case with covered land and this fast rise in population and land acquisition for housing are the major reasons behind increasing demand of agricultural products which can easily be accommodated using Hydroponics.
Hydroponic System is a method of sowing plants in an artificial atmosphere in which nutrients are provided through water instead of soil and by controlling the environmental factors like Humidity and Temperature to increase the production. Commercial interest in Hydroponics was developed among farmers for about 20 years ago, but again today this interest has renewed among cultivators launching Hydroponic systems. This is the specially the case in areas where there is growing concern of water scarcity and less available space for cultivation.

data.projectName: Development of Infant formula milk and its scale-up production
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: The infant formula milk belongs to dairy substitutes and is a synthetic replica of mother’s milk.  Formula milks are generally produced by blending carbohydrates, fats and proteins in proper concentrations using special techniques. Although there is nothing better than mother’s milk for infants, but sometimes it becomes necessary for infants to take formula milk in conditions such as absence of mother, infant allergy to lactose, traditional trends, improper composition of the imported relevant products in comparison to regional requirements, etc. The formula milks available for infants in Pakistan are imported products and are quite expensive as well. Hence the aim of the present project is infant formula milk production at national level that must contains required nutritional enriched diet to infant along with cost effective benefits. To achieve this aim, the objectives would include  production of milk-based formula from fresh cow milk (source of lactose and protein), plant sources (as vitamins, fats, whey protein) and fish oil extract (a source of DHA and EPA). Moreover, the extraction of the different essential and nutritional enriched components/ingredients of formula milk from specific natural raw material resources is of main interest as well. The methodology would involve standardization of fresh cow milk, followed by clarification, pasteurization, condensation, homogenization, spraying, mixing and finally processing. After production, formula would be tried on mammalian infants (rabbits and/or monkey) for product development and commercialization. The product would contain 50-60 parts of carbohydrate, 20-25 parts of lipids, 12-15 parts of protein, 1.5-2.5 parts of mineral salts and 2-4 parts of water, per 100 parts by weight of dry material.

data.projectName: FATF Challenge: Designing Long Term Policy Model for Pakistan
data.projectDigest: FATF presents a complex challenge to Pakistan. On the one hand, the country is faced with the menace of terrorism, which it has been fighting for over two decades now and sacrificed a big number of its people and resources. On the other, the country is faced with traditional security threat from India. This latter challenge is transforming into soft security challenge in the sense that India employs its resources to carry out international propaganda, lobbying, and diplomacy to push Pakistan into disadvantageous position in International political and economic system. Yet another challenge is the continuous instability in Afghanistan and presence of a number of terrorist organizations there, which make Pakistan further vulnerable. It is also worth mentioning that the super-powers that convinced Pakistan to enter in the War on Terror also did not come to the defence of Pakistan when it was being put on the Grey List.

data.projectName: Development of a multidimensional air quality management system to mitigate Lahore Smog
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: As the capital of Punjab and a vibrant metropolis, Lahore has experienced rapid development in the past two decades. The population of the city increased by an average growth rate of 4.07% from 1998 to 2017. In 2010-11, the economy was estimated to be around Rs. 945.6 billion. Its size went up to Rs. 1227 billion in 2014-15. The economic prosperity coupled with rapid urban growth had a severe toll on the city’s environment, especially its air quality. Since 2011, every winter Lahore gets covered in a thick blanket of smog. Smog is a combination of fog with several other air pollutants, e.g. particulate matter, smoke, aerosols and oxides of nitrogen, sulfur and carbon. This results in poor visibility, reducing even up to 25 m, and an increased risk of respiratory and cardiovascular diseases during the winter months. In December 2017, the Honorable Lahore High Court constituted a Smog Commission (SC) to formulate a “holistic” smog mitigation policy for Punjab. The commission highlighted that the data available to assess the prevalence of smog is scant and sporadic, and it advised the stakeholders to improve smog monitoring capacity as well as to implement measures to prevent it. The mitigation of Lahore Smog requires the development of a state-of-the-art air quality management system. To this end, this project proposes a multidimensional approach to mitigate Lahore smog. This approach integrates smog monitoring with effective policy-making with due consideration to socio-economic aspects of air pollution and requisite legal procedures.

data.projectName: Capacity Building and Skill Enhancement for Traceable Value Chains to Increase Mango Export from Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Food quality and safety have become as important requirements of modern food system. Overtime, concerns of sellers and buyers about quality of food are increasingly demanding  the details and background of food production systems.  As a result, traceability is emerging as one of the fundamental pre-requisites  in food production system especially for those connected with export. Pakistan draws it strength from agriculture sector where horticultural exports especially mango are significant.  There is strong potential of increasing mango exports subject to adoption and strengthening of proper traceability system which can respond to all query about any aspect and stage of the whole production and marketing system.  Field observation from a recent project on institutional reforms for improving horticultural markets in Pakistan exposed that current knowledge and capacity of mango value chain actors about traceability and decent work is not very encouraging and they need capacity building and skill enhancement to respond positively to emerging market opportunities . This is also vital to develop decency in domestic markets. So proposed project will focus on Punjab and Sindh provinces, approaching around 500 stakeholders to conduct baseline study and then after developing manuals, deliver training to them to improve their knowledge and skills. Further, advocacy for the subject would be started through policy dialogue and proper dissemination.  Potential collaborators have expertise in the filed  and they together can set approach to achieve project's objectives in time.  It is anticipated to use the foreign expertise of German and Brazilian professors to develop and deliver the training material.

data.projectName: Development of immunity genes based genetic markers for the screening of mastitis resistant animals
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
The dairy industry is one of the fast growing industries in Pakistan. Livestock contributes 55.1 percent in value added GDP of agriculture and has remarkable potentials to expand. There are many economically important livestock diseases in Pakistan (Khan et al., 2013). Mastitis is one of the shocking maladies of our dairy animals causing production losses to our livestock industry. According to the field surveys of livestock diseases of Pakistan, mastitis is ranked as number one disease of our dairy animals. It negatively affects the milk production, quality of milk, and farm economics. Increasing the disease resistance among dairy animals is therefore desirable because without controlling this disease, the national goals to develop dairy farming on commercial and scientific lines as well as the production of wholesome milk which conforms to the standards of WTO Accord would remain elusive (Bradley 2002). It is very difficult to comprehend with this disease because numerous environmental and genetic factors are involved in the origin and development of mastitis. Susceptibility and resistance to mastitis is a complex trait influenced by genetic variation of animals. Among these variations, the polymorphisms in immunity genes are principal key factors in defensive mechanism of mammary gland (Burton and Erskine 2003). 
This project will focus on polymorphism analysis of immunity of mastitis dairy animals (cows and buffaloes) and its association with mastitis. From molecular perspective, it is very important to develop immunity genes polymorphism based markers to identify the mastitis resistant and susceptible animals. Ultimately this study will envisage to improve the inherent animal health status and lay down the foundations of breeding for enhanced immune response.

data.projectName: Implication of solar technology and ecofriendly nano composite materials for providing safe drinking water in preventing water related disasters
data.projectDigest: As water is essential for all living system to retain life on the planet, it is indispensable to provide the drinkable water to the people for their good health. Drinkable water will always be the need of even a common man in all region of the globe. Global industrialization, which is inevitable for better life and its sustainability, always need better water treatment methods which are environment friendly. This project provides such an idea of using electrocoagulation powered by solar energy with ecofriendly nano composites for water treatment. There is no need of any harmful chemical during whole process. Successful development of mechanical apparatus and proficient completion of this project will ensure the patented methods for treatment of water and will provide sustainable solution to rapidly emerging water pollution. We shall also make sure to provide extra parts for water treatment plant along with entire setup so that people can use it for long term without any inconvenience for relatively long period of time. In short, this project is of great importance for common people and will provide very sustainable solutions to large number of problems. Water treatment plant is actually the hottest topic of all environment related issue.

data.projectName: TESTING OF LOW-COST MONOLITHIC STRUCTURES FOR NAYA PAKISTAN HOUSING PROGRAM
data.projectDigest: This research aims to address the National-level challenge of exploring innovative alternatives for low-cost housing by testing monolithic structures. There is major gap in knowledge/research on this subject in Pakistan, whereas globally it is a cutting-edge agenda for innovation. Monolithic structures have an intrinsic advantage of cost reduction over conventional composite structures because their curvilinear character enables loads to be distributed equitably across a larger surface area rather than becoming concentrated at a few points of a building. This reduces the need to add extra reinforcement or materials at any points of load concentrations, thus reducing material and labor costs. However, till the recent past such structures were expensive to construct due to the cumbersome design effort required for calculating the complex curved surfaces involved, and also due to heavy cost of the difficult curved formwork required during construction. Both these costs have become redundant due to the availability of time-saving engineering software solutions and also with advent of simplified inflatable formwork alternatives, respectively. Sufficient knowledge is available in published discourse for replication, but there are two significant particularities of the context of Pakistan that require a careful testing study before adaptation can be initiated in Pakistan. Curvilinear character of monolithic structures prompts careful testing before adaptation in the traditionally rectilinear construction context of Pakistan due to two particularities: limited availability of skilled construction industry workforce to handle curvilinear construction; and, socio-cultural acceptability of the relatively unfamiliar appearance of monolithic structures.

data.projectName: Stacked-Trait Transgenic Next Generation Maize for Smart Agriculture.
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan maize is cultivated on more than 1.0 million hectors of area, that produced 3.3 million tonnes of grain yield (Govt. of Pakistan, 2017-18). High demand of maize grain for poultry and livestock feed preparation require high yield of grain production per acre.  Major causes of low yield in Pakistan includes drought, high temperature, insects, pest and weeds. The use of the granulated pesticide is a routine practice to control the pest in the field. The farmers used poor illiterate labor that dropped the granular pesticide in the plant whorl manually.  The advancement in the genetic engineering techniques make it possible to build up the persistent resistance within the maize genome. The Successful use of Bt crystal protein encoding gene is one of the examples which is extensively used by the developed countries like USA, Canada, Australia and many others. Global warming is a serious issue that impact the crops yield adversely worldwide specially Pakistan. CEMB has developed protocol for transformation in maize and have successfully transformed Cry1Ac, Cry2A genes in local inbred lines.  So, this project will further help to develop resistance for drought, heat, major insect pests and glyphosate/glufosinate in local maize lines.

data.projectName: Analysis of Human Commuting Patterns: The Missing Link for investigating the Spread of Dengue in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Due to an overabundance of people. dengue is persisting in different regions of Pakistan and its extinction from the community is less likely. Therefore, the general aim of this study would be to explore the effect of human mobility on the transmission and persistence of dengue in Sindh and Punjab. The specific goals would incorporate (1) determining the root cause of outbreaks in terms of human mobility and daily commuting, (2) evaluating meaningful associations between human travelling, vector exposures and pathogen persistence, (3) developing independent contact networks, and (4) analyzing high/low endemic areas that act as reservoirs of dengue and using them to find priority/high-risk zones. A retrospective study can be used to map recent movements of infected people, pinpointing the hotspots /infection reservoirs from which they acquired the infection and others to which they may have transmitted it.

data.projectName: Smart Irrigation Management System
data.projectDigest: The research is aimed to develop a solution for optimal use of available water resources for agriculture need in Punjab in order to promote water productivity.   A Smart Irrigation Management System (SIMS) needs to be developed where irrigation water allocation is made on near real time basis by calculating crop water demand, monitoring weather forecast and knowing the available water reserves. Output generated from weather observations and satellite images can be very helpful in making informed decisions related to crop water allocation in a canal command and also guide farmers to use alternate sources of water to avoid crops water stress and vice versa. There is a dire need to integrate remote sensing, GIS, artificial intelligence, and Information & Communication Technology tools and develop a smart irrigation management system. SIMS would facilitate irrigation managers to take informed decisions for optimally using canal water and also guiding farmers to use alternate sources in required proportion.

data.projectName: Go Green Pakistan- A new approach to contribute quadruple enhancement in the efficiency of photovoltaic with the bimetallic Ag-Cu Nanowires Transparent Conductors in new Bimetallic Titanium and Graphene hybrid quantum dots.
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: This project aims to deepen the understanding of how to make cleaner and greener Pakistan by full filling the energy demands of Pakistan through solar energy.  It is high time that the government of Pakistan should invest in long-term strategies to solve the electricity crisis. This unprecedented dilemma does not only require supply side options but also compels efforts to address the growing demand for electricity. Electricity generation from solar power is a chief energy source in the move to clean energy production. No greenhouse gases emissions are released into the atmosphere when we use solar panels to create electricity. Keeping in view the 2020 slogan of Pakistan “Go Green”. We will synthesize nontoxic bimetallic silver copper nanowire transparent conductors in bimetallic Titanium -Grapheme quantum dot photovoltaic which will contribute the quadruple enhancement in the production of electricity naturally.We will synthesize cost effective, nontoxic and environmental friendly bimetallic Titanium -Grapheme quantum dot solar cells. Solar cells based on these quantum dots could convert more than 65 percent of the sun's energy into electricity. Frequencies in the infrared and far infrared regions that are characteristically difficult to achieve with conventional solar cells can be obtained using environmental friendly bimetallic Titanium -Grapheme quantum dot solar cells. Half of the solar energy reaching the Earth is in the infrared region. A quantum dot solar cell makes infrared energy easily accessible as any other.

data.projectName: Smartphone-based telehealth approach to reduce the burden of diseases in resource limited areas of Pakistan by innovative low-cost point-of-care diagnostics of microPADs
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest:
Analysis of a patient sample is paramount for disease diagnosis and treatment. Common, analytical modalities include ELISA, PCR/RT-qPCR, HPLC, GC-MS, LC-MS and NMR. These techniques, though highly reliable for diagnostics, are out of reach of most patients due to high cost, lack of good diagnostic laboratories/expertise. As, poor patients usually live in remote areas where disease burden is high and limited or no access to advanced diagnostic facilities, thus need low-cost, on-site/point-of-care (POC) diagnosis.
Microfluidics (manipulation of minute amount of biofluid samples) helps to develop portable healthcare diagnostic devices/kits. Whitesides lab (Harvard University) suggested using paper to fabricate Microfluidic Paper-based Analytical Devices (microPADs), as low-cost screening/diagnostic devices. MicroPADs could meet the ASSURED (affordable, sensitive, specific, user-friendly, rapid and robust, equipment-free and deliverable to end-users) criteria of WHO. 
Therefore, in this HEC-GCF, we will develop not only microPADs for variety of clinical analytes/pathogens but also integrate them for telehealth applications in remote areas. Telehealth functionality would be added to microPADs by embedding Quick Response (QR) code to read on-chip information by developing application software for smartphone-based POC diagnostics. This innovation will have real-life applications in screening/diagnosis to improve healthcare by low-cost tests to reduce national disease burden and health expenditure.

data.projectName: UAV based Crop Monitoring and farm management system using deep learning
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
Cotton is one of the most important fiber and cash crops of Pakistan, which earns foreign exchange for the country. Although, Pakistan is one of the leading countries of the world in cotton production .There are many reasons behind low cotton production such as low literacy rate of farmers, lack of advanced technologies. 
In this study, a low-altitude UAV platform with multispectral camera will be developed for the detection of pest infestations, disease instigated by plant and diagnosis of the nutritional status of crops for precision agriculture. This work mainly focuses on discrimination of healthy Cotton plants from infected and its nutritional status through calculation of spectral band and Spectral Vegetation Index; and designing a frame work for low-cost crop monitoring system. An intelligent detection system will be developed using convolution neural networks from labeled UAV multispectral imagery. Moreover, the UAV will be used for spraying pesticides over cotton plants where diseases have been identified, in uniform manner to control the pest. 
This research anticipates that low-cost UAV based platform with multispectral camera and state-of-art deep learning techniques would paved the approach for Cotton crop monitoring and management at farmland.

data.projectName: Leveraging China-Pakistan FTA (CPFTA) for Pakistan's garment sector
data.projectDigest: The textile sector is still unable to map the current capacity of cotton yield and garment manufacturing. We believe that the new phase of Free Trade Agreement (FTA) with China presents immense opportunity for Pakistan's textile sector. We need to Map the future demand of ready-made garments (RMG) and the capacities of Pakistani firms to supply to China in the RMG category with high demand. The study intends to use quantitative and qualitative techniques. Primary data will be collected to map the cotton yield and textile sector capacity. The study will use STATA software for mapping purpose. Similarly, qualitative and quantitative data will be collected to map the current capacity and need of textile sector of China. Then the study will use a Computable General Equilibrium (CGE) model to simulate the impact of various policies that can enhance productivity of RMG sector to supply to China and benefit from second phase of FTA. The study intends to use a two-country CGE model using MGTAP technique. We believe that project will be very interesting for the Ministry of commerce, Federal Bureau of Revenue (FBR) and textile ministry in particular and Government of Pakistan in general.

data.projectName: ALIVE - ArtificiaL Intelligence for Improving the Performance of Software Defined Vehicular Network-based Fog computing Environments
data.projectDigest: Intelligent transportation system (ITS) is an emerging next-generation transportation system and has recently received significant attention due to its diverse set of services, e.g., autonomous driving, intelligent traffic management, intelligent control, and intelligent dynamic information services. Therefore, ITS can be considered basically from two perspectives. (i) Road safety: Citing a report of the World Health Organization (WHO), the petition said Pakistan was ranked first in Asia and 48th in the world for deaths caused by traffic accidents.  ITS applications can be used to improve the road traffic system, including to avoid traffic accident. (ii) Socio-Economic: A major driver for the growth of next-generation applications and business models is the evolution of Fifth Generation (5G) networks that are readily available. 5Gs in conjunction with Vehicular Ad hoc Networks (VANETs) and Cloud Computing enable the development of vehicular cloud networks that support the execution of computation and processor-intensive applications. The existing approaches proposed for ITS lack in providing reliable communication support to those applications, which are delay-sensitive and need a quick response with very low latency (e.g., traffic safety applications). Using Software-Defined Vehicular Network-based Fog Computing (SDV-F), 5G, and artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms, ALIVE proposes an efficient communication framework to provide ultra-reliable low latency communications in highly dynamic environments that is still a crucial challenge. Second, ALIVE provides a socioeconomic benefit analysis in the context of Pakistan. Third, through workshops, we, along with the relevant stakeholders, will devise a strategy and policy to implement the ITS in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Overcoming the malnutrition problem in Pakistan using mushroom proteins
data.projectDigest: The problem of malnutrition is increasing with the increase in the poverty rate in Pakistan. A large number of populations are unable to get a balanced diet due to limited resources or low income. Because of malnutrition morbidity rate also increases both in children and adults as the malnourished body is unable to resist diseases. Almost half of all the children in Pakistan are chronically malnourished (stunted) while 11% are acutely malnourished (wasted). This situation leads to high mortality and morbidity rates among children less than 5 years of age, impeding their mental and physical growth and leading to significant economic impact on the country’s development and prosperity. Protein deficiency is the most serious issue to be addressed for maintaining the health status of the population up to the mark. To overcome the protein deficiency as well as to provide the therapeutic agents that will be effective against different diseases, the  current study will explore the nutritional and therapeutic properties of Pakistani species of mushrooms which includes Agaricus bisporus (button mushroom), Pleurotus ostreatus (oyster mushroom), Lentinula edodes (Shii-take mushroom) and Volvariella volvacea (straw mushrooms). From the literature review, it is clear that there is no data available about the protein contents of these mushrooms, though these are routinely used in some parts of the country. In order to further investigate the protein contents and nutritional value of these mushrooms, the current study will focus on proteins of above-mentioned species of mushrooms and will explore the total protein contents of each species. The purified proteins of mushrooms will further be studied for their therapeutic and nutritional values, immunity enhancing, anticancer activity.

data.projectName: Generation of Deep Learning based Chest X-Ray Radiographic Reports
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
One of the most promising frontiers in health innovation is application of Artificial Intelligence in the field of medical imaging. Visible images of inner structure of human body are captured through medical imaging for diagnostic and treatment purposes. According to World Health Organization, an estimated two thirds of the global population does not have access to basic radiology such as a simple X-ray. Global shortage of radiologists is adversely effecting healthcare delivery both in developing and developed countries. The problem of radiologist brain drain from Pakistan is well documented by V. Bari in his article published in Journal of American College of Radiology. Increased investment can compensate for scarcity of physical infrastructure in relatively shorter time period but development of skilled human resource for healthcare sector requires decades of investment and training.
Automated processing of medical images and their associated radiographic reports can augment work of a junior radiologist towards effective diagnosis. Pakistan’s ill-equipped healthcare infrastructure requires such technology intervention and innovative problem solving to effectively deliver services at scale. We propose a research project that will deploy image processing and Clinical Natural Language Processing (CNLP) to generate automated clinical narratives of chest radiographic images using deep leaning techniques.

data.projectName: Bayesian Techniques for  Prediction of Impact of CPEC  on the Air Quality of Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
In the current economic crisis at home, Pakistan is compelled to act swiftly to come out of the current situation.  China Pakistan economic corridor (CPEC) is a silver lining in the current economic scenario for Pakistan. However, most of the projects included in the CPEC can have their impact on the environment of Pakistan. For instance, about three-quarters of nineteen power projects under CPEC will come from coal-powered plants. Furthermore, new trader routes and industries in the special economic zones under CPEC will also impact the environment of Pakistan.  
Keeping in view the current quality of air in Pakistan, will the environment and people remain safe as Pakistan carries out plans to invest billions of dollars in coal-based power plants, new trade routes and economic zones under CPEC? To answer to this question a detailed study is required before we could predict what would be the actual impact of CPEC on the environment of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Development of Innovative Eco- Friendly and Antimicrobial Natural Dyes from Actinobacteria and Their Applications in Textiles: A Step Towards Green Revolution in Textile Industry
data.projectDigest: Textile industry is a leading export sector of Pakistan. It provides 57% percent of the total exports, and about 8.5% of the GDP of Pakistan. The textile dyeing practices mainly depend on the synthetic dyes which cause significant pollution issues especially water and land pollution due to the release of wastes and effluents in to the water channels. More over development of innovative, bioactive (antimicrobial, insect repellent), textile dyes, finishes, fabric etc from natural sources is the need of time to fulfill the requirements of modern textile trends and their increasing demand in the medical textile. The actinobacteria are Gram positive filamentous soil bacteria with high GC content in their DNA, and are established antibiotics producing organisms and produce exo-pigments as by-product in fermentation. These pigments are natural compounds and are biodegrade able and also some time exhibit antimicrobial activities. This project aims at the exploitation of these pigments in combination with antimicrobial compounds to develop the cost effective and environment friendly textile dyes, which could be used as an alternative to synthetic dyes. These natural dyes on one side will help to reduce the import cost of synthetic dyes in textile sector and on the other side will be environment friendly and applicable to the development of modern anti-infectious fabric for general and medical garments.
