data.projectName: Establishment of Integrated Resource Recovery Centre at Arid Agriculture University by the adaptation of Low Cost Technology
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
Developing countries are often lacking of waste recycling and treatment Facilities, where waste is still dumped in the open environment (Song et al., 2015). United Nations Human Settlement Programme has introduced a decentralized solution named as Integrated Recovery Resource Centre (IRRC) for solid waste management in secondary cities and in small towns in Asia-Pacific Region. The IRRCs are successfully operating in Vietnam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Thailand and Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Pakistan. The objective is to recover value from waste and provide livelihood opportunities to the urban poor. 
The first pilot IRRC in Pakistan was established in Jammu Kashmir Housing Society G-15, Islamabad, in 2014 by the collaboration of Arid Agriculture University and UN Habitat following the model’s success elsewhere in Asia.
Replication Potential in Arid Agriculture University
The analysis suggests that community-based waste management approaches offer a ‘best solution for cleaner Pakistan and value for money solution for donors and governments. They would also help address multiple targets under the Sustainable Development Goals, including SDG 3, SDG 6, SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities), SDG 13 (Climate Action), SDG 14 and SDG 15. In the specific case of Islamabad, there is an urgent need for replication and up-scaling of this successful model to other areas. The IRRC appears to offer a highly cost-effective way of improving waste management in the fast-growing cities of Pakistan. Expansion of IRRC will lead to large scale waste segregation and establishment of recycling industries in the country.

data.projectName: Block chain Based Traceability and Verification System for Textile Manufacturing and Exports
data.projectDigest: The proposed research project is designed to meet one of the major challenges to Pakistan’s textile industry i.e. how to achieve sustainability and trace ability in a fool proof way that fulfills the requirements of cyber-age generation-Z consumers and be in line with sustainable development goals (SGDs) of United Nations. This will be accomplished in way that Pakistan’s textile exports, at present, are mainly limited to staple products whereas, the hyper-cognitive generation-z is more inclined to buy premium, sustainable and more individualized products and the proposed blockchain based framework in this project will ensure to achieve above-mentioned requirements. It will not only satisfy the consumer but also help our textile value chains to enhance their exports and broaden their markets. The framework envisaged in this research project will be multiplatform compatible software, the heart of which will be its blockchain based cryptographic approach for handling the data, that will ensure both the consumers and all other stakeholders for the transparency of the supply chain. This will result in significant enhancement of our textile exports and decrease of the wastage of country’s natural resources by mitigating damage to the environment.

data.projectName: Radiogenomics of Brain Tumors – An economical solution for underprivileged, remote, and/or resource-starved clinical sites in Pakistan Duration of Project: 36 months
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Public Health Relevance (in Pakistan): Low-grade (LGGs) and High-grade gliomas (HGGs) are quite prevalent
in Pakistan. SKMCH&RC alone scans 1000 cases of LGGs and HGGs per year. There are very few clinical
facilities in the country equipped with histopathology and molecular analysis, expert neurooncologists and
neuroradiologists. Moreover, the total cost of a diagnostic exam is (at least) PKR 84,350 which is well above
the average monthly income of a middle-class individual feeding, on average, 6 family members. There are,
currently, no radiogenomic tools available in Pakistan for accurately predicting tumor genotype based on
multiparametric MRI scans only. The patient must proceed for an additional complicated (invasive) biopsy
followed by expensive molecular analysis for gold-standard prediction of tumor genotype. Robust and
accurate prediction of tumor genotype based on MRI scans only will significantly rule out risks and cut-down
costs by avoiding additional complicated invasive procedures.

Research Goal: Install a completely noninvasive and free of (patient) cost, radiogenomics framework for
robust and accurate diagnosis and prognosis of low-grade and high-grade gliomas for the underprivileged,
remote, and/or resource-starved clinical sites in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Low Cost Renewable Energy for All:  Hybrid off Grid and Grid Connected Architectures for Residential, Commercial and Industrial Applications
data.projectDigest:
The aim of this project is to provide green and clean renewable energy at a low cost through indigenous technology development using this project. This project will develop an off-grid and grid-connected model for different electricity consumers. This research includes the development of low wind speed turbines, sewerage water turbine, new energy storage system and fuel cell development.
The efficiency of Renewable Energy System (RES) will be improved by using cooling and reflector technique for solar cells, development of low speed wind turbine as high speed wind turbine technology is well established and high wind speed might not be available everywhere, design of low head hydro turbines to use the hydro turbine for low heads applications. This project also involves the design of sewerage/ drainage pipe integrated Pico and micro hydro turbines for generating electricity from sewerage water available at commercial multi stories buildings. For integration of RES, the project will utilize latest developed topologies for grid integration and synchronization in grid connected mode and energy management strategies for off grid users. The project aims to develop super capacitor based energy storage devices to be used for higher power density industrial applications.

data.projectName: CPEC as a cultural Invasion to Enclothed cognitions, Perceived Self-concept and Cultural Identity of Gilgit Baltistan Dwellers
data.projectDigest: This enlightening and insightful research is based on a pivotal aim of divulging the various outcomes in response to the foreign movement related cultural invasion in psychosocial living patterns of local dwellers of Gilgit Baltistan. By adopting triangular research, main goal is to reveal the imminent threats to indigenous enriched Balti culture in addition to the transformations in the perceived self-concept, identity patterns, cultural adherence of the local community which is likely to turn hazardous in wiping out the centuries old and intact cultural patterns that has fascinated the people around the world to this charismatic land of beauty and enthrallment. This is hypothesized that foreign movement in the Gilgit due to CPEC is posing imminent threats to their centuries old preserved intact cultural patterns of living, their perceived self-concept, enclothed cognitions and their cultural identity intactness. The sample will comprise of three generations sociologically and developmentally distributed across three phases of adulthood such as early, middle and late adulthood who had been living there since their childhood. The research will be carried out by adopting trifold triangulation phases. The findings carry significant implications as culture reservation policy guidelines will be formed as an influential outcome of this research venture.

data.projectName: Centralized Free-Space Optical Communication Network for Zone-specific Multilingual Voice Transmissions for Museums in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
The proposed project “Centralized Free-Space Optical Communication Network for Zone-specific Multilingual Voice Transmissions for Museums in Pakistan” delivers an ICT based solution for automation of tourists’ visits to the museums in Pakistan. The outcome of this intensive, collaborative, research would be a simplified ICT based solution which could be understood by the following scenario.
Consider a visitor (national or international), speaker of language X and Y only, enters a museum. He/She collects a map, a dedicated headphone and/or a smart phone from the information desk to enjoy the intellectual heritage and historical cultural objects. He/She arrives at some cabinet, full of ancient artifacts, and listens to the details about the objects in that cabinet from his headphone along with an option of browsing in smart phone. The headphone (dedicated receiver) receives this real-time information from the lights installed in the museum. He/She walks to next cabinet and automatically listens to all the details of the objects placed in that particular cabinet. He/She walks around various zones of the museum and receives to all interesting details automatically from lights via headphone without the need of any guide of his language or being disturbed by others. The visitor returns back with satisfaction that he fully enjoyed his/her visit.

data.projectName: Reshaping Tertiary Education through Learning Analytics
data.projectDigest:
Higher education sector in Pakistan is facing a plethora of challenges, including lack of resources, scarcity of qualified manpower, overcrowded classrooms, inconsistent governmental policies, and quality of the intake. Further, due to financial constraints, the federal government is gradually reducing the budget of Higher Education Commission (HEC). For the year 2018-19 Rs.45 billion were allocated and only Rs.21.465 billion were released, and for the year 2019-20 only Rs.35.830 billion are allocated. In this scenario where government is slashing the budget for higher education the big challenge is “How can universities promote student success and decrease cost of imparting higher education?”  
This project harnesses the potential of Learning Analytics (LA) to develop models that can bring new insights into the learning process of the students in a BS(CS) program and provide feedback to improve the chances of student success and reduce the cost of imparting education. This project will investigate four areas in this regard.  (i) How curriculum planning affects student success, (ii) Personalized remedial teaching and learning system for student success, (iii) Hybrid courses for cost effectiveness and its impact on student success, and (iv) What are the appropriate methods to provide feedback to teachers, students, and administration.

data.projectName: Design of an AI Tool for Automatic Building Damage Assessment in Calamity hit areas using Satellite/Aerial Imagery
data.projectDigest:
The impact of climate change resulting in extreme weather and abrupt weather changes is affecting us more than ever before. We are witnessing an increasing trend in natural disasters. The analysis of 7,255 recorded events between 1998 and 2017 reveals that 91% of the total natural disasters are climate-related disasters. Moreover, according to the Global Climate Risk Index (1999-2018), Pakistan is among the countries, which are most vulnerable to climate change. 
The climate change calamities, which may be based on ‘Geological’, ‘Hydro-meteorological’ or ‘Human-induced’ factors, all require an immediate situational awareness to provide adequate relief. A prompt damage assessment is an open problem world over. In Pakistan, where the relief infrastructure is primal, a delayed or false assessment means loss of lives at a catastrophic scale. A prompt identification and localization of damage, especially, damaged buildings after any disaster is critical for Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Recovery tasks. It is imperative not only for search and rescue operations but also for rehabilitation tasks. Hence, we propose to utilize the unprecedented advances in the domain of machine learning in this domain, by automating the building damage assessment process, while using satellite/aerial imagery of a calamity struck region.

data.projectName: Microfluidic assisted encapsulation of plant-based drug in polymer-conjugated silver nanocarriers for breast cancer targeted therapy
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is the second most breast cancer affected country in Asia. The conventional therapies such as surgery, chemotherapy and radiotherapy cause many side effects that kill the healthy cells and tissue damage. The plant-based drugs arise as an effective source of anti-cancer drugs because of their relatively less side effects. However, their usefulness is limited due to the poor biodistribution at tumor site in human complex body. The localization of these anticancer plant metabolites can be improved by encapsulating them in nanocarrier to direct the encapsulated plant-based drug specifically to cancer cells, thus leaving the normal cells unaffected. However, the non-uniform size distribution and shape of nanocarrier diminishes the biodistribution of drug in cancer microenvironment. The currently available methods lack the inappropriate drug loading. As a proposed solution, microfluidic devices promise controlled synthesis of drug loaded nanocarrier with high precision. This smart on chip drug delivery system will deliver drug encapsulated in nanocarriers to the localized and targeted site without harming the normal cells. This efficient drug nanoformulation technology ultimately eliminates toxic side effects, and may causes comfort to patients in future. It will also enhance the economy of Pakistan due to low cost indigenous cancer treatment.

The localization of these anticancer plant metabolites can be improved by encapsulating them in nanocarrier to direct the encapsulated plant-based drug specifically to cancer cells, thus leaving the normal cells unaffected. However, the non-uniform size distribution and shape of nanocarrier diminishes the biodistribution of drug in cancer microenvironment. The currently available methods lack the inappropriate drug loading. As a proposed solution, microfluidic devices promise controlled synthesis of drug loaded nanocarrier with high precision. This smart on chip drug delivery system will deliver drug encapsulated in nanocarriers to the localized and targeted site without harming the normal cells. This efficient drug nanoformulation technology ultimately eliminates toxic side effects, and may causes comfort to patients in future. It will also enhance the economy of Pakistan due to low cost indigenous cancer treatment.

data.projectName: Development of Policy Guidelines for Water Management, Productivity Enhancement and Sustainability of Groundwater Aquifer
data.projectDigest: In arid and semi-arid regions, interaction between surface water and groundwater plays an important role in geo-hydrological system. Interaction is often complicated by agricultural activities including water diversion, groundwater pumping, irrigation. Deep percolation of fresh irrigation water is causing dilution of underlying marginal and hazardous groundwater due to flow processes caused by natural hydraulic gradients. Groundwater pumping further induces these gradients and causes vertical turbulence enhancing, mixing of fresh and saline resources. This study is to identify technical and policy options for managing irrigation water with enhanced productivity and sustainability in Rechna Doab. Groundwater model in integration with surface water model will be used to analyze surface and groundwater interaction. The research project will provide reliable data on irrigation practices and water use efficiency in Rechna Doab that will be further used for modeling conjunctive use of surface and ground water for sustainability and productivity enhancement of irrigation water. A range of viable technical and policy guidelines to improve the productivity and ensure the long-term sustainability of finite groundwater resources in Rechna Doab will be identified. Data on groundwater quality will be gathered along with options to use the marginal quality groundwater, safely and productively.

data.projectName: TechHub as innovation platform for Pakistani Startups
data.projectDigest: The proposed project suggests how to bridge the gap between academia and industry. It does so by proposing and building a technology portal using AI & ML technologies with a solid framework for its adoption. That is, potentially, this portal will have the capacity to can make autonomous recommendations for knowledge and technology flow between academia and industry aimed to offer strategic guidance in the process of start-up creation, i.e., technology needs of the industry and science & innovation taking place in academia in the form of research, surveys, and startups. Such technology portals with simple features (not as proposed here) are numerous and few are very successful generating millions and impacting innovation spread significantly. In order to implement the proposed framework in the context of Balochistan, we shall collaborate with a national partner i.e. ITU that already has taken similar number of initiatives such as Plan9, PlanX and TechHub with the PITB. In addition, we shall collaborate with international partner, Dr. Anna Visvizi, from The American College of Greece. The proposed project directly aligned with SDG goal 8 i.e. to promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all.

data.projectName: Impact assessment of diet enriched with Moringa plant in a malnourished rural Pakistani population.
data.projectDigest: Malnutrition, especially among children and women, is so important that three of eight WHO’s “Millennium Developmental Goals” deals with it. Malnutrition in children cause underdeveloped immunity, stunting (low height for their age), deficiency to long term brain function and also results in high number of diarrhea associated deaths. People living below the poverty-line have limited resources and decreased access to nutritious food especially proteins, vital nutrient for growth in young children. Pregnant and lactating mothers and women of reproductive age are all at higher risk of nutrient deficiencies. This problem is worse in rural Sindh as compared to the urban areas. The solution that we propose is a nutritious plant called Moringa oleifera (locally called Senjana), which is indigenous to Indian subcontinent, has great potential but unfortunately underutilized in Pakistan. This plant has high amount of protein, iron and other vital nutrients. Recently, we have received funding to plant 40,000 Moringa plants in households of Matiari district and to educate the population about the uses and benefits of Moringa. Here in this study we are proposing to measure the health impact of Moringa leaves and fruit use as food and compare it with red meat usage in the rural Sindh.

data.projectName: Sustainable Green Energy using IoT and AI
data.projectDigest:
Globally and particularly in Pakistan, where access to remote areas is considerable difficult due to weak land connectivity and road haulage infrastructure. During the winter season owing to the fact that there is profuse snow in the region, providing reliable energy access and its associate operational and maintenance (O&M) is not an easy process. Therefore, the installation of renewable energy plants in distributed grid structure in remote locations is on the rise. Globally, the trend is green energy, therefor wind farms based both on and offshore accounts for 21% of US, 18% of Europe and 4% of China’s energy mix. Since the international trend is towards global energy following the same footprint, Pakistan in April 2019 announced to constitute 30% of its energy capacity from renewable sources such as wind, solar, Micro hydro and biomass by 2030.
Researchers at NCAI UET Peshawar are ambitious to leverage advanced technologies for uplifting their energy infrastructure to ensure the sustainability of renewable energy power plants via reducing maintenance costs. The proposed solution is to implement Internet of Things (IoT) based smart system for data acquisition on existing’s infrastructure health and efficiency statistics with an added layer of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to forecast failures and enable proactive preventive measures. Such a solution can be plug & play and modular in nature so that it is optimum for usage on the existing infrastructure without disrupting the system. The solution has been planned to revitalize the monitoring ecosystem in Wind turbines and Micro-Hydel Power (MHP) generation systems. This system will provide integration of the monitoring data of all the available renewable systems to bring a holistic solution to the existing challenges.

data.projectName: IoT Based Decision Support Framework for eHealth- Applied as a Module in Smart City Implementation
data.projectDigest:
The quality of life largely depends on the quality of health services. The history of eHelath starts from 1990 onwards in the form of small projects and initiatives of organizations, Public Private Partnership, and Donor agencies. eHealth can play vital role in connecting remote areas to cities for specialized consultations.
Currently there is no Public Sector eHealth program in any province in Pakistan. Provinces can implement eHelath services at provincial level in near future. This needs significant evidence in cultural and regional context. eHealth projects which are currently active in country should put special emphasis to study feasibility, cost effectiveness, sustainability and acceptability of services. 
There are no studies performed to identify residents’ perception of eHealth impacts and attitudes toward eHealth, just a few have assessed relationships between eHealth development and community satisfaction. 

This project aims at provision of eHealth services to the residents of a segment of the colony where Internet of Things would cover the ehealth devices based on Cognitive Radio Newtworks as communication platform. 
The details of the conceived project can be put in more cogent manners, had there been some more time. The details submitted here might have some variations.

data.projectName: Next Generation Modular and Configurable Battery Manufacturing
data.projectDigest:
Due to the lack of resources and infrastructure global challenges like energy and environment are far greater for a country like Pakistan. To counter these issues, Government of Pakistan (GoP) is focusing on renewable and green energy solutions. Recently, Electrical Vehicle (EVs) Policy is approved to utilize clean energy by reducing fossil fuels usage and its carbon emissions. Since, batteries are the most expansive component in EVs, therefore, their indigenous designing and production will bring sustainability to EVs industry. However, currently Pakistan lack such facility and batteries are to be imported, which will obviously increase cost of production and maintenance for the EVs, making it less appealing for the general public and harder for government to implement the EV policies.
This research focuses on indigenously designing and developing batteries for domestic and EVs usage. It will provide low-cost and cleaner energy storage solutions by considering all aspects from cell selection to module design, pack design, battery management and safety systems and battery production system. The batteries will be designed using modular and configurable approaches to facilitate ease (dis)assembly and reusage of cells for other purposes. The project also aims to develop a scalable pilot production line to assist automotive industries in developing full scale production set-up for batteries.

data.projectName: Exploring frameworks and factors for relocation (offshoring), productivity, performance, and competitiveness for industries in SEZs and SMEs.
data.projectDigest: The grand challenge for industrial economy of Pakistan is industrial performance and competitiveness of industries established and establishing in and outside special economic zones (SEZs) allocated under CPEC. Since massive depreciation of Pakistani rupee in 2019, accumulated inflation, un-employment, cost of production, and stagnant growth in exports, the challenges for Pakistani firms to be competitive in international markets have increased. However, Pakistan still holds advantages that could be hitched towards better economic growth, gaining substantial share in global production and exports because of SEZs development and CPEC. In this context, Pakistan aims at establishing resilient and potentially productive industries to initiate a new era of industrialization jointly or side-by-side with Chinese companies to be based in SEZs. Therefore, it is very tectonic to study one of the themes of “industrial performance, productivity, competitiveness and re-location of industries in SEZs” under the priority theme of “Development Economics”. To serve this purpose, in this project decision making framework for relocation decisions of firms will be developed. Furthermore, the critical operational capabilities, identification of critical success factors of productivity, performance and competitiveness will be determined. Multiple case studies of firms will be conducted by engaging industrial practitioners using iterative grounded theory approach.

data.projectName: Reform Processes, Gender (in)Equality and (Dis)Empowerment in Less-Developed Societies: Prospects and Challenges for the Women of Newly Merged Tribal Districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (Pakistan)
data.projectDigest: This project probes into questions such as, how the merger of FATA with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa will address issues of equality and empowerment for its female population? and in what manner such reform processes will affect the tribal women’s legal, political and socio-economic position. The tribal women have suffered under discriminatory and oppressive cultural norms and governmental neglect, which have not only deprived them of their due rights, but also victimized them through a denial of public spaces in the political, economic and socio-cultural realms. The tribal women have also disproportionately suffered as a result of a prolonged spate of conflict and war in the borderland, which has additionally made them displaced and disgraced. The reform efforts of the recent governments provide a good opportunity to assess the socio-cultural, political and economic prospects of mainstreaming claimed through these reforms i.e opportunity to empower the tribal women with the provision of access to political representation, legal institutions and socio-economic opportunities. The project will adopt qualitative methodological approaches of data collection and analysis and collect data from 7 newly merged tribal districts. The targets of the project will be achieved through collaborative effort involving multiple academic and non-academic collaborators.

data.projectName: Detection and Prediction of Cyber-crimes in the Dark Web
data.projectDigest: In recent years, a great number of organized crimes and illicit trade practices are taking place in the cyberspace. To have anonymity during illegal operations, criminals, crime syndicates and the terrorists are resorting to the Dark Web.  Since the Dark Web operates in a multi-layer security environment to keep its users anonymous, it works as a safe haven for the criminals. To find such illegal activities and to identify the associated cyber criminals in the Dark Web it is necessary to search the Dark Web to identify the users and their networks. The data gathered through the search process needs to be intelligently analyzed to obtain the trends of malicious activities and the interrelations across the malicious users. The result of the analysis could be used to monitor the activities and detect the anomalous and illicit events. The whole task revolves round three coherent and concerted processes, namely, the search, analysis, and detection through regular monitoring. Each of these processes are challenging and requires innovative techniques. In this project several innovative approaches are envisioned to carry out the necessary research to handle the search, analysis, and detection of crimes and identification of criminals and their networks in the Dark Web.

data.projectName: Eliminating Farmers’ Poverty Trap
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
The Project takes a holistic, targeted and functional approach to solving the food security problem in a sustainable way. Lack of efficiency in the agriculture sector has triggered a vicious cycle. We as a team will target the root causes of this inefficiency through targeted, well thought-out and tested interventions. Following are the key reasons behind food insecurity:
1.	Lack of Resources at the Farm Level
2.	Under-developed farming communities
3.	Obsolete farm machinery, methods and inputs 
4.	Lower Quality and Quantity of Yields 
5.	Food Insecurity
6.	Inadequate field analysis specific to region(s) 
Targeted interventions will be designed and implemented to eliminate root causes of all the above mentioned factors, thus breaking the vicious cycle of poverty, inefficiency and food insecurity.

data.projectName: Enabling Rural Connectivity with Low-Cost 4G/5G Pop-Up-Networks (PUNs) for Healthcare and Educational Needs of Disadvantaged Communities
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: Internet and mobile technologies have a transformative impact on communities.  According to 2019 GSMA report on the state of mobile internet connectivity, around 10% of the global population is still not covered by mobile broadband. In Pakistan, the situation is even worse with more than 20% of our population living without broadband connectivity. This lack of coverage is concentrated in rural and remote areas of Pakistan lacking basic healthcare and educational facilities. Our main objective is to develop innovative low-cost technological solutions, technology education programs, and social-business models for providing high-speed & on-demand mobile broadband connectivity to address the healthcare and educational needs of disadvantaged communities in rural and remote areas of Pakistan. The project has two broad dimensions i.e., technology and sustainability. We will design low-cost self-organizing 4G/5G pop-up-networks (PUNs) using off-the-shelf technologies that will enable pop-up -clinics and -classrooms in rural areas. To make the project sustainable, with the help of rural community, we will develop technology education programs, social-business models, and will assess the benefits for scaling and policy recommendations. The project is collaborative in nature, well supported by sectorial partners, and international collaborators. The project brings together faculty from science, education, business, and economics background.

data.projectName: Composite materials: Next generation solution for Pakistan’s future manufacturing economy
data.projectDigest: The first decade of 21st century has witnessed a paradigm shift from conventional metallic materials to the composite materials, being light weight, durable, cheap, quick to fabrication, for different applications. The global market of composite materials is growing at CAGR of 7.7%, and there is huge potential for Pakistani manufacturing/ construction/ sports/ automotive industry to adopt composite as alternative material. The objective of current proposal is to provide scientific/knowledge-based solutions to meet national needs and upgrade it as exports-based industry. The GCF is split into eight work packages namely exploration of composite materials as an alternative in construction (WP1), composite materials in automotive and aerospace industry of Pakistan (WP2), composite Materials in Sports and household applications (WP3), development and adaption of novel technologies for composite fabrication (WP4), development of nanofiller reinforced biopolymers for Packaging (WP5), development of eco-friendly elastomeric nano composites (WP6), development of functional polymers for composite applications (WP7) and marketing and Implementation (WP8). These work packages cover different aspects of the domain including composite materials as replacement of conventional materials (WP1, WP2 and WP3), introduction of newer fabrication technologies (WP4), novel functional composite materials (WP5, WP6 and WP7) and the harnessing their social impact (WP8).

data.projectName: 3 years
data.projectDigest:
In Pakistan, due to scarcity of freshwater, agricultural land is insufficiently irrigated. Wastewater from tanneries represents a potential steady source of water if it can be treated to remove toxic hexavalent chromium. The purpose of this collaborative project is to develop approaches to purify wastewater by the action of microorganisms for subsequent use in crop irrigation and food production. 
Chromium (Cr) is extensively used in various industrial processes such as mining, alloys manufacturing, tanning of hides and skins, and pigment production etc. However, it is regarded as the priority pollutant due to its highly toxic, teratogenic, mutagenic and carcinogenic nature, and U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) also categorized it into Group ‘A’ human carcinogen. 
In the short-term, the highly chromium-resistant microorganisms isolated in the course of this work will be produced on a large-scale for use in the treatment of tannery wastewater in lab-scale trials. The innocuity of the resulting wastewater for crop irrigation will also be tested for growth of vegetables for food production. Finally, chromium reduction processes involving the isolated microorganisms will be implemented for full-scale application in the treatment of tannery wastewater.

Finally, chromium reduction processes involving the isolated microorganisms will be implemented for full-scale application in the treatment of tannery wastewater.

data.projectName: The future of Transactive Energy Systems for Pakistan – a techno-socio-economic study.
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Electricity powers the engine of progress and is deemed necessary for growth of nations and their prosperity.  Electric grids, however, are changing rapidly transitioning from a monolithic monopolistic government owned entity to a democratized and distributed network of grids much similar to how internet has evolved over time. In Pakistani context this provides an even more challenging and exciting opportunity.  Where at one end, Pakistan is energy starved and constrained due to the financial limitations and steady growth in population, but at the same time, the diversity of need, and the severe scarcity of the electricity provides an opportunity to test, model, evaluate and build energy systems. The challenge is a techno-socio-economic problem requiring an understanding of the consumer behavior, and needs and building the technology solution to resolve the energy demand issues of the country.  To this end we propose a multi-disciplinary study to survey, model, simulate and propose next-gen energy solutions for different consumer sectors. Then use this to conduct a need analysis of technology which feeds into the infrastructural and technological solution building. The consortium to conduct this study includes NUST, LUMS, University of Karachi, GIFT University, Namal college, AJK University, Sky Electric, K-Elecrric and CPPA.

data.projectName: Bioaugumentation of pH effected soils with effective Rhizobacteria for enhancement of phosphorous solubilization and Chickpea yield
data.projectDigest:
Chickpea is one of the important crop legumes widely grown and consumed in sub-continent especially in Pakistan, India, USA, Middle East and Africa. Chickpea is among the oldest pulses and a crop legume of great value owing to its high protein contents. In comparison to the other countries, cultivation of the chickpea crop is greater in Pakistan and India, however, it’s per hectare yields is among the lowest in the world. Considering the total cultivated area and gap between actual and potential yield of the chickpea in Pakistan, there is a great opportunity to develop modern agriculture methods in order to improve the chickpea yield.
The soils in Pakistan where chickpea is cultivated are alkaline in nature. It has been reported that, acidic and alkaline soils renders phosphate bioavailability to the plants and thus reduce the overall productivity of the agriculture systems. One of the promising methods could be the use of soil and plant root microbiomes that contains phosphate solubilizing and plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria for the improvement of the chickpea yield in pH effected soils. These microbiomes represent a diverse microbial community of beneficial bacteria that have the ability to colonize plant roots and stimulate plant growth and development. In addition, application of such beneficial microbes also helps in competitive inhibition of plant pathogens by improving plant immune system. Besides, extensive research, soil pH is still considered as a major factor responsible for the low productivity of agriculture systems. Therefore, the aim of the proposed project is to screen and develop enriched synthetic microbial communities for improving chickpea yield in pH effected soil systems.

data.projectName: Evaluation of Micro RNAs as Therapeutic Targets and Tools in Chemo-Resistant and Sensitive Malignant Tumors of Breast
data.projectDigest:
Breast cancer occurs in both males and females but it is one of the leading causes of deaths among females worldwide. Pakistani females unfortunately have the highest prevalence of breast cancer in Asia. The major obstacle in the successful treatment of breast cancer is the resistance offered by the cancerous cells to various chemotherapeutic drugs. Many contributors have been identified to confer drug resistance to malignant tumors of breast (Mansoori et al., 2017). The microRNAs are among the recently identified factors which have been linked with the activation of drug resistance related molecular pathways in breast tumors (Majumder and Jacob, 2011). On the other side of the coin, many studies have reported the exceptional potential of microRNAs to be used as a therapeutic agent and enhancing susceptibility of drug resistant breast tumors towards certain chemotherapeutic drugs (Liu et al., 2019a). However, the mechanisms through which microRNAs cause resistance or sensitivity to drugs have not been fully understood. This project is therefore being initiated to study microRNAs induced resistance or sensitivity mechanisms and evaluate the role of microRNAs as therapeutic targets and tools for successful treatment and management of the disease. 
Breast cancer is not only the national health problem but indeed a global issue. This project is an attempt to reduce burden of chemotherapeutic applications and associated side effects on patients having chemo-resistant tumors. The life expectancy and survival rate of the breast cancer patients will be considerably improved. Other benefits of microRNAs guided treatment strategy include higher efficacy and cost effectiveness which make it more suitable choice especially for the least patients having chemo-resistant tumors.

data.projectName: Disruptive innovative program on investment in human capital, and training to develop knowledge-based economy
data.projectDigest:
The importance of knowledge-based economy (KBE) in this century is obvious. One of the most important pillars of KBE is to develop a competitive knowledge economy through value addition. As Improve Pakistan’s score on the World Bank Institute’s Knowledge Economy Index from 2.2 to 4.0, and increase internet penetration to over 50% is the key object   and a major task in vision 2025 Pakistan   (Commission, 2014). 
Human capital competencies are a key component of value in a knowledge-based company, yet few companies report competency levels in annual reports (Tocan, 2012). Human capital is the new scarce resource in the knowledge economy compared to financial capital in the old economy. The skills and knowledge of people are of central importance to innovation and to economic and  productivity  growth,  with  a  well-educated  and  highly-skilled  work  force  essential  for success in the KBE (Arundel, Van Cruysen, & Kanerva, 2008). 
The knowledge-based economy” is an expression coined to describe trends in advanced economies towards greater dependence on knowledge, information and high skill levels, and the increasing need for ready access to all of these by the business and public sectors. The application of Information Communication Technologies (ICTs) has adopted a substantial importance and become inevitable for knowledge economy. Advances in information technology are recognized as a tool for economic growth. The project focused on the production and management of knowledge in the frame of economic constraints, or to a knowledge-based economy. In another meaning, it refers to the use of knowledge technologies to produce economic benefits. This project will covered local school and colleges in district Multan Punjab Pakistan.

data.projectName: AN EMPIRICAL ECONOMIC ANALYSIS OF AGRICULTURE PRODUCTION AND SUPPLY CHAIN BEHAVIOR AMONG FRESH PRODUCE IN THE CONTEXT OF CPEC AND PMEC (PAKISTAN MIDDLE EAST ECONOMIC CORRIDOR) INITIATIVE PIONEER MODEL)
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Regional connectivity framework can help to address SDGs regarding food security and hunger. The transportation cost of fresh produce becomes relatively high due to nature of the product and mode of transportation. CPEC is initiated under the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), to exploit geographical linkages for cost reduction and increasing market access and competition. Pakistan has extensive trade ties and comparative advantage in trade with Middle Eastern countries based on social, cultural and ethnic linkages. The gravitational model support distance and economic size for flow of fresh produce. CPEC has potential opportunities for Pakistan, in terms of reducing distance and expanding economies of size and scale. Distance will be covered by road, rail linkages developed under CPEC. Size will be addressed through agricultural investment in model farms. This has created an opportunity for fresh produce of Pakistan to be transported through sea instead of air, thus, reducing cost of transportation by 80 percent. Pakistan can exploit this opportunity by developing Pakistan Middle East Economic linkage to get maximum market share of fresh produce. Value chain analysis of fresh produce in Pakistan and China will provide an opportunity to exploit the potential of emerging markets.

data.projectName: Safeguarding the marine environment by developing integrated assessment and treatment systems for run-off from Lyari and Malir rivers
data.projectDigest: Coastal salt marsh environments are highly productive ecosystems besides their environmental and economic benefits. Lyari and Malir rivers collect industrial and domestic wastewaters which are polluting the Karachi coast and deteriorating the coastal life and habitats alike, that are intricately linked with human sustenance and quality of life. This necessitates accurate assessment of the quality of wastewater dumped into the Arabian sea and developing effective and sustainable ways to protect the marine environment. Coastal salt marshes represent a rich resource but complex ecosystem and to achieve our objectives, an integrated, multi-disciplinary approach seems to be the most appropriate way forward. To improve the quality of waste water received by the Arabian sea coast, sustainable primary wastewater treatment plants will be developed on lab-scale which would be scaled up for practical application. Public partnership would be exploited for scaled up treatment plants as various industrial giants are disposing the industrial waste in Malir and Lyari rivers without treatment. To achieve the objectives for regular pollution monitoring, state-of-the-art pollution monitoring laboratory will be established at CEMB and additionally a mobile testing lab will be procured to accomplish the task.

data.projectName: Coastal Marine Ecology Monitoring and Assessment Using Indigenously Developed Unmanned Underwater Data Acquisition & Analysis Systems
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Coastal marine ecosystem plays a vital role for sustainable development and economic growth of a country. Pakistan’s coastal region constitutes one of the main resources for food, employment, and economic revenue, and is a potential source for living, mineral and natural resources. 
Presently, the marine ecosystem of Pakistan is being threatened by environmental challenges that are causing degradation of marine biodiversity of this region. It is necessary to devise suitable mechanisms which can assist in monitoring adverse effects so that remedial can be incorporated.
In order to meet this essential national requirement, a system comprising of hardware and software components for underwater marine ecological data gathering and analysis is proposed.  For this purpose, unmanned underwater robotic platforms will be indigenously developed and used for collection of data using sensors mounted on these unmanned vehicles. Collected data will be analyzed by Marine Scientists.  
Coastal and marine ecological data will be gathered from Marine Protected Areas such as Churna will be collected and analyzed by the team experts.  These areas feature coral reefs which are exceptionally biodiverse in nature. These reefs experience significant direct and indirect anthropogenic pressures, and provide a sensitive indicator of coastal ocean health, climate change, and ocean acidification.

data.projectName: DEVELOPMENT OF NATIONAL MUSHROOM RESEARCH CENTER (NMRC) IN UNIVERSITY OF KARACHI FOR OPTIMIZING RESEARCH & COMMERCIALIZATION.
data.projectDigest:
Mushroom is an edible fungi and a vegetable of unique importance. It has become an integral part of fast growing fast-food & cuisine network in Pakistan. This is a nationwide project that will cover two urgent solutions of public and scientific concern.
First issue is the, 
•	Absence of a reference center that can report edible and non-edible wild mushrooms in Pakistan. 
•	Diseases of mushrooms have been little addressed. 
•	Introduction of foreign strains has been little commercialized.
Second is the technology transfer for local communities of remote areas. Such remote areas are widely distributed under various agro climatic zones of Pakistan. They include but not limited to the Northern Himalayan mountainous regions, deserts of Punjab & Sindh province, barren mountains of Sulemanki region in Baluchistan. It indicates that mushroom production has wider scope in Pakistan if optimized on sustainable basis. 
Hence a project has been designed to establish a National Mushroom Research Center (NMRC) for the research and commercialization of Mushroom technology in Pakistan. First phase of the project will be the establishment of research facility at University of Karachi. It will include a Mushroom biotechnology lab, Mushroom pathology lab, Growth chambers and storage rooms.

data.projectName: Sustainable utilisation of water via efficient management of rivers and storages
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Efficient river management is essential in improving water resource utilisation and in ensuring steady socio-economic development of a country. However, river flows are adversely affected by unregulated in-flows, e.g. due to heavy rain and hill torrents, which, if not forecasted and managed in a timely manner, cause flooding. Moreover, mismanagement of the water storages can also cause flooding, or water scarcity at times, with a huge socio-economic loss to the country. It is therefore necessary to improve the management of water resources and employ innovative socio-technical approaches for the conservation of water resources.
	Pakistan has been experiencing flooding and water scarcity year after year, and it has seen a rising trend in the recent past. This is not only due to the lack of effective prediction of unregulated flows, but also because of not utilising the indigenous small storages along the rivers and because of not properly accommodating river related multi sectoral constraints. The proposal aims to explore some of the critical stretches of Indus River, and demonstrate the potential of effective prediction and management methods, based on control engineering techniques, to solve the existential water crisis in the country.

data.projectName: Tackling Plastics: Sources-Sinks-Solutions
data.projectDigest: The accumulation of plastic in the environment is a global concern. Knowing with precision how and where litter is generated and its associated toxicity; its link to biodiversity/human health is important to target priority areas to address the problem. A recent projection has revealed the plastic waste will continue to be disproportionately high in Asian continents in the future year. However, at the same time, plastic waste can be used as a useful feedstock for energy production and chemical synthesis. Therefore, in this work, we set out to see both sides of the coin. First, we will access the magnitude of plastics, risks and relate it to the economic burden it shares. This will enable us to take the necessary policy and mitigation measures to minimise the impacts. At the same time, we aim to develop new routes for selective degradation of plastics to release chemicals for meaningful use (microbial fuel cell), and seeking biomass derived ecofriendly alternatives to plastics together with community and youth engagement for better management.

data.projectName: Critical Metals in Photovoltaic Cells to Produce Renewable Electricity from Sunlight
data.projectDigest: Sunlight is one of the greatest source of current and future energy resources of the world. Depletion of nonrenewable commodities including fossil fuels, nuclear fuel and up to some extent water have placed greater stress on the production of electricity from renew¬able sunlight. According to International Energy Agency electricity production from renewable resources will be increased by 50% between 2019 and 2024. The expected exponential dependency on solar energy is due to its massive and widespread availability. The solar energy that reaches the earth every hour counts more than all the energy currently exhausted by human activities each year. Electricity generation from sunlight increased demand of major silica, aluminum, copper, zinc, lead, iron and critical cadmium, indium, gallium, selenium, germanium and tellurium commodities for manufacturing the photovoltaic cells. Silica, aluminum, copper, zinc, lead, and iron are readily available in the earth crust. However, photovoltaic cells critical elements that used in advanced thin-filmed photovoltaic cells with extremely high light absorption, conductivity, electricity efficiency and durability are scarcely available in the earth crust. The main focus of the current research is to  explore cadmium, germanium, indium, gallium, selenium and tellurium in zinc–lead, copper , bauxite and coal deposits of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Upgradation of Rawal Dam water quality by applying coagulation coupled with membrane filtration for removal of trihalomethanes and trihalomethanes precursors.
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Pakistan has ranked third in world countries facing acute water shortage according to a report by International Monetary Fund (IMF). The current proposed study is focusing on water quality of Rawal dam as this is a main source of drinking water for Rawalpindi and Islamabad. But the overall water quality of Rawal dam is not upto the mark even after treatment. People of twin cities are left with no other option rather to buy bottled water for their potable means. Bottled water is an expensive option and lack the necessary mineralization required for human body. More than half of the population of twin cities and particularly residents of low income areas cannot afford the bottled water and are compelled to drink the contaminated water. This is a very alarming situation and great challenge for the capital of Pakistan. Occurrence and limit exceedance of trihalomethanes in water supplies is a national and international challenge (EPA, 2007).  This research challenge can be addressed by coupling the coagulation with membrane filtration. Chemical coagulation will increase the size of natural organic matter particles in the form of large flocs and ultimately enhance the removal of natural organic matter from water and downstream application of membrane separation will decrease the availability of natural organic matter for trihalomethanes formation (Amjad et al., 2015).

Occurrence and limit exceedance of trihalomethanes in water supplies is a national and international challenge (EPA, 2007).  This research challenge can be addressed by coupling the coagulation with membrane filtration. Chemical coagulation will increase the size of natural organic matter particles in the form of large flocs and ultimately enhance the removal of natural organic matter from water and downstream application of membrane separation will decrease the availability of natural organic matter for trihalomethanes formation (Amjad et al., 2015).

data.projectName: Indigenous development of nanocomposite coated cutting tools for manufacturing industry
data.projectDigest:
China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) is important for Pakistan to overcome its economic woes, social and energy problems. Industrialization is one of most influencing factors in economic growth in terms of improving life standard of a common Pakistani. Manufacturing industries contribute in economy in terms of exports, employment, foreign exchange earnings. But all manufacturing processes use machining processes for better product. The cutting tools is basic component of any machining process. In Pakistan, industries are spending much income to import basic tools and components to meet their operational needs. 
The Cutting tools life is very small because its cutting motion generates high stress and high temperature which triggers failure. To resist the wear failure, tool must have high hardness, thermal stability, oxidation resistance, chemical inertness, fracture toughness. Currently local manufactured cutting tools with different coatings are using in the industry but its substandard quality badly effect the machining process.  Multi-layered nanocomposite coated tools are not manufacturing in Pakistan which have good combination of high hardness and thermal stability. In this project we will develop different multi-layered nanocomposite hard coated tools which  will enhance productivity by increasing metal removal rate, without compromising the tool life.

data.projectName: Ultrasonic Assisted Machining Technology for Advanced Composite Materials Used in Sustainable Energy Equipment
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan has a wind power generation potential of 135 Giga Watt, but the actual share is only a few percent in power generation mix. The limited number of wind farms operating in the country consist of imported wind turbines. This gives rise to the need of indigenous design and development of wind turbines. As turbine blades harness energy from the environment, they need special consideration in terms of long-term performance in usually harsh weather conditions. 
Wind turbine blades are made from advanced composites such as Nomex honeycomb structures, aerogels and carbon-fiber composites due to their high-strength, lightweight, resistance to temperature and humidity. To accurately manufacture the profile of a wind turbine blade, a special purpose machining process, ultrasonic assisted machining process, is used. The machining system consists of ultrasonic generator, transducer, horn, spindle and the cutting tool (rotary or knife-edge), axially vibrating with ultrasonic frequency.
This research proposal aims at acquiring the ultrasonic assisted machining technology, gaining experience and hence investigating the optimized cutting parameters to guarantee an energy efficient and high-quality machining of advanced composites for profile generation of wind turbine blades. This will comprise one major step in indigenous development of small and medium scale wind turbines.

data.projectName: Development of a novel nano-enabled allergen-specific immunotherapy as curative treatment for milk allergy
data.projectDigest: Millions of people are affected by food allergy throughout the world including Pakistan. Significant surveillance on prevalence of food allergy in Pakistan has not been reported yet. Among food allergies, milk allergy is the second most prevalent in Pakistan specifically in infants.  Unfortunately, no effective and practically applicable treatment of milk allergy is present so far. Recently, Allergen Specific Immunotherapy has emerged as a potential allergy treatment, however, to achieve long term efficacy is quite challenging. In milk, casein are the major milk allergen protein and its structure is thus suitable to develop an allergen-specific immunotherapy. On the other hand, addition of medicinal plant extracts like Curcumin, Quercetin and Piperine etc. that are known for their anti-allergic potential may enhance the quality attributes of the allergen specific nanoparticles. So, slow release of Casein with anti-allergic bioactive compounds can be a good strategy to enhance tolerance to milk allergen. Therefore this study aims to develop a novel nano-enabled immunotherapy against milk allergy by encapsulating anti-allergic bioactive compounds in casein nanoparticles. Nano-encapsulation of curcumin with Casein will serve as a model to explore other bioactive compounds’ interaction with casein and their effect on immune tolerance by in-vitro assessment. On successful results, clinical trials will be preferably performed in the allergic patients.

data.projectName: Proposal to Achieve Group Antenatal Care through an Integrated Development Model; Feasibility and effectiveness for Sindh, Pakistan
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Pakistan has a high maternal mortality ratio of 140 / 100,000 livebirths, and one of the highest neonatal mortality ratios of 46/1000 births. The vast majority of neonatal deaths occur due to three main causes including sepsis (36%), preterm labor (28%) and birth asphyxia (23%). More than one-third of maternal and neonatal deaths occur within the first 24 hours of birth and most of these can be prevented by providing good quality antenatal care (ANC) and facility-based skilled intrapartum care. Therefore, our primary objective is to determine the impact of Global-ANC, government's Poverty Reduction Program and the combination of G-ANC plus PRP on maternal nutrition, compliance with ANC and outcome of newborn in the first month of birth.  We will measure mother’s nutritional status by Hemoglobin level, mother’s weight, birth weight of the newborn and the survival rate at the end of first month of life.

data.projectName: Quantitative microbial risk assessment and management of coastal communities of Pakistan: a solution-driven approach
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
Coastal communities, comprising 10% of the population of Pakistan (M.M Rabbani, 2008), mostly working offshore, are dwelling in the vulnerable state on or near the surface of the water. These free-floating and coastal residents do not have the essential elements concerning access to safe drinking water, sanitation systems, and health care. The offshore communities are more prone to acquire waterborne diseases as they dump their daily waste into the water bodies. These habits build the contamination load in already polluted water systems that make various health risks for inhabitants. 
Quantitative microbial risk assessment of a floating village located at the Manchar lake (one of our preliminary studies) revealed that the probability of infections of lake and drinking water on consumption was high and calculated to be 72 % and 68 % of fecal contamination, respectively. As a result, the prevalence of the disease was found high in the free-floating communities. Our observation also revealed that coastal communities did not possess an effective communication system to disseminate information and emergency alerts for offshore communities related to health care. That was also the main reason for the transmission of the pathogens. Thus, this multi-sectoral study will address these problems and their solutions for offshore coastal communities.

data.projectName: CO2 conversion to valuable chemicals using hydrogen through biomass gasification
data.projectDigest: A relatively recent concept of carbon dioxide conversion to the value-added products including fuels and other chemicals has made its way into the research activities as it serves the dual purpose of reducing carbon footprints as well as sparing fossil fuels. The conversion of CO2 into single carbon containing chemicals is relatively easily achieved however inherent thermodynamic stability (?Gf° = ?396 kJ mol–1) and inertness associated with C-C coupling reactions is a major hinderance towards its utilization for liquid hydrocarbons. Using a combination of reverse water gas shift (with ?H573K = 38.0 kJ mol–1) and Fischer Tropsch (with ?H573K = –166.0 kJ mol–1) reactions is among the promising pathways to produce liquid hydrocarbons from CO2. There are some advancements in finding a suitable combination of heterogenous catalyst system to selectively obtain long chain hydrocarbons from CO2, but low yield of C5+ species (about 16%) owing to excessive hydrogenation forming methane is major obstacle. A combination of dual catalyst system (metal oxide on zeolite) provides good selectivity for liquid hydrocarbons however the catalyst is prone to forming coke inside zeolite pores.

data.projectName: Sustainable Manufacturing by Integrating Advanced Robotics and Automation Technologies in SMEs (SMART SMEs)
data.projectDigest:
Small and medium sized enterprises (SMEs) are the driving force of many manufacturing economies including Japan, China, Brazil and Malaysia. The importance of SMEs in the industrial development of any country cannot be overemphasized. From Pakistani perspective SMEs constitute nearly 90% of all the enterprises, employ 80% of the non-agricultural labor force and their share in the annual GDP is approximately 40%. Nations all over the world give huge importance to SMEs for stimulating economic growth by enhancing their support to SMEs through developing and implementing an integrated SME Development Framework, which clearly lays down roles and responsibilities of institutions to support SME development in a holistic manner.
Despite importance of SMEs, recent trends and statistics suggests that the process of growth of SMEs in Pakistan has slowdown from last few years due to shorter product life cycle and decreasing customer tolerance time. The slow pace of growth of SMEs can be attributed to absence of advanced and latest technologies within manufacturing sector. The PI, through this research project aims to initiate research and development process on integration of industry 4.0. in manufacturing sector by transforming existing SMEs to SMART factories. The integration of advanced technologies within existing SMEs has the potential to give rise to manufacturing sector of Pakistan and make it capable to compete with industries of other countries which will not only benefit economic growth of the country but also produces employment opportunities.

data.projectName: A demonstration and evaluation of efficacy of inclusive low-cost sustainable  housing and associated assistive products
data.projectDigest:
The Grand Challenge Thematic area being addressed in this proposal is focused around Urban planning. The proposal addresses the Pakistan National challenges of 1) limited quality living spaces with respect to all types of comfort; 2) a need for low-energy consumption buildings to avoid overloading local supplies and reducing the carbon footprint of energy generation; 3) buildings and interior fittings and products that accommodate the needs of elderly and disabled people; and, 4) the need for an integrated approach to water supply and sanitation within building systems. 

The aim of the project is to deliver realized solutions for low-cost, sustainable efficient living spaces and associated products through the application of novel ways of integrating electronic products and systems into houses and products, through additive manufacturing and non-conventional building and product materials, based around wood pulp products.

The National challenges are aligned with the United Nations (UN) Sustainable Development challenge goals to end poverty; and, promote inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all.

data.projectName: VITAL – Vitamin-D deficiency, Impaired lung functions and  Tuberculosis from indoor Air pollution in Living environments  A growing health challenge for residents of Lahore, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Poor quality of the indoor living environment is a critical public health menace with severe health implications. Unfortunately, the indoor air pollution (IAP) is not considered as environmental hazards and public health issue at the policy level in Pakistan. This study investigates the causal linkages between built environment induced IAP with its associated biomarkers of health loss such as vitamin D (Vit D) deficiency, tuberculosis (TB) and impaired lung functions. Middle-income households of Lahore, Pakistan was chosen using machine learning-based two-step spatial clustering. The study will be operated in three work streams (WS). WS1 - measuring the indoor environmental parameters of the chosen households. A questionnaire-based survey will be conducted on 1500 residents for information on housing design, ventilation system, energy use, healthcare behaviours, TB clinical symptoms and markers for respiratory disease. WS2 –include a prospective two-stage longitudinal randomised clinical trial study. WS3 – developing structural relationships between the energy use, health risk and design index. The significance of sustainable cities and communities are forayed through evidence-based recommendations to improve indoor environmental quality. With support from the collaboration of national/international organizations, this study attempts to impact a million lives who are unaware of health burden that their own house can create.

data.projectName: Tackling Antimicrobial Resistance of Food borne  Zoonotic pathogens of greatest concern  in one health perspective
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
Increasing antibiotic use is driving an increase in antibiotic resistance, in both humans and animals. Because resistant bacteria can be transmitted between humans and animals through contact, food products and the environment, the use of antibiotics in animals plays a role in human health. More antibiotics are used in livestock and agriculture than in humans, more often to promote growth or prevent disease than to treat sick animals. Many of the agents commonly given to animals are the same antibiotics relied upon to treat human infections, raising concerns about depleting the effectiveness of these agents at the expense of human health. In many cases, the same strains of resistant bacteria are found in animal, human, and environmental sources within the same community.  Present Project proposal is designed to address and tackle the AMR in zoonotic bacteria in food including milk/milk products, meat (beef, mutton, poultry)/ meat products. 
                                              Through this collaborative project we are interested to document antibiotic residues and  zoonotic pathogens present in the milk, meat and milk and meat products meant for human use. Secondly we are also interested in antibiotic resistance profiling and its molecular basis in  these zoonotic pathogens ( E.Coli, Salmonella, Brucella, MRSA etc ) in particular. The project will also focus on the   development of molecular diagnostic approaches to diagnose antibiotic resistant genes in the zoonotic pathogens those are most common reason for antibiotic use in dairy animals and poultry birds. Thus reducing the use of antibiotics in animals. The information obtained will be used to change the behavior of farmers and veterinarians regarding use of antibiotics in poultry and Livestock.

data.projectName: Development of transgenic resistance in Potato against salinity and drought stress by the expression of ABF gene(s).
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Potato is a valuable food crop worldwide. Potato plants are highly exposed to salinity and drought, which adversely affects the tuber yield, quality and commercial value. Pakistan is the seventh largest potato producer, but currently substantial losses have been reported in potato crop yield due to the high susceptibility to adverse environmental conditions. Latest estimates indicate that approximately 23% decrease in total potato production in Pakistan is due to high temperature, drought and salinity. The development of transgenic potato varieties with higher yield and enhanced tolerance to adverse environmental stresses is a main objective of this project. Keeping in view, the project focuses on the development of transgenic potato plants, with the constitutive expression of the potential candidate ABF4 gene. To evaluated the ABF4 gene expression on tuber yield and quality (sprouting and carbohydrates content) and resistance against salt and drought stress. As according to an estimate salinity and drought are the predominant abiotic stresses that affect plant life and serious losses may occur resulting in arable lands of more than 50% by the year 2050. Hence food security is a major issue in the coming years.

data.projectName: Pakistan Civil Service Effectiveness Index (PACEi)
data.projectDigest: In pursuance of the vision of Honourable Mr. Imran Khan, Prime Minister, Islamic Republic of Pakistan, we have a proposal for developing an index, aiming to measure the effectiveness of the civil service, that is, Pakistan Civil Service Effectiveness index (PACEi). PACEi would provide Government of Pakistan (GoP) a tool for assessing the overall effectiveness of her civil service and identifying areas needing continuous control and reforms, if required. PACEi aspires to become an essential tool for performance improvement in the civil service of Pakistan. The extant research maintains that effective civil service can play a pivotal role in the prosperity of the country. However, it is yet to be clarified that what makes a civil service “effective”. Recently, in 2019, a global index namely International Civil Service Effectiveness (InCiSE) has been developed by the University of Oxford and the Institute for Government, the UK. They developed InCiSE by integrating available civil service indices of 38 countries. Unfortunately, InCiSE has not included Pakistan, for an obvious reason that no such index exists here in the country. By the way, InCiSE has some limitations as well, for example, concerning the assessment of organizational effectiveness, it needs to be more inclusive. It does not embed certain aspects of effectiveness, e.g., goal attainment. Furthermore, since the index is global, therefore, it does not cater to the context of any specific country like Pakistan. While, PACEi would focus on the Pakistani context. Moreover, it would be more inclusive in terms of embedding all four aspects of the competing values framework (CVF), i.e., internal process, open system, goal attainment, and human relations.

While, PACEi would focus on the Pakistani context. Moreover, it would be more inclusive in terms of embedding all four aspects of the competing values framework (CVF), i.e., internal process, open system, goal attainment, and human relations.

data.projectName: Augmentation of traditional defenses with moving target defense
data.projectDigest: Majority of the defenses employed for networks todays are static in nature. Such traditional defenses create information asymmetry, giving the attacker an unlimited amount of time to study the defenses, craft an attack and exploit the network. The current proposal aims to reverse this situation by augmenting the traditional defenses with novel Moving target based defenses such that the overall system changes its parameters (like the hardware platform, the operating system(s), The run time environment, the application being executed, network characteristics such as IP address, ports etc) continuously thereby increasing the uncertainty, time and cost for the attacker. It also addresses the problem of hidden backdoors that could remain undiscovered in a breached network for an extended period of time due to static nature of defenses.

data.projectName: Designing of Flexible Polymer Based Composites with Advanced Electrical Properties for Energy Applications
data.projectDigest: Rapid increase in population and modernization lead to worldwide increase in energy crisis due to the ever increasing energy demands. The progress of any country is based on its energy resources to meet its energy demands. Need of time is to provide inexpensive energy production and storage devices with advanced properties. Dielectrics are used fundamentally in every area of electronic industry and great attention has been given to the advancement in dielectric materials technology. In pursuit of developing high?performance dielectric capacitors, numerous efforts made to enhance their energy density and the storage efficiency for their wider applications in power electronic industry, self-charging power textile and military arena. For large scale application, these high-performance dielectric capacitors generally require low-cost fabrication, microstructural modifications for enhanced energy storage properties and advanced mechanical properties. The present research proposal aims to synthesize flexible dielectric materials with highest energy storage performance. Dielectric capacitor materials will be synthesized with high mechanical strength, flexibility, high charge storing ability with very low energy loss. Moreover, easy available, environmental friendly, easy to handle, more stability and most importantly cost effectiveness will be the key properties. Resultant material products can be used to produce energy devices like capacitors, transistors, dielectric gates and photovolatics. It will contribute to research related to energy harvesting. Also it will contribute to Pakistan’s electronic and electric industry to fill the gaps between energy demands and available energy resources.

data.projectName: Alleviation of aflatoxin contamination in peanut by the identification of candidate genes for flavonoid biosynthesis
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Food security has been a major concern over the past years all around the world. One of the major food security concerns is Aflatoxin contamination that has destructive health out-turns and financial consequences.  Improving access to better quality food is fundamental to every living individual. Currently, under the age of 5, over a 150 million children have experienced chronic malnutrition and the number is increasing every year.  Food security in Pakistan has been under a persistent threat during the last decade, a period concurring with a global food crisis that peaked in 2008. According to WFP, about 95 percent of Pakistan’s 121 districts have suffered hunger and diseases linked with malnutrition and food quality. The pervasive spread of microbiological, chemical or other food safety hazards in food continues to be a severe issue to the food authorities. These world problems can only be tackled when the quality and nutritional value of food is enhanced. Peanut crop, also known as groundnut is a widely grown crop all around the world. It is a plant-based protein which makes it the best candidate for tackling issues like food security and mal-nutrition. Flavonoids have been reported to minimize the production of aflatoxin in crop plant by providing resistance against Aspergillus flavus. Discovery and characterization of flavonoid candidate genes will be a step forward in developing peanut varieties exhibiting elevated levels of beneficial flavonoids. This will not only boost peanut production but also upgrade the peanut seed and oil industry by combating the global issue of allergies caused aflatoxin in peanut plant.

data.projectName: Evidential Monitoring to Devise Strategic Action Plans with Solutions to Combat Smog and Protect Bio-Environmental Health
data.projectDigest:
Air pollution and population health, there are many combinations of stresses that affect human health, the health of other organisms, and ecosystem functioning. The solutions to combat air pollution issues like smog will have wider interrelated impacts, that will likely to be even more beneficial in a broader analysis. This proposal will give emphasis to a series of plans, goals, and measures aimed to understand why, how, and from where the smog arises. Smog is caused by emissions which comes from different sources, including traditional crop burning practices, brick kilns, vehicle fuel emissions, wood burning and from various industries. 
With the innovative solutions and research orientation, this project proposal offers a systematic procedure to engage national and international experts from the academia, government and related industries. These collaborations will be helpful in nurturing students, solve industry related problems and devising pragmatic solutions to combat those problems. 
The collaboration among different academic and sectoral partners will not only help in understanding the problems in depth, which will drive to devise rational solutions for betterment, but will also yield sustainable solutions along with enabling to devise mechanism for prevention and mitigation through regular monitoring, scientific analysis and rectification at the source.
