data.projectName: Climate Modelling Initiative in Pakistan in Support of Integrated Climate Resilience
data.projectDigest: The optimization of regional climate models for local use is imperative for deliberating on the critical impacts of climate across multiple sectors, to support strategic development and to enhance the capacity of decision makers to adapt to a rapidly changing climate. Such research activities are particularly relevant for Pakistan, which will continue to remain extremely vulnerable to climate change and its associated impacts. This project seeks to augment the national ability to engage on climate science for the benefit of the agriculture and health sectors, as a first step, to demonstrate national capabilities in this field. By optimizing regional climate models to local context derived from the technical expertise of national and international partners, several conclusions will be drawn.  These include, but are not limited to, agricultural productivity and air quality that can enhance outreach and decision-making among stakeholders across government, private sector, academia and the common man towards collective action under climate adaptation, using state-of-the-art technology, techniques and data dissemination platforms.

data.projectName: Ameliorating symptoms of b-thalassemia by manipulating ?-globin levels through gene editing technologies
data.projectDigest: The prevalence of beta (?)-thalassemia carriers is about 1.5% worldwide which is further high in Pakistani population (5%) due to prevalence of consanguineous marriages in the country. ?–thalassemia is caused by mutations in ?-globin gene resulting in compromised ability of hemoglobin to carry oxygen after birth. More than 350 mutations in ?-globin gene have been reported which exert functional consequences on the hemoglobin synthesis in children. Before birth, fetal ?-globin is involved in the formation of hemoglobin. The fetal ?-globin genes are ordinarily silenced at birth and are replaced by the ?-globin genes. It has been an established fact that natural conditions causing lifelong persistence of fetal ?-globin ameliorate the debilitating effects of ?-globin gene mutations. So, therapeutic reactivation of fetal ?-globin gene is being considered as an ideal and novel treatment of ?-thalassemia patients. We propose to re-induce the expression of fetal ?-globin gene by disrupting BCL11A enhancer site in LCR region of ?-globin using CRISPR-Cas9 technology in Hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) of the effected children. Gene edited HSCs will be evaluated for enhanced expression of ?-globin and fetal hemoglobin. These HSCs will be utilized for autologous transplantation in the effected children to ameliorate the symptoms of ?-thalassemia.

data.projectName: Computational Development of Sustainable Energy Materials
data.projectDigest:
The requirement of sustainable energy is not only linked with the search for alternative and renewable energy resources but the development of such systems that can help to save the energy consumption and the efficient use of energy is also very important to achieve this goal. The depleting conventional fossil fuel resources, increasing world population and globally polluted environment are the great challenges faced by international community. Pakistan is also facing all the above mentioned problems along with sustainable energy crisis. In this scenario, the computational development of sustainable energy materials can help to address these issues and our proposal is based on the computational development of hydrogen storage materials, rechargeable batteries and MAX phase materials.
To play our role in the core area of research of hydrogen storage materials and to compete with international community, we propose that complex hydrides, and nanomaterials are those potential materials in which hydrogen can be chemically bonded to the metal ions to resolve the issues in the safe & durable storage and usage of hydrogen at favorable kinetics and thermodynamics to make it economically feasible alternative/renewable resource of energy.
The computational study of crystal and electronic structures of Lithium and Magnesium based cathode materials, and other properties i.e.; energy density and intercalation voltage,  can lead to the development of promising rechargeable batteries to fulfill alternate energy requirement.
The MAX phase compounds can reduce the energy consumption and cost by improving the efficiency of fuel consuming engines. 
Keeping in view the above mentioned research plan, our proposal can play an important role to achieve the goal of sustainable energy.

data.projectName: New image processing techniques for water-quality monitoring through coffee ring pattern classification of water crystallization.
data.projectDigest: To improve access to clean water for people around the world requires knowledge about sources of contamination and the ability to detect the chemical contaminants. Generally speaking, most individuals routinely using a given water source do not have quick and easy methods available to detect contamination; instead laboratory work, expensive equipment and specialized knowledge are required. The aim of this project is to develop a method to detect water contamination in an easy and cheap way, using an application that can be run on a personal smart phone. In this project we propose to use the ‘coffee-ring effect’, produced by dissolved minerals and chemicals after water evaporates, to analyze multiple components in a single drop of water. The software application will allow the general public to test the quality of their own tap water by simply uploading a photo taken from a smart phone.. The software program will use image analysis of water droplet residue and comparison with characteristic mineralization patterns to determine varying levels of different minerals. The software will recognize characteristic mineral patterns through algorithms to detect water contamination.

data.projectName: Translational Research for Cancer Theranosis: Diagnosis and Treatment
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: Cancer is one of the non-communicable diseases affecting the health economics of developing countries. Besides improved 5 year survival rate with conventional therapies still high mortality and morbidity is the cause of major burden in a society. All over the world efforts are being directed to provide molecular disease and patient specific treatment modalities which has resulted in emergence of immune therapy, gene therapy, photodynamic therapy and radionuclide therapy. A personalized treatment approach is desirable to reduce morbidity in these patients which utilizes tumor specific biomolecules directed diagnosis and therapy. Nanoparticle based targeted drug delivery is one of the new approaches towards precision medicine for oncology. It proposes chemotherapeutic drugs encapsulation in nanoparticles targeted against specific tumor antigen to improve their efficiency, efficacy and reducing side effects at normal tissue by delivering high controlled release target specific doses. Nanotheranostics  can provide combination of various imaging and therapeutic options in a single nanocarrier like combining imaging radionuclide on a nanopolymer/ metal oxide loaded with anticancer drug or  photodynamic agent. In this project we propose use of microfluidic devices as well as chemical methods to synthesize nanoparticles to be loaded with anticancer drugs and radiolabeled for diagnosis and effective drug delivery.

data.projectName: Indigenization in Microsystems Prototyping for socio-economic development of Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
The main objective of this proposal is to launch another progressive activity to train people in the area of MEMS prototyping that include MEMS design, microfabrication, test and packaging. Existing MEMS design, test and packaging expertise/facilities available at different Pakistani universities will be utilized besides the proposed prototyping/microfabrication facility that will contribute towards the indigenous development of MEMS based microsystems to achieve SDGs in Pakistan. 
An extensive reach out program is being proposed in this proposal to launch a large scale R&D activity in MEMS in potential universities and institutes across Pakistan. For this purpose, need analysis with respect to the MEMS application will be carried out and academia and local industry will be motived to participate in this activity. Outcome of the need analysis will be utilized to establish a purpose built microfabrication facility for quick device prototyping with the help of our foreign collaborators. Different MEMS Design tools will be provided to the universities to promote MEMS design activities. Local trainings will be arranged for the researchers and students to train them on these design tools as per indigenously developed microfabrication processes. We strongly believe that this activity will help to develop customized, ready to use functional MEMS devices indigenously for different application covering the requirement of different stake holders in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Blood and Bone-Marrow Derived Stem Cells Alone and in Combination With High-Power Lasers for treatment of Musculoskeletal Injuries in Dogs, Cats and Horses in Pakistan”.
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Animals kept for transportation, sports, or as pets (dogs, cats and equines, i.e. horses, donkeys and mules), contribute a major part of annual GDP generation. While large animal and pet practice is  highly paid, averaging 3 lacs per month, the equine industry, contrarily, completely lacks basic diagnostic and therapeutic clinical equipment. Stem Cell Therapy is the ultimate and most effective treatment which covers many untreatable ailments, not covered by other recent commercially-launched regenerative therapies (Platelet-Rich Plasma/PRP, Shock wave Therapy). PRP and Shock Waves, along with diagnostic Color Doppler Ultrasound, being offered as ambulatory/ stall-side facilities, address the common, major acute and chronic ailments of the musculoskeletal system in dogs, cats and equines, i.e. tendinitis, osteoarthritis, wounds and muscle strains/ pain. Despite promising results, the major set-back with these therapies is that they do not offer protection against recurrence of injuries. In such scenarios, Stem Cell Therapy offers an ultimate, complete, most effective treatment solution till date. Additional benefits are that animals with neurological deficits, fractures and spinal cord dysfunction, which were earlier euthanized, are now treatable with Stem Cell Therapy. Stem Cells used together with other regenerative therapies (i.e. PRP and Shock Waves), bring greater success and 100% recovery, which is not possible with PRP/ Shock wave alone.  This project involves consortia of related common clinical challenges effaced by three animal species in Pakistan, and their long-term effective treatment solutions.It covers use of an automated stem cell kit and their clinical applications on routine client-owned cases in cats, dogs and horses.

data.projectName: A multidisciplinary consortium to tackle newborn calf diseases to ensure sustainable economic development of meat and milk industry in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Livestock farming is the backbone of rural and urban economy. According to economic survey of Pakistan 2018-19, Livestock sector share 60.5% in agriculture and almost 12% in national GDP, with annual growth of >4%. There is immense potential to improve these figures up to international standards if we revolutionize our livestock sector linked with meat and milk industry. Currently, we suffer huge disease outbreaks due to different pathogens, lack of efficient vaccines and poor nutritional plans for our cattle and buffalo population. 
The cattle and buffalo population is dependent on surplus progeny in order to produce more meat and milk but sufficient numbers of healthy calves are not produced due to devastatingly large number being affected by different diseases and poor management in their early life. 
The neonatal calf mortality at two week old is one of the highest in world recorded in Pakistan at 39%. This issue has been given top priority by the Prime Minister’s initiative for saving the calves and livestock industry.
Most of the locally produced vaccines are not fully protective and imported vaccines are very costly to afford by farmer. We have brought together a consortium of national and international team members including leading scientists, industrial partners, government research institutes and private dairy sector to identify the top priority areas to target. Hence, we target is to produce new range multivalent vaccines locally and design new nutritional formulations in order to produce healthier calves. These will exponentially reduce the disease-linked economic burden from meat and dairy industry in order to meet local needs and also earn valuable export revenue to improve Pakistan’s economy.

data.projectName: Drinking Water Management: Sustainable Water Governance through stakeholders’ Engagement and A Water Research and Technology Park in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
UN has warned that Pakistan is among adverse water scarce nations and big urban centers of Pakistan which are dependent on underground water will face a hazardous situation in coming decade. 64% of the total population of Pakistan did not have access to safe drinking water and water borne diseases kills on average 110 children each day in Pakistan. Despite massive funding from World Bank (WB) and Asian development bank (ADB), drinking water initiatives in Pakistan always end up with a new failure, resulting in 74% of water supply projects as non-functional. 
Such alarming situation certainly demands for more focused efforts to ensure social, financial, technical and environmental sustainability of the water systems in Pakistan. The current project has proposed a water governance model incorporating Stakeholders’ engagement for an effective and efficient sustainable water management and its demonstration in one of the urban center.  Furthermore a Water Research and Technology Park has also been proposed that will serve as a hub for knowledge creation, sharing and storage, creating and demonstrating state-of-the-art technology and governance models for the supply of safe and adequate drinking water, assessing water quality and usage, introducing water conservation strategies, providing trainings and consultancy services.

data.projectName: Artificial Intelligence based Secure Knowledge Management Platform for Healthcare Services of Hepatitis Big Data
data.projectDigest: This proposal aims to develop a secure and evolving knowledge management platform to support medical practitioners to better treat patients of Hepatitis across Pakistan. Hepatitis takes over 400 lives every day in our country and we have world’s highest rates of hepatitis C, therefore, we want to become an assistive hand for Government of Pakistan, using our proposal, so that it is able to eliminate said lethal disease by 2030 as asked by WHO. Hence, the research objective of the proposal is to develop a knowledge management platform to address the disease of Hepatitis B and C which is a national challenge for our Government. We aim to develop a system which is (i) intelligent, fueled by novel artificial intelligence and big data based models and algorithms, (ii) knowledge rich, making use of wisdom of multiple doctors (Crowd Wisdom), detailed historical data of patients and diagnosis,  social trends, daily lifestyle patterns of the patients, and (iii) provides security and transparency to the data of patients and diagnosis of the doctors. In this way, our platform aims to facilitate the medical practitioners for prediction of Hepatitis, its diagnosis, prognosis and prevention, healthcare analytics, and disease management. Hence, the ultimate aim of the proposed platform is to improve the quality of life by controlling risk of having and growing the said disease. We understand that the proposed platform is flexible and hence can be adopted for any other diseases.

data.projectName: Comprehensive Cataloging of Loss-of-function Mutations Within the Pakistani Population
data.projectDigest: The major goal of DNA sequencing is to decipher the function of gene in the human genome. Loss-of-function (LoF) mutations can damage both copies of a given gene in humans, and downstream functional effects of such ‘human knockouts’ can provide eventually the precise understanding of that gene function. There is always a bridge between the discoveries of sequencing information to the exploration of proper human gene function. Human knock-out represents a potent clue to mimic the therapy to any disease state, therefore could provide consistent knowledge to develop medicine. However, this task is further complicated by the fact that genetic variants can change over time, leading the reversal of gene function, earlier if it was repressed by chromosomal inactivation. Generally, human knockouts are rare in any local population, but still this way of finding gene function is an innovative way. Human knockouts also depends on ethnicity. In this study, we will explore with the Pakistani population the extent of gene knockout considering: 1) ethnicities, and 2) non-communicable diseases (NCDs) phenotypes. This outcome of this study will help us to determine the novel but knockouts in our local population that might lead to drug target development and precision medicine.

data.projectName: Geological, Geochemical, Geophysical and Advance Remote Sensing study of the Geothermal Energy Resources in Pakistan: Implication for a Sustainable Livelihood
data.projectDigest:
The current use of coal, natural gas and oil reserves provides 80% of the global energy requirements and these resources will deplete in the estimated 103, 33 and 31 years’ time span, respectively (EIA, 2013). Therefore other renewable energy resources like geothermal energy can produce 240 GW electricity from the identified resources in the world and can replace the dwindling supplies of fossil fuels in the future. Geothermal Energy is a renewable source, its potential in the upper earth crust is about 50,000 times more than the cumulative oil and gas reserves of the world (Zaigham  2009). It is a sustainable, clean (CO2-free), base load energy resource that is independent of season and available for 24 hours. 
Pakistan is an energy deficient country but having plenty of renewable energy resources (Gondal et al., 2017). Novel strategies to exploit the existing Geothermal energy resources in Pakistan can offer sustainable economic growth and enrichment of the energy endowment in the future.
Bench marking the US growth of electricity generation through binary geothermal power plants, it is expected that geothermal systems of Pakistan can run the same binary geothermal power plants for electricity generation, and could become a game-changer in the current energy crises.

data.projectName: Hybrid Nano grid: a smart and sustainable energy solution
data.projectDigest:
Sustainable generation and delivery of energy is central to achieving sustainable development and is directly linked to the socio-economic development of any country. A stable power supply is indispensable to guarantee a high standard for living conditions, scientific research, agricultural growth and industry. Sustainable energy is also one of UN’s priority areas to ensure universal access to energy resources, as none of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) can be met without major improvement in the access and green energy services in developing countries.
Distributed generation (DG) as a local power source has a lot of potential to ensure energy availability, sustainability and reliability. DGs are considered a valid, viable green option that can save transmission and distribution losses and are cheaper than centralized power generation. A consortium comprising faculty members from well-known institutions of Pakistan, including USPCASE UET Peshawar, LUMS, USPCASE NUST, Quaid-i-Azam University, COMSATS, and GIKI, as well as global leaders in research such as the University of Cambridge UK and University of Cornell USA have agreed to work on developing a Nano grid system, where energy is generated and stored locally at the household scale, without having to rely on an external grid.  SMEs - Solaronix (Switzerland) - and a startups - Future Solar Gen, Pakistan, - will also be part of this consortium.  The consortium will work on the design and fabrication of a hybrid 10KW nano grid by integrating three key technologies to be developed indigenously, namely solar photovoltaic (PV), fuel cells and batteries.

data.projectName: Bringing Heritage to life through Augmented and Virtual Reality
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Cultural and natural heritage is an irreplaceable source of inspiration for future generations. It is our legacy from the past, what we live with today, and what we pass on to future generations. It gives a sense of belonging to people, and a reason to understand and the value of roots. Although tourism has increased in Pakistan for the past few years, but the total number of tourists still remain low. 2015 saw 536,000 tourists in Pakistan which has increased to 1.9 Million in 2018. One of the most important between them is archaeological site in Taxila which was discovered in 1980. There is a need of preserving the tangible archaeological sites in the country, and tourism is at the core of it. Thus, the project becomes very important to save the culture and show it to the World to attract tourists.  The project specifically aims to digitally preserve heritage sites of Taxila along with provision of variety of assistances such as maps, signage by utilizing applications of Information and Communication Technologies.  The project aims to bring the expertise of interdisciplinary fields from art and design, artificial intelligence to wireless communication to create 3D visualization of heritage site of Taxila based on virtual and augmented reality. Upon successfully completion and deployment of the project the nationals would be able to: view real Taxila Heritage site inside immersive virtual environments at home, and secondly, upon visiting the site in person, they would be provided with augmented reality applications on site that would enable them for indoor navigation inside the site, also be their story-tellers by reconstructing the original site with embedded visual effects (avatars, animations) to aid their understanding on spot.

data.projectName: Water conservation practices and it’s economical assessment under the climate change scenarios across Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: In the current study, we will investigate the climate change impact on water resources (both surface and groundwater resources) of important basins of Pakistan. Moreover, the economic impact of water conservation techniques on water resources will also be investigated which will be an applied and interesting part of this research.

data.projectName: Development of Miniature 3D construction Prototype
data.piUniversity: Balochistan University of Information Technology, Engineering and Management Sciences,Quetta
data.projectDigest: Construction industry is evolving by introducing new technological advancements. These technologies are leading construction industry to a whole new level of efficiency. 3D printing of concrete is one of these innovative technologies [1]. In this method, concrete is deposited layer by layer along predefined geometrical axis [2]. 3D model of structure is made in a CAD software which is then sliced into layers and a G-code is created for 3D printer. The movement of print head along the predefined path is controlled by the code while concrete is pumped to print head through a hose. The thematic area of this research is to develop a 3D printable cementitious material using locally available resources in Pakistan. The implementation of the 3D printing on large scale in construction industry is the key issue. By countering the problems, 3D printing could be taken on large scale in the construction industry by doing further research

data.projectName: A blockchain-based distributed platform for storing sensitive healthcare data
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Despite the increase in public health facilities, Pakistan's population growth has generated an unmet need for healthcare. Pakistan’s private health sector operates through a fee-for-service system but unfortunately these hospitals are unregulated. As the government is geared towards the integration of technology into our everyday lives, this unregulated sector may cause a disaster in terms of data breech. The internet of things (IoT) is composed of smart devices that are embedded with a variety of sensors. The devices can sense various parameters and then communicate them over a network. Owing to the presence of security, privacy and scalability concerns; IoT based healthcare is a particularly important area of research. The healthcare data is generally highly sensitive in nature and privacy/ confidentiality/ integrity of the data is a big concern. This research is aimed towards designing a framework that is an amalgamation of state of the art technologies such as IoT, Blockchain and Searchable Encryption for the healthcare. This will enhance the trust in the healthcare systems and comply with the HIPAA and GDPR regulations.

data.projectName: Farm-to-shelf solution for yield-improvement and post-harvest loss reduction
data.projectDigest:
The agricultural sector of Pakistan is confronted with two major problems. Despite the lion’s share of the labor force primarily being an agrarian country – with over thirty nine percent of the country’s workforce being affiliated with the agriculture sector as reported in Labor Force Survey 2017-18 – the country still struggles with agricultural produce. 
On top of that, the agricultural produce post-harvest goes to utter waste. The situation is worsening with every passing year where the agricultural produce has seen a decline over the years and the post-harvest waste is on the rise.
With the advent of Internet of Things (IoT) paradigm, possibilities of increasing agricultural yield and reducing churn and wastage have increased in magnitude. The usage of sensors, ubiquitous crop monitoring, precision agriculture and similar smart approaches has been demonstrated to increase yield and reduce food wastage. 
In this project, we propose a full-fledge solution that focuses on both increase in agricultural yield as well as post-harvest loss elimination. The project is based on the IoT paradigm, and makes use of off-the-shelf as well as indigenously developed sensors to monitor cash and sustenance crops during their entire life cycle as well as a connected network of vehicles to ensure that the post-harvest wastage is minimized via controlled temperate, smart packaging and/or near real-time marketplace re-routing. Academic collaborators for the project include partners from outside of Pakistan, bringing to the project their expertise and experience in their relevant discipline. The panel of collaborators has expertise in Internet of Things (IoT), smart systems, sensor development and other areas that are closely inline with the solution proposed in the said project.

data.projectName: Disaster Response, Recovery and Risk Management (DR3)
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is prone to a number of natural disasters like earthquakes, floods, accumulation of snow and forest fires. Every year a large number of lives are lost and infrastructure is damaged due to these calamities. In order to minimize the human losses and also deal with such extreme emergency situations the urgency of first responders and rescue services are very critical. Communication services play a pivotal role in such scenarios. It has been observed that these natural disasters badly destroy the communication infrastructure leading to delayed recovery operations. The aim of this project is to establish continuous and reliable communication between people in the disaster zone and the rescue workers to carry out the rescue operations effectively. The project proposes three-tier communication architecture: first spanning the disaster region, second the multi-hop connectivity of disaster region to the command centre or infrastructure through airborne devices, and third the processing and bi-directional communication carried out from command centre or some infrastructure. In tier 1, temporary coverage is established among the already existing devices (held by people in disaster zone). This will be achieved by utilizing the best available device-to-device (D2D) connectivity options. The device discovery and localization is an integral part of this tier. data.projectName: Efficacy of Audio version of CBT based Self-help Manual in Improving Mental Health of Mothers of Children with Autism in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The proposed research project aims to assess the efficacy of audio version of CBT based self-help manual (Naeem, Irfan, & Ayub, 2015) in improving the mental health of mothers with children having Autism. Self-help has proven to be a viable option in fighting against the barriers that stop people from seeking the much needed professional help (Cuijpers, Donker, van Straten & Li, 2010; Milgrom et al., 2016). Especially in a developing country like Pakistan, with limited resources and man power, with mothers being burdened by far more than just raising a child in the best possible manner, and with low awareness of needs and their fulfillment in the context of mental health, self-help is an option that if explored and developed well can bring about a positive change. In this research, the audio version of CBT based self-help manual will be converted into a mobile app for better accessibility. Hundred mothers of children with autism will be selected from three major cities of Pakistan: Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad. They will be divided into intervention and control group. A pre-intervention assessment will be conducted with mothers to identify their negative automatic thoughts, depression, anxiety and stress level. A training session will then be conducted with intervention group to brief them about the techniques which they will be required to practice on their own for 8 weeks. Followed by, a post-intervention assessment with mothers will be conducted to assess negative automatic thoughts, depression, anxiety and stress level. Three months later, a follow up assessment will be done with mothers of intervention group to assess enduring changes in mental health. T-test will be used to see the efficacy of the audio version of self-help techniques in improving mental health

data.projectName: Improving treatment and control of extensive drug resistance pathogens in Pakistan by whole genome sequencing
data.projectDigest: Infections with antimicrobial resistant organisms requiring complex diagnostics and expensive treatment are a burden to health systems across the world. They pose a particular threat to low middle income countries including Pakistan where such infections stretch available resources, severely impacting national health and economy. This crisis has been compounded further by the emergence of extensive drug resistant (XDR) pathogens. XDR pathogens are not only difficult to treat, but their emergence can potentially be linked to travel and export restrictions posing a further economic risk. A major factor hampering efforts in addressing the threat posed by XDR is limited in-country capacity to diagnose and manage such infections. In order to address the challenge of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in the country, there is therefore an urgent need to expand such capacity. This project proposes a multipronged approach to improve detection and treatment of XDR pathogens in Pakistan .

data.projectName: Innovative Financial Governance and Digital Reforms: An Empirical Research Project addressing FATF and new age of Dynamic Financial System
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
The policymakers in Pakistan today are battling with a dilemma of regulations vs de-regulation. On the one hand, the economy is faced with the financial risk exposure towards Financial Action Task Force’s (FATF) recommendations which is constantly hammering social, economic and financial sector of this developing economy; hence requiring strict regulations. On the other hand, the increased globalization and fourth industrial revolution of digital reforms calls for a need to promote ease of doing business in the economy to encourage investment. One solution to these concurrent national challenges is to increase financial innovations and digital reforms in Pakistan economic and financial governance.
The innovative governance and digital reforms in the financial system have fundamentally changed the operational systems across the globe. The current project focuses on developing financial intelligence governance model for Pakistan through digital landscape enhancing, financial system screening, financial users’ due diligence and transaction monitoring by employing digital financial typologies. It would provide seminal base to mitigate the financial risk exposure against money laundering and terror financing in line with FATF. This research is timely because it is the need of hour to visit digital reforms and bring innovative governance in financial system that would not only facilitate the financial users but also combat money laundering and terrorism financing in line with FATF recommendations . These promising initiatives are also well aligned with Pakistan’s Digital Economy Chapter to boost digital economy bridging the new age.

data.projectName: Pilot Project for Electric Urban Public Transport System
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: The project aims at developing a pilot project for electrification of urban public transport through conversion of a public transport vehicle with an Internal Combustion (IC) engine, into an Electric vehicle (EV), and furthermore enable its operation for a specific route by incorporating solar energy infrastructure for charging of batteries. The project addresses two of the thematic areas of the Grand Challenge Fund (GCF) simultaneously, the conversion of public transport vehicles into EVs with charging infrastructure primarily dependent upon solar energy, is proposed with the vision to reduce oil imports for both the transportation and power generation sectors, thereby enabling a sustainable energy solution. On the other side, adoption of the proposed solution will reduce the Green House Gasses (GHG) emissions which is the core issue of climate change and environment.

data.projectName: Green Infrastructure for Sustainable Urban Wastewater Management and Pollution Reduction
data.projectDigest: Provision of economically and environmentally sustainable wastewater treatment for small communities remains a big challenge, but constructed wetlands may offer an economically feasible solution. This study is proposed for upgrading urban settlement by treating the domestic wastewater using green infrastructure (constructed wetlands). The project serves local community of residence of houses where no sever system exist and for a housing scheme who do not have a waste treatment plant. The project has three parts in one part individual houses will be provided with solutions for treatment and reuse of the wastewater by domestic treatment plants and second part will involve a residential area which is a private residential scheme covering  500 houses and a large scale treatment system will be designed and constructed at their site with private-public venture. While the third part will be taking care of pathogen eradication and the prevention of antibiotic resistance by optimizing the microbiome of a constructed wetland. The third part will be in collaboration with foreign collaborator Professor Ian Jones of University of Readings UK. The Technical expertise will be provided by Critical Greens PVT (Sectoral collaborator).

data.projectName: 2D materials based flexible and integerable energy devices for wearable and portable electronics and photonics devices
data.projectDigest: The discovery of 2D materials in last one decade is going to make a profound effect on the future of electronics and photonics products. The potential of use of 2D materials on almost any substrate will realize devices that would be flexible and wearable.  The internet of things (IoT) would also require such devices, which would require minimum processing. There is going to be a paradigm shift in the industry within next 5 to 10 years as the synthesis of 2D materials becomes mature and techniques mastered.  The advantage in 2D technology is that it will not require sophisticated synthesis and fabrication techniques needed for Si or III-V based semiconductor technology. 2D materials are being hotly pursued for energy conversion devices, i.e., solar cells or energy scavenging from the environment. If this happens, the next logical step would be to integrate the energy conversion devices with traditional electronic and photonic devices. This will open up a huge area of research development of isolated system on chip (SoC) devices of all kinds.  The present proposal is based on setting up a facility to synthesize 2D materials of various kinds on various substrates and develop energy conversion devices of different kinds like solar cells, piezo generators, electromagnetic energy scavenging devices, etc. The potential of such devices for use in flexible and wearable electronics and photonics is huge. Such devices have also shown to have huge potential in the personal medical care as well.  The project is a combination of science and engineering.

data.projectName: Augmenting the export potential of animal population through mass scale vaccine production and its role in poverty alleviation in Balochistan
data.projectDigest:
Livestock sector is linked with poverty alleviation in the province, as 70% provincial population is directly or indirectly involved in livestock rearing activities. It is an important sector of rural economy contributing about 40 % to the provincial GDP. According to one estimate, the province maintains 40 million cattle, sheep and goat population. Based on these population, there is need of 300 million doses of different vaccines in a year. But the center (CASVAB) produces and provides free of cost approximately 10 million doses collectively of all 8 vaccines per year to the provincial Livestock Department. It covers hardly 5 % of the animal vaccination. Remaining 95% animals remain unvaccinated throughout the year in the province. Animals become more prone to disease and livestock farming face many challenges in term of low production and reproduction with minimum health coverage. 
	To help in the national GDP and uplift of 70% poor rural population of the province the export of healthy animals and meat is necessary. This goal can be achieved through to improved animal health through mass scale vaccination against different diseases and to collaborate with public private partnership to transfer the technology and improve employment in area.

data.projectName: Development of Amine-based Graphene Oxide Absorbents/Adsorbents for CO2 Capturing Applications
data.projectDigest:
The proposed research project aims at Climate Change and Environment. World is facing serious challenges regarding rising of Earth's temperature. Sun rays enter in Earth's atmosphere are absorbed and part of these rays are reflected off the Earth's atmosphere. These reflected rays are being absorbed by Earth's atmosphere due to the presence of certain greenhouse gases (major contributor is carbon dioxide) that cause Global Warming. The main sources of these greenhouse gases are power generation plants (energy sector), vehicles and domestic. Scientist and researchers are working since decades to find optimal, feasible and economical solutions for capture of these greenhouse gases before their discharge to atmosphere.
Currently, different processes are in place both on laboratory and commercial scale. These methods face serious challenges in terms efficiency, economy, losses, corrosion, technical difficulties to establish on commercial scales. The current project is delineated to develop a novel and innovative carbon dioxide capturing process, targeting its feasibility both on laboratory and commercial scale and keeping in view the economic aspects as well. Carbon dioxide capturing will be performed via two proposed routes of manufacturing amine loaded Graphene Oxide. Graphene Oxide is emerging as a promising material in the field of energy and environment.

data.projectName: Treatment Of Arsenic Contaminated Groundwaters and Assessing its Health Impacts: A Pilot Project in Three Endemic Districts of Sindh Province
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest: In humans, chronic toxicity of As can produce a vast range of conditions such as cancers, renal diseases, diabetes mellitus and a unique skin disease known as Arsenocosis. Any intervention aimed at minimizing the effects or prevention of Arsenic poisoning is in direct scope of climate change and environment and also the sustainable development goals of the United Nation under the ‘Environmental conversation and improvement strategies’.  Pakistan has alarmingly high levels of ground water As levels and around 60 million of the population drink water that has medium to high levels of Arsenic toxicity. Interventions can be made to minimize the effects of As in the potable water at community levels by treatment techniques such as Co-Precipitation, Coagulation and Filtration, Precipitation and Filtration Unit at Household Scale, Removal by Iron-doped Activated Carbon (AC).  This study will be of its own kind in Pakistan as there will be a consortium and collaboration between three important sectors previously working in Silo for combined collectives effort to improve health status of communities: chemical inquiry assessments (Biochemical analysis by environmental geologist), removal of Arsenic from drinking water (Medical and environmental engineering and Commercial Sector) and assessing Health effects of Arsenic and effects of water treatment intervention (Clinical Medical Sciences).

data.projectName: Design and Application of a Novel Electrochemical Bio-sensor Kit for Detection of Dengue Virus
data.projectDigest: Virus detection is the biggest challenge of our society. The ongoing situation of the Corona virus in Wuhan China produced a serious impact on the health care systems  and indicated the need of new and rapid technologies to detect the virus and cancer at early stages.  This project aims to discover the state of the art technology for the sensors to detect dengue virus combining biological and electro-chemical technologies.  The health care services and management in the basic health units and hospitals of  rural areas of Pakistan has unavailability to detect Dengue virus in timely manner. This project will focus on the development of novel  bio-electro-chemical sensors for the early detection of dengue virus and also feasible for the related studies for early detection of cancer, virus and other lethal diseases present in Pakistan. This project can be placed as a national emergency in solidarity with China and can impact CPEC as a defining project for virus and disease detection.

data.projectName: Capacity Building of Fragmented Local Nonwoven Textile Industry for Global Competitiveness by Tackling Healthcare Challenges
data.projectDigest:
The proposal aims at supporting Nonwoven sector of Textile industry of Pakistan to upgrade it to contribute towards economic growth of the country by addressing global health challenges. Based on WHO health statistics, resources available in textile industry and economic impacts of expected outcomes, the proposed project has been designed to achieve the following objectives: 
1.	Perform targeted R&D efforts to diversify product range of existing nonwoven industry from low value consumables to high value medical textiles that can be utilized to: 
a.	effectively prevent air and water borne diseases.
b.	inhibit transmission of infectants.
c.	offer effective wound management.
2.	Capacity building of nonwoven industry to produce advanced healthcare products.
Outcomes of this project will not only be employed to address the most highlighted global healthcare challenges but also contribute to socioeconomic development of Pakistan by facilitating the local textile industry to capture a significant world medical textiles market.

Tripping of high voltage transmission lines lead to blackouts that can last for hours before it is restored. Depending upon the area of tripping, power supply can be disrupted paralyzing at times an entire city or a region and bringing life to a standstill. The event has a direct bearing on the economy in addition to the losses incurred to the power system adding to the energy crisis in the country. Insulators play an important role in undisrupted power delivery. One of the probable causes of tripping is the flashover across the insulators installed on the high voltage transmission lines mainly due to the environmental effects. 
In this project, we propose an optimal design and type of the insulators keeping in mind its operation and maintenance with specific consideration to the increased pollution based on the ESDD (Equivalent salt deposit density) and NSDD (Non-soluble salt deposit density) that mainly impacts the performance of the insulators. This is also one of the long term recommendations of the committee.
Thus, the main goal of this research is to address an already existing energy crisis and established issue of tripping by customizing the design of the insulators through industry-academia collaboration between subject matter experts, manufacturing and testing at EMCO, and delivering to NTDC for implementation in the field.

data.projectName: Indigenous Development of Traction Motor System for Electric Vehicles (EVs)
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan is passing through severe financial crises. In this hard time, Pakistan is spending around 13 Billion USD of its precious foreign exchange reserves per year on fossil fuel imports. More than 50% of the imported fuel is consumed by transportation sector primarily by the gasoline vehicles. The alternate transportation can be Electric Vehicles (EVs). 

EVs offer a number of advantages such as, they are environmentally friendly, more energy efficient, have lower maintenance cost and longer life. However, they are very expensive. EVs cannot be commercialized in Pakistan unless their performance and prices are comparable to their counterpart gasoline vehicles.

The primary goal of this project is to bring down the price of an EV by designing and manufacturing a key component; Traction motor system, indigenously in Pakistan.
The main outcomes of the project are,
• To design and fabricate Traction Motor
• To design and build the traction motor drive
• To build state-of-the-art Research and Development facility in UET Peshawar to conduct research in the field of traction motor system

data.projectName: Development of Novel Inhibitors of the SARS Coronavirus (SARS-COV-19) Enzymes Using In-Silico Techniques.
data.projectDigest: We want to develop novel inhibitors of the different enzymes of the novel coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2) that are helping the virus at its different life stages inside the human body. Through the development of these novel inhibitors (drugs) we will be able to halt the so that the COVID-19 infection at different stages of development. Our aim is to modify the already availble  drug candidates that are effective against MERS and SARs which are the close virus family members of SARS-Cov-2.  For this purpose we will use the novel designed inhibitors (drugs), which  will be docked with the specific enzymes and  respective proteins that play crucial role in viral life cycle. Through this way those inhibitors that provided the best molecular docking results in terms of free energy of binding will be selected. Those selected drug candidates will be further evaluated  for their suitability through molecular dyanmics simulation which will provide the interaction with the enzymes in virtual time. We will selected the favorable drug candidates and with the help of  pharmaceutical industry or international collaborators these drugs will be synthesized and will be tested against the specifc enzymes in in vitro and in vivo. Those drugs that showed promising results will be further evaluated through clinical trials for their efficacy and toxicity.

data.projectName: Artificial intelligence and thermography based Covid-19 scanner
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest:
Thermography is widely used for the identification of heat, humidity and thermal patterns in health-care applications. In struggles to identify the extremely infectious virus causing Covid-19, thermal cameras are used at the public places for rapid screening of large numbers of people by measuring the body temperatures non-invasively. These thermal cameras are costly and have limitations such as it only measures surface temperature which can be affected by environmental conditions such as frost, moisture, dust, fog, and smoke. Therefore, a low-cost and intelligent thermal camera is required which would also overcome drawbacks due to environmental conditions. 

 The use of thermography for health-care is an excellent example of current technological advancement. In the early days of thermography, it was used for military applications. In 1934, human skin was described to be a good emitter of thermal (InfraRed) radiation. And afterward, the thermography is considered as a possible method for skin heat measurement and, later, as a potential alternative to facilitate diagnostic imaging in medical science.   Therefore, in this work we proposed the development of a real-time, low-cost and thermal imaging camera for Coronavirus fever detection called Intelligent Thermography Scanner for Coronavirus (ITSC).  The ITSC can integrate multiple thermal cameras each having 76 thousand near infra-red thermal sensors having a resolution of 320x480 and 9 frame rate per second. It uses a high performance real-time embedded system and applies a stereo imaging and deep learning algorithm that identifies the complex temperature pattern signatures of Coronavirus infected subject.

data.projectName: “FORMULATION AND CHARACTERIZTION OF NATURAL COMPONENTS BASED HAND SANITIZER BY EXPLOITING INDIGENOUS FLORA OF PAKISTAN”
data.theme: Development of disinfectants particularly using indigenous herbal ingredients
data.projectDigest: Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19)) has rapidly spread across China and around the world, causing an outbreak of acute infectious pneumonia. No specific anti-virus drugs or vaccines are available for the treatment of this sudden and lethal disease. Among the preventive measures, washing of hands with hand sanitizer is at the frontline; killing viruses. The requirement of hand sanitizer are in high demand. In this hour of need, the underdeveloped countries like Pakistan need to formulatea hand sanitizer, from a natural origin with minimal toxicity and equivalent efficacy. In the past decade, scientists have made a considerable effort to identify multiple component herbal formulae in traditional medicine with anti-SARS-CoV activity. Based on these factors, there is a general expectation that ethnomedicine would be a valuable weapon in the armory against SARS-CoV. Through literature review, several plants will be identified with antibacterial and disinfectant properties. The extracts of these plants will be prepared in the laboratory and determination of minimum inhibitory concentration of the plant extracts will be performed. The next step will be the preparation of pilot scale formulation and its characterization. This formulation will then be subjected to different bioassays and stability will be launched in the market.

data.projectName: COVITATE: An AI-based Online Portal for the Computational Biology and Vaccinology for the COVID-19
data.theme: Information Collection and Dissemination IT platforms)
data.projectDigest:
The coronavirus disease 19 (COVID-19) is a highly human-to-human transmittable and pathogenic viral infection caused by Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Corona Virus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), which emerged in Wuhan, China and spread around the world as pandemic. Until now, several outbreaks have emerged in other parts of the world, such as, Italy, Iran and other European countries including the USA. There are efforts being performed to find a vaccine for the COVID19 however, there is no success yet because of the high rate of mutation in COVID-19. Therefore, there is a dire need of a portal where the mutational data from various strains of corona viruses genome sequences is being stored, can be accessed and eventually analyzed by Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based simulations to find possible vaccines, or any drug target.
We propose here an online platform  (COVITATE) for accelerating the research in the areas of COVID-19 vaccinology as well as for the discovery of the drug candidates. The platform will be hosting the all available genomic data from across the servers in a one single platform. The portal will have multiple functionalities and plug-ins with famous databases, such as, PDB, UniProt, and etc., One important function of this portal is to predict the effect of the mutation on the structural stability of the translated gene product of this mutated gene (i.e., corresponding proteins), and its interactions with the corresponding human protein partner.

data.projectName: Development of hand sanitizer against SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) by using the indigenous plants/herbs.
data.theme: Development of disinfectants particularly using indigenous herbal ingredients
data.projectDigest: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is an infectious disease caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). In 2019, this disease was first reported in China and then spread globally, leading to the ongoing coronavirus pandemic of 2019–2020. Up to 29 March 2020, 666,211 confirmed cases and 30,864 deaths have been reported globally. However, in Pakistan 1,526 cases and 13 deaths have been reported up to 29 March 2020. The number of COVID-19 patients is continuously increasing. Presently, there is no cure for this disease. Contaminated hands are one of the sources of virus contamination. According to WHO guidelines, frequent hand washing and use of sanitizer is one of the preventive measures against this virus. Now, the problem is that where frequent use of soap and artificial sanitizers can damage the skin, there is no specific sanitizer available for SARS-CoV-2. This research will help to develop the hand sanitizer by using the natural herb/plants which will not only have the antibacterial and antiviral activity but will specifically active against the SARS-COV-2. Furthermore, with its antibacterial and antiviral potential it may be used for future pandemic diseases.

data.projectName: COVID-19 Mechanism for Ambulances Using Deep Learning and Fuzzy Logic
data.piUniversity: Abbottabad University of Science & Technology (AUST), Abbottabad
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest: Novel Coronavirus-19 (COVID-19) is a new strain of coronavirus that is not identified in human beings previously. It is observed that people of different ages are effected from this virus, especially those having body diseases, blood pressure, diabetes, heart problems or having weaker immune systems, are effected the most. Recently, the outbreak of this virus has severely affected people around the world with increasing death rates. The increased death rates are because of its spreading nature among people through their physical interactions. It is very much important to control the spreading of the virus and also, to detect the symptoms of the people during the initial stages so proper precautionary measures can be taken timely. To control spreading of the virus, we propose Ambulance based COVID-19 detection mechanism VCDM to reveal the related symptoms of a person. The VCDM make use of symptoms as headache, flu, fever, cough, chest pain, shortage of breath, tiredness, nasal congestion, diarrhoea, breathing difficulty and pneumonia. The symptoms are considered as parameters to reveal the presence of COVID-19 in human beings. Due to the ambiguous nature of symptoms in humans, we utilize fuzzy modelling and deep extreme machine learning techniques.

data.projectName: Clinical Diagnostic Method and Treatments for Coronavirus 2019 Infection (COVID-19)
data.piUniversity: Pir Abdul Qadir Shah Jeelani Institute of Medical Sciences, Gambat
data.projectDigest:
The world experienced the outbreaks of coronavirus infection that threaten global pandemic in 2002-2003 by Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) and in 2011 by Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS). In both cases, the causative agents (SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV, respectively) were newly identified coronavirus in the genus Betacoronavirus with zoonotic origin that leads respiratory disease.      Since its first reported case in late 2019, the infection has spread to other regions in China and other countries, and the transmission rate, the mortality rate and the clinical manifestation emerged. However, it will take months and maybe years until we will fully grasp the whole picture of the characteristics of the pathogens and its likely origin, symptoms and the host immune responses to combat the infection.
Knowledge of molecular immune pathogenesis, diagnosis and treatment of COVID-19 on the base of the present understanding of SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV infections, which may be helpful in potential therapeutic targets for combating the SARS-CoV-2 infection.
The project to help out to find out the on the base of immune pathogenesis with diagnosis of COVID-19 and provide a ideas for the prevention of SARS-CoV-2 infection, based on the availability resources of Pakistan with applying recent research progress of SARS-CoV-2.

data.projectName: Cost-Effective Point-of-Care Graphene based Corona Virus Detection Kit Prototype
data.piUniversity: Karachi Institute of Economics & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: This project will focus on the development of cost-effective point-of-care diagnostic kits using a Graphene based bio-sensor and its associated electronics to enable a label-free and real-time virus detection. The designed system would be similar to a hand-held Glucometer with disposable sensor-strips and a battery-operated reusable reader. The system will perform virus detection using a single drop of blood or swab within a few minutes. This system will employ label-free 4-port RF impedance analysis establishing selectivity through the unique di-electric signature of the virus without needing chemical or biological reagents or antibody for bio-functionalizattion of the sensor. This system can connect to mobile networks of healthcare workers or places to establish cloud connectivity for distributed large-scale biological surveillance system and to incrementally develop a database for AI based classification of the virus mutations in the future. This project will deliver a prototype system with sensor, electronics and application integrated with a compact foot-print on a bench-top in the lab for future scale-up and productizaion into a complete mass-producible hand-held device

data.projectName: Steam Chamber therapy for the quarantined patients and suspects of COVID 19 in Pakistan
data.theme: Indigenous manufacture of Low cost Intensive-care equipment
data.projectDigest: COVID 19 has been a global pandemic as per WHO and to date it has affected 644,570 individuals over 198 countries, nearly 50,000 sentenced to death due to this virus.  COVID-19 (a positive sense, single stranded RNA virus), uncontrolled outbreak effecting worldwide and has no cure yet. This novel coronavirus is a temperature sensitive virus the outer layer consists of fat, which is degradable and cannot bear temperature above 55oC. Doremalen et al, 2020  has shown that coronaviruses can be inactivated within a minute by disinfecting surfaces with 62-71% alcohol, or 0.5% hydrogen peroxide bleach or 0.1% sodium hypochlorite. Higher temperatures and humidity also tend to result in other coronaviruses dying quicker, although research has shown that a related coronavirus that causes Sars could be killed by temperatures above 56°C or 132° at a rate of about 10,000 viral particles every 15 minutes. The current project aims to target this weakness of the virus and provide a physical means of steam chamber therapy to the patients and suspects of this virus to reduce the viral load ex-vivo and in-vivo. As it would be first of its kind to establish the steam chamber locally and then optimize its treatment protocol, a few trials would be conducted among a small group of patients, which is harmless and investigate its validity and effectivity.

data.projectName: Whole genome sequencing of a large number of COVID-19 from Pakistan and development of point of care diagnostics via CRISPR/Cas13a system
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: The COVID-19 has entered Pakistan from multiple routs including China, Iran, Europe and USA. RNA viruses with big genomes are known to mutate faster, making it essential to sequence entry rout based large number of COVID 19 genomes from Pakistan. We intend to use next generation sequencing in collaboration of Beijing Genomic Institute (BGI), Shenzhen, China and Dr. Alessandro Marcello, Group Leader and the designated resource person on COVID-19 from International Center for Genetic Engineering (ICGEB). Trieste, Italy. Pandemics, like COVID-19 needs faster, robust, easy to use and field deployable diagnostic system. To increase our capacity for the diagnosis of COVID-19, the class II type VI RNA guided RNA cleavage system (CRISPR-Cas13a) offers an efficient alternative to diagnose RNA viruses with unprecedented precision. This system was exploited for the diagnosis of RNA molecule in Specific High-sensitivity Enzymatic Reporter unLOCKing (SHERLOCK) technology with attomolar sensitivity. This system has been shown to detect different viruses in human samples. The CRISPR-Cas13a diagnostic system will be developed in collaboration of King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) . The developed diagnostic kit will be validated on real samples in collaboration of Aga Khan Hospital and commercialized through NextDek Healthcare.

data.projectName: Prospective, Randomized Phase 2 Clinical Trial of Mesenchymal Stem Cells(MSCs) for the Treatment of Corona Virus Disease 2019(COVID-19)
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
Since the outbreak of coronavirusdisease2019(COVID-19), many researchers in China have carried out clinical trials on treatment based on Western medicine, traditional Chinese medicine or a combination of the two.  However, most of these trials were small (median sample size 100) and the bulk of potential therapeutic strategies remain in the experimental phase and currently there is no e?ective speci?c antiviral with high-level evidence. 
Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) are one of the most studied and important adult stem cells. A large amount of evidence shows that MSCs can migrate to and return to damaged tissues, exert strong anti-inflammatory and immune regulatory functions, promote the regeneration and repair of damaged tissues, resist apoptosis and inhibit tissue fibrosis, and reduce tissue damage. Existing data shows that possible beneficial effect of MSC can be attributable to immunomodulatory properties. 
We propose a prospective, phase-2 randomized-controlled clinical trial to assess the safety and efficacy of MSCs as an add-on therapy to standard supportive treatment for patients with moderate/severe COVID-19.  The primary outcome measures are improvement in clinical symptoms and decrease in oxygen dependency. Initial data from small studies on COVID-19 patients is suggestive of marked improvement among severely ill patients.

data.projectName: The Covid 19 Pandemic Portable Ventilator
data.theme: Indigenous manufacture of Low cost Intensive-care equipment
data.projectDigest: The Covid 19 pandemic has effected various nations worldwide including Pakistan. Presently, we are in process of facing a surge of increasing number of cases which may eventually overwhelm our healthcare facilities.  Severe Covid 19 infections can result in respiratory failure leading to an inflammatory process affecting the alveoli which are the functional part of the lungs. This pathology is termed as the Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). Such cases need to be put on mechanical ventilators, the potential demand of which might exceed the available resources as they may already be allocated to patients with different conditions. The Covid 19 Pandemic Portable Ventilator is a system designed to allow rhythmic compression of an AMBU bag which is modified to deliver a sustained positive end expiratory pressure (PEEP) to keep the alveoli open open with oxygen. The device will be simple to operate, portable and cost effective with the ability to provide reliable ventilation in either adult or peds patients for hours. In order to minimize the possible risk of infection, we will design a transparent box/hood that will be placed on the patient`s head for preventing aerosol transmission of virus.

data.projectName: Development of low-cost disinfectant and sanitizer using indigenous herbal ingredients warranting skin health improvement
data.theme: Development of disinfectants particularly using indigenous herbal ingredients
data.projectDigest:
Coronavirus disease (COVID-19) is an infectious disease induced by a newly discovered coronavirus that was first identified in Wuhan, China in December 2019. Since then, the virus has spread at an alarming rate to become a pandemic affecting 197 countries and territories around the world. Numerous countries, including Pakistan have initiated a complete lockdown to contain the spread of the virus. At present, as there is no approved vaccine or medicine available to fight the virus, our only defense is precautionary measures such as social distancing, washing hands and wearing protective equipment. However, the mounting numbers of confirmed cases of COVID-19 have triggered a global shortage of protective equipment, ventilators and hand sanitizers. 
A former President of the Karachi Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KCCI) reported that Pakistan’s demand for hand sanitizers soared from 1200 tonsper year to 3000 tons (Express Tribune, 2020). Consequently, this sharp increase has led to widespread shortages and a staggering spike in rate by over 200%. The prevalence of COVID-19 and the growing demand for hand sanitizers has led to an urgent need to develop low-cost disinfectants using indigenous herbal ingredients. In this present scenario, as our economy faces a serious crunch, it is pertinent to tap our local resources instead of relying on imports to ensure minimum strain on our economy. The broad objective of current project is to develop local low-cost disinfectants using indigenous herbal ingredients that would not only cater to the rising demand of this product but also ensure that it is available at an affordable price.

data.projectName: Radiography based preliminary screening methodology using Generative Adversarial and Deep Networks to support PCR based COVID-19 testing for large scale population examination
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest: COVID-19 disease encapsulates short-term and long-term challenges for our medical system. The short-term issue is to comprehensively test all the suspected cases, as well as the population at large, to sweep the population of the corona virus. The long-term problem is to have acquired data sorted out in a manner, where is useful for Artificial Intelligence based models to support the virus detection, prognosis and surveillance. We propose to design such a solution, where we address both these issues. In the short-term approach, we propose to devise protocols for data collection using inexpensive, readily available means, by working with clinicians to establish a standardized publically available dataset. This data will be utilized in off the shelf intelligent learning models to devise preliminary screening strategies, so the suspected patients not having COVID-19 can be filtered. Our long-term approach is to utilize the data in custom built network models, along with data augmentation so that our solution becomes a standalone prognosis framework, to perform the preliminary screening.

data.projectName: Health Risk Assessment By On Site Surveillance Strategies to Track SARS-CoV-2 in Hospital Environment & Developing Testing Kits for Community Screening
data.projectDigest: The world is currently under siege of coronavirus- SARS-CoV-2 (chronic life threatening pneumonia-nCovid-19). The critical challenge is how to respond to this pandemic health emergency. Developing accurate, rapid & cost-effective methodologies for extensive testing and early warning systems for better preparedness is key approach. COVID-19 has penetrated throughout the world at an exponential rate and in this perspective studying genomic polymorphism of SARS-CoV-2 is important for developing appropriate diagnostics and thereafter interventions to control infection. Therefore, having large sequence data for SARS-CoV-2 is not only key to its better surveillance but will also help in developing optimized detection kits and thereafter developing effective vaccine as well as epidemiological models. Moreover, based on variations in viral load in patients or circulating virus variants, high proportion of patients are diagnosed as false negatives. Therefore, in this context, we will address dual challenge, firstly detecting increasing risk of exposure to community-nosocomial widespread of SARS-CoV-2 by screening hospital settings and its ambulance services as well as symptomatic and asymptomatic community. This will ensure safe working environment for hospital settings as well as allow enhanced community testing by improved point of care detection and long term surveillance of COVID-19, for better preparedness and damage control.

data.projectName: Development of Recombinant vaccine against SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19)
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The SARS-CoV-2 epidemic was started in December 2019 in Wuhan China and  (WHO) declared it as a pandemic on 30th January 2020. Till date the virus has infected almost 964603 people with 49242 deaths. It is growing exponentially. However, there is no approved vaccine or drug to control and cure the SARS CoV-2 infection. The medical practitioners are trying the repurposing of existing drugs to cure the infected people. The number of confirmed infected individuals in Pakistan are raised to 2386 with 32 deaths and the future is unpredictable. The province Punjab is at top with 922 cases and Sindh at second with 761 cases to date. The vaccination is a best way to control the infectious agents. In this difficult time an effective vaccine against SARS CoV-2 is desperately needed. The SARS CoV-2 is an enveloped virus with positive RNA genome. It has two major antigenic proteins including, spike protein (S) and nuclear capsid protein (N). Recent researches showed that most of the B cell and T cell epitopes among the SARS CoV-2 infected individuals are directed against the S and N protein of virus. The current project is aiming to identify the most conserved antigenic determinants of these viral proteins by genome sequencing and immunoinformatic analyses. Such identified antigenic determinants will be clustered, and expressed on the bacterial outer membrane vesicles, which are highly immunogenic compartments extruded from the outer membrane of bacteria. The tailored OMVs containing antigenic determinants of SARS CoV-2 proteins will be tested for their immunogenic responses in test animals. Further effectiveness will be assessed by virus neutralization assay followed by the determination of antibodies against these antigenic determinants in recovered patients serum.

It has two major antigenic proteins including, spike protein (S) and nuclear capsid protein (N). Recent researches showed that most of the B cell and T cell epitopes among the SARS CoV-2 infected individuals are directed against the S and N protein of virus. The current project is aiming to identify the most conserved antigenic determinants of these viral proteins by genome sequencing and immunoinformatic analyses. Such identified antigenic determinants will be clustered, and expressed on the bacterial outer membrane vesicles, which are highly immunogenic compartments extruded from the outer membrane of bacteria. The tailored OMVs containing antigenic determinants of SARS CoV-2 proteins will be tested for their immunogenic responses in test animals. Further effectiveness will be assessed by virus neutralization assay followed by the determination of antibodies against these antigenic determinants in recovered patients serum.

data.projectName: GIS Based Modelling, Mapping & Web Dashboard for Coronavirus (COVID-19) Spread in Punjab Province of Pakistan
data.theme: Information Collection and Dissemination IT platforms)
data.projectDigest: Pakistan like other countries of world is experiencing spread of Coronavirus disease (COVID-19) which can cause severe illness and fatality. The coronavirus cases in world is reaching to 933,688 cases. The Government of Pakistan is taking steps to control the spread of disease by taking various measures like lock down of cities, provision of health facilities to patients, sealing the houses and streets of affected people, closure of schools, colleges and universities. All such actions could prevent spread of COVID-19 but also affects the activities and economy of country. According to Pakistan’s National Action Plan for Coronavirus disease requirement there is an urgent need of robust technology-based system which provides real time monitoring of COVID-19 spread. The main objective of this research is to develop Coronavirus disease (COVID-19) surveillance and monitoring system by combining mapping, modelling and online GIS services for all districts of Punjab Province of Pakistan.  The project activities include: (i) collection of patient and disease data from Punjab health department; (ii) utilization of data for GIS mapping; (iii) application of GIS maps for analyzing the spread pattern of disease; (iv) identification of hotspots; (v) preparation of health risk zones; and (vi) development of Web-GIS Coronavirus disease (COVID-19) monitoring system. The project collaborators include COMSATS University Islamabad-Abbottabad Campus, Urban Sector Planning and Management Services Unit (Urban Unit) Lahore, University of Calgary Canada, and Curtin University Australia. All researchers from these universities and experts from Urban Unit have qualifications, experience & publications in GIS, remote sensing and modelling for accomplishing this project successfully.

data.projectName: Indigenous development of portable and cost-effective point-of-care integrated platform for detection and necessary mitigation of CoVID-19
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: The CoVID-19 has caused a significant damage to public health and economies worldwide. Several cases and deaths are reported so far in Pakistan and this count is expected to increase in future. A testing facility that can be rapid, and cost-effective to general public is urgent unmet need to avoid disease spread. Furthermore, individuals who had a history of travel and contact with CoVID-19 patient within last 14 days who themselves need to be tested and self-isolated, remain ignored or non-trackable and therefore are a source of subsequent increase in disease burden. Recently, a consortium of UK Universities has developed a hand-held simple, low-cost, portable, isothermal rapid molecular diagnostic platform that can process six different samples simultaneously within 30 minutes. The device is sensitive, specific, requires minimal training and therefore can be operated by healthcare professionals and can facilitate tracking diseased and contact patients. In collaboration with the UK researchers and national partners, we propose validation and indigenous development of this device and necessary training to concerning individuals. Collectively, we will be able to develop and implement the system for wider adoption within few months to help the government in mitigating and eventually beating the CoVID-19.

data.projectName: CT Scan Diagnosis of Covid-19 (CTDC)
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest:
Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19), first identified in Wuhan, china in 2019, is caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome, coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). It is highly infectious and has rapidly spread globally infecting almost 199 countries with 752,385 positive  cases and 36,210 deaths, and is continuously on the rise. It was declared as Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) by World health organization (WHO) on January 30, 2020 . Pakistan confirmed its first two cases on February 6, 2020 and as till date the total positive cases are 2192 with 31 deaths.  The key factor to limit this pandemic situation is the early testing and diagnosis of the virus. The virus also affects the lungs and affected lobes, ground glass nodules, fibrosis stripes and different antigen etc. can be recorded in chest CT images.

In Pakistan limited availability of RT-PCR testing kits has slowed down the number of tests per day, therefore, CT scans came up as a second option. This project will address this issue by using Artificial Intelligence methods to examine CT images for symptoms like  typical, intermediate, Atypical and negative images.
