data.projectName: Seroprevalence of Antibodies against COVID – 19 among close contacts of index patients in Pakistani Population
data.projectDigest: This proposed study targeted to determine antibodies levels among close contacts of COVID – 19 index patients in Pakistani population will be a multi – center study which will include close contact participants all over the Pakistan to generate database at National level. This data will help policy makers regarding prevention and control of this infection and to predict its morbidity and mortality and its re-emergence. This will help in the determine the occurrence of this COVID – 19 as subclinical cases resulting in their natural immunization contribution to herd immunity. This will help our population in better understanding of disease which is currently facing severe problems (psychological, physical and economical issues due to lockdowns) due to this disease and to come out of panic situation currently prevailing. Herd Immunity in our local population among these close contacts can safeguard and serve as defense line for eradication and control of COVID – 19 infection. The results of study will highlight importance / need for vaccination in our population.

data.projectName: Characterization of COVID-19 at Molecular Level in Pakistani Patients Using Next Generation Sequencing Approaches for the Examination of Immune System Responses and Designing of Vaccine
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: COVID-19 is caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus that is recently declared as a pandemic. People with weakened immune system, chronic medical conditions, older than 60 years and pregnant ladies are major targets of this disease.  Like many other diseases, genomic profile of Pakistani COVID-19 patients will also be required to design vaccines and treatments. Differential genes expression is very crucial for prevention, improvements in diagnosis and treatment of associated problems with COVID-19. Therefore, it is very important to consider new technologies in the field of genomics, such as next generation sequencing (NGS), for the holistic study of normal, infected, recovered and deceased COVID-19 patients. Comparison of differentially expressed genes among these categories of patients will highlight the differences at immune level. Complete mechanism of immune responses in patients will provide the accessibility to the treatment of diseases. Traditionally, vaccine designing and development was based on the fact that patients may have unlimited supply of cells which can bind to antigen. However, due to the diversity, often antigen cannot be recognized effectively. Answers at holistic level are required that what is going on in our immune system and how these responses can be adopted to further design the vaccines.

data.projectName: Genome wide analysis of immune patterns of COVID-19 in human and other potential hosts (bats, cats and dogs)
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Recent COVID-19 pandemic outbreak has been declared as public health emergency of international concern by WHO. This viral respiratory infection is recoverable due to host immune response in most of the patients exhibiting mild to moderate symptoms. Therefore, a better understanding of genetic and molecular mechanism underlying immunity against COVID-19 is one of the essential research areas in this regard. The proposed study involves genome-wide analysis of all the potential regions of host DNA related to innate and acquired immunity. Although major focus of this study is the genome analysis of Human subjects who have been effected by COVID-19 during current pandemic in comparison to the normal human control subjects. In addition, the genome-wide analysis of common breeds of cats, dogs, and bats will also be conducted for a deeper understanding of mammalian immune patterns. Cats and dogs are included in the study as they are common pets and may be a source of spread of infection. Bats have been considered for this study as resistant controls as the act as natural scavengers in the environment and their immune system is regarded the most efficient against common viruses and bacteria. Samples will be collected from human subjects recovered from COVID-19 infection as well as control subjects who were at risk but remained uninfected and from healthy controls who remained in self-isolation during the epidemic. Biological samples will also be collected from dogs, cats and bats. DNA will be extracted and quantified from all the study and control samples from humans and animal subjects and Whole Genome study will be conducted through Next Generation Sequencing followed by bioinformatic analysis using appropriate tools. Data will be compiled and reported after expert analysis.

data.projectName: Development of Nebulizer for Aerosol controlled drug delivery for COVID-19
data.theme: Indigenous manufacture of Low cost Intensive-care equipment
data.projectDigest:
Scientific community is rushing to determine the cure vaccination or treatment of COVID-19. Since, it severely affects the respiratory system, hence several investigations are in progress that are based on inhaled medications. As per WHO Landscape analysis of therapeutics published on 21st March 2020, One of the leading breakthroughs in the prevention and treatment of COVID-19 has been reported by United Kingdom based biotech firm Synairgen. The medicine is inhaled by patient and is designed to boost the patient’s immune system to help them fight off the virus. It contains interferon beta, a naturally occurring protein, which orchestrates the body’s antiviral responses. Moreover, two more inhaling based treatments have been proposed and are in the research and approval phase. 
Nebulizers are mostly used for inhaled drug deliveries. Special precautions have been instructed for the use of Nebulizers (jet type  commonly used in healthcare industry) for the treatment and prevention of COVID-19 as nebulizer therapy in patients with pandemic COVID-19 infection has the potential to transmit potentially viable COVID-19 to susceptible bystander hosts. Nebulizers generate aerosol particles in the size of 1-5 µm that carry medication, bacteria or Virus into deep lungs. Since, the development of treatment and vaccination is in progress it is pertinent to improve Nebulizer design that can produce the required conditions such as temperature, humidity, pressure and especially the requisite particle size for deep lung drug delivery. 
Unsafe use of primary device such as Nebulizer has potentially burdened the expensive and much sophisticated intensive care devices such as Ventilators. Instead, the expected effective drug-delivery mechanism for COVID-19 shall likely be using the Nebulize

data.projectName: Identifying epidemiological determinants of Corona Virus Disease (COVID-19) among Pakistani population
data.piUniversity: Peoples University of Medical and Health Sciences for Women, Nawabshah (Shaheed Benazirabad)
data.projectDigest: Corona Virus Disease 2019 (COVDI-19) has so far caused more than one million infections and 50000 deaths. Elderly (>60 years), males, smokers and people with pre-existing diseases developed more severe disease globally. Only 6% of Pakistani population are over 60 years however they are exposed to more infections than western populations. There are inconclusive evidence that chloroquine use for malaria are effective against COVID. BCG (a vaccine used to prevent Tuberculosis, TB) is believed to prevent infections not only caused by TB but also by other viruses and bacteria due to its non-specific effects and similarly worm infestation may prevent from several chronic diseases. All of this may be due to cross-immunity or enhanced general immunity among exposed population. This may put Pakistani population at high or low risk of COVID-19. Thus, we designed a project to study: the relation of COVID-19 with childhood BCG vaccination and chloroquine; relation of obesity, smoking, comorbidities and nutritional status with COVID-19 severity; and clinical presentation (signs and symptoms) and severity (mild, moderate and severe) of COVID-19 in Pakistani population. We are conducting a study to compare COVID-19 postive patients (mild and severe) with COVID-negative patients and study their characteristics and factors described above. ?

data.projectName: Mathematical and Epidemiological Modeling of COVID-19 Pandemic in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
The last two decades had witnessed that mathematical and statistical models played an effective role in understanding the transmission of infectious diseases like Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) in 2003, Swine flu in 2009, MERS CoV in 2013 and Zika in 2016. These models helped in evaluating the impact of control programs in controlling the spread of the disease and reducing the morbidity and mortality. The outbreak of the recent novel COVID-19 has aroused several challenges for the researchers due to its random spread across the globe. Several pieces of research have been done in the Globe so far to underline the myths but none of them has some conclusive remarks about the spread and the control of the disease because each country or region has its own dynamics that determine the spread of the disease. Pakistan like other countries has its portfolios like low literacy, high dense population, lower health facilities, etc. that placed the people of the country at high risk. None of the research has been conducted so far in the region that models the spread of the infectious disease concerning its local context. 
In the proposed research, some Evidence-Informed mathematical and statistical models would be tailored to estimate and forecast the spread of the COVID-19 by considering the local parameters of real-time data (fates of cases, control measures), biological information (transmission biology, pathogenesis, host range, etc.), epidemiological information (risk factors, sensitivity and specificity, etc.) and demographical information (host demography, contact structure, population characteristics, etc.).  The proposed models will use the SIR, Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) or some time series modeling techniques to simulate and to fit best the local data.  The

data.projectName: Development of inanimate solid virucidal surfaces
data.projectDigest:
Contacts with various contaminated surfaces is major reason for fast spread of contagious diseases. Breaking the chain of contamination is viable solution to fight against COVID19 and other such diseases. High-touch surfaces in hospitals or emergency and protective equipment like mask, hand gloves are exposed to viral load and provide major route of cross contamination and spread. Viruses stay active for several hours to days depending on the type of surface. Covering human- reachable surfaces with virucidal materials would break the chain. Laboratory-based studies are available in the literature which show that certain materials can instantly kill the viruses when encounter it. However, no such product is available in market. This project is designed to prepare material with potential antiviral activities indigenously and to coat/imbed them on surfaces like fabric, wood steel, aluminum etc and finally to test their efficiency in killing viruses. In addition, to scale-up the production of virucidal coatings and bring them to market.
This project will require expertise in (1) material preparation, (2) BSL3 laboratory facility and (3) product development. This project is consortium of three Universities; Najma Memon and M. Hassan Agheem from University of Sindh, Muhammad Raza Shah from University of Karachi and Zeeshan Khatri from Mehran University of Engineering and Technology. The three have responsibility of material preparation, virucial activity testing and product development, respectively while NanoClo is sectoral partner in this project. Similar activities are also initiated in USA and Israel, however, no products yet.

data.projectName: Development and Clinical applications of Rapid Diagnostic Kit for COVID-19 through lateral flow Immunoassay (LFIA)
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest:
SARS-CoV-2 (previously known as 2019-nCoV), which causes the COVID-19 disease, is the latest Corona Virus strain to be identified. 
Pakistan is one of those countries that have also been reporting COVID-19 confirmed cases and need to develop rapid COVID-19 testing kit to handle possible outbreak and subsequent treatment which can be used in hospitals, clinics, testing laboratories, businesses, schools, airports, seaports and train stations. RT-PCR is considered the standard diagnostic method, however it is associated with a number of limitations e.g., 1) Time consuming. 2)Requires specialized labs and expertise.  These limitations make RT-PCR unsuitable for use in the field for rapid and simple diagnosis and screening of patients. 
Testing of antibodies of SARS-CoV-2 in patients’ blood is a good choice for rapid, highly sensitive diagnosis of COVID-19. Furthermore, detection of IgM antibodies tends to indicate a recent exposure to SARS-CoV-2, whereas detection of COVID-19 IgG antibodies indicates exposure to the virus some time ago. Assays can be performed in central laboratories (CLT) or by point-of-care testing. For PoCT a single specimen of blood is usually obtained by skin puncture. Unlike PCR methods an extraction step is not needed before assay. A Chinese group has developed point-of-care lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA) test which can detect IgM and IgG simultaneously in human blood within 15 minutes with high sensitivity and specificity.
The present project is being submitted focusing on the development of rapid LFIA test kit for the detection of IgM and IgG antibodies against COVID-19 in human blood to facilitate screening of maximum population.

data.projectName: Epidemic (COVID-19) Risk-Based Decision-Making Tool for Interdependent Regional Workforce Systems
data.projectDigest:
The outbreak of the coronavirus named COVID-19 has resulted in mortality, morbidity, and disrupted the global economy and is spreading onwards. In Pakistan, due to infectious and contagious nature of COVID-19, this epidemic has the potential to have immediate devastating and prolonged effects on the working population, which consequently affects workforce levels available to industrial sectors.  
Coming towards significant among the many challenges: Firstly, an optimum allocation of available resources due to lack of prediction modelling and epidemic surveillance is a great challenge for policy makers. Secondly, workforce disruptions in recent pandemic of COVID-19 adversely impacted regional economic productivity significantly in the production and supply chain of commodities on immediate basis. Thirdly, while the interdependencies among industry sectors are increasing with time, the recovery of the region is further slowed down by the ripple effects among economic sectors leading to direct and indirect economic losses in an economic region. 
To address these challenges, this research proposal will cover a thematic area of disease epidemiological modeling, which will attempt to integrate statistical dependence relationship with COVID-19 and workforce recovery in a dynamic Input-Output model. It will assist all the beneficiaries and stakeholders from public to  private sectors, NGOs, hospitals, rescue  organizations, and most importantly the industrial sector.

It will assist all the beneficiaries and stakeholders from public to  private sectors, NGOs, hospitals, rescue  organizations, and most importantly the industrial sector.

data.projectName: Real-time Spatio-temporal mapping of Covid19 Spread in Pakistan using Crowd-Sensing
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest: As Covid19 cases rapidly spread across the globe, there is a need to monitor and track the spread of the infection with respect to time and space. Such information would be valuable not only for medical teams tackling this infection, but also for governmental bodies for devising strategies related to control of Covid19. In this project we aim to make use of crowd sensing technology to gather real-time information about the appearance of symptoms in the population at large. Crowd sensing is a wellknown method to gather huge amount of information from the public in a very short span of time. Making use of a number of communication technologies e.g. SMS, Social Media Platforms and Mobile Applications, users will be asked to enter anonymized information regarding appearance of any symptoms. Such information will be mapped temporally and geospatially by making use of timestamps of the information received, as well as localization information of the user. The collected information will be stored in a cloud databased and will then eventually be mapped on a map divided into 10 km * 10 km grids, which will be updated temporally as well. This information would quickly provide information to the authorities about the density of individuals which are showing common symptoms in an area, and this information could then be exploited by the governmental bodies to track the spatio-temporal evolution of the COvid19 spread in Pakistan.

data.projectName: CARE
data.theme: Information Collection and Dissemination IT platforms)
data.projectDigest:
The world is currently going through a tumultuous time due to the on-going COVID-19 pandemic.
As it is known COVID-19 is a viral infection of the respiratory system with high probability of transmission. As currently no cure is available, the only available method to prevent the infection from spreading in general population is to practice social distancing.
However, social distancing is leading to great socio-economic impact on countries. Pakistan with its massive population of which a large population lives is either living below poverty line or is engaged in daily wage professions is facing a plethora of issues. These issues can have significant impact on Pakistan’s financial and/or medical resources which are already stretched to limit.
In order to prevent Pakistan’s economic and health institutes from being overwhelmed while ensuring provision of basic life necessities such as food, medicine etc. it is imperative that modern technology is used to ensure that contact between confirmed and potential infected individuals and general population is ensured. In addition, a system should be devised which facilitates essential movement of members of general population which ensuring that movement history of any future infection cases can be tracked to ensure all potential contacts can be traced automatically.
Hence a system for Persistent Surveillance for Prevention of Disease Spread is proposed.
A wrist wearable smart device based on Internet of Things (IOT) concept having following sensors will be developed:
-Body Temperature
-Pulse Rate
-Blood Pressure
-Blood Sugar
-Skin Enzyme pH
-GPS Sensor
-GSM equipment
-Memory unit

 AI / ML cloud computing based back-end software controlled at government level which would get information from the devices via GSM Comm.

data.projectName: Real-Time Coronavirus Affected People Identification in Pakistan using pH Litmus Paper Masks
data.projectDigest: Nowadays, Coronavirus disease (COVID-19) is the most common issue in all over the world. The basic means of spread of Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) coronavirus is the contact of mucus tissue with contagious condensations and through acquaintance to fomites. Knowledge of persistence from this infected virus is required for taking appropriate measures. To protect the people from this virus, different measures are introduced in the world like, wear a mask, wash hands for 20 seconds for the number of time in a day, use sanitizers, stay home, separate from each other, lockdown mosques, lockdown markets for longtime, lockdown, Musjid al-Haram and Musjid e Nabvi in Saudia, etc. To diagnose, coronavirus, medical tests are very costly in Pakistan. It is not affordable for the poor people of Pakistan as well as other under developing countries. Similarly, the masks that are introduced in the market are not of good quality. In this project, we have proposed the cheapest method for detecting coronavirus affected people. In our proposed method, pH Litmus paper masks are introduced to diagnose the coronavirus affected persons in society. When a virus affected person will wear this mask, its color will be changed through droplets, sneezing and coughing by Acids and Bases. Even though these masks will be suitable to create distancing between people in society by its color discrimination.

data.projectName: Development of indigenous plants based disinfectant formulation
data.theme: Development of disinfectants particularly using indigenous herbal ingredients
data.projectDigest: The cleaning and disinfection of hospitals wards, clinics and ambulances after patients treatment and transportation are very crucial practices for avoiding microbial and viral infections to other people using these facilities .  Due to recent COVID-19 outbreak, the risk of viral infection through touching the infected surfaces has increased.  Currently, chlorine based disinfectants are used to disinfect surfaces in clinics, hospitals and ambulances which are expensive as well as corrosive to a number of materials and also leave residual effects after applying. Besides hospitals and other health care units, the people are also much concerned about disinfecting various inanimate surfaces in their home thus the demand of effective disinfectants and sanitizer has increased exponentially. The market available disinfectants formulations are mainly consist of hypochlorite or chloroxylenol solutions.  Our previous studies showed that the essential oils and methanolic extracts of Mentha spicata, M. longifolia, Artemisia scoparia showed excellent anti-bacterial and anti-fungal activities against various human and plant pathogenic strains.  In this study the essential oils and solvents extracts of these plants will be formulated into disinfecting agent. The formulated disinfecting agent will be tested against various pathogenic fungal and bacterial strains through in vitro bioassays. The field trials will be conducted on various types of surfaces to check the effectiveness of prepared formulation followed by counting microbial infection through plating method. We are expected to develop highly active and cost effective disinfecting agent out of selected plants.

data.projectName: Pervaporation technology for low-cost production of dehydrated alcohols and solvents for disinfection and medical applications to fight against COVID-19 pandemic
data.theme: Development of disinfectants particularly using indigenous herbal ingredients
data.projectDigest: Considering the present situation of COVID-19 pandemic, there is an abrupt increase in demand for sanitizer/viricide to disinfect all types of surfaces and bodies that can be the potential carrier for spreading the virus. WHO and FDA have also indicated an unpredictable augmentation in the demand for hand sanitizers in their awareness campaign. Alcohols, particularly ethanol is a prime antiseptic ingredient in the sanitizers which is also used worldwide in healthcare facilities for viricidal activities. Although, 18 distilleries in Pakistan are producing ethanol up to 96% purity from the fermentation of the molasses in sugar industries. However, production of medical-grade anhydrous ethanol of purity > 99% is a big challenge for such thermal distillation processes due to a very low flash point of the concentrated ethanol (< 20 oC). Therefore, it is crucial to introduce energy-efficient alternative technologies to extract the maximum proportion of medical-grade alcohols, particularly ethanol from molasses to hamper their use in medical applications. In this context, we propose 1st of its kinds of permselective composite membranes (PCMs)-integrated pervaporation (PV) molecular separation technology. We aim to simultaneously produce and industrialize PCMs-integrated pilot-scale PV rigs to cost-effectively produce medical-grade alcohols as disinfectants to fight against coronavirus pandemic.

data.projectName: Identification of drugs effective against SARS-CoV-2 through combining deep machine learning, molecular dynamics simulations and in vitro studies
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Medical University, Islamabad
data.projectDigest: The ongoing pandemic of Coronavirus Disease 2019 has posed a serious threat to global public health with more than 1,000,000 confirmed cases and 55,092 deaths reported till April 03, 2020. With no approved treatment or vaccine available, this emergency situation calls for immediate development of safe and effective treatments for SARS-CoV-2. Drug discovery is a process that takes years, therefore, an effective and efficient approach in this emergency situation is to repurpose already existing drugs to treat SARS-CoV-2 infection. Computational approaches offer a time efficient and effective way to make expedited discovery of effective therapeutics. Our highly skilled multi-disciplinary team of computer scientists, bioinformaticians, physicians and virologists has designed an innovative study that will use an integrative drug repurposing methodology using different computational techniques and in vitro studies. The study will combine advanced deep learning computational techniques, molecular modeling techniques of 3D docking and molecular dynamics simulations to shortlist effective drugs against SARS-CoV-2 by screening databases of FDA approved, experimental and phytochemical (herbal) drugs. This will be followed by in vitro analysis of shortlisted candidate drugs. FDA approved drugs identified through this novel combination of approaches can immediately be repurposed for clinical use. Availability of effective treatments for SARS-CoV-2 will have significant public health, social and economic impact in Pakistan and the World.

data.projectName: Artificial Intelligence driven Modeling for Policymakers in Epidemic Disease Management and Control
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest:
The world has experienced a new potent challenge in the shape of Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-2019). The current capacity of the country for responding to the outbreak needs to be augmented. Capacities like Case management, risk communication and Infection Prevention & Control (IPC) at healthcare facilities are among the challenges. Assessment must be initiated rapidly on evaluation of the existing health infrastructure, evaluation of the existing organizational infrastructure and risk assessment and communication.  So, this project is focused on the development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems and Disease Epidemiological Modeling using Big-Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence.
For keeping the epidemic spread curve under control, the authorities have taken stringent measures. These are welcoming in controlling the situation in the short run. However, in countries like Pakistan, where the social fabric is so strong and religious affairs have significant influence on the code of social interactions, it seems cumbersome to sustain these measures. So, there is a need of more concrete measures which can be adopted with the help of reliable sufficient parameters.
The model we are proposing will help the authorities with these parameters for decision making.

data.projectName: Development of Rapid and Low-Cost Coronavirus (COVID-19) Detection Method for Low Income Population of Balochistan
data.piUniversity: Balochistan University of Information Technology, Engineering and Management Sciences,Quetta
data.projectDigest: The world has experienced a new potent challenge in the shape of Corona virus disease 2019 (COVID-2019). The outbreak that began in Wuhan, China, has rapidly disseminated worldwide affecting 204 countries with 54,190 death claims including 53 in Pakistan. WHO has declared world health emergency worldwide, as it presents many clinical and public health management challenges as a result of little understanding of viral pathogenesis, risk factors for infection, natural history of disease as well as effective preventive measures and public health response and containment interventions. Balochistan, is at the center of the coronavirus outbreak as a result of the quarantine crisis at Taftan with 100+ individuals being tested positive. Among the govt’s dedicated facilities, only Fatima Jinnah Chest Hospital is serving as the testing point for coronavirus in Quetta. With no antiviral treatment nor vaccine available, the earliest diagnosis of the patients and subsequent immediate quarantine is the only way to save the lives of people and prevent further human-human transmission of the pathogen. This project is designed to upgrade the existing departmental microbiology lab into WHO standard BSL2 lab for COVID-19 detection and overcome the costly, time-consuming and laborious detection technique of RT-qPCR with rapid and low-cost alternative.

data.projectName: Determining SARS-CoV-2 virulence along with actuating the scope and vivacious kinetics of ACE2, HAT and TMPRSS2 receptors in Pakistani population to predict disease severity, possible clinical interventions and vaccine efficacy
data.piUniversity: Balochistan University of Information Technology, Engineering and Management Sciences,Quetta
data.projectDigest: The Spike proteins are the main structural proteins of Corona virus which gets attachment with the receptors of lungs named angiotensin-converting enzyme-2 (ACE2).  To infect the lungs the S protein of Corona needs cleavage of S into S1 and S2 by other receptor proteases which break the S protein into its segments. Transmembrane Protease, Serine 2 (TMPRSS2) and human airway trypsin-like protease (HAT) are involved in this activation. We aim to determine the differences of sequences and gene expression of these receptors before and after virus infection (Cell lines, biopsies). The sequencing of the Corona virus would help to make epidemiological and evolutionary relationship of Pakistani Corona virus with the World. The best antigenic sites for vaccination and treatments would be predicted.  The change in nucleotide sequence of these receptors in different individuals and different populations may affect the attachment of S protein with lung receptors, as a result some ethnicities, individuals or certain age groups may be more susceptible and others may be resistant. The sequencing and gene expression studies of the lungs receptors for Corona virus would help to make best treatments/ inhibitors strategies against the virus. Due to limited studies, this proposed project is in benefits of Pakistani population.

data.projectName: Deciphering cytokine storm immune patterns of COVID-19 infection and their control strategies
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Coronavirus disease 19  (COVID-19) virus emerged in China in December 2019 causing significant acute respiratory disease especially in vulnerable population. World health organization declared it as pandemic due to threatening millions of lives and an estimate of 40 million deaths if not controlled urgently. Currently, COVID-19 has spread to 200 countries across globe and cases worldwide were at 799,441 and 38,726 deaths. COVID-19 in acutely infected patients is known to cause a hyper-inflammation called as “cytokine storm”. This lead to severe irreversible changes leading to patient death, hence we recommend identification and treatment plan for cytokine storm in acute patients. Current management of COVID-19 patients is supportive and the acute respiratory distress is leading cause of mortality. Today, doctors lack the full understanding of this syndrome characterized by hyper-cytokinemia followed by multiorgan failures. There are global efforts to produce and identify therapeutic agents to control this cytokine storm caused by COVID-19, control hyper-inflammation and cellular viral entry in infected lungs. In this project we aim to achieve the following:
1-	Characterize the immune patterns of COVID-19 infection using flow cytometry
2-	Comparision of healthy, infected and recovered patients immune cell populations 
3-	Deciphering the early and key players in the cytokine storm of COVID-19 in acutely infected patients 
4-	Identification of top 3 cytokines involved in recovery and/or fatalities in infected cases
5-	Identification and proposal of existing FDA-CDC approved therapeutic agents to control cytokine storm

data.projectName: administration of traditional herbal formulation to boost the immune system:a possible way to encounter COVID-19
data.projectDigest: The current situation demanded an urgent need to develop the strategies to cure and prevent the disease. The disease severity depends on the immunity status of the individual. The infected geriatric population and individual with past disease history are at risk and they are more prone to disease because of compromised immune system. After the attack of virus the immune system of the infected person start synthesizing various inflammatory markers in increased amount which then induce inflammation at the infected organ. As the infected organ in COVID-19 are lungs therefore the inflammation lead to pneumonitis, acute respiratory distress syndrome, respiratory failure, shock, organ failure and potentially death. The administration of anti-inflammatory, antioxidant and anti-infectious supplements has shown beneficial effects against infections. Nigella sativa (black seed), Zingiber officinale (ginger), Cinnamomum verum (cinnamon), Syzygium aromaticum (clove), Illicium verum (Chinese anise star), Crocus sativus (saffron), Peganum harmala (harmal) and honey have been consistently reported to have immune enhancing properties. Therefore, in this study a combination of herbal formulation using these herbs is suggested as an immune booster for the prevention as well as treatment of COVID-19. These herbs are indigenously available and have traditional use to cure bronchitis, cough, cold and fever.

Nigella sativa (black seed), Zingiber officinale (ginger), Cinnamomum verum (cinnamon), Syzygium aromaticum (clove), Illicium verum (Chinese anise star), Crocus sativus (saffron), Peganum harmala (harmal) and honey have been consistently reported to have immune enhancing properties. Therefore, in this study a combination of herbal formulation using these herbs is suggested as an immune booster for the prevention as well as treatment of COVID-19. These herbs are indigenously available and have traditional use to cure bronchitis, cough, cold and fever.

data.projectName: Molecular diagnosis for monitoring & control of CoviD-19 viruses
data.projectDigest: COVID-19 has the potential to have devastating effects on lives, society and the economy in Pakistan, where peaks in infection have not yet been reached. The COVID-19 pandemic is a relatively new and rapidly changing challenge that requires urgent multi-targeted action to protect public health, reduce the burden on healthcare services and to save lives. We will apply and develop multi-targeted molecular approaches to better understand, monitor and control coronavirus SARS-CoV-2 infection in Pakistan. It is extremely important to minimize and slow the rate of transmission in order to gain time to tickle this fatal pathogen strategically. In order to better understand how SARS-CoV-2 is spread and transmitted from person to person we will investigate fomite transmission, i.e. the spread of virus by touching surfaces. Using carefully designed experiments we will investigate how long active SARS-CoV-2 virus particles remain on different surfaces and objects and under different conditions of temperature and humidity. The World Health Organisation emphasises the need for more testing to beat COVID-19, hence our proposal to boost testing capacity in Pakistan. Alongside the urgent need for more testing, it is also important to better understand the SARS-CoV-2 virus at the molecular level using various computational and experimental approaches that will assist in strategies for therapeutic development.

data.projectName: Development and characterization of natural herbs as antiviral  drug
data.projectDigest: Recently, world is facing global threat  in the form highly transmissible COVID-19. The  novel corona virus with the single stranded RNA structure have caused pneumonia outbreak to the general population. In Wuhan, China, a novel and alarmingly contagious primary a typical (viral) pneumonia broke out in December 2019. It has since been identified as a zoonotic coronavirus, similar to SARS coronavirus and MERS coronavirus and named COVID-19. The WHO declared the epidemic of COVID-19 as a pandemic on March 12 2020  In order to treat this  viral disease world is facing serious challenges.  Recently, few French and USA based scientist have successfully done clinical ltrials on the  hydroxychloroquine and azitromycin.  However, there is a need for the improvement based on the  side effects of these medicine and  applicability to the patients of different age and sex. Therefore, we proposed here the natural herbs as an alternative to the earlier used drugs. For example,  heena called as Lawsone has the chemical structure similar to that of the  hydroxychloroquine.  Moreover, Lawsone is well known for its antimalarial and antibacterial properties. Thus, Lawsone is potentially a good choice to be investigated for the various emerging viral diseases.

data.projectName: Development of serology based diagnostic tool to source track and propose mitigation strategy for nCovSARS
data.projectDigest: The COVID-19 is a major public health concern of this century and due to massive global impact the nCov-SARS has become a global pandemic disaster. Since, the only solution to control the spread of COVID-19 is to stay quarantined which has led to a global lockdown leaving the world in the worst economic crisis. Prevention of the disease requires screening and immunization of the population. A developing country where the majority is living at the edge of the poverty line cannot practice lockdown for a longer period. Keeping this in mind, controlling the spread, morbidity and mortality of this disease, it is best to safeguard the population through proper screening and immunization. However, the availability and performance of existing imported diagnostic kit based on RT-PCR is a major limiting factor in mass screening. WE PROPOSE to develop a serological diagnostic kit and to source track the potential epicenter for any future outbreak by identifying asymptomatic carriers. Our HYPOTHESIS is that mapping of asymptomatic carriers through development and optimization of a serology based test kit will be effective in controlling the spread of disease. Our GOAL is to develop the ICT kit to screen asymptomatic carriers and isolate them to reduce spread of infection in the community. This will not only limit the spread but allow us to mitigate the predisposing factors of the disease, reducing environmental load and economic crisis as well. The planned METHODOLOGY will be to clone and express surface glycoproteins of coronavirus using state-of-the-art HaloTagTM technology in E. coli followed by quantification through Bradford assay. Further, the protein will be processed with an immunological reaction with the hyper-immune sera for the development and optimization of ICT kit. M

data.projectName: Development of vaccine for COVID-19
data.projectDigest:
COVID-19 has spread across the globe with unseen speed and ferocity. It's forced the cancellation of major events including the Tokyo Olympics and sent the world into self-isolation in an attempt to curb the spread. Health authorities and governments are attempting to flatten the curve and mitigate extensive transmission in the community, while scientists and researchers turn their attention to the coronavirus causing the disease: SARS-CoV-2.
Since it was first discovered as the causative agent of COVID-19, scientists have been racing to get a better understanding of the virus' genetic makeup and trying to unravel how to effectively treat infections. There's no cure and medical specialists can only treat the symptoms of the disease. Many different treatment options have been proposed and some older drugs seem to be associated with positive outcomes -- but much more work is required. However, the long-term strategy to combat COVID-19, which has spread to every continent on Earth besides Antarctica, is to develop a vaccine. There are multiple attempts in progress to develop vaccine against COVID-19 globally. But those would be very expensive for developing countries like Pakistan. Hence there is a dire need to develop indigenous COVID-19 vaccine. Here we propose development of COVID-19 vaccine that would offers potential for prevention and treatment of COVID-19.

data.projectName: Developing Cloud Based AI Platform of RT-PCR Scanning Machines for Rapid Novel Corona Virus COVID-19 Diagnosis and Tracking
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest: The purpose of this research is to pave way for establishment of remote diagnosis points across the country. The remote diagnostic points will be equipped with COVID-19 testing kits and a Thermo- cycler unit. The Thermo-cycler is a device used to run RT-PCR test. Each Thermo-cycler will be connected to a target remote station application via a USB connection. The target remote station application will append the Thermo-cycler test results with the respective patient’s data (such as CNIC number, name, age, location, current address) and transfer them through internet to the centralized server station that will be receiving data from multiple remote diagnostic points. The central server station will be equipped with an Artificial Intelligence (AI) application, indigenously designed in this project, which interpret the values provided by the Thermo-cycler and provided results either the patient is COVID-19 positive or negative. The results will be transmitted back to the remote diagnostic point from where the patient will be released or quarantined depending on the results obtained from the server. In case of positive result, the AI application will also update the national database for identification of COVID-19 patient along with the necessary information regarding the patient such as CNIC number, name, age, location, current address. This information is further relayed to a web based application which will help in identifying the geographical distribution of new patients across the country and thus help in identifying hot-spots for COVID-19 so that the local government machinery can be mobilized to curtain the outbreak in particular locality.

data.projectName: Evolutionary Analysis, Preparation and Evaluation of quantitative Real Time PCR (qRT-PCR) and ELISA-based Detection Kits for the Diagnosis of SARS-CoV-2 in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
In December 2019, an outbreak of unknown fatal respiratory infection was emerged in Wuhan, China.  Early it was assumed to be spread from Huanan Seafood Market, later the researcher have suggested it may not be the original source of virus transmission to human beings. The causative agent was identified as a novel coronavirus and later renamed SARS-CoV-2 by the International Committee on Taxonomy of Viruses. The SARS-CoV-2 is genetically similar to 2002-2004 Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (SARS-CoV) and bat SARS-like coronaviruses. The virus exhibited quick human to human transmission. The SARS-CoV-2 binds to receptor on human cell surface called angiotensin converting enzyme-2 (ACE-2) and spread through respiratory tract. The SARS-CoV-2 has been spread to >160 developed and developing countries causing a serious pandemic situation. Majority of people infected with SARS-CoV-2 developed severe respiratory illness, including fever, cough and shortness of breath. Mortality in most cases has been seen in the elderly and individuals with co-morbidities or weakened immune system.
Mainly, we are planning to developed new qRT-PCR and ELISA kits against local SARS-CoV-2 strains and minimize the import from other countries. It may result in cost effective and efficient approach under the current pandemic situation. Diagnostic kits developed in proposed project will help to cope with the current pandemic situation in the country. In this way, we will offer diagnostic kits for timely detection and will be able to assist Federal and Provincial governments in this battle against SARS-CoV-2.

data.projectName: Formulations and preparation of topical antiviral herbal disinfectants from the native plants of Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.theme: Development of disinfectants particularly using indigenous herbal ingredients
data.projectDigest: Presently, the emergence of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), a causative pathogen for coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID 19) is a major health concern in human beings throughout the world. This virus transmits from man to man spreading via droplets, infected hands or inanimate surface with the incubation of 2-10 days. So far, the only way is sanitation and eradication by using surfactants. Several disinfectants are available in the market; however, they are associated with many disadvantages. Most remarkably, these are of antimicrobial nature tending to be very expensive and often require uptake into a cell to inactivate a virus or stop viral propagation. In the present scenario, there is need to develop wide range of effective herbal disinfectant for sanitation and maintaining good public health. The present proposal aimed at preparing and formulating topical synergistic composition which can be used as slow release devise such as hand cleaners, soaps and bath gel, sanitizer, mouth/throat wash, air spray. Various solvent extracts of selected medicinal plants rich in secondary metabolites (flavonoids, saponins, coumarins and terpenes) shall be used either sole or in combination for the formulations followed by antimicrobial activity and formulations. In vivo skin toxicity of final formulations shall be checked for cytotoxicity.

data.projectName: AI-based Real-time prediction and surveillance system for COVID-19 and other infectious diseases
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest:
We propose to develop an Artificial intelligence-based real-time prediction and surveillance system for COVID-19 and other infectious diseases implemented in MATLAB. The proposed model will initially be trained for structured data. Spread and prediction results will be announced through the web. Android app will be developed and tested primarily for the general public to avoid traveling into a specific area if it is at high risk. 

General Objectives: 
a. Develop an AI model for real-time spread and prediction of COVID-19 and other infections. 
b. Test the model with preliminary data and devices along with Beta testing.  
c. Development of an android app to share the warnings and travel risk assessment to the general public. 
d. Establishment of a local deep learning system shareable with others working on AI.

data.projectName: Seroepidemiology and geo-fencing of COVID-19 in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Sever Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS-CoV- 2) or COVID-19 is declared pandemic currently, which needs no detailed introduction. There are several genetic variants reported from different parts of the World, causing Corona virus respiratory syndrome. These variants are different genetically from the COVID-19 isolated from other countries as well. The present proposal envisages the sero-epidemiology of different variants in Pakistan and to relate the prevalence in relation to the history of travel from different countries etc. The sampling will be undertaken throughout the country alongwith companion suspected animals also. Initially Complement Fixation Test will be implemented to screen different serotypes of COVID-19 and then for final genetic comparison will be done through quantitative PCR. It is expected that we will be able to decide the vaccine type and know the role of different animals and other risk factors in disease spread in Pakistan.

data.projectName: InfoCURE
data.theme: Information Collection and Dissemination IT platforms)
data.projectDigest:
Currently, the total number of confirmed cases in the world and specifically Pakistan is showing an exponential growth with death toll on the rise, despite lock down in most of the countries. The knowledge sharing gap and lack of genuine information between doctors and the general public as well as Pakistan lacking the ability and capacity for introducing new systems, that could help mitigate the information gap between the doctors and pandemics, could result in the loss of precious lives.
With the advancements in technology, the flow of information gains new peaks every day. But this information flow comes with its own risk – false information or in other words “fake news”. With the general public unable to access doctors and physicians in this time, everyone is trying to disseminate information without properly evaluating it from a professional – a doctor or physician. In view of the current pandemic, false information has led the world to practice the use of unauthenticated medicine, believe that people in their 20s and 30s can’t get sick and “it is just a flu” etc. These practices have led to the loss several lives. 
Therefore, a unified and authorized platform – for doctors and front-line paramedics in the current situation, and in case of emergencies ranging from earthquakes to avalanches to general disease outbreaks – that could debunk all the false information and present the general public with verified information is significantly needed.

data.projectName: Design and Development of Breathable steam tunnels for Inhalation by large population
data.projectDigest: As per International literature, steam inhalation has numerous benefits especially in the light of current respiratory pandemic. Steam Tunnel design and development is proposed for exposing large population to positive effects of steam especially where the population density is high  (urban areas). Nicely placed tunnels shall be walk through tunnels for people entering or exiting a area so that sufficient steam is inhaled before leaving the tunnel. It is a preventive measure especially to address current pandemic but also for future to arrest respiratory diseases and for general well being. It has the propensity to sanitize garments and other personal effects.  This concept is different from Disinfectant tunnels.

data.projectName: Detection and Tracking Contagion Using IoT-Edge Technologies: Confronting CONVID-19 Pandemic
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest:
Our RRG project’s research activities propose a smart edge surveillance system with a wearable smart product (gadget) that effective in remote monitoring, advance warning and detection of wearing person’s fever, heart beat rate, cardiac conditions and some of the radiological features to detect the infected (suspicious) person. In this way interaction chain can be observed or monitored for identification of infected/suspicious persons.
According to world health organization (WHO) protective health measures in addressing CONVID-19, the social distancing, home isolation and home quarantine could slow down the spread of the infection, interrupt transmission and reduce case numbers to low levels. The health and societal impact of this research project is to develop smart edge surveillance systems we can, to help public health authorities, researchers and clinicians contain and manage this disease. Research outcomes of this project will provide a continually updated map/pattern of communication chain of infected persons for CONVID-19 that may span around in our national community. It would make significant contribution in better understanding of epidemic, patterns of spread, develop diagnostics. 
As mentioned above, the solution to this vital issue i.e. H2H tracing lies under the phenomenon of IoT and edge computing mechanism.

data.projectName: Immunophenotyping of acute SARS-CoV-2 infection: a comparison between asymptomatic, mild and severe COVID-19 patients
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Amongst viral infection, including all zoonotic viral infections, Corona virus stands out leading to global epidemics and pandemics. SARS-CoV 1, MERS and SARS-CoV 2 have collectively landed many into hospital ICUs, pushing the healthcare burden to its threshold. data.projectName: Title of Project:	Epidemiological modeling and forecasting the effects and severity of COVID-19
data.projectDigest: The first human coronavirus was Identified in 1960, the latest version of coronavirus is COVID-19 and firstly identified in the seafood market of Wuhan. It is betacoronavirus, transmitting from animals and humans to humans. It has been compulsory to model the working, structure and evolvement method of this virus using Artificial intelligence (AI) and to predict the upcoming effect, trends, and severity of this virus. By modeling, we will be able to predict the fatality rate in upcoming years, its severity rate and parameters, precautionary measures and development of drugs accordingly. There are some databases such as GISAID [2]  that are keeping the track of the rate of spreading, evolvement and genetic changes. Using these databases and with the help of AI and phylogenetic effects, we can develop such systems that can predict the trends, effects, and severity of COVID-19. As there is no specific medicine exist that can target and cure this coronavirus, so, it is important to predict its severity level for the precautionary measures. We are going to develop a system that will be able to forecast the severity and genetic evolve rate, its flow, vulnerabilities, interval intervention and immune as well as eradication points of COVID-19. For the implementation we will take the data from authentic data repositories, use data mining and machine learning techniques to validate our extracted features, and use deep learning models for forecasting. Our sectoral collaborator will help in data cleaning and development aspects.

data.projectName: Tying Rapid Responses to Smart Testing: Empowering Local Government Response in Pakistan’s COVID-19 Outbreak
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest:
This project leverages a unique partnership with provincial governments and testing partners to explore the question of how the Pakistani government can deliver an evidence-driven rapid policy response at the right level to maximize lives saved and minimize economic costs in two steps: 1) developing and piloting systematic smart testing to collect real-time data on virus prevalence and transmission, thereby decreasing uncertainty about transmission patterns, and 2) providing evidence-based real-time feedback to government counterparts on localized (district-level) situations and the effectiveness of policy responses. Building upon initial pilot work in Lahore and Islamabad which tested the feasibility of our smart testing model of 100 airport immigration staff, we propose generating a repeated cross-sectional sample of COVID-19 testing data in Pakistan in order to examine and understand transmission vectors. 

We will first focus testing on populations one-degree removed from the virus who are exposed but not necessarily symptomatic (for e.g., frontline airport/border staff, hospital and quarantine facilities staff, those living proximate to positive cases) to give an accurate representation of prevalence. We will then work with government officials to provide them real-time information to inform their policy decisions and track their effectiveness on subsequent prevalence.

data.projectName: UV light Based Disinfection system and Personal Protection Gloves
data.projectDigest:
Proposed project is development of tools for disinfection of medical apparatus to indoor rooms to large open areas. As deadly corona virus pandemic is still out of control due to its potential of transmission via a variety of routes, disinfection of following objects and places are one the essential things to control this disaster,
•	Medical apparatus, suits in hospital for doctors and staff
•	Indoor patients, testing laboratories
•	Streets, stairs, parks, malls, trains, buses, planes, etc
Ultra Violet light has ability to disrupt genetic material and kill virus cells and sanitise hospital wards without the need for chemicals. Commercially available roaming robots with multiple UV bulbs emit concentrated UV-C ultraviolet light, which destroys bacteria, viruses and other harmful microbes by damaging their DNA and RNA, so they can’t multiply. This could reduce dependency on chemical-based disinfectants such as hydrogen peroxide, which require rooms to be left empty for several hours during sterilisation, making them impractical for many parts of hospitals. Similarly, manual outdoor surveys can not be achieved as it might not reach certain corners.

For corona virus disinfection purposes, following tools are proposed to be developed,
1.	UV light based portable disinfection Gloves and face shield
2.	Autonomous unmanned aerial systems (UAV) for difficult terrains with UV light and spraying tanks for location based disinfection with no dead ends
Above tools will not only ensure more safely of our frontline fighters (Doctors, medical staff, etc) but also effective and timely disinfection of large areas using technology.

data.projectName: Path Analyses of Biopsychosocial Model of COVID-19: Risk and Protective Factors
data.projectDigest: The main objective of this research project is to explore what demographic, biological and psychosocial factors lead to the complete recovery from COVID-19 in patients who recovered from COVID-19. The study will further explore in detail the effectiveness of various foods, herbs and liquids as suggested by experts. The effects of certain foods containing vitamins C, B and E and superfoods (eggplant, pumpkin, carrot, berried, onion, garlic, fish, olives, nuts, whole grain and honey are all high in antioxidants) or anti-inflammatory agent e.g., turmeric, which contains a natural compound called curcumin. Moreover, the study will explore many psychological factors i.e., loneliness, anxiety symptoms, depression symptoms, insomnia and social support as covariates in dealing with coronavirus.

data.projectName: Predictive Epidemiological Modeling on Covid-19 for Pakistan in formulating the policies
data.projectDigest:
The covid-19 pandemic has shown its devastating impact in more than 200 countries and territories across the globe with overall more than 1 Million confirmed cases till date and over 58,000 deaths(03 April, 2020)[1]. Pakistan is also suffering with 2637 cases and 40 deaths [2] and the number is on the rise.  
Public health strategies to fight any epidemic always require epidemiological data of the disease. In case of covid-19, different patterns of disease spread and case fatality rate has been observed in different regions of the world, especially in the countries most affected by this pandemic such as China, Italy, Spain and USA. The irregular trends pose difficulty for Government and practitioners to develop effective health strategies. Pakistan with increasing number of cases, urgently needs the disease epidemics which could help policy makers and stake holders to develop effective action of plans to combat the virus.  Furthermore, the impact of interventions such as quarantine of patients, closure of workplaces, educational institutions and outpatient departments in hospitals and finally lockdown in the provinces should be calibrated to show the effectiveness of these measures on the mortality and morbidity statistics and the possibility to fight against this pandemic.

data.projectName: Artificial Intelligence based crowd surveillance for reducing the spread of COVID-19
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest:
Crowded places are a hub for the transfer of contagious diseases, particularly those airborne diseases. In Pakistan, crowded environments are quite common, for instance, in banks, at govt. offices such as tax office, etc. These places help in rapid and mass transfer of mostly viral diseases if even a single person inflicted with the disease (including carriers) is present. This is most common when such a person is showing only minor symptoms but can be responsible for transferring it to other healthy people.

During a pandemic or even to avoid one to happen, it is important that the spread of such diseases is properly contained without having to resort to extreme measures such as a complete lock-down. Such solutions are not sustainable in countries like Pakistan. We propose an Artificial Intelligence based system that helps monitor crowds for potential disease carriers using CCTV cameras. The advantage is that such cameras are already widespread and could be used for this. We propose to use machine learning and computer vision techniques to aid in crowd identification, activity detection (such as a person persistently coughing) and temperature detection (person having fever). Such a person, if identified, can be separated from a crowd and help to prevent a rapid spread of a viral disease such as the COVID-19.

data.projectName: Tracing COVID-19 in Pakistan using Next generation genomics and proteomics approaches
data.projectDigest: fSARS-CoV-2 has succumbed 55 thousand people to date with a more than 1 million infection cases globally. The virus emerged in late December 2019 in Wuhan, China and now has been spread in 204 countries around the world. In Pakistan, there are more than 2500 COVID-19 positive cases and it still increasing. CoV-2 has 96% genomic identity with previously reported SARS coronavirus back in 2002 and 2003. Despite the efforts to combat the CoV-2 around the world, there is an exponential increase in positive cases since WHO announced COVID-19 a pandemic. In Pakistan, initially, CoV-2 was transmitted to local population by international travellers from Iran, Italy, China and UK. So, this is expected that infected people in Pakistan would be carrying multiple strains of CoV-2. Recently sequenced genome from travelling carrier of CoV-2 in Pakistan shows a mutated strain related to China outbreak. Genome sequence from local strains is still required to trace CoV-2 infection patterns and develop active immunization methods related to Pak-Cov-2. This will help to study the changes in CoV-2 proteins like Main Protease, Papain-like protease, E-channel and Spike proteins using multiple biophysical tools. Changes in the proteome pattern of COVID-19 patients will allow to study the mode of infection and will help in identification of potential biomarkers for COVID-19. This study where allows comparative genome and proteomics analyses of multiple CoV-2 for viable diagnostic tests development and vaccine targets identification, it will also allow to analyse efficacy of any developed and marketed vaccines/drugs against Pak-Cov-2 strains

data.projectName: Development of AI based Coronavirus (COVID-19) Pandemic for automatic prediction and monitoring using Machine and Deep Convolutional neural network Models
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest: COVID19 (first reported in Wuhan, China in December 2019) can cause severe respiratory illness, capable of spreading from person to person. A significant number of patients expire within 2-3 weeks after infection (~3-5%). COVID19 was declared a pandemic on Mar 11, 2020. The Centers for Disease Control (CDC) and Prevention, the US agency projected (Mar 25, 2020) that the number of infected individuals and deaths are expected to rise exponentially in the coming months, far from reaching their peaks. Currently, the country is facing the facility of ventilation system capacity and testing kits even expensive for COVID19 patients across the country in most of the hospitals and health care systems. The number of the lung CT can rise to an unprecedent rate in the foreseeable future, which will be challenging for radiologists, clinicians and effecting patients care. Thus, we require such an efficient system through which we can process the CT images of COVID 19 patients to inform the patient care, CT lung temporal changes, survival, progression and recurrence of COVID-19 patients. We proposed to build and train an efficient AI system, which can automatically predict these factors at early stage for further treatment/ quarantine the patients in an efficient manner.

data.projectName: Understanding Locally Transmitted SARS-CoV-2 by Molecular and Computational Approach: The Glass Half Empty
data.projectDigest: COVID-19 is caused by SARS-CoV-2 virus infection. Currently there is no vaccine and anti-viral therapy available to treat COVID-19. It has been observed by whole genome sequence that our locally transmitted SARS-CoV-2 is genetically mutated. The outcome of those genetic mutations are still unknown. Therefore, it is an immediate need to understand the pathogenic pattern of our locally transmitted SARS-CoV-2 strains. Current study is designed to use molecular and computational approach to analyze pathogenicity related genes and proteins by depicting 3D proteins models of locally transmitted SARS-CoV-2.  Furthermore, by using molecular docking techniques putative drug target sites will also evaluated. These research objectives will be helpful not only to find immune pattern of locally transmitted SARS-CoV-2 but also helpful in predicting possible drug options to treat COVID-19 in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Targeting SARS-CoV-2 Main Protease as Treatment Strategy for COVID-19
data.projectDigest: The first case of novel corona virus infection was reported in December 2019 but the first quarter of year 2020 witnessed corona virus disease-19 (COVID-19) pandemic havoc in the world. The developed countries like USA, China, and Europe are going through serious turmoil with death toll exceeding 54000 as of 3rd April 2020. Several treatment modalities and strategies have been used to grapple with SARS-CoV-2 infection; however, none of them seemed to be remarkable. Until today, no vaccine or drug is available for COVID-19. Researchers are striving to develop vaccine and find existing antivirals, and recently, FDA issued “emergency use authorization” for two antimalarial drugs to avert COVID-19. It is, therefore, indispensable to immediately discover potent molecules to prevent virus-human cell attachment or inhibit viral replication and growth within the cell. Among several strategies to cease virus life-cycle in the human cell, the inhibition of the main protease enzyme is characterized as the best drug targets for coronaviruses. Using this approach, several protease inhibitors are discovered for the treatment of HIV and HCV infections. The aim of this project is to target SARS-CoV-2-Mpro as strategic approach to treat COVID-19 by discovering inhibitors using combined computational and experimental drug discovery techniques.

data.projectName: Investigating Immunohistopathology of lung tissues of COVID-19 patients
data.projectDigest:
Recent outbreak due to coronavirus pandemic has greatly affected the whole globe even both developing and developed countries. In Pakistan to date 2458 cases has been reported with 35 fatalities and the whole country is lockdown due to their pandemic scale, while around the globe 1,023,729 people are suffering from coronavirus with 53,993 deaths. A number of studies have been reported demonstrating the epidemiology and surveillance of SARS-CoV-2 and their pattern of spreading. However their detail pathological changes in the lung tissue remain to be identified. On the other hand there is less information and report about pattern of immune system to COVID-19. 
It is more important to know the changes happening in the immune system of patients and how to cope with such situation. For this purpose the goal of current project is to explore structural changes of lung tissues and the role of different cells and immune factors which will give us a background for the development diagnostic procedure in early encounter of COVID-19. Histopathology and immunohistochemistry is the core element to find the molecular mechanism of disease and their early diagnosis is of urgent need for COVID-19 to be explored. To describe the histopathologic changes in the lung of patients with COVID-19.

data.projectName: “Development of an Antiviral and Immunomodulators Safe Herbal Products Through Ethanobotanical and Phytochemical Evaluations of local Medicinal Herbs”
data.piUniversity: Karakurum International University, Gilgit, Gilgit Baltistan
data.theme: Development of disinfectants particularly using indigenous herbal ingredients
data.projectDigest: The ethnobotanical and natural products studies are main research area for the rapid discovery and development of the new drugs and herbal products against the challenging diseases. The present worldwide COVID-19 outbreak, and other viral infectious diseases are strongly demanded to develop the safe natural, and regular therapies due to shortage of   antiviral drugs in the global markets. Additionally, the available synthetic antiviral drugs indicated the different-strong adverse effects in the patients. Most importantly, the present worldwide COVID-19 outbreak required the anti products and immunomodulators to control the COVID-19 infection on time.  Thus, the world scientific communities are strongly intended to discover the safe anti drugs for COVID-19 and others viral infections as soon as possible. The rapid outcome of the proposed project will  disinfect the present COVID-19 outbreak.

data.projectName: Development of reusable respiratory facemasks and medical gowns for protection against COVID-19 using conventional and innovative textile manufacturing techniques practicable in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Currently, most of the market available gowns and facemasks in Pakistan are not known to provide required level of protection and give a false sense of it. This poses a risk to wearer, especially, the healthcare workers. Moreover, almost all available products are disposable, and may become one of the causes of spread of pandemic as they themselves become carriers of the virus once disposed-off. Disposable nature of these PPEs also results in huge demand in order to assure provision of a new gown/mask every time it is needed. This demand is further intensified by the fact that most of our industry do not have technology to develop these disposable PPEs.
The proposed project aims at development of reusable PPEs assuring required protection levels and quantities. This will be accomplished using facilities available in local industry through optimization and modification of textile structures and their post treatments (lamination/coating/finishing). Further, innovative integration of nanowebs, scalable to industrial levels, will be employed to achieve required protection and comfort levels simultaneously. The developed structures will be validated to ensure the provision of required protection levels. 
The proposal has been based on the fact that optimized woven/knitted/nonwoven structures enhanced with laminations/coatings [5-6] can lead to textiles suitable for standard facemasks and surgical gowns. Further, nanofibrous webs incorporated in textiles through electrospinning have been found to produce PPEs with significant increase in protection and wear comfort . Additionally, techniques have been established where this technology can be scaled for bulk production.

data.projectName: Treatment Modalities and Strategies: Passive Immunization treatment for COVID19
data.projectDigest:
With the new Pandemic COVID19, Pakistan is in grip now a days, with death rate 1.35 till 31.3.2020. We know that there is no vaccine available till date but we want to use the older concept of using Passive Immunization which has been practiced since 1890. 
We want to develop passive immunotherapy against SARS-CoV-2 with the help of donated blood samples from recovered COVID-19 patients. And later on, from the horses after the success of few trials. 
We will use the plasma with antibodies against SARS-CoV-2, recovered for COVID-19 infection recently. With experimental and computational work, we are planning to optimize, produce and test human polyclonal and monoclonal antibodies for treatment of patients with COVID-19. The Plasma Treatment for Coronavirus has been started to get its First Trial Run in New York. “Passive immunization with antibodies has proven to be highly efficient for treatment and prevention of infectious human diseases for which vaccines are not available,” says Dr. Bruce Sachais, Chief Medical Officer of New York Blood Center Enterprises. 
“Therefore, we believe that antibodies represent a weapon of choice to treat the disease and prevent continued spread of the virus in Pakistan.”
“The objective is that if we passively infuse someone who is actively suffering from COVID-19, the antibodies may temporarily help the patient to fight against this infection more effectively, and get better a little bit quicker,”. This can control the mortality rate to some extent.

data.projectName: Development of a point-of-care lateral flow assay (LFA) for the rapid detection of SARS-CoV-2 specific immunoglobulins
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: The best way to control COVID-19 is to test, isolate and -if possible- treat. For testing – at the present – a SARS-CoV-2 specific real time RT-PCR is the gold standard test; however, this requires expensive equipment, expensive reagents and experienced personnel to carry out the procedure under BSL 3 lab conditions. The major objective of the proposed study is to design, assemble, optimize and validate a lateral flow device (LFD) for rapid screening of humans for the presence of antibodies to SARS-CoV-2. Development and assembly of LFD components will be carried out and multiplex format will be adopted. This project involves working with recombinant SARS-CoV-2 proteins (to be provided by foreign collaborators) and there is no involvement of live virus propagation or exposure to the virus at any stage of the project. Hence, the project can be carried out in BSL 2 laboratory of CVAS, in Jhang, under the OIE guidelines. After assembly, the LFD will be validated by using know positive and negative COVID-19 sera. Once the LFD is developed and its specificity and sensitivity is determined, a field sero-epidemiology study comprising 300 individuals will be carried out. Academic and research collaborators will play their specific role under proposed project.

data.projectName: Development of COVID-19 IgM/IgG antibody rapid test kit
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: COVID-19 is an infectious disease, caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), which has so far caused the death of  ~42,000 people out of ~870,000 cases of infection (as of March, 2020). At present, there is no treatment or vaccine available for COVID-19. Similar to other respiratory syndromes, the COVID-19 infection is manifested by symptoms such as cough, fever, and pneumonia, necessitating the availability of fast, portable detection tests which display high specificity. Currently, polymerase chain reaction (PCR) based tests are used for diagnosis of COVID-19, however these tests are expensive, time-consuming, require technical expertise, and are mostly not performed on-site. In the absence of preventive or therapeutic strategies, rapid on-site detection is urgently needed to contain the spread of SARS-CoV-2, even if such tests are applicable to late stages of the infection. In the proposed work, we aim to develop a local cost-effective strip based assay for rapid on-site detection of antibodies (namely COVID-19 IgM and IgG) in blood samples of infected individuals. Thus, the proposed assay could be employed for rapid on-site screening of suspected/infected individuals for diagnosis of COVID-19, and could be adapted for the development of other immunological assays for conducting large-scale epidemiological studies.

data.projectName: Establishment of Diagnostic facility for the detection of COVID-19
data.projectDigest:
COVID-19 is a new strain of coronavirus identified in humans. It is emerged in Wuhan, China, in December 2019, and has since been declared as an outbreak by World Health Organization (WHO). The disease fatality rate is more in children and old age people. The COVID-19 has affected the China, USA, IRAN and European countries while in Pakistan, about 2360 cases and 33 confirmed deaths are reported. Pakistan is underdeveloped country and has limited availability of diagnostics equipments and kits, so actual data of disease speared and cases are less authentic. Same is the case in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa where only 26 cases are reported positive due to only one diagnostic facility available. 
Real time PCR is authentic and approved techniques by WHO for COVID-19 detection. The technique is beneficial in both the early and late stage of the disease and superior to the IgM and IgG based detection. Urgent establishment of CORONA diagnostic facility is require to enhancing the testing capacity and point of care diagnostics.
In the proposed project, real time PCR diagnostics will be offered to Government and general public as well free of cost.
