data.projectName: EMPATHI-Emergency associated Mental health issues of PAkistani front line health workers and their management through Tele Health Intervention
data.projectDigest:
The Chinese experience of COVID-19 show that mental health disorders and burn-out are common among health-care staff working on the front lines of the outbreak response. These include doctors, nurses, para-medics, hospitals and lab support staff. Given the nature of outbreaks (sudden onset and rapid), the health authorities have little time to train these front-line workers on building resilience and coping strategies to deal with the situation that these workers find themselves in, resulting in a plethora of psychological problems. The situation is further compounded by a lack of formal mental health support for health-workers even in normal times (in Pakistan), making it very difficult for the front-line workers to find help, resulting in decreased efficiency. Building upon the experience of China, we propose online mental health support provision to Pakistani front-line workers in the COVID-19 outbreak in the country. We aim;
a.	To determine the burden of common mental health disorders among the front-line workers and their coping strategies and develop resilience/coping guidelines and a video training module for the front-line workers
b. 	To conduct process evaluation of training implementation and assessment of effectiveness of the training.
c.	To Establish a tele-counselling service portal and evaluate its effectiveness.

data.projectDigest:
Coronavirus COVID-19 has become pandemic and creating chaos all around the world. The spread of the coronavirus has been rapid and aggressive. COVID-19 can enters in respiratory tract of a person though breathing in environment having COVID-19. When COVID-19 enters in respiratory tract it first interact with cilia present on ciliated epithelium. Cilia are hair like structure and they are continuously rotating like motor to propel mucus. They have great ability to transport inhaled viruses or pollens that are deposited on the airway surface liquid (ASL) to the stomach. 
In this project we will study the mathematical modelling of ciliary flow in respiratory tract infected by COVID-19 because it has become a challenge for researchers to understand the relation between coronavirus (COVID-19) and ciliated epithelium to determine the mechanism of inhaling oxygen. In literature it is seen that viruses and bacteria when interact with the ciliated epithelium they decrease the ciliary activity by reducing cilia beat frequency. In this research we will analyze how the effect of temperature, humidity and drugs can increase the ciliary activity when respiratory tract is congested by viruses.

This project will help the society in following manners
1.	Mechanics of clean air (nonpolluted oxygen) travelling from upper respiratory tract to the lower respiratory tract (lungs).
2.	How the viruses like COVID-19 effect the ciliary flow.
3.	How temperature and humidity help to increase the efficiency of ciliary beat for cleaning the inhaled air in the presence of COVID-19.

data.projectName: Conjoint BCG vaccination and hydroxychloroquine as an intervention to COVID-19 in susceptible individuals
data.projectDigest: COVID-19 virus infection has spread to every inhabited continent of the world, infecting more than half a million people in merely a few weeks. There is an urgent need to find cure and stop its exponential growth, however lack of vaccine and efficacious drugs hinder such efforts. Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ), an anti-malaria agent and BCG anti-tuberculosis vaccine have recently emerged as promising candidates to prevent COVID-19 infection. However, both candidates need to be rigorously tested in clinical trials for their safety and efficacy against development of COVID-19 infection. Here, we propose to treat high risk population, which is in direct contact with COVID-19 positive patients, with HCQ and BCG in an attempt to prevent spread of COVID-19. The study population will be rigorously monitored for development of COVID-19 during the treatment period. We hypothesize that HCQ and BCG will reduce the incidence of COVID-19 in susceptible population. If our hypothesis is true, HCQ and BCG can be effective tools to stop spread of COVID-19 infection. Both HCQ and BCG are cost-effective, easily available and cab be produced at mass scale which make them ideal candidates in the war against COVID-19.

data.projectName: Experimental drug trial to treat moderate, severe and critically ill patients of COVID-19 and analysis of associated molecular markers
data.projectDigest: As yet, no definite cure is available for COVID-19 infection. Some drugs used in other diseases have been shown to possess potential efficacy in corona virus infections, such as COVID-19. While new drug and vaccine development is in progress, repurposing existing drugs and treatment methods may be applied to save precious lives in this pandemic. It appears prudent to treat all cases who are moderately, severely and critically ill patients of COVID-19 infection to improve the prognosis. Conflicting results are reported with preliminary research in this regard apparently due to the study design or presence of confounders. To address such issues and find a more robust scientific evidence, randomized trials are needed. Hence, this study is designed to conduct randomized, single-blinded clinical trials with selected antiviral drugs and/or immunization to treat moderate, severe and critical COVID-19 infection. This study would also assess pharmacogenetic and other molecular markers with treatment outcome(s).

data.projectName: Skin friendly antiviral herbal sanitizer for the prevention and treatment of coronavirus: A lead pilot study
data.theme: Development of disinfectants particularly using indigenous herbal ingredients
data.projectDigest:
Toward the end of December 2019, a novel coronavirus (2019-nCoV) with human-to-human transmission and severe human infection, originating in Wuhan, China, was identified. This virus has affected many persons in China and spread to over 200 countries in a very short time. By 2nd April 2020, 1016128 confirmed cases and 53069 deaths have been reported with this dangerous viral infection. World Health Organization declared that the outbreak of 2019-nCoV constitutes a public health emergency of international concern and issued temporary recommendations under the International Health Regulations. 
While specific vaccines and antiviral agents may be the most effective methods to prevent and treat viral infection, there are not yet effective treatments that target the 2019-nCoV. 
Plants used in traditional medicine present a potentially antiviral activity. The potentially antiviral plants would be selected for extraction depending on the accumulated compounds in plants parts. Each extract would be filtrated and stored in a refrigerator at 4 °C. Primary screening of these extracts would be conducted by Cytopathic Evaluation assay in triplicates on Vero cells infected with 2019-nCoV in 96?well microtiter plates. The extracts that exhibited activity in Cytopathic Evaluation would be analyzed at eight concentrations for antiviral assay. The assay plates contained virus and cell controls and the samples.
The workable objects would be:
•	Collection and identification of plants followed by extraction of medicinal component
•	Sanitizer formulation development and physicochemical characterization
•	Preliminary screening of antiviral activity with corona infected cell line
•	Report  submission and dissemination of outcomes

data.projectName: Bio Disinfectant for use against COVID 19: Formulation and Evaluation for general hygiene practices
data.theme: Development of disinfectants particularly using indigenous herbal ingredients
data.projectDigest: Popular disinfecting agents are toxic chemicals that are not compatible for all surface types. An alternate option to conventional disinfectant is plant based disinfectant. In order to combat the recent coronavirus pandemic a rapid cost-effective local formulation is required that can be used not only in house holds but also in hospital, quarantine facilities. Organic formulations are ecofriendly and are favorable to sick, hypersensitive people. The natural formulation is also promising towards children, pets and special needs patients. In developing the bio disinfectant, different variables must be considered to ensure consistent performance such as surface types, material of construction, concentration of disinfectant, contact time, effect of temperature, effect of pH, antimicrobial and cytotoxic activity. Rotation of active ingredients must also be explored for long term use. Scientists have successfully observed various natural ingredients as potential bio disinfectants such as Curcuma longa, Allium sativum, Terminalia chebula, Mentha Spicata, Citrus aurantifolia, Cinnamomum iners, Tea tree, Thyme & Oregano oil, Vinegar, lemon juice, baking soda. Mangrove extract also showed promising results against, fungi, bacteria and viruses.  The proposed research is for formulation and evaluation of cost effective bio disinfectant against COVID-19 that can be used for Personal protective equipment PPE.

data.projectName: Wearable and Implantable sensors and systems
data.theme: Indigenous manufacture of Low cost Intensive-care equipment
data.projectDigest:
The proposed topic of his research is “Wearable and Implantable
sensors and systems” will contribute significantly in the field of wearable electronics with
applications in healthcare. E.g,  Respiratory Monitoring System for COVID-19 Patient
How Wearable and Implantable Technology is Changing the Future of Health Care?
Wearable and implantable technologies sense parameters of various diseases and can either transfer data to a remote center, direct the patient to take a specific action, or automatically perform a function based on what the sensors are reading. For example, if blood glucose is running high, insulin could be automatically administered. Nowadays people talk about personalized medicine, but no one talks about personalized public health recommendations, but they should all be personalized, at least at the level of age and gender, and, with the help of wearable technology, truly personalized.
Why? Current trends in patient preferences need to be incorporated at an early stage into the design process of prospective clinical sensors. Electronics are also very interesting as implantable devices, combining electronic intelligence with extreme miniaturization. Electronic implants challenge scientists even more: the bio stability of the sensors should be guaranteed during the lifetime of the device, which is often difficult, since proteins or other components of the local body tissue tend to react with the surface of sensors, which might change their electronic readout.
My Own Assessment and engagement in Future: The comprehensive discussion of mobile biomedical sensor technology could be present in this proposal. It was found that sensor systems needed to be small, Low cost, discreet, unobtrusive and preferably incorporated into everyday objects and for human body.

data.projectName: Prediction of COVID-19 severity and host immune response through mutation data of Coronaviruses: Validation of results using experimental techniques
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Human coronaviruses have been infecting humans since mid-1960s.
The most recent human coronavirus strain SARS-CoV2 (or COVID-19) has emerged from Wuhan, China in mid-December 2019. This strain of virus belongs to genus Betacoronavirus. It has evolved from SARS-CoV that caused an epidemic in 2003. 
COVID-19 is an RNA virus and such type of viruses mutate after replication in host cells. 
A person may have one or more than one type of virus.
in china and US people with more than one type of corona-virus have been discovered.
Keeping above scenario in view, we can say that COVID-19 is rapidly evolving. Thus it will create difficulty in developing a vaccine because immune response to both types of virus might be different. Therefore, we are proposing here to build a model that can forecast pattern of randomly mutating regions and predict changing host immune response.  Outcome of this proposed model will be validated by sequencing genomes of isolates from Pakistani patients and determining their immune response.

data.projectName: COVID-19 Disease Outbreak Modelling, Early warning to strengthen preventive efforts through Artificial Intelligence
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
The proposal is aimed to design and implement an integrated digital solution (ahead then publication of research papers) for strategic planners and decision makers in real time with the help of data driven (real time) affective dashboards based on simulations and predictive models.  With the help of mobile/web applications data will be collected about the Convid_19 patient and suspected patients. The data will be employed in running the epidemic models including IR, SIR, Compartment and Social Network (Contagion) to understand the rate of spread that will be mapped on GeoMap over a dashboard. The data and the knowledge produced by the epidemic models will be cascaded towards the surveillance engine that will identify the community and places with higher threats. 

Identification of localities and communities (and then individuals) with high risks of infection will be helping the decision makers to lock down a locality or the entire city. Social networks will be developed from the movement trajectory of the patients (by tracking the mobile application) that will identify the community of suspects around him. Secondly models of local community structures/interactions will be developed and aligned with the spread models that will help us in understanding a closer estimate of spread, this will also develop an Lock Down or isolation plans for individuals/communities instead of an entire city.

data.projectName: Crisis Assistant (Pandemic Spread Prediction and Task Support System)
data.piUniversity: Balochistan University of Information Technology, Engineering and Management Sciences,Quetta
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest: In order to help level the playing field in the fight against COVID-19 pandemic, in this project, we will develop a unique and multipurpose Surveillance System (for both mobile and web) using big data analytics and artificial intelligence. This platform will allow for tasks that are normally monotonous, such as data collection and visualization, to be easily automatized. The project aims to use state-of-the-art big data analytics and machine learning algorithms for prediction and forecasting of the spread of the diseases and identifying vulnerable populations. The application envisages wide spread use by both citizens and governmental personnel providing both parties with what they need, such as a volunteer database allowing for efficient allocation of medically trained reserved personnel, or for citizens by connecting high-risk groups with those who are able to provide food or medicine deliveries. Additionally, the platform will gather data in a centralized way (via multiple channels, such as: official statistics, crowd sourced data, social media, or self-reported information) allowing for easy generation of statistical reports and data visualization, it is planned to make this data and analysis available via application programming interface (API) to ensure widespread use, interoperability, and transparency.

data.projectName: Assessment of COVID-19 Management at Public and Private Health Care Institutions: A Convergent Mixed Methods Approach
data.projectDigest: The medical management of COVID-19 is paramount for managing patient symptoms and minimizing the mortality rates. However, equally important is the overall clinical care within health care facilities for early recognition of infected patients, for initiating infection prevention and control measures, for improving patient prognosis, and for providing safe and supportive care for any arising complications (WHO, 2020b). A more holistic and comprehensive approach (from admission to discharge) to care for patients with COVID-19 would be beneficial for reducing the work burden of health care system, institutions, and front-line care providers and minimizing the chances of cross-infection. However, no studies have yet been focused on exploring the overall management of patients with COVID-19 patients in health care facilities. Given this, ths projects aims to assess the processes and strategies used to manage patients with COVID-19 in health care facilities in Pakistan. Gaining this knowledge, would be helpful to develop contextual and tailored guidelines from within the Pakistani context for effective management of patients. The development of contextual and tailored guidelines and their implementation, in turn, would reduce the COVID-19 burden from the heath care system and institutions.

data.projectName: Development of modeling tools for continuous rapid assessment of COVID-19 epidemic in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Two key challenges in responding to the novel coronavirus (COVID-19) are: 1) the level of under-reporting of cases and 2) the true infectiousness of the virus. Until the level of under-reporting is properly understood it is not possible to know the true case fatality rate of the virus, or to estimate the degree of social penetration it has achieved. Once this is known it is possible to better estimate the true infectiousness of the epidemic, and in particular to identify undetected mildly-symptomatic cases that might be maintaining the epidemic without coming to attention of public health authorities. Once these two properties of the virus are understood it is possible to develop effective strategies for virus eradication, to model their impact, and to determine the health system burden due to the disease. 

This project will use Bayesian statistical analysis and mathematical modeling tools to 1) identify the level of under-reporting of COVID-19, 2) estimate the true case burden in Pakistan, and 3) compare policy options for the most effective and cost-effective strategy to eliminate COVID-19. Bayesian statistical analysis will use the complete data on COVID-19 cases on the Diamond Princess cruise ship, which is available to researchers through their Japanese institutions, and the age- and sex-specific information from the comprehensive testing regime undertaken in South Korea, to estimate the true burden of COVID-19 disease in Pakistan through comparison of age-specific death rates. Mathematical modeling will then be applied to this true burden of disease to estimate the infectiousness of the disease, its epidemic path, and the possible impact of various intervention strategies.

This project will use Bayesian statistical analysis and mathematical modeling tools to 1) identify the level of under-reporting of COVID-19, 2) estimate the true case burden in Pakistan, and 3) compare policy options for the most effective and cost-effective strategy to eliminate COVID-19. Bayesian statistical analysis will use the complete data on COVID-19 cases on the Diamond Princess cruise ship, which is available to researchers through their Japanese institutions, and the age- and sex-specific information from the comprehensive testing regime undertaken in South Korea, to estimate the true burden of COVID-19 disease in Pakistan through comparison of age-specific death rates. Mathematical modeling will then be applied to this true burden of disease to estimate the infectiousness of the disease, its epidemic path, and the possible impact of various intervention strategies.

data.projectName: ISOLATION, PURIFICATION AND ENRICHMENT OF IMMUNOGLOBULIN G AND IMMUNOGLOBULIN M FROM HUMAN PLASMA OF RECOVERED INDIVIDUALS FROM COVID-19 DESTINED FOR PASSIVE IMMUNIZATION
data.projectDigest:
The current project is based on the immunological studies covering the potential of disease induced immunoglobulins as treatment regime. 

We would be able to generate the concentrated antibodies specific against coronavirus (Covid-19). These antibodies can be used as serum therapy. This project can be further extended to develop rapid diagnostic kits for detection of Covid-19 within 15-20 minutes, which require additional funding. 

Aside from a Covid-19 vaccine, antibodies from recovered patients could provide a short-term “passive immunization” to the disease. Those antibodies can be extracted from the blood serum of surviving patients and then injected into infected people. Passive immunization usually lasts for a few weeks or months, after which those borrowed or donated antibodies, get broken down by the host body within about 30 days. While drugs to treat patients with covid-19, and vaccines to prevent infection are being developed, a fast acting, stopgap serum therapy could be useful as a first aid for high-risk patients. 

Apart from convalescent plasma, small scale concentrates of immunoglobulins prepared from convalescent plasma collections provide higher potency and greater consistency than individual units. The feasibility of production of large scale of diseases specific immunoglobulins concentrates can considered for longer term, based on the course of epidemic, access to large numbers of suitable plasma collections, and the available infrastructure for manufacturing such products under GMP.

The pilot project in short term will take 2-3 months but after successful clinical trials the project can be extended for longer run that will lead to its manufacturing and commercialization that require additional 6-8 months

data.projectName: Development of Point-of-Care System for Pre-Diagnosis of COVID-19 Disease
data.piUniversity: Karachi Institute of Economics & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The outbreaks of infectious diseases cause not only huge human losses but also bring massive economic losses in the past. Recently, emergence of novel coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic has also raise serious health concerns, among all the nations globally. On March 25, 2020, WHO announced that there are more than 509,164 confirmed cases worldwide with the overall death toll increased to 23,335 globally, while in Pakistan there are 1,057 cases are reported throughout the country [1]. After China, the worst situation has been observed in Italy, Spain, United States and Iran where thousands of people identified with the virus and reportedly the existing healthcare infrastructure is unable to accommodate the new patients effectively [2]. In case of such outbreaks the abundant number of suspect patients rushed to the clinical laboratories and hospitals, resulting into the collapse of entire healthcare system. This is the most vulnerable part of any healthcare system during pandemic disease. To prevent this, a point-of-care (POC) system has been proposed in this work, which will facilitate the existing healthcare infrastructure. The POC system will reduce the burden of our clinical laboratories and hospitals, by evaluating the early diagnosis of lungs damage with modern sensing and data analytics techniques.  In this proposed work there are five different sources of data will be taken into consideration. This includes historical data, crowdsource data, visual data, acoustic data and electronic sensor data. These all sensor data has been fused and, with multi-sensor fusion technique a cloud-based system is proposed that will enable to predict the disease. The cloud system can also supports the digital diseases surveillance system by using AI, IoT and big-data analytics.

data.projectName: Understanding, Awareness and Epidemiological Modeling for COVID-19
data.projectDigest:
Today, the whole world facing a big challenge posed by the novel Coronavirus disease (COVID-19) recognized in December 2019. The COVID-19 disease although started from China, it has been spread throughout the world with an exponential growth affecting more than seven hundred thousand people, and more than thirty-three thousand people lost their lives due to this infectious disease until today. At the first stage patients show symptoms like fever with mild respiratory problems e.g., cough, while the patients reported severe breathing problems (dyspnoea) at later stages of the disease. Although the COVID-19 outbreak is recent, numerous studies have been made to understand different aspects of this disease [1,3]. 

In the context of Pakistan, except few summary statistics including the number of confirmed cases, death and recovered cases, unfortunately we do not have access to a detailed data collected on a number of COVID-19 patients. The unavailability of the primary data is a serious concern for all the stakeholders who are involved in studying the different aspects of this disease.
The objective of this research is to collect, analyze and model the data for the COVID-19 confirmed patients in Pakistan. The main objectives of the study are following:

•	A thorough literature review of the studies available on COVID-19.
•	•	Epidemiological modeling, like compartment models, of the data focusing on the statistical tools available for the said task.
•	The development of a website and/or a mobile application that can give different information about COVID-19. In addition, the website and/or a mobile application will be equipped with an epidemiological modeling procedure, build within the project, to determine if a person is a susceptible for the COVID-19.
•	Prepare guideline

data.projectName: COVID-19 Clinical Diagnostics and Recommender System
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest:
There exists a dire need to develop effective solutions for COVID-19 diagnosis and to improve the patient care through optimal utilization of resources. The proposed research project aims to develop a COVID-19 diagnostics recommender system with focus on COVID-19 detection and severity index prediction to facilitate the doctors and paramedics staff to make informed decisions about patients’ treatment considering the extremely scarce resources e.g. ventilators and relevant equipment’s. Additionally, the recommended practices and treatment should be transformed into knowledge that could be shared with other local and foreign hospitals. This will ensure efficient utilization of these crucial and limited resources to the most deserving patients based on their medical conditions. 
The proposed research project is timely as the COVID-19 becomes pandemic across the globe and still the scientists are unable to find the cure. At this moment, if we can determine at the very early stage of examination that the suspected patient is COVID-19 positive with severe condition then the doctors and paramedic staff can concentrate more on those critical patients.

data.projectName: Artificial Intelligence (AI) based Nano-Biochip Detector for COVID-19
data.piUniversity: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, China
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest: A novel corona virus (2019-nCoV) is a new corona virus that has not been previously identified.  In early assessment it is reported that COVID-19 is not living organism basically  it’s special type of protein molecule having external lipid on its outer layer/surface  can infect/damage the lungs severely, if not recognize at their early stage. Which causes much causalities over the globe? Since January 2020, about 30420 human casualties are being reported (till now) due to attack of COVID-19 and more than 660000 people are affected from this pandemic disease. Still the causalities are ongoing and this acute disease has caused much panic in all over the world. Early detection of Covid-19 is a big challenge and it will be contribution tremendously to the humanity as well as research and development. In current project, polymer coated with suitable biocompatible novel material constructed biochip will be developed successfully and characterized by using various/manifold required characterization techniques. Synthesis of desired morphology biochip made by novel nanomaterials will be fabricated with collaboration of Dalian Institute of Science and Technology, China and PIEAS, Islamabad, Pakistan. Some relevant characterization will be performed at GC University Faisalabad. The biocompatible/bio-safe characteristics of biochip will be tested at Virology Department NIH, Park road Islamabad. Artificial Intelligence software for specific COVID-19 pandemic protein detection will be installed with the collaboration of Spark Auckland, New Zealand via computer work station. The basic idea is when biosample of COVID-19 relevant protein will interact with the developed nano-biochip, through artificial intelligence it will recognize general COVID-Virus family in first step of detection.

data.projectName: Rapid diagnosis, molecular epidemiological modelling and treatment options for Covid-19
data.projectDigest:
The  Pandemic Covid-19 has  caused  severe damage in  health, economy and  social sectors. In order to cope this challenge  and similar challenges in future, every country has to adopt strategies in local perspectives.  At the moment the major challenge in Pakistan to cope this issue is the lack of capacity to estimate accurate disease burden and appropriate treatment.The estimate of accurate disease burden is required to handle  outbreak effectively.  
This is a multi disciplinary  study designed by group of experts belonging to diverse range of speciality  to  tackle outbreaks in local perspectives. The project team comprises of leading  Medical doctor, Medical lab Scientist, Pharmacologist, Cell Biologist, Virologist and Molecular Microbiologist. 
  This study proposes development of several kinds of rapid, economical and reliable methods to diagnose Covid-19 infected patients. Another big problem in Covid-19 associated research is the requirement of very expensive and difficult to maintain  (BSL-3) Laboratory. Therefore, it is difficult to test efficacy of local herbs to cure  disease in the laboratory. For that, we propose to establish in vitro cell culture method to find compounds that  prevent the  attachment of virus surface protein to human cells.
In short our  findings will directly contribute in improving  Covid-19 associated health and economical issues of the country.

data.projectDigest: The novel coronavirus (COVID-19) first case was detected in the city of Wuhan China which is the capital of Hubei province on December 31, 2019. After developing the pneumonia without a clear cause and for which the available vaccine or treatments were found not effective. data.projectDigest: The estimated deadline for the control of ongoing Corona viral pandemic (COVID-19) seems unpredictable so far. Despite, a lower mortality rate (~2%) compared to other recent viral outbreaks (SARS 10% and MERS 35%) of the same viral family, COVID-19 is considered more dreadful due to its highly contagious nature. Starting from China in December 2019, the pandemic has spread exponentially worldwide with over a million reported cases and 40,000 deaths so far, world leaders along with scientists and healthcare specialists are trying to establish counter measures to stem devastating effects of this pandemic. We are going to purpose an RNA based vaccine therapy which can boost the immune response against the nCov-2. RNA/DNA vaccines are proving to be a promising candidate for vaccination. RNA based vaccines can be designed rapidly, does not possess any toxic/safety issues, are reproducible and can generate both innate and adaptive immune response with a large immunological memory pool, therefore a protection lasting for longer period of time. As the nCoV-2 contains positive sense single stranded RNA as genetic material and uses its surface glycoprotein “S” for purpose of interaction with ACE-2 receptors on lungs, therefore S coding RNA sequence can be used as a potent vaccine target.

data.projectName: AI – Assisted Remote Sensing based Efficient Resources Distribution and Basic Health Monitoring Facility
data.theme: Information Collection and Dissemination IT platforms)
data.projectDigest:
For a poor country like Pakistan, a Pandemic such as CoronaVirus is devastating for its economy and development. Without any doubt most issues in the country are due to mismanagement of resources, whether in health or food distribution. If in such times the authorities do not manage the distribution of these resources in masses efficiently, god forbid things will go out of hand. The need for a system to ensure stability in this time of crisis is utmost necessary to avoid mayhem.
In this proposal we propose a system in which we address the challenge associated with Food and health-care resource distribution in the prevailing situation of COVID-19 outbreak in the national context. Morespecifically, instead of gathering all the needy individuals at a certain place for collection of food or health-care resources, anyone in need of health care resources or food supplies can post their request via online application. Each individual with a unique CNIC number and Mobile number will be able to post their request for Food or Health-care supplies once. Our AI- Assisted Remote Sensing based efficient resource distribution model will utilize regional request and health information, along with remotely sensed regional settlement and population information to allocate resources efficiently to deserving applicants.

data.projectName: A Single and Two-Stage, Closed-Tube, Molecular Test for the 2019 Novel Coronavirus (COVID-19) in Pakistani Population
data.projectDigest:
The 2019 novel coronavirus (COVID-19) is a newly emerged strain that has never been found in humans before. At present, the laboratory-based reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) is the main method to confirm COVID-19 infection. The intensification of the COVID-19 epidemic overwhelms limited clinical resources in particular, but not only, in developing countries, resulting in many patients not being tested for the infection and in large queues of potentially infected individuals waiting to be tested while providing a breeding ground for the disease. I will describe here a rapid, highly sensitive, point-of-care, molecular test amenable for use at home, in the clinic, and at points of entry by minimally trained individuals and with minimal instrumentation. Our test is based on loop mediated isothermal amplification (COVID-19 LAMP) and for higher sensitivity on nested nucleic acid, two stage isothermal amplification. Both tests can be carried out in closed tubes with either fluorescence or colorimetric (e.g., leuco crystal violet LCV) detection. COVID-19 LAMP performs on par with COVID-19 RT-PCR. COVID-19 RAMP has 10 fold better sensitivity than COVID-19 LAMP and COVID-19 RT-PCR when testing purified targets and 100 times better sensitivity than COVID-19 LAMP and COVID-19 RT-PCR when testing rapidly prepared sample mimics.
the objective of the research is to  design
1.	Rapid, accurate, inexpensive and highly sensitive, point-of-care, molecular test amenable for use at home, in the clinic, and at points of entry by minimally trained individuals and with minimal instrumentation.
2.	Tests can be carried out in closed tubes with either fluorescence or colorimetric (e.g., leuco crystal violet LCV) for accurate detection of COVID-19.

data.projectName: Artificial Intelligence based decision support system for COVID-19 Questionaire.
data.projectDigest: Due to the shortage and high cost of COVID-19 test kits widespread testing of suspected patients is so far not practical, and given the size of the population testing opportunities for public are expected to remain limited. Pakistani hospitals have been using certain unvalidated proforma to screen suspected patients who should be subject to testing or isolated. Pakistan has performed roughly 15000 tests till now based on different scoring systems used in the different parts of country(6). Only (roughly) 15% of these have turned out to be positive showing very low sensitivity of these proforma. Most of the variables used in these scoring systems are very vague. Some of these variables are present in any other illness like common flu (cough and runny nose). Some are always present whether a patient has the illness or not (Age >60 and previous illness with medications) and few of these may not have been known to the exposed ones (exposure to covid-19 patient).  While the efficacy these proforma is expected to remain  limited, their performance can be improved. First, number of features/variables in the existing proforma need to be made rich with input from experts in the disease and experiential evidence of COVID-19 symptoms in patients of other countries. Second, instead of using subjective scoring schemes the data can be fed to a computer to train an Artificial Intelligence based software/machine that may provide decision support to the health care worker whether to send the suspected patient for test, or to isolate them (in hospital or home), or to be sent back home without isolation. Consequently, an online/mobile application will be developed which can be used by ordinary citizens as well as primary health care units to assess the risk of individuals having COVID-19.

data.projectName: RCBT
data.projectDigest:
The coronavirus disease recently emerged and declared as pandemic by WHO has created threat for lives of millions of people in the world. It has caused widespread concerns for government. Because of its pandemic status, the outbreak of COVID-19 has been very stressful for millions of people and affecting their mental health. Fear and stigma due to COVID-19 have gripped the world rapidly and have not stopped people from distressing. WHO has been found involved in providing guidelines for managing COVID-19. Hence medical and preventive strategies are the most crucial at this stage, but immediate psychological guidelines for people are also important because of social stigma that is leading people to hide symptoms of coronavirus to avoid discrimination. They may not seek health care when they need it during health risks.  

Therefore the present research is planned to provide psychological support to the people experiencing stress due to COVID-19. The goal of this research is to manage the social stigma, panic, and preventive behavior among people staying at home, diagnosed patients, and frontline doctors and nurses. As the people are being social distancing, an internet based psychological treatment will be more effective that will be employed through skype and watsapp in weekly sessions of maximum 20 minutes. Therapy will be given through emails, text messages, and/or individual face-to-face online support.

data.projectName: Using Mobile Technology to Track Human Mobility Patterns and Investigate the Geospatial Spread of COVID-19 in Sindh
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.theme: Information Collection and Dissemination IT platforms)
data.projectDigest: With the ongoing spread of COVID – 19, it is imperative that not only the virus but also the people being affected by it are tracked over time. Global solutions to counter the pandemic are being explored and implemented around the globe. At present, fully implemented dashboards are in effect and have no doubt used accurate methods to track, monitor and inform the number of newly reported cases and deaths as well as the progress of the virus. However, due to gaps in official reports and clustering of data, a complete picture is not always painted from a spatial point-of-view. In this project, the first and foremost objective is to curb the spread of the COVID-19; to do this, we wish to use innovative tracking methods of human movement across areas and combine with geo-spatial mapping techniques so that we may provide better insights on case identification, outbreak risk and high-priority areas.

data.projectName: Rapid development of cell culture based vaccine against COVID-19 local isolate of SARS-CoV-2
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
COVID-19 emerged in China in December 2019 causing significant acute respiratory disease, spread to 200 countries and World health organization declared it as pandemic due to threatening millions of lives if not controlled urgently. Currently COVID-19 cases worldwide were at >1M and 55,526 deaths. Whereas therapeutic treatment plans are being explored, an urgent need for a vaccine to against the local COVID-19 isolate is needed as currently more than 8 different stains are circulating in this pandemic. There are global efforts to produce COVID-19 vaccine but we in Pakistan need to urgently start working on our indigenous COVID-19 vaccine that will be specific to local viral strain. In this project we aim to achieve the following:
1-	Characterize local COVID-19 strain 
2-	Growth of COVID-19 in BSL-3 cell culture system 
3-	Develop cell culture based COVID-19 vaccine
4-	Preclinical trails of COVID-19 vaccine in transgenic animal model
5-	Disseminate vaccine efficacy results with stakeholders 

A unique strength of this project is our multidisciplinary team which includes local and world class virologists, vaccinologists, medical doctors, veterinarians, immunologists from University of Health Sciences (UHS), Institute of Public health (IPH -BSL3), University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences (UVAS -BSL3), Qatar University (QU) and Canadian scientists from world class vaccine and infectious disease center (VIDO-InterVac).

data.projectName: Development and preclinical trials of novel multi-epitope vaccine candidates against SARS-CoV-2 causing COVID-19.
data.projectDigest:
The novel coronavirus, SARS-CoV-2,  causes a severe respiratory infection named COVID-19 which has been found lethal. The World Health Organization declared COVID-19 as a pandemic. Scientists across the world are still looking for drugs that can inhibit viral infection and long-term prevention through vaccination. Therefore, development of an effective SARS-CoV-2 vaccine is an immediate requirement. Currently, many infections are controlled by multi-epitope vaccines, and in the proposed project, different immunoinformatics tools and software will be used to design multi-epitope vaccines using protein subunits of SARS-CoV-2 that can activate both, B- and T-cells. The proposed candidate vaccine models will be further evaluated and validated by using molecular dynamics simulations and in-silico tools. 
The gene coding for stable MVCs will be synthesized after codon optimization and initial sequence analysis. The gene will then be cloned in T7 promoter based recombinant protein expression system using Escherichia coli BL21. Conditions for the maximal expression and production of recombinant protein will be optimized. The recombinant MVCs will be purified and validated through Circular Dichroism and  MALDI-TOF. The purified recombinant MVCs will be tested in Vero cell lines for efficacy and dosage studies. The optimized conditions will further be used for preclinical studies in mice models. The biological safety and toxicity studies will also be performed for further validation.

data.projectName: Development of commercial grade biobased antibacterial/anti-viral hand hygiene delivery systems; Disinfectants, Hand Sanitizers and Wipes
data.theme: Development of disinfectants particularly using indigenous herbal ingredients
data.projectDigest:
Antiviral based hand hygiene delivery systems i.e. disinfectants, hand sanitizers, and wipes have not enough track records of published data. Due to the majority of the Islamic population, not accepting to use alcohol impregnated materials and compositions; alcohol-free formulations are needed to develop.  
Transmission of enveloped viruses particularly Corona Viruses (CoVs) can be halted using alcohol-based or alcohol plus acid-based disinfectants applied on low-risk surfaces and food contact surfaces. Alcohols (ethyl alcohol and isopropyl alcohol) are bactericidal and virucidal. Ethyl alcohol destroys the lipophilic viruses (influenza, vaccine, and herpes) and hydrophilic viruses (rotaviruses, rhinoviruses, enteroviruses, and adenoviruses) except polio and hepatitis A virus.  Similarly, isopropanol is fully active against lipid bilayer viruses but not active against non-lipid viruses. Ethyl alcohol preferred over isopropanol because of its increased virucidal activity against enveloped viruses. Beginning at a concentration of 42.6% (w/w) and ranging up to 70%, the ethanol is effective within against SARS coronavirus, MERS coronavirus, ebolavirus, influenza A virus including the human type H3N2, avian type H3N8 human type H1N1. Several other non-alcoholic virucidal formulations have also been proposed.

data.theme: Information Collection and Dissemination IT platforms)
data.projectDigest:
This project has three main facets. None of the currently available Apps controls the duplication of assistance from all sources. The proposed App will fill this gap by offering the facility to check how much aid a person has received from all channels. 
The second facet is aimed at developing a Volunteer-database App for database, Biosafety training, and certification of volunteers to complement with Corona Tiger Welfare Force (CRTF) initiative of GOP. The third facet is aimed at developing the Biosafety training manual and training to 1000 volunteers to address the training needs of CRTF volunteers. There is a lack of such training manual tailored for the specific environment of developing countries like Pakistan. Initially, the project will offer Biosafety training to 1000 volunteers of CRTF. Meanwhile, the project team will request HEC to instruct at least ten public sector universities to launch Biosafety training to the volunteers of CRTF.

data.projectName: The Transmission Dynamic Model and Risk Prediction of Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) in China and Pakistan
data.projectDigest: This interdisciplinary project integrates related technologies, such as epidemiology, theoretical epidemiology, applied mathematics, and closely focuses on the theme of the prevention and control of Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19). The purpose of this project is to present the spatial-temporal epidemiological model and investigate the risk prediction of COVID-19. By quantitatively studying the factors that contribute to the transmission, the rate of transmission, and the dynamic process of COVID-19, we intend to reveal the characteristics of the epidemic transmission and to understand the key factors of COVID-19 transmission, which could determine the effective strategies to control or prevent the transmission of COVID-19 virus. The research directly respond to the significant problems that need to be urgently addressed, such as how to prevent and control the impact of population movements on the epidemic of COVID-19, and how different is the spread of COVID-19 to different age groups. Moreover, with the advantages multidisciplinary technologies in modeling, we could evaluate the effectiveness of prevention and control measures more precisely. Therefore, this project is expected to provide theoretical and technical support for the scientific prevention and control of the outbreaks of infectious diseases based on the perspective of big data in healthcare.

data.projectName: Probiotic Metabolic Products  against Transmissible Coronavirus (COVID-19)
data.projectDigest:
Probiotics Improves immune biomarkers, indicators of good immune function associated with protection from pathogens which  improve gut barrier function – gut barrier integrity is important as a first-line immune defence and can be affected by several threats including infection. The present project may help to understand the mechanisms of action of probiotics during viral infections of the respiratory tract; It is possible that probiotic bacteria could bind to an invading virus, thus inhibiting virus attachment to the host-cell receptor, by direct interaction as an adsorptive or trapping mechanism; stimulation of the immune system by interleukin, natural killer cells, Th1 immune response activity, and IgA production; production of antiviral agents (e.g., hydrogen peroxide, lactic acid, and bacteriocins.
We strongly support the reinforcement of our immune system by any scientifically valid strategy, Combining a healthy and balanced diet together with prebiotics, probiotics, vitamin supplementation, among others, could help us to reinforce our immune system during the COVID-19 outbreak.

data.projectName: Optimal Policy Learning for COVID-19 Prevention Using Reinforcement Learning
data.piUniversity: Kohat University of Science and Technology, Kohat
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest: Machine Learning algorithms have made tremendous progress in different domains  particularly in health care  in last decades. However, these algorithms are focusing on the diagnosis of diseases or forecasting future results, but not on the treatment of diseases. Diagnosis of disease is a very important step and is the first step of treatment and machine learning algorithms can help in treatment to some extent, but finding the best policy to treatment of a particular patient has been a challenging problem for health care industry. Reinforcement Learning (RL) has recently gained more popularity in video games, where agents can learn the environment by interacting with the environment and getting feedback and during this process learns good and bad actions. In this project we will use reinforcement algorithm to find an optimal policy for three solutions i.e. lock down, sanitization and quarantine. We will simulate human population and will develop a simulated environment based on the existing knowledge of the spread of COVID-19, where simulated human will interact with the environment and learn optimal policy for lock down, sanitization and quarantine.

data.projectName: Development of Toehold Switch Based Diagnostic Device for Rapid Detection of SARS-CoV-2 with high specificity in a Low cost setting
data.projectDigest: Corona Virus disease (COVID-19) caused by the novel SARS-CoV-2 has spread across the globe and has been declared as a global pandemic affecting about one million people worldwide as of 02 April, 2020. Currently, there is no vaccine or treatment available for treatment of SARS-CoV-2 virus and the diagnostic methodologies rely on utilization of reverse transcriptase PCR which are laborious and time consuming methods. In the current scenario, mass-scale testing in the minimum possible time is one of the key factors required in order to confine the pandemic of COVID-19 which has killed around 50 thousand people within 3-4 months of its eruption. However, due to higher cost of equipments and chemicals and limited availability of diagnostic centers for SARS-CoV-2 testing across Pakistan, finding alternative approaches for rapid, accurate, and cost-effective diagnosis of SARS-CoV-2 virus are necessary. The current project will focus on development of a portable, low cost but highly specific diagnostic kit for the rapid detection of SARS-CoV-2. The project involves a protein that allows synthesis of color producing protein after specifically binding to mRNA of coronavirus. In the absence of the coronavirus RNA, color producing protein (chromoprotein) will not be produced resulting in no change in the color of the solution. Current study focuses on development of a low cost diagnostic kit (biosensor) with high specificity for the rapid detection of SARS-CoV-2. Besides, no expensive equipments will be required for the detection of novel coronavirus. Moreover, the synthesized diagnostic kit is portable producing results within two hours.

data.projectName: Development of a rapid, low-cost, point-of-care diagnostic Kit for COVID-19  using one Health Approach

Keeping in concern, the current situation of Pakistan, the emergency lock down and availability of limited man power and diagnostic facilities are the challenging issues which are keeping the work flow and stamina of health care workers underway. The medical doctors and nursing staff are suffering from extreme crisis with overburdened patient ratio, limited experience in conducting diagnostic tests and on spot solution to the suspected patients. The epidemiological assessment of the diagnostic kit is also important issue which would enable us to classify and rate the efficiency of the kit under development.  Sample collection of case defined patients, their brief demographic information and optimum results would be the key indicators which would also quantify the successful measurements of the proposed projects. The proposed project is entirely based on the prior research themes as China, USA, South Korea and France have also cope the challenge of patient work load by developing rapid diagnostic kits as per directions of WHO.

The proposed solution is also in line with recent FDA approval for use of remote patient monitoring devices .

data.projectName: Ethnobotanical studies of Selected Medicinal Plants, Phytochemical Profiling and bioavailability testing using Advanced techniques (for COVID-19 therapeutic Potential)
data.projectDigest:
In spite of the remarkable achievements in the healthcare sector over recent decades, inequities in accessibility and affordability of these facilities coexist throughout Pakistan. Nature provides another, more reliable source of antiviral agents; viz. plants phytochemicals; almost 40% of currently available drugs are direct or indirect derivatives of plants. Pakistan’s KP province has been blessed with the diversity of medicinal plants. Thus, we aim to explore and document the indigenous knowledge of medicinal plants and herbs and test their therapeutic potencies for the treatment of Corona virus as an alternate treatment option. 
 A number of studies aiming to identify potential therapeutic plants for more effective control of health issues demonstrate the importance of plant species in health care system. Plants are rich source of phytochemicals which have been proved to be responsible for their antimicrobial, antioxidant, hepatoprotective, and other therapeutic activities. Thus this study is aimed to explore the therapeutic potential of medicinal plants for the treatment of COVID-19. This will be done by collecting indigenous knowledge on selected medicinal plants, extraction and testing for their phytochemical profiling and enhancing their bioavailability by preparing nano-Suspensions of the selected medicinal .Based on the results the most effective treatments can be recommended for COVID-19 using local medicinal plants.

data.projectName: Disease Epidemiological Modeling COVID-19
HOST GENETIC DIFFERENCES IN DETERMINING THE RISK FOR COVID-19 IN PAKISTANI POPULATION
data.projectDigest: The current COVID-19 pandemic has presented researchers and clinicians with confounding contradictions: while the disease poses a well-documented risk to elderly individuals and those with some preexisting health conditions, it has also been linked to severe disease or death in some younger adults. Genetic studies and association analysis have revealed the relationship between genetic differences and susceptibility to infection with viruses such as HIV, HBV, HCV, dengue virus, tuberculosis-causing bacteria, leprosy, meningitis cerebrospinal and malaria-causing parasites. How sick, the novel coronavirus, will make population of Pakistan? The answer may be in genes of our population. COVID-19 host susceptibility studies are ramped up internationally, to search for potential host genetic markers for COVID-19 progression.  Proposed study is an attempt to identify those genetic markers in Pakistani population. The findings will determine those at risk of serious illness and those who might be protected, and they might also guide the search for new treatments.

data.projectName: Isolation, Characterization and Viral Selection (SARS-CoV2) using Cell Culture for the development of Vaccine
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest:
Coronaviruses are a large family of viruses that can cause illness ranging from the common cold to more severe diseases like Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS) and Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS). A novel coronavirus was subsequently identified as the causative pathogen, provisionally named 2019 novel coronavirus (2019-nCoV). The current outbreak of coronaviruses (COVID-19) across the globe creates an immense threat to human health. It is of paramount importance to develop a rapid, reliable procedure for the detection of circulating coronaviruses in Pakistan. Phylogenetic analysis of these 2019-nCoV genomes and those of other coronaviruses will be used to determine the evolutionary history of the virus and help infer its likely origin. Homology modelling will be performed to explore the likely receptor-binding properties of the virus.
The aim of the current proposed study is to develop and deploy robust diagnostic methodology for use in public health laboratory settings in AJK, Pakistan.

•	To identify the different circulating newly emergent COVID-19 by using different PCR methods.
•	To improve the primer design for rapid detection of circulating coronaviruses by using different PCR approaches. 
•	To uncover the sequences of most variable regions of viral genome of the detected corona viruses in a community of AJK, Pakistan.  
•	To understand the distribution of corona viruses based on sequence homology and variations in their gene’s segments by using phylogenetic analysis along with known strains from the same & other geographical regions.

data.projectName: Assessment of seroconversion of SAR-Cov-2 among Pakistani Population for development of  vaccination and management policy
data.projectDigest: COVID-19 is an infectious disease, which has flu like symptoms but can proceed in some case to fatal pneumonia. Although disease originated from Wuhan, Chine but rapidly became global health emergency and pandemic. At present, most part of the globe is experiencing this infection. Due to aerosol transmission, it is quickly  spreading in the communities. As higher proportion of people are infected, only way to properly diagnosis is by WHO recommended  method (RT-PCR). Most of the individuals get SARS-CoV-2 virus but do not develop COVID-19, hence are asymptomatic carriers, which are source of infection.  Such asymptomatic  carrier. however, develop immune response and are termed seroconverted.  The main issue is that these asymptomatic people  are not included in the total  counts of cases from any country, hence true infection rate is missing.  This project aims to  determine the seroconversion in Pakistani population  as way to predict the approximate estimates of infected population using serological method which can detect infection  without requiring special laboratory in shorter time.  These estimates and associated variable modelling will  provide baseline of data for developing  policy  for plasma therapy, vaccination and surveillance  of COVID-10 .

Such asymptomatic  carrier. however, develop immune response and are termed seroconverted.  The main issue is that these asymptomatic people  are not included in the total  counts of cases from any country, hence true infection rate is missing.  This project aims to  determine the seroconversion in Pakistani population  as way to predict the approximate estimates of infected population using serological method which can detect infection  without requiring special laboratory in shorter time.  These estimates and associated variable modelling will  provide baseline of data for developing  policy  for plasma therapy, vaccination and surveillance  of COVID-10 .

data.projectName: Development of rapid multiplex qRT-PCR based COVID-19 Nucleic Acid detection kit
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Medical University, Islamabad
data.projectDigest: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is an infectious disease caused by the virus strain "severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2" (SARS-CoV-2). WHO has called on all countries to ramp up their testing programs to slow the advancement of coronavirus pandemic. With skilled manpower and availability of adequate funding, in-house development of testing facility is possible in PIMS hospital. It is projected that the current proposal would establish a cost-effective and efficient fluorescent multiplex RT-PCR (F-MRP) based system for detection of COVID-19 using nucleic acid amplification technology. The rapid multiplex F-MRP kit will be a molecular testing panel designed to aid in the diagnosis of patients with respiratory syndromes, in about two hours, by differentiating the novel coronavirus from 11 other viral respiratory pathogens. The proposed multiplex profiling panel will detect 12 respiratory viruses (SARS-CoV-2, SARS CoV, bocavirus, influenza A and B viruses, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), adenovirus, human metapneumovirus, enterovirus and parainfluenza type 1, 2, and 3 viruses) from a single nasopharyngeal swab specimen. It will provide rapid solution to clinicians for differentiating SARS-CoV-2 patients from other respiratory pathogens. Moreover, it will capture the evolving in-vitro diagnostic landscape to assist in prompt infection control and environmental decontamination.

data.projectName: Corona Infodemic: Identifying outbreak hotspots and countering digital media misinformation
data.theme: Information Collection and Dissemination IT platforms)
data.projectDigest:
Coronavirus also known as COVID19 outbreak has posed several challenges to the daily life of people living in various parts of the world. Currently,  people rely on social media platforms like 
Twitter and Facebook for the latest information due to limited mobility and lockdowns. The accurate and reliable information related to a pandemic is needed to be disseminated in society to counter public fear by handling misinformation. In literature, the misinformation is detected by extracting lexical, topic-based, user behavioural, user profile, and Natural Language Processing (NLP) features. The literature survey reveals automatic misinformation detection for Pakistani Twitter users is ignored research area due to  NLP limitations to handle Urdu text.  In this project, we aim to develop the system to understand and mitigate the effects of misinformation on social media about COVID-19. For this purpose, we will develop algorithms to detect misinformation from Pakistani Twitter in English and Urdu text. Next, we will identify users and misinformation hubs responsible for propagating misinformation to aid in minimizing the negative impacts. Also,  we will study the impact to trace how misinformation affects public attitudes, fears, and beliefs. This project will help the nation to minimize panic or stigmatization in society.

data.projectName: Community Perceptions and Concerns of COVID-19 in Pakistan: A Twitter-based semantic analysis
data.theme: Information Collection and Dissemination IT platforms)
data.projectDigest:
The thematic area of this project is Information Collection and Dissemination IT platforms. Based on this theme, our project aims to conduct research work on exploration and information dissemination by Twitter blog on COVID-19 outbreak through the tweets and related hashtags. The goal is to evaluate the effectiveness of Twitter as a source of epidemiological data on COVID-19. All the information will be gathered and reviewed from the users of Twitter with the help of an online questionnaire which will comprise the information of months, cities, gender, occupation, the number of infected individuals, and the number of fatal cases of Corona Virus in Pakistan.
Besides, the study will utilize Natural Language processing and statistic based on users' tweets through amazon service.  Lastly, the project will approach a novel research methodology by developing algorithms on the collection of data using amazon based monitoring tool. The study will help in understanding the benefits of technology usage in countering epidemic problem and will facilitate in predicting the unexpected situations and possible mishaps.
This project study will increase understanding of the influence of the Corona outbreak on the perceptions of community and society, which will be beneficial to the community and our Country. Furthermore, the project will help policymakers for devising policy for countering COVID-19 related problems effectively through social media. Our results will prove to be beneficial for society in general and policymakers in particular.

data.projectName: Screening of indigenous medicinal plants for synthesis of low cost anti-viral sanitizer and disinfectant.
data.theme: Development of disinfectants particularly using indigenous herbal ingredients
data.projectDigest: The recent COVID-19 pandemic have changed the global scenario dramatically. One of these inevitable turnarounds is the rise in the consumption of disinfectants in healthcare facilities and alcohol based hand sanitizers. Taking advantage of this situation, substandard disinfectants and hand sanitizers made their way extensively in market and made the fight against COVID-19 more difficult. This scenario makes sense to look for indigenous herbal and medicinal plants based synthesis of cost effective disinfectants and hand sanitizers.  In this proposed study we will particularly look to screen out a set of medicinal plants and herbs including Thyme, Lemon balm, peppermint, Neem, Ginger, Garlic, Lemon, Sage, Kalvanji, basil, fennel and dandelion extracts for their antimicrobial and antiviral activity. After assessing their ability to kill microbes and virus, different formulation having varying concentration of these extract will be made in addition with less concentration of alcohol as compared to presently used concentration in market. All thee formulation will be assessed against a set of potent pathogens including bacteria and fungi. As, currently no facility is available in Pakistan for the culturing of COVID-19 viral strain, closely associated viruses in term of structural components will be used for analyzing anti-viral efficacy of extracts formulations. Meanwhile, search of international collaboration will be carried out and formulations samples will be sent abroad for their antiviral activity. After the susceptibility testing against bacteria, fungi and virus, final formulation will be selected to synthesize disinfectant as well as hand sanitizers with careful hazard analysis and side effect studies.

data.projectName: Diagnostic Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence Software for Rapid Detection of COVID-19 on chest radiographs
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest:
Early and accurate case-detection is the cornerstone of every epidemic control. For the COVID-19 pandemic, timely case-detection enables health systems to deliver an appropriate response, reduce community transmission and improve patient outcomes. Diagnostic algorithms, however, need to be adapted to the local resource constraints. This will require alternatives to expensive testing used in developed countries. Low-cost screening approaches, such as chest X-ray (CXR) interpretation with artificial intelligence (AI) software, have been extensively validated in multiple settings and are already being utilized at scale for mass-screening of TB in Pakistan. Although AI software has been shown to be effective in COVID-19 diagnosis through CT-scans, there is no available evidence for their role in chest X-rays.
We propose to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of existing AI software. They are available free-of-cost and adapted for COVID-19 detection. The study will be conducted using existing infrastructure and resources of partners in order to ensure quick implementation. If effective, use of AI supported CXR that are already in use across the country for TB elimination can be immediately deployed to support the COVID-19 response. Limited resources can then be diverted from expensive testing towards implementing community-based control activities.

data.projectName: Designing and characterization of low cost ventilators and purification equipment’s for cure and further prevention of affected COVID-19 patients
data.theme: Indigenous manufacture of Low cost Intensive-care equipment
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan’s government and private hospitals have a very small number of ventilators, which will be too deficient if there is a significant surge of new cases of coronavirus, data shows.The key factor in justifying strategy and effort of any country will be hospital capacity, and within such facilities two aspects are crucial – the number of beds available for patients who come with coronavirus complications and ventilators, which accompany those beds in intensive care units (ICUs).The situation of ventilators which is a huge stress even on the health systems of developed and resource-rich countries is varied in Pakistan with picture varying from province to province.
Statistics of installed ventilators are as follow. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) has around 150 ventilators. Balochistan, all government hospitals put together have only 49 working ventilators. Punjab’s public sector hospitals have nearly 1,300 ventilators. Sindh has nearly 110 ventilators
The above mentioned statistics are quite inadequate for the basic requirements of hospitals. All countries affected by coronavirus are doing an urgent stocktaking of ventilators that their health systems have. Even the well-resourced system like Italy is finding it challenging to provide ventilators in large numbers, which should be commensurate with the number of serious patients. It is stated that even the United States does not have enough ventilators and ICU beds if there’s a noteworthy surge of new cases. As with Italy, the health system could become overwhelmed.
So, the million dollar question is: will there be enough ventilators as the pandemic spreads? As the coronavirus spreads, there are continuing concerns among hospitals, public health experts and government leaders that ICUs would be hard-pressed to handle a surge

In this project we proposed the design and development of low cost and easy to use ventilator for COVID-19 patients.

data.projectName: Blocking the entry of COVID-19- through computationally designed proteins and phytochemicals
data.projectDigest: Recent emergence of novel corona virus 19 (COVID-19) from Wuhan city of China with no known treatment has frightened the modern world. Developing treatment modalities against novel corona virus is need of the time. By stopping the entry of viral particles into the cells of respiratory tract can be a very promising target. The receptor of this virus (ACE2), a host protein binding with the viral spike protein (S) of virus to start the entry process. The computer aided designing of protein binding molecules is routine used in research organizations.  Designing proteins which can bind more efficiently the viral S protein than ACE2 or can hinder its binding with ACE2 protein can act as very potent antiviral agent. The proposed project is to test the activity of designed proteins and molecules from local medicinal plants for their potential viral entry inhibition activity. The success of the proposed molecule might lead to identification of a treatment modality against this deadly virus.

data.projectName: Drivers of Contracting Corona Virus; What Explains the Variation in Corona Cases and Death Rates
data.projectDigest:
While secondary data for studying district level epidemiological patterns and building models may be available readily online and through various sources, for individual level data collection we may have to wait for the pandemic to be over. 

We can even start working on data analysis and epidemiological / statistical modeling using secondary even before the pandemic is over in Pakistan as it does not require field work. 

The proposal builds on the existing initiatives being carried on by various institutions such as University of Oxford which is studying which policies are more effective than others in stemming the rise of new cases.

 https://www.bsg.ox.ac.uk/research/research-projects/oxford-covid-19-government-response-tracker

 However, the study is based on country wide data and it does not cover sub national variations such as variations within Pakistan. We want to address how various factors explain sub national level variations at district as well as individual level. What contributes to contracting corona virus and variation in the death rates? The idea is to discern policy, sociological, and behavioral factors to understand the contracting corona virus and death rate.  This information can help decision-makers and citizens understand the robustness of various factors in fighting corona virus, aiding efforts to fight the pandemic.

The major challenge has been lack of knowledge on the treatment and prevention. In the past four months since SARS-CoV2 was first reported in China, some hypotheses have bene proposed. It is however, observed that the disease has a very different pattern as it is moving from one country to other. Therefore for Pakistan it is important to assess the effectiveness of the treatment regimen to be prepared for a time when the disease will hit the population hard. We will test the effectiveness of the antimalarials, antibiotics and anti-fungals simultaneously in improving clinical outcomes, as well as reducing the duration of hospital stay in patients in Balochistan.

data.projectName: “Rapid Discovery of Immunostimulants and Antiviral Natural Products”
data.piUniversity: Karakurum International University, Gilgit, Gilgit Baltistan
data.theme: Development of disinfectants particularly using indigenous herbal ingredients
data.projectDigest: Formulation of herbal medicinal products, and discovery of the active natural products are the main research area in field of chemical and biological sciences to develop  new drugs for the challenging diseases in global pharmaceutical industries. Ethnobotanical leading phytochemical investigation on medicinal plants based on bioactivity evaluation is useful research way for the rapid discovery and development of the new active products against the challenging diseases. Various viral infectious diseases and recent  worldwide COVID-19 outbreaks  strongly demanded to develop the safe  natural immunostimulators and antiviral disinfectants products for the rapid control of the theses viral infections. Formulation of herbal medicinal products, and discovery of the active natural products have strong history in field of development of new drugs for the challenging diseases in global pharmaceutical.   Most importantly, the present worldwide COVID-19 outbreak urgently required the significant immunostimulants and anti viral herbal/natural products for the rapid control of  the COVID-19 infection in time.  Therefore, the proposed research proposal based on ethnobotanicl analysis, bioactivity evaluation and phytochemical investigation on the medicinal potent species of Picorriza distributed in pastures of Gilgit-Baltistan region. The outcome of the proposed study will lead us for the development/formulation of the safe immunimodlating and antiviral herbal/natural products for the repaid disinfections of the COVID-19 outbreak, and other viral infections.

The purpose of this research project will be to identify the mediators that help to explain that how and why an independent variable influences the disease outcome and to understand the path mechanism between them. The mediators are the underlying factors which if identified properly then it can be broken the chain that leads to severe conditions.  
Furthermore, the moderators will also be identified that are causing the wide spread and fatalities due to COVID-19. data.projectName: Multi-target approach to discover potential therapeutics against corona virus and understand the target sites of neutralizing antibodies in vaccine design perspective
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: SARS-CoV-2 infections have created alarming situation worldwide accounting for enormous economic burden. In this proposal we are using  multidisciplinary and multi -target approaches for drug discovery and understanding the viral immune response mechanism in vaccine design perspective. In this regard we have three associated aims incorporating aspects of immediate as well long term outcomes. Drug re-purposing by screening library of FDA-approved drug to identify inhibitors of SARS-Cov-2 essential enzymes will have immediate impact. Identification of potential drugs from traditional herbal plants and organic compound libraries by targeting various viral factors particular viral surface glycan clusters to inhibit its entry will be highly significant in drug discovery. Moreover, we are aim to understand the target sites on the virus of neutralizing antibodies present is the sera of individuals who recovered from the infection which will provide structural template for vaccine design.

data.projectName: TeleDoc (A Tele health System for real-time Access to Patients Data and Surveillance of Disease)
data.piUniversity: Sir Syed (CASE) Institute of Technology, Islamabad
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest: The World Health Organization (WHO) warns that the most at-risk populations are: “older persons and persons with pre-existing medical conditions, such as lung disease, high blood pressure, cancer,  heart disease or diabetes.” People with these conditions seem to be at increased risk of becoming gravely ill if infected with the corona virus. These older person ca be patient, hospital staff or even senior doctors their selves.  The proposed project consists of research to integrate smart imaging and healthcare device with conventional patient management system for real-time collection of patients’ data. These include digital portable x-rays, stethoscope, ophthalmoscope,  ultrasound for collection of data related to lungs, respiratory sounds, human retina and other organs like kidney liver etc respectively. The research have shown that how COVID-19 and corona virus have effected lungs and other organs like retina etc [2-3]. Inclusion of thermal camera in this system will add another perspective of initial screening of suspected cases.  Now combining these smart acquisition devices and their analysis along with conventional telemedicine system form a solution which is need of the hour. This will help in collection of actual data at real-time to enable proper surveillance of such breakout.
