data.projectName: Development of point-of-care molecular diagnostic platform for rapid naked eye detection of SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19)
data.projectDigest: The outbreak of SARS-CoV-2 has become a public health emergency of international concern. The pandemic may become more devastating in underdeveloped countries like Pakistan due to limited healthcare facilities. Early detection of virus is crucial for combating the spread of coronavirus. For SARS-CoV-2 detection, it is so far relied upon conventional molecular methods like rRT-PCR which is expensive, time taking and requires trained personnel and cutting-edge instrumentation. Therefore, a simple and inexpensive method that allows for rapid detection of SARS-CoV-2 with high reliability and great potential for point of care (POC) application is highly needed in COVID-19 outbreak emergency. We aim to develop a colorimetric assay based on previously described Loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) method for the robust and cost effective diagnosis of SARS-CoV2 without requiring complex diagnostic infrastructure. LAMP specific primers designed for Pakistani SARS-CoV-2 isolate (MT240479.1) will be employed for the amplification of virus genome fragments at a single temperature in less than 30 minutes. Furthermore, viral RNA isolation procedure will be simplified and strand displacing DNA polymerase will be produced indigenously for use in LAMP ultimately reducing the assay cost. The assay will also be integrated in a handheld POC device with the help of foreign collaborators.

data.projectName: Development of phylogenetic based high quality online surveillance system and Diagnostic Kit
data.projectDigest: COVID-19 is an infectious disease caused by a newly discovered coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2). SARS-CoV-2 is enveloped positive stranded RNA Virus with major characteristic of their high rate of genetic mutation, which leads to evolution of new viral strains and is a mechanism by which viruses escape host defenses. Unfortunately, the genetic sequence of SARS-CoV-2 is not studied in meaningful way from Pakistani isolates. Todate, there are only two sequences of SARS-CoV-2 from Pakistan. It is difficult to understand its mutability or comparability with other isolates. Limitation of online authentic resources is main hurdle towards drawing meaningful information for the development of diagnostic kits and drugs discovery for Pakistani SARS-CoV-2 positive patients. This project has been proposed the development of high-quality bioinformatics databases and tools for tracking of hotspot regions of SARS-CoV-2 genome globally. Though, a few Real Time RT-PCR detection test kits have been developed in different countries but so far only two were declared as gold standard kits by WHO. Therefore, a reliable and precise detection system of SARS-CoV-2 is required. Real Time RT-PCR diagnostic kit will help the country to cop-up with current pandemic situation on the one hand and will help to increase diagnostic capacity on other hand.

data.projectName: Synthesis of multi-epitope  Pancoronavirus vaccine peptides  by application of Artificial Intelligence algorithmic and  Immuno-informatics methods
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
The proposed project aimed to develop multi-epitope subunit pancoronoviral vaccine peptides using artificial intelligence (AI) based logarithmic and comprehensive immunoinformatics methods. Such potential vaccinable candidates can serve as a blueprint in effective vaccine against coronaviral infection prevention from multiple coronavirus strains. Earlier Vaccinable peptide sequence for epitope based vaccine in case of Alphaviruses, Hepatitis B & C, HIV, HPV and Influenza viruses for recognition of potent immunogen have shown effective result. Multivalent pneumococcal vaccine is commercially available and is successfully being used in Pakistani population for preventing pneumonia. Infact, the multivalent vaccine has contributed significantly in declining Pneumonia incidence in Pakistani population.
Currently, the number of people infected by COVID-19 is increasing at a rapid pace. The sociocultural and religious norms of Pakistani society makes the social distancing and self-quarantining measures difficult to implement which is very much advocated and required for restricting COVID-19 pandemic.  Treating epidemic cases can easily overwhelm Pakistani medical systems capability in handling and managing patients. Therefore, preventive measures in the shape of potential vaccine can serve as an attractive and a rather realistic option in restricting the COVID-19 epidemic. Till date, to our knowledge, no pancoronaviral vaccine exists. This study will employ rigorous data mining international sequence databases NCBI and GISAID for SARS CoV, MERS and COVID-19 strains reported from last 17 years around the world.

data.projectName: Functional characterization of Receptor Binding Domain (RBD) to angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) cell receptor in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
data.projectDigest: Yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) is a model organism utilized for virus research. They are natural hosts for viruses since they possess their own indigenous viruses. Yeasts have been exploited for studying plant, animal and human viruses. Many positive sense (+) RNA viruses and some DNA viruses replicate with various levels in yeasts, hence allowing study of those viral activities during viral life cycle. Yeasts are single cell eukaryotic organisms. Hence, many of the fundamental cellular functions such as cell cycle regulation or programed cell death are highly conserved from yeasts to higher eukaryotes. Consequently, they are especially appropriate to study the impact of those viral activities on interrelated cellular activities during virus-host interactions. Yeasts demonstrate numerous unique advantages in virus research over higher eukaryotes, like yeast cells are easy to maintain in the laboratory with relatively short doubling time. They are non-biohazardous, genetically modifiable with small genomes that permit genome-wide analysis of virological and cellular functions. Current research involves genetic modification of yeast cells to produce Y-shaped proteins (monoclonal antibodies or simply recombinant proteins), which will be extracted and utilized to treat patients infected with COVID-19.

data.projectName: Prophylaxis for COVID-19: Comparison of Three Groups; 1. Drug: Hydroxychloroquine, 2. Salts: Nigella sativa (Kalonji) and Star Anise (Badian-Khatai) and 3. Placebo.
data.projectDigest:
Currently, COVID-19 is a enormous threat to community health worldwide. Presentl, the novel virus (SARS-CoV-2) is extremely contagious i.e. 5 -50-times more deadly than normal influenza with mortality rate 0.3-8%. Hence, it is urgently required to work on the possible interventions.
The drug, Hydroxy-chloroquine, a low-cost anti-malarial with immune-modulatory properties, is an expectant prophylaxis for COVID-19. Chloroquine, a similar salt with a high toxicity profile, has shown benefit in clinical trials conducted in 100 SARS-CoV-2 infected patients. Recently, hydroxychloroquine, has been revealed to have better efficac.
Since centuries, Nigella sativa (Kalonji) and Star Anise (Badian Khatai) are claimed to be anti-inflammatory, antioxidant and immunomodulators. There are numerous studies on their beneficial effects as prophylaxis and treatment of seasonal flu, fever etc. 
This study will test if hydroxychloroquine or Nigella sativa (Kalonji) plsStar Anise (Badian Khatai) may be used to prevent the development of COVID-19 symptoms/disease in persons who live within an area who has been labelled to have diagnosed cases of COVID-19 in comparison with Placebo group 
If any of the 2 experimental groups is shown to decrease the risk of developing symptoms/disease of COVID-19, this could be extremely helpful to lessen the mortality & morbidity of COVID-19 epidemic/pandemic.

data.projectName: A complete modeling of Spike (S) protein and Nucleocapsid (N) protein by Computational resources
data.piUniversity: Federal Urdu University of Arts, Sciences & Technology
data.projectDigest: Outbreak of novel Coronavirus gains attention for therapeutics development. It is highly pathogenic and spreading epidemically into the human population. The mortality rate is too high that raises red epidemiologic flag. Reproduction rate (Ro) in Wuhan is 2.2 or even more (1.4-6.5) or increasing day by day in different countries. In humans two common coronaviruses i.e. HCoV-229E and HCoV-OC43 are found and cause mild illness, in contrast novel Coronavirus that cause severe illness including fever, edema, destruction of alveolies called as Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS-nCoV) and characterized atypical pneumonia. Newly identified virus belongs to ?-coronavirus. In this worst condition there is a high need for effective and safe development of inhibitors to cure against life threatens infection. This proposal suggest for development of antiviral potential leads to combat infection. In silico strategy is a powerful tool to shorten time and reduce cost as compared to de novo drug discovery. There are several platforms available to solve conspiracy of SARS-nCoV 2019 including pharmacological based network and clinical laboratories, modeling and dynamics simulation techniques is one of the promising technique to quantify the novel or potential lead by implementing drug-genes signatures available  in the literature. This proposal present integrative research based on Human interactome network with in short time frame.   Our strategy based on available molecular information of previous coronavirus (SARS), as scientific community reveals that novel coronavirus have close relationship to SARS. The objective of this proposal is to target Spike (S) protein and nucleocapsid (N) protein of virus. Molecular docking will be very helpful to obtain theoretical results.

data.projectName: Rapid diagnosis of COVID-19  using fluorophores, DNA and next generation genomics
data.projectDigest: With the outbreak of Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19, the disease caused by a novel coronavirus SARS-CoV-2), we are currently experiencing a worldwide emergency affecting all societies. It is now posing both a serious threat worldwide especially to vulnerable populations and a daunting challenge to the global economy. One of major concerns about the disease is the lack of a robust and easy to use diagnostic assay. Current diagnostic tests for COVID-19 include reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) and real-time reverse transcription PCR (qRT-PCR). However, molecular diagnostic methods are expensive in terms of cost and time and require specialized expertise limiting its use when rapid diagnosis is required for fast intervening decisions. We are proposing here a novel method to label and modify coronaviruses using calcium chloride (CaCl2), fluorophores and DNA. This approach would allow us to detect viruses more rapidly than the currently available methods. Whole Genome Sequencing of SARS-CoV-2 viruses from Pakistani COVID-19 patients will performed and a comparative genomic analysis will be performed. The genome analysis will help identify the target protein to design assays for specific detection of SARS-CoV-2. data.projectSummary: With the outbreak of Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19, the disease caused by a novel coronavirus SARS-CoV-2), we are currently experiencing a worldwide emergency affecting all societies. It is now posing both a serious threat worldwide especially to vulnerable populations and a daunting challenge to the global economy. One of major concerns about the disease is the lack of a robust and easy to use diagnostic assay. Current diagnostic tests for COVID-19 include reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) and real-time reverse transcription PCR (qRT-PCR). However, molecular diagnostic methods are expensive in terms of cost and time and require specialized expertise limiting its use when rapid diagnosis is required for fast intervening decisions. We are proposing here a novel method to label and modify coronaviruses using calcium chloride (CaCl2), fluorophores and DNA. This approach would allow us to detect viruses more rapidly than the currently available methods. Whole Genome Sequencing of SARS-CoV-2 viruses from Pakistani COVID-19 patients will performed and a comparative genomic analysis will be performed. The genome analysis will help identify the target protein to design assays for specific detection of SARS-CoV-2. It will also help us understand the origin of SARS-CoV2, how it has crossed the species barrier and how we can predict similar future events.

data.projectName: Preparation, Formulation  and Evaluation of Cost effective Herbal base Disinfectants, & Antiseptics  against Coronaviridae
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.theme: Development of disinfectants particularly using indigenous herbal ingredients
data.projectDigest:
Coronaviruses are divided into Alpha, Beta, Gamma and Delta coronavirus groups. Coronaviruses are responsible for a wide variety of existing and emerging diseases in humans and other mammals (including food animals) as well as in birds (including poultry). In human beings previously, it has caused severe acute diseases like SARS-CoV-2, MERS and COVID-19. Based on what is currently known about the virus, and about similar coronaviruses that cause SARS and MERS, spread from person-to-person happens most frequently among close contacts (within about 6 feet). This type of transmission occurs via respiratory droplets, but disease transmission via infectious aerosols is currently uncertain. Transmission of SARS-CoV-2 to persons from surfaces contaminated with the virus has not been documented. Transmission of coronavirus occurs much more commonly through respiratory droplets than through fomites. Current evidence suggests that SARS-CoV-2 may remain viable for hours to days on surfaces made from a variety of materials. Cleaning of visibly dirty surfaces followed by disinfection is a best practice measure for prevention of COVID-19 and other viral respiratory illnesses in households and community settings.There are several commercial antiseptic available in market having chemical sanitizers as a base which has some disadvantages, adverse and side effects. Their frequent and long time use can lead to some side effects and skin irritation. Several plants extract and essential oils are being most widely used and well-documented for their antiviral activity. 
Present study aimed to formulate effective, safe, nontoxic and low cost herbal disinfectant / hand sanitizer against corona virus taking the example of Infectious bronchitis virus which a prototype virus of coronaviridae.

data.projectName: Development of a low cost  diagnostics kit based on Reverse Transcriptase-Polymerase Chain Reaction
data.projectDigest: The proposal  explains the development of a low cost molecular based diagnostic method for COVID-19 disease, employing reverse transcriptase PCR technology. The current test method is based on expensive Real time PCR machine, with a set of selected primers. Pakistan is totally relying on  imported kits, enzymes,  crucial chemicals and equipment required for the testing of disease.  Due to  COVID-19 pandemic, there is worldwide huge demand for the diagnostic supplies. RT-PCR based diagnostic test  is costly and is out of  reach of a common  man, due constrain in the supplies, from abroad. Nucleic acid based test are considered as gold standard in Diagnostic. Here we describe a method in which the test could be done on a commonly available thermal cycler, using specifically designed primers. It is planned to develop a low cost molecular based diagnostic test, using reverse Transcriptase polymerase chain reaction. For setting up the method synthetic gene would be used. The test will use the enzyme reverse transcriptase for the synthesis of cDNA from RNA, isolated from the subject. cDNA will be amplified by using commonly available thermal cycler instead of real time PCR machine. Chemically modified primers based on  DNA or its derivatives like PNA will be employed for maximum efficiency. The locally developed test will be at least ten times economical then the nucleic acid based test available in the market.

data.projectName: Adoption of E-education under the COVID-19: An Emergency Management Perspective
data.theme: Information Collection and Dissemination IT platforms)
data.projectDigest:
In the past two decades, the world has faced several emergencies again and again like a disaster, infections, and diseases outbreaks. Not only developing countries, but well developed countries like the USA, UK, China, Italy are suffering in this panic situation. Considering the importance of social distancing in this viral infection pandemic, humans need to reorganize the daily activities and education is one of them. In this way, e-learning has quickly become the new standard for education. However, the students and faculty members from different contexts are differently responding to this situation and also experiencing challenges due to the change in education system during this pandemic COVID-19. 
Emergency management for the education system can help to reduce the challenges. The current study will investigate and test the four elements of emergency management theory mitigation, preparedness, response, and recovery from HEIs students and teachers’ perspective. The study will be completed in four phases employing mixed methods research approach and will come up with a practical framework to apply during and after emergency. Data will be collected from four regions online and in case of availability of the respondents the research team will try to expand the research population to get in depth and exhaustive insights. The results of this empirical study will be helpful not only for Pakistan but for the other countries as well.

data.projectName: A mathematical approach to understand the Corona Virues infection in pakistan.
data.projectDigest: In this project we will construct a mathematical model for the study of dynamics of corona virus in Pakistan.   We will divide the internal community of Pakistan in four classes. The effect of four external source classes Iran, Afghanistan, China and Saudi Arabia will be imposed. Using the previous data of the epidemic we will approximate the various parameters and using these parameters the dynamical system will predict the expected near future of Pakistan. The external sources can be increased or decreased therefore any other country will be able to modify the system according to their own situation. The prediction of the system will be important for the policy makers to make suitable policies and measures for maximum safety of the public.

data.projectName: Modeling the Socio-Environmental Factors of COVID-19 Transmission in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The novel coronavirus known as COVID-19 has become a reason of global crisis in the form of a pandemic. It is highly contagious disease with high rate of human to human transmission. It was first reported in December 2019 in Wuhan, Hubei Province of China. Within a few weeks, it started to spread globally. So far it has claimed thousands of lives and is expected to affect millions of people around the world till it reaches its peak. There is no study available in the scientific literature for Pakistan about the COVID-19 local patterns. Very less is known about the social and environmental perspective of COVID-19 transmission. Hence, the understanding of this disease in the social and environmental perspective is important. This project aims to find out the relationship of various socio-environmental factors which contribute in the transmission of COVID-19 in Pakistan. This project shall consider the local weather parameters (e.g., temperature, relative humidity etc.), social aspects (e.g., human population density, urbanization etc.), and COVID-19 confirmed cases (gender, age etc.) to find their mutual relationships. The research shall be translated in to policy options and general provisions to inform policy makers and general public for mitigation of COVID-19 in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Mathematical Epidemiology of Novel Coronavirus COVID 19: Analysis of Spread and Control by Modeling and Simulations along with Stability Analysis
data.projectDigest:
The wide spread of the COVID-19 coronavirus and the lack or inefficiency of purposeful and result based intervention is a great call for other empirical and scientific interventions which seeks to review strategic models and recommendations of social and scientific research for disease control.
Mathematical Modeling will contribute to analyze the spread and control of this disease. The updated models should be obtained to understand the current epidemic and forecast the future concerns and helps us in decision making regarding preventions. 
The optimal solutions of the models is highly desired to understand the accurate behavior of the COVID 19 spread and mathematical strategy should be given to handle the control parameters. Basic reproduction number will be useful to analyze the transmissibility of the infection and make the understanding to give the safety measures. 
The estimation of the spread up to 1 year must be required and it is possible due to mathematical modeling to analyze all the included parameters at the same time. Fractional derivative can contribute vital role in understanding the hidden nonlinearity in the model and also given the more accurate results as fractional derivatives have memory.

data.projectName: Syndrome Based Epidemic Pre-emption
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest:
Health is an important factor in the social and economic development of Pakistan. The Global Human Development report ranked Pakistan 152nd out of 189 (GHD 2019. With more than 40% of its population urban, the risk of communicable diseases and potential epidemic / pandemic is significant.
 
Existing measures are limited to conventional approaches of screening and isolation, social distancing, household quarantine and school closure etc. These approaches however have had limited success and cost hugely in economic terms as witnessed currently in case of COVID-19.

An effective strategy is to detect an outbreak through syndrome-based infectious disease surveillance system.

Such system, once implemented and operational, can significantly improve the quality, efficiency, safety, and cost effectiveness of detection, control and mitigation of epidemics by supporting the health officials to 

•	Plan control strategies
•	Define populations at risk  
•	Develop emergency health response administrative hierarchy; 
•	Rapidly mobilize mass immunization programs
•	Allocate important epidemic response resources 
•	Estimate the requirements to control the epidemic (drugs, vaccine, human resources, transport, financial resources) 
•	Identify and ensure competent laboratory support 
•	Coordinate and communicate with general public and health care community
•	Strategize post-epidemic scenario

data.projectName: State-of-the-art gel electrophoresis and gel documentation system for rapid detection of novel coronavirus (COVID-19)
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.theme: Indigenous manufacture of Low cost Intensive-care equipment
data.projectDigest: Gel electrophoresis and documentation is an analytical technique commonly used in clinical and research laboratories. In this project, we propose the development of advanced gel electrophoresis and gel documentation system which is part of polymerase chain reaction (PCR) to detect the onset of disease. RNA extracted from oropharyngeal swabs used to detect the particular analyte which is involved in causing disease such as coronavirus (COVID-19). The advanced gel electrophoresis unit can adjust four parallel electrophoresis tanks. Each four tank can be programmed/optimized with different parameters. In this way, increased number of samples can be analyzed for the detection of analyte at a time. Hence, the detection timing can be reduced to handle bulk of samples that are being generate in the present scenario in which coronavirus cases are increasing day-by-day. The currently available setup in molecular analysis laboratories lack this functional property. Furthermore, our proposed setup is cost effective. It will reduce 50 % price which international brands offer. In Pakistan, this product is not being developed locally. The laboratories which have gel-electrophoresis and documentation system imports from the international market. Its production with more advanced parameters will increase efficiency, capacity and affordability for diagnostics/research laboratories to buy it.

data.projectName: Development of needleless electro spun nanofibers with herbs N95 plus face mask
data.projectDigest:
The world is facing one of the biggest pandemic of modern time in the form of COVID-19. First line of defense against COVID-19 are personal protective equipment (PPE). Unfortunately due to spread of worldwide pandemic there is shortage of PPE. To prevent the spread of virus, simple face mask are not enough as they tend to leak and hardly provide a barrier against airborne virus. To stop the spread of COVID-19, N95 mask is recommended as PPE for health care workers. N95 are a class in masks which are certified by the NIOSH, described as filtering 95 % of the airborne particles.
    In recent developments, nano fibers are studied and found with huge potential for filtration purposes based on smaller size and dimensions of pores. The biggest hurdle, however, had always been considerably slower rate of production of fibers. Needleless electro spinning has proven to have been able to, produce 15-40 times more nano fibers as compared with conventional method. The concept of needle less spinning will be further enhanced in this project and better results will be achieved. The nano fibers will be deposited on conventional mask outer layers and perform function of middle layers and make major filtration.

data.projectName: An Innovative Proposal for Making Pakistan Free of Hunger and Poverty- A lesson from the Economic Crisis created by Coronavirus Pandemic
data.theme: Information Collection and Dissemination IT platforms)
data.projectDigest: COVID-19 has given several lessons to the world, who now realizes that economic prosperity for everyone, and not merely economic growth, is required for fight against crisis. The world also realizes that the faith based philanthropic behavior of local people is a major source of support, hence should be properly institutionalized. The question, then, is that how can we take advantage of the philanthropic behaviour of our own people in a formal way in this crisis. This project aims to provide implementable model for the maximum mobilization and efficient utilization of charitable funds for making Pakistan hunger and poverty free in short as well as long run. We will provide workable models to the government of Pakistan for tackling the issue of hunger and poverty, without putting any pressure government budget. We will also provide alternative business models based on field work. The implementations of the model will enable Planning Commission of Pakistan to meet the top 2 Sustainable Development goals before the target year of 2030. The proper implementation of model is likely to help us in achieving Economic growth with shared prosperity for everyone (the current motto of World Bank) and that too without foreign aids.

data.projectName: Knowledge, Attitude and Practices among Various Health Professionals, General Public and Cholistani Nomads: Implications for COVID Control Efforts
data.theme: Information Collection and Dissemination IT platforms)
data.projectDigest: The instructions of social distancing by the government regarding COVID-19 have not been taken seriously by the Pakistani population. In specific, the far-flung Cholistan desert nomads never got the true essence of this initiative. Cholistani nomads are extensive pastoralist livestock-keepers, adopting a seasonal migratory pattern in search of food and water, within the Cholistan desert and its outskirt cities (Bahawalpur, Bahawalnagar, Rahim-Yar-Khan). Thus, they are the most vulnerable populations for disease infection/spread. Furthermore, their ultra-conservative nature promotes various misconceptions and stigmas. Understanding of socio-cultural and economic aspects of populations is vital for improving the health of poor/rural/vulnerable populations. A knowledge, attitude and practice (KAPs) analysis should be conducted in order to attain the knowledge as to how different people react to COVID-19. At the moment no such information is present in the literature except for a Chinese report. The present research proposal aims to assess the level of knowledge, attitudes and practices adopted by various communities towards this pandemic (n=3000 respondents). It will incorporate various health professionals (medics/paramedics, veterinary & para-veterinary personnel), general public, and Cholistani pastoralists. Separate questionnaires allied with Focus Group Discussions/Meetings (FGDs) and Participatory Rural Appraisal (PRAs) will be utilized. The variables/measures will include demographics (age, gender, marital status, education, occupation, residency etc.) and KAP. The data will help government devise strategic initiatives for COVID-19 containment.

data.projectName: An Assessment of the Current practices and challenges on biomedical waste management in Pakistan under COVID-19 Pandemic
data.theme: Development of disinfectants particularly using indigenous herbal ingredients
data.projectDigest: Various studies have observed health and environmental issues in health care waste management in developing countries like Pakistan (Ali et al., 2016; 2017a, b, c; Ansari et al., 2019; Omer et al., 2012). With the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic continuing to spread and its impacts upon human health and the economy intensifying day-by-day, governments are urged to treat waste management, including of medical, household and other hazardous waste, as an urgent and essential public service in order to minimize possible secondary impacts upon health and the environment.During such an outbreak, many types of additional medical and hazardous waste are generated, including infected masks, gloves and other protective equipment, together with a higher volume of non-infected items of the same nature. Unsound management of this waste could cause unforeseen effects on human health and the environment. The safe handling, and final disposal of this waste is therefore a vital element in an effective emergency response. Effective management of biomedical and health-care waste requires appropriate identification, collection, separation, storage, transportation, treatment and disposal, as well as important associated aspects including disinfection, personnel protection and training. It is essential that waste from designated COVID-19 medical sources, is given due attention and priority it requires in order to ensure the minimization of impacts upon human health and the environment from these potentially hazardous waste streams.

data.projectName: Monitoring immune pattern of rapid biomarker cytokines and kinetics of antibody responses in COVID-19 patients.
data.projectDigest: The public health menace of Corona Virus Disease (COVID-19) caused huge health and economic losses due to trans-boundary and human-to-human transmission. Following entry of 2019-nCoV/SARS-CoV-2 to human host, a cascade of immunological responses are elicited by a storm of cytokines (IL-1?, TNF-?, IFN-?, IL-6, IL-8, IL-33), immune cells and antibody (IgM/IgG) responses. However, immuno-pathogenesis and kinetics of immune patterns triggered during COVID-19 remains obscure, despite availability of 2019-nCoV sequencing data. Therefore, it is imperative to monitor kinetics of immune responses in asymptomatic, subclinical/mild, clinical/severe, convalescent/recovered and sero-convertor COVID-19 patients for disease outcome and correlation with our demographic characteristics. We aimed at deciphering kinetics of non-invasive cytokine and antibody immune responses in COVID-19 patients compared with healthy control (HC). To ascertain the objectives, a cohort of COVID-19 positive/exposed (n=384) and HC (n=100) individuals sera/plasma will be collected from COVID-19 centers in Punjab as per WHO’s ethical/sampling guidelines. Above mentioned cytokines and viral antibodies (IgM and IgG) will be measured in sera/plasma of COVID-19 patients and HC by specific ELISA. Data of immune markers of COVID-19 patients will be correlated statistically with clinical data. The project will provide proof-of-concept about immune patterns of COVID-19 and rapid point-of-care-testing-(POCT) of infected/exposed population in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Title of Project:	Antimicrobial and Antiviral Herbal Disinfectants and Green Hand Sanitizers: Environment Friendly Technologies for Richer, for Poorer
data.piUniversity: Karakurum International University, Gilgit, Gilgit Baltistan
data.theme: Development of disinfectants particularly using indigenous herbal ingredients
data.projectDigest:
Viruses are fatal for both human and animals. There are countless viruses exist on the globe and many of them cause serious complication in human body. Herpesvirus, HIV, influenza, hepatitis, coronavirus, SARS-Cov, MERS-Cov, etc. are among the among the top studied fatal viruses. It is very clear that diseases caused by new viruses cannot be treated and cured with the existing antiviral drugs. Therefore, the prevention and control of viruses by using best practices like indoor and outdoor fumigation and cleaning with safe, effective and selective herbal disinfectants and habit of green hand sanitizers to maintain hygienic condition is the best strategy to avoid pandemic outbreaks in future. They are eco- friendly and more suitable to household applications than conventional chemicals.
The main goal of this proposal is to introduce hebal based desinfectants and green sanitizers alternative to hazardous conventional chemicals by using a valid mixture of botanical pesticides from 10 medicinal herbs. Our approach will require significant interaction between the Pakistan and overseas cooperating partners to achieve target objectives. Most of the initial extraction, fractionation and formulation would be carried out at the department of Chemistry Karakoram International University, whereas anti-microbial studies will be carried out at the department of biological sciences, KIU. The pesticidal studies will be carried out in collaboration at National Nematological Research Centre, University of Karachi. In addition to this, the anti-viral studies will be performed in the laboratories of overseas collaborators in Malaysia, China, and Netherlands.

data.projectName: TARGETTING CORONAVIRUS: GENOMIC TO PROTEOMIC LEVEL ANALYSIS
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest: A major public health crisis has emerged as a result of the emerging Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19). According to the World Health Organization (WHO), there had been more than 5.5 lac confirmed cases and more than 25000 deaths by 27 March 2020, and the COVID-19 was declared a pandemic the same day. In rapid/early response, based on comparative and pan-genomic analysis, we would analyze the conserved sequences to sort out the structural and functional drug targets. We will carry out the re-profiling and re-positioning of FDA approved antiviral drugs and thousands of natural molecules against potential conserved domains. For the delayed/time taking plan, we will continue to work for identifying the antigenic proteins and potential epitopes for developing prophylactic vaccines.

data.projectName: Indigenous development of Textile Gears from locally available materials for COVID-19 outbreak
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Safety from the coronavirus is the prime challenge. This safety can only be optimized by wearing protective gears which are capable of stopping the virus interference with the gear wearer. 

In this project protective gears will include face mask, face visors, gowns, googles, gloves, bed sheets, curtains which are necessary to combat against COVID-19 outbreak.

Currently, the materials used for protective gear are imported in various forms and then protective gears are developed. Identification and hybridization of locally available textile-based materials which can be used as protection against COVID-19 is one of the purpose of this project. Once techniques for hybridizing locally available material are developed then various varieties of protective gears can be made. This will ease in the supply chain for the production and a availability of protective gears. 

In this project both academic and sectoral partners will be involved. Academic partners will do their research part and the sectoral partner will help to use their resources for the development of the protective gears.  

Identifications, hybridizations, standardized testing and development will be the main phases in this project.

data.projectName: An Intelligent Integrated Infectious Disease Surveillance System Based on Big Data Analytics
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest: Recent advancement in the field of biomedical has been done to diagnose serval chronic and acute disease with well-known symptoms, many diseases still have heterogeneous symptoms which creates load for the public health sector. To address such problems and to protect Pakistani from serious infectious diseases, the artificial intelligence-based infectious disease surveillance system has been proposed to monitor, predict, control and prevent diseases. Infectious diseases are required to monitor nationwide to help the government and health care departments in the early response and preparedness of them. To predict any epidemic outbreaks and their trends. The Data will be gathering from all health care departments of Pakistan, clinical laboratories, genome databases, internet, outbreak investigation reports, and other disease surveillance system to protect the Pakistani nation. The system will be a multi-function program that includes the surveillance system (consisting of web and mobile applicaation) for data collection, compilation, analysis, and sharing of health data as well as predictive models for the prediction of future circumstances. It will allow public health departments to obtain data needed to monitor, control and prevent the occurrence and spread of these health conditions. Also, researchers can do bioinformatics analysis that will help early prevention and identification of markers that will allow the discovery of vaccines.

data.projectName: Transforming phytonutrients into immune boosters and main protease (Mpro) inhibitors using green extraction technology for the prevention and treatment of COVID19
data.projectDigest: The emerging epidemic of COVID-19 has killed thousands of humans worldwide and the deadly situation is still prevailing around the globe. According to WHO, Coronavirus vaccine is 'at least a year' away. But this deadly virus isn’t giving the world that much time. Thus, apart from vaccine development, there is an urgent need to discover novel therapies to battle COVID-19. One such emerging approach is to characterize immune boosting and viral protease (COVID19 Mpro) inhibiting activity of phytonutrients to halt the viral replication and proteolytic maturation. This project is aimed at development of anti-COVID19 Mpro enriched extracts and immunomodulators to provide safe, effective and economical treatment to COVID-19 patients. Based on our recent in silico results, we have identified four (Hesperidin, apiin, rutin and diosmin) natural potent inhibitors of COVID19-Mpro. In addition to targeting COVID-19 Mpro, hesperidin has also potential to inhibit the COVID-19 at all stages of the infection by interacting spike glycoprotein and ACE2 receptor. Interestingly, hesperidin’s oral bioavailability, favorable safety and tolerability profile further affirms the potential of hesperidin-based therapies to be ready to go on the shelf, for the rapid production of antiviral drugs. Thus, natural anti-COVID19 Mpro enriched extracts has potential to be quickly translated into clinics with incredible outcomes to treat COVID-19 infected patients.

data.projectName: Supercomputer Assisted Pharmacoinformatics Protocol for Rational Repurposing of Therapeutics for COVID-19
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Human infections by the SARS coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2) are known to be closely associated with interactions between the viral spike protein (S-protein) and specific human host receptors, such as the Angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) receptor. Using early SARS-CoV-2 genome data and standard template-based modeling techniques, 3D structural model of the SARS-CoV-2 S-protein was built. Further, protein-protein docking calculations were performed indicating that although SARS-CoV and SARSCoV-2 do have a several differences in their sequences, both have favorable binding affinity for the human ACE2 receptor2. Therefore, structural model of the SARS-CoV-2 S-protein-human ACE2 complex represent a reasonable target to disrupt the viral S-protein-ACE2 interface. However, the development of novel small-molecule therapeutics (drugs) takes years, with trials and regulatory approval taking between 10 to 15 years . Given that the outbreak of SARS-CoV-2may quickly become a global challenge, it would be of great benefit to identify and repurpose already well characterized small-molecules and approved drugs for use in combating the disease. Here we propose molecular dynamics simulations with virtual high-throughput screening in an ensemble docking protocol to identify well-characterized drugs, metabolites, and/or natural products that may disrupt S-protein- ACE2 receptor interface stability or the ability of the S-protein to recognize the ACE2 receptor.

data.projectName: Nanoviricide Liposomes as a natural therapeutic strategy against COVID?19
data.projectDigest: The recent outbreak of pneumonia-causing COVID-19 around the globe and in Pakistan is an urgent global public health issue. Considering the potential threat of a pandemic, this study is a multi-pronged experimental study that will be conducted to evaluate the safety and efficacy potential of compounds isolated from over 150 in-house-made extracts of medicinal herbs as anti SARS-CoV-2 through its ACE2 receptors. The study will relate diverse investigational therapeutic agents based on rich tradition of herbal medicine in Pakistan to a control arm. If one therapy demonstrates to be efficacious, then this treatment modality may become the control arm for comparison(s) with new trial treatment(s). The bioinformatics analysis will be conducted to screen higher binding capacity with Receptor-Binding Domain (RBD) of SARS-CoV-2 virus by molecular docking in collaboration with Bioinformatics Department QAU. The optimized natural compound showing promising binding potential with RBD will be manufactured as nanoviricide biomimetic liposomes based on suitable biomimetic immunomodulatory materials in collaboration with School of Life and Biomedical Sciences, University College London. Nanoviricide biomimetic liposomes adjuvants with natural products is striving to envisage streaming through the blood stream, penetrating through the body, capturing and destroying the offending virus particles. These collaborations on pharmaceutical sciences, plant sciences, nanomedicine and bioinformatics will provide a strong breadth of scientific expertise to provide cutting-edge technological solutions for treating COVID-19.

data.projectName: Formulation of herbal disinfectants and evaluation of  anti microbial efficiency
data.piUniversity: University of Kotli Azad Jammu and Kashmir

data.projectDigest: Corona Virus has caused serious threat to human beings because of its highly contagious nature. The virus has killed thousands of people with and increasing its target population in to millions. It has hit the advanced countries like USA, China, UK, Italy, Germany, France and Iran very badly. The virus has caused infection in thousands of people in Pakistan while the number of patients is increasing every day. Since no treatment of the disease has been reported yet, we can opt the precautionary measures to reduce the risk of spread of the virus. Hands are the primary mode of transmission of Corona Virus.  Hands and surface washing has been recommended by WHO for controlling its spread. The present research is aimed to evaluate the antibacterial efficacy of various herbal extracts from Melia azedarach , Menta spp., Xanthozylum almatum, and Adhoca Vasica using different solvents and water. The anti-microbial activity of the formulated herbal hand wash gel will tested against selected bacterial strains by spread plate techniques and the results obtained will be compared with commercial antibacterial standards. The results will ensure the incorporation and utilisation of herbs in the formulations to give better effect for disinfecting the hands and other surfaces.

data.projectName: Establishment of Primers/Probes Synthesis Setup to Enhance the Indigenous Capability of Development and Production of Covid-19 Diagnostic tools and Vaccines
data.projectDigest: In the light of the emergence and spread of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) there is dire need of primers and probes to be used for the research purposes as well as diagnosis of the disease affected patients. PCR primers are short fragments of single stranded DNA that are complementary to the DNA sequences of flanking regions of target DNA. These primers are produced synthetically and main components of the molecular diagnostic kits and systems. As due to the COVID-19 pandemic spread all over the world all businesses of life have been affected and it is very difficult to purchase necessary items for testing including the primers and also very time consuming process which no country can afford at this testing time. DNA synthesizer is a machine which is used for the synthetic production of primers So this project has been designed to establish the setup for local production of DNA probes and primers at CAMB, University of the Punjab. Different research groups are trying their best to develop the testing kits for COVID-19 and this project will help all those groups in the timely availability of basic components of the kits. So the procuring of DNA synthesizer will be very vital to make the country self-sustainable in primer synthesis which will facilitate in the development and production of testing kits as well as vaccines and other research projects. This setup can help in future also to counter any new epidemic in time before its out of control spread. The amount exceeding the maximum limit of HEC will be provided by the University which has been agreed upon by the Worthy Vice Chancellor.

data.projectName: Use of Cholistani plants and synthetic drugs as antiviral agents against avian Corona and three other RNA poultry viruses
data.projectDigest: The study will be based on the antiviral evaluation of some Cholistani plants and indigenously made synthetic drugs at Department of Chemistry, The Islamia University of Bahawalpur. Twenty six plants from different families have already been screened against different poultry viruses including Avian Coronavirus strain Infectious Bronchitis (IB) in previous studies. All the plant extracts and synthetic drugs were tested through in ovo antiviral assay. No. of plant extracts and synthetic drugs were found effective against different poultry viruses including Avian Corona strain IB. Some drugs were also tested on live sick birds and found effective. Five drugs were active against New Castle disease virus (NDV) – Lasota strain, six were active against Avian Influenza virus (AIV) H9N2 strain and two were active against, IB Virus (IBV) from Corona family.  In current study, we will purify and test the principal antiviral agents through column chromatography, TLC and HPLC and structural identification will be done by GC/LC-MS and IFTR. All the natural and synthetic compounds will be tested through specific pathogen free (SPF) 9-11 days old chicken embryonated (CE) eggs. The quantification of viruses will be done through Hemagglutination (HA), Hemagglutination inhibition (HI), Indirect Hemagglutination (IHA) PCR/qRT-PCR techniques The IC50 of each active compound/fraction will be calculated. The most active compounds/fractions will be further used in vivo studies. After basic screening of these antiviral drugs, the selected drugs will be sent to Department of Medical Biology, University of Quebec at Trios-Riveres, Canada for antiviral testing against Covid-19 corona virus. All the drugs were also be tested in different pharmaceutical formulations like hand sanitizers, herbal tea

data.projectName: DIAGNOSTIC ACCURACY OF CHEST COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY (128 SLICE) FOR DIAGNOSIS OF CORONAVIRUS DISEASE-2019 TAKING REVERSE-TRANSCRIPTION POLYMERASE CHAIN REACTION AS GOLD STANDARD
data.projectDigest:
Recently an outbreak of novel coronavirus diseases 20019 i.e. (COVID-19) has spread quickly in Wuhan city of China1 and later in all over the globe as pandemic viral disease. Initially clinicians have focused on identifying and describing the clinical features, course and treating the patients.2   Confirmation of infection requires nucleic acid testing of respiratory tract samples (eg, throat swabs), but clinical diagnosis may be made based on symptoms, exposures, and chest imaging.3   At present, real-time reverse-transcription–polymerase-chain-reaction (RT-PCR) assay for COVID-19 has been developed and used in clinics. Although RT-PCR remains the Gold standard to make a definitive diagnose of COVID-19 infection4, the high false negative rate5 and unavailability of RT-PCR assay in the early stage of the outbreak restricted prompt diagnosis of infected patients.6
The current proposal is aimed to see the diagnostic accuracy of chest CT taking RT – PCR as gold standard as  in many settings CT is readily available while the provision of testing kit is not present at moment(as in many settings CT is readily available whereas RT-PCR testing kits are not available at present) . Moreover, CT is cost effective and has high diagnostic accuracy as found in literature. Hence, in current study if high diagnostic accuracy is found then in current scenario we can take help from CT to diagnose as early as possible. The early diagnosis can help the better prognosis of the patients.

data.projectName: Integrating Multipolar Sectors to Strengthen Biosafety, Biosecurity and Infection Prevention and Control to Fight COVID-19 Outbreak
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: COVID-19, a public health concern worldwide, has been observed a sever threat to health professionals. Developing countries like Pakistan where there is no Biosafety, Biosecurity and functional Infection Prevention & Control (IPC) programs, to tackle COVID-19 can cause high morbidity and mortality in health-care settings. Moreover, Pakistan’s health resources are not sufficient to tackle this disease burden. The doctor to patient ratio in 1:1000, which results in doctors dealing with more patients with limited resources. Any breach/gap in proper SOPs, guidelines can increase the risk of acquiring nosocomial infection. To achieve highest level of effectiveness and respond to COVID-19, multiple strategies and practices should be adopted. IPC program with a dedicated and trained team need to be in place.  In third world countries with limited or inexistence of IPC and biosafety, biosecurity programs minimum requirements need to be in place as soon as possible. For this purpose, a multipolar strategy where multidisciplinary experts will work under one roof to develop and implement guidelines and to train the health professionals as well which is front line force. IPC strategies will prevent or limit the transmissions in health care settings. This program aims to build strategic infection prevention and control (IPC), with an additional provision to health-care settings with a goal to help and improve protocols in infectious disease management, limit nosocomial transmission and support rational consumption of personal protective equipment.

data.projectName: Dynamical Aspects and Parametric Estimation of COVID-19 Outbreak in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
The COVID-19 has been confirmed to reach Pakistan in February 2020. As of April 2, 2020, there have been more than 2000 confirmed cases in the country, including 107 recoveries and 31 deaths. Punjab is currently the region where the highest number is over 800. Various regions across the country have imposed lockdown until early April to prevent the outbreak. They include Punjab, Sindh, Balochistan and Azad Kashmir, while in Gilgit-Baltistan self- isolation is imposed indefinitely. Keeping in view the COVID-19 outbreak in Pakistan, a discrete-time susceptible-exposed-infected-asymptotically infected-recovered (SEIAR) model is proposed. We discuss existence and dynamics of disease free and endemic fixed points for proposed model. We compare our theoretical results with observed data of Pakistan related to COVID-19 cases.
Keeping in view the present epidemic situation of world, it worthwhile to point out that mathematical modeling plays key role for prediction, implementation of control measures and the investigation of infection characteristics. This project deals with dynamical analysis of a novel discrete epidemic model for outbreak of COVID-19 and its comparison with observed data of Pakistan. Moreover, chaos control methods are applied to control irregular and fluctuating behavior of the model, which leads to implementation of realistic measures for control of COVID-19 outbreak.

Infect it is need of hour to build instruments for real time detection of coronavirus with accuracy.  The aim of this project is to develop new drugs and derivatives of the already existing antiviral drugs to increase their efficacy to combat with Covid-19.

data.projectName: Lab on a chip (LOC) based Simultaneous Diagnosis and Geo Mapping of Multiple Viral Infections.
data.projectDigest: According to the Ministry of National Health Services, the confirmed COVID-19 cases in Pakistan are now above 2000 with 26 deaths. Although the spread of COVID-19 in Pakistan is not at an alarming level compared to many developed countries, still the country is in a partial state of a health emergency. The two big challenges of Pakistan are limited diagnostic capability and information platform with real-time geo-mapping. The change in season may also result in the emergence of Dengue, Malaria and other infectious diseases. Pakistan ranks 149 in 188 countries in the first global assessment of the country's progress towards the UN health-related Sustainable Development Goals (SGDS) therefore need to adopt the next-generation IoT biomedical technology is urgent. In this project, we aim to develop Lab on a Chip (LOC) based simultaneous diagnosis and geo-mapping of multiple viral infections (COVID-19, Malaria, Dengue, and HIV) requiring urgent solutions both domestically and internationally. The project has two main objectives, first, to fabricate a reliable, cost-effective LOC based POC device for the on-site simultaneous diagnosis of multiple infections and second, geo-map the diagnostic data to identify hotspots and growth patterns, contact tracing modeling of affected people and initial assessment report generation.

data.projectName: DEVELOPMENT OF REAL TIME BASED RAPID AND COST EFFECTIVE DIAGNOSTIC ASSAYS FOR SARS COV2
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
COVID19 is a major threat globally and has been declared as a pandemic. The most effective way to confirm an individual being infected with the virus. Pakistan has already witnessed a huge shortage of diagnostics kits and we had to rely on external donors for the import of the diagnostic kits. The global demand of these diagnostic kits created a severe shortage of aforementioned kits thus making it difficult for the resource limited countries like Pakistan to cope up the demand. Thus there is a high demand of designing the indigenous assays for the detection of SARS CoV2. 
Our project aims to design most sensitive and target specific real time based diagnostic assays for the detection of the SARS CoV2. RT-PCR based testing is highly sensitive and specific technique which allows to detect viral RNA in infected individuals. This technique is not only cost effective but also saves time, allowing us to detect various SARS-COV-2 gene targets in a single reaction in less than 2 hours. We have already developed our assays and tested them on lab controls as well as initial 37 clinical samples. More comprehensive testing with larger sample cohort will be conducted during the grant fund time any improvements required during the testing on larger cohort will also be conducted. 
The designed project will thus not only serve a baseline for the establishment of indigenous diagnostic assays but will also be further commercialize after the approvals from the respective authorities to be used for the benefit of general public as well as making the kits of export quality. Thus the reliability on imported kits will be reduced. The project in the long term will establish a trained workforce to cope up the diagnostic requirements of the country to fight any unforeseen epidemic in future.

Only some of the data is backed by strong evidence, while the rest is misleading and exaggerated. These figures surfacing are giving birth to conspiracy theories, which have the tendency to cause harmful actions such as mis-allocation of resources, panic buying and lock-downs. It is the need of the hour to develop an Information Technology generated tool capable of managing and authenticating the mass data ad developing high evidence standards.

data.projectName: Molecular understanding of COVID-19 response in Pakistani Population by using Metabolomic and Proteomic Approaches
data.projectDigest: Under this project we have developed a consortium of interdisciplinary scientist from two premier institution including clinicians that are involved in handling COVID-19 Patients. This project will focus on the understanding of the pathogen-host interactions of COVID-19 in Pakistani population by analyzing the serum samples of case control study comprising of COVID-19 patients, in the viremia phase, in the acute phase, and in the recovery phase along with age and gender-matched healthy controls. This project comprises in three parts, First part (PI and his team responsibility) will focus on the comprehensive metabolomic and proteomic analysis using advanced mass spectrometry tools. Second part (Co-PI-1 and her team responsibility) will explore the immune response of Pakistani population against COVID-19 by the analysis of cytokines and chemokines interferon and TLRs. Third part (Co-PI-II and her team responsibility) will focus on the repurposing of FDA approved drugs for their anti-inflammatory potential against those cytokines/ chemokines which will show strong association with COVID19 and identified in the second part of the project through in-vitro screening. Outcome of the project will be useful to understand the pathogenesis of COVID-19 at the molecular level and the immune response of Pakistani population which will highly beneficial and helpful to open up new ways to design therapeutic and detection strategies against COVID-19 infections.

data.projectName: COVID-19 AND MENTAL HEALTH IN PAKISTAN
data.projectDigest:
Covid-19 is having notable effects on the health of the people of Pakistan and is bound to also have significant psychosocial ramifications, especially for mental health. It has been documented that epidemics/pandemics trigger much wider psychological epidemics. As the number of people who sicken and die increases, and the economic losses associated with Covid-19 add up, the risks to our population’s mental health increase, and the damage is likely to continue even after the infection subsides. Therefore, a grounded understanding of the psychosocial impact of Covid-19 is crucial, which can then become the basis of mitigation activities. 

This nationwide study aims to examine the Covid-19-related psychosocial vulnerability and mental health issues among different population groups across gender, age, and socioeconomic status. The participants for the study will include the general public, Covid-19 survivors and their families, as well as members of response teams working during this emergency. Both quantitative and qualitative methods of data collection will be utilized. The study will be conducted by a research team (PI, Co-PIs, Research Associates) and supervised by a “Guidance and Supervisory Group” (GSG) comprising eminent Psychologist/s, Sociologist/s, Anthropologist/s, and Economist/s.

data.projectName: SCOP: Surveillance of CoVid19 in Pakistan using Machine Learning
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest: The proposed project is focused on providing critical real time data about the infected patients from the remote districts of Pakistan using digital technology and machine learning; we will be able to strengthen the routine infectious disease surveillance system for efficient and timely management of infectious disease as COVID-19 . The first phase of the project will involve SCOP (Surveillance of COVID19 in Pakistan) application development, for obtaining and organizing, all relevant data and developing a COVID19 prediction model, through machine learning (neural network/deep learning methods) using the online daily reported data from Pakistan . The developed model will be tested by splitting the online data into training and testing sets, before being applied to the real time data collected through the SCOP application. The second phase of the project will involve piloting the SCOP application in one of the hospital settings at Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and applying the prediction models to the real time data collected. Third phase will involve scaling up the SCOP application and prediction models to at least 3 major hospitals in Peshawar. Weekly graphs, trends and numbers will be presented and predictions made for the upcoming weeks. Secondary analysis, to study the risk factors/predictors associated with COVID19 morbidity and mortality, will be conducted. Findings of the project will be presented regularly on the dedicated website, publicly accessible, and results will be disseminated to the relevant stakeholders through conducting online workshops.

data.projectName: Preventive and Prophylaxis Management against COVID -19.
data.projectDigest:
First case of COVID -19 was reported as novel corona virus in the city of Wuhan, China in December 2019. Despite the lockdown of the city  the epidemic spread rapidly. WHO declared it as an pandemic on 11th March, 2020. Symptoms of COVID-19 are cough, fever, fatigue, body ache, nausea, vomiting. It may progress to  severity of pneumonia and multiple organ failures.
Thus it is highly contagious frequent washing of hands with soap, avoid touching face,wearing gloves, mask, cleaning surfaces with disinfectants. Also personnel preventive equipment is most required when attending to corona virus infected patient. Also quarantine and isolation is important when infected for at least 14 days. 
Diagnostic test for this are RT-PCR( similar to SARS and MER ) Other more swift testing is developed by Abbott and other pharmaceutical companies. 
Treatment options are various antiviral agent which have been under consideration along with the anti malarial drugs (Choloroquine/ Hydroxycholoroquine) along with antibiotic ( azithromycin) are under trials . The plasma antibodies of recovered patients are also being induced into severely ill patients to provide them with passive immunity. In this pandemic the Doctors, paramedic and nurses are highly at risk of  getting infected and prophylactic or empirical trials have to be conducted.

data.projectName: Empirical and In-silico Identification of antiviral activities of natural compounds from Pakistani and Chinese traditional medicines against SARS-COV-2 to treat COVID-19
data.projectDigest: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) caused by Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Corona virus 2 (SARS-COV-2) was first diagnosed in December 2019, Wuhan, China. Till April 2, 2020, 956,778 COVID-19 cases have been confirmed globally, including 75,303 new cases and 2450 cases infected this deadly virus in Pakistan.  Currently, no vaccine and antiviral drug available to cure COVID-19. Medicinal plantsfrom Pakistan and Chinese Herbal medicine (CHM) have traditionally been used to treat number of diseases and ailments for centuries. Medicinal plant consists of secondary metabolites such as alkaloids, polyphenolics, glycosides, lectins, terpenes, steroids and saponins, flavonoids, tannins, coumarines, saponins etc which can be used for treating COVID-19. The present study is designed to find out potent, safe and effective drugs which have antiviral activity against SARS-COV-2 Spike and Main Protease. The finding of this study may be used for the treatment and prevention COVID-19

data.projectDigest:
COVID-19 is now a day’s pandemic disease spread all over the world. It affects 190 different countries and the death rate is increasing day by day. The people of Pakistan, which is an under develop country posses limited research facilities and grants as well are also suffering from this lethal disease.
 This chronic disease basically affect lungs of a healthy human body leads to pneumonia and in some cases cause death if it becomes severe, so it needs the development of drugs which may be used for the treatment or prophylactic use of COVID-19. Up till now no vaccine is being synthesized in any laboratory so it is a basic need to prepare any useful and effective drugs for the treatment of COVID-19. Chloroquine and hydroxy Chloroquine with the combination of azithromycin is now been approved by FDA for the treatment of this disease. Chloroquine is the drug used for malaria and it is not antiviral drug, but it showed therapeutic efficacy against COVID-19, but precautions should be exercised when making premature interpretations, as clinical trials are still ongoing and interim trial data have not been yet made available. It becomes accumulate in food vacuole where it is thought to prevent pH-dependent detoxification of heme, produced by parasitic consumption of haemoglobin to free amino acids. Speculation on Chloroquine-induced anti viral effects includes inhibition of pH-dependent viral fusion replication and prevention of viral

data.projectName: Economic Impact Assessment of COVID 19 on Pakistan Economy
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.theme: Information Collection and Dissemination IT platforms)
data.projectDigest: Agriculture is backbones of Pakistan economy by contributing 19 percent in GDP and provision of raw material for agrobased industry. Along with the impact of COVID19 on different sectors of the economy, it badly affects the agriculture sector of the economy.  During lockdown period, input supply to the agriculture production system is adversely affected as agriculture production system is segregated system involving majority of the rural households. due to nonavailability of transportation, output was not able to reach in the hands of consumer. prices also fell down due to consumer consciousness. In urban areas prices of commodities were also affected adversely. This study is planned to analyse impact of COVID19 on livelihood of farming community and ultimately on Pakistan economy. Primary data of 500 farming families from four provinces will be collected through well-defined questionnaire prepared after consultation with all the stakeholders in the field. Data will be analysed for estimation of impact of COVID19 on livelihood typologies o the farming community. This data will provide baseline for macroeconomic study using CGE modelling framework for analyzing impact of COVID19 on Pakistan economy. For macroeconomic study GTAP version 10 database will be used for CGE modelling. Results of the study will provide important policy guidelines for rehabilitation of economy at micro and macro level and developing a national mitigation strategy.

data.projectName: Exploring the potential of antiviral agents to inhibit Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) replication
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: In this project, we will evaluate potential antiviral agents, both synthetic and natural products/extracts, against SARS-CoV-2 in cell culture model. A set of heterocyclic compounds from thiazolide class will be evaluated against SARS-CoV-2 due to their broad-spectrum antiviral activity. FDA-approved anti-HCV drugs sofosbuvir, daclatasvir, ciluprevir and asunaprevir will be evaluated due to their interesting docking interactions against SARS-CoV-2 protease (6LU7). Moreover, a large number of flavonoid/ phenolic docked against SARS-CoV-2 protease (6LU7), compounds, i.e. gallic acid 3-O-gallate, 5-O-galloylquinic acid, gallocatechins, dicaffeoylquinic acid, diferuloylquinic acid, 2-S-glutathionyl caftaric acid, methylrosmarinate, 6,8-dihydroxykaempferol, quercetin, quercetin 3-O-galactoside 7-O-rhamnoside, apigenin arabinoside-glucoside, myricetin glycoside, naringin, baicalin, silybinic acid, procyanidin dimer, theaflavin 3' 3-O-digallate, ellagitannins sanguiin H-6,  punicalagin and glycyrrhizin demonstrate good inhibition potential. Extracts containing such compounds will be analyzed using LCMS/MS and evaluated against SARS-CoV-2 in vitro using BSL-3 facility at DESTO-Karachi and/or at BSL-4 facility being built at NIBGE. Extracts exhibiting good activity, indigenous availability in bulk and having acceptable safety profile will be identified. Active FDA-approved drugs and extracts will be recommended for trials, while synthetic compounds will be further investigated. Industrial collaborator will help in formulation, registration and bulk-scale production. Hopefully, these efforts will help to identify antiviral agents for desperate masses.

data.projectName: SAFE ADN EFFECTIVE HERBAL FORMULATION FOR PREVENTION AND TREATMENT OF CORONAVIRUS (COVID-19)
data.projectDigest: The recent outbreak of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) in the Chinese city Wuhan, caused by SARS-CoV-2 raised global health concerns. Chloroquine contains quinoline pharmacophore which occurs in several natural compounds and synthetic derivatives displaying a broad range of biological activity. Because of the urgent need of the medicine for the COVID-19 patients it is not possible to synthesize the new molecules to treat the dying population. It is observed that medicinal plants have been the source of countless medicinal compounds and leads for drug discovery and can be successfully used against COVID-19. Recently China has approved glycyrrhizinate an ingredient of liquorice roots to control COVID-19. Another rich tradition of herbal medicine Rhubarb in China is also tested against COVID-19. Siberian biologist suggest using dyer's woad (Isatistinctoria/ Isatisindigotica) as a complex measure for the prevention and treatment of COVID-19. In the present project we will prepare the evidence-based formulation using natural product(s) for the treatment of the COVID-19. Molecular mechanisms of the active compounds will be established, and dose will be optimized using the clinical patients. The project will be the accelerated joint activity of the natural product, formulation designing scientists and clinical experts involved in treatment of the COVID-19 patients and biologists.

data.projectName: Rapid Prototyping of RNA Vaccines using local viral genomes and computer-aided design
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest: In this project we propose the use of computer-aided design and real-time DNA sequencing of SARS-CoV-2 samples from Pakistani patients to identify the exact strains prevailing the country and how their sequence is evolving, use computational analysis methods to identify the best candidates for RNA-based vaccines that can easily be fabricated at scale under GMP conditions in cell-free systems and immediately taken into pre-clinical trials in animal models.

data.projectName: Plasma Immune Marker Protein Profile Expression of COVID-19 patients and survivors
data.projectDigest:
COVID-19 patients and survivors blood profiling may give a way to virologists to develop vaccine or diagnostic kit because the goal in vaccination is to replicate the body's natural immune response to viruses. Many researchers worldwide have just started to see distinct immune-cell populations and other active immune marker proteins in the COVID-19 patient's blood who recovered. Currently, very limited data and there is only one diagnostic RT-PCR test is available, however for treatment management, in Pakistan and other countries, debate is going on to transfused convalescent plasma for the purpose treatment in current COVID-19 patients. This is not a new idea, in 2005 three patients with SARS in Taiwan were treated with 500 mL convalescent serum, resulting in a reduction in serum virus titer, and each survived [10].
The problem in this procedure, at the time of onset of diseases we have to wait for the patients to recovered and after 2-3 weeks their discharge, contact them for voluntary donation of their plasma with consent. Moreover, the donors will be considered when the nucleic acid test / viral RNA detection by RT-PCR of the sample taken from the respiratory tract remains negative. Moreover, there is one also mandatory step required which proper blood donation screening (HBsAg, Anti-HCV, AntiHIV, Syphilis and Malaria) and then one can start the Apheresis procedures. Therefore, current proposal is aim to identify some immune markers proteins in patients and survivors which can linger long after COVID-19 infection has faded. After identification of some potential markers, serological test can be done for validation of findings which could be cheaper and faster than RT-PCR.

data.projectName: Contagious Spread of Covid-19 in Pakistan: An Investigation for Capacity Building by SEIR(Susceptible-Exposed-Infectious-Removed) Framework
data.projectDigest: The ongoing major disease (COVID-19) that put the health in huge threat reported by China. It was originated in the end of 2019 in Wuhan, where it has claimed more than 3200 by corona virus. In Pakistan the contagious spread of this disease was in the February, 2020 where it has claimed 2445 cases on April 3rd, 2020. The government of Pakistan has adopted precautionary measures to control the contagious spread of COVID-19 i.e. hospitalization, lockdown, isolation, quarantine (social distancing). The general public reacts both negatively and positively towards the precautionary measures of government. They face a lot of problems like frustration and boredom, inadequate supplies, fear of infection, inadequate information, strict travel restrictions, closure of educational and non-educational institutes, loss in economy of country. The basic purpose to conduct this research is to investigate; how government and general public of Pakistan can be able to build their capacity by formulating efficient and effective control. In this research study, we adapt “Susceptible-Exposed-Infectious-Removed (SEIR)” framework. The structure of model is concise and captures the course of COVID-19 contagious spread successfully, and thus sheds light on understanding the trends of the outbreak along other variables.

data.projectName: Early diagnosis and monitoring of COVID-19 pneumonia using “COVID 19 Pneumonia Diagnostic System (CPDS)
data.projectDigest:
Non-availability of early-stage detection and monitoring system for COVID-19 acquired pneumonia in remote areas and quarantine centres in the cities still a challenge for healthcare staff. Therefore, there is a high need for such a device which could detect COVID-19 pneumonia in the early stage especially in remote areas and monitoring affected patients during their treatment.
Despite health care technology advancement, still, there is no device available in the market which could detect COVID-19 pneumonia in the early stage or monitor the severity level of disease among patients except expensive and time-consuming blood tests and monitoring equipment. Therefore a device will be developed which will be accurate, affordable and user-friendly to assist health care staff for COVID-19 pneumonia diagnosis or monitoring the patient’s condition. The proposed device will develop an innovative intelligent system COVID-19 Penumonia Diagnostic System (CPDS) using vital sign parameters (pulse oximetry (SPO2), heart rate, Blood Pressure (BP), respiratory rate (RR) and temperature) to diagnose COVID-19 pneumonia.
Ziauddin University will develop device hardware whereas Coventry University will develop software and will carried-out clinical trials. This innovative system will support government efforts to reduce the public mortality rate especially in remote areas of Pakistan. The hospital will get less risk and burden of COVID -19 pneumonia patients due to remote diagnosis, monitoring and treatment.

data.projectName: Stem Cell Therapy:Treatment of COVID-19 Through Mesenchymal Cells
data.projectDigest: In Covid-19, Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) and pulmonary fibroses is a life-threatening inflammatory lung condition associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) due to their immunomodulatory properties are increasingly being studied for the treatment of ARDS and have shown promise in multiple studies. The therapeutic effects of MSCs are exerted in part in a paracrine manner by releasing extracellular vesicles (EVs), rather than local engraftment. MSC-derived EVs are emerging as potential alternatives to MSC therapy in ARDS. In this review, we will introduce EVs and MSCs in ARDS which is caused by Covid-19 in severe cases.
