data.projectName: Molecular docking analysis of potential antiviral compounds from selected spices and in-vitro studies of the targeted compounds/ extracts against 2019-nCoV
data.projectDigest:
In context to public health response this proposal needs rapid activation. Because, it targets to screen potential compounds from different spices (black cumin seeds, turmeric, cloves, cinnamon, ginger, garlic) to fight off this continue threatening and spreading virus, 2019-nCov. Through preliminary computational study, non-structural proteins of the virus will be targeted to check out potential of bioactive compounds of above-mentioned spices through MOE. The potential compounds will be studied for their effectiveness against this virus by in-vitro analysis.
The compounds showing high binding energy or inhibitory potential might be considered good candidates against this threatening and highly infectious 2019-nCoV. 
In-vitro efficiency of screened compounds will be tested by two ways: 1. Compounds will be purchased, 2. Phenolic/ethanolic/water and oil extracts of the spices will be formed depending upon presence of potential compounds. Antiviral capacity will be checked against each viral-expressed-proteins in HEK293 cell lines. The concentration of compounds will be optimized by cytotoxic assays.  Compounds minimizing viral expression might bring into market after in-vivo trials. Major outcome of this proposed study will be achieved by inhibitory expression of viral proteins by extracts/oils of these spices. These extracts/oils can be promptly used as anti-2019-covid therapy simply by taking steam.

data.projectName: Combating health-related misinformation during the COVID-19 pandemic
data.theme: Information Collection and Dissemination IT platforms)
data.projectDigest: Corona is a new virus that has infected more than 1 million people within 3 months and killed over 50,000 patients. Given the rapid progress in mobile technology, we no longer depend upon government run television and radio channel to get our news. Platforms like Facebook and Twitter have become the mainstream source of information for general public. Unfortunately, Facebook and Twitter posts are unregulated and are shown to spread misinformation and chaos amongst public. We will study the manner in which general public of Pakistan is interacting with social media platform using a step-wise approach using techniques of ‘netnography’. Netnography is a technique of modern research that allows researchers to examine how human interact and form an understanding of any phenomenon through internet. Once we have identified trends of public interaction with Facebook and Twitter, and the extent of misinformation, we will present our findings to various groups of stakeholders from the government and non-governmental organisations, health professionals, academicians, and general members of the public to develop a set of recommendations to prevent the spread of misinformation about Corona virus. Our research will help government to inform general public about Corona virus in a safe and effective manner.

data.projectName: Assessment of stool and serosurveillance- creating evidence base for better diagnosis
data.projectDigest:
In the month of December 2019, first case of Corona virus disease 2019, which is caused by Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus-2 was observed in China. The virus soon become unstoppable and the WHO called it a pandemic due to its uncontained and sustained spread across multiple geographies. 
The biggest worry now is that SARS-CoV-2 can ravage countries with frailer health care systems like Pakistan with a population of more than 200 million. Highly congested urban populations provide multiple seeding opportunities for the virus to accelerate and gain a foothold. 
One of the lessons learn from the countries facing biggest epidemic of COVID-19 such as China, Italy, Spain and the United States of America is to increase diagnostic capacity in a short period of time. Here we propose a study to test the alternate diagnostic methods for COVID-19. The objectives of this study are  
1.	To assess the sensitivity of stool testing and its comparison with routine diagnostic methods based on nasopharyngeal swabs
2.	To test the efficacy of serodiagnostic method for COVID-19 and its comparison with routine diagnostic methods based on nasopharyngeal swabs

data.projectName: Improving outcomes for people in mental health crisis: A rapid response to mitigate the psychological impacts of quarantine and beyond in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
data.projectDigest:
"Effective crisis management does not start with the critical incident response. It encompasses four integrated phases: preparedness, prevention and mitigation, response, and recovery." (Reeves, Brock, & Cowan, 2008)
The December, 2019 coronavirus disease outbreak has seen many countries ask people who have potentially come into contact with the infection to isolate themselves at home or in a dedicated quarantine facility. According to a recent study from medical journal The Lancet that the psychological effects including confusion, anxiety and anger to sleep disturbances, depression and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Given the developing situation with coronavirus, higher education organizations urgently need to responds to the needs and produce guidance for the public. In circumstances such as these, rapid response to mental health concerns are recommended by WHO.

The proposed project is an attempt to respond to these unprecedented situations and the psychological impacts these can have on people. Our society is facing mass quarantine and shut downs for the first time and the social isolation are affecting people in unforeseen ways. Therefore this study is a rapid response to the unpredicted circumstances the pandemic has thrown in our face. Effective coping strategies will be proposed, regarding mental health interventions in khybar Pakhtunkhwa. The outcome of this action research will be greatly helpful for individuals, community and for the government which is panicked how to deliver.

data.projectName: In- vitro inhibition of coronavirus through screening of traditionally used medicinal herbal/plant extracts
data.projectDigest: Coronaviruses cause acute and chronic respiratory, enteric, and central nervous system disease in many species of animals, including humans (Weiss & Navas-Martin, 2005). Moreover, vaccines have not proven any effective in protecting against this novel infection due to the highly recombinant nature of the virus. More efficient methods of viral prevention or treatment are clearly needed. Plant extracts may be a potential source of agents for defending against COVID-19. Historically, plant extracts have been widely used to treat various medical conditions. The use of plant extracts as an alternative or supplementary COVID-19 treatment or prevention strategy has not been extensively investigated. Secondly, the use of these extracts or the active ingredients from these extracts for long-term treatment or prevention strategies poses some toxicity concerns. These concerns, combined with the difficulties often encountered when translating in vitro research into in vivo treatments], suggest that in vitro identification of a number of different antiviral plants for future in vivo studies is important. Keeping in view the need of solution for these problems, the study is designed as an effort to search for a coronavirus specific therapy. In this study, we will screen 10 traditionally used medicinal extracts for their ability to reduce the virus in MHV-A59-infected mouse DBT cells. data.projectName: Artificial Intelligence Surveillance System for Infectious Disease (COVID-19) in Karachi (AISS-K): An integration of Healthcare and Spatial datasets
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest: Effective infectious disease control heavily relies on precise disease surveillance systems. Strong city or district level mapping systems will form the basis of an effective nationwide surveillance and control of communicable diseases. Presently, the world has witnessed coronavirus disease 2019 [COVID-19] causing global pandemics.  Karachi city is one of the major cities of world where major chunk of population is living in unplanned areas that are densely populated. In current scenario, no disease surveillance system exists in the city or even in the province that integrates health care unit data with spatial databases e.g., geographical location, culture, environmental setting, living patterns etc.  It is envisioned that the advancement of AI methods for infectious disease Big Data analytics encompassing geographical data could improve our ability to observe public response on disease outbreaks and to predict disease diffusion accurately, which can help authorities to take timely response measures to control infectious diseases such as COVID-19. The project will be carried out in four phases, viz.; a) Data collection b) Analysis of data using AI and BigData approaches c) Development of Surveillance system for each district of Karachi and d) Implementation of the system.

data.projectName: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle based spraying system for the control of epidemic disease COVID-19
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.theme: Indigenous manufacture of Low cost Intensive-care equipment
data.projectDigest: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle systems (UAVs) are presently in limited use for the efficient control of epidemic diseases globally. Usage and advancement of civil unmanned Aerial Vehicle systems in Pakistan presently lags behind military Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) technology advancement because of uncertain regulatory and technical concerns. Civilian usage of UAVs have prospective to boost emergency efforts and efficient disaster management. Finest design of UAV spraying system for such epidemic disasters will lead to such unmanned spraying vehicles which deliver supreme possible efficiency and uniformity for emergency assistance and relief response while tackling public safety distresses and regulatory requirements. A case study is proposed that establishes usage of a civil unmanned spraying system to a disaster relief mission with the intent on the efficient control of COVID-19. The concept locally design and utilizes unmanned vehicle for the fast spraying of disinfectant at optimal height under which virus can dangle in the air, roads or surfaces. Currently, UAVs based disinfectant is under rare application in the advanced countries for efficient agriculture pesticide, herbicide and insecticide disinfection.

data.projectName: Molecular phylogenetic study of bat fauna and Identification of COVID-19 in some selected areas of Pakistan”
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Benazir Bhutto University, Sheringal, Dir
data.projectDigest:
Bats are comprised of more than 1200 species worldwide that constitute 20% mammalian fauna of the world. They are distributed everywhere except few places like Antarctica and some isolated Oceanic Islands. They are broadly divided into two sub orders microchiroptera and megachiroptera. Microchiroptera are the insectivores bats while megachiroptera are the fuigivores bats. Bat fauna of Indian Sub-continent is comprised of 119 species belonging to 37 genera and 8 families. Pakistan bat fauna is rich and comparable to the sub-continent bat fauna which is comprised of 52 bat species belonging to 25 genera and 8 families. It constitutes 28% of the mammalian fauna of the country. Bats are gregarious living as colonies in the trees, tree cavities, old buildings, crevices of walls, ceiling of the floors, tree foliage, caves and mines. They are almost living close or in the human  
made infrastructures. Therefore, some time they directly come in contact with human population. In Pakistan bats are not thoroughly studied yet and they still need a detail survey for additional species. According to Walker and Molur additional species are expected in the country. Therefore, there is a dire need to explore as much as maximum bat species in the country. Tradionally, bats were identified on the basis of morphological features, while in the recent days molecular phylogentic analysis are the most accurate techniques to identify species in majority of animal fauna. Therefore in this project bats will be identified on the basis of their molecular phylogeny. These additional species will help us to fill the remaining gaps in the bat fauna of the country and will be used as source for other studies as well. No, doubt bats play most important ecological role such as biological control or pest

data.projectName: COVERS: COvid-19 Virus Expert Recommender System
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest: We propose to build a recommendation system that will utilize the data and ICT platforms and equip people, health workers and government organizations to better deal with this epidemic. The proposed solution will be composed of three modules and will directly address two thematic areas including: development of infectious diseases surveillance systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence, and information collection and dissemination IT platforms. The first module will use a data driven approach to understand the disease prevalence and spread. The module will integrate location services and mine data from social networks to identify the disease hotspots and people and communities who are most at risk to contract the virus. The second module will analyse lung images and speech signals, obtained using computed tomography and mobile phones respectively. The hypothesis here is that segmenting pathological lung tissue and evaluating speech signals could help in an early identification and diagnosis of this disease. The third module will follow the structure of a telehealth platform, but here the system will give its users appropriate recommendation to deal with conditions which could lead to COVID-19 infection.

data.projectName: Rapid metagenomic MinION sequencing for accurate characterization of clinical nasopharyngeal swabs from SARS-C0V2 infected patients
data.projectDigest: Disease outcome of Covid-9 might be dictated by the presence of co-infections of viral and bacterial pathogens in the respiratory tract of the patients. These co-infections are often missed out because the focus of diagnostics is on Covid-19 and are not fully characterized in perspective of Covid-19. Currently, the serological screening kits confirm the seropositivity of the patients but do not tell about the active SARS-CoV2 infection in the patients. Also target specific kits do not encompass the co-infections which can potentially complicate the outcome of Covid-19. Therefore, it is very critical to rapidly detect and genetically characterize the evolving SARS-CoV2 as well as the co-infecting pathogens in SARS-CoV2 infected patients. Current project is proposed to use a random antigen detection MinION sequencing approach which could target the entire population of microbes in the clinical respiratory samples form COVID-19 positive patients as the use of metagenomic approaches will likely also provide a check on sequence divergence. This is particularly important for SARS-CoV-2 as the virus could undergo recombination with other human coronaviruses and may also affect both vaccine and antiviral efficacy. Therefore, a rapid, sensitive and simple diagnostic approach will be much valuable to the effective control of this outbreak.

This is particularly important for SARS-CoV-2 as the virus could undergo recombination with other human coronaviruses and may also affect both vaccine and antiviral efficacy. Therefore, a rapid, sensitive and simple diagnostic approach will be much valuable to the effective control of this outbreak.

data.projectName: Indigenous Development of a Scalable Ventilator using Proportional Electro-pneumatics
data.theme: Indigenous manufacture of Low cost Intensive-care equipment
data.projectDigest: It is aimed to indigenously develop a reliable and scalable ventilator system using electro-pneumatics in the context of current COVID-19 outbreak. The existing efforts in low-cost development of ventilators, locally and internationally, lack the requisite reliability which is vital for such biomedical equipment. The limitations include overheating of motors resulting from long operation of resuscitation efforts, noisy and often erroneous sensed data and uncertainties emanating from using lab-grade components, to name a few. Therefore, the proposed system uses solenoid-operated electropneumatic valves to reliably actuate double-acting cylinders with automatic control of tidal volume and breathing-frequencies. The switching of cylinder-position is further interlocked with the pressure sensor to increase the reliability. It is also aimed to make such system scalable where one controller and supply can serve multiple units, unlike the existing approaches such as using splitter-valves. Moreover, the system is controlled by industrial-grade programmable logic controller (PLC) which is supported by a user interface (HMI).

Tracking the contact interactions of individuals can effectively early identify the secondary infections and isolate them thereby reducing the rate of disease spreading. However these contacts are hidden. In this proposal we aim to apply artificial intelligence methods to accurately identify these contacts .

data.projectName: Indigenous Development of Portable Narrow Spectrum-UVC Disinfectant Device for restricting spread of Infectious Disease
data.theme: Indigenous manufacture of Low cost Intensive-care equipment
data.projectDigest:
The coronavirus (covid-19) has affected about 1 Million people in the world so far
and total death toll has reached about 50,000.  Experts have warned that the death toll may rise to millions in the current pandemic. Researchers have also estimated that the overall antimicrobial-resistant infections can result in 10 million deaths each year by 2050.

The World Health Organization (WHO) suggests keeping your hands and surfaces clean by washing with soap and water or by using appropriate disinfectants. However, Soap and liquid disinfectants may not be an appropriate solution in all situations, because virus can be anywhere, such as on door handles, laptops, mobile phones, books, currency or vehicles.

The Ultraviolet (or UV-C) light is a reliable source of disinfection from micro-organism. The UVC is being used for sterilization of water, air and surfaces. However, the exposure of conventional UVC light to living organism can be harmful. For example, it can damage the eyes and burn the skin. 

The standard germicidal wavelength of 254nm is harmful to the fragile layer of the skin. Recent studies have shown that a narrow spectrum of UV light ranging 207nm to 222 nm, can effectively kill the pathogens without harming the skin or eyes. 

In this research, we will design and develop a portable, handheld narrow spectrum UV disinfectant device The proposed device shall consist of far-UVC (207-254 nm) illumination source, optical reflector, UV filter and rechargeable battery. This product will provide narrow spectrum - UVC technology in a handheld, portable,  rechargeable and affordable solution, that is safe and convenient for hand or body disinfection and may be utilized in everyday common place settings.

data.projectName: Rapid detection of RNA based virus (coronavirus) using real time RT-micro-PCR and MD studies of genetic modification of RNA based viruses
data.projectDigest: The rapid spread of coronavirus requires a fast, efficient and real time detection of virus. Covid-19 is a RNA based virus, which requires a host to replicate itself. The project envisages the understanding of interaction of virus with cells and proteins at the atomic and molecular level. It also aims to develop real time micro PCR device with capability to amplify the viral DNA and detect it efficiently. The device will be portable and can be used remotely with multiple testing ability.

data.projectName: A comparative analysis on the effects of virtual versus traditional class room on student’s satisfaction.
data.piUniversity: Preston Institute of Management, Science and Technology, Karachi
data.theme: Information Collection and Dissemination IT platforms)
data.projectDigest:
As universities and colleges increasingly embrace new technologies and leverage them not only to enhance their traditional curriculums but also to extend course offerings beyond the college campus, opportunities for increased student-faculty interaction have been created.

The traditional approach of face-to-face office hours has been shown in previous studies to be infrequently used by students, who cite lack of convenience or accessibility as the main deterrents (Pascarella 1980; Nadler and Nadler 2000). 
Hooper, Pollanen, and Teismann (2006) found that virtual office hours increased effectiveness and participation of students enrolled in an online introductory mathematics course. 
Hence, there is a need for a research study to compare the effects of a virtual versus traditional classroom valuable on student satisfaction.

data.projectName: EFFECT OF HCQ PROPHALAXIS IN FRONTLINE HEALTHCARE WORKERS IN RWP
data.projectDigest: Covid 19 cases are progressively increasing in Pakistan placing a great risk and demand on frontline health workers . Todate 1870 patients have tested positive in Pakistan and expected to have a steep upward slope.The public sector university in Rawalpindi RMU is a major screening centre. Personal protective equipment has had variable failures in protecting health care providers in Italy and globally including Pakistan. Hydroxychloroquine is being used in primary/secondary prophylaxis with con?icting evidence worldwide. The bene?ts of primary prophylaxis of FHW with daily HCQ use at 200 mgs daily is unknown. Therefore we propose a pragmatic randomized trial of HCQ 200 mgs daily versus placebo for 3 months in FHW at RMU to determine differences in timing and appearance of symptoms with positive RT PCR for covid 19 in FHW. The alternate hypothesis is that HCQ will be superior to placebo in protecting FHW. Primary outcome measure will be a decrease in symptomatic and con?rmed Covid positive cases in HCQ limb. Secondary outcomes will include adverse drug reactions and adverse events. Study will be a 1:1 parallel arm pragmatic trial. Randomization shall be in permuted blocks. Study would be triple blinded with allocation concealment and intention to treat analysis

data.projectName: Molecular epidemiology of COVID-19 in pets, livestock and their owners in Punjab, Pakistan.
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: The novel coronavirus disease commonly known as COVID-19 is a severe and deadly viral disease of respiratory system affecting the lungs causing pneumonia in humans. It was first originated in Wuhan, China in December 2019 and spread across continents all over the world affecting hundreds and thousands of people. Many studies have been reported regarding epidemiological disease modelling of COVID-19 in human. Meanwhile few studies have also reported the presence of COVID-19 in dogs, cats and common housed animals in present pandemic. These reports raised the serious concern in the present pandemic whether the COVID-19 is transmissible to humans from animals or animals to animals. Pakistan is an agriculture state and mainly depends on the livestock industry. In this regard the present study is designed to provide the epidemiological baseline data of COVID-19 in livestock, pets and the owners of these animals. The samples from pets, livestock and their owner with specific history of symptoms will be collected, transported to laboratory and will be processed and anayzed for COVID-19. The present study will also be helpful in finding the correlation of disease transmission from animal species to humans in present scenario.

data.projectName: Investigating and modelling the immune patterns of COVID-19 in response to localised climatic factors in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Environmental scientists have played key roles in protecting the general public from viral illnesses by carrying out climate-disease investigations. In order to work on the overall goal of this proposal, which is to “flatten the curve” of the coronavirus pandemic in Pakistan, it is imperative that the immune mechanisms of COVID-19 infections and recovery be investigated in relation to the local climatic factors including the most important one – temperature. This is a novel virus and much needs to be studied, including epidemiology, at the local and regional scales in order to ensure disease prevention and management. During the colder months, our immune system is lowered due to the fact that our bodies lack in vitamin D, which the sun helps generate and which is an immune-system booster.
One major national challenge is to swiftly curtail the spread of COVID-19 and to build immune mechanisms. This proposal will address a major challenge of disease communication under local climatic factors, primarily temperature. This research will be conducted at national level by focussing on all local areas of disease prevalence and potential areas of future spread. There is also evidence that the spread of SARS-CoV-2 Coronavirus is likely to be constrained by climate.

data.projectName: National Action Plan In Wake Of Covid-19 Outbreak in Preparedness And Response: Pre Vs Post Cases Arrival  “Gap Analysis”
data.projectDigest:
In the wake of current COVID-19 spread, each country took various measures including screening of international passengers at airport, establishment of quarantine centers and isolation, screening of symptomatic, contact tracing etc. The Govt of Pakistan took immediate measures to prevent this infection and its spread in the country and national action plan was prepared and got some early success in preventing massive spread of the disease. However, with arrival COVID-19 cases in the country some shortcomings were observed at policy and implementation levels, both at national and provincial levels: resulting in spread of the disease in the country. Therefore, it is important to assess the strength and weakness of this national action plan.
This study shall provide insight about the weakness and strengths of the national action plan to combat the COVID-19 crisis and shall strengthen Pakistan’s capacity to develop best action plans for the timely preparedness and comprehensive response on any unseen outbreaks/pandemics in future. This shall eventually help to save socioeconomic resources and to reduce national morbidity and mortality rates.

data.projectName: Development of Smart Body Temperature Sensor and Pandemic Hotspot Detection through Machine Learning
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest: The proposed project will contribute towards early diagnostics and in some cases, pre-warnings of the COVID-19 pandemic hotspot areas. The accurate measurement of human body temperature, which is a prerequisite of reliable COVID-19 screening, will be made possible through the contactless handheld devices. The temperature sensing can be augmented with related body conditions. The augmented information will include geotagged data of the suspected patients. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) based algorithms deployed on the cloud server will perform the data analytics in soft real-time to generate a personality blueprint of the suspected patient. As all the data will be available at central cloud servers, state-of-the-art AI and ML algorithms will be developed to perform pattern recognition and pandemic forecasting for COVID-19. The data and gathered insights can be shared with relevant government agencies and healthcare department for preparing and planning for an efficient response strategy by healthcare authorities at regional and national level for dealing with COVID-19 pandemic and can also be used in future to deal with other such calamities.

But with all the improvement in the scientific society regarding strategies to dealt with disease the current CORONAVIRUS pandemic still caught us unprepared. In the present situation where there is a huge surge in patients falling ill to COVID-19, the health care facilities world-wide is crippling under the burden of the disease. All the health care facilities facing the shortage of basic supplies required in curbing the spread of infection. Additionally, most of the current face masks are not designed in a way to protect a wearer from exposure hazards for a very long time. It is critical to ensure a better and long-lasting protection to health care workers. Another major issue faced by the health care facility is inefficient sanitization/disinfection of work environment. We are proposing an idea where not only an efficient and long-lasting PPE will be designed to protect the frontline healthcare staff from CIOVID-19 but also a persistent, target specific and active surface cleaner.

data.projectName: Detecting COVID-19 using  person’s voice with Keras, TensorFlow, and Deep Learning
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest: In this project we proposed a quick, easy to access, effective, online COVID-19 diagnostics tool using person's voice with  Deep Learning techniques. The person’s voice is synthesized online which includes his or her coughing sound, pattern, Dyspnea (shortness of breath) sequences along with fever, sore throat, and travel history of the suspected person. Later, these features are used for modeling and training of the deep learning models to detect the signs of COVID-19 infection in a person. Afterwards, model will be validated and tested on distinct dataset samples to compare the accuracy of the results along with the guidelines and expert opinions provided by the pulmonary experts regarding respiratory dis-order and COVID-19 infection. This will help to trace, test and isolate the people with the disease aggressively at large scale and will help in containing the outspread as quickly as possible.

data.projectName: Anti-Viral Herbal Hand sanitizer and disinfectants
data.theme: Development of disinfectants particularly using indigenous herbal ingredients
data.projectDigest:
As it is already known that preventive strategies for COVID 19 are currently  better as a cure is still being worked upon. Our proposal is to formulate a hand sanitizer and disinfectant using dietary ingredients that have already established anti-viral properties against Influenza -A and other viruses that cause flu like symptoms. By doing so our purpose is not only protecting the entry or contact of virus to the host but if contact occurs by using our sanitizer we hope that further spread to other household members can be prevented.
As it includes herbal ingredients, the chances of side effects will also be very low.
Besides that we will test its susceptibility by performing tests and will also compare our sanitizers and disinfectant  with others being used by feed back from the community and health care workers.

data.projectName: Development and Implementation of D-COVID Tunnel
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
There is currently no cure or approved vaccines for the Novel Corona Virus Infection Disease (COVID-19). While the vaccines are under trial, the only way to fight the COVID-19 is to reduce the exposure to the virus. Our proposed project “Design and implementation of disinfectant tunnel or gate” is a preventive measure to control the spread of COVID-19 in Pakistan. Therefore, we intend to design the low-cost disinfecting passageway that will serve to disinfect the person’s hands and clothing before entering any office, laboratory, hospital, restaurant, station and airports. The transmission of novel virus involves infected droplets that can adhere to different surfaces for hours to days. The tunnel will ensure to stop the spread of the virus, possibly denaturing others of its kind such as Influenza Virus, Herpes, Rotavirus, Rhinovirus etc. 
The expected completion time for the project is less than a year. Moreover, the future research implication of the study is its associated impact on the overall society. The commercialization of the disinfectant gates, especially at the entry and exit of the airports, stations and institutes, can stop the spread of contagious diseases including COVID-19. 
The above mentioned research will be conducted at the Biomedical Engineering Department, Mehran University of Engineering and Technology, Jamshoro in collaboration with Liaquat University of Medical and Health Sciences, Jamshoro and ISRA University Hospital, Hyderabad and Aga khan University  Hospita,l karachi.

data.projectName: Syndromic surveillance of COVID-19 through machine learning and AI
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest:
During the past few decades, Natural Language Processing techniques have been widely used in biosurveillance for detecting disease outbreaks from health related data sets. Chief complaints and triage notes at an Emergency Department provide good source of data for the detection of such disease outbreaks. Timely review of chief complaint summaries can save time delay due to extensive laboratory testing. 
Syndromic surveillance focus to measure the size, spread and tempo of outbreaks with the aim of monitoring disease trends and providing reassurance that an outbreak has not occurred. After the anthrax letter threat in 2001, a range of projects were initiated in US to classify chief complaints into syndromic categories and detect disease outbreaks using supervised machine learning methods9. 
The objective of this project is to evaluate whether syndromic surveillance detects local outbreaks of respiratory infections including COVID-19 without losing true signal among false alarms. The free-text chief complaint reports routinely collected by duty medical officers in Emergency Departments and outdoor clinics of Basic Health Units or Tehsil Health Units of Primary and Secondary Health Department, Punjab, during patient registration will be used for the proposed syndromic surveillance. Supervised machine learning methods will be used effectively to perform syndromic classification of free-text chief complaint reports, forming the basis for an automated approach to syndromic surveillance. The project will evaluate distinct machine learning algorithms and will test the efficacy of different models to detect the preliminary predictive signal extracted from free-text chief complaints alone.

data.projectName: Clinical course and predictors of mortality of inpatients with COVID-19 in Pakistani Population – a multicenter study.
data.projectDigest: Provision of better health services is the fundamental responsibility of every state, so the results of this proposed study will help to explain the Disease Epidemiological Modeling for clinical course and predictors of mortality by COVID – 19 in Pakistani population to cope with adverse events to decrease burden of mortality by this infectious disease. As COVID-19 Virus strain has different genetic makeup from those strains in Wuhan, China and Iran, and, is behaving in a different manner in Pakistani Population. So, the trends, proportions, and predictors from those populations may not be generalized in Pakistani population due to genetic diversity, different environmental factors, healthcare system and mutations in COVID-19 genome. Results of this proposed study will help researchers and healthcare policy makers to formulate guidelines regarding specific clinical course and medication to control this pandemic by reducing mortality rate to cope with this deadly disease. Medical Record Files of the patients who expired after diagnosis of COVID – 19 from Government healthcare facility from all provinces of Pakistan will be reviewed for data collection. To achieve our objectives of clinical course and predictors of mortality, our research team will visit all dedicated Government hospitals of Pakistan for data collection. Data will be entered and analyzed using SPSS version 25 for descriptive statistics and comparative statistics.

data.projectName: SARS-CoV-2 - Genetics, Drug Repurposing and Hunt for potential Anti-viral lead molecules through Virtual screening
data.projectDigest: The outbreak of COVID-19 in December 2019 in China, which later spread worldwide, started global health emergency with predictions of sever implications, if not controlled on time. This initiated global efforts among scientific and medical community to combat this infection through various means. For a sustained control and protection, development of potential anti-viral drugs is one of the targeted approach. Although, designing and developing a panel of new druggable molecules are always encouraged as new strains of the viruses emerge due to their speedy rate of mutations, however in the current situation, drug repurposing study is one of the most effective and quickest approach. As this is new strain of Coronaviruses, therefore, proper analysis of the genomes of SARS-CoV-2 is mandatory to proceed with further drug repurposing as well as the identification of novel anti-viral molecules. This project involves investigating the genomics of the new strains through comparison with native isolates which will be helpful in diagnosis. Besides that we will also understand a number of factors that involves the pathogenicity,  genome conservancy, and potential targeted genes which will ultimately be selected for identification of potential drugs. Furthermore, as part of this project drug repurposing study is also included with is one of the quickest approach to identify potential drugs that can be used in COVID-19.

data.projectName: Enabling Radiologists to Detect, Explore and Understand COVID-19 from Chest X-rays Using Explainable Artificial Intelligence
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest: A most vital step in fighting against COVID-19 is efficient screening of infected patients to provide them early care and isolation in order to reduce the spread of the virus. Although the polymerase chain reactions (PCR) testing is a gold standard screening method for detecting COVID-19 cases [6]. The screening process has high turnaround time (which has implications) and test kits are in very limited supply, making it imperative to explore alternative methods to detect and prioritize suspected cases. The radiography examination has been employed as an alternative screening method. It involves conducting chest radiography of suspected cases and analyzing radiography images (i.e. Chest X-rays (CXR) ) to find visual markers related with COVID-19 infection. Realizing the potential of CXR to detect COVID-19, although various artificial intelligence systems based on deep learning is proposed to detect COVID-19 from CXRs [9-10, 13-14], the systems are black boxes to radiologists. Such a lack of interpretability creates a hurdle in understanding the decision making process, critical factors underlying the disease and behavior of the disease, leads to prevent AI systems from being widely adopted [15-18]. The goal of this project is to use explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) to develop a framework for radiologists to understand bio-markers of the disease, decision process of AI system, critical factors underlying the disease and behavior of the disease.

data.projectName: Development of rapid diagnostic test strip for early detection of Corona virus in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: It is a global emergency as it has affected 205 countries in the world and by March 30th 2020, about 872,696 people are infected worldwide and 43,269 have died of COVID-19. In Pakistan, 1865 confirmed positive cases and 26 died. The rapid detection of corona infected patients can save many lives. According to WHO, the early detection of Corona virus is key to combating the spread of infection. This is also important for accurate detection corona virus. The social impact of this disease is much more than the mortality percentage. There is a huge demand for rapid test kits that is not still fulfilled by many countries including Pakistan. While with PCR it is not possible to run thousands of tests on daily basis. Even there is huge demand for PCR chemicals that are no more available in market to be purchased by hospitals and labs. The cost of PCR (approx. 8000 Rs) is even not affordable by common people. The development of rapid diagnostic strip in our country by using our own resources will fill this supply and demand gap for diagnosis. Moreover, this will be available at economical cost and will be easily affordable.

data.projectName: Development of a low-cost method for rapid diagnosis of COVID-19 infection.
data.projectDigest:
Corona virus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is rapidly spreading to almost all countries of the world [1]. Pakistan is also affected by this tragedy and the number of people affected by COVID-19 is on the rise. These numbers are likely to increase with the passage of time. The best way to check the spread of disease is the identification of people infected with the virus and their prompt isolation. Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) is the best method for diagnosis of COVID-19 especially in the pre-symptomatic period [2]. Real Time PCR based commercial diagnostic kits are available in Pakistan but their average reagent cost per test ranges between Rs. 2000 to Rs. 3000. Moreover, availability of the real time PCR machines is another major limitation due to high cost of the equipment.
This project aims to develop a low-cost real time PCR kit with an estimated cost of less than Rs. 700 per test. In addition the use of GTI-PCR Reader will be able to replace the expensive real time PCR machines. The proposed research would enable the development of low-cost PCR for widespread application throughout Pakistan. 
The low-cost testing can be applied to screening of the immediate household of the index cases of COVID-19 infection thus allowing their prompt isolation and preventing further spread of the disease.

data.projectName: Multiplex PCR-RFLP based diagnostics development of SARS Coronavirus 2.
data.projectDigest: COVID 19 is the type of respiratory infection including pneumonia and other complications caused by a novel virus named SARS-CoV-2. This is a member of family coronaviridae. This is the third major pandemic of the 21st century and surprisingly the rest two were also caused by the corona viruses. Therefore, it is not amazing to say that this is the century of coronaviruses. Currently humanity is passing through a very critical time with reference to control of this novel bug that has caused 47,264 deaths globally till date. Among the challenges that need immediate addressal are development of therapeutics, efficient vaccine development, successful control and sensitive and efficient diagnostics of the virus SARS-CoV-2. In poor countries like Pakistan we are facing the difficulties with reference to availability of the diagnostic kits and the cost involved for each test is very high. Therefore, the development of indigenous diagnostics assays will be very contributory for the economy of the country as well as for the Pakistani nation. The project that I am presenting here for the development of diagnostic assay is not only economical, feasible, expected to be sensitive as well as accurate but also be possible to get the results in 6-8 hours. The multiplex PCR based technique will be applied followed by RFLP that will make it two tier test and will enhance the specificity and sensitivity of the obtained results.  The optimization of the results will be significantly important and is expected to be achieved with some efforts.

data.projectName: COVID-19 Cellular Inhibition by Targeted Deglycosylation, Antibodies Enrichment from Plasma and COVID-19 Disinfection
data.projectDigest: Targeted deglycosylation of spiked S protein of COVID-19 will be designed to inhibit cellular penetration. COVID-19 is enveloped by spiked S protein which is N- and O-glycosylated at target sites. This glycosylated protein interacts with ACE-2 to form endosome. This attachment allows formation of endosome and thus cell penetration occurs. The COVID-19 cannot penetrate its cell if the Spiked protein is deglycosylated. For this purpose, PNGase F, a deglycosylation enzyme, will be delivered at target site to serve the purpose. Moreover, Isolation and purification of Antibodies will be made from Recovered COVID-19 patients for production of vaccine/treatment. Antibodies produced naturally to resist particular disease can be used as vaccination. In case of pandemic COVID-19, there are number of recovered patients in Pakistan. Serum analysis of these patients will be helpful to study the type of antibodies produced in these patients against COVID-19. These antibodies can effectively be isolated, purified using advanced chromatographic tools and can be used as a basis to formulate vaccine/treatment against COVID-19. Project also includes the development of Cleaning Solutions for economical ultrasonication based sterilization of medical equipment. Lastly, Synthesis of cost-effective disinfectants for COVID-19 will be accomplished for ensuring complete sanitization.

data.projectName: Preparation of Natural Herbs based Immunity Booster & Treatment Formulation for COVID-19
data.projectDigest:
In December 2019, an outbreak of unknown fatal respiratory infection was emerged in Wuhan, China.  Early it was assumed to be spread from Huanan Seafood Market, later the researcher have suggested it may not be the original source of virus transmission to human beings. The causative agent was identified as a novel coronavirus and later renamed SARS-CoV-2 by the International Committee on Taxonomy of Viruses. WHO has named the disease as Coronavirus Disease-2019 (COVID-19). The virus exhibited quick human to human transmission. It is declared as pandemic and spread to >200 countries and territories. Majority of patients present severe respiratory illness, including fever, cough and shortness of breath. More than 2000 positive cases have been reported in the country so far which is increasing with every passing day (till date 31st March, 2020). There is no specific medicine or vaccine available against COVID-19. However, China has recovered and won the fight against using traditional Chinese medicine (TCM). Mainly, we are planning to develop herbal formulation of our indigenous herbs already proven to be effective against COVID-19. The Agriculture University of Dera Ismail Khan is exhibiting an ideal climate zone for most effective used herbs. Initial dose will be adjusted by the Physician of Polycilinic hospital and then will be used at mass level on patients admitted in hospitals or tested positive for COVID-19. 
This will be an added advantage to introduce cost effective and comparatively less side effect medicine to cope with the current pandemic situation in the country. In this way, we will offer the cultivation at large scale also to save the foreign reserve used for medicine import.

data.projectName: LOW COST SANITIZER AND DISINFECTANT TO MANAGE COVID-19 TRANSMISSION BY USING NATURAL MEDICINAL OILS
data.piUniversity: Lahore College for Women University, Lahore
data.theme: Development of disinfectants particularly using indigenous herbal ingredients
data.projectDigest:
The present project is focused on the development of disinfectant and hand sanitizer using indigenous medicinal plants containing aromatic oils. Pakistan is an agrarian society which relies on the use of herbal remedies for most of the chronic diseases. Present project will help the community in three ways: Firstly, it will ensure the availability of safe, cost effective hand sanitizers and disinfectants secondly it ensures the continuous availability of hand sanitizers and disinfectants in market so that every single person of the community can have access to this local made sanitizer and feel safety for himself and his family. Thirdly by the use of pharmaceutical products with naturally obtained aromatic oils could play a vital role in alleviating the spread of pathogenic microorganisms and environmental problems associated with the indiscriminate use of synthetic chemicals especially resistance against antimicrobial. 
Essential oil will be obtained by hydro distillation from indigenous potential plants; different combinations of essential oils will be tested against microorganisms to obtain minimum effective concentration. Qualitative and Quantitative analysis shall be performed for oils. Pharmaceutical characterization shall be performed on developed products as per official monographs. Lastly,Pharmacological and toxicological studies shall be performed .

data.projectName: Vision based smart solution for the protection of COVID-19
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest:
The world pandemic (COVID-19) known as the corona virus Covid-19 is zoonotic in nature and transmit from animals to humans. Currently, this virus has spread almost 90 percent countries of the world by effecting 950,430 people directly or indirectly till date [3]. As, this era belongs to the fourth industrial revolution and everything goes towards the automation. So, that’s why community looking towards the Artificial Intelligence industry to provide the automatic and efficient solutions. These solutions will be helpful to community in order to tackle and overcome the reasons behind the spread of Corona Virus. In this proposal, we have proposed the solution based on the computer vision techniques and algorithms. The main reason behind the spread of the corona virus is the social interaction. If we automatically make sure the social distancing using cameras installed on the metro stations, railway stations bus stands and all public places, then it will be a great achievement. 
So, in this proposal we have proposed solutions that will help the community to make sure the social distancing and identify the persons who have symptoms of (Covid-19). By doing so, we will be able to stop and control and the spread of corona virus. Our algorithms based on the features, which was extracted using the deep learning and machine learning based approaches. It generates real time stats along with the statistical reporting on social distancing and corona virus patient’s identification. Our collaborator will help us to make sure the availability of the data to train our proposed algorithm.

data.projectName: Quarantine Patient Monitoring System (QPMS) for Health Care of COVID-19
data.projectDigest: World Health Organization officially declared the COVID-19 a pandemic. It has spread globally, and medical resources become insufficient in many regions. At the current stage, it has been spread all over the world so the most important thing is to care the effected patients. All over the world, quarantine places have been designed to keep these effected patients for at least fourteen days so that it should not spread to others. But it’s very difficult to care these large number of quarantine patients with less paramedical staff and resources. To overcome this problem, we are going to propose a reliable, efficient and easily deployable quarantine patient monitoring system (QPMS) that can play a vital role in providing basic health services to the quarantine patients that can be at remote areas like villages or towns or at near border area of the country where basic health facilities are not available.  In this project, an automated and intelligent system will be developed to remove all these challenges by using IoT module to collect patient data and data analytics using machine learning for clinical decision support system to detect the abnormality and severity of the patient. Basic model of the proposed system consists of different phases including a PDA, Electronic Medical Record (EMR), Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) and a web based or mobile application for the Doctors on their Laptops or Mobile Phones to analyze the patient data. For this purpose, untrained or less trained medical staff available at quarantine places can collect data of the patients through PDA attached to the patient. This PDA has different medical sensors that are compulsory for COVID-19 patients. This PDA has also a local monitoring application to display patient data for analysis.

data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest:
Six types of coronavirus have been identified that cause human disease: four cause mild respiratory symptoms, whereas the other two, Middle East respiratory syndrome (MERS) coronavirus and severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS) coronavirus, have caused epidemics with high mortality rates. COVID-19 is the infectious disease caused by the most recently discovered coronavirus. It is genetically related to the SARS-CoV-1 virus that was outbreak in 2002. It's called the coronavirus because the scientists who discovered it, felt its distinctive spiky surface looked like a crown, or corona in Latin. These spikes allow the virus to hijack human cells and wreak havoc on our health. According to recent study the genetic material of COVID 19 is similar to one found in bats. The most common symptoms were fever, dry cough, and difficulty breathing. 

An international effort to share X-ray has helped produce a growing body of evidence which doctors can use to diagnose those most seriously affected. The radiologists have revealed white patches in the lungs of COVID-19 affected patients, called ground-glass opacities. These white patches indicate pneumonia, as the spaces which are normally filled by air are being filled with something else instead. In most of patients with MERS coronavirus infection, initial radiography had shown some degree of abnormality, with Ground-Glass Opacities (GGO) being the most common finding. Similarly, GGO is the most common radiologic finding for COVID-19. Some Computer Aided Diagnosis (CADx) systems based on deep learning have been developed to assist radiologists and doctors.

data.projectName: CT as a diagnostic tool in COVID-19 patients
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Medical University, Islamabad
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest:
In order to overcome the big lacuna in patient workup which will result in Pakistan becoming one of the top countries with COVID-19 if it goes undeterred. I propose the fusing of X-ray and CT scan images with AI technology in order to formulate a diagnostic tool which is sustainable, available for the detection and subsequent management of COVID-19 patients. The incorporation of AI into the scanned images will subsequently reduce the need for Human Resource in the shape of radiologists on site to read the images and a provisional diagnosis will be available instantly. The system will also have online image transfer facilities for radiologists to comment from home so that there is patient diagnosis available around the clock. This telemedicine facility will enable our premium centre, Pakistan Institute of medical Sciences which has the model isolation unit of the Federal Government to liaison with other COVID-19 facilities in the country and this will result in a nationwide early diagnostic tool which can subsequently be used international liaison as well.
The integration of AI technology in this study has two main objectives. Firstly, to provide effective, accurate and innovative methods of early diagnosis of COVID-19. It is very difficult to differentiate the pattern of COVID-19 with other types of pneumonia. Secondly, the artificial intelligence based proposed system will be effective in reducing the workload of medical professionals and bringing down financial costs.

So far there is a big gap to get complete data related to morbidity and mortality rate of COVID-19 patients in Pakistan. (8,9)

data.projectName: Coronavirus Disease-2019 (COVID-19) Pandemic
data.theme: Development of disinfectants particularly using indigenous herbal ingredients
data.projectDigest: The proposed research work deals with treatment of viral diseases.Viral infections play an important role in human diseases, and recent outbreaks in the advent of globalization and ease of travel have underscored their prevention as a critical issue in safeguarding public health. Despite the progress made in immunization and drug development, many viruses lack preventive vaccines and efficient antiviral therapies, which are often beset by the generation of viral escape mutants. Thus, identifying novel antiviral drugs is of critical importance and natural products are an excellent source for such discoveries. In this research proposal, we summarize the antiviral effects reported for several natural products and herbal medicines. On the basis of these facts we can further explore novel antiviral agents from medicinal plants of Pakistan through screening and isolation techniques which may be effective in treatment of COVID-19 pandemic.

data.projectName: Uses and Impact of ‘Open Data’ Technology for Analyzing and |Tracking Pandemic Disease
data.theme: Information Collection and Dissemination IT platforms)
data.projectDigest:
‘Open Data’ is collection of easily accessible data that is to be available for general use without any restrictions. ‘Open Data’ is gaining momentum in literature and interview for the purpose of research. Therefore many developed countries are planning to start getting involved with ‘Open Data’. Moreover, the focus is shifting from opening as much data as possible towards realizing the benefits of ‘Open Data’.
‘Open Data’ analysis has been taken up contemporary as a new trend in the world of information and communication technology. With technological advancements many countries are showing interest in opening their governmental data to the public. Moreover many benefits and positive impacts have been identified playing a role in the eagerness of countries to implement ‘Open Data’ programs. Some of the discovered benefits of ‘Open Data’ includes transparency of data and accountability of the government, participation and self-empowerment to the citizens, economic growth, and stimulation of innovation through re-use of data. 
The research explained how the fact that when Government opened their data both internally and externally improved their capacity to innovate. Lastly, this research described how some of the tasks mentioned previously could be outsourced by the government, bringing a new actor in the ecosystem. There are plenty of data sources that might provide a different angle on the spread of Pandemic disease like Corona Virus and large public datasets from cities, countries and government agencies. With the access to ‘Open Data’ the analyzing and tracking of Corona Patients is largely observed.

data.projectName: Pharmacological application of molecularly identified  immunity booster local medicinal plants as potential candidates to control the COVID-19 disease across Pakistan
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Coronavirus Disease-2019 (COVID-19) emerged in December 2019 as an outbreak of unexplainable pneumonia in Wuhan city, Hubei province, China. By the end of March 2020, this outbreak spread globally and this novel virus, Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), infected 858,916 confirmed patients while 1938 patients across Pakistan (http://covid.gov.pk/). In China, 76052 patients have recovered from this disease from a total of 81518 patients and this recovery rate is highest in the world so far which have been believed to achieve by using Traditional Chinese Medicines (TCM) especially the medicinal herbs (Yang et al. 2020). Pakistan also has a lot of antimicrobial medicinal plants which not only boost the immunity system but also have cure potential against the bacterial and viral diseases. From international literature, some useful herbs against COVID-19 have been identified which are found locally and can be utilized as immunity booster and remedial candidates (Yang et al. 2020). data.projectName: Herbal Sanitizers containing walkthrough gates; a practical approach to prevent COVID-19 in hospital and community settings
data.theme: Development of disinfectants particularly using indigenous herbal ingredients
data.projectDigest:
The aim of the proposed project is to develop fully automatic walk-through gate with herbal sanitizers to prevent the spread of Ongoing pandemic of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19).  The  outbreak is declared a pandemic by World Health Organization (WHO)  and Public Health Emergency of International Concern on 30 January 2020.  The virus is mainly spread during close contact and by small droplets produced when people cough or sneeze.  People may also catch COVID-19 by touching a contaminated surface and then their face. Complications may include pneumonia and acute respiratory distress syndrome and no any known vaccine is available so for.  
Only possible solution is to prepare hand sanitizers which will provide  symptomatic and supportive therapy.  Use of automated walk through gates for the applications of the prepared sanitizers with herbal sources will be unique and quite applicable in the current situation of Pakistan. Hand sanitizers will be prepared by use of recommended concentration of ethanol obtained from sugar mill and herbal sources of different extracts. These walk-through gates with the additional benefits of sanitization will provide the better solution of this emergency conditions to prevent the spread of the fetal virus not only in patients but also in the community.

data.projectName: Open-label Randomized Controlled Trial on Chinese Patent Herbal Formulation Yinhuang Qingfei Capsule ---- A Fast Approach for the Treatment of Pakistani COVID-19 Patients
data.projectDigest: Since December 2019, COVID-19 rapidly spread to almost the whole world. Unfortunately, it is also happening in Pakistan, so it is urgent to identify some therapeutic interventions, and to learn from Chinese experience of excellently containing and treating COVID-19 within two months (Jan-Feb 2020). Among the different strategies, Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) have played an important role. Several TCM patent drugs and formulations were found to be significantly effective in COVID-19 patients. One of them is Yinhuang Qingfei Capsule (YQC). This project is designed for the fast clinical trial of YQC in Pakistan for the treatment of COVID-19. The manufacturer, Hunan Anbang Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (Anbang) will be an important partner. It is worth mentioning that, Anbang has carried out the successful clinical trial of YQC in ICCBS, University of Karachi, during 2019. They have established the local office in Karachi and shipped 10,000 boxes of YQC as donation to support Pakistan. On the basis of the long cooperation between ICCBS and Anbang (China), our team is proposing this project for the benefits of COVID-19 patients. By establishing the efficacy of YQC in Pakistan, a fast solution for the treatment of confirmed cases of COVID-19 in Pakistan will be achieved.

data.projectName: Rapid Construction of isolation ward/ hospital using Light Gauge Steel Framed construction
data.theme: Indigenous manufacture of Low cost Intensive-care equipment
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan, as of now, has above 2000 reported cases of COVID-19. The natural way to stop the virus from further spreading is only through quarantining potential ‘carriers’. Building isolation wards and emergency hospitals from scratch in the shortest possible time all over the country is certainly not possible via conventional cement-concrete construction practices where a simple structure can take months and years to build. 
Fabricon Pvt. Ltd (Fabricon 2020) has Indigenously developed specialized machinery for fast track construction of Isolation Wards, Clean rooms, BHU's, Field hospitals, Clinics, etc. Using the worlds leading Light Gauge Steel (LGS) Framed construction technology. Using this technology one can build an isolation ward of 100 beds in a matter of a few weeks. This is through a fully computerized CNC Roll Former Fabroll 500 that is designed and built-in Pakistan. It is portable and can be easily transported on a truck to the construction site and has all the essential functions that are found in any international brand of Roll former. To our advantage, all the structures erected through framed construction technology can be easily relocated to other zones in the shortest possible time, without any loss of materials.

data.projectDigest: The proposed project will accelerate the early detection and will achieve more rapid and widespread testing capacity in selected remote areas of Hazara and Malakand division of KP. The proposed method is robust, rapid, cost effective and most importantly will be used onsite and in field or various points of entries  for the detection and screening of 2019-nCoV. data.projectName: Fabrication of Antiviral protection stuffs (facemasks, gloves and medical kits) against Corona Virus by antiviral Bi-metallic Alloys Impregnated on activated carbon non woven Fabrics
data.projectDigest: This research proposal will respond the low cost and effective protective antivirus masks, gloves, gowns and medical kits especially against Corona virus for common citizen as well as para- medical staff in Pakistan at large scale. Proposed project relates to an impregnation of antiviral Bi-metallic alloys on activated carbon non woven fabric-containing component for fabrication of personal protective products. it is expected that activated carbon cloth, when impregnated with Bi-metals (such as an antimicrobial metals such as silver, Zinc and copper) results in a cloth having antiviral and virucidal properties. The combination of outer and inner layers with the metals impregnated cloth will serves to draw a line of viruses from a static and mobile environment into the cloth assembly where they can be captured. Once captured, the virus particulates are held and killed within the structure of the cloth assembly. Proposed research will offer to provide both creating masks that is breathable but efficient at filtering-killing viruses within few minutes. Research will also exploit the ability of proposed bimetallic alloys and nano diamond impregnation on cotton, fabric, spun bond, melt blown and activated carbon clothes as antiviral respiratory prototype masks to block Novel Corona virus.

After developing the modified versions of these products, the pilot study (small clinical trial) will be followed in COVID-19 Positive cases. If the positive results come then large clinical trial will be conducted. The preliminary toxicity on syrup Sudori and instant Jhoshanda

data.projectName: Development of Point-of-Care antibody-based testing kits for COVID-19
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: COVID-19 outbreak, caused by a novel coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2) is an ongoing major pandemic with > 0.6 million cases and >2500 deaths worldwide. Both symptomatic and asymptomatic COVID-19 patients can transmit the virus; diagnostic testing for COVID-19, therefore, is critical in containing the further spread of the infection. Real time-PCR (RT-PCR)-based test for the amplification of the viral RNA is the most common test currently employed around the world for COVID-19 detection. This test, however, is costly, provides delayed results (2-3 days), requires specialized equipment, and cannot detect whether someone previously had an infection or not? An antibody-based test, on the other hand, does not require sophisticated equipment, can detect past infection in recovered patients, be considerably cheap compared to RT-PCR-based tests and provide results within hours without compromising the sensitivity. Here we propose to develop antibody-based ELISA (enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay) and dot blot assays for COVID-19 testing. Our team at LUMS routinely uses ELISA for the detection of viral antibodies and dot-blot immunoassays for detection of various other proteins. We believe that both tests will be cheap and could be performed in most labs or even hospital setting around the country without any additional requirement of equipment (Point-of-Care testing).

data.projectName: Clinical Risk Prediction Model for Hospitalized COVID-19 patients in Resource Limited Settings
data.projectDigest:
COVID-19 is a novel infection with serious clinical manifestations, including death, and it has now reached more than 180 countries and territories. This viral pandemic places extraordinary and sustained demands on health systems and health care providers. Of patients infected with COVID19, about 15% have severe illness and 5% have critical illness. Overall mortality is estimated to range from 0.25-3.5%. Case fatality rates are much higher for vulnerable populations, such as persons over the age of 70 years (>14%) and those with coexisting conditions (10% for those with cardiovascular disease and 7% for those with diabetes). Due to its disease characteristics and high reproduction number (R0), it is estimated that 30-70% of the population will get infected. Such demands can create the need to ration medical equipment and interventions, and is reportedly being considered already in different regions. For instances, in Italy, physicians have proposed directing crucial resources such as intensive care beds and ventilators to patients who can benefit most from treatment. Daegu, South Korea faced a hospital bed shortage, with patients dying at home while awaiting admission. In the USA and UK, protective requirements for health workers have been downgraded, causing condemnation among providers 5. This rapidly growing disparity between supply and demand for medical resources even in many developed countries presents a fundamental question: How can medical resources be allocated fairly during a pandemic such as COVID-19. 
Objective: To develop a clinical prediction methodology that can help with prognosis of hospitalized COVID-19 patients in the resource-limited settings. 
he primary outcome of interest would be in-hospital mortality.

data.projectName: Automated Low Cost Portable Mechanical Ventilator
data.piUniversity: CECOS University of Information Technology and Emerging Sciences, Peshawar
data.theme: Indigenous manufacture of Low cost Intensive-care equipment
data.projectDigest:
According to the World Health Organization (WHO), some 80% of people with Covid-19 recover without needing hospital treatment [1]. However, one person in six becomes seriously ill and can develop breathing difficulties. In these severe cases, the virus causes damage to the lungs. The body's immune system detects this and expands blood vessels so more immune cells enter. Ultimately, this can cause fluid to enter the lungs, making it harder to breathe, and causing the body's oxygen levels to drop. To alleviate this, a machine ventilator is used to push air, with increased levels of oxygen, into the lungs. Sometimes, the ventilator also has a humidifier, which modifies adds heat and moisture to the medical air so it matches the patient's body temperature. Patients are given medication to relax the respiratory muscles so their breathing can be fully regulated by the machine. People with sever Covid-19 symptoms may be given ventilation using facemasks, nasal masks or mouthpieces which allow pressurized air or mixtures of gases to be pushed into the lungs.
Unfortunately, the number of Covid-19 affected patients having critical condition are exceeding to the  available ventilators in the hospital as a result, a ventilator shortage remains imminent in many parts of the world [2, 3]. The overwhelming demand of ventilators in many countries has compelled our team to think about the production of ventilator, which is easy to develop, simple to operate, shall be portable and of low cost. Due to the right mix of team members, a mechanical engineer, electrical engineer and MBBS doctor, we already been able to conceptualize the basic design of ventilator. Now, we need the resources to transform the conceptual design to tangible product in a form of automated low cost portable ventilat

data.projectName: Employment Loss, Food Security and Awareness to Mitigate Risk among Urban Dwellers during Crisis Period
data.projectDigest: This global pandemic (COVID-19) might partly be considered a WASH disease which requires precautionary measures such as regular hand washing, drinking more water etc. That is why we propose to find the availability of clean drinking water in Katchi Abadis of Pakistan. Most of the slum dwellers are working on daily wages. We would analyze the impact of employment loss during this crisis. We further propose to find the situation of food security before and after this crisis. At the end we would identify high-risk locations and suggest how to help those individuals who are not well to isolate. This project will create awareness among dwellers of Kachi Abadis to avoid the risk of any pandemic due to unhygienic practices and how to mitigate other risks such as employment loss and food security through different awareness campaigns.

data.projectName: Development of Homemade Facial Mask for General Public: An Opportunity for Unemployed Daily Wager Due to Covid-19
data.projectDigest: With a Covid-19 pandemic looming, nations and policy makers need to decide how they can best use available resources to protect their people against severe illness and death, and to mitigate health and socioeconomics effects for society as a whole. Much research is under process to develop optimal strategies for the use of personal protection equipment. There are only limited data to assess the potential effectiveness of non-pharmaceutical interventions to reduce the risk of transmission, including the effect of different kinds of face-masks worn by the general public or by patients. The current Corona epidemic-Covid-19 created havoc and thousands people died around the globe. In these circumstances, WHO recommends that simple home-made cotton mask can be used in severe attack of epidemic. Therefore, study in hand attempt to commercialize the facial mask for general public who are threaten to be attacked by corona pandemic. Moreover, daily wagers and poor females will be attached in this project to sew the facial mask. data.projectName: Early detection of Corona virus by Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) device
data.projectDigest: Over the outbreak of the new corona virus, called the 2019 novel Corona virus (2019-nCoV), the World Health Organization (WHO) declared a global public health emergency on 30 January 2020 that primarily originated in Wuhan city, in the Hubei province of China. The WHO officially named the disease as corona virus disease 2019 (COVID-19) on 11 February.  The diagnostic tests specifically for COVID-19 are emerging needs to screen and confirm patients due to the  manifestation of the COVID-19 infection is highly nonspecific, including respiratory symptoms, fever, cough, dyspnea, and viral pneumonia. Currently, standard molecular technique is used for COVID-19 is the real-time reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (rRT-PCR). This protocol has been documented and available online on the WHO website since 17 January 2020. However, rRT-PCR method is time-consuming process, results obtain can be up to 2 or 3 days. Also, requires sophisticated laboratory equipment, which is often located at biosafety level 2 or above lab.  An alternative molecular amplification technique should be deploy to overcome the current time-consuming and laborious detection by rRT-PCR. In this scenario, a point-of-care (PoC) device using Loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) method that could be rapid, cost-efficient and robust, can be used onsite and in the field and no need of trained technician to operate.

data.projectName: Low cost, non-invasive monitoring mask for COVID-19 symptoms (fever, cough, shortness of breath) linked to a cloud server with smart analytics
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.theme: Development of Infectious Diseases Surveillance Systems using big data analytics and artificial intelligence
data.projectDigest:
It is not very straightforward to identify COVID-19 patients, especially in the initial stages, and thus many countries, around the globe, have resorted to complete lockdowns as a preventive measure. Once a patient is identified, the main diagnosis is her immediate isolation and monitoring of symptoms. The healthcare providers are quite vulnerable to be exposed to the patients in such cases and thus are at high risk to be infected themselves.

To overcome the above issues, we propose to develop a low-cost non-invasive vital monitoring mask for COVID-19 based on the three most widely used symptoms for its diagnosis, i.e., fever, coughing and shortness of breath. This mask would be connected to a central server where the acquired data would be processed to identify COVID-19 patients based on anomaly detection techniques. The real-time monitoring of data would also enable us to better understand the trends in patients and thus identify future patients based on machine learning techniques. Moreover, the geographical location of patients would also be known, which would lead to a better resource allocation at the macro level. This device would also enable us to protect healthcare staff from exposure to the positively tested patients.
