data.projectDigest:
Solid waste management (SWM) is the biggest and widespread issue in both rural and urban areas of both developed and developing countries. Sahiwal, being the 21st largest city of the Pakistan by population, produces about 40548 tons of the solid wastes annually and will become 56071 tons annually by 2033. Till to date, all the solid wastes are disposed into dumping sites and roadsides which suppress the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) like SDG-3, SDG-6, SDG-13, SDG15.
In the present scenario, there is an urgent need of an alternate and reliable SWM to the existing disposal method to meet the SDGs and to save the life of living beings by minimizing the environmental pollution and hazards. The main focus of this project will be the RDF and Landfill solid waste into useful by-product. The objectives of this project are:
•	To provide an adequate SWM system to collect the high quality solid waste
•	To segregate the solid waste for further processing with existing segeration facility
•	To recycle and convert the solid waste into useful and less or non-toxic materials
Therefore, the outcomes of the project will directly benefit the community (SDGs-3, 6 & 13) as well as the local government (SDGs-8 & 11).

data.projectName: Interaction of toxic gases and nerve agents with defective Carbon nanostructure materials
data.projectDigest: The increasing threat of toxic chemical warfare agents and toxic gases in society, finding of the suitable materials and processing techniques to adsorb or detect chemical warfare agents and toxic gases to protect working personals of civil society is necessary (a peaceful application of chemistry). In this project, defective carbon nanostructured materials such as carbon nanotubes (CNTs), graphenes, graphene quantum dots, carbon nanofibers etc will be explored as a possible candidate for adsorption of toxic gases at room temperature. These adsorbing materials can be used either in sensing core materials or in clothing. Particular attention will be focused on elucidation of interaction of with carbon nanostructured materials. Defective carbon nanostructured materials fabricated by ions irradiation are likely to sense/adsorb toxic gases. Ion beam irradiation technique can be used to make defective carbon nanostructured materials. We have the facility to make such kind of materials using charged particle accelerator. Functionalization of carbon nanostructured materials with suitable groups will also be explored for this new class of advance materials.

data.projectName: Climate Resilient Agriculture Production in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through integrated assessment and development of climate youth ambassadors
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is a country with an inherited agricultural base. Given the previous few decades climate developments has become a great challenge for the agriculture sector of Pakistan. Analyzing Pakistan’s economy, it can be seen that agriculture is the backbone of the economy. Economically, climate change has widespread detrimental impacts on water, food, and energy security conditions of Pakistan. The variation in temperature and uneven distribution of rainfall patterns are negatively affecting agriculture productivity in various parts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP). Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province (KP) is assessed to be one of the most vulnerable provinces of Pakistan to the negative impacts of Climate Change. KP experienced even worse flooding in 2010 – the worst in recent history - resulting in displacement of hundreds of thousands of people. A large proportion of the population lives on or slightly above the poverty line, and the vulnerability of this group worsens in the event of a natural disaster. Unfortunately, our local communities are neither aware of the impending phenomenon of climate change nor prepared to fight its potential challenges. Keeping in view the adverse effects of climate change and unequipped and ill-informed local communities in the KP, the current project proposes to analyze the impacts of climate change on agricultural crops and to develop the adaptation strategies for current as well as future rainfed production system, that are directly relevant to the NDCs of Pakistan submitted to UNFCCC. Initially, the evaluation of climate impacts on crops productivity and farmers well-being will be determined by collecting data of different crop growing localities of KP. The results obtained from this project will enhance the resilience in the agriculture sector.

data.projectDigest:
Fecal samples will be collected from children with diarrhea aged 2–60 months presenting to health care facility including primary, secondary and tertiary health care facilities around Islamabad Capital territory like BHUs, RHCs and CHCs. A standardized questionnaire will be completed during the enrollment interview to collect the following detailed health information: demographic, environmental, socio-economic status, water and sanitation, breastfeeding practices, other clinical conditions, vaccination history, frequency of diarrhea episodes and anthropometric measurements.
Along with taking samples parents will be counseled in detail about water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) strategy, breast feeding, nutrition and vaccination.
Stool samples will be analyzed for causative organism by PCR, Culture sensitivity or Gene Expert if diarrhea is more than 2 weeks. Endoscopy will also be done if helicobacter Pylori is identified and there is haematemesis.
Therapeutic intervention according to identified organism will be done.
At the end of 2 years impact on the prevalence of diarrhea will also be assessed.

data.projectName: Artificial Intelligence Center of Excellence for Life Sciences
data.projectDigest:
In the current era, life scientists depend on medical instruments that can produce millions of laboratory data in a day or two. To get on-time fast results a high-end computing system with an intelligent programming environment for life science is required.
Therefore, in this work, we proposed a center of Artificial Intelligence and supercomputing that utilized supercomputing systems and intelligent methods to analyze and mine the molecules, biophysical, genomics, microscopy, medicine, and radiology data and help scientists to generate knowledge to develop new treatments and understand living organisms by utilizing analytical and intelligent computational techniques. The proposed Center for life sciences will merge the artificial intelligence and High-Performance Computing systems to utilize life sciences data and understand living organisms using analytical and computational techniques. At the heart of our hardware solution is a low-cost compute node, which we call as “server”. This server uses heterogeneous processing cores including the Central Processing Unit (CPU), Tensor Processing Unit (TPU), and Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA). These servers can be combined to form a centralized or decentralized cluster. By integrating several of these clusters develops a supercomputer. Thus, offering a high-performance computing platform that scales with the remote processing needs and financial budget. To program the supercomputing system for life-sciences applications, we also propose an “AI Programming Framework” that executes the applications on the servers of a single or various cluster located in centralized or decentralized locations.

data.projectName: Towards the Application of Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Livestock Management - A Pilot Project to uplift Socio-economic Conditions of Rural Women
data.piUniversity: Capital University of Science and Technology, Islamabad
data.projectDigest:
This project proposes the empowerment of rural women through technological innovations in livestock management. An Intelligent Decision Support System (IDSS) is proposed that will make use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies to provide informed decisions on livestock management through a mobile app. The proposed IDSS will provide notifications and alerts to women farmers on health, feed and reproduction aspects of the livestock management. The mobile app will provide access to vaccination centers, veterinary facilities and feed suppliers. This will address the target 5.B of SDG-5 on gender equality that emphases on the use of enabling information and communication technologies for women empowerment. 

An extensive capacity building program is also proposed to complement the technological solution for the development of skills and knowledge of rural women in livestock management. A series of outreach activities including seminars, workshops, farm visits, practical demonstrations, group discussions and one-on-one sessions on livestock management will be arranged for rural women.

data.projectName: Yak conservation and establishments of methods to preserve its milk in powder form: an initiative to formulate immunity boosting formula for infants in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Pakistan has one of the highest prevalence’s of child malnutrition as compared to other developing countries. Low birth weight, inadequate feeding, maternal illiteracy, less birth gap and socioeconomic status are main contributing factors. To address this issue, there is need to develop some alternative strategies of feeding to infants such as upgradation of formula milk taken by infants. It is reported that formula and cow milk has some ingredients such as hormones, artificial ingredients and chemicals that contribute towards lower immunity, lower growth and weakness of memory. Recently, research has been done on Yak milk and it is found that it naturally contains conjugated linoleic acid (CLA), Immune Globulin (IG) and Lactoferrin (LF) (enhance the immune function), lactoferrin (almost Zero in cow milk) and lacto protein (tissue development and growth), 18 amino acids (8 are not synthesized in body). Pakistan has large population of Yaks in Northern areas (> 10,000 domesticated yak), people domesticate yak for milking and other traditional values. Keeping in view above mentioned facts, present study designed for Yak ex situ conservation, with aim of mass production of milk. Secondly, to standardize formula milk using yak milk as basic ingredient due to its unique composition

data.projectName: Melting heat effects on mechanism of heat transfer in hybrid nanofluid flow subject to homogeneous-heterogeneous reactions over a nonlinear curled curve stretching sheet with shape factors
data.projectDigest: The aim of current project is perform comparative study of shape factor (Blades, Platelets, Cylinders and Bricks) analysis of Molybdenum disulphide MoS2 and Graphene oxide GO water based hybrid nanofluid (HBNF) towards nonlinear curved sheet. In addition, a comparative study of nanofluid and hybrid nanofluid will be accounted. Mathematical modeling and analysis will be carred out in the presence of curvature, melting effect and heterogeneous-homogeneous reactions. Diffusion coefficients of reactant and autocatalyst will be dealt similar. The physical quantities namely fluid velocity, heat and mass transfer aspects, skin friction, Nusselt number will be analyzed for curvature, melting and heterogeneous-homogeneous reactions. Boundary layer approximation will be used in mathematical formulation. Suitable transformations will be employed for arising differential equations into nonlinear ordinary differential equations. The resulting nonlinear system of equations will be solved by bvp4c matlab solver. Physical argument will be arranged through theme of this project. The physical parameters obtain from the proposed mathematical modelling might be helpful in reducing machine work in terms of skin friction and heat transfer rate

data.projectName: Eco Islam Module for  Entrepreneurship Students
data.projectDigest:
The meaning making process according to the Islamic worldview has an extremely important and special place for the natural environment as containing the divine signs (ayat). Most of the Pakistani Muslim students are not cognizant of this fact. Our societal habits  of over-consuming and wasting can be addressed through the right religious pedagogy. On the production side, these students when they turn into entrepreneurs and business professionals, will translate the imbibed Islamic-ethical ideas into zero-waste and zero-environmental harm policies for their respective businesses. The purpose will be to cultivate such an Islamic critical- ethical reasoning skill within these students that they can take the right policy decisions themselves and have the internal motivation and drive to implement those policies leading to fruitful actions. 
The current curricula used by various educational systems within the Pakistani schools teach students about climate change in their science and social studies textbooks. The Islamiat or Islamic Studies textbooks are bereft of such critical thinking exercises and discussions where they could relate the Islamic insights to the contemporary problems and global issues of Environmental Degradation and Climate Change. As Muslims, we are least concerned and bothered about our religious and ethical responsibility toward the environment. The best way to change the status quo is to use religious and ethical reasoning to have a lifelong impact on individual thinking, decisions and actions of our current and future generations.  Our proposed curriculum is meant for such a  change.

They do not however consider the responsibility of conserving and protecting the environment as a religious obligation. If the Pakistani business students, at various stages of their educational trajectory, are made to see the correlation between the environmental responsibility and religious worldview there is high probability that they will choose and act in ways that are conducive to the environmental and societal well-being. This could in future become part of the national (Islamic Studies) in curriculum prescribed for schools, colleges, universities and madaris.

data.projectName: Turning sea water into drinkable conditions along with clean energy through electrocatalysis on the new materials
data.projectDigest: The project is designed for the locality of Karachi through the splitting of sea water into clean water along with clean energy.  The sea water is not drinkable in the current form due to several dissolved salts which make water hard in nature and also it can not be used for the cleaning of clothes due to its hardness. Further the treatment of sea water consumes lot of energy, cost and involves complicated process.   Now it is possible to  use new technologies at low cost  for the exploitation of sea water. Therefore, the project is designed to split the sea water into hydrogen and oxygen . Further to add, these fuel cell technology can be applied to use hydrogen and oxygen produced from sea water into the development of fuel cell. This way renewable energy can be obtained and also the end product will be the steam which can further treat with simple approach and turn it into the drinkable water. The project resolves the two issues of Karachi, one energy and other the clean water. Thus, the proposed study has dual advantages for the local people of Karachi and also at national level.

data.projectName: INNOVATIVE MODEL OF ACADEMIA AND COMMUNITY NETWORKING TO REDUCE NEONATAL MORTALITY IN RURAL AREAS OF DISTRICT ISLAMABAD
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Medical University, Islamabad
data.projectDigest:
The proposed project aims to design and implement an innovative cross-sectoral and inter-disciplinary model of networking between academia and local institutions and communities to reduce neonatal mortality due to asphyxia and sepsis in rural areas of district Islamabad. The project would also demonstrate the role of research at higher education institutions in effectively addressing local socio-economic challenges. Key components of the project are:

Objective 1: Assessment of Existing Healthcare Facilities 
Objective 2: Capacity Building
Objective 3: Early Detection and Care
Objective 4: Networking and Community Outreach
Objective 5: Knowledge Creation and Policy Impacts

The planned activities and resulting outputs, under the above objectives, have been designed to bring together various research elements together in an integrated approach for achieving the project goal. Thus, gap analysis of healthcare facilities, building institutional and human capacities, research to support more accurate detection and treatment of infections, community outreach and social mobilization, and networking among collaborating partners have been designed to comprehensively contribute to achieving substantial improvements in the treatment of high-risk cases and thereby reducing neonatal mortality rate. This project also plans to produce cutting edge research and results that can be upscaled for national implementation.

data.localySocioEco: With 42 deaths per 1,000 live births, Pakistan is among the top three countries, along with China and India, with very high neonatal mortality (death of a newborn within the first 28 days of life). Almost 300,000 neonatal deaths occur every year in the country that account for an alarming 12% of annual global neonatal deaths. The two leading causes of neonatal mortality in Pakistan are asphyxia or breathing difficulty at birth (22%);and sepsis or infection (18%). This socio-economic issue is also a major challenge in Islamabad, like all other provinces and regions of Pakistan, especially in its rural areas. Weak public sector healthcare system at primary level, fragile testing and diagnostic facilities and lack of collaboration between key institutions are major causes of this serious issue.

data.projectName: Plastic Recycling for Road Construction and Restoration in Azad Kashmir, Pakistan
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest: Plastic pollution is a major threat to the environment which results in pollution and global warming. Plastic usage and disposal increases day by day, and overfilled the rivers, drainage's and roadsides, resulting in environmental pollution. Same way, the road covers the almost areas of AJK but are not in good quality. Some of urban and rural areas even lack road access due to high cost and people suffer shortage of food and other necessary household accessories. Therefore, the road demands in mountainous regions increased day by day. Another major problem is the corrugation and potholes on the highways constructed in Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, due to improper storm water management. Therefore, the aim of proposal is to utilize the plastic waste for road pavement in AJK, and it is relative new idea, economical and eco-friendly technology. In future it will be consider as a best way of Green and Circular economy compared to linear economy. The quality of bitumen/asphalt will be modified with a plastic usage. The benefits of proposal will be the positive impact of recycling on the environment i.e recycling creates jobs, keep plastic pollution out of the environment, recycling of plastic waste conserves natural resources, minimize global warming.

Azad Jammu & Kashmir (AJ&K) has an area of 13,297 square kilometers with 10 districts and the population is 4.11 million with a high population density of 304 persons per square km. The urban population is 17.4% whereas 82.6% of the population lives in rural áreas (P&DD, 2019). Approximately 18% of AJ&K population lives below the national poverty line and 25% can be considered as multi-dimensionally poor. Moreover, there are concerns over declining agricultural productivity, a rising population, lack of private sector growth and environmental degradation, and climate change. The ability of Government of AJ&K to plan and deliver road infrastructure projects effectively will determine the future pace of growth of AJ&K. So, there is need to develop highly efficient technologies for industrial and domestic wastewater treatment which requires minimal energy input and provides effective water treatment solution.

The project outcomes will be helpful for gaining sustainability goals i.e clean water and sanitation, good health and well-being to ensure sustainable water supply. A team of chemists, local government is part of this project, so that device design and catalyst synthesis can be done through out in a systematic way.

Anti-microbial resistance is one the emerging problem in Pakistan. In developing countries, acquired bacterial resistance to antimicrobial agents is common in isolates from healthy persons and from persons with community-acquired infections. Complex socioeconomic and behavioral factors associated with antibiotic resistance, particularly regarding diarrheal and respiratory pathogens, in developing tropical countries, include misuse of antibiotics by health professionals, unskilled practitioners, and lay persons; poor drug quality; unhygienic conditions accounting for spread of resistant bacteria; and inadequate surveillance.  The selection and spread of resistant organisms in developing countries like Pakistan, which can often be traced to complex socioeconomic and behavioral antecedents, contribute to the escalating problem of antibiotic resistance worldwide.
Literature review reports AMR as a serious emerging problem especially in infants and adolescents in Pakistan. Also, on Animal side the waste usage of antibiotics is a serious threat to human population in the form of milk usage without any withdrawal period prohibition.

data.projectName: Drinking water analysis of district Swabi for detection of heavy metals and contaminants of emerging concerns (CECs): Water purification by using indigenous and sustainable solar light technologies
data.projectDigest: Water is one of the most important necessities for the survival of life on earth. The natural waters are frequently contaminated by heavy metals and toxic organic pollutants through various anthropogenic activities, constituting a global socio-economic issue. Particularly, water contamination and water borne diseases is a growing socio-economic issue in the developing countries, such as Pakistan. Drinking water analysis is an essential step towards the water purification, which is a basic Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and is the primary objective of our proposed project. The next objective of our proposed project is the provision of clean water to the local community. The proposed project is divided into three major steps, i.e., (i) collecting the drinking water samples from different union councils (UCs) of district swabi, (ii) testing the collected water samples for analysis of heavy metals and toxic organic pollutants by analytical instruments and (iii) investigating and developing indigenous and sustainable technologies for water purification. The output of the proposed project will contribute significantly towards the local funds and scientific community.

data.projectName: Development of a Bio-Fertililizer and Biochar based product to increase potato production under low organic matter content soils
data.projectDigest:
The combined use of beneficial microorganisms and soil amendments like biochar is essential for increasing nutrient solubility and yield in agricultural sustainability. Consequently, the proposed project has been designed with the aim to develop a bio-fertilizer and biochar-based natural product to improve the growth, yield and quality of potatoes grown in calcareous regions with low organic matter content. Initially, beneficial microorganisms like arbuscular mycorrhiza fungi (AMF) and phosphate solubilizing bacteria (PSB) will be isolated in laboratory and their inoculums/biofertilizers will be applied to potato seeds in combination with biochar in greenhouse conditions. Potato growth, physiology, elemental (Fe), biochemical and molecular parameters will be recorded in alkaline calcareous soil.
 After completion, the development of new biological soil fertilizer will be an alternative to known commercial fertilizers, and will be suitable for good agricultural practices used in potato production. Necessary attempts will be made to commercialize the product. The main deliverable of the project will be the development of a new product mixture of bio-fertilizer and biochar which can be used both in decreasing the high soil pH and increasing the content of soil organic matter in the region, where potato farming is most popular. As a result, soil rehabilitation and productivity will be increased within the scope of good agricultural practices. (relevant to UN SDGs No. 2 &3).

data.projectName: Cyber-secure Pakistan: Protecting National Cyber Space & Critical Infrastructure
data.projectDigest:
Traditional government processes and businesses are transforming to digital solutions to provide swift services, increase in revenue and ease of management. Cyber-attacks on national web portals & applications are increasingly used to steal critical data and to defame both government and corporate reputation. A single, effective cyber-attack can have far-reaching implications including monetary losses, theft of intellectual property, and decrease in consumer confidence and trust. Cyberspace is a huge socio-technical system, with human component being the most significant and susceptible for compromise. 
 
Cyber Secure Pakistan aims to address both local and national cyber security challenges by protecting the cyber space and associated critical assets. It integrates threat detection, mitigation, analytics, advisory, assessment, awareness and training in one eco-system that aims to prevent cyber attacks and to reduce national vulnerability to cyber crime.

data.projectName: Development and Introduction of Production Technology of Morels (Guchhi mushroom) in Mountain Region Gilgit-Baltistan Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Karakurum International University, Gilgit, Gilgit Baltistan
data.projectDigest: Gilgit-Baltistan has play a pivotal role for sustainable development of Pakistan. Although they have a quite trivial geographical area, but they serve as a catchment for the Indus River, upon which a majority of Pakistan's irrigated agriculture and hydroelectricity depends. It contains important natural forests, widespread mineral resources, and a wealth of biodiversity as well as world's highest mountains, and a rich cultural and archaeological heritage. The core problem of Gilgit-Baltistan is food security because cultivated lands are less than one kanal/capita. Cultivation of mushroom crops in existing agriculture system of Gilgit-Baltistan can help in improving household income and food security. The increasing population of Gilgit-Baltistan and facing food security issues it is best choice to consider to developed indigenous production technology of mushroom. The farming communities of the region can be empowered for improving production skill of mushroom technology which can be main source of income generation in near future.

data.projectName: Genetic modification of Tomato to Control ToLCNDV through CRISPR/Cas 9
data.projectDigest: Tomato Leaf Curl New Dehli Virus (ToLCNDV) is the emerging issue in the modern agriculture. Tomato has been reported as an key host to ToLCNDV in Pakistan. It can  damage tomato crop from 75% to 95% once strikes. This study is focused to control ToLCNDV by application of state of art technology  CRISPR/Cas9 based approach against conserved regions of different genes responsible for different viral activities. For this purpose, a twenty base pair sequence called protospacer  will be designed from the different regions of the virus. The best protospacer will be selected through  agro-infiltration screening of CRISPR/Cas9 based constructs in tomato plant followed by agro-infiltration of infectious clone of (ToLCNDV).  Molecular analysis will be performed to determine the viral titer in  control  and experimental plants. The selected protospacer will then be stably transformed in tomato through Agrobacterium mediated transformation. Putative transgenic tomato plants will be studied in T0 generations by using different molecular techniques for confirmation of successful introduction of sgRNA into plants and determination of its knockout efficacy. Technically, the knockout is expected to be in the  conserved region of the virus  hence will result in interference with its replication inside the plants.

data.projectName: The role of money management Fintechs in affecting households’ saving-behavior: A natural field experiment in Sindh Province Pakistan.
data.projectDigest: The economic growth, investment and saving ratio of a nation are closely integrated. It is well established economic rationale that countries with higher saving rates tend to have higher investments, ultimately translating into higher GDP growth. Pakistan’s economic growth has primarily been consumption-driven, making the growth pace unsustainable and causing severe macro-economic imbalances to recur over time. According to Pakistan Economic Survey (2019-20), the national and domestic savings have been on downward trajectory for past many years. To address this issue, using a blend of natural field experiment and cross-section methods, this study attempts to assess the impact of money management Fintechs ( Fintechs refer to Digitally Mobile-based Financial Services) on the individual’s financing decisions and in particular saving behavioral-patterns. Fostering saving habits and improving digital financial literacy of the youth in a province of Pakistan having World’s 5th largest youth population can generate multi-dimensional socio-economic benefits and thus can be an enabler for various Sustainable Development Goals-SDGs. Particularly, study would help meeting SDGs#1.4 that targets “access to basic financial services with appropriate new technology to all”, and SDGs#9 targeting industry, innovation, and infrastructure. Taken together, the implications of study would be of great social, economic, and regulatory interest.

data.projectName: Dendrochronological analysis of National Heritage (Juniper forests) of Ziarat Baluchistan, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Baluchistan is considered as forest deficient province across Pakistan. The geography of and nature is mostly termed as range lands across the province. A few areas where the elevation range reaches up to 3000 feet, occupied by some conifer species like Pinus gerardiana in Zhob and Juniper excelsa in Ziarat. The Juniper forests declared as Archealogical Heritage site by UNESCO, the purpose is to preserve the Juniper forests and the reason is these forests consists of trees which almost 4000-5000 years old. By carrying out the dendrochronological study on this site, will enable us to study about the previous historical events of the region and also by constructing the climate proxies up to thousand years. This study will be baseline study for preservation of this heritage and also will be a handful study for future policy making.

data.projectName: Improvements in the Production of the Second generation Ethanol Using Date Wastes as Raw Material
data.projectDigest:
Bioethanol from biomass is a alternative option to replace fossil fuel. Bioethnal is renewable, non-toxic, biodegradable and more ecofriendly. Pakistan is the among the top countries for production of date fruits and millions of tons of wastes in the form of date palm trunk and fruit wastes are generated annually. The unavailability of proper techniques for recycling of these wastes in value added products is not only a real economics lost but also a risk for environmental pollution. The date wastes are rich in polysaccharides and potential feed-stocks for second generation bioethanol production to contribute the growth of Pakistan economy in a greater extend.
Therefore, proposed project is designed to develop the production ethanol using simultaneous scarification and fermentation using date wastes (trunk and fruit wastes) as substrate.  The pre-treatment of date wastes will be optimized by using different method such as acid, alkali, hydrothermal, hydrogen peroxide and enzymatic pre-treatment. The effect of pH, temperature, fermentation time, yeast and date wastes concentration will be optimized for maximum production of bioethanol by different yeast species. Finally, the industrial feasibility of protocol will manage for commercial production of bioethanol.

data.projectName: Deployment of e-Mining System for Sustainable Development of  Mineral Resources in Gilgit-Baltistan
data.piUniversity: Karakurum International University, Gilgit, Gilgit Baltistan
data.projectDigest:
Mining of natural raw materials, their processing and value addition, consumption and utilization within the society and finally their release as wastes and emissions is generally referred as “societal metabolism of natural mineral resources”. Growth and sustenance of human society is dependent on this societal  mineral resource metabolism process. The diverse geology of Gilgit-Baltistan (GB) is endowed with economic mineral resources. A sustainable utilization of these raw mineral resources is both rewarding and challenging. A rudimentary mineral sector in GB fails to fulfill these societal needs and creating conducive livelihood opportunities. Therefore, the mineral sector of GB needs to be transformed into an efficient, modern, transparent and sustainable mining industry. 

Sustainable societal metabolism of natural mineral resources in Gilgit-Baltistan's fragile mountainous environment is a local and regional challenge. This R & D endeavour is envisioned to deploy “e-Mining System GB” as a digital platform that will provide:
1) Online portal as authentic point of reference for public dissemination of geological and mining data, information and knowledge,
2) Mineral cadastre system for transparent and efficient governance of mineral resource development projects,
3) Mining management system for maximizing financial and social benefits from a sustainable mining industry

e-Mining System will provide a common platform providing substantial and ongoing partnership between government, private sector, communities and civil society. This will leverage the transformative power of collaboration between the mining industry and other stakeholders and result in progressing towards sustainable mineral development projects.

data.projectName: Green Recycler: Conversion of non-biodegradable plastic waste into liquefied Petroleum gas (LPG) through environment-friendly process.
data.piUniversity: CECOS University of Information Technology and Emerging Sciences, Peshawar
data.projectDigest: Currently, Pakistan is facing two major environmental, social and economic challenges: a) poor waste management and b) energy shortage. If the waste is not dealt with priority, it is likely to cause major health problems, sanitation issues and deteriorating aesthetics of the cities in Pakistan. Plastic burning, which is often used in rural areas to get rid of plastic waste, results in CO2 emissions (in addition to several other harmful gases) which creates the greenhouse gas. Our innovative solution aims to effectively overcome these challenges by converting plastic waste into LPG i.e. waste management and energy production, simultaneously. Our aim is to reduce huge piles of plastics and to use this as raw material for energy (LPG) production. The proposed solution involves development of business-scale automated and controlled recycling of non-biodegradable plastic waste into LPG and designing of business structure to make this solution practical and self-sustainable. The setup will be designed to meet the targets of Industry 4.0. Involved processes are environment-friendly without any kind of harmful emissions. We have successfully developed a prototype of our solution with the capacity of 30kg non-degradable plastic waste recycling with more than 50% conversion into LPG and remaining useful byproducts.

data.projectName: Protein recovery from extracted Chlorella sp. and potential applications of its residue for soil and wastewater treatment: Process modelling and optimization
data.piUniversity: Balochistan University of Information Technology, Engineering and Management Sciences,Quetta
data.projectDigest: Algal biomass has been emerged as 3rd generation green gold bioenergy resource. This biomass has several advantages over terrestrial crops such as quick growth rate, high oil contents and require less area for cultivation. Moreover, it could be cultivated in fresh, marine and wastewater. After oil extraction the spent algal biomass could be recycled as feedstock for livestock, bio-oil production and in environmental sector. The extracted Chlorella biomass contains about 70% unconverted protein. Which is a valuable byproduct and must be quantified. The protein free extracted biomass is termed as residual or waste material. At larger scale process a huge amount of this solid waste is expected to be generated and needs to be managed. This protein free residual material could be recycled for biochar production to be applied for soil and wastewater treatment. The prepared biochar will be applied for industrial effluents treatment i.e. textile industry. This concept is not only beneficial for recovery of valuable products from algal biomass but also emphasizing the zero-waste approach for algal processing industries. Moreover, the proposed work would be highly beneficial for algal industry with Pakistan perspectives.

data.projectName: Development of Sensor for the Non-invasive Detection of Lung Cancer
data.projectDigest: In the proposal, a photonic crystal will be prepared and used as a heptanal sensor that is the biomarker of the lung cancer. This sensor will be fabricated via a vertical convective self-assembly method with monodisperse microspheres polymerized by co-monomers, namely, methyl methacrylate (MMA), N-isopropylacrylamide (NIPA), and 3-acrylamidophenylboronic acid (AAPBA) in the presence of template molecule-heptanal. After the polymerization, the microspheres and heptanal will be removed , which will result in a 3D-ordered interconnected macroporous structure in which numerous nanocavities derived from heptanal imprinting are distributed in the thin wall of the formed inverse polymer opal. Owing to the special hierarchical porous structure, the molecularly imprinted polymer opals allow rapid and ultrasensitive detection of the target analyte. The interconnected macropores are favorable for the rapid transport of heptanal in polymer films, whereas the inherent high affinity of nanocavites distributed in thin polymer walls allows the sensor to recognize heptanal with high specificity. More importantly, the heptanal recognition events of the created nanocavities can be directly transferred (label-free) into a readable optical signal through a change in Bragg diffraction of the ordered macropores array of the sensor and thereby induce color changes that can be detected by the naked eye. At last, clinical samples from lung patients provided by a collaborator in various hospitals of Islamabad and Lahore will be tested to check its practicability to detect lung cancer.

data.projectName: Intelligent Internet of Grains (IIoG)
data.piUniversity: Sarhad University of Science and Information Technology, Peshawar
data.projectDigest: Given the current storage situation in the country, according to one recent research reported in media, by 2025, the food department will not be able to stock around 270,000 tons of wheat. In the past, it has always been recommended for the government to create large capacity silos as well as offer concessions to the private sector to share the remaining burden of wheat storage. However, due to shortage of funds, the plan has never been easy for various governments to materialize. Among other reasons of less interest in silos construction is their belief that it would be difficult to keep them operational due to power crisis in the country. Fundamentally here we see two main challenges in the post-harvest losses and grain storage. The first one is faced by a farmer who is lacking modern technology driven storage facilities to retain his production for longer periods of time. What happens here that the grains usually get damaged or if unable to store he ends up selling his grains at a lower price and even buying them latter at a higher price. Eventually what he falls in is a poverty trap. Secondly, a serious challenge is faced by the government who lacks funds for building large storage facilities for maintaining the national food reserves. Our proposed work utilizes  distributed storage facilities to optimize grain storage lifetime at the farmer end and avoid spoilage losses using Artificial Intelligence, Machine learning and Internet of Things (IoT) technology

data.projectName: The Big Challenges of Small Dams: Promoting Socio-economic Welfare through Sustainable and Resilient Reservoir Management in the Namal Valley, Mianwali
data.projectDigest:
Constructed in 1913, Namal Dam irrigates approximately 50,000 acres of cropland in the agrarian district of Mianwali through a reservoir fed entirely by rainwater. Apart from its primary purpose of irrigating the downstream area, the dam and its tributary rainwater torrents also play a major role in the socio-economic activities of the upstream population in the form of farm irrigation, fisheries, animal husbandry, recreation and wildlife preservation. The local Irrigation Department operates the dam outlets keeping in view the interests of all (often competing) stakeholders. However, the absence of a risk evaluation & early warning system, compounded with political pressure from the local communities often results in sub-optimal (and sometimes disastrous) effects, ranging from floods to drought in the surrounding area. The problem is further aggravated with the advent of climate change with unprecedented inflows to the lake occurring more frequently and at a more massive scale. Many small dams in the region have similar ecosystems and communal dependence grown around them. We therefore face the local challenge of “ensuring sustainable regulation of small dams that fosters socio-economic security for all stakeholders involved in a way that ensures resilience to the effects of climate change”. Thus, the challenge not only directly addresses SDG 13 (climate action) but also addresses SDG’s 11 (sustainable communities) and 12 (responsible consumption) for the Mianwali District.

data.projectSummary:
Constructed in 1913, Namal Dam irrigates approximately 50,000 acres of cropland in the agrarian district of Mianwali through a reservoir fed entirely by rainwater. Apart from its primary purpose of irrigating the downstream area, the dam and its tributary rainwater torrents also play a major role in the socio-economic activities of the upstream population in the form of farm irrigation, fisheries, animal husbandry, recreation and wildlife preservation. The local Irrigation Department operates the dam outlets keeping in view the interests of all (often competing) stakeholders. However, the absence of a risk evaluation & early warning system, compounded with political pressure from the local communities often results in sub-optimal (and sometimes disastrous) effects, ranging from floods to drought in the surrounding area. The problem is further aggravated with the advent of climate change with unprecedented inflows to the lake occurring more frequently and at a more massive scale. Many small dams in the region have similar ecosystems and communal dependence grown around them. We therefore face the local challenge of “ensuring sustainable regulation of small dams that fosters socio-economic security for all stakeholders involved in a way that ensures resilience to the effects of climate change”. Thus, the challenge not only directly addresses SDG 13 (climate action) but also addresses SDG’s 11 (sustainable communities) and 12 (responsible consumption) for the Mianwali District. 

Through this project, we propose a multidisciplinary and multi-stakeholder approach, using four project components to ensure sustained socio-economic security of the Namal valley with the capacity to absorb stress and shocks induced by climate change.

data.projectName: Energy-growth-environment nexus: Using Nonlinear and Asymmetric technique from Pakistan
data.projectDigest: This study contributes to extend literature on the nexus among energy consumption, agriculture, capital and economic growth in Pakistan. Time series data from 1971 to 2020 utilizing Non-linear Autoregressive Distributed Lag (NARDL) model. The NARDL testing results will affirms asymmetric co-integration among the variables. We will also employ asymmetric causality test to examine the causal nexus between comprises variables. Asymmetric causality will be test between positive shocks in energy consumption and economic growth. Therefore, the study will discuss the link between energy and economic growth. The energy–growth nexus is presented in four hypotheses with implications for energy and growth policy: (1) The conservative hypothesis (unidirectional causality running from growth to energy); (2) The feedback hypothesis (bidirectional causality between energy and growth); (3) The growth hypothesis (indicates unidirectional causality flowing from energy to growth); and (4) The neutral hypothesis (means no causal effect).  The feedback and growth hypotheses have revealed the link between economic growth and energy policies, whereas the conservative and neutral hypotheses have shown that there is no association between energy and economic growth. This research help the policymakers to revisit their policies regarding industrial, agriculture and energy sectors by attracting foreigner investors to invest in energy sector.

data.projectName: A commercialized portable RF and Microwave therapeutic system for cancerous tumor treatment
data.projectDigest: Cancer being the most threatening disease is building up the pressure on the medical infrastructure of Pakistan. The lung and breast cancer cases have gone higher than expectations in the last decade. This invokes a dire need of enhancing the treatment capabilities in terms of Pakistani hospitals infrastructure and also to provide our medical doctors with state of the art equipment to treat and fight cancer.  The existing treatment facility is mostly based on surgical treatment of cancerous tumors, which is in modern medical practices not only getting outdated but also suffers from post-treatment complications. To improve the treatment quality, a paradigm shift towards the non-invasive cancer treatment is highly desirable and need of time. The develop countries have already adopted it and treating their cancer patients in effective way with minimal post-treatment impediments along with less treatment time. The non-invasive treatment systems are not locally manufactured and thus considered to be very expensive imports for our medical infrastructure. The proposed local production of the cancer treatment systems will have multiple societal benefits: uplifting of our local bio-medical industry, a step towards the sustainable cities and communities, easy approach of cancer patients to advance treatment at an affordable cost, and equipping our medics with the modern treatment tools.

data.projectName: Intelligent Mapping of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Detailed, accurate and up to date maps can provide insights into the economic and social condition of an area. Recently, satellite-imagery, phone-call data, social-media posts, etc. have been used to map the spread of disease, the health of crops to the economic well being of the area. The generated spatial-temporal information helps consolidate the data and see the bigger picture. Geo-spatial information is not only helping government and planning agencies to design policies but is fueling many current businesses like ride-sharing service, real-estate business (e.g. Zillow). It not only allows larger groups to identify the client market, its facilitating people in making their day to day decisions. Unfortunately, Pakistan, like many developing countries, where such information is vital for planning both at  government and private business level, lacks the means and resources to manually collect such information (2017 census, required 90-thousand enumerators).  We propose to create a platform for the Intelligent Mapping of Pakistan. Basically using Machine Learning for Satellite imagery and Geospatial data analysis to create information-rich maps. To show its effectiveness, as use cases, we propose to develop strategies & machine learning tools for mapping challenges faced by Pakistan in three different sectors namely education, economic  well-being & agriculture.

data.projectName: Impact of tillage practices and organic inputs on soil physical properties, soil fertility, growth and yield of crops in a maize-wheat cropping system
data.projectDigest: Excessive tillage, undue withdrawal of water for flood irrigation, indiscriminate use of chemical fertilizers, and burning of crop residues in the field have diminished the soil structure, created severe shortage of water for irrigation, increased the cost of chemical fertilizers. These approaches not only have reduced the crop yields and enhanced the overall budget of crop production, but have also seriously affected the livelihood of farming community and socioeconomic conditions of the country. The increase in crop yield, by restoring soil fertility and maintaining soil health and adopting best management practices (BMPs), is the only viable option. Site/regional specific BMPs may include conservation agriculture along with retention of crop residues. However, more promising results may be obtained through the combined application of organic fertilizers and conservation tillage. Accordingly, the study will be carried out to investigate the effect of tillage practices and organic inputs on soil physical properties, soil fertility, growth and yield of crops in a maize-wheat cropping system.

data.projectName: Remote Health Intelligent Intervention System (RHIIS) for Rural Areas of Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
In this project, we address the 3rd SDG “good health and well-being” by developing a Remote Health Monitoring for Intelligent Intervention System (RHMIIS). The system will enhance the quality of healthcare by incorporating the Internet of Things, Artificial Intelligence and Machine learning techniques. The patient’s data (from IoT sensors, lab tests and backlog etc.) will be processed at the cloud. The cloud will implement a set of machine learning algorithms that will process the patient data and automatically generate health related diagnosis and recommendations. The suggested diagnosis and recommendations will be communicated back to the respective physicians. Wearable sensors, such as, blood pressure sensors, electrocardiography sensors, temperature, oximeter, weight and glucometer will be used for collecting data from the patients. This information will be transmitted through sensor-gateways to cloud, where data will be stored, mined and predict health status of the patient by employing different machine learning techniques which is a key difference between our proposed framework and traditional remote health monitoring systems. Effective implementation of the proposed project will solve the health issues of people living in rural areas. 
The main outcomes of the project are,
•	To design and build custom IoT modules for remote health monitoring
•	To design and implement Artificial and Machine Learning algorithms for different disease diagnosis (cancer, cardic diseases and diabeties etc.)
•	To design and implement telemetry and telemedicine that will connect BHUs with physicians
•	To completely solve the health problems of rural areas

data.projectName: “Business Development Education at Incubation Centres of Pakistan and Allama Iqbal’s Philosophy of Economics: A Curricular intervention”
data.piUniversity: National University of Modern Languages, Islamabad (NUML)
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan with second highest youth population needs more than 2 million jobs per annum. According to World Economic Forum, there will be more freelancing than traditional jobs in 2025. In this situation, promoting entrepreneurship is among a very few viable solutions to support economy of the country. HEC is promoting entrepreneurship in youth through Business Incubation Centers to produce future businesses and employment opportunities for society. Many curricula have been introduced to equip potential entrepreneurs with right knowledge and leadership but all lack indigenous content. It is deduced that Iqbal’s philosophy of self-reliance, risk taking, innovation, resilience and leading the world, needs to be incorporated in the curriculum to get best results.      
This project titled: “Business Development Education at Incubation Centers of Pakistan and Allama Iqbal’s Philosophy of Economics: A Curricular Intervention”, will provide a framework in the light of philosophical doctrine of Allama Iqbal, the National poet of Pakistan, filling gap in business development education, at the BICs of the higher education institutions and other incubation centers of Pakistan, from local perspective. It will foster interdisciplinary research culture in host university i.e. National University of Modern Languages. This project will address SDG-4 (Quality Education) and SDG-8 (Decent Work and economic growth)

data.projectName: Smart Monitoring and Prediction of Sewerage Overflowing Manholes using IoT enabled Sensors and Networks in District East of Karachi
data.projectDigest: Karachi being the largest city of Pakistan ranks world’s 10 least livable cities, according to world’s urban livability index 2019. The severe air pollution, solid waste debris, and overflowing sewerage manholes in Karachi have increased the health risks to Karachi residents. Particularly, the city is currently facing issues related to the improper management of overflowing sewerage drains/manholes which have negatively affected the city’s production, economy, and public health. The main reasons for such polluted situation of the city include improper monitoring and identification of the sewage overflowing/blocking locations, shortage of budget for acquiring latest equipment, and lack of digital technology adoption in the stakeholder organizations including Karachi Water and Sewerage Board (KWSB) and local Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC). This project proposes a smart internet-of-things (IoT) enabled sensors and network system for digitally monitoring and localization of overflowing sewage drains (manholes) of selected areas of East district. The cost effective deployed arrays of sensors will continuously monitor the manholes and transfer the sensed data to a central unit via IoT enabled wireless nodes for further analysis to predict the overflowing hazard using artificial intelligence techniques. The analyzed data will then be used to identify the seriously affected locations, their past history and predict future trends in order to take the necessary precautionary measures efficiently to address the sustainable development goals (SDGs) of the city related to pollution/sanitation and health complexities.

data.projectDigest: Kidney stone diseases (KSD) are common worldwide disorder of mineral metabolism. Its prevalence is at alarming rate, causing significant morbidity with a considerable economic impact, in both developed and developing countries. In Pakistan, the burden of KSD is growing which is aggravated due to lack of community awareness, consumption of unhealthy foods, low drinking water, self-medications which lead to higher burden of Chronic Kidney Diseases (CKD) and poor access to renal therapy in result to impaired health and hence causes substantial economic burden on the country. Furthermore, the resource restricted settings, coping with this becomes further complicated due to unavailability of sufficient community-based data and weak socio-economic status that could help with targeted prevention. Based on previous findings, the present project, aimed to explore the risk factors associated with Kidney stone formation in Hazara division of Pakistan. After finding the root causes of KSD information will be provided to the health concern regarding the optimized food therapy and other associated factors which can potentially curtail the cost of hospitalization and enhance compliance in general.  Overall, the outcome of the project will support public policies and the surveillance of kidney disease that will result in minimizing the social and economic burden.

data.projectName: Improving Urban Water Management: an interdisciplinary application of smart urban infrastructure to study water demand in Karachi
data.projectDigest:
In light of the poor water security in Karachi, the government along with the World Bank have recently committed to investing over $2 billion into the water system. An evidence-based understanding of the problems is needed to ensure that these investments are effectively spent. While much of the discussion regarding Karachi’s water crisis focuses on a ‘shortage’ in water supply compared to water demand, this perceived water shortage is not informed by credible empirical analysis. Another major challenge is the high-level of non-revenue water (NRW) in the system which prevent Karachi’s water utility (KWSB) from being financially viable. The high NRW levels are partly due to a lack of domestic water metering and a water pricing system that does not account for actual water use. 

This proposal seeks to develop solutions to reduce NRW in Karachi’s water system and enable KWSB to become financially sustainable.  This proposed research seeks to develop (i) a scalable network of cost-effective smart flowmeters that are able to accurately measure and remotely transmit flow information to a cloud-based central server, and (ii) a sustainable water pricing structure that account for household income and nature of domestic water use.

A major cause of the dysfunctional water management in Karachi is a high proportion of non-revenue water (NRW), up to 60% by some estimates. In doing so, this proposal directly addresses two SDGs: Goal 6 on Access to Water, and Goal 11 on Sustainable and Inclusive Cities.

data.projectName: A  sustainable approach through the use of Single Cell Protein (SCP) as a feed ingredient in aquaculture
data.piUniversity: Government Sadiq College Women University, Bahawalpur
data.projectDigest:
Single Cell Protein (SCP) is a term first used in the 1960’s to produce microbials in masses by the use of fermentation process. Later, the use of SCP as an alternative source of protein received much attention and is thought to resolve the protein shortage issues worldwide (Abdel-Azeem and Sheir, 2020). 
Fishmeal has been the primary source of protein in many formulated fish diets as it is relatively  cheap and provide a range of protein requirements for fish (Hardy et al., 2018). However, the fishmeal price has been increased three folds since then and become an expensive source of protein. As a result, an urge to find alternative sources emerged and different researches are being conducted to identify and evaluate alternative protein ingredients for their suitability as fishmeal replacements (Hardy et al., 2018). 
SCP is a potential replacement to deliver multiple solutions through a numerous products and production methods. However, this technology requires considerable research, development to explore its full potential (Jones et al., 2020). This project is designed to explore this emerging technology for its possible uses and advantages in aquaculture in Pakistan. If successful, this technology will reduce the use of plant-based fishmeal and provide sustainability in agriculture.

data.projectName: Pollution source tracking in rivers and tributaries in KP and wastewater management for healthy rivers/tributaries
data.piUniversity: CECOS University of Information Technology and Emerging Sciences, Peshawar
data.projectDigest:
The water quality of the Indus river system and other small rivers is being deteriorated due to the indiscriminate discharge of sewage and industrial effluent.  This Proposal suggests an assessment of the water of the river system in KP using microbial and chemical source tracking, which can differentiate the origin of contaminations such as human and animal sources, domestic, and industrial sources.
The outcome of the study will be presented as a comprehensive temporal and spatial water quality report for all rivers in KP. It will also include the source of a pollutant tracking report (with identification of major industrial polluters), a design protocols report for installation of new and retrofitting wastewater treatment plants within five major cities including identification of suitable locations, a manual for best management practices for major polluting industries, and a strategic action plan for installation of wastewater treatment plants in collaboration with the implementing agencies. 
The study will provide a platform to build capacity among local water and sanitation agencies, graduate students, researchers, and faculty members in terms of water quality mapping, pollutant source tracking, advanced instrumental analysis, and microbial analysis.

data.projectName: Fabrication and Designing of Imaging System Using Microwave for the Detection of Breast Carcinoma
data.projectDigest: Every women is in  a risk of having Breast Cancer after 40 years of age. Breast cancer is the deadliest disease in the world and for females it is the top diagnosed with the highest mortality rate. Globally the screening and diagnosis of breast Cancer  is a real challenge especially for developing countries like Pakistan. In last two years the patients ratio increase up to 38% among all other types of cancer. Whereas the death rate is about 50.2% in 2019. These two factors alert the Pakistani health experts to find the reasons of this. One main factor is diagnosis of breast cancer in very advance stage at which to cure the patient is almost impossible, other are age restrictions as well as the size of the patient. X-Ray Mammography (MG) is the gold standard  technique for breast cancer diagnosis but its can not apply for young patients (less than 40 years of age), has high false result ratio specially for dense breast patients and it also failed to diagnose  tumor at early stages. WHO and Cancer societies strongly recommend yearly screening of every women after 40 years of age but Pakistan do not have enough resources for this. Due to all these limitation, a novel technique is at clinical trials level in the world known as Microwave Imaging Technique (MWI) is planned to devolpe in Pakistan due to atmost need of it. MWI  is low cost, high in result accuracy and equally useful for all age and size of the patients. a statistics proved that the number of patients of the age 15-30 years are increases day by day but unfortunately MG is strongly prohibited to use for screening and diagnosis therefore Ultrasonography (US) is used now a days. But  US is failed to diagnose deep solid tumor in patients. MWI is effective in this case also. MWI overall is a potential tool.

data.projectName: Biochar-Based Fertilizer: For Reducing Nitrogen Leaching, Greenhouse gases emission and Enhancing Nitrogen Use Efficiency and Plant Growth
data.projectDigest:
The current research project ‘’ Biochar-Based Fertilizer: For Reducing Nitrogen Leaching, Greenhouse gases emission and Enhancing Nitrogen Use Efficiency and Plant Growth’’ has been designed to enhanced nitrogen use efficiency and reduce leaching from urea fertilizer.  This result in nitrate leaching, ammonia volatilization, and nitrous oxide emissions which are severe environmental problems by contaminated groundwater quality. Subsequently reducing N use efficiency causes high N losses, and high economic costs. Thus, to reduce N release but enhance plant utilization of N fertilizer had been a priority demand for sustainable agriculture worldwide. The major environmental impacts associated with fertilizer use have been linked to leaching and runoff of nutrients, especially nitrogen, which causes aquatic eutrophication. The use of fertilizers has been considered by environmentalists as a key source of water and soil environment pollutants. Biochar is a byproduct of biomass pyrolysis and is usually characterized as rich in recalcitrant C with a large surface area, and diverse functional groups. These unique properties of biochar facilitating to hold nutrients, predominantly N, in soil and solution. Application of functionally enhanced biochar products in small quantity could be a low cost but high agronomic efficiency. Due to unique characteristics, biochar could be blended with urea fertilizer for concurrently increasing crop yield and reducing environmental risk.
We hypothesize that (1) Biochar Blended Urea (BBU) will enhanced N retention from urea through reaction and surface adsorption; and (2) Application of BBU could reduce N release but improve supply for plant growth.

data.projectName: An impact study of provision of flavored milk on early childhood development, learning and school attendance
data.piUniversity: Lahore College for Women University, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Pakistan faces challenges of children’s access to school, and according to the Annual Status of Education Reports in Pakistan (2018) a large number of children attending school are not learning to the expected levels. Household poverty and childhood hunger are the main barriers towards children’s attendance at schools, normal physical development, cognitive readiness, and productive adulthood in our country. The proposed project intends to address the United Nation’s Sustainable Development Goal 4 by identifying the impact of flavored milk intake (fortification with minerals, vitamins and fibre (inulin) on anthropometrics, (micro) nutritional status, faecal microbiota) composition, by underprivileged early age children (4-8)in public schools of district Lahore to map their physical development (height and weight), social emotional health, cognitive progress and attitude towards school. A team of experienced applicants from sociology, psychology, education, research methods, food and nutrition and dietary will participate for the intervention. The project will use multiple quantitative and qualitative tools of investigation for capturing consolidated results. The project findings will promote engagement with policy makers, public-private partnership and academics in Pakistan. The recommendations from the study will be presented to UNESCO Institute of Statistics custodian for SDG 4, the Global Education Monitoring Report and UNICEF.

data.projectName: Biological Control of Parthenium hysterophorus; An Invasive weed from AJK, Pakistan
data.piUniversity: University of Kotli Azad Jammu and Kashmir
data.projectDigest: Parthenium hysterophorus, is an invasive plant species which is spreading at alarming rate in Pakistan including Azad Jammu and Kashmir. The species is not native to area and has become a serious threat to the carrying capacity of our ecosystem. It has started from road sides and has reached to range lands and farmer fields. It is approaching towards forest lands. Due to its invasive behaviour, large number of seeds production on one plant, resilient seed characteristics and fast spread, it is destroying the local flora and fauna. Unfortunately, there is not a sustainable solution to control the spread of this weed except biological control. We propose a sustainable and environmental friendly solution to control the wide spread of this noxious weed. We propose multidimensional biological control of Parthenium using potential competitive plants selected from natural flora, rearing and using biological agent Zygogramma bicolorata, plant based green nano-particles, winter rust and a bacterial strain. This comprehensive study will evolve a substantial strategy to combat with spread of this harmful weed in Azad Kashmir and Pakistan

data.projectName: Synthesis and application oErrorf super absorbent polymer in agriculture
data.projectDigest:
Superabsorbent polymers (SAP) are  as a class of polymeric materials that have the property to absorb and retain a large amount of water and other aqueous components. Their composition is three-dimensional polymeric networks that do not dissolve in water but swell in aqueous medium. The SAPs are replacing the natural ones because of their certain characteristics like high absorption capacity, durability, and availability of wide varieties of raw materials. Due to their hydrophilic, non-toxic, biodegradable, and biocompatible properties, they are the most desirable products for various applications such as  agriculture, bioremediation, biosensors, and tissue engineering. Agriculture is one of the growing sectors due to the increased requirement of food to meet the growing demands of the large world population.  The  technology causes the release of agrochemicals in a controlled fashion[1].
Super Absorbent Polymer is a macromolecule absorbing polymer that has water ability up to 100,000% by osmosis procedure  and they form the granules to enhance soil properties[2].
Super Absorbent Polymers/ Hydrogels  are prepared from cross-linking or suspension polymerization. The polymer so formed is has  ability to swell and form the gel depends greatly on the quantity and type of cross-linker material  used[3]. Several other types of monomer used to prepare are non toxic, non irritating in nature and they are tested as non biodegradable with very low degrading ability of 10-15% per year[4].

Our proposed  summary of the project is  manufacture of these SAPs using various monomeric materials and then apply that polymer to various field crops and plants.

data.projectName: Evaluation and optimization of plant based compounds for their antiviral potential against SARS-COV-2
data.projectDigest: COVID-19 has become the major dilemma of current year. The life has become halted world over in order to prevent the  spread of infection. Combating a viral infection requires precaution and treatment go hand in hand. development of vaccine has significant importance with regard to  preventive measures.  The need of the antiviral drugs arises when we consider treatment of the already infected world population with low immunity. Plants have been a source of leads and scaffolds for drug development due to the fact that plants have gigantic exposure to the viral infections through out their life cycles.  We have chosen four compounds that have proven antiviral activities against different virus for screening and evaluation against SARS-COV-2. We will test harmaline, harmine, harmlol and berberine  against viral protein synthesis. Our research will be guided by molecular docking analysis of the compounds against specific proteins  which will then be screened and validated through wet lab analysis by optimization through derivatization.  We postulate that upon successful execution of above mentioned project we may be able to  come up with the potential antiviral drug candidates.

Coronavirus spread as pandemic has enveloped 188 countries, with 18 million confirmed cases and 700,000 deaths worldwide. Another surge in the cases and re-occurrence of the disease are potential scenarios in the current situation. In Pakistan, the recent updates included 19,770 active cases, there have been a total of 281,863 reported cases with 6,035 total deaths so far. Any re-occurrence and viral mutations could also prove catastrophic for the already halted economy of the country that is battling poverty, hunger, inefficient healthcare services and minimal access to medicine. 
Pakistan is a developing country with huge economic burden on healthcare industry due to current pandemic which is expected to increase the poverty by 8%. The pharma companies in the world are working towards an effective vaccine. However, the vaccine may only be good for the population that has not already been affected and effectivity of vaccines is limited due to variations in the serotypes. For the patients affected with the diseases, there will be need of the antiviral drugs. Preferably the leads can be taken from local plant sources that can act on specific viral pathways to disrupt their growth and progression and provide the affected people a ray of hope for cure. For instance Sofosbuvir is  potent  against has HCV targeting NS5B protein. Pakistan is blessed with diversity of herbal flora which provides lead for the development of drugs for various ailments. 
In the current project, we aim to take the lead from the nature, prepare natural product derivative and evaluate those against COVID spike and Mpro proteases for possible inhibition.

data.projectName: Molecular Pathways Linking Diabetes Mellitus with Alzheimer's Disease
data.piUniversity: Cholistan University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Bahawalpur
data.projectDigest: Diabetes and Alzheimer's disease are two important diseases which are seriously affecting the underdeveloped countries populations including Pakistan. Pakistan is considered to be at the 4th place in South Asia in terms of diabetes mellitus prevalence (one of the central risk factor of Neurodegenerative Diseases) in 2020. Pakistan is among those developing countries of South Asia where very few epidemiological investigations have been conducted regarding the prevalence and burden of various disorders, particularly Neurodegenerative Diseases. A recent survey of this kind suggested that 10 million people are affected annually by Alzheimer's disease. There are over 2 million people affected by Alzheimer's disease in Pakistan and the numbers are rising gradually with the passage of time. The proposed project will investigate molecular pathways linking Diabetes Mellitus with Alzheimer's Disease and it will help in reducing severity of Alzheimer's disease in Pakistan by earlier diagnosis.

data.projectName: Measuring and Improving Student Cognitive Engagement during Online Learning by integrating Pedagogical Knowledge with Computer Vision
data.projectDigest: Engaging students in a traditional classroom requires planning, designing tasks, employing a diverse skillset, utilizing effective teaching strategies, monitoring progress and readjusting strategies, evaluating and reflecting using meta-cognitive skills from the instructor.  In an online environment however, observing students’ behavioral, affective and cognitive engagement become extremely difficult. Even with good network connectivity observing multiple students during asynchronous or synchronous classes is a daunting task. This gains more significance in the post-COVID world where online and distance learning is emerging as a new normal in education.  Artificial intelligence and computer vision provide a unique opportunity in this scenario.  From an educational perspective, students’ engagement has three main dimensions: behavioral, affective and cognitive whereas behavioral and affective can be gauged by visual cues through computer Vision algorithms.  Combining existing pedagogical knowledge for observing student’s engagement with visual cues provides us with the framework in which we can assess students’ online engagement.  This input, of student’s online engagement, can assist the instructor in assessing her class and engaging students more effectively. This project will bring multiple perspectives together by integrating pedagogical knowledge with computer vision to measure and then improve the student engagement during online teaching and learning and help in capacity building of data science in educational research.

data.projectName: Development of Portable Photo-dynamic Therapy Prototype for the Treatment of Cutaneous Leishmaniasis in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
data.projectDigest: Cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL) is a skin infection that has a social and psychological impact on the infected people due to the resulting disfigurement of skin, especially on the face, nose and lips. Moreover, the disease is related to poverty-stricken areas of Pakistan and is prevalent in almost all the districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP). Beside the regular infection Public health Department KP, and local people are facing a continuous outbreak of the CL every year which cause a huge economic loss to the Govt and effected people. Scarcity of the relevant drugs and related toxicities are the other issues associated with its treatment. This project is aiming to design a photodynamic therapy (PDT) prototype to treat and manage CL at local health centers. The device will help in quick elimination of the parasite from the infected patients, therefore reducing the number of doses and time required for the healing of wound and hence will reduce the economic burden on local government and common people. Furthermore, this novel approach will reduce chances of skin disfigurement and minimize the social and psychological impact of the infection as well. Moreover, the technology can be transferred to Afghanistan, Iran and India for revenue generation.

data.projectName: Indigenous wastewater treatment system: A solution for water shortage and to improve food quality in peri-Urban Area of Multan
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest: Wastewater is an alternate source of water which has long been neglected and/or improperly used. In Pakistan, only 1% of wastewater is treated by industries before being discharged directly into rivers and drains. Multan is the fifth largest city of Pakistan in producing wastewater (66 × 106 m3) annually and its receiving water bodies include river Chenab, irrigation canals, and agricultural lands, causing significant health and economic risks. The freshwater resources are being used as a wastewater carrier and authentic sources are reporting the increasing concentration of emerging organic contaminants in the rivers of Pakistan. In current project, the treatment of wastewater is suggested by the sustainable and cost effective techniques, i.e. construction of wetlands (CW) for pre-treatment and introduction of Graphene-TiO2 sodium alginate based aerogel for the effective removal of emerging organic contaminants. The following parameters including total suspended solids (TSS) EC, SAR, RSC and pH, Chemical oxygen demand (COD), Biochemical oxygen demand (BOD), total soluble elemental concentrations will be determined. After treatment, wastewater can substitute for freshwater and contribute significantly to agricultural irrigation to address the global water scarcity. This project will help in finding an economical way of treating wastewater and identifying the potential constituents of CW suitable in local conditions.
