data.localySocioEco:
In most cities of Pakistan, the wastewater from municipal areas as well as from the industries is disposed of in natural surface bodies without any treatment. It has been reported that about 212.2 million-gallon tons of sewage are being thrown in water bodies and there is no proper mechanism for sewage collection and treatment/safe disposal.
Such practices are causing environmental pollution. The sewage water is used for irrigating various crops in the surroundings of the cities. The farmers also prefer to use this water because wastewater is a precious source for farmers as pumping cost from sewage nallah or drains is cheaper than a borehole and wastewater also have some nutrients and organic matter, which makes the practice more accessible to farmers with fewer financial resources.
Continuous use of wastewater may lead to environmental problems such as degradation of soil health and groundwater contamination and phytotoxicity.
However, untreated/raw industrial effluent being discharged by factories, which ultimately gets mixed with the urban sewage, may contain excessive amounts of heavy metals/metalloids like cadmium, chromium, nickel, manganese, zinc, lead, etc. These metals/metalloids in soil, if present in excessive quantities to permissible levels, may enter the food chain, thus becoming toxic to plants and human beings.
At least one-tenth of the world’s population is thought to consume foods produced by irrigation with wastewater. It has been estimated that at least 20 million hectares in 50 countries are irrigated with raw or partially treated wastewater.
Wastewater is mainly used in urban agriculture, which often supplies a large proportion of the fresh vegetables sold in many cities, particularly in developing countries.
Pakistan has an estimated discharge to surface water bodies of 7.57x 106 m3 per day. Less than 5% of this wastewater is currently being treated in municipal wastewater treatment plants and there are no established provisions for the reuse

data.projectName: Water Management, Testing and Purification: A Model Project Towards Safe and Clean Water
data.piUniversity: Mirpur University of Science and Technology (MUST), AJ&K
data.projectDigest: The local challenge of scarcity of pure drinking water has been identified in an area comprising of 3 villages situated at lower reaches of the top hills within a round trip (by foot) of 4 hours. People fetch water by foot covering 1-2 hours distance from the contaminated perennial spring resource. Two water tanks, one near the water source and other 1500 meters downhill will be constructed. Water from second tank will be distributed under gravity.  A water filtration plant will be installed at Chhoachh for poor population. A model water testing and research lab will be established at MUST, Mirpur. Twenty percent cost of AAS, infrastructure and space will be provided by the MUST. Spectrophotometer, COD, DO, pH, conductivity meters available in the Chemistry Lab will be utilized for water testing and research. PI and co-PI will organize awareness seminars at MUST and will deliver lectures in Schools/colleges. Three mini water testing labs at three adjoining districts will be established by the Local Government which will also work as sample collection points for the Model. PI & co-PI will organize workshop to train the manpower for preliminary water testing at Mini labs. Cohesive approach of PI and co-PIs from Punjab University and MUST and local government will help making the project completion successful.

data.projectName: Multi-locations trials of common bean candidate lines for commercialization, its interactions with microflora and preparation of bio-fertilizer
data.piUniversity: University of Malakand, Chakdara, Dir, Malakand
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is a major importer of various legumes including common bean; however, there is a huge potential to grow common beans Nationally. On the basis of experimental trials in the botanical garden and research field of University of Malakand, several common bean varieties are able to grow in this region. To select the candidate lines for various regions of Pakistan, multi-location trials will be conducted at PGRI (NARC), Sheringle Dir-Upper, Kalam and Naran. Further, these lines will be studied for disease incidence, environmental stresses and crop yield. Finally, the most suitable lines for each location will be selected on the basis of yield and resistance to disease. In addition, it is well known that legume have diverse and rich microflora, specifically rhizobia found in the nodules and other rhizospheric bacteria. The isolation of these bacteria will help us to disclose the plant growth promoting (PGP) bacteria and its effect on soil nutritional quality. The isolated strains will be further characterize for drought and/or salinity conditions according to the climate of that area in which common bean will be grown. After characterization, the plant growth promoting and drought/salt tolerant potential bacteria could be used as a bio-fertilizer. Overall, our aim is to commercialize the common bean candidate lines and explore its microbiota for bio-fertilizer.

data.projectName: Epidemiologic studies of sleep disorder in adult Pakistani population, its major risk factors and associated diseases
data.projectDigest: Sleep is one of the most important function of life. Human sleeps one third of his life. Disturbance in sleep or quality of sleep leads to number of dysfunctions of human body. Lifestyle and daily base activities of older individuals are correlated with sleep disorder. I will investigate prevalence of sleep disorder, association with other health problems in older educational population of Punjab, Pakistan. To assess sleep patterns, sleep disorders, prevalence and associated health problems in educational population including school education and higher education. I will make a wide survey among educational population. Survey will be done through a questionnaire. Different questions about sleep, physical activity, lifestyle and mood will be asked to participants and note their response. After assessing sleep patterns and recognizing people who will be suffering from sleep disorders I will go for assessment of associated health problems among participants. For this purpose, I will check and note blood pressure and I will take blood samples of 100 participants to perform CBC test so that I will be able to assess other health issues in those participants who will be suffering from sleep disorders.

The social pressure to build house, ends up in several eventualities like tense marital life, divorces, murders and suicides, mainly because of the motives that are directly or indirectly linked to the unbearable cost of house building. In the case of Pakistan, population explosion and unplanned urbanization coupled with consistent neglect of housing on the part of Govt. has made this problem more ever severe and compelling. 
So adequate, stable and affordable housing framework is required not only to provide shelter to citizens but also to secure law and order in society and for psychological well being of young middle and lower class population. There is lack of clarity that what constitutes the adequate or affordable housing in the context of Pakistani middle class, the answer however is not RCC (Reinforced Cement Concrete) as it is high cost construction and employees’ high-tech materials, advanced construction technologies and systems.
Rammed Earth construction could serve as promising answer not only to the sheltering requirements of low income middle class of Pakistan but also indirectly provide answers to environmental and energy considerations as rammed earth construction reduces the carbon foot print and uses a method of centuries old building technique with a modern as contemporary rammed earth uses a mix high quantity of low and low quantity of high tech materials.
One obvious objective of this project is to introduce this method of low cost, environment friendly and energy efficient method of construction as a viable alternative to RCC  and overcome the prevalent skepticism about Rammed Ea

data.projectName: Towards transactive energy system – Blockchain based smart grid framework
data.piUniversity: Sarhad University of Science and Information Technology, Peshawar
data.projectDigest:
here is a huge dependency on a utility provider (respective DESCO) which acts as an intermediary as well. A prosumer (Electricity producer + consumer) can not sell its surplus electricity to the neighboring consumer. Rather it has to go through the DESCO which creates a monopoly and revenue reduction for the respective prosumer. Furthermore, the existing centralized electricity management system controlled by the utility provider has failed in services such as interrupted electricity, quality of services, and real-time pricing. 
A distributed peer-to-peer energy trading model will maximize the profits for the electricity producers while at the same time it will provide uninterrupted electricity with better quality and economical rates to the end consumers. Through this approach, the consumer shall also get rid of indigenous backup solutions. The distribution infrastructure will strengthen since the supply and demand requirement is met locally with fewer line losses.

data.projectName: Enhance Research and Educational Cababilities via Establishment of Research and Medical Genetic Service at National Institute of Child Health (NICH)
data.projectDigest:
This research and development project aims to establish a first-ever comprehensive medical genetics service in a public hospital that would include a designated medical genetics clinic, a state-of-the-art genetics laboratory, and a genetic counseling training program at NICH (second largest children hospital of Pakistan), to serve hundreds of children and their families with genetic disorders. The need of establishment of this clinic rides on the shoulders of a much larger need to (i) train the local physicians in medical genetics, (ii) conduct research on population-specific genetic variants and management and prevention of genetic disorders, and (iii) spread awareness of hereditary disorders among the general population.   the high burden of genetic disorders in this patient population, there is no structured clinical genetics service currently available in the country. Irrespective of their socioeconomic strata, children with genetic disorders and their families do not have full access to this integral aspect of clinical medicine. The reason for this is two folds: (i) a lack of trained genetics experts, and (ii) a shortage of advanced genetic testing laboratories.ne with the sustainable developmental goals, this project aims to develop a comprehensive clinical genetic service and training program at NICH by:
a) establishing a telemedicine genetics clinic at NICH staffed by the US-trained medical geneticist and genetic counselors.
b) to upgrade capabilities of an already existed , self-sustaining genetics laboratory facility to perform state-of-the-art genetic testing.
c) to initiate a first of its kind, comprehensive genetic counseling certification course.

Pakistan with a population of over 220 million has a pediatric population of 35%, one of the largest in the world. With the high incidence of interfamily marriages in Pakistan, there is a high incidence of inherited disorders and birth defects among children. Medical genetics plays a vital role in the diagnosis, management, and prevention of these disorders. This service is currently not available in Pakistan due to a lack of research infra structure and trained genetic professionals and advanced genetic laboratory testing. data.projectName: Financial Literacy, Gamification and Decision Making: An Overview of Practice, Research and Policy Guidelines for Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Financial products and services have become increasingly accessible to public at large. Exponential growth in financial products, the complication in financial markets, and changes in demographic, political and economic factors motivates the need of financial literacy. Financial literacy can help people to evaluate battery of risks and opportunities associated with financial industry and it contributes to improve financial decision-making of public at large and benefit to economy and society. But conventional ways such as lecture based static learning, classroom exercises and face-to-face learning activities often seems boring. There is a need to make financial education engaging, pleasurable, and interactive called Gamification. The objective of this project is to compare the level of financial literacy of public at large of two selected districts i.e. Sahiwal and Rawalpindi on the basis of several grounds and develop a computer/mobile application i.e. provide gamified solution of this issue at both the selected districts in local language of the districts. This increase in financial literacy will help to improve household saving decision, & investment decision of the local residents. Therefore, it will help to remove the poverty, and increase the level of quality education which will contribute to the economic growth of the districts.

data.projectName: Productivity Conundrum, Stagnant Growth, and Unemployment: The Case of Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Development Economics (PIDE), Islamabad
data.projectDigest:
The 8th goal of Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) aims at Promoting sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all. However, provision of productive employment to the ever expanding labor force is a major challenges for the State. Employment is generated by sustainable economic growth driven by high level of investment. However, Pakistan has not been able to attract high levels of investment and achieve sustainable economic growth. Low investment and growth is the result of lower firm productivity. Diagnosing the drivers of the firm productivity is, therefore, critical for growth and employment. Understanding the nature of lower labor and firm productivity is important for ensuring high growth and provision of productive employment. 

In Pakistan, labor and firm’s productivity is declining over the years. Despite technological revolution, the productivity of firms has been stagnant in Pakistan. During the last couple of decades, per-hour output productivity has declined substantially and has been taken over by China, India, and Bangladesh. The decline in labor and firm productivity has resulted in declining of total factor productivity and growth thereby reducing the State’s economic capacity to generate enough employment opportunities to absorb the expanding labor force.

data.projectName: Identification of viral strain in poultry industry could help us safeguard economic losses
data.piUniversity: Mirpur University of Science and Technology (MUST), AJ&K
data.projectDigest:
In the past three decades, commercial poultry production in Pakistan expanded rapidly. Small scale rural poultry farming has emerged as a profitable commercial enterprise and is being transformed into elaborate business, now refer to as poultry industry. Poultry products being the richest sources of high quality animal protein for human consumption play an important role in promoting health and vitality of the people. Poultry products meet the protein requirements of human nutrition but there is a wide gap between the availability and demand of animal protein in Pakistan, compare to other livestock products like beef, mutton and milk. Poultry products in the form of eggs and meet which can be obtained on a larger scale with greater efficiency of production in short period of time.
Efforts are needed to improve the production performance of broiler and poultry birds through interventions in breeding, management, and nutrition and disease control.
Some of the poultry diseases cause economic losses on large scale due to high rate of mortality. Amongst the various bacterial, viral and parasitic diseases, an infectious bursal disease (IBD) has gained significant economic importance.
The infectious bursal disease was first recognised in 1962 in Gumboro district of Delaware (USA), hence name. Currently it is an important disease of poultry throughout the world. In Pakistan the disease was rare up to 1983 but now it is widespread in commercial poultry and inflicts heavy losses.

data.projectName: Metal free nanocomposite based electrochemical sensors for the assessment and quantification of electrochemically active nitrogen rich adulterants in local animal milk samples of district Sialkot:
data.piUniversity: Government College for Women University, Sialkot
data.projectDigest: Food adulteration is of global concern and can be directly related to the sustainable development goal of human health and well-being. A huge proportion of population in Sialkot relies on local milk resources. Unfortunately, in Pakistan, adulteration of milk is common practice. In this scenario, the role of Government accredited quality control laboratory is to facilitate the qualitative identification of adulterants in milk samples. Thus, there is utmost need to develop a simple, low cost and efficient analytical tool that could monitor and quantify adulterants in local milk samples. In order to make the false protein content in adulterated milk, nitrogen rich adulterants are commonly added. These nitrogen based adulterants can pose serious health problems to human beings. Concentration of these adulterants above the recommended level can cause indigestion, acidity, ulcers, urolithiasis and bladder cancer. Unfortunately, conventional analytical techniques are failed to detect this false protein content. In this perspective, metal nanoparticles based electrochemical sensors have emerged as a suitable and efficient analytical tool for adulterant determination in milk and milk products. In this proposed study, metal free nanocomposite based electrochemical sensors will be employed for the quantitative determination of nitrogen rich adulterants in local milk samples.

data.projectName: Capacity Building of District Education Authority and Development of Inclusive Evaluation System
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) number 4 particularly stress on quality education as it is the key to improved employment, reduced inequality and providing the individuals with equal opportunities. Rahim Yar Khan (RYK) is the industrial hub of Punjab yet the performance of the education sector is extremely inadequate. According to a report by Alif Ailan and SDPI, despite Punjab ranking high across provinces, RYK fares at the 32nd position within Punjab out of 36 districts and 68th nationwide (Alif Ailaan & SDPI, 2016). This indicates the dire need of improving the governance structure of the already devolved education sector. This research proposal aims to improve the governance system through capacity building of district education authority’s workers and incorporating the feedback of parents, students and teachers through a smartphone app that adds to the dashboard of data accessible by provincial and district administrative teams. The proposal suggests holding training for data analysis and budget making of district education officers, deputy education officers, assistant education officers and the school head teachers. Despite having the powers of annual planning and management of resources and staff, these officers lack the ability to analyze the data and utilize the findings to drive the policy making.

data.projectName: Managing Irrigation Water Resources for solving water scarcity in Province Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: Towards improving water usage, adoption of irrigation technologies and pricing
data.projectDigest: The province Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is currently facing water scarcity problem which resultantly barrened some of the agriculture lands and orchards. The increasing demand for food, cultivation of more water consuming crops, increasing water losses, use of traditional irrigation methods, nominal Abyana charges and ineffective water institutions calls for managing existing water resources. This research aims to make situational analysis of the water productivity and water use efficiency with suggesting ways to improve water usage in the agriculture sector of KP; estimate the virtual water trade and crop water footprint to have informed policy for supporting water consuming crops; identify the best available irrigation technologies’ practices followed by their adoption by the farmers to save water; evaluate the current structure of water charges and its recovery with suggesting options to determine the water prices through market forces using contingent valuation approach; evaluate the existing institutional arrangements for irrigation management and irrigation technology adoption and water pricing and to identify the potential gaps/ pitfall in KP. This study will use both qualitative and quantitative approaches and will be conducted in collaboration with academia and relevant industry addressing the SDGs 6

data.projectName: Transforming Municipal Solid Waste into Eco-Friendly Renewable Fuel
data.piUniversity: Mirpur University of Science and Technology (MUST), AJ&K
data.projectDigest: Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) is the fourth largest global emissions contributor. The major cities in Pakistan generate approximately 30-40 million tons of MSW (approx.65%organic, 35%inorganic) every year. Most of the country’s waste ends up landing in streets, roads, empty plots, water reservoirs, sewerage lines or landfills. The mismanagement and inappropriate dumping and burning of MSW are creating serious social, environmental, and health issues such as urban flooding, air and water pollution, toxic smog and the greenhouse effect leading to climate change and thus, risking the lives of the community. The recent urban flooding in Karachi is a result of the clogging of sewerage lines and drainage systems because of MSW accumulation. In this context, instead of dumping or burning of MSW, waste to energy conversion technologies need to be employed so that most of MSW is recycled and converted into an invaluable, sustainable and eco-friendly source of energy. This proposal suggests using Hydrothermal Technology for the conversion of MSW into renewable fuels which can be further used in brick and cement kilns and thus, reduce import bills in addition to the reduced environmental pollution. This circular economy approach can create new business opportunities as well as jobs for the locals.

data.projectName: Esterase Inhibitors As Possible Therapeutic Agent In Alzheimer's Disease & Cognitive Aging isolated from Terrestrial Plants and marine resources: Approach  to Explore and  Improve Mental Health Related Issues In Society
data.projectDigest: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is an age-associated neurodegenerative disorder and most common form of dementia in elderly people. Currently, 45 million people are affected worldwide and estimated to be doubled in next twenty years.  As there is no cure available, this project is designed to investigate bioactivities of novel compounds extracted from various unidentified marine and land resources. Based on initial In-vitro screening and computational analysis of novel neuroprotective compounds, in-vivo studies will be performed on AD animal models. In second phase, genetic expression of AD related genes in AD patients of Pakistani population will be analyzed to develop baseline data for the first time in Pakistan. Ultimately, this study would help to develop new therapies to prevent multiple age-associated conditions via discovery of novel marine/land resources, as therapeutic agents against AD. By expanding the horizon of the project from lab to society, mental health care center will be established to create awareness among people with provision of consultancy services. This platform will be used to collect scientific data at national level for Govt Officials with constitution of Alzheimer’s Association of Pakistan while medicinally important marine resources will be conserved in marine technology park.

data.projectName: Volumetric changes in Oropharyngeal Airway in class II patients treated with functional appliance: A comparative three – dimensional Cone Beam Computed Tomography study
data.projectDigest: Patients present to orthodontists usually for treatment of their malaligned teeth. Most of these patients in Pakistan have a small lower jaw as well. This discrepancy in jaw size is suggested in international studies to lead in narrowing of the respiratory tract leading to future respiratory diseases, obstructive breathing and snoring and sleep apnea. In our study we have to use an advanced x-ray machine called the CBCT which measures in 3 dimensions (3D) instead of 2 dimensions (2D) like other x-ray machine and can measure the volume of the upper part of respiratory tract. This CBCT will used to measure change in the airway volume before and after treatment of the small lower jaw by the orthodontist. This will aid in better treatment planning and early treatment will save the future cost of many other problems related to narrow airway.

data.projectName: Comparative transcriptome profiling between Gossypium arboreum and Gossypium hirsutum to identify biotic and abiotic stress mechanisms and benefits of foliar nutrition on these stresses.
data.projectDigest: This project addresses SDG’s pertaining to “No Poverty” and “Zero Hunger”. Most of the cotton cultivated land in Pakistan is owned by small farmers. Yield losses and fewer incentives for the farmers over the years have generated economic loss fear across the small farmer’s community suffering from deteriorating socio economic conditions. This fear has resulted in the contraction of cotton cultivated area from 3 million to 2.3 million hectares since 2015 to 2018.  The decrease in cotton productivity has directly impacted the country’s 39% labor associated with agriculture, and have miserably effected their livelihood. Additionally, the use of foreign exchange for cotton fiber import is another burden on the economy of Pakistan.  American cotton (Gossypium hirsutum) is cultivated over 99% of the area under cotton cultivation in Pakistan. The production of cotton is labor and cost intensive. The biotic (viruses and sucking insects) and abiotic (heat, drought and salinity) stresses have resulted in decreased productivity. This proposal addresses the improvement of cotton production by foliar nutrient sprays and exploring the novel genetic mechanisms in Gossypium arboreum which has the natural stress tolerance capability.

data.projectName: Fully Automatic Baking and Rotimatic Machine
data.piUniversity: Sir Syed University of Engg. & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The new tradition of life is to convert all manual works into accurately done by machines. Therefore, we proposed a fully automatic Tortilla, Chapati, Pita, Bread Baking and Cake (TCPBBC) maker machine (TMM). There are many machine available in the market for almost every task to do in the kitchen, there are mixers, grinders, coffee makers, and dishwashers to name a few. In comparison, there aren’t high capacity automatic TMM appliances available in the local (Pakistan) market. One of the major reasons for this could be the fact that TMM making isn’t a generic and mechanical process as chopping, grinding or wiping. It is a highly complex task and requires significant human labor. It requires estimating the correct quantity of ingredients for mixing and kneading the dough, and skill to roll it into a perfectly round shape. It continues to know the optimum temperature to roast the rolled out dough to get puffed steaming golden brown TCPBBC. TCPBBC making are multiple skills that acquired different skills workers and perfection in all task need practice and patience. Doing these tasks with machine makes designing very complex and all processes are quite a challenging. There has been some manually operable and semi-automatic roti making devices in the market but they are not multipurpose, low capacity and not fully automatic.

data.projectName: Renewable Energy: An Integrated Approach with Sustainability and affordability in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan’s energy mix mainly relies on gas, oil and coal and this dependence has serious consequences due to the depleting reserves of oil and gas and also that it is detrimental to environment. All the stake holders need to gear up the efforts to utilize the renewable energy at affordable and sustainable ways in communities. Renewable energy share has to be increased in overall energy mix of the country for a sustainable and clean & green Pakistan.

The integrated hybrid system will reduce the unavailability of energy due to intermittent nature of standalone wind or solar system. The wind turbine will be fabricated locally in order to promote the local industry and high tech research will be carried out in solar cell and batteries to improve the solar cell performance and storage battery.

data.projectName: Maternal and Neonatal Health Transformation through advanced mHealth Novel Application in  Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Neonatal mortality as well as maternal mortality are considerably high in Pakistan as compared to the rest of the developed world. More than half of the births are either unattended or attended by untrained personnel. 

Healthcare workers (HCWs) along with the mothers can effectively contribute in early neonatal care but unfortunately they too lack the knowledge and necessary training.  Providing essential training to healthcare workers and raising awareness in a low literate population may help in timely care thus saving precious lives of babies. 

In the recent years, the accelerated advancement of Information and Communication technology in healthcare system led to the development of mobile health (mHealth) and brought sustainable changes in healthcare services

Our objective is to develop mHealth application that would help by providing standardize care information for the mother, her fetus and the newborn at appropriate times.

data.projectName: Human Activity Recognition for Obsessive Compulsive Disorder
data.projectDigest: Health is strongly connected with socio-economic development as a healthy population lives longer and is more productive for the society. Better health and well-being of individuals both physically and psychologically helps in acquiring better education and employment which also leads to poverty reduction. Ultimately this makes possible the socio-economic development of the society through the effect on all important factors i.e., education, employment, and income. The increasing importance of mental health and psychological well-being has been well documented lately. Among the various mental health disorders, Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (OCD) has become increasingly common, especially among the younger population. Recognizing the importance of this disorder, the objective of our proposal is to create a system, based on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, that can assist in the determining the intensity and behavioral aspects of this disorder among patients and to provide doctors a tool for its detailed monitoring. To make this system, we propose to use inertial sensors such as accelerometer, gyroscope and magnetometer which are commonly available in smartphone and smartwatch devices. A deep learning based algorithm, which relies on such big data, is proposed to recognize the behaviors and would be used to generate reports based on these recognitions.

data.projectName: LCF:  Industrializing Peanut Sector of Chakwaal through Technology, Policy and Governance
data.projectDigest:
The farmers of Chakwaal needs crop varieties that do not demand much water and can survive and grow on rain water only. The land of Chakwaal is very fertile and rich. Along with other crops, the peanut is widely cultivated in the Chakwaal. The farmers struggle a lot for six months long to produce a peanut crop. They earn almost nothing from peanut if cost of human resource and land is calculated. They are small holdings of 20-30 kenals. The farmer community most belong to the poor families and remains under poverty due to very less income. 

The project is planned to address the above challenges and start industrialization for peanut industry of Pakistan. The project will achieve SDGs there as rural income will increase, poverty will decrease, quality of life will improve and living standard will rise. The project will achieve an integrated development of peanut cluster under cluster innovation concept. The project will be planned and done by Riphah Institute of Public policy along with Bin Qutab Foundation as implementation partner and other collaborators like Sargodha University Agriculture college, Indus Pak Corporation (agri engineering company), CPAD-IRP for monitoring and evaluation and local farmers.

data.projectName: GIS Disease Mapping: Tracking of diseases, observing trends and making policies for timely intervention
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is the 5th largest population in the world according to the statistics of 2019. Pakistan is facing a double burden of disease (BoD). Infectious diseases like tuberculosis, hepatitis B and C, malaria are endemic and affecting somewhere around 20% of the Pakistani Population. The overall HIV prevalence is still below 1% but with high rates of unscreened blood transfusions and currently 7.6% of drug abusers, an upward trend is obvious. Non-Communicable Diseases; diabetes, hypertension along with Injuries and Mental health now constitute the other half of BoD. The purpose of surveillance is to empower decision makers to lead and manage more effectively by providing timely, useful evidence . Our aim is to develop a centralized real-time GIS-based Disease Surveillance System (GIS-DSS) and provide a spatial epidemiological platform to understand disease geographic variation and related social, behavioral and environmental determinants for timely interventions and policy development.

data.projectName: Developing Technological Solutions to Improve Road Safety
data.piUniversity: Sir Syed University of Engg. & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
1. Road crashes impact the socioeconomic growth of a country. Most of the victims of road crashes are young motorbike riders, who contribute significantly to the family earning an overall country’s economy. According to the statistics published by Road Traffic Injury Research & Prevention Centre (RTIRPC) for the year 2015, around 30,000 people were injured, and more than 1,000 lost their lives in road crashes. About 45% of the total injuries reported to RTIPRPC were male between 16 to 30 years of age. Motorbikes and pedestrians have been identified as the most vulnerable road users. A significant number of road crashes can be saved by developing the solutions for the main causes of accidents identified through the data collected by RTIRPC during 2007-15. 
2.	Local Challenges
The following challenges will be addressed in this research:
i.	At present, drivers do not worry about their speeds on roads in Karachi, as there are no posted speed limits and no mechanism in place to penalize over speeding drivers. 
ii.	In the absence of posted speed limits, speed limit enforcement cannot be performed. 
iii.	No scientifically estimated speed limits exist in Karachi and other cities of Pakistan.
iv.	Various types of speed humps are observed and constructed on various roads. There is no standard, and there is no study on the usefulness and shortcomings of various types of speed humps.
v.	Wrong-way movements are observed frequently on all roads, and there are no measures in place to control it.
vi.	Signalized intersections have been removed without considering its implications on road safety. Does it improve congestion at the network level? What are its consequences on the safety of road users, especially pedestrians?

data.projectName: Prototype Development of a Novel Reconfigurable Multiband Bandpass analog Filter for 5G Wireless Communication Systems
data.projectDigest:
Modern wireless communication systems have a significant impact on today's society and the world economy. The typical applications include modern military and civil radar systems, 5th generation cellular radio technologies, and entertainment through satellite television. RF and microwave filters are one of the core components in all these systems, which are generally used to distinguish between wanted and unwanted signal frequencies.
The analog RF and microwave filters are used to perform various tasks, including frequency selectivity, spectrum allocation, interference reduction, and frequency multiplexing. Hence, to perform these tasks, more than one filter is required in the wireless transceivers. Moreover, these modern wireless systems have stringent requirements on compactness, lightweight, and cost-effectiveness. 
In this project, a noval miniaturized and cost-effective reconfigurable multiband bandpass filter for 5G wireless systems is proposed. The multiband performance will reduce system cost, size, and weight. For example, if a wireless system requires three frequency bands of operations, then three different bandpass filters are generally deployed to handle each frequency band. However, the single triband filter will obtain all three required frequency bands, reducing the overall cost of the system. Moreover, the reconfigurable properties of a bandpass filter will be useful in frequency tuning and can adjust the electrical parameters for better frequency response after fabrication. The potential local market is the upcoming 5G wireless technologies.

Pakistan gets a significant economy boost by investing in the digital economy. The backbone of the digital economy is communication system technologies. Like other countries, Pakistan needs to implement 5G systems soon. 
Analog filters play a very vital role in the designing of 5G systems. data.projectName: Survey and Documentation of Energy Conservation Literacy of Pakistan for the Promotion of Sustainable Development
data.projectDigest: The energy conservation literacy is the competency and motivation to use energy knowledge in a useful manner to practice, communicate, and participate in society for sustainable development. This study explains energy literacy dynamics of Pakistan keeping in view Douglass North’s theory of Institutions integrating formal and informal perspectives affecting the energy conservation literacy. It also assesses the sustainable energy practices by approaching the literature on ‘Sustainable Development Goals’ (SDGs) supported by UNDP. The 7th SDG is to ensure universal access to affordable and clean energy by 2030. The study deliberates the overarching question: How much is the prevalence of energy conservation literacy among the stakeholders in the energy systems  of Pakistan; and how it can be raised? Specific argument of the study is, “The relationship between dimensions of energy conservation literacy and formal/ informal institutions have affected the dimensions of energy governance of Pakistan.” The particular objective of the research is to explore the level of energy literacy among the producers and the consumers of energy and to raise the energy literacy to promote the SDGs 2015.

data.projectName: Real time monitoring of water supply at Karachi Water & Sewerage Board (KWSB) Pumping Stations
data.projectDigest:
Water is the most important part of life. With the increase in population, its shortage has been felt all around the world. Karachi is also suffering with this issue where Karachi Water & Sewerage Board (KWSB) is responsible to supply water in major areas of Karachi.
Unfortunately, KWSB lags in automation of its system. Proper water management and consumption data at sector level are missing, therefore water supply issues are increasing day by day. Due to absence of proper mechanism for leakage detection in pipelines including illegal connections, missing of announced water distribution scheduling in real time and no record of water utilization data at sector level, ultimately causes mental stress and financial burden on the consumers. 
Lot of water is being wasted as a result of this lack of information which affects badly on country’s economy. The consumers have to purchase water by paying money to private or government tankers. With no proper monitoring of water supply, pumping staff unfairly distribute water for some of their personal benefits.
All these problems can be solved by proper real time monitoring of water supply along with its datalogging whose access is available to all of the stakeholders.

data.projectName: Achieving Universal Health Coverage in Pakistan: Strengthening the public insurance for the vulnerable communities.
data.projectDigest:
In Pakistan, a total of 0.5 million children and 9,700 mothers 
die prematurely every year, and a large fraction of these deaths occurred in the vulnerable communities. The poor household also face highest burden of non-communicable disease including heart disease, diabetes, cancer, and injuries. Majority of these deaths could be avoided if the poor had access to better quality medical care. Access to quality healthcare is costly and limited due to the affordability. The inexpensive public hospitals are overburdened and cannot serve the huge health care demand in the country. Government of Pakistan is providing free of cost private hospital care to poor through public insurance Sehat Sahulat Program (SSP). Relatively little is known that how effective is this new intervention and what services are still missing to the poor. Proposed multidisciplinary project partners with SSP to study the SSP program for Tharparkar District (one of the most impoverished regions in the country), patients/users and provider of the services will be studied in detail. The lessons will be drawn to upscale the public insurance in the country and ascertain the missing health care services. The main focus will be to identify measures to strengthen the universal healthcare insurance mechanism that can potentially save millions of lives across Pakistan in the vulnerable communities.

data.projectName: Women’s Informal Micro and Small Enterprises  in District Mardan Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: The Challenges and Opportunities
data.projectDigest: country. Despite nearly half of the country population female labor force participation is extremely low in formal employment sector in the country. It is statistically shown in Pakistan Labor Force Survey 2017-18 that among the female labor force participation rate in rural setting it’s covered only 22.3% in formal sector while 77.7 % women are engaged in informal sector in rural areas. The main reason of informal women workers in Pakistan is poverty and gender discrimination in formal employment. Informality is associated with less access to finance, gender discrimination, social norms which restrict women outer mobility and interaction with men and men dominated markets. It is very important to recognize the skilled women informal micro and small business as one of the major contributor to national economy.

data.projectName: Integrated water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) management for semi-urban and rural communities: benchmarking study for Kotli Azad Kashmir
data.piUniversity: University of Kotli Azad Jammu and Kashmir
data.projectDigest: The sustainability of water resources in AJ&K is threatened by not only by climate change but also by population growth and pollution of water resources. This situation calls for special water use strategies for sustainability of water resources. Project objectives include strengthening of knowledge base of water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) for informed decision making, developing reliable decision making support tools, optimal modelling for customized needs and operationalizing WASH management systems. This will be a first ever comprehensive bench marking study that will present a situation analysis of current processes and performances, identify potential opportunities as well as challenges faced by stake holders. The research project will be based on a combination of primary and secondary data. Unpublished data of governmental agencies and international comparative models will be used for customizing optimal model for local settings. Final research paper will be helpful to policy maker for better future planning and implementation of WASH management strategies. The research Project is in line with national agenda of government’s efforts towards Goal 6 of SDGs (clean Water and sanitation). The co-benefits of the project through forward and backward linkages will lead to coverage of other SDGs like climate action and improved health

data.projectName: Applications of m-polar fuzzy set in decision making problems
data.projectDigest: For the growth and development of democratic countries, free and fair elections are required. An accountability is essential for such kind of elections. It is necessary for the peaceful environment of society and for the justice of all political parties. It is a major part of sustainable development goals. But Pakistan’s elections in this respect is a bit depraved. Due to this, the winner is blamed of allegedly rigging by all defeated parties after elections and terms the elections unfair. There is a special need to give a right decision for elections. Since Pakistan is a multi-party democratic country where in the national and Provincial assemblies, political parties are appeared for competition of seats. Particularly, in district Gujrat, political parties are PMLQ, PPP, PMLN, PTI and any independent candidates. There is always a hard competition between them. It a big challenge in Gujrat as well as in Pakistan. To handle the hard problems occurring in elections, we can use the model based on m-polar fuzzy set to select the appropriate candidate conveniently. This would increase the reliability of that selected party between its followers and the voters. [1] An m-polar fuzzy set on R is exactly a function I:R??[0,1]?^m. This concept has both theoretical and real life applications. It can be also used in decision making problems. For this, it is required to meet the group consent. Also, it occurs when a company selects which design for manufactured goods and when a family decides to visit any place. Here, we consider the case of election in the district Gujrat by using the concept of m-polar fuzzy set.

data.projectName: Particulate matter emission reduction in urban air using diesel particulate filter (DPF) and local manufacturing of related solutions through capacity enhancement of local industry.
data.projectDigest: Poor urban air quality has negative health affects and are linked to higher chances of asthma, cardio-vascular diseases and cancer especially among the aged population of big cities. The buses and trucks especially with older engines emit black smoke due to poor engine performance and the absence of a exhaust gas cleaning devices. Poor fuel quality also plays an important role in the higher than normal emissions. Black smoke is basically carbon nano-particles which are produced due to inefficient burning of fuel inside the engine cylinder. The cost and time required to improve the fuel quality and replacing older diesel engines is too high. An immediate solution in the short-term is to retrofit old vehicles and engines with diesel particulate filters which has been successfully employed in Europe, USA and other advanced countries during the last two decades. In the long term, diesel engine and fuel quality should be gradually improved to meet the environment regulations being adopted when the  required technology and knowledge becomes available locally through research and innovation. This project will help prove the feasibility of employing exhaust cleaning devices for diesel engines as the most economical solution to improve air quality of big cities like Lahore.  The training and education opportunities will prepare local academia and industry to develop affordable and innovative solutions adapted to local market and economy.

The increased costs of medical treatment and loss of work hours due to poor air quality are estimated to be in billions of dollars per year in Europe. data.projectName: Evaluating performance and productivity of heat stressed cows fed with selenium enriched probiotics as feed supplement
data.projectDigest: Dera Ismail Khan is considered as a hard area owing to its harsh environment. The environmental temperature often goes beyond 50C during summer season which is a potential threat to animal as well as human population. About more than 70% of population of DI Khan lives in the rural area where their livelihood is related to livestock production. The potential threat to livestock production is a heat stress during summer season which inflicts the farmer’s community with economic losses. Owing to the lack of proper housing and management systems for animals such as cattle, sheep and goats they are more prone to heat stress during high ambient temperature. Milk production and meat production is decreased. Their immunity is decreased and become susceptible to other diseases as well. Most of the animals die due to heat stroke. Heat stress morbidity and mortality can be reduced through feed management and using various feed additives. Selenium enriched probiotics are considered as anti-stress. They reduce oxidative stress, inflammation and regulate liver functions during heat stress due to high ambient temperature. We believe that selenium enriched probiotics as a feed additive will be able to substantially decrease the untoward effects of heat stress during summer season, will restore the productivity, and eventually will prevent the economic losses to the poor farmer’s community.

data.projectName: Challenge to increase the production of ranges and improve the socio-economic condition of growers of Haripur District.
data.projectDigest: Pakistan exported record 24% of its total orange production in 2017-18 which helped to earned precious foreign exchange. However area and production of fruit is continuously decreasing over the last few decades. In kyber Pakhtunkhwa, total area under citrus cultivation was 4.8 thousand hectares in 2000-01 which reduced to 3.9 thousand hectares in 2017-18 with production of 40.2, and 30.3 thousand tonnes, respectively. Reduction in yield has compelled the formers to abandon the cultivation of orange which is creating sever financial problem for resource poor farmers. Our previous HEC funded study showed that orange growing areas of Haripur district are severely deficient in soil organic carbon which implies that soils have already lost their productivity. Application of conventional manure is not sustainable as it decomposes quickly. In this scenario, biochar is best known to restore soil health and increase production of several crops. data.projectName: Identifying key socio-economic divers of forest conversion for policy interventions in Dir-Khoistan Forest Division
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Benazir Bhutto University, Sheringal, Dir
data.projectDigest: In mountain areas of Pakistan millions of people living in or around the forest depend directly on forest for food, income and employment. Deforestation continues at high rate and not only effecting the lives and livelihood of mountains people but also responsible for the miseries of lowland people through floods.  Existing command and control policies failed because they focus on the forest sector alone, when in fact, poverty, households’ dependence on forest for food and income are the primary causes of deforestation. Research and policy action that consider multiple factors including those outside of the forest sector could slow down deforestation without effecting local’s income. Alternative polices that serve the twin objectives of conservation and poverty reduction require socio-economic analyses at the household level to understand factors that in?uence forest clearing decisions. This understanding will help policy makers to identify families for the interventions to stop deforestation. Specifically, the study will answer key questions for policy interventions regarding forest clearing. Forest clearing is area specific, in some countries rich and middle income groups are involved as they have resources while in other areas poor people are found guilty as they have the needs. Also, how households’ clearing varies with family size, off-farm employment, value of physical and natural resources, social status, tenure rights, access to market etc. are important research questions whose answers would help policy makers to identify families for interventions.

data.projectName: The Implementation of Mental Health Programme for Strengthening Primary Health Care in District Peshawar
data.piUniversity: Kohat University of Science and Technology, Kohat
data.projectDigest: The number of people experiencing mental health problems worldwide is reported to have risen to nearly epidemic proportions among youth adults and aged. This problem hits the whole world specifically amid the Covid-19 pandemic where the people were mentally depressed and tortured, though they were not infected. To minimize this issue and provide mental health facilities to the laymen, the department of Social Work has proposed this project to strengthen the primary health care with mental health care facilities. This project has two main components and will be conducted in two years as per the project guide lines. The first phase of the project is comprised of a research study that will be conducted in district Peshawar to highlight the underlying causes of mental health issues. In second phase sensitization campaign regarding mental health would run across the project locality with implementation of a proposed model. This phase will also include meetings with stakeholders, NGO’s working in this field, government authorities and policy makers to ensure inclusion and implementation of mental health in national policies. This model will achieve the mile stone of minimizing the mental health issue and will strive to eradicate will from society.

data.projectName: Formulation of cost-effective indigenous formula milk for meeting the nutritional demands of Pakistani children
data.projectDigest: The market for milk formulas is large and profitable. Globally, it’s worth 47 billion USD per year, and the value of sales is projected to increase significantly in the run up to 2020.  Pakistan is the 4th largest milk producer in the world however, post-milking losses are quite high due to the lack of cold storage facility, poor transportation systems and inadequate processing approaches. According the Asian Development Bank report, milk losses in Pakistan are ranged from 15-20% or even more. This is the reason; Pakistan spends a huge amount on the import of infant formula milk (US$ 185.8 million in 2018-19 in milk-based foods). Additionally, several health risks are associated with the consumption of commercial formula milk due to poor quality ingredients and addition of synthetic nutrients which can cause severe degenerative disorders. Therefore, it is vital to introduce some suitable and effective strategies to develop a safe and low-cost product with better quality and nutritional adequacy for effectively meeting the nutritional requirements of infants. In this regard, the proposed project is aimed at formulating the locally manufactured formula milk to meet the nutritional demands of children and to reduce the import cost of by introducing the pioneer indigenous formula milk in Pakistan.

Hence, it is direly needed to reduce the import cost of milk foods and overcome the deficiencies present in the available milk in the market by adopting proper processing and preservation approaches for effective handling and utilizing of the produced milk. Therefore, the proposed project is aimed at formulating the locally manufactured formula milk to meet the nutritional demands of Pakistani children and to improve the effective utilization and processing of locally produced milk, particularly from non-cattle sector which is the ignorant part from processing point of view. The project will also be helpful in discouraging the import of formula milk and therefore, would save foreign exchange. Moreover, this would be the first ever attempt to develop such product, locally. Furthermore, at present, imported baby formula milk cost is Rs. 1300 - 2600 per kg which is expected to be within Rs. 500 per kg in case of local recipe if developed through R&D. A

data.projectName: Molecular screening of hereditary intellectual disability in families from Azad Kashmir: A step towards genetic diagnosis
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest:
There are several types of intellectual disabilities and majority of these are not genetically characterized.  Collectively, these diseases affect 1/5,000 individuals. ID is considered as a big socioeconomic burden and health care challenge in both developed and developing countries. In most of the countries an increasing proportion of the health care and educational expenditures are allocated for the care of individuals with ID. 
A lot of research has been done on mental disorders in the world, but no significant research has ever been conducted in the Azad Kashmir region of Pakistan. Azad Kashmir due to its ethnic diversity and social customs, harbor large consanguineous families which ca be used to identify pathogenic mutations through next generation sequencing or Whole Exome Sequencing (WES). In recent past, Principal Investigator (PI) and Collaborators have reported two novel genes (TRMT1 and FMN2), which are involved in intellectual disability in Kashmiri families (Kathrin et al., 2018; Rosalind et al., 2014).  
Identification of ID causing genes in Kashmiri population can provide an opportunity to understand mental health in a better way. Although the progress in genetic studies, over the past two decades, has increased our understanding of various forms of intellectual disabilities, there are still unknown pathways that are essential for a normal brain development. PI has already identified significant number of families with intellectual disability from different regions of Azad Kashmir to identify the underlying mutations but research progress on these families is hampered due to the limitation of funding resources.

data.localySocioEco:
According to World Health Organization (WHO) report of 2017, mental health is an emerging problem that needs attention for the attainment of sustainable development goals (SDGs). WHO classified mental health problems into different types and some of these mental health issues are treatable. This study is focused on a specific type mental disorder i.e. intellectual disabilities (ID) for which underlying genetic factors are not completely known. Individuals with ID have limited cognitive abilities and are usually dependent on their families for routine life matters. The exploration of genetic players responsible for ID will help to understand and manage mental disorders in a better way. The current study will involve genetic analysis of more than 75 Kashmiri, Pakistani families segregating autosomal recessive ID by using Whole Exome Sequencing (WES). Identification of causative genes in these families will help to explain the genetic nature of ID in the Kashmiri population. 
Currently no specific treatment is available for genetic forms of intellectual disability. Therefore, genetic testing and carrier screening can serve as an important tool for management of families with IDs. Nevertheless, it is important that the correct diagnosis is made in order to provide accurate information on prognosis and to offer informed genetic counselling. Prenatal diagnosis is possible when the mutation (s) causing disease in the family is known. The expected results of this study will be helpful in the investigation of carriers of intellectual disability in suspected familial cases of Kashmiri population.

data.projectName: Development of Autosomal DNA Testing Kits and Population Databasing of Malakand Division
data.projectDigest: DNA typing has revolutionized crime-solving ability of the law enforcement agencies. It has become a valuable technology in forensic sciences. The DNA evidence is routinely presented in courts for different purposes. The evidence consists of combination of STRs which is called DNA profile. The difference in these STRs is length polymorphism i.e. they differ in length in different people. There is currently only one DNA-testing facility in our province which is overburdened. Our law enforcement agencies rarely, if ever, collect DNA samples from a crime scene. These agencies lack the commercially available kits due to their steep prices. The project plans to develop less expensive alternative to the imported commercially available DNA testing kit for use in forensic casework. Hence, we plan to study the allele frequencies in Pakhtun population. The population database may be of use to crime scene investigators, law enforcement agencies and courts of law to determine DNA profile matching of a suspect with that of a crime scene sample. With support of this population database, DNA testing in the Pakhtun population will become admissible evidence. The instant study will be a stepping stone forensic DNA testing and help in SDG of Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

data.projectName: Development of smart vaccine storage boxes
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan's polio eradication drive is facing severe challenges primarily owing to poor infrastructure. In days of vaccination drives, field workers face numerous challenges and one prime challenge is keeping the vile usable for longer durations of time. Especially the objective is safe delivery of vaccines/doses to remote areas for door-to-door activity. The mobile boxes are surely the current practice in field operation; however, it is weakest link in the whole cold-chain, which is used to keep the vile safe for longer durations particularly when working in scorching summer days. The loss of vile potency, owing to excessive exposure to heat through infiltration and/or 'cold burn' owing to unregulated temperature in storage box, is a prime reason for failure of several polio campaigns in past. Moreover, the potency & validity of vaccine vile has itself been the reason which has caused even loss of life owing to socio-religious pressures targeting the vile potency, its life & expiry.  

In the present project we are proposing a solution to fix the weakest link of the ‘cold-chain’ involved in the transportation of polio vaccines. The ‘mobile smart PCM box’ is proposed to be used with temperature regulation, integrated with IoT enabled sensing and regulating device in PCM (phase change material) packed box. This box shall transmit the actual variation of temperature within the box to the control-centres where the temperature and effectively the conditions of the vile can be monitored. The project shall equip the field workers with regulated, long duration, temperature controlled boxes which shall ensure the temperature regulation for safe vile delivery. The box shall provide the public confidence and reliability in the cold-supply chain of vaccine.

The goal of the project is to develop a reliable, long duration, temperature regulated cold storage for field operations and long distance transportation of polio vaccine vile. data.projectName: IOT BASED VERTICAL ORGANIC FARMING USING AEROPONICS / HYDROPONICS
data.piUniversity: Karachi Institute of Economics & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Vertical Farming Technique applies to agriculture process using vertical stacking in a controlled
environment. Using Hydroponics and Aeroponics technology, soil is substituted with liquid based
solution tanks or often nutrient based solution may just be sprayed. Vertical farming technique borrows concepts from green houses to artificially control humidity, temperature, light etc. Modern era technology allows superior control using Internet of Things (IoT) enabling distributed control of such environments in all situations at all times by placing all monitored parameters at a website and allowing remote control to actuators according to the wish of the farmer. This is especially suitable for agrobased economies like Pakistan’s which are facing increasingly drought-like situations and have dire shortage of water for suitable irrigation. By using IOT technology for intelligent vertical farming; new types of crops, genetically superior crops or yield of certain crops may be increased tremendously with minimal use of water and creation of an artificial climate if the natural climate is not favorable. Due to the use of controlled, closed environment, it is not necessary to use pesticides or herbicides. Due to increased urbanization and reduction of farming lands, vertical farming can ensure high yield with a small footprint of actual agricultural space. Another advantage is that food miles may be reduced to bring down price of food by bringing crop production closer to the cities.

data.localySocioEco: Balochistan covers 44% of the total land of the country making it the largest province of Pakistan. However, it has least population as compared to the other provinces of the country. It constitutes around 5% of the total country’s population and is the most underdeveloped province of the country with high rate of poverty. The overall housing condition in Balochistan due to multidimensional poverty comes out as terrible in comparison with other provinces. Only 23% houses in the province were made with burnt brick/blocks walls. On the other hand, 83%, 66%, and 54% of the houses in Punjab, Sindh, and KPK are made with burnt bricks/blocks walls, respectively. In similar way, 68% of the houses in Balochistan have mud walls while 15%, 28%, and 23% houses in Punjab, Sindh, and KPK have mud walls, respectively. Mud is locally available material and is most energy efficient building material due to its ease of processing. Mud has been broadly used for building construction in Pakistan. Advantages of earth include availability in large amount, low cost, easy to use and excellent fire resistance etc. However, it has some disadvantages, such as its durability, which can be affected by rain, wind, and others. It is imperative to improve the durability of mud construction materials. Therefore, this project will focus on the techniques and materials which will improve the durability of mud construction material.

data.projectName: Design and Commercialization Strategies for Emerging Technology based Products & Services in Developing Markets
data.projectDigest: A number of Pakistan-based companies are making use of the emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence and machine learning, to develop digital products and services (Khan, 2019). These technologies have brought opportunities for product design as well as new set of challenges that require innovative design and commercialization strategies (Verganti et al., 2020). Specifically, in emerging markets where the customer needs are distinct from their developed country counterparts and the market infrastructure is predominantly informal, these strategies need to align with the business environment in order to be effective (Radjou and Prabhu, 2012). Companies that understand these strategies have significant opportunities to unlock value (Anderson and Markides, 2007). By studying cases of digital products developed in Pakistan, this research would identify the design and commercialization strategies being adopted by technology firms in emerging markets and investigate the factors driving the success of these strategies. Since only 2% of the digital products being developed by startups in Pakistan are successful in the medium term (Jazz, 2017), an understanding of these strategies can lead to development of technology products with a better product-market fit and business sustainability (Hall et al., 2014).

data.projectName: Modelling doctors’ preferences to incentivise equitable access to health services in rural areas
data.projectDigest: This novel research idea focuses on the equitable access to health services in the rural areas of Pakistan to ensure good health and wellbeing which is the third sustainable development goal of the United Nations. This research is going to employ primary surveys and discrete choice modelling to investigate doctors’ willingness to practice in rural areas, as well as their preferred mode of practice, i.e. on-line health service, mobile hospital, or a clinic in a rural village. Based on the analysis, a set of recommendations will be developed to attract and retain doctors into providing health services in rural areas.

data.projectName: Study on comparative performance and acclimatization of different type of crossbred calves produced by crossing indigenous (Bos indicus) influenced crossbred cattle with exotic renowned beef breeds.
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest: Livestock are central to achieving many of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and directly relevant to most of them. The beef farming can improve the livelihood of both rural and urban low-income families.  Successful beef projects can be initiated in the state of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJ&K) through implementation of Research and Development. To do research on beef production is the need of time to increase the availability of protein for rapidly growing population. This study aims to investigate the adaptability of exotic breeds of beef in local environmental conditions and increase the livelihood generation of rural communities through beef production. A collaboration will be developed with the Department of Livestock AJ&K, NARC Islamabad, and Poonch University Rawalakot for animal husbandry and veterinary services. The exotic beef breed will be reared under intensive production systems. The performance of crossbred beef will be studied through different traits such birth weight, growth rate, daily body weight gain, mature body weight, meat quality, and tolerance to heat stress. As a result of this study an advisory group will be established for the provision of advisory services to the farming community interested in starting the beef farming at household or commercial level.

data.projectName: Characterization of venom genes of local snakes: A step to development of Recombinant Anti snake venom
data.piUniversity: Liaquat University of Medical and Health Sciences, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest: The snake bite envenoming is frequent in tropical regions and is cause of hundreds of the causalities annually. The WHO has declared snake bite envenomation as neglected tropical disease. The anti-snake venom (ASV) is the only available treatment to overcome and reduce the lethal consequences of venom and save the lives. Unfortunately, the available and the conventionally prepared ASV is not fully effective and preventive for all the patients; bitten by different snake species. Above all, it is not locally manufactured thus the availability of ASV and its health related consequences have significant socio-economic impact on the local population. It has been established that composition of snake venoms is variable among members of the same species due to geographical and environmental effects on the venom associated genes, so it is very first milestone to characterize the venom genes of local snakes to develop a synthetic recombinant ASV. Recently, the de novo genome of Indian Cobra has been revealed with maximum information about the genes encoding the toxin proteins, which constitute the core part of the venom. The present study has been aimed to characterize the venom genes of 4 big snakes of the genome, find genetic variations and its impact on the toxin proteins. This will be a milestone to the development of locally designed recombinant ASV.

data.projectName: Effects of Structured Physical Activity in Sarcopenic Elder Population
data.projectDigest:
Sarcopenia is an age related disorder that significantly declines the efficiency of musculoskeletal system by decreasing the muscle mass and force with resultant disability. As there is improvement in the quality of care, life expectancy and consequently the elder population is on the rise. Multiple risk factors of sarcopenia include the physical inactivity, malnourishment along with advancing age and gender. Aftermath of developing this condition results in increased risk of fall, decreased mobility and social independence and increased chances of frailty and mortality in elderly. Without the availability of the pharmacological intervention to the reversed the progression of this disease, main reliance is on the non-pharmacological interventions. There are also territorial differences in the prevalence of sarcopenia across the globe due to differences in ethnicity, race and physical activity levels. The role of physical activity and exercise is well established in reversing the age related the skeletal muscle mass and improvement in skeletal muscle strength. 
Pakistan is developing country in South Asian region. There is currently no sub specialty of geriatrics with elder people being treated and managed under the umbrella of medical practioner. European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People (EWGSOP) develops and updates consensus guidelines in diagnosing sarcopenia.  The Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia (AWGS) reports the need of different life style intervention to counteract the progression of this disease. Currently there is no data available to report the prevalence of sarcopenia in Pakistan. There is also a need to promote the importance of physical activity especially in the venerable population like elderly to promote their health and well being.

data.projectName: DETERMINE THE CAUSES OF ENDANGERMENT AND RURAL COMMUNITY INVOLVEMENT IN WILDLIFE CONSERVATION ACTIVITIES IN HIGH ALTITUDE FOREST ECOSYSTEMS
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Benazir Bhutto University, Sheringal, Dir
data.projectDigest: The proposed project will determine the causes of endangerment of wildlife and suggest on how to implement active participation of rural communities in conservation. Pakistan has the worst wildlife species endangerment rate as compared to other regions. Many wildlife species have become critically endangered, endangered, threatened and vulnerable due to human intervention, i.e., habitat loss and degradation due deforestation especially for agriculture expansion, human settlement, illegal trade of wildlife species, introduction of invasive species, climate change and pollution. These are major factors represent the risk not just to flora and fauna, but also cause food scarcity and increase human poverty. To address the issue of declining wildlife populations and halt the biodiversity loss in the proposed sites, a wildlife management strategy should be developed with the collaboration of rural communities. This will provide employment for rural communities and reduce the poverty. Overall, the goal of the project is to develop a new scientifically rigorous and standardized approach in the analysis and interpretation, and to identify the current status (demography), habitat requirements and threats to endangered species. The proposed project will ensure the involvement of rural communities and collaboration of wildlife department to reduce poaching or illegal hunting activities. This will reduce the risks of endangerments of wildlife species and enhance the population in the target areas.

data.projectName: Nano Catalyst based conversion of Biomass and solid waste into syngas for power generation
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Benazir Bhutto Women University, Peshawar
data.projectDigest:
Peshawar being the oldest city with a population of about 4 million generates more than 1000 tons of municipal solid waste/day. The rate of waste generation is increasing every year with projected 1800 tons/day by 2030. Waste management sector in Peshawar is already facing many problems as more waste is produced than the available facilities. The city should be capable of handling around 2000 tons/day of waste in 2030/there should be a viable alternative solution to waste management. Estimated waste generation of the city has been calculated as 1120 tons/day, 70% from the households and rest from other sources. It result in water contamination due to leachate from solid waste. 
The waste can be converted into energy, this will not only solve the energy problems, but also result in considerable waste volume reduction. The Biomass and solid waste if converted into renewable energy can be used as energy source.
In order to achieve the renewable energy production, we aim to utilize the solid waste. Separation of waste on the basis of their nature and processes such as drying, shredding and gasification, which will lead us to energy production an alternative of the conventional energy sources such as oil, gas and coal.
