data.projectName: Sustainable development of concrete structures by using Self-healing concrete technology with cementitious materials and expansive agents (CSA)
data.piUniversity: Quaid-e-Awam University of Engineering, Sciences & Technology, Nawabshah
data.projectDigest: Industrial cementitious waste material along with expansive agents, and geomaterials will be utilized in concrete during mixing phase, which trigger healing rate/calcium carbonate precipitation reaction and thus cracks in concrete will be filled/healed/recovered automatically. Thus, structures overall performance and sustainability will be improved by saving huge amount of money which is being used in maintenance work
data.projectSummary: Industrial cementitious waste material along with expansive agents, and geomaterials will be utilized in concrete during mixing phase, which trigger healing rate/calcium carbonate precipitation reaction and thus cracks in concrete will be filled/healed/recovered automatically. Thus, structures overall performance and sustainability will be improved by saving huge amount of money which is being used in maintenance work
data.localySocioEco: CCement is the one of ingredients of concrete which is very expansive and releases a huge amount of Co2 which is dangerous to the environment. To reduce this risk many researchers have partially replaced the cement with different Industrial wastes like fly ash, silica fume, glass powder, blast furnace slag and Rice husk Ash etc. Pakistan has a large agricultural economic sector and produces a substantial amount of agricultural waste material that has little current economic use. Rice Husk is one of those industrial/agro waste and almost 120 million tons/year is being produced in the paddy field. RHA contains almost 85% of silica which is considered to be high pozzolanic materials. Therefore, utilizing these materials in concrete will reduce the environmental hazards produced by the wastes. Furthermore, we will introduce new technique in terms of self-healing concrete by adding expansive agents along with the RHA. Because the cracking in concrete results not only in reducing strength but also effects overall the durability of the structures specially sea-shore structures. So, by using these materials we can trigger healing phenomenon fast and cracks can be controlled, thus durability and mechanical performance of the structures can be improved. In Pakistan, highly funded projects like large dams, irrigation systems face cracking issues and maintenance of those structures requires not only skilled labor, time but also handsome amount of money. Therefore, introducing self-healing concept in concrete by using waste supplementary cementitious materials along with the expansive materials the service life of concrete could be improved and by self-repairing the maintenance cost could be reduced.

data.projectName: Economic Uplift of Mohmand via Marble & Livestock SMEs
data.piUniversity: CECOS University of Information Technology and Emerging Sciences, Peshawar
data.projectDigest:
A comprehensive review of the available literature was undertaken in order to identify the potential economic drivers in Mohmand. Following were the key factors considered to identify the key economic sectors and subsectors: 
•	Job market dynamics 
•	Training facilities 
•	Natural endowments 
•	Trade associations and chambers membership 
•	Socially accepted occupations 

The agriculture, fisheries, livestock, transportation, mining, construction and trades are the sectors overall economy of the merged districts is based on at the moment. Based on literature review, government priorities and input from the stakeholders, following sectors are considered to have the potential for future skill development initiatives in merged districts: 
1.	Marble 
2.	Agriculture based businesses/ Agritourism.
3.	Construction 
The shortlisted sectors/subsectors have a significant contribution towards districts economy and livelihood. Huge marble reserves are found in five out of seven tribal agencies with an estimated production of 570,519 tonnes and around 2,000 workers are involved in marble quarrying only. Similarly, an estimated 300,000 pine nut trees exist in South and North Waziristan Agency. The revenue from these trees for the local population is approximately PKR 3 billion and the beneficiary of this business is mostly female group of the population. Construction is also one of the potential sectors with the higher contribution in economic growth of the districts. Living standards of targeted households to be improved and vulnerability to shocks reduced. At least 50% of the poorest households in the targeted areas will be developed. Improved socio economic conditions and opportunities with good quality of life.

data.projectName: Nutrition, Food Security and Physical Activity in Relation to Communicable and Non-Communicable Diseases among Adults in Lahore, Pakistan; Strategies and Future Perspectives
data.projectDigest: Diseases like COVID-19, Diabetes and heart diseases are a major problem for the population of Pakistan these days. A large number of Pakistani people living in different provinces and districts suffer from these diseases. These diseases have potentially serious socioeconomic consequences, through increasing individual and household impoverishment and hindering social and economic development. They also impose a disproportionately large burden on the health care cost at the national level along with social and psychological costs at the individual and household levels especially in low- and middle-income countries. Lifestyle factors including food and physical activity play a very important role in the prevention and development of these diseases.  Many of these diseases are preventable and can be managed through change in lifestyle. This proposal will generate evidence in the form of data collection including prevalence of diseases and related factors like food intake and physical activity from all union councils of Lahore district to get reliable, generalizable and holistic picture of the reason for the diseases at hand. This evidence will be used to develop targeted interventions to see the effectiveness of balanced diet and physical activity measures among the population of Lahore. In the last stage policy measures will be recommended to the government to prevent and manage this huge problem.

data.projectName: Bioengineering high amylose in wheat using genome editing to improve human health
data.projectDigest:
This project focuses on SDG No. 3 which relates to good health and wellbeing. Poor diet/food is known as one of potential health risk factor that can be manipulated to prevent the high prevalence of noncommunicable diseases (diabetes, obesity, arthroporosis, cardiovascular diseases and certain cancers especially bowel cancer) in Asian communities and the deaths attributed to them. Wheat is our staple food and the large part of population drives its energy from wheat. The health benefits from foods of plant origin especially whole grain cereals are  scientifically well established and their contribution to good health is widely acknowledged. 
Therefore, it is worth mentioning that enhancing the nutritional level of such foods constitutes a promising strategy for addressing issue of poor diets. Wheat has special importance in this strategy because of its well-known health-promoting contribution and alsoas an ingredient, which is well suited to produce different foods that appeal to consumers. Resistant starch is a kind of fiber that feeds good bacteria in the large intestine and consequently helps improve gut health and alleviates the risks of poor diet-related chronic diseases such as heart diseases, obesity, diabetes and certain cancers. With this in mind, we proposed bioengineering of wheat starch to produce more resistant starch by altering starch branching enzymes using genome editing technique

data.projectName: Early diagnosis and monitoring of Pediatric Pneumonia using Pediatric Pneumonia Diagnostic System (PPDS)
data.piUniversity: Sir Syed University of Engg. & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The proposed project aims to reduce child mortality caused by Pneumonia especially in rural areas of Pakistan. Despite major advances in the healthcare sector, almost 20% of child deaths are caused by pneumonia. Child mortality due to pneumonia has increased in recent years owing to the unavailability of medical equipment and trained medical staff, in the majority of rural areas. The situation can be tackled by having an intelligent system capable of early diagnosis of pneumonia with simple and implementable technology even in the absence of specialized healthcare staff in remote areas. We have suggested the usage of simple temperature and PPG sensors that wouldn’t cause discomfort to children. The information from these sensors will be processed and using a state-of-the-art algorithm, the extracted information shall be used to diagnose pneumonia in pediatric patients. The entire process will be automated eliminating the need for specialized consultants and healthcare staff. The suggested sensors are already in wide use in hospitals so the system integration shall be easier. Thus, making the Pediatric Pneumonia Detection System (PPDS) suitable for healthcare facilities in rural areas where physical and human resources are scarce. The PPDS is also expected to share the burden of work of physicians in Urban areas and shall reduce the cost of expansive X-rays and CT scans.

data.projectName: Susceptibility profile of Vaccine preventable diseases; Implication of sustainable steps
data.projectDigest: Pakistani children quite frequently become victims of preventable, infectious and communicable diseases and also play as a source of transmission for other children and siblings. Polio and measles are main threat to our community. These preventable diseases are costing us in terms of high morbidity and mortality. Pakistan has high mortality and morbidity rates of infants, neonates and under five children due to measles and Polio which indirectly leads to psychological trauma to mother and increased population due to lack of surety. This also leads to increased financial burden for treatment, increased hospital admission, over-burdened health care facilities, over worked and over crunched health staff and loss of work of bread winner. Pakistan is also under International Health regulations due to Polio. To overcome all these barriers and to achieve sustainable development goals, it is necessary to strengthen immunization program to avert this vicious cycle. Immunization reduces infectious disease burden and will lead to good physical health of children. According to WHO , in low and middle income countries, value of life-year protected is approximately 1.5 times country’s per capita GDP. This research project will help EPI programme management for strengthening and capacity building of health force. It will also decrease threats to health security at national and global level. So, in a nutshell, this project will have a positive impact on socio-economic aspect of our community

data.projectName: Behavioral Intervention for Sustainable Agricultural Practices: A Field Experiment for Water Conservation
data.piUniversity: Capital University of Science and Technology, Islamabad
data.projectDigest: According to International Monetary Fund (IMF) Pakistan is ranked third in countries facing water shortage. It will cross absolute water scarcity line (< 500m3/ person) by 2025 (Ashraf, 2016). This shortage of water is adversely affecting agriculture sector of Pakistan which is the largest contributor to GDP (24%). Although technological advancements have been made in agriculture sector continuously, farmer’s preference for traditional methods and lack of knowledge, familiarity and advice along with lack of insight for long term cost benefit analysis is posing major hurdle in effectively utilizing technology for proficient use of water resource. In order to address this issue the proposed project will design an indigenous Behavioral Insight program targeting efficient use of water by farmers. The feasibility and efficacy of this program will be tested through field experiment with the local farmers in Rawalpindi district of Punjab province. The project will aid in addressing SDG 6 (Ensure availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all; target 6.4 & 6.b). Agriculture is one of the biggest water consuming sectors in Pakistan and an effectual management of water resource will not only help to address SDG 6 but will also contribute to promoting sustainable agriculture practices (SDG 2, Target 2.4).

data.projectName: Municipal Solid waste treatment through thermal and biochemical techniques for generating renewable energy
data.projectDigest: The waste generation is increasing along with the increment in population of Pakistan, which has now become a key issue of the country, poses severe environmental and health consequences for every component of ecosystem.  Major portion of this waste is municipal solid waste, generally termed as trash, released from towns and cities. This needs to be removed from our natural environment to prevent further spread of diseases and pollution.  This project is especially designed to address issues related to solid waste disposal for not only encountering its ecological and environmental impacts but rather to utilize it for renewable energy source in multi-prone directions. The solid waste material generated in Abbottabad city from domestic, commercial, and other sources will be used for research purpose and the outcomes of the study will be shared with local municipal department. The research is also aimed to optimize the thermal and biochemical treatment of the MSW with better results of degradation and energy generation along with minimal toxic output/threshold.

data.projectName: Cardiometabolic Health - Community based Registry, Primary, Secondary Prevention and Treatment Optimisation Programme (COMET-Big Data)
data.projectDigest: Cardiometabolic disease (CMD) spectrum (cardiovascular diseases, diabetes and their sequelae) are associated with significant morbidity, mortality and economic implications. According to WHO, CVD is now number one cause of death worldwide and in Pakistan 29% of death is directly caused by CVD. A recent survey showed that 26% of the Pakistani population has diabetes. Primary and secondary prevention and optimal treatment especially in the community has shown clear benefit in management of CMD. In this project, we propose the establishment of a model community-based programme for the delivery of evidence-based, efficient and cost-effective management of CMD spectrum in Pakistan. The programme is aimed at reducing the mortality, morbidity and associated socioeconomic burden associated with these conditions. Individuals will be screened for CMD and will divided into prevention and optimal treatment arms. The patient registry/Big Data (up to 50,000 patients) will be used for epidemiological and other cascade research studies/trials. Investigative studies into novel environmental and biological risk factors will conducted. Innovative IT and AI solutions will be used for patient education and predictive modeling respectively. Local stakeholders including the community, public and private healthcare institutions, public representatives and industry will be engaged at all levels for maximizing the intended benefits  and the general well-being of the community at large.

data.projectName: What Conviction Rates Reveal About the Criminal Justice System: An Examination of the Police, Prosecution, and Judiciary in the Punjab
data.projectDigest: The UN’ Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 16) on the access of justice and accountable and inclusive institutions is premised on the concept of the ‘rule of law.’ Acemoglu and Robinson have clearly shown how ‘rule of law’ underpins all development as upon it is predicated the establishment of inclusive institutions which then spur on growth and development. Hence, SDG 16 is the pre-requisite for a number others SDG’s to take root. For example, gender and other inequalities (SDG 5 and 10), cannot be achieved until the rule of law is established which guarantees equality. Similarly, there cannot be any sustainable economic growth (SDG 8) or a reduction in poverty (SDG 1), nor innovation (SDG 9), unless inclusive institutions based on the rule of law are established. Without the rule of law, it would be very difficult, and in some cases impossible, to achieve several other SDGs.

data.projectName: Establishment of Regional Center for Determination and Screening of Drug Residues in Food Commodities  at University of Haripur
data.projectDigest: In current era, as per World Health Organization (WHO), antibiotic resistance is one of the biggest threat to the global health, food security and development. According to WHO, more than half of all death in developing countries occur due to communicable infectious diseases. With the passage of time, infectious diseases such as tuberculosis, Pneumonia and foodborne diseases are becoming the most challenging to treat due to failure of antibiotics. The rise in antimicrobial resistance to antibiotics gradually increases in both human and livestock sector day by day due to improper use of antibiotics. Failure in antibiotics lead to increase stay at hospitals, loss of financial resources and due to prolong infection, the disease can get more chances to spread to others individual. The excessive use of antibiotics in livestock sector contaminate food products such as milk, meat and eggs which indirectly become part of human body and play critical role in development of antimicrobial resistance. Presence of antibiotic residues in animal food products also compromise food safety and create hurdles international trade of the animal food products. There is dire need to develop safe food in the market for both human consumption and increasing the economy of developing countries like Pakistan. The current project will develop a platform for determination and screening of antibiotic residues in food commodities and develop guidelines for community, farmers and policy makers about proper use of antibiotics and development of safe food for market.

data.projectName: Microbial chitinases; production and application as bio pesticide.
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan is an agricultural country so farming is considered a backbone economic activity. Although there is agricultural activity in all areas of Pakistan, the country is still far from realizing the large potential yield that the well-irrigated and fertile soil could produce1. Wheat is by far the most important crop in Pakistan and is the staple food for the majority of the population. Rice is the other major food grain. About 2.1 million hectares were planted with rice, and production amounted to 3.2 million tons, with 1 million tons exported2.
Agricultural products, especially cotton yarn, cotton cloth, raw cotton, and rice, are important exports. Nearly 71% of Pakistan’s pesticide market is import dependent and annually imports approximately 80,000 tons of pesticides. The current use of pesticides in Pakistan is about 1,30,000 metric tons, of which approximately 90% is applied to cotton, rice, fruits, and vegetables3.
According to the World Health Organization (WHO), there are an estimated three million cases of pesticide poisoning each year which lead to nearly 220,000 deaths, primarily in developing countries4.
Pesticide use in the country is widespread. The impact of pesticide overuse is felt far away from the fields where it is applied. There is a need to replace those chemical pesticides with Bio pesticides5. And this project is exclusively based on the microbial production of ecofriendly bio- pesticides for all purpose crops.

data.projectName: Save Nature Save Future: Awareness and Sensitization Campaign to Rehabilitate the Jinnah Stream, Islamabad.
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Zulfikar Ali Bhutto Institute of Science & Technology (SZABIST) University, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Islamabad, the capital of Pakistan, is a city of natural streams. Sadly, the streams are currently full of stinking raw sewerage. It is due to the discharge of raw sewer into the streams. The proposed project aims at addressing the lack of awareness and issue of the insensitivity of the members of the community. Its objective will be achieved by spreading awareness and sensitizing them about stream pollution. Secondly, preparing a community-based organization for the sustainability of the initiative. The proposed work is a local challenge, in line with the Vision 2025 of Pakistan, Clean and Green Pakistan initiative of GOP, and SDG #6 (Water & Sanitation).

One of the contaminated nullahs, which was once the Jinnah stream and hub of socio-economic activity, has been chosen as the pilot project of the initiative. 

The methodology is based on the AIDA mode. The project activities include; (1) conducting pre-post awareness and sensitization surveys, (2) data collection, (3) formation of volunteer force, and (4) research report.

SZABIST Islamabad will spearhead the local challenge in collaboration with Ministry of Climate Change, Research-intensive university, and CESVI International. It will ensure the right and successful implementation of the project from conception to completion and sustainability.

data.projectName: Capacity building of mango growers for certified nursery production in South Punjab
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest: Mango is the second most important fruit crop of Pakistan in terms of production volume and is grown in all provinces & Southern Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK). The area under mango is increasing in Pakistan but not enough seedlings are available to farmers. The productivity of nurseries is decreasing due to lack of correct and modern protocols of nurseries. In spite of the large size of the mango industry in Pakistan, the nursery segment remains under developed across the whole mango industry. In Pakistan, presently, mango nurseries are being grown in mango orchards under the canopy of large tree, while developed mango growing countries established their nurseries in containers using potting media in green houses which are located separately from mango orchards. Orchard soil often a source of various insects, pest, diseases and importantly the weed seeds which damage the nursery plants by confronting and competing for nutrition and space. This situation established need to develop a new system of mango plant production under isolated, insect and disease free shade houses and potting media with the following properties: free of pests and diseases, balanced nutrient contents. This project has been envisaged and proposed to improve mango production by raising high health nursery plants and its provision to mango growers with improved technology to bring more area under mango productivity to meet local and foreign market demand. It is worth mentioning that only in Punjab mango occupies handsome area under its cultivation. It is pretty much sure that if this project is approved and implemented in zeal and zest spirit, it certainly would improve quality, yield and production of mango would virtually go along way, not only help to alleviate poverty of the mango farming communit

data.projectName: Simplifying Text Comprehension for Urdu Speakers: An Investigation Using Deep Learning
data.projectDigest: Complex sentences in text lead to many difficulties including creating comprehension hurdles for learners and for low literacy users. Researchers have been working on identification and simplification of complex sentences. However, the body of work focuses majorly on English and research on other languages, especially on Urdu, is in its infancy. Urdu is the most widely understood language in Pakistan. Research into Urdu text simplification will yield extensive benefits, firstly by facilitating instructors and learners with simplified text to enhance understanding, and secondly, it will serve as an information access aid where low literacy is a problem. Apart from these tangible benefits, any research into Urdu language will also help preserve our rich heritage. We propose to build an Automatic Sentence Simplification system using the state-of-art Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning techniques. Our project is designed by qualified specialists from 3 National universities and 1 international university to create the required corpora, bootstrap and eventually come up with a good sentence simplification system for Urdu. We focus on the Urdu comprehension problem for two specific groups, school children and readers having comprehension problems, i.e. dyslexia. Project runs in parallel, with focus on well-designed surveys, corpus creation; Machine Learning based system building and iterating over to end with a working text simplification system based on Deep Learning.

data.projectName: Genomics and speed-breeding enabled rapid development of wheat varieties with improved heat tolerance and nutrition for Sind and Baluchistan
data.projectDigest: The project aims to develop wheat varieties that can withstand and give higher yield under high temperature conditions. We also aim that heat tolerant varieties will have additional benefit of high nutritions like grain iron,  zinc and phytase. We will use innovative DNA technologies to identify the genes for heat tolerance and biofortification.  Furthermore, new drone-based imaging platform will be developed which will use thermal sensor camera to select heat tolerant germplasm in the large field trials. At the last we will use 'speed breeding' technology which uses the extended photoperiod using LED lights to accelerate the development of varieties. Conclusively, this initiative will accelerate the efforts to develop climate resilient high nutrition wheat varieties suited specifically for Sindh and Balochistan and generally for all Pakistan.

data.projectName: Commodity based disease-free trade model for the production of exportable meat from Cholistan
data.piUniversity: Cholistan University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Bahawalpur
data.projectDigest: There is a huge potential in livestock industry of Cholistan for food security and revenue generation through exports of milk and meat products ensuring food security of Pakistan. Cholistan is natural habitat or savannah supporting a large population of sheep, goat, camels and cattle. The natural resources for grazing is an additional benefit. To exploit maximum potential of the area in terms of enhanced production and access to international food market, livestock department has already taken an initiative for the establishment of disease free zone in the area and currently, campaign for regular programmed vaccination for progressive control foot and mouth disease (FMD) in line with disease free zone has reached at its phase-IV. FMD and peste des petits ruminants (PPR) diseases are more focused being transboundary in nature according to OIE; PPR being the target for global eradication program by FAO and OIE launched in 2015. This future-oriented endeavor as pre-requisite to ensure sustained exports’ based foreign exchange requires investment and keen interest from all stakeholders; and is facing a great challenge and opportunity at the same time. For example, current challenge is to ensure stoppage of virus circulation in relatively un-common host species like sheep and goat calling for the establishment of surveillance zone in Cholistan. Secondly, according to OIE guidelines, contagious and zoonotic diseases like PPR, CCPP, Pox, brucellosis, trypanosomiasis and tuberculosis must be controlled for declaration of disease free zone while currently, FMD control program is in progress. Thirdly, movement of animals should be restricted to Cholistan habitat. Fourthly, commodity based trade produced in Cholistan require the establishment of model abattoir and meat processing

data.projectName: Effects of High performance Work Practices & administrative corruption on organizational performance of Public enterprises: A case of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Being a developing nation, Pakistan’s government is trying hard to enhance the performance of the government firms by introducing private sector?s best practices in the public sector. To achieve this purpose, government has introduced creative reforms in Public Enterprise sector in the category of New Public Management (NPM) reforms. But inspite of this, the performance of public enterprises is not as desired. Moreover, corruption is negatively affecting the organizational performance as well as the economic indicators of the country. Hence, this study is performed to estimate the impact of multiple variable that are affecting the performance of Public Enterprises in Pakistan. This research is directed to inspect the direct relation of HPWP (High Performance Work Practices) on OP (Organizational Performance), by contributing to the phenomenon of „?Black Box?? through the mechanism that how HPWP directly affects organizational performance. As well as, this research will examine the mediating effect of JS (job satisfaction), EP (Employee Performance), and OC (organizational commitment), in between the relation of IV and DV. Furthermore, the researcher will also explore the moderating effect of administrative corruption. Hence, this research will provide deep insight into how the perception of HPWP affects the overall performance of public sector companies in Pakistan through the indirect and direct impact on administrative corruption.

data.projectName: Intelligent Health Assessment System for Power Transformers in Transmission & Distribution System in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: In this project an intelligent framework is proposed for identification of percentage fit or unfit of power transformer in 220 KV Grid-station. Conventionally all of the transformer oil tests are done after 6 months and decided about the fitness of transformer oil , coils and bushings etc. , but in the proposed project all real-time measurements of faults effects are done using digital sensors and these signals are processed online so that intelligently the percentage fit or unfit may be identified and sent the intimation information to NPCC in real-time so that proper planning steps can be taken at remote access.

This data definitely cannot predict the remaining life of transformers  and there is a need for a complete reconfigurable online monitoring system so that to assess the complete health of transformers like the moisture condition of the transformer insulation , carbonization status of transformer oil indicating the dielectric response ,  estimating the life of paper insulation , signal conditioning  statistical data techniques to be used for online monitoring and health assessment of the transformers . This useful data received by NPCC or RCC’s will be a vital tool for finalizing the fit or unfit of Power transformers to be an additional but essential part in System Security Load Management carried out by NPCC in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Performance Enhancement of Photovoltaic (PV) Systems for Hot and Arid Areas of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Every year the country loses billions due to the power sector distortions and according to 2018 Global competitiveness report, Pakistan still ranks 115th in 137 economies in reliability of electric supply. Therefore, an uninterrupted supply of energy is a desperate requirement of the country. Power generation using renewable sources of energy like solar energy and wind energy, along with the benefits of cost saving and clean environment, is the ultimate demand of current times. Among the various systems available to harness renewable energy, solar photovoltaic (PV) systems are especially promising due to their low cost, easy installation, low maintenance and wide availability. The performance of PV systems is adversely affected by dust accumulation on PV surface and high temperatures, conditions widely encountered in Pakistan. The proposed project aims to provide solutions to these problems. For dust accumulation, the solutions will employ surface treatment techniques while efficient and low-cost cooling systems will be designed to reduce the PV temperature. The proposed project will result in the enhancement of PV performance by providing cost-effective solutions to the masses and contribute to the solution of the energy crises in the country.

data.projectName: Evaluation of Clinical and Hematological parameters in stress-induced-hyperprolactinemia and to assess its association with antidepressants.
data.piUniversity: Sir Syed University of Engg. & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Prolactin is a polypeptide hormone secreted by the anterior pituitary gland to induce lactation and other reproductive functions. Several endogenous substances have been found to affect the prolactin level, such as pregnancy, lactation and sleep), neurological diseases and hormonal disorders. Hyperprolactinemia is defined as elevated prolactin levels above gender-specific normal levels, which have been variably defined in previous studies. The prevalence has been shown to be much higher (ranging between 10% and 55%) among women than men with reproductive disorders. Stress is also an important physiologic cause of hyperprolactinemia, and its clinical significance is still being explored. Stress response also includes the release of prolactin, which is of significant clinical relevance as there is substantial evidence that prolactin plays a significant role in the development of stress-induced pathology. Considerable prolactin secretion occurs when animals are exposed to physical or psychological stress. In male mice, 15-minute period of restraint stress causes a 7-fold increase in circulating prolactin levels. Studies also reported that hyperprolactinemia is a common adverse event associated with antidepressants medications used in the management of mental disorders. The data on prevalence of hyperprolactinemia among psychiatric patients receiving antipsychotic medications are lacking in Pakistani population. Therefore, the objective of the current study is to evaluate possible clinical and hematological factors among patients with hyperprolactinemia and to assess its association with various psychiatric disorders. The study might be helpful in understanding the clinical management of psychotic disorders with the consideration of prolactin levels in stress.

data.projectName: UAV Swarm and IoTs for Efficient Waste Management of Karachi
data.piUniversity: National University of Computer and Emerging Sciences, Islamabad
data.projectDigest:
Karachi has a dire problem of inefficient waste management with heaps beside the roads and streets in most of the parts of the city. There are some areas where waste is accumulated despite the frequent cleaning by the waste management board. The proposed project will ensure that all the garbage reaches the collection centres and thereby the landfill sites for waste treatment.  A swarm UAV and IoTs will be incorporated in the infrastructure of Sindh Solid Waste Management Board. The swarm UAV will locate the sporadic waste and fixed cameras will be installed at the locations where heaps regularly get accumulated. Bins will be made smart using IoTs so that there levels along with their locations could be monitored. Such monitoring will result into timely vacating the bins and keep the surroundings clean and biologically safe. IoTs will also be used to track the transportation of garbage from the collection centre to garbage transfer station and landfill sites. The data retrieved from the IoTs will be used to plan the fastest paths for the vehicles thereby saving the fuel and avoiding the waste logging in some areas.
A clean and healthy environment is likely to  contribute to prosperous growth of the city and improve environmental and economic condition. 
This research aims to address this problem through a combination of Internet of Thing (IoT) devices and a swarm of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV).

data.projectName: PREPARATION OF DURABLE INSECT REPELLENT FABRICS BY PLASMA TREATMENT TO PREVENT MOSQUITO-TRANSMITTED DISEASES
data.piUniversity: Women University of Azad Jammu and Kashmir Bagh
data.projectDigest: The mosquito-transmitted diseases (such as dengue fever) are of severe concern, and several millions of peoples are affected worldwide, including Pakistan. Instead of medical treatment after the disease is initiated, self-protection against the mosquitos is preferred, particularly in endemic areas. The insect-repellent coating on fabrics (in the form of clothing) can be used to prevent mosquito bites and resultant disease transmission. Unfortunately, the laundering resistance of insect-repellent coated fabrics is very low (washed out after a few washing cycles). The plasma treatment before the deposition of insect-repellent coatings (such as permethrin) can improve the hydrophobic behavior of fabrics and coatings adhesion strength. Recently, in collaborative work with Brazil research group, we observed that long-lasting insect repellent coating could be deposited by plasma treatment, with exceptional lauding resistance [1]. Unfortunately, from a decade, Pakistan is experiencing an epidemic dengue fever in many provinces, as declared by the World Health Organization (WHO). As suggested by WHO, the reduction in mosquitos biting activity and self-prevention is necessary, instead of complicated medication after transmission of disease. Here, we proposed that insect-repellent fabric can be prepared in Pakistan, with a low-cost and long-lasting performance, by using plasma treatment, which would be beneficial to prevent dengue fever transmission.

data.projectName: Design and development of an efficient indirect regenerative evaporative cooler
data.piUniversity: Mirpur University of Science and Technology (MUST), AJ&K
data.projectDigest: Mirpur division of Azad Jammu and Kashmir is in the surrounding area of Mangla dam. Mangla dam is biggest water reservoir of Pakistan having catchment area 33,334 km2. [1] The total area and population of division Mirpur of Azad Jammu and Kashmir is 4388 km2 and 1,650,951 respectively.[2] The humidity level of ambient air is very high. During summer season the cooling demand is very high to achieve thermal comfort. Therefore, air conditioning demand is rising drastically that causes peak loads and low voltage problem in the region. Mostly air-conditioning demand is fulfilled by direct evaporative cooler (swamp coolers and vapor compression-based system). However, due to high outside humidity these systems could not meet the thermal comfort requirement. People are shifting towards vapor compression-based systems that are high electricity consumers and are in-economical. Hence, middle class families are suffering from a lot of thermal comfort issues. Therefore, an efficient solar driven indirect regenerative evaporative cooler is proposed that is capable to cool the inlet air below its wet bulb temperature and does not add humidity in the supply air. The electric energy consumption of this system is 50-80 % low as compared to conventional air conditioning system. [3] Further it is also capable to enhance the electricity production of solar PV panels by cooling via utilizing its working/exhaust  air.

data.projectName: ECO-GREEN AND SUSTAINABLE UPSCALE DEVELOPMENT OF MICROALGAE-BIOFUEL PRODUCTION USING NANOADDITIVES WITH SYNERGICAL PHYCOREMEDIATION OF WASTEWATER
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Benazir Bhutto Women University, Peshawar
data.projectDigest: Energy crisis has generally created economic constraints and because of this researchers and policy makers are trying to find more efficient and environmental friendly technologies with less climatic effects. Production of biofuels using renewable indigenous resources have enormous potential to provide energy independence. New technologies will help in creation of new jobs and industries at local level and protects the environment. Microalgae is an indigenous resource that have the capability to produce biofuels with an advantage that they do not compete with food crops supplies and utilizes wastewater for their propagation. Wastewater usually contains several toxic compounds that have hazardous effects on health of animals, plants and humans. Current study have three main objectives (a) energy independence in terms of local production of biofuels using indigenous resources; (b) micropropagation of microalgae using wastewater supplies and also removal of its toxic compounds and (c) clean environment with low health risks due to water treatment and reduction of greenhouse effect. The technology developed in this proposed project has the potential to provide new economic opportunities and generate social impact by reducing toxic effects of wastewater and air pollution on health of living organisms.

data.projectDigest:
Modern information and communication technologies (ICTs) have generated tremendous amounts of data in various sectors. The commercial sector can reap the benefits of ICTs with swift growth by realizing the importance of big data analytics. Big data analytics is a favorable choice for building energy managers to perform low cost, more generic and detailed real time analysis in short time ensuring the maximum customer satisfaction without compromising on regulatory issues. The use of data-driven technologies can play a substantial role for analyzing the building’s energy consumption patterns to optimize its operation. 
The main aim of this research is to establish a high-tech platform named as “MUST Energy Data Analytic Center (MEDAC)”. This unit would serve the three phases of development, firstly the design of energy data platform which includes: memory modules, processing units and software tools. The second phase deals with the accomplishment of energy data collection arrangements consisting of number of sensors and actuators for operational monitoring. In future, this will lead to the extension of smart metering data management system for the city of Mirpur AJK. Lastly, the utilization of designed infrastructure will be carried out to develop algorithms for smart operation and anomalies detection.

data.projectName: Genetic Testing and Counselling Initiative: From Awareness to Management of Inherited Disorders in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
Genetic defects are important cause of mortality and lifelong disabilities in many cases. These disorders effect millions of people in the entire world including Pakistan. The global prevalence of all monogenic hereditary defects or Mendelian diseases has been estimated about 10/1000.  Inherited disorders are more prevalent in Pakistan as compared to the western countries due to several reasons. Consanguineous marriages and extended family size are among important reasons of high incidence of patients with inherited defects in Pakistan.
Objectives of present study include: 1- Screen families locally with inherited disorders (including Skin disorders, Skeletal disorders, Neurological disorders, Eye disorders and hearing/speech disorders) for genetic mutations reported from Pakistani population. The mutation panels for these selected disorders will be designed based on reported data from our local population 2- We will council families with a detected mutation regarding their future marital decisions. 3- We will conduct symposia (both onsite and online) to spread awareness among healthcare providers about management of genetic disorders. 4- In last phase, Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) platforms will be used in collaboration with reputed foreign laboratory/University for families without any detectable mutation.

data.localySocioEco:
Inherited disorders are one of the largest group of non-communicable diseases. These disorders cause mortality and lifelong disabilities among the affected individuals, and put significant socio-economic burden on caregivers/affected families. Consanguinity, the marriage among close relatives, is one of the risk factors associated with increased number of patients with these anomalies. However, in many cases management and prevention of inherited disorders is possible through creating awareness among the masses, and offering genetic testing and counselling to the affected families. 
Large data set of frequent genetic mutations for some of the prevalent genetic disorders is more or less available for Pakistani families. Broadly, we can divide them into Skin disorders, Skeletal disorders, Neurological disorders, Eye disorders and hearing/speech disorders. There is an ample need to identify mutation panels for these disorders in Pakistani population, based on available data, and screen families with these disorders in large numbers to identify mutations. This will help to provide genetic counselling in these families to make them decide scientifically about future marriage decisions. Awareness among healthcare providers about role of consanguinity in spread of these disorders and management of inherited disorders will help to reduce burden of these disorders from the population.

data.projectName: Impact of Behavior change intervention on households drinking water quality and burden of water borne diseases in District Jamshoro
data.piUniversity: Liaquat University of Medical and Health Sciences, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
The total population of District Jamshoro is 1,018,634 which is accommodated in four talukas i.e. Kotri, Manjhand, Sehwan & ThanoBula Khan. The total estimated households in District Jamshoro are 103,686. The population of the targeted district is mostly deprived of clean and safe drinking water which is the leading cause of water borne diseases and mortality in the area.

Project Plan:The proposed project will be a community based interventional research undertaken on households of selected union councils of all four talukas of District Jamshoro; the households will be selected through cluster sampling. The duration of project will be 24 months.

data.localySocioEco:
Health of any nation is closely interlinked with ecological factors such education, environment & economy, etc. The health profile of developing countries necessitate their governments to increase their budgetary allocations towards health. In terms of total health expenditure as a percentage of the GDP, Pakistan’s budget spending has remained as low as 1.1%. Pakistan has to expend a cost of Rs. 112 billion per year on water, sanitation and hygiene related diseases and more than Rs.300 million per day in terms of overall health costs and loss of income. 

Quality of drinking water is paramount for public health especially to children’s health. In Pakistan, 30% of all diseases & 40% of all deaths are due to poor water quality. Besides various biosocial determinants of high mortality, diarrhea especially in children as well as in adults is one of the most important & preventable determinant of mortality. In Pakistan, 13% of the total population comprises of children < 5 years of age. Unfortunately the under-five mortality rate in Sindh is reported as 104/1000 live births.  Further, despite of 95% of households having access to an improved drinking water source, only 7% of them use an appropriate water treatment method; this results in water borne diseases especially in children. In Pakistan about 60% of the total number of child mortality cases are caused by consuming untreated water. The water quality monitoring survey conducted in rural and urban areas of the country revealed that the access to safe drinking water is only 15% in urban and 18% in rural areas. 

The behavior change interventions directed both at identified individuals and the community generally having poor water quality is a way of strengthening communities by imparting skills for managing drinking water quality at consumer’s end.  This is the most cost-effective strategy to meet criteria of the Sustainable Development Goal 6 leading to sustainable health benefits.

data.projectName: Developing the Integrated Solid Waste Management Model for District Korangi Karachi, Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Present study aims to develop an integrated solid waste management model for the Korangi District of Karachi. Proposed model will be based on zero waste approach. Main elements of the model; i) introduction of proper waste collection system in the study area ensuring 100% waste collection from domestic, commercial and industrial facilities, ii) Developing a waste transfer station which is socially and environmental safe and acceptable, iii) Developing a waste transfer/transport system for the collected waste, iv) developing a waste segregation system (manual as well as mechanical) ensuring 100% separation/segregation of recyclable and reusable items from the waste stream, v) developing a waste composting system for the organic waste (leftover after segregation) with economic and financial analysis of composting, vi) identifying/developing a final waste disposal site. Although the proposed model is based on zero waste approach however, final waste disposal must be developed to ensure the sustainable model operations. Proposed model will also investigate the technical and financial viability of waste to energy option. 
Proposed model is aimed to be economically self-sustained with zero/minimum outside investment. An important feature of the model is that it can be implementable throughout the Pakistan with appropriate modifications accordingly with the geographical area.

data.projectName: Anticancer potentials of Toremifene citrate and its derivatives against breast cancer: Synthesis, in-silico, in-vitro, in-vivo and toxicological evaluation
data.projectDigest:
Breast cancer is the most prevalent cancer type in females worldwide. According to the GLOBOCAN report, about 2.08 million new breast cancer cases were diagnosed in 2018, accounting for 24.2% of all cancer cases. It is the leading cause of mortality, contributing to 15% of total cancer deaths specifically in less developed countries. However, recent evidence suggests that there has been an alarming increase in both incidence and mortality rate in low- and middle-income countries. Pakistani women having a higher risk of breast cancer, whereby one of  every 9th woman in Pakistan is having breast cancer. Unfortunately, the rate of deaths due to breast cancer is also increasing annually and studies have reported different figures that ranged from 40000 to 10000 women per year. The average annual cost of breast cancer therapy varies i.e. $60, 637 to $129,387 depending upon stage of the disease. No pharmaceutical industry in Pakistan is manufacturing Toremifene citrate. We have proposed to synthesize this drug and its derivatives by performing in-silico analysis. Furthermore, this drug and its derivatives will be subjected to characterization like Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR), Physicochemical analysis, anticancer studies and toxicological parameters will be evaluated by using cell culture technique, RT PCR, acute and chronic toxicities etc. 
After initial findings and screening of appropriate derivatives a suitable carrier system i.e. mesoporous silica based nanoparticles will be developed and evaluated in detail.

data.projectName: Issues in Tax System of Pakistan and a Way Forward: Views of Government Officials and Corporate Managers
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan is facing consistent incremental increase in fiscal deficit each year. In 2018-19, it was 8.9% of the GDP and in last year, 2019-20, it grew to 9.1% of GDP. The increasing fiscal deficit is due to ill performing tax system. Revenue realization is one of the fundamental requirements of a stable economy. This requires the much needed revisiting of tax system to identify the problems and discrepancies in tax system. So that corrective actions may be undertaken in time. The ineffectiveness of Pakistan’s tax system is consistent despite the fact that successive governments have initiated many steps to make it more efficient. 
The introduction of Tax Administration and Reforms Program (TARP) in 2000-01 saw emergence of Income Tax Ordinance Act 2001 and Federal Excise Act 2005. Moreover, Sales Tax Act 1990 was also amended to make it compatible with voluntary payments. Factional distribution of powers and functions was the essence of these reforms. However, besides all these, the system is unable to deliver yet. Low tax to GDP ratio is persistent and still remains a problem. 
Pakistan’s tax system is under performing since decades despite of certain reforms like introduction of Tax Administration and Reforms Project (TARP) 2000-01. TARP leads to introduction of different tax laws like Tax Ordinance 2001 and Federal Excise Act 2005. Moreover, Sales Tax Act 1990 also gone through amendments to enlarge the tax base. Despite all these, fiscal deficit is creeping every year. The share of public expenditures is declining and its financing is becoming challenging in every forth coming budget. Adequate tax collection is vital to run wheels of any economy. So, here the problem is, the inefficiency of the tax system. The tax to GDP ratio is not increasing and is less then 10%.

data.projectName: The Economic Impact of Covid-19: A Study of Small and Medium Enterprises in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: This study focuses on the economic impact of covid-19 on small and medium enterprises in Pakistan. This study implies quantitative research methods to identify the economic cost incurred to small and medium enterprises in Pakistan due to the implementation of stay-at-home policy. The data will be collected in the form of predefined questionnaire from the local small and medium enterprises from the four provinces including Sindh, Balushistan, Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The sample size for this study will be calculated by Cochran formula for unknown population. Multiple regression model will be used to identify the impact of covid-19 on small and medium enterprises. For data presentation and analysis statistical packages STATA and SPSS will be used.

data.projectName: Dietary Restriction of Advanced Glycation End Products (AGE): A Strategy to Prevent Non-Communicable Diseases in Pakistani Population
data.projectDigest: One of the SDG targets of Pakistan is to reduce premature mortality from non-communicable diseases (NCDs).  Rate of NCDs including diabetes cancer and cardiovascular diseases is increasing dramatically in Pakistan. Advanced Glycation End products (AGE), are harmful compounds formed in food, when cooked at high temperature in dry heat. Therefore, foods that are fried, broiled, grilled or roasted would produce higher dietary AGEs than foods that are boiled, poached, stewed or steamed. Additionally, processed/packaged food and drinks is the biggest contributor of body’s AGE pool. Scientific evidence across the globe indicates that AGE cause damage to the tissues in body and they are linked to development and complications of diabetes, neurological disorders, cancer and cardiovascular diseases. In several countries, evidence indicates that low AGE diet reduces risk to develop NCDs. However, these studies are lacking in Pakistani food and population. Here we hypothesized that our population is consuming processed food rich in AGE & dietary restriction of AGE may prevent development of new diseases in healthy population and improve prognosis of non-communicable diseases in patients. Preventing chronic diseases is a vital investment. Pakistan lack an operational policy, strategy or action plan to reduce unhealthy diet and/or promote healthy diets. The proposed study present Low AGE, diet intervention program in adults and children of Korangi district Karachi.

data.projectName: Environmental Degradation, Food Wastage, and Food Insecurities: Problems and Solutions
data.projectDigest:
Food wastage is a grave problem that has drawn vast attention from across the globe for its dreadful impacts on the overall climate and living beings. Food is wasted due to various reasons such as having inefficient production facilities, lack of knowledge and expertise, employing wrong practices and natural disasters. Also, food is wasted when consumers fail to store or consume properly. Sometimes food remains untouched and gets expired.  
Food waste that ends up in landfills produces a large amount of methane – a more powerful greenhouse gas than even CO2. Combinedly these greenhouse gases (Methane, CO2, chlorofluorocarbons) absorb the huge amount of infrared radiation and heat up the earth’s atmosphere, causing global warming and climate change.
This project is aimed at exploring the causes of food wastage at the consumer level, its effects on the overall environment, and the income inequality role in food wastage behavior. Furthermore, the project aims to find out if or not awareness sessions regarding food wastage create any change in the behavior amongst the control group.  In the end, this research will provide possible solutions for the betterment of environment.

data.projectName: Tracing  of Hazardous  Elements in Processed and Raw Dairy Products of Sindh Province
data.projectDigest: In the province of Sindh, there is a variety of dairy products whose main ingredient milk comes from cows and buffaloes with different hormonal treatments. In this study, we would like to study aluminum (Al), lead (Pb), cadmium (Cd), selenium (Se), and arsenic (As) contents in different dairy products (process and raw) available in the local market of Sindh province. The presence of such elements in food or natural and human-made materials can accumulate in the human body and cause adverse health effects. For this purpose, Laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) is a versatile spectroscopic technique that can be employed for tracing such elemental determination assisted by inductively coupled plasma mass spectroscopy.

data.projectName: Smart Water Grid for Sustainable Ground water Management of Nawasher Town, District Abbottabad
data.piUniversity: Abbottabad University of Science & Technology (AUST), Abbottabad
data.projectDigest:
Groundwater has provided a reliable source of high quality water for human use. Rapid population and economic growth, urbanization, and unsustainable consumption of groundwater in domestic, industrial, and agricultural sectors have aggravated water scarcity in different regions of the World. Over the last few decades, Pakistan has tried several strategies to manage the overexploitation of groundwater; however, finding a workable and viable solution remains a challenge. The overuse of groundwater in irrigation and domestic use is of major concern.
To overcome aforementioned challenges shared by , Water and Sanitation Services Company Abbottabad (WSSCA) in sustainable groundwater management system, this project proposes an Internet of Things (IoT) based platform for smart water grid that will monitor and optimize real-time groundwater usage, storage, recharge and depletion of groundwater in Nawasher, Abbottabad, Pakistan. The aim of this research is to ensure water quality and sustainability based on groundwater availability, groundwater usage pattern, and involve the stakeholders (groundwater users and WASSCA) to develop a better understanding of demands and utilization of the groundwater resources. Furthermore, smart IoT based platform will help to implement net water metering and reduce the human intervention in monitoring and will achieve considerable efficiency in the sustainable groundwater management system.

data.localySocioEco:
Availability of water in adequate quantity and good quality is essential for poverty alleviation and economic prosperity, leading to good health and high productivity, food security and continuous socio-economic development. A perfect balance that meets the society water demands, without exceeding the unmanageable threshold of water supplies is crucial for the effective management of the resources.  Due to rapidly increasing water demand in Abbottabad and the fact that the easy solutions to increase water supply have largely elapsed. However, people of Abbottabad tend to take water almost for granted. Only when there is an acute shortage, is the true value of water and efficient management realized. Furthermore, flat rate water billing is applied in Nawashar Zone of District Abbottabad, which provokes waste of water as no incentive is given to those households which save water. On the one hand, in terms of future service expansion the policy of flat rate do not generate enough revenues and on the other hand in long-run this results in poor level of service for the entire community.

In this research proposal, a framework for sustainable groundwater management will be proposed for the Nawashar Zone of District Abbottabad, which includes groundwater assessment and monitoring, groundwater-quality management, and a reliable real time data acquisition system using Internet of Things (IoT) based on smart water grid for groundwater management. Smart water grid will monitor quantity of water in pipelines and will help to identify water losses due to leakage in specific section and preemptive measures can be taken to prevent further losses, which will save groundwater resources and more revenue which may be used for pumping. Furthermore, the proposed smart water grid will be useful to monitor real time water usage at household level, which will help to implement net water metering and charge each household as per usage of water.

data.projectName: Poverty Alleviation through Sustainable Agri. Production by empowering small farmers
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest:
Agriculture is the lifeline of economy in south Punjab with cotton as its essential ingredient. The agrarian economy is currently not performing well as majority of small farmers are loosing their confidence in cotton profitability. There is huge yield gap between average farmers and progressive farmers and bridging this yield gap will benefit cotton farmers, rural population as well as Pakistan’s economy.  With cotton being a major cash crop, millions rely on its harvest for a sizable portion of their income. The enhanced income will contribute to reduce hunger, improve food security, better employment oppurtunities and industrial activitiy thus helping in better outcome for SDG 1, 9 and 10. 
The main objective of the study will be to accelerate the economic growth of the country by improving the productivity levels of the average farmers, bridging the gap between average and high yielding cotton growers in the districts of Multan and its surroundings. The proposed study includes an in-depth sitution analysis to estimate the yield gap and issues in sustainable cotton production. Skill and productivity level will also be estimated to gauge the skill level between progressive and average farmers. On the basis of situation analysis results, gaps will be identified for capacity building and awareness strategy will be chalk out for the small and average farmers of the study area. This will include establishment of Science and Technology Backyard (STB), seminars, workshops and focus group meetings. In the end, impact assessment of the farmers will be taken place.

data.projectName: Equipping Graduates with Employability Skills: A case study of District Peshawar
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Benazir Bhutto Women University, Peshawar
data.projectDigest: Population of Khyber Pakhtunkhawa is growing at a rapid rate.  The census 2017 revealed that province has a total population of 35.524 million with 18.023 million males and 17.501 females.  The figure for female population illustrates that without investment in this segment, socio-economic development of the province will remain in disarray. Though number of Higher Education Institutes (HEIs) has been increased in the province but still female employment in the formal sector remains insignificant. One of the determinants that can be attributed to the female unemployment is lack of adequate skills.  It is time that female graduates are equipped with both hard and soft skills so they are not only able to compete in the market but are instrumental in job creation. For the acquisition of said objective female graduates of District Peshawar will be imparted training on soft, digital and entrepreneurial skill and significant contribution will be made towards quality education and gender equality of SDGs.

Canada

data.projectName: Development of an activated carbon bio-filter prototype for the removal of pharmaceutical residues, micro-plastics and their degradation products from water
data.piUniversity: University of Kotli Azad Jammu and Kashmir
data.projectDigest:
Access to safe drinking water contributes to improved health, helps prevent spread of infectious diseases. Leaky pipes, intermixing water and wastewater results in water contamination with harmful chemicals, pharmaceutical residues (PhR), micro-plastics (MPs) and microorganism leading to water borne/water related diseases.  All this constitute about 80% of all diseases and 33% of deaths in country. Pakistan National Conservation Strategy reported that water-related diseases represent 40% of the communicable diseases, which raised concerns of stake holders. Conventional water treatment is ineffective for pharmaceutical residues and MPs removal but activated carbon adsorption is documented to be effective. Beside adsorption, bioactive activated carbon filter offers biodegradation as an alternative strategy for PhR and MPs removal.
The study is aimed at PhR and MPs surveillance and treatability studies with biodegradation assisted activated carbon filter for their removal at affordable cost to ensure safe drinking water, local community being immediate beneficiary. 
The project would enable in achieving access to safe drinking water (SDG 6.1), reduction in water-borne diseases (SDG 6.1.1), improving water quality (SDG 6.3) and sustainable water usage for combating water scarcity (SDG 6.4) and SDG 3: good health and wellbeing as a result   of improved water quality.

data.projectName: Corn Byproducts Processing for Value Added Polysaccharides
data.projectDigest: Corn is one of the most important cereal crops. Corn kernels are the major useable products and the rest is considered as corn byproducts which include corn silk, cob and husks. Every 100 kg of corn generate 18 kg of corn cob that is either used in animal feed or left with no use. Similarly corn silk is a byproduct and left without any use that poses an environmental hazard. With increasing population and limited resources in developing countries, the alternate sources of nutrients or nutraceuticals like polysaccharides and other functional ingredients should be explored. Corn byproducts are rich in, fibers, phenolic compounds and functional polysaccharides. The optimized extraction of these functional polysaccharides can serve as source of essential nutrients, nutraceuticals, functional ingredients at one end and at the other hand the processing of these byproducts will minimize the environmental hazards. Corn cob and silk are rich in functional polysaccharides and other bioactive compounds and can be used in the formulation of functional food ingredients with nutritional and health benefits. The proposed project will help in the effective management of the agriculture waste and provides a way forward for utilization of corn byproducts for value added polysaccharides

data.projectName: Highly Secure Digital Credentials Verification System in a Software as a Service Model and the Digital Backbone of a National Blockchain Network
data.piUniversity: Sir Syed University of Engg. & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Universities, colleges, secondary education programs, schools, local bodies, professional organizations, and many other organizations have a common need to verify the authenticity of a certificate or a document to ensure that it was not altered in any way. The process of validating such document is a manual process in many organizations, requiring a lot of resources, and is time consuming. Students from remote areas and people needing such verification have to travel long distances, that often takes multiple trips and someone time event takes months to get their credentials validated by the appropriate institution.

In the era of digitalization, Pakistan needs a system that is highly secure in keeping record, is temper proof, and can guarantee results in a timely manner. Distributed Ledgers technology, commonly known as blockchain, guarantees decentralized, unalterable, and secure data and resource storage and verification system. The Blockchain based cryptographic technologies restrict hacking as the information is managed by the centralized data. 

This project will develop a Blockchain based “document verification platform” to validate documents/certificates of any organization/institution whether public or private. These may include authentication of documents and certificates, identity verification, simple contracts document verification, digital signatures, and other certificates documents verification.

data.projectName: Production of eco-friendly bricks at industrial scale: Alternative to conventional burnt clay brick
data.projectDigest: Brick has been used as the construction material for thousands of years, yet the manufacturing process remains conventional, as it hardly changed from sun-backed to burnt clay bricks. This research proposes the utilization of geopolymer-brick as an alternative to conventional clay brick. The geopolymer-brick is low-cost, sustainable, utilizes waste material and has better mechanical properties. The research has two-pronged impact; first it will give low-cost and high-quality construction material, second it will be helpful in poverty alleviation. Out of 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) adopted by United Nations, this research is strongly connected with SDG 1, SDG 3, SDG 6, SDG 8, SDG 9, SDG 11, SDG 12, SDG 13, SDG 15 and SDG 17.

This research proposes the utilization of geopolymer-brick as an alternative to conventional clay brick. The geopolymer-brick is low-cost, sustainable, utilizes waste material and has better mechanical properties. The research has two-pronged impact; first it will give low-cost and high-quality construction material, second it will be helpful in poverty alleviation. Out of 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) adopted by United Nations, this research is strongly connected with SDG 1, SDG 3, SDG 6, SDG 8, SDG 9, SDG 11, SDG 12, SDG 13, SDG 15 and SDG 17.
data.localySocioEco: Brick is the basic unit of construction and its cost is the highest among all materials for grey structure in case of residential building construction. Clay brick is being manufactured at large scale due to its higher demand. The conventional clay brick is burnt at 1000-1500 oC. The high temperature requirement utilizes high amount of fuel and results in higher CO2 and toxic emissions. The brick kiln process is slow, hectic, produces compromised quality brick and is environmentally dangerous. Brick kilns are responsible for smog across Pakistan. To tackle physio-mechanical and environmental issues, an alternative brick is proposed, which will utilize industrial waste by-products such as fly ash, rice husk, sugarcane, bagasse ash and blast furnace slag etc. Moreover, sandy clay or dune sand, not considered good for clay bricks, may have potential for manufacturing of geopolymer brick (eco-friendly and sustainable construction material). Keeping all that in view, an alternative way to produce geopolymer brick has been proposed in this work, which needs low temperature (less than 100 oC) for very short time (about 1 day). Our proposed work provides geopolymer-brick at industrial scale as an alternative to conventional clay brick. The geopolymer-brick is low-cost, sustainable, utilizes waste material, and has superior physio-mechanical properties and environmental benefits. Therefore, the proposal addresses the issue of low-cost housing, waste handling, higher quality sustainable construction material and environment concerns.

data.projectName: Family and Community in time of COVID-19 (FACT)
data.projectDigest:
The coronavirus pandemic will have manifold consequences on social, political and economic well-being for most of the world’s population. Public health experts are concerned about the adverse mental and emotional impact of social distancing and isolation, especially amongst vulnerable populations such as women and children (Graham-Harrisson et al, 2020). In Pakistan, the pandemic is expected to exacerbate problems of gender inequality, poverty, and social marginalization, and further strain the credibility of weak governance systems. Using an interdisciplinary perspective, the proposed project aims to address how the pandemic impacts families and their responses to the unprecedented circumstances unfolding each day. This in turn will help to inform comprehensive policy responses to this ongoing disaster context. 

The project draws on an intersectional framework to explore the following thematic areas: (1) Gendered Division of Labour; (2) Youth, Health and Education, and (3) Institutions in a Time of Crisis. Together the thematic areas will provide an internationally comparative, longitudinal lens on local responses to a global health crisis. With its focus on understanding the impact of the pandemic on youth mental health, women’s productive and reproductive work and outreach of information networks, the study directly aligns with the SDGs.

data.projectName: Development and Production of Polyester (polyethylene terephthalate) Staple Fiber with Intrinsic Antiviral/antimicrobial Properties
data.projectDigest: The current project is focused to promote local functional textile industry by developing polyester fiber with antiviral/antibacterial properties. Antimicrobial textiles provide the benefits in hygiene, odour control and protection of the fabric from microbial attacks. In addition, in these fibers, the formation of unpleasant odors is reduced making the textiles pleasant and fresh smell after use. Therefore, antimicrobial products have long been used in health care environments for hospital gowns, patient clothes, curtain, bed cover, etc. Current project is designed to develop cost effective antimicrobial polyester fiber blended with nanomaterials locally due to several areas that need attention in this field. First of all Pakistan still lags behind in technical textile products as neither the government nor the textile industry has made any serious efforts towards synchronizing textile products with the emerging needs of the world market by developing higher value-added products. secondly, antimicrobial textiles prepared and claimed so far at international level are textiles coated with antimicrobial agents on surfaces and they lose antimicrobial potential after several washes. We claim to prepare functional fiber that retain antimicrobial properties throughout its use.

data.projectName: Donatigent: Intelligent social networking platform to contribute towards society
data.projectDigest:
The aim of this project is to use state-of-the-art technology to collectively realign our directions to achieve sustainable development goals of Pakistan through the wonderful system of charity. A social networking based online platform is proposed to coordinate our charitable efforts. This platform will be equipped with Artificial intelligence (AI), Computer Vision and Geographical Information System (GIS) based helping tools for effective coordination and execution of charitable ventures in a decentralized fashion. This platform is named as Donatigent; an Intelligent Donation Platform. It will be self sustainable and not-for-profit venture. 

The primary users of Donatigent will be the ordinary citizens who want to manage their donations themselves. Through Donatigent, they will have the option to donate monthly food-ration, school books, medicines, clothes or coupon-based donations. These donations can be picked from the donor homes and delivered to deserving families against minimal charges. The travelling road path of picking and distributing donations from/to multiple locations will be optimized through intelligent algorithms. Image processing based scanners will be deployed on smart-phones to authenticate the provision of donations.  Database records will be maintained to avoid duplicate donations. GIS based reports of geographic regions will be automatically generated to showcase and fine-tune donation trends.

data.projectName: Development of optimal traffic signal design approaches to improve the performance of signalized intersections in Lahore, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Traffic congestion happens whenever demand exceeds the capacity of a road network. It results in losses of billions of dollars around the world every year. It often happens at intersections since road users try to compete for the limited space. It can be frequently observed at signalized intersections in Lahore, Pakistan resulting in several negative consequences including delay, air pollution, excessive fuel consumption, driver frustration, traffic accidents, and signal violations among others. This project aims at providing financially viable approaches for designing and operating traffic signals in Lahore using the existing resources. The proposed design approaches will help in improving the performance and reducing the negative effects of congestion at the signalized intersections in Lahore, Pakistan.

data.projectName: Data Driven Model for Dialysis Patient Scheduling in Dialysis center Azad Kashmir
data.piUniversity: Mirpur University of Science and Technology (MUST), AJ&K
data.projectDigest: Chinar Dialysis Center is a charity-based health service located in backward area of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, with total capacity of 28 beds, one machine per bed and serving 140 selected regular patients. Due to limited resources center is denying to take new patients, however the number new patients are increasing in area, which ultimately increasing denial cases that is damaging the reputation of Institution and not fulfilling the objective of Institution. Chinar Dialysis Center wants to improve the patients scheduling to accommodate more patients with available resources. This research will focus on provision of improved patient scheduling by enhancing the bed utilization. The research will produce a database that can be used to develop the Online application for Center, that will produce the automated patient appointment scheduling that can create space for new patients.
