data.localySocioEco:
The Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is some very high mortality rates coupled with extremely expensive end-stage treatments like dialysis and kidney transplants (Lysaght 2002). A major hurdle faced by developing countries, in the containment of this disease is a lack of localized digital databases. The need for regional or local digital databases is necessitated by the high variability of the disease all around the world, which is influenced by many different factors including but not limited to various environmental, demographic, socio-economical and ethnic differences (Mills et.al. 2010). 
In Pakistan, no reliable local digital databases exist and studies on CKD management are also far and few. The availability of treatment facilities for CKD in Pakistan are scarce to the extent that in all of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, there exists only one facility, namely, Chinar Dialysis Centre, which is run by a charity/donation based non-profit organization. It has a total capacity of 28 beds only and currently providing a treatment to 140 selected regular patients. Considering the limited resources, the facility is unable to take new patients, while the number of new cases in the region is consistently on the rise. This increasing demand for treatment cannot be catered to by the organization under current set-up, which is in turn damaging the repute of the facility. A new the database as well as the scheduling system is required for efficient and effective utilization of all the resources available at the facility’s disposal. 
The current research shall focus on the provision of an improved patient-scheduling service by enhancing the bed-utilization through a data-driven decision support system. This shall be achieved through the development of an efficient localized digital database, which would form the basis of a web-based scheduling application for the centre. This online application shall generate the automated  patient appointment scheduling to create space for new patients.

data.projectName: Probing the multi-purpose role of Fourier-transform infrared micro-spectroscopy in the rapid, low-cost and accurate diagnosis of prevalent local diseases, and quality control of drugs and herbal medicines along with molecular fingerprinting.
data.projectDigest:
The project targets the multipurpose utilization of an advanced molecular micro-spectroscopy technology i.e. Fourier-transform infrared micro-spectroscopy (FTIR-MSP) for the first time in Pakistan. Realizing the local community needs of Pakistan and third point of UN’s Sustainable Development Goals i.e. Good health and well-being (UN SD Goal Nos. 3.3 and 3.4), the project is divided into one leading and two supporting projects. 

The first and leading part deals with the cost-effective, rapid and accurate diagnosis of prevalent diseases of local communities such as liver disorders, respiratory infections, tuberculosis, diarrheal diseases, kidney diseases, kidney stones, myocardial infarction, cancers and other common infections and diseases using FTIR-MSP. The purpose of using this technology is to reduce the cost of diagnosis which would eventually lower the burden on the economy. Therefore, this technology may help in improving the quality of life and well-being by facilitating the diagnostic process for the poor, resulting in better management and control of diseases. 

The second supporting part of this project comprises the use of the same technology for checking the quality control of drugs manufactured by different national and multinational pharmaceutical companies. The third supporting part covers the molecular fingerprinting of herbal medicines available in the local market.

As economic burdens and test costs discourage sick and poor to get tested. The delays result in the late diagnosis, during which there is a possible spread of diseases as well as the chance of diseases to enter into the critical stage. In this project we propose to introduce a new technology namely Fourier-transform infrared microscpectroscopy (FTIR-MSP) for the fast, accurate and low-cost diagnosis of important diseases of our community for the first time in Pakistan. data.projectName: Economic Valuation of Restoring Ecosystem Services in River Swat: A Choice Experiment Approach
data.projectDigest: The ecosystem of River Swat provides habitat for 50 species of freshwater fishes and provides hosting grounds to a number of migratory birds. Unfortunately, water of the River Swat is polluted by a number of sources such that dumping and throwing of solid/municipal waste, discharge of sewerage water and industrial effluents, and lack of proper sanitation system for the hotels and residential areas. The pollution in River Swat not only affects the aquatic life but also the ecosystem services provide by the river. There are many different ways to restore the ecosystem services in River Swat such that creating dumping grounds away from the river side, diverting the discharge of sewerage water and industrial effluents from the river, and introducing a proper sanitation system. These approaches would however require some form of financing. One possible way to finance the ecosystem restoration programs is to impose tax on the residents. However, the prior information that the residents are willing to pay the tax for financing such programs is necessary. In this regard, we will be lunched a choice experiment survey and will collect data on the attitude of the general public towards the restoration of ecosystem services in River Swat.

data.localySocioEco: River Swat provides habitat for various flora and fauna, a number of fish species and waterfowl. The ecosystem of the river supports 50 species of freshwater fishes and provides hosting grounds to a number of rare indigenous and migratory birds species. Unfortunately, water of the River Swat is polluted by a number of sources such that dumping and throwing of solid/municipal waste, discharge of sewerage water and industrial effluents, and lack of proper sanitation system for most of the hotels and residential areas all along the River. The pollution in River Swat not only affects the aquatic life but also the ecosystem services provide by the river. Therefore, the restoration of ecosystem services in River Swat is necessary. There are many different ways to restore the ecosystem services in River Swat such that creating dumping grounds for solid/municipal waste away from the river side, diverting the discharge of sewerage water and industrial effluents from the river, and introducing a proper sanitation system for the hotels and residential areas all along the River. These approaches would however require some form of financing. One possible way to finance the ecosystem restoration programs is to impose tax on the residents. However, the prior information that the residents are willing to pay the tax for financing such programs is necessary. In this regard, we will be lunched a choice experiment survey and will collect data on the attitude of the general public towards the restoration of ecosystem services in River Swat. The main objective of the proposed study is to measure the total economic value of restoring ecosystem services in River Swat. The secondary objective of the study is to determine the factors that affect the respondents’ willingness to pay for restoring ecosystem services in River Swat. For accomplishing these objectives conditional logit and mixed logit regressions will be conducted using data from 664 respondents in seven tehsils of District Swat

data.projectName: Empowerment of women through income generation for family support by adopting silk cottage industry
data.piUniversity: Lahore College for Women University, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Sericulture industry is an agro-based industry. It not only provides opportunities through jobs, but also helps to boost rural people's socio-economic lives. It is a considerable source of earnings for poor farmers and can help to uplift the economy of our country. Sericulture industry is a major source of employment as it provides employment opportunities for many people and reduces urbanization. Rearing family can earn the income approximately equal to the monthly salary of a government servant of BS-16 from 17.5 grams of eggs. However, the income can be increased depending upon the quality of eggs and number of packet reared. Unfortunately, this industry has not been on the list of priorities of our Government. Aims of this project are to motivate, educate and train poor rural women to adopt sericulture to support their families, will facilitate other researchers in Pakistan to explore the potential applications of Bombyx mori silk in different field and boost up the dying sericulture industry in Pakistan. Academic collaborators will help in disseminating the information to target audience through seminars, trainings and social media. All the project's collaborators will encourage and provide technical assistance to poor rural families to adopt sericulture for generating their income.?

data.projectName: Role of academic interventions in accelerating the process of project to product conversion during FYPs at engineering universities in Pakistan? What can be learnt from global practices of University Spinouts (USOs)?
data.projectDigest: Engineering students have difficulties in finding jobs after they graduate. One of the solutions to this problem could be that they develop their Final Year Projects (FYPs) in a way that they are able to sell it and start a business afterwards. But it is difficult to design and deliver a training that can help these students in developing such projects. This project, therefore, is trying to learn the method of devleoping and delivering such trainings from top engineering universities of the world. This training will be delivered to engineering students and then we will see what differences it makes and how these students can develop their business after graduation when they take this training.

data.projectName: Assessing and Redressing Forced Child Labor in Khyber  Pukhtoonkhwa
data.piUniversity: National University of Modern Languages, Islamabad (NUML)
data.projectDigest:
Forced child begging involves forcing children to beg through physical or psychological coercion and falls into the category of forced labor.
Forced child begging offers an important focus for the struggle for children’s rights in that it represents one of the most extreme forms of children’s exploitation and is an indicator of the state failure to protect their children.   
Forced child begging have different forms.  The children may be forced by their parents or guardians or by third parties, including cases of children trafficked into begging by informal networks and criminal gangs. It is linked to drug addiction as well and the victims are mostly the youngest.  
Children who are forced to beg are commonly beaten and suffer other kinds of abuses by those who are forcing them and from individuals they encounter as they beg.
Poverty and its consequences lie at the heart of much forced child begging. Children are viewed as a burden, and because their vulnerability itself may stir the charity of others, they can be treated as a financial opportunity rather than a child with rights. This leads to a devastating situation for the family in particular and for the society as a whole.

data.localySocioEco:
For many years, Pakistan’s reputation has been notorious as one of the worst child labor offenders. More than 12.5 million children are involved in child labor in Pakistan. According to 2018-19 Pakistan’s Labor Force Survey, showed that of those children aged between 10 and 14 years active in child labor, 61 percent were boys and 88 percent came from rural areas.”
In Pakistan, 38.8 percent of the population is living in poverty, with one in four individuals living in acute poverty. For many citizens in Pakistan, it is hard to find a job or to secure one paying enough to provide for a family. Students from impoverished backgrounds who are unable to enter school are most likely to become affected by child labor in Pakistan. Many child workers are often abused where they work, suffering beatings or torture. Many children are sent to live with middle class and elite class families to perform as domestic servants. Jobs like these become particularly dangerous for children, as they are at the risk of physical and sexual abuse without real supervision.

data.projectName: Prioritizing impediments and solutions to develop self-employment for spouseless women and people with disabilities
data.projectDigest:
The Title of the Proposed Project is “Prioritizing impediments and solutions to develop self-employment for spouseless women and people with disabilities”. 
Widows and people with disabilities are at a greater danger of coverage to tough dwelling and working environments linked with worse wellbeing effects i.e low down income and larger service uncertainty (Emerson, Madden & Graham, 2011). Employment delivers a chance for fiscal self-sufficiency and performs a crucial part in welfare and way of living for widows and people in ill health (Curnock, Leyland, Popham, 2016). Away From the fiscal influences for widows and disable persons, being jobless also excludes the linked non-income gains of contribution in the labor force like societal attachment, community participation while also reducing suitability for work-sparked revenue (Zwicker, Zaresani, & Emery, 2017). The global leaders decided to revive the social order by improving sustainable development goals under the 2030 position, having 17 goals and 169 associated targets. Sustainable development is accomplishing the needs of the present time without forfeiting upcoming potentials (Assembly, 2015).  This study focuses to improve the quality of life of the local population, to investigate the impediments in the way of spouseless women and disable persons in Swabi and to find solutions [handicraft centers, training, provision of Sewing machines, workshops and seminars] to develop self-employment opportunities for spouseless women and disable persons in Swabi. 15 centers [each with 40 + 40 females morning and evening for 3 months training; total 80x15=1200x4/3=1200x8= 9600 females] will be trained and sewing machines will be provided for their safe future For data collection, Community Based participatory Research (CBPR)

data.projectName: Introduction of Point of Care Ultrasound in Emergency Medical Care of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The purpose of this project is to train the physicians in bedside sonography for emergencies. This modality does not replace the need for official Ultrasound and other radiological assessments for definitive diagnosis. We realize the importance of a seasoned radiologist in making decisions that can impact long term patient care. Our training in POCUS will not only help differentiate life-threatening emergencies but also triage patients for discharge. The perfect example of this is of a patient presenting with testicular pain. The sensitivity of POCUS for testicular torsion when performed by a Pediatric Emergency physician is 100% with a specificity of 99.1%6. A child presenting to the E.R. can be rapidly diagnosed of having this etiology, and either goes to O.R. for treatment or goes home for more detailed outpatient radiology for definitive diagnosis and treatment in the absence of torsion.

data.projectName: Development of Efficient Bio-electrochemical Systems for Sugar and Food Industry Wastewater Treatment
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
The treatment of sugar mills and food industry effluent is energy extensive and poses a big challenge to these industries of Pakistan under the directives of the Super Court of Pakistan. This problem can be solved by employing the bio-electrochemical technology that not only promises biological wastewater treatment but also offers a simultaneous production of electricity. The bio-electrochemical system is a novel and innovative technology that could allow direct harvesting of energy from wastewater through microbial activity with simultaneous oxidation of organic matter in wastewater. Among all MFC parts, electrode materials play a crucial role in electricity generation. A variety of electrode materials have been used, including plain graphite, carbon paper, and carbon cloth. However, these electrode materials generated only limited electricity or power and there is a need to elucidate the electron transfer mechanism between engineered microbes and the electrodes, thus overcoming the polarization limitations of the microbial fuel cells. In this proposal, a novel synthetic methodology will be adopted to introduce cost-effective novel pentacyanometallate-based (PCMB) Prussian Blue Analogues (PBAs) as electrodes. Due to the unique physical and chemical properties of the PBAs including high conductivity, high surface area, corrosion resistance, and electrochemical stability, they are extremely attractive for fabricating electrodes and catalyst support. Based on the results from the electrode design studies, a complete BES (Bio-electrochemical System) will be developed.
The scope of this research proposal to team up to develop efficient, green, and high performing BES that can simultaneously treat the sugar and food industry wastewater and produces electricity.

data.projectName: Solar Thermal Electric Power and its Potential in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Women University of Azad Jammu and Kashmir Bagh
data.projectDigest: Energy is the most valuable source of human life like water and food, which plays an essential role in the economic development of a country. The statistics shows that the entire requirement of energy in the world is mostly fulfilled by the electricity and in turn the electricity is produced by different renewable and nonrenewable sources. In 2016, Electricity generation from fossil fuels (Oil, Coal and Natural gas) accounted for 67.3% of total electricity production of the world [1]. The fossil fuels are limited in the world and their use at current rate will finish the known sources in few decades and we will leave the next generation without fossil fuels. The Energy through fossil fuel is also a great threat for climate through global warming due to carbon dioxide emission. To save the world from global warming and to save some fossil fuel for next generation, it is high time to track the use of renewable energy much more vigorously than is the case at present. The best possibility for energy production without using fossil fuel is thermal solar power in the world’s deserts, with overnight thermal storage. Pakistan generates more than 60% of its power from fossil fuel sources (oil, gas and coal), which are imported. The cost price of electricity produced by the fossil fuel is too high and the government has to subsidize the electricity which results in circular debt in billions rupees. The electricity prices also effects the manufacturing cost, which in turn damage our exports. Fortunately, Pakistan is situated  at the best geographic position where average length of the day in many parts of the country  is 11-13 hours and a average temperature is about 25-30 0 C throughout the year, which is very favorable environment for solar thermal power production.

data.projectName: CPEC
data.projectDigest:
The proposal addresses the three main socio-economic issues, which are under the umbrella of SDGs. The first issue is the unemployment in the locality which is relevant to (Economic Growth – SDG-8). The second issue is the low quality of education, especially the female education in the Pakhtun belt of the Southern areas of Khyberpakhtunkhwa (Education SDG-4) and the last one is the gender-based violence and violation of women’s rights (Gender equality—SDG-5). 
In Phase-1 (SDG-8) the problem of economic growth will be resolved by opening the Chinese Model school. By Luck the The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) is passing from the Southern areas of Khyberpakhtunkhwa.The CPEC, is heralded as a ‘game changer’ for Pakistan’s economic development (Ibrar et al., 2016). There is no such school in KhyberPakhtunkhwa. The dire need has been felt to open such schools for the working folk and the business class, so that they could interact with the Chinese for the trade and investment and thus promoting the economy of Pakistan. 
In Phase-2 (Education—SDG 4) the quality of female education in southern áreas of KP will be focussed. The southern áreas of KP are Pakhtun belts where parents do not send their females to schools/colleges which is affecting the overall quality of education in KP. This issue will be resolved through awareness seminars for parents and conducting the workshops and seminars in the southern áreas of KP.
In Phase-3 (Gender Equality --- SDG 5) the focus will be on the gender issues. Through this Project the gender issues like gender-based violence, violation of women’s rights, will be resolved through awareness seminars and conferences and “Gender education” course at IER, Gomal University to achieve the sustainable goals of gender equality.

data.projectName: Poverty alleviation of camel farming community through increasing camel milk yield and marketing interventions
data.piUniversity: Lasbela University of Agriculture, Water and Marine Sciences, Lasbela
data.projectDigest: Camel is unique animal species which is blessed with God gifted potentials of milk and meat. In Pakistan, Balochistan has highest camel population in the country (41%). Despite of this good number of camels, the camel farmers are living ultra-low-level poverty ridden life. It is found that camel milk is not sold by camel farmers due to having religious and cultural misconceptions which is the major cause of poverty among camel farmers. It is estimated that camel milk of 2880 million worth rupees is produced in Balochistan annually however, not even a single penny is earned from this God gifted source. In foreign countries and in mega cities like “Karachi”, there is huge demand of fresh camel milk.  Hence, it is essential to address this socio-economic issue. Considering these facts and field circumstances, this project is designed to have good blend of field work and research experiments. Different activities/phases of the proposed project include educating camel farmers through field schools, presenting commercial camel dairy farm model, enhancing milk production in different feeding strategies, facilitating in milk collection, transportation and marketing, processing, and developing milk products on experiment basis. All phases of proposed study are well integrated to achieve the major objective of poverty alleviation of camel farmers.

data.projectName: An AI based Multilingual Ecommerce Portal to Support and Enhance Business of Local Market and Export Industries
data.projectDigest:
Sialkot is third largest export city of Pakistan which has market of USD 2.5 billion. Sialkot Chamber of Commerce and Industries has 10X plan for next 10 years.
Information technology has changed the process of product development, marketing, selling process, and communication channels that revolutionized e-commerce due to which business can be operated 24 hours a day but in Sialkot, there is not a central authority which support the e-commerce business and deal the challenges (e.g. no centralized facility for consumer/producer hunt, unavailability of custom design product facility to the local and global customer, trust deficit, insecure payment process, supply chain management, language barrier, shipment and logistic issue) faced by the export industry. 
The proposed research is about developing an AI based E commerce portal with multiple language support (i.e. Urdu, English, etc) to boost the trade of Sialkot’s Exporter, Traders, Industrial and local businessmen by dealing the local culture of Sialkot Industry like Ali baba (china), flipkart(india) E-commerce portal understand the local culture and prevailing the markets.
This is right time to build a central e-commerce portal for Sialkot industry to boost business in local and international market and proposed research will deal the said statement.

data.projectName: Impact of Coal Power Plant on Agricultural Production in Punjab, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: To meet electricity shortages in Pakistan, many non-renewable energy-based power plants were established in the near past. At a time when most of the developed world is moving towards renewable energy, many developing countries like Pakistan are relying on coal-powered energy plants. But the usage of coal in power generation plants has an impact on animal health and crop production in the area. This project aims at highlighting the effects of coal power plants on the agricultural sector of Punjab, Pakistan. The agriculture sector being a primary natural resource for providing food, suffers because of these hazardous effects. Since sustainable development rests on the idea of attaining and maintaining long term economic prosperity, social up-gradation, and environmental protection and conservation, it is critical to highlight the issues posing a threat to the ecosystem. Investigation is required to explore the effect of emissions from coal power generation sources on crops and livestock health and production under local settings. Although global warming is usually given less weightage in the production process of developing countries like Pakistan, the instant impact of emissions on animal health and productivity of crops is a serious concern for agricultural policymakers.

data.projectName: Electronic Rapid Pathogen Test Kit and AI System to fight XDR-Bacteria Epidemic in Pakistan using miniaturized Bio Sensors with CMOS IC for POC Testing and Public Life-Line Systems’ Bio Monitoring
data.piUniversity: Karachi Institute of Economics & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: This project proposes the development of a point-of-care electronic test-kit for rapid pathogen detection and early disease detection, which is supported by a backend server employing Artificial Intelligence. The main aim of this system is to thwart a potential drug-resistant-bacteria pandemic, termed as the next pandemic after Covid-19, that seem be originating from Pakistan and other developing countries from Asia and Africa. This kit would employ bio-sensors using advanced materials which would be designed in Pakistan, UK and China and, by enabling early disease detection in medical diagnosis, wide-scale biological contamination monitoring of OPDs, public-places and life-line systems such as water pipelines, this system aims to disrupt the increasing trend of microbial resistance in Pakistan. According to WHO, Pakistan is among those countries where the recent sampling of sewerage water has indicated high antimicrobial resistance and presence of several superbugs (Typhoid, TB, UTI) with a high minimum inhibition concentration, potentially rendering antibiotics against these germs ineffective. Low-cost, portable and accurate bio-sensors based rapid-test kits that be ubiquitously applied to a wide range of applications can enable early detection of diseases, bio hazards and would improve the overall sanitary conditions of the localities and  at national level.

data.projectName: Antenatal Care at door -A great step in Reduction of Maternal Mortality
data.piUniversity: Liaquat University of Medical and Health Sciences, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
In Pakistan, like other low and middle income countries (LMICs) the maternal mortality rate is high. The main factors associated with higher maternal mortality rate in the country include non-availability, non-accessibility and underutilization of antenatal care facilities, which are associated with poverty, illiteracy and cultural factors. Provision of antenatal care at the door step can help in tackling the increasing trends of maternal mortality in the country. In addition, addressing the issue of maternal mortality and factors associated with it requires several other measures such as the support from the relevant government organisations; proper training, transport, support and provision of incentives to health care professionals, support and care at the community level, and active involvement of the health care administration at the District and sub-district (Taluka/ Tehsil) levels. 
The objective of this research study is “to reduce the maternal mortality rate by providing and enhancing antenatal care at the door step of pregnant women.” Goals of the project can be achieved by providing training to midwifery and antenatal care staff at the government health care facilities at sample of basic health units and rural health centres. The training will be provided through interactive workshops by experts in the field of antenatal care, obstetrics and gynaecology. The trained midwifery and antenatal care staff will carry out regular filed visits to the assigned villages on a weekly rota basis.
 All women who are either pregnant or planning for a pregnancy will be registered to the study. The registered participants (i.e. women) will be provided with cards bearing unique identification/registration numbers, These women will be followed through out the pregnancy.

data.projectName: LCF: Achieving the Earthquake Resilient Community in Mirpur District by Turning 24th September 2019 Earthquake into Knowledge
data.piUniversity: Mirpur University of Science and Technology (MUST), AJ&K
data.projectDigest: Earthquake is a potentially devastating hazard that threaten lives, destroy property and disrupt life sustaining services and societal functions. The potential losses from earthquake hazard in terms of lives and properties are increasing in Mirpur AJK. The 5.8 magnitude Mirpur Earthquake of 24th September 2019  strongly felt by ~1.4 million people caused 38 deaths, 3,149 fully and 11,036 partially damaged masonry structures equivalent to US$98 million. In active seismic countries like Japan, Taiwan and Western US large magnitude earthquakes are frequent, but it is very rare that the death toll rate crosses double digits. The reason for such resilient built communities in these countries is better understanding of earthquake preventive-built environment by multidisciplinary investigations to turn the past earthquake disaster into knowledge and future practice. This multidisciplinary (seismologist, geotechnical & structural engineers & social scientists) and multi-institutional (Universities, SDMA AJK, PWD AJK and MDA) project is aimed to first investigate the Mirpur earthquake and develop physical and socio-economic earthquake prevention model to achieve earthquake resilient community in Mirpur district. The outcome of the project will not only achieve UN SDGs  11 & 17 but also reduce the economic losses during earthquake by guaranteeing safer and earthquake resilient built community.

data.projectName: Sustaining the economy, culture and environment through Sustainable Tourism Development in Swat
data.projectDigest: The Swat district in upper Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in northwest Pakistan is a cherished tourist destination. It receives about 1.5 to 2 million tourists each year. Its main tourism is because of its natural beauty and climate. Although, tourism promotion is on top of the agenda of the federal and provincial government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to generate revenues, strengthen local economy, create employments, and present the positive image of the country, but the current tourism practices are not sustainable and may negatively impact the local economy, natural environment, and local culture in the long run. Therefore the proposed project is an attempt to investigate the bottlenecks in the current tourism practices and provide solutions for the long-lasting and sustainable tourism practices. Furthermore, the proposed research aims to address the gaps in tourism policies and build the capacities of the locals (tourist guides, porters, women, local community leaders, and SMEs) so as to provide quality facilities to the tourists and boost the local economy for the improvement in overall standards of living.

data.projectName: Implementation of Immuno-chromatograhic strips for the detection of Acute and chronic Toxoplasmosis in Human and Food animals
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: One-third of the world’s population is infected with Toxoplasma gondii, which can cause toxoplasmosis in the developing foetus and is dangerous for people whose immune systems are compromised through disease or chemotherapy. T. gondii is also recognized as a major cause of abortion in farm animals such as sheep and cattle. The disease is manifested as severe encephalitis in human. In the life cycle of toxoplasmosis, cat serves as final host and all warm-blooded animals serve as intermediate hosts. Cats as final host can excrete millions of oocysts in their feces. Intermediate hosts include warm-blooded animals which can have tachyzoïtes (fast multiplying stage of T. gondii) in their blood in the acute phase of the disease. These intermediate hosts can have bradyzoïtes within the tissue cyst (silent stage of T. gondii) in the chronic phase of toxoplasmosis. It can be transmitted among intermediate hosts by either vertical (mother–fetus) or horizontal (carnivorism) transmission. Several diagnostic procedures are available commercially to detect antibodies in the blood of infected toxoplasmic patients in developed countries like France and USA. These diagnostic tests are available such as PCR (Polymerase Reaction), ELISA (Enzyme Linked Immuno-Sorbent Assay), WB (Western Blotting) and Agglutination. P30 also named as SAG1, is a major surface protein of toxoplasma which has been a potential candidate of diagnosis for toxoplasmosis. It has both markers of IgM and IgG antibodies. We had already produced rec-P30 of T. gondii in our research laboratory. We have already tested antigenic capacity of rec-P30 in mouse model. We have validated its diagnostic value in human and animals through ELISA. There is no rapid detection test (RDT) based on LFC available commercially in the world and in Pakistan which could be used in medical and veterinary sectors under field conditions to detect toxoplasmosis. Our prototype is likely to be scalable at commercial level and would be easily adopted by commercial diagnostic laboratories.

data.projectName: Development of bacterial resistant rice (Oryza sativa L.) hybrids for sustainable yield
data.projectDigest: Rice is the 2nd major cereal crop, which is widely cultivated, consumed, and exported. Super Basmati rice variety is the most popular among consumers, farmers, traders, and exporters due to its high quality grain and aroma. However, susceptibility of this variety to different diseases is a major problem. Among these, Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae, the causal agent of bacterial leaf blight (BLB) is considered to cause severe yield losses (Arshad et al., 2015). In severe epidemics, crop loss may be as high as 75 percent, and millions of hectares of rice are infected annually. The most-common method of defending against rice bacterial blight is the cultivation of rice varieties with genes that confer resistance to Xanthomonas oryzae infection. Xa1 to Xa33, have been identified in rice plants, and some, such as Xa21, have been integrated into the genomes of commercial rice strains. These resistant rice varieties have been largely successful, dramatically reducing yield losses in many rice-producing countries. A cloned gene, Xa4 will be transferred into three widely-used Pakistani rice varieties through an Agrobacterium-mediated system. PCR and Southern analysis of transgenic plants will be performed to check the integration of the Xa4 gene into the host genomes. Fate of transformation will be checked in the transformed plants. The selected Xa4 homozygous resistant transgenic lines with be propagated as new varieties or utilized in hybrid rice breeding. Besides that some new bacterial resistant genes may also be identified and transformed in rice to develop resistance in rice cultivars against bacterial pathogens.

data.projectName: Production of VP2 viral vector vaccine for Infectious bursal disease
data.projectDigest: The poultry industry contributes significantly to the national economy. One of the economically important diseases which poses a major threat to the poultry industry is infectious bursal disease (IBD) caused by the virus, IBDV. A viable option for controlling the disease is vaccination of chickens; however, currently-available commercial IBD vaccines are not manufactured locally, except limited quantities of the killed and live vaccines. In our lab, we have produced a modern vaccine (adenoviral vector vaccine) against IBD which has been tailored to the local needs, taking into account variations in local IBDV isolates, and this vaccine exhibits efficacy comparable to commercially available vaccines. In the proposed work, we aim to optimize and up-scale the production of our locally-developed vaccine and commercialize it in association with industrial counterpart(s) to make the vaccine easily available to end-users. To this end, technical expertise and knowledge for vaccine production will be shared with our industrial counterpart(s). The industrial counterpart(s) will also contribute towards up-scaling the vaccine production, conducting large-scale field trials, immunization studies, formulation, packaging, certification, and commercialization of the vaccine. A successful execution of the project will save foreign exchange and will contribute significantly towards sustainable development of the poultry industry in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Production of engineered Endolysins for the treatment of wound infections by difficult to treat pathogens in diabetic patients
data.projectDigest: The delayed healing of diabetic patient's foot wounds is a major complication, which mostly leads to removal of wound body part. The infection of wound area with the antibiotic resistant bacteria is the major hinderance in early healing of the wounds. The alternatives with strong antibacterial activity against the antibiotic resistant pathogens present in the diabetic wounds are need of time. The bacteriophage encoded endolysins are a very promising antibiotic alternative in this scenario, however the narrow host range along with barrier of outer membrane in gram-negative bacteria are major hurdles for their use as potent broad-spectrum antibiotic. We are proposing to engineer the endolysins to increase their breadth as well as will equip them to cross the barrier of outer membrane in Gram-negative bacteria. The developed endolysins with increased breadth and antibacterial activities will be assessed for their stability in different available ointments and sprays available and used for topical application in skin wounds. The combination of the developed endolysins with suitable ointment might lead to develop a product, which can efficiently control the growth of antibiotic resistant bacteria and will help in healing the wounds in diabetic patients.

data.projectName: Smart Irrigation base on Fito-monitoring Technology under Climate Control Conditions
data.piUniversity: Muhammad Nawaz Shareef University of Agriculture, Multan
data.projectDigest: Water applied to the crops mainly by surface (gravity driven), sprinkler and drip irrigation methods. These are the traditional and predominated irrigation methods used by the farmers in Pakistan and many other countries. Basin, border and furrow are the main types of surface irrigation. Efficiency of the surface irrigation methods is very low ranging from 30 to 50 percent. In the pressurized irrigation systems (sprinkler and drip) also called High Efficiency Irrigation Systems (HEIS) pipes are used to convey water from the source to the points of use and therefore efficiency of these methods is much higher than the surface irrigation methods. Although the pressurized irrigation systems are costly, but water saved and other benefits (increase in yield, saving in labor, etc.) often overshadow the cost. In future, existing irrigation water supplies will be under more stress due to increasing urbanization and industrialization. More economic value of water for the non-agricultural water use puts increasing stress on the existing irrigation water supplies. Objective of this project is to explore how increasing irrigation water demands should be fulfilled in future, particularly in Pakistan as well as in other developing countries in general. A Floppy sprinkler system (FSS) as a new innovative irrigation method was introduced by project team through technology development funded project. Floppy sprinkler system (FSS) is a method of applying irrigation water which is similar to natural rainfall. Water is distributed through a system of pipes usually by pumping and sprayed into the air through FSS, so that it breaks up into small water drops which fall to the ground. The pump supply system, sprinklers and operating conditions must be designed to enable a uniform application of water. The floppy sprinkler consists of a plastic pipe on which a flexible silicon tube is mounted. When water passes through the tube it snakes to and fro while slowly rotating through 360°, forming uniform droplets similar to rain drops without any mist formation. In the continuation of the previous work, a computer-based program for determining the crop water requirement for high crop yield, nutrients requirements, temperature variation under climate control condition at different growth stages is being proposed with FSS irrigation method. This system can be integrated with the network of different sensors such as soil moisture, nutrients requirement, temperature variations and yield productions will be placed at different places in the field to give real time irrigation requirement and irrigation scheduling as call fito-monitoring technology. With this system, it will be able to manage the irrigation quantity and irrigation frequency specifically during the kharif season when temperature is high. The real objectives of this proposed research are to develop fito-monitoring technology at indigenous scale and implement for climate change condition such as Egypt and south Africa did same practice for frost control as many studies recommended for sprinkler irrigation.

data.projectName: :  Secure Delivery of IMS Based Next Generation Network Multimedia Services
data.projectDigest:
Introduction 
In this part we discussed the key terms whereupon this research is based. In addition introduction to cutting edge next generation multimedia is additionally introduced here. Toward the finish of this section, IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) Releases are described. We will characterize and clarify various terminologies those give the foundation to convey this works and will be utilized over and over in our project. These terms incorporate Next Generation Networks (NGN), Service Delivery Platform (SDP), IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) and Telecoms and Internet Converged Services and Protocols for Advanced Networks (TISPAN).
Next Generation Network
In future all the tele-communication center and access network will utilize IP for the transportation [1]. The types of network in which traffic of all networks will be shipped through IP packets is known as NGN. As per ITU-T the definition is "A Next Generation Network (NGN) is a packet based network ready to offer types of different services including telecommunication services and ready to utilize various broadband, QoS-empowered transport services and in which services related architectures are autonomous from hidden transport related technologies. It offers unrestricted access by clients to various services provider. It sustains mobility which will permit predictable and consistent delivery of services to the user [1].
Service Delivery Platform (SDP)
A platform for integration of telecommunication and Information Technology (IT) and creation of new services ranges above the boundaries of network and technology is known as SDP. SDP implementation facilitates the development and deployment of new multimedia services. The implementation of the SDP is not an easy task. A lot of improvements and enhancements are required in the existing technologies and infrastructure in order to implement SDP [8].


IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS)
IMS provides architecture for the Fixed Mobile Convergence (FMC) that includes variety of protocols. Session Initiation Protocol (SIP), standardized by the International Engineering Task Force (IETF), is of the main protocol used by the IMS. In 1999 a forum known as 3G.IP launches the project of IMS. Currently 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP), 3rd Generation Partnership Project 2 (3GPP2) and Telecoms & Internet converged Services & Protocols for Advanced Networks (TISPAN) etc. are working to standardize the IMS [2].

In IMS authentication is the part of the registration process. Since before registration no authentication mechanism is employed so, it is very easy to launch register flooding and other attacks by using the spoofed addresses. So strong intrusion detection system is required to filter messages.

The endeavor of this project is to develop a secure middleware and efficient & secure methods to subscribe and provide multimedia services in IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) based Next Generation Networks (NGN) using role/statistical/machine learning techniques.

Firstly we will study and analyze the existing security mechanism of the IP Multimedia Subsystem, and then we will add a new security layer in-between of IMS core and application plane. In order to protect the application plane from different types of attacks, this middle layer will scan each and every packet that moves from IMS core to application plane. If an attack is detected the request will be discarded immediately and the attacker will be blocked. This layer will protect the whole application plane of the IMS. Security of IMS application plane will add up in the success of Next Generation Networks. It will boost the confidence of the users to use NGN services and will attract the operators to deploy NGN services. 

Secondly a service success depends upon few well known parameters like delay minimization, efficient bandwidth utilization, privacy, applicability in maximum real life scenarios, etc. So this project also include a module to enhance the four most popular IMS based NGN multimedia services. These four services are Presence, Messaging, Push to Talk over Cellular and Multiparty Conference. Efficiency will be achieved by modifying the existing session setup, registration, service creation and service subscription procedures. Inclusion of new value added features in these multimedia services is also the part of this research work.

So that open source will be deployed as IMS core. Now the second question is about IMS application servers. Again we already have these servers and we just need to customize them according to our requirement. data.projectSummary:
Introduction 
In this part we discussed the key terms whereupon this research is based. In addition introduction to cutting edge next generation multimedia is additionally introduced here. Toward the finish of this section, IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) Releases are described. We will characterize and clarify various terminologies those give the foundation to convey this works and will be utilized over and over in our project. These terms incorporate Next Generation Networks (NGN), Service Delivery Platform (SDP), IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) and Telecoms and Internet Converged Services and Protocols for Advanced Networks (TISPAN).
Next Generation Network
In future all the tele-communication center and access network will utilize IP for the transportation [1]. The types of network in which traffic of all networks will be shipped through IP packets is known as NGN. As per ITU-T the definition is "A Next Generation Network (NGN) is a packet based network ready to offer types of different services including telecommunication services and ready to utilize various broadband, QoS-empowered transport services and in which services related architectures are autonomous from hidden transport related technologies. It offers unrestricted access by clients to various services provider. It sustains mobility which will permit predictable and consistent delivery of services to the user [1].
Service Delivery Platform (SDP)
A platform for integration of telecommunication and Information Technology (IT) and creation of new services ranges above the boundaries of network and technology is known as SDP. SDP implementation facilitates the development and deployment of new multimedia services. The implementation of the SDP is not an easy task. A lot of improvements and enhancements are required in the existing technologies and infrastructure in order to implement SDP [8].


IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS)
IMS provides architecture for the Fixed Mobile Convergence (FMC) that includes variety of protocols. Session Initiation Protocol (SIP), standardized by the International Engineering Task Force (IETF), is of the main protocol used by the IMS. In 1999 a forum known as 3G.IP launches the project of IMS. Currently 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP), 3rd Generation Partnership Project 2 (3GPP2) and Telecoms & Internet converged Services & Protocols for Advanced Networks (TISPAN) etc. are working to standardize the IMS [2].

In IMS authentication is the part of the registration process. Since before registration no authentication mechanism is employed so, it is very easy to launch register flooding and other attacks by using the spoofed addresses. So strong intrusion detection system is required to filter messages.

The endeavor of this project is to develop a secure middleware and efficient & secure methods to subscribe and provide multimedia services in IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) based Next Generation Networks (NGN) using role/statistical/machine learning techniques.

Firstly we will study and analyze the existing security mechanism of the IP Multimedia Subsystem, and then we will add a new security layer in-between of IMS core and application plane. In order to protect the application plane from different types of attacks, this middle layer will scan each and every packet that moves from IMS core to application plane. If an attack is detected the request will be discarded immediately and the attacker will be blocked. This layer will protect the whole application plane of the IMS. Security of IMS application plane will add up in the success of Next Generation Networks. It will boost the confidence of the users to use NGN services and will attract the operators to deploy NGN services. 

Secondly a service success depends upon few well known parameters like delay minimization, efficient bandwidth utilization, privacy, applicability in maximum real life scenarios, etc. So this project also include a module to enhance the four most popular IMS based NGN multimedia services. These four services are Presence, Messaging, Push to Talk over Cellular and Multiparty Conference. Efficiency will be achieved by modifying the existing session setup, registration, service creation and service subscription procedures. Inclusion of new value added features in these multimedia services is also the part of this research work.

So that open source will be deployed as IMS core. Now the second question is about IMS application servers. Again we already have these servers and we just need to customize them according to our requirement. Our scope in this project is to develop role/statistical/machine learning techniques based intrusion detection and prevention system for IMS core and providing new mechanisms that makes the available services secure and efficient.

data.projectName: COVSCAN: IoT-enabled IR Temperature Screening device
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
Considering the public safety in current COVID-19 out-break, an IOT based non-contact temperature monitoring system integrated with RFID authentication, crowd warning and face mask detection is proposed. It comes with an interactive Android application, and a web-portal to manage users, temperature records, warnings and alerts in real time on daily/weekly/monthly basis.
Present device is specifically designed to enable the society to commence the business by ensuring the proper compliance of SOPs and reliable screening of infected people. Some additional features that this device can offer are given below,
•	Avoid Long queues: The scanning/operation process of present device is quick (2~3 seconds to scan/authenticate/store/notify a single user). Moreover, device can be installed at final entry points rather than the main entrance. This will help significantly reducing the long queues seen at several places while screening temperature.
•	Human-less Operation: The device is fully automated wall-mount/mobile module with wireless connectivity. Unlike the present methods of handheld passive temperature screening, it does not require a human to operate and check temperature of each person individually. This avoids human error, allows fast operation, prevents the risk of infection to person operating the device.
•	Temperature Records/warnings/alerts/Storage/Data analysis:  The device keeps a record of user’s temperature, mask history and crowd detection which may later be accessed by system administrator. Policy makers may take appropriate decision based on this data.
The project direct beneficiaries include but not limited to Companies, Organizations, Educational Institutions, Factories, Malls and Restaurants etc. Whereas, indirect beneficiaries include, government bodies and policy makers who can design policies, take decision based on data collected on a bigger scale, e.g. from organizations in a city, province or countrywide.

data.projectName: Design, Development & KHTT of GNSS Receiver for Commercial Applications
data.projectDigest:
The proposed research is focused on the indigenous design, development and Know-How-Technology Transfer (KHTT) of Software and Hardware based Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) Receiver for commercial applications. The common example of GNSS Receiver is a GPS receiver that is present in all smart phones and trackers of vehicles. This simple component has a multi-million dollar industry in world and growing at a very fast pace. 
GPS receiver gives the precise user position and time using a constellation of 24 US satellites. There are many other global navigation constellations namely the GLONASS by Russia, Galileo by EU, Beidou by China and upcoming NAVIC by India. GNSS has multi applications in the areas of transportation (aerial, space, rails, marines, roads), agriculture and farming, urban planning, construction, mobile health, navigation, electric distribution, e-commerce etc. 
The proposed research focuses on developing the software & hardware based GPS and Beidou receivers with the collaboration of research partner at Pakistan and academic partner and consultant from China under the umbrella of IST, HEC and National center of GIS and Space Applications.  It will not help in developing the indigenous product and technology but will also help in Technology Transfer and will pave the way for the attainment of Sustainable development goals (SDGs).

data.projectName: Development of instrument free technology for rapid and on-site diagnosis of poultry Salmonella infections using antibody probed immuno-magnetic bead (IMB) based system
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: Salmonellosis is one of the major zoonotic diseases responsible for causing gastroenteritis and other symptoms in poultry birds, humans. The persistence occurrence of Salmonella in chicken, poultry feed, eggs, and contamination at different handling stages results in significant morbidity in the infected birds and the consumers resulting in huge economic losses. But still the diagnosis of Salmonella is not a common practice and if performed, it is based on laboratory culture methods which are very time consuming, or PCR based detection method which is although very sensitive but needs skilled persons and expensive and sophisticated equipment for detection. The diagnostic assay discussed in this project will be first time applied locally, for a rapid and on-site detection of Salmonella on the basis of visual observation. This is an innovative approach in which we’ll combine the principles of immuno-precipitation and ELISA without using any sophisticated and expensive equipment. The interpretation of the test is based on the visual observation for colour development in positive samples. This test is also comparable with the other diagnostic tests In terms of sensitivity and specificity.

data.projectName: Development and Small-Scale Manufacturing of Human Rabies Vaccine in a Serum-Free Medium Using Fixed Strain Cultivated in Vero Cells
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest: The world’s oldest, virulent and neglected zoonosis Rabies caused by a virus; is 100% fatal and vaccine preventable. It is a single-stranded, RNA-enveloped virus of negative polarity with a simple 12 kb genome organized into 5 genes that codes for 5 structural proteins: Nucleocapsid protein (N) Phosphoprotein (P): cofactor of RNA polymerase, Protein of the matrix (M), Glycoprotein of the envelope (G) and RNA polymerase (L). Dogs are the vectors and reservoirs of rabies and not only accounts for 99% of human infection rather 40-50% reported mortality (including children) is also attributed to them. Moreover 4037 dog bites cases were recorded by National Institute of Health (Pakistan) from 2005 to 2010. Lack of knowledge and awareness regarding the pre-exposure (PreEP) and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) exist on the part of the healthcare professionals. Therefore, using a well-established technology of Vero cell manufacturing system for generating inactivated whole virus vaccine is the most feasible as the regulatory authorities have a considerable experience with it.  In order to validate its potency, stability, and immunogenicity we will also perform animal trials using both ID and IM regimen in line with protocols and SOPs approved by regulatory authorities (WHO, FDA, etc.).

data.projectName: Transformer Health Monitoring and Predictive Maintenance System
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Transformers are the most used equipment in Power Distribution Network.  These devices are locally manufactured and being imported used by power distribution companies and private sectors include industries, housing schemes etc. The losses rate in transformers is more than 30% due to overloading and theft.  As there is no monitoring system equipped with transformers, the events remain curtailed.  We propose an intelligent monitoring and control system for ordinary transformers to transform them into Smart Transformers. The smart system comprises of sensors deployed on the transformer,, AI edge computing, wireless data transfer technology and cloud server. Advanced algorithms of Artificial Intelligence process data to monitor the transformer's health, log abnormal events, and avoid complete failures and control the overloading and fault propagation into the network. An anti theft early warning and tracking system will limit the widespread theft and asset loss problems. This will increase the transformer life, efficiencies, the securities and permanent damage caused to the transformer.  This can help the county to save the overall billions of rupees spend to replace transformers every year.

data.projectName: PROJECT “ SADAR” (Arabic word used for chest/heart Solution through Artificial intelligence based Detection, Administration and Rehabilitation)
data.piUniversity: Sir Syed (CASE) Institute of Technology, Islamabad
data.projectDigest: The core idea is to use AI based Algorithms on inputs provided from POCUS Heart Ultrasounds to detect and monitor the cardiac anomalies , in order to detect/monitor COVID 19 patients (especially those with previous cardiac issues) in general and to disrupt the Ultrasound market in particular.The proposed product SADAR shall provide automated analysis of the left ventricle, from 4CH and/or 2CH views, including single and Biplane: EF, End-Systolic Volume (ESV), End-Diastolic Volume (ED) Stroke Volume and Global Longitudinal Strain. Studies show that assessing the heart’s RV size and function is a key indicator of cardiac dysfunction including pulmonary embolism and heart failure. SADAR shall provide automated analysis of the right ventricle, from 4CH modified/ focused apical view including:  Fractional Area Change (FAC), EDA, ESA, Free Wall Strain and TAPSE. Myocardial injury is present in >25% of critical cases and presents in 2 patterns: acute myocardial injury and dysfunction on presentation and myocardial injury that develops as illness severity intensifies.

data.projectName: Pre-Farming Controlled Crop Assessment Simulator to Enhance the Crop Quality for Optimum Yield and Agricultural Sustainability
data.projectDigest: Increasing population of Pakistan is a dominant factor that influences economic sustainability and food security. Pakistan’s economy heavily depends on agricultural exports.  So far, no standardized sets of Optimum Cultivation Factors (OCF) such as appropriate level of water supply to crop, seed quality, appropriate fertilizer, best pesticides spray are available in Pakistan. The lack of appropriate OCF standardization leads to the low annual yield.   Due to low yields over the years, Pakistan imports 2 Million USD consumable crop to fulfill self-growth. For economic sustainability and to cater the food security of increasing population of the country, a proper pre-testing and standardization of OCFs is necessary to increase the annual yield. This project is aimed to develop farming simulator equipment that will perform pre-farming under controlled environments for optimum yields. The equipment will mimic the actual farming at lower scale with diverse sets of seeds, fertilizers, pests and water management. This will help to standardize the crop Optimum Crop Cultivation Factors.  The equipment will be used as tool in fertilizer and pest industries, farmers, Government sector, seed production centers and universities. Further, new fruits and crops that can play role as cash crop for the export will be tested in simulator.

data.projectName: Conversion of existing fish farms to recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) with floating solar panels
data.piUniversity: Shaheed Zulfikar Ali Bhutto Institute of Science & Technology (SZABIST) University, Karachi
data.projectDigest: As aquaculture cultivation is a purposeful task therefore a controlled environment is necessary for cultivation like in agriculture. Unlike traditional fishing, the cultivation in aquaculture needs extra care for better development and productivity of fishes. This environment is provided by using artificial techniques through different devices such as aerate the water to keep dissolved oxygen levels high enough for fish to survive and thrive, pump water to and through the raceways and tanks and replace water lost to evaporation, seepage, and leaks. As, it is a fact that pumps and motors are the highest power consuming devices of electricity therefore a lot is energy is consumed in providing controlled environment.  The proposal is focused on developing a system that can sustain the demand of energy using alternate energy i.e. solar panels. Solar energy can provide the power to drive closed-system aerators and pumps. The basic components of a PV system for aquaculture are not unlike any other system used for pumping water continuously. The solar panel in this project will be developed in a way that fulfills dual purpose, one is to generate electricity, other is to provide the shade to the ponds. This will result in keeping the water temperature low, hence improving production of fishes under the shade. The immersion of solar panels in the water will also allow them to cool rapidly which will result in increased efficiency of solar energy conversion.

data.projectName: AUTONOUMOUS SURVEILLANCE SOLUTIONS FOR PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTORS
data.projectDigest: Surveillance is basic requirement of any site in commercial, domestic and industrial sectors. Existing surveillance systems are not capable to deal with all kind of anomalies due to human negligence working in central watchdog units. It is highly desirable to formulate a system that can deal with all kind of site anomalies using state of the art AI based machine vision technologies. Our proposed system is sate of the art site surveillance system based on edge computing devices, processing camera streams for protection of particular sites replacing the existing manual or semi-automated surveillance systems. Proposed system is efficient and robust in term of processing and accuracy of anomaly detection making the surveillance process reliable. End product of our proposed system will be a compact and cost-efficient device fabricated using emerging edge computing and deep learning-based object detection and recognition algorithms. IP or web camera will be interfaced with proposed surveillance device for detection of onsite events. Device will be affordable for various industries depending on the coverage area and will have a central control where the end user/consumer can access and analyze the on-site activities. Reports will be generated based on anomaly detection and intimations.

data.projectName: PAgri-IoT (Pakistan Agriculture-Internet of Things) Smart Farming Based Decision Support System For Optimum Crops Yield
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is lacking the use of Smart Farming applications. Currently the information about the progress of crops is collected manually and there is no centralized national database where the progress of crops can be collected from the deployed sensors in real-time followed by solid policy decisions. Finances must be poured for the monitoring teams which have to travel to the remote locations and collect the required data manually. Therefore, there exist a need of Solar Powered Real-time Monitoring system in smart decision making which can be utilized for optimal yield. Therefore, this project aims to develop an integrated system using remote units and android application to collect real-time data for processing, and analysis to improve the overall farming operations and management for different crops of Pakistan.. The proposed software will have the capability of integrating and analyzing data streams from multiple nodes (sensors, and weather stations) which will be deployed in Okara, Sahiwal, Pakpattan, Lahore and Gujranwala. This Project will be executed in collaboration with the Sectoral collaborator Potato Research Institute (PRI) Govt. of Punjab, Sahiwal, Pakistan.

data.projectName: Design and manufacturing of surgical instruments using metal ijection molding.
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Metal injection molding (MIM) is a metal forming process in which metal powder mixed with a particular binder (the mixture is called ‘feedstock’) is forced to enter in a mold cavity using high pressure. The pushed metal powder attains the shape of the cavity in the mold, which is the sintered to attain the required strength, thereby shrinking the compact about 10-15%. 
The MIM technology is game changer for mass production of metallic components with intricate shapes, however, it is restricted to small components less than 100 grams. The objective of the current proposal is to develop and mature the MIM technology especially targeting the surgical industry of Sialkot. More than 4000 surgical industries are located in Sialkot where millions of metallic components are fabricated using conventional technologies, which are significantly slow and labour-intensive. The proposed technology will help to boosting the production rate thereby increasing the exports.
The project was envisaged on the need indicated by surgical industry people in Sialkot. It was realized that it was possible to adapt MIM technology for surgical industry. The technology will be matured at the University and will be transferred to the industry after fulfilling legal and ethical formalities.

data.projectName: Developing commercially viable Cadmium Tellurium solar cells in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Photovoltaic cells are expected to contribute significantly towards the global energy supply mix by the end of the century. An increasing demand of energy, scarcity of fossil fuels, a need for low carbon energy generation and advances in cheap solar cell technologies make the technology appealing. Currently, Silicon solar cells form the backbone of the industry, owing to decades of experience as well as long and stable lifetimes. However, Silicon solar cells present a large barrier of entry due to stringent purity requirements and expensive fabrication facilities. As an alternative, researchers have developed thin film technologies (such as Cadmium Telluride (CdTe)), as well as third generation technologies such as perovskite solar cells, where the latter currently suffer from stability issues.

At present, almost all solar panels deployed in Pakistan are imported either as individual cells, or as modules. There is close to no capacity for indigenous development of Solar cells. In this project, we propose an ambitious aim of setting a roadmap for commercial, scalable production of Cadmium Tellurium (CdTe) solar cells in Pakistan. The word will be carried out in close collaboration with our industrial partner Thin Film Devices Incorporated (TFDInc) US, a company that specializes in thin film coatings. Together, we will first develop lab scale CdTe devices and then develop a business case for a small/medium scale manufacturing plant in Pakistan, seeking funding from local industrial stakeholders and investors.

The word will be carried out in close collaboration with our industrial partner Thin Film Devices Incorporated (TFDInc) US, a company that specializes in thin film coatings. Together, we will first develop lab scale CdTe devices and then develop a business case for a small/medium scale manufacturing plant in Pakistan, seeking funding from local industrial stakeholders and investors.

data.projectName: Smart Electricity and Water Production along-with Preservation of Water Reservoirs
data.piUniversity: Pak Austria Fachhochschule Institute of Applied Sciences and Technology, Haripur
data.projectDigest: The Energy demand is expected to increase by 8-fold till 2030 and 20-fold till 2050 in Pakistan. The urgency reason for energy structuring is critical situation of hydro, coal, oil and natural gas dependency. Hydro-energy has reduced significantly with unwanted sediments, e.g., old setups like Tarbella Dam. coal, oil, and gas energy sources only fulfill 0.3% of the energy needs following the weather complexity e.g., summer and winter on extreme scales. However, the most emergent and economical usage of Solar energy has the potential to tackle all these challenges! Therefore, we researchers at Pak Austria Fachhochschule Institute of Applied Sciences and Technology, Haripur along with other well-known researchers of this domain from the leading universities of Pakistan have developed and proposed this plan. This is a novel Floating Solar Cell energy production along with by product plan for Pakistan. For example, in our district Haripur, Tarbella Dam surface area of calm water is about 250 Square Kilometer. Moreover, KhanPur Dam may have a surface area of calm water that is about 57 Square Kilometer. Furthermore, Mang Dam which is situated in our University premises has a surface area of 366270 square feet. Besides dams and water reservoirs are abundant in nature not only in this district Haripur, but also existing at large scales in the whole country. These water reservoirs are evaporating exponentially, particularly in summer season. Such water reservoirs maybe used in a way where they can be covered by Floating solar cells and unwanted evaporations may be stopped. This will help to maintain the underground level of water at sufficient scale. On the other hands, we can generate electricity by these at large scale, approximately 25% of hydro electricity generation in Pakistan. This does not only provide the demanding supply of electricity to the industrial units but also decrease the carbon emission rate which may be increased with other oil and coal resources. In a nut shell, clean and green Pakistan with full of energy (electricity) can be attained with production of floating solar cells in Pakistan and their usage to the local reservoirs. For this reason, we have established a link with Akhter Solar Limited (UK based company). They have factory unit in Hattar Industrial Area, Haripur. This is a unique and promising opportunity to fulfill the energy resources for Pakistan beyond the boundaries. Akhter Solar Ltd is pleased to contribute/co-finance for production of the required product in this embryonic project per in their capacity. A pilot test of Pakistan’s first floating solar cell production unit will be done on partial surface area of Mang Dam Haripur. This dam is situated inside of PI institute premises and maybe considered as best option of using it as a pilot test of the project. Moreover, the slogan of PAF-IAST is based upon skilling Pakistan. We are optimistic for its possible implementation and brighten future of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Autonomous Solar Panel Cleaning Robot
data.projectDigest:
Power generation using solar cells is becoming popular with the passage of time. Initially these systems were very costly and hard to establish. The research will also include a brief cost comparison between robotic and manual cleaning techniques. Moreover, an autonomous robot for cleaning of solar panels will be developed and tested on commercial installations.

data.projectName: Introducing indigenous sugarcane sett cutter planter to the sugarcane stakeholders of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: The proposed project is about indigenous sugarcane sett cutter planter for mechanized sugarcane sowing in the country. Sugarcane planting is very labor intensive exertion and involves sett cutting for preparing seed material, furrow opening in the field, placing setts in furrows, mixing of fertilizer, application of insecticide and cover of setts with the soil. These operations are arduous, energy and labor intensive. Conventionally sugarcane planting operations are done manually. Few John Deere sett cutter planters are available in Pakistan but these are not suitable for our field environments. Therefore, our farming community could not adopt said planter. Principal investigator has designed and fabricated sugarcane sett cutter planter to address the acute problem of labor shortage and high production cost of sugarcane in Pakistan by using indigenous raw material. It is tractor drawn sett cutter planter and can be operated by ordinary tractor available at small farmer field in the country. It is very economical and performs better than expensive sugarcane sett planter available in other countries. It opens furrow, applies fertilizer, cuts cane into setts, places setts in furrows, apply pesticide and covers these setts with soil in a single operation. The objective of this project is to disseminate and facilitate the farmers to adopt this technology on commercial basis.

data.projectName: Development and Standardization of Value-Added Designer Breads: Conserving Resources, Export Potential and Public Health Benefits
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Food is the necessity and right of any individual in any country to survive. The prime segment of national strength is its population. Healthy population leads the nation towards progress avoiding un-necessary expenses to health issues and adapting productive activities. The food security is a challenging issue of current times in the world including our country. About 40.2% population is facing stunting growth, 18% are facing wasting disease problem, 25% is underweight in our country, 20.5% population is undernourished, 44% children are stunted, overall, 36.9% are facing food security (WFP 2020). This type of statistics in human growth is directly linked with food and with this situation, the dream of prosperity will never come true. This food scarcity becomes more devastating on uneven distribution of food items or resources in the population. Despite of plenty of resources in our country, we are facing a significant food security challenge, while developed countries, despite of having less resources, are self-sufficient. The other main escalating factor in food shortage is wastage of resources in uncivilized way. Another linked problem is the deficiency of minerals (ZN, I & Fe). These minerals deficiencies are causing serious health issues in children, adults, and women (Rajendra 2012).  Obesity is another issue of developing world. It can be controlled with the use of designer breads made with this purpose. The wise use and equal distribution of food stuffs can alleviate the problem of hungry population. The use of technology and value addition may help to overcome this situation in developing countries as it helped in developed countries. This project is designed to search alternatives and introduction of technology to utilize the resources in a better efficient way by improving the shelf life, storage time, fortification with minerals and hence improving export potential by the application of value addition in the most consumed wheat products and to assure even and sustainable distribution of bread to eliminate hunger.
