data.projectName: Development of a Rotibot: Transforming a Prototype into a Product-Grade Automatic Roti-Cooking Machine
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest:
The objective of this proposal is to convert the already developed prototype of a low cost Rotibot into a product for commercialization. We have developed 10 machines of beta version. This product would automatically knead flour, make dough, flatten the dough and cook roti.
The prototype and beta version was developed through HEC TDF funding. We have achieved all the deliverables successfully. Four different version of prototype have been developed and tested successfully. 10 machines are fabricated (few are in making) and process is optimized in each iteration. For product and consumer based design, we have had discussions with a product designer and after these changes in the design, we will be able to commercialize it.
Millions of household in sub-continent and expatriates of sub-continent origin cook roti/chapatti every day as part of their staple food. Cooking roti is a quite involved and time taking process. A fully automated appliance will bring significant convenience in the life of millions of people. One similar product, which is available in international market is very expensive (Rs 1 70,000 per piece) and the company has not been able to meet the demand resulting in the back log of almost 0.3 Million units. The South East Asian population hosts a significant majority of lower and middle class people. Most of these people either would not prefer to buy such an expensive machine or cannot afford to buy it altogether, consequently, another aim is to make the machine available to a larger market by introducing it as a low-cost product.

data.projectName: Prototype wastewater treatment plant development for the seven distilleries of Sindh
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
Distilleries are one of the leading industries relying on indigenous agricultural products (Sugar cane molasses) and exporting ethanol hence bringing foreign exchange to Pakistan. One of the biggest issues in the distilleries is the production of high strength wastewater (Chemical Oxygen Demand:120-190 g/L; Total Dissolved Solids: 90 g/L) that contains many toxic compounds. Distilleries utilize the spent wash for the methane production that runs boiler and makes industry self-sufficient and do not need any extra natural gas. Even after treatment the wastewater still contains 30 g/L COD that is very high to discharge into water bodies as NEQS for COD is less than a g of COD.

data.projectName: Indigenous Development of Automatic Syringe Pumps for Intravenous Infusions of Covid-19 Patients in ICU
data.piUniversity: Sir Syed (CASE) Institute of Technology, Islamabad
data.projectDigest:
With the rise in Covid-19 cases in Pakistan (321,877 current cases) and throughout the world (40 million current confirmed cases) more and more patients are being admitted into the ICU and emergency wards but due to lack of critical healthcare facilities in the hospitals of Pakistan, the death toll is gradually rising in Pakistan making up to around 5000 total deaths. Amidst this critical situation where the mortality rate is rising day by day, there is a significantly high demand of developing local emergency healthcare equipment such as ventilators, syringe pumps etc. to fight against this contagious disease. 
Therefore, the indigenous development of portable syringe pumps on large scale in Pakistan can sufficiently provide emergency and ICU units of various local hospitals with this valuable medical equipment to help doctors treat Covid-19 affected patients properly and safely by allowing them to maintain a safe physical distance. The development of a local portable syringe pump device will also lead to a positive managerial impact, with a substantial reduction of time to monitor patients by nurses/doctors. This will definitely result in a better management of human resources and will also cause reduction in the nursing cost. This development of automatic portable syringe pumps also replaces the conventional manual IV infusions which are less efficient and less accurate, thereby, increasing the efficiency of infusion process.

data.projectName: Development of a sustainable Indigo dyeing process: Application of green reducing agent and analysis of colorimetric properties
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
The present research involves the development of an environment friendly dyeing of cotton with indigo dyes. The main objective of the project is to replace the conventional reducing agent, sodium hydrosulphite/sodium dithionite with an organic or biodegradable alternative. The activities mainly involve the process development by selecting a suitable reducing agent and optimizing the process parameters by experimental design technique. The feasibility of different kinds of reducing agents (commercial and natural products) would be explored to attain the maximum benefits. 
The scientific hypothesis is based on the attainment of the desired colour strength and fastness properties with a green reducing agent against the conventional. The process developed would be essential to the field of conventional textile colouration which would be highly beneficial for the local and international market.

data.projectName: Smart Ambulance Care and Readiness in Emergency & Disaster (SACRED)
data.piUniversity: Capital University of Science and Technology, Islamabad
data.projectDigest: Heavy traffic conditions in urban areas severely interrupt the ambulance services in an emergency situation, like accidents, earthquakes, or other disasters. In most of these scenarios, time is crucial to provide emergency relief and proper health care, in order to save lives. However, much time is wasted during the ambulance travel, and then the time-consuming initial diagnoses at the hospital, eventually causing death of a large number of patients. CUST will collaborate with its industrial partner Jazz, to develop and deploy a prototype of smart ambulance service, which will provide immediate relief and initial health care during the time a patient is transported to the hospital. The service will be continuously in communication with the hospital (a) to get advice of a doctor as per the patient’s condition, (b) monitor patient’s condition using ambulance medical equipment as well as a number of sensors, and communicate this information to the hospital via Jazz Cloud, (c) prepare the hospital in advance for the appropriate treatment needed for the patient, and (d) divert the ambulance either to a nearest clinic if the patient’s situation gets deteriorated rapidly, or to an appropriate hospital if the required facility is not available at the initially targeted hospital.

data.projectName: Transition of Antenna and Measuring System from Pilot Product to Manufacture
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
To impart a quality education to the future pillars of the nation is our prime objective. Talking on the engineering side we always think on a line how can we make our youngsters  as a creative and research oriented engineers. This can be done only if our labs are well equipped and must meet the challenges of the time. Antenna measurement is very important Lab for Electrical / Microwave and Telecom Engineering for UG level. In the present scenario Antenna field has become very popular because of 5G applications. Looking towards the importance of the said area in near future, we proposed an idea of development of “Antenna Training and Measurement System” to HEC and got funding of RS 10.124 M for the development of such a system under TDF plan of HEC.  The project is completed and pilot product of such a system has been developed in 04 different versions (with  1 GHz source only, with 3 GHz source only, with two sources of 1GHz and 3 GHz and with three sources of 1 GHz , 3 GHz  and 10 GHz.).  
Now our issue is the mass production.  But moving of pilot product to mass production is really a challenge. It is a complex process that combines creativity and procedure. It has been observed that the common obstacle to a successful market launch is the transition of the pilot product to manufacture. R&D is still required for this transition.
Lab-Volt a Canadian firm is also providing such Antenna Training and Measuring System but is very expensive.  The price quoted by Lab-Volt through his agent, Intermark Islamabad, is US$ 22,433= equivalent to Rs. 3.70 M @ Rs 165 per US $ of today rate. This price doesn’t include GST and Income tax etc. The minimum requirement of a class with 50 students is 15 systems as per PEC/ HEC requirement.  Country like ours can’t afford this heavy cost and again in US dollars. 
The Test Bench of same quality and with some better features have been  developed with TDF funding. Our developed Antenna Training and Measurement System is a low cost  with price  of Rs 0.3 – 0.7 M depending on the version specified.  The antenna measuring system developed by Lab Volt has the deficiency of understanding level which is the requirement of today’s antenna engineer.  The proposed antenna training and measurement system will fill this gap. 
The research proposal presents the idea how can we transmit this developed pilot product to manufacture stage and can reduce the cost further.

data.projectName: Eco-friendly compressed earth interlocking bio-healable bricks to promote sustainable infrastructures.
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: One of the major reasons behind smog is conventional clay brick manufacturing that is energy intensive and eco-hazardous process which utilizes excessive energy, releases harmful gases and particulate matter during firing process ensuing smog. Moreover, Pakistan is the third largest country which is operating approximately 12,000 brick kilns to meets the needs of construction. To overcome this problem masonry-based Interlocking Compressed Earth Bricks (ICEBs) are proposed. ICEBs are versatile, economical, durable, easy to use and environment friendly. ICEBs are blocks of soil compressed by a press (manual or automatic) into the shape of a block along with addition in fractional amount of stabilizer (Cement or Lime). The durability of ICEBs is yet a challenge for researchers to address. The recent project proposes bio-triggering of soil borne bacterial species to improve the durability without compromising the cost of brick elements. These bios prompted ICEBs will consume CO2 in their bio-metabolic process to autonomously heal the induced structural and non-structural cracks. Hence, the developed ICEBs will offer an affordable and environment friendly option to the construction industry of Pakistan with least maintenance concerns.

data.projectName: Demonstration of Biomass Gasification at the Potential End-Use Sectors for Dissemination and Marketing of Technology
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Industries in Pakistan have been battling with the energy insecurity of the country. The available solutions in this respect are either reliant on expensive fossil fuels or intermittent power production. Industrial captive power with an indigenous and fully captive standalone clean energy technology has the potential to transform the industrial sector of Pakistan. Biomass gasification technology is one such technology that offers a vast set of value addition prospects to various sectors. Despite providing for captive power to the industry, it has the potential to offer industrial production of value-added products, provide for process heat in lesser intensive process applications and a clean and productive municipal waste management solution. This project aims to demonstrate this technology through state of the art demonstration units at all of these potential end-use sectors in collaboration with a manufacturing partner. This would enable the commercial take-up of this technology and the solution's formal introduction to the industrial and waste management spheres of Pakistan.

data.projectName: Indigenous Development of Advanced Target Tracking Remote Weapon Station Standalone System
data.projectDigest:
Computer vision is an integrating scientific field that deals with how machines can be made to gain high-level understanding from digital images or videos with regards to automation control system. Nowadays, computer vision plays an essential role in military and defense applications. At present, tracking has become an extremely important part for various defense missions. Numerous countries are beginning to modernize their mine-resistant ambush-protected (MRAP), armored patrol vehicle (APC), and infantry fighting vehicle (IFV) with automatic controls. As part of this movement for increased survivability, countries are adopting remote weapon station (RWS) systems to move the operator inside the vehicle, removing the soldier from enemy’s fire. Advanced target tracking (ATT) RWS utilizes robotic vision system for automatic target tracking and provides the interface to remotely control the platform on which the machine gun (e.g. AAMG) is mounted, from inside the base station i.e. battlefield tank or armored vehicle. This system not only ensures the safety of the commander / soldier but also increases the probability of hitting and damaging the target effectively. Moreover, applications of this system are not restricted only to battlefield tanks and armored vehicles but also have utilization in naval and air defense systems, security and surveillance in restricted areas.
 
In order to fulfill security requirements, Pakistan needs to import these expensive systems from developed countries. Recently the tender for Protector RWS of 12.7mm AAMG was uploaded on PPRA website by ARDIC, HIT, MoD, GoP. With our commitment to provide low cost indigenous solutions to national organizations, we have already developed a prototype as a proof of concept for Automatic Target Tracking (ATT) System working in real-time. This can be further developed to a military grade ATT RWS as a good quality commercial end-product in Pakistan with far less investment. This will not only remove our dependency on the foreign expertise but will also release a great pressure from national exchequer. Furthermore, indigenous development of Protector ATT RWS project will not only fulfill our requirements for upgradation of all armored vehicles along with air defense and naval defense, but also provide us an opportunity to enter in the global market and to generate a huge amount of revenue by exporting that system. Moreover, we intend to develop trained human resources and establish a thriving industry that will lead to job opportunities for talented students, researchers and graduates in the field of engineering and technology in Pakistan and overcome job crisis in this field due to lack of local industry.
We, at University of Sialkot, are collaborating with Advanced Research, Development and Information Center (ARDIC), an R&D setup for the research, development and integration of advanced armored systems at Heavy Industries Taxila (HIT). HIT will support us with in kind resources, including their mechanical facilities to develop the mechanical platform of the system and will provide us with a military (MLT) standard (STD) embedded computer for commercial end product development. HIT will also facilitate the testing of the end product and will bear all the cost related to operation of its armored vehicles. Moreover, a highly trained workforce at HIT will guide the commercial development of RWS. The collaborative industry has connections in the local and international market that will help in commercialization of the product.

data.projectName: Restoration of petroleum contaminated soil by bio-stimulation, bioaugmentation and phytoremediation with local dominant plants in lab and pilot scale
data.projectDigest: Crude oil polluted soils have become very important environmental problem. Natural degradation can lower down the limited amount of initial hydrocarbon (HC) level in soil and with the passage of time hydrocarbon degradation becomes difficult. In the District Chakwal many crude oil drilling places were discovered in the recent years. Where oil exploitation and transportation have contaminated the soil. The size of contaminated site is more than 12 acre in this District which requires a cost effective technique to restore this soil for use. In the present project different bioremediation approaches will be used in lab scale and most suitable approach will be used in pilot scale in an area of 2530m2 surrounding Chakwal crude oil drilling well. In the first stage, different organic wastes will be used for composting in order to provide nutrients to microbial community to degrade HC and to improve soil texture. Microbial number and diversity which usually becomes low as the time passes, to overcome this hydrocarbon degrader’s culture will be applied. Phytoremediation with native grasses will be performed in the last stage of this project, to find most competent plant for hydrocarbon removal from the soil and to be use in full scale project.

data.projectName: Building Up Integrated Payment Aggregator for Universities of Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Modern Languages, Islamabad (NUML)
data.projectDigest:
With the advancement in telecommunication, electronic payment systems are rapidly replacing the traditional modes of payment that involved personal contact between depositor and collector and after covid-19, progress toward conversion from traditional methods to e-payment and digital financial services increases. Most of the universities of Pakistan are still using manual or semi e-fee challan systems which have a hectic fee generation and collection process, largely making them dependant on Finance staff and financial institutions. Students of almost all universities of the regular users of digital services such as digital payments or e-payments, internet access and professionals in smart phone usage provides infinite opportunities to succeed as going digital or e-payment system. Principal investigator associated with National University of Modern Languages (NUML) in partnership with Ecofin (pvt) Limited and AKSA Technologies intends to develop a payment aggregator to host unified electronic chalans with an open access to all existing banking customers through Alternate digital payment channels. This payment aggregator will also benefit potential educational institutions i.e. in first step, all universities and in second step private colleges and school to subscribe without incurring any capital expenditure. 
The prime concern of development of Payment aggregator is to provide user-friendly, efficient and reliable digital fee payment system to more than 2 million students and will launch integrated transparent medium of fee management for more than 160 universities. This will not only benefit to students and universities but  will also be a step toward a digital Pakistan. In this product i.e. “Payment Aggregator”, following key interventions will be made:-
•	Universities export data set against invoices generated into aggregator through provided Access.
•	Payment aggregator will make this dataset public for scheduled financial institutions.
•	Students will be informed through SMS notification.
•	Students will visit payment aggregator and enter challan ID provided in SMS/eChalan
•	E-challan will be presented on screen.
•	Students/ guardians will pay the dues through their own respective bank account. 
•	Students/ guardians will be intimated about fee submission confirmation through SMS 
•	Aggregator will export payment file into university bank account (any scheduled bank) and internal finance system.
•	Funds will be credited into university central account on day 1.
 
Ecofin (Pvt) Limited and ASKA Technologies will provide support i.e. 20 million (75%) in the development of “Payment Aggregator” and to share expertise during all phases of development as; (a) requirement analysis phase, (b) system design phase (c) implementation of system design, (d) testing of prototype and (e) assessment and commercialization of payment aggregator for all universities, private collages and school in Pakistan.

data.projectName: Development of Nutraceuticals using Nanocarriers for potential Delivery System: A Smart Food Technology for Breast Cancer
data.projectDigest:
The recent adaptation of lifestyle especially junk food consumption has led to many complex diseases. The improper nutrition and changed basic food habits are threatening human health worldwide. The primary cause of death in most of developing countries is because of cardiac issues followed by cancer, arthritis, and numerous others. These rapidly growing disease complications have endorsed the advanced and expensive treatment approaches in pharmaceutics. However, risk of toxicity or adverse drugs reactions (ADRs) related to modern medicines led to consider the complementary or alternative medicines and functional food-based approaches for the human health management. Breast cancer is one of the most diagnosed cancers in women around the world. Natural products have an imperative role in the synthesis of anti-cancer drugs which are more cost effective with less side effects. Pakistan has a diverse range of medicinal plants, some of which have potent anti-cancer properties, and this is an unexplored source of safe oncology drugs. Now a day’s consumer being disappointed with high cost anti-cancer disease-treatment approaches are diverting their attention toward the complementary or alternative beneficial therapeutic products with lesser side effects.
Nutraceutical’s health benefits have been well demonstrated, but their therapeutic applications for the prevention of diseases are highly research oriented. In order to take the maximum advantages of bioactive compounds (nutrients and non-nutrients), responsible for the functionality of nutraceuticals, promising applications have been suggested based on combinations of individual, well characterized phytochemicals. This attractive approach would allow synergic situation that would minimize the dosages, eventually decreasing the toxic side effects, while becoming instrumental in the prevention of an array of human health problems, particularly cancer. The bioavailability of nutraceuticals identi?ed as valuable bioactive compounds, in the frame of a speci?c clinical entity of health disorders, can be enhanced with the help of advanced carrier system based on nanoparticles. Nanoparticles have been investigated as an ideal delivery systems that could contribute to control release and to ?ne-tune pharmacokinetics, bioavailability, and bioef?cacy. This smart technology would contribute to improve the stability of encapsulated bioactive nutrients and non-nutrients against environmental changes.
The proposed project aims to develop and transfer the technology using combinatorial therapy for breast cancer based on intelligent food (nutraceuticals) together with nanoparticles which will improve the bioavailability of bioactive compounds and provide an effective therapeutic option without any undesired toxicity. If the aims of project will be achieved, it may enhance understanding about scientific basis of smart food based on nutraceuticals, which will improve the knowledge of drug efficacy in Pakistan pharmaceutical industry and society will get benefit through the use of smart and safe food products for human healthcare.

data.projectName: Automatic Language Identification Device and Mobile Application
data.piUniversity: National University of Modern Languages, Islamabad (NUML)
data.projectDigest:
This project focuses on the development of a device and a mobile application for automatic identification of spoken languages from speech utterances. Language Identification (LI) has a wide range of applications in e-health, tourism, speaker recognition, mobile/telephone monitoring, prison call monitoring, e-learning, and machine translation. In this project an LI device will be constructed/fabricated which can be installed over telephone lines and also on public places to acquire information about the ethnicity of people in the nearby area by classifying languages they speak. Moreover, a mobile application will be also developed which can be used in the tourism industry to help the tourist to recognize the language of locals and subsequently translate into other languages. In case of e-heath, both the device and the mobile app will connect patients with doctors speaking the same language(s). In education sector, they can be used to monitor and recognize the medium of instruction in the face to face and online teaching environments.
The first step of the project is corpus construction. The corpus will cover international languages like English, Chinese, German, Arabic, Japanese, Korean, Hindi, Urdu etc and regional languages of Pakistan such as Urdu, Punjabi, Pashto, Sindhi, Balochi and Kashmiri. The second step is training of machine (Artificial Intelligence Algorithms). In the next step, identification of languages in the spoken utterances will be carried out using a fabricated LI device and mobile app. The LI device will be fabricated in collaboration will the National Institute of Electronics, Islamabad where as mobile app will be developed in collaboration of Yoan Sytems, Pakistan. The proposed project is a step forward to develop resources for regional languages of Pakistan, also developed device and mobile app will create a cash flow and revenue.

data.projectName: Detection and DNA-barcoding of SWEET gene(s) alleles in Pakistani rice landraces for informed decisions on bacterial blight-resistance by the rice growers and entrepreneurs
data.projectDigest:
Bacterial blight (BB) disease is a major food security threat to the rice crop in Pakistan and the world alike. Susceptibility (S) of rice to BB depends on major host S genes in the host hijacked by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae (Xoo) pathogen via its transcription activation-like effectors (TALes) injected in the host. A class of major host S genes, the SWEET genes family, is transcriptionally induced by the cognate major TALes of Xoo in a gene-for-gene susceptibility manner to create a state of susceptibility. Extant populations of Xoo from rice growing regions of the world induce only 3 of 21 SWEET family members present in the rice genome as susceptibility targets. The rice-Xoo system, contextual to SWEET genes-TALes, has been extensively explored in various rice growing regions of the world. The context, relative to Pakistani rice-Xoo system-, however, has not been explored yet. 
	Screening of Pakistani rice accessions will be done in the current project. Tester rice lines mutant for the 3 SWEET genes will be challenged with Pakistani Xoo strains to identify the candidate SWEET gene(s) responsible for susceptibility. Likewise, tester Xoo strains, lacking in major TALes will be used to identify the specific major TALe(s) conferring virulence to Pakistani Xoo strains. Resistance in the selected rice accessions will be confirmed by RNA expression and promoter sequence analyses of the candidate SWEET gene(s) in question using real time(RT) quantitative (q)- PCR analysis and DNA Sanger sequencing, respectively. Non/low expression of the candidate SWEET gene(s) will amount to resistance in the selected rice accessions. A “diagnostic toolkit/protocol” to detect BB-resistance in Pakistani rice accessions will be the product of this project in addition to knowledge generation and skilled human development in the form of PhD, M.Phil and B.S. students. The product can be commercialized to Pakistani rice growers, entrepreneurs and exporters as broad-spectrum BB-resistance detector, a step toward the development of “super rice”.
The project uniquely combines both basic and applied research aspects. Applied aspect consists of screening for the resistant allele of SWEET gene(s) via rice-Xoo interaction, as a component of toolkit/protocol development. Basic aspect consists of validation of resistance via RNA expression and promoter sequence analysis of the SWEET gene(s) in question. 
	The PI has worked for several years on molecular rice-Xoo interaction at Kansas State University, USA (Post-docs) and Tsukuba University, Japan (PhD), utilizing recombinant DNA technology, Genomics, and Proteomic approaches. Co-PI has worked on BB of rice for several years in Japan and China. PI also has collaborations with Universities of Missouri and Florida, USA, CDRI and PGRI and,NARC, Islamabad, and Engro Chemicals,  Pakistan (letters enclosed), all of which will be helpful components to successfully execute the proposed project.

data.projectName: Enriched vermi-based integrated product (vermi-biofertilizer): Utilization for Tomato production in Azad Kashmir, Pakistan
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest: the aim of current research is to develop the plant growth promoting bacteria-Vermi-compost integrated product (PGPVB+VC) and seed coating technology for the improvement of tomatoes production in Pakistan. Our mission is to develop organic vermi based microbial biofertilizer that not only increased the seed germination, growth and development, but also fulfill the country need. To obtain higher tomatoes production, vermi-compost and PGPVB (Plant growth promoting vermi-bacteria) will be isolated from earthworm’s gut and used as integrated product. The seed germination, seedlings, and vegetative growth parameters will be analyzed. The nutrients uptake and protein profiling of tomatoes will be examined. The coating of integrated product will be carried out for better environmental adaptation of vermi-bacteria from fluctuating environmental conditions. This coated form of the integrated product will be commercialized and promoted. Hopefully, the results would support the utilization of PGPVB-vermi-compost product for the tomatoes production in Pakistan as vermi-biofertilizer.

data.projectName: Exploiting modern technology and enhanced policies for bridging the gaps between farmers and the markets: A methodology to cut the middle man.
data.projectDigest:
The agricultural productivity has certainly increased in the country due to the usage of advanced machinery and modern farm practices. Theoretically, this increased output should have been complemented with the increased income of the farmers. However, the farmer's income only represents a meagre share of the total income generated per acre, whereas, the middle-man takes majority of the earned capital. The dominance of middle-man is often severely criticized for worsening financial conditions of the small farmers. However, it’s also true that without the help of a middleman, the small farmers will not be able to arrange even basic farming ingredients which include, but not limited to, seed, fertilizer, and even the diesel for farming operations. The financial dependence of farmers on the middleman makes him an obligatory component of our agriculture. However, with increasing cost of inputs and decreasing governmental subsidies with an intention to make agriculture a self-sustainable sector, the role of middle man needs to be eliminated so that farmers could afford the increasing cost of production while getting maximum benefit out of farming.
We plan to develop a three-tier policy that will initially limit the role of the system of middleman in the province and ultimately leading to its extinction afterwards. In the three policy tiers, the plan is to include: 1) the farmers, 2) the consumers (whole-sellers, exporters and the general public), and 3) the provincial and the federal governments. To link farmers and the consumers, we will make use of modern technology whereas, the government will facilitate that linkage through friendly policies. The idea is to directly link the farmers with the consumers thus ending the middle-man's dominance. Whereas, the financial assistance for the farmers can be sought from cooperative firms, banks, and even the joint stock companies (JSCs) under our proposed financial assistance program.

data.projectName: Evaluation of indigenous flora of Swabi and adjacent valleys of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa for insecticidal bioactivity and development of a bio-pesticide formulation
data.projectDigest:
Excessive use of insecticides not only damages the environment but also results in development of resistance to pesticides. Moreover, the insecticides are usually indiscriminate in their action and destroy populations of friendly/non-target insects. It is therefore necessary to search for effective but low cost and environment friendly alternatives. One potential area for such insecticides is the use of insecticides derived from plants (botanical pesticides). Many such plant species have been identified which contain chemicals that are lethal to insects due to the fact that they disrupt the behavior, or biological processes of the insects. Pakistan is rich in biological diversity and indigenous flora has been reported to contain pharmaceutical and insecticidal properties. However, phyto-chemical assays needs to be conducted to identify the appropriate plant chemicals for their effect on insects and possible use as alternate insecticides. The present research project aims at exploring indigenous flora of district Swabi and adjacent regions for plant chemicals having insecticidal properties. The exact level of toxicity/repellency, mode of action, effectiveness and efficacy needs to be determined prior to their use against insects on a large scale. In this project, medicinal shrubs and herbs will be collected through extensive surveys of the study area, particularly from six ecologically diverse sites i.e. Swabi, Buner, Mardan, Nowshera, Swat and Gadoon. Necessary help will be taken from the already published work regarding diversity and photochemical composition of plants. Extracts from plants will be evaluated through a series of bioassays for their toxicity and/or repellency against various insects of economic importance but locusts, army worm and termites in particular. Botanical extracts of interest will be further tested in two or three-way combinations against insects under lab and field conditions. Bioactive constituents will be identified and isolated and utilized for a bio-pesticide formulation. Potential compounds will be will be submitted as patent in coordination with M/S Crop Max Pesticides.

Proposed research work is purely of applied nature and is based on the fact that some of the indigenous flora of study area would contain certain bioactive phytochemicals, which can exhibit insecticidal and/or repellent properties against insect pests including the future and current threat ‘Migratory locust’. 

I.	To explore and evaluate the bioactivity potential of indigenous flora of Swabi and adjacent regions against different insect pests of economic importance. 
II.	To find out synergistic effects of most effective botanicals will be determined using their binary and/or tertiary combinations. ?
III.	To find out the bioactive molecules/components of these botanicals expressing insecticidal or repellent actions against insect pests through biochemical analysis ?
IV.	To evaluate the most effective plant extracts under semi-field conditions and to formulate in to a bio-pesticide to be submitted for patent.

data.projectName: Performance and Recovery of Flue Gas Energy from Boiler via Heat Exchanger
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan is a developing country, with industrialization on the rise, for better economic conditions in the country. Most industries utilize boilers, with various feed sources. In the perspective of growing demands, efficient boiler systems are critical for optimum industrial production, to ensure stable, continuous, and reliable production line operation in the industrial sector. Coal-fired boilers are characterized with lower efficiency and greater carbon emissions compared to gas-fired boilers. The flue gas has temperature greater than 150degree Centigrade. The flue gas has large quantity of latent heat consisting of 10% ~ 11% of lower calorific value. Researchers claim that if this latent heat can be partially recovered, the boiler efficiency can be improved by a large margin.
Fuel fired steam boilers or waste heat recovery boilers are used in industry for completion of various heat related processes. There are various methods of heat recovery applicable in the industry. Some methods can recover greater energy compared to others, and thus improve overall boiler efficiency. There are numerous advantages of boiler heat recovery, including greater efficiency, thus lower fuel consumption and conservation of additional fuel cost, drastic reduction in air pollution, due to lower quantity of flue gases emission from the industrial plant to the atmosphere. This advantage further gives benefits of saving costs on additional equipment, such as pumps, filters, etc required for handling flue gases. 
The existing boiling systems installed in the industry use Carbon Steel Fin Type economizers. Usually, economizers (fin type) made of Carbon Steel are found for flue energy recovery. However, material of Carbon Steel does not allow to recover energy of flue gas to greater extent, as risk of corrosion increases with reducing flue gas temperature, the feed water does not extract available energy from flue gases and flue gases keeps discharging at very high temperatures. The heat transfer reduces with increasing layers of carbon deposits. We, therefore, propose Stainless Steel 304 Shell & Tube type Heat Exchanger as one option and Stainless Steel 304 fin types as another option.
In our proposed system, we prefer to utilize this heat by installing SS304 shell & tube heat exchanger or fin type heat exchanger to either drive single hot water chiller in closed loop if air conditioning demand exist or utilize to heat water for processes in closed loop or for heating boiler feed water temperature. The technology "Recovery of Boiler Flue Gas Energy via Stainless Steel Heat Exchanger" will be able to solve current industrial, economic and technological problems for the development of Pakistan to a significant extent. For commercial viability, one boiler size is chosen that is commonly installed across various industrial systems can be installed on any fired boiler or waste heat recovery boiler. Such boilers are commonly found in industrial sector.
Our collaborators from Iceberg Industries will facilitate in execution of proposed technology, and accumulation of results. We propose to distribute the project in Mechanical and Electrical Engineering based phases. A team under PI would carry out the electrical part, consisting of sensing, monitoring and control, while another team under Co-PI and sectoral collaborator would work on the mechanical design and development of the economizer. The prototype economizer software-based design will be carried out by the COMSATS team(Mechanical), while hardware design and prototyping will be carried out in corporation with the industrial partner. Sensor based display for monitoring and control will be designed by COMSATS team

data.projectDigest: Medical community in most of their treatments use digital images for diagnosis and further surgical operations. With the advancement in digital image processing techniques, medical applications use digital image processing techniques as a tool for better detection and diagnosis purposes. These techniques are directly embedded in the medical instruments (CT and MRI) causing better image analysis and suggestions. Furthermore, the demand for more accurate and visually pleasing images is increasing with the explosion in the number of digital images taken every day. But digital images are frequently corrupted by different types of noise that result in loss of most important information, i.e., edges, corners and other sharp structures. In medical images, most common noise that affect the image analysis in random valued impulse noise which is usually added to the image during acquisition or transmission. To preserve the image details, image restoration is considered as most important pre-processing step in digital images processing (DIP). Most of the subsequent processes, i.e., object recognition, object tracking, segmentation, compression etc., may affect badly if the input image contains some noise. In this project, we will investigate most common noise types and develop an efficient tool that can be embedded in medical instrument for better noise suppression and detail preservation.

data.projectName: Development of Microbial Cell Factories for Mass Scale Production of Glycyrrhetinic Acid
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
The history of Biotechnology dates back to ancient writings from around 6,000 BC that give an indication that the Babylonians and the Sumerians used microbial yeast to make beer. By 4,000 BC, the Egyptians has started making leavened bread with yeast. In China, the production of yogurt & vinegar was among the first uses of biotechnology, and molds were used for skin infections as topical treatments. Later on in 1928 Fleming extracted antibiotic penicillin from mold. Fermentation techniques were used on large scale in the 1940’s for making industrial quantities of this new drug. The first genetically engineered organisms   were created in 1973 by academic United States scientists Herbert Boyer and Stanley Cohen created the pioneering genetically engineered organisms - This captured the interest of investors. Pakistan has the potential to benefit from biotechnology to the maximum and divulging headfast into the field may provide immense opportunities to scientists in the development of agriculture and health sector.
Today, it is increasingly becoming difficult to get access to advance technologies in developed countries. Therefore, it is imperative that indigenous R&D programs are initiated by indulging into the development of processes and production of biotech products locally at a much lower cost citing local availability of cheap feed stock for fermentation industry.

data.projectName: ASHRAY: IoT-inspired Intelligent Water Comfort and Gas Savings on International Scales
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan’s gas shortage and dwindling domestic production needs no introduction. While addressing a seminar on Sept. 09, 2020, the prime minister warned that the country is on the verge of a major gas crisis, which is going to become much worse next year. One of the major causes of this demand-supply gap in Pakistan is consumption efficiencies in the residential sector. About half of the gas supplied to residential consumers is used for water heating, primarily achieved through storage tank-based water heaters (aka geysers), which only offer an efficiency of about 25%. While a typical household in Pakistan uses warm water for approx. 4 hours a day for bathing, kitchen chores, laundry and other needs, these geysers, which are equipped with manual thermostats, operate 24/7 and that too at their highest operating point, needlessly wasting gas for heating water that remains unused for larger periods (e.g., 10 PM to 6 AM).

To address this problem, Zaheen Machines (Pvt Ltd) invented Jal Bujh, a programmable geyser thermostat that transforms existing geysers into gas saving appliances. Jal Bujh allows users to program temperature settings of the geysers through a smartphone app, adapting usage to match the needs of household and avoiding waste of gas. Depending on the weather conditions in a region, Jal Bujh can save up to 25% (down south) to 75% (up north) natural gas used for water heating. Jal Bujh has an install base of over 6000, and the product is endorsed and actively marketed by SNGPL  through a printed advert on monthly gas bills.

In this proposal, we propose ASHRAY, the next iteration of Jal Bujh based on learnings from large install base and market. ASHRAY merges the existing features of Jal Bujh with an IoT enabled, AI based smart controller that predicts water usage and produces hot water at around the same effectiveness as instant geysers, but with the quality delivered by storage based geysers.  ASHRAY will have three more significant features:

i.	Self-programming through AI and machine learning, observing hot water usage by the household.
ii.	Autoignition for firing the burner without the need for a constantly on pilot lamp which extinguishes in case of gas load shedding – making Jal Bujh ineffective. 
iii.	Power module for local energy harvesting, battery management and power provisioning.
iv.	A backwards compatible industrial design, enabling integration with existing geyser offerings of OEMs without any modifications to their assembly lines. 
 
Based on pessimistic estimates of an MIT trained energy expert, Jal Bujh increases the geyser efficiency by 25%, offering a 3.5% reduction in natural gas bill for the country amounting to 100s of millions of dollars a month in foreign exchange savings. ASHRAY, with its intelligent design, can double this efficiency gain to 7% or more of the total natural gas consumed by Pakistan in winter months.

ASHRAY concept has been co-developed by a team of LUMS researchers and Zaheen Machines. The LUMS members of the team will provide hardware and software expertise to design, develop, test and assemble various subsystems of ASHRAY. The project contentedly leverages the expertise of Zaheen Machines, as sectoral partners, in launching a successful product. The sectoral partners will provide market research, system design, product management and backwards-compatible industrial design capability.

data.projectName: Development of indigenous mycotoxin inactivating enzymes (laccases) based product to combat the threat of mycotoxicosis in poultry: A One Health Approach
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest:
Mycotoxins are fungal secondary metabolites, contaminate food or feedstuff and poses a serious health threat to both humans and livestock population. Fungi including Aspergillus, Penicillium and Fusarium grow on variety of livestock and human feedstuffs due to inadequate conditions of harvesting, storage, handling and processing. The most commonly observed mycotoxins that cause a concern to human health and livestock include aflatoxins (AFB1, AFB2, AFG1, AFG2), ochratoxin A (OTA), fumonisins (FB1, FB2), zearalenone (ZEA) etc. These causes serious human and livestock health problems including carcinogenesis, hepatotoxicity and nephrotoxicity etc. 
At present, different strategies have been adopted to detoxify feedstuff contaminated with mycotoxins include physical (irradiation, adsorption and toxin-binders) and chemical methods (acid and base treatment etc.). These methods have many shortcoming e.g. reduction in nutritional value and palatability of the foodstuffs. The irreversible detoxification of mycotoxins through catabolizing enzymes and their coding genes is a safe strategy to decontaminate food and feedstuff and can be applied to address the issues of global trade, sustainability and maintaining the nutritional value and palatability of feedstuff. In Pakistan the environment is favorable for aflatoxicosis and ochratoxicosis in commercial poultry. The consumption of mycotoxins contaminated feed adversely affects the performance of livestock/poultry including decrease in productivity, and weight gain. The consumption of meet by human from these species with mycotoxin residues can cause carcinogenicity, hepatotoxicity and nephrotoxicity in humans. Currently we have isolated, characterized and optimized the laccase production from P. stutzeri  WR5 strain. Some initial studies are needed to develop mycotoxin inactivating enzyme (laccase) product. This product will help to reduce the severe health hazards caused by mycotoxicosis to human and animals. This would be an innovative biological strategy to inactivate or detoxify mycotoxins to save humans, animals and environment using one health approach.  The developed product will have a commercial application in grain industry, poultry feed industry and commercial poultry production. The technology transfer between institute and industry will help to enhance capacity of local industry. The proposed research will also help to provide human a safe and healthy environment through decontamination of feed ingredients and mycotoxin residue free meat. In large the proposed project will help in creation of new job opportunities through development of new product locally and provision of healthier meat products (mycotoxin residue free) from poultry for our society.
 The development of product P. stutzeri WR5 laccase having properties to diminish the toxic effects of single or multiple mycotoxins (aflatoxin and ochratoxin A). Therefore, the objectives of proposed proposal will be (i) Analysis of redox potential of P. stutzeri WR5 laccase for improved detoxification potential/efficiency. (ii) Mutagenesis of P. stutzeri WR5 strain for hyperproduction of mycotoxin inactivating enzymes (laccases). (iii) In vitro detoxification or inactivation of mycotoxins (aflatoxins and ocharatoxin A) in feedstuff by employing indigenous laccases (iv) Pilot scale production of indigenous laccases in 300 L fermenter. (iv) In vivo application of P. stutzeri  WR5 laccase enzyme in poultry feed to ameliorate the toxic effects of aflatoxins/ ocharatoxins A and residual detection in meat at BZU Poultry Farms (Academic collaboration) and commercial Poultry Farms. 
Industrial partner will help in field trial at commercial poultry farms, sale and marketing of prepared product. The successful completion of this project will also help in product development and technology transfer for the biological detoxification of mycotoxins of food and feed industry.

data.projectName: Commercialization of Rapeseed Variety Hasnain-2013 on Sustainable basis using Cyber Physical Systems (CPSs) Monitoring
data.projectDigest:
Seed is the carrier of modern technology; a group of Plant Breeders have developed a rapeseed variety through the cross of Brassica (Brassica napus x Brassica juncea).  The variety out performed in National Uniform Mustard Yield Trial (NURYT). It has the distinction of wavy leaf margin, light green color, early maturity, pod shape is curved silliqua, black seed color, high yielding and resistant to prevailing diseases and insect pest attack. The Hasnain-2013 a rapeseed crop variety in the 33rd meeting of Provincial Seed Council (PSC) at Agriculture Research Institute Tarnab Peshawar was approved after fulfilling all the formal requirements. Being the newest variety and having the potential to be adopted by the farmers for highest yield the project is designed with the objectives of production/procurement of 30 M. ton Hasnain-2013 seed during two years period. The seed will be procured from selected growers/farms during two year of the project at attractive prices to be fixed at the start of each season by a committee. After processing the seed will be sold to the farming community through seed marketing companies. Federal Seed Certification and Registration Department (FSC&RD) will be involved in the whole process of variety maintenance and seed multiplication. Project will also establish a close liaison among all stake holders (farmers, seed companies and oil extraction industry) on sustainable basis.
During 2019-20 availability of quality certified seed of oilseed crops remained limiting factor and all seed sown were imported, which is not only burden on our hard earned foreign exchange reserves but also increasing dependency on corporate sector while still having good potential rapeseed Variety Hasnain-2013. Maintenance and commercialization of our own available crop genetic resources is the need of the hour in the prevailing Intellectual property rights (IPRs) regime where Traditional knowledge (TK) and Sui generis system of indigenous genetic resources protection is inevitable. In this backdrop here in University of Haripur Khyber Pakhtunkhwa having the status of being in the food basket of the region intends to work for the commercialization of its own potential Variety Hasnain-2013. 
This project will be unique of its sort owing to the use of information technology in the monitoring of product marketing; special monitoring sensors will be used having complete record of class/category, lot. No., production year, variety name and technical name of the variety seed on its bag. Commercialization of this new variety using Cyber Physical Systems (CPSs) monitoring will help market quality certified seed and will discourage low quality uncertified seed because the project will monitor real time location of seed at any stage. In this way our farmers will have quality seed and there will be low risk of failure or low yield. It will be a step forward in the national objectives of self-sufficiency in edible which at present is huge burden on our hard earned foreign exchange reserves.

data.projectName: Establishment of new rapid diagnostic platform for the detection of virally-induced immunosuppression
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
World health organization estimates a billion cases of illness and about a million deaths/year from different diseases that transfer from animals to humans.
Many new highly dangerous bugs lead to large numbers of deaths and huge economic losses, like the current world-wide lockdown after corona spread.
In this project, we will study in depth why and how these animal bugs (viruses) jump to humans and shut down their body defense systems that is responsible to fight these bugs. 
We aim to develop rapid laboratory methods to quickly detect this defense shut down in body when bugs attack. 
We plan to discover new drugs to boost body defense system against these bugs. We will also manufacture new local affordable drugs to kill those bugs efficiently as imported drugs are very expensive.
Lastly, we also plan to construct a highly advanced mobile laboratory that can be quickly driven to localities where dangerous bugs erupt and control them effectively using our products. 
Our team of specialist will produce low-cost products and commercialize them using social-technical-economic plan to ensure their success in general public. The benefit at national level includes: a reduced economic impact by decreased disease burden, a better human health will improve their life standards and less impact on the budget spent on treatment cost.

data.projectName: NANOBIOFERTLIZER (Nano-Encapsulation of Plant Growth-Promoting Rhizobacteria (PGPR) with Silicon dioxide Nano-Particles for Wheat Growth)
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Modern agriculture is embracing the innovative approach of nano-biotechnology for the development of nano-biofertilizer to combat major issues of crop production, sustainability, and eco-safety. Nano-encapsulation protects biofertilizer components containing plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) and thus can resolve the limitations of biofertilizer particularly inconsistency ineffectiveness, enhances shelf-life, and allows the controlled release of the PGPR. Our previous studies have well-established results regarding wheat improvements in growth by nano-encapulated PGPR, particularly with silicon.  We have also confirmed the efficacy of this plausible combination of silicon nanoparticles and isolated PGPR in terms of its better nutrient absorption from the rhizosphere. These pilot-scale studies, including some Ph.D. researchs, have shown the practicability of this approach. SiO2 NanoParticles (SiO2NP) were prepared from silicon dioxide and characterized by scanning electron microscopy and Energy dispersive X-rays pattern. Potent strains (screened based on plant growth-promoting traits) were nano-encapsulated with SiO2NP. SiO2NP positively influenced wheat plant growth. Therefore, the present proposal has been designed to upscale the production of SiO2NP with the help of Aurega, it's quality testing and fields trials (at research farms of PMAS-AAUR and UAF; farmers field of Aurega group) before commercialization.The final product may be able to provide a return over investment upto 25-30%.

data.projectName: IoT Connected Beehive Monitoring System- Smart Ecosystem
data.piUniversity: Pir Mehr Ali Shah Arid Agriculture, University Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
The mission is to create a complete digitalized ecosystem for beekeeping and honey farming. The
proposed project includes development of a proprietary technology, which helps beekeepers better
understand the conditions, issues and view statistics by remotely accessing their farms. They will not
only be able to increase the productivity but also able to monitor the quality of their yields. The
software in local language will enable them to view the information and the status in real-time. This will
further enable them to standardize their product (honey) for exports.
Overall project includes below technologies;
• IoT connected Smart monitoring/production Ecosystem for Bee Colonies
• IoT connected Mobile/Web application for Workers and Corporate Farm Owners
Proposed IoT Solutions with Data Analytics Algorithms will help to conserve bee colonies, increase
productivity, better manage honey trading and business operations and government decision makers.
Major benefits of the technology includes;
• Increased Honey Yield
• True Source Identification through IoTs
• Reduced Operating Costs
• Improved Quality Monitoring and Productivity
• Data Collection and Analytics

data.projectName: FutureSity-Employment Readiness Platform
data.projectDigest:
Graduate unemployment rate in Pakistan is at 16.5%, with more than half a million unemployed graduates. 78% of Pakistani Employers were Dissatisfied with University Graduates found in Graduate Employability: Employers’ Perception Survey Report 2018. With annual University enrollment of 1.6M, number of unemployed graduates will be over a million by 2025. Such a high number of educated & unemployed youth will become a national security challenge. Higher education systems need to be reimagined for the “Future of Work”. data.projectName: "Development of nanostructured coatings using thermal  deposition technology"
data.projectDigest: Nanostructured materials can offer unique and superior mechanical properties such as high hardness, strength, corrosion and wear resistance compared to the normal microstructured materials commonly used in engineering. Therefore, this capability has made nanostructured materials of considerable interest world-wide. However, the challenge remains of how to successfully manufacture a nanostructured material to a reasonable size without losing the nanostructured during manufacture. One avenue which has considerable potential for success is the use of thermal spraying techniques to deposit nanostructured coatings onto component surfaces. This research concerns the development of thick nanostructured cermet coatings  using novel “engineered” nanostructured powders which have been designed with the ability to maintain its nanostructure during the thermal deposition process. This research will produce ceramic/metal coatings based on WC-Co-Cr-Ni-Al2O3 system and these coatings will offer a three-fold increase in surface hardness, corrosion and wear resistance. The development of the next generation of advanced nanostructured surface coatings with superior mechanical properties offers enhanced production performance, efficiency and competitiveness to all industries concerned with erosive-corrosive degeneration of component surfaces such as in power plants, petrochemical plants, agricultural tools (and sugar processing machinery in mills).

data.projectName: Development of an MMT/Bentonite based sand modifier fertilizer ‘Bentilizer’ to induce desert fertility, support plantation and revers desertification, assuring Environmental Sustainability and Food Security besides softening related SDGs
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: The project visualizes to develop a Fertilizer composition special for sandy environment, using a material Bentonite capable of holding moisture and adsorbing other nutrients for a longer time with slow release avoiding the loss of fertilizer by leeching making it possible to grow plants or in Sandy zones . Fundamental research has been done in various parts of the world but its application and viability in sandy zones is to be established along with optimization of treatment conditions like concentration of Bentonite, Concentration of various fertilizer nutrients(NPKS) and frequency of irrigation. The experimental design to be followed is RCBD (Randomized Complete Block Design). Initial experiment will establish viability in normal temperate zone while next stage will be a field test in more sever conditions. Successful testing will help in reclaiming or even using sandy (useless) soils for increasing forestation and crop production thereby improving employment, greenery/ forestation, environment, and food security besides meeting a no. of Sustainable Development Goals as set by UN.

data.projectName: Academia-Industrial Linkages for Commercialization of RDF Palletizer Machine and Eco-Friendly Biomass Stoves for Meeting Rural Energy Demands
data.projectDigest:
Persisting energy crises as a result of depleting fossil fuels are drastically affecting the sustainability of the communities. This is a particular problem for rural areas where it becomes very difficult to supply the sufficient energy to meet the daily life energy demand, in particular, heating energy used for cooking purpose. The major reason is very long distances from main energy supply line as well as the line losses. There is a need to introduce the advanced technologies to meet the rural energy demands with the indigenous resources. On the other hand, solid waste, generated in different domestic, agricultural, commercial and industrial activities, is also a major problem these days. Conventional dumping of this huge amount of solid waste in the open land is not a suitable option as it causes different social and environmental problems. Controlled combustion of solid waste has been found as an attractive way to manage and treat the solid wastes as it reduces the initial volume significantly. Energy generation is another benefit which can be used in place of fossil fuels like coal etc. in the boilers and other firing stations. However, utilization of solid waste as an alternative to the fossil fuels need certain processing to make it feasible and efficient. Refused Derived Fuel (RDF) pallets formation is one of the waste-to-energy techniques in which the raw solid waste is converted into an efficient fuel energy generation. In the proposed study, a new technology will be introduced consisting of a pilot scale RDF pelletizer machine and eco-friendly stoves for cooking purposes at the rural areas. Under this concept, the palletizer is proposed to be installed at central community scale for the production of small RDF pallets. The produced pallets will be consumed in the eco-friendly biomass stoves. In this way the proposed technology will be helpful to meet the rural energy needs as well as to uplift the livelihood of rural communities by installing small business units at the local and community scales. This will also attract the entrepreneurs for startup businesses.
The project will be executed in a very close collaboration with technical experts and researchers from different departments/institutes. Dr. Abdul Ghafoor (Co-PI-I), being expert in machinery designs and manufacturing, will contribute in the designing of the RDF pelletizer machine and biomass stove. Dr. Abdul Nasir (Co-PI-II), Associate Professor, Department of Structures and Environmental Engineering will help to execute the project based on his very vast experience with research projects. Dr. Muhammad Nadeem (Technical Expert) from the Department of Farm Machinery and Power, University of Agriculture, Faisalabad will provide the technical assistance for installation of the RDF processing unit at the community scale and further demonstration of the proposed technology.
The project will be executed with a very strong collaboration with Dr. Mian Ilyas Ahmad Associate Professor, Research Centre for Modeling & Simulation (RCMS), National University of Sciences and Technology (NUST), Islamabad. The methodology of the project has been discussed in detail with him and as a collaborator, he will assist in the execution phase of the project and in mentoring of the research students as well as commercialization of proposed technology.
The project will be executed with a very close collaboration with Mr. Ghazanfar Sharif, CEO Sharif Engineering Works, Faisalabad. The company will provide technical as well as commercialization assistance for the proposed technology.      
The research project will also be executed with the international collaboration of Prof. Dr. Andreas Bück from FAU Erlangen Germany who will provide the necessary guidance during the project.

data.projectName: Improving physiochemical and reconstitution properties of milk and juice based nano-encapsulates developed by Spray Drying Technology and its commercialization
data.projectDigest: Nano encapsulation is widely used technique used now a days in nanotechnology. Among different techniques employed to produce encapsulates, spray drying is a convective drying technique used to transform a liquid foods (such as milk, juices etc.) in the form of a formulated solution emulsion suspension or slurry into a dry free flowing powder. Encapsulation assists sensitive and fragile materials to survive under processing and packaging conditions and stabilize the shelf life of the active ingredient. Encapsulation is used to overcome all challenge by providing viable texture blending, appealing aroma releases. Disease preventing and health promoting properties of different nutrients and bio-agents have been demonstrated. Another benefit of encapsulations is less evaporation and degradation of volatile actives, such as aroma, which usually contains mixture of volatile and odorous organic molecules. Besides, flavors are about the preservation of aromatic additives. Teaching and Research activities improve in the university and thereby research and development linkages established at National and international levels. This project will fulfil the gap between the researcher and the industry to economize the indigenous equipment’s at very low cast. The Basic Importance of this project is to add value addition in the raw material consequently help the food security and safety of the country. Moreover PhD and MPhil students will be facilitated to conduct their research experiments by varying the parameters on the newly develop technology.

data.projectName: OFTEN: Output Forecasting Neural Network based Virtual Quality Assessment Tool
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Manufacturing Industries Pakistan struggle to uplift export profile by raising their quality assurance mechanisms due to several barriers including low access to real-time product quality assessment checks. Raw material, process settings and ambient conditions play important role in determining final product quality. Typically, the quality tests are conducted with a time lag and in mixed methods mode, resulting in considerable loss of product and raw material in case of test failure. With the help of Novatex, one of the leading PET manufacturers in Pakistan, we have developed and prototyped product quality predictive tool which provides highly accurate product quality predictions several hours ahead of time. The Predictive tool in the form a software product is highly customizable and applicable to a variety of manufacturing industries in Pakistan and abroad. Through this support fund, we will be scaling the product to be available commercially with the help of Novatex and M. Anwar Brothers.

data.projectName: Micropropagation of potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) for disease free seed production
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: The tissue culture lab at Agricultural Biotechnology Division has developed novel protocol for invitro techniques, explant preparation and media formulations  with significant improvement in efficiency and economic propagation of crops i.e., potato, cotton, sugarcane. For healthy and quality seed production at Agricultural Biotechnology Division, innovative tissue culture conditions were optimized for local potato varieties. Potato varieties have degenerated with passage of time due to increase in load of microorganisms; bacteria, viruses, fungi and nematodes under field conditions. Potato germplasm of 4-5 varieties with inherent high yield potential will be collected and subjected to invitro biotechnological interventions for economic production of healthy invitro potato plants and seed tuber on optimized media. After the production of prebasic seed at host lab, minitubers will be produced at fields of industrial partners i) AGB seed corporation ii) Zulfi Seed Corporation and iii) Yousuf Ali & Sons Seed Company under the guidelines provided by source lab. Biotechnological and technical support will continue from source lab during testing and multiplication of healthy potato seed tubers at collaborator’s facility. The certified potato seeds will be multiplied and available to potato growers at different places throughout the potato growing regions.

data.projectName: ESTechPAK – Real Estate Technological Platform for Affordable Housing in Pakistan Using Big Data
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
The proposed innovative digital platform will help to improve and secure real estate national investments and low-to-medium risk decision making for the common citizens of Pakistan. It will further meet the growing demand for affordable, resilient, accessible and sustainable housing - facilitating small/medium sized investors to contribute in generating economic activity and jobs. The proposed system will specially encourage women in Pakistan to invest in property portfolio with confidence and trust (who otherwise keep their savings in the form of gold-ornaments due to lack of opportunities for a secure asset-backed investment). 

The outcomes will also serve the needs of Real Estate Regulatory Authority (RERA), a recent initiative by the government, which will take care of property disputes that eventually freezes people investments resulting as all-around losses. Overall, the proposed research will fit into the larger framework for Naya Pakistan Housing & Naya Pakistan Housing Accelerator Programs, thus addressing Sustainable Development Goals 8 and 11, while aiming to provide employment opportunities and overall boosting the real estate sector in the country.

data.projectName: Smart Glasses for Visually Impaired Using Deep Learning
data.piUniversity: Balochistan University of Information Technology, Engineering and Management Sciences,Quetta
data.projectDigest: The world is progressing in every aspect now-a-days; it would not be possible without the help of technology. By technology we achieved things that were once a part of our imagination. With the help of technology we aim to build smart glasses for the people who are visually impaired or partially blind so they can see and interact with the world without feeling left out. Basically the smart glasses will consist of a camera, number of sensors attached to it and a small GPU for processing the data. On the software side, we use Machine learning and Artificial Intelligence to detect objects with accuracy and with low latency which can help the user to make decisions while walking. There is so much research on the proposed project from different universities all over the world. In China, researchers conducted a study to make a better and efficient version of smart glasses by adding a navigation system to it. Demographically, around 2.5 to 3 million people are blind in Pakistan and they are using traditional sticks for assistance which lead them to face many problems and accidents because of a lack of knowhow about their surroundings. In order to address this problem, we came up the solution of commercially manufacture glasses for the visually impaired or partially blind which would attract a plethora of buyers all across Pakistan. By this venture, not only we will be carrying out an entrepreneurial endeavor but also contribute to society and help people with blindness.

data.projectName: Indigenous Fabrication of In-Pond Raceway System (IPRS) Technology Equipment and Floating Raceways, Its Economical Availability for Promotion of Sustainable Aquaculture
data.piUniversity: Lahore College for Women University, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Proposed project is upscaling of the project under Technology Development Fund Program of HEC (TDF03-132). In this project, innovative In-Pond Raceway system (IPRS) Technology was introduced in Pakistan in 2019. Benefits of this technology include conservation of land and water, least contamination of discharged water, diversification of species cultured in different raceways. Successful pilot scale trial of IPRS technology was completed in early 2020 and production of 10,711 kg/hectare at average FCR of 1.24, was achieved. Several farmers are interested in adopting this technology, but major restraint is large capital cost of IPRS equipment and construction of cemented raceways. Therefore, proposed project has been designed to indigenously fabricate IPRS equipment and replace cemented raceways by floating PVC/fiberglass raceways. After implementation of this project, Pakistan will be second manufacturer of IPRS equipment and first in floating PVC/fiberglass IPRS raceways. There is vast market for this prototype in Pakistan. Presently, estimated area of registered fish farms is 107,008 ha in Pakistan while average production is 1,487 kg/ha from total farmed land. If production of 16,000 kg/ha is targeted from IPRS farming then above mentioned total production can be achieved by using only 9,943 ha, conserving 97,065 ha of land and natural water.

data.projectName: Development of Commercial Model and Software interface for Transformer Health Monitoring System
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
The project is related to development of a monitoring system as replacement of “Dissolved Gas Analysis” for distribution transformers. It records and transmits operating parameters, and can detect & classify possible faults using feature extracted in frequency and time frequency domain. Alarms/warnings are generated regarding expected failures and maintenance. Lab prototype has been developed and tested. Algorithm accuracy is upto 85%. 
The lab prototype has been tested on a single transformer and data has been collected on a simple internet page developed on free web interface. The industrial product has to be installed on each transformer (node), hence it is required to develop machine to machine communication, data interface software, development of required query system. Telenor Pakistan has developed IoT platform which can help in quick development of such system moreover, they will also provide data link between all nodes and information center. 
It hence the downtime reduces significantly. There are around 38,000 distribution transformers only in KE network and all over the country their number is more than a Million. There is a great need to automate transformer maintenance. Moreover, it will also be step towards realization of smart grid which require self aware hardware in the system which can be monitored remotely. All the power distribution companies in country are the potential customer of the developed technique and product. 
Besides, software and data interface, it was considered prudent to involve transformer manufactures and supplier. Pakistan Elektron Limited (PEL) has largest share in Transformer market of Pakistan. There partnership will be instrumental providing required knowledge base out of their years long experience in the field. PEL will be providing information, data support and information regarding transformer faults and working. 
With the support of HEC in conjunction of industrial partners, it is very likely that the product will be commercialized successfully and following are main contributions from each partner:
a.	NUST (PI, Co PI and team)	- Working Prototype, algorithm, testing and industrialization

b.	HEC				- Funding for Research team and software development

c.	PEL Pakistan			- Data, field knowledge, industrialization partner

d.	Telenor Pakistan 		- Data link and IoT partner and expertise provider
