data.projectName: Synthesis, Characterization and Evaluation of Advanced Stationary Phases in Liquid Chromatography.
data.piUniversity: University of Malakand, Chakdara, Dir, Malakand
data.projectDigest: Although many materials are used as stationary phase media but they have low permeability (high back pressure), lower sample loading capacity, inferior separation efficiency and long analysis time. Partially porous silica monolith particles based stationary phases are considered to be the promising stationary phases in liquid chromatography due to high permeability, increased sample loading capacity, improved separation efficiency and short analysis time (fast HPLC analysis). The current project will focus on the syntheses of stationary phases based upon partially porous sub1-2 µm silica particles with large pore size of more than 350 Å. Variety of the new LC stationary phases including, polystyrene modified, C18 modified, urea-C4 modified, urea-C8 modified, chiral stationary phases, molecularly imprinted polymer based stationary phases, and mixed mode chromatographic stationary phases will be synthesized and packed in the column. Polystyrene modification of the silica monolith particles will be carried out to prepare the multimode chromatographic stationary phases by the incorporation of polar ligands. The newly prepared stationary phases will be characterized and then packed in home assembled stainless steel column via slurry packer incorporated with tapered connections. The monolithic architecture will be induced inside the column during packing which arise due to different shape of the particles such as spherical, oval, bent etc. and will ultimately lead to the production of different flow through channels. Packed columns will be evaluated using the homemade HPLC system for the chromatographic performance of the column and real time analysis of different samples. The newly developed columns will be checked in detail for proteomic, Glycomic, glycoprotein analysis and analysis of small molecules. As a future perspective, columns will be coupled to mass spectrometry for the detailed exploration of glycosylation sites ultimately contributing to the Glycomic and proteomic libraries. Beside materials synthesis a homemade HPLC system will be prepared in current project for sample analysis.
data.projectSummary: Although many materials are used as stationary phase media but they have low permeability (high back pressure), lower sample loading capacity, inferior separation efficiency and long analysis time. Partially porous silica monolith particles based stationary phases are considered to be the promising stationary phases in liquid chromatography due to high permeability, increased sample loading capacity, improved separation efficiency and short analysis time (fast HPLC analysis). The current project will focus on the syntheses of stationary phases based upon partially porous sub1-2 µm silica particles with large pore size of more than 350 Å. Variety of the new LC stationary phases including, polystyrene modified, C18 modified, urea-C4 modified, urea-C8 modified, chiral stationary phases, molecularly imprinted polymer based stationary phases, and mixed mode chromatographic stationary phases will be synthesized and packed in the column. Polystyrene modification of the silica monolith particles will be carried out to prepare the multimode chromatographic stationary phases by the incorporation of polar ligands. The newly prepared stationary phases will be characterized and then packed in home assembled stainless steel column via slurry packer incorporated with tapered connections. The monolithic architecture will be induced inside the column during packing which arise due to different shape of the particles such as spherical, oval, bent etc. and will ultimately lead to the production of different flow through channels. Packed columns will be evaluated using the homemade HPLC system for the chromatographic performance of the column and real time analysis of different samples. The newly developed columns will be checked in detail for proteomic, Glycomic, glycoprotein analysis and analysis of small molecules. As a future perspective, columns will be coupled to mass spectrometry for the detailed exploration of glycosylation sites ultimately contributing to the Glycomic and proteomic libraries. Beside materials synthesis a homemade HPLC system will be prepared in current project for sample analysis.

data.projectName: Synthesis of Graphene-embedded Polymer Membrane Integrated with UVC Light Technology for Microbial and Metallic Contamination Removal from Water
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
The proposed project is to develop an efficient water filtration solution for home as well as industrial use that can eliminate the maximum number of contaminants (microbial, chemical and physical) from general and industrial waste effluent, using green synthesis of a graphene-embedded polymer membrane integrated with UVC light technology. For this Project, the UVC device has already been developed and tested by the collaborator/primary industry partner. This work will also be done in collaboration with University of Engineering Technology (UET), Lahore, who will facilitate in developing a low-cost, eco-friendly production method for ‘wonder’ material, Graphene. The proposed project work consists of identifying the best polymer substrate to serve as the membrane in which the graphene material will be embedded. 
Combining the already developed UVC device with graphene-embedded nano-filters poses an ideal solution to eliminate all (99.9%) the contaminants that can make polluted water reusable. The University will develop a membrane filter, optimize it at different temperatures, with respect to pH change, and conduct water permeability, filtration efficacy and bio-compatibility tests (monitoring toxic effect on human cells). Application analysis will be done against microbial and chemical contaminants at different concentrations of water samples collected from various sources.

data.projectName: Application of Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) Technology in Enhancing Food Security and Sustainability: A Case of Agriculture
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Apiculture/Beekeeping is one of the essential livestock subsectors, which contributes significant importance to the livelihoods of the people in Pakistan, but despite the favorable natural environment and the potential for establishing sustainable livelihoods in rural areas, it often lacks the necessary ?nancial and technological support required to exploit fully its great potential in enhancing food security in Pakistan. 
Beekeeping is currently experiencing serious difficulties associated with a significant reduction in the production of natural bee products. Compared with other agricultural enterprises, beekeeping is a low-cost venture with the potential to have tremendous impact in improving household livelihoods, food security and the national economy. However, inef?cient technologies, insuf?cient knowledge, environmental degradation and low production are some of the key challenges faced by the sub-sector. If food security situation and the vision 2020 is to be fully realized, it will be necessary to plan for the possibility to increase production of Honey in apiculture, among other things.
This project “Q-Bee Management Solution” aims to disrupt the bee-keeping market in Agriculture by providing effective, timely and user-friendly monitoring system based on Industrial Internet of Things. The IoT user-friendly capabilities have remarkably altered the potential usages of the Internet. Once the users adopt the technology then it could develop and optimize the decision-making processes, as well as the controlling measures, which lead to more productivity and sustainability.

data.projectName: combination of dry powder formulation of bedaquiline, moxifloxacin and kenamycin  for the treatment of multi and extensively drug resistant tuberculosis
data.projectDigest: Tuberculosis (TB) is highly infectious disease caused by mycobacterium tuberculosis. Pakistan, with an estimated 510 000 new TB cases emerging each year and approximately 15000 developing drug resistant TB cases every year, is ranked fifth among B high-burden countries worldwide and it accounts for 61% of the TB burden in the WHO Eastern Mediterranean Region. It is necessary to add one of the previously developed drug bedaquiline in the standard second line therapy for the drug resistant patients. Results related to bedaquiline from previous literature research showed some adverse side effects like QT prolongation and increase in liver enzyme. Our aim is to develop the inhalable dry powder formulation of bedaquiline to reduce the adverse effects and use it with second line regimen for the multi and extensively resistant tuberculosis patients. At academic level, design-to-design properties and functions such as elimination of adverse reactions, improvement of efficacy, assurance of stability during distribution & adding usefulness based on various data such as chemical and physical properties, efficacy, safety and stability of bedaquiline will be obtained from preclinical studies. Technology transfer dossier (TTD) document will be shared with industry and after validation studies the product will be commercialized.

data.projectName: ICU Ventilator
data.projectDigest:
Ventilators are integral part of modern ICU. This equipment is very expensive and sophisticated. Its import not only effect the hospital budget but also county’s import bill. Patient has been heavily charged for ICU care due costly equipment. Small cities and far flung area hospitals don’t have ventilators and thus critical patients have to bring to big cities.  Its local manufacturing will not only reduce the hospitals budget but also put relief on patient’s bill thus have great impact on health care of the society.
The current surge in demand has led to a worldwide shortage. Since the start of the pandemic (covid-19), the Government has been working hard to secure supply and start domestic manufacture of ventilators as well as critical personal protective equipment. Pakistan educational institutions and industrial sector have great potential for designing and locally manufacturing of medical equipment. This successful projects will increase the business opportunities and jobs for engineers. The availability of these machines will ensure that our hospitals are well equipped to withstand future surges in intensive care cases.

data.projectName: Waqf as a Virtuous Institution and Means to Socio-economic Welfare in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
An Islamic economy comprises three sectors namely market economy and beyond market economy that comprises the virtuous and the mutual cooperation sector. Having seen the principles of Islamic law of contracts covering mainly the ‘exchange part’, it transpires that the main theme of Islamic socio-economic system revolves around socio economic justice and care for the poor and the indigent. 
Waqf is a civil societal institution and crucial part of the ‘beyond market sector’ of Islamic economy.  It is one of the traditional Islamic institutions based on philanthropy, the others being zakah and Sadaqah in general. In Islamic history, waqf-based institutions had been the main providers of education, health care and water resources. Pakistan is among the countries where huge amounts of charity are given to the needy and the social sectors, but that charity has to be formalized in proper manner. The primary objective of this research project is to suggest a waqf based practical and sustainable model involving the rich and philanthropists, the State institutions and banking and non-banking financial institutions in Pakistan. The proposed framework would provide education, health and other civic amenities to the public in general and the poor and the indigent in general.

data.projectName: Optimizing Drag and Lift Forces around Obstacles submerged in thermal non-linear flow fields: Implementation  of an Efficient FEM based Solver
data.projectDigest:
This project is concerned with the development and software realization of numerical simulation techniques which allow the computation of hydrodynamic forces on obstacles of various shapes submerged in nonlinear and non-isothermal flow fields. The objective is to optimize these hydrodynamic forces to obtain practical advantages in the design of shapes and structures that interact with the fluid. Since the scientific challenges regarding the modeling and detailed analysis of the fluidic transport processes in presence of thermal considerations are mainly related with different scales in space and time, Therefore Finite Element Method with higher order elements will be set as base for the simulations.

In CFD, the drag and lift forces are major quantities of interest for fluid solid interaction problems. These forces can be computed through the integrals over the boundary of the obstacles.
The dimensionless analogue of these quantities is given by drag and lift coefficients to evaluate the quantity of resistance and lift of object in fluid field, such as air and water.  Beside the other quantities important in a fluid flow system, our focus would also be on the computation of drag and lift coefficients.

The design of corresponding numerical prediction tools for such highly complex flows, and hence for the analysis of the interplay of drag and lift forces with temperature as well as with non-linear viscosity in fluid structure interaction flows, calls for very accurate and efficient simulation strategies. Therefore, the validation of the developed codes using benchmark computation will be done by consulting with the academic collaborators utilizing their expertise.

data.projectName: Fabrication of enzyme-free 3D nanocomposite electrode with new architectures for glucose sensing
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: Diabetes is a global epidemic that threatens millions of people’s health. The control of blood glucose (sugar) is the hottest issue. Poor control of diabetic can damage the body and proper control of blood glucose can be lifesaving. The measuring method of blood glucose is a worldwide issue. In Pakistan, diabetes patients are increasing day by day. The available electrodes in the market are based on the enzyme (Glucose oxidase) which is tedious, expensive and not reusable. Under this project, we will synthesize three-dimensional nanocomposite electrodes by utilizing the carbon nanomaterials, noble metals/metal oxides nanoparticles, etc. on a 3D template result of high surface area, high porosity with minimization of agglomeration. Such a novel enzyme-free glucose sensor will show high sensitivity, low detection limits, high stability, easy to use, low cost, and reusable. Our proposed electrode will be able to beat commercially available enzyme-based electrodes. We hope our research project will be contributing to a new role to develop a healthy society. This research will facilitate those poor peoples are living below the bottom level and surfing such painful epidemic diseases. Our 3D composite structure electrode, owing aforementioned properties that will be markup a new target for the upcoming researchers.

data.projectName: Nanostructured Catalysts for Electrochemical  and Photoelectrochemical Water Splitting: The Evolution of Renewable Hydrogen
data.projectDigest: This project is based on designing and fabrication of nanostructured catalysts for electrochemical and photoelectrochemical water splitting. The main theme of the project is the production of hydrogen using low cost and efficient electrolyzers such as water. Due to the limited supply of natural resources and the constantly intensifying use of fossil fuels, scientists are motivated for the serious hunt of renewable and eco-friendly sources of energy. In several applications, hydrogen fuel cells have developed into attractive contenders in transportation and electrical power generation due to their encouraging performance. Hydrogen fuel cell involves the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and the oxygen reduction reaction (OER) that require a catalyst to drop their electrochemical overpotentials up to zero and to attain high current output using sunlight or electricity. This is a long-term technology pathway, with the potential for no greenhouse gas emissions. Thus, developing innovative catalysts at the nano level and refining the performance of a fuel cell is extremely compulsory and remains a great challenge.

data.projectName: “Exploring Reasons of Industrial Failure in Azad Jammu & Kashmir”
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest: Industrial employment is considered as key to the development; however despite of many efforts, the industrialization in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) failed to function. Many industries in AJK become non-functional while many other industries, for which abundant resources are available in AJK, could not be started. This is despite the fact that the previous governments of AJK have declared their deep interest in industrialization. The failure of industries leads to numerous problems including employment generation, worker owner disputes, lower productivity and poor infrastructure development. The present study is design to explore the reasons of failure of industrialization, through a survey of all stakeholders including the owner of sick and failed industrial units, industrial workers, the government official and politicians. Hence, this study would be beneficial and important step for all those who aim to promote industrial units in AJK. This study will contribute in reduction of the factors having negative effects on employments, growth, and income; encourage new investors to establish their industries. Since, the revival of industries help in generating revenue, employment and output, therefore the beneficiaries of research are many including the industrialists, Azad Kashmir Mineral and Industrial Development Council, the Revenue Department and those who may be able to secure their jobs in industries. The findings of this research will encourage the government to formulate its policies and strategies to flourish friendly investment environment for investors to establish and re-established their industries in the AJK and job opportunities for youth.

data.projectName: Novel facultative Methylocella strains are active methane consumers at terrestrial natural gas seeps
data.projectDigest:
Climate change is the biggest threat whole world is facing today and one of the main culprits involved in this climate change is methane, a potent greenhouse gas having the global warming potential 34 times greater than that of carbon-dioxide. Rice cultivation is a major source of methane (released from the flooded rice fields as result of anaerobic metabolism) and climate change. Since rice cultivation cannot be exterminated because it is the most important practice to feed seven billion people. Therefore, we need to find sustainable solutions to control methane emissions from rice-cultivated fields, without compromising the yield and production. There is a silver lining in the form of natural biological sources such as the bacteria capable of consuming methane gas. 

Our hypothesis is that the production of methane in rice fields, also stimulate methane-utilizing bacteria. Therefore, the focus of the research project is to identify and isolate the bacteria (using next generation genomics) capable of consuming methane gas before it is released. Such bacteria will be helpful in future to minimize the emissions of methane and ultimately in reducing the global warming. Despite being the remarkable microorganisms, investigations of methane-consuming bacteria have never been performed in Pakistani soils.

data.projectName: Harmonizing the University and Madrassah Curriculum, Teaching Methodology and Research Approaches at Under Graduate Level in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Modern Languages, Islamabad (NUML)
data.projectDigest:
Deeni Madaris are independent institutions and the government avoids interference in their internal affairs. They prescribe their own curriculum through their scholars and ulama. However, the Govt. took some steps for integration of religious education with formal education system. But no satisfactory results have been achieved due to misunderstand of the Madaris and the Govt. It is the dire need of today to bridge the gap between religious education institutions (especially universities). Due to the difference between the modern education and religious education system, conflicts arise in society on intellectual, social, economic, political and even personal level, which destroy the unity of nation.
This project is about exchange of teachers and students from madaris to universities and universities to madaris to create harmony and tolerance. Counseling and training sessions of teachers from madaris and universities will be conducted before exchange of teachers and students at each level. A pilot project for one semester / 4 months will be run between the department of Host and Madaris. On the basis of findings of pilot report, The Project will be executed among major madaris and universities in major cities of Pakistan i.e. Islamabad, Peshawar, Lahore, Quetta, Karachi, Muzaffarabad (AJK) and Gilgit Baltistan (GB). Reports and feedbacks of each exchange will be collected and analyzed for further programming and execution. A seminar will be conducted at the end of each evaluation the report and feedback to highlight the importance of acceptance of both educational systems for developing peace and harmony in the society.

data.projectName: Candidate predictive biomarkers for target therapy among metastatic   triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) naïve and treated young premenopausal women
data.projectDigest: Breast cancer (BC) is the second most common leading cause of death in women and accounting for 30% of all new cancer diagnoses in 2019. It has several subtypes in relation to the molecular features which includes Luminal A and B, estrogen receptor (ER)-positive tumors, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) and triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). However, TNBC is the most biologically aggressive histological subtype which has very poor prognosis and limited treatment option. However, TNBC is found mostly in younger women, under the age of 50 with higher risk to relapse. The risk factors for TNBC includes age at menarche, age at first birth, lack of breast feeding, high parity and abdominal obesity. Therefore, there is a dire need to explore new molecular targets for the treatment of this disease which could be useful as prognostic or predictive targets for novel therapies. The current proposal is design to emphasize the identification of the potential blood biomarkers isolated from young premenopausal TNBC patients as well as the burden of TNBC among all breast cancer subtypes at public and private sector setup.

data.projectName: RECYCLING BIODEGRADABLE FRACTION OF MUNICIPAL SOLID WASTE AT SOURCE LEVEL; DEVELOPING PROTOTYPE MODEL FOR HOUSING SCHEMES & EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTES OF PAKISTAN
data.projectDigest: The one ‘central reason’ of the failure of municipal solid waste (MSW) management system in Pakistan has been that a waste with very low calorific value managed through a centralized MSW management system designed for MSW of very high calorific value from developed country. So far, Lahore in Punjab said to be the pioneer and only city with proper MSW management system has been acquiring about PKR 1,400,000,000.00 per annum with total expenditures of PKR 12,976,966.00 for collection and transportation of MSW only. However, the revenue generation from MSW management system has been negligible, hardly being <1 percent of the acquired budget from Government of Punjab. An effective alternate to the existing centralized MSW management system is source-level recycling of biodegradables by establishing well-designed and sanitation-ensured composting sites in residential colonies and educational institutes of Pakistan. Through proposed approach of recycling biodegradables at source-level, the collection cost will be reduced up to below 20 percent of the current collection and transportation cost. By diverting biodegradable fraction of MSW from out of place putrificaction to managed aerobic decomposition at an appropriate site, the proposed project will create opportunities for new jobs as well as improvement of air, land and water quality.

data.projectName: Identification of Teachers’ Professional Needs and  Establishment of Continuous Professional Development (CPD) Mechanism for College and University Teachers
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: This research proposal is designed to identify teachers’ professional needs and establishment of continuous professional development (CPD) mechanism to enhance professional competencies of college and university teachers. The study will be descriptive in nature and multi-stage simple random sampling technique will be adopted for its completion. The questionnaire, interview protocol and observation sheet will be used for data collection. Population of the study will be comprised of the Deans, Chairpersons. Professors, Associate professors, Assistant professors and Lecturers of higher education institutes like, university and college teachers of public and private sector. The sample of study will be consisted of; eight (08) Faculty Deans, forty (40) Chairpersons, twelve (12) Professors, sixteen (16) Associate professors, eighty-eight (88) Assistant professors and one hundred twenty (120) Lecturers of the universities and colleges will be taken randomly from the population. In the long run, the continuous professional development mechanism will be established in KFUEIT for organizing trainings of university and college teachers according to the training roadmap of NAHE, HEC modules. The module leaders and competent resource persons will be hired for training sessions.

data.projectName: Production and Evaluation of Recombinant Foot-and-Mouth disease Virus-like Particles (VLPs) for the Effective Control of Foot-and-Mouth Disease in Pakistan
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Each year, foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) leads to enormous economic losses to the livestock industry due to high morbidity in adult animals, reduced animal productivity, mortality in young animals and restrictions to global trade in animals and animal products. Currently, the killed whole virus is widely using to control FMD. However, vaccination is constrained by lack of or incomplete protection. Nowadays, virus-like particles (VLPs) are considered to be an effective and safe vaccine candidate against several viral diseases including FMD. These virus sized particles are comprised of several copies of one or more viral structural proteins that spontaneously assemble to form virus like particle without incorporation of the genome. Unlike other inactivated FMD vaccines, the VLPs do not need any high containment facilities for its production and also reduce dependence on cold chain for transport and storage of vaccines. The FMD VLPs vaccine could also facilitate differentiation between vaccinated and infected animals (DIVA). Thus, FMDV VLPs vaccine will be an ideal candidate vaccine to be used for FMD free zones. Considering the importance and need of the country, this project has been developed for production and evaluation of FMDV VLPs vaccine using local isolates.

data.projectName: Preparation of Indigenous Manual Based Intervention for Lowering Anxiety and Depression Levels among Pakistani Youth
data.piUniversity: Capital University of Science and Technology, Islamabad
data.projectDigest: Mental health care is one of the most neglected fields in Pakistan. In recent years both research and news reports have highlighted the increasing incidence of mental health issues among Pakistani youth and lack of adequate mental health care facilities. Therefore, this study will develop a manual based intervention for lowering anxiety and depressive symptoms among youth. The study will be conducted in two phases. In phase I (year 1), a systematic review of the literature will be conducted along with focus group discussions. The systematic review will explore the risk and protective factors of anxiety and depression among youth; and the focus group discussions will explore the perception and experience of anxiety and depression among youth (18-24 years age) and health care professionals. In year2, preparation of the intervention based on the results of systematic review and focus group will take place. In year 3 control trial will be conducted to test the efficacy of the intervention. This project is expected to help build a reservoir of easily accessible mental health interventions to enhance growth of youth; and contribute towards economic growth by empowering human resource of the country as well as help Pakistan achieve its Sustainable Development Goals.

data.projectName: Development of Phytostandard Kits with their Chromatographic and Spectral Data for Academic and Industrial applications
data.projectDigest: This project describes the development of phyto-standrads kits allow the rapid and cost-effective identification of common and bioactive secondary metabolites of plant origin which can be beneficial for both, academia and herbal industry. With this proposal, multiple phyto-standrads kits will be established and validated for different chromatographic users, TLS, HPLC, HPLC-MS and HPLC-MS/MS under tightly controlled conditions.  The Kit will be developed against fifty common bioactive secondary metabolites of plant origin. A database of selected natural products will also be established with their integrated chromatographic data, H-NMR data and HR-ESI-MS/MS data. Application of the developed kits will also be explored on selected medicinal plants of herbal company. An excellent team is constituted for successful execution of the project which includes people from academia and industry; an internationally well known herbal industry of Pakistan, Hamdard is joining hands with us along with other disciplinary scientists. We will also jointly organize a workshop in collaboration with industry for training Pakistani scientists and industry people in the effective utilization of developed kits and the subsequent analysis through developed databases. The developed product will be commercialized and make accessible to the scientific community at national and international levels.

data.projectName: An Analysis of Ecological Footprint in Rural Urban Areas of District Swat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
data.projectDigest: Ecological footprint (EF) is the measure of humans demand on nature i.e. how much productive land area is required for producing the products and resources consumed and the waste generated by humans. The problem of ecological overshooting is being faced by many areas in Pakistan. The present study aims to estimate the ecological footprints at household level taking into account the food, housing, transportation, consumer goods and services in district Swat. Besides, the drivers of the total ecological footprint will also be estimated. This study will use primary data which will be collected through questionnaire designed by the Stockholm Environment Institute (SEI). The information obtained will be converted into EF though calculator of SEI. The analysis will also be extended to rural urban areas of district Swat. The study will use a sample of 1063 households from 7 tehsils of district Swat. The sample size will be proportionally allocated to rural and urban areas of the each tehsil. The descriptive statistics will be used to compute and analyze the total and components of the EF while regression analysis will be used to estimate the impact of various influencing factors of EF.

data.projectName: Indus River Flow Monitoring using Satellite Radar Altimetry Data and 2D Flood model.
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest: The proposed project is an extension of a successfully completed project that suggested a low-cost approach for national surface water level monitoring in Pakistan using satellite data. The prior project investigated and validated the applicability of satellite  for deriving the Indus River water levels.  This success gave us an incentive to investigate more on the utility of satellite data to augment the low-frequency gauging network at the Indus River and monitor river flows at the selected locations by developing rating equations (relating river levels with flows). We also intend to develop a WebGIS-based The River Indus Monitor (TRIM) to access processed data to the end-users. There are 18  satellite tracks of the satellite missions Sentinel 3A & 3B passing over the Indus River in the Sindh Province only. Each of these tracks can be considered as a “Virtual Station” (VS) for water level monitoring. TRIM will provide time-series water measurements at river locations (VS) lacking gauge measurements.

data.projectName: Development of mixed-matrix membrane separation system for carbon capture from industrially-simulated post-combustion flue gases originating from various fuel sources
data.projectDigest: CO2 is considered to be one of the leading promoters of climate change. It is originated as a product of combustion of fossil fuels used in power generation plants, process industry, automobiles and others. The UN Climate Change Conference emphasized the urgent need for establishing international measures for reducing greenhouse gas emissions which will create increasing pressure on all over the globe and on various industries in Pakistan. Primary energy requirements of the world are currently being fulfilled by burning of fossil fuels and these hydrocarbon-based fuels are likely to be the dominant source of meeting global energy demands for the next few decades. Use of fossil fuels to meet energy requirements makes carbon capture indispensable to reduce CO2 emissions into the atmosphere and mitigate worldwide climate change. Carbon emissions into the atmosphere can be readily extenuated by capturing CO2 from flue gas by applying suitable separation technique which demands investments in economically attractively and practically feasible separation technologies. Research and development on carbon capture has grown rapidly over the past few years and requires further advancement to address technical challenges, thus leading to economically viable carbon capture technology. Efficient CO2-capture technologies can be equally applied to both stationary and mobile sources to control the level of CO2 emissions into the atmosphere. The proposed research program is aimed at developing technologies for managing carbon dioxide emissions from fixed and mobile sources. The main objective of this project is the development, characterization, testing, and evaluation of separating systems to reduce CO2 emissions of fixed as well as mobile post-combustion sources.

data.projectName: Establishing mutant strain of Aspergillus fumigatus using CRISPR/Cas system
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Aspergillus fumigatus is a saprotrophic fungus residing primarily in the soil. It causes Aspergillosis, a deadly lung disease, in humans, animals and birds. Toxins produced by this fungus, especially the gliotoxin, have been studied extensively to understand their interactions with other secondary metabolites. Their genes have also been studied extensively in order to see their role in toxin production. An important gene encoding the nonribosomal peptide synthase (gliP) of this fungus has been reported to be able to participate in the synthesis of gliotoxin.

A system comprising clustered, regularly interspaced, short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) and CRISPR-associated (Cas) protein is revolutionizing the field of gene editing. This system uses the parts of bacterial adaptive immune system to create double stranded breaks (DSBs) in the DNA and it can be applied to virtually all species to create mutation in the desired gene at particular location. The aim of this project is, thus, to use CRISPR/Cas system in order to create a mutation in A. fumigatus to develop a mutant strain. The gliP gene, based on its significance, has been selected as a target for this project.

Pakistan is lagging behind in establishing and implementing state-of-the-art CRISPR-Cas system for educational and research purposes. This initial project not only aims to find the solution of this deadly disease, Aspergillosis, through applying this revolutionizing CRISPR technique, but will also do a lot in establishing CRISPR-Cas gene editing set-up in Pakistan which will go a long way for future experiments on genome modification.

data.projectName: “Creating Women’s Empowerment by Developing the Narrative from Iqbal’s Perspective”
data.piUniversity: National University of Modern Languages, Islamabad (NUML)
data.projectDigest:
Empowerment of women and girls is critical to building stable, democratic societies; protecting human rights; fostering international peace and security; growing vibrant market economies; addressing pressing health and education challenges; and their development initiatives will prove to be effective.
Allama Iqbal, was fundamentally a humanist. He specifically has discussed about importance, role and rights of women in a society. This research is made to create women empowerment in Pakistan, through developing an indigenous narrative in context of cultural, religious and social boundaries from Allama Iqbal’s perspective. 
Based on this research report a draft of national level curriculum/ course work will be designed on the theme of proposed research, to be introduced to the end-users, i.e. the centres of excellence and department of women studies in universities of Pakistan which so far mostly teach westernized theories and content. 
This research will add value to the Education Industry in Pakistan in terms of women empowerment awareness and availability of text to teach the discipline in national language, Urdu would itself bring indigenous perspective.
This study will meet Sustainable Development Goals #4, 5 and 10 for Quality Education, Gender Equality and Reduced Inequalities respectively.

data.projectName: Analysis of the role of acid invertase in grain yield of maize under high temperature and water stress
data.projectDigest: Climate change induced high temperature and water stress are challenging crop production in Pakistan. These stresses badly affect crop growth however their impact is more pronounced when these stresses occur at the reproductive stage. In Pakistan, the year 2019 has seen a strong heat wave badly damaging the grain production in maize in spite of a good vegetative growth. This shows vital changes in plant metabolism at reproductive stage due to high temperature and water stress. Acid invertase is an enzyme involved in translocation of sugars from source organs to developing grains, the sinks at the reproductive stage. The literature shows that a damage to this enzyme badly affects grain production. This project plans to identify maize hybrids tolerant to high temperature and water stress. These identified maize hybrids will be studied for the acid invertase activity and grain yield formation under stress conditions. Boron and silicon are important elements under stress conditions and will be studied for their possible role in improving acid invertase activity under high temperature and water stress. The identified hybrids and the nutrient recommendations will be useful for the farmers and the scientific information will be useful for the breeders and researchers.

data.projectName: Amniotic membrane embedded phytoextract primed stem cells construct for wound healing
data.projectDigest:
Stem cells have ample regeneration potential and widely being used for skin reconstruction in developed countries. Skin wounding due to disease, old age, and burns (heat, chemicals, radiation) is a serious health and socio-economic issue. In Pakistan, the higher incidences of burns (e.g., Bahawalpur oil tanker fire incidence), bomb blasts, and diabetes greatly increase the incidence of wounds leading to deformations due to burns or limb amputations due to diabetic ulcers. 

Conventional therapies do not provide satisfactory effects. Various cellular and a-cellular substitutes are commercially available in advanced countries. These substitutes are very expensive and unavailable in Pakistan. Only few of non-cellular substitutes are available in Pakistan despite their dire need. Amniotic membrane obtained from discarded placentas after deliveries have remarkable wound healing properties. 

Hence it is proposed to develop bioengineered constructs using amniotic membrane and primed stem cells in combination. In this regard at first various priming strategies will be explored to improve stem cell efficiency and loaded onto amniotic membrane to develop easy to use efficient substitutes. The optimized cell based constructs will have clinical application, be patentable and great potential of commercialization.

data.projectName: Synthesis and modelling of geopolymer concrete with its application in 3-D printing: Sustainable and digital construction practice
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest:
The rapid urbanization has led to an increase in the construction industry which is one of the largest consumer of the world’s energy. Concrete, being the primary construction material is a mixture of several un-sustainable material. Binders and aggregates contributes to the majority of cost and CO2 emissions from concrete production. The objectives of the research can be summarized as:
•	Geopolymer concrete (GPC) by using environmental friendly binders such as metakaolin, ground granulated blast furnace slag, fly-ash or the combination of suitable binders will be developed.
•	Waste foundry sand (WFS) is being disposed in landfills in large quantities by foundries in Pakistan. The coupling effect of GPC with WFS will be evaluated. 
•	Artificial intelligence techniques i.e. artificial neural network and gene expression programming will be implemented to model the mecahnical properties of GPC based on a vast experimental database. 
•	GPC will also be characterized based on its initial and final properties under different conditions to evaluate its use for digital/3D printing.
The end-users of the project are the construction industry and metal casting foundries which are facing sustainability issues. Moreover, the anticipated environmental benefits align with the motives of Prime Minister’s recently launched Clean and Green Pakistan (CGP) campaign.

data.projectName: Vaccine development for Newcastle disease virus in poultry
data.projectDigest: Newcastle Disease (ND) virus belongs to the family Paramyxoviridae. Poultry birds including domestic, commercial layer, broiler and breeder flocks are infected by ND virus. It is a huge problem on the world’s economy than any other animal virus and cause high morbidity and mortality. Vaccination is generally considered to be the most effective method to prevent this infection. However, there are some risks associated with available vaccines against ND. For example, there is a possibility that live viruses may revert back to virulence and cause the disease in the vaccinated poultry and other birds. Moreover, generally the killed vaccines of ND virus are poor inducers of mucosal or cell mediated immune response. Furthermore, DNA vaccine has poor immunogenicity, high cost of production, and unsuitability for mass administration. Hence, in this proposal we aim to design epitope based ND vaccine by predicting B and T cell epitopes from two structural proteins, i.e. Hemagglutinin Neuraminidase (HN) and Fusion (F) proteins of NDV. Such kinds of vaccines specifically peptide vaccines are based on the approach to predict and prepare B and T-cell epitopes. These epitopes are immunodominant and can induce immune responses specific to those predicted B and T cell epitopes. Moreover, during immunity progression, B-cell epitopes of the target molecule may combine with T-cell epitopes and make this complex immunogenic. We will predict B and T cell epitopes using various bioinformatics tools accessible in Immune Epitope Database (IEDB). After prediction of the epitopes, the epitopes based vaccine will be validated by constructing the plasmid and the viral proteins will be expressed in E. Coli. These expressed proteins will be used to confirm the immunogenicity of virus in the poultry.

data.projectName: Performance Evaluation of Multiple Aerators Installed in Series at High Head Overflow Spillways: Case Study of Mohmand Dam
data.projectDigest:
Water is life and management of water resources improves quality of life. Growing water demands in Pakistan have once again paved way for planning and construction of large dams to store and harness surplus water. Large dams house high-head spillways, capable of releasing high magnitude floods. A design engineer is faced with various concerns and challenges that must be addressed properly to prevent damage to spillway and other dam structures. One such important concern is Cavitation along the spillway chute. 
High-head spillways are mostly provided with steep chute slopes where high flow velocities can develop negative pressures, resulting in cavitation at concrete surface. Many researchers have studied the problem and proposed remedial measures. One such widely practiced measure is the provision of aerators on spillway chutes. Aerator performance must be ensured to be as intended, so that spillway cavitation damage is prevented. At times, multiple aerators are proposed at spillways with high-head and steep chute. The spacing between multiple aerators must be properly fixed so that entrained air is enough to prevent cavitation. Also, aeration must not be excessive to initiate unwanted flow bulking. This research proposal focuses on the performance of multiple aerators installed at high-head overflow spillway.

data.projectName: Epidemiology of bovine tuberculosis and its public health significance in Punjab, Pakistan
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Mycobacterium tuberculosis is one of the primary causes of human TB and developed countries are giving importance to add M. bovis to their ongoing eradication and control programs. However the zoonotic potential of Mycobacterium bovis is still underestimated.  One Health approach is based on the concept of interdependence between human and animal health sectors to address the major health and economic issues. In Pakistan One Health approach has been introduced recently and very little practical application of the concept is available. Interdependence of human and animal health is neglected issue in Pakistan. It has been reported that M. bovis is the key pathogen of approximately 10% of total tuberculosis cases in humans in developing countries thus poses a noteworthy threat to global health. The countries, Bangladesh, Pakistan, India, China and Indonesia together share half of the burden of tuberculosis worldwide. Pakistan has been enlisted among twenty two countries which account for the overall TB burden and also ranked among five countries responsible for TB globally. A direct effect of infection on milk production is obvious and decreases the milk yield 10 to 18% and meat production by 15%. In addition to this the culling of dairy and beef breeding cattle at the cost of slaughtering imposes 30 to 50% losses. Tuberculosis is a monetary burden to society in term of human fitness charges.  This disease is also a hurdle in socioeconomic development of society as 75% of the TB patients age ranges between 15 to 54 years, which is the most productive age.

data.projectName: GRAPHENE OXIDE FUNCTIONALIZED WITH IONIC LIQUID FOR SOLID PHASE MICROEXTRACTION OF SELECTED REGIONAL PESTICIDES FROM ENVIRONMENTAL SAMPLES FOLLOWED BY HIGH PERFORMANCE LIQUID CHROMATOGRAPHIC DETECTION.
data.projectDigest: The instant project is designed to reduce the aftereffects (pollution) of selected regional pesticides sprayed on sugarcane, wheat, maize and tobacco. Normally pesticides have been used for the protection of various crops from the pests (flies, insects etc). Further, it is worth mentioning that the pests not only effect the growth of the crop but also their long lives (characteristics) have proved. Therefore as and when human/animal utilized it as food. In this scheme graphene oxide(GO) modified with room temperature ionic liquids (RTILs) will be utilized for extraction of selected regional pesticides using solid phase microextraction (SPME) technique (first if it’s kind in Pakistan). So as to provide fast, more reliable and simple procedure as compared to the existing cumbersome and toxic techniques.

data.projectName: Editing of Unpublished Original Pakistani Urdu Stage Plays In the light of Social, Cultural, Historical and Political Scenario
data.projectDigest: Research and critical Studies have been carried out on Urdu novel,poetry. but unfortunately, Urdu Drama in general, and stage drama in particular has been neglected altogether. Although, this genre is directly linked to its social. Cultural, historical, and political life.There has been some compilation and cataloging in the past, but a huge gap exists towards its accomplishment particularly in the past half century. This situation is putting the entire Urdu play literature at the risk of heritage loss and also depriving the young researchers to access the data published till date. Hence, there is need to address this issue on urgent basis. It is important to note that stage plays are strongly associated with social, cultural and historical perspectives. The current study has been designed to save and compile the cultural heritage of Urdu stage drama and analyze some selected plays in retrospect to cultural, political and historical perspective. In this connection, manuscripts will be collected from educational institutions, art councils and other related organizations all across Pakistan. Additionally, one selected play will be staged at the University of Education, Lahore and presented to the students, teachers and masses; the socioeconomic and political relations of the play will also be explored in this activity.

data.projectName: Improving Urban Water Management: an interdisciplinary application of smart urban infrastructure to study water demand in Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Much of the discussion regarding Karachi’s water crisis focuses on a ‘shortage’ in water supply compared to water demand. However, this perceived water demand in Karachi is not informed by credible empirical analysis and is based on unverified assumptions. Another major challenge is the high-level of non-revenue water (NRW) in the system which prevent Karachi’s water utility (KWSB) from being financially viable. A big reason behind the high percentage of NRW is the lack of domestic water metering and the consequent use of a water pricing system that does not account for actual water use. 
This interdisciplinary research proposal provides an empirical basis for solving these challenges by (i) developing a low cost smart flow meter and IoT based connectivity framework that is able to accurately measure and remotely transmit flow information to a cloud based central server and (ii) devising a sustainable water pricing structure that account for household incomes. This research effort will provide two key solutions to Karachi’s water challenges: (i) a quantification of spatial and temporal patterns in domestic water usage that will improve current demand estimates and projections, and (ii) evidence based equitable water pricing strategies that will help increase revenue to allow KWSB to achieve financially sustainability.

data.projectName: Hyaluronic acid-functionalized Cyclosporine A Nanosuspension Enema for Targeted Therapy of Ulcerative Colitis
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest:
Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a major type of inflammatory bowel disease that affects millions of peoples worldwide. The UC patients suffer from rectal bleeding, diarrhea and weight loss. The untreated UC can lead to colorectal cancer. Cyclosporine A (CSA), an immunosuppressive agent, has long been used as rescue therapy in severe steroid-refractory UC. However, the commercial oral formulations of CSA (Sandimmune Neoral®) have increased systemic bioavailability which results in severe side effects in patients. Therefore, local therapy with CSA enema could be a safe strategy for treating UC patients. However, we hypothesize that pure CSA microcrystals have poor water solubility and are too large to effectively penetrate colitis tissues, limiting the extent of drug delivery to affected tissues and inflammatory cells prior to clearance.
Nanoparticles (NPs) have the potential to accumulate in the colitis tissues due to the disrupted epithelial barriers functions and the immigration of inflammatory cells. NPs accumulation in colitis tissues would lead to improved therapeutic efficacy and enable localized treatment, which reduces systemic toxicity.  Here, we propose the development of a CSA nanosuspension (CSA-NS) by applying nanotechnology to enhance solubility and penetration in colitis tissues. Further, the surface of CSA-NS will be modified with targeting ligands (hyaluronic acid-HA) to prepare HA-CSA-NS that could enhance uptake by epithelial cells and macrophages in colitis tissue through receptor-mediated interactions, which are mainly involved in the inflammatory process.

data.projectName: Decompositions of Lie Derivations (Triple Lie Derivations) of Generalized Quaternion and Octonion Algebras in Lie, Inner and Jordan Derivations over Semi-prime Rings
data.projectDigest:
Let A be any commutative or semi-prime ring and K=H(A), (O(A)) be algebra of generalized Quaternions and Octonions defined over base ring A. A derivation d is a map from K to K which generally behaves as a derivative. Some well-known types of derivations are Lie derivation, Jordan derivation, Lie triple derivations, generalized triple derivation etc. A Lie derivation adopts a standard form f = T+P where
T: K to K is a derivation and  P: K  to Z(K) is an additive map such that
P([K; K]) = 0. 


We are interested to see whether some types of derivations or its variants of K  can be decomposed  into Lie derivations, Jordan Derivations and additive central maps of A so these variants are in some standard form. Also what can be matrix form and generators of these algebras?

data.projectName: Yield optimization of biodiesel sourced from local seeds and waste cooking oil for their use in unmodified diesel engines
data.projectDigest: Internal combustion engines (ICEs) are prime mover of any economy. These engines, primarily, run on fossil fuels which are continuously depleting and harshly damaging the global environment. Smog, a direct consequence of the unregulated emissions, has started affecting our major urban centers especially in the province of Punjab. The economies with no indigenous oil resources are adversely affected by the fluctuating oil prices in the international markets especially in the backdrop of the political conflicts in the oil producing regions. The imbalance generated by the imported oil products offsets all and any socio economic initiative. Pakistan falls under the category of the countries which do not have indigenous oil resource and it rely heavily on the imported oil. Fast depleting oil reserves has necessitated the replacement for these conventional fuels. Pakistan, being an agricultural economy, has vast land which can produce both food and fuel. Production of these sustainable biofuels, from various seeds as well as from the waste cooking oils, can lessen Pakistan’ heavy reliance on imported fuel. These sustainable biofuels can fully or partially substitute the diesel fuel. The performance and emissions characteristics of these sustainable fuels should be investigated and compared against the diesel baseline. It is also pertinent to test the biodiesel blends with water and nano-particles and examine the effects of their usage in combustion chamber.  This project is timely proposed and is going to help the new investment of 400 billion in Allama Iqbal Industrial State, going to be established at Faisal Abad, in addition to the existing automotive manufacturers.

data.projectName: Development of Slurries for 3D Printing of Ceramic/Polymer Scaffolds for Bone Tissue Engineering
data.projectDigest:
The use of ceramic materials has gained a lot of interest due to their unique properties such as hardness, biocompatibility, chemical stability, and have been used for potential applications. Additive manufacturing (AM) /3D printing is advanced method to fabricate the ceramic components. Research in the optimization of printable material, expansion of materials selection for 3D printing, as well as 3D printing methods are opportunities that are yet to be explored. 
Bone tissue engineering is a promising method for treating fractured bones, in which a three dimensional (3D) porous scaffold  is implanted in a body using variety of materials such as bioceramics, biopolymers, biometallic and biocomposites. Bioceramics are materials with specific biocompatibility and functionality, and can be used as bone implants to restore the function of bones. 3D printing of bioceramics is very challenging because the number of available materials with specific properties are very limited and yet to be explored. 
The main objective of the research would be optimization of slurries consisting of ceramic/polymer materials and optimization of 3D printing process for bone scaffolds. The proposed research work will reveal the possibility to print bone scaffolds starting from raw material to the final product (artificial bone implant for dental and orthopedic applications).

data.projectName: Performance Evaluation of Masonry System under Blast Loading
data.projectDigest:
Government buildings are fabricated from unreinforced burnt clay brick masonry in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Pakistan. These buildings are being targeted with improvised explosive devices in the terrorist activities after 9/11 continuously. Consequently, thousands of public buildings mainly school buildings were partially damaged or fully collapsed due to improvised explosive devices, detonated in close vicinity. These public buildings are reconstructed again with the same construction materials and practices without proper scientific knowledge of blast loading phenomenon and the expected response of buildings. The quantified response is classified and limited to military establishment of developed countries only.
Studies have been carried out to find the response of masonry buildings against blast loadings. Similarly, application of retrofitting techniques such as FRP, polyurea, polyurethane, aluminum foam, engineered cementitious composites, enhances the response of brick masonry. These techniques are either expensive, inherent limitations in applications or require specialized techniques for field applications. 
Therefore, there is dire need for indigenous and economical solutions against the blast loadings in terrorist prone regions of Pakistan. In the current research, different masonry systems such as unreinforced masonry, ferrocement overlay masonry and adobe walls as well as full scale rooms will be tested against blast loading. Subsequently, the performance of masonry systems will be evaluated.
In order to carry out the research, different walls, and full scale rooms will be tested against the stipulated threat levels (kg of Trinitrotoluene- TNT and distance of center of explosion from the target structure) in the field. The pressure-time history on the test specimen d

data.projectName: Geostatistical Tools for Spatial Distribution of Dominant Disease-Pest of Apricot and Management Using Trunk Injection Delivery System
data.piUniversity: Karakurum International University, Gilgit, Gilgit Baltistan
data.projectDigest: Fruit sector of GB is facing many challenges in terms of biotic and abiotic factors. Among the biotic factors; diseases pests (shot hole and fruit fly) are well adapted in apricot orchards; hence posing the most serious threats in the region to the production and profitability. To manage the pest and diseases infestation phenomenon; the injudicious use of synthetic chemicals in agriculture system has triggered many complications to the overall ecosystem such as water, soil, animals and food commodities, purging of non-target beneficial organisms. To curtail the adverse effects of synthetic pesticides; it is imperative to introduce plant extract based bio-pesticides alternatives, which are useful and safe. The conventional sprayer machine is not feasible to adjust spray quantity based on tree canopy and unnecessary discharge in terms of the amount as well as non-target areas. Trunk injection delivery system is being used in developed and developing countries successfully with good results due to its precise application. Thus the current study focusses on an effective injector to resolve these problems. The successful accomplishment of this project will help in achieving the national targets of poverty alleviation and sustainable food security. It will open new opportunities for the export of high-quality apricot.

data.projectName: Development of high performance adhesive systems for light weight structural applications – A project for the development of energy efficient vehicles for the aerospace, aviation and automobile sectors.
data.projectDigest: Current work is aimed to promote latest manufacturing trends towards  the development of high performance light weight structures such as for unmanned vehicles (UAVs), air craft’s, composite cars , ship parts and aero planes. The research would play its part by providing joining techniques for the use of light weight structural materials in mechanical assemblies. Adhesives being versatile joining materials can address the limitations of mechanical fastenings and welding. However, adhesives strength can be greatly affected at temperatures above 200ºC and in moist and humid environments. They are extremely sensitive to the conditions of the joining surfaces. Their softening temperature, known as glass transition temperature, plays critical part in determining the strength of adhesives. Current work is focused to develop and standardize adhesives joints using higher glass transition temperature adhesives, optimize their mechanical strength and conclude about their applications and limitations in respect of  hot and humid service conditions. This would require achieving compatibility between joining materials, adhesives, surface preparations and curing conditions. i.e. temperature cycle, application pressure , adhesive thickness etc. 3 types of materials and 5  types of high performance adhesives would be analyzed to  benefit space programs, automobiles and UAVs development besides immense future research prospects.

data.projectName: Molecular Characterization and Development of Attenuated Vaccine Using Local Strains of Contagious Pustular Dermatitis Virus from Small Ruminants of Cholistan
data.piUniversity: Cholistan University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Bahawalpur
data.projectDigest: Contagious pustular dermatitis (CPD) also known as Orf, contagious ecthyma, scabby mouth or sore mouth is one of the transmissible viral diseases of small ruminants mainly affecting sheep and goats production worldwide. The causative agent of CPD is a Parapox virus from Poxviridae family which gains access epidermal cells via damaged skin and causing proliferative localized skin lesions of oral mucosa, lips and nostrils. The disease is endemic among small ruminants in many areas of Punjab/Pakistan and cause significant economic losses to livestock owners. The CPD causes decreases in production, reduced market value, has no effective antiviral treatment, an animal welfare issue, and known to have zoonotic importance. However, CPD is an ignored viral disease in Pakistan and there is a need to determine the economic losses (direct or indirect) caused by this disease. Vaccination is the only remedy to control an infectious viral disease in an endemic region like Pakistan. Currently, there is no vaccine available in Pakistan to prevent the disease especially for farmers who purchase animals from livestock market for fattening and subsequent sale. The vaccine is also required to control the disease at initial stage of any outbreak both in traditional free range and commercial flocks and for export of live animals over long distances. A necessary step towards development of vaccine is to understand the genetic diversity and phylogenetic relationships of local CPD viral isolates. However, there is no information available about genetic diversity of CPD virus causing natural outbreaks in Punjab/Pakistan. Keeping in consideration afore mentioned points, current project is planned to develop a live attenuated vaccine using local viral strain of CPD.

data.projectName: Synthesis of Multinary Chalcogenide Semiconductors and their Photocatalytic Hydrogen (H2) Fuel Production
data.piUniversity: Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology, Rahim Yar Khan
data.projectDigest: The human population is increasing at alarming level but there are limited sources of energy overall in world to meet the recent human requirements. Only transportation systems consume about 40% of the overall fuel resources, so this system demands other sources to derive the community vehicle. On other side our main energy source “fossil fuels” reservoirs are depleting. World has set some alternatives for the fuels and energy demands to power modern world economy and to overcome energy disaster. Hydrogen H2 gas is attracting fuel due to renewable and sustainable. It can be produced with conversion of water to hydrogen under sunlight but its production is globally limited to 0.1%.  Our aim of project is to develop this chapter of H2 production by synthesis catalyst which can harvest solar light as energy source to decompose water into hydrogen fuel. To obtained success in this project, we have designed and proposed fabrication of multinary chalcogeniedes semiconductor nanomaterials which will act as the best light absorber catalyst to harvest solar light and decomposition of water into hydrogen fuel.

data.projectName: Novel 3D woven hybrid composite-based bullet protection for vehicles
data.projectDigest:
Historically, certain metals (wrought, cast, high-hard and ultrahigh-hard steel, aluminum, titanium), ceramic and other materials were used in bullet proof vehicles. These have certain disadvantages higher in weight, welding problems, lower fracture toughness, higher cost, etc. These parameters ultimately lead to increase in vehicle weight, reducing mobility and range in given amount of fuel. One of the possible solutions is to replace metallic panels with composites structures, which are lighter in weight, have excellent specific strength, stiffness and energy absorption. 
Depending upon the woven reinforcements, composites are either 2D or 3D composites. 2D woven composites have certain issues like, poor through thickness properties, lower damage tolerance, etc. 3D woven composites have 10-15% improved damage tolerance, but rare used in ballistic applications. Also, no indigenous composite solution is available for ballistic protection in vehicles. Depending upon the level of protection in vehicles, a ballistic panel consists of a thick front ceramic plate and a textile composite backing plate (Both jointly called hard armor plate ‘HAP’).  This study will focus on the development of novel 3D woven hybrid reinforcement based ballistic composite panels (with fillers) by joining ceramic tiles for European ballistic protection level B5/B6 equivalent to NIJ level III.

data.projectName: Bridging the employability skills gap in the higher education through training interventions concentrated on soft and technical skills for Pakistani Millennials: The implications for the Executive training Centre (ETC)
data.projectDigest: According to a recent study by Shaikh and Jamal (2019), Pakistani workforce is categorised into three generations out of which Pakistani Millennials or Pakistani Generation Y is comprised of more than 60 percent of the present and potential workforce of Pakistan. However, when it comes to the employability skills, this particular generation lacks the expertise in the basic soft and technical skills which are crucial for attaining employment opportunities. Hence, among the several other factors, it has been observed that lack of training and education on these basic employability skills is the reason why Pakistani graduates have failed to penetrate in the local and international labor markets. In this regard, the proposed project establishes the need for the identification of the desirable employability skills from the perspectives of the employers in the current work context of Pakistani organisations so as to train the Millennials effectively. Therefore, the proposed project will involve a prior study of the generational persona of Pakistani Millennials, particularly in terms of their preferred training methods, in order to train them with the implementation of their generationally specific or tailored training methods. In doing so, the proposed project emphasises upon the role of the Executive Training Centre (ETC) at the Departmental level in imparting the key employability skills within the young graduates. Hence, the outcomes of this proposed project will be the attainment of employment by the University graduates.

data.projectName: Induction of drought tolerance in maize mediated by mixed bacterial consortium
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan, maize is the 4th largest growing crop after wheat, cotton and rice. Maize (Zea mays L.) is the highest yielding cereal crop, its area increases day by day as population increases. The production of maize is 3.5 million metric tons, which is very low. This low yield of maize crop is because of various biotic and abiotic factors at different stages of growth.  Among these factors, water shortage is the main problem globally.  In the present project we aimed to develop drought tolerant maize by using mixed bacterial consortium of lactic acid producing bacteria, L. coryniformis and salt tolerant endophytic bacteria isolated from maize roots. This mixed bacterial consortium will be employed to maize seeds for improving the growth and yield of plant by observing different germination and field parameters. The proposed experiments will ultimately improve the quality and quantity of products and will also upgrade the agriculture economy in future.

data.projectName: Process upscaling for biodesulfurization of automobile fuels (diesel and petrol) to meet Euro-4 equivalent sulfur standards
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: Air pollution and smog has evolved as a major urban issue in Pakistan. Although there are many factors which causes air pollution however, sulfur has been a main culprit in automobile fuels. We are still using Euro-2 equivalent fuel, which permits 500 ppm sulfur. As per the current government's anti air pollution measures, the Euro-4 (sulfur limit 50 ppm) oil will be implemented in Pakistan. Hydrodesulphurization is being used by the refineries to reduce the sulfur in transportation fuels. It can desulfurize aliphatic and acyclic sulfur containing compounds, however, the sulfur present in aromatic dibenzothiophene and benzothiophene, especially their alkyl derivatives, are difficult to desulfurize due to the sterically hindered nature of these compounds. Microbial removal of thiophenic sulfur from petroleum oil may offer an attractive economic complementary/alternative to hydrodesulfurization treatment due to the mild operating conditions and greater reaction specificity of biocatalysis. In current study, first, a microbial cocktail will be prepared for biodesulfurization of a wide range of thiophenic compounds present in transportation fuels. Then, the process of biodesulfurization of transportation fuels will be upscaled to attain Euro-4 equivalent sulfur standards. In addition, the genome based microbial profiling will also be carried out to understand the molecular mechanisms of petroleum biodesulfurization.

data.projectName: Digitalizing Folk Wisdom: A project of collection, translation, and study of folk literature in major Pakistani languages
data.projectDigest:
The contemporary world is speedily building a cyber megalopolis. This internet supercity will house goods from various parts of the planet. But the disadvantage of living in a fully globalized world would be that most of the omnipresent ‘global’ would have little or no share from our ‘local’. Unfortunately, online representation of Pakistan’s cultural products is very low. This would not just alienate Pakistan’s youth in this new internet metropolis but also leave them vulnerable to foreign cultural onslaught. Therefore, it is imperative to digitalize our folk literature. 
I propose “Digitalizing Folk Wisdom: A project of collection, translation, and study of folk literature in major Pakistani languages” to collect from the far and wide of the country 2000 items of folk literature (tales, qissas, poetic narratives, etc.) in oral form. These literary pieces coming from seven major Pakistani languages (Balochi, Brahvi, Pashto, Punjabi, Saraiki, Sindhi, and Urdu) will then be transcribed in Roman as well as Perso-Arabic scripts. All of them will also be translated into English for foreign viewers/readers. The audio texts, along with their transcription and translation would be placed online. The transcription and translation would also be published in book forms to be studied critically.

data.projectName: Development of functional feed for Labeo rohita and Oreochromis niloticus
data.projectDigest:
Feed is the most costly component of aquaculture which has more than 45-60% running cost of system. By optimizing feed with reference fish species requirement and economical ingredient selection, aquaculture practice could be made more productive and economical.
Currently, for culturing of either fish species in Pakistan, conventional feed is used to feed the fish under cultivation. In conventional fish feed majorly fish meal is used as protein source and animal origin oil is used as fat source. These components are costly on the one hand and are problematic to the environment on the other hand. There availability becomes problem even at high price and fluctuated during the year. These are readily vulnerable to spoilage and aflatoxin toxicity.  So by replacing these components with plant origin protein and fats we can not only reduce the cost of feed but also save the environment.

data.projectName: Equitable English Learning Experience: A Gender based Study of Remote Areas of Balochistan
data.piUniversity: National University of Modern Languages, Islamabad (NUML)
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan is one of the worst performing countries on gender equality index and the situation is worse in rural and backward areas, specifically in Balochistan. There lies huge disparity among girls and boys even at the school level. Therefore, the present study aims to provide equal experience of education specifically English literacy to both the genders. For this, a two-year long project has been proposed that covers, the on-ground analysis of circumstances and then providing practical solutions for eliminating the problem of gender inequality in schools of Khuzdar and Lasbela District. 
During the course of project, interaction sessions with the students, locals and teachers will be held. After having a detailed view of reality along with the socio-cultural contexts, various training sessions will be conducted for teachers to train them for effective gender neutral teaching and how can they motivate other children specifically girls of the region to attend schools. Furthermore, awareness rising will also be done to inform the parents about the need of female education and to motivate them to send their daughters to school.
Not only the training and awareness will be provided but their impact will also be studied as part of the research. Therefore, after a few months, the PI and team will visit different schools of Balochistan to see the change. Finally, results will be drawn at the end of two years’ time and a report will be presented.

data.projectName: A Discriminant Analysis to Predict PhD Completion of HEC Scholarship Awardees
data.piUniversity: National University of Modern Languages, Islamabad (NUML)
data.projectDigest: The purpose of this project is to explore the relationship between pre-scholarship criteria and doctoral student performance ratings and to develop a model to predict student persistence to complete or not to complete their PhD after getting the HEC Indigenous and International Scholarship. Higher education commission HRD department is responsible to gauge the students for the award of indigenous and international scholarships. The decision makers have a responsibility to minimize bias, select the most appropriate and efficient student who has urge to complete his/her degree within time and resources. Despite of all the efforts done by the HEC concerned department to provide the scholarship to only those candidate that has ability to complete PhD, many of student fail to complete PhD after getting scholarship. Till today, no other study is available that assess the effectiveness of already established scholarship merit criteria’s. This study going to check the effectiveness of already established criteria and will provide a new criteria score which help the HEC to select or reject the candidate for scholarship which base on statistical grounds and guaranty of more chances to complete PhD. Pre-scholarship variables and post acceptance performance ratings will be used in this cross-sectional predictive study.
