data.projectName: Engineering a Laccase-Xylanase bifunctional enzyme to improve biomass conversion
data.projectDigest: In pulp and paper processing industry, xylanases and laccases are involved in biobleaching and pulp delignification processes. A designer bifunctional enzyme with xylanase and laccase activities, is likely to give an increase in catalytic turnover number and limit the processing timing. Multiple bifunctional chimeras (Bsu-Lac.Bsu-xyl and Bsu-xyl.Bsu-Lac) from Bacillus subtilis laccase (Bsu-Lac) and xylanase (Bsu-xyl) genes will be prepared in end-to-end fusion (either fusing C or N terminals of polypeptide chains) with a short linker in between. Domain insertion also will be studied for construction of bifunctional enzyme by limiting its size. Glycosyl hydrolases family 11 domain from Bsu-xyl (29-211 a.a) will be fused with single to multiple copper oxidase domains by inserting the GH11 domain from xylanase into multiple loop regions of laccase structure. Previous results, from our group, show considerably high activities of individual laccase and xylanase enzymes against their substrates. A stable/bifunctional chimera preparation with genetic organization/shuffling of laccase domains with xylanase will allow enzyme to work in a better way by limiting the substrate diffusion and improving enzyme kinetics. For this purpose, laccase domains will be separately cloned and expressed and enzyme assay will determine activity of individual enzyme as well as in a chimeric form.

data.projectName: Engineering stem cells for in vivo delivery of specific therapeutic peptides via paracrine peptide-transduction
data.projectDigest:
Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) and a large subset of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) are blood cancers that are driven by the same genetic abnormality called the Philadelphia chromosome (Ph). Underlying this abnormal chromosome is the fusion of two normally separate genes to a single hybrid gene (BCR-ABL) which encodes a protein that causes leukemia by disrupting normal signaling pathways in blood stem cells. Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKI) are drugs that specifically block the overactive enzyme activity of BCR-ABL and are highly effective in treatment of Ph+ leukaemias, which previously were fatal in the vast majority of patients. Unfortunately, the leukemia eventually returns in most patients with Ph+ ALL, with life expectancy measured in months, and in some patients with CML. Chronic side effects and the extremely high cost of this life-long treatment are additional disadvantages. 
. In this study stem cells will be transduced with unique construct which will allow the these cells to secrete the therapeutic peptides and at the same time the peptides will be taken up by the recipient leukemic cell by enabling theses peptide cell penetrating. This novel approach will definitely improve the therapy status in resistant and refractory leukemic patients.

data.projectName: Student Services and their Impacts on Students’ Academic Life in Public Sector Universities in Pakistan
data.projectDigest:
Previous research in the field of higher education in Pakistan, on the one side, reveals explicit dissatisfaction of faculty members and students from teaching-learning process and on the other side there is no evidence of the provision of standardized student services. The IASAS (2002), and Abu Hasan et al. (2008), strictly argue to provide students services in HEIs on the basis of public will. The services empower the students to expend more time on their studies and enable them to learn beyond the classroom. Student services available in universities build the foundations of student-university relationships on the grounds which are further than limited study periods of students (Baig & Khan, 2010). The current study is an attempt to evaluate the extent of availability and accessibility of students services in Pakistani universities. The role of provided services in students’ academic life will also be calculated to investigate the effectiveness/ineffectiveness of the services. The statement of the problem will be;
Analysis of Prevalent Student Services and their Impacts on students’ Academic Lives in Public Sector Universities in Pakistan

data.projectName: Role of Nitric oxide in the Biology of Nematodes
data.projectDigest: Nitric oxide (NO) is a colorless gas, very reactive and extremely important for vital processes in almost all multi-cellular animals. The role of NO is well established in most animals, humans and in plants. For instance, in humans, it plays a major role in widening the blood vessels thereby relaxing the muscles to keep the blood flow under control., while in plants it has a role in growth and development as well as in plant defense. In nematodes (except from C. elegans, where it acts as an anti-aging), we simply don't know the role of NO at all. Therefore, this proposed research will be looking to investigate the effect of this gas on the life parameters of both beneficial and harmful nematodes. Nematodes are commonly known as round worms and have immense importance. the effect of NO on nematode survival, development , longevity and pathogenic behaviour will uncover plenty thereby opening a new area of research. If found positive for insect parasitic  nematodes, will add to their successful commercial use as biopesticide

data.projectName: Substituting traditional protein sources in poultry diet with low cost and more sustainable insect protein
data.projectDigest: In poultry nutrition, the production of soybean meal (SBM) and fish meal (FM) is environmentally and economically not sustainable. Protein-rich insects are one of the options to replace conventional protein sources. This is due to their high feed conversion efficiency, rich amino acid profile, high mass production potential, low emission levels and land area requirement.  Only a limited number of insect species have been evaluated for their dietary potential as animal feed whilst most of the insect species have quarantine limitations. Present project is planned to investigate native insect species by exploring their mass rearing potential on local bio-waste materials. Their dietary potential as poultry feed will be studied. This will include assessing their nutritional values including their chemical composition, proteins, fats and mineral contents. The response of broilers and layers will also be documented in shape of their growth and development, nutritional value of meat and eggs, effect on intestinal morphology, any toxic effect and diseases. Consumer acceptance will also be studied for the potential candidate insects. The results if successfully achieved and adopted at commercial scale can help farmers and feed processors get 20-25% more return on investment. It will put low pressure on environment and biodiversity.

data.projectName: Development of Cost-Effective Structural Concrete Formulation using Limestone Calcined Clay-Based LC3 Cement Blend with Domestic Resources and its Application in a Pilot Project
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: Concrete is the basic building material employed in the world today, and the third-largest source of greenhouse gases. The reduction of CO2 emissions from the cement manufacturing process lies in the reduction of its clinker content - an intermediate product produced through the burning of limestone and clay. Recently formulated LC3 blend contains 50% lower clinker and its a one-to-one replacement of conventional ordinary Portland cement (OPC). The blend has 40% lower carbon footprints, has low cost and can produce with abundantly available low quality of clay. In this project, we will map a few promising clay sites, produce LC3 in the laboratory as well as in bulk and will use the resulting concrete for a small scale pilot project. Early versions of blended cement have low mechanical properties as well as inherent workability issues, thus could not able to replace OPC as mainstream cement. The execution of the pilot project which will be the first of its kind is very important to bring the stakeholders together on one table. These include cement manufacturers, design consultants, builders, raw material providers, government policymakers, and international organizations including World Bank and other funding bodies.

data.projectName: National Consumer Confidence Predictor Using Social Analytics
data.projectDigest: The industry challenge is that the official Consumer Confidence Index (CCI) published by State Bank of Pakistan may not reflect the true state of Pakistani economy. In Pakistan, official CCI covers households’ perceptions relative to the last six months and their expectations for the next semester, including personal financial conditions, overall economy, unemployment and consumption of durable goods. The CCI index is based on survey conducted by State Bank of Pakistan. Analysis of the official CCI index in comparison with the actual statistics reveals that as official CCI decreases, actual Consumer Spending, Consumer Credit, Gasoline Prices and Private Sector Credit increases, indicating inconsistency between official CCI and actual state of the economy. However, the official CCI is incapable of reflecting true condition of the economy consequently it provides little value (or no information) to industry player and end users. It is might be due to inherent limitations in the way it is computed. Contrarily, we proposes a novel method of social media analytics that utilizes big data and data science to predict the national consumer confidence using large data sets from social media (37 Million users) as data flow is growing faster than trade and finance in today’s digital era.

data.projectName: Genetic Diagnosis and In Vitro and In Vivo Disease Modeling of Neurodevelopmental Disorders
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Our genome is made up of DNA sequences that contains all the information for our body structure and function. Changes in this DNA sequence called mutations or variants can have adverse effects and may lead to abnormal function of our natural biochemical processes and consequently to disease. These mutations can potentially transmit to offsprings. Our proposed project is aimed at identifying those mutations underlying neurodevelopmental disorders and then explore the mechanism by which mutations affect other biological processes leading to abnormal phenotype. To achieve these goals, we will first identify mutations by sequencing all protein coding part of the patients’ genomes and then test the pathogenicity of specific mutations in zebrafish embryos. In the next phase we will explore the functional consequences of disease causing mutations and related downstream biochemical processes in relevant cells. The disease causing mutational data generated in this project will be helpful in genetic counselling of patients and their families and screening of individuals at risk. Results of our experiments in cells and in zebrafish embryos will inform us of previously unknown disease mechanisms that can ultimately lead to better disease understanding and therapeutic interventions.

data.projectName: Silica based Nanoparticles as Hemostatic Agents for Controlling Internal Bleeding
data.projectDigest: The aim of the current project is to develop and evaluate cost effective, less toxic, more efficacious and stable nanomaterial based hemostatic agents for intravenous administration, in order to halt uncontrolled bleeding rapidly. Designing, preparation and evaluation of silica based nanoparticles, loaded with aprotinin, and encapsulated with a biocompatible polymer will be carried out. This formulation will be an alternative to the traditional topical dosage forms, such as gels and ointments, which cannot be used to stop internal bleeding. Nanomaterial based hemostatic agents will be formulated using various types of metals and biocompatible polymers, followed by their optimization and extensive characterization. In vitro drug release studies shall be performed, and mechanistic studies will be done. On the basis on ex vivo results, final formulation will be selected for further in vivo studies in animal models, including dose adjustment and determining chronic toxicity profile.

data.projectName: Exploring efficacy of gene editing in reversing the debilitating effects of ?-thalassemia
data.projectDigest: Beta (?)–thalassemia is one of the most significant hemoglobinopathy having 5% carriers in Pakistani population. There are more than 400 known point mutations within the ?-globin gene causing severe symptoms. However, ?-thalassemia symptoms can only appear after birth, as ?-globin is the predominant globin producing fetal hemoglobin (HbF) before birth. Moreover, there are inherited mutations at ?-globin promotor that result in increased expressions (20-30%) of HbF. These mutations have been advantageous by increasing the survival of adult sickle cell disease patients. Therapeutic reactivation of the fetal ?-globin gene is being considered as an ideal therapeutic option for ?-thalassemia patients. Recently a modified CRISPR/Cas 9 method, prime gene editing, has improved chances of getting only the edits the researchers want. The reduction in ‘off-target’ effects has made prime gene editing a safer and more applicable therapy. A single bp T>C mutation at -175 from transcriptional start site at ?-globin gene has been reported to increase the HbF levels up to 37%. Here, we propose to induce the -175 T>C mutation in ?-globin gene promotor by Prime gene editing. CD34+ Hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) from ?-thalassemia patients, will be edited for this point mutation to elevate ?-globin protein and functional HbF.
data.projectSummary: Beta (?)–thalassemia is one of the most significant hemoglobinopathy having 5% carriers in Pakistani population. There are more than 400 known point mutations within the ?-globin gene causing severe symptoms. However, ?-thalassemia symptoms can only appear after birth, as ?-globin is the predominant globin producing fetal hemoglobin (HbF) before birth. Moreover, there are inherited mutations at ?-globin promotor that result in increased expressions (20-30%) of HbF. These mutations have been advantageous by increasing the survival of adult sickle cell disease patients. Therapeutic reactivation of the fetal ?-globin gene is being considered as an ideal therapeutic option for ?-thalassemia patients. Recently a modified CRISPR/Cas 9 method, prime gene editing, has improved chances of getting only the edits the researchers want. The reduction in ‘off-target’ effects has made prime gene editing a safer and more applicable therapy. A single bp T>C mutation at -175 from transcriptional start site at ?-globin gene has been reported to increase the HbF levels up to 37%. Here, we propose to induce the -175 T>C mutation in ?-globin gene promotor by Prime gene editing. CD34+ Hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) from ?-thalassemia patients, will be edited for this point mutation to elevate ?-globin protein and functional HbF.

data.projectName: A novel environmental friendly rapid method development for metal ions determinations in micellar media
data.projectDigest:
Metals are very much important in biological and environmental studies. Metal ions like Fe(III), Cu(II), Mn(II) and Zn(II) are essential. Other metals like Cd, Hg, Ar and Pb are poisonous, above a certain concentration level. While, even the essential metals can be poisonous at too high concentration. Scientists have found that very small concentrations of certain poisonous metals can have profoundly detrimental harm on living beings. Different procedures are available for the determination of metals ions, including ICP-MS, ion chromatography, anodic stripping analysis and electro-thermal atomic absorption spectrometry. Many of these procedures are expensive, time taking and less sensitive so we are interested in developing rapid, convenient and sensitive procedure for the metal ions determination.
The metal-chelate complexes formed in the surfactant media are more stable, than those formed in the absence of surfactant. In the present project, rapid, sensitive and convenient simple procedure is proposed to the determination of metal ions at trace level using new complexing reagent in derivative mode and various surfactant systems. The procedure is simple, inexpensive and environmental friendly to the investigation of metal ions in different matrixes instead of the solvent extraction which is toxic and time consuming.

data.projectName: Neglect of Moral Development in Higher Education is Menace to Society: Bringing reforms is need of the time
data.projectDigest: Imparting moral education is the need of time, taking into account obvious moral decline in society. Recent research shows downfall of moral competence among university students. The main objective of the present study is to develop and implement moral development strategies for university students for individual and societal benefits. This study consist of three phases – planning, implementing, and evaluating. During planning phase, panel discussions with subject experts and focus group interviews with students and teachers will be conducted to explore what moral issues to use for guided reflection, dilemma discussion, integrated curriculum, and community service, to foster moral development. The number of sessions will depend on data saturation. Once the module is decided, these strategies will be implemented on university students (n = 500) and teachers (n = 200) during pretest-double posttest control group quasi-experimental design. Women participation will be maximized with rationale that they are agent of social and moral change. Four levels of moral development strategies will comprise four treatment groups for intervention to be compared against control group. It is hypothesized that students exposed to intervention will score high on posttest measure of moral competence than students in control group. During evaluation phase, the efficacy and effectiveness of intervention strategies will be assessed using randomized controlled trials (RCTs) with students (n = 1000). All data will be triangulated to refine the moral development strategies before a large scale application in higher education institutions. The modules developed will facilitate mature decision-making among university students and promote their citizenship.

data.projectName: Ecological adaptation of salt tolerant crop species to utilize saline water to sustain crop production in salt affected soils
data.projectDigest: Pakistan lies in arid to semi-arid region of the world with high temperature and low rain fall. The average annual precipitation during spring and winter is about 270 mm and vary from 600 to 800 mm in the mountainous zone, and 80-150 mm in the desert regions. Due to low rain fall and high temperature scarcity of water and salinity stress is becoming alarming issue in the field of agriculture. There is need to conserve water and soil in Pakistan for better Wheat-Cotton production.The production of these crops is declining with passage of time due to lack of good quality water and change in climatic conditions. The current work is planned to focus on the selection of available wheat and cotton genotypes to survive against salinity and water stress. These experiments will be conducted under control as well as in fields to study plant physiology both at root and shoot level with spatial and temporal experimentations for climate change impact assessment. Soil health indicators like organic matter, organic carbon and essential elements will be measured. The water conservation strategies like mulching, farm manures and crop residues will be used to improve water and soil healthduring salinity and water stress.

data.projectName: Mapping an in-depth genetic diversity of Infectious Bronchitis Virus (IBV) in Pakistan and development of serotype-matched recombinant IBV Vaccine
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: A sustainable growth of poultry in the country is persistently challenged by a number of infectious diseases such as infectious bronchitis (IB) that occurs frequently in their susceptible hosts (chicken) including the vaccinates. Owing to similar clinical picture with other respiratory viruses and limited disease diagnostics, disease remains misdiagnosed and/or under-reported where actual status of prevailing variant/s inconclusive. Current IB-related studies are limited to clinical evidences, seroconversion, and partial S1-gene based genotyping which is not conclusive enough to understand prevailing variants, and subsequently devise appropriate control strategies for IB particularly in terms of inclusion of appropriate variant/s in the vaccine regimens. Proposed translational research aims to 1) isolate and identify IBV from poultry-dense localities in Pakistan, 2) elucidate genomic nature of prevailing variants, 3) conduct challenge-protection experiment to determine the efficacy of currently used vaccines, and 4) development and evaluation of a novel reverse-genetics (CRISPR/Cas9)-based innovative vaccine. The proposed activities will be conducted in liaison with national and international institutes where molecular characterization of prevalent variants along with challenge-protection experiment will facilitate inclusion of suitable variants in the vaccine schedule while development of recombinant vaccine and its patent will be a step forward in devising novel interventions for control of infectious diseases.

data.projectName: Grain growth in three dimensional polycrystalline microstructures: A study on some complex problems at the  intersection of Geometry, Topology and Graph theory
data.piUniversity: Karakurum International University, Gilgit, Gilgit Baltistan
data.projectDigest: Cellular structures can be found in many natural systems from microscopic scale to macroscopic scale, including polycrystalline metals, soap foams and biological tissue. In many situations, the grain/cell/bubble walls move under the influence of their surface tension (capillarity), with a velocity proportional to their mean curvature. As a result, the grains evolve and the structure coarsens. Coarsening refers to the fact that some cells grow while others shrink and disappear. Understanding this process in any cellular structure contributes to controlling it and tailoring it for particular needs and applications. MacPherson and Srolovitz proposed a three-dimensional model that gives the rate of change of a cell volume in terms of simple geometrical quantities: the grain mean width and the total length of triple lines bounding the grain. However, applying this calculation to grain growth in polycrystals is somewhat suspect since it considers only geometrical properties of grains neglecting the topological changes associated with face creation and elimination that occur during grain growth. So the question is, does the theoretical result help us understand growth in real materials? Can it be taken as a starting point from which to develop more complex models? These are basic scientific questions with direct implications for real world materials. Making materials with desirable properties requires control over grain size and grain boundary type distributions. Gaining predictive control over these properties requires a detailed, verified model.  In this project, we are going to take into consideration both the geometrical properties and the topological changes, deriving a new grain growth equation  to describe the dynamics of 3D grain growth in polycrystalline structures.

data.projectName: Development of smart injectable bioactive glass for potential application in periodontal infection and infrabony defects
data.projectDigest: With an increase in demand of minimal invasive procedures, there is a noticeable increase in thrust for finding ways to develop biodegradable and thixotropic materials for bone regeneration in critical clinical situations like periodontitis (inflammation of periodontal tissue). Periodontitis is an infection that damages the soft tissues and destroys the hard tissues that support the teeth and leads to the loss of teeth and jaw bone. The existing remedies involve use of membranes, scaffolds and bone grafts which require massive surgical procedures. This study is based on the development of a novel injectable hydro-gel from biodegradable bioactive ceramic and organic polymer. This combination will use the bioactive and biodegradable property of its constituents. The end product will provide an alternate bone tissue substitute necessary to promote bone regeneration especially in infrabony defects of periodontitis. The resulting material will be characterized by different analytical techniques to evaluate the structural, physical and thermal properties. The bioactivity of the prepared injectable will be studied by soaking in simulated body fluid (SBF) for different time intervals while cytotoxicity will be studied by cell culture studies. The bone regeneration will be studied in rabbit model. These injectable materials can be directly injected into the bone cavity or bony defects and have maximum contact with all the surfaces. So they eliminate the risk of dead spaces, risk of infections and need of any complicated surgery.

data.projectName: Building up an Alternative Investment Market for SMEs: Challenges and Way Forward
data.piUniversity: National University of Modern Languages, Islamabad (NUML)
data.projectDigest: SMEs’ sector is the growth engine of Pakistan’s economy and contributes 40% of annual GDP of Pakistan. Similarly, there are approximately more than 3 Million SMEs in Pakistan which constitute nearly 90% of all the enterprises in Pakistan but there are nominal avenues for them to raise funds from capital market as well as financial market. In order to tackle such types of problems in UK, LSE launched AIM in 1995 which has captured 78% market share capital market by 2018. In this project, we would focus on three dimensions i.e. (a) why should AIM be initiated in Pakistan? (b) what kinds of legal and operational frameworks are required for AIM in Pakistan, (c) how AIM can be a sustainable primary and secondary market in Pakistan. We will deliberate upon legal and operational framework of AIM by conducting Focused Groups Discussions (FGDs), interviews and roundtables and consultation with SMEs and legal team of regulatory bodies in Pakistan as well as UK and in second part, we will focus on the valuation and short-run and long-run pricing performance of Initial Public Offering as well as market performance. This project would be completed in collaboration with PSX and Pace University US.

data.projectName: Evaluation of enhanced efficiency nitrogenous fertilizers for NH3 and N2O emissions in a rice-wheat cropping system on normal and marginal salt-affected soils
data.projectDigest: Use of nitrogenous fertilizers without any significant addition of organic inputs is depleting the soil organic matter and increasing nitrogen emissions rates particularly ammonia and nitrous oxide. In this project, existing conventional and enhanced efficiency nitrogenous fertilizers (EENFs) such as polymer coated urea, neem coated urea, bioactive nutrient fortified urea etc will be evaluated, firstly in an incubation study to estimate proposed N emissions on normal and marginally salt-affected soils. Based on the results of incubation study, some efficient EENFs will be further evaluated in lysimeter experiments under rice and wheat rotation in normal and salt-affected soils. The treatments will be applied to examine NH3 and N2O emissions and NO3- leaching losses from conventional N fertilizers; and EENFs with and without organic amendments (Biochar and compost) for onward measurement of Nitrogen Use Efficiency (NUE).  The promising EENFs and other treatments will finally be tested under field conditions. The outcome of the project will be identification of the best performing products (EENF), which are not only capable of enhancing yield but also capable of reducing N emissions. This project will entail activities aimed at disseminating the information generated by the research among the stakeholders (fertilizer industry, policy makers and farmers etc.).

data.projectName: School-wide Assessment and Intervention of Social, Behavioral and Emotional Problems of Secondary School Children and Development of Preventive Measures
data.projectDigest: A recent study (Lipson et al., 2017) provides most comprehensive evidence that the percentage of students with mental health diagnoses increased from 22% to 36%.  In Pakistan, society’s volume of social problems —including abuse, neglect, defiance, anger, intolerance, disrespect and interpersonal conflicts are spreading profusely into the schooling process at an alarming rate. Hence these complex issues need to be addressed at school level to create safe and healthy environment. The objectives of this project will be to make school-wide assessment of secondary school children for their social, behavioral and emotional problems. and intervene. Multi-tiered approach based on Response to Intervention (RtI) framework will be adopted Secondly, teachers will be trained to intervene with the help of training modules and thirdly, to design a preventive plan. Four model secondary schools will be selected for identification of students' social, emotional and behavioral patterns of malfunctioning. If there are mental health concerns, the assessment provides direction for behavioral management strategies. Teachers will be trained to address these challenges. On the basis of results prevention programs will be designed to assist students for their mild or transitory problems.   These Preventive interventions will be based on modifying risk exposure and strengthening the coping mechanisms of the students.

data.projectName: Climate Change Risk and Human Security: A Study of Selected Districts of Punjab
data.projectDigest: The proposed research aims to assess people’s perception about climate change risk and its impact on human security in the form of food, health and economic security in selected districts of Punjab province. Practically, indices of climate change risk (measured through people’s perception) and human security will be constructed that will be based on the information gathered through well-structured questionnaire from 500 household selected through purposive sampling from the districts of Rawalpindi, Sialkot, Lahore and Multan. These constructed indices will be used subsequently to estimate the impact of climate change risk on human security. As formation of perceptions regarding climate change is a long term phenomenon those households will be chosen for the survey who have been living in that area for at least last 20 years.  For the purpose of dissemination of information seminar is intended to be conducted in which officials from the Ministry of Climate Change, academicians and researchers will be invited. Moreover, a policy brief will also be formulated and disseminated for public in general and local and national authorities in particular with the purpose of helping in human and institutional capacity building regarding the adaptation and impact reduction regarding climate change. Furthermore, various awareness campaigns will be initiated to help sensitise and persuade people towards adoption of various adaptation strategies.

data.projectName: Control of  dengue fever epidemic by detecting dengue fever virus and insecticide resistance in local Aedes mosquito population
data.projectDigest:
Dengue incidences have been reported from the big cities of Punjab including Sargodha division.   There are chances of dengue fever epidemics. Chemical insecticides especially pyrethroids have been used extensively for the control of mosquitoes once the dengue fever patients recorded from an area. The abundant use of chemical insecticides leads to resistance to chemical insecticides. The phenomenon of resistance in mosquitoes threatens the vector control.  There is a dire need to detect the presence of virus in mosquito population before the onset of dengue epidemics and chemical spray. 
Mosquito larvae and adult will be collected from at union council level from District Sargodha. The larvae and adults will be identified in laboratory. The female adult mosquito population will be subjected to the dengue virus detection. The areas having population with dengue virus will be highlighted and communicated to health department for fogging. Bioassay of field collected dengue mosquito larvae will be performed against insecticides (pyrethroids and organosphosphate (temephos)) used for mosquito control to detect the level of resistance in local population by comparing the toxicity of Collected larvae with the susceptible larvae (susceptible strain from LECA).  Overall, this research will help to forecast the dengue epidemics and make a rational decision to use larvi-and-adulticide.

data.projectName: Ethnobotany of Cholistan: toward rangeland management through indigenous knowledge
data.projectDigest:
Cholistan desert possess a great botanical diversity of xerophytic plants and hosting nomadic human tribes from centuries. These are pasoralists and animal keepers. They are very much concerned with the wild vegetation for forage, food and medicine for their livestock and also for their own. They are also naturalists and have keeping tremendous knowledge of their wild ecosystems and its management. It’s all their valuable ancient knowledge which they have gathered through generations to survive with animals and plants from centuries. Unique indigenous herbal diversity, traditional therapeutic use recipes and pastoral economy of the desert make it more important to explore and preserve its flora for alternative income source. Indigenous knowledge of range vegetation management is not only helpful in improving sustainable animal productivity but may also be significant in biodiversity conservation and household food security.
Mostly management and conservation of range vegetation is focused to restrict that area from local community. It minimizes the potential forage source for livestock and limiting income source for local inhabitants. Therefore a range resource management program based on indigenous knowledge of local inhabitants will be more fruitful. Further, exploring medicinally important plants from folklores and their phytochemical verification will not only diversify livelihood options from pastoralisms to herbalism but may also helpful in indigenous vegetation conservation and understanding. It will be a locally developed range resource management plan addressing the whole desert ecosystem by opting medicinal plant trade another livelihood source. So, the prime objective of this proposed study is to document indigenous knowledge of local communities about enviro

data.projectName: Next Level Mutation Testing: Do Fewer, Do Smarter, and Do Faster
data.projectDigest: Today, our modern society heavily relies on software. In fact, we cannot imagine a world without software. Software, at low level, is computer code / instructions for the computer to follow. Software developers write those instructions to implement the working software. However, they can make mistakes while writing those instructions. Therefore, they also test the software for any errors so that it can be delivered error free to its users. On the other hand, software is delivered to its users very fast nowadays. For example, every day we see new software updates for our mobile apps. To deliver software at such fast pace, software developers automate the testing process by writing another set of instructions (referred to as test suite) to test the software. Since the test suite is also the computer instructions written by developers, developers might also make mistakes in writing those test suites. Then, the question arises how do developers test the tests? Mutation testing is a technique widely used to assess the effectiveness of test suites. data.projectName: Genetic Improvement of Common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris) from Azad Jammu and Kashmir using Marker Assisted Breeding Techniques for Cultivar Development
data.piUniversity: University of Kotli Azad Jammu and Kashmir
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is facing serious problems to feed its growing population. Climate change and water scarcity have put question mark on food security and sustainability. The economic circumstances are not very promising while the expenditure in imports puts more pressure on economy. Common bean (Phaseolus vulagris) commonly known as Red Lobia is one of the pulses being imported, despite of its production potential and consumption in Pakistan.  The crop has been ignored and there is not a single improved cultivar available in Pakistan for farmers. The yield is not promising and farmers utilize the seeds of their own harvest from decades. Common bean is 3rd major crop of Azad Jammu and Kashmir after maize and wheat being grown in different agro climatic conditions and altitudes ranging from 1200 to 9000 feet from sea level.  Present project is proposed for genetic improvement of common bean germplasm from AJ&K through marker assisted breeding for improved yield and nutrition. The land races (200) of crop will be collected from AJ%K and their agronomic performance will be evaluated. The nutritional analysis and molecular characterization will help in hybridization of selected genotypes for cultivar development. This project will help in evolution of improved bean variety.

data.projectName: Seismic Assessment & Retrofitting of a Major Hospital in Karachi
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
A severe earthquake is one of nature’s most terrifying and devastating events, resulting in widespread destruction. Apart from huge economic and social disruption, such events also have a sudden and massive impact on the health status of the population affected. Experience from past earthquakes throughout the world clearly shows that the health facilities in the affected area are the key to launching an immediate response.
Knowing Karachi is the hub of economic and commercial activities of Pakistan and since Karachi is located near the tri-junction of tectonic plates. With nearly 20 Million population (7th largest megacity of the world), having insufficient healthcare facilities, it becomes imperative that an immediate Seismic Assessment of major hospitals in Karachi are carried out, given the importance for an efficient response to emergencies and the need for a functional health care infrastructure in the aftermath of a disaster.
To the researcher’s knowledge, there is no previous study, to evaluate the seismic performance of hospitals in Karachi. This research is to set forth the basis and will be beneficial to the disaster management agencies of the country that will allow them to develop useful information regarding evacuation maps, seismic retrofitting decisions, disaster response planning, etc.

data.projectName: Treatment of Poultry Diarrhea with Environment-Friendly Natural Substances: An Innovative and Cost-effective Solution for Gizzard Ulceration induced by Mycotoxins and Bacillus cereus in Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Poultry industry is a successful story of agriculture in Pakistan. Its annual growth is 8-10 percent annually which reflects its inherent potential. Annual poultry meat production is about 1276 metric tons which contributes more than 31% of total meat production in the country. In field conditions different imported mycotoxin binding substances are used in the feeds to avoid mycotoxins problem in poultry. All the components of such products present in Pakistan in excessive quantity at negligible prices but unluckily these are not being used as mycotoxin binding agents. Under field conditions imported toxin binding agents are incorporated in the feeds to avert the deleterious effects of mycotoxins in poultry. These toxin binding agents invariably comprise of clays (Bentonites. Zeolites), Yeast or their cell wall components, and/or some herbal products. These are imported from European countries, USA and Latin American countries. All these materials are present in Pakistan in rich quantity at negligible prices but unfortunately are not being used as toxin binding agents. A huge amount of national money is invested on the import of these products. About 7-10 billion rupees are spent annually on the import of feed additives and toxin binders to reducing the losses in feed in poultry feed manufacturing. Currently average price of good quality imported mycotoxins binders varies from 700 PKR/Kg (6 USD) in Pakistan to 50 RMB(7USD) in China. All these materials are present in Pakistan in rich quantity at negligible prices but unfortunately are not being used as toxin binding agents. Local Good quality mycotoxins binder will be available @ 150-200 PKR/Kg (1-1.5 USD).

data.projectName: Synthesis and characterization of metal decorated high surface area porous sodiumaluminosilicate and aluminotitanates for environmental control and energy security
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
Currently, fuel cell vehicles, sold and manufactured through several different companies like Hyundai, Honda and Toyota. They practice 70 MPa compacted hydrogen storage which is quickly fetching the customary of industry. By storing hydrogen at this pressure requires costly cylinder-shaped carbon fiber fused tanks. Significant energetic expenses together with geometrical restrictions and economic costs are related with compressing hydrogen and supplying to storing tank. During quick filling, thermal effects from is enthalpic expansion mean that hydrogen need to be precooled at about -40 oC to avoid overheating, that additionally rises the energy consequences that is related by using hydrogen at high pressure. Thus emerging low pressure, low cost substitutive methods for storing hydrogen remains aim for long term. 
Physiosorptionaly storing hydrogen in higher surface area nanoporous materials at low pressures with adsorbents likewise Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs) displays significant potential in this respect. In comparison to utmost other solid state storing methods, hydrogen physiosorption is also fast and fully reversible and in comparison to chemisorption.
The present research project is mainly focused to overcome the current challenges of hydrogen storage. It is believed that the strategy of incorporation of hydrogen permeable transition metals into high surface area porous zeolite will effectively improve its storage capability.

data.projectName: Investigation of Quantum Transport in Topological Insulators
data.piUniversity: Kohat University of Science and Technology, Kohat
data.projectDigest:
Topological insulators (TIs) is a new class of quantum matter with an energy band gap in the bulk and gapless electronic conducting states on the surface. These surface gapless helical states are protected by time-reversal symmetry where the spins of carriers are orthogonally locked to their translational momenta, causing suppression of back scattering by disorders/impurities. Because of the robust gapless helical conducting surface states, TIs have attracted a lot of attention in fundamental physics and triggered potential applications in spintronics, Josephson junctions, nanoscale transport devices, topological quantum computation, topological insulator field-effect transistors, and many others. 
In view of the intriguing magnetic properties exhibited by the Dirac fermions of TIs, this project will focus on investigating the ballistic transport properties of Dirac fermions on the surface of a three-dimensional (3D) topological insulators (TIs) attached to a spiral multiferroic oxides (SMO).  In particular, applying the formalism of quantum mechanics, we will focus on the investigation of the following effects that arise due to the coupling of spin degrees of freedom of TIs with the proximity-induced exchange field of SMO:
  (i) To study the spin-dependent wave packet transport on the surface of 3D TI attached to SMO.
 (ii) To investigate the quantum Brownian motion of Dirac fermions in the system.
(iii) To explore the nonlinear effects in the transport of Dirac fermions.  
(iv) To find the ratcheting effects of the Dirac fermions.
 (v) To study the conductivity in the quantum regime using Kubo formalism.
The potential applications of this research project are expected in spintronics such as spin-valves, magnetic tunnel junctions, spin filters, and so on.

data.projectName: Synthesis of Hexagonal Boron Nitride Nanostructures for its Potential Applications in Biomedical and Nuclear Feeding
data.piUniversity: University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Muzaffarabad, Azad Kashmir, Muzaffarabad
data.projectDigest: Nanomaterials of hexagonal boron nitride (Nanotubes, Nanowires, nanosheets, nanofibers, microtubes, and micro-flakes, etc. ) have superb physical, mechanical and chemical properties suitable for a range of potential applications in the field of neutron sensing (solid-state detectors), bio-medical and microelectronics mechanical systems (MEMs), etc. Being a wideband gape (~ 6 eV) semiconductor with larger cross-section (3840b) for thermal neutron, BNNS has the potential to be used as a sensing element in solid-state neutron detectors for higher detection efficiency. In addition, these nanostructures are second (2nd) generation materials with highly non-toxic nature and excellent biocompatibility. These properties have made it an excellent choice for a variety of potential applications in the field of bio-medical including Boron-neutron capture therapy, hyperthermia, and targeted drug delivery, etc. Thus the project will deal with the synthesis and characterization of different h-BN nanostructures. The as-synthesized nanostructures after characterization will be tested for its potential application.

data.projectName: Nation-wide Sequencing and Characterization of the Pakistani Gut Microbiome
data.projectDigest: The human microbiota includes microorganisms that reside on multiple human body sites such as the skin, gut, and oral cavity. The human-associated microorganisms play beneficial roles in human health such as helping in food digestion and regulating our defense response. Numerous microbiome-sequencing projects have already been completed worldwide and efforts have moved from their basic description to use in therapeutics. Pakistan, however, has lagged behind in this race. Here, we will build on our expertise in microbiome sequencing to screen 200 "healthy" participants from across the country and characterize their microbiome via metagenomics, next generation sequencing, and bioinformatics approaches. We will compare the healthy Pakistani and Western microbiota and identify bacterial groups either over- or under-represented in the Pakistani gut and link these associations to our health. The healthy microbiome will thus help us identify the role of local diet and social norms in shaping our gut microbial communities and their possible associations to health. This work is expected to gauge the interest of local industry to develop microbiome-centric therapies such as microbiota transplant to treat metabolic diseases. This project will serve as reference for several follow-up studies and open new doors of investigation in microbiology research in the country.

data.projectName: Urdu Literary Research: Use of Digital Resources, Methodology and Terminology
data.piUniversity: Lahore College for Women University, Lahore
data.projectDigest:
Early patterns of literary research in Urdu began to emerge in 18th century. Then researcher mostly took their task according to their individual interests, guided by their self-established rules and patterns.Till the end of 20th century, in almost two hundred years, Urdu literary research has crossed many important mile stones. Many research manuals are available now for new researchers to maintain both the uniformity and standards. Researchers today, are having an opportunity to reach out to a lot of digital libraries, E Journals, J store, E books, Digital archives, Scanned files of documents, Micro files of old texts, E newspapers, web papers, Digital sections of world’s largest and most important libraries e.g. British library London and Bodleian libraries oxford, and what not.
Unfortunately Urdu literary Research is ineffectively lacking proper tools, terminology and procedural details to benefits this huge, rather biggest yet easily accessible source of information. This inadequacy of Urdu literary Research can be addressed with the establishment of digital research manual, with newer set of terminology and methods to provide the researchers a way to improve and enhance their ability individually and more.

data.projectName: Synthesis of New Aromatase Inhibitors through Bio-Catalytic, and Conventional Synthetic Approaches-Drug Leads for Breast Cancer
data.projectDigest: Aromatase is the key enzyme in the estrogen synthesis, and its inhibition has been validated as key approach for hormone (estrogen) receptor positive (HR +ve) breast cancer. Breast cancer is one of the deadliest, and the second most common cancer across the world. In Asia, Pakistan has the highest rate of breast cancer, usually one in nine women develops carcinoma of breast in some stages of their life. About 70-80% of all newly diagnosed breast cancer are positive for estrogen receptor. Inhibition of aromatase in breast cancer (HR +ve) patients decrease the supply of estrogen to tumor cells and thus reduce its proliferation and growth. In post-menopausal women or women with reduced or with eliminated ovarian function aromatase inhibition is the key target for treating breast cancer. During the current research proposal new and novel structural analogues of available steroidal aromatase inhibitors will be synthesized by green chemistry. The fully characterized new analogues of existing aromatase inhibitors will be evaluated for their aromatase inhibitory potential. The active compounds will be further evaluated against human breast cancer HR+ve cell lines, and also against human normal cell line. Compounds with potent inhibitory potential against aromatase, and non-cytotoxic effects may exhibit better profiles in comparison to available drugs, and thus can serve as lead molecules for the development of new and safe aromatase inhibitors for the treatment of hormone-dependent breast cancer.

data.projectName: Value addition and Standardization of Moringa oleifera for     export
data.projectDigest: Moringa based products (such as food supplements, cosmetics, skin and hair care products) are very high in demand in the developed world. Moringa cultivation has a great impact on nutrition, health, agriculture, water, sanitation, biodiversity, environment and finally on the economy of our country. Despite multiple uses of Moringa, in Pakistan this tree is still underutilized. Therefore, it is planned to promote Moringa production on large scale for research and value addition and subsequently for commercialization. Quality control and standardization of Moringa based products is prerequisite of export. Standardization (chemical and biological) has a great impact on quality of finished product. Sheer chemical standardization of herbs is not sufficient for therapeutically active formulation. Therefore, biological standardization will also be employed for establishing clinical efficacy of plant-based products. Thus, attention will be focused to do some dedicated efforts to strengthen Moringa research in vast area of Cholistan desert to fully explore its potential, quality and finally to step in successful entrepreneurship of Moringa agribusiness.

This research will provide an  opportunity to the local students/scholars to get practical exposure in the field of archaeology and ancient genomics and  promote multidisciplinary research within Pakistani archaeology by integrating ancient genomics.

Results of the molecular analysis of the human remains will help to  reconstruct the demography and health trajectory of the local population. The genomic data obtained can be further used to trace ancient infectious diseases, which may be helpful in the field of disease evolution and immunology

data.projectName: The strain induced modulation of optical properties 2D materials for next generation flexible electronic and photonic devices
data.projectDigest: In the present proposal, 2D layers will be synthesized on various substrates to determine the strain in the synthesized SL caused by the lattice mismatch, particularly on ultra-thin Si substrates (30-50 ?m). In addition, external disturbances will also be employed to produce strain like irradiating with high energy ions, exposure to acoustic waves, etc. The rearrangement of atoms of the 2D material will be studied in detail computationally and its effect on electronic band structure using Raman spectroscopy and low temperature photoluminescence spectroscopy. Transmission electron microscopy and ambient scanning probe microscopy will be employed to study the surface reconstruction and electronic band structure in the vicinity of defects.  In addition, density functional theory (DFT) with combined with kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) techniques will be employed to model the growth of 2D layer and effect of strain on the electronic and optical properties of strained 2D layers. Pressure sensors, polarization dependent photodetectors and gas sensors will be fabricated using strained 2D layers.

data.projectName: Unraveling the signaling network of CLE peptides (CLE9 and CLE25) linked to cysteine biosynthesis pathway in ABA-mediated stomatal closure in Arabidopsis thaliana
data.projectDigest: Global warming is one of the major causes of frequently changing in the weather to more extreme condition that leads to drought, low humidity and high temperature. Being immobile in nature, plants encounter large fluctuations upon the onset of these abiotic stresses that leads to massive agricultural losses and improving crop tolerance is a major goal of plant scientists to ensure global food security. Plants induce physiological response to environmental signals by regulation of stomatal aperture via ABA production which is well characterized signal to minimize water loss. Dramatic progress has been made over the last years and the molecular mechanism of many pathways has been revealed that regulate the balance between growth and acclimation. One of the important progresses is the discovery of small peptide CLE25 that acts as a long distance signal and helps in stomatal closure and stress response. More recently, the identification of sulfate and/or cysteine in ABA mediated stomatal closure might also mount an effective defense against abiotic stresses. Advancement in the functional genomics, loss-of-function mutant is considered as a powerful tool to explore the potential function of genes. We propose to further elucidate the signaling network between the CLE9 and CLE25 peptides and cysteine biosynthesis pathway in stomatal closure where different mutant lines of the sulfur assimilation pathway (among them oastlB, serat2;1, sir1;1, sultr3 Quintuple) and also ABA impaired mutants such as nced3, aba2, aba3 and aao3 will be analyzed.  Thus, the identification of signaling network in the proposed study will help to explore the role and biological relevance of CLE9 and CLE25 peptides with cysteine biosynthesis pathway in stomatal closure in Arabidopsis thaliana.

data.projectName: Fabrication of flexible dye-sensitized solar cells based on textile coated with carbon nanocomposite as counter electrode material
data.piUniversity: Mehran University of Engineering & Technology, Jamshoro
data.projectDigest:
Demand for energy and its resources, is increasing with every passing day due to fast outgrowth of population and urbanization. Fossil fuels make up to 80% of global energy production and these conventional energy (petroleum, natural gas and coal) resources are at the verge of getting extinct . Solar energy  is considered as a potent replacement for fossil fuel and is one of most abundant and readily available energy source .
The devices that transform sunlight in to electricity are known as PV cells or solar cells. Dye sensitized solar cells (DSSC) is one of the newer PV cells  that has global attention  among solar energy research groups due to its easy fabrication technique, low cost, and environmental sustainability [4].
According to our hypothesis, Different carbon nano composite such as carbon nano tubes, activated charcoal, graphite, graphene can be considered as a potential candidate for the electrocatalytic layer for DSSC CE.  Graphite is known for its excellent conductivity, good chemical stability, and low cost availability[6]. With the addition of some porous materials in to the graphitic composite, its electrocatalytic activity can be enhanced. The inclusion of porous materials in to graphitic matrix will create defect rich morphologies, taht play a crucial role in charge tranfer and hence generate electricity. Similarly, the highly conductive carbon based (MWCNT, activated carbon, graphene) coated on flexible substrate (PET sheet, fabric) can be used to enhance the electron transport at the counter electrode and can be used for energy harvesting. We believe that, our proposed Textile-integrated electrodes for flexible DSSCs structure will demonstrate highly efficient, and sustainable low cost photovoltaic device.

data.projectName: Improving Groundwater Aquifer by Spatio-temporal Assessment of Groundwater Recharge Potential in Water Scarce Areas of Rechna Doab
data.projectDigest: In Pakistan, the surface water resources are unable to meet the requirement of crops water. Due to scarcity of surface irrigation water agriculture has been shifting on the groundwater. Groundwater is contributing up to 60% for raising of agriculture in Pakistan. In rice growing areas it is contributing up to 70% of crop production. Watertable is declining with time and threatening to the irrigated agriculture and food security of the country. Since management of aquifer system in accordance to recharge potential could be very beneficial to meet the alarming condition of water scarcity. Due to lack of groundwater research in Pakistan, this study will focus on the groundwater recharge potential specifically in Rechna Doab. For this real time groundwater monitoring system will be installed in problematic study area. Scarcity of groundwater potential information is another dilemma of current time for this groundwater modeling will be performed for estimation of current and future potential of groundwater in problematic area. This research study will help for delineation of areas of potential recharge and formulation of stratifies for judicial use of groundwater recharge in future. Results from these research calibrated models would be highly beneficial to address the existing and future groundwater problems.

data.projectName: Transforming the Conventional Supply chain management to BlockChain Based Digital Supply Chain Management: A Study of Pakistan’s Oil And Gas Industry
data.projectDigest: A huge chunk of the cost in  Oil and Gas industry of Pakistan is incurred due to the limited capacity of traditional supply chain management. This  study aims to propose strategies to transform the traditional supply chain on an alternative and modern supply chain ,which is termed as block chain based digital supply chain(BCBDSC). Due to its capacity to have high degree of traceability, visibility and verfiability, The BCB digital supply chains are considered as the most efficient and effective. This study will identify the challenges in the way of transforming the conventional supply chains to the BCB digital supply chains and will devise appropriate strategies to help firm for this effective transformation. In doing so , research will also focus on highlighting the major limitation and strengths of conventional supply chain in Oil and Gas industry of Pakistan. This will help to devise better strategies for transformation.  The study predominantly depends upon the experts surveys and analysis of extant literature.

data.projectName: Development of Vision-Based Insect Flight Tracking Environment for Flight Performance Estimation of Perching & Prey-Predator Maneuvers
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest:
With every passing day, the role of miniature air vehicles (drones) is gaining importance in the security domain.  Considering the competitive advantage that small drones offer, imagine the gains achieved by having micro/nano scale drones. Although challenging, it is possible to detect the small scale drones and counter act against them. Detecting a micro/nano scale raises the surveillance bar. However, designing aerodynamics and kinematics at tiny scales is an open research problem. 

One way of designing micro air vehicles is by mimicking flying insects. Insects (house-fly, honey bees, locusts) perform amazing manuevers with precision and speed. Bio-inspired aerodynamics is an active area of research.  So far studies involving flying insects have either been done manually, which is time consuming process, making long term observation difficult. On the other hand, automatic insect tracking methods consider insect as a point mass.  The role of different body parts in generating a complex motion (take off, perching) is missing in these studies. The aim of this project is to track numerous parts of the flying insect using a video camera.
There are two major developments which have made such insect observation possible. Firstly the current deep learning based computer vision methods have shown robust tracking of different parts of multiple humans. Inspired by these automatic human tracking methods we plan to track multiple parts of flying insects. Secondly, the advent of affordable slow motion cameras allow capturing the wing movements of flying insects. Flying bugs move their wings with a very high frequency. Standard cameras were unable to capture these wing movements.  We want to combine these two major developments to design flying insect tracking system.

data.projectName: Development and Performance Evaluation of hierarchical nanocomposites for harsh environments
data.projectDigest:
Polymers are of great interest for their low-density, good processability and reasonable cost. They are being used extensively in most of the important applications such as packaging materials, coatings, transparent, optical, biological and medical materials except structural ones where high strength is the major requirement. However, this limitation can be overcome by incorporation of reinforcing fibres into the polymers to make composites. 
This project attempts to design and fabricate a new class of high strength composite materials that should both be extremely resistant to chemicals and capable of withstanding intense situations with extreme fluctuation in temperatures and pressures as well, like air jets, marine ships, submarines and when subjected to oil field applications, for instance in risers for exploitation of oil deposits. 
Conventional fibres and CNTs can be combined to develop a structural material hopefully, with both the superior mechanical, environmental and chemical performance, and significantly reduced service life costs. Although preparation of polymer composites is vastly progressing, however, the preparation of hierarchical composites, with envisaged exceptional mechanical performance, is still a great challenge. It is aimed to study a suitable way to make the hierarchical composites with improved fracture toughness along with superior mechanical, electrical and thermal properties.

data.projectName: Development of advanced pro-angiogenic wound dressings for  patients in Pakistan with diabetic ulcers and burns injuries
data.projectDigest:
Around 15% of diabetic patients will develop difficult to heal ulcers on their feet or lower legs. Diabetes damages the ability of the body to form new blood vessels so delays normal wound healing.. Failure to heal can often progress to amputation.  There are also high numbers of patients in Pakistan with superficial or partial burns-here the challenge is to stimulate new blood vessel formation to ensure rapid wound healing. For both there is a need to develop a simple effective dressing which can be easily applied to stimulate wound healing
We have assembled a collaborative Pakistan/UK team to translate our patented research on using a small natural sugar to stimulate new blood vessel formation and wound healing into an advanced wound healing dressing that will benefit many thousands of patients within Pakistan.To achieve this we will work with a dressing that is well accepted for clinical use in Pakistan-wax coated cotton dressings produced by Cotton Craft Pvt Ltd and used in all major burn centers in Pakistan. Cotton Craft have committed to support this programme and work with us and our clinical innovator champions to develop these as wound care products for Pakistan and other developing countries.

data.projectName: Investigation in Advanced Energy Harvesters and Energy Storage Devices for Self-powered Flexible Energy Systems
data.projectDigest: The problem under focus, which is applied and interdisciplinary in nature, lies at the heart of energy storage systems. In this project, intrinsically flexible organic materials will be designed, synthesized and applied to develop the flexible  supercapacitor (SC) devices for subsequent energy storage applications. While creating the molecular design, process strategies such as introducing side chains, utilizing the interactions of hydrogen bond to increase flexibility, or designing three-dimensional network-like structures will be considered. The results of such study will be helpful to figure out relationships between molecular structures and their intrinsic flexibility as well as capacitance. High performance materials will be applied to fabricate flexible supercapacitor devices, which will undergo some rigorous in-situ mechanical, electronic and electrochemical tests. Prototype devices including sandwich structure, planar structure and fibre structure will be exploited for energy electronics regimes. SC technology developed in this project will be integrated with flexible photovoltaic modules to achieve the functionality of self-power. For the fabrication of the so-called flexible self-charging power pack (FSPP), various flexible SC modules (connected in series) will be connected to flexible cell, through a power management board. This board will allow to optimize both the performance of the energy harvested by the PV cell and charging of the SCs. Finally, the FSPP will be connected to the wearable pH sensors to certify the continuous monitoring of glucose levels without the use of external batteries or human intervention. The number of SC cells and PV modules will depend on the power consumption of the pH sensing technology. These devices will achieve high energy-storage ability even under high flexibility and expected to yield a great potential in wearable electronics in the near future.

data.projectName: The bifacial field effect passivation of dielectric AlOx/SiNx stacks in PERC solar cells for improved performance
data.projectDigest: Harnessing energy from the sun, which emits immensely powerful energy from the center of the solar system, is one of the key targets for achieving a sustainable energy supply. Light energy can be converted directly into electricity using electrical devices called solar cells. According to the Fraunhofer report 2019, c-silicon wafer based PV technology has worldwide share of production of about 95 % in 2017. The current project is focusing on fabrication of solar cells with high efficiency and low cost/watt. This project will be under the title “The bifacial field effect passivation of dielectric AlOx /SiNx stacks in PERC solar cells for improved performance”. The objective of this work is to fabricate silicon solar cell by using surface passivation with certain dielectric stacks both on front and rear of PERC solar cell. The effect of field effect passivation is to reduce the surface recombination velocity. The dielectric layer enhances the solar cell ability to capture sun light. The solar cells are characterized in terms of cost / watt. Current solar cell technology strongly relies on the silicon. The cost/watt of silicon solar cell based technology is being pushed continuously to achieve the non-renewable based electricity cost/watt. The journey from solar cells to solar modules have many applications from house hold lighting to offshore oil drilling as well as from industry to agriculture.

data.projectName: ICRG:  Development of Nanomaterials based Tactile Sensors for Tele-Manipulation in Robotic Surgery
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Recent advancements in medical robotics have minimized most of the limitations related to open and minimally invasive surgery (MIS). The MIS procedure requires surgeon to manipulate the slender surgical instruments and at the same time view video on a 2D screen. This results in disruption of natural hand-eye coordination and requires rigorous training. The advancements in robotic precision and computer-enhanced technology lead to minimally invasive robotic surgery (MIRS) procedure which allow surgeon to manipulate surgical instrument through tele-manipulators or computer control. The main limitations of both MIS and MIRS procedures is that the surgeon does not get any sense how hard is the interaction of surgical instrument with  tissue during the surgical procedure.  The state-of the art commercially available robots for MIRS procedures like Da Vinci from Intuitive Surgical Inc. USA, even lack  tactile sensing capabilities. In this project, we aim to develop both ZnO nanowires and MEMS based tactile sensors for force and vibration measurements, vibrotactile actuators for the tactile displays and miniaturized accelerometer for the evaluation of the vibrations produced by vibrotactile actuators. This project will demonstrate possible potential of the micro and nanotechnology in greatly improving the current tele-manipulation systems based tactile sensing for the robotic surgery.

data.projectName: Archaeology and Heritage of the British Period in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa
data.projectDigest: This project will record and analyse the archaeology of the British Period in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, and where appropriate draw on historical sources from local and European sources.  The archaeology and material culture of the British Period in Pakistan is little studied, and there is a wealth of material that can be used to explore issues of interaction between the military and local communities, of subversion and resistance, and of the lasting legacy (or otherwise) of this period on society in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa.  By recording the remains of different aspects of British Period activity in the region, such as urban layout and the construction of cantonments, cemeteries, landscapes of British military activity and conflict such as pickets, battle sites and barracks, changes to transport and communication such as railways, bridges, roads and canals, a major data set will be generated that can be analysed in different ways and on different scales in order to understand more about nature of the British Period here and how it differs from better studied places such as central India

By recording the remains of different aspects of British Period activity in the region, such as urban layout and the construction of cantonments, cemeteries, landscapes of British military activity and conflict such as pickets, battle sites and barracks, changes to transport and communication such as railways, bridges, roads and canals, a major data set will be generated that can be analysed in different ways and on different scales in order to understand more about nature of the British Period here and how it differs from better studied places such as central India

data.projectName: Diagnostic, prognostic and predictive biomarkers for oral squamous cell carcinoma
data.projectDigest:
Oral cancer is the second most common cancer in Pakistan. Although oral cancer is common in Pakistan but the available published work is limited. Most of the published work is in local journals focusing on basic aspects of oral cancer with reporting of merely frequencies and percentages.
We plan to conduct a follow up study with the potential of improving the management strategies of oral cancer in Pakistan through early detection and provision of tailored treatment options for each patient. 
Through follow-up clinical studies (upto 5 years), we plan to develop contextual guidelines for surgical and medical management of patients with oral cancer.
Moreover, we plan to understand the biology of oral cancer through investigating changes at the molecular level using a technique called “Next Generation Sequencing (NGS)”. Understanding disease biology is important for identifying new molecular targets for treatment purposes.
Analysis of NGS data is challenging. We plan to produce an analysis plan for NGS data through artificial intelligence. 
The proposed project has the potential to address two thematic priority areas “medical and allied health sciences” and “artificial intelligence”.
This project would involve experts from the field of medicine, engineering, biological sciences and multinational companies.

data.projectName: Deforestation in Pakistan: Combating through Wireless Sensor Networks (DePWiSeN)
data.piUniversity: Balochistan University of Information Technology, Engineering and Management Sciences,Quetta
data.projectDigest:
Forest decline can effectively be reduced by restricting the human activities (cutting trees, mining, etc.) and improving tree health. The manual real-time monitoring of the forest and to prevent unauthorized activities and observe plant health/soil condition is practically unattainable.

In this proposal, we aim to design a wireless sensor network (WSN) based solution to combat deforestation in Pakistan. Balochistan province, where Juniper and Pine Nut forests, which have an economic share of 2-4% towards the provincial GDP through timber and dry fruit industry, are officially declared under threat [9,10], would be taken as a case study.

The proposed system will be low-cost, autonomous, real-time monitoring and response system. It would be a true implementation of Internet-of-Things having three key elements: 1) wireless sensors to monitor heat/smoke for fire detection, noise/vibration to detect unauthorized tree cutting, nano-sensors for tree heath; 2)  Monitoring and Data Acquisition Centre; 3) Response unit (drones, water sprinklers, CO2 cylinders). This system will ensure continuous monitoring of the forests and timely response to counter an unauthorized human activity, fire and tree health degradation.

data.projectName: Olfactory Response and Host Plant Feeding Preferences of Desert Locust to Common Plants in Punjab Province of Pakistan
data.projectDigest: LLocusts are among the most dangerous and cross-continental agricultural pests worldwide. A large swarm can eat up to 1.8 million metric tons of green vegetation, equivalent to food enough to feed 81 million people. The locust control is critical to food security worldwide and requires multidimensional approaches to combat this issue. Recently, locust outbreaks strike Pakistan, around 300,000 square kilometers of farmland is vulnerable to the locust outburst. While some locust control systems are still curative, and the socioeconomic consequences of locust outbreaks have led to an increasing paradigm shift from crop protection to preventive management. This project leads to understand the fundamental to applied aspects by employing nonpreferred plant volatile extracts, entomopathogenic fungi (EPF), courtship inhibitory pheromones, acoustic avoidance communication, olfactory communication, and nanoparticle embedded biopesticides. These experiments will be performed in the laboratory, semi-field, and field and expected to the development of eco-friendly nanoparticle embedded biopesticides and predatory ultrasonic/neuro wave transmitters. Finally, the outcomes of this project will provide a strong basis in effective preventive management strategy that relies on an improved knowledge of the pest ecology, behavior, electrophysiology, acoustic anti-predatory behavior, and locust management in Pakistan that ultimately leads towards the development of efficient control strategies

data.projectName: Enhancement of global competitiveness of Pakistani textile export value-chains by capacity building and product diversification (KnowTex)
data.projectDigest:
Being the largest organized, export oriented industrial sector, the role of textile industry is very crucial in economy of Pakistan. This sector is contributing 58% (13.56 B USD) in exports and provides employment to more than 35% of the workforce. During the last ten (10) years, the growth in Pakistan’s textile exports was 28%, whereas the textile exports of Bangladesh (36.6 B USD) increased by 177%, Vietnam (36.16 B USD) by 256%, India (37.01 B USD) by 64% and China (266.5 B USD) by 48%.  
The slow growth in textile sector is badly affecting the overall exports, current account deficit and new employment generation. The biggest challenge for Government during the recent past was to increase (double/ Textile Policy 2014-19) the textile exports but could not succeed. Lack of innovation, product diversification, value addition, low productivity, absence of Pakistani brands in global market and inconsistent government policies are the main reasons of failure. 
The main objective of this project is “the transformation of textile sector to knowledge-based industry for enhancing its global competitiveness through capacity building, product diversification and innovation”. 
The project is divided into 8 work packages: exploration of high value indigenous natural fibers, development of value-added textiles from Baluchi wool, transformation of textile industry to manmade fibers’-based textiles, indigenous development of novel & high-end textiles, and capacity Building and showcasing capacity of industry on an online portal.
This project will help to improve the global competitiveness of Pakistan’s textile exports and lay foundation of a knowledge-based textile industry.
