data.projectName: Tackling food security by controlling ticks and tick-borne diseases in bovines
data.piUniversity: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore
data.projectDigest: Ticks and Tick-borne diseases are a potential threat to humans and animals worldwide. They cause huge losses to farmers and country's GDP. Transmission-blocking vaccines for Bovine babesiosis, theileriosis, and anaplasmosis targeted against tick host remain a high-impact animal health strategy. A cost-effective tick-targeted transmission blocking vaccine should be broadly protective and clear the pathogen within the tick vector. In this project, we will provide a potential candidate for the development of anti-vector vaccines against wide range of hard ticks and the cell-line based vaccine will be tested in lab and under field conditions for protection against tick-borne diseases. The vaccine produced against theileria and babesia which will be first checked in lab animals would be monitored in its true host animals under field conditions. For commercialization of the vaccine and its provision to the farmers, this vaccine technology will be handed over to the Government run vaccine production units so that it could reach the end-user and disease prevention target will be achieved. The unique aspect of this project is that it builds on the previous scientific accomplishment between the Pakistani and international scientists to address the critical knowledge gaps in our understanding of the functions of tick proteins in vector competence. The significance of the proposed work will work on many tick species.

data.projectName: Creating Technological Foundations of Data-Driven Policy Making for Sustainable Urban Development
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: The overarching goal of the project is to enable the use of technological innovations in data gathering, data analytics, and data-driven decision making for addressing complex problems that have become the hallmark of Pakistan’s urban spaces. In order to achieve this broad objective, the activities within the three-year project duration will focus on six separate, albeit intertwined verticals (applications) of an urban system that broadly span the pressing problems of urban sprawl, urban environment, health, and urban mobility. Each one of the six verticals will be guided by intricately linked horizontal themes that have been designed so as to guarantee the transdisciplinary nature of the project as well as to ensure long-term impact. The most obvious of these horizontals relate to technology (data collection and generation, development of algorithms for novel data analysis, and development of software toolsets), albeit with an emphasis on ensuring that the technological solutions adhere to the principles of equity, transparency, and social acceptability. At the same time, long term impact will be enabled through a strong focus on advancing data-driven decision making and evidence-based policy design practices in Pakistan, as well as through capacity building of relevant stakeholders.

data.projectName: Developing “drugable’’ CRISPR/Cas9 for treating ?-thalassemia and sickle cell anaemia
data.projectDigest:
Beta-thalassemia and sickle cell disease (SCD) are among the most common genetic diseases caused by mutations in the HBB gene, which encodes the beta subunit of hemoglobin. The global prevalence of this gene is estimated to be 3% and ~400,000 children are born with a serious hemoglobin disorder each year. In Pakistan, it is estimated that each year ~10,000 children are born with ?-thalassemia major (severe form of the disease) and the total number of registered thalassemic children exceeds 60,000. These children require regular red blood cell transfusions along with iron chelation therapy, which are often associated with iron overload and organ damage. 
Several studies have estimated that <1% of patients with ?-thalassemia major in Pakistan expect to live beyond 20 years, representing severe unmet needs for alternative therapeutic approaches. On the other hand, SCD is one of the established causes of anemia and the estimated prevalence in Pakistani population is roughly 4%. We plan to i) utilize autologous CD34+ cells, generate induced pluripotent cells (iPSCs). Skin biopsy will be obtained from individuals with SCD and ?-thalassemia. These CD34+/iPSC cells will be edited by CRISPR/Cas9 to repair HBB gene using HDR approach ii) disrupt BCL11A gene for reactivating the expression of fetal hemoglobin. Moreover, we will utilize Nanoliposomes, Organometallic compounds or direct Cas9 protein delivery using peptide transduction technology for cellular delivery of CRISPR/Cas9 system. The proof of concept will be tested in appropriate animal model. To sum up, this study will explore a potentially safe and efficacious therapy for patients with SCD and ?-thalassemia using an in vivo delivery system of CRISPR/Cas9 technology.

data.projectName: Development of bioactive hospital textiles and protective suits against viruses and bacteria by immobilization of nanomaterials
data.projectDigest: According to WHO, 511 million people get infected due to hospital acquired diseases and 13.3 million people die of these diseases.  The main reason is the passive nature of textiles being used in hospitals nowadays i.e. they do not have antibacterial and antiviral properties. Similarly, the personal protection suits used by doctors, nurses and paramedical staff are not active against pathogens.  In case, they get contaminated with viruses or bacteria, they harbor them and become source of their spreading to anyone they come in contact. In the wake of present pandemic, threat of spreading viruses and bacteria from hospital textiles and vulnerability of doctors, nurses and paramedical staff have increased manifold. In this context, the present project has been designed to provide solution to aforementioned problems/threats. For this, textiles will be treated with different nanomaterials having antiviral and antibacterial properties. These nanomaterials will be immobilized on fabric surface using silane coupling agents which will help attach them to have high washing durability. These fabrics with antibacterial and antiviral properties will be used for bedsheets, curtains and blankets at hospitals. Moreover, lamination of nylon/polyester/polyethylene/PU/PTFE film inside nanomaterials treated fabric will prevent penetration of viruses and bacteria into suit made of these fabrics thus providing complete protection to doctors, nurses and paramedical staffs.

data.projectName: IVIG production from convalescent plasma of COVID-19 survivors: a low risk, high efficiency passive immunization strategy against SARS-CoV-2
data.piUniversity: DOW University of Health Sciences, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
Passive immunization is a technique in which antibodies formed in one individual (donor) are given to another (patient) to save him/her from a life threatening infection. The two strategies of passive immunization are 
•	Transfusion of whole plasma 
•	Processing of donor’s plasma to purify antibodies 
Current situation of new Corona virus disease, known as COVID-19, needs an ultimate strategy to help prevent and control infection. Vaccine against this virus is under development and will take longer to be available for public. An emerging solution is use of plasma obtained from recovered patients of COVID-19 which contains high amount of antibodies against the virus. Despite of its usefulness, few risks and limitations are associated with plasma therapy including presence of other blood components, possibility of virus transmission, and blood group matching which may adversely affect the already suffering patient or cause treatment delays. In contrast, purified antibodies is low risk option as viruses are killed during antibody purification process, other blood components are removed and blood group matching not required.
The proposed project aims to produce purified antibodies through fractionation of plasma of recovered COVID-19 patient. Once produced in optimum amount, the antibodies can be a more effective and safer option than plasma transfusion.

data.projectName: Computational Modeling for COVID-19 Epidemic in Pakistan: Predictive Modeling of Disease Morbidity, Mortality and Assessment of Demands on the Intensive Care Units
data.projectDigest: COVID-19 epidemic broke out in Pakistan in February, 2020 and over 2,000 confirmed cases have been reported. The reports of local infections suggest community level infections are now in play. A diagnostic test based on RT-PCR for COVID-19 specific sequencing has been launched throughout Pakistan on limited scale. We propose measures to develop surveillance methods by use of machine learning tools on the data obtained from testing and symptomatic information to model the spread of COVID-19. This will contribute in accurate assessment of age groups of patients, symptoms, disease severity, and mortality based on the existing data and evidence generated in this study. As we move forward into unknown territory of the nature, prevalence, target population, mortality caused by COVID-19, two points are critical: 1) ability to triage, and 2) assessment of prevalence and disease severity. Accurate and quick assessment of patients and ability to accurately determine the prevalence in a given population to be able to make population level predictions is vital. The predictive-models based on antibody prevalence and machine learning based predictive modeling using population based clinical data and COVID-19 antibody prevalence can improve triaging, procurement and deployment of key resources to contain this disease and save lives.

data.projectName: To be decided
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest: COVID-19 is an infection caused by SARS-nCov2 virus.  Virus entered into nasal passages, can persist in the nose without causing infection, or cause mild infection, or cause severe fatal infections. The observed differences in disease severity are attributed to old age (increase susceptibility to severe infection in older adults) and underlying co-morbidities (diabetes, cancer, and other immune suppressing conditions).  Together with these factors, immune responses also play a central role in determining disease progression and severity.  The study propose to investigate immune responses associated with each disease states, while controlling for co-morbid conditions, age, and ethnicity. Immune patterns identified in each disease scenario will be translated into an immune signature (combination of molecules and pathways), which will be used to the assess the risk of developing serious fatal infection, thus allowing for early intervention and prevention of fatalities. Immune signature associated with asymptomatic carriage state, will serve as surrogate for protective immune response to disease.  Neutralizing antibodies to viral structural proteins (S, M, N and E) will be tested for their ability to passively protect against SARS-nCov2 in mouse model of infection.  Epitopes of immunogenic proteins will be tested for T and B cell specificities for vaccine design.

data.projectName: Immunological Viralogy and Genetic Basis of COVID-19 Patients
data.projectDigest:
COVID-19 is caused by SARS CoV-2 that is mainly transmitted by contact and droplets. Since the first case diagnosed in Pakistan, 26th Feb 2020, the outbreak has spread nationwide. Number of diagnosed patients has been increased upto 2500 cases with 30 deaths. Most patients have mild symptoms after infection, some patients developed severe symptoms and dies from multiple organ complications. Many factors involved in pathogenesis and severity of COVID-19 in Pakistan including host immunity and genetic that response to Viral infection. The pathogenesis of SARS-CoV-2 and its variation in infection in humans is unclear.
This Project will focus on Immune Pattern and genetics of local patients. The immunological changes, antibodies level in different Patients groups, recovered and local healthy population with HLA typing, Cytokines level and expression and variation of immuno related genes will be analyzed to find therapeutic targets and immune-modulators. Viral RNA will be extracted from COVID-19 patients and by sequencing Genetic variation of virus will be analyzed to find immunogenicity for Viral and Host interaction. By this research the potential pathogenesis of COVID-19, Its Molecular Mechanisms and other key players including localized factors (ethnic, genetic, travel history, life style) will be studied and findings will be shared with policymakers for public health.

data.projectName: Phylo- and immuno- dynamics of SARS-CoV-2 infection in Pakistan: relating COVID 19 disease severity in with viral diversity
data.projectDigest: The SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus, has been declared the causative agent of COVID 19 disease pandemic. We started to diagnose cases of COVID 19 in Feb 2020, at The Aga Khan Hospital, Karachi and within a month it tested 1610 suspected cases of whom 123 were positive for SARS-CoV-2 infection.  Patients came with a variable travel history and or possible local transmission and their disease severity varied greatly. It is of great important to understand the dynamics of the growing epidemic of COVID 19 in Pakistan. For this purpose, we propose to study the molecular epidemiology of SARS-CoV-2 strains by doing viral genome analysis amongst different isolates. Further, COVID 19 cases present with variable symptoms, mild flu-like, moderate or severe respiratory distress. data.projectName: Development of RT-LAMP Assay for Early Detection COVID-19
data.projectDigest:
Detection of SARS-CoV-2 (Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2) using Reverse-Transcriptase Loop mediated Isothermal Amplification (RT-LAMP) is proposed in the study. At present, detection of this novel coronavirus currently termed as 2019-nCOV (COVID-19) is largely dependent on conventional PCR or real time PCR techniques (real-time PCR). Despite of high sensitivity and specificity, conventional PCR based techniques do require specialised instrumentation (PCR machine, Gel Electrophoresis apparatus, Gel documentation System). Keeping odds of limited specialized instruments, skillful personnel availability and prolong processing test duration  RT-LAMP assay is strongly advocated. This will reduce undue burden on our present laboratories offering RT-PCR facility and delayed reporting. It will also reduce risk of specimen exposure during transfer across provincial or regional borders. Additionally, it will refine a need-based screening using in house facility.    
After cDNA synthesis, in RT-LAMP based approach, 6 target primers specifically designed against a predefined genomic region of 2019-nCoV (genome Reference Sequence: NC_045512.2) will be used.  Based on binding affinity, these LAMP primers should be able to amplify the respective target. Specimen cDNA along with primers, polymerase, SYBER Green dye, water, dNTPs, MgCl2 is placed a constant temperature (conventionally 65°C). Both amplification and detection of respective concatemers can be completed in a single step. In order to confirm presence of virus either change in PCR cocktail color or solution turbidity are already established indicators for LAMP. Additional, confirmation of amplified concatemersby using agarose gel electrophoresis can be omitted after RT-LAMP validation.

data.projectName: Indigenous Low-Cost  Production Of Ultra-Pure Taq Polymerase and PCR Mix  For COVID-19 clinical diagnostic Kits
data.projectDigest:
In clinical virology, the discovery of RT-PCR has provided a remarkable insight into the study of viral infections. This emerging technique is shown to be used not only for the viruses and bacteria but also for the quantification of parasites, fungi, and various protozoans. (Bankowski & Anderson, 2004; Shah et al., 2018; Sting et al., 2019; Trindade et al., 2020).
For (qRT-PCR) based diagnostic of corona virus and other human pathogens different kits are available. Prices for these kits are increasing and exorbitant from last year. For pandemic conditions as the current situation is for novel corona virus, it is quite difficult to manage these kits for clinical diagnostic at large numbers low cost price. Pakistan cannot afford such a financial burden because of its current economic condition. CEMB has already developed a clinical diagnostic kit for corona virus diagnostic and recently started test for patients. This kits has an expensive ingredients which we import, that is PCR mix which can easily be produced by developing a low cost indigenous ultra-pure Taq polymerase. Kit price can further be reduced to 1/10 and can be provided for whole nation at government level. In house production of low cost diagnostic kits will help government to perform massive clinical test in pandemic conditions as we are facing for COVID-19

data.projectName: Development of a reliable, economical and high throughput serodiagnostic method for early detection of COVID-19
data.projectDigest: We are facing the huge uncertainties regarding the extent which the present pandemic disease have caused in terms of loss of human lives and its socio-economic impact worldwide. In order to control the spread and treat such an infectious disease, we must have a reliable, economical and high throughput diagnostic procedure as well as an effective vaccine and other medicines for treatment. The currently available diagnostic methods based on RT-PCR or detection of IgG/IgM, do not meet all these criteria. In our opinion methods based on sensitive and reliable serodiagnostic seem to have the potential to meet these targets. Due to highly variable response in different individuals against antigens use of a single antigen for detecting antibodies produced against the viral proteins is likely to have very low sensitivity resulting in missing many positive cases. The research being proposed under this proposal shall develop fusion molecules based on multiple antigenic elements which will detect wide range of antibodies produced in early stages of the infection The results obtained from this project are likely to make important contribution in developing a reliable, cost effective and high throughput diagnosis of the disease in its early stages. This would be an extremely important contribution in diagnosis and prognosis of the disease and thus in its control. The protocols developed as a result of our research can be used to develop diagnostic kits, which can be put into commercial production after approval of the relevant statutory bodies in the country. Different human corona viruses have much in common with respect their general structure and the sequence similarities of the various elements involved in pathogenicity, like the similarities found between the SARS-CoV2 and SARS

data.projectName: Conductive polymers-coated sulfur enriched porous carbons as self-supported and flexible cathodes for lithium-sulfur batteries
data.projectDigest: Pakistan’s total power capacity of renewable energy was 4.2% and the government aims to increase it to 30% by 2030. As the population continues to grow, so will the demand for cheap energy, and an economy dependent on fossil fuels is creating drastic changes to our climate. Government needs to conduct deliberate preparation for the transformation of national energy to renewable energy sources, which is the need of the hour and should be treated as a national cause. The cost of batteries in solar projects is more than 30%.  In Pakistan, lead acid batteries are widely used with low backup and recycling capacity. Lithium ion-based battery banks have high backup therefore, gaining popularity. Battery industry is need of the hour. World is working on Li batteries to receive uninterrupted, durable and long-life electricity with once and low cost. Many scientists are also working on flexible batteries. The suggested batteries in this proposal are Li-S cathodes, with free and flexible battery structure. Moreover, it also suggests solution to the previous Li-S batteries issues like encapsulation of the sulfur, long term cyclic constancy due to integration with SWCNTs with low volume and high efficiency.

data.projectName: Vocational Training and access to decent work for women domestic workers, transgender individuals and persons with disabilities: Reflections on Gender, labor and equality for social inclusion of disadvantaged groups of Hazara Division
data.projectDigest: Gender equality, social equality, and availability of decent work opportunities are among the fundamental rights of every human being. United Nation’s (UN) 2030 Agenda for sustainable development particularly emphasizes upon safeguarding these rights for all citizens. However, some segments in Pakistan, in general, and those residence in less developed areas such as Hazara Division, in particular, do not have access even to these fundamental rights. Women domestic workers, transgender community, and persons with disability are among the most disadvantaged groups existing in the society that are continuously being ignored by the policymakers. One of the important problems facing these groups is the lack of availability of decent work opportunities which is a fundamental human right as explained in Goal 8 of the UN’s sustainable development agenda. Lack of access to decent work is causing several other problems related to social inclusion, access to justice, poverty, gender inequality, violence, and discrimination. Therefore, the primary objective of this project is to facilitate access to decent work by providing vocational and sensitization trainings to selected disadvantaged groups in Hazara Division. Qualitative ethnographic study and quantitative surveys will be performed to analyze the current social status and socio-economic problems of the selected groups. Customized trainings and sensitization programs will be designed and executed for each of the selected groups i.e. women domestic workers, transgender individuals, and persons with disability. The results of project will help in achieving sustainable development goals by ensuring decent work and social inclusion for the selected disadvantage groups in Hazara Division in particular and Pakistan in general.

data.projectName: Metering the aquifer using smart monitoring and data-driven approach to assist in devising adaptive groundwater management strategy in Balochistan
data.piUniversity: Balochistan University of Information Technology, Engineering and Management Sciences,Quetta
data.projectDigest: Water scarcity has become existing pressure on water resources will exacerbate due to exponential population growth and climate change. The past two decades, deep groundwater drilling for tube wells with an average depth of 300 m has resulted in lowering the water table at a rate of 2-6 m per annum. The current declining ratio of underground water in the province may lead to the water scarcity not only in the region but also in the urbanized hub and capital of the Balochistan province i.e. Quetta valley.  This project aims to use a sub branch of Artificial Intelligence (AI), i.e. Machine Learning (ML) to model and explore the groundwater budget in the selected sub basin of Pishin Lora Basin (PLB) in Balochistan Province. Additionally, in Balochistan province, the other sources of groundwater have been the dug wells, tube wells, springs and karezes (though now dried up, nevertheless it was considered the most important reliable resource of water for irrigation purposes). This proposal aims to identify by using a data-driven approach, the reasons of ground water depletion i.e. “falling water tables” in the selected sites from district Quetta. Hence, the proposal is also directly aligned with Pakistan Vison 2025, which clearly prioritizes the access to adequate supply of water to all (domestic, agriculture and industrial purposes).

data.projectName: Strengthening of Quality education at Gilgit-Baltistan by using digital platforms
data.piUniversity: Karakurum International University, Gilgit, Gilgit Baltistan
data.projectDigest:
According to Education Statistic-2016-17, about 35000 students were enrolled in secondary, higher secondary and degree levels education in public sector and private sector of GB. This enrolment is increasing at an average of 15% per year. Affordability, access and quality are the three major challenges for the education in the in Gilgit Baltistan (GB). The absence of digital and online platforms for teaching, learning and assessment of secondary and higher secondary education sector in GB, further worsens the quality and accessibility challenges, particularly during natural disasters. The challenge became more severe during the recent pandemic, when none of the schools and colleges in GB could provide education to their students for more than six months. Besides non availability of digital and online platforms, the poor capacity of the teachers in use of ICT for education is another major challenge. 
Based on the, successful experience of Karakoram International University (KIU), this project will attempt to provide customized Learning Management System (LMS) to the selected schools and Colleges of GB from public and private sectors, develop the capacity of teachers in these institutes for curriculum development, teaching, learning and assessment for digital and online systems.

Therefore, the only source of livelihood for the inhabitant of this region are private and government sector jobs for which they need sustained and quality educational opportunities.  As a result of Covid-19 pandemic followed by closure of schools, the teaching and learning processes are badly affected in this region. In order to address the said situation, at the global level, distance learning, online education, blended education, which relies on stakeholder’s acquaintance with the modern technology, have emerged as new phenomenon. However, limited exposure to online education and limited understanding of online pedagogies, both the students and teachers in GB are experiencing new kind of challenges that prevent them from getting benefit from these new mode of learning.  
The objective of this project is to develop a state-of-the art digital platforms (Learning management system and mobile apps) for schools that would enable the students and teachers to cope with the current situation and future challenges. Additionally, it is expected that on one hand the provision of digital plate form will expose the students and teachers with the modern technologies and on the other hand the teaching and learning processes will be improved through the integration of innovative teaching practices.        
Consequently, these measures  will equip the students of GB with the expertise compatible with the need of the 21st century organization where innovation,   creativity, multitasking,  and problems solving skills are considered as pre requisites  for securing better employment opportunities. Further, it will enhance readiness of GB education department for future shocks.

data.projectName: Climate change adaptations for indigenous coal desulfurization using ionic liquids
data.projectDigest: Pakistan has approximately 175 billion tons of Thar coal reserves (Rajar, 2007), but unfortunately its use in Pakistan’s energy projects is negligible (Economic Survey 2019-20). As coal is an economical fuel for thermal power plants therefore under China Pakistan Economic Corridor out of 23 energy projects 10 are coal fired power plants (CPEC website). Our country despite of having world’s 7th largest lignite coal reserves (Malkani et al., 2016), only 02 power plants are using local coal. Lignite is low quality fuel because it produces more smoke and less heat. Accelerating market prices of crude oil and natural gas in addition to shortage of available resources redirects the reliance on common fossil fuels. Import of 30 million tons of coal in 2019 is revealing improved economic activity but underutilization of indigenous reserves. It is accepted that coal is not only a dirty source of energy but main contributor to greenhouse gases including SOx, acid rain and water pollution. If local coal market is promoted, the challenge will be to maintain a good balance between socio-economic development and environmental transformation. The study is designed to develop cleaner and sustainable use of coal by reducing sulfur dioxide emissions before and after combustion processes of the coal.

data.projectName: Pre-mature Fruit Drop: A Local Challenge of Apple Growers in Rawalakot, Azad Jammu & Kashmir
data.projectDigest:
Out of seventeen Sustainable Development Goals, present study can contribute towards the realization of Goal 2, Goal 13 and Goal 15. 
Pre-mature fruit drop is an important cause of fruit loss in apple industry and has been recognized as severe problem in apple production for many years. Pre-mature fruit drop in which fruits are shed from the tree before ripening phase prior to horticultural maturity can occur in several apple cultivars. The pre-harvest drop is affected by various horticultural and climatic factors, but basic conditions of fruit set (synchronic bloom, transfer of pollen, etc.) still do decide definitely the fate of the flower in spite of the best weather conditions. Beyond a set quantity of fruits, the tree is unable to bring up larger load. A system of auto regulation works in the background and causes the drop of a fraction of fruits in spite of the accomplished fertilization and the equality of physiological precedents. Rawalakot is an area of Azad Jammu and Kashmir which is blessed with suitable climatic conditions for growing of apples. However, most of the fruit drops before harvest due to various factors. One of the factors is abscission of young fruit primordia which is triggered by hormonal imbalance. Studies showed that different plant growth regulators alter the growth behavior of plants which neutralize the enzymes responsible for generating the abscission zone and result in fruit drop reduction. However, no attempt has been made to deal with this problem in Rawalakot. Therefore, this study has been designed to evaluate the effect of different plant growth regulators on pre-mature fruit drop and biochemical characteristics of apples grown in Rawalakot.

data.localySocioEco: Apple (Malus domestica Borkh.) is one of the most popular temperate fruit. It requires abundant moisture and protection from strong winds. Apples grow well in areas with low temperatures and fortunately Rawalakot lies at an altitude of 1800-2000 m and latitude of 33-36° in North Eastern Pakistan, under the foothills of Himalaya and its climate is very much suitable for growing apples. However, quick variations in climate have been observed during the last few years such as comparative warm to very cold temperatures. These temperature fluctuations have resulted in a severe pre-mature fruit drop of apples in this area. In some cultivars this drop exceeded up to 20% while in some other cultivars this pre-mature fruit drop exceeded up to 50%. In recent past, this pre-mature fruit drop of apples in Rawalakot has resulted in severe economic losses to the local growers. Thus, there is enormous need and scope to work on this local challenge in this area. So far no studies have been conducted to find out the actual cause of this problem in Rawalakot. Therefore, this study has been designed to address this challenge using various techniques including the use of plant growth regulators.

data.projectName: Factors Inhibiting Beneficiation of Gemstones in Pakistan: A Mixed-methods Value Chain Analysis of Mining and Trade in Gemstone Industry of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa & Gilgit-Baltistan
data.projectDigest:
Pakistan’s Gemstone industry has been regularly reported to be amidst crises (see, e.g., Pakistantoday, 2014; Ahmed, 2017). More than a decade ago, the Government of Punjab (GoP) identified a plethora of challenges and problems faced by the gems and jewelry industry of Pakistan. According to the report,
Pakistan’s gems and jewelry industry suffers from limited investment in research, product development and training, low levels of technology, traditional mining techniques, underdeveloped lapidary facilities and skills, high raw material costs, poor international marketing and branding, underdeveloped designing capabilities, limited linkages with domestic and international support infrastructure, limited identification and certification, and lack of hallmarking. … Due to lack of adequate processing facilities and skills, limited understanding of gemology and lack of standardization and certification, approximately 75 percent of Pakistan’s exports consist of un-worked stones, representing a significant loss in value added. Gemstone cutting and polishing is done on a very limited scale and that too with outdated and underdeveloped techniques. There are only two commercial certification labs in the country, which are not internationally recognized. Lack of recognized lab infrastructure often leads to underselling of precious stones as well as lack of buyer confidence. Commerce is mainly conducted on a person to person basis with no established pricing structures. This imposes a significant transaction cost on the buyers and sellers. (GoP, 2006: 4-6)

data.projectName: Bioconversion of hazardous Parthenium into nutrients enriched azolla and rock phosphate blended organic fertilizer
data.projectDigest:
Till date several scientists have produced different types of organic fertilizer by using only the locally available organic wastes but no one (existing gap) has utilized Parthenium together with nitrogen rich azolla and phosphorus enriched rock phosphate (RP) for organic fertilizer/vermicompost preparation. Therefore, the current novel project/idea has been designed for the first time with the proposed aims to manage the local noxious Parthenium hystrophorus through bioagents transformation into a high quality/nutrients (N&P) enriched azolla and rock phosphate (RP) blended vermicompost and to verify its role on crop productivity and soil health as a possible substitute to chemical fertilizers.
	Initially, through the application of bioagents (earthworms and isolated PGPRs), nutrients (NP) enriched vermicompost will be prepared by blending a known quantity of azolla and RP with parthenium in vermiboxes. Afterwards, in comparison to chemical fertilizers, its efficiency will be assessed on the growth and nutrients uptake of wheat & maize crops in a greenhouse experiment. 
	After completion, the main deliverable/results of the project for researchers and local farmers will be the transfer of dangerous parthenium, azolla (high N content) and indigenous RP (high P content) into a beneficial product/vermicompost that can be used as an alternative to chemical fertilizers for improving crop production, well being of the farmers community, country's economy, producer health and environmental safety (relevant to UN SDGs No. 2 &3).

data.projectName: Achieving SDG 6: Inclusive Governance of Urban Water & Sanitation
data.projectDigest: Peshawar faces increasing demand of water and inequitable accessibility to water and sanitation services due to growing population, rapid urbanization, unsustainable and conventional water use practices and lack of regulations – issues linked to water and sanitation governance.  Our proposed research intends to address the following overarching question: What are the key factors that determine access to water and sanitation in different areas of Peshawar? The research project addresses the issues of access, service delivery (institutional mechanisms), inclusivity and sustainability for water and sanitation (WatSan) services. We aim to understand what are the institutional, capacity, operational (resources), and equity (power relations) related enabling factors that ensure access to potable drinking water and improved sanitation  in the urban areas  as well as barriers that constrain access to these essential services in the same city while these services fall under the mandate of the same governmental departments /entities.

data.projectName: Community-based Solid Waste Management through Active and Effective Participation
data.projectDigest: Pakistan is among the countries with serious challenges to public health and environment due to rapid, and unplanned urbanization. Research indicates that only 60% of the waste is collected from major cities in which 90% ends up at open dumping sites. Islamabad alone produces around 1000 tons of waste per day, which mostly finds refuge in its peripheral areas. Bhara Kahu, it’s peripheral area, is one of those waste dumping sites. The proposed project will be carried out in two phases. In Phase one, a baseline survey of the proposed project area will be conducted to estimate the quantity and type of the household waste, and also to assess the Knowledge, Attitude and Practices of the dwellers about SWM. Phase two proposes to introduce 3Rs (Reduce-Reuse-Recycle) strategy for solid waste management on two levels. First at household level, where women can play crucial role in segregating and managing domestic solid waste. Secondly, to devise mechanism of collecting waste from households to recycle. The project proposes to actively engage the community through different sustainable social mobilization techniques for clean and green Bhara Kahu. Lessons learnt through this project can be beneficial in replicating the project strategies to the other urban peripheries.

data.projectName: Urdu sign language to speech conversion for mute people
data.projectDigest:
Any society’s progress in social welfare can be measured by looking at how well their disable population in integrated into becoming a useful member of the society. For a society where the disables are left dependent on others, will burden its economy, and halt their overall growth. Enabling disables is beneficial to all members of the society. And for a developing country like Pakistan, with its limited resources, and world’s fifth largest population of disables, their integration becomes a matter of utmost importance. Mute, and Deaf-Mute people can easily be integrated into useful members of society. This will not only reduce their dependency on others, but also improve their quality of life. The only thing in the way of their progress is their ability to communicate. Even if they learn sign language, vast population of Pakistanis do not understand sign language. So, their ability to communicate does not increase significantly even they learn sign language. Integration of disable people into the society becomes responsibility of every member of the society.

This project proposes a wearable system that can recognize the sign language, and a speaker unit attached, which will speak out loud sign language. This way a mute, deaf-mute person would be enabled to a job where he can communicate his thought to people who do not understand sign language. At the completion of the project, a fully functional glove, with an ability to recognize signs will be developed. We believe that such system will directly play its part in overall progress of Pakistan, as each member of the society will become a useful contributor to countries economy.

data.projectName: Coloration of polyester fabric at room temperature using advanced structure color technique: A practical approach towards green environment and energy saving
data.projectDigest:
In the textile apparel industry, color is the most fundamental feature that makes our products beautiful and attractive to consumers. After coloration in textile industry, a huge amount of dye is wasted and drained, which contributes to environmental pollution due to toxicity. Hence there is urgent need to address this by replacing the toxic dyeing process. 
Apart from toxicity, dyeing polyester fibers is achieved at high temperature, i.e. polyester fabric dyed at 200 ?C in continuous method and 140 ?C in exhaust dyeing method for 1 hour. This results in high thermal budget which consequently adds to the cost of products apart from energy consumption. Therefore, development of new method based on low energy consumption at lower temperature is imperatively desired.
Currently, the structural color is emerging technology with potential to replace traditional dyeing process. This coloration technology is non-toxic, environment friendly and based on green synthetic methods. Our proposed method is based on structure coloration which allows dyeing achieved at room temperature in environment friendly way by reducing the energy consumption in textile industry.

data.projectName: High resolution flexible time-temperature indicator (FTTI) for food quality control
data.piUniversity: Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology, Topi
data.projectDigest: The shelf life of food items is highly dependent on its stored temperature. Monitoring of safe temperature is crucial for cold chain food items being transported across Pakistan. In order to assure food quality throughout the supply chain, there is a need for a sensor to monitor the time and temperature to determine its shelf life. This indicator is called a time temperature indicator. The project PI has successfully developed a novel flexible time temperature indicator (FTTI) that has the additional advantages of being flexible for attaching to any curved surface as well as high resolution of time scale for better readability. The FTTI will monitor three storage temperature conditions of 5 °C, 15 °C and 30 °C respectively. This project will upscale the production for the industrial sector. Pakengimed has kindly provided its manpower, technical, managerial, and premises as industrial support accounting for 71.4% of the project funding supported by HEC. It will also be beneficial for the medical industry for safe transporting of vaccines/medicine. With a market gap for FTTI, we aim at improving quality of vegetables, fruits, meat and dairy industry. Our novel device holds tremendous potential to be exported, boosting the economic growth of our country.

data.projectName: Security & Threat Intelligence Platform for Capital Market of Pakistan
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
NED University and National Clearing Company of Pakistan Limited is planning to jointly develop Pakistan's first AI-based Cyber Security Solution, named as Security and Threat Intelligence Platform. 
The solution will be an integration of advanced tools such as threat intelligence, artificially intelligent behavioral monitoring, asset discovery, smart intrusion detection and vulnerability assessment models. With such features, a solution can be of great benefit to the financial sector in Pakistan.
With increase in online businesses and transactions in Pakistan, the cyber threats have also increased [1]. Therefore, Cyber security enthusiasts in the country strongly feel that this endeavor could make Pakistan self-reliant in the Cyber security domain. This project can result in more capable and knowledgeable human capital which shall further develop innovative and cutting-edge solutions. Most importantly, control over data and its security will be strengthened which is necessary for Pakistan in this age of cyber warfare.
We are aiming for the industry to benefit from academia and vice versa. If such collaboration prospers, Pakistan won’t need to import cyber security solutions in future and thus the country's trade deficit will gradually reduce.

data.projectName: Industrial Scale Development of Waterproof Cum Heat Resistant, Montmorillonite Clay Modified High-pressure Plywood Composite (NustoPak Wood) from Renewable-Nonedible Agricultural Wastes
data.piUniversity: National University of Sciences & Technology, Rawalpindi/Islamabad (NUST)
data.projectDigest: Proposed project deals with industrial level scaling up of already developed prototype method and product of our research group. In our lab, we have successfully developed method for synthesis of adhesive phenol-furfural resin from extracts of Saccharum munja and peanut shells while biomass residues of these feed stocks extraction were employed as filling materials for manufacturing of plywood samples. This designed method has advantage of no left-over waste material. Moreover, water proofing, heat resistance and mechanical strength were improved by impregnation of functionalized montmorillonite clay into these prepared plywood samples. Results of this study were published into HEC ‘W’ category research journal while 02 patents related to method design and product were successfully filed. Pakistan is an agricultural country and enriched with minerals reservoirs. Fortunately, raw materials required for this project i.e. renewable biomass including agricultural reside and nonedible plants, and minerals i.e. montmorillonite clay are available in ample quantities. Thus, this project has good potential to develop cost effective and improved quality plywood products that are marketable and can generate positive cash flow. Although industry has shown encouraging response for commercialization of our method and product. However due to COVID-19 lockdown financial crunch, they could not 100% support this project. TTSF platform is an optimistic opportunity to support promising partnerships between academia (HEC & NUST) and industry (K.D.C. Boards (Pvt) Ltd & TASCO Mines (LLP)) to facilitate the transfer of university developed technological research to industry and the commercial sector.

data.projectName: Development of efficient Biological water purification systems for industrial wastewater
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: Industrial wastewater is a pollutant of concern now a days and enlisted as priority pollutants need to be treated. As wastewater of the industries are dumped directly in rivers and streams which makes them polluted and when used for drinking, are becoming cause of waterborne disease outbreaks.  In this regard this project proposed a biotechnological solution for the purification of the wastewater for one industry. This technology is environmental friendly and gives a good appealing view when reached on its full bloom with plants. Furthermore, this water purification system is far more economical as compared to the other technologies available in the market, as it does not required any electricity or chemical for its running. This will improve the living standard of local people by giving them safe and healthy drinking water, by reducing microbial load and also reduce the pressure of water scarcity by providing the opportunity to the industry to reuse the treated water for their agriculture land other processes. This technology development at one industry will be a set as an example for other industries to adopt this economic and environmental friendly technology for their industrial wastewater.

data.projectName: CONSOLE: Machine vision based industrial Inspection system for quality assurance
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest:
The current practices of quality assurance are manual inspection of products which comes hand in hand with increased risk of human error and is coupled with increased chances of undetected faults thereby, reducing the probability of the product to comply with international quality assurance standards. As a consequence of lower quality assurance standard, faith of customer/client is lost resulting in reduced profit margins. A few developed organizations in Pakistan with the capability to bear the cost of automated systems for quality check are limited to a single defect of the product. 
In view of the above context it is essential to automate the quality assurance and quality inspection practices of Pakistan thereby improving the quality of the product and increasing product acceptance in local and international markets by reducing human error and undetected faults. The proposed automated system for quality assurance addresses the variance between local and international product quality expectations. 
The developed Smart Quality Assurance system prototype for manufacturing industries employs sensor network for acquiring data and apply AI based approaches, thereby allowing the system to identify multiple manufacturing defects simultaneously in a cost effective manner, along with reduction/elimination of the time constraints offered with manual quality inspection and also minimizes the probability of undetected faults/error associated with conventional quality assurance practices resulting in increased inspection quality and capacity. The system developed is flexible enough to expand to various other defect features as per the industrial requirement and can be scaled up for various other industrial goods/products.

data.projectName: Large-scale production of indigenously developed pellet biofuel in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan
data.projectDigest: Wood pellet biofuel prototype has been developed/manufactured at Lab-scale (pilot project) in the Department of Forestry and Wildlife Management, University of Haripur, KPK under small grant pilot project 2019-2020 funded by Directorate of Science and Technology, Peshawar. pellet biofuel is increasingly used as a cooking and residential building heating biofuel in the modern world and has mainly replaced petroleum oils and firewood because it is low-emitting, eco-efficient, cost effective, energy-rich, renewable, and environment-friendly biofuel. Therefore, a low-emitting, cost effective and efficient wood pellet biofuel prototype has been developed at Lab-scale in the Forestry Lab of the University of Haripur, KPK. Indigenous technology (Pelletizer machine) for pellet formation was developed in Gujjar Ghari Engineering works (Local engineer) in Mardan city, KPK (Pictures of pelletizer machine are attached below). data.projectName: Development, production and commercialization of Aleosin-based wound healing scaffold
data.piUniversity: National University of Medical Sciences, Rawalpindi
data.projectDigest: The proposed project will lead to the development and commercialization of a wound healing scaffold that will be finished and packaged in the form of a bandage. The key innovation in the scaffold will be the presence of a wound-healing substance called Aloesin. Aloesin is a natural compound found in the Aloe vera plant which is used in skin protection and treatment worldwide. Currently, available wound care products in the market either only cover the wound such as bandages, or act as antibiotic agents such as the ointments. The second feature of the scaffold that makes it superior to available products is the sustained release of active drug molecule (aloesin) which will accelerate the wound-healing process and reduce the need for frequent replacement of the bandage. The polymer used to make the scaffold will be a mixture of cellulose and chitosan. So the safety of all the substances used in the making of the scaffold, ease of use, and the degree of innovation in the product will make this scaffold a leading wound care product in the market.

data.projectName: Transfer of a sustainable floating treatment wetlands technology to sectoral partner for the treatment and reuse of wastewater
data.piUniversity: Pakistan Institute of Engineering & Applied Sciences, Islamabad (PIEAS)
data.projectDigest: The discharge of untreated wastewater into the environment is a main reason for the contamination of clean water resources in Pakistan. The traditional methods for wastewater treatment are not applicable in Pakistan due to their high capital, operational, and maintenance costs. Floating treatment wetland (FTW) is a highly suitable alternatives for effective wastewater reclamation. The innovation of this green technology relies on the fact that it does not require chemicals, electricity, and skilled manpower for its operation and maintenance. Moreover, it is a low cost, self-sustaining and self-operating approach for the remediation of wastewater. NIBGE-College-PIEAS has already developed FTW for the remediation of municipal and industrial wastewater. However, this technology has not been promoted and marketed in the country. In this project, a multifaceted approach is proposed to transfer the developed technology to a Sectoral Partner for its large-scale application in the country for wastewater treatment and reuse. This involves the promotion and marketing of the developed technology, and its application thorough a sectoral partner at commercial, industrial, and residential units for wastewater treatment and reuse. The outcome of the project will render several benefits to Pakistan, including clean water availability to our next generations, and reduction in water pollution.

data.projectName: Designing of a Versatile Prototype based on the application of Ion Exchange Membranes, for Efficient and Cost Effective Recycling of Industrial Waste.
data.piUniversity: NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi
data.projectDigest: With energy cost rising and environmental problems worsening, the challenge currently lies in the development of cost effective and efficient technologies for waste treatment and waste recycling by sustainable resources. Ion exchange membranes (IEMs) have attracted much attention to achieve the energy task and to alleviate environment related issues by its wide-ranging applications from pharmaceuticals to waste treatment, desalination to water purification and energy production to energy storage. Its application extends into many industrial and electrochemical processes including, Reverse Electrodialysis (RED), Pressure Retarded Osmosis (PRO), Electrodialysis (ED), Fuel Cell (FC), Microbial Fuel Cell (MFC), Diffusion Dialysis (DD), CAPMIX batteries, and Redox flow batteries. These membranes have found little application in Pakistan due to its high cost. Most of the researcher imports these membranes from China or Korea at the cost of US $ 150/ m2 excluding the charges of shipping, Freight and custom duties. The challenge currently lies in the production of IEMs by eco-friendly and cost effective methods. Our R&D, have synthesized these membranes by environment-friendly and cost effective methods with special emphasis on its applications regarding water desalination, acid recovery and caustic recovery from waste. Our membrane cost is approximately US $ 15-30/m2. Current proposal is designed to transfer this developed technological research to industry and to connect the stated application of IEMs with sustainable development goals. For this purpose, a small membrane stack, based on the concept of Diffusion Dialysis (DD) and Electrodialysis (ED), will be designed and prepared at R&D sector for specific application of waste treatment and waste recycling. Practical use and optimum performance of this small membrane stack will be analyzed by using simulated waste sample. This stack will be tested for recovery of acids and bases by waste recycling process. After testing of small stack R & D will design the larger stack and prototype device in order to overcome the challenges in scaling up the stack. Hopefully, it would be a first step towards the economical recovery of acids, bases, metal ions, sulfure and many other useful chemicals from industrial effluent and industrial waste. This technology can be harvested in densely populated delta areas, where rivers with a low salinity flows in to the saline sea, where industrial brine is discharged, and the areas where industrial effluent/waste water is discharged. Proposed technology is not implemented in Pakistan, consequently this project has been designed. Our R & D will transfer the technology of membrane production to our industrial partner so that industry can produce consistent and homogeneous membranes, at low production cost. Methods of designing of such membranas can be patented. This proposal mainly focus on the designing of prototype stack, which will be equipped with our prepared Ion Exchange Membranes (IEM), for specific application of waste recycling. Our industrial partner will assist PI in the development of membrane based prototype for specific application of waste recycling. For this purpose industrial partner will co-finance upto 50 % of total budget in kind. After successful development of this process and successful designing of prototype stack at laboratory scale, our industrial partner will license the patent for commercialization of prototype stack and for membranes. Applications of this technology ensure the sustainable consumption and production pattern so hopefully it will provide cutting-edge services to cover the entire energy value chain for both developing and industrialized nations. After completion of this Project our industrial partner will be able to commercialize this prototype stack and address all the industries for the treatment of waste water, waste effluent, waste organic matter, industrial brine along with the recycling of this waste material as a practical, economical and beneficial application of this technology.

data.projectName: Commercialization of Specialty Multigrain Flour (MaxGrain®) developed for intended baked products utilizing indigenous cereals; A step to improve nutritional status of the masses
data.projectDigest: Wheat is the staple diet of Pakistan with 70% gross utilization, grown on 36% of cultivable land compared to 16-19% for all other cereals. Usual Pakistani diets are comprised of roti/chapatti made of wheat along with some vegetables/pulses and dairy products, and occasionally meat and fruit. In this proposed project, specialty multigrain flours will be developed to produce dietary diversity in Pakistanis diets without affecting their food budgets. Blending other cereals in wholegrain form in different proportions might help to overcome the nutrient deficiencies caused by utilizing wheat alone. The technology for development of multigrain flours (named as MAXGRAIN™ flours) will be transferred to the partner industry (Rehmat Wheat Products, Pvt. Ltd., Lahore). The industry already has an existing food supply chain and contact with various suppliers / growers of cereal grains, which will ensure the continuous supply of the materials needed. The industry also has well-trained, technical, manufacturing, quality and sales workers who will contribute to project success.

data.projectName: Automated Urdu Broadcast Media Content Extraction and Analytics
data.projectDigest:
We live in an information age and mostly the data is in unstructured form. According to Alexa, Youtube is the most visited social-media website in Pakistan, with 500 hours of video uploaded to it every minute from around the globe. For information extraction, effective management, enabling information access, and getting insights, video transcription is required.  Manual transcription of the video is drudgery in the era of computing. There is need of broadcast media content analysis system to get insights and manage this information for benefitting consumers, businesses and governance. 
This project focuses on broadcast media to develop intelligent systems to extract spoken and written content from such videos in textual form, organize this information and derive useful text-based analytics, e.g. allow topic based searching, speaker based summaries, automatic subtitling and more. This will facilitate these users in sifting through the enormous amount of Urdu video content being pushed online on daily basis. Automatic subtitling of video will help people with hearing-impairments in understanding the audio-visual content. Using the insights gained from analytics, advertisement agencies will be able to place the ads at the right place on right time. It will also help media regulatory authorities in regulating the broadcast media content more efficiently.

data.projectName: A Fully automated closed loop Anesthesia Machine with EEG based Depth of Anesthesia Monitoring
data.piUniversity: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), Lahore
data.projectDigest:
This project envisages local development and production of EEG controlled anesthesia machines.  This project will integrate an EEG-based DoA monitoring module that will control the anesthetic agent quantity in response to its effect on central nervous system. The proposed DoA monitor will utilize EEG-based features and machine learning tools to classify the patient’s state of consciousness and adjust the dose accordingly. This will allow accurate management of muscle relaxation and pain inhibition without overdoing it, thus having positive impact on the overall condition of patient and helping in early recovery without leaving any side effects. 
This will be the world’s first “patient-specific” anesthesia machine that incorporate EEG-based DoA monitor to control the drug dosage implemented using System-on-Chip (SoC). To develop the above system, the project is divided into following tasks:
To develop the above system, the project is divided into following tasks: 
1) Revision of Implementation of EEG based novel depth of anesthesia classification algorithm [Algorithm Development] 
2) Low-Power and small form-factor implementation of EEG DoA system [Hardware Implementation] 
3) Revision of mobile anesthesia apparatus (OXYMED 3000-PLUS) 
4) Integration of EEG DoA system with revised mobile anesthesia apparatus

data.projectName: Development of a patient monitor and remote medical data sharing  for vital signs and mental stress
data.projectDigest:
The vision and the broader picture of our project is to develop a local facility and capacity for medical device manufacturing and conduct research in this rapidly growing area. In this application, we are proposing an indigenous development of a patient monitor that can not only monitor the conventional parameter (SpO2, Perfusion index, heart rate, respiratory rate, temperature and ECG) as displayed on the commercial device but also add new features such as stress measurement and non-invasive blood pressure using photoplethysmography (PPG). Although, the existing commercial technology does provide displaying blood pressure but that is accomplished using exerting cuff pressure that if used continuously may cause complications such as fatigue and damage to the relevant vascular system and muscles. Our proposed technique of monitoring blood pressure using PPG would be accomplished using the same optical sensor that would already be in use for the acquisition of heart rate, SpO2 and respiratory rate. 
Measurement of mental stress has been in the spot light of the new IoT based gadgets since the availability of smart watches and smart phones, however, its validation and clinical reliability has remained a concern for the health providers. This part of the project would cover the aspect of research novelty in terms of using a new technique of using PPG and Galvanic Skin Response (GSR) for the estimation of stress measurement. All these eight physiological parameters would also be sent remotely to be accessed using android smart phone for the clinician to evaluate the condition of the patient and prescribe any medical or treatment. The developed mobile application may also be used by the users to store clinical data and share with potential healthcare providers. 
The PI, who is amongst the pioneers in the field of Biomedical Engineering, has a waste experience in project execution and medical device research and development. Photoplethysmography and measurement of other physiological measurement has been his key area of interest. The PI of the proposed project has been working in the area of PPG and SpO2 measurement using his own novel technique which has already been developed and published. His expertise would be utilized to implement the proposed strategy. The PI and his team has national and international research collaborations and conducting research in the area of brain computer interface, biomechanics, neuro-engineering and development of biomedical instruments such as ventilator.
Remote patient care technology has already been developed by one of the sectoral partner. The developed patient monitor that comprises of all sensors would use this solution as a strong platform for storage, evaluation and sharing with other healthcare providers and users (keeping all the ethical perspectives intact).
There is a huge market of patient monitors that has to be used by every hospital at patient bed. There is an estimated number of 200,000 plus patient monitors currently in use in Pakistan and this number is in rise as every month there is a new hospital being established either in private or public sector. 
Our aim is to save foreign exchange by developing this technology indigenously and contribute in local healthcare system by making these physiological parameters available online for the healthcare providers to assess patients’ condition. Indigenous development would help bring the cost down due to savings in terms of taxes and duties which eventually becomes almost double the actual cost of the equipment these days.
